name: Red Wings: Aces of the Sky
detailed_description: Red Wings: Aces of the Sky is an arcade action game that puts you in the middle of WWI aerial battles. The game combines the action-packed dynamics of classic flight games with modern arcade gameplay and detailed, stylized 3D art. Play solo or with a friend in 2-player local multiplayer mode. Upgrade your pilot progression skill tree to improve your stats and aim for the best score. Witness the birth, rise, and fall of the talented Red Baron, Manfred von Richthofen—the best ace of the war, credited with 80 victories. Become a part of his squadron or lead the hunt to take him down in Story Mode with two separate campaigns (Triple Alliance or Triple Entente). Key features: Play 50 story-driven campaign missions and relive the aerial combat of World War I (playable also in local multiplayer) Pilot 12 warplanes, each with their own unique skins—make your plane crackle with electricity, glow up the night sky with radioactive trails, and much more Fly with a friend in local split-screen co-op and get competitive in Versus Mode—fulfil objectives, battle each other, or play hide and seek in a Hide N' Seek match Challenge yourself in survival mode—fight off enemy waves, take down balloons and giant Zeppelins, or test your skills in timed missions For the best gaming experience, we recommend playing with a gamepad/controller .

_childDocuments_.review: I played the demo and it was OK enough. It turns out that the "Free to Play" component is just the demo again, but the demo still exists. The "DLC" is the real game itself. That doesn't make sense.Don't think that this is a spiritual successor to Crimson Skies. It isn't. There is no landscape to fly around, no "world" to explore. There are three mission types: shoot down all the enemies up in the clouds, fly through a series of hoops, and a 2D-ish top-down bombing thing. These repeat over and over with minor visual changes. You decide.

_childDocuments_.review: Here's the deal - this review on the steam system is of a 4 mission DEMO - not a free to play game. The verbiage being used here is troublesome. More on that later. OK, based on this DEMO, its a fun game with exceedingly basic controls and gorgeous art. You can't fly upside down (inverted) or do loops. Loops are pretty basic and the plane feels like it wants to do them - so i'm not sure what happened with the development there. I'm a pilot so I like seeing how game developers handle flight in games. I took a more thorough look at some aspects of the game in my review:  Suffice it to say that this demo doesn't give a great first first impression (one of the 4 missions you get to play is essentially a collect-a-thon). The art is great and I had a good time with the demo, but it is only a demo. Be sure to check the reviews of the 'add-on' for the reviews of the full game, which costs more money. Lots of positivity in these reviews because of it being f2p. Its not f2p.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an easy game to recommend, though I'd have trouble identifying who I'd recommend it to.The issue is that World War 1 is kind of a historical nerd exclusive setting. You don't get vast weapons/ship choices of sci-fi dogfights, afterburners and missiles you'd get with WW2, or the cool creative storytelling that comes with the creative fictional settings. Instead, you get gentleman with funny English/German accents that hide in the clouds and put on a jolly good show in the air. For a non-nerd this setting is pretty slow and dull.This game isn't slow and dull, but a solid arcade dog-fighting game. To sum up the realism, you collect magic healing rings and your ultimate attack is to barrel roll into the enemy. The developers sidestepped around the common WW1 issues by adding special moves to your arsenal. Invincibility Barrel roll? Check. Instant turnaround? Check. Wingmen that take on the role of modern missiles? Bingo. A pretty cool insta-kill where you pull out your pistol and snipe the enemy fighter? Hell to the yes.Combine this "Enhanced" WW1 flight mechanic with multiple mission types, upgradable skill slots, unlockable planes, a couple unique enemy types and some cutscenes showcasing the usual boring WW1 stuff... and you get Red Wings. This game is exceptionally well-made and mechanically its well-thought out out. But this final product is made for an audience that I don't know exists. It plays casually but it's still a generic WW1 setting that won't hold casual attention for long. For a historical nerd such as myself.... WTF IS BARREL ROLL AN ATTACK!? (Translation: the lack of historical accuracy and flight mechanics like gravity and the sun just feels lacking during this era of flight)Despite some balance issues and an overall feeling that its slightly longer than it should be, I've really enjoyed this game.  And if you happen to be this mythical audience that I don't know exists... its well worth a sale price.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: Tried the game again in late 2021. They have fixed the resolution issue I was having when I wrote the original review (below), but nothing else. This is still a flight game that doesn't allow either joystick or mouse input. It's honestly bizarre. I'm sure they lost a lot of money on this game, which clearly flopped, and all it would have taken to get maybe 5X or 10X more people playing it would have been to provide the conventional, expected sort of controller support for the genre. You'll see the dev who responded to my original review below said they didn't include joystick support because they wanted "an arcade experience" -- I mean, it's hard to even know where to start responding to a comment like that. Have these devs ever been to an arcade? Where do they think joysticks even came from? Well they'd be right to say not the arcade -- arcades just popularized the joystick and made it a household word. But of course arcade games borrowed the joystick from (..wait for it) airplanes. So I guess what I'm saying here is that it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ insane to make a game like this without joystick support, but beyond that, no mouse support. Mouse is the fall-back for PC gamers who don't have the right equipment. I have a gamepad that I recharge and use maybe every year or two, mostly to see if it still works, but then I put it away. Why? Because I'm a PC gamer, gaming on a PC. I have a keyboard, I have a mouse, I have a HOTAS. Come on, devs, you really just dropped the ball on this one, and you were told you dropped the ball, and instead of picking it up, you left it there on the ground. What a waste.---ORIGINAL REVIEW:Huge disappointment. I've been waiting a long time for this game to release, as I'm a fan of simple, arcade-style flight sims. First thing I notice is the resolution in inexplicably fixed at 1176x664. There is a resolution selector, sure, but that's the only resolution you can select. Next, controls. As a PC flight sim fan, I of course have a joystick. So, plugging in the joystick actually disables the menu system in the game since I guess it's only set up for a gamepad. Does not work at all to control the plane. That leaves keyboard controls, which aren't any fun on a flight game. Apparently no mouse control.So that leaves a flight game that only plays in somewhere around VGA resolution, that doesn't allow for joystick or HOTAS input, and instead forces users to steer with their keyboards. Took me right back to 1992. Highly not recommended.---RESPONSE TO DEVELOPER COMMENT:I'm not a game developer, but I understand how difficult it must be to put together any big project like this, and how infuriating it probably is to see reviews like mine, so I appreciate your constructive tone. I agree with your focus on an arcade style experience, but would suggest joystick support would actually contribute to that goal and better approximate arcade controls (at least last time I visited an arcade). You don't need realistic flight controls or even 'roll,' but joysticks allow for better control in a flight sim and are just more fun for many of us. As a PC game, the one platform where gamers really have the joystick option for flight games, it would be an important control system to support even in a more casual game.I don't know why the resolution is stuck but I uninstalled and reinstalled the game, and it won't move from 1176x664. I have a 4K monitor and a GTX 1080 Ti graphics card, and I've never had a similar experience with another game.For me, keyboard controls for a flight sim just don't cut it, and I'm not a fan of gamepads for PC games, so I'm happy to follow the game but won't play again until joystick support is added. If you're able to do that, I'll be happy to give it another shot and update the review.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this product free on steam during the Mar2021 promotion and immediately found it fun and engaging. The flying is similar to Sky Pilot and Crimson skies although set during World War 2. There are 2 campaigns for each side of the conflict with about 25 missions during which you will gain skill points to level up abilities and also gain access to new aircraft. It has a co-op mode although I haven't used it myself. This game kept me coming back after my initial play and I ended up finishing both campaigns and unlocking some of the crazier skins for some of the aircraft. Great fun and although I got it free It is worth picking up on sale If you like the idea of a WW2 arcade flight game.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, this is an arcade type game. This is NOT a fighter plane simulator of some sort (like Ace Combat series)if you expect a realistic flight control/plane maneuver, this is not game for you. For instance, you can only control pitch and yaw+roll combined to turn the plane. The shooting (strafing) physic is straightforward. You shoot straight into enemy planes, without bullet trajectory. And because of limited flight control i mentioned before, it is hard to dodge enemy bullet, without some special moves involved.But for arcade-y game, this is good. You hop into WW1 era planes, shoving bullets to enemy planes. Graphics good, for controls, you definitely needs a controller.. once more, treat this game as an arcade type flight games, and it will give you fun. Altough, as a flight sim lover, personally i'd like to if this game give some options, at least for manually control pitch, roll, and yaw of the plane..

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the first few missions but then it gets annoying starting around mission 8 or 9.  If you do the level well you get "stars" to upgrade your ship.  But it can be quite challenging to get the stars on levels where its based on the score.  They use a multiplier if you kill the next plane within a few seconds. 100, 200, 400 etc - but if you don't hit / kill on you are  back to base score and trying to get 25000 is very annoying with that.  You end the mission with a score of 2000 and you need 25000 to get the stars LMFAO.  The ones with timers aren't as bad imo.Starting on Mission 9 - enemy planes keep smashing in to your plane (kamikaze central) - not one or 2 but near all of them.There are these levels of "refueling" where you have to run through 50+ circles - which are just an annoying / filler level. First one was 26 circles , next one was 50 - which is where the game was uninstalled.The upgrades you get are also unimpressive - was hoping for ones that improved the damage  but they are mostly related to better cooling or better against armor (which regenerates on the enemy planes - flying tanks??) or seconds off the cool down timer of abilities (rolling)

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed what I played so far. There are so many flight games, yet so few that take place during WWI. This is not a sim, obviously, with radar and shields and fuel-refilling balloons, but those things don't bother me; I'm not looking for a sim - I'm looking to fill the WWI flying itch that never goes away.It's like any other air or space combat game; fly around and destroy the enemy, and there is obvious aim assist going on which I really appreciate, because I suck at these kinds of games, often swinging my plane wildly just trying to lay a bead on an enemy, and with planes flying all over it helps.Being able to hide in clouds was also a nice touch, as are the lovely cel-shaded graphics. Colorful, rich, with beautiful and varied terrain with nice little touches of its own such as explosions happening far below you.It's nice to have a beautiful to look at and easy to play WWI flying game. Takes me back to Warbirds on the Lynx (remember THAT?). If you're looking for something more hardcore this may not be for you, but I feel like the game was made just for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Looks nice, runs well... Thought it might satisfy the itch of wanting to play the original Crimson Skies again. Sadly, not at the moment...Controls have been updated, it now has configurable controls and joystick support... (Original review striked out at the bottom)That being said, The HOTAS support still needs a lot of work. I like the fact that you can use more than one input device at the same time (tbf most modern flight games do this now, but it's still nice to see). So I can use my CH pro throttle and VKB joystick to fly the plane.The controls menu could do with a little work so you easily see which control you've already configured on one device (instead of having to switch between the selected devices you're configuring). However it does work as it is.I'd like to see an advanced controls option too, something more sim like. Separate yaw from roll and have them on their own axis for instance.I like the art style, reminds me of Crimson Skies. I can see a lot of thought and work has gone into some areas of the game.It's not all good though. You can fly straight up, or straight down, but you can't go upside down...? Pulling back on the stick, expecting to loop over... NOPE! You have hit the invisible nose hook that won't allow you to pull back any further... It's like hitting an invisible wall. Feels wrong. Like riding a motorbike that's stuck on train tracks.And the joystick input only seems to register while the stick is physically moving. I move the stick slowly left, I'll fly around in circles. I move it quickly left, I make one little jerk about 5° to the left. As soon as the stick stops moving, the craft stops responding to it's position like the stick has reset to it's neutral position (it hasn't). This is the real killer for me. Makes any sort of hope of precise flying a laughable dream at the moment.That being said, the dev does appear to listen to feedback and want to make improvements (he added HOTAS support and configurable controls after all). So if the issues get fixed, I look forward to updating my review, again.

_childDocuments_.review: I got it from a good friend, and it is a good game! My laptop is not a gaming computer, without a dedicated graphics card, but the game runs smoothly! I just have to wait for it to load for a few minutes, but once it's ready, it is great! The controls can be tricky if you want to not use resources like auto-target and quick turn, but once you master them, you can play it pretty naturally. The graphics have an interesting cartoon drawing, what is great and adjusted to the age where the plot is developed, during the 1st World War. The clouds are kinda annoying, but they are part of the skies, right? The sounds are realistic and they also give me a feeling from that time. The sounds of the wind, shots, engines, explosions are great. I wish there was an original soundtrack, but it is not a big flaw.All things considered, I recommend it as a relaxing and fun game! A perfect game to play when you want to relax and dogfight other airplanes!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the sequel to the best arcade game with Airplanes "Skys of Fury DX". The first work was not published on the PC and does not even have an online PvP mode (its only negative point, by the way) and still has better ratings than this game (Metacritic 68 vs 79). This is a huge setback for a second part, which should actually be better than the first, and Red Wings is actually the worse game. Why? The answer is simple. The first part actually played a lot like this one.It was an arcade game and had very similar mechanisms. In Red Wings more game modes were added, better controls, better customization options, a real multiplayer mode, all things that the game urgently needed and also improved ... but! The developers thought it wouldn't be a real improvement if you didn't add fancy game mechanisms that would completely destroy the realism ... Yes, the realism in an arcade game! That’s the crux of the matter, Skys of Fury was a great arcade game, but you still felt like you were in a battle over the skies of the First World War. And that was the secret of why it's a better game. I'm disappointed because I was really looking forward to this game and now a third part has been announced "Red Wings American Aces" ... Well I guess they'll add more nonsense and don't rely on the roots of the game series and make it worse. It could have been so easy. Take the mechanics of Skys of Fury and just add more content! More planes, different missions (with bombers for example), a solid PvP mode with squads, etc ... Well, ultimately it's just a game and a missed opportunity ... too bad.

_childDocuments_.review: Arcade-like WWI-era dogfighting game with cartoony graphics. There's a survival mode, a tutorial, and a 'story' where you can play as a pilot from the Triple Entente or Triple Alliance. It's pretty fun to play, there's a bunch of challenges and the controls are easy enough to pick up and do well in - yet always have room to do better. Everything seems to be designed around the xbox/ps controller style using a 'neutral button graphic set' (twin stick, four shoulder button, and four face buttons) so people using other layout types may run into handling issues.Movies play out like a comic book reading, I do like that they have subtitles.BRRRRRRRRRRRT goes the plane. If you're looking for an arcade dogfighting game and just want to shoot down planes without all the extra sim stuff, this is a solid pickup.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Wings: Aces of the Sky

_childDocuments_.review: The most fun i had in a very long time, the game has a clear vision, it's honest about it and completely succeeds in achieving it's goal. It has a modest but perfectly executed art style, it has upgrades, skins and challenges. All those elements contribute to an engaging and fun game loop. Red Wings also has the quality of life features you'd expect from any contemporary game. If more developers followed their vision like these guys, we'd have more great games like this one. The game was free a couple of days ago but it's certainly worth the asking price and probably more.  BUY IT. Ps: It's more fun than any of the ace combat games I've played, and i played many. WWI air combat is where it's at. No boring missile lock on in this one. Just pure machine-gun dog fighting fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Red Wings: Aces of the Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little game. Not realistic AT ALL, but I imagine that's not the point. It's trying to be graphically stylistic - which it is - and an arcade-style, accessibly fun flying game. Kind of reminds me of Wings for the Amiga, but with a triple decker warplane of CHEESE. This game makes Wings look like a realistic simulator. I don't love it, but I don't completely hate this game, don't get me wrong. I'm kind of on the fence. But if I had to rate it... 3.5 out of 5. And that's being generous. At first I found it so crash-prone that I gave it two stars. But it seems to be better now, so I edited the review and gave it a positive rating. It's just so unrealistic. At least it's fun, and runs well on old/weak hardware. It just takes a bit more disk space than I think it should, given how simple it is. Ah, well, that's cheap now. I just picked up a 240GB SSD for $18, so I ain't gonna cry.

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion this game deserves a better rating than the 60% it currently has.Many of the negative ratings are related to the fact that the base game is basically what was the demo prior to release and that the full game is contained in the DLC. This was a somewhat unorthodox and really unfortunate decision made by All in! Games, because the DLC representing the full game has almost no ratings, while a big part of the negative base game ratings are likely from demo-only players and most positive base game ratings are likely from DLC buyers.I enjoyed the casual game play, the smooth controls (with my Xbox 360 controller) and the cartoonish but nice looks. Having bought the DLC, I finished the single-player campaign with both the Germans and the Allies and also played through the three wave mode difficulties.However, there are a few design choices and bugs that are a bit annoying:- The menu navigation is cumbersome, especially if you want to change your plane and/or skill point allocation between missions or for the same mission. You always have to restart navigating from the main menu.- Due to a bug, the skill menu did not work for me post-mission, but only pre-mission.- There are many likeable and good looking plane skins to unlock. However, for many of them to unlock, you will need to earn a lot of skill points first, like from finishing most campaign missions with 3-star ratings. This means you will unlock most skins only towards the end of the campaign. And as it does not provide much replay value, you have only limited occassions to use all those unlocked skins.

Runs smooth and the graphics are unique enough to admire for a play through.

The gameplay itself is fun and simple enough, and trying to get 3 stars every mission so you can get more perks and become stronger is very satisfying. Also, I didn't get to try it but the game does have a local/split-screen co-op campaign, co-op survival and versus mode, and they look nice.

_childDocuments_.review: My thirst for more WW1 Aviation games has been quenched once moreSo far, i'm really enjoying this game. Despite it's simplistic art style, it still looks very beautiful and runs smoothly because of it. The gameplay is fun aswell, you can use four different moves to aid you in combat (especially the Final Takedown move, which is incredibly satisfying to use). I also like the fact that the game features some aircraft, which are rarely seen in these types of games (if at all), like the Hansa Brandenburg D.I or the Bristol M.And yes, you could argue that this game is a copy of Skies of Fury DX, but i would consider it more of a spiritual successor as there are some differences and improvements, like the addition of bombing missions, much more detailed and varied locations and much better visuals overall. Personally, this game was worth my money and i think it will be worth yours too.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun Arcade flight shooter (crimson sky vibes). The most efficient way to kill enemies is to barrel roll(you are invulnerable) into them.No idea what the single player story is all about, narrative is all over the place. Replayability comes from unlocking 3 stars for each mission.To unlock skins, there are stages that require chaining kills to get your combo meter going to attain high score (this is the worst aspect of the entire game). Unlike combo games(Arkham Batman), the enemy AI will focus on you. Here the enemy planes are flying all over the place, reducing your chance to chain your combo meaningfully. There are a total of 4 types of missions in single player :time based, score based, refuelling(Superman ring types) and seek enemy balloon. Mission then rinse and repeats with newer enemies coming in. _childDocuments_.review: Red Wings is an arcade flight combat game. You fly around shooting enemies and using four special abilities.For some insane reason this flying game doesn't use the mouse outside of the main menu. It's such a bizarre choice, and it makes the game really awkward and unpleasant.Another weird choice is the design of the icons. There is an icon with an arrow turning around and one with a boomerang. The ability to turn around is activated with the boomerang, the barrel roll with the turning arrow. It's needlessly confusing.The rest of the gameplay is rather dull as well. Enemy planes show up, you shoot them down and new planes show up. Even the aiming is boring, you don't seem to need to lead your shots.Red Wings does have decent production value but this obviously cannot compensate for the bad gameplay. I wouldn't recommend this if you (also) got it for free, let alone pay €17 (!!) for it.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: only get this game if it's free, otherwise don't bother. Badly made console port. I wouldn't buy it for more than 1€ / $.First, I have to add that I got this game for free on the free giveaway, and I'm honestly relieved that I didn't had to pay money for it. There are a lot of things wrong in this game, which could otherwise be a very fun and interresting game, in a time when WW1 games are pretty rare... which is a bummer.change key bindings: non existant. This is a poorly done console port. Playing this game with the keyboard is a pain. So if you don't own a controller, don't even bother... especially if you don't have a QWERTY keyboard. Thanks mister developer, keybinding existed in the 90's already. It's 2021 now !VSYNC: non existant. Enjoy your screen tearing. Na just a joke, the developper just wants you to learn how to force VSync on your graphics card drivers. That's not the business of the developper,m right ?AI: non existant. It isn't that bad in the campaign, as you have allies flying with you, but in survival mode where you're the only one, all enemies tend to kamikaze in your plane. This is so bad that there's actually a skill / upgrade in the game so that you gain points for enemies crashing into you when you use your invincibility skill. This skill has a 8 seconds cooldown and it's far to long compared to the amount of suicidal pilots. This would have made sense if this game was in space and the enemies some sort of amoeba or suicide bugs.Physics: non-existant. Going up or down won't have any influence on your speed. You also can't crash, as the ground doesn't exist and you get teleported when you exit your "combat space". Even for an arcade game this is bad.Speaking of teleportation: enemies simply teleport next to you when you have the annoying "enemy renforcements have arrived".The audio/radio cues are annoying as hell (on a timeline when radio didn't exist on planes).Oh, and if you get hooked by the 50 mission statement, then you're pleased to know that there is NO difference between the entente or alliance campaign. They have EXACTLY the same missions.... so you have 25 missions that you have to play 2 times... but in fact you'll play them several times because they all have a rating system, but you don't know the conditions before you finished the mission. So you'll play every of thos 25 missions several times... and then you multiplay by 2.And there are also missions that need a specific SCORE to unlock the plane skins, but there's NO score indicator... you basically have to guess your score and if it's OK to finish your mission.Last, remember the N64 and the worst game on it: superman, where you had to fly throug rings ? You get the same here...don't ask me why WW1 pilots had to fly through wings but here you go... The first missions are OK and feel more like a timesink, but then, oh, the rings begin to move up and down, and are hidden in clouds. Oh and you're on a tight timer to go through a ring, emaning if you miss one you're basically dead.Now, you could simply take the right plane for the right mission, right ? WRONG. You can't change your plane between missions. You have to aboard the mission to get back to the menu. But it doesn't matter, the differences between the planes are marginal at best... never felt a certain plane was better than the others.Last but not least, the game uses hitscan mechanics. Right, no need to even thing about leading your target. No matter if it's 1 mile or 10 feet away from you, your bullets wil magically hit if the target is in your reticle...which of course is glued thanks to autoaim.The only upside I found for this game are the graphics, they look nice cartoony. but that's about it.

It's also very amateurish in some ways, like the fact that there are really no graphical settings (including Vsync) and the existence of a skill, which I imagine the devs envisioned as the most important one since it deals damage and heals, that plays a brief cutscene every single time you use it. It's cool to watch it once or twice but after that it's just an endless interruption. Having said that, it's not awful. It's a basic but perfectly fine title that you could find enjoyment in for a couple hours. The normal asking price however is very misguided so I'd wait for a sale, wouldn't be a bad purchase for like 3 bucks.

_childDocuments_.review: 4/10Red Wings is an arcade dog-fighting game that tries so hard to be like Snoopy Flying Ace, but fails to understand what made that game work so well. Admittedly, I haven't played that game in over a decade, but I remember it being very fun and was something that I kept going back to a lot. I was hoping that Red Wings would at the very least be fun while not being as fun as my childhood game, but it isn't even that. Also, Xbox Game Studios, get a developer to port Snoopy Flying Ace over to PC.+ Weapons have good impact.+ Good aesthetics and graphics.- Repetitive soundtrack.- You can't add extra weapons to your planes. You only have one weapon to shoot your enemies with.- There's no quick dodge move that doesn't operate on a cooldown. This isn't ideal when enemies have near perfect accuracy.- All the levels function the same. They all may look different, but there are hardly any stage hazards or geometry in general to make themselves stand out.- Enemies have near perfect accuracy. This isn't ideal when there are a dozen of enemies shooting at you and you have to hope that you're near a health/fuel pickup.

_childDocuments_.review: Red Wings: Aces of the Sky is an arcade 3d plane shooter that plays around 1916 during WW1The game has a story mode, co-op and survival. versus for if you wanna challenge your friendsStory mode is... more or less something i didn't expect to be that mediocre yet wasn't surprised to be "that bad". the narrator explains how it felt being a pilot and sometimes about the war. not a Oscar story but that's really about it. worth buying some popcorn and a soda for that if you ask me Game play is straight forward, categorized into certain types such as: score, time, fuel and objective. with 4 skills that are very vital and important for every plane you are engaging and different planes to choose from that are suited for different missions. well considering how easy it may be starting, trust me, even i as a gamer myself, this game has one of the biggest skill level requiring if you want to get all 3 stars, finish the game or just get achievements including co-op and survival. its not you learn this and understand this, then you progress. its more of you have this, you do this and you must do it perfectly. i would definitely understand if the arcade machines back in the 90's were that difficult to win against, but its not machines winning against humans, if you just sit and understand for a moment that its made to be impossible. nowadays its just ridiculously hard to even stress yourself to be that kind of gamer who doesn't get even appraise for doing something others cant, so what is the point of making it hard yet unrewarding at the same time? as all gamers have been The audio and art style are very fascinating and well made. i never have experienced something such beautiful and appealing for a indie game like this before.For how well simple and well done the game is made, the price sure is quite a bummer to see but of course recommending it during a sale is what i can all say Sure in conclusion i recommend it to every average gamer that likes to skip some time and play with friends together for fun times. please just don't take it serious like it could have been something like War Thunder.... we don't do that here

_childDocuments_.review: Red Wings is a console ported arcade style third person vehicle shooter game with a "flight sim" theme (but no flight sim substance).   It's set in a loose rendition of World War 1 and attempts to create dogfighting scenarios. This is 100% focused at being a console game for console peasants.  PC gamers will immediately be insulted by the suggestion to plug in a console peasant childrens toy gamepad, despite having KB+M right in front of them.  Presumably console developers don't know about PC gaming peripherals like HOTAS, either.   However, older reviews complain about there being a lack of Y axis inversion but I note the developers seem to have added that, so there's something. While there's 4K support, the game assets are fairly low poly (presumably to cater for the primitive console appliances the game was designed for).  Unfortunately that means PC gamers need to once more put up with compromises made for console peasants.   Likewise the gameplay is heavily dumbed down to cater for the target audience (PC port here is clearly an afterthought/cash grab). Despite all these limitations, flaws and compromises made to appeal to console peasants, the developers seem to think this is worth more than some AAA flight sims, with an eye watering $20 USD price tag for a console port.  You can play War Thunder for free, and it's superior in every respect to this.   There's a number of far better flight sims on Steam that are far better, much cheaper, and without console peasant compromises, so it's impossible to recommend this.

_childDocuments_.review: It's your basic first person 'red baron' arcade shooter.   Unfortunately, there's very little more than that. But, without the things thrown in, it is very very repetitive.  There's also the issue of earning starts for finishing quickly or scoring a lot, which means you end up playing so far, hitting a skill wall and having to keep replaying missions having earnt enough stars to unlock a couple of power ups and repeat this over and over, meaning the game looks really long, but you're just doing the same things with a power up added in. Don't get me wrong, it's fun, it's frustrating, but there's not enough to keep you coming back for more and more unless you do just want to keep doing the same but slightly harder mission each time you play.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun, light arcade air combat simulator. Good thing is that is simple, the controls feel OK on a game pad, and there's some variety in planes, skills and few different mission types.  Flying exists mostly in a groundless vacuum of an arena high up in the air,  which is  a bit of shame since this would be more at home for WW2 type planes, and not having those landing and take off mechanics and close to earth dog fights would work better for the time period they were imitating in this alternative world.  Perhaps the developers thought that era was done to death but still.  Didn't have a chance to play multiplayer yet but I think that's where this thing would be most at home, quick matches with friends. It's an OK game especially for free/discount. Gameplay suffers from lack of button reassigning- which is something really annoying as one of the worst special moves, calling up the squadron,  actually requires to a target lock to confirm the use, during that you cannot use your other abilities, which is infuriating in during dog fights when you accidentally press it. Killshot special moves animation is always the same and too long, in the single player mode it is useless without its upgrade points and available far too often, this is obviously some multiplayer perk that isn't needed in singe player if you are smart about game design. Speaking of which, this game has some of the most poorly conveyed hoop flying I've seen since GTA SA.The sometimes cartoon-like atmosphere clashes with the seriousness in the cut scenes, its kinda telling when you have to award achievement badges for people to actually look at them how much most players find them useless and boring. But again, for a the right price, nice bit of arcade fun.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of WWI planes and with many hours spent on simulators, I can say that this is the best arcade game on the subject I've played since now, and the one that makes the fun playing as close as a "real dogfight". The graphics are nice and with a cartoonish touch, the story mode is good and the playing is fun. I've first tried to play it with keyboard and it was very hard, but with my cheap Amazon controller I've enjoyed it a lot. The furballs in the sky with enemy planes turning and shooting are entertaining and challenging like in a simulator, but the powers and skills make it fast paced and entertaining like a game.I suggest you to buy it only if you have a controller, at least 'till they make it more playable on keyboard, but if you have one, it's a lot of fun. I hope the developers will make some adds to the game, maybe different missions like bombers/zeppelin escorting, more various bombing runs and so on. And most of all, they gave it a 100% discount for some days, so I've had it for free

MORE GAMES YOU MAY LIKE [url] PRESS ' Morbid: The Seven Acolytes looks bloody brilliant .' - Eurogamer ' Morbid: The Seven Acolytes is a top-down action game with Bloodborne vibes. ' - PC Gamer REVIEWS Noisy Pixel - 8.5/10 Finger Guns - 8/10 About the Game You are the last surviving Striver of Dibrom. Your duty, for which you have trained your whole life, is to defeat the Seven Acolytes, accursed and powerful beings, possessed by malevolent deities called Gahars. Experience epic bosses and a multitude of bloodthirsty encounters as you build your character. Challenging foes, mini-bosses, and memorable large-scale boss fights with fully orchestrated music, are central to the world of Morbid. To overcome these obstacles you must master the combat, as well as improve your character and gear through a wealth of elements such as Quests, Perks, Runes, Upgrades, and Looting. Explore the diverse fantasy world of Mornia abundant with deep and immersive lore. The Gahars have bound their twisted minds to the flesh of the Seven Acolytes, for without hosts they cannot survive. You must slay the Acolytes, thus ridding the Gahars of their flesh. Succeed, and you'll free the kingdom from the heavy yoke of their terror. Fail, and the malicious gods rule on, as the Acolytes rise anew, and madness prevails. Features Overview -Experience epic, brutal boss encounters and explore a diverse array of environments -Perk levelling system with multiple ways to build your character -Deep, immersive lore with NPC's to meet throughout the world -Over 25 Unique Melee Weapons, such as Swords, Axes, Maces, Spears, Two-Handers, as well several guns ranging from Pistols, Shotguns and Rifles -Epic fully orchestrated soundtrack comprising of 18 tracks -Health, Stamina and Sanity management is important as you traverse the world If you're interested in the following games, Morbid: The Seven Acolytes is for you: -Bloodborne -Dark Souls -Dark Souls 2 -Dark Souls 3 -Blasphemous -Demon's Souls -Nioh -Elden Ring -Dead Cells -Titan Souls -Salt And Sanctuary -Hollow Knight -Death's Gambit
short_description: Morbid: The Seven Acolytes is a Horrorpunk Action RPG filled with Lovecraftian horrors and Cronenbergian gore, making it the most gruesome take on the isometric Souls-like genre yet!

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of fun! It's basically a pixel version of Bloodborne. If you enjoy that sort of stuff, you'll enjoy this.First off, great graphics, gameplay, and lore. There is some seriously beautiful pixelart. Some of the best actually. And the music is on point too!As for gameplay, I had a blast. Sometimes the hit boxes seemed a bit weird. Sometimes I'd get hit when I felt like I was more than far enough away. Same goes for me hitting enemies. It wasn't a huge problem, but sometimes it was a bit bothersome.Difficulty. I know I'm probably going to be a pariah when I say this because I've seen people complaining on the forums, but it was a bit too easy for me. I didn't even end up unlocking the "Die 100 times" achievement.  Aside from the last boss (which took me four attempts), I beat most bosses on the first go, and those that I got beat by rarely beat me twice. Which leads me to my next point...The elemental system is confusing and there's just too many elements. It's near impossible to know what elemental exactly works well against what enemy. In Bloodborne (which this game clearly was inspired by... which is fine by me because it's my favorite game!) there was a (relatively) clear system where enemy types belonged to a certain group (Kin, Beasts, etc) and that group was weak against a particular element. Maybe this game could benefit somewhat from a system like this. If the elemental system worked better, the enemies could be tougher under the assumption that the player could just use the right elemental shroom for help. Maybe drop some more hints in the game somewhere. There's a whole bunch of NPCs in the towns that just quote from a random list of phrases. Maybe some of those phrases could give us some clues?This kind of falls in with the previous paragraph, but I wish it had better explained it's various stats. I still don't know what the fist icon means and I beat the game. I understand that the devs tried to do the From Software vagueness-as-a-feature thing, but I don't think it worked here. Vagueness is okay, but it's probably best not to be TOO vague, which is a trap I think this game falls into.I know it looks like I just ripped into this game, but honest to god I had a blast! The problems I just listed, yes they are kind of annoying, but they certainly aren't game breaking issues. Seriously. I say give this one a try! I loved it. Maybe you will too!

_childDocuments_.review: Style over substance. Please don't get fooled by how good this game looks like I did and believe the reviews.  The ONLY positive thing i can say about this game is that the art is really nice which seems to have been the focus. This game suffers from a ton of issues. Both you and the enemy attack hitboxes are bigger than they should be. The enemy AI is completely braindead. Every enemy including bosses have about 2 attacks maybe 3. Boss fights are tedious and unchallenging due to the issues listed above. Exploration isn't rewarding because of many dead ends with nothing in them but enemies.I can't stress enough how much i don't recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game.It has great soundtrack and graphics, and the gloomy ambiance is both extremely well-rendered and declined in a variety of ways. Enemies and bosses look amazing, and the story's interesting, and addresses an adult audience more boldly than most games of this genre.Now the gameplay just isn't satisfying. Even though it may look like it draws a lot of inspiration from Dark Souls, it plays more like a poorly executed Hyper Light Drifter, just with entirely different aesthetics. It's just so slow. It is by design, and I get that the devs wanted the action to look and feel heavy, but even the lightest "builds" (encumberment not being a thing, only the weapon you're using determines how fast you attack) will make you feel like there's massive input lag to every action, and every dodge roll feels like a cry for help.Due to this, just about everything in this game is painstaking, as everything takes a lot of time to die, and zones are vast and swarming with enemies. Not to mention there's a lot of unneeded roaming around, as there are a huge lot of paths that lead to nothing, but you still have to make the effort if you want to find the occasional useful upgrade.Morbid also has an underwhelming content issue. There's a ton of different weapons, but only a handful make sense to use, as the rest are either unreasonably slow, or plain worse, stat-wise. Also, the enemies are numerous, but a majority of them (including a good half of the bosses) just behave and are dealt with in the same way. Land an attack, maybe two, parry/dodge away. Rinse and repeat. This sort of gameplay never felt more like disguised QTEs to me as it did in Morbid. Some NPCs will also give you quests, but will never reward you with anything meaningful.Finally - and it was a big deal to me - there's a lot of missing information, sometimes in critical departments. The game is just way too blurry about how powerful items are, how long buffs last, what the sanity bar is and how it affects gameplay, etc.In a nutshell, I loved looking at it, but hated playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: Had to refund the game, the first impression is quite bad and closing to the 2 hour mark i found that while the art direction is very well made and quite striking, the combat is shallow and uninspired with clunky hit boxes, an infuriatingly slow protagonist and some of the most basic tactics i've seen in a souls-like.If you want a 2d soulslike you'll get far more value from Salt and Sanctuary.

_childDocuments_.review: Morbid is a good game. At first I was wondering why it wasn't so talked about as Hades or Hollow Knight, but after a couple of hours I understood why.First the good:Morbid is very close to what a soulslike would had looked like if it was released as a Sega Saturn pixel art soulslike. The pixel art is astonishing. The enemies design is superb and the game really have that disgraceful atmosphere the genre requires.The combat system has the bases to be a great soulslike game. What separate it from a real soulslike is that the game is not that hard.The bad:The level design left a lot to be desired. All areas of the game look the same, not in terms of visuals, but in terms of what to do. We basically are lost and have to find the way to proceed, with nothing remarkable to differentiate one area from another. The storytelling is soulslike style, but fail to keep things interesting like Hollow Knight does. The combat system though very cool, don't bring much new stuff after a while.Most of the game is very repetitive, often getting to the point of being boring.I enjoyed the game, played until the end. Fighting the Acolytes is very cool, but to lore is not that intriguing although is nice to read their stories.Although I liked the game, I don't see myself getting back to it.

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say about this game. The art is what's going to draw you in. The grotesque world that somehow still has colors, the monstrous creatures, the areas that have thick atmosphere. But then you start playing the game and the problems start to pop up one after the other. The artstyle is beautiful but but everything is cluttered, you don't know where you can pass and where you cannot, The combat is clunky and slow. The stamina bar lets you more or less do 1-2 hits with bigger weapons and maybe 3 hits with smaller weapons before you are winded. The dodge takes up too much time and eats a huge chunk of your stamina. The parry is so unintuitive that it is useless. Sometimes it works sometimes it does not, the window of parry is super short and it actually just deflects one hit, but does not stagger the enemy. Meaning they will continue to beat you up. Ok there is no mini map, but the only way to see where you are is when you are on this game's equivalent of a bonfire...Seriously. And the map is pixelated and unintuitive. The combat is literary hit the enemy ones, dodge their attack, hit the enemy one, dodge their attack, wait for 5-6 sec until your stamina has come back, rinse and repeat. The quests are uninspired fetch or kill quests, the rewards are uninspired as well. The enchantments on the weapons are a hit or miss - some of them do not do anything. I have not seen any benefit from using the lifesteal, poison or fire enchantments, in my opinion they either do nothing and are bugged or are useless.  I beat a couple of bosses and mini-bosses until I got to the big city, where the enemies are even more spongy and have more or less no animation tells for what they will do. Also their attacks are hard to dodge as they don't indicate their reach in any way. Absolutely a game that had almost no playtesting and was just made hard because "hurr durr darksouls hard git gud play 10000 hours and shut up" Don't waste your time.

_childDocuments_.review: Morbid: The Seven Acolytes is a isometric action game. As the only survivor of Strivers of Dibrom, players need to navigate through the accursed kingdom and battle against the seven Acolytes of Gahars, further freeing this land from the terrifying clutch of this eldritch deity. I have a mixed feeling for this game. On one hand, I really like the artstyle and the designs of each mob. The eerie, creeping, bodily-horror always seizes my eyes, and the sense of dread emanating from mere pixel sprites invariably tantalizes my taste for this kind of pixel art. Yet, on the other hand, the level design is quite weak, falling short of depth and the incentive to explore. The combat is sabotaged by enemies' easily-exploited movesets, inaccurate hit boxes, and some questionable design choices. Still, Morbid: The Seven Acolytes manages to deliver an decent, albeit flawed, experience for lovecraftian horror action game.The game presents a fantastic artstyle in both levels and enemies. The bodily horror of each enemy design, or as the developers stated: "Cronenbergian" horror, is disturbingly terrifying and yet eerily mesmerizing at the same time. It pushes the limit of your sanity. Every encounter is a testament to the reality you think you know, as well as the visual presentation of how further the cruelty of this malevolent deity could go. The aesthetic of the level is also something worth experiencing. From the dreaded beach where corpses, ship wrecks, and unspeakable beings washed ashore, to the garden filled with unknown plantation and monsters lurking between the grass; from the seemingly civilized steam punk city only teeming with eldritch horror from the inside, to the strange woods in which inhumanity experiments are conducted wildly and unsightly, for the screams never leave between these leaves.Other than the impactfull aesthetic, bosses in Morbid: The Seven Acolytes provide moderate challenge and some with tragic but charming lore. In general, all the bosses possess limited moveset and no noticeable changes when health drops to certain degree. Some may deem this easy, and for a time I do have this kind of thought. However in retrospect, I find this design fair and square. In my opinion, the agility of any mobs should be designed around that of the playable character. The developer seems to have the same philosophy and creates these bosses with predictable but still manageable movesets Nothing ridiculous, Nothing unbearable(maybe Yaga Moer has too much going on, too much blood splatter may cover up the ground spike attack.)In Morbid: The Seven Acolytes, weapons have no superiority over others, for each of them has its own advantages and disadvantages. This feature can avoid situation such as players enjoy A weapon but forced to use B weapon later on because B outshines A in any way possible. Players can use whatever they want and upgrade it with runes. Simple and solid. While I do find myself adoring this feature, I somehow feel no sense of progression about this system. Most the action RPGs implement weapon level upgrade system for the sake of empowering characters, and to a degree progression mark. Upgrading a weapon to max level not only shows players' dedication to that weapon, but also fulfills the sense of progressing through harder levels. This is the feeling Morbid: The Seven Acolytes currently lacking for me. I really enjoy using the poison claw, but the limited upgrade system cannot drastically improve the game play.One of the fatal flaws of this game. The level design is just mediocre at best, unrewarding at worst. To put it simply, every level is merely "run a long way around, find the short cut, pop the pox, and fight the Boss." This design may work fine for the first few levels, but when stretching to the whole game, it really feels like a chore rather than a adventure. The devs do try to encourage players to explore some narrow path to find various upgrades, which players only need to simply find and turn at the right corner. The game needs to put some work in offering the incentive, igniting the spark of wanting to explore this part of the map, either through clues or some side quests. Then rewards those who are observant enough to see through the clues.The wave-based attacks (crow's screech, sperm of Gahar's sanity attack, automaton's stomp, etc.) have the most deceiving hitboxes. The actual hit box is bigger than the animation suggests. This is annoying because you cannot reliably judge enemies attack and solely maneuver the character to where the attack will exactly end, forcing you to either dodge or take the hit. In some case this situation really throw my pace off. Take the automatons in Yortael for example. They have the ability to shoot several fire balls when the player is far away. Most of the time you've better stay near them since their melee attacks are more manageable. Here comes the stomp. If the shock wave depicts exactly as it presents, I would stay within automatons' melee range. But for the deceiving nature of the attack, I am forced to dodge away and face the more annoying fire ball attacks.Most of the enemies are really helpless when you stay on top or below them. Their already-limited attack do not do them justice. You can basically and literally sit on their heads and watch as they vainly attacking the air. Fortunately some bosses and elites are spared from this fate due to their wider attack range.

_childDocuments_.review: I had this on my wishlist for a long time and finally bought it despite mixed/low reviews and although i don't regret finally getting it i wouldnt recommend it. The music and the visuals are good. I like the enemy variety and the bosses i did fight were just fine. The sanity mechanic was a bit confusing but then really annoying when you don't have an easy way to heal it outside of very limited resources. The weapons confused me as I would have two swords where either one shows as slightly stronger but does massively more damage, or one shows as way stronger but is barely any better. It feels like either the numbers are wrong or there is some back end mechanic for damage that we are not made aware of. This is also not taking weapon buffs in to account. The game does have a very satisfying parry system that it underplays the importance of. I felt like i was grinding against a wall until i figured out that most enemies need to be felled with parries or they take forever to go down. The biggest reason i stopped playing though is the lack of a map. Each area looks distinct enough from one another but each area is also a horrid maze of samey looking textures so its hard to tell where you are and where you are going. The rest points have a map but it doesnt say where you are so its basically useless. This issue gets compounded when you die to a boss then have to remember the pathway through the maze back to the boss. The simple addition of a map on your pause screen or something would elevate this game so much, for me at least.

_childDocuments_.review: It is not fun. The combat is uninspiring, all melee weapons I've seen have samey attacks. You left click once then left click again. Some of them attack slower than others, but it is all the same attack. The enemies are not interesting, you hit -> roll away -> hit -> roll away, it is incredibly boring. The loot does not make sense, you're given these runes to slot into your weapon very early on. However there are no ways of taking them out. You can only destroy all of them. Which means there should be no reason for the lesser runes to exist since you will want to fit the best runes in, it is not like a big fire attack rune takes more space than the small fire attack rune. The level design is bland, it is seperated by zones and each zone are scattered with not important loot and some linear pathways. I only fought one boss, and it has three attacks in total, THREE.

_childDocuments_.review: Morbid: The Seven Acolytes is a challenging game which generally incorporates both the good and annoying elements of a Souls-like experience. Still, it manages to stand out thanks to its strong dark fantasy presentation, rich Lovecraftian lore, and gameplay systems that offer methodical combat and plenty of features to make the adventure satisfying. It’s a difficult game, for sure, but it doesn’t forego quality-of-life features for the sake of being difficult, and so in this sense, many players outside of the Souls fandom can get something out of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Morbid: The Seven Acolytes is a top-down slasher with a world reminiscent of Nightmare Creature/Bloodborne, etc.TL;DR - I would definitely recommend AGAINST it. Enemies are laughably exploitable. Many walk towards you at a casual pace and can be struck down before they get to enter their offensive range. Their sprites only face left and right, and unfortunately that’s the direction most of their attacks travel in. Simply attacking from the north or south makes most of them a formality. They at least make up for it by hitting hard when they do land shots.Fortunately the devs implemented a parry system in a somewhat smart attempt at getting you to stand in the line of fire of these easily evaded strikes.With the correct timing this can boost the damage of your following strike up 500%, but the window for getting this ‘perfect’ parry is really thin. Most of the time you’ll get a normal parry (a decently sized window), but this only offers damage negation and rewards you with a few i-frames behind it to start up your attack. There’s no damage buff from this kind of parry and you’ll get it about 60-80% of the time, so you may as well exploit the enemies by abusing the aforementioned blind spots.Early on, the game introduces a crouch walk mechanic for stealth business, but most enemies don’t have a large aggro range. It seems every bad guy is deaf as you can simply run right up behind them, spin around and execute your heavy attack while they remain completely oblivious.Somewhere after the 2nd Acolyte, every other boss seems to become a tank. Fortunately this is where the items and upgrade system come in. The game sprinkles a handful of Blessings throughout the world, tiny breakable statues found not too far off the beaten path. These let you spend your skill points and buffs like taking less damage and doing more damage against bosses. The real difference maker though is an item called Limb (literally a severed leg), which buffs your melee for FIVE WHOLE SECONDS in return for making you lose all sanity. Combined with Broccoli (infinite stamina) and another one that gives you increased attack speed, then bosses encounters become DPS battles as you face-tank all their offence. This pretty much outright exposes the 'Sanity' mechanic as being nothing to be concerned about, despite the item description making it sound like a big negative for over-buffing.Low sanity results in 'spectres' appearing in the world, purple versions of the regular enemies, just as easily dispatched. The spectres appear seldomly so it’s not even like you get overwhelmed by excessive numbers of enemies. Spectres don't even spawn in bosses arenas, so you may as well over-buff and throw your sanity out the window. You've got nothing to be scared about.There’s many other items in the game, your typical status effects (Poison, bleed, ice, fire, etc.), but you can never tell if these are having any effect. There’s no additional sound effects, hit sparks remain the same, no symbols added above the enemy health bar or change in colour. I don’t even *feel* like I’m doing noticeably more damage. These supposed buffs are borderline placebos, yet they make up roughly 75% of what you pick-up throughout a playthrough.There's a handful of side-quests, where you return to an NPC (if you recall where they were with no markers) with the head of a mini-boss or other quest item found just lying around. Unfortunately their rewards are a handful of non-unique items you've likely accumulated dozens of already.Around the map you’ll encounter flesh gates, designed to prevent you from running direct to your goals. The switches to bring these down can either be: A writhing lump of bloody meat or A vanilla enemy with nothing to signify they’re in control of the gate.To add to the confusion these switches can sometimes be found several screens away from the flesh gates they bring down.They may also only bring down one of the gates in a region with many. So there's backtracking past multiple gates just to figure out which one it brought down.The Final Acolyte is the only boss with more than one life bar, but he's also slow AF, so guns  (the game has them btw) finally became useful. The ammo surplus I’d built up throughout the playthrough kept me fully stocked for two health bars of zoning and climaxing with some comfy face-tanking.The lore is that some otherworldly force called The Gahars came down and wanted to take over/enslave/etc. and seven people sold out humanity and became…The Acolytes(!), so you'd think you eliminate the seven traitors and THEN face The Gahars, but you just beat the Seventh Acolyte in the cathedral....and that's it. Fade to white. Roll Credits. The world/story/art are fairly cool and I'd give a sequel a shot if they ever get there, but Morbid:TSA is unbalanced and AI has huge exploits.

_childDocuments_.review: Morbid: The Seven Acolytes isn't a bad game nor is it a great game.If there was a mixed review option on steam, I'd give it that but, here's the run down of it:CombatWeapons in this game are usually quite fun to use, some examples being the Spear of Mornia, Mechafists and the Sane's Bane - these were all weapons that were quite fun. I can't comment on the rest of the weapons as in comparison to these (except the Spear of Mornia, which also sucked), all the other weapons were really just kinda... trash. The game provided no incentive to use other weapons (except maybe in the case of Sane's Bane reducing your sanity on kill - but even then, just using a grand rune of terror negates it fully). The weapons are fun but not well-balanced.The combat is simple but is still quite fun. You have 5 distinct options: Normal attack, heavy attack, roll, ranged and parry. It all basically is what it says on the tin, you can click M1 once for a normal attack, hold it for a heavy, yadda yadda. And this isn't to say it's *bad* - personally, I am a big lover of the Souls franchise so this was completely okay with me. It did not give the freedom to truly use ranged weaponry (due to it being quite weak) but overall I rarely had any issues with the combatThe consumables the game has to offer aren't plentiful - your generic run of the mill "Increase HP", "Increase Sanity", "Buff weapon with X" sort of happenings which is fine. You have consumables outside of that but I never really saw much reason to use any of them - with exceptions being made for cases like the Lazarus Flower which were incredibly useful, healing all sanity, lots of HP and removing any debuffsWhich on the topic of - there's debuffs in this game? I never once encountered them and that's after having 100%'ed the game. And that applies to your character, too, I didn't really ever observe much being done in terms of having elemental effects added to your weapon.DesignThis is one of the few things I don't really have anything bad to say about - the art style of this game is really nice. Each area feels completely unique, when you look at an area for example on a youtube video after playing it yourself, you can tell immediately what area is what. The art really helps instil the atmosphere and an amazing well done to the artist on the team.Inventory management in this game is honestly horrible. You have quite a small inventory, which is fine - it incentives you to commonly head to a shrine in order to deposit your findings. What I *did* take issue with though is the fact that you have extremely limited space even in your stash, limiting just how many weapons you could even keep hold of. Granted, as I said before, it's not that big of a deal as none of them are really useful but still - kinda of a weird thingThe level design in this game is quite... poor. The actual design of the levels? Incredible - from a factory city to a bogged down mad scientist's swamp - absolutely loved it. But actually traversing these levels was frustrating at best usually. Rarely ever any indicators and the "map" was so poor that it might as well not even be in the game.Enemies and boss designs in general though were really good. The fights were clean and fun, and any new encounter typically gave you a chance to study it before it murderised you or you murderised it - enemy encounters and bosses done right, honestly. Some bosses were tied to quests, and in fact, a lot of the quests are quite boring but overall - it was still good.All in all, is this game worth 20 quid? No. Maybe about 15? I wouldn't pay 20 quid for this, though. I would recommend getting it on sale, it's definitely a good time to spend quite a few hours on - and I do look forward to seeing what the company next produces. They have talent, just need to hone it.

_childDocuments_.review: Except the art style, the rest are plain.Morbid: The Seven Acolytes is a rogue-like game with little story. There are quests but described in the most simple way, you don't need to finish to proceed - so they are not important, and most NPCs give the same one line answer, it looks like devs put every effort into developing monsters and world design. Each map has 2-3 exits connected to the next map, player can roam freely but eventually has to find this connection, and This could be difficult as the only way to access the map is to visit one of the shrines. Once leaving, player is on their own so best to remember the direction of places. The monsters look good and they vary in different forms, fit in different maps - swamp, tomb, garden, mechanical city... but most attack in the same way, just like the player does. Besides, all the weapons and equipment feel exactly the same, player need to stash well to make space for new items. I avoid most of the regular monsters to save time, the essential boss fight is kinda challenging and they have special attacks, but not that unbeatable even though my level is significantly lower. I enjoy the game pauses to let the player give a final hit.The world is worth seeing, but without the map I run into dead ends many times, finding the right path is not fun. There are secrets and treasure boxes and blessings but none really worth the detour. In addition, player need to kill certain bosses in order to enter certain areas, the game should give better instruction on that, let alone those red flowers blocking the way were confusing. The game ends as soon as the last boss is slayed, which feels too sudden.Overall an okay game for me, I only recommend those who also enjoy this art style.

_childDocuments_.review: This an ok souls like game with a lot of bad design choices. -They made a map but can only be accessed through the bonfire (chair at this game). You can't use it running around, the map doesn't even tell you where you are.-Some enemies have wonky hitbox.-Getting skill points for upgrading blessings is a chore you have no clue how much you need for next points. So I end up not really upgrading any blessing to its full, some I can't even upgrade at all.-Elemental Runes sees to have no effect at all to the point its useless. Just use attack speed rune in weapons and I think Sane's bane sword is the best in the game. -Fast travel is only on selected chairs not all chairs, bad design-Keybind options is not even complete-Parry and shooting is on same RMB why not separate them? Mouse and Keyboard are not running out of keys to bind-The game has bestiary but still only accessed in the chair and still doesn't provide any info what monster is weak to what element so that feature is outright useless.-Side quests are useless, The rewards you get are the same things you get  while exploring, pathetic design.-The final area is just throwing dozens upon dozens of enemies at you to say "Oh this area is the hardest".-That Toad boss is the hardest and most annoying one it just spams aoe, tongue attack and summons all at once at you in a small area giving almost no breathing room and you stamina is slow to regen in this game. I only manage to beat it by spamming my healing and stamina consumables and just tank everything till it dies. It's even more annoying than the final boss which does the same but you have a big arena to run around and it has 3 life bars and the toad only has one.-On NG+ your healing potion resets to 0 so you have to find the again. Bad designThere is still some enjoyment to be had in this game. Just be wary of its flaws.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for November 2022, this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before December 6th, 2022, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.A Pixel-art Souls-like.Another attempt at the popular formula, Morbid: The Seven Acolytes goes with a more stylized look, but a recognizable combat system.  Morbid has a heavy focus on parries and stamina management rather than dodges, making it similar to Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice.   There are also only minor penalties when players die and an absence of corpse runs to regain lost items which reward more experimentation. Morbid: The Seven Acolytes can feel great when the player nails the system, but frustrating when the player runs out of stamina without realizing it.  Parries are so essential that it’s hard to overstate that, but the difficulty here is pretty reasonable.   However, the early enemies were not as impressive, and I hope to see more variety after the first Acolyte, at least I hope so. Pick this up if you like Souls-like games, and enjoy these graphics, the game is very bloody, but in this pixelated style.  Still, this is a pretty interesting take on the formula and I look forward to seeing even more. If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: The first few hours are fun, but once the areas get bigger and more confusing - it becomes frustrating. Every time you leave the area - all enemies respawn... made a wrong turn and exited the area? Well, good luck in chopping the same hordes of enemies once again. In later areas many monsters are just annoying to deal with. The game itself is really not that hard, but insanely methodical. Dodge-hit-dodge-hit-dodge-hit-wait for stamina to refill-hit-dodge-hit...Most weapons feel the same and unless you invest those very rare attack speed runes - all of them are just very slow. The more you progress into the game, the slower most new weapons get. The whole experience is frustrating. At least it was for me.Most areas are really hard to navigate, lots of dead ends. You can only see a map at the shrine and it doesn't even show your current location anyway ^^. Useless.Game looks good and responsive enough, but it's janky and needs polishing.

_childDocuments_.review: Is it a masterpiece? Yes, if you enjoy isometric pixel art and challenging combat. Fans of soulslike action RPGs get new food.The backstory of the game is dark and depressing. At the beginning, our main character wakes up on a beach, full of horribly mutated fish and half-rotten corpses. It looks as if we were on board a ship that smashed on the cliffs and the surf washed us up. Luckily there is a sword next to the dead body next to us. We are a warrior, the last survivor of the Order of the Strivers of Dibrom. Our task, for which we have trained all our lives, is to defeat the Seven Acolytes, cursed and powerful beings possessed by evil deities called Gahars. We must kill the acolytes and thus save the kingdom. If we fail, the evil gods will continue to rule and madness will devour the entire world. More information will not be revealed at first. If you want to know more, you have to examine the items you find and talk to the few (more or less) sane people you meet on the adventure. The graphics also provide clues as to what has happened in this desolate world.The world of Mornia is dark and oppressive, with aggressive, disfigured creatures that were once human or animal. Under the rule of the Seven Acolytes, Mornia has completely decayed, only fanatical followers of the acolytes have the right to live. Everywhere disgusting plants grow, which when destroyed release flying creatures that attack us immediately. Even some disfigured creatures have these annoying flying parasites inside them, which are easy to overlook after killing their host. Fortunately they do not endure much, a short blow with the sword is enough to kill them. In addition to our task of defeating the Seven Acolytes, we also receive a few secondary tasks from the inhabitants of the country. When we complete these, we usually receive a reward, be it information or a useful object. Most levels are small labyrinths in which certain paths are blocked by rampant plants that retreat when their roots are destroyed. A cursed fishing village, rotten swamps or dead forests, each with their own types of enemies, await us on our adventure to destroy the Seven Acolytes.Our character is predetermined, there are no adjustment possibilities at the beginning of the game. We play a nameless female warrior, a well-trained fighting machine. With the melee weapon she can make two attacks, either a fast or a heavy but slower blow, which also requires more stamina. Running is not her favourite discipline, here she quickly runs out of stamina, which however regenerates quickly. To escape from a dangerous situation, she also masters a forward roll, she can block enemy punches with the right timing and then strike all the more brutally herself. With her long-range weapon she can fight enemies at a distance, but the ammunition is rare. She always starts with five shots, which can be refilled with "Krombi's Canisters". She uses two weapons - one for close combat, one for ranged combat. By using runes she improves her weapons. However, the runes are then fused with the weapon - (more or less) permanently. Special mushrooms can also be used to improve a weapon. Our heroine carries weapons and other items around in her inventory, but she can carry a maximum of 10 each for the consumable items. There are no items other than quest-items, consumables (such as tablets, food, runes, mushrooms...) and weapons. Clothing or equipment can neither be found nor improved. By the way, there is no currency or trader either. When the inventory is full, you have to throw away old items. Realistic but hard.Three essential values of our warrior are permanently displayed on the screen in a bar: life energy, endurance and our mental health. The life energy is refreshed during the game with (disgusting) food or our special healer stone, and some weapons suck the life energy of our opponents. The endurance used up while running or fighting automatically increases again, while we can restore our mental health with special medicines. By taking a special petal we become faster for a short time and get more endurance, unfortunately the side effects are also severe: we lose our mind and this eventually leads not only to pink flashes in our eyes but also to the fact that every killed enemy resurrects as an illusion, so that we have to kill it again. So we should think carefully about taking the petal, especially if we have no medicine to restore our mental health.Fighting usually means melee, attack/block/evade and pay attention to your endurance. We can also sneak to stalk enemies from behind. Normally, however, this is not necessary as many opponents stand around motionless until they discover us. We can also approach them from behind at normal speed and kill them without danger. Some enemies stand fixed at one point, but others patrol certain areas until they see us. If they spot us, they usually attack us directly, which also means they run directly into one of our well-timed attacks. Ranged fighters try to keep their distance. In general, contact with enemies does not cause any damage, only their attacks are unpleasant. It takes only a few hits until we have lost all our life energy. The fights can be controlled well as long as we use our attacks with care and dodge enemy blows. Compared to games like Hades, the fight is very sluggish, wild button-mashing does not lead to success. By killing enemies we gain experience points, which we can use at shrines to improve our character. The game contains more than 25 melee weapons with partly very different characteristics - experimenting with them is fun.We can meditate at the shrines scattered throughout the country - in other words, save the game. While we replenish our life energy and ammunition, our mental health remains as it was. All already defeated enemies, including the mini-bosses, are present again after waking up. At the shrines we can also see an overview of open side missions and use the quick travel function. The "Morbid Menagerie", an encyclopaedia of items, enemies, NPCs or information found so far can also be accessed here. We can distribute collected experience in the form of skill points to certain areas to further improve our warrior. With every defeated acolyte we learn new skills to become stronger and stronger during the course of the game, which still does not make the game easy. Already a short inattention, and even the smallest enemy kills us. With the mini-bosses it is enough if we receive 2-3 hits. The magnificently staged boss fights against the acolytes are really challenging then, because they can take a lot of hits, unlike the mini-bosses. Altogether the game is difficult, although not inhumanly difficult. A death has comparatively little effect - we wake up completely healed and rearmed at the last of the numerous save points. All objects found so far are preserved, so we do not have to search for our corpse.The game is playable in a screen resolution of 3440x1440, but the screen is distorted in width. My XBOX 360 and One controllers were recognized without any problems, a control with keyboard and mouse is also possible. Challenging action role playing game in isometric view. Combat is slow paced, miss and you are in trouble. The graphics are drawn in dark pixel style and remind us of classics from days long gone. Exploring the decayed and corrupted world of mutant creatures and fanatical enemies is a lot of fun, and the well-done bosses (the Seven Acolytes) are a source of frustration and a wonderful sense of achievement when you finally defeat them.
