All within the first hour of playing. So this game is also insanely short for the asking price.The diablo style limited inventory system is needlessly cumbersome.Glancing through the other negative reviews, I can say that I agree with most of them, so if you need more reasons not to buy the game just look at what everyone else has said.----------------------------Heres quick list of some other 2d/overhead/isometric actiony games I would strongly recommend over this.-Bastion-CrossCode-Hyper Light Drifter

_childDocuments_.review: So far I'm loving the game. There some valid criticisms in the other reviews, but despite that I'm liking it very much.Visuals are great - beautiful, detailed, stylish. Grand pixel art. Music - surprisingly good, very atmospheric, perfectly fitting.Combat is slow and methodical with a lot of staring and waiting for the right moment, striking and rolling away  and then all over. If you're good enough you can strike, then parry and counter attack.Heavy attacks have a long wind, can be interrupted and when you commit to a direction you're stuck with it but that is what makes them satisfying when you land them properly.Movement is also painfully slow (although a little better after the update) and running costs stamina (although less after the update). But I actually like that. It makes movement part of the challenge and I love that in games. Walking is mostly unfeasible and running is fine, but you have to plan a step ahead so as to not get yourself in an ambush with no stamina.Enemies are beautifully animated and although they each have relatively few attacks, they are of good variety and are well executed. There are the standard variations of quick and slow strikes, charges and various projectiles but there is also a good amount of areal attacks with spikes and corrosive liquids that stick to the ground and change the battlefield dynamics. This plays particularly nice with the top-down perspective.Some enemies deal psychic damage as well as physical that makes you go crazy in a Don't Starve way. The crazier you get the more frequently a phantom rises from the fallen enemies and you have to fight it as well.There's also a sneaking system. On it's own there doesn't seem to be much difference damage wise but it is a nice way to smuggle in some easy heavy hitters. However later you can find a blessing that boosts damage for a stealthy build.Speaking of blessings, the character progression is a little weird. In order to use points from level ups you'll first have to find blessings that you can equip. Each gives a particular benefit, can be upgraded using points and can be freely swapped during rest. But you find the first blessings rather late . It's not a good decision for first impressions but the system is otherwise decent.      The game could use a map or at least a bit better directions to where you need to go for each quest. The gameplay can get a bit repetitive, but if you take it in small portions it's really nice.

_childDocuments_.review: Been trying out lots of souls-likes, but I'm just bouncing off of this one. Great art, fairly good music and sound design, but there are several issues with combat that are making it not enjoyable.Proper spacing when fighting even normal, derpy enemies is so necessary due to how easy your attacks are to interrupt, how little damage you really do without using the charged up attacks, and how enemies don't seem to get stunned even by any of your attacks. Only viable strategy I found was to spam long range stabs with the spear weapon, or to wind up heavy attacks while the enemy was approaching me and then dodge away. I'm not a parry-god, my reactions aren't good enough for that.Absolutely pointless to pull more than one enemy at a time. Very easy to run out of healing items after only a few mistakes, and without your flask you have to rely on the gruel to scrape through to the next check point.The first boss was incredibly difficult due to all of these combined factors, which is generally a staple of these kinds of games, but what made it even worse was his propensity to use a little backward shuffle to punish me for the audacity of trying to get behind or dodge through him while avoiding his high damage frontal attacks. This moves does damage and interrupts any attack I was attempting to use. Also, apparently enemy *hitboxes* do damage to you, so if you mess up the dodge or the boss simply walks into you (combined with the fact that getting hit stuns you), you simply get to lose half of your hp bar. The boss is 10 times my size and we're fighting on a narrow bridge.His hp pool was also insultingly high. Heavy weapons barely scratched him, so using light weapons was a complete waste. Large portions of the fight were spent simply walking away from the boss to try and regenerate stamina because of how often I had to dodge. Took about 10 tries to beat, and the final attempt was about 6 or 7 minutes long.Generally, the first boss in a souls game is where I'll learn whether or not I'll enjoy the rest of the game. It's possible that the rest of the boss fights are *not* like him, but I already was not enjoying combat that much to want to slog through more of it to find out.

_childDocuments_.review: Because I loved the art design so much I threw $5 at the dev team and picked it up on ps5 where I finally completed the game. It's frustrating to me because what fantastic looking art and great character / monster designs dragged down with over ambitious poorly executed gameplay. Progression is horribly paced where weapons will be immediately worthless not 2 minutes after obtaining them or sometimes totally inferior to items you already have. There is a small nuance of weapon variety but honestly until the very very VERY end of the game (literally the final Boss) all you care about is Damage and weapon Reach. Ranged weapons are far more simplistic, Damage. Thats it. The upgrade system is a bad gem / rune socket style deal, done poorly because to remove runes you have to destroy them all AND it requires a consumable item to do so. Since progression is so fast you only care about the top end runes or maybe the second highest. If you can nab it on a sub $10 sale and enjoy the art style enough you can have some fun. Its about a 3-6 hour game depending. With all the issues I have with gameplay and the short length the full price is exceedingly high in my opinion-original review here-Original pea soup and gray GAMEBOY games have better mechanics and more satisfying gameplay. This is pathetic and I'm sad I bought an unrefundable copy. Enemies cant rotate. Why does this matter? Imagine someone made a Zelda game where plenty of enemies cant attack you if you approach them from the top or bottom of the sprite. Oh look the Morbid dev team did! You CAN be an idiot and attack left to right if you want...I guess? And a few enemies have complete AoE attacks or just do ramming attacks for collision damage. But even IF the combat can threaten you heres the constant loopAttack once. Dodge Away. Attack once. Dodge Away. Wait for Stamina. Repeat forever and ever. Oh sure you can chain attacks for like, three swings I think? But enemies dont flinch or stun from what I can tell so far so its a death wish to stand and trade hits. You get mediocre ranged attacks. You get alternate Heavy/special attacks that are so slow they are worthless. And maybe you even get mediocre Magic (I dont know for certain yet) but I can imagine it will be as dismally effective as anything else. Super slow movement for player and enemies, stack on some janky detection, and you have a big serving of "Eh. Meh. Whatever" Except... well this game is pretty stylish. _childDocuments_.review: Morbid: The Seven Acolytes is a top down perspective souls-like game. It takes inspiration from Lovecraftian horrors and Cronengergian gore. It’s very atmospheric, the graphics are dark but easy on the eyes. Though it’s tagged as a souls-like the loot system and character progression is widely different and it’s one of the best parts about the game. Check out my full gameplay review video for Morbid: The Seven Acolytes. I go into great depth about the Story, Graphics, Audio, Gameplay, and other noteworthy things I feel needs to be mentioned:  Disclaimer: I received this game for free. I was not paid to promote or write a review. All thoughts are solely my own. Thanks!The story starts off scarce and throws you right into the action. You start off waking up on a beach and there’s monsters in every direction you face. You loot a bunch of your friend’s bodies and fight your way across to safety.There are NPCs scattered throughout the world that provide hints and small amounts of lore, but to truly learn about why these monsters exist and why your character is fighting them, you need to find lore books and read the small excerpts on your own.To summarize, you are a Striver, you have been trained since birth to fight against the evil that has taken over this world. These monsters are called Gahars and they maniphest from the dark sanity that resides in individuals. They’ve taken physical form over time and even persuaded the strongest humans to vessel their power and they’re the ones known as the Seven Acolytes which are the main bosses in the game that you’re hunting.The atmosphere and pacing most definitely feels like a souls game. You’ll be conquering many different large levels and it’s all connected in an open world format to explore.Your character has many different actions to perform. There’s fast attacks, strong attacks, rolling, sneaking, firing your secondary weapon, and using consumables. Items can be found by looting them off the ground, destroying the environment like crates, and defeating enemies and bosses.I mentioned that loot-system and character progression is a bit different than souls games so let’s talk about that next. To level up you simply beat down enemies until you hit a level threshold; after that you’ll have banked a skill point that you use to improve perks that you’ve collected while exploring.You don’t start off with any skills, instead you find them and can equip only a couple at a time. For example you can have 1 perk that increases your health and another that speeds up your stamina regen. Weapons, consumables, and upgrade runes are plentiful, drop constantly and are found all over the world. Each weapon has their speed stat as well as damage and move sets depending on weapon type. Upgrade runes can be inserted on any primary or secondary weapon you find. You can mix and match perks, elements, and they can be removed at any time using a special consumable you find.There are NPCs scattered all around in these areas and while some are just flavor text heavy there’s quite a bit of quests that can be accepted and reward you with various goods like weapons and runes.The graphics are what really drew me into Morbid: The Seven Acolytes at first, it’s charming, fun to look at, and reminds of the Super Nintendo 16-bit era. Enemy designs are gross and bosses are gorgeously morbid. The sound design is surprisingly good. It has that sort of soundtrack that you’d hear during Dark Souls games, you know that sort of chorus-y like epicness that induces stress and ramps up when needed.I definitely recommend Morbid: The Seven Acolytes. There’s a lot of content here and though there are a few bugs I’ve encountered like demon walls reappearing and exploding after getting rid of them there’s nothing that’s game breaking I’ve come across and the small things can be ironed out in patches. Check this one out, it’s pretty good.

_childDocuments_.review: Whenever I play a 2D souls-like the mechanics tend to get lost in adaptation, and while it's easy to nitpick this game, it has a good foundation to improve. You can finish the main story in about 7 hours, I was enjoying it for the first 3 or so, but it went downhill from there because the developers didn't balance the mid-late content, including most of the bosses. I could give more than a few examples, but for now, I'll just say that final boss took me 30 seconds to brute force, on the first attempt (any decent weapon + 1 charge of sanity debuff will melt anything). To me a 'souls-like' genre is all about those combat nuances - looking at the enemy, anticipating the attack, and acting accordingly; this game does the methodically paced combat well at first, it just does not stay that way. I found myself not using the block for 90% of the game, mainly because it's not rewarding and most of the regular enemies can attack very rapidly after you blocked the attack. Even if you do manage to block consistently, usually you have enough time to hit once, maybe twice, so you might as well poke and roll because it's safer than anticipating those attack frames. The traditional soul's currency has been replaced with the experience-based system which makes the game less punishing, although I am not sure if that is a good thing. Whenever you get a level-up you also get a skill point which can be used to upgrade one of the perk cards. After the first boss, you will have 2 available slots and 3 different bonuses to choose from, but you will unlock more as you explore the world and kill bosses. More than any technical and balancing problem in the game, I found that I was not enjoying the character progression because you don't get to make any unique builds. Now there are weapons with on-hit effect and some attack faster than others, but generally speaking, you work with what the game gives you, it's not the same as building a warrior or a mage. Even though the game has many runes and consumables, the only one that stands out to me is the attack speed modifier (which is sad), it's the only one that makes the combat more fun. All of the perks are passive bonuses so they don't push the gameplay in unique directions.There is a decent variety of melee and ranged weapons, although I did not notice any stat randomization, if it had some it was very marginal. I would recommend adding a generous range for each weapon because I got tired of you giving me 10 copies of each. If you going to recycle low-tier gear in the late game, give it higher stats too, right? I will say one positive thing about the loot system, many hidden areas give fun weapons so it's worth looking for them. When it comes to elemental modifiers, I am not sure how the game expects me to know if enemies have some resistance or not. I guess I should mention that game has a sanity system which is kind of a cool concept for a Lovecraftian world, it affects your stats and the spawning of certain enemies (I think). At the time of this review, I don't think that you can change between weapon slots on the controller, not unless you have the inventory open - kinda sucks because I want to switch between heavy and light weapons. Better yet, the devs should implement a system where 2 different weapons can cycle between attacks with buffed frames.The navigation and the side quests were a bit confusing. The only way to check on the quest is to be at the shrine, and even if you read the notes, the game does not have the names over the characters so you can easily forget who gave the quest. When the quest is completed, it should put a yellow aura over the character. I managed to play through the game just fine, but I would say there were at least 3 instances where the progression was not self-explanatory.+ decent variety of weapons that are hidden around the world+ I find the attacks satisfying, the heavy weapons kill in 1-3 hits with upgrades, as they should+ shrines work as waypoints, upgrade hubs and lore libraries + animation is pretty good+ some side quests and achievements  - I think most people would agree with me that we need a way to store items outside of the inventory. You also can't switch between loadouts unless the inventory is open. Furthermore, I think you can do something cool with multiple weapons, for example if you cycle between 2 weapons, the following attack could have higher frames. - you may need to nerf that item that gives damage at the cost of sanity, and increase boss hp. I killed the last boss  under a minute on the first attempt, it removes all of the fun from the fights and completely ruined the game for me because of it. Even without the item, the health is a bit low. It does not need to be a lot higher, just not 2-3 hits per enemy, maybe 10 to 20% for regular enemies and bosses depending on how far you are in the game.  - again I didn't notice much in terms of stat randomization. If it's in the game it was not noticeable enough. It would be much better if all items had better range in stats so you have a reason to compare identical items. Even better, give them a chance to roll some additional modifiers additionally to those rune slots.  - put the names of the characters next to the dialogue. If you completed the quest, highlight the quest giver. - why are they just boring passives that don't encourage any unique gameplay builds. Add something that changes how you play, some synergy, I don't know, not flat stats over and over. - the window for attacking after a block is very short, I am not even sure if it has a window, it looks like the enemy just cycling through normal patterns so you get hit a lot for blocking. Stun the enemy for extra 0.5 seconds or something, I mean honestly, blocking is pretty risky in this game.  - most of them kinda suck to be honest, as in getting hit by invisible blocks. The toad and the witch boss are complete clusterfaq in general.It may seem like I crap all over the game but I genuinely think it could be a lot better with some polish. I hate to blame 'balancing' because it's not something that is easy to objectively explain until you feel it yourself, it's just that this game is really not designed to be challenging for 7 hours. Make the progression in items a bit more engaging with random stats, and perhaps buff the difficulty a little. My biggest problem overall is just the lack of unique character builds, your blessings don't provide any fun strategies.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving this a positive review with a few caveats, with my limited play time I may update my review with more experience. A large flaw to how this game is built is due to limitations of the enemy sprites and animations. You as a player have animations for, and can attack in, 8 directions.Enemies cannot. They only have animations for left/right directions. I can sympathize the reasons why with the level of detail in this game. Making assets look this good is HARD. Making 8 different animations for each enemy object is.... well soul crushing, especially at this quality.In that respect, if you do not line up with the enemies 'attack window' they will need to orient, and it is very easy to exploit attack from directly above or below, since the enemy cannot attack back until they are on the same Y Axis space. Often times I see enemies think your hit box is the wrong way and will attack away from you.Large sweeping attacks and projectiles mitigate this issue somewhat, but for the early melee it is very apparent.Combat AI and detection is a mess, some due to bugs, others due to the limitations their assets place upon the framework in general. Enemy's also need to have more varied attack cool downs, there is very little window to counter attack and enemies seem to attack on a fixed timer with the only other things taken into account are if you are in range, and maybe if you are above or below the enemy.Outside of implementing 8 direction capable enemies, I can't see many of these issues being realistically resolved, though a larger window to punish an enemy after evading would help some.The art and theme is great and you can tell they spent and lot of time and effort polishing in that respect.I consider it worth the asking price, with a bit of a warning given in the mix.

_childDocuments_.review: This was short, and you can tell because it took me 16 hours to beat the game. In my opinion, any game that is basically less than 25 hours, is a short game. However, the better question is, did I enjoy this short game? All I can say, after beating the game, is that it's a very, below average game. Here are the reasons why I say that:-What was the point of guns? No, I'm serious, I played most of the game barely using my guns. Not only do they do very little damage, the ammo is very limited, and you can't buy anything in the game.-The combat is annoying, since you can't really stand up against the enemies face-to-face. They either hit faster than you, or have attacks that you can't block. Speaking of blocking, you can't block, but you can parry, and if you do a perfect parry, you can do a counter that does massive damage. The problem is, getting that perfect parry is super confusing, it doesn't say if you can get it if you parry before the attack lands, or exactly when it lands on you. The best defense that your character has is either running away, or rolling, and it is amazing that they got a good rolling system. Also, you can't stun them with your attacks, meaning that they can hit you, even if you hit them first.-The story is okay, I think. I mean, the main thing about it is the action, so the story isn't really that impressive. To make it short, evil gods corrupted and gave power to some minions, you're the last of an order who swore to kill them, and you go around killing them. That's it, there is lore in the game, but that's about it.-The music is mostly meh, I didn't really pay attention to it, so I don't have much to say about it.-Graphics are good for a pixel art game, and very gory. So, good points on that.Overall, I can't recommend this game in good faith. If you're a fan of Soul-like games, then you can give this one a try, but it might be better if is on discount.

_childDocuments_.review: Same as SaintNot, I'm just gonna quote because... Well... Lazy. Just played the game 45 mins and I already see all this problems. That's a shame because the art is gorgeous ...```What can I say about this game. The art is what's going to draw you in. The grotesque world that somehow still has colors, the monstrous creatures, the areas that have thick atmosphere. But then you start playing the game and the problems start to pop up one after the other. The artstyle is beautiful but but everything is cluttered, you don't know where you can pass and where you cannot, The combat is clunky and slow. The dodge takes up too much time and eats a huge chunk of your stamina. The parry is so unintuitive that it is useless. Sometimes it works sometimes it does not, the window of parry is super short and it actually just deflects one hit, but does not stagger the enemy. Meaning they will continue to beat you up. Ok there is no mini map, but the only way to see where you are is when you are on this game's equivalent of a bonfire...Seriously. And the map is pixelated and unintuitive. The combat is literary hit the enemy ones, dodge their attack, hit the enemy one, dodge their attack, wait for 5-6 sec until your stamina has come back, rinse and repeat. The quests are uninspired fetch or kill quests, the rewards are uninspired as well. The enchantments on the weapons are a hit or miss - some of them do not do anything. I have not seen any benefit from using the lifesteal, poison or fire enchantments, in my opinion they either do nothing and are bugged or are useless. I beat a couple of bosses and mini-bosses until I got to the big city, where the enemies are even more spongy and have more or less no animation tells for what they will do. Also their attacks are hard to dodge as they don't indicate their reach in any way. Absolutely a game that had almost no playtesting and was just made hard because "hurr durr darksouls hard git gud play 10000 hours and shut up" Don't waste your time.```

_childDocuments_.review: Morbid: The Seven Acolytes is a console ported 2D retro pixel top down twin stick brawler "Action RPG" with the "soulslike" moniker.  "Soulslike" is a codeword to let you know the developers found a cheat code for game dev easymode... basically if you make a game punishingly difficult you don't need to bother making as much content because gamers have to repeat the same fights over and over again.  Gamedev problems require gamedev solutions.  Sigh.  Anyway this retro pixel crapfest has the key selling point that it's dark... which basically means this is gory looking like Diablo 3, but has worse graphics, worse gameplay, and less content.  And a higher price tag.From a technical perspective, the game doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.A choice was made to use obsolete, decades old retro pixel "art" as a substitute for contemporary PC graphics.  It's unclear if this is due to lack of budget or talent, regardless, the overall visual quality of the game is extremely low as a result.While there are options to change the resolution for the game, all this does is scale up the simplistic 2D art assets used to make the game, which makes little or no difference to the graphics quality.  Without any other substantial graphics tweaks, it's not possible for gamers to improve the lacklustre 2D visuals.Because this is a console game, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the inferior console gaming appliances that the game was designed for.  These are unfortunate compromises and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was a second thought for the console-centric developers.  The game is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for consoles forces upon a game.  Once more, console peasants have made gaming worse for everyone.Some of the defects in the game can be attributed to the choice of using the GameMaker Studio construction kit/toolset.  This is a very poor quality toolset favoured by amateur developers as it's cheap and requires little in the way of development skill, but unfortunately has very limited capabilities.  Just as you can't make a silk purse out of a sows ear, you can't make a great video game if you use a terrible engine.  GameMaker Studio is often used to make retro pixel shovelware and cash grabs.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.Morbid: The Seven Acolytes has the ridiculous, laughable price of $25 USD (for a crap pixel game), for which you could easily get any number of AAA games, let alone the sheer number of free games available on Steam.  For context, these guys are seriously charging more money for this console ported pixelcrap than you could get Dark Souls, Diablo 3 or The Witcher 3 for.  Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm leaning to yes, but I wish I could give it a mixed review. I see the art direction, the aesthetic, and it's all very appealing. It's why I finished the game really. I'm a sucker for the genre and the occult so it gets a thumbs up from me. What I'm saying is I can enjoy this as a walking sim.There's just a lot of balancing issues that make this game far too easy, but it's still just engaging enough with new environments, enemies, and weapons being thrown at you that it keeps you engaged.It's very bare-bones in the mechanics. You can dodge or block/parry with well timed blocks as defensive maneuvers (the parry is very 50/50 with some enemies),You can swing your weapon or pepper enemies with ranged weapons as offensive maneuvers. I at no point in the game feel like I needed to block, parry, or use any ranged weapons to beat this game, which is disappointing. The parry effectively just gives you an instant charged attack when you land it, is completely not punishable because parrying is ALSO blocking, making it so you can parry as long as you have a stamina bar.Even though that sounds OP, it's still just as easy to charge an attack and get the results of a parry without the effort, because you can roll out of ALL your attacks before AND after they land to cancel any recovery you might have worried about after swinging your huge metal slab with all your might.TLDR here; There's 0 risk and 0 punishment to anything you do.In terms of variety, they do a pretty good job in the first half of the game of drip feeding you weapons that make sense to use and feel good But once you unlock any gauntlet weapon and are capable of basic math, you'll understand how ridiculously over tuned gauntlets are.With 4 gem slots on almost every gauntlet, you must suffer between choosing to do 80% more damage, or 40% more attack speed. And that's not 40% as in 150% to 190%. That's 40% MORE. From 150% to 210%.Thankfully the gauntlets are not too bad because they consume as much stamina as any other weapon, draining your stamina super quickly and creating engaging scenarios where you can do quick burst damage and kite when your stamina is low-OR just get rid of your stamina bar!BROCCOLI IS A DISGUSTINGLY OVERPOWERED BUFF giving you 15 SECONDS OF UNLIMITED STAMINA where you can forever roll, punch, and block as you please, and only gets worse later in the game when you get a blessing that INCREASES BUFF DURATION. Not that you need it, because with 4 maxed out runes and mechanical gloves you will be killing almost every boss in the game in under 15 seconds. The final boss took 30 though. But not for the reasons you'd hope.This would be fine if consumables were rare, but with just doing all the side quests that you complete passively by exploring the world, you get loaded with more sh*t than you can store in your stash. I never felt like I had any less than 8 of whatever I needed ready to go.There IS a mechanic that interrupts your attack if you get hit, but the MOMENT you unlock a fist weapon, this mechanic becomes obsolete,This style of play is entirely enabled by blessings giving you things like stamina regeneration, increased attack speed, increased buff time, reduced damage, increased health and boss/elite damage... and again the consumables like broccoli that just give you unlimited stamina. You seriously by the end of the game will have 7 slots for all of these blessings. You will at no point feel like you have to sacrifice any GOOD blessings because you either get a noob trap option like increased xp that you have to sink your "extra xp" into to level up, more ammo for the worthless ranged weapons, and stealth... or just take the blessings that boost your survivability and damage.That being said, I understand you can limit yourself on what you use to challenge yourself if you want, but the game will never make you feel like it's difficult beyond self imposed challenges, and when you take away buffs and blessings you're left with a point and click adventure.TLDR; Game is engaging but easy, don't play if you're looking for a challenge. Do play if you like the aesthetic.
_childDocuments_.name: Morbid: The Seven Acolytes

_childDocuments_.review: It's certainly no AAA, but it's pretty good for a small game. It actually isn't much of a souls-like. No real penalty for dying other than having to respawn at the last shrine. Combat is slow and methodical, and your healing item gets refilled when you rest at a shrine. I guess that is enough for some people to consider it souls-like.The environment and enemy designs are solid. In particular, the bosses all felt pretty distinct from each other. There were only a couple enemies that I felt were poorly done. The mechanics and story are pretty shallow, but honestly the game is short and the pacing tight enough that I didn't mind. I finished in 6.5 hours all bosses + quests. If it were much longer than that, I probably would have started to get sick of it.All in all, I enjoyed it. I appreciate a cheap game that can be finished in 1 or 2 sessions. I probably wouldn't buy it at the full $25, and will likely never reinstall it now that I'm done, but if you can get it for ~$10 it's not a bad way to kill some time.

_childDocuments_.review: Morbid: The Seven Acolytes - Got this one from trading some other game for this one.As someone who has not yet delved into souls games i enjoyed my time with Morbid, lovely graphics/pixel art, was interested in the lore from the very start and the combat was fairly enjoyable. Boss fights were somewhat challenging (Mammoth and Toad personally worst for me) but once phases were understood and had the right sword they were doable and fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Morbid: The Seven Acolytes

_childDocuments_.review: The combat in this game is kind of miserable. It takes forever to dodge, the character doesn't always move or attack in the direction you're aiming in, enemies can't be staggered, you are always staggered upon being hit, and the enemies have priority if you both hit each other at the same time, meaning you will be staggered and deal no damage to them. It's not hard because you can farm a ton of bullets and cheese your way through the combat, but it's tedious and boring to do that. It's a pity, because the setting, graphics, and story are all great, it's just the mechanics that drag it down (deliberately so, according to the devs on the Steam forum). It turns a fun hack and slash into a slow grind-o-thon and causes everything to screech to a halt. I've actually just downloaded a cheat program just so I can enjoy the game without the game stopping me from enjoying it, which makes it hard to recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Morbid: The Seven Acolytes

_childDocuments_.review: Purely okay. Easily worth it when 90% off, so I'll recommend it.Slow paced but decent combat. At first it's very difficult: the first boss was by far the hardest enemy in the entire game for my playthrough. But once you get a decent weapon and blessings, it becomes fairly easy. In fact I never died to a boss again, but the ordinary enemies got me a few times.The game is generally fun enough, but is full to the brim with missed opportunities and seriously lacks gravitas and momentum. It just feels uninspired and takes no real risks. The level design is also very repetitive, always some twisting maze that lacks any sense of place. They really should've varied the layouts up more. The moment you walk into an open space you already know it's a boss... You never get surprised.I feel like a game that's trying to be lovecraftian should give you some allies that are slowly losing it, or something. The sanity mechanic is kinda thin.There are some nice touches I liked. When you're parrying the sound changes pitch based on how close you are to perfectly parrying, so you can actually learn how to do it. Most souls-likes I don't even bother trying.Overall, I had some fun, but it's mid as hell.
_childDocuments_.name: Morbid: The Seven Acolytes

_childDocuments_.review: This game was so fun and very satisfying to play. It is my introduction to the Soulslike genre and I have to say I am not mad. The bosses were challenging, the quests were doable and the rewards so worth it. I figured out the smaller little details, which I should have realized but happy I learned it at the end. I do like how, even on easy the game didn't pull any punches. Favorite boss of the game, even though I got so mad at her, was Tristiana. She was the official hard boss to me and I felt so good learning her attacks and patterns. Also, the parrying wasn't hard, most enemies you can parry. Even the hogs when they are charging, you can parry them. It is a tight window but you can do it. The sanity bar wasn't hard either, less sanity hard hit damage more sanity, you can gain more EXP. I will be honest, I can't wait to play Lords of Ire when I get a better PC. AND even the final boss was so satisfying. Thank you for making the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Got this game 85% off.It's a straight forward souls-like. However there is no level system or stats to increase. Instead you get a skill point and apply that to 'blessings' (e.g. Increase hp bar size, do more damage to bosses). Defeating an acolyte gives you an additional blessing slot. I'm a fan of pixel art; but, this game's particular style stresses the eyes a bit. It can be difficult to tell where you can and can't walk as it all blends together.The audio is fine. The combat works; but, can be frustrating. I never bothered with trying to time parries, it's not worth it. It's not a long game, and it's not all that difficult.If you're a bit addicted to the souls genre, you'll probably enjoy this. Get it on sale though.
_childDocuments_.name: Morbid: The Seven Acolytes

_childDocuments_.review: I'd like to give it a mixed or mediocre review but I can't, so I'd like to judge this game as indie and be more benevolent but the price it's 24€ and I don't think that's an appropiate price for this game. It does nothing totally wrong but it does nothing totally right. The NPCs and quests are irrelevant and do not offer nothing besides the rewards (no interesting plot or characters). The combat feels janky, and I don't know whether it's me or the game but I'd suggest avoiding the parry, it's the clunkiest part of the combat. I've also read complaints about the sanity mechanic but I haven't experienced nothing like that, I experienced the opposite, I had tons of items which made the last part of the game easy as ♥♥♥♥. I also expected more from the last boss, even though most of the bosses just took me a couple of tries, this one was on the first attempt.Besides all that, the game is purely linear it's A -> B -> C -> D -> E -> F -> G. There's a point where you can choose from 2 different maps on which one doing first but that's all. The bosses are not hard at all, the have 3-4 different attacks and they mostly follow a sequential patron. Attack 1, then Attack 2 and then 3. Finally, I can see a lack of polish, the stealth mechanic can be extremely exploited to kill mobs or just avoid them (you dont need stealth to avoid enemies though, you can run through most of enemies). I know this sounds stupid but also the textboxes for the dialogs, they look like they are taken from an introduction tutorial. It feels like this game just jumped in the souls-like genre train.Overall, the art looks nice but it feels like a heartless game, like if you asked ChatGPT what mechanics should a souls-like have and just implement them poorly with a generic dark atmosphere.
_childDocuments_.name: Morbid: The Seven Acolytes

_childDocuments_.review: This game combines pixel art with Metroidvania elements to deliver a grim, action-filled adventure. While not exactly a Souls-like, it borrows from that genre’s atmosphere and storytelling style. There’s a decent selection of weapons, some more fun to use than others, especially with unique powers tied to secondary attacks. Deflecting and rolling work well enough to avoid constant deaths, and classic mechanics like buffs, poison, and potions provide useful support. Collecting ingredients and items along the way helps you progress through to the end.The bosses are manageable, offering little in the way of real challenge. As for the story, it’s not a major draw—if you play these games, you likely aren’t expecting deep narrative. The music is decent, and while the controls can feel clunky, they don’t hinder playability. The frenzy mechanic adds an interesting twist: when activated, certain enemies return as “ghosts” after defeat to attack you again.Overall, it’s a laid-back game with a dark atmosphere and beautiful pixel art visuals. Recommended mainly during sales.Final rating: 5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Game is crazy good; if you're a Soulslike enthusiast, and have always loved the idea of playing a "soulslike but pixels" this is just the embodiment of that dreamCool maps, cool weapons, cool enemies and the bossfights are a pain down there, but when you get them right and win it's just very satisfyingI've read negative reviews talking about how the game is too slow or too hard, or there is no progression, but honestly, looking at achievements, 70% of players havent gotten past the first boss, which says a lot about the "too hard, too slow, no progression" comments imo (No offense, ive sweared a lot too while playing but its all perfectly doable if you put yourself to it) since the "progression"only starts after him, and you feel it a lot more towards the second halfThe art as well, some say it's kinda confused, and its true there is a lot of detail put into literally everything, but it doesnt really feel messy (you can see in the trailer that even with that level of detail it looks fine)If the game has a flaw is that is kinda short: you can easily finish it in under 10 hours (if you're good, so not me), so get it when its like, 7 or 10 dollars at most, otherwise it could leave you kinda disappointed(Even tho it comes with an NG+ so theres that to consider as well)Other than this, 10/10, a little shiny gem of a game, helped me relieve some tension during tough times

_childDocuments_.user: TTV in your name is lame
_childDocuments_.review: This game has great potential - the graphics are great, the music is great, the inventory and 'crafting' are good, there is a story. If you like the genre - looting, killing monsters, combining gems with weapons etc - you should play this game.That being said, there are some clunky bits that I found annoying to the point where I stopped playing. There are 2 weapon loadouts that you can switch between. Problem is there's no indication anywhere what is the selected preference.Parry is near to impossible to achieve, especially when fighting e.g the King.To hit someone or parry you need to face their direction, which is a bit hard when they're above or below.The secondary weapon is useless with a controller, since it requires to aim. If you have a secondary joystick on your controller the aiming direction will just jump around, making it very frustrating in a fight.From the very beginning, there is no indication on what you need to do. Fair enough, I understand this is not the hand-holding type, but still - you just get a list of things you have to do only when you interact with a shrine. There's also no sense of direction, just blindlessly run through the map slashing monsters until you stumble upon some quest item.I have no idea who I killed, where I am and where I'm supposed to go.This game is hard. I like a challenge, sure, but when adding the frustrations with the controls, it takes the fun out of it.Take games like The Messenger, boss fights are brutal - but still very enjoyable - while Morbid sometimes goes a bit too far - e.g you get stuck  in a pixel of fire or whatever, then you have blades flying around that you can't parry, your health goes down - with it the stamina and you're just stuck. You consume the whole stash of health things and then the next life you have nothing.Still, there is something about it that makes me play it. Unbelievable.

_childDocuments_.review: "Morbid: The Seven Acolytes" is a 2D-top-down Souls-Like in a grimdark-lovecraftian steampunk-fantasy-setting with gorgeously gory pixel-visuals and visceral animation. The combat (which was mentioned by most reviews) is somewhat wonky with seemingly irritated enemies against which you play a weird hit and dodge dance, but the boss-battles still feel intense and challenging. The game is more forgiving than most Souls-Like-Titles and if you have experience in the genre you can probably 100% it in around 5-8 hours. Some ideas and mechanics are good, like the runes that you can place in weapons and the upgrade system via different blessings. The insanity mechanic is also interesting. Give it a try if you can look past the flaws and dig it's style!
_childDocuments_.name: Morbid: The Seven Acolytes

_childDocuments_.review: If you approach this game looking for a traditional soulslike, it's possible you'll bounce off of it.However, if you approach it like it's a horror game(as in, something as atmosphere-rich and clunky as early Resident Evil or Silent Hill) with soulslike combat mechanics, you'll probably have a good time. Stamina regens very slowly, combat is somewhat clunky, guns have limited ammo per rest at a checkpoint making them better for picking enemies off at range you don't want to deal with, and you and enemies both can't alter the direction of your attacks mid swing; once you attack, you're committed to whatever direction it's aimed. It feels clunky and slow but does a great job of improving the atmosphere and forcing you to be careful.I've been looking for a soulslike horror game for a while and Morbid accomplishes that with flying colors.

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing this review I played under one hour, but here's my first impression on the game.The pixel art and the atmosphere are great, everything else looks, let's say, lacking.The combat system is quite clunky, and I don't speak about the attack speed/heaviness of weapons, which I actually like, but it's often annoying to see how you attack in a completely different direction to where the enemy is, due to the lack of an enemy locking system. The enemies (aside from the minibosses that I fought) have only one attack. Apparently the best approach to fight them is just to hit them with an heavy attack, dodge/run away from the one (or two/three in case of bosses/minibosses) possible attacks and repeat.Because of that the combat feels deeply unsatisfying and more of a chore than anything else.Perhaps the game will get better with playing it a bit more, but for nowI'd reccomend it only if what you're looking for are the (for now) only two great characteristics mentioned at the beginning of the review, but otherwise stay away from it. Definitely a title to buy on discount.

_childDocuments_.review: Enemy hits stagger you, your hits don't stagger them. This forces you to either hit and run or to master the coutner mechanic in this game. I usually like counter mechanics, in this game however, the mechanics seem unconsistent and the time frames for a "perfect" block are very small.  Now imagine the enemies being damage-sponges. So you either hit and run 15 times per enemy, or you do 5 perfect counter attacks. Per enemy. After the first boss you already get up to 3 such enemies in the same area. I only played up to after the first boss and enemies attacks and have no variety and their moving patterns are so boring, literally either charge you, idle at same position, or reset aggro and run away to spawn position. TLDR it is just not fun to play, and neither visuals nor story, ambient, music or anything else in this game incites you to keep playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable game for those familiar with Souls-likes or even someone who wants to get into the genre. There's a general attempt at worldbuilding and giving new environments to explore, which I appreciated. Some areas wore out their welcome, like Grimwald Grove (I think that's the name), and there's little purpose in the villagers you interact with, but you do sense a level of progression to the final boss. The world is, however, what you'd expect for a Souls-like dark fantasy. The music helps fill the atmosphere as well, so presentation-wise I think it hits what the developers were going for.Combat covers the basics and there's little reason to develop strategies. I often forgot I could parry except for one boss because I didn't need it. Item buffs are also largely inconsequential for how many types there are. This is a criticism of the items in general as well. The variety of items, weapons, and stat leveling indicate the developers wanted to make a more complex gameplay loop, but I don't think this matches the reality. Morbid: The Seven Acolytes covers the basics of a Souls-like and executes well on them, if stumbling on some things. If you're looking for a game to challenge you, this isn't it. If you're looking for something more casual within a dark fantasy world, I'll think you'll enjoy it. Recommend for short bursts, not long plays.This was part of November 2022's Humble Bundle.
_childDocuments_.name: Morbid: The Seven Acolytes

_childDocuments_.review: Another souls-like try, another semi-fail. If you're interested in these games, the developer says... well, none of them are as bad as this one, so no idea why I should have been interested. It was part of the Humble Bundle and on my wish list, but boy, it's quite disappointing, really.Took me 7 hours to complete, half of that was spent in the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ swamp trying to find my way around. At least it seems that way. All the other zones were straight forward. Go here, explore there, you know, fun enough, but that zone ... man ... especially with how weak you are and how strong the enemies are at that point.In typical souls-like fashion the game gives you little guidance. Your only real objective is to "get exalted". How you do that? Game doesn't tell you. Slaying bosses is the most likely answer, so you go out into the world, looking for bosses, finding a few road blocks along the way, looking at you Lady Placenta ... basically forcing you to find better equipment, level up, etc. Hence, said swamp area that almost drove me crazy. What the game also doesn't tell you is how "sanity" actually works... and to this day I still have no real clue, because there are conflicting information about this system on the internet. But I guess, lower sanity = more damage? Not that I'd have really noticed. The bar can be affected by loads of different items, but by the end of the game I just used up my consumables for the last boss and basically tanked through the damage, sanity be damned. Long live Brokkoli, my god, that item is OP. The game also doesn't tell you what elements are for or if you're doing more or less damage against an enemy, since there aren't any damage numbers...go figure.They tout "build variety", but basically it just comes down to "more health, more healing, more damage, more stamina, etc. etc." There's not a lot of variation, to be honest. The stealth system is pointless in this game, since you can't stealth kill most enemies, so why invest into that? The entire combat system is, unfortunately, where this game falls apart. You have 2 kinds of attacks: quick and heavy... the heavy attack 1 or 2 shots most enemies, but is always interrupted when you take damage. The quick attack deals less damage, but let's you immediately dodge out of the way. You also have a counter that can do massive damage. But only if you "perfect counter". If you don't you just negate all damage, which is fine as well -.-The difference between a normal and a perfect counter? I have no idea, I couldn't find a pattern, to be honest.The game then revolves around 1 attack, dodge out of the way, wait for stamina, repeat. Wow, so interesting. If you want to do a combat RPG, then your combat should actually be good. Which is hard in an isometric game, I get it, but most enemies in this game can't even bloody hit you if you are above or below them. Some just attack left, although you're right. They're completely out of their depth. Individual enemies pose almost no threat, other than "impatience", and boy, there are some bullet sponges in the game later on... and ofc you have a ranged weapon, which trivializes most tougher enemies without shields, if you want to use it. I didn't use it a lot, but I had basically more than max. ammo at the end.Unfortunately, most bosses don't deviate from this pattern much either: Get a hit in, dodge away, wait for stamina... dodge a few ranged attacks here and there. Lady Placenta was a road block for me at first. Dodging her attacks was easy enough, but I did almost NO damage to her. Came back a bit later, 1 shot her... And that's the problem with this game: The combat is just so boring and badly implemented that the nice art style, the story, the interesting environments, and the boss designs all fall apart. Not to mention that the zones don't really have much rhyme or rhythm to them. They're cool on their own, but lack cohesion. People have been complaining about how hard the toad is ... and I'm like: You can just stand in the back and shoot everything on screen, and almost never get hit 0oOnly the final boss was a slight challenge with his 3 phases (i.e. bullet sponge), but since I never needed to use items for anything else in the game, I had enough stuff to permanently heal myself, have unlimited stamina and just shoot him and his ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ from afar. As far as build variety goes: why bother? You get the weapon with the most damage that has enough speed to quickly hit an enemy and get out... and that doesn't use up half your stamina doing so. Meh.Oh, and that bloody map, which you can only view when visiting a shrine... and that is INCOMPLETE and leaves you guessing ... And what is up with the teleporting? The teleport points are just so weirdly put. 3 points are RIGHT NEXT TO EACH OTHER... yet there are no points to, I dunno, the other side of a map?! Thanks that I have to slog through the entire bog, the entire city, etc. again and again.All in all, 5/10 perhaps. Props to the art department.
_childDocuments_.name: Morbid: The Seven Acolytes

_childDocuments_.review: This is quite a fun little 2D souls like, I must say, but it's not going to be for everyone. The combat has a cadence to it that is rather slow by comparison to most souls games, but I think that is where it gets a lot of its charm from. Your attacks carry a punch that you can feel, but most of the weapons are a bit on the slow side, especially if you are doing their heavy attack which does considerable more damage. Most enemies are not all that intelligent so it's more about getting the timing right as you kite them around a bit. The art and music in this game are top notch, which you should be able to tell by just looking at the trailer. Body and eldritch horror abound and the sprite work is some of the best I've seen in the horror genre. Bosses are a bit of a mixed bag. Some of the bosses almost require that you switch from simple dodge-punish tactics that you use almost everywhere to performing perfect counter's because the punish window is just too small otherwise. That said adapting wasn't too difficult and it made for some interesting fights, but most of the time dodge-punish and kiting are the best go to tactics.The items and weapons are a little lackluster. I barely made any modifications because I couldn't decide what would be best for my weapons and enemy elemental weaknesses are not very obvious. However I did notice that when I got it right, I was doing significantly more damage to the enemies and you might as well fight bare-fisted if you get an element wrong.The lore is a little lackluster, evil gods move in, you are the last remaining hero set to fight them off, yada yada. Nothing to write home about but it's serviceable. Cannibals, mad scientists, and a lot of other standard tropes abound, but they are done well enough for what they are. That and the ending was basically non-existent, which was disappointing.All in all, this game is rough around the edges, but I found myself wanting more once it was all said and done, so this gets a solid recommend from me.

_childDocuments_.review: Feels weird at first, I hated the controls when I started playing but it grew on me and now I really like how precise it can be.Very slow and deliberate, attacks cost a bunch of stamina and your parry timing is really short. The game does punish you for mistakes but not too much so it never feels unfair.It's very well balanced - the progression system means you don't gain passive damage on level up, but instead must upgrade your weapons by adding gems to them. You'll find a bunch of these and a bunch of weapons to experiment, as well as many useable items with a hard cap on how many you can carry, certainly made to "force" you to use them, which is nice as I probably wouldn't otherwise.Enemies are fun to fight, some can feel very hard until you learn to parry them and some early enemies might even feel threatening later on if they're paired with other enemy types. Bossfights are interesting and not overly annoying.Music is certainly repetitive and too sparse, but weapon attack sounds are nice and enemies die with fun grunt sounds. It's not very well written but it's easy to go by just skipping all the text.Overall 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Very much on the fence with this game. The world looks cool but isn't very interactive and can be restrictive. You'll frequently try to walk off the main path and explore but end up running into walls that aren't always telegraphed. In fact, there are barely any secret areas/items worth going out of your way to find. There's a map but it's terrible. You can't look at it unless you're rested at a shrine and it doesn't even tell you what shrine you're at, so make sure you study the area.Combat is very basic. It has the bare minimum mechanics to be considered a souls-like. Instead of souls, you gain skill points. There are 2 attack types for melee weapons, fast and heavy, and a set of range weapons to shoot with. There's around 10-20 different weapons but 99% of them have the same moveset. They have different attack speeds and damage (physical and elemental). The bosses are neat, polished, and well done for the scope of this game. Earlier bosses were pretty easy but difficulty does pick up towards the halfway point. Only one boss gave me a lot of trouble. Don't expect a hard game.This will run you around 6 hours. I picked this up from a bundle for $5. For the price I paid, I can't complain, but I can't say I'd recommend this game to anyone unless you love souls-likes.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the game.  It's a straightforward rpg, the combat is pretty decent with its dodge rolls and parry/riposte mechanics, and there's enough to explore for a good 8 hours.  The art/aesthetic is right up my alley for horror.  There were some things I found a little lacking.  The quest system is insufficiently implemented to easily know where to go or what to do or who asked for what.  Combine that with a genuinely unhelpful map, you're left with just skipping it for the most part.  There are weaknesses and resistances in the game, but you can honestly just bully your way through opponents before it ever becomes a problem.  Storage maintenance was also frustrating at times, since you can only arrange/organize at save spots.  Overall I enjoyed it, but I think it sits in a middle ground--there's definitely better, but there's definitely much worse.

_childDocuments_.review: combat is either piss easy or toxicly annoying. no middle ground. but every enemy seems to be killed the same way. attack > roll > attack > roll. You can parry but it's got a small window and if you miss then you die, instead you can just roll and attack with little to no risk. You cannot break a block and enemies have infinite stamina. They also cannot have their attacks interrupted, but you can. So face tanking through a fight is not a viable tactic. Some attacks can't be countered by parry or dodge and have massive AoE. I got past the first boss and intended to keep going but the next area is filled with enemies that block all your attacks and you can't do much of anything except roll around and spam attacks until one of your attacks doesn't get blocked. It's annoying and so I just quit there.Stealth play is a nice inclusion as well, but like parry it's slower and less efficient than just doing the attack>roll spam. You will have a ranged weapon but you only seem to get a few bullets at a time and need to use consumables to refill it when you're out and about so you can't rely on it.I can't find much info about how the perks work, but from what I gather they will only amount to stat boosts and won't change the gameplay much.everything else about the game is great, but the combat is not fun enough for me to keep going

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start by saying I've never played a "Souls" game prior to this one, so take everything I say in here with that in mind.  This was actually a sort of warm up before I dove into them in the coming weeks.This game is designed to be pretty tough.  Most normal enemies can kill you with little to no effort if you aren't properly prepared.  While I did struggle with a lot of encounters at first, once I got a hang of the controls, it wasn't terrible.  I killed most of the bosses on my first attempt, and the ones I died to, I was clearly woefully ill prepared.  Honestly, I think most people that have played some sort of action RPG could pick this up and beat it with only a little practice.  And that's not a knock at the game; I'm just saying that in terms of "hard games" this one is fairly approachable.Aside from general difficulty, the gameplay felt pretty good.  I rarely, if ever, felt like I died because the mechanics screwed me over.  More than once, I recall yelling “AGH, I KILLED MYSELF AGAIN!” meaning the death was avoidable if I played better.  In a game that is meant to be hard, you need pretty tight controls, and I think this one ticks that box.The story is... there.  Most people that would want to play a game like this probably don’t care so much about the details of the story (which is mostly given to you through item and enemy descriptions), but it is at least interesting.  It’s very clear this game is heavily influenced by H.P. Lovecraftian works.  The overarching theme is there are these beings that exist on a different plane of existence that everyone is aware of, but they are taught to ignore.  They offer great power and salvation at the low, low price of using your body as a host.  Once they have infected your mind and body, they start to infect the world around you as well.  The protagonist’s goal, as the last remaining Striver, is to rid the world of these hosts – known as Acolytes – thereby severing the link to these other worldly gods.  Very dark and gory stuff, but really cool if you’re into that kind of thing.I only have 2 small gripes… the first of which I think can be fixed.  When making your first trip to the , there are 2 ways to “get in”.  Unfortunately, one of them is strictly an exit, only existing to help link more of the world together.  I like the idea in theory, but this confused the hell out of me (and from the discussion boards, a lot of other people as well).  This exit is treated the same as any other area entrance, having a gatekeeper that will let you pass once you meet the requirements, the only difference being there is a second gate once you enter the area.  The other unfortunate part is this “entrance” is likely to be seen first, making you think this is the right way to go.  I honestly completely forgot about the other entrance and completed a later part of the game first, actually making my experience a bit harder than it needed to be.  I have an idea of how to fix this, but I won’t go into detail here and will gladly share my thoughts if the devs are interested.The only other small gripe is the “Die 100 Times” achievement.  Yes, people are going to die a lot in this game.  Yes, it is a little funny to give players a cookie to encourage them to keep going.  But it feels like a means to drag out people’s play time when they finish the game (and get all of the optional stuff) and they’re barely half way there.  I spent another 45 minutes just farming these deaths after all was said and done.  While there is no “death counter” in game (that I’m aware of), my rough count of “farmed deaths” was about 50, meaning even for someone like me that has no “Souls” experience can make it through a game like this without dying 100 times.  This is just drudgery when you are at the end of what was a really fun game.  Sure, it’s optional, but it bugs the hell out of me when I have “that last achievement” and the game just sits at ~90%.  Anyway, this is a small thing.All in all, a really fun game that an average gamer could probably get through in about 15 hours.  Not too hard, but you definitely need to play strategically.  If you’re into tough but fair gameplay and have a thing for Eldritch horror, this is absolutely the game for you!

_childDocuments_.review: Took me 9 hours to beat the game.It's a complex, yet simple game. Easy to pick up, hard to master. This game has dodge and parry mechanics, but they can be a hindrance or a boon dependant on your skill level. If your not too skilful, you may find yourself dodging and running around a lot, which is perfectly okay. If you wanted to squeeze out that extra damage, you would need to master the parry mechanic, which can be quite rewarding if you pull it off, but a single small mistake can be fatal.It took me a while to learn in depth the damage mechanic, in fact I only actually figured it out when I went in to fight the last boss. I read some reviews about weapon types and which ones can be better online, but don't trust online guides, they are misleading when it comes to equipment. Instead, you should focus on your own personal style. Bigger longer range weapons are not always better. You may find that shorter range quicker weapons are better if your a faster paced fighter.The game is gruesome, while the graphics may be built like an aged game, you can clearly tell its made in a more modern engine, but this does not eliminate the graphic nature of a lot of the visuals. But then, if your reading this review, you already know that this type of game is built on the gore type appeal and it wont matter, but rest easy, the graphics wont fail you if you wanna see some grotesque gore.I don't often play games like these, I am more of a strategy gamer, but from what I can tell, its pretty good. I would recommend it to friends, in fact, I already have.

_childDocuments_.review: After completing this game, I've come to the conclusion that this is half of a game. The aesthetic is great; they did a fantastic job with the artwork... Gameplay is fun. HOWEVER, about halfway through, you start to get the impression that the developers ran out of money or time and cut features. The elemental runes/buffs? THEY DO NOT PROVIDE ANY ELEMENTAL EFFECTS... Unless you consider an animation sufficient, every elemental attack just acts as attack power up. No status effects whatsoever. All of the items pretty much do the same thing, but to varying degrees.... So some you just don't need, really. Parry? It's very precise timing and just way easier to hit/dodge/repeat.  Stealth? Doesn't really do much.... You can run past most enemies without them noticing. They all respawn in the same places, and follow the same paths. The only thing that will add variety is depleting your sanity meter, adding some random shadow monsters.  Some of the bosses are either overly easy or insanely difficult (but doable). Souls-like? HARDLY. The aforementioned mechanics make it a far cry from a true Souls-like title. Also, the same dialog is reused by many different NPCs, a common occurence in Morbid. I find that a little lazy. The game is also very short. It would be nice to see more stuff to do in game, like some sidequests or some more mini-bosses. It's like they had a ton of things planned for this, then just didn't do them. This is a shame... This game has potential to be so much more than it is. If you have money to blow (and there's a sale going on), you're not going to be totally mad at yourself for spending $8-$10. You'll get about that value and not a cent over. There isn't much in the way of replay value, currently. I would NOT pay retail for this. That is, unless the dev team is working on implementing some features and adding some chapters to this story. Let's hope so. But $25 for what you're getting currently? Hard pass. That all being said.... I still had fun. I enjoy the visual style. Just wish this were a whole game. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

_childDocuments_.review: If you're reading this review, chances are it's because you want to like the game. It's not going to scratch the itch that you feel when you look at it. It never really pulls back the veil between what you see at the start and the world you want to be in.  It's a game that goes at one speed the whole way, and doesn't have the animations or feel that makes other similar games stand out. So why the thumbs up? It's still not 'bad', it's just a bit meh, and I think that the developers - if they keep going - can learn from this one. The game has potential, and there are some risks in design that go beyond what others might have done, and it does its own take on Lovecraft that has fewer hangups than other games with similar budgets. I think the work on the worldbuilding signals some good capability here for other stuff in the future - there's just weird stuff with the combat (which many other reviews note) and pacing that could be revised.

_childDocuments_.review: Aboslutely recommended. As others have mentioned, its got a bit of hitbox jank but I think that's to be expected when the game is in isometric/top down view and there's some limits of the enemy attack animations, but if you understand that the enemies can attack pretty much directionally like the character can, then the hitboxes seem to make a little more sense.That aside, the combat was fun, the artwork was phenomenal, the inspiration from the Soulsborne games is clear and pretty well implemented for the most part (minor qualms with how the upgrade/rune system just seems to add flat damage regardless of element/damage type) but otherwise was quite well worth the time I spent playing it. If you're just jonesing for the next FromSoft title and expecting that level of production, then this wont scratch that itch, but if you've enjoyed homage games like Salt and Sanctuary, or some other 2D Metroidvania/Souls-Like crossovers for what they were as standalone titles with their own genuine attempts at breaking into the genre, you will enjoy this.

_childDocuments_.review: Where should i begin? So im a guy that love souls likes, just medieval/fantasy stuff with a lot of gore and cryptic lore. And i played a ton of indie attempts in that genre and liked quite a lot of them. And visually Morbid looks really good, no doubt. I have been looking at this game for months and following the news, reading reviews; which were quite negatively. Thats why i waited to grab Morbid in a sale. I played for around one hour now and there are some major issues that come to my eye. Main aspects are: lacking of enemy variation, lacking of weapon types and the way too easy combat. Killed the first 3 bosses and didnt even get hit, didnt nearly die a single time at all. The levels feel way too big and confusing, just unrealistically stretched to make to game longer, filled with the same consumables over and over again. And dont let me talk about weapons, yep they also throw the same ones over and over again in several times throughout the levels. Overall sound effects felt solid, just the soundtrack didnt create any immersion.So overall a game that catches your attention by an amazing visually design but in the end lacks the depth and variety. Its not challenging at all. Dont recommend at the state right now, im hoping devs work on mentioned aspects because this game has definetely some potential under its surface.

_childDocuments_.review: Morbid The Seven Acolytes is a cool little game.Pros: extremely good pixel art, the sound is great (for example the sound of your steps changes based on what material you are walking on) and the general vibe of the game, the gorish and monstruous creatures that walks on the land is just awesome.But it lacks on several aspects as well. The game is very short (8-9 hours of gameplay for a 25€ game is just too much), the game explains basically zero of his mechanics (the weapon type of damage, the runes, etc aren't explained, I went for most of my gameplay without runes because I tought I'd need to unlock them, while you can actually equip them from the very beginning) and the combat system is too bland, just swings, parry and dodge, I found only one weapon with a special skill in the whole game and it is average at best. In conclusion the gameplay is the weakest part of the game itself, and it's sad.It's still worth playing for the beautiful atmosphere and pixel art, but don't expect a masterpiece. Also beware that is a short game with very low replayability, so I suggest waiting for a discount since at full price it hasn't enough to offer compared to other similar titles.

_childDocuments_.review: , unless you really enjoy soulslikes, in which case I recommend it even at full price It´s okay.As a big fan of soulslikes I have to say that I had a pretty enjoyable time with this game, the art is great, the bosses and some enemies are really cool to fight and the sound design helps a lot with the lovecraftian atmosphere, it could use some polish but it is definitely worth the price. The game progression is quite interesting (but a bit underutilized due to the game´s length), weapons can´t be upgraded, instead you can find runes with different effects (like "15 more fire damage" or "3% lifesteal") and put 2-4 (usually, but it depends on the weapon) into any weapon. As far as stats go, you gain exp points by killing enemies (the more "sanity" you have, the more damage you deal and more exp you gain), but , instead you need to find "blessings" hidden in the world that once unlocked can be equipped (you can equip more the more acolytes you kill, pretty much becoming "stronger" by stacking passives) and leveled up with the points you get at "leveling up", you can swap them at any  checkpoint, on one hand this encourages experimentation and allows you to mix and match as you like, on the other this makes it so you never want to level up anything in case you might find a better blessing to upgrade in latter levels (which you will), the dev addressed this and I read in the forums that he plans to release a re-spec function to counter this, but as of the date of me writing this no such feature exists.The game uses a "diablo-ish" inventory system with limited space and (as of now) no chests to keep unique weapons or stash items, which is kind of a shame because some of them have really cool charged attacks but fall off in the damage progression curve late game and keeping them for the sake of it takes away a lot of inventory space.-, they are beautifully grotesque and have some very interesting movesets, they are probably the highlight of the game. There are 7 "main" bosses (the acolytes, duh) and other minibosses scattered around, learning their patterns and fighting them was always a good time. -, bosses and enemies are a joy to look at and places are usually really fun to explore-Weapons are cool, in general, there are way too many weapons with the same moveset but some have really cool designs and interesting charged attack effects that really took me by surprise- (explore, kill, die, checkpoint, repeat)-The "blessings" system is a really cool idea and allows you, for example, to play as a stealthy hunter no problem and, as soon as you reach the boss, go to a checkpoint and change to a more tanky or mobile build no problem.-The limited inventory space and low item caps means you are constantly encouraged to take only the more necessary items on your journey and cannot fall back on healing too much, also, farmable healing items heal you over time, so they never "replace" the limited healing.  -the game balance is all over the place, some weapons are really weak (specially some slow weapons) while others are insane (like a sword with the only drawback of losing 3% sanity per hit, which can be easily played around, or even ignored if you don´t mind the exp or damage penalty)-The sanity system is decent, but barely impacts the experience unless you have way too much or way too little (the "ghosts" that appear with low sanity are really cool tho), any fluctuation in between is barely recognizable.-There are quests in the game, but they are very undercooked I literally remembered they exist after finishing the game, you lose almost nothing by avoiding them (some exp).+/-the runes are kind of horrible, the lifesteal and sanity drains in particular are worthless, even fitting the special lifesteal weapon with all the best lifesteal gems you can get like 9% lifesteal, at most, so if you need healing you´re probably a lot better off just farming items, same with the sanity runes (to be fair, the consumable items cap at 10 units, which is actually a great way to balance this somewhat)+/-The art is great, but due to the perspective some passageways are obstructed or you feel like you should be able to traverse certain paths that you actually can´t.+/-some enemies need a little work, some are too tanky (like on enemy with lots of health AND a shield), while others have too predictable patterns and are very easily abused even if unintentionally, this can make the game feel too easy if you take it slow, but if you rush you can easily be overwhelmed +/-the death penalty is... well... nothing, this isn´t so bad but it makes the encounter lose quite a bit of tension +/-shortish game (7-12hs depending on optional quests, achievements and exploration), this wouldn´t even be important to mention but it does fell like a the blessing system needed more "room" to grow, also the "100 deaths" achievement requires you to die, on average, over 10 times per hour if you finish it under 10hs, which I find hilariousOverall I really enjoyed the game, it´s a little rough around the edges but if you are looking for a new soulslike to play this is a very solid choice.

_childDocuments_.review: Morbid: The Seven Acolytes is a very enjoyable 2.5D-soulslike that combines the gameplay from Dark Souls  and the inventory/perspective from Diablo, all with a tinge of old Zelda (at least I made that connection).One of the best elements of Morbid is certainly the art style with big, smudgy pixels; this is pefect for showing and at the same time not really showing the grotesque monster designs and hideous abominations you encounter on your quest. It leaves just enough to imagination to work really well. There is also some very nice lovecraftian lore that you can read up at the game's "shrines"; it's well-written and it fits the game's environments and monsters quite nicely. Aside from some weaknesses (fast travel system, some hitbox-issues, not too deep combat), I really liked this game a lot and can recommend it to everyone. It's not just the action part - the story is well-rounded and it sucks you in despite being quite simple. After a couple of hours you really get a good grip of what happened to the game's world and at least I wanted to see it through to the end.It's also on the easier side, making it well-suited for newcomers to the soulslike genre (and it doesn't really punish you for dying other that you restart at the last checkpoint/shrine).  I'm certainly looking forward to the small developer's next project!
