_childDocuments_.review: Well, I must say this franchise were forgotten when I first heard about it a couple years ago. But after going back to find more survival horror games I remembered this franchise and decided to give it a chance.The first game was impressive in its own way, it had some flaws, but this franchise had a great potential. So I gave this second entry a chance even though the reviews where telling me to turn back. And... Oh! Boy! I've should have listened.After finishing this game, my first impression was that the developers run out of budget to still work in this game and had to mash up everything they worked at that time and create a story around it. I'm probably wrong, but the release with so many bugs and patchs, the story feels detached with so many time leaps with poor connection, it's a major indicator that this game was rushed to earn more income to "finish" the development of this game.About the gameplay it was really a step back by removing the investigation button from the first game and turning it to a "cover" button that is barely useful through the game. Also, removing the key items list, removing the description of the itens and the possibility of examining them leaves the player with no sense of direction of what to do or checking the previous key item obtained.Crafting seem more like a close gap to the Haunting Ground series, but... Haunting Ground was never praised for the alchemy synthesis, but rather using the environment against the stalker was the best that that game had to offer.Stalkers now have a poor AI, they can't hear you running or walking anymore. They can only hear you if you burst through a door that only happens if you are running. And the new mechanic inspired in Forbidden Siren was... terrible. There is a reason why Forbidden Siren wasn't praised except for the fact it was directed by Team Silent and its gameplay was a major factor for that game become forgotten.It was sad how lazy this franchised was handled because it had already stablished itself and it had potential. But instead they just reused assets from the first game and copied more designs from other games which wasn't necessary at all.To the final touch, they have a bug (2 years after release and patches and they still have bugs) in the achievement "All Collectibles" where despite you unlock all movies, snow globes and files you still don't get the achievement.
_childDocuments_.name: Remothered: Broken Porcelain

_childDocuments_.review: Dear Darril: Hire a writer , please!! Someone needs to point out your mistakes. You'll become better that way.BE WARE. As soon as you click on the game MODUS LOGO ANIMATION MAKES SOME DANGEROUS LIGHTS THAT CAN CAUSE EPILEPSY (flashing red, blue and white repeated times)I played the first one and while it was pretty short and clunky I gave it a chance and found a good low budget horror game. The atmosphere and weirdness were the things that convinced me to keep trying.Broken Porcelain is a mess and I bought it after patch number 9 arrived. I can't imagine what it looked like before.It seems like everything was mixed inside a blender and what it came out was treated as a game. The graphics and music are great. I just can't understand what were they trying to do with the gameplay and how they thought the story was well told in this bizarre way. It makes no sense what things you have to do and why. The intro starts okay but suddenly the game starts and you are already running for your life without any understanding on what's happening. A familiar character that the protagonist seems to know very well has become crazy, but the dialogue you hear is void of any emotion. It looks like the voice actors didn't understand the plot either. So they just readed the script and called it a day.In my humbe opinion the art direction is on the right track. I think it's great. But someone on the storytelling or narrative department has little idea of how to tell the story or how the events take place.You just hear dialogues while you play that have nothing to do with what's happening. Also, there are a lot of bugs with the audio. Sometimes it's too low or too loud.There is a scene when you are spotted, and the game tells you to "find an alternate route" so I saw a button prompt over the balcony, I pressed it and the character jumped. Everything cuts to black. "Oh, a cutscene" I thought. No, I instantly appear on the last place I saved. No game over, no cutscene showing that you died. Nothing. You just teleport. Why there was a button prompt over the balcony showing me that I can press B there? Who knows. Developers wanted you to die I guess.  There are a lot of scenes like this.Inventory makes no sense. It's not intuitive. You just pick things and throw another without knowing. You can craft something and you have a little explanation of what that item does, but after  you crafted it the crafted item doesn't have an item description. So if you crafted 3 things, good luck finding wich one does what.You got a key item. Too bad you can't see them in the invetory, so you just forget what you have and what's your possible next step to advance.The brightness is a mess too. Super dark ( you can't see the enviroment so you miss items and places to hide) or too bright wich looks ugly. The best way to describe this game is: Inconsistensce. Hope they try to fix this. Is the least they can do for their clients. I'll change my review if I see improvements.EDIT: After patch 2.0 the game is playable. Still, the narative is all over the place. The jump to cutscenes is terrible. Everything happens abruptly and out of nowhere. The cutscenes take you from one moment in time to another without any reason other than make everything more confusing than it is.There's clearly no structure here. There is no mistery. Each dialogue is pure exposition. Characters make no sense and have zero background or personality. It's like playing a fastforward game. It feels like there are pieces or moments missing. The game doesn't make the time to introduce you to the characters. They just appear, do something and move on.Jenniffer swears all the time without reason. I get that she's "edgy", but please.Jenniffer's power should be a big reveal. But no, she just uses it.(All the gameplay problems are still there, so , clearly those are features that came with the strange mechanics )Too many bad things. It's a shame. This game deserved better. Profesional writers and narrative designers are important. This game needed one.
_childDocuments_.name: Remothered: Broken Porcelain

_childDocuments_.review: If "Tormented fathers" was bizarre but kind of linear, "Broken porcelain" is all over the place in terms of plot structure, weapons, gaming options and superpowers. You can feel that behind every artístic decision there's ambition and a willingness to make a bigger and better game than "Tormented fathers" was, but at the end you just feel that the game is changing (not necessarily evolving) every 5 minutes just because.What works in a novel or a movie (multiple storylines, multiple points of view, going back and forth) not necessarily translates well into a videogame, and unfortunately this is the case with "Broken porcelain". The plot is ambitious and ambiguous, and makes your experience as a player fluctuate, interrupting your game and your progress with ever changing and unexpected twists. First you dont have any superpowers, then you do have them, then you cannot use them, then they force you to use them, and you keep wondering: what the hell is going on?There're some bugs and the game is not polished (yet).Despite all these flaws, the game is entertaining and, sometimes, even successful. Some new bosses are genuinely frightening in a very tongue-in-cheek way And the whole game broadens "Tormented father"'s plot and topics, going in deep into some serious issues. All in all, recommended only if you like to play with shattered glass: you never get the full picture, and you can cut yourself, but there're good ideas and an addictive plot beneath all this madness.
_childDocuments_.name: Remothered: Broken Porcelain

_childDocuments_.review: Remothered is an indie horror game that is just riddled with bugs. My first bug popped up during the first 2 minutes of the game and after that I lost track. Voices are missing from many of the cutscenes and you have to read the subtitles in order to get the full story. Speaking of the story it is a jumbled mess that is hard to follow unless you played the first game in the series and are already familair with some of the characters already. The controls are stiff and moving the character feels off. Sometimes she moves when you want her too and other times she just crouches or walks which leads to you being stun locked by the 'Stalkers' a lot of the time. Combat is also just as frustrating as having her move since the 'Stalkers' AI can range from not hearing you behind them to suddenly hearing you from rooms away. All in all the best advice I can give for this game is wait before you buy it. In the state it is in it is not worth the full price tag. If you don't mind clipping through walls, enemies that get stuck on doors/walls/rugs, cutscenes were the characters jitter and flicker in and out of place (I even had one enemy go into attack mode and start attacking the character during a cutscene were you can't move cause STORY STUFF), and so many other problems that I can't even list them all then go right ahead and buy it.EDIT!!: I have now beaten the game 5 times. Every time there is a new patch I replay through the whole game to see how it is. My review still stands at DON'T BUY. Even with the 'fixes' the game still has multiple soft lock portions and glitches that just make you want to pull your hair out.
_childDocuments_.name: Remothered: Broken Porcelain

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Bundle for April 2021. If you are interested in the game and it's before March 4th, 2021, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.After an playing an hour to review for the Humble Choice April 2021 Bundle:This feels like a game made by people who didn’t understand what they were making.  The opening begins with a massive exposition dump of the first game that introduces more plotlines than a Metal Gear game all at once.  It’s a story that does not need to exist, as this title doesn’t seem to connect. However much of Remothered: Broken Porcelain seems to be introducing more elements of the plot without attempting to resolve or connect any of them, and before long the player won’t care about the story.  It’s just a big problem that the gameplay is even worse.  While the big creepy Stalker will scare you at first, actually being attacked by her makes you realize she has almost no way of damaging the player.  The game mostly involves sneaking around weak AI, trying to solve puzzles and deal with more awful scenarios, but everything Remothered does is low quality.  The animations, the sound, the AI, the gameplay, the controls, and there are still bugs.   Pick this up if you want a janky game, I don’t think I can recommend this to anyone else.  It’s extremely rough in every single aspect. If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge fan of games like this. Clock Tower, Haunting Ground, the first remothered, ect. It's undeniable that the game had a huge, fair share of bugs. But there's something to be said about the constant, near bi-daily patches to fix it that show how the devs are putting a lot of effort into fixing it. And that being said! If you liked the first, you'll like this. If you haven't played the first, Tormented Fathers, go do that, then come here, you silly goose!See you at the top of the world.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd pass on this one till they iron out some more of the bugs. Story is good and music is fantastic but overall the controls were horrible. _childDocuments_.review: Just like the first one this game is an incompetent, irritating waste of time.Apparently not leaning from their mistakes from the developers created an even worse experience as the game play is poorly made, buggy and often nonsensical. Why the hell is the button to open containers and doors the same as the one that picks up items? In a game like this where you could potentially be desperately searching for weapons and tools, you can accidentally shut the cupboard you're currently searching. Most of said items are completely useless and you only ever need a defence item and something to throw. The game introduces scenarios and fights without explaining basic concepts (possibly because of bugs) to the player so it turns into a war of attrition trying to figure out what you are supposed to do. There is no context or logical progression for some of the puzzles you just have to stumble into the solution and sometimes even when you do it still doesn't work.Scenes come and go with no rhyme or reason with jarring cuts and jumps to different times only made worse by the loading screens that mess up the timing of the cuts. Thus the story is hard to grasp and the characters and their relationships are meaningless as its told out of order because the writer thinks they are more talented than they actually are. Which is a huge problem because the relationship between the main characters turns out to be the lynch pin for the entire series. It is hard, if not impossible to engage with any of the characters and their relationships since the story is out of order in some horrible attempt at in medias res. And ultimately comes across as a failed attempt at pretentious. You cannot maintain tension when you put characters into life threatening situations then immediately you show the same character years later perfectly fine. Also cliff hangers don't work when you cut away to random scenes for literally 10 seconds to go back to where said cliff hanger left off.Also the multiple references to sexual assault and how its handled comes across as trying too hard to be seen as a mature game for mature audiences, but ultimately has the opposite effect. The perpetrator of the sexual assault is so cartoonishly over the top that ruins something that should be a serious reveal for the series. And it comes across with the tact of an edgy teenager.What story there is, is delivered in boring overly long exposition dumps that often just repeat things you've already had dumped on you ad nauseam. In one of the worst ways I've seen story conveyed to the player there are several videos played in a row that feel like they just exist to pad the run time of the game.I do not understand how a developer has not improved at all and in some cases has gotten worse. Or how they can't seem to understand and implement basic logic to how their games are made. Just like the first one it has completely killed any desire to ever play another video game. It is a vortex of suck that drags everything else down with it.Do not buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Remothered: Broken Porcelain

_childDocuments_.review: Both games have a great story and if you play them one after another, the story make more sense.I had only one bug on broken porcelain that made me restart, I guess the wait for patches made it worth it.The gameplay can be tedious but they improved it quite a bit in broken porcelain with making the characters movements being less clunky (except for the main character of the first game, guess they took the same body animation), adding a skill tree, some easy crafting, more stuff to do and explore, autosave, healing, special power, better voice acting, etc.I would say the enemies are sometimes too smart and you may find it's "bxxxhit", how they got to spot you. But in a way, it's more realistic that they will check hideouts even if you make no noise because you stay there too long. I also did like when we had more than 1 stalker.The frustrating part is mostly when you are stuck between a corner and a enemy, but they will now usually trow you on the floor before them so "you can escape" (problem that solves what the first game had).- It's a big homage to Clock tower horror games (so play Remothered if you are a clock tower or outlast fan)- Try to play the first one first, even if it's clunky and not so fun (use a guide if needed for the items to find), so you can enjoy at 200% the second game who is way more fun, way longer and highly improved.- The story is really good and talks about heavy topics like  PTSD, Alzheimer, identity, abuse,... etc. If you just want a horror game for just the hide and seek part, maybe pass your way.- Don't play it if you don't have patience. It's not a Resident evil/Silent hill (shooter) neither a Kid's horror game like 5 night of freddy kind (jumpscare mania).

_childDocuments_.review: First part of these saga I played in 2019 on PS and was excited. I missed the release of Remothered 2, but when I have seen this game is available in Steam- decided to buy it. Mixed reviews have embarrassed me, but the wish to see how Remothered story finished - was much bigger.The main plot of Remothered: broken porcelain is both: prequel and sequel of Remothered: tormented fathers. If you haven’t played the first part or have forgot what happened there - the game gives an ability to see a quick retelling of events.The game very competently reveals the story. Here tells very clearly how the story began and how it ended, so after beating the game I had no questions left about the saga. While in the first part all main plot was hidden in notes, here all plot is shown in cutscenes. For me, this is undoubtedly a plus, I was able to free myself from reading matter, and in return I had the opportunity to fully overlap with what was happening.Gameplay is mainly the same as in previous part. You have a gaming location and a place where you are able to save. All game you should pass by stealth and hiding. While here I have seen an ability to defeat yourself and knockdown an opponent (don’t remember was this ability in previous part or not).Difference that I can match - instead of having a big location with three save places, we have different small locations with one manual save place + many autosaves.I haven’t seen any critical bugs or crashes with the game. Due to all gameplay differences I didn’t get so much scare as was during tormented fathers part. I had a feeling that this game is less hardcore, maybe it’s because of understanding stealth principles from previous part, or maybe due to new defeating mechanics.I was really disappointed when have seen mixed marks in Steam, because I enjoyed the game.This game can’t be recommended to everyone, due to special game mechanics, as one saving place in the location and mainly the stealth game. This game would perfectly fit to those who played previous part and enjoyed it, others may not understand it. After I played Remothered: Broken Porcelain - already bought Remothered 1 in Steam and going to replay it.

_childDocuments_.review: Broken Porcelain initially intrigued me with its captivating story and Jennifer as the protagonist. As a fan of Jessica from Outlast 2, I saw echoes of her in Jennifer's character and grew fond of her. However, my experience was negatively afffected by frequent crashes and the frustrating combat controls. I tried my best to overlook the technical issues, even replaying some parts to progress. Yet, the constant bugginess and the struggle with combat controls eventually reached a breaking point. It became too much to bear, and I had no choice but to give up on the game.It's disappointing because I genuinely wanted to appreciate Jennifer's journey and explore the intriguing narrative, but the technical shortcomings proved overwhelming. I hope future updates or patches address these issues, as the potential is evident.

Watched the story on youtube, I pity the guy who played it from start to finish.At first, I thought the story would be decent, but it's just a rough mix of .Completely nothing to have from this one. _childDocuments_.review: Do not understand the hate that this game got. It was brilliant; almost as good as the first one. I only encountered a couple of bugs (which didn't impact the game much) though I heard the bugs were worse before. I suspect that like with the first game, a lot of people didn't like it because they didn't understand how to play the game. If anything I found the AI in this game more forgiving than the first. It has  great gameplay, atmosphere, setting and story. Liked the characters too, although I found the characters in the first game more interesting. If you're patient and like stealth in games then you'll have a great time with this. I'm really sad though that the creator abandoned this IP and that there will be no 3rd sequel. A trilogy was planned as were more graphic novels. I think its such a waste as its an an amazing survival horror series. It really feels like an authentic old school one. If both of these games had been released in the 2000's then they would have been very highly regarded. Please don't listen to the bad reviews, its really great and adds a lot more to the story of the first one.  And if you haven't played the first one, then what are you doing?! Go play Remothered: Tormented Fathers and then come back to play this one too. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: after putting this game off for nearly 2 years based purely on the launch negativity, in fear of it tarnishing my view on the series, I decided to finally play it; and I am glad I didI decided to stay away from the game for so long due to negativity regarding bugs / mechanical designs, ones that I read had "permanently impeded progress, requiring a restart", and other glitches of significant value like invisible player, invisible AI, scripts breaking, etc.. so I stayed away from the game - months later, I see that Broken Porcelain still hasnt recovered from its rough launch, in the sense of drama surrounding it, so I continued to stay away from the game.It wasnt until I was once again interested, after having shown two of my friends Tormented Fathers - so I checked the state of Broken Porcelain once again - the videos were not convincing; they were rather negative, but they were also not fresh, either, so with that in mind, I decided to play it for myself, to really find out if it was a bad game.I ran into no bugs that impacted my gameplay to any degree (though I did see minor visuals, but this was on the main menu screens, regarding my mouse cursor) and I did not have to restart the game for any reason. I must admit that the feeling of controls is the weakest part of this game, my only real complaint being that it feels like my character is sliding on ice the last 0.5 seconds of ending my sprint, and seems like there is a very small delay to how she accelerates when moving in the direction you are moving - its extremely hard to put into words, but it just feels akin to older game movement, I suppose to simulate actual running IRL (since no one is going to 90 degree corner whip instantly, perfectly, especially with how much FASTER your char is, at least 3x faster sprinting than Tormented Fathers)this movement, in combination with the framework of the game being modified slightly, makes it possible for you to be bodyblocked and hit for free - I got caught in a corner by a bodyblocking Stalker 4 times in my entire playthrough (5+ hours), which is a bit annoying when it occurs, but I only actually died once because of it. the AI are designed to throw you in a different direction if they can detect you cannot move, but are taking damage. overall, this was my only real complaint about the game.those things aside, the story and characters of the game made up for the slight clunkiness in controls, 10x over, easily - the characters in Broken Porcelain have a more diverse personality, and it all meshes together nicely. the setting of the game, the Ashmann Inn, is beautiful environment set in the day, but that doesnt retract from its creepy and isolating atmosphere. it also features new mechanics that allow you to escape, like vaulting obstacles, scrambling through crawldoors and more, which you'll definitely need for the boss fights, a new dynamic introduced by Broken Porcelain. I do not want to spoil anything at all, which is why its all vague, but its in my opinion that Broken Porcelain (outside of the feeling of gameplay controls) did everything better than Tormented Fathers.the puzzle elements of Broken Porcelain were handled much, much better than in Tormented Fathers. in TF, you usually find collectables/notes that give you clues on what to do, or your/another character blurts out context clues to help you. despite this, TF is still a confusing game for some people to advance on the puzzle side of things, so they may refer to a guide. for Broken Porcelain, the descriptions of your objectives are written much better, and your character will much more often remind you (more than once, unlike Tormented Fathers) what your objective is, or ideas on how to maybe approach. I only got stuck a few times, and that was moreso on my memory being awful than the game being non-intuitive.last but not least, there seems to be a "perk" system where you can upgrade passive skill effects (this seems to have replaced the defense weapon upgrade block from Tormented Fathers), and although I didnt find it a necessary to use this perk system, its a nice little addition that give some slight replayability. an example is "you move 2% quieter, up to 20%), and its more interesting than simply holding M1 at a block like in TF, so I'll take it.the games controls feel a little clunky compared to the first, but any dismay about the movement I had was massively offset by how much I enjoyed the rest of the game, especially the story. if you are an avid fan of Tormented Fathers, and you've been holding out on Broken Porcelain this whole time like I was, I think you should genuinely give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Remothered: Broken Porcelain is a sequel to a decent game, Tormented Fathers, which was borrowing heavily from classics such as Clock Tower and a little bit Resident Evil for its basic concepts, to give us a short but intriguing stealth-horror adventure.This one.... is just gross. Gross and schizophrenic just like most of the cast involved.The plot revolves around Jennifer, an orphan brought to a newly opened hotel under the Etna, to work as a cleaner. It doesnt take 10 minutes for the story to fly well above its own expectations, as a person who's supposed to be trustworthy, randomly spills the beans about every minute detail of the owner's life story to a random orphan from a reformatory. After the load of infodump is nonchalantly thrown in the player's face, in a couple minutes everyone goes insane just like in the first title, and its up to Jennifer to find a way to escape the hotel, uncover its mysteries, and possibly get to know who she is.Now, let me tell it to you straight, the plot is absolute garbage. This is the single most infuriating thing about the whole ordeal. Forget the bugs, which I have encountered very little after 10+ patches thankfully. The idea is good in concept, but the execution is, pardon my French, total horsecrap.While I could very well forgive the first game because it started right in the middle, and despite its last segment it managed to tell what it had to pretty well, this one is a narrative abomination. Expository dialogue, random infodumps, unclear flashbacks about stuff that doesnt matter (it does only to generate highschool drama to appeal to the gay community, and ONLY for that purpose), vulgar and distasteful dialogue, very questionable choices - there is a brutal murder of a dog in full view, no camera change, no prior warnings, and it was never present before that moment, meaning it was introduced just to make the player feel sorry - swearing left and right to generate shock.Halfway through I felt genuinely sick, and that's saying quite a lot. Everything that was being said, could've been said better, in a more tasteful manner, with better direction, and decisively better dialogue and pacing."Show dont tell" is non existent yet again, but this time around I'm not going to forgive the devs. They have learned nothing.At times, both in the gameplay department and storytelling, it looks like there were more than one person directing this mess at once. First, its a series of side effects of a drug, then its a disease, then its a parasitic infection that can be controlled, then sure lets throw in some hypnosis. Jennifer is a mary sue with a magic power gifted to hear by her mother ... because yes. This power grants her the ability to use a moth and fly across the rooms and corridors of the hotel, torment the stalkers which will be stunned for a brief moment, and execute scripted sequences that require her to press a button.In practice, this power is next to useless in the game proper and it's only mandatory during scripted sequences.There are some improvements in the gameplay compared to Tormented Fathers, despite everything. For one, the player can now move faster while ducking. Running is way faster in general, which is great, and the Diversion Items that can be thrown show a clear indicator that tells you where the object will land.Apart from that, the rest is a massive downgrade. The inventory is ridiculous: there are no Key Items anymore, so you cant use a key directly by pressing the "Use" button as it has been completely removed. This means that when you get a key item it will be used automatically on the door that requires it, making it confusing to locate the next progression. In place of the Key Items, there is a CRAFTING function. Yes, somehow the devs felt it necessary to craft additional objects in a game full of them at every corner, while omitting items needed to advance the story. To top it off, there is also a Skill Upgrading system... in a game that lasts 5-7 hours. Needless to say, the only Skill worth upgrading is the sprint and stamina, because any other "skill" is next to useless and it wont be used anyway.But the worst offenders are the lenghty scripted sequences that replace the genuine moments of tension of the stalkers in Tormented Fathers. Broken Porcelain is a very streamlined game, closer to an interactive movie experience than a real game. We are looking at a potential new David Cage - please no - with lots of buttons to press and forced scripted encounters.At one point, I was controlling a character that kept getting stabbed and hurt, but she wouldnt die, ever. It was then that I realized that the whole sequence would have me survive no matter what, so I just let it play out, the enemy grabbed me for 5-6 times before it ended and I "won".Other times however, there are encounters with the stalkers that the game requires you to incapacitate in a very specific way, contradicting what was taught immediately before then. This makes it frustrating and unintuitive and all the fun gets sucked out of the experience, which is not about horror and tension anymore, but more button pressing, scripted events, and lots of vulgar dialogue.At one point a scientist said a line that was probably written by a 12 year old, completely out of character, and I bursted out laughing while the character I was looking at was tied up on a chair crying. Definitely not the kind of reaction anyone would want from their audience. The voice actor was probably not aware of what the context was, because their delivery felt uncertain.What more can I say... I stopped playing after the end battle, inside the "interactive" epilogue, because the very last scene required me to run around the empty hotel chasing a character that wouldnt die and she'd end up stun-locking my own character after each hit. This should be proof enough.Remothered: Broken Porcelain is a textbook examples of devs not learning from their past mistakes, and a clear example of terrible direction and extremely convoluted narration. I dont know if there will be another game in the series, but what's certain is that this one sealed my next purchase. I'll be waiting for reviews and a good discount.tl;dr 4\10 blend of Last of Us 2 and RE2 Remake with none of the benefits of either of those. Avoid unless you're really starving for more stalker gameplay and you've already played everything on the market.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:-The winter lodge aesthetic looks really nice at times.-The voice acting is decent, although nothing memorable.-Some of the puzzles are decent, others are meh.Cons: (oh where to start...)-This is probably one of the buggiest games I've seen all year, tied with Marvel's Avengers.-The story development and dialogue at times is completely bizarre, not unlike Ride To Hell: Retribution.Things just happen haphazardly for no reason, and the game expects you to just go alone with it.-The player is given no reason to either like the main protagonist, nor care what happens to her.-The animation quality is borderline subpar in many areas.-The gameplay devolves into endless repetition that may drive you as insane as its villains.Overall: Speaking as someone who greatly enjoyed the prior game, Remothered: Tormented Fathers, Remothered: Broken Porcelain does little to expand and improve on the foundations of its predecessor. It ultimately goes farther in the opposite direction. It's a boring, sometimes hilariously bad horror game that fails to scare anyone after its first few halfway decent attempts.Edit: After the first hour, the game became so boring that while I was streaming it to my friends via Discord, that my friends began literally asking me to end it because of how boring it was. That is, when we weren't alternatively busy hurting ourselves laughing so hard at some of the weirder bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: Sorta amazed by the bad reviews for this game?? It's true that the Remothered franchise may not be for everyone, but it's certainly right up my alley! Broken Porcelain is a step up from Tormented Fathers in nearly every way possible - better graphics/animations, expanded gameplay, and (in my humble opinion) a great expansion to the overall story. Darril is a master at recreating the atmosphere from classic survival horror games / niche Italian horror movies. If you've followed the game as closely as I have, you'll start to notice a long lineage of inspiration from all sorts of horror classics. Some people have said that the plot was bad, but I feel that's a shame and misses the point - though the story is admittedly a bit off-the-wall, it's a perfect homage to giallo horror and the eccentricities of the genre. Through this lens, Tormented Fathers and Broken Porcelain are true masterpieces.As far as bugs go - yeah, it's a newer indie game, so of course you'll encounter a few. That's just how it goes sometimes within this market. What you don't see often is the type of quick response we've seen by the developer to sort out these issues - it's amazing! You can tell they listen to their customer base and are getting fixes out as fast as they can. People reviewed the game early on and have caused it to receive a mixed rating, which isn't fair for the current version. The game as of now is in a very stable and polished condition.I could go on forever about how much I love this game and the Remothered franchise, but I'll leave it at that. If you're a fan of survival horror cult-classics like Rule of Rose, Clock Tower, Haunting Ground, etc- you will certainly find something to love about this game! I hope people can look past the mixed reviews and help support this amazing title and the dedicated team who make it. In the meantime, I'll be eagerly anticipating the third and final chapter! <3

_childDocuments_.review: Not bad, not amazing, has a little bit too much going on. This game, compared to the first, is more focused on looping the entire story together, with prequel and sequel sections. It takes away from the original "mansion puzzle" all-in-one gameplay style that made the first Remothered great. I also don't believe it should have had such a collection focus, nor skills to upgrade. The first game had 19 things to collect and the gameplay was balanced without needing skills to upgrade core mechanics. Seemed a little bit like padding for time and a faux sense of progression.And without spoiling much, the only reason to replay the game are for achievements that literally don't matter for story whatsoever. An achievement at the middle or end of the game, only for an achievement, doesn't alter any story or gameplay. Once again, feels like padding. But good on them for adding achievements in the first place. Overall the story is unique in idea (between the whole franchise), but falls quite short at the end in my opinion. It's not a resolution I would have wanted, but that's okay, that's storytelling in a nutshell. The jumps between past, present, and future were hard to distinguish at times, only because I believe that was the point. Keeping the consumer confused until they are ready to wrap up the story, kind of old-school writing, but I dig it. I enjoyed the focus on Rosemary Reed as with the first game, with the player feeling like Jennifer is the main character, but isn't. I see it as she is the conduit that allows the lore/story to flow while figuring the entire plot out. Once again, not amazing, but not horrible. Solid playthrough and story from both games. The first was alot more structured and oldie survival horror, so I liked it more for that reason. I had no game breaking bugs, nor anything that stood out as completely unfinished (maybe the voiceovers, production quality wasn't always there, but it wasn't all bad). Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: There are a lot of things I like about this game and franchise. I love the story and aesthetic, but this entry was not fun to play. The first Remothered lived up to their homage to PS2 survival horror games. But this one just abandoned all of that and it suffered because of it. It brings modern gaming mechanics that do little to improve the game play. The "boss battles" are tedious and annoying, stuck hiding til the stalkers weren't looking and striking repetitively. The distraction items seemed to do little to nothing. And, personal pet peeve, I hated the change to throwing items at stalkers compared to the first one. The crafting did little to add to the experience, and I never noticed a change to stalkers when hit with different status effects. This is without acknowledging the bugs, one of which made me restart the game just to finish one boss battle. I have a lot of affection for elements of the franchise and its story, but this entry did not live up to what made me enjoy the game compared to Remothered Tormented Fathers. This one has a lot of answers, but it did feel like a chore to get through.

_childDocuments_.review: Remothered Broken Porcelain after many patches is now a good game, unlike when it launched. _childDocuments_.review: Beautiful. Somehow even more so than Tormented Fathers. The graphics are gorgeous, and the soundtracks in the game are so amazing, I actually listen to them in my free time occasionally. I have no idea why people are saying this game is boring - it's quite the contrary. The dialogue is very realistic; at the beginning of the game, Lindsay and Jennifer have an argument and it's actually realistic and even a bit funny. It feels like each character has their own personality, and it's nice like that. I'm glad this game was so cheap when I got it compared to the original price, but I would have bought it either way. I have seen people say that the game's story sucks, but I think it makes a lot of sense, especially if you play both this game and Tormented Fathers, which is one of my favourite games ever. I would recommend this game to anyone. It's dark enough to please anyone who wants to play a game with a creepy atmosphere, but not too scary as to make you hate the game itself, and I think that is a perfect combination. There were so many things to do that I was a bit concerned that I'd forget the controls, but they're enough to where I didn't have to constantly look back that the tutorial, which I am thankful for, and the simple controls (left click, right click, control, etc) didn't take any fun out of the game (it actually made it more fun. I hate spending half the game looking back at controls). There are also some nice secrets, and a lot of achievements to complete if you run out of things to do once you finish the game. I'm not one for lore, but this game actually made it pretty interesting to search for connections between Broken Porcelain and Tormented Fathers. Thank you for such a wonderful game, I don't regret buying at all. Probably gonna play it a few times over, too.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough one, I'm kinda torn between giving it a positive or negative review.Let's start with what I liked:-The graphics are quite good, the environments look good, the lighting is nice, the characters are (mostly) well designed.-The sound is really moody and helps to deliver a tense atmosphere (especially the ambient sounds).-The playable area's are well designed (despite seeing some decorations over and over, again).-The "general" gameplay is okay, pretty much feels like the original game.-the new gameplay idea's they tried to implement (with mixed results in my opinion)Now to my gripes I have with the game-the Storytelling (the story itself is fine!): The storytelling feels like they had to rush this thing to get done proberly.For example, we have several time jumps, which itself wouldn't be that much of an issue (if at all), what I dislked though was the sudden jumps. You barely got to play a certain area and just when things start getting real scary and panic is building up: BAM! Area finished and it jumps directly to the next story bit.The biggest gripe I have with that, are the cutscenes (like you're trying to escape and suddenly you're jumping through a window, it feels like half of the cutscenes are missing, it happens almost instantly without being able to predict what the characters will do, next.-The scary parts (which are nice) are too short.-Most of the items are useless in my opinion, in most situations you're just better of sneaking past the enemies.The area's feel too cramped and narrow (with a few exceptions), therefore in my opinion it doesn't it usually isn't necessary to use distraction items (except for a few exceptions)-Crafting: pretty much the same. You'll find crafting ingredients all the time but I hardly had to use that crafted stuff (which is basically only adding some stun-effects to the distraction items)-The Bossfights (yes, it does have those) feel underwhelming, in my opinion that's one of the things that should've been left out of the game, or at least different than stun and nailgun the bosses.-If you get caught during certain areas it just resets you 2-3 steps away from your last position.-this one you should take with a grain of salt: I kinda missed the executions that you get to see if you're beeing finished off by an enemy. Maybe I just didn't die enough or at the right time to see that stuff but that's something I kinda missed.The first game seemed more gory in that regard.-Skills: it's a nice idea to be able to level up certain stuff like being able to use your special skill longer but the game doesn't really require you to skill that stuff, might as well left out that stuff in my opinion. On the other hand it doesn't hurt, either.-the prompts (lie icons that should appear if you're near an collectible item) don't always show. You have to take a step back and fiddle around until you finally get to pick up the item. This happened several times.-Bugs: I encountered some bugs but so far the devs are pushing out patches on a regular basis.That being said, I played the game not right when it got released, therefore there must'Ve been alot more bugs that are in the game, after the patches.Still, I believe the game was released too early and the game should've been tested more thoroughly before releasing it.Despite it's flaws and quirks I still enjoyed the game, so I'm inclined to give it a positive rating but I'm certain that the majority of the other customers probably won't be that happy with the current state of the game. Therefore: I recommend it, but you better take a closer look at other reviews and watch some gameplay before buying it.(maybe a score will help:  6.5-7.5 out of 10)

_childDocuments_.review: Video Review here:      On one hand Broken Porcelain can be beautiful at times with vivid imagery, a foreboding atmosphere, and a story that can be beautiful and heart wrenching at its best moments. Unfortunately the package that it is contained in, is a Broken mess that most players won’t want to slog through to get at its brief moments of beauty underneath.     In the main portions of the game you’ll be hiding and sneaking around the Inn, trying to complete the various tasks that are requested of you. When the gameplay is at its best this can be fun and heart pounding as you try to avoid a crazed stalker and sneak around them while you get the tasks you need done. This aspect is very similar to the first game, though they did decide to streamline objectives so you rarely have multiple things that you are looking for at any given moment. For the most part this works, but sometimes your instructions can be so incredibly vague that I would often stumble into what I needed to do rather than actively put it together.      On paper, even with its issues the main gameplay loop here sounds like it should make sense. Get key item, avoid pursuer, and move forward through its story, very much in line with the first game, however this game has also added a limited form of combat to the game and… while the game was stumbling before, it falls flat on its face when it comes to combat. Jennifer can only attack enemies in one of two ways. The first way is to sneak up behind them while you have a weapon in your inventory. Doing this will allow you to stab the enemy with whatever you have in your inventory. This… frankly… doesn’t work… at all. The game gives you a starting pursuer to try and practice this on, but every time I would try to sneak up behind her she would inevitably always turn around right before I’d have the opportunity to actually stab her, and I’m not exaggerating when I say this. EVERY SINGLE DAMN TIME I tried to sneak up on her she’d turn around. And here’s the thing… this confrontation with the pursuer isn’t an option, It’s MANDATORY.     The whole game is like this, a mix of bugs, bad game design and frustration with a decent story and beautiful artistic direction. Were this a movie I would have to laud it for its creative vision, and despite the flawed aspects of its story I would have probably enjoyed it… but this isn’t a movie, it’s a game, and no amount of artistic integrity will fix broken game design. I can overlook certain levels of a game being unpolished and if a lot of the issues are ironed out in the patches that they state are coming, I might recommend the game then. But that’s not where this game is now, right now Broken Porcelain is a Broken nightmare in all of the worst possible ways.

_childDocuments_.review: Players of Remothered: Broken Porcelain are well aware of it's current existing bugs; however, I'd prefer not to judge the story and the entirety of the game based solely on that, when I am confident, that the developers shall do their best to make the necessary modifications for their players' pleasurable gaming experience, The story is a direct continuation of one of my favourite games, Remothered: Tormented Fathers, where we get to understand the narrative of certain characters in further depth, alongside receive closure on the remaining questions of the previous game. The overall plot connects on a beautiful and deeply-sad love story, surrounded by fields of neuroscience and religion, accompanied by tales of hatred, revenge, manipulation and wanhope,I would highly recommend acquiring this game, if you are looking for a good story; however, I would also recommend giving it some time, until the bugs are all fixed, to make sure you get the best out of this game. Playing the first game, I believe, is essential to enjoy this one at its fullest. Remothered: Tormented Fathers remains my favourite, solely on a subjective reason — dire attraction to Gothic environments; however, I do have to point out, that Remothered: Broken Porcelain did a nearly fantastic job with immersion, making you feel a part of the environment,I do hope we'll see more of the Remothered, perhaps of different characters and stories, as I shall remain their loyal admirer.

_childDocuments_.review: To preface I played the 1st Remothered (Tormented Fathers) and then immediately went onto Broken Porcelain. I overall enjoyed the game but there were somethings that did feel like a step back when comparing it to the previous games. I am going to try and avoid spoilers in this.Pros:- Graphics are a massive upgrade. Animations aren't as stiff, and the faces look a lot better compared to the first alongside much better animations.- Music. The soundtrack feels good and commonly goes well and elevates the scenes that it appears in.- Length. The story went on for longer than I expected and gave some answers to questions that I had through out Cons:- Glitchy. These were by no means game killers, but things I did notice that took me out of the suspense. There were sometimes small graphical glitches, i.e. characters loading in one place and then snapping to where they should be. Rarely there would sound effect's not firing which could make for some confusing cutscenes. AI in one of the fights towards the end could be a bit wonky.- Not Scary. I did not feel as threatened and as scared as I did when playing the first one, you are given more tools for survival and even in the cutscenes the game rarely scares and instead gives exposition on the story.- Tutorials. The tutorials in the game don't tell you everything, 2 instances I know of this is Snow Globes, I had seen a couple of them from exploring but had no idea how to collect them so ended up ignoring them until I figured it out completely by accident, and it took me until 2/3rd's through the game to figure out that there are upgradable abilities, having collected 'Moth Keys' that I had no idea what they were used for.  Other notes:- Plot. I can imagine that the plot maybe doesn't sit well with a lot of people, however, I did find myself enjoying it and being engrossed in what was being told. Twists that I didn't really expect because it felt a bit strange when thinking of the first game, however, after sitting with my thoughts about them, they do make sense in some way. Only issue I have with the plot is there is a lot of jumping around from past to present which to some may kill their immersion.- AI. You don't spend as much time being chased/sneaking as much as I would have liked, with often times I could just run past the enemies and try and make it to the next 'safe area'. I, on occasion, found myself being trapped in a corner by an assailant which I could not get out of, but this happened like once, or twice in my playthrough and as mentioned above in a boss fight towards the end the AI can get a bit mangled in itself.- Moth Eye ability. The ability is cool in concept, but is awkward to use and is very rarely utilised unless explicitly made aware it should be used for thisTL;DR - I enjoyed this game, and would recommend it. It's nice to have a continuation of the Reed's story but at the same point it doesn't feel like it lives up to it's horror ceiling as demonstrated with the first game, accompanying story elements that gives Reed's story an ending that I did not expect but still welcomed.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a fan of Remothered: Tormented Fathers. I'm a fan of Remothered: Broken Porcelain. I think R:BP is a relatively good follow up to the original game. The Inn is creepy AF. There's some serious atmosphere  going on in this game. Graphically, it looks quite nice at times, if not a tad on the dark side as far as lighting goes. This of course does help to set the mood for the stealth-based horrors that await you as you try to escape your pursuers. If you played R:TF, then you know that stealth will play a big part in this game as well. Unfortunately, that seems to be this game's biggest shortcoming so far. I won't mince words when I say that the stealth mechanics in this game are largely broken at this point. Broken in that enemies will see or hear you when they shouldn't be able to. Broken in that they'll pursue you to a hiding place but then seemingly not leave the immediate area occasionally, making it nearly impossible to avoid a confrontation the moment you leave cover. Trust me when I say that before long you'll be wishing for a cardboard box (MGS for life!!). The good news is that if you can manage to sneak up on an enemy with a defensive weapon you can get in a critical hit.  The bad news is that with the aforementioned issues you may at times find doing so as challenging as the Man Pig boss from the first Manhunt game, or perhaps a Clicker or other enemy type from The Last of Us series, on the higher difficulty settings. If you don't want to get the game now, perhaps give it a week or two for some additional fixes. This is still a pretty good game that perhaps suffered a little from a slightly early release.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been meaning to review the original Remothered for ages now.  It's still going to happen, though I'll happily throw down some of my feelings on Tormented Fathers right here.  That game was the equivalent to a gory low to mid budget horror slasher that somehow broke out a bit from its core audience and attained a cult status, even flirting with the outskirts of the mainstream without becoming too much of a household name.  Imperfect?  Beyond a shadow of a damn doubt but it was good to have a new 3rd person horror name (alongside Dreadout and more recently Eldervale) carve out its own piece of innard-splattered ground in the pantheon.  It introduced a cool new horror antagonist in The Red Nun and got by with its lurid vulgarity, oddball plot devices, tense if somewhat rickety stealth evasion and pseudo combat while dropping a nod to many of the past greats including Clock Tower, Silent Hill, Resident Evil and Haunting Ground.  That's what the makings of a solid new name in horror usually does from movies to books to games.  To say the least, I was pretty excited at the prospect of how a sequel would take the series further.  I'm going to skip the rather silent development of the game and all of the absolute chaos surrounding its release.  I finally purchased the game nearly a year later after multiple patches, in hopes that months upon months of time would bring us at least a playable and hopefully at worst barely decent game.  Another reviewer somewhere above me said it best, "This game is an absolute pile of manure."It's not fixed.  On a high-end PC this game deleted saves, suddenly doors would stop opening and I couldn't progress, enemies would go to walk away from a locker that I'm hiding in only to jog in place and block me from leaving, keys I needed would vanish from my inventory, there'd be sudden crashes...  I did manage to finish for whatever reason although I can assure you that at least 3 hours of my close to 9 hour playthrough were spent by saving in every slot possible for fear of losing progress and closing/reloading the game more times than I bothered to keep track of.  It's still a bugged mess.  You'll probably be able to finish it but to do so you better back-up those saves and be prepared to reload at a moment's notice.  The performance is trash even when it does manage to miraculously run for a continuous and oh so gracious half hour.  Hiccuping frame rates, missing animations, object clipping, downgrade visuals...  Yeah, it'll run but half of its parts will fall off all along the marathon trail.  It's so sad to see this because the germ of a highly improved game is buried beneath this graveyard of survival horror junk.  You play Jennifer this time and as you explore Ashmann Inn you've got a heightened arsenal to build makeshift close combat and ranged weapons from; pelting your enemies with poison laced bottles, shrugging off attacks with souped up scissors or assaulting the game's prime foe Porcelain with a nailgun.  Oh, what could have been!  What is there of the combat definitely teases how much better this could have been than the original but the fact of the matter is the system is broken and unfinished.  There is also stealth combat that sees you being able to lure and distract enemies with radios, alarm clocks and more, allowing you to sneak up behind them and unleash a torrent of say scissor stabs that feels satisfying to pull off...when you can pull it off.  You'll glitch through enemies like Casper the Friendly Ghost or sometimes the hit-boxes won't read...like...at all...man.  Enemies will become vaporous and float right through your grabs and I've had bosses that needed their asses kicked get stuck in the walls and become unhittable.  This might not happen to you, maybe the game will give you its best all the way through but on a high-end rig I sure put up with some trash across every inch of this landfill.  As stated earlier, I couldn't even shake a decent performance out of the P.O.S.  Wrapping up the core gameplay of sneak fighting and the usual find this item to access this area investigation, Broken Porcelain is brimming with a hugely ambitious story that is tarnished by utterly terrible direction.  Cut scenes will jarringly start or stop with no rhyme or reason, every leaden scene devoid of careful touches like appropriate music, fade-outs or fade-ins, their mouths moving when talking or even good voice-acting.  I loved the work Darril did with the first game but seriously, what the hell happened here, the low-grade indie horror Hegis' Grasp runs circles around this.  At least it respected its budget and had a cool Revolutionary War Time setting.  This is just so sad to see all around.  Not only is it bad but outside a select chapter or two, it's so generic.  There's an upgrade system just to have an upgrade system.  Little of the stats make any difference.  The game is easy as sin anyway.  I just wish this stayed in development.  It's hilarious watching playthroughs of this after the fact (I held off largely all of this time other than watching about 15 minutes of the demo and 15 minutes of the initial release) but it was misery to play for about 80% of the time you could actually play it.  I would have taken overly ambitious + mediocre but it's rough to get through the CONSTANT barrage of scenes.  There's a lot of story in this.  Maybe as much as actual playtime.   There's too much story frankly and there are so many twists it's hysterical.  When I said overly ambitious story earlier, I forgot to say..."Yeah, I mean it was no good but it was overly ambitious!"   I could go on and on here.  Picking on the decrease in control quality (I originally typed deceased accidentally...that worked too) or the fact that brief segments of assuming other characters have been so poorly tacked on and the one specific chapter I'm thinking of is nearly pointless (Rosie, you out there?  She's probably at some dead-end bar drinking gasoline to forget this sequel)...  None of it works well or at all but the lousiest part about Broken Porcelain is that there were some fun parts, brief flashes of how great this could be.  The first chapter was the best and seems to be where all of the resources went and battling Andrea even at its glitchiest was a good time...the parking garage shootout where you're armed with a nailgun and Porcelain tries to stab you to death is tense and frantic...a couple of parts still manage some dim light even if they aren't what they could have been.  At its current stage, 10 months after its release Broken Porcelain is so vaguely playable that you might be able to finish.  That is if you don't get fed up with the thing first.  I try to complete every game I own at least once and somehow I got this monkey off my back.  I'll never go back to it though and it will only be remembered to friends when they asked me if I've played anything they should avoid lately.  It also feels like what was meant to be a trilogy was packed into two games, as once the curtain fell I do sense that the story had some sort of end.  An end for all of the characters was reached and that means we simply won't get another offering.  Honestly, after this mess, I don't think I'd bother to waste such cash on the possibility of more undelivered promises.  Bottom line?  This felt like playing Crying is not Enough.  I gave that a 3.5 and there's no way that if I'm calling out numbers, Broken Porcelain deserves any higher in my opinion.  Some people liked it and to that I say I'm glad somebody liked it because I sure as hell didn't!

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually do reviews for games, but this game was hilariously worse than I expected.When the game came out, I did hear about all the negativity surrounding the game, so I decided to wait a few years to see if it got better. I got the game on a good sale, but I will say... It wasn't even worth the cheap price I paid for it.The game's 'shock value' adds literally nothing to the game, except being there just to add shock. Adding nearly every insulting words possible, and even insinuated pe*oph*lla is disgusting.The graphics were fairly decent, but I cannot say the same about the story, pacing, enemy coding, voice acting or even the cutscenes!Cutscenes were all over the place, they make no sense at all on what is going on to the point that the cutscenes feel like they were half-finished when the game was released.Enemy Coding is so lackluster, you can easily lose enemies and they never really felt threatening, the only time they did was if they pinned me against the wall, and I couldn't escape.Story was... something, I have seen bad stories but this one just takes the cake. It is all over the place, it involved VERY forceful writing, and unnecessary plot points that could have been worded better, or even omitted entirely.Voice Acting is where the game falls apart completely. Line delivery by Ashmann was very forced and terrible, it sounded like he never did voice acting before and probably hated what he had to say. Jennifer's voice acting was hilarious, I couldn't take her seriously, same with Andrea, Elisa, Gloria and Lindsay. The pacing also felt off, it felt like it was meant to be a much longer game, what with the game giving you a place to upgrade your player's stamina, moth usage, and even how long you can stun enemies. Which isn't needed all that often after you reach the upgrader.From how quickly the support for this game was dropped, it makes me think the Developers saw it as a lost cause. Chris Darill also said the game isn't what he wanted. (Ignoring the fact he wrote the game and directed it, so he had final say on everything).All in all, do not get this game, even on sale. It isn't worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a 7/10 for me. I'm not sure what the game was like upon day one of release but I had little to no bugs nor did I get trapped, glitched or stuck anywhere. I think that's where most of the negative reviews come from, the other half is the confusing ass story and I only say that because this game expects that you play the first one... the writing is a bit amateurish and cheesy at times, characters change tones and accents. This could've easily been solved if they did a second take. The new mechanics aren't too bad and easy to get used to. This game is well worth your money and time playing if you're a fan of classic survival horror. This game breathes classic Italian horror of Dario Argento. The atmosphere and hauntingly depressing yet charming music fits the theme of the game well and the survival horror elements are straight out of the early 2000s golden age of horror, though more refined. The story and setting are like a mashup of the movie Phenomena and the game Rule of Rose. The devs must've been fans.I can't wait for the 3rd and last Remothered game, I hope the devs learned from this one that it's better to refine a game and delay release then release a buggy game and patch it after everyone gives the game poor reviews.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: the bugs I mentioned in this review are now fixed.Broken Porcelain is better then its previous entry, Tormented Fathers, in many ways. But why, just why would you devs launch the game full of bugs like this? This is not a beta/early access version, it's the full game! Icons!• Wonderful story, full of plot twists and revelations• Nice soundtrack• The perfect horror factor • Great scenarios• I like how the gameplay feels more nice then Tormented Fathers: you have much more scenarios to explore, not being "stuck" at just one place. The stalkers aren't after you all the time like before, so now you have a chance to catch your breath sometimes, do some puzzles meanwhile, etc. • Some bugs that I experienced, but now devs fixed them• I felt bad for If you're a survival horror fan like me, wait for bugs to be fixed so you can play this like you should. This is a amazing game. Instant classic.

_childDocuments_.review: "Remothered: Broken Porcelain" is a haunting and immersive experience that truly stands out in the survival horror genre. The sense of mystery and tension is constant, making every moment feel suspenseful and unpredictable.One of the standout aspects of the game is its character design. In particular, one of the characters strongly resembles Velma from Scooby-Doo. This instantly recognizable look adds a nostalgic touch for fans of the classic cartoon, while also contributing to the game's quirky yet unsettling vibe. The character exudes a similar brainy, resourceful personality, which adds a layer of charm to the overall dark and intense storyline.While the game does have a steep learning curve, it's a rewarding experience for those who enjoy strategic gameplay and psychological horror. "Remothered: Broken Porcelain" excels in keeping players hooked with its rich story, intriguing characters, and terrifying atmosphere. Highly recommended for fans of horror games who are looking for something unique and thought-provoking!

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR = Decent game, with some bizarre design choices, completely fails in the "horror" department, but still enjoyable, buy it on sale for 15$ CND at most only.I had to really think if I wanted to recommend this game, the thing is... it does a lot of things good but also a lot of things bad. But ultimately, I did enjoy my time with it.. and would love for then to finish the trilogy (this is part 2). First of all the story just gets more wacky and nonsensical the more you progress, but hey I am someone who enjoys stuff like the YokoTaroverse (Drakengard/Nier timeline) and Kingdom Hearts, so I am fine with that. The story does enough to want to see what happens next... even if at times its hard to follow, I did shed a few tears at some key points... and thats always a good thing. Also, I read that the creator of the legendary horror series "Silent Hill" was really impressed with this duology and stated that he would love to collaborate... part 3 could end up being epic. Ultimately, you should only play this game if you like the story, everything else is just meh.The sound design is as good as it was on the first one, and it had decent graphics, so no complaints there, although I did get a bit tired of the hotel by the end of it, as it makes you revisit it several times throughout the game.The enemy designs are even worse than the first game this time around, you got stuff like a fat lunch lady, a regular guy with a gun... a maid...yeah nothing really scary. One of the new main bad guys is a guy with a porcelain baby mask... which just look laughable. The iconic Red Nun is back, but this time she has a flamethrower lol... if you are looking for a horror game, sadly you are out of luck here, most encounters just end up being annoying but doable, and I never really felt scared or in any real danger. This time around you can even use items to knock out enemies, yes you can knock out the person stalking you with a few bottles and a letter opener. To be fair games like Resident Evil had stuff like the big hulking Nemesis you could knock out with some well place bullets, but this games whole gimmick was that you were defenceless against crazy psychos so you had to constantly hide... but in this game, there is really no point to hide at all. The game even gives you even more powers as you can upgrade your characters "Moth" powers, including unlocking a drone-like one that lets you see where enemies are.One of the main issues I had, was that this game does not explain alot of stuff, it has a few tutorials here and there, and lots of survival horrors don't give you certain information as they expect the player to figure out certain things by themselves to give a sense of "survival", but for example.. as I mentioned the "Moth Powers", at no point does it tell you that you can upgrade them and how, even in chapter 1.. I figured it out cause I googled wtf those collectables I was getting were for, otherwise I probably wouldn't had figure out it out until several chapters later.. this information which is rather crucial. Another collectable that you can also get right from Chapter 1 requires you to either throw something at it, or wait till you get the Moth Bot power halfway through the game, however since the game does not tell you that, I was stuck there left clicking thinking my game had bugged and not letting me pick them up.. since they look just like every other item.Speaking of items, they somehow went backwards from what they had done in the first game. First of all they added "crafting" which is such an overused mechanic, everyone is sick of it by now. Then, you cant tell if an item is an ingredient, a base or a defence item.. the first game had little icons that immediately told you what type of item it was, in this one you have to just keep picking them up to figure out what item it is. And then, when you run out of your 3 inventory slots and you pick up something, rather than switching your active item with what you are picking up... it replaces it with another item in your inventory, so lets say you got 2 good items and a garbage one, and you want want to replace that third garbage one with another good one... you need to press "Pick Up" 3 times, until the garbage item is on the ground. Its just not intuitive at all, which is bizarre as I mentioned... cause they already had a good system going in the first game. With all that said... I am really excited of what the last part of the trilogy will bring, they always say the first and last parts of a trilogy are always the best, and the second one always ends up being like an unloved middle child. As a side note..I made a joke in my review of the first game about how "plain jane" the main character looked, she has some scenes on this one, and they managed to make her look like a total "sexy femme fatale".. so thats always a plus for me lol

_childDocuments_.review: Remothered broken porcelain is a story about Jennifer, the girl who went missing in the first game. You have been kicked out of your group home for being reckless and defiant and have been place in the care of another at a hotel where you are serving as a maid.The story is quite good and much more in depth than the first game. You met up with another girl named Lindsay and together you form a bond and eventually plan an escape from the hotel. The people who work at the hotel are under a mind hive control who will stalk and try to murder you for trying to flee. You have weapons like knives, bottles, and decoy items, but they all break after a single use. Using stealth is going to be your main source of staying safe.There’s also a lot of collectibles in the game from photos, news paper clippings, notes, and globes that unlock statues in the main menu.The graphics and animations are improved over the first game as well as the game engine. Everything looks great and movements are smooth looking and don’t look janky or awkward. The sound and voice acting is also good and nothing really cringy.Some things I didn’t really like was the stalkers were easily triggered and that would cause a chase. Only after you fully leveled your skills in silent movements did it become somewhat better but the triggers still happened even when crouched.There was a lot of loading between scenes that could have probably been better handled with some sort of transition. It just felt weird when a chapter or scene ended you had to wait for a loading screen.Some of the boss fights felt confusing on what to do as you don’t really get any hints and you could be stuck there for a bit trying to figure them out.Also the dog gets stabbed and dies and this apparently trigged some people but I myself did not see any big deal as it’s just a game.I played this on steam deck and the game ran excellent with near max settings with medium shadows and it was an almost constant 60fps during game play. Cutscenes got weird sometimes and ran around 45 fps. It’s too bad this game got bombarded with negative reviews when it was released due to bad performance, as it runs great now but the damage has already been done. It’s a good game now that it’s fixed.7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I won't pretend this game wasn't a bit buggy when I first played it on launch. I won't either pretend that my absolute adoration for this game and the first are affecting my ability to make an objective review.However, if you enjoy well thought out, convoluted stories with twists and turns, and are a fan of stalker-type games á la Haunting Ground or Clock Tower, give this game a chance. But play the first one first (duh), I see a lot of reviews mentioning they don't know what's going on with the story but they didn't play the first one? I mean...obviously?Even before any patches I didn't come across any bugs that were a total gamebreaker for me, but within 2 days all the major ones I did notice had been fixed by the developers because they are actively listening to their community and fixing up the game accordingly. That in and of itself is impressive these days where there's a tendency to publish a game and leave it as it is, and ignore your player's reports indefinitely.They have even tweaked game mechanics that were not necessarily broken to begin with, but once recommended enough by players were adjusted to improve the overall experience. This is rarer still, for developers to admit the way they designed something may not have been the most intuitive and not just say "That's how it was designed."Give this game a chance. Whether you haven't bought it yet, bought and refunded, or are leaving it uninstalled in your game library and waiting for more updates, you WILL find enjoyment in this game if you are a fan of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: I recently played this game for my April 2021 Humble Bundle Review. The section talking about this game starts at 10.10 of the below video. These are my impressions after an hour of gameplay - I will update this review if I ever do a full review.The plot is poorly told and just convoluted as hell, especially for someone who hasn’t played the first game. I don’t even care to explain the premise of the game to be honest, after 30 minutes of playing I couldn’t even tell you. There is so much info-dumping here, that you can’t actually retain and process it all because it is dumped on you so fast. It seems like they didn’t hire a writer for this project at all. The most basic rule of storytelling – show don’t tell, is completely ignored here. I mean the first of many cutscenes for the intro is literally a 1-2minute long summary of the last game. Just telling you exactly what happened. Imagine if talking about the last game was revealed to the player through notes or as side details in human-like dialogue???Another example is where this lady straight-up monologues about her creepy employer’s life story to you for 3 minutes, even though she apparently thinks this kid is annoying and a nuisance. That’s not how people are – if you think someone is annoying you don’t yap at them spreading secrets.The gameplay doesn’t bring anything new to the table really, extremely standard mechanics. A crafting system even though you can only carry 3 items, which is extremely limiting and annoying. Your character walks at the speed of a snail. There are a couple jump scares, lazy. They also do the good ole' introduction section where there is no escape and you have to die to progress. Such a lame trope.The graphics look blurry and the voice acting and lip syncing is weird – the audio doesn’t always sound like it is coming from the person who is speaking, and the girl you are playing, who looks around 10 – sounds like a 25 year old. It doesn’t seem polished at all.Stay away from this one. Check out my video if you want to listen to more of my thoughts on this or any other of the games on this bundle. If you found this review helpful, a like or subscribe would be much appreciated :)
