_childDocuments_.review: As you've probably noticed, some people have really enjoyed this game and others have not. I fall into the category of one who doesn't mind the Realm of Chaos campaign that many others despise. Yes, at times it can be annoying, but as someone who has plays the Vortex campaign in Total War Warhammer 2, I'm quite used to this type of campaign and don't need to wait for Immortal Empires to come out.Some pros to the game:- Decent Faction Selection (base game has 9 Legendary Lords from 7 different factions).- Map is very large and allows for diversity in what enemies and friends you come across.- Individual Faction Mechanics for every faction that adds some flavor to each one.- Skarbrand the Exiled punting most characters across the map.- Graphics are pretty good especially on higher settings.- Modding Community is wonderful.Cons:- Immortal Empires isn't out yet. Less sandbox-ish for now as you are kind of forced into playing the Souls Race unless you have a mod that turns it off.- Limited Units as of now for each faction, especially the Daemonic factions.- Cannot play as the Warhammer one and two races. This doesn't faze me, but I know it affects a lot of people that fancy playing the Empire for the 50th time.- Anti-Player Bias still is strong, but much better than what it was at release back in February of 2022.Conclusion:Personally, I think the game is worth it and it is only going to get better as we progress further into the year. If you are waiting for Immortal Empires, then I would hold off until later this year when the beta gets set up for that. If you really want to try out new factions like Cathay (which is new-ish to lore) and the Daemons, then I would recommend getting this game. I hope this helps you all make a good decision!

Are coders just working from home most of the time with no oversight, then it's oh #$% we have to release this game soon? There are certain sections of the map where your fps takes a huge flop. Why was this not addressed prior to release? Clearly, something is up with the meshes in the terrain. It sure makes you wonder where are the managers are at while the coders are building their products. QC seems to be rare in gaming developing nowadays. Just release buggy messes and let either modders fix the game or slowly fix some issues over the lifespan of the game *cough* Cyberpunk. I would be embarrassed at the state of the game if I was in charge of the development. Pros:-terrain in battles are beautiful-some interesting chaos units with pretty cool animations-chaos factions add interesting conflicts to the campaign-being able to swap out gear on the daemon prince and affect his looks is niceNegs:-performance drops in sections of the campaign map can really tank fps-buildable towers in siege can be a bit too op-very little new content from previous WH games, just a new map and chaos unit mods from WH2 have broken out chaos into different factions. Hardly any new units to the series besides for the 2 new human factions. -a number of factions won't do any expansion in the game (rats example)-trips to chaos realms to grab tears is meh at best- still no blood dlc, which i don't understand why this still has yet to drop along with the games at launch after WH1

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR Great game, I think it is now the best in the series. Very expensive if you get all the addons, would wait for sales. Whilst I have 189hrs on TWW3, TWW2 - 1k hrs, TWW1 - 400+hrs.One of the best points of this game for me is the Immortal Empires map which lets you go around the Old World and back. It is entirely possible to complete a campaign and not have to deal with some of the other factions. Granted my play is heavily biased towards the Empire (favourite faction, I rarely get bored with them), and for that I cannot recommend Thrones of Decay enough on that front as it really improves the state of play for them.For those that want something more varied you have every race from the Old World to choose from, Beastmen, Elves, Bretonnia, Dwarfs, Chaos Dwarfs, Demons, Dark Elves, Skaven (Yes yes), Greenskins, Vampires, Tomb Kings, Norsca, Warriors of Chaos and more. The mechanics are smooth, and this is a game that you can always come back to and try something new, and with teh balance tweaks they have done most of the units and combinations are viable now which is awesome. The primary downside is to get all the factions will cost you £130 just for the main games full price, however I have seen some cracking prices at sales (picking up TWW1 & TWW2 for £19.98 - pre 04/11/2024 - and £39.97 for all 3 is a BARGAIN) Whilst I own all the DLCs you could save a few pennies just picking and choosing the ones that cater to your favourite factions.Zero regrets with getting the game on release, CA have really come through in the end despite hiccups. If you are a fan of Warhammer, this game gives some great little lore drops and easter eggs, all while you rampage to bring everything under one banner.

_childDocuments_.review: Somehow, this sequel plays worse than its predecessor. The combat feels incredibly detatched, the units are hard to see, the unit outlines are incredibly translucent and difficult to make out, MULTIPLE systems that would ostensibly function, fail to... all in all, give this one a pass for now. Wait for the Grand Campaign, then wait until it's either on sale or the gameplay is patched back to game 2 levels.In terms of campaign, it's nearly-strict improvements all across the board. Diplomacy is finally interesting, the alliance system is fun, the outposts in allied settlements is a fun touch with some entertaining possibilities. Unfortunately, the colorscheme is actually intolerable and a headache to deal with.And, finally, Kislev is hot trash right now. All their units are in less-than-dwarf unit sizes with better-than-Empire stats. They do NOT play like a Human-Elf faction, they need more numbers for their regiments, they need better performance against a majority of their enemies whom are more elite and have superior numbers, and they lack a dedicated halberd unit that can counter charging monsters. Best they get are Ice Guard Glaives, which are obscenely expensive. Their lack of a dedicated combat hero, like a Bogatyr or something, a parallel to a captain of the empire, stands out horrendously. Ice Witches seem like a great idea, until you realize you're going to be fighting Demons of Chaos (Who are about as elite as it comes) and you need a general that can actually handle themselves.Something feels very off about this game. Nothing seems to feel as impactful, things don't seem to do real damage to one another unless they're melting, and overall it feels like this game is entirely new instead of an evolution of TWW2. None of the strengths of the previous game feel like they're present.

_childDocuments_.review: It is painful to write this review since i play total war games since rome total war yet here we go, again..  In order for someone to enjoy everything that this game has to offer, he has to pay 🥁🥁🥁 263€..Seriously, that's amazing that they can get out with this, but is it?Who enabled them to get this far? Well, we did it. Thinking that things will get better..With every broken release, we rewarded them with our money and they just kept going, and going without fixing any of the bugs, addressing the balance between the factions and so on.The first Warhammer total war was released back on 2016, it had its bugs yet it was a fresh installment in the franchise and most of us were exited with what was to come. Then came the first DLCs which were alarming but the "hype" was still strong.With the release of the 2nd Warhammer total war, they added a couple of factions and a new campaign and here is where it gets interesting. In every other title in the franchise that would be an expansion/DLC for the core game like the Age of Charlemagne in Attila total war yet here the majority accepted something like that and yes, it is awful. Then came the extra DLCs with additional lords that were also overpriced yet people still found my review back them as funny even if at that time i stated the obvious missing features and bugs.Now after so many years we still have (without mods):- random crashes in battles - random crashes in changing turns- awful siege battles, the outer walls are like decorations, the inner towers are like a joke and it is pretty weird since they created Empire total war and they could just place towers manned by missile troops and have extra barricades by the units in order to actually feel that you have ground control- awful battle optimization, create a doomstack of strong missile units and you are good to go even if your enemy has armored knights or infantry since the ai is weird focusing on the lord most of the time.- awful bonuses for the ai in battle map and campaign, i mean if i played against someone that uses cheats then i would just stop playing yet in almost every total war title and here there is no exception, the ai will probably beat you but only because it's cheating, so if you play against a hard ai it will not just outsmart you, it will get the bonuses and beat you, challenging isn't it? I thought that a strategy game is all about finding the most fitting strategy to overcome your opponent- no formations for the troops like shield wall, testudo, schiltron, pike phalanx, fire by rank and so on, and the long requested mix between melee and missile units which will be useful for the starting troops to counter the beasts of this world- no meaningful upgrades for the units, it feels that the experience bonuses are like a joke with no real impact in the battle, same goes for the technology buffs of the units- no visual unit upgrades by the armory like in medieval 2 total war or like in Attila through the technology tree- awful balance between the factions, no counter strategies for certain skills/abilities- very few lord in accordance with the lore of warhammer universe, i can think of almost 40 khorne heroes yet the game has 2, well, we actually  know why- poor compatibility with the mods in workshop. sometimes it's the modders fault but most of the times that comes a new patch then all of the mods need to be reworked in order to be playable- Governing systems between races are missing and the one that the empire has it's still not fixed with each electoral faction almost acting on each own without being able to allied with each other..At the end of the day, they just lost a costumer since i will never buy another of their titles if they insist on the same money grabbing  practices...

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game but one particular design choice ruins it for me. The economic rules that apply to you, do not apply to the AI. I don't know the specifics but it seems like money and income does not matter to them. While the player struggles to get a decent army, the AI attacks you with 2 full armies while only having 3 settlements or so (even on normal difficulty)Don't get me wrong, it sure is possible to win, I did a lot, but it kinda destroys the immersion for me. Before realizing this, I tried to came up with different strategies to win against an enemy faction, which was very fun. Like with smart movements, conquering there smaller settlements and try to starve them out. But it just doesn't matter to them, like it would to the player. The game forces you to play just in that one particular way to be succesful. And for me, that has little to do with an immersive strategic experience.It seems like the higher difficulties just pushes the "AI Cheating" even more instead of making the AI smarter. If everyone involved, AI or player, had the same, yet faction specific economy, this game would be a 10/10 for me and I could overlook the little flaws in diplomacy, OP legendary commanders like Gor Rok destroying an army of 1000 without even getting damage and so on. And it would be such an easy fix: just give the player the ability to set this "handicap" manually! I don't get it.

_childDocuments_.review:
Far beyond the world and its petty wars there exists a dimension of pure, malevolent magic: The Realm of Chaos. It is a terrible place, incomprehensible to the mortal mind. It whispers promises of power, but to behold it is to be seduced by it. To relinquish your soul to it. To become it.

The four Ruinous Powers rule over this place, ever seeking to slip their bonds and engulf the world in a tide of daemonic corruption. Nurgle, the plague god; Slaanesh, the lord of excess; Tzeentch, the changer of ways; and Khorne, the god of blood and slaughter.

On the border between the worlds, two mighty kingdoms stand sentinel: the stern warriors of Kislev and the vast empire of Grand Cathay. But each is beset by its own trials, and now both have cause to cross the threshold and send their armies into the Realm of Chaos.

The world stands on a precipice. A single push will plunge it into cataclysm. And there is one who schemes to achieve just that, an ancient figure who desires nothing less than to wield supreme power. But to succeed, he will need a champion...

name: Ready or Not
detailed_description: Be sure to join the Ready or Not Discord server to keep up with the latest updates, find recruits for your squad, and have a good time! Los Sueños - The LSPD reports a massive upsurge in violent crime across the greater Los Sueños area. Special Weapons and Tactics (SWAT) teams have been dispatched to respond to various scenes involving high-risk hostage situations, active bomb threats, barricaded suspects, and other criminal activities. Citizens are being advised to practice caution when traveling the city or to stay at home. It has been noted that while Los Sueños is still seen as a city where riches can be found, for many more the finer things in life are becoming less and less obtainable. “The city is sprawling with cramped high-rise apartments and decaying affordable housing, which has been exploited by the criminal underground like a malevolent parasite,” states Chief Galo Álvarez. “In a city where people are just trying to survive, lawful action from the LSPD and the LSPD SWAT team remains an integral force preventing the stretched thin social fabric in this city from snapping under this chaotic strain.” In response to the burgeoning violent crime wave inundating Los Sueños, Chief Álvarez of the LSPD has enlisted the stalwart support of David ‘Judge’ Beaumont as the Commander of the LSPD SWAT team. Shortly following this announcement, the LSPD has also confirmed active recruitment for additional talent to join this specialized tactical police unit with the mission of bringing peace back to the city. “This assignment is not for the faint of heart,” comments Commander Beaumont, “Extremists, crooked politicians, countless weapons, human trafficking, and illicit drugs and pornography… the world of policing in Los Sueños is fraught with real and harsh realities, realities that the everyday person isn’t necessarily confronted with. These are realities that you will need to navigate with your team within the proper bounds of the law or face the consequences and make matters worse.” The Los Sueños Policed Department has officially posted new details on Commander “Judge” Beaumont’s updated assignment with the LSPD SWAT team: New Expectations: Whether this is your first time in Los Sueños or not, the city has changed and so too have the tools and methods with which we conduct our work. The haunts you might have seen or heard about are re-imagined, and so have the angles with which we approach each call. Furthermore, we’ve received reports that identify at least 4 new high-risk police districts which we suspect may require future tactical intervention, plus at least 4 existing high-risk districts that underwent massive upheavals. Take Command: The role of the Commander of the LSPD SWAT is to compose their team from a large roster with unique talents, give tactical orders, meticulously plan, and carry out missions. Commanders are obligated to conduct each mission with integrity and look after their team’s mental and physical health. Officers with unaddressed deteriorating mental status may be unable to properly perform their duties or even feel compelled to quit the force. Incapacitated officers may be temporarily unavailable for missions, with the tragic prospect of death leading to a permanent loss. For SWAT Commanders in unusual circumstances based on individual choices they opt for, deadly mistakes may lead to their own permanent fatality. SWAT Team Quality Enhancement: Much anticipated improved SWAT training procedures, tactics, and experience in the LSPD has led to an overall increase in the quality and quantity of officers in our roster. Expanded tactical versatility allows our officers to take on any challenge with renewed confidence, blending coordination and independence seamlessly. There is also additional basic training now available to SWAT members to keep foundational knowledge and muscle memory in top shape. Equipment and customization: We have access to the best weapons and equipment that the LSPD can offer to fulfill our exceptionally dangerous role, including many new acquisitions. However, customization isn’t limited to the equipment we use. Through close-knit comradery while performing remarkable actions alongside the team, you’ll earn the clothes you wear, the patches on your sleeves, the artwork that may adorn your skin, and potentially even the timepiece on your wrist. Lastly, we have overhauled our headquarters' training facilities to better test our loadouts before heading out on call.

short_description: Ready or Not is an intense, tactical, first-person shooter that depicts a modern-day world in which SWAT police units are called to defuse hostile and confronting situations.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this game enough. It is a very realistic portrayal of close quarters combat, down to extremely minute details, such as entry and exit wounds - even arterial bleeds if someone is shot in the neck. This game is best enjoyed with friends, but can also be enjoyed with an AI team that you can customize. If you don't have training, you can certainly learn in this game, but they are lessons that are learnt in blood, so learning can be frustrating. If you are prior Military/LE, your training will certainly help. Do the little things that you might have been taught. The AI act very erratically, and the second that you might forget to check your rear or stop paying attention, you will pay for it. I absolutely love that. Real life isn't easy, don't make this game easy.Side note, I'm surprised that there aren't nearly the amount of glitches that I had in a triple A shooter like Battlefield 2042. They are actually very few and far between, and I don't really notice them often - mostly, it's the occasional weapon glitching through the floor or wall. This game has enormous potential - it's truly a worthy successor to SWAT 4, and I think with some tweaking, additional content, and tools for content creators to make maps, weapons, gear and etc; This game could absolutely grow beyond the Developers original dream. My main gripe is mostly the AI, for instance when you spawn on a map such as the meth house, or port hoken, and a guy spawns in the front yard and immediately starts shooting at you. It's kind of immersion breaking, and annoying - considering there should be a Police cordon after the SWAT team is called in the first place, and this can get annoying when you get spawnkilled multiple times in a row. The civilian AI can be pretty janky too, and it can be really annoying when they run away from you, and open up a door with bad guys in it that come out shooting. The AI can vary in terms of effectiveness too, and can either be really stupid, or pinpoint accurate with split second response times, and will wallbang you through a wall when there was no way for them to see you.Friendly AI could definitely use some work as well - sometimes they will go to their points of domination, sometimes they will just go through the center of a room, and might cross in front of you as you're engaging a threat. Other times, they follow so close behind you in a train, they might trap you in a room. Less than lethal options definitely need refinement. There really almost isn't a point in using them - the Stinger grenades and the flashbangs are identical in function, but I seem to get shot less when using flashbangs, so I might as well use them instead. CS gas should be extremely useful, but is more of a burden, because you can't see anything, and the area of effect is very small. So usually, you can't see anything, and you're getting shot outside of the gas cloud. The Pepperball gun also seems to only work for a couple seconds, so if you're not shooting a suspect continuously, they will immediately start shooting before distance can be closed. Pepper spray and tasers are really only effective for non-compliant civilians, but a muzzle thump to the melon works just as well - so there really isn't any point in bringing them either. You'll find that the most useful tools are just the Mirrorgun, Door Ram, Breaching Shotgun, Flashbangs, and Ballistic Shield in certain circumstances. For the most part, it's just not rewarding enough to use less than lethals; Sure, you might get more points, but the risk of getting shot is so high, it's just not worth it in my opinion. As a consequence, capturing 2 armed suspects can really be a pain in the ass at times, especially if your flashbangs land behind something that blocks the effect for a suspect, which can literally be any piece of furniture in a room.Other than that, I think this game is amazing - and simply just needs polishing and additional content, but even now, the replayability is extraordinary, I can't praise the developers enough for their attention to detail. This game is worth every dollar. P.S. If you're in the mood to laugh, put a C2 charge on a door when a suspect is right behind it. The result is hilarious every single time.

_childDocuments_.review: Ready or Not is very much a successor to the PVE focused tactical shooters from the early 2000s to the early 2010s (SWAT, Rainbow Six), and with 1.0's release certain pro's and cons start to shine through. the short summary is, the game is well worth a buy, especially if you grew up playing tactical shooters.  there are some glaring issues that prevent me from showing AAA developers that RoN did what they claim to do but better and with much more polish.- Gunplay, the guns in the game sound damn near perfect, the animations are smooth and quick, and the variety of guns and attachments means you can play through the campaign twice and never use the exact same loadout.- Sound design, the sounds in the game are crisp and clear when they need to be and unobtrusive when they need to be. enemy footsteps and dialogue very clearly helps place suspects in the maps, and environmental noise i.e. planes, helicopters and ambient neighborhood noises never drown out important sounds from the npcs on the map.- environmental story telling, In each of the maps (even before 1.0) there was always a ton of environmental story telling (sometimes to a fault). Trying my best to not give spoilers each of the maps from the clutter that serves as obstacles to navigating the map helps to tell the player exactly what is going on at that location. Some maps will be continuations of stories started on other maps (thank you come again to twisted nerve to carriers of the vine). However as this is a game involving some very horrible people some of the subjects can be heavy, ranging from Drug dealers  to  (guys i found Megan!)-Character Customization, the cosmetics in the game are perfectly tied to progression through the campaign missions and feature a variety of options so you can cosplay your favorite military operators just like a real police officer.- The enemy AI, I really want to like the AI in the game, however they need a ton of work.  single suspect seems to have some very intense special forces training, because i have never seen a twitch streamer and his entourage snap onto a team of SWAT officers and lay accurate fire with zero hesitation. While I myself have never been shot by a bean bag or a real bullet i feel like most people would stop and keel over after being shot (even with body armor), but not RoN suspects, they'll regularly take 3 or 4 shots to the neck and chest and keep going. That contrasts greatly with the player being sent reeling (blurry screen and exaggerated flinching) from just 1 shot. please VOID make getting shot mean something to the suspects and maybe instill a desire to not get shot into the NPCs as well, as many suspects will also stand back up and start fighting again after surrendering with 5 guns pointed at them.- Gun Handling. While the guns in RoN sound great and look great, they suffer from the same thing a lot of shooters use in their mechanics for balance in PVP, over-exaggerated recoil. Do you really expect us to belive that SWAT officers with multiple years of experience and (hopefully) 100s of hours of weapons training is letting their rifle jump as much as they do in RoN? combine this with the lackluster bonuses provided by grips and muzzle devices and you'll be picking your attachments mostly for aesthetic purposes only (aside from suppressors those are pretty necessary if you're trying to keep the suspects from going even more agro).- S Ranks. Achieving an S rank on a mission requires that no one dies in mission (yes even the overly aggressive and tanky suspects) Granted this is more of a nitpick, but i want to unlock the tattoo options so this is staying a con until the AI is better or they lessen the requirements to get S rank.- Your Team's AI. the ironic part to this is a couple days ago i watched VOID's video talking about the improvements they made to your AI teammates for 1.0, how the team will move out of the way to give you a clear sight line for shooting, and how the AI will organically move to allow the player to better navigate around rooms. Too bad those changes don't seem to be here yet. 10 missions into the game and AI will complain that I'm in the way when moving to stack up (despite claims that team lead can join the stack in any position and AI will rearrange to accomodate), teammates will crowd the player as you check small closets and bathrooms (I love you too guys but i'd like to leave the literal poo covered bathroom.). So Ready or Not is an extremely solid tactical FPS, definitely worth a buy if you like shooters and want a very compelling PVE experience. The only issue is that there is a plethora of small (TBF these could be technical nightmares to try and correct I am not a game developer so I don't know) issues that keep it from being outstanding. some minor tweaks here and there and you have a solid contender for GOTY 2024. With that out of the way I need to go bring order to chaos again.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, review update.  Now that the game is "out", it's gotten worse, lol.  The enemy AI have been given so many new abilities since my last review, to the point that they are over powered.  Then there was an update that gave them the ability to react to any amount of the players hitbox, even if the only part of the hitbox visible is like, your pinky or something, the enemies will just start blasting through the wall at you and track you for like, 5 seconds or something.The lighting in the game has gotten worse, a lot of areas are either way too bright or way too dark, a no real in between.  The player has gotten nothing new, as far as game mechanics to put them on the same level as the enemies you combat.  Like, my biggest gripe is when the enemies before wanted to take cover, they'd just crouch behind an object, similar to what the player has access to.  Now they have a full cover animation set, and can even do blind fire, which the player can't do.  They can now even go through small gaps in the map, which the player can't do, as well as crawl through vents on some maps.  Didn't expect this game to get so out of hand.Also, as far as a cover system for a first person shooter, I'll reference you to Rainbow Six Vegas.  Ya, not recommended in its current state, wish SWAT 4 was on steam, at least I got it on GOG, lol.Old Review:  Dec 25, 2021-♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love this game.  I look forward to playing this every day, it's so fun.  I used to play SWAT 4, a butt load back in the day, and this game fills its shoes so well.  This game is easily a spiritual successor to the SWAT game series.  I even went through the effort of rebinding my keys to match how I had them in SWAT 4, it's really amazing.I wish the developers the best of luck on getting this game all polished up, and look forward to the finished game.  I do hope they add more police factions to play as, would be sweet.  Hell, even a "First Responder" mode would be sweet.  Like only pistols, and a two handed weapon from a police cruiser, no additional equipment.We'll see, for now, amazing game as it stands.

_childDocuments_.review: Please for the love of god, fix the stress system on single player. For one, there is no reason to limit the number of cops I can put in therapy at any given time... other than to fluff the gameplay time and add frustration. Second, the stress system is inconsistent, especially when considering members of the team have the SBAGS perk which should mitigate negative effects, but they dont. Third, adding to the inconsistency of the stress system members can either flatout leave the force or get forced into therapy/time off. Both of those outcomes suck. Like I can lose a member of my team completely after grinding to unlock their perk just because they were over stressed from watching me get head eyes'd the previous run. The other outcome breaks your own game with the therapy limit giving me a free therapy session randomly. I just think the whole idea was executed poorly and adds nothing but frustration. ♥♥♥♥, even firing a cop stresses out my whole line up, why?! I'm the only one who should be getting stressed, I'm getting one tapped through walls and my team is doing random things and not following simple instructions or getting glitched on an obstacle. The stress system flat out needs to go or be completely re-looked at. Like I have the entire city of Los Suenos with multiple medical facilities everywhere yet I can only use three therapists at one time. Cool realism. Wall bangs and over-clocked AI with laser beam accuracy are a thing. Ready or Not is still good, overall concept is awesome. Some things need to go, others need fixin', rant over. Actually no, rant continues. Do the AI characters even reload? I swear if they do it's like they have the slight of hand perk from Call of Dooky. No time between volleys at times, just 80's action movie quality shooting going on here. They run around full speed with full autos, laser precise accuracy. It's infuriating, no wonder there are a handful of mods already to adjust this whacky crap. What's up with the NVGs? Like they look awesome, you even implemented IR devices for them, but the game doesnt seem to need them. Like nearly every mission is in daylight or bright building and it's well lit in the darker areas. There is no random time of day adjustment per level so it really stays consistently stupid. The AI can track you just as easily in the dark as they can in daytime, like they have Predator vision and can sense my heat signature. The very few night operations are so bright even to the naked eye and it's really disappointing considering how well done the NVG's are. But yeah the maps are so bright as a baseline and it makes the dim chem lights a stupid function as well. Like there's even a mod for them to be brighter which shouldnt be necessary. Your team places them all over the place in these super bright environments and all it looks like is a slim green line on the ground. Can hardly notice the ambient lighting from it's source. Seems like a wasted resource for UE4. With all the coding for lighting being generated by the AI when they drop chem lights everywhere, causes more strain on the machine running the game. It's a shame that you guys couldnt get the night time and dark environments done correctly, or at least cause the AI to interact differently depending on their environment. This game is good but should still be in early access with all the issues I've noticed. I even have encounters where certain AI entities will not have a torso and will just be a floating head with hands until you look at them from a specified angle. _childDocuments_.review: While I do like the game, it's not playable in the current state unless you really really really really really like the idea of playing slow counter-strike. Actually, no, that's wrong; It's only slow for you, all suspects will lean like boxers as they sidestrafe while putting bullets into you with incredible accuracy- Crackheads, gang bangers, terrorists, narcos, all of them might as well be tier one specops in the unmodded game. This has been a problem for ages, but it's an incredible issue after 1.0, especially when this issue has been on the to-fix list for so long. The developers seem to have trouble understanding the appeal of swat-like games. The gunfights, while fun, shouldn't be the focus of the game. The reason SWAT 4 was so beloved is because it was immensely satisfying to breach rooms, arrest perps, and order your team around. As it stands, breaching rooms is impossible due to the aimbot AI, arresting perps is difficult due to lack of consistency with grenades, stuns, and intimidation, and ordering your team around is an exercise in defeat as they fail the most basic tasks such as throwing grenades at the deploy marker, switching to a lethal sidearm if they run out of less lethal ammunition, rushing forward into open doorways to secure dead bodies and weapons, and assaulting criminals without being ordered to. You should be able to arrest some criminals just by staring at them angrily, especially the low level thieves and drug addicts. Why is it that when a group of five massive, heavily armed men in tactical gear are staring at these one-off criminals they suddenly decide that now is the perfect moment to throw away their lives? Is this supposed to be part of the game's flat, tired political statement? Is this what was based on the police interviews the developers said they did? If it makes the game frustrating, it should be revised on until it's fun and respects the objective of the game: Arrests come first, shootouts are a last resort. As it stands, shootouts are your only option unless you like dying.The missions are also awkward as hell, with many of them having seemingly been changed behind the scenes for unknown reasons. For example: Why does an obese, childish, pedophilic twitch streamer have a gang of seven heavily armed thugs running around half of the apartment block? Is he a streamer, or is he a Judge Dredd crime lord? I remember the reveal trailer for that mission showing him alone, and the official channel stating it would be the game's new introductory mission. Now it's just another killhouse, like every other mission has become with the new AI. When SWAT 4 is such a well-documented and beloved game, you would think more care would have been taken to learn from that game's strengths and weaknesses. So far, the most I've seen to connect the pair of them is "bring order to chaos" and "you're in my way, sir". And yes, despite what I've seen some people say on forums and comments, this is a SWAT sequel under a different name, saying that "it's ready or not, not swat" doesn't fix the problems with the game, you're just being dense.All in all, horribly rushed out 1.0 releases are a plague on the games industry and this example is no different. I still like the game once i installed mods that have fixed the developer's shoddy work, but I've been playing SWAT games since I was a little kid, and this game is doing everything it can to make me regret buying it out of nostalgia and love for tactical shooters.

_childDocuments_.review: An awesome love letter to fans of Sierra's SWAT 3/4. While it IS first person shooter, you have to get the COD mindset out of your head when stepping into this. Game relies heavily, sometimes unfairly so, on law enforcement's rules of engagement and  requires the player to at least give warnings / not fire if suspect surrenders / watch for civilians, etc. RoN offers many neat and "buffy" law enforcement customization options as rewards for getting certain grades in completing missions. Your squads come with their own sets of game changing perks as well which adds more to the gun. If you're looking for slow and methodical "thinking man's" shooter, this is it. The active mod community has some neat stuff in there, too! Check them out.While I've enjoyed the game a ton and still do, there are some negatives...Your squad can be "moody". I've found that the AI will just not address suspects 10 feet away from them, not cuff them, or just leave a surrendered suspect / civilian and walk by them sometimes. I've walked back and forth to see what they'd do and sometimes they'd cuff / secure or just ...ignore them. Your squad will sometimes literally stand in the line of fire and you'll watch them eat a ton of bullets and (sadly) go down.Suspects feel like they have "wall hacks" and sometimes (not always!) I've been shot through walls.That being said, no game is perfect and if you want something different than running and gunning, this was a good time!Hope that helps! PS- congrats on the promotion, Chief Alvarez

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Everything in my old negative review has now been addressed or reduced to the point where it is no longer an issue, can be remedied in some other way, or that I am confident is going to be fixed completely.There was a point where I thought Ready or Not was riding on the coat tails of SWAT 4 nostalgia and was headed down the path of yet another failed "slow paced realistic tactical shooter", but the development team is really buckling down and getting ♥♥♥♥ done, and for once I am quite optimistic that Ready or Not may just turn out to be what we wanted.In my old negative review I went on at length about artistic direction and how I was disappointed how RoN was taking its story. I was worried that it would be  to market itself as dark and gritty, but was too afraid of being genuine and would instead toe the line of what is acceptable. RoN has gone above and beyond in this regard, especially with the new missions they've promised. The team seems truly committed to their artistic vision, something that I was too stupid to see until they had the time to work on RoN's front-end.One complaint that I still have, however, is how much RoN seems to be leaning towards multiplayer/Co-op play at the expense of the singleplayer experience. Something reflected in the level design. With how colossal RoN's map layouts can be, how limited your equipment slots are, and how stupid the SWAT AI can be, maps can be frustratingly difficult to play because you simply don't have enough fingers to plug all the holes around you if you don't have a fully manned team. I hope we get more maps like 4U, Voll Health House and Sullivan's Slope which don't take upwards of 20 minutes to complete, and can be comfortably done solo or with a small team.

_childDocuments_.review: A true spiritual successor to SWAT 4. Game is pretty polished, albeit with a few more bugs left to iron out, not related to core gameplay however. It's the perfect blend of being able to clear a mission either tactically or by just having fun and messing around, and unlike SWAT 4, the score shows you how "true-to-real-life" you were. Devs are amazing, transparent, and hard-working to bring amazing updates.  It made me happy to see that a multiplayer game released in 2022 doesn't have unlockable content, loot crates or a battle pass. All content is available from the get go. While supporter edition does give you a multicam uniform for the operators plus a few guns, I view them all as cosmetic upgrades, and just as an extra thing to make supporter edition worth it's cost. In my view, supporter edition is worth it just for supporting the devs alone, not to mention early access to updates and a private discord server for earlier access to news about upcoming updates. All in all, it's an amazing game, and definitely worth giving it a shot if you're into tactical gameplay or messing around with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: Ever played the SWAT games? No? Ever wanted to? Well than you are in luck. This game is a spiritual successor, beautifully crafted, and well excecuted.This game is a slow paced, first person shooter with an emphasis on tactics, and high damage fire arms. The AI for single player is very well done, although they sometimes glitch through a wall when stacked up, or have small issues with their pathing once in a blue moon, is very responsive to your commands and will excecute them without hesitation. They will even drop a hostile faster than I had expected. This game has a fantastic sense of atmosphere allowing for serious immersion. From the level of sound design, to the guns, and lighting.The optimization is on point, I have had yet to have any dips in frame rate at max graphics with my 1070 and I7 7700, and 32gbs of DDR4 RAM. (I struggle at times with games like Squad or Assassins Creed Valhalla).Now for the part yall are waiting for: The GUNS!!!Every gun has serious punch, from sound to damage. Even the hostile AI guns, ranging from glocks, to Tech 9's, and even M4A1's and Sawed Off double barrel shotguns will drop you hard. But so will your guns drop them hard. When I fired my pump shotty for the first time I jumped out of my skin for a second, as I was not expecting how loud and punchy it was gonna be, now I cannot wait to fire it every time it is in my hands. Most games dumb down the sound of firearms, but not this one!And a really good hint for beginners, your MirrorCam is your best friend, Check EVERY DOOR for booby traps. Good luck, have fun, and always keep your head on a swivel!

The enemies have the aim of genetically enhanced super soldiers that can sometimes apparently see through walls and concrete pillars. A for instance was, myself and two AI are looking directly down a hallway guns aimed, and a douche stumbles into said hallway not knowing where we are but still managing to getting one shot off killing me instantly. For those of you out there saying that's realistic, I call ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ especially for just how often it happens making a 30 min mission a total wash. These crack shot crackhead enemy commandos also have a will of iron making them insanely difficult to take alive, even after taking a hit from rib shattering bean bag round and having several guns on them they will take the first opportunity to bust a knife out of no where and carve your ass up. _childDocuments_.review: Oh my, oh dear, it's really damn good... Beyond just how lovingly crafted the game's visuals and ambiance are and how just completely immersed I feel every time I boot the game, I gotta say: I have steeled nerves from literal tens of thousands of hours of PVP in realistic clutch-oriented shooters like R6: Siege and Escape from Tarkov and this game gets my adrenaline PUMPING while I'm literally fighting against COMPUTER OPPONENTS. That should tell you all you have to know about how absolutely dialed in this game's difficulty is. There is nothing about Ready Or Not that pulls its punches. Some of the content is genuinely extremely bleak, and is depicted with grueling accuracy. One scenario is a school shooting, and another is a terrorist mass shooting at a hospital. To say the visuals and dialogue in these scenes aren't pretty is putting it very, very lightly. And yet, despite the sobering subject matter, it's still somehow also a fun tactical PVE shooter for gun nerds to LARP with the boys in. It's sleek and it's really fun and addictive to play, with lots of challenges and cosmetics to unlock that give it really great replayability after you're done just experiencing it. It plays just fine solo, too, you can play squad leader and do the missions with some really well-designed AI, plus there's a cool Commander mode that tosses some department sim elements into the mix for those who like a run-based approach with more permanent consequences for failure.Some downsides to note: if you're not playing solo then I would recommend 4-6 players to get the intended difficulty, and the the AI you play with definitely needs some work. Like i said the design is great, the command menu is fantastic, but the AI suffers from a lot of bugs, for example: poor pathing that gets them/you stuck on things, reacting very slowly/not at all to enemies entering areas they're covering, and having to give them the same order 2+ times before they move, to name a few. However, as long as you don't play unreasonably fast or make the AI do the heavy lifting for you, the system will generally serve you well and can expected to be improved upon in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: For a game that's "fully out" and charging you 50€ instead of 35€ as it did before, the game sure feels rough. I don't mind the obtuse and unintuitive controls, but my issues are mainly with the game's stupid AI - enemies can sense and shoot you through walls, have crazy aim, and the time from them reaching for their gun and already firing at you is less than half a second. Even at the first missions that are supposed to be "entry level" difficulty. Oh right, game has no difficulty. Not even the "realistic" mod that you can download can salvage this.I've played Swat4 before, and that game didn't use to reach such levels of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. In addition, I noticed that you have a fairly decent range of guns that you can switch between... but the game doesn't have any information on them. No weapon stats... some of them will tell you what sort of ammo they use. Is that good? Is it bad? Yes? No? Why? Why not? You have to go by with the descriptions of each gun and accept it as the absolute truth, but you see no stats whatsoever. No information how much rounds a magazine can hold. A revolver usually has 6 bullets in the drum. Some have 5. How much does the magnum have? I don't know. Equip it and take it to the gun range I guess. What are the assault rifles fire rates like? I'unno. Fire modes? Damage values? Nah, you don't get that information. ♥♥♥♥ you. You don't need to know it. But it'll make you second guess yourself if you've made the wrong decision when you see that hobo over yonder run off after you shot him 5 times in the back with JHP (hollow point) rounds in the back with an assault rifle.When you take fire from the enemies (if you're lucky and you don't get one-tapped in the head from across the map) will usually make you bleed. But when you shoot at them, they don't bleed (or bleed out) for that matter. No idea why this mechanic is only a one-way thing.I cannot in good faith recommend this game. Not until they add some sort of difficulty slider for the AI. Being sensed and shot through walls and other solid objects is genuinely unfun.Edit: Since this game has an ingame mod browser, I've tried downloading a couple mods; the same works via a mod.io integration. The few mods I tried to download are for AI behavior, a mod that makes it so the shield doesn't get cracks in the bulletproof glass pane when shot, and I can assure you that none of these mods work. Shield glass gets cracked the same way, and AI can still spot you from across the map and shoot you through impossible angles. This game has the potential to be fun but is fundamentally broken.

_childDocuments_.review: It's an extremely detailed (for a game that's still under early access) tactical SWAT team simulator.From things like proper use of flashlight (if you light the window from the wrong angle it will blind you),through completely unpredictable behavior of enemies like  which makes you stay on your toes the entire time and treat everyone as potential hostile (and the game heavily penalize you for killing someone you were not supposed to), to (graphic warning) .You also get a big collection of around 60 different items to choose your loadouts from, to prepare for the tactical scenario you expect to face (different kinds of ammo, mirrors to check under doors, infrared googles, battering rams, lockpick guns, c2 explosives and lethal and non-lethal guns and many others), so you can fully customise your approach to any given situation.All the afromentioned things, make the game feel like realistic yet tasteful simulator of what police SWAT work actually is.The biggest flaw as of now is the friendly AI, which constantly get stuck at worst and do the whole job in your stead at best, not leaving you any enemies to fight with.I also don't agree with comments that call for nerfing of enemy AI, while the enemies are unreasonably strong and have godlike aim, the whole point of the game is to not let them shoot first, so IMO nerfing would made the game too easy and take out the need for tactical approach.In summary the strongest point of the game is it's realism, but is most fun you will have with coop players,or if you're playing the game alone, make the friendly AI wait at spawn, otherwise they will ruin your experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I've had my eye on Ready or Not for a few months now, and I have to say I've thoroughly enjoyed the 50-ish hours I've put into playing this. Granted, there are a few gameplay issues, but overall the game performs just spectacularly, and as advertised. It really takes me back to my days as a teenager when I religiously played the hell out of Rainbow Six: Rogue Spear.Some issues I've encountered:- Random crashing- AI squadmates getting stuck on doors when given the order to breach- Enemy weapons disappearing or getting stuck behind objects so you can't secure them as evidence- AI squadmates responding poorly to enemy combatants (looping the callout to surrender or pacify, despite the suspect firing at them - or just outright being blissfully unaware of an enemy shooting into the room)Some praises:- This game is 100% better with real-life squadmates. It really challenges the players to focus on concise and effective communication between each other.- The mods available on Nexusmods really improve the overall gameplay, and I've had a blast trying out player-created maps, weapons, optics, and utility addons.- The developers don't shy away from disturbing content. It's refreshing to see this level of realism in a game, and it makes you think that yes, while this is a work of fiction, there are absolutely parallels to real-word crimes and the horrors that come with them (Mass shootings, bomb threats, human trafficking, and even some darker subject matter).I bought this game when it was on sale (I believe it was 10-20% off), but I would gladly pay full price even for Early Access. With the wealth of content available from the modding community and the devs (who should be lauded for their transparency with regular progress update videos/blog posts) constantly working to polish this game into a final product, I expect many more hours of gameplay from Ready or Not.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game for an early access release. If you ever played SWAT 4 and liked it, you'll definitely like this game. Weapon mechanics are superb (only thing I could ask for is more nuanced weapon customization), movement and handling is good, gunfights feel brutal and violent. Could use some smaller maps that are faster scenarios. The ambiance is just amazing, the scenarios have dark (but grounded and realistic) stories and details. The sound of this game is just amazing, hearing people clear rooms down the hall and hearing shots go off at a distance (but not far away enough to be safe) just puts you on edge. The suspects yelling "Eat some of this!" then shooting through the walls of a house just shows the danger of this kind of combat. There are funny moments to be had as well for some reprieve from the tension. Not to mention, this game is super fun with friends, I was already enjoying the challenge with just AI, but playing with my friends made it just that much better.My main gripes are just that the AI can be very good or absolutely brain dead, some maps feel too big almost (sometimes the SWAT team gets called to a 1 story house with 1 or 2 suspects), and some of the customization options don't make sense from a realism perspective. On the AI - Everyone has hit on it pretty well, the gist is that they can either react with inhuman speed and don't really give you the opportunity for a fight to be drawn out. Definitely makes for a challenge sometimes, unfortunately not in the right way. Maps being too big - Some maps feel too big to be played out quickly. I don't mean sprinting through the map, I mean it just takes nearly 30 minutes to methodically move through and clear the map. Even then, you might spend a few extra minutes walking around a bunch of dead and handcuffed people because you forgot to report an arrest. Some smaller maps that would take ~10-15 minutes to complete the entire scenario would definitely help this. I don't think these smaller maps would be without replay-ability due to the somewhat randomness each map already has.Some of the customization options don't make sense from a realism perspective - I know balance is supposed to be a thing, however for claiming to be dedicated to realism some of the options don't make much sense. Why do I have to choose a taser over a handgun when many times an officer in the real world would likely have the option to have both? Why can't I have both an IR laser/Visible laser and a white light on my gun at the same time? Why does someone have the same amount of ammo with an SMG as a rifle (SMGs use smaller and lighter ammo, and smaller and lighter mags)? Why can't I add more or less mags/ammunition to my kit? Just small gripes that I think borrowing features from some other games could fix (Ground Branch kit and gun customization namely). All in all, the gripes don't necessarily make the game unplayable in it's current state and that's something to be said where a lot of the times some of the games coming out nowadays these things could ruin the experience. Don't get me wrong, there's some work to be done by the devs to get this game to be a gem. If this is just EA, I'm beyond excited to see where this game goes and what kind of work the devs can put into this as there is massive potential in this.  It's already going in the right direction.Easy 9/10 for potential and current content as only an EA title.Great graphics, great atmosphere, challenging (work as a team and pay attention to details or die), good gun play, and above all, tons of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game *IF* you enjoy tactical shooters. This is one of those games where you will get severely punished and have a very bad time if you come into it thinking you're playing Call of Duty. The AI are highly skilled, you are not invincible, and your squad dies if you tell them to do stupid things. It's true that the game isn't perfect. There are occasional instances of AI enemies seeing through hazards and obstacles, but your AI squad mates generally can too. Your squad won't always get their flashbang throws on the money and that can be annoying. This next thing isn't a bug per se, but it's also true if you've seen people say that sometimes you can pop a suspect in the chest like 3 times and they just keep coming. I don't think it's that big a problem, but it can affect immersion in a minor way on occasion.Overall, this game excels at a lot of things. The audio/visual experience is pretty stunning. The situations you will find yourself in feel real. The best way to describe the gameplay experience is long periods of tense silence interrupted by brief moments of terrifying chaos. When you clear a room, your strategy and execution count. It's you or the other guy, every time. Attempting to subdue instead of eliminate comes with risks, just like in real life. The maps are generally quite large, filled with lots of fatal funnels and plenty of open flanks. The equipment available to you gives you a LOT of freedom to contend with those challenges, and it's a lot of fun figuring out how you're going to safely breach and clear a large space without losing anyone.But just to repeat to anyone seriously looking to buy--it's not a run and gun shooter. You will have to take your time to succeed, and a lot of players don't have the patience for this.

_childDocuments_.review: Update after release. Devs fixed AI companions a bit. At least they become much more responsive and can clear interconnected open spaces in one go. They arrest suspects on their own and grab guns on the floor, that's a relief. They don't react to gunshots near them. They don't move without orders. They magically start acting by themselves after player is dead. Wonder why I can't order them to simply proceed on their own while I'm alive.CQB maps are good, you can clear them room by room and I like them. Some of the maps have lots of open spaces with lots of openings. And you don't have sniper coverage like in SWAT 4. You have 5 men and supposed to clear an area of two football fields with dozens of potential ambush points and 20+ heavily armed gang members.Bots are the biggest pain in the game. They fixed their accuracy a little. Chance to hit you heavily depends on weapon type and range. But not the enemy type. They have different skins, but they all act the same. Like seasoned soldiers. Bots cannot be suppressed, ignore wounds, able to spray and pray and still hit you from 300+ meters. Incapacitate equals kill. You can hit the leg of suspect with 5-6 rounds because he ignores wounds, incapacitate him and still fail objective to arrest him.All of that leads me to unfortunate conclusion. It's not a police game, it's a shooter. Good aiming and reaction always beats tactical approach. If you want single-player experience like SWAT4, you won't get this here. This game is multiplayer oriented. That's why there are lots of gunmen on each map, everyone shoots without hesitation and maps are designed in a way to split players across map so they won't get in each other's way. I even have annoying countdowns before start while playing solo. Why? I'm all alone here. Basically, it's CS against bots with lots of useless tactical gadgets.I mostly play single-player games. Don't recommend this game for single-player.

_childDocuments_.review: "Ready or Not" is a tactical first-person shooter that has quickly garnered attention for its intense realism and strategic depth. Developed by VOID Interactive, the game plunges players into the gritty world of a SWAT team tasked with defusing hostile situations in urban environments. With its focus on authenticity and team-based tactics, "Ready or Not" offers a compelling experience for fans of hardcore tactical shooters.Realistic Tactical Gameplay: "Ready or Not" excels in its portrayal of realistic SWAT operations. The game emphasizes tactics, planning, and precision over run-and-gun shooting. Players must carefully coordinate with their team to breach rooms, use cover effectively, and manage threats with a level of caution that mirrors real-life counter-terrorism operations. This commitment to realism extends to the game's ballistic mechanics and the handling of weapons, providing an immersive and challenging experience.Detailed Environments and High Stakes: Each mission in "Ready or Not" is set in a meticulously crafted environment that can range from tight office buildings to sprawling residential areas. The scenarios are designed to keep players on edge, with unpredictable threats and high-stakes decisions that can significantly impact the outcome of each mission. The level design not only adds to the game’s tension but also enhances replayability, as different tactics can be applied on repeated playthroughs.Robust Team Coordination Features: Communication is key in "Ready or Not," and the game supports this with robust communication tools and commands that can be issued to both AI teammates and human players. The ability to give detailed orders allows for precise tactical executions, and when playing with others, the game encourages a level of cooperation and communication that is deeply rewarding.Immersive Audiovisual Experience: The sound design in "Ready or Not" is exceptional, with realistic audio cues that can help players identify enemy movements, gunfire from different weapons, and environmental interactions. Visually, the game employs dynamic lighting and detailed textures that enhance the atmosphere and tension of the gameplay. The interplay of shadow and light not only looks great but also plays a functional role in the tactical gameplay.Engaging and Varied Game Modes: Beyond the standard mission-based campaign, "Ready or Not" offers a variety of game modes that challenge players in different ways. Whether it's conducting a raid under a strict time limit or handling a rapidly unfolding hostage situation, the game provides numerous scenarios that test tactical skills and decision-making under pressure.ConclusionIn conclusion, "Ready or Not" is a standout entry in the tactical shooter genre, offering an experience that is both challenging and rewarding. Its commitment to realism, combined with excellent level design and communication features, makes it a must-play for fans of tactical gameplay. The game demands sharp thinking, tight teamwork, and a strategic approach to each mission, making every successful operation feel like a true accomplishment. Whether you're a tactical shooter veteran or a newcomer to the genre, "Ready or Not" provides a deep, engaging experience that pushes the boundaries of what tactical games can offer.

_childDocuments_.review: There isn't a lot of content here yet. The civilians/criminals don't have many lines and they get repetitive quickly. The bots can get stuck in small areas, which there are a lot of. For example, in the drug house level my bots get often confused when I tell them to breach a door in the compact area to the left of the front door where the two small rooms and bathroom is. I told a bot to breach with a charge and my bots were not smart enough to move and a bot killed a friendly bot standing next to the charge. Often times in this room the bots will not follow breaching commands as well because they can't path. The gameplay for most modes boils down to:-Mirrorgun door for traps/hostiles/civilians-Tell bots to breach with different equipment-Clear room-Walk around and handcuff people hearing the same 3 lines of dialougeI have not played co-op maybe that is more fun, but overall the enemy AI doesn't put up much of a fight once stunned obviously so I think you would run into the same tedium of mirror-banging-clearing every door in the building. Maybe they need to make enemy bots wander through doors more so you don't feel safe mirrorgunning every door? I think that improving the atmosphere would go a long way, adding more dialogue, making the different squad members have personality and banter. So far everything feels muted. Nothing here is really bad it's just not exciting and it is repetitive.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Good update, the only thing that needs to really needs to be done is a slight AI Nerf to enemy AI, and one slight rework to SWAT AI1.0 update was 100% worth the wait, the new maps all have an incredibly good atmosphere and set the tone really well with both great sound design, as well as an IMMENSE amount of detail on every single new map.Overall this update has done well with the gunplay, though I sometimes feel like suspects take more shots than they should, it has most definitely improved from the last few updates where I could literally put a 12 gauge slug into a suspects head and they would shrug it off like an average Tuesday. 7.62 seems like it has more kick now aswell which is good considering the recoil of such a calibre.As for nonlethals I now actually feel a reliable usage of beanbag shotguns, they actually seem to stagger the enemy now which at least in my experience had been an issue which led to me delegating all non-lethal operations solely to the VKS, Now I actually see a reason to have beanbags utilises as while the VKS is more consistent stun, the beanbag has more of an impact on forcing a suspect to surrenderI want to note that I both agree with, and don't agree with the taser being added as equipment instead of a secondary, on a good note. Its alot nicer to have a nonlethal besides a taser, on a bad note. AI Will draw their secondaries which can ruin an S tier attempt (they will even draw them and die if they have no secondary ammo but more on this later)The sound design has gotten SIGNIFICANTLY Better! I can actually tell where suspects are coming from at all times, which was definitely an issue before 1.0 as there would be times where audio would come from different angles from which the suspect was actually pushing you from. In my time of playing since the full release I have not encountered this a single time!I'm not even sure where to start with this one, the map design in 1.0 is frankly, staggering. All of the new maps are amazingly detailed, with great sound design that really fits the tone of every single map, The new maps have a great mix of CQB Areas as well as open areas needing either a tactical approach or pinpoint accuracy. Overall 10/10 on the new maps.Also the new station is a significant improvement.Overall the new UI for weapon loadout customisation is much better in my opinion, it doesn't take long to get to, and is overall just more simplistic with less alternate menus than before. There's not really much more to it than that more of a QOL thing The swat AI has come a long way in this new update, now assisting in arrests and cleaning up evidence, this is an extremely welcome change especially with the AI now being more competent and having overall better aim and pathing.However, There is a minor issue which I have found to be quite annoying. This issue is the AI running out of primary ammo and always swapping to secondaries, even when secondary has no ammo. This can be a major issue for nonlethal runs when you want to stop your SWAT AI from killing suspects to achieve that perfect rank S on the mission, they will either just straight up swap to the pistol, stand still and die, or if the pistol has ammo they will swap and kill an enemy, thus invalidating the S rank. This is a very niche issue but I would like to see it addressed So overall I believe the Suspect ai has become slightly too strong for three reasons,1. Suspects love to wallbangIve already noticed on numerous occasions, the ai will see me for a mere second, run behind cover, and proceed to perfectly wallbang me without much issue even if I move from the location I was originally sighted at. This is extremely annoying especially in cramped areas where its not always possible to hit a quick one tap on a suspect. Or in areas with multiple suspects where you are able to hit one, but the other uses that time to get behind a wall and BAM, your dead before you can realise he was shooting you through a wall.2. Suspect accuracy and response timeI also have a slight gripe with the suspects accuracy and response time, I find they are extremely accurate even from long ranges which IMO doesnt fit a majority of the suspects we fight, the only ones I would say would be befitting of the stats the current suspects have would be the "left behind" as they are EX Military. 3. Unwillingness to surrenderNow hear me out, nonlethals work great against suspects trying to get them to back down, but for some reason the same doesnt apply to a suspect that has taken a 12 gauge buckshot and survived somehow, which I dont really understand.I have noticed a few visual/ animation bugs that I would like to note, this are not fixed as of the most recent version and may be fixed in the future1. Vests/helmets not crouching with you in the team view cam, This isnt really a major issue, just kinda breaks the immersion for me and can be slightly annoying when an ally is peaking over you2. While a surrendered suspect is turning away from you his legs will turn in a rather odd manner and delayed from their body moving which looks quite off. This is a very minor issue but has still had me scratching my head a few times, I want to note this one isnt constant and is quite rare to come acrossAbsolutely! I believe Ready or not is 100% worth the money, the maps are amazing, combat is smooth and overall its extremely fun with friendsYes there will be times where the game can be frustrating because you get shot through a wall, or just cant seem to get the right RNG for an s tier run. But overall the pros outweigh the cons in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: Ready or Not is like if a serious SWAT team met a bunch of well meaning but hopelessly clumsy friends who somehow got their hands on tactical gear. The game promises high stakes action, but what you really get is a front row seat to a comedy of tactical errors.First off, the realism is off the charts so much so that I found myself questioning my life choices. Who knew that clearing a room could feel so much like attempting to organize a family gathering? I swear, the amount of friendly fire in this game rivals Christmas dinner at my aunt's house. One moment, you’re clearing a corridor like a pro, and the next, you’ve accidentally shot your partner because you mistook them for an enemy classic move!The sound design is eerily immersive, especially when you accidentally set off a flashbang. If you’re looking for a way to bond with your friends, just know that nothing builds camaraderie like simultaneously blinding each other and then panicking as you try to figure out who’s who. You’d think we were playing tag with a bunch of rabid raccoons instead of a tactical shooter.And the AI, Oh boy! They’ve got a mind of their own. One moment, I’m communicating a plan, and the next, my teammate decides to play Rambo and rushes in, only to trip over their own shoelaces. Spoiler alert. they don’t sell “cool points” for that in the after action report.Ready or Not delivers a perfect mix of adrenaline and hilarity. If you’re ready to engage in some serious tactical goofiness with your friends or if you just want to experience what it’s like to be an undercover clown this game is for you. Just remember, communication is key... unless you want to reenact a scene from a buddy cop movie. Happy gaming!

_childDocuments_.review: Boy I might get hate for this.LD;DR: It's just a shooter. A really hardcore shooter. But *just* a shooter.I only played two dozen missions, maybe three. I have three gripes with the game1. PerformanceEven if I do want to roleplay and get into it, I'm constantly sucked out of it by the game running like ass. Specially for a 1.0 release, this is just ♥♥♥♥. I don't expect the game to run flawlessly, I only expect it to not impact gameplay, yet it does. Constantly.And ♥♥♥♥ me, it's not even a GPU bottleneck. Despite how unoptimal the lighting setup in this game is, switching to low barely improves performance. Guys, CPU bottlenecks are most often on you, so what on earth did you do behind the 1.0 build?2. BugsIt's a 1.0 release. You had a year of Early Access, what the hell happened. ♥♥♥♥ it, it's not just this game, I don't want any game release as a buggy mess. But this is ridiculous. I watched a Stanag mag come out of my teammate's ass as we were walking, headgears just float above people's heads, we open a door, close it, the sun is still shining through and it's painfully bright, I spawn in without arms, we host a private lobby and it's open, but ♥♥♥♥ it who cares, we can't even join.AI aims at us in one frame, dead body ragdolls shoot up in the sky, sometimes you can't even see dead bodies until you walk up really close. Oh and I can't even tell my teammates because I literally cannot hear them ingame, everything's setup correctly, no voice audio is coming through.I feel like I should emphasise this: We only played two missions. TWO.3. It's just a shooterRight, story time!When the game came out last year, me and a friend of mine had an argument. I told him that this is just a shooter, you can literally play it like CoD. He said that's dumb.Anyways, we played a round on the skyscraper map (I think, it was a year ago), I was the last man standing. I said watch this: And I cleared the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ building alone. Because it's just a shooter. Good reaction times simply payed off.Did that change in 1.0?...kindaThe AI now reacts to you much faster. I appreciate that? It's now harder than ever to play the game like CoD for sure.. but you still can? And I noticed that while my friends were trying to play it tactically, I just whipped at the gunner's head and shot. Like.. that's it. I find that playing tactically is still not required, it really, really feels optional. And not just that, if you can't aim well it's still kinda game over, you have a limited amount of tactical gear to give yourself an edge anyways.And besides, why on earth would I actively try to play super tactically? From what I saw, I only unlock skins. I'm sorry, but the last decade of AAA games really conditioned me to give a grand total of 0 ♥♥♥♥♥ about skins, so what's there for me in this?And at this point it looks like this game isn't made for me, and I just made a bad purchase and this whole rant is pointless. But is it really?I was sold on an immersive SWAT (or SWAT like) game, that's not your average shooter. The early access release kinda was just an average shooter. Now the 1.0 release is still kind of an average shooter. But more hardcore.For real, I could just open any shooter with bots, I'll pick CS2 cuz it's easy to setup, put a bunch of bots in Office, set their difficulty to some insane godlike level and that's basically it, **in terms of difficulty**...I guess I'm just butthurt over how much I spent on something that ultimately just disappoints. There's so many great games out there, and 50$ for this technical mess is such a high ask.

_childDocuments_.review: I genuinely believe this game fails at the only thing it tries to do, which is to provide a fun, immersive, realistic breach and clear simulation with friends or bots.The small amount of guns and gear this game allows are not balanced at all, and some of the content straight up does not work properly (ballistic shields) or has no feedback at all and leaves you puzzled as to whenever or not they worked. (tasers, pepper sprays, every single grenade and launchers) The game also does not show you any stats when it comes to gear and weapons. I know the game is supposed to be realistic when it comes to penetration and calibers, but you just have no idea on how this translates in game without testing it yourself, and even then.The game has a severe lack of polish. It is riddled with minor bugs, and a few major bugs here and there. There is almost no feedback to your inputs and the gunplay is severely lacking. Even the recoil feels floaty and strange, and don't get me started on your character's movements. I'm sure this is a conscious design decision, but even my grandma was faster, and even without that taken into account, your character feels like a dumpster skating on ice. The hitboxes in the game is straight up hitbox gore, and you will hit your friends in the back of the head even though you're not aiming at them at all. Civilians will take more than a second to react to anything you do, will not react to your gunfire, and won't even react to tasers and pepper spray. (It just makes them calmly sit with their hands up .. RIP Immersion !)The AI is dumb as a box of rocks. First, don't even try to play with bot teammates, they fail in every single department. As a result, I've been playing mostly with friends .. as for the rest, the enemy will sometimes fire endlessly in the ceiling (They have infinite ammo and magazines of course) They will also either rush you at the start of the round or just wait like nothing is happening, which pretty much boils every run down to killing everyone at the start, and then looking for the stragglers for hours on end. I also mentioned how unresponsive the civilians are in my earlier paragraph above. The mod support is atrocious. Beware thee should you download any mod, because I can guarantee you will spend hours trying to fix your game so other people can join. Everyone needs to have your exact mods installed to join, and even once they do, the game might still think they don't. Disabling your mods does nothing. Disabling the checksum (which is supposed to fix this issue) does nothing. Even uninstalling your mods altogether also sometimes has no result. To this day, we still don't know what eventually fixes the problem, but if the game wants to screw you on a particular day, you won't get to play.Outside of that, the game has a severe lack of content, with only a handful of firearms and even less gear. I get that this game is only supposed to showcase gear used by S.W.A.T, but the United-States is not the only country in the world. Plus, the game would really benefit from choosing content over realism in that regard, it really feels like the dev team uses realism as a excuse for being lazy. Finally, the experience is just not really that fun ? While the difficulty is not something I particularly noticed, as the game is rather easy when it comes to my skill level, but the game will never fail to make you search for hours for the last remaining enemy. Why not just let them escape and make you lose points for not being fast enough ? Or even have them come at you ? I cannot in my right mind like this game. As a side note, this game was previously highly ambitious, and even featured some PVP modes, after which the devs decided to go the lazy way and feature only one type of gamemode with only a handful of maps (Don't even try to argue the maps have several "gamemodes", whatever you choice is makes nearly to no difference) and despite that, it still failed to perform such a simple task. This game in its current state is absolutely not worth its price, and judging by the time it takes for the devs to update the game, and how much "content" is shipped in those updates, it is safe to say this game might never be finished.
