_childDocuments_.review: Don't feel like reading the whole thing? Down at the bottom is the conclusion and score given to the game! :)You enter with a team of SWAT officers into a building. The complex is enormous, and there is a deafening silence; as you spot a hostage, you realize they are signaling to you with their hands towards a door. You open it, and there is a terrorist inside. Ready or Not is an irregular co-op FPS in which you play through dreadful situations that pays a great deal of attention to details. The title's difficulty is serious as the atmosphere lets you soak in the situation's intensity. Doors can be booby-trapped with explosives, some enemies can become Jonh Wick, quickly dispatching you, and you must also ensure the hostage's security. The result is fierce gunfights in which coordination is critical to play objectives and providing a good chance of clearing the mission!Guns have an impact and can be customized to suit the player's playstyle, they are all unlocked from the get-go, and some accessories change how you play. You can take night vision for night maps or mirror guns to see below doors on layouts with tonnes of rooms. Enemies are unpredictable; they can double back to previous rooms or create elaborate ambushes. I had fun trying different approaches until I found one that clicked with me and the mission to beat those extreme raid maps.The best part of the game is the little details found in it. Maps have cellphones ringing on desks, structures are worked so flawlessly they look real-life wise, and the title map design is so good it appears to be done by architects. In addition, the sun's light can move and make it more difficult to see what's in the next room due to the harsh sunlight! There are different modes, with raid being the most predominant. Raid missions will test you to the limit as they feature lethal enemies and require multiple runs for a clear. That extends the game's replayability and can easily net 10-20 hours of gameplay. Grabbing your friends and tackling these missions make for entertaining game sessions that are memorable and fun! I had a good laugh when one of my friends blew himself opening a door that was an explosive trap!Ready or Not sound design is spectacular as you can issue commands to hostages and enemies to give up. It integrates into the gameplay as you can use these commands to make enemies speak, revealing their location, and the direction of the audio becomes a hint as to where to watch out for. The voice acting is similar to what one might expect from a police movie.When foes engage with the players, music will play to increase combat tension. The style of music is anxious and unnerving, following a loop that keeps you on edge as you check your corners and land your shots. Once combat is over, the creepy silence sets in again, making you feel uneasy no matter what.The game looks so beautiful one could believe it had ray tracing, as the reflections on the floor have unbelievable detail. Each map is distinctive from one another with the level of graphical fidelity replicating surfaces and brightness. The visual content allows the severity and gore of the situation to be more realistic on the screen. The game was tested with an RTX 2060, 36 GB of ram, Intel Core i7-11700K - Core i7 11th Gen Rocket Lake 8-Core 3.6 GHz LGA 1200.The results were 50-60 FPS on ultra with some drops to 30 FPS at times, while the game ran at 78-90 FPS with the settings set to medium. There can be a bit of a clunky feeling to the camera when snapping your wrist for fast movement, and talking with teammates by holding the key "V" was bothersome in the middle of gunfights. As an additional note, press the "L" once the mission starts to change to team voice chat, as it is easier for your teammates to hear your voice.  is a unique game in which players must eliminate threats, arrest suspects, and prioritize saving civilian life. A tactical FPS that tries to push into a more horrific direction, it is worth the price if you have friends to play with it or plan to make new ones in-game. I recommend the title to players who enjoy realistic simulations and want to try a more tense shooter experience.9/10  AMAZINGIf you enjoy and find the review helpful, please follow my curator StarsDeck!

_childDocuments_.review: Basically spiritual successor to SWAT series.Technically, for an early access game this one is surprisingly polished, I've played a few missions and I must say, from time to time my fellow operators did some weird things (such as opening door through wall), but all things considered, this does not look like early access at all. You can buy it and enjoy it even on singleplayer. I'm still looking forward to play it in CO-OP.Feature-wise, the game is pretty rich in content already, all things considered, but there's lack of any tutorial. Learning during normal play seems kinda fun though. Opening a door and exploding moment after was the last thing I expected. I wish there was an option to give orders to specific operators, not only fireteams. Having both would be nice. Also, the game is really punishing if you're the first one to enter the room. You can't take control over any alive operators, if you die - mission failed. About controlling operators - nice feature to have would be to take control over operators, or give them orders without direct sight - like looking through their bodycam. Sometimes I forgot to queue an order for clearing a room and I need to backtrack all the way to the first entrance to issue it.The immersion and experiences are quite unique however, in positive manner: sure it feels like SWAT 4, but (for now) the only game that gave me jumpscares was Escape from Tarkov. The scheme is almost exact: you can hear grass growing and suddenly somebody starts shooting you god knows where from, even if you expect to be shot at.Definitely worth buying, even at current state (early access). I'm looking forward for content updates, and maybe some new features.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm completely rewriting my previous review. I gave it a thumbs down because the soft objectives as a concept are pretty annoying. The game is good, I like it, and I was unfair on my previous review. It's very intense, you are constantly on the edge of your seat, but some things need change. The most glaring issue is the AI, for which there are mods, but an official revision of the AI would be preferrable. Sometimes you get wallbanged from a random direction, but their accuracy is pinpoint. As for soft objectives, I still believe something should be done about them. It can be annoying when you miss a civilian or some evidence and you can't complete the mission, although I understand it's the premise of the game, but it's a game, so wasting time looking for something is tedious, especially on bigger maps. I also think they should add a running speed, maybe make it so enemies detect you while running and ADS time gets heavily increased, but at least give us that option. I wish there was an option to adjust gamma and contrast which, again, is an artistic decision to not have them, but maybe give us the option.Overall, the game is very good, even for solo players like myself. A lot of amazing maps, AI teammates work fine (most of the times at least), the feeling of danger is constantly present, customization is ok (although I prefer Ground Branch kind of customization). You will like it, even if sometimes you need some patience. I was very unfair previously, and wrote my review after ragequitting and arguably awful level (Greasy Palms), but everything else is enjoyable most of the time.

_childDocuments_.review: When it comes to tactical CQB games, RoN should be one of your top choices. While other games in that genre cover other more military kind of "settings" of armed combat, this one is for the SWAT lovers. I think the most important aspect about RoN is that good movement and gun mechanic. While it lacks "prone stance" and the in depth weapon-customization other games have and finding the right clickpoint for opening doors can be a tricky thing in stressful situations, the haptic is great in this game and I would say one of the best. Doesn't give you any superiority ove your enemies but it feels least frustrating compared to many other CQB shooter: it ain't arcade but it doesn't give you the feeling that you are in a nightmare, when you strafe for example. Other cool aspects: - very active mod community with lots of cool maps and mods- graphics are good. Not more, but not less either- AI is one of the better out there - it's not perfect, but at least it makes sense and doesn't feel like it is cheatingOn the con side: - lots of clipping - very difficult without a good team (well that's normal for the genre)- the devs were very active until a few months ago but updates happen, they are always significant.All in all one of my favorite tactical shooters.EDIT After the 1.0 update:Day one conclusion: the 1.0 update makes an already good game even better! The new maps, the sound rework, the AI. Everything improved. YOu want the #1 tactical CQB game currently on the market? Buy RoN!

Yes there are times where i got one shot from some completely stupid angle or something else immersion breaking happens.Yet those moments are forgotten very fast because theres so much to like about this game.- Great maps: Theres a huge diversity of settings. Going from small gas station, through farm of cultists to huge villa. Additionally every map has many details that help the storytelling. Briefings only include the information thats known to control, but you can discover the details as you go. And overall theres just so many little details to appreciate. On the night club mission you can for example hear phones going off everywhere, because the incident has blown up in media and the little things like this just really add so much to the experience and immersion. - Great Sounds: Guns sound good. Shooting and getting shot at sounds good. Voice acting is pretty good for the most part and the only criticism id have here is that some npcs really talk too much which makes them repeat their lines a bit too often. Little things like walking through a room with a bunch of casings on the floor sounds like youd expect that. Explosions and flashbangs going off sounds awesome too and the effects have a good amount of punch to them. The music supports all of this perfectly with genuinly intense tracks.- Great Customization: You can change so many things about your loadout. Take more mags for your primary but less pistol mags. Or less mags and more tacticals. Many non lethal options as well. You can tailor your loadout to a specific playstyle or map. I havent even touched most of the available equipment even though i really like to adjust everything to a new mission i play and fail first. Added to functional customization comes also a lot of visual customization, that has to be unlocked via progress (or mods).Oh and you can also adjust the loadout of your teammates.- Great "teamwork" even for Solo Players: The AI has its highs and lows. I heavily recommend looking into some mods to tweak the behaviour to your liking. Sometimes your team AI is useless and doesnt react correctly to threats, sometimes the enemy AI reacts to threats (you) too well. With mods it gets a lot better though and using different tactics is really enjoyable. It gives the game a lot of replayability value.While i could put down more points, the sum of it really is that theres so many things in this game that are well thought out, many small details that add a lot of value in the greater scope. But there are also moments that break your immersion or are just frustrating. As said in the intro. This game is ambitious and i cant help but forgive many of its faults for that. Some times things dont work too well, but man if they work this really is one hell of an experience. If you like to get immersed into this type of game, there really is no substitute for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Title: Ready or Not - Crippled by Constant Crashes and UnplayableReview:I had high hopes for Ready or Not, but my experience was unfortunately marred by persistent crashes that made the game virtually unplayable. After spending just 1.1 hours trying to enjoy it, I decided to refund it, and here’s why.The game’s core mechanics and tactical gameplay have a lot of potential. The concept of team-based tactical operations and strategic planning is right up my alley. However, the frequent crashes completely undermined any enjoyment I might have had. I was booted out of the game every 10 minutes or so, making it impossible to get into any meaningful gameplay or fully appreciate what the game has to offer.The crashes weren’t just occasional hiccups; they were consistent and disruptive. Each time the game crashed, I lost progress and had to restart, which quickly became infuriating. The instability made it feel like I was wasting my time rather than engaging in the tactical action I was looking forward to.On top of the crashes, there were issues with performance and optimization. Even when I did manage to get into a match, the game ran poorly with noticeable lag and frame drops. The combination of these technical problems made the overall experience frustrating and far from enjoyable.In summary, Ready or Not could be a fantastic game based on its concept and mechanics, but the constant crashes and poor performance turned it into an exasperating experience. After spending 1.1 hours battling these issues, I decided to refund it. If the developers manage to address these stability issues in future updates, it might be worth another look, but as it stands, it’s not worth the hassle.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a SWAT game. 100% of all suspects you encounter are hyper-aggressive, fearless, non-human hiveminds with zero self-preservation instincts, obsessed and hellbent on killing you with no other goal in life. The very first millisecond they hear you, they immediately snap onto you, and get permanent wallhacks on your exact location for the remainder of their life, and start shooting with near-perfect accuracy, while strafing at sprinting speed. If a single bot doesn't ace the entire team, they'll just attrit you to death, since most gunfights end up with you trading shots with them, and they outnumber your entire team 4 to 1. That's assuming you can trade shots, because the armour system is complete and utter RNG: sometimes you can facetank a dozen 7.62x51 rounds at point blank, others you get two-tapped in the tip of your pinky finger by a 9mm-wielding hobo junkie pixel-hunting you from the other end of the map. The game has a severe lack of actual SWAT scenarios. There are no situations to de-escalate and suspects to arrest. The only way you are able to arrest armed enemies is using non-lethal weaponry on them, which magically makes them reconsider fighting you to death.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm gonna give a pretty honest review going over good and bad, I still enjoy the game overall but I'm still quite critical. I'm normally just playing with just my brother but when quietly sweeping a house, poking around corners and breaching through doors I can't help feeling a whole new level of immersion. The developers have done an awesome job at making the players feel nervous and tense as well as making them feel like every choice they make could lead to the mission failing as quickly as it begun. I've had some really enjoyable experiences while playing this game. However I have a bunch of complaints, I'm usually forgiving with game developers but as steam has no in between rating for game I'll just rate it up because I still enjoy the game. The graphics are great and each map looks incredible yet their has still been no adjustment on the lighting for some of the maps, the AI still wall hacks and has a quicker reaction time and aim to that of any human. Mind you, I enjoy difficult tactical shooters with hard AI but I need to draw a line somewhere of how overpowered AI can be. I feel most weak, untrained suspects, despite being "poor desperate criminals" still use the most advanced expensive weaponry. Most enemies use full auto, so each mission feels like you're fighting the same guys and suspect rarely surrender. It feels more like a tactical shooter where you play as a soldier rather than a tactical police game when you're playing as a cop. Too many enemies have aim bot and shoot through walls and have inhuman reaction time, many players use mods to fix this issue as it's never been addressed. There are plenty of videos online that display these AI issues. Again, every enemy has a fully auto switch apparently which makes every mission feel the same. Like how can some small poor small time criminals rob a gas station with AKs, SMGs, at most you'd feel they'd have a Glock. I also feel like there isn't a lot of maps where you not fighting a private military or security agency like come on, there should be maps were father takes his wife and kids hostage or welfare checks gone bad or hell even bank robberies something that's common and fun, sure bank robberies are over done but people love them. There is a map when you need to arrest a family making full auto switches. The map looks awesome however this mission doesn't stand out because that's basically every enemy in the game.While I appreciate the devs compressing the game file they have still not rendered the game. It still runs like s#@% at times with freezes and frame rate drops, and mind you I'm running on a beast of a PC. Overall I do still like the game but I have many complaints, while ready or not has a special place in my heart I don't believe its in a fully release state and that price tag is certainly a laughable decision. Considering the last update was on my birthday last year I was hoping many of the issues would be addressed. Again I've been a long time supporter and I'll probably always have a special place in my heart for this game but their are still things that bother me with this game, don't even get me started on the streamer map, like what the f#@% was that!Overall I will say the maps are great when they are not being deleted, the devs have Grass is Greener Syndrome, they are never happy with maps so they keep removing them which is ass. Gun play is some of the best in gaming history. AI is ♥♥♥♥, the most unrealistic I've seen in a long time, like if its a meme then your AI is bad. It may be a big claim to make but I think the ONLY WAY TO PLAY READY OR NOT AND ENJOY IT IS BY DOWNLOADING MODS THAT FIX THE ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ AI.

_childDocuments_.review: THUMBS DOWN UNTIL THE DEVS FIX THEIR AI.TL DR; The game has great worldbuilding with its maps and map design, but lacks coherent story. The AI is bonkers, Commander mode and SWAT AI management is just tedious, and the RoE is just plain wrong. Game was launched unfinished/rushed for the holidays, you need mods for it to be realistic. Unfinished game.The Good:This is a natural sequel to the old SWAT series, and the realism and story telling through the different maps is very good! Highly recommend to anyone who likes the slower pace of tactical shooters, be it ARMA or SWAT 4. It might feel too slow for COD players, but when the proverbial feces hits the spinny thing, you gotta think, move and act fast!HOWEVER:360, wallbanging, noscope, aimbot Suspect AI is just infuriating - Devs have a long way to go to make the AI actually act like human beings with self preservation in mind. I get it if we are up against a ♥♥♥♥♥ out druggie that would storm you, but giving the same "class" aimbot and wallhacks doesnt make any sense. Same with your regular hoodlum being the second coming of John Wick and not fearing for their life while staring down the barrel of 5 SWAT officers yelling for compliance. Final map also has too far of a range for compliance to work, they really dont care, but still detect you from across the map, so you end up having to shoot them with lethal. AI Mods make it slightly better.SWAT AI is dumb as all hell, they cant shoot to save their lives, and instead of moving when getting hit, they will just stand there and take it. They also do not have the same viewrange/viewcone as the suspect AI has, so they will stand there getting shot through a small hole and not fire back. Micro managing the SWAT AI is tedious at best, having to tell them even the smallest thing like what way to look, and even then they might just not react to your commands, so you end up having to repeat the commands over and over.RoE is also kinda wack, if someone shoots at you, you shouldn't be penalized by getting less points for shooting them back, such an easy fix too; if you or anyone in your squad gets hit or suppressed by a suspect, that suspect can be shot back and still count towards a perfect score. No LEO in their right mind would pull a taser or pepperspray at a suspect armed with a rifle!There is no real way to know what score you have on a map before the end score screen AFTER running through a mission, so if you wanted to 100% S rank it, you better write down you progression, because the game doesn't tell you. Alternatively you have to see what tattoos you have already unlocked to see how far you have progressed.And Commander mode; The micro management of your fellow officers is just annoying and tedious - WHY do they have to unlock their traits, aren't they fully training SWAT officers? Are they training "on the job"? I didn't sign up to be a TO for these chumps! HOW are they on the SWAT team if they get anxious or stressed by getting shot at, no real SWAT team would have mentally weak officers like this!Gunplay is good, however, less than lethal like the pepper balls have too long of a delay before working, you end up shooting more than needed, even when you whack the suspects in the face with it. CS gas disperses too slow and the SWAT AI treat all grenades as if they where flash grenades, so they will throw in a CS canister, just to then immediately move in instead of waiting a second or two for the gas to disperse. Bean bag shotgun works well. AP vs JHP doesn't matter, just go for AP in all cases. 40mm grenade launchers have too little range, considering the LONG ranges one might encounter on some of the maps.Since Void is giving us the proverbial middle finger, here is one back to them from me: 🖕

_childDocuments_.review: INITIAL EARLY ACCESS REVIEW!!!Ready or Not is an amazing tribute to one of the best shooter series ever: SWAT. It brings me back to the days of playing Rainbow Six and SOCOM games on the PS2. So far the devs have done a great job getting in the basics from SWAT and the gameplay is very similar. Many aspects from SWAT 4 have been brought over, like the squad commands and gamemodes. Overall the game in its early stages is more than playable and enjoyable. Great game to play with friends both casually and professionally. So far there are 6 fully detailed maps and 2 "Legacy/Unfinished" maps to choose from. The modding community is already hard at work in recreating some SWAT 4 maps and even some original maps. The game engine used allows for easy modding and after only 20 days, the mod page on Nexus has reached over 100 mods and the Modded or Not discord has even more. The guns are well designed and include a much wider range of manufacturers compared to SWAT 4 with its limited arsenal. The AI of course have a lot more firearms to choose from and in the future, more firearms will be added to the SWAT team arsenal. Already the devs have posted their plans for a January update with improved voice lines for NPC's and more firearms. If the devs keep this up, we should expect updates for the game every month with some fresh new content. They also promised to release smaller patches in between major content updates.So far as an early access game with limited content, I've gotten around 22 hours of fun with friends and with AI. Future updates will add to that play time without a doubt and I look forward to the future of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Ready or Not is a tactical first-person shooter that brings players into intense, high-stakes scenarios as members of a SWAT team. The game’s main draw is its commitment to realism, which can make each mission feel tense and unpredictable. The environments are detailed, the AI is sharp, and the overall atmosphere is gripping, making every encounter feel like it could go wrong in a split second.One of the most talked-about aspects of the game is its dark humor, particularly when it comes to dealing with civilians. While the game’s realistic approach means you’re supposed to handle these situations carefully, the unintentional humor that arises from mishandling civilian interactions can be surprisingly funny. Whether it's accidentally flashbanging a room full of hostages or the chaotic moments when a terrified civilian bolts at the worst possible time, the game’s unpredictable nature often leads to absurd, laugh-out-loud situations.However, this humor is set against a backdrop of gruesome and realistic depictions of violence. The game doesn’t shy away from showing the brutal consequences of your actions. The gunfights are intense, with bullets having real stopping power, and the aftermath of a firefight is often messy. The realism here isn’t just for show—it makes the stakes feel incredibly high and every decision critical.

_childDocuments_.review: Lots of potential for a great game, unfortunately all of the below are true:- AI inconsistently responds to both lethal and nonlethal damage (even unarmored)- AI can sprint and walk faster than a snail's pace (you cannot)- AI have superhuman levels of health and pain tolerance (injuries do not cause them to produce noise, and they can survive 3-4 rounds of 5.56 AP / 12 Gauge Buckshot or Slugs)- AI are sometimes immune to gadgets (Gas/C2 Breaching Charges/Flashbangs etc.)- Civilians and Criminal AI both act without regard to their own safety, or even within the logic of their goals (Civilians will just stand around in the midst of firefights, literal Terrorists within the scope of the game's narrative will drop their weapons when surrounded, only to attempt to cut you with a knife - why wouldn't they keep their firearm if they had no intention on living?)- Physics objects can cause evidence and bodies to be voided, breaking the game's scoring system- Criminal AI interactions can cause evidence to be voided, breaking the game's scoring system- Game cannot consistently distinguish between appropriate use of force, breaking the game's scoring system (I've had friends be killed and myself shot by 1 NPC, only to receive a score penalty for injuring and arresting them)- Level geometry and physics objects can cause you to get stuck or clip outside of the map, killing you or rendering you useless to your team- Level geometry contains seams in the environment that are invisible to the player (Enemy AI can use this to attack you, however)- Due to high enemy resistances, bullet penetration cannot reliably be used as a mechanic to the player's benefit (although you will certainly die from it)- Game suffers from horrid storage and hardware optimization, leading to a 90+ GB install size, crashes, and massive frame drops even on a $4000 PC- And lastly, this same chugging applies during loads and within the game's lobby, leading to frequent disconnects and the occasional mandatory Install Verification in order to restart the game (not my case, is the case for half of my friends)Sadly, there are far more issues than what I've just listedBut to make an even more in-depth list would be beyond time consuming If you're willing to tolerate all of the above with a group of friends, or if you have hope for the developers to resolve most of these issues, then this game could be for you.But if not? Then you should give this game a hard pass

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who was apart of the Supporter Edition from the very early beta versions of the game, who's S ranked every mission in the game on 1.0, I cannot recommend this game in its current state. If you want to go through and shoot everything in sight, it's a fairly fun shooter, but as a tactical police shooter taking inspiration from SWAT, it falls very short.The biggest issue currently is that Suspect AI have no variety what so ever and are extremely accurate and aggressive. They all act very similarly, whether they're a drug addict in their crack den, a homicidal maniac barricaded in his home, or straight up terrorists shooting everyone in sight. A meme among the community is that every mission in this game makes you feel like you're assaulting Osama Bin Laden's compound, and that's not very far off. They constantly fake surrender with 5 guns pointed at their head. They constantly rush past corners and into open areas, despite knowing you're there. They constantly resist non-lethal or even lethal shots until you spam F. The root of this issue is the suspect AI are currently programmed to be very aggressive and offensively mind-set, even on defensive maps like barricaded suspects, with very little difference among them, leading to a game-play experience that is extremely predictable.And because there is very little difference in the suspect AI, the missions become the same thing, over and over again. You're most likely going to be shooting 80% of the suspects you encounter, no matter what kind they are, and the game gets very repetitive after you've completed Commander Mode. A prime example of this disconnection is the streamer den mission. VOID advertised this mission as going into a streamer's home who has been swatted, with a false 911 call about him shooting his mother to death and taking his brother hostage. This mission could of been this game's Fairfax Residence, with very little suspects at all, just civilians falsely accused of a crime who have no idea you are there, who may be armed or not, perhaps falsely believing their home is being invaded.Instead, VOID decided to make it another ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ trip into Fallujah. Why are there 10+ gangsters in this mission with automatic weapons and shotguns? I understand there's some kind of illegal server farm (which has people walking around with guns as if they're constantly expecting the cops???), but why are these people in the streamer's room and in the hallways? I don't really care if there's a reason for it, it just speaks again to this game's issue of having stale, repetitive missions and how much missed opportunity there was. Clearly, VOID was afraid that a slow paced tactical shooter wouldn’t be liked by mainstream audiences, and that’s why most missions feel like a shooting gallery.The ROE for these missions are pretty dumb, with S rank always requiring you to bring every single suspect in alive, which basically requires you to spam beanbag shotguns, gas, and F compliance yell until your fingers hurt. Why do I need to bring in actual Jihad terrorists or school shooters in alive to get an S rank? For missions where the suspects are defensive, I can understand that mentality, but for missions where lives are at risk or the suspects have offensively assaulted a location, why would any police department have that kind of ROE? They wouldn't.If you don't install an AI mod like I had to do, be prepared to deal with AI who can snap shoot you through walls. The way the devs programmed it is that if you fall within a certain "visual cone" within 500 meters, the suspects immediately identify and turn towards you with a 0.1 (yes, that's actually how it's programmed) reaction time. Because of this, they can spot you through the smallest holes in geometry, which usually results in you getting shot through walls randomly whilst walking through open areas. The most infamous example of this is the postal office warehouse.There's also a lot of other issues currently which makes the game seem half-baked. Lack of QoA (can't save outfits in customization, no gun stats), lackluster story, god awful optimization (I have a 4090 and the game still runs like ♥♥♥♥ sometimes),  VOID clearly rushed this release to capitalize on the holidays, and it's hilariously sad to see how it has backfired on them, going from 40k daily players back down to what it used to be around 15-10k.For those unaware about the history in recent years with VOID, they've mishandled this game. They rarely had updates in early access, despite making 2 million dollars off of it, and most likely more off this recent release which I hope they put towards improving and fixing the game, instead of a rumor which I will go into down below. VOID is a small company, so I can understand that things take time, but this release in particular came out of nowhere. It really did feel like they got our hopes up, trying to market the game as finished, when in reality it wasn't and they just wanted to grab as much money as possible off of the holiday rush.There's talk that VOID has begun preparing to abandon this project in favor for a new one. All I can say is if they do that, they aren't getting a penny from me in the future, and I encourage you to do so the same. It's a real shame to see a project you were invested in turn to such a wet fart.Wait until VOID fixes the issues to purchase the game (2.0 coming 2027!)

_childDocuments_.review: It pains me to write this. This game was almost amazing. And in many ways the issues I have with it are ultimately small things that could have easily been fixed. But they arent fixed. And they are game breaking for me. The missions I played prior to refunding, you were expected to clear the area of all hostiles AND "rescue" all the civilians. Which i think is overkill once you have cleared all the hostile forces. Though, my first mission i spent way too long trying to find the last civilian so i could actually end the mission and had to go to the discord to ask and find out you have to use the "search and rescue" function to help with this. Well, mission 2 i ran into the same issue. spent more time after i cleared the area looking for civilians than i did actually clearing the area. Very boring stuff. and the option 6 search function didnt do anything to help with it. so i just quit and refunded.Ultimately, beyond that, the AI is very clunky when trying to get your squad to follow commands. And thats not something you can be fighting with in a tense active shooter situation. I need them to almost be anticipating what I need them to do, not fighting me for basic things like not wanting to stack up on a door until i issue the command 3 times. Stuff like that is very disappointing to see. Because the graphics are amazing (if not a little poorly optimized, but still plenty usable), the stories and situations you are placed in are eerie and unsettling (in a good way) the combat is realistic and actually feels tactical (though could use a bit more flexibility in functions) and overall for being an indy dev title, this was an amazing product. Its just not playable for me because of bad AI and mission completion requirements that force you do go on an easter egg hunt every mission for no reason.

_childDocuments_.review: Ready or Not is a fun new game, its tactical and reminds me of Rainbow Six Siege & the classic S.W.A.T. games.TLDR Gameplay is all about loading into a map, arresting all the civilians and suspects at the scene as you play a SWAT member, all the while securing evidence and dropping bad guys with guns that are hiding behind doors, corners, and obstacles. Its actually great fun with friends, and can lead to some funny moments ifyou got some goofy-ass friends with you. I wouldn't buy it for full price as of right now, since you can get through all the maps with some friends or solo, in roughly 5 hours or so. $40 for 5-6 maps and 5+ hours of gameplay dosent seem quite worth it to me, but overall it's still a fun game and does what it does super well; It's hella tactical, you HAVE TO plan what you do before you do it (unless you play on easy you bum) and playing it on the hardest difficulty with friends is the most fun way to play this game.I recommend it on a sale or if you value your money differently, pick it up for a few hours/sessions of fun if you want a SWAT based shooter.Honestly, this is what R6 Should've been and still should be, but instead I gotta scratch my tactical shooter itch with this since R6 became too arcadey.Great game! The AI though, is kinda questionable.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: ***EDIT**** This game has received a good bit of love since writing this review and has taken many elements in a great direction. It is still a tough experience solo, but much of the cheapness has been addressed. The modding community has also created great additions to the game. I do recommend the game now but I'm leaving the original review below********This is a game where I love the idea of it. The execution of the game is close to being great, but falls short to the point that I cannot currently recommend it. There is such potential for Ready or Not to be an absolute gem, it just needs more love and attention. For the strengths of the game, there are a few notable elements that I absolutely love. - Gun audio: firing a weapon is very satisfying. This is one of my largest complaints in most modern games but Ready or Not has absolutely nailed the audio. - Slow and steady gameplay: this is not a COD game where you run room to room mowing down hundreds of enemies. You need to be cautious and approach with purpose. The game knows how it wants you to play and it is amazing when it works well. - Selection and customization: Right from the start, you have several weapons, vests, and resources at your disposal. For these strengths, the negatives are more numerous and impactful. -Enemy AI: It doesn't take long to look into the negative reviews to see this this complaint. Despite having tweaks to the AI system, the enemies are absolutely cracked. In a system where you can die in just a few hits, there needs to be a balance that this game has not even come close to achieving. It is to the point where you feel like you're a random civilian who has picked up a gun for the first time going against trained military snipers. Oh, and some of them are essentially snipers picking you off from a deck while you wonder what's shooting at you as soon as you loaded into the a mission-Suppression system: As soon as an enemy shoots at you, your vision blurs, camera shakes, and your accuracy tanks. A very poorly implemented system given the native difficulty of the AI that rarely misses to begin with. -Friendly AI: far less cracked than the enemy. However, I don't mind this as much. What I do mind is that they will stand in every doorway they can and block you from navigating the rooms. You also cannot push them out of the way. They either need to be commanded or you need to move enough to allow them to enter the room. -Player movement: you move at a snail's pace. There is no sprint. If an enemy gets the jump on you, the only option is to quickly locate and dispatch them (very hard due to the suppression system), or slowly walk out of the enemy LOS (unlikely given their amazing accuracy). -Unclear system: it can be confusing how to use various pieces of equipment, figuring out how to alter your squad, and navigating certain menus. It also takes a good minute or two to load into a mission. If you fail, you need to watch the entire grading system list out each element of the mission and does not allow you to skip. -Optimization: the game lags, stutters, and crashes even on better PCs. I can go on with many of the negatives I see about this game. However, the main complaint is that the game creates an unrealistic sense of how dangerous common enemies can be for a SWAT simulator. The cracked aiming creates a system that is far more frustrating than fun. It's a shame because there's great potential here, but it misses the mark. Unlike the enemy AI.

_childDocuments_.review: There's not much right now because it's in beta but what's there is really solid.This isn't like other shooters where you are a tank. You will die instantly if you are caught off guard and you can only take a few shots (depending on the weapon), even with the heaviest armor. Also, your injuries will impair you for the rest of the match, and when you are bleeding you can't see ♥♥♥♥ until you 'heal yourself' (by pressing F, whatever that means).The enemies will also shoot through doors or walls and you can do the same. Overall I would say the AI isn't exceptional. You can gun down a bunch of enemies in one room and their friends will just be chilling upstairs, but it's still difficult. If you aggro a group of guys they will try to hide and catch you off guard or flank you. Sometimes perps will pretend to be innocent and then try to shoot you if you look away.With good tactics I managed to clear most of the levels with a friend, but you need to be smart and use tools like the mirror gun to peek under doors, as well as flashbangs/gas/etc to breach. Some doors are also trapped which can really ♥♥♥♥ you if you don't disarm them.One thing I will say that's amazing about this game is the sound and feel of firearms and gunfights. Guns are LOUD and when ♥♥♥♥ hits the fan, smoke fills the room and it can feel like complete chaos. There is a shield which is pretty useful, but you can't aim well with a sidearm while using it (you mostly need to rely on laser dots), and the shield is far from impenetrable. If it takes enough damage or you take a shotgun point blank it won't save you, and you can still get injured even if you don't die. When you shield is getting shot your camera also shakes all over the place and the glass panels break.Overall the game is really immersive, fun and intense.

_childDocuments_.review: Ready or Not so far is the unofficial successor to SWAT 4. Apart from knowing your objectives there isn't really any story. You essentially make the story by how you and your team work together.Graphics are very well done and make each hallway, open area and room tense. Gun models, armor, grenades, lighting etc. are very detailed and keep you immersed.Sound is phenomenal. Guns are very loud and all sound unique. Reloading and checking ammo (by holding R) sound realistic and crisp. Footsteps are never too loud or quiet and they also make things intense when you hear them from the other side of a door or another room.Like I said before it's intense. This game is not for anyone wanting to run and gun. This game is meant for slow progression and tactics. Enemies are incredibly deadly and can kill you in one shot depending on where they hit. Same goes for you. Team A.I. and enemy A.I. need a bit of work but it's mostly solid. Sometimes enemies will strafe way faster than they should be able to and they hardly ever miss. I've also had one mission where one seemed to spawn right on us. But it was only once in the nearly 8 hours I've played so far. No two missions are ever the same as spawns are randomized which keeps you on your toes. You also need to be careful about who you shoot as killing civs will really affect your score. There will also be flashbang and explosive traps. Some you can see and some you can only detect by either 'peeking' the door or using the mirrorgun. The other thing that helps is deciding on either flashbangs or cs gas for grenades. Without the correct gear your team will be affected by them which can also lead to death. Sometimes enemies seem to ignore grenades but it isn't often. Civs and enemies will also sometimes run away to another room or leave the area entirely and hide somewhere. Keep an eye on the ones who put their hands up because there is a chance they'll decide to change their mind. Online is a mixed bag. _childDocuments_.review: Mediocrity when firing on all cylinders, but mind-numbingly atrocious when it isn't.Ready Or Not has a gargantuan fan base ready to dive on top of the game, primed by the OG Rainbow Six's of yesteryear. VOID Interactive only needs to deliver and relish the fanfare that is heaped upon them. Somehow, it misses this mark by an impressive margin.I liked some parts of the gunplay, but your character feel sluggish to move, peek, and react. This becomes frustrating, when you have the drop on an enemy that manages to swing around and one-tap you before you can bring your weapon up, even when using more agile weapons such as SMGs.Enemies disappear — you'll see want skulking in the next room over, walk over to arrest them, and they disappear. They also seem to spawn in cleared rooms, meaning you'll seem them running around in rooms behind you that you've just cleared.Your allies will consistently body block you in doorways, with fatal funnels becoming a delicious four-man romp of no one being able to move. It's like experiencing red-tape, in-game!If you manage to down the teleporting enemies, after clearing every room in the building at least twice, now the pixel hunt begins! The pixel hunt comes into play if you need to find special objectives, like crystal meth — you can't finish the mission until you find bags of crystal meth, which are not included in gargantuan storage rooms of bagged crystal meth. No, the bags you have to find tend to be hidden under shelves of pitch-black rooms, where your own flashlight blinds you because everything in this game is apparently made out of reflective tape. I  walked quickly around a building for a full hour, doing nothing but trying to find two crystal meth bags — I managed to find one before I alt-F4'd.The optimization is impressively rough — even after eliminating all hostiles, you'll still wildly swing from 8 FPS to 150, and back again. Nothing is occurring minus a search for these damn magical bags different than the hundreds of other ones, and the frame rate is more unstable than Elon Musk.For all of these issues that had me pulling hair out, we could reasonably point to the early access period where bugs are expected. However, if a game is in open early access, where consumers can purchase the title in exchange for game play, that game play can similarly be judged from its execution. And the execution here is sorely lacking in all fronts, from audio to graphics, UI to mission mechanics, AI to gunplay.Yet still, there's one more problem.VOID is selling special early access — which we'll call Earlier Access — for double the cost of the main game. This Earlier Access gives players custom skins not in-game, and also gives access to the experimental branch — you know, what most users use to explore new patches to see if certain bugs and issues have been fixed in Steam's Early Access program. So not only is the title itself atrocious in execution, but the developers don't appear to either understand how Early Access tends to work, or are so fixated on the possibility of making extra cash that they're indifferent to game play experience.Dodge this. I wouldn't make my nemesis play this game. The community is just this hard-up for a new tactical title.

_childDocuments_.review: Really really fun but insanely hard, like a normal enemy will turn a corner and headshot you from across a long hallway, doesn't matter what armor you're wearing or how good your reaction time is. But the gameplay is insanely unfair. First level is reasonable, about 5 enemies who are pretty perceptive. Second level is 10 enemies that can shoot you while taking perfect cover behind support beams on another floor and by the time you realize their location you're already dead. It just gets exponentially harder until the 5th or 6th level where my group of (skillful) friends would get close to the end of a level before an enemy would consistent get the jump on us no matter how carefully or tactically we played.I like difficult enemy AI but balancing is clearly in order. This is a solid 8.0 of 10 experience that is a bit light on content but hoping for more updates and releases as it establishes itself.

_childDocuments_.review: Singleplayer AI is terrible after recent updates. Your teammates are next to useless! They are frequently just in the way, and have limited commands that are useful. For example, they will not opt for less-lethal engagement unless it's equipped as primary. They will use a less-lethal sidearm, BUT only after commanded to equip riot shield (meaning you cannot equip them with breaching shotguns or mirror-guns). Teammates are NOT able to use any of the less-lethal grenade launchers, pepper spray, or battering ram. When equipped with the mirror gun, teammates will occasionally say a room is clear, then immediately encounter enemies firing at you after opening the door. Teammates that deploy grenades also fail to "aim" them; this is annoying when enemies are down a hallway and your team tosses a grade directly in front of the door, stunning YOU instead.This latest update to the AI "morale model" is far from realistic, and has turned this game into "shoot-to-kill" only, making tactics irrelevant. Civilians refuse to surrender even after tasing/pepper spray until at least three of your team are in the room with guns drawn. CS Gas grenades rarely affect anyone outside a 5ft radius, and neither civilian nor enemy AI seem to surrender quickly after deployment of flashbangs or stinger grenades. With or WITHOUT mods the enemy AI almost never surrender, have 10x better accuracy and damage than your teammates, and seem to ignore collision physics when it comes to shooting you behind cover. When any AI DO surrender, they often stop in doorways that are in line-of-fire of enemies that can't be seen from your position; there is no option to "call" surrendered persons towards you.I have not played multiplayer, but expect it would be more enjoyable/realistic to verbally plan tactics with friends. THEN you may have a chance to defeat the relentless AI enemies. If you intend on Singleplayer only, wait until this game is out of Alpha.

_childDocuments_.review: Ready Or Not is one of few early access titles in recent years that has delivered on promises and ensured that their game is in a working, playable, and satisfactory state before its entry into the early access field. Its development and current state even surpasses some full-release AAA games. Most early access titles like to excrete code, slap "Unity" or "UE4" onto their game, and hope that it's enough to warrant full-price for half of a game and a regretful bank transaction statement, but Ready Or Not appears more than promising and reassuring.Did you like SWAT 4? Do you like the idea of working as a SWAT team in a gritty and desolate world of crime? Do you like opening, kicking, knocking, breaching, or blowing up doors? Ready Or Not effectively acts as a spiritual successor to SWAT 4, with satisfying graphics and incredibly intense gunplay. With you and 4 AIs, or yourself and up to 4 friends, you can breach, bang, and clear rooms together, apprehend suspects by means of pepperballs, tasers, or bullets if it comes to it, and secure hundreds of civilians that are typically less-than-compliant.Current criticisms:- I have punched, tazed, pepper-sprayed, pepper-balled, and even shot this armed suspect. Why does he refuse to surrender, stumbling through 12 rooms over the course of 8 minutes?- Who sends a SWAT team into a HOTEL or a CAR DEALERSHIP without giving them a floor plan?- Does every civilian's mom have a Mexican maid?- Why do civilians run towards the armed suspects with machine guns more than they run towards the SWAT team moving in to rescue them?- I'd like to move this civilian I restrained before he gets mowed down in the crossfire because he's sitting in the doorway.Great and fantastic game. Hope they can keep up with their promises.

_childDocuments_.review: First thing I'd say is that this game is definitely worth the $40 price. If you like room clearing or realistic shooters, then you'll love this game. 11 hours in and I'm still invested in the game. The only problems I've had are a few times that bullet penetration does not work at times, the AI are also either programmed to miss half a mag on you or annihilate you within .0001 seconds of seeing you. I'd advise that you have a few friends that are willing to put down 40$ to play, as teamwork is quite necessary in this game. Plus it's quite fun to clear rooms with friends. There seems to be a few times where unarmored enemies in sweatshirts have taken 4 or more rounds of .308 caliber without going down, in which I wonder how someone could survive that much .308 haha. _childDocuments_.review: The SWAT 4 successor we needed, and what Rainbow Six should have become.This game is phenomenal. If you love tactical shooters, then you need not read more, just get it.For those on the fence, or who want more specifics, here goes:Gameplay:smooth, addicting, endlessly replayableThe gunplay, and just moving around the environments feels great, and really puts you in the moment. Top notch, with plenty of variety in weapons and equipment to experiment and try new tactics, either for fun, or to earn those coveted S ranks.Story:Haven't done much of the "story" mode yet, but from what i've seen so far, and heard from others, it is very well done, though likely not what most are here for. It's basically just an excuse to play through all the levels in a set order, and adds continuity to all of them, managing your fellow officers, and their mental and physical health as you progress, as well as eaning bonus abilities/skills for them. The ai is much better than it used to be, but i still personally prefer live teammates. The ai is definitely good enough though, and your allies will generally hold their own, especially if you kit them out effectively for the mission.Free Play:The missions can be unlocked and played freely through multiplayer lobbies, as well as the "practice" mode. "Practice" is the solo free play mode, removing the team management and continuity, and just letting you select a mission to play at will like in multiplayer lobbies. This game is fantastic with friends, and many of the randoms i have met through early access and now with 1.0 have been great. There is a good variety of levels, and i find the majority of them quite fun.Level Design:The amount of detail, visual/environmental storytelling, and even the soundscape of many of the levels is damn impressive. Some maps are small, and some are huge (deceptively so in some cases), some are pretty simple, and some a hectic and challenging even for experienced teams. I can't wait to see more in the future. Personal favorites are the Nightclub, Hospital, and Border Reserve.Progression:The only unlocks in the game are additional levels and cosmetics. Cosmetics are earned through earning certain scores on certain maps, and provide a great incentive to earn those higher ranks, while not impacting the core game at all. Just as it should be done.Variety:The missions cover a vast array of environments/building types, and there is no shortage of weapons or equipment to mess with. Every gun and piece of equipment is viable (with minor bias towards certain things on certain maps), so it's really down to player preference what you take. I absolutely love this, as i hate feeling stuck in one playstyle all the time. The variety across the board is excellent. Performance:There have been some issues with frame drops on certain levels (like the downstairs of Voll Health House), but nothing game breaking, and i assume this will improve in a patch or 2. Supposedly this is also worse on DX11 than DX12, though i haven't checked myself, so i can't confirm that 100%Graphically the game is fantastic.AI:The ai, while still rough in places, and occasionally inconsistent, is vastly better than what it started as. The amount of things the ai can do basically guarantees hiccups will exist, but i haven't experienced anything major. Inconsistencies in reaction times (something you could argue is realistic actually), inconsistent reactions to flashbangs and gas (something present in every shooter every, to be fair), stuff like that.The ai will fake their deaths, find hiding places to pop out of, surrender and then pull a knife on you when you get close, run away and refuse to cooperate, attempt to flank, etc etc etc.So many memorable scenarios can play out in any given mission, and it just makes the game all the more replayable.Overall, i say an easy 9/10The game just keeps getting better. Huge props to the dedicated dev team, and i can't wait to see what else they add.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: After the most recent update the game's difficulty seems to have been scaled for the better. Civilians and enemies now act more natural. The game apparently also did more for the multiplayer lobbies, before this update the host could just restart the match if they died and if they left the mission would quit, not just find a new host, it should now be more of a voting system, so this is also for the better. I'd still like to see AI teammates be present as fillers for when playing with 2-3 friends to make the missions more possible to beat. Information about your weapons, what does the attachments do to them, does AI react on flashlight etc. is still missing and is some of the most important features a SWAT Sim should have IMO. Health in the game is still terrible. My friend got shot in the face point blank with a shotgun and didn't take any damage, and when I get shot in the arm with a pistol my character bleeds out in 3 seconds. Please also fix the health in this game. Ready or Not is a really realistic game when it comes to tactical shooters inspired by SWAT. Games aren't supposed to be realistic to the point it becomes not fun and a steep learning curve, in my opinion (since it's my review). So when the current meta of FPS have health regen or at least more hitpoints then RoN (Ready or Not) it's very hard to migrate over to. This is mosty fine though since the game punishes you for failing (as it should) but when the AI start shooting you through the wall over and over again, you either add more hitpoints to the game, decrease their accuracy or allow revives. Civilians never listen when you tell them to put their hands up and instead run around into firefights, you can see videos of this online, making you fail the mission whether it's your fault or not. Maps are HUGE. There's no way for you to play a short breach mission with the boys (10-15 minutes games), so instead you invest an hour on a mission to fail it by someone spraying you down through the wall. I would not recommend RoN for the current state it is. It has great potential but Early Access is usually for games that are at least playable. And €35.99? How would you put that on a game that isn't even finished yet?Edit: Also on the map where you raid the Meth Lab there's like a 25% chance that an enemy will spawn so close to the spawn area that it will kill you immediatly. And then you can rewatch the 20s load screen again and again :)

_childDocuments_.review: Let me get one thing straight, the entire concept of this game is amazing! I got a good 100fps before the update, and now I only get 45fps and I'll randomly drop to <20fps every time I'm shot or open a door. Teammate AI has regressed. Before the update I was able to effectively maneuver my squad, and eventually completed the hermit achievement. Now the AI gets stuck on each other, ignores commands, or simply just freezes. At least they actually fixed the "Search and Secure" command. Making the newest DLC 10$... for only three levels... and you can only access most of the new content on multiplayer. Yeah thats..wow. The dorm level is so linear, that I was practically falling asleep halfway through. I suggest you wait a couple weeks, maybe month, before giving this game a chance. _childDocuments_.review: Ready or Not is tactically pleasing, fun FPS game. VOIP Interactive outdid themselves with this iteration. The arrest and detain aspects are very realistic, also well done. The one issue I have with this game, again, it is in early access, so these problems will be patched, is that host migration is not fully, (or properly), implemented. When a host leaves the game, the other player(s) lag out, causing them to be forced from the session before the host can re-join the game. Overall, yes, I would recommend this to gamers. _childDocuments_.review: Okay, so my brother and I played this game for a full weekend plus some and it has great potential, but there are some serious issues. I would recommend the game if you know what you're getting into and you're willing to put up with Early Access/Beta (feels like Alpha at times) issues. I'll explain a bit more.1. Bullet Registration - I would say somewhere in the realm of 70% of bullets don't register when shooting someone. I tested this multiple times where the AI didn't know I was there, I would shoot about 5 times and maybe one or two would register actually hitting the target. And yes, I know for a fact I was on target. There's also times where you shoot and they react and as they are reacting they are invincible. I have to at certain times unload 15+ rounds into one person just to get them to drop. By that point they've already shot me and half my body is red or I'm dead. To me, this issue is my main problem with the game. In a game where it's about shooting, bullets HAVE to register otherwise is it really even a game..? My brother and I even tested this at the range at HQ and even there it seemed some of the bullets weren't registering. So that's issue number one and I will admit is extremely frustrating.2. AI Response - This is multi pronged. One issue was stated above briefly but I'll add to it here. When you pop into a room and start shooting they sometimes go into a "surprise" animation that lasts a few seconds. During this animation they are completely invincible and don't react to being shot. I can't tell you how many times we would bust down a door with multiple suspects inside, I'd shoot the first suspect about 5 times then swing to the next and then the first one that I shot would blast me because none of the bullets registered when I shot them. The other issue with their response is if they're turned around with their back to you and you start shooting them, more times than not they'll turn 1/4 of the way, shoot and hit you while not even aiming at you. Super frustrating as well because not only are they not aiming out you, but once again the bullets are registering.3. AI Aiming - This is pretty straight forward but the AI's aim is precise 99% of the time. To the point that they literally almost never miss. Now this probably wouldn't be as much of an issue if the above issues didn't exist. But their bullets seem to register every time while the players bullets do not.4. - AI Shooting Through Objects - The AI can shoot through objects but we can't. Either that or it's the bullets not registering. A few examples are: Chain link fences, walls, cloth/sheets and carts/shelves. Sometimes it seems like it works and we can shoot through these objects but 99% of the time I can shoot right on target and the dude just stands there, back turned, turns 1/4 of the way around and then blasts me and kills me one shot.While all of this is extremely frustrating and pushing me away from the game, when things do work it's truly incredible. When the bullets register, the AI react appropriately, aren't invincible and you can shoot through objects like the AI can it just simply feels great and is extremely enjoyable. The only issue is that works MAYBE 10% of the time. We MIGHT get one shootout per run that just feels good and works, but even that percentage may be high.So for now, this is my review. It's a great game when it works but has fundamental flaws that absolutely needs addressing. So if you know what you're getting into and are okay pushing through these issues while the game gets developed then go for it. Personally though, I would say wait for a few more updates and read reviews then to see if anything has changed. I'll try to update this down the road as the developers continue to develop the game.This has potential to be an amazing game and be on my list as a favorite, but as it stands right now, it has a ways to go.

_childDocuments_.review: Ready or Not is an extremely tactical shooter, that looks to be the successor to the SWAT games. I would also say it has a few gameplay elements that might be comparable for a Rainbow 6 Siege but good PvE for anyone not familiar with SWAT, and for those I'm sure more will get that comparison. There are a few bugs but nothing massively bad or game breaking. 8 maps are available right now and are quite solid. For an Early Access game thats like its in Alpha its pretty impressive even in the state its in now. Guns feel real good too, and all the ways you can deal with situations are quite impressive. It also has some insanely challenging and hard modes like hostage rescue that will force you to ensure you do absolute stealth. AI is crazy smart and good, there are many mix up animations and scenarios they will use from shooting around corners and pretending to put there hands up for arrest all to quickly pull a gun out on you. Graphics look pretty good and will improve later on as well. This game does not mess around and there isn't an easier setting for gaming journalists or casuals. So be aware this game is not easy. Each mission has a lot of telling of stories of the scenarios as well, and rooms and locations of objectives, people, traps, and enemies are always random.8/10 - I in its current alpha like state give it a solid 8, with some interesting more ideas and things to come like drones and other equipment, guns, and maps, this game is definitely worth its price even in this early access state and has a lot of room to grow, even when at its foundation as of now, is quite impressive.

Already an extremely steep price for an early access title, let alone one this early in development. That would be bad, and I could just shrug that off, but I didn't know, nor was this ever made apparent, is that I did not in fact buy early access. I bought early-ish access. Updates are pushed to people who bought the supporter edition a few weeks in advance, regular edition buyers will receive news of the new update on the games update feed in their library, but must wait an undisclosed amount of time before they can play it, in the words of moderators on update discussion threads this amount of time is "a couple of weeks, usually, until bugs are ironed out".The supporter edition is 150 dollars in my currency (AUD). 150 dollars for what? To get updates on time, and a few cosmetic skins. Steam discussion threads are full of people with no sense who think it's a good idea to just piss money up the wall defending this absolutely scummy pricing model. "yeah it's called the supporter edition and it's so expensive because it's for people who want to support the development of the game." Yeah? Like what many of us did by trusting the developers to produce a good game and treat consumers fairly despite their already steep price point of 50 bucks? Is that not supporting development? What was my 50 for then?"If you won't buy supporter edition then just wait don't be impatient and entitled". Well you are damn right I am impatient and you are damn right I am entitled. I paid 50 dollars, that's far more than I've ever paid for an early access game, games in far more complete states than this, games with far better polish, games that received regular updates and communication from devs, and often including an experimental branch (and never behind an additional paywall), we are entitled to our money's worth and many of us don't feel we are getting that.There's no justification for it, there is absolutely no reasonable argument why 50 dollars is not more than enough money to get access to the game with updates on time. You want to have a 150 dollar version of the game with a few cosmetic skins? Hell, maybe even a bonus gun or 2? Fine, still scummy but whatever. But 150 dollars to get ACTUAL early access when the regular edition is already 50 bucks is just not understandable.It's such a shame because I really do like this game would love to have been able to leave a positive review, but I cannot do so in good conscience while the developers put updates behind a paywall. I'd still be complaining if the pay wall was 5 bucks, let alone 3x the price of the base game JUST TO GET UPDATES ON TIME (and some some skins... whatever). Updates are very far apart, and often very thin in terms of content. At time of writing there has recently been a much awaited massive updated released. This update was announced to come out last month but was continuously delayed. It finally dropped, many of us were excited to finally get our hands on this long awaited updated BUT WAIT! Did you pay for the supporter edition? Oh, too bad. Guess you'll have to wait. How long? Dunno, can't tell you. Sometime, maybe soon, maybe not. Who can say? It's a terrible way of doing early access and it is indefensible.Insane. Anyone who happily pays that price, I don't care how rich you are, you have no shame. I don't know what level of content and polish a game would need to have in it for it to be worth 150 dollars, but this is certainly not it. I wouldn't pay 150 bucks for some of my favourite games of all time, let alone a game that isn't even finished yet. This pricing model is simply disrespectful.

_childDocuments_.review: A compelling representation of today's police force. You are the one who dictates what kind of SWAT agent you want to be. I may not be in the force, but I can almost bet this game does a great service to those who have conducted operations in this field.An immense amount of effort was put into this game, and it truly shows as a testament of love for the USA's police force. It brings forth harsh realities like sex trafficking, terrorism, drug abuse, and homelessness, but through the lens of a SWAT officer.I'd be lying if I said this game hasn't inspired me to join the police force myself. It's that good.My only complaint is that it isn't fleshed out enough. It doesn't look like the devs expected this kind of popularity, and so the story is a bit bland. It gets really interesting at the very end, but then that's it.Although this game is a masterclass of our time, more work can be done on the story aspect of the game. I feel like we just touched the surface of what this game can truly be.TLDR: Worth every penny.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game ruined by enemies that are immune to flashbangs, can shoot you faster than a human can react, and can target you through walls. Yes, it's a slow paced, tactical shooter, but even getting the drop on enemies, gun aimed at them, you can get shot the moment you tell them to drop their weapons. A game about SWAT should be focused on taking the enemies alive if possible, dead if necessary, but if you dare deploy less lethal options you WILL die. Some constructive criticism for the devs, who will certainly ignore it as they tend to do: fix the bugs. Got softlocked in training three times, softlocked when I died in Ironman and couldn't get to the main menu. Also, let me skip the score screen. Playing single player, you have to wait 10 seconds after accepting the mission, then wait through a loading screen, then wait ten more seconds before the mission will start. Between that and the score screen, it can take minutes between getting shot through the wall and dying and being able to try again. Why no 'quick restart' option?

_childDocuments_.review: This is the most tentative recommendation I could possibly give this game, It is essentially a modern update of SWAT 4 which is overdue the problem comes in some the details.  For one the AI can be a bit finicky on your side but straight cheating on the opposing side.  Mods can remove their wallhacks and dampen their superhuman reaction time but it still feels inexcusably lazy by the devs that it was like this for 1.0.  The thing that really frustrates me is the singleplayer mode has no "Restart mission" option so you have to alt-f4 if you want to start the mission over if one of your guys gets beamed, or a civilian gets dropped.  If you quit normally it will kill your officers and send the surviving ones to therapy, if you extract you have to go through multiple annoying screens just to restart the mission, and even then it may still jack up your officers stress and it won't un-kill any that get downed in mission, so alt-f4 is the only real option if you don't want to waste your time.
