_childDocuments_.review: This game is genuinely fun at times but it’s not all there. It feels more like frustration condensed into a little jar and the game going through developmental hell doesn’t help. I like the idea, premise, art direction, some gameplay mechanics and some level design but as a whole experience it’s awful. It’s blatantly unfinished and should not have been released 1.0 of December 2023. I feel as if I can't mention anything about the good parts about the game because they’re so overshadowed by constant issues. I don’t recommend paying full price for this game let alone at 50% discount.The biggest issue and probably the biggest point of criticism is AI. It is absolutely beyond ♥♥♥♥♥♥. If you thought Escape From Tarkov scavs were bad then I would say that Ready or Not suspects are on equal footing. You are not going up against some gang-bangers in the hood. They’re clearly cracked special-forces units being deployed to Los Sueños. Those armed robbers at the gas station in the first mission? Those guys are actually undercover Spetsnaz operatives. But seriously, though. Why is it like I’m fighting an army of T-800 Terminators? Suspects are so aggressive and cheat so much. They see through walls, will shoot you through them and have laser aimbot accuracy. They also have no self-preservation. On the same first mission I went around the back on the left side and zip-tied two people outside. One civvie and a suspect. I checked under the double doors and there was no one. I ordered the team to open and clear (no grenades). I go left and there’s two doors - one directly in front and another to the right with a staff only sign. I was checking under the front door and got blasted through both the wall and door that had the staff only sign while I was using the optiwand. The suspect then opened the door and blasted me some more, retreated further back into the room they were in and grabbed a hostage. There is no reason that should have happened. It was a quiet entry with no breaching devices or explosives. If it’s because they heard me zip tie someone outside that’s just equally stupid. For a game that boasts “realism” it already fails that. I have also had issues with the mission “A Lethal Obsession” where suspects would sometimes use doors wired with explosive traps to try to get to me and either blow themselves up or kill me and the entire team stacking up outside it because they can clearly see me through walls. There are some other oddities with suspects that don’t make entire sense. They have no self-preservation and will always try to fight you rather than surrender. You’ll go to zip tie someone and they’ll pull out a knife. Some suspects will actually feign a surrender and get to their knees before pulling out a hidden pistol. I like that idea but not with how frequently it seems to happen. I can understand that for  suspects to be doing these things but it feels like it's almost all of them. I can understand terrorists doing it but not some random private security guard or generic no-name gang-banger. I want some suspects to run and hide and I want others to try and fight. Not everyone should shoot you at a moment's notice. Some suspects do try to hide and run away but it happens so little. Suspects can hide under beds and in closets but that's only available on a small handful of maps. Some maps have holes in the walls and suspects can move between them but more often than not they use them to attack you from behind rather than to try and get away. Non-compliance is also a good idea but doesn't play as I feel that it should and is more of an annoyance than anything. How many beanbags do I have to dump into a guy before they get to the ground? I have emptied entire mag-tubes while mashing the “yell for compliance” key for it to all be ignored. Some suspects just outright ignore tasers, beanbags, the pepperball guns and the pepper spray can. CS gas seems to be the only effective non-lethal option. There is no way to force someone to the ground if they ignore compliance and there really should be an option to do so. There's also plenty of dialogue that makes no sense given the context. Why are the civilians in "Neon Tomb" defending terrorists and saying they did nothing wrong when I blast them for shooting me? Terrorists in "Relapse" also sometimes act as if they are innocent and did nothing wrong when you zip tie them. It feels out of character. Los Locos members are always aggressive towards you once zip tied and some will have lines about asking for deals so they can be cut loose. That makes perfect sense for them. The terrorists should have much more aggressive and fanatical dialogue. The SWAT AI is also beyond useless. It feels like I’m constantly babysitting. They can’t do anything right and frequently ignore commands. It works okay enough if things do work. They seem to have a hard time engaging anything out of the room they are currently in and will typically ignore threats outside of it. They constantly struggle with “move and clear” commands and won't do them. This is especially apparent when stairs are involved. They’ll prioritise zip-tying people and collecting evidence instead of fighting back when getting shot. Sometimes you’ll have to issue a command a second or third time just to get them to do something. I don’t know why this is but the SWAT AI will sometimes move towards civilians and suspects backwards or diagonally to zip tie them. Commander Mode isn’t great either and it’s half-baked. It’s the de facto single player mode. You have a roster you fill out and each officer has a trait that can be unlocked after doing some missions with them. The traits don’t seem to do much and I forget they are even there. Sometimes when doing missions or failing them stress of a team member will go up and then you have to send them to therapy. That’s it, that’s Commander Mode. I feel like there should be more to it but that’s it. On top of all these issues the game’s performance isn’t optimised and it's filled with bugs. If you told me this game was made by Bethesda I’d believe you. Performance isn’t consistent and gets pretty bad on some missions. “Ides of March”, “Valley of Dolls” and “Relapse” are some examples of missions with awful performance that I have experienced.  There is also so much clipping and it really shows how unfinished the game is. NPCs have clipping with their clothes and so does the SWAT cosmetics for you and your team. As an example, gas masks don’t fit correctly on suspects faces and the headband clips through their heads. Some of the other bugs I have encountered is that sometimes the HUD bugs out and places itself in the top left corner of your screen. The phone/PDA thing that you use to manage your roster and check mission briefings can become unresponsive when opening it and won't let you select anything. Sometimes NPCs become shadow-people and have a completely black texture. Sometimes when leaning with the taser it won’t hit it’s target and that makes me think it's hitting an invisible collision mesh. I’ve had SWAT AI yell at suspects standing outside closets. I’ll shoot them with a taser to get them to comply and they’ll either rubberband or warp back inside the closet and exit it. Zip-tying downed suspects or civilians sometimes causes them to ragdoll and launch very slightly into the air. SWAT AI sometimes can’t see suspects in a room when entering and won’t engage them. Sometimes suspects in that same room will only engage the player and ignore the SWAT AI. Honestly, anything I’ve mentioned about the AI can be assumed as bugs or just ♥♥♥♥ game design. Ready or Not’s modding scene is in its infancy but there are some AI reworks and fixes for things.

_childDocuments_.review: Ready or Not, a game that has already captured the hearts of many in its early access phase, has recently unveiled its Version 1.0, marking a significant evolution from its previous iteration. As a veteran player who has spent countless hours in the early access version, I approached the full release with a blend of excitement and curiosity. What I discovered was a game that has not only improved but has been fundamentally transformed, offering an experience that feels fresh and invigorating.The first thing that strikes you in Version 1.0 is the overhauled user interface. The main menu and police station, crucial hubs of the game, have been completely reimagined, setting the tone for the rest of the experience. The attention to detail is evident, and these changes contribute significantly to the game's immersive quality.The improvements extend to the map levels as well. The developers have meticulously enhanced every aspect of these environments, resulting in a more cohesive and believable world. The AI, previously a point of contention, now boasts a semblance of intelligence, fundamentally altering the way you engage with the game.The gameplay mechanics have undergone a comprehensive overhaul. AI behavior, a critical component of tactical shooters, has seen significant improvements. Enemies now exhibit smarter movements, capable of navigating through complex environments and reacting more realistically to player actions. This heightened intelligence not only makes the game more challenging but also more rewarding, as it demands a higher level of strategic planning and execution from the player.The graphical fidelity of Ready or Not has always been a strong point, and Version 1.0 continues this tradition. The environments are richly detailed, and the lighting effects add a layer of realism that is truly captivating. This visual splendor plays a significant role in the overall immersion, making each session feel like a step into a vividly realized world.The narrative in Ready or Not is well-constructed, with a clear and engaging storyline that unfolds across the levels. The game's sound design deserves special mention. The background music and environmental sounds create an atmosphere that is both tense and immersive. The footsteps, the echoes in the corridors, the distant shouts—all contribute to a soundscape that is as realistic as it is unnerving.The voice acting, particularly in the 911 calls, is exceptional. It's not just the quality of the acting but the emotional weight it carries. These moments often leave a lingering sense of unease, a testament to the voice actors' ability to convey distress and fear in a convincing manner.One of the game's strongest suits is its replayability. With a variety of weapons, tactics, and approaches at your disposal, each playthrough offers a new experience. The scoring system encourages players to continually refine their strategies and aim for higher achievements.The modding community further enhances this aspect, constantly adding new levels, weapons, and elements that keep the game fresh and exciting. This thriving mod scene is a crucial component of Ready or Not's longevity, offering players endless opportunities to explore and experiment.Version 1.0 of Ready or Not is a triumph of game development. It takes the solid foundation laid by the early access version and builds upon it in every conceivable way. The game offers an experience that is both challenging and rewarding, bolstered by excellent graphics, sound design, and a strong narrative. For fans of tactical shooters, Ready or Not in its current form is an essential play, offering an experience that is as immersive as it is intense. Whether you're a returning player or new to the game, Ready or Not is poised to redefine expectations and set new standards in the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Hearing about the 1.0 release I was interested in playing this game again with friends since we played the early access and despite its issues we thought the dev team would iron those out and make the game a true successor to SWAT 4.After playing for a few hours I care safely say that it is still the same janky game except you can no longer pick the maps and situation you want and have to unlock them in order which is annoying. The enemies are all still ridiculous and the game still runs very poorly.The issues with the AI are very apparently in the new stage 24 megabits per second in which the team go to investigate a barricaded suspect streamer who is actually just getting swatted and is not actually at that time doing anything to warrant the cops kicking down his door.This streamer who you must arrest has his fortnight crew or something with him because the second that door is opened his entire team attack you with shotguns and one guy had an AK-47, remember these are supposed to be a bunch of guys in an apartment and not a terrorist cell. Now because you have to arrest the streamer you can instantly fail the mission by shooting the guy. Mind you when you go into the house screaming "police hands up" he will unload a shotgun into your team, pull a handgun and mag dump you and then maybe he will surrender. If this was real life the cops would have shot him the second he attempted to raise the gun but this game forces some BS were you cannot shoot them.Annoyed my friend and I gave it another go on the crack den mission where I had a perp walk out of a room armed and looking at a wall. I told the suspect to surrender to which they turned, raised the weapon and fired twice at me in 1 frame with no animation of them turning or raising the gun to give me maybe 2 seconds at least to make a decision, it was just instant and after that I just gave up trying to convince myself this was anything like SWAT 4.

_childDocuments_.review: "Ready or Not Multiplayer: Frustrating Lag Spikes and Glitches Ruin the Action"I have to be brutally honest: playing Ready or Not in multiplayer mode has been an absolute rollercoaster of frustration and disappointment. The promising premise of intense tactical gameplay gets obliterated by rampant technical issues that turn the experience into a digital nightmare.Let's start with the lag spikes. They hit like a sledgehammer out of nowhere, yanking you out of immersion at the most critical moments. Imagine maneuvering through high-stakes missions, only to freeze mid-action due to inexplicable lag. It's beyond infuriating. These spikes aren't occasional hiccups; they're regular and ruin the fluidity that multiplayer gaming demands.And oh, the guns! Prepare for a magician's act because your precious firearms have a penchant for disappearing into thin air. You're locked and loaded, ready to take on the cartel, only to find your primary weapon vanishing into the digital abyss. It's comically tragic and utterly unacceptable in a game that touts realism and tactical precision.Speaking of the cartel enemies, the rulebook seems to have been thrown out the window. They've apparently been granted bulletproof enhancements while you're left scratching your head. Suddenly, it takes an army's worth of bullets to bring them down. The balance is so skewed that it's no longer about skillful strategy but an endurance test against bullet sponge foes.To add insult to injury, the enemies donning body armor, designed to provide protection, seem to have missed the memo. Instead of being a formidable challenge, they crumble like paper under the slightest pressure. It's baffling and breaks the immersion when armored enemies turn out to be the easiest targets.Ready or Not promised an intense, tactical multiplayer experience but falls flat on its face due to these crippling issues. Lag spikes disrupt the flow, guns vanish into thin air, enemies become bullet sponges, and armored foes are oddly vulnerable. Until these fundamental flaws are fixed, this game is a frustrating mess that's best avoided in its current state. Buyer beware—you might end up more frustrated than entertained.

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of realism-based shooters, Ready or Not hits that sweet spot I’ve been searching for. This game isn’t your typical run-and-gun style; it’s about strategy, teamwork, and being smart with your approach. For anyone who’s into the tactical gameplay of titles like Arma 3, Escape from Tarkov, or Squad, this game is going to feel like a breath of fresh air. Ready or Not goes all in on that realistic SWAT team experience. It’s got that same intensity you’d find in old-school tactical shooters like SWAT 4 or the more modern vibes of Rainbow Six Siege. Every corner you turn and every door you breach feels tense, making you second-guess every move. The attention to detail here is on point, with tactics and planning taking center stage. If you’re a fan of games that make you think and use strategy over pure reflexes, this is the one. Honestly, this game shines brightest when you’ve got a good squad by your side. Coordinating with your buddies to clear rooms, secure hostages, or take down threats is some of the most satisfying gameplay I’ve ever experienced. When you and your team are moving in sync, it feels like you’re in a scene straight out of a tactical thriller. If you’ve enjoyed team-based gameplay in titles like Insurgency: Sandstorm or Project Reality, you’ll get a kick out of this. There’s something special about a game that makes you slow down and think about every decision. It reminds me of the intensity from classic games like Operation Flashpoint and even the strategy elements of Commandos: Behind Enemy Lines. The realistic approach makes every mission unpredictable, and that’s what keeps me coming back for more. If you’re into tactical shooters that prioritize realism, then Ready or Not should be at the top of your list. The thrill of clearing out locations with a well-coordinated team is unmatched, and the game rewards strategy and communication over simple reflexes. For fans of realism-based shooters like me, this game is pure gold, and it’s worth diving into with your squad.Whether you’re a die-hard fan of the genre or just looking for something different from the usual shooter experience, Ready or Not delivers a solid, immersive tactical adventure that’s hard to put down.

_childDocuments_.review: It really pains me a lot to give this game a negative review, I've been waiting for it since the first announcemente in 2017, and I've been playing it since the first open beta, I've had a lot of fun with friends in multiplayer, specially during the beta, but as of the current state of the game I gotta say this game was not ready for a full release.After more than 200 hours on this game and having completed most of the achievements except for the medal of valor (get S rank in every mission) I feel confident enough to give a review and criticize this game in full.I'll leave a list down with the good and the bad stuff of the game so you can come to your own conclussions before buying.I'll start with the GOOD STUFF:-Extremely fun to play with friends-The gunplay is probably the best there's in the FPS genre-Guns not only look and sound good, they feel really satisfying to use, I can't think of a single gun I dislike-The free lean system is the best thing they've implemented so far, it works really well for small peaks and ducking when getting shot, and it's a fun system.-Slow paced gameplay which feels like a relief, specially after the oversaturation of hyper fast shooters.-Every mission feels challenging, yet fun, specially with friends-Maps look really good (I still prefer some of the old ones, but new ones are great too)-The briefing add for the final game it's a really nice and immersive implementation-You can customize your operator-The game looks really good graphically-Character models are great-The lore is pretty interesting-Ambiental storytelling is really fun, and I still discover new stuff constantly-The suspects and civis are distributed differently on every playthrough which gives the game A LOT of replayability-I still discover new stuff that can happen or stuff the suspects can do, even after 200 hours of gameplay.-In-game mod support and a great mod community-Extremely good mods-Great community-You can still unlock most of the accessories, clothes and stuff in multiplayerTHE BAD STUFF:Friendly AI issues:-They'll obey orders only half of the time you give it to them-When you give any order that requires them to move on their own "open/move and clear", "stack up", "deploy X", etc sometimes they don't go directly to the place you send them and instead take a long path to the objective alone.-If you give the order "open and clear" or "move and clear" they will start clearing the entire map and splitting themselves until receiving a different order, this will get them all killed one by one more often than not.-The auto pick up and auto arrest thing they added to the AI will get them killed a lot and doesn't really help at all.-The way they clear rooms doesn't make sense a lot of times; they'll get into a room facing a wall and get shot in the back-They will always prioritize switching to the secondary weapon before reloading, even if they don't have any ammo on their secondary weapon, this will get them killed a lot.-If they have a shield and no ammo on their pistol they'll switch to their primary weapon and get hurt or killed.-They won't use their shields most of the times.-When "opening gas, sting or flash and clearing" they will drop the grenades in the most ineffective possible way, most of the time they won't have an effect at all.-They don't duck and they rarely take cover under fire.-They will ALWAYS start yelling at suspects and civis on sight, killing any possibility of a stealthy approach, getting YOU killed a lot.-Sometimes they aim like John Wick, sometimes they miss EVERY shot, it's incredibly inconsistent.-Their grenades are inconsistent, sometimes they'll use 2 grenades (having prepared up to 4 for each) and the "deploy grenade" or "open flash, smoke or sting" option will be greyed like if they had no more left.-They will only use 1 GRENADE per grenade launcher, they don't reload it, and the option will be greyed as well.Enemy AI Issues:-Extremely inconsistent, sometimes they one tap you on sight, sometimes they don't hit anything.-Even the lowest goon will have a "John Wick" moment and one tap kill your entire team and you with a pistol.-They'll track you throw walls once they get on alert, but they'll conveniently do things like leaving the place you're mirroring or you placed your team in a stack formation on doors even if they're not on alert-They'll shoot you throw walls-They'll see you throw smoke and shoot you like if it wasn't there-They have infinite magazines-Even the most petty criminal will fight to the very end with everything they have and pull multiple weapons on you-Every single suspect, no matter of how petty they are will ALWAYS fake surrender, sometimes pulling up to 4 weapons on you -I've got a crackhead pull 4 weapons on me on twisted nerve (a tec-9, a sawed shotgun, a pistol and a knife)-They take a stupid amount of less than lethal shots before they start complying (up to a pepper ball magazine or 4 bean bag bullets)Equipment issues:-The grenades are at their worst state, they're extremely inconsistent. -The new CS gas sucks so bad, it creates a thick smoke screen that only affects your sight, enemies will shoot throw it like if it wasn't there.-If a gas falls under a bed, cabinet, or any small surface the smoke won't come out.-Stings and flashes have a random chance of exploding on enemies feet and not affecting them AT ALL.-Grenades bounce inconsistently-Sometimes when you throw grenades into a room and they disappear and appear on your back, this is more frequent with smoke grenades-There's no short throw option for grenades.-C2 will one shot civis, but only stun suspects-Less than lethal options are too few and inconsistent-The Less than lethal shotgun is extremely lethal, one headshot is always a kill, so as a less than lethal option is not worth it.-You can't shoot between metal bars or relatively small spaces (up to a basketball size) with bean bags or pepper balls, they'll always collide like if it was a wall.-Smoke grenade launcher bounces too much and in random ways, making it extremely impractical.-Pepper spray is currently useless because enemies will still shoot you with their John Wick aimbot even when blinded by it.-Since now tasers are gadgets you can't equip them with shields anymore-The meelee option is too slow and practically useless for anything but hitting fake surrendering suspects, the animation is pretty ugly too and the hit scan is pretty small.-Can't add camo to weapons :(Multiplayer:-Lots of crashes-Longer loading screens-No campaign for multiplayerCommanders Mode:-They removed mission types (IE:Barricaded suspect, Hostage Situation, Bomb Threat, Active Shooter) to add commanders mode-No retry option, every time you fail a mission you have to go back to the HQ, select the mission, launch it, and load the map.-The stress system for officers is annoying and not fun.-As a campaign mode it barely adds anything-With the game current status it's not fun at all-Should have the possibility to play it in multiplayer, even without bots, the officer skills system could be an interesting thing for multiplayer-Doesn't add much, it's not too different from "practice mode" except that you can't select missions you haven't unlocked, officers have permadeath, and you have to leave the mission and go to HQ every time you fail a missionIronman mode:-Don't... Really, don't. I did it. It's not worth it. It's not fun. Something in you will have died whenever you finish it.Practice mode:-Should be named Arcade_______________TLRD: Overall it's a good game with a lot of issues, at it's current state it's not worh $50. If you are considering buying it I  recommend you wait until the devs fix the game or for a big sale, SPECIALLY if you want to play SP or have no one to play with. The SP is just not fun. I really hope they fix the game and that I have to delete this review in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: "Ready or Not" isn't just a game for me; it's a gripping experience that has evolved with each update and iteration. The initial phase with the Alpha PVP mode may have disappointed many, but with the Coop release, the tables turned, rewarding those who saw its potential.After years of anticipation since "Swat 4," a new chapter was finally unveiled with Version 1.0. The team AI has reached its zenith – smarter, more effective, and, above all, more realistic. The tight teamwork in battles is remarkable; they act tactically wise, covering corners and forming strategic formations.A significant leap forward is the addition of background stories to missions. No longer just catapulted into scenarios; instead, dialogue and 911 calls provide a captivating context, intensifying immersion. Finally, you can understand why you're in a particular building and the challenges you face.The option to send team members to therapy is not only an innovative addition but also a human aspect in the game. It shows that developers aren't solely focused on action but also address the mental strain on characters. A team consists of people, not just pixelated avatars.Overall, "Ready or Not" has proven, through its progress and profound enhancements, that it's not just a game but a journey. A journey that not only revives the nostalgia of "Swat 4" but also paves the way for a new era in the tactical shooter genre. Personally, it's more than just fun – it's an emotional rollercoaster full of intensity and teamwork.As a devoted Close-Quarters-Battle (CQB) enthusiast, I'm always on the lookout for the next adrenaline rush in the tactical shooter genre. "Ready or Not" has not only exceeded my expectations but truly blown me away. As someone impressed by the SWAT games, this title not only continues the tradition but elevates it to a new level – and that is genuinely legendary.The attention to detail in CQB moments is breathtaking. Every step in a tight corridor, every door that swings open, and every moment of tension are masterfully captured. The team AI, functioning like a well-oiled machine, makes immersing into these tactical missions an unparalleled experience. As a lover of tactical shooters, I appreciate not only the visual brilliance but also the strategic depth that "Ready or Not" provides.The decision to delve into the background of missions and infuse characters with more personality has transformed the game for me into more than just a shooter. It's an emotional journey where I'm not just fighting for survival but also forming a connection with virtual characters. The addition of the therapy option for team members shows that the developers don't neglect the human aspect – a dimension often overlooked in other games.In a gaming landscape dominated by spectacular graphics, "Ready or Not" has proven that true beauty lies in the depth of the player experience. As a CQB fan and a lover of tactical shooters, this game has not only impressed me but also touched me emotionally. It's more than just a game – it's an epic journey that captures the essence of tactical gaming and presents it in a way that deepens my passion for the genre. Bravo, Void Interactive, for a masterpiece that has conquered the hearts of tactical shooter enthusiasts like myself.A monumental thank you to Void Interactive for years of tireless dedication and commitment to perfecting "Ready or Not." Your unparalleled effort has not only given birth to a game but crafted an epic masterpiece that redefines the boundaries of the tactical shooter genre.In every line of code, in every polygon of design, one can feel the love and care poured into creating this game. It's as if you didn't just develop a game but infused a passion in the form of code and graphics. "Ready or Not" is more than a product; it's an artistic dedication that extends through every movement, every shot, and every moment of tension.The decision not to rest on laurels but consistently work towards improvement speaks of a pursuit of perfection that is not only admirable but also rare in the gaming industry. You haven't just released a game; you've continuously refined your vision to offer players an experience that not only entertains but also captivates.Every enhancement, every patch, and every update reflects your dedication that goes beyond the ordinary. You haven't just perfected a game; you've taken a community of players on a journey deeper than many could have imagined.In a world where game development is often characterized by time constraints and commercial pressures, "Ready or Not" stands as a shining example of artistic integrity and the pursuit of excellence. Void Interactive, your efforts have not only created a game but also garnered admiration and gratitude within the gaming community that is truly legendary. Virtually raising our controllers, we salute you – for a game that has conquered not only our screens but also our hearts. _childDocuments_.review: I have upgraded my PC and played for more hours. Time to update the review!!!!The graphics in this game are still very nice. Although, the game tends to have poor optimisation when something new comes out. It's worth waiting for some patches after an update before playing again.The game play is rather slow, but that should be expected. I wish I had more free-look angle and maybe more move speed, but there's a small fix for that which I will talk to you about later. For shooting, weapons within the same category feel very similar, the only really defining difference being damage and situational effectiveness. The SR16 for a long time has been considered extremely powerful for it's low recoil and high damage output.As far as I have found, there's nothing that really destroys the game . The most common bugs I see is corpses phasing through walls and some weapon evidence being extremely difficult to find.The modding community is amazing. DLC quality changes to the game for completely free. These changes reach from small appearance changes to completely game-changing content and tweaks. One example of an appearance change being a weapon model replacement. However, there are mods like Gunfighter Improvements, A.I. behaviour changes, and new weapons all together.The price has gone up from Early Access ($40USD) and is now $50USD. For the state of this game, $50USD is not all that worth. If anything, $40-$45USD was probably a better price for this game. If this game does go on such a sale, I recommend trying it out with some friends. Otherwise, wait another few major updates or so.New section so that I can talk about something I noticed. The development plan for this game sounds good, and the updates aren't 100% disappointing. However, the development is extremely slow for the quality of the updates. I'm not a professional in any way at making games, so I do not know how much effort the devs are actually putting in, but the updates just don't feel worth for the time we wait. I feel like if more people help the development team, it would be a large help for the future of this game. The slow updates if not sped up may be the fall of this game.For $50USD, you get a very decent quality SWAT4 sequel. Great graphics, decent game play, and access to a large modding community that will help you play even more. However, the development is slow. I will let you decide whether it is worth or not.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game with friends, but if you're gonna try to solo complete it you just need to understand that its not going to be fun, you are hardly ever going to lose because of something that you did. I was waiting so long to buy because the first thing I thought about when the game was initially announced was okay this is gonna be a buggy indie mess. Still, all this time later, the game is stacked to the brim with broken BS. The environment hitboxes for you will be absolutely awful, but for the enemy they are perfect to the pixel. Imagine how much fun it was to always lose engagements to a headglitcher before I realized that they were literally invincible. In certain situations, the enemy will have a 0.1 second reaction time (someone timed this) which is faster than any human, meaning, unless you dug in the files, you wouldn't know that you have an exactly 0% chance of winning an engagement against someone who is aiming at a doorway during an S rank run. The focal point of the game, the arrest mechanics, are absolutely busted. You must be behind the suspect and on the exact same Y level as them in order to make an arrest. Enjoy  getting swiss cheesed every single time you have to spend 3 minutes arresting a guy on the stairs. Getting a suspect to quit fighting (which is required for all suspects for an S rank run) is up to completely random chance. The worst case of this I had was on the third level. The main suspect you need to arrest took 2 entire mag tubes of bean bag shotgun rounds before giving up. I had to shoot, let him go through his agony animation and shoot again (5 whole minutes of just sitting there and shooting this guy). By then the entire maps enemies had closed in on me and I immediately died. If you want to get all your achievements you just have to accept that it is entirely rng based. You will be fully equipped to beat every level after your 3rd-5th attempt but will only not do so because of some glitch. Maybe your evidence falls through the floor or your arrested/dead decide they want to tpose in the air and make completion impossible. It feels as though nothing in this game was playtested or thought through besides lethal gunplay, everything else was an afterthought that they had to add to their gory killing simulator, and yet they still require it for perfect completion, and by extension, your character customization. It's a cool, enjoyable game, but to claim that this is worth 40$ with such little polish is stupid.

_childDocuments_.review: This "release update" was truly a step backwards. Somehow the game has more bugs than ever, crashes frequently, and has horrible frame rate. I loved the game when it was in early access, looking past the cracked enemy AI and small bugs that made levels unable to be cleared sometimes, because I was really hopeful for what future updates brought. However, this recent update not only removed nearly half of the gameplay features, but also disrespected the game's early supporters in a way I've never seen before.No longer can you switch up missions with different objectives, such as raid, hostages, bomb threat, and barricaded suspects. The missions are what they are, all because it didn't make sense for their single-player campaign that nobody asked for. On top of that, some mission maps have been reduced, entire sections blocked off and inaccessible for reasons unknown; This causes some levels to feel smaller and ill-thought out. The suspect AI, which has been broken since first release, has never been fixed. I'm very surprised that they carried this crackshot superman AI all the way to release. It's almost as if the developers don't play their own game, or even listen to the community for feedback.As for the people who bought the supporter edition of this game, I can say that I've never seen a developer not only remove the supporter gear/loot/equipment, but to then replace it with a half-baked replacement that isn't even exclusive anymore. The supporters get a few guns that are just re-skins, but they used to have FBI HRT player models that are no longer in the game. Yes, the developers gave the supporters "different" multicam uniform customizations, but they hardly feel exclusive due to the fact that multicam patterns are available on regular uniforms. This may not seem like a big deal, so what, it's just some cosmetics. This feels incredibly disrespectful to the people who shelled out an extra $80 US to support the development of a game they loved.Overall, this release is not only a massive step backwards from early access, it's also slap to the face of the player base that has been following since the game was announced years ago. If you want to play a methodical shooter with friends that actually works, buy Ground Branch instead.

_childDocuments_.review: - Ready or Not started off as a promising rookie in the Tactical Shooter sub-genre. Seemingly with a glint in their eyes, it went through a long period of Early Access in an attempt to be the perfect spiritual successor and contemporary interpretation of the renown local veteran, .Unfortunately, the only thing time on the field offered to Ready or Not was jadedness. Doing the right thing turned out hard, and the benefits for so would most likely not pay off. It grew authoritarian in its dullness, abandoning its ideal vision and adopting instead a gorged caricature with a strong beating heart that pumps incompetence.The gameplay of Ready or Not (RoN) can be summed up as a hardcore PvE game where a small team of heroes will usually go against a battalion of incomprehensibly suicidal felons armed to the teeth that need to be put down at all costs. You can see some very  on the net, where players will dynamically enter a civilian building and annihilate every "bad guy" with gunshow levels of lethal weaponry to choose from.This would all be fine as a premise, if not for the fact the intended way for a game like this to be played, and the way its score system works at the highest level and difficulty, would be to have the ideal of  There's a big gaping hole in the core of RoN which makes its gameplay loop a boring failure, noticeably: Even in the event you are willing to ignore the game score rating and barge into civilian households with a full auto Armor Piercing weaponry under zero objections, the game will force you to locate and apprehend civilians in the map and other "evidence" garbage before you finish the scenario, just to rub it in that "it's a SWAT game". This also happens to be the excuse for there not being a "run" button, a match made in hell itself.RoN uses the Unreal Engine 4 (UE) to a good amount of its potential and enjoys displaying high fidelity assets in detailed environments with innumerable amounts of shades. Unfortunately, this may as well be the uniform for any self-entitled UE powered game.What RoN does with its uniformity is create a lot of visual pollution. A lot of things seem to be placed just for the sake of being placed, as if it's trying to justify having paid for those assets. Some of them are out of scale with the player size, giving you the impression the city is some sort of society composed of Elves and Dwarves; maybe the gameplay loop would have been more coherent if it were.Lights and Lasers work out terribly depending on the graphical setting, often "reflecting" or being drowned by other ambient lights. Needless to say, all these things combined makes target acquisition more difficult. It appears the game is "so realistic" it is attempting to emulate an early onset of cataracts upon the player character.The "visual storytelling" is not too subtle. It displays lots of off-screen violence, sometimes you get extremely contrasting architecture such as an entire cave system built on the backyard of a crackhouse with schizophrenic drawings on the walls. Really nails it in that we don't take the war on drugs seriously enough, and that the bad guys are so evil they'll shoot the dog!There is a lot of audio, but it often gets drowned out by the gunfire or the 20 second long screams of agony from suspects with sixteen new additional orifices paid for by the local municipality. Subtitles are full of typos and mondegreens.RoN tried to be virtuous and stand up when nobody else did when it comes to making a Tactical Shooter, and for that it quickly gained some credit. There is some gameplay and eye candy when it is in its best behavior, but a little time and experience will quickly show you its ugliness with a thoroughly broken soul.In the event you're not willing to put up with blind trial-and-error until you too start seeing there can only be degrees of guilt rather than innocence in the crowds, I'd recommend skipping this title or waiting for a hefty sale with a mod list for a first playthrough.If you kept up to here, consider checking the following:- - -

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a spiritual successor to swat 4.They need to address a few critical issues.crashing during loading or returning to headquarter. Poor performance and stuttering with an rtx 3090.The game renders mirror and glass horribly, 0/10, even older titles does it better.This issues with glass makes it penalizing because the AI can see you before you see it.Enemies NPC don't have line of sight it seems. They have sphere of detection that are as big as the map it seems. I came silently behind one, his head did a 180 degree and instantly down me with a headshot despite not having LoS. This issue is even more prevalent in dark maps, the AI sees you but you don't. Even if you use NVGs. Tiny wood crack in the wall? They will gun you down, you are preparing a C2 charge? They will shoot through the wall.Civilians NPCs are also still primitive, they don't react to crossfire. So they will be standing straight up during a crossfire between you and the enemies. They also don't obey the police, so you need to get physical with them. They can kill you in 2 punches which is non-sense. So tazer is a must, pepper spray has a poor hit detection and punching doesn't work as they punch you before you can.They did improve your allies but they are still unreliable. The search the room order for evidence works 1 time out of 10. Also, your friendly NPC are NOT your friends. They have low accuracy to target the criminals but they have 100% accuracy to kill you. I don't trust allies that are ready to murder you on sight. That's no brotherhood. I know it's an Easter egg from Swat 4. But that also makes me never ever trust a buddy who is going to gun me down because I did a double tap on a target that went on a firing spree.Lastly, if you get annihilated. Toc will scold you for dying and not reporting beyond the grave your death. That's the dumbest voice line I've ever heard and that score thing is even more idiotic.You salute your fallen brothers in the line of duty. You never ever spit on them for serving the country and falling during duty.Overall, the game can be "fun" at times. It is mostly frustrating and not that fun or realistic.It has weird RoE logic, you get shot at first and die by aimbot headshot then you are allow to make them surrender as you are not allowed to kill them. Be gentle with mass murders, they have feelings.Just know, this game is very narrow on what you can and cannot do. Even when the situation doesn't really makes sense.

However, it's important to note that the game is not fully optimized yet, although it has improved significantly since the beta stage. When diving into the game, be prepared for a challenging experience, as lack of knowledge can make it difficult. You might find yourself searching online to understand which equipment is best in certain situations or what attachments to use. At its current state, I don't believe it's worth the 50€ price tag; a more reasonable value would be around 15€. It can be an enjoyable experience, especially when played with a group of friends interested in this genre, but be mindful of its existing issues.

Until I started playing... The game has horrible optimization, to the point where I spent hours figuring out best settings and even wrote a whole guide on it. But even aside from that, the AI... Man the AI. It was decent before the 1.0 update, felt hard but fair. But now, it's just ridiculous. The AI essentially plays like a TF2 Sniper bot with auto aim. For 25 bucks, I was holding my tongue, waiting for VOID to fix and tweak with patches, but now after the price increase I have to say STOP, do not buy. At the very least wait until they patch up the horrible performance and stuttering and tweak the AI. Even then I can't recommend it as a fully polished game with the level of content provided, especially after they banished mission select. So the only way I recommend this game is: The performance goes back to at least how it was before 1.0, the suspect AI is tweaked to be more fair, AND the game is on a hefty sale.

_childDocuments_.review: The modern reboot of SWAT 4, this game captures the heart and soul of the SWAT series with modern graphics and mechanics. Now that the 1.0 version has released, the AI squadmates are superb, the levels have been connected to each other with lore, menus made simpler, and the game given a great deal more purpose. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR at the bottom.7/10Its should be known that this is not a police simulator. You are SWAT or FBI, meaning the suspects are already known to be combative and probably armed. Keeping that in mind, I do wish it would be less like Counter Strike and provide additional options to resolve matters peacefully. I'm thinking more like the Barricaded Suspect mode. There is little difference in the game between Barricaded Suspect and Raid.The Raid mode could also be improved a bit by not having the AI already armed and prepared. Not sure the level of coding that would be required to have the suspects surprised and either give up or need to retrieve their weapon from say another room for example.It just seems like everything always turns into a gun fight and the only way to actually arrest a suspect is to breach, flashbang, rubber ball grenade, or taze them. Otherwise, they WILL shoot you. There's no chance to deescalate or even have a stand off whereby they may put down their weapon and submit without violence. At least not that I have ever seen.Other mechanics are good, my personal favorite is when they drop their main weapon and go down as if they surrender and then draw a hand gun. Keeps you on your toes. Just hoping for opportunities to settle situations peacefully if possible in the future.There are minor bugs, but they are typically addressed in a timely manner. As of this review: 11/27/22, there are no game breaking bugs that I have discovered.TLDR;Wish there were more options for peaceful endings instead of shoot outs every time. Minor bugs but they seem to be addressed in a timely manner.

_childDocuments_.review: Ready or Not is a great idea executed badly. Instead of cutscenes, the game tells its narrative through context and environmental storytelling. It's quite a barebones narrative, but I found it satisfying enough to get 80% of the way through. I wish I could stay and sing its praises, but I can't. I don't recommend this to anyone, under any context.What drove me away was the SWAT AI. They can't see you, and will constantly walk into you. They'll push you out of cover during firefights, and will shoot (and kill) you if you're ever between them and a suspect. If you clear a small room, they'll block the door and not move even if they're attacked by suspects. The suspect AI are basically TF2/CS:GO bots. They don't behave like people, running around and attacking you if they see you. They're not difficult to defeat, but it's sad when the game hypes up your confrontation with Amos Voll and then Amos Voll turns out to be another CS:GO terrorist(he even looks like one!) with a P90 who doesn't even have voice lines.

_childDocuments_.review: If you’re looking for some screenshots  to view all the ones I took for this game.Ready or Not (RON) takes place through a series of locations where organized crime has gotten out of hand enough to warrant the intervention of a SWAT team — that being you and your either AI-controlled or human teammates. All set in the fictional city of Los Suenos and its environs, these engagements will have you face anything from deranged preppers to terrorist groups and crime syndicates. Even though these missions are standalone from one another, some have an underlying plot that relates them to one another story-wise: these situations are all plausible and fleshed out well enough for a tactical shooter, with many indirect narration elements, dialogues and documents shedding more light on the events. Visually, RON doesn’t spare anything about realism and the brutality of true combat, with gore being abundant when needed, alongside the screams of injured suspects and blood. All maps are visually excellent also due to the recent upgrade to Unreal 5; their worldbuilding is rich in detail and immersive. If you want a realistic shooter that doesn’t cut corners in a lot of things, you’ve found it. From terrifying cartel smuggling tunnels to clubs piled with bodies after terrorist attacks, the immersion is assured. Special mention goes to the sound design, standing a notch above most other shooters.Levels differ massively in size and complexity, from wooden shacks to extensive multi-layer hotels and facilities. Aside from either killing or arresting all suspects depending on the parameters, exploring everything thoroughly is extremely important to get the higher mission ratings. Much evidence is scattered through each level, some static, some changing each time - they’re called ‘soft objectives’ and may even be mandatory to complete the mission at all. There’s no in-game map, so memorizing the operational layout during the preparation phase at your base is fundamental, even though the locations of these assets aren't always specified. Other than that, suspects and civilians may hide in closets, under beds, corners and actively roam around. Suspects and civilians aren’t only triggered by line of sight but also by noise and alerts given by others, expanding the tactical depth.Fights in RON are slow-paced, tactical and high-stakes. Despite armor, a few shots or even a single high-caliber round are all it takes for both your teammates and the enemy to hit the floor. Mainly, there are two ways to go about any map: lethal and less-lethal; the first utilizes firearms, alongside support gadgets such as flashbangs and tasers, to engage criminals in firefights, likely killing several of them. The second uses specific gear that only stuns and demoralizes the enemy, which is riskier but also more rewarding, since an alive arrest is worth many more points. You’ll have a limited amount of magazines, grenades and utilities, and you’ll have to use them smartly, alongside entering from the most strategically viable points, to get the best drop on each room full of suspects and minimize risk. Everything is paced as it is in real-life, so there’s no running, and the bulk of your armor will incrementally decrease your action speed in favor of protection. Suspects have variable degrees of expertise in a realistic way, too: some random gangsters robbing a gas station won’t be nearly as lethal as hardened cartel thugs at the Mexican border, the latter also sporting much heavier weaponry, and even laying traps. The gunplay rewards accuracy, positioning and trigger discipline, and heavily punishes impromptu gunfights without adequate cover or support. The rules of engagement differ depending on the map, and penalize you for excessive use of force. For instance, unless you’re against terrorists, you’ll always have to warn them to drop their weapon, discern between criminals and civilians, and pay attention to their behavior to make sure not to kill them if they’re surrendering. Also, you’ll need to get specific persons of interest out alive regardless, even if they’re hostile, so always having a non-lethal teammate or option is the best course of action. RON does an excellent job in portraying real life SWAT operational procedures and might take a while for newcomers to adapt to a playstyle that is “ask questions first, shoot later”.Every gun and gadget is unlocked from the start, while all unlocks depending on ratings are purely cosmetic. On one hand this is good because you’ll have all the options available to try and experiment from the start, but on the other hand it detracts from the progression experience. Still, there are achievements and many cosmetics related to getting the coveted A+ and S ratings.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a tactical shooter, slow-paced, but tactical. Utilize your teammates' and their respective tools to come out successful in a number of mission types including but not limited to: hostage rescue, bomb threat, barricaded suspects, active shooter situations. There's a metric-ass-ton of detail in this game, and in a situation where you're only one member of an elite unit of up to 5 operators, details matter. In seconds, a relatively calm atmosphere can erupt into mesmerizing chaos which could mean the difference between life... and death. Only a select few have the know-how, grace, resilience and patience to accomplish the toughest missions this game has to offer. The only thing left to ask is... are you Ready or Not?This game is still being developed to it's full potential. From what I've seen, there's a lot more to come and it's going to fill the itch for tactical gameplay that so many of us yearn for. A clean entry into a room is rewarding but the mission doesn't stop there, there's still more rooms to be cleared and an objective to accomplish. A content update is much needed in the way of maps and mission types, as well as an improvement to the quality and quantity of combatant-AI before this game sees the numbers it deserves. For now, the content is becoming stale. An element of randomization is necessary to keep the game feeling alive, as not all situations should play out the same. This game does it's best to emulate real life with a number of mechanics, including slower tactical pace, civilian commentary, the opportunity to make an arrest instead of kill someone, the possibility of a suspect pulling out a weapon or running at you before an arrest can be made, and a number of other details that will surely improve over the life of this game.For those seeking a MULTIPLAYER EXPERIENCE:As of right now (4/3/2022), this game does not have PvP modes; the first playable release of this game had a very rough PvP mode which was indeed received poorly by the supporters of the game. I have heard players in my public lobbies say that they want this game to be a PVE-only experience. Others however feel that PvP is a necessary feature to implement and that the detail and tactical pace of Ready or Not would be perfect for a new tactical PvP experience. The Community from my experience:So far, most of the people I have encountered in public lobbies seem relatively chill with good attitudes and a willingness to work together. HOWEVER, as with any multiplayer game, there have been a good number of trolls and toxic players. Thankfully, the game gives the host of the server the ability to kick or ban players. People also have a tendency to rush through the maps. Rushing through a tactical shooter like Ready or Not will more than likely get you or a teammate killed. I've observed that many players who enter a lobby and rush objectives only to die will run out of patience and just leave. In my opinion, it's just lame. It leaves us with one less player, and it defeats the purpose of playing a team-based shooter. If you're not going to utilize a ballistic shield, and rush in front of it then you're a certified-dumbass. If you decide to stack up on each other and determine the best approach to the next room, then you're playing the game. Of course, we all want a piece of the action, but this game is NOT Rainbow 6 Siege. It's a cinematic and immersive experience which requires teamwork and communication, and no one will pat you on the back for rushing in and clearing a room because A) we're fighting against bots and B) it seems to be better both in terms of points and the respect of your teammates to apprehend suspects as opposed to flat out killing them. If you want to run around and do your own thing, there's a Single Player mode in which you can control AI teammates to accomplish any task necessary for an elite SWAT team. If you've read this far, don't be the guy that ruins a good thing for 4 other people. It's a game at the end of the day, it's up to you to enjoy what it has to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: Hi there! Firstly, I'd like to thank you for taking the time to review and iterate that we encourage constructive criticism as a policy. I apologize that you feel in any way duped or held out from with regards to our release schedule.To clarify a few things, the build in question is an experimental test build that Supporter edition owners are generally given access to a week(or less) before the full release of an update to all players.Now, why do we do this? The primary reason is that we're a small dev team, and so having a 'soft launch' to a smaller audience allows us to better sort out game breaking issues that may cause significant problems for the larger audience. This was a decision that was made after consulting with our development team, who felt the best method for their work flow was to have a testing period/branch before the full release of patches.We have been very open that updates follow from the experimental test branch to all owners of Ready or Not shortly after, and with the most recent update this occurred within just a few days. We made sure to clarify this as our policy when we announced Ready or Not was coming to Early Access, and we have done so again in recent weeks across social media.We understand being frustrated at not being able to play, absolutely. It is simply important to understand that we have reasons for releasing onto an experimental branch first, and it is in the best interests of our work flow for producing content as well as the end experience for players.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if you're looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.Ingredients:6 tablespoons unsalted butter1/2 cup white sugar1/2 cup brown sugar1/4 cup water1/4 teaspoon cinnamon1 pinch salt5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced1 pastry for double-crust pieDirections:Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, a good fps that supports co-op! Tons of missions in a variety of settings. Enemy and civilian layout changes every time you play the missions so each mission has a lot of replayability. You plan and run the missions how you want. Want to go non-lethal and be super tactical? Cool. Want to go on a guns blazing warpath? Send it. Want to permanently ruin the eyesight and hearing of human traffickers by using an ungodly amount of flash grenades? Why not? The graphics are great, the detail is impeccable, the controls feel right, and combat is fluid. This is like R6 Siege, but without the toxic community and trash servers.After completing the game 100%, I have a few critiques to add. My biggest problem with the game after the most recent update is that the enemy AI are gods. Their reaction times, their aim and their awareness are impeccable. I would like a little more balancing in their skill based on who they are. Random gangsters holding up a gas station? Maybe make their gun skill and awareness lower. Trained fighters of a terror cell? Sure, they probably should be a little better than a random cop. There are also some bugs and performance issues here and there, but the devs are really fast with patches, so I'm sure by the time you read this, they'll be fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: As of this review I only have about 4 hours but I can safely say this game has a ton of potential and I am excited to see it in its development. This is one of those games where you want to come back to it almost immediately after having turned it off. Very good bang for buck as it is right now even at an early access level. There's enough content to keep you around and having fun.PROS: - Gun handling and animations/sounds are solid. The look and feel of every gun and animation is very silky smooth, has that satisfying feeling like there's actually weight to them especially as the character reloads and checks mags.- The sounds in this game are amazing, can't wait to see what they do for more immersion.  the floor board creaks and ambience    in some of the locations are AAA quality stuff.- UI is crazy simple. You cant mess up. Ubisoft and Dice, plz take note.- Commanding your AI team is also very easy. Just like, button presses, man.- Graphics are nuts, aside from a few oddities. example: Civilians, Enemies.- Intense gameplay. Each playthrough is unique as enemies/traps/civilians are never in the same place. Keeps you on your toes.CONS:- Sometimes walking around feels clunky. Corridors and some rooms are small and AI squads if you are playing SP tend to get in the way a lot.- Because of the movement speed in this game being what it is with.. *reads notes*... No sprint button, moving to cover can sometimes be..painful. Especially painful when you watch the AI that killed you run faster than the speed of light, while shooting. Having said this would ruin the slow methodical approach this game has to tactical gameplay. Adding a higher move speed with a scroll wheel speed throttle like tarkov does would probably make it feel better IMO.- Some of the Civilian VO's are on par with BF2042 one liners.- This isnt really a con but it made me sad you couldnt also trick out your AI squadmates weapons. would make NV and IR scenarios look cool.- Enemy AI are kinda 1 dimensional as of this review, but they are still difficult to take down in a firefight. They seem to have 1 repeated pathway in an area unless they flee, and from experience the enemies in adjacent rooms with a way into the room being contested seem to never provide backup. They just leave they homie out to dry. In fact I'm not entirely sure the AI react at all to sound from yourself or Squad mates.Please remember this is an early access game so many things will improve/get changed entirely. For now it is a SOLID early access games with hours and hours of playtime in it, with much more to come in sure! Definitely recommend picking this up.

_childDocuments_.review: When the trailer first hit in 2017, I immediately fell in love with Ready or Not. The concept and visuals of the game blew me away, as it was something I had never seen before. I rewatched that trailer hundreds of times, and got goosebumps every single time. When the game first came out, I was more than excited to finally play it. The gameplay at first, and still is, a bit broken.    The enemy AI has always been my biggest gripe with this game. They are way too accurate and don't even give you a fighting chance. Some street thug who can't even hold their gun correctly, will hit you from 50 feet away, and incapacitate you. You shoot them in return, they barely flinch. With the help of mods though, suspects have been more balanced and makes the game more enjoyable in that regard. Another thing I didn't like about last year was the fact that it took a whole year to even get an update. As much as i enjoyed the 1.0 release, having to wait that long for it was excruciating.      The rest of the game though, is absolutely amazing. The customization is now more diverse, there are almost double the maps, which are all detailed and immersive, and the guns feel and shoot really well. Regarding the maps, they did rework a couple of them completely, which I didn't really like. The Farm map, I prefer the old one. The Port map, I prefer the new one. The Hotel map though, the old one was easily the best map in the game, ESPECIALLY when you did the raid scenario. That version of the map was the most fun you could have in this game, but I think there were lighting issues that made them have to scrap it and make a different one.    All in all, I really love Ready or Not and would recommend it to anyone who likes FPS games, especially on the realistic side.

_childDocuments_.review: This game so far is amazing, and shows a lot of promise! I've seen how this sort of work is done first-hand (never been on a SWAT team though) and have to say it comes closer than any game, mod for a game or anything like that have to real-world ROE for law enforcement. Was that an armed subject? They dropped to their knees, are they just pretending and waiting for you to turn your back? Round a corner; 2 people and less than a second to figure out if you shoot or not. It's a game where you must move methodically or you'll pay for it - KIA by a tripwire trap or shotgun to the face because someone heard you coming.TL:DR section - Pros:+ Realistic Rules-Of-Engagement, with a point system to tell you where you screwed the pooch on SOP+ Clever AI - it's still A.I., but NPC's are varied and have different responses every time you play; yell at someone to get down and they'll argue with you while the guy in the next room comes running with a gun...+ Varied tactics - you can block doors so a room with 3 entrances has less, use shields, blast doors, or be hippie-friendly and just pepperball everyone alive until they surrender (hint; not likely)+ LOTS of room for expansion; the campaign for this (if they have one) will be intense. The missions already focus on some real-world, really f@@ked up stuff, but it's really what you see dealing with the scum of society.CONS:- No running. Really, no running... But the AI gets to run all they want! (Home key makes you move at a jog)- Wonky interaction key: one-key commands simplify things, but the button for open doors/kick doors/use special tool/stop bleeding/yell to comply are all the same button. I have screamed at doors to put their hands up... Alerting everyone around me that I'm apparently an idiot.- Limited melee; there are no takedowns (arm-bar) only a sort of muzzle-punch with your firearm, leading to some "unlawful use of force" when people won't move or get down fast enough... This is SWAT, if you don't get down when you're told to... You will be 'summarily oriented with the taste of floor'.- The co-op is an absolute blast, but if you only have one person to play with, the game removes the friendly AI team-mates... It would be awesome to keep at least one or two for helping carry special gear.Bottom line; the game needs polishing in some areas, sure... But so far it's visually amazing and super fun to play; and some moments aren't fun, which makes the setting feel more realistic - you will see things that will make you question what you know about the society you're living in, and how blissfully ignorant people are.Watch your corners, check mags often, use your tools, stick together and remember the motto of the special forces:"Slow is smooth: smooth is fast."

_childDocuments_.review: Ready or Not (RoN) is a fascinating case study in how people will lap up a poor quality product if it is the only one of its kind to have released in recent memory. It is not worth the high asking price for two simple reasons: it should still be in early access, and SWAT 4 exists. RoN is a game plagued by issues. It runs poorly, is riddled with bugs (many still present from early access), has terrible AI and hit-registration, there are buttons that have no functionality at the time of review, and the devs straight-up lie about features added to the game in highly polished dev-diary videos; Case in point of this being your friendly SWAT AI.Your SWAT operatives will constantly disregard orders, ignore enemies directly in front of them, get in your way, chastise you for getting in their way (for instance like when you're taking their position in a 'stack,' which is something the latest dev video on AI said you could do but can't), and have truly suicidal tendencies. They will charge off alone constantly, and prioritise collecting evidence over dealing with bad guys, which both get them injured and killed all the time. Moreover, they have many pathing issues that will get them stuck, either getting them killed or rendering them otherwise useless.Meanwhile, the enemy AI is still as omniscient (and omnipotent) as in early access - shooting through walls at people they never could have detected and pushing you from across a building at the precise moment you reload or swap gear. Their aim is also perfect, which when  combined with their high damage resistance makes them feel overtuned. Each suspect also acts the exact same as one another, from terrified kids sticking up a store to hardened vigilante-veterans - they all act more like murderous robots than what they're meant to represent: living, thinking people. Besides the fact that this ruins both variety and immersion, it makes every level a slog against an enemy that does not react to multiple gunshot wounds with even so much as a flinch and shoot through walls with 9mm without ever reloading once. The game is a one-trick-pony, and it shows.   RoN is beautiful, with highly detailed maps that truly do ooze atmosphere. Even in spite of the deluge of enemies it can sometimes throw at you (often more than you have ammunition for if playing in co-op without a full squad) that are adept at ruining a 'horror' level's atmosphere or just go against common sense, the level design is the best part of the game. However, it does not make up for the rest of its shortcomings alone.  This game had so much promise, but every time I play it there's always yet another set of glaring and infuriating issues that make me wonder: why am I not just playing SWAT 4 instead? Hell, half of the features that are meant to be in RoN are already part of multiple mods for that game. Just play that instead; it's far cheaper too!

_childDocuments_.review: Came back to this recently to see whats changed. Good news is the enemy AI is much more tolerable now. Enemy actions more sense with random street thugs being more hesitant to instantly start shooting and far fewer cases of getting gunned down through a solid wall.  But the game still has many more issues. Bugs, optimization and crashes are still a persistent problem. The game was ported from Unreal 4 to Unreal 5, which means folks on older hardware are more likely to have issues running the game. Even on my 4060 Ti I get random frame drops I can't connect to anything.AI squad behavior still likes to break. Enemies have a habit of throwing their weapons into another dimension  when surrendering which means lost points for the mission if they can't be found. Multiplayer has a lot of problems such as character equipment not displaying correctly, miss matched head and body skin colors, and enemy weapons being invisible for clients.I also feel like all the guns perform the exact same. There are no stat blocks or anything to indicate how one weapon my function compared to another. Just a small unhelpful description. It doesn't even indicate which shotguns are pump action and which are semi auto. Aside from the revolver all the pistol feel the exact same. Maybe that's just a me thing.Game still needs quite a bit of work but it's making progress. Maybe worth it on a sale but certainly not at full price. -----------------------------------------Old-------------It's so close to being a solid successor to SWAT 4. The mechanics are mostly solid but there's some serious issues. The biggest problem is the enemy AI. They don't act like people, they act like machines. Enemies have insane reaction time, perfect aim, and and can track and shoot you through walls. Cover becomes meaningless. They'll also no sell bullets and grenades and continue to gun you down no matter what. It really feels like the TF2 bot crisis is following me into other games.Your own AI teammates also constantly have issue following orders. You can tell them repeatedly to stack up on doors or deploy equipment and they'll just stand there doing nothing. The teammate AI also makes getting perfect scores on long missions impossible. To get a perfect score you have to take everyone alive but even if you load up the team with less lethal weapons you can't take away their lethal sidearm. So you can spend 30+ minutes crawling through a mission, get close to the end, tell your team to clear a room, only to have one of them pull their sidearm and kill a suspect, ruining the whole thing.If you play I HIGHLY recommend the AI re-balance mod available through the Mod.io option in game.

_childDocuments_.review: I've waited for the devs to address the still glaring issues present since beta hopeing that after full release, a steady stream of balance patches and tweaks would be rolled out. Unfortunately from what I have seen, the devs do not seem to care about the issues or criticisms in their game and seem to consider it finished and not in need of further development.The main issues are as follows:1. AI. The AI, as practically everyone will tell you, is completely bare-bones, nonsensical, and as it were, "on crack". Regardless if the suspect is a trained milita fighter or a junkie from the ghetto suffering from withdrawal, the response time of AI in this game is around 250 ms. The average human REACTION time is 250 ms. The average human RESPONSE time is around 500 ms. What likely happened is the dev in charge of the AI did a quick google search of what the former was, confusing it or not knowing the difference of the latter and just plugged in the value of 250 ms as the AI's delay for action. This results in every single individual perp in the game acting like they are Neo from the matrix and doing a quick 180 and landing a shot on you that shouldnt be possible, especially not for untrained and undisciplined street thugs. Made worse is their bare-bones coding. Regardless if you are concealed in the dark, behind actual concealment or even cover, so long as even a pixel of your body is within their line of sight, they will spot and engage you in the most basic display of coding I have seen in an otherwise seemingly high-production product.2. Hit registration. This one is self explanatory, stuff that should be hitting, isn't hitting. You will even have a small room of people close together when a gas grenade goes off in the middle of them. You wait a few seconds, as you should, for the gas to fully spread out and you hear the gagging. You go in to make the arrests and somehow, one of the AI is standing completely unfazed as if the gas did not exist RIGHT AT THEIR FEET. They will spot and engage you, sometimes killing you and someone else before POSSIBLY acting like they are actually in a room filled with CS gas with no protection on. In a game where the AI respond to your presence with the speed of a super soldier and where every shot counts, this is an obvious problem.3. Mission variety. Before, you were able to select various scenarios in multiple maps ranging from hostages and active shooter to a bomb threat. The idea was that each map would be fleshed out to have more than one scenario upon full release so that there was replayability. Some of the maps in EA only had one scenario and it gave us all great anticipation to see how other mission types would play out in them. God knows for what reason then that in 1.0 the devs literally gutted content and replayability from their game to make each map a single scenario only. No more doing active shooter in the gas station and then once more as a bomb situation (this map had every scenario) or experiencing the altered map layout due to the different mission.4. This comes from anecdotes as I only had the basic version of the game, but apparently there were exclusive items for the bigger supporters that got removed from the game entirely on release. One reason I've been told, is that the devs couldn't get the models to mesh properly with all the new characters they added, so they just got rid of it. This issue should be taken with possibly half the shaker of salt as I have heard it said many times, but as I care little about this subject, so only slightly more than the devs do for the quality of their finished product, I'd rather not waste time chasing claims around but do feel it is at least worth noting in case it is true.

_childDocuments_.review: It's one of those games that, for me at least, fall into that middle category, not positive, not negative. Though I will say there's a lot of positives, the negatives have a higher impact on gameplay.As for positives, the hand-crafted maps, the creepy atmosphere, the music all work to create an immersive experience. The gunplay is good, there's customisation to your guns and your character, although they don't impact how you approach the game much.For negatives, I think the biggest problem is AI, they either stand in place while you scream at them, or run around like madmen, or for some reason snipe you from who knows where, killing you instantly. There's been so many situations where I played with my friend and we were immersed, clearing out the map, only to find an NPC that just stands there, doesn't react to shots, doesn't react to flashbangs, but after 20 seconds just starts shooting.
