_childDocuments_.review: Me and most of my current friend group met on this game, so I can always appreciate that. Other than that, this game is not worth $50, and the developers have eroded all patience the community could provide over the years.Lets start with the basics. Ready or Not is a SWAT simulator where you are handling a wide variety of dangerous situations, from robberies gone bad, to organized crime and domestic terror organizations. There are several loose stories told throughout the game, predominately displayed via environmental story telling. You the player, and four other SWAT members, either AI or player, traverse through these levels, and bring order to chaos. You detain civilians, and arrest or kill any suspects, depending on reactions. You have a wide variety of weapons and gadgets to choose from, allowing you to tailor your load out to the mission, and your squad. There is a single player career mode, which give your AI team mates perma-death, and trauma based on the outcome of the mission.Now, with all that out of the way, lets get a few things clear. Eighty percent of what I mentioned above has been in the game for about a year, and is either in an equivalent or worse state of play ability in comparison to how it used to be. In particular, game play mechanics have regressed, and AI has not changed whatsoever, still showing the same problems they have had for well over a year now.The developers understanding of suspect reactions is laughably bad. They have regressed the AI back into a .250 ms standard reaction time, compared to the slightly longer reaction time the AI used to display in some earlier builds. While this may seem like the developers "accurately" modeling the human reaction time, it is completely wrong. That number earlier is actually the average speed at which the human body can process visual data, not the speed at which it can react. On top of the .250, there is an average of .400 ms in which it takes the human body to act on the visual data, meaning a suspect's reactions should be closer to .650 ms, rather than .250ms. What this translates to for you the player is the suspect reacting faster than humanly able, and killing you before you have a chance to respond, even if you have the drop on them, and they are surprised.This leads to the next problem, variation. Some maps, you are dealing with skittish teenagers holding up a convenience store. Other times, organized crime, or terrorists. All AI reacts the same. They all have the same super human reaction speed, and they all are willing to die fighting cops. This would make sense for terrorists, and maybe some of the members in the criminal gangs, but why is a 16 year old inexperienced teen able to do the same? Its absurd, and turns the game from SWAT simulator to military shooter, where you are better off shooting first and asking questions later. Another problem is ROE, or rules of engagement standardization. Every map, you have the same ROE, you cannot shoot until the suspect shows hostile/lethal intent. Again, this makes sense for some maps, like the gas station robbery, but why is this the case when I am fighting terrorists with suicide vests, who have already killed 60+ people? Its entirely absurd.On to maps. The game has added several new maps with release. These maps are fine from what I have seen, holding up to the high standards the developers seem to have for such maps. What is not fine, is the developers axing all game modes except barricaded suspects for release. Prior to release, each map in RoN had 3-4 game modes attached to it. Each game mode brought unique challenges, and sometimes even closed off, or opened up parts of the map to change how they played. These are all gone, and with it goes eighty percent of the replayability the game had to offer. As a small, but not insignificant note, some maps are missing proper collision detectors, meaning the AI can wall bang you pretty easily. Again, this has not really changed since early access.On to gunplay. At a glance, RoN has tons of guns, suggesting tons of variation and kit and style, based off of what you take. In reality, almost every gun plays the same. What you really have, is the choice between taking an SMG, a rifle, or a shotgun. Nearly every gun in every category is dominated by the same few calibers, and what is different is often worse. .300 Blackout is identical to .223 in game. 7.62x51 and 5.45x39 often offer more recoil for rounds that require more shots to kill a target. 12 gauge often needs multiple center mass shots, even against unarmored targets to kill, and every handgun kills in about the same time. This would be less of an issue if different style guns had different attachments allowed, but every gun runs the same 2-3 attachments. You also cannot take a flashlight and an IR laser, and IR floodlights are not even and option. This dramatically limits gun variation, and betrays just how limited gun play actually is.This brings me to the last big problem in this game, the developers. They refuse to communicate with their community, and relay little to nothing. They had the gall to pay gate an exclusive developer discord behind the $120 supporter edition. And then they did not even bother to respond to their questions. They spent a year refusing to fix bugs in order to release the game, with most of the same bugs still present. These developers made $50 million in a single year off early access(before taxes), and this is what all that money has to show for it? A few new maps, and a significant amount of content cut.Oh, and they have also banned people for criticizing them or spreading information, wouldn't be surprised if they label this comment as "misinformation", and ban it too.This game is not ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ready.

_childDocuments_.review: Day 1 - Rookie MistakesMy first day on the job is a disaster. I accidentally shoot a civilian, miss my target multiple times, and even manage to kill my own teammate with a grenade. It's a rough start, but I'm determined to learn from my mistakes and do better tomorrow.Day 2 - Taking ControlI'm starting to get the hang of things. I lead my team through a hostage situation and manage to neutralize all the threats without any casualties. It feels good to be in control and see my training paying off.Day 5 - Upgrading My ArsenalAfter some successful missions, I've earned enough money to upgrade my gear. I splurge on a shiny new assault rifle and some high-tech gadgets that I'm not entirely sure how to use yet. I can't wait to try them out in the field.Day 8 - Going UndercoverToday, I went undercover to infiltrate a gang hideout. I spent hours carefully crafting my disguise, only to be immediately spotted and shot at as soon as I walked in the door. It's back to the drawing board for my undercover skills.Day 12 - In the Line of FireI'm starting to feel like a seasoned veteran of the force. But just when I think I have it all under control, I find myself under heavy fire from a gang of heavily armed criminals. I dive for cover and return fire, but it's a close call. I might need to work on my reflexes.Day 15 - Saving the DayToday, I saved the day in a dramatic hostage situation. I negotiated with the hostage-taker and managed to convince them to surrender peacefully. It was a tense moment, but it feels good to know that I helped bring a peaceful resolution to the situation.Day 18 - A Close CallI almost didn't make it out of today's mission alive. My team was ambushed by a group of armed robbers, and we were outnumbered and outgunned. But with some quick thinking and expert teamwork, we managed to come out on top. I think I need a vacation after this one.Day 22 - Taking Down a KingpinToday, I took down the kingpin of a major criminal organization. It was a dangerous mission, but I managed to stay focused and keep my team on track. We apprehended the suspect without any casualties, and it's a major win for the good guys.Day 25 - Ready for MoreAs my time with Ready or Not comes to a close, I find myself reflecting on the thrilling and hilarious moments I've had on the job. From rookie mistakes to high-stakes takedowns, it's been a wild ride.But above all, it's been a game that's kept me on my toes and made me laugh out loud at some of the absurd moments. Ready or Not is a great addition to the tactical shooter genre, and I'm ready for more.

_childDocuments_.review: The game and its mechanics are great, its fun to control your own SWAT team. The AI is good and the structure as well as the way things work is great. However...The number of missions featuring themes of CP (Child P*graphy) is absolutely ridiculous and incredibly sickening. As far as I am aware there are 3 maps (could be more but I dont even know if I feel like continuing to find out) containing themes of CP. While I know this theme is prevalent and needs to be talked about, the amount of missions as well as the way they are handled is concerning. There is a data centre map where the crime of CP is mentioned but not explicitly shown. That would have been fine, mention it, make the player think about why you are clearing out this data centre. Why on earth would you need two more maps? The maps in question are called Brixley Talent Time and Valley of The Dolls. The first features a man who runs some sort of daycare or child hire agency, I don't really care what it is. It shows photos of children, screens on monitors mentioning explicit things that will be done to minors, it has a recorded voice message inside a camera of a man speaking to a child who isn't willing to participate in being videoed. There are schoolgirl outfits dotted around the map, as well as much much more. The whole place is creepy and awful, its unecessary. You have all these photos of children on the wall, why? What is the point?Then we get to Valley of The Dolls. Yet another CP themed map. Here there is a basement in which the criminals are running their crime. The map is generally explicit anyway, but what lies in this basement is truly horrific. There are photos strung up of minors, mostly  girls I think in bikinis/panties and bras. You can collect the evidence which specifically titles it "Illegal Photos of Minors" or something along those lines. Why on earth is this necessary? Who in the right mind makes a map, designs photos of minors and thinks it a great idea to put in the game? There are also of course other things in the basement, like children's cots, schoolgirl outfits etc. Things alluding to the crime. I know it is important to shed light on the things SWAT faces in the game, but you could have done that with just the datacentre map, giving the player an idea of what is going on and letting them be sickened by that. You do not have to ruin someone's day by putting such explicit images and themes in a game, especially with no prior warning. It is just so unnecessary. This game is also known for developing a school shooting map early in its development. That was removed, so why not this too? There are plenty maps that showcase what SWAT does. Like drug busts and house hunts etc, including something like this, so explicitly, is horrible. For that reason, I do not recommend this game until they remove such maps. It ruins the fun most people want to have with a game. Before anyone comes and complains about it being an 18+ game and being explicit, I know. I have no issues with the violence in the game or anything of that nature, I know what type of game it is. But surely, most people can appreciate that so much inclusion of CP is unnecessary and stupid. When you are including 3 whole maps, which take a while to design, you have to start wondering whether the devs of this game should be getting investigated.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, but it's far too buggy to recommend in its current state.  Ever since the 1.0 release the game has been riddled with countless bugs that almost make it unplayable.  I haven't had a chance to test it in multiplayer yet but as far as singleplayer goes your friendly SWAT AI are pathetic.  They'll often block doorways, refuse to listen to commands, or follow your commands completely incorrectly.  One time during the career mode one of them planted C2 on a door and then as he detonated it, all of them walked into the door killing themselves.  Additionally, the enemy AI has wall hacks and aimbot.  I have been shot at through walls before (when the AI couldn't have known I was there).  I've also had me and two other friendly AI be instantly killed after a suspect rounded the corner.  Despite all of us facing the suspect and being a good distance away from him, we were all instantly one tapped.  Its not like its SWAT vs SWAT, its SWAT vs criminals; I wouldn't expect a gangster with a Glock to be able to see us, identify us, aim at us, and shoot us that quickly with that much precision.  The enemy AI is just far too decisive and accurate, especially compared to friendly AI.  My final biggest gripe with the game is the suppression mechanic.  When you're shot at by an enemy, seemingly regardless of the situation/weapon being used, your character will have a panic attack.  The weapon sway gets unbearable, the screen gets blurry, and it makes it near impossible to land your shots.  I don't know if this is a realistic mechanic or not as I haven't been shot at before in real life, but realistic or not it ruins both the fun and fairness of gunfights (especially because the enemy AI doesn't seem to suffer from it).  SWAT 4 doesn't have this mechanic, and the game feels completely fine without it.  These aren't all the issues in the game, but they are the biggest ones in my eyes, and they really make it an unenjoyable experience.  I could be wrong, but prior to 1.0 all of the issues I just mentioned didn't seem to be as bad, which is rather disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall the game is rad. I have really been having a great time with it when playing either solo or with friends. Obviously with friends is most likely going to be the more fun option. That said, it's not perfectThe Good- The maps. There are a lot, 19 iirc, and they are all interesting and diverse. There is not a single map I dislike, imo they are either good or better.- Friendly bots are useful and accurate if you utilize them well. You can rely on them to cover an area without needing to be babysat.- Weapon selection is very nice. Most guns will be familiar to most shooter players, and they are enjoyable to use. This also applies to the devices available to you like the mirror gun and breach gun. All do their jobs well.- Coordinating with friends is very enjoyable. Making a plan and watching it unfold successfully is very rewarding.The Bad- The sounds need a rework. Specifically the  directional sounds. There does not seem to be anything in place to determine if a sound is above or beneath you, and sounds to the left or right can be very inaccurate.- Everyone has said it, and I'll say it again. The suspects are insanely accurate and aggressive. A meth cook is just as deadly as a trained terrorist with the objective of killing. All suspects shoot on sight. At times suspects will wall bang you without any indication of where you are, and they will hit and kill you. It's very strange. This can be overcome with the Cracked But Sweet mod for the time being. Enemies remain deadly, but there are actual opportunities to catch them off guard at times. - The performance definitely needs some optimization. I don't have the issues others have mentioned like less than 60 frames persistently, but I do stutter a bit when first loading into a map or HQ. During a run there may be isolated instances of a frame drop but so far they have been very brief. Despite it's flaws I can't help but acknowledge that I have an incredible amount of fun when playing Ready Or Not. All of these issues seem realistic for the devs to be able to fix if they so choose.

_childDocuments_.review: [08/2024 - Home Invasion Update] Oh boy, after so many years... the long-lost hope has become a reallity. And Ready or Not does not only look but it also plays and feels like a truely worthy successor to ! RorN features immersive tactical gameplay with very solid weapon feedback, dynamic and aggressive npc behaviour, an overall nice level of detail and a campaign mode with bot partners for solo-play. Although RorN definitely shines when played in a human based squad. Regarding the overall gunplay, it is almost as good as in ARMA, SQUAD, etc and is definitely far off such casual/arcady gunplay like we know from CoD or BF2042. There are 18 maps in the base game and 3 new ones in the home invasion dlc (only the host needs the dlc). And additionally there is a MOD system integrated into the base game, that allows for easy access to community based content with ~600 creations, mainly comsetics but also some new maps. Although RorN was officially released back in Dec. 2023, now 8 months later, with the switch to the UE5 ('Home Invasion Update') RorN finally feels truely ready to be a base for even more to come. Though RorN is still not perfect - mirrors should reflect everything like initially, an improved mission briefing and a real crime scene entry would work wonders, too as well as more atmospheric sound fx to support the overall map atmosphere in general and an improved proportion/size-ratio would make RorN perfect... But what the heck VOID Interactive had the courage to create a succesor for a kinda presumed dead SWAT series, and they achieved an honorable and worthy successor!

_childDocuments_.review: EARLY ACCESS REVIEWThis is a serious shooter folks, make no mistake. This review comes from primarily a FPS/racing sim fan. Now this is a spiritual successor to SWAT 4, you will see comparisons to it from just about any other review so I will avoid that. Quick TakeFirstly, it's a very nicely done game. Graphics are excellent, guns look and feel superb, audio is great in terms of immersion, dynamic range and balance, power from shots and explosions. I like the multi-function reload which seems to be a staple now (R to check, quick reload or tactical). Leaning and various clearing/recon tools are implemented well. General GameplayHow hardcore is this game? Well, you can't sprint. There's also no prone. No regen health, armor doesn't do much. Ammo types for non-armored, piercing or non-leathal. Stealth is optional, but generally advised. All maps will have a "Barricaded Suspects" mode, which is challenging enough, but a couple also have Raid, Bomb Threats, Hostage and other scenarios which require you to move even faster, add objectives, or adjust your Rules of Engagement. Great variety of maps in terms of size and setting. Overall tone is pretty dark, this is the really seedy side of law enforcement with some heavy themes and scenarios, people groan when bleeding out, yeah don't play it around your kids. I love its portrayal though, tons of detail and maps and cases are created with real care and passion to each subject.Rank with other shootersI would rank it more sim than Insurgency: Sandstorm, about the same as Ground Branch. More akin to pre-Vegas Rainbow 6 games. Probably close to Arma and Tarkov but I haven't played those. Movement and general interaction is slower than Insurgency, yes you're going to want to clear those corners and move purposefully and carefully here. You have miliseconds to make decisions, pick and identify targets. Encounters are too close to consider bullet drop or muzzle velocity. Enemies react erratically or organized, depending on the scenario (nice touch).Weapon customization Pretty comprehensive, though basic. Usual selection of rifles, pistols, shotguns, SMGs. Most are appropriate SWAT carry, with some extras / outdated stuff (good for roleplaying as street cop, etc). Can mount your sights, suppressors, brakes, ammo type, lights etc. but no extended mags, and no canted sights that I saw, might be added later as you can tilt your gun. Most encounters are pretty tight, even on the bigger maps I've not needed anything more than 1x magnification, though your mileage or playtype may vary. MultiplayerI've only tried a couple of co-op runs, however low success rate as if the host dies first they tend to quit and leave all your work to waste. So it's definitely much better with friends on mics to coordinate operations.Cons/AnnoyancesAdvise to devs at this stage of development, firstly the non-compliance of some citizens is downright annoying. I know there are some brave ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ who consider all police (even SWAT) as nothing but glorified security guards, but seriously, in a game this is pretty annoying how bad it can get, when lives are at risk, people dying, guns pointed right at you. Better with a mod, but pls either make them a bit less resistant, or more lenient penalty for a good pistol whipping.Some NPS animations and models are pretty jank. Not too bad, though in a game as immersive and good-looking as this, the crazy clipping through walls when restraining and rag doll on bodies does stand out.Friendly AI could use a lot of work. When they do work, they function very well, but they do get hung up on environments a lot, and also there's a maddening delay in responding to commands  when time is always of the essence (or ignoring completely, without even saying so or why). Also, they tend to block you and take a tad too long to move out of the way.Only other thing I would add at this point is to move a little quicker in ready-low, can get a bit tiring combing the map for that one last citizen.ConclusionLove, highly, HIGHLY recommended, will keep an eye on this one. Community is keeping the hype going strong with some really well done mods. Optimized well, looks great on my RTX 3060, but also runs smooth on my GTX 970 at lower res/settings. Give it a shot if you like tactical shooters!

_childDocuments_.review: Great game with a lot of potential. It's foundationally very solid. The variety of guns, accessories and tools this early is pretty great. It also looks awesome, even on the lowest settings.Where I can see it getting stale quickly is in the progression, or lack thereof. With the amount of weapons, tools and game types they have, it could have been a great incentive/learning curve to introduce only a few weapons, tools and maps to start. Whilst it's nice to have access to everything immediately there is currently no meaningful progression or replayability on each map/game mode beyond trying to beat your "high score", which also feels like it needs work.There are lots of non-lethal weapons in the game, which is great, but there really isn't much incentive to use them. It doesn't really affect your score at all should you try to do an entirely non-lethal run, which I think is a mistake as going non-lethal is exceptionally more difficult. Also having the option to turn on/off modifiers in the game to make it easier or more difficult, with the more difficult modifiers increasing your high score potential at the end of the game would at least add more reasons to keep coming back.The enemies and objectives can spawn on random parts of the map, and whilst that's great, having the maps layout remain the same each time I can easily see becoming stale. This is likely a more personal feeling, but if they were to randomize the maps layout on top of enemy spawns each time, that would drastically increase replayability. Games like Due Process have done a great job randomizing map layouts whilst keeping the theme/tone the same. The differing game modes add some extra flavour and variance, but they still -feel- almost identical. Random events or a series of progressive events that can only take place in certain game modes would make each run feel more tense and unsure of what to expect in each run.I think the game could be phenomenal if the devs are able to add enough randomization and progression components that make sense. There's enormous potential here and what they have already is great fun with friends, but I think the game really needs to add many layers in order to keep the tense feeling you have every time you open a door or turn a corner. I'm only 4 hours in and I'm already feel a lot more comfortable playing the game than I'd like, and I'm pretty bad at FPS' overall. Feeling like you're too comfortable or familiar with certain maps will only lead to players getting bored quickly and the community dwindling.If the devs add meaningful unlocks/progression, a plethora of random events and random map elements then I have no doubt this game will be one of the best FPS' you can play.

_childDocuments_.review: Ready or Not is the epitome of games that appeal to the idea of tactical shooters, without actually being that at all. Combine this with the constant over the top shock bait and you have a game that falls short and regresses from its ancestors, rather than innovating and reinvigorating the genre in modern times. A good example of what I mean are the levels in this game. The most glaring problem is the complete lack of replayability or even the lack of being able to plan anything meaningful at all. There's never anything like a clever exploit left in the intel or a risky opportunity to try. Every mission feels the same because they are the same, which is going on a bug hunt and killing the bad guys. But it's probably clearest where the developer's mindset was when you look at the design of the levels themselves. While they are obviously inspired by real world situations, they are also very obviously designed for a video game. The Campus map is a great example. It makes zero sense... Instead of dealing with the challenge of long open hallways and tight classrooms with little cover, you deal with a twisting maze, and how convenient that the shooters decided to target only  one building.This game isn't all terrible, but it's a disappoint.. I probably even understand the dev's choice, but the fact remains that the game appeals to a different, broader audience, rather than the audience that this game's predecessors had.

_childDocuments_.review: Do I recommend this game: yes.Do I recommend this game for people who get easily upset at defeat, disappointed at a lack of tangible progress, or infuriated at stupid deaths they FEEl could have been prevented but just couldn't see coming? No...But also, yes.First of all, the audio in this game is important and exquisite. Guns don't just make bang noises, they feel real. Every bullet feels like the powerful shot that it is, and this is because neither you nor the bad guys are bullet sponges like Call of Garbage: We Destroyed a Classic.Graphically it looks good, it achieves an immersive realism without distracting you with ridiculous pretties nor ♥♥♥♥♥♥ textures, though it really lands a realistic feeling. You're not so much clearing a level as much as tactically making your way through the living room of a villa, etc. You. Will. Lose. Doesn't matter how good you are, your skills have been honed in bullet sponge games. It takes 1, maybe 2 good shots to end you. You're not carrying 2 assault rifles and 1,000 rounds apiece either, it's a fairly realistic SWAT load out, and you will quickly find you are a mere mortal.If all of this sounds good then definitely buy it, it's a solid game and I've had fun with it. Multiplayer with friends makes it even better because you can go to voice chat and communicate with (hopefully) intelligent humans instead of giving orders to bots who, though their AI is good, they're still bots. It feels like old school Ghost Recon giving them orders with keys, mp is much better.Lastly, and I think this is pretty important, this is a massive game. Current install size is 90+ gb and as they update and add possibly new maps or whatever that size will grow a bit. It's worth every kilobyte though.

_childDocuments_.review: Ready or not? NOT READYI dont want to be disrespectful to the dev team. I know they are a small studio and work hard. However they have no shame in asking for a product full of bugs and half-baked features 50 Euros (in my region at least - Eastern Europe) and call it a 1.0 release. This very much feels like a mod in a real AAA shooter. My main criticism:- When starting the game using DirectX 12 I have frequent stutters so it is unplayable. On DirectX 11 it is fine.- Physics in the game are buggy as hell (objects clipping through other objects, dead bodies "shaking" on the floor instead of laying motionless (I think it is called "ragdoll" bug)- Movement feels slow (I just probably need to get used to it but currently it is annoying). You can only walk and not run. - If you miss an enemy on a mission where you are supposed to neutralize them all good luck with the backtracking and trying to find that one single dude hidden somewhere in a building with 30 - 50 rooms. You can spend half an hour trying to finish the level because of it.- The gore in this game looks like from 1990. The same blood puddle under every corpse. - Enemy AI seems brain dead and overall its design rushed. Using no cover, just standing and shooting. So far I did not encounter any variety in enemy design (completed 3 missions). All enemies are aggressive by default and try to shoot you and are literal "sharpshooters". I find this very unrealistic and lazy. I am fine if some enemies are very skilled at shooting but not all of them should be. Also none of the enemies have any routine. They dont talk to each other. Dont sit, have a cigarette when I first surprise them etc. This is quite immersion-breaking also.Overall I would say the game is not worth its price. It has way too many bugs/issues and lazy features. Buy it on a 60 - 70% sale or wait one year and check if anything improved.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried and tried and tried and tried to enjoy this game, but too much of it put me off. Way too much. I actually think the environment/environmental storytelling is done pretty fantastically, but outside of that I think the game falls flat.MOST of the mechanics are extremely jank. Most of it. The AI is very jank, and the immersion is broken pretty quickly because of how dead not just the AI, but the entire EXPERIENCE feels. The shooting is also problematic, but I'll get onto that later.There's no core sense of cohesion or "story" or throughline of anything. The police department is an ugly, messy maze that's clearly poorly managed. You have no direct sense of chain of command, you just wander around and take missions at will. There's a very barebones "Recruit/talent" system for your team, but it feels tacked on/unnecessary, especially the whole psychological aspect. I know there's some impetus there to tackle the whole PTSD aspect of police-work, but the way it's implemented feels like ticking a box, not like it was crafted with genuine care. Things like this I think are best done with great attention/detail in a holistic sense, not something that you could mechanically liken to a "stress bar", because gamers will naturally see the "code" between the lines and just click whatever buttons will reduce it. That's not how a mechanic feels impactful. Very $10 indie game feeling to it, complete with stock model cloned faces for your team. As such, it seems one of many aspects the game could have done without.Speaking of the department, for some reason you walk through it all with your long rifle/weapon drawn, God knows why, (kills immersion), and you move very slowly because the devs decided to forego a sprint/go faster/book it option, which again, God knows police/SWAT NEVER run, right? Right? This was nonsensical. Seriously. You can run with plates on, and helmet, ammo, 25 pounds of gear, etc.I LIKE the concept of many of the systems at play; commanding AI, having 2 teams, especially being able to look at their camera feeds. (Always reminds me of ALIENS). It strikes of more classic Rainbow Six games. But the gunplay is just so-so. Specifically there is an issue with the inability to alter the brightness or size (shape?), and placement (further/nearer) of dot sights. Something PLENTY of other games do today. Managing ammunition and overall kit is frankly a chore. Only with great difficulty can you do things like forego carrying a sidearm (if at all, if memory serves) or set up a nonlethal kit. The UI just isn't that friendly. A fast radial menu or kit screen where you see your trooper and all their gear, and you can do things like add or remove magazines for a given weapon with a single left/right click of the mouse, and drag and drop armor/helmet types and so on, would feel snappy and satisfying, as opposed to clicking a drop-down. It takes undue time to set these things up or swap between loadouts because you need to slowly saunter across the police department to the loadout area, which like every place in the department, is entirely uninteresting and non-interactive and dead. I created 3 or so loadouts and frankly didn't want to ever bother with that again.There is hardly incentive to prioritize non-lethal as well, save for when the mission demands it. After a while I realized that attempting to non-lethal takedown every hostile in every mission was just making it harder for myself, and (to be fair it's somewhat realistic) given its much lower reliability in reducing a hostile to a non-combative in record time, there's just no powerful motivation to ever use things like pepper ball guns or tasers when you can spam a few stinger grenades at the enemy.Another shooting-related issue is being for some reason unable to choose different size of ballistic shield, or to be able to aim down the sights of the pistol while using one. I just don't get that decision. Unless you're in kissing distance, not ADSing your pistol around the shield is just awful practice. Being able to place a dot sight on your pistol in the first place also makes this much easier. Neglecting this practice is just idiotic.(Examples:  ,  ,  )The voice acting is generally pretty good, and the music is very well done and subtly done.The biggest, overall problem all of this creates for me can be summed up in this way; the tone feels unearned. It's going for dark, serious, gritty, "mature", but it's half-sincere, if at all. All of the oomph is in the environmental detail alone. The AI lacks any great writing or nuance or "story" or character. The internet streamer stage made this clear to me. It really reads like a socially conservative 50~ year old's view of every perceivable excess or depravity of internet streamers/gamers. It reads as hilariously out of touch. Like the dude is at once a paedophile, porn addict, streamer, gamer, furry, anime addict, and a troll? It seriously gives you "Not in MY Christian neighborhood!" vibes. The police are unilaterally good guys out to lock lock up the degens, is one way to interpret it. And it's a wildly tone-deaf message for modern America, if that is the message. It might not be, because any attempt to have any kind of message besides, "Hey, this is super dark and serious and stuff", is just not there in the first place.

_childDocuments_.review: What in the world happened to this game? It was way more fun when it was in early access. I returned to it after a year or two of not playing to find that it's been gutted of maps and game modes. It used to play like a sandbox but now it's on rails, and replayability has been discarded. Performance is noticeable worse too, which is confusing to me since the game is technically released now and I didn't used to have problems with stuttering and low frame rates when I played before. Even on the same maps that look unchanged since then.A problem with the core mechanics that has been an issue for as long as I can remember and still isn't fixed: arresting armed suspects is virtually impossible without shooting them or using a flashbang. Everyone from lowly street thugs to private security are suicidal in the face of a heavily armed SWAT team; even when they are caught off-guard and held at gunpoint by the player, or have been hit with pepper balls or tasers. In short, less-lethal options are very underwhelming and not as effective as you would expect from a game about being a law enforcement officer.On the opposite end of the spectrum, and one that appears to be a new addition: your bot teammates will now turn hostile and kill you if you shoot a civilian or a detained criminal. So if you are like me and have ever wanted to clear an entire level like a psycho, that is no longer possible, cuz the developers said so. Even accidental kills will trigger this, which becomes a big concern if you're using a high caliber rifle or armor piercing ammunition. Why not just leave it the way it used to be where you get a harsh scolding over your radio and a large score penalty at the end of the mission? Is it really that important to the devs that NPCs in a video game are not unfairly killed by the player? I understand applying this kind of mechanic to public multiplayer lobbies where griefing is invariably an issue, but I am talking about singleplayer. No fun allowed.

_childDocuments_.review: Purchased, played solo, played with a friend, tried to fix issues, and eventually refunded. Ultimately really wanted to enjoy this game, as I love SWAT 4, but for the reasons listed ahead, I could not enjoy it and would not recommend purchasing.Ready or Not is very poorly optimized, this game jumps frame rate like there is no tomorrow. Jumping from 20 to 240 second to second gave me a headache, and even after limiting the frame rate it continues to jump, crash, and spike at seemingly random intervals.The suspect AI in this game pales in comparison to SWAT 4. Every enemy in this game acts like a fully trained military operative who's main objective isn't to get out of the situation alive, but rather to make sure your whole team is dead. Perhaps this makes sense on higher end maps with mobsters, or even terrorists, but when even robbers of a local gas station act like military trained personnel who want to kill you or die trying, it really breaks the immersion of the experience in a way that SWAT 4 never did. On top of that they have extremely accurate AI, shooting you through frame wide gaps at time and killing you the moment they catch a glimpse of you. Suspects will also continue fighting after multiple gunshot wounds with minimal loss in aggression or accuracy. This combination of extreme skills mixed with scenarios in which suspects should be expected to be inexperienced and panicked leads to a frustrating experience that ruins immersion and ultimately leads this games AI to live in the shadow of its spiritual predecessor: SWAT 4.Lastly, but in my perspective most importantly, this game contains AI generated art and assets. As some other reviewers have written, such content is an insult to creatives everywhere, and damages the possible well being of would-be and current artists who create art of all kinds within the entertainment industry. With the uproar about this I doubt VOID Interactive was unaware of the harm and plagiarism involved in AI art. If VOID isn't willing to hire artists to create all of the art within the game, then I personally can not recommend buying this product. I'd recommend picking up SWAT 4 instead if you're looking for something similar, as even without mods I find it to be a significantly more satisfying and immersive tactical shooter which also respects artists around the world!

_childDocuments_.review: Ready or Not is a worthy (Although not official) successor to the famed SWAT 3 and 4. Purely tactical, extremely tense and difficult but rewarding. This Ladies and Gentlemen is the true SWAT Tactical experience brought to life with more modern tools and approaches that we could of only dreamed of whilst playing SWAT 4.Firstly, I would like to preface that this is an early access review - the game is in it's early stages, missing content, features and general polish. However if you're interested in this game and are willing to drop the asking price, this game is absolutely worth it. Right now as of this review, I've only experienced the PvE experience, however a PvP experience is said to be featured at a later date. Biased as I may be the PvE is where this game is for me anyway.Which leads nicely onto the PvE experience. Ready or Not features multiple maps each with multiple gamemodes or situations, namely being Barricaded Suspects, Raid, Active Shooter, Bomb Threat and Hostage situation. These gamemodes are all unique in both the way the maps are laid out and the methodology required in order to take them on both effectively and more importantly - successfully. This game is  do not be dismayed when first starting out, you will fail, many times.Ready or Not features both Singleplayer with AI teammates and a Multiplayer element. The AI is pretty decent in it's current stage but does need some tweaking here and there, nothing unusual. They're fairly competent and know how to cover angles and perform room clearance without much input from the player. On the other hand is Multiplayer, up to 5 players. This game is an absolute blast with your friends, teamwork is absolutely mandatory and great communication is a gel that binds a plan together. I've not had a more fun tactical experience with my buddies for a long long time and this game certainly scratches an itch in that regard that I thought would not be scratched for a good while.Another thing that stood out to me over the course of playing was the sound design. It is absolutely  When I use a breaching charge I feel like my organs have shifted, it is pure bass. It is glorious. It reverbs and it contorts through the environment, it does exactly what it should, and the firearms behave the same, it is amazing to experience. Albeit loud but hey it's 'mersion.Whilst I could continue to sing praises about this game, there are some downsides so far that I should address. (Please bear in mind that these are most likely already going to be addressed due to the early access nature and I'm really just clutching at straws here). As of now the arsenal and gadgets at the player's disposal is quite limited - I expect this to change over the course of development. I would also like to see bots as an optional addition in Multiplayer games, maybe you don't have 5 people and could do with an extra AI or more to order around and provide assistance. Players should be able to designate AI to be ordered around in order to fill extra slots.Other than to continue listing lack of content that is almost guaranteed to be added throughout development such as more maps and things of that nature, I'm going to close it here. This game is absolutely worth the money. You may see it and think that the price is steep, well let me tell you - it's a small team that has made a AAA quality product and their attention to detail and realism is exactly what it should be. People are not exaggerating when they say it is SWAT 5. It is what we've been waiting for. It is a truly tactical joy. I cannot recommend it more.

_childDocuments_.review:
Ready or Not is an intense, tactical, first-person shooter that depicts a modern-day world in which SWAT police units are called to defuse hostile and confronting situations.

VOID interactive has consulted with police teams globally to create rules of engagement and a scoring system that are both challenging and realistic. In order to push the bar further with realism, Ready or Not models ballistic penetration, ricochet, kevlar and plate dynamics, as well as projectile expansion and momentum.

Explore a deep and involved weapon handling and player maneuvering system, geared towards providing officers with an unprecedented level of control over their situational effectiveness. Ready or Not utilizes a simple and organic control scheme which won't have players fumbling around, forgetting dozens of key bindings.

Organize an approach, then execute the mission in real time. Officers can decide to deploy with items such as ballistic shields, door rams, tactical ladders, and much more.

Bring order to chaos online with friends through a tactical cooperative experience, lead a crack team of AI-driven swat members in a solo, story-rich campaign, or battle a rogue organization in a fierce and competitive multiplayer environment.

_childDocuments_.review: I was waiting for this game as soon as I saw a short clip from it. Weird, SO weird.The gameplay is largely "walking simulator", with a bit of platforming. You start in this weird little island city, surrounded on all sides by... well, yeah, "Sludge". You're not really going to find out why, the game isn't that way inclined. It's much, much more about discovering the weird and wonderful people littering the various structures, from the apartments to the fast food restaurant to the building sites. Everyone has their own odd vibe, and the sense of humour here really shines. More often than not, whatever character you run into is going to say something that brings a chuckle.So where does this all go? Well, you unlock some items which allow you to move around. You can fast travel/teleport to various landmarks, you can unlock a glider so you can fly around the city. You're also collecting slugs, and spraypainting your logo all over the place, and larger pieces on billboards. BUT, this is the only real limitation of the game, it doesn't necessarily go anywhere else. You're running around, talking, laughing, tagging stuff. If you're hoping for deep narrative, this isn't it. If you want a colourful and super eclectic experience, this is a great example!

_childDocuments_.review: The game that I expected Sludge Life to be differs greatly compared to the experience I came away with. Even if you’re tempted to generically classify the game as a collect-a-thon or a mini-open-world, Sludge Life ends up presenting itself as much more. Sludge Life seems to avoid any explicitly game-like objectives. Hunting around for tags is mainly used as an extrinsic push to lead you to areas you’ve yet to explore. The most interesting stuff you find tends to have no numerical in-game value associated with it. The game even touches on unexpected topics with a satirical yet serious tone. Sludge Life is way more interesting than you’d expect for a game that has contextual auto-peeing.I've begun to truly appreciate games that have little to no distance between the 'play' button and actual gameplay. From the beginning of Sludge Life, you essentially have free reign over the whole island. The only thing separating you from your ambitions is distance (and maybe two helpful items). You are tossed into the game with no other premise than to follow your instincts, find new places/items/characters to interact with and do some tagging along the way. Basically, everything is ‘optional’, but you still want to run around and see it all. Movement is simple yet quick with a generous mantle that often saves you from the vertical consequences of messy jumps. Getting around is enjoyable enough to rouse the movement-shooter enthusiast part of me that gets hungry for more mobility mechanics whenever it catches the scent of intrinsically rewarding traversal.The islands you hop between include plenty of passive stories that draw connections to other places, people, brands, and events. Places and things that characters mention usually physically exist within the islands and coming across them brings you deeper into the narrative of the spaces that you’ve explored. The many political undertones that make the Sludge feel grounded and lived-in further enhance the believability of what once seemed to be no more than an odd parkouring indie game. Most of the people here have a tangible role in this gloomy, gross, and isolated labor society.The laptop pause menu is a fantastic example of Sludge Life’s creative use of diegetic elements. The laptop’s retro interface makes it stylistically appealing and consistent with the technology found elsewhere in the game’s world. It’s intuitive to use, as it should be if it were someone’s real personal computer. Furthermore, the various features of the laptop reveal details about the norms of this society as well as the personality of Ghost themself. Another clever way in which the laptop is used is to keep gameplay information off your main screen. There is no HUD or ‘tag counter’ to clutter your screen and break the illusion that Sludge Life so creatively casts.While the warped/hard-edged pixel filter is a large part of Sludge Life’s signature presentation, the visuals became very nauseating very early on. Thankfully, the game allows you to turn off and alter a variety of settings (including the main filter). There’s also the option to add a much-needed reticle to the center of the screen. After spending a bit of time taking in the uncanny default visual effects, I thoroughly recommend diving into the settings and customizing the game to fit your needs.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is proof that video games can be art.This game was given away for free from another digital video game storefront. I played it there, and fell in love with it, so I also bought it on Nintendo Switch. Then I also bought it here. The biggest concern I see people deal with before buying this game is that it won’t have enough content to justify the price. Since this was my third playthrough, I was able to complete all the achievements within 4 hours, but that’s not really the intended way to play.The intended way to play is to let the insanely engrossing world and aesthetic pull you in and fall in love with the vibe that it just absolutely oozes. Play it without the intention of “finishing” it, and it has more than enough content to justify the price. Explore the world and realize that primary “objectives” should be treated as a fun little bonus that just conveniently happen to be there to provide additional fun. I guarantee you’ll enjoy your time in this world.

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this short adventure game. Basically, it is 3D platform puzzle gameplay, where you have got to reach designated locations. The level design is excellent, and there are charming characters with witty dialogue to keep you exploring. The anti-establishment jokes had me chuckling throughout the five-hour tour of this industrial-destroyed island.Urinated off the tallest building on an Ubuntu Linux desktop using a keyboard and mouse control. The gamepad also worked well enough. The game uses the Unity Game Engine. It has an excellent soundtrack that fits into the narrative, as the player passes by radios. There is some replayability, also, with multiple endings and multiple, optional layers of NPC interactions. I had a lot more fun with this game than many other more expensive adventure games, and it had some sophisticated gameplay that felt well-edited for maximum fun. Despite being tounge-in-cheek satire, this is not a half-assed effort. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, get ready for a sentimental one with a few spoilers.Sludge Life pulled me in with its attractive art style just from the steam page. It was on sale at the time for like.... idk, 2 dollars, and so I picked it up. I didn't expect the game that I got.Opening up sludge life, you're greeted with a nasty desktop that has some warpy effects as you move the mouse around. It sets the tone with the almost blurred VHS filter that I don't quite have the words for. Entering the game, you literally just throw your ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ computer at the wall and see a dirty, messy room of a storage container that functions as an  tutorial to the movement the game. Floaty, but on point and satisfying, Sludge Life plays almost like a greatly simplified, streamlined Mirror's Edge. No running on walls or any of the complex maneuvers, but the running, vaulting, etc mechanics are just plain addictive and it makes you wish the map was  bigger once you finish the game.Onto actually playing, though. The gritty, nasty visual effects blend right into the tone of the game, with choppy lettering reminiscent of subtitles from the 80s-early 2000s. It really brings you back to a place that, for people who have at least grown up within the past 20 years, feels almost nostalgic, lost, and homey at the same time. The dialogue is brilliant, comedic, and precisely in tone; One can go from hearing someone talk about how some lady with a scar on her eye stole their washing machine, to hearing someone muse about life and their purpose here, to finding the girl who stole the washing machine and having a nice conversation with her. The people feel like real people, stuck in this sludge of a dump. The way people are either apathetic, philosophical, absurd, or whimsical feels organic and real, the way that one would feel just talking to people they know. Playing through the game, I got a real feeling of understanding for these people, and a connection between my own sludge life and theirs. This game feels like rock bottom, like everyone knows that there's nowhere further down than here.This game reached me at a very apt time in my life. I won't go into detail, but it's had me feeling a lot of the same ways that this game feels. Lost, wanting for an escape, and just wanting to find your place in all of it. It's helped me kind of redirect my gaze towards it all in at least a small way, and it's helped.The gameplay tasks of tagging spots is also very neat, and the game gives you plenty of tools to both easily achieve your goals and have a lot of fun doing it. There are multiple spots in which you've got to be a little crafty or clever to get to it, such as a hidden item needing a vent that i eventually found before immediately talking to the person who gives the player a clue about the vent. It was a fun moment.There's a camera (that has a different file directory than your regular screenshots) that can be used to both seek out tags and take pictures of them, or really anything else you might want. In short, Sludge Life is a beautiful game that has a lot to say about the world, but doesn't have to directly say much to get to the point. The world feels both lived in and stagnate, like everyone there is alive but have simply given up. Everyone is on strike, so not even the CLOPS (police) will try to do anything about you unless you walk right up to them, in which they'll smack you and usually have a pretty funny line to boot. Almost makes you  to get hit. I still haven't found everything in the game, with about 2 achievements left to get, but from the first night i played sludge life I knew that it would be a very special game for me. I've heard that there's a second one out, and I cannot wait to play it once i get the money. Until then, I recommend you play this game at least a little high if you smoke, as it really helps the atmosphere eek into your bones i feel, but it's not necessary to enjoy the experience. I hope this review helps. "Hey, Two Eyes. Tell me what this SMACK smells like."

_childDocuments_.review: I initially played through the entirety of Sludge Life on Nintendo Switch, but I decided to play through the game again on Steam, now that I own a Steam Deck. I already loved Sludge Life, but after revisiting it, I can comfortably say it is my favorite game published by Devolver Digital (not counting Sludge Life 2, I haven't beaten it yet, but I will likely find it to be an improvement), and among my favorite indie games of all time. Sludge Life boasts a unique gameplay premise with tight controls that revolves around tagging as many walls with your graffiti as possible by using first-person parkour mechanics. The more walls you tag with your artwork, the more rep you gain, which allows you to collaborate with some of the local taggers and create impressive artwork together. The world isn't too big, but it's compact, with a lot to explore and details to uncover. Sludge Life is all about the little details— between the cigarette butts and drawings littered on the floor of the playable character's home, to hidden switches in the offices of CEOs, there's a lot to appreciate. Sludge Life is also endlessly entertaining with its wonderfully useless gameplay mechanics, such as a dedicated fart button, urinating when standing near open toilets, and being able to smoke the cigarettes that you find around the area. Sludge Life's soundtrack, although of very good quality, feels somewhat same-y, with a lot of songs sounding kind of similar to each other. Regardless, the music of Sludge Life is very enjoyable. The visual design and audio design are Sludge Life's crown jewels. The visual presentation is unique and mesmerizing, coupled with impressive and colorful punk artwork shown in the game's graffiti, which has served as a big inspiration to my own artwork. Similarly, the sound is a feat of its own. Every little sound is accounted for. I recommend playing Sludge Life with a good pair of headphones for a better impression of this. Sludge Life is a loving and hilarious tribute to graffiti and hip-hop culture that is well worth your time and money, especially if you are looking for something unique and artsy to dive into. It's a short burst of pure genius that I can confidently STRONGLY recommend to anyone who takes video games seriously as an artform.

_childDocuments_.review: Essentially everything I would want in a weird, psychedelic exploration based walking sim.It's bizarre, has fun mechanics that stop it from becoming boring and tedious and almost every area has something completely unique and interesting to look at or interact with. It also has a great sense of humour but also some interesting ideas on society that luckily don't encroach on being preachy or annoying. Just enough to make you think, then move on to taking a photo of a cat with two buttholes.In addition to this I really loved some of the mechanics that were unnecessarily fun to use. I'm a sucker for items in games that make you feel like you're really interacting with them. For example the laptop having it's own desktop and app, the camera functioning as a guide but also allowing you to take pictures, which was honestly a wonderful addition considering how strange the world is. There is no reason to take photos other than for yourself, yet I took over 100. The apps all feel unique and semi realistic and interactable objects and people in the world make it feel just that bit more real rather than an empty wasteland to wander around in.The feel of the game was the most important to me since it could have been a boring walking sim but it luckily succeeded massively in that department. A few negatives purely for fair criticism.Firstly and mainly, the performance is horrible. The graphics are quite simplistic (but fitting for the theme) yet it would have consistent frame drops and chug horribly. This is the second time that a game from this developer (Heavy Bullets is the other game) has performed terribly with zero reason due to low graphical intensity. Not only that but both of these games are within a category of around 3-4 games that I have never been able to find the cause of the issue and never truly fixed. Some advice for anyone having the same issue of huge frame drops, turn off vsync and crank the FPS limiter to the max amount, this caused the frame drops to not stop, but only drop to a much higher level, calming the hitching. This is also proof that it isn't my hardware struggling to run the game since it ran better at a much higher frame rate which disguised the hitching.Secondly it's short. Personally I thought it was short and sweet and the world is interesting enough to explore due to your own curiosity.The issue comes in when I say that I got this game for free (I believe it was free due to a promotion of the sequel that is soon to release).This game usually retails at $15. I don't think there is anywhere near enough content for that cost. Personally I would say it should be around $7/£5.I was able to complete this game to %100 in 4 hours and as stated before I was taking photos and exploring for the fun of it. Without me entertaining myself I could have completed the game, secrets and all within 2.5 hours. There is a reason this game can bee speedrun to 100% in less than 25 minutes.The thing is whether this is an issue to you. Since I got this game for free I had absolutely no issue with the short length and enjoyed every second. If I paid $15 for it and completed it just after the refund period ended I would feel like I had been scammed.Little issue, the climbing can be frustrating. Luckily there isn't a huge punishment for failing to climb something but it is worth mentioning.I would also like to mention that one of the other games from this same developer, High Hell also had near identical issues to this game. Incredibly short, performance issues and crashing, frustrating movement. Although I do like Sludge Life it is worrying that the issues that plague this developers games haven't been rectified as new games are released, Heavy Bullets was released in 2014 and the performance issues are identical in this game. I will have to try Disc Room and see how that holds up.Enough complaining because I do actually like this game a lot. It's rare to find a game where exploring is so satisfying and captivating and the world is so unique and insane that it can surprise you everytime you go somewhere new. Although the issues I have talked about might seem major, they really aren't to me. I just felt obligated to mention them since Steam reviews don't care for fair and informative reviews and I want people to understand the game fully before paying for it.Overall it is nice to see the developers of this game find a genre that allows players to fully experience the weird world that they wanted to create. This game feels right. It allows the player to interact with the strange universe that was present in High Hell without the restrictions of a level based shooter all while fully fleshing out the world and leaving the player with a fully realised experience of weirdness and intrigue.Is it worth the asking price? No.Is it worth the short amount of your time it takes up. Absolutely.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game during the free-to-keep promo and had a bit of fun exploring the strange island of Sludge Life for an hour... but I wouldn't recommend paying full price, or really any price, for this game. The gameplay mostly consists of walking around the island and occasionally interacting with certain objects or spray painting the environment in predetermined areas, plus listening to NPCs - and the unique art direction and funny interactions (press 'F' to fart) had me consistently engaged for the game's hour-long length.However, the conversations with NPCs are very short. The platforming is sometimes wonky. And, most importantly, there are many areas where almost nothing can be interacted with, leaving the visually impressive map devoid of genuinely interesting gameplay. Plus, there are multiple endings to Sludge Life, but none of them are actually communicated to the player properly - you just have to wander around and find them on your own. If this game was longer, with far more available interactions around the island, I would probably be able to recommend buying it. But I can't recommend paying $15 for an hour of walking around, smoking and looking at graffiti.The store page for the upcoming sequel says that Sludge Life 2 will be "twice as dense" as the original - I hope they deliver, because the actual content of Sludge Life is wayyy too spread out. Had I bought this game for full price, I would have been sorely disappointed, and I would only recommend trying out Sludge Life if it goes free-to-keep again in the future. 3/10

_childDocuments_.review: is quite a challenge to accurately classify, because it dabbles in so many things at the same time. Foremost, it's a first person adventure, complete with traversal tools and quirky NPCs to interrogate. There is literally no height you can't reach or room you can't access. As you progress, you'll then discover an assortment of collectibles, ranging from objects you can pocket to locations you can tag. While not specifically a puzzle game, trying to reach certain places, open certain doors, or perform certain to-do tasks require lateral thinking. Shoot hoops, smoke cigs, fly high with shrooms, fiddle with apps on your virtual laptop.Interspersed within your exploration are a colorful cast of characters. There are no fetch quests or dialogue options, and none say more than a few repeating sets of lines, but that's fine: They provide hints, humor, or socio-economic commentary that feels uncomfortably familiar even today. As you raise your street cred you'll find fellow taggers stop giving you the cold shoulder and unlock special collaborative murals. Spread your art across the island to... well, win nothing really, but unlock a special trippy ending if you know where to go.The real highlight for me was the puzzles. SLUDGE doesn't look like it has any business being a puzzle game, but it has its fair share of surprises. Discovery is its primary objective, and to list them all would ruin the fun, but here's a couple roundabout examples: A fully fleshed out strategic minigame you can play on your laptop, entirely optional. A deadly laser grid blocking your path. A graffiti spot you can't reach on a satellite dish. A door that slams shut as soon as you get close to it. Changing your dietary preferences(?)For all its strengths, SLUDGE has a couple of demerits. It lacks a clearly defined plot, and its endings don't really provide any closure. Its inclusion of drugs has gotten the game an unfortunate ban in Australia (the C key is literally dedicated to using cigarettes). It's short, and it lacks replayability after you've uncovered every secret, unless you're a speedrunner.The game's longevity will depend largely on how much you're willing to invest in it. It's possible to reach its good ending in as little as 5 minutes, provided you know exactly what to do. Experienced blind, it's about a 1-2 hour dive, and then maybe another 1-2 hours for secrets and TO-DO tasks (aka achievements). Given this, I find it tough to recommend at full price. Wait for a sale, or if you see this in time, add it now and keep it forever before 3/30/23 - presumably a limited time promo for its upcoming sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Graffiti Town. A bit of a note before we begin. I've played this game before as I've owned this on Epic Game Store and 100% twice before and I haven't fully replayed it once it came to steam, hence the low hour count.Story:You play as Ghost. A graffiti tagger who decides that it's time to be the best tagger in town and so you decide to traverse the corporate town owned by GLUG and tag it in your own unique style. There's really not much a story in Sludge Life. There's tons of dialogue as pretty much every citizen of the town will talk to you and have multiple things to say, but it's more of a relaxing exploration game with some visual storytelling. The dialogue here is weird and funny and really matches the weird tone of the game. Graphics:When I first saw the developers game High Hell, I fell in love with the art style. Grimy nature, saturated colors and just a weird style really was satisfying to look at. Then Sludge Life came along and when I first saw it in action it felt like a great continuation of the style. The corporate town is visually very pleasing to explore and is actually designed in a way where every bit is packed with detail. It's mostly consumed by filth and grime, but there's more cozy corners like an apartment complex with people just hanging out, a basketball court and of course the highlight of the game which is the graffiti which just looks absolutely awesome. Audio:The soundtrack of Sludge Life is a very experimental techno feeling one and I genuinely like it's weirdness. Everything about it just fits it's weird tone and whenever you come across people just sitting back and listening to these tunes, it's just a fun little addition.There's also a bunch of other really satisfying audio designs like the spraying or that little jingle that says Ghost whenever you tag a spot, it's really cool stuff. The way the audio is designed is great and it definitely feels like a lot of care was put into making it feel like it matches the world.Gameplay:Sludge Life is a very simple exploration game where your only real goal is to tag spots across the town. You walk around and will hear a spray can shake which indicates that you can tag that particular spot, but some places will require an unorthodox way of getting to them.I genuinely loved my time with Sludge Life, playing this game is a very relaxing experience and something about it just mellows me out, however I do have to admit that there's some issues with the core experience, but I really want to begin with the positives.The exploring part is genuinely a ton of fun. You can find a lot of weird stuff and you being nosy is both rewarded and penalized (don't worry, it's sort of a joke). Around the world you can find items that can help you traverse the world faster or even find computer programs including a pretty addictive mini game called Crypt Keeper. The traversal is probably the games biggest problem. The movement feels a bit too slippery as jumping, getting up the ledges and just getting up high buildings requires a bit of practice. There's really not much indication what kind of distance you have to jump to grab a ledge and sometimes you won't grab it even though you're supposed to which will require you to find a different way up (don't worry though usually there's a few different ways to get to the same spot). which could get annoying when the one you want to do isn't really possible. At first I hated it, but after I got the hang of it I genuinely had a blast using it, but it's still could have been so much better. There's also not much to do in the game, once you mop up all the tags, there's some fun side activities you can tend to (doing the 100% isn't difficult and won't take longer than a 3 hours at most) and I definitely wanted to get that 100% when I finished the main quest, but once you reach the end, there's really not much reason to go back to it.Verdict:Sludge Life is such a unique and fun game, which you can just sit back, relax and tag some spots, while exploring a bizarre world that is just fun to explore. While there are some issues with the movement, it did not detract from my enjoyment of the game and I have no trouble recommending this. Bring on Sludge Life 2.Final Rating:8.5/10Pros:+ Gameplay feels fun and relaxing+ Exploring the world is a ton of fun+ Great art style+ Really good audio design Cons:- Movement feels a bit janky- Short If you liked this review please consider joining  and

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels unfinished.The store page is somewhat deceiving -- the world and gameplay is actually pretty empty and half-baked. You'll mostly be playing in silence (no background music, hardly any ambience) with awkward controls (no parkour or any unique movement gameplay) in a scattered map that feels like it was made for Garry's Mod.The main theme of spray painting is hardly present too. All you do is just go to predetermined locations in the map and left-click to tag walls. It's a repetitive collectathon but with no solid, fun gameplay to hold it up.

_childDocuments_.review: Pure fun/chill game. The goal is to tag 100 spots scattered around the world. This involves a lotof jumping and finding ways up to places. You can use items to help you locate and reach these, like a glider. You have to find these first though. The platforming can be awkward and frustrating - not too bad once you get one of the itemswhich allows you to teleport back to where you were if you happen to fall.A pretty short game overall but highly amusing and worth every minute exploring in my opinion. The whole game I was asking myself, "Is this what being high is like?"... There's so many weird things to see and people to talkto. The people don't speak any worldly language either. I think they speak "Sludge"which is like, beep boop beep bip bip or some kind of 8-bit language I guess?There's a small open world for you to explore.Lots of funny and weird things/people to see and talk to.Collectables and mini games.Unique art style. Multiple endingsSince I got it for free, I'm very impressed. I wouldn't pay full price though.Maybe £6.00 or something but that's just me. I've added the next game to my wishlist though based on the short fun I've had with this. Fairly easy achievements but some of them were annoying. You have to do a couple in one sitting/session. They reset if you exit the game. One of them is to eat 20 slugs - not too bad if you use a guide I guess. Theone that's annoying is a mini game you unlock by finding it as a collectable in the world. You have to defeat the last boss which is very RNG based, or inother words, you have to get lucky and hope he's not surrounded by baddies or it's basically impossible and you have to do the 20 whole levels all over again. The graphics are a bit bad but in a good way but there's a VHS filter you canturn off (which I only noticed hours into the game) but it makes it so much morebearable to look at. From the main menu go to Config > Hacks and then toggleoff the VHS filter. Simple as that.

_childDocuments_.review: You can smoke whenever you'd like in this game, which may seem like an odd thing to praise, but I haven't really seen a mechanic like that in games where the entire point is seemingly to immerse yourself in the world. Crouching on a couch next to a whistling bird man, lighting a cigarette, and listening to faint music in the background just really sets a great tone. How about spray paint a big combo tag with a friendly tagger, front flip off the sign, and light a cigarette while walking away. It's just the little things that add such a nice touch to an already nice package that'll keep me coming back to this game when I just want something to relax to.

Every single aspect of the art design of the game flows perflectly to create this uniquely weird yet belieable world that is a charm to visit, with all it´s oily disgustingness. Just based on how completely unique it is, I would say Sludge Life it´s a must have.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a weird game, like the kind of game you play when you are high at 2 in the morning. As for what in the seven hells this is... It is a first-person platformer, a graffiti simulator, where you explore a dystopian city, have I mentioned that its a psychedelic trip that will make you question your sanity. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a simple and concise experience for what it's worth. A fun narrative and visual style brings together this small open world, and with a short playtime to 100% (I'd say at most 4-5 hours), this could be a great weekend experience with friends, or with a drink (or both). _childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game enough. It's such a fun, bizarre, creative experience. It took me roughly 4 hours to 100%, although you can probably do it faster, so it's not a lenghty game, its' strenght really comes from the exploration the game allows you to do. Creative world and characters, a lot of exploring to do, fun writing. Very open, the player really defines the game as it never tells you what to do. Does not hold your hand, literally throws you into the spawn point and then you figure out what you're looking for in Sludge Life. You also have 3 endings to achieve, and with only 14 achievements, it's actually really fun to 100% the game, even for someone who is not traditionally an achievement hunter like me.Sludge life oozes brilliance and is one of the best examples of how creative indie games can get.

Everything down to the dated aesthetic, the WTF? humour and uniqueness of it all to seeing weird things like  This game is so up my alley, it's like I died and travel back in time and left to explore this sewer island in the middle of nowhere. Don't get me wrong, there's a lot of weirdness in this game, but it is left at your degression to mess around and figure out what to do, like tagging your name everywhere or learning about the subtle lore of the 'city', completing 2 of the mini-game. If the weirdness is too much you can stop at any time, take a break, and come back to it whenever. Lastly, the map isn't that big so you'll be getting familiar with the environment in about after 2 hours, but the game isn't that long (as you could probably tell from my playtime) of completing 9/14 of the achievement, still, I was satisfied with this experience like no other small bungle of exploration games I've played. Even way, it doesn't stop this game from being one of my faviourite this year and soon looking back on it as a very prominent classical simulation game in the 2020s. Purchasing this game boiled down to whether you can you handle this drug-endorsing experience (and I hope the answer is yes if you're off-age, kids don't do drugs).
