I would not recommend this game on the basis of how unplayable it actually is, not because of the gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: If this was under 10 dollars, I would recommend it as a decent time waster. Right now though I can't recommend it. I liked the visuals and sounds. The concept looks interesting: Explore a universe, explore planets, harvest materials to survive and build things, find new ships and new party members. Sadly, the exploration is pretty much pointless since there is nothing unique to discover. Harvesting materials is either busywork so you can keep travelling or to build modules that only make travelling more efficient, which is moot since there is hardly any point to exploring. Exploring planets with your party is also repetitive since there is nothing really unique to discover. No cool items to find nor lore or secrets. You can discover new ships, which sounds great, but their only difference is the looks and how much space they have. The point to having more space is just to make things less tedious which feels unrewarding.The game play loop is basically repetitive maintenance to get materials and fuel so you can get to the next place so you can get materials and fuel etc.So, how is the story then? The premise is interesting, but the execution is extremely shallow. The characters act and talk like they are 12 years old and although the story introduces some cool concepts the way it unfolds feels immature and like I said: Shallow. There are multiple endings it seems, but the one I got felt very unrewarding without any choice in how it turns out (The judge ending) and I did not feel like doing the busywork to get the other ending(s)Final verdict: If you can get this game for a big discount and want something mindless to just keep clicking through then it's decent. For it's full price or until they release an expansion which greatly expands the game play I would say to skip this.Alternatives for this game would be games like Diluvion, Rebel Galaxy or Between the Stars.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't in good conscience recommend this. Maybe in a few months (or years, at this rate) when the big issues are ironed out, things will be better, but considering that this game was meant to release a year ago, it should be incredible by now. Good:-The ability to drag resources directly into the fuel, oxygen, or hull is the best quality of life improvement from the original game I could have asked for. -The increased interaction with other life is very enjoyable. The trading system is awesome (if a bit overpowered), and I like building a massive crew. Bad: -Expeditions suck, for many reasons, and other people have explained the main failures better than I can. Some of the less game-ruining ones, however, I'd like to discuss. For one, the mini-game to find anomalies is incredibly tedious, and adds nothing. Sweeping a planet for the 20th time isn't fun, it's just a waste of time. Also, what's the point of multiple anomalies per planet if you can only actually visit one? From a gameplay perspective, having to choose is interesting, but there is no in-game explanation for it, which just makes it frustrating.-It's easy. From someone who beat Omega Edition multiple times, it's *mind numbingly* easy. I understand that the difficulty was the biggest criticism of the first game, but a hard mode would be nice. Specifically, the fuel costs are nearly negligible, expeditions have basically no downsides, there are too many slots, and there is no longer any incentive to min-max. Out There Omega was, at its core, an inventory management game; this game has somehow managed to trivialize that aspect of it. Bugs: -Wormhole generators aren't very useful, entirely due to their map. You have almost no frame of reference: your goal pointers go away, your trail is gone, and it changes the way you've angled the camera. This cost me a game.-Sometimes, when you've finished an expedition or looked at an abandoned ship, the game thinks your cargo hold is open when it isn't. Clicking the button to close it does nothing, and exiting to the main menu and coming back is the only solution. -Expeditions cause ridiculously low frame-rates. The graphics option in the settings does nothing to alleviate this.-If you fly away from a planet you have discovered an anomaly on, but haven't visited, the anomaly disappears.I desperately wanted to like this game, and I honestly feel robbed. I expected much better considering the original Out There's quality.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a neat game, and better than the original Out There (in my opinion).  However, it's INCREDIBLY limited and doesn't let you do things in any logical manner.  The first example, when you get the opportunity to create bunks for your crew, you are FORCED to discard or destroy something (if, like me, your ship is full) to make the component.  And, if you were trying to make room, it FORCES you to put it where you made room.  No, you can't move components around, you have to disassemble them and you lose resources in the process.  And you can't stop the tutorial from forcing you to do it RIGHT NOW.  And it does this EVERY TIME you get a required component.  Sure, it's an OCD thing, but if you're not going to make the game user friendly, it's not worth a positive review.

_childDocuments_.review: Not really much play here.  The seems to be a lot going on with all the ship components and resources, but you get basically everything in the first 5 hours.  And since you have access to it all there really was no replayability desire.  Endgame is a boring chore as you are just jumping as fast as you can to get to the story points, there are no threats or progress at this stage.  Character progression is nonexistent as you complete the game with characters at level 2, with none of their skills or classes were necessary or added anything to gameplay.  Effort was put in to make this a "non combat" game, but in doing so conflict was removed.  This makes the gmae unchallenging and dull, and there is not enough "chrome" to bring it to the level of a visual novel.Suggestions;Don't force the "roguelike" this game would play just as well in a set universe (like a starflight type game)If it's a set universe you will be able to add more set challenges, with multiple quest lines occurring simultaneously  This would give you time as your game mechanic for conflict if you really need to keep guns off the ships.  Perhaps helping the different races might lead to different endings and replayability?  Time as a factor would make lots of those character abilities do something, if you had limited time on an expedition then maybe the skill that lets you move more hexes would have meaning, but now where there is no time limit what does it matter?More than anything the game feels like a shell for a space MMOrpg, thouvgh I doubt the developers are that ambitious.Bottom line right now, just no good.It's pales in comparison to FTL (2012)It's got less gameplay and story than Starflight (1986)It can't even compare favorably to the original space roguelike on the old apple][ computer "Sundog" (1984)Sorry, Out There:  Oceans of Time 2/10

_childDocuments_.review: A daring attempt to expand on Out There: Omega Edition, but sadly lost focus and fell flat.New ship management gameplay can be fun; ship navigation feels largely the same as OTOE; UI is streamlined with hotkeys, can have softlocks occasionally though but nothing can't be fixed with good old alt+f4, remember to save often.Unfortunately the core feature of OTOE: survival, is not here in OTOOT. Staying alive is so utterly trivial you have to actively sabotage your run to be in real danger of an early game over. Another core feature of OTOE, learning alien language is also getting sidelined here. Choosing the right response will only slightly alter the inventory of alien vendor and recruit roster. Hell, you can safely ignore the shopping system entirely, since resource is hardly a problem.And lastly, to me the real crime is the writing in this game. In OTOE the random events that happen when you jump to a new star did a good job setting the atmosphere of the game -- the dread in face of the unknown, the wonder of the universe, the helplessness of flinging oneself into the void using utterly inexplicable alien technology, the struggle to tread the fine line between functional and lunatic and functional lunatic, and mixed with a healthy does of body horror. But all this, is absent in OTOOT. The random encounters become few and far between, and what left of them reads as bland as the instructions printed on the back of your instant noodle package. The new protagonist, Cpt. Nyx and her sidekick are not that likable, and the main plot is... whatever. The canon ending also somewhat undermined the plot of OTOE, Oh and there's one steam achievement,  , which is broken at the time of writing of this review. And the community manager over at the official discord confirmed there's no planned fix in sight, making it impossible to 100% this game. If you are into that kind of thing, avoid this game.

_childDocuments_.review: It's OG Out There but 'bigger and better'. I can't really explain it any better.I can however list a few issues:- Very rare UI bugs (none are critical, you just have to restart the game if it happens).- Early game expeditions should be much more punishing RNG-wise, right now it's actually harder to do late-game ones (and please don't bring back expedition timer).- There's something wrong with expedition rendering/generation stuff - depending on the location it can bring even the mightiest CPUs/GPUs down to it's knees.QoL suggestions:- Hotkeys for space views (planet/system/galaxy)- Allow skipping all cinematics/animations (ie end of expedition)- Perhaps 1 spare space in drill/post-expedition screen to allow moving stuff around when you're fullBalance suggestions:- Nerf early game Archon ship - it's way too good, especially morale/comfort - you don't  have to replace it until you get Nyx's ship- I think it's worth specializing ships, that is locking some slots to be cargo/tech/module, otherwise it's not really worth swapping themP.S.:To all the people comparing the game's writing to Mass Effect - have you actually played ME lately? Because if you did you'd remember how weak ME writing is. This game is ME-ish at best, but condensed as necessary to fit the game loop. It is ME in 10 lines of dialogue it requires to progress the story. If you somehow think otherwise I'm going to disappoint you - you're delusional. ME has always been and always will be your average overarching space opera, which actually reminds of Kojima's MGS writing. And just to be clear - I've played ME & MGS on both consoles & PC multiple times (mostly on consoles).Overall, it's a great successor to OG Out There barring some bugs & a few balancing issues.

_childDocuments_.review: Huge fan of the original. Sadly my first impressions of this sequel were not great. Initially I was put off by the poor quality of the animations in the cutscenes; having a quality on par a bad mobile MMO. And the writing in the intro/tutorial is pretty bad too, not to mention it's all there just to set up one of the worst possible plots. None of what unfolds gives you any reason to care about any of the characters, let alone anthing that happens with regards to the plot.As for the game mechanics. Surface exploration felt underwhelming to play, though it looks good. As for the core gameplay, I feel like this incarnation suffers from the same problems as the original, where there's an optimal depth to plumb for fuel, and an optimal depth to mine. At least the previous mobile game had the decency to keep the probe slider at your preferred setting. This game is worse by virtue of resetting the probe slider to a default value and making you have to specifically dial in the value on the probe slider each and every time.At this juncture my journey abruptly ended. Was playing the game via cloud gaming service 'geforce now'. 40 minutes in to the game and geforce had some problems and had to close. When I logged back in to geforce all those 40 minutes of progress were lost. Nor did I feel like I really achieved any interesting gameplay during those 40 minutes. I don't mind games being difficult, but 40 minutes is a long time to spend retreading the exact same ground because the developers can't be bothered to figure out how to do saves properly. A hard game can be fun, especially when the difficulty is well defined within the context of the game world. There's no reason this should stop the game from being robust in the face of the real world.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fine little space explorations and survival game. The survival mechanics come in two flavours: (1) Managing ship resources (fuel, hull repair elements, O2, morale) and (2) away missions on planets where your away party has some abilities and an item to help manage the dangers, perform actions, and O2 supply if relevant. The away missions happen on a tile grid.There is no combat.This game has no voice over. However, dialog cut scenes are short, have just a few lines of dialog per character, and progress is at the speed of the player. There is no choice during these dialog cut scenes, just pace management so you can read your speed (again, short sentences).The graphics are appropriate for this kind of game. The developers failed to use standard library and resolution & scaling approaches to support a variety of screen dimensions. This may make the game hard to read or play for some players.There is no wide-screen/ultrawide screen support.There are black bars instead.The left and right "screen" limits are narrow, making certain side-scrolling mechanics effectively broken (there are two fun operators, > and <, which would have meant it was not broken if they were used with the x-axis cursor position).The game is short. For me full completion was 17 hours. I took my time.On a $/hour entertainment scale, this game is poor.However, the game mechanics are limited and the length is very appropriate for the game. I was ready for it to be done. So it's just about the price.All in all, a decent game with a few flaws that don't get in the way of enjoying the campaign and the mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: ModernFox really delivered by fixing the "Incompatible Save" bug! My previous save worked immediately after the new update and I just couldn't be happier. It took a few hours to really get into the groove again but I have to say I'm enjoying the hell out of this game. It's addictive and somewhat hardcore yet also casual because it's all turn-based which means I can play even with lots of distractions or breaks. I wholeheartedly recommend!! Thank you so much for fixing the issue ModernFox!I feel like I've still only scratched the surface of what's in this game. There's a wild, cosmic story, interesting technologies like terraforming and strange alien ships to find and take over.It's most fun when you get a ship big enough for extra technology and a crew of 8+. There's activities like space exploration, mining, probing, gathering resources, away team expeditions.Some of the details that I really like:* The cool graphics, colors and animations* The excitement of finding a new abandoned ship that has the specs I need to switch to* Learning the alien language one word at a time and then guessing how to respond* Simple and yet complex in unexpected waysThe main things I'd like to see improved or clarified:* Not quite sure what the unexplored checkbox in Galactic map is for* Not quite sure what the Storage Arrays are for* I want to see Expedition details, including Passages and Risks, while selecting away team* Better consistency in controls across all views (see below)Mouse controls could be more consistent across all views:* Consistent mouse button across all views for rotation  - I recommend: Middle mouse button* Observe or Scan action needed across all views  - I recommend: Right mouse button* Action - travel to, move to, enter, interact with  - I recommend: Left mouse button

_childDocuments_.review: Overall good game.Story: "Out There" haha geddit? This is my biggest gripe with the game because it feels like the biggest missed opportunity. Characters and their motivations are mostly esoteric, and most character interactions are over and done with in less than a minute. It feels very roguelike, which I suppose it is, but it's also frustrating because it feels like an RPG storyline compressed into like 500 lines of dialogue. As the most egregious example, at the end of the game (obviously SPOILERS) I am allowed to ask one question. I get THREE CHOICES and when I pick "yo who made this weird ♥♥♥♥ the whole game is sorta based around" I get, not in so many words, "the developers, moron."Bruh.Meanwhile I'm surrounded by better questions, in my opinion, like "What the everliving ♥♥♥♥ happened around Earth!?" The funniest ♥♥♥♥ is there's a character in my crew for most of the game who definitely knows, but I can't ask them.BRUH.The game handwaves all of this sort of questioning I imagine my crew would be desperately interested in with, basically, "it is beyond your understanding." The worst kind of cop-out. I get that sometimes answering the questions makes a setting boring and the interest is in unanswered questions, but usually this is done by having people who have answers be all dead, or utterly insane, or out of reach. Out There has them join your ♥♥♥♥♥♥' crew, say "beyond ur understanding lol" then like, I dunno, travel with you for weeks or months or years and just sorta awkwardly stare at you in the hallway on your way to the mess. It is very frustrating.At one point literally billions of people die and the dialogue around that is like, two paragraphs worth.Gameplay:Gameplay overall is good. You are constantly juggling resources and there are a lot of resources to juggle. Fuel, oxygen, hull, and morale will end your game. Space is gargantuan and basically bereft of space travelling life in the OT universe. If your fuel runs out nobody is gonna come by, ask for some Galactic Standard Credits TM, and fill you up. You just float alone in the void and eventually die.Speaking of "credits" there's no such thing. In space everything is done in barter, which makes sense when you're interacting with planets that as far as I can tell run the gamut from "megalopolises that haven't seen a ship in years" to "tiny tribal villages." This makes storage an incredibly important resource because aside from a few infinitely-storable trade goods (think art and things) you need to both have stuff to sell and the space to accept the stuff you want.On top of managing your storage space you're also constantly eyeing new blueprints, rare resources to build those blueprints, and then when you finally get everything you want you find a ship with 10 extra slots and now you have to do the whole thing over again. It keeps everything from getting boring.There are flaws here too though. Your performance and resistance cap out at 10. Nothing tells you this, so I kept trying to pump up one or both before I realized I'd wasted a ton of time and effort on more-or-less literally nothing. Certain technologies, placed next to each other, have synergies. But nothing tells you what has synergies, or what those synergies do. You just have to guess, which is infuriating for some of the higher-end technologies. Often this is pretty easy to guess; engine related things should be put next to the engine for example. But whether or not something works out is kind of a crapshoot. Drill upgrade next to the drill? No synergy. Telescope upgrade next to the telescope? Synergy.Graphics/Sound: Middle of the road honestly. Nothing awed me. Nothing made me think "this is garbage." I was just like "yes this is a game and these are sci-fi sounds." Definitely wouldn't spring for the soundtrack.Overall: Like I said at the top, overall good game. It's fun. It's absorbing. The plot is good enough/interesting enough for me to care about it, which means it isn't terrible it just isn't good either. Same can be said about the graphics. If it's worth 20 bucks for you to ♥♥♥♥ around in space for 10-20 hours, buy it. Otherwise, don't.

_childDocuments_.review: Phew, I'm giving this the thumbs up - It IS the Out There that we know, love and remember but it just takes a bit a of digging to get there....First, the downers:-the game is not as slick and stylish as the original. There is more graphical horsepower on display here, but somehow the simplicity of the original game's animation and the paired down character images were (for me) more mystical and evocative of a surreal sci-fi mood. The 3D rendered characters don't do it for me - bring back the lush portaiture artwork we have previously seen in Out There Chronicles and Sigma theory. - the music and sounds are just dull in comparison to the thumping swagger of the originals. Seriously could they not just release a modded version with all the original music and sound effects? I miss it...- the gameplay is a bit fiddly at first, but thats OK because it leads to the uppers...which are The Uppers - Yep, this game does capture the free roaming spirit of the original game but you have to stick with it to find that out. There are the same quixotic and risk/reward scenarios to encounter and a rich vein of sci-fi lore to explore. - It took me a while to get used to the additional crew and exploration mechanics, but now I'm there and they add a new dimension to the game whilst all the old anxieties around oxygen, fuel and hull are there. This game doesn't have the elegant, simplicity of the original game, nor the artistic and musical flair, but for all that this is still an authentic Out There experience. The feeling is closer to that of an expansive table top game, with varied and satisfying universe to explore. Worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Out There: Oceans of Time

_childDocuments_.review: I have to spend fuel to travel out of a system and back to a system so that I can "rest" before I can go on another expedition... Which will likely strand me... The game isn't so intriguing that I care to tolerate that mechanic. If I'm landed on a planet then why can't I just rest without spending fuel or oxygen? The answer is because there is no "resource" to spend that makes sense, so they make you arbitrarily spend fuel and oxygen and hull points to regenerate characters and prevent you from doing too many expeditions back-to-back... This killed any semblance of immersion I had.
_childDocuments_.name: Out There: Oceans of Time

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game and would be back for another run through soon.  The early game is a bit challenging because of the number of slots available on your starter ship, but that kept it exciting and it is very satisfying when you get a nicer ship with more space to work with.   Starting about mid-game,  this becomes more of a relaxed jaunt through space, just enjoying the spacy ambiance.  It is simple and relaxing with gameplay being straightforward.  It is a nice way unwind.I only ran into only one bug on my first playthrough, and it was with the autosave system.  But the developers are very active on discord and are planning to address this in the next patch.  They even sent me a fixed up save file.  It is good to see more games in the space exploration genre and I wholeheartedly support indie developers in this space, which is my favorite genre of games to play.  There is no space combat in this game, so the focus is purely exploration with a little bit of resource management and survival.    I think there is a solid foundation here that the devs could potentially build upon. More depth and meaning to that exploration game loop (without necessarily tying it to a storyline) would be very welcome for example.  Overall, I would recommend this to someone wanting to spend a few hours in a casual space-themed game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sucked in. I came across an anomaly shortly after finding a new ship that put me off course. I was on the brink of being out of fuel when I happened upon the husk of the ship I stripped. It still had fuel but I couldn't transfer it. I had to rebuild enough systems to make it a tanker and scout nearby systems without a telescope for gas giants to scoop. Took a while just getting enough gas to move the tanker around. Then I had to backtrack to where I left my ship. Doing all this without running out of O2 was hairy, but pulling it off made me a fan!

_childDocuments_.review: Buggy, wait for a few patches!- A last-minute change before release (no more time limit on away missions) made many abilities and items literally useless.- Two crashes to desktop in 4 hours (but barely any progress lost, thankfully).- After bartering, I lost all items I offered, but gained none of the things I bartered for.- Many of the choose-your-own-adventure prompts make no sense for your crew, or the environment.- Typos, and some strange writing that seems to generally be not native English.- Other players in the forums have reported other bugs I haven't seen.The game has nice graphics and music, and these issues are fixable. If you are interested, make sure to check recent patch notes before you buy. I will probably come back and play more after some patches.

_childDocuments_.name: Out There: Oceans of Time

_childDocuments_.review: It is a survival game, in space. It can be very hard to start, resource use, blueprint availability, what abandoned ship you find all lead into a different experience. The game is not short, taking me some 11 hours. However I also had a ship that was optimised with nearly all blueprints and 90+ bar oxygen use, if you want to play my way it will take you longer. Tip - when your ship is high level - jump black holes everywhere you will save an unholy amount of time. If you understand the vastness of space, a journey of seemingly insignificant people doing great things and take pride in knowing that you resource managed your way out of a nightmare then you will enjoy this game. If you have played Out There the original then you will enjoy this just as much.
_childDocuments_.name: Out There: Oceans of Time

I know I didn't play it long, but I didn't much care for being unable to turn off the planet-to-planet travel animations (only the system-to-system ones) and the somewhat misleading title.Between the two, I prefer the first game.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros : Spacescapes are awesome, ship detail is incredible, fluidity of play is good, quite a lot of space to explore.Cons : a bug or two trying to heal and the game didn't update the animation, wasn't sure if a heal happened, spent a few extra action points (totally fixable, I'm sure), would love a big more "side-track" quests - you have free roam, but the number of plot-quests are limited, perhaps this is on purpose to allow for future updates or DLC's. Your 3 ship attributes really tether you to short trips to keep your stocks up (fuel/oxy/hull) and morale takes a hit pretty quickly on a multi-jump push. It's better than it was before in the beta, but could use a little more optimization. Would love a bit more autonomy to make multi-dozen jump moves (perhaps future quests would force you traverse the tendrils of the galaxy or bisect it more than 20-50 hops).Suggestions : More ship selection - I'd love to see a ship even larger than the Vanguard (50-75 slot Starship of some sort). This would give you capabilities to keep the ship upkeep and fuel reserves well in balance with a long cross-galaxy traverse. Also, finding other humans would be kinda nice - you get the impression that Nyx and Sergei are impersonal officers unable to draft their own kind :p I still absolutely recommend this to others - there's so much potential for add-ons, DLC's or even mods with the traverse-able galaxy as large as this.
_childDocuments_.name: Out There: Oceans of Time

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the first Out There, and this one is even better. Better graphics, more things to do, and the added Expeditions mechanic really gives the game more weight as well. Definitely worth the price. No performance issues, running at a buttery smooth 144fps, at least for me, I read a review of someone not getting great FPS but the lowest mine has dropped is 90fps, with graphics on the highest setting, and it's only happened briefly. Jumps right back to 144. A must have if you think space is cool.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the story line of this game. The mechanics were simple and streamlined. I wasn't bogged down by the need to do repetitive tasks over and over again just to earn xp. To help put it into perspective, my crew had a max level of 3, so visiting planets and doing missions was more or less optional. I am not saying that there are not some tasks that require repeating (ie fueling up, repairs, oxygen), but they do not seem so overbearing that it feels like a grind. I was able to finish a version of the story line in about 6hrs and I am excited to play again to unlock/complete alternative story line endings.

_childDocuments_.review:
The successor to the award-winning Out There, Oceans of Time blends roguelike, resource management and interactive fiction for a space survival epic where death is one wrong decision away.

As Commander Nyx, explore a vast galaxy that is different every time you play, as you search for the Archon; a cosmic villain set on dominating the civilisations of the galaxy.

Encounter other strange lifeforms and learn to communicate, trade, and conduct diplomacy as you build a coalition of allies in your mission to find the Archon.

Recruit new members from the alien races you cross paths with, and build a team capable of traversing the cosmos. Manage your crew, your ship and its systems; the mission's success is down to your decisions as Commander.
_childDocuments_.name: Out There: Oceans of Time

name: Hades
detailed_description: ALSO FROM SUPERGIANT GAMES The god-like rogue-like returns! About the Game Hades is a god-like rogue-like dungeon crawler that combines the best aspects of Supergiant's critically acclaimed titles, including the fast-paced action of Bastion , the rich atmosphere and depth of Transistor , and the character-driven storytelling of Pyre . BATTLE OUT OF HELL As the immortal Prince of the Underworld, you'll wield the powers and mythic weapons of Olympus to break free from the clutches of the god of the dead himself, while growing stronger and unraveling more of the story with each unique escape attempt. UNLEASH THE FURY OF OLYMPUS The Olympians have your back! Meet Zeus, Athena, Poseidon, and many more, and choose from their dozens of powerful Boons that enhance your abilities. There are thousands of viable character builds to discover as you go. BEFRIEND GODS, GHOSTS, AND MONSTERS A fully-voiced cast of colorful, larger-than-life characters is waiting to meet you! Grow your relationships with them, and experience thousands of unique story events as you learn about what's really at stake for this big, dysfunctional family. BUILT FOR REPLAYABILITY New surprises await each time you delve into the ever-shifting Underworld, whose guardian bosses will remember you. Use the powerful Mirror of Night to grow permanently stronger, and give yourself a leg up the next time you run away from home. NOTHING IS IMPOSSIBLE Permanent upgrades mean you don't have to be a god yourself to experience the exciting combat and gripping story. Though, if you happen to be one, crank up the challenge and get ready for some white-knuckle action that will put your well-practiced skills to the test. SIGNATURE SUPERGIANT STYLE The rich, atmospheric presentation and unique melding of gameplay and narrative that's been core to Supergiant's games is here in full force: spectacular hand-painted environments and a blood-pumping original score bring the Underworld to life.

_childDocuments_.review: What could one say about one of the most popular games in recent times that hasn't already been said, many times over, by many a youtuber, game reviewer, steam player, or the zeitgeist in general, hasn't already? I'll say only that playing this was a blast and a reminder of why I always was so drawn to Greek mythology.
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: Where to start with Hades. Supergiant delivers with every single game they give, and this is no exception. Words cannot describe the joy I feel that this studio is finally getting the recognition it deserves. Hades drops you into the plot right away, giving you the bare minimum and making you feel confused in a giant world of enemies trying to block your path. The more you fail, the more you grow, and the more experience you get. You get stronger with each run, unlock new abilities, weapons, and even relationships. For a rogue-like, the plot is surprisingly in depth, and the interactions between all of the characters are incredible.On a technical side. The soundtrack is, as always, perfection from Supergiant. The music in Hades has a grit that fits perfectly with the aesthetic and environment of the game. The graphics are colourful and easy to look at, and it feels smooth and easy to play. The voice acting is out of this world, perfectly encapsulating the character they represent.The best part of this game is that you can play it however you want. YOU get to choose the weapons, the playstyle, the boons from your fellow Gods and Goddesses.Supergiant, you've done it again. Congratulations and well earned on your biggest success yet!!
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: Preliminary review, edited version coming up once I've made some more progress.This game has the potential to become my next Gungeon, it's that good. The amount of content and story including completely nonsensical random fun bits is staggering, the soundtrack, visuals and gameplay are extremely on point. 2 escapes have been successfully completed at this point in time and there's only a sense of tiny dents made in the fabric of Hades. If this keeps up and the game manages to make me try other weapons that aren't the spear, I'll be able to play this all the way into mid November, every day.10
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: I, as a major fan of all previous Supergiant games, almost instantly bought Hades and, my man, this is a BLAST. Amazing character design (both visual and script-vise), variable and dynamic gameplay, astonishing soundtrack (big props to Darren Korb, as usual), and, listen here... You can... PET CERBERUS. LIKE LITERALLY RUB HIM BEHIND THE EAR MY GOD. Seriously, this is one of the best rogue-likes I've played (and I've played almost all rogue-likes for the past 8-10 years) and this gem is still in early-acces. I mean, imagine what it will be when it is released. Insta-buy, if you ask me. Keep up the good work, Supergiant :)
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: 9 out of 10 stars would HIGHLY RECOMMEND. First of all, the art work is ABSOLUTELY STUNNING, the gameplay is highly entertaining (especially more so when you've found your preferred weapon and build you're wanting for each run). In the game Dead Cells there was a story line but it felt like you had to go out of your way to learn more. In Hades they made the story fit effortlessly into the gameplay with new dialogue after each death, picking up new items and weapons will trigger new dialogue from friendlies which can lead to more items/upgrades/abilities. To me, that alone is really impressive from a roguelike/roguelite game. The amount of detail in this game is perfect, you can tell the developers took their time with this game and didn't just rush to get it out like most developers now a days do, unfortunately.
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: Hades is a masterpiece and a testament to excellent game design. Everything from the controls, gameplay, difficulty curve/control, narrative, pacing, music, particles, replay-ability is nearly perfect. Meta-progression is satisfying through and through. Hades is a must-play in my opinion, and you are missing out on a true work of art by taking a pass. Avoid spoilers for and emotionally invest in the characters of Hades, as it is nothing short of a wonderful experience that you won't regret. On-boarding and tutorials of features are smooth as silk and highly thematic, allowing both casuals/non-gamers and hardcore players to enjoy this title.I struggled to find any parts of this game that I had issue with, to little avail. Browsing my boons during an escape attempt is a little awkward at first because of the diamond grid arrangement. Sometimes I'd end a play session after unlocking stuff in the House of Hades, and forget to move to another rooms for the auto-save to kick in, so I'd return with that stuff yet unlocked. The song selection interface seems to have gamepad navigation issues (e.g. I was unable to select Orpheus' Lament while it was only one unlocked). Beyond these hyper nitpicks, there's not much else I'd change about Hades.Also, you can pet the dog.
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: 10/10. From a massive roguelike fan. Worth the hype. Do yourself a favor and play it. Game of the Year easy for me. Supergiant Games delivers again, as they always do. This game completely and entirely lives up to all the wonderful praise and hype it's gotten. It speaks for itself. Supergiant is the gold standard for an indie developer pulling an early access game and listening to community feedback in such a way to make the perfect game that both fit the developer's vision and make it fun for the players. It's an extremely solid roguelike with fun, challenging, and dynamic gameplay that gives you so much agency in how your runs go as well as how you play. Every weapon has a multitude of playstyles and versions of them that genuinely change gameplay and feel fun to use. This game also knocks it out of the park with its narrative structure. Having a roguelike that has a compelling story and meaningful progression of the narrative is a rare sight, and Hades by far does it the best of all that I've played. Not to mention the characters that make the story flourish are all interesting, lovingly presented, and fully voice acted. It genuinely makes the between-run sections of a roguelike some of the most compelling. I can't sing the praises of this game enough, it's my game of the year, it's worth every penny and then some. Do yourself favor and play it. Easy 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: I've bounced off of countless roguelites and never really understood the appeal of Supergiant games, but this one got me. The character and story crumbs are surprisingly good ways to stave off the mid-game progress plateau that makes other action roguelites grind to a halt. Can't recommend this enough.

_childDocuments_.review: SuperGiant Games made the decision to engage in epic game store exclusivity.After watching the no-clip documentary about this game, it's clear that having a high review percentage on store reviews (primarily the ones hosted on Steam) matters to developers. Hosting a game exclusively on a store that does not allow users to leave feedback on their experience for other customers to review is fundamentally anti-consumer. It only benefits one party, the developers. SuperGiant gave their reasons and to be fair, they were pretty rational. Among other reasons, I can understand wanting to avoid negative reviews that are based on a deliberately incomplete, early access game. Avoiding the need to translate the game to multiple different languages for the steam release was also something I had not considered. At the end of the day, SuperGiant can rationalise it all they want but this will always be a mark against them.That being said, the game itself is fantastic. I thoroughly enjoyed the art, the soundtrack, the voice acting and the combat. One aspect that really impressed me was the sheer among of unique dialogue that's present in the game. Even when I was actively looking for it, repeating events only began to happen around 25-30 runs in. It felt like every time I returned from a run there was more new plot/character development to explore. Finally, the last thing I want to highlight is how well SuperGiant naturally represented minority communities in the game. I grow tired of how often minority groups are retconned to the detriment of the story or at worst, included at their expense. This really was a refreshing breath of fresh air. Writers, take notes please. If I am being pedantic, the mechanism to unlock the hidden weapon aspects isn't designed well. You have to exhaust the entire story dialogue pool of an NPC to access the necessary hidden weapon aspects dialogue. The problem is every time I would try to cycle this person's dialogue by doing a run I would just progress the story further, meaning I would have to do even more runs to get the dialogue option I need to unlock the hidden aspects. This problem would be solved if I could just talk the NPC about the hidden aspects whenever I want if I meet the unlock requirements.I have other small problems with the game (I would have liked if boon dialogue ran in the background while you looked at your choices rather than being completely front loaded) but as a whole it's a great experience and I'm looking forward to their next game. Well done SuperGiant.

_childDocuments_.review: Hades is a hack and slash roguelike game from the masters of 2D action games Supergiant games, and Hades is no different from its predecessors in this vein. It is a complete package from start to finish as you try to escape Tartaros, with the storyline advancing even on attempts you fail meaning unlike some roguelikes where it can feel like you're pushing against a wall you never truly feel stalled.I would recommend this game, and have, to pretty much everybody you will not regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the few very well made Rogue-lites. A lot of quality of life elements that help combat the inherit RNG dependency of the genre and give player more control over the runs. Surprisingly good story and writing on top. Combat is more or less refined Supergiant's style arcade action, fluid and generally devoid of issues. And, as per usual, extremely well made dynamic OST.Few rough spots here and there, mostly related to the genre they've chosen. As such - reliance of story progression on specific consumable item usage. Which is likely to force you to grind a bit in second half of the game, if you didn't behave in the predict by developers fashion.Inability to clear previous difficulty remaining rewards by going higher difficulty, making some of the runs to "complete" clearing of difficulty feeling not as efficient with your time.Very very odd choice of initial hidden aspect unlock. One weapon has a unique requirement for that unlock, very likely to be your first one to be unlocked and doesn't represent the requirements for every other weapon except itself. This one in particular is just bizzare, it's almost like it was designed to mislead the player until they go out of their way to google the otherwise used requirements. In a game that is otherwise very much inclined to hint and directly show the player the inner workings and benefits of items, quest chains and actions.Overall still a very solid experience despite those few rough spots. And updates seem to be rolling out rather steadily, fixing some of the issues the game had.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is utter trash and a complete scam, both in marketing and narrative. The entire PREMISE of the game is to break out of Hell, but when I acheive that feat, I am sent back down and mocked by the devs with their oh so witty characters. Not only are you not able to beat the game, the developers decided that their gameplay was more important than their story and really dropped the ball. Cerberus is a loyal friend of yours, and the ENTIRE point of the final floor is about him not wanting to hurt you. That he WON'T hurt his friend. But that gets tossed out the window in the third phase of the fight with Hades, where Cerberus BETRAYS your trust and attacks you alongside your father. This angers me. This infuriates me. How can this game have an amazing story when they sacrifice it for gameplay? Not only that, but this in turn means that Hades was holding back all this time, another narrative fallacy. He wanted to keep his wife safe, yet didn't want to enough to win against his son using his full strength. He held back and let his son further endanger his wife time and time again. Also, you get NOTHING for beating him at his full power?This story falls apart when you really think about it, and I won't suffer it any longer. I'm officially done with this game. It tried to be Dark Souls and ultimately failed. What a joke.

_childDocuments_.review: Hades is a fun game, that does some interesting things with its structure. It's one of those "roguelike but with some persistent upgrades" deals, with the interesting note that being a roguelike isn't just a conceit of the genre but a core part of the plot. Your character is the rebellious son of the greek god Hades, trying to escape the underworld with the help of the gods of Olympus, and every time you die the river styx carries you back to the house of Hades at the center of the underworld. It'll probably take you quite a few runs to beat the game for the first time, but there's a larger story that requires you to beat the game several times, followed by a bit of a handwave explaining why you can keep playing after you reach the true ending.The gameplay is quite good and the visuals are as pretty as in everything Supergiant makes, but the thing that really holds the experience together is the writing. The game has a huge amount of dialog which is parceled out a bit at a time after each run, and it really makes the characters all feel like real people with personalities, whose relationship with the protagonist and to a degree even with each other truly evolves over time in response to what you do.
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: Hades starts with the son of Hades, Zagreus who is fighting to leave the underworld and must travel through his father’s kingdom to gain his freedom.  Much like most Roguelites the concept of Hades is deceptively simple.But before long players will fail in their quest, and pass on.  Zagreus will then be sent to the House of Hades.  From there, players can start interacting with the court of Hades.  After the first run, the House of Hades will be a little empty.  There’s, of course, Hades and Cerberus his faithful hound.  Players will also see Achillies and a goddess named Nyx, as well as Hypnos, who is Nyx’s offspring.  Over time, more characters will appear.  If it’s not obvious by that, Hades is based on the Greek Pantheon of Gods and through that gives the player a chance to not only be the son of Hades but also able to interact and meet with many of the famous figures in Greek Mythology.  While many gods show up, such as Zeus, Poseidon, and Athena, there are also famous figures in Greek Mythology, such as Theseus and Sisyphus. When these characters show up, Hades will also provide some interactions.  Every character in Hades has small discussions with Zagerus and there’s always something for them to talk about.  Whether it be story elements of their life or their appearance in-game, to Zagerus exploits, to even what Zagerus is currently doing.  A story in a rogue-lite sounds like a minor feature, but in Hades, it’s actually a very strong and central part of the experience.   The characters in Hades are from Greek Mythology but they also have a lot to say and contribute to the overarching narrative.  While this is still a rogue-lite where players are intended to play through, die and repeat, Hades also has a reason for these actions as well as characters I found myself caring about.  Just beating the game once also doesn’t end the story, but instead adds to a complex narrative where several characters and situations are playing out at the same time.   It’s part of what kept me coming back after my first win, but it’s also what keeps me interested each time a character shows up just to see what they might say this time.  The story is such a strong part of the game that after fifty hours or so, there’s still a lot of content and even an epilogue that I was working towards.   The story will only go so far, especially in a rogue-lite.  Rogue-lites are intended to be played multiple times over and over while players work towards a goal and in this, Hades excels. Hades works like many games where players are expected to dodge attacks and strike back at enemies.  Players can take one of six weapons into the dungeon on each run, and each of the six weapons has its own style.  The sword is the most aggressive of the group but also contains a special attack that will push back enemies.   The Spear allows players to throw the spear and have it return to the player’s hands, with both actions damaging enemies.  The Bow, Gun, and Fists act as you might expect, however, my personal favorite weapon is the Shield which feels like something from Captain America including an ability to throw the shield and have it ricochet off multiple enemies. Hades is broken up into rooms as players progress through areas, and each room will reward the player with an item at the end of a battle.  Each battle is both challenging but also well-paced as to not become completely overwhelming, giving players a choice of what reward comes in the next room helps to give the player some agency as they move through the dungeon. Players will often run into the gods of Olympus as they progress through the dungeon, and each one will bestow a boon on Zagreus.  These amount to upgrades which will usually increase Zagerus’ power, or provide some benefit to help him survive the dungeon.  There’s also the hammer upgrades that will change how each weapon works in a minor way.   Players will seek out these sets of upgrades as they make their way through the dungeon in the hope of getting strong enough to reach the end. However, once a run is over, all these upgrades are removed, and Zagerus must enter the dungeon fresh once more.   Yet, there are still rewards to be had and permanent upgrades to obtain through currencies found in the dungeon, such as darkness and a mirror that will allow Zagerus to unlock upgrades which will also increase his survival rate. Through a combination of learning the game, unlocking mirror upgrades, and getting boons, players will make progress through Hades underworld over and over.  And perhaps reach the final boss, maybe even triumphing over it. I actually accomplished this around my 25th run, and even after I’ve played at least 70 runs, I went back and tried the game from scratch and it’s still relatively hard.  Hades isn’t a game about just rote memory or a focus on perfecting the game, but rather a game about watching your character grow, become more powerful and one day accomplishes the unthinkable. And even after that point, Hades isn’t done, and instead gives the player more to chase.  Whether it’s a new challenge for your favorite weapon, which Hades provides in a difficulty mode called the Pact of Punishment where players have to choose optional challenges to increase the “heat level” to earn more rewards, or different weapons there’s always something new to do, and the random factor means no two runs ever feel the same. But there’s also something magical about Hades' difficulty, where it never gets too easy, but it also never is so challenging players feel like they aren’t making progress.  While there are challenges, Hades is a welcome breath of fresh air.  It’s a game that’s both satisfying to rogue-lite fans and fans who are new to the genre. Hades is also remarkably addictive to the point where I’ve struggled to put it down.  It’s a game where I constantly want to play one more round and suddenly it’s 3 AM and I missed my bedtime by a couple of hours.  This didn’t happen once or twice, but rather multiple times in the same week and then again on the following week.Even after beating the game, this addictive quality of it has yet to dissipate, and for a twenty-five dollar game that I’ve already put over fifty hours into, that’s a very good sign, in fact, that’s what I expect from an amazing Rogue-lite.But there’s one last fact that really makes Hades shine to me.  I struggle to really find an issue with Hades.  The gameplay is extremely tight and engaging.  There’s both a huge challenge and a welcoming nature to the game (including a god mode that will make Hades progressively easier if necessary).  There’s a story that keeps me interested in the game, but also gameplay that makes me sometimes skip the story just to get to the next big fight.  There are amazing moments of triumph and success and even when I fail, I want to return to the fight as soon as possible, because that feeling of progression is still there even when my run is cut short. The thing is Hades is just brilliant, and it’s a game I would recommend to everyone.  This is a game not to be missed, and honestly, Supergiant deserves accolades for this title.  While Bastion was amazing, this is almost certainly their best game yet, and that’s a very high bar. If it’s not clear, then allow my arbitrary scale to make it so.  Hades has earned a 10/10This is as close to perfection as games can get, and honestly, this is incredible. Check Hades out, you won’t be disappointed. _childDocuments_.review: One of the best games ever made!Gameplay is awesome. Artstyle and animation are flawless. Sound design is beautiful (I often stop to listen to characters singing); and voice acting is marvelous. The story is compelling, and the way you advance it a little bit between every run makes me excited to go for another escape.I don't normally like to die in games. But Hades doesn't let you resent death. It's not failure. Death becomes an old friend. Sometimes I even welcome it. And at moments where it would be frustrating (like losing repeatedly to a boos), the game does a good job on making light of it with funny remarks and nice dialogues/interactions that make it seem it was planned to be that way; as if the Fates are actually determining whether you should advance or be held back.I'm in love with Hades. And in all my 37 hours of gameplay, there was never a dull moment. I never felt bored, nor have I felt like I was doing a chore (fetch this, grind for levels, gather resources, etc). This is one of my all time favorite experiences in gaming.
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: When I first saw this game was created by Supergiant I instantly knew I HAD to have it. When I saw it was a Rouge-lite/Rougelike I REALLY had to have it. When I PLAYED THE GAME I KNEW IT WAS A MASTERPIECE. But let me tell you one thing; this game will suck you in and keep you there. _childDocuments_.review: I have to say that I think this game is probably the greatest roguelike game I've ever played. _childDocuments_.review: Truly peerless narrative within its genre. Everybody always talk about ludonarrative dissonance, but nobody ever talk about ludonarrative harmony and man, Hades's parts sing in beautiful harmony.

_childDocuments_.review: 151 Games in my inventory at the time of writing this. Out of those 151 I have beaten 28 titles from my collection. Of those 28 I have 100% only Hades.The amount of charm and replay value packed into this game is astounding!Around every run is a new bit of story that never once felt resentful or grind-y. If your struggling focus on putting darkness in the mirror and you will eventually overpower where your stuck and the story will progress. The story its self is a beautiful tale of family with Chthonic level family problems. Which brings me to another point the story... Blood and darkness is there a lot of it. Greg Kasavin, the creative director for the game, revealed that Hades' script contains over 300,000 words. This is a huge number, and to put this in perspective, the game's script is longer than the classic epics of Ancient Greece, The Iliad and The Odyssey combined.With every run I found that I never resented dying for me being salty at unfair mechanics is just a normal part of gaming these days, especially with the "we'll just patch it after launch" mentality that has become so pervasive and toxic to the industry. This game on the other hand is a well balanced, finely tuned masterpiece that goes one step beyond and allows you to fine tune it a little bit further to push your play style after your first complete run you get the pact of punishment.I  found myself playing with the pact of punishment and pushing my own ability to their max. In most of my gaming experience I do not finish games I either play till I get bored and have decided I've experienced more or less what the game has to offer. Or the games are too hard and I just don't care enough to "git gud" if its not fun it inst a game I'm going to put time into.With Hades I found myself actively searching out every little thing I can do, I still haven't seen all the possible weapon and boon combos and still find runs satisfying even after completing 100% .Supergiant Games, you've got a new fan for life... Now if you could just add a few garden improvements to the house contractor.Hades is my game of 2020.My personal tips if your new:Give a nectar to Thanatos to get his trinket.Equip the Pierced Butterfly (Thanatos Keepsake) Kill ALL Enemies without getting hit (Hard to do with the sword IMO Shield of Chaos makes this easier) Especially easy with Poseidon or Zeus on the special.WinAthena on Dash is a life saver for being able to dash through projectiles.

_childDocuments_.review: I get bored easily. With everything. Games will have some stupid little thing that annoys me and I'll shut it off and never pick it up again. I legit have game ADD. Is that even a thing? This game cured me of the illness I just made up but possibly may be real. This game is quick moving. You use your powers (sometimes temporary but hella powerful) to kick ass in every round. A round lasts as long as your life lasts. You go from room to room until the round is over. Once you clear a room, you usually have a choice of what "type" of room you want to enter next. One may give you power-upsOne may give you moneyOne may give you permanent upgradesand so on...When a round is over, you go home and talk to your Greek God or Goddess cousins, your ♥♥♥♥ of a dad, and as time goes on you get choices to do other things. It's cool cause all in all, death ain't so bad cause you still have stuff you need to get done at the house. It's addicting as hell. Which is good, cause you're in hell. It's funny. Wasn't expecting that part. You die and instead of getting pissed off, you can't wait to play another round, and plus you get to go back home and pet your three-headed dog. In hell. Every time you die. See, there's puppies and heaven and hell. we can't lose! 10/10 Want to call out of work and play this and ruin my life

_childDocuments_.review: 5/5 game. Full achievements and that's rare for me. Go buy. read on if you must. Hard to write a review for a game already so beloved and actually adds something to the conversation. Yes, this game is one of the best action rpg rouge-likes to exist. Easily top 3. Even if you don't like the combat, the story and art are superb. I would say the game delivers a 5/5 experience on multiple fronts. I'm only going to talk about the negatives extensively, because everyone else probably has already talked about the positives into the ground. I have nothing unique to add in that regard. The Gripes, Most of these were only noticeable when I started increasing the heat (difficulty) for the "pact of punishment". For reference, it was mostly when I was going for the 32 heat skelly statue. So these are kind of self inflicted to a degree, but I do think a game should be "fair" somewhat at higher difficulties. - The SPEED enemy perk. There are a number of perks you can give enemies with the pact of punishment. Random modifiers that give enemies unique abilities. (Think elite enemies from games like Diablo). I found almost all of these to be completely fair and something to overcome. Well, all of them except SPEED. What is speed you ask? Almost exactly what it sounds like. Enemies move way faster, and execute attacks way faster. Sometimes to the point where you can't strike an enemy without taking damage. Now, at lower heat levels this can be fun. You essentially have to adjust the dodge timings in your head and go faster yourself. But when you are at 32 heat and there are a number of negative handicaps occurring all at once, speed becomes a death sentence on certain levels (increase enemy counts, stacking perks, increase trap damage). Like sped up witches for example (ranged enemies). With speed, a witch battle in asphodel becomes one of those bullet hell games where your screen is mostly enemy bullets. The one exception to other bullet hell games though, is that you can get mini stunned every time you get hit with one of these bullets. meaning you can't just dodge straight to the center and focus on killing them as fast as possible. They will chain stun you into oblivion and your health will go from 150 to 20 in a second. So you have to wait to make your move. Dodge around until a pause in attacks and then strike. Oh, I forgot, they have speed. So this window is reduced to a second. Some speed encounters for me lasted Forever because of this tiny window. And even with patience and timing, a speed enemy level might still half my health. Now you can easily overcome a situation like this with the deflect boon (allowing you to redirect the bullets back to the enemy) but you don't always get this boon option (or don't want it). With the existing mechanics of the game I think speed quickly became a perk that made me hate playing the game. - Shield enemies. Shield enemies only exist in one area of the game (thank god) but they do something that goes against what I feel the point of the game is. Shield enemies can only be attack from behind. There are  a few exceptions to this rule but 95% of the time you will be forced to dodge behind them to actually do damage. On top of this they have their own attack moveset you have to wait for before going behind them otherwise you WILL take damage (its a circle attack that hits behind them). This means, like the speed mechanic, your attack window is reduced and it slows down the game. The biggest joy of this game is that the combat is extremely fast and snappy. You are constantly jumping around like a cricket on cocaine and dodging enemies like Neo in the matrix. Everytime I would see the "near miss" text pop up on screen, meaning I executed a perfect dodge, the dopamine center of my brain would have a mini explosion. Shield enemies essentially force the opposite sort of combat experience. Especially on 32 heat. Why you ask does more heat exacerbate this problem? Well, I'm glad you asked. Because instead of dealing with 3 shield enemies where you're waiting for all 3 of them to be done with their attack to strike, now you're dealing with like 8. And because there are way more and you have to dodge around the map and cover more distance, These 8 shield enemies begin to stagger their attacks. Meaning the window for your attack closes even more. Sometimes to a window shorter then 1 second. Oh, and don't even get me started on shield enemies with speed. I could throw my controller on that one. - Traps and LAVA. There are a number of traps in the game. Some of these traps shoot bullets, some try to hit you with a staggered melee attack, and some are delayed area bombs. All of the previously mentioned traps are easily avoidable and can even be used to your advantage (because enemies take trap damage as well). Lava on the other hand is obnoxious. Unlike the other traps which have delayed strikes and dodge-able zones, lava just sits there. If you step on it you have about a fraction of a second to get off before you start burning. Traps do immense damage, and lava is no different. So even if you dodge off of lava in time, you can still take upwards of 10 damage for such a mistake. On heat levels of 32 or higher with the trap damage increase, this damage can ping you for even higher. Stand on lava for more than 1 second? May god be with you. Now you may be thinking, why are you complaining? Lava can't move. Just don't step on it. Well, lava can have some weird hit boxes. You could be standing near the shore and it looks like you are on solid ground, but you still burn. Some levels have so much lava everywhere that the standard dodge distance will almost always land you on some sort of lava. Some enemies are flying and can sit (like a witch) over a field of lava and you unfortunately have a close ranged melee weapon. This means you have to jump in and out extremely quickly (usually taking damage anyway) of the lava to even attack this enemy. The other traps can usually be disabled for a time when they go off. So you can active a trap purposely just to make it inert for a bit, and then fight in that safe space. Lava has no such feature. ITS LAVA. It doesn't deactivate, it exists. And it exists to burn your literal BURNING FEET you were born with as a god. Lava does not compromise, it takes. I hate lava. - Repeating dialogue. Now while I did praise the game for an amazing story and characters with a novels worth of dialogue its not all gold nuggets. Many of the characters you talk to will say the same thing they said last time but just in a different way. Not a biggie, and a very minor gripe. - The BOSS SPIN. This one is probably personal to me, because I have a square brain and real time combat has always not been a strength of mine. Both the final boss (Hades), and Theseus have this move. Essentially its a delayed spin attack that is indicated to the player with a pre-spin white line circle. You would think that the timing on this attack is easy to anticipate because of the white circle indicator. WRONG. I can't tell you how many times I've been hit by this move. Either because I instinctively dodged towards the end of the indicator (when I feel like the move should go off) or because I tried waiting for the correct window and the move happened too quickly for me to react. I don't know how to fix this problem because even after 80 hours of play I don't think I understand the move window still. It almost felt like a move that was un-dodge-able. What was my solution to this problem? Get a boon through Hermes that gives me at least +2 more dodges and spam dodge my way through the attack. Now, I didn't always get this boon so sometimes I was forced to try and learn this annoying dodge window but I could only ever get around a 50% dodge rate. Also, Hades fight version 2, via pact of punishment, has about double the amount of spins attacks which makes even attempting that modifier immeasurably frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: Best roguelike I've ever played. I enjoyed everything from the Greek mythology story and characters, to the boons and keepsakes that enhance your builds. My personal favorite weapon was the Shield of Chaos. It's immensely satisfying to block incoming attacks, charge a powerful bull rush, and obliterate your enemies to clear each encounter. This, of course, is only one of countless possibilities offered by Hades' combat. The sword, spear, bow, rail-gun and twin fists offer unique strategies, upgrades, and even stories about who wielded those weapons in the past. Each battle is further enhanced by "casts" and "calls" which you receive from gods who want to help Zagreus escape the underworld.My two favorite gods were Poseidon and Dionysus, but they're all well written and well voiced. The boss battles also introduce interesting characters, my favorite being Asterius the Minotaur. My other favorite side character is Eurydice, who sings beautifully and offers you a choice of helpful boon upgrades. Every facet of Hades is finely crafted and offers an enjoyable experience. The story is well written, the combat is addicting, and the scenery is gorgeous from the deathly dungeons of Tartarus to the lush landscapes of Elysium. All of this is amplified by the amazing soundtrack. The only gripe I can offer is that I had to button-mash a little too much at some points. Aside from that, Hades one of the best games I've played in a while.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing this game for less than three weeks and I've put 57 hours in. It's really good. If Spelunky 2 hadn't come out this year, it'd be a lock for my GOTY. As it is, it's in my top two and don't ask me to choose between my babies. So, about the game. It's a supergiant game, so, interesting story, great soundtrack, gorgeous visual design, tight gameplay. I do think this is their best effort so far, everything just has that extra bit of polish and elbow grease put in. This is a rogue-lite, hack and slash/beat-em-up game with slow, permanent upgrades. The first time you beat the game is really just the end of the first chapter as far as the story goes. The story is fed to you in tiny, ignorable (if that's your jam) pieces over time. I've made fifty something runs, beaten the game around 5 times and I still don't have all the answers, and I'm still getting new dialogue from the NPCs I interact with. This game is genuinely great and worth whatever you pay for it. (Also, Dusa is the best, and if anything happens to her, I will kill everyone and then myself)

_childDocuments_.review: This game is by far the best rogue-like on the market and is game of year material. It's also the only rogue-like I've seen that takes full advantage of it's nature. _childDocuments_.review: First, I literally H-A-T-E rogue-like games, no exception. The reason why I initally bought the game is obviously because it is a Supergiant Games title, and this didn't disappoint as well like their other products. Supergiant did use their unique art style, voice acting and of course music again and they grasp you till the end. Characters, combat fluidity and writing are top notch. Each run is nearly different than the previous one and after events are so vast that virtually no dialogue or interaction with a character is the same.If you're on the same page like me and have no patience for rogue-like games, Supergiant also thought and added an option called "God Mode" which allows you to reduce your damage intake and make it more bearable. I personally went to the Epilogue with this option and %100 the game. One thing that I have found really exhausting is the dialogue options and their randomized approach. Of course they're not actually randomized and require certain level of requirement set before you continue the story; however it really exhausted my when I try to %100 and see the Epilogue. You basically pray to RNG gods to get a specific dialogue from a vast variety of dialogue options for one character, so your chance is quite minimal. That approach for completionism is the thing that I most disliked about the game since it artifically extended my playtime. Tried some good builds and was fun, but wouldn't play that extra 20 hours otherwise.It's a solid 9 or 10 out of 10 of course and a must play.

_childDocuments_.review: When I got this game (December 2019), it claimed that it was early access, but what I got was a more complete game than the majority of games that are released at full price.The concept of a roguelike RPG never crossed my mind quite the way it is implemented here. Dying is supposed to be part of the fun, but I never quite felt that way until this game, where I could rage at the boss that beat me, knowing all the while that next time I would be a little stronger, even if I didn't have the same weapon and ability combos.The other thing this game does well is subtly urge you to make different builds by randomizing rarities and improving certain effects. It's a good way to prevent complacent gaming, because you are incentivised to pick the strongest available option rather than the same one each run.I haven't made it out quite yet, but believe me, I'm gunning for Olympus!

_childDocuments_.review: Hades is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ masterpiece of a game. I HATE roguelikes, yet I love this game with all my heart. I'll be honest, I'm not the best at these kinds of games, but I found Hades very approachable and enjoyable. I did eventually take advantage of the game's god mode to make thing's a little more manageable (all god mode does is reduce the damage you take) since I kept dying somewhat quickly. I had fun before I turned god mode on, but the game actually felt beatable when I turned it on. It still took me a total of 18 tries and 11 hours to beat the final boss for the first time even with this god mode on. One of the things I love about this game is that while you start over when you die, progression items carry over, which gives a sense of progression that no other roguelike I've played gives. In a way, dying in Hades can sometimes feel useful and rewarding, since you can now spend or save all the items you've collected while playing.The combat in this game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing. The many different weapons all feel different and have their own play style. You'll very quickly get used to one of these weapons and will want to try and beat the game with it. For me though, I actually beat the game for the first time with a weapon I didn't like too much. That just goes to show though how good the game's combat is. Even with weapon's you aren't used tom, as long as you're good with them, you can succeed. Since this is a rougelike, there are a lot of random aspects to the game. My favorite of these random elements are the "boons" (powerups) that you can get on different floors. These are gifted by multiple gods that help you along your journey. There are SOOO many different abilities and ability combinations that It would probably take over hundreds of plays to see them all. Like the weapons, you'll find specific powerups that you like more than others and you hope they'll be there every run. But, like with the weapon, I actually won against the final boss for the first time with a super weird set of powerups. Again, it goes to show how well this games combat is set up. These random abilities can all work together so well. The story of the game is also a highlight. Without spoiling much, the playable character (I'll call him his nickname, Zag) is trying to escape the underworld to see the surface. It's a simple enough story at first, but every time you die, some of the story might unlock. You also get to talk to multiple gods in the house of hades, which is also where you can upgrade yourself and your weapons. These NPC's always have something interesting to say, and most of the time it's something related to your last run. Considering every line is voice acted, this is super impressive! There are so many different lines to hear, and the voice acting is just perfect.I really like the music in this game. It's nothing I'd listen to outside of the game, but it gets your heart pounding in those intense moments.The upgrades that you can unlock after dying feel worthwhile and useful. They all have different purposes, and depending on your play style, you'll end up focusing on certain upgrades more than others. The weapon upgrades also feel nice and upgrade the look of your weapon. The artstyle. THE ARTSTYLE!!! THIS GAME IS SO BEAUTIFUL!!!!! My score for this game is an 11/10. This doesn't mean it's perfect, just that its a masterpiece. I barley have any problems with this game, and the ones I do have can boil down to me just being bad at the game. BUY THIS GAME!!!! I will continue to play this game until I get burnt out of it.

_childDocuments_.review: I am extremely bad at games. Unbelievably bad. One-stage-behind-in-evolution bad. Not only am I bad, but I'm also not really keen on trying to get better. I have a full-time job, I have other hobbies, and I have ♥♥♥♥ to do around the house. When it comes to games, I just wanna bask in my escapism without having to try too hard at anything. So this is a review from... that perspective. This game is great in every way I could think to assess it. As someone who's terrible at video games, I was most worried about the gameplay. However, God Mode (which gives you +2% defense every time you die, up to 80% total) makes it really accessible for me. You still die a lot, which is the point of the game, but between God Mode and your power-ups I don't think it gets frustrating. I think the devs were thoughtful in how to implement a story-mode level difficulty while maintaining the overall experience of the game. There are so many different weapons and power-ups that I could customize to my play style to make things easier, but a lot was still random to keep things interesting. It was a great balance and I had a lot of fun experimenting with different combinations. I was also worried that the game would be too repetitive to stay interesting, but that wasn't the case. In all my playthroughs, I don't think I heard repeated dialogue even once. I looked forward to what the different characters would say next and the interactions they might have with other characters. Of course the gameplay itself is inherently repetitive, but if you're experimenting with different weapon/power up combinations, it doesn't feel that way. The art, the writing, and most of the voice acting was phenomenal. The character designs, the landscapes, and the color palettes are incredible. I hope that they release a gallery in future updates. Overall, you can tell that this was a game made by people who LOVE games. Their care and thoughtfulness is evident in every detail. I highly recommend it even if you generally write off rogue-like games for being too hard, like I do. I just finished my first escape and I feel so good and cool!!  There's so much left to explore and I'm really excited to keep going!
