_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. It's fast, fun, and easy to get into thanks to it's simple formula. Try to escape hell, a series of random rooms filled with enemies, by clearing the rooms and getting to the exit. When you die you start over. Each run takes between 15-45 minutes, and can be saved and loaded part-way, so its a great game to pick up and put down as you feel. The replayability comes from the progressive, mythological narrative, the range of tools for you to choose from before each run, and the combinatorics for you to solve during each run, for you to actually escape. The game is tied together by it's cool stylization and generous personality, to such a charming degree, I'd give it 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Brings together the quick and dodgy fighting style of Dark Souls, the dungeon crawling of Diablo 3, and the rouge-like leveling of Risk of Rain 2. _childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: Hades became one of my favorites and it is the best roguelike for me. One of the rougelike games I've played recently was Dead Cells, which is also great, so I expected it to have a more or less similar genre formula. But it definitely exceeded my expectations. Although the gameplay cycle is built on repetition, each run (escape attempt) is unique, achieved by the different weapons with distinct style of play, their aspects and a combinations of Boons, abilities bestowed by the Olympic gods. Every time you escape you progress through the story and reveal more about the characters, relationships with other gods and the mysteries of their origins. The hand-drawn artwork of the game is simply beautiful, the character and environment designs are detailed and visually pleasing. The soundtrack is incredible, with an end credits song so good I couldn’t skip it.This game is a masterful blend of storytelling, art, and gameplay with high replay value. It was totally worth playing and I can't recommed it highly enough. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: I hate rogue-lite games, extreme difficulty and permanent loss of progress, and heavily reliance on RNG to determine the quality of a run. I do however love SuperGiant Games. Hades is one of my favourite games of all time as it has so much more to offer. The storytelling is the best that a SuperGiant game can offer and the excellent satisfying gameplay and breathtaking soundtrack that SuperGiant is known for. All the characters are well written and lovable, meaning that it was a joy to die and return to the start of the game again. There are so many mechanics that reward repeated playthroughs, different playstyles permanent upgrades and a huge selection of extra things waiting to be discovered to unlock different storylines and uncover secrets. 10/10 game.

_childDocuments_.review: The first roguelike I ever played was enter the gungeon, and I loved that game, so when I heard about this game I knew it was right up my alley.  This combination of a rogue like with an actual good story is amazing as it motivated me to keep try again and again just so I could talk to the different characters throughout the game and try different combinations with the boons and weapons.  The music is phenomenal and at times I would sing along.  This game is a must play for anyone who enjoys rogue likes and I would even suggest newcomers to the genre to give this game a shot because trust me, it will be worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: ive never seen a game quite as perfectly made as hades.- the gameplay is smooth and engaging, riveting enough to want to play the game for its own sake- the roguelike aspect of it is balanced amazingly, there are very few boons or items that dont seem like they could be made powerful if you focused a build around them- being only a roguelite, there are some permanent upgrades and you cannot keep the run going forever, but this makes it so that the run never truly gets out of control and loses its gameplay value, and the permanent upgrades make it so that if you feel stuck, you can hopefully push yourself further with more upgrades.-  the shop in general is great, ive never seen a cosmetic shop for a SINGLEPLAYER GAME that i so thoroughly enjoyed buying thing out of- this game has the most likeable characterization of any video game character ive ever encountered, its *that* good. its definitely helped by the absolute gargantuan amount of stellar voice acting the game has- the story is something also really well done, but i'll not spoil it here, what i will say is that the game also has a bunch of mini-stories that slowly progress as you play, keeping tings fresh and interesting- the pact of punishment is a perfect way to add difficulty without feeling cheap. the player controls their own difficulty??? thats so cool@!!!!10/10 good game play it now

_childDocuments_.review: I am that person who never completed Sekiro, Dark Souls or Demon's Souls, because it is just not my type of games. I thought that Hades will be very similar to them, but I just could not hold myself from trying when I saw how beautiful it looked. And you know what, I already spent more than 30 hours on it and I am not stopping. The game is amazing, every run is so different and I just cannot say how well-written is the story. I actually loved to suffer in this game. I already feel the emptiness in my heart, because I do not know what to play after this masterpiece. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: Hades is an isometric hack n slash/bullet hell with procedurally-generated dungeons. You play as the son of Hades, who is attempting to break out of the Underworld, and you utilize various weapons, power ups and currencies to do so. TL;DR, the game's fantastic. It has a lovely art style, emotional story, amazing music, overall very good voice acting and very fun playstyles for most anyone. I think the only thing that annoys me about this game is a stupid fishing minigame (totally optional) in the latter half, and the protagonist himself is a Gary Stu who can get frustratingly annoying at times with how he talks. But other than that, I enjoyed the whole play through. it's a little easier than your typical roguelike, but there are in game challenges to alleviate said deficit.
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: I escaped. And now it's time to escape.Hades is a beautiful game with an intriguing narrative. The latter of which is more often than not left out of the rogue like/lite equation. Sometimes entirely. So it was greatly appreciated. The folks at Supergiant know how to deliver an atmosphere, that's for certain. But it gets the actual key ingredient of a good like/lite right as well; progression balance. I always felt like I was accomplishing something, unlocking something, or just plain getting better each time I played a loop of Hades. This pleased me greatly and often led to the "one more try.." situations.It does perhaps suffer from too many layers inside and outside of the gameplay. Don't get me wrong, I'd always rather have too much than too little. And I will put the huge caveat here that I play games without spoilers. A game like this is primed for me to completely miss the "meta" or whatever you want to call it. But you inevitably have to leave some avenues untouched until game+. A lot. Most. The overwhelming majority even! There's more than one weapon you can use, each with their own learning curves. I never left the default sword because learning another would be a break in my progression momentum. There's a handful of different currencies to collect and spend, but I likely missed that "game meta" on some of them and never accrued remotely enough. And so I didn't expand on the game areas they bought. There's a gift/friend system for all the characters you interact with, but they're all deep and have seemingly particular requirements to complete that are guesswork. With so many characters/Gods to choose it was a roll of the dice which to commit to. I ultimately only completed one of those. That's just a few examples of the layers. I'm barely past the tip of the iceberg and then game+ opens another whole can of worms with run/loop modifiers/challenges. I was drowned in unlockables and knew I never would, nor would want to, "100%" this game.But that's subjective. It's rad as heck all that is there for the people who want it. Whether they're the true champions or the weirdos that follow scripts of how to play games. There is oodles and oodles of dopamine accomplishment hits to be had and then another pile more. I just felt the strong parts of the game, specifically the story, couldn't keep pace with all those branching tunnels there were to explore. Then the gameplay is competent and fun enough to wield, but it can't do the same heavy lifting as other games in the genre. I won't call it a weakness, but the gameplay is shallow enough to notice. I'm nearing the end of my journey. I most definitely have to "escape" a few more times. I most definitely want to finish exploring a couple those 'tunnels' I started down. But will I even touch half of all of what Hades has? Nope. Which again, is awesome in its own right. I just can't do the 100's of hours with it like I have with others because the depth isn't in the gameplay, but elsewhere. I will unfortunately have to escape the game itself soon.Absolutely recommend the game wholeheartedly. Great fun. Whether you beat it once or dozens of times, you'll always be rewarded with something. All the praise is well deserved.It's a darn near perfect game on Steam Deck!

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games in many many years, it deserves all the awards it won. Fell in love with the artwork, music, voices, gameplay, grinding. Losing yourself in this world feels so good, everything fits together perfectly. What i really enjoyed is that the game starts really slow, and the more you play the more you unlock and discover. Many games flood you with all the information at once and it gets annoying and frustrating. The pacing is PERFECT.

Come for the fast action combat and rogue light progression, stay for the memorable characters and story.Edit: 17 hours in and still in love with this game. Now of the opinion that this is the best game Supergiant has made.Edit 24 hours in. This game is in my top 10 best games of all time. The music is superb and never feels out of place, I especially love "Out of Tartarus" and "Good Riddance". The story is amazing and the characters are incredibly well-written (especially Cerberus... I love Cerberus). Overall I highly recommend this game! The amount of effort and love put into it really shines through.(Also Meg could punch me in the face and I'd just thank her.)

_childDocuments_.review: I don't play roguelike games, but I might look into them after this. Gameplay was fun and exciting, the smooth voice acting was wonderful to listen to, and it was a thrill to finally reach the top floor after dozens of attempts. There is still much more to do after successfully escaping the first time which I'll probably get around to completing. Best boy - CerberusBest girl - Nyx
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so damn good I can't really convey the amount of joy I've been able to get out of it and continue to get from runs, the build diversity is staggering with 6 different weapons each with 4 different mods that change the way each weapon plays then around 100-140 boons(or more I'm not sure but adding in duo's and legendary's its gotta be in the triple digits) that all interact and change they way your character or weapon plays. I wasn't expecting this when i bought it, i thought this would be your run of the mill rogue-like on the level of gungeon or noita and while those are both amazing games in their own right hades is heads and shoulders above all the others not only with its mechanics, build diversity, story(yes, somehow they fit a very satisfying story in a game like this), this is the first game I've played in quite a while where it left my expectations in the down in the dirt soaring far and away past what I thought was possible in such a package.If you like rouge-likes, if you like quality, don't look at anything else this evening(or morning), buy this and never look back, your first 1-3 hours you're gonna have a challenge on your hands but its gonna be fun and once you unlock the majority of the weapons and start finding the style that suits you its gonna be off to the races, just hang in there till you hit your stride and accept the couple early failed runs, even the failures are often successes in hades.I really cant heap enough praise on this game, right now the 20 hours i have in this are from 2 days of non stop play other then when i had to stop to go to the store, take a shower or sleep, when i could conceivably be playing this i have been and right after i'm done writing this(because i feel i owe it to this game) I'm gonna eat the bare minimum of calories and start playing this again until i have to sleep. My only concern is that i'm afraid they wont make some dlc so i can support them with more funds as well as get some more content from this game, I'm still very far from running out of cool stuff to do, i just don't want it to end.Is good, Is really really good.

_childDocuments_.review: The story, art, ambiance, music, etc. is so RICH. It's been a LONG time since I've played a game I didn't get frustrated with for dying frequently, this game encourages you to die frequently.I'm a huge fan of Bastion and Transistor, so going into Hades and getting that rich storytelling + action (from new refreshing angles each time) has just made me love Supergiant Games that much more.Honestly, 10/10. I. Love. Hades.
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: What an amazing game.I've been hearing about Hades for years but never gave it a chance because it just looked like the completely different genre I enjoy. Boy I was wrong.The game is fantastic, the art style is mesmerizing and the voice acting is incredible.It's the most fun I've had playing a game in more than a year. Highly recommended to everyone.A game of this caliber at this price is a steal!Side note - this game really gets you into the whole Greek mythology rabbit hole.
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: As a master Gungeoneer finding another dungeon clearing rogue like means I've found my home. This game has beautiful graphics and incredible voice acting. The story is captivating and all of the characters have amazing personality, wants, needs, and backstory. Now for the actual game play. This game is incredibly punchy and bouncy. It genuinely fills a void that even Gungeon cant scratch. All of the weapons you can unlock are fantastic and change this game majorly from weapon to weapon. One moment I'm hacking my foes apart, next i'm basically playing gungeon with the rail, then I'm blocking all damage as I dash around with shield. The boons you get from your family members, the gods themselves, make this game a 11/10 for me. Making this game incredibly replayable and just so fun. Hyper Super Mega Recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: Don't usually like roguelikes, but this one does progression really well. Player death is woven into the story in a fun way and provides more unique interactions with the characters. Dying (or giving up) is required for you to build your character more and to reveal more of the story, and is actually a welcome break between bouts of nonstop fighting. _childDocuments_.review: Overall score: Bad roguelite, pretty good combat, good novel.I'm recommending against it because I came into this wanting a roguelite and was pretty disappointed to find how shallow that aspect of the game was.You will see very close to everything this game has to offer in the first 10-15 runs, and everything beyond that is just grinding for snippets of lore, or you electing to add challenges to the run.------------------Coming out of the gate, combat is fast and fluid, easily chaining or varying types of attacks being used amid dashing around the arenas at a lightning fast pace.Early combat is an exciting flurry of attacking and dodging.  Learning the arenas and abusing the terrain to your advantage.There's a few progression systems in place to slowly advance the strength of the character, however some of those systems accentuate the problems I see in this game.  Namely the lack of gameplay depth.There's a 'final boss' who will be the final boss for the entire game.  Once you've beat him a few times, the game doesn't really change.Sure, there's still weapon upgrades.  And there's a system in place to let you add various challenges to your run, but at the end of the run, you won't have seen anything new, mechanically. ------------------I'd contrast this to other roguelite games like Binding of Isaac.  Granted Isaac has more progression, but if we pretend that's not the case and just examine the core elements of individual runs themselves, BoI has a metric ton of items that will change the way that every run feels based what items you happen to find.Hades doesn't have that.There are a handful of upgrades and much smaller handful of interactions that can occur between those upgrade, of which you can realistically expect to see 0-2 of per run.That,  moreso than anything else, gives the game an incredibly flat feeling and if you're playing the game for mechanics, you'll quickly start asking yourself whether you're going to see anything new (you won't).------------------That brings us to lore.  No spoilers, but lore seems to be the real main draw of the game, it's the only thing that advances as you repeatedly pummel the final boss.  And there's tons of lines of dialogue for every character throughout the game.  I can comfortably state there's more dialogue than exists in any other game of this length.  You're not likely to see a character repeat a line of dialogue.So if you want a fun high-speed game with short runs and a metric ton of lore, then this is the game for you.However, if you want a deeply mechanical roguelite game that can keep surprising you with new fun combinations of abilities and effects that you can experiment with and perfect through many runs, this isn't going to scratch that itch.

_childDocuments_.review: style, present in previous releases like  and , shines brightly in , too. A key part of that style is a rich plot with well-written, well-realized, well-acted characters. Impressively, the game’s identity manages to stand out despite being rooted in the extremely familiar world of Greek mythology.You play as Zagreus, hunky prince of the underworld and sulking son of Lord Hades himself. Each run represents an attempt to escape from the underworld to the mortal world on the surface, away from your wrathful father and back towards your unknown mother. Along the way you encounter your highfalutin Greek god relatives, from Artemis to Zeus, eager to help you come home to Olympus. Each death sends you back beneath Tartarus to the bloody pool in the House of Hades, where you interact with fellow dark residents to further the plot or just pet your three-headed dog Cerberus. structures its entire plot around the fact that you’ll die and play again many times. Even after you beat the game once you won’t entirely know what’s going on. To experience this story, you need to do a lot of fighting. Fortunately, ’ combat matches its narrative when it comes to gripping you and never letting go. masterfully nails its minute-to-minute mechanics alongside the larger character and story progression. - Gorgeous art and lush music- Rich characters and emotional storytelling- Great voice acting- The story and characters are fascinating- Addictive weapon and ability combinations- Roguelite structure is inherently repetitiveDISASTER | BAD | MEDIOCRE | OKAY | GOOD | GREAT | AMAZING |

_childDocuments_.review: The problem with a lot of run-based games in a similar vein to Hades is that you always end up with a few runs where nothing much happens, or you unlock some currency to spend on permanent unlocks and that's it.With Hades, every death means you'll have those currencies, but you'll also be able to advance dialogue and plot with the various characters. _childDocuments_.review: The Narrative and the Core Gameplay are pretty good, i will any day shower Supergiant with praise with the way they present, develop and polish the characters but as a heavy roguelite lover i have some issues with the game. While i refunded the game on steam, i later got it for switch and finished it way more than a couple of times, and that is where the problems started to be noticed.As you progress and clear the game, it starts to ask you to do it again and again like a  would, but its pretty clear that Supergiant had some struggles in the way to incorporate this elements to it, because, while the game is asking you to do it again and again, its not rewarding you for doing it, the only new things it shows to you are dialog. Nothing changes on the way you play the run, sure, you can add challenges with the pact of punishment, but i rather find it more as an escape goat to not balance the dungeon and give it more variety, something the genre is known for.And thats the main problem with it: You break the game with a couple of builds and every build become the same, you dont encounter different enemies, you dont encounter different allies, you dont encounter different powers.Your 1st run and your 100th run will always feel similar because there is no variety to it. you can only do so much, and while the game prouds itself in the incredible script it has i just wish they would had done the same with the variety of gameplay.I really do hope they make a DLC, an expansion or something, because it become one of my favorite action/hack & slash indies, but the way it presented itself as a roguelite felt lacking. _childDocuments_.review: Hades is not a bad game, but your enjoyment of it may well ultimately depend on your preferences concerning playing additional runs through roguelites after a victorious run. Sometimes I enjoy it, and sometimes I don't. With Hades, the game was fairly entertaining, but I actually enjoyed other roguelites more, and continued doing runs through them even after a successful run. With Hades, however, I was pretty bored with the game by the time I finished a single run, and don't have fond memories of it, even now, months after having stopped playing it.Given the game's character and narrative qualities, speaking to the characters in the game and seeing what changes/happens with characters as I played was interesting to me. However, I was a bit perplexed when I finally completed a single run after dozens of hours of trying, only to learn that I had to complete at least NINE more successful runs to get the game's true ending. At that point, I didn't even want to bother with one more successful run. I played a bit more after that, though not very seriously, just getting a few gems and things to unlock some stuff in the lair, before ultimately admitting my boredom and disinterest in the game, finding the "buy-in" of nine more successful runs to get the true ending too steep of a price in time and frustration for me to pay.I don't hate Hades, but it's one of my least favorite roguelites I've ever played. I found Slay the Spire, FTL, Neon Chrome, and various other roguelites far more rewarding and enjoyable for the time investment when compared to Hades, but if you're unemployed, and/or if you don't really play a large number of games, then that might not be an issue for you. =)

_childDocuments_.review: Hades has a lot going for it. It is basically Diablo mashed with Dead Cells and given both a Greek pastiche and a much stronger story. The story is wonderfully voice acted, even though a number of pronunciations are off, which comes across as jarring. Nonetheless the story is the highlight, the driving force behind the game. It keeps you wanting to play. That is, until you reach the end. As with Dead Cells before it, the end isn't actually the end, you need to go back and repeat the whole game over again and again and again. There are only four levels and they don't actually vary that much except in terms of the rewards you gain along the way, said reward will make or break your play through. This makes the game just a long, interminable grind, and this is why I cannot recommend Hades - minimal effort crafting a variety of levels and encounters coupled with grind/busywork just to experience the story. That feels like lazy design and a slap in the face by a studio known for crafting compelling narratives.Look, the game isn't horrible. It has good music. The stylized graphics are spectacular, and the action can be delightfully frenetic; though, this can lead to very Diablo like situations of "where's my cursor?!" Even though there is a high contrast option for the cursor to help you find it, its not enough; though, I've yet to see an isometric game that has fixed this issue. However, everything it has going for it cannot outweigh the grind that it foists upon the player.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Hades is unmistakably a Supergiant game, and their finest one at that. Hades represents a culmination of all the things that made their previous games so enjoyable, but also adds a sprinkling of additional goodness on top.You'll play as Prince Zagreus, son of Hades. as he battles his way through several layers of Hell to reach the surface. Along the way you'll ally yourself with both the gods of Hell and Olympus, slowly expanding your repertoire in hopes of reaching the end.Supergiant's trademark art and musical style truly enhance the experience. As is customary with Supergiant, their game is filled to the brim with beautifully drawn characters, from your enemies to your allies. However, I've always thought the most memorable parts of Supergiant games were the music, and Hades is no slouch. Each area and boss battle is heightened by Darren Korb's compositions. Unfortunately, the music will often take a backseat to the action onscreen. This, however, is a testament to the quality of the gameplay, rather than the quality of the music. Finally, the game has an insane amount of voice acting, and somehow it's all good. Darren Korb as Zagreus brings a lot of life into our undying protagonist, and after all these hours I haven't gotten sick of his voice, or anyone else's for that matter.Hades' gameplay loop is what keeps you coming back. Hades' greatest strengths are its simple but enjoyable combat and the extreme amount of freedom of choice. Bastion's isometric combat translates well to Hades' rogue-like setting, with only a little more added complexity, such as dash attacks and casting. They've essentially just added sprinkles on a formula that already worked. Choice has also been a strong suit for Supergiant, as they've included very precise ways to change your loadout and make their games more difficult in the ways you want to in their previous games, such as the Shrines in Bastion or the Constellations in Pyre. They've done so as well in Hades by not only providing you with an array of starting weapons and trinkets, but also with the boon system and the heat system. This has allowed Supergiant to slide naturally into making a rogue-like, as if it has all led to this.Hades has set a high bar for rogue-likes, for indie games, and for Supergiant. If their next game is as good as Hades, or even better, it would certainly surprise me.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly addicting, I haven't had this much fun with a combat system in years. Dead Cells but 3D seems to be a common comparison, but even Dead Cells feels sluggish compared to Hades, every move is can be pixel perfect, every attack timed and positioned perfectly, controls are tight and if you get hurt, you've only yourself to blame. _childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this game is a 10/10. It's a rogue-lite set in Ancient Greek times where you take the role of Zagreus, Hades' son, to attempt to escape from the Underworld. You have access to a variety of weapons, including a spear, a shield, and a sword. When you're not running through the Underworld fighting evil monsters, you will be talking to characters in the hub world and developing relationships with them. This is a nice way to break up the pace and so you won't be too frustrated with dying often. I haven't gotten too far in this game, but so far I'm really surprised by the number of features you have access to throughout the game. TL;DR: I highly recommend this game. Play it.

_childDocuments_.review: Hades is the first Roguelike game that I have ever played and the first thing that struck me when starting this game is how beautiful the art style is. _childDocuments_.review: *The* best roguelike I've ever played. It balances plot progression, gameplay challenge and novelty perfectly. By using enormous amounts of bite-sized pieces of dialogue on every single interaction and encounter, it keeps you engaged with the story and characters without having to sit through lengthy exposition dumps *and* doesn't let the gameplay turn into a mindless grind.The gameplay itself is also very enjoyable, with multiple weapons that can take on different aspects, different upgrades to every ability you have and additional difficulty you can take on if you feel like you're getting too good.The only criticism I have is that sometimes it gets a little too button-mashy due to the many effects on-screen that make it hard to see what's going on and force you to spam dash-attacks.All in all, it's an incredible game with an engaging story, likeable characters, fun gameplay and plenty of replay value. _childDocuments_.review: Ok, so. Where to begin. First, if you enjoy good games, you'll enjoy this. Assuming you can play-of course, which i understand is something of a problem for some people...But they also include a god mode, for a more story based experience. Or mutable hard modes, so you can customize how you want the game to be harder, instead of just a stock "hard mode"I guess we began there, so lets move to the gameplay. it takes elements from all of supergiants previous titles and refines them into a stained glass masterpiece of combat, choice, pace, and story. there are six weapons, and each of those weapons has up to 4 different forms it can eventually take, which change how it looks but more importantly how you fight with it. You start with a sword. relatively simple attack combo, special is an aoe slam. one form encourages combos-for a short time after a special move, you have a chance to crit with normal attacks. Another has your special dislodge your cast-which is a mutable ability you start with that, mostly, will implant itself in an enemy until it dies (or a longish timer). So you could cast-special-cast-special. This is just one weapon of 6, and does not take into account how Godly Boons could effect things. You want your cast to be a chain lightning ball? Or a frost laser? You want your attack to shoot out a magic seeking arrow each time you hit? You want your special to give enemies a debuff that causes them to take damage after a few seconds? or make them do less damage *and* fight for you for a bit? You want your dash to reflect projectiles back at enemies? We got that and more. Story is more difficult for me to get into. It's revealed as you go, and not in a...it would be easy for it to arbitrarily lock things off at points, and go "UGH I COULD SAY MORE BUT I WONT", but it all flows delightfully, as i win...or when i dont. The characters remember what i've done and who i've done it with, within reason. Athena remembers when I've won with her, and Ares remembers when I didn't. Within reason, but its GOOD.  It's hard to describe without spoiling, but suffice it to say if you've played a supergiant game before you're getting that and more besides. Characters! Each and every character is wonderful and I can't say too much here without spoiling the surprises you should find on your own. But you can pet Cerbie. It's delightful. They look good, sound good, act good, the writing, its all so delightful. Finally, the music, as ever, is friggin amazing. I don't possess the skills or words to describe it, but as before, it all just fits and flows and is so damn good. This is probably too long of a review, but I have just nothing but praise for Hades and for Supergiant and for each and every person working there.

_childDocuments_.review: Super Giant games always have incredible artistry. The visuals are fantastic, the writing is fantastic, the score is fantastic, the voice acting is fantastic. Super Giant games have always been ok in the gameplay department. Bastion was simple but effective, Transistor was very easily broken, Pyre was a Visual Novel with occasion bouts of simple gameplay. The problem with Hades is that it leans into the gameplay, hard, and has some of the worst gameplay Super Giant has created thus far. Retreading the same few areas over and over quickly becomes a chore, after two run the first two levels become a solved game and Hades forces you to replay them over and over to get new content. Weapon balancing is all over the place with some being completely worthless and others allowing you to effortlessly walk through the game with 0 damage. Bosses are pose 0 threat, have inflated health pools, and must be fought over and over again. When an enemy is between you and a wall it's a guaranteed kill, but the game still makes you mash attack 10 times before they die. By the end you're picking buffs not based on fun builds or becoming more powerful but more for what will waste the least amount of your time. This game has incredible talent behind it, but unlike other Super Giant games it does not respect your time. The game is a gorgeous slog, and without some major reworking I could not possibly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot get over how much I love this game. + Excellence and care were poured into every nook and cranny from graphics, menus, sound effects, voice overs, writing, characterization. The list goes on. For characterization, as an example, Zeus talks like the type of rich and successful uncle who I would visit and for four hours straight, all he'll be talking about is himself. It sounds right and it's consistent.+ I have "rougelite" filtered out of my steam store because I don't like repetition. But Supergiant made Hades different in that every run is the same but they put in enough "newness" to make it not feel repetitive. Bite-sized servings of story, lore, added gameplay mechanics are served through different runs making me want to know what's next.+ The combat feels great and every weapon feels like a new game in itself. I would put here my favorite but it changes every few runs. A few weeks ago it was the shield. A few days ago it was the sword. The gun I once absolutely hated and was my longest run. I was convinced it was the worst weapon selection. Then I loved it and it was my fastest run by far then hated it again. Same with the fists. Who knows what I'll like and hate next?+ Even if I lose on a run, I never feel angry or frustrated in the same way that I did in Sekiro cause that game welcomed me by stomping on my face repeatedly... which I loved in a troubled love and hate abusive relationship way. The setting of Hades doesn't take itself too seriously and even losing a run feels like I'm moving forward. I'd say it's a difficult yet chill game if that even makes sense.+ In Supergiant we trust. Loved Bastion and Transistor. I didn't like Pyre but I can't deny how polished it is. Please continue making excellent games. Please don't sell to Ubisoft/ Bethesda/ Microsoft/ EA etc. Please. ----- As a parent, the only game time I have is after the kids are asleep. For the last two weeks and counting, I've been operating on 3-4 hours of sleep a day. It's probably not sustainable and I'll address it just after this other one more last really final final run.- As I mentioned above, while some people like rougelites, I really don't so Hades is an exception. There's a point though on it's veeeeeeerrrrryy long end game content that I felt like I was scraping the bottom of the barrel for slithers of story content. It made me feel frustrated and impatient as these story beats are usually after every 30-50 minute run (plus the non timed parts). My love for this game was turning into irritation so before my love for it dissolved completely, I opted to uninstall and decided that at that point 66+ hours in, I was completely, finally, and really done.

_childDocuments_.review: Supergiant Games have a certain artsy feel to them. Incredible production values as well as very particular art direction. Bastion and Transistor are mostly beloved for their narration, visuals, music... What about gameplay? I always thought the fell a little flat. Hades... doesn't fall flat. Hades soars through the sky, like Daedalus escaping the Labyrinth of Crete. The gameplay is very finely crafted. There's a lot of fun stuff, many equally valid build options, different weapons which all play and feel unique - and to make things better, the game actually switches things around as you go as to keep things fresh, so you can't even be fully sure of how exactly the run will go. I'll leave it at that, the surprises are one of the more lovable parts of the game. Let's just say the game gives you plenty of incentives to splice things up a bit - and you'll gladly accept them, like Theseus accepted Ariadne's thread.If you watch the trailer, you'll notice the gameplay is incredibly fast-paced. Too fast you might think. But no, the actual game is EVEN FASTER - and it somehow manages to be that fast without the feeling of loss of control. You're always aware of what's going on, your actions calculated and precise, cutting through the underworld like Achilles at the battle of Troy... once you understand the workings of things, which I admit, takes some time. It's easy enough to pick up, though, so don't worry about that. It will all come naturally.So the gameplay is great, amazing even. As a roguelike + roguelite affectionado, I'll say it's up there with Dead Cells, maybe even better. But it somehow manages to spice things up even more with its incredibly charming world and characters. I mean, it's Supergiant Games' take on the greek myths, what did you expect?You play as Zagreus, a son of Hades, who wants to leave the underworld - and dies over and over trying. After every run, you get to talk to the inhabitants of the House of Hades - your fantasticly disfunctional family and their entourage - who comment on your exploits. You banter with beaten bosses, old teachers, mythological characters, all with wonderful characterisation. Same of course goes for the Pantheon of greek gods. If you thought Disney's Hercules did that well, check this out. It's a lot less silly while still being charming and humorous. Poseidon as the cheeky uncle is probably my favourite.It's easy to get lost in this exhilarating adventure, with every victory granting great satisfaction. If nothing else, grab this over the holiday season, and enter the underworld like Orpheus once did! (ok, not quite, that story went TOTALLY different)TL:DR: Incredible gameplay, amazing world. P.S. Aphrodyte is hot and Theseus makes me want to punch his face.

_childDocuments_.review: “Hades”,  single-player, character-focused family drama. Like many great stories, its premise is simple. You are Zagreus, prince of the underworld, and for reasons yet to be discovered, he wants to leave his literal hell of a home. Hades, the temperamental father of “Zag,” is determined to impede his son’s escape by setting up a series of security checkpoints, that being said It's the first time I have ever played rogue-like genre, which means the player is expect to die over and over again, But it’s in death that the game’s narrative begins to sing.This game has found the secret to (almost) eternal storytelling: a play loop that repeats itself, but dialogue that doesn’t. Interesting things happen all the time, in conversations and chance encounters as well as in battles, and no matter how long I spend with Hades I feel like I am only just getting acquainted with it.The best part about the game is music, When I first met Eurydice, I genuinely just stood there listening to her sing for a very long while. It's beautiful, nostalgic and sad. This game is so good, the NPC really feel like people and I care about them. _childDocuments_.review: Regardless of whichever term you use to define Hades, whether that be roguelite or roguelike, Hades' metaprogression design undermines the roguelike experience I have come to enjoy and appreciate. For this reason, I cannot recommend Hades for the roguelike it claims to be because there are so many great rogue-esk games out there. If you're looking for an RPG with roguelike features, then look no further, but if you're expecting to scratch that pure, grindy, random-as-all-hell roguelike itch, remember... you've been warned.Hades' action combat may in fact be the best part of the game, which is great considering the majority of the game is spent slaying the creatures of the underworld. Attacks chain together well and induce a flow state pretty easily. Quality action combat, to me, is all about . Hades accomplishes these two aspects well. It is a game that expects you to play fast, and the infernal arms (weapons) bring a modest level of depth to the game's combat.However, boss variety is lackluster at best. This is evident when the first two zones attempt to bring variety by  modifying the bosses of those zones. All together there's only a handful of big boss fights in the game, and only the late stage fights bring a real sense of challenge to a run. If you're dying to Bone Hydra in the late game, I'm guessing you've fallen asleep at the wheel and should probably go to bed.Hades takes metaprogression, the overarching progression system of roguelites, and cranks it up 1000%. Character stats can be purchased through an in-game currency system... stats like extra lives, bonus damage, and bonus health upon entering each room. These are massive power shifts that make the game drastically easier as a player progresses. This shifts the goal posts. Suddenly, Hades went from a game about escaping the underworld to a game about collecting the resources to escape the underworld at a later point in time.The progression in Hades actually detracts from the random nature of roguelikes that I love. There's hardly a difference between a good run and a bad run in Hades when Zagreus is fully upgraded... which feels strange coming from a genre that I've come to associate with replayability. In most games, RNG feels awful. In roguelikes, RNG unleashes the inner-gambler in me who can set the world on fire with a god-run. In Hades, maybe I raise the base damage of my already insane loadout by 8%. Sick. This is the antithesis of the genre no matter which side of the fence you put Hades on, roguelike or roguelite.Hades has brought a level of aesthetic design to roguelikes never really seen before. Each character of Greek mythology is brought to life by  of quality, voice-acted lines. Also, the underworld has probably never been depicted in a game with such an artistic eye, but...Does any of this make Hades a better game  Not really. (In fact, I found myself skipping dialogue regularly to get back into the fight). Hades is by all means a Supergiant game with all the bells and whistles that come with a Supergiant game, but at the end of the day, art & voice-acting play such a small role in defining the quality of a game & especially a roguelike. There's a reason roguelikes like Dungeon Crawl Stone Soup & ADOM are still adored & played to this day. Spoiler: it's not because they're the prettiest games on the block.While I can appreciate the artistry in the comic-book-like graphics of the characters and zones, they don't solve the systemic issues I have with Hades.So much of the depth and complexity that comes from a run is removed from Hades and stuck into an overarching progression system. Character stat bonuses, weapon variety, and zone permutation upgrades all happen outside the scope of a run. For this reason runs become easier & easier as you progress in a way that detracts from a run's possible outcomes. The distance between god-runs and bad-runs is shortened, making for the majority of the runs to just feel OK. Hades may be a great mythological RPG, but it is far from a great roguelike.
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: Supergiant knocked it out of the park with this one. The combat feels like Bastion and is as good as ever, with a variety of new weapons at your disposal.But what seals the deal is that the world is beautiful and the characters are really interesting - I couldn't wait until the end of each run to build up the house of hades and advance my relationship with other characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely fun & quite fast-paced! Satisfying hack-n-slash action with a lovely range of weapon options. The God Boon system is absolutely amazing, really just makes every run a different challenge. Combine this with the fact that chamber layouts constantly change and surprise encounters are bound to happen, you're forced to think on the fly to formulate a good skill tree every time. Having to think of saving/spending money every run adds a welcomed layer of complexity as well. Seriously, the only reason for you to stop is being titled, it does not get boring at all!!Collection is also a huge aspect of the game. Dozens of collectibles and choices associated with them as you kill your way through the chambers of hell!Medium -> Hard. For the usual avid gamer, the base difficulty offers a fair and fun challenge. I can't speak for those who are very experienced in rogue-like games. However, the devs, being the angels that they are, have added Hell Mode and God Mode. Hell Mode is the mandatory extreme setting for the sadists. God Mode isn't actually what it sounds like. If you find yourself in a pickle, activate God Mode to receive a base 22% damage resistance up as a helping hand. Every time you die and reset an escape, you get +2% for that stat. So your learning curve will be a bit smoother as you go along! You can switch off God Mode any time you please. Heavens, if you're me and you're super super passionate about Greek mythology then finding this game would be like receiving a personal hand-written love letter that was sent to your bedroom window by a magical bird. I'm incredibly in love with all the characters in the game and how they're written with such distinct personalities!!! Supergiant's interpretation of Greek gods and monsters is just downright lovely. It's also absolutely brilliant how the interactions and dialogue and story moments flow harmoniously with your dungeon runs, decisions and deaths/resets. I think almost every single thing is voice-acted. It's insane. Every character just feels alive. You have so much dialogue to unlock, and you've got a friendship + gifting system to warm up to your favourite boys and girls. You can romance certain characters:  So if you've ever wanted to date a Greek deity then now's your time!Being a fan of Greek mythology definitely makes this game 100% better, but even if you're not, let's admit one thing: Who doesn't want to roleplay as the angry teenage son of the King of Hell, God of the Dead Hades? You're literally infernal royalty. With cool powers and weapons. And you rock. Familial drama? Teenage angst? Hormones? Hubris? Yes, please. Beautiful graphics. Not everyone will like the art style, but I suppose you can already see this for yourself! Controls are intuitive and responsive. Very simple buttons on KB + M!Buy it! Good time guaranteed. If I haven't sold you by now then I'll just remind you that you can pet Cerberus almost any time you see him. Yes. Your dog is the three-headed hound that guards the gates of Hell. And he's the best boi.
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: HADES is an absolute masterpiece from SUPERGIANT Games. The developers have taken the roguelite genre to it's finest point. Everything from the art style, gameplay, and story is flawlessly executed to hand you the most satisfying experience possible for your money. I've played through quite a few roguelite games and have been left wanting more from them. Not so with this title. HADES offers a steady progression system that keeps you coming back for your next unlock or story moment consistently as you play.A huge variety of weapons, boons, keepsakes, enemies, and bosses makes sure that no two runs are the same.10/10 would ESCAPE again.
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 if you are a fan of roguelikes this is A MUST HAVE!! Takes the best aspects from every roguelike available right now- room to room decision making from slay the spire- better permanent progression than rogue legacy- bullet hell style combat from binding of isaac.  This game has it all.  Extremely in depth and extensive progression.  Great build diversity with the weapon and perk system. Every one of the 6 weapons plays extremely differently.  Combat would be generic if it was not for the "Boon" mechanic which drastically changes everything from the way that your character dodges to the way that they attack or cast spells. Incredibly satisfying story- and every last character has an incredible amount of charm and are extremely memorable.  Couple this with the games top end voice acting and dialogue and you're left with a phenomenal story telling experience.  I cannot exaggerate how ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ perfect this game is.  Just get it.

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10, absolutely love this game! I'm a big Greek mythology buff myself so i love when i can point out or recognize certain things within the plot. _childDocuments_.review: I can't say much that hasn't already been said better by other people. However, I can say that despite having a 14+ year stint on Steam and hundreds of games owned (with combined thousands of hours played), Hades is the first game that I have EVER 100%'d on the platform. _childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: Hades is a great game, the difficulty is steep at first, but after multiple runs it never gets old, there's so much variety available, and along with the great story and excellent soundtrack, this is another lovingly-crafted game from SuperGiant which I am happy to put more hours into.Worth noting: end game doesn't begin until you've beaten the final boss 10 times, so there's no shame in turning on Godmode if you want to keep going.
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: Played this for over 50 hours on the Epic store, one day couldn't log in to the launcher and so decided to just buy it on steam since I was considering starting fresh anyway. And wouldn't you know it, Supergiant are so cool that they just imported my save here!Solid gameplay with solid rogue-lite progression. Though this game is the first actual story rogue-lite out there. Due to this it does kind of force the story on you, even though you can skip it dialogues if you hate them that much, but the story progress with each run is exceptional, with the characters being fun and interactions very well thought out. The first 40 or so hours as the game kept developing I didn't hear a single line repeated (except for the generic combat "Got it." shoutouts I guess).Pair all of the above with Supergiant's signature Soundtrack and art and you have an excellent rogue-lite worth sinking your teeth into
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to say that a game is perfect, but Supergiant Games have come very close with this one.Combat is incredibly fun and just about never gets boring or dull, the amount of different builds that you can do is astonishing, and the rogue-lite nature of it takes the sting out of failure.After finishing the main story, pushing "Heat" is incredibly fun and really changes things up, although you can push Heat before finishing the main story, if you would like. "Heat" levels are basically modifiers that you put on your next run which make it more difficult and change things up, keeping it fresh and adding loads of re-playablility to an already very re-playable game.Story, characters, and voice-acting are all stellar as well.Highly recommended and worth full price.Steam Awards Game of the Year IMO for sure!
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: GOTY.So here's the thing, if you're new to rogue likes you might get a little frustrated, but unlike most rogue likes the story here is amazing. After you "beat the game" once, there's story related reasons to keep going. You're done, but you're not done.Then you beat it a few more times... You think you're done, but you're not. There's still more reason to come back and get the true ending.All throughout this you're getting stronger, better, and getting a deeper understanding on how to build each run.If you're struggling, there's a god mode available. Every time you die your resistance to damage is increased. You can turn this on and off whenever you like and it does not effect the story, progression, or achievements. The graphics are great, the combat is clean and crisp, everything about this game is damn near perfect. Sorry dead cells, Hades is here.
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome improvement and refinement to the rogue-like genre! So much persistent stuff is in this game that the repetition doesn't feel like a grind (yet). I just hope this means EarlyAccess means they'll add more gameplay to it so I can keep playing this longer!
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing Supergiant games for years, ever since Bastion. I certainly liked Pyre and Transistor, but Hades is the first game that made me remember the magic I felt with Bastion--and the first one that I think betters it, in every conceivable way. From graphical fidelity, to masterful storytelling, great combat design, incredible option select and choice, and the ability to keep you coming back no matter what for new experiences, new high scores, and the best roguelike I've literally ever played (and I've played a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of roguelikes), Hades is easily 2020's game of the year, and in my opinion, one of the better games of all time.
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece, SuperGiant Games at it's finest, don't let the early access fool you, the game has more content than some of the fully released games in steam, you'll have hours and hours of getting to know the characters, the enemies and all of the underworld, so go ahead, treat yourself and buy one of the best games in the market. (Since this review the game has left early access and has added a lot more content, everything I've said stands true still.)
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: Well, this is definitely biggest one Supergiant Games made so far. Compared to previous titales it has greatest replayability value with always randomized levels, enemies and rewards. It feels a bit like Dead Cells or other roguelike with having to start from the beginning after you die, but death is not the end here. Even if you are killed by some wretch in the first room after leaving the house of Hades, it would move the plot when you come anew from the pool of Styx. As with each time you visit your home characters present there may change I even went ahead and killed myself few times to get ones I had business with to appear. Combat has its roots in Bastion but with greater divestity thanks to different aspects of weapons and varied set of gods boons you collect on your way. Sadly there is lower number of soundrtracks compared to previous Pyre. They are longer though and while mostly did not impress in the beginning, grew on me after so many runs through the underworld levels. But music is still great and did not drop from the level of past games. Darren Korb and Ashley Barrett have their own characters, like in Pyre, and as always delivers. There was also highly surprising track for final boss battle under extreme conditions that would remind you of certain fighting games and with a good reason ^^[SPOILERS PROBABILITY]While other Supergiant titles felt like concentrated story games, this one has its minced in-between and during your escape attempts through underworld. It is not a bad thing, as plot quality is probably about the same, which was always a strong part of this developer products. But generally speaking, while storytelling and how it goes is good, general theme a bit lacking, as strictly speaking it was just rebellious son trying to get out of home and away from his fater, later to get out and find mother and later to get his family together. Yes, it is too simplified and there is much more to it, but still... feels a bit less. It is also a first "good" world events took place in compared to prevous games - there is no world destruction, no city desctruction, no dark traditions of banishing people to desolate lands and make them fight to prove worth and get back. Only few words were said about wars in world above among mortals, that increase souls flow to underworld. But that's it, despite being in underworld, it is not depressing and there is very happy ending even.
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games of 2020. It puts an interesting spin on the roguelike genre, using the repeating iterative nature to tell a larger overarching story. There are so many different weapon and boon combinations that make each run feel unique. The writing is stellar and generates so much original dialogue, even after a hundred runs.
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the ultimate form of art! I'm not even over-exaggerating. I hesitated to buy this game because I was not a big fan of roguelike games, but this, this game is so much different than "usual" rogelike games. You actually feel the progression of everything, and not just hit harder or have more health. The gameplay is smooth as butter, music is top-notch, visual is unbeatable. And the story, I thought it would be boring because it's a roguelike game, but oh boy was I wrong. The story is amazing!! _childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: I am a big fan of Supergiant games and got sad when it is first released on EPIC. This month after it got released on Steam i am super happy to have bought this game. The OSTs are super fire! The animations and the hand drawn artworks combined with excellent voice acting really makes me love this game more and more. I love how it challenges players to come back again each time you die on the Hades and grind your way again to make yourself stronger. Being stronger and learning from your mistakes is the key. You select a specific door you want to enter and then think what is the right path for you. Hades is a combination of action fun and great decision making on how you spend your points and which door to enter every time. It's cool soundtrack will surely pump you up. Excellent game again by the group of Supergiant! Whether you are a new fan or long time fan, you must surely give this one a try!
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: 66 hours in Early Access play and I'm still not even close to bored. The devs really said it best when they say that Hades is already a big, feature-rich game, and I can't wait to see the full release version in all its glory. Am I afraid that I'll lose all sense of time and play it another 60 hours without feeling like I've made the slightest dent in the replayability? Sure. Do I care? Not really. _childDocuments_.review: This is a good game until the random difficulty spikes, and I don't mean the ones that you choose. The game seems to figure out you are running a powerful set of boons and equipment and then just punishes you and takes a lot of the fun out of the game. The progression is very slow. If you like real rogue likes I don't recommend this game as it is the most frustrating thing you can possibly play. Other rogue likes you feel like you build your character to the point you can beat the game but this is counters most of what you pick up along the way. I've played it a fair amount because when you have a good run it is very rewarding but then it crushes you. Very frustrating. Could have been a great game but nothing is more frustrating than getting dominated while on the easiest setting after 37 run throughs.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most complete games out there. Everything is very well done. Writing is good, voice acting is great (Hades especially), good level design, fast-paced combat, beautiful animations, many different playstyles with different weapons and their aspects, interesting enough story, dialogues never get repetitive even after ~70+ runs., which is actually insane! Every run you work towards something, that's the main hook of this game.Great game to waste 100h of your time.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the clear winner of game of the year.Every thing in this game is so fleshed out and well put together.You can tell they really cared about this game.It may appear to be a simple hack and slash rogue like, but its so much more.Before you start a run you pick your weapon, which has 2 attack modes.You also have blood diamonds (spells) and casts (spells that recharge during battle and are often OP)While playing you get boons(Skills) from certain gods. you decide what elements you want to put on you gear while making your run.I've played for 40 hours now and i still havent gotten out lolHades is the worst dad everBut excellent game 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: There are many video games that are not good. This is a good video game. As someone who dislikes roguelikes on principle, this is one of the only good ones. It makes you want to keep playing through drips of lore and through constant gameplay advances even when you lose. The writing is phenomenal, the action is fun and responsive, the RNG doesn't destroy your runs unless you're seeking something very particular (like trying to unlock certain end-game weapon stuff), and you are incentivized to make the game harder for yourself so that it never becomes a boring chore to slog through regular mobs. The more I play, the more I feel the love and passion that Supergiant put into this, and it brings me endless joy to pick up on both subtle design aspects (the way that somehow I always manage to know where Zagreus is even if I don't see him or I'm not even looking at him continues to astound me) and the tiny snippets of writing that they clearly had a lot of fun scribbling in. This is a good video game. You should give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I've ever played and easily the best rogue-like along with Risk of rain 2No game has handled player death betterIn runs you are not only thinking bout how far you'll go but how much resources you will take to make you permanently stronger for your next runsPlus it's also a neat Dating Sim with beautifully voice acted characters

_childDocuments_.review: This game is truly phenomenal.  Art & Style: Excellentthe Art style is really consistent, and striking, and despite being a little dark.  Doesn't feel depressing or sad.in terms of art and style though.  The best part is the Voice acting,  There must be at least 300 different lines from all of the different characters, and the Characters are all wonderful, and really fun to experience.The characters are mostly Greek gods, but there are some other characters from greek lore, like a medusa and Achilles.Gameplay: ExcellentThe controls are tight, fluid, and feel good, both with controller and with keyboard mouse.It is my favorite rogue-like action hack and slash game to date, and sets a high bar
_childDocuments_.name: Hades

_childDocuments_.review: Is it even possible to go wrong while choosing Supergiant Games? Well... i think notThis is yet another example of a great game. _childDocuments_.review: One of the best, if not the best games officially released in 2020. The concept, art style, gameplay, and music immediately caught my attention, but the more I played, the more I found myself drawn to Zag and his interactions with the various god or inhabitants of the underworld. The writing and voice acting is exceptional, managing to convey the personality of each character clearly and in an interesting way which makes you want to go for just one more run to unlock new dialogue options. As I'm nearing my 200th hour since I started playing at release, I can safely say this is one of the best games I've ever played and has easily made its way into my list of timeless favourites.Supergiant has done an amazing job with this game and I cant recommend it enough if you have an interest in Greek mythology or rogue-likes.

_childDocuments_.review: I get killed.Return back to the beginning, only to get to know the characters.Then the addiction of trying to escape again kicks in....And it gets late....Just going to try one more time.I also need items!Lovely art! All the characters looks dynamic and have good designs that fits them. Like how some random colour dots of green and purple makes everything so vibriant. The areas looks cool, and stylish. Fits the games gener and its story. Pleasing to look at. But I hate lava. :S Chatchy music, it gets stuck in your head. _childDocuments_.review: Put simply, Hades is a very fast-paced rogue-like based on Greek mythology. THE PROS+ Great artwork and soundtrack (just like any other Supergiant game)+ Gameplay is incredible, it never gets tiring slaughtering Hades' minions while you battle out of hell+ The controls are really responsive, you definitely feel like a Greek hero (which you actually are in this game)+ A decent enough representation of the Greek mythology. If you've read any myths, you'll feel right at homeTHE CONS- Not all characters have enough unique dialogue for your repeated escape attempts. E.g., Achilles always has something new to say while Ms. Dusa runs out of lines very quickly- Sometimes the RNG can screw you over pretty hard. Yeah, it's fun to experiment with builds on the fly but sometimes you just want to min-max- There are some utterly useless boons and build options- In contrast, some boons and build options are utterly game-breaking (e.g., literally any boon with health regen)Overall, Hades is highly recommended, just make sure to not get addicted too much

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Supergiant games or roguelikes, go ahead and buy this game. You won't be disappointed.Releasing the 1.0 Update, porting it to the Switch while also reworking the engine and STILL keeping the quality so damn high during a pandemic is just nuts. Hades might be one of the few examples of an Early Access title done right. The amount of community feedback taken, the sheer number of updates and the size of content added in is astounding. And everything has such exquisite polish to it. Onwards to the game. Very rarely do we see a roguelike game with such a heavy emphasis on the story but Hades manages to do it right. The interwoven gameplay and story makes dying in this game something that I've looked forward to rather than dread because I know I'll get to learn so much more about the world and the story while also getting stronger. The combat is very varied with every run offering so many unique powers, the art is breathtakingly gorgeous and the music is Darren Korb at his best. This might just be the best Supergiant game so far. P.S: I highly recommend the Noclip documentary series on this game to see how much love, care and effort went into making this masterpiece.TL;DR: 10/10 game, allows you to pet CerberusEDIT: 20 hours on the PC version and I'm still having an absolute blast.

_childDocuments_.review: What an amazing and unique game, this is the best indie game I have ever played since Hollow Knight. Supergiant games have outdone themselves and completely blown me away with HADES: Beautiful visuals, stellar soundtrack, fast paced, varied, challenging and fun gameplay, very tight controls, next to no bugs, huge amount of content and a vast post-game and on top of all of that great voice acting, likeable charatcers, good humour and an okay story too (not amazing by any means but still servicable enough). My only actual complaint is the post-game being a bit too grindy, I mean, not only it takes insanely long to upgrade everything and buy all the cosmetics but you even have to struggle to get to the actual, true ending (by struggle I don't mean completing a challenge, no you have to get through unreal amounts of specific dialogues, events and encounters that are either completely based on rng or can be triggered by very specific actions). But the upside is that you get to play and experiment with this game more which is great and it always feels fresh both gameplaywise and by also basically never running out of new dialogues. Oh and even though this game has a ton of cosmetics, none of them require any real world money, no microtransactions, you buy the game you can get everything through good old gameplay. This game is a definite contender for game of the year in my opinion. A must play.

_childDocuments_.review: Unlike rogue-likes where you simply start at the beginning every time you die, Hades advances the plot with literally thousands of marvelously acted lines of dialogue. Even defeating the final boss is not the end, but another step in uncovering a story that brings you back again and again and again.Combat is fluid and frenetic. _childDocuments_.review: Ok, apologies in advance, but soapbox time. This game was robbed at the Game Awards, frankly it could and maybe should have won pretty much every category it was nominated for, but particularly Best Direction. How many other nominees in that list actually direct a team they expect to keep working with, using the very best talent at their disposal to pull together gameplay, design, writing, and music in such a delightful way? A studio that doesn't force its staff to work themselves ragged, or out of their family. But no, the award ended up going to a studio that did just that. What a shame.So, as for the game itself? It's probably one of the best games I've played this year, and my personal GOTY. It's not the game I've played the most, but then I wouldn't call it's genre my favourite. However, when I do play it, I enjoy it for most of the aspects explained in my rant above, and each one on it's own is a reason to pick the game up. The game is a roguelike/roguelite isometric hack-and-slash, I think? Your goal is to escape the Underworld, and it's mostly a story about family, and I'll leave it at that because the game does the reveal better than I would. When you die in your runs, you keep most of what you earn, and use it to improve in your next run, so there's always a constant progression. The game also has a "God Mode" that makes the game progressively easier for those struggling, making it a far more accessible title than similar games in the genre.There are a few aspects I think could be better. Progression relies on spending different resources on different things, but the game is a little stingy when it comes to handing them out, especially resources for more expensive things, but I gather this is partly to incentivise you to mix up your runs. It does, however, make the late game more of a slog than I'd like.Overall, I'd argue this game is a strong contender for GOTY, as well as any other awards that are up for grabs

_childDocuments_.review: Hades became one of my favorite games in a span of just a couple of days. The story is amazing, and the voice acting of this game is on a whole other level compared to similar titles. You relate to each of the characters and therefore emphatize with them and grow attached as you progress with Zagreus, who is by far one of the most charismatic and likeable protagonists I have ever seen.  The game is somewhat difficult, and I would not recommend it to casual players, though God Mode is always available if you want to focus on the story. _childDocuments_.review: Hello! It has been a while since I have posted a review but this one is worth writing about.I've been a fan of Supergiant games from the get-go because they never fail to disappoint. Each game they have come out with has a different gameplay / thus caters to different styles of gamers.  But as far as I have seen, they always deliver a flawless product. A huge fan of "Bastion" and "Transistor" -- "Hades" is amazing.. but again, it depends if this is your type of game.With that said, my comments on Hades:                 -  Story! <3  Based on Greek Mythology. You play one of the sons of Hades (Zagreus) who wants to get out of "Hell".  You defy your father and try to  leave it even if he tells you it is impossible. Along the line of your escape from "Hell" for reasons which I shall not spoil, you get to encounter other Greek mythological Gods and creatures.. who help you along the way or not.. so if you're into the mythology, that is a very big bonus.                  - Game-play! <3  It is rogue-like.  You clear a room of mobs, you go to the next room.  ;)  Along the way, random different Gods and Goddesses give you an upgrade out of 3 choices. The choice you make will customize your gameplay and what you can do throughout that run which makes it a unique experience every time. However, be prepared to die. You *will* "die" over and over and over and get sent back to Hell - But, the kicker is that you can upgrade your skills based on what you have done on each run after you "died".  That idea is philosophical to me - like in life; we make mistakes, but are rewarded by learning from them and come back better / stronger and try again.  Perseverance! ;) ! We can upgrade our character in several ways by unlocking new weapons or changing specific beneficial traits on ourselves or on the weapons over time as we collect gems and so on.       - Personal Experience! <3 * Visuals - It is beautiful - there are so many intricate artistic details that I notice every time. Breathless!* Sounds - The soundtrack by Darren Korb is always impressively done. The soundtrack is worth it.  The voice actors are well-chosen, including Darren Korb himself as the main protagonist's voice (which I can not get enough of, sorry~ just so cool!).* Performance - For my specs, this game runs smoothly in my rig. However, I am not sure but  I personally recommend a Keyboard + Mouse combo because of the accurate aiming which is very important in this game rather than a gamepad - but that is up to the weapon and it is up to you.                  ~~~~All in all: The various weapon choices and weapon upgrades make it so much fun! I went from being frustrated at first from dying to compelled to keep on playing due to how endless and very interesting their upgrading system is.. and now.. I am completely addicted since I've grasped it and feel like a boss!  Haha. There are so many things to unlock and so many combinations that *it always feels fresh*. I highly recommend it.  I truthfully have nothing bad to say about this game and it is a BONUS if you love Greek mythology.It is a masterpiece in my mind - but whether or not it is your thing is up to you!My two cents and I hope it helps! <3

_childDocuments_.review: Supergiant's foray into the world of roguelikes and rogulites is a resounding success. Well balanced, addicting gameplay is coupled with a strong narrative that pushes you to complete runs over and over so you can progress the story further. The weapons are all fun to use and multifaceted each in their own way and combined with the variety of boons provided to you by Zagreus's many Olympian relatives, and the randomized levels in the rogulike aspects of the game's design ensure that every run will feel different. The characters are all well written and interesting and helping them progress in their own stories alongside your own journey is a delight. Hades deserves all the acclaim it gets and so much more and it makes me incredibly excited to see what Supergiant has in store for the future.
