_childDocuments_.review: Fun game but short, and full of questionable moralistic stances.Our Hero puts an end to life as they know it in the most advanced and prosperous city in the world because reasons.  The thinnest and weakest one was that giving people something to strive for sets them against one another.  What in the living f-?  Is this some kind of utopic absurdity where the proposition is that humans are only competitive because of external social constructs?  The Worst Thing (tm) that this must-fall utopia has done is kidnap children and remove their past traumas by replacing traumatic memories with positive ones.  Yes, that's right.  The very same thing that three out of four US adults do with prescription drugs is the Reason Why Everyone Must Die.So overlooking these sophomoric justifications for dismantling the best place on earth, the game plays pretty well and is sometimes genuinely funny.  I can overlook the really hyperbolic attempts to paint Capitalism As Evil.  The only thing more absurd than Objectivists are Socialists.  In the game Our Hero fixes the Best Place In The World by forcing everyone to be equal (not kidding), including criminals.  Because Reasons.  Then he walks away like a michael bay star walking away from an explosion.  It Was The Right Thing To Do.  Because.All that said, this is a weak buy recommendation.  Worth a playthrough - 11 hours long at the most, a linear narrative.  Not worth 40 bucks.  Zero player agency, zero replayability.  Still, amusing.  Get it on sale.  Laugh along with me at the eye-roll moralism.

_childDocuments_.review: Nothing you haven’t seen before in terms of writing and world-building, but Beyond a Steel Sky is still brilliant. I loved the comedic tone and the dialogues. Your character embarks on an adventure after a child is kidnapped from their community. He’s an outlander in the city where he must find the kid—a city controlled by a council divided into: Minister of Wellbeing: Oversees the health and happiness of the citizens.  Minister of Comfort: Ensures the comfort and satisfaction of the populace.  Minister of Plenty: Manages resources and sustenance—food, etc.  Minister of Aspiration: Encourages ambition and personal growth (think *Black Mirror*, Season 3, Episode 1, Nosedive).  Minister of Safety: Maintains law and order within the city.  At first, these roles sound great, but they’re merely illusions that enslave people and confine them in the borders of the city, turning them into "pets" rather than normal human beings. It was really fun to explore this "perfect utopian" city.After the main plot ends,—saving the children—the last act was very satisfying in tying the governing plot together. The Hollywood-style ending was a perfect fit for the goofy, fun tone, imo. I love exploring the question of "What makes us human?" and Beyond a Steel Sky hits just the right spot.  Gameplay-wise, it’s a classic puzzle-solving, “work with whatever is around you” type of game. The puzzles aren’t too complicated, and the small map designs help keep things from getting boring. The graphics, odd NPC movements, and occasional animation issues can pull you out of the moment, but overall, it’s a good ride.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR;I only recommend this game to people who are fans of the Beneath a Steel Sky. While it was overall enjoyable as a fan, it is quite flawed.Full review:Being a long time fan of Point and clicks I was thrilled when I heard about this sequel to Beneath a Steel Sky. Unfortunately, I was somewhat let down. Mainly by the game being so short but, several other things bothered me as well. Twice the game glitched so that, if I happened to be in an area that wasn't exactly where I needed to be, characters would say things that spoiled the story(dialogue from the next time you would've been there). One was a huge spoiler that basically ruined most of the ending.Graphics: 4/5I really enjoyed the stylized graphics and I felt the city design was cool. Too bad you don't really get to explore any of it. You are limited to only a few(and some are rather drab) areas. The views were nice though!Sound: 4/5The music in this game was good. Very much what you would expect from a space fantasy show or movie. The voice acting was great as well. Score, Voice acting and graphics really saved this game for me. I just wished fosters steps made just a bit more sound and also changed sounds depending on the surface he's walking on.Story: 3/5While I found the concept of the story to be decent. It wasn't exactly original and it did play out well at all IMO. The beginning and the end were fine, but everything in between seemed quite flat and often forced. Frequently it felt like things were being said or done as an excuse to get to the next part of the story. I did very much enjoy some of the characters but those were the characters you interact with the least. In fact, I felt character interaction overall was fairly limited.Gameplay: 2/5This is where it really drops for me. If the story and gameplay in a Point and Click aren't absolutely top... well, that's kind of the whole game. Controls were very often clunky, unintuitive, and sometimes outright frustrating. I didn't enjoy most of the puzzles. Once again many of them felt forced and pointless. Like I was being lead by the nose the entire game. I'm at a loss for a word more potent than linear to describe how little you can do, say, or explore in this city and, because of this, I never really felt immersed.Score: 13/20 Only recommending for fans and because I would like to see more games like this but with some improvements

_childDocuments_.review: What makes Beyond a Steel Sky a trademark “Revolution Software” game? STRONG STORYTELLING AND ENGAGING, LOGICAL PUZZLES INTERWOVEN WITH THE PLOT AND FUNCTIONAL TO IT.Just as other classics under the belt of Revolution Software, the plot of Beyond a Steel Sky is enthralling, and the world building, lore, characters and puzzle mechanics are rich and immersive in a way that is rarely seen in adventure games.The story harmonizes very well with a comic book style aesthetics, including panels and speech bubbles, retrofitted in a 3D space through cel shading. It feels like playing an interactive comic book, and that was exactly Cecil’s goal, as per his words in a recent interview.But Beyond a Steel Sky doesn’t just repeat a winning formula. It strives to innovate and create, thanks to a brand-new puzzle mechanic. In the dystopic world of Union City, our protagonist will have to solve puzzles that go beyond the combination of items in his pockets, and that seems very fitting, considering the presence of AI in every aspect of that society.He will have to use a hacking tool to rewrite the logic components of machines, devices, or anything electronic, thus changing the logic of the world and cause things to happen, even hilarious things and funny gags. Thanks to this hacking mechanic, puzzles are interwoven in the story; they are functional to it and to the story pieces, instead of existing just for their own sake, or to challenger players. NPCs living in this world controlled by machines, don’t question anything that happens to such devices… they just try to make sense of it. I have to admit: there is a sense of over reliance on this hacking gizmo and an overall lack of challenge for the player, once you figure out how to use it to its full potential. Every character has a strong and well defined personality and will interact with the world in a very realistic way (for the circumstances, at least). Dialogues among characters are always believable, sharp, charming and witty, especially between Foster and Joey. Despite the masterclass writing and aesthetics, though, I think Beyond a Steel Sky would have benefitted from a longer development.  Glitches, disappearing hotspots and weird camera angles hinder the player’s experience and gameplay, and very often NPCs fail to get out of your way, or get stuck in the environment. In one such cases, for example, an NPC failed to move away from a vending machine I needed to use to solve a puzzle, and I had to reload a previous save file. The same happened quite a few times due to disappearing hotspots or bugs. However, the pull of the story and the charming characters more than makes up for these minor annoyances.Apparently, there seemed to be no need to make a sequel to Beneath a Steel Sky, a 90’s point and click game, and definitely not a lot of money to earn. This is definitely a work of passion and love, the telling of story dear to Cecil’s heart, in a fantastic universe that lends itself to even more stories, despite its conclusion.***My curator page

_childDocuments_.review: I've had this one for a while. It honestly took a while to get through. Some background: I came to Beneath a Steel Sky as a well-intentioned birthday gift from a grandparent. By the time I got that game, it was not compatible out of the box with my system, It was already a bit of a relic. But, with some struggle I got the game to work on my machine and it left a massive imprint on me, where other adventure games bored or disinterested me, the strange tone and setting of the first game just grabbed and held onto me.Coming from that place, I was initially a bit overwhelmed. I didn't have any real expectations for what Beyond would be like in story or how it would hold up as a successor game, but modern adventure games *also* really don't interest me. The story is pretty different, at times where it actually feels connected to the old game, it's mostly via these brief nostalgia-laden set pieces. "Do you remember the thing?" is a question the game seems to ask often. And I get it, but that is the only real sense of connection it seems to have. Tonally, it's telling a very different story, making a very different point, and the Steel Sky elements almost feel like they're bolted onto a game that didn't start out in that universe.I still had fun. The concepts in play with the puzzles at the very end were very cool to me. This game has an interesting point to make, even if some of it really just doesn't feel a whole like it actually has much in common with the predecessor game. A lot changed in the years between these games. I can't fault discontinuity too much. It still rises to be a fun adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: I was afraid that this belated sequel to "Beneath a Steel Sky" would be dreary and 3D gadgety. It took me a while to get into the right spirit, and the comic-style intro sequence surely did not help. But after a while, it became … hypnotic. These omnipresent mind-numbing motivational slogans and bizarre droid interactions are fascinating, and I love the tongue-in-cheek humour when the facade of this happy-happy place cracks. The developers really had me on board when I was able to hack the dispenser to spit out a can of Spankles instead of sounding a burglar alarm when using the crowbar on it. They also did an excellent job in the characterisation of the people you meet along the way; I am sure I met this Raquel in her rebellious phase. Some unforeseen plot twists (or maybe I am just easily impressible) are welcome, as are well-integrated nods to the predecessor game. Lots of popcultural references to spot without them being too obtrusive (off the top of my head: Total Recall, Dr. Mabuse, Metropolis, Monty Python's black knight, and obviously Blade Runner). I was wondering what this gameplay reminded me of, and an aspiration brooch design of Nico Collard and George Stobbart gave it away – this is a 3D version of the design you might have seen in the “Broken Sword” series. So, is this game perfect? Of course not, some hiccups in the gameplay when characters don’t remember that you have talked about certain topics with them before, and the voice-acting is a bit annoying to my ears. It is also too structured for my liking as the problems you have to solve are served in little chunks. But all-in-all an atmospheric game with a great concept, interesting characters, and compelling storytelling. Whether you enjoy staring for hours on end at Mr Foster’s chiselled derriere is totally up to you, though.

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't much of a review, more like an appreciation post for Revolution Software for making this game.Beneath a Steel Sky was the very first point and click adventure game i played, some 20 years back. It came in the demo disc of the first gaming magazine i've bought with some of the little money i could save up as a kid. I loved it back then and i still love it when i replay it from time to time. Coming back to Union City in a more modernized fashion was as much of a joy as the first time. Held off on buying this for a while and ended up getting it on the winter sale for dirt cheap, but if a third installment ever comes to fruition, i'll support Revolution in a more timely and fully priced manner 100%.

_childDocuments_.review: It's fine? I think? The original game is famously unfinished, releasing with only a fraction of its ideas intact. It's quite clear that Cecil and Gibbons had wider designs for - probably - a grimy comic book. The narrative in the manual speaks to so much. But it's also understandable. Revolution has always been an ambitious studio, dreaming up games that really should take an army of developers to make, and yet pulling it off with less than 5. And thinking of the timeframe - they didn't have the infinite resources of Skywalker Ranch or a myriad of Sierra dollars.But Beyond has been "in the works" since as early as 2009. If it had an announcement and a trailer it'd be the Duke Nukem Forever of adventure games, but Revolution always maintained non-committal commitment to it. The 11 years in the oven don't show at all. In fact, it might be a little crispier on the edges when the recipe really called for golden-brown.So - what's good?Stylistically, the game is distinct and yet eerily familiar when compared to the original. It's astonishing how the art direction appropriately matches the original. From rusty walkways in the top level to mid level glistening walkways, the game matches the original in virtually every way, and that is some masterful continuity.The characters are generally well developed and interesting, with the exception really of Robert himself who is just some guy. One of the top Steam reviews notes that Joey isn't acerbic enough - I'd suggest the writer of that review didn't get very far in the game. The humour is clearly "tidied up" a little bit to focus a little bit less on the puerile aspects that Beneath did, but Joey's attitude is attuned perfectly to how we know him.The puzzles are well designed, such that I didn't use the hint system or lookup any guides. This isn't to say that they are easy, but rather that they do a good job of helping you identify what it is you need to progress. The hacking mechanic has you "juggling" components around, and observing the environment and characters which makes the puzzles very satisfying to solve. Once they click, they click. This is an adventure game that makes you work, but gives you everything you need to succeed. Absolute top tier adventure game puzzle design. A fun side effect of this is being able to make appliances, robots, and screens do amusing things - like making a barker d-RYD aggressively or excitedly welcome visitors. You can "die" just like in Beneath, but doing so just sends you back to the mere moments beforehand, so it's without consequence.So it's a well-rounded adventure game all in all, and in terms of base formula, an absolute prime example of the genre.What's not great? Well. It's a Revolution game. So the plot isn't slow-burning, rather it is...slow to ignite. Revolution have a habit of creating a compelling setting and waiting until the final act to fully introduce you to your motive and even antagonist. Up until those moments you're just sort of exploring. The first Broken Sword did a better job at this, but you still don't even have a clear "enemy" until, really, the final cutscene. So is the case here. You explore Union City and get a general feeling that it's an image, likes, and retweets obsessed culture. Social media and social credit are intertwined and liking the wrong post sends you back up to the factory level. Also people have robot slaves. Okay, cool. What's the...problem? I don't think everyone would really be in total agreement that this society is bad thing.So other than the hook of knowing some kid from your village has been taken, you don't REALLY have a huge amount of motivation. Revolution have kind of assumed that you hate the idea of a Black Mirror social media dystopia and hoped it would be enough to keep you going.Equally there's not much clear motivation going for the first "villain" character you meet, except his sinister moustache and job description. WHY does he hate your guts? What's in it for him? Even at his moustache twirling climax he failed to convey exactly what his passion is, except "I love this city". Sorry, that's not enough. Pure blind patriotism is expressed in so many different ways - Texans and Albertans drive oversized trucks with breedable hips because oil and gas is king, the English get blind drunk and misappropriate St George's Cross while kicking a ball around because something is king, I guess. Or they join the armed forces and serve with pride or something. Even the most jingoistic is still driven by *something*. Except this guy.And then when a bit part character from Beneath suddenly turns up with a secondary antagonist to help you out, nothing ever explains why or how they came to turn against their city that apparently everyone just loves unquestioningly.And then the finale is literally a rubiks cube. That's enough said there. Or it would be if the "logic problems" you present to the AI were actually...logical. Computers cannot be argued with, they understand binary only - quite literally, but there's "this statement is false" and then there's "yes but what you think is right is actually wrong". Even ChatGPT has better safeguards against the latter.All of this is presented and conveyed through odd plasticey animations with a very odd understanding of eye contact. I'm autistic and generally have a hard time with eye contact, but good lord even I don't look at the floor when I'm threatening someone with a gun.SO is it good? It's not terrible. It's a Revolution game - fantastic concept, passable presentation, likeable and diverse characters. But... in typical Revolution fashion, you just don't know what's going on until the end, and the end is wacky and a bit out there, and while trying to deliver a philosophical parable, falls flat because even after nigh on 20 years in the oven, Revolution weren't quite able to come with an intelligent argument against the social media dystopia other than "actually it's bad". Adventure games do a better job of parables when they have you doing the thinking (a la Blackwell).

_childDocuments_.review: Though this was more of an impulse purchase, Beyond a Steel Sky wasn't too bad... though it was far from great.Not having known that this was essentially a legacy sequel to the 1994 adventure game Beneath a Steel Sky, I was surprised to learn how much history the aforementioned game/series has. The game kindly catches new players up with the existing story, which helps situate you in the world of BaSS. You play as Robert Foster, a "Gaplander" in the far future and who clearly owes his fashion sense to one Rick Deckard. Foster lives in a village tucked into a sprawling desert known as "The Gap" (not the one that sells jeans), where life is simple and traditional. Things are upturned for Foster when one of the children from his village is kidnapped and taken to Union City, a coveted metropolis closed off to all but the worthiest of people. Making your way to the city, you meet fellow Gaplanders, poetry-writing robots, and a nice-looking fella that sells mini sausages. And they said the future was bleak.However, once you breach the walls of Union City, you begin to uncover a conspiracy that (quite literally) goes all the way to the top... and this is where my issues with BaSS' story and writing come in. The game clearly has a lot that it wants to say about the nature of utopias and egregious government oversight and societal control and free will and so on and so on. But it never seems to actually say anything about it that hasn't already been covered in other works of science fiction and dystopian literature. I more or less agree with much of what the game posits, but I felt as though the morals and messages could have been delivered and dissected better. The game seems to be in so much of a rush to have you solve its central mystery that it doesn't allow the other story and narrative elements room to breathe. However, this pales in comparison to my main criticism of BaSS: the puzzles. I will freely admit that I'm not too familiar with the adventure genre, but I know a good puzzle from a bad one, and unfortunately this game has more of the latter than the former. Some puzzles' solutions were so obtuse that I wondered how I was meant to solve it on my own. The game does offer some mercy in the form of a "hint" system at no cost or penalty to you, the player, but perhaps there's something to be said about it when there's even an achievement in the game for finishing it sans hints.That being said, the game's presentation was one of its highlights. After Jet Set Radio Future shaped my early gamer-brain, I've come to love cel-shaded art styles - and BaSS has just this. While the animations and character models are often clunky, they are admittedly quite nice to look at, and this game being co-written by Dave Gibbons (of Watchmen fame), it makes sense that there's a sort-of comic book-style aesthetic to it. A particular standout was a moment when you ascend to a recycling plant high above the city and you're offered your first proper view of the beautiful metropolis, shimmering like an oasis in the middle of the Gap.Overall, I did enjoy what Beyond a Steel Sky was going for (most of the time), but found that the slow pace of the opening, oft-obtuse puzzles, and disjointed writing took me more out of the experience than immersed me in it. Still, I do give this a light recommendation for any fans of the original game or adventure games in general.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall its a decent adventure game, and was very excited playing it. As i progressed i began thinking this maybe one of the better adventure games, sadly my enthusiasm began to dissipate once i reached a certain puzzle involving a poet and how to get his speech, from that point the game became very average, I still enjoyed it but there was too many hack type puzzles and not enough inventory puzzles. What i didn't enjoy much was the social engineering vandalism by the main character.  As a game on its own merits; the game is good, but as a sequel it was a bit of a let down. I admire the 3D world aspect rather than being a 2D side scroller, i just wish they had taken a page or two from Escape from monkey island which is also a 3D puzzler. I still recommend this game as it is engaging to play and has you wanting to return to complete it. The story is decent enough, the voice acting is great.

Firstly an over reliance on hacking puzzles. Secondly it suffers from a lot of graphical glitches and bugs. _childDocuments_.review: Beyond a Steel Sky is a beautifully designed game to go through and probably a better attempt at 3D gaming by Revolution than Broken Sword 3 and 4. I loved replaying Robert Foster again, after having played Beneath a Steel Sky; though doing this with comic-book style 3D graphics was really great, especially in the conversations, Foster's monologuing, and the background conversations when exploring.The puzzles are good in this game - the hacking element was a really nice idea, and certainly an interesting arrangement in solving some of the game's puzzles, as was the recreation of the previous game's computer world environment. The game still has some of that nice quirky comedic elements in it, and the plot twists in it were a surprise - one bit was a total surprise, which allowed me to reunite with a character I liked in the previous game. I would certainly recommend playing this with a controller - that was nice to use in this game, and easy to get to grips with the gameplay with one.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: If it's not entirely clear at first glance, the game is pretty much a modernised point & click adventure game. I read multiple people mentioning playing the previous game (Beyond a Steel Sky) is not mandatory to play this sequel, but I'd argue many important narrative references will be lost without at least some knowledge of the previous story, and characters/events might feel like they appear/happen out of nowhere, At the very least, if you don't feel like playing a much older game at this point, I recommend reading a summary of the first opus.In any case, the world building is great, while the story itself is fine (not great). The ending, for sure, is disappointing in its wholly inadequate attempt at philosophising, blatantly throwing lazy social commentary in the form of propositions that are neither convincing nor as logically sound as the devs seem to think. It's a shame, because there is absolutely good potential for a reflection about utopia, dystopia, and happiness as a fundamental moral ground: it just demands so much more nuance and efforts, and in this case, was not sufficiently explored in depth before the last "philosophical confrontation". The story in general tends to require some significant suspension of disbelief: how you can freely go around committing crimes in a supposedly all-controlling city able to track anyone's actions at all time seems weird, for instance.Glitches apart, I loved the visuals. It has a balance of details and cartoon effects with a very distinct charm. And although the city feels rather lifeless when looking outside of the location we're standing in (you won't see much happening at a distance), this ends up easily forgivable. I also particularly enjoyed the soundtrack, which has this kind of cinematic, superhero vibe at times. There aren't superheroes here, but it works very well! Voices, on the other hand, are bad, some exceptions aside.The gameplay is simple enough to learn, with some openness to emergence (or in other words, potential to cause slight chaos here and there). Yet, the experience remains relatively linear, and solutions to puzzles are never terribly complex. There is the occasional very obtuse set of expected interactions to be wary of, which is typical of this type of games. Nothing time, or worst case scenario a guide, won't solve. Truth is, most of the game is rather on the easy side of things, and I'm not aware of long-term unwanted consequences to any "choice" the player may make.For some last considerations, I'd note that the game does contain multiple noticeable "errors/bugs", although at this point none that were entirely game breaking in my case. So lots of glitched camera views, textures taking way too long to load, the main character not knowing something he should know because you haven't done "exactly" what the game expects you to... to name a few.Overall, I've enjoyed my time sufficiently to recommend the game. In the end, it showcases a relatively interesting cyberpunk world, and is a nice modern twist of the older point & click style favoured by the previous opus. This is not a masterpiece though, to be clear. And it doesn't exactly compare that well to other games at the same price point, so you may want to wait for a rebate. 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: This was a fantastic game. Very likeable characters, calm gameplay and a lot of exploring. The puzzles are not hard and not easy. Just right. The story is nice and you get really sucked into it. You want to finish the game. Despite the fact that is has a little 'cartoony' view, it still looks quite realistic in terms of graphics. This game was a job well done. Kudo's for the developers!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: It took me far too long to realise that the had made a sequal to "Beneath a Steel Sky", which I played during my teen years. Having played it, I would say it is a worthy successor. All the elements that made the original game worthwhile are still there: the snarky humour, the lore, the feeling of the game being from Roberts introspective look at what is happening. This is also enforced by that fact that the results of actions take in the first game are what drives the story in the sequal. The main new element that this game introduces to gameplay, a 3D world, is used to the fullest. That gives a whole new level of being able to interact with, and explore, the world.The only downside I experience is that it is a relative short gameplay. But if that is what is required to be able to deliver a game with a good story, then I am really OK with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed playing this. I was a big fan of the original Beneath a Steel Sky on Commodore Amiga but could never finish it due to bugs and crashes.The comic book graphics are superb especially some of the Watchmen and Blade Runner stylizations. The voice acting and characters were entertaining and distinctive. In terms of plot the final two acts are both shocking and poignant. The hacking subgames were very enjoyable.This is not a game for everyone. Some may find it slow paced and some of the physics are a bit clunky. NPCs bumping into each other or trapped. Frustration when there is puzzle which I don't see how anyone could ever solve without the hints. However I enjoyed the relaxed pace and was always curious to see where the story would go.If you were a fan of the original or 1990's point-and-click adventures, give it a go.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond a Steel Sky is the sequel to the 1994 cult classic Beneath a Steel Sky, now in full 3D while maintaining it's Point-N-Click adventure roots.The story sees Foster returning once more to Union City in order to rediscover the sinister truth behind the facade and why gaplanders are being kidnapped.The game features a hint system that more games of this nature could benefit from, and while it's not needed often, there are times where it comes in handy. Especially around the Hacking Tool which is this games "thing", that allows you to manipulate various machines and robot logics around, but parts of the hacking is used so infrequently, that by the time you need to utilize it proper, you'll likely have forgotten all about how to, leading to some tricky puzzles at times.That said Beyond is a solid game, both technically and gameplay wise, and a fine addition to an oft forgotten classic genre, the point-n-click adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: A sequel released more than twenty years after the original game, Beneath a Steel Sky (which has been available for free from GOG for a pretty long time). Is the sequel worth playing to fans of the original, and perhaps more importantly, do you have to have played the original to enjoy this game?The game's plot is understandable without having played the original game; they include enough information about the original game both as fan service and as an attempt to onboard new players that you should be able to play through it just fine. However, a lot of returning characters and elements hit much harder if you have the full context of the original game, and it's a much more enjoyable experience with that context. I would recommend either playing the original game (it's about 2.5 hours and available free from GOG) or watching a playthrough to maximize your enjoyment of this game.So is the game worth playing for returning fans? I would say yes, although with caveats. First, obviously there is a big difference in perspective and gameplay. The game's plot is also a big step down from the original, and the writing suffers near the end of the game. There also appears to be a plot hole regarding events at the end of the previous game which becomes relevant near the end of this one. However, even with that the writing is great otherwise and captures a similar tone to the original. All the puzzles are pretty simple in this game and usually involve the new hacking mechanic. Ultimately, if you were satisfied with the ending of the original game and didn't want to see any more of Joey and Foster, I wouldn't say this game is a must play. But if you want to see Union City with modern graphics I can easily recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond a Steel Sky is great sci-fi adventure and follow up game from Beneath a Steel Sky.It was extremely nostalgic to jump back into this universe and I enjoyed every minute playing it, from returning to Union City and meeting old faces to jumping back into LINC space.If you are an fan and enjoyed Beneath a Steel Sky then I would recommend this game.Be Vigilant!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: It is a sequel to that game about a guy and his robot Joey from my childhood. Quest/adventure type of game where you speak to characters and do some actions to trigger scripted events. Has humor with real world references, has actually interesting characters. Has in-game tips of multiple levels (from vague hints to specific actions what to do to move forward). A bit cheap looking. Should run fine even on potato PC. It's not too long (took me 10h). Overall I do recommend it if you're into that type of games.P.S. Btw, original game from 1994 - Beneath a Steel Sky is free on steam.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: "Beyond a Steel Sky" is a classic point-and-click adventure game, albeit in 3D. It's a sequel to 1994's "Beneath a Steel Sky" and references characters, places and events from that story. You can play the original here on Steam for free, and I highly recommend it. It's a bit janky in places and some of the puzzles require some lateral thinking (or a walkthrough, if you're impatient like me), but overall it's a well made, well written and well voiced story. A must for adventure game and sci-fi fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this because I was a fan of the orignal Beneath a Steel Sky in it's day - the dystopian futuristic setting was really captivating.Beyond a Steel Sky is faithful to it's origins and continues the story of Robert returning to the now utopian city that he left in the capable hands of his lifelong robotic friend Joey.He learns that Joey has left the city, and a council of elected officials are in charge. On the surface the city appears perfect and happy, but there is more than meets the eye.Using the unreal engine, Revolution was able to craft a wonderful looking game that appeared true to it's comic book origins. Including vignette style text boxes and shading that really gave it an ink-on-paper look rendered in beautiful 3D.The background of the cityscape inspired strong feelings of nostalgia in me as it was a true embodiment of the classic Beneath game I played years ago.The puzzles were very well done, I was actually very impressed - as I have played many illogical adventure games that become a constant source of "reading the walkthrough." Thankfully for the audience, there is an in-game hint system that allows you to give yourself a hint if you get stuck on what to do next. The system is paced in a way too that accidental mis-clicks aren't going to trigger 5 spoilers when you really only needed a small push in the right direction.Beyond a Steel Sky was expertly done and I highly recommend it. The story itself was engaging and really kept true to the original. If you haven't played the original (as it probably around 30+ years ago now) it is significantly more unforgiving, but "Beyond" allows you to review the story and be brought up to speed, so it is not necessary to have played it to enjoy this sequel.If you enjoy a 3rd person adventure game, puzzle solving, and an original futuristic dystopia: pick yourself up a copy today, and support the devs on their great work. You won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is visually pleasing, the puzzles are interesting and sometimes tricky, but always logical. It felt nice to finish some of these while being a bit stuck, yet without googling for the solution. Game's style and animation are working well, despite a bit of simplified graphics. It is clear that the motion capture was used to achieve such organics. The only drawbacks are that the game is a bit short. 10 hours including the "stuck" moments.The second drawback is crashing. _childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: This was a sequel to a game that happened 20 years ago. Before I played this game, I did research, consensus said I didn't need to slug through it, however, I would definitely recommend looking into watching a recap as certain parts of the ending was kind of confusing to me, and I feel if I had slugged myself through, this would have made a bigger impact.Besides that factor, and besides the story having plot holes and some of the characters dialogue not making logical sense, taking those out of the picture, I really enjoyed this point and click adventure. The puzzles were really interesting, instead of thinking with portals, you think with hacking, and the puzzles for me were pretty straight forward and not insanely difficult, which I appreciated. You can easily get all of the achievements minus one on the first play through, and as long as you make a manual save during a certain time in the game, you can reload and get that last achievement within about a hour.I would highly recommend this game while it's on sale, as besides the points mentioned above, it was extremely enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I had so much fun playing this! Revolution Software are possibly my favourite developer. The comic art style is great, and the story is too. The puzzles can be quite hard (at least for me anyway) but there are helpful hints along the way! Some of the puzzles are a little repetitive, and it would've been nice to see a mix of things in there (constantly hacking to get into places which is a swap was a bit tedious) I do own the original version which I'm considering playing now! I streamed this too which was also fun!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: The first game I've ever played to give me vertigo. And it was great.Honestly, I wasn't expecting it to live up to my nostalgic love of Beneath A Steel Sky, and maybe the writing and puzzles aren't quite up to the standard of the previous game... but, I loved every moment I spent in the new and improved Union City. I have now played the game twice through and, every few months, I look at it and wonder if I should play it again - and there are very few story-based games that I have ever wanted to play through multiple times, but I find Union City as compelling a setting (if not more so) than, say, Rapture.The story has it's flaws, especially towards the end where I feel things get a little rushed and simplistic puzzle-wise, but the characters, setting and art style make up for it in abundance.I hope to see what becomes of Union City in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the original I picked this up on sale after a while of umming over it. From the outset, I loved the original having played it a number of times over the past 25 years. Initially i was a little wary of the new style but it grew on me, it feels like a comic book which feels apt. I'd recommend anyone considering the game, if they have not; grab the original (it's free in places) and play it first. There are a number of references to the orignal. I only encountered one bug during its unique puzzle mechanic though it didnt get in the way of progressing.  Overall it was great to continue the story of Robert Foster. I cant recall the original price but I got it on sale in the £10-15 range which felt about right.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, and a must-play for anyone who enjoyed the original.  Superb graphics and sense of immersion.  Audio doppler effects work great as you move toward/from a sound source.At times I felt the dialogue a little tedious / overdone, but the interface made it easy to move on.  Voice acting is generally very good, with the occasional dodgy Aussie accent thrown in.Puzzles are mostly on the easy side, but still required some thinking through.Great end-game sequences and build up.Looking forward to the next one!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10This game is great! Who knew that making a sequel after 16 years could actually turn out well if you just give it a reasonable scope (looking at you, Duke Nukem Forever, and then looking at you, Return to Monkey Island, with approval). We've come a long way since 1994, but more so technically than in storytelling when it comes to point and click-puzzle games. Gone are the 2D-perspectives, replaced by 3D-environments where you can explore freely. Gone are the days of pizel-hunting, with interactable elements being carefully displayed in such a way that you notice it but still have to explore in order to figure out what you SHOULD interact with. Beyond a Steel Sky is a modern sequel that takes the correct steps in following the development of video games.Set ten years after the first game, you are once again controlling Robert Foster on a quest to Union City. This time to save a kidnapped child. Along the way you meet colorful characters, solve puzzles and have a few laughs. The game is roughly 5 hours long (9 if you want all of the achievements) and delivers a fun story with just enough serious elements in it as to not feel outright silly. Now, what is really good and bad about this game? Well:+ Fun story with interesting characters+ Puzzles that are very "fair" in scope. Rarely do you find them either baby-easy all of the time, but neither hair-pullingly hard.- Performance issues and graphical quality is bad. The game looks like a 2013 game, at best.- AI-problems. People move around like they are in Zoo Tycoon. They do not feel lifelike at all.Still, this game is great. You NEED to play the first one in order to fully appreciate it, but Beneath a Steel Sky is a FREE GAME. You can just get it from steam, GOG or probably Revolution Games website, if you wanted to. That game is great as well, give it a go!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: This reminded me a lot of Telltales Borderlands game with its setting and humor. I highly recommend playing Beneath a Steel Sky first because of all the easter eggs and I think it makes the story stronger. The ending had a moment where it punched me in the feels, but then it hilariously destroyed that mood by literally stepping over it. You'll get it once you see it.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent sequel to a classic. Good story, great vibe, nice visuals, good voice acting, all-in-all a very enjoyable game. I was lost a good few times during my playthrough, but luckily the built-in hints system is very well made to give you a little push but not reveal everything at once. I liked this game better than the modern Telltale games I've played (Walking Dead, Batman x2, Back To The Future).
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Its fantastic, It feels super modern and nostalgic at the same time, they nailed it. if your a fan of revolution software games and/or the original game or just point and click adventure games in general then you won't be disappointed. Pros- Beautiful graphics, from the first scene I was blown away. Game is decently optimized. Running everything on max settings at 1440p on a vega 64 I can only remember a handful of times it dipped below 60fps. - Excellent voice acting.- Humorous dialogue and banter between the characters.- Brilliant story and world building.- Solid controls and UI. The inventory system arguably wasn't the most optimal but it worked just fine.- Interesting puzzle mechanics, I was hoping they would do a bit more with the hacking aspect but regardless it was fun to play and no real head scratchers, game flowed along nicely. - Decent soundtrack.-Collectibles if that is your thing.-Robust saving system.Cons- No hot spot reveal tool as far as know.- Can't be played exclusively with the mouse, i.e you must use keyboard or controller to move about.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Programming the Z80 - seriously! That was the book I read in the 80s to learn Z80 programming and here it is referenced in this game. Amazing! Just for that I had to give this game a thumbs up. Overall the game is original, funny, tongue-in-cheek. If you liked the Outer Worlds, you will like this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: A modern sequel to a venerable adventure game.  The game looks well. It is fully 3D with comics stylization. Animations are a bit stiff, especially during conversations. Voice-overs are consistently great.  The gameplay is an evolution of a classical adventure game with an inventory. It is upgraded with a full third-person movement and new hacking mechanic that is based on manipulation of flow-charts. Puzzles are generally logical and well made.  The story follows from Beneath a Steel Sky, after a time skip. It explores the supposed utopia created in Union City and its effects on its citizens and neighboring areas. The writing is good and the story was interesting all the way to the ending.  It is a great way to continue and modernize a game from entire generation ago.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best adventure games I've played in a long time!Beyond A Steel Sky takes everything that was excellent about the first game (voice actors, humour and storyline) and combined it with a fantastic new plot that continues to expand on the original, great 3D graphics, a little action and an excellent soundtrack.If you've played the original Beneath A Steel Sky this game definitely will not disappoint you.Revolution Games have always had a knack of coming up with timeless, fantastic graphic adventures and this is proof that they still haven't lost that touch. The Steel Sky adventures though, for me at least, are their real masterpieces.Whilst the Broken Sword games are good with a similar sense of humour and engaging game play there is just something about the Steel Sky games that keeps bringing me back (must have played Beneath A Steel Sky several times and I'm still yet to grow bored of it).
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Own this game on other systems too. A really fun adventure from the studio behind the Broken Sword series and of course, Beneath A Steel Sky.Beyond picks up years after the events of Beneath and is distant enough you don't really need to have played it before playing this. Though, as Beneath is free, I'd recommend playing that too. Beyond sees you playing as Robert Foster living his life in the wastelands (called the gap), when a machine suddenly attacks and steals a child from the community. As Foster, you are tasked with finding the child and to find out why he was he taken. The gameplay is a mixture of detective work and puzzle solving with a fun twist that allows you to hack machines to aid you on your mission.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: If you played and liked Beneath a Steel Sky, then this is an obvious choice. It is fun to go back to Union City, see what has happened since you left Joey, (ken?), and Hobbins in charge of it. The game has a nice mix of story, puzzles and fan-pandering. It is very enjoyable.If you never played Beneath a Steel Sky, though.. it is harder to say. If you like puzzles that consits of manipulating objects and characters, you will probably like it. But in the end, the gameplay is quite old-school -but-in-modern-game-engine.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: A worthy successor to Beneath a Steel Sky.  Even if you didn't play the old 1st game and you just like point and click adventure you may enjoy it.  I bought this game and played it back when it first came out and there were some bugs, but nothing that overly frustrated me.  Several patches have been released since then so hopefully the bugs are mostly gone now.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: This is simply a great game in every respect! It doesn't try to rewrite the original story, but rather builds on it, and it does a great job, even surpassing the original. The music is epic, the cartoonish graphics are great, and the views are breathtaking. All contributing to great ambience and story. And, as a plus, the jokes are still there.In the end, it is refreshing to see a game that honours the original in such a great way.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I'm incredibly torn on how I felt about this game. If you enjoyed Beneath a Steel Sky there's enough here to tickle that nostalgia and for you to enjoy yourself, but the game itself was just...meh. It's personal preference but I found the ending absolutely unsatisfying. It's the problem with continuing a story after the "Happy ever after" in that you'll have to break it to make a new story and this just didn't click with me.it's absolutely worth a pick up if it's on sale and if you enjoyed the first one but 8 hours and it's finished. Without the nostalgia kick, this would be considered lackluster and a too clunky to be enjoyable.I'll give it a recommendation based on the above
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I was hyped since the moment I first heard about the game coming out, until playing 1-2 hours into it. I guess I had high expectations from Revolution, but got a Broken Sword 3D era replica in the end. Well, you can't expect much when they do the same to the Broken Sword franchise.I can't say it's a bad game, hence the thumbs up, but if you have built up some expectation for that long after the first game, you should curb your enthusiasm (cue the music).
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Not a bad game. I'm happy with it considering I got it on discount. Honestly wouldn't recommend buying at full price. Story is good if a little lack luster. I found myself aggravated a few times at the clunky controls. Puzzles are simple enough but somewhat thought provoking.  Not one I will be playing through again. But happy enough with the purchase. Kept me mildly entertained for a day or so.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: My review is positive, but I must say - the game left me QUITE ANGRY.I played through the prequel - the super old game that is, to learn the story before diving into this one.So I know the friendship between Joey and Foster goes way back, they survived the hardship of the Gap together. The game never ceases to remind you, that they are "best buddies", "friends forever".Mild spoilers below ->Major spoilers below ->Da ♥♥♥♥ is that, right?!Beside that, the story is interesting and I enjoyed the hacking mechanic - that being said, it could be much more complex and have some hidden secrets.The inventory system can be extremely annoying at times - like, when you try to use and object on a person, they just keep moving and the inventory closes. With some characters I spent like 5 frigging minutes to manage to do that.But the story is good :D
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: The long awaited sequel to one of my favorite, if not my absolute favorite, adventure game of the 90's, Beneath A Steel Sky. Naturally I was excited to play this, and it delivered on many fronts. A continuation of the story, in a new three-dimensional environment. Perhaps not the same level or density of humor as its predecessor, the story and puzzles are definitely worth it.My only real problem with this game is the bugged "Two-Faced" achievement, in which one has to view both of Songbird's endings, the good one and the bad one. I won't spoil the details in this review, but at a certain point in the story this achievement should trigger, and it has never unlocked for me, despite having taken all of the correct steps, and having played through the game 4 to 5 times already. It's the only achievement that prevents me from "completing" it, as far as Steam is concerned. The devs haven't really responded much to this issue, and I've received no real technical support, despite my asking several times. It's possible even they have no idea how to fix this bug.I've technically unlocked it, though, so I guess I can count it as a fully completed game, even if Steam won't.Despite that personal issue I have with the game, and to a degree with the devs, I do recommend this game. Complete Beneath A Steel Sky (also on Steam) first, and then play through this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Loved every minute of this one!This one will be a "play again".  Great graphics, storyline, characters, dialogue, and immersive atmosphere...classic scifi.  Reminds me of some of my old favorites like Full Throttle, Tex Murphy, the Dig, etc... and the P.I. Garrett books.  I will anxiously await the next one!!  Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: A good game that follows the spirit of the original game. Sometimes thought the puzzles were a little too easy but it was entertaining.For those who have not played the 90's game Beneath a Steel sky, I think you should play it first. This game will be so much better then. Wish there was a sequel to this game. I grew up with this type of game and I like them.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing game and brilliant sequel to the 1994 original "Beneath a Steel Sky"! Just like it's predecessor, this is similar to a "point and click" type adventure game where gameplay is relatively simple, composed almost exclusively of puzzle-solving, with no combat, no character development and a simple inventory. In this sequel however, the world is navigable in 3D.The focus is on the storyline, dialogue, and world of which this game excels at. The story arc is interesting and keeps one engaged throughout the game, the witty dialogue is well delivered by good voice acting (with diverse accents), and Union City (the world) is beautifully reconstructed in 3D. The 3D render style is similar to Borderlands, giving it a slight comic-book effect.The game's core gameplay however - puzzle solving - is a bit simple and is dependent on one particular mechanic (hacking). The gameplay is probably meant to be relaxing, allowing one to enjoy the story and dialogue with little frustration and can be completed anywhere from 10 or probably more hours (I skipped quite some of the audio dialogue relying on subtitles)Story = 4/5Graphics = 4/5Audio = 5/5Gameplay = 3/5Replayability = N/AOVERALL = 4/5My overall impressions are - Well Recommended
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: A well written game with loads of charm and character.I appreciate the humor it brings to its overarching discussion of dystopian themes. As a fan of Beneath a Steel Sky, this is a worthwhile continuation of what that story was trying to explore. This time with a twist of the dystopia being well-meaning.Graphics are sort of Borderland-ish, but not really. They stand very well on their own, and add to the experience.NPCs move about, do things, and react to what's going on, which adds a sense that the world is alive. This adds to solving puzzles in creative ways, using the patterns of the NPCs, or even *their* interactions with the environments. Classical music recorded by actual live musicians elevates the experience. Desert scenes get this kind of Lawrence of Arabia-type swells that are just amazing. I didn't see the music discussed quite enough when the game was being reviewed. On the flip side, PC controls can be a bit clunky, especially when targeting an NPC for interaction.No major qualms on my end. Fully recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: A great modern follow-up to the original game that I played all those years ago. The characters, humour and story of this game far exceed the limitations of the original.  Having said that, I would recommend playing the original game first as it will be necessary if you wish to fully understand the story of this second game.While I'm always sceptical of point-and-click games in 3D instead of 2D, I think they did a fantastic job with the art style and atmosphere of this game.  Sometimes the music didn't feel quite right but that may just be my preferences and on the whole I can't complain.The central puzzle system used in this game is quite different, however I found it refreshing to try something different.I only encountered a few bugs but I was able to work around them.  As with every game, make sure you make frequent manual saves....and what's with all these references to my home country, Australia?
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: For starters the game worked with very few bugs.The best part of the game was when the main character took the profile of a dead person so that they could enter the city and then enter their home. When they did the dead persons wife was totally down with the fact that a complete stranger, who was male, was in her home walking around freely and masquerading as her dead husband. Her biggest concern was getting enough points to go to the gala and doing damage control on social media as she put it. She then spent hours in the bedroom with Minister Alonso while I was goofing around learning about a dead guy so that she could go to the gala which I later sabotaged anyway. The dead guys robot didn't even notice their master was a completely different person just that they lost weight. Amazing I pissed myself laughing. A less classic part of the game was cleaning bird poo wasn't exactly the escape I was looking for in a game. I wasn't really sold on the graphic novel style of the game. I also didn't find the hints helpful and had to go online and do the walk through which was annoying.   I could have been speared the semi weird nudity in digital world as well.  The game had a really good ending though.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: The critisism of fans proved to be right: the game is so good to come back for after the first part that was published a long time ago, and which I got free when I joined Good Old Games. Thank you Steam for publishing this game! It's entertaining and has a lot of good thought put into it. This is a nice adventure game that puts your brain in use, while enjoying an atmospheric, futuristic city life in the middle of a rural landscape.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR - GREATI wasn't sure what to think going into this game.  I have complicated relationship with the original game Beneath a Steel Sky.  It's a cult classic for a reason, great characters and acting, a good story with complex themes and a hilariously bleak and scathing view of humanity's future.  But it's definitely a product of it's time and I especially didn't really like the way the puzzles were presented and while I really enjoyed the interplay between the extremely dark moments and the comedic moments, the balance between the two wasn't always handled well (Foster's reaction to what LINC does to Reich for example).None of these things were a problem this go around.  They took the good stuff from original, added 25 years of gameplay and story innovation and crafted a truly fantastic game.  This time, they found the perfect balance to the dark/comic elements so I was constantly amused but when the serious moments came they hit you with the correct emotional weight.  Joey is even better, and despite only being your "sidekick" for only a portion of the game (though it's sizeable) he becomes one of the all time great "adventure game sidekicks".  They incorporated bits and characters from the previous game in ways that were always surprising and interesting.  I was especially shocked when I finally ran into !I'm also a big fan of art style.  The comicbook-ization of the 3D graphics looks great and really fit the tone quite well.  There were a number of small graphical issues (such as hair or clothes subtly shuddering or the camera ending up behind an advertisement banner or something during dialogue) but I did notice a major improvement from the initial release which felt very buggy.The way the juxtaposed (yeah, that's right, I went to college) the original games grimy dystopian nightmare with the bright, garishly colorful utopian nightmare of this game, set 10 years later.  I also really liked the reveal of how it all happened and the reasons behind why the villain(s) did what they did, and how Foster played his part in that.  Because of that, though, I was a little disappointed with the ending after the climax.  It didn't ruin the game for me, but I felt like it undermined a lot of the great points that were made during the climax section.Spoiler-filled explanation:  Despite my quibble with the ending, I found the game to be extremely entertaining, the acting was great, the puzzles were well designed and the hint system was fantastic.  All around one of the best adventures I've played and I recommend it to everyone whether you played the original or not!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: A really well-done implementation of the point-and-click adventure genre in a 3D engine. It has real puzzles and the familiar "steal or break everything that isn't nailed down" mechanics. I found the characters very well-realized and fun to talk to. Joey is fun when he's around, sometimes getting in the way, just like in Beneath a Steel Sky.If you haven't played Beneath a Steel Sky, I'd recommend doing that first. It's available for free and runs on just about any device with ScummVM. "Beyond" has a nice balance of jokes and call-backs without being drowned in nostalgia. Several of the callbacks made me laugh out loud.I did encounter a few bugs, and needed to quit and reload once or twice to get things moving again. Sometimes it tries to hold your hand a bit too much (like, not allowing you to initiate the interview until you've looked at the right page of MINOS to identify a Ministry. I had made notes of the symbols of each ministry before I even got into the city, so I didn't need to do that! Argh.)
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: A classical Narrative driven linear puzzle/adventure game. It was a refreshing change of pace from more modern styles of game design. The narrative is solid with only a few cringe points, and the sense of humor is mostly on point. The puzzles can range to moderately simple to challenging due to the solutions being abstract and/or multi-layered. There is an optional clue system to help you avoid getting stuck,  it starts with a small hint and works up to almost walking you through the puzzle.  The games visual aren't mind blowing or anything but I appreciated the comic book aesthetic.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: A very good game. I do wish it was longer so Joey and Foster got to interact more. (You'll get it later) I do wish Foster got more time to be emotional and meet the other Ministers sooner too. Mostly just small story blips I found strange, but I understand there's a scope to maintain. All in all it was a refreshing Utopian Distopia game with a very charming premise and adventure. Really my only main complaint is how Foster did Joey dirty for 10 years and they just brushed it off. At the end I really felt like Foster was just brushing off any responsibility he had to the city or Joey himself. :/
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I love this sequel to Beneath Steel Sky.A brilliantly written adventure, set in and around the dystopian Union City.Robert Foster and Joey return to rescue a missing child. full of well-crafted witty dialogue, puzzles and non linear storyline,Cool graphics and a very addictive narrative style point and click gameplay,with fun-to-solve puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I found myself using online walkthroughs for much of the game. Many solutions are not at all easy to piece together. This is not a stealth, combat, collect things, side quests, etc sort of game. Instead, there is a great deal of dialogue and interaction of the point and click variety. The story is on the light side of the scale. The cut scenes increased as the game progressed. However, I enjoyed playing it. The voice acting was good and so was the city world where almost all of the story takes place. There is zero replayability.  60/100
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: "Beyond a Steel Sky" is an outstanding continuation of its 1994 predecessor, "Beneath a Steel Sky". With fantastic graphics and gameplay, the game is highly immersive and addictive. I met "Beneath a Steel Sky" this year and played it just before "Beyond a Steel Sky", and I believe that the sensation of the gamers that knew "Beneath..." since its release, with this fantastic continuation, must have been indescribable! Revolution has definitely gone over the top with this sequel! My grade for the game is 10!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest, as a fan of the original I wasn't expecting this to be any good, but I gave it a try nonetheless.I'm happy to say that it lives up to Beneath a Steel Sky, of course some things change because of the change to 3D but it definitely keeps the spirit alive and I had a lot of fun playing it despite some minor technical issues. I'm going to mention just eh one that broke the experience completely for me:- Character collisions. They don't resolve collisions at all, if suddenly you collide with a character, instead of trying to move around, go back or find another way to go to where they're supposed to be, they will just push forward, pinning you in a location MANY times and making you unable to move, which ends in having to restart the game to be able to continue, that got me really angry.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Overall great game! If you like oldschool adventure games you will not be dissapointed.The puzzles are on a good level and the story and phasing is good troughout the game.The characters are pretty great except for the main character who just comes of as an annoying ♥♥♥♥.The biggest downside of the game is that it drops a reference to one of the dankest vines ever.... but it does it at the completely wrong place and time to work effectively.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Great story with well thought out characters, great voice dialogue and voice acting, graphics were good - not over the top.  The world and society in which this story takes place in was well created.  The puzzles were very much in line with the story and not out of place puzzles for puzzles sake.  They were not difficult but still fun to solve.  I very much enjoyed this game.  While there were some story plot holes and inconsistencies everything was still very cohesive.  Most games with high production values skimp on the story and characters and invest everything into graphics - this game does not.  They achieved a good balance among the various elements that make for a very fun, enjoyable, and appealing game.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely a worthy successor. LOTS of callbacks, with an ending that goes bittersweet-preachy-downer-meh. Interesting concept, well told, with a twist that you can see coming if you pay attention to the dialogue throughout. Definitely recommend, although TBTH the 3rd person gameplay really adds nothing to the adventure-game genre xD. Keyboard controls felt totally unneccessary. The fact that is the ONLY word of caution I have for you should be a good sign about the overall quality!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: If you played the original, then you will want to play the sequel, plenty of throw backs etc to wet the appetite with. If you didn't play the original, it's available free on Steam, but it's still a game worth playing, you just might not appreciate some of the nuances as much. It's been refreshing to play a good old school point and click adventure but with that modern twist, though there is a tiny part of me that would love to have seen a 2D platform version, but that's neither here nor there really. There's some replayability, without being bombarded with an infinite amount of endings and the added dev commentary is a nice touch so long as you took in the story/conversations first time around. I hope this game becomes successful enough for a third installment somewhere down the line... Oh and THANK YOU for staying away from a DLC model (for now 29/07/21). 5* 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Wow... Just finished playing through Beyond a Steel Sky and I have to say that it was an incredible experience.I didn't pay full price but I can say that after finishing it the game is well worth it even without a discount, for a 15 to 20 hour story drive game it ticks all the boxes.Really hoping that they make a sequel and I feel that there is enough there the creators to do this.Fantastic, please make more!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: (Warning lazily formatted text block ahead!)Usually when it comes to sequels, especially sequels that are release so long after the first part, I have very low expectations.I have very little to complain about the graphics; I'm not fond of the cel-shader, but in this game it was, ahem, quite adequate.Soundwise the game also holds its own. Only thing to complain about stems from a purely audio production nerd kind of place; I noticed that some of the ADR was a bit mismatched tonally, sometimes an EQ (or perhaps a mic) was mismatched, other times the accoustics or post processing, but then again, this seems to happen with most games with lots of voice-over.The puzzles in the game range from very easy to "Oh come on!", the latter namely being the last QDos-puzzle which I will spoil for you here:  I was expecting some sort of semi-complex maths puzzle, or something.One little irritant for me was the Milo-part of the game. I had totally forgotten about Milo and why I should even care, so at the reuinion I was a bit "Meh", can't we keep mucking about in the city a little longer? :-) Maybe a flashback or dream sequence in the middle of the game to refresh why we are so adamant to get to him. Maybe I was just smitten with Orana and forgot all about kids. :-)And lastly, the hack-tool had so much more potential for fun, but that road was not taken. Sure it was fun hacking all the signs and what not, but there could have been more, like opening secret areas (there might have been, but I missed it) and getting an achievement for extracting 100+ soda cans (Yep, I tried that one), or something.This review from a guy who played Beneath A Steel Sky on the Amiga back when it was released and has that memory incorporated in his spine.Verdict:Nice game; Get it, if not for nostalgia, then just because it's a decent game, and if you haven't played Beneath a Steel Sky; Geez, go play that one first, it's a classic, and the lore will be useful in Beyond a Stel Sky.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I played the first original game, despite it being so many years ago,  I enjoyed the first very much and to be truthful, did not expect to enjoy this as much as the 1st...  Well I was proven wrong.  I did enjoy this a lot, it took me a bit of time to get used to the way things worked, but it did bring back some memories of the first one.  The graphics were pretty good (despite seeing inside Foster at times!!!!), one part was shockingly funny,  This does get you to think what you are doing and sometimes without realising, it does drop hints on your next move sometimes.  It's a pleasant game,  If you ever played the 1st one, then I think you will LOVE this one, this is also great for the ones who have never played the first game.  I prefer point and click games and would highly recommend this game.  I thoroughly enjoyed working out each stage and interacting with the other characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Simple, non complicated, straight forward game - similar to games like Dreamfall and Grim Fandango. The story is good, has a very straight forward and linear playthough, with a good ending. Worth playing if you enjoy chill games with puzzles, nice visuals and a good Hints system to guide you. There are occasional bugs, but nothing major or too troublesome. I would recommend this game at a discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I put more then 8 hours into this game. Probably like 13 or 14. All in all I enjoyed it. I've played the original about 10 times so I was familiar with some of the games terms/references I guess you could say. I wish it would have been a little more expansive to say, although the original was a point and click adventure, and this although still sort of the same did have more of explorative aesthetic to it. A full on open world Beyond A Steel Sky would be sweet though. Maybe even some sort of expansion/dlc in the future. I may have some achievements I can go back and complete, but I'll save all that for later. Maybe they can come back and kidnap the Milos kid or something and then we can have another go. lol!! A++ :)
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original when I was a kid and I was very dubious about returning to something lodged deeply in nostalgia, was also wary about it being a more modern 3D approach. Thankfully all my doubts were unfounded as the game is just absolutely fantastic. Great puzzles, great storytelling, just a great adventure that feels both modern but also a beautiful tribute to my point and click childhood. Also I don't think the screenshots do justice to how great the visual style of the game is, with a great comic book feel throughout. Great to see Revolution doing what they do best.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: As a massive fan of the original, I was a little worried going into this...I needn't have been! Beyond A Steel Sky is a respectful, rich and intelligent new chapter which moves the story we started in the original along nicely.Excellent puzzles (though not tooooo challenging!) and some new mechanics, plus a continuation of things like LINCSpace give an overall cosy feeling to this dark allegory on some of the less excellent aspects of human nature, control and societal engineering.The few bugs I encountered were by no means game breaking: - NPCs have a tendency to get in the way, and can also end up playing unexpected cameos in key dialog - Camera clipping is an issue.. I kept seeing fosters disembodied teeth when the camera was too close - Some of the MINOS screens do not work great with a controller (I'm looking at you, lab control console!)Overall an excellent game - can't wait to see where the story goes next!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: For people who have played the game this one is based on (with it's pixel graphics charme) this game here brings back memories in a totally new full 3D cell shaded comic look. You meet old friends, make your way through some scenes of that big automated city again, being on the hunt once again for a yet unknown conspiracy.Puzzle design is of middle level difficulty, sometimes you have to interact with things you thought you'd already know a second time to trigger some story progess, or try every kind of interaction possible to accidentally get the one which pushes you further. But mostly fair.Technically I had to lower the graphics settings from extreme to high for my RX 580 to not let it overheat for a longer time on a level of about 70 to 80 degrees celsius, but have a bearable level of about 50 to 60 degrees celsius (It's a cel shaded environment anyhow, so you don't lose too much detail by doing it). Sometimes some NPCs tend to get stuck in some areas, so when that happens you better have a savegame ready, since you can't kick NPCs free of their miserable locations, and regular savegaming strongly recommended to avoid stuck NPC situations.Only the humour is a bit different and not necessary omnipresent, though where funny things happen they make you 'whow, what? yeah, ookay, haha!'. And the things you can interact seem not always deliver something worth for story or atmosphere. But that's criticism on high level, all in everything the game does things right.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: Bloody good little game. It feels like a solid sequel to the original while making it a bit more modern in design. Sometimes not ideal since the interaction points move with people and objects and that can make it hard to access at times but that's about the only thing I can think of as a negative.Oh and they pronounce 'aluminium' correctly! That's reason enough to buy it
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: I remember playing beneath a steel sky as a kid back in the 90's and it left me with a taste for dystopian fiction with its strong narrative and likeable characters. The sequel 20+ years in the making was worth the wait, in my opinion. Its narrative is strong and provides us with multiple interesting characters that are a pleasure to interact with. There are plenty of nods back to beneath a steel sky and good amounts of humor and dark moments making it perfectly balanced in its setting. The ending also got to me in no small way.There are a few minor technical issues such as the occasional FPS drop but then again I'm running it on near ultra on a somewhat old PC. Overall, the art style, the story, the characters and the choices are fantastic and I thoroughly recommend playing the game and its prequel if you have a love for dystopian and utopian fiction.I hope some day to return to Union city again for another adventure as it is one of the more unique settings in post apocalypse futures in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond a Steel Sky

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first ever fully immersive 3D game I've ever played that follows the game mechanics of classical point & click style adventure games. I was hoping for something new, but was completely gobsmacked by what this game offers. It's easy to become completely absorbed into the story, because it's both captive, well worked out and very beautiful.
