_childDocuments_.review: Behind a thin layer of humor is a story about politics and the media's role in it. You're asked to editorialize and shape a narrative that has substantial impact on how the story unfolds. Is it moral to censor this? Is it safe to release this footage to the public? These are questions you're asked to answer, and your answers have consequences. The game does some leg work to make both sides justifiable options, but I feel like some of the ways they got there felt a bit unfair at times. The developers ultimately seemed to want to avoid letting their personal beliefs seep too far into the narrative, but you can definitely tell they're trying to work around them. The player will need to take a step back at times and objectively analyze a situation to fully understand it, because the game will frequently frame things in ways that tell you how to feel about them. Maybe that's just meta-commentary on what you're doing in game, but if it is then I feel like it's something lost on people in a lot of the discussion around this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Not For Broadcast assumes you in the role of a backstage TV operator. Flick through screens, censor swear words, make sure everything runs smoothly. An important detail to note is that the game only has 3 "stages" right now, with more being added later. Even so, I still feel like this is a project well worth contributing to.While the gameplay is reminiscent of Papers, Please, what with your behavior changing the story in several ways, the aesthetics is really the greatest strength of Not For Broadcast. I myself have a knack for british humour and television, and this show not only makes fun of, but also embraces it fully. There were scenes that had me laughing audibly whilst trying to maintain my focus of the gameplay.The gameplay is rough, but works well enough. There's a lot to keep your eyes on, and unfortunately this means that it can be hard to appreciate the well-edited newsclips while you're playing. Sure, you can watch these later, but because there's currently no way to scroll through these, you have to watch them all over in real time, with no way of skipping forwards. But once again, it really is the aesthetics and athmosphere that shine the brightest. The personalities of the cast, the absurd british humour, it's all there and it's beautiful.Overall I feel that there are some necessary additions that need to be made:- A way to control clips in the archives, like a fast-forward, slow-down, etc.- A better hint at what to do when - Probably a minor thing, but all the names in the credits have the exact same font and size as their titles (Director, Programmer, etc.) which is a little jarring to look at.These nitpicks are minor, however, and I really did enjoy the game a lot. It's a brilliant idea, executed incredibly geniunely. Looking forward to more content.

_childDocuments_.review: Picked this up because I love FMV. Sadly, not one I could recommend (although I'll likely play to the end). The gameplay and concept are probably the game's strongest elements. The mix between FNAF's technological multitasking and Papers Please's governmental bureaucracy proves pretty fun - although some segments are a bit slow and some a bit overwhelming, there was never a moment where I was done with the gameplay itself. However, the FMV - the writing, acting, set design - that's where the game really ♥♥♥♥♥ the bed. I get that this is an indie project, but most of the actors feel more like youtubers doing a cameo than actors playing a role - even the lead anchorman spends most of his time doing a B- impression of David Mitchell. The humor itself is fun at times, but often obnoxiously "epic random", and the nature of the game means that several gags just go on way too long.There's massive mood swings too - the "off camera" sequences, when you're offered some choices in your day-to-day life, have no comedy in them whatsoever. You wrap up a news show where a man in a gimp suit falls out of someone's closet, and then go home to your dementia-ridden grandmother and truant son. I'm writing this review after finishing the "lockdown special", which manages to go on for entirely too long, feel dated, and unfunny - not leaving me in a great headspace.I'm only two hours into the campaign, so take this review with a grain of salt. Maybe the game really picks up near the end, and I end up loving it. Either way, only pick this up if you can handle some really, outrageously bad acting and writing - yes, that's below the standards of an FMV game.(P.S: Why is this like 60 gigabytes? Do you think they could've compressed the footage a bit more?)

_childDocuments_.review: It's very rare that I've had a game have such a wide emotional range, but Not For Broadcast absolutely brought me to tears with both laughter and sadness. Definitely a satire on the same ranks as Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy or Fahrenheit 451. The main cast is also brilliant, with Megan and Jeremy absolutely killing it in every scene they are in. _childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game's mechanics and pace. However there are some issues with the content that make playing it kind of a bummer.The narrative's reliance on hacky, sometimes offensive comedy tropes weakens what could be a really groundbreaking experience. I think these tropes also hinder the game's message, so far as one can be discerned (as the game tends toward ridiculing whoever it can). In the first three game segments, we have:	1. A group of stereotypical theater kids. Included are a preening, flamboyant young man, a vapid, self-obsessed blonde, an over-eager social justice warrior type, and an intellectually disabled young man whose inability to navigate a sleeve is played for cheap laughs. 	2. A black man, recently released from prison, offering systemic critiques of the justice system while partying with strippers and a mariachi band. 	3. Government programs funding the arts and infrastructure are depicted as stupid or vaguely sinister boondoggles. I just think in 2020 this sort of writing is lazier than it needs to be. It's especially glaring in light of the narrative's strengths. The game, through its mechanics and narrative, reveals that those who work in media often have a financial incentive to portray individuals and organizations in a positive or negative light. The game's politics are often cute enough to carry the weaker segments; the recently dispossessed rich are played up as spoiled toffs with stupid accents, government critics are depicted as philanderers and police advocates hypocrites, celebrity politicians are liars and drunks. The news anchors are satisfyingly snide and self-absorbed. This is a real highlight of the experience for me. I genuinely like parts of this game so much, it's a real pain in my ass to sit through jokes that would've been stale in the 90s. ("Math's really important!" "Okay [intellectually disabled young man]. " "Math's really important!" "Yeah okay [intellectually disabled young man].") I also feel like, if I were disabled, or a person of color, I'd probably be doing more than wincing through these segments.At the end of the released Early Access segments, the devs say they read these reviews, that they read everything. To be clear, the game does have some aspects I think are thoughtful. These include gender neutral names for the protagonist and their partner, a consistently scathing take on capitalist consumerism, captains of industry (Sophia Remmington is a great Elon Musk stand-in), and sports culture, and some laugh out loud funny bits of banter among the news crew. The game also manages to spoof the stupid way the media portrays scientific endeavors. My intent isn't to cancel this game, whatever that would mean. I do think, though, the devs maybe haven't considered these angles, or if they have, dismissed them too quickly. Maybe it's too late to influence the writing- some segments clearly have already been filmed and I am excited to watch those, to be honest- but after playing through the game so far several times, I came away feeling a little icky, and I felt like I had to express why. Hopefully the devs can dig that. I am looking forward to where this is going.

_childDocuments_.review: Not For Broadcast is easily one of the best, and most promising, FMV games that I’ve experienced in quite some time. And it’s not even completed yet.IntroNot For Broadcast is a unique FMV based game to puts you in the role of a person running the National Nightly News broadcast. The game is largely a satirical parody of the news and many political topics. It’s quite humorous and is spot-on in its satirization. If this sounds like a game that you’d be interested in, do read on, it’s quite fascinating.StoryThe story to Not For Broadcast takes place in the 1980s when a radical party is sworn in as president of the country. The new party vows to take money from the rich and eliminate poverty with it but your actions in the game determine how the public views the new party and the people that show up in the game’s scenes.Currently, there’s around 3 hours worth of content to experience but this will increase drastically as the game continues its development. It’s also worth mentioning that if you get offended easily, this game probably isn’t for you because it satirizes everything you can possibly think of when it comes to politics. I personally found it quite hilarious and enjoyed it quite a lot.GameplayAt first the game seems kind of daunting, what with all the buttons and actions you have to use/take. In reality, it’s actually quite easy to learn but tough to master. The game features a pretty in-depth tutorial at the beginning of the game where your predecessor walks you through the various buttons to make it easy.Before the news begins, you must first power up the machine and then select the adverts you wish to feature in the broadcast. Once this is done, the news begins and you must use the buttons on the left to select the screen you wish to show during the broadcast. The actual broadcast runs 2 seconds slower than the one you must edit so you must make your choices fairly quickly. There are also sections where you must censor any swears that the people on the screen say. There are also sections where you will need to avoid interference in a mini-game of sorts on the right monitor. You use a dial to move the dot up and down to avoid the green sections of interference.Once the day is completed your results are tallied and you earn money based on your performance. You can then use this money to purchase upgrades and new equipment for your studio. There are also cosmetic toys to buy to spruce up your surroundings as well.There are also story elements mixed in with the gameplay as well where your choices affect your character’s personal life. These are currently done in a sort of visual novel style setup with art showing up on a nearby TV and you must read the text and make your decision from the choices given. Some choices have pretty major consequences so choose carefully.The ArchiveWhenever you finish a day’s broadcast you’re immediately taken to the archive section where you can watch the entire broadcast that you just made your way through, check out the many humorous ads that you featured in past broadcasts, and even see behind the scenes during commercial breaks.VerdictOverall, this game had me laughing out loud on numerous occasions and I thoroughly enjoyed my time with it. I’m quite excited to see how the game improves over the course of its continued development and I wish the developers luck in their endeavours. If you’re a fan of FMV games as much as I am, this is definitely one to keep an eye on.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine your life as a TV news editor/censor in dystopian England. Now imagine that world with the same humor as Monty Python. The game is actually full of gameplay and it’s not just some weird interactivity so it can be excused as a game. Without mastering the controls and gameplay loop you won’t get very far at all. You sit at a desk with six monitors in front of you and it’s your job to either censor the rebels or the government. Your choices will determine who lives and dies and affect your own personal life.You start with basic controls and the game doesn’t get too crazy at first. There are four monitors that can be switched between numbers 1-4 and there are green, orange, and red LEDs under each one. The next monitor is the live camera and the last monitor is the delayed broadcast that the people see. You can adjust the volume for each of these broadcasts. On your far left are the power and switches for each board you control. These are only used at the start of each chapter to turn everything on or during certain sequences to mess up your broadcast. On the far right is usually nothing outside of an occasional thing and underneath the desk are video tapes you must load during commercial breaks. It’s important to play some and not others which affects your pay and ranking. Advance is the government tapes and Disrupt are the rebels. It’s important to play the Advance tape during the second break to get max points.Your main job will be flicking between cameras when the green LEDs light up. Certain shows will only have one fixed camera and you can’t stay on that camera for more than ten seconds or the audience will get bored. You can flick to an orange camera for a few seconds to mix things up, but flick to a red camera, and your ratings drop. Things get tricky later on when people go off script and there are multiple people talking. You also have to watch your censor meter. When people cuss you have to press space during the red segments or your ratings drop fast. Later on, you can censor the Disrupt pro-talk with blue waves or censor Advance pro-government talk with orange waves. The last meter you need to watch is your broadcast signal. This can be adjusted with the mouse wheel once it starts going out of sync. Later on, you can tune in to a Disrupt broadcast for an anti-government playthrough by following the orange waves instead of the white ones.While that’s the basic gameplay there are some other things added later like audience reactions and during songs you can flick the cameras to the beat of the song for a rating boost (which is really hard and doesn’t ever seem on the beat). You really need to focus and watch those LED colors as they’re the main thing you will watch. Sometimes you can be pro-government or anti-government by keeping the camera on certain subjects or even loading tapes from Disrupt in certain chapters. It’s up to you to censor the people’s voices or play along.The game is constantly engaging and you never get bored. This gameplay loop sounds fun, but it wouldn’t matter if the content you’re watching is boring. Thankfully, it’s utterly brilliant. The humor is very much along the lines of Monty Python. One broadcast segment has you editing a sports match of people tossing an invisible ball into a trash can. It’s hilarious. Another scene has a reporter, Patrick Banon, not realize he’s live on the air spewing anti-government remarks, his camera woman steps in for him, but Megan Wolfe (the female news anchor and one of the main characters) calls her Patrick Banon to cover everything up. She is now Patrick Banon throughout the rest of the game like no one would know. But it’s all played off like it’s half-serious. The writing is just perfect and I couldn’t stop playing the game to see more of the humor rather than find out if Advance would get overthrown or not.There are many mockeries of real-life people and events. There’s a COVID-19 pandemic segment in which killer dolls are breaking out of a facility and everyone has to stay in lockdown. There are celebrity mockeries of Chef Gordan Ramsey, Ariana Grande, Donald Trump, and some that could be a swath of other politicians or celebrities. There are so many characters, skits, and segments, even the commercials are hilarious and you can easily miss them if you don’t turn the volume up on the delayed broadcast. Of course, there are elements that are thrown in like killer dolls attacking the studio and you need to click on them before they shut things off, a heatwave that causes equipment to shut down, as well as flickering cameras, and controls that lock up. You will be very entertained during the 9-10 hours it takes to get through one playthrough.There’s also a second part of the storytelling that I can’t tell if it’s done on purpose or not. You play through a total of seven years as a broadcast editor, but the in-between segments are text-based and shown over what looks like low-budget asset flip-style graphics that you would see on a rip-off Steam game. It’s a stark contrast from the excellent writing and acting, but I think it’s done this way on purpose. You do make a few choices in these segments that affect how your family perceives you. Responding to your daughter or wife a certain way. Your success in being pro-government gives you more money and gives you an easier life which reflects in these segments. I never got attached to myself, Alex, or my family as it just felt like interludes.With that said, Not for Broadcast is an insanely well-written FMV game with a fun gameplay loop that is easy to learn, but tough to master if you want good ratings. I love the branching paths and the replay value is very high as there are entire skits that you won’t see based on your choices. Every actor is great and especially the character Jeremy Donaldson. He’s a fantastic character and is wonderful to see on screen. I love how you can rewatch the segments and mute each camera to hear what went on in the background while another shot was being broadcasted. Members arguing in the studio in the background is always fun to see. I just wish the checkpoints were closer together. This really hurts the game a bit as some chapters are up to an hour long and you must rewatch for up to 20 minutes to get back to where you failed. I also wanted to jump in at any checkpoint to replay a segment to see the alternative footage, but due to the choices needed in previous chapters, you have to replay the game again each time. For what it’s worth, this is one of the best indie games to come out in recent years and revolutionizes the FMV-style game.

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely write reviews for games, but something about this one struck a chord.When I first saw this game on Steam during the Lunar New Year sale, I didn't really take a good look at the descriptions or screenshots. I assumed it would be a looping, arcade-style game about controlling a broadcast that gets harder every couple of minutes. Something I'd play for a couple of hours each day, but nothing more.Boy was I wrong.First, let me say this. This game is 100% worth the price. While the main story is only 6 hours, there are  you can unlock and a bonus broadcast at the end of the game. The replayability is simply fantastic, and this game could keep you entertained for weeks, if you went through the story, picked different options, , etc. This game has so many variations that you could easily watch a full playthrough on YouTube, buy the game, play it, and not have the experience ruined. Provided you don't watch a playthrough with all the endings.The game does an excellent job of getting you attached to some characters, and making you despise others. Some characters have you going back and forth in how you feel about them like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ metronome. One thing that amazed me is the acting. You might not have heard of any of the actors, but they do a damn good job. They truly made all the news programmes that you control feel . There was rarely a point where I felt like I was playing a game.I seriously cannot praise this game enough. And my praise doesn't do the game justice. Buy the game. .

_childDocuments_.review: Got this game for 50% on the latest Steam sales. Previously added it because Papers Please is one of my all times favourite and this game has similar mechanics. I hesitated due to the game being Early Access but the deal was too good to pass.I had a blast during the first chapter, which includes the first 3 levels of the planned 10 levels. The game premise is unique with innovative gameplay. I quickly got immersed myself in the broadcast, the editing and the mechanics. I liked the actors and the british humor, which for me is not always guaranteed. Let me expand on this.The game has a lot of acting, a lot of FMV. The actors do a hell of a job here, obviously far from movie level, but it looks professional and their commitment and motivation shows. In general their acting is better than in some low TV productions..British Humour is not really my cup of tea and often misses the mark for me. For example, I had watched some Monty Python movies and found them boring. However, there are exceptions, like the Red Dwarf TV series, and in Not for Broadcast I found the British Humour acceptable and the sketches were funny. There are multiple references to modern popular culture.You should know that the game Early access development was severely affected by the COVID19 crisis. The devs had to cancel shooting for Chapter 2 and instead released a bonus chapter (The lockdown update) which is basically made from quarantine. It is an admirable effort and in a way it shows their dedication, but the outcome was bad and it really shows when you compare to Chapter 1.The game needs plenty of polish, which is expected from a title in Early Access. In their statement they wrote, back in January 2020, that they expect at least 18 months of development before the game is complete and I think it will take them much longer given the current circumstances.In retrospective, it could have been better to wait until this game is out of Early Access as right now it just offer a few hours of gameplay, even if they are very good. I will probably revisit the title by then.In the meantime I do recommend this game as long as you do not mind the Early Access status.

_childDocuments_.review: I never write reviews, however I had quite a few thoughts on this one. I hope the devs can read and maybe respond.I really recommend this game, even if you don't think you are interested in the genre. It's just the right amount of challenge for me, the actors are personable, funny, and similar to real life, and there are many realistic features. I also like the fact that you can replay any past broadcast you've done as if you are a viewer, and it's satisfying to pull off some great shots. I also like the political side of the game, and the amount little details are crazy (e.g. what people say off shot in the 'rushes', which are the four camera feeds you can choose from to broadcast)I'm also really thankful for the simplified life mechanics. I never likes similar 'life' games (e.g. Papers Please) because for me at least the economic part of the game is too detailed. Although it's still present in this game, you don't have to manage it down to the dollar.I saw a few other reviews complaining about the size (40gb as of this review) however it's fully justifiable due to the sheer amount of quality video in the game.One word of warning however (and the reason I have to stop playing :'( ) is the performance. I thought this game would be easy enough to run, thinking 'it's based around one scene and a few videos, I can definitely run it on my integrated graphics' (yes I read the requirements but thought to try it anyway). No. This game is actually quite detailed, and up to 6 feeds running at a time can put too much of a strain on my system (8GB, integrated UHD 620, i3-8145-U, potato amirite) so after a point I had too many crashes and game-breaking video stutters to play normally. I would have hoped to see more graphics options, however the ones already present (setting video to half res, shadows etc) were helpful to an extent. Don't think this will affect most of you with graphics cards, but I am sure there will be a few similar to me on laptops that I don't want to disappoint. I'm not blaming this on the devs, just I really wanted to try this game out. As a result I won't be refunding and am very hopeful for more to come in the future. I can't really express how much I really recommend it. Buy it now, worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: I have to say that this game is awesome and different from every other game I have ever seen.First, it shows how broadcasting works and the influence that the TV has on people, depending on their interests."Not for Broadcast" is surprisingly well made (so far on chapter 1). It already delivers:- Well written and funny storyline, which also gives food for thought, mainly on politics, where at the same time, makes fun and parodies of certain types of people and beliefs, showing openly characters' hipocrisy;- Your choices (commercials, pictures chosen, etc) influence the news to come, so it already has replay value, as different broadcasts can be seen on each playthrough based on previous days;- A kind of "Papers, Please" personal style of life choices, where you are always on pressure by all the possible choices you have, and all of them may or may not have greater consequences in the future (You can already see some on chapter 1, if you play multiple times).- Nice and engaging gameplay. I don't know exactly if broadcasts work on that way, or that the broadcast professional really controls all those variables to call it something near a "TV Simulator", but I imagine it has the main aspects of how broadcasts are controlled on air.For me, it is visible that a lot of effort is being put on this game development. It has great and spontaneous actors who perform naturally. It is really funny to watch the commercials and the details of all the parts that "shouldn't" be broadcasted, as it shows the real nature, problems, opinions of the characters and how two-faced all of them are in front of the cameras. So even on that, they have dedicated to make it look like real.Those are my opinions so far. I will come back to update once we have more content.

_childDocuments_.review: I randomly bumped into this game during a sale, It looked rather interesting and i saw little to nothing about it so i said "Why not" and gave it a shot. A political party has recently been elected and it's up to you to sway public opinion while also managing a personal life with your family.Gameplay: Being Channel 1's broadcaster comes with a load of responsibilities. You are tasked with Commercial Breaks, Dueling against signal disruptions via minigame, Bleeping swears, and showing what is currently being broad casted to the public by changing cameras on points of interest. After work is over you're given a Text Adventure esque experience in which you're given a situation in which you're given a situation that requires your input, Your choices don't have immediate effects but i imagine further down development such things will come true.Current State of Updates: For new buyers due to recent world events updates may not come as commonly or as large as one may wish, But please have patience the developers are trying there very best to push out content to make all of us happy! And as soon as things go back to a safe state production will continue as originally planned on there road map. Rating: 10/10Note: As of writing the game is rather light on content though has a fair replayability factor. I feel that this game is a worthy investment of your time and money especially when it's fully released.

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't a game: this is a story. You're in the story. You're controlling the story. Now you've ♥♥♥♥♥♥ everything up and ruined the world, good job, I hope you're proud of yourself.I have never felt so in control in a game like this before. Never before have I felt genuinely guilty for my choices in a game.The writing is exceptional. It achieves some impossible balance between (particularly British!) hilarity and heaviness. "It was like a rollercoaster" is a terrible cliché that doesn't even come close to it. No, one minute I was feeling great, the next I'd be feeling like the worst person to have ever been birthed, and another ten seconds later laughing at funny silly sofa selling man.I wish I hadn't played this game. I wish I hadn't played it, so I could open it up, and play it afresh, all over again, making the same silly choices I did over and over again. On the other hand, I want to go back. Make different choices. It's a feeling of genuine regret. I know, I know I could just start a new save. But I don't want to start a new save. I want to go back. To actively unmake choices I made in that first naive play-through.The gameplay itself can be a little stressful (what more could you have really expected given your job in the game!), but there is the option to enable/disable certain parts of the gameplay to make things more manageable if you so wish.There is also a lot of reading, much like those story books where you'd have to turn to different pages depending on your choices, but it really helps expand the story. There are - at time of me writing this - 9 broadcasts in the main story, a tenth broadcast which "isn't canon" but you still play through as a part of the main story, and an 11th bonus broadcast- plus the broadcast get longer and longer as the game progresses, so there is plenty of actual unique hands-on content.In my opinion, this game humbles every other entry in this genre. Deeply humbles them, too. If you're "thinking about buying it, but not sure", stop thinking, start buying. You absolutely will not regret it. I cannot put into words how much I loved this game. I always expected I was going to enjoy the game- I'm currently at university studying broadcast tech, after all- but never in a million years did I expect it to hit as hard as it did. Truly, a masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: Just to be clear: This game is very, very short right now. My time shows 9.4 hours, but 5 of those were idling, and I have  completed the game. There seems to be a lot of replayability, but it is still very short. Additionally, this is an early access game with apparently very huge ambitions in terms of the story, so be prepared that it might never get fully resolved.So far, there is little more than the tutorial.The game is very strange and has a large amount of humor mixed into it. I honestly don't love the constant humor and slapstick, but it is funny. I would have rather had a game that focuses on the very serious subject matter of an impending dictatorship, but I suppose it goes into the British way of things with the humor.The actual gameplay is incredible. It's very similar to Papers, Please in terms of the complexity of completing many tasks at once, focusing on a lot of different things, and trying to get it done well. There's a clear inspiration from Papers, Please. The game has a great bit of difficulty, but it feels like you can really get into it with skill.I'd recommend this as is. It's a good, creative, and unique game.

_childDocuments_.review: A very well done game. Choices actually matter and make a huge difference. Split second decisions have consequences that are either immediate or will have ramifications very late into the game. There is actual replay-ability because As far as choice matters games are concerned, this one is easily in the top 3. Keep in mind that every choice you make matters - even the ones that are presented in a different way compared to the broadcast room. This one is not explicitly stated in-game, perhaps intentionally. I also liked the acting and the actors as well, the story is very well written. It starts off a bit cliche, but it becomes its own thing towards the end.  It does make for a compelling tale. The game-play is a bit mixed. It starts off innocent enough, then there is a bit in the middle of the game that is so annoying it could make you just drop the game and never return.  However the game picks right back up after that hump and is mostly an enjoyable experience after that. And if the difficulty is at any point a hang-up for anyone, the difficulty is very customizable and achievements are not affected even you choose to play a game with all mechanics turned off.Overall it's a great game in terms of both story and game-play. It has flaws, but it is a game worth full price. The game is long if you go through it once, and it could be massive if you decide to replay it multiple times.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, first of all, thank you to all the producers and people that took part in the making of this game.I am absolutely mind blown!The concept is really something out of the box! I have never played anything similar to this.You are basically the editor for a news channel, covering interviews in a variety of subjects. Your job consists in choosing the best cameras, bleeping out swear words, cut off images not suited for the audience, and even avoid interference to have the best image.Surrounding all this concept, you have an amazing story being developed, in which you take direct part, as you have control over the feed you pass on to the audience.Lots of choices to be made, not only "professionaly", but also at home, as the story also goes there, waiting on you to take the decisions you think are the best to choose from.The acting is really over the top! _childDocuments_.review: The game is an absolute masterpiece. There is so much I wanna say but a lot of it will spoil the game. I'm gonna keep this review spoiler free. To start with, this game has one of the best stories I have seen in a game in a long time. The world building, characters, and just everything story wise is perfect. There are 14 endings as well. These ending are not just slight changes from each other easy. They are completely different from each other. This game is also very easy to learn but can but is also hard to master. It is very replayable as well since you will not get to see everything on your first playthrough. I am currently at the beginning of my second playthrough and am still having a blast playing it. The are some things that will happen in the studio to make it harder, but if your not a fan of that and just wanna focus on the story and not have to worry about losing audience and other hazards, then there is a mode with that disabled (although I would not recommend it as iit takes part of the fun out of the game). Some choices in the game are very difficult to make as well. You might find yourself questioning if you made the right decision after you make it. It will also leave you wondering what would have happen if you chose differently. The soundtrack is also amazing as well. One cool thing is that every ending has different music in the credits (From what I have seen so far). The humor in this game is also really good. _childDocuments_.review: I may not have finished this game yet, but holy cow is it amazing. Where do I even start? I suppose first I'll ease anybody's worries about the gameplay seeming repetitive or lacking replay value, as I would argue that the game featuring a lot of the same systems throughout it is a bonus, as you get to improve your skills as you go, or choose to go back to a previous Day and try again. Also I must say the moral tests and things that game presents is insane, I felt so absorbed and enthralled the entire time, unable to take my eyes off the screens as I frantically make sure the signal isn't stuffed up, attempt to listen to what the characters are saying, and all while making sure I get the perfect shots.Speaking of the characters, the acting in this game phenomenal! Cinema-worthy even! So good in fact that sometimes I'm too enthralled to even realise that there's a hoard of dolls climbing up my radio tower, haha! But in all seriousness this game manages to strike an astounding balance between being hilariously witty with it's dark humour, and incredibly intense with it's scenes that throw you off guard.Of course I'm not going to try and spoil anything, but I do immensely recommend that anyone should try this game out. It tests not only your reaction time and multi-tasking skills, but also your morality and beliefs. That replay button that pops up at the end of every section certainly helps to make you wonder......did I make the right decision?
_childDocuments_.name: Not For Broadcast

_childDocuments_.review: I'm glad I gave this a go, and I would love to love it. Honestly I do like it, it's certainly a breath of fresh air with its unique and interesting mechanics. Unfortunately it suffers from not knowing what it's really trying to do. It wants to be political, but doesn't really know what politics it's doing. It wants to be a black comedy, but doesn't know how to balance the humour with the tone. It wants to take influence from, and then subvert Five Nights At Freddy's and Papers Please, but doesn't understand what made those games so easy to get the hang of.It wants to give the player maximum freedom and create emergent gameplay from that, but it gives the player  freedom, in a story which is quite rigid in the ways it can play out. It wants to have lots of buttons and features, but is too quick to throw them out in favour of even more new things to learn. And of course, you don't know if you're doing well. You're just doing, and hoping the mysterious gremlin behind the screens approves of your decisions, without telling you why.The characters are fantastic, and the dialogue is great. But you'll eventually find yourself only playing because you want to see the Nightly News team gossiping behind the scenes, which you'll mostly do between levels watching the tapes back separate from the game itself, since when you're actually playing it's impossible to focus on anything that isn't important in the moment.You can pick sides, but which side do you pick? You won't know because you don't know anything about anyone. You can make choices and all of them seem bad, which would be cool if this was one of those hardcore "you can't win" types, but it really doesn't come across like it's intentional. It just feels like there's too much going on and there wasn't anyone on the development team to say Basically, I think this game should have been less. Much, much less, over a longer period of time. The idea was great, and unfortunately they knew that, and couldn't restrain themselves.I would love to see what else comes from these people, as they're absolutely onto something here, and I'm a sucker for anything that tries something new. I'm glad this game exists, and I don't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the story of a man named Alex. Alex worked for a company in a big building where he was employee #1992. Employee #1992's job was simple: he sat at his desk in room 1992 and he pushed buttons, slid faders, and avoids interference on a control board. Live feeds came to him through a monitor on his desk, suggesting him what buttons to push, how long to push them, and in what order. This is what employee #1992 did every day of every month of every year, and although others might have considered it soul rending, Alex relished every moment that the feeds came in, as though he had been made exactly for this job. And Alex was happy.And then one day, something peculiar happened, something would forever change Alex, something he would never quite forget. He had been at his desk for a long time when he realized that not one, single sense everyone says from the feeds for him to follow. No one had shown up to give him clarifications, call a meeting, or even say hi. Never in all his years at the company had this happened, this complete revelation. Something was very clearly wrong. Shocked, frozen solid, Alex found himself unable to move for the longest time, but as he came to his wits and regained his senses, he puts his foot down and delivers a message.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a weird one. It is a good game, i really liked it, all the mechanics are good (Except the one with the frequencies, that was boring), but i don't really like the message this game gives. They want you to believe that they are simply in the center of the political spectrum, everyone is wrong and the neutral people are the only reasonable ones, but I actually believe that the developers are kinda right-wing or something. The left are portrayed in this cartoony fashion, and they are the baddies, they want to take all the money and give it to everyone, and that's bad! Meanwhile, the right-wing is portrayed simply as dumb and vain people, they are just a group of conspiracy nuts at first, and they want their money back, because they earned it. But as soon as the baddies (left) do something horrible that everyone can agree it's wrong (), the right-wing people become smart, and reasonable, and they are the solution to this autoritative deviants that control everything, and you have to help them, otherwise, they will kill all your family. I don't really care, i'm just roleplaying as a character in this weird world, and i think it's trying to be funny most of the time, but it kinda gives off those vibes. Left bad, right bad, but left worse. I didn't take it too seriously, otherwise, i should be kinda offended. Still, it's a good game most of the time, funny, engaging, good acting, good sets, good music, a lot of attention to detail, etc.

_childDocuments_.review: Really, an amazing game.For the gameplay, it's decent.In the broadcast center, I wouldn't say it's gripping, and it does sometimes get in the way of the experience, but it is engaging. It keeps you occupied, if you're not interested in a segment you can focus more on the management.I've seen people say they dislike the text adventure portion, but I think it's a vital addition. It breaks up the demanding gameplay of the news room, gives you a different, more down-to-earth perspective of the events. It's a bit rough, but it adds to the overall experience for me.The branching narratives are fun and I think well incorporated, I was very curious about what other routes would lead me to.In replaying the game, I've been really impressed with how many branches there are, with 11 endings and many changes between segments throughout the whole game. Repeating segments that you've done before can be uninteresting, but for a first replay there's enough changes to make up for that, and a lot of foreshadowing that you won't have noticed first time around.The acting and the writing are a lot of fun. The actors are genuinely talented, there's a good mix between comedy and satire, and meaning and drama. The main cast are strongly written with their own agendas and history playing into their interactions (jeremy donaldson my beloved).The music! Music can single handedly make me buy a game, and I think its importance in this game is forefront. It's phenomenal. It's got the quality of a professional, with the creativity of an indie. Its eclectic inspiration spreads from tango, to rap, to country, to rock, to musical theatre. There are multiple songs to fit with the various endings you can achieve and they're all an excellent send off to what you experienced. Jason Orbaum did a stellar job with it.Finally, a bit of detail on the story. As a summary, I loved it. It subverted my expectations multiple times. Minor spoilers:

_childDocuments_.review: Of course in early access, not everything will stay the same, whether this will be the visuals or some of the actors who appear. Just reached the end of the game (So far) and very excited for the release of further episodes. If you didn't read the synopsis on the steam page before scrolling down, then here's a summery:Your name is  walk into this empty studio room to clean or something, the landline phone rings, guy quits and leaves you with the baby sitting job.Personally I would walk out but, being a game all about choice, you aren't allowed to walk out, and if you decide to get fired on purpose from something you weren't even assigned to do, it's  meaning you have to start over again (Thankfully not from the very beginning but before a pivotal moment)The game also follows the usual "Sit n' Survive" games, just with a little more relatable real world stress with the need to keep viewer rates up, make sure you've got the right camera on, don't stay on the same camera for too long, mess with the signal, check whether the system's overheating , listening to multiple sounds coming from different feeds, censoring crude language to make sure parents don't sue the news for allowing their "Innocent angel" to overhear something they already use way too much  and other complicated stuff... It's almost like getting a real job, but without the effort of going out and finding one!Something that I think needs to be done for an update is the ability to skip forwards or backwards when reviewing the footage you've already edited and sent out to the gullible masses (Pretty much us) and other filmed footage, and the option to edit the size or transparency of the subtitles, they can sometimes get in the way of options.Other than that, I'm really eager for the next episodes and more of the mechanics, I just hope it won't get too cluttered.

_childDocuments_.review: An incredibly interesting and insightful work about government, family, and choice. I can only imagine the planning that must have gone into the game, and the time spent working on the many different endings. While I have only completed one ending of the game, it is undeniably a fun and engaging game that had me coming back again and again. It balances humor and intensity in a way that would be easy to fumble, and crafts a narrative through line that is maintained both within the "gameplay" and the interstitial segments where the player has to make choices for the main character Alex Winston. While getting all of the endings would be a time intensive and perhaps unreasonable ask, the fact that your choices DO matter gives the player a sense of agency that other games that attempt this branching narrative style fail at. The gameplay is rather easy, even on hard mode, unless you are looking to ace every section, which would likely happen on a second or third playthrough, but engaging. The feeling of cutting together a broadcast is a unique experience, and surprisingly gratifying when done right. Give this game a go if you love story-centric games, and want to experience a unique and interesting story.

_childDocuments_.review: Ooh boy. I originally left a review for this game back in early access, when it only went up to The Lockdown. Since then, the full campaign has come out and with it, a lot to say.TL;DR: Buy it. Gameplay is fun and the story is engaging.!!!THIS REVIEW WILL CONTAIN SPOILERS!!!The following observations are in no particular order. This is more of a stream of consciousness than a review so bear that in mind as well. 1. The writers really stepped up with making Advance more of a gray-area. Previously, the player was given no reason to side with Disrupt as you had seen nothing wrong and their leader was ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Alex Jones. Now, the player is given a pretty tough choice on who to side with... which brings with it a whole slew of new problems. I would like to take a moment to bring up Fallout New Vegas. Yes, I know, quite odd. But in that game you are given pretty good reasons to side with and/or against the major factions. The NCR and the Legion are far from perfect, but in them you can see capacity for good. With Disrupt and Advance... their capacity for good is heavily outweighed by the bad. Advance literally has elderly death camps and has apparently taken over the entire world through nuclear war? While Advance starts off good by redistributing wealth, we are quickly shown that they have a fierce propaganda network, LITERALLY using 1984's Newspeak (cops are now "CCOs" Advance's Hitler Youth type thing is called "The Advance Go-Getters," etc...). Disrupt, on the other hand, wants to bring back the rich and is later revealed to be a puppet organization for a military coup. So the player is left with NO "good" guy to put their full support behind. It really comes off as quite odd. I don't know if this was a thematic choice (more on that later) or just lazy writing. it's just... weird. 2. The themes of this game seem to be a bit over place. At first, it clearly seems to be leaning in the direction of “don’t believe everything that you see,” and “Our worldview is controlled by just a few people.” However, later on in the game it gets ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ crazy. Once the game becomes a parody of the View and Ellen (no I am not kidding, I was shocked playing the last two broadcasts,) it seems to be talking about how there is no true “good” in the world and that everything, no matter how quaint things may seem, have a seedy undertone to it. Once again, it just seems like an odd choice.3. In my earlier review, I stated that the family bits had no relation with the overall plot. I suggested that they either be removed or heavily revamped. As it stands, they still suck. So many days pass and we never even see what our family looks like. Just gender neutral names and they/them pronouns for our main character and their S.O. While there’s nothing wrong with being a they/them, the problem is that it only further detaches the player from the already faceless family. When the main character refers to Sam (their fiance) as “they” in multiple cutscenes, it just makes the player feel so far away from anything related to the family. When both of my kids died, I felt nothing simply because I don’t even know what they look like.4. This game has FOURTEEN endings. I only got one so maybe things are extremely different in the other endings. Maybe everything comes up roses or it all goes to ♥♥♥♥. Who knows. There are so many minor choices you make in the game that it is hard to tell JUST WHAT causes these branching paths.5. I remember in one of the updates there being an upgrade system that encouraged you to do well. However, that has been removed entirely and with it, money’s purpose. Since the family parts bear no relation to the plot there is little motivation to do well. Money means nothing, so why do well on broadcasts? Just seemed like an odd choice to remove it. That’s all of my thoughts for this game. Subject to change depending on the other endings but who knows. I know it comes off as negative but I really enjoyed myself and found the actual story engaging.Just buy it, it’s fun.

_childDocuments_.review: This game showed a ton of promise! The first 30 minutes are incredibly engaging as you get thrown into a new job with a lot of promise and a LOT of power. unfortunately, the game seems to peak with its second level, where things are flying off the handle but still relevant enough for you to understand what's going on and follow along with the story. Soon after that, the game's flaws start showing and the pacing issues come up front and center. The game starts throwing in a bunch of new gameplay mechanics that add nothing to the experience and take away from what actually made the game so interesting. There are tons of unresolved and unadressed story threads, a lot of cringey and strange skits that go on for WAY too long, and whenever you try to mess with the broadcsasts a little bit to prevent yourself from falling comatose of sheer boredom, the game punishes you for not following its very strict and limiting formula. I'm mainly upset about how promising this game was at the beginning, but lost touch of what made it great before we even hit the 1 hour mark. Stuck in there for another hour to give it a chance and see if the experience would pick back up a little, but came to regret that choice because it didn't at all. :(

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing this review after Chapter 2. I've been playing video games for 30 years. When you've been playing this long, it's easy to be blasé, to find games derivative or devoid of any interest.Once in a while, you try out a game that shakes you out of this mindset. is one of them.Dystopian political sims aren't anything new, but they haven't ever been presented quite like this. The developers have come up with a way to mix FMV, absurd comedy, choices matter, high school drama class, politics and rhythm game... and it is somehow more than palatable.There are dozens of typos in the subtitles, but that's pretty much the only criticism I can give this game.This is an outrageously ridiculous but very important game, one that you should most definitely play. It's not perfect in any way whatsoever (there are better FMV games, better political games, better choices matter games, etc.), but it somewhat coalesces into something unique and far greater than the sum of its parts.I really can't wait for Part 3. Well done.

_childDocuments_.review: 7.5/10 - 7/10 for the DLCNot For Broadcast is a FMV game that plays like a job simulator type game like papers please. Normally I would pass on this, but the story, characters and excellent B movie like acting make up for the limited gameplay that usually hinder FMV games. The story is mostly satire, but is also a politcal thriller that gives a very 1984 like warning about communism (for once) and touches on Leftist themes as well, such as the participation trophy generation and modern feminism. It also touches on right wing topics as well, so nobody is free from criticism here. The actors also do a great job at making their characters there own, even if some of it is in the so bad its good way.Unfortunately, as with most FMV games, the gameplay is rather limited. Usually just swapping between cameras to keep the audience invested and censoring out swears, but sometimes throws a few other things your way. The most common gimmicks are also the most annoying ones. The interference mechanic does nothing apart from divert your attention from the screens apart from when you can jack into Disrupts broadcasts, and the the far to common musical sections has you swapping cameras to a beat. I really hop this game gets a sequel that makes the gameplay more meaningful.As for the DLC, most of it is good, though also irrelevant to the main story apart from bits of your life which gives some backstory to Peter Clement. Its worth playing but get it on sale and pass on the spooky dlc if you aren't interested in the entire season pass.Still, this is by far one of the better FMV games out there, which for me is impressive considering most movie games I tend to pass on.

_childDocuments_.review: I won this game as a giveaway via the developers' live stream this morning. []Not For Broadcast is a deliciously wacky & nerve wracking story adventure game that takes a cue from games like Switch Blade (sega CD) and Five Nights at Freddies in a completely unique way. It's challenging, yes, and sometimes *shockingly* frustrating -- but the story that weaves through the different news broadcasts is riviting and the humor is absolutely spot on. i laughed; i laughed lots. i also want to say that i entirely respect that, in a very subtle way, they made the game accessible to whatever gender you are and who you presume your partner to be. while you are both given names, they don't force you into the character situation - it's left for you to believe it to be as you like. thank you.it's a bit of a short game at 2.8 hours, but rest assured i'll be giving this another play through to see what other options i might have picked would have. AND there are more episodes to come -- at a totally reasonable price i'll be picking those up too.  the dev team included a brief message at the end that they're going out to film more as soon as this whole pandemic situation clears up. thanks for entertaining us while we're stuck at home! The full motion video is used in a charming and effective way, and you will feel like you are directing a news show. Gameplay is very much rhythm and experience based, and the difficulty ramps up quite a lot. But to be fair, it appears that getting perfect scores is mostly for bragging rights and some additional stuff and you don't need to ace a stage to continue in the story. The game also features some narratives parts inbetween days with some choices that will sure to come back to haunt you later. Plus it introduces new features every single day, that give you much more control on how the story will advanche, but I hope they will not piling on new challenges until it will become too messy. Right now it is still a very approachable game and I hope they keep it that way.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a "choices matter" fan with even a glancing interest in Soviet politics/history and/or Animal Farm and/or 1984 and/or recent U.S. decline and/or dystopian novels... well this is too juicy/fun/brilliant to miss. It's brilliantly done, especially if you have familiarity with the USSR/related cultures, imo. Unlike many of these games, I'm actually keen to do a replay right away to see how, indeed, my choices mattered. (Plus I played on easy to learn the game, but want to do a more challenging mode on replay) It's a decent time investment--about 8 hours for each play-through (ish)--and relative to the price point, I highly recommend it. It's good bang for buck, especially if you grab it during the Steam sale, as I did.  I was impressed with the acting and writing in particular, as well as the parody songs/performances. Everyone goes all in and it's engaging all the way through. The only aspect I found mildly annoying was the interference challenges... fiddling w/ that knob is tedious! Kudos to the whole team behind this, including/especially the director(s)--whatever notes you gave to the various actors were A+++ for nailing tone/satire, especially all the "celebrities." Chef's kiss.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; unique, enjoyable mechanics combined with a surreal humour and dedicated devs mean you should absolutely give Not For Broadcast a tryNot For Broadcast may be best described as a mixture between Papers, Please and We Happy Few. As with Papers, Please, the gameplay is focused around a novel and, at first thought, potentially menial task; in the case of Not For Broadcast, managing the editing of the live National Nightly News, with each new day bringing greater complexity to the task. What starts as a simple set of instructions morphs into a chaotic management of buttons, bleepers and screens, the goal to keep the National Nightly News on air without (too much) disruption. Alone the gameplay of Not For Broadcast is interesting and fun, presenting an accessible but entirely new genre of live TV management which is refreshing to get to grips with.However, where Not For Broadcast shines, but where it is potentially striving for a particular audience, is in its theme and content. Not For Broadcast is set in a British dystopia, akin to We Happy Few's pastiche of Brave New World, focusing on a surreal world with sinister undertones, rather than the full-blown grayscale tyranny found in Papers, Please, drawing from 1984. There are differences compared with We Happy Few of course, namely that rather than Joy, the drug plying the people in latter is a political movement, Advance, whose populist policies hide potentially nefarious plans but also due to the story-focus of Not For Broadcast, the game held together by the actors playing the irate presenters or the bewildering guests. The humour of Not For Broadcast is certainly an acquired taste - think Monty Python or Shooting Stars - and would be, no doubt, confusing (or intriguing) for non-Brits but I personally found it funny, even laughing out loud on occasion.This is not to say that Not For Broadcast is perfect; some of the mechanics can be infuriating at times, such as the static slider and not all of the jokes, especially those in the commercials, land perfectly. However, without a doubt, Not For Broadcast's small flaws are carried by its unique mechanics, surrealist humour and, above all, the dedication and commitment of the NotGames team, evident in their updates and their newest Lockdown Update, to provide players with additional content in lieu of the next installment planned. Not For Broadcast is clearly a labour of love and you should absolutely give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting concept but nothing about the mechanics, characters, segments, or narrative fits together in any kind of sensible cohesive way. Though it is often entertaining until the last few broadcasts long overstayed their welcome while doing nothing new mechanically or when it's adding odd elements of pointless family expenses, drama, or tragedy.An FMV game that has you taking over the vision mixing, censoring, ad picking, headline lean, and other tasks at a news station just as a new political party has been elected. Your choices on what to air at certain times, choices made in text segments between broadcast days, and which and if you follow certain orders or suggestions while doing your job can see the story take different paths or characters actions and fates change over a span of around 10 years.The actual mechanics end up keeping things evolving over time tend to be dull, often poorly explained to begin with, and trying to get a particular result can lead to confusing moments. Both poor and nonsensical as any kind of political commentary which hurts text story and choice moments drama, tone is all over, segments can overstay their welcome but each broadcast day does have a checkpoint after each ad break. Often entertaining and funny when not focused on the main plot (unless you aren't entertained by a particular segment and find yourself needing to do dull tasks for 10-15 minutes before it ends unless you fail out of it or worse miss something for the narrative you wanted to do then have to go through the whole thing again) but then, due to the style of the game, you will be punished for paying too much attention to the actors and may need to see things you missed after the gameplay segments where you can review the footage that was broadcast, play the ad videos without listening into studio talk or orders, or view the moments that weren't completely available to you. When you preform actions for narrative purposes, sometimes it hurts your broadcast and possibly your score for the segment, but letting the more obvious things happen like playing certain ads or allowing the broadcast to be disrupted don't damage your score or really cause you any problems with getting fired or arrested.Screenshots:

_childDocuments_.review: Not for broadcast is a great game for both its fun and stressful management of a news broadcast and its willingness to call out a government that is seen more and more in today's society. Positives: -Not for broadcast has a very engaging interactive story, I have played through about 3 times now, each time the events, some of the dialog, and the overall reaction of certain characters change depending on how you play.-Has good keybinds and fairly intuitive gameplay, takes a playthrough or so to learn but does not take long to get good at the job.-Has a very Papers-Please feel but once finished may arguably be even better then papers please was.-Has a challenge system that lets you replay broadcasts in fun variations of them.Negatives:-Has a non-intuitive system of money and money management.-Defiantly takes a lot of time to get into, broadcasts are long but do have points where you can pause them.-The music system feels clunky with it often being hard to hit the rhythm max-The conversation sections feel very repetitive in their 10/3 timing with very little forgiveness for going over that 10 second time, makes it feel like during sections that the camera shouldn't switch you have to switch it just for the game play feature.Overall I highly recommend the game, enjoy and if you can, have a peaceful night.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this because I thought it would be like Papers Please. And, it sort of is. The gameplay itself is pretty good, especially when you add in a challenge or two. But, for a story heavy game, the narrative is dumb. It suffers heavily from tonal whiplash, often trying to jump from comedic to grim back to comedic in only a few minutes. And why does your choice of headline retroactively affect what has happened? And despite working in the news, why don't you know anything until two seconds before it's being broadcast live? They also refuse to name the country this is happening in despite making up other fake country names, which makes for awkward dialog with a lot of "this country" in it.And for a political game, the story sounds it was written by people who studied political theory solely on r/politicalcompassmemes and think the USSR was a 'liberal' state. The game's rather progressive socially, but it has very little subtlety with other matters, and usually just has you pick binary "good guy or bad guy" choices. It has big bad 'Advance' throw out random policies that make little sense for an authoritarian government to run. For instance, Advance run extremely progressive taxes, and I constantly get the feeling that the writers *hate* progressive taxes. Despite Advance committing actual atrocities and war crimes, it feels like all anyone cares about in the resistance movement is "I used to be rich, and now I'm not, and that's bad". They talk vaguely about freedom sometimes, but usually only in the context of "being free to be rich". I knew going in that they'd have this taxation be a plot point, but I thought they'd be more nuanced about it, rather than parroting conservative, pro-big business talking points.Advance feels like a hardcore libertarian's scaremongering tactic, warning about such evil government activities like funding the arts, allowing euthenasia, and taxing the rich. Those are Advance's three main policies, and the game portrays all of them as leading directly to fascism in a year or two. Now, to be fair, they satirize a lot of things in the game from around the political sphere, but...1: Forced neutrality is not neutral. It's a form of media bias. Ironic, huh?2: They aren't exactly being neutral when they paint one side as a literal dictatorial 'new world order' and the other as the only freedom fighters willing to stand up for what they believe in, and makes it a binary choice between them. The game paints this as freedom versus oppression, and pretty consistently spins financial equality as bad. It's like the game is saying to the player "supporting arts funding or taxation basically makes you a fascist".As another example of 2, minor spoiler: ...So, game's fun, has good representation of minorities, but the narrative has really gross and distracting undertones. Or maybe I'm just a dumb bleeding heart liberal. Take your pick.Edit: Oh right, how could I forget probably the worst message in the game? Spoilers for midgame:

_childDocuments_.review: So the concept of the game is really interesting. I was really enjoying it at first, because I really liked the idea of being essentially a TV producer, and organizing segments of a live news broadcast. But it seems like the game decided to never expand on that, doing the same thing over and over again in favor of this weird dark comedy storyline about oppressive governments, media propaganda, and some of the most unfunny "lol randum" comedy I've ever seen. There was this one like 8 minute segment where I had to sit through these two idiots playing this game where they have to get this ping pong ball into a garbage can, which presented like a high school improv where everyone was just doing wacky things, all of which were meaningless slapstick while I was just switching cameras back and forth, only to end the segment, and be presented with a "choose your own text adventure" in between gameplay that was stark and solemn by comparison. By the time I was bored of the low quality, 2010 Youtube-tier "comedy" routines, I had begun to realize that the only interesting part of the game had become repetitive, just switching between cameras and censoring ultra-British swear words that I've never heard before. I stopped when the game introduced a mechanic where I have to keep tiny little baby protesters off the TV antenna by shocking them off, in between switching cameras and censoring. The storyline is about an oppressive, seemingly communist government engaging in hardcore 1984 fascism, that the writers are cutting with goofy "random" humor, and none of it flows well, or presents itself in the way that it's intending to. Big meh from me.

_childDocuments_.review: Great, funny story. Closer to a film than a video-game, but great nonetheless.Gameplay-wise; it's multi-tasking. Making sure the camera is pointed to the right person, not at anything that might make viewers switch off. But also making sure that the camera stays static. Moving away for reactions-shot or wide-shot to keep the viewer engaged. Bleeping out bad-words or words . Anyway if you're reading this review, you probably know how the game works, and I love it.Its only problem is that the gameplay affects the story only a little. Mostly branching with "Play this tape or don't". Where, the similar game, , has a branching system that is integrated directly into the gameplay.The story seemed pretty absurd to me at first. It's also difficult to be listening on the characters while doing camera-work. That's why being able to see your own saved broadcasts is a great feature. On repeat playthroughs, stuff starts making sense. I noticed things that I didn't notice on my first go. The characters are all great and hilarious enough to play the game multiple times. And the humorous tones and the dark tones match particularly well somehow.A niche game, but a great experience.Alan was Right.

_childDocuments_.review: If the Early Access tag worries you, rest assured that this is a case of it done correctly. An FMV game on par with the classics, like Night Trap The current state of the game includes one of four promised episodes from the . There are three segments, each containing three newsroom sections and several text-based choose your own adventure style portions placed in-between. A single playthrough had taken me around two hours, but there is plenty of incentive to replay episodes, such as: branching paths that are influenced by the decisions made by the player both inside and outside of the newsroom; the opportunity to view alternate news feed that the player had missed in previous sessions, including cutting to the news presenters when they believe the camera is focused elsewhere, leading to indecent situations (at the cost or to the benefit of concurrent viewership); and aiming for a higher final ranking. The experience can also be altered by purposefully including shocking footage instead of following the planned narrative--will we introduce this CEO using a photo of their inauguration or a photo taken depicting them while brazenly drunk? How will this choice affect the viewer's perception of the representative, and will it have an impact on the station's relationship with their respective company? Aim for an increase in viewership, or go against the wishes of your superiors? Dilemmas like these are commonly presented throughout a playthrough, but the larger picture is sadly still to be seen in future updates.The development team is very responsive in discussions regarding planned content in the forums, and transparent when faced with feedback. They've even made the decision to completely re-shoot footage for future updates in order to provide the best experience possible. This is definitely a project that is worth investing in.

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost, this is not a casual game, it starts off rather easy but the difficulty ramps up quickly, having to deal with multiple mechanics at the same time and I can imagine later versions will get more complicated.Not For Broadcast is a modern FMV game where you play as a broadcaster for a news station, having to keep the audience entertained by keeping order in the chaotic world of news and deciding what to and what not to show. In between broadcasts you have COYA sections about the protagonist dealing with family life and troubles. So far the game is around 1 to 2 hours long with decent amounts of replay value. Choices do in fact matter as what might seem like a small issue can lead to huge results. Also the game has a rank system that goes up and down depending on how interested the audience is. It's worth noting the ranking system is rather strict as even a small mistake can cause your rating to plummet. Doing something especially stupid, like playing an ad during a news section, will instantly end the game and make you replay the segment, which can be up to 10 minutes long.About the politics, the game, at least to me, seems anti-centralization, but that could change as the story progresses.EDIT: FULL RELEASEWell I was mostly right about it being anti-centralization, it does take a more middle ground than I expected. My opinion of the game is still the same as before, also there's a total of 14 endings so it's got replay value if that matters. Althoug I can imagine it'd be a pain because from what I can tell, the news broadcasts for the most part don't change all that much outside of a few key moments. For a total game length, I'd say it's about 10-ish hours long for a single playthrough

There are so many paths to go down that every playthrough I’ve done has had something new.The cast, their characters, and the writers truly made this game. You can tell how much love and passion was put into this game (as cliche as that sounds).  Also thank you for the inclusion of a story mode for those of us who wanted to focus on the story!

_childDocuments_.review: No spoilers in this review, everyone should experience this for themselves. Just finished my first play-through. Rarely do I think games deserve a 10/10. This is one game that I think deserves such a rating. This game accomplishes so much at once in its story, presentation, and gameplay that I have yet to experience in any other game. It manages to be a hilarious collection of sketches with great dialogue, a biting satire of politics across the spectrum, and a very poignant statement on media, political movements and the rhetoric they use to persuade people to support their causes. While I was expecting a rather straightforward story a la Papers, Please (Which I love) but instead sent me on a journey with many twists and turns which it goes through while still retaining its strong message and narrative consistency. This is accomplished through the masterful writing and presentation of information in each of the segments, made even more convincing by the incredible comedic and dramatic performances by each of the actors involved, in particular the main anchors and Advance Party leaders. Just given these praises I would be totally on board if this was just a show, but Not for Broadcast manages to be a fantastic and engaging game as well. The mechanics both emphasize the points made by the story while also having a significant effect on the story as it goes along. I'm already noticing major differences on my second play-through to the first, but the gameplay is also just fun to master as you attempt to edit the perfect news segment amidst the often chaotic events on the broadcast screens. This is one of the best video game experiences I've ever had, it will certainly be my top game of 2022. If you like politics, comedies, games like Papers, Please, or even if you are looking for a good show to watch I would fully recommend this game. Easy 10/10 I will be playing again. Thanks for reading and if you can, have a peaceful night.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a fan of simulation games, so when I found this one, I went into it with only the impression I got from the screenshots thinking it would be a rather simple PCR simulator. I got what I was hoping for, except in a very different way than I expected. As a side note, sharing the same name as the protagonist created a more immersive experience than I sometimes would have liked, albeit that is not to be taken negatively. places you into the role of a control room operator for a news station, assigning you various tasks ranging from mixing different video sources to playing sound effects at appropriate times. Mechanics are gradually introduced to you, scaling difficulty as the game progresses. While certain rules have to be obeyed, the game leaves a lot of room for personal choice, in more ways than one might expect at first. These features also allow for replayability, trying out new choices, perhaps to hunt down some of the many achievements.Gameplay itself is rather straightforward as the player is confined to the production control room, which makes them focus more on the many recorded segments themselves.The player will be able to follow a multi-month long story, both from a personal and from a nation-wide and global perspective, operating as a news channel CRO. The story is, however, very much dependent on player choices, creating multiple differently branching storylines that can be explored individually. The player will furthermore find themselves facing split-second decision making many times, possibly making them question their choice afterward. relies heavily on recorded, real life video segments. The surrounding environment is kept simple, yet pleasing for the liminal space the player finds themself in. Over the course of the game, a few changes can be noticed, but the main design remains steady.Similar to visual design, the sound is almost entirely composed of real life recordings, with a few sound affects added. places a surprising amount of power into the player's hands given the limited tools they have at their disposal. Able to choose between  the player can mix the news broadcast very much to their liking, with corresponding consequences. I would not call the game difficult in itself, this is however dependant on a player's own expectations.  has implemented a few ways to even encourage challenge-seeking players to give it a go, with multiple game modes to choose from.I've nominated  for the "Most Innovative Gameplay" award in the 2022 Steam Awards, which is also my reason for composing this review. It turned out to be a game hiding so much more content than visible at its surface, requiring players to observe and choose carefully to uncover every secret they can find, and it does so in a unique way with an obviously great amount of effort put into it by the developing team (during COVID-19 restrictions, nonetheless). is by all means a must try for anyone interested in simulation as well as peculiar, random, witty and sometimes even distressing story.
