Party House was the only game I played for like a week. Out of the 50, the only games I haven't been able to get into are Block Koala and Combatants.and I'll be obsessed with Campanella 2, Velgress, and Valbrace, for who knows how long.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: So much more than just a collection of 50 small arcade games. Most games are fully worked out concepts that are really fun and creative. This entire pack brought me back to the days of playing flash games and just browsing through collections. Specifically Nitrome, with the wide variety of pixelart games made by the same developers. The games range through a wide variety of genres and concepts. So no matter what genre of games you like, there will definitely be games in here that you enjoy. At the time of writing this i have played the game for more than 10 hours and I feel like I am nowhere near discovering everything i want to do. I have beaten a few of the games, but there are several that I enjoy a lot that I still want to complete. I believe there is even an overarching secret/puzzle that I haven't even started looking for. Most games are really challenging, but in the right way, I immediately want to jump back in after every loss.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: There's a wide range of genres and they're all done pretty nicely. Some of the games are a bit rough, but if you talk to friends or look at guides there's usually enough in there to help you get through whatever it is.The music (where it exists) is catchy and liable to become an earworm. This game's had years to bake and it shows.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This game is themed as a homage to 80s-era retro games, but the real secret behind UFO 50 is that it's actually a tribute to 2000s Flash games in the best way possible. I've already dumped a shocking amount of time into it and I still feel like I've only scratched the surface of this collection. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: It genuinely hurts me to say this, but... I didn't like it. Don't lynch me just yet! I love the concept of this - 50 retro throwbacks in one? And (almost) all of them actually creative, fresh and thought-out? AND it's made by highly competent devs? Hell yeah, sign me up! But then I played it... I'm sure to some extent it's just me (which is ultimately also why I decided against a negative review), but even though I'm generally a huge fan of retro and arcade gaming - hell, it makes up the overwhelming majority of what I play nowadays! - I think what I'm figuring out right now is that I don't actually like NES games.Both home computer titles from before that era and console titles from after that era click with me much more than the particular space in time that this collection aims to emulate the feel of. (Successfully so, I might add!)Point being - I'm sure it's good, but it's not for me. And should you also have some qualms with specifically NES/Famicom era gaming, you might want to do some more research before taking the plunge as well.That said, I hope this game ends up being a huge success for all involved, because I genuinely do love what it's doing.... Now you may lynch me all you like.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Growing up in the 80s this is pure nostalgia bliss, feels like real lost media.Almost every genre you can think of, incredibly simple control scheme, the graphics and music are beautiful, and capture the feel of the era perfectly.The games are all brutally difficult and there's very little handholding, which is true to form but might turn off a few people.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: It is currently 5am, I’ve been playing this all night, so sorry if my wording is insane.Don’t let the first game fool you. It is purposeful. Play on.I was initially worried about buying this because it appears to have the potential to be a ‘play for an hour and never again’ kind of game, which recently has been the case for when I revisit nes/snes/megadrive games.I caved and I’m so incredibly glad I did. Any worries of ‘motivation to play’ you have, forget them and buy this. If you are a retro game fan this is absolutely going to scratch a very particular itch. The blend of modern optimisation is incredibly well done. I skim read reviews a few days ago and the phrase ‘half baked’ kept popping up. Disregard this. People can’t seem to grasp beautiful simplicity from games in 2024. To use the word ‘simple’ even positively seems wrong because so far each game has had its own particular cleverness to it that makes playing each one so exciting, even if some may ring familiar, a uniqueness appears from it and it rarely crosses your mind the thought of ‘this feels like (game)’ Even games that didn’t quite click with me I have the need to revisit them to try and get better at them and progress if possible. The grip UFO50 has on me already is insane. Treat yourself and buy this. I can’t wait to play this with my dad who got me into gaming and introduced me to older consoles at a young age. I hope one day online multiplayer is added but with the magic of modern technology there are ways. Having official online would be fun though, with maybe global leaderboards alongside the ones already there. Those would be hilarious to look at. Overall this is YEAASSUESYSYEYSYYSEHDYSHSYSHSYSHAYESAAAA AAYAAAEAYAYAYYAYEAYAYYAYEUSYYAYAYAYYAAYAYESYAYAYESYAAYYAYAYAayeysyYwooooooWOOOOOWOOOOOOOOWOOOOOOOOOWOOOOOOO
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Going into this conjured memories of a bootleg 100 games in one cartridge I used to have that was mostly full of bloatware & copy pasted games for the sake of making the number bigger. In reality, it feels like I found a dusty old box in an attic which contained a console I'd never seen before and 50 banger games. I expected to play each one for a few minutes and move on but you can spent literal hours on a single game.I've played 16 games so far, beaten 6 and cherry'd 4. My only criticism for now is the order they are presented to you by default can put some players off. I'd recommend picking randomly from the list or choosing a genre you know you'll enjoy. Also worth noting that certain games  really benefit from being played earlier than others .Overall, the amount of content packed into this more than justifies the cost of admission (especially if it happens to be on sale). Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I would pay £5-£20 for a lot of these games individually. This is an outrageous package that I'll be playing for a long time.A lot of the games initially have the clunky feel of Commodore 64 or Atari 2600 games. But if you play enough of any of them, you realise that Mossmouth have applied modern indie sensibilities and the learnings from 40 years of game development to make something genuinely fresh.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely worth it. Any of these games could 100% have been a disk or cartridge from their era (and an alternate universe).  Their influences are clear though they also stand completely on their own, and the ways they've reinterpreted old game design concepts (and more modern ones, like deckbuilders, tower defense and idle games) are unique and interesting.  Any one of these would have set you back the full price of a cartridge back in the day, and it really is a steal to get the whole collection for this much.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: The experience of bouncing around the game’s 50 available titles — spending an hour on a sprawling RPG, swapping to a puzzle game to clear a level or two, then checking your notes for the side quests you need to finish in a platforming adventure — is the most fun I’ve had with the medium in years. 20 hours in on UFO 50 and I haven’t even *touched* half the titles, I’ve been so engrossed in the rest. Easiest 10/10 of my life — not every game in the collection is 10/10, but the way it all comes together is nothing short of masterful. Really, really good.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: As someone with fascination of Action 52, this game is like a dream come true. A multi-game pack that are not just playable but extremely good!This game will have games that really jives with your taste, but it will also have 20 games you thought wouldn't be as fun as they are. And yet, the sum is greater than the parts, as each game seems to add to the universe of which they were uncovered, a sort of cohesion between them all.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible! I heard about this only yesterday and I knew I had to support this project. 90 min and I have only touched 1/50th of what this game has to offer. Played about 6 games with the tower defense game being the most played so far. I can't really say much other than so far what I have played has been really good and I am amazed these guys put together 50 games for this collection. Even if you aren't into retro these are the kind of devs that should be supported. Even though I have a huge backlog of games and technically could have waited for a deep sale I wanted to give these guys the full price for the game they deserve it.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of great games here, some are great for local co-op. It's nice being able to hop into and play a game within a minute. It's nice experiencing tight, core gameplay loops and not needing to wade through 20 layers of meta progression systems and player retention mechanics. I'm pretty sure I'll be coming back to this for years to come.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Been playing this game for over 10 hours now and have only played about 10 games - most of which are "early" titles in the game's chronological order. I haven't even played the longer, more interesting titles that UFO 50 has to offer, yet I'm already having this much fun?? I can see this being a game that I play for well over a hundred hours. There's so much variety, with excellent visuals and music, and even the weaker games are at least interesting thanks to UFO 50's faux-history. This truly is a game greater than the sum of its parts with how everything ties together in such a smart way. And these are things I've picked up on just from thoroughly playing 10 of these. I can't wait to see what other surprises this game has packed into the other 40!
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Clunky controls, obscure game rules, punishing difficulty.... this is absolutely like an anthology cartridge from the late 80s / early 90s. For the price point, this provide 50 fully developed games (ok, maybe 42-ish given that some of them are similar).If you're 35+ you probably want to buy this. Do it!
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: When I heard that the guys over at Mossmouth were going to be bringing back 50 of UFO Soft's classic titles from the LX console for PC, I couldn't believe my ears, and yet here they are. 50 classic titles brought back from the 80's like we never lost them in the first place. Mossmouth has done a fantastic job at preserving the feel, sound, and look of these vintage games, games that I thought would be lost to time forever. With a library spanning 8 years, from 1982-89, this collection has it all, from the strategic battler Attactics, to the side scrolling beat-em-up Fist Hell, to the eerie point-and-click mystery Night Manor. It even includes some of the lesser popular titles from back in the day, such as UFO Soft's pioneer title Barbuta, and the controversial Quibble Race. If you loved these games growing up as a kid in the 80's, or are a kid now looking for some retro classics, you will definitely want to pick this one up.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: A monumental achievement - a must-play for anyone deeply entrenched in either the 8-bit past or the indie present. So content-rich that you could feasibly dislike 75% of what's here and still walk away with enough to justify the price. A release that feels important in that it seems to be definitively making people outside of nerdy niche spheres internalize that old games were (and still are) good, actually. Go in blind and enjoy the ride.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend it but ill put some gripes i have with some of the games ive tried out of the collection in the hope maybe they could get tweakedThe Western themed RPG combat is mockingly slow, like the developers are taking a piss at anyone who enjoys turn based combat or something removing so many delays and slow enemy death animations would make it less "authentic" but definitely less of a drag to playA lot of the arcade games suffer from a modern day difficulty curve were the start is easy and picks up the pace over time, problem is most of the arcade games are pretty short (even for arcade game standards) and dying on the last stage just to get sent back to a piss easy baby level makes it feel like you are waiting for the game to actually let you playIt would be less of an issue if some of the arcade games also had their pacing smoothed out, in the drifting car game there are times were there are no enemies on the screen and most of the games have transitions between levels that cannot be skipped or sped up
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Basically every single game in this collection is a fully realised title, some of which would stand if released by themselves. And yet, there's 50 of them in here. I think it's safe to say that this game has it all, and the best way to play is to just embrace the variety, float from title to title, and see what sticks. Don't let the quantity of games wear you down, just select titles that look interesting, try for a few minutes and move on. Do this and before you know it, you'll be in hours deep.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 is a special game, a massive feat for the team and for indies in general. These are some of the most fun and creative games I've played in years and they all literally only use two buttons and a d-pad. Here's a checklist of a few things to see if you'll like the game:Do you like short and sweet arcade experiences?Do you like fun short burst multiplayer?What about drawn out strategy multiplayer?Maybe a deckbuilder or two?Got a penchant for metroidvanias?Or would you like to sink your teeth into a full JRPG?In the mood for a spooky point and click?Do you like games that are fun?It's a meme to say "there's a little something for everyone" but in this case it is 1000% true. I challenge anyone to try out a few of these games and say they didn't enjoy any of them. It won't happen. These games just ooze charm and you can tell they were all made with passion and care. I haven't even touched on the presentation, music, graphics, and meta narrative that lies underneath it all. Just believe me when I say this is a landmark game, not just indie. People will be talking about this game for a long time.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Yo, listen up, let me tell you 'bout a game,UFO 50's the title, it’s bringin' the fame!Fifty games packed in, retro delight,On the LX console, it’s outta sight!First, we got Barbuta, platformin' fun,Secrets galore, man, you’ll never be done!Jumpin' and runnin', it’s a wild ride,Adventure awaits, let’s take it in stride!Next up, Party House, bringin' the vibe,Deck-building madness, you’ll thrive and you’ll jive!Throw the dopest party, make it the best,Invite all your friends, let’s put it to the test!Then there’s Grimstone, a world full of thrills,An RPG in Hell, with monstrous chills!Epic quests await, in a land so dark,Fightin’ for glory, let’s make our mark!So grab UFO 50, don’t miss out on the fun,With friends by your side, you’ll never be done!Dive into the pixels, let your joy unfurl,Just remember, kids, keep your dreams in this world!Stay away from drugs, that’s the way to be,Focus on the games, let your spirit be free!
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This is basically everything great about discovering video games in the first place, somehow.I was extremely excited about this release and it has somehow managed to blow away my expectations in every regard. Top notch presentation, design, and art. Such an awesome love letter to people who really love games.PS BARBUTA 4 LIFE
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: What an incredible achievement in game design! This is Mossmouth we're talking about (creators of Spelunky), so I'm sure nobody is surprised by the sheer quality and creativity on offer here. Even so, this is one of the most impressive efforts of game design I've seen in a while.UFO 50 is more than simply an assortment of retro-styled video games. It is a love letter to and reimagining of gaming and game design philosophies of the '80s. Many of the individual games are quite excellent and addictively replayable even by modern standards, sure. However, the big picture of the collection also takes players on a journey through the evolution of a fictional game studio.There are games here of just about every genre. There are quick, arcadey games and epic, thinky adventure games. Action games, puzzle games and everything in between. It's like finding a dusty console in a bin in your attic and firing it up for the first time to discover a whole library of classic games that you never knew existed.There really is something for everyone here and even if only a handful of the games really stick with you, it's still absolutely worth the pittance that Mossmouth is asking. At $0.50 (or less if you catch it on sale) per game, this is an absolute steal and several of these games could have easily sold individually for $10 or more.Highest recommendation if you have any patience and interest at all in retro games.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most impressive game(s) I've ever played. Each game I have played really feels like it's from the 80s. Each one is polished, and has its own charm. There are plenty of big, or 'epic' games as UFO 50 classifies them, and plenty of games you can boot up and play quickly. This has quickly risen to the top of my favorite games of all time!
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This game sounds too good to be true and somehow, it just isn't. Yes, you'll spend more time on some games than others and sure, some are better than others, but NOTHING I've played has felt like filler. Each of these games is built on a clever idea and designed with such a focus on elegant simplicity that probably about 80% my 38 hours has been spent on 5 or 6 games (and not because those are the only ones worth playing, those 5 or 6 are so fun I didn't even want to play another)The obvious influence here is the NES era, which was well before my time, but this will also appeal to kids of the Flash Games era, people who like perusing game jams, or anyone who likes to blindly explore a well curated collection of cool ideas. For the most part, these games do not have explicit tutorials or instructions. If you are a fan of learning a game through experimentation and like to microdose Aha! moments, you will love this game. If productive struggle frustrates you, you might not. -This plays flawlessly on Steam Deck-Many games contain both singleplayer and multiplayer (which are often slightly different game modes, which is to say the single player is not just a worse version of a multiplayer game)-Even the single player makes for fun 'pseudomultiplayer' as you learn a game together-I play a lot of puzzle games and while not everything in here is a puzzle game, they all scratch the "figure out what's going on" itch-Every "What's your favorite game?" thread has had a TON of variance in the responses so there is truly something for everyone hereIf you enjoy exploring clever ideas executed cleanly, $25 is beyond a bargain and I haven't even tried every game yet.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: It's fantastic!  The first game in the chronology, Barbuta, is a bit of an odd one to start with, but if you want to fall in love right away, find a friend or loved one and play Hell Fist!!  It's a Double Dragon-like and it's just perfection! The art & music throughout the package are to die for.  Every design is so cute and pitch perfect.  They way they introduce each game, the menus and animations, etc, are just so good!  This is a game your wife or girlfriend will love simply for how many cute characters and interactions there are in every game.I've only tried 7 or 8 games so far, but there isn't a single one I won't go back to as of yet.  Animations, controls, and feedback are fantastic, and (almost) every game is easy to comprehend without instructions in under a minute.  That's how brilliant the design is.  I can't wait to discover more!  Thank you Mossmouth!
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a major high watermark in indie game development, and a significant milestone in the art form. It's a slow burn to begin with, but it will get it's hooks into you if you give it time, and the marriage of old school fun with high level intentional artistry, is deeply compelling. It feels like the most classic Nintendo game, but goes above and beyond even that high bar. It is an anthology yes, but it is also clearly a deeply cohesive artistic vision. Out of 50 games, only 2 are lemons (Combatants, and Planet Zoldath). And stay away from Barbuta until you've got the bug. Start with Warptank if you need an in. Enjoy! Such a rare treat.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This is an incredible collection of games and the sheer amount of work on display is mind blowing. At this point I've tried about 30 of the games, and while some are better than others, the cohesive vibes make them all worth checking out. Definitely a must play if you're a fan of retro games, pixel art, and genuinely charming experiences.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Currently my indie game of the year.  Many of the games in this collection are unforgiving and set you back to the start of that title.  Pisses me off every time it happens... Still keep playing though.  A ton of different genres in here.  The idle game one runs while you are in other titles.  Start that one early.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Buy this game. Seriously I want everyone to buy this game, I've only really just started, having only played slightly more than half of the games in the collection, and already I can say this feels like one of the best (and brutally hardest) games I've played in years. It absolutely perfectly feels like an 80's retro game collection made by people with the design philosophy behind some of the best indie games of the modern era. That is, of course, exactly what this game is, but it's impossible to overstate just how much it truly feels like that. You are certain to find even a handful of games you really click with and fall in love with, a bunch more that you like and want to keep playing, and honestly so far only 2 of the games I've played have I actively disliked at all. The amount of content everyone can get out of this game, the price is an absolute steal, this could easily, justifiably be a full price game. It is a true labour of love and yet another showcase of just how unique and amazing indie games are in the modern day. Thank you to Derek and the team for this absolute gem, I can't wait to pour dozens or even hundreds of hours into learning and finishing all of these games.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Are you kidding me? I expected this to be good, but it's terrifyingly good. We must've spent half an hour on Bug Hunters before even touching anything else. Rail Heist is easily as good as everyone says. If I could change anything - Pingolf needs a 4P mode, and maybe a level editor. _childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I have been abducted and brainwashed by UFO 50. I can't put this game down. 50 actually amazing games bundled in one package for $25. You might not like every game here, but if you can appreciate retro styled/inspired games I'd say you're guaranteed to find at least one you like. Or two. Or five. A lot of these games could probably make it as independent titles with how big they are. But when they're all in one collection they elevate each other so much. You can easily jump out of one game and into another, and for me that seamlessness keeps things fresh and fun. I've completed a handful of games in my 43 hours of playtime so far, and I still have 12 whole games I haven't tried yet.Not to mention the meta-narrative story and secrets woven across the collection. I've barely explored that side of UFO 50, but the fact that it's there is just another layer to what this game has to offer.For the price and the variety of full and fantastic games, UFO 50 is truly a steal. I cannot recommend it enough.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Disclosure: I got an early copy of the game for work. I've played every single game at least a little, and many of them quite a bit over the last few months, even while some were still being worked on.In short, there's not a single one I didn't enjoy at least a little bit, though some were tough to get into. Many of them I enjoyed a lot.My personal ton ten are:- 07 Velgress, the fast-paced action platfomer. I love getting into a zen state in which I see the path I must take to get as many coins as possible as I climb; when you're familiar enough with the platforms to know exactly how fast they'll decay, so you're not climbing in a panic anymore. When you're climbing calmly, you'll know you're on the road to mastering Velgress.- 10 Devilition, the tactical puzzler. Finding the perfect placements for all of your explosives is extremely satisfying.- 12 Avianos, the tactical resource war game. It's a perfect game for me. It has birds and dinosaurs and fantasy and tactical gameplay. I beat the game in one sitting because I couldn't stop playing it.- 13 Mooncat, the platformer with unusual controls. It takes some getting used to, but it's not actually very punishing since you're never sent very far back when you die. It's also just a beautiful game to see and listen to. Great vibes.- 22 Porgy, the undersea action explorer. It's just satisfying to play. It feels good to explore a little more each time, to map it all out and note things to come back to, and to grow in confidence as you take out the boss enemies. It's full of mysteries dying to be uncovered.- 28 Rail Heist, the stealth puzzle platformer. Just a strong concept overall, and extremely satisfying when you figure out a foolproof strategy to get your goods and escape unscathed.- 30 Rock On! Island, the tactical action defense game. It's not that complicated, but it takes some time to master. Heads up that you can upgrade your weapon at the base if you've got the resources!- 37 Valbrace, the dungeon exploration action RPG. You might want some grid paper on hand. Another game full of secrets and satisfying gameplay. New enemies can be rough when you first meet them, but there's always an effective strategy.- 40 Grimstone, the western jRPG. I just love jRPGs, even the clunky ones from the 80s that always require a fair bit of patience and grinding, but it's definitely not everyone's cup of tea. Still, there's a lot of game here to love if you're into it like I am.- 45 Mini & Max, the action exploration platformer. Just satisfying to play from moment to moment, with a world of stuff to explore. A clever setup with cute, compelling characters and tons of secrets.I haven't played the multiplayer games with friends yet, but I'm excited to try those out. I bet Elfazar's Hat is a blast with 2P coop.Anyway, I think there's something here for almost everyone. Take your time and give each game a shot. Every single game is packed with love.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever played a game where, midway through the adventure, you find some minigame inside of the game that you end up getting obsessed with? A la Gwent (Witcher 3), Tetra Master (FF9), or the arcade game in Stardew Valley? Imagine 50 of those in one package and you have UFO 50.There's truly something special here and I have so much more to go. The way it works is - each game becomes silver when played, gold when 'beaten' and cherry-colored when beaten under special conditions. Maybe it's beating without dying, maybe it's while getting the highest score, it varies game to game. So in my in my 15 current hours I have gotten silver in 5/50 gold in 2/50 and cherry in another 2/50 of the games. One of the cherry's (Barbuta) took me 7 hours to solve with all of the secrets. Then I played Mooncat, which was another joyous 2 hours. The other 5 games make up the other 8 or so hours, so they vary in length greatly. Every one of these games feels like it could have been your favorite game as a kid in the 80s and, even when I don't like the game itself, the charm built into it compels me to play more. That is to say, not every game is going to be for you, there's plenty I played and will likely not play again. But every game oozes passion and a desire to do something unique and, most importantly, fun. This collection is extremely fun and there is something for everyone. It's my 2024 GOTY. If the trailer at all is appealing to you, I can recommend it without hesitation. If it's not appealing, but you love games, it's worth checking out for the concepts, art, and music alone. I can't wait to play even more of it.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Perfectly captures the feel of getting a CD-Rom of 100s of old shareware titles and going through them, except most of the games in UFO 50 are actually good. From a game design point of view, i'm blown away. Most of the titles I've played have an interesting mechanic, and many of them are enjoyable. Absolutely worth the price of admission.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: The progress of video games from their birth up to now is a fascinating journey. When the shift from arcade cabinets to consoles happened in the 80s, it brought with it the start and popularization of genres that are still going strong today. Seeing what developers were thinking up while severely limited by memory space and graphical capabilities can be really cool. Experiencing them firsthand… well not so much.UFO 50 tells the tale of a fictional console from this period of time where video game were learning to crawl. The games it offers are all made with the idea that they came out alongside games like Metroid, The Legend of Zelda, Final Fantasy, Contra, etc. It’s a clever idea to tell the story of game development, and these fictional games are fully fledged experiences too. This is by no means a low effort undertaking. And as far as being accurate, they are pretty successful at recreating that era, which is kinda the problem. Those games I mentioned? Those were the ones that managed to rise to the top in a sea of garbage. UFO 50 isn’t just recreating those games, they are also recreating the failures.When I loaded up the first game in the pack, Barbuta, the fact that it was an obtuse piece of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ was cute. The controls were clunky as hell, the sprite work was very basic, and the mechanics were incredibly vague. When I loaded up the next 10 or so games and they were almost all just as frustrating to understand, the charm quickly wore off. The thing about old games is that while yes, many of them were like this, there were at least manuals or material that you could read which would explain the rules and goals of the game. You don’t get that here. UFO 50 also seems to be under the impression that the majority of games made in this time period were punishingly difficult and extremely fast paced, which is just not true. Many of the great console games of the 80s are pretty accessible and are much more reasonable in their difficulty and focused on precise timing and pattern memorization over fast twitch reflexes. Games like Castlevania and Ninja Gaiden were outliers rather than the norm. The fact that there are 50 full games to explore really works to the detriment of the overall experience when so many of them are simply not fun to play. I tried out just over a fifth of the games, and the excitement of exploring the library and trying something new faded away just as fast as it arrived. I found more interest in reading the history blurbs for each game that told stories of developers and studios, but even that was rather short with just a single sentence per game. I respect this game for trying to make an interactive experience out of looking back at the history of games, but I just don’t find it fun. I’d rather hunt down and play the real games which inspired the ones here.

_childDocuments_.review: It's almost unbelievable how good this pseudo-retro collection is. Most of the game design decisions made inside of it are absolutely stellar, I truly adore such delightful gameplay.I am 10 hours in, current completion (just the golden award, not the cherry challenge) - only FOUR games (out of 50!!!, not touching RPGs yet!), some games require an hour, some of them are deep enough to sink 10-20 hours into (moreover, there are a few roguelikes involving unique level generation), some of the games can be enjoyed every weekend as crazy, even addicting couch brawlers on par with Nidhogg, Samurai Gunn, Duck Game or Towerfall Ascension, absolute MOST of the collection is a polished, top-notch retrogaming experience, still reading the review? You will love UFO 50.My conclusion here - now I perceive it as the Little Pandora's Videogame Box, insatiably taking your time, giving you sleep deprivation, crushing your plans, playing with your nerves... but at the bottom of the box lie nostalgic, warm memories of NES/SNES/SEGA/GB gaming era, sense of achievement upon beating that hard rival/zone after dozens and dozens of tries and the last, but not least, pure gaming joy.

_childDocuments_.review: This pitch of this game makes it sound like you're getting 50 NES-Style mini/arcade games, which for the price would actually be a pretty worthwhile value.What you get is about 30 real genuine retro-inspired full fledged video games, and 20 of the minigames you were expecting. The value is insane. Multiple games in this pack could charge $10 themselves on Steam and probably do well. For the price this is worth grabbing because the act of just grabbing at games at random is really fun and SOMETHING in here will click with you.Highlights for me so far:Night Manor - Retro horror point and click adventure with multiple endings. Genuinely spooky.Warptank - Puzzle game about being a tank that can only teleport to whatever surface is vertical. It's got tons of levels and is really well designed and fun.Valbrace - First person dungeon crawling mixed with Punch-out style combat. It's a blast. Get a notebook to draw your own map.Grimstone - A FULL JRPG. IVE BEEN PLAYING FOR 10 HOURS. IT'S GREAT.Fist Hell - Coop beat-em up that's really tough but fun.Overbold - Smash TV but you have upgrades between rounds and can gamble on making the next round harder to get more cash to upgrade with. Tough but addicting.I haven't even tried every game in here. There's so much. Get this.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely insane value. After going through one time, 17 of the games landed on my faves, and many more will be added as I work through and try to get things. _childDocuments_.review: Didn't hear about it until it hit the social media waves, great game but I don't expect everyone to be a fan of all 50 games.Story: You get a collection of games from a fictious UFOSoft company that starts from its "First game" through 50 games that span a decade. Starts from a difficult barebones exploration game all the way to strategy games, full fledged RPG's, action games, racing games... all playable on the "LX console system." Even the historic "Don't put your name in games" trope is throughout as people use aliases.Gameplay: So you get 50 games, and each game has two levels of completion. One is the "Beat the game" gold trophy and then you get a cherry "Challenge" clear. Ranging from speed runs, score runs, deathless runs, finding things that require a level of finesse and expertise to achieve. The games in the collection run the gauntlet of every genre, and different levels of depth of some of those genres. Some of the games are really good, some of the games are ok, and some you are going to hate and wish it didn't exist. Controls are simplistic with dpad and 2 buttons and some controllers will accept stick VS dpad if you prefer that. Graphics: Its the 80's era stuff, not for everyone but definitely fits the theme of the game. As you play games in "chronological" order you start to go from base sprites to some detailed shading and things as the games get more advanced in sophistication but you aren't leaving a late 8/16 bit era vibe.9/10, but some of the gems outweigh some of the turds if you are willing to try all the games.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: The love to old school gaming from the MSX to PC88 is out in force with these games. I beat an optional boss just for the hell of it. All of this in 27 hours. I haven't even tried the other 40 games but for only 25 bucks this is a steal.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolutely incredible collection. I went into UFO 50 thinking most of the games would be simple, arcade-style experiences or interesting ideas without much fleshing out, but I couldn't have been more wrong. Every game is crafted with care and precision, and even the shorter ones left me amazed at their sheer creativity. And there's such a wide array of genres too -- it's got the usual platformers and shoot 'em ups you'd expect from an 80s throwback, but there's also puzzle games, strategy games, at least one roguelite, adventure games, multiple fully fledged RPGs, stealth games...it's such a joy to browse through the catalog and see what the next treasure will be.Even if you stick to your favorite genres, there's probably still dozens of hours of fun here. If you set out to 100% every game, it'll be more like hundreds of hours. This is the real deal. If any game in UFO 50 actually did release back in the 80s, it'd be a beloved classic to this day. _childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 is a game that had a lot of thought and effort put into it.. but it's just not good. While I understand that the overall point was to make up this whole fake developer that existed in the mid to late 80s, and said company basically did nothing but ape other developers, a lot of the games just feel bad to play.Take Rakshasa, which is essentially Ghouls n' Ghosts except with a more Contra-like map. Unlike either of those games, your character controls like a quadriplegic, your weapons have a range that can best be described as "annoyingly too short", you die in a single hit and you have one life. There is a "revival" mechanic that involves collecting things without getting hit, but that too is bad because enemies can spawn on the collectibles as you collect them, do contact damage, and have hitboxes from the first frame they pop into existence. There are also games like "Xevious but with objectively worse controls", "Lunar Lander only now there are enemies and a ceiling and the game can only realistically be finished by warping", and one that is effectively Syobon Action and is nothing but rote memorization as to which part of the ceiling or floor is going to collapse without any warning. If anything, the fictional UFO Soft is more like LJN, the company that did nothing but crap out movie tie-in games that sucked. I'd say avoid this unless you're a sadist.

_childDocuments_.review: Could you put a price on finding a box containing an unreleased game system from the 8-bit era complete with a library of 50 games?  If you grew up with an NES this game will take you back to being a kid again.  That feeling of trading carts with your friends on the schoolyard, renting a game from the local video store and finding it came with no manual, receiving a game you've never heard of from your grandparents for your birthday, saving up all summer mowing lawns to buy that game with the cool fantasy themed box art. UFO50 is an instant classic and must buy for anyone interested in the 8-bit era.

_childDocuments_.review: It's been so long since I played a game that I really had FUN playing. There are so many that look good, and they're clever, and the effects are neat, but I find it increasingly hard to find a game I crave. I sit there plucking up the energy to play. That's not how it should be.Then, on a complete whim, I bought UFO 50. The price is ridiculous - expensive enough that I felt stupid for not buying a major release that I'm *supposed* to enjoy, and cheap enough that if even a couple of the 50 games are fun then I got my money's worth.  Well surprise surprise, they're all Awesome! I've only played 4 of these so far, and I'm already completely satisfied from them. I just completed by second game and had that smug sense of achievement that I haven't felt in years.  I immediately wanted to have my friends and family play too. It's one of Those kinds of games!So yeah, if you have ever enjoyed retro games (8 bit, 16bit etc.) then stop thinking and just buy this. $0.50 a game and way more fun than those adrenaline pumping safe A-list games everyone's talking about. _childDocuments_.review: I don't think there is ever going to be a 'perfect' moment to review this game. It is so notoriously BIG. Colossal. Monumental in size and scope.  In a nutshell what it is: A fake imaginary company has made a set of games for a imaginary machine called LX. These are the games that have been 'salvaged' (from a garage?). In reality it's like loading up a ROM set for some unknown console from the 1982-1989 era and diving in. Games reflect that. So why should you care? If you are into anything retro then check it out but if you are having doubts then please look into gameplays and reviews. Some are refunding because they dont like the first game that is deliberately very plain. After all according to the fake development story 'it was made in secret as a side project at work and nearly got the dev fired'. And from there the fake game company story opens up as you play the 50 different games, all available to you right away. And the Meta.... there is actually a 51:st game as well that covers all the games but that is for the player community at large to find out and it will take time so if you want to contribute to this wild treasure hunt for meta and secrets buy in now and get into it. For once here is a game that has not been spoiled to pieces yet and it will take considerable time before it is in such a state, the content is just so massive. 10/10 potential, GOTY 2024 potential and GOAT potential.  Period.  Impossible to give a proper x/10 grading now as my hours are not even close to what they should be.

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played Night Manor so far. Just beat it tonight. I got to the "bad" ending on my own, but got stuck on the "good" ending because there's one door that *really* doesn't look like a door and I completely missed it. So I cheated and looked up a playthrough. Glad I did, though! Awesome game.I commented on this elsewhere, but I really love how they've back-ported modern game design into the retro form-factor. I grew up playing NES games. I know how difficult they could be and how painful the puzzles could be. By comparison Night Manor is extremely generous. I'm told you get a little bonus for never "dying", but there's no major consequence if you do die. You're just placed back at the start with all of your progress saved.There is one puzzle that I didn't get on my own and I somewhat resent the game design for it. There are a *ton* of objects you can inspect that have descriptions designed to tell you not to waste your time investigating them any further. But one of those objects actually has a critical clue hidden inside and you need to use a specific item on it to get that clue. Otherwise it's nice to see how far we've come in the field of game design.Some things I loved:* When the monster shows up your cursor shakes in fear and you need to fight it.* If you shoot the monster the cursor changes into a little crosshair.* There are a number of photos, dark corners, and mirrors where you will see a flash of a face or hand. Just a small touch but very cute.* The endings have a twist.* The dark theme and aesthetic. I don't feel like any 80s games had this quite so well figured out. It feels like a classic 80s horror movie turned into a NES game and given the polish that SMB3 got. Very Resident Evil inspired but running within the technical constraints of a NES-like system.If this game was available on the NES I am sure of 2 things:1. 80s parents would have assumed Night Manor was going to turn their children into satanic worshipers.2. We'd consider this one of the greatest NES games. Absolute credit to the creators here, but this is mostly down to how we stand on the shoulders of giants. Taking modern wisdom and using it within old constraints makes our progress really stand out.

_childDocuments_.review: this isnt meant to be clown react bait but i sure feel like im going to get a bunch for saying all this.put simply, this is extremely not my thing, frankly. i only liked 8 out of the 50 games because the vast majority of them to me felt either too obtuse, too difficult, or just straight werent fun or engaging to play. if youre someone like me who doesnt exactly have the highest of attention spans for games especially when it comes to 8 bit retro games you're likely going to bounce just as hard as i have off this. the description says "we carefully chose what elements to modernize" but frankly i don't think they tried hard enough, the vast majority of these just feel like good ideas for games that are not fleshed out past the initial concept and were needlessly shoved into the limitation of "fake nes game" which ends up making them play like sh*t half the time because two buttons is nowhere near enough for what they're trying to do. if it werent so tied up in trying to be nes adjacent then this would probably be an enjoyable exploration of weird ideas for games. presentation wise its also kind of a huge ball of missed opportunity and disappointment. this came out well after last call bbs, zachtronics' final game which also went with a "this system definitely existed, heres some of the games for it look" vibe and the sheer level of comprehensiveness that title went through to make it look and feel like you were truly reviving old hardware and software was astounding. ufo 50 however doesn't really feel like it tries at all with this; in fact it feels like the whole set up of the fake system and company was completely an afterthought more than anything else that is so bafflingly slapped together that it feels as if they shouldn't have bothered.it feels...confused. it wishes to evoke being a flashcart for the aforementioned fake system vibes, but the way it approaches doing this - and in general how it starts up - gives it the vibe that this is more of an "atari 50" style approach where it is a modern piece of software compiling the historical gameography of ufo soft for future generations to experience. it doesnt seem to know if it wants to be one or the other, and as a result we have this bizarre situation where everything outside of the games also seems to somehow be within the fake system which doesnt really make much sense to me. and then you have the really clumsy menu system which feels like it wouldve been far better suited as a list with screenshots and game info being perpetually on screen off to the side so it can be more easily conveyed what the heck is going on in a game. the dusting off animation is only cute the first couple of times, when you have 50 of these games it becomes a weird brief element of tedium tbh.like visually this entire thing is bloody gorgeous but the entire encasing premise that surrounds these 50 games is disruptive to the entire concept in a way that actively bothers me just as much as i think that the way it advertises it self in the description is a little too generous and stretched from the truth. so yeah its just. tl;dr this is a bag of bizarre design choices, poor difficulty curving, false expectations and missed potential for me. you'll probably like it. but i really did not, in a lot of ways that really irk me. but hey, that's games, it aint all for everyone is it now. im curious to see what exactly theyll be changing in upcoming patches if at all and i might revisit this in future if it gets tightened up more and is less busy trying to mimic old nes games of yore slightly too hard.

_childDocuments_.review: In the current gaming landscape, the unabashedly retro UFO 50 feels like a breath of fresh air. Firing it up feels like the perfect antidote to what often feels wrong with modern game design. No need to spend hours getting through the opening cinematics and tutorial stages just to find out that it's the same thing you've already played a thousand time before. Just a few button presses and you're in. For anyone who grew up before the PlayStation era, the types of games that make up this collection should be instantly recognizable: adventure games, puzzle games, sports titles, and many more. When you launch a new one, the basic gameplay tends to be immediately obvious. Despite relying on only two buttons, many of these have a surprising amount of subtlety and depth; some even take hours to finish. UFO 50 isn't content just to rehash the tropes of those genres, but adds its own twist to whatever it does. The golf game isn't just a golf game, but also a sidescrolling sci-fi platformer. The adventure game isn't just a adventure game, but a procedurally generated open world exploration game. As such, what really makes UFO 50 stand out is not the way it is retro but the way it modernizes old tropes.Playing these games doesn't feel like they were made by someone taking their first steps towards understanding game design - rather they feel like a creative outlet for someone feeling burnt out from spending years on large game projects. These comparatively tiny games (some can be played from start to finish in as little as 15 minutes) seem to have no room in a gaming industry that favors blockbuster titles over small yet imaginative projects. In a strange way, I found that spending hours on UFO 50 didn't make me nostalgic for the glory days of NES, but I found myself missing the Flash game scene where a small game with an interesting idea could unexpectedly find itself in front of millions of players around the world. As such, I hope UFO 50 can find itself an audience large enough to inspire a cottage industry of similarly high-quality titles.
