_childDocuments_.review: I rarely leave Steam reviews, but its equally as rare that I'm blown away by a game like I have been with UFO 50. Considering the price of $25 USD, the package has an insane value, with 50 games at about 50 cents per (as a reminder) fully-fledged game. Even if you don't LOVE every single one, you're bound to find a least a couple that sink their teeth into you, sometimes taking an 1-5 hours to experience everything in. There really is something for everyone here, if you're okay with the charming 8-bit aesthetic, and don't mind not jiving with 100% of the content in a given game, I think UFO 50 is well worth a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: A collection of great NES-inspired games for fans of retro games.As of writing this review, I have only tried around half of the games on this collection and have enjoyed around 85% of what I have tried. The collection has platformers, tactics games, a JRPG, metroidvanias, and more.If I had one complaint for the collection, it would be the absurd difficulty of most of the games. They are fun, but these games feel like they took 'NES hard' a bit too seriously at times.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: In 2021 I got really into retro games, particularly from the NES/SNES era.  There is a unique charm to those games, games that were made before design ideas were solidified.  They could be more experimental, sometimes for the best, sometimes for the worst.  But the enjoyment of experimenting with and figuring out games like that is something special.  Something that is much harder to come by with modern gaming, which often have to tread established paths for the sake of survivability. This game (collection) somehow manages to recreate that experience, it is like discovering a long lost gaming time capsule.  Filled with truly unique experiences, and while some of the ideas inside this collection don't jive with me necessarily, the vast majority of the games are incredible.  The experience of tinkering and fiddling and just immersing yourself in this game is something I will not forget soon.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: The mad lads at Mossmouth have done it: they've gamified the concept of playing videogames. For anyone who enjoys digging through archived media, piecing together the connective tissue between the works, and falling in love when you least expect it. UFO 50 is more than the sum of its playable parts, it is a meditation on the world's strangest most fascinating form of entertainment and a love letter to the incredible people behind it. There is a reason why those bored business software engineers were destined to take that first bold step into a new realm of creativity and imagination. When given the right tools, art finds its way out of the soul. #1 Thorson Petter fan signing off.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Action 52 if every game was a banger.Each game has 3 main goals. A Gift (usually get halfway through a game), gold cartridge (beat the game) and cherry cartridge (100% a game, beat a high score, time trial etc).The real genius is you will boot up a game, think it's a stinker and think "okay I'll just get the gift and move on" but in doing so you will teach yourself the mechanics and actually appreciate the twist on a genre. Next thing you know you are playing 10 hours of Party House going for the cherry.It's so much more than 50 games in 1. Everything works together in ways it's hard to explain. If you love video games you owe it to yourself to buy this and rediscover why you fell in love in the first place.This should be Game of the Year.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: There's a nice mix of classic arcade games and more modern/experimental games done with a retro aesthetic. All of them extremely high quality. You aren't going to personally like every one, but there's so many that you're bound to find at least a handful you really enjoy. Party House alone made me feel like I got my money's worth.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 feels like a miracle in today's gaming landscape. I've only played 5 titles, in mostly chronological order (play Pilot Quest early!), and each title has been enjoyable in their own way. The joy of discovering what each of the fifty games are, how they play, and familiarizing yourself with its nuances is a wonderful experience. Since these games are old school, each title demands your attention to progress and failure is pretty punishing; such as in Barbuta and Bug Hunter. You can tell each game had a lot of thought and care poured into it, even when some titles seem janky on purpose. UFO 50 has so much charm and a crowning achievement in gaming for the quality it delivers and the value you get from a $25 dollar purchase. With 50 separate, realized games, there's something for everyone!
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Something for everyone, this collection will likely pan out to be the greatest bang for your buck value for years to come, and an essential for anyone's library the same way Team Fortress 2 was.My only issue with the game is that apparently it's intensive enough to require a dedicated GPU for it. On the one hand, getting all of the games to work properly, let alone be fun to play, is a mammoth accomplishment. I think most of the games were smartly designed and justified to exist apart from their influences. On the other hand, the fact that my computer I bought just four years ago with 16GB of RAM struggles to handle games with pixel art is insane to me. It can handle Bloodstained, but not this? Not without putting the video settings available to be low, anyway.But make no mistake - this collection is legit. Some of these are strong enough to be standalone titles and I hope that maybe without a strong enough demand from players, we could see a Campanella 4 or a Mortol 3 or a Warptank 2. Their design concepts have too much potential to be left alone.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 oozes style masterful game design.I've barely scratched the surface of what's on offer, but I've seen enough to recommend UFO 50 wholeheartedly. This is something special. Evey game included has depth and polish. There's a delicate balance of old vs new styles of game design and mechanics. It feels nostalgic and new at the same time, and you get to have that feeling fifty times.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: A masterclass in game design. If you can push past the prickly beginning, you will find a treasure trove of incredibly well polished and cleverly designed full games spanning a huge variety of genres. Every single game in the collection is interesting to explore, and most are basically digital crack. Perhaps one of the best bang-for-your-buck games ever.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: been looking up for this game since it was annouced, really wasn't expecting it to be this GOOD.I've been reccomending this to several friends but i will understand if this isn't their type of game, to remain faithful to the era these games were supposed to be released some old-fashioned aspects will turn people away, such as difficulty selection, lack of checkpoints, and always starting on level one in most of the games.but without these the experience might not be as genuine. Amazing game, will show to my dad.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: An endlessly impressive look into an alternative universe where there was another competitor in the console wars of the late eighties to early nineties, UFO 50 is, believe it or not, a collection of 50 games [note: there may or may not be more than 50 games] all of which offer fantastic blends of modern design concepts with old-school design limitations. A fascinating set of games, all fun in their own right, with an intriguing overarching story and alternate reality 90s mascots for you to get attached to.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: 36 hours in and I've only played about half the games. I know it's been said many times before, but I am in awe of this project and how much depth there is to this game. There is so much variety to package that inevitably there is something that will click. Arcade action, puzzle, strategy, metroidvania, deckbuilder, it has so much to offer. Another underrated aspect is that every game limits itself to the d-pad and two buttons. This really shows the versatility available even with limited button inputs. I'm so impressed and could ramble about this forever. If you have any appreciation for retro games PICK THIS UP.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I would highly encourage you to ignore al the negative reviews that played for less than an hour and came to the conclusion that there's no depth to it, it still might not be for you but I feel like I've only barely scratches the surface so far, I've not even tried over half the games yet. Above all else it's a game about game design, which just scratches such sn itch in my brain, some of the games are fairly simple NES style arcade games while others offer some pretty astounding hidden depths. If you really sink your teeth in each game you can really tell the devs went above and beyond to make each one a real experience, and theres 50 of them!! Now excuse me while I go back and sink another hour into Magic Garden.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: The LX2 was a console in the 80's with a lineup of unusual games. The companies and programmers and designers all had complex lives and stories. In another reality. Not ours. That is the conceit of UFO 50 - you get to play the emulated games from a history that never happened, a decade not from our earth, but one parallel to it. Each game has a story, a history, none of which happened in our timeline. All the games are at least interesting, and some are quite good, even great - just as you would expect from several years of a console's life. This is a wonderbox of surprises and little joys, and if you can play along with the alternate universe notion, it is like stepping into a childhood you never had, from a world so close, yet not exactly, our own.I have greatly been enjoying, and savoring, this collection from another earth. If you are weird like me, you will too. This is worth your time, and your money.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: i would be lying if i said some of these games didn't turn me into the Freakin' Angry Video Game Nerd but the overall quality is so high - even in the ones that have admittedly overtuned difficulty - that it's impossible not to recommend this. i spent more time on just Bug Hunter, Avianos, and Devilition than i spend on some entire games that i've paid more than 25 dollars for, and i haven't even gotten to 70% of the games on UFO 50's roster. crazy!
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I've tried out 30 games out of 50 at the time of this review and I've already encountered 5 I would've bought on their own merits as standalone games, plus another ten that I thoroughly enjoyed the limited time I played them for. You will come across games in genres you don't care for here, and maybe 3 or 4 duds, but if you're one of those "hours per dollar" people you're going to blow past that here even just from trying out each game let alone trying to beat a handful of them.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I love video games. And as a person who loves video games, I love video games that love video games. I just finished Astro Bot last week, a game designed to celebrate the history of the PlayStation systems while also taking a look into the future of what lies ahead for the genre of 3D platforming. I think it takes a special game developer to be able to harness that feeling. To understand that concept, and feed it back to the player in a meaningful way, and that game captures that feeling almost perfectly.This game (or, collection of games) takes that celebration of PlayStation games, picks it up between its index finger and thumb before launching it 2500 feet away. Astro Bot is incredible, as a game and as a celebration of games, and yet this game is a celebration of ALL GAMES, and the experience of loving games.Inside this game are 50 games, all unique spins on concepts you’ve likely seen if you’ve ever perused the vast library of early NES or MasterSystem games. However, these games all come away as the best possible outcome of their parts: they take those concepts, apply something new to them, and make them feel new and exciting. Not only that, but the lack of information here is incredibly fun. This is the first game I’ve played where I wish I was part of a Gaming Book Club, because this game would be what eats up that time. This game facilitates that kind of gameplay.To say that this is an indie game that will be regarded as one of the greats is to do a disservice to everything that is happening here. This is a peek into a gaming legacy that never existed in the best possible way— and a box of ideas executed so well that you’ll find they grab hold of you in a way your classic Donkey Kings and Pack-Guys never did.The devs of this collection love games, and gaming history. They deserve all the awards for this. I cannot believe there are 50 of these. I cannot wait to play them all, to really sink time into them, and experience their secrets. This is such an exciting piece of media and I’m so glad I got to be here for part of it. Hope that if you have read this far, you will too.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Just...wow. I'm gonna paraphrase another reviewer who pointed out that this game takes the framework of old NES games (similar gameplay and aesthetic limitations) and adds modern spins on all of them. From Bug Hunter's Into The Breach style breadth of information to the wider amount of movement expression in its platformers, UFO 50 is more than the sum of its parts. It is 50 excellent games.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Very impressed at how deep each game is. For a game which is a collection of 50 games you'd think each one would be surface level mini games. Surprisingly, each game is fleshed out and can offer hours and hours of content. Some of them are very difficult too. It shows the best sides of 80's era videogames in a complete package. I could see completionists taking hundreds of hours to get everything done. If I had a complaint, it would be the odd choice to only have two buttons for all 50 games. It felt like a needlessly limiting constraint for some of the more complex games. Otherwise a pretty fun game.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I expected to admire this game for it's wild ambition and scope but to not gel with the games itself as old school stuff hasn't grabbed me before. I was very wrong. I've only tried 10 games, and of those I'd say three are genuinely brilliant, five are interesting and good fun, and two are not my bag but I can appreciate the idea. I can see this sucking up most of the rest of my year, and il be dipping back in to these first ten for many hours more.Amazing achievement and great fun!
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I still can't believe this is exists. The fantasy that those cheap, bootleg, "50 games in 1" rip off plug and play consoles alighted in our naive young brains has finally been made real. I'm not even done looking at all the games but I've already found at least 10 that I know I'm going to spend hours and hours on.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played 3 games in the collection so far, but they were all fun and interesting games that feel like a throwback to old school games with a much better understanding of game and level design than most companies had back in the day. Even if the other 47 games are garbage I feel like what I've played already has justified the $25 purchase. And I would bet another $25 that there's going to be plenty more amazing stuff for me to find. Honestly, I was shocked that this game is only being sold for $25, because I was expecting to have to pay around $50 or more. It's an absolute bargain for this price, you will probably find something you love here.That said, I will caution that this game takes after retro games. If you don't like retro games at all, this might not be for you (although, I don't really like retro games much and I'm enjoying it). More importantly, it might take more time than you're used to before you start clicking with a game. In 2 out of the 3 games I've tried so far, it took me a good 10-15 minutes of play time before I really got into it. So if you dip your toe in for 5 minutes and you're not feeling it, try sticking around for a little more before you hop to something else.Overall, what I've played of this game so far is great. There's a ton of variety too, so most people can probably find something to love here, assuming the quality remains high throughout the collection. Highly recommended
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to write an in-depth review for those people on the fence about this game and not buying into the hype wholeheartedly. UFO 50 is absolutely a labor of love by it's developers, and as someone who grew up in the era these games are imitating they absolutely should appeal to me, but they do not. There is a classic trap that many "old school but new" games fall into when trying to emulate the era. That is the fallacy that old games had to have insane difficulty spikes and punishing game play.Take a look at some classic NES games for illustration of what I mean. Any Mario game will start off easier and slowly ramp up the challenge as you get deeper into the game, however the curve is balanced by not only doing that super late into the game but also by introducing new power ups and giving you alternate routes if you are clever enough to find them. Even games like Contra that are notorious for their difficulty do not punish you for not making pixel perfect jumps or exact to the second timing on your inputs. And even in the rare cases where games did expect that level of skill such as Ghost And Goblins, or Megaman, they kept the gameplay loop interesting enough that you wanted to keep trying.And sadly UFO 50 does none of that. Every single game in this series will give you one or two levels to get interested in them and then SLAM you with an insane difficulty spike. And there are also many games in this collection where the game play loop is just...bad, or boring, really really boring. Add to that the asinine control schemes of many of the titles, as well as the lack of easy to follow instructions... I just do not think this collection is the right choice for most people who are not absolutely desperate for new content from the 80s-90s era of gaming. Having said all of that there are a few games I enjoyed such as Ninpek, Mortol (both games), and Warptank. Warptank in fact easily stands up to even the best games of that era in my opinion. But at the end of the day having just a small few games that I enjoyed did not make the collection worth the price to me. I appreciate the dedication of the developers who participated in this, but at the end of the day they missed the mark on the vast majority of these games. I genuinely believe that nostalgia for their childhood is a huge factor in why so many people gave this collection positive reviews.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: It's not fair...I already have too many games to play and now I have fifty more?!In all seriousness though, it's difficult to express just how much of a technical and artistic achievement UFO 50 is. All the games have enough of a shared aesthetic that it's very easy to believe they all came out on the same hardware, but there's still a truly massive variety of game types, lengths, difficulties, and art and music styles. You can even follow the growth of the company's skill through the years, from the obtuse but mysterious debut title Barbuta to the exquisitely designed final release, Cyber Owls.Is every game going to resonate perfectly with every player? No, but there's such a wide variety here that you'll likely find enough that keep you coming back over and over again. As for myself, have sampled every game and "favorited" 17 games so far which comes out to a criminally cheap $1.47 per favorite - and that's not counting the four games that I enjoy so much that I think any one of them would be worth the full price on its own.This collection is an instant classic, a definite GOTY 2024 contender, and a shining example of what games can be if they are developed for passion instead of profit.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Takes me back to playing new NES games on the floor in a friend's basement in the early 90's. or later days when you'd burn 1200 NES ROMs to a CD and play them emulated on an modded original PlayStation. This is amazing. And compared to most pack-ins I've played, so many of these are ingenious. Never thought I'd be describing a game as a refreshing take on "Snake," or, "Pong." Not to mention all the strategy puzzlers. The games are better than your average PICO-8 best-of collection, but compared to that particular experience, you lose something of the weird outsider art vibe. Don't get me wrong, there's plenty of weirdness and innovation to be enjoyed if that's your vibe, it just never quite reaches that border-line unplayable sublime peak inscrutability of certain other retro-modern experiences. Putting all these games together into a collection of 50 was a masterstroke of marketing - so many of these really need to be played in bits and pieces because it takes spaced repetition to really assimilate the required playstyle.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I'll give a more complete review once I have played more.The simplest way I can put it is--if you found a turbografx or sharp x68000 in a storage unit loaded with 50 games with all kinds of genres represented but no manuals.  That's essentially the experience you're getting.Many of the different games vary a bit in difficulty but I'd describe it a bit as 50 puzzles to solve.  Every game where I feel it's difficult, it's because I a) don't have a manual and b) part of the game is figuring out and testing mechanics to find the easier path through the game.  Some games I indeed found this frustrating, as games from the 80s--especially your strategy titles, would have 50-100+ page manuals detailing all kinds of game mechanics details.To some degree, that is this game's gimmick and although this was initially a massive turn off to me.  This turned around as I see the insane attention to detail and how the reward structure exists in each game.The entire package has an insane amount of charm and nostalgia.  You will recognise many similar arcade and video games you'll played that inspired these games.  Everything has nice quirky twists and there's plenty of feel of the ol nethack 'the devs dd indeed think of that'.Definitely worth it.  Even if there's like 5 games in this you really enjoy, you'll get plenty of enjoyment out of this at the price point.Also note--there's a ton of these games you can play with friends over steam/remotely excellently.  This is a major add and thought to a package like this.--Updates on specific games:Velgress is absolutely terrible.  I hope the devs address issues and feedback that have been brought up about game's difficulty.  Many of my friends would find Velgress unfun and lacking in game design.  I've been through about half the games so about 20 of them being good and fun and I feel rewarding to the player, that is--if you follow what you're being shown and learn the game...it's reasonably possible to finish all the achievement for it as a new player within a reasonable time.  Velgress is not so and you're not even afforded the opportunity to practice the harder parts of the game so you know how to better prepare or even understand how things work.  Grind 5+ minutes to get there, lose in a second without learning anything.  That's the terrible experience that dark souls is that some have converted the grotesque idea that that is 'good' game design.  No, no it is not.Even worse is Star Waspir.  It's incredibly rough to play, with background scrolling and bullets everywhere that it's incredibly difficult to actually see what is happening.  The game, similar to Velgress is short, but needs some serious work as I'd say this one is nearly unplayable and really unfair unless you specifically are an expert I guess in this genre and don't have disabilities that make it difficult to play.  Star Waspir is the worst game so far in the 50 I've played.  It, similar to Velgress, has all the worst of the genres it mimics and none of the good.  As a raidenx clone, it has the strange property that options/side guns take damage.  This means you constantly have to collect upgrades on a playfield you cannot actually tell what is going to damage you and because the gun options are awful (you pick from 3 ships, all are terrible) between the ships, you're left with this really awkward game.  There are 2 powerups and you must spell a 3 letter word such as EGG for a score multiplier, or GGG for a gun or EEE for a TEMPORARY gun upgrade.  Naturally losing a ship means you lose all gun/options as well, so losing a ship frequently means immediate game over despite not being able to permanently upgrade the gun.  The options can shoot homing missiles and give you better angles your main gun cannot do well.  They also made the really awkward decision, despite having 2 buttons, to only allow you to rhythmically tap to spread fire or to hold for constant fire.  It hurts quite a bit to be constantly doing this and the spread shot is terrible anyway because the screen is loaded with projectiles to avoid too fast anyway.  Hopefully more patches are coming.  The rallyx/crush roller game didn't need the cherry score reduced if Velgress/Star Waspir aren't getting their difficulty and really accessibility issues fixed.  But these also require more work than simply lowering a score threshold.  If you had HP or something, both would probably be fine.  Otherwise you have so many winners in ufo50, I'd not let 2 games ruin it, but they're so significantly different than the rest of the catalog, it needs to be noted.  As I said prior, the rest of the games careful play/paying attention/solving the puzzle that is finding advantages in game mechanics, etc. will reward a player of ANY skill level and that's a reasonable achievable goal to any reasonable player.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like exploring a BBC Micro or early Amiga and a case of random floppies. Modern game design helps take the edge off in terms of controls and some design decisions but many games are difficult and require some time to learn and become good at. Quite a few are deeper than expected, there's a Metal Storm-esque mech metroidvania, a JRPG about cowboys, 2 fun twists on Humans/Lemmings, at least 2 excellent turn based strategy games, and an action based dungeon crawler to name a few. Everyone will have at least one favourite game out of the collection, probably from the more complex ones, but even the smaller arcade style games are fun to play though some don't entirely follow through with their ideas and feel a little too basic.There's also a meta story about a fictional developer for a fictional 8-bit system and hidden codes you input to unlock a few different things including alternate modes for some games and a hidden extra game. Even if you don't engage with this part of the package it's still worth the price of entry as the bulk of the content lies in the games that are all unlocked and presented from the start. Some of these are so good the contributing developers really need to expand those ideas. The micro point and click horror game in particular is a 10/10 worth the price of entry on its own. Similarly the Metal Storm style metroidvania needs a sequel, no questions asked.Lastly, the negative: difficulty in some games is punishing for the modern gaming mindset and might put some people off before they discover the joy of exploring and coming back to these games like you would in the '80s. It's not a knock on UFO 50 for being difficult, but a few of the games would have greatly benefited from at least a small leaflet style manual to clue the player in on a bit more information, even us older gamers can be left in the dark on a couple of small details that would have not been a frustration if explained or hinted at.Verdict: Buy it if you want an instant collection that far surpasses its value. Feels like picking up an old BBC Micro at a car boot sale and rummaging through the disks to see what's fun.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: May as well leave a review now because I anticipate playing this game for hundreds of hours. I've never anticipated a game so much and somehow UFO 50 still lived up to the hype. These are extremely challenging games, and one of the magic common threads that weaves through all of them is how learnable improving your skill is in each of them. It can be a little crushing early on feeling like an inadequate gamer if you run through all 50 games 5 minutes at a time. But if you go back for a 2nd or 3rd try and are willing to dig deep, nearly every game presents an extremely satisfying challenge after you finally get the win. The alternate win conditions (cherry carts) give some replayability and additional motivation to keep playing; or at least they're doing that for me. If you're a nerd for great game design, love a concept album type of vibe, are an achievement hunter, or just love a series of challenges across a huge variety of genres, I recommend checking this out. I think this is a once in a generation type of game that will be talked about, speedrun, and refined for years.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I tried all 50 games before posting, some longer than others.Most of the games are simple, most of them are smaller than others, but none of them feel incomplete. They're all a wide variety of genres and most of the games are completely unique from the others. Some of them are pretty straightforward, and a few of them feel borderline experimental. It's ... weird.My only complaint is most of them play very slow, even slower than an NES game would have played.I'd say for 25 bucks, you'll definitely find at least a handful you'll enjoy. I certainly enjoyed at least half of them. Works great on Steam Deck, which really feels like the best environment for a collection like this.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece. The amount of content you're given for the price tag is phenomenal. You probably won't love all 50 games but there is such a variety of creative games, that there are going to be many games you will adore. The length of games will vary greatly from game to game.Its's basically a modernized beefed up NES library. I've played all the games and only fully completed a couple so far, but I've seen enough to know that I can't wait to fully dive into each one. It has rpgs, metroidvanias, racing games, rougelites, shoot em ups, puzzle games, point and click horror, and all kinds of insanely creative games with fresh inventive mechanics and ideas that are not seen elsewhere. This is an easy recommend at full price. Easy to pick up, hard to put down.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Peak FictionWhile not every game will be a hit depending on what type of player you are, there is definitely a few games in the collection that will be favorites for someone. I am not exactly a massive fan of this era of games, nor did I grow up with them, so I'm not exactly biased towards the 'genre'.Add on the presentation, music, background story, and general retro games qualities it all adds up to be an experience like nothing else. Also, with a price tag of $25, at 50 cents a game its quite the deal. At the time of writing this review, I have 40 hours played have beaten 5 games and played 25 games in total. So there is a lot of content available for the price, and none of the games could be described as mini-games (like WarioWare).If I had to describe UFO 50 in one word: Charming
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Probably too soon to give it a proper review, but I wanted to say I like everything about this game "collection".  It's like it's 1989 and I'm at the video store deciding which game to rent for the weekend and only being able to look at the box.  Instructions? Already missing from the last person who rented it.  Internet walkthrough? Doesn't exist.  Every game I messed around with was a lot higher quality than I expected.  I can't wait to give each game a deep dive and take my time figuring out how they each play.  I can see how anyone who didn't grow up in this era wouldn't appreciate it though.  But for us..older people...it's a no-brainer.  Get it.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This is really an incredible game. I wasn't entirely sure what to expect, I assumed there'd be 50 bite-sized games and I think that would've been perfectly fine. However, it was anything but.The 50 games in UFO 50 are incredibly high quality, varied, full experiences in their own right. Everything from classic arcade style games, platformers, strategy games; the game is bursting with creativity and care. There are so many games in this that I'd buy on their own and be able to put hours and hours into.I'm not super fond of every game in the pack, but I think that's part of the beauty of it. In representing the entire history of a fictional game company's output, they also represent all the historical limitations, experimentation, and variety that comes with that.I think this game is an incredible achievement and well worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I originally bounced off these games hard because they felt like they wouldn't be much my speed. I am not used to playing NES games or any older, more brutal arcade style titles with little direction. I thought that I'd be shoveling through a pile of garbage for the few small gems that may be there. Boy was I wrong. The game is excellent. Lots of unique ideas, lots of exciting games of entirely different genres, local co-op, mysteries, beautiful art, carefully crafted music; it's truly a full package. Of these 50 games, I've tried a mere 7, beaten 2, and enjoyed several of those with the couch co-op functionality. There's still much more to see and do, and none of it has been dull thus far.I'd love to see more ambitious projects like this one and I sincerely hope that some of the games in this package get expanded upon into even bigger games, or maybe even inspire other games of a similar nature. There is a lot to love and I'm glad that I gave this a chance.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: The more that I play of UFO50, the more convinced I am that this is my personal 2024 GOTY which is high praise considering Balatro also came out this year. I've only tried out 20 out of the 50 games so far and I'm having a blast. I've currently cherried (fully completed) 10 of the games and I'm slowly working my way through the other 10 and and I still have 30 games left! This game might not be for everyone, but if you enjoy old school games or pixel art, then you're likely to find at least 1 game in the collection worth your time. As an experiment, I'll try to keep this review updated with a max 3 sentence review of each individual game that I cherry below (potential spoilers):A fun little puzzle game focusing on strategically camouflaging to avoid predators, find collectibles, and return to the safety of your home. Not too difficult, but I had a pleasant hour with this oneLove child between snake and pac-man. Really addicting to shoot for high scoresI had a blast playing this one. The mechanic where you decide how difficult the next round will be by purposely increasing the number of enemies for a better monetary reward is a wonderful risk-reward system that exposed my greed many timesArena fighting game where each character has a unique movement mechanic and weapon. This one caused a bit of frustration as I felt like sometimes the CPU was essentially cheating, but I had enough fun where I've come back to play a round even after getting the cherryPoint and click horror game that is unique in the collection. I thought the puzzles were very solid and the killer/story was interesting to me. The music also really adds to the atmosphereThis is essentially the Upwell to Downwell's existence. It be ben quite chaotic as you panic jump and shoot your way up and out of the pit. Heavy "one more run" energyArcade autoscroller ninja game. When playing through the collection in chronological order originally, this was the first game that made me think there was more to UFO50 than what I thought. That being said some of the later games in the pack definintely sent Ninpek down my tier listSubmarine metroidvania. This one was tough to get into at first. The early game is absolutely brutal, but as you get upgrades to your sub this quickly climbed to be one of my favourite games in the pack so farI think this one could've used some expanding. Its essentially just a virtual horserace gambling simulator and while the quibbles are cute, I wish there was a bit more to the gameDeckbuilder roguelike focused on throwing the best party by filling out your rolodex with party guests that give you popularity and money. This is probably the most complete game in the pack and it is consistently touted as an amazing game. There is room here for this to be a standalone game as it, the random scenarios are very addictingThis is a unique spin on pong where you play as a samurai with unique hits and movement abilities that was quite fun to play. The characters have different playstyles and I enjoyed learning the best way to play each different samuraiIts a fun mario kart-lite that makes very in-universe sense. It was a nice palate cleanser, however the lack of different maps and no CC settings for varying levels of difficulty makes this one of the least fleshed out games in the packI enjoyed Kick Club, its a level by level affair where you need to use a soccer ball to destroy enemies that are personifications of non-soccer sports. I think they're a bit too stingy with the lives and the lack of a save and continue function made cherrying this game slightly frustratingMooncat is amazing. The less you know about it the better, but the music is phenomenal and the gameplay is intuitive once you get used to itA somewhat bullet hell game about escaping an evil magician's hat. I enjoyed the upgrade system and the game was fair when it came to gathering extra lives. I do feel like some of the earlier bosses and minibosses are easier than the final bosses which was a bit disappointing.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: If you've got any nostalgia from sitting around and playing retro, cartridge based games that only used a couple of buttons, UFO 50 is the best deal on Steam right now.  Otherwise, it might *only* be an insanely good deal.It's like somebody grabbed an NES or Master System from an alternate reality and dropped it into your steam library.  If the fictional console featured in this game was actually competing against Nintendo and Sega, back in the day, I have no idea which company would've won the console wars.  They do have the advantage of more than 30 years of game design philosophy to draw from, but the games do honestly feel as if they were legitimate games from back in the day.There are a couple games on here that honestly are worth the cost of the whole pack.  Many of them are worth five or ten dollars on their own.  Every single one is worth more than the 50 cents per you pay to get the whole collection.  You'd have paid around a thousand dollars in 1980s currency to buy the equivalent to this collection back in the day, or spent hundreds at a rental store to try them all.This collection is a real gem.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a true gaming feat. I truly cannot express how incredible of an achievement Derek and the rest of the team pulled off here!! I have 46 hours and I've only beaten 3 of the games. The depth of the experience here is insane. Not only are there 50 full games... but there is a meta narrative weaved into the mix with the fictional 'UFOSOFT' company. And you may think "oh that's cute"... but the meta narrative plays out like an in-game ARG! Using the in game terminal you can follow scavenger hunt style riddles that will truly test your knowledge of the collection, to unlock even more content!10/10 Absolutely the game of the year. You owe it to yourself to at least try this game.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 is an experience that can only be seen through experiencing the details, the challenge, and the amazing package for yourself. Get this immediately if you're a fan of one of these parallel experiences:- Playing around through a list of top 50 "sleeper hits" ROMs you found on - If you remember the /ole/ glory days of finding crazy hard indie games from communities on the web circa 2005-2015 [think TiGsource]. - Browsing period-accurate attempts to demake/remake pixel art- Enveloping yourself in one legacy company's art, lore, history [totally did this with Falcom & Ys games recently].There really is nothing like this and the team is nothing short of legendary. 8 hrs in and I have barely scraped the top of the ocean here. Some of these games are not my genre, but it's more than made up for in the *extremely* my-genre ones.  Give a large amount of games a chance before thinking about a refund, you're going to get hooked!
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I have beaten 15 games in 15 hours, getting at least gold. And I think I spent over 3 of those hours on Barbuta because that was difficult to figure out. I don't think the difficulty is too high for most of these games as some people say. The games have a clear challenge that you need to complete and it is very satisfying to complete them.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Obviously a work of a passionate dev team, Derek Yu delivers again.The variety is huge and the dedication to thoughtful design is clear. Each game has been fully treated, this wasn't driven by profit and deadlines, obviously made to a high level of quality to fulfill the team's vision. I loved the concept and am a huge fan of Yu going in,  but what a fabulous and special collection this is. I know I will be playing this for years as I work on completing the cherry pie! I have still only been into around 20 games at the 11 hour mark, and have just started dabbling in coop/multiplayer with friends, and I can't wait for more.Inspiring work of concept and design, read Derek's book if you enjoy his games or design in general. I love his philosophy on difficulty, mystery and exploration. Truly refreshing. The art and music are just so stellar as well, no half baked releases here. _childDocuments_.review: This is a very cool game that's made very well, one that focuses on developing NES era games like those games were developed in the 1980's, it's faithful to that, to a fault. There's a ton of creativity here, but what you're essentially buying is a collection of 50 mostly flawed games that do not come even close to representing the best of the NES and that's entirely on purpose. I don't regret buying it. For many, this will just be a curiosity, its fun unpacking all the games and giving them a go, but if you intend to beat any of them, like I did, you're not in for a fun experience, difficulty can be punishing, enemy placement can be harsh, controls can be obtuse and sometimes even awful. It represents a long bygone era of gaming, an era that's gone for a reason...  I still recommend the game, I feel the initial experience of playing these for the first time is really fun. Some of the games have a lot of mechanical depth and surprise you by just how creative they can be, that's worth it far more than actually trying to beat any of them.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: An extremely impressive endeavor.  They literally made 50 full games which somehow all genuinely feel as though they could've been made in the 80's.  You're probably not going to like all of them, I know I didn't, but with 50 to choose from spanning several different genres you're bound to find at least a few that really grip you.  I just finished the collection and I liked around 23 of the games enough to feel like they're worth completing, which I plan to do.  This isn't to say that the other 27 were bad games, however, just that they didn't land with me as well as the other ones did, and if you play this game I'm positive you'll have a similar impression once you find the ones you really enjoy.  Picking out your "faves" is a fun aspect of UFO 50 and as you can see by my playtime that can take quite a while (I've only finished a few games and I feel as though I've already gotten my money's worth).  To top it all off, the games aren't just random and disjointed, but rather linked to a fictional game company whose influence and evolution is reflected as you travel through the 1980's.  Anybody can find a ton of value in UFO 50.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: It's difficult to give this review, as it's actually a collection of 50 games, not mini games, but complete and very distinct games. Some held me more, others less. But as a collection, it's a great tribute and manages to capture the 8-bit era well, and with a modern game design vision. Not to mention the lore itself about the fictional company that created these games, which gives descriptions and an entire chronology about its games. There are even sequels, and you clearly see the evolution from one title to the next. Some of my favorite gaming experiences have all been comprised of diving deep into various consoles libraries and engrossing myself in unique eras, distinct art styles, and finding what games speak to me. The team has found a way to bottle this experience and gamify it beautifully.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best gaming experiences I've had, hands down.Try the games chronologically, at least to start. Experience the jank and be patient - play it like a collection of games from the 80s that you found in a shipping container. This is something that was meticulously put together with so much love, so that when the player gets a hold of it, you're just along for the ride. UFO 50 was crafted, refined and refined again - the love shows in the tiny details. Every single game has an innovative design principle or brilliant gimmick which could carry it as a standalone game. Some have multiple. When you put the whole thing together, as so many others have said, the full experience reminds you why games can be so much fun in the first place.Suspend your disbelief, dig in, and let the devs take you on a journey. You absolutely will not regret it.50/10
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Whole reviews could be written glazing nearly all of these 50 games for being unique and fun experiences. Beyond the specifics though, the joy for me was getting to have so many new games to explore for the first time. It’s like an advent calendar for retro games where every one you play next can be vastly different from the last but always meets the same standard of quality set by the rest. The fun of UFO 50 is discovery.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I do not understand the hype for this mini-game collection nor the overwhelmingly positive reviews. The store page proclaims "These are NOT minigames or microgames" but many of them literally are and many are very shallow though some are more substantive. I get that it aims for an old Atari or NES vibe, of which many will be one-trick arcadey style games, but good lord it takes all the wrong parts of those antiquated games. For me, the thing I like about old games are the simplistic controls and straightforward game design, not the crushingly rigid game controls and harshly uncaring user experience. I've not played all the games yet and there is a smattering of the one's I've played I do like. I'm sure I'll like a few more but most are dead to me and all carry some sort of grievance(s) knocking the whole experience down.Many games are rigid to the point of being wretched. For example, at least one game has ladders you must climb but you cannot approach them while holding the climb button (up/down). No, you must stand in just the right spot then release all movement and climb buttons and then carefully only press the climb button. You also cannot jump onto the ladder or off of the ladder - you must painstakingly climb every single rung. Additionally, in this game all movement, including ladders, is excruciatingly slow. To hit every room on the "map" There's no game save or save states.There's a turn-based RPG and its in-game menu is atrocious. Would you like see how close each party member is to leveling up? That's not in the overview menu. You have to go into the stats page for each one. Can you cycle though the stats page for each character? Nope, you must back out, navigate to and select the next character. The left and right directional buttons do nothing. Also, half the screen is empty. Sure, very outdated games behaved this way but that's not what I liked about them.All games only utilize 2 buttons in addition to movement, not even a 3rd button start/pause/menu (there is a global system/pause menu). Some require mashing but there's no option to have a secondary "shoot" button set to auto-fire, for instance. One game has a built in auto-fire for its weapon but only one batch of 4 shots and you have to shoot switches so if you don't press and release quickly enough then you'll just turn the switch back off. Ugh.Many games have bizarre mechanics. These can be interesting and add to the game but they are almost never explained. Figuring out games is almost entirely trial and error. There will be lots and lots of error. They could have included "instruction manuals" for folks who aren't all that into trail and error and error and error. Every game is rife with some sort of grievance, if not several grievances. Whether this be horrible difficulty (by way of things like pixel perfect controls as opposed to any compelling gameplay design), bewildering mechanics, or just plain bad UI.One awful UI is the game menu. For some reason this mindlessly sticks to the 2 button only schtick. Want to cycle the sort options? Nope, no button for that, you must go into the system menu, never mind the 8 dead buttons on the controller (hours later I accidentally discovered if you try scrolling off the list of games you can change the sort option.. great thing to hide...). Wonder what each game even is? Well, you have to actually play it because there's no screenshot or anything when you hover over it and to even see basic info, like loosely what genre its like, you have to manually open a details popup for it, which is vapid, and you cannot cycle games from this popup. You have to cancel out, navigate to the next, and then open the tiny little vapid info popup again. Again, I get what it's going for but really they could have done something like "back of the box" info/art for each one.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to wait to share my thoughts till I played enough of the collection to feel pretty certain about where it stands in my mind. I've thoroughly played all but maybe 8 games, having beat 5 and "cherried" one. With that in mind, this is not a review based on the sum of all 50 games, just my value assessment based on what I have played. Also, my hours played don't quite accurately reflect my playtime, as there were times where I accidentally left the game running.My earliest video game memories are playing games like Solar Jetman, Code Name: Viper, A Boy and His Blob, and Star Tropics - games that were bought together for cheap at a consignment shop along with the NES to play them on within a year or two of the Nintendo 64 being released. In an age where I was not spoiled for choice, my choices among the batch were often esoteric or unwieldy in design. Add to the fact that these games came without a manual and before GameFAQs, and I was left with exercises in patience and determination. They more often than not ended in frustration, but incremental progress kept these games in the back of my mind as I'd think of ways to get around a part that I was stuck, and I'd be lulled back to the TV to give it another go later. If you didn't have a similar experience, your mileage may vary a fair bit here.UFO 50 is, at least for someone with the prior context that I have, a rare kind of video game sorcery. The words that kept coming to my mind was "staggering" and "enchanting" as I went blind into each game and had an "ah-ha" moment when I realized, or at least began to realize, what the "thing" was that was going on, and then realized how much more was left to experience in just one game. As someone who admires the hard work, thought and talent that goes into seemingly "simple" games, playing UFO 50 has enriched both my perspective on games made today as well as the games made in a time when nobody knew the secret formulas for making instant hits.One of the games that best captures this is, in my opinion, Onion Delivery. I won't say much to avoid taking away from the discovery of the game, but suffice to say it's a lot like the first Grand Theft Auto game if we hadn't figured out driving controls for games yet. When first playing it, I laughed out loud when I realized how to control the car, because it just felt like how game developers in the 80s might have thought driving controls should have worked. The result is hardly intuitive, but does make a kind of sense and, when mastered, feels good as you zip around avoiding traffic.Of the other games I've played, some are just plain delights and others are brutal challenges, but getting to experience them all, and look forward to ones I haven't yet, has been worth the price of admission twice over. I really feel like that anyone who appreciates both the history of games as well as the thought that goes into making games will find enough to appreciate in this collection to be satisfied with it, even if there are games they don't like. In a time in which the industry feels defined by cynicism, UFO 50 feels like being a kid with a secondhand NES, trying to figure out what the hell he's doing, and that's been pretty neat.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I genuinely think this is an incredible watershed achievement in the Indie gaming space, and something I hope gets the recognition it deserves. This collection of games does it all, from strange and esoteric platformer to cute mario-kart style racing game, multiple types of strategy games, and even a horror-themed point and click adventure. At times I genuinely had to remind myself that no, these actually aren't undiscovered gems, but modern games made by today's designers.This is a game collection about games, about the joy of discovering something new, about seeing these fictional designers grow and change and produce interesting software over time. Little hints of story and reoccurring themes, like how Big Bell Race is obviously a (still very fun) cheap asset flip of Campanella, and how even the words "Campanella" and "Barbuta" used as game titles hint at one of the fictional developers having Italian ancestry. This game collection is wonderful, plain and simple. Please, if you can, let yourself step into another world for a moment, and take the time to try genres and styles of game you wouldn't have played otherwise. What the team here has done is truly make a space where it feels like you can "Play Forever", where the developers have been able to create fifty odd, fun, interesting little experimental retro games while relatively unshackled to the expectations and opinions of what is expected of a modern indie title. UFO 50 is something truly valuable and special, easily worth the asking price and very much worth the wait. As i continue to play, I only become more and more impressed with what they were able to accomplish.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Nah, sorry. While I often play and replay old games, the 8-bit era ones are always the ones I am most divided about, even though I grew up playing them and I often launch something ZX-Spectrum-like after reading another issue of Retro Gamer magazine. I own 12 gaming consoles, for god sake, including a Panic Playdate - but none of them are 8-bit ones. And there are reasons for it.I understand the effort that went into these games and I understand the joy people can get out of them if they are really into 8-bit games, specifically.But personally, after reading reviews and being told that this "will remind you why fell in love with games in the first place", by "combining a familiar 8-bit aesthetic with new ideas and modern game design" I expected something else.I fell in love with games for many reasons, but junk controls, permadeath, complete lack of instructions and unforgiving difficulty were not one of them. Just because there was no choice back in the 8-bit era does not make it somehow better than it was. It wasn't.

_childDocuments_.review: It perfectly captures the childhood feeling of exploring a bunch of random games that your friend let you borrow. There are so many genres represented here, you'll likely come away with a new appreciation for a type of game you never even considered.This collection holds surprises at every corner and is a constant delight. Best of all, if you find a game to be super unfun, no problem. There are plenty more to try and all of them bring a creative spin. I love this game.

Some of my highlights are Bug Hunter, Camouflage, Rail Heist and Campanella 2. I'd love to see those games and others fleshed out into full games - but again this format works so well because I can happily return to stuff I might not otherwise stick with, like Mooncat which maybe wouldn't work so well on its own, but is awesome in this context.Only real gripe - Warptank's jerky scrolling hurts my eyes

I've only played a very small chunk but I'm loving every moment. If you grab this you'll likely find one or more of the 50 games becoming a favorite.Don't sleep on this.

_childDocuments_.review: You know that feeling of not being sure if you want to boot up a game because you're not sure it's worth your time? Well, why not get a game that has 50 games inside? Solves everything.Seriously, there's something here for everyone. I've only opened up about half the games, and I've put multiple hours into many of them. The music is great, the pixel art is phenomenal, and the 80s vibe is perfect, while still having modern and fresh design. If you find the 80s aesthetic appealing, this collection is a must play.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think this game needs my help to convince anyone to play it, so let me just give a tip to anyone starting UFO 50: Boot up the 44th game Pilot Quest first, as it has idle game mechanics in it, so the automated processes you set up will continue to make resources while UFO 50 is open. I would recommend you start it up first so that you bank resources while you play the other games.

_childDocuments_.review: This feels like an unmissable, unforgettable indie game landmark. As someone who's incredibly interested in the design of games, this feels like it's made for me, but even if I just wanted to have fun for fun's sake, I can imagine this being one of the best things I could possibly pick up. It's been in standby on my Steam Deck nearly constantly for a month now.If I did have some gripes, it's that too many of the action games have that NES-era type of design where 1–2 hits is instant death. I like hard games, but it does grind my gears a little bit when the challenge is so all-or-nothing. Then again, maybe a big part of these games' target audience do enjoy that, so I try not to hold it against it. And for all the frustration, it really does give me a sense of mastery when I start to find a flow in those punishing games.

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably the first time I've played a "new retro" game and actually had it truly feel authentic.I've only now just played a bit of all 50 games on offer, and I can say I'm very excited to dive deeper. This is essentially what Action 52 should have been. _childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This is shockingly good and its all I've been thinking about for the past week. Currently at 40 hours and I haven't even scratched the surface. I can't stress enough, these aren't 50 mini games, these are 50 full games, many of which I would be happy to buy individually. People compare this to Action 52 which I feel is a little off. For me, this is reminds me greatly of when I purchased a CD full of random roms and emulators while on holiday in Asia, as well as one of those 50 in one Game Boy Colour cartridges. All legit well made games, but a mystery what you're getting. This may sound odd but I'd recommend purchasing UFO 50 as blind as possible, its a real treat discovering what each game is one at a time.I haven't put time into many of the 'epic' games yet but the games that have been my favourites so far are: Bushido Ball, Hyper Contender, Kick Club, Mooncat, Mortol 1 and 2, Overbold, Party House (play it multiplayer with remote play!) and Rail Heist.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute treat. Making your way through the catalogue and finding the games that really click with you is a joy quite unlike anything else offered by gaming today. Having grown up with an NES certainly helped my ability to appreciate these titles and slot back into that distinct, crunchy groove, but even so they're full of modern day quality of life improvements that make these retro games the way you remember them - and less how games of the era tended to ACTUALLY play. As singular games, there are some absolute all-timers here. Night Manor, Valbrace, Pilot Quest and Golfaria (amongst many, MANY others) would have found significant success if released as standalone indies today, let alone as part of this ridiculous package. But as a whole, UFO 50 weaves a story of a fake video game company - their highs, their lows, their iteration and technical advancements - that is fascinating to work your way through.If you have any fondness for retro games, do not sleep on UFO 50. It may just be Games of the Year.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Really torn on this. Because there are a few great games here. But some are just complete trash. Others desperately need an instruction manual and are only difficult because they don't explain the gameplay properly to you. The worst ones are the ones that are really deep, like Lords of Diskonia, start great, and then in the last level they're just like "eff you, this game is nigh-impossible now." It's really deflating to pump hours into a game and then hit a wall you don't even wanna figure out how to climb because life is too short and the game just isn't fun anymore.I guess I recommend it? But read about the games before you play them, and don't be afraid to bounce if one gets annoying.And whoever designed that last level in Lords of Diskonia, I hope you stub your big toe everyday for the rest of your life.

_childDocuments_.review: The best value for money on steam.I don't like to review a game without fully experiencing it first, but it feels silly to delay a guaranteed recommendation because of just how much is in this game. I've still only played around half of the offerings (in 80 hours), partly because I've tried to beat each game I've tried, but also because I want to savour the experience as long as possible. If you're an indie developer, or believe in video games as an art-form, you owe it to yourself to play this game. _childDocuments_.review: While a lot of people have drawn comparisons between UFO 50 and the old "Action 52" cartridge for the Nintendo Entertainment System, there's really no comparison. UFO 50 is a package of 50 original (meaning "new", not "classic") retro-style games bundled up into one purchase with a little bit of overarching meta-story. There are all kinds of retro games; if you enjoy classic titles from the 8-bit era, then buy this now.To be clear, this is fifty games. Not a collection of minigames, and not "a couple of good games and 45 trash programs." Every single game is complete with its own title screen, mechanics, levels, and so on. Some sprites do get re-used but it's pretty sparing, at least up to the first 25 games. It's fifty real retro-style games, and while some of them can be beaten on a lunch break, the game rewards you for excelling at these titles with high scores or quick clears, and the difficulty means you'll be struggling at those challenges for a good while.The meta-plot is basically that you (or someone) find an old computer gaming system in a storage unit and you boot it up to see what games there are. Back in the real-life 8-bit era, the distinction between a "home computer" and a "game console" was not so clear, and so the "LX" computer lies somewhere between the Nintendo NES and 8-bit home computers like the Commodore 64 or the MSX.Indeed, many of the games in UFO 50 feel more like home computer games than console games. Certain titles evoke the feel of MS-DOS or even PC-98 games, while others are very clearly aping the NES or PC Engine style. However, none of the games are bone-stock reimplementations of retro game tropes. Every single title has something pretty fresh and interesting going for it, with some very clever mechanics on display.I'd like to say that the games are incredibly authentic to their retro inspirations, but the degree of authenticity varies a lot. Some games feel like they really could be NES ROMs, while others have too many colors, too many sprites, and anachronistic gameplay functions. There's also the fact that all of the LX games (games in UFO 50) are made for a wide-screen aspect ratio as befits a modern PC game.Personally speaking, the games (at least, the first 25, which I've tried) do kind of skew a little bit toward the puzzle genre, and even the action titles often have puzzle elements to them. I don't hate this, but I'm , so this makes a lot of the games extremely difficult for me. However, that doesn't apply to every game, and in most of the titles the stakes are (perhaps a bit anachronistically) pretty low, like having infinite credits or lots of checkpoints. I've managed to clear a few games already, so if I can do it, almost anyone can.If you look at it from the point of view of being a gamer in 2024 buying fifty games at once, this package is a phenomenal value. Even if you only enjoy a handful of the games, you've still paid just a few dollars for those games, and if you like them all, well, that's $0.50 a game. Are you really going to miss out on fifty games for $0.50 each? I thought not.

_childDocuments_.review: The good:✅ 50 games and even a cheat code device, just like the old days.✅ Many different genres to choose from, so there should be something for everyone.✅ The games link together in some interesting ways I won't spoil.✅ The music is great!The bad:❌ They emulate some things a bit too faithfully.  Back in the day, Nintendo Power would rate games on their control scheme.  Yes, fixed jumps and horribly slow walk speed were common, but they were also seen as flaws even back then.  Even Mario Brothers had air control for jumps!  And NES emulators have given us speed-up buttons.❌ Some games just may not appeal to everyone.  There are a few that just aren't for me, but that only matters if you're a completionist and want to master every game, since you can have gold/cherry versions of each cart by beating it.❌ The games are Nintendo hard.  They're not very clear and they don't give any explanation and there are no manuals this time.  Others may see this point as a plus, not a minus, but back in the days of the NES some of us were buying printed strategy guides, reading Nintendo Power, or calling their tip line.  Or sending them physical letters because we wanted to know what on earth those weird spells like DIOS and BADIOS and MAPORFIC did in Wizardry: Proving Grounds of the Mad Overlord.  And some of us read the manuals for every little clue, even the ones that made no sense because our controllers didn't have microphones in them like Japan did, so we couldn't kill that annoying enemy in Zelda the way Japanese kids did.

_childDocuments_.review: UFO50 is seriously some of the best bang for your buck you can get on the video game market right now. There really is something for everyone here. Not all the games are winners for me, but I know that some games I don't like are beloved by my friends, and vice-versa, and that's pretty damn cool to me! And even more than that, I think almost every game in this collection captures the feel of its era perfectly, even down to the smallest details. There were multiple times when I really forgot I was playing a game released in 2024. Honest to god GOTY contender
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Possibly one of the most impressive achievements in gaming in a long time. Every last game is a full experience and each of them does something unique enough to warrant playing them. If you are getting into gaming for the very first time and aren't sure even where to begin, this is probably the best place to start
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 is both a brilliant collection of games from an alternate reality and an incredible love letter to genuinely amazing cult hits from the 8 and 16 bit eras. If you have historical context for what's being shown in this collection, it makes it even more charming AND enjoyable. Amazing homages and takes on titles like Metal Storm, Wind Jammers, Star Tropics, Sweet Home, River City Ransom, Space Harrier, Kirby Dream Course etc etc etc the list goes on and on. These nods and inspirations are FAR from rips offs tho as they are clearly not only inspired by their sources but have inspired new and refined mechanics. Some even being completely different takes on the same idea mashed together with new genres creating something familiar, yet entirely new at the same time.  This is a collection of devs and designers flexing both their history and knowledge of game design and giving us something from another timeline crafted with love and skill.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly charming visuals and obviously great variety: if you buy the game, and can vibe with the visual style, there will almost certainly be 3+ games in the pack that you'll enjoy enough to be worth the price of entry. For me, those games were Rock on and Overbold. No doubt there are other gems waiting for me in the pack, but how much enjoyment I got out of those two titles already had me pretty satisfied. I would just highly suggest avoiding 100% completion.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Really unique and phenomenal project. Each game is usually an excellent production all of it's own; one of the best arcade style games I have ever played is nestled in here (Campenella). Very very wide genre variety as well. I'll leave the precise genres a surprise, but the trappings of retro game genres and design do not necessarily apply here.Games lean to the shorter side from what I have played (they typically fit in the confines of an old nes game lengthwise), and there are 1 or 2 games I feel could use just a little more polishing. However, given the sheer quantity and overall quality that is provided, I don't see this as a huge issue.You could spend a very, very, long time 100%'ing everything in here. If retro style games are palatable to you, this is a universal recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of these games needed more music. Composers are an important part of the equation, DEREK. You should treat them well, DEREK.Barbuta- The primordial ooze that gaming was born in.Bug Hunter- Not really for me! But I eventually got sort of okay at it.Ninpek- It feels like so long ago I beat this one. A great game for showing off!Paint Chase- Super clever! I want to try the two player.Magic Garden- So good! It's begging to be put into an arcade cabinet.Mortol- Pretty sure there are fifty games on Newgrounds like this.Velgress- HELL YES. I was locked IN player this.Planet Zoldath- My friend Azurill is addicted to speedrunning this so I won't badmouth it.Attactics- Pretty fun! Not an all time favorite. I'd be willing to give 2p a shot.Devilition- May have been the most difficult game in the pack for me. I bled for this one.Kick Club- Do you kids remember BUBBLE BOBBLE?! Sure you do! Hits my nostalgia just right.Avianos- I *did* try the two player on this. I'll always remember the wizard army.Mooncat- You snuck a modern indie game into this pack you weasels.Bushido Ball- I love Lethal League and this is sorta that? CPU is a bastard.Block Koala- Fifty levels and one music track is cruel DEREK.Camouflage- How about some more levels for this one instead, huh?Campanella- The length of this one with no checkpoints is pretty messed up! But still fun.Golfaria- I wasn't expecting to like this one but it turned out alright!The Big Bell Race- Weakest game in the pack, I think we'll agree.Warptank- This one is a blast. Just a great little experience.Waldorf's Journey- YES. FLY FREE YOU SPECIAL BOY.Porgy- Starting you out with five seconds worth of fuel is a bold choice!Onion Delivery- The first of a few games I would classify as spite clears.Caramel Caramel- Why must you add game mechanics that make me take my eyes off the ship??Party House- The key to getting me playing deckbuilders is to hide the fact that it's a deckbuilder.Hot Foot- Really *needs* a 2p to be much fun.Divers- I don't know if the game mechanics were that special but the mood is unparalleled. Rail Heist- Without the mandatory time limit I would have liked this better!Vainger- That map is not very helpful! You guys it's not VVVVVV it's Alien Soldier. Rock On! Island- I'm not good at tower defense and this was not an ambassador. Pingolf- The punishing nature of the game is just inherent to golf, so I can't get *too* tilted.Mortol II- I'm thankful for the multiple paths that let me skip half the map, lol.Fist Hell- I'm actually pretty disappointed in this one. Didn't need to be *quite* that faithful to the old titles when stuff like Streets of Rage 4 does it so much better now.Overbold- This one took a while to beat but I can't tell if I was just playing myself.Campanella 2- Yeah I dunno how to feel about this one. Lots of work in service of platforming that's just kinda there.Hyper Contender- Donkus for president.Valbrace- I feel like I used the rapier to cheese my way to the end of this. We take those!Rakshasa- Weird weird difficulty curve where playing better makes the game easier. You know?Star Waspir- I have *no idea* how I cleared this one. I entered gamer mode.Grimstone- You need final boss music in your jrpg DEREK.Lords of Diskonia- The most needlessly cruel game in this pack. I wanna try the 2p though!Night Manor- A fantastic game, got sucked in and cleared it in one go.Elfazar's Hat- The game this is based on is right on the tip of my tongue...Pilot Quest- Well that cherry requirement can go to hell, lol.Mini & Max- So much work went into this! Needs more traversal abilities and less waiting for bugs!Combatants- People are down on this one but I thought it was... okay?Quibble Race- Could be fun with two people....Seaside Drive- HELL YEAH. Too good to be in a pack of fifty games, tbh.Campanella 3- My favorite of the trilogy!Cyber Owls- Metal Gear had more than one music track DEREK. You can afford to pay for more songs DEREK.

Most of the platformers and sports games are too hard for me but the strategy games are some of the best games i have played in years.
