_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 feels like nothing else on steam. It captures the feeling of unboxing a new console at the holidays. It captures that feeling you might have had at the video store where you pick a game you're going to spend a weekend with based on the box art and you know it looks cool but really have no idea what you're in for. It captures what it was like living through an era when of gaming when it felt like you never knew what was coming next.  It captures that feeling of going to a friends house for the first time and finding out they have a whole shoe-box full of games you've only heard about and they are excited to play them with you.That is all to say nothing of the endlessly remarkable pixel art, unique game designs, unexpected depth, variety and replay-ability.  This is not a game you should skip or overlook. I've been playing ever chance I get and I still feel like I've barely scratched the surface.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This is a monumental achievment. I really recommend to get gold for every game before moving on to the next and trust that the developers have crafted an experience for every game that is worth that time commitment. I hear a lot of reviewers (pods, youtube e.t.c.) who say that they jumped around a lot between games and I do not think that is the optimal experience with this game actually. But to each their own!
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 and the biggest surprise of the year.  If you love video games you need to play this game. So many BANGERS. I keep asking myself "how can this be ONE game? HOW???? These are not mini games. These are GAMER GAMES that kick your ass and surprise you over and over. I'm in shock. One of the best games I've ever played
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best value in gaming history.  Unseating the Orange Box was a mighty feat, but it has finally been accomplished.  Contains multiple "your favorite new game" games.  The presentation is immaculate and the subtle references to every game and genre imaginable is there.  The design on the games is perfection, capturing an incredible balance between old school style control and UI schemes with modern game design sensibilities.  Fantastic work.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This game is actually so much fun.At times you will start up a game, play it for 10 minutes, frown at it and close it.At other times, there are games you will play for multiple hours, fully excited, sometimes mad, always hooked.I love what they did with this game. There are many oldschool collections, but a collection of a Fantasy Studio that never existed to begin with, all with genres and ideas that weren't there at the time, is AMAZING.There were some games I didn't enjoy to much, like "Golfaria", "Onion Delivery" or "Pingolf", all of them I played for not even 10 minutes each.But then there are some absolute gems like "Rock on! Island", "Night Manor" or "Pilot Quest" each of which I played for multiple hours and will keep on playing a lot (except maybe Night Manor, as that is more of a "do once and done" deal).I am serious, if you are at all positively attuned towards Retro Games, get this game, it REEKS of charm.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. There should be a game or two or a few for everyone! Surely dont like every single game, especially since I am not a classic retro gamer but the whole collection is so impressive with highlights like Party House, Warptank and Mortol spinkled in, that its a very cool experience throughout.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't bought any single player games in years. I got into the habit of just playing the same old online team stuff, but this... I'm probably going to clock in around a thousand hours over the course of a year or so.I kind of wonder if larger developers will copy this style... I know a few of them do game jams, but the outcomes of those almost never come to the public. Then you have some of them complaining older game designers with experience making games like these are a dying breed. Hmmm. UFO 50, is it the future of the industry?
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: It's a variety pack of games themed after SNES/NES games (inspired by the train-wreck that was action 52 from what I've read), but on a made-up video game system instead featuring 50 actually good small games of varying genres.I've only played around 10-ish of the games so far, but I think I can safely bet that this will end up as one of the best games released this year. Most of the games I've played so far have been really well thought out and unique across the genres they are in; it reminds of me of the days around 2010 in which flash game websites were still around and providing a pool of interesting variety content which you were free to sift through. They aren't ALL amazing (to me, anyway), but not a single one so far has been bad.Update:Now much further in (tried 49 of 50 and completed more than I had before), I'd say there were only a few I thought were flawed or mediocre. Otherwise, it's 95% good or gold, with some standing out as games that I could legitimately see a high quality sequel being made for (that isn't limited by using two buttons), but I won't spoil which ones are which here. Absolutely phenomenal game/collection that's well worth the asking price.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy discovering a game's mechanics and behavior through play, this is a slam-dunk choice.I've loved nearly every game I've played in this collection, but I'm also a big ol' nerd about game design stuff. Big enough of a nerd that I taped four sheets of copy paper together to draw a physical map of the Barbuta castle. (There are several great games for map-making fans, incidentally)The breadth of game genres represented here is impressive, and the inclusion of "gold" and "cherry" challenges for each game is a simple-but-effective push toward understanding each game's nuances. The collection is more than a sampler platter of ideas - it's a lot of fully-realized self-contained games with clever designs and fresh ideas.I could ramble on and on about the game (and I probably will in a google doc at some point) but this is probably enough for a Steam review. It may not be a hit for every game-player out there, but for people who *love* games it's an instant classic.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: The is an incredible collection of games many of which I would happy to buy individually. They aren't "mini games", but instead fully realized in depth games that have been fully developed many of which will take a very long time to complete. Getting all of the achievements in the batch of games would take hundreds of hours if not more.The games span many different genres. You will undoubtedly find games in the collection that you love regardless of your particular interests. Some are devilishly hard, but this isn't off putting because there are so many games. I expect to be playing games in this set on and off for years to come. I am sure I will keep circling back to it.If trapped on a desert island and could have only 1 game (actually 50) from Steam - this is it.A master class achievement. This collection would be worthwhile at 5 x the price.If you like ANY retro games from the 80's / 90's era, this game collection belongs in your library immediately.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: The games are very minimalistic in their essence, which is all right, I guessThey are not minimalistic on its features, though, they are pretty inventive and captivating, which is goodWhat really irritates me is this: They are extremely minimalistic in the explanation of how the games work.They don't explain - or even hint - the existence of many possibilities of the gameplay. You often find yourself playing a game for 15 minutes just to find a really basic feature that was there all the time and the game expected you to either guess it or google it.I was right away hooked to this game Bug Hunter. It was not easy to get far in it, but I was very involved with it and kept trying. After 40 minutes of gameplay I found out that you can actually target and destroy energy tanks, which make them explode and kill enemies with it, and that is a VERY important feature. Took me even longer to find out that if you move from high grounds to the top of an enemy, you instakill it. There are many other examples of things that should DEFINITELY be explained, if anything, just out of respect for the player. After you actually learnt by trial and error how the game works, it gets WAY less difficult, and it makes me wonder: what's the idea? The challenge is mostly to understand the game than actually beating it? Is that what people are calling good design?I played bug hunter for like 45 minutes, but didn't want to test all other games, because that would take me much more than 2 hours and I wouldn't be able to refund it. I tested a bunch of them, though and the same trend was very apparent.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Fifty lovingly hand crafted games from every genre wrapped in a nostalgic retro-themed bow. Portrayed as coming back to an old NES-like console to relive the memories in an All-Stars esque collection. Each game, to the fake company producing them, has its own history throughout the decade of the 80's.The charm is indescribable, and is a love letter to gaming as a whole. Just the first game took me hours to beat. You're bound to find something you like. It's fun, engaging, and brings the creative spark back to games that I haven't felt in a long while.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I have played only around 6 of the 50 games and have already spent 10+ hours. Barbuta, Bug Hunter and Mortal are already worth the price, but with Night Manor (which I skipped ahead to, out of curiosity) it's clear that this collection is packed with authentically old-school classics. Easy recommend, if you don't mind the high challenge and jank that is characteristic of games from the era this is based on, this is about the best value you can get from a game.----- EDIT AFTER 50 Hours. I have kept to my word of savouring the games and have now only opened about 20 of them, having completed 11! Considering I am still less than halfway through the game, once again, unbelievable value.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of retro or indie games then this is for you!  I've only played a handful of the games so far but they are all really well done. They may appear simple at first but there is surprising depth to them. So far Magic Garden is my jam.Update:  House Party is addictive! It's basically a "deck building" game and really clicks once you understand the mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best games I've ever played. If you liked old NES and Genesis games that made you learn how to control the game well before you could progress, you'll like this collection. I would have payed the price of this game for the few games I've beat so far, and I still have 47 games to go. It is seriously such a cool idea, and all the different developers that worked on it did a great job. You can tell the Downwell and Spelunky guys worked on some of the games for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: For you to put out a big game that deserves to be put in the S tier of any game released in 2024 is a big ask already. For you to put out 50 SMALL games, a majority of them deserving to be put in the S Tier of games released in 2024 is Impossible. To put them all in one great big bundle pack with it's own world and lore? ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing.UFO 50 has some blatantly fantastic games in it that really need to have expanded standalone versions available to play. If this game gets workshop mod support like Sega Mega Drive/Genesis Classics has, that's it. This game is a killer for any AAA producing company that says small games can't be as good as big games that take 5+ years to develop, tease, advertise, and release.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing I've only touched the first 12 games, going in "release order." It really nails the premise of finding a big pile of dusty floppies in a storage unit and booting them up to see what they are. All you get for them is a quick blurb, some "trivia" about the history of the game, and the controls - in some it really adds to the feeling that there should have been a manual you just don't have so you gotta puzzle out how the thing really works. It hasn't felt unfair about this so far though, which is great. Essentially you are getting 50 really well polished and unique game jam games with a theme. That means if you, say, try the first game "Barbuta" and decide it's not for you - that's fine! Pick a different one! You don't gotta like or even beat all these things. Don't be a silly person on the forum.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO50 is both a beautiful love letter to retro game design, while also showing how general game design has evolved since. Setting aside most of our technological developments, we are able to get a clear view at retro and modern ideas being brought together, not to mention all the new innovative concepts being brought into the mix.UFO50 is amazingly inspiring and incredibly fun. It's exactly what the industry needs at this moment in time.P.S. Mini & Max is so good. A game hasn't managed to make me audibly gasp in a while, let alone twice a minute.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: These games ROCK!! Each of the ones I've played so far are so nuanced and creative. The graphics and music are endlessly charming, and each new track and art style blows me away. I can't put this game down, even if only ten of my favorites were part of this game I'd still pay way over $25 for them. My top three favorites so far are Rock On! Island, Attactics, and Quibble Race. This collection of games is a triumph.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played them all yet.A few of these games feel a little too interested in emulating the technical limitations of their era, but some of these are genuinely brilliant games that stand on their own that I'll play for at least a dozen hours each. Attacticks (!!!), Velgaria, Bushido Ball (a great windjammers demake), and Rail Heist (such a unique design!) are all highlights so far.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Great lore and secrets, as to be expected from the developers of Spelunky 1 & 2.All of the games I've played so far have felt fun, new and addicting, while giving me memories of old NES classics.50 games, of which 25 are multiplayer games and 11 are co-op games.I haven't even scratched the surface yet, and can't wait to see all the secrets and games the game holds.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 is a game I would have happily payed $60 for. Fifty (mayyyyyybee more?) games for the low price of $25 is a criminally great deal. And yes, what we've got here are 50 video games. Not micro games, not mini games, not game-jam games. Every game in this collection are fully fledged games that would have been a full priced cartridge in the 80's. The fact that they all have a cohesive palette and sound font is elevated even MORE by the clear iteration and evolution of the games as you play them "chronologically". There is a vast array of game genres, and even if you don't connect with a bunch of games here, there is no doubt in my mind you will become strongly hooked on several more, sinking hours into many of the offerings available. Even my 11yo child who swears she hates "simple graphic" pixel games has gotten hooked. Great games are great, regardless of resolution and fidelity, so even if you're put off by chunky pixels I defy you to sample each game here and not become enamored with several of them.Good luck; have fun.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing this review, I have only started 24 of 50 games. I have completed 11 of those games, and cherried only 10 of them (which means either played to 100% or completed a hard challenge depending on the game). Even though I have yet to even experience half of the game, I can confidently say that UFO 50 is phenomenal.To be clear, I have not loved every single one of the games I've tried so far in this, but I think that it was intentionally designed to be that way. Some of the games in here are purposefully very obtuse in order to emulate the feel of some of the real life games of the early 80's and before. Some games are simply part of a genre I don't like. And some games are so challenging that I just don't want to bother mastering them right now when I still have other games to experience. But none of these games are poorly made, and I honestly have yet to try anything that I really dislike.UFO 50 offers 50 high quality retro inspired games, and while only a dozen or so of them could truly stand on their own as a full experience by today's standards of length, it is such a nice bundle that keeps finding new ways to surprise me. I highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I have only played about half of the games in the collection so far and there are about 10 where I've said to myself I would've paid $10 for a separate Steam release.  That's an amazing hitrate.  Just an outstanding collection that I'll be playing for years.  Perfect on Steam Deck, too.  My standouts - Night Manor 🍄, Camouflage, Warptank, Bushido Ball, Rail Heist, Seaside Drive, Party House, Bug Hunter.  If you get stuck or mad at Barbuta, just play something else!
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: A compilation of 50 unique games where the DNA of 80s classics meets modern creativity. UFO 50 isn't just a collection: it's a true declaration of love for video games.Each game plunges us into the unknown, with no tutorial to guide us. Here, it's all about exploration, experimentation and figuring things out for yourself. The controls, inspired by the NES, are simple and accessible: a directional cross, two buttons. Nothing superfluous, just the essentials for immediate fun. And yet, underneath this apparent simplicity lies incredible depth: ingenious mechanics, well-hidden secrets and, sometimes, the need to draw a map or write down our discoveries in order to progress. UFO 50 is a brilliant tribute to retro games and an ode to the diversity of gameplays: action, puzzle, RPG, shoot'em up... Each title is a universe in its own right, rich in challenges and surprises. No microtransactions, no modern horrors, just pure, sincere gaming, designed to be explored, shared, replayed endlessly or even mastered as a speedrun for the most tenacious.Whether you're nostalgic for pixels or eager for new experiences, UFO 50 is a universal work that will touch you. And once you're in, it's almost impossible to get out. Ready to take up the challenge?
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I'm currently 7 hours into the 'JRPG' style game which I genuinely thought would be something I'd hate when I first read the store description.  I don't think I'm particularly near the end of it either. Off that alone I'd say UFO 50 is insanely good value. A number of other games I tried seemed really interesting but I'm trapped in cowboy hell currently.Unsurprisingly runs fantastically on my Steam Deck
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: A love letter to the design of games, told through a fake game company spread out through 50 unique games made just for this. Nostalgia is not the seller here, it's innovative and great design restricted to a d-pad and 2 buttons. There's a spread of a bit of everything you could want here, from platformers to strategy games to a Western JRPG to dungeon crawlers with hidden meta-gaming spread throughout. Even if one game is not your jam, there's plenty more to choose from.Personally, I've loved every single one so far. A once in a generation type of release. Couldn't recommend it more. UFO Soft is one of the best publishers out there.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 is one of the most heartfelt & interesting pieces of collaborative art to have ever graced the world - none the less the videogame industry.It's a deeply loving look at a history that never was, elevating the memories of our past atop the progress of nostalgia's future.I could continue to pontificate on how perfect UFO 50 is, but I'd rather leave off with something more succinct.UFO 50 f**ks so hard & I'm so thankful for all the effort everyone put into it. It's special & precious & I cherish its existence. 🤍💜✨
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This didn't click at all for me. I played plenty of the games available, and none of them had enough fun elements in them to play further. It is very technically impressive - it truly feels like an 80's videogame console, with really amazing pixel art and effects. As an avid old NES player, and yes, owner of an actual bloatware Action 52 cartridge - the appeal is there! It is nostalgic. It is very pretty.But it's not fun. The only game I got any fun out of was Pingolf. The game design on display here says on the store description "combining 8-bit aesthetic with new ideas and modern game design". There's plenty of clever gameplay in that sense, it just isn't fun to play, basically none of it. Confusing RPG. Floaty platformer. Generic SHMUP. Streets of Rage clone. Yes I learned to play them, they just weren't fun! I feel the wrong ideas were followed in chase of that nostalgic display - would these games be of value as themselves or as part of a collection, or was it more that the developers wanted to make sure it FEELS like a game collection from 89? Would you actually WANT to play games from that era? Because whatever modern twist they added to the design, it wasn't enough.Right now it feels like a throwback bloatware collection. The appeal is purely nostalgia, the games are very shallow - as it was back then. It's sad, because I was expecting to surely find something really cool here, rummaging through this vast collection of games. The visuals and commitment to the bit is insane. I love games like these. I love Mossmouth.But UFO 50 didn't click, and there wasn't fun in it for me.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Great for fans of classic retro games who also prefer some more modern accessibility. Many of the games are still difficult, but not as unwelcoming or unbalanced as the actual old titles often are.Just skimming through the library trying a few games for a few minutes, getting stuck on a particular game for an hour, or returning to a particular game in order to finally get a grasp on how it works - it's a highly varied and greatly polished fun time!
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I don't often leave reviews but I have to for this title--this game is an exceptional showcase of the pure talent and ingenuity from all developers involved. Truly amazing that something like this is able to exist. Congratulations Derek Yu on having your vision with this come to fruition in such perfect fashion after seven long years.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I'm about 30 hours in and UFO 50 might be the best game of all time.Each game is an enigma. Most games provide you with little instruction. They force you to use your intuition and observation skills in order to figure out the rules and master the games. This job is made easy by the excellent design work and feedback on display.While most players may not click with all fifty games, there are many to love for all tastes.There's also a holistic mystery moving through the package that the player can slowly uncover while going through the library.The value here is second to none, buy it now!
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Assuming you play each game for only 6 minutes, thats 5 hours of gameplay. Then you go back and play the 10ish games you really enjoyed, thats gotta be atleast 8 hours of gameplay right there. Im currently at 18 hours played and ive only beaten one of the twenty game i wanted to go back to. This game is well worth $25 even if you hate half the games. This feels like one of those chinese emulator machines where you can play a bunch of ripped nintendo games, except from a universe where game design was 20 years ahead. Alot of these are games really fleshed out.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 is what happens when you ask a game developer what their "desert island game" would be.This collection is truly remarkable; there is something for literally everyone.The developers did a remarkable job creating a mood and atmosphere surrounding the IP's of this fantasy console. Each game feels distinctly unique, but holds the same kinda of familiarity between them that really sells the console as a cohesive entity.Derek Yu and his cohort of impassioned developers have done something truly artistic here. It's so refreshing and inspiring, and they pulled it off flawlessly.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 This blast from the past will keep you entertained for a long while ! Don't like a game ? Move on to another ! And at times, you'll find yourself coming back to the games you didn't like and still find things to enjoy in those ! What I also like about this compilation is that the games and their worlds are somehow interconnected in many different ways, giving this ensemble a very cohesive feel !PLAY FOREVER
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: none of the games are that engaging and fun - I grew up on the NES and it was fun to check out each of the 50 games in this collection as throwbacks, but nothing really holds my attention that well. I got an enjoyable ~10 hours scratching the surface of everything, but struggled to find anything that made me want to keep playing. keeping the comments on because I would love to know if there are hidden gems that I'm just missing.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 is one of the best games I have ever played and potentially the best indie game to ever release. It takes all the lessons learned throughout decades of game development and applies them to the style of games that were created in gaming's infancy. There really is something in here for everyone and not in the sense that you'll like only part of a game. There is a full length game that you will like in here.You may think that because there are 50 games in the collection that there must be a sacrifice of quality for the sake of quantity. This could not be further from the truth. Each game has a remarkably unique identity with fully fleshed out ideas. From arcade-y high score games to a fully realized and surprisingly deep JRPG, the quality remains consistently best of class. One of my favorite aspects of this game is the narrative about the dev team that is created through playing their games. You see the games slowly increase in complexity, implying lessons learned by a team of passionate developers that truly want to make fun games. You see the technology get better over the years, resulting in higher graphical fidelity. The company changes names at one point. One of my favorite things is seeing the company logo change over the years. It really breaths life into this company and makes it so believable that they really existed. This is truly a must play game. If you love ANY video games, you will get value out of UFO 50.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, after looking at 25 of the games (including all of the ones that I had most anticipated), I can say that this collection failed to grab me. Only Valbrace, a first person dungeon crawler, was enjoyable for me. Many of the games seemed to have high potential but felt half-baked. Seaside Drive, for example, is a seemingly great shmup title, but its main gimmick (drifting to charge) felt poorly implemented and awkward at best. Is the game a success? In some sense, yes, as it is a creative idea that is executed according to the designer's vision; but ultimately, no, since it fails to live up to the standard of the games it seeks to emulate or draws inspiration from- basically, it's not clear why the game should exist. This is how I felt about everything I came into contact with. Lots of games are clever and well made, but either due to their control scheme, narrow scope, or a subversive gimmick, are ultimately not the sort of thing I would ever go out of my way to play. I wish I could say that the whole of UFO 50 were greater than the sum of its parts, but in the end it just doesn't add up for me. Why play the beat-em-up, shmup, platformer, puzzle game, rpg, etc. in this collection when I already have better games in my library? I'm not saying these games are bad, and they certainly aren't all boring, but they're just... mediocre, on the whole. Digging through the collection and turning up dud after dud only reinforces this feeling. While the collection is stylish overall, visual/character design quality varies widely between the games. If you are just here to hang out and get immersed in this anthology, I'm not sure your stay will be worthwhile on the back of the eye-candy alone. That said, the music in this collection is a definite highlight. I'd be interested in buying the soundtrack for this game, were it available.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: If you're the type of person who likes to revisit the games you played as a kid, get this one.50 really well-designed and unique games with just the right amount of that nostalgic 'jank' to feel challenging, yet not unfair. Even if the influences are pretty evident sometimes, it doesn't feel like i'm playing a copy of another game someone already made.Do yourself a favor and don't spoil yourself by checking guides.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Put simply: there are 50 games, and no bad ones. Not every game has been for me, but every one is of high quality, and almost all have a unique, inspired twist from its source material. Actually unbelievable that this (frankly insane) game collection was executed to this level of quality, and genuinely one of the best deals you can get on steam right now!
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: A love letter to an era of gaming, this delivers on its promise and more. The games are meticulously authentic - sometimes to a fault! - but strikingly original. Even the simplest games feel complete and distinctive, and have surprising nuances and thoughtful designs, and a few standouts could stand on their own today. Favorite game: Vainger
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing amount of content and passion went into this. Each game has depth and the majority are hard-as-heck. Lots of genres and world-building. I've only scratched the surface of a lot of the games, and can tell that I will come back to this for years and years. If I could only have one game in steam, I think it'd be this.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This is 50, high quality 8-bit games for your Steam collection which have been developed by a variety of developers in the past 5 or so years.   It's weird because this game is packaged like it's one of those multi-game cartridges from the 80s that were largely garbage, but each game here is well thought out and unique from each other.There's literally every kind of old 8-bit game here - puzzlers, shooters, rpgs, questing, side scrollers, everything.  Some games, by their nature, are more in-depth than others but each one is worth the time to explore.This game isn't for everyone, though.  For the coolness that it is, UFO 50 is still a simple 2-button d-pad game and has the same amount of depth that the NES cartridges offered.  So if you don't yearn for these 'good old days' of CRT gaming then you may not care for this, which is fair.Personally, I'm pleased with this.  In the 4 or so hours I've played, I've tried about 8 or so games and more than half have some serious depth.  80s kids would love this. Probably 90s kids too.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: If you were born before 1990 and played video games as a child, you might just love this. For me, it captures the feeling of stepping into a game store or video arcade as a kid, seeing all of these games I knew nothing about and letting my imagination go wild.Some of the games in the collection are pretty simple, but well designed. I can't explain what it is, but they have an addictive quality that makes you say "Just one more try..." each time you hit a Game Over.All of the games feel authentic and you could believe they are games that actually existed in the '80s, but they are almost all quite unique. They clearly pay homage to certain titles but they all provide their own twist.The authentic feels means that some games are a bit clunky, but this is part of the charm. The goodwill earned with some of the better titles encourages me to play through some of the clunkier ones to really see what it's about. Even if you don't love every game, you feel like you are experiencing a part of video game history (even though it's all a fiction).I've played fewer than 20 of the games so far, and I am excited to continue discovering more. If the entire collection were only the games I've played to this point, it still would have been well worth the cost and the time.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I pirated this because I wasn't sure I would like it enough to drop £20 on it, and it turned out to be SO ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good I couldn't possibly justify not buying it. I grew up with a NES, and everything I've played here has been like a fascinating look into an alternate past.Highly recommended. (Don't judge the quality of the whole thing by Barbuta - it's deliberately jankier than most of the other titles.)
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't like every game. But I liked enough of them. And I liked them enough that I would recommend this game.Rail Heist is a fantastic platformer-strategy game where you have to secure money from a train, then escape to a horse. But you only have 9 seconds to make your moves before the lawmen take their turn, with XCOM-esque Overwatch mechanics in play.Night Manor is a point-and-click adventure game where you solve puzzles while avoiding a fungus-covered killer. There's tons of spooky details, like animations that rarely play when you enter a room.Magic Garden is a cross between Pacman and Snake - rescue Oppies so they trail behind you, then drop them off at the Star Spaces. Dropping off enough gives you a 'power pellet' that lets you take out enemies, but bumping into any of them or your trail of Oppies ends your game.Waldorf's Journey is like a really atmospheric version of those "shoot the cat out of the cannon and see how far it goes" games, except you're a walrus and you have to collect seashells.Mooncat is a beautiful weird platformer with binary controls. Two inputs: Go Left, and Go Right, and everything else is a combination of those inputs in different orders or combinations.Party House is a deckbuilder where the goal is to have 4 special guest cards at once. Gain Popularity to add new Guests to your rolodex, Money to expand your house to allow more guests at once and use their abilities to manage your Trouble-causing guests so they don't get the party busted.And Porgy - well Porgy sucks but they can't all be winners.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible collection of games that celebrates the past, present, and future of game design. Many of the games combine classic and modern game mechanics in fun and inventive ways that we'll no doubt be seeing knock-offs of in the near future.I guarantee there will be a handful of games that will immediately hook you and you'll play straight to the end, but being able to quickly hop between games means you never end up feeling too bored or frustrated even with the ones that don't initially grab you.  You'll quickly sink many hours slowly progressing across a wide range of games by doing a dungeon run here, a puzzle there, another platforming level, or getting farther in the unbelievably well-made horror game.The only thing I'll caution is that many of the games intentionally lack any form of instruction, which may leave you feeling lost or frustrated. The games are 100% designed with this in mind, but if that kind of puzzling doesn't interest you then you might not want to pick this up.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: as someone who never grew up during the era that this game represents, I wasn't sure if this game would be for me, I always found NES games to be too difficult and too obtuse at times, but playing through this collection has been an absolute joy, yeah it can get really hard with some of the games, but the creativity and passion on display makes me want to get good, to see all that this collection has to offer. UFO 50 is a really special game, highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Out of the 50 games included in this pack, there's about 5 I'm not super into. Each of which I've seen someone online claim as their favorite. I don't know how a small team comes up with 50 unique game concepts and knocks so many out of the park, but they sure did it. Can't recommend enough, you will find a new favorite here guaranteed.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty cool collection of ideas;  legitimately 50 unique games in a variety of genres styled as the releases on a fictional 1980's game console.  Recommend initially trying them all in chronological "release" order, as you can really see & feel the designs grow in complexity as time goes on in the UFOverse. While not every game is necessarily my cup of tea, the concepts are solid and without filler. The best ones here are worth the price of admission alone.  With the diverse genres included different players will gravitate to different games as their favourites.  I will say that some of the platformers are quite difficult and hitting Cherry status on all seems like quite the challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: It's like a retro compilation from another reality.  Very cool concept that I have been impatiently following for literally years.  So glad to have it in my hands.  THESE ARE NOT MINI GAMES.  These are GAMES.  You're getting 50 brand-new retro-style games for less than half the cost of a single AAA game.  VERY WORTH.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I'm in awe that UFO 50 actually exists and with so many sub-games which are so much better than I expected them to be.  It has great games which are well within my wheelhouse -- a real-time tactics game, a sokoban game, a deck-builder -- but the in-game collectable system encouraged me to try out so many things outside the genres I usually gravitate toward and I have repeatedly found that those games are also fantastic -- a platformer-adjacent UFO piloting game, SHMUPs, even 'sports' games.  I'm repeatedly struck by how special UFO 50 is, and also left wondering if there will be anything that pulls off the same gimmick of a fictional retro game collection as well as it does, ever, in the future.  I'm 50 hours in, and I feel like I've barely scratched the surface of many games which I want to do a deep dive into!It's my 2024 game of the year, no question.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: So many high quality games and so little time. This honestly feels like one of those multi-game cartridges that you could buy for the NES. You get 50 full games with half of them having some form of multiplayer/couch co-op support. Tons of hidden secrets to discover and overall just an amazing and interesting experience that you won't really get anywhere else. This game could have easily been priced at $50 USD but it ended up at half that. I highly recommend getting this game if you love retro games and if you want to experience something completely new from the 8-bit era.Also I really enjoy how the game adheres to the rules of an NES controller with a d-pad, start, select and A and B. It makes using the nintendo NES controllers really fun with this collection.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game, its so unique and different and every game has its own identity and feels very polished. I have 7 hours at the time of this review and have only played half of the games at this point. Each one has been enjoyable to a degree and a good number of them have been super addicting.I particularly like how each game has a way to 'complete' it to get a gold cart, and each game has a few other more abstract goals to go for as well. Can't recommend enough
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 is like if your favorite childhood game console grew up with you instead of staying in the past. It may look and sound the same on the outside, and still use 2 action buttons, but it's evolved. We get Zelda crossed with an idle resource game, Metroid fused with a roguelike, and Outrun drifting its way into a shoot-em-up; there's no shortage of innovative ideas and genre mash-ups here. It's 30+ years of design advancements injected into classic games.Just as impressive as the individual games is the collection as a whole, and how the titles play off each other. If I die a disappointing death in one game, my mind is already queuing up what other games I can revisit to cool off or get hyped up again. UFO 50 has an astonishingly diverse library of games for every mood and type of classically-inspired challenge, and you have complete freedom to fine-tune your experience. With 50 full games you really aren't expected to love them all upfront, but there's absolutely something for everyone. The discovery aspect adds a fulfilling and fun layer to the whole package.The bottom line is that UFO 50 is like a Nintendo Classic Mini except with with a larger library of more innovative and fun games, and it's only 25 US Dollars. This is not a thing you sit down with and play through in a week and never pick up again. This is a whole console with 50 fully-featured games that simply get better and better with time and experience. If you're even 1% interested in this game, just get it!
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: The description is right:  While some of these games are short, every one was given the time and care of a standalone product. UFO 50 successfully captures everything I love about discovering new games and is easily one of the most impressive collections on steam.While the games have self-imposed limitations, the designs are very modern. I didn't grow up in the 80s and have no nostalgia for that era of gaming. But there's something freeing about these games giving you control right away. It trusts that you'll learn through experimentation, and the simple controls (every game only uses a d-pad and two buttons) allows you to learn quickly if you connect with a game. And if it doesn't, you're free to move on without impediment.And honestly, don't hesitate to move on once you understand the game and it's still not clicking. That's the best way to find your favorites without getting bogged down by the ones you really don't vibe with. I pity anyone with a completionist mindset going into this.The meta narrative is most effective if you open each game chronologically. You'll see this fictional 80s developer build off their previous work with each new release, including fleshing out mechanics, characters, locations, and even sequels to included games. You'll start to take notes of recurring developers and get a sense of their design preferences. And if you're really curious, the in-game terminal hides some of the collection's best secrets. With that being said, you don't have to engage with this aspect if it doesn't interest you. But I still recommend peaking at the "history" in each game's description once in a while.I can't think of a game or collection that surprised and delighted me as consistently as this one. A game design masterpiece. Do not skip if you have any interest in the concept.---As an extra, here's each of my favorite games in the collection by year. I waffle between these and all the "honorable mentions" depending on the day, so don't take it too seriously. Unfortunately, I didn't get to do much of the multiplayer when I wrote this either.GOTY by virtue of being the only game released in 1982. Essential to start with this one, but it's slow, obtuse, and punishing. All around not very fun to play, but I've played it for over an hour? Must be doing something  right. Start here, but move on as soon as the novelty of this clunky game runs out.In the vein of Contra or Ghosts N' Goblins. I haven't gotten very far, but it's certainly user error. It feels good enough that I keep crawling back.It's a platformer where you use your "lives" to create paths forward. I adore this one. It's clear where you need to go, but it effectively rewards clever solutions with more people in subsequent levels. Might have been one of my favorite games of the year on its own, and the collection is courteous enough to already disappoint me with its more complex sequel.Some of my favorite music in the collection coupled with a unique and very frustrating control scheme. You're essentially fighting all your ingrained platformer muscle memory to explore these alien levels. I don't blame you if you have a strong negative reaction to this like I initially did, but I'm glad I stuck with it. I keep thinking about this strange little game.There's a deck builder in here??? I have almost no experience with this genre outside of Balatro, but this game about throwing the perfect party has its hooks in me. Another great game that easily could've stood alone.An 80s console take on tower defense very similar to Bloons. The defense options are limited, but that means you're not getting any decision paralysis for what amounts to minor differences. An excellent, no fluff tower defense gem.This is a full, old-school RPG, complete with a unique narrative, choice in party composition, and turn-based combat. There's a satisfying timing mechanic to make combat more engaging, and it works for me. Doesn't hurt that I'm a sucker for a Western (not directly related but please also play the brilliant Rail Heist).An adventure platformer with a shrinking mechanic that allows you to explore your house at insect level. Not the most original idea on paper, but there's a lot to explore and the writing perfecly fits the tone. Just really well done.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: A great package of games. The vast majority of games are very original, it was rare that I could think of a similar game I'd played before. There's a lot of variety in genres, yet they're all well executed. Especially the strategy games are well made, with some really fun gameplay mechanics.Each game has three goals to achieve. which give little cosmetic rewards in the game selection menu. It's a nice inclusion, giving you an additional reason to play more of the games.The average quality of the games is high. The best games were so good that they could very well be sold on their own. There were a couple of games I didn't like, but it's no big deal when there are so many games included.If you'd like to play a variety of creative and mostly simple games with retro aesthetics, this is worth buying. The game is a great value even at full price, with so many complete games included.

_childDocuments_.review: fun collection of 50 different games from a fictional video game company similar to the nes. can't say i loved every single game but the ones i do are more than worth the price. you can tell the devs put a lot of time and love into this, each game is legitimately it's own game you'd have paid full price for in 1985. some of my favorite games have modern sensibilities but their recreations of 1980's platformers is very accurate. runs great on the deck.

_childDocuments_.review: Please play this. If you have even the smallest remote interest in indie games or the arcade aesthetic this collection is more than worth the price. The amount of games paired with the diversity of how each one plays makes it the most fun I've had with an arcade games in years, probably ever.It's a masterpiece
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I can't get over how good this game is. I'm not even particularly into retro games - grew up in the N64 era vs NES/SNES, and I often get frustrated by games that are too unforgiving. And yet, UFO 50 feels like an absolute masterpiece to me, as someone that definitely falls outside of the target audience.There are so, SO many excellent games in this package, games I could easily see myself pouring dozens of hours into by themselves. The value-per-game is unbeatable, but the quality of the games are astounding. Thoughtful game design around every corner, enticing throughline lore about the fictional game developer and their various IP's, all in a package that is an absolute love letter to games of that era. Even the difficult games, often quite unforgiving, tend to have something in them that makes me want to push through the struggle and master them.I knew an hour in that this was a great purchase, having found like 5 games that really resonated me. After 17 hours and all 50 games finally tested at least a little, this is up there for my GotY.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: 50 full-fledged games, not mini-games, for 25 USD. The games are fantastic and cover a wide spread of genres and playstyles, from platformers to puzzle games to idle games to shmups to point-and-click horror to deckbuilders to... well, you get where I'm going with this. The bottom line is this: your 5 favorite games out of this alone will be well worth the price of admission. In fact, any one of these games could be a standalone indie title charging anywhere from 5-15 USD on Steam. I don't want to harp too much on how good of a value this package is, though, because it might overshadow my main point: these games are good. These games are GOOD. Fun, engaging, addictive... When you turn the game off you'll find yourself thinking about them, wanting to try different strategies in them or wanting to try for a new high score. Whether you want to treat this game like a charcuterie board and sample different games here and there as they catch your eye, or grind hard for "cherry clears" one at a time, there's many hours of fun and engaging content in this package. My estimation of certain games only goes up over time, too. Games that might seem opaque or overly difficult at first work their way into your brain until you find yourself craving them, and my personal "top 5" favorites are always in flux. But whether I'm stumbling through the wonderfully weird and atmospheric Mooncat, exploring the charming overworld of Pilot Quest, or sweating my way through an intense bout of Bushido Ball, one thing's for certain: I'm having an absolute blast. Derek Yu and Mossmouth studios, as well as all the contributors to this incredible collaboration all deserve a big round of applause. Eight years in development have certainly paid off, and UFO 50 is currently my GOTY, beating out many big triple-A titles.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This game's existence is genuinely unbelievable. 50 is a hell of a lot of games, and even if it took a while for it to release, it is still a marvel of game development. Each game feels faithful to the NES era, but with quality of life improvements that have come with the growth of the games industry. Snappy controls and gorgeous pixel art. I have tried out a little over half of the games at this point, and  I can tell this is one for the history books. Most of the games I've tried so far have great replayability. Whether it's because of random generation or competing with friends for high scores, this is a game I can see myself playing for a long time.Do yourself a favor and buy this. It's 50 cents per game. It would be worth it if it was $60, but $25 is an outrageous deal. Buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: First of all I want to say something about the music. I'm extremely impressed by the amount and variety and (something that probably only musicians will notice) how there's microtonality/experiments with tuning/intonation in a lot of the tracks. While still managing to keep super catchy and powerful melodies.It's very innovative and fresh and I hope more video game composers do this. The games are very polished. They feel like full games on their own. With most of them you can clearly tell what was their direct inspirations. But they all have some interesting twist, so they don't feel generic. I'm very impressed with the amount of creativity and mastery of game design in this. If it looks like it's something you would like, you definitely will.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: An essential purchase, and one of the best value games on Steam. At the time of writing, I've played for 13 hours, cleared two games and only tried four in total.Each individual game is masterfully designed to pay homage to real games from the era, but with modern game design twists that make them all much less frustrating than many of their counterparts from the "real world". Plus there's not one game here that is a straight "copy" of a real '80s title; every one of these 50 titles has some sort of hidden depth or clever mechanics to discover, and it's an absolute joy to get to know each and every one of them.The more I play it, the more it seems like an interactive work of art as much as a collection of games. Everything is deliberately designed to get you thinking about classic game design and how things have changed over time. This is so much more than just "Action 52, but good". It deserves to be required reading on game design courses -- and should be considered an essential part of every Steam library.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: What a long wait for this one, eh?  Announced like eleventy billion years ago, this grand collection is finally here, and I've been quite excited for it.  Now, this one is kinda hard to review in the usual way...  What I want to do here is to give you a sense of what you'll really be getting here, because looking around, I've seen some complaints here and there about it, and it seems like some might be going into this not quite knowing what they'll get.The main thing to understand is that these are meant to be *true* retro-style games.  Properly emulating what games were genuinely like during the era that each one was released (mostly).  And if you didnt grow up with the NES (or similar systems from that time period of 8-bit consoles), these might seem rather strange in many ways.On Steam here, there are a lot of games that claim to be retro-styled, but in reality, that often just means the graphics... everything else about them is often very modern, and the size of the games is often quite big.  Often games like that have the sorts of mechanics in them that you really didnt see back then (often due to technical limitations, or design concepts that hadnt yet been realized), and so on.  Retro STYLE, but not truly representative of what actual retro games are like.That's not what this is.  You arent going to go into each of the 50 games and come away with like, a 20 hour experience with 80 levels and checkpoints and inventory systems and blah blah blah, for each single game.  That just aint what it was like back then, so that aint what you're going to get here.Just as an example, one of the games is called Magic Garden.  This is an arcade-style game, using the traditional "snake" mechanic of things trailing you, and having you grab things to build that up and then dropping them in marked places to get big points, avoiding enemies and such the whole way.  This all takes place on a single screen, and... that's it.  That's the game.  It gets progressively tougher as you go, and if you crash into anything bad, it's game over.  That's the extent of it.  Play to score points.  To many modern gamers, this probably sounds like it aint too much, but understand, this is seriously what a lot of games were like at that time.  This, back then, would have been released as a single, full-priced cartridge.  If you're not familiar with things from that time period, head over to Youtube and look up games such as Balloon Fight, or Clu-Clu Land.  Games of a similar scale, and indeed, they were full-priced products back then.  A game like Magic Garden, in this collection, very much takes after games like those.Similarly, you will run into elements that might seem very archaic, or things that the industry sorta left behind a long time ago.  There's one game that is soccer themed, sort of, and has you jumping around single screen levels, kicking the ball at enemies, which turn into food items when defeated.  This takes after the original Bubble Bobble, a very erratic platformer that used this exact design style (but you blew bubbles at enemies instead of launching a ball).  In a lot of modern games, you cant *really* lose.  Not truly.  You can always reload or go back to a checkpoint or whatever.  But many games werent like that back then.  In this particular game, you've got a couple of lives, it only takes one hit to kill you, and when you run out of lives, it's game over.  True game over.  No checkpoints, no reloading, no continues.  No saving the game either.  If you want to beat this game, you're going to have to do it in one sitting.  You're either good enough to do it, or you arent.  Unlike a lot of modern games, where you can pretty much always win eventually even with low skill because a real game over condition never happens.However, as you go chronologically further into the collection, the games start to get more advanced, less arcade-y.  Bigger, more expansive. Heck, there's a full-on JRPG in here.  Yet, even still, they will often use mechanics that might seem odd at first.  There's one game that is a horror-themed point and click adventure game.  A genre that isnt particularly uncommon even these days, but again, this is trying to emulate that old era, so a lot of the bells and whistles meant to smooth things out are not here.  Controls and UI and such are exactly as awkward as in old games like Shadowgate, and even that screwy room map from that game makes an appearance here (though it's just slightly less confusing than Shadowgate's map thing) as does loopy monsters just abruptly filling the screen, often leading to a quick death that comes out of nowhere.At the same time though, there are some things that are not quite accurate to that time, and typically for good reason. For instance, that JRPG has mechanics in it designed to reduce the hyper-grind that JRPGs back then were known for, because that element of those older games was just notoriously irritating to the point where, if kept in here, it could absolutely suck the enjoyment out of it.  Stuff like that.  And a bit of modern design trickles in at certain points.  Like in that garden game, enemies will very clearly telegraph where they're about to move, keeping things always feeling fair... which wasnt how things often worked back then.  Accuracy is great and all, but not if it just produces supreme irritation when it really doesnt have to.Creativity is also very high here, a lot of design concepts that are different yet familiar.  One game, Mortol, is this odd sort of puzzle platformer with a strange twist:  you need to die a lot, in specific places & ways, to progress.  But the mechanics that dont involve you drowning yourself or something all feel like they were taken right out of an old platformer, as does the general feel of the level design.  That soccer game is another example.  Plenty of games used the format it uses.  But that method of attack?  I cant think of a single thing that did anything like that.  NES games liked straightforward shooting or melee attacks.  That soccer ball sure aint that, and it makes for a much more dynamic experience here (which often was not the case back then).  Yet the game as a whole still feels accurate to the thing it's taking after.The other nice thing though is that, while accuracy is high, it does not try to unnecessarily emulate the many technical issues that often plagued older games.  NES games in particular were known for getting more than a bit loopy if there were too many sprites around at once (and that number really wasnt very high).  But that aint the case here, you can fully expect lots and lots of STUFF going on, often with big, vibrant sprites.One thing to keep in mind is that for the most part, these games are short.  Well, short by modern standards.  By retro standards, they're pretty typical.  On the NES, even many "big" games can be beaten in just a couple of hours (with RPGs typically being the exception).   However, replay value factors in here sometimes in ways that didnt really happen back then.  Some games use procedural elements for instance, which just didnt happen on consoles back then.I'm not quite sure what else to say here... it's hard to review a whole collection of stuff!  But I've loved every game I've tried so far.  That bug hunter one in particular is as addictive as caffeine.UFO 50 is clearly a love letter to an era of gaming that is long gone, yet still loved by many. As someone who grew up with and still plays old games, I'm very, very impressed to see such a high quality thing here, that truly feels authentic in ways almost no modern retro-style games manage, yet still having important differences where needed, and a level of creativity that didnt happen back then.  A very, very impressive design... and I've only gotten started with it. This game wont be for everyone, it's clearly aimed at a certain type of player.  But if it's your sort of thing, you're going to freaking love it... I know I do.

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 is the brain child of an entire team of independent creatives at Mossmouth, the studio behind the two popular roguelite dungeon (or maybe cave?) crawlers, Spelunky and Spelunky 2. UFO 50 is hard to describe as a “game” in the word’s singular form, for it is, as the name might reveal, a collection of 50 video games made by the indie studio over the span of 9 long years. To this end, this bundle of games is nothing short of monumental, both in terms of price-to-content ratio, as well as its sheer scope for a work of independent game design. UFO 50 can also be described as quite ingenious in terms of many of the ideas that it brings to the table throughout its 50 bespoke experiences as well as for its general quality over this exhaustive number of games, both big and small.Nine years, however, is a short time to make 50 games and though amazing, UFO 50 still suffers from the occassional objectively poorly designed experience, or even downright broken game, such as the community’s most reviled “Combatants”, an RTS with abysmal level design, horrendous friendly unit AI and pathing and just a baffling blatancy to its lack of polish in these and a few other areas. This collection, telling the fictional story of short-lived 1980s gaming manufacturer “Ufosoft” is clearly inspired and arguably even somewhat of a parody of those old, bootleg shovelware cartridges for the old Nintendo Entertainment System and the like, to this end, as well as to the end of delivering a genuinely interesting story of this fictional company throughout its 50 chronologically sorted offerings, UFO 50 also delights and helps to deliver on the lofty promises those bootlegers made back in the day to every child and parent out there.However, due to its arguable overabundance of games () and due to being made by Mossmouth, of all companies, who, if you’ve ever played Spelunky or especially its sequel, have a hard time discerning between fair difficulty design and playing an RNG slot machine sometimes, some games in this collection are held back and a few of them, though mercifully not the majority, show little meaningful difference between themselves and the shovelware that inspired this collection’s existence. Some of the games in the collection also commit the cardinal sin of borrowing both the good and the bad and archaic from the retro games of old.If you’re fine with the above, can hold back your completionist urges, to not let them sully your experience and can maybe hold out a little for some of the game’s bigger flaws and bugs to potentially be ironed out with time, then I highly recommend UFO 50, even if just to witness its novelty and get inspired by some of its more bizarre and interesting ideas.

_childDocuments_.review: There's so much to say about this game. I feel like I've barely scratched the surface. It is such an ambitious game. There are lots of games with large scope, but it's all by the numbers. It's all logical geometric expansion. There are shockingly few games made in the last few years made with any sense of excitement, or any sense of developers pushing themselves and gaming to a new limit. UFO 50 is that game, it is the game that no one could even think of, Action 52 but good? Who could come up with such a game? Who could actually follow through with this vision, and not chicken out? And I'm not just calling out AAA developers, but even indie devs, where is the passion? Everyone is phoning it in, everyone is happy to coast doing logical, straightforward, iterative, incremental, comfortable progress. Not this game.So the games themselves. I haven't even tried all the games yet, but what I've seen is more than enough for the price of entry and then some. Every game has terrific spritework, and with lots of variety as well. Very quickly you will take for granted the consistently high standards for the visuals, unless you are constantly focusing to take it all in. Not only does the game look great, much more important is how instantly readable everything is. Clarity is sadly something neglected these days in games, even 2D sprite based games, not so here. The only thing that you can kinda tell it's made by 6 dudes making 50 games with, is that there isn't *that* much music compared to say how much amazing spritework there is. Pretty understandable and less something to knock against the game and more to make you realize what a herculean task this is. All the games control well, everything is responsive and intuitive. And, it shouldn't have to be said but it does, the game actually runs totally fine I've not had any issues with anything relating to performance. The overall length of games can be a little bit short, a couple games stand out with that, but usually within normal bounds for actual old school retro games. With Camouflage I 100%'d it fairly quickly, definitely a lot shorter than any retail puzzle game I've played but honestly it's smart, there probably wasn't much more to squeeze with its game design. I'm not usually a guy to advocate for short games... but when you have 50 yeah it's a little different lol. I haven't yet tried the JRPG, holding onto that one for later.The styling of the games is quite impressive. There are some more straight forward games you'd expect from a collection like this, like Elfazar's Hat and Fist Hell. Then you get real weird ones, like Golfaria and Waldorf's Journey. And many games that are ostensibly within a standard genre, yet with real unique distinctions and design like Night Manor and Valbrace. There's very little straightforward orthodox design, and typically that's reserved for styles of games that aren't in vogue. I cannot even tell you how happy that makes me, the developers' eyes were on the prize. No pointlessly reinventing the wheel here. Night Manor in particular, I've always wanted to enjoy point and clicks, but frankly I've never been engrossed in them besides like Snatcher. But Night Manor, there's just some very obvious streamlining the genre should have done decades ago, there's real actual danger and tension, and it makes sense. And the overall experience is engaging, and it just makes me ask, where are the point and clicks like this and why were they basically never made? When you can outshine so much of an entire genre's output... while making FORTY NINE other games, that's a success.Just to talk about a couple games: I like Bushido Ball, it's my favorite so far. Elementally fun game in the vein of Windjammers, with just a bit more extra elements to spice it up. The game is just fun, well made, and a head slapping moment of "why isn't anyone else doing this???"Rail Heist: This is the game that really got me going when I tried this collection. I tried a couple games real quick, and then hopped onto Rail Heist and wow it blew me away. Such a unique set up, turn based timed platformer heist cowboy game. The fact the developers weren't afraid of such strong binary states and logic, such as getting in front of a lawman with a loaded gun is an instant death, is what makes this game so interesting. I feel like this style of design is basically dead, nowadays everything is so 'analog' which makes everything very relative and easy to faceroll if you have any basic skill at games.Waldorf's Journey: Charming, unique, genuinely funny and oh so slightly haunting. My wife and a friend were watching me play this game with captive interest, constantly coaching me on every jump, giggling at the signs. I don't think I've seen people have this sense of wonder from just watching a game since childhood. I'd call that a success. It is a bit short, though I know I've missed some things.Then there's the frame narrative. It's a sort of creepy pasta thing or something. It seems interesting, but not exactly sure where it's going. I think I have a few ideas of how to dig deeper into it? There's a sort of haunted/demonic undertone to things... I don't like that stuff but eh IDK where it's going it might be cool. It was an obvious idea to do a loose frame narrative like this for such a collection, and I appreciate the obvious effort that went into it. I guess I'll see how it turns out.Anyway, if reading this review didn't make you want to immediately buy this game and play it you have to ask if you're even a real gamer. I like 2D games, I like retro games, but I generally just prefer 3D and more modern(ish) games. But even then, it is plainly obvious what an incredible achievement this collection is. If you aren't talking about UFO 50, you don't "get it" at all. This game is about the highest recommendation I can give for a game. It is a steal at 50 dollars, yet they're selling it for 25. Buy this if you have ever enjoyed one video game in your life for even a second.**Edit** I forgot to mention, this game is actually low key a fantastic party game. Tons of multiplayer games, easy to have quick games constantly swapping controllers. I don't think the developers intended for this, but it's a great feature.

_childDocuments_.review: After 20 hours I've only touched 25% of the games in the collection -- they range in complexity and scale but what they all have in common is that they're incredibly polished, enjoyable experiences.The diverse collection includes plenty of platformers and arcade shoot-em-ups like you might expect, but I'm more impressed by the more unusual titles that combine genres in completely novel ways I've never seen before. Rail Heist is a platform strategy game (!?) where you plan out ways to jump, punch and break walls to steal treasure and outwit lawmen. These games aren't "What if we remade Elevator Action with better physics," they're all bafflingly novel and unique takes on new genres and new ideas you've never seen before.The most intimidating so far is Campanella 2 which seems to be what you get if you mix Spelunky, Blaster Master and Lunar Lander, I can see myself sinking 20 or 30 hours in that game alone!

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played 10 games out of the the available 50 but it really does hit you in the heart and remind you why you fell in love with video games in the first place. my personal favorite titles from what I have played is Magic Garden, a puzzle game cut in the same vein as Gomola speed on the TGFX 16 with a really nice and clean color palette. next is Kick club, which is a love letter to single screen action/puzzle games like Snow Bros and bubble bobble. Barbuta, which is a 2D side scroller action/adventure game, like a hybrid between Lode Runner and The tower of Druaga. lastly, Bushido ball, a deceptively simple 1 one 1 tennis/dodge ball hybrid, dipped in ancient Japanese flare, Almost reminds me of a Kunyu-kun sports game. there are games for every kinds of people here, (strategy games are my broccoli so i could barely play for more than a minute). UFO 50 is a definite must have for folks who grew up in the era of experimental games where video game archetypes are still in it's infancy and gaming trends have not been codified yet. 8/10 from me.Video games are fun.

_childDocuments_.review: The most fun I've had with any game in years, and I've only played like 10 out of the 50. Here are my 2 favourites so far: You're stuck in a room, but you shrink down and become tiny to explore the extensive world of tiny creatures within the room. The lore is rich and strange and I love it. Heaps of hidden mechanics revealed as the game progresses, making me exclaim with joy and surprise literally a dozen times. Banger soundtrack that I've been humming for weeks. I didn't grow up with 2D platformers, and in general I haven't found them interesting as an adult. But Mini and Max has me wanting to go back and play all the classics of the genre. 10/10. A deckbuilder where you have to plan the 'ultimate party'. Cute and fun concept. Challenging and interesting execution. The first scenario is really hard, but teaches the basic concepts; try the 2nd or 3rd scenario for an easier time. Other deckbuilders have yet to keep my interest, but Party House is in my brain now.Aside from this, I love fictional consoles and think they are an incredibly fun idea. And I love the experience of trawling through a collection of 50 games and finding favourites, and laughing in frustration at some of the ones that I bounce off. Blow the dust off another cartridge, read a couple sentences about the game and its history, then dive in and see what you find. It might be a game drenched in nostalgia for you. Or it might introduce you to a genre you haven't played.There's something here for nearly everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of the games in this collection are absolutely amazing. I loved Mini & Max as well as Grimstone and Velgress. It's unlikely that you will enjoy every game in the collection, since it's impossible to please everyone with a collection of 50 games with a variety of genres, but I think they knew that when designing this game. So many games have way more content than you would expect that even if you only play a few games you are definitely still getting your money's worth of content. I genuinely would have payed like $10 for just Mini & Max by itself, its so good.Also as a Linux user I can confirm that it works perfectly on Debian stable. I have also tested it on Debian testing, and the game lags to point it's unplayable, but I think it's an issue with Vulkan. Using the launch args "PROTON_USE_WINED3D=1 %command%" fixes it and works flawlessly once again. I believe it is because WINE uses OpenGL and Proton uses Vulkan.

_childDocuments_.review: If there have been any major releases over the past 10 years that are as consistently, unrelentingly fun as the average UFO50 game, I missed them. I honestly don't think the rest of the industry knows how to make fun games like this. Derek Yu and his friends know, and here are a bunch of them.Though I might not recommend all 50 of them, I'd recommend 6 or 7, which is more games than you usually get, and I can genuinely say that 47 of them, maybe all of them, at least brought me *joy* for a minute or so and usually far more than a minute, even though I probably wont have time to finish them, which is far more joy than you usually get.Maybe the reason UFO50 is such a breath of golden air from the before times is that the format allows games to be a little weird, to open hard, to end before they've outstayed their welcome and without trying to make themselves out to be more than they are. That is great stage for games, and it's very different to the hype-fueled spectacle oriented live service advertising and sales channels that the rest of the industry is enslaved to.My weirdest fav game here is Planet Zoldath, because I think it captures a proto-genre of figuring-out-an-alien-ecosystem, this genre really wants to be born soon and I will celebrate anything that resembles it even if it's clunky and simple, and also I guess because it's just big enough to challenge my (limited) sense of spacial recall without overwhelming it. My more normal favs are Warptank (it's flowy and cool), Mortol II (the world is freaky, and it's such a fresh, atmospheric gameplay system) and Campanella 2 (The true spiritual successor to Spelunky as far as I'm concerned).I'm eager to find out what *your* weirdest favs will turn out to be.
