_childDocuments_.review: Remember Retro Game Challenge, the collection of faux-retro games for the Nintendo DS?  UFO 50 does, and it dares to ask the question:  What if we made Retro Game Challenge...  but  and UFO 50 is the story of the LX computer.  It can be summed up as thus:  The LX computer is a computer whose story is told in UFO 50. That's as thin as your introduction to the game is.  Unlike Retro Game Challenge, which went the extra mile to illustrate what to do, how to play, meeting you with metered-out challenges to make certain you had a hang of it before opening you up to the full game, UFO 50 immediately asks if you would like to refund.The very first game, Barbuta, is a silent, low-fidelity port of Montezuma's Revenge to a DOS machine.  The colors aren't CGA, thankfully enough, but the pallette is about as deep.  The first game will take you about 60 hours to beat, most of which will be spent walking through the same eight rooms cycling the initial upgrades and trying to advance a single room before you get to start for the very beginning.  If you walk 'right' from the spawn point, you die immediately.The second game, Bug Hunter, is an inscrutable puzzle platformer whose main mechanic is you dying and being sent back to start.  Even if you manage to kill enough instant-lose eggs fast enough, you'll be told you didn't kill enough after ten turns and lose anyways.  I'm certain it was supposed to evoke the feeling of playing a game without the manual.  But they kept the joke going.The third game, Ninpek, evokes Alex Kidd in Shinobi World and Mappy, except Alex Kidd had health points.  After roughly 15 seconds, you'll die and be sent back to start.Manik Garden is Snake.  Just Snake.  The only innovation is a girl on the side of the screen that laughs at you when the controls freeze.All of these games, passably,  retro.  But restricted resolutions and pallette sizes seem to be all the care they put into the game to making it  retro; the foiables of the day were copy and pasted in from StackOverflow because the YouTube video said games like that  that way, but they never explore why.  Or use it.  Barbuta freezes and has a buzz at every screen transition.  This is because it was loading information from disk, in the old days - which no game had to do when the only information on the screen was a 16x20 grid.  Even the Vic 20 could load a couple dozen screens of that size type without resorting to dirty tricks.  There is no hit immunity anywhere, because old Youtube videos said we had no hit immunity back then (even though Wabbit for the 2600 had it in 1982).  It's not just the myopia of nostalgia:  it's the myopia of the nostalgia of the Nostalgia Critic and the Angry Video Game Nerd.But worse, There's no onboarding.  No guidance.  No setup.  None of the things you'd get with the classic games are present.  For a good example, consider the game compilations made by Zachtronics: Exapunks and Last Call came with print-and play "feelies" that evoke the feeling of old printouts and carefully thumbed through magazine articles covering for old games.   In Sega's acclaimed Genesis compilation, you get a text intro and can review the intro at any time.  In Retro Game Challenge, you get a small story that links game segments into short tasks - one minute, then two, then three, then four, slowly building up while letting you read in-game "strategy guides".  Even Nintendo's Virtual Console, dumping ground of old retro games, still lets you see the manual.These games were presented in "chronological" order, starting from '82 (with a console with an '86 pallete doing things we would start doing in '84).  So I thought, let's skip ahead to '89, the last year in the game's chronology. We have Cyber Owls, a genre mashup.  Surely, there, we have seven years of evolution?  And yes, while there is some faux-digitized speech, and the first semblance of something like characters in the art, it has all the foiables of the first games in the series.  The limited resources of Bug Hunter.  The fragility of Barbuta.  The only saving grace this game has is that you have a introduction NPC, Wells, who tells you what to expect; that doesn't help when the game haphasardly tosses you into a Streets of Rage knockoff, then a Rambo knockoff, then a Battletoads knockoff, then a Metal Gear knockoff.  There's supposed more levels past the first four.  I don't want to bother reinstalling the game to explore them.There's 45 more games.  I could go on, but I'm not going to.  I recommend you don't either.

_childDocuments_.review: Retro gamers rejoice!Having played 30+ hours and counting, I felt like I had to delete and rewrite my previously positive review to give Mossmouth even higher praise. Night Manor is the S**T! Absolutely amazing atmosphere and cleverly well thought out puzzles. I'm daft as all hell and got stuck a few times, but eventually figured things out.Haven't played every game yet, but I also quite like Ninpek, Mortol, Velgress, Kick Club, Vainger (amazing and hard), Valbrace, Elfazar’s Hat, Rail Heist, Kick Club, Magic Garden, Party House and Pilot Quest (it gets really cool once you figure it out). It's a really varied collection, and you'll probably find yourself getting cherry on games you're not quite fond of first, like I did with Big Bell Race. Don't get me wrong, it's polished and fine, I'm just not into single screen track racing games.Overall the game is easily worth full price. If you get it cheaper, it's a hell of a deal.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played the first twenty games chronologically at the time of this review, so I haven't played them all yet, but I had to share my thoughts so far.This game has already grabbed a hold of me. This is a collection of high quality games ranging from arcade style titles that can be played repeatedly to try and get a high score, all the way up to stuff like this Zelda-like Golf RPG where you have to explore the world. There is so much variety here and lots of value for the money. So many of these arcade style games are going to be great for playing on my Steam Deck when I only have a few minutes and don't want to commit to something more substantial, and all of the longer titles exude tons of charm and have very interesting gimmicks and ideas thrown in. I have found thus far that this game really shines in the puzzle game department, EVERY SINGLE PUZZLE GAME I'VE PLAYED HAS BEEN SO COOL, especially Devilition.And one more thing I wanted to mention, this is how I personally recommend playing this game: - Play the games in chronological order (default sort) from the first game to the last game. For extra spice, pace yourself and try just a few new games at a time. (I'm doing five a day for ten days personally.)- Give each game a try, but if a game is not connecting with you don't feel like you have to stick with it and try to like it. (I'm looking at you Ninpek) You'll find they have multiple games that are the same genre and although you might not like the gimmicks or game play of one, another may be perfect for you.- Every so often, go back and give some of the games you've already tried another chance. Some of the games take a bit of time to learn because of their "classic" nature, but once you begin to understand them they really open up and become quite interesting. (I passed over Mooncat pretty quick because of how weird it was, but after giving it a second chance it's now one of my favorites.)It's also important to note if you do play them chronologically, they start out fairly primitive because they are canonically the earliest games this imaginary company released and they where still learning how to best utilize the hardware and make games approachable. Barbuta is the first game and it feels pretty clunky and hard, but don't let it discourage you. I really hope people don't download this collection, try this game first, and go well this game sucks.TLDR: There is so much to like about this awesome variety pack of old school games. Make sure to give the games a chance and you're bound to find some games you'll love!
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: «God, I love video games so much».That's how UFO 50 makes me feel. It doesn't just let me enjoy the games it has on offer, it reinforces my love for gaming as a whole. Each one of the 50 games in the compilation is another complete mechanical system for me to solve and enjoy. None of the games are throwaways: each is creatively distinct, and each will be enjoyed by the right kind of video game enthusiast. The sheer variety of the games acts as a reminder of why I became enthralled by the world of video games in the first place. The completionist in me was having a great time too: UFO 50 gives you a trophy for every game you've beaten, and has a completionism challenge for every game on top of that, rewarding you with a cherry if you meet it. Also, half of the games have local multiplayer, and as I played through them, I often found myself thinking «this must be really fun to play with a friend!».The honeymoon period does eventually pass, but, as you can see from my play hours, it kept me going for quite a while. Eventually, it becomes apparent that some of the games are better than others. I definitely enjoyed the more arcade-like games like Magic Garden or Seaside Drive over the rpgs and metroidvanias. And some of the requirements for a cherry are much too tedious in comparison to others, which eventually put out the flames of completionism in me. But I had a great time while it lasted.Final score:Trophies: 40Cherries: 31
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: It may have taken way longer than expected, but UFO 50 was worth the wait.  Don't think of this as a minigame collection, because there is nothing "mini" about most of the titles.  They all are titles that could have been commercial releases in the 80s, or standalone indie titles today.  Whatever your genre preferences, you'll almost certainly find several games worth the price of the collection.  My own favorite, the western-themed JRPG "Grimstone", almost justifies the price on its own:  its roughly as content-rich as its inspiration, the first Final Fantasy.  And its not the only one, as the collection covers pretty much every genre you'd find during the 80s ( and several you wouldn't ).

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most ambitious and inspiring indie games I've ever played! I've only beaten Barbuta, Ninpen (with cherry), Magic Garden, Mooncat, and Planet Zoldath so far. The presentation and music are excellent, and although some games are intentionally abrasive as a homage to an older era of gaming, that gives some of the games a weirdly addictive quality. For example, Barbuta has some VERY annoying design decisions like a molasses-level movement speed, but all of the secrets and optimisations you can find for your route made me unable to put it down until I finished it. Really looking forward to discovering the rest of what this has to offer. _childDocuments_.review: I would by no means describe myself as a gamer; I'm just someone who grew up with the SNES as a kid, emulated in their teens, and to this day has always had a soft spot for retro and indie retro-style games. So with such a talented, decorated team creating such a massive tribute to this era of gaming, with an overarching meta no doubt, the whole premise of this collection almost feels made for me.I've enjoyed just about every game I've picked up; They remind me of my youth, but with a modern lens that makes things feel fresh and optimistic- For one thing, there are a lot more women in these games, in many more dynamic roles than the games I grew up with. The graphics are beautiful and punchy, obviously influenced by the NES and MSX but allowing themselves to be more than that, creating games that just look... Lush! Every game has something new to bring to the table while still feeling extant to the era- Inspirations are obvious but nothing ever feels samey or blatantly copied. This is all to say, every game stands on their own. The collection is truly a creative masterwork.The only thing I think needs to be improved: The performance and difficulty issues in this collection are just too much to ever make meaningful progress. I have a mid-range PC with a dedicated graphics card, and still my FPS jumps anywhere from 15 to 60+ in seconds, seemingly just based on how many sprites/background layers are on the screen- Which is authentic!..But also infuriating. And being told on the FAQ to just "play it in a smaller window" isn't very encouraging. Don't get me wrong, I love a challenge: I've gotten a few Cherry disks already... But some of these games are hard enough *with* slowdown. I genuinely cannot imagine a regular Joe who has fond memories of retro games being able to achieve Cherry on any of these games at 60+FPS. And with no Vsync, built-in frame-limiting, or any other way to curb that difficulty... It makes it hard for me to actually recommend to anyone who may need these modern amenities.Still: A really wonderful idea, and I'm so glad it's done so well. All praise well deserved. I just wish there was a *little* bit more of the modern game design it touts to have.

_childDocuments_.review: Just to preface, I'm approximately 50 hours into UFO 50. I have played 35 of the 50 games in chronological order and fully completed 18 of them. A full completion is referred to as a 'cherry' in this game. This game is incomprehensibly ambitious and I still can't wrap my head around how this was ever made and released at such an inexpensive price point. There really are 50(!) video games in this pack, each of which could have been released for $5 and nobody would bat an eye. Of course, some are better than others but there is not a single one that I've played that could be seen as being objectively bad. As you work your way through this fictitious developer's chronology, you'll notice a marked increase in video game complexity and scope, which makes me so much more excited to try out the remaining 15 games. Many of the earlier, more simplistic games took me 1.5-2 hours for a cherry completion but the newer RPGs, puzzle games, strategy games, metroidvanias, and even an immersive sim-like are taking me upwards of 5 hours per game to cherry.One tangential complaint I have is this game's handling of achievements, it should have shipped with 100-150 achievements with 2-3 per game to meet the gift, gold, and cherry requirements. The current achievements are extremely unrewarding and frankly dull.I believe UFO 50 is a must-own for any gamer who even remotely enjoys the NES/SNES era of video games, and for those who don't, this is an excellent introduction and what may become an eventual deep dive into what made these games so iconic. Almost all of these games, if released in the 80s, would be talked about like Mario and Zelda are today. A tremendous accomplishment from Mossmouth.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally write reviews, but after being able to portably play an absolute GEM from my childhood I had to give this a thumbs up. _childDocuments_.review: This is one of the greatest achievement in RETRO-gaming ever. I can´t honestly fathom how much value, creativity, intelligence and love is poured into this project. Every. Single. Game. is complete, and special. Most of the games, i would easily have spent upon 2-10dollars, just to buy one game. It´s honestly incredible that you get 50 of them, for this price.I cannot recommend this game enough, I´m currently fighting my way to complete every single cassette, something that will probably take 100 of hours. Will update this review with a review of each game, as time goes one. But honestly, BUY this. Support this developer. If you ever loved retro gaming, this is the ultimate compilation.Game: Devilition. Puzzle/Strategy. 10/10.A very interesting mix between puzzle, the Amazing Machine and turn based bomberman. You banish demons from a tilebased city, and need to chain explosions together to rid them all, without harming the villagers. Very clever, original mechanics. _childDocuments_.review: So, at this point, I've finished about two and a half of the 50 games on offer. Notably, there are several others I'm planning on playing extensively. If you're just looking at a value perspective, it is hard to beat, should you like games that are retro in both execution and appearance. That being said, this feels like so much more. The sense of discovery, joy of mastery, and lore that the game builds about an imaginary game company is like nothing else I've ever experienced. I don't think this is for everyone (though, with the quality and variety of experiences on offer, I imagine most will be engaged by at least something). However, for a certain sort of person, it is like nothing else I've ever tried. _childDocuments_.review: This collection has some of the most interesting and unique games I've ever played. There's also a lot of polish and quality craftsmanship in several of the titles, despite some being intentionally clunky and obtuse. I also love a lot of songs in this game (and I tend to be picky with OSTs).I can confidently say that anyone who buys and plays this will find a few games at minimum that they really like. If you like action games, puzzle games, strategy, platformers, arcade-style, or open-minded to unique genre hybrids, then there is a game for you.Might be one of my favorite releases of 2024. _childDocuments_.review: There is such a huge quantity of titles within this game that it is hard to trust that they are all worthwhile -- but the quality is all top notch. The first few titles (chronologically) may cause you to bounce off -- I would encourage folks to stick with it. Once you start hitting row 2 and 3 you are bound to find some titles that are appealing to you. The variety is quite astonishing and the level of polish and depth on every single title is nuts. Perhaps the greatest part of this collection is that when you start to feel burnt out, there are so many other games that are super easy and quick to hop into and start playing. The more I play the more I find myself going back to the first games that I initially didn't like -- as you get immersed in the design the appeal grows. Overall it is really a great blend of nostalgia and modern game design sensibilities. Overall value is off the charts -- and the whole "fictional game company and system with it's own lore and history" thing is well executed. The more you play it, the more it delights.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of 8-bit games, buy this collection. If not, it may be hard for you to enjoy these games. UFO 50 is a collection of 50 different, complete games, from a fictional system that never existed. You can play them in any order. Each game shows the year it was made and they get more complex as the years go on.There are many different genres to experience. Platforming, strategy, RPG, turn based tactics, RTS, sports and many more. You probably aren't going to enjoy every game in the collection, but with 50 games, you're going to find something to latch on to. These are not mini games. Each game has a beginning, middle and end. Each game also has a bonus objective that you can try to achieve. If you satisfy the requirement you get an item for the garden. The garden is a special screen that you can visit from the main menu that will display all of the items you've received. When you are on the garden screen, you will see a multi story house and a lawn. It's fun trying to unlock the item from each game.There's a lot of mystery to these games, which I enjoy. There are no manuals and you often won't know what to do, but you learn by playing and exploring, which is how it used to feel to play NES games. There is an excellent CRT filter. I like playing with the "soft" filter, which adds just enough texture to really make the games pop. I hadn't really been following this game, but it sounded interesting and I gave it a try. I have to say my initial reaction after playing for the first time was negative, because I wasn't blown away by the first games that I played. But something about this game kept me coming back for more. The more I played, the more I started to see the actual depth in each game and the full breadth of what this collection delivers. Check this game out, and enjoy playing a fictional console from the past that you wish you had growing up.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 is unapologetically my favorite game I've played this year. The amount of varied gameplay, the unexpected depth from each of the 50 games, and more than anything else the awesome feeling of nostalgia that takes you back to a gaming era where half the fun is figuring out what the hell you're even supposed to be doing in a game is great. I highly recommend giving UFO 50 a try, ESPECIALLY if you fondly remember the 8-bit era.

_childDocuments_.review: Very well made and precise with a great deal of depth. _childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 is not only a great game, but its also a interesting and well thought approach to the micro game genre. With so much creativity and charm oozing out of every pore that it can.UFO 50 is what happens when you take Action 52, but actually make it good. Mossmouth has done an amazing job replicating the limiting power of the NES while still holding onto the refinement of modern game design. Taking the basis of classic NES titles and refining them into addicting games worthy of time.Velgress is a good example of this. It takes the gameplay of Kid Icarus and tweaks the formula to create a faster paced game that rewards skill and decision while still holding onto the core elements of Icarus.Avianos is a tactical strategy game where you aren't just expected to overwhelm your opponents army, but also maintain your own economy in a way that no other tactics game I've seen has done.Rakshasa is a Ghost and Goblins type game that still keeps a lot of the original design elements that made Ghosts and Goblins difficult while also circumventing that challenge with a unique revival system.Night Manor is a point and click horror game that surprisingly creates and eerie atmosphere that games like Clock Tower pioneered.The List goes on, from Bushido Balls intense reflexes to Mortols extra life system. Every game has something to love and has so much thought behind every aspect. Add that with the completionist challenges, a virtual pet garden that grows the more you play each game, and the hidden lore behind the fictional UFOsoft company, and you got yourself one of the best retro indie games ever made.

_childDocuments_.review: Only 10 of the 50 are decent, perhaps 20 if you like old-school player-hostile design (not seeing any of the "modern game design" the store page promises). Very demanding in both tedium & reflexes, no manuals explaining anything beyond the basic controls, no ability to customize the experience (adjusting difficulty, etc...), only 0-1 save slots in-game, etc...Only get this if you've run out of NES games to play.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is perfect for those of us who admire retro games, but also appreciate modern conventions. As many others will say, the value here is INSANE - i've already sunk 7+ hours into the heavily inspired by Final Fantasy/Dragon Quest game Grimmstone. Many of us waited over 6 years for this collection to drop - but now I understand why it took so long. Each game has been meticulously polished and has its own unique vibes and charms. Ok gonna stop reviewing and go it play it more ;+)

_childDocuments_.review: Just an incredible achievement of game design, and it's cheap as hell for the amount of content. I think there's definitely something here for everybody, but especially if you're into retro games, enjoy a large variety of styles and genres, and like to figure things out yourself without too much handholding, then you'll likely have an excellent time exploring the library of games. I've only played about third of the games so far, with one gold cart for beating a game (Mooncat) and one cherry cart for 100% (Camouflage), so I know this is going to keep me entertained for a while.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Its insane how much content is packed into this. My favorites are: 1. Valbrace, which is a first person dungeon crawler with punch out style combat and a manually drawn rune system for casting magic, which lets you just guess spells if you want.2.Warptank, where you're a tank who sticks to walls and ceilings with the options to either shoot, or warp to the opposite wall. A simple concept which is explored to its fullest with great puzzles, and a whole overworld between levels with some interesting secrets.3.Bushido Ball, which is wind jammers with samurai and ninjas And many others, which even if I didn't like them at first, they eventually wormed their way into my heart. Goty for sure
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: It's not easy to understand the scope or enormity of the achievement that is UFO 50. It's a love letter to a bygone era or maybe a call to action about an era you missed. There's a indescribable joy of getting a box of games and trying them out one by one. Naturally not every game will speak to you, others might feel like they've been waiting for you to discover them your whole life and you are amazed that it took this long for you to discover it. This game is romantic, enthralling, fascinating and shows what this medium is capable of. On the off chance you've made it this far and it isn't crystal clear. You should buy this game and play it immediately.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent collection of games. Such a wide variety of aesthetic inspirations, genres, and difficulties. And of course, the framing of this all being the software output of a fictional game company, from the faux-historical blurbs discussing which developer did what and so on, to the "sequel" and "spin-off" games, just adds so much charm.I haven't found a dud so far (have at least booted up around 20 of the games at this point), but my particular favorites right now are Camouflage, a clever stealth-puzzle game where you control a chameleon who has to strategically reach various locations in order to change colors and walk past enemies undetected, and Overbold, a Smash TV-like top-down shooter where you fight waves of enemies in an arena, acquire prize money to buy power ups, and can optionally (and should probably if you want to stand a chance at the end) add extra enemies to the fights to up your winnings- at the risk of losing, of course.Definitely going to end up being my favorite game to come out this year, and while it's too early for me to say for certain yet, I could possibly see this end up being one of my favorite games ever (a descriptor I'm picky about giving out).
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most incredible accomplishments in gaming history. These are 50 fully realized and complete games, not mini games. That’s not even the most incredible part though, the most amazing part of UFO 50 is that almost every single game is interesting at the very least, to borderline GOTY at its best.I find myself getting burned out on a lot of games pretty quickly. I’ll spend 60-70 dollars on a game and have fun with it for a while but grow tired of it and just race to the end or sometimes not even finish. UFO 50 feels like the cure for gaming burn out. None of the games have overstayed their welcome and even if they did, there’s 49 other vastly different games for me to try out in seconds.This is the best deal in gaming and I can’t recommend it enough. There is something here for everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Making a metroidvania with enforced permadeath after 99 attempts seems like it would be an annoyingly frustrating experience, but Mortol II somehow manages to pull it off with some of the cleverest design I've seen in a long time. The game is designed with the knowledge that you'll run out of lives several times over before reaching the end credits, and so the map rewards knowledge and planning ahead, tactically using your lives during one game to scout out a safe path for the next. In addition, since each of the five characters has a unique sacrifice ability that permanently alters the map (at least until you run out of lives), it doesn't demand perfection to succeed. In a way, it almost resembles a speedrunning challenge, but by tying success to lives instead of time, it creates a wholly new experience. I haven't gotten to the end yet, but I know the route and I feel that success is within my grasp. If you're looking for a fresh take on the metroidvania genre, I highly recommend checking out Mortol II.You mean to say there's 49 other games here?
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I've come across in ages, though I suppose it is cheating a little.. Even then, just one or two of these have been able to keep my attention and excitement up quite a bit more than anything from a 50 in 1 game pack has any right to. All the graphics are awesome, although in exchange the music gets repetitive after a while... Even that is pretty great at first, before you realize you're gonna be hearing one or two songs for the next 3 hours. Seriously though, shout out to Bug Hunter for being such a fun puzzle game in particular, and also Grimstone for being a whole RPG in the midst of all this?? Also also just shout out to like every game except the first one for being so fun :)As a whole, one of the best deals I've ever seen in gaming, absolutely recommend it!!

_childDocuments_.review: It's ok.  I grew up on the NES and Genesis and honestly not many of these really resonate with me, I'm just not sure which classics they are trying to build off of.  To be fair I've only gone hard on about 20 of the 50 games so I'll leave it a positive review for the time being and will revisit when I've gone through them all.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: UFO 50 is a splendid package. Complete with faux history and trivia for each game, this is a collection of diverse, creative, and genuinely enjoyable games that can last you several hours each. The experience of discovering each one for yourself is one I would recommend. Playing this (mostly) blind was one of the most magical experiences I've had with video games since I was in the single digits. I've yet to dust off every game, but my current favorites are Rail Heist, Mortol, and Bushido Ball. (11/8/2024)
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: You're walking down a corridor. The corridor has 50 doors. You assume to various tiny rooms. You open one of the doors. Inside, you discover an entire world the size of Narnia. You shut the door, intimidated.And then you remember there are 49 other doors.UFO 50 is a wildly joyous and original title that consists of a breathtakingly massive collection of games that never existed, by a company that never was, each of which winks at you and invites you in to discover its secrets.It perfectly captures the way we rosily (one might say self-deludingly) remember the games of yesteryear having made us feel. That sense of mystery, the joy of discovery, the basic core mechanic that changes the entire game and you don't realize it until you've played it for 300 hours because lol WHAT manual? You borrowed this game from your cousin and then he moved to Ohio, and the internet doesn't exist yet.The emotional arc of playing this game goes "Haha, this looks cute->Ooh, this one is fun->Wait, this game has a surprising amount of depth->Wait are they ALL this deep?"And then a chasm opens up underneath you.It's pure joy with just the right amount of artistically authentic friction.I hope this game sells a million billion zillion copies and knocks the entire industry on its ass.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: We blaze and Onion Delivery all night and just laugh NONSTOP at how much we both suck. The Magic Garden song has been stuck in my head for a week. We made a Mooncat drinking game. This is such a great game/collection whatever you want to call it. It would be considered shameful to not buy it if you're still reading.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: 1.5 hours of my playtime is currently just in one game. I can see myself spending a lot of time in this collection. I can't believe there actually is 50 full games in this collection. And so far each one I have played has felt like it understood what was good in older games while also modernising it enough for it to be enjoyable still. Glad Mossmouth found these 50 games in someone's storage unit.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I waited 7 years for this game collection, and I'm surprised I didn't have to wait another 7. It's mind-blowing how many clever & original games can be found in UFO 50, and I've only seen half of the games so far. UFO 50 also pushes its feats further to weave a fictional continuity between every game - it's compelling to say the least, without venturing into spoilers!If you can't find enough games in UFO 50 to justify the astonishingly low $25 price tag, you might not be a fan of video games

At 50 cents a game this is totally worth it.edit: played some more games. played Mooncat. what the ♥♥♥♥ was that. new favourite for sure
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I dont think ive ever seen a love letter to video games quite like UFO 50. Its so immeasurably impressive that the devs were able to capture so many genres and niche little "NES throw away" title feelings. Every one of these games feels like I could dig it out of a bargain bin for 5$ and I mean that with the highest regards. Theyre fantastic, theyre clunky, theyre weird, and some (not all) would be ahead of their time. What a beautiful thing this collection is. _childDocuments_.review: This might be my game of the year.If you love video games - not just RPGs, not just Metroidvanias, not just Shmups - but you love all sorts of video games, this game combines nostalgia for the 8 bit generation with some modern sensibilities and a twist of indie gaming whimsy.It makes me think back to those lovely days on TIGSource the late 2000's when Cave Story and La Mulana were new phenomena and every day somebody was posting a demo of their latest genre mash-up. But it also reminds me of renting NES games and marveling at the strange things people created before video games began to clearly define genres and conventions. It's a tribute to the classic days of gaming.In addition to by-the-book platformers, RPGs, and shmups, you'll get turn-based heists, deck builder parties, and a crazy taxi demake where driving recklessly gives you life.It's a ridiculous bargain at twice the price. You're sure to find at least one game that absolutely clicks (Party House is my weakness of choice).Play it casually to collect garden decorations or play it intensely to score all the delicious cherries, there's something for all skill levels. Just don't let this masterpiece pass you by.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Ignore any negative review on this game, they just don't get it. This pack is INSANE and is worth every penny it's wild. This is a pack of 50 games stylized to be in the era of NES - Early SNES while also having really neat fake history associated with a console that never existed.What makes this so unique is that the way the games progress is similar to how games progressed in real life, they started more simple, arcadey and overall one dimensional, and as time passed they get more complex, have more depth, and experiment with mechanics. Some of the games are also really LONG like, long long, not like play it for an hour, like full-fledged indie game. It's honestly amazing how fun some of these are especially some you can even play with friends. So far i'm enjoying the most the Bird strategy game and the Windjammers-like Samurai game the most as they are super fun to play with friends.This pack is an awesome bang for your buck, if you're not into older games you may not enjoy it, but give it a try if you love the era of NES/SNES games!
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: Fifty 8-bit video games, each with their own genre and weird quirks, none of which hold your hand but all of which are designed in a way to help you figure things out yourself, all tied together with a fictitious timeline and publishing history, and $25 for all fifty games. If any of that appeals to you, then UFO 50 is worth checking out. Even if you don't appreciate all 50, I'm guessing you'll have a great time with at least 10 of them. My favorites are #10, #21, #26, #40, and #45.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot of really fantastic games here that are included just like any of the other but they stand out so much that you wonder why this game is so generous with it's quality; this game provides exactly what you would want out of a collection of 50 micro games. Despite being micro, the games are sometimes long as hell or repayable forever!! This game will one day be a goated game to return to every once and a while for years to come. 10/10

Some of the games were not my cup of tea and the overall difficulty was tuned very high, but I really enjoyed the variety and how well this recreated the feeling of playing old NES games without having a manual at hand. _childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: 50 small games. All in different genres. Puzzle games, platformers, sport games, multiplayer games (that you also can play alone), deck builders, point and click games. It has it all.Try and beat every single game for a gold cartridge. Every game has an extra challenge for a cherry cartridge as well.Super well done, and perfect to play with a controller or on the steam deck.
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I already know that this is my GOTY for 2024. Yes, it's actually that good. UFO 50 is downright insane for what it is and for such a low price point. The developers put so much love, effort, creativity, and thought into this monstrous project that I'm completely in awe.This game is an absolute must have if you love retro games and are interested in topics such as video game history, game design, ludology, art, and/or experimental storytelling. There's so much content to digest here, they obviously took much inspiration from many beloved video games released in the 80s and early 90s. I don't think there's a single game I dislike, all of them range from good to beyond amazing.If you really care about seeing all the secret then you'll likely be spending months if not years on this/these game(s).
_childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: This game has legitimately made waiting for anything a joy, because now I can just boot up my steam deck and play any game on UFO 50 and be sure to have a fun time. It's an amazingly addictive set of games, there's literally something for everyone in this collection, and these aren't short games; they have so much depth. There's even a whole SquareEnix-esque RPG in this thing!! If you want the best value for your buck you can't go wrong with this.One thing I will say is that, akin to classic retro games, there are a few games in this collection that are not very photosensitive-friendly; essentially, any of the shmups. If you are photosensitive, keep this in mind when selecting what games to play. There's plenty of other games in the collection that don't involve flashing effects.

_childDocuments_.review: GOTY Material, a truly unique collection of old style games that take inspiration from the old and the new. From everything ranging from idle games and tower defense games masquerading as if they were made on old hardware to traditional old games. Now not every game in this collection is a gem. I've ran across 3 games which seem truly terrible almost by design, but I've spent tons of hours in this collection and found so many treasures.I STRONGLY RECOMMEND STARTING BOTTOM LEFT. _childDocuments_.review: Keeps the best part of old-school games (not wasting your time, genuine challenge without being obnoxious for the sake of it, doing more with less) while still benefiting from modern design and smoothness. These are the games we could have gotten 20 years ago and didn't. They're here now, for like 50 cents a pop. Hell yeah. Don't start with #1; log in to Pilot Quest (which has some idle game aspects you can get started right away) and then try Ninpek, Big Bell Race, Devilition, and Bushido Ball for a nice sampler pack.

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like how I remember those old Dreamgear 50-in-1 plug in plays I had as a kid in the mid 2000s feeling. They came in clutch during the post-Hurricaine Katrina fallout and despite those being not the best made games, having 50 of them to pick from still always felt so exciting. I never expected to ever get that feeling again but this game gave that to me and more. I've been excited for this game since it was annoucned 7 years ago and it's surpassing the expectations I had for it. I genuinely think this might end up being my game of the year and I've only played 6 of the 50 games so far. _childDocuments_.name: UFO 50

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played 5 games and not completed any, but this is already a 5-star review from me.As someone who played games all through this era it *very* much captures the spirit of gaming in that time. Don't get me wrong - these are very much modern games, but the experience of comitting to a title because you bought it, and *finding the fun* is so spot on. People will be discovering these games for years to come.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm about to go STUPID on this review, so if you want the TL;DR then look no further. Just imagine 'Action 52' but it's actually a masterpiece. That's it.Okay, to the meat of it. UFO 50 is a collection of fifty real games (made by Mossmouth), except they're made by an imaginary company (UFO Soft) in an alternate timeline spanning from '82 to '89. And when I called it a masterpiece in the TL;DR, I really meant it. I don't mean that every game is perfect, although I do think there are a handful of perfect games in the pack. What I mean is that, as a whole, this collection was masterfully crafted with true expertise in game design and it's history, AND an incredible artistic vision from a crack team of fantastic devs. If you want to go in blind after seeing the screenshots and reading a few reviews, this would be the place to stop. I will talk a bit more about the game as a whole at the end of this review, but for now I'm just going to drop fifty mini-reviews straight from the heart.01) Barbuta - LoZ 2 but not really, just don't die to traps. 7/1002) Bug Hunter - Into the Breach if it was on NES, with it's own twist of course. 9/1003) Ninpek - Just an evergreen action-platformer, think 1 long stage of Mario but there's more action. 8/1004) Paint Chase - Splatoon 0 but you're driving an F1 car instead of shooting water guns. 7/1005) Magic Garden - Snake 2, simple fun but there's not much to write home about. 6/1006) Mortol - A VERY unique action/puzzle platformer, incredible lives-economy. First taste of perfection. 10/1007) Velgress - Downwell 2: Upwell, but Derek made this one and not Ojiro (the Downwell dev). 8/1008) Planet Zoldath - A dash of LoZ 1, a hint of Toejam & Earl.. Not really but kind of. 7/1009) Attactics - PvZ on NES but it's FAST, and you must attack with tactics. 8/1010) Devilition - Rube Goldberg machine in a game, it's so good I need more. 9/1011) Kick Club - Bubble Bobble 2 but it's sportsball and USA world is taking PEDs. 7/1012) Avianos - Civ 0 but you're birds and your gods are dinos. Another one I just want more of. 9/1013) Mooncat - Bite-sized lil' platformer with very unique and fun controls. 8/1014) Bushido Ball - Windjammers me. Pong 3 me. 7/1015) Block Koala - What if Sokoban was on crack? Answer: it would hurt my tiny head. 6/1016) Camouflage - Now THIS is my type of puzzler. Don't get caught slippin'. 8/1017) Campanella - AddictingGames helicopter flash game but it's way better. 7/1018) Golfaria - Don't sleep on this game, an open-world adventure with golf movement and it's good. 9/1019) The Big Bell Race - Campanella Kart. Simple as. 7/1020) Warptank - VVVVVV but you can shoot, and there's more action with less puzzles. 8/1021) Waldorf's Journey - Toss the Turtle on NES. S'good. S'really good. 9/1022) Porgy - Dave the Diver as a metroidvania but there's no restaurant stuff. Brutal first 15min but still great. 8/1023) Onion Delivery - Bite-sized NES Crazy Taxi. The rain really sucks though, like BAD. 7/1024) Caramel Caramel - Gradius but take a cute pic of your enemy before you take their life too. 8/1025) Party House - Blackjack's cooler cousin, like if gambling was a drug. Pure dopamine. Hit-hit-hit-hit-NOOO. 10/1026) Hot Foot - Beanbag-dodgeball, pretty tough but pretty fun too. 7/1027) Divers - Ironically much less like Dave the Diver than Porgy. Nice, classic RPG with turn-based combat. 8/1028) Rail Heist - Semi-turn-based strategy platformer, figure out the perfect route and execute your heist. 9/1029) Vainger - What if Metroid and VVVVVV had a baby? Spoiler, it's awesome. 9/1030) Rock On! Island - Really solid tower defense game, it's no BTD6 but it's great. 8/1031) Pingolf - Pretty good mashup between golf and pinball, more on the golf side. 7/1032) Mortol 2 - Great sequel, fun twist on the first. Less linear and less pointed because of it though. 8/1033) Fist Hell - Double Dragon if you were beating up zombies. Good wood. 8/1034) Overbold - Smash TV could NEVER. I mean NEVER. Stop here and call it UFO 34, it's that good. But don't... 10/1035) Campanella 2 - Spelunky and Campanella and Metal Slug are having a threesome and I WANT IN. 9/1036) Hyper Contender - A pretty unique and simplistic "fighter". At first I was "no way" but then it turned "YEAH". 7/1037) Valbrace - Wizardry dungeon crawling, Arx Fatalis magic, and some funky real-time combat?? Perfect blend. 10/1038) Rakshasa - What if Ghosts n' Goblins was even harder? It's pretty good, honestly, with some nice quirks. 7/1039) Star Waspir - Ikaruga on NES with an interesting letter-combo system. Tough cherry but great game. 8/1040) Grimstone - Oh, it's cowboy FF1? Oh, and we in HELL? Yeehaw, pardner. 9/1041) Lords of Diskonia - Strategy shuffleboard w/ a fantasy skin + some interesting depth. Not really balanced though. 5/1042) Night Manor - What an incredible point-and-click adventure/horror game. Incredible writing. Not long enough. 9/1043) Elfazar's Hat - Very cute and very fun shmup here. Only issue, like Night Manor, is that it's not long enough. 9/1044) Pilot Quest - They put an IDLE GAME in my UFO 50?? And it's got a real adventure game in it too! 8/1045) Mini & Max - Sing it with me,  SMB2 but it's perfect. Wtfwhyisitsoperfectwtfbestgame 10/1046) Combatants - Derek made a fun game but it's hiding under this unbalanced, RNG dependant mess. Yu piece. 6/1047) Quibble Race - Papa never should've taken me to the races... All in on Hadeezer. ALL IN. 8/1048) Seaside Drive - Ojiro did WORK, this game is snappy and well-designed and it's fun and MMMM. 9/1049) Campanella  3 - Super solid shmup, almost Elfazar levels but not quite. 8/1050) Cyber Owls - The GAUNTLET, but not the game Gaunlet. Dash of MGS, Altered Beast, Contra 1 Stage 2, and more. 8/10Now, if you're still here and you're still wondering, NO. This game is not just re-hashing a bunch of old retro games that you may have played before. I may have said things like, "This game is X if it was on the NES but Y!" In fact, I know I did. But that doesn't mean it's just a lazy copy-paste. These games are fresh and a lot of care went into modernizing certain aspects of retro-game design that may not hold up to modern standards. A lot of unique and really fun concepts were injected into classic titles to make them iterative and exciting, rather than being monotonous and lifeless. Sure, some of them didn't hit for me, but others were personally immaculate. And, by my count, there are more 10's than there are 6's. There's so much variety too, you're bound to find something you love. Genres ranging across the board, playtimes from ~1hr to 20+hrs, it's like there's something for everybody. And in a weird way, it also feels like the sort of niche piece of media that was created by X for X that would normally feel inaccessible. Like, I could see this game being your favorite game-dev's favorite game. That's the vibe that it has. It truly feels like a masterfully crafted love letter to gaming as a whole and a particular period in it's history. And I love it <3At the time of review: 50/50 Golden Disks, 18/50 Cherry Disks. The cherry grind begins.

_childDocuments_.review: There are so many ways an idea this ambitious could fail.  Or just be middle of the road bleh.Instead, each game feels loved, like it had a champion in the room fighting for it to be the best version of itself.  Like Spelunky and Downwell, the design choices in these games feel incredibly specific and intentional.  There isn't a throwaway in the collection, even the games I vibe with less are still clearly labors of love.It's all the spirit and bursting creativity of a game jam, with the polish of a Devolver Digital release.Easily the best game I've played released in 2024.

_childDocuments_.review: I've only tried 36 of the games so far, but every single one is something I want to go back and play more. There is so much more than I was expecting here. These games are meaty. Many of them I already know I'm going to spend hours and hours with. I'm not sure yet, and the mystery is exciting...

_childDocuments_.review: I don't like numeric scores at all, but this game comes as highly recommended as I possibly can.If you've never experienced the joy of pirating all the best games for a classic console and immersing yourself in title-after-high-quality-title, this will probably *ruin* that experience: these games are empirically better than 99% of 8-bit games I've ever played. Details I like about this game: - Consistent pixel width, no subpixel motion (that I can notice)- Scanline simulation (sexy)- OST, sfx, etc all seem to come from one synthesis system, creating amazing cohesion title to title- Minor intra-title thematic references (ex. references to Campanella and Avianos in Rock On! Island)
