_childDocuments_.review: Doom 64 has always been one of my favourite doom games. Even back when i used to play Brutal Doom 64 I still loved the game. The level design has held up extremely well, better than Ultimate Doom and Doom 2 in my opinion. As for this port, it's easily the best one out of the bunch. Brutal Doom 64 changed far too much and is incredibly unbalanced on high difficulties, Doom 64 Retribution was very inaccurate, and Doom 64 EX was good, but was based on an old sourceport and had a few issues. This port cleans up these issues and overall improves the experience. The mouse aiming is silky smooth and this port is incredibly optimized, I have a toaster of a pc and I ran it at 1080p and I never once had a single hitch during my playtime. As for the new content, the Lost Levels are a great inclusion, they're challenging and have even better level design than the original Doom 64. Nightdive have done an extraordinary job with this port, and I definitely am excited to see what they do next.

_childDocuments_.review: Even though I still have my N64 and all my games, and even though Doom has always been one of my favorite FPS franchises, and even though the first 2 Dooms are what really ignited my lifelong love of video games, I never played this on N64. I only tracked down a copy on N64 about 5 years ago, but never got around to playing it. Each time I've played it was on the PC port. The first time I played it through was only a few years ago. I'm now playing through it again on Steam. This is the last game that really felt like Doom in all the distinct, classic ways, except for the music, which is here a more ambient, atmospheric soundtrack than midi-metal soundtrack. This is an excellent game that is still endlessly fun to play a couple decades after it came out. Level design, the slight modifications of the enemies without losing their distinguishing features, the traps, the labyrinths, the constant sense of dread and claustrophobia and hellish, otherworldly danger, the classic weapons and the few new ones, everything here is very well done. The game deserves this new sweep of attention it is getting during Doom Eternal's release. I'll eventually get around to playing Doom Eternal, but Doom 64 is more than sufficiently scratching my Doom itch right now. Doom 3 was a good and interesting deviation from the Doom formula, Doom 2016 was obviously a highly laudable technical accomplishment, and was fun, but really lacked a lot of the elements that define Doom in my mind. I expect Doom Eternal to be more like that one, and someday I'll see if that's true. Doom 64 reminds us what Doom once was, and will probably never be again.

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say? The game still holds up after all these years. Can't speak for younger players\those newer to the franchise, but this old game still keeps you on your toes at max difficulty and is a great piece of nostalgia for Doom vets.3 good things:1. Choosing super creepy ambiance over the traditional MIDI metal was a nice touch (reminds me of Doom 3 if it were made in '97).2. Level design\layout is really good for the time period and feels appropriate for the combat scenario. The levels don't get boring\repetitive in my opinion.3. The Unmaker and the ability to upgrade it was a nice touch and like Doom (2016) makes secret hunting especially worthwhile.3 bad things (I really struggled here):1. I've always had mixed opinions about some of the secrets in the Doom games which you'd spend ages trying to figure out (I know it's optional). I'm all for a clever scavenger hunt, but when it involves being at the right place\time when you destroy a final barrel, it's super easy to miss\never figure out without a guide and I don't get much satisfaction out of it. More frustrating than anything.2. I think it's great that we got a proper PC port, but they kind of goofed some of the weapon keybinds IMO, such as the Super Shotgun & regular shotgun being tied to the same key. I definitely got used to it (since ammo conservation often doesn't necessitate using the SSG for every enemy so I can switch back and forth) but seems like a quick fix.3. It'd have been nice if they'd added a Mission Select setup similar to Doom 2016 where I can go revisit\replay old levels with my existing loadout from the latest point in the campaign, right from the main menu. It'd help in the case of missing a Demon Key for instance. You can "warp to level," but it's not the same IMO.All in all - solid Doom game that I'm glad to have finally played. Don't how I missed out on this in the old 64 days. 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This game saved my life.I am 27.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you

_childDocuments_.review: A phenomenal game! For those who don't know, Doom 64 is a direct sequel to Doom 2, due to size limitations on the original hardware, a few enemies were cut, namely the Revenant, Archvile, Chaingunners, and the Spider Mastermind.I actually enjoyed this game more than I did Doom 2 due to its stronger level design. The level design is much more complex and dynamic here, they were really pushing the boundaries of the idTech-1 engine. This game sees vast graphical improvements over its predecessors too, dynamic, colored lighting makes an appearance for the first time in the engine, which really sets the mood during these levels. Speaking of setting the mood, this game ditches the metal music of prior Doom titles in favor of incredible, unsettling ambient tracks made by Aubrey Hodges. This dark atmosphere they were going for practically oozes out of every pixel of this game and it's just amazing. The puzzles are a bit cryptic at times, I had to use a guide a few times or I would've never been able to figure out some of this games puzzles. Some of them are well designed and fun though. Back to the topic of enemies though, the enemies that were included were given a redesign, most notably, the Pinky (and by extension, Spectre) looks much more menacing, the Cacodemon was given an appearance somewhat similar to the Pain Elemental from Doom 2, and the Pain Elemental was given a complete redesign and looks nothing like it's Doom 2 counterpart. In fact now the stupid thing has two mouths to shoot lost souls from, so get acquainted with that chaingun fast. The Imp was redesigned to look more creepy, and now has a alternate version called the "Nightmare Imp," a purple, translucent Imp that shoots faster projectiles. The Arachnotron was redesigned to look creepier, and now shoots from dual plasma guns in volleys of 5. I like everything they did here EXCEPT THE PAIN ELEMENTAL more lost souls is always a bad thing lmao.They added one new weapon to Doomguy's arsenal, technically it doesn't have a name (unless you count Doomguy saying "What the !@#%* is this!" when he picks it up as a name), but due to the similarities to an earlier scrapped weapon concept, its been dubbed the "Unmaker" a demonic laser-style weapon using plasma ammo that tears demons asunder.... well not quite yet. The Unmaker is pretty lackluster when you first pick it up, being basically a glorified plasma gun. It needs upgrades in the form of 3 "Demon keys" that you can find in secret levels to reach its full potential. If you get the second and eventually third upgrades for this weapon, it's sheer damage output rivals, and sometimes outclasses even the BFG 9000. I never shot the BFG once in this game because the Unmaker is just that good at both single target elimination and crowd control. Oh, while we're on the topic of weaponry, the chainsaw now has two blades, awesome.Get this game. despite it being made by Midway, and the limitations they had to deal with, they understood the assignment here and delivered. this game is a worthy successor to Doom 2 in my eyes and I highly encourage you to try it.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOM 64

_childDocuments_.review: I played through this on the steam deck, the real play-through time was somewhere around 20-25h, so if you like Doom I, you will like Doom 64, it's heavier on puzzles, I played on the steam deck, and I had to rewire the run button because otherwise you can't do all the puzzles. The good:-A much more polished game, than Doom I and II-it's hard, but not as hard as Doom I-Has some replay value (4 difficulty levels)-you get to kill lots of demons and zombies-I had fun figuring out some of the puzzles-I got gyro working on the deck, and it makes aiming a lot better-the game is so dark that I had to play in complete darkness to avoid glare on the glass, which made for great atmosphere, but also made me look like a crazy person.The cons:-I didn't have fun with some other puzzles-the game is very intensive, which can be good, but it also means that I had to take long breaks between each level, makes the game last longer-Sometimes I really had to look up solutions of the puzzles-the last boss level sucksFinal Verdict:If you liked Doom I give this lost gem a chance, it's still a pretty good game even today, I mostly had a blast working through it two levels per day, one in the morning, and one after work in the evening, so some two weeks of quality entertainment (24 levels + final level)
_childDocuments_.name: DOOM 64

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of the best games I bought for literal pennies. It's a Nintendo 64's iteration of DOOM - however! - this time with a slightly different atmosphere built by somewhat uncanny soundtrack. You feel more alone and abandoned rather than badass like in classic DOOM. And it's one of a kind experience, definitely worth checking on your own. Either way, it's a great game. Not a long one, but no doubt it's worth the price (especially if it's THAT low), had fun for as long as I played.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOM 64

_childDocuments_.review: I never played doom64 when it was first released, and like many others I assumed it was just a slightly updated port of the original doom. I piked it up on sale for very cheap and thought I'd try it out. I was surprised to find it's actually a new doom game (I guess doom 3 in the original timeline) and up there with the best classic doom/retro FPS games in generally. Atmosphere is great, graphics are still good enough for those of us who still like old school FPS, and the level design early on at least is surprisingly good. In some ways the combination of horror atmosphere, run and gun old school game-play and levels which feel intricate but are designed to be surprisingly intuitive really remind me of Dusk. Can definitely recommend at under £5.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOM 64

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has played a lot of Doom 2, especially coming back over the years to play some hard wads - let's face it, Doom is still one of the best shooters out there - I can recommend the game.What to expect coming from Doom 2?Pros:- New maps, which most of are quite nice- New sound, music, sprites- A new and good hitscan weapon (let's be honest, it's overpowered)- No ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ machinegunners!- Sometimes weird but fun architecture movements on mapsCons:- Often, monsters just spawn out of nowhere (seems a bit lazy)- The pain elemental is even more of a ♥♥♥♥♥, given that lost souls now seem to fly faster and longerNeutral:- At some points, monsters need to be killed for progression (e.g. to make a door open)- No revenants- No archvile (a con in my book, but I'll let you be the judge)- Overall less hitscan enemies (which is nice) and projectiles seem to move slower
_childDocuments_.name: DOOM 64

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first of the classic DOOM games I've played now. I'm motivated to play the rest.While this game is a little slower than I'm used to with DOOM 2016 and DOOM ETERNAL, I do enjoy the creepy atmosphere and the challenge the game pushes. I do prefer the music from the other DOOM games though. In terms of horror vibes I think the Original Quake did this style better. However this doesn't mean I won't play this after one play through. I'm quite invested into this game. I'd encourage anyone to try this whether you've played a DOOM title before or not.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOM 64

_childDocuments_.review: Doom 64I only thought there was Doom I, II and IIII guess this game was originally released on the Commodore 64 or it must be made in (19)64... All kidding aside from the little I have played:-It runs great on modern PC's-Graphics are pretty decent (especially considering it' probably a game from 1964?)-It plays like Doom, it feels like Doom, it tastes like Doom and it smells like Doom...So this must be Doom!!!Play this game or be Doomed
_childDocuments_.name: DOOM 64

_childDocuments_.review: Good ol' FPS! There was a Doom 2 WAD in order to play this game from N64, but finally it came on Steam. It has 32 levels in addition with some secret levels and the so called "lost levels" (the ones that were cut from the original game). It is challenging at the hardest difficulty, but it is worth it. I had a lot of fun playing this game. I absolutely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOM 64

_childDocuments_.user: 2's a Party but 3 is a Crowd
_childDocuments_.review: The best classic doom game, great levels, great demons, all the little negatives have been fixed, plasma rifle though is sadly useless due to the powerful unmaker, one demon key outclasses it, this port also contains extra levels with a new story, sadly there the chaingunner, revenants, archvile, and spider mastermind don't return, the only new demon is good but its just a harder imp varient, visuals are amazing besides the zombieman and shotgunner looking way too similiar, fantastic game, 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: DOOM 64

_childDocuments_.review: Is DOOM 64 good? Short answer: Yes! long answer: DOOM 64 is DOOM 3 before DOOM 3 ever was DOOM 3 on paper. I never played this one until it came on pc, and I am so glad I did because I am a fan of the horror atmosphere. I also do like how this actually feels like DOOM and plays like DOOM, it is what DOOM 3 should have played like in my opinion, so no complaints from me here as a DOOM megafan. You are still a badass in DOOM 64, here to send hell back to where it came from. You are a spacemarine, the best of the best, who has survived hell not one, but two times counting the events of DOOM 1 and 2. DOOM 64 is a sequel to the events after DOOM 2, where the mother of all demons has started to resurrect the hellspawn you have killed, so it is connected to the original DOOM storyline. A solid DOOM experience I can easily recommend, I give it a 9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOM 64

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't as hard as DOOM II (playing on "I own DOOM skill), but a good visual experience with the old engine. Plays just like it should. Secrets are hard to find, but the end game tally doesn't say found 0 of 3 as an example. Just 0, so you have no idea if there were any at all.The map is fixed in size near as I can tell, making an overall view difficult. The original DOOM games also showed things interactive on the map. I haven't seen that so far in DOOM 64. If you played DOOM/DOOM2 this is a shoe-in for fun. I'd suggest a level higher than in D/D2 as this game seems easier to stay alive.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOM 64

_childDocuments_.review: Doom 64 is amazing. I only recently found out it was a standalone Doom game and not just a Nintendo 64 port of the original. The game has a different look and feel to Doom and Doom 2, even though it is firmly a member of that family. You can tell there was some inspiration from Quake in the mix, with the game being slightly slower and having a more tense atmosphere than Doom and Doom 2. It is also evident where the limits of the Nintendo 64 impacted the game in terms of how much they could cram in. Even so, the game is great and they took advantage of the strengths of the Nintendo 64 to provide a very unique experience which still holds up in 2022/2023. The game has quite a unique look which I must say did not convince me as far as screen shots are concerned but looks beautiful in motion. Even the new look monsters, while everyone will have his own subjective preference, really grow on you. Audio wise it is a vast improvement.If you are a fan of Doom and Doom 2, then this is unmissable. If you are a fan of DOS shooters in general, then this is also a very strong recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOM 64

_childDocuments_.review: As a veteran of the original DooM and DooM ][, I can say that this game is now right up there with those two classics in my mind. Some really inventive levels and new twists, plus atmosphere. In many ways, reminds me of how I enjoyed the special hidden levels in the Sega Saturn version of Quake - true to the original without seeming tired.I do think the ending could use a bit more messaging to let the player know what they need to be doing before they get there. That's my only quibble.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOM 64

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent new Doom game rather than a port of Doom to the N64. There's a host of brand new levels(40 with the new Lost Levels in this rerelease), new graphics and lighting, new scripting and level design(loads of shifting geometry), remade sprites with higher resolution. Doom 64 does do things a bit differently at times. The classic chiptunes are replaced by spooky ambiance, though it's pretty good spooky ambiance and there is an even bigger emphasis on puzzle solving your way through the levels, which can break up the action for a touch too long if you get stuck. Probably my only complaint is that some solutions to advance require strictly made jumps that are a slog to retry repeatedly, but this is certainly the best version just for the options to quicksave/load for those. The slightly smaller roster also puts this game slightly beneath Doom 2 for me but that's a personal call, like arguing about whether a game is an 8.5 or a 9. More than worth the five bucks.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOM 64

_childDocuments_.review: Very well done port, the cons is that probably this plays better from a controller but I am so much used to keyb+mouse that can't play it differently. Love how they have included the new Lost Levels chapter, very well done. If Nightdive will add freelook and autoaim on/off they'll surely attire way more players, but for me it is okay as it is now. Maybe a little fix about collision over walls and moving platforms would be appreciated too.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOM 64

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: It's DOOM 64 so the game itself is greatCons: The port is pretty bad, crashes every 10 minutes, a minute long unskippable boot sequence (which is really bad combined with the constant crashes) (EDIT: You can type -skipmovies in the launch options to skip the company and engine intros), and little things like no number value for the FOV slider. Really i'd have no issue giving this a thumbs up if the crashes were fixed.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOM 64

_childDocuments_.review: Great game and a classic. I prefer this doom since I played Doom on the PS2 port, so I am used to the creepy atmosphere and amazing sounds/soundtrack that Aubrey Hodges made for the ports.Expect tricks, traps and some demon killing fun! Collect keys to progress further into maps, find secret weapons and health packs. Sometimes you'll even find a secret but then get hit with a trap and before you know it, that super shotgun you collected as a secret is out of ammo since the game decides to reward you with a Imp trap.For me, the soundtrack and sounds really make the game feel perfect. Perhaps its the nostalgia I get, but it just makes it so much more satisfying when you're blasting demons out the way to get to the exit. However, if you're used to the PC Doom, then don't expect to see the Chaingunners or certain other demons that were in the original. Remember, this was a port and not that much memory was in those system back then. But don't worry, the game makes use of the Pain Elementals & Lost Souls to make up for some of the changes. Enjoy!
_childDocuments_.name: DOOM 64

_childDocuments_.review: This is my favourite shooter ever. It's one of those games where the first time you play it it feels pretty good, but of the era, but the second time however, it feels amazing. You're familiar with it now and the levels feel buttery smooth. The sprite work, colours, difficulty, secrets, extras and new content, they just feel perfect. This is one of the most atmospheric games I've ever seen. Ever since falling in love with it I've purchased it on every platform available, you could say I'm obsessed. Nightdive did a phenomenal job.I Recommend playing this game with your own tunes and go crazy, because even though the soundtrack is good, the game isn't really a horror game.Literally my number one game recommendation other that Nightdive's release of quake, but this game is even cheaper.10/10 I understand the criticisms, but the game has a quick save, come on now.

_childDocuments_.name: DOOM 64

_childDocuments_.review: It’s a shame that even back in the 90’s, DOOM 64 was already late to the party, because this is probably one of the best DOOM games ever released. I don’t know if it’s because I had really low expectations or if the revamped version from Bethesda did a great job, but going through the same old formula felt strangely refreshing with DOOM 64.A well-respected gaming website gave this game a score of 4.8 out of 10, which might had been a fair rating for the original Nintendo 64, but it doesn’t do justice to this refreshed version from Bethesda. DOOM 64 looks just like any old DOOM game, but with Quake’s gameplay. It immediately rang a bell when I got the super shotgun and started killing the hellish monstrosities like I used to do in Quake. It didn’t feel like the classic double-barrelled shotgun from DOOM II, but it was quite amusing nonetheless.One thing I wouldn’t miss from DOOM 64 are the “puzzles”, though. The eighth level in particular has a gotcha to obtain a certain yellow key that wasn’t fun at all to go through. Perhaps the devs tried to bring a bit more variety to the gameplay, but DOOM is fundamentally all about mowing down hordes of hellish spawns and that’s what the audience expects, anyway.Putting that unfortunate design choice aside, the action in DOOM 64 is appropriate and it is definitely worth to try out if you’ve played the original MS-DOS titles but didn’t have a Nintendo 64 to try this exclusive at the time. It is a strange time travel in the game’s saga, because while it is still a DOOM game, it plays quite differently from the first titles. I would say that it feels like an intermediate between DOOM II and DOOM 3, where the action feels like the former but there’s a grim aspect that somewhat resembles the latter. But don’t worry: you won’t need to decide whether to use a flashlight or a gun. :)
_childDocuments_.name: DOOM 64

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed the classics buy this game.If you already have the cartridge on the N64 buy this game.If you hopped in during the rise of the recent "boomer shooters" renaissance buy this game.If you played Doom 64 Retribution in the past you should have already bought this game.If not then...Doom 64 is an FPS originally developed by Midway Games that is incredibly dark and atmospheric thanks to the spritework and ambient soundtrack composed by Aubrey Hodges, which really helps delivering the experience.This re-release, handled by Nightdive Studios, it's a very faithful port (except very minor differences that first timers shouldn't care about as they don't compromise the experience in any way, shape or form).It shares the fake 3D nature and gameplay style of Doom I and II (so no free aim for you except via modding, for that I'd suggest using a source port, but that's beyond the scope of this review), has a more refined level design compared to the classics but tends to be on the easier side, and also contains a new set of levels that connect to Doom Eternal (do you really care about this?), and are a nice addition and challenge to have.What else to say?Do you like FPS games, especially old pre Half-Life ones? You'll most probably like this then, guaranteed.And just play on the hardest difficulty, or else it will be TOO easy, trust me.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOM 64

_childDocuments_.review: Listen up, maggots. DOOM 64 has arrived on PC, and let me tell you, it's a bloodbath. You wanna know what's awesome about this game? EVERYTHING. The weapons, the enemies, the levels – it's all pure carnage, and I love it.Now, let's talk about the weapons. You got your classic favorites like the shotgun and chaingun, but there are some new toys to play with too. The plasma rifle will melt your enemies' faces off, and the Unmaker is like a Swiss Army knife of demonic destruction. And don't even get me started on the BFG 9000. That thing is like a nuclear bomb in a gun, and it's my personal favorite.Speaking of enemies, DOOM 64 doesn't disappoint. You got your usual suspects – imps, demons, and whatnot – but there are some new faces too. The nightmare imps are a real pain in the ass, and the motherdemon will make you regret ever stepping foot in hell. But no matter how tough the enemies are, I've got a solution: just rip and tear until it's done.The levels in DOOM 64 are dark, moody, and just plain badass. There's a real sense of atmosphere that sets this game apart from the rest of the DOOM series. And let's not forget the music – it's like a heavy metal concert in hell, and I'm the headliner.Now, some of you might say that DOOM 64 is too hard, too brutal, too unforgiving. Well, let me tell you something, weaklings: that's the whole point. This game isn't for the faint of heart. It's for those of us who like to get our hands dirty – and covered in demon blood.In conclusion, DOOM 64 on PC is a must-play for anyone who loves fast-paced, gory action. It's like a symphony of violence, and I'm the conductor. So strap on your armor, grab your weapons, and get ready to show these demons who's boss. It's time to rip and tear, until it is done.

_childDocuments_.review: The strongest entry in the iDTech0 library, and the strangest by far.The level design is excellent, lighting superb, and it is a strong return to form for the original DOOM gameplay before exiting the iDTech0 engine.Mood is creepier and more ambient than prior DOOM entries, bridging the gap between classic DOOM and DOOM 3's horror/suspense focused gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOM 64

_childDocuments_.review: Doom 64 is the great "forgotten" Doom game that some, myself included,  would argue to be the true Doom 3 over the 2004 main series entry. Somehow retaining both the older Doom game's fast and frantic action and also combining it with Quake's far more morbid atmosphere resulting in arguably a far more unnerving experience than Doom 3's attempts at horror. While it is fantastic that the game is finally unshackled from the ancient N64 hardware this port does have elements that leaves a lot to be desired.Doom 64 is canonically the third Doom game, taking place after the events of Doom II where Doomguy, being the only experienced marine to survive both the initial Mars moon invasions as well as the aftermath on Earth, is sent to a remote UAC base that has once more began to spew forth demons into the universe. Amusingly with the newer Doom game's releases focusing on the Doom Slayer this lost chapter of the Doom saga is now canonically placed seeing the main character here continuing on to become the main character for the later games. Where this leaves Doom 3 is anyone's guess, but the story of Doom 64 joins the dots to show how Doomguy ended up in hell to fight the demons for all time.Story aside (who cares about Doom lore?) the game is tonally a far darker game than its prior outings, both visually and audibly with a stronger lighting system and a step away from Bobby Prince's old midi scores. Simply adding coloured lighting to Doom as well as a stronger contrast between bright spots and the shadowy expanses covering most of the levels changes the old goofy adventure against the camel sampled imps to squinting into the darkness to see if there is an odd sprite moving about. Further to this is the darker, more ambient score by Aubrey Hodges, pulling away the old heavy metal midi and revealing a darker, more industrial backing. More than anything the horror comes from this element and its constant creep in tone slowly becomes the primary unnerving element. Where I initially found it cheesy in the opening levels, by the later hell missions it was so heavily engulfing that during my first playthrough I had to stop on occasion just to take a break from how suffocating the atmosphere was.Further highlighting the atmosphere is the level design. Doom has always had fantastic levels and Doom 64 is no exception. While none of the original designers were working on it, a lot of the moments scream of pure, dickish intent like the finest moments of Romero's works. Sometimes it is a little bit much as on a couple of maps there are fast firing, homing missile traps at locations that is little fun to contend with, but as a whole its suitably fiendish without going too far. Atmosphere wise however it is an interesting prospect in comparison to similar titles of the time. While Doom has always leaned far harder on the abstract designs, more about the flow and feel of a game than if it had any practical purpose, Doom 64 feels like an odd blend of both the abstract and real, where tech bases have desk terminals and some things that could be perceived as industrial equipment it equally has moments where you would think "what is this supposed to be?" This was in a post Duke Nukem world where other contemporary tiles tended to have real world logic applied far more than the typical iD fare and so Doom 64 ran the risk of seeming dated. Despite this the majority of Doom 64 takes place in hell alowing for a far more abstract feel to work well and expand on the ideas already implemented in the older games of the series. In comparison Doom II's unholy cathedral can vaguely be seen as a cathedral of some form, but that would require a good degree of imagination to pull off. The hell levels in Doom 64 with the true 3d environments seem to have various forms of coherent themes that have areas that have a vague semblance to human society, but are all slightly off in ways to make them uncanny. A large temple may contain a library, a torture chamber or various armoires and bastions for defence, only to be located next to a maze of corridors that seem illogical or various pits filled with flesh and bone for inexplicable reasons. The structure being formed by an eldritch logic that is just beyond the grasp of your own thinking and confounding the player, further enhancing the already thick and moody atmosphere by the visuals and sound.Aside from the aesthetic values, Doom 64 plays like the previous entries in the series. Fast moving, high action and requiring little in terms of wit or intellect to get through. You are still a dude with a shotgun murdering thousands of demons over and over  level after level with little in the way of plot, which can easily be ignored if you wish, bogging things down. Despite all the superb "show dont tell" world building the game has, if you did not like the prior games this will be equally stupid. Conversely if you liked the first two entries, Doom 64 is easily an equal to those.CONTINUED IN COMMENTS: Port quality.

_childDocuments_.review: This was the one, that I played first somehow.At that time: I did not know there were others.Now I know this was technically the 3rd game.It came out originally in 1997 and it was great.Really fun to play through. Nostalgic mayhem.I'm so glad to finally see it available on Steam.Doom 64 is for sure my favorite classic Doom.And It's quite sad it took so long to be ported.We had to wait 22 years to get this on Steam.I guess N64 emulators do exist and It is good.But still, It's so nice to have an actual PC port.A proper widescreen support, high resolution.Story-wise it's a follow-up of Doom II, simple.But let's be honest, story didn't matter there.Classic Doom games are all about gameplay.It's the classic first person shooter with gore.Doom 64 offers a very dark and creepy vibe.Even the audio design is rather atmospheric.It's definitely impressive for that time period.Furthermore: This isn't just a port, It's bigger.Completely brand new levels are added here.They are called 'The Lost Levels' and It's gud.Like really gud, very enjoyable, I truly liked it. No. Is it better than The Ultimate Doom? _childDocuments_.name: DOOM 64

_childDocuments_.review: Doom 64 was that kind of the hidden gems that was part of the Nintendo 64 library,That was until a little while ago when someone finally came along and made a source port.Doom 64 is a great game.Doom 64 has everything that made Doom 1 & 2 great but with some Quake feel to it.This port is pretty much doom ex but a little bit more vanilla then doom ex.If that's not your thing you can use this game's .wad file to doom ex.This port also comes with a new episode witch is very nice.The new levels are fun to play and have fun and weird secret areas.Overall there is only three things I have issues with the first is at times the games a little laggy on proton.The second thing is the fact the only way to skip intro movies is by launch options and the final issue is how the key binding moves as your trying to set bindings.So yeah this port not bad.Over all I'll recommend this port because unlike Duke Nukem world tour this port doesn't take a good game and put it blender of bad ideas.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOM 64

_childDocuments_.review: It's the only Doom game besides the original that truly captures the spirit of Doom perfectly. Midway did a great job and you can tell it was done with nothing but respect to the source material. Everything important is here and everything new is fitting. It actually looks and feel like a proper Doom sequel. What I love about Doom 64 is it does what Doom 3 tried to do, but does a far better job of it. It managed to add more horror into the game without messing it all up. Doom 3 was very far removed from the original style of Doom and didn't at all feel like a Doom game, whereas Doom 64 feels like one of the best Doom games. It's definitely a masterpiece in its own right, and while some parts definitely annoy me, that would describe pretty much all Doom games. I mean, with over 30 levels, some part is bound to piss you off. Great experience and easily one of the best in the series. Don't skip out on this.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOM 64

_childDocuments_.review: REVIEW #73DOOM 64----------I love me a good, old-school DOOM game, and with time, DOOM 64 has become my favorite out of the handful of 90s-era releases from the series. The higher quality presentation of graphics and sound, the colored lighting, the new level scripting system, and the moody background ambiances are an incremental but definite step forward from the original two MS-DOS games. This new PC re-release of this D64, originally a Nintendo 64 exclusive, not only brings all of those improvements back with password-less saves, higher resolution and keyboard/mouse, but it also features an episode full of lost levels and password-less saves.Add the fact that DOOM 64 on its own is a really fun game on its own (despite a couple of levels that make the game feel a little stale and a new enemy art design that may not be as appealing as the original to some old-school DOOM players), and you've got an excellent title that any fan of the series (or any 90s-era FPS, for that matter) should consider. I love this one.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOM 64

_childDocuments_.review: Tedious shooter with a lot of backtracking between switches, simplistic level design, hideous monster design and non-existent soundtrack (compared to, say, System Shock 2 or Thief). I'm a fan of retroshooters in general, but there are simply better alternatives than this.The intro theme was cool, but that's pretty much it.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOM 64

_childDocuments_.review: Doom 64 was my introduction to the Doom franchise as a little kid. I would watch my dad play it on our N64, marveling at the graphics, the sound design, the weapons, and the eerie atmosphere. Playing with the N64 controller was unwieldy, so my dad never got very far into the game but my imagination would run wild with what the game had in store for players who managed to delve deeper into Hell.Fast forward 20 something years later and this remaster hits stores. I had played Doom64EX, which required an actual Doom64 ROM in order to work, and was a bit of a pain in the ass, but I was still enamored with the game. Coming back to it all these years later, and it still hits the same way it did when I was a kid. It feels so good to play; the weapons are punchy and have added effects that weren't in the original Dooms (such as the chaingun shaking the screen while you fire it), the levels are great with some challenging secrets to uncover, some of which utilize the new (for the time) scripting, enemies are beautifully designed, and the atmosphere is second to none in the Doom franchise. If you're a Doom vet, you might get a decent challenge out of it. Or you might find it a bit too easy. Either way, though, this is a must play. More Doom is always a good thing.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOM 64

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know what to say other than that this game rocks. It's easily the best doom when compared between the original 2 doom games in most ways. The sounds, the enemy models, and the music is all really improved here. granted I have played a whole lot so far, but I'm the game will still be good after a while.

_childDocuments_.review: A very solid implementation of the original Doom 64, that's all good, it's a solid entry in the series though you may find the audio and visuals more depressing than the rock-album-cover attitude of the original 1/2/Final. Remember, if all the moaning and crying babies really get to you, you can always mute the music and play anything else in the background instead. (Protip: You can do this for every game ever where you can disable the music.)What's actually ♥♥♥♥♥♥ is the bonus campaign that's supposed to be a bridge between 64 and the modern reboot, and that's because it's full of the same crap those modern entries rely on, where wave after wave of monsters teleport into the same lock-in room from out of nowhere, amazingly implemented in the original engine where entities could not be created on the fly, and every monster you will ever fight in a level is already standing somewhere in that level as soon as it starts. So, if you're buying it just to get the extra campaign and you strongly disliked that stuff about the modern Doom games (and a lot of modern games), you're gonna be disappointed with that specific part.Still, a lot of fun to be had here, and I recommend it, especially if you've played 1/2/Final but never this one.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOM 64

_childDocuments_.review: Very unique take on the classic DOOM formula, leaning heavily into the atmosphere and horror DOOM3 tried to capture. The Aubrey Hodges soundtrack adds so much to the mood of the game, and the colored lighting and mapwork are extremely well done, adding to the demonic setting the game conveys. Maps are mostly well done, though throughout the game and especially at the later half there are some frustrating puzzles and I had lots of points where I just didn't know what to do to continue a level. Art design is good as well, with enemy sprites looking less exaggerated and more fear-inducing. I absolutely think any DOOM fan should at least play this, as it has a very distinct style that none of the other games really capture, besides Quake 1 and 2. The Lost Levels are great as well, they serve as a good companion piece to DOOM Eternal if you plan to play that.

_childDocuments_.review: I will separate two thing in my review: the game, and the port.Is the game worth playing if you're a classic Doom fan?Depends. There's still running and gunning, but the game is moody, slower. There's no metal to make you feel pumped, just unnerving ambient. Monsters are in this late 90's brownish palette, looking creepier, but less distinct than in classic Doom. But once you get familiar with the game, it's very satisfying. The weapons have a great feel, even if they're crippled by very limited animation. Their sounds are eargasmic. (Well, all sounds in this game are good). The combat is challenging but very satisfying- for most of the game, especially closer to the end, I would often find myself in disbelief that I managed to survive some more intense parts. Things can get really crazy sometimes and it feels great. Plus, the game's story makes it a great coda for the classic Doom- many people call it a "real Doom 3" and I really get why.ATTENTION- if you suffer from migraine seizures or are sensetive to strobe lights- DO NOT PICK UP THE FIRST SOUL SPHERE IN MAP04. The strobe that turns on when you do is like the early 2010's "YOU DESERVE SEIZURES FOR YOUR POST" troll gifs. Since it's pretty early in the game, when classic Doom fans would still not get used to how different it is, I know more than one person who abandoned the game after that. Frankly, this is a really ♥♥♥♥♥♥ game design, making the game punish the player with hard enemies is cool, making the game punish the player (or around a dozen % suffering from said problems) with seizures or debiliating headache is just dumb. I wish they could give an option to disable it instead of seizure warning screen that adds few seconds to your loading time, each time you launch the game.And what about the port?I've never played the original, but I've played Doom Ex, which was flawless. This port is based on it. I personally hate filtering and resizing because it just looks blurry to me, thankfully you can disable it. I wish I could disable mouse in menus as well, it can get really frustrating to operate this weird scrolling. Other thing that is a minus for me, compared to Doom Ex, it misses some features but adds useless stuff like  login (it does absolutely nothing, I think you get some Doom Eternal cosmetics if you do it but otherwise it's just logging in, taking some time to do so every time, for no profit for player whatsoever). Still, since Doom Ex creator did get money for it, plus he made some maps (that I wasn't able to reach yet) I'm happy to pay those few dollars for his works, and for the work of the original Doom 64 creators. Plus, since WAD files have somewhat recognizable data, I hope this port will make the game modable, while preserving its original feel.So, tl;dr: buy this if you like Doom lore and shooting at stuff, don't buy it if you don't like late 90's gritty aesthetics and unnerving ambient, and whatever you do, don't pick up the soulsphere on the map 04.

_childDocuments_.review: Damn son.DOOM 64 was nothing like what I expected, it is a massive improvement over 1 & 2 in my opinion. The visuals and sound offer a much more sinister and spooky atmosphere, the difficulty is amped up even further and it's really addictive once you get into the rhythm! I can't stress enough how different the atmosphere is in this game than before. Enemy models look more detailed and gruesome, lighting and environments are claustrophobic and gloomy. But most importantly to me is the music, or lack thereof. DOOM 64 sounds straight up a like a great horror game. Eerie ambience and reverberating voices echo each space. Any fan of horror games I would recommend the soundtrack (if nothing else) as It sets the tone perfectly, I haven't heard anything like it on the N64! (I do for the record also enjoy the heavy metal devil horns rock that Doom is usually known for (and that sexy smooth samba elevator music in DOOM 2 wtf lol)Also, the challenge is punishing but fair in most cases. Except the Lost Soul (flying flame skull) is really irritating this time, little bugger will never leave you alone!8/10

_childDocuments_.review: About friggin time!If you're curious about the base game and have never played it before, this is the TRUE sequel to DOOM II. It picks up right where that one left off, and the game has redesigned enemies and whatnot. The atmosphere is by far the best in the entire series with a much more evil and sinister feeling throughout (I was terrified of this game as a kid, but never with the other original dooms), the levels are mixed more with a hybrid of medieval gothic and hellish theme, the music is more dark ambient than 80s metal, and the level design is more puzzle based than previous games but thankfully without being too frustrating. If you get stuck, you will usually be able to find your way after searching for a couple of minutes, it's not too bad honestly like you would expect. Along with the original Doom (yes over Doom II), I personally think that this is actually the best game in the series. As for THIS port itself; absolutely amazing stuff, just as expected from my bois at nightdive, the kings of boomer shooter remasters. This is nearly a flawless port, capturing all of the magic of the original while adding some new essential features. 60fps (as opposed to the 30 or so of the original), higher resolutions, smoother textures, controller support, an entirely new and exclusive episode, manual/quicksaves, as well as the original password system if you want to play the game how it was back in the day, and a plethora of others. I think the only things that I don't like about this port is that you have to be connected to the internet to play (I'm assuming, since it always connects when you start up the game), as well as the fact that you can't skip the company intro logos even if you've already seen it. It takes up 30 seconds of your time every single time you want to start up the game which is rather excessive imo. And lastly, I really wish there was the option to play coop or deathmatch in here with some deathmatch exclusive maps and steam workshop so others can make maps and keep the longevity of the game going. We'll see in the future.As it stands now, this is a DAMN good port, and one that is definitely worth MORE than the asking 5$ price. STOP SLACKING AND BUY IT!!!!

A bit different from how Romero did Doom - where he kinda put some of the better maps at the beginning and mixed them around. If you like Doom 1\2 and Quake 1 - you would probably like this game too.

_childDocuments_.review: I rate Doom 64 3.5/5. Pretty good.  This creepy game (with really creepy ambient “music”) is even better on PC than it was on the Nintendo 64.This is a very good port of the version of Doom which was released on the Nintendo 64 gaming console. While its environments are not nearly as big and the enemies are not nearly as numerous as those in the first Doom or in Doom 2, this is still a fairly nice and creepy retro game with pretty good level design. PC gamers interested in every Doom game which has come out should definitely play this through at least once. While it is a fairly short game (it took me only 8 hours to play through), at only 5 USD it is well worth the price and can often be gotten on sale for even less.+Great use of what were evidently extremely limited Nintendo 64 hardware resources. Good level/puzzle design. Still feels like a classic Doom game.+As in prior Doom games, there are several difficulty levels.+Fairly responsive controls which can be rebound to any keys.+The light levels seemed just fine on a modern 1080p computer monitor. Did not seem too bright or too dark to me, but stayed true to exactly how I remember it looking on the Nintendo 64 (except now the game has even better resolution).+Nice lighting effects.+I didn’t notice any bugs or errors. The game ran perfectly for me.+/-This game has some extremely, unbelievably creepy ambient “music” but it isn’t really fun to listen to like the first two Doom game’s soundtracks could be.+/-The sound effects work well, with every single sound having a particular meaning but the sounds are of fairly low quality and tend to sound a bit muddy.+/-Doom 64’s levels are usually smaller than those found in the first Doom and Doom 2 and usually have fewer enemies as well. There’s not as many different types of enemies as in Doom 2 either (except Doom 64 has a unique boss monster). This was all probably due to the severe technical limitations of the Nintendo 64 game console for which Doom 64 was designed. However, the levels are still well made.+/-Rather than focusing on being as action-oriented as Doom or Doom 2, this game focusses on being creepy and often succeeds (thanks in large part to the amazingly creepy ambient music). Doom 64 also has some rudimentary colored lighting effects which the first Doom games did not have (they hadn’t been invented yet when those games were first released). The result is an odd, creepy game with some interesting lighting which retains the classic Doom retro gameplay style.+/-The new weapon, the “Unmaker” seems almost too powerful even in its default, non-upgraded state. Once you get it, the plasma gun and the BFG 9000 (which you get almost immediately beforehand) become almost totally obsolete and so go mostly unused for most of the game since they all use the same type of ammo. There’s also almost never enough enemies around to justify the large ammo costs of firing the BFG 9000.-This is a fairly short game, taking about 8 hours if played through casually.-No alternate endings (other than dying). The game’s ending is also nonsensical. Your character chooses to remain in Hell?! WHAT. What is your character, some sort of militaristic reincarnation of Jesus with guns?!-The first two Doom games had a cooperative mode so you could play it with others (in addition to a player versus player mode) but Doom 64 apparently does not. The absence of this seems odd.-As in Doom 1 and Doom 2, this game has a few secret alternate levels to find and explore but I think actually doing so would be fairly tedious (I found one). I wish all the secret levels were also accessible from a menu after the game is beaten on any difficulty level but they’re not. Game developers shouldn’t hide their hard work.-Why are the minimum system requirements so high?! There is no way the now very, very old Nintendo 64 had the equivalent of 8 GB of RAM or a GTX 660 yet this port claims to require something equivalent to this. Doom 64’s graphics are actually a few steps below those of the PC version of Quake 2 (an even earlier game) and yet the system requirements for Doom 64 are greater. This game’s requirements should be far more flexible so as to work on a far greater variety of machines. It should be possible for the same, fairly low-end game to be set to different preset speeds so it can work with radically different processor clock speeds.

_childDocuments_.review: WOW, I'm actualy suprised by how good this is. In fact, I think this is my favorite game of the original trilogy. The graphics, the atmosphere, the music (or lack there of), it's all executed so well. I'm shocked that this game is hardly mentioned unless you search for it specifically because it really has so much more to it than one might think. Just to make this clear: This is NOT a simple port. It's a fully new DOOM game that was exclucively available on the N64, however, it's releas date coupeled with it's confusing title made many people think that this was just a port and thus OLD. And in the 90's, that was basicaly a deat sentence. And that's such a huge shame. _childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: At the time of writing all of my experiences are based off Doom 64EXIn regards to this exact port I can't say anything as of yet  however, it is largely based upon 64EX which I’ve never had any issues with whatsoever.Easily one of the best FPS ever made, and is what many (myself included) to be the “true” Doom 3. Unlike its predecessors 64 dumps the sci-fi theme, replacing it with a much darker, and high contrast color scheme, when combined with the new enemy sprites, larger usage of satanic imagery, the , and even the new technological advancements(advanced scripting, fog effects, new lighting effects, among others) in the engine put 64 more within the realm of horror than anything else. However, unlike Doom 3 this game still retains all of the action of the originals, instead of being a janky  tech demo. Overall the level design is quite good, even if it can get a bit repetitive at times such as in Unholy Temple, Dark Entries, or Blood Keep. This time around there are more puzzles which are mostly based around switch combinations, and moving objects/platforms that utilize the new scripting in the engine,  as opposed to keycard/switch hunting like in Doom 1&2, or Hexen. Despite the new scripting, and horror based theme there are less environmental hazards than in 1&2, now only being used when it serves purpose rather than just doing it for the sake of it like in Doom 2’s infamous level “The Chasm”. Not much else to say in that regard other than the game looks great, and has some of the best official doom levels ever; Dark Citadel, Even Simpler.All of the weapons from Doom2 return with all new sprites, as well as some tweaks which are most prominently seen on the BFG, Chainsaw, and Chaingun. Unlike the original, this BFG seems to rely on a cone shaped area  based upon the player’s vision rather than tracers, which doesn't result in it being bad, but the damage output does feel  if you’re used to the Doom 1/2 counterpart. On the flipside the story for the Chainsaw & Chaingun are basically the same: they’re high on speed and feel incredible, best in the entire franchise. Similarly to Doom 2, 64 introduces one new weapon: The Unmaker. Being found in only a small handful of levels, its a relatively decent alternative to the Plasma Rifle, but is largely unimpressive. Unique to the weapon though is the ability to upgrade it with a collectible known as demon keys (found within 3 of the game’s 4 secret levels). Once fully upgraded the Unmaker becomes even more overpowered than the original BFG, allowing you to decimate hordes of enemies, and even the final boss within seconds. Unfortunately enemies are Doom 64’s weak point. Due to the limited cartridge space: missing are the Chaingunners, Revenants, Archviles, and Spider Mastermind, and on top of that the Shotgunners and Zombiemen now share a singular sprite. In replacement we get the Mother Demon (final boss), and the Nightmare Imp; essentially a Spectre variant of the Imp that has a faster projectile. Despite the missing enemies Doom 64 does an excellent job of keeping things interesting with it’s limited roster, and the effects of missing enemies aren't really felt until the last stretch of the game. Even with its shortcomings related to cartridge space its much more than simply a port of Doom with the 64 slapped on top. Hell I'd even argue that it's a better experience than  both Doom 1&2, and most certainly better than Plutonia, and  Evilution.All in all, 64 has stood the test of time, and it’s status of being a cult classic is well deserved.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOM 64

_childDocuments_.review: Whenever I talk about Doom 64, people always say, "Oh, that was a port of Doom to the Nintendo 64, right?"Nope. It isn't. This is an entirely new game, and one you should really check out if you're a fan of oldschool Doom.Some fans call this the "Real Doom 3", and for good reason. While it plays like Doom, and while it has (mostly) all the same enemies and weapons you'd find in your usual Doom games -- Imps, barons, cyberdemons, you know, the whole crew -- the tone of the game has taken a heavy Gothic horror slant to it. Everything's darker and moodier. Monster sprites are more realistic and grotesque. Sound effects are all new; some, like the Star-Trek-sounding doors and the "whoosh" sound of a monster's thrown projectile, are seriously unforgettable. Music is all ambient and horror-esque (one track famously features a sample of a baby crying). There's a new weapon that hasn't made it into any other Doom game, and a pretty awesome sidequest related to it -- if you find three secret levels and find the secret items hidden within them, the gun becomes so powerful that you basically get to skip the final boss fight altogether.Level design is a bit different here. Unlike classic Doom, Doom 64's map scripts can spawn monsters wherever they want at any time. This makes monster ambushes much more frightening, as you would walk into the middle of a room only to have monsters appear all around you, or turn a corner to suddenly find that monsters have repopulated a room you thought you'd already cleared out. Some maps use this to create battle-arena rooms with multiple waves of enemies. Maps can also trigger stuff when certain enemies are killed, so you might be locked in those battle-arena rooms until everything's dead. The scripts make it seem as though the floors and walls themselves are possessed by demons who just want to toy with you at every turn.Monster properties have all been reworked, too. Mancubus fireballs now travel annoyingly slow, making them oddly more dangerous. Arachnatrons fire a double-stream of plasma which moves surprisingly fast and can snipe you from across the level. Lost Souls are far more aggressive. Pain Elementals shoot two Lost Souls at once, making them one of the biggest threats in the game. And the Cyberdemon not only shoots some seriously fast-moving missiles, but he fires them at a downward slant so you have to dodge the splash damage when they hit the floor. Personally, I loved all of the monster changes; it's been a long time since Doom monsters have made me feel afraid and uncomfortable to fight them up close!My criticisms of this port are:* Every time you boot up the game, you have to sit through about 8 logo / credits screens before you even get to the title screen. This takes almost a full minute. I wish I were joking.* The game's sprites look like blurry garbage unless you go into the graphics settings and turn off "filtering" which is on by default for some unfathomable reason. * There are more than a few "where the hell do I go now??" levels. * Three or four of the levels will probably drop you into an inescapable acid pit with no reason or warning. Even for oldschool standards, that's a pretty low blow.* If you want to see the fully-powered lasergun, you'll absolutely need a FAQ to find the second demon key level. While I mostly was impressed with the cleverness of the hidden secrets, this one's just unforgivably obtuse. Ditto if you want to find the level "Hectic" (which also unlocks cheat codes and five bonus levels when beaten)Doom 64 is a tragically overlooked cult classic in every sense of the word, not having gotten an official re-release until now. While it's true that a few fan-made mods have already brought the game to PC with varying levels of quality, Doom 64 as a commercial product is finally free of its decades-long shackles to the N64 cartridge, and maybe it'll finally get the widespread appreciation it deserves alongside the rest of the classic Doom campaigns like TNT and Plutonia. Plus, alongside the release of Doom Eternal, they've even added a short new campaign with a half-dozen maps that supposedly tie the story in with Doom 2016 in some way. (Most of the new maps are combat-heavy and feel like scrapped deathmatch maps, which isn't a bad thing.)Oh yeah, and it's on Nintendo Switch too, if you're into that!8 / 10! (Achievement hunters: 100% requires you to beat nearly all of the game on the hardest difficulty. Heavily depending on how skilled you are at classic Doom, how much you like to save-scum, and how much you'd want to check a FAQ, this could take you 12-20 hours.)

_childDocuments_.review: To many people back in the day, DOOM 64 might have sounded like nothing but a Nintendo 64 port of DOOM, judging by the title. They were wrong, since this is a completely new game! Initially, it was going to be called "DOOM: The Absolution" according to reports, but the stupid naming convention Nintendo imposed wouldn't allow it. Without taking any merit whatsoever from the masterpiece that is DOOM 3, this feels much closer to a third installment of the series, since it's more technically advanced than the previous DOOM titles and expands on them, as a true sequel would.This DOOM title differs quite a bit from the previous games, due to cartridge limitations. It plays out similarly to DOOM II, but a few demons were cut, like the Arch-vile or the Revenant, weapons were reworked, controls were altered to fit the monstrous N64 controller and less demons will overwhelm the player simultaneously. Nightmare difficulty was planned, but "Watch me Die!" ended up being the hardest one here, being similar to Ultra-Violence instead. We now play it with keyboard and mouse which makes it a walk in the park, since it was balanced towards N64 controller players, where movements and aim couldn't be as precise. It can still challenge the player of course, but for experienced DOOM players however, this will be a breeze. Maybe as hard as DOOM, but significantly easier than DOOM II.The heart pumping Metal covers with MIDI tracks were replaced by atmospheric and eerie soundscapes, and everything is darker this time around, both in tone and literal lighting. The vibe leans more towards Quake than DOOM. It's funny how the edgiest and creepiest DOOM came out on a Nintendo console of all places! Maybe this direction was influenced by console limitations, who knows? Regardless, it's highly appreciated.This is an enhanced version made by Nightdive Studios, with many tweaks to make the game playable on PC. There's a new map pack, "The Lost Levels", whose sole purpose is to link old school DOOM events all the way to DOOM 64 directly to DOOM (2016) and DOOM Eternal lore! This makes DOOM 64 a solid entry in the series' lore, rather than a separate universe like DOOM 3, which is a whole other can of worms. There's also achievements, where this guide will come in handy:

_childDocuments_.review: When it comes to 90's Doom, it doesn't get better than this in my eyes.Doom 64's levels are perfect, with progression that feels intuitive, switches and key items being easily discernible able from a distance, secrets that keep you well stocked on ammo that aren't too cryptic, wide open spaces to fight harder enemies. Basically it's what I love about Doom 2 with level design that feels more like Doom 1 and even a little bit of Doom 3's atmosphere. It's got everythingVery glad this gem was released on steam and other platforms cuz playing this on og hardware with an N64 controller and 12 character passwords sounds like a nightmare.

_childDocuments_.review: If, like me, you still enjoy the old Doom games (or the remastered versions at least), then this is a very good continuation of that formula.The new modernised controls are excellent. Just like 'DOOM Classic Complete' on PS3, this game lets you use the left stick for movement and strafing and the right stick for turning. Both are fully analogue inputs so you can adjust your movement speed, strafing speed and turning speed in real-time (I don't know how much of this was included in the original). You can also use the left trigger to interact so you don't have to move your thumbs off the sticks.The updated graphics look really good on my 1920x1080 monitor, while still retaining the retro style of the original. It's not 'true HD' but it looks like it's been upscaled to some degree.Nightdive Studios always do fantastic work when updating '90s games, and this is another example of that.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOM 64

_childDocuments_.review: Doom 64 on the N64 was a game that I couldn't really get into. The galaga shaped controller really made it difficult to enjoy even simple movement puzzles, and the visuals on the system, though for the time definitely nice, didn't sit well with me. I passed Doom 64 to the side for a long time, opting to play Doom 1 and 2 through mods and what not instead.Now that Doom 64 has been properly, OFFICIALLY, ported to the PC, and I finally put in the effort to play this game and beat it, I can easily say that Doom 64 is now one of my favorite Doom games. This, this game right here, is the true Doom 3, which is funny considering that it was originally made by Midway but whatever.Using the right settings, Doom 64 can look quite crisp (though it does make enemies look a little weird up close). The guns are meaty and pack a punch; you can feel the kick of the super shotgun. The music, though I would have preferred it to be the over the top head banging metal Doom is known for, is a welcome addition to the game and lends Doom 64 a different feel than Doom 1 and 2.Also, I cannot wait for mods to appear so that all the missing monsters may return; like a mod that differentiates the Zombiemen from the Shotgunners would be fantastic, because base Doom 64 does not show the difference (due to the hardware limitations of the N64 of course).If you like Doom, get Doom 64 (you probably already do since you pre-ordered Doom Eternal ;D ). If you like old-school FPS games, get Doom 64. If you own Doom 64 and have not played Doom 64 because you're too busy playing Doom Eternal...

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say about Doom 64? It was the first FPS I played as a kid. The dark atmosphere and the ambient soundtrack in combination with the sound effects really sell you on the feeling of being alone and distraught. Some may miss the Revenants and Archviles, but they make up for it with a much more threatening Pain Elemental and more aggressive Lost Souls. This game was a perfect way to wrap up the Classic Doom series and now it bridges to the new Doom games. The game is simple, fun and doesn't get in your way while you're playing. _childDocuments_.review: A classic game from the elder Doom era, Doom 64 was about defining the atmosphere in a new way back then. Many years ago, on the Nintendo 64 a version of the Doom franchise had been released, which was quite different in terms of graphics, music and ambience. The music on the PC used to be action like, but for D64 it had been changed to a moody, dense and creepy set of noises and disturbing pieces of music. Also all sounds had been newly made and the biggest change had been the graphical appearance. Music and sfx was very similar to the PSX version of Doom, yet the PSX still featured the old fashioned graphics.D64 changed it completely.The result was a more atmospherical and significantly darker Doom experience, in which the invasion of the hellish minions appeared much more spooky than in the original games. The levels supported the new style and featured as well technos bases, as hellish places. Levels like "Altar of Pain", "Into the Void" or "Downfall" really gave me the chills especially because of the disturbing soundtrack.This port is running nice and smooth, I did not encounter any problems.
_childDocuments_.name: DOOM 64

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this. It's faithful to the classic Doom formula, but the enhanced graphics and lighting augment the experience and are a nice touch. _childDocuments_.review: Glorious port of one of the best Doom entries ever, even the dev of Doom 64 EX worked on this version.Right now this is the best way to play Doom 64 on PC.It is really well made, even tho it asks you for a  account, but if its linked to your Steam, that is okay, you don't need to worry about it.The game is a bit brighter than its N64 version but that is not a problem at all.Expect the game to be harder than Doom and Doom II, not as evil as Final Doom but it does have some nice traps and tricks to keep you on your toes.Wish they added a multiplayer component to this just for fun, but it's okay, this game originally didn't had any, so they stuck true to the source material.I highly recommend this game if you are a fan of boomer shooters and/or a fan of Doom in general
_childDocuments_.name: DOOM 64

_childDocuments_.review: It's doom, but not, but is? This is a very interesting entry to the series. To start off, the port is fantastic. Modern resolution support, the sprites and lighting look great, and the levels themselves look awesome. The main campaign is pretty cool, the bonus campaign is alright, and the "fun" levels are a good challenge but not utter ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ - they get to the point and aren't a forever slog. The game is missing some enemies from doom and doom 2, but does add a new weapon. There are also all new weapon sprites and sounds, and the enemies are more or less the same but with new sprites and sounds. Its a nice fresh look and feel. The engine is an upgrade over the original, as it now supports multi-level areas which provides for some interesting level design. This game kind of acts like a bridge from the doom games to quake. The shotgun seems just like the quake one, and the feel of the soundtrack is way more grimdark and eerie than the midi metal of the original doom games. With the advancements to the engine, the architecture and level design feels a lot more like quake too. Its cool to look at the redesigned imps and see exactly where the design for the doom 3 and doom models were conceived. If I had to gripe, I would say that the new satan laser or whatever it is, is kind of lame. It uses energy cells so you have to decide between using that, the plasma gun and the BFG. It makes the plasma gun obsolete (which is fine because the new plasma gun is not nearly as cool as the old one) but kind of defeats the purpose of a new weapon. Aside from the plasma gun, some of the other changes to weapon sprites and sounds kind of sucked too. To me, the biggest let down was the change to the supershotgun; it doesn't sound nearly as cool, and there's no reload animation. Major bummer. The pistol and the minigun seem meatier and more badass, but the rocket launcher and BFG seem ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ than the old games. The new mancubus and arachnotron sprites and sounds are a downgrade from the original as well.There were a few occasions throughout the levels with some "puzzles" that were tedious. When I fire up doom I want to rip and tear, not play a shell game with a megasphere.As a final observation, the lost souls are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ psycho meth heads in this game. They attack super fast compared to the original doom games. The only saving grace is that they have much fewer hitpoints. I woulnd't say its a downside, in fact it makes an enemy that used to be kind of boring into a threat.

_childDocuments_.review: This a long lost game that I never played before that falls under the Classic DOOM Series. It is without question the best DOOM Console game that I ever played next to PlayStation DOOM. In 1997, the Nintendo 64 released a console exclusive DOOM game was not a port of the original DOOM from the late Midway Games & although my parents got me a Sony PlayStation instead, I missed out on this game. But there has been source ports of DOOM 64 following but not an HD Remastered Version. However, Bethesda has finally decided to Re-Release DOOM 64 for the PC/PS4/Switch, so now the Classic DOOM Series is Complete. A DOOM game that's gone back to basics, a swan song to celebrate everything that came before and after it.Both DOOM 64 Remastered is a love letters to the Classic DOOM Series & has been remastered as one last encore before moving on to DOOM Reboot Series after DOOM 3's Remastered Version. _childDocuments_.review: Honestly I think this is the best classic Doom, but why? Well, here are my reasons.The story seems more developed than in the previous Doom games, since the ending makes you feel proud of finishing the game by killing the mother of all demons.Gameplay is the same as other classic Doom games: grab weapon, start shooting demons. Of course there are keys to help you progress through the levels just like in previous Dooms. Sadly you can't jump, so you have to run to jump through gaps.This is the first Doom that used real 3D, although enemies and objects still being sprites, but makes the game look much cleaner than the previous games. Some stages are really well designed and give that "abandoned space base" or "hell" vibes.Soundtrack is a mix for me: I love how it gives horror vibes, but I hate that metal music was removed because it's an important component of Doom games. Still, it sounds excellent to hear music that gives nightmares.This is surprisingly the only classic Doom (3's BFG edition doesn't count) that has archievements. They are easy to get if you introduce the levels' code, but it loses the fun. If you do the archievements manually, I recommend you patience and a guide, since you will die a lot here.And for last, what about the price? It's a really good deal, since it costs 5€ and in sales it costs less than 1,5€. In conclusion, if you want to play classic Doom, this is a must-buy, and if you like the game, there are archievements to, when you finished the game, show everybody.
