_childDocuments_.review: I had previously reviewed this game closer to launch, but in retrospect I decided that old review was incomplete and outdated, and so I have deleted it and decided to start over the review from scratch.The first thing you should know about this game is what it is, and to get into that I'm going to have to address something very specific about it. Contrary to what the user tags say on the store page, this is not a Metroidvania. There is not one large interconnected map in which you collect new powers to unlock progress through, or even that on a smaller scale across multiple maps. If that's the kind of experience you are looking for, it's not here.So what is this exactly? It's much more akin to a combination between the Mega Man Zero series and Monster Hunter, entirely in 2D. There's a main town area in which you equip yourself with items and gear, and then when you are ready you enter into the bar which allows you to choose whether to play solo or online co-op. You choose a mission, each of which taking place in one of several different maps, and you attempt to complete the objective within a time limit. There's an RPG style level up system through which you gain EXP at the end of every mission and then if you gain enough EXP you will level up and choose what stat to allocate a skill point into.There's no true character creation feature. There's four preset starter classes and two unlockable classes. You can customize name, voice, and colors somewhat, and equipped weapons have their own unique sprites, but that's about it. Otherwise, characters of the same class will always look the same. Bandit, one of the two unlockable classes, is unlocked by completing a certain set of missions. The other, Oracle, is unlocked by reaching the ending of the game as any of the four starter characters. Each class has their own movesets, and uses DP, or Dragon Points, a bit differently. DP is typically built up by attacking enemies, and is a resource used for class specific dragon powers.Occasionally you'll be rewarded with Dragonite, which can be used to change your DP power element. This will change the color and function of your draconic body parts. This can come with changes to DP costs as well, so choose wisely. If you end up with a change to your dragon powers you do not like, you will have to earn another Dragonite to change it again.Sometimes when fighting a boss a special glowing orb will appear and begin floating over the boss arena. If you attack it enough it will heal you and grant you a time limited infinite DP bar, which allows you to use your special class specific dragon powers without having to worry about running out of DP points. This is your opportunity to deal some big damage, but don't forget that you are not invincible and can still be killed if you're not careful.The game is primarily built around co-op and is heavily mission focused. Offline solo play is doable and can still be a lot of fun, but if you want to get the most enjoyment out of this game it's recommended that you play with friends. Unlike in recent Monster Hunter games such as World and Rise, you cannot simply visit the individual locations casually and kill things at your own pace. You must be on a mission to visit any of the main gameplay locations.Every time you beat a mission, you unlock a harder version of that mission. For example, beating a level 10 mission might unlock a level 25 version of the mission. It's generally recommended that you use a character and gear suited to the level of the mission. As the difficulty increases, the time limit also decreases. There's different types of missions as well, such as "Defeat all enemies", "Defeat the boss", "Obtain a specific item", and even some special specific ones for certain missions. With some mission types the mission will clear as soon as you complete the objective. With others, you will be given an option to end the mission when you are ready via a glowing purple area you can interact with.Some gear can be simply purchased with money you collected in the stages, but this gear is generally pretty garbage and should be replaced ASAP if you want to maximize your efficiency and surviveability. Instead, you should focus on collecting necessary ingredients to craft and upgrade specific gear pieces. You can get certain ingredients from completing certain missions, and you'll also get upgrade materials from completing missions as well.Don't forget to stock up on healing items and status curing items as well. You're especially going to want to make sure you have something to take care of poison with you, as this can easily be the most dangerous status element. While poisoned, you will gradually take small chunks of damage over time. However, poison can take much longer to wear off than other status ailments, and could very easily shave almost the entirety of your health bar if left unchecked.When defeating enemies, sometimes they will drop healing items, status restore items, and even stat boosting items. You will consume any of these instantly when picking them up, gaining their effects. Beware however, not all items are good to pick up. For instance, purple mushrooms will poison you. Do not just mindlessly grab everything that drops, think about whether it's useful first.If your HP does reach 0, all hope is not lost. You have multiple tries per mission, and can revive with full health when reaching 0 so long as you haven't run out of retries. You do not lose progress from using a retry, you simply get back up on the spot and continue where you left off. However, you will fail should you run out of retries.As for the music and visuals, it's all rather high quality. The OST seems to all be full orchestrations and the visuals are high quality pixel art. You can also zoom the camera in and out unlike most other pixel art games, and the animations are all quite smooth as well. Overall high praise from me here.With all that out of the way, I do have a few nitpicks regarding this game. For instance, I would have liked to see a greater degree of character customization in the game. I'm fine with canon default presets, but in a class based game like this it's nice being able to make your character look the way you want them to and so it would have been nice to be able to choose gender and recolor the characters more extensively. It's not a deal breaker by any means and it's not even really all that big of a deal, but that's why I'm including it as a nitpick.Additionally, I would have also liked to see the individual mission areas exploreable without having to be on a mission. There's a feature like this in recent Monster Hunter games, and this would have been a fun alternative for collecting items you need for crafting at the black market, or even just for grinding experience for when you don't feel like taking on missions. Again, not really all that big of a deal but it's a bit of shame it's not here.Overall, if you're a fan of Inti's other games such as Mega Man Zero and Azure Striker Gunvolt and also into games like Monster Hunter, this is a really fun and content rich mix between these concepts and is a lot of fun to play with friends. Just don't get your hopes up if you're a huge fan of Metroidvanias because that is not the kind of experience you're getting into here. Go into this expecting Mega Man Zero as a Monster Hunter-like and you'll be getting a lot more bang for your buck.

_childDocuments_.review: I got given it by Tem so she'd have someone to play with, and then she played it solo anyway. What a goon. >:oAnyway the game is good I think. It looks good, it runs well enough (Unless you're online with someone with a weaker connection) and the basic loop of twonking monsters and grabbing treasure chests in hope of getting better gear is a classic. There is a story but honestly it's very weak, like most other games of this style. The soundtrack is decent, though for gods know what reason  so you have to right click the speaker on windows tray to access sound mixer if you want to hear voicechat or anything else while playing.One point that definitely deserves praise is how different the characters and their builds can be. There's always an optimised route but generally most of them can go for at least two different playstyles, like having the Empress focus on doing normal melee damage or using her dragon cannon attack. One thing to note is that two classes, Witch and Oracle, are quite in-depth to learn as they require you to do specific inputs in a tight time limit while in the middle of combat.The game's difficulty might put people off though, know ahead of time that it is a hard game that expects you to grind for better gear and spend level up points efficiently. There's almost no benefit to playing single player either; everything will focus on you and if you're a DPS build, will generally kill you in 1-5 hits. Multiplayer allows for other people to take focus, heal each other AND receive higher exp for beating missions. The literal only "downside" is enemies have increased health. That's all. I would heavily recommend having a pal to help you or asking in the forums or something. It's fun as a game to dip into for a few hours at a time, but remember that if you want to make real progress, unlock all the achievements or unlock the two extra characters, you'll have to put in dozens of hours. Finding guides and such is still a pain at the moment, a bunch of information is hidden on a discord and people are still learning about the Oracle and Bandit so there's very little on them too.One last important thing you should know; this game is designed for controllers. It IS playable with keyboard (I have to because my pad died ; ;) but you have to manually bind all your keys at the main menu, and it's going to be pretty difficult to adjust. Myself I go for a WASD movement, IJKL face buttons setup with LB (Dash) on space and Start on tab. QE UO for other shoulder buttons or whatever, Numpad 2468 for right stick camera control. You can probably make it more efficient for yourself but that's what I go with as a suggestion. :x

_childDocuments_.review: My single sentence description of this game is "If Mega Man: Zero and Monster Hunter had a baby."And it is a beautiful baby.Made by the creators of Mega Man: Zero, and has a very similar playstyle and art which will bring nostalgic joy from those of you who loved MM:Zero (myself included.)In a Monster Hunter like fashion, you choose a mission from the "Mission Board" and attempt said mission, usually having a challenging boss at the end. You get loot from chests and monster drops that you can use in later missions or spend in town to exchange for gear or consumables or (now in 3.0) upgrade gear. Eventually you'll be able to challenge tougher missions or higher difficulties to get better loot.You farm a mission to get loot, so you can farm a tougher mission to get better loot, so you can farm an even tougher mission to get even better loot, so you can farm........ The MonHun formulaThere are now 6 characters to choose from with different playstyles.   The "Standard" EmpressThe "Tank" WarriorThe "Floaty Glass Cannon" Shinobi  The "High APM Glass Cannon" Witch  The "High APM plus buff management" Oracle  and the "RNG Resource Management" BanditWith some areas that can only be accessible by certain characters, make sure you have a diverse party to access all the loot.Play with friends, with online matchmaking (playerbase permitting), or even solo.Now for the cons.It does have that MonHun formula, so it also has that MonHun Grind. With some drops being in the single digit or lower percentage drop, it can get repetive.  While it does have HP scaling for more party members, it is much easier in a party. Compared to the Switch launch, going solo is much easier, but having others to divert the boss' attention allows for an easier fight overall.There are a few difficulty spikes.   The first few are just significant leaps in incoming damage (but that can be mitigated by dodging).   But the one that I'm currently attempting to break through is a huge HP increases with bosses. (A lvl 65 boss takes 7 minutes, the lvl 80 version takes 30)All in all, if you enjoyed the Mega Man: Zero or ZX series, you will have a ton of fun, even if you dont enjoy MonHun like grinds.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Very unique game. Much more fun with friends. The spellcasting system is very fun. Who wouldn't want to make nearly 40 inputs just to cast a single max level spell?I've never found a game quite like Dragon Marked For Death and I don't think I ever will. There's some inherent magic to this game that I can't quite put my finger on. I think the major aspects are the uniqueness of multiplayer platformers and the use of RPG classes and roles in a type of game that normally wouldn't have them. Due to those factors being huge contributors to the game's feel, it works far better when you have people to play with. The online is empty, so if you want to give this game a shot I recommend getting a friend or two to play it with you.The game is very much guilty of many of the things the negative reviews will say. There's not a lot of enemy or stage variety. You'll have to replay the same quests many times over due to often insane difficulty and low item drop rates at higher levels. The systems are poorly explained and many mechanics are hard to wrap your head around. The in game tips menu helps out a lot, but can lack description in some places as well.That's not to say that all is doom and gloom though, there's certainly plenty that this game has going for it. The feeling of playing an RPG party and fulfilling your roles with a group of friends is incredibly fun. I primarily played the Witch in my time with the game, and I feel of all the characters, she plays into this the most. She's both a healer and an incredible damage dealer, but can require protection from teammates in order to operate at full power. The spellcasting system in DMFD is my favorite of all time, perhaps rivaled only by Magicka. Spells take long sequences of button presses that you have to memorize, and a single wrong input will cause the spell to fail. In return for this difficulty, the Witch's spells are devastating, with many of the 3rd level spells being essentially screen clears against regular enemies and doing huge amounts of damage to bosses. At first, these spells take far too much time and concentration to cast, so you'll only really be able to use them against bosses with the help of a Warrior's shield, but as you get used to the inputs and you begin to memorize the spell better and better, it becomes almost subconscious. The button inputs for the spells are forever ingrained in my mind, and I feel like that's the closest you can get to the feel of real magic.If you've made it this far into this review then I applaud you and leave you with some parting advice. If you do end up playing the game, definitely check out the steam guides. In particular there's a guide for the Bandit that has a link to a very important spreadsheet. It tells you what stages you need to clear in order to progress both the story and the questline to unlock the Bandit. Finally, if you decide to play the Witch, try rebinding your right joystick to the face buttons. This made some of the spellcasting inputs (namely heal and level up) far easier to input quickly.

_childDocuments_.review: A great game by the guys who made the Mega man zero games!The game has fun game play and a rather unique take on a co-op action rpg. Each character has a unique kit, and different play styles. I highly recommend playing this game, especially if you have friends to play with, enemies do become bullet sponges as the game progresses, having a party makes the game a lot easier, turns out synergy is a good thing. Unfortunately there aren't a lot of people trying to play online.And I need to talk about the Witch, she has the coolest magic system ever, mash in inputs to make a spell. They don't make all the spells obvious—they just tell you to look at the command list. She has a great repertoire of spells she has 4 Elemental spells, Fire, Wing, Ice, and Electric, 3 support spells, levitate, heal, and illuminate. All of which (except for levitate and illuminate) can be modified. You can strengthen, condense and give your spell homing. There are 3 levels of strength which increases damage on each step, condense makes your attack hit multiple times, and homing will make the spell either land on an enemy or track an enemy. It's a great mechanic that I'd love to see in more games.Also it should be said that if you fail your input or let the meter run out you will be stunned for a second and small magic orbs will fall from you, they'll deal damage to enemies but casting a spell is always better. (if you use macros for her you're a chump, mash like a man)

_childDocuments_.review: When I first saw this game, it was only for the Nintendo switch. It looked interesting, but the lack of having online on my end made it less then desirable. Now that it's on steam, I picked it up to play and can sadly say I'm still playing solo. At the moment, there are not many people playing publicly like in most other games. That's not to say no one is online, for there is a discord server dedicated for the game. That aside, the gameplay has been very interesting. The game is set up to where you benefit when playing as a team, but you can still play solo without to much trouble. Enemies are plentiful, and treasure is easy to find. However, there are some issues. First of all, you see the exact same enemies form start to finish. The one time I thought I saw some new enemy group I got excited, turns out it was just another generic enemy your going to see for the rest of the game. The bosses are a little more varied and interesting. The next problem comes from multiplayer. When you choose a quest in multiplayer you are locked into that quest and only that quest. Even when you finish it, you have to back out of the room and make a new one just to play a different quest. I would like to have an option to choose the next mission after the current mission or something like that. On the bright side, this does make farming a little easier. I'm not entirely sure how the missions are ordered currently, but I would like the option to change it based on location or minimum level. As of the time I have completed the story with two characters. All in all, I give it a solid 7/10. A great game, but you should probably wait for a sale to pick it up.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like there is an audience for this game, but I honestly can't think of who to recommend this to. Especially at the game's retail price point.It plays like a side-scroller beat em up on a 2D plane, but feels lacking in move variety outside the Witch class (She lacks baseline mobility, and has to remain stationary to use her moveset on top of that.) But has maps built like a Metroidvania, a lot of verticality and a lot of areas that require specific mobility kits (characters) to reach them. Has the equipment, stat (STR, INT, VIT), and grinding systems of an RPG but lacks an expanding moveset to keep things interesting. It is incredibly easy to get lost in the maps that are available, with little to no guidance on where to go within each one. And with each map being large vertically AND horizontally missions take a while to figure out what the goal is. Each map seems to be reused multiple times, occasionally with "invisible walls" that aren't displayed on the map preventing you from accessing areas you've visited before, not really shortening the maps just blocking certain paths from being taken around the map. And it's weird that the game reuses the maps as often as they do considering they offer each map at 5 level intervals from when you unlock it (Example: you unlock a map at level 10 and it goes from 10, 15, 20, 25... etc)I didn't find the story all that compelling past the opening personally, but it was also difficult to find what were "main missions" and what were "side missions" so it's hard to tell you for sure what to really pay attention to there. A lot of the missions boiled down to I lost thing, people, or monsters took over this place go get it back.There is co-op, but it was a little buggy with the blue-guy's movement powers. He can charge into specific walls and open up places but this:  happens a lot and they have to go back and charge more to fix it.Menuing in attrocious, be prepared to spend tons of time inside the game's various menus figuring out what specific building you need to visiting in the town in order to adjust your quick action items, where to craft items, where to obtain X material to craft said items or accessories, and unequipping items in order to upgrade them. That's right to go from +1 to +2 on an item you have to unequip it then go back into the shop.Overall I feel the game lacks the depth of the genres it is borrowing from. At the start it was entertaining, but quickly became a grind and then a chore. I wasn't able to finish the story only getting to level 26 before all the prior Cons listed outweighed my desire to see the end of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: The people complaining got F I L T E R E D.The game's fantastic. It seems a bit shallow at first, but it opens up substantially and there're varied playstyles for each character. Also, there's a lot of information available about the game, but it is horrifyingly difficult to access; you'll have to learn for yourself how to accomplish what you want to do, or you'll need to search through the community maintained discord server. You can complete the game with minimal effort, but there's an optional post-game grind to level 100 that's pretty intense. A lot of your best-in-slot drops come from farming high-end versions of previous levels. At certain difficulty levels, levels get different enemies, bosses get more mechanics, and obviously, everything's got more health. The barrier for entry can be offputting, but pay attention to the affixes on weapons/armor (the text at the bottom of the item description box), and you'll do fine.Overall, I highly recommend the game, though 40 bucks is a bit steep. If you're a fan of grindy megaman-esque games, it's worth it. If you're on the fence, the game's often on sale for 20 bucks, which is a much easier pill to swallow.8.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has the foresight to list drop tables on the mission select screen, and because of that, it very quickly devolves into running the same mission over and over to grind that one drop.I realized this at about hour 6.  I'm sure by the end of this, I'll have an hour to run a dungeon, that will only take 5 minutes to get to the boss if I just ignore everything else, and whom I will be able to kill in ~20 seconds to see if he drops those rare gloves, and if you stripped that repetition away, the game would be pretty barren.This isn't necessarily a condemnation of the game. I for one, am ok with this but only barely. I'm the type that plays pokemon in-game with wiki pages open to route lists and encounter tables. The type who tries to "solve" Skyrim as though it were a puzzle. And I'll probably continue playing this game until I have 6 nigh-unstoppable killing machines and enough extra resources such that switching builds between solo and multiplayer isn't an issue.But I was looking for another Crosscode. At it's current price point of 40$, I thought a veteran company like inti could satisfy that craving for the sublime, but I seem to be naive.TLDR: If Warframe played like Megaman Zero, which I am ok with, but was hoping for something like SotN but more linear.

_childDocuments_.review: Combat is repetitive and not in a fun way either. You'll have more fun playing "Dungeons and Dragons shadow over mystara" and if you have a console just stick to "dragons crown".  You'll grind most of the same bosses and enemies over and over due to the abysmal variety. Many of the weapons you grind for is useless because of the black market having a weapon that you'll use for almost 20 levels, then you'll replace it again and be stuck with it for another 20. The issue from this is that each class has a few weapon types but the black market weapons only have 1 type and they are just soooo good, that you'll never have a need for another weapon if you want damage and bonus stats. The characters have their strengths and weaknesses. Worst of em is probably mage. There was a short lived MMO called "Pi story" that had mage classes have to type in spells in order to cast em. cool, but it made combat miserable. In dragons marked for death, you'll have to remember multiple sequences for many different spells and unless you're using some sort of cheat that allows you to just hot binds all the sequences for fat slappy spells and heals. you aren't going to enjoy that class. Missions in this game start of alright. pretty standard  RPG quest, except so many of the missions just blend together with so often with little diversity in the way its done. It starts feeling all the same and again, going through the same map, again and again with the same enemy type is just sleep inducing. Okay, there is slight variety. You have a green slime, and a red slime, yellow slime and blue slime. each with different weaknesses. Then you have a goblin, green goblin, red goblin and yellow goblin, each with different weaknesses. You see where this is going. pallet swapped enemies. I bought this and convinced two of my friends to purchase this game, and this was the worst purchase all of us ever made. now they don't trust my suggestions anymore.Pretty art, nice pixel graphics and a nice soundtrack. that's the only upside this game has going for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me prefix this by saying I don't dislike this game, I just can't recommend it to anyone at full price and if you're playing it by yourself then I don't think you'll have fun.There's some interesting story bits here and there, but it's not enough for the $40 price tag. That's wayyyyyyy too high. This type of game should be priced closer to something similar such as Mercenary Kings at $20. Let's say you do enjoy what you see here and you want to play with someone online...1) There's really no one playing online. At the time of this post, there's 14 players online and who knows is those 14 people are even in your region2) Good luck convincing a friend to drop $40 on a game they've never heard ofOn the flipside, the character playstyles are all VERY different and I love that about this game so much, at least the main 4 you start with. The mage operates completely differently than the warrior in that there's manual spell incanting which is awesome. It also has character stat allocation, weapon acquistion and upgrading and crafting.The problem with the weapon upgrading and crafting is that it's kind of expensive to do so with no way to see what the final result of an upgrade will be (i.e. if you go from +0 to +3, you won't know what passives will be on a weapon). Also, the passives early on aren't really that interesting and there's a weird amount of trash weapons you can buy and find that you'll never want to use as the cost to upgrade the next tier of weapon would be too much instead of just waiting for a weapon to unlock with better passives. There's very much a right way to spend your money and a wrong way. The weapon variety, per weapon also doesn't exist. A light axe +3 and another light axe +3 are always the same. You're done, no reason to ever look at a different one. They will always have the same passives and stats unlike in a game like PSO, you could have two different handguns and maybe one will do more damage in the forest area while one will do more damage in the mines. Something like that would have kept the weapons a bit more interesting. You'll go a decent amount of time using the same weapon.Also, there's a weird problem about how information is delivered to the player. There's a ton of information you won't know unless you browse into the button help and tips. This is fine if you love to read to be a better player, but most people don't want to absorb walls of text in order to feel like they are playing correctly. i.e. AGI is VERY important to the warrior. Actually, I'd say it's so important that you should try to dump nearly all of your level up stats into it which common sense would not dictate.Anyway, it's fun with a friend and if were cheap. If those two conditions are met: get it. If not, pass.

And for a while I sat here looking at it going...which should I do which should I do???But I finally came to terms with giving it a thumbs down and here's why.(Btw if you want a more detailed review with some in-depth knowledge then check out my video on my youtube channel, link below. Thanks)I think the game overall sets out exactly what it means to. It gives you exactly what you're expecting. And for the most part the game is really good. I did have a few errors when I first started playing however.  Like my game only opening up in windowed mode. Only has controller support no PC control support. It crashed and froze on me once. But after those first few hiccups it was going really well. And while I was playing I was having fun and getting invested and enjoying myself.But the reason why I can't recommend it, is because it's meant to be played with friends or online multiplayer. But no ones playing it online. And with a 40$ pricetag most people aren't even gonna spend the money. In this corona virus times, a lot of people aren't working and can't spare that much money on a game like this.So the reason why I can't recommend is based on its price tag and based on the fact that you HAVE to have friends will to also spend the money and play the game with you. Now if you already have friends or disposable income then yeah sure, feel free to pick this up. If you like pixelated games with fast fun side scrolling action/adventure. You'll love this game. _childDocuments_.review: First off, I've mainly played through most of this game with friends. I've got diddly on how the 'rando' multiplayer works. As for bugs, only one stands out for me. The first time I boot the game for a session, if I alt-tab, the game screen locks so I have to relaunch. 6.5/10. Game has been described by others as "Mega Man(insert here) meets Monster Hunter". I... guess, though I hate Monster Hunter, so I'm biased. It's got some Metrovania feel to some of the levels, though you don't really get 'upgrades' to help map navigation. The best you'll get is maybe a speed or jump boost, maybe something to give you back your 'mana' for class skill spam. Everything your character or 'class' can do to get through a level they have from the start. Some classes can breeze through most of the navigation(Shinobi) only missing out on some chests or convenient back-track loops, while others have to slog through slowly(Warrior). Level navigation is much quicker with a diverse party. There's sadly not a whole lot of map variety, with each map having a few quests associated with it. It's very noticeable on certain maps you may not enjoy, like the tower map. ♥♥♥♥ the tower map.Combat wise, it's not that technical. The only class that seems 'limited' is that the Warrior is a straight up melee character. All the others have ranged options, even though there might be a 'meta' build that takes them into melee as well. As for builds themselves, there's a small amount of wiggle room, though not so much for the poor Warrior. Pick melee, magic, or 'Holy' attack tactics, and dump into the corresponding stat(s) is the go to for leveling. There are items to reset your stat investment for testing, as well as changing your character's primary element, so there are options. As for enemies, the trash mobs are basic, and can be easily dispatched before they even do anything. The game's togglable 'aggro' indicators not only show who the monsters are aiming for, but gives their location for quicker clearing. Bosses usually have a few to several attacks, with maybe the addition of a couple more or just faster/more projectiles on harder difficulties. The story is lackluster, with either translation or outright spelling errors. It's main positive is that cutscenes are either skippable, or you can toggle quick text displays. Makes the story bearable if you don't care for it, or have already seen it. There are a few different endings with set circumstances to 'unlock', so if you enjoy the story you have that to look forward to. Just don't expect much except text for the unlockable characters.All in all, game shines with more players. If you've got some friends willing to give it a try, or the genre fits your interests, give it a go.Edited for clarity.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the only negative review that talks about the gameplay not the fricken portDragon Marked For Death is a unique game. You see the side scrolling platforming action, lots of stuff to beat up, loot, levels, etc. You think you're getting some sort of co-op Gunvolt Metroidvania, but you're not. The formula is MonHun, some of the worst parts of it too. You're thrust into reused, overlarge context-free levels with some vague direction, a time limit, maybe your co-op buddies are here too, and a bunch of pointless unthreatening baddies between you and the boss. The levels are exercises in complete boredom because one character is basically Copen from Gunvolt and the rest can barely manage a jump for their platforming. The enemies are tedious, unthreatening, and unrewarding, so you eventually get bored of pointlessly chopping out their "bloated enough to remind you this is an RPG, not an action game" health bars and get on with finding the boss or objective, one of the few sources of actual loot for this level.Yes, you're playing a platformer where both the platforming and content is boring filler.(EDIT: Oh geez, it gets worse the more you play. Imagine 15 minute long escort missions over these boring maps and boring enemies where the escort can only be coaxed to jump with loads of little fidgeting. Imagine a level full of almost a dozen lock-you-in monster closets that are just "The same six monsters that aren't a threat in the slightest attack you." Imagine a gimmick level that requires you to find power sources in the map to charge an elevator repeated  at least five times because there are several missions that reuse this level with PRECISELY THE SAME GIMMICK with nothing changed except what's at the top of the tower. And half the rooms in the tower are windy just to slow you down for no reason. There's NOTHING in this game that doesn't waste your time.)Then you reach, mercifully, a boss, one of about six ugly bosses reused constantly through the game. Now the bosses are MonHun too. Fat things designed to be whacked by 2-4 people all at once and designed to be fought by four different characters with different styles so you're dealing with a thing with a giant health bar that spends about a third of the fight sitting around thinking of what to do next before it hits you for nearly all your health making you down a healing item. (Don't get me wrong, the patterns are definitely no-damage possible and at least the standard Inti Creates memorize BS mostly stays out at low levels). (EDIT: Oh and it's an RPG so of course there are ailments like being unable to attack for ten seconds because you got hit once. THERE IS NOTHING IN THIS GAME THAT IS NOT TRYING TO WASTE YOUR TIME!)You do all this for sweet loot from the boss and boy howdy you'll be disappointed. A +2 stat item that goes in one of your four equipment slots, none of which change the gameplay beyond what numbers you do with the same attack combos you will be using all game.It's a MonHun loot farmer with boring overall levels, meant for co-op (Though THANKFULLY they appear to have patched solo play to be actually viable by the time for the Steam release. It was intolerable at low levels on Switch.), without anything mechanically good enough to be worth MonHun style repeat play. While there are definitely far, far worse things to grind at, I found this game to be a disappointment on every level. And though I have ripped it pretty hard, I will relent and say Inti Creates stepped outside their comfort zone here. They have attempted a mix that I don't think has been done before outside of that one PSN/XBLA Castlevania MonHun style game. Effort and creativity went into this, and I respect that, but it came out a resounding failure in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: This negative review is because of the port as of the time of launch. >No resolution support past 1080. If you want to turn down the volume you have to do so in windows. >The controls are Keyboard or controller. No mouse support and it feels much better on controller in my opinion. >Japanese only voice acting which is a minor complaint for me but others might not like it.Text has multiple options.All in all this is a console game and feels like a console game which isn't the worst thing in the world, but for the price tag of $40 I would have expected better.Edit: To make it clear why this review is a negative is not because of the gameplay at all. Its because this was a very lazy port from console to PC. The lack of mouse support, even just for menus, is a major turn off for me. There are options for rebinding keys on both controller and keyboard. When rebinding controller it highlights a button and wants you to press the button you want bound. For example "Dpad up" is highlighted and you press the button you want bound to Dpad up which would probably be Dpad up. It doesn't give you an option like "Dpad up does jump". You have to cycle through all of the buttons on the controller to rebind anything and they don't tell you what any of the buttons do.  Its slightly easier to rebind the keyboard because you can select which button you want to rebind, but all it shows is what button it is on the controller, still having no idea what each button does. The default keyboard controls are just all over the place and don't really make sense for me. _childDocuments_.review: Ok where do i begin...The story initially is pretty solid with interesting characters and fun ideas.The gameplay is also pretty solid (don't play witch tho, she is nigh on unplayable singleplayer and feels practically completely unplayable late game) up until "the grind" begins which i also DO NOT recommend.The late game grind has all kinds of issues not even the least of which is it's uncreative design (not a singular unique new map or enemy all they throw at you is lazy reskins of enemies you have allready fought before but this time with longer immune phases and way higher numbers) which causes the entire gameplay to turn in a slow grindy slog.Then there is the "issues", i played this game in online multiplayer near exclusively (since you know... witch) and the LFG discord server is genuinely really nice.The servers and engine of this game genuinely really seem like they were not made for online multiplayer nor to be played on pc causing many technical problems like crashes, desyncs, random disconnects and in my case the final quest of the game just decided to become completely unplayable after 15 ish clears (its a boss gauntlet and it will now ALWAYS under any circumstance (even after a reinstall) crash on boss 21 out of 24) The story can however be a lot of fun with friends and the gameplay is undeniably very varied with  characters that have movesets that are so varied that it will feel like you're playing one of 4 different games entirely which is pretty cool.It's just with the issues the game causes and the insanely high amount of salt this can generate that i DO NOT recommend you to continue the game after you complete the story since continueing afterwards is neither fun nor worth it in any way.

_childDocuments_.review: As expected of the Megaman Zero developer, the game looks great with its pixel art style. The music itself is serviceable, but the sound design for combat is pretty nice imo.The main part of the game can be played solo with all characters. Some characters might be more difficult to solo with, but still not impossible to play through the main game solo.But it is still nice if you wanna have fun with your friends.You can leave it at that because from this point you see 20~22 out of 24 bosses in the entire game.But even then, these bosses are quality encounters.Once you start transitioning to mid-game, you'll need to start learning an actual boss pattern. This is the part where you start to get good (in an unironic way) and the quality in each boss fight also went up as their level increased.Some of the boss's attacks are seemingly impossible to dodge at first, but they're all avoidable with either good positioning or evasive movements.I'd say it's the main source of enjoyment and replayability when you fight the same boss. Being able to read all of their attacks like the back of your hands then retaliate when the opportunity is presented for you.That being said, the grind from mid-game to late-game is quite excessive when you transition from early-game.These are not part of the main story so you aren't required to do them by any means. But if you want to do it, I'd heavily suggest finding at least a few ppl to grind with you. One last thing: the learning resource for this game is very difficult to find. Even vital stuff like a basic game guide can't be found on Youtube (at least in English, you can find the Japanese guides easily though), so if you're interested in learning some in-depth game info you might need to search for a discord server for this game.

Many bosses have little to no windup on attacks that can cause a myriad of status effects and have absurd contact damage in a melee-focused 2d game. _childDocuments_.review: I recommend for the coop and gameplay even though there are some issues with this game design-wise.Game is very fun, it just leaves a lot to be desired as well. All things that can hopefully be redeemed in a sequel which I would love!Just to list the major issues off:Why is the town so needlessly large? This would have been fine if there was anything to do within it, Namely invite and see party members.Empress has the lowest skill ceiling among the characters. Witch and Oracle have so many options compared to the others its crazy that Empress really only has 2 attacks and 1 ultimate. This game is clearly inspired by Mega Man Zero but theres no input attacks on Empress? Would it have taken too long to at least make the tail hookshot have a hitbox?The difficulty spikes after level 30 missions to the point where I started needing to be 10 levels above the mission level. I imagine this is to promote more party play which is a terrible way to do it.I would have preferred not needing to beat every mission in the game to unlock the 2 characters so as to have some new challenges when I got to play the others.The story was very hit and miss, more miss than hit actually. I don't get why we are a vengeful dragonblood casually doing errands. I would have imagined these characters to be seething with rage and incapable of taking as much ♥♥♥♥ from random people as much as they do. Wordlessly to boot, there is not satisfaction of having the last word on any of the immoral characters that are properly setup to make players hate them.The changing elements feature, I did not find out about until past level 40 as empress. I also think theres no point in costing a dragonite for this.Empress has very little to do among shopping and weapon upgrades until very late in the game. Even then, everything is soo pricey that it actively discourages experimenting at all.Empress' grapple nodes are very few among the midgame, so much so that her grappling feature barely exists in the game, only at the beginning and end of the game.A lot of missions and levels are really easy to get stuck in. Sometimes it not clear what you have to do and you have to guess your way through.Some good things:I really like the asymmetric gameplay of the characters. Though I believe something could be done to improve warrior and Empress' mobility. Even a switch weapons button would have been nice to use the shortsword moves for mobility.This is the first game where I heavily relied on items to get through. Thats a cool accomplishment as I am normally the type to avoid using items for no good reason.Stil, great game. really hoping to see a sequel eventually.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing more of the game, the stages actually aren't as bad as some people make it out to be. The stages themselves are fairly varied, have had 5 different maps and even when you're brought back to them, the encounters are scripted for each quest. Only downside is definitely enemy variety but the boss variations and additional attack patterns make up for the lack of themed enemies.Characters although quite standard can be tweaked to specialize in the abilities you like. Mage I recently found out cast elements you specialize in more efficiently and quickly. Warrior can get different shot types that give new utility.All in all, my opinion of the game just got better overtime and it's not boring playing other characters because your one character just can't do it all so theres a point to coop. I feel alot of games tend to just make your character all encompassing regardless of what class they are which is frankly boring.------------------------------------------First impression as a mage is pretty good. You have a simple spell system that you need to execute on the fly under a time limit which is quite novel to me.  The game makes you go against some basic logic while playing since the mage can't jump or run very well so I had to take contact damage to avoid an attack. Something which I don't quite feel like is good design in late game when touching something could mean you die in 1 hit.Stages are pretty well designed but the complaints about them reusing stages and enemies are quite valid. Although the stage is well thought out and is mostly accessible with 1 character. The thoughtfulness and effort in design is wasted because treasures, traps and enemies are randomized for each part of the stage.All in all great first impression.- equipment is mainly passive buffs- grinding hits you really fast. i.e you need alot of money to upgrade unless you're playing stages way above your current level

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good fun. It's a time sink with Dark Souls inspired character stat customization paired with Megaman level side-scrolling action. I guess you could call this the Salt Sanctuary of sidescrollers ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°)Nevertheless, you will spend much in this game making big number go bigger. Highly recommended to play with friends to increase XP gain and to increase fun. The final smashes after hitting the small ball (Dragon Sphere) are also really flashy and clutch, making a tough fight even easier to plow through.Make sure to do thorough research on each class and the elemental contracts, while the game doesn't look like much--it definitely does not reward going into things blind. It can often feel like there's no goal, but should you do research on builds and weaponry, it'll easy to keep finding more and more to do. Some cons I would share for this particular PC port is the lack of resolution options (no 4k? Really?), and the instability of some of the quests. There's a particular endgame quest that causes frequent crashes more often than others, possibly due to story triggers present in the quest itself. The game is quick to load, however, so the frequent crashes are less of an issue and more of a nuisance. There's the nuisance of when booting the game, the sound and controller options are out of whack--make sure to start with headphones off your ears and that you enable the gamepad option so you can bind controls.Hope you found this review useful and do enjoy if you do decide purchase!

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first review I've ever written, and probably the only one I'll ever write.I'm mostly just giving pointers into how to get the most enjoyment out of this game.First and foremost: join the Discord server for the best possible experience! You don't use Discord? I recommend you start using it. If you don't join the Discord server, you most likely won't enjoy this game.The in-game matchmaking system is less than ideal, and the Discord has an extremely active and helpful community that you can coordinate quests with in their dedicated LFG channels. Before the game had drop tables visible within the game, the community was able to create their own spreadsheet containing every weapon/accessory in the game, and the quest where it is dropped. Those tables are still actively updated to assist you in your quest for loot. There is also a list of all of the quests and objectives you need to do in order to progress the story, because this game doesn't do any hand-holding.Discord Invite Link: Now to the review:First, each mission has a baseline Quest-Level (Q.Lv), and then additional Q.Lvs you unlock by completing the previous difficulty that give you upgraded versions of old weapons, or brand new weapons with a higher level requirement. The Q.Lvs go as high as 110, currently, and the bosses get additional mechanics added at various intervals in the progression through Q.Lvs.The final quest in the main story itself has a baseline Q.Lv 30 (the "DLC" that is included in the PC version finishes with a baseline Q.Lv 50 mission, but all of the missions are typically more difficult than those in the main story). Those people saying they only finished the game in 7 hours only scratched the surface of what this game has to offer.The max player-level is 100, and it takes a considerable grind to reach that on even a single character.You get out of this game what you put in, and only playing through the main story will just have you scratch the surface. I have over 300 hours on the Switch, and there are some people with over 1k hours in the game (I know one player that has over 2k hours).I love this game so much that I bought it on Steam just to have the 3.0.0 update a few days earlier than on Switch, and, depending on how things go, I might switch over to the Steam version. I hope to see the PC get an online community as active as the one on the Switch.I hope to see you guys on Discord, and happy farming!

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR - If you like sidescrolling, quest based metroidvania like games, or feel like levelling up your megaman fix with rpg levelling mechanics, this is a really fun addition to your collection. It CAN get really repetitive after one playthrough, on single player. Multiplayer is personally untested as of writing this, but each stage in the game FEELS like it's made for it.I have a plethora of thoughts of criticisms and praise alike about this game, but I'll try and boil it down to a few points: Pros:   -Really fun visuals that invoke games like Megaman ZX or ZX Advent  -Gameplay that is similar to the above games, with levelling, equipment collection, and stat based builds like an metroidvania/rpg game.  -A unique set of characters and game mechanics for each that allow you to change aspects of their game play akin to   altering a character's moves in the smash brothers games for the 3DS and WiiU. When I first picked this game up, I was assuming the Bandit unlockable character would be almost identical to the shinobi, or a combination of it and the small sword using empress (as they share those weapons), and was pleasantly surprised at how different it played from either of the other classes.  -The never-ending hunt for better loot is strong in this game! Also, modifiers harken back to D&D in my brain as I'm upgrading my gear. :) Cons:-The plot is serviceable but basic, with cookie cutter dialogue that's slightly dressed up in flowery language that doesn't hide it very well. Also, dialogue doesn't change based on your characters, who are silent protagonists during story scenes.-The game reuses its resources - basic enemies, its stages, your weapons, and bosses - with a small amount of modification (colour palette swaps, slight aesthetic mods, in the case of the stages, slightly changing what rooms in the stage are accessible)-This game feels entirely built to be multiplayer, despite me playing through levels in single player. Related to this, as of yet I have had little luck finding groups/teams to play mutliplayer with, so that feeling begins to nag on you as you continue to play.*Spoilers*-One of the prerequisites to getting this games best ending is beating it with the four base characters, so that paired with the issues with its plot might get tedious for some people.Ultimately, I have to recommend this game based on how much I enjoy learning how different characters play, and how much variance there is under the different "contracts" that change their unique mechanics and elemental affinity. I have a soft spot for these sorts of games, but despite this one's flaws, the game play and it's aesthetics keep me coming back for another quest...or five....>.>

Can we get in-game sound options.  Mainly an option to silence the BGM.  I love the soundtrack.  I really do. _childDocuments_.review:
Dragon MFD is a 2D side-scrolling action RPG game where up to 4 players can play together in either local multiplayer or online multiplayer. Refreshing, feel-good level designs based around intuitive 2D-action-based gameplay await!

Features:

* Play through the game as one of four Dragonkin characters!
The characters, known as the Dragonkin, have forged a pact with dragons which granted them special new powers. You can choose any one of the Princess, Warrior, Shinobi, or Witch characters to play as.

* Each playable character has different strengths and abilities!
The Princess is a well-balanced DPS character, the Warrior is a Tank class character that protects the party with his high defense, the Shinobi is DPS that places emphasis on movement on tricky attacks, and the Witch can both heal her allies and damage her emeies.

* A fascinating and immersive dark fantasy world
Carefully drawn pixel art from some of the industry's best pixelmancers paints the entire picture and brings players right into the dark fantasy setting.

* Work together with your companions to progress through stages!
In Dragon MFD, working together with your companions opens up a whole new realm of possibilities when it comes to defeating enemies and traversing stages.

* Battle against gargantuan bosses!
Absolutely gigantic bosses that are bigger than the entire screen await our heroes. Work together with your comrades to take down these larger than life baddies!

* Dozens and dozens of hours worth of gameplay!
Make no mistake, Dragon MFD is a massive game for its genre. With single stages that span 200-400 screens, over 30 main quests, and tons of side quests to tackle, players have tons of playtime to look forward to!

name: ICARUS
detailed_description: ICARUS is a PvE survival game with both Mission-based and persistent Open World modes for up to eight co-op players. Endure a savage wilderness on Icarus, an Earth-like terraformed planet now considered humanity’s greatest mistake. From their orbital station, prospectors drop to the planet surface to explore, harvest, craft and hunt while seeking their fortune. Confront and conquer a brutal PvE world determined to wear you down From toxic atmosphere to savage wildlife, apex predators to destructive storms and forest fires, Icarus is a planet with a temper. Preparation and planning are everything, whether it’s to find a source of oxygen, stalk your next meal or stockpile supplies for a long journey into the wilderness. Go at it alone, invite up to 8 Steam friends to join your game or play on dedicated servers. Immerse yourself in a deceptively familiar, yet formidable, world The First Cohort of prospectors has been granted initial mining licenses for over 64 square kilometers of hand-crafted terrain, full of hidden caves and biomes to explore. Every single tree is harvestable, every rock can be voxel mined, every creature can be hunted. Tame and ride mounts, craft advanced tech to extract resources faster and prepare yourself for harsher challenges. Master three separate tech trees: planetary tech, player talents and the orbital workshop Unlock four tiers of technology from hand-crafted to advanced composites and electronics, plus 8+ different building materials. Choose from over 100 talents as you specialize your character in exploring, building, farming, hunting, taming, fighting and more. Return to the orbital workshop to exchange exotic matter for advanced tech and items with unique properties, which may give you an advantage on your next drop. Three Game Modes: Open World, limited-time Missions, or creative Outposts However you want to experience Icarus, you can. Forge your claim in Open World, battling the elements and apex predators for survival and testing the limits of your survival instincts. Accept timed Missions to mine exotics and earn Ren as you complete tasks for the power brokers overseeing the planet. Drop down to the planet with nothing, establish a base from scratch and escape in time. Let your creative mind run wild in the Outpost regions with regenerating resources and safe environments. About the world of Icarus Icarus was once destined to be a second Earth, but when terraforming collapsed - the air turned toxic and humanity’s hopes of colonizing a new world died. Icarus became a joke, a symbol of humanity reaching for the stars and failing. The xeno-engineers salvaged what they could, released modified embryos and halted the terraforming process. Yet when they discovered the cause of the failure - exotic matter - new interest was ignited. Valuable beyond reckoning, these ‘exotics’ sparked a gold rush and fueled political tensions back on Earth. Prospectors flocked to Icarus to complete contracts to extract exotics and conduct research for various factions. Those that survive return to orbit as seasoned veterans, converting their exotics into advanced technology, and taking on ever more challenging drops. Those that get left behind... are lost forever. --- ICARUS is being made by a team of survival game veterans at RocketWerkz in beautiful Auckland, New Zealand.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay loop:If you select scanning mission:1) Go to a marked location on your map2) Build a tower3) Start wave defense4) Climb onto your tower and start shooting animals in the face.5) Repeat 1-4 until your mission is done6) Return to your drop pod.If you select the other mission type:1) Go to marked location on your map2) Return to your podYes. This game consists of two kinds of missions. 3 if you count in mission where you literally do nothing (and your reward for those missions is also nothing... )There is nothing interesting here. This game has horrendous AI and all the challenge comes from over powered mobs you can't beat without cheesing if you don't farm and grind for days. If you don't want to cheese the missions from tower, you'll die repeatedly until the mission is done. Best thing about this game is it's graphics (which count for nothing if the game has no content. Just watch pretty pictures.) When I play this I actually want to pick up better games from my library which have been gathering dust for a while. I ♥♥♥♥ you not, I realized I wanted to grapple hook around the terrain, tame the animals, fight versatile animals with interesting weapons, explore points of interest, build vehicles... But this game has none of that. It does not matter which animals attacks you either, only difference comes from their HP and DMG multipliers and that is all there is. The animals are literally all the same with same movement patterns (Run straight at you and attack). The combat, which is main part of the game play loop, is bad... There is nothing to it. It's just so bad... Bad and boring.All the best survival games have their own gimmicks which separates them from each other. This one has: -Timed missions, but the timer does not matter... You never have the sense of urgency, you have literally one week (real life time) to walk around and do your boring tasks before essentially taking your rewards and starting the same boring mission over....-Weather conditions, but they bring nothing new to the table. You sit in your cottage / cave / rock hole during the worst storms and go about your mundane tasks during rain.This game is better plaid with friends, but what game isn't?If you like survival genre, play instead (all of these offer waaaaaay more bang for the buck):-ARK -7 days to die-Last Oasis-Subnautica -Unreal World-No Man's sky-Project Zomboid-Oxygen Not Included-Don't Starve (/together)-Valheim-Terraria-Starbound-Conan Exiles-Stranded deep-Green hell-The Forest-Tetris

How wrong we were…Most of the early adopters received the “Styx Map DLC” free, we all thought it was just an update and strides to right some of the wrongs, and to give us more content. This DLC eventually became a PAID DLC, what was once free, now another $15. During this entire “early experience” not once was there mention of “2 Parts” to the game, not once during its release did they say that this was only the first part of the game. These claims were made after criticism began.The REAL slap in the face was the “New Frontiers DLC”. This was the update that would finally bring us the game we were promised, the game we all had been waiting for, we were all ready and excited to play. BUT instead of fixing their mistake, addressing their false advertising, supporting the players that supported them from the beginning, they put it behind a pay wall….. The base game as it sits is not a finished product, you need the extra DLC to get what you’re expecting. These predatory cash grabs are disgusting and are far too common in the gaming space. The game as a whole is not bad and might even be decent. However, this is NOT a AAA game that can demand the money grab that they are, play No Man’s Sky, a company who messed up but did the RIGHT thing.

_childDocuments_.review: This review has a lovely video version, but follow your heart :)                Icarus is a whirlpool of jank and wonder that I cannot help but enjoy. The game opens with an ultra bizarre montage, featuring hearts bleeding gold, and staunchly obvious symbolism that deep thinkers and Metal Gear fans will pretend to understand. 	One moment, you're in a space suit, plummeting from orbit.  The next you're looking for rocks and sticks to make yourself simple tools. At the highest tech level, your knowledge allows you to make sci-fi space armor and 1860s weaponry. All to defend yourself from the ultimate enemy, the polar bear. None of that stopped me. 	To be honest, I had to do a lot more than squint to see a good game here. I had to put on a hazmat suit and venture into a mushroom cloud. The bad aspects of this game are impossible to ignore. Solo play routinely dares new players to uninstall with badly tuned enemies, and pointless corpse runs. Corpse runs are boredom concentrate, and are especially awful when the campaign has such abrupt difficulty spikes so early.  	In Valhiem, another game with corpse runs, you have one long campaign with meaningful armor and difficulty scaling. Icarus doesn't scale well, in difficulty, or in armor, and most of the missions don't last long enough to warrant corpse runs. In Icarus you respawn with the debuffs you had when you died. If the player doesn't feel like sitting through minutes of broken leg, and just wants to quit the game for a week or two, without leaving the mission. No problemo! Your character dies permanently.  	The mission design can be thoughtless, turning a good building game into a bad walking simulator. A solo missions that takes 30 minutes will reward half as much as a mission that takes multiple people dozens of hours. 	The combat is poorly executed. There is a strange delay that dampens the responsiveness, so even if you melee a wolf first, just wait a moment for the lag to pass, you'll get a wound. Based on that single fact alone, Icarus devs should've steered this game away from combat at every possible opportunity. When a bear swipes the air 20 feet behind you, and still kills you, you are thinking to yourself, "Why am I playing this game?" 	Imagine being so completely out of touch that you make the worst part about your game the cover character. Bears nearly ruined this game for me. They are so overtuned they diminish the meaning of every other enemy in the game. Does the bear need to be more durable than elephants, does it need to be able to outrun you like cougars, did it need to have a super saiyan version in the polar bear?  	Polar Bears are insanely overtuned, but also, you can kill them naked, at level 1, with a dinky bow made out of sticks you found on the ground. That's how bad the tuning situation is in this game.	Bears aren't enough of a skill check, and far too much of a cheese check. If you're near a body of water, you're an unkillable god of nature. Nothing can swim faster than you. Much like the concept of time or death, this cheese is absolute. You can also build a structure the bear has to get through. This mild cheddar isn't my preferred cheese of choice, but it gets the job done. Then there is a concrete shrub technique. This jalepeno infused cheese is spicy because the concrete shrubs can stop you to, but it tastes damn good. Once the player has elevated himself through various cheeses, he is ready for the final, most challenging cheese, running. 	If you run, you can dodge every single bear attack. As long as you can move fast enough, neither version of bear can hit you. A lot of the ways you'd prepare in other survival games don't work in Icarus, namely armor. If you're naked, a polar bear two shots you. If you have high tier armor, a polar bear still two shots you. 	And in a strange twist, weapons scale up way to much, killing polar bears in two shots. The strange tuning doesn't end there, because a series of different delicious pies will add far more combat strength than hi-tech space armor. 	While solo play is generally never as fun as co-op, there is rarely such a yawning cavern between the two experiences in games. in co-op, dying just means waking up to a friend ready to fill your macros back up if you need. No time lost on xp gained, no time lost on a corpse run, just a cause for laughter, and a grilled carrot if I want one. 	Co-op Icarus is an absolute joy to play. It pushes all the weaknesses into the background, and pushes all the strengths forward, while also giving the talent tree more meaning. Which brings us to this game's greatest strength, building. 	Structural integrity, weather proofing, leather curtains, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ my loins stir with excitement. This is where my preferences deviate greatly from the massive round table of nerds. I love building enough to do it over from scratch, every single mission. Especially when I get to bring sparkly, high tier tools with me. 	I think I would hate teching up again, every single time, but all content is defeatable with a stick bow, so I rarely spend much time teching up. Collecting enough iron to tech up in a single cave isn't bad at all, but finding enough copper and gold to get to tier 4 across a dozen caves is a nightmare of boredom.  	The talent tree makes gathering in Icarus a slot machine, and hitting the jackpot can give you enough stone to make a castle. I very much appreciate the speed at which Icarus allows the player to build. Icarus has an outstanding build to gather ratio, but the snapping system certainly has room to improve though. It also lacks decoration, but dropping food for a temporary banquet makes me feel crafty. After building a lot in games with no restrictions, it's nice to build in games like Icarus and Valhiem specifically for the restrictions.	It's just so easy to immerse myself while listening to the rain patter against the roof as a fire warms me up. Leaving behind a stone, weather proof structure feels damn good. As if Odin challenged me with nature, and I accepted. You don't need much sheltered space to actually get by, but creating sheltered space was stupidly fun for me, so I always happily created more than I needed. The building in this is my buffet, and I always serve myself to much. 	For all the cheese checks, combat lag, and corpse runs, there are moments of sublime immersion that make it all worth it. When I am in my death bed, made of swords and dragon scale, I will remember games like Icarus for immersing me so completely for a time. For in Icarus's most relaxing and mundane moments, I found a deep sense of joy to bask in. Something about Icarus really makes me appreciate the warmth of my friends. The warmth of a burning mansion is pretty cool too. 	This game is going to throw a lot of people off, in the same way biting into a twinkie and tasting pizza would throw a lot of people off. People who would logically expect to fight polar bears with a spear are going to be disappointed. Combat will never be the star of this show, but the crafting and building aspects of this game is completely ready to carry this motley team of misfit ideas.  It's just a matter of letting them. 	So this is my humble recommendation for Icarus, it comes from a place of love, that's also wrapped in caution tape. To be clear, I'm not recommending this game because I think most people will enjoy it. No, no. I recommend it because the nerds that do enjoy it, will do so with loins ablaze.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great, it provides a new perspective to other survival games that we are use to such as Rust or DayZ(which was made by the same dev as this game). Instead of just spawning in a world by the beach or in a random location, you drop into a new world as a prospector on a space ship. The landing animation is really cool, the building is awesome, bears also ♥♥♥♥ in this game(not literally but they will ♥♥♥♥ you up). Dying in this game is very punishing, if you die and have to respawn. You will accrue an XP debt which brings you back to the beginning of your level and your XP gain is reduced, I personally like this system but I understand it can be really annoying for solo players. Currently, you gain talent points until lvl 40 but can keep leveling up to 99.There are some bugs in the game, but for how massive the game is they are very minimal. Dev team is doing great at communication and making realistic and not a robotic responses. Response time for issues have been really quick, and the community mods in the Discord are great.If you're looking to dump 100s of hours into a survival game with friends or even as a solo, this is your game.I don't have any real complaints about the game, because i've been having fun playing it. _childDocuments_.review: -------------------- Original Review (9 hrs) ->  --------------------I have no idea why there are so many weirdly bad reviews - this game is very fun.I have played roughly 9 hours at the time of posting and have been awaiting the release of this game for a while.I am in a group of 3, we are all near level 11 and putting talents into various things to help the team more.We are full exploring the first map, including all the nooks and crannies.We built two bases on opposite sides of the map.We have faced storms, forest fires, death, animals, spooky noises, and fall damage...This game does require managing food, water, stamina, health, oxygen, and debuffs/buffs A few notes for players looking to come into this game:Update your drivers! - make sure your gfx are as updated as possible and make sure to mess with your sliders in game to increase YOUR performance! I play with my DLSS turned off and my shadow cascades at 1 - mostly medium/high settings for the rest. My PC specs are not great, I have a 6GB 1060, 3600 CPU, and 32GB RAM and my FPS are consistently above 50 - I have not seen it dip lower than that.REBIND YOUR Q TO DROP - it is SO easy to fat finger that keybind so move it to something else so you dont throw your bow/knife mid-combatUse your map to find your friends when they die! There are no real name tags in the game except when you are VERY close to friends or on the map itself. So use the map to navigate to them when they are downed.LEARN THE FIRE WHACKER ASAP - fires happen easily early on and you will regret not having it when the time comes....We have experienced NO bugs/glitches/exploits.The game is very fun though, look passed the negative reviews, give it a fair 1-2 hour shot. You are always able to refund it if it's not your cup of tea. But /please/ consider giving it a fair chance and look passed the dramatic reviews! It's a great game with tons of content.-------------------- Review Edit (244 hrs) -> Optimization has gone down for me --------------------Still playing this game with groups of 2-8.The one thing I can see is that this game is still hard on the host. We have opted into a dedicated server so we can all get around 30 fps..This game is fun. It has great replay-ability and is a great game for groups. The game itself is beautiful if you have a PC strong enough to run settings well. I think that would be my only gripe with this game: It doesn't seem optimized very well. PC Spec update: I have a 8GB 3070, Ryzen 5600X CPU, and 32GB RAM and my FPS range between 15-50 in online play. If I'm hosting it is consistently 15 FPS and this is with most settings turned down. On the dedicated server I get around 30 average. Still haven't ran into any huge exploits or bugs, personally. Sometimes when trees burn down or nodes get mined they desync from the server and leave an invisible box, but that's about it.My friends still burn our base down so - LEARN THE THWACKER. I do recommend this game still, I'm just hoping optimization improves.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start by saying that I have enjoyed some of my time with this game so far (some, not all). But as much as I want to invite my friends to play this with me, I just cannot bring myself to recommend it to them. The game is basically an early access game, and if it had launched with the early access tag, I would probably not have nearly as many issues with it. But as this is a 'released' product, the state the game is in is unacceptable. Yes, the Devs have been releasing weekly updates - adding new missions, items, balancing, bug fixes. And once again, if this was an early access game, I'd be singing their praises for keeping up these weekly updates. However, as a released product that is advertising that they will be releasing 2 massive expansions at some point (each costing the same as the 'core game') it does not inspire confidence that even after 10 of these weekly updates, I still cannot recommend this game to friends. Especially knowing that I'm basically recommending them a $100 game as the biggest draw was the combination of the terraformed, earth-like biomes giving way to strange and alien biomes, only to learn that the alien biomes are going to be exclusive to the $30 expansions. This game has a lot of promise, but at this point it feels like that's all it has going for it. So if you are interested in Icarus, here's my recommendation: Wishlist it, keep an eye on it, if it goes heavily on sale, give it a try, but what I've experienced so far is definitely not worth $100 if the expansions are going to be more of the same. Or, go check out Valheim for half the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, I previously reviewed this game as "not recommended" and since then the developers have improved a lot of the worst aspects of the game. Initially, it was supposed to be an ultra-unforgiving "exoplanet Day-Z" survival game but I think we've all learned that "unforgiving" is synonymous with "not fun".It's much more playable now. I rage quit far less often even though the enemy AI is still some of the worst in the survival game scene. There's still no option to play on a dedicated server or to find public games, which is a shame for those of us who are the only one in our circle of friends who plays games like Icarus.I'd still like to see a better way to leave prospects that suck. The game gives you very little indication of what you're going to have to do or what is even available to you before landing. Some maps don't have deep ore deposits which lock you out of a lot of the tech tree unless you want to grind ore chunks for days (you don't). If you leave a prospect with gear behind and it isn't insured, it just sits in your station UI mocking you because, at least for me, you can't delete the gear or go back to the prospect to retrieve it. I've had a backpack sitting in limbo for a month.But it's FUN now. Parts of it are tedious and the combat is ... not really combat... but if you like building a base and the necessities to survive while having an overall goal to achieve, this is one of the best.
