_childDocuments_.review: ICARUS The Planet that wants you DeadIn the first lesson, I learned that oxygen comes from rocks, yeast comes from thistles and that if you admire the view for too long, bears will show up and attack you, mostly in pairs.About 30mins into Icarus, the new survival game from Day Z's Dean Hall and team, I had a moment. I'd just been brutally mauled by a pair of bears and had morosely jogged back over to my corpse from the respawn dropship several miles away. It was dark and also stormy, and there were wolf howling and tracking my ass. As I desperately search in the dark for my dead body and reclaim my pack, i relaised that I wasn't frustrated with having to walk all that way in dark, cold rain but I was completely immersed.As a part of the First Cohort you are the first to arrive on Icarus. Part-adventurer, part prospector, we drop alone and in groups, to conquer a brutal PvE world determined to wear you down or tear you apart.We can only drop to the surface with limited-time permits to harvest the planet's resources before returning to space. However those that get left behind are indeed lost forever.Fortunately, your employer, the United Development Agency, has furnished you with a protective spacesuit for your arrival on Icarus, a terraformed celestial body that's rich with natural resources. But, unfortunately, it can only stand up to a couple of swipes from a bear before you're left unconscious and bleeding out like a stuck pig.ICARUS is a clear session-based PvE survival game for up to eight co-op players or solo. The tech allows the instance to be hosted for a period of time so anyone can jump in an out, you dont have to wait for the host.Basicly (i can assume) that the instance is held in cloud and the prospector to jump in first picks up the host with the save happening almost instantainously, very clever.The Bottom Line:This is one of the better survival games, and I have not felt this invested in a new title since Mass Effect 3 was released. The graphics are beautiful, the environment is atmospheric, and the gameplay is smooth and balanced (after a few patches). I would personally say this is better than Ark (if I was to make a comparison), but I understand why this wouldn't be for most hardcore base-building survival nuts (7 days to die).  I’m also pleased with the urgency that the Dev teams respond to bugs and the overall community.,In short, I love this game but be warned it does have a little end game (at the time of writing) and gets a bit repetitive, but if that's your thing (it is mine), then you're in safe hands. Great graphics, blueprints, skills and actions will keep you wanting to drop back down to Icarus to level up and take on the hungry and unforgiving wildlife and weather.The GoodBeautifully crafted worldChallenging survival environmentsPlentiful blueprints, skills and actionsGreat building mechanicsCleaver cloud hosting CoOpThe BadVery unforgiving at the startSingle play (outpost mode) needs a lot of workNeeds more end game content!Full review here: Want to read more reviews or write one yourslef the head on over to

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR - The Dev's have made a U-turn and it now has Open World so it's a yes from me now.Previously:Consider this still a not quite so disappointed no and here's why:- It's like many other survival shooter style games - Rust/Ark/Minecraft/7DaysToDie/etc. but the SP enjoyment isn't much to go on, there's QoL done by giving a Solo tree now however it's still difficult as a SP- You have to level your character up to unlock skills and blueprints to increase your options and survivability chances BUT they are VERY limited points and thus you will waste skill points on skills you could have lived without - leading to a new character creation and starting over. At this time of update a Talent respec has been introduced and a few more points given however it is still extremely limited!- It has mission timers (no longer in Real Time but rather In-Game which is a massive improvement) but once you are dropped into the mission, if the timer expires your character is gone forever. You can use the drop pod to finish/fail the mission and save your character, and there's a RL 90 day timer once expires they're gone. Several missions now have an insurance policy but this is limited to only a few mission so losing a character is still possible. (It should be pointed out the Devs have mass res'd dead chars a few times now which is a good sport on their behalf)- Speaking of starting over, every mission you start with nothing except your skills and perks, no items (unless it changes in the future for the better), so this leads to an attitude of speed running, why build up a base and getting the good stuff when the bare minimum is all the is required/expected and you will lose everything at the end of the mission anyway, so why bother... (and still this continues to be the case - a minimal mud hut it is!)- The hunting game aspect of it is enjoyable for the most part BUT there's just things that don't add up. For example, the animals can have x-ray vision seeing through man-made structures such as blinds and hunting stands. We won't even mention the OP vertical cliff climbing bears...- The atmosphere, literally the atmosphere. It can definitely do with some visual improvements and some mechanic improvements but overall the idea is exactly what you'd expect from a terraforming project gone wrong. When a flash storm rolls through it is EPIC and survival mode really kicks in as you try to keep your hastily built el cheapo makeshift thatch hut from blowing away or a tree falling onto and crushing it. The mechanic for 'storms' doesn't factor in the intensity so even light winds or showers can damage buildings and kill you from exposure, this has improved somewhat over patches but still occurs (not including Bears that eat through concrete like it's paper) it's not making any sense whatsoever...- The Devs are responsive and updates now come every week or so, and speaking of updates, they tend to reinstall the whole game every time which is super frustrating...Overall a controversial game that you will sink time into if it's your jam but steer clear if it's not heavily on sale or you aren't into a game that leaves you painfully feeling like you have gotten nowhere at the end of a mission.Slight update, watch this space, the Devs have stated they are looking at changing the whole starting over repeatedly so will be interested in where they go and if Outposts actually become the staging point for missions. If so, I'll definitely be changing to recommend because it's the one thing that I will only change my review for.

_childDocuments_.review: Icarus really surprised me, in a good way, though it’s not without its flaws. At first, it feels like playing a mix of ARK, Rust and The Forest.One thing that stands out is the voxel-based system for mining and building destruction. Breaking ores and stone feels great, watching your pickaxe break through a vein of ore is so satisfying. While it’s not a game-changing feature, it does add a nice layer of immersion, and I wish more survival games would experiment with similar mechanics. If not the mining, definitely the base destruction. That said, the game’s performance and overall polish leave something to be desired. Animations can feel clunky, some mechanics are unintuitive, and bugs occasionally but rarely disrupt the experience. It’s clear the developers are working hard, though, with weekly updates adding new content and addressing issues regularly. Yes, weekly updates!There are currently 3 gamemodes, Open World, Missions and Outpost. Basically; Sandbox Survival, Missions and "Calm Base building survival".You can play with 3 difficulties being; Easy, Normal and Hard. Despite some flaws, Icarus is incredibly fun if you’re a fan of survival games. It’s got a lot of potential and it brings enough to the table to keep you hooked. Definitely recommend this, try it out!

_childDocuments_.review: While I'm a big fan of the survival genre and enjoyed this game in general, I really cannot recommend this game. Here is why:1. The lack of lore, explanation, and logic behind game mechanics.Let me put a few examples first:  a. You landed on the planet, built something, finished the mission and returned to orbit. The next time you land at the exact same spot, the buildings you built mysteriously disappear.  b. You're wearing an environment suit and breathing from the oxygen tank, but somehow you get pneumonia inside a cave because of the air in the cave.  c. Whoever sent you to the planet can afford the cost of a drop pod, fuel, and environment suit but cannot afford a single pickaxe or knife or axe. So you have to start empty-handed.  d. There is an objective, and the drop pod tries to send you to a location ~10km away from your objective.Trust me, a random magic world with dimension warp would make more sense explaining all the mechanisms above. It feels like the devs just want those mechanisms to be in this game and did not give a ♥♥♥♥ on making them convincing. 2. 50%+ of playtime is running.By running I mean literally running. For most survival games, you EXPLORE the environment and are rarely running. In Icarus, since all missions share the same big map, I found that most of the time, I was running through the place I already knew. There is nothing to explore, no random events/resources/creatures, no need of gathering stuff, just plain running. And it feels like the whole purpose of running is to lengthen the playtime because, again, there is no lore or logic in it.3. Growth of the character feels meaningless very soon.Most of the talents are percentage increase in something. That is boring, and doesn't feel I'm progressing. Most of the talents I get are those increase moving speed. Blueprints are exciting at first, but soon you'll discover that most blueprints are useless - namely, all those from tier 3 and 4. Tier 3 and 4 blueprints require an insane amount of resources. Since you get reset every time and start bare-handed, there is no point in putting so much effort into tier 3 and 4. By the time you unlock them, you'll finish the prospect already if you choose to go straight into the mission. The workshop items are nice but the only they do is to save your first 10 minutes of resource gathering and base building. I think there should be more, like some game-changing or playstyle defining workshop items.4. It should be an EA title.Apart from the points mentioned above, there are still some important parts missing, like the ability to respec talents/blueprints, the variety of prospects, and the variety of creatures. The game feels like a game mechanism demonstrating prototype in current state. I would say that it still needs at least a year of polishing.

_childDocuments_.review: What other game have you played where the developers release a small content updates and fixes every week for over two years and counting?  *crickets* yeah... none.  Devs also have a list of requested features with the community upvoting them and then implementing most all of them over the last two years.  Where else are you going to find that?The DLC's are not required by any means and are purely cosmetic.  They have zero "pay-to-win" and don't have add any mechanics that are added from them.  You're not missing out on anything by not buying them.  The only ones I would recommend are the new large maps as they add new very large areas to explore and missions associated with them.  The base map is very large however and you don't need them. I've played Icarus from day 1 and the improvements and addons/fixed they've made to this game have been amazing, thoughtful, and meaningful.  This is one of my favorite survival crafting games I've ever played.  You find a little bit of anything you want here in the survival genre:-Timed objectives where you need to kill/retrieve/build something--check-Open world building and exploring at your own pace and taking missions from the main mission list on your own time--check-Purely building with little to no threats just for fun--checkIf you like survival crafting I'd give this game a shot.  No other developer has had the dedication and care towards their project like this one.

But end of the day its your money if you gonna buy it at its full set price then go right ahead, can't stop yah.Now there is more bad stuff within and even some good stuff i would like to speak on but that be large list and this is a free weekend review that doesn't even count to the total steam review % after all, so instead to shorten this review but still give some details about the game here are the three biggest main issues i had with the game. 1. Being not balanced. I played on the open world mode on normal what is set to as default. But the problem lies that this game at least on normal seems more hard then anything when you begin. Every thing that wants to kill you, your not able to even run away, in fact i found this out the hard way not even 4 mins into the game as i was collecting the starting sticks and stones off the floor not even that far from the drop pod i was attacked even spite running away, they always keep up with you and go slightly faster then your sprint, since i just started had no weapons and sure enough this outcome of not able to get away happened another 7 times before i finally not only had a base to hide from the outside danger, but a weapons to fight back only to find its still hard to kill, few times near inches from death. It really is a kill or be killed world.Now the easy mode difficulty does address this issue of the world being pretty much overpowering you by decreasing their moment speed, but the reason i didn't really play on easy as it also just -% the spawn rates of some things i would perfer to still be in the game to still be challenge, in fact it seems to really dumb down the game, so much thats its too easy for a survival game. At that point you might as well go play a life sim instead seeing how even those games will let you build and farm etc without survival elements. There really is some bad balance on going in this game even down to the crafting recipes.2. DX12 version sucks in performance wise it even states its recommend for RTX 3070 or better cards i have a 4070 so not massively far off from the same performances as a 3070 yet it runs like crap, even with DLS on it hardly made a impact, its so near unplayable, so i see why some steam reviews i've seen mention bad performances have come from. However picking to launch the game in DX 11 yields no issue at all, in fact it was super smooth even ran it at max settings for everything it works far more flawlessly, showcasing their is some major issue or bug on going with the game in DX 12 mode. They need to fix this, as after all its something they should of made sure was working before opening their game to this free to play weekend.3. Oxygen management! Accuse me! The forest zones look extremely very breathable to me, many plants and even animals are surviving without having to mine ore to take in oxygen, so why should i? I can understand other zones of the map like even the desert area but both these look extremely breathable. Seems weird add to the game, as pointed out it doesn't make sense. I understand its meant to be a sci-fi game after all but most of these animals our not sci-fi, they are animals we have Bears Wolfs Deer etc. But as told it seems not necessary and should be changed to were you don't have to deal with that in those two areas of the map but need it for other zones. Hope the game keeps on improving and kind thanks to RocketWerkz team for even doing this free to play weekend. Something that normally only always online paid games do more then these kinda of games, you really didn't have to but you did anyways.

_childDocuments_.review: It's definitely something one can put a lot of hours into. There's a ton of content and they continue to update it WEEKLY, which is just incredible. Sometimes it's just patch fixes but most of the time, there's new content of some form at least every month if not more. WHAT I LIKE ABOUT IT:* The crafting - there's a ton of crafting stations, though thankfully, they recently combined tiers so we don't have to have one of every tier anymore, which saves space. The way I have to craft this here and then bring it over there to craft it into something else makes it feel more immersive, more real. I like that they tell us where it's crafted from in the tech tree so we don't have to search every station. * The building - I love that we can change the building material on already placed. That's huge. We don't have to completely rebuild the base to change the material it's made of. I like that there's a wide variety of materials to use. There's at least 10 different materials to use and interchange. * The combat - There's a decent variety of weapons and each can be made stronger through talents. No weapon is left behind. They're all equally valid choices depending on the fight and your playstyle. * The graphics - it's a visually stunning game. Aside from access to water, I consistently see "the view" as the most important feature of a base location recommended by fellow players. * The music - it doesn't get repetitive like many games. It's subtle and I like that it changes drastically the moment you enter combat, whether you realize it or not which is often what helps me realize I'm about to be attacked. The nighttime music is ultra creepy and I hate it but it's fitting. * The talents (though I wish we had more so I could spec into more things) and the tech tree (which we do get the opportunity to spec into most of since we continue to psudeo-level even after hitting 60. (We level up and get more tech tree points but not more talents or actual levels.)* The gameplay types and difficulty settings - I like that we can adjust the difficulty settings on each mission and prospect but I wish we could continue to change them once we create and enter the prospect. I like that I can take a break from Open World where we primarily focus on expanding and upgrading our base(s), and go do missions either in the world where our base is, or on a new one. * The workshop gear - it can make it much easier to do missions later on. We can skip the early grind and go straight into the later game items that we're used to. I like that I can call down equipment from my missions or open worlds. WHAT COULD IMPROVE:* The crafting - please, can we craft from containers? That would be so helpful. Some items are used in too many recipes, in my opinion. Epoxy, for example. It's resource intensive to make and then is needed in great quantities in many end game recipes. It gets frustrating.* The building - why are there half pieces that we can't attach anything to? How does this make sense? Why I can't make the walls 1.5 high instead of having to make them 2 high? I hate that it relies on where I'm standing to place the item. It's not as bad as other games in this regard, but it's still a factor and I hate it. I want to just point. Put it there, please and thank you. * The combat - why can wolves attack me through the wall or floor (if you have a raised building) but I can't hit them back? How is this still a thing so many years after launch? Honestly. The mobs can hit me from WAY far away when I can't even reach them. I've learned to work around these issues as has everyone else but we shouldn't have to. This is an established game, not a new release of an Early Access game. These types of glitches shouldn't happen. * The workshop - the fact that we can lose our gear that we "paid for" is just awful. It's easy to accidentally leave something on a mission and be unable to retrieve it again. The "insurance" is a huge ripoff since we lose so much by using it and we have to wait 5 REAL LIFE days to get the items back. That's just asinine. That's just making it unnecessarily complicated and frustrated for no real purpose. I hate that items have to be in our inventory or the drop pod to successfully return to the station. They can't be equipped. This is also dumb and serves no purpose other than to make things more frustrating. *The food spoils too quickly, both in my bags and in the gardens. There are methods for preventing spoiling of food in my bags and containers but the only way to prevent it in the gardens is speccing far down a talent tree I otherwise wouldn't use.* Stop crashing every other hour like an early Early Access game!! Seriously. There's no excuse for a game of this age to crash as often as it does. No other game I play crashes as much as this one. If it doesn't crash, it glitches out and I have to log out and log back in to fix it. Very annoying. Overall, I really like the game but sometimes it drives me mad.

_childDocuments_.review: Sooooooooooooooo where to begin? I'll start at the beginning. Icarus first came out as a terrible game. I mean TERRIBLE. So terrible in fact I refunded the game after an hour. Missions sucked, no open-world concept, and no direction on what to do/how to play. This beautiful game was horribly overshadowed by its unoptimized crap fest going on with what it did to your pc while playing (my 3060 overheated on low settings). It was bad.Fast forward to today. The game is even better looking than before (not by much but still better) and it runs much better. The Dev team does weekly updates FOR FREE and add new content FOR FREE all the time. Now yes, they do add some DLC content that does seem a bit odd but nothing is pay to get ahead (it's a survival game with no PVP game mode) and honestly I'm good with shelling out money to this team to get some cool stuff to support them. There are still problems with the game, such as the rock loading instance that just got fixed (over 2 years later), BUT overall this has been the best 400 hours and counting I've gotten out of a game in a long time. Never-ending fun and it has multiplayer with dedicated server hosting capabilities. What's not to love?All in all, I give Icarus a 9/10 for the experience and fun I've had overall. Keep it up devs, I can't wait for the next update to see what you bring to the table.

_childDocuments_.review: I've followed this game through its development since day 1, but I haven't been able to play it due to its awful optimization until 3 GPU upgrades and a CPU upgrade later, every single one of which qualified for their minimum requirements to run the game. I now own a GeForce RTX 3060 and a Ryzen 9, but still struggle to maintain the game at 45 let alone 60 fps. Their discord which is supposed to offer a connection to the devs and updates on the roadmap is a mess, which went from being frequent and friendly notes on the work being done and the ideas coming to fruition, to now where it is just a venting chat where the devs complain about being behind and responding to any customer feedback with a "but do you know how much that costs?", also don't even consider criticizing or requesting anything for the game as apparently the game has another group of obsessive fans who won't let criticism slide and will rapidly swarm your chat with talks about the game being perfect in every way like it isn't a buggy mess of an early access game. As someone whose addicted to survival games I instinctively fell in with this game, but beyond the standard survival experience that this game offers and a kinda unique roguelite mission mode, there isn't much to be said. Content wise it gave me some heavy deja vu with the gameplay loop of ark, which for some games is a good thing, but not for this one. I really can't recommend this game unless you are truly desperate for a kinda new survival experience. I hope the devs stop with whatever they are doing cause the game is one optimization update and a little bit of dev transparency away from offering something genuinely unique and fun to play. But honestly, in this day and age, I just kinda expect this to turn into another dead survival game collecting dust in the hidden section of my steam library, hopefully i'm wrong.

_childDocuments_.review: Dull and boring after only a few hours. Completely unbalanced weapons, no point taking anything but a Bow or Gun. Combat is boring, and there's only 2 enemy types (reskinned into about 5 or 6). Enemies are such damage sponges and deal so much damage that the only way to beat them is to cheese them by standing on a rock or a building, so teching up is mostly pointless too since you can kill things from your rock regardless of weapon. Missions are all variations of "go here and collect this", and with no combat challenge or skill involved gets very repetitive very quickly.Devs are actively working on the game and doing weekly updates, but not touching the game's core issues. I'm sure eventually this will be a good game, and I'll be keeping an eye out until it is. But right now, I would steer solidly clear.(Review was originally positive after 3-4 hours; a shame that it got so boring so quickly!)Update: Reinstalled the game and tried it again, 40+ updates after I last uninstalled. Hopeful that with multiple fixes and changes, the game had gotten to a playable state.Boy was I disappointed. It still has the same issues; the performance has improved *slightly* but even with a powerful computer, still runs at an average of 45fps with massive frame drops in many situations. Combat is still tedious and you're mostly forced into ranged combat, most weapons are pointless, hitboxes (after the update) are still incredibly wonky. If an animal starts an attack animation, it's probably going to hit you even if you arent in the same spot anymore. Bears are bizarrely much easier than wolves or scorpions because you can abuse the physics to dodge their charges. __Do not buy this game - it's disappointing and a waste of your money. This phrase gets thrown around a lot, but this game genuinely does still feel like an Alpha__It's a hot mess that could be fantastic if the devs fixed the core mechanics and stopped introducing new "features" that aren't even relevant to a lot of the gameplay, but it seems like they have some fundamental issues they either can't or don't want to fix. Huge letdown, there's a product manager / producer somewhere who should be incredibly embarrassed that after 40+ updates the game is still in this state.

_childDocuments_.review: Icarus, the survival game I scoped out since release but never purchased. I held off on this one at first due to lukewarm reviews and later due to the cost of the experience (if you include Styx and Prometheus in that equation).That said, I'm glad I did finally pick this game up and I would recommend it to fans of the genre, but in particular people, like me, who really enjoy the early portion of survival games. The mission-based part of the game (the original part that many people did not like) is basically repeatedly starting over with nothing (a bit of a rogue like experience) and as you progress you do get to bring more things down with you that you purchase with meta currency that you are earning on each mission. This gives purpose to constantly restarting and the missions also give finite objectives for each "game".I've enjoyed the mission bit enough that I haven't even started the other types of games (which you can run concurrently) including open world (more like a classic survival experience with some of the elements from the mission based game mode), and outpost (like a peaceful building option). The same character can run all 3 types of games at once from what I gather which is neat. You don't bring things between the modes but you keep your talents and research unlocks.Basically, TLDR, I think this one is a must buy if you like the start of survival games especially and if you like the idea of a rogue-like survival game :) It does everything else pretty well and the storms definitely make survival more interesting, but I'd say the biggest difference is the sort of meta game of missions and unlocks. They also seem to be really active (weekly?) in content updates.

_childDocuments_.review: At the risk of sounding like a dramatic fanboi, I LOVE this game.  I've spent 400+ hours playing and loving Valheim and THOUSANDS doing the same in Minecraft.  This game is leagues better than both in literally every dynamic I can think of.  At the time of this review writing I have logged 23.9 hours of gameplay.  I bought this game 72 hours ago.  It's primarily what I do when I'm not sleeping or working. Now to come off my fanboi vibe, I will say I hope DESPERATELY that we can still expect patches in the near future.  There are some troubling things in the performance department.  DX12 and RTX performs horribly.  Unplayable.  Which is ok because it's still incredibly beautiful on DX11 without RTX.  The game also stutters a lot when it seems it shouldn't be.  For example I run a Ryzen 9 3900X with 32GB of 3600MHz ram and a RTX2080ti GPU.  The game only spins the GPU up to roughly 70% usage, CPU rarely peeks over 40% and there's loads of available ram yet the engine still stutters quite a bit.  It's not game breaking, but it is immersion disturbing.  There's also the issue with the way the shadows draw in.  It feels incredibly backwards to me.  They STOP drawing in at approximately 50% of the view distance.  Everything outside that range is just lit up bright as can be with no shadow at all.  It's wildly disorienting.  EDIT: Not long after writing this there was a game patch and the shadow weirdness seems to have disappeared.  THAT WAS QUICK AS HECK.Those two annoyances disturbing the immersion will NOT stop me from playing this incredibly fun and immersive survival sim.  I especially love the ROGUELITE nature they implemented with nothing being any more permanent than 30 days except your research, tech and talents.  And you can even lose that if you aren't exceptionally careful!Devs I hope I can count on you to keep working on performance and that shadow weirdness because I'd never miss a DLC or game from this group again!  SO GOOD!

_childDocuments_.review: Icarus now has its complete roster of modes that cater to most groups of players. Missions: TIMED expeditions that take you to different parts of the map completing objectives for payouts when done. You are paid in a currency that can be used to purchase unique equipment that give you a headstart in your next mission. They cannot be repaired (to my knowledge) and will break eventually. Some things break, others dont. Play the game to find out.Outposts: This is a sudo-creative mode with respawning materials while the world itself stays persistent. There are no time restraints in this mode so dropping in and out at your leisure is fine. There are no world bosses and you are constrained to a very small portion of the map. The main purpose of this mode now is to experiment with builds and the game itself while being in a relatively safe environment. Open World: IMO, this mode is the pinnacle of Icarus. You are given the entire map whether it be Olympus or Styx and it stays as a persistent world/save. You can also have multiple worlds/saves in the Open world mode at the same time. This mode throws the whole game at you and with a persistent world, your time investment  stays unlike missions. There are world bosses as well so there are many things you can craft here that you cant in the outposts mode. Cons:The game is gorgeous but it needs to be MAXED out in graphics to be gorgeous. Problem with that is the extreme graphics demand the game has. Its VERY hard to run at medium to high settings for some reason. Im on a 5800x | 2070super build so i also have access to DLSS and while it runs well, it doesnt run as well as i think it COULD. The performance issues were far more severe at launch so it has been getting addressed but it needs just a bit more. Game also has alot of pop-in. I HATE POP IN.Great game and overall and underrated name in the Survival Genre. Devs are crazy releases weekly updates with a dedicated blogpost for each one too. I recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: Icarus is a great game that I have played since the beta. When I first played, I remember thinking how hard it was and compared to the game today it really was too hard. At that time and I remember being so happy when I made it to level 4! I had died so much from the brutality of the infamous bears that when they sensed you, there was nothing you could do and you were basically gonna die. The weather was unforgiving too and it was almost impossible to survive. Every time you died you had an xp penalty that set you back from progression to the next level. It was hard. The game had real world timers which was unique to the genre at the time. It made you actually pay attention to a set amount of days in real life and gave you a sense of urgency to get that mission done. If you didn't log in or make it back to your drop ship in time you would lose your prospector to permadeath and you would have to start a new character and try again and hopefully not die.  It was a neat idea that just didn't go over well with the community due to real life not allowing players to get back to the game in time.      Well that was the old Icarus. The timers have changed to in-game timer so now your mission continues when the host logs in. And now with over 80 plus updates that we received every week, the dev team has done an excellent job listening to the community and working on the game and it shows. It really has improved tremendously. I would recommend this game to anyone who likes survival games. Or anyone new to survival, it's a great game to try.  It has a lot of great crafting and building mechanics and a great resource gathering system. You can play solo or play with up to 7 friends to get prospects done faster. It has open world where you can build and stay on Icarus as long as you want with no time limit which many players like. No more running on foot everywhere, you can now tame mounts to ride and it has a big talent tree that you can choose what type of survivor you want to be. If you play solo it has your own solo talent tree that is added to base talents for better chance of survival. The ambiance and ire sound of the game is pleasant to the ears too. The weather is very unstable and it's like Icarus is trying to consume you and sometimes it gets you, but the Exotics will keep you coming back for more.      To understand more about this game I recommend watching the live action Icarus short films named Icarus: No Rescue, Icarus: Fatal Sky and then Icarus The Seeker that you can find easily on the tube. It will explain a bit of lore and give you an idea of what it means to be a prospector. Icarus has only barely been explored... 9/10 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't get why this game isn't bigger than it is. Probably the best survival game out there, and it gets better every week. My favorite in-game memory involves my brother and I spending a whole day preparing for our first trip into the deep arctic. We crafted warm gear, enough building materials for a remote base, tamed pack animals, the whole kit. We started out at dawn, and made good progress, wandering aimlessly looking for a decent spot to settle. Then it all started to go terribly wrong. The buffalo carrying the building supplies fell down a ravine and died. I fell in after it and broke my leg. We limped along, picking off wolves and avoiding anything larger. Then it got dark. And cold. And it started to snow. We threw up a little shack and a fire and tried to keep warm. Then the howling and skittering started. We held them off the best we could, but by dawn my brother was dead, and I starved soon after. Hours of prep and planning amounted to nothing except maybe the most tense fun I've ever had in a survival game.

_childDocuments_.review: I am changing my old review from a negative one to a positive one.The main problem i had with this game when i bought it yesterday was its stuttering and hitching in the main branch of the game. I looked up solutions online and found some advice that helped a bit but still didnt do enough to really fix the problem. Then i wrote the old review where i did not recommend the game stating how it is the main reason that ruins the experience for me since there is no point in having a beautiful game if it freezes every 10-20 seconds taking you out of the immersion. Then a developer of the game responded to the review suggesting me to try the experimental branch since they are currently testing it for the exact problem im having which is stuttering and hitching, and sure enough after trying it the problem is now almost completely gone. It still isnt fully stutter free as i would like it to be but it is such an improvement that the game went from feeling unbearable to very enjoyable. I now have very short stutters about every minute or so and i will tell some advice on making the game run as smoothly as it can. 1. Close every backround app2. Set its priority to high in the Details section of your Task Manager (CTRL+ALT+DELETE)3. Right click icarus on steam, go to the beta tab and select the experimental branch4. Install and run ISLC (Intelligent Standby List CleanerDoing all of these things helped me from stuttering every 10 seconds for about half a second to about once a minute for about a fifth of a second.Icarus is a very beautiful open world survival crafting game with a lot of care and attention in many aspects that other games seem to neglect. The user interface is one of the best i have ever seen and the soundtrack is like a Carbon Based Lifeforms soundtrack with a bit of synth in it to give it a nice identity. Here is how the game works,Gamemodes      -Missions where a corporation you work for sends you to the planet to preform different tasks, you can build and do everything you can in the open world gamemode but completing a mission and extracting will give you a payout which can then be used to buy armor, weapons, equipment and building pieces from the organisation you work for to bring to other missions or the open world.       -Open world where you choose what to take with you and where on the planet you choosing where you start, afterwards doing pretty much what you want, trying to survive and thrive.      -Outposts where you spawn in with no threat and just buildCharacterWhen you start you will create and name your own character. Your character has skill trees for different things such as combat, survival, building, ect... but also comes with a tech tree where you unlock new recipes which come in tiers. The higher your characters level the higher tier tech tree you can unlock. Then there is the workshop where you can spend the money and exotic resources you can earn from missions to unlock new equipment bought from the organisation you work for. GameplayYou land on the planet with nothing or equipment you can bring with you if you have purchased any, if you are in a mission you will get your objective told to you by a man working for the organisation. Your job is then to gather the equipment and consumables you will need in order to complete the mission or if you are in the Open World game mode survive and thrive. There are basic needs such as oxygen food and water, different kinds of injuries many types of different enemies to encounter and quite a nice selection of weapon types, melee and ranged. The game has a stealth system and also includes swimming above and under water, where you can also hunt for resources or food. While the combat is basic it is actually very fun, enemies have weak spots and there are sneak damage multipliers rewarding patient gameplay.Developers The game is updated weekly with every update also having beautiful artwork to go with it. The developers are very helpful and have a section on discord with FAQ which i recommend checking out if you are confused about anything. A new DLC just came out which is apparently very good.  It adds a new map with many new items, creatures and missions but i have not played the DLC yet. My personal experience with the dev team in the one day ive had to know this game has been very positive.Final ThoughtsIf you are looking for a survival crafting game with a great aesthetic and quite deep mechanics with an interesting story and lore that receives regular updates and you dont mind that the game currently has some performance issues i would definitely recommend Icarus.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: After the separation of the solo and regular talent trees, the implementation of the respec system, as well as the stability fixes in Week 13, I'm editing my review accordingly and can now say I recommend this game in its current form. The developers seem to be going in the right direction to balance and help the game evolve, which is rare these days.After the Week 11 update, I am now stuck behind a map boundary that I cannot cross, otherwise the game crashes instantly. As such, in its current state (at least for me) it is unplayable and I am unable to complete my prospect. After looking at the Community forums, it is evident that this is a widespread issue for other players in other parts of the map.Progression to me is pretty straightforward, although no more talents after Level 40 also seems a bit odd to me. As a solo player, you're almost obligated to go into the Solo talent tree to start, as the buffs it gives you are pretty huge, and you get 6 extra blueprint points pretty early on. After that, you can only get bits and pieces from other trees unless you hard focus on one.Fluidity of graphics is also pretty choppy, whether you're on DX11 or 12. Having everything set to medium on an RTX 2070, I experience sporadic frame drop from time to time.The game is fun and pretty easy to pick up. But until the widespread crashing is addressed and fixed, and maybe after a bit of optimization, I cannot safely recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Icarus is a mediocre survival-focused build/craft roguelite game. Some have experienced some major bugs but I have only experienced very minor bugs. What intrigued me the most about this game was the roguelite gameplay loop of going down to the planet, completing objectives, returning to space, getting paid and buying upgrades...repeat. What I found was that most of the upgrades that you can purchase are not really upgrades but shortcuts instead. Survival suits or modules are upgrades. Those give defense or movement speed or resource efficiency upgrades (water container slots for example). A pick axe or knife that you can start with instead of crafting a very similar one is just a time saver instead of what I would call a true upgrade.The missions are fun if not a little generic but I like the idea of working through a mission web that gives the player choice on what kind of task they want to complete. One bad thing about the missions is that many of them do not tell you what you need to complete a mission. They just give a circle on the map to go to. You go to the middle of nowhere to some circle in the arctic zone and they're like, "Hey now build a barracks with 6 beds, a pot belly stove and a kitchen station". Why don't you tell me that from the get-go? Very annoying to have to make the long run back to base to make all the necessary items and return again.I like progression in games. Multi-tiered progression is what I love. A tech tree + talents + workshop "upgrades" + mission web to work through checks all the boxes for me. However, I recently hit level 41 and discovered that you do not receive talent points after level 40. I do not know if you receive tech points beyond level 40 but I have more than enough of those points to get all the things I want. The tech tree was great till I had all the stuff I wanted, so no more real progression there. No more talent points AND no ability to respec, so that progression has ended. The workshop upgrades are very minor and, imo, the upgrades do not really justify most of the effort to get them. That leaves the mission web. The mission web shows progression but it feels similar to when you play something like Fallout 3 where the level cap is low and you feel like you have barely scratched the surface of character progression but there are a lot of missions, quests and exploration to go. At this point, my character takes the back seat and that is very unfulfilling to me.Last real negative thing. Exp penalty for dying. I don't mind being punished for dying, I actually prefer it. How the exp penalty works in this game is that you have to regain ALL experience that you have received in a given level upon death. For example if you are 5k exp into level 21 and you die, you have to regain that 5k exp before progressing further in that level. If you are 20k exp into level 21 and you die, you have to regain 20k exp before progressing further in that level. I died when almost level 35 and basically had to redo the whole level over again (100k exp plus if I remember right). It is a ridiculous penalty.I would have a hard time giving this a thumbs down because I want to encourage the devs to keep improving their game. I do think it has a great foundation to become a much better game than it is. The game costs 30 bucks and I can say that I have played about 46 hours at time of writing this so. I am only recommending this game because, generally speaking, I had a fun time and if I focus mostly on the cost per hour ratio of fun, this game was worth it. If limited character progression doesn't stand in your way, this might be a game you are interested in.

_childDocuments_.review: I love OWSC. I bounce from title to title, and typically find that the majority are good, but also since they're in EA, they're jank as f***. Originally when I saw Icarus announced, I was hyped, based on what I saw in the teasers and trailers. Then I learned it was mostly broken on arrival, poorly reviewed, and the idea of roguelike survival didn't actually appeal to me.During one of the past steam sales, this game popped up again. I was surprised and excited to learn it added an Open World sandbox component, giving it a more traditional feel. It didn't immediately click with me and I put it aside. I think the biggest issue I have is the weird disconnect between what I'm doing on the planet, and where I came from to get here. You're telling me that I can be sent to a different, terraformed planet, but when I get there I have to cobble tools together with the loose stone and twigs I find laying around? It introduces so much dissonance that it's really hard not to feel silly building a thatch structure next to a pristine landing pod with all sorts of tech.With that being said: suspend your disbelief. Eventually I just threw up my arms and said "forget the space side". It's gone a lot further in aiding my enjoyment of this game. I'm able to appreciate the building and gathering system, both of which are very well done. Like Rust, but improved. The hunting actually feels really good, but I couldn't explain why. Where this game seems to really shine, so far, is in the progression/tech trees. I actually think they've nailed a perfect balance of experience and skills. There's a depth here that isn't exceedingly overdone, but just enough to spruce up the whole survival experience. I especially enjoy the various wounds and infections you can get, and the myriad ways to treat them.I have not played the mission structured version of the game, nor do I think I plan to. With both Palworld and Enshrouded leaving a lot to be desired, if you're looking for something a bit different but still the same to the existing flock of OWSC games, I do recommend picking this up!

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could recommend this game, I really do. I was so excited when I first found it and played in many of the betas. But unfortunately,  the fact that I can go for twenty minutes without seeing an animal, then all of a sudden boom, 10 wolves jumping me from all angles (and don't get me started on the 'bear out with it's wolf mates' spawn) makes this less a survival game and more a 'am I going to be lucky today' game.  The fact that every type of creature all just drops 'meat' also means it's pretty much pointless having anything but the predators in the game, as there is no benefit to hunting deer etc. when the swarms of wolves are easily enough to keep me 'fed'. I get that the predators are there to make the game challenging, but after my hundredth and something wolf kill in an area measuring km across at best and a couple of hours of game play, the feeling of realism is gone.Then there are the extermination missions. Only managed to play the first one, because I'm playing solo so the boss is impossible to kill. I've filled it with dozens of arrows, but then it runs off, spawns seemingly unlimited waves of minions, and recovers most of the health I've managed to whittle off it. All while being faster than me and able to wound me within one or two hits and shrugging off the fact it's got so many arrows sticking out of it I'm not sure whether I'm now hunting a porcupine.And that's ignoring the fact there are weather storms every five minutes so I have to go hunker down in a little 1x1 box near the boss area to not die of exposure IN A SPACE SUIT! Travel to another world they said... die from light rain exposure because corporations don't believe in the slightest bit of thermal insulation.No real aliens (other than the again infinitely respawning worms in the caves that are giant pain in the ass that offer no rewards), no real alien vegetation, nothing that actually makes this sci-fi. It's such a missed opportunity for something that could have been absolutely great.

_childDocuments_.review: I was in absolute love with this game. Playing every single day. I put 46.5h in just 1 week, pretty much.Still, I don't recommend it. Why? Because they have decided to suddenly add armor durability. Game has been released since 3 Dec 2021, NOW they decided to add this. To a game that is already extremely grindy to reach certain parts of the technology. To me, it's just a very bad decision. We already have to craft and deal with a lot of stuff, it feels like a great survivability. Then suddenly, BAM, yet another thing to worry about. Requires resources to fix the armor as well, it isn't just "fix and be done with it" like in Valheim.I like that they removed the time limits being based in real life, helps with the grindiness and rush you'd feel of having to hurry everything up but, still, it doesn't make sense.I love that they release pretty much every week with new content. But this just misses the mark for me.Every time you drop into a mission, you have to start from scratch, grind everything back up, no matter the mission. So the game in itself is already very grindy each mission to reach your technology level again. And now, deal with armor durability as well.Now, to be fair, you don't need to reach max level technology every single mission, there are missions where just reaching Tech 2 is enough. But if you wanna farm exotics and what not? You WILL have to reach  at least T3. So you will be forced to go into the "extreme" grind again. And now every time you get into combat, you'll have to fix your armor, which means you will have to go back to your base to do so,  and depending where you are, it's just a huge hassle.I think the main issue is that the developers are putting more and more barriers for us and forcing us to have to grind stuff out but still haven't resolved the transportation problem.  Transportation can be unlocked at T2.Also, this game should have NEVER been released as a supposedly full game. This was and still is, in Early Access. They are pumping a lot of content, which is good but it just feels deceitful. And they really have to fix the core issues before trying to add more grindy stuff that we have to worry about.------------------ EDITED REVIEW after Mounts update ------------------- Mounts are barely useful. The Moa is slower than you and the Buffalo is like a donkey but more annoying because you can't use shortcuts such as ladders to transverse mountains because the Buffalo will stay behind, meaning that you'll have to waste a lot of time going around stuff and EVERY single predator will try to attack it, even when you're busy in caves so your pet will die when you're doing other stuff.- The grind on T3/T4 is incredibly frustrating. This game is, 100%, to be played with other people. Unfortunately, it sticks the middle finger to anyone doing it solo, such as myself. Imo, the game should have everything for solo and then just do a multiplier in resources required and other stuff, based on the amount of players in a session. - I still can't recommend this game to anyone. I've tried selling the concept to a couple of friends but it's always a bust. The idea of just wasting your time on T3/T4 to then have it reset every single mission, is very off putting to most people. I know it's the whole concept of the game but maybe if the grind wasn't this big, it wouldn't be much of a hassle and this is even with things from the workshop.My recommendations are: - Fix the immense grind required (if you still want to keep this a "reset every mission"). - Have better / faster mounts. How can a single wolf or boar attack my Buffalo? That would never happen, stop with the incessant attacks, especially if I'm not around my mount and can't defend it.- Have a way to reset the Tech tree, especially as you move on later in levels because you get stuff from the workshop and some points on the Tech tree are rendered useless.- Have the Beacon much earlier in the tech tree, it's a huge complication to have to remember where everything is.------------------ EDITED REVIEW after Open World update ------------------I can now safely say that I recommend this game. After adding Open World, it's basically everything this game needed. I've played it and I've thoroughly enjoyed it. Yes, it lacks some content / purpose on the Open World but, it's 100% the way to go.The Tech Tree was a MAJOR issue, having to grind to T3/T4 every single mission to farm Exotics was incredibly time consuming and not respectful of my time playing, at all. Now with Open World and not losing bases, it's done :) None of my previous complaints are a problem now.I now recommend this to everyone and have been pushing it to have more friends coming to play.

Go back to his original character, log into his mission and continue on. And now the friend who shared his mission reward can now do the same on yours. All rewards are shared among all your characters on your account. Meaning you don't get x3 because you have 3 characters, you get same amount that any of of your characters can use to spend in workshop which is in your space port for benefits to items and gear and weapons and tools and bring those into your next mission. There is so much more you can do having this feature. There is open world endless mining, hunting, building, farming, fishing and so much more. Graphics are amazing, we get a patch every week for the last 105 weeks and they don't miss a week, and there are much more to come. The maps are absolutely insane and huge! also you can do missions which is separate from your open world but you can also do other missions in your open world too, There are rare exotics to farm to get even greater rewards which can be gained in open world and mission story games, oh and there are outpost missions as well. Team up with up to 8 players per game, or risk it all and do it solo. Build traps, Want to build a base super high up a tree, yes that's right Tree houses, Side of mountain or cliffs edge, over water or just out in the open. Or go into the Lava area and find the extreme creatures and new Boss. Also make sure you can handle the heat, you just might die trying to survive or get eaten by Giant Spiders. I have nearly 1,000 hours and I'm still having and endless blast at this game, And you can even take your chances in Promethius map and enter the Swamp, oh yes, Toxic everything there, Before you think your alright your running for your life, and this isn't just in swamp but every area of this game. Food buffs, Tech tree which is huge, Perk buffs which are chosen differently between each of your characters, each one has to level up and choose how you want them to be, for instance A builder class, hunters class, Traveling class and so much more on top of that as well. Did something wrong, can reset some stats and redirect them what you rather have. These developers have road maps weekly, they have a discord and they get involved. I can go on an on about what there is to do, but you should play it and you will learn the more interesting things. Remember just when you thought you was safe. You learn of a new interesting creature about to give you reason to run fast far and do what ever it takes to survive.  I love 7 days to die, but this Blows that away. I have a lot of survival games but this one is top notch the best Ever!

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game, I mean I really really want to like it, but this game does more to just shoot itself in the foot than most other survival games.  The problem is every good thing you can say about it, is immediately followed by a but.....So let's review.Story wise, forget it.  Unless you watched the videos there's literally nothing that tells you why you're on the planet doing what your doing.  Honestly I'm 100% ok with this.  Not every game needs to have a story to tag along with it.  Basically it was a terraform project gone wrong.  Again not a big deal.Visually this game is extremely pretty to look at.  All the biomes look extremely well done, every little detail is pretty close to real life, darkness is literally pitch black that no gamma can save and that's a good thing.  You shouldn't be able to see in front of you without a light or torch.   Buttttttt.......can your machine run this monster.  I'm running a 3060, i9, 64ram and this game chugs my machine.  You can tweak the settings and stabilize it a bit, but then you lose out on why this game looks good.The leveling system is ok.  Everything you do gives xp, which again, is a good thing.  Picking up a scrub?  XP.  Kill an animal?  XP!  Leveling gives you blueprint points which let's you build new items and talent points for your character which makes you better at X skills in the game.   Some talents are so worthless they beg the question why are they in the game.  Once you learn the game, it's almost guaranteed you make a new character to spec the right way.  Literally if it's not mining points, you did it wrong.  There's a solo tree which has no business being there because of the next point.  Update, talent points were given back, but the initial patch only gives you 30 back, you buy the rest, so it's getting there.Solo to coop.  I've only played this with another person and I have to assume if you had 8 people that could play this, then I bet this games true potential shines.  I can't see how anyone could play this solo.  The material needs alone would kill a person.Which brings us to the next stop.  Materials.  Using those blue print points you get to make cooler looking stuff along the way.  Bow and arrows, to guns, better housing, better ways to store food, the works.  All of it looks pretty good too.  Again the game doesn't skimp out on how detailed it is.  Work benches look good, housing looks good.  Butttttt.....did I mention all that stuff is going to take a metric ♥♥♥♥ ton of mats to create?  Like no joke it takes a lot of time to make something cool in this game.  Half the stuff doesn't even matter either.  That rifle you made?  Awesome isn't it?  Too bad the dmg it does means nothing to the original bow and arrow.  A head shot in this game is basically an instant kill minus a few creatures in game.  Even then the dmg creatures do to you is so minimal, you'll find yourself stabbing them to death just as easily as sneaking up on then.  It makes scaling almost pointless.Speaking of scaling and material issues, all of that comes to a big stop when you realize the mission you are on will take about 2 to 3 hrs of real life time.  Most missions are get x, kill x, or scan x.  By the time you're done the base meant nothing.  Speaking of bases.  Cool looking building right?  Get ready to start the next mission with absolutely nothing.  Tragic honestly.  Build my first base, loved the process in doing it, only to go into the mission realizing all my stuff was gone.  Great system there.  After all this you'd think it would be over right?  Wrong!  Welcome to the biggest debuff system I've grown to love and hate.  Some debuffs make perfect sense.  Jump from a high spot?  Potentially break your leg.  Spot on for survival.  Fight an animal and get hurt?  Now you're bleeding.  Some debuffs makes sense.  You know the ones that don't?  Storms.  Welcome to the part of the game where you're playing and now you may as well leave and wait 5 minutes for it to pass.  Also cave diving gives you a chance to get a pneumonia which literally drops your stam bar to zero.  Now you can cure it or cheese the system by running in and out of a cave 100 times.  Btw ore only comes from caves so have fun with that.  Finally the worst thing has to be that you are supposed to be on an alien planet.  Ah yes an alien planet.....with a normal looking forest, and desert, and snow, and animals......like legit rabbits, wolves, and bears. Oh which can all breath the air, but you can't and you constantly have to refill that o2 meter.  Change the story up and make us aliens from another planet, but we landed on earth!  See how easy that was?  Call the o2 meter something else and bam, you nix both the fact you have zero alien creatures or biomes....well besides the snakes.  Those are the only alien creature.  Now I came into this game knowing zero about the backstop, but when I saw I had to refill an o2 meter and the cool looking background planets, imagine my surprise when I saw a deer roaming around.  Like cmon man, give people some credit.  It really needs the No Man Sky overhaul otherwise this game is legit dead in the water.

_childDocuments_.review: Icarus is a survival game set in a post-apocalyptic world where players must gather resources, craft items, and build shelters in order to survive against the various dangers that roam the land. The game has received mixed reviews from fans, with some praising its immersive gameplay and deep crafting system, while others criticize its repetitive gameplay and lack of progression.One of the standout features of Icarus is its immersive gameplay. The game is set in a beautiful, procedurally generated world that players can explore and discover hidden secrets in. The crafting system is also robust, allowing players to create a wide variety of items and structures in order to survive against the dangers of the world.However, some players have criticized the game for being repetitive. The survival gameplay can feel monotonous at times, with players simply gathering resources and crafting items over and over again. Additionally, the lack of meaningful progression or story can make the game feel aimless at times.In terms of presentation, Icarus is solid. The graphics are good, with detailed character models and environments. The sound design is also well-done, with realistic sound effects and atmospheric music.Overall, Icarus is a decent survival game, but it has its flaws. While the immersive gameplay and deep crafting system are enjoyable, the repetitive gameplay and lack of progression can be a turn-off for some players.

_childDocuments_.review: Really excellent concept. Good marriage of a survival game with rogue-like elements. Probably not for the survivalist purist nor the rogue-like purist, but if you enjoy both genres this game will definitely appeal to you.  The biggest sell of this game is that this is probably the most active and high functioning dev team I've ever seen on any title. There is a staggering amount of communication and fixes being pushed to address normal issues that effect the overall game play or QoL. In any other game I've played in the past, these things could be overlooked or unaddressed for months or years. I have full confidence that this dev team is not only super capable, but that will continue to support this title with dogged insistence as long as there is a community of players to provide feedback. Really admirable. Only negative feedback I have is that the talent and tech trees are punishingly permanent. As of now there is no respec option and as you grow and learn the game your first character will be stuck with all the mistakes you made while learning. There are even some missions that force you to adopt certain tech just to complete them, which ultimately means that you have to waste skill points that you'll never get back. You don't even have a finalize option, where you move a few points around and take them back before exiting the menu--if you put a point in, its there, forever. Ultimately, you have to re-roll a new character to benefit from the learned errors you made before and keep shooting for that ultimate efficient build. However, this has also been a rewarding part of the process for me. It can be frustrating, but not something that takes away from the game in my opinion.Really pretty game as well. Lots of the performance issues I had at launch have been addressed by patches and it runs relatively smooth especially considering the amount of textures and effects being loaded around you in the world; fire, light, water, leaves, all the bushes individual leaves, etc.For this being a brand new title, with many years of content ahead of it, Icarus shines now and with time will only become more luminous. Def worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: Icarus is a great game with immense potential, and I’ve spent 60 hours enjoying it. However, despite having a good time, there are numerous minor quality-of-life issues that are quite obvious, but I’ll get to those later. So why am I giving it a negative review despite everything? Because I really want the developers to address these issues. The main one that killed my experience is performance. The game's optimization is terrible. Even on the lowest settings, I can get 100 FPS initially, but after a while, it drops to 40-50 FPS. On top of that, there are constant stutters and hitches when traveling through the open world, especially when exploring caves. After 60 hours, my patience wore thin. Optimization should be the developers' top priority.Another issue is the lack of small, obvious features. For instance, why can’t we bind Quick Stack to Storage? There’s a bind for Loot All but not for Quick Stack. Why is there no hotkey for repairing items, forcing us to use the context menu instead? Why can’t we craft items with a shortcut, like right-clicking, instead of selecting the item and then clicking craft? Why aren’t there binds to give commands to tamed animals? And why can we only split item stacks in half instead of taking a specified amount? These small things add up and become very annoying. It's disappointing that the developers release weekly updates but haven't added such simple features yet.The third issue is the building system. I spent most of my time constructing a decent-looking base, and I have to say, the building system in this game is terrible compared to others I’ve encountered, like Valheim, Satisfactory, or Enshrouded. Icarus’s building system is the worst I’ve come across. If you want to build a creative base, be prepared for hours of frustration. The current system is only good for constructing quick, blocky structures.Aside from these issues, the game is great and has huge potential. But in its current state, there are a lot of problems. I understand now why people are frustrated when the developers release new paid DLCs with more unoptimized content.

_childDocuments_.review: Very unintuitive. In general navigating the UI and keybindings feels like a chore. Doesn't botter explaining it much either. Even the explanations can't be trusted...I'm told by the game over radio to drink water from the lake as my suit can filter the bad stuff and I get dysentery. Adding on the chores part, you have to go through a super tedious process for getting wood..cut the tree down, chop the tree in chunks, chop the chunks in smaller chunks and then press a button or hold (but way slower if you hold) to pick the wood up chunk by chunk. Purely boring and annoying to deal with. Especially considering that for any rocks it's just hit the rock gain the rock. For wood they chose a super laborious process when most surival games applying the same principle as with rocks because they know realism would be boring here. _childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: Played during a free weekend.Icarus is a relatively polished and broad co-operative Open World Survival game and whilst it doesn't bring anything new of note to the genre it covers all the usual things you have come to expect and does so very well. The upgrade path is easy to grasp and progress along it it is well paced with a sufficient variety of resources.The build system is a little limited for the moment and does not yet include any curved pieces or even angled flooring but does support complex, functionally useful and visually appealing if somewhat restrictively boxy structures. Decorations are well thought out and allow a reasonable degree of freedom in placement. To put it simply I could never build exactly what I wanted but I was also never displeased with what I could build and most importantly I rarely felt like I was fighting against the build system. Hopefully we will see an upgrade to add snap points to half pieces and the addition of equilateral triangles at some point in the development cycle.Enemy variety is slightly better than the norm for these types of games, we will always want more but there is enough that you don't always feel like you are in the same fight at least. Some effort has been made to vary enemy tactics with the addition of predictable attack patterns for certain enemy types allowing you to sometimes learn and develop useful strategies but beyond that it is the standard 'passive enemies mindlessly run away and aggressive enemies mindlessly chase you down' fare that we are all familiar with. There is unfortunately no complex behaviour either scripted or adaptive to make things more interesting. I also did not witness any inter creature behavioural relationships beyond a few rare occasions of what may have been some creature running away from another. This is definitely a part of the game that is noticeably lacking; Even some very simple Predator, Competitor, Prey relationships would go a long way toward making the world seem far more alive.Character advancement is both broad and deep, all skills are broken down to serve all of the specific wants and needs you may have allowing you to build into whatever role you most enjoy playing. You can also respec your characters Talents for a small cost to adjust to specific scenarios. Unfortunately you cannot do the same with your Tech Tree, leaving you with many wasted points in Tech as you progress through the levels and there are not enough points available in the standard game to learn everything; This ultimately restricts your characters longterm viability as it is entirely possible through a few mis-assigned points to lock that character out of certain content permanently.Character adaptability to the environment is handled primarily through crafting. The game will throw many variations of hazards at you whilst opening up the ability to craft preventative and or curative items to deal with them. This system also extends into situational buffs such as increased melee damage or carrying ability etc in a way that allows you to boost your off abilities as necessary. This system is well fleshed out however I found that by the time I unlocked the recipes, crafting stations to make them and then gathered the necessary ingredients I had essentially moved beyond needing to use them. I feel this system would be better utilised if current consumables were moved down the tech tree and significantly more powerful ones added to the higher tech levels to make those buffs available when you actually need them and warrant continued use as you progress.The game does include a taming system and the ability to use tamed creatures as mounts or even pack animals. This is a nice touch but, given the aggression of most of the creatures towards your mount when you are not around, is a feature you will likely ignore more and more as you progress. The extra speed/carry boost just isn't worth the hassle of constantly baby sitting your pet that will be targeted and killed by random creatures spawning on top of it the moment you are out of hearing range of it. There are Talents you can take to somewhat reduce the chance of aggressive creatures attacking your mount but not to any useful degree. Inter creature behavioural relationships would again be beneficial here as would expanding pet commands beyond follow, stay, or fight; The addition of a flee and some sort of return whistle or even just a flee to me when in danger command would help a lot.Questing exists in the game, though in a very limited form; This appears to be expanded in the DLC but I have not had a chance to try that yet. Mostly in the base game it is of the go here and either kill x amount of y creature or defend this area for x minutes/waves. It gives you something to do when you are feeling kind of aimless which is always appreciated but it fails to give any reason to do it beyond a rather disappointing drop of reward items you probably have no use for. This is a failing most games in the genre suffer from and this game differs only in how very easy it would be to correct. The framework is all there to provide a reason for the players actions in their sojourns from an orbital station onto this terra-formed world to identify and test the environment and it's resources. It would be a simple matter to present this story to the player, include key milestones to work toward that advance the story and even add an ultimate conclusion that serves as both meaning to play and satisfactory resolution of play. It doesn't need a hoard of dramatic characters and deep themes with surprise twists, a story treatment would be enough; But it does need something to make this feel like more than a just a game framework or very large tech demo.Multiplayer worked perfectly for me, it was easy for my friend to join and we had no random disconnects. Actions in game synced cleanly and having a co-op partner greatly added to the experience. Everything else the game has to offer such as Graphics, Movement, Sound etc are all of high quality and for me the game ran smoothly and without any major issues.All in all if I was judging this game against all of the very many others in the genre I would give it a thumbs up, I certainly enjoyed my experience, were it not for the issue of price.There is no polite way to put this so I will be blunt, the price tag of this game is delusional. This is a 25-30 USD early access indie game that they are trying to charge $120 USD for with every indication that they will continue to charge even more for each and every future update; The justification for this seems to be to pretend that the game is no longer in early access and that the ongoing patches to the game are expansions and not the very necessary feature updates they clearly are. I can only imagine this is a result of an inexperienced Chief Financial Officer who simply does not understand how to price a product in the PC Gaming market.Whilst I certainly understand the need to ensure everyone gets paid and the desire to make a profit off of your product what the CFO seems to fail to understand is the higher you price your product the more you narrow your potential market. This game is actually priced all but entirely out of the PC gaming market, you could purchase two brand new AAA games for the same price they are trying to charge for this feature incomplete early access indie game. Even if by some bizarre series of events this game managed to capture the attention and wallets of all the 'whales' in PC gaming that fraction of a percentage of the market would be insufficient to cover the cost of development. By closing their product off to the average consumer this game is all but guaranteed to fail financially.At $30 for the complete game this would be a clear winner for my co-op group and you would have had six more sales, at $120 it is a complete joke and you have nothing; Even RocketWerkz's CFO should be able to understand that math.
