_childDocuments_.review: Tl;dr this is an early access game masquerading as a complete game with some interesting mechanics but is about as unbaked as your aunties homemade minced meat pie after a hard night of boxed white wine - get it on sale for $5 and play with some friends in a year or two when (if?) the developers get around to finishing the game.Good stuff first since it's a short list: - There's a nice big old talent tree with tons of awesome looking talents, which is one of the things I find survival games  have. If they do have them they're anemic as ♥♥♥♥, where as this game has multiple trees with really nice looking QoL perks. Sadly, you won't get to use more than 15% of it (more on that in the negatives....). - When the game doesn't run at 20-30 FPS on a 2080 TI @2k, it's beautiful. Best of luck finding a guide that helps you figure out which options decimate the engine and then praying they actually work. On the other hand, I'm genuinely impressed (technically speaking) that a company managed to find a way to make Unreal run  than Unity for an FPS. - The building and crafting is fun despite all of the various issues with both. Making bases is enjoyable, the multiple tables are nice, progression makes more or less sense (though it's stupidly expensive and grindy) - Despite being an awful grindy overall experience it's still somehow fun to play with friends, at least until you get to the end game missions and realize that you spent $27 on a running/mining simulator with combat mechanics implemented by a toddler - Some cool save-game tech; your game ('prospect') gets uploaded somewhere central any  you were playing with can resume it, at any time, and play it with or without you. This is a great approach since there's no real time limit in-game for completing things (just real-life time), so people can play at their leisure and make progress.Transitioning to the cons...: - Nothing is explained. Apparently, everyone was expected to play the two previous betas/open events and know what all the gameplay mechanics were, how the missions worked, that your character gets permanently deleted if you don't finish (or abort) a mission in X real-time days (yup!), that exotics (the end game in-game currency to buy cool unique "workshop" items) require a specific quest chain to unlock (the game now highlights these missions after some patches, at least). - Sometimes your cool unique workshop items get deleted and you lose them and have to repurchase them. No, not because you left them behind on a mission, because the game just decided to delete them. Why does this suck? Because they require in-game rare currencies (either golden dollars or purple exotic dollars) that come in small quantities from grinding missions and . - The talent trees are huge but you stop getting points at level 40. This gives you enough points to get 2 trees pretty filled out, but since you had no idea this was going to happen, you've got points spread out over random ass trees all over the place as you were having fun exploring. Naturally, though, you can respec - oh wait, the developers have never played a game with a talent tree before so that's not implemented either. Coming soon (TM), though! - The AI is about as smart a lobotomized penguin and all of the animals behave exactly the same. Prey runs and comes back to the  same spot you shot it, so hunting amounts to either 1) crit and 1-shot everything, 2) don't crit, wait for animal to pat back to you then murder it with a crit. Predator combat is either 1) bring more friends and pincushion it down with arrows, 2) crit and 1-shot everything except polar bears, 3) if it's a polar bear, crit it and glitch past it or unstuck and get teleported 15 feet away and re-engage, 4) get glitched and 1-shotted yourself when the enemy is 15 feet away and contemplate all the other things $27 could have got you (have you even tried Wendy's new breakfast sandwiches? $27 is a  of sandwiches!). - The game runs like crap and it seems to be on a completely random basis; find a guide on Youtube and pray it has an affect on your FPS. - Dropping items on the ground sometimes falls them through the planet, deleting them permanently, because this game is  early access - Crafting at later tiers is abysmal. For example, end-game benches require 40-80 gold, and on average you'll maybe get 40-80 gold ore (crafted 2:1 into ingots) from tier 2/3 mines. You need a lot of benches. This basically means all of the end-game is: run around the map decimating every mine (which have fixed amounts of ore, doesn't respawn), then hope to god you can craft the benches to make the mission materials you need at which point you then ♥♥♥♥ off back to space and lose 100% of your progress only to do it all again in the next mission. - Crafting in general is just terrible. We don't tech beyond bows for weapons or basic bone arrows for ammo as all it does is force you to play the same mission longer, re-grinding the materials you used for either item. The game is also of course very realistic - an aluminium arrow (1, mind you) naturally takes 1 copper ingot, 4 aluminum ingots, and some epoxy. Yes, 4 aluminium ingots. If you've never Googled what an "ingot" of metal is, today is the day you should, then Google "arrow head" and try to wrap your head around how they fit 4 ingots of aluminium in one arrow. - Playing without friends is a nightmare; play with friends or wait until the devs address solo play. It's just taking the already massive grind and multiplying it by the lack of friends you have. - While mining in a cave you get a permanent stamina debuff no matter what armor you are wearing, because . You also randomly develop pneumonia, which there is a later-game fix for, but no one cares because all it does is make you take 15 minutes versus 10 to grind out the mind-numbingly boring cave mining expedition. - Fun fact: 100 stones in a pile weighs far more than 100 stones in your inventory, because the stone pile is full of extra  - Dying in the beginning is awful (massive XP debuff you have to work through), dying after level 40 is 100% completely irrelevant as XP no longer matters at all.It's got potential. Somehow, despite all of that awful experienced, I almost clocked 60 hours and that was largely playing with 1-2 other people. With more I'm sure the grind would be less noticeable.This definitely feels like a come-back-in-a-few-years kind of game and see if the developers have got around to completing it. Right now it's just frustrating and unrewarding.

_childDocuments_.review: 12/17/21Just Don't buy this game. Just take a look at my playtime. I started with it thinking, not bad...then beta ended and they released it.  It's a grift that forces you past the steam refund timer. The start of the game is spending 10 hours to unlock blueprints to build a wooden shelter and tools. Every mission after that is the same. Spend 4 or 5 hours building a shelter and harvesting resources, then 20 minutes to do the objective. The first 5 hours of every mission is the same, gathering resources for a shelter that doesn't fall to a storm. You start from the wooden hut age and progress up. Every mission starts in one of three locations, so the map gets really familiar really quick. You keep doing more missions thinking it might get better or have more content. It doesn't. There's all of 4 types of missions all copy pasted. The entirety of the 4th tier of blueprints is either not in the "full release"(Coming Soon!) or they are completely useless and a waste of time to gather resources to craft. This game is a complete scam. I would not be surprised if the updates cease and it's abandoned like Starforge...look that one up on why steam removed it because this gives me the same vibes.12/06/21I've decided this is going to be a living review because I constantly find more items that just make this feel more and more like an incomplete and unpolished game. More bugs, more graphical issues, etc. I will update this when needed with a date stamp of what I find, as well as strike them out when they are fixed. I'm no human factors engineer, but clearly none of this was tested, proofread, or fixed if already found. The updates will be found timestamped after the initial review==========Initial Review==========This game is fun, but in no way can be labeled a full release lest the evolving industry standard of "If it builds it ships!" continues. I would only recommend this game if it had an "Early Access" tag added on the steam store page, because that is what this is and people will have a better idea of what they are purchasing - access to test a game in development. Is it worth $30? ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ It's a rather subjective question nowadays. I say to myself yes, but wouldn't say yes with a straight face to someone else posing the question to me without caveat after caveat.Issues:You need a supercomputer gifted from Hera herself to SUSTAIN 60fps. After an hour of play the framerate will drop periodically until it reaches ~40 and you restart the game. Possibly a memory leak or an intrusive garbage collector, either way this is not optimized for performance. Besides a few new plant species and a longer mission tree this is indistinguishable from the last two beta builds.Bugs. Lots and lots of bugs. Plants that have a spoil timer decay after grown in the crop plot. Squash, Pumpkin, Watermalone. Don't bother trying to farm them.Items regularly fall through the floor of the world. Every time an item falls on the floor, Anubis flips a coin. Imagine Imhotep at the end of Mummy Returns, but it's your {insert expensively crafted item here}You may find yourself flying and experiencing the woes of gravity after stepping on the wrong geometrically inconvenient lump of grass.Animals randomly become incorporeal beings incapable of interaction from the outside world, but are fine interacting with it at will. Imagine a quarter metric ton grizzly charging at you, completely incapable of taking damage and shoves you into the hillside, and now your body is half fallen through the world. You cannot harm it, but it doesn't feel the same way about the mechanics that lead to this unfortunate outcome. It strikes, you take one last breath, you die, and upon returning you discover your body belongs to Anubis.Pros:You can be a beta tester on a weekday.========End Initial Review========This next section is to describe bugs I find along the way. Time stamps and version of the game included. As said above struck out when fixedFindings 12/06/21 - 1.0.11.87997-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Talent: Fireproof SealantFireproof sealant shows +25% burn chance on wood.Really? Is this accurately reporting a 25% increase from the backend and this point increases the chance to burn my structure down or is this a typo no one has found in the past few months? If it's the latter, why isn't the value pulling from the backend? Just post the value from the backend instead of updating a description anytime the value changes during balance tweaks.Wildlife constantly stuck in felled trees. They just get stuck there and constantly run into the tree and jump. and jump. and jump. and jump.Control clicking crops into crop plot has a chance to delete the stack of crops (without planting them). Discovered as I was control clicking the grown crops in and out to gather and plant. Could be a race condition on player interactions and global clock.If I have time to waste I'll come back to farming crops plotsI just tested this while posting to ensure I wasn't spouting bs and realized lower stamina = faster actions.This is a bigger issue than just pneumonia. Having lower stamina means more actions per minute. This system needs a major rework. I've done pneumonia + cave debuff, pneumonia only, cave debuff only, and no debuff outside. The trend shows my stamina allows more hits per minute the lower it is.----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Findings 12/07/21 - 1.0.14.88121-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Constant disconnections from game server I am hosting...and playing alone.Error Code: Invalid Prospect Information - 001Invalid prospect information (from backend/session)MAJOR lagspike when the client cant receive a heartbeat from the server.Invisible mountains/terrain.Some terrain is under this invisible ground/wall. Animals will spawn under this invisible wall and still be able to attack a player unable to fight backAnimals can hit you seconds after you kill them. Along similar lines, there is no way to dodge anything. If they're targeting you, their attack has 100% chance to hit, even if you are clearly too far away to be hit-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Findings 12/08/21 - 1.0.18.88412-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Bottled Foods in stacks do not return empty bottlesNo talent points after 40. At lvl 41 and 42 I did not receive a talent point but any time I log in it says I have an unused point

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the answer to the "endless" and "aimless" survival games out there, where after you unlock everything and you find the best loot, there's nothing interesting to do anymore and you get bored. Icarus has the solution!If you really like "open world" "survival" games, this one is for you!Pro:  - Innovative idea to play in "sessions" - Great visuals - Replayability - Great PvE (PvP will come when everything is well balanced, with something like a ranking system) - Play at your own pace - Complex "skill tree" and "blueprint"Cons:  - a few bugs still, but comparing to the huge amount of content in the game, they are irrelevant.I don't care much about graphics if the gameplay is good. This game has them both!Every now and then, I play a building/survival game for a few hours (something like 7 days to die, Empyrion, DayZ, Space Engineers). I play it again after a few months and I forget what I was doing, so I start from scratch. I grind a few hours until I get a decent level and a "basic" base. I play it again a few months later and I start from scratch again. Icarus solves exactly this issue! Starting from scratch actually makes sense here.

_childDocuments_.review: I picked up Icarus excited to experience a unique game-loop for the survival genre. The idea of being able to drop into a prospect, collect materials that you can spend when you complete the prospect and go back in more prepared for the next prospect is an awesome one. Unfortunately, Icarus falls short with this fantasy. The prospects seem to fall into one of two categories... 1: Run around for hours to reach some random object and interact with it, then return to your dropship and leave. 2: Collect a ridiculous amount of gold and copper in order to make the two items you need to complete the mission, run for a while to the place you gotta complete the mission, then run all the way back to the dropship. The idea of having a limited time to complete a prospect is interesting, but in practice it just ends up adding an extra step to every single mission that adds to the ever-present feeling of grinding. What's more is that the grind doesn't lead to much reward. The meta-game collection of rewards definitely help make the game a *little* less repetitive, but you can't upgrade your drop ship to allow for stations to be brought up or down from the planet - upgrades are solely items that affect the player themselves. So there is no way to skip the early game grind of setting up a boring, basic building and the same crafting stations over and over and over again.I was never very excited for the storm system, because I'm not huge on being interrupted in games like this when I have an objective in mind that I am actively working toward. I understand the concept and the potential for this system to shake things up, but it feels tacked on. Half the storms do nothing but seem to make your character run slower, and the other half will completely derail whatever you're doing or even destroy your entire base while you're miles from home trying to collect gold or copper ore. The storms are boring at their best, and more commonly frustrating.I was also wary of the limited time for prospects, because of the limited time and storm systems, other aspects like building and planting are almost entirely pointless endeavors unless you decide to disengage with character progression and play prospects that grant no rewards.  Are you doing a prospect that will take a while? Build a 3x3 stone structure and never think about storms again. Are you doing a shorter mission? Build nothing, or like a 1x2 wood structure. Either way, you'll likely spend very little time being creative in this game because nothing persists from prospect to prospect.The balance of many of these prospects are a mess. There are missions that will leave you spending tens of hours running around desperately trying to find a few more gold ore nodes so you can afford to craft the one item that is required in that prospect. The rewards for these missions are absolutely not worth the time spent, and the challenges within these missions are repetitive and bring very little joy moment-to-moment.Finally, the game is not finished. There are game-breaking bugs - bugs that will cost you to lose items that took you dozens of hours to collect and build up. At the time of writing, I would be further along if I stopped playing 30 hours ago than I am now. I lost 90% of the items I had earned in a bug that occurred three times. If you forget to put some MacGuffin item in their dropship before going to orbit, guess what? You are now unable to complete that prospect and will have to start over despite the item you needed to return orbit being in your pocket! There are so many visual bugs, back-end server issues that are constantly being updated, and balancing of enemies needs a lot of work. The game feels very much like an early-access experience with little chance of that changing in the short-term.The things that make this game stand apart from it's competitors either suck the fun out of the game, or just suck. Pass on this game for now, maybe in the future it'll be playable and the core game-loop will feel rewarding and enjoyable - but it'll be a while. tldr; game is repetitive, frustrating, broken, and feels very far from finished at the time of writing. Pass on it.

_childDocuments_.review: General Disclaimers:- I love this game.- I have a lot of respect for the philosophies of the developers.  As a developer with four decades of experience, I recognize the potential these developers have, but they are not there yet.  They make a lot of rookie mistakes.  But that can be overcome with experience.  The important stuff, the stuff that has to be inherent and cannot be taught, these guys have.  They will be really, really good someday if they stick with it.tl;dr:The game is playable and fun if you have a great deal of patience, but frequent bugs and bug fixes that create new bugs or break previously fixed bugs are common and potentially frustrating.  You can put in a lot of hard work only to lose it for one reason or another.I believe the developers are passionate about their game and their players, and you just cannot teach that.  It is rare and something I greatly appreciate, and I can put up with an awful lot when I know the developers really care and are really trying.So if you can deal with the frustration then definitely buy it, otherwise wait and see how it develops..Pros:Devs have excellent ethics and are committed to their players.  They really seem to care.  This cannot be overstated!Devs are working hard to fix issues and add new content.Concept is good.Mechanics are good when they work.  Most work.Gameplay is really good.  The game is super fun when you don't run into bugs.  So, fun most of the time.Art is really good.  Except Hyenas.  Hyenas look like the lovechild of a Dingo and a Greyhound >:-)Cons:Devs are green and make rookie mistakes.  It sometimes feels like they either have no idea how to fix a bug and just slap bandaids on symptoms, or no time to fix it correctly.- Example: I am not sure what bug was being fixed, but an early patch extended geometry bounds, creating invisible walls.  One of these walls blocked off a cave, eliminating the possibility of getting the resources within.  Was that really the correct fix?  If so then the fix was incomplete, since they unintentionally eliminated a game asset.  You can see the cave, you just can't enter anymore.QA is either non-existent or understaffed or also new.  Too many bugs get through that should have been caught by QA, especially with proper regression testing.- Example: At the time of this review there is a mission that breaks after the player has put in a ton of time and effort.  How does it break?  There is a crate that holds required equipment that cannot be interacted with.  Seriously?  How did THAT get through QA?Because of the above two points the game can be incredibly frustrating at times.Locomotion (movement through the world) has flaws, especially when sneaking.  You can think you are moving carefully down a steep hill and suddenly get thrown off to your death.  When sneaking you can get stopped by the smallest things, or you can suddenly have sneak stripped off by the terrain (which is especially fun if threats are nearby).Hostiles can spawn on or very near you.  Sometimes in groups.The game uses peer connections, which have a few drawbacks and risks. The one I wish to point out is latency and delay, or lag in general.  Because you are dealing with a player who is hosting, you are at the mercy of his connection and the strength of his machine as a server.  Additionally you have periodic connections to official servers.  This can leave you with horrendous lag sometimes.  For instance, I have shot a wolf with an arrow and had to wait THREE SECONDS for the hit to register and the wolf to die!  It is not that rare to shoot something only to miss and miss and miss because the host does not agree with the client on where the target actually is.  This can lead to outright misses, or hits that should be critical hits instead registering as regular hits.  This can be a super frustrating way to die, knowing that the thing that just killed you should have been dead five times over.- Example: My friends and I have been killed by wolves that had a muzzle full of arrows, but not a single headshot counted as a crit.  With the weapons we use one crit would be fatal to a wolf.  But what is actually a body shot to the host looks like a head shot to the client due to lag.In closing:I really like the devs, I think they will be really good someday.  I really like the game, and can ignore the frustrations for the most part.  Even my professional ones (dev pet peve's, like missions breaking because no one thought to check to see if a crate could be interacted with).  I am not saying that I don't sometimes have to take a break for a bit after a particularly frustrating bug, but I keep coming back because I know the devs are trying.  They and their game have a ton of potential, and that buys a lot of leeway from me.  So if you are like-minded and can tolerate the frustration, DEFINITELY get this game!  Otherwise you might be better served by Wishlist it and picking it up when it is a little more refined.I am giving this a Not Recommended due to the current state of the game.  Reviews should be based on reality, not hope and expectations.

_childDocuments_.review: Does it need to be optimized? Yes! But behind the poor optimization (which will be fixed) is a beautiful survival game with a lot of really cool, unique mechanics. Have you ever played a survival game where a storm will appear out of nowhere that fells trees that may or may not fall on your base? Or a storm where lightning strikes a tree that starts a forest fire that may or may not burn your house down? You will experience that and more with this game. People say animals spawn in front of them and attack, but in 20 hrs i have not seen that, what i have seen is that killing animals and having carcasses around actually attracts the predators of the game. Sometimes the world does feel a bit empty because of how big it is, and how the animals act (bears tend to be deep in forests, you will find more animals by water sources), so they do need to add more animals/structures to add more encounters in the world. The tech and talent trees are robust and have tons of options in regards to how you want to build your character. With that being said,  the game is gorgeous and has had a better launch then most other survival games, behind the minor problems right now is a survival game with huge amounts of potential.

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely write reviews for games.I've spent a little over 30 hours in the game at the time of this review, because I really want to give this game a fair shake and I respect the fact that Dean Hall and RocketWerkz are trying to expand the Survival genre here. I understand launch difficulties and server issues that come up around them - none of my beef with this game has anything to do with that.The game is intentionally tedious and obtrusive in the worst possible ways. There are four talent trees, Survival, Construction, Combat, and Solo. The Solo tree makes no sense and forces anyone who wants to take points into it into a Solo-Only mindset, as these talents *do not work* if you are in a multiplayer game. This is a completely baffling design decision that blows my mind. The tree shouldn't exist.There's no respec functionality whatsoever, and talent points stop at level 40. If you want to try different builds, the only solution is to make another character, which seems like an absolutely bizarre design decision without any real thought put into it. Characters are not disparate enough in terms of their talent selection to warrant alt characters, so you don't get enough of a meaningful gameplay experience change by rolling a new character to try different talents that might make your life easier. If talents were so impactful that they made the player's character feel meaningfully different from others, then I could maybe see a degree of permanence being important - but there isn't, so it makes no sense in my eyes.Most missions follow a set formula. Land, spend 60% of your time in the mission teching back up to whatever level of technology and assets needed to complete the mission, 20% of your time completing the mission, and then anywhere from 10-20% of your total time in the mission is spent trudging back to your dropship. None of the mission timers we had ever felt like we were 'under the gun', with most missions giving anywhere from 3-7 RL days to complete, while the mission themselves took anywhere from 3-4 hours of playtime to complete. There isn't any way to facilitate faster travel aside from movement speed talents, so these last 10-20% of missions are actual wastes of time as you run through the landscape as fast as you can to get back to your dropship, so you can leave and go somewhere else - these trips can easily take up to 15-25 minutes, depending on how far the objectives are from your drop. There is nothing challenging about it - it is simply more tedium tacked on that doesn't respect the player's time.The missions themselves are usually cased around a biome, which is a set map that you'll complete multiple missions on. This sounds fine - except for the fact that each individual mission requires you to leave the planet at the end of it. When you return to that biome to tackle a new mission, all of your building progress is gone, but the map is the exact same otherwise. On the first winter biome, we had to build virtually the *exact same base* in the *exact same spot* no less than four times because we had multiple missions for that biome. This feels incredible repetitive, doesn't respect the player's time, isn't challenging and just feels lazy.Death is a mechanic that also makes no sense to me. In a multiplayer session, if you are killed, you drop to the ground and can be revived by a teammate. The only penalty for death in this instance is a reduction of Food / Oxygen / Water stats, which can be easily remedied. The only time you have to actually contemplate a respawn is if nobody can revive you, which in the majority of instances where you have 3 or more players, is exceedingly rare.In solo play, this is an entirely different animal. If you are killed in solo play, you *must* respawn, and take an XP penalty as well as lose all your equipment. The dropping of the equipment is fine and understandable, but the XP penalty boggles my mind. As of the time of writing this review, the XP penalty is scaled to the amount of XP you are currently into a level. So if you're 90% of the way from level 9 to level 10, the XP penalty is HIGHER than if you were just 10% of the way into a level. If this is a bug, I'm glad to be proven wrong. Even if it isn't, the penalty is staggeringly high, and massively disincentivizes solo play.There are other issues as well, many of which are covered in the other reviews plastered here. The Mixed aggregate of reviews is fair - the game itself has some good moments and the framework of the game is interesting. As it currently stands, I'd highly encourage prospective buyers to wait and see what RocketWerkz does to address everything. If you do still feel inclined to buy it, make sure you're playing with friends - as with most games, it's better when you have buddies to play with.Edit:I will say, I've given this some thought and there's a few things right off the top they could do to make things immediately better. For those of you who have upvoted and brought attention to this review, I appreciate it.Edit: 8 June, 2022I give Dean Hall and RocketWerkz credit - they are listening and trying.Most of my initial suggestions (which I had to delete to conserve space) have been addressed to a reasonable degree. The new map, Styx, looks to promise some actual continuity between missions in some context (according to their devblog, missions now can change the map in between missions). The timer change to RL time makes sense, and the hardcore mode added alleviates any remaining concerns I had on that front. I still cannot recommend the game, but I'm a lot closer to it now than I was six months ago. It's very obvious at this stage that the staff is very committed to turning this ship around, and I've kept quiet tabs on it as they've progressed. Most of what they've addressed is core functionality of the game that was just unfun - and rightfully so, that stuff needed to be addressed first. I do think if you've read the progress and see potential with the title, it's worth investing in - but you should see it as an investment, not a game really ready to sink a ton of hours into right now.I think they also realize that there's just not enough interesting and exciting enough incentives to actually play currently beyond chasing exotics for gear. What will get me back into this game is a sense of persistence. I personally want to be able to be able to land on Styx or Olympus (the two current maps) and complete *multiple* missions before returning, so I can get the benefit of not having to rebuild the same base over and over again in the same general area. Good luck, guys.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like sandbox style survival games like Rust and Valheim, take a look at this game.You are a prospector in a space gold rush. Drop on to an Earth-like world with no technology, and survive against vicious wildlife and unreal storms. You harvest/hunt/craft to gain XP, which allows you to unlock more recipes and talents as you go. Manage oxygen, hunger and thirst as you scavenge the planet for "exotics", the new material everyone is after.There is a mission structure that will provide you with currency to purchase equipment to speed up further drops onto the planet. Once your mission is complete, jump back in your drop pod and get your next mission.There is some Jank to this game. As the other reviews state, it takes some time to massage the graphics settings to match what your computer wants. (I'm playing on a 580X and have my settings low for the most part. The game looks like early Rust for me, and I don't mind at all). Mission triggered wildlife spawns can pop up on you without much warning. Occasionally broken down trees will fall through terrain, but there is not much loss of material when that happens.I had 40+ hours over 3 of the 7 beta weekends before launch. I expect to have 100+ more now that the game is out.Good luck prospectors. If you can, bring friends. It always helps to have someone watch your back for bears at night...

_childDocuments_.review: So last time i played icarus i made a text document about the items you can buy with exotics. There are only a few things that  are worth it.If they changed anything here, then i might update it but im pretty much done with the game and my friend group has moved on because there is such a lack of permanency, it got annoying to start over so often. 	HAMMERS: AkiraThe akira repair hammer is good because you can hold it and be protected from a storm. Other than that its a hammer, not much else Tetsuo This repair hammer is not worth it because of the movespeed reduction. I would consider it a entirely neutral and not worth the money. Repair hammers arent used all that often anyways so your money is best spent elsewhere	AXES: LieNot worth it. The buffs, damage and other qualities make this axe too expensive for what its worth. If attack speed was doubled rather than +10% then it would be worth it, but even the MXC axe gives the same yield as this, so it would be better to just be a little slower than the Lie axe and bit the bullet for the basic axe and save your money for other things Sen/HeikeBoth solid choices for better axes. Heike is better because you dont need to move as much while cutting, but you will need stamina always, so Sen is not as good. 	PICKS: Sui-Shi/JushiOnly worth it if you have disposable money and exotics. The cost benefit puts platinum only slightly behind and titanium, though out of reach, better than both in every way. I would put my money in jushi only because iron is more valuble to have in large quantities early game, and the reason you pick these items is to have them immediately. Dong/KuangKuang i have found is actually better than dong only because i rarely go through the entire pick, and the only time i truly needed multiple picks was when i had to build a generator to get to the tundra across an avalanche. Otherwise i would build an iron pick and mine, or use this as a steel pick. Ores are more important than wood, so picks>axes. 	SPEARS: Dida/JijuJiju is the only one worth getting at this price because of the incredible sprint buffs. When dealing damage, the dida will deal the same amount of damage but kill bears only 15% faster, and to melee a bear under any circumstances without a bear trap (carved out rock to prevent it from climbing) would be foolish anyways, so you are better off speccing into spear speed and outrunning it so bowmen can shoot it. Gong Bu/XingXingXingXing is a glass cannon item that makes you faster but more vulnerable, but that 5% isnt that bad. Good option for being faster, no dealbreaking downsides other than a little more expensive than it should be. Gong bu is not worth it because even though you attack faster, you still consume a ton of stamina, and in a life or death suffering situation, the Xing would save you if you had pneumonia and cold. 	KNIVES:SichouSecond Best knife. No downsides. Would not invest in however because of the existence of qie marginally outclassing it in every way other than the slight downside of stam usage. Qie, Daokou, ShuiQie is the best knife for utility hands down. best stats, and a downside that is ignorable/not relevant or percieveable. Shui is a downgrade entirely and should never be used or unlocked, the percieved threat makes this a downgrade from the bone knife entirely. Daokou is only worth it if you really like throwing knives, but throwing such an expensive item and risking losing it is a dealbreaker. The damage of a thrown knife is outclassed in range, speed, reliability, damage and consistency by both bows and spears alike, so i consider this knife entirely useless. 	BOWS:Zhang HuAside from being fast, the longbow instantly outclasses it because of the 25% damage buff the longbow has. Purchasing this is a waste of money in every way. Ji/JijingJi is worthless, if not the worst. The movement reduction negates the talent that makes you faster while holding a bow, making this into a slightly faster wood bow with more durability. Do not buy. The Jijing is a straight downgrade from the longbow in every way. nothing more needs to be said. 	ARROWS: FlangeI dont have this unloocked, however it seems like a waste because other than doing more damage, it is outclassed by the other arrows easily, especially Wenhe, which gives 5x more arrows that do the same damage and break 10x less, for the same cost. VenomPoison is criminally underpowered and this is not worth it. periodNerveMay be worth it very circumstantially, like being persued by a polar bear and you need to escape, but otherwise useless and outclassed by the WenheWenheWorth it to get. Plenty of ammo, lots of damage, amazing break chance that is equal to i believe steel arrows (?) and makes for a great starting quiver 	ARMOR:CarbonAll of the carbon armor is entirely worth it. Resistences are good enough to survive as many hits as fur (almost) and good enough to survive in the heat or cold easily. Skipping early game armor makes all of this worth it	ENVIROSUITS:S5-IIStandard issue and no other first options. You have to get this and all players will have it eventually if they purchase anything. S5-XGood stats and required for progression. no getting around this.GustavGreat early game choice with phys resist and util slots for food, water, and oxygen. totally worth it to have early. FermiNot worth under any circumstances. Entirely outclassed by Hark in every way. Do not waste money on this overpriced optional.DuoNeeded for progression. Cheap and gives 2 module slots, which are priceless. HarkThe research cost decision for this outweighs the Fermi entirely. By the time you have fermi, you could have had Duo and hark, with hark unlocked and fermi not. To unlock hark, it costs 450. 550 if you want one. To unlock fermi, you have to pay 600, and another 100 just to get it, so you save 150 by not getting fermi entirely. Fermi has all the same stats as hark, except for the +10 Physical resistance, so since it is cheaper to buy hark and unlock it, and unlock duo at the same time, Fermi is already obsolete by the time you reach it. This is also the best suit in the entire game. 2 mod slots, more stealth, natural physical resist, and its dirt cheap, and you wont ever lose it (until you either delete it or lose a character). There is no concieveable reason to not get this. Bihu/DongtianOnly worth unlocking Dongtian just so you can get to the armor. Even then, once you unlock it, its too expensive to be worth the lack of a module slot and the added cold resist. Crafting this is unneded and wasteful. The icons look cooler than the other envirosuits. 	VACCINES:Tier 1 are expensive but hardly worth it. The only 2 worth it are anti bacterial/parasitic since pneumonia and parasites are the most common. Poison is useless because only cave worms envenom you. Contusions are incredibly rare, making thinning useless. Tier 2 is a straight upgrade and only worth if you really need it. Tier 3 is not only incredibly expensive, but outclassed by the cheapness of its tier 2 counterparts. Just take 2 tier 2s and save your exotics. You save 550$ and 250EX by neglecting the tier three vaccines. There is no concieveable positives behind tier 3s. I have spent nothing on vaccines, but if they are permanently consumables and not rechargable, they are a complete waste of money with no exceptions. All ailments they cure could be curbed by playing smarter or alternatively unlocking herbalism 2.	SUIT MODS:Mass dampeners are amazing. more movespeed, the better. They are cheap as well. _childDocuments_.review: A fantastic sci-fi running simulator game!Explore a uniquely terraformed alien world, millions of miles from Earth, where you find absolutely nothing alien. You still have trees, rabbits and deer, everything you would find on Earth, but don't forget it's not Earth cause your character runs around in a spacesuit.The typical running simulation loop comes down to this:Drop down in your spaceship, but you have no survival gear on you.- 1 hour gathering/hunting and crafting items to prepare yourself for the run.- 20 min running to reach your destination- We have some wildlife to hunt! But it's only available at night. 1 hour waiting for it to become nightfall.- It's night! 1 minute to complete objective. - Spend 20 min running back to your dropship to leave the planet.- Leave everything behind on the planet.- Neglect to bring any survival gear again in the next drop.So here's the play breakdown 50% gathering/crafting/hunting49% running around1% objective clearingIf you love running simulators like I do, then this is a great game. But please bear in mind running only takes up about 50% of the time. Until game increases the running distances between objectives its a thumbs down from me.

I feel like a lot of them could be incorporated into a lesser number of tables. For example, the fishing table could easily be added to an upgraded crafting and kitchen table. The anvil could be added to an upgraded workbench or smelt and etc. Another small issue is the hard mode really isn't that hard. The multiplayer is seamless and enjoyable as well. I would recommend this to anyone who enjoys survival or base building games.

_childDocuments_.review: After investing many hours into the game, I took a break and returned only to discover that my character no longer existed, and all my progress had been wiped out. It appears that there was a migration of characters from the server to the user's local machine, which I was unaware of.I must admit, I found this experience frustrating and disheartening. The game's developers should have implemented a system to allow character profiles to be stored locally from the beginning, and they should have made it easier for players like me, who are returning after a long absence, to download their profiles upon return.Losing all progress and having to restart from square one can be demotivating. It raises concerns about the reliability of the game's data protection and makes me question whether I might face a similar issue in the future. In today's age, safeguarding player data should be a top priority for any gaming company, and the lack of proper data protection in this game is disappointing.Considering the potential risk of losing hours of progress without any fault of our own, I am hesitant to recommend this game to others. While the gameplay itself might be enjoyable, the data loss issue overshadows any positives, making it difficult for me to wholeheartedly endorse it.In conclusion, I hope the developers address these data management concerns promptly, as it greatly impacts the overall gaming experience and the satisfaction of players. Until these issues are adequately resolved, I cannot recommend this game to others, as the risk of losing progress is a significant drawback that hampers the overall enjoyment.

_childDocuments_.review: I have followed Icarus's development from the very beginning days since it was announced.  I've been excited for a game in the survival genre that featured persistent character progression for a long time. I've been active within the Icarus community () throughout trying to learn everything there is to know.Closing in on 500 hours in game (+189 in beta) should indicate that I've already experienced all there is to do by now so I feel comfortable reviewing the game for real and updating my earlier launch review which can be seen here: . I have experienced everything that is in this game. The full breadth and scope of content and progression. I have unlocked everything and have fiddled around with everything you can craft. I've helped figure out a lot of the meta speedrun tactics, including playstyles that many other's use. I've played every previous beta weekend from BW1 through BW7 and been playing on average around 60 hours every two weeks since it's official launch.  When I'm not playing, I'm active answering questions on the discord or reddit or helping icarusintel's team.  I can say with confidence that this game is positively a fun experience If you do not, you might be better suited to wait for additional content to come. I can say this based on having already seen and experienced all that there is currently and knowing the game following it well enough to know what is to come yet will only improve it. I can also confirm that it has gotten better every step of the way and the devs have impressed me by having more than shown a willingness to address the issues in a timely manner while remaining transparent throughout the entire process. Not everything they have done has been positive changes but they are quick to take in feedback and make necessary fixes. I have full confidence in them fixing issues as they arise going forward. The dev's commitment for their game is there 100%. It's refreshing to see it too. It's a rare thing in the gaming world to be so responsive and transparent with the fans.   I am super excited for what Icarus will become as it continues to evolve and grows. The scope of the game's features is only going to improve further over time as they add to it. It may not be  now, missing some elements we thought would be in it at launch [I.E. Alien creatures/biomes]. Some might even say the game isn't "done" with missing veins and such in some missions but they have a very good base skeleton or bones of the game with which they can build upon.The base structure of systems in place of which they just keep adding to and tweaking with new content and mechanics is solid. The planned stuff is really exciting too. They will continue free weekly-content and QoL updates along the way but I am less concerned with what it is like right now, after 3 months in, and more interested in what it's like in 1 years time. Admittedly the game does have some minor issues —as it stands — so I will start there. ■ Focusing on the game's performance it can slowdown when hosting. And during storms where trees often are struck by lightning and catch on fire. The game's framerates can drop drastically. The devs have yet to fix this. At times the game engine's performance issues might see random drops or hitches but overall the gameplay experience is quite smooth. ■  The overall level of difficulty also is kind of slacking. If by design it can be too easy for an experienced gamer. Some might consider the game to be too mundane or dull then because of this.■  Combat especially isn't very complex or engaging for the player. With just the second tier of crafted bow and arrows one can basically handle all the creatures currently in the game and most of them can be one-shotted and insta-killed with the kill cam's damage boost. Because the kill cam gives a large damage boost to ensure the animal actually dies when the animation zoom in happens for the auto-homing missile arrows. This Fallout-esque combat basically is not challenging for the player at all. Entire weapon types are negated by strictly better options. For example. Hardly anyone uses spears or even throws knives because shooting a bow is better and swinging a knife is faster than a spear swings which makes it strictly better. The spears not having the ability to block or negate some incoming damage means nobody uses them. Guns even are often an afterthought because bows are so good and way easier to get. Which begs the question about the new alien creatures, that eventually will come out, will they be any more fun to experience if the combat isn't fixed? You can side-step to dodge bears making them not much of a challenge besides managing your stamina. I'de like to see more character ability within combat like charged attacks, blocking/negating damage, etc.  ■ By far the most major gripe I have with the game is the  and they don't change. They should be randomized so that they actually change every mission where they would appear or which veins become active but instead once you've done a mission once you know where to go the next time and it completely negates ever needing the radar to scan for them.This is one thing that MUST change for the game to have any degree of replayability and ultimately longevity in keeping my interest levels in it. Even when new missions/new content comes out to experience eventually we will complete it and that is fine but what keeps you coming back and offers the true replayability is the general gameplay loop and the main part of it — extracting exotics — is fundamentally broken because of this one design choice to not make them randomized but static. It's simply unfun and unfulfilling to know where you gotta go everytime. No challenge of exploration. We are Prospectors? Pfft■ Missions in general are too short minded in terms of their objectives and as a result over too quickly. Not giving players any reason to stay down and tech up playing for as long as the extended timer allows for. If they gave some mission types (I.E. Exploration missions) optional objectives that you could choose to complete, it would fix this issue almost entirely.That or branching missions where you get more and more objectives in succession. ■ The graphics are on par with AAA titles and comparable to the best this gen has to offer. With full RTX Global Illumination and Ray Tracing ON, the game's lighting and textures are lifelike. The backdrops are gorgeous to where I often momentarily stare off into the night sky in awe of their beauty. If your PC can handle epic settings use them. Many players will lower their graphical settings thinking it gives better optimization though. While a stable performance without crashing the client is ultimately all one needs in any game boy does it ever look good though when you really crank up everything. You can also take some really nice screenshots with the built in photo mode tool. ■ The audio work stands out as top notch here too. Sound effects such as the pings and tings you get when voxel mining out nodes, the wind whirling around you during the storms, trees creaking and cracking and the thud when they hit the ground. It's all very well sounding and helps ground the player into the game setting and goes along way to making it believable.Review continued in here due to length restrictions;Clicking says malicious so just copy paste url into web browser. It's just googledocs Steam... increase your character limit for reviews!

_childDocuments_.review: I've played many survival games and this one, I believe, will end up in the number 1 spot the way they are going. Even though it is released the developers continue to pour their live into the game, adding a much needed sandbox open world, added worms to protect caves, adding fixes and tweeks based on user feedback. WOWThe concept is simple, a terraforming accident created an unusable world except for prospectors. You are given a suit (who know how many people used it before you, it has seen better times) and you are sent down to Icarus with the purpose of getting everything you can. Especially the unexpected rare element that screwed up the terraforming.  You need to use the environment and resources to create a safe place to live and continue to expand your technology and resources to locate that extremely rare ore. Along the way you will discover an unforgiving world filled with animals for food and animals that want you as food. Then just as you begin to get comfortable (you carved out a small home in a rock with a campfire nearby) in comes the storms that can be so fierce that trees are ripped out of the ground.To add to the discovery aspect are caves littered around the mountains. The mountains leave large vertical walls and along these walls is the occasional cave, or possibly just a wall that indicates you can mine materials from it. Even the caves are unsafe as there are poison spitting worms that are heavily armored. But if you can hide behind a rock and aim at the head you can quickly bring them down with you bow. Once they are gone you need to create some light for visibility and mine the harder to get ores. Iron, Copper, Gold, (some clean water), and as you improve your ax you can get the more precious ores like Titanium and Platinum. So the risks are worth the rewards!The game has a few quirks but the devs are working WEEKLY to improve the game and fix any quirks that come up. I'm very impressed with the company that never cared to just dump and run because the game was "finished".  For example, the original game had missions and you had to get materials, build better and safer homes, and finish your mission. And when it was all done, you had to start all over again with the next mission. A recent update (where I began playing) was the addition of a static world. And, at higher levels, you can still receive missions to complete but in this static world where you do not have to constantly start over again. This is a sign of devs that love the product, care about the idea, and respond to complaints that caused people to stop playing the game wishing they had not spent the money. Speaking as a retired developer, GREAT JOB GUYS.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is amazing.  RocketWerkz has, in my opinion, tirelessly poured so much effort in to bringing this game to what everyone wanted.  There is challenge, they added persistence with open world, Alpha creatures provide a nice dangerous boss element, mounts/tames are awesome.  The visual changes to benches, textures, and environment are so much nicer then original review.  I am engaging with all aspects of the game and loving it.  Could not recommend this game enough for those who enjoy a "somewhat" grindy survival craft game.  After 99 weeks of updates I can happily update my score to be 9/10 in the genre.  I look forward to what RW brings to us in the next 100 weeks.  I think this is a solid game overall.  Session based survival game feels really good, but it is very easy to get over the survival components of this game.  It only becomes challenging when you venture out in to some of the objectives, but even in that case it is still fairly easy from what I have seen so far.  I think they need to add some more difficulty to the game including making hostile storms come more often (damaging to structures) and also need to make creature AI better as well as add more variety of dangerous things.  Combat is good but seems very weird in some circumstances like being weird that I can fire an arrow like a mile across the map and one shot kill a wolf for instance.  I also think that they need to add, perhaps through the workshop where you spend the in-game currency you earn, a way to respec a characters talents/skills.  The whole point of this being session based seems to me to be you keep character progress but start over adventuring each time.  However, if I make a mistake in my point allocation for my character I have no choice but to either accept it or restart.  Not a great feeling as far as I see it.  I think this is a solid start, but it feel like it perhaps was not "release ready" but maybe should have instead been early access until they had more variety(?) This game is grindy so if you do not like that perhaps it is not for you.I personally wish this game could have had procedurally generated maps. :( That being said I think they need to have more options for maps in this game.  With there only being one map it makes it easy to figure out where everything is (i.e caves, biomes, creatures, water sources, etc.) and adds more hurt to the survival aspect.  That being said I think the biomes are well done on the current map we have.  I also think we could stand to have more variety of animals and it would be nice if water exploration played more of a role in the game.  It was fun when my friend and I got stuck in a thatch structure in the arctic biome playing whack-a-mole to repair the base while a big storm blew through all to end up setting it on fire by accidentally standing in the fire. The skill tree/talent tree seems a little weird to me based on how many points you can spend.  It almost seems like this game intends to punish small group/solo play.  It feels like I am being pushed away from some of the more cosmetic items and "less than optimal" choices unless I am making a character to play as a specific thing in a group dynamic.  Almost seems as though they are trying create "meta" ways to play the game.  An example of this being, I remade my character, again, and this time when I made it I skipped things like cloth armor and went to leather as first one, or thatch and wood buildings where I waited for level 15 to get stone as examples.  I literally was able to hollow out a big rock and make a usable base inside of rock until hitting level 10+.  Not that I am saying this is good or bad living in a hollow rock, but it is what it is LOLI think the gathering system is good and the talents work nicely with them except the weird 1% chance to fully harvest thing, that is weird because it almost NEVER goes off :D I think that building is not to bad but it would be nice to have more options for building and to have the snapping system work a little smoother.  Sometimes I feel I have to have my character flip upside down to get something to place.  It is weird to me that so far it seems doors and windows do not take damage.  Even when my house burned to the ground my WOODEN door was sitting there in a crate that I could loot. The crafting options are good and I like the variety.I do think this game has some performance issues.  I did have to turn my settings down to medium so it would stop lagging when I try to aim my bow.  I also think the texture rendering makes it way to easy to hunt animals since you can just get a far distance from tree line and see through all the foliage.  This is a problem because anything you can see, you can kill from like the other side of the map LOL  I have not had any crashes and I will say it was nice that during a launch weekend there was almost no down time.  Still no real downtime even at the time of this review.While I have outline many things here that I do not like, I am enjoying the game a lot and intend to keep playing. It has good things and bad things but if I had to rate it I would probably say ~7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: One year anniversary update: So, I've been away for around a year or so and came back to check out the update and they added AMD Fidelity FX, which is a big deal for a system like I have, and I have a pretty good computer because I'm a custom builder and technician, so I was really disappointed with the way the game ran when I originally bought it, but everything has been resolved. You have to check your settings, because the game will degrade rendering quality and performance on auto settings, so you have to tune it yourself, but the game now runs properly and I have no complaints with the game and will take it for what it is, but it's far from a perfect experience, and I got so frustrated with the game I quit for a year, so there it is. I'd recommend it because it's probably the best survival experience you're going with this quality once you get your settings properly adjusted, and it's my kind of game, but I was expecting more at this price point, so I don't know if I'll buy their DLC, but the game is decent, and a year ago I wouldn't have recommended it, and didn't, but now I would, because my main complaint with the game was with how it ran, but now it runs properly on AMD so I guess it was originally for Intel, so now that it's been fixed I'll just accept it for what it is, and now that I can actually play the game on my custom build, and now I can learn more about it and play and see if I like it or not, but I've played fifty hours on bad settings, so I know what the game is like, and had it running pretty good even back when it came out, but it had performance problems, but now it runs great, so I'm not going to keep complaining about what has been resolved, so thanks for fixing the issues and we all appreciate the effort that went into getting these issues resolved on the new motherboards, so now we too can enjoy the game, and it took a year, but there it is, and I'm not sure how long it took, but it wasn't fixed on release and I'm just now checking back, so it took a year for me to witness, so there it is. I'll removed my negative review and move on with my life. My opinion about the game is it is a bit bland, and doesn't have a lot going for it besides the building aspects of the game, so it's less of a survival experience and more for people who like to build stuff, but I'll try the game again and see if it's any better now that they've done their updates, and I'll check out their quests, because before all I did was their sandbox and it's not that great of an experience, so maybe you have to engage in their mission structure for the game to be better, so I'm not sure, because I haven't gotten that far into it and checked everything out yet, but that's been my experience, and it's decent, but had a lot of problems when I played it last, so I'll keep playing and see what I think it now that the performance issues have been fixed. _childDocuments_.review: Most frustrating game I have ever played. Not a hard game by all means, its pretty simple... just frustrating. Its like someone had a lot of good ideas but in the end there is nothing to connect them.Honestly I have to say I bought it because of the advertisement. The videos were incredible and it seemed like there was a thrilling story with really good characters to be experienced...and then -No storyline, just tons of different dumb quests given to you by faceless corporations.It is clearly meant to be a multiplayer game, but doesn't let you play with strangers if you wanted to choose so.All the obvious breaks in the plot that make it hard to suspend disbelief (Looks and behaves like earth, my environmental protection suit gives me pneumonia when I am in a cave, polar bears are psychic and will detect you through objects, not a single trap in a game that relies heavily on hunting, as a spacefaring species your technological answer that you bring from a space station is---a 3D printed axe for tree cutting?!?...)Everything is an endless frustrating loop. You land on the same map, in the same location and everything you once built is gone. Everything needs to be built with your own two hands. Start from scratch with picking rocks, chopping trees with a stone axe etc. etc. etc. Crazy weather shows up like on a clock. Its not like one really bad storm once in a while to be remembered... Its a crazy storm every few minutes. Whatever you do, drop it and run back to your base and start fixing everything or else you loose it.Stamina feels like its sole purpose is to make sure you don't progress too fast.Any predator anywhere seems to have one task: slow you down.Need to built something? Sure, just stand there for 5 seconds, nothing happening...just a timer clocking off to slow you down.Landed on the planet? Conveniently not where your mission objective is, so you spend an hour to just run in between recharging stamina and fending off predators. Oh, and forget about ever having a vehicle...you can manufacture machines and concrete, but not even a bicycle.You die? No biggy... you just loose all your XP for that level...no matter if you were 1% or 99% close to the next level. Grinding to get to the next level? Better hope that no bear shows up at 98% How does that make sense??Finally the bugs: After my whole house got destroyed in one of the countless storms and I wasn't close enough to fix the timber walls immediately (as they get destroyed by any storm... as timber houses do...) I logged out in frustration. Then log back in: All the left behind contents of my destroyed things are gone.The polar bear that killed you lays down to have a nap on your bed in which you respawn...to insta kill you again and proceed to sleep there.You enter something thats marked as a zone on the map but to trigger progression in the quest you need to walk over an unmarked spot in that area.Animals will get stuck in things on the map, walk unfazed through a forest fire, clip right through your building if they got into it etc. Feels like a game from 20 years ago.Very, very disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game way more than I thought I would. There's a few things still to iron out but overall this is a solid game, as long as you go into it knowing a few things. The biggest departure from normal is that the game focuses on your character. Because of the mission structure and building mechanics, you really focus on building up and protecting your character rather than your base or pushing through the story. It does a great job of pacing you without making it grindy. All in all, it's a wonderful game that puts an interesting twist on the survival genre. That's not to say it's perfect. It's not, but I'll go over the few possible hang ups below.1: The game starts off with what we like to call the "La Croix" setting. Everything looks kinda... staticy. The trees, the grass, the shadows, all of it. It takes a couple minor graphic adjustment, reducing the shadows, turning off the grass, and turning off a NVIDIA setting and boom! The game looks great.2: Your base goes bye bye after each "mission". A lot of people don't like this but I REALLY like it. Let me paint you a picture. You find a cool spot, you build a base, get it all snazzed up with crafting benches and whatnot. Then you set out to explore/whatever and then you find a REALLY cool spot and say to yourself "sunuvabiiiiiiiiish, I should have built HERE!" but you've done all that work and can't be bothered to do the move so you just go back home sad. Well now you can build there on your next mission because you have to start from nothing anyways. Granted, you DO get an outpost where you can build your super base and it stays, so you get the best of both worlds. 3: Because you have to start over each mission, it can be not fun for some people but let me paint you another painting. You've done all the early game struggling and now you're comfortable. Now all you have to do is prance around, snag a little food here and there and contemplate if you should put up the blue drapes or the green ones. Then all of a sudden... it hits you... "now what?" The game is boring because there's no struggle, there's no challenge, you're just kind of... existing. So you stop playing and find another survival game and do it all over again. With this, you don't have to worry about that hitting you. You start over with all your knowledge and build what you need to suit each mission. I love it.4: If you die, your character is gone. That's not exactly true but hear me out. If you're playing with friends (and you should) and you go down, your friends can revive you and you're fine. Most missions allow you to respawn but at a painful cost. All your XP progress to the next level is gone. So if you're lvl 10 and you're 1/2 way to 11 and respawn, you start at the beginning of 10 again. Apparently there's an xp penalty gaining that xp back but honestly, I didn't notice it. Hardcore missions on the other hand, if you die.. bye, that chatacter is gone.5: Some people mentioned tons of negative status effects. There are several, but there's just as many positive status effects and honestly, they aren't that bad. God forbid you play like a sensible person and don't go traipsing around in a lightning storm getting blasted to smithereens. 6: The weather hates you and will demolish/ burn down your house. I love this but I can see where people don't like it. You don't just build a house and wander off. The weather in this game doesn't like you and wants your house to go away. So you'll want to repair it as needed. It's not a constant thing, just... ya know... Check it every now and then.7: The tech tree needs to be reorganized. there's a few things that you can "buy" but can't use or make until you're a higher level and unlock something in a higher tier. It's rare and really weird. No "but it's actually a good thing" for this. It needs to be addressed and from what I've seen, it's being addressed.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: I've seen some weird negative reviews saying you need all the DLCs to enjoy the game. No you don't. This game has been updated weekly with new content added for free regularly for more than 2 years. Yes, DLCs have additional planets with new creatures/biomes or cosmetics, but anyone reading their description would see that they're optional. You can buy them after you get bored of the main planet and furniture. That side of the game is one of the best monetization approaches I've seen, where you continue developing the main game that's single purchase, but also get additional funding from things that dedicated fans can purchase but new players don't need to start.I still have beef with devs for multiple wipes I experienced AFTER the release from Early Access and the way optimization has been (I haven't played in abt a year because SURPRISE with a demanding game that has poor optimization it's hard to find friends whose PC can pull it off), but what I can't fault them for is offering DLCs for a game that was fully released in 2021 yet still receives gameplay content all this time later.Can't recommend it with the way it's developed. Like many people here had a 100+hr progress wiped with a very slim window for recuperation, that I, being a person that doesn't check all of my games all the time, missed.  Innate servers  were a step up among other coop survivers that I would rather pay a sub fee to the devs than a side server that's just gonna rubberband and stutter me all the time.I love the gameplay and the recent additions of mounts and more plants for growing. I don't mind the grind and restarting in missions doesn't bother me since I like the process of starting every time. It's the technical side that pisses me off. Optimization is still horrible, the mentioned wipe (had another one recently when for some reason it started addressing a different steamid folder than the one where all the data was. _childDocuments_.review: Overall, the game is good. Buy it.BUT... there are a few negatives. The lore doesn't fit too well into the game, sometimes can be boring on single-player and can also be boring on the way back to the drop ship after the mission is complete. The game can also be quite difficult with some animals having lots of health and some areas hard to survive in. If you like and play many survival games, this shouldn't really be a problem. The game doesn't run too well on even really beefy PCs, but if your like me, you could probably tolerate it. Also the crouching looks kinda bad, not a big deal though.The biggest problem in my opinion, isn't necessarily a bad thing, but it puts some people off buying the game, which is understandable. The game is very repetitive. You do a mission, get good stuff, leave the planet, go again. It can make the game get boring after a while. Everything you have worked long and hard for just goes, and you have to do it all over again. It can get annoying and it can't really be completely changed as it is the core of the game. I do have an idea for a fix though... Make it so that the reason you need to get back up to space is because there's a big storm that comes round every so often on the planet and you need to leave before it will kill you (it is a deadly storm). Then, once you drop down again, you find the ruins of your old base with some of your stuff there. This way, you don't get completely reset but you do get stepped back a little. Just an idea. My current 40 hours was pretty much all in one week with my friend a while ago. We grinded, did a bunch of missions, and then get a little bored. I didn't, to be fair, but my friend was playing ARK and Rust with his other friends at the time and he enjoyed them a bit more. But I can say the game will be fun for around 40 hours. I think I'm going to pick it up again and replay it from the start, and this time try and do more missions.Another big thing that annoys me that is a real problem, and not subjective, is the bugs. There are quite a few bugs and texture issues, my game crashes sometimes and my character I spent 40 hours on got wiped for some reason. I think it might be a feature of the game where if you don't play frequently enough your character gets wiped. If that is the case, then that's an awful feature and the developers should remove it. However, my friend's (who I had done everything with) character was not wiped and he could still play on his character. This confused me but it didn't bother me since I wanted to start again nonetheless. But the other bugs can get annoying, but they won't completely ruin your game.One thing that can also get annoying (but it is also very good) is the frequent updates. This is just a pet peeve and nothing big and I do like the frequent updates but it means sometimes when I want to play the game I can't because i haven to wait for the update to install. But I do enjoy every weekly update. The developers are very active in supporting the game and the community is very nice. The game is also VERY grind demanding with is good as it can keep you busy but it can get a little boring but once you get an item your worked hard for it feels good. Those were some of the bad things out of the way.The game is good though. The graphics (when they actually function) are incredible. All the models for the animals look good although the character animations need some work. The resource gathering is actually kind of relaxing and I really like the way the crafting system works, with learning the blueprints, but I don't think it fits in too well with the lore. Effectively turn your brain off and ignore the backstory and have fun in the game and what it does well. The core things that scare people away from the game are in the marrow of the game and can't really be changed with out a completely different game being manufactured. The map is also quite well designed although some bigger caves and deeper maps would be sick and offer a lot more. Overall, the gameplay aspect is super fun. Don't expect this to be as good as Subnautica or Valhiem though, those games are S tier.But seriously - PLAY WITH A FRIEND. You will have much more fun if you experience it with a friend and it makes the experience easier (while not being too easy) and the game supports it really well with the crafting system and level grinding. I had a tone of fun in this game and for that I can thank the developers. This game is not coherently bad, but it just has a few flaws that take some people out of it. There is lots of missions and lots to do and get immersed in so if this is your thing then you will have tons of fun. I certainly did, which is why I can recommend this game

Don't like the singular DLC they releasedYou have many choices in the game, different missions that have different tasks such as scouting out a new part of the planet, scanning very rural parts of the planet for data, killing specific animals, or even basic sandbox survival. The game offers very great gameplay, rewarding patient players and people who enjoy progression. Each mission you go on, you finish and return to the space station, leaving all of the contaminated materials behind on planet Icarus. In the event that you want to come back to the same area and find the previous house you  made destroyed, it is because the game puts you on a different mission, not the same one. If you want to keep all of your items, buildings, resources, play a the sandbox survival mode instead of playing the missions. New players also don't understand that if you keep your character in a prospect, time keeps ticking even when you are offline. Storms still happen. They can break your home if you don't have it built properly. Overall, I believe this game is a 8/10 and a 9/10 dev team. Weekly updates are very rare and having a dev team that listens to their player base is also rare.
