_childDocuments_.review: I would say give this a try if you like open world/crafting/survival many elements are done right and the Dev's appear to be trying hard to address customer complaints.Revised - Came back to this game after letting several months patch and read the patch notes. Was excited to see that many of the complaints below seemed addressed.1. Introduction continues to be very weak, but many of the more counter-intuitive components have been reworked, so I would give this a pass.2. Combat mechanics continue to be bit wonky, but with the introduction of many new types of armor and weapons, with some rebalancing, it at least doesn't seem to be a 'whichever side gets the drop' wins.3. Harvesting got a tweak to make it easier to collect additional resources per trip, resulting in fewer trips, still don't understand why you need 5 lbs of metal to make a single arrow though...4. Progression finally got a RESPEC approach, but be warned this is a point-buyback system, where you have to spend in-game currency to rebuy points back INDIVIDUALLY. I still strongly feel that this prevents people from exploring other areas of the game that are either currently broken, or just straight useless (see: FARMING). I'm not going to give up mining speed or weight just to grow crops in 60 real life minutes when every 90 seconds a t-bone steak in a fur coat throws itself at me. Skip farming, focus on harvesting, health, and stamina and you can forget about needing to respec. Then read the patch notes every month as they try to figure out why no one farms...5. Real life timer was 'mostly' removed, the timer now counts down while you are in-game instead of the real world. I believe there are still a few missions where you only have 30 days though, these are few and far between. The in-game timer is very generous, and they have added a 'difficulty' option allowing you to pick an easy mode where you cannot lose your character. I have to say the added option of increasing/decreasing difficulty for increased/decreased reward was a clever balance.____________Old review_____________Expect this game to flame out and die as a cautionary tale of what could have been, or be patched very swiftly. Make your purchasing decisions based on more recent reviews than mine or wait a bit longer and see what happens.Great visuals, and really strong foundation for a future game. I love the animations, sound, the storms and destructible base mechanics are cool. The introduction for new players is non-existent, you have to discover everything for yourself as this game will not explain anything to you, and in some cases that can result if you losing all your character progress (not just mission).The combat mechanics are hit and miss, it mostly devolves down to if you see the predator before they see you, as you can kill most everything in the game with a single long-range sneak attack using a primitive bow. However if you get surprised attacked, it won't really matter what armor you are wearing, you will be dead in 2-3 hits. This creates a real struggle as a new player trying to get started till you understand the mechanics (which aren't explained). However once you understand that the answer is go "full murder-hobo", it gets a lot easier to manage since the MOB AI is trash.Mid-Late tier harvesting and crafting has terrible balance, you need mountains of resources to craft anything Tier 3+, which is really annoying since every mission requires you restart from scratch with an empty inventory. Seriously, a single T3 arrow costs 5 ingots and 2 other materials to craft. This results in having to make supply runs specifically to craft 17 arrows or 40 bullets.While I enjoy the early game a ton, I was frequently left wondering just exactly how many 'ore runs' I would have to make to complete a given mission and wondering if I could save 50% of the build-up phase and just run through the glacier using a bow and arrows with bone arrows instead of a rifle...Levelling and progression is straight broken. The old formula of only getting so many points and having a ton of options is pretty common, but the game includes NO ABILITY TO RESET your talent trees, which means if you decide you want to try another build, or discover you would be better off with another setup, they only recourse is to start a new character. This is patently absurd, it takes around 30-40 hours to hit level 40 and discover you have no option other than starting over? This alone convinced me to put the game down and move on.Additional warning, the game has a "real-world" timer mechanic, essentially you get some portion of real world time to complete the mission, most commonly 7 real-life days. While this adds a welcome pressure to getting the mission done, please note that if you fail to complete or abandon the mission within the allotted time, your character will be killed and you will have to start over. A mechanic that attempts to force the player to log in and play with a specific frequency or they die, is a horrible design for players who want to revisit this game sometime in the coming months.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I've been waiting a while to buy Icarus, I was hyped at launch but reviews told me to avoid, it looks like reviews have improved with 2 years since launch and with a few hours at the free weekend i thought I would try it, I somewhat regret my decision.  I enjoy survival games, and this ticks a lot of boxes for me however, the game is not sunshine and roses, it is very buggy still, given its been out two years now. Animals still walk around with the most basic animations I have ever seen, caves lack diversity 11 hours in, they all look the same cut and paste caves across the map. Clearly there are some animals added in as part of missions to make it harder but they have ZERO AI, like it makes Sega's Aliens AI bug look smart. These placed animals walk a set path and lose agro if they walk 5 meters from the path and instantly heal. It's clear to see timed events where randomly 3-4 wolves or odd horses will come and attack you no matter where you are. Animals that spawn in as part of a defend mission will always spawn in the the same spots and take the same paths. _childDocuments_.review: LV1 to LV34I played this game to past LV30. I liked this game instantly. Survival on another planet. Good story hook. After LV30 I did hardcore solo and died. Sad but it happens. So I started over and I discovered that all the missions I had unlocked with the first charater were still unlocked. I still had the credits too. So I started again. I was getting close to 25 and died on hardcore again. The grind is long so I had an idea. I was dieing when I got to hard core but since the missions were unlocked I decided to start on hardcore. The first time I bought a spear and landed, then I died. So I tried it again, bought another spear and made it out. I went from LV 1 to LV 34 on one mission. It was the hardcore desert mission.I dont really think I should have been able to do that. I made it because of all the predators. Their are a lot of predaters, I count the pigs in that, and the desert means no cover to hide. Aproch them and they come to die. I leveled very quickly. Plus the mission was a very long one. Even after I finished placing all beacons, and I did take my time about it, it was still several houers of waiting before I could leave. So I built a base by the drop pod and power leveled while I waited for the timer to go down.I think the game has some problems. It think its predator to herbivore ratio is off. There are a lot of predators. The teraforming made them more aggressive so they would be killing more prey, probly more prey then they needed. Even without the aggressive behavior their are not enough animals for them to eat. I think they did this to give the player something to fight. And they have to be fought, their are a lot of them and they attack often, like in the desert. Their are worms to fight but this being another planet I would hope to see other worldly things to fight instead of constantly attacking animals.The second problem is the grind. This is not the player grinding levels but instead the forced grind. I watched one how too video for the game that sujested watching a movie after everything was done. They were not joking one bit. After all the mission objectives are complete their is sometimes a timer, an actual timer, that has to run down before the mission can be turned in and reward collected. I suspect this is to encourage exploration. This is a big world and thier is much to see but if people only do objective and leave then they don't see it, don't live in it. Problem is that the people that just want to get it done will watch a movie for the timer while the people that want to see the world would do so even without a timer.I like this game and I think it has a lot of potential. It is open world and that means a lot to me. No loading screens at all. Enter a building or move to a new region and it is seamless. In this open world their is a lot to see. The artwork is well done. When looking at the mountains I feel peaceful. The wild is that, wild. It is unmarked and I get to walk through it. Its camping from my living room. I like this game because it is a survival crafting game. The survival is real. I have to eat food and drink water. That might sound like a no brainer but I have played games with "survival" and no need for water. Here their is need for water food and air. As a bonus the food actually does things beyond filling the need. The food provide buffs. Good for planning for a  fight or an adventure. Speaking of adventures, since this actually is a survival game, those adventures have to be planned form route to rations for the road. A lack of planning means death.This game needs work. It does. I can hide behind a rock and a predator cant see me but if I stand up in my house with walls all around me the predators can detect me through the walls. It need work but it is moving in the right direction.  I recommend this game It is worth getting and worth supporting.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: I, literally, stopped playing this game because of it's stupidity in application. Instead of using sprinklers to water crops, you have to use ultra-expensive things like hydroponic crop plots. Scope attachments (at this point) don't even have scopes. And there are various other things that annoy me but you, literally, have to invest DAYS (real time) to get where this game really starts to work right and then, at that point, you have to go to the other side of the map because you've mined the necessary resources away.THe bugs are INSANE and people, who play with me, lose their experience when going back to the station and i let them all go before me because the game cuts people out if the host goes first. I'm just TIRED of it.This game is not a fresh concept, it's an old concept with a slightly different twist. It's survival with air you (the entire world around you can breathe it) can't breathe. No zombies, just you against nature with a really pointless element....you can't breathe the air. Oh you can drink the water, eat all the plant and animal life...but you can't breath the air.The animals are, literally, stupid and i mean stupid for "animals". They will stand there and let a predator kill them even when standing inside a safety area. And where are the "true" fences to keep the Moas in?The space suit is a STUPID mechanic in this game.It is, literally, "man vs wild".I honestly feel like the "space suit" / non-breathable air was a wasted mechanic in the game. I would remove it because it both, gets in the way and makes no sense compared to the other things you can do naturally.This game is cloud saved so anyone can come in and play the game while another player is gone. However, if you "end" the mission early (and leave the other players behind) they all don't get their share of experience so, don't do that. Whoever "hosts" the mission should be the last person to leave the planet.The extreme weather is REALLY impressive and a major factor you have to deal with. Also, if you're hosting a game, be sure to leave LAST and make sure all other players have made it back to the space station first.There are a few cons like the map has "cracks" in it where timber falls into the ground and you lose it sometimes and not all the game mechanics are worked out (May 2022, and things may change in time) so don't let that sway you, it's still a good game.Like in a zombie game, stealth and head-shots count...remember that.There is one thing i find INCREDIBLY stupid about this game, the penalty if you even fall unconscious.Actually, there are probably a lot of coders (with survival games) that might really hate this project because it makes a bunch of them useless, it has everything they have but it far less complicated than some survival games mechanics-wise. Finally, it gets to be a tireless grind and you get tired of this game pretty easily after a couple of weeks.Note: I do not allow comments because this is a "review". A review with comments is no longer a review, but a conversation hence comments defeat the purpose of you telling how "you" perceive the game and not others attempting to question your point of view. A personal review should remain that person's take and no one else's, that's why they have forums....do it there.A word about the coding of this game: I've got games that are more graphically intense than this game and this game "drags" my computer so it's not coded well. When you can compare games that require more power and have better graphics doing well, the hardware isn't the issue.That being said, a true "Gamer" never let's another gamer sway them, what you like or perceive might be totally different from what another likes and there's nothing wrong with that. Play YOUR way.

_childDocuments_.review: Now, what do I say about Icarus? Well first part would be the sheer ambition. The game map is big, I'd go so far as to say Biggly Big, because I keep hiking down the trail and thinking I'm almost there, only to open the map and see that mountain over there is where I need to make my first turn. I should also point out, that that's the first map available, a second has been released which I haven't seen yet, with almost a guarantee of more to follow.The gameplay loop is interesting too, You hit the planet with an objective and have to choose between building up a home base to build better gear and supplies or simply take what you can carry and nomad this baby up. once your mission is done you head back to the pod you landed in and fly back up to payday!On to the station stuff. This is where you equip yourself before each drop, you can use the payouts from completed missions to research and create specialised equipment to take down with you, better jumpsuits, modifiers for said suits, pre-made hammers, pickaxes, knives, bows, armor and even oxygen tanks, Though the best stuff needs something a little more exotic to craft.Spawned randomly around the map are exotic deposits that can be found in small chunks in caves, mined out of the ground in deep ore deposits (which takes some time but is quite safe), or in enzyme geysers (which attract everything in the world that owns teeth). Exotics are the special currency that you can only get from your own discoveries, the missions will pay you but the exotics are your job to find.It should be noted that this is where the game loses all the people who didn't do their research, you lose everything not station-worthy when you leave, meaning your house, any planet-built equipment and anything you brought down with you but left behind when you left. I can see why, rocket fuel is hard to come by when orbiting a somewhat colonised catastrophe and they can't afford to keep metric tons of crudely made tat in the station. The buildings fall over because the planet is routinely hit by massive storms that knock down basically anything not rooted in the floor. Nothing survives those storms, It's a new adventure every drop.You can specialise in certain things too, mining or hunting and such. If you have some pals to play with you can all keep a job to keep the mission running smooth, Jim makes the house because he can keep it cheaper and sturdier. while Mary's off spelunking for gold with her larger inventory and Brian's halfway up a mountain fighting off a jaguar with his nice shiny +15 damage rifle. You all work better together. Anyhoo, this is the kind of game I like, It's accumulative work, your work pays off to make you better every time, and you can always bring in some friends to make Icarus a little bit less hostile! Or you know... get eaten by a polar bear, or a scorpion, or a pack of wolves, or a massive sod-off sandworm.Enjoy Icarus, it wants to kill you.

I don't think it's the biggest deal as long as it gets fixed fairly quickly, which it seems to have done so.Gameplay: Love, love, love it, i've been having a blast with it even when i was playing solo and i can see myself getting lost into it for hours. _childDocuments_.review: At 1st it started like an ark survival evolved game but once you play it how it is supposed to played as missions it gets good.   Take you average survival game. You start you build up your base and the explore the whole world. You make your own fun.  With Icarus you explore sections of the map at a time and complete missions. Build your base up as much as you think you will need for the current mission, complete it, go back into space, come back in a different area with new goals build your base again.   It manages to take what makes survival games fun, like base building, and not get boaring. Most games you build your base once and you are like. "Welp that was fun...now what?"  The environmental effects are some of the best I have seen in a game. When you accidently place a wall torch in your wooden base, because ark has trained you to think this is fine, then frantically try to put out the flames before it engulfs your house, it reminds you of common sense. Also watching it burn with the fire physics was oddly satisfying.

_childDocuments_.review: Update after a year: I've spent a good amount of time playing this lately. Unfortunately everything in my original review still holds. The grind for late game items is ridiculous with the number of crafting benches and components and materials required, and this is made much worse by the lack of any kind of pinnable to-do list. You have to remember every step - this is made at this bench, that is made at that bench, those things are used in this other bench to make this part, which is one of 4 I need to make this thing. And you have to repeat this every single mission. Enemies just run at you. They will often kill you without much chance to use any skill in the fight, unless you can jump on to a rock and cheese them.The open world map with missions is a cool feature, and is how the whole game should be, Unfortunately the missions there are very limited.This game is a wasted opportunity. It would be amazing if they took the world and the missions and replaced all of the frustrating grinding and crafting with fun grinding and crafting.==========The good: This is a fairly fun co-op survival game. It does a few things quite differently - it is timed mission based, with missions allowing anywhere up to a few weeks real world time (but much less in game time). You can hunt, craft, farm as well as do your objectives. Its not super hardcore survival, diseases and things are usually just timed debuffs, but you have to manage food, oxygen and water too.The bad: The worst thing about the game to me is the grind. Grind is generally fine in games but it has to be enjoyable too. Some missions might require you to build certain things but those things are both level gated and also require unlocking with potentially lots of prior requirements to unlock on the tree. So you are left grinding XP to level up for hours and hours and hours, but the grinding is not really that fun. In early game the most efficient way to level is to craft stacks of bandages, destroy then, and recraft over and over. This is not compelling gameplay in any way. Holding down F in a forest is also a pretty good way to level up early on, again not really that enjoyable.For a game about PVE, the E is pretty underwhelming. There's not a lot of strategy from the wolves and bears, they just run at you. It's fairly easy to cheese them by luring them to water and swimming backwards pumping them full of arrows, or just get them stuck on a rock.Later game there's a fairly crazy amount of crafting benches and components required, without any kind of automation or crafting list supported it is a bit annoying tracking allll the different materials you need to craft the materials to craft the materials to make the thing you want to make.Graphic performance is also absolutely appalling. I am getting down to 14fps with a 1080 and i5-10600 with a mix of high and medium settings. And while it looks good, it doesn't look good enough to justify that performance.Overall: I can't recommend this game until they spend a year or so fixing it.

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't sure how I would feel about session-based survival, but the majority of timers I've seen through my progression thus far seem very forgiving for what's asked of you. You have a lot of time to explore, and most importantly, establish a presence so that you can prepare for the task ahead.Pros:- Very strong graphics, and other than the occasional blip when I run through a dense forest during extreme weather, it runs very smooth on a 3080- Amazing weather effects that can actually impact the environment and your settlement- Great sound design, the clinks and clangs of tools feel and sound great, and the atmospheric sounds are pleasant during the day, and terrifying at night- Co-op for up to 8 people; I play games with a group of roughly 10 friends and acquaintances, so finding games most of us can play together is pretty difficult- Deep tech and character progression with a lot of options, especially when factoring in multiplayer and specializing alongside friends- Satisfying destruction of resources as you gather from them- You keep all of your character progression between "prospects" (missions)Cons:- The introduction to the game is pretty rough as of this writing, it does a very poor job of setting the player up for the scanning mission- There's no "take all" hotkey that I can find, which is surprising given how common the hotkey is in games revolving around a lot of loot/resource collection and management- Inventory is restricted by both slots and weight, so unless you've played games like DayZ, it's going to be a bit of a headache to get used to early onThat's it, not a lot of cons for me at the time of writing. I will come back and update the review once I've had more time in the game. Here's my longer-winded overview on it:The truly interesting element of this game is that its progression revolves around session-based "prospects" where you complete various missions for a reward. The catch is that you're on a timer (though the timer seems rather forgiving).If you successfully complete missions, you get rewarded with special currency to progress through various equipment options to make the initial start of each prospect a little easier.You also level up while on missions and can unlock equipment, workstations, tools, weapons, etc. as well as talents that make you more effective at performing certain actions (or make you more resistant to the environmental effects of the planet).It's been a lot of fun so far, as a survival fan. Word of warning, if you don't like unfinished products then just add it to your Wishlist for now.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Refreshing with wonderful potential, but simply not ready for mass consumption... yet.There's a lot of great things about this game. Enjoy the player progression, absolutely love the prospects system, and visually it's a stunning experience. That being said, as of this review it needs *a lot* of refinement.The dynamic difficulty curve is definitely way off right now. You'll go from wolves being a threat, to a joke. Bears will go from being easy to impossible to kill w/o glitching them in the water. Predators never give up once they've seen you and are currently just a boolean "You die" or "You don't die", with no option to flee. In many cases you're simply unable to avoid due to a valley or other bottleneck in the terrain.You'll see a lot of other posts from socially challenged people that will tell you to just stop whining and work on your situational awareness. As a long-time player of the survival genre, there is a lot of truth to working on situational awareness in this game, but there have been dozens of instances where a friend watched a bear or wolf literally spawn on my head, in the open, without any warnings to indicate I was in trouble beyond hearing "We're dead" over discord.Stealth hasn't been much help in avoiding bears either. I can crouch and walk right up to a wolf or boar even when they are looking in my direction, but a bear will come charging from the top of a hill or cliff while I'm crouched at the bottom waiting for my health to regen.The weather system is a wonderful addition but it's just an absurd amount of RNG right now. While playing with a friend, we had 3 thunderstorms back-to-back, without any pause between them, and ended up spending nearly 30 mins just sitting around repairing our wooden shelter as it was deteriorating at an astounding rate, and we still lost half our stations when all was said and done. The weather should be rather unpredictable, but there needs to be some kind of limitation to the frequency of the more severe weather events.While I'm marking this review as not recommended, I'd like to append "yet". Once the kinks are worked out, this will be a prized addition to my collection of survival games.

_childDocuments_.review: FRUSTRATION. This is my summary of this walking/running simulator.The horrible game mechanics (missions/prospects):This game is sold as a survival game where you can develop you character, build a nice and cozy base and .... But don't be fooled , what you really do in each "mission/proscpect" is : RUN  for an hour, do ONE stupid action and RUN back to you ship during another hour. Building a base only add to frustration as it don't bring you anything better to complete the objective.No exploration:The full map seems to be quite big but during a prospect you are limited to  a portion of it.  Sadly, you run to your objective and don't spend time exploring because there is nothing of interest to find. (No dunjons, secrets areas, hidden deadly beasts ... _childDocuments_.review: I can't currently recommend this game. I know I don't have a lot of playtime, but this all feels way to familiar. I wish companies would have learned from the disastrous launch of No Mans Sky. Don't promise things, or show gameplay with features you aren't going to include when you launch the game. If you show it off in a trailer, but hit a snag or developmental issue where it can't be included let your fans know. This isn't an ALIEN world, at all. It's basically the mountains of New Hampshire or Colorado. There is no Alien anything really (Yeah I saw the Mini Worm). All the wildlife is the same here on Earth. This game reminds me of The Forest, just with better graphics, and no homicidal cannibals lurking around every corner and underground. However, on Earth it is a hell of a lot easier to kill. On Icarus, ha! Let me spawn in brand new noob level 1. "Hello, mister wolf." Oh you are attacking me, sweet three four swings of my stone axe, and you're dead, but I'm at 25% health. Eat some berries. Health slowly rises, what's that in the distance? "It's 3 wolves, I got this . . . Oh ♥♥♥♥ . . .they're all level 18 or higher . . . Mommy . . ." That's the thing, the wildlife in here is hard, almost too hard especially being lower levels. Second mission in, I go to activate a relay, and then a warning wildlife is attacking, and I am instantly surrounded by 3 level 22 or higher bears and a level 20 wolf. I'm dead. This happened again and again. Even with weapons. For a game that says co-op and single player, this is not single player. Trying to play this by yourself is extremely hard.  This in of itself wouldn't be so bad, but now lets talk about the in game timer. This is based off of real world time. Not in game time. That means if you don't get off that rock before the timer hits zero, PERMA - DEATH. You lose everything, including your progression. Doesn't matter if you have a real world issue where you physically can't log in, once the timer starts it doesn't stop. If this was an in game timer it wouldn't be so bad, and could really up the sense of urgency and paranoia of having to get off the planet or risk being left behind, like the live action trailer. Then they could implement a survival timer, where you have to try and survive until the next drop occurs. It would really add to the gameplay element. It would also allow for in game critical events or rescue type operations where you have a very short window of time to complete a specific task or emergency. Also you better like to BUILD, REBUILD, and REBUILD some more. Better name yourself Bob the Builder. I mean literally every . . . time . . . you . . . go . . . on . . . a . . . prospect . . . Every single time. Nothing remains when you leave Icarus. It all disappears, which turns the base building/crafting into more of a repetitive chore, than a fun experience. This too, could be better implemented especially if they allow for Semi-Permanent structures and supplies. This could have been an extremely cool game mechanic, where your buildings and supplies began to degrade overtime. The longer you wait between drops the more degradation that occurs. Lastly, I was pretty excited for this game, and was looking forward to a new spin on the survival/base building mechanic, but this isn't it. There are some cool things in the game, lie the water effects, and the way trees and rocks break down as you collect them. That is much more realistic, but way more things need to be implemented before I can recommend buying this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, I don't even know where to begin but let's name a few reasons:- For a full release title, performance is . I've spent well over  hours trying to find reasonable settings and I still haven't found it yet.- Multiple "coming soon" crafting items  missions. If this is a full release game, there is absolutely no reason to have something labelled "coming soon" unless the game isn't in a finished state.- Several errors left in the game that  - The games description on Steam mentions . The only thing in the game that is alien is a cave worm, a bigger cave worm (boss) and Oxite. Everything else is earthbound: pumpkins, berries, carrots, squash, watermelon, etc. The wildlife? Wolves, bears, cougars, hyenas, fish, elephants, zebras, etc. Not a single thing here is alien. - If you go back and take a look a their earlier announcement trailers, you'll notice  actual alien creatures, including VEHICLES! None of that is present in their "full release game". If your defense to this one is "they said it'll be added in later" then you've proved the entire point of this review.- Animal levels in the game have zero purpose outside of a few extra XP given. They don't do more damage and they don't have more health. - Missions are clearly copy/pasted and rushed. Go to three areas, scan them, leave (or close to that same formula). - Outposts  completely leave out predators, ultimately handicapping you on essential resources for advancement. No option is given to add those predators into the game at any point. Considering the desert biome is mostly predators, I can only imagine how empty that biome actually is in sandbox mode.Devs, I appreciate the free key and effort you've put into this game so far and I will admit there is a fun game sitting here. This isn't your fault, the project leads failed you on this one and rushed it out for holiday sales. Shame on them releasing this as a Full Release title.Yes, I left a review at 1.4 hours. It didn't take long to see this wasn't a finished game. Yes I continued to play for ~30 more hours. To those who feel this invalidates my review, that's fine. For those looking to understand ; I spent ~10 hours troubleshooting looking for the "my game runs fine" middle ground I kept seeing in the comments. Needless to say, the game still runs horribly. I continued to play beyond those extra troubleshooting hours because there IS something fun about the game. I can't tell what, but there is a foundation there for something great. I also wanted to see what else the game had to offer. To see if things got better. I think that's fair. If anything the fact that I  don't recommend this game after sinking more time into it should further valid my review. I gave it a fair shot.I've been reading comments mentioning that  simply because I received this game for free. I encourage you to think a bit differently regarding your stance. The fact I have received a game for free doesn't mean it automatically receives a positive review. If that was the case, you'd never get an honest review. If I'm recommending against this game despite getting a free key, that should speak volumes to you.This is typical PR speak. If we can just keep it real with each other, everyone would benefit from honesty and transparency. You failed to reassure me or anyone else. You managed to admit nothing outside of you , yet in the very next sentence you state  but what you described is  what an early access game is. Don't get me wrong, I'm on board with you all fixing the game. However this is an incredibly misleading and dangerous tactic to advertise your game as a full release when it is nowhere close to being full release.If I had to take a guess, they fell behind on development, bought basic assets for resources/ animals and tossed it into the game either as the final cut or as placeholders until they can actually finish the game. They labelled it full release because they wanted to avoid the stigma "early access"  brings. This is easily comparable to the original launch of No Man's Sky; Over promised, under delivered, fix later.

ICARUS is a session-based PvE survival game for up to eight co-op players.

Endure a savage alien wilderness on Icarus, humanity's greatest mistake. Survive its brutal environment as you explore, harvest, craft and hunt while seeking your fortune.

From their orbital station, prospectors drop to the planet surface for limited time sessions, where they learn to endure the alien environment, complete faction missions and search for valuable exotic materials. Those that survive return to orbit as seasoned veterans, converting their exotics into advanced technology, and taking on ever more challenging drops with newfound knowledge. Those that get left behind... are lost forever.

For almost two decades, this series of tactics-RPG visual novels has been beloved by Japanese fans for its spectacular music, art, characters, and story. Now it finally returns to its origins on PC. This sequel to Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen , first released more than a decade after the original game, is a great place to jump in to the series! The local monstrosities nearly devour you before you meet your rescuer, a beautiful girl named Kuon—who has animal ears and a tail. She names you Haku⸺ The Japanese hit tactics-RPG visual novel series returns to PC at last!

_childDocuments_.review: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception and Mask of Truth are two halves of the same story and can't really be broken up. Thus, I will be reviewing them as a whole.This is my favorite VN of all time. The story, characters, sound, art, world, and gameplay all come together to make something magical and I think a lot of other people- even those new to the genre- will be able to enjoy it as well so I’m just going to gush about it and hope that convinces you to try it.Overall, the story will take you about 80 hours to get through on your first go. It seems like a lot, but that time is used very effectively. The characters are organically built up and the way I got attached to them over time is something I’ve only really felt the likes of in the original Mass Effect trilogy. The world gets very fleshed out with both ancient secrets and more mundane details that make it a very rich, interesting place to be. The story takes its time setting up big scenes so they hit like a truck and then paces itself with more lighthearted moments like wannabe Robin Hood pitching gold bars through people’s windows or giving a catgirl a suggestive backrub or getting drunk and stupid with your bros. Then it’s back to political maneuvering, destiny, war-crimes, mecha Godzilla battles, and suffering.The 2D artwork is absolutely gorgeous. The style is distinctive, the artists actually know anatomy, the sprawling landscapes make the world come alive, and the coloring is superb. The 3D sections were designed to run on the Vita so they’re chunky, but they don’t really distract. The screenshots can tell you more about this than words can, so I’ll move on.I still listen to the soundtrack on Spotify on a regular basis. Not every track is fully orchestrated, but even the parts where they didn’t splurge on the production values have excellent compositions that pull you further into the mood. When Utawarerumono pulls out all the stops, it won’t lose to any other video game OST and the way those songs are placed elevate the already good scenes into another world. It almost feels mean at some places. Like, I’m already an emotional basket case, why do you have to rob me of any semblance of dignity I have left by putting that on? On top of that, you have great voice acting for every line in the game. My only complaint about the audio is that one track, Sadame, is underused for how good it is.Utawarerumono has tactics gameplay sections but they’re by no means the main attraction since they only make up 10-20% of the playtime. They’re not going to dethrone tactics giants like Disgaea, but that’s not their job. Their job is to compliment the story, bring you into the action, and break up long sections of reading. For that purpose, they do quite well. If you’re a tactics veteran, there’s enough depth and polish to keep you entertained to the end. If you’re a tactics noob, there’s a turn rewind feature that will make sure you get through just fine. For major encounters, the gameplay is integrated surprisingly well with the story, and the final bosses of each part are made with a lot of care and extra touches so they don’t lag behind how bonkers the story is going.Mask of Deception has to focus a lot on world building and setup for story to come and doesn’t quite hit its stride, so it’s “only” great. Good news is, that it gets even better. There is also a bit of a hump in the middle where there’s a long slice-of-life section that drags a bit, even if each individual part is well done. However, you’re well rewarded for getting past it and it’s a minor inconvenience compared to the worst parts of other great games.

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest, I have a love-hate relationship with this game. After the plot reaches its climax, the story is really exciting, and people can't wait to know the ending. However, the foreshadowing and daily life of this work in the early stage are a bit too long, and it is easy for most players to lose interest in the game in advance. The combination of traditional Japanese RPG and visual novel is a cool decision for players who have never been exposed to such games before, but the content of the game cannot be said to be perfect. The main storyline of this work took me about 20 hours. As a supplement and improvement to the details of the plot, Dream Arena also extends the RPG battle part of the game, suitable for those players who like SLG.The music and character design are both wonderful. This game is suitable for players who want to try a classic Japanese RPG game or a visual novel of fantasy world. However, the shortcomings of this work and the problem of the player group are destined to be difficult for this game and series of works to expand the audience.

_childDocuments_.review: Having heard great things about Utawarerumono, it was obvious that I was going to play it at some point. The only issue I personally had here is that I’m not really fond of playing on a handheld, although it offers a lot more mobility than a PC does. Lucky for me, Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception and Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth got a PC release after the PS Vita version launched back then in 2017. It was a surprise for me as well when the games got announced, along with the first game Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen. You see, Mask of Deception is a sequel to the first entry and takes place in the same world, although supposedly it’s possible to start with the, technically, second game, as long as Mask of Truth is played after it since it’s the grand finale and continues the second entry.Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception works with amnesia and thus, our protagonist suddenly wakes up without any prior memories. On top of that, it’s quite cold as he finds himself in a snowscape, but that’s not all, the world overall is unfamiliar and new to him. Suddenly, he gets attacked by a monster he never saw before. While trying to escape, a mysterious girl is appearing who saves his life, although there is something strange about her as she owns animal ears and a tail but seems human otherwise. Having found him, she feels responsible for him as he probably won’t be able to survive all alone. When she introduces herself as Kuon, she learns about his amnesia and decides on his name, Haku.The first thing that comes to my mind when I recall what I heard about Utawaremono would be heavily story-driven. Although I enjoyed its story and reveals a lot, which I never saw coming at all, most of the game tends to be rather light-hearted and full of slice-of-life scenes. The player will get through a lot of typical Japanese comedic scenes, just like in an average anime. Sometimes I found the scenes where Haku gets beaten up by several girls quite amusing and other times I found it was a little bit over the top but I suppose it was meant to be this way during picking up a lot of the harem anime premise. Whilst I didn’t expect this game to include that many slice-of-life scenes, it offers fan-service scenes as well in a, once again, comedic style.Yet Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception containing a lot of light-hearted scenes isn’t a bad thing at all, but it greatly contributed to the character development. You see, this entry is supposed to be a build-up for Mask of Truth, so it makes sense that the prior game functions as an introduction where it mostly gives their players a better understanding of their personalities. To be honest, I ended up sympathizing with each character and even when the game turns enemies into allies, I could still easily accept them due to their lovely personalities. Admittedly, I’ve always been a fan of several friends sticking together even during hardships, which is definitely the case here. It’s just wonderful when I saw the cast constantly helping out each other and never betraying each other.Visual novel elements aren’t the only thing available here but the player goes through different kinds of battles as well to spice the story up. After all, when gameplay gets added, it makes the game a lot more interesting. In Mask of Deception, the battles are only a very minor part and the player will find themselves mostly reading. The few fighting sequences that are spread through the game are implemented really well into the story and always fit the current happenings. Overall, they work like a turn-based RPG, although the goal isn’t always to defeat the enemies. Battle-wise, there are different preset combos of attacks, which contain several combos that you can unlock with level-ups. After the first time beating a stage, the members get a lot of XP, although it’s harder when you want to grind outside of the story.Luckily, when the player achieves a game-over, Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception is generous enough to give the option of either restarting the battle or rewind to your desired point. Sometimes, when the fighting scenes included follow up battles besides the first one, restarting brings you back to the very first battle, which turned out pretty annoying since the first one is always easily beatable, but since fallen allies remain dead for the follow-up fight when they’re tied together, it makes sense that the player finds themselves back to square one. Additionally, I liked the idea of the combo chains although they’re predetermined as the player has to actively press a key to trigger them, whilst I still have no clue how to trigger later attacks, there is also the option of just using the auto-chain feature where the game perfectly triggers all attacks.Graphic-wise, Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception works with two different styles. One of them is the typical presentation of a visual novel with a gorgeous art style and CGs. The game works with subtle animations here and there that greatly helped with the immersion during thrilling fighting, where you’re not having a battle per se but only read about it, and comedic scenes. Other than that, the game switches to 3D visuals that are even more animated and was a refreshing change. The player can already tell when a fight might very likely come up and I found this style very charming as it reminds me of the older JRPGs I’ve used to play.Whilst I was first confused about Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception containing that many slice-of-life scenes, I found it was essential for the build-up. The player doesn’t know what is happening at first, as they get thrown into this unknown world and are first getting familiar with the characters before the story gets revealed in any way, but that made the story only better for me due to me being already utterly attached to each of them. The fighting parts became more and more engaging to me until the last arc was very suspenseful and I ended up rooting for the cast. The battles offered a lot of refreshing change as well so the player doesn’t only have to read but can interact with the game as well, although most of the time, they will still find themselves reading a visual novel. That being said, Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception is a game with a great story, once you get past the long light-hearted introduction, with engaging battles, that made me especially curious about how Mask of Truth will turn out.

_childDocuments_.review: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception is a VN/J-RPG about an amnesiac man named Haku and a woman named Kuon that go on a journey together with various characters. I'm not going to talk about every single thing that happened in the story, nor will I recant it. I'm just going to say what I think made the story great. The game begins with Haku waking up in a strange tent with no memories (he even forgets his name), with a woman who has been tending to him while he slept. I usually dislike amnesia stories - I find many of them annoying, because usually something stupid happens, like the amnesiac character hits their head on a brick and gets all of their lost memories back. Or they see and/or hear something they had heard/seen before they lost their memories, and that somehow causes them to regain all of the memories they lost. But that doesn't happen in this story. Haku's amnesia is used as a tool for us, the player, to experience the strange world around him anew, which allows us to gain exposition we otherwise wouldn't have if, say, Haku didn't lose his memories and already had experience with that world.The woman who had been taking caring of Haku while he was asleep is Kuon, the headstrong animal-human hybrid girl. I'm not exactly sure  animal, but it doesn't really matter. Kuon and Haku's dynamic was very enjoyable. Haku's carefree, lazy, and brash personality clashes with Kuon's responsible, determined, and hardworking personality, which creates some enjoyable moments of comic relief. Some might ship them, but their relationship is more like a brother-sister one, Haku being the younger sibling.There are  of characters in this game that all have a significant part in the story. While I do think some got much more attention than others (*cough* Nekone *cough cough*), the game does a pretty good job of juggling everyone. It doesn't feel like the characters are crammed in all at once ― they gradually take their place within the story at times that make sense, meaning they don't feel forced. It was impressive.I was surprised to see the amount of slice-of-life moments/subplots, but they actually weren't a drag on the overall plot-line ― they helped me feel closer to the characters, while making me believe the characters actually got to know each other in a way that made the ending have its impact.The combat in Utawarerumono is fun. It uses a grid-based playing field with a turn-based system, where enemies and characters are splayed across the map. The frequency of a character's turn depends on their SPD (speed), which can be increased along with other attributes by using BP. I like that the combat is sort of like a game of chess ― you move your pawns around the board in a strategic way, so you find openings to attack, while avoiding being attacked by enemies. In some stages, you really have to try to think ahead, because a move you made 10 turns ago can affect the outcome of the current turn. It does feel kind of bogus because that takes nearly a level of insight fortunetellers have, but it's certainly possible to plan ahead in some instances. Another cool thing are the action chains. These are a set of attacks performed by a specific character, and if timed correctly, can land critical hits on an enemy. What I liked was each character's action chain is different, even characters that shared the same "class" (there aren't distinct classes in this game, but there are characters that have similar abilities).However, compared to the amount of VN in this game, the combat parts aren't much (with the exception of post-game dream arena). I would say it's about 75% VN and 25% combat, so people who would strongly prefer a game that prioritizes gameplay over story, I suggest passing on this game.The English translation is perfect. I don't recall ever seeing a grammar mistake, misspelling, or misuse of a word. Also, the UI is smooth, fits with the theme of the game, uncluttered, and isn't distracting at all.I loved the glossary. It was a unique feature I'd never seen in a VN before this one, and I really appreciated it being there. Being able to read extensive knowledge on the people, animals, location, and culture about the in-game world was very helpful. It wasn't a crutch, and it isn't needed due to the story not giving enough exposition ―it's there for players who might want to read up more about the world the story built.The art is purely phenomenal. The line-art is crisp, the coloring and shading makes it pop, and brings the world to life alongside the writing. At some points, I just stared at the screen because the art was so beautiful. It's the reason I have so many screenshots of this game. Amazing game that has beautiful art and music, and has great writing and characters. It's understandable if you'd rather wait until it's on sale, but it's completely worth full-price for 65-70+ hours of gameplay. It's apparent a lot of meticulous care went into this game. The music, art, writing, and voice-acting come together to create an awesome experience. This game ruined VNs for me, because this one raised the bar.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all this is part one of the Utawarerumono duology, which is the sequel to the original Utawarerumono. I highly recommend watching the anime for the original Utawarerumono (the 2006). While it is not entirely necessary to enjoy part 1, it will really help understand the world and some of the events that occur. Also Part 2 will have a bunch of moments that will be difficult to understand without watching it. Furthermore, DO NOT TOUCH THE ITSUWARI NO KAMEN ANIME I REPEAT DO NOT TOUCH IT WITH A 30 FOOT POOL, it takes away many plot points and overall is not very well done and will leave you very confused so I repeat DO NOT TOUCH IT. In the case you have though, its okay you can still read this, as mentioned before, many big plot points were left out of the anime, and many scenes in general were not in the anime, so reading the visual novel is still a wonderful experience. Also I highly recommend avoiding using youtube to listen to any of the soundtracks in the show, many of the CGs they use for backgrounds can be big plot spoilers so until your done the entire series I recommend avoiding youtubing anything related to this series.Anyways enough warnings time to start gushing about this series.The Utawarerumono has official taken the spot of my favorite series of all times. Everything about this series is fantastic as heck and I cannot even begin to express how much I love this series. Part 1 is a great intro to the duology as we enter a world filled with many mysteries surrounding it while at the same time being introduced to one of my favorite casts of characters out there. Everyone is super loveable and they only grow to be more loveable as the story progresses. This part has plenty of slice of life moments that I personally enjoyed a bunch but even if your not the biggest fan of slice of life, if it is something you can at least tolerate, it is a important build up for the more serious moments of the story. The strategy section of the game is pretty meh but its tolerable and only like 1% of the actual game and is something that can be easily breezed though. There is so much I want to talk about this story, the characters and everything about it but I want to avoid as many spoilers as possible so ill just say this I rate this game 10000000000/10 it is so good and If it’s a journey you decide to undertake, it is a journey you wont regret going on. Also Kuon is best girl <3

_childDocuments_.review: Update: I finished the whole trilogy and here are my thoughts on this game:- Utawarerumono is a visual novel series, developed by Aquaplus. Currently the main games in this series that you can find on Steam are Utawarerumono: Prelude to the fallen, Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception and Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth. This is the second game in the trilogy.-  Yes but I highly recommend you to finish Prelude to the fallen first because the events, the characters will have much more depth if you already knew them in Prelude to the fallen.- No. This is not an eroge. if you want Eroge, you can play the first game but keep in mind that the steam version of it doesn't have R18, because it was a port from console.- Getting the whole trilogy on sale is highly recommended.- It is highly recommended that you should finish the first game before playing this game. The story is fantastic and the world building, the character development throughout the story is awesome. You will enjoy every moment in this game, even fillers.- - Personally I think in term of story, this game is more well written than the first game.- The game has a 3D turn-based tactical strategy element, which is very refreshing compared to any traditional visual novel. The game mechanic is also improved from the first game (like new chain rings, counterattack,...) but some things like Unit rotating is removed, which is, to me, a big stepdown. Other than that, the gameplay is awesome. - You can either play as a hardcore gamer in hard mode or just enjoy the story with pretty simple turn-based gameplay.- The game's default resolution is 720p, which is a real disappointment to be honest.- Character sprites are gorgeous. the CGs are even beyond that. - I'm not gonna judge the 3D graphic because this is, mainly, a visual novel. 3D characters look really cute tho :3- This game has a very stacked cast. You can find Inori Minase, Risa Taneda , Saori Hayami and a tons of famous seiyuus in this game. You won't be disappointed by the character VAs- The BGMs are superb. Some of them are reused from the first vn, which is very nostalgic. - The OP is sung Suara, who also have sung most of Utawarerumono songs in anime and visual novel. Suara and Utawarerumono, you can't find a more perfect duo.Conclusion: Awesome game, awesome series. it's a must play. Also if you want to watch the anime, Mask of Truth's adaptation, Futari no Hakuoro is coming this July 2022.

_childDocuments_.review: All in all, it wasn't a bad experience. I gave a thumb down because for how much the game costs, I felt like I played half a game. My playtime says 34 hours, but the game really only starts in the last 15 hours or so. For a VN, the story is decent. In particular, I like the world-building and the political intrigue a lot. However, there are 2 problems with the story-telling. First, there are ways too many slice-of-life events, especially in the first half. Slice-of-life is nice to build up the bonds between the characters. However, the amount of these "let's cook together" or "let's hang out together" events is excessive at time. There was a stretch of almost 4-5 hours straight of these events. Second, the game left way too much for the sequel. I get it. Every game these days tries to set up a series. But this game goes too far. As I said, the first half is just filler after filler. Even when the game picks up in the second half, some events are left unexplained for no other reasons than to sell the sequel. I can't use an actual example from the game, so I'll make up a similar example. Let's say you meet a guy that carries around a pink cat. However, NOBODY ever thinks to ask about the pink cat. There is no reason why nobody should not be curious. They just don't ask because well, you need to buy the sequel to know. This is just plain manipulative.The gameplay is a decent grid-based TBS. Overall, gameplay is pretty easy because your team often outnumbers the enemies. The biggest problem of the gameplay is actually that it does not happen often enough. There's only 17 or so stages. Each stage is also very short. The game can use more battle stages early on. Sting is one of the developers of this game, so the gameplay has the same issue as another Sting's game, Tears to Tiara. The issue is that damage is too high. Anybody on your team or the enemies can kill someone in one-shot or be killed in one-shot easily. Random mob with their normal attack often takes off 60 to 70% of HP. Because damage is so easy to come by, none of the other stuffs like buffing or sigil matter as much. Battles become a damage race. You're trying to burst the enemies down before they do the same to you. Speed scaling is also an issue. I have a battle in which a character takes 11 turns while another moves 3 times. Not much to say about graphic. The background drawings are very nice. Character designs however are disappointing. All the girls are drawn with this "big-eye" anime style that is, quite frankly, ugly. The guys end up looking way better ironically because their eyes are normal scale. The game text goes on and on about how some characters have goddess-like beauty. All I can see are the same 8 year-old giant-eye anime face painted on top of different hairs.Overall, it's not a bad game. I plan to go and buy the sequel right after writing this review to be honest. However, I feel like the game goes too far to get you to buy the sequel. It felt manipulative at times. There's a right way to set up a sequel and a wrong way. This is the wrong way.

_childDocuments_.review: Utawarerumono. It is one of the popular Japanese franchise series developed by Aquaplus. The series is a tactics & visual-novel hybrid with an emphasis on story, nice art, and impressive soundtracks. It originated on PC back in 2002. Since then it has led to 2 anime series, with the 3rd currently in the works, and the variety of other spin-off projects. This time DMM GAMES and ShiraVN played a major role in bringing the game to Steam globally.If you're the old gamer who already played the first episode, you can feel the nostalgia, because you can meet the Utawarerumono world after a considerable time has passed from the first episode. And if you are new to this series, you will continue to have an interesting curiosity about the worldview and background of this series. FYI, it's okay to start with this episode, Mask of Deception first.The game is quite kind. For users who don't know the first episode, this game slowly explains on worldviews and terms. As a result, story progression has a rather slow pace, but this means that you can enjoy the game leisurely. Starting with your daily relationship with them, exciting events and battles await you. At least playtime is over 30 hours. This game keeps the basics of SRPG well and the visual novel part is of high quality.Depending on the view point, your evaluation or feelings may vary in this game. When we put each series into the one called Utawarerumono, this trilogy is a masterpiece. But if you look at the Mask of Deception separately, this may be somewhat lacking. The various stories with the characters and the description of the game worldview fully illustrate the appeal of this series, but the main story is rarely progressed.Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception. This is a pretty welcome series. It features nice SRPG & ADV hybrid with much more polished anime artworks and details. In Japan, the series has sold hundreds of thousands of copies. Of course, this second episode may be somewhat lacking as a standalone. Main story progress is slower and the number of battles is relatively small compared to other episodes. Nevertheless, if you remember this game and its animations, this will be a good gift for you, and new users will be a good opportunity to get to know the charm of the series. Recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: Nearly three years after it was first released in the west on PS4 and Vita, us PC players finally get the chance to play Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception and Mask of Truth, the second and third games in the Utawarerumono series. It's about time honestly, as these are some games I have been wanting to play since I first watched the anime adaptation years ago.So for those unfamiliar with it, Utawarerumono is a series of visual novels with tactical RPG elements. The gameplay consists of the player going from reading various story events and dialogue to tactical, turn-based battles on a grid. As with most VNs that have gameplay elements, the focus is not on the gameplay, but rather on the story. However, with Mask of Deception and Mask of Truth, the gameplay is actually pretty good and doesn't feel like it was just tacked onto the experience. It may be no Disgaea, but it has a decent amount of depth to it at least, much more so than I often see with such VN hybrids. The game also provides a couple difficulty options to accommodate for both those that just want to experience the story and those that want more challenging gameplay. On normal difficulty, the battles are pretty much a breeze, but on hard difficulty, not so much.As for the actual story, well, that's something that Mask of Deception and Mask of Truth do really well. Although Mask of Deception is technically the second game in the series, it is set up in such a way as to make it easy for newcomers to enjoy. I personally have never played the first game (which is simply titled "Utawarerumono" and does not have an official English release yet) and had no problems getting into Mask of Deception. The same cannot be said for Mask of Truth though, which absolutely requires that you play Mask of Deception first, lest you be really confused as to what's going on. For those that still want to experience the first game in some form, the 2006 anime is generally considered a good adaptation. I watched it years ago and, while I may not remember much of it, I liked it enough to want to get into the games.Once you actually get into the story, you'll be met with some well-written characters, a vibrant fantasy setting that's big on world-building, and some pretty good overall pacing. The games provide a good mix of serious storytelling and more character-oriented slice of life scenes as well. In fact, I like to think of the two games as brothers. Mask of Deception is the younger brother, who is rather innocent and just wants to have fun in this fantasy world with all of its neat characters. Mask of Truth, on the other hand, is the older brother who has lost his innocence and has experienced the hardships of life. While Mask of Deception does have its serious moments, Mask of Truth is when the real story story kicks in, when everything starts coming together. It's quite the ride and there's a good reason why Mask of Truth is sitting at the #12 spot on VNDB's list of highest-rated visual novels.The art and music, as with the story, are also pretty good in both games. I ran the game at 1440p and, while that is an upscale from 720p, the art looked fine and I didn't notice any blatantly blurry assets or backgrounds. It was definitely some good news, as I'm a big fan of the fantasy aesthetic that the games go for. The music also perfectly matches this aesthetic, with a great blend of energetic battle themes and more laid-back, traditional tracks for the game's dialogue scenes. As someone that has already been listening to these soundtracks for years, it was cool to finally hear this music in-game.And of course, seeing as how these two games have never been released on PC, I should mention the quality of their port. To sum it up, it's pretty good as far as VN ports go. There's all the standard settings one would expect in a VN release, including text speed, auto-mode speed, skip options, and a voice cutoff toggle. However, both games go one step further with fullscreen, borderless, and window options, multiple resolution support, completely rebindable keyboard controls, protagonist voice toggling, and even customizable button prompts dependent on what type of controller you're using. Some of these may sound pretty standard, but with visual novels, sometimes they are hard to come by, so it's nice to see them included here.And before I wrap up this review, I should bring up the censorship question. Both games were released as 15+ titles in Japan, so there's no H-scenes like in the original 2002 PC game. This version of Mask of Truth is the exact same as the Japanese version, but this version of Mask of Deception has one CG that has been changed from the Japanese release. I'll go ahead and throw that CG up on-screen so you can see what was changed. It's a very minor change, but I know that a lot of VN fans are passionate about the subject, so it needs to be noted regardless.Overall though, both Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception and Mask of Truth are solid games all things considered. Great art, great music, gameplay that actually doesn't feel like a distraction from the main story, and a story that's both unique and well-written. The two games have a lot going for them and the fact that they're actually decent PC ports is also a nice bonus. It's about time we got them on PC and now it's just a wait to complete the trilogy with the release of Prelude to the Fallen, a remaster of the first game that is also slated to release on PC.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: Utawarerumono is a pretty old and famous series (especially in Japan). The first game released in 2002 and was ported to consoles later. It was an adult tactical role-playing visual novel. Yes, adult, there's a lot of R18 scenes in it. However, it was not the main focus of the game. Both the writing and gameplay was pretty much excellent, leaving positive feedback from players and reviews everywhere.  Later in 2006 an anime adaptation was released, featuring great animation (for 2006) and amazing OST.  I watched the anime about 12 years ago and around that time also completed the original 2002 PC game with an english fan translation. The main point here is that even if you didn't play original game or didn't watch anime, you can still fully enjoy Utawarerumono: Mask of DeceptionRemake for the first game been already released in english under a title Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen, so it's just a matter of time when it will be available on Steam. It's already confirmed that all 3 games will be on PC. 1. Utawarerumono(2002) or (remake) Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen (will be available later on Steam)2. Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception 3. Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth - the grand finale of this series.  Okay, the most important information right off the bat.EAT THIS, WINDOWS 10!I switched to Windowed Mode and didn't got into any troubles so far.I. , i tried to play with both for awhile to check. I settled down with a gamepad, though. Any gamepad is fine, as long as it resembles something like XBox or Dualshock controllers.II. The second most concern i saw is "720p/30FPS". Oh, come on! This is a visual novel with turn-based strategy RPG gameplay, what would 60 FPS accomplish here? Better text scrolling speed? The game is perfectly fine as it is. It would be an entirely different matter if it was an action/fast-paced game, though. III. And the last one , there was only 1 problem scene, where's a small kid received some spanks. I'm sure it was done because some crazy countries may see that as "OMFG, CHILD ABUSE! TO THE COURT, COMRADES!", that's why it was changed.  Ugh, if you want to talk about the story, you need to write a book, not a 5000-letter-limit Steam review. Broadly speaking, the game is heavily story driven experience. A girl named Kuon finds you in a forest, while (you) completely blanked out and without any memories to boot. Strangely, you are speaking (and thinking) like a normal modern 20century human, so there's that.Sadly, she doesn't know who you are and where you are from. Thus starts the beginning of your adventures to obtain more information about the unknown fantasy world and yourself.  I must say the story and the characters are especially well written. Some people may be biased towards JP games due to a lot of cringe/facepalm moments, however, Utawarerumono doesn't have those. Of course, there's some traditional JP fanservice scenes, but they are hella fun & hilarious. Main character Haku is especially well done, everything he says or do follow common sense or situation he's in right now. I can't praise MC Voice actor enough for an amazing job he did, making it x10 more hilarious due to his great VA skills.  - , with gorgeous character art, backgrounds and FULL VOICEOVER. (with pretty famous VA's to boot)- During visual novel stuff you can just enjoy the story and character interactions, however, sometimes the game will ask you where you want to go and will offer some prompts.The story is quite rich and some scenes may take awhile, so you can grab a cup of tea.As for battle gameplay, in the beginning the game will ask you either about Normal or Hard difficulty, feel free to take up the Hard difficulty if you want a bit more challenge.Unlike other games, Hard difficulty will offer more enemies on each stage, thus increased your EXP and such. Leveling here is done in two ways:- When your unit attack, you will receive an EXP after attacking. This is similar to old Front Mission and Vanguard Bandits games.- When you finish a new stage, you will receive A HUGE LOAD of EXP for first time clear, up to a few levels if you don't grind.Grinding stages has it benefits, since you can acquire extra DP and use them to increase the stats of your choice. is not really complex here, with HP/ATK/DEF/SPD. There's elements in the game too, you can check menu to confirm strong/weak elements anytime in the battle, so don't fret too much, you don't need to remember it.  In order to keep the player busy and not sleeping during battle parts, the game follow the tradition of the first game from 2002. During your attack, there's an event where you need to press your action button in synch to deliver a 100% critical hit. For example, a combo attack consisting of 3 hits will do a 100% critical hit with each strike if you press the button with correct timing. Critical hits do more damage, especially true for casters.There's two types of event like that, in one you need to press button and in another you need to hold it and release at the right moment. That one with the "hold" is related to spellcaster characters mostly. would be "Rewind" which allows you to "go back in time" up to 50 last turns during your battles. Didn't get that juicy Crit? Rewind and try again.Honestly, i think 50 is way too much xD Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception is a briliant strategy JRPG with well written story, unique characters and fair battle system. Good job on PC port, featuring support for Windows 7 (even if not mentioned) and adapted controls for KB+M. - This review was presented to you by "Casual Game Reviews" Steam Curator.

Hard is easy, redo function makes it childs-play. Thus, having it be easy to breeze through allows it to be engaging enough to engross you in a battle, yet doesn't require you to engage your brain and you can watch the "scene" unfold like a movie. 4/10 SRPG, but 8/10 for overall concept of it.Drawn CGs are great, 3D graphics are from the PS3 era, with weird animations and slightly-deformed models. 9/10 CGs, 5/10 3D. 8/10 overall. (math don't work like that, I know)Music 10/10 The soundtrack excites you in battle, makes whacky scenes adorable, sends dread in tense situations, but most of all: Hits. Right. In. The. Feels.Music is extremely well done, and really sets this aside from other visual novels.Mask of Deception sacrifices itself for an 10/10 sequel.  9/10 for character and world building though. 7/10 overall for this game's plot.10/10Would be a 8/10 if they had to squeeze character introductions and world building into the playtime of Mask of Truth. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR:  Play this game ONLY if you are going to play the entire trilogy, because its basically a very long prologue to the third and final game. You can play the third game without it, but you will get more out of the experience if you play this one first, and you will get more out of this game if you've played the first one. Also, final important note, the Protagonist DOES get BETTER. It might seem unbelievable while playing, but it's true.Long Version: Ok, so if you've played the first game, Prelude to the Fallen, this game is going to feel familiar, but comparatively light. The game is essentially a visual novel with occasional tactical combat elements. Whereas games 1 and 3 feel nearly half and half visual novel and tactical game. This one is more like 2/3 or 3/4 visual novel with very, very little combat by comparison. The combat itself is also significantly less deep and fleshed out then it is in either the first or third games.At first this game has seemingly little connection to the first game, despite being a sequel, it clearly takes place in the same world, but in a different country across the sea from where the first game takes place. You play Haku, a man who awakens with amnesia and slowly rediscovers his past along the way, allowing him to ask the same kinds of questions we the player would ask if unfamiliar to the world. (My understanding is that this game was made with the assumption that most players wouldn't have played the first game since they were released rather far apart. [upwards of 10 years]) A small spoiler that I believe makes the game more enjoyable is this: (Skip the line below if you don't want it.)Kuon, the secondary protagonist and character who finds Haku at the beginning of the game, is the daughter of your character from the first game.Knowing this brings a lot of player to game connection improving context to the dialogue and character interactions as the game progresses. (At least in my opinion). The story follows Haku as you make friends and come under the employ of a high ranking government official who is exactly as wonderful a person as he seems. Over time the group becomes one of your employer's greatest shadow assets, and helps shape the fate of the kingdom, mostly for the better. Along the way Haku slowly regains his memories, which he learns make him a person of particular importance to this specific land and ultimately the group gets caught up in events that will change the kingdom forever, at great emotional cost to Haku and those close to him. The story ends on a bit of a cliffhanger because, as mentioned in the TLDR, it really is a giant setup for the following game.Most of the game chronicles the day to day lives of the primary cast, clearly covering the course of several months (possibly a year or more?). The group grows closer, bonds are forged, and shenanigans ensue. In terms of flavor, those familiar with anime will recognize all the the tropes they're familiar with here, for better or for worse. The game is unnecessarily cheesecakey, but for the most part they are comparatively classy about it, there's just a lot of fan service that is clearly there for that reason alone. Despite this, character interactions feel genuine, the occasional gems found in reference to the first game are almost all good, most of the primary cast is likeable. Personally I can tell there's a culture clash, because certain repeated interactions clearly considered "normal" in-universe try my patience, but overall its enjoyable. My primary problems with the game are that the combat is less complex and enjoyable than in either of the other two games, and that for the majority of the game I find Haku unlikeable, especially in comparison to your character from the first game. Who is great almost from the get go. Haku is possessed of qualities that aren't uncommon in protagonist characters both negative and positive, in fact he possesses several of the same traits as the primary character from the first game; but they are largely portrayed in a less than flattering way. For example he proudly proclaims that he is a layabout who tries to avoid work and would gladly spend his time drinking rather than being of use to society. But one of his most useful traits is his genuine cunning and in a classic "give the hard job to a lazy person" way, he often comes up with brilliant plans and solutions for the groups problems. But most of the time this is not done in a way that makes us as players look at the protagonist in a good light and even when it IS framed positively for us, he gets no credit from the rest of the cast for it. This character framing is clearly intentional, especially with hindsight from playing the third game. But having to play an unlikeable character through what felt like a very long story, was draining and dull enough that were it not for the very intense and fantastic final few chapters of the game, I might have been uninterested in picking up the third one.That being said, the trilogy as a whole is pretty fun, and the stuff you'll get because of playing this game made putting up with it worth it as the final game played on.
