_childDocuments_.review: Don't be alarmed by the playtime, I've finished both games on the PS Vita and bought them on PC because I just love the series so much.I found out about Utawarerumono by complete accident through a random pic of Kuon on Telegram, the name sounded somehow... familiar, so I looked into it and found the games, started playing the first one on PC and it was love at first sight, it is now my absolute favorite game series of all time.I'll make a proper review of the first game once the remake comes out on Steam, but I'll say it's absolutely necessary to play it first in order to enjoy Mask of Deception to its fullest, so either play the original 2000 game, or wait for the remake.It's a VN game with some tactical battles, the gameplay has some neat mechanics and I enjoy it quite a bit, but it's absolutely not the core here, don't come in expecting a fully-fledged strategy RPG, the focus here is on the story, and some stretches can go for dozens of hours of reading with no combat happening for a good while, so know what you're getting into beforehand. However, I was never really a big VN kind of guy, and Utawarerumono completely changed my mind, so if you don't usually play VNs, still try getting into it with an open mind, and you might be pleasantly surprised.Mask of Deception hooked me as much as the original did, the characters are instantly likeable and the world-building is top-notch. Haku is a very lovable idiot and Kuon feels like a mom.It's a slow-paced game, but in a very good way, you'll come to appreciate the "slice-of-life" like moments much more when things really start kicking into gear, the character development and interactions are just amazing.The ending to this game is one of my absolute favorite endings out of any media ever, and is one of the most brilliant sequel hooks I've ever seen. Mask of Deception, in the end, sort of feels like a MASSIVE PROLOGUE to Mask of Truth, and I admit I was slightly disappointed by the fact it has fewer battles than the original, but don't let that fool you into thinking it's not a worthwhile experience. It's still an absolutely amazing game with memorable moments on its own right, and the fact that it takes so much time to develop the world and the characters, is what makes Mask of Truth such a delightful experience. Mask of Truth wouldn't be nearly as good as it is, without Mask of Deception preparing the ground for it first.The two games should be taken in as a whole, Mask of Deception being the AMAZINGLY GOOD prologue that is only made even better by how absolutely brilliant Mask of Truth is.This is more like a 2-parter, and I'll talk more about the games in my Mask of Truth review.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is resolution locked to 720p. If you have the computer specs to run an upscaler I'd recommend it. Magpie -  - 2d art comparison - 3d battle comparisonScreen shots don't do it justice. The image is very blurry without it but looks great with it imo. In game 4k vs Anime4k 3x.Took me 28.5 hours to read this at a quick pace on hard mode according to my save. Post game battles were not done.This is a sequel to Prelude of the Fallen and anyone telling you not to play it is leading you wrong. It isn't just reoccurring characters in a wink wink sort of way. Story bits aren't explained since you already know them from the first game.The story starts off pretty slow with not much going on. Mostly slice of life antics for the first 15 hours. Then it starts getting interesting and stays that way up until the end. The ending sets up the next game in a great way and makes you want to start it right away. Some don't seem to like the main character. I thought it was refreshing to see a normal person instead of a perfect JRPG hero out to save the world. He's lazy and probably has a drinking problem. But when push comes to shove he finds a way to make it work. Grows quite a bit over the game.The battle system is massively improved over the first game. The problem is there isn't a whole lot of it this time. Only 17 stages (although a few have two in one) compared to the 36 in the first. The game is much more balanced so you aren't a walking dead machine this time. BP cost scales with each use so putting all into attack is possible but it adds up. BP is also not given out as much compared to the first. Your units are still pretty powerful but the enemies this time are as well. On hard they can easily kill your units in 1-2 attacks. There are a lot more skills and customization of items. Zeal gains and uses have been tweaked for a much more fun system. I find the final battle poorly balanced around hard since without grinding you are 10-14 levels below it and it'll AOE 1-shot your units. Lowered to normal to just quickly beat the game.Overall great game. Really enjoyed the characters and their interactions. Can't wait to read the finale.For being an all ages game this is a lot more risqué than the prequel in CGs and text.

_childDocuments_.review: Personal impression about the visual novel perspective:This is my second playthrough, I played it first on the PS Vita, and decided to get it too on Steam. Don't expect much from Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception, from most of its plot you'll have a tranquil, relatively shallow story with not so many successive battles, you might even spend hours with just listening to the character's interactions without a single battle, from time to time you might feel like doing some "Free Battles" just so you can get something interesting to do; in itself the game is quite slow and it can get boring at times, if you lie in bed while playing you might have the risk of falling asleep (happened to me a couple of times). The game starts to get good on the 2nd half and in overdrive at the end.Why do I recommend it after talking so bad about it, you may ask? Because the sequel is worth playing this game, enduring its slowness and from time to time boring exchanges is worth it, its the very detailed and extremely important buildup to what happens in Mask of Truth. Endure the game, try to enjoy it, try not to miss a thing since some developments in Mask of Truth are related to what happens here (same with Prelude to the Fallen, although I played the original translated by a fan a long time ago when Steam wasn't as famous as it is now and with ALL the content ;)), I might play it too too see how they changed it in the remake.On another note, if you are playing it because of the anime, then you'll definitely feel like the anime left too many important things out. Yes, this game is better than the anime of course.Personal impression about the strategy perspective:This is a very simple tactical game, this is no Fire Emblem, but it is still quite interesting to keep you enjoying the battles and immersed in the story, as sporadic as these battles might be. All battles are fun and can be hard at times (mostly because of a flaw), of course, you can power level out of those battles since you have access to the Free Battle system, that allows you to repeat previously done battles to gain BP (Bonus Points) that lets you use these points to improve the character's stats at a cost. If you are having issues with a battle, doing a couple of free battles might help you on your way out.Pros:- Lengthy story with lots of details and character development.- Fun and simple battle system.- Lovable characters from start to finish (<3 Kuon).- Plays with your nostalgia quite a bit, making it enjoyable.Cons:- Too much character development makes it feel repetitive at times.- Battle system has a flaw (won't spoil what it is; and was fixed in Mask of Truth).- It feels like the game takes too much time getting serious, and when it does... THE END.Persevere through this game and you'll be rewarded in full with Mask of Truth.

_childDocuments_.review: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception is the longest visual novel i have played yet. It is a bit shorter than it's sequel, Mask of Truth. I have finished it in 37 hours and i am glad a sequel is available, as i am writing this review i can't wait to read what is next. My first thoughts was that the game looks pretty good and that it can't be bad if the developers bothered to remaster a series that started in 2002. I can feel it being old enough since it acts differently than modern anime, its old in the good way. It is some kind of Isekai, the main character (supposedly you) loses his memories and wakes up almost naked in the cold of the snow. He would've died 3 times if it was possible if it wasn't for his luck of being saved by Kuon, the girl that gives him the name of Haku. This is where their adventure begins, adding more people to their party, making things right and protecting the ones who are dear to them. It looked boring at first, but this is how many good shows begin. At the start it gives you a feeling of disgust, then you wonder why you like it as the story gets better, and at the end you absolutely love it. The graphics are good for everything except battle maps, but they didn't decrease the quality of my experience whatsoever. The soundtrack is also very good, would be a waste if you muted it to play whatever you are listening to daily. The characters are not animated, a bit of a shame. The size is not huge compared to some other VN ports i know, good for people with not so much space like me. 9.5/10 - A great story, would watch the anime even if the same things happen in it. Very sentimental, exactly what i am aiming for in games and anime. My favorite visual novel series for now.If you want more detailed reviews on awesome games consider following , our curator page.

_childDocuments_.review: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception is the second game in the Utawarerumono Series. It is a visual novel 80% of the time and the rest are turn based RPG with tactical combat.MoD start with a young man suffering amnesia lost in a mountain and trough a series of events he came to the capital city of the country Yamato doing odd jobs as "fixer" while eventually stumbling into a political schemes and became deeply involved. it is a slow game, its purpose are to introduce players to its world and characters trough the MC's point of view. depend of your point of view, this slow, deliberate worldbuilding might feel like a slow crawl, but for me it works as a great introduction to the world. their major political powers, major figures, also your friends and the protagonist. as Phase 1 of the Mask series, Mask of Deception works very well. you will learn to love the characters, the world and become fully immersed. MoD ends with one of the best sequel hook ever created that will kick the story into high gear and a very satisfying emotional climax. the first 80% of the game are relaxed, almost slice of life-y and the end are like an accelerating rocket pushing to escape orbit.the combat itself is simple, easy and mostly non intrusive. you have a grid of squares, each unit have their own move and attack range. the attack are separated with different skills, in with each skills have a QTE input that determine your critical hit like Paper Mario / Super mario RPG. music is great, there is no english dub but the japanese voice acting is great.if you like game with detailed worldbuilding, lovable and various cast of characters but interesting underlying mystery check out the game

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, but with a few flawsFirst off, the gameplay is a lot better. Improved combat systems, better character progression, better maps and, more importantly, better difficulty options. Normal is about equal to Prelude hard mode, and hard mode is actually a decent challenge in this which was nice. Aside from the final boss (which was annoying and overtuned on Hard), the game is very well balanced and fun. No more stacking attack with bonus points (which work differently) and just one shotting everythingThe problem? There isn't enough gameplay.The game has WAY TOO MUCH FILLER. The filler is much better than it was in Prelude and the writing quality is better overall (there were a bunch of scenes that got a genuine laugh out of me VS Prelude where I felt uncomfortable half the time), but it's spaced out so poorly. For most of the game you can easily go up to 5 hours without a single combat section. I like filler but I don't like it when it delays the gameplay so much. Prelude to the Fallen felt like a standard SRPG but this just felt like a raw VN. There were so few gameplay segments that by the time I unlocked my characters final strikes, I was already on the final boss so it didn't even matter.Also, the overall story is worse than Preludes. Mask of Deception basically serves as an entire games worth of worldbuilding and character development for it's sequel, and because of that nothing really happens until the very end of the game. If Prelude to the Fallen was a 9/10, this was a 7/10. Get it on sale because you need to play it before you can play Mask of Truth. Either that or watch the anime. The game is 90% VN, 10% tactics game so you'd probably get a better experience with the anime if you don't like filler or VN storytelling

_childDocuments_.review: I remember reading Utwarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen & giving it a rather mixed review, citing average gameplay & rushed, disjointed storytelling as being the biggest negatives of an otherwise enjoyable experience. My willingness to recommend that game was contingent on how much I might enjoy the sequels & whether or not I found the payoff to be worthwhile - Sadly, two thirds of the way in, I'm still waiting to make up my mind.To start with a positive, the game is absolutely stunning, to the point where I'd call it one of the best looking releases I've seen so far... In the VN portions of the title, that is. The SRPG sections are still stuck looking like early PS2 games up-ressed a bit, but that doesn't detract from the experience in any meaningful way besides being a bit jarring the first time or two. Some of the character art is a little weaker than others, but overall, the game looks spectacular & the variety in sprites really helps sell the current emotions of each individual. The OST is a small step up from the original title, with a few new tracks complimenting a strong selection of returning pieces from the original, although I didn't find it to be spectacular overall.The new cast is arguably a bit stronger overall than the original, though there's enough familiarity there for it to be a comfortable experience coming from Prelude. You could also jump straight in to Mask of Deception & not miss out on any major story points, but I'd recommend not doing that, as the commonality between setting & overall theme makes the whole experience stronger when enjoyed as a package. The world building remains excellent, even if some of my concerns from the first title continue to be an issue in this one.My biggest gripe is a carryover from the first game that I struggled to put into words until I actually sat down & thought about what it was that was annoying me so much. During the slice of life periods of the game, you're given a list of mini-stories that you need to complete before the main story itself continues, but this selection process comes in place of a naturally flowing story. You're not really choosing between which little side adventures you want to go on because you have to do them all anyway, so what you're really doing is excusing the developer for being either unable or unwilling to write one long, cohesive slice of life section, instead providing individual story chunks that can sometimes feel jarring when read in a particular order. I'm a big fan of slice of life in general, but I found that these little "choice" sections took me out of the experience on more than one occasion, which is a shame since the characters & the world itself are very impressive.As for the combat, my overwhelming feeling towards it is one of apathy. It's fine, & if you decide to go into the options menu & speed it up, it's almost completely ignorable. Playing on Normal, I didn't bother looking at any spells or even equipping any items until the last encounter of the game, partly because encounters were just mind-numbingly easy & tedious, & partly because a good 80% of the encounters you come across are just busywork with little to no meaning in the overall plot of the story.All that said, I'd still say Mask of Deception has the better story & pacing overall compared to its predecessor, so if you enjoyed that, then you're very likely to enjoy the sequel as well. None of the things I personally take issue with are new, either - If you didn't mind them in the first title, you won't mind them here either.In conclusion, as much as I enjoy the world & the characters (both of which are fantastic), there's just been too many minor issues up until this point that have culminated in an overall feeling of annoyance towards the game itself - Mostly because it feels like it's so very nearly excellent, & that's what hurts the most. If not for those immersion breaking interludes I'm sure the tone of my review would be almost fanatical in its positivity, but this sort of choice system has put me off other titles in the past, & will surely put me off titles in the years to come. There's a lot to love about Utwarerumono, & hopefully you can play it without being affected by certain elements as much as I have, but me personally? I'll be heading into the final chapter of the trilogy hoping for something to make all of it seem worthwhile in the end, despite loving so much about the core of the story & its characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: The sequel to Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen does everything its predecessor did just as well. Expanding this large world to an even bigger scale, where all characters fit perfectly. Bonds strengthened over time, memories of trifling everyday matters and good times - this is all the characters hoped for, so how dare anyone take that from them? They will not falter to this so-called fate.These fifty hours of meeting new people, being greeted by familiar faces, caring for one another, almost felt too short. Perhaps it's just me, but I wanted even more from this story. Acting as a stepping stool for the last title of the series, it set an amazing narrative to be continued.I can't praise this one enough, but the only thing I will not forget myself for not mentioning is the voice acting, especially Haku's. I have never in my life heard such great voice acting, and all that is Fujiwara Keiji's work, who unfortunately passed away last year, may he rest easy. His work will live on forever.So, just experience the unique work Utawarerumono is. Every second of it is worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great visual novel that truly is a slow-burner. I fell asleep like twice during the game because the OST was just too peaceful, and there was nothing dramatic going on during the first 20-25 hours of the game.  If you're here for combat, though, the battles and gameplay sorely lacks during the story.  After you beat the main game, it unlocks additional battles, which are pretty brutal compared to the battles during the game.  You'll have a chance to use more of your fun abilities and final strikes too.  I enjoy the combat a lot since it reminds me of Stella's Glow/Final Fantasy Tactics-lite.

_childDocuments_.review: It’s primarily the tale of Haku, the aforementioned amnesiac, who awakes in an unfamiliar tent under the stewardship of Kuon. Feeling some kind of responsibility towards her new ward, she sets out to ensure he’s able to make a life for himself without her, despite having an absolute blank slate for a past. Except, it’s never really that easy; Haku’s not especially interested in finding a job and doesn’t grab on to any of the threads of purpose that Kuon often tries to provide him. He has no established trade; that vanished along with the rest of his memories, and he isn’t especially skilled in anything obvious. Then giant bugs attack. Then the pair fall in with a group of travelling guardsmen to repel them and befriend a travelling princess riding an adorable oversized bird. Subterranean slime monsters become a thing, bandits need saving from banditier bandits and there’s a near obligatory miscommunication involving public baths. Eventually, the group arrives at the massive capital of Yamato. It’s here all the heavy drinking starts.The plot proper certainly starts to slow down once the group hits the capital. Battles become a lot less frequent and big stand-alone events become less common. Instead, Mask of Deception, very gently, starts making your care about its cast of seemingly random miscreants. It does so by making you a creepy voyeur while they simply get on with the mundane activities of their lives. Haku, it turns out, will never be content with being the typical amnesia-suffering protagonist, supplied as an undisguised self-insert for the player. That kind of nonsense takes far too much effort. Instead, he’s content to coast as much as he can, easily manipulated with promises of free booze and days off.Working within the roving guards inside the capitol, he’s given a base of operations and a slowly growing collection of people to work with. Kuon, for her part, tags along under the guise of a motherly caretaker, hoarding all Haku’s earnings and proving a small allowance so he doesn’t blow it all on a grand night out. But she makes choices that belie that role, constantly accomplishing her requirements for sticking around, but then reinventing them so she doesn’t have to leave the group.It’s little personal evolutions like that which make Utawarerumono’s hard focus on character building so engaging. It’s rarely ham-fisted, always dropping little titbits of information you might initially decipher as completely throw away, only to present themselves in deeper shades of relevance later. It hides things in plain sight, rewarding the reader by letting them work things out for themselves. For example, the game never once tells you how Kuon and Haku met; he just woke up in her tent one day and that was that. But I know. And I know simply because of a series of heavy silences or guilty glances or loaded one-word replies through several tense situations. It’s brilliant writing that’s confident in both its own execution and the reader’s intelligence to put everything together without it being presented in crayon. It painstakingly builds everyone this idyllic little existence they carve for themselves, shows how they each grow within each other’s company, within responsibilities both earned and restricted. But it’s never destined to last forever. You know that. Perhaps more importantly, they know that, too.

_childDocuments_.review: I had postponed this review till the time I could complete Mask of Truth and now that I have, I can confidently say that I enjoyed Mask of Deception as much as I enjoyed Mask of Truth. Both of them together complement each other very well and just elevate the entire experience. Where before I never cared much for SoL in visual novels, Mask of Deception destroyed that notion. I have never once been made to look forward to going home from work to boot up a game like this one for some good old, laid back fun SoL. The humour just struck a chord with me so fast that I was dreading the time when this game would stop being laid back and become serious eventually. I loved the lively setting,  the characters that I deeply care for, the drip fed lore, the awe at seeing the Eight pillars for the very first time and every thing else Mask of Deception has to offer. _childDocuments_.review: This is a great visual novel with a surprisingly deep tactical combat system.  If you're interested in a fantasy story with adult characters, great writing, beautiful art & music, and crazy plot twists, you should play this game -- especially because it's necessary to play it before the sequel, Mask of Truth, which is easily one of the most amazing stories I've ever experienced.To break it down a little further, this game is about 80% visual novel to 20% SRPG.  There's usually an hour or two of reading that is then followed up by a battle in which you control several characters on a grid-based map.  The story is a little slow-paced at first; this game is very heavy on worldbuilding and has a ton of details about its culture, food, and history.  If you enjoy digging into a complex setting, there's a lot to enjoy here.  The character development is also very nuanced and deliberate; perhaps the worst thing about it is that it's not obvious just how well everything is done until you replay this game again after finishing Mask of Truth so that you can see exactly how all of the character arcs are set up.  The first few arcs in the game move slowly and spend a lot of time introducing you to characters and their casual lives, but after the plot really gets moving, it's a rollercoaster to the end that finishes with a series of amazing plot twists.  Do keep in mind that this is not a standalone game by any means; everything here is a prologue that leads into the events of Mask of Truth.  On top of that, this is technically the second game in the series; it's designed so that newcomers can play it without being familiar with the original, but you'll miss some cameos and references, and knowledge of the original is really necessary to enjoy the final game.As far as gameplay goes, every character is unique; there are no classes or generic units, and every character has a unique set of abilities.  The stages in the story are fairly easy; there is a Hard difficulty mode, but SRPG veterans will still find that to be on the easy side.  The game does, however, have several post-game maps that ramp up the difficulty and really show off the complexity of the battle system, and I highly recommend playing the post-game if you like the gameplay at all.I would be remiss if I didn't note that there are some technical issues.  This is a port of a PS4 game, and the port does a lot of things right; it's stable, keyboard inputs are fully remappable, and it has several different joystick button and key icon sets to choose from.  It does have one big problem, which is that the internal rendering is locked at 720.  If you're playing on a higher-resolution monitor, there are noticeable jagged edges on the font and on the 3D models in combat.  It's not game-breaking, and you can make it look better by using ReShade to tweak anti-aliasing and scaling options, but it's still annoying; hopefully the developer will address it.

_childDocuments_.review: Mask of Deception is the start to one of my favorite stories of all time.  The journey of the lazy schemer and reluctant hero Haku, his self-proclaimed guardian Kuon, and all the other colorful characters is unforgettable.  If you're hankering for a world you can just lose yourself in for 60+ hours, you can't go wrong with this game and its sequel.  It deftly mixes comedy and drama, action and romance, slice of life hijinks and political intrigue in a way few others have managed.  Fair warning: these games are visual novels first, strategy second.  Deception only has a few battle maps, actually, so don't go into this expecting Fire Emblem with cat girls. It's more like a grand fantasy novel, where you can participate in the battles.  The pacing reminds me quite a bit of Trails in the Sky, and if you liked the first and second chapters of those games, you can expect a pretty similar pace to those two games here in Deception and its sequel Truth, with Deception taking its sweet time building up the world and its cast, and Truth really hammering out the big climactic moments.I discovered these games originally on PS4 and didn't expect much--figured it was just going to be a bargain bin anime game, but it's way more than that.  Please give these games a chance--they might surprise you like they did me.

_childDocuments_.review: While you can start with this game, you definitely should play  first. While being its own story, the game rewards players of the first game with callbacks and characters that make the experience 10x sweeter.From a technical aspect, the game is a massive step-up from the previous game, which isn’t surprising as Prelude came out 13 years before. The gameplay is more complex, making it much more enjoyable than the straightforward approach of the previous entry.The story is slow at first, choosing to develop its cast first and familiarize the player in this new area of the world. The Slice of Life sections are a treat and the stellar voice acting & OST will have you immersed. Once all the pieces are in play, the game shows you what it’s been building towards. it's not as emotional as the first game, but it perfectly sets up the stakes for the final game. The ending was once of the best cliffhangers I’ve experienced in media and had me staring at my ceiling throughout the entire credits.

If you're here searching for a decent story, I think you should play this game. Be open-minded for the first half, and just enjoy the slice-of-life ride. It's an investment for the nuances for the second half, The story just keeps getting better and better as it progresses (and you need to continue to the next game. LOL)The Tactical J-RPG part of this game is meh. It's actually quite forgiving for people who dont like this kind of mechanics (you can redo moves/actions freely). You can treat the first game (Prelude to the Fallen) as a prologue instead. If you notice my bias, this is because I enjoyed the game so much. _childDocuments_.review: So Utawarerumono, if you think this review is unbiased go somwehere else. In this review im going to talk not only about mask of deception but also mask of truth and prelude to the fallen, why you may ask? If you start with mask of deception you most likely don't know wbout utawarerumono or it's modern name prelude to the fallen, but there is no need to write review for mask of truth because entire existance of mask of truth is very big spoiler, dont look at steam page dont google anything because it's based out of quite big spoiler from mask of deception.Before I end this lengthy introduction it is time to say something quite important. You can start with mask of deception, not reccomended but works, you wont know refferences and you are going to get some spoilers about it but it's good enough, but for any reason dont go with mask of truth if you dont know 2 previous titles, even anime from 1st game will be good enough because 1 and 2 are prelude, foundation for 3rd which connects old with new, 2002 and 2014 sequel which culminated in 2016.Why utawarerumono? There are few factors which im going to write about in this review 1story2characters3musicPart 1:I'm going to talk here about 1 and 2(im going to reffer to games by numbers since its going to be lengthy anyway)So let's start with 1 it starts with your good old(well 2002 but it was old back then) amnesia start, what I love about the story is that you dont get final goal, all you have is some things happen and you end up running a nation and then what? care about it and that's all, story escalates things about his past surface and story gets quite interesting from that point.2 Here things get quite original, in this story you are not hero saving the kingdom, you are his little helper, this game is slower than 1 since you can treat it like just half of a game, just like Suga(writer of the story) made a game and higher ups told him that is two game material and they released it so(not blaming them, this game is reaaaaaaally long), this part is more about building the world, and introducing new region to the story, and laying ground for events from final part of the trilogy, it takes it's time but it's not empty, story happens it's just..well first half of the game, all spicy parts are always for 2nd half which is separate game even longer than this game(60-70 hours compared to over 80)Story is lead through two phases, first you have your good old slice of life till things start to happen and you embark on adventure or do some task important for the story, and once it's complete hero comes home and lives his daily life while you get to know more of the characters he accompanies which leads us to:part 2 charactersThis is where strength of utawarerumono comes from, imagine spending tens of hours with characters, you know their best and worst, and they are written very well. You really get to like this bunch of characters, main or companions or just episodic characters.Hakuoro, main character of 1st, it is your responsible likeble leader, nothing exceptional which doesn't mean that it's not a great character, his supporting cast is absolutely top notch you really feel life in them, even opposition is more like someone being unlucky to be on wrong side of a spear rather than villain doing evil for sake of it.Haku, which is main character of 2, here is what i absolutely praise and love. Imagine slacker always looking for chance to talk his way out of thw work and go drinking with bros, but when situation is dire he can think really quick. The point with this character is to see how he changes in span of two games, the point where he starts and where he ends. It is absolutely most heroic character i ever seen, after what happened in the story you really give him respect for his acts, he may not have power level over 9 thousand but compared to who he is, and how much he can it's quite high ratioAs for supporting cast, since this game is more about worldbuilding and character development, and Suga had 12 years to become better at writing and you have 60-70 hours game instead of 40-ish length of previous game you really get to know there characters from all of the angles and really care what happens with them, if they may be in danger you care more than "oh i like this npc, oh something happened to them, oh whatever" of quite lots of storiesPart 3 music1st and 2nd game have diffrent composers, 2 gets few of tracks adapted for new but it's 3rd game which combines both as it combines two regions and stories into grand finale.When 1st game doesn't have really great soundtrack(in 2002 it didn't even have voice acting) it catches up with songs sung during the gameSimiliar situation happens with 2nd and 3rd, while those have new composer and singer, soundtrack on itself is way more solid and songs are kept in same really high quality state.So final part without number but word:epilogueIf you are here, wow that's quite long review here and you are at this point. So bit of my personal experience with the game, part where it's about me and the game not game itself. It started quite standard, i watched anime, it was absolutely top tier, really high up my list. Year later i decided to give a try to it's source material, at first it was quite pleasant experience but soon i was completely in. Anime suddenly from 10(given quite rare from me) went to medicore and i realized how much utawareumono lost due to shortening the slice of life parts, despite knowing how it ends i went through it with pure passion about it, then it ended, instantly went for sequels. 2nd was worst out of trilogy(dont get me wrong, 1st is full story 2nd is first half 3rd is 2nd half) but i had quite a lot of fun with it, then 3rd and then it was over. This game doesn't hold back on punches to the feels, when it wants you to laugh you laugh at the top of your lungs, when it wants to be serious or sad, it conveys it really hard.  Is it worth it? Absolutely, best story i found to this day, and i'm looking for over 3 years for something that might topple it from the top.As my final words of this review my highest praise reserved only to "that one and only" story:I hope I can live long enough to find something better.

_childDocuments_.review: Starts out as an average slice of life story in an average fantasy world with demi-humans, but is actually a . The start and middle of the game have a lighthearted tone and nothing really amazing happens. The plot starts to develop after that though. While i have not played it at the time of this review, apparently Mask of Deception is a set up for its sequel: Mask of Truth. _childDocuments_.review: Now that was what called a speechless ending, Mask of Deception truly was a spectacular sequel of the original Utawarerumono (2002), it expanded the world of Utwarerumono perfectly by extremely detailed world-building, solved unanswered questions of its prequel and continued the intriguing lore of Utawarerumono universe. _childDocuments_.review: Pros-Art is bright and adorable.-Characters are cute and interesting initially.-Premise of the story is intriguing initially.-Combat is simple but fun.Cons-Your main character is a designated monkey, the butt of every joke which is the source of 75% of the humor.-The writing gets idiotically stupid to the point of offensive.-Characters quirks become tiresome and grating.-Pacing between story and combat is terrible, you'll forget there's combat after 2-3 hour blocks of story only for the combat to last 5 minutes.While I initially enjoyed this game what is essentially a visual novel must be judged on its story and the story that started fun and intriguing quickly grew grating by the 12 hour mark.To eleborate on your main character being a buttmonkey and why this gets very annoying. Every joke is at his expense. Every misunderstanding will be his fault regardless if it is or not. He rarely deserves the abuse gleefully hurled in his direction but that's whats supposed to make it funny I take it. It was funny... at first. Now its predictable and exhausting.The writing also loses several dozen IQ points around the 10 hour mark when *MILD SPOILERS* your main character who is an amnesiac illiterate whose dangerously weak compared to the fantasy world he's in is made the leader of a group of adventurers. Let that sink in. What's worse, the main female protagonist is a worldly, ultra competent, charming, beautiful traveler and apothecary.  Her being the leader should be obvious but she decides for the main character that he should be, then points out later that him not knowing anything about the world he lives in or being able to read is an embarrassment on the rest of them since he's the leader... see, cuz its funny that everything is his fault... get it? The other characters in your party have even less of a reason to be in an adventuring party but I'll stop to avoid further spoilers.In closing, a charming VN with gameplay that QUICKLY grows wearisome the more you play it unless you check in your brain at the door and chose not to think about to hard about whats going on. I couldn't do that so It overstayed its welcome for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Have been waiting for a long time because I'm not a console player. Finally Utawarerumono has come back to its origins on PC, with the two new sequels. Utawarerumono: Itsuwari no Kamen aka Mask of Deception (MoD) in English, is just a game building up the whole new world (in the future) of the 1st game, where there are more and more people with cultural things. Yes, this game is just the opening of Utawarerumono: Futari no Hakuoro aka Mask of Truth (MoT) (but actually the real meaning when we translated the name to English is "The Two White Kings"), it is definitely a significant step momentum to bring up the plot of the final game to the zenith of epic. Let me say this, Aquaplus decided to release MoD 12 years after the 1st game, so that they have to create out a new story, not really and directly related to the prequel but somehow maintain its original. A lot of guys said that MoT was much better that MoD, I also think that's true. But you really can't deny that MoD literally the 1st thing needed to build up the story in MoT, because if you do not play MoD, how can you know about who is Kuon, who really is Oshtor, what is happening now and etc... in MoT? You can even wonder why Karura and Touka appear here although they were existed only in Utawarerumono: Chiriyuku Mono he no Komoriuta (the 1st game, in english is the title 'Prelude to the Fallen')? So yeah, though MoD is not as good as the 1st game or the last game but this game also has A BUNCH OF universe-building and it's absolutely the 1st step you guys have to take and after that you can move to Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth. Thanks for reading guys and hope you buy & enjoy this franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: I waited a long time for the newer port of Prelude to the Fallen to be out before playing this game. Having done so here's my spoiler-free review:- Plot is really slow compared to Prelude to the Fallen. The concern here is not so much "there is less combat" in-between (which there is less), but more so the slice of life content seems to barely advance the plot or the personality of the characters. It is OK, but I feel it was executed better in the prior game. - Side Quests menu are not available here: You learn in the first few minutes of the game you can do "Free Battles" (i.e. revisit the battles to grind). This is OK, but in Prelude, they went the extra mile and added side quests. This added a bit of voiced content with battle, which was a nice touch. Considering the plot, they had room to add this here, but they did not.+/- Combat is similar but different from Prelude. This game does not have combo attacks. However, they gave each character more than one combat chain. + No more "healer only unit". Some characters can heal on top of an attack (In your first battle you learn this). + There is some motivation to re-do some free battles for a bit extra voiced content. I will not mention it further, or this would spoil the fun. - There is some really strong wording on some character's translated voices which I don't think matches properly with the character's personality. + Art seems better than Prelude to the fallen. +/- Item system is more shallow: There is less lore to them. Some weapons could also customize the attack pattern in Prelude. Here, items center more in "support role", which may change combat but not so much its effects. There are no specialized items for characters here.+ New ring patterns make things less dull than "press when the circle hits the dot". + Combat from each character is more unique. I can't say more without spoil, but overall the attacks feel less "DPS/Tank/Ranged" and more specialized classes.- In this game, the way you are facing does not affect damage (you can't even position where the character is facing either). In Prelude, you could. Long story short, I played this game after reading it is "35% action here and 65% action on Mask of the Truth". It is indeed the case. Hence, if you are uncertain if this is worth your time, I'd recommend you try Prelude to the Fallen first, I feel that is the better "rounded package". If you like what you see, then you can try this one hoping Mask of Truth will balance the slow pace of this one later. The plot is satisfying, it is just really slow. This game will make more sense if you play Prelude to the Fallen too, which will alleviate the slow burn.-------------Some suggestion for the devs (if they ever read this):In Prelude to the Fallen, at a few missions, you could control the more "generic unit" in the field. None of that in this game,  however. This is a visual novel first and foremost, so I did not hope for this but, it would be nice in future games if we could be given more control on training said units and/or sending them in battles in a way that may affect the visual novel as optional content (much as Prelude had). Considering the plot theme of the games, there is plenty of room for something like this.

_childDocuments_.review: An overlooked gen Utawarerumono mask of deception is a glorious story that enthralls the player with interesting lore, character, and writing. The gameplay of mask of deception is a refined masterpiece for any tactical rpg fan. Though this game is amazing I can not say it is without flaw, the pacing of the game is flawed with this being a prologue to the sequel mask of truth though, that does not excuse the really poor pacing of story to fight. overall this game is an 8 out of 10 but can easily hit 10 out of 10 depending on the person.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer:Completed on Normal difficulty in just under 45 hours on steam deck. Ran flawlessly.Make sure you play "Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen" BEFORE playing this game.Short Review:This series is a masterpiece unlike anything else I have played. Its truly amazing from start to finish.It has everything: Times of joy and sadness, mysteries and big reveals, it takes itself seriously then its both ridiculous and hilarious. All the characters are well written and the story never gets boring.Personally I played this for 1-2 hours most nights before bed and found it hard to put down.I doubt its the sort of game you want to no life though, think of it more like a TV series and watch an episode at a time. Space it out a bit, its a perfect game to finish the day with.More details, no spoilers:Do not skip the prequel game: "Prelude to the Fallen". I won't say why but just do yourself a big favour and play that game first.I want to talk about how great the story, setting and characters are here but I don't want to spoil anything, just go in blind, if you liked the prequel game then its just as good.I'm gonna say mostly the same as I did with the first game: the presentation is the only thing letting the game down. The drawings are excellent but that's all you get 95% of the time. Its very much a visual novel with some combat. There's nothing wrong with that because the writing carries it but, if it was fully animated it would have elevated the experience significantly.The combat was harder than the first game, I had to turn it down to Normal because on Hard mode the enemies were quickly out levelling me and the only way to beat it would be to grind so it didn't seem worth it.That's it really, I just hope we get a full remake some day. It's too good to remain as a mere visual novel.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: Very difficult to rate this game by itself, since it's really one half of a bigger package together with Mask of Truth   But like with the original Utawarerumono (and its remake Prelude to the Fallen), this is a hybrid visual novel/strategy RPG with a strong focus on story. If you're a gameplay-focused player who just wants to battle, skip these games. The plot and characters of this game are a noticeable step up from the original/Prelude, and often maintains a strong pace throughout (can lead to a night or two of continous sleepless gaming), though there are a few sections where you will find "slice of life" segments back to back which can feel a bit stale, and some of the comedy may fall a bit flat. Once again, a strong cast of characters carries this game, and the main characters are all new to this game, while a few returning faces can be encountered every now and then   The game's plot is incomplete on purpose, and is completed in Mask of Truth. So really, only buy this if you plan to play both eventually. The best way to play is to buy the series bundle and to start with Prelude (but not the "complete" bundle because that includes spoiler DLC)
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: A really nice visual novel, a bit heavier on the story than the gameplay compared to its predecessor.Note that you don't "need" to have played the first game to play Mask of Deception, you'll mostly miss a couple of references but nothing that makes the story impossible to understand.Also, I've got to applaud the translators for this game!

_childDocuments_.review: Mask of Deception is the sequel of the original Utawarerumono from 2002 which has now been remade to Utawarerumono Prelude to the Fallen. Mask of Deception is the first half of the story and Mask of Truth is the second half.I highly recommend this visual novel trilogy it is easily one of the best pieces of fiction i've ever came into. The story, the characters, the music, and especially the character developments are one of the best i have ever seen. it is that good it is Peak Fiction as some may say.Remember the order to play the trilogy:1.Prelude to the fallen2.Mask of Deception3.Mask of Truth

_childDocuments_.review: First off let me preface this for anyone who was wondering, YES this game is a lot better than the first instalment (prelude to the fallen). With that being said I don't think prelude is skippable. I think if you are a fan of mystery/political stories, with a lot of slice of life moments mixed in to develop character relationships and the world, this is the game for you.Similar to the first game it starts off as mostly slice of life, dropping subtle hints at whats to come later on when the story picks up. I'm not gonna beat around the bush, there are A LOT of slice of life moments, which I was fine with because i enjoy that type of thing, but it might not be for everyone. With that being said, the pacing and quality of the slice of life segments in this game are what put it a notch above its predecessor. The combat system is largely the same, and takes up id guesstimate around 30% of the game or so, so nothing new there. Another thing I think puts this game a league above Prelude, is the main character. Haku is just so funny and loveable, and really is a unique main character. Found myself laughing out loud multiple times, and I really felt like I was on the journey with everyone having a good time. The hours of quality slice of life moments help reinforce this feeling of comradery and the game would suffer without them in my opinion.As always the OST and artwork is great so no complaints there. Overall I'd give this game a 9/10, I really couldnt ask for more, and it sets up the sequel perfectly.

_childDocuments_.review: I originally tried this game based off of my love for the 2006 anime adaptation of the original Utawarerumono title. Its world had this mystical, ethereal quality that absolutely absorbed and captivated me. Consider this a joint review of both Mask of Deception and its sequel, Mask of Truth: it is no exaggeration to say that this has easily become my favorite anime-esque story and world of all time.The main (but not only) strength of this franchise is world-building; only a few crafted worlds out there can captivate me in a similar manner. Lord of the Rings, Made in Abyss, Tower of God, Adventure Time and Utawarerumono in my mind are the champs. What they all have in common is that the writer(s)' passion for their work comes through to deliver a vivid, original, creative, and detailed world that is like no other (at least for its time- obviously loads of lesser writers were inspired heavily by Tolkien over the decades). Utwarerumono delivers everything that leaves me entranced and constantly craving to know more. Its world initially appears simple- something of a medieval Japan-inspired world where different regions have different cultures (and animal ears). It has tons of attention to detail about the culture and environment around you as it takes you through its leisurely pace, and as things like regional cuisine, flora/fauna, and traditions are discussed, they become available in the in-game glossary for those wanting to know more. It strikes you as an exciting, colorful world, albeit a fairly normal one for a fantasy story. Yet as the pieces fall into place, and you learn more about yourself as the protagonist, you uncover more truths, and your mind is blown by the nature of this world. It will leave you stunned, and that is all I can say without spoiling. 10/10The next thing to be mentioned is the art and music. They are both gorgeous on the eyes and ears. The music is something truly extraordinary. Suara sings music for the opening and endings (including the anime) and also during certain impactful scenes, and is absolutely breathtaking. Her songs perfectly encapsulate what is so beautiful about this game, and is a perfect accompaniment to every scene in which her voice is present. The normal BGM composed by Aquaplus is also very good and I listen to the entire soundtrack regularly even months after finishing the game. The art also is really pleasing to the eyes- character designs are all A+, and the scenery is also gorgeous. I will say that sometimes, I wish they showed more. A few scenes feel kind of lazily done in that they don't have a sprite for an object/prop being discussed in the story, or will occasionally have certain scenes happen through only dialogue, without showing anything (often for comedic purposes, but I wasn't a fan of that nonetheless). This is fairly uncommon, though, and it kind of makes sense that they wouldn't, say, design an entirely new outfit for a character for a one-off scene, so I can forgive it given how good the rest of it is. 9.5/10Then there's the plot and characters, which I will include in one. This gets a strong 9/10. Sometimes there are minor pacing issues with the story. For example, the beginning of the story has tons of slice-of-life scenes which give way to heavier plot as the story goes on. I don't have a problem with the amount of these scenes, I only wish they would be spread more evenly throughout the story so as to not make it so asymmetrical, since sometimes when the plot got too heavy I wish it would give a little breathing room towards the end, whereas I'd occasionally get a little tired of the lack of progress towards the beginning. However, it works very well overall- the slice of life scenes complement the plot nicely by fleshing out the characters and world little by little, and do an excellent job at making you invested in the characters and the outcome by the time things get serious. Speaking of which, you'll love most if not all of the characters- they each have complexity to their character under the surface as you get to know them, and all have charming and interesting personalities. My only other quibble is that I wish the story had more scenes without Haku present- there are some here and there, but it's occasionally hard to get a full grasp of how certain characters feel and are motivated when they are 90% seen through the lens of the protagonist. I will say that the story truly gets into full swing in Mask of Truth- Mask of Deception is a very good setup for the climax, but still a setup nonetheless.The weakest point of the game has to be, well, the gameplay (a.k.a. combat) ironically enough. But fret not- it's only like 10-15% of the game. If you buy this, treat it as a visual novel with a little bit of mediocre gameplay sprinkled in. Not to say it's bad per se, but the controls are fairly clunky and the camera movement WILL frustrate you. It isn't difficult or time-consuming, but it also isn't a highlight of the experience. It's just turn-based combat on a grid-based battlefield with an elements of mechanical skill in timing crits right. It has a bit of nuance but is really nothing special. 6/10Overall, if you have 90 hours of time to read visual novels, I can't recommend these two enough. It was an incredible experience. Make sure to watch the 2006 anime first (the original game got a remake that is supposedly coming to Steam in the future but for now it's only on Playstation much to my dismay) as these games have some references and callbacks that will make you appreciate having seen the previous story (it's not totally essential, that is just my recommendation for maximum enjoyment). 9.5/10, absolutely read/play this if you're looking for a story to be engrossed in.

_childDocuments_.review: I played Utawarerumono : Mask of Deception and Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth on PS4 first and completed both games and I was amazed by the story. This game is more of a visual novel most of the time so be prepared for that, because before I got to the first bit of game play, 1 hour of reading and listening had already passed. In total it took me about 80 hours to complete both games and even tho I prefer games with a bit more game play, I loved the story and can recommend this game for it.The RPG elements are well done and I loved that getting a critical hit is based on skill with a timed button press, and there are some good fights on hard mode as well. For the rest placement of the characters are important as well and as you unlock more and more characters you can get some cool combo's to do some real damage with multiple characters at once.One thing that amazed me is the good quality in voice acting, sound effects and music and it really helps set the mood and it will make you laugh, and put tears on your eyes.

_childDocuments_.review: It's about on par with what you'd expect if you've played Prelude to the Fallen. However, this one suffers from not being as self-contained as the original. For one thing, there are several character cameos which you can only appreciate if you've played the first. For another, the game ends on something of a cliffhanger. In the words of Michael Corleone: your "true enemy has yet to reveal himself" even once you've finished the game. For this reason, Mask of Deception is one of those cases where it's hard to recommend for a new-timer, but it's a shoe-in for anyone who enjoyed the original. The comedy, the fanservice, the artwork, and the surprisingly interesting setting all make their return, so there's a lot here to enjoy for fans of Prelude to the Fallen.Gameplay-wise, there are fewer battles here compared to in Prelude to the Fallen (only 16 story battles, interspersed throughout ~22 hours of visual novel stuff). On the flip side, enemies are far more menacing now, and some of the post-game battles are actually challenging... although it's challenging in a "why am I losing 2 units before I can do anything" sort of way, rather than a "this is an interesting battle that makes me think" sort of way. Yeah, gameplay really isn't the key selling point of Utawarerumono, but that's okay; as in Prelude to the Fallen, the SRPG bits never hinder the game. At worst, they're just okay.I'd still need to underscore a flaw I've seen with both Mask of Deception and Prelude to the Fallen: character development, or lack thereof. For a visual "novel," both Utawarerumonos I've played don't approximate the caliber of character development and writing I'd expect of typical literature. Characters are certainly likable enough in both games, but virtually every single one begins and ends the story with the exact same personality. Almost every character can be described as a composite of one or two "anime tropes" and thus don't feel like real people. In fairness, I don't get the feeling that the series is ever going for anything more - and I do have to emphasize that characters/situations are indeed likable enough to keep things entertaining - however, this is a flaw worth mentioning in case you're searching for something deeper. As a slice-of-life-anime-turned-into-an-interactive-medium, it does the job it sets out to do.Oh, it's also worth mentioning that there's no way (at least that I can tell) of re-reading previous events of the story. This seems odd and unrealistic for a "novel," so I'm glad that they put that feature into the Steam port of Prelude to the Fallen.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a long time fan of the anime-version of this game and its prequel. Suffice to say I loved that they continued the story and the music overall is just gorgeous. _childDocuments_.review: Hands down, the best character-driven game I have ever played. A must play if you want a fantasy Visualnovel-ish JRPG with fantastic character. Fantastic world building. The story itself is good, but the real purpose is to make their character shine.Every character is lovable and has great chemistry together.The joke also great and incredibly funny, making every session enjoyable, even a 30–60 minute session after work. _childDocuments_.review: I'm currently playing through this game still but so far I have to say it is already one of my favorite VN's out there. Between the beautiful art, great characters, amazing OST (It's a shame that the composer passed away last year), fun if a bit simple combat, amazing voice acting (Rest In Piece Keiji Fujiwara and thank you for your roles as Haku and Nishitani from Yakuza 0) and great world building this series can stand upon itself as one of the best the genre can produce. One thing I can tell you this game has is very good girls. Between Kuon, Rulutieh, Nosuri, Atui, Aruru and Munechika it makes it really hard to pick best girl sometimes. But joking aside this game is rather chill as for much of the story you are learning about this world from the perspective of someone who is foreign to the land, it's people and how their society works. Spread throughout the story are these comedic slice of life segments that are very entertaining. Still though the game gets fairly fan servicey in parts, which is a plus from me, so beware if you are not into that. The combat is of the SRPG genre and it plays very similar to games like Disgaea, Final Fantasy Tactics, SMT Devil Survivor, Agarest War, Tactics Ogre and Xcom. But like I mentioned before the combat is rather simplified compared to other SRPG's.All in all I would say this trilogy is well worth your time and money especially if you're into visual novel's. I would even put it up there with Stein's Gate, VA-11 HALL-A, Ace Attorney and Zero Escape as my favorites in the genre. P.S I still need to play the remake of the original, which I have played with the help of an English fan patch and modding in voice acting from the PS2 port.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: Heavily recommend! One of the best visual novels on the English market, finally ported to PC instead of being a console exclusive. The musical score is phenomenal, the characters are awesome (except for two twins), and the artwork is amazing. The only negatives that I would have is that the game only has a CG and Music Gallery, but no sprites/background viewers. Also, do yourself a favor and put all combat settings to "fastest" and turn on autochain. You really don't need the extra benefits that criticals give you except for the final boss.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: The game inherits the pros and cons of the previous game (Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen), that being a slow pacing, an ok SRPG gameplay, and a satisfying main story but is slightly better in every way. Even though the pace of the game is still slow for the majority of the game, these parts of the game are more enjoyable than the previous game with a nice mix of funny and serious moments to build the many characters that are in this game. The SRPG gameplay is also slightly better (making it slightly better than mediocre) because you can use zeal (the game's equivalent to SP in other games) without needing it to reach its maximum value and more characters have healing skills. The main story of the game. For those that don't want to be spoiled on the main story, all I can say is that it is as good or even better than the main story of the previous game (which is very good).
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic but very slow visual novel with a wonderful cast to take you through it's story. Just like Prelude of the Fallen, the VA work is out of this world top notched, and is accompanied by a just as out of this world soundtrack.However, just as the first half or so of Prelude is very slow, filled with mostly fun, comedic slice of life of moments with plot beats sprinkled throughout, Mask of Deception here is about 80-90% of that. The meat of the potatoes doesn't much show up till' the last 10 or so hours. So if the characters don't really hook onto ya, you'll probably find yourself struggling to get through it real hard.With that said, it ends on a BANG, and does an excellent job of getting those hooks out for you to immediately hop into the next and final entry. Especially with the little post credit scene that plays with the absurdly out of left field beautiful song: Koi Yume -Dream Of Love-. God bless ya Aquaplus, I just can't put this series down!
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: This is the second game of the Utawarerumono trilogy, with both of the Mask games being a sort of closer together sequel duology to the first game. This can be a decent starting point with some particular strengths, as it was written 10 years or so after the first game. Regardless, I would very much recommend playing the first game, Prelude to the Fallen, before starting the third.Primarily, this game is a visual novel with TRPG/SRPG gameplay, with a large focus on text (around 20% gameplay to the amount of story scenes). It's fun to just sit and view the story, but you shouldn't expect too much interactivity in the story scenes. A lot of time in this installment is spent setting up things that shine on a replay and in the sequel, and are full of foreshadowing and setup. There are some annoying tropes used around the start of this game in particular, but the overall plot is very strong, intriguing, and emotional. The soundtrack is amazing, and the voice acting is incredibly good. The gameplay side is pretty fun, albeit not nearly as good or balanced as in Mask of Truth. However, the gameplay is quite good at telling story in particular, so it doesn't drag the game down.The story of the Utawarerumono trilogy is one of my favorites ever, and I very highly recommend it. The worldbuilding in this game is absolutely amazing, and there's even a glossary that fills up with terms as you hear them. It's an amazing, mysterious, and emotional tale that really will stick with players. If you're getting this game, you should really view the entire trilogy for the full impact of the plot.I would like to warn of a few things while recommending this game, though: The PC port is pretty meh. The game is still amazing, but resolution and framerate are both poorly locked on the PC version, which may have some impact. ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Also, if you're curious about the play order deal I mentioned at the top: Playing 2-1-3 order could also be good, and a stranger one some people like is playing the first game up until the start of the final arc or so (a slice of life scene involving a character's doll breaking marks the general point), then playing this game and then finishing the first. This order sort of cliffhangers you, but you could consider it. Just playing in order is perfectly fine and something you can't go wrong with, though.If you have more questions, consider joining the Discord through the subreddit :)

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a fan since the *cough* fan patch of the first game came out, so I'm a tad biased because of the nostalgia to come back to this series finally.While the writing isn't the most perfect compared to other high-tier VNs, the story content itself certainly makes up for the weaker written points. The art style is very very nice too, and refreshing compared to your stereotypical styles! The backgrounds are lovely, fitting perfectly, and the music itself is well orchestrated, not too intrusive to disrupt the flow but definitely noticeable and tends to be thematically appropriate to the scenes.Not sure what else to put, if you enjoy slow-paced feudal-period stories, with a dose of mystery, war, and comedic moments then it's totally for you.One downside I noticed, but I think it stands out mostly in the sequel, is that alcohol is vastly overused (even if it was used copiously in the feudal times?) as a story point.Also, Kuon best girl, I love her interactions with Haku.

It is basically 20 hours of filler after the beginning until the plot starts to pick up, combat is very sparse until this point as far as I recall.If you can trudge past the first half of this game (the pain varies from how much you like/dislike the slice of life and comedy filler, either way there is SO much of it) then congratulations, you're set to stick with this series for the rest of the journey. _childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: I would absolutely recommend this game. If you ever played the original Utawarerumono, then you can't miss how the story continues. If you haven't, it's 100% worth it to play that game and then continue with the rest of the trilogy. All of the strong points of the first game are still here. Great storytelling and worldbuilding, the characters are endearing, and it's full of very emotional moments. The music is still on point; just like in the previous game, you can bet that every scene will have an appropriate track that matches the moment and makes the experience all that much more impactful. The gameplay is a massive upgrade over Prelude to the Fallen. All of the awkward mechanics that didn't feel very good have been reworked. Equipments are simpler to understand and use, but at the same time they also have more strategic depth. The overzeal mechanic makes you pay attention to what gives or drains zeal and strategize around when you'll fill the bar. There are no co-op attacks unfortunately, but they do return in Mask of Truth. The game isn't too hard even in Hard mode, but it's also more balanced than in the previous game and you can't trivialize the tougher maps with broken mechanics. The Dream Arena (the post-game maps) offer a decent challenge, so if you're a fan of the gameplay then this is made for you.The plot of the game is spectacular, but you need to be a bit patient with it at the beginning. I thoroughly enjoyed every part of the game, but the start is admittedly somewhat slow. Once again, you begin with an amnesiac protagonist trying to solve the mystery of who he is an how he got where he is. Little by little he recovers his memories, and he also shows the kind of person he is through his interactions with his newfound friends. Haku is a great character, honestly, and I grew to love him as much as Hakuowlo and even more. The early parts has a lot of slice-of-life and minor action bits here and there, but somewhere near the middle of the game the action really picks up and never stops from there.Overall, it's a great game and I think that if you have even the slightest bit of interest in VNs and/or SRPGs then this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible story, mediocre gameplayHaving played the original version of the first game, this wasn't very challenging as a game. They've made attack patterns more elaborate and addeed equipments and so on, but where they've complicated things they've failed to add challenge. I didn't use the between battles exp grind functions, barely equipped items and I still played through on Hard mode with only a few defeats on the badassest bosses. In short, thye've added unnecessary padding to a battle system that doesn't urge yo uto use everything at your disposal.That aside, the story is incredible. Full of unexpected surprises and plot twists, neatly tying a new story to that of the prequel, opening your eyes to the secrets of the intriguing world a bit more. Worth playing through, just make artificial challenges like no equipment if you truly wish to be challenged for strategic prowess.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game. It's hard to explain much without spoiling anything but... the plot, characters, and worldbuilding are fantastic. Most of the game is pretty light-hearted and comical but then it really picks up toward the end, and the ending left me speechless. I can't wait to dig into Mask of Truth (the direct sequel)...
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: You take up a role of a bum with amnesia. Your main goals in life are eating, drinking and lazing around. You achieve these goals by somehow attracting a bunch of pretty girls whose personalities can be summed up with one, maybe two words. As in any decent anime, your inner circle also includes a total bro character. Can you guess what happens to him in the end? It's not a spoiler if you've seen it happen at least 7 times before!There are about 15 plot battles total across 30 hours or so of gameplay, each battle taking about 10 minutes to complete. The rest of the game is mostly filled with pursuit of your main goals. The plot doesn't really kick in until you're half way through. If you somehow manage to click and autocombo your way through these impossible odds, you'll be rewarded with an inconclusive ending pointing to a sequel and a picture of main girl's butt.10/10, it's okay.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: The next installment to Utawarerumono series. This time, we follow another protagonist named Haku. This can be considered a sequel to the Prelude of the Fallen although it can be played on its own (I do not recommend doing it for you are missing the references from the first game but it's doable to play this entry on its own). Set in the land of Yamato, you play as Haku and his ragtag band of people from various walks of life. It's the same format as the previous game but with overhauled mechanics in battles like removing the need for positioning, adding jump mechanics, healer-based character can now attack (unlike Eruruu who can only heal and not attack), The introduction of various attack style with different effect, range and buffs, the overhauling of Zeal method where in past game you can hold on to your max Zeal while in this game, once you hit max zeal, you go into the state of Overzeal and got a buff for the period of time while your Zeal decays. There's a lot more benefits but you can just go and play to see the benefits to Overzeal. Overzeal changes the playstyle where you must act fast instead of playing it safely with your Zeals. Some attacks now even consumes Zeal.The OST are still fire, as usual.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: Before I say anything else let me just put this out there. This is not an adult VN and it never was. Prelude (the first game in this trilogy) was originally an adult game, but later versions of it did not have those scenes. So don't buy these games expecting to patch in some raunchy scenes - because you can't as they don't exist. Don't be put off though - they don't need them to tell the epic tale of Utawarerumono.Two things:First. For some reason people are calling this port good or pretty good.When actually its not good at all. The battles feature fighting on the 3d map where you'll have noticeable lag combined with a 30fps lock. Using a smaller monitor should reduce the lag and let you enjoy the game more (game is a port from PS Vita). Playing with a 4k monitor will definitely cause some framerate drops/lag.That being said you can tell right away that its a high quality VN with great character designs, music and that extra "something" most VNs lack.So while the port isn't great it is still a great VN.And Second. Play Prelude first or watch the anime (the first VN). Its not out yet on PC, but its amazing and definitely ramps up the enjoyment.Reviews/comments saying this is a great place to jump into the series are crazy. Its not. The previous VN takes place in the same world years beforehand. You'll learn about the world/lore and meet a lot of characters that do show up during Deception. Watching the anime is a great substitute. The original series (Prelude) can be streamed on Funimation's website and likely other places as well.How good is this Trilogy? Good enough to get full anime adaptions/ports/translations for all three VNs. Nuff said.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has some very strong positives, which more than outweigh notable flaws that hold it back from greatness.+Exceptional characterization in a vivid setting, making you really care about the story+Excellent graphics with a consistent visual style+Interesting tactical RPG mechanics (zeal system, chained attacks, quick-paced battles)-Weird, awkward fanservice with pedophilia jokes; the game seems to want to pretend to be an H-game without actually having nudity or sex-An incredible amount of filler, especially in scenes involving eating, drinking, and shopping. Cutting about a third of this content would make the game more interesting without sacrificing any character development-Battles during the main game are too easy (even on 'hard' mode), have a lack of variety in victory conditions, and are spaced poorly--too infrequent early, with filler battles late
