_childDocuments_.review: Audiovisual this game is a beauty. More then any game I've ever played this looks and feels like an anime, and a pretty good one at that. Backgrounds are beautiful and detailed, voice acting is top notch and the english translation is wonderful. I normally never do this but I put this game on the big screen in the living room and put it on auto and while there's not much animation the art is so good that it feels like the whole thing is animated.The story starts with the protagonist waking up with amnesia. He doesn't even remember his name. Sounds like a cliché but it's actually interesting because he wakes up in a fantastical world with all kinds of weird creatures. This is interesting because he reacts like any one of us would react if in that situation: surprised and overwhelmed and scared I guess. Luckily he meets Kuon who takes care of him and whole bunch of other people along the way I won't say anything more about. Now, I know this game is actually the second in a trilogy and while I haven't played the first I can tell you the experience of exploring and getting to now this real world together with Haku is what makes in intriguing to me. Had I played the first game, that experience would definitely not have been the same. I recommend everyone to start here when you're interesting in the series. I can't understand why they would choose to do an amnesia angle in the second game but there you go. This game was released first in the west though so perhaps the developers felt the same way.After a few hours of getting to know this strange new world and it's inhabitants pacing issues start to arise though. There's a LOT of filler in this game. Yes, slice of life parts are essential but we don't need hours and hours of filler at a time. The middle of the game has more filler than main storyline. In fact, I wouldn't be surprised if I timed it that 50% or more of the game is actually filler. This 30+ hour game could easily be 10 hours shorter. Then when the main story picks up again, completely out of the blue you get a lot of information at once which kinda dampens the mystery, to then go back to filler again... So I started skipping the filler until I noticed I was actually skipping through some essential parts like introductions of new characters and it spoiled my whole experience. Something else I'd like to mention about this is that the humor is hit and miss. Some of it is charming but there's one particular running joke I found disturbing. The protagonist is physically a weak man. During the course of the game he often gets attacked by some of the other female characters, mainly Kuon. These attacks are for comedic effect and it's usually after he said something stupid. They are meant as jokes, nothing more. If they were just slaps on the cheeck and such I could take it as a joke. But there are scenes where you can actually hear his bones or skull cracking vividly. I found this deeply disturbing, well beyond a joke and it made me feel very uncomfortable. I can take a joke, no doubt, but how am I supposed to care about these characters when they physically abuse the protagonist like that?There's an amount of fan service as well. It feels out of place in the otherwise wholesome story. If you play japanese VN's though, sadly this is something you have to accept. I'm not against fanservice per se mind you, but it should fit the rest of the story and not just be added as eum... "service".You'll notice I haven't said anything about the turn based strategy battles. That's because there's not much to tell. They are few and very far between and are too casual to mean anything. I commend the developers of only adding battles when there's a storyline reason to do so and not add them at inopportune moments just to give us more gameplay. Other than that though there's nothing to tell, there's no strategy to them, just move and attack anything you see until the last man is down. They didn't really provide the variety I expected because there's not enough of it but it's fine that it's there.What started out as a very promising VN and did get back on track is dampened by pacing issues and too much filler. This is what keeps Utawarerumono Mask of Deception from being a genre classic.FYI There's an anime of this game (again, the first game is ignored here) as well which I haven't watched but is a lot shorter so must cut out some of the filler.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend the whole series, easily. This is part 2 of the wild ride and the beginning of Haku's story. Notably was released on steam before the translated remake of the first game. That being said, you should absolutely play that game first, followed by this one. Some say Mask of Deception is around 30 hours. It took me twice as long to clear it(I took my sweet-ass time with this), so YMMV.Still can't discuss much without potential spoilers. It should be understood that this game is a VN first and foremost and an SRPG second, so if you've got a problem with reading a lot of text, this isn't for you. Once you've accepted that, you've got nothing but a great time ahead of you. Kick back, relax, get to know the new cast, and enjoy the game. If you like this one, you can confidently jump into Mask of Truth and expect one hell of a conclusion to the series.The SRPG side has been revamped for this and Mask of Truth. Characters have more extensive movesets, and zeal works a bit differently. No weapons/armor equipment like the first game, but there is a greater variety of character skills and scrolls to work with. The DLC for this one features characters from a totally different series, so you don't have to worry about spoilers this time around.Great VN, fun SRPG levels. I had a total blast with this and Mask of Truth and can easily recommend it. Just, again, don't play these out of order. Only forewarning is that people seem to complain about the development of Deception. I wouldn't let that discourage you from playing. It's introducing a new setting, and a character that's new to the world around him. Much like you, the player, he's taking everything in each passing day and has a lot to learn. It takes some time to develop. Just keep going. Also, the way the game opens and segues into the main theme is so well done. If that doesn't make you want to continue, I don't know what will. Have fun.Eruru > Kuon btw. RIP Keiji Fujiwara. You did a phenomenal job as Haku.

_childDocuments_.review: Sequel to an eroge that came out in the early 2000s that randomly got a sequel like 10+ years later.This is a pretty good jumping off point for the series even if you haven't played/watched the original Utawarerumono, though you'll miss out on the hype when some of the old cast shows up. I do recommend that you play the original ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°) /remake, Prelude of the Fallen, before playing the final game, Mask of Truth.The story starts off pretty light-hearted tone, with a tinge of intrigue. This entry in the series mostly focusing on the day to day life of the characters, giving you ample time to get familiar with the cast as the story ramps up. Similar to the Tales series skits, most of the dialogue aren't really consequential to the plot, but it really does help with flushing out characters as well as their bonds with one another, and helps players feel invested in them, admittedly it is a bit slow to start, but i promise the pay off is well worth it. It's a bit tough to explain the series to someone who aren't familiar with the series, but in very simple terms it's Fire Emblem with cat girls with a lot of reading (like a ton of reading), really in depth world building and a charming cast of characters. If you're familiar with visual novels it might be taken surprised by the fact that unlike most visual novels there's really no choices to be made during conversations, going down specific routes to end up with your favourite waifu, though in it's place there's actual gameplay, i'm sure some visual novel enthusiasts ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°) will probably find it a bit off putting but as a result the writing is pretty tight since there's only one focus.Gameplay:Truth be told i haven't played too many grid based games, most of my experience are from this series, some FFT that i borrowed it from a friend and Fire Emblem 3H.Like most grid based games, you move around your characters and do battles, each characters have their range and attacks, characters take their own turns depend on how much speed they possess, nothing ground breaking here compared to what I've played in the genre. What sets the game apart from others in the genre are the combos, with each attack there are prompts to press a button to continue the chain and perform critical hits for a bit of extra damage and zeal gain, a bit like Paper Mario. Zeal is a momentum based resource that is gained/spent whenever perform an action and once your zeal hits 100 you gain an extra turn, no zeal cost for any ability and some stat increased/effects based on the element of the characters, as well as a special finisher unique to that character, similar to the Overlimit state in most games in the Tales series, and it lasts a few turns depending on the character. Similar to Pokemon each unit has a corresponding element, which have a weakness and strength depending on the opposing element. Character progression takes the form of a standard leveling system, you gain exp when you perform an attack and you gain exp at the end of battle, you also gain BP to allocate to stats for each character that participated how you see fit, none of that having to save scum because your character didn't roll the correct stat :^)The game has 2 difficulties, normal and hard. Normal is a good starting point for someone new to the series or someone who just wants to take it easy and experience the story. Hard is for someone who has experience with this genre of game, it isn't ball bustingly difficult and the game is rather forgiving with a generous rewind system. The main game itself isn't riddled with a lot of combat but if you're looking for more, there are post game maps after you've cleared the game. The next game in the series has a larger focus on the combat.As someone who isn't well versed in grid based games i found it pretty fun, with systems unique enough to differentiate itself from other games in the genre. The difficulty curve feels pretty smoothed and well designed with no huge spikes. My real only complaint are story missions are spread a bit thin compared to the other games.ArtI'm not sure if you've noticed but the game is pretty anime, the CGs can get pretty spicy at times but never any actual nudity, though the game does try really hard to remind you that the series used to be an eroge so if you have a problem with it, don't buy the game and complain that it's too anime or something dumb like that.Jokes aside, all the characters are well designed and beautifully drawn overall, the aesthetics of the game have this very lived in rustic charm to it.I generally recommend the series as a whole, but i can understand if you don't want to sit down and read for 20-30 hours and you're in luck since there's an anime adaptation (Localized as Utawarerumono: False Faces) of this game if you want to get the tl;dr version of the story, if you enjoyed it i recommend playing this game since it's more in depth and the anime changes some events/scenes from the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Most Role-Playing Game players would be put off by how this game paces itself. However, if you're planning to get this game, bear in mind that it is TECHNICALLY a game, with working mechanics and its complexity, but Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception is in truth, a VISUAL NOVEL given a more interactive layer beyond clicking dialog choices. And unlike the usual VN, this game's beginning, climax, and end are all linear. There are no secret endings nor are there flag-raising events and choices that affect the story.This title's main weapon is its story. Though not the best around, it builds the world, characters, and events properly enough to make you go on and finish it. Luckily, I already watched the anime (Utawarerumono, 2006) so I already had a grasp of what was going on and who these characters are supposed to be, especially the cameo characters. If you like something different from the typical shonen anime, try the anime out. It's old, yes. But it still holds up in many aspects (definitely not animation though, you'll be seeing a lot of reused animations and footage there).All in all, a fine game for a niche audience. I enjoyed it since I like VNs and such. Utawarerumono was always a niche franchise, and only a dedicated fanbase will appreciate this game and the series itself. To those who want to get into the franchise, be warned that it is an acquired taste, but is worth it. Not perfection, mind you, but enough to elicit interest and make it stay.P.S.This game is tagged for sexual content, but this is not an eroge. If you're looking for an eroge with RPG elements, look elsewhere, as this game does not have sex nor explicit fanservice. I recommend Kamidori Alchemy Meister or a handful of Kagura Games' selections if you prefer something more adult with good game mechanics.P.P.S.It was all Nekone's fault. If you finish the game, you'll get my drift.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the second Utawarerumono game, but it's disconnected enough from the first that you don't need to have played or seen the first. Characters from the first story appear in this one mostly as cameos, but those characters play a big role in the next game, Mask of Truth. If you intend to play the entire series, you’ll have to go through the first story eventually. The 2006 anime adaptation of the first game (2002) is solid and hits all the major plot points; I hear the anime  (2015) adaptation of Mask of Deception sucks, though. Important plot points are excluded, and make some of Mask of Truth’s story nonsensical. Don't buy this VN for the strategy RPG gameplay, this is a traditional visual novel. "Traditional" as in it's 40+ hours of reading, with a lot of slice of life filler, harem elements, and fanservice (no sex scenes though). Half the pictures on the steam store page are of the SRPG gameplay, but that's 5% of the main game. I never lost a battle on the hard difficulty, so it's not much of a challenge, but the combat is well designed. 5% of the  game is combat—after the story, there’s a postgame segment (the only part of the game without full voice acting) of 14 battles that are a lot harder than anything in the main game. You have to learn to manipulate facets of the combat system, and manage your units’ skills and positions carefully. The mode is unforgiving, with enemies capable of killing your units in one combat round, which, in my opinion, is a staple of good SRPG gameplay. The fact that that lethality is missing in the main story makes decisions a lot less interesting. The game’s rewind feature makes the challenging postgame fun rather than frustrating. I had a great 9 hours with the postgame. Supposedly, Mask of Truth’s combat is a lot better throughout the story.  Now the main part: the story. On the whole, I loved it. I’ve been reading fan-translated VNs since 2007, and I’ve hated most of them because of the combination of bad translations with bad, too-long slice of life scenes. The translation here is top-notch—no translations from English as a Fifth Language students here. People who know some Japanese might get upset at the way some phrases were translated, but they were changed for well-considered reasons. 100% faithful translations are garbage, and miss the point of translating. The slice of life fluff, though, is still here. In fact, it takes ~25 hours of slice of life before important stuff happens. What’s different is that, surprisingly to me, I either didn’t mind the slice of life segments, or straight up liked them. I’m still not sure why. I think it’s because of the combination of better character writing, the main character not acting like a desperate horndog around a bunch of girls, the plot relevance of the characters getting closer, and the charming voice acting. Some of the scenes are genuinely cute and funny, whereas a lot of VNs’ “funny” scenes make me wonder why I’m reading this VN written for idiots. In fact, it feels like this VN’s humor has western influences. A bunch of scenes play out like a cross between Seinfeld and K-On, with a “Kramer” busting open the door, helping himself to tea and confections, and turning a mundane scene into a noteworthy one. The game is 99.9% voiced and the voice actors did an amazing job. The little (and not so little) noises of emotion that the girls (and guys, actually) make are great; more so than any other VN or anime I’ve heard. i've never gone back so much to replay voice lines before this game. The verbal tics are on point, and remind me of Higurashi. Nekone's "nano desus" are chou kawaii, Kuon’s “kana?’s”, Atuy sounds like a valley hick, Anju sounds like a dignified royal brat, Rulutieh sounds like a shy, Munechika has big mune-chis. Even stronger are the political intrigue and the characters that drive it. It’s just a shame that Mask of Deception has so much setup that this part is understated, but I’m told Mask of Truth has more of this in spades, and that VM is rated better than this already well-rated one. There are problems, though. The main character perpetuates some stupid VN staples, much like the protagonist of the first Utawarerumono game/anime. They're both amnesiacs who are given the red carpet treatment throughout the story, instead of being treated like the nobodies they are. I can’t blame this entirely on bad writing, because it's actually somewhat justified by the stories, but I’d swallow it a lot more easily if the protagonists would deliberate more on the unearned trust they keep getting. In the first game/anime it's pulled off much better because of that protagonist's competence and bearing. Plus, he's treated with indifference for longer. Here, the protagonist earns admiration too quickly.  There’s an issue with the huge number of characters in a story told from only one perspective. Some of them get shelved for long stretches, even when it doesn’t make much sense. Especially memorable are two ugh-inducing fanservice characters. That's when the story feels like it should really start picking up, but no. it's just softcore porn for a short (but unrelenting) stretch, until those characters are placed on the shelves with the others. None of the characters are allowed to take center stage for too long, even when they really should, according to recent plot. And why is Kiwru even in the game? He’s one of the best combat units, but I was looking forward to more male characters in the story. Ougi and Kiwru hardly qualify. The last problem is that Moznu is the only pure waifu in the game, and you mess with his life.

_childDocuments_.review: The general problem with this game is that it is an okay one that follows an incredible one. It tries to follow up the performance of Prelude, while setting up for the next game. It works but it doesn't work... well.Let me first say that the combat was great. It was great in Prelude and it still continues to be great in Mask of Deception; Utawarerumono does this turn and tile based combat the best out of most games in the genre, in my opinion. The problem was, because I found the visual novel parts so trying, it felt like there were only a handful of battle sequences.The overarching story of Mask of Deception is actually quite good, it is worthy of it's predecessor. But man, most of the cast feel like a bunch of nobodies half the time. As you can imagine, this is one hell of a problem in a mainly visual novel game. In Prelude, Hakuowlo has side stories with every playable character AND with a lot of the side NPCS. It makes you feel their pain and loss, even if that side character was an NPC. I would go so far to say that even the most annoying characters of Prelude still elicited empathy from the player, that was how well written it was. I don't think we had a single one-on-one side story with Ougi or Jackdwalt? I didn't know these characters at all, they might as well have been Soldier No. 2 and Soldier No. 3 in my party. And it sucks because I WANTED to get to know them, they seemed cool!On the note of characterization, there was near-no romantic tension or build up between Haku and Kuon. Before the ending scene, they seemed more like close friends or mentor/student. Hell, Haku has more romantic development with Rulutieh and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Oshtor than he does with Kuon. I knew their romance was endgame but the writing did nothing for me to be excited for their romance.I feel like I must say this: the voice acting is incredible. If there is any fault with the characters being undeveloped, boring or annoying, the fault certainly doesn't lie with the voice actors.Ultimately, the reason I have to give this a Not Recommend is because I cannot in good faith recommend a game with uncomfortably outdated, creepy and sometimes paedophilic scenes if it's only an okay game. Prelude had them too, don't get me wrong, but I could roll my eyes and stomach it for Prelude because the overarching story was incredible and the characters were dearly lovable, or at least sympathetic. There's only so much my discomfort tolerance can take when it's just an okay game, and I'm not inclined to recommend this experience to anyone else unless they, like me, loved Prelude that much.This game was okay enough for me to want to play the third game; I've heard the third game is on par or better than the first. But as it stands, the only way I would end up recommending this game is if the third one is outstanding; then in that case I would recommend people to just... grin and bear through this one to get to the third one.

_childDocuments_.review: Aquaplus makes another banger. This game was intended to be a sequel to the original Utawarerumono, which is now called Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen, which is an amazing game in its own right, but playing this game only heightens your appreciation for this series. The worldbuilding is great, the OST is one of the most unique I've heard (The sound team at Aquaplus is very talented) and the BGs, CGs, and character art is some of the cleanest art ive seen in a long time, with Amazuyu Tatsuki my goat and Misato Mitsumi doing the art for this game, (and of course all the graphics guys that do a great job). They previously worked on titles by Leaf, like Comic Party, Tenshi no Inai 12-gatsu (read it it's peak) and ToHeart2 and many more, all of which I love dearly. The gameplay is actually a big step up from the first game, despite being older, requiring the use of actual strategy and planning in several battles. The game has some very unique and colorful characters, Haku being my goat, and Kuon is wife, along with all of the other characters I love and can't wait to see more of. Overall, Mask of Deception is a totally faithful and wonderful sequel to the first game, (which you need to play first) and I cannot wait to play Mask of Truth. Thank you Aquaplus

_childDocuments_.review: I usually don't write reviews, but MoD deserves one with a thumbs down.  I bought it thinking it was going to be TBS with VN elements or vice versa. It's none of those options.VN tipically have choices, there aren't any here. It's the resume of an entire anime, where hours pass between fights, something interesting or plot related. Around 75% is filler, even several secondary or support characters. Story would remain the same without them.The first half of the game is almost purely slice-of-life events, lacking character development, with many stereotyped characters who don't evolve at all or right before the game ends. There are few plot elements until the second half.Pacing is inconsistent, most of the time nothing happens and when the plot moves forward, it's usually very slowly, or rushed. The end of the game feels very rushed, leaving a cliffhanger with many misteries, events unfinished or in the dark. There are ways to leave a game open for sequels, U:MoD doesn't do it right.There are a total of 17 TBS battles, fairly easy in general. I don't mind that, but several units, skills and talents are unbalanced in a power race, looking to destroy enemies in 1-2 attacks. This is more obvious as tha game progresses. Also, since it seems you didn't have enough with the resume, there are cutscenes in the middle or after battles, and a few of them are quite long.There's a few more issues but I don't want to waste more time with this game. Overly priced, I can only recommend to get it with a 75% discount and only if you are desperate.If you look for a VN or games with choices, there are gems around steam at lower prices.If you look for an anime RPG game with better narrative, better world building  with charming characters and much more content for a lower price try Recettear: A item shop's tale

_childDocuments_.review: What a waste of time and money. Plot starts moving around 15h of "gameplay" and 5h later you will see credits roll. And that is with "hard" combat difficulty, on normal it will take an hour or 2 less (there all only around 15 fights in whole game). It is 100% linear, not even a single "fake" decision. And game ends so abruptly you just need to buy the sequel.I liked some of the background images and combat system is OK from QoL point of view: there is no grinding required, you call rewind whole turns as you wish. And that is about all that is good. Almost all characters are braindead, you cannot throw a stone without hitting some princess, and game favours adding more and more characters, even if they are thinner than sheet of graphene. Plot is also as simple as it gets. If it wasn't for a splash of gore here and there, and a few flashes of tits I would be sure the target demographics is 10-12 year olds.

_childDocuments_.review: Shame, after the first one being quite good, this one was... well... just plain not.I'll assume you've played the first one before you read this, if you haven't, then go buy and play that one first anyway. Come back here later, if you really liked it and just want to continue the overall settings story.First, the story... it's indirectly related, still connected clearly to the first, but generally not the same characters/location/etc... Unfortunately, it's kind of bad. The characters, the writing, the general plot, it feels like they decided to make a version meant for young teenagers, simpler joked, worse human, simplified and entirely predictable plot points. I literally did not get surpised once during this story, every point was predicted by me a bit in advance, and not in the oh it would be cool if X is X type, no, just the "ah... it's probably just X being X given how this is going" obvious type.Overall, it was just missing the quality that the first one had, not really a great story. Now, that doesn't mean all characters are bad or anything, some characters are likeable, though they are often written poorly, and a few definitely not likeable at least to me. The main value I feel after finishing it, is probably just how it sets up for the third game.Next is the gameplay. There's less of it than in the previous one, by a decent bit it feels like. Mostly just a visual novel this time. Honestly might be for the best because they changed the gameplay for the missions/combat. Besides largley being uninspired, the combat and ballance itself is worse. And they changed some designs like sharing XP to non participating units. Now, only those in the missions you pick get XP, and there's not enough slots to deploy everyone, even if there is everyone there in the story side for that fight. Until... the final mission, then you get to deploy everyone, but you'll probably have two underelevedl characters that literally deal like 1 damage to the enemy then, and die in one hit. Though given the questionable ballance and stat setup this time that can happen anyway, battles are much more frequently about enemies just doing stupid amounts of damage in one hit, rather than the more tactic styled gameplay the last one had. It wasn't perfect by any means, but definitely better than this ones.Overall... it wasn't terrible, but not good. Purely on it's own, not worth the considerable time it takes to finish I feel, only maybe given how it connects to the larger story that the third one might continue on with. Well, here's to hoping.

_childDocuments_.review: My VN experience is very small: Danganronpa, Zero Escape, Phoenix Wright. You get the idea.However, my JRPG experience is big. PS1 era and after, with some retro games.Story-wise it felt similar to a fast Trails of Cold Steel game. It doesn't pad but when it does it's only to introducethe world and the characters better. It has a certain 3-4 hours timespan where the pacing is kinda off, and the writersjust decided to put a lot of "slice of life" events in a single chunk. This was for me the slowest part of the game. But overall the pacing is very good, especially from halfway and until the end. I also heard that the pacing remains great for the direct sequel, Mask of Truth, which I haven't yet bought because I want to 100% the achievements here first (unless I get a bug).Like most of anime stories it has its share of tropes, but I found them entertaining. The characters range and it's a matter of preference but personally I enjoyed them all, with a few exceptions which I will not name because it's spoiler territory.The SRPG elements are simplistic, but they're not "Shining Force 2 simplistic". It also has an infinite rewind feature that also lets you choose which step to rewind back. In the normal game duration I tried to use it sparingly, and besides there's no such thing as a permadeath so why bother rewinding? There's also post-game content which, as you might have guessed, more battles and no plot, so people who play this for the plot may not care. But I enjoyed both the story and the gameplay.Given that the game has infinite rewind feature you can safely start on the hardest difficulty. It's almost about as hard as Fire Emblem: Three Houses on Hard, meaning "Hard = Easy/Normal".Outside of the 30 fps lock I had no other problems performance wise.I recommend this game to anyone who played Trails in the Sky and Trails of Cold Steel because the world building, tropes and pacing are *somewhat* similar, except I like this story more on many things which would be again a spoiler if I say.Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Massive improvements in both story and gameplay over the first game (Prelude to the Fallen). Also keep in mind that this is the first part of a duology and mostly serves as a setup for the second part (Mask of Truth). And a warning: do not search for anything related to the second part as due to the nature of this story it's very easy to get spoiled on important events.Biggest improvements in terms of story over the first game are the pacing and the balance of "Slice of life event scenes vs plot" while simultaneously avoiding falling into a formulaic loop that would prevent the story from progressing at a satisfying pace. While this game keeps the same formula as its predecessor (story -> bunch of SoL events -> story -> SoL -> repeat), I have rarely felt annoyed by the pacing this time. Perhaps due to the fact that the story is much less repetitive and the events are better integrated without feeling so disjointed from the rest. I have even heard several people mention that Mask of Deception has some of the best pure SoL side scenes they've read in story heavy VNs. The characters also feel a lot more fresh/modern and less one note compared to Prelude.The gameplay improves a bit partly because of removing the position based damage modifiers and partly by making all the maps essentially open fields (thus removing the player's ability to create chokepoints), instead focusing on more difficult and complex enemies. However, the main story still doesn't provide any especially difficult encounters that would require you to do some complicated maneouvering even on Hard difficulty. But the individual character kits are a lot more interesting and allow you to do some fun stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: Mask of Deception and Mask of Truth, which are effectively the same story and I don't think I could really review them separately, definitely make up a unique and very fun experience. It's about 70% Visual Novel and 30% SRPG so keep that in mind as the store page tends to show them off in a more action oriented light than the games themselves. Deception starts out slow, and while at first I was unsure about it, I have to say their taking the time to flesh out the world and characters really pays off. By the end you really wish there was another 30 hours of this cast just goofing off and going on side adventures. Truth is pretty much all main plot after it ramps up later in Deception and boy does it go hard. Definitely very well crafted, and easily my favorite fantasy visual novel series. Very fun world and characters which I truly wish I could spend more time with. One thing to note, this does require some knowledge of Prelude of the Fallen, the prequel game. I was quite satisfied with just reading a synopsis of Prelude and referencing the wiki for the random prequel characters as they popped up. Did not feel like I missed out much by starting with Deception. I will probably go back to prelude but I thought it worth mentioning. I think my only real critique is that the SRPG combat has some really swingy difficulty. Mostly pretty easy but some of the late game fights add a lot of difficulty in ways that I can only describe as mechanically frustrating. Overall great series though, I hope they make more games in this world. This is the only visual novel series where I enjoy spending time with the characters so much that I intend to reread it which is probably the highest praise I can give.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a slow-paced visual novel + tactics RPG to get into, set in a fantasy world that's blended with science fiction, with multiple layers to the plot, and with writing that continuously builds on itself, look no further and get ready to experience an unforgettable journey!Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception (MoD) takes place approximately two decades after Utawarerumono: Prelude of the Fallen (PofF), but you don't need to play PotF first to enjoy the story as it was definitely designed for players new to the universe in mind. If you're anything like me and love the challenges that come with solving the questions and mysteries of the plot on your own, I recommend MoD, Mask of Truth (MoT), and then PotF in this order, just like how I played! If you want a linear story experience, one where you can also enjoy the easter eggs hidden in the Mask games, you should play PotF, MoD, and then MoT in this order. Story: 8.5/10The world-building in this game is amazing. The game is even equipped with a glossary and pictures to showcase the unique foods, culture, people, and endemic life in this world! The plot development is generally slow throughout this game, but it's worth every moment as the writing continuously builds on itself, and in some cases, even comes full circle, unfolding the brilliance and magic of the author's vision. The best way I can describe this game is that it's like a 40 hour tutorial that introduces you to the world of Utawarerumono and its characters, along with the game's overall battle mechanics, but does so by surrounding you with the warmth and company of your boon companions, sharing cups of sake at night, and marveling at the beauty of the full moon. It's got some serious moments, plenty of hilarious moments, some pensive moments, but all-in-all, the ending of MoD sets up for its sequel so well, you really can't help but feel the need to start MoT. Also, this game is fully voiced in Japanese, and the English translation is so good, you'll be learning Japanese in no time!Gameplay: 8/10I truly enjoyed the gameplay! Each map is a grid featuring environment and the game uses a unique leveling system for all characters, all of whom have unique abilities and perks, but this is not your standard tactics RPG. For example, if you're trying to get a critical hit in, the game will skill check you to see if you can land it! That's one of my favorite parts of the game. For some characters, I am nothing less than critical hits galore, but for others, I can have anywhere from a 0%-40% chance to crit. But that's not all! During fights, characters may even speak to each other via speech bubbles, filled with comedic grunts and other voice noises. It really makes each development that much more enjoyable. The only thing holding the gameplay back is that experience is limited; characters can only gain experience if they participate in battles and fights, so if there is no room to deploy some of your characters, they will not gain experience and will eventually fall behind. Difficulty: 5/10 I am a seasoned tactics player, so the game wasn't really challenging. Music: 9/10The music is phenomenal. You'll eventually see why.

_childDocuments_.review: This game acts mostly as a setup for the sequel: Mask of Truth. I would strongly recommend buying both at once because this one ends on a cliffhanger. Playing the prequel: Prelude to the Fallen, is not necessary to enjoy this story.Although it claims to be an RPG/VN mix, it is more accurate to say that it's 98% VN, occasionally interrupted by a battle (of which there are 17 throughout the whole main game). This part of the Utawarerumono series is mostly slice of life and foreshadowing - all of the conclusions come in the sequel, but although it can be meandering at times, it serves as a great set-up for the later twists. A lot of the story beats of the sequel would not hit as strongly without experiencing this game first.That said, when the game lists 'reference to alcohol' as part of their mature content warnings, what they mean is about 10 hours of characters drinking and chatting or chatting about going drinking.

_childDocuments_.review: Sequel to Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen, Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception. In my opinion, this is better than the prequel in many ways.First is the story, I would say the story overall has very nice pacing. Slow at the beginning then it went very smooth till the end. At the beginning, there are many slice of life moments, different characters hanging on the streets, chatting some dumb stuff. When it gets to the serious moments, it gets very hyped. I should say the battles later on are very intense. If you have played the prequel, you know what I mean. Then, we have the sad moments. It definitely hits super hard. Make sure you don't rush the story tho. I had a lot of fun from various scenes(Funny ones, intense ones or straight up dumb stuff). The story overall is better than the prequel. Then the characters. No matter the character designs or the character writing in the game are very well done. I should say most of the side characters had their moments. Rulutieh, Atuy, Nekone and Anju are all great side characters. Don't forget about the main characters though, Haku and Kuon are excellent characters. Then we have Ukon and Sakon, fun characters. They made me laugh quite a bit. You will see why. The character writing in this game has much more depth than Prelude to The Fallen.Gameplay: There is a huge change when it comes to the gameplay from the prequel. In my opinion, this game is way better. Each characters have more special attacks some can only be used in specific conditions. Although the combat system is a bit complicated due to different effects that can applied to a character, the gameplay is way better than the prequel. I had a lot of fun. If you don't really like the gameplay from Prelude to The Fallen, this one should be the game for you. Music: I think I don't need to mention much. I think it is as good as the prelude to the fallen. Songs are great. I think remixes of some of the songs from the prequel are also very good.I see some people arguing about playing which game first. I would say Mask of Deception is much more friendlier than Prelude to The Fallen and there are no big disadvantages for not playing Prelude to The Fallen as the game will explain some of key points to some of mysterious behind the story. However, you can try to play the first one first then go and play this as well as you can get to understand all of the characters from Tuskur and some of them will be a major role in Mask of Deception. Hope this review helps. I love this game and the prequel. I will try Mask of Truth in the next couple of days.

_childDocuments_.review: The turn-based combat in this is a bit more interactive  but still doesn't require much thought much like in prelude to the fallen. The story in this is much more of an adventure plot than war so there's more world building here. The events that follow after selecting a destination in this are a lot more coherent than in prelude to the fallen also the game's literacy and vocabulary are much better too. There's not quite as many battles in this unlike prelude to the fallen (it was a war story after all), but they are much more difficult. The use of "The Legend" theme is much more effective now that there's characters that have already been established from a previous entry. Previously it did nothing for me when I was introduced to a character that I knew no history of whenever that theme started. I enjoy the characters in this much more than in Prelude to the Fallen even though they are pretty tropey.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate VN in general, and only bought this because I really liked the anime and wanted to see more of Haku and the gang having fun in the capital. However, this game was a pleasant surprise. The story is so good that I actually enjoyed the visual novel part of the game. Every line is voiced, and the background sound and music always fit well. If you like Utawarerumono, it's most likely due to the story and sound. This game does both perfectly. Haku is also a much more interesting character than as portrayed in the anime. Not that the anime is bad. This game is that good.As for the tactical combat part, they're good too. Not too easy, not too difficult. They also give you QTE when using skills, so you're not simply left hanging while watching your unit do a move. Successful QTE gives a crit. It's such a nice touch.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic visual novelThe art and CGs are greatThe story is fantastic and goes to some dark places with occasional humor to balance those moments outIts a SRPG segments to break up the gameplayWhile it isn't deep, it is pretty funOverall I enjoyed it a lot and am looking forward to playing the sequelsPersonally loved the ending is ends on a pretty great cliffhanger
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: Strong recommend if you like great worldbuilding, a likable cast of characters, and a sweeping epic storyline that does both slice-of-life and grand politics moments very well.--This is the second visual novel in the  series, released about 13 years after the first one, and the improvements in writing are noticeable. Characters are less trope-y, romance and social topics are handled more tastefully, and the pace just feels more tightly wound and focused this time around. The main cast of characters is very likable, and there is a surprising amount of nuance to how each character thinks and works their way around the scenarios presented to them (Especially Kuon, she's a great character and probably one of my favorite VN characters in recent memory).The tactical combat gameplay is okay- I found it more streamlined than the cumbersome gameplay of the first game, but it's still easy and rather mindless compared to other similar games on the market. However, it does it's job as an occasional break from reading, and the investment I had in the story and characters helped make the combat sections more enjoyable.Overall, I think this visual novel (and it's sequel, ) is much better than the first one, and definitely worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: Somewhat similar plot twists to the prologue. Combat seems less tactical and more reflex based. Mask of Deception does end on a cliffhanger so playing next game Mask of Truth is necessary to progress the story. My main issue is that protagonist is well, a complete failure and very unlikable (for me at least). Nevertheless the game is very good and well worth playing. If you liked the first game most probably you will like this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: This is another fantastic anime game. If you are interested in the series, start with the first one, Prelude of the Fallen. Both games have been fantastic. The first one is split probably 1/3 combat, 1/3 story and 1/3 relationships. This one is about 1/2 relationships and 1/4 combat + 1/4 story. Overall a very satisfying series. I will say that this one ended somewhat abruptly, but I am guessing the final will pick up where this left off.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the second of the trilogy, I think. The first game was very interesting, but had some lengths. This one also has some moments where I thought "I don't care for those secondary intrigues, let me watch the main story", but they were less numerous than in the first.Gameplay wise, I find it better, but also it is a bit lacking some things I loved in the first, i'm not sure what, but maybe a bit too few battles between the VN part?The story and characters are wonderful. I hope that the next game in the trilogy is a sequel because the plot is open and this feels like a first part of a big plot. For anyone who love good VN stories, with a bit of tactical gameplay for the battles, this is a good one. No doubt.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: Second entry in a great VN series. Mechanically this is the game that shows its age most as actually the oldest release, as its missing a number of QOL features found in the prequel and the sequel such as exp being earned by all units even if not in the battle, or healers getting exp for healing.This game is very much a title focused on setting up the second part, so its quite slow and more interested in building up and introducing the characters, much like the first entry of an arc of the Trails series. The characters are all great though, and theres alot to like here, and then it ends on a cliffhanger that makes you really want to dive into the final game.I would recommend you play Prelude first for the references to that game made in this (and even more so in Mask of Truth).If there is one main criticism to take with this series on steam, and this applies to all 3 Utaware entries, its the quality of the ports. All 3 games are optimised for 720p, all assets and internal rendering are set for that resolution, and the games are locked to 30fps. There is a dll you can find in the discussions for the mask games that will bump up the internal rendering resolution to your current window resolution, but there's nothing that can be done about the 30fps and hud elements sadly. At least since the game is 90% VN and then a Turnbased gameplay style, the 30fps doesn't hurt it too badly compared to other more action oriented gameplay styles.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: This is the second part of Utawarerumono series. In terms of "gameplay" experience, I'd say the combat system is smooth and isn't as rough as the first one. Then again, this is a visual novel with a hint of tactical rpg gameplay to it and not a pure tactical rpg. Do not expect some sort of complicated combat system. The story starts off slow and it has a lot of world building. If you like the first part of the series then you most probably would enjoy this one as well!
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: Not as good as Prelude to the Fallen in my opinion but that could be because Prelude was my first ever VN so it will always hold that place of introducing me to a new genre. That being said.. GOD these games are outstanding, if you haven't played these or even haven't played a VN before just do yourself a favour and buy it. Make sure you play them in order though because the stories are back to back. Just beautiful..
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: Kuon. She never gets less annoying.If you're wondering when this gets good. It is only in the last cut-scene/story segment. So you have to struggle through ~30 hours of itKuon thinks she's the main character, and maybe the author/writer does too.Nearly every scene or character interaction or action you'd expect the main character to do is taken by Kuon instead.The character you play as is the comic relief sidekick character. I found it frustrating and stressful.Everything about the story and world building feels inferior to the first game and it feels like general Japanese culture has leaked into the universe where the writers have gotten lazy.Having played the trilogy, I can say that Kuon never gets better. This is her story, not yours.I enjoyed the last 15 minutes though.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: After completing all 3 games (Prelude to the Fallen, Mask of Deception, Mask of Truth), this was an absolutely stellar experience. I looked forward to every day I was to get back to the game and progress the story. I wish there was more but am very happy nonetheless to have had the chance to play this series. Although I’ve now completed the story, I still get to play Monochrome Mobius, so there is yet a bit more of this world to enjoy.If the “visual novel” tag tends to turn you off, then please understand this series is a “kinetic” novel. There are no choices, no routes and no self-insert character. It is primarily a narrative experience that you can simply set the dialogue to auto and enjoy watching as though reading a book or listening to an audio-book. There are tactical RPG gameplay sequences when story battles come up, but they are not difficult and largely you will simply be watching the story.I highly recommend the entire series.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: Great visual novel combined with an SRPG. The SRPG's interface is not as developed as Fire Emblem's, but it's good enough. Visuals are pretty rough for a modern game though, especially the title screen UI being blurry on my 1440p screen. 3D is capped to 30fps even though it only uses low poly chibi style models and environments. Not a huge deal for me though since the story and world-building is the main reason why you would play this game in the first place. It also ended on a good part of the story, making you want to play the sequel immediately.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: Great game with a huge but very good cast and a huge cliffhanger in the end. I don't like the politics and sci-fi aspect of the first game so the adventure in a fantasy world (no isekai, no OP cheat, no gaming gimmicks) is my favorite part of Mask of Deception. Hopefully the final game still has some of that. Also, it's fortunate that we can play the whole trilogy now instead of having to wait for the third game to come out later. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: Despite all the things I am about to say, I still recommend this game for what it is."Mask of Deception" is the awkward middle entry in the series. Playing after "Prelude to the Fallen", "Mask of Deception" establishes the base for "Mask of Truth". It is necessary in its role. It also adds new, interesting mechanics to combat, and its story is mostly wholesome and pleasant.The downsides are that the fan service aspects that refer to the first game dominate a bit too much of the story.I wouldn't play this just on its own, but rather as the first, weaker half to "Mask of Truth", which is where the series shines once again.In conclusion: This is a good game. It is great at doing what it aims to do. Sadly, it is surrounded by a prequel and a sequel that either have a more interesting story (Prelude to the Fallen), or have far superior gameplay (Mask of Truth).Unless you have a lot of money to throw around, I would probably wishlist it and wait for a sale on this one, though I still recommend playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: To all wondering which GAME TITLE to buy, I too was confused about what game was the first and which I should buy. So I leave a few key points..There was nearly a decade long gap between the release of first game "Fallen" and release of the two sequels Mask of Deception/Truth."Fallen" The first installment has an entirely different cast of characters from another time altogether.  It made a far better third game than a first. IMO. Its combat is very basic and AoE isn't utilized very much. It also lost its mature content (which was arguably weird) but still hints at some events.If you are interested in Utawarerumono, go ahead and buy and play Mask of Deception and then Mask of Truth. Again the story is entirely set apart from the first game, the combat has more engaging features, it has more sprites and unique locations, and it's story moves MUCH further and is more creative and ambitious than the first installment.Enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: Please, even though you don't HAVE to read the first one in this series, I really recommend you do.  I won't go too in depth here, but this game sets up the last game perfectly, and is heavy with slice of life moments to help you connect with all of the characters, and I gotta say it was really well done. the last 10 hours or so really picks up and sets it up for the epic finale.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: There might be some minor spoilers so read on at your own risk.The second title in the Utawarerumono series, Mask of Deception continues the story albeit in another country following a new protagonist and entirely new cast. You don't need to play the first Utawarerumono game Prelude to the Fallen (henceforth Prelude) to be able to follow and enjoy the story, but it can help tie things together when some characters from the first game do appear (mostly as cameos).The feel and mood of the story is quite different from the first, so for those who have played the first and expect more of the same, that's not exactly what you will find. The best way to describe it is there's a generational shift in how the world is and the writing feels... younger.Pacing:There is considerably a lot more dialogue in this game than Prelude and at times it feels like you have to go through 1 or 2 hours of text before the next battle, so it feels a little a little slow at times but that could just be world building and character development. Things start to pick up towards the end.Combat in the game does seem more challenging compared to Prelude of the Fallen and you may find yourself using the rewind function quite often even on normal difficulty. Enemies are scaled quite evenly to your party and have more skills available to attack you with. You probably won't even need to replay battles to grind level your characters, but it can make it easier. Replaying battles do not give bonus exp at the end like Prelude does iirc, so you only get a few bonus points you can save up for boosting character stats in addition to the exp earned by characters attacking enemies of similar levels in battle.The tactical aspect of the game also evolved to include jumping spots on the map and environmental buffs to characters of certain affinities depending on weather.Items:There are no more usable/consumable items in the game compared to Prelude. However, there are a lot of equippable items (accessories) that provide buffs and multiple characters are able to perform healing with their skills, as opposed to only one in Prelude. In terms of re-watching the story, this game sadly does not include the feature of jumping to different scenes and viewing them individually after beating it, but then there are so many scenes it'd be hard to keep track in the first place. Overall I liked the game and recommend it. However it is written as part 1 of a 2 part story, so keep your save file if you intend to play the next chapter and want to reap the benefits of the time you put into this game and carry it over to the next chapter.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: A fitting, a wonderful second installment to the Utawarerumono.The writing remains top notch, with each character feeling extremely fleshed out, and almost impossible not to get attached too. The music score is gorgeous, and I've found myself listening to it over and over again.The gameplay, while still relatively unnecessary, arguably, has received severe improvements to the last installement, and feels quite a bit more complex and enjoyable.Difficulty is still, of course, rock bottom, but considering that this is a story-driven game, it matters very little.The ending  I still look forward to going through the final chapter of this wonderful story.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: If you like the anime, you will probably like the game as well. Compared to the first game (Prelude to the Fallen):- Less play time (~30 hrs main plot, a few more hours for the dream arena)- Less fighting scenarios- A richer fighting system with more character skills- Less fighting + more complex system = harder to get familiar with it- Enemies in fights do a lot more damages- Slightly more deviations from the anime (~80% similarity), probably for the reason of making a few more fighting scenariosThe music, artwork and voice over are as good as the first and make the game an enjoyable experience. I would give it an 7.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: It is highly recommended that you have played the first Utawarerumono game or watched the anime adaptation of the first game before you play this second game. You'll get much more enjoyment out of it if you do. However, doing so is not mandatory, as you'll understand the story of this game just fine even without the context of the first game. Just expect some character appearances and world events to fly past your head. Now that that's out of the way, I'll briefly talk about why this game is good. Mask of Deception is basically a 30-hour long "buildup" to the climatic third game, Mask of Truth, which is widely considered to be the Muv-Luv Alternative of Utwarerumono. As such, most of Mask of Deception is simply world-building, getting to know new characters better, and slowly getting to the bigger plot. The game does this mostly through light-hearted, low-stakes slice of life/sitcom antics. While this sounds boring on paper, I enjoyed every moment of Mask of Deception. Usually, in visual novels, the sitcom stuff is usually the boring part that you have to grind through in order to get to the "good part", the plot. Well, here, I'm happy to say that every part is the good part. The sitcom and slice of life stuff are genuinely very funny, and I came to really like the characters. I was also excited to see old characters that I've come to know in the previous utawarerumono make an appearance. The world of utawarerumono also got a lot bigger and detailed with this installment. The plot really starts to heat up towards the end and launches us nicely into the third and final game of this trilogy. I highly recommend this game and the entire trilogy. It has been a very immersive and entertaining experience, and I look forward to seeing this story through to the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: Utawarerumono Mask of Deception is a really well made experienceThis is the second game of a trilogy and is an alright starting point, though it would be better if people interested in this game play Prelude of the Fallen first as that is the first game.This game is very good, however I did not truly enjoy my time with it and I felt there were so many tropes used that I not only disliked, but felt repetitive and there were so many moments that I just read for the sake of reading.HOWEVER, this game truly pays off if you play the sequel (Mask of Truth) right afterwards, and if you combine the 2 experiences together, it is an unbelievably joyful experience filled with twists and turns that make the overall experience unlike any other. Playing the whole trilogy is something I recommend, playing this game as a by itself experience is not something I recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: A really great game. This game cannot be really separated from its sequel Mask of Truth(Futari no Hakuoro), but I will try to review it based on this game alone as much as possible.First thing first, anyone looking to play a great Turn-Based Strategy game may be dissapointed. It's not because this is a bad Turn-Based Strategy game, it's because the game itself more focused on story aspect so play this with a Visual Novel in mind. The battle system itself is simple and quite good. I have some experience in this kind of genre so I play on Hard difficulty. Even on Hard difficulty the game is not that hard and you don't need to do any grind to beat the game.Now the story. The story overall is really good if you consider all of the game or at least just Mask of Deception and Mask of Truth. I, myself will consider it a masterpiece. But, if you only look at this one game, first half of it are just slice of life things including character introductions and their relationship buildings. Many people will dislike it because too much of low tension relaxing daily life thing, but for me each of this are piece of episode on each characters relationship with other characters. Great character and relationship building like this affect on how you will feel about them in their unfolding future conflict. Now for the other half of the story. The story suddenly ramp up and hidden conflicts rain down on the story following a certain impetus. Here is all what those first half-hater waiting for. From now on it is full on action, conflict, backstabbing, conspiracy, strategy, and tragedy.And now for the pros and cons. Pros:-Great character and in game event arts. I really love the art personally.-Good 3D battle graphics. Not that cool, but good. The animation and special effect is good.-Good Turn-Based Strategy gameplay. Not that good as I feel it wasn't really the focus of the story, but good enough.-Great overall story. With all game combined, I personally consider it as masterpiece.-Each character have their own personality that build up as the story goes.-There is level system but you don't need to grind any of your character. Your usual party setup is enough to beat the game without you going out of the way to grind you characters even if you play on Hard difficulty.-Many famous Japanese Voice Actress/Actor so those who enjoy it will love it very much. Overall all VAs doing great jobs on this game.-Great English translation. If you understand Japanese you may feel "Wait, that he isn't exactly say that!", but looking on the context it is not a really wrong translation and is still in line with those characters.Cons:-Battle system gameplay may pale in comparison with many other Turn-Based Strategy games. -First-half of the story maybe too slow paced for many people. And you CANNOT choose to miss them.-If you want to raise level of all characters it will be quite hard as normal grinding reward you with really small experience points and stage first time clear bonus only applied to used characters.-Free Battle mode(play previous cleared stage) only useful to get missed achievement and grind for small exp. So, most people may not even need to play it.-The story ending give you the need to play next game as this game is not really a standalone game.Conclusion:A really great Visual Novel with Turn-Based Strategy battle system as bonus. The story is really great and it is recommended to play at least this and the next one(Mask of Truth) but it is better if you play the first one(Prelude to the Fallen) too. Even if you don't like the first-half of the story, please bear with it as it will get really good. You can set to be able skip unread story in the setting but I don't really recommend it. This game is not a standalone one so prepare to play the sequel after you finish this.If you want a great story game and don't hate Turn-Based Strategy battle system, I really sure that this game series is a really good one.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: This is more of a review of the whole series rather than just this game. This series is considered one of the top VNs of all time so hold onto your seat or something as there's three games to all play. With the prelude, Utawarerumono mask of truth and mask of deception, it's a mature story, that gets you, it's the only rpg game I can think of where all battles are story related and all have meaning that I played. Characters even talk during battles so gameplay sections feel less like an interruption to the story but more so a continuation of it. As I see a lot of jrpg feel the need to put a battle in every 5 mins sometimes even leaving the story alone for 8 or so long battles with little to no relation to what's going on in the story. Like they're afraid players will lose attention to the game like their attention span is super low or some such, always thought that was super annoying in a lot of jrpgs. Like characters would be talking about something super important only to have random monster battle 605 pop up and bang never continue what anyone was saying, story section over, story-wise games that do this just make it feel so stunted. Like short story sections are only a reward for the gameplay sections and they're completely separate, which makes no sense why can't story-based games be a part of both. Not that I hate all games that do that, some are worse than others, it's just after so many games doing that it gets a little frustrating after playing so many. But with Utawarerumono the story never takes the backseat never gets cutoff to pad time or whatever, this allowed the story to always be at the forefront, the story exists to be told, it takes center stage at all times and never stops shining, I feel this made it feel more real, and then also more epic when you do go into battle as there's a major reason and no disconnect from said story.For Disclaimers:-First off Now this is anime styled game so obviously there's anime artwork and tropes if you're fan you'll like it as it's pretty good in that aspect, if not well you probably stumbled into a weird area in steam. I'm already corrupted from past experiences leave while you still can, it's more than likely not for you.-There's long down times within the story and it takes time to pickup were things get intense like most stories, so sticking with it will help it's a slow burning game but I for one enjoyed those times just as much as any of other times in the story. A lot of the time the mood in those are directly related to what happened before hand so even in those times it feels a bit more real as action isn't shoehorned in all the time as that makes no sense in story setting like this.-If you're here only for action or strategy in the turn based sections this probably isn't a game for you. As you might've guessed it's mostly a VN and there's peace times like E.g where characters go do normal things they'd do in their normal life. That allows you get to know them more and just have fun moments were people are not fighting for their very lives which lets the story show the more living out their lives side of the games world. To see exactly what these characters are even fight for in the first. These parts can be pretty interesting as it can show the games world's inventions and commodities, it's where a lot of world building is. Again that's not for everyone, but if you played something like a VN before this is perfect for you. -2 As I made this review after my second playthrough of the game. The only reason i'm pressing the above part is because way back for the first time a played this it was on playstation I rented it from gamefly and one of top reviews(out of the three that were there) at the time it came out(so isn't like that anymore) said something along the lines of there's no gameplay, too much talking and reading, returned it after 10mins. Besides wanting to commit toaster bath from having the pleasure of reading that "review" I realized that holds some truth for some as it just wouldn't be the game for them and that's understandable whether that constitutes giving it a bad review or not is entirely different conversation. So for me this was an eye-opening experience, for the story itself made me feel things I never had before. if I had to describe it without being too specific, it's a story about losing yourself, losing/gaining feelings, while accompanied by characters that all feel pretty real in their settings. They have their own things they get upset about, they bring others happiness in different ways, they have drinking parties to get over things, characters try to laugh at the face of their problems in their own ways. The world-building continues throughout all three games and feels accomplishing. You can tell by the name of the game as with a mask, it means hiding your identity, it means to lie, a lie can become real with enough effort, but if you live in a lie long enough can you ever go back after becoming what you lied to become?
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the trilogy. What a rollercoaster of emotions.You don't have to play Prelude of the Fallen to enjoy this game, but I advise you do. You might miss out on backstories or subtle references.Story is great. This game focuses a lot more in 2 aspects if you compare it to PotF: Character development in a slice-of-life event approach (which I really liked but might not be everyone's cup of tea) and military/political affairs.Music is great, voice acting is great nad Amazuyu Tatsuki's art is even greater so good luck not loving the characters.In this 2nd novel, this improved on some aspects of the combat, and broke others. Has its quirks but its passable.Highly recommended, the trilogy earned a place in my heart!
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: The point at which they decided to end the game and make you open your wallet for a "sequel" will frustrate you, but otherwise, a good game.  I wish there had been a higher difficulty option though, Hard wasn't that hard, the only real challenge outside of a few surprises came in the extra stages.
