_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: Better worldbuilding, deeper gameplay and a more consistently engaging story than Prelude. First third is fairly slice of life/vignette heavy, but I didn't mind (just missed battles a bit). Very much one half of a whole, so the ending lacks the emotional oomph and closure of Prelude's, but this is almost certainly the better game overall and in all other respects. 9.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: Considering the time gap between the first game and this one, I assume it wasn't a planned sequel. Even so, I wasn't disappointed by the result. Even though it starts similarly as the first game "amnesiac man gets found by cute girl and taken care of", you quickly can tell their personalities are pretty different, compared to the first game's counterpart. As such, the story doesn't feel repetitive and can be just as enjoyable as the first game. I could keep on going, but I think you get the picture. If you liked the first game, I'm 99% sure you will like this one as well
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly, this game feels hastily done in comparison to its prequel. Which also had some obvious issues with mediocre gameplay. In it's entirety the game is much shorter and the story progresses slower than Prelude but honestly, if you played the 1st one you've probably accepted it for what it is. That's why this game still gets a thumbs up for me. Because even with less gameplay and a less fleshed out story the characters are where this series shines and that doesn't change in this.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: Originally, I watched the anime for this game in particular in 2019, finished it, and realized that this was originally a trilogy of visual novels, and I was unsure if I really wanted to dive into it because of that. I ended up by this game when it was one sale PS4 not long before the PC release. I bought it again while it was on sale a while ago, and have beaten it for the second time.I might edit this later to add in my full thoughts and copy-and-paste it after I beat Mask of Truth again, but to put it in a few sentences, I've never experienced a piece of fiction in my life that has managed to physically strangle me with the ending. This small saga as a whole is something I wholly believe is worth experiencing. If you're not sure about the visual novel aspect as I was, I would encourage you to try it anyway, but starting with Prelude to the Fallen.In all fairness, the saga as a whole is probably a 9/10, maybe a 9.5 at best, but personally, it is a masterpiece with no equal. That says enough, I think.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: This game is required to play the next game, Mask of Truth.It's a beautiful tale, my first game into the series. Prelude is very urged game to play before this, but not required. This was my second playthrough of it, after the feels trip it gave me I couldn't touch it for a very long time.Going through it again, I could pick up on almost all the nods to the Prelude cast, which was extremely refreshing. I believe my emotions got the best of me and I didn't take in everything my first round. It was fun, I wish it never ended; that changes happened. I could read a light novel or buy multiple novels of the slice of life events that happen with the main character and his crew. I want more, and I won't ever get it again.Thanks Keiji for being my Haku, I'm sorry I didn't play with your voice on at first through Deception. Your expressiveness was amazing and I enjoyed listening to your marvelous voice, you are forever timeless, wherever you are now.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a pioneer title with a unrivaled storytelling? NoIs the game play flawless? NoWhat you will get, is a story with a lot of story depth and very likable characters. I found myself being invested in every character and their journey through the game. The soundtrack is fantastic, one of the best game soundtracks I have heard and placed very well to immerse you into the story. The battles in the game aren't really challenging, but that's okay, it doesn't need to be, as its a story and not a turn based strategy game.I loved this story. I will look back at this series very fondly and whenever I hear the artist Suara or any other tune from this soundtrack. I will be taken back to this world and the wonderful moments I had with this story.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: It's one story told through two games in case someone who doesn't know. You also can't play just Mask of Truth without Mask of Deception and expect to understand everything, there's no point.Mask of Deception was great, but I have to admit, I had to force myself to get through some of the more less exciting parts. Some of the dialogue felt a bit boring at times, but it wasn't any deal breaker and it wasn't that common. It's more like a fantasy slice of life than anything else for the most part which is fine, in fact, it was necessary for us to get to know and love this really fantastic cast of characters and getting attached to them. The emotional impact on the second game felt absolutely huge because of that. The comedy is pretty good, the voice acting is superb, especially Haku's. Japanese voice acting is usually great in modern games anyway, but hearing Fujiwara Keiji's (Haku's voice) performance is on another level and that's the highest praise I can give. I liked the battle system, it's pretty simple and usually you don't have to think too hard, but you can still mess up and your units die pretty easily if you're not paying enough attention. The game ends with a cliffhanger which the second game picks up right after.The following can be said about both Mask of Decelption and Mask of Truth, there were some music I really disliked, but there are a lot more that I absolutely loved, they were outright beautiful and filled with emotion, so overall I was more than pleased. But what I wasn't pleased with was how it's a 720p/30 fps port. The game came out in 2020 and this is absolutely unacceptable. While it doesn't hinder the experience, this kind of lazy port is a big no-no.If you like VNs and don't mind some turn based strategy battle system, this one's a must buy, especially if you can get it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: Good series. I recommend buying all of them if you like this one or any of the others. They're worth the money.Pros:-Interesting characters, a big variety with each feeling quite different than the other. -The story is an emotional trip, made me laugh, cry, and get angry.-The tactics rpg game play was fun. It changes a bit each game but still stays entertaining. Harder to make characters OP in MOD and MOT. -Music is good of course. I mean it says it in the tags.-Mask of Truth continues the story. -Its a harem VN but also not a harem VN.Cons:-This one is a bit short. Beating it in only 30 hours.-Mask of truth continues the story. Needing to buy another game to continue something I obviously want to finish. [if they had a part 3 i'd buy it too]-Cliche anime stuff-For all the drinking of tea and sake the main dude does he never uses the toilet, completely unrealistic.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first visual novel and I'm really surprised. The world building is really good. The characters are memorable and easy to like (except for Nekone, stupid kid). This is a visual novel so don't go expecting battles all the time, it's there just to spice things up.The PC port is great. Every key is remappable and I can choose my icons whether I use keyboard or controllers. The icon options are insane, old and new xbox buttons, PS3 and PS4 buttons, keyboard. How many games much expensive do that? None in my library.I played this without playing Prelude to the Fallen due to it not being available here when I started this game. It's fine starting in this game despite what hardcore gatekeepers will say, I still loved the game and understood most part. There are a lot of media out there where the later parts were first released than the prequels. However, at time of writing, Prelude to the Fallen is available, so you can grab that first.I bought Mask of Truth immediately after finishing this, it's a must.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: As the ultimately generic Muv-Luv was a prelude to the masterpiece which was Muv-Luv: Alternative as is the Mask of deception in relation to the Mask of truth.Plotwise there is a lot of things Mask of Deception could be accused of but once you'll get to the sequel, you'll see most of them are justified in a very skillfully handled way.Suga Munemitsu like a chess player setting up a piece after piece preparing for the grand finale of the series. Slowly and steadily introduces the player to the world of Utawarerumono once again with almost overwhelming amount of lore illustrated by an enormous glossary, beautiful art style and top notch voice acting.Playing the predecessor from 2002 isn't necessary but I highly recommend it merely for the sake of full clarity of the story and appreciation of how well the author maneuvers our characters of old.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game, with some lovely world building and a gripping plot! Some people might be turned off by the abundance of slice-of-life segments between the main plot. _childDocuments_.review: Whilst I'm no fan of censorship, it is the story, visuals and music that make this series the best visual novel/anime series ever in my opinion. _childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: Very good VN game. If you like anime and deep mystery stories this is a very good choice to pick to play when you want to just chill and enjoy a story. The game doesn't have much real gameplay as there is some turn based RPG style combat situations, but they are less than 20% of the story. As writing this review the first part "Prelude to Fallen", which is a prequel to this story hasn't been released in steam yet, but you can pick this as your starting game for this amazing story. "Mask of Truth" will be the last part and will finish this story that you start here.9/10 points from me and I only take 1 point off as I would have preferred little bit more combat and for the story to not be so linear. Amazing game.ps. There is anime series for this too, so you might want to check that out. Do recommend playing the game first so you get the full enjoyment of learning the story.

_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: Something to be aware of, Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception is a VN first and foremost, and RPG-style battles are sparse and between. While game is rather long, it has only 17 + 16 battles (all battles can be replayed). All characters, including protagonist, are voiced.Storywise it's an adventure, taking place some time after first Utawarerumono game, but featuring different place and characters, so knowledge of prequel isn't really required to understand it. Main character is Haku, man with no memories of his past, or even world surrounding him. Rescued by traveller Kuon, has no choice but to tag along with her. One thing leads to another, and innitial search just for work and place to live, gets them involved in political intrigues, wars, and past best forgotten.Visually game is just lovely. Like in predecessor, CGs and character sprites are amazing quality. During battles (and some cutscenes) characters use 3D models, and while not everyone may appreciate "big head" JRPG style models, their details, design and animations are sure eye catching. Game is locked at 30 fps, but it's not a big deal IMO in a VN / turn based game. Small screen tearing may happen when watching pre-animated movies, for reasons I cannot exaplain. Battle system has been fleshed out compared to first game, it's not very complex, but perfectly functional. All mechanics are pretty well explained in lore/tutorial log, and I recommend to use it. While game seem at first to use RNG elements, that's not really the case: "random" factors (use of specials, bonus moves) seem to be predefined at start of battle, so rewinding battle will not change results.small advice: if you can't find BP menu in usual place after completing game, press esc while in battle preparation screen.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: A great strategy RPG/Kinetic novel trilogy, probably the best made so far. Unfortunately Mask of Deception is the weakest of the three games, in story terms it really is just a lead up to the next game, Mask of Truth. All the seeds of the story of MoT are sown in this game, but Mask of Deception suffers from a lack of pacing, being very slow with a great amount of slice of life skits, character exploration/development and world building, but very little actual story development until the last act. I would recommend this game to anyone who enjoys the Japanese style of storytelling, it lacks the usual cop-outs (anime character archetypes) which usually comes with this, and it tells a great story in an interesting archeotech world. The game element is good, being a strategy rpg similar in concept to final fantasy tactics or fire emblem.If you like this game definitely get Mask of Truth, but first go back and play the original Utawarerumono from 2002. Yes it's still good, and you will thank me when you realise you are getting the whole story.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: Story: 9/10Music: 8/10Gameplay: 7/10Completion time: 35 hoursSelected difficulty: Hard You can see this as a traditional JRPG with turn-based combat similar to Fire Emblem, focused more on the story than on combat or gameplay.Great story and 'okay' balanced combat mechanics - UI might be a bit clunky on mouse and keyboard, so I suggest using a controller for this. In gameplay, strategy plays a large role as you will often notice your units being outleveled by your enemies. However, it is possible to beat the game without having to grind Free Battle, or replaying the battles multiple times (You retain EXP and Level even if you fail and restart), and the game is quite forgiving providing these features. That way, even less experienced players in RPGs won't get stuck on any one stage for too long. Despite all of this, again I must emphasize that the combat only secondary to the story, and their story is pretty damn good. I'd certainly give it my recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception

_childDocuments_.review: This game is 90% VN and only 10% RPG so keep that in mind before you buy this. The story is pretty slow at the start of the game but after you manage to get through around 2-3 hours it actually become much better. Easy way to see if the story is interest or not, you can check out the anime adaptation which did a decent job in my opinion. The RPG part is also decent not any special and not that hard (the sequel did improve on this part) since I beat the game without a single grind in free battle. But you will still have fun with it if you are fan of game like final fantasy tatic or fire emblem.

_childDocuments_.review:
Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception is a grand tale that will enchant the hearts and minds of players as it takes them on an incredible journey. With a beautiful visual novel story experience, intriguing characters, fast-paced SRPG combat, world-class soundtrack, and more, the game is the perfect escape for adventure gamers!

Mask of Deception begins atop a snowy mountain where the protagonist awakens in an unfamiliar wilderness, surrounded by deadly creatures, with nothing but a hospital gown and a splitting headache. However, hes rescued by a beautiful girl named Kuon, who sports both adorable animal ears and a beastlike tail. Finding that the hapless man has no memory of anything, Kuon decides to take the amnesiac into her care, naming him Haku. As their journey takes them across the land, Haku will encounter colorful characters, build deep relationships, battle ruthless enemies, and find himself inexorably dragged into the political machinations of the mighty nation of Yamato.

name: Tesla Force
detailed_description: The Tesla Force Difference When compared to the previous game Tesla vs Lovecraft, in Tesla Force , the gameplay transcends the limits of the arena. You will have meaningful choices both inside and outside the arena, beyond simply acquiring upgrades. You can choose your path to travel, along with the challenges and rewards that come with it. You can risk it by challenging the Elite Monsters for Rare Perks , or you can play it safe and settle for lesser rewards. About the Game The cosmic horrors are awakening. It's time to call upon the heroes of science and eldritch knowledge to defend mankind from an assault from the outer reaches of reality! Endlessly replayable rogue-lite Randomly generated levels Wild array of devastating weapons Intense top-down shooting action Large selection of perks to customize your hero Over a dozen unique abominations to destroy Play as Tesla, Curie, Lovecraft or Shelley! Choose from four brilliant heroes of esoteric knowledge: Tesla, Lovecraft, Curie or Shelley! short_description: With science as your super power, charge up your coils and zap into action! Tesla Force is a rogue-lite top-down shooter featuring endless procedural gameplay with tentacle splitting action. Play as Tesla, Curie, Lovecraft and Shelley and blast the cosmic horror back into the galactic abyss!

_childDocuments_.review: "." - Marie CurieTesla Force is a gloriously over the top, roguelite twin stick shooter and a tale of Nikola Tesla inadvertently opening a portal at the Wardenclyffe Tower and awakening the cosmic horrors while trying to provide free energy, wireless transmissions and a life of leisure to everyone. In 1916.Let me just continue with that bonkers story for a second. Before everything goes Cthulhu, a young Marie Curie pops out of a second portal in an almost Ghostbusters uniform and yells at Tesla he kind of goofed. Tesla stoically accepts that, picks up a shotgun and one of his inventions and proceeds mowing down cosmic monstrosities and closing down portals in a tutorial mission that ends with him flying off in a mech. Now if that doesn't sound like electric currents of fun and escapism at its finest, I don't know what does.After the tutorial, the game immediately throws you into the first chapter and to the map of Miskatonic county, the New England setting used by Lovecraft in many of his stories. You can choose missions here and you will have two at the beginning. Your first run will probably end quickly as a light brunch for one of the many swarms of otherworldly horrors trying to hug you. When you die, you'll spawn at the Wardenclyffe Tower and be greeted by Miss Curie again. You'll be introduced to the Doomsday Clock mechanic which ticks down whenever you're on a mission. When it ticks a full circle, Cthulhu performs a dark ritual and grants the horrors worldwide a perk and makes them stronger.This is when the procedurally generated missions kick in. There aren't a ton of map variations and missions, but there's a sufficient amount that it doesn't get stale while you close down rifts, survey hives, fix machinery, collect crystals and batteries and employ a multitude of weapons and high tech gadgetry against the cosmic horrors stalking your every move. You can't see the rewards you get after every successful mission until you upgrade the relevant ability, but you can gain a perk, a weapon or something mysterious, represented by a question mark. You’ll also sometimes get missions on a run, like killing a certain amount of enemies, rewarding extra crystals if you finish them.Whenever you fail, you'll respawn at the Tower. Experience gained and crystals collected in the run stay with you, everything else is lost. Experience unlocks upgrades, perks and abilities which you can then purchase with collected crystals and further upgrade. You can unlock weapons which you can then choose when starting a new run, research permanent upgrades, unlock 5 perk slots that you can pick and change every run and purchase starting abilities for each run. Upgraded weapons drop during runs and this is a bit of a grumble since weapons are not equally useful and it's very luck based what you will get and consequently how you'll fare on a run. It's not a big annoyance though, as runs go quickly.Combat is fast, fluid, flashy and the shooting is satisfying. Your dodge ability is a teleporter backpack. Drops from horrors include the standard health kits, weapons and their already mentioned upgraded variants, abilities, short lasting weapon buffs, including nukes, that greatly increase your speed of tentacle removal, crystals for upgrades and energy cells. Parts for your mech also randomly spawn and when you collect enough you get the ability to summon a giant robot for a limited time that makes sushi out of everything that even dares to wave something slimy at you.The game is divided into 3 chapters and each is played as a separate run, making things a bit easier. There’s a boss at the end of each run and those fights are really bombastic and fun. You can replay chapters from the beginning and all the missions will be immediately visible on the map if you restart.There are 4 playable characters. Nikola Tesla, Marie Curie, Mary Shelley and H.P. Lovecraft. A true genius level, nobel prize winning, science fiction pioneering, misanthropic force. Tesla and Curie are unlocked at the start, the other two have quests that you need to finish to unlock them. Each of them has slightly different stats and abilities, e.g. Curie can dual wield small weapons and Tesla can use energy cells to recharge abilities.Now that it’s out of Early Access, it’s polished, gleefully fun, has a good amount of replayability and a solid amount of upgrades and things to purchase. It may sometimes seem that the grind is a bit too much, but considering how short runs usually are, it’s a perfect break game. It even includes new game+ cycles.Folks at 10tons Ltd really know their twin stick shooting. As this is a spin off from 2018’s Tesla vs. Lovecraft some may complain that it’s the same game or a large expansion pack, but this one stands on it’s own and the asking price is fair. As Miss Curie would say, “Eat Science, fishsticks!”: 17 achievements, some tricky ones, like the Lucky Number and Untouchable, but permanent upgrades and good perk combinations solve everything. 100% completion is very skill based, should be ~15-20 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Tesla Force

_childDocuments_.review: Upfront, I really love 10tons for their minimalistic, crisp, short-leveled action twin-stick-shooter-games with high variability and extremely addictive flavor (if you’re German, I’d call them “kurz und knackig”). Actually 100%ed nearly every title from them until now. But Tesla Force, oh man, it really pains me to say this, but this is a step back. Don’t get me wrong, I don’t want to say that the game is bad, but it’s just kind of a roguelite spin-off to Tesla vs. Lovecraft. It’s got exactly the same mechanisms and gameplay, the only differences are 4 characters (2 of them are pretty useless), and instead of lots of designed levels, this time we only get 3 ‘segments’ with procedurally generated sub-levels with varying objectives (only 4 or 5). Therefore all in all the game is much, much shorter. There’s even no reason to master several cycles of these segments, because it actually doesn’t change anything, not even giving you additional cutscenes. And you can get all achievements in the first cycle as well.Final verdict, if you like 10tons and like Tesla vs. Lovecraft, go for it, because it’s at least 5 hours of additional fun, especially in coop mode. But only on a really heavy discount, because, as I said, the game is much shorter than the original. Nevertheless I’ll still give this a thumbs up, just because I love 10tons so much, but please, guys, put some more effort into your future games.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine someone took  (which is an  game) and slapped together a user mod to turn it into a roguelike. But never polished it and actually broke half the existing things in the process. You get to see a ton of the reused content but it all somehow feels worse.The game isn't completely awful, but it's semi-broken and simply much, much worse than Tesla vs Lovecraft. Skip this and buy the original game instead.- The map is a total mess. , can you comprehend where I am or which paths I can follow?- Perk rewards for completing levels can be white, blue, or green, and I still don't know the difference- I don't understand how "quests" are given. Are these daily like in TvL or what?- I still don't fully understand what batteries can do or how much I should care- The permanent upgrade for "+5% chance of finding loot" doesn't explain what "loot" is, does this spawn more permanent money or just more abilities etc?- Teleporting over items no longer picks them up. If you played TvL you know this is a big deal- Teleporting through enemies does not deal damage unless you have a perk for just that- Awful writing. A character you've never heard of says you must save the world before it's all gone, to which Tesla says "that sounds bad, I should go then". I'm not exaggerating- No voice acting (only subtitle text) makes garbage cutscenes. Of course it's not a story-driven game but they went for the story and implemented it this badly- One of the enemy types tends to get stuck in the open. It did work fine in TvL, too- Weapon balance seems to fly out the window when you find Jacob's Stick which is fast, strong, fully piercing, and auto-aiming- Super slow progression. You used to get a new perk every dozen seconds or so in TvL. Now you get one every several completed levels. This sucks- Perks are too weak. TvL perks could change the game dramatically (not even mentioning the rare "Epic" perks!), but these are all "+10% damage" kind- Two starting characters play the same. Unlocking the third one is far too tedious. And the fourth one I have no idea how to even unlock- Ironically having actual objectives beyond "shoot everything and survive" made things much more repetitive- You never have to clear the level, you just complete the same objectives over and over and get out, shooting some monsters on your path. Zzzzz- Tiny UI icons. I up-scaled the UI in the options but doing so makes the .- Actually at max UI scale you cannot even close the menu by clicking X at the top because it's off-screen now. WTF I just want my ability indicator bigger- When you pick up an ability you drop your current one - even if it had 0 charges left!! - and it will look identical to any fully-charged ability- If time is slowed down and you leave the mission, the whole escape animation still plays in slow-mo... painfully slowly- When you leave the mission the map zooms out to show you the whole level with pitch black background to destroy all the immersion being in a world of a sort- When tasked to destroy the statues, the first one often gets destroyed on accident because it spawns under you while you're still in mech- I could go on and on about small things but I think I wrote enough tbh

Tesla Force :/Buy Tesla vs. Lovecraft though.It's really good.Cheaper too.Doesn't feel like a shell of a game.And actually endlessly replayable.

_childDocuments_.review: Tesla Force is a rogue-lite twin-stick shooter. It is playable solo and in co-op sessions with up to 4 players. You are also able to use steam's Remote Play Together feature - allowing you to play online with friends. They don't need to buy the game that way!The story isn't really important here but it's atmospheric. The cutscenes in combination with the music and overall feeling are great. You move your character with the left stick and aim with the right stick. Shoot with RT and that's it. You'll have a special ability later in the game, can change weapons, and go into a Mech, which is a nice way to spice things up. A level takes max. a few minutes to complete. This means a run doesn't take much longer than 30 minutes. Levels are procedurally generated. While that may be true, I wouldn't have noticed. After a few runs, you'll run into the same looking levels over and over again. Yeah, maybe a few objects are different but you won't notice. The enemies and objectives are different enough though. You also have many different weapons, abilities, perks, and more. There is a lot of content right now. Two characters are available from the start, the other two will be unlocked later. Talking about that, it is a roguelite game after all. You will need to start over and over and over again to collect crystals that allow you to unlock new (starting) perks, weapons, and more. Playing in co-op makes the game more fun. Like I said, with the RPT feature you don't need to buy more than one copy and your friends can just join without even installing the game. The latency is good enough. It worked perfectly fine in Tesla Force. Usually, the run is over if you die. If someone in co-op dies, you can revive them later. It's a nice game for in-between. It's also a pretty good mindless second-screen game but I couldn't resist listening to the music of the game and getting into this atmospheric world. Even for casuals who aren't fans of the genre, this can be a fun game. Thanks to the roguelite aspect and fast-paced gameplay, you'll fastly be in a mindset of "just one more run" and "in the next run I'll beat the boss".It's a good game for casuals, for in-between fun, and especially for people who want to play something in co-op during these hard times. The base price of 15 USD/€ is justified enough. Die-hard fans of the genre should wait for a sale since this doesn't bring something really new to the table.
_childDocuments_.name: Tesla Force

_childDocuments_.review: The twin stick shooting is solid (of course, 10tons perfected that ages ago) but right now all the other aspects of the game need a lot of work and polish. The roguelite elements are very bare and lacking, balance is all over the place, and the game is exceptionally easy. Maybe wait on this, it's got some work to go.Edit: Forgot to mention, my playtime is only around 4 hours (I fell asleep with the game running ), and I have unlocked all the content and beaten the game at the highest available difficulty. I am fairly certain 10tons is working on more content, but right now this game is very short and there's not much to do. Will update this review as the game is updated.UPDATE: UPDATE. The game has had it's 1.0 release. Not much has been changed. There's 2 new characters, but they play 95% the same as the main character. Still hardly any content, and you can still waltz through the entire game on the hardest difficulty without hardly any issue. would say this one is a hard pass.

_childDocuments_.review: I received this as part of the Humble Bundle Monthly subscription. I paid for the previous game early on and felt it was worth the money. For the cost of this second game, I expected a lot of new content, not just a recycled version of their last game presented in an endless mode with a couple more characters. Needs more perks, more abilities and more variety to be worth what they're asking you to pay. Buy the first game instead, it feels more cohesive.The weapons are also poorly balanced. There are two or three weapons you will use because everything else is way too weak to be viable.

No surprise, not really much "to unlock" in the long term.In 4.5 hours you have all the weapons, most of the perks and suddenly ... Your runs are all the same. _childDocuments_.review: Quite a funny game. The scenario is so simple that it could be summarized in two short lines. The objectives are repetitive because there are only four of them. Throughout the game, you have only one mission: to be dropped on a map full of opponents to kill them all while completing certain objectives (defend a zone, fix a tower, collecting pieces all around the place, destroying statues). The bestiary is also very poor with a total of four or five different opponents excluding bosses. Boss fights certainly have something epicness but you'll soon reach a point where killing them is as effortless as breathing air. Once you complete the game for the first time, you unlock the game + which is essentially the same thing over and over and over again. I am actually and basically testing myself to see how far I can keep going in this. 'Tesla Force' does not even bother to propose an ending worthy of the name.Music is repetitive. I encountered major visual and graphical issues. When foes come by waves you can suffer from major FPS drops. The gameplay is paved with minor bugs here and there. You can play different characters (including Lovecraft himself) but it doesn't change the omnipresent and unavoidable repetitiveness of it all.

_childDocuments_.review: Tesla Force is a roguelite top-down shooter game.First of all, the game isn't meant to be rushed, but I did manage to get past through the entire game in 3 hours. For a game this expensive I would've expected a lot more content, Tesla vs Lovecraft (the game I would suggest to play over this one) lasting me more than double the amount of time! There are cycles and upgrades to grind the game further, but knowing it will be the same re-used content it just makes it somewhat meh.Now in general I wouldn't have given it a negative review because I hold 10tons games close to heart, but this one was a deception to me. I really thought there would be far more content and a lot less bugs (no, not the monsters). First of all, the game is extremely RNG dependant. In one run I got a BFG and annihilated any monsters on screen all the way to the boss, in my final run I was stuck with an underpowered close-range shotgun against the final boss of the game, which I got in the level right before the boss (I was stuck with an Ion pistol before that.)As for the bugs, well maybe an oversight but half the time I don't know what stuff does. Hovering your mouse over icons should give you some explanation and having to go through 'Character menu' every time is annoying. The most OBNOXIOUS bug is the teleport that randomly starts working! Perhaps this wouldn't be an issue with good RNG, but I lost an entire run right before the boss because my teleport ability randomly stopped working for an ENTIRE MINUTE. This is unforgivable in a game that ends your 20 minutes long run when you die, especially since some monsters almost 2-3 shots you with 120 HP!Ranting done, the graphics are on par with all other similar games, so nothing to say about that. The music was alright, it's definitely not on Neon Chrome's level, but it's not bad. The sound effects were OK. The gameplay in itself is fun, but the game is too short, too repetitive, feels unpolished, is buggy, unbalanced and too RNG dependant.Overall, worth playing if you get it really cheap, or just purchase Tesla vs Lovecraft instead.

The game is basically your generic twin-stick shooter game, except it has got some 'Slay the Spire' and 'Risk of Rain' mechanics thrown in together with a traditional rogue-lite twin-stick formula. Where you have 2-3 paths and once you select one, the other ones disappear. 3) Finish the map objective.4) Go back to #2 until you find a boss5) Kill BossWhy I kinda recommend this game:* The gun play is fast and fun. A full run can take ~10-12 minutes.* It runs on low powered machines (it's my way of saying this game is ugly)* There are lots of numbers! And they go up!However:- There are maybe 7 different types of enemies in the game. You mainly fight 1-2 for 80% of it- Lots of weapons but they mainly behave the same way- There are only 4 map objectives (this includes boss maps)If you don't mind simple, repetitive, mindless gameplay, in exchange of making things go boom then this game is for you. 100% Achievement in ~10 hoursI give this game 4 tentacles out of 8

_childDocuments_.review: This is kinda tough to review. In that, if you're new to the 10tons 'Tesla-verse', by all means jump in, have yourself a ball (and you will). However, if you're a "Tesla vs Lovecraft" vet (like myself), what you're looking at is an $17 expansion pack. Some new weapons, characters, and enemies. A new gameplay mode and missions. But, the same graphics, music, sound effects, and gameplay. The new stuff is all good for the most part, but none of it is essential or must have. 10tons has been accused of double (and triple) dipping before, but they've never made it this blatant. At the end of the day, I think this would have been better served as a full-priced game for newcomers, or a $7-$8 DLC expansion for owners of 'vs Lovecraft'.So I'm recommending it. ( More health, dual wielding etc)CONS: Game pace and sense of growth/ power is significantly slowed down. This is my biggest issue with the game. In TvL you would constantly be getting upgrade cards in every round by killing enemies so you always feel like something cool is being thrown at you. In this game you get 1 upgrade at the end of each level... that's it... instead of getting 5-10 upgrades a game that reset between rounds you get 1 upgrade per level completed that lasts until you die.CONCLUSION: This is Tesla vs Lovecraft with a shinier coat of paint, a few characters and new pointless elements added that slow down progression and hinder the fast paced fun of the first game. _childDocuments_.review: If there is a developer that knows how to make a twin-stick shooter, it's 10tons. Having played Crimsonland and Neon Chrome in the past, I can fairly say they've come a long way, and learned how to make rogue-lites while they were at it. Tesla Force is one of the best games of this type of I have played, let alone the best of 10tons. It's addicting, colorful, and rewarding to play, and has up to four player local/remote play coop besides.Visually set in the nebulous early 20th Century commonplace to cosmic horror, the game sees inventor Nikola Tesla, a man with vision beyond his time, activating his famous Wardenclyffe tower- only for it to open a rift for extradimensional horrors to pour into our reality. The players, as Tesla or other personages of note; Marie Curie, Mary Shelly and HP Lovecraft, must harness the destructive power of weird science and lay waste to the invaders.Tesla Force plays extremely well, with tight controls, smooth framerate even during extreme visual effects and a diverse range of weapons and perks, none of which I have used thus far feel particularly underpowered, save maybe basic starting weapons. Playing with a mouse and keyboard feels extremely natural and responsive, and the overall gamefeel, especially of enemy feedback to your attacks, is far better then Neon Chrome. One particularly nice feature is that you have a dodge ability, a teleport, which moves you in the direction of your movement, and not that of your aim- an important distinction, as I find the inverse extremely disorienting. This teleport has limited charges but they regenerate reasonably quickly and it can be upgraded through perks and unlocks. There is an onscreen indicator, a stack of chevrons, indicating both how many teleport charges you have and in what direction you will teleport. Returning from earlier 10ton titles is a health ring around your character and also a reload time indicator on your crosshair, meaning you don't necessarily have to look away from the action to your HUD, and in this game, that split-second of eye movement could make the difference.Following a brief tutorial you will arrive at Wardenclyffe Tower, a playable menu screen and your base of operations. From here you can switch your current character, activate coop play, purchase persistent upgrades using pink crystals dropped from enemies, and change which cycle of New Game + is active if you have finished a run before. Higher cycles mean meaner and more numerous enemies, but also more drops. When you're ready, you can begin a run at one of three locations. Only the city of Arkham is initially available, and completing that unlocks the Farm, and then the Caves. When I played a demo build of Tesla Force the entire game was a single run, but it's now split up into smaller runs a la Immortal Redneck. I think the game is a bit more fun this way, and it makes for quicker, tighter gameplay sessions. An additional mechanic that was not in the demo I played is the "Doomsday Clock", a running timer on your HUD that is somewhat like the difficulty timer in Risk of Rain or Kingdom Gun: Whenever the clock makes a full rotation, the enemies gain a perk, like more health, move speed or damage. Notably, finishing a stage objective does not stop the clock, only actually exiting the stage does- So you have a choice whether to farm enemies for more drops or cut your losses and immediately end a level. The Doomsday level persists between stages and only resets after a run is over.At the beginning of any stage, you'll start out in Tesla's Sparrow mech- an electrical, dual-minigun-equipped beast that reaps groups of enemies readily. However, it is only usable for a brief time barring upgrades to its duration, and taking damage will shave yet more time off that duration. However, you can use the mech again whenever you pick up its four parts in the stage. Tesla and Curie control this mech directly, while Shelly uses it as an AI-controlled ally with a brain jar bolted to the top of it. Lovecraft meanwhile foregoes the mech entirely, instead summoning a floating Aberation with a continously-damaging beam attack. To summon this creature again, he has to interact with summoning circles scattered throughout the stages.Enemies in Tesla Force are extremely numerous: Dozens on screen at one time, with more constantly spawning in as you fight. They move fast and hit hard, but thankfully most of your weapons have either a high rate of fire or wide cone of effect, or some other unique quality- The Jacob's Stick, for example, chains lightning between multiple enemies, while aptly-named BFG has a generously large splash radius. You can carry any two and more frequently drop in-game, especially if you do the "Seal the Rift" levels. Getting a multikill will drop a bonus temporary powerup, like extra shots or a smart bomb, and these powerups can send you into a vicious cycle of screen-clearing kills, obtaining more powerups, and so on. Very rarely will you kill only a single enemy at a time. Enemies drop a variety of goodies: new weapons, "energy cells" that look like batteries, crystals,  powerups, and abilities. The abilities have limited uses but you can purchase upgrades to their effectiveness and number of uses. You will also sometimes come across "shrine"-type structures that you can pay a cost in batteries, crystals or health for various benefits. These are usually worth it if you have the resources to spare.Between stages you are presented with a map of the area and a choice of stages. You can also view the current Doomsday enemy perks and your character sheet. Initially you won't be able to see the whole map of a run, until you purchase the "Radar" upgrade. At max level, you can see the entire run and can plan out your route ahead of time. A separate upgrade allows you see what a level will offer as reward- this could be a choice of new weapons or perks, with some also having a random event that presents you with a "choose-your-own-adventure" type set of options. The results of these options seem to be fixed, so you can learn their outcomes to your benefit, like interacting with the Curios in Darkest Dungeon. There are different stage types with different in-level drops, and knowing what you'll find in a level can help you plan a route. "Survey the Hive" levels offer health drops, "Destroy the Statues" yields more crystals, "Fix the Inhibitor" gives extra batteries and pauses the Doomsday Clock for a brief time, and "Seal the Rifts" results in extra weapon drops. There are also optional "Elite Monster" stages where you fight a miniboss for a large crystal payout and a guaranteed rare perk choice, and the required final boss fight as the last stage. So far my experience has been that if you're strong enough to make it to the final boss, you're strong enough to beat it. Getting there depends on your upgrades and luck with RNG, with the balance shifting towards the former as you accrue crystals- a metagame I greatly prefer. Each character has a different interaction with the abovementioned batteries: Tesla can use them to use his ability if he's otherwise out of uses for it, Curie can use it to teleport if she's out of charges for that, Shelly uses them to regenerate her shields and Lovecraft can use them to change map routes or reroll perk choices. Of the four characters, I would say Tesla and Shelly are more generally useful, the former mostly due to being the starting character with no stat weaknesses, the latter due to her shield and AI-Controlled mech summon. Curie is inherently slower and with less health, and depends on specific weapon setups for general effectiveness- she is able to dual wield pistols. Lovecraft's benefits are primarily metagame based, though he has the advantage of his floating critter being able to cross gaps, which is especially useful in the Caves region.Tesla Force is extremely fun and I highly recommend it to any arcade shooter or roguelite fan.

_childDocuments_.review: This is kinda a remix of the Tesla vs Lovecraft, it re-uses a lot of the assets, but significantly changes the metagame. Instead of a chain of arenas with resetting progress, you get a repetitive RNG roguelite, where you get skills between the arenas. There are only several types of tasks you perform on the arenas, and the variety of maps is small. So as usual for 10tons roguelites the beginning is really dull. Only when you grind and unlock some new weapons and skills it starts to be fun.So, this time there are four playable heroes, and they are very distinct in their playstyle. A bunch of new guns and skills were added, and you can save currency and buy some stuff before starting the run. It allows for powerful builds accomodating your chosen character, therefore reducing the RNG nonsense. Well, and i did never get a lot of end-game guns randomly, i had to buy them to try them out. And the costs are really high. After finishing the game i saw only like half of the stuff. On the new game+4 i still did never touch last tier guns, or the mysterious tier guns, which costs a ton of currency and people say you can't unlock it anyway. I never saw two of the usables too. Oh, and they are almost useless now, because usable abilities do not recharge nor auto-unequip after you've spent them. The only point if you are making an ability-centric build with a character that can spend batteries (another currency) to have more charges. Switching them manually is more of a chore for the other three characters, and they are rarely powerful enough. You can encounter exchange shrines on the arena to transfer one currency into another or health. And you can accidentally destroy one type of the shrines, but none of the others. That would be an interesting universal mechanic, but also a punishing one, since in the endgame you cover the whole screen with projectiles. Maybe it's just a bug that one type can be destroyed.Tesla vs Lovecraft is a great game even after they've nerfed all the fun parts to death. This one is just good, and only if you force yourself through the dull slow rogue-lite beginning. It's just like Neon Chrome in this aspect.All achievements are working, but a couple of them are really pointlessly grindy.

_childDocuments_.review: I initialy gave a negative review during beta testing. I am pleased to say the  latest releases turned me from sceptical into a more enthusiastic player and re-edit significantly my initial review. Out of the issues/ dev choices I still find while playing:Campaign progression:Splitting the campaign in chapters is okay but why the hell did the devs resets weaponry and perks while starting a new chapter ???Not only there is no storyline to back up  such balancing, but also it simply kills any sense of achievement and progression into the campaign. I can hardly think of any shooter having made this kind of call and for good reason:  Once you killed a boss, your reward is to keep going....naked. Meh ! Out of the ongoing issues I had since the release:UI: --PerksArt direction is schizophrenic and harbour a steampunk art and iconography on most department except character perks. Perks icons are coming straight out of an over colourful and cartoony 7+ kid game. Tesla vs Lovecraft was way more coherent in that respect. Gameplay -You cannot teleport through short crevasses, even though distance separating both sides of the rift are much shorter than your teleport jump.-Mecha teleport is a mess and does not allow you to cross a passage you would not be able to walk into, even if the narrow passage is much shorter than your teleport jump.-No logical explanation either to define when or why you fire one weapon instead of the other, neither when it is going to switch.  -To this date the “chtonian bestiary” has not much expanded and it seems fair to assess that 90% of the 3D game assets  are identical to Tesla vs Lovecraft.IF Tesla Force is as thoroughly maintained and rebalanced in the future than Tesla vs Lovecraft, I have no doubt it will keep growing on me, and outlive its predessessor in my library.

_childDocuments_.review: A very repetitive game that is nevertheless good chaotic fun in small doses.The game consists of three chapters. WIthin each chapter, you have to progress through several missions that consist of a single objective each. At the end of the chapter, you fight a boss. The game purports to have 'endless replayability' and random level generation, but none of this is meaningful - there are only 4 or 5 different mission types, and the random level generation consists of assets placed in slightly different patterns around each small arena. As a result, one playthrough and you'll have seen everything the game has to offer multiple times over.There are upgrades both within each chapter, that you buy with batteries, and overall, that you buy with crystals. The drop rate for these batteries and crystals is not great at the start, until you upgrade the passive bonus that increases drop rate. Thus the starting grind is very slow, and you'll need ever increasing numbers of crystals to get the upgrades you want.All of that said - the game is still really fun. Once the drop rate is maxed, monsters will constantly be dropping bonuses ranging from frost bullets to multiple barrels to increased fire rate. It's entirely possible to saturate the entire screen with your bullets. With extra teleports you'll be zooming around the screen dodging monsters while completing your objectives. This is really fun gameplay and it's just a pity the rest of it is slightly substandard.You certainly won't be playing this for hours on end, but a quick 20min chapter every now and again might be good fun. Get this on sale or in a bundle.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit 2:After playing the game in its final state, I can no longer recommend Tesla Force. I feel rather disappointed at the final state of the game, and I believe it is significantly inferior to Tesla vs Lovecraft in terms of enjoyment and mechanics. This comes down to the lack of actual balance in the game. For example, in this game, there are several types of levels, one of which is Closing the Aether Rifts. This type of level was the hardest in the initial version of the game; rather than balancing it, the developers simply nerfed it so hard it is now the easier kind of level. That is roughly demonstrative, across the board, of how balance was applied to Tesla Force. I can understand why, because while Tesla Force was in early access the developers had another game release (Dysmantle) that performed substantially better - so I can't say that the lack of concern for Tesla Force is surprising, but that doesn't mean I like it. Edit 1:This is my first revision of my Tesla Force review after beating the game on the default difficulty. My biggest criticism is the fact that how good of a run you are going to have is very, very luck-based. The first half dozen games I died without making it to the first boss. The game where I finally completed a run, I got a bit of good luck with perks, beat the first boss, and then pretty much creamed everything with ease until I got to the Final BossMy main problem with this game is the lack of balance. In Tesla vs Lovecraft, the lack of balance was fine, because all of the perks and weapons only lasted for the usually under 3 minute level you were currently playing. In Tesla Force, the complete lack of balance between perks and guns is a bit of an issue. I kept a level 2 gun until a level 6 version of the same gun dropped. I kept the level 6 gun until its damage was too low and I had to pick up a level 10 version. I kept the weapons so long because the type of weapon was far more important than the level. Some of the perks are so much better its not funny. Crystal Healing FTW, take that science, crystal healing works the best! Its better than regeneration! (most of the time)This game IS in Early Access so I'll keep it recommended, but there are a few things that would HAVE to change for me to keep my recommendation once it gets a full release: 1) A bit more story to the campaign. As it is there's no story, even for a 10tons game. 2) A bit of a longer campaign. I was kinda sad when the game ended, as it is. 3) A bit more balance so that there's something between "You don't get gud enuf perks and git rekt" and "You get great perks and go around slaying all the monsters  like you're Darth Vader and they're alliance soldiers." On that note, I find it strange that people are complaining that Tesla Force is easy. I wouldn't say that's quite it. I'd say that its more accurate to say that any successful run is likely to feel easy, because you die quickly unless you get the right perks. But if you don't get the right perks, I'd honestly say that this is probably the hardest 10tons game there is.Original Review:Have been waiting for this game since it was originally scheduled to come out. So far... Compared to other 10tons games:1) Compared to the 'prequel' to this game, Tesla vs Lovecraft, its quite different. In each level of Tesla vs Lovecraft, you level up get perks and pick up weapons, and you lose those at the end of the level. You also have some permanent upgrades you can buy between levels. 2) The second game that Tesla Force seems to take inspiration from is Neon Chrome, in the sense that its a roguelite and when you die, you start at the beginning, losing most of the upgrades you've earned. (However, in Neon Chrome every few levels there was a "save level" you could choose to start from on a new run.) However, Tesla Force doesn't seem to offer as many upgrade options as Neon Chrome, and many of the upgrade options for Tesla Force seem to be non-permanent. (IE, you can buy perks at the beginning of a run, but they only last for a run, similar to the perks you pick up between levels). It also seems like (for those of you who played the alpha release during the summer a few months ago) that 10tons has altered the difficulty of some of the mission types so that some of the mission types aren't much, much harder than others, as they were during the alpha. Which is nice. Overall I'd recommend Tesla Force, though currently I'd probably recommend you try out Tesla vs Lovecraft and Neon Chrome as well, and I think I liked them a bit better. But 10tons is really good at making twin stick shooters, you should collect them all. ;)

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love 10tons topdown shooter games, and been playing them since first, old Crimsonland.I was initially - slightly confused with Tesla Force because I played a lot of Tesla Vs. Lovecraft (on PS4) - but reviews helped, so I'm leaving one as well.I thought this was sort of a DLC, or an expansion - it is not, it is sort of a "reimagination".In Tesla Vs. Lovecraft, you go from level to level, and you fight always starting from scratch, looting abilities and weapons only for that one level - with few perma upgrades.This game, on the other hand, takes the concept and turns it into a roguelike!As the dev's table very nicely explain, there's procgen, you get to keep the weapons, you keep the perks, you keep the abilities. You have perma-upgrades, you collect cells so you can use them depending on your character - Tesla uses cells to activate abilities beyond their normal charge allowance, Ms. Curie uses them to teleport, when teleport is out of charges, and so on.I played for one hour, and I finished the Arkham - you may think this is short, but there are (for now, devs keep working on it) 3 different regions, and there's NG+.All in all, this game is absolutely _awesome_, even if it reuses a lot of concepts and content from Tesla Vs. Lovecraft.I never thought it would be possible to create two different games using same assets, and have them both be very playable and fun - but here's the proof!If you love top down shooters, buy it even if you own and have played Tesla Vs. Lovecraft. You won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: Tesla Force is a console ported 2D top down twin stick shooter and a sequel to the mobile app, Tesla vs Lovecraft.  This looks and feels like a copy+paste of the original game, very little seems to have changed (5 new weapons, apparently). The game looks fairly well polished for a copy+paste of a mobile app, but the console peasant nature of the game is overwhelming.  Twin stick shooters don't do well on Steam for obvious reasons... this is PC, not a console peasant gaming appliance.   That aside, it's still worth mentioning the visuals aren't the let down here, it's the boring console tier gameplay. The developer was unable to come up with decent level design or game/story flow/plot, so they opted to try to use samey repetitive procgen as a substitute for adding content to the game.  As a result, the game doesn't actually have any content worth mentioning.  Developers must learn that procgen is not content.In some ways it's a shame to see so much effort going into the visuals and polish for such a shallow game, but I guess that's the crux of the console gaming experience, and it makes me glad to be a PC gamer.
_childDocuments_.name: Tesla Force

_childDocuments_.review: Roguelite twin stick shooter fun. If you liked the first game, you will like this one as well. This one has is more replayable. Each run is brand new with different modifiers. As you continue you unlock better guns and ability that help you get farther each run.Levels are quick burst of actions with different objectives (collect this number of things, destroy this number of shrines, ect) to add variety to the gameplay. I like how easy it is to just boot up and start playing. If you are looking for a quick short bursts of action and replayability, this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Tesla Force

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely less stressful than original Tesla vs Lovecraft, somewhat more easier after grinding a few levels. Ion Rifle and Daisy Chain gun are overpowered, making game easy, but buying perks makes it replayable somewhat.  After beating this one (cycle2 seems same and not much more challenging) going back to beat the Original Tesla vs Lovecraft. Works decently on the handheld battery!
_childDocuments_.name: Tesla Force

_childDocuments_.review: Much better than Skeletal Avenger and Undead Horde, in my view.Still uncommitted to the full rogue-lite upgrade system, but the weapons are more fun than it those games, gives the chain-lighting fun of the tesla theme.There are some persistent upgrades, but they are not as obviously required as in the two games mentioned above. Can still get grindy to get them, but you're less reliant on them (and more reliant on which perks and weapons you get on a run).Not the most inspired game, by any means, and I still prefer Neon Chrome a Jydge to this, by a country mile. Those game had a lot more variety and customization. It felt like you were trying to figure out good enough builds and overcoming specific challenges rather than just grinding to replay the same levels on higher difficulties, as 10tons seem to have been doing since then.The game wants you to replay it at higher difficulties, which I don't find very fun at all - especially given the low variety of weapons and perks. I've beaten the game once, on the first difficult, and I feel like I've seen 80% of what is has to show. At this point, it would likely get grindier than I'm comfortable with.Still, I enjoyed it during that first run. Take that as you will.
_childDocuments_.name: Tesla Force

_childDocuments_.review: Recommend with caveats.So, I played this game to completion (i.e. all "cycles"). It looks like stuff was planned to be made/added but never was: final weapon upgrade and further cycles. Though, I admit after a cycle or two the game does not offer anything new, just get through to the boss fight.At the usual price (In Europe) over over 15 Euros, it is not a good deal. Get it on sale or some bundle.
_childDocuments_.name: Tesla Force

_childDocuments_.review: The game is quite fun, with very basic mechanics and an interesting level of challenge. It forces some game replayability a bit, because in the end, it only has 3 maps. But it quickly comes to an end. After completing the game, it allows you to repeat the 3 maps, with a slight level of difficulty, and supposedly whenever you finish at that level of greater difficulty, it increases again.... It is worth it (when purchased on sale) for anyone who wants one simple game, to have a little fun, without much need to have a strategy... Total rating 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Tesla Force

_childDocuments_.review: You know? This is a Fun game, with it's Randomly generated Map, rewards from completing, it's really fun, also, there's a lot of Upgrades, Power ups, Abilities, Weapons, PerksBUT... The Number of Achievements.... is too FEW ! It's like once you get every other achievements, the game had no reason to be playthrough, I can say this game's shelftime will be like 4~6 hours of content, I am planning to get all the achievements, and perhaps even max out all the skills, perks....Getting it on a sale is good, too few achievements Sadge
_childDocuments_.name: Tesla Force

_childDocuments_.review: I've never been a big fan of endless wave shooters but given that I liked 10tons Ltd roguelite games called Neon Chrome and Skeletar avenger I was ready to give Tesla force a chance and I'm glad I did.Tesla force is quite similar as how Skeletal avenger is played and progressed, you have small arenas you clear out and then select from map which area you move to next. And if you die during the run you'll be returned to hub-area where you can gain permanent upgrades or change your player character.I'm not sure is the game too easy in my opinion after beating the game or was I just very good at this game as  stats indicate that average completion of the game takes six (6) to eight (8) hours where as I managed to beat the game little under three (3) hours without a big challenge. There is however NG+ option available so I definitely want to return to this game one day and find more challenge within it.Only real negatives I had about this game was how limited story elements are in the game and unlocking new player characters requires a very precise style run to be completed (collect XXX pieces of this material during a run), where as I would have wished that new playable character unlocks upon defeating first and second chapters.If you into roguelite games with good gameplay Tesla force is a fine pick on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Tesla Force

_childDocuments_.review: could easily play this for hours with a controller or keyboard. good enemy spawns and intuitive player interaction, nice clean ui, everything very direct. could actually do really nicely as a mobile/switch port. one bit of the bottom of one map was hard to see through and i ended up dying but that's really avoidable. much love for including one of my fave authors <3

_childDocuments_.name: Tesla Force

_childDocuments_.review: Fun twin stick shooter, a nice follow up to Tesla vs Lovecraft. Recommended if you want a solid but not ground-breaking top down shooter, especially if you want to play co-op.
_childDocuments_.name: Tesla Force

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, fast-paced top-down shooter. Many different weapons and perks. Combat is intense. Difficulty - on the easier side. The more permanent upgrades you unlock the easier it gets. They should have went the roguelite rout and allow players to upgrade only during the playthrough (from mission rewards or during combat) - this way it would be always a challenge to get to the last boss. But they went more casual way and it's ok. It's fun to be overpowered, just gets old pretty quickly.Overall it's a great game. I would have loved having much more different mission types. It's a bit too repetitive after several hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Tesla Force

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, turn-your-brain-off game. Shoot hordes. Collect random weapons and items. Spend crystals to unlock more stuff. I dig it. Really short and easy to cheese, though. I beat the entire game (all cycles) probably around 9 hours, maybe less. The other hours are from messing around with friends in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tesla Force

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, and even better if you enjoy battling Lovecraftian horror nasties. 10tons knows dual stick shooters, so the gameplay on this is excellent as expected. I like the changes over Tesla vs Lovecraft as it keeps the game moving better and is less reliant on RNG due to being able to start off with a couple perks and your weapon of choice. You also can play as someone besides Tesla, though IMO Tesla is the most powerful (almost unlimited ability use with gifted bonuses) while Shelley and HP seem pretty weak. After 20 hours I've pretty much done everything, so more creatures/levels/items/etc would help longevity. Very much enjoyed the 20 hours getting here though, and looking forward to more content or more 10tons games.
_childDocuments_.name: Tesla Force

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun but there's not a lot of content here. The game says it's left early access. However there's only 3 difficulty levels and the game is very short right now. When you beat the game on its hardest difficulty, it says that's all for the beta please check back later. Take me 8 hours to go through everything that's available so far. _childDocuments_.name: Tesla Force

_childDocuments_.review: This game has taken everything I loved about Tesla vs. Lovecraft and turned it up to 11.The change in game mechanics for the ability to buy weapons, perks, and powers to start with is amazing. _childDocuments_.name: Tesla Force

_childDocuments_.review: Ok I really like the twin stick games from this company.  I love the two cyberpunk ones that this company makes.  Each one of their games has a different personality.Ok, so here it goes.   I have a blast playing it.  The point of this game is to beat back the hordes of monsters from Cthulhu and save the world. Tesla Force is a rogue-lite top-down shooter featuring endless procedural gameplay with tentacle splitting action. name: Aliens: Dark Descent
detailed_description: In Aliens: Dark Descent , command a squad of hardened Colonial Marines to stop a terrifying Xenomorph outbreak on Planet Lethe. Lead your soldiers in real-time combat against iconic Xenomorphs, rogue operatives from the insatiable Weyland-Yutani Corporation, and a host of horrifying creatures new to the Alien franchise. You are the commander. They are your weapon. Infiltrate large open levels and annihilate enemies with your squad, dispatching orders strategically and intuitively at the touch of a button. Tread carefully, as your foes will adapt their tactics to your actions while hunting you down because death is permanent. Forge unique paths for survival, uncovering shortcuts, creating safe zones, and setting up motion trackers in a persistent world where your actions impact levels forever. Customize your squad with a selection of different classes. Level up and specialize your soldiers with unique abilities and an arsenal of weapons, armor, and perks, for high stakes missions in treacherous territory. Develop your base to research new tech and improve your squad even further. Manage your resources wisely and take calculated risks to outsmart the deadliest creature mankind has ever faced. Can you and your squad stop the outbreak before it’s too late? • Face off in a gripping original Alien story against iconic Xenomorph creatures ranging from Facehuggers to Praetorians, Alien Queens and many more, including rogue human commandos and a brand-new threat unique to this Alien storyline • Lead strategically and change squad tactics from mission to mission, carefully managing your soldiers’ health, resources, and sanity, to avoid permanent team losses and mental breakdowns • Forge unique paths for survival in a persistent world, uncovering shortcuts, creating safe zones and setting up motion trackers to stay one step ahead of these creatures • Assemble and level up squads composed of 5 starting Marines classes, with dozens of specializations, unique abilities and weapons.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really worried whatever the developers will be able to pull off such an usual project well, seeing as a tactical, isometric game is certainly not the first thing I would think about when thinking about games in Aliens franchise. And thankfully - they pretty much nailed it. It's not flawless, as the difficulty at times feels very unfair but the game is still very fun and satisfying to play.In it, you are going to be controling a squad of marines, trying to find necessary resources to evacuate from the planet before the eventual doomsday timer reaches 0. Combine this with having to worry not only about resources (that you gain between days, but also find during missions) and the squad's psychological state (which decreases the longer they spend in stressful situations and on the mission alone) and you end up with an addictive mixture, where you are consistently try to push the progress as much as possible, knowing that any mistake can set you back to the last checkpoint or safehouse, which can at times be 30 min ago. It works great... and it's a shame that when the things fall apart, especially in later areas of the game, it feels unfair, due to how the timers related to encounters work and how the logic for alien aggression progress is written.And to answer a common question with Aliens games - no, you are not going to be fighting only aliens - there are human enemies from 2 different factions. There are also some references to "engineers" but thankfully, unlike the recent awful movies - they are relatively minor. And while the new addition of one of the enemy types is a bit questionable, it is not entirely out of place knowing the events of Aliens 3.Performance is also not too bad, although prone to common UE4 shader compilation and load stutter and the visuals are solid, especially for its price, with animations in cutscenes probably being the weakest element of the whole presentation.In the end - I would easily recommend this game. Not sure if it has enough content for more than one playthrough, especially that I do not recommend playing it on any difficulty higher than Normal, due to how BS it can get with its timers. But as it is - it is already lengthy enough and - in my opinion - worth the asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: I can not recomend this game yet at it current price, with frame drops soft/hard locking eazy to do with drone welding a door closed with it being on the outside, the AI is broken as alians will spawn on top of you and objectives are quite often glitched or not spawned in at all. the spawn rates for AI are OP as you cant move for 10-15 mins as they spawn too fast in most missions.

_childDocuments_.review: It's amazing how well a tactical RTS translates the terror and tension of the Aliens setting. Before playing this game I would have never thought this genre would work. After 100%-ing it, I absolutely want more. The same way Alien: Isolation flawlessly adapted the first film, Dark Descent perfectly captures the feeling of the second.I very strongly recommend this if you're a fan of Aliens or real-time tactics games.To offer some criticisms, mainly in the form of hopes for a sequel: The XCOM style squad management could be expanded more, both in visual customization and class differentiation. I found zero use for the Tecker class that wasn't covered by the random hacker trait that any other unit could acquire. I also would really like to see repeatable short side missions that could offer more opportunities to level up your roster. Especially combat focused. Lastly, the soundtrack really was lacking. The tracks used worked fine and fit the soundscape of the film, but they do get repetitive towards the end of the game. The biggest miss in the soundtrack is not having a mission select theme and a mission victory theme, like XCOM does gloriously.A small detail I want to highlight: If your soldiers get critically injured on a mission, but survive, they can have limbs amputated and replaced with mechanical prosthetics. This is a really cool cosmetic feature that XCOM doesn't have. Sadly, it's rarely seen in my experience -- I usually either beat a mission with only minor wounds or lose the entire squad. No in between.All in all, one of the best games in a franchise full of both hits and misses. I really want to see more. Bring on Dark Descent 2!
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting and fune take on the RTS style that still scratched that X-Com itch, and felt like I was in the movie. Only real drawback is replayability. I'm okay with the same major plot points being hard-wired (again, a la X-Com) but with no mission progression change or map variations, I think I'll have to wait till I forget the story/maps/missions in a year or so to make the New Game+ worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Overall great game with nice graphics and interesting mechanics but i sent for refund due to random autosave system, you cannot save manually. If this would be better system you can setup frequency or if this would be smarter with picking up milestones it would be fine but for example you will have some cutscene, then bit of tutorial and you need to do something. if you mess up then it loads before cutscene and tutorial. Yes you can skip cut scene but not tutorial. After few times it gets really tedious and could be easily avoided by saving after cutscene. Also you have no indication of when it was saved apart from going to load menu and checking there. So if you dont have limitless time only hour here and there you are buggered. Turned game off right after completing objective (hey, it seems like logical point of doing autosave), when i loaded it back afterwards i lost about 20 minutes of gameplay and that was on easy with frequent saves. Sorry devs, if you like being little gaming edgelords that is perfectly fine but give option to skip all that nonsense to players that would love to play this game but do not enjoy playing same way as you do. And don't come up with stories of "stress and tension", i have enough on this at work. Games are for me to relax.

_childDocuments_.review: First game since AvP that gave the feeling of the Aliens Universe, that gave you that creepy nervous feeling while playing.Is the story insanely original? No, but it's good enough that it's not an issue.The graphics are acceptable, good enough that it doesn't pull you out of feeling like you're in the Aliens universe.The sound is great, instantly took me back to Aliens (2), voices are so so but again acceptable.The combat feeling is reminiscent of a hybrid of X-Com and a RTS, I happened to love the X-Com franchise so I mean this in the best possible way.I've played this for 3 days and already accumulated 34 hours, finishing the game, and would most definitely recommend this for anyone who misses either X-Com or the Aliens universe.

_childDocuments_.review: 5/5 starsThis game is a hidden gem. It has been a long time since I played a game with such good gameplay and most importantly, such good and amazing storyline. _childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game, two full play though's and a little playing around in between. _childDocuments_.review: This was surprisingly good. I played about 2 weeks after launch and did not encounter a single crash or bug at that point. Solid graphics, decent story, decent main character voice work. It's squad RTS with a pause. It will take satisfyingly long to upgrade soldiers, weapons, etc, and you'll never really feel overpowered as the hive is relentless.I feel like they captured the feel of the universe quite well with just a couple exceptions, which are mostly sound related. The guns and aliens all sound as they should, but there are little things like as you're sneaking around levels your Marines are still barking orders at full Marine volume which takes you out of the sneaking experience obviously. Also, for whatever reason they didn't use the movie sounds for the powerloaders, cryosleep chambers, and APC. That's a weird choice as surely they had license to do so and those are immediately recognizable sounds so it's weird and noticeable that they're different in game.Also, the camera is in desperate need of the ability to change the pitch. You can zoom in and out, but the angle you're looking at things is more or less always the same and I'd like to see a bit farther in front of me. Hopefully someone will mod that in at some point.Those rather small things aside though, it was quite a fun game, definitely has a number of tense moments and I feel pretty confident that I'll play through it again in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best alien game in 3rd person. Story is great, difficulty medium is challenging. Dont run, walk in most scenarios and get yourself a recon sniper cause its useful as hell. Cons are there are some bugs sometimes uncommonly where character get stucked and not moving.  And you cant do anything but loadback.
