_childDocuments_.review: the fact you can't control your marines individually completely ruins the experience. line of sight is a crucial aspect of the game and there's always one that gets tagged because the dumb mofo is not hiding like you want it. you want to bring in your sniper, but you have to select the entire group so you expose everyone to enemies sight and tigger the 'alarm'.speaking of alarm, if it rings you trigger a progress bar for X amount of time. it is however possible to chain the alarm by triggering the alarm again from stragglers filling up the progress bar and there's nothing you can do about it.id mention the bugs but i suppose they got fixed after i stopped caring.

_childDocuments_.review: The one game in the Alien franchise least likely to give you a fear induced aneurysm or make you soil your pants. (Disclaimer: Least likely does NOT indicate 0% chance. It's still the Alien franchise.)Okay, introductionary joke done, down to the nitty gritty: this game is a pretty damn good stealth based small unit strategy, with an eye on picking your approach and battles and managing your ressources. Your squads health and sanity are ressources. I'd say it runs well, is challenging but not completely unfair - the moments where the game decides to spawn a drone from the hive entrance you are currently passing by can be a bit nerve wracking, but mostly, if you play it smart, you got a good chance at victory. Knowing when to pack it in and run away to try another day is also part of that.The story fits the universe, the visuals are on point, the Aliens are bastard coated bastards with bastard filling, your marines run out of ammo, sanity and health just before you make a fatal missclick, and you are going to sometimes just need a break. But it is good.Also, big one, there is no manual saving, apart from deliberately creating a shelter and resting, since that triggers the autosave, so, save scumming, while possible, is a bit harder. The autosave in general however is pretty decent, once you know the limitations and how to manage your squads ressources.I enjoyed it, even though sometimes I wished I could have deployed more marines or given some of them specific tasks, but then again, that would have circumvented parts of the story, even though you can see some of the twists coming from lightyears away.Anyway, Weyland-Yutani, building better worlds, inquire about our job openings.I liked this game, quite a bit, I can't play its First Person cousins at all, I like the Alien franchise, I hate the Alien franchise (in the good way).
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting. A bit "sudden death syndrome" in places. But ... it's got a string. Plays out a sensible narrative of a team of colonial marines encountering the aliens, with tough choices about equipment and skills. Really feels like you're trying to stretch what you've got.Same with your crew. Every deployment allows more time for the aliens to build up. So make the most of them. But ... you wear your guys out with longer deployments. They'll get injured. If badly, can you carry them back? They'll pick up new psychological scars too. They'll just get *tired*. How much equipment do you send them into the field with? They can collect more... They can make shelters in the colony to recover...Park the ARC up and let the big guns do the talking. At least that gives breathing room.What is the cost? Every individual choice seems that it costs something. In that sense reminds me of "state of decay".
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: As a die-hard fan of the Alien franchise, and Aliens being my all-time favorite movie, this game is fantastic! It has all the feel of a proper Aliens shooter game, but the xenomorphs are actually scary (even the base-level drones) and not just bullet sponges. A mix of a stealth survival horror and RTS, this game feels like a fresh revival of the Alien franchise! I would put it right up there with Alien: Isolation and Aliens Fire Team! Personal Rating: 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:Aliens: Dark Descent 8.5/10"The best Aliens game since Aliens: Isolation, different genre, but a bastion to what Aliens games can be.""An XCOMlite without all the annoying bits of XCOM (such as the infamous 99% shot chance resulting in a miss)"Thoughts:If you like Tactical based games like XCOM, but want the additional challenge of it all playing out in real time, I would recommend this game wholeheartedly.An amazing installment to the Alien Universe, and one we definitely needed as it has been 9 years since we had a good one.Playtime varies with your own meticulousness or difficulty setting, so I'd say it is probably about 20 hours of gametime if you just shoot for the end on medium. But it can take a lot more with the aforementioned variants.Long Review: **Pros:*Ambiance & Sound Effects -Not much to say but they were good. The Aliens sounded like Aliens, the guns sounded very much like in Universe, and great sounds for the vehicles and their weaponry too.The one thing I can say stood out is the "detection" tune, its very suspenseful which is good, you hear it and quickly go "Who sees me? Can I get to cover quick, or take them out before they alert the Hive?"The one weird Sound Effect I think would be from the Lurkers, when you go into their range they make a rattling sound like a rattlesnake which made me laugh.*Exploration -All in all this game doesn't seem too large at first glance, with only 11 Missions and it's finale, which seemed more for exposition (though still enjoyable). However, each of these zones are very unique in their aesthetic and some quite grand in scale. The allure is in all the hackable doors, or breakable walls, there is so much that is hidden that can help you and the rest of the Otago so exploration is very much rewarded.Theme/Immersion -I've only played on Nightmare so far, but the Aliens are a force to be reckoned with, the best way to approach all the missions is "quickly and quietly," you aren't welcome on Lethe (the game's planet) anymore. The game has two great systems, the Infestation system, and the Aggressiveness system that go a long way in reinforcing my prior statement. The Aggressiveness system is a sign of Hive activity, the more the Xenos See you, Hunt you, or Fight you the more active the Hive will become. This means more Xenos, more patrols, and the eventual Onslaught, when you cant hide nor escape, as the Hive will send a large swarm to end you. So it creates an atmosphere of dread, you want to avoid contact with the Xenos, you don't want to linger, the Xenomorph becomes an entity to fear because if even one spots you, it can mean the end.The Infestation level is a supplement to the overall difficulty and the Aggressiveness system, as each day the world becomes more Infested, which means more Xenos, more threat.**SPOILER WARNING**There are missions where the power gets cut on you, or your motion detector isn't functioning. Terror sets in because without a motion sensor they could be around any corner and you wouldn't know, and without the lights this game is Very dark, you can pretty much only make out shapes or what is directly in your Marine's flashlight. Immersion level *Chef's kiss**The Story-There were a couple moments where I couldn't take things seriously, such as in the very beginning cutscene the fat and lazy boss' last name was MacDonald. And, without spoiling the ending, lets say it felt very shonen anime. But outside of those small instances, overall the story of Aliens: Dark Descent is a very good one. It is very thematic to the Aliens Universe, Corporate Corruption, Desperation against such an unstoppable creature, the parallels of greed/ambition and delusion. Can't help but like the Main Cast as their ramshackle base of a crashed ship slowly gets on its feet as you learn more about Lethe, and why it has become infested with the Xenomorphs. **Pro & Cons:*Enemy Variety -This is a Pro & Con because when it comes to enemy variety only the Xenos shine here; though as the main antagonist, in my opinion, they shine bright enough to overcome the dimness of the humans. Humans have a few different types that you will have to fight, but for the most part even on Nightmare difficulty they act the same. Take the closest cover and shoot from it, no other form of tactics or abilities. Which is a real shame because you could have enemy flamethrowers or grenades but nothing. I just flamethrower at their cover, they just stand there and burn to death.The Aliens are great though, they have different combat styles, some actually have abilities that can be dodged or canceled by using your own abilities (so interaction between the opposing parties abilities, fantastic), and they will try to dodge bullets and grenades you shoot at them, truly the ultimate lifeforms. The AI *Team AI-The smart AI system they had, Squad Priority or something, definitely made this a more player friendly experience. You don't have to micromanage each and every squadmate, based on their traits, gear, and class it will choose who is best for the job you assign.However, this can lead to some annoyances when you WANT to micromanage, as this system makes it impossible to do so.For instance many times I would want my recon to snipe a target, but the recon loves to be in the back of the group. So the other Marines may be seen, as you dance your team back and forth so the recon can finally get line of sight and shoot.Enemy AI -Often, this AI would be quite good. The Xenos or other foes would make patrols, stand sentry in key locations, attempt to flank you, or even leave what I referred to as "Lurkers" (Aliens hiding in vents), on your path or in random rooms to discourage sprinting everywhere.It was also great that they took notice of firewalls from flamethrowers, which felt rewarding to cut off their path or funnel them a particular way using those flamethrowers (Enemies will attempt to not walk in fire unless you block all paths to the Marines).However; the game, naturally, also always knows where you are, and sometimes in turn that means the enemy does too. There is a stealth element to this game, in fact it is Extremely important to making the mission successful. But many times the enemy would just gun it for my team. I know that they are supposed to be attracted by sound, and if one spots you, then your last location will be the first place they check when Hunting you, but many times I wasn't hunted, or if I was, I would use sounds to lure them away from my direction, but the enemy would ignore the distractions or despite not having seen me in a long time would know exactly where to search. (I've watched the motion tracker as I've run back and forth in a room, the enemy followed me outside the wall trying to meet me at the door I chose for the exit). I doubt this is intentional, but its worth mentioning, it is quite annoying or can put you in a bad spot.**Cons:*Crashing/Stability-This game crashes A Lot. Out of my current 47 hours I think the game crashed about 12 times? I know that the development team has been hard at work fixing it, I've read the patch notes. But it wouldn't be fair not to mention that there is some issues with the stability currently, which is the main thing that hurt my overall rating. Wait to buy so they can clear them up, or launch at your risk (there are only autosaves, and when your team takes a rest).There was also one mission where the cutscenes worked perfectly fine, but after one "Narrative moment" the game was lagging like it was connected to a far away server, the Marines and environment texture became choppy and so did their movements and actions.Overall, a great game and worth the price, regardless if you're a fan of Aliens or not. It is friendly enough with it's smart AI for those unfamiliar or new to tactical games to give it a try, and a must buy if you're a tactical game lover.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - Very fun. Kept me busy for about 35h roughly.Some bugs. Hope they keep working on it. Potentially DLC later.Mix of Turn based macro (Days for sorting things out) and RTS in-game. Can slow down the game using space to use abilities, or on easy pause game to decide what to do.Great mixture of pacing, resource management specifically the tools, medkits, and sentry guns, the upgrading of squads and mechanics so even if something goes wrong it's not the end of the game but instead allows you to stay in it. Creating your squad is pretty fun. The bugs can be frustrating (The gameplay ones, not the enemies) but with a patch already out, I'm hopeful they keep working on them. The storyline is fun and engaging. Took an interest in the characters through great writing & cutscenes.I finished on Nightmare on my 1st playthrough, took me roughly 35h, also played around in Normal after. Normal seems like the run n gun difficulty, not too pressing. Nightmare seems like the Aliens way of playing. It's dangerous, and need to figure out game mechanics to overcome the enemies, but when it clicks it becomes a blast. Having a marine down, do you leave them behind? Carry them to evac? How about enemies that are coming, can you put down a distraction with mines & sentries? Many different tactical approaches & gameplay mechanics meant I always had a blast. I'd recommend if you're a fan of the Aliens series, or tactical games like XCOM etc.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: This is actually a XCOM based squad game but every thing is dealt with in realtime or slo-mo.There are no turns, u move your whole squad with one click on the mouse, want to scavenge that box and weld that door, np. 2 of your squadmates each fill out 1 task with the lmb while the other 2 take cover behind that box with rmb!  This is so smooth that this feels like whole new gaming genre. I play on medium difficulty and have cleared the first map for 53%. 4% at game completion on a slowly played 6 hours. And yes u can re-send squads to earlier visited locations. All in all, a good entry for the alien franchise due to vibe, story, cutscenes and last but not least an amazing game with even better gameplay. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly good. I was skeptical about the game play but it is really solid.I highly recommend this game. Story is nothing special and there are still a few bugs that can be quite detrimental. As with the studios last games (battle fleet Gothic). They make really solid game play experiences but the thing it lacks for me is a sandbox. They make a system that could function exceptionally well in a sandbox but then don't deliver the freedom of one.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: As an avid XCOM player, this game scratches that itch hard, and vastly speeds up the pace, and raw panic for you and your marines by making it an RTS.There were times of pure moment to moment crisis-management and panic with split-second decision making when I got caught out without a good fighting position during an incoming onslaught, and I LIVE FOR THAT, IT WAS GREAT.The atmosphere and graphics are top notch and fit the setting super well, everything has that Aliens feel, from the small cattle town to the dockyards and the old, Nostromo era ship, to the high tech and the new skyscraper HQ of Weyland Yutani, all of it feels authentic and looks great.This goes double for the Xenomorphs and Marines, both the sound design and looks.My only wish in this would be for the music to have been a more triumphant score on the end mission screen, it's lacklustre at best,I only have two downsides, one major and one minor.--Major--The bugs I encountered were annoying and required restarts of the game to fix, singular marines being unable to run, unable to crouch hide when pressing shift, I even had an instance of one guy bugged who was stuck pretending to be carrying a civilian, and trying and failing to operate the only elevator requiring me to restart to the beginning of the mission and wasting 1:30 hours of playtime.That said the patches have been frequent and large and have fixed a lot of issues already, so I have faith these will soon be fixed.--SPOILER WARNING----Minor--TL;DRThis Game is to Aliens, what Alien: Isolation was to Alien.I bought it and it's become one of my sleeper hits of this year.Just don't play it on ironman until most of the bugs are fixed.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so good!It absolutely nails all the important things about the Aliens series: - set piece design (gorgeous, detailed, inspired 80s-tech sci-fi with morbid atmosphere; the graphics are perfectly in-theme here)- the plot... and how it ties to gameplay (to me this is the game that truly develops X-Com ideas, and does in an very clever way) - a great balance of the speed of events and suspense (better than the recent Alien Prometheus+ movies in terms of direction, better than most Space Hulk PC games in terms of gameplay)
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: This game can be a lot of fun, the atmosphere on most of the missions is well executed and the gameplay is stellar. I do have a few gripes though. For one, the pacing of the individual levels is well done, but the pacing of the overall game is very poor whenn it comes to how they handle all the specialized enemy types. Both the Crusher and the Praetorian, which are the only miniboss enemies in the game, are both introduced in the first three levels. And while I may be biased on this final point, having more than one xenomorph queen feels like it should be quite a big deal, but it actually cheapens just how indimidating they're supposed to be. You have to kill 6 or 7 of them in this game, and you don't even get to be clever about it. Nobody gets in a power loader or drops a cave on them, or uses high-explosives. You just shoot it until it dies. Which is pretty easy to do if you just keep walking backwards.I do have other minor gripes about the marine classes and lack of enemy variety, but really, this is a good game. I'd recommend picking it up during a sale.There is one thing I wish this game had, and that's a random level generator, or a custom level generator. And if you could make your own levels with scripted events that could be even better. I think these would help add to the replayability a lot.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Before even taking into account the game play, I have to commend the art and sound teams... it's not close... it's spot on what an experience in this universe should look and sound like. The pulse rifles, the sentry turrets, the music all fit perfectly. The amount of visual clutter and detail in every environment is beyond anything I've ever see in such a game -  the environments feel real and 'lived-in'.At first, game play felt a bit awkward and unnecessarily restrained, but stick with it. I am very accustomed of being in full control of each party member in games like this. It feels counter intuitive to not be able to micromanage every move order/action. After 1.5 play throughs, I still feel the same way, but only for specific actions. For example, not being able to move a marine with a unique skill take point as you walk around is irritating and can effect missions quite drastically if they're not in the ideal position. Overall though, I think they made the right call eliminating a lot of pointless micromanagement, but some adjustments to the formula would be appreciated.The story isn't going to win any awards, but it's still well presented and the interactions between characters feel genuine. I would have liked it if one or two other characters got a bit more 'screen time', but it's fine as it is.The UI and controls are mostly excellent, but do yourself a favour and don't play with a controller... Mouse and keyboard is the only way you can react quickly enough to a lot of what the game throws at you.Bugs - and no, I don't mean the aliens - are still present, but most of the big ones from release are gone. Haven't had any crashes since the recent patch.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: The best "Aliens" Game in many years full of tense moments with rather solid gameplay. the individual maps and objectives and good and varied is let down a tad by alright overall plot and a underwhelming if not poor last missionBeen good updates so far fixing problems and adding new game plusDefo a recommend

_childDocuments_.review: Lots of unfortunate glitches and bugs that make this game unplayable at times. Very frustrating to sink a hours into a mission just for a single marine to suddenly get stuck on a piece of environment and then subsequently slaughtered. This should be a fun game but it's holding itself back with all of the problems.

_childDocuments_.review: A solid real time tactics game in the Alien universe. Mechanics are not so hard to grasp, lightning and voice design are nice. Aliens are really fast and deadly, squad upgrading and management is satisfying.Sadly the last mission and the ending feels botched. If you can ignore that - the game is 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This is what I was waiting for since I started playing XCOM.  I truly recommend this game to all XCOM lovers and all ALIENS fans.  The tension, the fear, the environments are so on point to what you would expect to a game from the ALIENS genre.  This made me rewatch the ALIEN movies all over again and after watching the movies, I play the game and it is truly immersive that lets you really play careful of the lives of your marines.  It feels like I am in their shoes all the time with them during missions.  Over all, really GREAT GAME! cannot wait for future story missions DLC and if there will be a possibility to crossover with the PREDATORS franchise after this..
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: These designers understand the property; any future game based off the second film needs to copy their homework.++ 'fear of the unknown' and 'the calm before the storm' from the film is reflected in the game as you must cautiously search every dark crevice for your objectives not knowing what's ahead, and when the ♥♥♥♥ does finally go down, 'it's game time.' + xenos are a true threat that must be destroyed at a distance and a single one has the potential to mess up your whole squad; they're not punchable zombies.+ motion tracker is integral to your decision making, not just for show+ even the shoulder lamp plays an integral role for searching and scanning+ welding to create barriers and bottle necks is a mechanic just like the film, not just some scripted event for progressing a linear level+ true to movie aesthetics and equipment; no useless neon lights on everything and tons of quantity-over-quality loot guns, just the basic film weaponry with a few extras from the technical manual.-- still more human on human (weyland aggressors) combat than I would have liked - this is the most unpopular feature to have ever reared its ugly head since A:CM.  Paranoid civies ie. Alien Isolation is one thing, mindless stormtrooper/Umbrella Corps types also armed with guns has proven uninteresting.- remote turret gun has wrong movie sound, used pulse sound, actually had a more traditional machine gun sound in the film- space-madness colonists missed chance to show how brutal '10mm explosive tip caseless' is; they should be getting blown to bits instead of tanking a ton of rounds like they're on space meth.- the mad science stuff angle is weird, and though in-line with expanded lore comics, will come off as off-the-rocker to the average fan who is only familiar with the film; Alien Isolation found the best middle-ground to exist believably in the film lore.- cut scenes could look better but this was no doubt a budget constraintSo not many complaints, it's a solid entry to the Aliens library that finally does right by the fans and lore.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: As a massive fan of the ALIENS universe and brutal strategy games like XCOM I have to say I'm loving this game so far. I recommend playing on NIGHTMARE with restrictive saving that way the game just feels way more tense. Brutal fun! I look forwarding to seeing what the future brings to this game. MODs will will amazing!
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: WOW, just one hour in and I am HOOKED!If you are an Aliens fan and cannot wait for the next Aliens movie, this game will completely scratch that itch! The prologue itself is the best part of any Aliens movie, the Aliens soundtrack and atmospheric music, lets you feel you are playing in the movie itself! This is the best prologue I ever played in any video games (movement animation is top notch too!) Some parts really also feels like playing Dead Space in 3PS with some jump scares. So true to the original Aliens movie visuals! The walls and gates of the colonies look just like in the movies, the marine armor and camo, the shuttle transport and even the USS Otago look just like the USS Sulaco in the second Aliens movie! (in fact, I highly recommend rewatching the second Aliens movie when you play this game for better and deeper immersion!)Gameplay wise, this is almost a XCOM2 reskin in a good way.No XCOM2 wannabes have ever nailed the things this game did:1. The cinematic introduction to the chiefs of each part of the base (almost exactly how it felt in XCOM2)2. The squad ready screen where they stand in front of the vehicle is almost completely XCOM23. Given a voice and face to "Commander"However, I like that they didnt go TBS with this but RTS. TBS in such a title will kill the pressure and suspense. It will kill the panic and rush that you should feel as a player as the Aliens are coming down on you. The environmental engineering is so good it feels like what XCOM2 was trying to achieve in its original alpha tech demo which didnt happen. I am just hooked!

_childDocuments_.review: 1.Nice action RTS gameplay.2.Challenging mission the whole game till the end.3.Very well done optimize.4.The horror that you think you can't find when you play rts game. You will find it in this game.1.You can't choose leader of you squad make some skill of you soldier does't work as it should be and You can't adjust soldier position either.2.Upgrading you squad and weapon mechanic is to few for my taste.3.Some of Cinematic camera in the game kill you in the game cause it change position of camera in the middle of fighting.Game worth it price even when full price.Enjoy the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Common, but entrancing story arc in the Aliens universe.  The game started fine and got better as it went because of more story development, capable marines, and refined tactics.  Two big positives are the leadership skills and the slow motion if desired.  The base line weapons were damn near spit ball guns, so the leadership skills and slow motion were essential to utilize.  Seemed like there were good balances with respect to resources in the game- not enough to be wasteful, neither too scarce to be ridiculous.  Liked that saving in the game is tied to rest, which was tied to stress.  It did not feel tedious though.    Graphics were not over-the-top, but decent.  There was pleasantly a lot of detail in the maps.  Upgrading the marines is a bit random, but in a good way.  Soldier classes were done well with some nice perks as they leveled up.  Something I was not fond of was the frequency of random enemies.  Why is there always a bad guy around?  One sentry dead, two dead, three, four, etc.  It felt pointless because the baddies kept spawning.  There were some glitches, but nothing game breaking.  I enjoyed the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Scaling on Random Events/Campaign events is completely ridiculous. On harder difficulties this game becomes way too much deal with. At Dead Hills, I ran into the issue of spawning a Crusher, having to Kill the Queen, while also having to deal with back-to-back onslaughts. Boss rooms need to isolated, making it so that an already difficult boss isn't made worse by random mini-bosses/drones. Squads just don't have the ammunition to deal with that, especially that early on in the game. I have tried to beat this area for a few hours with no success, I do keep getting further and further each try, but its hopeless, I run out of ammo, command points, and repair points (so no more tactical analysis) at the end of each run. I like randomness of spawning a mini-boss once you piss off the aliens enough. Its an interesting mechanic that definitely adds a lot to the mundane-ness you feel running around collecting resources and completing tasks. But it hasn't been scaled properly at higher difficulties and it makes boss-fights downright unfair if you spawn one right before or after. I'll return to this game at some point and try again, but discovering that problems with scaling exist like this hurts my opinion on this game. There are obviously features that weren't tested to the fullest on ALL difficulties. I think this game is good, despite the lackluster voice-acting and the goofy game mechanics it has been great playing this game. But I've reached a limit on how much I'm willing to put up with.Later on in the game, sure this situation wouldn't be much to deal with. But in the first area, with a squad that's all low rank, with basic weapons, skills, and traits...Its just too much. The only way to get through this area is to hope random chance doesn't perfectly align a mini-boss and a boss fight together. This problem should have been anticipated but it wasn't.Their is reason games like Elden Ring prevent other enemies from joining a boss fight. Boss fights, especially at high difficulty settings, are meant to test and break you already...by tacking on other enemies/mini-bosses it makes things completely unfair and greatly reduces the impact of player skill. I'm sure at some point I'll eventually pull off the right combo of movements, command point uses, etc. all in a strict proper order...But that is in no way what an RTS should be...Having to guess-and-check your way to the right combo of moves and prayful RNG is an absolute contradiction to the word "strategy."---EDIT---After multiple attempts I was able to finally recover my marines by running back to the APC and coming back the next day to complete the mission. While I now recommend the game after learning a little more about the mechanics, I still think there is an issue with the scaling and "boss mode" areas. I'm sure at lower difficulties it isn't much of an issue, but with higher difficulties, too much RNG is required with time, positioning of enemies, etc.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished my first pass through the campaign on medium difficulty.The game isn't perfect and there are some legitimate gripes that others have already expressed in their reviews.  I'm not going to go into them myself because this game is just so much fun!  As someone who used to play RTS a lot in my younger years but stopped due to needing to micromanage every little thing, this game is a breath of fresh air.I love the stealth aspects of the game and the ease of manoeuvring around a level.  In stealth and when things get hot the different command points (ability) options are very very cool and open up at a good rate through the campaign. Needing to decide whether to spend a CP for a stealth option or keep it back in case you are discovered is a neat way to balance your resources.  I love the level design and exploration in the game.  As well as being given the option to complete the game (mostly) at your own pace.  Most of the levels were very fun and had great side objective options. I don't usually play a game again after finishing it but the New Game+ option is intriguing me.  No promises I'll make it all the way through a second time but with the amount of hours I've already sunk into the game I would say this game was definitely worth my time and money.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Great concept, huge fail. Limited ammo, limited health, limited resources in general, and yet, the game spawns enemy after enemy after enemy, even though you just cleared out an area behind you, here they come again. I can't do these cheap thrills and cheap ways of making a game challenging, anymore. It's a game based on strategy and tactics, and when you use those tactics and the game just spawns people behind you for no reason and you have to use all your resources just to keep going, it gets really cheap feeling and frustrating as heck. Man, I had high hopes and this is just junk. Everything else about it is great, but this one thing did it for me. Quit the game and uninstalled on the second operation where it kept spawning these guys running at me with sledgehammers from behind, EVEN THOUGH I just cleared the freaking area out! Where are they coming from, the Alien landscape rock caves. Give me a break, what a waste of my time.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: *EDITED* I initially gave this game a thumbs down, but after realizing I'm just not a big fan of RTS games, it's not fair I negatively review a genre I don't enjoy. What I did experience wasn't for me, so I'm leaving my comments below, but I would recommend this game if you do enjoy RTS games and to read over all the other positive reviews. This game may be for you.===============I know this game is getting great reviews, and I definitely don't speak for everyone here, but I did not see the appeal:1. Game is full of glitchy movements and weird animations.2. While I love the fact the game is challenging and has limited saves... it's pacing is horrible. Not everyone wants to sit and play a game for long periods of time before it saves. I made it to my first mission, go into the building, and then I had to stop playing due to work. When I loaded my game up... I was back at THE START of the base LOL I had to go through all the base tutorials again, then relaunch the mission. Why didn't the game save at the start of the mission, at least?3. Combat is... OK. Nothing overly exciting. Stealth around, shoot, use a few abilities, shoot more.4. The start of the game is VERY slow and the story, quite frankly, isn't that interesting. Dialogue is poorly written and just cheesy, and the serious conversations aren't that exciting.5. Controls are annoying. Edge scrolling drives me nuts, and I'm not a fan of point and click movement. WHY the devs didn't let us move with WASD... is beyond me. Especially since the game primarily consists of you moving your squad around a map/level. Point and click would make sense if we could select/deselect certain squad members, but you always move as one unit... so the constant shifting your mouse around and double clicking to run and single clicking to walk is frustrating.Basically, the game had a slow start, boring characters, nothing overly exciting about the story, and I wanted to make sure I could refund before I passed the 2 hour mark. Doesn't mean you won't enjoy this game, and maybe it gets better, but it definitely didn't grab my attention in the first TWO HOURS I played LOLI would recommend trying it. Maybe you'll like it. You can always refund like I did if you don't.

_childDocuments_.review: First things first... If you're a huge fan of Aliens, and anything related to the Colonial Marines. This game is probably right up your alley.Dark Descent gives you a taste of everything you probably love about Aliens; from the guns, to the usage of the ARC as an APC, to the dropship footage, and amusing quips from it's pilot Hunslet. The banter of the squad, and the incredible sense of fear and dread as you move through corridors, trying to achieve your objectives. Squad building, and skills are very much like XCOM, so plan your squad, and weapons wisely. Some missions call for a different set of skills, you will have a base, just like in XCOM, and you can research things, etc.While not a Turn Based Tactical RPG, this game gets so many things right about gameplay and fits right into it's own unique genre. It works, and if you like RTS, and you like games like XCOM, as well as horror survival, you'll love this, but keep in mind.... This is not an easy game, and you will not be just running in and shooting stuff. This IS a strategy game, and you will have to plan properly, and try to be stealthy. Your guns are for when all else fails, and the ♥♥♥♥ hits the fan, just like in the movie. You don't want to encounter a Xenomorph if all possible, you'll know they're there, and sometimes you will have them on your motion tracker, but you do NOT want to engage them if possible.All in all, this game is a 9/10 for me.Some things i would have liked to see, is more extensive squad customization, like MUCH more extensive. Different armor, more weapons, more faces, hair, all of it. I would have also liked the ability to get a tad more hands on with the ARC, but maybe in a sequel or something. I am very happy to see the game has mod support though.My hope for a future game, is something that allows me to travel with a ship from planet to planet maybe, with several missions per planet, take on the role of a Xeno task force of sorts.

_childDocuments_.review: Updated Review:This is my GOTY for 2023. Absolute most fun game I've played in 2023. If you are an Aliens fan, and a fan of difficult gameplay - buy this one immediately.I nominated for many steam awards including innovative gameplay. The gameplay of this game, the build customization, and the difficulty curve are what make it such a great game.I would describe the gameplay like this: Inspired by X-COM, but a Real-time strategy. Stealth like a roguelike game, mixed with the cover system of Company of Heroes and the small squad control of like one of those original StarCraft campaign missions where you didn't have a base - like the science vessel mission. Combine all this with kind of a brutal detection system and difficulty curve. It's more fun than any isometric game I've played. Fairly stressful, and very rewarding.I would also like to say Kudos to the developer Tindalos, and Arak at Tindalos on the Focus Discord for being very receptive to fan input through the release process.When they released the NG+ update for the game, there was an issue making NG+ from an older save file. Me and another guy pinged Arak on the discord minutes after release, uploaded our saves directly to Tindalos, and it was hotfixed the next day. I think if Tindalos were given more feedom to output much needed DLC's and content (think mod support? a map editor? Something like this) would go a long way to the game's longevity.Some issues with the game:There are still some bugs I'd like to see fixed - like destroyed eggs detecting the squad.While the level / map designs are all fantastic - they are all static. There is still RNG in spawns and patrol locations, but the game being so static really limits the replayability. I still replay it like crazy because I love it, but each subsequent playthrough basically is on a lower difficulty curve just because of my experience at playing the game.If this game does not get future DLC / expansions / or a sequel, I will be very sad about it. it's one of the most deserving games of 2023 to get more content. I would buy up every bit of paid DLC immediately, just to support the developer.While I would be sad, I would also encourage developer to take what they have created (even if they are only allowed to take their experience from their creation) and put it toward a new IP. Develop their own game that they OWN with similar gameplay and mechanics. Most innovative game. I'd love to play more.You'll see my hours haven't increased much - that's because I've been playing it on XBOX for a while, working on learning how it runs on consoles so I can have a better understanding of how it plays on consoles.GOTY 2023 for me.Original Review:Never imagined I'd enjoy a game that makes me stressed out, but I do.This game is fun, frustrating, difficult, and unforgiving of mistakes. The Aliens world is awesome. Killing xenomorphs is as fun as it is anxiety inducing. I could probably play this game every day. There's plenty of different ways to play it and build your squad, and I'll probably play it until I've tried them all.The "death clock" in the game isn't particularly fun, I imagine I will turn it completely off after I beat Nightmare and Hard mode, although it adds some more challenge to the game, it also prevents you from just fully leveling up every marine.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't sleep on this game.  I'm not sure why it hasn't gotten more attention.  It's one of the best depictions of James Cameron's vision for Aliens. While its not quite Aliens meets x-com, I found the fire team-based squad tactics to be fun and engaging.  And at its current price point, there is simply no reason not to pick this game up.  Some early reviews mentioned bugs, but those have almost entirely been squashed.  There is a mission where a sidequest is still busted, but it doesn't seem to impact progression at all.  Love this game.  Among my top three of the year.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a "yes" if you like horror games. The gimmick of the game is that xenomorphs are terrifying and hunt your squad relentlessly (with basically zero other objectives) when you make noise, or exist, etc, and that hunting leads to stress from rightfully perceived imminent death. All that is fine. Now, you're telling me we got big open tunnels we can't possibly conceive of any way to close off once discovered unless it just happens to be behind a weldable door? Even though we've seen makeshift walls and dropship bombs do it (and we might carry grenades and do carry C4)? Yeah, right. Left that off so the enemy has plot armor in a game that prioritizes the horror rather than the strategy, which means the strategy is "don't get seen or heard". Well, several of the effective ways to do that (re: sentries + motion tracker noise while hiding) don't grant experience points (outside of defense phases) even when it's the marines doing it (rather than the probably invincible ARC). So, effectively dealing with the enemy grants no experience (in almost all cases), but that's what you likely need to do to make it long enough to accomplish objectives. Then I'm 10 hours into the game, many missions deep, and you're telling me I have to place my sentries in a no deviation tutorial-style way? And you picked a layout they're going to predictably get wrecked in? Really? Am I supposed to believe it's the stress talking in that situation?I'd have turned the difficulty off if I knew all that... and I'd have to start over to do that now. Wonderful.

_childDocuments_.review: Picture a real time XCOM, but your squad moves as a singular unit, mix it with some stealth elements and a bit of survival horror, like Alien: Isolation, and you get Aliens: Dark Descent.The bulk of the game is exploring large settlements, where you'll go through all kinds of buildings and tunnels in environments that I feel perfectly capture the Aliens vibe.  The atmosphere is moody and dark, and the familiar ping of your motion tracker will constantly have you scanning your surroundings.  Each mission you partake can be broken up into multiple deployments.  This means you are able to extract your squad whenever you wish and return later.  This also allows you to revisit other areas to collect anything you may have left behind.  The missions also have multiple primary and secondary objectives, as well as hidden items you can find to help your squad, and your ship/base.  Combat is very simple, and a lot of fun.  it can be a bit tricky to get the hang of it, so thankfully the game slows down when you open your command menu for your squad.  You can also set this to pause the game when you open the menu.  Each unique ability requires a Command Point, which slowly regenerate and you have a limited amount of these, so one must really be mindful of your tactical choices.  Your squad also will get stressed out, which causes them to have negative effects in combat, and also these can affect the rest of the squad.  Each Marine will react differently, and as the stress levels build up, so do the negative effects.  There are often times where it's best to avoid combat and detection, as prolonged engagements really take a toll on your supplies, and your Marines.  When you are not on mission, you are on your ship.  This functions similar to the bunker in XCOM, where you can research new weapons and tech, upgrade and promote your Marines, and heal them when they are wounded in between missions.  The story is by no means award winning material, but it does seem to fit well into the Aliens universe style of writing.  Don't expect much in the way of the narrative, except a bunch of cliche's and predictable plot twists.  That being said, I enjoyed the story.  Mostly.Pros:Good atmosphereEasy interface and controlsFreedom to complete missions as you wishCombat is funClassic Colonial Marines armaments, Pulse Rifle, Smart Gun, Flamethrower, Shotguns and auto sentriesChallenging without being unfairCons:No manual save optionAutosave is inconsistent, and doesn't always save after an objective is completedStealth sections do exist in the game, and I found them to be rather tedious and frustratingEvery time you kill a Xeno, your squad gets hunted for a brief period of timeSome missions seem to drag on too long with poor pacingStory is mediocre, even by sci-fi standards, But i still thought it was decent enough to move the game alongIf you're a die hard Aliens fan, and felt like the last handful of games with the Colonial Marines have been a let down, I think you'll be surprised at this title.  Don't go into it thinking it's an action packed FPS.  It's quite the opposite.  It does a great job at building the tension between encounters, much like how the movie did before the Marines found the hive.  For $40, it's really hard to say no to this game.  If you're on the fence, wait for a sale.Overall, 7.5/10Not perfect by any stretch, but it delivers a pretty solid game for the price, and mixes familiar elements to make a fairly unique Aliens game.

_childDocuments_.review: Strong recommendation for aliens fans.  Solid recommendation to general gamers too.GOOD:  * Graphics and Sound are good.  * Game play is pretty pretty smooth, but you definitely need to read and understand the mechanics (they explain as you progress) or you are going to be in a world of hurt / frustrated.  I was in a such a rush, I missed the detail that welding yourself into a room allows your team to rest + rearm + creates a save game point. * A day in the corps is like a day on the farm.  Every meal a banquet.  Every formation a parade.BAD* Marines say the same 2 lines every time you issue an order which is frequent, annoying and breaks immersion.  I'm sure they'll patch that or give an option to disable it.* I don't like the regulation cornbread either.Gameplay example:Squad was deep in an alien hive with massive stress, no medkits low ammo, an inured civilian and marine BOTH of whom needed to be carried (which severely slows your movement speed)Had several failed attempts at extracting.However, we did have more sentry guns than we could carry (6).  So I had to the marine who wasn't carrying comrades, run ahead and place sentries at key positions.  Then sprint back and up the ones watching our back.  Sort of daisy chained the sentries like a slow moving caterpillar all the way to the exit.  At one point we had a "Massive Onslaught" approaching.  So I had the two marines carrying, drop their people so they could effectively fight and use abilities.  It worked and was very satisfying.If this sort of story appeals to you, you should definitely check out the game.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a surprisingly good game. It has RTS elements such as battlefield fog, real time combats and resource management, but also simplified them so it doesn't take too much time to learn the game. The detailed explanation for everything in the game when you first encounter them also helps. the prologue also gives you a few deploys to learn everything step by step. As a RTS fan, I like how the game play is, It's simple but have some depth to it, and I don't have to learn everything to finish the story. However, one thing I dislike about is the controls. all squad members move as a whole, yet the enemy detection is for each individual, and I didn't see a way to adjust the position of the marine I need to use (usually the recon for sniping). I wish they allow the control of a individual marine. The story is very "Alien" style, no bs romance, just human trying to survive under the infestation. you can adjust the difficulty during game so it wouldn't be hard to go through the game at all. if you want a challenge, the game also provides a new game+ option for addition challenge and upgrades available.I wish there's more IP turned games like this.

_childDocuments_.review: If you want a tactical game experience that captures, in essence, the hectic last stand of the colonial marines at Hadley's Hope then this is a close as you are gonna get. If you enjoyed the gameplay of XCOM then you'll enjoy this. Its a faster paced more real time, realistic, version of XCOM. The story is a lil flat so far. Also some of the characters. It suffers a lil from "modern audience" syndrome in that the colonial Marines are all but lost puppies without the direction of the company rep, who happens to be a rather unlikable character who's there to girl boss her way out of trouble at the expense of male cast members. This is where it falls flat a little as anyone who's seen the Alien and Alien's films know that a character like Ripley is not awesome at the expense of her male costars, she is just awesome in of herself. The difference between well written characters and "modern" characters. That said its not too intrusive and doesn't undermine the action of the game itself. Well worth a playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, lots of intense game play and atmosphere!I've seen a few bugs (Hints: the "Rest" button doesn't persist after you've spent the tool resource to seal a door for resting your squad so, if you miss clicking it, you have to un-weld/re-weld for another opportunity to rest, space station elevator doesn't always open to allow the squad to walk out, leaving you trapped and having to reload the game, others..).One part of the game I really DON'T LIKE is STRESS:- It's too significant in it's impact on game play, not because it particularly degrades marine performance it's just annoying to listen to the game complaining about it! (constant messages from the ARC commander to rest, marines bellyaching etc.)- It doesn't add anything to the experience because the marines (and the player) are more at the mercy of the ever increasing and stacking stress bars than, they are at the mercy of the aliens!  (in other words, it's a never-ending distraction for the player)- Having to - waste - a tool resource(s) on welding a door to overcome stress is not fun!  Especially considering that, tools aren't in great supply in the campaign maps and the (scarce) resources you pick up here and there are better spent elsewhere! (like upgraded weapons)The stress system could seriously be un-invented.  OR, at least remove the requirement to use a scarce resource for welding - safe room - doors only!Other than that, a very good game and worth the money!

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty solid addition to the Aliens video game arsenal.  Very reminiscent of the 2nd film.  Aliens: Dark Descent is essentially a real-time version of X-COM where you build out a squad of different specialists and deploy them into mission after mission to gather resources, rescue people, discover new tech, and advance the plot.  I felt they really nailed the atmosphere, narrative, and visuals.  There were however a lot of bugs throughout my play-through... BUT a pretty major patch was just released that appears to address a lot of them.  Also, while it is a very tactical/stealth game, there were several times I felt encounters were more luck based than skill, sometimes requiring multiple reloads until the AI decided to behave as intended (such as one time where I recall an enemy sprinting across the map directly to my squad even though I had never ever been detected).  Overall, I really enjoyed it and definitely think it's worth a look.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: I'll give this game a thumbs up, with a one clarification and a couple qualifications.To clarify?  Your marines are not the top of the food chain.  You can go full rock and roll through the missions, but the game will make it hurt.  Much of the game will revolve around sneaking and setting up ambushes to kill xenos and their allies before they can raise an alarm.  And picking your fights when you have to and where they are most advantageous.On the qualifications, there is still an unresolved bug where if you bring back the wrong person (this is made clear fairly early in the mission) you will suffer a bad event.  This objective was and still is bugged as of the writing, it doesn't matter if you choose correctly, the bad event still happens.Secondly, I have some issues with the final mission.  The non-spoiled version is that level feels like the devs just wanted to wrap the game and phoned it in.  For more details, I'll keep it mild but spoilered.  A good game overall, but needs some patching.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Legitimately worth a play if you are into tactical RTS style games. You'll have a blast!Lacks in replay-ability unless you are an achievement hunter or just want to "do better" because of a linear, non-dynamic campaign. That aside, it is an absolutely phenomenal tactical RTS and I didn't think I would love it as much as I did. There are legitimate jump scares where you just go dang....I'm done for, and slowly accept your fate.... or manage your command points and barely scrape by? Great game, and glad to pay homage to a slightly forgotten franchise. I hope the developers look into furthering the story of this game through DLC and perhaps add a more dynamic element where you simply take back land/settlements taken by the aliens/humanoids and reinforce it before you can figure out how to stop them. Could include more research elements (not just xeno based), resource management as it is already implemented would work perfectly for it, and maybe settlement upgrades that include predetermined sentry placement, sandbags/defence areas, greater "daily resource intake", and "cannon fodder" militia for defense. A "play how you wish" style campaign DLC would be amazing. But that may be wishful thinking.

_childDocuments_.review: Very strange (yet still flawed) gameplay; with a cheesy story that could've been written by an AI prompt of "generic sci-fi action", and a surprising amount of polish.The game is strange in the sense that, even though you can feel the lack of budget and time pressure in certain areas of the game (story; voice acting, possibly some of the ways the mechanics work), it generally doesn't detract from the main experience.The biggest issues for me were (playing on hard difficulty):* The game can bug out quite hard at times - e.g. marines can often lock up after using the RPG and the only way I found to unlock them is to let them get hit by an enemy.* The game sort of wants to be a stealth game but also a murder party at the same time, and punishes you in different ways for going with either approach. I found that maxing out the "Aggression meter" actually makes the levels easier since you no longer have to worry about triggering Massive Onslaughts (xeno hordes) at inopportune times, making being detected far less of a pain.* It can be really, _really_ frustrating to see your entire squad fire on a single xeno for like 5 seconds straight and not hit a single shot. This is even with accuracy bonuses.* Some of the upgrade slot upgrades seemed... useless, at least for my playstyle.* The trauma mechanic is interesting, but I found that outside of the trauma that causes an increase in reload time, you can sort of just ignore them (even at max level trauma).* The AI pathing is really suspicious at times, combined with the way the game decides to spawn in xenos, can make certain areas near impossible to deal with in a stealthy manner - sometimes it's easier to trigger a detection and dash through a whole bunch of the map, then explore it leisurely once the hunt is over.* Sometimes xenos just don't respond at all to sound and the game doesn't seem to explain that this is intended. Xenos can also decide/bug out to never move, which can often force you to trigger a detection to deal with them.* Loads and loads of smaller quality of life and annoyances.I know the above is a lot of negativity, but the rest of the gameplay genuinely makes up for it. There's real potential in this formula if the devs/some other devs manage to iterate on it; map mechanics, and base/marine management even further.Highly recommend - just ignore the story even exists though tbh.

_childDocuments_.review: DON'T BUY IN CURRENT STATE!!!(Final edit: The game outstays its welcome after roughly a third through the game. The game is ruined by a focus on endless enemies, and an emphasis on stealth, without providing much mechanics for it. About half the map design is good, and some of it is horrible, a complete mismatch with gameplay. You can abuse many systems because the AI is very bad. Even on hardest the game isn't hard, just tedious with endless enemies, and broken mechanics. Core game idea is good, but implemented quite badly. Atmosphere, and estetics are great, but the story is mostly just noise, with some really bad stuff at the end. Some stupid mission aswell, where you just run around with one character, going EXACTLY where they tell you, not a game at this point. Wait until they fix the numerous bugs, and would personaly get it on a sale. Since about half the content isnt worth much. Did really enjoy parts of it, especially a clutch rocket to the face...) STEALTH GAME, with some heavely punished action parts...It's a stealth game with bad, and few stealth mechanics.Imagine spending 90 procent of your time looking at a motion sensor, looking how the AI clearly knows where you are, and are just poping out new enemies that wander in your general direction.I watched one of my turrets kill 20-30 aliens just poping out of the same hole, and walk out the same door, just to get shot. And be back again in 15 sec, just to do it all again. Over, and over, and over...I still enjoy the game enough to keep playing, but its a shame how good this game could have been. Maybe they will give us more options over our campaigns in the future. But I cant recomend it, in the here and now.The game itself is a mixed bag, some good, some bad, and some really bad. There are frequent bugs, some of which ruins your "runs" by costing you the resource, without giving you the benefit. And some bugs are game-breaking (you can not proceed, and must reload) Voice-lines for example, that accompanies certain actions, play just as often for the wrong actions. Such as "Here they come!", but no one is approching. It's very frequent.You can rest in the game, by welding yourself inside a room. This cost one resource, but sometimes the prompt to rest doesnt appear, after you have spent the resource.You can't burn the eggs with the flamethrower, just let that sink in.Got another bug, where it says that all my marines are not in the elevator, and I will loose those that are not in it, if I use the elevator. Everyone was clearly in the elevator. So I reloaded an earlier checkpoint, got the same message again when I got to the elevator... Tried using using it, didn't loose anyone... Broken mess of a game.Found another bug, were my guy stopped shooting. The gun is on his back, while he just walks around. Died again to bugs, playing with limited saves is not to recomend. This is not a one time thing, had it happen to me four times. Don't play with limited saves.The characters get stuck from time too, which can kill you.And there was this one time durring a mission, when the game grabbed my hand so hard that it got me killed. It stopped me from placing turrets, unless I placed them exactly where they wanted me to, this is a problem by itself. If I hold your hand, and places your chess pieces by my hand, you are not playing chess now are you. I'm playing through you. But it gets worse, the markers that showed me where to put them, was not visable on the map, just in the "normal-view", but you turn the camera all the time, so I missed it. So I ran around for a good long while, and then when I wanted to place it, where I wanted. I couldn't and died. Had to redo about 30 min. This was the fifth mission by the way, not the tutorial.Positives:The atmosphere.The general idea of a persistent XCOM campaign in the alien universe.Most of the ideas, sadly not the ideas that you end up doing the most of.Negatives:Infinite enemies. As in you kill 150 in one "run" and they just keep coming.Spawners, that just pops out a new aliens every 15 sec.Short patrol paths.clearly keeping a minimum amount of roaming enemies, around your current position. A bit shallow. Welding should be a free action.The AI just runs straight at you, no "hunting" or flanking.And the "Alien agression" mechanic ruins the game a bit.Alien Agression mechanic:The aliens are infinite, and when they spot you they come for you in waves. And each time it triggers, the area gets more intense, for the rest of that "run".There are almost no ways of killing them without attracting the hive. So you are heavely punished for fighting the aliens. Which turns the game into a very shallow stealth game.Solution:Have a local infestation level, which is reduced when you kill the aliens, and the queen.This also effect the global infestation level. So that you can push it back, if you play well.Give each level a set amount of enemies, which you can reduce to zero.They should still roam, and track you. And if they find you they will follow, and attack you as a group, waiting for an oppertunity. To attack intelligently.Stealth should be used early until you have a better understanding about the situation, and to avoid wasting resourses/ammo. But it shouldn't be the only way to play the game, were fighting is just a way of reseting the stealth. Leading to some immersion breaking exploits of the game systems.If you decide to get the game, I strongly recomend that you adjust the difficulty as follows:-Enemy health very low (to get the accureate feel of the fire power and abilities that you use)-Enemy reaction time very slow (this will solve some of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in the stealth, such as being able to burn eggs, before they alert the hive. Trust me)(correction, you cant burn the eggs, even if you extend the time...)-Agression growth very slow (now you can play the game like the movies, and acctually search and destroy, without feeling like you are fighting several hundred alies, when it really should be something llike 80-150 aliens in most locations. Hadleys Hope in the movies, had between 20-30 families if I remember correctly. Not an unending horde)-Put the amount of days to finish the campaign on very limited (This will be your difficulity, and force you to make longer and harder "runs")And I know there are plenty of people that like to make games hard, and I fully agree. But you will only be frustated, and forced to just sitt and wait. They dont roam organicly, in big random patterns, they just hover around you, and infinitly respawn.This is not so much a problem in the earlier levels, yet can still be because you have next to no tools to handle it with.Dont use limited saves, too many issues and bugs at the moment.And if any developer might be reading this. You got a good idea here, just iron out the bugs, add some more campaign settings, and move a away from the stealth, and the frantic hordes. Slow down the pace, make it more methodical. Maybe more focus on ammo. Find more ways to make the game difficult, we like hard, and tense games, but this is not the way. One of the few decent alien games out there.

_childDocuments_.review: Middle Thumb.Seeing the percentage of people who have the award for completion of the 11th level I must say the following:Someone here, again, does not understand what the player has come here to do. _childDocuments_.review: Video review: 👉🏻 ✅ Positive points:😔 Negative points:There's only like twelve missions in the game, but the maps are huge and you can leave at any time to re-group and lower the alien hostility meter. You're expected to complete them over the course of multiple missions, though I'm sure there will be players who does everything all in one ago while being constantly swarmed.What the game really needs are randomized maps to increase replayability. I can imagine this game becoming a good roguelike if it did. But also procedurally generated levels are almost universally less interesting than purposely designed ones.During gameplay controls are very solid and there is a slow-motion (can be changed to pause) that can be activated at any point to alleviate any concerns of not being able to respond quickly enough with a controller. 👉🏻 Add more diverse enemies,👉🏻 add more game modes (Survival, Assemble the squad together and reach a certain point by each member of the squad from different ends of the map etc.),👉🏻 add random map generation, and this game will be the diamond of the last 10 years.

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this game for the most part. The atmosphere is great, it looks great, the game play is tense. There is a lot going on that I was really happy with, and as a fan of the Alien universe in all of its forms, I felt like this was a great gift.  But the game is far from perfect. The death clock was a problem for me, and when it became apparent that I wasn't going to beat it, it felt like there was no reason to continue. I also didn't want to restart, because there was always the chance that I would just fail again. As a feature, I found this demoralizing. This problem has been resolved by making the death clock optional, but during my initial play through this was not yet the case. I also disliked the last chapter, when I finally reached it. I felt that it was intensely lack-luster in almost every way, which is pretty disappointing when its so hard to reach the end of the game. I'm not sure what happened - it just felt like the last level was tacked on. It had so much promise and then just failed to deliver. Still, though I will probably never play the game all the way through again, I will definitely revisit it from time to time just for the atmosphere. It was an interesting and unique experience that mostly got it right, and the caveats didn't ruin it entirely.

_childDocuments_.review: Aliens: Dark Descent manages to both ask and answer the question, "How do you make a horror game tactical?"The answer to that question is that you subject the player to a constantly escalating sense of tension, where the need to retreat is balanced against the need to push forward, and success and failure tests on a knife's edge of needing to use your resources effectively under the constraints you're placed in. After many games that treat them as cannon fodder, this game manages to pull off the trick of making xenos still feel dangerous even as you gun hundreds of them down.However, there are some caveats that I must mention which can drag on the experience. First, while the voice acting is generally good, a limited pool of lines and actors to deliver them leads to the moment-to-moment voice lines feeling too frequent and repetitive. More concerning though is that there are several script errors that remain in the game at launch time that can soft-lock your progress until you revert to a prior save or even restart the mission entirely. These will certainly frustrate you at some point.However, even with that I recommend the game, provided you can stomach a little glitchiness. If you can push through a bit of jank, the experience is worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Aliens: Dark Descent is a pleasant surprise because it is an incredibly faithful and entertaining squad-based strategy game. It looks just like the 1986 movie and brings enough new to the table to keep things fresh. It has an interesting story, told fairly well both during and in between missions. Managing a group of Marines across the 20-30 hour campaign is satisfying as you kit them out and heal both physical and mental wounds. Combat is challenging and dynamic, rewarding careful positioning, stress management, and deployment of key abilities, although individual unit control could have elevated it further. While the stealth is a bit wishy-washy, it is still rewarding to avoid alien threats by watching the handy motion-tracker. And despite some technical blemishes, Aliens: Dark Descent is the quintessential bug hunt of 2023.

_childDocuments_.review: In Summary==========9/10 ratingA must play for fans of the franchise>> PROS :: Excellent music, graphics, gameplay, story & game adaption of Alien series.>> CONS :: Voice Acting uninteresting. Not enough base building. Long story campaign. No skipping tutorial.  Buggy (phrasing) with glitches from interface issues to broken character rigging.Long review==============This is one of the best adaptions of the Alien franchise.Much of the game is a homage and a wink to the original films (yes even Alien 3).The maps are gorgeously detailed down the the smallest detail from a pinup poster on a locker to the computers and xenomorph nests.The Sound & Music====================The music is as eerie as the genre.  I still hear the tense build-up theme from when your squad is about to be spotted.  It builds the dread and anticipation.The music plays homage to the original source. Much is from the 1 & 2 films, specifically the xenomorph encounters. You hear that epic theme music of trumpets and drums as the aliens rush your squad.OFC, the most iconic and most disturbing sound will be the motion tracker chime. You'll be as cautious and alert everytime you hear that iconic 'ping'....'ping'...ping...ping..ping..ping..ping.ping.ping.ping.pingpingpingpingWeapon sounds are true to the film. Smart Rifles and Pulse Rifles sound as they are expected to. The only thing that is a downer are the voice acting for marines on mission. They're to generic, they feel unmotivated and just feels like the actors are just reading their lines.The only descent acting comes from the main cast of the campaign story. Graphics==========Excellent quality and the visual effects stay true to the theme of a dark, 80s scifi genre. The lighting, weather effects and even the lamps on your marines add a level of tension and suspense that'll keep you on your toes.The aliens have their own special attacks, even from head butting to dodging your bullets.  As well as acid blood splatter if they get to close.The maps are beautifully designed with clear references to the films in mind, a true homage with care and research done to their designs and layout.Gameplay==========The game itself feels like it could be a spawn of X-Com Enemy Unknown & Xcom 2. The only difference, however, is the lack of base building. Just mostly dealing with Squad management, weapon construction, Troop management & researching new gear.As you progress in missions, you'll also acquire resources for your team. These items can be used to upgrade and research new items and your troops. As well as use on the field.New enemies are introduced every mission. So you face a new threat with every new quest you embark upon.your squad can develop negative traits after missions. Not just fatigue but they can lose a limb, which will require a prostetic. But also trauma on the field, which will affect their abilities on the maps. Even during missions, prolonged engagements will put mental strain on your troops, to much and they'll start to falter in effectiveness, if not treated.Conclusion==========Overall, the game is a fantastic continuation of the series. The story was a surprise and did not disappoint.I hope it gets a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: In short, gripping and tense atmosphere, the combat and difficulty encourage a slow and careful progress as every encounter can lead to catastrophic consequences for your marines. Story is works well with an interesting ending but mission stage structure can be confusing. Within Aliens Dark Descent you control the movements and abilities of a squad of marines as a single unit. They can auto target enemies, but you can target specific ones to focus their fire. The marine's abilities are grouped together. They are only available if the individual marine is available or capable of using it, such as if an ability requires the use of both arms (such as a special weapon or suppressive fire) but they have an arm injury, then this wouldn't be available, or if the marine is... dead. The aliens target whichever marine they want, usually which is closest, and you don't have control over the squad formation. It can be frustrating as combat and targeting is based on lines of sight. As an example, when using the Recon class sniper ability but everyone apart from the recon can see the enemy, you have to awkwardly move the squad around rather than get the recon to move into position individually. The mission structure can be confusing as mission areas have a few 'floors' (ground floor, basements/caves, building floors). You are able to extract and return to these areas, so don't have to complete them in one sitting. You are encouraged to obtain all resources and items within these areas which contribute towards use in further missions and item creation. These areas are persistent so items taken don't return in subsequent deployments. 1 area doesn't allow you to return to a floor after a story mission event and in another area you cannot return to from the ground floor, wasting a deployment, which you do have in limited numbers for story reasons. Your marines have their individual stats, health, armour, ammo and stress. You also have negative traits or traumas caused by stress increasing past certain stages. The squad has a pool of command points (used for abilities that refills over time and through kills).When seen by Aliens they are alerted to you moving to your last seen location and searching until this alert phase ends. The more the aliens are alerted to you the overall aggressiveness increases which leads to greater numbers and stronger types of aliens. When in combat, taking damage and generally in alert status the marine's stress increases. As you progress through the missions you work through ammunition, deployable turrets, through your medical supplies (used for treating injuries and stress), you can rest in secure rooms to recover from stress using another resource to weld doors, but this is also a finite function. You can find all resources during missions but you cannot rely on them. These systems work well to discourage combat as a long term solution to complete the missions, identify and create choke-points, then extract at the right time. An alien encounter at the wrong time and place can get everyone killed or abducted very quickly this makes every encounter exciting.

_childDocuments_.review: This has many ingredients of a great game.But it falls short at delivering emotion and it is not believable.New personal you acquire has no face - is only introduced as numbers and later as names. You need to track names to know who is who. A simple portrait and maybe a background story would've done a lot for building up emotion.Things are heavily scripted and obviously so, with repeated patrols, dead aliens being respawned, taking away from an emotional experience. Leaving you with a game you don't want to experience but only optimize.For instance many events are heavily scripted and there is no threat at all until you press a button. In one case this is very obvious as you can see a horde of aliens running about outside of the map back and forth to make a stressful situation. Until you realize the situation does not change until you press a button. Only then will the aliens enter your area. This feels pretty terrible. There are many such things.In one event your marines will leave your sentries behind. You actually don't need them for the event, so you will have to load and play the event again without placing the sentries to keep them.Marines carrying people walk slower which makes things believable. But everyone of them can carry a sentry and run about with all the other equipment. When your realize the gamey things the illusion breaks.Boss aliens loose their terror, because there are masses of them.It is a shame, as many things are executed very well.So if you are more into number games and gamey games, playing the mechanics and optimizing, this might be for you. But if you look for an emotional experience look elsewhere. This is a bit like a b-movie.EDIT: Oh yes, and the bugs. Mesh rendering bugs where the face of a marine gets stretched in a cutscene. Holes in meshes.

I find that my biggest dislike is the inability to control individual units, like in X Com, but it is still highly enjoyable. The skills and tools are well done and implemented.The game is not completely trouble free, but the fix is just restarting the mission before launching the mission. The game does have a couple of game breaking bugs that I ran into, but fortunately the saves to restart a mission saved me each time. Both times was dealing with a foe that did not spawn.In short, I highly recommend Aliens Dark Descent. This game is highly enjoyable, so much that I am playing through a second time straight after.
