_childDocuments_.review: It's an odd one. If you expect from the devs of Battlefield Gothic 1 and 2 to create a game in which you control individual soldiers... this ain't it. But if you expect a cool story, fun mechanics and love for the franchise and for detail then you'd be right!How does the game actually play like?It plays a little like Desperados or Jagged Allience only that you control your characters as one unit. They might have individual traits and can take on specific tasks (like using their sniper rifle), but for the most part you control ONE unit (with a lots of arms and legs).Still when it comes to level design and gameplay those games are a closer match than for instance Battlefleet Gothic.There are stealth missions and stealth elements in some missions, but this ain't Alien: Isolation! When you NEED to stealth it feels a little shoehorned in. When you don't need to do it you probably won't :)There is also a 'base management' (rather resource management) aspect between missions, but that's less than secondary imho.What I liked about the game:Surprisingly, the campaign isn't too long. Not too short either. Just about the right amount of content and barely anything feels like repetition... and that despite the fact that you re-visit certain areas!Also surprisingly, it's very atmospheric even despite the not super-immersive isometric perspective. Not so much creeping horror like the Alien movie, but good action with a veeery bleak touch like Aliens.What I didn't like:non-skippable non-cinematic cutscenes! Stop that! Patch it! NOW! With (almost) no option to save the game whenever you want you mostly rely on savepoints. Some of them occur just BEFORE a non-skippable cutscene. Some are your main savepoint before a particularly difficult section. Some of the cutscenes I can repeat from memory now. They are not that great.Several mechanics are pretty unintuitive and only reveal themselves during gameplay. The way investigating suspicious survivors is handled in one mission, how rare certain resources are, how exactly repeating missions work,...It's not a maaajor issue, but it left me scratching my head a couple of time and caused me to take longer breaks from the game.TL;DR: Good game! Just make sure you know what type of game it is!

_childDocuments_.review: Aliens: Dark Descent is a very tight strategy/Management/XCom style game that brings some very cool new things to the table and makes all those new things shine.The main change from your classic squad strategy game is that there is no turn style combat, and instead it is replaced by real time micromanagement of a 4 marine team with different skills and perks. This is probably the best part of the game and, at first, the one that I was most scared of. It is implemented brilliantly, and even playing on a gamepad the controls were very responsive and it felt great. Missions are open ended, which means you can deploy a squad to a zone, do a couple of objectives and go back to base if you see your marines are no longer fit and then come back with a new squad the next day.Another important part of the game is the fact that combat is not the main priority of the missions (even if there are some "boss fights" here and there). Most of the time your squad of marines will be hiding from aliens and trying to achieve the mission goals as smooth as possible. Combat only occurs when the aliens see you, and the more they do the harder the fights become so it is a priority to do things silent and fast. The last part is the fact that this is,after all, an Alien franchise game, so it is full of tense moments and you need to manage the stress on your marines as they face the xenomorphs and see horrors happen.  As stress grow, they will start to be nervous, miss their shots and even freeze and usually it is a good sign that you need to go back to base.Overall a very impressive game, even if it is not for the faint hearted, and I wish some of the mechanics implemented here are brought to other strategy games in the future and become the new standard.

_childDocuments_.review: To start, my first play-through was on medium difficulty. I meticulously explored every area of every map, picked up every single item, piece of equipment and hidden objects and had great fun doing so. My second play-through was on Nightmare and No One Can Hear Them Scream mode (a combination of the hardest difficulties) along with the "New Game +" mode, allowing my marines to attain level 15 while giving new experiences along the way. The mechanics are well thought out, generally optimised and quite true to the original Alien lore and universe (although there were no shields in the original universe!) I'm looking forward to another campaign, perhaps another NG+ play-through with different marines.Some minor downsides - nothing overwhelming or fundamentally broken:- Control over the camera is occasionally taken from the player to show a certain cutscene or event in the game - this occasionally results in damage to your team since you cannot observe the full area until control is released. Additionally, the game does not always return the camera to where the player had it originally (e.g. orientation) so if you like your camera aligned with a particular direction, you'll be adjusting it often.- There are some fairly basic bugs such as team members getting stuck in cover that necessitate a reload. While generally not a big problem, this can be frustrating when playing on Nightmare mode along with No One Can Hear Them Scream mode (where you can't save as normal).- There are the occasional moments where you are forcibly extracted and can risk losing equipment or missing hidden items (e.g. datapads) without prior notice. In my first play-through, I reloaded back two missions as I had missed a datapad that I thought was retrievable later (that area of the map had been permanently closed off following objective completion).Overall, a fantastic game with some mechanics that are extremely fun and definitely one I've thoroughly enjoyed getting all the achievements to score a Perfect Game on!

_childDocuments_.review: It has a lot of human fights for an alien game... But overall the dev did a fine job coming up with their story so far (I'm not done yet). Every time I died there never was no explanations either. They could have done those parts a bit better.I also wish we could skip the campaign dialog's for us mediocre players that have to replay from last saves after a fail. Only cinematics are skipable. Also everytime we get those in game dialog's, the camera angle is taken over so we see the intended objects in proper focus, and once the cinematic is done it stays on the new angle which is annoying, and disorienting. Would be nice if the camera angle would automatically revert to what the user had before, but thanks to the minimap, I've learn to point North again as the first thing I do. Overall good game, definitely recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10!It's a good Alien game! It's not a 10/10, but it's a really fresh take on an Alien game stacked against other games in the series that I think ranks higher than a lot of them.The story is ok, but good enough to drive the plot to different locations, showcasing the level designs which I really think are the highlight of the game. Some levels felt directly inspired from movies, where as other levels fell nicely handcrafted to be something different not really seen in the Alien universe.I'm unsatisfied by the concept of having to retreat from levels due to stress, but like the idea of the stress mechanic playing a large part of the game. The banter from the main protagonist and marines is ok but you fall into the loop of every 3rd fight ends with a marine stating "That gun is a frickin lawnmower!" and it gets stale. The guns however sound just like they do in the movies and that's pretty rad!The level of customization with the marines, both cosmetics and ability wise really lacked. Due to the absence of personality, I never bothered to customize the marines or color their armor. The abilities are either essential, or super bad. Classes were the same. Medics and gunners feel designed enough with a clear purpose and techers,Recons and "Sargents"  the game? The Sarge yells at the squad to not stress out...and thats...it. Recon can use a sniper that's useless, unless you can find a big bug baddy to chunk for health. Recon sniper is an ability vs a gun and feels out of touch with the game cause the game is claustrophobic hallways at mid/short range, so not sure why it's there. Techers are the IT staff that can hack a door, but it cost tools to open doors? I mean, people don't throw screwdrivers at laptops to hack into them so that's odd to me. I would have rather see them bypass without a cost and then suck at something like not being able to heal.  Would have loved to see a flamethrower class or maybe a solely shotgun user as well. Overall, not blown away by the level of depth/strategy in the game in terms of class utility mixing.Lastly, The game is an XCOM clone or heavily inspired, but the base building sucks, and research was dull. You go back to your base every time you end a mission, and the loop for me was "heal, treat PTSD, go again" A  good idea not properly executed but it wasn't unplayable!Regardless of my list of frustrations, I had fun! It's exciting and nerve wrecking to see blips show up on radar and beep louder and faster as they approach you like in the movies. I was happy to see a variety of Alien creature designs and not having to fight only the "warriors". Making noise but blowing up a wall to get resources created risk. It was always a "good"stressful to get a warning that bugs were on the move and setting up a corner with sentrys to hopefully out DPS a wave of bugs before the got to your squad. Several cut scenes and in game cinematic pay homage to Alien scenes from different movies and it's always appreciated as someone who like the Alien films.The game respectfully doesn't pretend to be a triple A experience and was marketed at a nice $40, but is easily a steal at sub $30. I got 37 hours out of it and hope the next Alien game/movie keeps me coming back for more! I would love to see a sequel in the future!If you are an Alien fan and have not played it, I'd say look for a sale and check it out! It's a fresh breath of air in terms of some RTS games and feels like it's something that could be really special if a sequel is provided in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Dark Descent is a real time strategy game where you control a squad of 4-5 marines completing a variety of objectives to escape from a planet now overrun by aliens, a cult, experimented on humans, and enemy soldiers while using a damaged troop carrier, the USS Otago, as a base where you can manage your Colonial Marines and research upgrades.The prologue of the game has you controlling a Weyland Yutani administrator who escapes a station that has been overrun with aliens after she activates a quarantine procedure that destroy an escaping infestation and another ship while heavily damaging and grounding the Otago, a troop carrier whose personnel rescue her. Both her and the marines attempt to quarantine the outbreak while saving as many people on the planet as they can while trying to find a way to escape the planet and bypass the satellites that will shoot down anything that passes low orbit.Mission have you choosing and equipping between 1-5 marines of five available classes and completing a variety of primary and secondary objectives on locations like derelict ships, space stations, research bases, alien hives, dockyards, corporate offices, destroyed living spaces, etc. While the missions are linear in their progression you can go back to areas you have been to before to gather supplies or find missing datapads, though it should never be necessary. At any point that you are able to reach the vehicle that deploys with your marines you can choose to extract your squad to refill ammo, supplies, and possibly switch out marines if yours have been wounded or traumatized. Stress can build up while under attack or hunted that can raise trauma levels and give each marine a variety of passive penalties until they spend time with a psychologist on the ship, on the normal difficulty this never happened for me. As in most games like this, depending on the amount of damage a marine suffers they will have to spend a certain number of days in the medbay before that can be deployed again. For ever doctor that you start with on staff or rescue during missions or during random end day events you can use one to lower the time needed to recover for a marine by one day, even using multiple on the same character. Certain wounds can also lead to penalties in a mission until healed or might lead to a body part needing a prosthetic, thought I never did have anyone lose a body part. Going on a mission will also cause a marine to become tired, to lose that status they have to sit out the next mission or they will have a penalty to their bravery (stress defense) and accuracy. Going on a mission while tired will cause them to become exhausted which will now force them to rest for two days.While on a mission your marines constantly move as one group, though depending on where everyone is in their formation you might have only one who is in a position to be spotted by an enemy or who has a line of sight on a target. Once an enemy engages them they will all automatically attack targets but you can set priority targets be clicking on an enemy or engage a target that has not engaged you yet by clicking on them. You can pause or slow time down (depending on the option chosen in the gameplay settings) to bring up a list of commands that allow you to use special abilities or special weapons and gadgets you have equipped at the cost of command points. You get four command points that slowly recharge over time to do things like having a soldier use suppressing fire to slow enemy advance at the chosen angle, use a weapon like a shotgun, flamethrower, or sniper rifle, set a mine up, set up a motion tracker that can be activated to lure enemies in, throw a flare to increase accuracy in its AoE, etc. In addition to command actions you can also order marines use equipped gear like medkits, tools to seal a door or to hack or repair things in the environment, to set up or reload sentry guns, or to use ammo to reload their own guns or to set up explosives to blow up weakened walls. Certain rooms are marked as potential safe areas and completely sealing a room allows you to rest which will lower stress and may have other effects depending on the classes and skills of your marines.The way that everyone moves as a squad both works very well while also creating problems. On one hand it makes things simple to control most of the time, I never once had anyone get caught or stuck in the environment or running some different path from everyone else, etc. On the other it can make using cover or hiding awkward when suddenly one person isn't quiet able to fit on a cover spot. Formations options to change how people are standing would have been nice as having no control frequently has the person equipped with the tool you need standing in a spot that isn't fitting for the situation. Your marine with the flamethrower and shotgun might be behind everyone, your recon class you typically would want in front is somewhere else, your most wounded character isn't standing near the center where it is safter and keeps moving to the frontline, etc. Interacting with objects will typically have the closest person run over to do it before they rejoin the squad when they are done, this is usually fine but you might have a more combat focused character suddenly trying to open a door, or it just assumes you want your tech guy to drive the power loader or medic to extract samples from an enemy body when they might be one of your most combat effective character or equipped or injured in a way where you don't want them doing that.There are five classes a marine can become once they hit level three and lose their generic rookie class. The most useful classes that I always had one of was the Sergeant and Recon classes. A Sergeant increases your command points by one, lowers the recovery time of command points, and has an ability that prevents stress from increasing for 30 seconds at the cost of one command point. Having a sergeant meant I never had to worry about stress after the first few missions and always had better access to my most useful abilities. A Recon class makes the squad move a little faster and has a variety of what I found useless gadgets to track enemies on top of the motion sensor you already have, what they also have is the most useful thing in the game which was a silenced sniper rifle that they can use as soon as they become a recon class. Spending a command point to aim an instant and silent kill shot at lone enemies combined with the use of your motion tracking and ability to hide in cover really opens up stealth options that can see you having a much easier time getting through missions in one attempt as you avoid being hunted or increasing alien aggression as those hunts build up. They also allow you to exploit many of the encounters with groups of human enemies where you can just snipe them without engaging in the fairly poor gun battles you can get into. The Gunner could easily be the remaining 2-3 spots in your squad. The gunner has access to the smartgun that holds more ammo, fires faster, and can be set up as it's own sentry on top of the dedicated sentry guns you have while your gunner fights with their secondary weapon. They make the entire squad better at suppression fire for each one in the squad and get a passive bonuses to getting dismembering or critical hits on enemies. Like in most strategy games Medics have a variety of skills for helping you a bad situation that you probably could have avoided if you brought someone along who wasn't a medic. The best thing about them is that this is finally a game where just having one of them on your team can lower after time required to spend in the medbay by 30%, making them much better than XCOMs medics. The final class is the Tecker which the game makes almost useless for some reason...Full Review:

_childDocuments_.review: You know I thought I was going to hate this game prior it to coming out. I remember hearing there was a real time tactics/RTS being made in the Aliens universe and I thought this is going to be awful. Even after seeing what was released for it at the time and watching several convention videos showing little bits of game play I was really on the fence about this game. I only bought it because I'm a fan of the old series. Like a lot of people playing this. It took me a while to get into it but by the end of the game I actually think it's really good game. I'm glad they tried something else for a change. Being a fan of RTS and some RTT games as well it didn't take that long to understand how the mechanics work and for the most part they do so really well. You have everything Aliens shows you available to use. Plus loads more new stuff and some extra heavy weaponry that's not in any of the films to use later on. You often get the use of an APC you can deploy (with you troops if you wish inside) to different parts of the map. It will assist you in combat too if anything comes near it. The maps are fairly large too and there are usually multiple maps within one. So for instance you'll be on the surface of one and then take an elevator down or up to which takes you to another maps. They're all quite maze like a times too with lots of places, rooms and goodies to collect and explore.   The graphics are really nice looking too (although peoples faces and hair looks pretty bad, but you're not close enough to really look at their faces apart from the squad selection screen). Lots of detail has poured into the environments and even the "skyboxes" look amazing. The game has done the best out of any game to nail the look and feel of "Aliens" so far. (I just wish they used the proper pulse rifle sound and door opening sound from the film). I'm amazed they managed to make an RTT game actually scary and tense, it's quite impressive. People compare this to something like most recent XCOM games. While it takes some inspiration from it, to me it plays more like Desperados 3. It's all real time, you have abilities to use. Instead of controlling one person at a time, you control a squad that moves as one and attacks as one. Using sentry guns, the suppression skill and flares to aid you in combat at certain points is really a life saver.The game is heavily story driven and cinematic surprisingly. The story is quite interesting too, if not a little bats*** at times. There are some really cool moments in it. There are some really well done cinematics too with nice framing and epic moments. The lip sync and character animation could've been a lot better though. Of course accompanying all this is a damn pretty good musical score taking influence from all of the original 3 Alien films. I really hope they keep improving the game. Or that they add some more content. Or more story stuff. Something co-op related too would be awesome. Two players controlling their own squads and helping each other out etc..If you're a fan of the franchise, give it a chance and try it out. It's well worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that grew on me the more I played it. It completely nails the Alien atmosphere and feeling of tension, which is incredible considering its seen from a top down perspective. But having hordes of aliens chasing after your incredibly fragile and easily traumatized marines is pretty nerve wracking, especially in the earlier missions when your firepower isn't that great and your options are limited.The gameplay varies between two general states: running around trying to avoid being seen by the xenos and running away while fighting the xenos. There is no way to wipe them out. They will keep coming back and getting stronger and more numerous the longer you are in a mission. The more you get spotted, the more tense things get, until it eventually becomes too dangerous to continue and you are forced to extract and come back a day later when they have calmed down. Each mission takes anywhere from an hour to three depending on how thorough you are, and I didn't get bored throughout the game. The story is pretty good, if rather predictable for an Alien game. This game does feel rather unique though. I haven't played any other game with mechanics like this, and its definitely worth getting.

_childDocuments_.review: I have 100% completed the game and all achievements.I changed it from positive to negative after completing the story campaign.Whilst it enjoyable and my own personal preference at the end was disappointing it is worth buying, just not yet. Wait until they actually fix the bugs and errors, a lot of disappointed players on discussion board with corrupted and broken saves.I am continuing to play it as its one game I should be able to get 100% achievements, however one of the secret ones is incredibly time consuming, RNG and currently involves reloading the same save file for 6hours trying to get lucky with getting my marines torn apart repeatedly >.< I'll list the goods first then potential spoiler at the endPlay with the lights off and headphone on.Alien(s) fanSome cutscenes are just great!!The audio and atmosphere is greatLiking the set designs and layouts of mapsFor everyone saying its a poor version of Xcom, whilst I love the Xcom series it actually plays more like Commando series, Desperado and Shadow Tactics:Blades. to make you're missions easier your supposed to maximise stealth, hide around corners and behind counters, then pause and slow time for the tactical options. Instead of failing when you break stealth the mission and difficulty of the level get progressively harder until you eventually die or have to retreat. You can replay mission ares to collect loot and objects you miss as many times as you want (within the global day timer) and as long as it doesn't specify state it is a 1 deployment missionSome general models/facial movement, not so greatEvery once in a while it feels the graphics drop from ultra to low poly, using RTX 2080, 32gb, I9-9900 processor.Watched a couple of clips of gameplay and I was a bit sceptical but really enjoying it so far and enjoying the story, glad I listened to some books on audible recently as they've given me an early insight into one of the main characters early on that others may not have (not that the characters were in it, but from certain actions the character does).For a change i'm playing on story mode first, I usually play on hardest settings first, I get the feeling this is going to be brutal on the next play through :D On story mode you can happily run and gun the majority of the time, or set down arcs of fire and not worry so much about stealth, using terminology from other games> every time you kill an alien and are noticed it increases your "wanted level" also known as hive aggression. Being noticed progresses time on aggression, this will advance your difficulty on a map from easy, medium, to hard. AS the aggression level rises you will be hunted, "hordes" will appear to track you down and also the ELITE and more powerful variety of Alien mutations will emerge to try and decimate you with special abilities.*I've seen some reviews complain of lack of ability to Ping or add a waypoint on your map. Press down the middle mouse button :)One thing I would like to see as others mention is the ability to ungroup the squad, set up 2person fire teams, or even jsut let my scout walk around a corner first because nearly every time it has no LoS whilst everyone is in the open triggering the alert reaction counter of an alien somewhere.That being said, don't forget you don't have to send 4 people on a mission, I have just sent 1 scout out on their own, equipped with the silencer for precision shot and flashlight mod to shoe hidden aliens in the dark. Kill or be killed, clearing the way for grunts to get massacred after :D***AFTER COMPLETING IT**After several game crashes and save breaking bugsThe ending was disappointingAll your efforts, squad, equipment choices etc come down to a pre-scripted squad and weapon choice.There is no final Boss fightOver-climactic, whilst beautiful and with that omg wow factor ends in multiple cut-scene sequences sequence...If you are ok with no end battle and jsut running, then thats ok you'll be happy with the endif you are happy to use predetermined characters and loadout and making your squad non existent, this is for you.If you're ok with "it's about the journey, not the destination" this game is ok for youWhilst I enjoy the journey, bugs, stuck characters, crashing game, corrupted saves, I might take in the scenery whilst walking to a shop but I still end up disappointed if its closed for no reasonplaying again on nightmare with the limited save option, the save points are terrible, no autosave at the start of a boss fight "you may die here" you could end up with a 40minute wasted death in some situations as I'm trying for the achievement where marines get their limbs get ripped off and get replaced with prosthesis but there is more chance that they just die than anythingSome more random bugs i have encountered:Turrets failing to deploy, clicking sentry on the blue outline to redeploy, but the characters do nothing, clicking X to cancel but this also does nothing, other than reverting to an earlier save point its gets permanently broken and counts as a deployed sentry, on nightmare with limited saves = lot of time wasted.Dropping an injured marine, but character doesn't register it dropped them so ends up stuck using a pistol and then a second marine also has to carry the person. _childDocuments_.review: This game honestly is better than I expected. I will say there are bugs and things I would suggest in a remastered edition or a sequel/ follow up game. The setting of this game is great and the atmosphere is actually pretty scary at times especially when you are trying to do stuff while tons of enemies are around and you are trying to avoid firefights. While close to the end and not giving spoilers the story is pretty good and making me want to know what happens next. Weapons/ classes are interesting with each one bringing their own use. You can customize you characters within reason and give them skills based on what you see fit.As for suggestionsFirst off I feel as though the hard timer that gets dropped before everything is done for comes too early by a level or 2The ability to field 5 marines is cool but it is never really brought up till you find the thing that allows it and even then it instantly goes into a cutscene of you recovering it then ending the deployment causing you to waste time on the doom counter that is in place.Customized class abilities feel like they need to be more diverse with once you unlock the class there is no reason why people would not pick stuff like silencing a sniper or being able to bring back downed Marines. Also the tech marine feels pointless at first because a perk that allows other marines to unlock doors and stuff.Also possible limits on how many of a certain weapon can be in a squad would be nice I run 3 plasma guns a smart gun and a regular pulse rifle (for the grenade launcher) and the ability to do 3 concurrent plasma overloads just destroys any threat even the boss xenos in seconds.

_childDocuments_.review: Every decision made by the designers of this game is wrong. Instead of being a heroic 3/4 view game, or a tense "make every shot count" game, this is a game of clinical psychology, where you worry more about someone's stress and associated effects than you do hunting bugs. As much fun as arranging items in a backpack. I feel honestly ripped off.::edit:: Dawn of War had xenos, and that game, all of them, were super fun. This game misses everything you can find in any number of similar titles. There's not even a chance to get attached to a given soldier because they're all expendable and interchangeable. Feh, whatever.

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever wanted to play XCOM: Survival Horror? Oh, but it's in real time, so you don't even get the benefit of infinite planning. At best, you get to watch xenos matrix-dodge your shotgun blasts in slow-mo.There's the occasional rough edge with pathfinding, the movement dialog could be toned down a bit, and some of the cutscene facial animations are... dangerously near Andromeda-tier, but don't you fear, there's plenty else here.Oh, and the prologue is pretty stiff. Push through that and it's not so rough.

_childDocuments_.review: For fans of the Alien franchise this is a must have. The crushing stress is very true to the films and to sweep dark corridors with your team feels epic. And when things get chaotic, which they do...a lot, you better hope you have supplies and a decent defensive position.Overall I loved the game, but a few things did feel a little off to me, such as: The command resource, while I get the point of it it was not a fun mechanic to be restricted by at times. The need for your squad's tools was in my opinion a constant and the regeneration of the resource a little too low to be a smooth mechanic to work with. Some of the personality traits of your marines were a right pain to deal with, as a consequence I didn't bring a few of my soldiers to any missions as it would have delayed progress further, seemed unnecessary. Nice bit of complexity that sadly ended up feeling limiting due to it always being a negative trait, now if they had a positive trait to balance out the decision if it's worth bringing a marine with a really bad personality trait to your missions then I would be fine with the system.Stealth...this was annoying and more times than not didn't work. Especially noticeable when you carefully go from cover to cover down the one path you can and need to go down and there's a vent with a xeno in it, because why not, and the lack to deal with said xeno without triggering a hunt made it feel like there was no point to trying to be sneaky and careful. The faces and customisation for your troops seemed a little bare bones and rushed. On missions it doesn't matter as you neither have time or the perspective to see it, but on the Otago it would be nice if they looked a little more polished, currently they look smudged and...oddly shaped. Minor detail, but to me that matters.The linked Med-kit with the Naproleve resource, the choice on whether to treat wounds or relieve stress was tricky, I liked that it wasn't always easy to know whether stress outweighed actual injuries, but when your troops are wigging out, even with traits to help them not do that, before the real waves have even started it was painful to give up the resources when there wasn't any med refills around, and most maps didn't have very many of them. So this would have been a little less irksome if either there was a separate resource for Naproleve, or if stress didn't ramp quite so quickly outside of big waves.Small sadness about the iconic gun sounds not being exact. Licensing issue? Biggest wins about this game for me: It's probably the best so far at capturing the chaos and brutality of 'Aliens' and the nerve wracking suspense of 'Alien' and feels connected to the universe the films created. It stretches things a little but so long as you are not a puritan about these things and just want to enjoy yourself in that universe it delivers.The dynamic lighting is gorgeous and adds so much to the atmosphere, and it's very creepy not having the flashlights to rely on at times and everywhere you don't shine your flashlight feels like a potential threat in waiting, and that to me added so much to the atmosphere while playing. They nailed that.Prosthetics! I was honestly amazed that this was a feature when I encountered it, freaking awesome. My Techie lost his left arm and because of that I thought he was a goner, as it turned out once I got back to the Otago he was prepped for surgery and a few days later back in the squad and lived through the rest of my campaign. The game ran very smooth for me, no issues at all, no crashes, no stuttering and seemed 99% bug (not the xeno kind) free. One bug I did encounter was with a repaired synth in your squad one of your actual marines tended to sometimes get stuck in terrain and couldn't be gotten out, happened especially in narrow places with crates to loot... but that was it.Details like abductions, facehuggers skittering towards your team in inopportune moments and the might of the big xenos was terrifying to deal with... in the best possible way.For me I would rate this 8.5/10, not a full score for the minor things mentioned, but should those get addressed then it would more than likely be 10/10 for me.I waited for a good opportunity to get the game and don't regret the purchase, I have just finished my first playthrough and I'm sure I'll do more. Can definitely recommend fans of 'Alien(s)' and gaming this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Jesus Christ, this game is good! I've rarely seen an entire franchise, and especially one of my favourite Movies (Alien 2) being so really well transferred into a game before. It captures everything that movie was and is about, and more. In very general, you have a game here which is squad tactics like X-Com, but in real time, mixed with the Alien franchise. And it's darn well. The sounds are epic, the looks are decent, you can customize and level up your Marines between missions, improve their loadout, oh, and you get a freaking APC (tank/armored personell carrier) within the missions to drive your team around, and yes, it shoots the crap outta enemies. It's also got this stressing atmosphere for a change which shows us humans despite all our weapons NOT being superior to an alien species, you gotta fullfill your missions, watch your motion tracker, and use tactical skills and your smarts to outmaneuver alien patrols. Or go right for them and shoot the crap outa those xenomorphts and show them what steel humanity is made out of. But, this will activate "the hive's" aggressiveness, and it will send waves of lethal aliens at you. Your choice.The game has also got some very innovative gameplay features. And it's difficult at first - simply because the enemies are freaking intellingt, they dodge you and flank you, they try their best to get into melee range and if they are close enough and you still manage to kill them without your squad being shred to pieces, they explode in a freaking acid cloud, hurting or killing your Marines. Aside of armour and hp values your Marines also got a stress level, which increases the more crap they see and witness, and the more they gotta fight for their lives. This levels up - or rather down - in 3 levels, from "we're okay" to "that's getting scary" to "let's just get the hell outa here." And all those stress levels grant debuffs on each soldier, even long term trauma effects which you gotta heal in med bay between missions (you got enough soldiers, no worries). You can combat stress in missions through creating a safe room, meaning you gotta weld some doors and give your Marines a short break. This is also when the game saves - yep, there's no regular save option, only between mission progression and/or when you created a save room. It's tense, it's rather not the random super easy game - but also not a super challenge once you know your way around, it's kinda fair. It's also got beautiful optics and is extremely good in capturing the Alien franchise's flair. Also super good cut scenes and story telling. This game will be for you if you like strategy games like X-Com and/or the Alien franchise. I'd give this a solid 9/10 but only because I hope they will one day bring Predators, which are in the same universe, and/or the ability to maybe play as the aliens and an alien hive, too, into the game, one day - as a gladly payable dlc. Respect to the devs, you've managed to fully merge one of my alltime favourite movies into an extremly well executed game. Super unexpected, good job!

_childDocuments_.review: Best Alien game since Isolation. Immensely enjoyable and rewarding gameplay. You can tell the developers love both the Alien franchise and gaming in general. The game recreates the atmosphere of the Alien universe perfectly and they managed to come up with an interesting and original story within the setting. If you're a fan of the setting and/or the genre it's a no brainer. Cons: Didn't like the RNG aspect of choosing perks for your marines. Getting unlucky with perks really stings on higher difficulties. Also the voicelines for player idle are WAY too frequent and overtuned. Your marines will harass you to get moving if you stop to think about what you want to do for more than 5 seconds.

_childDocuments_.review: Aliens Dark Descent does a wonderful job of capturing the feel of the original aliens movie with its graphics and gameplay. though it has a few flaws. in general i recommend it but hope the developers fix the issuesPros:-Good Visuals that are faithful to the movie and help you get immersed. 99% of the props are accurate to the movie and -Amazing Game-play and Level design. the mechanics capture the feel of the movie and keep you on the edge of your seat. they make you always feel under threat or moments away from death.-Solid story that keeps you mostly engaged throughoutCons:-Audio is extremely bad. the Voice Acting in the game is atrocious with only one good performance from the Sergeant and dropship pilot, everyone else is either mediocre or bad. there are only 4 voices (2 for each gender) for your marines and only 1 sounds good. there is no line variety so you will hear the same line every time you do an action. most line deliveries are flat and when creating a saferoom you hear what seems to be developer placeholder voice actingthe pulse rifle sound effects are weak and doesnt sound like the pulse rifle at all.

_childDocuments_.review: Dawn of War 2 and X-Com had an Aliens themed love child.  The squad control style is unique, but very enjoyable.  Above all it does an incredible job capturing the suspense and tension of a proper Aliens title.  I never imagined a horror/suspense theme could work in an RTS of any style, but the enemies are dangerous enough and supplies/morale are limited enough that the urge to hide from monsters is more than just a stealth mission gimmick.It can be buggy at times, and the character models aren't top notch, but I've had a lot of fun with it and would recommend it to anyone who would care to hear "Dawn of War 2" "X-Com" and "Aliens" in the same sentence.

_childDocuments_.review: Quite fun and scary at the same time. Top down RTS with all the aliens that makes you have to consider your deployments carefully and what your load out is. You manage your squad, armory, med bay, workshop, training center, trauma bay all on the ship you ended up blowing up and crashing because you decided to implement Cerberus Protocol to contain the Aliens. Pretty sure the Sergeant is a Synth. Do not like that there is no actual save function at all only autosaves that are not very consistent because id have put a few hours in and end up getting a squad wiped only to revert way back and my progress is gone. _childDocuments_.review: So now that they've fixed a lot of the major issues that were present during my first playthrough I am switching my review to positive and writing a proper review.So basically this game is an real time tactics game like Commandos except if you played as one big blob of units instead of individual units. The blob hivemind determines which unit gets sent out to do tasks that require only one of your units to perform like welding doors or setting up sentries. But otherwise it's a RTT game that is about stealthing through space facilities avoiding Alien aggro, setting up stealth kills, and when things go wrong/or as part of main story events, setting up killing floors to ensure you don't get overwhelmed by the Alien Swarm.The aliens are pretty dangerous, one drone catching your team off guard can chip away at your team health, three catching you unprepared can potentially be a unit lost. But if you play well and actually use your abilities the danger in this game isn't a few aliens, it's the swarm and attrition. If you've played Risk of Rain, there's a system in that where the difficulty timer ticks up and things get harder over time, this game has that but only during a hunt. Being detected by an alien triggers a hunt where the aliens in the level start coming to where you were detected to kill you. The hunt lasts about a minute I think and while the hunt is in process the difficulty meter ticks up. One hunt will cause it to tick up a notch by the time it ends and three notches triggers an increase in the difficulty level and a massive onslaught event that you have to set up defenses for otherwise you'll get destroyed. So put simply, you stealth in this game to avoid triggering onslaughts and keep the difficulty level down. You can survive both of those things, but you have limited resources and when those both of those things will drain you of ammo and health.Your marines also suffer from stress that rises when things go wrong, during hunts and also (if they have developed phobias) when exposed to their phobias. There are 4 stress levels for each unit and each new level reached will add some debuffs like a decrease in accuracy, them causing stress for other units, a decrease in your command point regen rate and so on. So you aren't just managing health and ammo, but also your marine's mental state. You can recover from stress by getting your guys into a room, welding off all doors in and resting, leaving the current mission (your progress saves and you can redeploy) or by popping some chill pills (but it uses up medicine that could be used for healing wounds).The game has an XCOM like overworld situation where when you leave a mission you enter a command phase where you can research guns and tech, treat marines wounds and mental states, promote and upgrade your marines and so on, and then deploy onto missions. But it's not procedural gen stuff like XCOM. There are about 10ish? hand crafted missions, your progress in them is stored when you leave and you pretty much have multiple attempts to do the mission with different squads. Leaving and coming back just gives you a chance to regroup, resupply and reset the difficulty timer. The XCOM stuff is a little undercooked to be honest, it's there, it works but it makes you wish they'd leant in a little harder into it and making a procgen game that could be replayed a bunch rather than (or in addition to) the somewhat linear not very replayable set of missions they currently have.For the most part the game works pretty well. The game is tense during stealth and chaotic outside of stealth (chaotic fun). I had a lot of fun playing it and want more, but ultimately it was only about a 30 hour game for me, which for the price is really good, but don't expect XCOM levels of replayability. As I mentioned initially, you play as a blob. This is clearly a decision aimed at making the game accessible and having it work for controllers, but it introduces a lot of frustration into the mix where you wish you could just micro each unit specifically but you can't. This means you have to fiddle about a lot to get your sniper into position to have LoS to take a shot which is REALLY annoying. Having the game auto-select a unit to do an action when that unit is one you'd rather have on standby (because they have the RPG for example) is annoying too.  There's a way to manually select who you want to do certain tasks for some things but you have to fiddle with extra button presses after selecting the thing to interact with and I actually went my entire playthrough not even knowing you could do that.There are scripted sequences where the game introduces a hard event, so like a cutscene showing a boss you're going to fight. The game usually tells you when you're about to trigger one of these events and asks you if you're sure and to prepare. The problem is sometimes you prepare and then it pulls the rug out from under you by forcing you into a new arena where your preparations (mines and sentry guns) are left behind and you can't get back to them until later. Rug pulls like this really suck.The game has a lot of small decisions like this that made me go "wait, you really decided this was a good idea? How could you be so foolish when with other parts of the game you were so smart?" Alone they're not that bad, but there's enough of them that I felt like the game could have used an editor standing behind the devs with a water bottle and for each of these things, being like "NO! BAD DEV! STOP!" and giving them a spray. The human enemies are truly awful and each time they're in the game it turns from a solid 9/10 game to a 5/10.We're pretty starved for RTT games so if you're looking for a new one to play, I'd recommend this one to you simply because there's not really any competition. But it's good enough that I'd recommend playing it even if there was a glut of them. It's one of the few good Alien™ games. This game is to Aliens what Alien Isolation is to Alien.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of cool concepts were attempted here unfortunately the whole thing is a buggy, oversimplified, ui/ux mess.I don't usually get excited for a game in a beloved IP because too often they lean heavily on their IP to be good games, and ending up failing to deliver. Despite being an obviously lower budget game, Dark Descent held some promise. The Previews make it look slick and we polished, but that's simply because you're not driving the action.The tutorial is an absolute dog. In reviews, there's a lot of comparisons being thrown around here, XCOM, Darkest Dungeon, etc. The game warns you it's "difficult" and it's important to pay attention to the tutorials, but it's mostly because the menus and controls don't make sense for KBM, and are extremely clunky in realtime. Menus and functions are buried under menus, under menus. This makes the stealth elements that much more frustrating. I can't tell you how many times I failed the "stealth" section of the tutorial and had to go back and skip a cinematic because guess what - the autosave sucks too. Hey - go click a stealth green hotspot over there, then press another key to "hide". it's worse than an early RTS with specialized keys and functions grouped together in nonsensical ways. Get detected? You are dead. And not insta-fail dead, but deluding you into thinking you might have a chance by firing off a few shots before getting 2-shoted and out. Once you get your squad it's no better. Your special abilities and functions are in buried in two separate menu/screens with combat actions in one, with a completely different ones than the context sensitive click on unit ones. Sprint? Sure, only until we feel like it. Want to cancel that stance/action? It's another esoteric key press. Hoping to sprint / hide in one smooth action? Nope, control is clunky and at worst detrimental to the brutal stealth mechanic. My squads in early 2000s RTS were be able to automatically adapt to their terrain. The "nearest" marine capable will perform n action leaving it impossible to maintain a strategy.Most things you'd want micro control over are automatic, so there's no sense of engagement, and those things that should be automatic, aren't. It's a confusing muddle mess with teams and units that never feel quite like they're listening or on their "A game" with pathing. Animations, voice acting, voice sync in cutscenes with laughably bad characters that can't quite decide whether they're a caricature or photo-real, failing on both counts.Having heard / seen outside of the tutorial from streams and other resources, you can tell there's a much bigger world out there other the mess fo the realtime mechanics - but hoo boy.  I am afraid to play it again lest I lose my ability to return this janky mess by running over the two hour mark.

_childDocuments_.review: Just once, I'd like to be able to recommend a game without a caveat. Sadly, this is not that game.The game itself is amazingly well thought out. Character advancement, class skills, storyline, mission pacing they're all fantastic. The game manages to evoke the horror of Aliens incredibly well, tied to soundtrack that's a brilliant homage to films. Here comes the but…. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, it’s filled with bugs and sadly the ones you can’t shoot with a pulse rifle are spreading. The latest patch made things noticeably worse for me. I’ve had to reload saves, leave missions and come back the following day so that an objective will activate. The worst one a quest that can’t be completed as there’s no interaction prompt for the log.I do recommend this, but at the moment my advice is hold off for now and wait until they fix more of the problems.

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved this game. The respect and love for the franchise is evident; It has all the interesting and captivating elements from the films while still being innovative in characters, story and new lore. I in particular loved how cinematographic the game is! The cutscenes are really cool and the way the gameplay tells you the story through tasks at each level feels also organically integrated for the narrative. The variety and fun of mechanics is in my opinion great game design. Customizing your marines gear, appearance and skills made me care for them and strategically think on how to specialize my team for mission success. The game amazed me on how well it captures the essence of the Aliens film. After playing colonial marines and fireteam I must say this game is the best on the vibe-essence because it captures perfectly both the action and horror aspects. In other games I felt unstoppable with the iconic pulse Rifle but in Dark descent you have to very often hide and select optimal routes. You have to be clever instead of generic action. Every time one of my marines were abducted and carried deep into the hive or they said one of the limited but powerful lines of panic as the iconic "game over" I felt empathy. Also the stress and trauma mechanic lowering your marines performance and the possibility to cure them with therapy was a interesting addition. Horrible too was that you can read the specific wounds affecting your marines and you have vissible effects as slow moving or poor shooting, or even they can get unconscious so you should assign other to carry them back to safety.Fighting hordes with Turrets, safely exploring the map using a drone, hacking doors for shorter paths, using silenced sniper rifles to avoid calling attention... that was super satisfying capturing the Tech part of the USCM. So, to summarize my opinion: This game is fun? Yes.  Has good lore? yes. Is a generic and forgettable use of license? no. Makes you feel like a USCM commander? yes.The game off course has some flaws. In particular it had bugs which i was surprised to experience as I supposed by now they should have fixed most. Sometimes the UI commands did not work, the camera became locked or unreal ungine crashed. Anyway these bugs were not at all a problem as reloading solved all. Also some scene dialogues felt generic or obvious and I think a better more natural and deep writing could have been done. In general I really liked the voice acting and cutscene quality so those meh parts were upsetting considering the great quality of most parts visually and narratively.Oh, also the Datapads similar to the Text logs in Isolation are worth reading! They have interesting data on the main story or more personal individual stories of persons in such a horrible franchise universe.I must say as a huge fan of the alien franchise I am very biased ahaha. If the game was awful I would have tried to find something good... fortunately this is not the case. I enjoyed a lot the game. Actually, this is my first Steam review!  It was so good I had to write a review.Aliens dark descent is the best game capturing the horror, action and strategy of the second film. It has the  Sci-Fi, distopic, biology-science, philosophical and ethical deepness and quality of good Aliens stories.I recommend it a lot for old and new Alien fans. I bought it on sale and feel the price-quality was very very satisfying. I inmensely appreciate all the work put by so many people into doing this amazing game.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent Game, had a blast playing it, felt so very much like being a colonial marine in the first 2 alien movies, they absolutely nailed the ambiance, and the world design with the blocky analogue devices and tech was straight out of the movies and was just excellent. Technically worked flawlessly but for some weirdo slowdowns on a couple sections of a level for some unknown reasons.Game mechanics worked exceptionally well, if a bit simple. The feeling it gave me was that it played a bit like Company of Heroes 1 squads, but in the Alien world. The game rewards a cat and mouse stealth gameplay a lot, and this is likely how you will end up playing, which may not be to everyone's liking, but it makes for a tense and exciting experience.The plot was okay, i am no alien lore expert but it felt like it followed the beats of aliens 1 and 2, transposed onto another ship, another planet and another crew, which worked just fine. The post end game part had me rolling my eyes a bit, but it still worked okay i guess.Overall a very enjoyable (if butclenchingly tense) experience, fully recommend for a different experience in the world of tactical squad rts.

_childDocuments_.review: A really well made X-Com like Aliens game, though the combat is not turn based but instead the core gameplay is real time tactics it still  very much has a lot of influence and elements from X-Com such a doom timer, a main base you upgrade stuff from between missions and other similar pieces,  alongside those it has its own original elements such as that all your marines are affected by mental stress which can cause them to perform worse in missions and even get psychological traumas overtime that need a psychologist to cope with or a special perk you get from levelling your marine.You control a set of 4 and later on 5 marines in a squad that moves together as a singular unit, though it works fairly well for the most part they should've made it so we can also have more individual control over each marine which would spare players from some occasional frustrations especially when attempting to be more sneaky because the game's squad system keeps positioning your silent sniper in awkward spot in the formation while you are attempting to silently take out a Xeno. So it would be nice if they are less glued together, something they should take in consideration for a potential sequel or maybe even an update in the future for this.When doing a mission you can EVAC any time you want, so if things are getting too out of hand such as supplies running low, marines too messed up or the game's dynamic aggression levels increased far too high for you in the mission you can get out of it and rest up your marines and prep a new team to continue the mission the following day. Any doors you opened or welded, any items you picked up, enemies you killed, progress you made will all get remembered the next time you get back there so being careless can be costly when you return for a 2nd or if needed 3rd deployment on the same mission. I managed to beat all of the missions with just 2 or 1 deployments on Normal difficulty and it was a pretty good challenge i must say, this is not an easy and forgiving game and medium strikes a good balance i feel personally but there are two more higher settings and also the ability to fully customise your difficulty, so if you perhaps don't like doom timers at all you can set it to so low it becomes basically a non-worry but perhaps you want the Xenos to be incredibly dangerous and you can then set them to very hard while setting resources to normal. There is also an ironman mode which limits you to two auto saves, while the regular mode lets you have about 10 ish auto saves, there is no manual saving per say outside of getting your marines inside a room, welding all the doors and hitting the "rest" button which heals their psychological statuses and gives other benefits alongside also saving the game.There is also stealth in the game and usually it's advised to keep yourself hidden as much as you can, however don't think you have 100% stealth the game, it's not designed in that sense and eventually some of the later missions you have to start engaging in combat some more. If you force yourself to stealth too much it can become detremential to your enjoyment, so use both stealth and combat in a smart way, just cause you got spotted doesn't mean that's it, you can still escape before more show up, hide, and distract enemies to pull them away to another part of the map. Utilising both stealth and combat together instead of soully focusing on just one is the best way to go.Visually majority of the game looks fantastic, the environments, the mood, the detail in said environments, lighting, shading, effects, weather and sound design are all stellar but the only thing lacking are the human faces and their facial animations which are very subpar. Story is fairly interesting, i wasn't expecting much out of it but i got a pretty engaging story involving alien cults which only the dark horse comics and some books explored in the past, though it feels some side characters very much didn't have enough time to really develop into anything since majority of the story is largely focused on two characters, so when some of the side characters perish you feel nothing as they were mostly just background noise often and not much else.- The aforementioned limited individual control of marines- The game is buggy, i didn't experience anything too crazy bad but i did have some lower and meidum sized problems , moments of Xenos just freezing up when they die, two times Xenos got stuck inside a welded door which made the door un-destroyable for them, i had the game once spawn an onslaught (horde) on a side of the map where they could not reach me, had a few times where a marine got stuck on a piece of the environment, one mission where you go down into some mines caused the game to randomly eat all of my RAM dipping my fps 1 but reloading the game fixed this issue, had one moment where my marines opened fire while in stealth for no apparent reason, - All missions are story missions, i was expecting there to be some non-story missions you can take on in between the story ones but there is not, all missions you jump into are story missions, those story missions have a good amount of side objectives to do and pretty large levels to explore, go through and approach in your own way, i just felt like i wanted also some non-story levels to do and complete for extra resources or other things- I wish the main base/ship had more things to upgrade and work on- There is a about 2 missions or maybe 3 that don't involve your actual squad mates but instead the main and side characters of the story and feel more like interactive story bits and not too much else, they stick out and should've not been done the way they did it honestly, would've been better if it was just a really long cut scenes rather or completely re-make those missions to involve your actual marines instead.- Performance is somewhat sketchy, not bad but not amazing it depends on the missions, some can have odd stutters, others run perfectly fine.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is good but not great. Theres' a lot of good, but also bad and ugly.The good:Great capture of the lore, story is sounding and interesting. Graphics are solid and a lot of effort was made in designing the game. Coming from XCOM TBS, I had doubts but the RTS (with slo-mo) system is FUN! The controls can be a bit funky at start but make more sense later as you get experience with them. I like how you operate as a single squad (downsides explained later) as you really need all the firepower you have to take down enemies. The command point system works really well and is an original mechanic. You really feel the confinement at almost any time and leaving indoors reliefs you from that feeling as you make a run to the ARC for safety. Long, really long missions. Interesting trooper development and level up. Music and sound fx are awesome. The bad:Level up system needs more freedom (eg class selection). Squad loadout menu is difficult, especially pre mission. Squad cannot split up which dumb down the tactical layer. I gave it positive critique earlier but as you progress in the game you get specialized classes which make more sense to split up which could offer more strategic layers in your missions. Cover system is pretty much useless. The ugly:Horrible tutorial integrated in story. Limited customization of troopers. Could use some more voice variety. I give it an 8 out o 10 all in all though i wouldn't pay over 30 bucks, for that price its reasonable what it has to offer. Game didnt max out its potential but maybe we see a sequel or DLC that improves upon the shortcomings.

_childDocuments_.review: 1 out of 5 Stars. Not Recommended. Absolutely suggest a Hard Pass on Aliens : Dark Decent. It's hard to over-emphasize just how much I hate this buggy, un-intuitive and poorly conceived game. Major issues ...Soft Lock Glitch : It's mission killing, random, no work-around. Restart the affected Mission if saved.Limited Save Slots : Yeah, your older saves will be overwritten. Save too much you can't restart missions.Bot Stress : Always goes up, but never goes down unless you use limited resources (Meds & Rest/Save).Resources : The entire game is one gigantic "Go For" game of consumable resource fetching ... pathetic.Difficulty : No matter what difficulty level you play, the game will increase it as you progress a mission, requiring Rest/Save & Withdrawals. It's not challenging, it's just deliberate Dev obstruction of progress.Story : Simple, trope-filled and predictable story that takes too many hours to advance between Swarms, Glitches, Gopher & Rest/Save. Anti-Player Dev-Team : To compensate for short story & poor mechanics, Dev's scripted Player failure in to some missions. Every sub-mission with Maeko will generally require multiple runs w/o cut-scene interruption. Just another example of Dev-Team's anti-Player Progress intent. Not challenging when mission rules change and opfor bots insta-spawn, insta-spot and insta-kill; it's just annoying. This Dev-Team sucks.Bot Squad : Dumb as a box of rocks. Sometimes will auto split party in to enemies & ignore attacks.*** Original Review Below ***The Developer's choice to use an isometric perspective was just bad and the bad development decisions just kept cascading from that baseline of bad. Controls and actions are awkward and often require multiple levels of menu depth. Aside from the actual glitches that were shipped with  the retail release, sometimes game progess can be stopped simply by the interaction of "squad" elements in the environment, due to poor pathing and cohesion.The never-ending resource hunt. In order to distract from a very short and simplistic story, the Dev-Team added the resource gathering sub-game to Dark Decent. Not only will you gather resources for your ship, the Otago, but you'll also need to constantly gather  sub-resources for your squad. Combined with an atrocious Inventory management system, the resource grind simply delays story-line progress.Game-play is dictated by the Dev-Team decisions and their poor scripting skills. The game deliberately punishes the player for non-stealth game-play with massive onslaughts almost guaranteed to result in a "Man down" condition. Even when the player conforms to the dev-team's preferential stealth mode the game mechanics consistently impede player progress with focused swarms that require significant idle time "hiding" to avoid. So, if you want to play fast you get hammered, but if you comply and play passive you sit and spin on your thumbs instead of playing the bloody game.The Bot Squad is too random and emo. The "squad" never operates at an optimal level, because the Dev-Team chose to add ridiculous random negative traits and assess performance penalties for any kind of contact, or even proximity to the Aliens which the squad is story-line trained to combat. Also, not only do you have to grind particular Bot Squadies to advance them, but you have to pay for each of their individual advancements with another kind of resource. again, the Dev-Team goal throughout Dark Decent seemed to have been to impede Player progress.Graphics and sounds are "meh". The isometric perspective, even when fully zoomed, features low-res modeling and VFX. The sound design is basic and nothing rises beyond that level to draw the player in to the moment. In fact, I quickly grew tired of the looped Bot soundbytes and the canned alien noises. Neither the graphics, or the sound help to immerse the Player in the story.The story is very trope laden and short. I suspect that if it were not for all the deliberate barriers to Player run-throughs the game's story could be completed in less than four hours of casual play. There just isn't much meat on the bones of the Dark Decent script. The voice acting is fair, but the rendered scenes are \unimpressive.You can find all the cut-scenes chronologically assembled for streaming and I would recommend you skip the game and just watch those story-line videos.I can't believe IGN rated Alien : Dark Decent 7/10, but ranked Alien : Isolation at just 5/10. NEVER TRUST IGN.I could go on, but you don't want to read it and I'm sick of typing about this terribad game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is freakin amazing!I picked it up over the weekend as it was on sale and honestly, I am surprised by how good it is. For us folk who love Alien, man - they have nailed the setting.Going in i expected a fairly decent tactical squad game, but the detail in the squad command, the handling of the squad, the combination of exploration and defending against the aliens, the use of the ARC, the fact the maps are persistent - it all works so brilliantly well. It also helps that they look stunning both indoors and out, full of interesting interiors. And the torchlight reveals for interactables is such a subtle, effective way to up the exploration element.Add to this the flavour of the marines, the injury systems, their appearance changes as they equip new gear or roles - it's just tick, tick, tick. And the damage systems - losing limbs, getting knocked out then dragged off, decapitations, face huggers, acid spray - it's got it all.I also love how with the map persistance, things like supplies dont grow on trees. Theyre quite costly to fit out marines and give this really balanced incentive to go back into maps looking for them. I've read the overall replayability is low but im hoping with time and the games success, more content is added or the game expanded.Sounding a bit fanboy frothy here, but kudos where kudos is due. The game is so much better than i anticipated. Massive kudos to the devs, you've made a killer Aliens game. There are a few small flaws etc but the overall experience is simply top notch.Was a big fan of Tindalos thanks to Battlefleet Gothic Armada 1 & 2 but yeah, this game is freakin fantastic.

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is fun but it really penalises you heavily for outright combat, so if you're looking forward to digging in and blasting some aliens, be prepared to suffer heavy penalties to stats and accrue trauma and wounds. Some of the mechanics aren't explained terribly well (like the consequences of infestation levels) and I find it frustrating that there's limited XP and finite missions in a single run. Once the game is done, you can't level up other marines and try other squad builds. One campaign does not provide enough XP to level two squads to maximum. NG+ is there, but you can only use it once and it's fairly linear. Though the gameplay is good, the game itself would benefit (in the longevity sense) from an endless mode, perhaps with RNG maps and objectives. The audio, the maps, and the story are all great if you're an Aliens fan. I do find the CONSTANT cutscenes extremely tedious, though. They aren't bad, they are just plentiful, frequent, and invasive. Prepare to have control of your camera taken away every few seconds, even right after a cutscene has just happened mere moments before. I find it a really puzzling and clumsy design choice, especially in contrast to how well thought out the rest of the game feels.

_childDocuments_.review: I did not see myself liking this as much as I did, but I did and I still do.I'm personally a fan of RTS games that promote your critical thinking, coordination and planning abilities above all else, and where this game excels the most is in situations where you're in a tight situation that forces you to adapt and coordinate accordingly.Generally speaking, this game will force you to manage your squad's health, stress levels, your resources (ammo, tools & medical supplies) as well as how much time you spend idling between missions. For some, this might be less enjoyable than it is stressful, but I think there's a particular sense of satisfaction that comes in executing a plan well rather than just throwing bricks at it until it works, which is what this game is mostly about.It also helps that the game has a pretty great artistic direction to it, focusing on gloomy atmospheres that make every level feel extremely desolate and dark, appropriate for the atmosphere of an Aliens title, and even more so when you consider the fact that you practically need to pay attention to your surroundings, because if you don't, you put your squad at risk of dying to a group of enemies you simply didn't catch in time to react to as they were wandering on the next half of the map.Great game, needless to say I would recommend this to any RTS enthusiast.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm on the fence with this one, wish steam had a neutral option.The game is a squad based RTS that lacks direction in my opinion. My reasoning behind that is the game very much wants you to go the stealth approach and avoid combat as much as possible due to the hunt mechanic that gradually starts ticking down whenever you've been spotted by an xenomorph.This makes the level harder due to more xenomorphs spawning and chasing you down. Now to avoid all of this you need to hide behind certain placed props, like crates, fence etc. This is where the problem comes in, for a game that pushes you to play this way, the stealth mechanics are lackluster to say the least. You can only hide behind certain select props, you can't even hide or take cover up against walls.Oh and the save feature is horrible, there is only an autosave that you can't specify the timing on, and there is no indication when it saves. The only reliable way I've found a way to save your game with is when you deploy your squad or when you spend materials to seal of a room when deployed, so your squad can rest. Other than that, the story is pointless, to keep it spoiler free, you trigger a quarantine in the prologue and then you spend the rest of your time trying to get off the planet Lethe.The artwork, atmosphere, and sound design are all good and in-line with the movies. The guns feel good, abilities are decent, graphics are meh... Nothing special. There's a few bugs I've encountered, like one of your marines can get stuck in the terrain, or when you loot a chest you don't get anything from it.Overall I had a pretty good time playing. it's hard, intense with perma death for your marines.6/10

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay really captures the industrial visual design and tense atmosphere of the second opus of the saga, James Cameron’s Aliens (1986). In nigthmare mode it manages to always keep your squad under deep pressure. Enemies may spawn everywhere, alien agressivity grows anytime you break stealth, soldiers get stressed and mad, to save and calm down you need to create a bunker within welded doors, when it becomes impossible you are forced to retreat to your ship but days are counted and can’t be spent blindly : you really get the sense of being overwhelmed by unforgiving horror of the movie (but with an overall irrealistic trend, since it’s possible to open a door in the dark with flashlights or stealth kill ten persons in a room without being noticing). On the artistic side, characters are bland and the story less humble than Alien : Isolation (in the aesthetic of Ridley Scott’s first statement). Cheap cultists already seen in so many games actually manage to control the creature (the movies are about the impossibility of doing so, even Alien Ressurection), and you get no sense of fighting an intelligent hive. The military system is taken too seriously, where James Cameron movie was an ironic criticism of a military hierarchy giving orders by radio and on-board cameras but incapable to react to a living and collective animal intelligence. The very last map is visually good but poorly used. All of that impedes the game pretention to be a new meaningfull addition to the Alien universe, but doesn’t reduce the pleasure you get to play it.

_childDocuments_.review: After what feels like an eternity, an Alien game has finally hit the market that masterfully captures the eerie atmosphere of the Alien movies and presents it in an interactive format. This game is not just another addition to the Alien game series, but it stands out for its ability to skillfully capture the creepy and terrifying flair that made the Alien movies so famous, offering players an immersive experience.It’s important to note that this game is not intended for those who simply expect impressive graphic splendor. It’s not about dazzling players with high-resolution textures and photorealistic environments. Instead, the focus is on creating an intense and captivating gaming experience that immerses players in the dark and threatening world of the Alien movies.Overall, this game is a refreshing change and a must for all fans of the Alien movies who want to experience the unparalleled feeling of horror and fear that characterizes the movies in a game. It’s a game that captures the essence of the Alien movies and offers players an unforgettable experience.
