_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Outstanding theme, atmosphere, gameplay and control. I'm an OG Aliens fan born in the 70s and this game blows me away. They nail the tension and survival-horror aspects of the movie 100%. Gameplay (once you get the hang of it) is intuitive and fluid. There are many 1st person Aliens games out there (going all the way back to DOOM: Aliens TC) but this is what I've always wanted. A tense, pensive, tactical squad-based game with resource management.Combat is fierce and satisfying. Setting up a killzone with sentry units and suppressive fire as a tsunami of xenos launch themselves at you is just insane. Boss battles are epic and very unforgiving. But aside from these moments, the game absolutely encourages you to stay quiet and undetected. If your marines are detected, they will stress. If they stress for too long, they'll be prone to shooting wild and/or using up more ammo. And if you run out of ammo, deep in the hive, far from extraction, game over man. Forcing the player to learn when to fight and when to stay quiet is one of the game's greatest strengths. Case in point: nervously checking your motion tracker for movement, seeing none, you enter a room and are terrified to see it is full of eggs - which are now opening. You now have two seconds to decide if you have enough time to quietly back away out of sight before a half dozen facehuggers hatch - or eff it launch a grenade to clear em out and wake the entire nest. You now have 1 second to decide. Absolute masterpeice game design.I have minor quibbles with a few things - there are still a few bugs (ha), and I think in some areas the balance can be tweaked. I'd personally love a Nightmare+ mode where saving is live (no reloading whatsoever) and the slow feature is not quite as slow. Also the squad based control is superb but occasionally I'd prefer more granular control. For instance, taking individual control of a recon unit to get into position for a snipe. It is clunky having to move 4 or 5 marines when all you want to move is 1.But these issues are very minor. The game is incredible and I cannot wait for future content.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Very solid game. I bought it on sale and it was worth it. It's not a AAA title and there are some bugs.But the gameplay is fun and the story is good enough to keep you on your toes :) I wish there were more maps and locations to explore and build the team, maybe with secret challenges, but well. It's okay for what it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Great tactical squad gameplay and a bit limited but good campaign management element combining Aliens universe game. Probably does not have a lot of replay value at this point but that might change in the future. There are some minor bugs and performance related issues during long gaming sessions but nothing too serious. If you liked games like Jagged Alliance, Xenonauts, UFO Aftermath/shock/light or Aliens universe then you're probably going to enjoy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: So, I had to quit the game and go to work, just to find out when I got home that it didn't save. Now I have to start the entire mission over. No thanks. Uninstalled. Stupid feature. Even Returnal found a way to allow "Suspend Cycle" (ironman mode saving) without allowing save scumming. Don't buy until they fix this.Also, you can't skip the tutorial.Save upon exit and allow a tutorial skip and I will thumbs this up.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Great mix of RTS and survival/horror gameplay. One of the freshest gameplay ideas I've played in years. Kinda feels like XCOM at points, but the RTS nature is significant. Also captures the feel of the license well. Would definitely recommend.Side note: I've encountered a few bugs that caused me to have to reload, but there have been several patches by now and that's happening a lot less now.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: The game is like a 7.5/10 from a purely RTS perspective. It definitely hits a certain itch and the dynamic gameplay keeps things fresh with the different spawn points for the aliens and the "being hunted" mechanic. Youll play the same mission and get into different engagements at different locations. Utilizing your sentry guns and your abilities is definitely fun and the resource management keeps things tense and provides some intense moments where you have to consider extracting off of the map early versus continuing towards your objectives.From a perspective of someone who enjoys alien it's probably a 7/10 as the RTS genre is pretty niche and the gameplay may not be the most fun for someone who enjoys the alien franchise as its gameplay loop is definitely the most unique out of every alien game thats previously been released.From the perspective of those who enjoy both the alien franchise and RTS games (me) the game is a solid 9/10 and I could not recommend it enough. It is 100% worth the purchase at full price. I purchased the game at an extreme discount as it has been on my wish list for a while and I wish I would have bought it and experienced the game earlier. The story isn't anything crazy but definitely has some interesting concepts, but the gameplay loop is definitely fun enough to keep you playing, but just the aspect of controlling a squad of marines with different classes and leveling them up to unlock new guns and gear is what really gets you attached to your squad. Definitely worth the purchase!
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a bit broken in a few ways (save bug on lvl 7, various issues with doors not working, squad members falling through floors, etc), but I absolutely love it. The Commando's-esque gameplay in the Aliens setting is a great match and there is arguably more of a decent narrative than there needs to be. The ability to keep the action slowed down while your marines are firing accurately, popping off special abilities, and plotting a path forward gives you the option to keep moving at all times instead of simply holing up and waiting for your marines to clear the horde. The eventual power accumulation of your squad may undermine the original Vietnam allegory of the Aliens film, but turning your Xenos-fodder-marines into a moving wave of lead-spitting-death is undeniably rad.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun, but not worth the 40 euro pricetag. What bothered me at some point were the mouths of the characters. The mouths of the characters in the cutscenes don't fit what the characters are saying. In the beginning this is hilarious, but after some while it gets annoying.. Wait for a sale. If you like xcum, you'll probably like this as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, I would recommend this game, especially if your a over head military type gamer.  Can whip through it in about 50hours or less on normal or easy. worth playing tho on harder difficulty. Auto-save is fine, manual save requires you to enter a room you can make safe, and rest, which is fine and cool. Med, tool, sentry and command points are simple to learn, balanced on finding supplies as you play through. I do feel the weapon selection could be expand more, only having 4-6 options on weapons, depending on class might even be less options.  Being able to come a go on the map during any mission is also neat, means your not required to finish what your doing if you wanna head back to main head quarters. Marine set up is good, decent start on customizing. It will take you awhile to level your marines up. I feel the skills and leveling could be a little more expended, but its a good start. I haven't run into any glitches or issues running the game, but my system wont have an issue, not everyone runs same system, it does require good graphics if u wanna enjoy it fully, the detail is great as you play through the maps. Will be excited when they allow it for SteamDeak. Good maps, not a bunch though. Would be neat if they came out with some side DLC that opens up more areas and more to the story. DON'T get me wrong though, story is great, ending i got a little annoyed with, but over all, great. If your a Aliens fan, this is a game you'll like, esp if you've play over head commanding games. I have no real negative things to say, i do like the game. There's potential in building more to this game and i hope the creators do that, Aliens is and always has been a story cash grab. Oh, 1 thing negative, the Marines repeat their comments a little too much and don't have many different things to say, feels like a broken record sometimes.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty good.  The most important thing in an Alien franchise game is it's atmosphere and immersion.  This game accomplishes them skillfully.  And it also is a pretty compelling tactical game that gets you feeling tense from start to finish.  It's not perfect, but what it accomplishes is pretty great. Worth a buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Looks great for this kind of game! Have never played x-com due to not being interested in the goofy setting or  their version of turn based combat, but I'm enjoying this quite a bit. Recommend if you enjoy the Alien universe or want to try out a unique real time strategy game that focuses on methodical room clearing, navigational challenges, and thinking on the fly when the aliens come to play all to the backdrop of excellent environmental art.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: I changed my mind on this game. Initially I was disappointed and irritated by the mechanics. Sometimes there was a deadly delay in orders being followed and it led to frustrations.I made myself push through and underneath is a story rich (I enjoyed it) RTS here. There is so much more that COULD be done with it. Adding deeper RPG like elements would increase immersion. Having more influence about what ship parts to repair or develop would be fun. Having a system of rank which actually makes a difference to squad cohesion etc would be awesome. That said, what is there is enough to enjoy and play through.It does require a reasonable amount of trial and error at the beginning and some of the frustrations remain but in general, I do recommend this game as a fun and engaging RTS.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: This game is essentially Alien Survivors and it's already is one of my favorite games of all time. Dark Descent improves upon Vampire Survivors by requiring you to be smart with your strategy & tactics. Otherwise, you'll never survive the legitimately scary and capable enemies. You also get good 3d graphics, and an immersive narrative/world-building. What more could you want out of a Survivors-style game.My only complaint is that there are still some bugs where one of your squad may get knocked down, but because they got knocked down in some odd location, you aren't able to get to them to revive them. I've had to restart from last save several times because this happened.I would also love it if the developers explained a bit more about the logic used by the prioritization system. When you click on an item or do an action, the priority system automatically selects the right marine for the job. This works right 95% of the time, but sometimes it picks the worst person for an action and I'm left without a critical skill. For example, I only equip one marine with the pulse rifle with underslung grenade launcher. If they are busy doing an action, I lose that capability and it's killed me on more than one occasion. As I said, the system works right 95% of the time but it would help if I understood the system better so I could be smarter in those tense moments.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game. Maybe not GOTY predtender but still very entertaining and faithful to second Alien movie athmosphere, probiding lots of lore for those who like such things. During my 34h playthrough I did not encounter any bugs. Any inconveniences were results of choosing to operate whole squad as single entity.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Once, a woman whom I was dating (and whom I didn't particularly like), told me that she may be pregnant right before I got on a flight, and told me she'd have the results of a pregnancy test after I landed. During that flight, the plane flew into a massive tropical storm.  And the city I was flying to had a volcano erupt near it.  And the government had a coup, leading to civil unrest.  And then the plane started running low on fuel.  This flight was *less* stressful than a session of Aliens: Dark Descent. When your squad of marines starts off with negative traits, then experience intense stress, suffer wounds, encounter exhaustion and then develop full-blown trauma, you realise you may have a game that hates you as much as a woman who lies to you about a pregnancy before you get on a turbulent flight to a chaotic destination.  But you know what?  You still stick with that woman.  Because that's what you do.  Because you clearly don't have enough stress in your life.   Peace and calm is for wusses.  We're in the colonial marines now, bub.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Already Finished it!TLDR: You like the Alien license? You like X-COM? Then you will love this game!Is it like X-COM? No! But it takes a lot of ideas from it and does something different to keep it fresh.The game has some jank here and there, sometimes I was going mad and had to load very old saves to bypass some softlocks, but patches will iron them out I am sure.Other than that: Absolutely nailed the atmosphere, sounds, music, feel of the movies. The gameplay loop was great and you are free to do whatever you want. The ending was a bit disapointing (kinda fits the universe)... but lots of questions never got answered. Probably setting up for DLC or sequal? Either way, it was a good time and I can't wait for more.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic! It’s extremely well made, with a great story and amazing graphics. it’s the whole package. Took me around 30 hours to finish the campaign, and if you’re into RTS games, this is a must for you.Having said that, it’s no walk in the park. Every session felt like work, and I needed breaks to recover. The death clock mechanic didn’t bother me much, maybe I just got lucky the way I played it since I had more than 18 days left. Had I known about this before starting the campaign, maybe I would have played it differently... Maybe I would have spent more time on the side quests to max level my marines before the death clock kicked in.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Worth your time and money, especially on a sale. This one gives you what you want from an X-COM style game, but you get the aesthetic of ALIENS horror, in a real-time rather than turn based set of rules. It's game play loops through waves of suspenseful exploration, into bouts of extremely high stress preparing, fighting and maybe running!Beautiful level design, interestingly you play on each level multiple times, there's set objectives and you extract at any point, able to go back in if your marines are too shook up. The squad and your marines really grow on you, their roles unique and balanced enough to want them all different specialisations.It's a decent story that has you exploring a different aspect of ALIENS lore, focused on the dark side of Weyland-Utani's experiments in the colonies, where they have a lot of power.A fun, sometimes spooky adventure in the ALIENS universe. Friends reading, buy on sale if you like ALIENS and RTS.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Unique spin on the xcom mechanic, the combat is more dynamic and interesting than its spiritual descendant but I did find the character upgrading to be lacking...immersive and thematically very strong, the game play loop is also addicting and difficult to stop playing...if you're a fan of xcom or the aliens movies then it's a lock that you will like this, there are a few technical issues but didn't hasn't stopped my enjoyment so far
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting game like a mix between alien swarm and XCOM.Good cinematic. story is intriguing. Atmosphere is on spot. The best about this game is like you are watching a movie.This is a difficult game. I played on medium, one lvl above the lowest, story mode level, and I have to constantly load my save just to finish the mission.Tutorial is extensive, but stretched too long. I am writing this review when I am at atmospheric processor, 4th or 5th mission, 21hr in, and I am still getting tutorial of new mechanics. Just teach them all at once at the first mission.RTS combat is tense and demanding because everything is permanently limited. Ammo, tool, med kit, squad HP, time and squad's metal is continuously deteriorating. Combining with some questionable design and balance, the whole game is insanely difficult and almost unplayable without save scumming.Med kit and tool you can decide how much you bring to the field, but one marine only bring one of each max, in and out of mission. While med kit are only for heal and reduce stress, tool are for decrypting door, weld door, repair sentry gun, repair synth, reveal map, tactical analysis.Tools are needed for so many essential game mechanics.You need to weld door to create shelter for rest to reduce stress. Do not understand why cannot rest on the ARC but you need to weld 1 or more door to create shelter to rest to reduce stress for 100 points. If you wanna reduce another 100, you need to break the door, find another room and repeat the process again. Using more than one tool, but stress build up can be insanely fast and sometimes the mission or story necessitate build up of stress. Moreover, not every room can be shelter. So, if there is a whole area with only 1 shelter room, you can only save at that room and that could mean hours of progression between save and it is just annoying when you searched rooms after rooms and corner after corner and hours after hours just to lose all progression.You need door decryption to enter certain rooms for resources and reveal map. Each encrypted door cost one tool and each floor cost another one to reveal. So if you wanna enter one encrypted room and unlock map for 2 floor, you are already using 3 tool right away and you can only bring max 4 into the field and the site usually have less then 10 tool.You need to repair the sentry gun and synth first in order to bring the sentry home. Each broken sentry requires one tool. So if you bring 4 sentry and the alien got lucky and damaged 2, you may find yourself not able to bring back 2 sentry gun because the whole map does not provide this number of tool or you need those tool for other purpose like rest or reveal map.All in all, you have many many essential usage tied to one single consumable which is very very few and permanently limited. This forbids use of game mechanism for real strategic plan like welding doors to stop alien patron from entering because you are always having those tool for other purposes and those purposes are almost always unsatisfied with the number of tool you have.On the other hand, med kit is on a fair spot or even cold. Sometimes you feel like you have excessive of these kits. I have 15 in base and 4 or 5 on mission site. They are not usually needed if things go smooth. If things go bad, you don't need them either because your squad of marines are going to die or loss consciousness very rapidly and you can only bring them back to base by then.The game makes you control a squad of 4 marines as a whole unit and your marine will do your task automatically. However, the things is their A.I. is not always what you desire. First, the choice of marine may not be desirable. Example, AI ask a marine with mine to open a chest or set a detector, but you want to lay a mine at the same time. You request multiple actions and AI ask one marine to do everything making the process very long. Second, the action they take. One notable dislike is your marine always run to do your action but they will slowly walk back to the squad when the action is done making them an vulnerable target to be spotted or capture. This also makes you difficult to control as everyone may be scattered around the room and slowly walking.Campaign and Base gameplayThe game has you on a clock of level of infestation and this clock go real fast because you only have one deployment per day. Marines easily wounded and the period of wound can go up to 7 days, and they have tired and exhausted effect each cost 2 days to recover, and they have psychiatric therapy to go through which may take 3 days to complete. Intensive training causes exhausted after you take them out of intensive training, so 2 days no mission. The worst thing is the new day event when the player start next day. 2 options for each event, do or don't, and most of the time do event will have 2 outcome, successful or fail. On my play through, though not finished, I encountered 3 times the event of marines loss hope and you either give a speech so all marines may either get rid of tired or exhausted if successful or become exhausted if failed or guarantee losing a deployment next day. I chose speech for 3 times and for 3 times all my marines became exhausted for 2 whole days meaning no deployment for 2 whole days, unless some marines have the mind of steel perk that grant them immune to tired. By the time I write this review, I have only done 4 or 5 mission but I am already on infestation level 3 because the game keep giving me events that skips my deployment. It gives me plenty of time to heal my marine but not by my strategic choice.EnemiesThere are human enemies in this game and they are bullet sponge. Like even non-augmented human enemies takes multiple shots to down and they come in groups. This is extremely annoying because ammo is very limited in this game, Adding on the human walk among alien ♥♥♥♥ in this game story, difficulty easily raised because you can easily run out of ammo and die without ammo. The game did tell you to extract freely to fight another day, but given the fact that you may need multiple days to get one deployment and there is an infestation level ticking, time is limited and every deployment counts. The player do not really have the choice unless the squad is actually unable to fight anymore.The alien AI is the single most factor that makes this gameplay not enjoyable for me. Mission length is not infinite. The game have this alien awareness meter and hunt cycle. Alien detection causes aliens in the region to hunt you and the hunt cycle last for a period of time even all of them died, For the duration, the awareness meter keeps going up and eventually trigger onslaught and awareness increase and spawn of category 2 alien. When the awareness reach hard, the mission became very difficult because many alien will spawn at once and spawn almost constantly covering the whole area. Fighting them is possible but amount of ammo does not sustain that. While the game encourages you to do stealth, the stealth mechanism is bad. Most mission site consist of corridors and Other than sleeping aliens and eggs, overcharging detector causes the alien to go straight to the detector literally. They may sometime go right the room where squad is hiding because the room is in between the alien and the detector. Sleeping aliens are another issue. They are not waken by sound but by visual. Kill them  triggers hunts if not using command skill silent precision shot, but only recon class has it. Stay in their line of sight triggers them and your squad is almost guarantee dead if the player try to stealth but failed because the squad is surrounded by multiple alien usually when triggered.Worst of all, alien moves unpredictably. They can move fast and know exactly where the squad are even not being hunted.The game has some new things for the genre but it is on the harsh side and can be real frustrating most of the times.Try on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Since my first review of this dumpster fire of a game I have played a bit more of it and things were going okay until encountering a hive/Xeno queen......how exactly is that even a balanced thing??? Most of your squad/Marines are going to all be rookies they'll all come with either cowardly or scum something like that which doesn't exactly define success now does it?? May as well throw strategy out of the window because there really is no "strategy" involved in whatever this game is trying to be, so if you love all things Ridley Scott related just stick with the movies from the first one from 1979 Alien and on through the AVP movies because this game is the dumbest thing I've ever seen. _childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a bit of a mess. It's much more of a stealth game than I was expecting, and not a very good one. Including instant death mechanics. The bad autosave just makes it even worse. For instance, the game autosaves BEFORE a cutscene, then it places you in a very difficult stealth section where you'll have to repeat it several times. Then when you retry you have to watch the cutscene again beforehand. The first time I saw the cutscene I enjoyed it, but by the third time I'd learned to hate it. The game doesn't have any tools or abilities you can use to help, such as throwing an item to draw the alien away. You'll end up crouching behind something so it doesn't see you as it slowly walks towards you and there's nothing you can do. If you don't move it will find you, if you move it will find you. And then you'll have to watch a cutscene before you can try again. The game is very disappointing, I didn't make it through the prologue.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: This is actually a good game, that needs to be said up-front. It's a truly unique strategy game, it feels like playing an Aliens movie in the best way possible, the levels are gorgeous with the amount of detail in them and it's fun. And it's a little bit scary actually! They made a scary RTS! That's a huge accomplishment.But the bugs are the absolute worst bugs I've encountered in a game in years. These are aggravating, swear-inducing, progress-eliminating, fun-killing bugs and they're all over the place. These are not glitchy textures or weird lighting, these are bugs that made me swear in frustration.I have only had a single crash, but most of these bugs create a situation where you must reload a save which is almost as bad as a crash as far as I'm concerned.You only save the game after level-transitions, Resting in a locked room or after certain objectives. Except, I couldn't save after resting on one particular level. Some bugs you encounter are only fixed after reloading. Sometimes a marine will get stuck "interacting" with something forever. They run around and can interact with objects, but they can't shoot, be healed or use skills so they're useless until you reload. Sometimes a marine gets stuck inside of an object and they're useless for the rest of the mission. Reloading DOESN'T fix that unless it's a save from before they got stuck. The robot drone that one of your classes can get gets stuck ALL THE TIME and is not worth reloading to save.Getting spotted by an alien changes the dynamic of the game. You mostly never want to be spotted. Sometimes aliens spot you instantly. Sometimes your marines open fire on an alien before it has spotted you. Sometimes aliens spawn inside of a vent that you are walking next to and spot you instantly. Sometimes you are locked in a cutscene and an alien will wander into it, so that when you pop out of a cutscene it spots you.Oh and soft-locking because objectives won't trigger! Pick up an item and use it on an objective? Game sometimes says you never picked it up, better reload. Move into an objective room? Game's stuck on previous dialogue, will never give you a new objective.Sometimes you can do an entire 2 hour mission and not one bug comes up and you feel like you just did an entire Aliens movie and it's sick as hell. Sometimes you replay the same 20 minute segment 4 times because Sargent Rueiz can't use his arms and your previous save is from mission start.The frequency of these bugs is sometimes multiple-times per mission. It's infinitely frustrating. There is such a good game underneath all of this but it feels like I'm being trolled. Like someone took this good thing and made it worse on purpose? And It's so much more frustrating because the game IS good but these bugs muck it up!I cannot recommend anyone buys this until they've done like 3 bug-fixing patches. It IS a good game. When it works. So wait for it to work.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Overall Aliens Dark Descent is a pleasant game. So far it is something new in the genre - a mix of real time XCOM in the Alien Universe. It plays great, its easy to get into and the atmosphere is very nice.BUT there is one thing that completely destroys the game: the lack of a proper save.In this game you pretty much have to weld your team inside a room in order to save. What that means is, you have to collect resources inside the map to be able to weld a room. You either need 1 or multiple resouces for that. Those resources are limited and are also used for other actions like quick abilities, revealing maps, etc. So not only do you have to use your resources to save a game, you have to find a proper room to do so and be clear of all threats. In almost all maps it will take quite a bit of time to aquire and find a weldable room. That means, you CAN NOT save whenever you want and not leave the game whenever you want. If you do, you have to start over from the last save which, in many cases, can set you back by a lot. The welding mechaning and letting your marines rest is awesome on its own (if it would function correctly, since in a lot of times it is bugged where you have to use double the amount of resources) but only having this mechanic to save is beyond me.Until they at least give a more friendlier save option and get rid of the incredibly annoying bugs even multiplying this annoyance, I unfortunately have to let it sit at negative since it sucks every fun out of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Captures the aesthetic and atmosphere of the movie. Simple controls, yet many things to think about. Good variety of tasks and missions. Decent cut scenes, also can be skipped. Visuals are good. Some base and inventory management.Rename and customise your marines. Lacks voice options, but the voice acting is of a decent quality. You get an APC

_childDocuments_.review: Good tactical game that manages to stay true to the Aliens expected action. There's a strong "boardgame feeling" in the game design, but it's not a bad thing :)I like how it doesn't get complicated for nothing while still providing interesting tactical challenges.I especially like level resource persistency (what you consume, and what you do remains) and how you are the one deciding at any time when to extract and come back another day to finish the mission.It leads to interesting decisions and tense moments when maybe you decided to push it a little too far...and are now facing stressing moments retreating to your closest evac point with limited resources and some barely alive marines. Good game :)
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: We all know what the best Alien game is, but this is definitely the best Aliens game. I've never played a tactics game that feels so intense! Only a couple of missions in so far but everything here is very impressive and captures the feel of the 2nd film very well. I was surprised there's actually a stealth system to try and sneak around them and plenty of options to try and hold your ground when it hits the fan. Also surprised by how good the story is so far! Feels like a plot from something like one of the Dark Horse comics and voice acting is really solid. Hats off to the composer as well, nailed the Aliens sound and plenty of new marching/brass themes. Thanks for the ultrawide support as well!
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent game. It really captures the tone and feel of the original Aliens film. Leading your squad through dark corridors filled with xenos is tense and, at times, frantic but very satisfying. I'm a long time fan of this series, and this is the best video game in the series since Alien: Isolation.Others mentioned technical issues. _childDocuments_.review: From a gameplay standpoint, Aliens: Dark Descent (ADD) is an interesting creature. In many ways it is a Tactical RPG: You have a squad that, overtime, levels up and obtains specialized roles. Each mission brings in resources that you can use to upgrade their equipment, etc, etc. What makes it interesting is the systems you have to manage for your squad in real-time: in addition to Health and Armor, you have Stress and Trauma. Stress is a quantitative measurement of a Marine's progress to the next Trauma, and a Trauma is a negative status effect (ex: Increased stress when using a flamethrower, increased ammo usage, decreased accuracy, etc). Traumas can be short-term, which go away as soon as the stress is relieved, or long-term, which take many in-game days to go away.Basically, ADD acknowledges that fighting Xenomorphs comes at a cost to ones mental and physical fortitude: The more pressure you put on your marines through combat, the higher their stress goes, the higher their stress goes, the more likely they are to experience both short term and long term traumas. This brings an element to the game that I have yet to encounter in other TRPGs, because you're presented with a system that actually favors avoiding combat where possible to save your strength, so the combat you can't avoid can be done efficiently.From a story standpoint, this game definitely had me hooked. While the setup is one we've seen before: Marines isolated on a planet with Aliens, Tindalos wanted to give this a lot more intrigue to keep the player interested, as . Tindalos also did a spectacular job of incorporating story components from the Aliens Extended Universe, and creating some really good story moments that make this feel to Aliens what Alien: Isolation felt for the original Alien.All-in-all, I strongly recommend this game. Like any TRPG, there is a learning curve here, but once you figure out the gameplay systems, it really does a good job of keeping you engaged as you build out your team. It is really rewarding when you finish a mission cleanly as well!EDIT: After 100+ hours, still love this game. Although the last level is a bit of a gimmick, the trip to get there was a blast each playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: Aliens: Dark Descent is a squad based real time strategy game that can be described as a cross between "Colonial Marines" with "XCom". What sets this game apart from other representatives of the franchise is that "Dark Descent" first and foremost strives to be a faithful adaption of  J. Cameron's 1986 Aliens movie, rather than just another representative of a gaming genre in an Aliens dress up.As such, it assembles aspects from a whole slew of genres under its umbrella: horror, stealth, tactics, resource management as well as frantic action! And it works! Despite presenting itself from a top down perspective, the dense atmosphere had me sucked in very quickly, and I'm glad to say that the subtle hammering of the motion tracker has lost none of its potency when it comes to creating tension.As for the Xenomorphs, they are handled very close to their movie counterparts.A single Alien is hardly a threat to a squad of Marines with Pulse Rifles, but a whole bunch of them can overpower you very quickly, if you are not prepared for their onslaught.In order to be able to stem the tide, the game provides you with all the beloved toys from the USCMC arsenal: Pulse Rifles, Grenades, Flame Throwers, Shotguns, Smartguns and, of course, everyone's favorite: the Sentry Gun!In other words: fans of the movie will feel right at home.With all that firepower at your disposal, one would think that you could simply shoot your way through every mission. Well, you could in "theory", but it is a really bad idea.As a matter of fact, you want to avoid combat as much as possible, and the reason for that is due to limited resources and the implementation of two mechanics: "stress damage" and "the hunt".Whenever an Alien spots you, it will alert others to your presence. Make enough noise, and the whole hive will awaken.Getting chased relentlessly will take a toll on your squad's stress level until your soldiers reach their breaking point and go nuts.While the game offers ways to mitigate stress and the negative effects that accompany it, you always want to pick your fights carefully; even as your soldiers level up and become stronger and more resilient.In short: Dark Desscent is probably the best and most authentic "Aliens" experience out there, so if you liked the movie at all, you really should check this game out.

_childDocuments_.review: Dark Descent is to  what Isolation was to .It's faithful to its source material in terms of both theme and gameplay.I especially liked how this game restores the Xenomorph to an extremely threatening position.  Whilst other games in the franchise tend to make the monstrous creatures less imposing, the titular aliens in this game put your squad in constant (and very real) mortal peril.I really loved having to work with the stress mechanic. The marines are tough, but they sure as hell aren't fearless.  Fighting the aliens harms the mind just as much as it does the body.  As their stress mounts further and further, each marine will begin suffering debuffs, such as shakey hands (worsening their aim), or confusion (hampers your ability to use special commands).  If they're stressed out enough, they'll begin developing traumas, such as paranoia (stress increases when in large squads), depression (starts out with increased stress) or an assortment of phobias (stress increases when nearby certain things).You have the ability to customise your marine's appearance, and they each feel unique thanks to certain personality issues and tendencies they can have.When you inevitably get attached to certain marines, this game will not shy away from making you watch them die horribly.  They can get burned by acid, gunned down by human opposition, or torn apart by Xenomorphs.  Your squad can get facehugged, heabitten, or put into comas.  One of my marines had his arm torn off, and had to be fitted with a prosthetic once he was carried back to medbay.  You can't manually save, either, and instead the game autosaves at various points, so if something goes horribly wrong, you may simply need to accept it and move on, or surrender a considerable amount of progress.  I think this decision was one of the games biggest successes.  You need to plan carefully, act wisely, and think things through, because your actions have serious, long term consequences.The game also expands on the  universe wonderfully, and it's absolutely rich with new lore, whilst staying perfectly authentic to source material.  As a big fan of the franchise, I could tell the developers were, too.The gameplay struck a very good balance between simple and complex for me.  There was no need for micromanagement of each squad member, but this did come at the cost of some strategical options.  You can't split up, the squad moves as one at all times.  This means you're limited in positioning and manoeuvering, but there are generally workarounds to get certain marines in certain positions away from one another.Despite an array of weaponry at your disposal, none of your combat options wind up obsolete.  Skills from the early game still have many uses after you unlock late game equipment.  These tools, when combined with the ability to open up and block off paths, focus suppressive fire on certain areas, and set up defensive perimeters at your own discretion, the combat of this game is exciting and challenging.  If you're caught unprepared, it's a struggle for your life that you're likely to lose, but if you strategise and plan ahead, you can take control of the situation, and come out (relatively) unscathed.You'll be playing defence far more frequently than offense in this game, and actually, your best bet is to simply sneak around and avoid conflict as much as possible.  Your marines truly do face a dark descent through hell, and I'm all here for it!I appreciate the application of Xenotech in this game.  It gives you something to do with all the corpses, for one, and offers a grounded exploration of the use these creatures may have to Weyland Yutani.Much to my surprise, the plot and characters of this game had me engaged throughout.  While it isn't anything incredible, I felt compelled and interested in the story and wanted to progress it.If that was all, I'd give this game 5 Stars, but despite my enjoyment while playing it, and my fondness for this franchise in general, Aliens: Dark Descent has a serious problem.  It is absolutely riddled with bugs (not the space kind) and glitches that vary between comical to game breaking.  Fact is: if you play this game, you will encounter bugs.  If you're lucky, they'll cause you some mild annoyance.  If you're unlucky, they'll set you back a couple hours.  Plenty of bugfixes have been rolled out, but the game is still plagued with them.  On numerous occasions I was forced to load earlier saves due to glitches ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ me over. Sometimes something would happen, and I wouldn't be sure if it was an error or not, like strange pathfinding, AI, and inconsistent command responses.  In the end, I found myself having to use exploits and oversights to even the odds against a game that sometimes did not work.Unlike many other modern games, which are fundamentally flawed, Aliens: Dark Descent has a  chitin solid foundation, and a lot swinging in its favour.  I have confidence that after a few more rounds of thorough bughunting, this game can truly meet its potential.  I'm holding out hope that an expansion will come soon, with a set of brand new missions and challenges to overcome!

_childDocuments_.review: It's decent enough, but falls short of its potential. I've spent many hours playing XCOM 2, which this game at least somewhat has to compare itself against.First and foremost, the game severly lacks variety. Every mission plays nearly identically, and none of the unlocks with perhaps the exception of the flamethrower have the ability to alter the gameplay significantly. In XCOM 2, every loadout item counts, and appropriate use can save your bacon.The game also has a bunch of bugs that I ran into. Several times the stress meter bugged out at stress+++, eventually filling out the stress meters on my entire squad forcing me to reload. I also got soft-locked once during the tutorial. I've also had issues with ultrawide support, which would consistently break after taking refuge in a room. These are apparently not new, which suggests a lackluster post-launch support by the developers.Possibly the most annoying aspect of the game is the sound bites. Some of them are cringe-worthy on their own, but the constant repetition is infuriating. Some also don't make sense - if you send your squad to hide behind cover, they slowly walk towards it, and then have an out-of-breath quip about how they took cover.Music itself is mixed strangely at times, occasionally missing entirely giving a weird quietness to menus.The game would have benefited from an xcom-esque world map where you can choose side-missions as they pop up. Instead it's very railroad-y.I'm rambling. I guess at the end of the day I had fun, but I'm not going to replay it.

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommended.Let me start by saying that I'm just happy that for once a game in this day and age isn't completely broken on launch, I'm playing on ultrawide with all settings at max without issues (AMD CPU, nVidia GPU), I've so far only encountered 2 issues (and I'm on the 3rd location):Occassionally the marine pathfinding gets stuck to/from long route tasks, very easy to resolve.There's a significant fps drop if you got "hide" enabled while in cover and then start moving without disabling "hide", as if the game then keeps checking every little piece of cover to see if you're using it.For 40 euros it's a good game, I've leveled a few guys, unlocked a few upgrades, progressed through the story, stopped an abduction, lost a marine, had a marine lose a limb, found out how OP the silenced sniper is, the list goes on.I am quite anoyed with the bad traits that marines get, I feel like the in-game stress is enough of "marine management", then ontop of that after a mission they get tired and if you bring them anyway they'll get exhausted, and for trauma they need to go to the psych ward several days or suffer permanent debuffs that keep getting worse, hopefully we'll see a mod that just straight up removes in the near future or at least makes them less of a headache.Graphics-wise I'd say it's okay, the effects are pretty decent, but textures sometimes look like a 6 or 7 out of 10 quality, like the marines or the enemies if you zoom in too much.The real content-complaint I'd have is the voice acting, of the marines, of the enemies and the story folk, they all sound so B-tier and it doesn't help the squad or tactical guy tell you to "stop camping" every 30 seconds even though you're in cover to hide from a passing patrol, also hope there will be a mod to reduce the frequency and volume of those specific voicelines.I was also worried about the "End of campaign timer" that some games have these days and which I hate, I don't mind timers on like optional stuff where you get rewarded for getting there on time, but having a senseless timer just to create a false sense of urgency is just rubbing me wrong, luckily the game allows you to tone that setting down even if you want to put the rest of the difficulty at max.All in all though, the gameplay loop is solid and fun, if ♥♥♥♥ gets too hard you can always just bail, because the world and team are persistent, so you can just come back and finish the mission with a new squad or even to loot any buildings you know you left items in due to running out of space (just don't bring anything on missions, that way you can bring more back to the base).If you like Aliens and if you like RTS or you liked XCOM2, then this is a very easy recommendation, especially considering they priced the game to it's quality (not like those games that launch like trash but charge you 70 dollar).

_childDocuments_.review: Aliens Dark Descent, what a gem of a game into the Alien Franchise so to speak.The game itself is often referred to "XCOM" which is far from same. The only XCOM like element is the UI screen in your base of operations, otherwise, it is very much it's own game.The mechanics involve squad based stealth, management, real time action based combat, where every decision counts. You have a plethora of resources to manage, right down to your marines ammunition.Do you reload that sentry turret? Or do you pass up and keep some mags for your marines smartgun? Do you launch a grenade to kill those 2 drones entering the same room as you? Or do you let them by as you sneak around them, allowing you to save ammo, not stress your marines or alert the hive causing a hunt to be launched for your detection?The implementation of the squad based system works and as hybrid as it is, there are few games that have done it correctly. Think Dragon Age to a degree which is a more accurate reflection of the combat.If you are a fan of the Alien IP and movies, you will absolutely appreciate the art, asthetic, sounds, right down to the squelching of your marines boots going over a hive growth. They inspiration taken from the franchise is apparent with the APC being utilised as ground command vehicle, which you can use to transport your marines around a map where applicable and it can defend a location or attack on the move.Gameplay wise, there are a few bugs I have encountered, one of which is quite disruptive however, overall, absolutely would recommend and I am sure they will address those in the near future. Definitely meets the price point for the time you get out of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Had to come back because this had one of the worst endings and ending sequences to a game I have ever played in my entire life, made me genuinely wonder if I had brain damage.Tbh I actually wanted to leave a positive review but I feel like the rating is way too high for this currently. Its a decent game, the atmosphere and world building is good, but the gameplay can fall flat. The idea of having the squad be loosely controlled is fun in theory but can be incredibly frustrating if the AI makes poor choices, sometimes coming off as a halfbaked xcom rather than a fully priced game. It makes up for this with the real time combat being tense and somewhat scary in portions but the stealth mechanics are awful to work around and mandatory which almost counterbalance this completely. The consequence for failing the stealth isn't a cool fight, its usually a reload, the game keeps your resources scarce to make your combat feel important but this just leads to you being unable to handle substantial threats beyond essential encounters. I had times where I would fight my way to resupply at an armoury only to realise I had lost more ammo getting there than the three mags the game would give me. It tries to make up for this by allowing you to leave and redeploy with new marines and supplies whilst keeping progress, you will rarely do this however. Marines take ages to heal, you need to wait a full day to redeploy and there is an enforced timer on completing the game in a certain number of days. Whats meant to be risk reward becomes save scumming awkward stealth being more viable than playing the fun portion of the game. At a 50% discount the value is there but at full price it feels fairly buggy and also quite repetitive. The xeno AI can be even worse than the marines, the praetorian especially goes from scary stalker to roving schizophrenic pretty quickly. The voice acting for a game like this tends to be low quality but the cut scenes are quite well done, however the in mission lines are INCREDIBLY repetitive due to how many actions you will be making in a real time RTS mixed with low sample numbers.My biggest complaint comes back to the save scumming. The fact its sold in this tactical strategy form when in actuality you will spend a LOT of time reloading saves due to weird difficulty spikes, random bugs or mission events being INSANE and completely unpredictable isnt fun. Rarely will it feel like your fault that something has gone wrong and more that the game screwed you for minimal reason, you'll always be pressing the "Prepare for this event, its gonna kill you" button in a mission, finding out what it does and then preparing for what you now know is going to happen. Because these range from locking you in a random room, spawning a queen to just mass swarming you from everywhere all of which require VERY different strategies. Imagine opening a door expecting to face the big baddie so you set up all your turrets, then a cut scene plays, your marines walk in and leave all of the gear behind and it catches fire so you're fighting 300 runners alone.Honestly there's a lot more small complaints I could make but if you're willing to put up with its clunky nature the experience is worth it at a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: Aliens Dark Descent is an over the top real time strategy game where you control a single Colonial Marine fireteam of four (five once upgraded) into the depths of a planet reminiscent of the movie Aliens (1986). There is many set pieces that look straight out of the movie and many references to the classic films. Featuring many features from marine customization including renaming of your marines and a class, trauma, stress, trait and leveling system. The game forces you to think and make quick decisions to survive the Xenomorph infestations on the planet Lethe where you have crash landed. Prepare to lose marines as you descent into darkness to complete various missions on many different levels. You need to get this game it's worth every single cent and does the Aliens franchise license justice!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: A very nice survival strategy game that comes very close to the movie experience and enhances it with well thought-out gameplay mechanics new to the genre and generally well written and directed cutscenes. In mission, I'd say this is a very decent experience, although the 'base management' could have been elaborated on, as it does not nearly come close to the big inspiration that is XCOM: 2 All in all, it exceeded my expectations and has me yearning for more.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so this game is not bad by any means, but I wouldn't call it the most polished game. There are numerous bugs that happen incredibly often and can cost you anywhere between a few seconds upwards of 30 minuets because the autosaves in this game are atrocious,Characters often get stuck in doorways or while running resulting in them dying which means you need to reload a save from 10 minuets ago.Enemies are sometimes just not damaged by things such as grenades or shotguns even if they are in the red.Opening boxes sometimes just don't give you what is inside of them, including ones required to continue the campaign resulting in another resetEnemies just sometimes know know exactly where your squad is after you overload or make a sound with your drone, causing them to barrel towards your troops on the other side of the map of the noise.Besides the bugs there are these two gripes of mine and that is character accuracy. Your soldiers cannot hit ****! Their accuracy ranges from anywhere between 40-60+% and you may be thinking that's not too bad but when a single Xeno Runs through 5 people raining hellfire on it only to then maul a good chunk or outright kill someone it's becomes a little irritatingAnd next is the doomsday counter. I personally didn't have much of a problem with it initially, key word being initially. I was flying through this game playing on the hardest difficulty because I have a lot of experience with games like this Xcom being the big standout as this game makes a decent attempt to replicate the feeling of having the odds stacked against you. But as I approached the final mission i realized something I am 1 day short of beating the game. Which might not sound like much but that one day means I have to go back two hours to complete the game, and that is if the last mission is possible with my squad of 5 on just one attempt. There is no way to set back the clock, even by a day which means I just loose, the worst part about it is loosing doesn't give you any unique screen or anything it's just "You loose would you like to load a save or go to the main menu" No dramatic scene of the planets surface getting glassed by nukes, just a generic "you died' screen.The Gameplay is decent, very unfair and incredibly clunky at times but it is still fun and provides a unique experience. I know i signed up for the hardest difficulty but even at the end I only lost 1 soldier, and that was souly because I sent him in as cannon fodder to quickly finish a Sidequest so to lose via the clock catching me is incredibly irritating. Another gripe I have is the lack of enemy variety. There are god knows how many xenomorph forms yet they use the same boss like 8 times, and the two minibosses after your 1st encounter with the crusher are just fodder. My final complaint is the lack of soldier individuality, your soldiers all carry the exact same gun, minus the gunner whos signature gun becomes obsolete once reaching a certain  lv. But each soldier besides maybe the technician or the sniper basically don't do much of anything especially the medic who is kinda just bad and serves to fill out the squad once you get the apc. But even then they all feel the same, the sniper being the best of them all since he can just silently snipe enemies across the map.The game has a whole lot of potential for dlc content or just a sequel, but due to the bugs and abhorrent saves i cannot recommend.Sorry for the wordy review the only way i could word every complaint or opinion would be to make a 20 minuet YouTube video

_childDocuments_.review: I really really enjoyed this game, but it is definitely not without faults. It feels like they ran out of money about halfway through, and that's a huge shame, because what they got done with what they had is my favorite Aliens game since AvP2. Really smart, tense game design that successfully replicates the most important parts of the 2nd film. Unfortunately also absolutely chock full of bugs, and not the kind you want. In every session I played there was an instance where my controller stopped responding,  some animation got stuck, or some scripting bug prevented me from progressing. It can honestly be shockingly buggy. Yet... I really enjoyed myself?As a life long fan of the movies and the Dark Horse comics, this was a really good time, I thought. I was sad when it was over. Here's hoping Tindalos gets to make a sequel. Maybe pay some more voice actors and add some mod support along the way?

_childDocuments_.review: Survival horror? More like stressful horror. I'm so stressed while playing this game that I can play it once a day and my marines are stressed too. So much stress and anxiety.Goods:- Best Aliens game with marines- True to the lore with all the tech, visuals and weapons. Features new varians too like the sniper rifle etc that is pretty dope, made to really fit in the lore- One of the best Alien franchise games, people say Isolation is the best but I'm too much a scaredy cat to play it- Tactical gameplay is dope- You can lose your favorite marines, FOREVER! Be prepared to train all your extra marines when you unlock the training room- I love the length of the missions. They are not short at all, can take up to 2-3 hours but you can always extract from the area back to base to take a break. So far there was only one mission for me that forces you to complete it at one sitting (I haven't completed the whole game yet)- Story is ok, your basic Alien franchise stuff but with unique twists that make it even more interesting- Sound design is on point with the movies- Art style and immersion- Ambience- MusicBads:- Even with my PC and max settings the performance is on ok level. Graphics aren't even that amazing.- Cutscene lipsync is pretty bad but once you get used to it you won't notice it anymore- Cutscene quality for me at 1440p is pretty meh- Stress, you will lose your hair and start hearing the motion sensor beeping outside of the game- Character models for marines look so outdated that it's hilarious at some points. - PSA: NO MANUAL SAVING, be careful- You can only save by leaving the mission, passing a day in base or checkpoints- Had few crashes and had to reload a save due to a bug. Wouldn't launch a major scripted sceneThe negatives are more on the technical side and since the game is still fairly fresh they are still patching it. Lucky I didn't play it on launch as I saw some major game or progress breaking bugs mentioned by people. I give this one 8.5/10 and it's a must have for all Alien fans, tactical addicts and even survival horror fans. This will make you sweat.

_childDocuments_.review: I will be honest with you. I didn't believe that you can create a good RTS game set in the Alien universe. You would think that commanding an entire squad of hardened marines would make the game less intense. I was horribly wrong. The game is simply excellent. It combines satisfying gameplay with great atmosphere and intense missions. The premise is simple. The planet Lethe is slowly being infested with xenomorphs. The protagonist initiated a lockdown and  you must repair the Otago (your flagship) to escape from the planet. In order to do that you need to complete 12 missions.You control a group of 4 marines and order them to complete mission objectives. Orders are issued in real time with the option to use either slow motion or pause. The objectives are varied and tied to the narrative. During level exploration you can find datapads that give you additional insights what happened on Lethe.  You can also find crates with medicine, repair tools, materials, ammunition and other. In between missions you can manage your marines on the Otago . You can decide which marine should receive extra care to heal faster, go on therapy, decide which equipment should get unlocked etc. It's not overly complex but enough to keep you busy and force you to think about your decisions. When it comes to direct gameplay at the start of the mission your squad is undetected. That means few xenomorphs will patrol the are. Once detected your marines are hunted, if enough detections occur the alien hive with launch an onslaught. If you survive and still get detected the aliens will send a category 2 alien (either crusher or praetorian). After all of that the aggressiveness level increases. There are 4 levels of aggressiveness :easy, medium, hard and maximum aggression. At stage 3 or 4 you should consider extracting the squad because the aliens will eventually overwhelm you.Speaking of combat it was very fun and satisfying .You have enough unique skills and equipment to keep it varied (mines, grenades, flamethrower, rpg, plasma rifle, shotgun etc), the enemies are difficult enough to keep you on your toes, the sound effects are great (that pulse rifle sound is chef kiss) and the overall feel of combat is good. The missions themselves are varied in locations and objectives. The maps are also quite big which forces the player to face a constant battle of attrition. Will you complete the side objective? Will you make a detour to grab additional medkits and ammo? Can your marines handle more pressure from the xenos? If you decide to extract your squad the mission progress is saved, you lose 1 day ,the planet infestation level progresses( basically it a chance to spawn more enemies) and you can start with a fresh squad and reseted alien aggressiveness . Additional pressure is applied once you complete around 50% of the game. A doomsday clock launches. If you fail to complete the campaign before it finishes ticking you will die in nuclear fire.  Is it punishing? Well I've completed the game on normal and had 7 days left. Later I completed the game on nightmare and was left with 4 days. In both cases I really took my time with missions and soldier management so it's not super punishing. The devs also promised to work on the ability to make it obsolete. You can also customize the campaign difficulty at the start which is always a nice feature. The plot itself isn't super complicated but it's good enough to not irritate and it had a few special moments.  So the game has lots of things to love: atmosphere, combat, non tedious base management, good story, long missions, unique blend of stealth etc. Unfortunately it had also it's bad moments.  Personally I found 1 marine class underpowered and avoided using them on missions. The other 4 classes did have good balance though. The enemies have spawn points but can also appear randomly in vents which can lead to multiple detections and mess up your mission. Finally I hated that you couldn't change your squads formation. You control all of your marines at once. You can't pick one marine and give him a specific order. The game decides for you  which marine should unlock the door, collect a sample from the alien etc. This can mess up your orders and in a combat scenario can lead to a potential disaster. I cursed many times when my recon was the last squad member to enter a room and because of that he didn't have line of sight on his target. That led to some frustrating situations. The game is difficult. I've completed the game on normal and I struggled more than once. You can always customize your difficulty in the campaign though. The game has some minor bugs. I haven't experience any major ones like quest softlocking etc. Overall I highly recommend the game. It's not super expensive and It's definitely worth the asking price.  If you like the Alien universe and challenging RTS game you should feel at home.

_childDocuments_.review: Some reviews almost got me discouraged but I am glad I gave it a shot. This game captures the very essence of Aliens movie. The missions, squad management, sounds, ambience, visuals, everything is so atmospheric.The pros:- great story (feels like a standalone movie)- well designed mechanics (stress levels, time slowdown, perks, squad management, sneaking, weapons, making shelters, etc.)- level design - constant pressure and suspense - music and sound efects - there is even the vehicle from the movie to move you around!The cons - the game is hard (even on normal, you are gonna have a lot of hard times but then it is much more rewarding when you finish the mission) - game is saved only in predefined moments during the mission (in the end I enjoyed it because it makes you focus on the game and not on when to save. This makes it more immersive. And more stressful :D )TIP:  You can also use elevators to save because every time you use the elevator, the game is saved.If you are an Aliens fan, this is a must.Overall rating:  9.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed Aliens: Dark Descent. It’s a good RTS with some interesting mechanics and a difficulty that increase based on how you play it and how long you manage to be on “display” vs the xenos. Definitely recommended to the fans of Aliens franchise and the RTS genre.Here’s the short review:+ good mechanics (stress management, stealth phases, resources and ammos) + story well written+ challenging+ Combat management- few bugs- relatively short- sometimes fps dropsAnd now the long one’s:☼ Graphics ☼☐ Bad☐ Alright☑ Good☐ Beautiful☐ FantasticThe graphic is good, you don’t need a very strong PC to run it. Sometimes happens during some actions or some loading an FPS drops but is not very problematic.♬ Music ♬☐ Bad☐ Alright☑ Good☐ Beautiful☐ FantasticThe sound are well done and in line with the tension that you need when you’re playing a game like this.☠ Difficulty ☠☐ Easy☑ Average☐ Easy to learn / Hard to master☐ Hard☐ UnfairI found the game challenging in a positive way. The difficult in the campaign increase as time passes and ever inside every scenario the difficulty increase based on how much you fight the xenos: the more time you spend on sights, the more the hives increase the effort to take you down, even calling toughter xenos to hunt you down. § Bugs §☐ Bugs destroy the game☐ Lots of bugs☑ Few Bugs☐ You can use them for speedrun☐ Nothing encounteredI’ve encounterd two bugs but they are not game killing: if your entire squad is not in the elevator this one doesn’t move (I’m looking at you damn drone); one marine stuck opening a door and I had to reload the save.☯ Story ☯☐ There is none☐ Bad☐ Alright☑ Good☐ FantasticIt’s a good story and some cutscenes are really good to watch.⚔ Gameplay ⚔☐ Frustrating☐ Sleepy☐ Boring☑ Fun☑ ChallengingThe mechanics are very well done: you have to manage the stress of your squad while in fight, the ammo and the resources are limited and you have to roam the map to find them, the fights are fast paced and you cannot spam your skills as they took time to refill the action points. It’s preferable going stealth most of the time but some fights are unavoidable so you have to evaluate if is the right time and place to fight. What I really enjoyed is the fact that the situation could go very bad suddendly if you make a mistake with the risk to losing your troops easily۞ Game time / Length ۞☐ Really short (0 - 3 hours)☐ Short (4 - 8 hours)☑ Few hours (10 - 30 hours) [if you focus on the main story]☐ Long (40-60 hours) [if you complete everything]☐ Very Long (61-100 hours)☐ Extremely Long (101+ hours)Took me 34 hours to finish the campaign and find all the collectibles.$ Price / Quality $☐ Full price☑ Wait for Sale☐ Don't buy☐ Refund it if you canThis is a must play for Alien Franchise fan, so if you happen to find it on sale definitely grab it.

_childDocuments_.review: So I am only just passed the first real mission you get after escaping off the station as the assistant director and have to say, I am loving this game. This game is a fun experience where you really do feel like you are against the aliens. You deploy with a squad of four or five (later I assume) and have to go about finding things like supplies, ammo, etc. in the map, as well as complete objectives. I am playing it on EASY because I absolutely suck at these kinds of games, but I still find it challenging. It's not like your guys just go 'oh there's one *bang* aaand done.' The aliens still provide a challenge that can get your guys killed rather quickly. I had to restart the first real boss fight at least five times because of those ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ FACEHUGGER ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ GRABBING MY MEN. You will die and you have two choices: Accept that and play the game as intended, taking the loss like a chad and a good player....Or be a scumbag like me and load a save...If you can. There are no saves during the mission, at least from what I saw, unless you reach a checkpoint before a major fight or if you rest in a room, the game will save there. Marines are not dumb and I thought I would have a problem with positioning, but they all kind of act like one blob of guys. They don't really move by themselves unless you order them to search something, but even then the squad will post up and defend that marine, unless called away to do something else. The game can feel a little unfair at times, ngl, with the first boss having four facehuggers in the same room that can just one shot your guys pretty much. The first boss fight I had to restart was just because of them, not the actual boss, and that is because those facehuggers FLY across the room. I ran my guys to the opposite side, away from the facehuggers, trying to get some distance and I swear they have tiny rocket boosters because they propelled their asses forward. The management aspect isn't really anything hard. It gives you chances to decide on something like 'spend resources or your guys can't heal' or 'give the marines a day off to rest so they are all good, or push them and take a penalty' things like that. Supplies are used for buying guns or upgrades for soldiers, research is used to research better equipment which you get off dead aliens, pretty simple stuff. I will say it is kind of annoying when you have to try to look for small things in the world or those Facehuggers, because by the time you see the little icon pop up to shoot them, it's kind of to late and you might lose a marine instantly, so it does feel a little unfair, but I get why it's hard to see them.TL;DR. DO YOU LIKE XCOM? DO YOU LIKE THE ALIENS MOVIE? ARE YOU OKAY WITH A GAME THAT WILL KICK YOU IN THE NUTS WITH STEEL TOED BOOTS A LOT? BUY THE GAME.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is great for many reasons, but there are issues.Soundtrack appears good, atmosphere is fairly immersive, A.I. has some interesting quirks like side-stepping aliens to avoid marine fire- No mod support- No squad positioning- No squad formations- No direct squad member control for actions- No barricade placement- No door breaching- No stealth mode for marines - run or walk around as loud as possible, shouting orders ( They never whusoer )- No squad specialization? Why do all marines know how to extract dna? No doctor/scientist required?- Limit of 4 to a squad?- ARC cannot be used to ram aliens, transport additional ammo or supplies, which makes no sense- Supplies collected and not spent when you evac are not taken back and cannot be used again ( very dumb )- Without squad control marines bunch up for their acid bathI  hope they improve the game and add further functionality, but i doubt it. They could have done so much more with the aliens IP.Update 2024:Game has received 0 updates or patches to address bugs despite its big success in the last year.

_childDocuments_.review: As an Aliens fan - this games awesome.It's certainly in the "AA" category of game, where you can 'feel' the budget limitations but there's a definite passion and love for the source material to be found here.The main gameplay kind of reminds me of the series Full Spectrum Warrior where you have no specific control over an individual marine but control the squad as a whole, with some specials that call upon the individuals within the squad.Combine that with an XCom style base management aspect and the whole thing works really well.I'm hoping the game sells well enough it allows them to swing back and revisit some of the areas that could be updated relatively easily with patches (audio lines primarily - needs some variation in number and tone from stealthed to stressed to all out action. As it is, theres one set of MAYBE a dozen repeated lines).I'm hoping DLC also adds some variety beyond another Weyland Yutani set of corridors and rooms.Solid 7/10 gameplay experience that for an Aliens fan is more a 9/10. Great work on trying something different with the license and the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a fan of the Alien franchise and this game does not disappoint. This review might contain spoilers, so; SPOILER ALERT!I liked the atmosphere from the start. I'm only a casual gamer, I do not strive to play a game on highest difficulty or anything. At first the game was relentless. My marines were picked off one by one because at first I simply wanted to take out as many Xenomorphs as possible, bad mistake haha, especially in tight spots or dead ends. The moments of being detected, hunted and the Aliens loosing your "scent" give of the right feels. It's like cat and mouse... I like the progression ingame and the increase of the xenomorph threat/infestation during missions/the entire game pushes you to make haste, go faster and take risks.The end however feels a bit rushed and is a bit underwhelming, for me personal. "Main" characters lose their lives, your regular party stays behind and the Otago takes off into the distance right after you complete the final mission. There is no final dialogue, you can't check up on your regular party of marines etc.Because of the ending I simply wanted to have a couple more missions in the game. Also, seeing the leveling of my marines (only 4 becoming lvl 10, which I believe is too few with all marines still alive completing the game) it makes sence if there were 1 or 2 more missions in the game.The game has some minor bugs (up to 4 times the game simply froze up and didn't respond afterwards) and sometimes a Xeno gets killed of the walkable path but drops a "sample" that you can't collect, but a question mark gives the idea that there is something there to collect. It happend to me 3 times to wich I'm certain this was the case. I for one can't wait for a second part, expansion or DLC that adds new missions.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute "Gotcha" game.  Tutorial is longer than the Steam refund window. You wont even by on your first independent deployment by 2 hours. Janky movement system - marines move together as a team, and it's random who does what. Sometimes when you unlock a door, the game takes a few seconds to figure out you opened the door, so the pathfinding sends you in a completely different direction. Combat is painful at best. You have one deployment a day, and ever day adds "aggression" to the hive. You can't complete all objectives on a single deployment, so you are constantly having to return, forcing the missions to get progressively harder. Marines take stress damage ( a la Darkest Dungeon) and become more and more unhinged as you play. Ammo, meds and tools are all in scarce inventory, and you constantly have to loot what's on the map to get more. But each map has a finite supply. Marines level up extremely slowly. Even in the guides, it stresses that you need to stay for as long as possible on each mission to get a squad of max level soldiers by end game. There are a few ways to cheese this - namely calling Aliens to your APC so that it can mow them down for you. Game pulls the current Xcom 2 "gotcha" mechanic where you can completely sweep a level of enemies, then one just pops out.  All aliens are faster than you, can deal more damage than you and can take way more damage than you. Plus, your marines are just babies. 5 minutes into a mission, they are functionlessly insane, panicing, wasting ammo and meds and forgetful of their skills. Eventually you can unlock smart gunners, snipers, etc. But their skills are mostly useless. Want your sniper to use that nice rifle of his? Yeah, that is a limited skill. By the second deployment area, you only have 3 command points that sloooooooooowly regen over time. Want to use your shotgun, flamer or sniper rifle? Each of those skills takes a command point. Once they are gone, it can take about a minute to regain one. Let's play theater of the mind shall we:Marines deploy on planet. They are tired, even through they havent been in combat in a day or two. One marine is a coward, and another is paranoid. Just being in the squad they lower both your command point regen, as well as add more stress. Get to the first room, bam - you're already at 50-75% stress. SIngle alien pops up, you struggle to kill it with your now fully panic'ed team. You're being hunted, and the aliens know exactly where you are. They attack in small waves. It doesnt matter, because none of your guys can ♥♥♥♥ anything and their skills have already ended. You finally wipe them out and ONSLAUGHT. WTF...what's that? Oh hit's a horde attack mode. Okay, find a defensible position with your limping, nearly dead, panic'ed squad. Oh, what's that, a crusher has arrived. Oh, and to put more topping on this crap pizza, every night you "rest" between deployments, you will face a random event card. These cards are always aweful. First they had bad dreams, so I had to make hypersleep beds (lose all technicians for a day and everyone is tired - debuff), next day two guys get into a fight (now they are wounded and exhausted), then there was a lab accident where a doctor spilled acid on herself. I can do nothing (30% of losing the doctor), or try to save the doctor (all doctors are busy for an entire day). How the heck are you supposed to slog through this when you start every day worse off than the previous day?Game over man, game over. This review was written at 6 hours in, and I cannot fathom this getting any better.
