_childDocuments_.review: Was a little hard to figure out at first, but once you understand the concept, you will get a definitive "aliens" experience. You have to consider your squad's movements carefully and at times, the game can be quite tense, in the way a good "aliens" game should be. Your map doubles as a motion tracker and like in the movie, your constantly keeping an eye on it, timing moments carefully between contacts, moving your squad between cover, planning your route as you go. Also consider engagements carefully, you can't just go in guns blazing. Once they see you, more will come, particularly if a swarm is triggered. Engagements are fast and furious even in slow motion. The stress mechanic is something new, but it makes sense, as it adds to the whole dynamic of carefully planning and executing. Of course, things don't always go to according to plan and you'll be forced to improvise. Aliens get stronger over time, there wasn't a single tool or ability I didn't put to good use, although I managed to beat the campaign without unlocking all the weapons. Hats off to the developers, this was a challenging game and a surprisingly enjoyable and experience. I hope they make a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! A love letter to Aliens fans. Really interesting mix of real time and tactics. The real time element keeps the pressure on, which keeps it tense and exciting through the whole game. I'd say this does for Aliens what Isolation did for Alien - it captures the essential elements of the movies. The story is decent, enough to hang the game on and comparable to the Alien spin off novels and comics (a few nice nods to the old Dark Horse comic series in the lore, which I enjoyed).It's quite a tough game, and be prepared to restart levels and sections again, and impatience will get you killed quickly.Graphics are nothing special these days, but lets say "good enough". There are a quite a few minor glitches and bugs, nothing that totally broke the game, but just lots of little things. It says unsupported on Steam Deck but I played though it just fine, the game pad controls work well and you can have medium settings with stable 30fps or drop down to low settings for better performance. The game only allows saves at certain points so being able to just suspend the Steam Deck was a benefit.I suppose some people will complain about the lack of MP, but I only play SP games, so not personally bothered. Took me 53 hours to complete first play through on medium, so as far as I'm concerned that's plenty of content, and I'm sure at some point I will try again on hard. Not many games that hold my attention even for that long, and if they release some mission based DLC, I'll be up for that.

_childDocuments_.review: One word describes this gameALIENSRemember Alien Isolation?Remember AVP 2010?Remember ALIENS?Remember RTS games?Take Isolation's Presentation, AVP's constant feeling of dread, Aliens Colonial Marines story and shove it into a RTS formula. It came out amazinglyThis game takes has two layers that Strategic layer and the Tactical layer.Strategic Layer In the Strategic layer you customize and upgrade soldiers, you heal the wounded, you build new weapons, do research, progress the story and select missions to go on. deployments can only happen once a day and when you cycle the day you can get random little side missions that have a percent chance of failure and will also use up that next day or you could skip it.. It also allows wounded soldiers to heal and research to progress. As you go on missions the infestation level will rise increasing the threat level of the xenomorphs in the tactical level. Once you are ready to do a mission you go into the tactical level and hopefully you command your squad better than Gorman did.Tactical LayerThis is the part of the game that will keep you on the edge of your seat. Those customized soldier that you dote on and upgrade can give them nicknames. This is where they can die. This part of the game has the ever beeping motion detector which is the most iconic sound in the Aliens franchise constantly beeping telling you your knocking on deaths door and the moment that beeping gets louder and faster xenomorphs are on your squad. you have to react quickly don't freak out hit that space bar to go into slow-mo and hope you managed your limited resources well, and fight the fear. As you explore the map you will complete objectives find supplies to use in the tactical and strategic level and save people to add to you team.  The only "Safezone" in the tactical level is at the APC and even then it only has one turret. Stress, Ammo, Medical, Engineering, Tac points, and hit points these are the basic resources you need to manage to not only survive the endless xenomorphs but to do so while under threat of losing your precious marine who you have invested skills and missions to level them up, good thing you probably picked the option that allows for save scumming and not Iron man where the game save only before and after the mission. Now that you beat that mission you might have missed some objectives and now you have to go back.... sucks to be you.The Game They say this game is hard and it is. If you are not used to faster pace rts's like StarCraft, Command and Conquer, MechCommander, and Dawn of War 2 this game will be extremely hard for you. Better play on story mode. However if you love the Aliens universe and are willing to try it do it, the game will give you everything you asked for and maybe some you didn't. Good ol' quotes, the best aliens atmosphere, great sound design, amazing cut scenes that are of movie level quality and characters who are more then skin deep... hopefully not too deep.The ControlsWhile this is a RTS the controls are rather unrefined for mouse and keyboard (have not tried controller) not bad just not the best good thing you can change them. considering its a squad based RTS you would think you could control each soldier individually as well as in a group and you can but you have to fight the game to control individuals because i suspect the game would actually be too easy if you had proper control over each unit. consider this. you are in a room with two doors and xenomorphs are coming from both you would want to weld one while having the rest of the soldiers set up to defend the other you have certain skills on each soldier and you want the best ones for the job however you cannot command specific units to do things you just have to hope the right one is doing what you want.Score:   8/10Presentation 1/1: Amazing feel of the Aliens UniverseVisuals          0.5/1: Great movie level cinematic's, in-game cut-scenes look like assSounds          1/1: Beep beep beep beepCharacters   0.5/1: Not the greatest but definitely not badBugs              1/1: Very few to noneStability         1/1: Haven't crashed yetCustomization   0.5/1: there is unit customization however its rather limited and the faces aren't greatGameplay      1/1: Both Layers are excellent the fact you can customize marines really adds to the whole tense nail biting tactical levelStory              1/1: While predictable its not about the destination when it comes to Aliens movies or games its the trip to get there.Controls     0.5/1: While decent i just wish i had greater control over the individual unitsPS: I hope it gets mod support

_childDocuments_.review: Aliens: Dark Descent is without a doubt the best Aliens experience since Alien Isolation. However, just because it's the best experience *since* then, doesn't make it on par with what, to me, is one of the greatest horror experiences in all of gaming regardless of your attachment to the Alien IP.Aliens: Dark Descent is extremely unique, and while it's fun, it's not going to be for everyone - and this includes huge fans of the lore and the property. There are instances where the game can feel sluggish and even downright boring, but a big part of that has to do with the fact that there is a lot of walking around in bloated environments (though they're detailed), and more often than not rooms and areas have very little to uncover. It makes exploration feel like an afterthought, and it's because of that the side quests feel not nearly as important as just focusing on the main story unless you're someone who *really* needs an extra medkit or two.The game is hard—very hard—but Aliens: Dark Descent is also patient and forgiving where it needs to be. However, it's worth noting that the game's flexibility towards the player also rests upon how strategic they're going to be. For example: You could Rambo your way through the missions (which are long and compiled of many micro-missions within), but a failure to prepare for boss fights (of which the game warns you is coming up) or going back to the Ortega (Your ship, not Jenna) could risk having your marines killed-in-action, abducted by a Xenomorph, or be so stressed out that they'll collapse, go into shock, and likely won't see action for quite some time as they recover in the infirmary. Playing it in a more methodical manner and being mindful of stress levels, stats, when to go back to recoup before deploying again (the game autosaves/has checkpoints so you don't have to worry about starting missions all over again when you leave) will actually reward the player tenfold. It's a clever way to get the player to think like actual military personnel and strategize before continuing on. Aliens: Dark Descent will work with you to ensure that you survive, but they also make it known that Xenomorphs are (predictably) very dangerous, and anything could happen when going out on a mission which is why it's always good to be prepared and make sure that you're utilizing any equipment, skills, and the sort in a resourceful manner.It's like Diablo meets XCOM sprinkled with some StarCraft and Age of Wonders. I know that sounds absolutely wild, but it's a really unique amalgamation of these that I felt meshed together surprisingly well. It did, however, unfortunately risk any sort of ergonomics and user-friendliness, though it was clear that they tried the best they could to make it clean and accessible - but there's only so much that can be minimized and streamlined when working with so many mechanics and functionalities that each one of those games' respective genres calls for.It's also worth noting that while my playtime at the time of this review is just under five hours, I've seen about 20+ hours on the Xbox Series X|S version of the game. It's optimized rather well on both PC and Xbox, and I found myself playing the bulk of my PC duration on Steam Deck even though it doesn't officially support it. While it no doubt takes a graphical hit on Steam Deck, its performance is rather stable and fluid, and it's a nice experience to play in handheld even though its font is incredibly small on all platforms. You can, thankfully, adjust this to your liking, and options are plentiful to make sure that everyone gets the experience they're looking for (including a 'Story' difficulty level that will be much more forgiving for those that don't want to have to be on edge as much).I think the biggest achievement in this game is without a doubt its cinematics, though. Every time a cutscene would play I would get so excited because of how well written, directed, and produced it was. Truthfully, if Aliens: Dark Descent was a CG feature-film instead of a game, I may have even liked it even more (and even argue that this be the best "movie" since Aliens), because that's really where the game shines the most. The production quality is through the roof in these, and it's a shame that the in-game portions simply don't live up to the quality of its cinematics even though its opening moments were just as strong and powerful as the cinematics that followed. It unfortunately begins to fall off into a tedious and mundane trek as the hours pass by, and eventually I had to admit to myself that I would eventually retire the game as I simply wasn't having fun anymore. It's important to note, though, that I never hated it or don't think it's worth picking up; I'm just the type of person that believes pacing is immensely important, and the pacing was just all over the place with Aliens: Dark Descent. There were times I could play for hours in a row and time would pass me by in a flash, and other times where I would get twenty minutes in before I was like "that's enough" and quit the game to move on to literally anything else that would be more enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: Fills an uncommon niche in an oft abused IP, so it gets plenty of credit even if there's plenty of negative complaints.Fireteam management and mission conduct hits a niche that hasn't been touched terribly well since Starship Troopers Terran Ascendancy.  The feel/tech is there from Aliens.   The tension/difficulty feels right. Unfortunately, the story and characters are fairly atrocious, with little logic to it all.  The emphasis on stealth mechanics can make the experience tedious.  The artificial limitation of manpower/firepower (no fireteams supporting each other, no air support really, etc) is immersion breaking -- at least the ARC vehicle provides some overwatch.  Even 6 hrs in, a tutorial is still interrupting you, holding your hand and forcing your choices.   Even though there's personnel management, the game randomizes a limited choice of options for each of your Marines' progression (ie. class/role/perks), which means while you have some choices, you ultimately don't feel in control of your own roster or organizational structure.  The alien cultists are just ridiculous.Regardless of gripes, this has still led to a captivating experience for a fan of Aliens, the USCM, and tactical squad strategy.

_childDocuments_.review: Really addictive title, had a blast playing through. Everything is very close to the immersion of the movies and the lore. Lots of props, armors, weapons, vehicles and voice lines are recognizable to trigger many nostalgic memories.The plot is very enjoyable, sometimes vague but in the end definitely interesting.It fits right into the movies and the books. The feeling of it being plausible adds a neat atmosphere to it. Everything is inscenated through epic cutscenes and chilling soundtracks. Game can get very creepy at times too.The gameplay is super addictive, the squad mechanic functions SO GOOD, it really surprised me. Its not clunky, not chaotic and simply smooth. The marines act according and effective. There are a few situations where their pathfinding is f*cked up but its not a big problem after all. Stuff mixes between hide and seek, managing ressources carefully but also pushing and running or holding an area to defend yourself. If you get seen too often by the critters youre gonna have massive problems with later parts in the mission so you gotta be careful. Also managing wounded and sore marines after the missions.Progression is a big point here, every new unlock either in terms of new weapons, new traits or new xeno tech has direct impact and every tool is satisfying to use after all. You wanna mix your squad with every available class and tool to be suited for different situations throughout the missions.The graphics are top quality imo, as well as the environmental sounds and the soundtrack. They really took solid attention to details, even footsteps sound super satisfying. Its a joy!Performance is solid as well, sometimes dropping some frames randomly but overall stable and playable even on old hardware, big thumbs up for that.What the game made very special for me after all was the fact of possibly going game over throughout the playthrough. You got a limited amount of ingame days to finish the missions cause of lore reasons. Also the longer you spend on playing and replaying missions as more agressive the alien hordes get. The small push of "you better hurry up" added a nice amount of immersion right there and rounded everything up. You can expect roundabout 20 hours of gameplay for your first walkthrough if you take some time and play on normal. Keep in mind there are still quite a few bugs, lots of them can be sorted out by reloading a save, re entering an area via lift or simply waiting for a bit. Its a mixed bag, some arent really a problem, others definitely are and there have been a few moments where it really killed my fun. So i hope devs will invest more love into that area,Overall a lovely addition to the Alien Universe, a very unique and fresh gameplay experience combined with thrilling moments and intense action. We need more of that stuff!Definitely recommend getting into it, fair price for a great title!

_childDocuments_.review: The cringy/juvenile plot and dialogue gets a pass because the gameplay is solid and fun.But the numerous bugs, some of which can potentially cost a mission, are a hard Not recommend.Bugs I've experienced:- A elevator suddenly not working and the crew waiting forever for it to start... which by the way, for anyone experiencing that, it's caused because the droid can get stuck on  wall instead of taking a corner and will stay there until you notice and go all the way back for it... which hilariously can also happen to the alien queen...- Giving an order to the crew and the only want who wants to take on the order is the one carrying an injured crewmember on his shoulder... so he cannot undertake the order, and no one else does, either, because the guy insists on being the one to do it... despite not being able to...- Giving an order to move while a crewmember is busy doing something should result in two things:A) He moves while carrying the order. Like for example shooting the shotgun.B) He carries the order and then moves. Like for example setting up a mine or opening a box.Whatever the case, they start walking or running to the position the squad moved at, following the issued movement command and speed.However, on certain occasions, mostly when shooting a bazooka or healing a crewmember, a member of the squad may just stay still after he finishes, and will only move again after you click to move again a few times. Should you fail to notice, this being a real time strategy game, the poor soul may have triggered the "alien alarm" or be overrun by enemies. A few seconds make a huge difference in this game.- Sometimes when a crewmember was downed, their body floated along the ground unnaturally until finishing the last movement order, on one such occasion I tried to carry him to safety and despite the mechanics seemingly okay, the body was floating three five meters in front of the guy carrying him, instead of over his shoulder. A minute later I ran a bug I previoulsy mentioned: I couldn't open a door because the only one offering to press a button was the one with his hands busy, so I put down the body... which suddenly teleported all the way back to when I had picked him up and messed up the mission. In fact, I returned for him and I couldn't even pick the body anymore. I was left with the choice of either restarting a whole mission or killing a valued member of the crew.Fun game until that stuff happens. The core ideas and elements of the gameplay are pretty good (albeit easily cheeseable at least on hard difficulty).

_childDocuments_.review: So this is the first comment I've ever left. So that should tell you how strongly I feel about this game. TL;DR: I really enjoyed this game, but honestly it could have been better if they allowed you to change the squad up, and did away with tactic points, and just used the CD instead. The game-play is actually really good, but it falls short in a few places that make it easier to just sneak past everything rather than engage.  The story line is FANTASTIC though. If you're an aliens fan buy it at full price to support the devs (they deserve it for their ethic in releases a game in a released state instead of release now patch later mentality.)  If you don't like aliens but like tactics games, just buy on sale.                                                                                ---Game-play---So let me preface this by saying; one of my all time favorite games is a game called The Red Solstice. It is EXACTLY like this game, but with better game play. Oh how I wished they copied that game's squad aspect. That would have made this my favorite game of all time.For instance, in that game you can split your squad up and set up ambushes, or you can time delay like this game and give individual orders for your guys to carry out. You can't do that in this game, which REALLY hinders the "tactic" aspect of it. It basically turns it into a glorified sneak in sneak out don't get seen game, since being in combat really really hinders your marines ability to fight. So there's really no point into a shoot out, because you WILL lose, even missions that require it.  Another thing that REALLY hampers this game is the Tactic Point system. There are times where I'll have 5/5 points, and all my skills will be on CD, but the skills will be on CD, and times where I have no CP but all my skills will be ready. It kinda messes with the flow of the game, They should have gone with one or the other. (Honestly in this type of game CD is the better option) Also, the flares should be unlimited, with a 3-5 second CD. It would enhance the eeriness of the game, and help the flow of combat, especially when combat is mandatory. Also, personally, I just really want to enjoy the game, I mean the actual game, I want to see every pixel, and enjoy the work of art I'm playing. But (rightly so) the game is very dark, so there are times my marines are shooting and I have no idea what hey are shooting at until I see the neon green explosion.  I WANTED TO WATCH THE ALIEN DIE DAMN IT. buuuut since all the lights are off I missed the shoot out, and that just bugs me because I should be able to see what my marines see.Now I know I've been pretty hard on them, but that's because I can't help comparing it to The Red Solstice (which is a total clone of this game even the story is similar.) But that's not really fair to this game. Aliens has plenty of stuff going for it. The APC is fantastic, you can just send it on strafing runs to take out anything that's popping up on the motion sensor. and then follow it in, or just have it carry you to the point closest to where you're headed. It's a lot of fun to run the enemy over in in.  The gameplay is also really fluid, and fun to watch. really the only issues I have with it are what i've listed, and most of those are just quality of life improvements. Nothing game breaking just ways to improve it. It's just that I know what this game could have been, and feel a bit let down by it. But that by no means means I hate the game. I'll play it to completion, and enjoy every minute of it.If the mods are reading this, PLEASE look at what red dawn does, because game-play wise, that would have made your game  as perfect as a game can get. It would also add replay value, since it would add a ton of diversity to what you can do.                                                                   ---STORY---Aliens is one of my favorite movie universes, and that is where this game truly shines. Oh man there's been times during this game that my heart felt like it was going to burst out of my chest. the OH ♥♥♥♥ moments are truly spectacular. That's where this game really, really shines. They captured that PERFECTLY.  The story line fits the theme, and the source material and is a worthy addition to the Aliens Universe. If you like that type of stuff you will love the story. It's pretty intense, and has jump scares and plenty of "welp I'm dead" moments that this type of stuff is renowned for.    The only real issue I have is the ability to leave midway through the mission. It makes the stress meter worthless, and breaks the immersion into the game IMO, they should have shortened the missions, and forced you to stay until it was done.                                                                         ---Sound---So the sound is where this game really shines. IMO it really matches the feelings they are going for. other than that I really have no other opinions on it, it's well done, well executed, and has no reverb issues on my surround sound. Since you HAVE to put a number to make it a review I guess I'll put that here, and try to make the numbers reflect what I've said. Lets see:Game-play - 7.5/10 Story 9/10Sound 10/10Overall enjoyment: 8/10                                                                               ---Conclusion---Now I'm not saying this game is awful. It's actually really good. But it simply could have been better. that's just a fact. It's like they ALMOST made the best game ever, but stopped at the finish line and said NOPE. Which really bugs me because it's clear how much these devs LOVE this game. I mean it shipped with virtually no game breaking bugs, or CPU issues, or memory crashes, or anything that virtually every game released in the past 10 years has been a victim of because they priorities the release over doing it right. Which they did. So kudos to you guys for doing it right. As both a consumer and a gamer I truly appreciate it. Oh, and if you read my essay... er review... to this point, Thank you for reading! Feel free to leave a comment.

_childDocuments_.review: Aliens: Dark Descent sees you take control of a squad of Colonial Marines, tasked with finding and eliminating the source of a xenomorph infestation as it progressively gets closer and closer to taking over the planet. Dark Descent takes the form of a strategy, squad-based, tactical, RTS type thing game where the player gives orders to their units in order to take out the enemy hordes in the most precise and efficient manner.I am a long-time Alien fan, but I initially passed on this game because I've never really been into RTS games or stuff similar to that genre. I decided to eventually pick it up because the action of "being" a Colonial marine looked interesting enough despite the type of game it was. Now considering I haven't really played any RTS games before, I was initially incredibly overwhelmed. There's a lot of information to take in, a lot of rules that the game has to explain, a lot of mechanics to take into account. Dark Descent definitely warns you of this as you start your first new game, stating that it is a difficult game and stressing the game's codex feature that provides snippets on all the rules and mechanics. The first couple missions were very stressful for me as I was learning all of the mechanics and figuring out how to best play the game. However, once everything finally clicked Dark Descent ended up being a super fun experience. Figuring out how to tactically take out the alien hordes, managing Marine stress levels and ammo management, learning how to properly cycle out squads of Marines so that you're never stuck with too many Marines on the bench. The setting felt authentic to the Aliens universe for the most part, with generally great sound design, gunplay, and enemy types.In terms of negatives, I can't speak specifically on the RTS genre aspect due to unfamiliarity with similar games. That being said, I can speak on some other gripes I had with Aliens: Dark Descent. I feel that the difficulty spike ramped maybe a tad too quickly, with mission 1 feeling at times as difficult as some later missions. Voice acting was a little mediocre, with limited Marine voicelines and pretty rough facial animations as well. The Marine upgrade system felt in some points extremely vital for some class-specific skills and at other points incredibly useless with the more general Marine skills. I disliked some of the mechanics in-mission, such as how killing one xenomorph suddenly causes a massive Hive Hunt, even if that xenomorph wasn't able to communicate with the Hive before you killed it. Marine death felt like a bit of a strange mechanic, as it was very serious if a Marine died but the vast majority of the time when *one* Marine died, the rest usually died shortly after, meaning I would be prompted to load from my last Save and re-do the scenario with my squad still fully alive, so whenever I had one Marine die I jumped the gun and just re-loaded the Save anyway, functionally disregarding the death mechanic entirely.All that being said, I thought Aliens: Dark Descent was a very enjoyable experience. I don't think the RTS genre or strategy games are for me, but I got a kick out of executing the tactical extermination of the xenomorphs. Would I go out of my way to recommend this game to an Alien fan or RTS fan? Maybe not, but I think this was a pretty cool new way to experience more Aliens-focused content in an action-focused as opposed to horror-focused manner.

_childDocuments_.review: Abstract:  Combat good, story bad.  Worth buying.Aliens: Dark Descent is a nice variation on the XCOM game style.  You manage your soldiers just like XCOM.  They get injured and need to recover, there are different classes to choose from, and as they level up they gain perks.  If they get injured they need time in the Med Bay to recover.  Psychological damage is a bigger factor in A:DD, and a psych treatment ward is also provided.  As soldiers level up you can research better weapons (but nothing that's not in the movie) and alien-pheromone-based aids.   This feels just like XCOM, and that's no bad thing.But while your base is in a crashed ship that you need to repair like XCOM, you have no control over the repairs and you get no new upgrades from it.  The game just tells you what percentage of your ship has been repaired.  You can make it go faster by rescuing civilian engineers on missions, but you can't actually seek engineers to rescue: they either show up, or they don't.  So there's zero strategy to ship repair, an entire XCOM element that's missing.   Research and weapons development are also much more limited than XCOM; no real decisions to be made there, either.  This all feels disappointing, apart from the combat system it feels like a stripped-down version of XCOM.The combat system is very different, though.  Where XCOM is turn-based and you manage each soldier individually, A:DD is real time and your entire squad moves as a unit.  They can walk and still shoot, or run and not shoot.  There are boxes to open and special weapons you can trigger (grenade launcher, sniper rifle, flamethrower, etc.) and the game chooses which soldier will execute that command.  They did a nice job on this, the squad acts intelligently.  I've not had any issues where the squad does something stupid in response to my orders.  But because you can't move individual soldiers, I find the sniping rifle to be useless; on a cluttered map you just can't force the guy to stand where he has line of sight to the target.They also made the APC an asset in combat.  You can't exactly drive it, but there are various places (bus stops, basically) on the map you can send it to, and it will kill everything it sees along the way.  This isn't overpowered, its more of a convenience that helps occasionally. It's a very nice addition.Firing on the move is required; always have your squad walk away from the aliens as they shoot.  It gives you more time and the aliens seem to have trouble doing melee attacks on moving targets.  Combined with the real-time combat and dramatic music right out of the Aliens film, this constant movement makes the game more exciting than XCOM, I think.Ammo management is an issue.  Your soldiers don't carry many clips and they often run out too quickly, forcing them to fall back on pistols, (which aren't enough to fight many aliens).  So you sometimes run out of ammo and need to go home, which means the game's ultimate deadline moves one day closer before you can finish the mission.   I didn't care for this; I prefer XCOM, where changing magazines is a brief tactical nuisance instead of a game-ending strategic nuisance. The squad also accrues Stress when aliens are hunting them, and that becomes another ticking clock that can force an early end to a scenario.  More on this later.Soldiers ALWAYS get injured.  In a complete campaign on Easy mode, not one in ten soldiers got through a scenario without being wounded.  It's much bloodier than XCOM in this way.  Keeping enough active, mentally healthy, rested soldiers available for the next mission can be difficult.  This feels tedious and prevents you from having a "favorite squad" to concentrate all the experience on;  you just can't keep the same 4-5 soldiers healthy and rested all at the same time.So I liked the basic system, and I liked combat.  It really does feel like you're in the Aliens movie.  Some of the soldiers' dialog is taken from the film.  So that's good.What I DIDN'T like: the plot and the characters.  The plot is just stupid, sometimes so bad it's cringe-worthy, and it contributes nothing to the game.  When you get the option to press spacebar to skip a cinematic, DO IT.  Don't succumb to the "but I want to enjoy all the content the first time I play" mentality -- there's nothing there you will enjoy, and no decision you make will be influenced by the plot you skipped.   The cut scenes are far too long and some can't be skipped.  There are logical leaps that defy explanation, as if some part of the plot got left on the cutting room floor, creating a continuity error.The NPC characters are rubber-stamp caricatures and none of them are likable or interesting.   That's a common fault in many games, though -- you can't do much character development, so you start with a stereotype everyone already knows.   But even the protagonist character (Ripley by another name) isn't fun to watch.   I keep shouting, "This woman does not speak for me!" at the screen.Some of the scenarios are pretty awful.  Spoiler:  in one mission, an alien gets loose aboard your ship.   (Super-spoiler: someone in  your crew sabotages you to improve corporate profits.  Homage, or cliche'?)  Despite having a ship full of marines, you have to fight the alien single-handed.  Without a weapon.   It's not so much that it's a bad scenario (it's a nice change of pace to be unarmed), it's just that the plot contrivance they went through to justify the scenario is so idiotic that it shatters the illusion. It just feels stupid, like they stuck a Donkey Kong level in the middle of the game.  And (spoiler) the final boss fight is unique in that you don't fight the boss.  You just run away and nuke the site from orbit.  It's a lousy note to end the campaign on.The graphics... they're OK.  The rendering is hard enough to make the fan on my graphics card work constantly, so I guess they're doing something nice, and the scenery is quite attractive and very much like the movie.  But I can't say I was wowed.  I think the dark/gray palette probably undermines the nice graphics. The characters, though, are just ugly and misshapen.  The artists wanted them to look like serious, grim soldiers, but they end up just looking like they're scowling.  You can edit their faces, clothing, etc., but they still look angry.  It gets old and seems like shoddy art work.Saving games is annoying AF.  You can't.  The game automatically saves when you take an elevator to a different level or weld yourself into a room to rest, and before a boss fight, but that's it.  If you make a mistake and your squad gets killed, you have to re-start that level from the last auto-save (usually, the beginning of the level).  I get it, they want to make the game more challenging, but this isn't the way.  If you want an Iron Man mode make it an option.Also, the psych system... You build up Stress while in combat and for some time after you're spotted.  It rises pretty quickly and starts giving you disabilities, and restoring stress is expensive (you burn limited resources).  So if you want to complete the scenario in one mission you have to avoid combat as much as possible.  Let that sink in: it's a combat game that penalizes you for being in combat.   I'll admit that makes the game feel more like the movie, but I'd rather blast stuff.  I'm not asking for a stand-up fight, just a bug hunt where you actually WANT to hunt the bugs.Overall I'm glad I bought the game and I enjoyed playing it.  I'm not sure whether it has replay potential: unlike XCOM it's the exact same list of missions in every campaign.  But I think I got my money's worth.  I would recommend it to anyone who loved the Aliens movie and anyone who appreciates the XCOM style of game.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally a game to scratch that Xcom Itch. I originally dismissed this game upon hearing the words "squad" and "RTS", expecting to have a tedious and painful experience of having to keep track of multiple soldiers with no tactical pausing to make strategic decisions.Boy was I wrong, you have a squad of 4 marines but you control them as a group, it's clean, fun, and tactical, you gather a host of abilities that you can utilize via the tactical pause/slow-mo to give you time to analyze the situation and act accordingly. You can finish a mission in one deployment or return to base to come back and finish the mission with a fresh squad. Once you return to base you can research, build, train, and heal your troops.If you're a fan of xcom don't be scared by the RTS labelOnly downsides are the audio, specifically the quantity of troop lines and fight music. I found myself getting a bit annoyed at hearing the same soundtrack play with each combat encounter, and hearing my troops shout the same line everytime a give a move order. _childDocuments_.review: This game was surprisingly a lot of fun. I went into it with no expectations and I enjoyed mostly every minute of playing this. I've never been able to commit to squad-style tactics like XCOM, but this was a nice change of pace and similar play style that was easier to commit to. The only issue is the saving and loading. Unfortunately my playthrough was cut short near the end when i got about an hour into mission 9, had to save and get off for the night, then tried to reload the game in the morning to continue it. It started the mission at the very beginning with the camera locked around the starting area. My squad was already past the office level of the mission, and the APC was on the map, but behind a locked area. It was as if the game thought I never did any of the mission (even though I was an hour in) and all of my units were no where on the map (because they were underground). Ultimately it was game breaking because I refuse to lose that hour of progression so I ended up watching the rest of the game on youtube.However, my issue could've just been caused by the fact that I play on two different computers and rely on Steam's cloud saving. If you don't rely on cloud saving like I do, then you likely won't have that issue. In the end, the game is a lot of fun and a good challenge. The storyline was interesting to follow. Some of the voice actors were great, like Maeko and Harper, but some others were hilariously bad.

_childDocuments_.review: SPOILERS; tldr get it on sale if you really like Aliens. If you don't just play XCOM. PROS:- Pretty fun, and the real-time system works decent.- Decent story, but with some flaws (more on that later). - Good length, despite complaints. Any longer and it would've dragged.- Gets a little crazy with xenomorph variants, but still feels faithful to the Alien franchise.- There's a lot of optional datapads with some worldbuilding; little details like that are always appreciated. CONS:- You can't move marines individually, and it causes problems frequently. - I like the stress system, but it's way too aggressive, and just gets annoying. - Marine dialogue is cringey and nonstop. Every 15 seconds someone is saying "It's quiet... too quiet." or something similar. It's literally constant. - They don't seem to have spent a dime on any military or law enforcement consultancy. They're still calling magazines "clips" in 2024. Everything military is cliche and unrealistic. - It doesn't seem like they're going to add any new content. You get what you get. - The second half of the final mission you're invincible and it's impossible to fail, and you don't even get to use your marines. It's very unsatisfying, and then the story ends pretty abruptly and poorly. Annnddddd, its DEI as all hell. Grab a beer if you plan on reading. The MC, Hayes, is a girlboss asian woman deputy administrator of a space station. She is surrounded by incompetent, rude, fat, cowardly, and lazy white men. She saves the day and escapes her ship, then commandeers an entire military operation alongside a sergeant despite having zero military experience. By the end of the game even the sergeant is out of commission and she's running everything, and shows up in the final mission in marine gear to suddenly be an invincible badass despite admitting earlier she has no idea how to use a gun. Haye's boss? Girlboss old lesbian haircut woman. The head doctor on ship, who bravely refuses to abandon her patients? Girlboss black woman. The compassionate psychiatrist who cares for the marines? Girlboss indian woman. The extremely competent head mechanic? Girlboss black woman. Dead sheriff you find that bravely died in a last stand defending her people? Girlboss black woman. Grizzled head of security you recruit as an ally? Old black man. About 2/3rds of the NPCs you meet in missions? Black women, and usually bald, for some reason. Haye's other boss? Fat slob white man who refuses to listen her about the aliens. Catcaller in the breakroom? White man. Coward who breaks and attracts the alien? White man. Scientist who betrays everyone and lets aliens on the ship? White man. Evil scientist that kidnaps sergeant's daughter? White man. Entire cult of evil alien worshipper enemies? ALL white men with southern accents. Sergeant Harper is an okay exception to the rule, but even he has to rely on Hayes and eventually succumbs to... headaches? The other sergeant is probably the best character despite little screen time, and he dies at the end for no reason. You can't customize your marines, so they end up 50/50 male and female (very realistic for any infantry unit) and about 10% of the time a white male.At the end of the story, Hayes sacrifices most, if not all, of the marines, including two major characters, instead of just leaving the planet, because she "made a promise" to Harper and had to get his daughter out. You could argue it's because of her psychic powers' potential, but that reason isn't even fleshed out or implied. Who need good writing when can just girlboss everything?

_childDocuments_.review: A solid real time tactics game and a solid Aliens game. Keep in mind: unlike what you might expect, you can't control individual marines. Squad always moved together and is controlled as a single entity(with some minor exceptions). It more or less makes sense in context(individual marines are practically helpless against aliens, after all), and is thematically fitting, but either way, it's more of a Cannon Fodder rather than Shogun Tactics. Oh, there' is a tactical pause too.All in all, worth its price and a must-buy on sale if you like Aliens universe or tactics games.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall this game is a EXCELLENT addition to the many aliens games through the years, mixing a solid blend of stealth and unique RTS combat goodness, well worth the cost. Details wise though, it definetly has some nasty rough edges, so lemme go over the good the bad and the ugly (aka: bad that wasnt a concious decision)Good+Combat is solid, each encounter is fun and is balanced on a knife edge. +Stealthing around the map leaving motion trackers and baiting enemies toward trapped areas is excellent+ Enemy variety is extremely good+ solid xcom style base with good upgrade varieties+ difficulty feels very well balanced. + enemy combat AI is surprisingly good, doing things such as trying to drag off downed marines. Bad-Story ranges from serviceable, to downright terrible, particularly toward the end.-Certain mini "Story" missions feel half baked and unnecessary -Final mission in particular is a colossal letdown both story and gameplaywise.Ugly-Voice acting gets extremely repeteative, and varies wildly in quality -There are some occationally nasty bugs that can ruin gameplay (such as being unable to rest and save in safe rooms)-Sometimes the "cinematic" camera will rip you away from combat to show you a story thing you ran past, which can get the squad killed. Gripes aside, having played virtually all of the other alien games out there, this is still one of the better offerings, and well worth the cost (I got it for a birthday gift, but would not be sad to have paid bucks for it)

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing! Must play for Aliens fans!I've been a huge fan of the franchise for almost 30 years. I've played nearly every mainstream Alien/Predator/AvP game and I can confidently say that this has been my favorite, and by no small margin. I never knew I needed an Aliens tactics game in my life, but here I am playing through the campaign a 2nd time on a harder difficulty instead of playing something else like D4 because nothing is quite hitting the spot like this has.Pros: Sound Track. The score has been amazing! Incredibly immersive.Atmosphere. Fantastically dark and foreboding.Gameplay. XCOM with Xenomorphs! "Let's rock!. The Sanity/Health system was fun to work around. I thought it would be a chore at first, but having to decide if I wanted to risk taking a squad out for a second time or letting them rest was really interesting. Sending a under leveled squad in while the stronger squad rested sometimes lead to my whole force getting wiped because I wasn't anticipating the increase in difficulty so quickly, and ended up loading a much earlier save and losing half an hour +. Sometimes I risked it for the biscuit and took my main squad on 2 missions in a row just to find out the next mission was extra hard and of critical importance and now I had a bunch of rookies going into a big fight... I really enjoyed the challenge and strategy.Story. (No spoilers) The story for the most part felt like it stayed true to the franchise. There were a couple of twists that turned my head a bit, but after thinking about it didn't seem completely out of question for the universe so I just let it slide and moved on. But all in all I enjoyed the campaign, not the most unique plot ever, but I had a great time.Customization. The character customization is quite good. Not the most options for changing marines appearances but decent enough. Multiple class options, and most of them have felt impactful in their own way.Monetization. I'm honestly shocked they released this at only $39.99USD. I would have gladly spent $60-70 on this game and felt it was worth every penny. As of writing this post the only Micro transaction I've seen for the game is a cosmetic dlc for only like $4.99USD which gave an armor skin option (for the entire platoon, not just 1 character like most games these days) and a Cat to bring a little fun to home base. This Imo is how "Micro" transactions SHOULD be. Micro, fun, game wide. No complaints whatsoever. No season passes or any of that nonsense in the game (as of writing).Should they ever release a campaign dlc or expansion I'll be buying it asap.--                                                                                                                      --Cons:Bugs. I've had some mostly minor bugs, but honestly it's been surprising how few I've run into for a newly released game. I had the faces of my squad stretch and contort horrifically while they ride the elevator. But it was pretty comical.The biggest issue I had was in one of the later missions I had made my squad hide behind cover, and after the fight 1/4 members wouldn't leave the cover no matter how many times I clicked all over the screen or tried to force the other 3 members to run through them to try and dislodge them. I eventually ended up leaving them behind to die, but thankfully they got attacked before I had gone too far and after they were downed I was able to use my Medic to revive them and then they could miraculously move again. Only ever happened once so I'm not overly concerned, but figured I should mention it.--                                                                                                      --Overall I'd say I very much so recommend this game! P.S If you read this far you are quite the trooper! I appreciate your time and hope any of this wall of text was helpful to you.

_childDocuments_.review: A surprisingly good real-time with pause tactical combat game.  The overall campaign is reminiscent of xcom, but it plays more like somebody threw in a dash of darkest dungeon after switching from turn based to real time.  The levels are large and interesting, the classes work well together, and the game rises in difficulty well.  I think the opening level when you have a real squad of marines was the strongest part of the game but the length was just about perfect, it ended right as I was ready to be done with the more stressful and more precision requiring late missions.The game finally gets stealth right by making stealth not a thing you need to do to live but one you want to do because fighting aliens wastes resources, generates stress, and advances an internal clock that makes successive encounters rougher.  It also accepts stealth through superior firepower, if you can kill something instantly even if you do it loud it doesn't trigger a hunt until an actual live alien spots your actual team, which leads to some interesting strategies.The story is perfectly servicable.  It exists, it's aliens, it won't really make you mad.  The voice actors and everything are good, but the game isn't trying for any fancy twists or big new lore in the setting, it's just executing a standard tale quite well.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of Alien, this game is a must play. With the exception of Alien Isolation, no other game comes close to re-creating the kind of tension you feel in the movies. The game play itself is quite smooth, and easy to pick up the controls. The main issue I suspect some players will have is adjusting to the combat, as it feels a lot like an X-COM game, until you initiate a fight. With X-COM you have the luxury of turn based combat, giving you all the time in the world to line up the perfect shot (and then miss) With Dark Descent it's real time (though you can slow time whilst executing orders) which really adds to the stressful feeling of trying to plan out your attacks and fallback plan when you suddenly find yourself being hunted by a swarm of Xenomorphs.The stress isn't just being felt by you either, your poor marines will be experiencing fatigue, and stress, in addition to the risk of life or limb when they are under attack.Missions and the story are in keeping with the feel of the Alien universe, the character dialogue is perfectly suited to what is going on in game, and in general the game really feels like it has been built by people who have some genuine love for the IP.The game has a few small bugs, but nothing that will break it. Hopefully we'll see some DLC/expansions in the future, as this game has everything it needs to build on a very solid foundation.

_childDocuments_.review: While it can be a little buggy and is definitely a more difficult game, I thoroughly enjoyed my time with it. None of the strangeness I encountered was game-breaking, though it did cost me some damaged marines here and there. The atmosphere is great, the sounds and music pulled right from the franchise, and the missions are worth exploring. I'm an Alien and Xcom fan, but I have to say the comparisons to Xcom only come in to play with the management section of things, and while it is almost a copy of those screens at times, it is very minimal. Research is instant, upgrades are instant, and there really aren't a ton of them. Other than the little things, like eggs reappearing when you go through doors, or not being able to click on parts of the map when a piece of scenery, like a rail-line, was in the way, my biggest gripe was the way cutscenes, both cinematic and in-game were integrated. Oftentimes, they would put aliens in positions they never would've got to, or cut you off from other things, or just completely remove you from a mission with no warning. The actual map exploration and fighting are really where this game shines and my brother was playing it at the same time so we could compare experiences. I was more stealth, relying on the silenced sniper to go undetected as long as possible, and he went in shooting. I like that there are so many approaches and tactics to each situation, and most of the gear options are all quite useful. Solid Alien game that I hope we see more of in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Game perfectly encapsulates the look, sound, and feel of the "Aliens" movie. Probably the best game that's captured that vibe (just as well as Alien Isolation captured the "Alien" movie)The game combines a surface level between mission screen of X-Com, pretty similar squad management, with a unique RTS style gameplay. You control an entire squad of marines as a single unit. Its a bit weird at first and ultimately it sacrifices the ability to micromanage with a streamlined game play that works 80% of the time.85% of the game is explained very well. the remaining 15% can be frustrating at times (like how you can't train marines past level 4 in training camp, but the game doesn't tell you so your marine just sits there doing nothing and is also unavailable for missions). There are also a number of bugs that range from annoying to game stopping. Which can be frustrating as while the save system adds a lot to the tension, it can be annoying to have to redo anywhere from 10-30 minutes of mission. If you're a fan of the Aliens universe, and particularly of Cameron's "Aliens", this game is a 9/10 and a must play. If you're a fan of tactical strategy games, this game is probably 7/10 and worth a look.

_childDocuments_.review: "Another glorious day in the Corps! A day in the Marine Corps is like a day on the farm. Every meal's a banquet! Every paycheck a fortune! Every formation a parade! I LOVE the Corps!"This is the Aliens game I have always wanted. One that shows that the Colonial Marines are an elite force of ultimate badasses who can turn xenos into mincemeat while reflecting that the situation is utterly terrifying for them and that these aliens can overwhelm with ridiculous ease. I love how the game makes discretion the better part of valour, encouraging you to find ways to avoid confrontation until absolutely necessary but gives you the tools to unload with everything you've got when that happens. It's tactical top down strategic combat with a survival horror coat of paint and a dose of X-Com. Hoo-rah indeed.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: It's barely a positive.First of all, it's a solid game.Has that XCOM feeling, but the combat and movement are all real time (with slow-mo).It makes the world look more alive, and gives the tension (you can't just think sitting still).However, there are 2 glaring negatives:1. Stealth system is a core mechanic in game, yet it's the most un-fun. I love stealth games. I loved Dishonored series, Assassin's creed, and hell, I played bunch of rogue in Skyrim, too. However, the stealth in this game is just not fun. The enemy move pattern is not predictable, and can see you from outside your vision, and the game barely gives you time to react to hide. (You might just rage-quit because of this in prologue even at lowest difficulty). Did I also mention that the game is really dark environment with black Alien? You also can't tell which obstacles really block the vision, so you are constantly guessing. Oh, and the maps are designed really poorly in terms of stealth (for thematic purpose, they look great), so hiding spots really don't exist where you want them.  I've had numerous moments where I was stuck in a corner of a map, since the enemies would just move back and forth, and there is no way out. So hell, it's time to take out the big guns, right? But that leads to second problem.2. This "hunt" time. If an Alien finds you, they will enter a hunt mode, even if you kill the Alien that spotted you right away. And once this hunt time starts, it lasts for certain amount of time, And Aliens in vicinity will constantly come towards you during that time. And the funny thing is, if you didn't finish off an Alien by the end of the hunt time (they barely have not seen you yet), they can see you, and instantly trigger another hunt time. But hey, why is it so bad that this hunt time keeps going? Oh, that's because your squad constantly gains stress during this time. And this keeps adding random debuffs to your team that synergize with each other to completely wreck you. In hard difficulty, this got annoying very quickly, especially at the nest area, where enemies spawn from every direction.I just finished the first mission "Dead Hills" in Hard difficulty, and I did not enjoy the "hard" part at all.There is a lot of other minor annoying factors in the game, that slowly drained my patience as well. (I really hate the main character, and every character in the game has 2 digit IQ. But hey, it's for PLOT)So, I'm gonna give it another go at lower difficulty.TL;DR: XCOM, but real time action + stealth. Stealth is a main feature of the game, but very stress inducing and not that fun. The game is also just rough in terms of game design. If you haven't played XCOM, I would recommend that game over this (for similar genre).

_childDocuments_.review: A real-time tactical game with RPG elements, stealth and persistent world.  Aestethically the game mines the licence well, from the iconic looks and sound effects to the moody background music. The environments are cluttered depressive retro-futurictic complexes and the natural environment consists of barren rocks and constant rain or drizzle. Characters are customizable, but not with a great amount of detail.  The game mechanics are a blend of XCOM 2, Warhammer 40k Dawn of War 2 or Red Solstice. The tactical phase is strictly real-time with whole squad acting as one unit. The game can be significantly slowed in a "planning mode" that allows comfortable use of special abilities. There is a heavy emphasis on stealth. ambushes and avoidance, since constant fighting increases enemy activity and drains resources and mental health of marines. The mission maps are persistent and can be abandoned and revisited. This is an important game mechanic and I usually finished the objectives in at least two visits. The strategic layer is turn based and allows for training, healing and equiping the squad. There are also various events that can grant resources or handicaps. In the later half of the game a "doom clock" is counting down to the campaign failure, similar to Avatar project in XCOM 2. This cannot be slowed or reverted, but it is managable (and can be disabled in settings of a new campaign). The soldiers gain experience based solely on fullfilled mission objectives or training on the base. Leveling up unlocks new equipment and abilities and allows removal of negative traits. Management of negative traits and mental health is very important and one of the limiting factors on how often the squad can go on missions.  The story is pretty standard for Aliens, with W-Y corporation trying to use the aliens, now with added cultists and rebelling colonists. Even with some campiness it was interesting and had some nice twists and turns.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Alien games are always hit or miss, and this one hit it on the head. Didn't think you could do horror well in a squad based tactical RTS, but i'm pleasantly surprised. A really solid game that can only be made better. Hoping this Genre and style of game takes off a bit more as it's refreshing to tactical strategy games that isn't turn based.Quality of Life Recommendations:--------------------------------------- Time it takes to swap between menus on the Otago- Not having to 'hold click' for every decision. Make it so I can shift click to make an instant decision. That way it won't be accidental, but I don't have to hold a mouse for over 30 seconds just to use all my doctors. - Please reduce the amount of times I have to hear 'Deputy Administrator Hayes' in the Otago Menus- Marine path choosing in some instances, if 3/4 marines are going down one hallway i really don't want one of my marines to split off to the other hallway especially when i'm running from a big bad.----------------------------------------

_childDocuments_.review: The REAL Alien: Colonial Marines!Don't be afraid of the difficulties presented by this game, I think you can enjoy the game at the easiest level while still getting the true essence of being on a  Xeno infested planet as a Marine. The atmosphere is near perfect, Aliens fan will immediately enjoy the art style, music, sound track and endless Aliens quotes. The gameplay is really fun, RTS crossover with Xcom style of squad management is a really good mix. The games wants you to be stealthy and you are role playing as a US Colonial Marine stranded on an Alien planet, so it should be rough! That said, this does not mean the game is a third person splinter cell stealth game, no. There's plenty of actions! Lots of guns, boom boom, and face huggers. And death... depending on the difficulty. [Not so good stuff]A few gripes exist in the game, first is the lacklustre voice reactions in some situation, at base, the same voice gets played over and over, music cuts off. And some in combat situation, same voice over and over. But oddly when a Marine gets nabbed by the Queen, they suddenly becomes a mute.Also the ending raises more questions than answers, sequel baiting scenes and some plot holes. But it's not as bad as Alien Prometheus or covenant. In fact, I really enjoyed the art design in the last level.

_childDocuments_.review: I was SUPER excited to buy and play this game. First I tried it on Gamefly for the PS5, wasn't a huge fan of the controls, and knew it'd play better on PC. I was right. So I was off to the races, and had a blast doing so!....And then I started noticing things. Bad things. Buggy things.Squad doesn't behave optimally at times....Squad doesn't use certain abilities - I have a sniper rifle, but I cannot use it, so is it automatic? When? I have literally never seen it go off, despite having a member equipped with it?Aliens seem a lot tougher past the first mission. Not just talking the runners, the minibosses, etc, talking about drones that seem to have gotten tougher with MY marine's upgrades. I don't think a game is supposed to reward your squad, get your squad stronger, but also make the aliens stronger by comparison. That's literally moving the goalpost. It's a cardinal sin.Then the game breaker bug. Fought a queen in Mission 5, one marine got facehuggered, queen was pounding on him, I get the facehugger off, queen knocks the medic to the ground, I get the medic up, finish getting the facehugger off, and the marine is just down. No coma. No facehugger. Nothing. Just down. I win the fight (queen was almost dead at the time anyway) and everyone is doing OK, but that marine that's down, is still down. I wait a minute. Five minutes. Ten minutes. He's not getting up. Not dead, no coma, not huggered, just knocked down. I cannot carry him. Well, I carry on with the mission, and get my squad - minus the downed marine - to the elevator. I think, at least I can call the elevator, and go to another floor, maybe the marine will get up then, or I can come back. Nope. Instead, the elevator is just sitting there, waiting for the marine to join up with the squad.The game is softlocked, and now I need to reload.Oh, and the autosaves in this game - which is basically autosave only for a "purist" experience - is going to make me lose A LOT of progress.Look guys and girls. This game is riddled with bugs. Don't buy it. The cheap price accompanies a cheap experience, and I will reload my save, but I am so, so, so disappointed they didn't do more Q&A on this before release. It's a buggy mess.

It can get very stressful if you don't know what you're doing or if you're in the earlier parts of the game.No need to restart your progress, just bite the bullet, learn it the hard way, lose some troops and enjoy the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 The environments are fantastic and so is the story it reminds me of aliens the movieCombat is both slow and fast with the game being a true RTS, in the game you will be expected to react to situations on the fly in which a single mistimed reload or foot out of place can, and will, result in disaster or even death.Instead of games like xcom you don’t control the individual marines but the whole squad, while we are talking about the boys in green let’s get into some detail. Each marine starts out as a rifleman and with one negative trait which effects how they do, it can range from stress to how much noise they make when sneaking around which is a bigger part of the game that you might think.The more you engage Xenos the more the hive becomes aware of your team, and the more it dose the more (and bigger) Xenos will be out, which brings me to the APC, the APC is a mobile weapons platform that acts as in mission transport and evac, if things get too hot before you can complete all objectives don’t be afraid to retreat back to the APC or even leave the area, you can always come back and complete objectives.The USS Ortego acts as your home base, and in this respect is very similar to modern xcom games as you will be jumping place to place unlocking new weapons, researching new xeno based technologies, and upgrading your soldiers in which there is many different classes, while we are on the topic let’s talk about the weapons, each and every weapon had very specific roll (besides the pulse rifle), so far I’ve only unlocked the smart gun which dose wonders in open spaces but in tight spaces it struggles for example unlike its previous depictions in games In conclusion, I’m not even 20% though the game yet I honestly can say it’s one of, if not my favorite games of the last two years
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:Engaging storyIts has the second movie feelingHas some good ideas from X-com when in your baseIt is not just a move from point A to point B like the Starship Troopers gameCons:Really hard gameHas a steep learning curveCG and character faces look awfulI've spent 1 hour and 15 minutes on the first mission with the marines alone. It is dark, you really have to trust the motion tracker not to stay on edge while exploring. Someone said in another review something that is true: the game becomes punishing the more xenos you kill. I've bought this game expecting it to be hard though, I didn't want it to be a walk in the park. In the Aliens movie only one marine survives in the end, remember? I've had to retreat from the first mission with 4 wounded marines and almost no ammo, completing only 6/14 objectives. We've survived to see another day. Expect really long and difficult missions, even with easier settings aliens can hurt you badly with acid when you kill them. It is just like the movie.It is a really interesting game so far. I'd say it is 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: The game designers really nailed the tension and action of the Aliens movie, when the motion tracker starts beeping I feel it in my chest. The big encounters are relentless, I don't even realize I'm holding my breathe until my guys get out safe. Game plays like a real-time X-Com and so far I'm having a blast.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: I am an A L () E N S fan and not an RTS player and I am thoroughly enjoying this game. The story isn't revolutionary but it is serviceable for a campaign within the the Aliens universe. Dialogue is a little wonky.The game play is intense. Xenomorphs feel like an actual threat you either have to avoid or use teamwork and strategy to defeat. Managing your marines has a lot of detail; besides customizing and upgrading, you have to give them medical treatment and trauma counseling. Your squad can crack under pressure and need to be managed as you would if you were a platoon leader.The environment, music, and SFX are straight out of the movies and do justice to the films. Game is challenging even on medium difficulty. One bad call, and your squad will get wiped out. It's a stressful game in all the right ways; watching your motion tracker, welding doors shut to keep xenos out, hunkering down with sentry guns and covering your avenues of approach when the hive sends a horde after your team.   Overall solid 8/10. Great game if your a fan of the Alien films and/or an RTS gamer.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic. It's a bit rough in certain regards and needs some help with optimization at the time of this review, but it was well worth the asking price of $40 USD. It's exactly the kind of experience I would hope for in an Aliens RTS ranging from extremely intense Xeno encounters and using every tool available to survive a mission. I look forward to any potential DLCs or Sequels this game may get and will be happy to revisit this title in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Great overall niche persistent (the map remains unchanged if your squad redeploys to the same location) strategy game which I hope I see more of with a decent story although some bits of the story are not tied off because more pressing matters arise but is still very true to the source material (please do yourself a favour and go watch the first and second Aliens movies to really appreciate this, this game is taken straight from the second Aliens movie but you have to watch the first one to understand it). I recommend that you play on hard difficulty (I’m currently on medium) because early in the game playing on medium you can get a pretty fearless squad of marines together who are well equiped but still requires you to do a little bit of thinking as you can’t change the difficulty mid game unfortunately. I feel hard would make the game more immersive which I intend to do next playthrough. The psychological effect on your squad and how they deal with the horrors of combat  as you push your marines further down the rabbit hole is a really cool mechanic too that I haven’t really seen before - it makes them feel very human (I know I would be scared as all hell if I were in a similar position). As they gain more combat experience, they become more brave which will allow them to cope better with the horrors of combat but sometimes they never really get over the trauma completely. Permadeath of marines can also easily be bypassed by just reloading to an earlier save when someone you like dies - I feel this could have been fixed by only allowing saving on the command bridge.Hopefully Tindalos Interactive does the same move with Battlefleet Gothic: create a first iteration, collect data and feedback, then create a perfected second iteration. I can literally still hear the ringing of the motion tracker in my head when I go to sleep, they must be nearby… - 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Disable the death clock and the game is a solid 9/10.The story is rather good, character build up was great, unit types and classes are great. I ran into minor issues with some event triggers and the death clock is quiet terrible due to some of the random events repeating constantly. The game does not keep many saves so this can bite you bad (restarting the campaign). I recommend turning it off to enjoy the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: I have never wanted a game to get just a bit more post launch support more than i want this game to get it. It is so close to being perfect, but there are a few things that really drag it down. the biggest problem probably being cutsences railroading you into boss fights, or bad tactical positions. Sometimes you are given a pop up warning you about the upcoming danger sometimes you are not. The iron man mode also provides 2 slots instead of one and doesn't auto save very often so instead of uping tension by making all your choices irrevocable it just makes save scumming time consuming but no less effective. The railroading, the iron man save system and the sound mixing on your ship are my 3 biggest problems. wish steam had a mixed option, still worth getting  if its on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: WARNING - potential spoilers! One of the best Aliens game I have played! Almost as captivating as Alien Isolation! This game is not without its flaws, with some bugs, limited voice acting cast and so on. Yet it adrenaline puping action with the perfect vibe, it captures the essence of all aliens films I think - some hsip design and the final level take inspiration from the first Alien, the whole marines and their equipment, Otago, their ship, the planet where it takes place - all from Aliens. The prison level, the mines and the wyland yutani commandos are based on Alien 3, the human/xeno hybrids take inspiration from Alien Ressurection, Maeko's design as well as the space jockey city remind me of prometheus, the large eggs look a lot like David's giant eggs for the proto xenomorph from Prometheus, there are various types of aliens. One thing missing is the predalien, but this is not a crossover game. Anyways, very fun experience!

_childDocuments_.review: First: I play offline, so the shown game time is WRONG. Steam should check my achievements, with that little game time i could have never reached level 10 achievements.This game is, what the movie Alien 3 should have been, a worthy successor to the great second movie. Good story, brilliant atmosphere and lotz of stress. (and thats not a bad thing in that  other games i dont like stress but here its great...) In some ways its like x-com, but the core gameplay, the action, feels like a new genre. Basically its a tactical real time rts, where you command your 4-5 man team as one RTS unit. (so you can play this game without pause, but i dont recommand that at the beginning, or the aliens will tear you apart...) I prefer turn based games normally, but in this game rts is a MUUUCH better solution.The alien ai is good, it patrols and hunts for prey, reacts to noise, evades fire when possible, makes jump attacks, that you can evade and tries to flank your sentry turrets. The game runs very good in high detail on my old 5700 XT in 1080p, WITHOUT FSR. With FSR everything runs good on ULTRA max Detail. The sound is perfect, it delivers great atmosphere. Only downside: For me the game is too short. 40 hours is ok for 35 Euros, but i would have prefered paying more and having a longer experience. My advice: Play it on HARD from the beginning, otherwise the great horror action tactic trip is over too soon.I will definitly buy every add on that brings new story campaigns. And a second part with maybe more complex strategic elements, would be great too. A little sidenote at the end: This game is 20 years after part 3, so the marines have better technology: plasma guns, tanks that arent damaged by alien acid, motion trackers that detect non moving aliens. Even a gas that reduces the numbers of aliens on the whole planet. Otherwise you would simply have no chance, against the masses of aliens. (over 25000 if all humans are infected)  GREAT GAME for a fair price. For me the best game i played in years, but i am a big aliens fan, so thats a little subjectiv opinion. And after the two patches i had nearly no bugs at all.Update: Sadly i have many bugs in my second playthrough. But only in the olduvai mine level.  1. Once i coudnt rest, it was no hunt, it was a rest room icon and all doors where shut.2. I could rest once in another room, with no shut doors.3. I wanted to evacuate and a drone attacked when my soldiers climbed into the tank. So far so good. But when i ordered my marines to climb out and fight, they couldnt fight the drone, it was unkillable and slaughtered my marine.Played that game a lot and only TODAY so many bugs ? Maybe because i play on hard now, with limited safes ? Another patch is needed.Btw: With my new 4070 FSR 2 looks great. Not that i would need it, but it looks better AND runs cooler.Update 2: The ending feels as if you hadnt any time and money left to make it as it should be: On the one hand this great looking "giger city", on the other hand only 3 soldiers, inkl. maeko, with std. pulse rifles and immortality ??? I imagine this "walking and running level" how it could be, with 5 marines, maeko, stern and the sargeant, actually fighting their way through, like it is done in all the other missions. The boss alien could be immortal and only scared away with flame thrower and grenades for example and of course you would have to guard cassandra all the time. THIS would be the ending this great game deserves. Nevertheless, I LOVE THIS GAME, BEST GAME 2023, for me. Update 3: Seems the bugs are connected with the difficulty: in my fst. playthrough on medium nearly no bugs. In my second on hard i had a gamebreaking bug in the olduvai mine. And now, in my nightmare playthrough i cant finish pharos tower, even if its finished already. Besides, the bug, that its not always possible to end some skills (surpressing fire), is at best annoying, sometimes it kills your whole team. Some minor bugs like aliens that are dead and  still stand, or dead aliens that are shown as collectable samples on the minimap and arent collectable .... more bugfixing is needed. But all in all most bugs are manageable.When the bugs are fixed, this game should get an IRON MAN mode. Since the game is so short, i really would love to find out, how far i can get on nightmare, WITHOUT reloading at all. :)

_childDocuments_.review: Of the many, many games based on Cameron's sequel this might be my favourite yet - an absolute blast from start to finish.The stress and trauma system in particular is excellent, and very similar to the one from the recent (and equally excellent) Alien TTRPG. I'd pay full price fow whatever dlc or sequels this team wants to put out, but I would love to see them be given the green light to make a full cRPG based on that system
