_childDocuments_.review: compared to the newest XCOMs:+ dense atmosphere (scary as ♥♥♥)+ ammo and all resources are finite, make bullets count+ arsenal mostly taken from the movie, and even the highest-tech weapon has its downsides compared to the "basic" guns, so every gun has its pros and cons. + so many references to the movie and they are done right+ everything is in real time, but you can slow down the time (still no time to pause and think, which adds to the atmosphere)+ no save scumming+ very realistic/believable fights, monsters, interactions+ lot of motivation to use the optional stealth mechanics+ all your soldiers have negative traits and most of your choices are either bad or worse+ I expected no story, but its actually on par with comics+ each mission is slightly different and you can always go back to the previous mission to pick up where you have left+ the game cracks few situational jokes that hit the spot. + all units are controlled as a squad, cant select individual marines (its usually good)- all units are controlled as a squad, cant select individual marines (its sometimes bad)- less friendly UI both in missions and in base, lot of extra clicks are required, the icons are not so obvious (but add to the 80s dystopian feel)- price (get it at 20 € or less)- cutscene graphics (all budget went to Aliens, which look amazing, humans look bad)- lot of the story is told by datapads you collect, but over half of them give boring info, that only build the atmosphere (capitalism bad, religion good, everything is hopeless)- the super annoying repeating voice lines everytime something triggers. You will hear the same message 30 times every mission. And you cant turn it off. = get someone to hold your hand when it gets scary, but go for it, its a good game

_childDocuments_.review: Cool game, unexpected and has some original twists to usual squad tactics games.The different aliens are well introduced and lead to some interesting cinematic moments.Some minor criticism:- it is difficult to get into and understand all the mechanisms. I only found out about the silencer for scouts halfway through for instance.- the daily events are often punitive, and bad luck at the start sets you up for failure.- on higher difficulties, you basically play the game in slow mode.Defo recommended for any tactics fan looking for something different
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Too much stealth. The game sold me on shooting aliens, but turns out it's a bare-bones stealth walk or let's sit and wait simulator. The most optimal way to play is to avoid as much confrontation with aliens as possible. I wanted to play as Corporal Hicks, but the game keeps forcing me to play as Newt.Another immersion breaking aspect is that aliens are terrifying not because of their nature (or their numbers), but because of how pathetically weak your marines are.Last but not least, beware that you cannot save at will, something which I find simply retarded in this day and age. You have a choice between two auto save systems, neither of which respects your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Weyland-Yutani Corporation is at it once more. Building an XCOM-esque RTS set in the Aliens universe, letting me wake up to breakfast in bed and another day in the Corps.Some of the animations/character syncing in the cut scenes are a little janky, but for the initial release, that's expected. So far at ~4 hours of game play, I’ve had 0 bugs or issues to complain or write about.Plays as advertised, with an intriguing story, and some interesting mechanics. At USD 39.99, worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Can't recommend this enough, it's right up there with RDR2 and Days Gone for addiction.The top down team strategy is a totally different play style to everything else I own, reminds me of Syndicate on the Amiga 500 in 1993 (30 years ago!)It's crazy hard & that makes it feel like being a character in the original movie... scary ♥♥♥♥!It can be a little buggy at times but the devs are working on it and keep the subreddit up to date so you know it's being fixed.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Genre - Squad Based RTS in the Aliens Universe (Xcom but with real time action, and the ability to pause)Best Single Player Aliens Game I've played, trumps Alien Isolation for me, as some of the game mechanics in that were just frustrating and dated. This seems to play more fluidly. I am worried about how much difficulty will ramp up, as only done the 1st mission (which seemed balanced on medium).I'd put Fireteam as the best Multiplayer Aliens game though. But between Fireteam and Descent, I'd take this.Aliens versus Predator on the Xbox wasn't a bad little single player RTS game, and this has its feel in places.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Never really played a squad based game before (could never quite click with them), not sure if its my like of the movies but I thought this game was superb. The pacing was good, progress felt meaningful, and in the main I thought the story telling was excellent. If you like the movies or you enjoy squad / RTS games, highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely surprise. I didn't think anything good could come to the  franchise after the sublime  came out and was, apparently, a commercial failure. The Steam user  said this game is to  what  was to  and I know what he means. I'll give a full review when I complete the game, but 6.5 hours in, on Hard difficulty, this is tense as all hell just like the best parts of , you feel limited on resources and you get punished for not being careful, and it isn't just another -ripoff as it is all in real-time - adding extra pressure to your decisions in combat.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, what a fun game.  If you like tactical games and the Alien's franchise, download now. This one is easy to immerse yourself in. For those wanting a challenge, this game can be dialed up to be very difficult, but there is also Story Mode if you don't like a little stress (I started with Story-mode to learn the game-play and it was too easy, so jumped up to 'normal' pretty quick). You still need to be able to read a map regardless, since your  objectives are not always dead ahead. The developers seem to be doing good patching any bugs, I've only run into one bug in 21 hrs of game-play (just loaded from last save point and all was good from there).No performance issues so far with the following:    Intel i5    16 GB RAM    NVIDIA RTX 3050    144Hz display
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: This is a surprisingly atmospheric game. The game is filled with the spirit of the alien universe. The nervous beeping of a motion sensor, brave music, armored personnel carriers and the doomed heroism of the Marines. I would like to be proud of humanity, which is faced with a xenos threat. I have not regretted a single moment of my life spent on this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: As an Alien, and Aliens movie-lover this game has blown me away. The atmosphere is just so perfect. It has no pretentious level-up system, no big talent-trees and it is just so fitting. My marines all have their own negative perk to start with. It suits the atmosphere of the movies so well. While playing missions, I feel constantly on my nerves. The sound of an alien approaching on the scanner takes me back to the 1978 film. And it scares the hell out of me sometimes when I get caught off guard. The stress system I think is very well designed. It keeps you constantly debating whether to press on, or maybe take some rest. This game is unique, I don't know of any other games that have similar gameplay. The fact that a game like xcom is turnbased, where this game isn't makes it even more scary. No minutes of carefully debating your every move. No, you have to move, NOW, make a mistake and it can always turn out to be fatal (I played on hard immediately, since I figured an Alien game should be hard, right?), but making no decision is often even worse. The lore, the story, the maps, the characters, the sometimes clunky gameplay, it all feels like you are stuck in a very bad place just like the people on the movies. I hope SOOOOOO much this game will get a sequel or prequel or whatever quel because I haveenjoyed it throughout! Some minuses: Replayability is not that high. It is more like a great experience, but after you had that experience, and know the plot, there is not much need to play again, for me at least. I have played the game two times and it cost me 98 hours so far (in the 2nd playthrough now). That is all I can think of actually lol. Highly recommend you play the game on hard from the get-go. If you are like me, and only experience it once or twice, make it the perfect Alien experience by challenging yourself. Keep frosty, soldier. Salute!
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: I'd consider myself to be a pretty big fan of the Alien universe. This game certainly has a great deal of fanfare so my opinion is going to be a bit bias. That being said, if it were a dumpster fire of a game, I'd say so. That's not the case with this game. If you're into RTS and Aliens, it's a no brainer.It's a pretty challenging game at times and it looks like I'll wrap up the game in roughly 35 hours. That's not too shabby for $19.99. That's right. I got it on sale, but price tag of $39.99 seems pretty fair to me.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Not as polished as I would like, but it captures the feeling of the Aliens (1986) movie. I found myself yelling "Marines! We are leaving!" far more often than I thought I would, which is a glowing endorsement to me. I prefer the squad-based playstyle over something like XCOM and I found the classes unique enough to warrant bringing one of each along. The story is engaging without leaning too heavily on the nostalgia factor. I just wish there were more missions and that it used the Aliens soundtrack more than it does. I hope that we get a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Kinda like "Gears Tactics", but not so polished and not so deep. Has some UI bugs, but the "Aliens" setting and stealth are why I liked it.  On the highest difficulty, you can get the right amount of tension and horror. But longer you play, the more you will be steamrolling the whole map with gigachads in your team
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic if you like the Alien franchise and the movie Aliens in particular. It captures the atmosphere of the films perfectly. Gameplay is fun and challenging enough to evoke a feeling of fear I thought impossible with a top-down strategic game. All the little systems and game mechanics work well together to give you an Alien experience that is only rivaled by Alien: Isolation (although this is a very different game). In some places (like character faces and animation in the cutscenes) one can see that the budget was rather low for this title. But man did they make such a good with game with limited resources. They focused on the things that mattered. Many big studios could learn a lot from studios like this (or Rockfish Games to name another one) that make great and in many ways better games with a fraction of the budget that the AAA (or even AAAA 😊) titles get these days
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a while since I played a game until finishing it.  This game is amazing, you will never get bored while playing it.  It is super hard, even in the story mode you can die.   I finished it in Story Mode and now I am playing it in standard mode and I'm at level 8 but it is so hard that I am stuck.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a good game but the bugs in this game are more deadly and terrifying than the aliens! Imagine just barely getting through a level with just the thick of your skin only to discover the switch you need to flip to get to the next level is broken because of a bug, and then you have to replay the level all over again! The game can also really benefit from allowing players to change the difficulty during the game. We dont all have the luxury of vast amounts of time to devote to games.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: A very unique XCOM esque experience. The atmosphere is perfect for any Alien fan and kept me on edge for my entire playthrough. The story itself wasn't ground breaking but was good enough. If you enjoyed any of the recent Alien novels, this falls seemlesly with that world and makes me excited for a sequel or some DLC to further explore the alien universe and go off on another bug hunt!
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, a good game. Does have some performance issues and bugs at this moment, but it is being actively worked on and improved. The story and plot is a bit cheesy, but I come to expect that from Aliens. If you like taking a more tactical approach to things this may be a good game for you. XCOM meets Aliens with a hint of TD sections with an endless hoard.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Only @ 2 hours into game I got stuck in the barracks screen. Spent several hours trying to fix the issue, based on recommendations on the steam support site. Nothing worked including deleting and reinstalling game. Asked for my money back and was rejected as I played the game over the 2 hour maximum.  Since the bug occurs around that time, and time spent trying to fix issue counts against the 2 hour rule, I was pissed. DO NOT BUY THIS GAME!
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot of interlocking systems that make a really fun game. Marines get wounded, stressed, they freak out, they run out of ammo, have the wrong special weapon in the wrong position,  they die. I've actually had moments where I feel stressed just like Gorman in the AC. I'm trying to have them retreat without running while more & more xenos close in from all sides while my Marines are yelling iconic lines (sometimes too often). The missions seem pretty simple at first, you point where the squad goes, they go. Doing cool automatic behaviors like taking turns looking down a branching corridor as they cross. But the missions have some variety to them. Some require quick movement & not getting bogged down. Others are best approached with a slow methodical base of fire style of play. Sometimes you want to make your squad run like hell, other times that gets your Marines killed. I spent the first half of the game stressing out about Aliens seeing my guys & galls & ripping them apart or exploding into an acid spray that puts down my smart gunner. After a while I felt confident to just make war on the bugs. Then my squad got so stressed out that they all developed phobias & psychosis.The character models between cut scenes seem like cutting edge PS1 models. But the story is engaging enough to be it's own Aliens film or comic series. I just hope mods come out for this game. Because I want to play it over and over.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: "THIS GAMES A FREAKIN LAWN MOWER"Jokes aside the game is incredibly unbalanced even on normal difficulty. I can appreciate a challenge but when one single facehugger spots you past mission 4 every freaking alien within a half mile radius zeroes in on your position. If you are lucky enough and manage to survive the onslaught of that the difficulty level of the map will rise and you will likely get a second worse onslaught horde. The game literally forces you to exploit cheese tactics like multiple sentries, exploiting the trucks invulnerability and OP cannon, deployable motion trackers as bait for either of the previous two, Or exploiting suppressed sniper rifles.Normal difficulty 2/4 should not require countless resets and cheesy tactics and hours of struggle to barely make it through. I am a huge fan of the alien franchise and with some minor tweaks to balance I could give this a thumbs up but in its current state I cannot.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: After almost 30 hours I’ve finally finished my first Aliens: Dark Descent campaign on medium difficulty. Thoughts so far is that it's an absolutely incredible, nerve racking, and immersive game. Perfect pairing for XCOM 2 and Alien fans. A bit buggy here and there but the devs have shown they take constructive feedback and plan on fixing known bugs. I do wish the tutorials covered more gameplay mechanics such as specialists abilities and how to rotate the sentry turret when you place it down but that’s what Aliens: Dark Descent content creators excel in helping with right now. I also hear the motion tracker beeping even when I'm not playing this game
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: A surprisingly good RTS, has an xcom lite feeling about it with enough variation to stand apart with its own twist on the genre. Character customisation is a bit fugly and limited but good enough. There's a slight lack of polish and a few little glitches but they are fairly rare and not game breaking. Worth a buy for RTS enjoyers and well worth it if you like the setting and lore of the Aliens franchise.The story is like one from the old dark horse comics. Focus have stated on their site the game is about 20 to 30 hours long but that seems like the time it would take if you made no mistakes, a lot of players are going to easily hit that mark in a few days and get plenty more time out of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Aliens: Dark Descent is without a doubt one of the most unique, intricate and challenging games I've ever played. The absolutely stunning visuals and aesthetics, alongside the intense gameplay and atmosphere make up for a truly immersive experience. Punishing yet rewarding, Dark Descent is sci-fi at its finest.Stay frosty, marines!
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: Its a solid single-player strategy game, with elements of xcom and alien swarm without being clones of either.There is no base building but between missions you go to your ship and can upgrade your troops/skip days to generate resources and heal at the cost of making the aliens stronger if you skip too many days.My only criticism is you can easily exploit and get unlimited resources by skipping days with little penalty (alien strength maxes out at level 5) before doing the mission that activates the "Death Clock".Do yourself a favour and turn off the Death Clock for your first playthrough as it prevents you from going back and exploring every mission fully before completing the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: This game took me almost 45 hours to complete on Normal.Really solid game with a good enough story, the narrative carried me to the end, because the gameplay was getting a bit repetitive. The locations were varied enough for the game to not look samey.Main cons were lack of polish, some objectives didn't want to trigger, occasional bug, one crash and lack of Category 2 Xenomoprhs (only two of them).Somehow I doubt that there will be a DLC, but I would welcome one, especially one that would add more Cat 2 Xenomoprhs.
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: This has been the first Alien's game in a long time to really feel like it captures the fear of the marines. Great story and can't just go guns blazing for a change which is refreshing. It can seem really hard but stick with it and read the hints etc and you'll soon be loving it. Can't really fault it so far but the RNG parts can really mess your run through up :)
_childDocuments_.name: Aliens: Dark Descent

_childDocuments_.review: The Meh: They really undersell the role of stealth in this game, it is a way bigger factor than I expected going in. I think I might have been more into it if it was turn-based? Hard to say. I understand the design decision, it just wasn't fun for me. If you get excited for that kind of gameplay in an RTS specifically, try it out! I found the combination awkward, personally, and had wished they went more in the XCOM direction.The +++: Atmosphere and authenticity are all there, this really feels like an Aliens game, perfectly captures the spirit of the second movie (which also had its share of stealth moments.) The ---: My negative review is mostly for the technical instability, I hit probably 3 major bugs or crashes in my playthrough before calling it quits and requesting a refund. I'll keep an eye on it though, should they ever go back and fix that, if for nothing else than encouraging studios to make more Alien games.

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably the best Aliens content we've received next to Alien: Isolation in a decade. It's also a simple squad tactical strategy game that can often panic you into fatal mistakes. The pros:1. The plot finally does something for this series other than "alien egg starts infestation." Very clearly based on both the TTRPG and old comic book/novel lore, Dark Descent makes me want to dive into the universe that Aliens is set in. In fact, it makes you feel like the Xenomorph is just one small piece to a larger story waiting to be told. They are what the Reapers are to Mass Effect, essentially. Also, this game will definitely piss off Ridley Scott, which is a plus.2. You are required to take your balls out of your purse and push on, gradually upgrading your squad, equipment, rescuing engineers, medics or marine recruits. Your marines are both cannon fodder and also your most valuable asset, so the game forces you to think long term as well as short term. If I try to save my smartgunner as she's dragged into the hive, will I lose my other high level Sniper and Tekker? 3. The interiors and exteriors of Lethe and the numerous stations and ships you're on are so detailed beyond what most would consider necessary, and that IS a good thing. You can somehow get lost in the architecture of the Weyland-Yutani living quarters while also forcing your squad to lay down suppressive fire and run for their lives. The planet itself has multiple biomes and even the desolate township of Dead Hills has backstories waiting to be found by the player. 4. The Otago as your Combat-Information-Center is, while not being the most indepth or innovative type of gameplay, refreshing to see. In fact, being able to exfiltrate your marines and return to recuperate is a brilliant mechanic mixed with the dreaded infestation level. As somebody who's last "squad tactical" game was Alien versus Predator: Extinction, I feel like this genre is now something I could get into thanks to this game. The Cons: 1. This game doesn't have many bugs, but the ones it DOES have are game breaking. I had two marines just "fall off" the map while taking cover in one of the middle tier missions. I was overwhelmed and couldnt even fail the game because my missing marines were still "alive". There are datapads that you are required to grab for side missions that just disappear or are non-interactive. Some Xenomorphs just die standing straight up, which while hilarious, is immersion shattering. I am sure they will fix these with time, but as a first-week player they did jar me.2. The animations and voice acting aren't the best, and hearing multiple actors/actresses do voices across the whole game makes it feel aged. The last game I know that did this was Skyrim, from 2011. Some of the dialogue is lifted straight from Aliens, which is to be expected for a series that can't help but give itself callbacks. Since the story expands so much on the series, I mostly let this pass, but it will stick out and annoy some people for sure.3. The ammo system is not amazing. While you can pick up around 30 clips of ammo or more in some missions, as soon as you evac, you lose all of it. Meanwhile, you can stack toolkits, medkits, and sentry guns. It's pretty stupid and basically discourages you from raiding armories if you know you're just going to go back there later on in another deployment. If I could change this, either let us stockpile ammo to bring back to The Otago or overhaul the system all together. 4. Customization for your marines was not a feature I was expecting to have, so at first I was amazed by the level of creative freedom a horror game was giving me. Unfortunately, the number of options in the customization menu for your marines is very limited, including the reuse of voicesets (As I previously mentioned). 5. The ARC/APC could've been given much more tactical use in the game if the mechanics behind it weren't simply to stage and move it to predetermined spots. There are even moments in the game where I felt like the devs were trying to suspend the logic of just using the APC cannon to blow a hole in a building in favor of making the player use an ammo clip to blow it up. I ended up walking my marines in front of the ARC just to give suppressing fire during an infinite onslaught, once. I noticed the APC will just drive through your marines, though. So yeah, I wish this had been changed. Addendum: The phalanx cannons or whatever they are called that's used to defend in the Middle Mission should've been an upgrade you could use on deployments. Again, feels restricted for story and balance reasons, but who cares? At a level 5 infestation, even if it was a heavy cost, those things could be valuable. 6. The difficulty gap between "Story" and "Medium" is ridiculous. I initially failed the campaign on Medium due to how hard it was, but then finished it easily on Story Mode. The Disparity is so bad that I want to roast the devs. It's like they knew they wanted to make a hard game but also didn't want to deal with complaints, so they just made a casual gamer mode. I'm not making this up, story difficulty turns the Xenomorphs into cardboard and other enemies into wet tissue paper. In contrast, Medium difficulty I was getting my ass kicked by cultists, commandos, and swarms of xenos that would just push through suppressive fire. I hope this is one day addressed.Overall, this is still my new favorite Alien game. I hope we see this level of care to detail go into the new TV show and movies.

_childDocuments_.review: I will start with this game is very unique, and unlike anything else in the aliens franchise. It definitely give me strong X-Com vibes, with game play kinda slightly like Star Craft, but simpler with it only being one squad. I like to think that its X-com's and Star Crafts special child, and was raised with love by the Aliens movie. That's because the cut scenes are very well made (have had some slight issues with some things taking a second to load like faces not animated, or deloading mid scene like boxes in the distance not being there) and i have been enjoying the story. It starts off strong with the end of the tutorial, having me feel like i was in the movie in a way, searching a settlement for answers, and survivors. They nailed a lot of the sounds, love the guns from the pulse rifle to the smartgun, the screams from the aliens, the increasing pings of the motion tracker, but i do hope they add some more voice lines tbh, they do get a little repetitive (they did do an update to help reduce the repetitiveness tho). Some of the animations do get a little old as well, but i didn't notice a lot of them. *Mostly just the aliens, mostly* (in combat i notice them doing things WAY more just because i would slow it down as i played). I'm not gonna lie, i wasn't gonna get this game. From the screenshots i saw, and it being a weird RTS, I thought it was just a money grab at the Aliens name. But i was wrong. i watched a video or two of some game play, and i was instantly hooked. Bought it before i was even home. And i love playing it. Scratches that same itch that X-Com does, has me sitting on the edge of my seat like the movies, and I'm having a absolute blast playing it. 10 out of 10 don't want it to be over, man! Game over!

Besides the crashes I enjoyed the game and will try at higher level.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has NO RIGHT being this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good. Seriously. I just watched Aliens and there are sooo many things in this game directly from the movie. From the APC vehicle to the way the flying vehicle looks to how your soldiers have flares, smart guns, flame throwers, I can go on and on. Theres even an achievement for rolling a xenomorph over with the APC JUST LIKE THE MOVIE!On top of all these things from the movie the game itself has some really solid mechanics. I prefer this game over XCOM and I'm a huge fan of XCOM. This game just has way cooler things in it and having real time combat versus the turn base combat XCOM offers is so much better. No more getting irritated for missing your shots and getting wiped. If you get wiped in this game its your fault. The game is pretty easy considering how the saves work but the game feels way better when playing ironman. It really does feel this is the way the game is meant to be played. All in all this is the best game ive played in many years and def my number 1 game of the year so far. Highly recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: This is  a really hard game on a number of levels. First you control a group  they move  as a group if a marine has a sniper rifle but in on the edge of a group they may have no shot and by the time they have shot you are in trouble. Second the aliens are quick  and you are going to take damage. Third traits can be brutal , Bad aim, slow, coward etc. Stress is a major problem. So you spend most the time avoiding the aliens and  creeping forward and running away as the Sh*t hit the fan fast in this game . No manual saves which suck especially when you are learning the game.  The atmosphere is great, the alien music adds to the tension.the feeling is pure Aliens. It is just tough  and hard to move forward as the difficulty cranks up . All in all a good game but it is frustrating. There are still a few bugs but generally fairly stable . Buy on sale and if you rage quit it doesn't matter.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this on a whim - very happy I did. I'd say it's closer to darkest dungeon than it is XCOM, with the mechanics of an RTS tactics game + the Aliens classic theme (Oh boy does it land the theme!). Each mission slowly ratchets up the amount of aliens that roam the map until you have to retreat (a la Invisible Inc) - but the neat trick is that your progress towards each mission is persistent! Along with the classic infestation level timer on the base management layer (a la XCOM), you always feel the tension of both impending doom and a strong desire to push just a bit further to get ahead of the curve.It's certainly not the best game I've played this year, but it's a unique, polished, and incredibly coherent strategy experience - and it's well worth the asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty good RTS X-com like strategy game. Your squad members have little quirks to mix up game play, sound design is fairly good in the sound effects dept. but man could it use something for the mission debriefing even if it was just the same song regardless of how well the mission went the silence is some how more immersion breaking than if it just played a random song from your local radio station. My only real game play complaint is this game not worthy of an iron man mode, I haven't come across game breaking bugs but scripted segments really ♥♥♥♥ you over not matter how careful you were. Also the Aliens have a fun habit of getting in between you and the goal so your basically required to kill them and raise the alarm. A good game but there are some sharp edges you should look out for.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the concept of the game. Honestly I liked just about everything about the game except two major issue's which I feel are so egregious they ruin the whole experience.The first problem is the event order. You fight an Alien Queen in the very first mission. That's right the big bad of the alien universe you fight at the beginning of the game. What a waste. They could have done so much more with it. Having several missions leading up to going deeper and deeper into more caves/tunnels would have been such a great experience, but instead they go here's an elevator, go down one floor and you fight a queen... on the first level. Makes all the missions afterwards disappointing because there's no where to go from there. but down.The second issue is what ruins the entire game for me. While the game leads you to believe there's a lot of action and alien shooting going on in reality it's pretty sparse. The game you bought isn't a shoot aliens game, but more of a hide and seek simulator. The game puts all your mission incursions on timers with some ridiculous stress system so if you're fighting aliens even if they aren't around in combat with you the marines build up stress which gives huge stat penalties and eventually just kills the marine. The only way to combat this is to NOT fight enemies ever. You just play hide and seek and run around doing missions while not attacking anything and you win. You can avoid 90% of enemies if you know what you're doing and the game is designed for you to play like this.Personally I like the framework of the game, but I would have liked to see the game be more focused on combating enemies at ALL times and less hide and seek. It wouldn't even be that much of a change because you're already limited in mission by health and ammo. I want to go in with my marines and shoot some damn aliens. Not run and hide like some wimp.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game if you know what you're getting. It does have boss encounters, and they typically break the atmospheric tension. Up to those boss fights, it's great. Overall, I really enjoyed it. I hate timed stuff, and it's a bit nebulous. For instance, you don't have to complete a mission on the first run. You can extract and go back a day later to finish it up while resetting the time-stacking difficulty within that mission. But...every 5ish (can't recall exact number) days outside missions (read every five missions) the global difficulty ramps up one tick. I don't know how hard this makes the game, so I've been running full clears in a single deployment.Overall, there's a reason it's $40 and not $60 or $70. It's a good game, and I think worthwhile if you like squad based RTS, or XCOM, because the overlay and between missions is XCOM. Combat is RTS with your squad. Or if you really like the Aliens IP. Definitely the best one to come out in a decade or so.

The sound mixing is not very good, volumes are not well matched together and it can differ between cutscenes and gameplay.Menuning is sometimes tedious, you have to rely on your mouse, you can escape something with escape key.There are still textures loading when cutscenes start....with a 4090 and a 5900x.Main characters are good enough but the marines faces in general are lacking, they feel too much as mixed elements, the results do not work all the time, ingame they're fine.On top of that, I faced a sort of softlock situation approachinig the end of the game. 1 day left , but I have to pass a day to start the next mission, resulting in a game over.I just finished the mission where you play Hayes only on the Otago, so my only solution is to load a previous save at least two missions before ! _childDocuments_.review: So, I'd like to start by saying I've never really done a review like this before. Following that I have seen James Cameron's Aliens 17 times, listened to the Audiobook version 3 times, and Vasquez was my first movie crush. I have to say this game had so much potential and I feel they actually sort of tried, but it just doesn't do it for me. This game took some of the best concepts from some really good RTS games and turn-based strategy games, mixed them all together and gave me very bland gameplay. You're first introduced to a very weak main character with some very heavy plot armor. Very quickly I was actually hoping she would die, 1. Because I didn't like her and 2. Because that would have set a way different tone for game. Infact there's a spot I feel like if she would have died, I would have been way more impressed with the story. Followed by some inaccuracies in how the Xeno's would act and attack. Some of the quips the Colonial Marines make are good and accurate I'd say (I'm a service member and we do say some NSFW stuff sometimes) The one line when they stumble into the dead body in the first mission about "Hating his job" Was actually pretty good in my opinion. But the bad absolutely outweighs it, you're given maybe half a dozen lines you'll get used to every time you make your party move somewhere. You get sick of their dialogue very very quickly. Tell me how an AvP RTS game from 2003 has better sound quality and design? Makes no sense at all, I felt nothing when an Alien died in this game, honestly didn't even feel scared for my marines or main character when they showed up. Now I understand doing anything, from book writing, movies, especially video games in this universe is hard to do because you'll have fans like me who are extra critical and ruthless, I was still hoping for slightly more. This by all means isn't a bad game, but here we are again, making me wish Steam had a way to give a neutral review. I will be requesting a refund  cause this just isn't worth 40$ to me. I honestly hope you all enjoy it so much more then me, because this did have potential and I would love to see better and high quality work like this.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite how critical I'm about to be, this is probably the second-best Alien game, after Isolation. If that's all you need to know, then go ahead and get it.Aliens: Dark Descent really wants you to think it's like XCOM. There's a squad loadout screen almost directly ripped from the Firaxis titles, a workshop & laboratory in your base where you can buy upgrades, and some light troop customization to play with your paper doll marines. But the similarities are only cosmetic. There's barely any actual research to do, and the strategy layer is almost entirely just about managing your roster. There is a doom clock, but no way to reduce the counter. The missions are linear, so there's no real decision-making to do about which one you take on next. The tactical layer has even less to do with XCOM, being real-time and not grid-based.None of that's necessarily a bad thing, just be aware that this isn't going to get you your XCOM fix if that's what you're after. Instead, this is a stealth game pretending to be an action-strategy title. You control your entire squad at once, moving them around the levels to complete objectives and scrounge for materials that you can use back on the ship to buy items and upgrade your gear.Levels are huge, spanning multiple floors and filled with dozens upon dozens of rooms and setpiece areas. Aliens patrol the map randomly, creating spontaneous firefights if they manage to detect your troops. Whenever they do, a "hunt" will start, which begins ticking up an intensity meter that spawns more aliens and stressing your marines out. By the time the meter reaches the "hard" level, things quickly become untenable, and your troops will be rapidly overwhelmed. The only way to reduce this meter is to extract your team and come back with another deployment.Missions can be extracted from and then resumed at any time, as long as your troops can make it back to the APC. That can be easier said than done in some of the twistier labyrinths, especially in the second half of the game. It's a good source of tension the further away from your escape point you go. To mitigate some of the running around, missions frequently allow you to unlock shortcuts and doors that allow the APC to follow you further into the level. The vehicle's big guns are also useful for setting up ambushes and avoiding detection, since for some reason APC kills don't alert the aliens.All this sounds great on paper, and when everything is working together there are moments of brilliance. But it's not all sunshine and roses.The game is, in many ways, a hot mess. Many of the systems feel like they're fighting each other. There's a Darkest Dungeon-like stress system that incentivizes quick, numerous runs, yet it's competing with the doom clock. It's not insurmountable, but it doesn't feel good. There's a heavy stealth focus, yet all your abilities are combat-oriented. Once detected, you're guaranteed to have about 30 seconds of aggression meter ticking up. This is the case even if you kill all enemies who've seen you. This means that being spotted by a single drone will ratchet up your entire squad's stress levels and effectively shorten the total time you can spend in a mission before another deployment. Your marines don't even gain experience for fighting, just for completing objectives.The optimal way to play turns out to be spamming motion trackers (which double as decoys) all over the map and dodging all combat until mandatory setpiece battles. Starting fights and using all your fun toys just punishes you by forcing multiple deployments that tick up the doom clock. It's better to avoid everything instead, which begs the question of why there are no stealth abilities (beyond arguably the silenced sniper rifle).Autosaving can be sparse, which in these huge levels means that you can lose up to 30m of progress when things go south. The game is trying to enforce the tension of an ironman playthrough on you, but players will run into too many softlocking bugs for that to be acceptable. There needs to at the very least be a quicksave that allows you to quit the game without losing progress if you don't have time for a full hour-long session. There's a manual save system of sorts, usable when you seal up a room with your marines inside, but this costs valuable resources and frequently bugs out and doesn't allow you to save at all. The resources are used up regardless.The resource economy in general is strange. Maps are littered with ammo, tools, and medical supplies, and they're saved between deployments. So it doesn't always behoove you to pick up everything immediately after you find it. Sometimes it makes sense to leave ammo or meds for future deployments. But you can't bring extra ammo with you, even for a cost, the way you can meds and tools. This means that it's usually better to leave all the ammo until you need it... which can result in a lot of tedious backtracking. Tools are used for everything from hacking to repairing turrets to sealing doors, but the aforementioned save bug means that it's a gamble to spend them for that.The devs could still stand to do a little bug hunting of their own, if you catch my drift. Voice lines from dead units, frozen enemies (that can still detect you), units clipping up through the ceiling, abilities becoming permanently triggered (suppressive fire is prone to this), negative ammo counts, and more all marred my playthrough. One climactic escape sequence was forced to restart multiple times because my squad simply stopped responding to movement commands.This review is still a recommendation, though, because the game's presentation carries it all the way. The cast of characters is plain but likable, and the story is mostly enjoyable. Mostly. It does get a bit silly toward the end, and veers into some nonsense at the last minute, but it was never enough to ruin the goodwill it builds up over the course of its 25-hour campaign. The levels are filled with lavish detail, and everything from the sound design to the visuals is filled with obvious love for the franchise.I had a good time with it, in many ways despite itself. With a few more patches--that I'm not sure we'll see, at this late stage--this might verge on greatness. As it is, it's a fun enough romp that comfortably sits at a distant second to Alien Isolation on the list of best Alien games.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the Alien franchise, you will be pleased to know that Alien Dark Ascent is a game that truly captures the essence of the movies and books. The game is set in a persistent world where you lead your soldiers in real-time to stop a new and terrifying kind of Xenomorph outbreak on Planet Lethe. The game’s immersive atmosphere is incredible, and it creates the same mood as the movies and books. The tension of knowing that there are several Xenomorphs behind you makes you feel cautious, and like the characters in the game, you feel the stress, emotion, fear, and adrenaline that the action shows.The game’s environments are detailed with incredible attention to detail, and the ambient sound makes the adventure more enjoyable. The game’s management system is interesting, and the ability to extract when everything goes wrong in the mission and then return to try a different approach makes the game less repetitive.Overall, Alien Dark Ascent is a fantastic game that will appeal to fans of the Alien franchise. The game’s immersive atmosphere, detailed environments, and interesting management system make it a must-play for anyone who loves the series.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really a hidden gem. It's gameplay is unique and fun. The atmosphere is perfect. At points, it feels like you're watching an Aliens movie that should have existed. The tension and "oh-sh*t" factor is cranked up to ten on Aliens: Dark Descent.I started on the hard level and got overwhelmed by its difficulty pretty early on. One tip I'll give is that you can change the gameplay mechanics in the menu from "slow-down while giving commands" to "pause while giving commands." Making this change made the game much more enjoyable and manageable for me. It made it more of a tactical game where you could think out your moves instead of having to react and choose the correct tactic instantly, which is not easy and often led to death.My only complaints would be that it does have a few bugs, one of which I thought was game-ending, but it ended up the person I was trying to save apparently got recaptured by the aliens and cocooned back at their base. This happened after I had to evac my squad in the middle of the mission and the map ping icon stayed at the old location of the survivor and never showed his new location where he was cocooned. The other complaint is that it gets a bit repetitive. I feel like this could be solved with an expansion pack that has more weapons and even vehicles (ATV's would be fun) to be able to mix up the tactics some.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent mish-mash of genres to create a creative and unique experience that feels just as tense to play as Aliens did to watch. This is a survival-horror/ real-time-strategy/ RPG-lite with an emphasis on stealth and strategic combat. For the dev's ability to coherently mash so many genres together alone, this game warrants your attention. Game runs very well at 1440p with an RTX 3080, i7 9700k and 32 GB of RAM and all settings cranked to max. While I do occasionally encounter bugs, they are minor (ammo pick-up icons that don't fade when they should, character repeating canned voice lines occasionally during a firefight, etc.). Just shy of 17 hours in (and roughly 1/3 of the way through the game based on level-count) and I have yet to encounter a bug that has hampered my enjoyment of the game. If you are in any way a fan of the franchise or have a passing interest in any of the genres this game manages to stitch together into one product, I couldn't see the game disappointing you unless 1) you are a hardcore fan and take issues with how the lore is expanded in this narrative (I personally enjoyed it), 2) find the game too stressful or difficult to enjoy (the default difficulty is harder than your average game, I'd wager, and more horror-themed than the average strategy title), or 3) you are a purist of the horror, strategy, RPG, or stealth genre and don't appreciate how this title curtails and simplifies mechanics from each genre to keep things manageable for a wider audience and easy to learn and play. This truly does feel like the Aliens analogue that Isolation was to Alien. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: It's okay. (seriously steam, mixed reviews, please)If it's on a sale. Decent graphics, okay story, fun gameplay but feels like mechanics needed a once over. Stress is a great idea, but instead of making marines act in dynamic, or erratic ways...they just pass out eventually...I'm sure there's a better way to manage it, but all I could find was using the same resource med packs use, and really just preventing their inevitable declines into coma town. _childDocuments_.review: When this game was initially announced it looked "ok" to me, not great, maybe worth checking out eventually on a steam sale. This week when the final launch trailer released I checked it out and was underwhelmed by it. However, as the week went on I began to see reviews coming in from some of my favorite channels (Worth a Buy and Mandalore gaming). The reviews were glowing and I decided to give it a shot. I am so happy that I did, this is easily one of my favorite tactical strategy games of all time and the youtube trailers absolutely do not do this game justice at all.There is a lot of tactical strategy like XCOM, Fallout 2, Jagged Alliance and the Aliens TTRPG. This game obviously takes a great deal of its inspiration from Aliens 1986, but it makes every Alien encounter feel extremely tense and dangerous. The Aliens in this are fast and ruthless, especially on the higher difficulties. Even if you have a lot of firepower if just one slips past your front line and lands a hit there is a very high chance your Marine will become injured and receive a minor injury. A decent chance they receive a major injury that will have consequences on their combat effectiveness for the rest of the deployment or a slight possibility of something absolutely catastrophic happening (a limb being severed such as an arm or leg, being struck unconscious from a concussion, comas, hemorrhaging etc.)Had a really desperate encounter where my squad had to infiltrate a hive, and things went from going smoothly to hectic very quickly. Long story short it was a very tense game of cat and mouse with combat sprinkled throughout leaving 2 of my marines incapacitated and having to carry both of them back to the ship for extraction. When carrying another marine you can only use a side arm such as a pistol, needless to say not very effective against the universes most lethal apex predator. Thats when I knew this was one of my favorite Alien games of all time.  Swapping between moments of tense anxiety to combat has a really great flow and makes the pacing for every play through feel different In addition the developers did an excellent job crating the environments. The worlds feel alive and lived in and you can really see their attention to detail and you just know they have a deep respect for this universe. Lots of environmental story telling and interesting design. My cons with this game are minor. Some of the animations are a bit stiff and customization options are a bit on the weaker side which is a shame. It would have been great if the visual fidelity was a bit higher for the individual marines I want to be that much more invested with my squad, that way when something goes horribly wrong (like a squad mate getting abducted and being dragged off to the hive), I would feel it that much more. This is a small developer studio and they really punched above their weight overall. I understand some of these things are likely due to budget constraints. But compared to the recent AAA game industry landscape where every release has to have a foreward apology letter, this is a breath of fresh air. Let me close by saying I have been a huge Aliens fan since I was like 12 years old. I grew up playing Alien 3 on the genesis and SNES and played pretty much every one since then. From Alien Trilogy on psx to the AvP series. Next to Isolation so far my impressions of this currently has it sitting at my #2 favorite in the series.

_childDocuments_.review: The long and the short of this review is simpleThe short is: if you like xcom type games but want something a bit more challenging, give this a try.The long, I'll start with the negatives.-bugs. Quite a few of them. Usually you can fix them by reloading a previous save but it's still common enough to be noticeable.-no endgame. At all. Once you beat the campaign, that's it. Which really sucks for this type of game that seems like it wants to encourage you to do stuff and level up your troops. But for some reason there just isn't any kind of endgame to speak of. Not Even a new game plus.-the character models are... simply put: really uncanny. Mainly the faces. Especially on the customization aspect with your troops-not many customization options in general. Yeah there's a few, but not much if you really wanna get into it. -could definitely use some gameplay changes. Specifically being able to manage marines both individually as well as in a group. As of current, what you can do with your squad is very limited. They all travel together in a group, the most you can do when it comes to individually managing them is sending one off across the map to pick up an item or something you forgot to grab. And even then, if you cancel that command, they will simply run all the way back to the group. What makes this worse is if said individual marine is about to be spotted. In which you will have to awkwardly balance placing a movment marker out of the way of the enemy's line of sight, while also not keeping it there to long that the main group ends up running into it instead (if that makes sense.)Not to mention the cover system is rather... iffy at best. Where you can't individually put marines in separate spots of cover, thus allowing for better area coverage and/or hiding, thus you're forced to dog pile every single marine you have behind one bit of cover. Which can work, buy there's a chance you'll end up with one numbskull standing out in the middle of the open cause the ai doesn't like to use cover in a way that supports four or more people. Thus getting spotted and hoard battle ensues.Then there's the issue with each marine class being able to do specific things. However the problem arises when you need one marine to do said thing, while the others have to drag themselves along.For example: I was sneaking through a nest of sleeping xenomorphs. Again, this is bad enough with the way the cover system works. However, if you have the correct skill for the recon class, you can silently kill enemies with a precision shot.However.The problem arises when your recon needs to be at a specific angle or position to make the shot. And as previously mentioned, this is impossible to do without moving the entire squad. Thus, you're forced to weirdly fiddle with the cover system trying to get your recon in the correct position for way longer then what it's worth, or, you're moving the entire squad out in the open, risking waking the hive via one getting spottedvia their part of the formation jutting out.Overall it's just not a good time and could easily be fixed if you could just individually command your troops. That by far is the biggest issue.That's all the negatives aside from bug specifics and texture pop in issues. But aside from all that, I still say the game is surprisingly fun. And with enough work, I'd say it could very easily be one of the best xcom style games out there. I'd say give it a try, maybe wait till it's on sale or had some more time to bug fix/make additions.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not perfect, but it's fun. It could use a lot more polish in some areas, but excels in atmosphere and nostalgia  generation, as a decades-long fan of the Alien franchise.The AI is pretty rudimentary and could use some work - marines will, rarely, get stuck while walking and be unable to unstick themselves, requiring manual intervention. The game is a little slow to start as far as fun goes - unlocking initial stuff felt like a slog, but is worth waiting for.Skills usage needs some work - if two marines have the same skill, I'm unable to choose which to use - the game chooses the closest marine, who inevitably gets interrupted if it's a close-quarters fight. That means it's almost impossible to deploy the flamethrower in close-quarters high-action moments, which is not how it should work.Hoping for more content added - it's kind of "minimum viable" so far from what I can see, but it IS viable. Reiterating: the warm-up is slow but it's worth the push, especially if you like the IP.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: This is an amazing game but not really playable in its current state due to bugs and balancing.This game really feels like an alien movie. Its creepy, stylish, movie-esque cutscenes, aliens are very powerful, and stuff goes downhill very fast. One wrong move can doom the entire mission. Autosaves only happen very rarely, meaning mistakes will set you back quite a bit. This makes the game a very tense experience.Because of this it is unbelievably frustrating if a marine gets stuck outside of a door for no reason and gets spotted, triggering a huge wave of aliens killing your squad and setting you back 10 minutes due to no fault of your own. Or you click a button to get command points back and nothing happens, so you click it again and suddenly it happens twice meaning you are now out of resources to repair your sentry gun, resulting in death. Or you set down a marine you are carrying and for some reason during this animation you cannot make any other orders, causing your squad to die.. the list goes on.Then, the balancing. I have no issue with hard games, but for hard games to be good they have to be skill based. That is not the case here. This game is incredibly unforgiving. Things spiral out of control very fast with no means for the player to stop it. I play on medium but I still just had to replay a save for multiple hours just to barely make it out during the FIRST MISSION. And the issue is, it does not feel like my fault. I snuck in undetected, I had full health, good tactics, used everything at my disposal. Then, there was a bossfight, that causes you to be detected, that causes you to be hunted, that causes a huge wave of enemies to swarm you, that causes you to be hunted MORE, that causes another boss to spawn... One one hand, this makes it feel like an alien movie. On the other hand, it feels like the player has no input on this. These are things happening TO YOU, not because of your actions. Even worse, after I finally made it out it did not feel like a success. I tried the same exact thing over and over until by sheer luck it randomly worked.These are all fixable things. Don't trigger detected state during or after a bossfight. Make xenomorph spawns less random. Give us some ability to autosave outside of a shelter, maybe once a mission. A little bit more hiding places here and there. But it needs to be fixed.Also, for some reason the game is incredibly unoptimized. Why is my 3090 sounding like a jet fighter barely making 70 FPS during the after action report screen?

I did have fun for some aspects of it but the developers really have a hard-on for making playing this game difficult for you. Between the quickly on-setting tired/exhaust (cannot use dude for 4 in-game days)mechanic. _childDocuments_.review: I used to play every game on hard, but I'm too old for endless retries, so I play this one on story and I'm still losing my squad occasionally (and definitely NOT because I'm sloppy... no-oh!!).Anyway, I really dig it and I hope there will be DLC or another part soon.Having been a longtime Alien-franchise admirer, I must say that some of the story beats are a bit too far-out for me, but don't count that as criticism, it's my taste.A few bugs here and there have usually been squashed by reloading and I never mind redoing a sequence, so all is good. _childDocuments_.review: Pretty good RTS squad game in a great setting. You set up your squad like in xcom games but the gameplay is real time.In your squad, everyone starts as a rookie and can become any of the other classes: sergeant, gunner, medic, sniper and tecker. are the backbone of your team, increasing command points and bravery, both extremely important since one resource is used for skills and the other to reduce stress gain (which induces debuffs).  are the only class with access to the iconic smart gun and are all around good damage dealers. Medics increase both the health points of your teams and the healing capabilities.  are broken (as is tradition in these games) during stealth/undetected phases thanks to their silenced sniper upgrade.Finally  have a cool drone that can explore/weld and do some extra defense/shooting, but are the class you try once and replace with an extra gunner or sergeant, since their distinctive class attribute (being able to open tech doors) is a common attribute available to all other classes., pretty to look at and fun to explore and fight in. There is a lot to enjoy in the environment and design. Especially with the flashlight mechanic, that invites you to aim around to better see what is around you.Has multiple ; easy, normal, hard and nightmare and custom. Includes a pseudo-ironman mode where you are limited to one pre game save and one in mission save triggered after resting in safe areas. . This setting affects how the game behaves while you are selecting your skills to use. You can freely choose one or the other at any time, but . With tactical pause you will have unlimited time to react to any enemy sighting and, for example, take your sniper shots to instantly avoid triggering an encounter. Meanwhile with slow motion you can be punished for your positioning and timing mistakes.Likewise for tough combat situations where with slow motion you will be hard pressed to make the right choices and may be even hit or interrupted for not being fast enough or choosing the wrong target.It’s strange that this setting is an option and not part of the difficulty selection with how much it can affect the actual difficulty of the game.I personally think the slow motion mode fits the Aliens setting better, since it adds an additional stress factor to combat that is not there with tactical pause., nothing amazing but it's good enough to support the gameplay. Of course it has a lot of recurring alien themes, like the comically evil Weyland-Yutani corporate drones.At the time I played through the campaign the game was in a good state but there were a lot of weird bugs, besides the Xenomorphs. Things I had happen; pathing issues, both marines and enemies getting stuck on something, an objective being impossible to complete for missing some kind of trigger forcing a reload, ammo counters disappearing for sentries, skills getting stuck in use (can be a benefit if it happens with something like reprimand, but still annoying), and a bunch of other minor things. Something else that wasn't a bug but was really irritating was being locked out of using my sentry turrets unless in a specific location during a specific story mission. Which led to me getting overrun during an onslaught I was unable to properly prepare for.Overall all things I expect to get fixed, but that you should keep in mind going into this game close to release.Overall .

_childDocuments_.review: Aliens: Dark Descent [DD] is fantastic game designed for fans of the franchise. DD provides exhilarating action that captures the feel and atmosphere of James Cameron's classic sequel to Alien, full of tight corners and tactical squad commands that truly makes you feel like Gorman in the APC on LV-426. From a gameplay perspective, DD offers a unique take on the franchise that allows you to see your marines in action from an RTS approach all in real-time, pressing your tactical acumen as a field commander leading a squad of marines. The addition of features such as combat stress and having to manage your team members and ranks for the task at hand helps to build the atmosphere so synonymous with Aliens, listening to your marines buckle under the pressure of the constant onslaught while you attempt to manage and navigate them through each deployment. Seeing a squad member you have levelled and equipped being carried away into the belly of the hive, only to consider if you mount a rescue or leave them to their fate only furthers to help deliver the experience Aliens fans are wanting from a game. Tactical, action-packed, tense, atmospheric. All of these words describe perfectly the type of game you will be playing here. An Aliens game hasn't been this good since Alien Isolation.

_childDocuments_.review: Aliens Dark Descent is a great AA-level game. It brings a great mix of real-time strategic gameplay with a story that fits the Aliens universe well. Having purchased this close to its release, I did bump into some rough edges that may or may not have been fixed by now: A character getting stuck in the environment forcing me to restart. Marine barks which are cringy and often too frequent. Some questionable save mechanics and a timed ending which can put your entire game at risk.That said, with a few updates or even some mods, this game is amazing and something that I hope the developers build upon for a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend!Top 3 game of the year for me. Being a huge fan of the original Alien movies, this game perfectly delivers on the fantasy of controlling the colonial marine squad from Aliens (the second movie). The game elegantly switches between sneaking past blips on your radar to not piss off the hive and making the inevitable stand against a xenomorph horde when you get spotted - keeping you on your toes all the way through. I am truly amazed that a top-down tactical squad-based game could create so many tense moments!  Before playing, I thought this would be "Xcom but with HR giger xenemorphs" - but this game feels much more unique due to the many little changes they have made to the formula, with the biggest one being real-time combat instead of turn based.Yes it is buggy, yes sometimes controlling a group of marines as "one unit" creates janky combat situations, yes some world building aspects fall a bit outside of the Alien IP -- but I could glance over all of this due to the tense moment-to-moment gameplay and surprisingly enthralling narrative. This was clearly made by people who love the Alien franchise and they should feel proud.

_childDocuments_.review: "They're coming out of the walls!" But seriously, great idea and execution. It's a different take on the tactical RTS genre, like and yet unlike XCOM. _childDocuments_.review: I'm still playing through it, but I've seen enough to leave a review.  Don't pay full price for this and it's worth it.It's fun enough, but you run into bugs fairly early on that should've been patched in the year+ since release.-loading from a saved game after rest, your stress levels have dropped, but you can rest again.  i don't know if this was intentional, but it's hard to believe that it is.  easily exploitable bug.-tutorial hanging.  got to the part of the game where a tutorial pops up explaining how to sneak around sleeping xenomorphs where i kept dying trying to figure out how to get through the warehouse.  specifically the second one that tells me to get to cover to get out of the line of sight.  that's when i discovered that occasionally it would bug and prevent me from clicking on anything or exit to the menu to reload.  only fixed by a game restart.  unacceptable when the warehouse was already making me mad enough to get throughunrelated to bugs-the concept of how you can save is cool and all, but if you're going to limit it to that, give me options for rest spaces that DON'T require my very limited amount of tools, that are actually closer to important checkpoints.  that way i'm not getting more and more annoyed at having to run back after a reload, and hearing the same boring one liners over and over again every time-i'm way over recommended spec, and at transitions it chunks up noticeably for a split second-the sense of urgency seems way over what you're capable of doing per day.  i haven't gotten far enough to see exactly what happens if you let it get too far, but it just seems grossly overstatedthat said, the game is interesting enough, but i'm only gonna play through this once and never again.  the devs didn't care enough about this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend this game to fans of Aliens and squad-based games.It comes with great atmosphere, a solid story and fun gameplay. _childDocuments_.review: Alien Dark Descent is an exhilarating and immersive gaming experience that will keep you on the edge of your seat from start to finish. As a fan of science fiction and survival horror games, I was immediately drawn to the atmospheric world and intense gameplay this title offers.The game's visuals are stunning, with detailed environments that truly capture the eerie and foreboding atmosphere of deep space. The attention to detail in the alien designs is commendable, and encountering them throughout the game creates an intense sense of fear and excitement.What sets Alien Dark Descent apart is its gripping storyline. The narrative unfolds with suspenseful twists and turns, keeping players engaged and eager to uncover the secrets lurking within the dark corners of the spacecraft. The voice acting and sound design further enhance the immersive experience, making you feel like a part of the harrowing journey.The gameplay mechanics are well-crafted, offering a perfect blend of exploration, resource management, and intense combat encounters. The game challenges you to make strategic decisions, weighing your options as you navigate treacherous corridors and make crucial choices to survive. The AI of the enemies is impressive, adding an extra layer of unpredictability and intensity to the gameplay.One aspect that deserves special praise is the game's attention to detail and realism. From the realistic sound effects to the intricate ship interiors, Alien Dark Descent truly captures the essence of being trapped in a haunted spacecraft. It's a testament to the developers' dedication to creating an authentic and immersive experience.In conclusion, Alien Dark Descent is a must-play for fans of the science fiction and survival horror genres. It offers a thrilling adventure that will keep you engaged for hours on end. With its captivating storyline, stunning visuals, and intense gameplay, this game is a standout in its genre. Strap in and prepare for a heart-pounding journey into the depths of darkness and the unknown.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best Aliens game I have played in a while.  It has everything you would expect from an Aliens movie right in the game.  The stress mechanic although annoying really brings in the fact that your marines are freaking out about fighting these enormously powerful and deadly creatures.  This game is not meant to be easy, the aliens will not only stress your marines out but you too because they are unpredictable at times.  Don't worry if you bang your head on the desk or find yourself reloading a save a couple of times till you get it right.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface comment with the following: I have made it half way through the 2nd mission at the time of writing this review. No spoilers.Very cool RTS game and faithful to "Aliens" lore. Very immersive in atmosphere and gameplay. I remember Fireteam elite that came out two years back, it didn't really keep my interest, missions felt repetitive and got boring after a while. Different kind of game, but it's all the more important when you know that game was a fastpaced shooter. This game, story gameplay and all sucks you in and keeps you meticulously checking every corner. The individual marine upgrades you can do balances well with the rest/ healing system. You can't keep taking out the same marines every time unless you want to wait 3-5 days. In this time bad things can happen to your crew, extending rest or healing periods, and not to forget the increase in "infestation" over time. This way you have to balance your troops and decide tactically which people are the right ones for the job (and so you can't take out your already leveled troops out every time). I can say a lot of great things about this game, the only negative i've experienced was with the squad AI. Sometimes they get a bit stuck when given an order to move somewhere. RTS Game: 8/10 Good implementation of squad management mechanics, abilities, and unique squad members. Gameplay somewhat unforgiving at times, but lends it self well to strategizing and making sure you engage the situation correctly. Sometimes buggy ai mapping. Overall very solid.Aliens Universe Game (so far): 10/10 Every Alien wants to kill you. *Ping*------*Ping*----*Ping*---*Ping*--*Ping*-*Ping*Ping*Ping* "Game over man! Game over!"

MY SAVE IS STILL HARD LOCKEDTLDR - I do not recommend the game because on my second day of playing, I encountered a game breaking bug where I can't move the camera or click on the screen to move my marine squad during deployment.  I have no idea how or why it happened, or what could possibly be done to fix it.  I loaded a save from the Otago and every time I deploy, the camera breaks and I can't do anything to move it, and I can't click to move my squad either.  Mouse scrolling doesn't work, keyboard keys don't work, opening the map works but I can't move the camera by clicking on a location on the map screen.  It's just broken.  I've deployed to the location I'm at before and it worked fine during my first play session.  EDIT: After research, this is happening to a LOT of players.  DO NOT BUY THE GAME UNTIL THE BUG IS FIXED!The first day I played the game, it was a blast!  Very universe faithful in sound effects and marine armor and outfit design.  They did take some creative liberty by adding things like UAV drones (not present in movies) that do make sense for a futuristic setting.  This, by far, is a better game than ALIENS: Fireteam Elite.  Game play has a nice pace and the marine stress mechanic makes sense.  Some of the negative unit attributes are absolutely debilitating to an incredible degree, making it extremely hard to overcome them.  The game is very transparent about incoming horde waves and it gives you ample time to set up some kind of defense, but it doesn't make sense that I would know it's coming in terms of realism.The number 1 overpowered mechanic is that you can keep placing static motion trackers around the map with an unlimited supply.  It gives the player WAY too much knowledge about enemy locations.  I think it should be a limited resource like sentry guns are.  Limiting the player to 4 static motion trackers, like sentry guns, would make it a more tactical decision and cause the player to have to keep picking them up and moving them.  They also persist between deployments, so once you've placed some, they are there for all subsequent deployments in that location.  The enemies ignore them as well, which doesn't make sense against human enemies.The marine injury recovery times are a little ridiculous.  Lightly injured marines take multiple days to recover, and I know it encourages you to use more than one squad, but it is still kind of frustrating when you manage to take good care of the squad during missions.  The stress mechanic and trauma mechanic, from what I see, are the real huge problems that the game won't let you address early enough.  After completing the first mission and 90% of the second mission, I still have no way of reducing the trauma level on my marines, which means they have a permanent debuff that I can't heal right now.  I got lucky with one marine and they got a perk that heals their trauma level by 1 each deployment.  My number one bit of advice, do not extract the marine squad from a deployment early, stay as long as you can with the resources in the mission, only extract when it becomes impossible to survive any longer.  You will only gain 1 trauma for that.  If you extract early and do a bunch of mini deployments, you'll increase the infestation level faster, and increase your marines trauma level faster, making the game extremely difficult very quickly.

_childDocuments_.review: A solid 8/10. Its a great starting point for Tindalos to make something really extraordinary here.[UPDATE] They made it now so you can turn off the doom clock. Similar to Dawn of War II campaign. At time of writing there is only the story campaign, which doesn't really provide you with any real replay value. The story is bad, and doesn't do a great deal of explaining some of the key plot points, and is simply only a vessel to set you up for the next mission, which is forgivable because the actual game play is really fun. I would like to see a rogue-like game mode where you just need to purge the planet of Aliens™, battling an infestation build-up timer instead of the doom clock they have now, which is trash. I'm hoping they have some new game modes in the works, or at least allow mods for the game. All that being said, the atmosphere is spot on, and I found myself many times in situations that could have been straight out of a movie. The game has some bugs that hopefully get fixed soon, but none of them are game breaking that I've noticed yet. There are little quirks that can be looked over, such as trying to sneak your squad through a maze and an Alien™ walks into the room, and your sergeant yells "HURRY UP YOU SLUGS!!" as you quietly slip out of the room and continue sneaking.  Overall, a solid GOOD game. though if they don't work on the re-play-ability of the game, it will probably fade away within a year.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm 10 hours in and plan on updating this after I am done. Overall, I think this game is great for a certain type of player. Let me make this clear. In my opinion, this is a stealth action RTS. This is a game that rewards you for paying attention to your motion tracker and picking your battles. Deployable motion trackers give you the ability to monitor movement in a range, but can be overloaded to draw attention to that area. The aggression system ramps up more and more the more you engage with the hive, and as they get more aggressive, more and more appear. Your troops suffer from stress while fighting/being hunted, which can then cause mental aliments that will negatively impact their ability to perform in the field. The game is delicate balancing act of stealth, resource management, and tactical engagements. It's a slow and tense experience that will test your ability to perform under stress and to see if you have what it takes to make the tough calls that comes with leading a squad.
