_childDocuments_.review: is a survival action game centered around shooting things with a magic gun. Not just enemies, but generally shooting up the world too, really. The world is ending in five minutes and it’s a lot faster to shoot down a tree, you know? I’m not kidding about the world ending in five minutes thing, really. In-game, that can be a few days but in player-time it is mere minutes. The premise of the game has you stuck in a loop where the world is ending and you must constantly turn back time to continue the fight against the impending apocalypse. You challenge various bosses throughout the world to gain gears and restore the world a little bit further with each rewind. Eventually you come across the final boss of the region, defeat them for a special gear and unlock a whole new region. Repeat as you fight against the chaos. There is more to the story but to be honest I was more interested in the gameplay loop and just absorbed enough of the premise to send me on my way and have an idea on what exactly I am fighting for.It's a cool looking game, I really dig the art style. I definitely found myself humming along to the music as well. Most important though is that the art and animation are clear. There is a lot of dodging in this game in order to weave through enemy bullets, attacks, and possibly even friendly fire from your own magic. It was always pretty clear what was going on and I was always in awe watching the interaction of magic with the environment. Fire spreading across a forest or oil, lightning zapping through rivers, etc. It’s a fun spectacle.Alright now here is the meat of the game! As much as I enjoyed it, I’ll have to concede that I can understand some disappointment with the game. Honestly, I never felt much like a wizard. There are never really any cool spells other than ones that work passively with the guns. It felt more like you’re a guy with a magic gun. I was okay with this, but this distinction might be off putting to someone else who night be expecting something more grandiose. Personally, I thought the guns we got were still pretty cool and fun, but I agree my mage never really felt like a mage himself and that anyone could wield these guns.Let’s back track a bit first to explain the premise of the gameplay loop – which is honestly pretty addicting. You venture forth through a world for the time limit starting at 5 minutes. Initially you’ll want to spend the time gathering resources to craft better bullets and research stations to unlock more bullets and abilities. But the real goal is to beat up the mini bosses to get gears in order to make actual progression toward the region bosses and unlocking the next region. Along the way, you can also extend the time limit by destroying chaos portals. By the late game, the time limit is never really an issue and you usually finish whatever you were doing with time to spare. Which is actually the ideal time to resource gather.Oh, if you die you drop everything in your backpack. But its easy enough to just try again. If you survived though, you bring all your goodies back to base which is where you can work on progression with unlocking and crafting new toys to play with. Honestly, I wasn’t feeling it at first but I figured it was a matter of needing to unlock more. Indeed, once I was regularly crafting things after each run it became an addicting loop of getting stronger after each run and wanting to find materials to unlock yet more things. For the most part I just stuck with a few types of damaging bullets and didn’t bother much with utility. But they are there and seem fun. I at least tried them out and there are bullets to freeze enemies in place whether its in time via stasis or literal ice. You can charm enemies to fight for your side. Or you can go my route and just burn and shock them to death. There are a ton of viable solutions though I suspect they’re not all balanced to be equal. For example, poison bullets seem like they’d be great but they are a bit more annoying to craft than lightning bullets. Poison bullets usually require some kind of poisoned body part to craft which is something you must get by killing enemies with poison. Meanwhile lightning bullets are gotten via charged metal which is easily acquired just shooting a wall or even making it peacefully in your homebase. Gunplay and combat is rather simple. You aim and shoot while you run around and dodge. As mentioned earlier, magic in your guns can interact with the environment and lead to neat interactions. It’s very easy to accidentally catch yourself on fire when spamming fire bullets and running around like a buffoon. All part of the fun, in my opinion. But there’s a whole other side of the game where you can even mitigate that with magical upgrades to your gear to make yourself immune to fire damage for example. There is a lot of crafting to be done! You can even craft decorations and the world around you if you’re into that – I’m not and preferred to get back to shootin’.Game runs fine.Operating System: Windows 10Processor (CPU): Intel Core i5-3570K CPU @3.40GHzGraphics Card (GPU): NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1070Memory (RAM) 16 GBWizard with a Gun got almost 20 hours of runtime from me and it was enjoyable. I never really felt frustrated by it (though it still provided some challenge and made me fear death) and it honestly probably ended right when I was starting to feel done. It did not overstay its welcome but any longer and maybe it would have. It gets repetitive but the gameplay loop is short and addicting with enough changes through the progression system to look forward to. I actively enjoyed going for “just one more run” wanting to get more materials to get even stronger. The regions also differed enough to have their own biomes of creatures, materials and hazards. Overall, I simply had a fun time as a solo player. I cannot speak for co-op but I recommend it as a solo game, especially on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I could ignore everything else and just consider this a nice little game to waste an hour or 2 on every once in a while... But after starting a second save and filling up a few chests with materials, I just didn't feel like continuing.Everything but the most hardcore survival games have realised that dealing with crafting within your base, is vastly improved by just making all inventory within base available to every craftingbench in base.Galvanic Games has not.They actually went to the effort to almost do it by letting workbenches adjecent to chests borrow from the chests inventory. Unfortunately, there's so many different materials, workbenches and recipe's that despite this feature it still only feels like a drop in the bucket of all the crafting and inventory management this game requires of you. There's other games where I've enjoyed engaging with the crafting and inventory management. This isn't one of them. My first run was carried by the sense of exploration, finding new enemies and discovering new bullet and powder combinations. Starting a new game, it doesn't feel worth slogging through all the crafting and reloading, just to play a somewhat basic, almost mundane isometric action game, who's progression is clumsily gated by the whole enemy level VS bullet level mechanic.

_childDocuments_.review: Good and fun game to spend a few minutes or hours to play with. I've been waiting to get my hands on this game since it got announced two years ago during the Summer Game Fest of that year on Devolver Digital's spot.Pros:- The concept is interesting and fun. Using guns as a means of casting magic ? Count me in!- It has support for mods, which's always great! There's only a handful right now but hopefully there'll be more later on.- It has a few elements from Don't Starve but thankfully you have a "base" of sorts which you can always come back and create your stuff in peace. There's neither a hunger system nor pitch black darkness during night, thank goodness.Cons:- After the tutorial all your missions are time-gated and you'll need to be fast to complete your objectives, which may induce some anxiety and pressure on certain people, and I personally find it to be annoying since I'd like to take my time with the missions, explore the map and know more about what's going on.However if you feel you can't complete a mission you can always enter the portal with the gears you've got and try again with better gear and resources.- Your character moves really slow, which's remedied through certain items. And there's no sprint feature, which would be convient since, again, you're racing against time to complete your missions.All in all this is a great game which I can fully recommend getting whenever you can.

_childDocuments_.review: This game suffers exactly from what Cult of the Lamb suffers from. Really nice art style that's visually appeasing, but it's EXTREMELY shallow and the gameplay feels super dated.The gameplay is, you shoot... and dodge roll. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Wizard with a Gun is a mediocre isometric shooter game that tries to channel Don't Starve and Magicka, extraction based games with a dash of crafting and partially succeeds. The content in the game is quite repetitive and bland, you don't get to really experience the "wizard" side of things at all, and the game is blatantly unfinished. You only get a handful of guns and a few types of bullets -- most of which you will ignore for the ones that actually do damage -- and basic stat boosting upgrades for your clothes. You have no abilities, there are only three kinds of consumable items, and your only movement option is a basic dodge roll. Instead of variety, the game offers an experience that is stretched painfully thin. That said, it is still enjoyable enough. Serviceable. 7/10.So, you've just bought Wizard with a Gun! You are probably expecting chaotic and fun gameplay with wild and crazy combinations of spells and a wacky world in the vein of Magicka, if you've played that! Well, at first it might seem that way while you are scrambling to get even the most basic of weapons and special ammo. The first few hours of the game will see you wandering around the world in the 5-minute extendable bursts of exploration, shooting and resource hoarding. Then you go back to your home base and build workbenches and research new bullets to increase your power. Wow-wee! Starry eyed and bushy tailed, you forge ahead and might even kill your first boss! Hooray! That's when the game will truly open up and show it's wild side! Right?After you have made it to the first couple of areas that the game has to offer, the realization will most likely dawn on you: what you saw in the first area of the game is representative of the  game experience you can expect. Your arsenal hasn't changed from the four guns you were shown in the first area, sans them being slightly higher tier versions that offer an extra mod slot per level. You have gained no grenades, no mortars, no abilities of any kind. You don't have magical beams or polymorphs, you can't manifest mines or generate a storm of dark magic to rend your enemies. All you have is a couple of basic guns and even more generic elemental bullets. And a couple of utility things that might be neat to play around with. If you remember to, and want to put in the effort.When you do research on your bullets, you will discover that the higher level bullets are nothing but numerical stat increases to cope with the steadily inflating armor and health of the enemies. Your fire bullets won't suddenly start generatic explosions or raging infernos of quickly stacking damage. Your destruction bullets won't cause anything other than a middling amount of basic damage without effects. Even adding oil to the fire might only slightly increase the damage it does for a few seconds before the effect fades. Yet, without your bullets being high enough level, you cannot damage the enemy, so grind you must.So, what's so bad about all of that? The problems is that the game is horrendously basic. The four weapons you see is what you get; no powers, no grenades, no wacky combinations that make your screen explode or beams shoot out of your revolver. You will unlock different kinds of bullets and some effects you can slot into the mod slots of the weapons, but you will never really affect how the guns themselves operate. The combinations you have available to you are extremely limited, and thus there is not much experimentation in the game. Your fire bullets will be the same fire bullets they were from hour 1 to hour 20. Same goes for your shock or cold bullets. Only the damage value changes between iterations. But you must research them nonetheless if you want to do damage.The amount of resources required for the bullet upgrades is considerable, though not insurmountable. Most of the game will consist of you farming for specific rocks, trees or enemies to obtain these materials so you can increase your bullet's power by some vague margin. Beyond the loop to buff your bullets, you do some minibosses and hunt for gears so you can progress to the next boss.The game is also incredibly easy for even a modestly seasoned gamer. Personally, I only died once and that was to a boss because of an environmental detail I did not factor in to the fight. It wasn't even the lass boss I died to, but the third to last one. All other bosses, including the final one, were more bullet spongy than actually difficult. The game did appeal to me enough that I do not consider it a wasted purchase. What mechanics there were along with the music and the art style helped me to power through to the endgame. I suppose I got my money's worth, but maybe wait a while to see what will change before you try this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Wizard With A Gun is an isometric rogue-lite that is reminiscent of Don't Starve, with much better combat and without the survival aspects.  A playthrough takes around 15-20 hours, during which you visit a variety of environments, face a handful of bosses, and expand your catalog of craftables/upgrades by scanning enemies and objects.  The bullets you use can come from 8 different elements, all of which have robust tech trees to spec as you like.  At release, it seems there are a few balance issues, where some elements are definitely more effective than others, but it is still fun to experiment with the variety of playstyles available.The artwork and music are incredible, but my biggest complaint with the game is the inventory management.  While there is a "quick stack" button, by half-way through the game, its lack of other quality of life storage features makes organizing your accumulated materials a bit of a slog.  Hopefully future updates can address this.That aside, I REALLY enjoyed my time with Wizard With A Gun and have already encouraged a few of my friends to give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: At first, I was really pleased with this game. A nice mix of crafting, exploration, resource gathering, and combat all sitting on top of a progression system with many options to craft unique guns. Learning the systems and uncovering all the different systems was fun; it's also quite casual, so you never felt overwhelmed.However, things start to fall apart once you get into the game. The combat never feels particularly challenging or complex; apparently, a wizard with a gun (and a dodge-roll button) is, by far, the most powerful combination in this world. There was very little thought needed when entering combat--generally just spamming your gun, dodging an occasional attack, and then chugging a health potion when I needed one. I never had to consider using the environment, craft a new gun, trying out different ammo, or anything else resembling a challenge. The visual language is also messy--you never really get the sense you're doWhere things really fall apart is the amount of grind. You're grinding resources, scanning for new technologies or decorations, and progressing through the research trees. There's a lot to unlock, discover, and progress through--which feels like the real focus point of the game. Like the res tof the game, I liked the sense of progression at first, as a lot of what you're unlocking opens up new builds and game-changing tech. Even that fades away quickly, as you're looking for 10-15 of a specific resource to upgrade your "Ammo Level" from 5 to 6, so you can do more damage to that Level 7 enemy. Pretty soon the loop of play the game > discover new content > unlock new stuff disappears, and the loop because play the game > look for a specific resource > upgrade your ammo type from level 6 to 7. Boring.The plainest comparison I can think of is Hades, which features a similar perspective, combat style, and rogue-like elements. Though quite different, this plays like a much slower Hades, with only one weapon type, and much less exciting combat. And without the combat feeling rewarding or challenging, it's hard for the rest of the progression of this game to draw me in.When you consider all the environments, types of enemys, fast-paced combat, a less visually messy combat system (more clear when you take damage/you feel like you deserve it), and more that you can get in Hades, I can't help but wonder what Wizard with a Gun could have been if more time was spent polishing its core combat loop to be something a little more interesting. It'd make me want to get through all the crafting and progression, rather than it feeling like a chore.If you are a fan of roguelikes, like the art style, or want to tackle this as a co-op experience, there's a good game here. However, there are far better roguelikes out there, in terms of gameplay, progression, and story, and really would only recommend this game to true fans of the genre. For most, this game is entirely skippable.

_childDocuments_.review: After beating the 2nd world boss, and getting relatively far in, I feel like I can leave a review. To some, this game wouldn't hit right, I'm not sure what people entirely expected, but I just expected cool wizard w/ a gun. Anyways, to sum it up, it's sort of like a mixture between Risk of Rain and Don't Starve. The RoR comparison being a timed run (when you go into the main world, you have 5 minutes, but can extend the time if you kill chaos creatures). The Don't Starve comparison being that you can craft, and essentially get better gear by progression. It's a survival/rogue like game. Don't read to deep into it, and give it a try. I like it, a lot of others like it, those few that don't...typically have valid reasons. Like I said, just give it a go, and see how you feel, personally I'd recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: So far I would describe it as fine. It has most of the pitfalls and annoyances of crafting/survival games,  but at least I didn't feel like I needed to sink several hours into the game before I could start doing cool stuff. Inventory and crafting management is completely terrible, and hoping this  gets addressed soon with a patch.I have two main complaints about the game-Fire rate doesn't seem to be visible when selecting what bullets to craft for a gun. This made telling some the major differences between the  various weapons not  intuitive. The guns  only show reload/range/clip, and bullets only showed damage. However guns also seem to have different rate of fire, but its  not explained anywhere and you would only see the difference when comparing the same bullet on two different guns.-The game feels slow. This could be something that changes later into the game, but it currently feels like I'm wading through mud to travel anywhere. This could just be from expecting it be paced more like Gungeon or Nuclear Throne, but I thought I remember seeing the game play faster in some of the gameplay trailers.Overall its been pretty cool. Though the survival parts are probably the weakest and most tedious part to play. Its definitely more "Don't Starve" than "Nuclear Throne".

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so it's a pretty fun game for a rougelike crafter.  Specially with a friend.  The loop is pretty good as you go out and get mats to upgrade your research on like... so many types of bullets and benches.  There's a surprising amount of options when it comes to choosing how to advance your combat abilities.Though I will say, for a crafting based game, it was missing a LOT of the quality of life things you'd expect games to have even a decade ago.  The grid that everything snaps to makes it so that walking around sucks as you can't walk between boxes and benches diagonally adjacent to each other.  Upgrading chests require you take EVERYTHING out of them, remove the old chest, build the new one, and put everything back, which is SUCH garbage.  Also, in multiplayer, you have to wait your turn at benches and chests as you can't access them together, making prepping for runs a little annoying.Also, everything I just mentioned, they the absolute last session I played this game.  And usually I'd congratulate the devs for this, but like, this was for version 1.2 of the game.  THESE ARE 1.0 FEATURES.  I'm  real sick of all these games coming out unfinished.  And what's worse, the end of the game is just a simple text box that's like "more content in the future."  I really doubt I'm going to come back to this game.  So while I do recommend this game, I would highly recommend you wait until the game is actually content complete.  You know, ACTUAL 1.0And you might think I'm being unfair because plenty of games have a similar model, but like, this isn't additional content they decided to come back and make later.  It's evident that this is content they clearly had in the works before release, but just said ♥♥♥♥ it, we'll do it later, release the game now. _childDocuments_.review: Yes, it's a fine game, a fun game, an agreeable game.  I'm taking my time while I play, but I figure I'm partway through the second chapter and there's another three or so to go, so... it's a 40-to-50 hour game without endgame grindery.  I've paid a whole lot more for much shorter games that I've enjoyed less, though this one was a gift so technically I paid nothing at all.It was on my wishlist because it looked like a wizardly spin on a western.  It isn't that at all, it's not that "precise" with its theme.  It's a Flash-looking twin-stick shooter set in fantasy-sorta lands with somewhat atypical monsters.Hopefully you know what Flash was, because this is a big part of the game's look and feel.  Anyway, baaaack in the day there were websites that hosted Flash games.  Flash was less secure than painting your phone's password right on its screen, and being that Flash was an engine that was rendered through your browser without a 3D card, it had a lot of limitations.  People made games despite those limitations, which leans towards a kind of style with rotating segments and overlays.  Flash animations were made by rotating various pieces, so a running character would have a thigh "piece" and a shin "piece", and by rotating and translating each piece you had a moving leg.To customize characters, you'd just drop say, a hat or hair, right atop the head piece. Just lay it right over.  If the location wasn't chosen perfectly, that costume piece might move sliiiightly differently than the thing it was supposed to hide or improve, and that effect is hard to describe other than "amusingly wobbly". Many Flash artists could not, or would not, draw a face.  They'd prefer to simply draw a black orb and put a couple dots for eyes.  And this game does all that:  orb-face-with-dots, stapled-on wobbly costume pieces, animations that look like rotating bits.  And that's fine, maybe I'm being nostalgic for it. My wife wanted to compare the animation and style against "Don't Starve", should that mean anything to you.In a somewhat nicer touch, you can rebuild and decorate your between-missions base.  There's a lot of furniture options if you really care to amuse yourself. Decorations have only one colour and orientation, but since the camera can't be rotated, it doesn't matter a great deal.As far as the game goes, I haven't really felt challenged so far.  I've died once, mostly from inattentiveness.  It plays in quick ten-minute bursts, with a bit of downtime between to pursue more R&D, fill in holes in the floor, craft more ammo, consider going out for another run and realizing it's been a few hours and sleep isn't a bad idea.  And I guess that's a sure sign it's fun enough.It's not the deepest game, despite all these ammo types, and there's not a great deal of plot, but sometimes there doesn't need to be a great narrative either.  It's a perfectly agreeable game.EDIT:  Looks like my time estimate was generous.  It took me 16.5 hours, though I did sort of hammer through the rest of the content quickly.  I was previously taking detours to mine rocks and wood to fix up the tower.Some people complain the final boss is a bit spongey.  Well, it does take quite a few licks to get to the center of that Tootsie Roll, true.  I beat him in a bit over 3.5 minutes, using a single blunderbuss, with ammo to spare.

_childDocuments_.review: A reasonably satisfying sandbox experience, although not especially memorable it remains enjoyable all the same.The game upholds some fairly decent presentation between the art, animation, music and general atmosphere of the world. Unfortunately the story is mostly obscure and hard to follow; told through scattered books which reference numerous places, characters and concepts that struggle to come together in a coherently understandable lore. The core story itself is a mostly generic fantasy concept that serves to rationalize the gameplay itself, and does not feel especially gripping beyond that.While some elements of the interface and controls can be a little finicky, especially in the middle of combat, the game generally plays quite well. For the most part it is not especially difficult or easy, and strikes a relatively engaging middle ground. The hazards are either fair or forgiving, with the only outstanding frustration being that if players run out of ammunition during a boss fight they cannot recover from that in any way. It is virtually unknowable how much damage will be needed to defeat a boss so unless players load up with extreme caution each time they risk simply running out of bullets in a place where they cannot acquire more. There are a decent amount of different combat options and elemental interactions that the player can tap into when playing, which helps to diversify the experience somewhat. The system does fall flat in some instances however. Players gradually acquire new tiers of guns, which largely defeats the purpose of equipping their passive modifiers when a new tier of gun will soon completely replace it. Similarly, loading up guns with ammunition may become obsolete at times because the player can just pillage half-loaded guns off certain enemies; which allows the player to skip levelling up their bullets entirely for a period. In general the game suffers from the classic problem of its diversifying mechanics often being too inconvenient to bother working with, and so while certain features are not completely useless it is often easier to just ignore them and power forward. By the end of the game those features become much more appealing as the easier methods wither in effectiveness, but at said point there isn't much content left to explore either.The world is a fairly generic and limited assemblance of biomes with a scant amount of environmental mechanics to actually diversify them. The unique environmental hazards that do exist are nearly all just debilitations gradually applied when standing on certain tiles. and thus every environment feels slightly the same. The environments and enemies are decently varied enough in their presentation but lack any kind of unique flair or innovation to really stand out. The overall game progression feels relatively typical and well paced but definitely could use a lot more substance at the end when players have really filled out their kit. By the time the player has potentially acquired a sizeable and stable amount of combat options the game is almost over, which makes the latter portion of this experience feel practically unfinished. There does seem to be plans to add more content in the future at least, so hopefully this will be addressed at some point.The basic presentation of the experience is polished and the gameplay is adequate, but the absence of a more coherent narrative or fulfilling endgame leaves it somewhat forgettable. Definitely compelling enough to be worth at least one play however, especially with the presence of multiplayer.If you're interested in finding more games like this I've probably reviewed quite a few on my curator page .

_childDocuments_.review: i was one of those many people who were like "kinda mid, but they have a bunch planned so i'm sure it'll be great!" and i heard that the studio had to shut down bc of finances and that a whole bunch of negative reviews were being dropped, so i decided to break my rule and leave a genuine one on the game.i didn't actually play a whole lot. i put it off for updates, so i'm in that "miss what i didn't even experience," and that was my fault! but what there was in the game was fantastic. even replaying bosses for resources never started feeling like a drag, the admittedly simplistic gameplay loop of be here -> get things -> upgrade -> win -> go somewhere else -> get things was actually rather pleasant with the core aesthetic of the game and the chaos mechanic was done really well and added a not-so-pressing sense of urgency to every time we went out. i loved the concept of "spells, but with GUNS," it was so novel to me that i had been excited for this game since the fabled archivist told me about it when it was still supposed to have 4 player multiplayer and it was still the funnest game i've played when it was only 2 player. figuring out what bullets did and keeping track of what gun had what bullets was so fun, it'd been executed so well.i loved this game for what it was, but there was a bunch of other things i was doing and i thought it felt a little bit empty, but it'd just been released and i wanted to see what was coming in the future, and i am so sad to hear that it's "nothing's comin' in the future, we can't do it." this game & you, the developers, deserved better. i'm looking forward to what you guys do in the future. the game is still absolutely worth the $25. i don't think there's anything quite like it, or ever will be again.

_childDocuments_.review: It's called Wizard With A Gun but to be honest, not once did I feel like a wizard. The whole game I felt like some average guy that has a gun that can shoot different kinds of bullets. There is a clear problem with the name of the game have no correlation with the actual gameplay.The overall gameplay is simple. You have guns and you can shoot. You don't have stand alone abilities and really no cooldowns. All bullets do act differently such as poison, water, ice, fire, oil, and lightning. These all feel different which is good, but a big problem is the fact that there is really no reason to use any of the bullets outside of the Lightning Strike bullet. This single bullet is extremely powerful to all enemies in the game and is very good at destroying structures to have an easier time getting resources. This bullet does have a cooldown but you can simply have all 5 of your weapons have this bullet type, then the cooldown doesn't matter.Resource gathering is simple. Kill creatures and destroy structures like trees and rocks to get various items. Different creatures and structures drop different items, leading you to want to target specific things for specific items. Some items can only be found in certain biomes.The biomes is fine. There are 5 total with each one having only a slight change in your gameplay. 1 is a poisonous swamp, making any water you step in, give the poison debuff. Outside of this though, there is no other mechanic in this biome. Throughout the whole game there is a clock in the top of the screen showing a day and night cyle. Problem is only one Biome actually uses this day night cycle as a mechanic. There is otherwise no reason for this clock to even be on the screen.Not very many weapon types in this game. There is a pistol, and smg, a shotgun, and a carbine...That's it. No rocket launcher or minigun or unique weapon. Many of the weapons feel the exact same outside of the smg having higher rate of fire and carbine having more range and dmg. The only upgrade you can do the to guns themselves is simply buying the same gun but a higher rarity. So white to a green rarity pistol but it doesnt have any different attributes or stats outside of the damage changing.Crafting in the game is fine. You get a high abundance of items from the very start so you don't feel short on supplies. By about the second biome you'll see that you actually have way more items than you need and will eventually get lost in your supplies if not organized from the start.The bosses are pretty cool, I actually don't have much to say about them other than the final boss being easier than all the other bosses. Killed it on the first try just from using the lightning strike bullet. Sure she destroys the ground but it doesn't matter since she is fought in the main world and not in an arena that is in a limited space like all of the other bosses.After defeating the final boss there is literally nothing else to do. There is no goal and nothing else to strive for.Would I recommend? Not for $24.99. If the price were to be $15 then I would say yes.(I played this game with someone that was in another country, the lag was bad but not so bad that it was unplayable)

_childDocuments_.review: I have been waiting for a while for Wizard with a Gun and it was alot of fun playing it at first.Thought it didn't last long and i found myself being bored with it by the second day playing with a friend.It didn't stop us from doing dumb things that only temporarily satisfied our craving for enjoyment.Simply said, this game feels like it is lacking stuff.Powders are limited and feel like they do the same:-Home under a certain condition-Leave a trail of an element-make the Bullet Faster/slower-make the effect of one bullets a bit strongerThe most fun things was putting momentum on summoned items but that felt like the game wanting us to do so and if im honest, there never was a combination that felt like "Oh i found something unique and funny" but morelike "yep, this is what the game wants me to do"I personally never had in issue with the grind as we have focused on one speciality (i went for Sorcerer stuff while my friend unlocked Alchemist things) and if we needed something new from the other classes, we had stuff to unlock it already.i don't know if it was how my friend and i played but there wasn't a challange anywhere. it was almost too easy until we reached the Barren sea where just suddenly a bunch of mini-bosses set us ablaze which didn't hurt us too much but was still annoying as hell and the endboss was a major dissapointment as we just shoved it around and it couldn't do anything to us. The ending was also a dissapointment. after defeating the big bad chaos thing it just fades to black and was like "Dass all Folks!!". Of course this is a over exageration because one could technically still customized their tower and experiment with new not so unique Bullet/Powder combination but lets be honest, not alot of people will do that.It felt tedious to pretend it was still fun and in the state it is now, completing the game will only give you a major dissapointment, so what i can only suggest is to wait for updates and hope they add more powder that actually are different enough from each other, add an endgame and maybe add a better satisfying ending

_childDocuments_.review: Taken as a whole, I can't really recommend this game to anyone who sees 'Wizard with a Gun' and might rightfully think that the game is about using guns to do magic.In a sense, it kind of is, but in effect, it really just feels like a basic setup of 'here are your four elemental affinities, have fun' game without actually doing anything interesting beyond unremarkable combos, like 'get an enemy wet for extra lightning damage' or 'freeze the enemy then shoot until they shatter'. Maybe I'm asking a lot, but it just doesn't do much with its whole premise.So, to drill down the issues:* Combat is kinda bad. You're a 2D character in a pseudo-3D environment, so it's hard to tell what will and won't hit you, and your options are pretty limited; as outlined above, the premise that you are a wizard with a gun is just a new coat of paint on an old set of mechanics, and not a lot of interesting spells or guns.* Story is kinda boring, and hard to follow. None of the essential characters you come across tell you much besides a few specific but uninteresting lines about being sad that the world has ended.* Movement just kinda sucks. That's all. Movement is slow, and it feels like you're fighting your own movement speed as much as you're fighting the enemies. Oh, and this becomes a real problem when you're fighting Chaos enemies, who actively destroy the environment around you and remove places you can move to, which is already limited because you're slower than literally everything and the only thing you can outmaneuver are static objects.* Crafting and storage mechanics are just weirdly difficult to interact with at times, and the UI can feel cluttered and tough to navigate.* Building mechanics are okay and there are lots of interesting looking buildings you can make, but none of them do anything, so there's really no reason to actually learn how to build stuff; there are buildings that seem perfectly tailored to be niche crafting stations for advanced weapons that are just purely decorated (i.e. a poison cauldron, a lightning pyramid, etc.)Altogether, the game was okay on release, and got a bit meatier as it was updated and got a proper final boss/ending, but I was super disappointed by the state of it, and it just never had the chance it deserved to be fully fleshed out and meet its true potential, especially with the road map and various bits of planned content that just never made it into the finished game, and all of the ways it seemed like the game's mechanics in crafting and combat would have worked if the game had reached that point.

_childDocuments_.review: While the game has its own identity, nice graphics (basically prettier Don't Starve) and good music, thats the extent of the praise I can give it to.The gameplay loop is very unsatisfying, with combat you've seen the entirety of what it has to offer within 5 minutes and it doesnt seem to evolve anywhere, and the base is where you craft and upgrade stuff, through an obtuse UI made of dozens of separate menus connected to multiple separate crafting tables.The game seems to want massive amounts of many different resources, there are tons of upgrades, many of them just being +5% damage or whatever, it was discouraging to come back to a raid to then not being able to craft anything new. We also didnt die once. There is no story, no cutscenes, no narration either.It is a pure gameplay game and the core gameplay simply isnt good enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfinished and massively wasted potential. The ending is a “you saved the world! More content soon!” screen before credits roll after you kill the final boss.Since Enemies have no resistances whatsoever means you have very little incentive to actually bring multiple weapons with varying skills, and every Element having their own research bench only further discourages fanning out as you quickly adapt one element and stick with it. There’s also rather little environmental or combo potential with your guns and their elements. Upgrading your guns or tinkering with spell modifiers is too uninteresting to bring any real joy. My personal highlight was putting “spawn ground” on Teleport Bullets since it meant I could just zip through the void instead of having to build platforms.Base Building and Crafting are uninteresting to bother with, safe for the first workbenches and floors with movement speed increase there is nothing beneficial to it when you spend 85% of the game outside of your base and receive no bonuses to e.g. smelting speed. Overall, a quaint little early access game with an interesting theme and nice soundtrack, but basic gameplay that doesn’t evolve beyond the first two hours. 6/10, not worth if not on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a fun game with noticeable flaws. Hopefully it all gets filled in with future patches. It do feel like an early access. Which does prompt me to raise my pitchfork or baguette equivalent.For now the first 5 out of 11 hours in singleplayer are quite fun (reduced a lot in multiplayer as a big chunk is gathering material, two inventory helps a lot). However as the challenge increase you need to use better tools and that mostly nulls two elements and one weapon. That's bad!Poison and fire are too weak, therefore heavily ammo inefficient. Hope you're ready to grind up more material!Shotguns are funny as they hurt you more than they hurt the opponent as AoE and trails you can add to it are so big you're inside their radius at all time. But at max AoE it does become a bit more reliable at offing enemies, a bummer its quite late for that.Thunder and carbines need nerfs. Flat out. Easiest and strongest damage tool in the game with minor combo potential. (spreads over liquids, like it also needed to deal splash damage) Longest range, safest, highest damage.Needs more diversity. Most tools we have are too similar. A gun that shoots a bullet that you can't really customise, modifiers are for most part small number changes or does the same thing with a different coat of elemental paint.The lowest of the barrel being a modifier that adds the gimmick of an entire ammo type to any other. So you double dip instead of using just one at once and nullifying all your upgrades onto the original. Why? And why this one ?Needs tuning. The whole ammo system could be improved from the ground up instead of being highly generic.So far this doesn't 'wizard' enough. Enemies are more 'wizard'-y than we do. They have the indiscriminate fun stuff. The different attack modes, grenades, artillery strikes...

_childDocuments_.review: WwaG is a perfectly acceptable game. I'm not overly excited about it, but it also wasn't so fun that I couldn't put it down or wanted to rush out to tell me friends to play it immediately. The artwork is nicely done and colorful. The story is...well I didn't really bother to read it. There are books hidden around the various biomes filled with text but it's easy to skip them. Combat is twin stick shooter with a variety of modifiers for your weapons (fire, ice, poison, lightning, etc.). So why am I not super hot on this game? Several reasons. Traversing the map is frustrating because there are holes you can get stuck on, or poison tiles which look incredibly similar to non-poison tiles. The primary chaos enemy can also create new, unexpected holes which exacerbates the issue. You do eventually find a way to recreate land, but that's also frustrating to use. Healing is also frustrating. I played on Steam Deck with the joysticks. Weapons are cycled using the shoulder button or holding a shoulder button to get a selection wheel. Healing is done with the X-button and there is also a healing wheel displayed when X is held. The frustrating thing is that when a healing slot is exhausted it doesn't immediately move to the next non-empty slot. Instead you need to hold X to bring up the wheel and select. This is awful because it means your thumbs that should be occupied with navigating and aiming are now both tied up with the healing selection choice, leaving you standing still in a time where you suddenly needed healing. Some other minor gripes are that it is very repetitive and not terribly challenging. Each time you unlock a new biome your bullet damage levels effectively reset. You then collect essentially the same types of resources as you did in the previous biome to level up your bullets again. Rinse and repeat for 4 biomes. There's no need to worry if you are using the right bullet type against an enemy because all of them will work just fine. I played through and rolled credits, and I'm satisfied with it. If you are interested in a twin stick shooter with colorful art you could do worse, you could do better.

_childDocuments_.review: This game doesn't really feel finished. Had it on my radar from when it was announced a few years back, missed out on the pre-order sale but was able to get it later down the line from another sale so I was pretty excited to play. And I was, at least for the first few hours. The grinding nature wasn't too bad if a bit annoying as queuing up what I wanted to research or build next did start to get really tedious to the point where more often then not I was lacking supplies to improve on anything. Base building was okay if extremely bare bones and not easy to really customize the area to your liking until you were a lot further into the game where the basic supplies can be used to decorate without having to worry if you have enough to upgrade anything. Storage management was a chore through and through. The enchantments could have been a bit more robust, still don't know why the mask has an enchantment slot available but no enchantments to actually put on it.Combat was actually pretty nice give or take if a bit clunky in areas. Although the different bullet types didn't give as exciting of a experience as hoped. Although that may be chalked up to personal play style. Mostly ended up defaulting to destruction bullets cause hey, why have worry about getting poisoned or set on fire by your own bullet effect when you can use old reliable? Though my enjoyment of the combat ends at the Riders. Those fights were challenging and had me thinking of what would work best against them, the final boss was so underwhelming that I didn't even have to worry about dying. Even the bounty bosses gave me more of a challenge then the supposed big bad of the game.Continuing on the final boss, this may be a personal problem of mine but I have no memory of the journals telling you that you can bring the Riders with you. There's an entry that talks about the void skimmer but it's probably meant to infer that if you can fix the skimmer you can bring in the extra help. By that point I was just about to fight the final boss and hadn't fought any of the gold bounties yet. It took looking it up to be able to figure out how to fix it.Despite its issues the game is enjoyable. Maybe there's a difference with playing with others rather than playing by yourself like I did. Is there a chance of me playing it again? Yes because while I'm disappointed in areas there are still things that I find enjoyable. I love the story, I get excited finding the materials I need, I love the art style of everything. But in the current state its not really recommendable to people. It has some charm but not enough to ask people to get at full price. Hopefully the devs will continue to update the game because there's a lot of potential.

_childDocuments_.review: Wizard With A Gun; what a kickass name. It really gives it to you straight, right away. You're a Wizard. You've got a gun. Really, hard to beat that. What the title doesn't tell you is, you're also a wizard about to feel the most sorrow and sonder that any wizard has ever felt for a gameplay loop. The atmosphere out in the world is serene, wistful almost, as you watch your timer tick down. Your predecessor stands by and watches, exhausted, as you tackle each day with vigor and efficiency she hasn't been able to summon in herself for a Long Time; like you're really trying to stop that timer. And you can  her watching you, while you work away at gathering materials and arcana, while you learn everything you can about the world she's given up on. My heart aches thinking about it. Otherwise, the mechanics are fun and compelling. If you like circular gameplay, this is the game for you. Gather resources, explore, level up, repeat. Spend some of your excess materials decorating your kickass new wizard tower. Oh and... try not to worry too much about all that "outside of time and space" stuff. Its fine! Its your cool tower and there's nothing distressing about it!My only true complaint is that multiplayer is 2 players only at this time, but it looks like 4 player support might be on its way? All around solid and fun game, new content on the way, and again.  With A . A+

_childDocuments_.review: Wizard with a Gun is a stretch of a title. I'd call this game faceless dudes with spicy bullets. The mechanics are all there but it lacks any flair. The spells are just power-ups. There's some simple combos but nothing super thrilling. The game is just revisiting the same generated map and going to different area types in search of materials to upgrade and make bullets. Do that 4 times and unlock the final boss. The aesthetics and stylization are worth playing the game for but expect to be headshot by someone off screen while you enjoy them...

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Twinstick shooter sandbox with a lot to like on the surface; quite fun but feels unfinished.More content in the future is promised, so perhaps you should wait and see before buying.-Gameplay is tight when you're in the few bossfights the game offers-Spell creation is something I love to see as a mechanic in games and Wizard with a Gun gets a lot of things right about it-Pretty decent enemy variety for each area, they all feel distinct-Crafting and building is what you would expect from survivalcraft type games, with resource tiers tied to each of the 4 areas-Not too much of a grind to get things you need, reasonable-The most well-structured sidequest in the game is the tutorial-It is unclear when you unlock new gun blueprints and you're more likely to use a dropped weapon than one crafted at the NPC-The 4 types of guns each feel samey throughout the game, aside from the spells you stick on them-Ending is bafflingly abrupt when compared to the flashy animated intro-Overworld lacks challenge aside from when you are being completely overwhelmed (Only died 1-3 times completing the game in singleplayer)-Lategame has some spongy enemies (hope you enjoy kiting in an arena that is actively being destroyed)-Many narrative threads are left dangling and most backstory/lore is delivered through notes or a recurring NPC (I can't help but wonder if there was intended to be more story, especially considering the ending)I'll likely update this review/pile of bulletpoints in the future after more is added to the game.

_childDocuments_.review: First few hours offer lots of variety and a are fun to explore. Later gameplay has you grind to be able to do damage to bosses.Lots of grind. Early grind is rewarded with power and variety. Later grind is a barrier to fight the boss accompanied by an insignificant power boost.Very few enemies are challenging enough for combat to be engaging. That's especially true once you upgrade your bullets so you're not under-leveled.To clarify on boss/enemies levels: If your bullet level is lower than enemy level your damage gets a massive reduction and at some point you do no damage at all. If you remove this system an average player would beat it in about 3-4 hours without rushing. Bypassing those artificial limitations is vast majority if your game.People compare it to Don't Starve games and it's really not even close. Don't Starve keeps the tension up, because if you don't play/craft you die. Every upgrade helps you survive easier. In this game the only reason to craft is bypassing that level barrier to fight the next boss.The game's broken down into 5-15 minute sessions where you kill and destroy everything for materials. You also unlock recipes by scanning things and creatures.The shooting and collection component is fairly basic, BUT elemental bullets and bullet modifiers introduce an interesting dynamic to the game. For one, effects of different types of bullets can combine into stronger effects. Bullet effects also modify materials you're getting. Half of the gameplay is figuring out how you get a particular material that you thought would appear later in game. Granted some materials simply require you to progress to start appearing, but many come from sources you have access to immediately if you apply correct effect to them. If not for effect variety and creativity I'd give it a 4/10, because . First 3-5 hours give you lots of different tools, but after that it all boils down to choosing and upgrading elemental bullets (and picking up upgrades that work with them). You have many elements to choose from, but this game punishes you for not focusing on branch of elements. Technically it just wastes your time without rewarding you, but it's kind of the same thing...After the first few hours you'll notice enemies have shields and in short, if enemy shield is much greater than your bullet level, your bullets do nothing. If you don't focus on 1 specific build low bullet levels will prevent you from doing any damage.Different elemental effects and interactions between them is the biggest strength of this game, but having no reason to use them (other than curiocity) and being punished for experimenting is the biggest weakness.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is from the standpoint of a person who's beaten the entire game once with a friend, so keep that in mind when I make points about gameplay, as it may shift my views. The presentation of the game overall is top notch. The visuals are distinct and nice to look at, the character designs are fun, and the music is simply great. And while I didn't pay all too much attention to the lore and writing, I can say that the dialogue the NPCs give is quite charming. As for the gameplay, I find it quite fun. The gameplay loop of venturing out, getting stuff, and powering up is rewarding, especially as you witness your arsenal grow. This can be extra rewarding with a friend, as you coordinate and synergize certain attacks, and multitask to get as much out of your wilderness dives as possible. The game itself also feels great to control and play. I found the guns super satisfying to use, and enemies equally satisfying to gun down. Blend that with the pretty snappy controls, and it's just a fun time. The base building aspect is also a nice side activity inbetween the more fast paced action, and is almost completely optional if you don't care about that stuff. I'd say the survival elements blended in quite well, too. It was fun to figure out how and where to get certain materials. While this could get annoying after a while, the game is short enough that I found it to not be too big a deal. The ending section was frankly, a disappointment. The final boss had no fanfare, minimal buildup outside of lore, and the ending was literally just a couple lines of text on a black screen before cutting to credits. While the boss itself was fine, it didn't have the gravitas or energy that a final boss should have. It felt like the ending of an early access game, except on one that's fully released. The fact that it didn't seem to have it's own theme unlike the rest of the bosses certainly didn't help. The game is also short, me and a friend beat it in 12 hours while trying to get everything we could. Personally, I'd say that it's good value, but others might not be so inclined. And, an  This game is not four player, even though some of the marketing has four wizards, implying four player, it only supports 1-2 players as of the writing of this review. Gameplay wise this changes nothing for me, but if you wanted to get a game to rough around in with some friends, sad to say you'll probably need to pass this up. While there are definitely a few hiccups along the way, and the game may fumble at the ending, it's a relatively short, but fun high quality experience to share with a friend. If you're interested in it, give it a shot. Even if you're not, go listen to the soundtrack, it's really good.Tl;dr: A fairly brief, very high quality experience that's made even better with a friend. Just don't expect much out of the ending.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game.  I did have fun when I was playing out in the world, balancing collecting resources and progressing, and theorycrafting a build to go back out in the wild.On the other hand, every time I got back to the base, it felt awful.  Everything took real world time to build and prep, and having to self-manage an inventory system is something I will never enjoy.  It feels to me that the game might have been a crafting survival game at some point, where timegating and imperfect inventory systems make sense, but keeping that system when you're in a base, and there's no meaningful time or location pressure is awful, because I feel like it wastes the player's time for no reason.I don't recommend the game right now because I don't think it knows what it wants to be, but would be willing to give it another review if they rework the base to not waste so much time.

_childDocuments_.review: Played during free weekend. This is one of those games I'd play through something like Game Pass, but wouldn't buy myself.I had a good bit of fun in the first two hours while playing with friends, but the game shows you more or less everything during that time. There is an extreme shift to long grinds in the 2nd biome, the swamp. Combine what is classically considered one the least liked biome types with a rough transition to a long grind and you quickly realize how stale Wizard with a Gun will be.As well, one of the best strats for the first boss is for one of the players to die and haunt the boss as a ghost. When a player becomes a ghost, they can instill fear in an enemy. This causes the enemy to flee and prevents their attacks during the fleeing action. In other words: you can do a soft stunlock on the boss while other players attack through repeated haunting.Maybe there is something fun buried deeper past the 2nd biome, but ultimately the game couldn't keep its own pace it sets in the first two hours.

_childDocuments_.review: tldr if you were looking for a survival base builder you may like it, give it a try. But if you wanted a more challenging experience since they advertise rogue like elements this would not really be for you, youd probably get bored pretty quickly with the combat.Magic gun building pretty shallow - craft bullets that determine your spell, and put in modifiers that slightly buff it. The modifiers are nothing special to make the spell actually interesting, just stuff like trails, damage boosts, homing etc. Different magic types have separate skill trees which is really annoying imo since it discourages actually mixing the modifiers/spells from different trees since youll just be required to keep skilling a single tree for progression (you literally cannot do damage to higher level enemies if you dont upgrade the bullets).Bigger problem though is that spell building even if it was cool, is not really needed since the combat is not a challenge whatsoever. The rogue like element is that you go out of your base on expeditions where if you die youll drop all your stuff. But the combat and bosses are so uninteresting and easy that you could probably beat them all without using the gun building. Just keep walking and dodge red lines, occasionally move out of enemy's range cause they have a tracking beam. I have played around for a bit, trying fire and lightning trees and beat the first boss without even being close to dying, even though i know ive messed up some attacks.

_childDocuments_.review: I do recommend the game for the price, and I definitely got my money's worth. The rest of the review are simply some gripes or thoughts my friends and I had on the game as we played through it. It's a fun game with a very cool artstyle, but the game itself falls a little short of expectations.The game itself isn't very difficult, making the game feel short. Because we could basically double our material collection by playing co-op, My friend and I were easily 3/4ths of the way through the game after only 2 sessions. Throughout those 2 sessions, we only had 2 downs and 2 deaths, and those were simply because I wasn't paying attention to a swarm of enemies. None of those downs or deaths were the result of a boss, which you'd expect to be more threatening than they are.The progression feels very off in the way some things are structured. Some resources can be obtained WAY earlier than you should be able to, for instance we were able to get cobalt, steel and sandstone a whole "tier" earlier than intended, which allows you to only make progress on certain bullet types, but not others. Other times you'd be given the means to UNLOCK something, but won't be able to craft it until you enter the next zone, which kinda feels like ass considering the unlock requirement is usually a comparatively difficult boss enemy.The combat itself can feel a bit repetitive and same-y. Enemies also don't seem to have an resistances aside from being too high level, so you end up just using the same combination of bullets for the entire run (once you unlock them). The selection of bullets is also very awkward. Some of the elements get a wide array of bullet choices to choose from, while Fire and Poison get 1, maybe 2 different bullets. Some bullets have upgradable tiers that increase damage, while others are one-and-done and can't be upgraded beyond the initial unlock. Certain types, like Fear, Charming, and Order just don't match up to the other bullet types in functionality and practicality, and go underutilized.The bullets do have a nice variety, and work well together, but don't MESH well together. You don't really spec into combo builds like you'd expect from an element-based system, it's more of a utility + damage of your choosing scenario. Element combinations are mostly "stun/freeze the enemy then hit them with any other bullet" rather than specific scenarios or special reactions, like Lightning + Fire. The reactions that DO exist in the game, like electrifying lightning, feel very underwhelming and usually only do chip damage. A LOT of these reactions are large AoEs and can hurt you as well, which leaves little incentive to use them over safer and higher DPS options.The game also has a decent emphasis or infrastructure for decoration. In my opinion, the game doesn't really lend itself to creative building, and someone who prefers functionality over aesthetics, this whole system feels like a loss to me. There's just not a single point throughout the game where you feel like you need to decorate, as those resources are usually required and better spent progressing through the various crafting and unlock trees.For a game tagged as a rougelike, it offers little to no replayability. The "random runs" you'd expect from a rougelike only matter when you start an expedition, which is basically just the timed material/progression run. The only randomness involved is each biome's layout. Outside of that, any future runs and playthroughs of the game will be exactly the same.Overall, despite these flaws I had fun. I do hope the game gets more content in the future, it seems like it could really use it.

_childDocuments_.review: Wizard with a Gun is a pretty good Co-Op game, I enjoyed this with a friend over the free weekend. As a fan of most of Devolver published games, I might be a bit biased but I don't really have any negative takeaways from Wizard with a Gun.The art style reminds me of some mix of Don't Starve and Awesomenauts, the combat is filled with pretty hectic gunplay, and the progression trees are large enough to feel like a deep experience mixing and matching gun types, elements, and passives creating fairly unique feeling guns. You can customize your base, completely optional but there are a large amounts of props and cosmetic buildings to create a custom home to your liking. it took me between 15 and 20 hours to 100% but your time may vary a lot, since i did a lot of experimenting with different elements.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, just beat the story as it is, gonna go for 100% achievements soon enough. This is a pretty fun game /so far/. I say so far since at the end you get a 'More To Come' for whatever that means. Judging on the content here alone though, it's pretty fun! The gameplay is pretty tight, I'd say, though you really don't unlock the most fun toys until late into the game. Until I was 3/4ths of the way through the game I was basically just using Bullet and then Bullet 2. More damage. Once you get to end game though? I had a pistol that shot slowing, sticky, oil that doused an entire area around the target, then a extra-lasting fire bullet that set half of the screen on fire in a blue blaze of flames, providing crits for the lightning bolts on my other gun.  It has a lot of fun toys, it's just really a share you're not going to experience like half of them until you're at least 8 hours in. The bullets themselves aren't that diverse, but the powders provide a lot of stuff you can play with. If you're feeling like they're pretty basic, I'd say try playing with that. I hate poison though, Sorcerer Rounds for LIFE. The inventory system is a little clunky and storage is always needed, but personally? I never had to grind at all. All missions I did except for like one was one where I was progressing the story as it were and I just picked up enough stuff to keep me going. For difficulty, the word on the street is pretty true: it's a fairly easy game. It's important to note I'm already pretty experienced with Top-Down Shooters, but I never actually died in the entire run. I came close a few times in the final area and against the second to last boss, but I no-death'd the entire game on first playthrough. Exploration is neat. It's a balance of running around the area and completing objectives that'll give you loot, the gears you need, and time. There's chaos fights scattered about that'll give you extra time on the countdown clock, though to be fair the end of the world isn't THAT deadly. Hell, there's an achievement for lasting 5 minutes. Still, you'll want to do them for the chaos enemy exclusive loot and time. Could this game use an update? Weeeellll, I think so. The bullets are diverse but it would be nice to have more kinda. Lighting is just either AoE or single target damage. Physics bullets kinda just... Exist. There's a lot of descriptions missing from decorative items and most clothing. There's not TOO many upgrades for said clothing too, and to Level 2 versions of enchantments labeled Level 1. Some polish could be nice for now and I'd love a DLC that shows a bit more of the lore in context. Yeah there's journals and notebooks laid about, but c'mon. We're WIZARDS, I wanna see the old towers, I wanna traipse through an automaton factory, I want to have airship duels and small town justice and all that jazz. There's a lot of potential with the setting and I'd love for it to be expanded on from what we have. Conclusion and tl;dr:Is it good? I'd say so.Is it worth $25? Yeeeah, I'd say so, though I could understand if you decide it isn't. Is there gonna be more content in the future? Hopefully, I think it could turn the game from an 8/10 into a 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: First, I want to start this review by staying and emphasizing, I REALLY wanted to like this game. I finished the final boss and unlocked almost everything, just to make sure I didn’t miss anything cool. The concept sounded like this game would fit into my description of a perfect game. I LOVE wizard/magic games. Think ‘Wizard of Legends’ or ‘9 Parchments’, where the focus is on the cool use of spells and how you utilize them. That's what I think of when I imagine a wizard game crafted with passion. This is not that. I don't even want to call this a wizard game! As there are very few ‘spells’, this game just consists of elemental DMG. There is very little that separates the bullets/spells from each other, besides status effects. Don't get me wrong, there are a few, like the TP bullet or the powder that summons ground below it. But the research system in this game makes it so inconvenient to unlock. The bosses were a nice change of pace, but were lacking in their AI, that almost everything could be dodged by moving in a circle around them (as long as you weren't spamming bullets). This game could easily be saved by the developers if they had just a little more passion. Like making the bullets behave like actual spells (like a bullet that summons an ice storm, or bullets that summon electric posts that chain electricity to each other, or a bullet the creates a black hole effect where it bulls enemies in) it would also be nice if some bullets or a powder gave you the ability to detonates bullets sooner. Or maybe having a way to modify your dash (other than making it longer). For example, have a blink that has a longer CD. Or be able to replace the dash with an ice stasis ability. Maybe a dash that leaves a fire trail. Maybe replace a dash with invisibility.IDK, this game just lacks love, maybe the modding community can add variety to the bullets/spells that wizard games need. TLDR; Game needs actual spells. Imagine any wizard game, now replace all the spells with fireball, but with different status effects. That's this game in a nutshell.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was an option in recommendations for “meh” and not simply a thumbs up or down. The short answer is the game is a solid “Meh”, and you should wait for it to go on sale. Not worth the full price.The short short answer: This game will give you Forest Whitaker eye… The short reason why the “Meh” rating: The Dev’s believe a revolver uses a clip, but they made sure that most of the cosmetics had lady lumps. Simply put, they did not think this one through. You can see this is evident when you watch their “behind the scenes” video and they show you what the focus was on.  The controls are wonky, half of the “spells” are useless, they fail to give accurate descriptions of spells and powders, and you spend more time grinding low level areas versus seeing anything new. I get that farming is an element of this game, but when you spend hours on the same location because you need the mats just to progress your spells/powders, just to find out those powders and spells do not do what their description says it can do, and then you have to re-farm to go back to the other powders, it gets boring fast.For example, you will get powders that can “speed up a spell” or “slow down a spell”, but it does not tell you what it enhances. Does it mean it can speed up the actual bullet? Does it speed up the duration of the spell when it makes contact with the target? Does it compress the total amount of ticks to a DoT, so it lasts less or longer, but you get more or less of the actual ticks? You will have to sit there, waste mats on finding out what the actual hell the powder does to the spell, and then go grind low level stuff again, so you can have the mats to replace the useless powders that you spent grinding to get in the first place. They fail in how weapon stats work. If you use the same powder, does the stack? Does it double its effects? Well how come this one powder can stack, and this one can’t? How come it does not show two conflicting powders and their negative results? Can a fire bullet leave a water trail? You’ll waste mats to answer questions you should not have to ask…Even the inventory is a mess. They failed at simple inventory management, and you will be forced to drop a lot of stuff because of it. You can carry/stack 50 frog testicles, but you can only carry/stack 20 stones. How come I can only carry 5 health potions, but 50 shrooms? You will also have to use certain machines at the home base, just to separate materials because you can’t do it in your inventory. As for the gun play, it’s sloppy. Your bullets won’t go where you want them to do, because they end up clipping an object. You will be forced to use powders that aim for you…but…they hit the targets they want and not what you want. It’s all over the place. How come you can hold the trigger down with the revolver and it shoots automatically, but you have to pull the trigger each time with a rifle? Do they even know how guns work? The music is generic and does not play half the time. You forget the story because of the mindless grinding you have to do.There are basic functions in the game they don’t tell you about. They expect you to already know this.It’s simply not this fantastic experience you were hoping for. On sale, it would be worth it. The opening cinematic sets the expectations of this fast past, wizard western…but it’s really more like Minecraft on LSD…

_childDocuments_.review: Good game that brings together a lot of different concepts into an attractive package, but can feel a bit shallow at points. The gameplay loop is great fun and the bullet customisation is good as well, although as noted below some aspects not greatly balanced. The fire bullet for example just ends up damaging you more than the enemy. While they've included crafting in chests which is great, it has a proximity limitation which makes it awkward sharing resources among different crafting stations. Considering your base is an entirely separate area, why not just have limitless storage that all crafting stations can draw from? The limited storage and proximity just adds a chore to the game in my opinion. Possibly my biggest criticism though is that levelling through the crafting tiers is very linear. You beat a boss, get a new tier of guns and bullets and immediately get access to the resources needed for that tier. I prefer gradual progression where you might be able to get more advanced resources at higher risk or effort, rather than just in leaps after a boss fight. Otherwise the game looks great, the gameplay is pretty frenetic and fun, the customisation is enjoyable and the story ain't so bad either. All in all a good game.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid 3/5 game. For the price it isn't terrible but I'd wait for a sale if you're on the fence enough to read reviews. The tl;dr is that the game is fun but lacks depth.In general, progression is weak. The biomes themselves looks nice but the overall gameplay for each is mostly the same. Same enemy design, same objectives, same guns, etc. There's only 4 guns, each new tier of gun simply being a reskin of the previous tiers with a stat boost so small you'd be forgiven for not noticing.Most bullet/"spell" options are mediocre compared to running Fire and Lightning. Poison is workable but Lightning Strike is so absurdly powerful you are legit better off running that one bullet in every ammo slot across multiple games just to circumvent its cooldown. Experimenting with different synergies is fun, the game just doesn't give many opportunities for it to really matter other than for the fun of it.The story is okay. The end boss is a complete joke and leads me to believe that the game was released unfinished just to get it out. As in there really isn't a boss, it's just a random enemy masquerading as something important.Multiplayer is the most problematic feature, though. It's extremely laggy even at the best of times, even for the host, who seems to have their ping matched to the co-op partners which is absurd. It also has the same issue every other ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ half-baked survivalcraft game does in that you cannot interact with chests or crafting tables when someone else is, which is a joke of a system that even Minecraft had solved when it started popularising the concept.All in all it's not a particularly terrible game. It's engaging enough for the price, with great visuals and a banger soundtrack. The general aesthetic/vibe it has going is awesome, it really just needs some more polish.

_childDocuments_.review: Some thoughts after a few hours of playing:- The loop is simple and easy to grasp, but doesn't deliver in terms of the difficulty I'd normally like to see in a roguelike.- I haven't explored the multiplayer yet but want to soon. I sincerely hope Galvanic decides to open multiplayer up to more than 2 players in the future if possible.- The spell customization seems to be very in depth and able to cater to anyone who picks the game up. You will have to go out of your way to gather the items necessary for each bullet type you want to make though. Some crafting materials even need different elements to drop which I found to be pretty neat.- I feel like there should be some tweaking done with the bullet damages in some cases. It oftentimes feels like just picking the one with the bigger number is the winning strategy, and I would rather be rewarded for being creative with my spells.- The gun-play was lackluster, but salvageable. Adding more weapon types in the future or special abilities to the existing arsenal would breathe some life into the combat. - Character/enemy designs are just wonderful.I've been waiting for this game for quite some time now, and I can say that I've had a good time thus far. I'm hopeful that things will get even better in the future!
