_childDocuments_.review: THERE ARE SO MANY ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ POP UPS ON MY SCREEN WHEN SOMEONE GETS A NEW CLOTHING ITEM I CANT ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ SEE WHAT IM SHOOTING AT. THE UI IS ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ HUGE AND OBSTRUCTS VISION. ENEMIES SHOOT YOU OFF SCREEN. ADD A HIDE UI FEATURE THIS ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ SUCKSedit: my conclusion from playing the free weekend is that the game is weirdly punishing for what they encourage. they want you to make builds and they want you to combine different bullets, but the system is so punishing for exploring those possibilities. i found it incredibly frustrating to get excited about a bullet combination, add my powders, craft my bullets, test it out to find that it does half health on a level 1 enemy (using bullets upwards of level 15). the worst part about it is that you'll now be stuck with bullets and powders in guns that are not interchangeable- they become useless. i don't understand the thinking behind that design. the duration of effects depends merely on the gun type itself so switching bullets/powders from gun to gun and the cost being universal wouldn't break anything. creating a build gets really expensive so if it doesn't work then you lost all the materials and then you have to re-build into what you had before which is even more materials. (all the upgrades are one time crafts for that gun, in that slot, for that specific moment). additionally because of the unforgiving exploration of build crafting, i found it really not fun when my co-op partner had settled in on a build while i hadn't found something else that worked that they were not doing. cooldowns on debuffs are universal rather being individual for the player. this means that if my partner freezes the boss, it cannot be frozen again for a period of time for ANY player even if they didnt touch it. therefore, there is zero reason for me to use freeze bullets if someone else is using them. which is fine but it doesn't really make sense for how punishing the build crafting system is. this was my experience with one other person, i cant imagine how convoluted and confusing it would be for 4 players to coordinate builds and have them ALL work/be viable throughout the game with how the systems are.despite the janky crafting UI and punishing systems, i still had fun in some aspects that i think the devs did well. the gun vfx and sfx were satisfying and the bullet hell aspect on some bosses and against hordes of enemies was fun. it was exciting unlocking new areas, encountering new enemies, and trying to scan those enemies while evading their powerful attacks. the chaos mechanic once the timer hits 0 was often tense and blood pumping when the world is crumbling around you and there are a million pink creatures trying to eat you. the rush to escape with your loot was fun too.i know there are tons of unique builds in this game, theres no doubt there are. the variety of powders clearly shows how much CAN be done but the process of discovering those builds in a game entirely centered around it is fundamentally flawed. for a game that i got to play for free over 3 days, i think my playtime and progress doesn't nullify my review. i believe i gave it a fair shot but i wouldnt personally pay $25 for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Wizard With a Gun is an excellent game so far. The atmosphere and aesthetics of it are perfect and the game-play loop is unique (at least to me). The game isn't hard or complex, but I don't think that is an issue. Not every game needs to be highly intricate or exceedingly difficult. This game thrives and be a chill experience exploring a bizarre, rapidly self-destructing world. The only downsides right now is that it is a little low on the total content. Luckily it looks like the devs are actively working on adding more to the game. I see some people complaining that the game is "unfinished" but the core mechanics are all their and functional and the current content is well crafted and entertaining. If your on the fence about the game, wait for some content updates and/or a sale, but I find the $25 price tag to be perfectly acceptable for what the game has to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: A wizard with spells is cool, but a wizard with a gun that also uses spells might just be even cooler.Wizard with a Gun is a sandbox roguelike shooter where you turn back time to travel to randomly generated biomes to hunt down enemies, gather crafting materials, and find all sorts of neat loot. The core game loop here is very defined. Each time you turn back time, a new timer starts, counting down until chaos invades the world you just generated. So you need to get all your gathering and hunting done in that short time, lest you be overrun by powerful creatures all resembling some sort of pink blob. Or if you are feeling lucky, you can stay through that chaos and farm those pink blobs for material to make even better items back at base.It’s back at that base that you’ll find the bulk of the game’s crafting mechanics. There’s simple crafting you can do on the fly, but also research tables, tons of different ammunition types, armor upgrades, elemental upgrades, and a full slate of objects, walls, and flooring to build if you’re into the decoration side of things. This was one of my favorite parts of the experience, just going down these research trees and trying out new weapon combinations.Just casually exploring usually gave me more than enough material for general crafting, it was only when I wanted something super specific that I would have to generate an entire level for it. I feel like a lot of games reliant on crafting mechanics like this fall victim to slower pacing as a result, but that is not the feeling I had here. Wizard with a Gun is fast and satisfying without sacrificing complexity. Of course this wouldn’t work without good combat, another area the game does a great job in. Hits have feedback, there’s a good amount of variety with the weapon choices, and as mentioned previously, the sheer amount of customization possibilities make it very fun to play around with.The game could use some improvement in the area of its level design and random generation. It’s kinda basic and lacks the unique structures, enemies, and other random events that really sell a good roguelike. As such, the actual act of exploring isn’t quite as good as it could have been, even if I still had a good time with it.The bosses have only a few attacks, aren’t all that difficult, and really aren’t that satisfying to beat. The quest system felt like it was implemented just to give a general direction when it could have been so much more. The game has some lore, it just isn’t explored to the extent that I would have liked. It’s not outright bad, just kinda basic and disappointing in comparison to the rest of the experience.Graphically, the game looks great. It’s not anything groundbreaking, but I liked the stylized, darker aesthetic with its heavy use of shading and outlining. This, combined with the lighting, makes for a very cool overall look, one that’s even better in motion as the animations are just as good. The music is less notable, but still fitting for the overall style the game goes for.I had no issues playing at 4k 144fps on my 3080 Ti. There aren’t really any settings to change outside of resolution, but it’s not a difficult game to run by any means so that likely won’t pose an issue for most. Controls are also good. I spent my entire playtime using just keyboard and mouse and didn’t feel the need to change any bindings.Wizard with a Gun is fast and satisfying without sacrificing complexity, the ideal formula for an action roguelike. It offers up some clean combat, tons of different weapon and ammo possibilities, and a crafting system that doesn’t feel intrusive or tacked on in any way. It’s a fairly solid recommendation for fans of the genre, even if it does struggle with its levels and overall quest system. Still, I had fun with it and would recommend it.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: I found this game to be a lot of fun! Some quick notes to point out before i get into my main ones, minor spoilers (nothing about plot/lore just some minor content details) this is your warning! I had a complete solo play through so I don't know how it is with co-op and there are some bullets/spells that I haven't used and In my 17 hrs of playing the game I have all but one gear and about 1 enemy that i haven't scanned (not including decorations), and all my points are not me complaining about the game just some things that I noticed that being said I have a couple comments about the game. 1) I found it easy, not baby levels of easy but easy enough to where I didn't die once throughout my entire play through. (Side note: I'm almost positive i didn't die but if there is an achievement for it I did not receive one so i might just be remembering wrong) Even if I did die it wouldn't have been more than a couple of times. (If there isn't an achievement y'all should put one in! It be dope but you don't have too)2) The normal enemies (or at least the elite versions of them) were a lot harder than the bosses. The bosses were cool and I love the lore tied with them but it felt like I was scrambling around and trying harder when fighting the elites. I just wish there was more attack patterns to the bosses because it became predictable.3) There is no need for bullet diversity. I found the spells i liked and pretty much stuck with them throughout my play through with some minor deviance but with the way that the upgrading works I couldn't really test the builds I wanted to unless I wanted to spend time grinding for mats. That being said I haven't maxed out my bullets on my main weapons yet i beat the final boss with ease, and it felt like that order bullets were less effective then all the other bullets.4) Cold bullets are OP. Super OP. OMEGA OP. Their cold effect slows down enemies which in turn makes their dash abilities go practically no where. That with the increase to freeze times makes it to where if you are ever low on health or trapped in a corner, cold bullets paired with a freezing one is a get out of jail free card. It doesn't do the most dps but that's not really needed when you have enough ammo to spare between all the guns and if you at least get the basic upgrades to the spells/powders you'll be doing enough damage anyways.5) Bullet types have no particular advantage/disadvantage vs enemy types besides getting you different loot. I don't want to delve too much deeper for spoiler reasons but I thought it was funny that I was killing the fire spewing monsters with bullets that catch them on fire.These things being said i still had a ton of fun with the game and I would recommend it to anyone wanting a chill rouge like they can play. I cant wait for the future content and will be spending my time trying to 100% everything before then. Props to the developers to making a game that is this fun and unique :)

_childDocuments_.review: I'm very disappointed as I just finished the game (current patch 1.1.1), solo of course.Don't get me wrong, I bought it during sales, the game is decent and running as intended.Despite excellent cinematic, nice world buildup and in-game graphics, yet, the entire gameplay felt just like a demo with proofed concept + some filler + mediocre ending.The crafting management is the biggest upset for me, simply put, not respecting small efforts that player made, in this case, instead of properly handling the issue, the game simply discards bullets and/or powders in the most lazy way.To be clear on which issues:- when refill bullets, overflowing ammo will be discarded (unless is round number or zero)- when change bullet type, leftover ammo will be discarded (unless is zero)- when remove existing powder, the existing one will be discarded- when change powder, the existing one will be discardedNOTE: to be clearer, discarded means completely removed from the game.If the game is in demo, I can let it pass.If the game refunds resources with some rounding, I can let it pass.If the game has automation to generate resources, I can let it pass.Yet, none of above. Which eventually creates more snowballing problems:- Bullet slots cannot swap between left-click and right-click**- Powder slots cannot swap up or down**- The powder of same kind uses one on top slot, which obviously an error, should be by highest level instead.**- Certain powder only works on specific bullet type, but there's no indication or warning that it does not work.- No clear description that certain powders do not stack (There're absurdly way too many people asking this on the official discord)**this should be improved regardlessAlthough this does not stop me from progressing the game, but this stopped the game from being great.For crafting guns, the game have the potentials but no. Player ends up with only one playstyle, which is "Wizard with 4 Guns", you shoot, swap gun, repeat.The techtrees on powders are designed specifically to fit certain case, and there's it, no enjoyment of discovering whether this Powder has new synergy with another. In short, the combination is VERY LIMITED. Although I have to say, the game did a great job in balancing resources needed for the techtrees. in this game, player could effortlessly craft the highest damage weapon and go ahead without further wizardcrafting needed.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game and had it on my wishlist for ages. Unfortunately its a let-down in quite a few ways and several key elements disappoint. So despite a cool soundtrack and nice design I can't really recommend this game.My main issue are the boring combat mechanics: You can dash, shoot, and walk - thats it! No cool combos or crazy spells to mix things up, just the most basic and boring functions. The same goes for enemies, they all have pretty much the same movement and attack pattern and their differences seem to be mostly cosmetic. So together the core gameplay is pretty unimpressive without any learning curve and wont keep you engaged for more than a few hours. It honestly felt like playing a cheap browser game at times.The crafting system is kinda lackluster too. Theres little to do but to collect ingredients and use them for minor upgrades. I expected cool ways to craft my own gun or come up with unique spells but theres nothing of that sort. Instead theres just boring grind. Handling of ingredients and inventory management is downright horrible so I sometimes wonder why the crafting is even in there. (A skilltree would have done the same trick tbh)So yeah, while the idea is cool and parts of the design are pretty solid the game is just no fun and definitely not worth its current price. Meh.

_childDocuments_.review: -It’s hard to say where Wizard with a Gun’s strengths lie; the story is uninteresting, the storytelling is relegated to journal entries, the gunplay is unsatisfying (downright unpredictable with a controller) and the challenge is at the behest of an erratic difficulty curve. The art style is at least pleasant, seemingly in line with other Galvanic Games releases, but this doesn’t really offset the myriad disappointments.On the surface, WwaG appears to be a highly customisable experience. A wide variety of weapons, bullets and “powders” are available; the latter allowing the player to modify projectiles like increasing Area of Effect or adding Homing behaviours to a bullet. Every item of clothing can be changed and “enchanted” for more health or better resistance. Hell, even the entire Hub World is almost totally rebuildable with a plethora of floors, walls and furniture to scan and unlock over the course of the game. It sounds like a game in which experimentation and unique approaches are rewarded……however, WwaG quickly devolves into a clusterf--k of shallow mechanisms spread across far too much ground. Weapons themselves are not customisable which results in them either becoming irrelevant very quickly or staying in your arsenal forever as new discoveries either immediately supersede them or fail to inspire.The variety of bullet options on display gives the impression of emergent gameplay options and interconnected behaviours. In practice the cost of the linked elements (losing a bullet slot) does not justify their use, instead encouraging the player to stick with maximum damage/destruction routes. Once the player has progressed part-way down an upgrade path there is very little incentive to deviate or experiment with new strategies.On the topic of upgrade paths: the way the game presents upgrades and gear customisation seriously needs a QoL pass. There are too many crafting stations for too few options. Resources are stored in chests that can be accessed by nearby stations (good). However the chests have to be very close to said stations (bad) and often multiple stations require the same resource, making it impossible to create a crafting area that isn’t extremely awkward to use without requiring the player to run around cherry picking resources for every upgrade (ugly). This could all have been solved with one universal storage point accessible from anywhere in the Hub.Ultimately, Wizard with a Gun felt like an exercise in time-burning. Very little new ground covered despite the novelty suggested at the outset. Maybe it’s better with friends but I don’t have any of those. I'd have given it a "neutral" rating if one was available.

_childDocuments_.review: This game clearly suffered from feature creep.I've had this game on my wishlist for about two years, because its artstyle and the promise of coop was appealing. But sadly, this game was created without focus.It could have doubled down on the combat, the crafting, the progression or the world, but it did not decide and did a littlebit of everything, making none of these choices suffice for a game.My personal fix for this game would have been the following: Make the home base completely static like in Bastion or Hades, visually pleasing and filled to the brim with the various progression systems. Then focus the rest of the work on the gunplay, the game is called "Wizard with a Gun" after all and sadly, you do not feel like a teleporting, gun-slinging maveric in the game.Then it could have been a great 8 hour experience. Now it's been a 16 hour grindy and janky slog.

_childDocuments_.review: A really cool idea, with really cool artwork, with an inventory management system that makes me wanna put my fist through the monitor. This game needs a small amount of quality of life changes that would make this wonderful idea work. Cannot recommend it as it is, however. I love ya, Devolver, but this wasn't it.Also. Do not expect this to be a dark souls-esque where you're dodging/hitting with a lot on the line. It feels more like a Bethesda take on difficulty, where enemies being more difficult means they hit hard every once in a while (and then you just retreat and heal), and you gotta hit them for 20 minutes. I'd love to see more difficult attack patterns and variations to spice things up.

_childDocuments_.review: Not worth the price tag.I played the original demo and was super excited for this game's release. So excited, in fact, that I avoided grinding out the demo because I wanted to enjoy the full game as much as possible.The ideas and concepts are great, but the game itself just becomes an uninteresting cycle of resource gathering, base organization, and spamming LMB at enemies. I really hate to hate this game. Both enemy and environment objects scale up (health/armor) as you progress, leaving little joy in actually being stronger. Realistically, you will only ever be as strong as your strongest enemy, no matter how much you try to grind Resources are locked behind progression, halting players who would rather just have fun with the elements and spell combinations Many bullet effects require you to hit an enemy  before the enemies actually become afflicted. This is immensely unnecessary and results in a waste of time, effort, and ammo. The thresholds should be lowered,  Multiplayer (2-player co-op) is very laggy. Devs originally planned 4-player but the lag literally made it unplayable. Rather than solving it, they just reduced the max players(They suck the fun out, they suck the time out, they suck the appeal out.)

_childDocuments_.review: Really hate not quite being able to recommend this. The game has great artistic direction, but at the end of the day it just isn't very fun.The combat is rather simple and requires minimal skill. It comes down to whether your bullet stats are higher than the enemy armor value. And you fix that problem by grinding materials. Sometimes you just need to shoot down a forest - one tree at a time.Another frustrating mechanic is all the inventory micro-management you do in your home base. Looking through a dozen chests to see if you had any pink tendrils for a crafting recipe just isn't very fun. Spending hours decorating your base with cosmetic items can be fun for some people, but is entirely optional. Spending hours moving crap between chests is not an activity many people find enjoyable, but here we are.Finally, while the game is mostly easy, there are situations in which you might get wiped out. And that means you can lose everything you spent the last 20 minutes acquiring, plus have to re-equip. And let's hope you didn't forget to deposit the game's equivalent of currency before going on a run, because ouch. On the one hand, yeah, kinda fair. But then it's also deeply disappointing for no good reason. If you play with friends, they can pick up your loot for you. On your own though, no fun at all.

_childDocuments_.review: The game feels very much like Don't Starve and Don't Starve Together with the inclusion of its multiplayer. I did not play with others but the single-player experience felt smooth and a little challenging at times. Progression is very easy and revolves around either taking small upgrades to your bullets or adding new combinations with supporting bullets such as oil and fire bullets. A little bit of grinding may be needed to fight some of the tougher enemies, along with stockpiling resources such as healing items and crafting materials. Your home base feels barren at first but as you unlock different progression items such as buildings and portals that take you deeper into the game's biomes, feels more like a quick stop to upgrade before you go in. The 5 minute timer before the world ends and the game ramps up in difficulty felt somewhat oppressive until you find rifts that after defeating 3 waves of enemies allows you to add time to the clock, continuing your run. I was never truly challenged apart from a world boss in the final biome and the final boss who can be more annoying than anything due to it taking away chunks of land that you need to rebuild. Bosses felt very easy even when fighting them 5 or so levels under their own. The soundtrack is amazing and fits the Western cowboy vibe very well. Overall I would say this is a great game if you like the art style and open world nature of Don't Starve while toning down the difficulty for most of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Simultaneously an underwhelming and overwhelming experience with little interesting gameplay. Cult of the lamb-style expeditions that go out into procedurally generated "dungeons" where you get all your resources for your home base. The game throws every system at you rather quickly, leaving you with a bunch of research/upgrade/crafting stations and no idea what to actually do with them or what you need them for necessarily.Instead of some sort of research tree where you unlock new crafting stations as you gain experience or whatever, you have to painstakingly slowly use an item to scan objects in the dungeons that you can then craft and place down in your hub.All world lore is provided to you via unreasonably long walls of text, it does not really inspire the player to spend time reading things- especially when you just want to first get to experience and get immersed in the gameplay and the book keeps whining at you to read its entries by obnoxiously highlighting the item in your hotbar.Probably better in multiplayer mode where you can at least keep yourself entertained with a friend.

_childDocuments_.review: The game feels like early access still. They have many cool systems in the game and a wide variation of spells.Shooting and Bullets feel very good and there is a huge variation in what all you can use, however I've never found a reason to use more than lightning and cold with the rifle. While the upgrade system gives you something to progress toward you, any progress you do make feels cheap. Getting to the next level of bullet is 5x better than farming a long time for a +1 to the current bullet. Looking for arcana has no point when you can get it from getting rid of rocks. There is no pressure from the time gauge and seems to only serve a purpose to stop action rather than keep it going. If you're going to fight a boss you'll make it there before the timer expires and the boss doesn't have a timer of its own. Movement without a potion feels grueling, I found myself farming placeable tiles just to get around the map more quickly.Base building feels like a gimmick in the game and i would really have rather had a static base with the upgrade altars and production buildings already placed so i didn't feel like i was missing something. This game has a lot of good qualities but misses the mark on everything it's attempting.

_childDocuments_.review: A phenomenal game that combines crafting and base building with a mild extraction shooter-lite.I love the idea of the extraction shooter but hate online / multiplayer games. I just don't have the desire to play to be better than other people who have endless amount of time. I would rather play against the computer in an experience that has been balanced by game devs.The loop is you have 5 minutes to go into a zone to gather resources before it collapses (which means the zone gets pretty lethal the longer you stay past that time). Back at base you use those resources to craft and build better gear which in turn means you can stay in the zone longer and take on bigger enemies and in turn get better and more resources.Ontop of this you have a fantastically wide array of weapon combinations you can craft with various degrees of elemental damage.Its the sort of game you can play for quick ten minute bursts or multi hour sessions. I love the balance between base building and crafting and then the combat and the tension of risk v reward.This is a great game whith a huge amount of content and depth. So many wonderful little things to discover..... like how i noticed last night a certain creature in the zone will heal trees if they are damaged..... and if you stand in their healing zone it also heals you. Just loads of little details in the game like this that make it feel so alive and fun to play.Runs perfectly on the Steam Deck as well. This is a game i can see myself losing hours and hours to.

_childDocuments_.review: My friend and I had a bead on this game for a hot minute and snagged it at release. While the idea and the style are interesting the actual game-play and core loop are not. The combat is unengaging and the base building is tedious while the research system is needlessly complex while also being largely pointless.Combat - shoot and dodge. You'll unlock different bullet types, weapons, and powders over time but there are no skills or actual magic or anything. Maybe that stuff is another 6 research tables deep after researching another 12 random things.Base building - its 2023 let me pull from chests ANYWHERE. Why does the chest have to be literally touching the crafting table? Better yet do away with chests and allow a global base inventory that is limitless and accessible via the menu with auto-sort and a filter system. The chests and inventory management are seemingly designed to slow the game down. Just do away with it entirely.Research - hope you like researching things to craft other tables to research other things to research more. Except there's very little reason to research anything. You're better off hard focusing a single magic/element like poison and just spending all your resources in that tree to maximize combat ability. In addition, why are there multiple tiers to bullets that are completely separate from each other? Poison Bullet 1 with 6 tiers that upgrade damage but then wait you have Poison Bullet 2 with 6 more tiers that just upgrade damage and yet you also have Poison Bullet 3 that has 6 more tiers that let you upgrade damage. Then you have to craft these bullets separate from each other. So now you're carrying tier 1 bullets in slot 1 and tier 2 bullets in slot 2. Pointless system. If you want a more in depth overview read revvy_'s review on here.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a mixed bag. It is chaotic shooter where you collect gears and craft equipment. You have 5 minutes to finish world, otherwise it starts throwing a lot of strong enemies on top of you, literally. Game does not stop when looking at map or inventory or even dialogues, so I have to prepare everything before entering world or build everything in my tower before I die and lose all inventory which I found no way of retrieving. The game also relies on you to do multiple runs because it is a time loop anyway and I feel like I achieved absolutely nothing after playing over an hour. You can also farm resources by beating objects. The controls themselves are pretty good, the world map shows you unexplored areas. I feel like this is not the game for me.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; guns and bullets needs to be CRAZIER and FLASHY, also make it HARDER with lots of enemies.Just to be clear, this is being posted as a negative review but i did enjoy A LOT many points that i experienced in this game and if i'm being honest i'm being unfair for not recommending this game >FOR NOW<. This game can be SO MUCH BETTER and i'm not saying this in a disappointed manner but rather in a hopeful and eager way!!! IT'S BURSTING WITH POTENTIAL!!! The foundation for a GREAT game is already there! i will not deepen into details about the positive points because that would make this review SO MUCH LONGER than it already is, but i have MANY good impressions on: 1- The visuals and theme in general are gorgeous 2- The base building aspect in the tower is very fun, pretty and very good to stir your creativity 3- although few, the enemies are very stylish (please we need more!!) 4- the music is ABSURDLY good!!! 5- many more points that i can't think on the top of my head but i do have a very positive outlook on the game! BUT... The guns and bullets is supposed to be the main selling point of the game but ironically the combat progression and guns are unfortunately uninteresting and repetitive... i could definitely feel the effort the devs put to make some creative gimmicks for some bullets like having bullets that interact with poison stacks and these were pretty clever, but it pains me to say that 80%~90% of them are not that interesting... for example; Lightning Bullets just simply arc between targets when you hit something and have bigger aoe when in contact with water... and that's it... yes this is to be expected of lightning effects but my point is, i feel like this is such an obvious design choice when it could've had so much more interactions and quirkiness involved in the mix... while playing i wondered "What if Lightning Bullets had interactions with crits since you get crit oriented powder effects from the lightning bullets crafting station" but unfortunately most of the other bullets stick to this same basic and tame design choices, we need bullets to be unique from each other! what i want is crazier guns builds similar to Noita's wands crafting!!! And about the guns... please allow us to tinker them in crazy ways to our likeness and not just the bullets! I want to tinker with my rifle rate of fire and turn it into a machine gun that fires automatic and faster than an smg, but have like only 6 bullets and it takes a good while to reload, you know what i'm saying? I'm probably imagining or projecting my feelings on this one but... it felt like an intentional choice from the developers making the guns and bullets so... tame might be the word...? some big aoe effects sure happens in certain ways, but nothing TOO crazy will happen because the game don't have the resources and mechanics to make it happen, and i feel like this a waste and somehow contradicts with what the game was supposed to be (at least in my mind that is...) . Besides Noita i can even think about Path of Exile as a good game to draw inspiration from when thinking about crazy abilities interactions. Make us a bullet that summons a clone of ourselves that uses one of our weapons, make us an powder that pierce enemies and ricochet between them, a gun that shoot two bullets the right and left one at the same time... i want combat to be DYNAMIC! fast paced even! lots of enemies in screen so i can shoot crazy and unpredictable bullets leaving trails everywhere and bursting them with other bullets effects and having a chain reaction!! a game can never go wrong with crazy interactions and combos, The Binding of Isaac and Noita is there to prove my point!ALSO!! please, enemies variety and more challenging and interesting boss fights or mini bosses that forces the player to think it through and have a more methodical approach, i wanna have my skills tested! if i'm having crazy overloaded guns, the bosses should impose a challenge for them!

Fry until golden, then add the beans. Pour in the cider vinegar, honey and spices along with 1 tsp or more of salt, to taste. Cook until warmed through, crushing gently with the back of your wooden spoon, then set aside.STEP 2The best way to make the guacamole is with a large stone pestle and mortar, but you can use a medium bowl and a flat-ended rolling pin instead. Crush the garlic, coriander and chilli into a rough paste. Scoop in the avocado with a little salt and crush roughly – you want it chunky, not smooth. Squeeze in the lime juice and set aside.STEP 3Mix the salsa ingredients in a small bowl. Heat a griddle pan or steamer and quickly griddle the tortillas or steam a stack of them to warm up. _childDocuments_.review: I was definitely inclined to check out this game after watching its road to completion since the original trailer for the Nintendo switch. I mean seriously, a game about wizards with magic guns?! heck yeah! But once I actually got the game my joy in it began to drain away. Let me just acknowledge a few things before continuing, the games art style is amazing! Just simply gorgeous. The game play is very fun and while repetitive, keeps the player coming back for more. The story, while complicated is for the most part well built and interesting. However, while exploring the world and story I kept finding time and time again very strangely political things finding their way into the story. For instance, i understand having false gods within a story, but some of the descriptions and character traits these "gods" have seem incredibly forced. Another thing that makes me uncomfortable is that there is a lot of tension between important characters and their families. I'd understand one or two characters having parent problems but almost the whole cast of characters has something negative in their story about their family. These originally, made me question whether I was going to continue playing or not, but what pushed me to uninstalling the game, was the company behind it. Now I understand many people like this game, and it IS well made, but when I found the same people who made this, made Cult of the Lamb, I was disappointed. Most people who read this will most likely like Cult of the Lamb, however, as a professed Christian that game holds many red flags for me. Now I don't care whether whoever is reading this gets the game or not, my decision for not playing this any more is because I didn't know what I was getting into. If you want it, by all means get it. This review is to warn people like me who don't understand what they are getting in to not to throw dirt at the game. As for the production team, you made a good game for the most part. But I will not support a company that makes a game like Cult of the Lamb.

_childDocuments_.review: My boyfriend and I beat Wizard with a Gun (both endings) and even though our taste in games can vary wildly, this one hit the mark for both of us. There was the farming, crafting, adventure and story line for me and then there was the min/maxing, fighting and strategy piece for him. Despite my absolute disdain for time-pressure games, I wasn't really sweating it at all for this one. You go out, you complete a run, you come back to sort through your spoils, unlock some trees, craft more bullets and out you go again.I like this type of art style and I didn't take the usual route of turning down or completely muting the music because it was all done so well.  It's not the longest game out there (much to my chagrin) and it doesn't seem to have a lot of replay value but it feels like a complete game and is fun to play with a friend or two. Due to the shorter play time, I'd say wait for a sale to buy.

_childDocuments_.review: Wizard with a Gun is a roguelite-esque collectathon where the main goal is to defeat the chaos and restore time.Whilst most achievements are fine, some really stick out to annoy you (bounties and difficulty).The 100 bounties will have you hunting down the same 5 enemies to kill and get a worse weapon than you already have.Where as the difficulty feels completely artificial, making the boss fights very lengthy and sometimes even unfair.-Great music and artstyle-Good variety of guns and "spells" to choose from-Complete ability to build and destroy your base-Half the spells are obsolete-Bounties are rng based-Making healing potions is a slogI personally adore this game and what it tried to do. Emphasis on .This game has really good core mechanics, and could've been a masterpiece were it handled better. The release was underwhelming and the lack of early access really put the expectations too high for what was not a finished product. Considering that, this game still has a lot of rough edges (for ex. ice bullets outclassing everything else for 98% of the game). There's also an inherent lack of post game importance as you'll just get a credits roll and a pat on the back.It's saddening that Galvanic Games didn't get to develop this game further, but I cannot blame Devolver for their decision as this was clearly just not handled correctly.And whilst the game is definitely not the best on the market; I still encourage you to try it out, as there's an enjoyable experience at the core if you brush off the mud.Closed development; pretty rough. But if you're into this genre you'll like it.

_childDocuments_.review: So close to great, but the connection issues are mad like I'm playing CO-OP in the same house as my Co-op partner both on Ethernet and the game will still randomly boot on of us every run or two losing us quite a lot of progress. Then when you try to rejoin it'll put you in an infinite loading screen and the only "fix" is both players restarting the game.Adding onto this later. While I like the game, in fact I WANT to love this game as it's premise, aesthetic and artstyle are to die for and whilst it's clear a lot of passion and skill has went into it this game, this game feels too over balanced to the point that it doesn't make sense to play around with the bullet and powder combinations because the most of the ideas you're likely come up with to make something neat/interesting has likely already been neutered by the devs in some fashion. It's clear the devs want to to play a certain way, they want you to use the mechanics (the powders, bullets and guns and how these things can be combined) a certain way and have restricted them accordingly, which is a shame. You might as well just stick to the baseline bullets and basic elemental bullets and not waste resources trying anything outside of that.Tl;dr: Sometimes you can balance the fun out of a game, sometimes you should let go of the fear of your players breaking your game and I think if I wasn't playing co-op I would be a lot more disappointed in it than I already am.I do however wish the devs the best, the news of the studio closing down is heartbreaking and I think with a bit more time and love this game could have been one of my favourites.

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't one hundred percent sure what this game was like when I went in, but I was pleasantly surprised. I was hoping that its visual similarity to Don't Starve was only skin deep since I'm not that fond of survival games, and instead I found a fast-paced and engaging roguelike that makes the most out what it has to offer. Pushing through the different biomes, upgrading my bullets all the time, was a satisfying gameplay loop that didn't wear out its welcome too quickly. It doesn't put much of a focus on narrative or characterization, but the artstyle and designs are good so it's still an enjoyable world to run around in.There are only a couple things that weren't so good. Especially once you get to higher levels, there can be a ton of visual pollution, leading to such chaos that it's hard to manage and easy to lose track of where you're aiming. Getting stuck on plants and such while trying to move around is never fun. I hit something of a slog toward the endgame when the hardest bounties start showing up, some of which take so little damage or heal themselves so quickly that even max-level bullets and powders on good guns barely tickle them. The enchanting system provides only very incremental character upgrades (40 health regen every few seconds when you have 2000 health and enemies hit for over half of that isn't much), so the only actual surviveability  comes from health potions, leading to a time-wasting grind.Still, I managed to finish strong, and Wizard With a Gun was a good time. A quintessential indie experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game, exploration system is very well thought out, base building is not so important that you spend too much time on making everything look nice, combat was excellent and really made me think about my resources, bosses were very well designed and at times challenging and difficulty scaling was very good. Only problems were: some spells were very overpowered and could one-shot most minibosses even later on, meaning that when I decided to use lightning bullets there was no reason for me to put resources into the other skill trees. Also the story was good for the most part, but it was difficult to care about any of the characters, which made the final twist less interesting

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game on the free weekend on Outlaw difficulty and managed to finish the entire story and get nearly 100% of achievements.  I did not buy the game at the end of the weekend but I plan to in the future.  I do think the game is absolutely worth purchasing on sale and is a blast with friends.  I wouldn't recommend playing on outlaw in the games current state, as it can start to feel very grindy to get materials.Although the Negatives section is larger than the positives, it is just because of the way i described my issues and not because there are more negative things to say than positive.The game has a wide variety of bullets that makes thinking up new combos really satisfying.  Their affects work differently depending on the gun you use which also encourages players to use many weapon types.  All of the normal bullet types feel balanced and have different combos to discover which makes the player feel that they have a lot of freedom (there are still options that are stronger which i will discuss below)I like that there isn't a player level, that way you aren't just invincible when returning to older areas (although you will slaughter them with leveled up bullets).Bounties are an absolute blast, you basically have to hunt down an enemy that is buffed up with some wacky effect like maybe shooting fireballs out or having a healing aura for other enemies.  I think its a really cool system that can be expanded in the future.  They can  add new guns into the pool if they want or new types of effects on the bounty enemies.  I don't know if I just didn't have time to find more but the only gold bounties I could find were the 4 required for some end game stuff (no spoilers), but if gold bounties could become a regular addition and the player could choose a weapon to be rewarded that would be great.The boss fights in the game are also very fun.  Granted, a couple of them are pretty simple in execution, but they are still a blast to fight.  They also have unique weapon drops and are able to be fought again if desired.  I do think they should make following boss weapon drops have their powder slots increased with the world, that way there is incentive to fight them again to get their weapons with more slots.  They can also increase their levels with the world like they do with bounty enemies.I think they tried a lot of really cool things with this game and I think its worth a try with a partner or as a team of 4 (I cant even imagine how hectic and fun that would be).  The game loop is super fun and rewarding and I hope they find a way to add in more content into the future.  With the way the game is structured it seems like it would be difficult to seamlessly update the game.  I think if anything, rather than adding new bullet types, they should work on adding more elemental interactions with the bullets we already have.  I think adding more player freedom to create unique builds and combos is what we need. (This section is longer due to my description and not because of an abundance of issues)While there are many different bullet types, there are a few bullets that are much easier to use early and stronger then others.  I don't think this is a deal breaker as certain bullets that are really strong without powder () can be overshadowed later in the game by building into the other basic bullets correctly, but it is unfortunate that bullets like  are strong on their own but then lack as many build options later in the game. It does encourage players to change off of that bullet later on, but I think that there's a risk that players will spec entirely into this bullet type and never even try the others to see the late game potential.There are, however, a few utility bullet types that are just objectively stronger.  I'm going to name the bullets by type in the text ahead as well as the combinations that are strongest with it, so if you want to discover the combos on your own don't read ahead.   This brings me to an issue that my partner had when we played that I think is very valid criticism.  It was enough to make them quit the game early (at the start of the final area).  I have only played the game on the highest difficulty, so it may not be as pronounced for the average player, but while the game seems to want players to try out bullet combinations and make unique builds, the way crafting bullets and powders works is fundamentally against it.  Both powders and bullets need to be crafted for each gun themselves, so if you have a sub-machine gun full of an ammo you like with powders you like, you can't move them into other weapons.  I don't personally think it is as much of an issue with bullets, but with powders it is  inconvenient.  The cost of some powders can really quickly add up, and if you want to change to different powders in the future, you have to craft it onto the weapon and destroy any powders in the slots you craft into.  It is a huge disincentive to try out new combos after you have ones you enjoy.  For me, I didn't touch force bullets until the very end of the game, and after finding powders that sounded interesting with them, I wasn't able to build my weapons towards it because I would have been force to destroy all of my powders to make them as powerful as my current builds.  With bullets it kind of makes sense because different weapons carry different amounts of bullets, but with powders, it is a a very strange decision.  Powders cost the same no matter the weapon they are put on and their strength is scaled by the weapon itself.  I think the devs should allow powders to be taken off of weapons and swapped as needed.  It is such a nuisance to be forced to avoid new areas in order to farm the necessary materials to make the powders you like.  This problem is also most pronounced .  This means that if you get better weapons while excitedly exploring the new area you have to go back to some previous biome in order to farm the necessary materials to craft the powders you want into all the empty slots on the new weapons.  It is a massive nuisance.  If the developers were trying to avoid players keeping powders forever, allow us to swap between weapons but make them have durability or a cap on the number of swap or SOMETHING.  It was enough to ruin the game for my partner and I don't blame them.  I was able to look past it and enjoy the rest of the game but it was a huge annoyance throughout the entire play through.  If this gets changed in the future my main issue with the game will be gone.My final critique would be with the chaos enemies and arcana.  Arcana is a material needed throughout the game to do everything from research new upgrades to crafting powders, but it is a massive pain to get.  Chaos enemies give a handful of arcana when they die so farming early game is a needlessly pointless grind.  I wasn't a hoarder either, I was recycling old weapons into arcana all the time, so the fact that there was still an issue was very annoying.  The later chaos crafting materials do recycle into a decent bit of arcana so there are some alright options later, but I think the amount the enemies drop really needs to be pumped up to avoid making the game grindy.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this on a free weekend so I spent roughly 18 hours playing this game for 3 days straight. What became imminently apparent was inventory management. The major problem in the mid to late game was the excessive number of items and early game chest size. The good thing is that the chest next to a crafting station takes the items out of the chest if you need to craft something. However, the bad news is that it can and will block your path 80 percent of the time. It can easily be fixed by making chests global and instead only accessible if a crafting station is nearby. The gameplay is perfectly acceptable, there are no major complaints about the combat. The only thing about it is that some things feel overpowered and underpowered. However, you can make pretty rewarding combinations that reward reaction time and skill. It also gives you some space to experiment with your setup as well. Which is definitely a major selling point of this game.  The optimization of this game could be much better. I have a GTX 3GB 1060, 64 GB of ram, and an AMD Ryzen 5 1400. In the late game where the map is fully unlocked, the game gets significantly slower and experiences frame drops frequently. It is not unplayable by any means, but it is something to be aware of. That and I noticed that load times were longer than early game.With all these factors considered I think that anyone buying this game should wait for a sale of 65 percent or more. 12.49 for me is pushing it as there are other games for a better price. Overall not a terrible game by any means but it has significant flaws that cannot be overlooked. 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: Wizard with a gun is an action adventure game.The game play is fun; from shooting down creatures and chaos eldritch monsters, to building a base of operations to get stronger and progress further. The art style is also something i find very charming, same could be said about its character customization options. Also the music in here is very nice and i do enjoy the tracks that play when entering the specific biomes of this game.The story in here is very enjoyable, a lot of its story elements are scatter around the world you play in, but as you slowly progress through the game however, you start to see what's really going on in this chaotic land. Also to note, the game had an update and the story is finished now, and yes, the extra few hours put into it was well worth it for the finale. I won't spoil though for those who want to see it for themselves.  The weapons in this game are plentiful and unique. However, the real powerhouse to all your weapons are your spells, which a lot of them have a lot of special properties. Some can burn, poison, charm, freeze, or even send your opponent flying at a wall. Leaving you with a lot of interesting combinations. The enemies and bosses can be summed up as one of two things; the easiest thing you have ever fought in your life, or you just died because you thought you could take on the lvl 15 enemies at lvl 8. But it's not all that bad though, the game does a great job of telling you when the enemy is too tough to handle. Plus you gradually work to higher levels of enemies as you play through the story, so you can fight the harder ones at your own pace.Conclusion, the game is a lot of fun. Whether it be solo or in 4 player co-op, I'd recommend this one to anyone who wants to give this game  a try.

_childDocuments_.review: I had fairly high expectations for this game seeing the cinematic and launch trailers, I followed the development and production, so I'd say my hype was high, and Wizard with a Gun didn't quite meet that hype. It is a great game, don't get me wrong, but overall this would be an 12/10 demo, and makes for a 6-7/10 game (Not bad!)For starters, I like the Don't Starve vibes, and of course the style of the game as well as the music and even the lore I'd say is pretty neat. The guns are fun, mix and matching ammo type and spells attributed to them is albeit nothing super out there but fun nonetheless, just complicated enough to give a plethora of options that feel cool and customizable without being overwhelming. The enemies are neat, the decorations are fun, the concept is all here. I've been playing it a ton these past few days trying to collect resources, overpreparing for bosses, decorating my tower, it's been a good time, however..As others have mentioned here the storage management in this game is kind of bad, you fill up quick with resources, you don't feel you can drop a lot, and you have to abandoned most runs with a full backpack. The chests are roughly the same size as the backpack so you need a ton of chests, which quickly clutters your tower. This game overall is missing some quality of life features, even small ones like having to hit the X button on all menu screens and not just hit the interact again (imo). The progression of bullets and spells isn't my favorite, having menus clutter with obsolete versions instead of trying to guide you through progression, outside of the main gun types all the gimmick guns you get from bounties seem like the drawbacks are just not worth using them, unlocking new rooms in your tower quickly becomes kind of boring as they don't unlock any new features, just different entries to the world, and the world itself I feel just doesn't have enough in it. I'd love more buildings to explore and NPCs to talk to. I honestly wish there were more just plain ole magic to go with your magic gun, just small things to make them seem more magical and less augmented weapons. Overall, it is telling that one of my major criticisms is that I just want more of this game. There isn't enough here, and again this would be a fantastic demo or early access game, but it's been a hot minute since it's release. With its lack of content comes a cascade of issues, like runs feeling samey or dull after a while. This could be a fantastic game, but for now it's just alright, it's good, and its worth the discounted price. I hope the devs continue to work on and update this game, because I still have the highest hopes for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good but left me feeling disappointed. It feels like 80-90% of being a masterpiece of a game, but I think you should wait until it's updated to being finished before buying it.(no spoilers)The game is solid. I like the art. The music is okay but sometimes feels a little repetitive. The game is fun, with minimal bugs (in my experience) and a solid gameplay loop. The lore is very interesting, but can be hard to follow in journal entries.It has a solid base for everything I wanted out of this game. But after completing the game, it didn't feel satisfying. By the end, I was having much less fun than I did at the start.As I played, I felt more and more limited as I understood the mechanics better. Your loadout has  finite amount of combinations, and although you can carry many guns, they largely share the same functions. (some of this has been addressed, which I'll talk about in a minute.)The guns aren't nearly as creative as one might imagine when you hear "magical spell guns." They can be modified by selecting different bullets and modifiers, but many that you might instantly consider (ie reload faster) don't exist. (There is a single clothing upgrade that can fill that function, however.)The modifiers and bullets that do exist have limited synergy, and can conflict with each other. Most don't stack, so if you equip more than one similar spell, one will overwrite all the others. (it wont even prioritize the strongest one.) Out of the 7 or 8 spell types, maybe half of them actually interact with each other in interesting ways. For how limited your choices are, there's still a lot of missed potential in what we have. Most of the elements amount to either damage over time, stun-locking, slowing, or area of effect. Nothing really feels magical, and the small selection we have isn't fleshed out completely to all work well together.My biggest complaint is that many of these aren't fully explained anywhere in the game. Many limitations have to be discovered by you, after you've already spent the resources to add them to your gun, and you aren't refuned the materials you used to find it out. Trying to make a gun with multiple area of effect upgrades or multiple trail effects will quickly disappoint you. And the cost does add up if you invested immediately with the assumption things stacked. It would be better if the game just prevented you from equipping conflicting spells, but it would be more fun if they actually either stacked or worked together in a balanced way. (ie lighting strike bullet with 4x area of effect now has 16x the cooldown. Multiple trails only conflict if they're opposing elements, ie fire and ice, or they combine to make a hidden dry ice effect, encouraging experimenting instead of punishing it with wasted time and resources.)One positive (and negative) is that the recent update added dozens of guns and a few minibosses to the game. Some of these are more interesting and unique, but they're hidden behind completing a mission to get a random one as a reward. The mission is just to find a specific strong enemy and kill them. While a nice minigame, the random nature means you have to farm these to potentially find the new guns, or even just a specific one. I completed a decent amount but probably only got 10 different guns, out of apparently over 50.Minibosses were added too, but I never saw them. I dont know what conditions I need to meet to fight them, but nothing was obvious about how to find them ingame.But this concerns me that the game might've launched too early, and they need to update it a few times to be what the devs actually envisioned.There's a few things which make appearances in the game which aren't implemented yet. On the store page of the game, one of the GIFs features an enemy which isnt in the final game, and I believe that there are enemies in the in-game list which also aren't added yet. I haven't seen them after searching and playing for 25 hours, but it's possible they're somehow hidden like the minibosses.My other case for this theory is the ending. The final boss fight is underwhealming, being just a slightly stronger version of a boss you fight numerous times throughout the game. The boss just has a lot of health now, and stronger attacks. There was never really a moment where I felt like I was in danger while fighting it, in comparison to some of the other bosses.After beating it, you are unironically awarded with a black screen with some text that almost exactly says "You did it! Congratulations!" The credits roll in near silence for 10 seconds before the music began (I think it wasthe main menu mudic, which is pretty solemn). There is no big finale, no flashy cutscene like the start of the game, and no (immediately obvious) post game besides grinding bounty missions. It felt like whiplash how quickly it was just done.The game is good on sale right now, but I'd preferred to have paid more and gotten the game in it's final form in a little while. Hopefully they don't need to make it paid DLC or the definitive edition.6/19/24 update: shocked and disappointed the studio behind the game is closing its doors. The game is on the verge of being excellent, and had a lot going for it. Although I was critical in my review, I can tell that the game had a lot of love and care put into it, and I still enjoyed my time with it despite my criticisms. Very disappointing ending to a promising upcoming game and studio, but I guess we truly are living in the worst timeline.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun survival game with 5-10 minute-ish runs. You can go at a fairly casual pace if you choose, though there is enough challenge that you can still get killed if you're being lax. The different weapons to research is pretty fun, though some types are a fair amount better than others. That said, different enemy types and weaknesses will force you to mix it up at least a little, so you can't really just plow through with one gun (I guess you could try though). IMO that's a good thing.Biggest weakness by far is the inventory management. You can only carry so much on your character, and as you progress in the game it throws and more and more different drops at you, to the point that you can easily fill your inventory within 1-2 minutes of each run. And then when you're back at base it's just a pain to run around between various chests to drop off all your loot. And crafting/research tables only let you use resources on your person and in neighboring chests, so there's still a lot of resource juggling that really doesn't add anything to the game but annoyance.Overall, I still had fun with the game. Currently reviewing the game at version 1.3.5, after the "Bounty of Guns" update. Seems like the dev is still working on more updates, including 4-player multiplayer update that's available in a beta form. Right now I'd say the game is pretty good, and worth the cost of entry. Maybe one day it'll be great, but if this is your type of game or you find it on sale, I'd give it a thumbs up recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: Mileage will vary a bit on this one. I can see where single player can result in the game being a touch lackluster. Having played exclusively in multiplayer, though, it's honestly a good bit of fun.Content-wise, the game is definitely a little thin. If you really rush the game and are hyper-focused on objectives and only care about bigger damage numbers, yeah, the game is gonna fall a bit flat. But if you play it to mess around with the options the game gives you and toy around with the various guns and work on scanning everything and making a somewhat cohesive base, you'll get a good run out of it, honestly. Sure, it's not game of the year material, and some incentive to keep playing after all unlocks and story are done would be nice, but it'd be an abject falsehood to say it isn't fun. Take it for what it is, grab a friend, and it'll be worth the price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: I've seen quite a few people downvote this one and...I have to agree with their thoughts, but not their verdict. This game isn't finished yet. Not by a long shot I'd wager. The developers seem to have a roadmap in mind for future updates and added content, which is a good thing! The problem inherent to that is...I'm not sure what more they can do to flesh the story out. You defeat the literal manifestation of Chaos at the end, the thing *that destroyed the whole damned world*, and...you're told there's more?I just fail to see what could be more important or terrible, thematically, than Chaos Incarnate. That said, it's enjoyable gameplay loop is well worth it, though maybe not at $25. Gunplay has a lot of variations with the plethora of bullets and modifiers and the addition of bounty weapons with unique styles is a nice touch. The music is good and tasty spaghetti westernish, and it's pretty tightly settled. The rouge-like feel is a bit of a pain, but that's how that goes so you learn to be good at dodging and I found myself engaged when things got hairy.A few minor bugs:-Chaos enemies, especially the final boss, can erase the ground they're on with their attacks and if they drop something, it vanishes. This happened to me on my first kill of the final boss, who dropped its story-important item into the void and I was left without any recourse but to redo the fight again and kill it on stable ground. The bounty store did this as well, dropping a gun into the abyss because I put it slightly close to an edge.-Music can drop in certain ways I can't identify, but it seems to happen when coming back to the Tower.It's not a bad game, at all! I've definitely seen worse with better polish, and there's a real shine to this one. Effort and love got put into this and you can tell. I don't know how they're going to continue the story or world, but it's interesting nonetheless. A good 15-25 hour timesink to relax and cast the Alakablam spell. I'd definitely recommend it, but I can't attest to the multiplayer since I didn't try it myself. Could be fun, though!Get it on sale, though. $25 is a bit much for this. I'd wager $20 would be more accurate.

_childDocuments_.review: Love love love this gem of a game - one of my faves the past few years. I have 70+ hours on PlayStation and rebought this for my deck and I'm still loving the gameplay loop. _childDocuments_.name: Wizard with a Gun

_childDocuments_.review: A survival game with objectives and an ending; Explore the four biomes in the world, find upgrade materials to level up your mana infused bullets and collect of the gears of time from elites and bosses to save the world.Aesthetics are cool.Music kept me going.Upgrades and experimenting effect modifiers keep things interesting.Combat is engaging if you bother with combos although I don't see how you can get far if you ignore them. The chaos enemies make it impossible to slugfest as they destroy floor tiles.Varied enemiesNot very difficult: the bosses are basically bullet hell stages except for the last one which is an anticlimactic endurance match on the overworld map. The normal stage enemies are fine except for the sand map as everything is super aggressive and will keep following you throughout, not difficult but very hard to see what's on your screen with all the AoE effects going off. I was playing solo and honestly got bored before the 3rd boss as it becomes very grindy as there's a constant need for materials and the gameplay loop forces you to go back to the hub world to reset the world timer and generate the gear objectives. You can decorate the hubworld with over 100 decorative items and 2 dozen floor tile, which I couldn't be bothered with, the most I did was fix most of the floor as 70% of it is damaged and makes it a pain to get around if you don't. I kept playing because of the music and how cool the game looks.It's disappointing and confusing that the game is only 2 player co-op considering that there are 4 wizards in the thumbnail/poster but after beating the game I saw that there is a mod on Thunderstore that allows up to 16 players in a lobby. I'm not sure how long that would last for since the game is really easy single player and having more players would obliterate any challenge but you could see how long your team lasts in the horde phase that happens after the 5 minute world timer.I liked it but it is another survival game, thankfully a short one. Worth the asking price.
_childDocuments_.name: Wizard with a Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game, the concept is cool, the visuals/gameplay work well, and the base building aspect is satisfying even if it's a bit useless. A few things tho, the game feels a bit grindy at times, you're constantly gonna need materials for crafting stuffs. The movement can feel a bit clunky sometimes, nothing ruining the experience until you get stuck with a bunch of holes in the ground and nowhere to escape.The game is a bit easy, you don't really have to experiment with different strategies or bullets to win, and you probably won't die really often either. There's no endgame, which was a bit disapointing, feels like early access even though it's not.Despite those few flaws i'd recommend getting it once it's on sale, had a lot of fun on my playthrough, planning to play again in coop soon.

_childDocuments_.name: Wizard with a Gun

_childDocuments_.review: Looking at this game, I felt it was obvious how it was gonna play and, for the most part, I was rightBut in addition to the isometric 2D roguelike sandbox stuff that I WAS expecting,  What I was NOT expecting was "Extraction shooter" to be thrown into that mix.You go out on your little expeditions in a similar vein to Cult of the Lamb or Don't Starve and build your little base back home (you can build in the overworld too but those buildings disappear after a run) and the goal is to collect the objectives as fast as you can before the timer runs out and the map starts falling apart, then it's go! go! go! back to the teleporter before the environment becomes too destroyed for you to escape. You can stick around longer and fight the endless spawning waves of chaos creatures, but the longer you stay, the more the environment breaks apart and the harder to kill the enemies become.I especially love the way the gunplay skill trees progress as there are several different schools of bullet magic you can choose to invest in. The hotbars have just enough space to fit one of each gun type (pistol, rifle, blunderbuss, smg) and the two build tools but you don't have to play that way. You want 6 shotguns? Go for it! You can choose to specialize in a specific tree of damage or spread your bullet types out to account for different scenarios. Each gun can house 2 different ammo types and the buff/debuff durations scale with the gun you're using (smgs build stacks fast but the stacks fall off faster, for example)Throw in the co-op multiplayer options and you can go even more hyperspecialized and be a gun cleric for your friends gun warlock build. I don't have anyone to play with myself but seeing just how many ways I can approach building my arsenal has me excited to get one of my friends into it.All in all, a really fun little game. If you like games like Don't Starve or Cult of the Lamb, you'll feel right at home with this one!
_childDocuments_.name: Wizard with a Gun

_childDocuments_.review: A great addition to the rouge-lite genre. Imagine Survival style collecting and crafting whilst also fighting your way through different enemies. Still a little rough around the edges with storage and movement, however the game has a lot of potential and I will be keeping a finger on the pulse of the updates for quite some time and look forward to seeing what they come out with!!!

_childDocuments_.review: THE GOOD: the game is fun, there are very fun mechanica, the crafting is not tedious and you get rewarded for your effort with powerful  and fun combos, if you prepare well you can beat the boss even at the first encounter, since the moves they do are rather simple but very effective at takingnyour health down, the story is narrated through dialogue and books you find in the world and you can choose to skip it if you so desire, the stile is fantastic and everything feels never out of place.THE BAD : while there are fun combos, it feels as if you are constatly restrained by the game, something is missing in the gun powerups, maybe the guns don t have enough range, maybe the fact your camera is fixed and you can t move it further back, but the gunplay resolves in a mess where you can t even see your guy sometimes, the combos are good, but most of the time you can t use them effectively since you would die by stepping too close your enemy or bullet trails, some weapon trees are complex and fun, alnd levelling them up is enjoiable and provides the feeling of progression, others feel incomplete,  the crafting is rather fast, but getting resources is painful, you walk around and shoot at items for hours, you have to then wait for the enemy to come so you can farm more materials and when you are satisfied you go back to repeat it again. THE GAME IS STILL UNFINISHED, i do not regret buying this game, i love it and i want it to succeed, however it s a bit of a scummy move to release it  in this state, THE BOSSES are almost too easy, the only thing that keeps you from killing them as soon as you enter a new zone is the fact that you have to repeatedly farm for MANDATORY UPGRADES to your power level that ARTIFICIALLY GATEKEEP you from  steamrolling the game, the way you upgrade bullets and enemy scaling should be changed to make less boring this process of farming upgrading to farm to upgrade to proceed, since almost all bosses are truly basic.I jave high hopes for this game however and will change my rewiew once the devs finish it. IT'S A GOOD INDIE TITLE but i recommend waiting if you don't like the genre.THIS WAS BEFORE THE MORE GUNS UPDATEnow the game, while still unfinished mind you, is a very good find, the only nitpick i can have with all the new guns is that some are useless the moment you get them since they have no slot, like boss weapons, why even give them to us if they have 1 slot or 2 just make them a random find but let it be powerful

_childDocuments_.review: This became one of my most anticipated games of last year, especially after the demo, and it lived up to my hype. The whole premise of magical guns is simply such good fun, and the game lives out that premise with a lighthearted art style which can still achieve a gritty western movie feel. The soundtrack from Ryan Ike is also a highlight (and the trailer song "Breath and Bone" is just epic).It has a tight gameplay loop as you make expeditions outside your wizard tower to harvest resources, collect gears from enemies, return to your hideout to upgrade your spells, and repeat. It can indeed feel repetitive at times, and progress is rather gradual. While the combat is engaging, it's not nearly as difficult as other action games, and while there is crafting, this is not a main focus as in a full survival game (though building out my tower is a favorite side activity, and somehow this achieves the best wizard lair experience I've seen in a game). For me though, this all combines to make WWAG the game equivalent of comfort food: fairly uncomplicated with an easy assurance of a good time. I think this also makes it a good choice for younger gamers as well. So, strap your arcane big-iron to your hip and get on out there!

_childDocuments_.review: Uh, lessee: imagine the look and feel of Don't Starve, but mixed with the color saturation and silliiness of Enter the Gungeon, with perhaps most bizarrely, the twangy, meditative soundtrack of RimWorld.So far I am enjoying the ♥♥♥♥ out of this game. My sister and I blitzed six hours straight together without even really noticing the first time we played it.The gameplay loops of going into the world, shooting guys, maybe fighting bosses, and collecting goods to build ♥♥♥♥ with back home is really cool. We're a few tiers into the tech tree, and we have a few structures completely emptied of upgrades. What this tells me is that this game SHOULD be able to avoid the Bottleneck Problem (resources becomes so scarce relative to the necessary numbers to craft that the game slows to a crawl). I don't know that for certain, because while there are like 30 different kinds of magic bullet (from damage to fire to charm to poison to poison *finishers*, where you can stack counters and then cash them out for big AoE, it's REALLY clever!), and the only thing I'm worried about is each of those bullets having like 5 or 6 researchable upgrades *PER TIER OF THE SAME BULLET*, which is just over 30 upgrades to fully get an entire line.Now, what will PROBABLY happen is that researching the higher tier is better than improving the lower tier, and that'll bypass the grind, but I'll be on the lookout for the bottleneck. I hate that ♥♥♥♥ and it's ruined games I really loved before (Graveyard Keeper comes to mind). I have a good feeling, and I'm leaving this as a rec until the game gives me reason not to. Cuz so far, that's my only complaint: resources may get grindy, and also the 'enemy armor too tough, find better bullets' is annoying when that enemy is a boss gating my progress to better bullets.Though I solved that by charming some weaker enemies around and they clomped that boss, so maybe that was the point.It's good!

_childDocuments_.review: Wizard with a gun is a rather unique game. It meshes elements of survival games, rouge-likes and sandboxes. There are two main areas; The Tower, which is your base of operations and a safe zone, and The Shatter, where you gather resources and try to survive.As you gather resources, you will be able to research and improve your weapons and bullets. For example, you could study an oil bullet, which would improve fire damage from a burning bullet. You can also apply powders to bullets, which are like modifiers. Powders range from simple critical chance and speed increases, to elemental trails and summoning platforms.The game is also being constantly improved by the devs, and new updates come out frequently. If you have a suggestion or feedback, you can also send it their way.All in all, the game is a fun little thing, where you play as a wizard... with a gun!

Some builds we had were too efficient that it even lagged our game so badly that we had to intentionally nerfed ourselves to play at a stable framerate. The game is also pretty short (for now), finished main story in 22 hours (multiplayer). But we know that there will be more updates and content in the future to look forward to. I think this game is worth it and although it is very short, every minute of it is be great game play. 10/10
