_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge Samurai Jack fan and it's cool to see the original voice actors after so much time. The graphical style of the game is also very well done. It was cool seeing locations and characters from the show being done in this new medium but even as a fan this story can't make up for the game play. The combat is annoying and repetitive in the worst way. You have few effective combos making you do the same two over and over since it's the only way to do any meaningful damage while also at the same time being stuck in long combo animations that make it impossible to dodge or parry with any accuracy. Enemies do huge damage with random unpredictable grabs and it takes FOREVER to stand up if you get knocked down. AI is totally sporadic sometimes standing completely unresponsive for 5-10 seconds other times a mob so completely swarms you that you get stuck in 30 second loops of getting knocked down and standing up before you can even move. Plus you have no control over your own sprint function which makes combat an even slower mess. I love Samurai Jack but i will not be playing any more of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: 🕳️ It may not be a big budget project, but it's a fan service magnum opus for «Samurai Jack» fans. Definitely made with love for the original. For a hack'n'slash, Jack has a wide array of easy-to-execute skills and an optional but varied arsenal of melee / ranged weapons. Level locations are filled with secrets, which adds replay value. Enemies & bosses won't wait for their own death, and in some aspects, a parallel with «Dark Souls» suggests itself here, since certain elements were clearly borrowed , fortunately, the most good ones, without useless mechanics (like losing souls). The game sometimes has problems with object collisions, but this isn't a problem, because platforming plays a small role. The overall performance is an indestructible good. Recommended to all fans of Genndy Tartakovsky creation.

_childDocuments_.review: There’s an episode in the Samurai Jack cartoon where Jack is forced to delve into the innards of an active volcano. It’s not the most hospitable environment, but the last stretch is particularly hazardous. Perhaps the most dangerous thing he comes across is a sheer drop down a shaft of rotating shards of razor sharp granite. He can’t just drop straight down -- the fall would kill him -- so he has to skip from shard to shard knowing that a single mistimed leap could plummet him to his death. Soon after, he reached the central chamber where unstable pillars of crumbling rock spiked unevenly from a pool of magma. Jack had to hop across them before they crumbled beneath his feet to reach his goal; the den of an ancient king, cursed to live within a mammoth body of volcanic rock. To free him from this curse, Jack had to defeat his goliath form, dodging man-sized hammers and flesh-melting bolts of burning lava.There’s a mission in Samurai Jack: Battle Through Time where you’re forced to delve into the innards of an active volcano. It’s not the most hospitable environment, but the last stretch is particularly hazardous. Perhaps the most dangerous thing you come across is a sheer drop down a shaft of rotating shards of razor sharp granite. You can’t just drop straight down -- the fall would kill you -- so you have to skip from shard to shard knowing that a single mistimed leap could plummet you to your death. Soon after, you reach the central chamber where unstable pillars of crumbling rock spike unevenly from a pool of magma. You have to hop across them before they crumble beneath your feet to reach your goal; the den of an ancient king, cursed to live within a mammoth body of volcanic rock. To free him from this curse, you have to defeat his goliath form, dodging man-sized hammers and flesh-melting bolts of burning lava.Battle Through Time often shows tremendous respect to its much loved source material, pulling entire sections from the cartoon itself and using them as memorable set pieces. But even when it’s not following its study case stroke for stroke, it still finds a way to fit in some of the most iconic characters from the show. One episode featured a robotic ninja clad, expectedly, entirely in black. The battle between it and Jack in the cartoon took place in an artistically stunning juxtaposition between light and dark, the ninja cloaked in shadows and Jack shielded by the light. While the theme may have been a little too complex to bring to video gaming life, the ninja still makes his presence known. He’ll appear in a bellow of black smoke, shower Jack in shuriken then vanish again. He’ll soon reappear, probably behind you, and become a frustratingly elusive foe, blocking and countering many of your own attacks while you try and keep pace. Problem is, he’s rarely alone. Enemies from across the show like beetle drones, Celtic demons and khaki-clad vaguely-Australian bounty hunters will all attack you in waves.For the most part, the beetles and friends are cannon fodder, designed to be mowed down with little effort, they’re main threat being sheer number rather than individual strength, letting a good player slice their way through an army, transitioning strikes and blows to form a smooth, interlinking combo of destruction. In a lot of ways, Battle Through Time is a throwback slasher, feeling less like current genre norms like Dark Souls and more like the original God of War. Bad news for fans of constant dodge rolls, I know, but it doesn't mean Jack’s a mindless button masher, either. Combos can be put together by chaining together fast and strong attacks while blocking, dodging and countering still play a big part in taking down the more wily foes. To begin with, your offensive options appear limited, but your opening arsenal of magical katana and humble fist can be swollen by exploration. Soon, you can find yourself able to equip bamboo staff, bulky or bulky warhammers, all offering different combat styles and all possessing unique combos you can further unlock as the game progresses. If all that direct combat doesn't appeal to you, ranged weapons like kunai blades and bows can be sourced. If that’s not enough, you are in the future, and there’s pistols and even machineguns available, if you look for them hard enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me cut to the chase and say that if you are looking for an amazing 3D hack and slash game with a wide variety of weapons and a truly unique aesthetic, this is the game for you!Samurai Jack: Battle Through Time has to be one of the best games I've played this year, and dare I say, one of the best licensed games I've played in general. It ties into the show's 5th season specifically, and even manages to surpass it in a few ways. (No spoilers, but you'll know what I mean if you play it) I would argue that you don't even need to have a particular attachment to the source material to enjoy this game.There is a good variety of difficulty levels as well. I was impressed by the details on the models, not even noticing that they were used for the cutscenes until I noticed the clothing damage being carried over to them as well. There are also a ton of skills you can learn to make your abilities more powerful, such as new weapon combos or upgrades for the amount of skill points you find.Overall, I highly recommend it. Now if only they would make a Sym-Bionic Titan game in the same style...

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a HUGE fan of Samurai Jack. I remember not missing a single episode on Cartoon Network when I was a kid and it's probably the most memorable cartoon of my life. I was craving for a Samurai Jack game back then and all I got was some flash games. I didn't know Shadow of Aku or GBA game existed. When I heard season 5 was coming in 2017, I literally lost my sh*t. Just like I did when I watched the announcement trailer of Battle Through Time. I'm so happy that my favorite childhood hero finally got a proper game of his own. Samurai Jack: Battle Through Time is a great shootout to old hack n slash games from the PS2 era. You'll hack and slash your way through several Samurai Jack episodes, meet your old friends, and learn new skills along the way. It may seem difficult at first but keep in mind that most of the combat mechanics are locked behind skills so the combat gets varied as you learn new skills. I won't talk about the story, but I will encourage you to collect every collectible item in game if you want to see a secret ending. Trust me, it's worth it. Another selling point of this game is that it was made by ex Ninja Gaiden devs and it truly feels like it's been made by people who knew what they were doing. However, it took them 5 days to fix the achievements after the release date so, that kinda made me doubt the future of the game. But hey, at least they got fixed eventually. Some devs don't care about that at all. I really hope we'll get more content in the future. I really want more levels about iconic episodes such as Jack and the Rave so I hope they will release them as DLC or something. I've also written a  about getting all achievements and completing in-game challenges in case you need help with them.

_childDocuments_.review: Samurai Jack, a massive part of my childhood, I loved the show so when I heard about this game i was pretty excited to say the least, I mean I've been on the edge of my seat for 2 weeks waiting for this game to release, but as it turns out I was kind of let down.Now I want to start this review with all the things I find good about the game, which is actually a lot despite me not recommending the game. I've gotten fairly far in the game within the 6 hours I've played at the time of writing this review, and I've got to say I'm impressed with all the stuff from the show they've added, a lot of familiar faces from the show, some of which I didn't even remember myself. They've even added in some weapons we saw jack use for less than 3 minutes such as the lightning staff he used when he made his comeback in season 5, which again is really cool to me, and something I like seeing.The game also looks pretty amazing, I mean they had to make a 2D cartoon into a 3D game, and I say they've done an absolutely fantastic job. The characters 3D models are spot on for adapting a cartoon into this game and play amazing, and the surrounding world looks great as well. Samurai Jack as a cartoon had a pretty hard to capture art style for a game but I think this does the job well and I have no complaints for it what so ever. Story: The game follows just after Jack and Ashi escape through a portal to go back in time, which occurs at the end of season 5, however in this game instead of escaping, Aku manages to stop them by sending Jack to different points in time to places he has been before, and we follow along as Jack defeats foes from the past, in order to escape back to past once again. A pretty interesting idea to take place after the end of season 5 and I think it works well for the game, yet again no complaints, the story is just fine.Now comes my complaints.My first complaint is controls. Now for whatever reason you can't customise PC controls and normally that shouldn't be too much of an issue but with this game it is. There are some controls that are absolutely horrific, such as the use/interact button. Now which button did the devs decided to use for this was it something simple and easy to reach like E? No, no it wasn't. They decided to use the J key. No, I'm not joking. Now unless you're a professional piano player you are going to struggle reaching over to this key especially with all the times you have to press it in game. Another key that feels annoying is The E key as that is used for quick fire ranged attacks, which isn't really necessary as that's what the middle mouse button is for, so at times I'll find myself wasting my ranged weapons when I press E to try and interact with something, which is annoying considering you have to buy ranged weapons quite a bit and they aren't the cheapest thing in the world. Apart from those keys there are no combat related keys that I have a problem with everything else is alright, but when in the menus it’s a nightmare. In this game you can't use your mouse to click things you have to use Q and E to go from left and right in the menu and use the arrow keys to go up and down, as well as having to press backspace instead of the ESC key to go back which makes it fairly annoying to use, but that's about it. Now for my second complaint, which really isn't anything too huge, but that is spending gold. In this game there are a lot of things to buy such as items to restore health, items to increase damage temporarily, ranged weapons ammunition (such as arrows and shuriken), actual weapons which you also need to pay to restore durability etc. But a lot of things are pricey, which is annoying as you also have to pay gold for increase your weapon level. For some perspective, a standard health item, that restores a fair bit of health is 1000 gold, the first time to train your sword level it's around 12,000 gold, and considering you need to pay quite a bit of gold on missions to buy said healing item, it can be hard to save up to train your weapons ,which I've noticed have started to become a bit necessary in later missions, especially seeing as on average I find myself earning around 6000-9000 gold a mission and that's with me exploring a lot of the areas including ones that are hidden or are not on the path of the main mission, and considering I spend about 1000-3000 a mission on health items which doesn't even factor in me buying my ranged weapons, than it becomes very hard to save up for training.One other small complaint I have is the background music is very repetitive and isn’t very interesting, I mean I was hoping for something a little more Samurai-y, if that makes sense, but the music isn’t very relevant considering there is a lot of fighting going on at most times during the game so, you’ll often just be listening to your slashing attacksNow comes my biggest complaint, which is the sole reason I do not recommend this game. I can look past the previous three things for the most part but I can't look past this and ultimately it is ruining my enjoyment of the game, and that is the blocking and dodging mechanics. To put it bluntly, they are complete garbage. The blocking mechanic basically feels as it's not even there. To block you must press F, but this is completely useless as it blocks one attack, and then you’re practically screwed. Now you may be asking what's wrong with that, well considering a lot of the time an enemy will attack you 3 times in a row, in a sort of chain attack, and it blocks only one attack, then you have to take the other two as dodging is going to help as you are stuck in the animation of taking damage, and if you somehow manage to jump one of three things will happen, the enemy will then charge attack you, there will be some other enemy to snipe you and damage you mid-air or both. So basically because of this the game even on normal difficulty feels incredibly hard, and annoying to play which is what ruins my experience. Because the dodging and blocking are so hard, fighting bosses feels much easier than fighting groups of enemies at times simply because you can defend yourself from the boss easier, that being said some boss fights are still annoying to play as you can’t block some of the attacks that determine the battle, and some just decide to spam attack you before you can do the same to them. And the dodging is just rolling away which if you’ve played dark souls before you should be familiar with, except this dodging is useless as even if you roll away somewhere enemies will just snipe you with lasers, bullets and arrows and that’ll give the up close fighters a chance to attack you. The dodging mechanic is especially useless on the 2D sections of the game where you are can only dodge to left or right, but regardless there will be enemies on both sides, so it serves no purpose there what so ever. Because these two mechanics fail to work in a way that benefits the player you’ll often find yourself having to deal with a wave of unstoppable attacks that keep going until you die, because the combat system is not smooth with these two systems not working, and often times you find yourself having to consume most of your hot water (healing item) just to survive a couple of enemies, and by that time you don’t have any for the boss, and God helps you if it’s an annoying boss (especially that bounty hunter couple which can just keep chain attacking you and you can’t do anything to one of them because the other will stop you) because you’ll end up racking more deaths than in Dark Souls. And what scares me the most about this is, this is when I was on normal difficulty, there’s still a hard mode as well as an extra hard difficulty after that.In conclusion the game would be enjoyable and would have a well-developed combat system if only the blocking and dodging functioned in a better way, which would also make it challenging for the player rather than impossible.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game ultimately but it has a lot of problems. It does not feel like this game was properly playtested until way too late in the development process. The combat is so close to being very good but a lot of poor decisions really bring it down and the last mission really shows off all the worst parts of it.The combat is fast, the animations are great, and the various combos and weapons are surprisingly satisfying. The problem is that the balance is all wrong. Many enemies are damage sponges, the damage you do seems inconsistent (sometimes you kill an enemy in a few hits, other times you barely do any damage to them), the enemies hit very hard, and the health drops are far, far too infrequent. A lot of the most important skills are far into the skill unlock trees and you don't get access to them until either near the end of the game, or on a second playthrough depending on what you prioritise. Even when you collect all the treasures possible in the game, you will not get nearly enough items to buy all the skills. Beam attacks from enemies are not done properly, they fire very fast and always stun so you get stunlocked very quickly if you're not careful if there are a lot of extremely minor enemies. There is a fight very early in the game where you fight a few standard beetle enemies and a bunch of the small green ones that fire beams. This fight is extremely difficult because you don't have any items or skills to help much with them, and they can stunlock you very easily since there are so many of them firing at you from every direction.Making this worse, enemies off-screen attack you all the time. The camera always focuses on the enemy you're fighting which means you cannot easily see the rest of the enemies. You will be hit from off-screen more than most other action games as a result.There is one boss that is constantly-reused throughout the game whose only real attack is that they keep spawning in regular enemies. The very last fight with them involves them calling down random enemies, some of which are the extremely big mini-boss variants. If the RNG is against you, it will spawn in multiple of these guys.It's such a shame because the look, the animations, the sound, everything about this game is so wonderfully done. This game could have been an easy 8/10 or 9/10 game that would be an amazing loveletter to Samurai Jack but the poor gameplay balance really drags this down. Most of this game is very much worth playing, and is an easy recommendation to anyone that enjoys Samurai Jack. But don't feel bad to put the game on the easiest difficulty, it's just not well-made enough to "git gud" at.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not quite a Devil May Cry or Bayonetta, but a very enjoyable action game, nonetheless. There are a good amount of combat options, moves feel snappy and responsive, it feels easy to get into a good flow. It's perhaps a bit too easy on normal difficulty for veterans of stylish/character action games. Stages are mostly linear with a few side paths for exploration, a good amount of visual variety in the stages and the game looks pretty good overall, seems true to the cartoonish aesthetic (although I've never watched the show so maybe fans of the show would have a more informed opinion on that front). Would recommend to fans of the stylish/character action genre.

_childDocuments_.review: A short but enjoyable adventure with surprisingly well-thought-out combat mechanics and enemy design that, despite being held back by less-than-stellar animations, still manages to be engaging.For those looking for a challenge, know that, on the highest difficulty, some of the encounters feel like they came straight out of Ninja Gaiden 2. The chaos and amount of projectiles on screen can be overwhelming at times. Whether that turns out to be a thrilling or frustrating experience may depend more on your personal preference rather than your level of skill.The lower difficulties should provide a smoother, more welcoming experience for most players, but there is a difficulty spike in the last stage that some may find off-putting. Don't hesitate to lower the difficulty to Easy if you feel like you need to, as it can take some time to not only unlock your moves, but also learn how to correctly apply them in combat.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm kinda torn. In some respects this game is amazingly good such as the combat being challenging and the hard mode being a real challenge (Read: Impossible), the enemies falling apart differently depending on how they are slain, and the visuals being rather incredible including Jack’s clothes becoming damaged as he does.But there is a whole host of issues that really made me dislike this game. The control scheme for mouse and keyboard is garbage. J is used to interact with characters, backspace is to go backwards, and enter is the confirm button. Some of it makes sense, like weak attacks, strong attacks, and ranged attacks being bound to left click, right click, and middle click respectively, but why is E also a ranged attack? Surely E should be Interact like many other games?I sure wish I could rebind the controls to suit me better! The F key is used for parrying, which is an absolutely mandatory ability to use, and you can even pair it with movement for a sliding parry which is FANTASTIC for closing distance! Unless you also need to move towards the right, in which case I hope you’ve got extra fingers to press both D and F at the same time! Also, there is a dodge move which I’m not sure why you’d ever want to use when you can parry-slide. It’s bound to Shift, which would be the best key for parry.The best thing to do is go read the controls in the menu before really playing. And, of course, the menu is super easy to access: just hit escape! Oh, and also hit the Home button on your keyboard. You use the home button all the time, right? Do you even have one? When was the last time you checked?I got through the entire story in one session, which is fine, but it wasn’t until I was ranting at a friend and trying a controller out that I realized that some ranged weapons can be AIMED! Things like the bow or revolver and be aimed down sights with the very, very intuitive CTRL key. Otherwise, thrown weapons can be aimed just by looking where you want to throw. Two different aiming systems for the ranged weapons; we’re spoiled for choices!Oh yeah, and the weapons. The game opens with the show’s opener and the classic line “…A foolish samurai warrior wielding a magic sword…” Why are there any other weapons? Do I really need a spear or hammer when I have a magic sword? Well, since the sword can’t break and everything else will, the answer is no. Oh, or you can go unarmed which does… less damage? Neat!The last gripe is the camera. Sometimes the game goes onto rails and we’re stuck looking at a side-on perspective with only 2D movements. The times it does this is random and seemingly without reason. This is made even worse by the aforementioned D and F controls and the fact you are frequently moving to the right.Also, there are random cutscenes that do not need to be there. Don’t take me out of my badass-samurai ass-kicking mode to show me a chest popping out of the ground or a doorway opening. I’m in the room, I can see it anyways! And the chests are generally not worth the time to takes for the animation to play.At the end of some fights, we also get a close up on Jack’s face. Neat, but why? He’s just scowling and not really being very emotive; there’s nothing new to see!If they fixed the controls (or you use a controller) and stop jerking my camera around, I’d be a lot happier. That being said, this is still a great hack-and-slash that will really challenge you.

_childDocuments_.review: Samurai Jack: Battle Through Time is an excellent addition to the beloved franchise. The game features engaging gameplay and a well-written story that stays true to the spirit of the TV show. Fans of the show and action game enthusiasts will definitely enjoy this title.The gameplay itself is fast-paced and satisfying, with a variety of enemies and bosses to battle using Jack's trusty sword and a variety of unlockable abilities. The levels are well-designed and offer a nice mix of exploration and combat.Overall, Samurai Jack: Battle Through Time is a must-play for fans of the show and action game enthusiasts. It's a well-crafted game that stays true to the source material and offers plenty of challenge and replay value.

_childDocuments_.review: Not only is the game visually beautiful with it's colors and art direction, (People who say it looks like a PS2 game probably don't own it, or are playing on low settings.), but the combat is actually fun and playing on the hardest difficulty reminds me of Ninja Gaiden. It's insane. Basically most enemies, (especially ones with throws) near one shot you. You have to blend ranged and close attacks together, shoot enemies about to attack to stun them, and use counters to avoid taking damage. Really really good! Props to the devs for doing such a fantastic job! An excellent and fun experience.EDIT: Going farther into the game (I'm playing on the harder difficulty), there seem to be some locations that need balancing. Could be patched later on, but it seems like the team didn't expect someone to dive in to Master Samurai with no New game + skills already. I'm stuck on a boss that is incredibly hard to fight and there aren't any shops or health items before it. So I might lower the difficulty and just move on. I've fought them over 60 times, about 3 hours of time, and not once have I come close to beating him. I've gotten through several levels and bosses without a problem so I think it's safe to say some balancing is needed here haha.
_childDocuments_.name: Samurai Jack: Battle Through Time

_childDocuments_.review: Combat is a touch clunky until you unlock some skills but after a few levels into Samurai difficulty, I'm torn between wanting to increase the difficulty and keep it. Enemies can combo you down very quickly and they are numerous. There is a bunch here to play around with and l am looking forward to at least one more full playthough. My favorite thing is the art style and cutscenes. Menus have fun artwork of Jack with the weapons reflecting on them. The 3d models can go from great (Jack, especially on the textures) to ps2 (in a bit of a fun way) like in Aku's case. If you read this and the game is still up, might be worth a pick up. If you ever get nostalgic or go through a Sam Jack marathon, it's worth adding to the end of the watch.
_childDocuments_.name: Samurai Jack: Battle Through Time

_childDocuments_.review: you don't automatically pick up coins & even "super" bar items automatically in the clumsy combat from things you kill in melee range, you don't even pick them up from breaking objects your model has to pretty much physically touch every coincouldn't tell apart icons, effects & drops only differentiated by colour instead of designauto un-locks from enemies you defeat & if you try to lock on again to get to the next enemy it locks onto the corpse for about 4 seconds in a past-paced fighting game, but it doesn't really matter because enemies wait for their turn to get beat up rather than attack you frequently enough for the parry to be worth unlockinglevel design & sluggishness is OK if we're comparing it to similar games from the early 2000s but not 2020is there a volume slider? couldn't find in main menu on initially starting the game blasting me at 100% volume
_childDocuments_.name: Samurai Jack: Battle Through Time

_childDocuments_.review: For a fan of the outstanding animated series this is a good purchase you shouldn't be disappointed.1.Gameplay-It's a fun Hack and Slash with a wide range of combat options weather that be the weapons or just what style of combat you want to use.2.Control-The controls of Samurai Jack:Battle Through Time are very responsive and tight Jack controls about as well as Kratos from the God of War series so if you have played God of War you should be able to pick this up easily.3.Graphics-This game takes the art style of the animated programme and makes a stylised and simply beautiful game no matter what graphical quality.4.Difficulty-Samurai Jack:Battle Through Time is probably the perfect difficulty for a casual playthrough not easy or hard a perfect middle ground and if you want a challenge there is a harder difficulty unlocked after beating the game for the first time.5.Cutscenes-The Cutscenes have a mixture of in game engine and animated cutscenes that look right out of the show even the first cutscene before the menu is the intro to the show.All the voice actors from the show returned to do the voices and they all do a good job but i wish that we could hear more of them since the dialogue in levels aren't voice acted.6.Levels/Bosses-Samurai Jack:BTT has 9 levels that range from 15-25 minutes and they are all fun and unique and have a boss fight at the end to give a more grandiose feel for completing a level and the bosses are all fine some are very easy like the graveyard boss and some are annoying because they'll manipulate knockback damage to keep attacking you but the ones that do it are the final bosses which makes more sense due to being near the end of the game7.Length-SJ:BTT is a 5-7 hour journey at least on regular difficulty which is good for something you can beat in a single sitting but if you enjoy longer games that require multiple sittings to beat i wouldn't recommend this game.8.Story-Same as the show Jack must return to the past and stop Aku and his evil with the help of Ashi from the 5th season.Overall-Samurai Jack:Battle Through Time is a fun somewhat short game that is an easy pickup for fans of the animated series or fans of hack and slashes.It's a beautiful stylised game remaining faithful to the series.Personally I would give Samurai Jack:Battle Through Time an 8.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Samurai Jack: Battle Through Time

_childDocuments_.review: I have a soft spot for this game and that's because if you play it on the higher difficulties it plays like a lite version of Ninja Gaiden 2 (Xbox 360) in the sense that every single enemy can be deadly and you gotta use every tool at your disposal and also get a feel of the usage of i-frames and other under the hood system mechanics to overcome some tight combat encounters.The game can be a little janky at times but it's a fun ride nonetheless if you love challenging character action games, besides Samurai Jack is a freaking amazing IP for an action game so it's an easy thumbs up all around for me.Certified hidden gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Samurai Jack: Battle Through Time

_childDocuments_.review: A surprise for sure, but a welcome one.With excellent cartoony graphics (pretty faithful to the cartoon it is based on), it shows a lot of soul, and appeals for old time fans and newcomers too.The combat reminds me of souls-like games with the basic "easy to learn, hard to master", even though it may prove very difficult to new players, with some practice you'll get it.*THE FOLLOWING PARTS MAY CONTAIN SPOILERS, YOU'VE BEEN ADVISED.*Story-wise it is very reminiscent of what we used to watch; Jack frees Ashi from Aku's control and declares his love for her. Ashi then goes against her father, using her inherited powers, she creates a portal to the past to escape her father's hands. However, Aku makes a time pocket trapping Jack in it, going through many trials for him to suffer.Jack goes on a personal mission to change things, defeating the trials Aku had made to him.Definitely a 9/10 if only it had a more intricate storyline and satisfying combat.
_childDocuments_.name: Samurai Jack: Battle Through Time

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this so badly. I started off with low expectations because the trailer made it look kinda corny.The combat is seriously boring. It feels like this game was designed for Jack to lose his sword, relying on you to use what you can find, much like the original final season.However, there's no reason to do that since Jack has his indestructable Magic Sword the entire time.Perhaps the original idea was for him to lose the sword again and obtain it later like a sort of Master Sword?

_childDocuments_.name: Samurai Jack: Battle Through Time

_childDocuments_.review: I was expecting a brainless slasher for a single playthrough. Instead I got a game that not only has an elaborate combat system but also it's extremaly punishing when careless. And to keep the player occupied after beating the campaign there is a whole lot of stuff to collect where unlocking all skills is vital to complete the game on the hardest difficulty which is just brutal.If it weren't just for the clunky parrying and dodging system and one of the most unfair checkpoint implementations I've ever seen then I would easily suggest this game to every action games enjoyers looking for a challange. However in this case, I would rather recommend it only to Samurai Jack fans since the soul of the Tartakovsky series is tangible here.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of the series you will enjoy eating up some more samurai time. The game is a souls like hack and slash that is short and sweet. They do offer some challenges after you beat the game, and a harder difficulty for some replay value. For 40 dollars, it was worth it for me and young me would of appreciated it.
_childDocuments_.name: Samurai Jack: Battle Through Time

_childDocuments_.review: Would I recommend this game to a friend? No.Would I deter them from buying it? Also no. I feel like this game falls a little flat on even the most unassuming fan's expectations.The combat is fun, and it's cute to see references from the cartoon here and there, but the story seemed very odd to me for the fast transitions between environments. I like the music, but it really would've impacted the player more to have music from the actual show (also, seems like a completely missed opportunity to not have the rave episode integrated in any way). Enemy variety is very low, weapons don't take too many risks, and the platforming is lackluster. The written dialogue to me seemed incredibly jarring - the script seems more general purpose and rarely if ever makes a call or attempts to fit in with a character's speaking pattern. The 3D modeling is very distracting, at least to me, however the voice work was excellent in the very small portions it was done. Personally, I think the cutscenes are for the most part disengaging (near the end of the game, Aku's 'army' is represented as a collection of about 4 dozen troops you've been fighting the whole game), and would've much rather sat through an animation more akin to the original show. I think that would've allowed the game to transcend the awkward 3D limbo while making good use of the IP. Speaking of, it seems obvious they didn't know what deserved a place in the game. Overall, I was a little disappointed in this game's story and visuals. The combat and the skills are fun and I could see myself wanting to 100% the game, but someone who is not a particularly strong fan of Samurai Jack will certainly not enjoy it even half as much as I did. I do not recommend this game with a $40 price point. $30, maybe, but this is not enough quality to justify the current price.
_childDocuments_.name: Samurai Jack: Battle Through Time

_childDocuments_.review: They didn't bother taking time and effort to make the game immersive. Two of the most annoying parts are, weapon durability and there being no voice acting. Why would there not be a proper voice acting for NPCs, there are already not many lines. Even some indie studios have phenomenal voice acting in their games, when Adult Swim does it, it just looks like them being cheap to me. I don't recommend this game, I thought I was being picky but my one other friend who enjoys Samurai Jack very much also couldn't bother finishing the game for the similar reasons, so I felt validated.
_childDocuments_.name: Samurai Jack: Battle Through Time

_childDocuments_.review: This game is hard and this game knows it's hard otherwise it would not give you fountains of health after every battle. I have beaten all of FromSoft's Souls and Souls-like titles, and SAMURAI JACK, on Master Samurai, was too much straight out the gate. I had to put it down to normal difficulty to progress. This is very much a hack and slash grinder within the Samurai Jack universe, and if that's your bag then it is absolutely excellent. An inventory system, weapon management including durability, upgrades, skill trees - I mean, it gives you any and all reasoning to want to play. The whole point is to play it over and over until you unlock all of your skills, and it makes that compelling with excellent mechanics and a vibrant world.Just for some context on its difficulty: I fought a swarm of enemies only to immediately be met with a double boss fight, ONLY TO IMMEDIATELY BE MET WITH A FUSED BOSS FIGHT. If you die at any point then you start over from the swarm ... and this was level one.Level. One.Yes, I recommend it. Gotta get back. Back to the past.
_childDocuments_.name: Samurai Jack: Battle Through Time

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty good licensed game and a decent character action/hack and slash game, more appealing if you're actually a fan of the show too. This game surprised me with how varied the combat system was, I assumed it was gonna be sword only but found it really cool you could throw many things like shuriken and scythes as well as using guns and bows. There's a lot of tools and options for combat which make its really fun and the combo system is better than expected. My only real complaints about the game is its length and the fact that some bosses and encounters are really cheap or just not well designed in general, especially on the final level. 7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Samurai Jack: Battle Through Time

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not a joke, it is really a proper action game! in fact, I did not expect it to be that good. but I really enjoyed itIt is a Samurai Jack game exactly what you hoped it would be. in this game you are making adventures through time in different eras and places where you are facing many varied enemies across varied environments in order to "return to the past, and undo the future that is Aku!"... not to mentioning the amount of weapons, various fighting styles and the skill tree which helps you to unlock many movements that add new compositions to your fighting style.This variety made the game really fun and it perfectly fits Jack's adventure.And like any other games, there are some negative aspects, the biggest is The Difficulty!: in higher difficulties even small attacks like bullets or laser will knock you down or they put you in a small room where dozens of enemies are spamming on you at once with no window to escape until you die!.... It's really frustrating. the other thing is a personal preference: It would have been better if the story was about a side adventure of Samurai Jack instead of re-telling the last season.In the end I think Hiroaki Matsui and his team at Soleil did a really great job.Verdict: 7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Samurai Jack: Battle Through Time

_childDocuments_.name: Samurai Jack: Battle Through Time

_childDocuments_.review: Great concept for a Samurai Jack game, with poor execution in some places. I played on the hardest (available) difficulty from the start, and so that's where I'm coming from. If you play on a standard difficulty, maybe these issues won't bother you as much (cause you won't die 1000 times), and you'll have a really fun time:1) NO CUSTOM CONTROLS - adds unnecessary difficulty to the game2) I hate the random save points; you don't know that they're save points until you reach a point on the map and see the auto-save icon pop up. That - combined with the fact that those SAVE POINTS ONLY TRIGGER ONCE and there's NO MANUAL SAVE - makes dying and retrying an area way more annoying than it has to be.3) (maybe nitpicky, but it pissed me off lol) Master Samurai mode is definitely challenging, but it achieves this in the most frustrating way possible. ALL ENEMIES CAN CANCEL ALL OF THEIR ANIMATIONS AT ANY POINT. Attack animations, movement animations, invincible animations, recovery animations - all of them. Have fun with mobs of enemies and bosses that summon minions.
_childDocuments_.name: Samurai Jack: Battle Through Time

_childDocuments_.review: Great nostalgia trip for Samurai jack Fans, but with only part of a good game in there. No major complaints, but a lot of minor ones.You visit the great looking environments from several episodes and meet a few characters, though they don't interact much. Combat gameplay is hit or miss, the combos and weapons are satisfying to use, but the dodge/block are plain unfair and could use more work. It feels like enemies have more iframes than Jack, often ruining your flow. Multiple times I got stunlocked for what felt an eternity. The camera control and targeting is pretty basic, it's frustrating to select your targets. Sometimes enemies get stuck, sometimes you get stuck outside the map. The game only saves on certain checkpoints, which means if you did any upgrades or inventory management and die, you have to repeat everything.The game starts pretty slow, and the fun upgrades take a lot of grinding. The tutorials are very basic as well, it took me a long time until I figured out several important game mechanics. One important and unexplained one was that you're supposed to use breakable weapons and let them break, since they drop a lot of experience to buy skill upgrades.Still, despite all these minor points I (usually) enjoyed myself, but for this price it could've use like a year of extra development for some QoL. I'm happy that I got it pretty cheap in a Humble Bundle
_childDocuments_.name: Samurai Jack: Battle Through Time

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, definitely DONT go for the hardest difficulty available since the start, this game seems it was made to be completed a few times, if you go for the hardest difficulty you will find the game highly frustrating.+ Good gameplay & replayability+ You can use a variety of weapons- Lacks polishing in a few combat areas/enemies- They could have done a full VO for the charactersI give this game a 8 out of 10, its a no-brainer buy it if you are a huge samurai jack fan or when its in discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Samurai Jack: Battle Through Time

_childDocuments_.review: I may be a bit biased, as I am a huge fan of the Samurai Jack TV show and I really enjoyed my time with this game. The combat is deeper than I thought it would be, with various melee and ranged weapon types and 3 different upgrade paths to manage. The game also proved to be a bit more challenging than I had thought as well. My only real complaints are that some enemy encounters felt a bit cheap and this is a more personal preference thing, but I am not a big fan of weapon degradation in games. Thankfully, these are only minor issues that can be generally be overlooked. The graphics aren't the most impressive thing in the world, but the game runs smoothly and looks pretty good on the highest graphical settings. Some people complain about the length of the game, but it being somewhat short allows for repeat playthroughs to flow smoothly and the game doesn't overstay its welcome. With loads of secrets to find, awesome boss fights, and a bunch of different weapons and tools to mess around with, Samurai Jack: Battle Through Time is a must play for fans of the show.
_childDocuments_.name: Samurai Jack: Battle Through Time

_childDocuments_.review: If your looking for a game that represents Samurai Jack and his adventures from the past (or future) then this is it! its a short homage to a delightful game with lush experiences and fan service that will bring a smile to your face. For what it is, i had a great experience besides the length and lack of gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Samurai Jack: Battle Through Time

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10 I recommend itThe combat & gameplay reminds of me Devil May Cry, and just having to fight as Jack is satisfying in a way. Your weapons will break if you use them too much (Except the Magic Sword) but luckily you can go to the "Da Samurai" and have them repaired, but I do like the concept that it's sorta of an Alternate Universe basically like a "What would happen?" scenario.I'm going to explain the story a little bit so SPOILERS if you haven't played the game or watched Samurai Jack (I would highly recommend if you do watch it, just so you can understand a bit better)The game only has 9 Stages which is short but it feels long when it comes down to fighting waves of enemies & boss fights that you will encounter in the game ALOT, you can probably finish the game within 4 Hours but it took me 13 because I went back & forth between Stages just so I can get the Collectables which are called "Corrupted Emperor's Kamon" and lemme explain why you should get these, it's not a requirement but it does contain something special.After you get all 50 Corrupted Emperor's Kamon/Collectables The game has a'lot to offer, and can kick you in the a.s,$ I had this game on Normal/Samurai Difficulty and it really was challenging for a bit, but when I was in the Final Boss Fight and trying to defeat Aku I had to lower the difficulty to Easy/Jack and I felt ashamed about it but I'm just relieved I got the ending I wanted.One of the Problems I have with this game, is that even though the Visuals do look nice time-to-time and can be beautiful but at times it will look ugly, just the graphics should've needed more polishing & work done, sometimes it was unappealing. Having to Parry/Block against enemies is hard as hell and you have to get it at the right time, I honestly think it's just a huge annoyance especially against stronger enemies.The price of the game is a bit too much and I would recommend to get it on sale, but to me it doesn't matter since I already spent $40 on it because I love Samurai Jack and I wanted to play this game despite the price range.Overall it's a fun & challenging game and I recommend it, I might even comeback to this game at some point in the future but time will tell. SAMURAI JACK IS BACK

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Samurai Jack, you should get this game. Game-play is super fun. Combat is responsive. And the mighty Jack is great. I really like the detail that when Jack loses health, his hair becomes messy and his clothes gets ripped off. Music is really good which I wasn't expecting to be honest. Not to mention the Art Direction. The stages look great and each of them has their own mood. The cel-shading on 3D looks great on the characters and the levels. Only thing I didn't liked that the campaign isn't long enough which you can complete in 6-7 hours. I really hope the developers would add a few extra chapters in the form of DLC I suppose. All in all. a solid game. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Samurai Jack: Battle Through Time

_childDocuments_.review: So after having just beat the game, I overall like it, but it has some big flaws that really present themselves on the 'Master of Samurai' difficulty. I'm annoyed to say that I was able to beat all of the levels on the difficulty on it except for Aku City and the Final level, where I had to drop the difficulty on the respective bosses of each to win.To give a tldr at the beginning, based on a hard-mode run, I'd give it a 7/10 at the lowest. It's a great, if short, game that is nice fanservice for the series and plays fairly well. It's no titan or anything, but the gameplay is very competent for what it is. There are enough flaws in the system, however, that, unless you're looking for a head-to-wall-banging challenge, I would not recommend doing Hard mode on the first run. It's certainly possible (as I said, I only felt to drop it on 2 separate occasions and this was on the Bosses of their stage), but you will most likely die often and it won't always feel like it's your fault and definitely extends the playtime (10 hours is what they suggest, I got it in 17).I'd recommend the Fists over the sword for your 'permanent' weapons (Jumping Strong is faster and has better tracking to help with small enemies) and for the breakables, the Hammer is the best of the bunch; it has a significant amount of hyperarmor and the ability to get Aggressive defense options that straightup block damage while attacking instead of just armoring through them as well.--As has been mentioned in the thread, while the game is very good, you can definitely feel the budget and it's most apparent on the higher difficulty as the flaws with the battle systems (primarily, I feel, hit detection) are most apparent here. Word of advice no matter the difficulty: LEARN THE PARRY and USE THE BLOCK! The enemies often have extended hitboxes on their attacks, especially the glowing red attacks that you can't block. Enemies will also get into a defensive stance quite often seemingly just because. This is important to know because, with these 2 combinations of factors, the enemy can often retaliate very fast (too fast sometimes) while you're mid combo and catch you off guard, dealing massive damage on hard.The worst part, though, is the mobbing that the enemies do. They're absolutely brutal at times and Jack does not get sufficient i-frames from getting hit so most of the time, if you screw up and start to get juggled, the enemies will just pummel you, so it's super important that you work on not getting hit in the first place. Unless you get the proper times to block down, be prepared to get ganked and wombo-comboed quite often.--As an aside, I think the Steam Achievements are bugged, cause I don't have any, lol
_childDocuments_.name: Samurai Jack: Battle Through Time

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this with a lot of caveats.The game is a retreading of the last season, even using a couple of animated scenes from it in the beginning and end. However it does do its own thing by trying to integrate elements from the show's lore all over.The combat isn't that great, I am gonne be very blunt about it. it is passable however and does give you the general feeling it wants you to get. It isn't as brain dead as Dynasty Warrios, but far less sophisticated than Devil May Cry. Also enemies tend to be annoying and often times you can get stun locked to death which is frustrating...The best thing about this game are the graphics and representation of the Samurai Jack world. You feel like you are going through an episode at times, and there is a decent amount of fan service to go about.I don't think this is a bad game. Far from it. I do believe it is a labor of love. I just think you need a certain mindset to get the most enjoyment out of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Samurai Jack: Battle Through Time

_childDocuments_.review: It goes without saying that this game is a love letter to all Samurai Jack fans. In a few words, this game is recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Samurai Jack: Battle Through Time deserves a lot more love and attention.Are you a fan of the series? Then you  to play this game, as the events within are confirmed canon, and written by the same writer as the series. Specifically, if you collect every collectible in-game it unlocks an alternate ending for both the game and the tv show. That being said, Samurai Jack: Battle through time is a fun game to , but not to 100%.  Luckily, you  need to 100% the game to get the alternate ending, just find collectibles in every level. Finishing the game the first time felt rewarding and nostalgic. Completing this game was an absolute chore, as higher difficulties do not get significantly harder, they just get more health and more of the enemies have stunlocking ranged attacks. The game also ran at a flawless 60fps on the Steam Deck, with no issues whatsoever.

_childDocuments_.review: As a long time Samurai Jack fan who watched the original episodes as a kid, I can say that this game stays true to the Samurai Jack series. Sadly the game is a bit short. It only took me about 8 hours to finish, but seeing returning characters and exploring familiar areas brought a smile to my face. The character designs are a tad bit cartoony, but I feel like they stuck with the original art style close enough. The only one I had a small issue with was Aku as he moved and talked like he was made out of clay. Overall, here is my review.Gameplay: Though the levels are fairly linear, you are able to explore around areas to smash crates, open chests, or find hidden items. Some items I was either unable to reach on my first play through or didn't even find. Jack moves and responds to controls very well. I had no issues with the game at all! There is also a shop where you can buy items such as healing, damage increase, damage resistant, weapons, and ammo. You can also upgrade weapons through training, sell items you don't want, or repair damaged weapons.Skills: There is a skill wheel where you can gain new weapon combos, combat tricks such as faster blocking or double jump, increase item inventory, and much more. Each skill requires a certain amount of blue and/or green essence to purchase. These are usually picked up throughout the level or from enemy drops. Some of the later skills start requiring gems that can either be given to you from characters or found hidden in the level. Don't worry about not being able to unlock all the skills on the first play through. Your new game plus will carry over everything so that you can continue upgrading and manage the harder difficulty settings.Combat: The combat felt great. At first you breeze through the first couple of levels, but the further into the game you go, you need to rely upon dodging, blocking, countering and attacking through openings to survive. There are so many weapon combos in the game that I couldn't remember them all. You are able to switch between 5 different melee weapons. Sword which is your normal basic weapon, hammer which hit hard and slow and good for crowd control, spear which attacks fast and good for closing in on ranged units, club which hits hard but is usually fragile, and fists which I honestly never used. There is also ranged weapons including bows, pistols, machine guns, and throwable weapons. Each weapon has a durability, meaning that if your weapon breaks it is destroyed and you need to use a different one. So be sure to swap it out and get it repaired at the shop.Enemies: There was a nice variety of enemy types in each level. Just to name a few there are the classic robot beetles, robot gators, zombies, and ninjas. Some enemy types do return in later levels, but it never felt like they were just there as filler. Each one brings different strategies to combat that you have to work around. Some fly, others stay back and shoot, some teleport, and others grapple. Dear gosh don't let the Imakandi tie you up! In later levels, the enemy will work together to make it more difficult. One such enemy combo I had issues with was a hard hitting hammer unit that had a long range spear wielder guarding his back.Story: Although this game is probably not cannon. I can see it fitting into the Samurai Jack series nicely. It takes place when Ashi and Jack are traveling back in time to defeat Aku in the last episode. But (without giving too much away) Aku foils their plan and Jack is lost in time fighting through waves of Aku's minions once more in order to reunite with Ashi. Everything takes place in this small window to make it feel like this could be a continuation of Jack's story and his struggles with the evil time bending Aku.Final thoughs: Though short, the game was fun and enjoyable, loved the voice actors and sound, levels were designed nicely, never ran into any bugs or glitches, and the graphics were alright. I give the game an 8/10. I would rate it higher if not for these couple issues I had with the game. 1. At times the game turns from a 3D adventure to a 2D side scroller. I believe this is to get you from one place to another faster, but I feel like the game would have been better if it kept its 3D visuals all the way through.2. If you are playing on PC be aware that there is NO KEYBINDING! You cannot change the key functions at all to fit your preference. I have read where people even tried going into the game files to change this but the files are empty. This option for PC users is currently being requested.

_childDocuments_.review: Samurai Jack: Battle through time is a surprisingly competent character action type game. It's no Cartoon Network site flash game and that much is for certain. It's got loads of content, secrets, upgrades to keep you entertained and a surprisingly deep and engaging combat system to top it off. Too bad that the game won't let you enjoy it as far too many enemies were "gifted" by those favorite tropes you like to see in every action game: super-armor, kiting, irritating AI that's designed more to waste your time than challenge you and boss fights that are less interactive than watching the actual show. More than 40% of combat time the enemy has a "blocking" state that is invisible to you. To figure out when you can attack the enemy is a trial and error kind of affair. You'll learn it eventually but it robs the game of its impressive combat system by having none of your sick styling moves matter because invisible, clinging blue shield. The game is filled to the brim with risk and reward mechanics like parrying and dodging, too bad that your rewards are tainted by clunky and seldom stiff animations resulting in your successful parry "rewarding" you with a flurry of damage towards an invincible enemy that punishes your parry after you complete your "reward" or your counter making Jack slide across the screen and outside the counter range making your "reward" a bunch of whiffed strikes at thin air that you can't cancel out of. You're better off cheesing the game the whole way through instead of actually learning how to play it, or so it feels at times. The story mode is a competent romp throughout the Samurai Jack series, sort of a last hurrah celebration that has you quickly shuffle through some of the more memorable scenes and episodes of the show. I've got no objections there, there's even a cheeky and sweet secret ending if you collect all of the Corrupted Kamon that, to some, might feel even better than the ending of the actual show. The boss fights are a severely mixed bag. Some of them are the best boss fights you'll have played in years (Scaramouche is a Devil May Cry-tier boss fight, seriously), some of them are ridiculous in terms of how uninteractive and busted they are. The second boss fight of the game, for example, is ridiculously hard and damage spongey, unless you find the one weapon that breaks it and just mash the button watching the boss' life bar explode in chunks to oblivion, reducing what might have been an interesting and challenging boss fight to a Pokemon-style Rock-Paper-Scissors affair. Sometimes it feels like different people designed separate boss fights as some of them are worth the game's admission price alone while some of them will make you groan and want to be done with them already. In the end, it's an easy recommend from me. It's not a fair game, it's not a balanced character action game. The camera will defy you and the game will become a first person game for no reason at all, the enemies will combo you into extinction locking you down in between two or three styling enemies with no chance to change your inevitable use of a continue, the boss fights will make you look at the clock, wondering when will the game graciously remove the boss' super-armor and let you play it already, sometimes your inputs will flat out not work and you will have to hammer your mouse 12 times only for Jack to stand still and get wrecked, you will be attacked by 12 different enemies with long-range projectiles with only 2 possible dodging attempts and successful hits from said attacks will send you full-screen back giving the enemy enough time for their cooldowns between attacks to reset before you get up. It's an unfair game, it's not an easy game but it never promises to be fair. It's clear that the devs knew what is broken in this game and what will make you feel like your very lifespan is having years being shaved off of it as your brain cells pop one by one as evidenced by the final level of the game. They knew the game was unfair yet those mad lads did what they did anyway. I think that was intentional. I think this feeling of exercise in futility feels Samurai Jack perfectly. Easy thumb up from me, next time try having your game have customizable controls on PC and maybe I'd like a feature where attacks come out when you press the button (I'm just messing with you, only about 3% of all inputs didn't come out).I don't know who asked your Samurai Jack game to be a Ninja Gaiden but that's what you got... Enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge Samurai Jack fan, so even though the game's far from perfect, I've played all the missions twice. So I'm confident in saying, that it'sa good game, severly hampered by it's broken upgrade system: 1) You start up with incredibly limited move set, which makes the game boring for a long while. In the end, there's enough interesting decisions to be make when deciding on how to attack, but it took me more than one whole playthrough to get to that point2)The game lock essencial quality of life upgrades far into it's skill trees - namely block cancelling (the ability to put your guard up before an attack animation eneded,). Another one is Bayonetta-like slowmo after a successful dodge - this one could work as an upgrade, but it makes the game much,much more fun, and I managed to unlock it at the final level. (on another note - there is no animation cancelling on dodges, which is a huge shame, as it would make the game much more responsive). 3) Unlocking more skills massively improves your basic attributes, like attack, defence and heal, to a point where after one health upgrade a boss went from one-shotting me to needing 3 hits to kill me. It feels terrible, as it goes agains skill-based gameplay. Moreover...4) The game is incredibly stingy with upgrade currency. If my estimation's correct, I will unlock everything there is to unlock somewhere in my third playtrhough. And those unlock are far from exciting - after grinding money for the last hand-to-hand combat upgrade, I will ad ONE hit at the end of my basic combo. For me, its shows lack of confidence, as the game got much, much more fun after I upgraded most of my stuff, and I keep playing it on higher difficulty levels, because I want to play it more - artifically prolonging in-game progression really hurt my initial impression of the game. For now, I give it 7/10. If I stopped playing after the first playthrough, it would be closer to 5/10. Reccomended on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: It's fine if you play games like this one, you'll see it borrows a lot. _childDocuments_.review: This is entirely reliant on the wikipedia dissertation, but apparently GenndyTartakovsky's initial assumption for the game was 'another loose cash-grab' recycling aspects of the show and heavily diluting them to fit some skeletal 'idealtype' of video game adaptation. Genndy didn't intend to have any involvement with this games development prior to a promising sentiment from adult swim: their stressing to the developers to make the game a genuine attempt at reconciling the cartoon with the video game form. So Genndy got his writers involved so as to maintain thematic and tonal cohesion between game and show. He really should have stuck to his initial bias.This game is arbitrary and unfocused, Jack's ethos becoming a violently distorted collage of properties the game developers engage on a purely surface level.The whole game is a misappropriation of Jack via: the most uninspired treatment of the show's mesmerising art-direction, inconsequential characters (who should be of consequence) and barely any attempt at story. And that essential action aesthetic that makes Jack, Jack is subsumed by an apathetic mechanical prison-- it's so limiting. If you love Samurai Jack, watch the show. If you love sword fighting games or whatever, play Sekiro. I really wanted to love this game, I love Jack, but it is penetratingly obvious this was some jobber work cashing in on a fleetingly relevant IP. I feel like the games marketing managed to somehow convince people otherwise. (What it does have are nice backgrounds (from a distance), your health loss is measured in battle damage and degree of hair-looseness, and it features the original voicecast. That's it.)

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of Samurai Jack so I was excited to play this, and I played it to completion. It really is an okay game, but I was left disappointed. The combat is fun, at first. But by the end it has kind of become repetitive and nothing new has been introduced. At some points it gets really hard out of nowhere, I lowered the difficulty level and some parts still randomly spike in how tough they are. The upgrades for the most part are really kinda boring and static. Grind X amount of points to unlock a new combo. There are some special attacks and moves that you can do, but are not told at any point. Maybe I missed some early popups, idk. I got through the entire game without realizing you can AIM your bow. I got frustrated at one point and looked at the controls and noticed it. One skill you unlock lets you grab and throw an enemy, and it says that you can steal their weapon. Does not tell you that in order to steal their weapon you have to be using your fists. That took forever to find out on my own.Some levels have secret areas that branch off the path but you don't know which is a secret and which is the way forward, and sometimes if you go forward you get locked out of a secret and can't go back. That is SOO frustrating!It's also really weird that they brought back the amazing voice actors to only do lines for the cutscenes and random greetings. You have dialogue with them that is just text. It's okay though because most of it isn't really important or interesting anyway, but you still gotta click through it. They also just stand there. Each one is an animatronic npc. It would have been so cool to fight alongside them or interact dynamically or do SOMETHING. The colorful characters is one of the high points of Samurai Jack, idk why they didn't utilize them better.And worst of all: THIS GAME DOES NOT ADD ANYTHING TO THE STORY. It's wedged in between already existing moments in season 5, and adds fanservice from some of the more memorable original show's episodes. Nothing new is added, nothing is changed. None of the returning characters really have much entertainment value, and I just found myself bored at their inclusion.This feels like a game I would have expected to see release with the OG show back in 2001-2004. And I mean that's okay. It's just really strange in 2020 and not something I would recommend.EDIT: After I 100% this game I can say that it does in fact have a secret ending which DOES provide something new story-wise. Everything else still applies though. It occured to me that this game might be an early victim of covid, which is unfortunate. I still would not recommend it at the full price of $40.

_childDocuments_.review: Well... that was a very interesting experience. When I was a kid I liked the Samurai Jack show so I was very excited to play this game. I started playing this game on the highest possible difficulty and was dying a lot that I thought it should be called "Samurai Jack: Prepare to die edition" but slowly grasping on everything that could give me an advantage such as new skills, some cheesing moves that can stun enemies I managed to finish it. Somehow I ended up playing this again on the new highest difficulty that you unlock after beating the game and even though it was almost the same hard experience I somehow enjoyed it. Pros:- Nice graphics that really well reflect the animation style from the show.- It gives a feeling that you are playing a "Samurai Jack" game.- Original voice cast.- Good puzzles and collectables.- Simple and nice level design.- Strange gameplay that somehow managed to make me get all the achievements.- Ending. Cons:- Combat is badly designed. Oh my... from where to start... . They added a lot of mechanics that are good on paper but in execution it came out terrible. I guess that they wanted to make a counter based fighting style but since usually you are fighting against a lot of enemies it is very hard to keep track on what you should focus to counter not mentioning that enemies attacks are not very signaling and usually very fast. In addition to that, enemies can cancel their attacks and instantly do some other action which again sounds good on paper but it is just frustrating in the game. What's more, enemies can block and evade your attacks. This gives them a short invincibility time that only adds to the chaos when fighting against a lot of enemies. You can also break the block but they can instantly go back to blocking or do some other action like evade... . Jack after hit doesn't have any invincibility frames to recover so very easily you can get stun locked to death since enemies are attacking nonstop from all directions from close and far range. The only solution to all that is to cheese whenever you can, using only moves that are safe and consistent and have everything calculated e.g. when to use special moves to reduce combat time to minimum. You can also do "supplies" runs (go to stage select and play a stage on the easiest difficulty) that I only managed to get familiar with after beating the game for the first time. This allows you to get all items that will help you stay alive for longer, or cheese enemies using distance weapons.- Weapon system. In the game you have a lot of weapons that fall into one of 4 types. It is cool and all but the sad part is that you have to repair them or they will break. Instead of wasting your money on those you can buy ammo for ranged weapons or throwable items that are very useful. You can also stock your money to get an upgrade in weapon type mastery... which again undermines the idea of having multiple weapons type because you will use only one type of weapons that you upgraded the most because without any upgrades those weapons really sucks, or at least on the higher difficulties.In general Jack's magic sword and his fists are unbreakable so the player is encouraged to use them.They should have just focused on the counter/ parry combat system, something like in Sekiro or Batman games instead of adding those strange game mechanics that do not work well. For some strange reason I really get to like this game even though I sometimes had some really miserable time with it. I guess Jack's adventure was also like that but he managed to get through it just like I got through this game...I can recommend only if you are a fan of the show or you like a game where you have to learn and cheese a lot, to proverbially speaking, "git gut".

_childDocuments_.review: i am really not sure how to feel about this gameit does hack n slash very wellbut its also ridiculously grindy, and if you do not grind for weapon upgrades by replaying the same levels multiple times you will find yourself backed up against walls with hp sponge enemies that deal overwhelming damage by the mid-point of the game.i found buying health items was screwing me over because it meant i couldnt upgrade weapons, and therefore was doing almost negligible damage at the halfway point, and instead i had to change my entire approach and just caveman mode the game while focusing only on sword upgrades so it could do actually decent damage. expect to grind. a lot. like way more than what should be necessary for a game like this. 10k gold for the first upgrade is a lot. 20k for the next is a ton. then 40k for the next???? you only make sometimes like 5k gold per run through a level, even with the gold+ item. really not sure what im doing wrong here, but thats a hell of a grind.the train boss in the aku city level is ridiculously glitchy and twice in the same night it flew off the stage and never came back, and i was soft locked. its been a known glitch since launch. they never fixed it. so have fun with that i guess because that boss is also super annoying and its a 2v1.the art of this game is great, but the gameplay seems lacking understanding to just add tons of padding in any place it can.maybe im just bad at this game, but having to redo the entire first half of the game to beat the EXTREMELY glitchy boss really soured my experience.also parrying in this game is incredibly jankim not sure how to even do it reliably and i have all the skills and know how to do them.also there are alternate weapons in the game, which is cool. what didnt seem to click until way later is that all enemies have specific weapon weaknesses and resistances.i appreciate the game trying to be more than just another beatemup, but i also think this game has a bit of an identity crisis. i honestly think its best when the game is just being a hack n slash against waves of robots like a musou, but then sometimes it wants you to 1v1 extremely spongey enemies (sometimes multiple ones) and i feel the combat falls apart there. it tries to be devil may cry or onimusha, but it misses a lot of what makes those games good. especially when it comes to the grinding. this game is GRINDY.this game expects you to replay the same level several times to get 1 of many crystals that only maybe a few chracters give you 1 of when you talk to them, per run of the level, just so you can level a single skill, which already has like 2 different costs on top of said crystals. just really bizarre and i dont know why anyone wouldnt find that really tedious.the references are amazing. the game genuinely gets me to smile and laugh. i like seeing these characters again. i love the writing. i just wish the game surrounding them wasnt such a jankfest.this is worth picking up for really big fans i guess, but if you expected refined gameplay i dont think this is the game youre looking for.also my god this game starts with a massive MASSIVE spoiler. just immediately. straight from the final episode of the show. so uh, get ready for that i guess.

_childDocuments_.review: Remember one and only rule that applies on EVERY GAME - Mechanics (rules) that targeted towards player makes project a GAME.In this concept, or shall I call it pre-alpha build, there's plenty of mechanics, but none of them works.Why am I saying that? Be cause this atrocity (I don't mean it in a rude way, but I couldn't came up with some other word which would describe this concept more precisely than this one) don't have ANY functional mechanics AT ALL.Visually it's very polished... ahem, "game", but that's it.There's plenty of mechanics that are broken, half of them works sometimes, others simply don't at all, and very few of them do work... but you won't find any use for them 'cause they're very situational. You most likely won't encounter such specific circumstances in which those would be useful, and if you DO fall in situations where you finally can use them as they are intended - this "visually appealing garbage" ignores it's own rules and breaks them all the time for your character and especially for enemies.As an example:Kiai move is your ultimate in short term that tracks nearby enemies and deals damage to them by automatically performing chain of attacks (or simply AoE ground slam if you're unarmed, hodling a hammer or a club), and these chain attacks TOTALLY miss small types of enemies be cause... their hitboxes are so small, that if they punch Jack standing in front of them, they ending up crawling below Jack's hitbox and it resulting in old gumba stomp instakill from Mario game series (and that's not even an easter egg...)Long story short - to kill these kind of enemies effectively you have gain enough spirit to use ground slam type of ultimate or... just stand on the place. Literally being AFK wins these sorts of encounters.  ᵇʳᵘʰ.Some of you who already played this game might say that you're going to die be cause of damage they deal.
