_childDocuments_.review: I have a lot of nostalgia from watching Samurai Jack as a kid and playing Shadow of Aku back in the day.  Gave me a lot of fun weekends and multiple play-throughs of enjoyment.With that begin said, it's incredibly unfortunate that less expensive modern titles can bring much more to the table than this barren and obviously rushed (Or lazily-designed) game.This would have been... "fine" for 6th gen consoles.  Not anymore.For one, A lot of the visual fidelity comes from the Unreal Engine's ability to generate these graphical effects honestly.  This deserves to be said considering they rely on this for the most part if you look at how little detail the environment actually has compared to a lot of games coming out right now.The levels are basic, almost elementary at this point.  Barren, monotonous enemy transitions.  Sections of 2D-style traversal that completely disrupt gameplay (what was the point of this design choice!?).  You can't run past sections of enemies, making you have to fight them even if there's no reason to do so if you just want to progress past the area.For being a hack and slash game, a lot of the combat is incredibly clunky in the beginning.  Yes, it does get better the further you progress into the game, but it doesn't really matter if the enemies aren't any fun to battle to begin with.  Even at harder difficulties, as long as you have health pickups, they provide very little challenge.At times, you get the rush of battling multiple enemies but it's immediately dashed away when you finish and the rest of the game's ridiculous design choices get thrown back at your face.Jack's lack of fluid movement early on, the sprinting mechanic and its delayed activation, the menu navigation, the inability to rebind keys, the barren landscape, the inability to run past sections, level designs coming right out of 2003.If you're a Samurai Jack fan, or maybe played one of the games in the past like I have, I highly suggest watching some gameplay or reading a couple more detailed reviews before making a decision if you *must* have it.If you're an average Joe just looking for a fun hack and slash, wait for a sale.  It can be a fun time but it's quickly beaten and will probably leave you with a sour taste after spending $40 bucks on it.If you like playing video games sometimes and are a working adult with a busy life looking to drop some time to enjoy your Saturday, I'd recommend looking elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're old like I am, you grew up with the rock solid lineup of cartoons from the late 90s and early 2000s.  I didn't get into gaming as much as I do now until my mid-teens so watching cartoons on TV was my main source of entertainment, and one of favorites back in the day was Samurai Jack.  If you know, you know, but the story of Jack's trials and tribulations through the past to once again have his chance at defeating the evil Aku was one of the best forms of media during its initial 3 year and 4 season run. presents itself during its 5th season, which aired 13 years after the cartoon's original showing.  With Jack and Ashi, one of Aku's “daughters” who had defected from Aku and fallen in love Jack, on the verge of defeating Aku once and for all, Aku desperately creates a time portal that throws Jack and Ashi far away from Aku.  While the two fall through the portal of time, Aku sends Jack careening out of the portal, throwing him into a section of time Aku controls completely.  Jack must re-live alternate timelines of his past and fight his way back to Aku to defeat him once and for all.Time travel should not surprise fans, but it's a nice easy way to check the boxes of all the interesting worlds Jack has done battle in.  There's a spread of old favorites like Aku's mines and futuristic cities, with newer venues within the show's 5th season that chronicles the show's timeline well.  Stages are jam packed with characters from the show, with the likes of The Scotsman and his daughters, Da Samurai, and Sir Rothchild all popping in to help Jack with items and hints to aid in his journey. artistically looks like a remastered PS2 game, and you can take that as a positive or a negative.  While the characters look fine and true to form, the stages, minus specific set pieces, feel very open and bland.  I do enjoy linearity for action-platformers, but besides some pretty backgrounds, there is not much to really enjoy looking at.  Each stage has breakables that include items like gold, throwables, and treasure, but it's like a sadly applied foundation to hide the blemishes.What  purely focuses on is its combat and longevity.  Combat is surprisingly deep for a system with two attack buttons.  Combos are done with light and heavy attacks, with the chance to parry and dodge, and timing these correct will slow down time and allow Jack to get a quick combo in.  Jack also can gather Kiai Fire for a special Kiai Attack which makes Jack invincible and does tremendous damage, holding these for boss fights are a premium “Get out of Boss Free” card.  Jack also acquires different weapons: clubs, spears, bows, guns, your own fists, and more are within reach; though throughout the campaign, I found Jack's magic sword the up and down best weapon to tackle fights.But the deep combat system has its flaws.  The lock-on system works to a fault where it will unlock after defeating an enemy, which does more harm than good.  The amount of enemies thrown at one time can be aggravating to manage with the faint audio cues for attacks getting overwhelmed by the rest of the ambiance of battle.  It feels almost like a sloppier , so be ready to get hit from off-screen a lot.  The real savior of 's combat are the boss fights, which are tightly tuned and challenging but aren't frustrating.  These boss fights show off how well the combat is crafted and offer a nice glimpse of what  should always feel like.When enemies are defeated, skill fire and bushido spirit are accumulated, which can be used to upgrade Jack.  The upgrade list is actually really extensive, with combos, extra items, and additional damage up for grabs.  You'll soon see that the list is too great for one run of the campaign to complete, so  implemented a score system to encourage repeat runs through the game's nine levels.  Scores go up with fewer deaths and items used, how fast you finish the level, and how many enemies you defeat.  Better scores net Jack more gold to use in Da Samurai's store where you can upgrade weapons, buy useful items, and repair secondary weapons.How much you enjoy the combat is going to directly affect how long your tenure is with , as the nine level story only net around 4-5 hours of gameplay on the normal difficulty.  Now are all those levels fun to play?  Sure.  Save the last two.  On Normal difficulty, casual players of action-platformers will cruise through, but the last two levels mark up a ridiculous boost in difficulty, almost as if the game expected a few re-runs on levels to grab more locked skills.  The last stage is wildly guilty of this, with a pseudo boss rush crammed with additional enemies which ends up being much, much harder than the final boss.  Beating the story mode does unlock special missions that include its own Boss Rush mode and an Endless Mode that unlocks after the story mode is completed on its Hard difficulty. is a weird enigma.  It feels like a remastered title that no one really asked for, and while I enjoy seeing one of my favorite childhood cartoons getting a current-gen rendition, it's sad to see that the love put into this game is not equal to the love I and others have for the franchise.  With a finely tuned combat system combating a very short campaign and frustrating design elements,  is the best  game ever made, though that's not saying much.

_childDocuments_.review: From what I can tell the developers actually love the original series, but didn't manage to nail the game mechanics right for fluid fun play.Good:The move-set is true to the original series, which for me is the most important thing. The visuals mimic the TV series too, in 3D form. The story is a simple revisit of some of the series' characters. The gameplay is like Deadpool's (sadly no longer on Steam), but slightly longer.Bad:The mechanics usually force you to counter an enemy for proper damage, which turns into a chore as you wait for one of them to attack you. Starting a combo on your own is dangerous and unsatisfyingly scratching the enemy as you slice/swing at them. They also don't flinch easily, so you're in danger of getting stun-locked for 80% your health bar.The gameplay becomes repetitive, and overstays its welcome a bit.Mixed:The large variety of weapons shows that the creators knew what was cool about the TV series. Sadly it feels pointless, as there's nothing exciting about the differences among weapons of the same type. The characters are fun, but sadly reused too much.If you're a fan of the series, you'd like this game. This is exactly the kind of Samurai Jack game we wanted to play 20 years ago (minus the spongy/tricky enemies).

_childDocuments_.review: I thought about whether I should recommend this game or not, as I have a bit of mixed feelings about it...StoryThe game is set after the events of the fourth season of the animation (the series had 3 seasons in the 2000s and the fourth one was made with the help of Adult Swim in mid-late 2010s). If you haven't watched the new season, things might be a bit confusing, but even then, there are a lot of references to earlier seasons, so you wouldn't feel like you've stepped in an unknown land and following the story is relatively easy. As the quality of the story, I think if you are a Samurai Jack fan, you'll love it, if you aren't then it's "whatever".GameplayFrom here, the issues come... I'm a firm believer of fast recovery in hack 'n slash games, because even if you are hit, you can still continue fighting, doesn't ruin the flow and this game sadly doesn't do fast recovery. You get knocked off and you stay 1-2 seconds on the ground, enemies aren't attacking and you are just sitting there. I felt enemies are unpredictable, like you stand there, waiting for them to attack, so you can parry, but they just snap attack, there is no winding up, so you take the hit. For some reason, someone decided that if you press block, while running, Jack will do a short dash, that's also a block, sounds nice, but you can't parry, so if someone lunges with an unblockable attack, but can be parried, you take a hit. Finally there is a small delay when you parry, which isn't good, but it was made like that by design, as you actually have an upgrade that makes it instant, problem is you won't get that upgrade very early... In the games favour (gameplay wise), I can only say Jack's attacks and combos are very smooth and nice to do.UpgradesCombos are locked behind upgrades, which is okay, in addition, you have more than just the sword, there are your fists, spears, clubs and axes, which is all nice and dandy, but say you don't want to use the other weapons, you can do that, but you still have to buy upgrades for them, because of how the upgrade paths are made, which makes no sense. As mentioned, instant block upgrade? It's a late game one. Probably the worst aspect of upgrading is the amount of resources you have to keep an eye for. You have Gold, which can be used in Da Samurai's shop, Skill Fire, which you get quite often, Bushido, which is slightly less often and variety of different jewels, which you find in chest or can be given to you when you encounter a character. On the last level of the game, I had 30K Skill Fire, but had no Bushido, so I couldn't buy upgrades. My next upgrade would be 5-10K SF and 1-1.5K Bushido, I could buy like 3-4 upgrades if it wasn't for that. In addition, jewels are scripted drops and if you are like me, who didn't return to previous levels, to farm jewels, you'd be behind on upgrades, again, this is not explained while you game. The game does not tell you this and I thougfht I'd get them as I play, a limited amount, so to make my choices for upgrades more important... Nope, just go and replay levels... I guess this is on me, but can't tell for sure. Make what you will of this honestly.Although I was fairly negative towards the gameplay and upgrades, but I don't think this is a bad game, just a flawed one. I guess if you are very good, don't get hit often, replay levels to get the better upgrades, the game can be quite fun. For me, this is a 6/10 game.

_childDocuments_.review: Just starting with this sentence. Review in short, if you like Samurai Jack and have seen every episode, I recommend. If you don't care about Samurai Jack or haven't finished it yet, I don't.This game is for fans. Art style, writing, voice acting, level design and weapons and such are all top notch. Gameplay, is not sadly. It's like a janky PS2 game, which I like, but it's frustrating to be hacking away at an enemy and he's not guarding, but his health is staying the same because the game wants you to take longer to kill him. During this time, he can still hurt and kill you. This is also true in enemy battles, which they can gang up on you during this time. There is also in later missions stun lock that will get you killed, with no i-frames for recovery at all. Just hit once at full health, and you're bouncing around getting hit with projectiles til all of your health is gone. It's worse in later levels, the first few levels I beat with no deaths , maybe 6 or 7 of them. The last couple I died so many times I had to lower the difficulty. I was sad to see that lowering the difficulty, much like upgrading your stats and weapons, have no effect on enemies really. They are damage sponges no matter the difficulty. The only difference in difficulty I see is that your special meter fills up faster for a bonus attack, and you get slightly more frequent health drops. This is pretty much the true ending to the series, which is why I played it, that and I love samurai jack. The intro, first cutscene, and last cutscene are animated. The rest of them are in game cutscenese, which look good to their credit. This seems like the type of game that will randomly be delisted, which is a shame as I had to buy it at full price, as it never went on sale during the past year and a half of steam sales.

_childDocuments_.review: Like Samurai Jack? Sick of all the Souls-like clones out there these days? Want an action game you don't have to spend all your free time playing just to get through the story? Just want to get back to the past (in more ways than one)? Then this is the game for you!Samurai Jack: Battle Through Time is a fun little hack &slash that's actually canon (more or less) to the series. It takes place right at the climax of the finale . The game follows what happened to our favorite 千ㄖㄖㄥ丨丂卄  丂卂爪ㄩ尺卂丨 during that interval.Key details:Positive:+ Original TV Show Voice Cast (Phil LaMarr is fantastic)+ Art feels well-translated from the 2D show to 3D models+ Combat is very satisfying, at least once you get a few upgrades+ Great visuals that work well with the combat+ Few, if any, "cheap deaths"+ Alternate costume (unlocked after beating the game, but appears earlier)+ Collectibles aren't too excessive and there's actually a point to them (I won't spoil it)+ Good references to the events of the show+ Runs pretty well, though one or two cutscenes were animated at 30 FPS for some reason+ A few challenge maps in addition to the story+ Difficulty can be adjusted in-game+ You can learn to jump goodMixed/Misc:~ Occasional platforming that feels a lot like what GameCube-era action games had, but it's not nearly as punishing~ Some fixed camera segments that are kind of cinematic but can make it kind of hard to see at times~ Very linear, level-based, minimal backtracking~ Nice weapon variety, but you'll be hesitant to use anything but the sword & fists too often because of the limited durability and ammoNegative:- Really short, like you could beat it in a single day short- Minor lines aren't voice acted (all cutscenes are, but lines during gameplay just have a callout play instead of actual lines)- Weapon durability on almost every weapon (WHY)- Camera can be a bit claustrophobic at times and doesn't recenter- Levels feel almost barren with few characters besides the enemies. While the game does make good references, only a few of the characters actually appear in the game, with most of them being either allies or enemies. Side characters and single-episode characters from the show don't appear at all.- Boss fights can get kind of repetitive, but they're still visually satisfying- Not a ton in terms of replayability, this is the kind of game you'll probably play once (or twice if you want to unlock the collectibles secret) and then put it down for a few years before playing again. If you're a Samurai Jack fan, the nostalgia will definitely bring you back when you eventually re-watch the show, but you still probably won't play this game all that often.- They left the theme song outSummary:Basically this feels a lot like a game from the 2006-ish GameCube/PS2 era of Nickelodeon and Cartoon Network game tie-ins, but pretty well-polished and with modern specs. Basically it's Shadow of Aku but better in almost every way, and it fits into the show's timeline.In short, is it worth $40? Probably not, but if you're a Samurai Jack fan and you like the classic action hack & slash style cartoon tie-in games of the mid-2000s, this is absolutely worth picking up on sale. It's the Samurai Jack game you wished you had when you were a kid, after the original 4 seasons aired.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's start with the story- Jack goes to a journey throught time in order to stop Aku and his sidekicks. some of the story and levels are based off the show but still feel unique in their own ways. I really liked the story and I think everyone who love Adventure-Action games would especially love it.Sadly, there are almost 0 interactions between the characters and there are not enough cutscenes, because they affect the story.I did connect to the characters but it really lacks in cutscenes that would have given the characters a lot, especially for people who haden't seen the show before they played the game.Art Style- Strikingly beautiful and unique. Every level felt amazing and every place felt fun to explore and look at although the show that the game is based on have a 2-D Cartoonish Art Style in it, where this game is 3D style which is disappointing given the fact that the game could have looks like the show, which would have been unique and beautiful!Additionally, when the player opens up the inventory, they'll be able to see Jack holding up an item or a weapon that is related to the category that they are at in the show's cartoonish style, which looks beautiful!Gameplay- Fun combat mecahnics that include weapon level up that feels unique and cool and a super good skill tree where every skill that you unlock with the game's collectible points that help you unlock skills, and every one of them feel unique and when you unlock every one of them you feel like your character has been highly improved. The game also includes many items that the players can get, buy, sell and use them to unlock skills. Some items heal Jack and some of them are used to increase Jack's attack and defense, or the enemies attack and defense but the game lack in these items, there are not enough of them which is disappointing it's supposed to have a lot given the game is a Hack & Slash game.Weapons: the game includes a decent amount of weapons that the player can get, buy and sell. there are swords, spears, clubs, guns, bombs, fists and more. Each one of them feel rewarding when used and each one of them doesn't feel different than other weapons from the same category which is good because than the player won't feel better or worse because of a weapon that he unlock intentionally. Every one of them feel and look super cool although there is durabillity on all of them except the Magic Sword and the Fists which are default weapons  It also doesn't feel like there are not enough weapons in the game most of the time.Level design- Really good and not linear. It has the basic dungeon crawler puzzling and rooms that are unlocked or locked by exploring and destroying certain statues.Every level feels big enough and every secret room is rewarding when found.Enemis and bosses: Every enemy looks and feels really cool and fits the game's world and story (which are taken directly from the game, which is good mostly because it might give the players who watched the 5 season-show nostalgia). Every boss is unique and is based on attacking agressively or rather shooting you in many ways.The game will be fun for people who have grown up watching the show or other cartoons, and is also good for people who love the combat and gameplay mechanics of this genre or even the kind of story that the game follows.Overall, the game looks beautiful but doesn't feel right in 3D and the gameplay mechanics are good but lacking in weapons and items. The overall feel of the levels and enemies are good but not unique most of the time. I'll give this game an 8.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: There was once a time when licensed games were are vast the ocean, and with that immense quantity came a lack of quality. Quality licensed products based on existing properties from other forms of entertainment were a rare gem. Nowadays, licensed games are much scarcer, and thankfully quality for those games have gone up. Samurai Jack Battle Through Time is one of those quality releases, albeit there are a few grave caveats to it.The story is pretty simple, although it contains spoilers for the final season of the show. Basically, Jack is sent into a timeloop where he relives a few of the events he experienced throughout his arduous journey. This also includes events from the fifth season of the show. It’s a trip down memory lane of the samurai’s life. The gameplay is quite similar to hack ‘n slash games such as Devil May Cry or Bayonetta, where you run between a series of rooms, each one containing a horde of enemies you need to take down before moving on to the next. You have access to your iconic magic sword of course, but on top of that is a variety of weapons of different types, both melee and ranged. Each melee weapon type has its own combos and moves, although they all have the same inputs across the board. In addition to this, you have a guard, a dash (which you can upgrade into a dodge) and a grab.For the positives, this game just feels good to play. Also when defeating enemies, they get cut depending on where you last sliced them. It feels great to clear a group of enemies and watch their feeble corpses get chopped in half and then sulk to the ground. You still have access to stingers, launchers and air slams. The weapon variety is nice and adds a little spice to the gameplay. Blocking feels great and you can also dash block and have access to two different forms of parrying. When Jack takes damage, his clothes become visually tattered just like in the show, until you’re running around in dirty rags with your unkempt hair flowing about. You also have access to an ultimate attack known as Kiai, which differs between weapon type but generally allows you to unleash an onslaught of barrages to take out multiple enemies. Furthermore, this game is incredibly faithful to the show and it’s wonderful to see a game like this honor the source material.As for the negatives, for some reason, all of your weapons except for the magical sword have limited durability, meaning that you could easily use your weapon too often and have it break and just disappear from your inventory. While you can have them repaired at the game’s shop, it just feels like a pointless mechanic that adds little to the game. In addition to this, I’ve noticed that Jack has a huge hurtbox while enemies have large hitboxes, meaning that you can easily get knocked back by the simplest of enemy attacks while doing moves that should normally be safe in any other game, such as the ground slam, with some enemies having attacks that can hurt you even if they don’t visually touch you, on top of some others just having attacks that reach way too far so much so that you can still get hit by them even when you dodge. Enemies also tend to guard a lot in this game and there doesn’t seem to be a way to break their guard other than to just keep wailing on them and pray that they stop blocking; meanwhile some attacks can break your guard or are completely unblockable, with no indication on which is which. On top of that, some bosses have invulnerable states where your attacks deal no damage whatsoever to them, and if that wasn’t enough, you don’t get a buffer from damage when you’re knocked down or back, meaning that enemies can continually wail on you and give you no time to recover. To summarize, it can be difficult to inflict damage and easy to receive damage, making the game needlessly more difficult than it should be. It definitely feels like the game is skewed against you. Also, this game has fall damage. WHY?!?!For some reason, if Jack’s health is depleted, he gets a little bit of health back and enters a rage mode where he gains increased attack. However, it only happens once so if your health is depleted again then you die, unless you use any healing item which somehow resets it and allows you to enter rage mode again. How did that fly under the cracks? Sadly, I wish this was the biggest complaint of the game. Throughout the game, you encounter various bosses from the show, but one particular boss fight is recurring throughout the entire game and it’s against Demongo. Sounds cool, right? Well, it is; for a while. You see, you fight Demongo way too often in this game to the point that it gets annoying. The fight involves Demongo summoning regular enemies you need to take care of, and when one dies, they leave behind a soul orb which you need to hit in order to damage Demongo before said soul orb vanishes. After a set amount of damage is inflicted, Demongo falls to the ground and you can wail on him. It would have been fine if you fought Demongo only two or three times, but to have a recurring boss fight that not only has ads but actively wants you to focus on the ads and not the boss is just the worst. On top of this, with each subsequent fight, Demongo gets more health and summons harder minions, and it’s gotten to a point where I was stuck for a bit on the final level of the game at the Demongo fight because he now had far too much health and summoned enemies you previously fought as bosses. It’s insane and it’s actively the game at its worst.I’m just going to come out and say that the last two levels in this game are straight-up bad. I did not have fun in them because they kept throwing exhausting amounts of enemies at me. The final boss of the game is also incredibly irritating; I spent an hour trying to get past him only to just run back to the shop at the beginning of the game and use all my money to stock up on healing items. One small aspect that also frustrates me a lot in this game is the fact that upgrading your skills is not straight-forward at all. You have two currencies to use, one of which is very common and the other which is quite rare. By the end of the game, you’ll have a staggering amount of the common currency, but you can’t invest in your skills at all because you don’t have enough of the rare currency. Worse, some skills require you to have certain items, and I never got the ones I needed ever; always the ones that I didn’t need. This is easily the least thought-out element of the game.I didn’t encounter a lot of glitches in the game, except for one major glitch where I died and respawned in a room that was closed off and I couldn’t get out, forcing me to restart the level from the beginning, which was not great considering that this particular level was not one I enjoyed to begin with.Despite all this, I still recommend this game albeit very softly. Do consider the negatives I mentioned because they could very much be dealbreakers. I had fun with this game, but I can definitely see others not because of some glaring issues.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty cute game that probably does require a passion for Samurai Jack. The passion for Samurai Jack helps balance your desperate longing for what you're imagining when you hear the phrase "ex-Team Ninja devs". This game has combat depth that's satisfying, but more satisfying in the relative context of the level of game you're getting, as opposed to the objective perfection of Ninja Gaiden.All that is to say: you'll be very happy with the combat depth when approaching this game as a passionate B-tier Samurai Jack tie-in game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty good, when you talk about graphics, length and story. The combat style is really adaptive and souls like. You need to dodge a lot during the boss levels, not to mention that you'll need to beat a lot of boss levels too! (there are 21 boss levels in total)The story does contain a lot of cutscenes, which is good in my opinion.You keep going to new places to explore as the story progresses. The ending was a little different than the ending in samurai jack's show on adult swim and I loved it.I'd rate this game a 8/10 in general.

_childDocuments_.review: It might sound bad, but Samurai Jack feels like an PS2/XBOX era style game. No. Not graphically. But in the way it plays.In fact, it feels like a very solid action game from that mid 2000's era. Think more along the lines of Jax and Dexter, Sly Cooper, and the like. Anyways, Battle through Time sends Jack... well, through time. Jumping from era to era, slicing and dicing your way through to the best of SJ's moments. Along the way, your old friends the Scotsman, Rothschild, and the Scotsman's daughters will give you items if you talk to them. Also Da Samurai is there to sell you items for coins.I only watched a little bit of Samurai Jack back in the day, so I only knew like... a quarter of the characters. But I could sense that there was close attention brought to the art style, camera placements, and overall feel that felt like a Samurai Jack cartoon.I will say the game does struggle especially in the later stages. For instance, it tries to encourage parry moves but the window to parry is pretty tiny. This can get overwhelming when trying to execute a parrying move when 5+ enemies are attacking you at once. (There is an option to increase that parry window, but I didn't get a chance to unlock it in my first playthough.) Also, it also struggles in accessibility due to not being able to remap keys.Overall, I had a great time with it. If you're seeking a hack and slash with a bit of difficulty and some of that old school collecting, then I'd recommend picking this up.
_childDocuments_.name: Samurai Jack: Battle Through Time

_childDocuments_.review: Samurai Jack: Battle Through Time was the game I didn't know I wanted right now. Story-wise it's a light-hearted romp through the Samurai Jack series with emphasis on the events in the final season. Gameplay-wise, it's a classic Hack + Slash. I played on the easiest difficulty, so that I could get through the story quickly, but I could see playing this game again on a higher difficulty for more fun! The highest difficulty is apparently really challenging. Still even on the lowest difficulty, I was impressed by the range of combat. The different moves and the different weapons kept the gameplay interesting. This game really does feel like a love letter to the show, and I was really impressed by the art style and the fact that they were able to bring back the voice actors from the final season. It's always challenging to transform 2D to 3D, and all in all I liked how it was handled here! I wish the story had just a bit more depth, but I still had a good time and it was nice to be able to reflect on the show that I love so much. _childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed samurai jack you'll likely enjoy this game. If I had to sum up this game in 1 word it would be throwback. Everything from the combat to the story, to the gameplay just makes this game feel like its a throwback. I would recommend that you find a way to cheat currency into the game and not take it very seriously. It's fun to hack and slash your way through most of the highlight episodes from the show as well as you get a different story that adds to the show instead of retelling. The plot of this game is very linear however if you were a fan of the show as a kid and you wanted a ps2 game but you never got it this is the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this out of nostalgia, but kept playing because it was fun. The difficulty can scale very quickly at times, but is manageable. I would've loved more voice acting when interacting with the NPCs, but it isn't something that bothers me too much and is something you get used to. _childDocuments_.review: This game gives you the nostalgic feeling of not only the series "samurai jack" but also the era of the classic ps2 type of  games. I would've preferred if the story was an entire recap of the series (season 1 - 5) and not just the hit moments. The game on itself is honestly really good, but lacks a lot of content, for example:-multiple outfits from the series you can change between-play as the other characters from the story-bonus-levels or challenge-levels-an arena similar to bloody palace (DMC-series)-vehicle levels (the train scene, the motorcycle scene from the series)Because the lack of this kind of content I don't think this game is 40 EUR worth, it's at maximum 30 or 20 EUR worth.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, Samurai Jack: Battle Through Time is an excellent game that you can play multiple times, and have a lot of fun playing. The gameplay is amazing, and the art is beautiful. The storyline is interesting, and keeps players tethered. Even players who didn't watch the show will appreciate the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Samurai Jack: Battle Through Time

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the show, I enjoyed the hell out of this game. Its a very simple hack'n'slash at first. But is gets better as you progress and get more abilities. The skill trees offer some variety on the combat and help a make things a bit easier. Something I didn't expect was how difficult this game is, I started playing on the hard difficulty and was suffering a lot. I switched to the normal difficulty and it was pretty nice. After beating the game for the first time I tried the hard difficulty again but with more abilities and experience. And it was awsome! So I really recommend the Master Samurai difficulty (hard) while replaying the levels, as it offers more enemy variety and a cool challenge. After you beat the game you unlock "missions", wich is a kind of arcade mode with waves of enemies to take on. The game is pretty short, and is not impressive, grafics are OK, combat OK, story OK and to me that was enough. Because this game didn't really need to be a huge thing. Its a short adventure and I love it.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I would like to say good job to Soleil the developers for making this wonderful hack and slash game! They did an amazing job of making it into a wonderful gaming experience for me!It's probably one of the most amazing hack and slash game based on a TV series that i truly enjoyed! The movements and combos are seamless when changing from one weapon to another.Though a word of warning to others who wants to play the game, the difficulty of the game ramps up quite high when you are doing a harder difficulty level. So you can probably try again with all your upgrades and stuffs.There are minor bugs which don't really impede on the experience of the game, so you don't have to worry on that.That's all i have to say on the game and if you're a fan of Samurai Jack, do buy it and enjoy the game as i have enjoyed it myself :D

_childDocuments_.review: I've been excited for this title since the announcement trailer and I've kept my optimism up even if there were small concerns concerning quality and any potential damage to continuity. Fortunately those concerns were gone as the gameplay is solid, fun, and makes good use of the "hack and slash" format. The skill tree currency can be kinda annoying to pick up sometimes, but the upgrades do have plenty of advantages you'll need later on. There is an interesting surprise for 100% completion although I haven't done it and I don't want to spoil it. However, the game is very satisfactory with the final boss and the other levels/bosses beforehand. So get your hot water, extra thicc pizza, sushi, haggis, whatever, and play this gorgeous game. The Scotsman said it was good, he was right!

_childDocuments_.review: The timing of this release was perfect as I just finished the show a few months with my little nephew (minus the mature season 5 for him hehe, he can wait like most of us). The graphics are different from the show but this is Samurai Jack come to life with vivid colors and various environments plus familiar baddies and friends from the show. The game feels polished and kudos to developer Soleil for really delivering on this, this could have been such a let down but clearly the creators were passionate about delivering a true Samurai Jack game. _childDocuments_.review: 40$ seems like a fair price. The game doesn't need an insane story because  we all know everything about Jack to begin with. There's not really anything more to Jack we could explore in a story, but maybe something about what happened to his friends after S5. Although, this game is more likely a test-bed for future games if it works out in sales.  The combat is very fluid and feels like the same system for Batman Arkham games. There's a lot of different combat options that keep the combat really fresh and you wanting to get more points to unlock them.  I really like how when you get damaged Jack's GI becomes more damaged.  There is also a special like ult that's also really fun in the spirit skill tree where Jack gets enraged and destroys everything.  Additionally, in the game there's a parry system like Dark Souls and all too.  The game can be anywhere from being really easy to being honestly kind of hard, it started to get hard for me around the point in which I reached the segment with the giant lava castle and rock people.However, I think I reached the point of the game where I've been getting pissed off. The random difficulty spikes are annoying and disrupt the flow of combat. Cheap ass enemies that stunlock you into oblivion are extremely annoying like the purple worms, and countering is pretty difficult. It makes me wanna close down the game super fast. The cheapness intensified towards the end of the end with Demongol(the most BS part of the game) and where seemingly infinite waves of enemies span. The stunlocking is ridiculous and you have to come prepared with a load of items not to die.Another thing I discovered late game was that bushido points get incredibly rare and so while you may have 30k or 40k skill points you can't upgrade Jack. Even though, the usual amount of bushido points you need is around 1k-1.5 k you will have to grind for them. Unfortunately, this makes combat  get repetitive because you can't get newer moves.Overall, I guess the game is average for me. I probably won't play it again although.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty cool platformer, great for anyone who is a fan of the show. I'm not sure if it can justify the price tag because I feel like I am more than halfway through after 3 hours, and I don't think there's gonna be a lot of replayability on this one unless you're going for full collectable achievements or something, at least in my opinion. The fighting is really fun and there are a good amount of enemy types, but ranged weapons are a little funky in this game and most weapons have a durability factor (which I don't really like... you can use up some weapons in a single fight). The boss fights can be tough, but having the ability to switch weapons mid combo allows for some cool openings and it feels a bit like FFXV in general minus the teleporting and magic. The skill tree is not bad but I feel like the progression system through there can be somewhat arbitrary. For instance, in order to unlock certain sword combos you will first need to unlock a hammer combo skill and things like that. Once you get a good amount of skills and weapon types, you will feel like a badass wiping out waves of Aku's evil minions. There are a few hidden items here and there but the exploration is pretty limited and you will most likely not get lost even without a map.  There is a camera focusing feature that is really cool too, which shows you the direction of your objective, and I don't think I have seen that anywhere else. Overall I would say its a decent and pretty unique game, and really came out of nowhere, but I might wait for a sale if you aren't a major fan of the series because it is also quite short it looks like.
_childDocuments_.name: Samurai Jack: Battle Through Time

_childDocuments_.review: Great trip down memory lane. Only just picked it up but it's pretty fun. I like the DMC-style. Playing it on Samurai level and some fights are pretty tricky if you don't dodge properly. Also, I can spend hours just sitting next to Da Samurai just so I can listen to his theme music, best feature of the game :D
_childDocuments_.name: Samurai Jack: Battle Through Time

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a Samurai Jack fan then you'll be sure to enjoy this game. The combat is entertaining and will keep your interest. I was surprised that the challenge and build potential was so specific as well as vast. Outside of souls-like games it's been awhile since I had to really manage my healing items and time everything perfectly. It's unbelievably satisfying when the gameplay and your plan match up exactly as you'd hope. Other than that, it's a huge nostalgia trip featuring several of the most iconic characters, factions, and locations from the show. I'm only 5 hours deep at the time of writing but I can't wait to finish my first run and start new ones to try out various builds. This is a love letter to Samurai Jack and it's a message that'll carry all throughout time.

_childDocuments_.review: The Game released around 11AM EST Aug 21. it took me only a couple hours to complete with pausing and stepping away to do something else in between. so it is short, but still filled with alot of action, it DOES have alot of the key characters in the show but its not as fulfilling as one would think and interaction is limited to short dialogue. its pretty much and quick playback of the show. despite what ive seen some youtubers post,(spoiler alert) there is No Alternate endings in this game that i have found. there are challenges to be had and fun simple combat mechanics  which initially will feel alittle heavy and clunky at first but as you upgrade the experience improves. i say for the initial price, combat gameplay and nostalgics plus the timeframe it took for them to put the game out i would say.....yeah its alright. i expected more but i know that it was just wishful thinking.****EDIT****so, i would like to amend that there is indeed an alternate ending that is achievable.

name: Dark Arena
detailed_description: You are the leader of the special operations, and it is up to you to find your way out of a very sticky situation - a genetics lab overrun by monsters of every shape and size. Using your advance suit and weapons, you must shoot your way through the lab, destroying the evil creations and saving the lab, and the rest of the world, from total destruction. It's humans versus genetically engineered monsters in Dark Arena, a futuristic first-person shooter that combines run-and-gun gameplay with strategic play and puzzle solving. The action roars through 20 levels. Players can access nine different weapons. Dark Arena also sports special multiplayer arenas for as many as four pals. The Game features Save States, to save progress wherever you want.

name: Timelie
detailed_description: Buzz Featured DLC About the Game Every second matters in Timelie, a stealth puzzle adventure, where you control time like a media player. Perceive future events to plan your escape strategy from the past, sneak an enemy, and manipulate time through this companionship journey of a mysterious cat and a little girl with a precognitive power. The Timeline ability gives players the power to control time just like a media player. Drag the Timeline left to rewind time and undo your past mistakes. Drag it right to watch your future unfold and gain you valuable information to change your past. Control both the girl and the cat simultaneously, timing their movements and actions to complement each other, escape detection, distract enemies, and ultimately escape the world they’re trapped in. Experience cooperative play for a single player like never before. Lose yourself in a vibrant world filled with colorful abstractions and surreal visuals. Explore strange realms filled with danger…but also discovery.

_childDocuments_.review: is a short puzzle adventure with stealth gameplay elements. It takes place in a mysterious realm where the player controls a vulnerable girl and a lovely cat. The objective is to avoid getting caught by the robots and escape this realm by making those characters help each other while playing with the flow of time.The difficulty of the game is just right. This condition makes the game playable by a wide range of players. Most of the puzzles are solved by the trial and error method. Instead of an undo option, the player is given the power to rewind time. Restarting a level may only be necessary on multi-staged levels.The stealth gameplay elements are based on hiding behind objects or in the dark, making deceptive noises, and making the right move at the right time. The time manipulation mechanic feels like using a simple media player within the game, allowing the player to watch past and future events to understand the solution for each puzzle.The characters are adorable, and the levels look mind-blowingly good. The music is quite impressive and fits the theme very well. The variety of music in such a short game is also noteworthy.The free downloadable content is slightly longer and much more difficult than the base game, and it is recommended only for the players interested in a real challenge. The base game, on the other side, is highly recommended for anyone who enjoys puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: Timelie

_childDocuments_.review: 100% achievement No. Yes (17 achievements). No. is a puzzle game with time manipulation mechanics. You'll be able to move your character and adjust it as you wish to reach the goal. It offers 46 levels with varying difficulty.- 46 levels with varying difficulty- Additional objectives on some levels for those who want some challenges- It takes time to learn how the mechanics work- Character switching tend to be unresponsive with mouseIntel Core i5-9300H 2.40GHz, 8GB RAM, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650The use of lighting is apparent to make the game look more beautiful. Buildings are simple-looking at first sight with a difference in colors and gradients due to the lighting. The main character, on the other hand, looks weird because of her sharp and big-sized eyes. Luckily, the game will mostly be played in top-down view and there are only a few cutscenes when you have to see her face.The game is a combination of several genres, mainly puzzle, stealth, and time manipulation. You need to avoid all robots at the level to reach the goal. Luckily, you are equipped with the ability to manipulate time as you will, enabling you to adjust your moves to precision without getting caught. A cat will also help you to distract the robots at some locations. The time manipulation interface reminds me of  where there is a play button on the bottom left and additional buttons nearby.It can be hard to learn how the mechanic works. There are barely any words in tutorials, forcing you to figure everything by yourself. Although the first few levels are easy enough to understand, I had trouble clearing some levels because I am not used to the mechanics. Take the cat's meow skill for example. I didn't know that his roar must reach the robot patrolling the area to lure them away. There were times when I was mad at the controls simply because I didn't understand them well enough. The game seems to be geared for keyboard and mouse instead of mouse-only. I didn't try controller, simply because I figured that it will be easier to move the timeline with the mouse. Some controls like switching the characters can be unresponsive sometimes. I was forced to use the keyboard just for that. Moreover, it's easy to click the wrong spot when you are using your mouse. I couldn't count how many times I clicked on the timeline, making me fast forward to a certain timestamp, instead of clicking on a spot for my character to move to.I finished the game in 4.6h. The rest of my playtime was spent checking out the  DLC, which I find to be hard to complete. The main game itself is on the medium-hard difficulty - you'll have to think hard at some levels, but it's not going to make you crazy about it.The most difficult part of the game is to execute everything with precision. You'll need to redo the same step over and over again because you are not fast enough, even if it's just by a few seconds. For those who want more challenges, some levels have an additional challenge to clear with some limitations. It will make the levels harder although you'll be rewarded with another cutscene at the end if you finish them all. These challenges aren't particularly hard if you are patient enough to revisit your moves over and over again.To be honest, I found the last few levels to be confusing and interesting at the same time. Some levels will be connected to the other, allowing you to finish a level faster or slower based on your attempt on the other level. I found it to be interesting, especially since it gives some insight into the non-existing story that the game has. However, it can be hard to guess which level the other level was referring to since the game never stated it. Moreover, switching levels can be time-consuming due to the slow loading screen and unskippable animation when you select a chapter.Hardcore players might find the game to be too easy, but they can always entertain themselves with the  DLC. To be honest, I only tried some levels, which is the reason why I didn't make a review for the DLC, and I found them to be more difficult than the main levels. There's hardly any room for mistakes in them - not only do you need to know how to solve the levels efficiently, but you also must execute them perfectly without any delay. I figured that I'll just stress myself over it if I continue, so I decided to stop.It might take some time to learn how  works, but the mechanics are actually simple. Levels are made in the right difficulty for casual players while hardcore players can take on extra challenges from the free DLC. The beautiful visuals and relaxing music also help to make you focused on the game. If you are the theorizing type, the game has a bit of story in the form of cutscenes, but since there is barely any word in them, I hardly can understand them at all. One thing for sure though: the cutscene at the end is touching, even if you don't understand anything. It's nice to see that the game can give an emotional impact without a coherent story. All in all, I thoroughly enjoyed playing , and I suggest you to buy it if you like the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? Yes, if you like unique, polished puzzle games.You control a little girl trying to escape from a surreal building, your goal is to reach the exit door in each room. To do this, you move the girl turn by turn, although you can just click on a distant point and she will run there, step by step. Deadly creatures patrol the areas and attack you on sight, so you have to avoid getting caught by them. The unique feature of the game consists of your ability to control time - you can backwind time any time. Your enemies always do what they did before, unless you divert/kill/imprison them. So the challenge of the game is that you watch what your enemies do, rewind time and then use your knowledge of the future to reach the exit. Discover where you are and if you can play with the little cat you meet. Really good puzzle game from Thailand. Manipulate time to reach the level exit.

_childDocuments_.review: Time manipulation is one of interesting video game concept. Even though it became a common genre in the past few years, there are few games that could deliver solid execution in term of both gameplay design and visual. Timelie is one of them.Timelie is point-and-click stealth puzzle game, developed and published by Thai people of Urnique Studio. Timelie tells the story of the young girl trapped inside surreal world. She discovers her ability to control time during her escape. She realizes the power as valuable tool to set up plan for escape route and unfold the truth of this world.Without spoiler, the game uses character animation, clear visual, and symbols as narrative. It results an interesting story without context to the audience likes what’s character motivation? And what challenge are they facing? I found it keeps engaging and very emotional satisfying at the end. The only problem is it can be vague for some people, but allows fan theories/afterthought to fulfill the story at the same time.Gameplay is genuinely a strongest point of Timelie. You firstly play as a young nameless girl to learn basic controls and understand overall gameplay. At the certain point, the game will introduce you a mysterious orange cat as controllable companion. The ultimate goal of each level is to bring both of them from point A to B safely. Sound simple, but not easy. Player also learns to avoid robot enemy’s line of sight using their movement and abilities. One can do something while another can’t.Speaking of abilities, the girl has ability to repair destroyed path and disable (kill) robot, but it’s not free and very limited. Each usage required power cube that player need to obtain manually in the level. Cat companion can meow to create sound and attract enemy within radius.The idea of Timelie is to set up your action sequence of both characters like interactive movie reel. The player can interact to timeline to observe robot enemy route. When should I move? When should I stand still? Can I use my companion to buy time for another character? These are things that keep popping in your head like bubbles. It’s thoughtful creative puzzle but well-design mechanics that allows free experiment. Got caught? Rewind and try another route. The more you progress, the more complex levels and multiple threats await player to learn level gimmick, trick enemy using environment, and sometimes think outside the box. Even though I stuck around 15-20 minutes in some puzzles, the execution phase after both characters finally escape level gives strong sense of satisfied reward to the player. Like reviewing your hard work.Timelie is a short game, but I think it’s fairly short and doesn’t drag player for too long to ruin overall pacing. You can complete the game within average 5-7 hours depended on how well you understand each puzzle without walkthrough. The game also features “time relic” as collectable by completing certain levels in most proficient way (for example; don’t use ability in level). It provides extra challenge and reward extra scene which is nice addition.However, it might leave some people for more like custom fan-made maps. I personally love some puzzles that affect the way you play in another puzzle as consequence. It’s pretty creative and has potential to expand gameplay. My last complaint is few puzzles are way too static and not much room for small error. Sometimes, you have to move precisely in order to avoid multiple enemies or match another character action.Timelie features its own art direction. It has simple assets, but gives clear visual to the player using colors, lighting, and animation to hint player how stuff works and connect without extra handholding. User interface is easy to understand and navigate. The game is powered by Unity Engine. The quality is polished and provides solid performance in my playthrough.Various sound effects during gameplay are also great, each object and mechanics give clear audio cues and indicates triggered action especially when player need to utilize movement to trick enemies. Timelie also has a lot of beautiful soundtrack to build up theme and emotional drive, well-crafted by two Thai composers. It fills with mysterious dark ambient, beautiful piano melody, and soundtrack of hopeful memories.Even though, I got gift from one of my friend. I’m glad to spend time in Timelie and willing to support more Thai indie developers for their creativity and video game passion. Timeline based puzzle that sounds simple, but execute effectively in both gameplay and visual. Highly recommend for puzzle enthusiast!
_childDocuments_.name: Timelie

_childDocuments_.review: Timelie is reminiscent of the Hitman/Tomb Raider Go games. You control a little girl with time-manipulation powers, on a grid style map to interact with various stuff, while stealthily avoiding patrolling robots. The time manipulation aspect makes this a quasi-turn-based puzzle game, but each level gets replayed back to you in real time after you complete them, bringing you a sense of satisfaction watching your character moving with such precision.Levels are incredibly well crafted, and some are indeed quite perplexing. Thankfully, there are only so many movement possibilities on a grid style map, so every level should be solvable by process of elimination, so long as you remain patient while remembering which steps didn't work.As far as game length goes, players should be able to complete this game anywhere from 4-10 hours depending on how good they are at puzzle solving. Being the completionist that I am, I went back and redid prior levels to net all the achievements, and it took me about 7 hours in total.Storywise, it's all rather cryptic, as the game has virtually no text, and the only additional clues to the story come in the form of glyphs. I'm sure there'll be others who'll try and interpret it, but that's not really my kinda thing.The only improvement the game needs is a better way to access the chapter selection screen. As it currently stands, it's unnecessarily tedious. But I suppose I understand the devs intention of wanting to preserve the time manipulation theme of the game.With charming characters and terrific level design, Timelie is well worth the play. Bravo to this Thai indie studio for creating such a well polished game. PS: If you find the game too easy, there is a free DLC with additional levels for the hardcore players, and I mean

_childDocuments_.review: I am a simple cat-slave, I see cat I worship.Joke aside, here's my first impression of the game. I will update this as I played.---3rd EDIT: 100% achievement:Forget what I said, I HIGHLY RECOMMEND this game to EVERYBODY who is currently, will be, and back to be, alive on this planet Earth. This game has the most well thought, designed, narrated, and soul-catching [beginning/ending] I experience in ages. For yourself, I beg you, please go into this game blind and see the 'Final Ending.' I promise you that it will be worth it.------2nd EDIT:I upgrade my recommendation from 'people who like puzzle' to EVERYBODY who want to see the best use of 'Time Manipulation' mechanic in both story and gameplay and overarching plot. Saying more will be spoiling.------1st EDIT:Some nitpick: -You can't skip/pause cutscene.---Graphic:There's a cute cat.First, the graphic and art direction is great. _childDocuments_.review: Pleasant isometric stealth/puzzle game where you go from one point to the other avoiding or distracting guards, collecting power ups, fixing bridges and opening/closing doorways. You can rewind or speed up time at any moment during a puzzle which actually works quite well in preserving the feeling of being challenged without also feeling frustrated, for the most part. Along the way a companion will join you to add progressive complexity but it is very much a single player experience throughout.Pure puzzle games aren't usually what I prefer to play, but the visuals and the time manipulation advertised drew me in. I was pleasantly surprised to see that the time manipulation did add an action element to the game to keep my interest, and as the levels got more difficult it just became more interesting. Most of the levels are fair but at a couple of points I was stuck for extended periods. At those times I wasn't even mad I just kept trying, thinking, trying again until I made it. Every victory felt earned and fired me up to tackle the next one.The story is vague to say the least, there are no words spoken and I'm not sure what the environment and what happens in the end is supposed to represent. If you collect all the relics and finish the last level again there's an extra scene after the credits which is a cliffhanger.The length of the game feels perfect, not because it has 'x' amount of levels and that's the magic number, but because none of the levels feel too long or repetitive, each one requires at least a slightly different approach, and once you felt like you've been mentally exhausted enough times, the game ends.

_childDocuments_.review: is a stealth-puzzle game developed by Urnique Studio and released in May 2020. Players control a mysterious girl with time controlling power and her feline companion. Together, they must outwit robots that seek to harm them. The game is a small package filled with well-designed puzzles, fantastic atmosphere and topped with a melancholic soundtrack. The puzzles never get particularly challenging, but they still feel satisfying when you figured out the most effective solution to a level. The game is brief (about 6 hours long to 100%), relaxing and never feels like it drags on for no reason. It’s the perfect game when you want to take a break from stress or from a more demanding gaming session. The goal of each level is basically to guide the girl and the cat to the exit door. Each level is a small labyrinth patrolled by robots that will chase and kill you if you enter their vision cones. Players must control the characters and navigate them to safety using many tools at their disposal. The game features a time bar in the bottom of the screen that you can pause, play, rewind, fast forward as you like. You can see the robots’ patrol routes and plan your moves by fast-forwarding, or redo your moves by rewinding. Each time you make a move, the time bar moves forward along with the characters (including enemies) in the map. The core gameplay is pausing, rewinding or forwarding time to learn about the enemies’ routes and avoid them. Both the girl and the cat have their own powers to utilize. The girl can operate panels to open doors. She also has 2 types of time-related powers. The first is gained by obtaining a white orb. The white orb can repair any broken floors or kill enemies on the level, and the effects of the white orbs can be rewinded. The second is purple orbs that repairs a specific part of the floor and the effect is permanent. When you obtain a purple orb, time reverts back to the start of the bar but with permanent changes to the level layout like inaccessible path becoming traverse-able. The cat can crawl into vents and he can “meow” to distract robots within the sound range. Basically every level is a combination of enemies, locked doors and broken paths that you must navigate by opening paths, avoiding, distracting or tricking enemies to reach your goal. When you reach the goal the game asks you to press a “play” button and it will show your moves like a video. It feels so satisfying when you watch your plans get executed and see the characters avoiding enemies by a hair’s breadth or create the perfect distraction and trap an enemy inside a locked room. Some of the levels feature extra challenges called “relics”. Relics are certain conditions that you must do when completing a level, such as not using the cat’s meow to distract enemies, or complete a level within a certain time frame. They provide extra challenges that require you a deeper understanding of the game’s system and levels. The levels are never hard, but you can still see how deliberately thought these levels are. The best levels that blow my mind are the few last ones that use the time gimmick really well. It would be a spoiler to describe it, but when it happened, I was very impressed by how cool it was. My only gripe with the gameplay that it basically become pretty predictable and easy, but the game never sells itself as a hardcore puzzler either. It might not be the game if you seek challenges that will turn your brain into mush, but the game is still fun. I never encountered any bugs, crashes or freezes. The game is polished from start to the credits roll. It runs perfectly too. Most of the in-game models are simple polygons, and the environment are drab, textureless walls and floors. It is intentionally simple to portray a lifeless, desolate laboratory hallway that you must traverse through. It captures the surreal and somber atmosphere perfectly. The girl and the cat are given bright colors as a contrast to the rest of the bleak environment. Both main characters are well-animated and their cute interactions are like a patch of light that symbolize their relationship with each other. Despite the darkness, they both give each other warmth and light. Sound effects are crisp and clear. I find some of the sound cues like robots being alerted are useful to time your moves to evade or trap them. There isn't really that much variety, but the sound is well done. Music is good. It reinforced the atmosphere of the game very well. The story isn’t really the main focus of the game. There are some scenes using some symbols that try to paint a picture of what is going on, but they are vague and don’t tell much. The main focus of the narrative is more of a highlight of the relationship between the girl and the cat. The cutscenes interaction between the two are always cute and adorable despite the bleakness in the rest of the game.  is a good casual puzzle game. It features a creative core mechanic with great execution. The game oozes atmosphere and charm, and the lighter gameplay makes it perfect for those tired evenings when you want to relax.

_childDocuments_.review: A very interesting puzzle game with time manipulation mechanics that you can 100% in about 6 hours.While the story is basically two 30-seconds cutscenes at the beginning and end of the game (and a floor with neon signs between chapters), the real twists and surprises come from the gameplay beats. Just know that there are things here that I think were never explored, as much or at all, in other games with similar time mechanics and it genuinely and pleasantly surprised me.If you like the art direction of the game and the concept of time manipulation as a gameplay mechanic, I recommend it. Wait a big sale if you think that the rateo money/hours of gameplay in insufficient, but do keep an eye on it if it piqued your interest at all.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a bad game, but it would work better as a mobile game. It basically plays like the tomb raider go game and at it's core is a creative maze. The story and themes feel a bit generic at this point in the game and the puzzles don't feel like they really do anything groundbreaking. One review site says it is a "nicely-made puzzle game" which it is. Windows Central says it is "One of the best puzzle games out there" which it absolutely is not. I'm also trying to understand why every positive review says the game is "polished". At this point in writing this review there are 9 uses of that word on the front page, which stands out as strange to me considering that the game doesn't feel particularly polished. If this were a mobile game it would be "polished", considering it is basically doing what tomb raider go did but with a much more focused style, but as a pc puzzle game it feels a bit repetitive. So is it fun? if you like mobile games. Is it worth $20? Not for me. Even with the well-done style and design, the puzzles don't feel very satisfying when they're solved and the game feels too repetitive to try and play more than a few levels in a row. As a mobile game I could see picking this up every once in a while and beating a level to kill some time. I don't think that level of fun really merits the overwhelmingly positive user reviews. It's like 600 positive and 10 negative at the time of writing this and I think that ratio is due to a lack of exposure to a broader audience.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm currently dealing with the loss of a most beloved pet, whom I saw as my family and my companion. That said, I did not expect to be so deeply touched by a puzzle game, one that doesn't even have a written story such as Timelie. It brought back good memories, but also the sadness I felt (and still feel) from time to time. It's safe to say I identified a lot with what I experienced in these 8 hours of playtime. :)The relationship between the girl and the cat she befriends whilst trying to escape whatever facility/place/realm she's held in is, to me, purely sublime. One could say that what the game doesn't deliver in written words, it does so in every one of its others aspects - Timelie doesn't *need* to have a written story. It perfectly conveys its meaning without it.As for the gameplay, the puzzles are diverse and complex, making use of mechanics that are easy to understand and play with, allowing people like me (who overthink the most simple of puzzles and end up doing everything wrong :P) to decipher and get past each level. Basically, you can control time by forwarding and rewiding the scenes, planning your route carefully after studying the enemies. The game allows you to try over and over again, essentially making it a trial and error gameplay. Don't be fooled, however, because it doesn't get boring or too easy to conquer - sometimes, what seems to be the simplest solution can have consequences later on in the story and actively affect how you solve other puzzles. Plan your steps with care!Visually speaking, what a stunner! The HUD is really clean and minimalistic, focusing on what's important: your timeline. The graphics are beautiful and the animations are adorable! The soundtrack is also good for the ears, quite atmospheric indeed. I'm glad I got to experience one of the best puzzle games of the last couple of years! Recommended both for the visual story the game tells as well as for the challenges presented in each level.

_childDocuments_.review: Timelie is a game that I wish I could recommend more than I do. I’m generally a fan of puzzle games so I thought this might be very much up my alley. Don’t let the isometric viewpoint and the stealth inspired level design fool you, this is a pure puzzle game. You have to navigate your characters past sentries while using switches to lock or unlock doors and use one character’s powers to restore broken elements in the level to open them up for traversal. So far, so standard. The interesting twist of Timelie is that it lets you rewind and fast-forward through time, so you can look ahead and plan routes around enemies, sync up your movements with their patrols and if you mess up you can easily go back and try a different tactic. I really like the way the mechanic allows you to iterate on your puzzle solutions very quickly and without much of a fuss. It’s a neat solution to the typical stealth problem of having to hide somewhere and wait in order to learn enemy patrol routes.The first couple of chapters were all fairly enjoyable. I liked how the game taught me its mechanics and how it explored those mechanics with its level progression. The addition of a second character in the form of a cat that allows you to distract enemies, and who can crawl through small vents to hide from them indefinitely was really cool. Both character’s mechanics complement the others nicely. And I especially love the way the game introduces the cat by first using her as an NPC before giving you control over her.What eventually soured me on the game a bit however were the last two chapters. Chapter 4 felt like the developers just grouped together the most frustrating levels that relied on a ton of trial-and-error and a bunch of almost frame-perfect timing between movements and actions and called it a day. It just felt needlessly annoying, so forgive me if I didn’t go out and download the DLC levels that promised even more of that frustration. Seriously, that’s how that DLC is advertised. It prioritized frustration by making the levels longer and harder to beat and thinks that this somehow counts as meaningful content.When chapter 5 started, I enjoyed how it recontextualized levels from earlier in the game and tasked you with maneuvering through them a second time on an alternate route while your former selves are also present in the level. I appreciate the concept of the game recording your own solutions and playing them back again later for you to find an alternate route, at least in theory. In practice however this turned into a frustrating mess because there’s no 100% guarantee that you’ll even be able to make it through a level, given that the game can’t make sure that the path you took last time doesn’t interfere with the possible solutions you have to employ the second time around. This only really works if there is precisely one solution to any given puzzle, so the designer can anticipate your movements. It also robs the puzzles of a degree of predictability which, given the time manipulation mechanic, should be part of the core engagement of the game and it reduces every puzzle into a quick-fire trial-and-error session where you’re constantly doing course-corrections. It’s unfortunate that the game falls apart toward the end like this. In more ways than one. Because even though the game makes it appear that you’re trying to escape from something here, there’s no narrative to be found anywhere. You could replace all the characters with random shapes in a blank void and nothing about it would change. Well, I say that, but that’s not entirely correct. The game does try to tug at your heart strings at the end when the cat dies, I guess, spoiler alert. I’m not sure it actually dies, but it has this sequence where the cat “sacrifices” herself to open up the final door and the girl mourns over the cat and tries to turn back time to get her back. But truthfully, I felt that the game really didn’t earn this moment, which is why I’m so nonchalant about spoiling it. To me it just seemed like a cheap way to elicit an emotional reaction from the audience. Sure, I like cats and I found her design and mannerisms cute in this game. But it just feels cheap and manipulative for a game to introduce something that a large portion of the audience is probably going to have a visceral emotional reaction to and then using that as an easy way to create emotional drama. Also, I’m not sure what that post-credit scene is supposed to represent where we get to see the girl wake up in her room and then get greeted by what looks like a prison guard, that just seemed like a total non sequitur.And while I personally didn’t go for all the relics, which rely on you figuring out ways to solve certain levels with some kind of unspecified alternate goal, like not getting seen at all or not killing enemies, I looked up the secret ending you get for doing so and it’s just a short sequence in the hallway outside of the girl’s room where she notices a boy who is probably implied to be the cat given their identical hair color. I have no clue what the developers aimed at here, it just seems like tacked on bullshit that makes it appear as if the game had a broader point to make or an actual story to tell when it doesn’t. I don’t often call things “pretentious”, but Timelie is pretentious. It pretends to be something it isn’t. Because what it is is a simple puzzle game. One that I enjoyed the first couple of chapters of but couldn’t in good conscience recommend because of the severe dip in quality as well as the quite frankly unjustifiable price tag. Yeah, you get free DLC with 30 additional levels that are apparently so frustrating that they take twice as long to solve than the regular ones. But that’s just that, more of the same and not in a good way.

But even then you could even just go in it blind and taking it without emotion, as a simple puzzle-game, and the game would still fully be worth playing: the concept of it is very interesting, and done with the right presentation for this kind of genre: you need to escape from those that chase you, getting to safety before things get out of control and you will remain forever trapped or caught.I don't want to spoil too much in this review, but I can say without reservation that it's a joy to watch the consequences and final result of your actions. _childDocuments_.review: A stealth puzzle game in which you must guide a girl and her cat companion through a surreal dream world that resembles pieces of a building, floating in an endless void and populated by robotic guards. The game features no spoken dialogue and is deliberately vague on plot details, leaving it up to the player to figure out the story (but who needs story when there's a cat that sits on your head?).In each level, the girl and/or the cat must navigate through a series of rooms and corridors to the exit. The girl can operate keypads to open and close doors, as well as collect gems that let her repair holes in the floor; meanwhile, the cat can fit through tiny crawlspaces and meow loudly to lure robots away from their posts. Some robots simply follow a basic patrol pattern while others take more complicated routes, but should one of them spot you, it will chase after you until either it reaches you and attacks or it loses track of you. You'll have to keep on your toes to guide the characters safely through each level.This is done by visually planning out the characters' routes beforehand, then watching them do it for real once successful, similarly to . What sets this game apart, though, is the timeline bar that lets you freely rewind or fast forward through time. This lets you alter the characters' routes and actions at any point, making it easy to correct mistakes, experiment with different paths, or sync the characters' movements to solve the levels faster. Some levels feature a collectible that can be obtained by speedrunning the level or not using a certain ability, encouraging you to rewind and try different tactics. Other levels force you to get the characters to the exit within a strict time limit, either via a robot shutting the only door to the exit after a while, or because the entire level is slowly vanishing from existence. Plus, if you find the base game to be too easy, there's always the free Hell Loop DLC to give yourself a real challenge.Time is infinite, yet we only have a limited amount of it to spend. Our choices in the past will inevitably affect our options in the future.  has built a game around these concepts, and pulled it off brilliantly.
