_childDocuments_.review: I think this is a perfectly fine game if you know what you're getting but can also lead to disappointment if you're expecting something different. Since Steam doesn't allow a mixed recommendation & the rating is high enough that a single negative recommendation wouldn't really affect it, this is submitted as negative.The game's description talks about time manipulation, but that's more window dressing than gameplay. Gameplay-wise, this is a sequenced move game, where the goal is to time your planned moves on the grid to the enemies' in order to metaphorically get keys, flip switches, and avoid getting caught.  Think any of the Go games — Hitman Go, Lara Croft Go, Deus Ex Go — and you'll get the idea.If you know this and you like these types of games, then it's a perfectly fine example of them. The additional twist of multiple characters that you have to control simultaneously adds a new challenge, though it is also occasionally annoying. If you're expecting a game with the time-manipulation to be more involved in the gameplay, you'll probably be disappointed.The closest I've come to actual time manipulation are the occasional objects that touching will reset the level back to the beginning, only with some of the metaphorical keys having already been used. ["Metaphorical keys": there are glowing white cubes that let you visually reverse time on parts of the map, restoring damage & allowing you to progress past a previously inaccessible route. Despite the graphical trappings, they're effectively just a variation on keys & locked doors.]At this point someone is going to bring up the rewind functionality that lets you move backwards in the move sequence — and you're going to use it a lot. Since any action automatically unpauses the game, you'll need to rewind a lot in order to get the two characters to act simultaneously. [e.g. Enter a move for character #1, which automatically unpauses time. Rewind back to when you entered the move, which also serves to pause time. Swap to character #2 & enter their move. Time again unpauses only both characters now move.] But rewind is 100% ordinary in these sort of sequenced move games. It's just normally not as noticeable.(Maybe there's something more further into the game. Don't know and it hasn't grabbed me enough to care at this point.)Graphics are ok. Something closer to the game's concept/store art would have been more pleasing.As others have said, this would have been a great mobile game, as these types of games fit well into a play style of picking it up, playing a level or two, and then putting it down.A good sequenced move game with some fresh ideas [having to move simultaneously more than one character] but the time manipulation feels more like theming than a gameplay element.

_childDocuments_.review: The time manipulation is really fun to play around with, and the game makes great use of this concept. Even though the game is around 5 hours long (shorter if you use a guide) it was still providing enough new mechanics to keep the puzzles interesting.There are some extra challenges called relics which you earn for completing the level in a certain way, and you need to beat all 15 of these to unlock the secret ending. A couple of them bring back a really interesting concept regarding time-loops, but these might be really difficult to solve on your own without knowing the trick. I recommend looking up a guide to check what the requirements are, but solving them yourself afterwards. Other criticisms is that the game does not mark in the level select menu which levels you need to replay, as well as not telling you what the parameters are (You pretty much have to look up a guide). Also the story was a bit weak, but I did enjoy the girl's relationship with the cat, and the secret ending was kinda cute.

_childDocuments_.review: Timelie is a beautiful and polished puzzle game. The puzzles are well crafted; any trouble I may have had solving them felt like it was on me. The mechanics are wonderfully simple. Each puzzle has a maximum time to finish it in, however you can forward and rewind time as much as you'd like to redo your plan. Rewinding is either step by step or you can it back to any point of time on the bar at the bottom. Encountering an enemy just forces you to rewind, not restart which makes the game very forgiving of mistakes. My playtime: 4.8 hours straight to end. 6.7 hours to complete everything.Collecting the relics gets you a cut scene after the credits.

_childDocuments_.review: Timelie is an isometric puzzle game that consists of manipulation of time, surrounding objects, and enemies in order to escape the various chambers.The visuals and character design are simplistic in a good way. The puzzles are well thought out. I liked solving them. They become difficult as you progress further. There is an intro chapter, four main chapters, and the fifth chapter, which is quite small. Each chapter comprises various chambers or levels.A couple of puzzles may become frustrating as you have to be perfect by 1/10th of a second. I had to refer to an online guide to get through them.There are no voice-overs, no text. The story is told using simple cutscenes and some vague symbols. I didn’t get it that much, to be honest. The ending was a bit emotional. The music is quite excellent, and the sound design also serves its purpose.You are accompanied by a cat that helps you solve the puzzles. Cute touch.The movement is grid-based. I played with a gamepad without any problem. The gameplay felt smooth. There is only one enemy type: aggressive robots. You’ll play hide and seek with them throughout the game.There are secret relic challenges in 15 chambers. You have to complete some chambers a certain way to get these relics. No worries. There is a chapter select option. And you can select any chamber you wish to play again. You may need to refer to a guide (for some of the challenges). After getting all the relics, you will unlock a small secret cutscene after the end credits.The achievements are chapter completion and challenge-related. Make sure to watch the credits till the end after completing all the challenges. It may take around 8 to 9 hours if you are going for all the achievements.After finishing the main game, you may revisit the chapter select option and access the extra DLC levels called “Hell Loop." This DLC is free to add to the library. The DLC has 30 levels with no story. I’ve played 3-4 levels and didn’t bother going further. Because the difficulty is quite absurd with these levels. They require so much trial and error with so many variables. I didn’t like it. Totally time-wasting and rage-inducing. I’m glad that it was not required for 100% game completion. Otherwise, it would have ruined my experience.Overall, I have enjoyed my time, with some frustrating moments here and there. If you are into challenging puzzle games, you may get this on sale.My verdict: 6.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Timelie is a game that I had pleasant time with. Usually I am not a fan of stealth games or strategy games because I find them either too anxiety inducing or boring, but that wasn't the case for this game. I found myself enjoying this game pretty early in and as I started becoming excited about what was in the next room instead of stressed over being caught. I’ve never enjoyed playing a stealth game before but this one won me over with it’s cute characters, nice gameplay, and beautiful visuals. I specifically loved the magic effects of this game, they were very pretty. It sounds kind of funny to say that a stealth strategy game is relaxing and a comfort game for me, but I think that’s why it’s great. It’s a very cute and comfy game with a cool futuristic aesthetic.I only have one or two critiques of the game. While I felt like the animation on the models of all the characters were very expressive and well done, that was not the case for facial expressions. The main character’s face didn’t have any emoting or blinking throughout the game. It was incredibly unnerving in a way that I don’t think was intentional (especially during the cut scenes). I would be very grateful if either the developers coded or a fan moded blinking and/or expression animations onto the main character. Also, the ending (including the secret one) felt a little anticlimactic and disappointing in comparison to the rest of the game to me. Overall, while it can be a little grindy for those who want the secret ending, it was a well designed game that was very pretty.

_childDocuments_.review: charming little iso stealth puzzle game!timelie (rhymes with lime pie)'s selling points are its polished, beautiful artstyle; simple-yet-moving story with everything shown, not told; and a gimmick of controlling two characters simultaneously, dragging a playhead around on a timeline (timelie?) to synchronise their movements.its greatest weakness is that it's an iso stealth puzzle game, the market for which is... slightly oversaturated; however, its twist on this concept keeps it interesting and fun.of course, not every game mechanic is introduced at once, and it starts off rather uninspiring in the first chapter, which might cause some players to abandon it; i was tempted. but past its weak beginning, it's excellent! most puzzles do a good job of introducing a new challenge that's satisfying to solve, with a few forgivable blips scattered onto an otherwise smooth difficulty curve. no one section or mechanic overstayed its welcome, and the puzzles feel nonlinear, with a few different solutions in the best ones, and some crazy interplay when your previous solutions are remembered in new levels.timelie isn't a must-play paragon of puzzle games, and it could've explored more thoroughly the mind-bending, accumulating puzzles in the final act. its mechanic isn't particularly new, as braid, thinking with time machine, and others have explored similar concepts. however, it confidently stands on its own beside those, and is certainly worth a shot if you're into that genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Timelie is pure stealth + puzzle gameplay not diluted with story, dialogue or cutscenes. Thus, players have to embrace stealth instead of spamming abilities and hoping something will work out.
_childDocuments_.name: Timelie

_childDocuments_.review: Timelie deftly leverages time manipulation to create puzzles with precision. The ability to rewind and fast forward freely gives the player time to think and experiment, making it possible to tackle challenges without the frustration of losing progress. In fact, failure doesn't even feel like a factor at all, which is genuinely refreshing. I did get stuck at times, but I appreciated the simple gesture of not having it rubbed it in my face with "You Died" or punitive load screens.There's a small dose of bittersweet story to enjoy as well, but the intricacy and novelty of the puzzles are what set it apart. Don't miss this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Timelie

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzle mechanics are original and well thought-out, but the controls are clumsy, and you often cannot zoom out enough to see the whole puzzle board. The puzzles aren't too hard, though; I could solve them all rather quickly, though I reached the ending with only 6 of the 15 relics. Some of the puzzles are great, forcing a brain shift that suddenly makes you go, "Aha!" Others are more about timing each step one by one, which will challenge your patience more than your intellect.The graphics are beautiful and the soundtrack haunting, but the story is more puzzling than the game itself, even if you get to the "secret" ending, which requires that you collect all the relics. Maybe things are made clearer in the  DLC, though. I haven't played it yet.

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay and UI are decent.  The graphic are nice enough.  The puzzles are okay.  Timelie is not a bad game.  It could be a LOT better, but it's not terrible. There is zero emotional payoff, even with all relics collected and the post credits "real" ending.  No questions get answered.  All the seemingly meaningful symbols you walk past turn out to be meaningless graffiti.  The whole thing ends up feeling unfinished and anticlimactic.  If I hadn't gotten it as part of a Humble Bundle, I'd be demanding a refund.

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a long long time since a puzzle game is able to make me squeeze this much brain juice....This game live up to its name, you play the game in a time line with the ability to lie in time. Most of these type of games out there with time rewind are super linear and predictable. But this game brings the plot one rank higher. You are not only solving a puzzle in timeline, you have to avoid certain time paradox caused by your own action. In later part of the game you will revisit previous puzzles with a pre-recorded you in it repeating a play through from your past, you need to avoid contacting your past image while solving the new objectives. It gets really complicated when there's more than one you in the same timeline. If you are a messy solver, you will be causing real headaches and trouble for the future you. It's amazing!The game music is great by itself, worthy to buy the soundtrack as collection imo. And it fits the game mood perfectly!It's been years since I felt so much fun in playing a puzzle game. Really really recommend this master piece! :3And they even provide a free DLC for hardcore puzzle solver... that Hell Loop DLC lives up to its name too. It's certainly hell mode! :3Honestly speaking, this DLC, although has nothing to do with the main story line... is the true honey jackpot of this game.. You will find yourself spending double, or even triple the time you use to finish the main game on these hell loop stages. _childDocuments_.review: Imma be honest: The cat is adorable and probably composed like 50% of my enjoyment of this game. Hits me right in my weak spot, ooof.Focusing on the rest though:Cool game overall. The general idea is to sneak past robot sentries and proceed from one level to the next. You have the ability to control time -- using future knowledge to modify and fine-tune your past actions -- and you also have a cat companion who can fit through small vents and meow to distract nearby sentries temporarily.The difficulty is about average, though there is a bit of extra challenge in the side-achievements for completing certain levels under tougher constraints (speedrun, no meows, no kills, etc). The soundtrack is very fitting - it's atmospheric, immersive, and easy on the ears. No Last Eternity in particular is a fantastic theme song.At first, I was bummed that the base game was so short (38 levels). By the time the game starts to hit its stride, it's over. But there is a free DLC (Hell Loop) that offers 35 additional levels -- most of which are harder than the hardest level in the base game. So if you want more, the option is there.

_childDocuments_.review: In the wide world of puzzle video games, Timelie stands out as being truly one of the greats. The mechanics are a wonderful mix of discrete locations with a continuous temporal mechanic that makes puzzles feel both deliberate and cheesy, in the best possible way. Tie all of this in with an end-game twist reminiscent of The Pedestrian, and we've been given a true hidden gem in the puzzle game genre.Timelie is not, however, without its shortcomings. The cutscenes are frequent, slow, usually uninteresting, and annoying, though easily skippable. Gameplay can feel slow as well, particularly before I got better with the controls. These problems overall were particularly pronounced in the beginning of the game, but got significantly better over time as puzzles got harder.Despite these shortcomings, by the time I completed Timelie, I couldn't help but be in awe of the game we were given, and I believe it is absolutely worth full price despite only taking me ~5 hours to complete.

_childDocuments_.review: NOTE: This review concerns the base game and does not include the "Hell Loop - DLC Puzzle Pack"."Timelie" can be summarized as "short, but sweet". This puzzle game consists of you navigating one-to-two characters towards the end of each level, while avoiding getting caught by enemy sentries roaming in each level. The key mechanic is the ability to control time, letting you undo actions that lead to failure and observe enemy sentry movement patterns as time progresses. There is just enough challenge in each level to prevent you from blasting through them with ease yet not too hair-pulling difficulty in most levels. Extra challenge lies in "relics" that are awarded in some levels after completing certain actions. These relics add an additional layer of difficulty and feel great when you find the right combination of actions to get them. Performance-wise, the game performs well on both Mac and PC. The soundtrack provides effective atmospheric tunes that enhance the overall experience. The art style is simple yet effective. Character models and animations look great. This game will satisfy a lot of people from different preferences for games.Not all games are perfect, and there are some issues with "Timelie". There are some levels that are mentally taxing and do require you to explore a multitude of options to find a correct solution. These usually amount to trial and error, repeating actions with minuscule changes until you find an optimal pattern. It's not often, but there are such moments. Some quality of life improvements are missing, such as the ability to chapter select from within the menu and some cut scenes not being skippable. The lack of indicators in the chapter select to see if a level already has its relic obtained is a confusing UX issue, but this will only apply to achievement hunters. A bar at the bottom of the screen akin to a YouTube progress bar lets you skip chunks of time, but sometimes the bar will think you clicked on it when you actually clicked on the environment, skipping time in large chunks with no way back to your original timestamp. Furthermore, with the addition of two controllable characters, sometimes it is not obvious which character you are controlling. While there is a story in this game, it's mostly up to interpretation - take that however you will.Despite some negative points here and there, this is a great package all around. A comfortable distraction at worst, and a fun brain-scratcher at best.

_childDocuments_.review: As far as puzzle games go Timelie is one of the better ones. It has a neat atmosphere, very interesting mechanics for puzzles, and some impressive music.The gameplay is simple: press buttons and stand on pressure plates to open doors, avoid enemies, use some limited abilities to influence the way you play, and move back and forth time to try and retry approaches in an attempt to reach the exit of each level. The usage of time as a mechanic is done extremely well, it forced me to think ahead, observe patterns, and plan in a way I had not done before. And when I figured out that some of the puzzles utilized previous mission’s results to influence your current mission I found that absolutely fascinating. The game really got interesting when it gave you not only the main character to control but a cat as well, meaning you had to get both to the end using different paths and utilizing their unique abilities to solve puzzles. It all works really well and I found the game to be a little challenging at times, especially if you are going for the secret ending, but overall I found that I really enjoyed how the game played. Of note, I attempted to play the second harder run of the game and found that ♥♥♥♥ to be absolutely grating, if you are really into this game I think that it is cool that they offer a massive challenge but it was not for me. But yeah, it was really fun, it was a very unique approach to puzzles and I can’t think of many games that top it. As for the story, it is minimalistic; no text, no voice acting, just visuals. It was not really clear what is happening, but the emotions built are pretty solid. I am a real sucker for cats and building a bond with the stray cat in the game was cute to see. If you came for a story I think you will likely be disappointed, but personally, I thought it was an interesting experience to try and interpret.The sound design for this game is pretty good in my opinion. The in-game sound effects are limited, but what they have is good. As for the music I found it to be pretty good overall, a lot of it is ambient, but I thought it was all well composed. Best of all though was the song at the end credits, I thought it was phenomenal and went ahead and picked it up. If you are not interested in the game I at least suggest that you look it up, No Last Eternity by Pongsathorn Posayanonth and Aun Jessada (it has both an English and a Thai version, both are good though I prefer the English because I like the lyrics as well). Overall I never felt like running my own music which is always a great sign, so I was very happy with the soundtrack.Graphically this game is very simple, it reminds me of Pokémon games in the way that it is styled (specifically the main character). What had the most effort put into it though was the environments, and overall I think that they are done wonderfully. I do feel that the game was not as colorful as it could have been so it generally feels pretty muted, but I did find that it made some of the neon colors really pop, so perhaps it was for the best. The atmosphere the game has though is really good, it is always hard to describe a visual feel but this one feels really good, it is just dark enough, it has a unique sci-fi feel, and it feels strong emotionally. Overall it is not a masterpiece, but it is visually appealing nonetheless.I liked Timelie a lot, I think it is easily one of the best and most unique puzzle games I have ever played. It was a bit challenging and I did have to get some help on getting the bonuses to get the secret ending, but I think this game is well-balanced in its base game difficulty. I did not have any really big complaints, I think this is a wonderful game and was really happy to have played it. So if you are a fan of puzzle games I think that this is a must-play.

_childDocuments_.review: A polished puzzle game in the guise of a stealth game.  Plot your path through the level...but don't worry if you get caught, because you can just rewind time to where you made your mistake and replot your path from that point without having to redo the entire level.It reminds me a bit of when Dr. Strange did the whole 14 million futures thing.  You get to pick the one that works!There are hints of a storyline here and there.  Where is this mystery place?  Is it physical or metaphorical?  What do those runes mean?  Whats the deal with that cat?  And wait...I just collected the 15 relics by completing special objectives during the missions...but what does that ending MEAN?All in all, it gave me about 8 hours of playing total.  It is worth noting that if you get into the game the dev also made some free DLC with difficult levels that you may enjoy too!All in all, I enjoyed it.  Difficult enough to be a challenge and engrossing, but the time rewind feature keeps it casual.  Definitely worth a shot!

_childDocuments_.review: What a fantastic little puzzle game. Though short, this is now in my "Top 10 Puzzlers" of all-time, next to "The Sexy Brutale" and heavy-weight "The Talos Principle", to give an idea of how much I enjoyed it.Solving a puzzle here feels like cheating on a Stealth-Action game; the main mechanics is that you can rewind or forward time at will, so you can time narrow escapes perfectly. Once you solve a level, you can then watch the action unfold in real time, and it looks really cool, with all those impressive moves you carefully built. This might sound repetitive (there is a lot of trial and error for your timings if you want to solve a level in a time-efficient way), but the well thought-out interface makes it very easy to advance or rewind a few frames at a time until you get it just right.Also, the puzzles had a perfect difficulty level for me -- they had me thinking hard at times, and every so often I needed a new idea, but I never had to look up solutions of anything. The story is only hinted at, but has a few well done dramatic moments.Finally, I thought the last few puzzles to be brilliant -- they caught me off-guard, but adapting to the new challenges made up for great playing moments, the kind you want to tell other people about.Score: 88/100.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: GoodClear Time: 5~ Hours100% Time: 5~ HoursSummary: An absolutely fine and interesting puzzle game. While I personally wasn't a fan of it's mechanics nor interested in the weak story there is no denying that this is a perfectly fine brain teaser of a game that will keep you engaged through it's entire length. It's also great for low IQ brainlets like me, where the final few levels are complicated enough they make you feel good enough to get that rush of dopamine that helps you stop feeling sorry for yourself for 15 seconds.Very similar to Lara Croft GO and Hitman GO. A top down isometric puzzle game where you start at point A, have to hit buttons and avoid patrols to reach point B. What's unique about this game is it's "timeline" feature which is basically a glorified restart/skip feature. A timeline appear on the bottom of the screen each level and as you go through the level it advances. If at any point you make a mistake, instead of having to restart the level you can just rewind the timeline to a point before you made the mistake rather than having to wait for a loading screen and retry. You can also advance time: click where you want to go and instead of waiting for your character to move you can just advance the timeline until they're there.From Chapter 2+ you also have to control a cat, you can distract in a radius but otherwise controls the same as the main character.The timeline feature is astoundingly fantastic. It totally eliminates the need for loading screens and it really shows the developer values your time. Did you make it to the end of the level only to realise you can't complete it because of a button you hit at the start? Just rewind to the start (which takes about a second, if that) and try again. Even if the puzzles aren't fantastic (which overall they're generally pretty good anyway) the timeline feature makes doing each puzzle totally hassle free. You'll never ever feel like you're wasting time because you can skip to any point in the puzzle. There is never a need to wait, reload or die. It's utterly fantastic and one of the best features in a puzzle game, or game in general.There are quite a few things I didn't like, but none of them compare to how much I liked the timeline feature which is why I give this a thumbs up. First, the story is almost nonexistant, yet the game does focus way too much time on unskippable cutscenes which don't really serve any purpose. The ending goes for like 10 minutes and you have to sit through entirely arbitrary story. Second, controlling two character basically the entire game was frustrating: there is never a clear indication of which character you have selected at any given time and I spent a good 40% of each level rewinding because I moved the wrong character. The puzzle mechanics themselves i'm not a particularly big fan of (not that they're bad!! It's totally subjective) but they're done well enough in this game.Last, some levels have "relics", which you get by beating a certain challenge on levels that have them. You don't know if a level has a relic until you beat it: if the relic is dim you need to rewind the level until it's light > see what you did that turned it off > don't do that. The challenges themselves aren't hard to do but some later levels have relics that require you to do specific things in EARLIER levels that don't have relics. Like, you need to have the cat stand in a certain position in level 3-? so that in 5-? you can meet the relic requirement. These relics are rare but they really suck. Having to go back and do previous levels to meet the requirement (which it never tells you what they are) is pretty poor design.Make the currently selected character way more prominent and obvious. Get rid of the relics that require multiple levels, or at least tell the player that a certain level has consequences for a later level. Let me skip cutscenes please.It's ironic that for a game that really loves making you use time efficiently, it absurdly wastes your time in anything that isn't gameplay related. I also really didn't like controlling two separate character to solve puzzles, I mean I can barely control myself in real life. I also can't believe that that it took a developer this long to have such an amazing feature in the timeline. It's really just such a simple idea...Super easy. Get all the relics (there is level select at any point in the game) and then beat the game, you'll get your 100%!!

_childDocuments_.review: Timelie. It's a time-looping puzzle game where you need to progress through a series of levels by sneaking past enemies as a girl or a cat (or both!), all while controlling time like a media player. Did you catch that? If you mess up, you can immediately rewind and try something new. It makes the gameplay very fluid even during difficult puzzles. It's one of the better sets of controls I've seen for a puzzle game.My only complaint is that the game is a bit short; I would have loved to play a few more of the end-game levels where you traverse backwards through the levels you just completed, dodging all the obstacles from the first round in addition to your past self. Cause we wouldn't want to mess up the timeline now, would we?Seriously, try this game out. It's great.

_childDocuments_.review: Quite the interesting direction they went with the time manipulation puzzle concept with great execution. With every puzzle you have a time bar at the bottom that acts as your reset and undo which allows you to move the playhead to any point to see how things occur or will occur in the allotted time.The character goes where you click and as she moves the playhead slowly moves to the right. Once they reach the destination the game will pause automatically so you never have to worry about losing crucial time. The game gives you the feeling of having to time things perfectly and in some puzzles it comes close, however, with the freedom you have to manipulate time it removes that unneeded pressure.Later on you will be accompanied by a cat that you will also have to guide through the puzzles with the girl. You are free to interchange between the two and help them help each other reach the exits. This part is where it really shines. They share the same time bar but yet have their own as well. For instance you can make a path for the girl and once you see everything will work up to that point you can rewind that used time back to a specific point you need to then guide the cat across that same time so you can be as efficient as possible.She has a power that allows her to repair broken bridges  with the cat's ability is to meow to catch the attention of the robots to steer them away from a blocked path or door.The puzzles themselves are challenging enough to make you not overthink while at the same time it's not a cakewalk either. Even the challenges that do add an extra level of difficulty aren't hair pulling hard either (this is left for the free DLC which is optional, even warns you about this and how it's not needed to completed the main story).Puzzle genre is one of my favorites and one thing they did which I have never seen done before that I can remember but absolutely love is that  Again even doing this they were still able to keep the challenge without it being overly difficult or too easy.I would love a sequel or at least another puzzle game with this same concept, it has been a long while that I came across a puzzle game where I felt satisfied.

_childDocuments_.review: Timelie is a puzzle game where you play as a little girl and her cat as she navigates time puzzles in her dream. The objective of every puzzle is to reach the exit while ensuring the cat and the girl do not get caught by any robot.Gameplay-wise, mouse and keyboard. A to reverse time and D to fast-forward time. Mouse to click on the points you wish to move to. What's interesting is that each character moves individually on their on layer, you can control each characters movement to move individually at their own time, while simultaneously moving them all at once. Think of it as a video editing software where you set the sound, speech, subtitles and other effects to occur at different timings of the video. Conclusion, do try Timelie. The puzzles are reminescent of Lara Craft: GO.1. Interesting PuzzlesThe ones where you have to deal with yourself are somewhat interesting. Not in the actual puzzle but in the concept of preventing a time paradox.1. ShortIt's over in 5 hours.2. LoreThere really isn't any lore to "glue" the player to the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Soft Recommendation for this one. Enjoyable, compact game about moving a girl (and then cat!!) to avoid getting bonked by robots or vaporized into nothingness.All your movement is based on a timeli(n)e which essentially boils down the gameplay to how efficiently you maneuver your characters on a frame by frame basis. That may sound tedious to some but there's a certain level of satisfaction in weaving around multiple, densely packed cones of sight.The game starts out fairly basic. You move the girl, she has some time powers, that's it. Then they introduce a second character, the cat, which can distract robots by meowing loud. Then they tighten up the puzzles so you really have to time each action down to the wire. And then finally, they further utilize the fact that this is a game about time, which I won't elaborate on since it might spoil first playthroughs but seriously, it should be obvious about what you'll pull in a time game. Definitely attempt all the 'secret' challenges for certain levels, gives the game a nice bite of... challenge (also lets you 100% the game as well).Personally thought the game could have ramped up the difficulty earlier, and they should have expanded further on the late-game stuff. But hey, engaging 5+ hour TAS-lite simulator.

_childDocuments_.review: Love the concept, visual vibes, and soundtrack.It was worth a short ride, and it's even more fun when I play with my friends as we tried to solve the puzzle together (but jus to be clear, this is a single-player game).First, the concept of "time control" power might have been used in some other games, Life is Strange being one of the famous title, but I personally love the way it is implemented into "media player"-like scroller. The movement are based on point/grid system, which I only found out later  it has to be that way instead of a "ASWD free movement".At the end of each stage, after "simulating" the movement and help the girl reaches the finish line, we have the option to review our gameplay in a perfect manner (although behind the scene it might took hours to solve it lol). I think this part is particularly interesting since it gives off the vibe that we're actually watching pseudo-cutscene instead of our own point-and-click gameplay.The puzzle is entertaining and I must warn you it relies on mili-to-nanoseconds timing for some higher levels. There is a lot of "trial-and-error" needed as you try lots of combination, and even split-second matters here. They say there is always be only 1 solution for each phase, although I haven't tried to find any other ways, I can see some truth in those words. The stages in each chapter has 1 "core gameplay"; in chapter 2 it's impossible to solve all puzzles without the help of the cat and ventilation, in chapter 3 it's all about timing and reading enemy's pattern, and in chapter 4 it's about . The earlier stages serves as an introduction some sort, and by understanding the core I mentioned before, we can solve the later stages.And the thing I love most is the "Easter Egg" of this game, which relates to its level design. That is simply mindblowing and conceptual!The game has 4 chapter + 1 final chapter, with an average of 10+ stages per chapter. I'm aware that puzzle-solving game has low repetitive value, so you might want to enjoy all your progress to the fullest while you're at it. I bought this at 50% discounted price, so IMO it's still worth it for a unique gameplay, level design, and good graphic and music that the developer put their efforts into.There isn't any "Story Rich" tag in this game, and I think we'll just have to accept the game as it is. Warning first if you're looking for a good story: . It did indeed confuse me first because there aren't hints to at least tell us if this game might be an analogy of something, all the way to the ending I'm still only interpreting the story pretty straightforwardly from what's happening right in front of my eyes. In the ending we finally got like, 5 seconds to get a gist of the story, but the rest is up for player's interpretation. And then, the  came, and within that 10 seconds, we are given a clearer hint to finally understand and wraps the story completely (putting aside of the open interpretation for the why and the how).Without the Secret Ending, I'm probably only feel like 80% satisfied, but watching the Secret Ending made up for the rest of 20%. That's how I'd describe it.Memorable original ending song, great puzzle and level design, fresh mechanism, and top-notch visuals (although not something new). Do not expect anything story-rich except for the open ending + secret ending.

_childDocuments_.review: I have never played a time-manipulated strategy puzzle game and I wanted to try this because it looked interesting. I thought it was going to be a mind-blowing experience from a gameplay standpoint. To be frank, I was indeed a little disappointed by the first few stages as they were too easy. I mean, how difficult could it be if we were able to undo a mistake instantly and redo it differently right? Despite that, I continued playing as I did not want to waste the bucks spent (it was on sale). The more I progressed, the more I felt cheated. Why? For thinking, even for a second, that this game was easy. Timelie is a hardcore brain-twister that will challenge you to think out of the box and into the fire, or be tempted to look at gameplay walkthroughs for hints on how to beat it, or both. After the first few stages, it becomes apparent (if not already) that a lot of passion and effort has been put into the game. From the model designs to the visual style of the game. There is a vision from the creators and it feels so fully realized here. There is a hint of a story from the puzzles as the creators have kept things ambiguous, but really, you are not playing this for the story, or even for the main storyline. You are playing this for the Hell Loop DLC! Yes. That free DLC which, in my opinion, should have been the main gameplay and the storyline mode be a bonus DLC instead. Here's why. I spent about 7-8 hours to finish the main storyline, according to Steam. As of this writing, I have also completed the DLC and that duration has reached 23 hours. 15-16 hours is the difference. Twice the time I spent on the main storyline. If you thought the main storyline was hard (yes it gets pretty hard), the DLC will make you question the existence of life itself. Then, you will only have a gesture of a word: Tenet.Because this is a thoroughly excellent game, I am a little bugged by some of its flaws. Let's talk about that.1) There is an unskippable animation for almost everything, and it adds up to quite a bit of accumulated waste of time. Things like doors opening, the camera zooming in to something and then zooming back out, etc. It is extremely cumbersome since some stages might require you to visit the main menu frequently, and you only get to the menu after a few animations. There are even animations for when you select a chapter in the menu. All unnecessary. The design is great and all, and maybe it adds "immersion" for some, but really, all I want for Christmas is to solve some puzzles. Let's get on with it.2) Because of the issue mentioned above, there are also long, unskippable "running along a long pathway" segments during the game that only shows the character progressing to the lobby after every chapter, and literally nothing else. I'm not sure what symbolic elements are present here, but we should not have to sit through this every time we complete a chapter because it is way too long and boring. Fortunately, all these animations can be skipped if you have seen them once. The menu animations can't be skipped though.3) Many stages require you to switch between a girl and a cat character. Every time you do this, the camera will center on the character you switch to. Personally, I wish there was an option to disable this camera movement and allow free cam instead. I always zoom out to the fullest because I like to see the whole map while strategizing, like looking at a chess board while planning for moves. However, the camera moves every time I switch characters, shifting part of the map out of frame and I have to reset it every time. It can get frustrating at times, but this is quite minor. I doubt it would affect many as much as it did me. 4) There is not much of a story in the main storyline. As mentioned earlier, the creators have chosen to keep things ambiguous. However, there is no identifiable plot either, save for some "plot twists" that just happens. I believe it is supposed to be some sort of a sad story at the end, but there was nothing that happened during the gameplay for me to care one way or another, except for the slight attachment I got from spending hours playing those characters. 5) No Steam achievements for the Hell Loop DLC. Like, seriously, why? I feel more accomplished playing the DLC than the main gameplay, but there are no achievements to prove that I was there. I think this is a tragic missed opportunity for a game this well thought out. Timelie is a truly well-designed game, able to surprise you and then demolish your hopes later on. The concept is simple, but not easy to play. When you do get to the end (especially if completely on your own without looking up for hints), there will be a sense of satisfaction that is hard to deny. Highly recommended for anybody who is looking for a challenge, and the DLC is not only worth the price of admission alone but essential playing as well. If the creators at Urnique Studio do develop a sequel to this, I would gladly torture my brain all over again.Note: I have read some comments that commented on some stages "cracking" or some bugs. I personally have not experienced any such glitches. The entire game worked smoothly for me. No issues whatsoever.
_childDocuments_.name: Timelie

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic stealth puzzle game with time manipulation. Very fun challenge and satisfying gameplay when you solve very tough puzzles!The story....umm...so yeah the story is very vague. You get hints of it, but there is no dialogue or subtitles throughout the entire game. You're just a girl who awakens in some weird abstract world that has robot sentries. She gets the ability to manipulate time and preform precognition (like Katana Zero!). She befriends a cat along her journey through this world and they work together to escape.The controls are simple. You move in a grid and control time like on a media player. You use this to see the robot patrol routes and how to get past them. The girl runs very slow, so if a robot sees you, you aren't outrunning them. So you have to get a good lead on them if you wanna trick them. As the game progresses you'll obtain a special ability on some levels. If the girl picks up a power-up, she can repair certain broken parts of the world that were not traversable.  She can activate keypads to open doors as well. You will also control the cat on levels as well. They can move a little faster than the girl, but still not faster than robots. They can, however, go through vents and small spaces. They can also meow which will distract the sentries and force them to investigate the noise. It is super satisfying to see your plan work out perfectly when solving the puzzles. You can switch between both the girl and cat while moving the timeline and play out their actions. Click on them to make them stand in place and go forward and backwards until you find the solution!I don't have many gripes with this game. The controls may be a lil confusing at first, but since you control time...you have all the time in the world to get used to it (sorry couldn't resist). The lack of story may shut some gamers off, but I think the gameplay makes up for it. Lastly, sometimes it's unclear how far enemies can see you. Sometimes you'll think you're out of their sight, but they catch you, and vice versa. Not a serious issue but something I wanted to point out.Final verdict? If you love puzzle games that will test your brain muscles, this game is perfect. I finished in about 6-8 hours, but if you're really good, you can probably beat it in 4. If you found the game too short and easy, there is a DLC campaign with harder puzzles to solve. I personally recommend not looking up guides when playing this, it is a lot more satisfying to figure out the answer yourself (I only looked up one because I was pressed for time one session). Thanks for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: I was incredibly surprised by how much i was moved by this game. The soundtrack is beautiful and is worth it to hear the music alone. There's no dialogue in this game, everything is communicated through the movement of the characters and the occasional laugh/meow/grunt. As a puzzle game, the mechanics are well thought out and it always feels like they try to improve on what is built on. Now I see some people say that the game is like a tablet puzzle game, and in some ways that's true but I feel the way its said discredits the game. In no way does this game feel like its rushed, cash grabby, or feel like very little thought is put into it. Its very obvious that the devs put their love and soul into this game.The story is a little vague but if you put on your thinking cap for 2 seconds, you'll get the gist of it. Despite me being able to beat this in 5 hours I felt pretty connected to the characters. I had some laughs  Overall I'd say this worthy of your time and money, and I can't to see what's next from the devs.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is excellent.  It is a rock-solid puzzle game. It's well-designed, well-polished, and a great way to kill about 8-10 hours.At its core, Timelie is a rather simple multi-stage puzzle game. Each stage is a small area where you must navigate from point A to point B, while avoiding being captured by robots - which mostly involves avoiding detection (though not always.)  To aid you in this task, you, the player, are given the -like power to fast-forward time (to observe enemy patrol patterns, for example, or to simply wait for the right moment) and rewind time (to undo a mistake.)  You can rewind all the way to the start of the stage. (In theory, there's a time limit, but I've never even come close to hitting it.) Later stages introduce a cat who can distract the robots by meowing, and later still you gain the means to destroy some of the robots.At the end of each stage you are treated to a nice cinematic (no UI elements except the mouse cursor) showing your character(s) making their way through the stage using your final solution.  One of my favorite things to do is time things exactly right so I was  out of sight at all times, à la .Where Timelie stands out, however, is the interdependency of these stages.  There are a number of stages, for example, which take place in the same area but at different times.  The specific path and sequence of actions you choose during earlier stages -- destroy this robot or evade, repair that bridge or go around -- will affect the state of the area for later stages, which can make those stages easier or more difficult.Of the 25 or so gameplay stages, 15 of them have a "relic" (achievement) that you can obtain by completing the level with a secret restriction, such as not using the cat's meow to distract any robots, or completing the stage without destroying any robots.  While playing these stages, you can see the artifact (it looks like a purple bug zapper) at the exit; failing the relic's requirement will cause the artifact to turn grey, giving a clue as to the requirement.You can replay any past stage at any time -- and unless you're  lucky, you'll need to do this for a few stages in order to get all of the relics (and thus 100% completion.)

name: Fallout 76
detailed_description: Fallout 76: Skyline Valley Expand southward to Skyline Valley – a brand-new region of Appalachia. Investigate the cause of the electric storm circling overhead and unveil the mystery around Vault 63 and its dwellers, including a shocking new Ghoul type – The Lost. Explore a brand-new region in Appalachia – Skyline Valley adds the rolling hills of Shenandoah to the southwest area of the map. Uncover a new Storyline – Discover the location of Vault 63 and meet its cabal of Ghoul dwellers. Act as the enigmatic overseer’s gun for hire as you uncover mysteries that could change -- or break -- the Wasteland Encounter a new enemy type – Meet a new type of supercharged Ghoul with electrifying weapons and armor and expose their origin. Chase storms in a new Public Event – Dangerous Pastimes brings together thrill-seekers to gather electrical energy from the skies but beware The Lost and other electrified creatures attracted by the storm. Summon a new Region Boss – Help to defend Skyline Valley from the very things created to keep it safe, a trio of robot titans: the Storm Goliaths. Digital Deluxe Edition The Skyline Valley Deluxe Edition includes access to the Fallout 76 base game, as well as the Lost Treasures bundle. Featured DLC The Lost Treasures Bundle includes the following bonus in-game C.A.M.P. items and cosmetics: Weather Control Station (Skyline Valley): Give your C.A.M.P an electrical red glow! V63 Power Armor & Jetpack Paint: Become a Vault 63 champion with this shiny new Power Armor and Jetpack skin. Vault 63 Door Display: Bring a piece of Vault 63 to your C.A.M.P. Moe the Mole Plushie: Moe the Mole really digs safety. V63 Chassis Display Frame: Showcase your Power Armor in Vault 63 style! Lightning Rod Pose: Harness the power of lightning with this pose. Fallout 76 base game required, sold separately. About the Game Bethesda Game Studios, the award-winning creators of Skyrim and Fallout 4, welcome you to Fallout 76. Twenty-five years after the bombs fell, you and your fellow Vault Dwellers—chosen from the nation’s best and brightest – emerge into post-nuclear America on Reclamation Day, 2102. Play solo or join together as you explore, quest, build, and triumph against the wasteland’s greatest threats. Explore a vast wasteland, devastated by nuclear war, in this open-world multiplayer addition to the Fallout story. Experience the largest, most dynamic world ever created in the legendary Fallout universe. Immersive Questlines and Engaging Characters Uncover the secrets of West Virginia by playing through an immersive main quest, starting from the moment you leave Vault 76. Befriend or betray new neighbors who have come to rebuild, and experience Appalachia through the eyes of its residents. Seasons Progress through each season and unlock free rewards like consumables, C.A.M.P. items and more by completing limited-time challenges. Multiplayer Roleplaying Create your character with the S.P.E.C.I.A.L system and forge your own path and reputation in a new and untamed wasteland with hundreds of locations. Whether you journey alone or with friends, a new and unique Fallout adventure awaits. Mountain Splendorland The story lives and breathes through the world of Fallout 76, which brings to life six distinct West Virginia regions. From the forests of Appalachia to the noxious crimson expanses of the Cranberry Bog, each area offers its own risks and rewards. A New American Dream Use the all-new Construction and Assembly Mobile Platform (C.A.M.P.) to build and craft anywhere in the world. Your C.A.M.P. will provide much-needed shelter, supplies, and safety. You can even set up shop to trade goods with other survivors. Fallout Worlds Play unique adventures in Appalachia with Fallout Worlds, which is an evolving set of features that give players the capability to play Fallout 76 in unique ways with customizable settings.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: "Seasons" have been added and the rate at which you can earn atoms has been slowed, with extra free junk in between. We'll see how this goes. Fingers ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ crossed.-------------------------------------------------------------------------------Bethesda's first crack at an MMO has been a very rocky road.Get it on sale, but just know ahead of time that you have a limited(800 weight) stash without paying for a subscription; as others' reviews probably pointed out.You can earn atoms by playing daily/weekly/monthly and doing the challenges, so you can earn the cool and useful things in the store; plus the store has something free every day.It can be buggy, in true Fallout fashion, with added possible network problems.Which, I assume, might be solvable with the subscription; as it allows private servers.I don't know, as I've not tried it. (Somewhat confirmed, though I assume you still can't play if the servers go down.)A lot of people complain that they added a subscription, but I'm trying to be a bit more open to the idea.If it improves the quality of things and also adds to the quantity, then I don't see the issue.So far it seems good.

_childDocuments_.review: I know there are lots of questions about this game in your mind. I had them too until free weekend. I tried it and bought the game. The reason behind it is not very simple. Let's read what I think.Not even close to be a masterpiece. Not good for pvp yet. Not a good survival game nor a good role-playing game. What is it then? It is the mixture of everything above.  I knew that this game's release was too harsh on players who bought it at that point. Yes, they are right and still lot's of bugs, exploits and unbalanced mechanism of player interactions. I would like to rate this game in four categories such as single-player, multi-player, technical, and overall. Singleplayer:I wouldn't recommend Fallout 76 to any player who wants to play Fallout series as single-player game. Why? Because quests are so simple, too repeating game play. You have to pay for single-player experience or private server experience with friends as co-op. Except your base and your quest line, everything on map belongs to server and it will reset everything else, once you logged out from the server or quit the game. Only plus of this game for single-player experience is that you usually feel alone and you encounter different events during your game play as other Fallout games.Rate: 4/10Multiplayer:I wouldn't recommend Fallout 76 to any player who wants to play Fallout series as multi-player game too. It's not a good game for competitive online gaming genre. There is no balance between players until you have the same level which is nearly impossible until end-game. Pvp is really bad in this game and seems it's not possible to be fixed. Best way to play this game as multi-player game is to play with your friends but still higher level player can come and kill you easily. There is no strong reward for killing someone in this game and it takes time to reach someone so it's not as easy as in GTA V.Rate: 3/10Technical: Same textures, animations, items, etc. from Fallout 4 are there. Server system is okay. You can find other players to interact more often than other survival, crafting games but there is a reason to find them or interact with them? I found many reasons to interact them but in this game I couldn't make any friends but enemies. I don't know what is the reason under this kind of an act but players prefer not interacting with you.There are lots of bugs and some exploits in this game which made selling items through vendors to other players banned. You can't sell any item with vending machines because of one exploit right now. I hope they will fix it as other bugs which still occurs. Rate: 5/10Overall:This is where I can recommend this game to people. It may not be a good single-player game nor multi-player game but it's a good mixture of it so if you buy this game expect some experience between. You will mostly play it co-op with your friends or single-player themed Fallout and see other players around. You can get killed time to time or kill other players for your own purposes and continue playing it alone or co-op.I can only recommend this game if you can play a game not less than 2 hours when you sit in front of it. Most of your playing time can be undone because of quitting the game. Anything that you do on map except your camping area and quest lines, will be the products that you gained from map, anything else will be undone. So it's better to play longer hours to get those products from what you built. Grinding is there and it's there because of this punishing system.Rate: 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Like Fallout 4 with a more diverse world space (all biomes are unique and distinctive), more refined gameplay systems (real-time V.A.T.S., more perk diversity, a more in-depth crafting system where you learn plans or scrap weapons to get new upgrades, and better base-building (place anywhere, more buildable items)), and, the ability to play with friends.The main negative is that there are no mods which means once you've done all the quests and explored the entire map, you've beaten the game. (In my opinion trying to get an infinite amount of play-time out of a single game is unhealthy, so this doesn't bother me much.) Getting to that point still takes probably 100 hours if you take your time and explore the world though, so it's not like the game is short.

_childDocuments_.review: Look.  It's a Bethesda game.  If you are a die hard Fall Out or Bethesda fan, you know Bethesda has it's issues but in the end it delivers.  Fall Out 76 is no different.  Yeah, it started off as garbage, and there was lots and lots of issues and yeah, some issues to the day still exist. However, I'm telling you, if you enjoyed Bethesda games in the past, you are gonna enjoy this game.  It's Fall Out 4, with a different story and best part is you can invite friends.  It has NPCs.  It has all the things that most people ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ about being missing.  Really, this is a hell of a game, and has kept me and my friends occupied for 229 hours (and I havn't even scratched the surface of the Main Quest). _childDocuments_.review: Do I like this game? Yes.Can I in good conscience recommend it to others? No.Bethesda regularly adds content updates, on the surface this may sound great, but this will usually introduce a boatload of bugs, many of which will not be addressed for a very long time. One example is a recent update fixed a bug where gunfire would ring out constantly, even after an encounter ends, this bug had existed since around 2020! 4 years to implement a minor fix like this a little concerning. The same update made a newly added weapon completely useless in VATS mode, a major component of the gameplay for many players. Its like Bethesda Austin, the office in charge of the development is void of quality and version control.Another annoying aspect is that attempts by Devs to 'balance' the game consist of nerfing what works, instead of buffing what doesn't, imagine grinding hours out with the RNG to attain the weapon build you're happy with, to log in one day and find you now do 40% less of the damage you did the day before, leaving your build worthless and the weapon you spent maybe 60hrs of grind attaining, nothing more than scrap. Would this scenario make you happy with the game or make you throw the towel in? The above reasons (amongst other things) probably lend to why the game has such a high attrition rate of players, it gets frustrating to play, leaving you thinking your time has been wasted and that the devs don't have a clue what they are doing.To summarise, would I ask my friends to give it a go? No, I'd be embarrassed to, they have standards this game doesn't meet and this game, while containing many enjoyable aspects, its an endless cycle of game broken, game not so broken.I personally believe the only way to fix the rotation of problems in this game would be a complete overhaul of the studio, the engine and the entire game, which will never happen.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Company is making decisions in the current PTS that will effectively kill their player base of course their poor updates lately haven't helped. Players unanimously have shown their outrage to the most recent PTS update. This has been met with deletion of reasonable opinion and banning accounts to silence a majority. Do not give these people your money move on and know the developers have no interest in what the current players think or say.Hey Everyone,The first thing I ask my friends when they tell me they're thinking about picking this game up is this. Do you like the fallout universe, and do you enjoy the lore? If not, this game may not be for you. If you are willing to give it a chance despite that please read more!This game isn't 1:1 on lore but boy is it a fun time discovering it here in West Virginia. Fallout 76 takes the good and the bad from the Fallout 4 engine and makes the map 4X bigger. On launch it lacked NPCs which was remedied by the Wastelanders patch last spring since adding even more with the BOS added this past fall of 2020. Often I find myself thinking each area has so many details, so many notes, and many references to the lives of the population before the bombs fell. Even at a high level I find stuff I've missed or new things to experience. In all of my experience the best part is definitely the people of Fallout 76. I have met many friends who I still talk to in Discord or friends who played hundreds of hours with me that still keep in touch even after they've put this game down.I've mingled with all aspects of the player base. I have played with the Raiders, with the casuals, with the XP farmers, and the RP vendors selling me medicine at a cheap discount. I am on a couple Facebook groups for trading and sharing of adventures as well as the Reddit. Everyone is so helpful in this game and I appreciate it. I always return the favor and look for new players who need help.Lets get to the good and the bad of the game.Going back to my main questions I will say even if you aren't interested in the lore or enjoyed Fallout 4 there is something for you here as an online game, but I don't feel anyone should force themselves to love the game if they don't want to play it. I have bought this for a few friends and not all of them thought it was their cup of tea but gave it a chance even playing up to 20-100 hours depending on the friend.My biggest way of explaining this game in a few words is to imagine Fallout 4 but with Destiny's party and public event system. This can be played in some sense "Single Player" I did just that for the first 200 hours or so. I spent time reading and exploring my way around Appalachia, but is just as fun running with other people! The game really has a way of bringing the community together with the event system. Often I find myself being that person running music through Soundpad just to add to the fun. You know playing Killer Queen, by Queen, while fighting the Queen.Again, this game isn't for everyone. I hope this helps you in your purchase decision. I hope to see fellow fans of Fallout in game and look forward to making more memories with everyone that gives it a chance and enjoys their time playing it. This game goes on sale constantly just wait until its 13USD and grab it! I don't blame you for not wanting it full price I penny pinch myself and buy most games on sale myself.Thank you,Faint

_childDocuments_.review: This game is what sullied the good name of the Fallout franchise. And for good reason, too. If you're planning on buying or even trying this game, I implore you to just think about if you'd be fine with more games releasing like this one did.I never left Vault 76. Some people may say that it's unfair I'm posting a review like this if I never progressed beyond the very start. But why should I progress any further if the bit which is meant to make me engaged just makes me irritated?- The game jumped between all my monitors very fast upon opening. This only happened the first time I played, but it's quite possibly a genuine seizure hazard, which worried me.The window then settled in the top corner of my secondary monitor, with the top of the window clipped off. This luckily(?) didn't obscure much of what I ended up enduring, although all of this but the strange position was fixed by a restart and changing graphical settings. Most of my 16 minutes playing were trying to fix this issue.- Upon opening, I immediately see an advert for the Atomic Shop. Having IAPs in a video game seems excusable if it's a free to play game, but it feels forced and almost dirty in this game. Not only that, but the menu has a big counter telling you how many (or in my case, few) atoms you own. The entire mechanism makes it feel like they don't care about Fallout anymore, they're just milking it like it's a quick cashgrab, which at this point it may as well be, if it wasn't for the roadmap, which I don't trust Bethesda to fulfil.- Starting a save file presented me with a landslide of visual bugs. There were more than I can count, and some were more painful than others. All of them were unexpected and unwelcome. The game's been out over a year and I'm still noticing a slew of problems before I've even seen outside the vault.- Not only that, but I encountered a number of other glitches, too. The door to the atrium wouldn't open, forcing me to restart the game before it worked. A Mr Handy just died and disappeared with no warning, and the others kept reverting to default positions. The Mr Handy related glitches appeared after a restart.Overall, I would not recommend this game, not just because it's a bad game, but because buying, and even just playing, this game, tells Bethesda that they can get away with botching releases and fixing them post-launch. This practice should not be condoned - if you ordered a burger at a restaurant but were told the patty would be added way after receiving it/not at all, you'd be understandably angry. Please don't buy this game. I adore the Fallout franchise, and it'd be awful if this was deemed acceptable enough for Bethesda to try this again. In fact, I'm so unhappy with this whole ordeal that I've spent more time writing this review than I did tolerating this game.Now be a good NCR citizen and play a Fallout game which is actually worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: Fallout 76 at launch presented the most utterly bleak post-apocalyptic environment in gaming history.  Everything you may have loved (or hated) about the last three Fallout games is here: engrossing environments, intriguing holotape storylines, entertaining robots, hordes of varied enemies, and atmosphere both beautiful and chilling in turn.  Everyone's complaint about Fallout 76 was that it did not have NPCs.  Well, guess what; now it does.  Go play it.  You will not regret it if you liked the previous first-person Fallout games for anything OTHER than conversations with other people (and, again, those are starting to come in now).  I understand that many people had problems with bugs and crashes, but I had no more issues than I do with any other game these days.Edit: I am finally giving the game a fuller replay with all the new stuff added in, and am getting angry that anyone is still giving this amazing game negative reviews.  Look forward to me writing a much longer positive review soon, all of you 0.8 people reading this.UPDATED REVIEW FINALLY TWO YEARS LATEROr, as Steam says:"You've played an additional 1,117 hours--would you recommend this game to other players?Inspired by the requirement to make a new review or update a review for the awards this year--I nominated Baldur's Gate ]I[ for nearly every category and I am not touching that perfect snapshot of a review from 2020, so Fallout 76 it is--it is finally time to come back and write a little more here.  Fallout 76 is now the game I have the most hours in on Steam, and it is not close--and that is not even counting the 500+ hours I put in when it was still just on the Bethesda Launcher.  Fallout 76 is my favorite post-apocalyptic game of all time, and I have played and loved all the Fallouts and Wastelands and even Fountain of Dreams (O.K. I admit I hated Fallout: Tactics and obviously never played Brotherhood of Steel because nobody has ever played it).  I have been playing post-apocalyptic RPGs for 35 years and this is currently the pinnacle of what I want out of such a game.Would I change a few things?  Yes, absolutely; it still could use more single-player reactivity and storyline, and it says something that even after playing for 5 years I still have not figured out how to launch a nuclear warhead since I am not willing to read a walkthrough to figure out something that I should be able to figure out in-game, but they constantly add new fun stuff to the game and I still have friends that play, and until both of those things cease I will continue putting in hundreds of hours a year.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was received free as part of the  linking promotion.Pros:(Literally None.)Cons:- Terrible performance and optimization: locked at 60fps, graphics quality the same from Ultra to Low, framerate very inconsistent. The Steam layout runs at a crisp 120fps but the game doesn't. That should say a lot.- Clunky mouse/keyboard controls: TAB to back out, LALT to grenade, etc. - Empty, lifeless world- Worse-than-PS2-quality graphics on all settings, including Ultra- Gameplay balancing is a horrible mess; can't play this game for a whole minute solo without dying at the beginning area. Always an entire horde of enemies who can 3-5 shot you, armor and good weapons are almost nonexistent, alongside this game's fetish of bolt-action weapons of every category which can't even do much damage on most parts- Expensive: Alpha quality product, Wastelanders update did not fix any of the major problems. - Fallout 1's existence: Monetization of private servers; I understand given servers require money to run on and Minecraft basically does the same thing with Realms, but here's the difference; Fallout 76 is straight-up just a terrible game. Minecraft, on the other hand, is a great game. Minecraft has more rights charging people for this service. - Microtransactions: Too many, even though its purely cosmetic. Sure, you can get them "free" by grinding atoms via challenges, but do people even care enough to do them?- Advertising: Same exact problem with Fallout 4; releases only one or two trailers before launch with almost no gameplay nor information about the game. Also, serious minus points for slandering Country Roads by John Dover with this less-than-half-assed product.Getting this game free via the account link wasn't worth it. You know there is something seriously wrong with a game if it's not even worth it for free. One of the worst games of the decade (of 2010s)? Understatement, one of the worst games of all time. Rather play Ride to Hell: Retribution. 0/10

_childDocuments_.review: It's 3 years later and the game is still buggy and experiencing performance issues.Here is a slightly chaotic list of some of the many problems I encountered during my 1 hour of playtime:Almost all the NPCs I interacted with were bugged, either repeating the same sentence over and over again or not talking at all.The plot is way worse than Fallout 4 and you can't immerse yourself in the world, because there are other players running around you all the time.Every 200 meters, there is a noticeable hiccup. I'm guessing the reason is that the server is giving your client information about the area it's loading.No toggle-ADS in a 2020 FPS game...For me, the default FOV is way too narrow, but when you increase the FOV the weapon models stay the same and are way too big and terminal screens are too far away from the camera and become hard to read.Every time I close the game, I get an ad for the in-game currency and sometimes there is even a screen-wide ad for the in-game shop when you go into the menu.The lighting can look good for the landscapes, but absolutely butchers face details, so NPCs look like they are made out of clay. And to clarify, I was playing on 4K ULTRA.This whole game feels like a fan-made Fallout 4 MMO mod and not a 100,000,000 dollar production from a company with 114 million dollars of revenue per year.If you are a huge Fallout fan and wanted a Fallout MMO, then this is likely right up your alley. (if you pretend that you don't see the bugs)For everyone else, this seems like a waste of time and money.

_childDocuments_.review: Most fun I've had in a LONG time.  Great openworld, story line, and adventure!  Lots to explore, learn and read for lore.  Learn about the FEV Virus and much more.  Online play is a lot of fun.  Especially the Scored Beast Events when the Nukes go off.  Also Exploring the recently Nuked areas is a wild ride.  The effects are awesome for it.  The world is very large and well laid out.  No vehicles but fast travel makes getting around fairly easy.Lots of guns and melee weapons with tons of cool customisation.   With the PERK System and the mods on weapons you can really setup your player to match how you play.  You can follow other setups people do like Bloodied, or Junkie setups or make up your own like I did.  Once you hit level 50 you can keep levelling and keep adding more legendary perk cards which is awesome.  You can get Legendary cards that auto unlock pick locking and hacking terminals.  Once you upgrade all the way you can do +3 Lock Picking & Terminals automatically.  Plus much more like making 200% more ammo.The junk system has been improved over Fallout 4.  No more carrying around all these parts.  Just scrap it into your chest and you can access it anywhere.  I suggest you get Fallout 1st.  The Extra a month is totally worth it with the Unlimited Scrap bin.  Quick Deployable Tent with chests and work table really helps for scavenging trips.  Plus other goodies per month and you also get a private server and customize server for you and your friends.  Plus the 1650 Atoms a month with it.  That would cost you more then Fallout 1st to buy separately.  Last thing the Scoreboard (aka: Battlepass) Is awesome.  Great way to make you keep working towards something.  New paint jobs, Power Armour skins, new armour paints, outfits, items for your CAMP (Base you can build anywhere) So makes you want to keep playing after your all done.  The events are also a lot of fun and keep the game going.With the gun comes some bad, and every game has its down points.  There is only a few small bad things with Fallout 76.  Which aren't all that much of a problem.  But worth mentioning.  1st the Engine for Fallout is getting fairly dated, definitely not Unreal Engine 5 ability.  You need a fairly good computer to run this game in high mode.  With an Intel i10 and a RTX 2070 10gb and only get 60 fps on Medium.Online play sometimes has a bit of lag.  Nothing too bad but its noticeable at times.  The occasional crash I've had about 5 crashes in 281 hours of play.But overall its my new favourite openworld shooter with fun adventure and exploring.  But 20 players all decked out in Power Armour with .50 calibre machine guns and Gatling Laser Guns trying to take down a Giant Scorched Beast on the edge of a Nuclear Explosions pretty wild!  To all the negative haters on this game.  If you don't like this game you must not be a FPS/Openworld fan and instead of giving this game negative feedback say its not your type of game and move on.  Because this game definitely is up there with one of the best Apocalyptic Online Openworld Adventure FPS games at the moment and hope to see ya out in the nuclear radiated wasteland! Don't forget lots of ammo and your Rad Away!

_childDocuments_.review: I was initially skeptical, given all the pitiful press this game has rightfully received over the years. However, a friend convinced me to try it for a free week event and I ended up buying it after just two days.This game is an MMORPG for people who don’t typically enjoy MMORPGs. If you’re looking for something like WoW or Destiny, then this isn’t it. Instead, Fallout 76 offers an online experience that’s akin to playing an improved version of Fallout 4.For me personally, it hits all the sweet spots of the modpacks I used in Fallout 4: improved graphics, quality of life features, and better combat.One advantage of jumping into the game this late in its cycle is that issues with lag and glitches are few and far between in my 40+ hours of gameplay. Additionally, I get to experience years of refinement and fixes.If you enjoy the setting of Fallout and relish the opportunity to show off your vast collection of items to strangers online, then this is definitely the game for you.

If you love MMOs, there are probably better ones out there.  If you love Fallout, play Fallout 4 or New Vegas again.
