_childDocuments_.review: I pre-ordered this game, and it will be the last game I ever preorder because it launched in such a broken state. Glitches, unstable servers, cheating griefers for days...While the game still has issues today, it's had its "No Man's Sky" moment via the Wastelanders update and Bethesda has only improved it further since. The griefers largely left after the worst exploits were patched out, the servers are usually stable, and most of the game breaking bugs had been swatted. The community in the game is great, lots of people go out of their way to help new players, and there are many Discord servers out there for FO76 which further enhance the social aspects. Voice chat is a must in game when starting if you're needing to communicate with folks.Let's fix some misconceptions - PVP is not forced onto you. DLC are free and everyone gets them when the game updates - we all play on the same game version. You don't need to buy a bundle to get story DLC content. The game has never been "empty" and is almost downright crowded with various NPCs these days. The items from the Atom Shop are 99% cosmetic, you're under no obligation to pay into the game, though Bethesda does fund DLC with those sales. Lastly, you can indeed play solo without Fallout 1st's private server feature.If you want to play alone and experience the story and lore I have some advice - obtain the herd mentality mutation along with the Class Freak perk and join a casual public team. It will give you buffs and you're not required to even be near the other players. When players attempt to assist you as a new player, they may rush you past all the story elements, so bear that in mind if they want to help you with quests.I'm a huge fan of Fallout, and I see no reason why fans of Fallout 3, NV, and 4 can't enjoy this game today if they approach it with an open mind. The only differences are the setting, timeline, and the fact that it's online. If you want to play this like it's Fallout 3, knock yourself out.

_childDocuments_.review: It's Fallout...it just works.For background on my review; I've logged thousands of hours into the game since it first launched. I started my F76 journey on PS4 and switched to PC when my PS4 broke. I've logged 726 hours on Steam at the time of this post and will definitely have more hours logged long after...and thats not including my time on PS4. As for the game: It's no academy winning award, but you will sink hundreds of hours into this game. If you've played previous Fallout titles and enjoyed your time, then this is a no brainer purchase. Yes, it's a reskin of Fallout 4, but new area, enemies, factions, npcs, ect. This game....was TRASH when it first launched, but I powered through and kept playing with my wife and a few friends. Over time it ended up just being me playing solo as everyone else moved onto other games because of the state of the game at the time. It was a soulless, empty wasteland with an occasional player or two.Now though, OH MAN. This game is where it should've been on launch and EVERY DLC is free! That alone is a huge statement seeing as how technically this game is an MMORPG. Yes, there are some bugs that have been present since launch and haven't been fixed, and yeah sometimes it takes me 3-5 tries to just LOG IN without having to CTR-ALT to desktop and restart the game to try again. (If anyone has any fixes or work arounds, please let me know! This has been like this since I first started on Steam). Other than the loading screen start, nothing else is game breaking, just annoying at times... just remember that it's Bethesda lol.Now, I've been seeing A LOT of talk about the Fallout 1st membership. Let me start with this... It is an MMORPG. EVERY MMORPG requires a subscription to play with the only exceptions being free to play and ESO/F76. Just as in ESO...once you buy the game its yours and you can play as much as you want, no subscriptions needed. Do you get an advantage of a subscription to F76? Most definitely and I wont even sugar coat it. Having a survival tent you can plop down almost anywhere and have immediate access to your storage bin, a bed, camping stove (and other things depending on which camp you have selected) is pretty amazing....and I haven't even touched on the Scrap Box you get for being a member. Just like in ESO, you get a separate storage for all of your scrap which, in itself, is game breaking. One of the biggest parts of the game is scavenging for supplies, materials, scrap, ect and the fact you can store an UNLIMITED amount with ZERO weight in a scrap box is incredible. If you choose NOT to do the membership, then you can only store so much in your storage bin before being capped out on weight. This causes a rinse and repeat of scavenging for materials whenever you get low or need some (which...come on. It's Fallout and that's the whole point, right?) So, with that being said, the subscription is totally optional, but you get everything and more for it which I highly, highly recommend doing. If you are used to MMORPGs...then this is no different.I'll continue on just a tad bit longer about the subscription perks... you ALSO get bonus Atoms you can use in the Atom Shop (money shop...its all just cosmetics and poses. The only helpful things being items that you place in your camp to generate materials regularly...helpful but not game breaking.) You get access to a survival camp which I mentioned earlier, exp bonus for the season (once you get your SCORE high enough to unlock it), and you get a PRIVATE SERVER!Now, the Private Server and Community as a whole. The Fallout Community is one of the most friendliest bunch of nerds I've ever met. Yes, there are those that are shunned by the community that are toxic and try griefing, but even the griefers are punished in-game by gaining a bounty in which, and I'm not kidding, the entire server sprints to and promptly kills. The bounty then looses their caps. The amount determines how many people they've killed, bases they've destroyed, locks they've picked. Now let me just say, Bethesda got rid of PVP modes because no one was playing them...friendly nerds, I'm telling you. There still is an option for PVP, but no one does it and if you are being targeted, you can switch to a pacifist mode which almost everyone is in permanently. Now, speaking of the Community, if you are a new player be prepared to be a STAR on the server. Everyone will rush to you to follow you and help you fight/give you a ton of free stuff. I'm guilty of keeping an eye out for new/newer players so I can help them out/dump a ton of healing supplies, materials, ammo, armor, whatever they need. There are so many wonderful players that would bend over backwards to help out their fellow player and that's what keeps me locked into this game. Private Servers are nice, but not really needed with how friendly everyone is. The only time I use them is when my connection is bad (you are the host of your own server, so it really helps with those that have bad internet), I want to claim a bunch of workshops to generate materials, food, ammo, or I'm trying out the new DLC/just wanna zone out. Like I said, not needed because everyone is amazing and you'll have more fun in a public server plus some of the world events are too hard for a solo player and are meant for groups. (Not hard as in dying constantly, but hard as in not enough time to complete objectives.)Speaking of workshops, you have the option of claiming a workshop zone in the world and upon claiming it, PVP enables for about 30 seconds. In the years that I've been playing I have never had someone attack me while claiming the site. If anything, the only time people show up to your workshop is to help defend it from PVE swarms/events. They get a bonus for helping you defend your shop and they get to get some fun kills in while at it. I wont understate this... EVERYONE respects everyone else's workshops. There IS an option to claim someone else's workshop in which PVP gets enabled again, but I honestly don't know what happens at that point because it's never been done/happened for as long as I've played. Everyone just moves servers, waits for the player to leave/log off, or just claims a different spot. If you are worried about workshops around the map...there are plenty and each offers a different bonus for materials, ammo, food, ect. Again, workshops aren't needed, but are really helpful on gathering what you need pacifically (you still need to return to collect your gathered materials/items every 30 minutes or so.)As for the gameplay; quirky characters/stories/lore, hidden gems and easter eggs everywhere (my camera is loaded with wacky findings lol). Gunplay is fun, explosions go boom, outfits and gear are fun to mix and match, and the strongest gear in the game can be crafted/earned through the story. There's a PERK system which is different from other Fallout games because you use cards to gain abilities/bonuses, but those are extremely easy to earn and you can create some amazing and funny builds. There's no "1 build to win them all", but you'll see a lot of players running a bloodied build, so if you see someone with barely any health and a BUNCH of radiation damage....it's on purpose and I'm guilty of playing this way. It's a high risk/high reward play and you don't lose anything for dying (other than your junk, but you get a marker to reclaim it). Even then, I still play around with fun builds. The only time you want to optimize is when facing world bosses, but you can also just throw rocks at them while everyone else massacres them and you still get the kill lol. I've seen level 5's at the endgame world boss just spitting at them while everyone else protects them/revives them and takes on the boss. Anyways, I'm out of words to type, so here's this: Just buy it and play. Endless hours of fun, extremely friendly community, and free DLC every 2-3 years. Expect the numbers to climb when Amazon releases the show. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: At first: I love the Fallout series and played Fallout 3 and 4 many hundreds of hours, over and over again.What I love about games is the atmosphere, setting, story, humor, creativity of game design and a consistent gameplay that's fun and not overly complicated or grindy.In pretty every category mentioned above, Fallout 3 is better than Fallout 4 and Fallout 4 is still way better than Fallout 76.Is Fallout 76 a fun game in it's own respect? Yes, it's ok-ish. It sadly is just way worse than its predecessors. Don't get me wrong: I don't criticise it for NOT being Fallout 5. It just shuold have been much more Fallout in my opinion if it shares the name.For example if you are a fan of the series: Don't you EVER think of comparing Three Dog or even Travis to the radio stations in Fallout 76, for example, it'll cause physical pain.The  of the game is something like a college excursion, with the teacher watching you and planning your trip. Nuclear apocalypse is a nuisance here and there, but hey, we're gonne build this city on Rock'n'roll... or something. The stories often lack originality. For example you'll find lots of tapes where people tell you kinda "everyday life's stories in the apocalypse" which are neither convincing nor relevant.It's all very serious in some way (lacking humor), but it's not as tough a world as in the other games (which doesn't mean the fights aren't tough, it's the world that is more idealised).  torturing and killing for fun and profit. Now, many of the Raiders are kinda nice gals and guys, a bit over the top here and there, but quite likeable fellows all together and you even can play as one!The  are interesting to explore, one of the few improvements compared to 3 and 4. But Appalachia is way too green. Where is the scorched earth, berift of life as we know it? No, just have some robos hover around, watering the lawn and paradise is not lost, it's yours anytime you want it. Perhaps that's actually more realistic, but it's way off the basic message of the game that nuclear destruction is nothing short of madness and madness only. And it kills large portions of the atmosphere. OMG, it is grindy. Be lucky and wait long hours to find the skill card you need if you want to be able to play your character the way you like (or must for a quest). Test your luck to find weapons with the mods you want, hope to get the blueprints if you dismantle them or you'll have to find another one and hope for the best. Or you buy the bluprints for the cost of a hundred weapons of the same kind from a merchant, IF you're lucky and it's for sale.You're eternally short of cash because all equipment is so expensive OR grindy to get. If you haven't got the right weapon with the right legendary effects, monsters always have the upper hand over you.I stopped playingf the game several times because of this grind. It's just boring and I don't need occupational therapy in my rare spare time.Finally, I'm max level and I can say "I played Fallout 76". I don't know if I'll continue to play it. I'm not very much interested in the main story or the several side stories. Not all is bad about the game, it's just that all taken together it's not really worth the effort for a fan of the series in my opinion.Am I just not liking MMORPGs? Perhaps that contributes. But Fallout 76 is not good as a Fallout game nonetheless.

Most other stuff is cosmetic fluff, including a nerf to atoms received coming with "Seasons."TLDR: if you own it, it's worth periodically checking in on Tuesdays but you will not find a sustainable endgame grind akin to other MMOs. This review is intended to be rather short but accurate. IMHO, rating should be in the 65-70% range, not 79%. For that reason, this review is negative, as I believe there is a bloat of players who have not yet reached cavity that is end game.<<<End of Review>>>[]

_childDocuments_.review: 🎮 Should be a neutral vote, but hear me out—it’ll all make sense.---TL;DR:➡ An addictive, substandard AA(A?) game that feels stuck in 2010 but survives thanks to its wholesome, kind, and yet way too indulgent (and addicted) community—and a TV series.➡ A shameless asset flip of Fallout 4.➡ A financial success overall, but as a gamedev, it makes my nose curl; it reeks of everything wrong with this games-as-a-service bigger-than-your-life-games era.➡ IMO, the IP would thrive under another developer.---💣 A Double-Edged Sword  Fallout 76 is a game you’ll develop a complicated relationship with.  You’ll love it and hate it in equal measure, as Bethesda exploits your addiction to its fullest extent. (💸) It’s a sweet torture, delicately engineered to give just enough dopamine hits to keep you throwing more money and time into it.---🖼 Graphics and Technical Details  - Visually decent but dated, with downscaled textures ripped straight from Fallout 4.  - The game’s code is a fossil of the Creation Engine, stuck with bugs Bethesda’s been dragging along since Skyrim and Fallout 4. (the power armor glitches are still there, for instance)- Weapons are "enchanted" under the hood. Scorched Beasts? Reskinned dragons.  - Netcode is laughably bad—24 players per map, yet it feels like an indie multiplayer experiment. Valheim did it better with a simpler peer-to-peer model, while Fallout 76 relies on an unreliable client-server setup.---📖 Gameplay and Storytelling  - Starts as a shallow, uninspired Fallout experience with mandatory online access.  - Post-Wastelanders, the story gets a bit better with NPCs and quests, but it’s still nowhere near the level of earlier Fallout games.  - Choices barely matter, if at all. Do not expect any RPG-like depth.- Around level 100 or so, the cracks start showing. By endgame, you’re just playing out of guilt, habit, or the hope that the next season will finally be good. And you're still somehow enjoyin it.---🔍 Hidden Mechanics  - Most in-game systems are either poorly explained or not explained at all.  - You'll keep stumbling across how things actually work hundreds of hours in—or find out by mistake online.  - This just makes things more confusing and frustrating than they need to be.---🛠 Bugs, Glitches, and Economy  - Bugs, glitches, and coding horrors are everywhere.  - Cheaters ruined the economy early on, duplicating items and hacking gear. Bethesda’s done some cleanup, but the damage hasn’t gone away completely.  - Overall, the game’s still far less stable than it should be in 2024.---👥 Multiplayer and Community  - Only 24 players per map, so the world feels surprisingly empty for an online game.  - The community is the only reason the game is tolerable—friendly, patient, and oddly indulgent of all its problems.  - Bethesda’s communication with players is still pretty terrible, even if it’s slightly better now than during its most infamous flops.---🍔 Comfort Food or Bad Habit?  Fallout 76 feels like comfort food—great for hanging out with friends or turning your brain off for a while.  But it’s a bad habit, and worse, it keeps you from trying better games that actually deserve your time and money. (trying to keep things short here :P)---🚫 Final Verdict:  I can’t recommend a bad habit. Don't start. And yes... I’m so guilty of it.

_childDocuments_.review: I really feel like I should preface this, I played both the original release launch and now the current NPC released update. I got this game for free as a gift from a friend who really wanted to play with me and I was hooked...But I feel extremely ripped off, getting the game, FOR FREE. I want you all to know that.This game is still the absolute buggiest multiplayer AAA mess I think I really have ever seen and all the positive ratings absolutely confuse me because I had the patience to try this game over and over, only to constantly feel like I was always getting robbed. NPC's are not even remotely polished either, considering I've wasted hundreds of resources of caps and ammo and junk to have the NPC not want to do the thing it's programmed to do, like talk to another NPC. One or twice, its a bethesda game... over 5 or so times? No, that doesn't get to slide.The quests are still an awful mess with some improvement here and there, but overall it is still just horrible. I've tried one where I needed to get a certain bug part... only for all the spawns to suddenly NOT want to give me said bugs anymore EVEN IN THE AREA HIGHLIGHTED THAT THE GAME WANTS YOU TO GO. NPC's are going to often bug out and not do anything, or crash your game and force you to restart everything with all your resources lost to the wind. Because that's fair. Once or twice is a given, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ten is just a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ disaster.The servers are still a jittering mess, constantly jumping frames even on the most stable of computers. Your frames will stutter, you will crash for no good reason, and even freezing just the same. There's no way to tell when it will happen, it just happens. _childDocuments_.review: Update 8/25/24  Someone at Bethesda has their head way up their.... I constantly see things that make it seem like all they care about is getting your money, rather than making this game a great experience.  the uproar over the legendary cores converting to scrip.. yikes. and because of that uproar, I saw references to the canvas bag debacle..  WOW.. just WOW.. if I had heard about that before buying this game on sale for $8, I would not have even given them $8 for it..    #$%^ these guys.  I think I'm done playing this game.Good job Bethesda...   maybe writing scenarios for quests in your games made you into the big greedy soulless corporation you portray big business as in your games..   Update 6/30/24    [Recommended.. with the caveat that, if you are a fan of the single player Fallout games, and particularly, their mod-ability... THIS IS NOT THAT.  And.. if you are ok with paying a subscription for a game, (I'm not) then some of the annoyances will be less so]Ok, I've gotta be honest, I'm enjoying the game..  what it took was figuring out how to play around the artificial restrictions.  they deliberately give you limited storage space in the hopes that it will.. I dunno.. annoy you so much that you will pay for the subscription..?  Gone is the ability, as with playing single player Fallout, to mod out the annoyances to your hearts content..  instead, I had to learn that if I want this game to actually be fun, I can't play it like I have always played all of the single player predecessors. Once I started ruthlessly getting rid of the stuff that MIGHT be fun to try.. some day.. you know, you pick up some cool legendary weapon with great stats.. that would only work if you had a completely different build, And because of the way you continue to earn perk cards, even after you've stopped earning any more SPECIAL points..  you might think.. oh, hold on to that, and I can eventually get the cards to re-spec and try different builds. Yeahhhh... no.  You can only keep the armor, weapons and food/aid that you ACTIVELY/REGULARLY use for one build..  (maybe two, if they are similar) You also have to routinely sell off the crafting materials once they reach a certain threshold (a stack of 100 for most things, and for a few particular resources that I tend to need more of (for instance the resources needed for repairing your guns), the limit is 300 or 400), because that junk/crafting resources WILL ADD UP FAST.  I had like, 200 lbs of steel in my stash. Once you stop hoarding anything and everything... THEN when you come across a stash box on your adventures, you will actually have space in your stash to dump stuff that you've been collecting while out and about, so you don't get over-encumbered, so that you can continue to play.. and then, at the end of the "day", you can go on your once a day selling spree at a train station or one of the major settlements and empty out your stash.. as much as you can before the vendors run out of caps (another annoyingly arbitrary restriction.   ...and i get it.. it's multiplayer.. you have to take into account the people who have no life whatsoever, except playing games, who would just leave everyone else in the dust because they could keep earning caps if there were not a game wide (fairly small) daily caps pool that all vendors share.  but it does seem pretty ridiculous that just because you cleaned out this vendors caps, now everywhere else in the world, no one will buy any of your junk anymore)So, yeah..  once you figure out that you can't play it the way you played the single player fallout games, and you have to work around the built in annoyances, the game can be a lot of fun. (still annoyed, but I can work within their design parameters.)  Update 6/12/24.  Wow..   more bad taste in my mouth from this game. Seasons? what is that? had no idea I even HAD points to spend...  what a great way to find out... "guess you missed your window to spend the points you didn't know you were getting..  and they are just gone now.. ha ha  F you!"      yeah yeah.. totally my fault that I didn't research this game... that I didn't know I had to do homework to make sure I knew all the ins and outs so I wouldn't miss anything..  whatever.  What a lame Developer.   It's not like I even care about any of the rewards you could spend the tickets on..  but, wow...  they really seem to not care much at all about the player experience.  just want to get your money. this game is designed to be annoying as hell and goes out of it's way to push you toward a 1st subscription. I'm actually not sure I ever want to give Bethesda any of my money ever again.....   hope you screwed over enough suckers with your 1st subscription to make it worth scaring off long time fans of your games.    I'll keep playing this game, because I want to see where the story goes.. but yeah... you may have lost a customer Bethesda.  not that you probably care..  there are lots of idiots who will still throw their money at you.Update 5/7/24: ok, it's definitely got some charm to it.. but like I said below, mostly it's the multiplayer aspect that saves it. if it wasn't multiplayer, I would have quit already. It's just as glitchy as any of the other fallout games, and it's purposefully made in such a way as to make it real enticing to want to pay for a Fallout 1st subscription... "oh...  ran out of storage space already?  well here is a fix for that.. you only need to give us real world money on a recurring basis, and problem solved!"  um...  no thank you. it's not THAT good of a game... and paying money to fix an issue you put in the game to make people want to give you money to fix... kind of a ♥♥♥♥ move.So I will play this game for as long as my friend and I are having fun with it..  but once the tedium of micromanaging your inventory and your stash, and your power cores, and your legendaries, and....    ugh.. yeah, once that overwhelms the fun parts..  I guess it's time to go install a heavily modded Fallout 4 again.    Still not recommended.. but if it's on sale (my friend got it for me for $8..  I definitely would not suggest paying any more than that for it) and you have always wanted to shoot the heads off of Supermutants with a friend by your side, then go for it.Update 4/19/24: started working... my recommendation after playing for a couple of evenings..  it's alright.  I guess it's worth the $8 when on sale.  I wouldn't say it's worth full price. What made Bethesda games great was the modding community that turned the turd games Bethesda dished out into some amazing experiences.  However, they were always a solitary experience.. until now.  So the multiplayer kind of saves Fallout 76... but just barely.  We'll see if my friend and I can get into some hi-jinx to make it a memorable experience or not... might be back to update, might not... but yeah... initial verdict is..  eh.. [shrug]Original post:Complete garbage..  doesn't ever get past "Signing in..."after Bethesda's pathetic cash grab in selling VR versions of Fallout 4 and Skyrim that they did no work on AT ALL to make actually work in VR, I kind of wrote Bethesda off...  only got Fallout 76 as a gift from a friend because it was on sale.. but, oh look..  another Bethesda game that doesn't work. _childDocuments_.review: First, hear me out:I love this game, I'm a sucker for everything Fallout ever since Fallout 3, and there's some real fun to be had in this game, I for one have almost 1000 hours of play time at the time of writing this review, but there are some things that you should know if you haven't followed the (mess of a) progress this game have had through it's time.FIRST: The negative stuffBugs, a lot of bugs, from not being able to simply fast travel at first try due to someone (or even you) having a mutation that's supposed to just heal you outside of battle to people (read: jerks) being able to buy stuff that you're actually not selling, this game is riddled with bugs, to the point that I wonder if Bethesda's team actually know what they're doing when they try to fix something and inevitably brake 5 other very unrelated things... It gets messy real quick. Most of the (worst) bugs have been fixed by now, but it's pretty common to read of new "features" (let's call it that) being "added" to the game every other week.The game does NOT run very well on anything other than Windows 10 OS, I suffered quite of problems (namely stutter issues) when I had a Windows 7 install and then I moved to Linux, only to find that, after a few weeks of perfectly good gameplay, the issues started there too. I think this is quite intentional by Bethesda since they were aquired by Microsoft, which in by itself is well known of employing some really shady mob tactics to get it's products into more computers. There's nothing in this game that should technically require Windows 10 or any of its features, and it even says on the "recommended" system requirements that it fully supports 7, 8 and 10 equally. Well I can say that it does run fairly smooth on Windows 10 but not on any of the others (Linux w/proton included), so consider yourself warned.NOW, the GOOD stuffThe community - this game has one of the nicest communities you'll find in a game, especially with this low of a reputation. Servers are usually filled with people that are very noob friendly and will go out of their way to help you on your low level tasks. I had some really good social experiences just by finding strangers and commenting on their camp.Trading -this is where F76 really shines in my opinion, when you're done with the main Wastelanders, Enclave and Brotherhood questlines, you'll be fairly high leveled to start some trading with other high leveled players, there are quite a lot of trading forums with a reputation system like Reddit's Market76 and the trading discord server. You're bound to have some really good experiences.The guns - the last good point in this game is, in my opinion, the guns. The vast majority of weapons have a very good feeling and are very fun to use, the gunplay is most excellent for a game that is considered more of a RPG nature.So, if you're willing to accept its flaws, F76 can be quite rewarding and fun to play, but its good moments are not enough for me to recommend new players to get into. Only venture into this game if you, like me, really, and I mean really, like Fallout.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best time to play Fallout 76.As somebody who barely lasted a month playing this game when it first came out and I decided to start from scratch with Wastelanders and I'm so happy with my experience so far. You can tell from the moment you finish making your character in the vault and NOT CRASHING that they made a lot work optimizing the game:- The loading times are better than before, The game doesn't stutter or drop frames like it used to; in the past I'd barely even get 30fps but now it barely goes below 70fps and when it does it sits around 55-58fps with almost maxed out settings.- The game is smooth, and I mean that in terms of interactions; seamlessly looting and scrapping stuff and going in and out of exterior locations (not to forget the fact that there are barely any interior locations which means less loading screens unlike FO4,) and in terms of latency; it's barely noticeable now and it doesn't get in the way of your enjoyment anymore, and the combat which is much smoother and enjoyable now; the A.I. is much closer to what we had in FO4 and not the brain dead enemies who either stand in place while looking at you not even shooting at you or rushing at you like maniacs like before, and when you shoot you ACTUALLY GET INSTANT FEEDBACK and not five minutes after shooting (if you played the game pre-wastelanders you know what I mean.)- The amount of content in this game is scary, I'm still in the beginning and I'm already overwhelmed... I guess it's time to waste +1000hrs of my life on this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I even get into my review of this game I will start with my biggest complaint about this game:  nothing about this game feels like it was intended for the PC community. If you hit the scroll wheel, it opens a radial menu. One of the most frustrating thing is using the menus in game because they are designed for analog sticks and not a mouse. I found the best way to navigate the menus is using C and Z and the various keyboard commands because you are going to have a headache trying to keep your mouse perfectly on the tiny "invite to party" or "fast travel" option. Now, lets get into it,Is this a good Fallout game? No. Not in any sense of the wordIs this a good first person shooter? No.Is this a good multiplayer game? No.Is this a good MMO? No.Then why the ♥♥♥♥ am i recommending this game?As a fallout game this is lacking anything that feels like fallout. It is bright, vibrant your first clue this isnt a fallout game is the rainbow loading screen, gone is the, "war... war never changes" with Ron Pearlman narrating our view of a burnt out abandoned wastes. But that in itself does not make this a bad game. You just have to accept the fact that there are going to be a bunch of people hopping around with jetpacks and mutations jumping 100ft in the air dressed as clowns with bugged guns shooting weird plasma energy flame thrower 50cal machine guns. Can that be fun? No doubt. Who doesnt want to jump 1000 feet using cheat guns? But is that "fallout" I say no.Is this a good multiplayer game? No, because with many of the quests i find it frustrating that i cannot actually complete them with my friends. For example, my friend is the party leader for the group and we are both on the same quest. He enters the instance as the party leader and I go in to help him. We are both on the same quest yet as i help him complete his quest I don't requiring us to finish his quest line and return to the beginning so that I can complete mine. This is bad design. We should, as a part of 4 with my IRL friends be able to adventure and quest together. Yet despite the fact this is an MMO the actual quests are designed for solo play.Is this a good FPS? Well, considering the majority of my gaming time these days is dedicated to ARMA3 and Escape From Tarkov I would say no. But it isn't as bad a as lot of MMO first person shooters it doesnt feel like im shooting numbers out of my enemies like other games i've played but the guns just dont feel particularly unique to the point i have a preference, in traditional fallout games you might prefer energy weapons over bullets or vice versa. Here, just take the best legendary weapon you have available and do away with explosives, grenades and landmines are heavy and useless. If you arent using some sort of beam splitter or some ♥♥♥♥ you are essentially handicapping yourself.Is this a good MMO? No, not by a long shot. It does not feel massive and it does not feel like a multiplayer game. But, it does not have a monthly subscription which is a huge bonus for me and Bethesda is actively improving the game. With the release of Seasons I actually have a reason to hop on and play if only to complete the season. The introduction of daily and weekly tasks is great in that it adds something to do and gives some much needed direction sorely lacking from the actual quests lines. As well as things I can actually accomplish with my friends, "hey dude wanna go hunt 20 ghouls using golf clubs?" instead spending 2 hours repeating the same questline 4 times so all my friends and I can actually play together.But again, why am I recommending this game? Because I received this game as a gift from a friend who just wanted another game we could play together that wasn't a punch to the testicles like Tarkov. The initial early game is extremely boring but once you hit ~20 the game starts to open up and becomes much more enjoyable. Granted I complained more than anyone on my way to level 20 and while most of my friends quit the game after 3 hours of play I wanted to give this game an honest try and at around level 26 is when I found myself actively wanting to play the game. Granted, I dont care about the quest lines or the lore any more its just a great time burner. I can hop on with my friend (the only one who plays) do a few events knock out a few daily tasks and log off.I see potential in this game if Bethesda continues to improve it and I have been surprised how friendly the actual player base is. Random people helping me get legendary items and such is unlike any MMO experience I've ever had and that alone is enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: **edit: Steel Dawn Launched a week early and seems to have improved server stability and fixed many bugs, in addition to being (so far) a great story content addition.**This game came out to a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of negative hype.  Some of it was deserved, some of it was not.Server stability was bad at launch. It was.  They weren't prepared. But, on the other side of that same coin, Diablo 3 was unplayable for several days at launch, and that was from the company who reinvented the MMO genre and brought it to the mainstream.  Online launches typically have server issues.One of the main crying points among complainers was the lack of NPC's and that the game felt empty.  This was a design decision, and a story decision.It was supposed to be empty and desolate.  We were supposed to be the first humans emerging from the vault.The game had robot npc's, and one questgiver in particular (a nannybot who thinks she's a raider) was fully voiced, to great effect.Now though, there are tons of human NPC's a few ghouls, and a super mutant npc, all fully voiced.  There are more traditional quest hubs, factions, and story arcs.  The other survivors have returned and the game is no longer empty.There have been immense improvements to every aspect of the game.99% of content can be done solo, and you can play for hours without interacting with another player if you wish, but if you want to group it's been made much easier with the introduction of public groups and the passive buffs you get just by joining.Many of the public events now give a server-wide announcement and allow you to fast-travel to them for free, also you can look at the event on the map, and see how long ago it started, how many players are participating and give yourself an idea of whether or not it's worth your time to stop what you're doing and join.  This is being done right. It brought back vibes from the old mmo Rift.  Public events and world bosses pop up, and people come together and defeat them. You don't have to have a guild or a group of hardcore friends, just jump in and start shooting/slapping/whatever you do.The player economy is gated to 1400 caps per day from selling to vendors.  People hated this, but now instead of each of 7 factions having a 200 cap vendor pool, they all share one 1400 cap pool, which is an improvement.  Also the addition of player vending machines gives a way to earn caps outside that(other than enemy cash drops and event rewards) by selling items, mainly crafting recipes and certain aid items and some of the rarer ammunition.The CAMP system lets you build a little base for yourself but unlike fallout 4, it's yours, and Preston m****rf*****g Garvey won't verbally assault you every three seconds because "aNoThEr SeTtLeMeNt nEeDs yOuR HeLp!!!!!!!!!"There are certain items that people consider Pay To Win.  I can see the argument, but I don't agree.  To me, the vast majority of these items are Pay To Convenience.  Like a refrigerator that will make food items spoil more slowly (yes the game has survival aspects, but I don't think you can die from hunger/thirst) or repair kits that allow you to repair a weapon or armor in the field without going to a crafting station.  The one exception to this is the scrapbox, which allows storage of unlimited scrap items and to me, removes the inventory management aspect of the game for subscription players.Anyway, that's a hype-free opinion from one actual player, instead of some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ youtuber trying to make stuff sound terrible and scandalous for more clicks.If you read this, and it piqued your interest, don't be afraid to give it a try.  The community is overwhelmingly positive, and people will go outof their way to help you if they find out you're new.  You don't really see toxic players, unless you Are a toxic player (they did something to keep toxic people on their own toxic servers I think.)

_childDocuments_.review: Ahh Fallout 1st, the single most effective way to torch all the goodwill Bathesda had accrued over the years, hard earned by many great games from the fallout, Skyrim, and Doom series.The only reason I got this game is because I loved fallout 3, Vegas, and 4, and I had pre-ordered it before Bathesda ripped off everyone by pay walling content. I activated it on steam and tried the wastlanders content, decided that if I was going to give it a fair shake I may as well try out one month of Fallout 1st. the game has potential, but still need major work to get anywhere near the game that it could have been.They pay walled basic functionality, and add content to the atoms store all the while their game is still a bug riddled mess, AI's still teleport across the map, and lag sprint at mach 10, as the server hitches, AI sometimes lay crumpled on the ground with a models bug. You can still get stuck in workbenches, terminals, doors and other game objects.The "Private game" performance lags and hitches as if it is being hosted by a hamster powered server from time to time, shot registration in private games especially after loading an area is spotty.when Fallout 76 launched there was a huge controversy when they ripped off everyone who bought the game with bait and switch, broken promises, and by saying the were not going to do refunds, and got forced to in several countries. they screwed everyone over by excluding basic game content like private games (promised power cores, find dead AI etc, all the while paying the same amount as it would cost to host a 4-8 man server of any other coop game, what a ripoff. there is no persistence with the workshops, after intercepted, inventory stolen, than sure get 1 month like I did and play it until the dull empty void that is Appalachia gets unbearable and then cancel like I did.Bathesda really missed the mark with _childDocuments_.review: I bought this game in late October 2020 and I already have 150 hours, this is my favourite ever game. When I first loaded into the game I wasn't entirely sure what to expect, for the first couple of hours I did some of the main story and was greeted by many NPC's. After completing some of the main story line I decided to explore Appalachia and was instantly amazed.This game's map is stunning, I have a mid-tier PC and have enjoyed the warm scenery quite nicely. The MAP IS HUGE. I've spent so many hours just exploring this vast wasteland - 150 hours in and I'm still discovering new locations and cave systems and so on. The landscapes range from big valleys and harsh hills making the game feel so much bigger. I guarantee you many people will love exploring this.This game offers so much to grind for, I'm always grinding to level up and unlock new perk cards to work on my fallout build - perk cards in this game make such a big difference to your play style. I've unlocked so many high level legendary guns yet I still get so excited to find a new one. With Bethesda's adding a free battle pass each season I always have something to grind and play for.As many of you know Bethesda had a very rocky start when this game released. As a new player I have seen nothing but more and more new content get added to this game giving FO76's players something to grind for, Bethesda still care's for the F076 community and it really is starting to show.FO76's community is the nicest community I have ever seen. As a new player many higher level randoms would help me out and give me weapons or meds to help me survive Appalachia. Everyone is the community is extremely caring.As a new player I have experienced LESS BUGS in Fallout 76 than I have in my 17 HOURS of FALLOUT 4 on PC. I have never once experienced a game breaking bug. Many fallout fan's come to this game looking a very story driven game and get upset (This is quite multiplayer driven, duh). I see so much hate for this game especially die-hard New Vegas fans and that hate on this game without giving it a try. Hell yeah you could've hated on this game when it released go ahead, but in it's current state its so unnecessary as the main arguments/myths are...(a) this game's bugs are horrible and make it impossible to play -incorrect (b) this is nothing like the original fallout's, they destroyed the fallout lore! -this is a multiplayer game focused on working together as a community with or without friends(c) this game relies on micro transactions and is based around spending money -incorrect (you don't need to spend a single dollar on this game once you've purchased it)I bought this game on 60% off but I'd be more than happy to buy it at full price. In it's current state I think many people will be very happy with the purchase. 10/10 would easily buy again.

_childDocuments_.review: It pains me to be this negative toward Bethesda, since they not to so long ago was my favorite developer and easily the studio with the game series I have put the most amount of hours into. In the recent past though, (probably after Skyrim), they have really gone down the pipe in almost all areas imaginable and it is really sad and painful to see ones favorite developer and game series get tainted like this. If I look back at the old Bethesda it seems they where one of the most passionate studios in the industry with the integrity to go their own way and with the single goal of creating the most open RPG experiences possible with the most immersive worlds they could create. It really felt like that was their grand vision and that all their talent was focused on that goal with nothing really getting in the way of that vision and it really shined through their games.Now they are among the most disgraceful in the business along side studios like Ubisoft and EA and sadly it seems to not change. These days it is microtransactions, card games, mobile games, subscription models, blatant "diversity" at the cost of quality and consistency, WoW clones, battle royale, limited time "offers," forced online and loot boxes that seem to be the priority instead of what was the priority in the past of creating the most immersive worlds possible. I hate to play with other players, especially in something like Fallout or Elder Scrolls so it is smart of Bethesda to force you to pay extra for being able to play solo. Smart. But extremely disgraceful. I don't need my own "server" to play solo, just give me an Offline mode where I can play the game normally in piece as I would any other game in the series without having a constant internet connection or any of that crap. I would more gladly pay full price for that vs a subscription even though I already paid full price for the retail version of Fallout 76 previously.It is also very annoying when It is impossible to take the world in Fallout 76 seriously when almost every character you hear or read about in the game is female and it is so obvious how they are trying to push the new trendy "strong womanz" agenda in a way that you almost could think that someone like Anita Sarkeesian was involved in this behind the scenes. There is even a sort of super hero underground "batman" base with exclusively super skilled women "super heroes" who appraently can kill 100 of raiders on their own. Just recently read in one database in the game about some guy named Freddy who is a real badass and miss his girl. Oh wait, no wait, "his" name was actually Freddie and it was a girl and it was her girlfriend she was talking about. This would not be bad in isolated cases, but the problem is that the whole game is filled with this and it gets completely ridiculous at times. I am not against women or any other group in games or any other art form, but it hurts the art when it is this blatantly "pushed" in this completely obvious way at the cost of the internal logic and believability of the world. Horizon Zero Dawn is a good example of a game with a strong female lead that does not feel contrived or like they made the lead female just because of some diversity/feminist quota to fill, or even better yet something like the female lead in the masterpiece of a movie Sicario. You can really see if someone respects the art they are making in the way they handle it and where they try to fill each role in the game/movie in a way that makes the most sense. The Godfather would not be a masterpiece and a work of integrity but a sort of wacky ridiculous comedy if they had to push for a quota of at least 50% women in the roles in that movie, even though it does not make any sense to do so in the context of the roles in the movie. It is sad to see when developers do not respect their art in the same way. Sure on could argue that Fallout is actually a sort of comedy (which it is in many ways) that one does not need to take so seriously so it does not matter if the new Raider faction is almost completely made up of females with a butch female leader at the top, even if that scenario would never be the case in real life and does not make any sense even in the games own internal logic. Heck there are mutants and monsters in this game so why so mad? The problem is though that the mutants and monsters actually make sense in the games own internal logic and universe, there is an explanation for them being there. There is no explanation to why the most badass raiders are almost all females, it is just obviously made that way because strong brutish females are the ideal in this outlook and the "quota" for them must be filled. It honestly would make more sense if it was they other way around with even more traditional gender roles in this universe since the culture of the games universe is sort of stuck in the 50:s. It would at least be a little bit less bad if there actually was some sort of contrived  "explanation" for why things are this way. Perhaps Vault Tec was experimenting with giving females huge doses of testosterone before the war so that they become much more aggressive. In short though it just does not make sense and it hurts the games internal logic and the sense that this is actually a "different universe" you are visiting and believing in where there is an internal logic to everything that makes you believe in that world. Something that again seemed to be a great priority at Bethesda before above scoring political good boy points. It is also very annoying to get back into the game after a year and still see many incredible simple things that would be fixed by modders in a matter of hours or days that are just totally ignored even after years of updates. For me specifically I just want something like the immersive hud that was a mod for Skyrim etc that made the HUD behave dynamic and show only when I actually needed it which enhances immersion greatly. I don't need to see all the HUD clutter on the screen at all times but for some reason there is an option to toggle off the crosshair and floating pointers, but not stuff like the compass etc and it seems the person who designed the options thought just having a HUD visibility slider is enough as a compensation even though using it to hide the hud elements makes Everything invisible, even what you are about to loot when over a container so you can't even see what you are about to pick up from a closed container which is just genius in design taken to a whole new level.I don't enjoy bashing either this game or Bethesda this hard and I would give very much to see they return to their grace and glory days. I really have my hopes in that Elder Scrolls 6 will be the game where they redeem themself and where we get that amazing experience of stepping into another world again where all the focus is on creating that world to be as immersive as possible. Where we can just play and experience that amazing world without having to be annoyed and nagged by forced online servers, microtransactions, loot boxes, battle royale and solo play subscription DLC. I am holding all my thumbs for that and that I can think and respect Bethesda as one of my favorite developers again some day.

_childDocuments_.review: Growing up I was always a Skyrim fan, I watched my cousin play New Vegas for roughly an hour one time. When Fallout 76 launched I bought it day 1 on PS4. I had a blast! It was mind boggling how many bugs were in the game, many preventing progression in the main story. It was fixed in about a week. I played all the way up to level 180.Around 2022 I came back but on PC starting a new character. The play-through was substantially more enjoyable the second time around. Very minimal bugs, nothing gamebreaking that I ran into. The game still felt extremely unoptimized with hard stutters and constant frame drops.FFW Early June 2024 I start a new playthrough. There have been many content updates since release, Many new questlines and stories to be found. The game feels so much smoother than it used to, atleast for me, maybe I'm just buggin. There is an occasional server issue but for the most part I am enjoying the game.Fallout 1st kinda sucks because an ammo box and scrab box save you so much space in the stash (being infinite storage space for ammo and scrap respectively). I can fully recommend this game if you just like to explore, find new gear, and put together different style builds. There are many ways to run around the wasteland. If you are enjoying the game and want Fallout 1st for the storage space, when your subscription ends you can still access bins and grab your resources, just can't put them back in. If the game is on sale (which it is $10 at time of writing) I suggest picking it up and giving it a try!Here's to hours exploring The Wasteland!

_childDocuments_.review: Considering the recent influx of players, I thought it was a great time to review this game.I had initially had the pre-order version of Fallout 76.  I was onboard the hype train and I was eating all the spoon fed BS that Todd Howard was feeding me.  I Jumped into my exclusive early access weekend and........I hated it.  Buggy, no content, no direction, griefing..  I immediately requested a refund.Cut to a year or so later...My brother tells me that it's on sale and it's not all that bad these days - certainly worth the  sub $10 price paid.  I give FO76 a second chance.    it mostly looks the same, but after a while I'm getting that it's all so much better.   There's quests.. there's NPC's that aren't tapes or robots, there's a general distinct lack of griefing.  It's fun.  Nearly 800 hours later, it's still fun.  It's the single most helpful and nice gaming community on the internet.  Is this game for you?Do you  like a casual dopamine treadmill?  This isn't a constant action game.  You can go AFK (not at a vendor please).  Death is mildly inconvenient - you lose the junk you are holding.  you never stop leveling, once you own all the perk cards, you then start filling up your legendary perks.  You get your gear then you start trying to roll the perfect combination of legendary effects (i.e. gambling - but without much loss).  You gather plans and build cool camps and have people marvel at the cool crap you've collected.   You can even trade a lot of the really good stuff you make for other really good stuff. Monetization model:  Do you NEED to be a subscriber?  No.  Each season there's a bunch or rewards you get for completing daily quests and other activities, you get free atoms (in game currency) and there's almost always a way to get the cool stuff for free.  Fallout 1st Subscriptions just add one major convenience - inventory space.   If you are collecting everything and crafting everything and keeping multiple armor and weapon sets for multiple gameplay styles (builds) you will face the last endgame boss - storage space.  Fallout 1st. gives you 2 unlimited storage containers- Ammo and scrap.   Do you need it? no, is it really convenient?  yes. Are you paying to solve a problem that Bethesda artificially created? Yes! From a revenue perspective they were going to gate-keep something behind money.  They had the choice:  Progress? Appearance? Advantage? They chose convenience.  I say, play it - it's friendly, fun, and it's casual.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I wouldn't listen to a lot of the negative reviews. Many of them either haven't played the new update and are reviewing the base game, and/or are just regurgitating what uninformed youtubers say about the game. Just play the game and see for yourself. It is a Bethesda open world Fallout game. If that interests you, then buy it. There are NPCs now so the primary complaint about this game that existed for so long is largely irrelevant now. And honestly, in some ways I would say this is even better than Fallout 4. 76 features a silent protagonist and a return to the more traditional style of dialogue with a plethora of interesting options and skills checks. The world is huge and diverse. The quests(that I have played so far) have lots of options. Factions with a reputation system. Deep crafting mechanics. Yes there are microtransactions. But they are NOT pay to win like many of the negative people are saying. Some convenience items sure, but nothing major. If you don't want to participate in it, then don't. Its as simple as that. Or if there is something in the Atom Shop that you just can't live without, earn Atoms in game and buy it that way. Thats what I always did.Overall I would recommend this game if you want another open world Fallout experience

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a history full of pain, suffering, disappointment, lies and greed. The state the game released in was unacceptable, like, actually 3/10 game. Then the whole drama with the 'canvas' bags and the moldy power armor helmets happened. Then there was the big outrage around Fallout 1st.Also, before anyone wonders, I used to be pretty high level, until Badthesda decided to turn off their launcher and didn't let me link my Badthesda account to my Steam account, thats why I only have 31 hours during the time of this review.This game was in a state that many, me including, thought to be unrecovable from, but somehow, they actually did it. Exactly 4 years ago when the Wastelanders expansion released. Suddenly, the game evolved from a 3/10 to a 6/10. Upon that new foundation, they build more and more, until we reach current day The Pitt. The rating of 6/10 has not changed, but the moment where you reach endgame has. Basically, the moment you reach endgame, the game goes back down to a 3/10. Endgame, at least what I consider to be endgame, is when you finished every quest in the game, after that, your goal now is to just get stronger for the sake of getting stronger... this is horrible. I mean, some people enjoy watching numbers go up, but I personally do like myself some actual gameplay. The quests themselves are literally all fetch or extermination quests, except for a few exceptions here and there, but at least its actually something to do, other than just mindless grinding for the sake of grinding, and also, what do you expect from an online RPG game? Huge cinematic quests with a bunch of cutscenes that last for like 20 hours of playtime? Lmao no.The endgame being this bad may deter some people from buying this game, which is understandable, but also know that you do have quests for a few hundred hours of playtime, so if you can get the game for 7 - 15€ somewhere, its worth it, at least if you also enjoyed Fallout 4.Now that I have been talking a lot of ♥♥♥♥ about the game in this review, let me name some things that I actually like.The map is amazing, and by the map, I don't mean the games map, but the actual map you get when you press M or Esc. The whole map is colorful and there are little pictures everywhere that you can use to orientate yourself. For example if you want to look up the map location of a place, instead of having to match lines and other locations with the image the guide provided, you can just compare the dozens of pictures and colors on the map with the guide you are looking at, ♥♥♥♥ is super easy and quick to do.The C.A.M.P system is also ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ epic, I mean, it does make me want to die occasionally, with some things not snapping correctly or at all, how there is barely any flat terrain, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ like me not being allowed to remove stairs due to part of the structure being "no longer accessible" according to the game, things apparently intersecting with invisible objects or things floating despite being on the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ground, and overall some limitations that severely hinder creative freedom. But the mere concept itself I love. Search for a location you find cool, go into your inventory, press Z, place, build your dream house... with the limited possibilites the game gives you lmao.Weapons feel pretty satisfying to use, which is not thanks to Bethesda being good at making games, its because ID made the shooting for Fallout 4, and Fallout 76 is basically just Fallout 4: Online, so its the same.The perk card system is pretty epic. I love build making, problem is that build making in Fallout 4 was barely a thing, because you could just kind of choose whatever perks you wanted. In this game they fixed this by having perk cards instead of just perks. You can level perk cards up and if you level them up, their stat requirement cost goes up by 1. So basically, if you have 3 strength, then you can either equip one level 3 card, three level 1 cards or one level 2 card and one level 1 card. This system works fairly well and I cant think of a way to improve it.Overall, like I already said, game is a 6/10 until you reach endgame, after that it goes down to a 3 and I don't think anyone will be blaming you for quitting at that moment. If you liked Fallout 4, then get the game. If you liked Fallout 4 and actually have friends to play with, definitely get the game.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Still very buggy, though I havent encountered anything progress halting or game-breaking. Microtransactions are NOT pay to win, despite what people say (except scrap box, definitely can be considered an unfair advantage). Game itself is very fun, with my favorite map from the series and lots of unique locations. Story isn't anything special, but the voice acting makes it more than bearable. Overall, a solid game if you can look past the bugs, and I recommend it to fans of the series willing to look past these cons.     So, I bought the game on Bethesda a few days before Wastelanders released, as I wanted to experience the game in its original state to see how much of a difference Wastelanders would make. First few hours were incredibly boring, and I almost regretted buying it. However, I pushed through and started to see how the game could be enjoyable. I enjoyed putting together stories through the holotapes I'd come across, and felt a strong sense of progress through leveling and starting to find more powerful weapons. However, like many of the complaints around the launch, the world felt lonely.     Wastelanders drops. I'm around level 25, with a good chunk of story completed, and immediately start the Wastelanders story. Right off the bat, the dialogue system felt better than ever, with view & DoF shifts, good voice acting, and likable characters. Skill checks & Fallout 3/NV dialogue menu return, which was a big relief. I play through the story, making steady progress and enjoying myself as I go. There were a few quests I hated (looking at you, Hornwright HQ), but aside from those it felt great. By the time I finished the story, I was level 50 with a solid setup.     Thats fine and all, but what about the world itself? With Wastelanders, many locations were revamped to include raiders, settlers, and other human factions. Some of these small locations are now my favorite to visit, as they really feel lived in, with their own small stories. There are now random encounters, many of which put a big smile on my face. Whether its two robots stuck in a conversation loop, settlers who need help fighting off local fauna, or wandering storytellers with tales of cryptids, they all felt unique and fitting of the world.     Next, the gameplay loop. The endgame is VERY grindy, and in a way many wont like. The new currency is capped at 200 a day, with many of the best plans costing over a thousand. I didn't get very invested in this grind, though, and still managed to get another 60+ hours out of the game. I loved walking around the world and trying to find every new location I could, finding spots to farm legendary weapons, helping new players with events, and slowly shifting my build from sneaky sniper to huge unarmed damage. While there is a clear meta for builds, you can very easily get by in the hardest areas using whatever build you want, as long as you pay some sort of attention to your damage output. Overall, the endgame is mainly focused on getting good legendary rolls, unlocking new blueprints for weapons, and perfecting/changing your build.     I see many complaints about the game that are either incredibly biased, misinformed, or straight up false information. On the "P2W" front, the only non cosmetic purchases are scrap kits, which allow you to store whatever scrap you have remotely (which is not worth it in the slightest), and repair kits, to repair on the go. However, there are repair benches scattered EVERYWHERE. You can barely go 30 minutes without finding AT LEAST one bench, and if thats not enough, there are free repair kits that are BETTER than the paid ones, which you get simply by killing an endgame boss, which many high level players grind. The only remotely P2W aspect comes from fallout 1st, of which complaints are completely valid. Unlimited scrap storage allows you to hold many more legendary drops, consumables, etc, which is a pretty sizable advantage. However, none of this allows you to get better gear, stats, or character progression than free players.     Rounding out this stupid long review that's probably a waste of time, is it worth the price? If you're on the fence, I suggest waiting for a sale. If you're a big fan and have seen gameplay that REALLY interests you, then I say go ahead and pay what you want. This game gripped me harder than almost any other game for nearly 3 weeks straight, which is unheard of for me (i usually only play a game for a couple weeks tops before getting burnt out and swapping games). I personally don't care about Bethesda's lying about the impossibility of features, only to add them later, as it has 0 effect on my enjoyment of the game, however I understand why many look down on it and refuse to purchase the game because of it.anyways any negative reviews are nitpicking and biased, i win, bye bye

_childDocuments_.review: This game has something for everyone. Very fun and lots to do. Play solo or with friends.Pros:*Decent graphics*Smooth gameplay*Lots of plans and recipes for crafting to unlock*Lots of skins*Lots of guns and armors and modifcations*Lots of quests and active events that trigger for random online players to all gather and work together to slay the event boss/enemies for drop-loot, xp and story completion*New Player Friendly*Good community willing to help and guide*You can randomize your own weapons and armor with Legendary buffs via reroll anytime.*There is hunger and thirst, status affects and radiation measurements to take into account.*Lots of perks to choose from and slots to save custom builds to make swapping them, faster/easier but not really necessary.*The scaling for enemies and level is very well done, zero issues with having tough mobs throughout your climb to lvl ******. *Fallout 1st is a great perk if you don't mind supporting and subscribing for around 12.99 but if you do not have this perk, it makes the game rather unsupporting for you to ever craft as you see fit or crafting big bases that look awesome cause you can barely store any scrap components unless that is literally all you want to have stored for your account and not accumulate any apparel items, gear, etc. Cons:*Storage capped and limits a lot storage inventory unfortunately. (You can manage having unlimited ammo and scrap storage with Fallout 1st subscription at 12.99, but that doesn't hold guns/armor/food/plans/gunpowder/misc stuffs.)*When we make purchases from other player shops, it is taxed.. to the game gods for no reason.... like 10%... so that 10% doesn't go to the selling vendor player and gets lost in limbo.*You can ONLY hold a measly $40,000 caps at any given time. That means when you hit your cap (pun intended), any and all additional caps you collect or get sent via Vendor purchase goes to limbo never to be seen again and yes that means it can be thousands depending on what you are selling at the time. *There should be higher tier legendary roll options to sacrifice more for specific Mods*Some events are dated, too much of a hassle to even participate in and rewards are not enough.*You cannot skin weapons or armor and gift them to friends.*Once you hit lvl 50, there are no higher level items, everything is capped at 50. They scale for your character and level but its weird. Also there some items can only get crafted to certain levels, like 35, 40 or 45, etc. When others can get the 50 treatment which sucks late game cause there are cool guns that you end up not even using as they are pointless, obsolete or underpowered most of the time but look cool or have cool skins.*There are far too many limitations for your base to be properly productive with a farm/garden, gathering resources, providing entertainment and being layed out conveniently for everyone to enjoy.*You almost have to have the Fallout 1st subscription if you want to craft stuff.... its bs.All in all, this game has a lot to offer, I found myself sinking around 60 hours or so a week at the start until I leveled up to around 120 or so. I still hop on daily to perform daily quests, gather loot, chill with people but I wish there were more events triggering more often, that we could have a higher capacity for caps being held, storage being held, crafting components being held, etc. This game is constantly being updated and appears to have an influx of newcomers as well. Enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: When I tried 76 during the free weekend, I thought it was actually a lot of fun. And it was; for a good chunk of playtime, certainly more than a lot of games, it's a solid multiplayer fallout experience.But once you've played for a while, you run into outrageously hostile design. As of right now, Fallout 76 is a glorified mobile game. The devs have absolutely no respect for their players or their time. There are limits on EVERY FEATURE -- arbitrary inventory limits and daily caps on loot and money make it so you just straight up cannot play the game. The loop becomes log on -> sell a tiny bit of loot -> hit the daily limits -> log off. It's ridiculous. It's as user-unfriendly as the most egregious free-to-play garbage, only sold as a 60$ game. It's full price! The players have already payed for the game, but the devs don't let them play it.Then there's the gameplay. At first, it's fun. Absolutely. But when you hit the aforementioned caps, it becomes a looter-shooter survival game where you CAN'T LOOT ANYTHING. It just becomes pointless to keep playing. And, unlike other fallout games that let you use whatever weapons you want, the game balance combined with the new perk system means you have to completely specialise into a weapon type to actually keep up with optimised players. Gone are the days where you carry a pistol, shotgun, rifle, and gatling laser for emergencies -- no, now you've got 4 different types of bolt-action rifle because those are what you built for.Honestly, you'd probably have some fun with this game if you bought it. I'd probably even recommend it if it's on sale. The bones are strong. But the design decisions are just so, SO player hostile that I have to write a bad review. Don't buy it. The devs won't respect your time, so spend it on something else.

_childDocuments_.review: My experience with Fallout 76 hasn't left me full, but also hasn't left me starving. The game has improved since launch (which is to be expected), such as bug fixes and adding NPCs, although those should have been accounted for before launch. In terms of gameplay, combat is enjoyable, but VATS feels clunky. The early game of Fallout 76 is great, exploring the map, finishing quests, and finding better loot. However, one issue that you will run into quickly is your inventory cap. You are given a stash box that has a 1200 weight storage limit. This might seem like a huge number, but within a week or even days you'll find that you are constantly forced to either drop or sell your items because of the storage limit, which of course wouldn't be a problem with Fallout 1st. This should not be forced onto players that don't want to pay $18 each month. Fallout 76 is also considered pay to win imo, not because of Fallout 1st, but the atom shop. While most of the items in the atom shop are purely cosmetic, there are items that can speed up the grind. The weapon repair kits can instantly repair your weapon without the need for gathering the materials. Yes, the early game is fun once that wears out, you'll be spending your time farming for better equipment, weapons, and materials. The game in it's current state is playable, but there are better options.

_childDocuments_.review: Every time I play this game, I fall asleep at the keyboard... so I guess I would recommend this game if (and only if) you have insomnia.On a more serious note: I think the game has fundamental deficiencies in its 'reward system'. A Video game (ideally) should reward its players for literally just playing the game (i.e. having fun via natural progression). F76 rewards its player base, not through a natural progression of the game, but through an extremely 'grindy' pay off system with diminishing returns of varying degrees. The play-ability and enjoyment of F76 is dependent on a player's inclination to 'shove' as much content in a single sitting, rather than simply progressing through the quest lines naturally throughout multiple sessions.There is an inherent expectation that the game should be played simply off of the merit that it provides a large amount of quests (content) without the consideration of the quality or intrigue value of said content. The game doesn't immerse you, it keeps you busy.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd say this game would be more of a yes, BUT.......Fallout 4 scratched a particular itch for me. Not particularly well, but it hit something other games could not. The world was interesting and fun to explore. Combat worked, and the weapon customizing was neat. Mods kept me around for a long time after the vanilla state got boring. Fallout 76 should have been that next itch scratcher. Appalachia is huge and actually is a really fun map to explore. I've still had moments recently of coming across day one locations. There's more weapons than fallout 4's vanilla. 10mm smg's and grenade launchers, oh my! I thought the scorched were cool the first time I saw them. I was like "heh, mutant hillbillies". Survival mechanics are integrated nicely in this. Better balanced than 4's.But instead of an itch scratcher, Fallout 76 is more of a rub. The beginning was rough. We all know that. I was one of the first to own this on Beth net. There were some funny(the dreaded power armor stance), and some not so funny bugs and game breaks. Some missions would break(still do sometimes) and you'd be sol. 76's base building was and still is too restricted compared to 4's MC Escher meets Max Max way of life.  Mods all come in the way of plans or scrapping, and 76's unlock rate is just plain bad on some guns(radium rifle). Some guns are plans ONLY. Mission structure is standard Bethesda, but half the interesting twists and dialogue and stuffed with mmo daily and grind mission structures. I expected as much, but still it's disappointing and the mission just are dull now. Timers for changes in mission stages in missions are also needlessly long or seem to hang sometimes, and it seems either scripts waiting on timers or timers waiting on scripts ♥♥♥♥ up quite a bit in this game. Some missions also need to be retried(preferably by server hopping) since spawns can break and vital items or people wont show up. And for the longest time, no human npc's. Scorched are downright boring to fight at high level. It's the same level 5 jerk with a shotgun, lead pipe, pitchfork, whatever, now just health bloated to ♥♥♥♥. Ghouls always suffered a similar fate, but they at least still get your heart going when you're getting mad rushed.Saying this, Wastelanders, the most recent update, really freshened up Fallout 76. Human npc's! Fun missions. More loot(plasma caster, what what!) and was something the game really needed. Fixed some of the issues people had. Plus new missions to grind our time away with(but not too much. we need 'limits') to receive new currency to horde for new ♥♥♥♥, yay!Other notes. I like the perk card system, but after level 50 it just becomes a card collect-a-thon. Fallout 1st is almost worth the money. Actually found myself using the private server option most plays in the end. Made the game feel way more relaxed and felt good to explore again. Stash box is great. Tent is great. Both should be up in the Atom shop as a purchasable product. 1st users should have more control over their private server, such as triggering events, setting enemy area levels and whatnot.I'll most likely continue with this game, but it does frustrate me because it could actually be good, not just almost good. Too many nags and the core mission structure leaves too much to be desired. I want the game to make me care about what's happening.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, a modern Fallout game could work as on an online game but not like this.It's full of micro-transactions, grindy and finicky weight limits.Even at the reduced $15 AUD I paid for it I feel ripped off.Cons:- Slow to login and frequently cannot join a queue- Frequent large patches that do not address core issues- All the cool looking items are paid "mini-DLCs" (as Bethesda would say it), not included.- Barely existent story and no, notes and holo-tapes don't make up for this- Bad voice acting and audio balancing issues- Weapon degradation is far more annoying than fun- Network lags decide the outcome of an encounter more than player skill- Pipe weapons and early character levels are boring and make you want to leave- Enemies are not balanced and character progression is "all or nothing"- Map and interiors are purposefully confusing and maze-like, boring! (no local map)- VATS does not work in an online environment (jitters, lags and misses)- Paying in-game caps to fast travel (in most situations), who is the character paying?- Bugged out Power Armor Chassis in many areas that effectively crash the game (cannot move)- Graphic glitches galore and constant Z-fighting for distant objects- Controls are horrible even if using an XBOX 360 controller- Controls are inconsistent on menus (e.g. scrap can be LT or X)Pros:+ The game has moments of fun after level 40 or so, when your character has more abilities+ Around four quests I played were fun+ They bothered to add new weapons and some shine+ Some side quests have story links to other Fallout gamesAfter playing, trying to give it a chance, I lost all my junk (crafting materials) to a game breaking bug and I quit.I resumed some months later and then intentionally adjusted my play style and became selective about which quests I did. (ignoring bland content) I had more fun this way.This game may crash at startup. The fix is the install the official Direct X Runtime and then restart the PC.In 2024 I checked in on the game and somehow it got even more buggy. Main quest final missions bugged out and unable to be completed. "NEW" content is too well hidden to reasonably find.
