_childDocuments_.review: I might only have a couple of hours here on Steam, but I have a few dozen hours on the Bethesda launcher. Mostly because I wanted to like this game. A lot of people hate it, and with good reason. I just find that there's not enough content in it after a year and a half to justify the price tag. This is primarily considering the Wastelanders update, which did fix a lot of problems. There's definitely more to do, and the world does feel more lived-in, but it still doesn't quite do it for me. I think a lot of that is because of how grindy it is. Yes, it's a Fallout MMO, but when you're doing a fetch quest five times for the same NPC, it gets old, fast. Think of it as Preston from FO4. It always seems to be the same thing over and over again, with little variation in between.The new locations are nice, and actually make the game feel like a part of the Fallout franchise, but it only really added what should've already been there at launch. Pair that with the fact that enemies sometimes turn invisible or invincible and it gets rather frustrating. Add that on top of broken NPCs that you can't talke to to turn in quests if they're doing something specific (i.ie. sitting on a chair, laying in bed, etc.) and it becomes a chore.There would be one thing that would change this review from negative to positive, and that's if they hadn't added in vital quality of life changes as ONLY IN A PAID SUBSCRIPTION. Your stash, which you can store items in for your character, has a pretty limited space, especially considering how much junk you need for the crafting system. They said adding in a feature that would allow for unlimited junk storage would break the servers, and then they added it in as a perk for a 12.99/month or 99/year subscription. That paired with a broken "block player" system, hackers making PvP untenable and outright unfun, microtransactions for a $40-$60 game, and the "private" servers that you can only get through the paid subscription, I can't recommend this game. If the subscription features had simply been added to the game instead of locked behind a paywall, I'd say it's worth it on sale. As is, I can't say it's worth more than $10.EDIT 04/28/2024: Much better now that it's had time to really start fleshing out what's in this world. Still not sure I'd recommend it, but if it goes on sale, it might be worth checking out. The buzz around it because of the new Fallout show made me give it another chance, and I look forward to seeing if it's deserved or not.

_childDocuments_.review: Not sure exactly how I got the game free, was a glitch in someone's system but I got the game for free so bare that in mind for this review lol. Also - for the TLDR version - get it on sale, play it with friends and its not bad at all. Frankly the cheaper you can get it the more value it holds and the easier it is to justify both the time sink it becomes and the ever growing desire to buy atoms/Fallout 1st you'll feel lol. I wouldn't personally pay more than $20 or so for it even if it fell off my account and I had to buy it despite all the fun I've had with it.____________________When the game originally was announced I was extremely excited for it, I had preordered it through Bethesda and was fully planning everything out. I had me some lofty goals of being a merchant and someone who could help lower level players get started, so on and so forth. Then the beta happened. I was part of the group that had the game, all 50gbs of it, nuke itself off their PC an hour before the play window opened. I struggled with graphical errors, the camp didn't work, it was just a lot of mounting frustrations especially knowing that - at the time - it was the "finished" game. I was one of the extremely lucky ones that got a refund request in before they began denying them. From there out I spent the next what year and a half? watching it as it was just a simmering dumpster fire with hack and bug and error happening one after another.Despite all the problems I had been holding out with hope it would get better - I own all the other Fallout games on here and intended to buy the game one once it hit the $15 or less threshold and was on steam. Honestly once the game dropped and I saw I was gifted the copy somehow, I ended up giving a good friend of mine $10 and we split the cost of him buying the game at $20 during the summer sale.  I have absolutely zero regrets about convincing him to buy the game or in splitting the cost with him. Hes sunk something like 150 hours into the game and I'm sitting at right about 100 and we got the game what a month and a half ago? We've spent so much time playing together - and since then two more of my friends have picked it up as well. It is still buggy and has graphical issues, it still has rubber banding issues. Its not a *good* game from a technical standpoint but really what Bethesda game is? They're a meme for a reason. However if you have people to jump into a discord voice chat with or to LAN party it up with somehow it is a good experience with friends. Doing the quests together can be fun. My friend has Fallout 1st and tonight we spent time in his private server just playing with the nukes and knocking out the seasonal campaign stuff. We played a bit of Nuclear Winter and while Battle Royal stuff isn't for me personally I enjoyed it. Even playing alone I have fun exploring and doing dumb stuff. I love that the game has a pacifist mode because I don't have to worry about other players - but even then I've only had people bother us twice and my buddy was able to easily knock out both people. I've had players just stroll up and give me really helpful items because they could. The game justifies my hoarder tendencies with these games and I love that lol.Its fun. Give it a chance. It has come a LONG way from where it started and seeing as its a service style game? It hopefully will only continue to improve.

_childDocuments_.review: I love fallout, And this game isn't bad per se, but it's one of the most repetitive game I have ever played. Daily Ops are a run and gun with no other options when it comes to ways to tackle them and the Pitt, while a great idea, is just more run and gun without the timer and the lackiest of lackluster rewards. Not to mention they added 3 needless and tedious dailies to even open it for the day. Now the Nuka event is here and its just a few new world events to spam ad nauseam and a world boss you can just stand still and shoot at. Event rewards (like the holiday scorched and mole miners) are pretty bad too since they cannot seem to come up with any new rewards for bothering with them, yet they can give us brand new, shiny stuff everyone week on the atom shop, which is scummy at best.The perk system is just horrible too. It worked with what the game was originally supposed to be, but at this point, with the way the game is currently played and being designed around, once you unlock the cards they should just be unlocked without a need to shuffle. There is absolutely no reason to have this system anymore and its more of an annoyance than anything. They did give us master perks to alleviate this a bit, but they designed these cards is a real "do you even play this game" way. They are limited to 6 and take way to long to max out to bother with for most.I want more story, more cultists, more maps, raids, worthwhile/new rewards and less of a focus on just throwing bullet sponges at us while we Leeroy Jenkins our way through absolutely everything because there is no need to do anything any differently.

_childDocuments_.review: Fallout 76 is the sixth-instalment of the Fallout franchise (excluding the spin-offs). The game is dedicated towards a multiplayer fallout experience and to be honest, I think they’ve done an amazing job with it. In my 60+ hours from , I have never once encountered a game-breaking server problem or any bugs that have disrupted my wandering in the wastelands. The greatest bug I have experienced was my friend floating (swimming on land), but it was entertaining and didn’t irritate us at all. Saying that, I really dig Fallout 76 and it is one of my preferred Fallout games to be released and I’m glad they brought it to Steam. Like the other games, you are a vault dweller being released into the great unknown. However, unlike the previous games, you are not alone. You start off being released into the wasteland with a basic weapon, and vital supplies. You then get guided into the wasteland with a very basic tutorial mission setting you up with the knowledge and equipment you need. I think the tutorial is thoroughly done and straightforward, making the game manageable for new Fallout players. The main goal of the game is just to explore the wastelands, build yourself a home and progress your character by finding superior weaponry. However, you are not alone in the wastelands. Not only players roam the map but it is also full of mutated creatures such as; massive bugs, terrific beasts and more. In my opinion, the gameplay is very enjoyable and keeps me going back wanting more and more. It offers a variety of things to do like treasure maps, boss-like battles, exploring nuclear zones, PvPing with friends. And also meeting new people! I’ve made plenty of friends exploring the wastelands and I’m sure you will too! The only thing lacking is the story , this review was written before the Wastelanders update which includes human NPCs. Overall, the gameplay is amazing and exquisite for the price tag. The game also offers a game mode called Nuclear Winter. This is Fallout’s battle royale with the twist of finding nuclear codes and being able to launch a nuke in the zone. I’ve personally had a lot of fun in it but if I had to choose a battle royale, I’d prefer to stick with Apex or PUBG. The graphics aren’t that great and the optimisation is poor. My framerate drops frequently in major areas and while running making it frustrating. This is a major issue that Bethesda needs to fix because it's my only complaint.

_childDocuments_.review: Fallout 76, despite it’s terrible bug infested launch and quite infamously negative reputation both online and amongst the playerbase for a plethora of reasons, 76 has recently had somewhat of a revival due to continued support from the developers addressing game breaking issues and bugs while also releasing free content updates increasing the longevity of the game continuously.I was unfortunate enough to purchase Fallout 76 when it was released and endured my fair share of game breaking bugs, infinite loading screens and continuous broadcasting from other players in proximity voice having apocalyptically loud domestic arguments but alongside the typically frequent mentioning of it’s technical faults, 76 at release was quite an empty game, there wasn’t really much to do that did not seem repetitive, the challenges were quite repetitious and unimaginative [Kill 30 scorched] there was a noticeable lack of N.P.Cs that weren’t robots due to giant mutant bat disease which lead to this apparent empty world which was quite ironic considering this was the first online multiplayer Fallout game…But there could be other reasons for that.Also don’t even get me started on the initial pricing for cosmetic items and decorative objects within the Atomstore at launch….I returned to Fallout 76 what seemed like decades later, tempted by the notion of owning a free copy on Steam to celebrate the release of its free expansion and when I began playing again I was quite surprised to see a large amount of improvement.Most of the gamebreaking bugs, crashes and infinite loading issues that plagued me were gone, leaving but a small minority of infrequent crashes when travelling to certain instances, but no longer did I observes hordes of roaming T-posing fire-arm wielding Scorched or creatures half consumed by terrain, instead there were people, both N.P.Cs and PlayersPublic Teams had become a thing with players being able to opt into groups of other players getting rewarded for taking part in events and being given stat or XP bonuses that increased over time spent in group.Player C.A.M.Ps (Houses/buildings, to the layman) had access to player vendors where they could sell their weapons, plans, recipes etc with very little restriction alongside the ability to find your own crashed Astronaut who will gladly nag you to death about their headaches and never leave the house just like a real companion would.In stark contrast to when I first started playing Fallout 76 I found myself actually enjoying going on quests for my allies and seeing the changes to Wasteland, both in actual locations like Foundation becoming a settlement for settlers and new creatures lurking around like the Sheepsquatch.As it stands Fallout 76 has dramatically improved since its infamous launch, added free expansions, cosmetics and seasonal updates and has become a game that I’m not ashamed to recommend, albeit on a sale ofcourse, don’t go in expecting a revolutionary Fallout Game with high expectations nor a standard run of the mill title in the series rather a different more action RPG feel in an open world.With all things considered, if Bethesda continues to support the game with hotfixes, additional free and cosmetic content, the seasonal expansions and more allies/quests I see no reason why the game would not flourish.

_childDocuments_.review: 1. Placing camps with established structures you have lost.2. Fallout first.These are my gripes. If they are fixed, Bethesda could be able to draw more players to this game.Camps. Sometimes people loose their camp placement. (Joining into a world where someone else placed their camp in your vicinity causes you to loose yours. It happens.) The beautiful buildings you created go into your inventory- where you are never able to place them again! The console cites way too many reasons you cant rebuild your beautiful buildings. SELECTED ITEM IS FLOATING.  SELECTED ITEM IS FLOATING.  SELECTED ITEM IS FLOATING! FURNITURE ENTRY IS BLOCKED. CANNOT PLACE IN WATER. And so many others. I have to be honest. When you work on making something for more than seven hours, and then find that you'll never be able to place it, It breaks your heart.Doesn't matter if its a 4x10 cabin strategically mounted on one foundation, or a 3x6 full foundation, on the flattest plane in the map.  You spend so many hours fighting the building rules, and building in frustration, until you can finally stand back and beam upon your masterwork. But you'll never get to see that house after you lost it. Please, I know Bethesda works very hard on updating this game, making it a welcoming place for new players, but they have not updated the camp rules! We cant even have a 1 Length x 2 Hi wall. The fact that we have a 2x1 wall, but not a 1x2 wall baffles me.Camps aside, I have had fun playing this game, I really have. I get a tinge of pride when a stranger visits my camp, or i can see the masterwork camps others have created. This game is full of good Samaritans, and its especially fun when you can give back. I have so much fun playing this game in fact, that I've never had Fallout 1st. Fallout first does offer many cool items, but you can earn these in the base game, and the ones you can't earn you can pay for with the atoms you accumulate with challenges. Therefore the only thing fallout 1st really presents, over basic players is the scrapbox. If you manage your junk, you don't even need it. 15 dollars a month is a lot of money to pay for something you already have.

_childDocuments_.review: Wanted to give the game a fair shake and at this point I think I have.  Even with NPC's this game is so utterly devoid of content it's a lifeless corpse.  Kind of like how Bethesda is defiling the Fallout IP which has been dead since F4.Pros:- What little story there is is fine.  Not good (NV), not bad (F4), just fine.  You get enough feeling for what happened after the bombs fell and the story is passibly bland.- The community is probably the most surprising element of the game.  The community of the game is spectacular and it's about the only thing I got wrong in my prediction for Fallout 76.- Perks are better balanced than they are in Fallout 4.  That's kind of like winning the Special Olympics, but it is fair to note that they changed the SPECIAL system and managed to improve it.- Freemium ATOMS dropped pretty easily in my playthrough and there really wasn't a point that I wanted something I couldn't afford.Cons:  - Not a lot to do after level 50 except farm gold, scrip and reputation.  Reputation really isn't really worth finishing and scrip just generates garbage legendaries that you can convert back into scrip so that you can roll more garbage legendaries again.  Daily caps on scrip and gold (understandable) make the grind unreasonable and adds to the tedium of it all.- A lot of the same bugs you remember from Fallout 3 are STILL here.  Yes, that's right.  Fallout 3. From 2008.  They say in Fallout "War never changes", but they should change that to "shoddy development never changes".  Enemies still clip through the terrain when killed with energy weapons, legendary corpses disappear at random, sneak randomly stops working (which is great when your build depends on it) and all kinds of fun issues you remember from playing any other Fallout game up to this point still remain. - NPC's that you team up with for missions are little more than bullet sponges.  Few are interesting and even fewer are useful.- Combat system is all over the place.  I can take down a 20 level higher than me legendary at half life one minute and the next minute I'm fully healed and get inexplicably owned by a basic mob almost twenty levels lower than me.  Hit boxes could use some work as I've swung through mobs before.  - I hated settlement building in Fallout 4, and thought Fallout 76 would be the game where all the work they did on this would payoff.  This was the game where settlement building made sense, and I figured there was going to be some sort of factional thing where users could build settlements or claim preexisting ones for factions.  I was sorely mistaken and I apparently had too high of expectations for this game.  You can't actually build a settlement; only your own place in the middle of the lifeless Appalachia wasteland and then visit other people's places on the other side of the lifeless wasteland.  - They're liars.  Private servers were supposed to be a thing at launch (they were not).  The ATOM shop was only supposed to be cosmetic (it is not).  Fallout 4 gave me the impression that Bethesda really weren't all that interested in the Fallout IP.  Fallout 76 has not changed my mind on this opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: Steps:1. Go to your Steam Library > Fallout 76 > Right click > Manage > Browse Local Files. You will see game location, and then go to Data folder.2. Search for these files and Backup your current "SeventySix - 00UpdateVoices.ba2", "SeventySix - 01UpdateVoices.ba2", and "SeventySix - Voices.ba2" (optional: you can skip this if you don't want to)3. Go to Steam Library > Fallout 76 > Right Click > Properties > Languages > Change from English to Japanese4. Click on Updates. Wait until it finish processing.5. Go to (step 1).6. Backup the new files "SeventySix - 00UpdateVoices.ba2", "SeventySix - 01UpdateVoices_ja.ba2" and "SeventySix - Voices_ja.ba2" (this is important files you need to backup)7. Only rename 2 new files into: "SeventySix - 01UpdateVoices.ba2" and "SeventySix - Voices.ba2" (remove _ja)(for 00updatevoices, no need to rename)8. Go to Steam Library > Fallout 76 > Right Click > Properties > Languages > Change back from Japanese to English again.9. copy the 3 new files that you have renamed earlier in (step 7): "SeventySix - 00UpdateVoices.ba2", "SeventySix - 01UpdateVoices.ba2" and "SeventySix - Voices.ba2"10. Paste and Replace into Data folder. (Step 1)11. Start the game.12. Go to game settings > Display > Turn ON General Subtitles and Dialogue Subtitles. That's all. Enjoy Japanese Dub with English Subtitles.

_childDocuments_.review: The most positive thought in the context of Fallout 76 is that we should be glad, because Bethesda produces computer games and not, for example, software for respirators.Just imagine that vision of some parallel universe, where what I just said is a reality and everyday life, especially when we consider it's 2020 right now. We should all put our hands together in a prayer (you too atheists!), because in the end our lives are not in danger, only mental side of our health is somehow exposed, but in this case solution is simple - just don't buy Fallout 76, no matter how big discount is, no matter how much Todd Howard is waving at you, smiling, telling you that "it just works" and you should try it on your own. No, you shouldn't, because this whole thing is simply not working. I avoided Fallout 76 for a long time after it was first released, and I started playing it when it was launched on Steam. I got baited by positive reviews pretending game is now fixed, and it's safe to buy it. No, it's not and never will, because engine used to make this Fallout is simply too broken and too old to handle multiplayer game.There's a large pool of bugs and glitches, and Bethesda is pretending that they're fixing them, but in reality every single fix is bringing back old bugs. It's always the same scheme -> something is not working -> after two months (or even more) they apply fix (which break something else) -> week later new update break it to previous state for another two months -> then they release another fix... this circle never ends. You stuck in dialogue with NPC and can't progress your daily quest? Your turrets attack your own structures? Your perk/mutation is not working? Game is perma-freezing on loading screens and you have to restart it every 30 minutes? You lost progress because servers stability is a joke? Welcome in Fallout 76, where in endgame you will face bug every two minutes! I could make a very long list of bugs and other problems players face, but it would be just too long and it's hard to guess which bugs are active now, because like I said previously - Bethesda mastered bugs rotation in this game.Optimization in this game is just like everything else - how it work (when it work) is depending on various circumstances and changes every patch they apply. If you just made new character, and you run trough early game in 60fps, then in endgame you will have 30fps with regular stutters. It is like this, because amount of items you carry and store in stash directly affects your framerate, and to be honest I've never seen something that much broken in any other game. Fallout 76 in a nutshell. But let's talk about something positive this game has to offer, and in this case first thing coming to my mind, is community this game has. People are friendly and very helpful, they will explain everything you want to know, no matter how long it will take. They will craft gear for you, give you materials, help with quests, build structures you can't build on your own yet. But there is a dark shadow hiding behind all those friendly faces. I am talking about small group (but very loud) of players, fanatics, trolls and sect-like minority. To understand what I am talking about, you can just browse Steam forums of Fallout 76 for 5 minutes and you'll see it on your own. Why I am mentioning them? I am doing this only because Bethesda is doing nothing about problem, they are allowed to keep offending and attacking people who dared (how dare they?!?!) to criticize Bethesda. They'll keep striking on you and reporting your posts, and you might end up warned/banned for speaking your opinion in mannered way. Yes, Bethesda has their own "freedom of speech" standards, and it's very close to what you can face in People's Republic of China.Imagine you can build various items in your camp, and then you can use them to get buffs for your character. Great idea, right? In theory, yes, but you have to use each item for 40-50 seconds to recieve specific buff, so if you want to get all of them you waste 5 (!!!) minutes of your time, and one hour later you have to repeat whole process. Everytime you want to craft/repair/build you have to manualy change your perks loadout, which takes a lot of your time, and when you're done you have to manualy switch to your main build. Bethesda promised to implement perk loadouts system months ago, but it's not just about that. The thing is, that whole perk system lack any logic and common sense, because perks should be splitted into two categories - active and passive, and crafting ones should not steal slots. When you want to buff yourself using items from your inventory, you have to scroll trough whole menu to find them one by one. Every few quests/events, you have to do general cleaning of your inventory, because game keep throwing useless (and heavy) stuff at you as "reward". Every single system this game has is unintuitive, frustrating and not rewarding, and every simple thing you want to do takes ages to complete. At first it seems interesting, because you discover new places while hiking, do various quests, and simply enjoy it. But this phase ends pretty fast when you hit midgame, where grind begins and you realize how many limits this game has. In order to reach endgame you have to grind, everyday. How much you can store is limited, how big you camp can be is also limited, daily quests, daily currency gain, everything is made in a way to make sure you'll play game everyday to reach your daily cap, and make just a slight or no progress at all. Everything from events on map to daily quests is repetitive and boring.Game is designed in a way, where player feel hounded and forced to play everyday in order to reach daily limits, and if someone play everyday, that mean there's higher chance he will spend real cash to get additional stuff or to buy premium. Fallout 76 preys on basic human instincts, the desire to show off, being noticed, generaly speaking - need to be "cool" in other people eyes. Everything in this Fallout is built like a wall surrounding all these behaviours and feelings. They might tell you, that you don't need all that stuff, but believe me, you want it. That's how human brain works. Atomic shop is a masterpiece when it comes to psychological manipulation, fake feeling of items availability being "limited" by time, so you have to buy them before they're gone, discounts lasting for limited time, great deals for premium owners. Atomic shop, seasons, game mechanics, boring daily/weekly challenges, everything this game offers in the end has just one common goal - to make sure you're attached enough to play everyday, so at some point you might start thinking, that it wont be a crime if you spend additional money to make your in-game life easier and more colorful. I understand servers do not run on fresh air and companies want to earn money, and there's nothing wrong with that. But this is paid game, not some F2P title for android. It's also impostant to mention, that every new feature (like the newest thing available in game - shelters) is hiding 90% of new content and fun behind a paywall. Bethesda is literaly moving border to see how far they can go, and how much they can earn before this $ fountain dries up. In the end it's up to you what you'll do with your money, just think twice before you give them to Bethesda.

_childDocuments_.review: I must spill my heart out here, this game holds so much nostalgia for the area I was born and raised. Going to Blair mount and seeing the huge earth movers and mining equipment my grandfather help oversee is almost otherworldly for me  to see represented in a video game. Add on a RPG and survival element to the game and its some sickly weird universe I can lose my self into for hours.... I can not recommend this game as it stands right now. The "One Wasteland" update in my option seems to change the pace and grind of the game. No longer was it like other titles of a nice rinse then repeat cycle of; Explorer, collect  then profit or redeem. Now the game feels like I fight most of my game play time in just sourcing ammunition for the next adventure just to waste it all on a rad roach or a few ghouls. Before one wasteland which was to -balance- the game for multiple people playing together at different levels, I felt like I was playing any other 3D Fallout title. The game now just seems like it's job more than a world to lose yourself. The feelings like the only thing to speed up gaining it is using a slow method of exchanging a set amount of an ammo type for another through a terminal. Ammo is hardly anywhere to begin with now even with perk cards to increase chances and vendors never seem to have much on hand. You can always buy it from players, if you got the caps, if they even have it or if the stay online long enough to get to them. You can buy it from some no-life on ebay and get banned.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a six year old game, broken on day one and retooled into something totally different from its intended programming. It looks and plays like a ten year old game, currently being sold and priced like a modern day AAAA game. Nothing in the game really matters either, your choices, the rewards, things you pick up, nothing means anything. The game is pretty much unplayable if you don't subscribe to Fallout 1st. Yes you can play, but you're playing a completely different game as everyone around you. Weight Management Simulator 76 is what you're playing. So you subscribe to 1st to not deal with the weight limit, and you quickly start hitting limits to the other currency systems in the game. Your game is now based around jumping from CAMP to CAMP to avoid the limits and penalties for having too much by buying expensive things you have no need for, so you end up trashing or dumping themWhile all this is going on, the game is crashing to desktop multiple times a session. Sometimes it gets stuck on basic load screens, sometimes it's a server error, sometimes it's because the excessive effects on the weapons in the game blind everything and freeze the game. So you reload and try and get back with the team you are on to finish the mission, and the game's main load screen locks up so you have to restart your computer. When you get back into the game, the server can not place your CAMP or you are not able to get back on the same server as your team, and you have to jump servers until your CAMP is placed. Each time you do this costs you time on your limited food and health buffs, so when you eventually do get back into the game, most of the time you have to go through all of that again In Fallout 76's defense. If you can get the game for free, and you can deal with the pay to win, fear of missing out tactics the developers are using to prop up this game as a face of the Fallout franchise, it does have a very unique community of users that are unlike anything I've ever seen in a game like this. The player base for the most part cares, the kindness and aid you see is almost startling and hard to understand at first. It's those people who make the game playable. Which is a rather difficult accomplishment considering the game has no communication between players beyond a rudimentary system of emotes that are locked behind seasonal rotating paywalls, so even if you'd like to communicate better, the game will not allow you to.

_childDocuments_.review: I was so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ excited, and did get some beta in on this game, and it was absolutely disappointing. Empty, boring, broken-ass closeup graphics with mega motion blur and poor FOV/depth of field, it made me sick to play for even a few hours.As recently as a few weeks ago I've made fun of people on forums / discord for playing it, booing it on ads, commenting snarky remarks under their sponsored ads, etc.But I did long for the days of New Vegas or Fallout 4, decided I might replay one of them when suddenly the free weekend came around. I thought I'd at least give it a try, see if the NPCs make the difference, how the graphics look now, and try it with my fiancee instead of alone.This game now, on the whole, is fixed in my eyes. If you told me a few years ago "hey, you can play FO4 on a new map with a friend or two" I would jump for joy, and i know that many fallout fans would say the same. I let the vile internet effect seep into my brain and poison me against something that I honestly genuinely knew I could probably like. I made a mistake. Don't jump on the "this game is garbage" bandwagon like I had (commenting on trailers that you'll never play it, etc) - it's boring. it's not original, and it actually comes across as ignorant to feel like you're important enough to warrant thinking anyone cares about your negative opinion. it's also HELLA IGNORANT to act like something is beneath you even TRYING it, especially if you call yourself a fan. before i tried this game i think i was way too jaded, heard bad hype, and didn't want to give in to the "ohhh we fixed it, don't worry!" vibe. By trying, in error, to not conform to the people who were saying it was good, I was bandwagoning with the even lamer side of "People are saying this is good so with 0 recent frame of reference I am going to argue that it is bad." It makes me slightly embarassed to think of now, because I know for a fact that I tend to do that with TV/Movies/Games yet I didn't even stop to think that I might be making the same mistake again.it's not fallout 300,000. the graphics look like brushed up fo4 graphics, the FOV default is nightmarishly low to begin with which is why i spent the first 4 hours feeling like my eyes were broken - set it to 90. turn the depth of field down ALMOST all the way. now you're just playing fallout 4, with new characters (loveable npcs really do make all the difference) new areas, less scrounging for ammo and more shooting guys who MIGHT ACTUALLY kill you.Things can change. People, and studios because of it, are inherently flawed. What they did, though, was not go "HEY ♥♥♥♥ YOU" and never fix it - they listened, and slowly they fixed it. Bethesda is now like any other AAA studio and super in it for the moolah, but you've gotta give Todd some credit, he did the dirty and didn't love the response he got but in the end they jumped on and improved the things that didn't work, and polished the things that did.The CAMP system is really cool, I love that you can't REALLY get into too much PVP unless you agree to it - and your stash is always safe, only you can access it. Worst case scenario some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ decide to blow up your camp while you're off running around, it's a learning experience for placing more turrets next time, or for just leaving your camp completely open to the public - if you don't store much in other containers / don't have anything actively mining you're not up to lose too much.So far in about 20 hours I've met 4-5 other people, all of whom gave me gifts, showed me where the good stuff on the level was / cap stashes / got me to follow them to large events where they mowed down all the baddies for us. Not one real person (aside from when I had a 10 cap bounty on me for government supply theft) has shot at me, or even moved toward me in a threatening manner. Most people make liberal use of the in-game emotes, with less voice chat as far as I've seen - which is honestly my preference so I'm into it!If you're THINKING about trying the game, because you loved Fallout 3 / 4 / NV - I recommend giving it the benefit of the doubt. If you think you hate it but have never played it, and are just bandwagoning because of word of mouth - rethink your stance. Maybe being "non-mainstream" is just as mainstream, but kinda boring and tiresome?

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR; They managed to make this game even more boring than Fallout 4!After playing this a couple evenings (around 6 hours) in total, I have no desire to go back. Movement and shooting is subpar to almost every other FPS/TPS game out there. And RPG aspects are also severely lacking: even the beginning of the game (where you actually expect some great content to hook you up) has only boring fetch quests where your decisions mean nothing. And it gets only worse from that point: the more quests you get, the more you realize that they tell no interesting stories and only make you running from point A to point B.Exploration is also extremely luckluster. Yes, the map is huge, yes, there are many landmarks and buildings to explore, but all of that is completely unrewarding since the game has almost neither loot nor interesting environment storytelling outside of the areas you visit via quests, and as I said above, even quests are extremely boring.And I am not even talking about the technical aspect which is extremely bad for a game released several years ago. I have 12900k, 32 GB RAM, Samsung 980 EVO Pro and 3080Ti, and Fallout 76 manages to stutter all the time! I don't care if that's poorly done streaming or unoptimized memory allocation, but this is simply unacceptable for a game that looks so much worse than modern ones yet fails to deliver stable 60 fps.P.S. The game is in the Humble Choice until March 7th, go grab it and be disappointed as well.

_childDocuments_.review: As a die-hard fan of the Fallout franchise, I was eagerly anticipating the release of Fallout 76. However, when I finally got my hands on the game, I quickly realized that my expectations were far from being met. Despite the good game-play elements, the drawbacks of the game hit me like a ton of bricks, leaving me feeling devastated and heartbroken.One of the biggest issues that I had with Fallout 76 was the inclusion of paid cosmetics in the game. It felt like the developers were trying to nickel and dime their fans for every little thing, even though the game itself was already plagued with so many issues. It was disheartening to see the franchise that I had loved and cherished for so long reduced to a cash-grab, with the quality of the game taking a backseat to profit margins.The game was also riddled with bugs and glitches that made it almost unplayable at times, completely destroying my immersion and making it difficult to enjoy even the most basic aspects of the game. To make matters worse, the placement of reused assets was incredibly lazy and uninspired, leaving me feeling like the developers had simply phoned it in and didn't care about providing a quality experience for their fans.Every time I tried to play the game, I found myself frustrated by the poor performance and uninspired design choices that had been made. The online-only DRM requirement felt like a slap in the face, as it prevented me from playing the game on my own terms and at my own pace. And as someone who had always enjoyed the ability to customize and enhance my gameplay experience through the use of mods, the lack of official mod support was a crushing blow that left me feeling helpless and deprived of the unique experiences that had always made Fallout so special to me.As if all of this wasn't bad enough, the negative reception that Fallout 76 received from both critics and fans alike was like a dagger to my heart. All of my hopes and dreams for the game had been shattered, leaving me feeling like I had been taken advantage of and betrayed by a franchise that I had always loved and cherished.It's tough to put into words just how much Fallout meant to me, and to see it fall from grace in such a dramatic and devastating way was like losing a part of myself. I can only hope that future iterations of the game will address these issues and provide a more satisfying experience, but for now, the memory of my disappointment with Fallout 76 will forever haunt me.

_childDocuments_.review: Fallout 76 is an abusive relationship masquerading as a video game. It begs for your attention, gives you trivial trinkets to lure you in, and just when you spend money on it, something outside your control changes; things break, months of effort are undermined, and you find yourself left wondering what you ever saw in it to begin with. Then, a little time passes, you think it must not have been that bad, there were fun times, and you find yourself reinstalling to log in once more, just to check in, see if anything got fixed or changed… but no. Even when they say they've changed, a little bit of time together reveals they really haven't changed at all.This is the only Fallout 3 or 4 style experience available that has multiplayer. That's the only reason anyone would buy or play this. Of its merits, this is a game from a billion dollar company that is fundamentally flawed and has been repeatedly broken by various updates over time. There's a black market for trading 'legacy' weapons and duplicated items and power armors (I don't care what you do, just stating it exists). Quests are still buggy and broken, along with NPC dialogues. Events like Mischief Night (the Halloween one) just disappear and get replaced with the way more boring 'Spooky Scorched' (itself a retread of their Holiday/Winter Event), while others like Fasnacht are buggy and broken even after multiple years of hiatus and reworked returns.I avoided playing this game at the time it was originally out; before then, there were only robot vendors in the game at train stations, and the game had a heavy pvp focus, so I didn't have a lot of interest (despite other options like a Survival mode and the late-not-as-great-as-people-said-but-still-fun Nuclear Winter). I picked it up when it came to Steam with the release of the Settlers dlc expansion, and the idea I had was, despite the negativity I heard surrounding the game, if they were going to keep trying to add things and fix it up, I might have to give it a look.It's been over 1,000 hours. Help me. For the most part, what I found was an expectedly buggy but surprisingly fun series of quests loosely related to established Fallout things with other people occasionally trying to kill me. While I didn't always engage with the action combat, I did spend a lot of my time building different bases across the wasteland, with mixed results. While the combat is sort of taken from FO4 and rejiggered to be 'live', the building is ripped straight from that game and then has a bunch of strange limits imposed upon it, generally ending up in worse results. Look, I understand I can clip items together, and I know some people exploit camp budget to achieve their ultimate fantasy house - I don't care, neither of us should have to. The building system needs some serious attention, and while those of us who really enjoyed that part of FO4 will be busy (especially with Shelters now, in addition to the lackluster Worlds) those who don't engage with that content are really playing only half the game.The result is a hybrid game that wants to provide a lot of things, but doesn't do any of them very well. Those who have played previous Bethesda games (Elder Scrolls in particular) will recognize some of the bugs and find ways around them or just ignore them - the games are fun anyway. Even in stacking those against this one, this is the buggier of the bunch. The multiplayer and additional stresses really just push this engine to its limit, and lag in all its forms, with enemies teleporting and players sliding around or stuck in various animations, abound on live servers - especially in the bigger fights like  where the majority of the server's players group up to take down one big bad and lots of little adds. It's crazy and chaotic fun, but as something that drops items mandatory to progression (by which I mean, to advance your power you should participate in these events) it's hard to look at and say it’s a selling point. And this is the endgame.What else? Well SCOREBOARD bugs almost every season, and apparently a lot of people willing to pay $130 to skip it entirely and get all the things on Day One. Play how you want, but have you looked at the items on the Scoreboard as far as rewards? 5+ player icons? Scrip? Lunchboxes? Skins for guns, some camp objects, and the newer 'lite' player allies maybe be objectively worth it for some, but with lackluster rewards often so prevalent, it's definitely hard to see how this is justified ATOP the almost necessary Fallout 1st ($12.99/mo) for a scrap box not beholden to a weight limit (the same trick they took from Elder Scrolls Online and their Crafting Mats bag). Just as often, the FO1st member rewards from the Scoreboard are regularly pretty bad, and while many of the best items come late in the award path, these later few seasons have had pretty bad rewards for the final rank besides. (Um, your current event is Vault stuff - it's a lot of yellow paint and uh… Responder's building kit? Not a Vault Tec one?)Shooting aliens is a ton of fun, and a great, heavy pressure event - but also punishing for solo players and the under-leveled, so be warned if that's you. Give the rest of these events a few tweaks and this level of effort, and you might have something to bring more people back to the daily loop.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a multiplayer Fallout game. Each server has a max of 24 people. You can get the Premium subscription and get a  server for you and your friends.  - When you want an open-world Fallout that combines the good points of previous games. - People who want lots and lots of socializing>. Controls are snappier and more responsive than Fallout 4.>. You're not a Mary Sue. Recipes, weapon schematics, weapon mods need to be learned beforehand.>. New Vegas-style speech checks. Not everything is about Charisma.>. Level scaling just how I like it - Enemy level scales, but they have a min/max.>. >. You get hungry/thirsty, but it doesn't kill you. You lose out on buffs though.>. Random repeatable quests that make life interesting.>. Vendors don't sell good equipment. You want the best items, you'll have to learn to craft.>. Remember how you're not a Mary Sue? Being unprepared can be fatal.>. Radiation/disease management - Good or bad, depending on your taste.>. No proper in-game chatroom. You only have VOIP and emotes.>. Areas take time to load if your rig or network is slow.All in all, 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Personally, I had quite a lot of fun with this as they seem to have fixed the issues that plagued it at launch. I'm not a fan of the slow progression and the gameplay loop of looting everything and scrapping it in survival games bores me, so I'll never buy this type of game for $60 or pay for DLC, but for $20 with all the DLC being free, I can look past the numerous things I dislike about it and just embrace it as being more Fallout. There are a lot of rough spots because the game is made for multiplayer in the events, but the events do not always attract players. A better setup would have been to make the exploration tuned for single player and make events occur in entirely separate instances with warps back to our previous locations should we choose to do them. That way they would be special and not an interruption. Also, they probably would have been easier to create and debug.Finally, I think adding NPCs to the world the way that they did it was a bad idea. Having an empty world (other than bad guys and other real players) was novel.  If the story had paid off that idea with eventually finding **some** survivors who were important and well-acted, that would have been great.

_childDocuments_.review: Fallout 76 is the game that just can't stop giving. Bugs. Big, big, bugs.Thought I would reload and play during the Oct 21 free weekend. Game literally crashes out of the load screen. Given my previous excursions into this bug filled, nightmare dumpster fire, I am not especially surprised, but am disappointed. Mind you, they, lost me as a customer ages ago when they announced that they are charging stupidly large amounts, just so I could have a feature promised at released, namely  my own server and mods. Bethesda simply doesn't give a toss about you as a player. They'd rather your cash than your opinions. Original review kept below for historical reasons:----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------This game has little to offer but endless grind. While I am definitely a people person, I hate multiplayer games and this is no exception. Too often what could have been a good experience is ruined by some idiot bouncing through and ruining the immersion.I'm a huge fan of the Fallout series and also of the Elder Scrolls, but this game is a masterclass in how to trash an IP. In reviewing a game, I often find it useful to see just how many people have achieved basic Steam achievements. In this game, as of the writing of the review, only 30% of players have reached level ten! And this is despite there being a free weekend of play in which double XP were awarded. In other words, if you buy this game, there is a 70% chance that you won't even begin to get into the story, or what it has to offer. Non player characters are lifeless, although the radio DJ is quite vibrant. Listening to holotapes is dull and the perk system is a nightmare, in which luck plays far to big a part (at 19th level, I'm still waiting for my second lock picking perk card) and combat feels like wading through mud. Graphically it is good and I experienced decent frame rates the entire time, although in many instances, I felt that the game was a fraction of a second behind where I was and what I was doing (hence the poor combat). As an example, when looking at a container, it takes about half a second for its contents to generate and appear.Bethesda wrung the life out of this game, all in an attempt to wring the dollars out of you. The Atomic Shop is a travesty. Needless to say, by excluding the possibility of mods, Bethesda has also excluded the very thing that made previous titles so damned good. Modders have always saved the day, both by fixing bugs, but also by allowing players to play the game they want to play, not the game that the straigthjacketed minds of the Devs think they should. The inability to set up private servers, or have decent storage, without paying great wads of cash on a monthly basis is both a broken promise and intensely greedy. If maintaining servers is expensive, why can't I set up my own private server on my own machine, like I can in other games? Nothing quite ruined my experience of a post apocalyptic universe quite like spending ages scouting a place out then attempting to sneak up on some enemy only to have "J87s65s", or whatever random come bouncing through at 40 levels higher than me and simply slaughter everything and everyone. Way to go for fun. Yay!! While my experience with the servers was stable there are some significant bugs in the game. Firstly, I played a melee character only to discover that the hit boxes are terrible and that I couldn't hit creatures standing right in front of me. As such, I soon regretted that decision and ended up relying heavily on ranged weaponry. Pathfinding for mobs is also poor. I claimed an workbench, so that I could mine, but soon discovered that it was attacked every half hour or so. Problem was that the attackers were too stupid to get inside the area, and I had to go outside in order to finish them off and thereby finish off the mission. On the hardware side of things, the game refused to connect to my headset and microphone, leaving me completely unable to talk to others inside the game. Quite embarrassing to be forced to remain silent, while people are talking at you. Given that I have experienced no problems with other software and the headset, I think I can safely say that it is a problem with the game.  To its credit, the game has significantly improved since release, but given that the good stuff is behind a paywall and you need to pay a significant subscription on top of your purchase price, I  suggest that you spend your money elsewhere.If this game had been purely single player, it would still have been crap on launch, but at least there is now sufficient content to buy it on discount, assuming you can handle not having mods and having do deal with other players screwing with your game experience.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing this game for over 100 hours (some hours from playing through the bethesda app). I feel like I have played enough of the game to voice an opinion. First off let me say that this game is fun, however, it is only fun if you are a fan of the fallout universe and do not mind the repetitive game play loop that comes with an online RPG, this being logging on daily to complete challenges and grinding the same locations and events legendary weapons which will in turn make you more powerful. If you think you will enjoy those two aspects then its worth giving this game a try as it has come a long way since its launch. The inclusion of "one wasteland" which scales the enemies to your level has helped improve the game massively, as newer players no longer feel limited to where they are able as they are able to put up a fight against most enemies. Furthermore, this allows new players to play with their friends who might be higher level than them. Although the majority of the playtime I have accumulated has been through playing solo (lmao what a loner), another new feature that was added which was public groups helped to combat this. The public groups allowed me to join up with strangers (which granted xp boosts depending on the group type) and complete event/daily ops together. Finally, the addition of NPC's to the game has really made the world feel more alive, this addition has by far been the best, with this Fallout 76 actually started to feel like a fallout game (which was needed considering the game is called FALLOUT 76). Overall, I believe that this game is worth the price for how many hours you can get out of it, and if you happen to see it on sale then its definitely worth picking up (as you obviously have an interest if you have taken the time to read all of this.) TL;DR - Game has improved massively since launch. Lots of content, easily a minimum of 50 hours. If you like fallout and online RPG's give it a go, especially if its on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so I didn't play this before Wastelanders. I had no interest in a PvP focused multiplayer Fallout game. I am not a purist though. I don't think Fallout 1 and 2 are fantastic. I started at 3 back in...2008? Or whenever it came out. I like the Bethesda Fallout games. Wastelanders brings back the fun of "wander in one direction until you find something weird". When you add in co-oping with your friends, it hits true sublimity. Oh and Wastelanders added a story. Not a bad story either. It's not good by normal game standards, but it isn't the standard Fallout "You are the best vault person, please go save your son/dad/dadson". You play just a person, from a vault, and you choose what you want to do. Wanna grind out dailies for possible rare drops? Do it. Wanna go hunt insane cryptozoological marvels? Do it. Wanna build a museum dedicated to how many beers you've found? Do it. Wanna follow along with the main story, side missions, and seasonal/weekly/monthly events? Do it. Do whatever you want! Its the post-apocalypse. All those spooky scary microtransactions that people wail and gnash teeth about are purely cosmetic nonsense. Indulge if you wanna play pretty princess dress up or HGTV post-apoc house flipping. THE MICROTRANSACTIONS HAVE NO EFFECT ON THE GAMEPLAY.Fallout 76 with Wastelanders is a good time. Is it perfect? No. It has glitches and weird bugs sometimes. Is it more Fallout 4? Yes. Yeah it's always online but if I can manage it with the world's worst rural DSL then you can scratch "my internet is too bad to play this game" off your list. I've put lots of time into it, and i've barely scratched the surface. I'll keep playing for a long time.Update 11/26/20: With the release of Steel Dawn there are now more reasons than ever to play Fallout 76. The devs are slowly chipping away things that annoy players and are adding quality of life improvements with every update. The new instanced dungeons and freeform group setup make the game even easier to play with friends or randos. Just get in there and enjoy the wild, wild wasteland.

And it losses connection randomly.You have to pay for playing in private worlds, custom worlds, and inventory space is very limited. Increasing strength does not do much. The skill system is replaced by cards that you can upgrade. It's actually OK, but not what expected from a Fallout game. And of course throws away all the RPG aspects that remained.The story really feels like they had to do a 180º turn to make everything right. You follow trails and trails of holo messages, letters and computers, and where you feel it was supposed to be empty, there is some random settler living. Or a character from another mission arc. It's like a mash made from lots of different ideas.It's just that. Bland, buggy, looks ugly... It's not a bad time, but it is not good either. Would definitely not pay for this. It is on the low end of mediocrity.

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't played since launch, only played a few hours at that time for obvious reasons. Just got done playing my first sitting revisiting Fallout 76. I played through Fallout 3, but no other FO games. I loved 3. Looking forward to trying out 1, 2 and, Tactics that I got for free with the steam promo.  I went for just over 8 hours today.Did the game crash? Yes, twice. Once at the end of character creator. At the end of character creator you are prompted to take a photo of yourself. There is a box with some options, one option is "show character - ON/OFF". When I toggled this, game crash (I never toggled it the 2nd or 3rd time). It also crashed one more time randomly when I was sitting in a chair.Were there bugs? Yes, in a certain building near where you fight Mr. Farmbots for a low-level event. I could hear enemies walking around and sounded like they were wading through water, but alas, no enemies, and no water. (Oddly I recall this same thing from like 2 years ago or whatever when I played for like an hour back then) I jumped onto a counter in the vault, having fun popping balloons, knocking over bottles, generally just wanted to wreck the place before I left and well, got stuck in a kitchen sink and had to remake my character for the 3rd time because it doesn't save until after you leave the vault. I tried to get out of the sink for like 20 minutes. Jumping, crouching, trying everything I could, was completely stuck in the sink. Also a dead feral dog that just kept twitching for eternity after I bashed it's mutant brains into a pulp. I felt bad. It was funny. SO, 8 hours, 2 crashes and a few minor bugs/glitches. Besides that, the game seems pretty awesome. Some people will argue that the graphics are "bad" or "trash" or "garbage" whatever gamer adjective you prefer. But tbh I thought the game looks pretty awesome. It's not the Unreal4 engine, but it's not crap, at all. The fog I thought was especially cool. I don't mind the bloom and all that, I like 'god rays'. I will say that night could be darker, it's not dark-dark. I like my nights pitch black tho. If you ever played SCUM then you know what I'm talking about, PITCH BLACK.   The building mechanic takes some getting use to for me, the keybindings are kind of weird compared to other games (I build in Ark-like, Conan Exiles). The camera was a bit obscured in the build mode, couldn't seem to fully see if wtf I was placing was going to fit right, and you can't seem to align things to the ground, it has to be flat. Boo. Materials seem plentiful. I was surprised at all I could build/craft by the time I set up my camp. (Coming from games where you harvest rocks/iron etc with a pick ax for a good while before you can build a decent amount of stuff) The 'pay-with-real-money' Atom Shop is kind of in your face, but it's all cosmetic so not too annoying. You will probably end up there on accident. I got a free emote.I wish the factions were more than just "settlers" and "raiders". Just the names feel kind of shallow and very "not-badass" Other than a few minor frustration outlined above, I had a great time. The fallout universe is here. It's beautiful, sad, bleak, death and turmoil abound. I enjoyed the holo tapes I found in the first town, they felt chilling and set the tone for me. The NPCs seem interesting, they are voiced and voiced well. There are other players and teams around doing their thing, interact with them, or don't. There's no raiding in the game it seems. You can't get at other players stuff...(EXCEPT SOME STUFF...I did jack some guys purified water out of his refiner things and took all the Tatu fruit in his garden. THANKS FLIPGUY123!!!). You can use their crafting benches too. Every base I came across was wide open. Very contrast to games where you have to worry about protecting all your crap with secret walls and deception tactics.Your stash box is linked with every other stash box. So if you stash your favorite weapon at your camp and find another stash box across the map, you can get it out of there. I guess it's cool, for me it's a bit immersion breaking but it's cool, it's whatever.Although I enjoyed the VATS in Fallout 3, I can understand how that system would be problematic in an online game, since it would pause the game to work in the single player FO3. I have a melee build going and had a good time smacking mutated opossums across the screen with a wooden sword-like board. Some robot enemies exploded into badass mushroom clouds. I enjoy the station animations and the cooking mechanic, crafting recipes on the campfire/stove is fun to me. I made opossum bacon. Follow me for more great opossum recipes.   Quests seem plentiful, at least at my low level. There are several different directions I could go.If you can get the game for like $20 I would say go for it. If you love fallout, you'll probably be okay with the current $40 price. There's a good chance you'll dump a ton of hours into it and get your moneys worth. I only regret paying the full $60 because I got it at launch and we all know how that went.  Thanks for coming to my Ted Talk. See ya in the wasteland... Stik out

_childDocuments_.review: Ah, Fallout 76 at launch—it was like arriving at a braai only to find out the meat was still frozen and the firewood was wet. But let’s give credit where it's due: just like a true Namibian cookout, with a bit of time, patience, and a whole lot of hoping, things did start to heat up eventually.Back in the day, trying to play Fallout 76 was like trying to start your bakkie in the middle of the Namibian winter—more hope than expectation. The game crashed more often than a learner driver at a four-way stop. And the bugs? They were more plentiful than mosquitos by a waterhole at sunset. You’d be minding your own business and bam!—you’re part of the scenery, literally stuck in a rock or a tree.But, here we are now, and I've got to tip my hat to the folks at Bethesda. They’ve turned that braai around. It’s not just frozen vleis anymore—there's some proper boerewors on the grill now. The updates and patches came rolling in like a good rainy season, making things grow and blossom. Now, the game has new quests, events, and even NPCs! Imagine that, actual characters to talk to, not just echoes in the wind.Sure, it’s not all perfect. Sometimes the server still goes down like a flat tyre on a gravel road, and the lag can be as slow as a Sunday afternoon drive in the countryside. But when it's running smooth, it's like finding a cold Windhoek Lager after a long day—it just feels right.So, to sum it up, Fallout 76 started out as a bit of a disaster, like a braai rained out by an unexpected storm. But now? It’s more like that same braai, but after the rain has cleared and everyone’s shared a laugh about how soaked they got. It’s not without its occasional hiccups, and sometimes you still find your gear mysteriously vanishing like a sock in a washing machine. But it's become a place you can have a decent time, especially if you’ve got some mates to explore the wasteland with.It's a reminder that even in the gaming world, just like in the Namib, with enough perseverance, even the driest desert can bloom.

_childDocuments_.review: First 50 levels is a straight up Fallout game.  If that's what interests you, start at level 1 and you'll have an enjoyable experience.  After you finish the main quest, its best to bail out if that's what you are looking for because after that, its a different kind of game.     If you want the MMO/Battle Pass experience take the level 20 bump and min max your way to glory.  After you've finished the main quest, the camp building and collections start in earnest and that's really all there is.   Nothing is really a challenge unless your goal  is to solo it all.  If you do not like or accept micro-transactions, you're really going to hate it.   You'll reach a point where all the stuff you want is a micro-transaction.  All the good stuff is in the Atom shop and community has made peace with it.  The community is generous to new comers and well behaved.  PvP is minimal and easily avoidable.  It's designed to be a PvP game and the community, together, seems to have just ignored that bit.   No one is interested.  I've played for hundreds of hours and seen people PvP a handful of times.   There are a lot of events and theme weeks which have all been put on farm mode by the community.  Advanced camp building requires a lot of out of game research.  There are a few people who have mastered it and make exceptional camps while the rest of us make the same square boxes crammed with the same collectables.  For the stuff that's in game, the grind isn't bad,  Keep playing  and you'll eventually get everything there is to be had.   In summary -  Fallout 76 is enjoyable.  There is plenty to distract you from its flaws  and the overall package is ok.  If you can get it on sale the main quest is worth your time.  Basic camp building is fun for a bit and if you're a masochist, the advanced techniques can make some magical results and keep you busy for hours.  I'm a little vague on what keeps me coming back but here I am.  It could be worse.

_childDocuments_.review: TL,DR: Its a great game but it essentially boils down to: are you prepared for an MMO style raid-centric game that, without you having power armour and top-of-the-line weapons by level 35, will grind you, your inventory, and patience down into dust, more often than not, just on the way to the raid where others can help you via their end-game gear.Before you think I'm furious at this game and wrote a wall of text to bash it, that thought is far from the truth, I haven't played in months, and I just enjoy writing, always have, plus I'm waiting for Fallout 4 to download...*again*. Anyway, the game  I'm obsessed with building and creating things using my imagination, and for that, it is...quite good, I'd give it a 6.5/10 in that regard. The community is...also good, very good actually, I had a lot of times where I'm exploring alone, see a guy in power armour running around like a train that doesn't need rails, we lock eyes, stare at each other from a safe distance, and either he runs off like the angel of death on a schedule or approaches me and drops some kind of loot at my feet and then runs off, which, honestly, aside from the worldscape, is my favorite part of the game, the people generally aren't griefers, and in an MMO, that's great, two thumbs up. They're also all big Fallout fans from what I have seen, some of the player homes I've found just by chance were so carefully and passionate crafted with knickknacks placed orderly, and everywhere! Was always awesome to see, even if it wasn't feeding my megalomania, it was really fun and satisfying seeing their passion. So, that's the best part, the people.Where this game falls flat on its face, breaks through the Earth's crust, passes all 9 circles of hell greeting Satan as it then passes Tartaris like a Japanese bullet train trying to escape Earth's gravity by going through the core and then launching itself into the sun to ultimately annihilate itself and you and all the patience you have ever built up throughout your life in a surpasses-any-dark-comedy level of negligence is when it comes to solo play.I'm a casual solo gamer most of the time, willing to go the extra mile when it is warranted and put on my elite gamer dunce cap: I don't want to experience Rust-level griefing from the god d*mn fauna that is everywhere, and which is, by the way, implemented well and has good diversity with cool ideas causing you to often sit there, crouched, staring through a sniper scope at whatever creature you just found, as you weigh the probability- no, guaranteed pain of dying 100 times in a row vs. potentially looting one or two cool things off of it.This game's wildlife is so hostile it makes Valheim (a game I have 960 hours in) and its creatures that will eat through 6 meter-thick medieval fortress walls just to kill you...look like a god d*mn tutorial on how to survive level 1 - 20, after level 30 - 35, if you don't have power armour and GREAT gear, which, by the way, I DO have great gear, just no power armour, you will become highlander except that your life expectancy will be...however long it takes you to run into the next living creature that isn't another player.I've never come across a game that is so unplayable as a solo player, there are raid bosses in other MMOs that are easier to solo than some of the common fauna in this game, that is by no stretch an exaggeration, which absolutely sucks because otherwise, I really like this game, but I need a whole post-apocalypse special forces team around me so that I might have a chance of surviving encounters that I often don't even know I'm engaging in, I just happened to be in the line of sight of something behind a tree, and bam, 2 - 3 shotted while utterly panicked for the 5 seconds it takes for me to die, and by that point, most certainly, frustrated beyond human comprehension because it happened 15 times already - in the last 20 minutes - while I was trying to get to: (insert almost any location except the desert).There's so much to like about this game, forgetting the corporate greed, its a great game, but only if you have 1.) power armour, and 2.) a group of people around you so that you, as a low - medium level player, can employ the survival tactic of a sardine, which is swim around in the cluster of friendlies until the enemy loses interest and goes away (or in our case, dies and gives us loot), which by the way, IS REALLY FUN, but its impossible to have a group large enough for such a play style without being in a dedicated discord, and by the time you realize that, this game will have p*ssed you off so thoroughly, to find the value in it will likely be irrelevant, which is where I am at.Let me explore the game without KNOWING I'm going to be erased from the face of the planet over and over and over again by fauna that my .50 cal minigun should clearly be able to eviscerate, or for instance, my grenade launcher, why do I have to go through this charade of being constantly eviscerated by things that have no place being as lethal as they are, it feels like I should be at the offensive capability of a level 80+ character in Fallout 4 while dying to level 5 -10 radroaches.It really feels like I have realistic damage enabled on myself, where a headshot is a headshot and I die in 1 shot to, for instance, a super mutant 80 yards away, and yet when I'm 5 meters away UNLOADING THE FIRES OF HELL (with a .50 calibre, 6-barrel rotary machine gun), I'm suddenly fighting a final boss, and its not, its just a green guy whose body took radiation like it was human growth hormone-who is armed with a bolt action plank of wood.Its so completely disproportionate, and yet everything outside of that, that I've experienced, was great. I even enjoyed questing, which I heard was an after-thought: the astronaut story was a great story, she really made me care about her, and then I go out and become a grim-dark parody of highlander because I ran into a big shrimp with legs or a single super mutant (and no I don't mean a mirelurk queen, though myself and my friend died to one some 40 - 60 times killing one of those, which was my exact experience soloing when I had a quest in a place with 3 super mutants, except it wasn't 40 - 60 deaths, it was 40 + 60 deaths).So no, I don't recommend it, you have to be a very specific kind of person to play this, and despite me forgiving pretty much any and every game to a point of absurdity for its mistakes, that type of person is just not me. If you can play this and not want to engage in self-harm on an hourly basis, I envy your patience.

_childDocuments_.review: Not even free is worth it, go play any other Fallout lolSo... You are still around? _childDocuments_.review: I'm a Bethesda version owner since not long after launch. There is no "I recommend on sale or a fan of the genre/IP" option, so if you want to play FO4 in multiplayer with survival options, you'll probably like this. The game has its ups and downs, like all multiplayer games. Other then the coat of paint, this game isn't much different then others in the genre. Most of the issues found in FO76 can be found in other multiplayer games, the difference is that most other multiplayer games don't have a massive single player following that was upset over a multiplayer game taking priority over their next favorite single player game.It plays like Fallout 4, a RPG Shooter. The perk system though based on level has some RNG involved in getting specific perk cards needed, it could be improved better (the story of all of Fallout's perk systems). The story IMO is better then Fallout 4, but that's not saying alot as no fallout stories are going to win any Oscars. The survival elements add more of a level of tediousness that all survival games add, more of extra button clicking instead of actual survival or having to make choices. Previously the no NPCs worked in the story, but makes no sense to the ending, it seems Wastelanders is fixing that. The broken mechanics of Legendary weapons and armor are even more visable then in the FO4. It brakes endgame down to the haves and have nots, RNG makes the grind for these legendaries a little unrewarding. The world is amazing even for being lifeless, the sights and visuals feel like you're seeing the world in a new light. The lore added kinda cleans up some of FO4's lore (ie X01 vs MK1) and add to to it in a large amount.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to preface this by saying that I actually like the game. The reason I'm leaving a negative review is because I want it to be so much better by simply allowing us to have way more storage. As it stands right now, you have to pay 15€ a month in order to have unlimited stash boxes for ammo and junk. Those take up a huge amount of space, and junk especially is dangerous to carry on yourself as it can drop on death and get lost forever. Your global stash is also limited to only 1200 pounds (I know, I know used to be 400 at the start, gramps) which means you basically have to stick to just 1 build and just a little junk, if you want to also be able to afford to store some unique gear, either for display purposes or just a personal collection. Eventually, whether you have a subscription or not, you will reach the stash limit and will have to drop, or stop collecting altogether, any items you get from events/quests/expeditions/whatever. Tell me, do you feel like playing a game just to drop absolutely everything you get for playing it, because there's nothing you can do with it, not even store for sentimental value? I personally don't. With the subscription, it is significantly better as you will not have to worry about your stash space nearly as much, you can afford to store dozens of weapons and armour sets without reaching the limit, but it still won't feel great after you play long enough.Simply increasing stash space for everyone, giving everyone unlimited junk space (and perhaps even ammo space) would make this game vastly more enjoyable. FO1st then could offer unlimited space for aid and/or food items, instead, which are way more optional and it's much easier to play the game without those.Other than that, as I said I really do enjoy the game and I would even say paying for a subscription is worth it, if you play at least a few times a week. It's one of the few MMO games that actually feels quite nice to progress through. It doesn't matter whether you are going to be meta gaming and aiming for the best gear possible or just doing what feels right - you will be able to fight your way through the vast majority of enemies, complete all quests, get most camp items you want, etc.As of right now, unfortunately, it seems like the game is taking the opposite approach by introducing even more handicaps for free tier players by severely limiting their options in progressing through seasons. Free tier players get 50% less of the in game currency, which means they can't even afford to buy another season pass with it next time. Overall, this season also yields 33% less currency for all players in general. On top of that, every page of the season has less rewards, most of which could also have been bundled into just 1 package, rather than split into multiple separate ones. Granted, at least this issue is pretty much cosmetic only, you don't really need anything from the season pass in order to enjoy the game, but still it's one of those thing that unfortunately seems to indicate that things are only going to be getting worse, not better. Let's not kid ourselves - the real end game in most online games is always cosmetics.TL;DR: the game is good, monetization is bad, stash space is awful, seasons are getting worse rewards wise.
