_childDocuments_.review: The game certainly got  better over the years but it also grows on you. If you like Fallout 4, you will like the 76. You don't need the monthly subscription to enjoy the game. 1200 lbs storage space is slightly limiting but perfectly manageable. You can always sell your 127 frag grenades to an NPC and free up a bunch of space.I had better experience using GeForce 3080 laptop card than 6900XT on my desktop but your mileage may wary.I like playing this game on laptop because fans don't need to run at full speed to have a good high-FPS high-settings' experience. Even during a Summer. You can spend 30 minutes exploring some kind of a ruin at the end of a rough day at work -- and instantly feel better after. But it is very easy to sink hours upon hours of free-time into this, building your camp(s), exploring, trying to follow various quest-lines and humming along with the oldies' radio station (or listening to some cherry-picked classic music tunes, or just the default atmospheric, very well-written soundtrack that got some nice Appalachian vibes to it).Adventure mode with 24 random players is a great option. Community is nice, I was never annoyed by anyone, folks share stuff with you gladly and buy your goods. It would be nice to have a text chat available, to make it feel more like a proper PC multi-player game. Maybe some day they Devs would actually do that, who knows, probably not, but it's not a biggie. New content is planned for years and years into the future. So the support of the game is guaranteed. It appears to have a cult following and a solid paying player base, so the game will live on for sure.Don't think too much about this. If you want more of that new-school Fallout experience, and the game is on sale -- make sure you got 76+ GBs of space on your drive, and hop on to join the rest of us, exploring this extensive, mad, over-the-top, retro sci-fi world full of dark humor and violence.

_childDocuments_.review: It is 1st/3rd person open world RPG.+Story+Graphics+Playtime+Coop/multiplayer+Weapon/armor modifications+Updates+Radio+Events-Bugs-Trading-Repetitiveness-Endgame-No chatMostly for fans of the previous Fallout games or anyone familiar with at least a Fallout 4 game.It may not be perfect but it ain't a bad game either, there is a lot of content to play through and game changing updates every few months. 50+ hours easy / time consuming  (may contain spoilers)The story was garbage at first, just listening through the holotapes scattered around and reading terminals..., this changed after the Wastelanders update which added human NPCs to the game.Now the story quests are 30% garbage and 70% good or better since the holotapes/terminals are still part of the questlines most of the time.Steel Dawn questline added in the newest update is finally something that we were waiting for, an actual questline with NPCs. I enjoyed playing through steel dawn quests and helping the Brotherhood of steel.Playing the game feels smooth, most of the hit registration problems were already fixed. Melee build is not very satisfying though in my opinion compared to other games and hitting something from 3rd person is sometimes impossible.It is pretty much Fallout 4 with some new stuff and multiplayer.But do not expect to one shot everything with your sniper rifle, unless you play a very specific build. It is not as easy to get overpowered compared to singleplayer Fallout games.Understanding how all the perk cards work can be a bit confusing at first, but it all makes sense in the end.It does not take the crown for being the best looking game in the world, but the graphics are on point. Character and weapon models look great. On the mid-high settings, the game looks amazing, and you can use the photomode to take some beautiful pictures that will replace the default loading screens.I always liked the Fallout radio stations, this is the one part where they did not go wrong.It is a big part of the game, unfortunately pretty much all the songs are copyrighted.Trading / currency and other limiters.Let’s start with the trading.You cannot trade in this game, you can only BUY and SELL you cannot trade an item for an item.Trading was a huge part of the Fallout series in my opinion and taking this out is very annoying.Trading with other players is all based on trust since you can only drop your stuff on the ground and hope that the other player does not take it and leave, I luckily had only a good experience so far.The second thing is the currency.There is a limit on how many caps, scrips, and gold bullion you can have at one time, I did complain about these in the past. All the limits were increased to a reasonable point and it takes a while to reach the maximum cap.Unfortunately, the main issue that the limits introduced stays in the game, the high tier items are valuable way more than the caps and are only traded item for item between players.It also feels like once you reach the endgame there is not much to spend your caps on anymore.Now for the third thing, the limits in general.I have to say that the stash limit is more than fixed, it is now double the amount it was when I have written this review 2 years ago.What else is limited?You are also limited on how many caps you can get for selling items to the vendors this resets daily, also you are limited on how many gold bullions you can get each day and how many items you can scrip.Thankfully these limits were also increased to twice their original value, and it is now way more player friendly.Nuclear Winter - R.I.P. was a Battle royale style PvPvE which was finally removed after all the time it was still in Beta and mostly broken. The 1% of players that played it cried about it in discussions but that’s about it.Fallout Worlds replaced the Nuclear Winter, in this mode, one of 5 settings applies and shakes things up in the Appalachia, for example, infinite ammo or increased enemy difficulty and such. The progress from the Fallout Worlds does not affect the progress in Adventure mode. You can create your own Private World with your specific settings if you have Fallout 1st subscription.I have to say that Bethesda did a good job at keeping this game alive, there were way more problems when I started playing it. A lot of the updates introduced new features and stuff.They made playing with other random players easier, by adding team groups.Allies are cool, but they don’t do much in the camps, they were way more useful in Fallout 4, in Fallout 76 they just stay in your camp and walk around.You can always play solo even in public sessions, the only problem is with the bigger events which are impossible to do without help from other players.Shelters! Added in one of the updates, they are actually pretty cool, all of them can be purchased without subscription now, I feel like they could make it easier to build inside since there is still a lot of limits but it is better than a camp workshop.Legendary perk cards are also a great way to reward players that have been playing this game for a while.I would say that all the updates were actually good and did improve the overall gameplay.I also have to mention the legendary crafting, which now allows players to have legendary Power Armor mods.Trading is still bad and pretty much does not exist.No ingame chat only voice-chat is just not good for multiplayer games.The game can feel empty once you complete everything.The co-op aspect is not as big as you might think, you will have to complete most of the quests solo.There are some game breaking bugs that are reoccurring way more often than they should.I was not sure if I should buy it, so I waited. Then it was in sale during a Free weekend, so I tried the game, played it for more than 20 hours in 2-3 days. So yeah, I would say it was money well spent.If you are deciding between Fallout 4 or Fallout 76, I would go for the Fallout 4 since it has way way way more content, the multiplayer does not add that much to the game, and most of the time you will be playing alone anyway.Sure, but can I recommend it to everyone? That’s the real question, I would say if you played Fallout 4 and liked it, you will most likely like Fallout 76 too, otherwise you better wait for some Free weekend to try it out and find if it’s your jam or not.Just because I like the game does not mean everyone does, I was going to buy it anyway, it was just a matter of time.👻

_childDocuments_.review: After a long period of time consuming gaming session on FO76. (I have played on Xbox as well with over 2k hours) I am writing my first review on Fallout 76.Fallout 76 started off rough, probably the worst launch- game I've ever played BUT it improved over all these years and still does and I am thankful to Bethesda that they didn't drop this game and kept updating it.The quality of life of this game is now on a good state and sometimes I don't get all the negative comments, reviews about it.It's playable, has NPCs and there is always something to do...Now I can't compare it to NV or 4,3,2,1 They are all unique in my eyes.76 is also solo-playable but it is the most fun with friends.PROs: Immersive map and there is a new upcoming area to explore soon (I am looking at you Skyline Valley q.q)Fun to play with friends, collect junks, eliminate threats, daily ops (although they get repetitive), do expeditions etc., BUT the most important one for me is the BASE Building and it gets frustrating on 76 but I have seen so many amazing works so many good camp builds and the community is a big +. They are all helpful, if you're new and just left the Vault the Veteran players will try to give you smoll stuff like (Stimpacks, Radaway) myself included;CONs: game can be pretty tedious if you don't like to repeat stuff. Like Dailies, Weeklies, Daily Ops, Expeditions, and the rewards will be somewhat same (RNG can also be frustrating sometimes) although they try to add more and more stuff with new patches. BUGS! (Bethesda is well known for dem bugs)There are micro-transactions (you can earn atoms from the scoreboard as well), but they're not game breaking as they're mostly cosmetics, camp pre -builds, camp stuff. While it is convenient to have FO1st for all the junk that you can store etc. it is not a must!If you don't like the PVP aspect of the game you can turn on the PACIFIST mode this will make sure that even if you shoot at someone you can't kill them and neither, can they. (Does not work on public workshops)For the next Fallout I would want a co-op mode tho and a lot more lore since I am a lore nerd.Love the Fallout franchise.Hope this helps and if you wanna game or something just PM me, I would gladly like to play with more people.xx Jyinx Recommend 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is a decent to good game built on a rotten foundation. This game is basically a multiplayer mod for Fallout 4. If you liked Fallout 4 and how it "felt" to play, like the game play, how the guns and weapons "felt" and the light character building you could do, as well as the settlement building, then I would give this game a 6-7/10 for you. The quality of the game could depend on the current patch. However if you didn't like what I described above from Fallout 4, then I would rate this game at a 4.5-6 for you, again depending on the current patch quality for the game. My major reasons for not recommending this game:The gun play and general combat has taken a step DOWN from Fallout 4. The move to online by taping multiplayer onto their game engine did something to it. Hard to say exactly, but gun play and most weapons don't feel as good to use as they did in Fallout 4 and frankly many other shooters. The servers are either not good or only decent most of the time. At many times when my internet connection is fine enemies will die several seconds after I stop shooting. Other in-game inputs, like using vendors (both player and NPC) lag for a few seconds after accessing them. These problems with servers affect a lot of the game. The game has significantly improved from release. However there are still bugs to encounter in many places. A Bethesda game like Fallout 4 eventually got to a place where you can now play it almost entirely bug-free. However since they copied and pasted most of Fallout 4 to Fallout 76 and the always online nature of the game it will seemingly never get to the point where you can play it with nearly now bugs. Every patch seems to introduce new problems. Every other patch a big problem. Overall this can be a fun game, especially if you have some friends that you desperately want to play a Fallout-like game with. However the quality of this game is not great. The world is great to explore, but the stories told here vary wildly in quality. Some are good, many are average, and just as many are boring.

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this game (got it at around 50% off) though I listed some cons below if it helps you make a choice in getting this game:)Personally, I enjoyed almost everything about this game (I got it after wastelanders dlc was released). The community is lovely and I've only met friendly players throughout my journey; nice variety of enemies; MANY MANY quests to do even after you complete the main storylines and a huge variety of locations to explore too. While I understand why some people hate the atomic shop (you have to do challenges to get atoms to buy stuff or you can use real money to purchase items from the shop), the seasonal scoreboard lets you attain many items from it for free by doing challenges too! It may seem grindy but honestly, I just do story quests and still manage to complete many challenges. Progressing the scoreboard feels really rewarding and fun and helps make the game more motivating too.I've had a lot of fun customising and building my own camp too and exploring other camps by players! It's a really refreshing game mechanism that lets you take a breather from all the fighting and just chill with your jukebox and wasteland radio playing 70s music. The building could be improved but overall, it has improved tremendously from when I first started the game. It's also really fun exploring to find plans for your camp or progressing the scoreboard to get plans to customise your camp too. Visiting other players' camps is also really great for finding inspiration for your build and I love how much effort everyone puts into building the camp! I also love the vending machines because it lets me buy ammo from others without having to grind too.I also absolutely love bumping into players and squatting and waving to them too:) everyone is so wholesome and I've heard of people dropping free loot for lower level players! Everyone is also very active in doing public events which makes the game more fun and it's really wholesome seeing people reviving players who have been downed. Although the map is huge I think there are only around a max of 20+ players on a server at any point of time so it never ever feels like you're constantly bumping into people. Rather, I get very excited every time I see people :D(However, please note that this is my first time playing a fallout game, though I can understand why people view this game to be inferior to previous series.)Though, here are some cons I noticed:- when there are too many guns being fired at the same time, the game audio glitches and becomes an extremely loud, high pitched, unpleasant noise that doesn't go away till the gunfire ceases - this happened to me during public events with approx 20 players and the final part of the original main story quest  - quests may get glitchy if you dont do it the way the game wants you to sometimes- story quests involving npcs may ignore the choices you make and go with the other choice (the game wants you to choose); though this doesn't really bother me; its more amusing than anything- if you're doing story quests with friends involving npcs and need to enter a building/location with a loading screen, only one person can do the quest at a time and everyone else gets some exp and caps for helping but no quest completion. (may be incredibly frustrating for people who do not wish to redo it from start though this is probably so people can make their own choices and experience the dialogues themselves)- very limited stash box space so you have to constantly find ways to reduce your stash (it is possible to increase your carrying weight by a lot though!)Overall, I thoroughly enjoy the game. I've just completed all the quests and am still having a lot of fun doing side and daily quests. 10/10 chill apocalypse game that is very fun to play with friends. I play it all the time with my bf and we have tons of fun panicking and running from assaultrons, floaters and wrecking supermutants! ps, I play this on 480p res because of my ♥♥♥♥♥♥ com but I still love it so you will too :)

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awful.Oh boy... where do I even begin with this abomination masquerading as a game? I genuinely tried to like this, but it seems the developers went out of their way to make sure no one could enjoy it unless their idea of fun involves mindless one-shotting, pointless events, and building a house for no reason whatsoever.Firstly, this game is laughably easy. In the first 10-15 levels, you're one-shotting everything in sight. After that, you might have to muster the energy to two-shot enemies until you eventually upgrade out of sheer boredom. Survival elements are a complete joke. Hunger and thirst mechanics? Please. They do absolutely nothing. The game inundates you with so much food and water that I ended up discarding piles of it, realizing it was just more clutter in an already cluttered inventory.And don't get me started on the stimpacks. They are everywhere. It’s impossible to die unless you actively try by going AFK. Enemies are a complete farce. They deal no damage; it feels like they’re trying to tickle you to death. Whether it's a fly or a super mutant, everything is scaled to your level and pathetically easy to kill. Encountering a super mutant at level 2 should be a challenge, but here? It’s like swatting a fly.The game's skill system, or lack thereof, is another slap in the face. No skills in an RPG? What genius thought that was a good idea? They replaced it with a card system, which might be interesting as an addition but is an outright insult as a replacement. This is Fallout, not a cheap card game. The complete removal of a traditional skill system in favor of these laughable cards is a disgrace to the franchise and an insult to fans who have come to expect depth and customization in their character development.Let's talk about the quests, or should I say, the soul-crushing chores this game dares to call quests. They are the epitome of uninspired drudgery. Imagine the most tedious tasks you can think of, then imagine doing them over and over again with absolutely no variation. That's what the quests in this game feel like.Continuing on, let’s delve into the sheer disappointment that is exploration. Gone are the days of stumbling upon intriguing random events or engaging with interesting NPCs. In this desolate wasteland of a game, there are no such joys to be found. When traversing the landscape on foot, don't expect any random encounters or surprises. Instead, you'll be greeted with the monotony of a barren world, devoid of any meaningful interaction or reward for your exploration efforts.Sure, there may be some events marked on your map, but they offer little more than mindless waves of enemies for you to obliterate with your overpowered character. Fast travel becomes your go-to method of transportation, and why wouldn’t it? When you can effortlessly dispatch any threat in your path without breaking a sweat, there’s little incentive to engage with the world around you.Gone are the days of stumbling upon hidden treasures or stumbling into unexpected encounters that enrich your gaming experience. Instead, you’re left with a hollow shell of a world, devoid of any substance or intrigue. It’s as if the developers went out of their way to strip away every ounce of excitement and wonder that makes exploration in a Fallout game so captivating.In summary, the exploration in this game is nothing short of a travesty. It’s a barren wasteland devoid of any meaningful content or engagement. If you’re looking for a game that offers rich exploration and immersive world-building, look elsewhere. This game is a prime example of how not to handle exploration in an open-world RPG, and it’s a shame to see such potential squandered in such a manner.If you are a complete casual who loves collecting meaningless cosmetic garbage, then this game might just be your cup of tea.  Want to spend your time gathering junk and decorating your base with utterly trivial knick-knacks? Then by all means, dive right in.However, if you want to feel like you’re actually playing a game, don't even bother touching this disaster. The worst part is, you can't even fix it with mods. That’s right—this travesty is strictly a multiplayer.I could go on about how bad this game is, but when the core is so corrupted, there's no point in beating a dead horse. Stay away, you have been warned.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a skinnerbox masquerading as a fallout game. grind for big number so you can grind harder for bigger number. intentionally miniscule scrapping rates and cap(money) accumulation to pad out your playtime and dangle the temptation of microtransaction timeskips in your face. levelled gear to force you to build or farm for new pieces as you level up, and a durability system to force you to piss away the resources that are already extremely tedious to collect. weapon mods, which are required to round out your "build" require scrapping dozens of copies of the same weapon to roll the dice and maybe unlock the mod you want, which you still have to spend resources to craft. mods also reduce the weapon's durability, forcing you to piss away resources more often just to keep using the only gun your build can use well enough.I only enjoyed freely exploring the old buildings and ruins. reading the little lore snippets and diaries that are sometimes hidden in those places is neat. this is counter to what the game wants you to do, though; its constantly wagging its finger in your face telling you to go do the progression quests and daily events that have the tone of a bombastic parody of what some out of touch boomer executive thinks fallout is about.go spend your money on a real fallout game.

This was horrible for me, as it was already hard for me to find ways to spend time with my son, as he is always out with his friends or just watching YouTube. So I decided to make a Steam account and get this game to see if I could maybe play alongside him. I loaded into the game, picked my character and started playing but I was stuck on what you where supposed to do. I asked my Son for help and he hosted a game for me to join. I loved it as it was the best time I had spent with my Son since my wife had died. This game has ever since brought me and my son closer again and now we actually spend time together outside the house together as well. This game reminded me that there's fun to be had in everything, and it has brought both me and my Son many happy memories.

_childDocuments_.review: Tldr: recent improvements in communication with the players on steam are giving me hope so I'm changing my earlier negative review to positive because I keep enjoying the core gameplay, fighting, and positive interactions with other playersNew review (positive) :)I'm changing my earlier negative review of this game because I see some positive developments recently, there are still some problems that have an impact on my enjoyment of the game and I'm still sore about the - to me and maybe other newbies' - surprise ending of Season 16. But: the key gameplay, fighting in the game (mainly melee without VATS), is fun for me and I'm happy that it's possible to deviate from stealth sniper builds even at higher levels (168 rn) without being punished by the game too severely. I also really enjoy positive interactions with other players, selling things I can spare cheaply and dropping them off in donation boxes and also finding stashes of surprise player drops to see what I can use myself.I haven't reached the ending of any main story quests yet, mainly because I'm too distracted by challenges, events and radiant quests to push them too hard but I also don't consider them the core of the game (just like the main story isn't the core of the Fallout 4 game experience to me).So, even though the game isn't perfect and some frustrations for the players feel like they are meant to be by design to keep masochists engaged, I'm raising my thumb after Season 17 was ended in a more dignified manner than the previous season - I wasn't able to reach reward level 150 (which seems to demand many more than the approximately 200 hours I played the previous season or Fallout First AND using paid boosts) but I'm happily playing my own way most of the time, figuring out how to do challenges by myself rather than looking up other peoples' methods and generally bumbling around even though my boosts are running out, because getting lost in the game is to me what the Fallout experience is all about and that can happen in this game and sometimes there are some nice surprises :)Since the warning to new players that I wrote at the end of my old review still feels as valid as ever I'll leave the old negative review in here (for anyone who still hasn't stopped reading ;-) )Old review (negative) :(Since the devs don't read the community forum anyway:Please put an ingame timer on Seasons, I'm devastated I lost my rewards!Season 16 ended the day before yesterday, without any warning that I was aware of. I was hoping the new season would start towards the end of June, just like the previous had towards the end of March. I discovered I was sorely mistaken after the 24 GB update... Now all the things I didn't yet redeem are gone, as is my chance of ever getting them, even though I unlocked them, I just didn't spend the tickets yet because I was hoping to reach level 100 and then redeem everything all at once. Huge mistake in a game where nothing is communitcated unless it has already happened, I can see that now.An ingame timer that shows when the season ends and how much time there is to redeem things would have helped hugely, other games do that as a month countdown, here I expected at least a week (other info DOES have timers, dailies, weeklies, special event weeks...)Not sure whether I'll continue playing due to heartbreak, but to avoid stuff like that in the future (and alienating lots of other players who won't even say a thing, just leave quietly) I suggest you put an ingame timer to make clear when seasons end, I even researched your homepage because there's next to no info ingame or on steam in general but I misread the announcement that the new season would start after another bonus period towards the end of the month, maybe that graphic was made before it was even decided when exactly the season would end?To anyone considering buying this game: the combat gameplay can be lots of fun (it is for me fighting unarmed without VATS), but the season pass is very grindy and not new-player or even new character friendly, half of the things you're expected to do a day are not spawning for you when you start out. I spent about four hours a day for the roughly sixty days I've owned this game to make the daily quotas because I wanted one level 100 reward (a building set) and the season stopped without warning when I was on level 96... People on the community forum suggested leaving negative reviews since the seasons are becoming MORE grindy (once I rerolled a challenge I couldn't do yet and got "complete 10 events well-fed" instead...) I don't understand why the devs are forcing players into overloading their already taxed servers by playing for so many hours a day, not giving you rerolls that stack (well, because you're supposed to pay for those, obviously) and forcing you to do dailies AND weeklies perfectly for almost the entire time the season is running if you want any hope of achieving the rewards. It's impossible starting out, which made me very sad.

_childDocuments_.review: It is very disappointing to see that the game is still not ready for ultra-wide screens.If you have a monitor like me, i.e. a 49" Odyssey G9 Gaming Monitor, 5120x1440, the game will not make use of its size, and will still display like the old Fallout 4, with a central window and 2 large black sides.At most, it accepts 21:9 / 2560x1080 (letterbox display, rather ugly), or 16:9 / 2560x1440 (full use of the central part of the screen, best solution, but half of screen only...).It means than only the center portion of your screen is used.Difficult to understand why such a game is still so old-fashion when it comes to the fullscreen resolution. I played F4 (+1300 hours) with a modified ini file, accepting the optimum but unsatisfactory 2560x1440, and expected something more modern with F 76. I guess I should have searched more on this topic before purchasing this game, my bad. But I played so many games accepting a full 49" screen, even old ones, that I expected something better from an AAA developer.Now, as you can see this negative review is ONLY about the missing resolution, not the game itself. Which I won't probably not play: for the same visual feeling, better to stick to F4.As I hopped for a renewed / rejuvenated experience, I guess I will have to wait (and hope) for the remastered Fallout 4 version coming sometimes this year, 2023...

_childDocuments_.review: First off, before I explain the review, since everyone has their own personal story about the game, I will also share my story of before and afterI pre-ordered the game literally the day after it was announced at E3, I was extremely excited to get the first moments to play the game and essentially get a head start. The beta launch was an absolute ♥♥♥♥ up, but even then I thought it could be salvagable. I got to LV 22 before just giving up. The world was incredibly boring, there was no interesting story to keep me invested, and there was a lot of bugs. I didnt touch the game for nearly a year and a half. Then I got it for free on Steam and decided "what the hell, lets see if anything's changed." The game is so much better. Compared to previously, its actually a pretty good game. Let me explain why.PROS:~The wastelander update added a lot of what the game needed: a proper story. NOBODY really cared about the overseer's story originally, there was essentially NO lasting story, but with the wastelander update, there is an actual purpose, there's an actual reason to care about your actions.~the new NPCs of the wastelanders, for the most part, are full of personality and color, it feels like real people (or robots), not one dimensional code  with the obvious "raider" trope or "wants to help everyone" trope~some of the views are downright breathtaking, even if the game doesnt have the best graphics. You will most often look over a cliff and have a sense of scale, you can see huge buildings and towns that appear as doodles on your map. ~I absolutely LOVE the idea of the camp, being able to build essentially anywhere you wish as long as it wasnt too close to locations.~Relatively speaking, there is a LOT of new content in this game even though it uses the same engine as Fallout 4. I saw a review saying that "This used 90% of Fallout 4's content", which is absolutely untrue. I say half the stuff in this game are new, there are new armors, new clothes, new weapons, new junks, new textures, new enemies. It is unfair to claim that this is "basically a DLC for Fallout 4", just like it is unfair to claim New vegas as "basically a DLC for fallout 3"~I never really had a problem with the atom situation. I feel like with a lot of challenges and achievements of stuff you basically already do, you can accumulate a lot of atoms by just playing the game. Sure, you wont be able to buy EVERYTHING from the Atoms shop, but you can at least buy a decent amount to customize your base and your character.CONS:~Like any bethesda game, there is a LOT of bugs and glitches, a few of them game breaking, but from my 80 hours of playing, not once did I experience one of those "game breaking" glitches, where an NPC steals your gun or someone steals all your stuff from your vendors. I think its just really bad luck to find one of those glitches~The dialogue can be a little iffy to work with sometimes, not being able to progress, so restarting the entire dialogue, which is annoying~Fallout 1st is just honestly a terrible idea. THATS just uncalled for in a $40 game. If this game was free, hell, if it was $20, then maybe I could understand that, but thats just dumb, even if it solves a problem I will address next~The storage limit is honestly tiny late game. at a measly 800 pounds with no way to change it apart from Fallout 1st, you will fill that up REALLY quickly with guns, junk, and things to sell to your own shop. If there was a way to just increase your storage limit permanently, with perk card of atom points, that would be great.~I'm still a bit iffy on the whole design of repair and scrap kits, they dont change TOO much since repairing armor and weapons is already pretty easy, but its more of a luxury than "pay to win"OVERALL:7.5/10Since I last played it, this game has improved a LOT. Not a single hacker from experience, no big bugs, and an interesting story. Its starting to feel more like a proper game. When this game came out, I would have given it a 5/10, but I have high hopes for it to perhaps be an even better game than now

_childDocuments_.review: (100+ hours of playtime from the Bethesda Launcher and have done everything)If you consider the game from before, Wastelanders is a wet dream. But the dream shatters once you realise that Wastelanders is just a cherry on the cake and not the whole thing. Because the core of the game is still flawed.The Wastelanders story is a joy to go through, it's mostly well written, it has a lot of dialogue and speech checks and progresses the otherwise mostly (as in anything that is before finding the Brotherhood) boring base story of 76. But once you finish the story of Wastelanders, the whole thing shatters and you realise that all the gauss miniguns, shotguns and everything else is under a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ grind. For gold bullion, which also includes a grind for legendary modules.The (core of the entire game) endgame is still the same flawed, odds stacked against the player, throttled grind that was there last year. You can't get more than 200 scrip a day, neither can you get 200 gold bullion a day when most of the stuff has costs in the thousands, and for finishing the campaign you get about 500 gold.This game is still centered around milking playtime and money out of the player and unless whoever it is that makes all this decisisions f*cks off, it will never change.I literally haven't sat down to play 76 this excitedly (even for most of the way through up until the ending) since i first played it. And it really hurts to need to say that it's still trash.(Gonna give props to the optimisation department, runs a whole lot more smoothly now.)Buy it for cheap if you want to see the story, but don't expect to be hooked on as you may find it incredibly boring or frustrating.TL;DR: What's great about Wastelanders is that it's not Fallout 76.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: Overall I'd say get the game when it's on sale. You'll be hard pressed to find more quality content for $20 or less. How much time and money you spend from there is up to you. I've always enjoyed the Fallout universe and despite all of its faults this game still has a great mix of things to love. I still play now and then with the new updates to see what's new. I'll upgrade my C.A.M.P. and see who stops by, and I'm seeing a lot of new players which is great. The updates have been consistent with added content, fixes, and performance tweaks and the community, especially new players, can keep things fresh (and helps me unload my cramped stash with freebies!). Just wish they'd do something about all the hacking/hacked weapons (not that it really matters much in PvE).ORIGINAL: Terrible shame, the entire game really. I've enjoyed all the "Bethesda" Fallouts but they're now simply resting on their laurels with brand name and half-ass everything. Since Fallout 3 my buddies and I have been talking about how great a multiplayer Fallout would be and then we get this. You've read it all: it's shallow, it's buggy, it's poorly developed, it's a cash grab, etc. etc. There is/was insane potential for this game, the graphics are great, the map is detailed, and you can see areas and flashes where a lot of care and thought went into the design and execution of some parts of the game. I got Fallout 1st for a year with Wastelanders cause I came back to the game thinking that would be the turning point. Not really. I still have a few months left on the subscription so I'll play regularly but after that I'm not so sure. There's definitely a lot of content and some of it is great, but you can pick the game up on a Steam sale and get 99% of the experience for a low entry fee (and low time cost because endgame is really just random chance at legendaries or trying to trade with people who have way too much time invested, so just stop when you're done). Honestly, I like building my C.A.M.P. and doing some dailies; it's a great game to kill a half hour on to unwind where you don't have time to get into a more involved game. Heck you can leave it running while doing other stuff and just alt-tab over when an event pops or someone wants to trade. But with that, I'm moving Bethesda to the "wait and see" game companies, no more pre-orders from me (e.g. Elder Scrolls 6).

_childDocuments_.review: [7-7-2024] Doing a little update after jumping back in...  The game is just a cash-shop farming simulator at this point. Theme Park doesn't even come close to describing what this game has become.  You'll find people running around in bright clown costumes, huge bobble heads, Christmas, Valentine, and other "whacky" holiday themed gear.   95% of all updates and seasonal content is for random garbage to put in your "player housing" thing that more or less nobody will see other than yourself if you're bored enough to sit at your own house for hours.  All the "survival" aspects of the game are completely gone.  You have effectively unlimited ammo because you find way more than you use.  You found mountains of legendary loot, most of it you recycle because it's garbage.  You are WAY better off sinking 50-100+ hours into Fallout 4, Fallout 3, New Vegas, etc than this mess.:OLD REVIEW:This game is Fallout 4, with "public servers" full of bugs and issues that will make any new players hate the game and returning players amazed how bad the game still is after all this time.New Players:   You'll be swarmed with high level enemy spawns while attempting to do quests because level 100+ players are warping around the map bored out of their minds but not killing things leaving enemies to stay and guard low level quest objectives.  The game spawns high level enemies if high level players are around, but doesn't remove them when they leave.Old Players:   The group/raid content barely exists.  By the time you level up past 50 (when you've just about unlocked everything in the game), you've explored most all of the content on offer.  You can grind out the same POI's over and over if you're bored.  The high level legendary enemies are generally bullet sponges so you spend most of your time farming ammo to unload on a few legendary enemies to hope for them to roll the stats you need.  Then... go back back to farming ammo again.They've been adding quality of life and other content since release, I would say if they keep this up, and fix many of the major issues that still exist, the game will be worth playing!  By worth playing, I mean playing it long enough to complete all the quests/content you want and then uninstalling it.   The "live-service" multiplayer aspect of this game doesn't add any value to actually playing it for longer periods of time.

_childDocuments_.review: After 3200+ hours since B.E.T.A. I think it's time to tell anyone who's new or plans to come to the 76 universe my thoughts on the game and how it evolved in 4 years to what it is today. I'm choosing to write a review here because it's probably the only place Bethesda cannot delete any criticism, unlike the official discord and now the retired official forums where moderators erase any post that resembles anything else but a praise to their games. Since this will be a mostly negative review I'm going to start with the cons instead of the pros here:1) Communication with the player base exists as long as the player base does not criticize the features of the game as they were designed by Bethesda. After 2 years of testing the changes on live servers - with disastrous consequences - a public test server has been made available to the fans - but still the bugs make it to live servers and the feedback is mostly ignored by Bethesda. All in all it's a "yeah, we hear you, but we're going to do things our way anyway because we know better".2) Every patch is a russian roulette. It may break some minor things or may take out the game entirely for a couple of hours/days depending on the severity. There is no patch that doesn't mess something up.3) Development is atrociously slow. Took them 2 years to bring NPCs to the game, one year and a half to bring the BOS questline, another 2 years to bring the expeditions to the Pitt. The new content is also becoming less and less polished and feels more like "we need to copy something from the older fallouts so we can keep people interested". Lately it seems they do the bare minimum when adding new content, because sometime ago they put on the roadmap and they can't postpone it anymore.4) There is an overpriced shop and a subscription fee. Both are optional, but without them you'll be missing some important quality of life features. The shop items are rotating thus you don't know when something you like may be available again and that's how they create the fear of missing out, putting pressure on you to buy it right now. Some goes with special offers for a limited time. And regardless of the subscription, the really cool stuff will be available in bundles that can only be bought with real money. It's not quite 16x times the details, but it's definitely 16x times the cost or more if you're not careful.5) There is a new battlepass every three months. It's called a season. Every season we get daily and weekly challenges that force you to login almost everyday if you want to get the cool rewards and those cool rewards are among the last on the battlepass. Sure there might be one or two in the middle to keep you going, but if you really want the good stuff you need to finish the season. It's considered new content. Used to be cosmetic only, now they're adding actual items to it so if you don't wanna grind like crazy afterwards, you'd better login daily and finish your battlepass. They're designed to keep the players paying the subscription when there is no actual content being released.6) It's a looter/shooter in the end. The endgame is getting good gear. But unfortunately this too has a major twist. Welcome to Casino 76, where you will re-roll everyday - for a limited amount of course - the stats on your gear. Legendary gear has a maximum of 3 attributes. Let's say you need a good chest piece and rolled the dice, you got 1 good attribute and 2 crappy ones. Next time you roll you do not get to keep the good attribute, you roll again all 3. Chances are you'll get 3 crappy ones and get pissed. Getting a good set of armor with the perfect stats could take you years - I am not joking. Next game that I buy with such mechanics inside it will be a straight refund.7) Nerfs. Every year or so, Bethesda decides to break something willingly. In the name of balance, or in layman's terms, whatever the kids on reddit are crying about. I will not get into everything which was nerfed to the ground, like melee and now explosive. Combined with what I've said in the earlier phrase at no.6, after gambling for a long time to get your desired legendary, when you see it nerfed into oblivion you'll be one angry customer.8) Now we go into the dark side. Which is stricly related to the gambling mechanics on gear and broken balance in the game since day 1. The dark side is the black market, the illegal trading of items for real money. Regardless of any speculation Bethesda is in on it too, it is real and it's breaking the game. Hacked items, duped items, things that were never supposed to be in the game are available to buy and use. Hell, there are even legit items for sale. Say you need a full set of armor and you're looking for certain attributes on it. Will you spend years trying to get it yourself, and by that time probably the thing is obsolete anyway, or will you be tempted to buy it online ? 9) PVP. Many veterans of the fallout franchise are not avid PVP-ers, so I suppose this was implemented for getting the attention of other types of players to the game. It's something they've been toying with since day 1 and failed in all possible manners. From game modes that got scrapped, like Survival (free for all PvP) and Nuclear Winter (battle royale), to forced PvP in certain areas of the map. Also PvP is plagued by black market items, without a proper set of armor, weapons and consumables any regular player has absolutely no chance of making it.10) PVE. For a new player there is enough to do to keep you busy for a good amount of time. It's not as bad as it was 4 years ago, but the content is limited to some degree. The real problem is what the future looks like, new content is becoming less and less exciting. What do I mean by that? Well, the first world boss was flying. The second world boss was walking. Now the third world boss isn't even moving. See where I'm getting at ? Wastelanders brought NPCs to the game and it was a major and a good change, then the Brotherhood of Steel arrived but it was way less content there, next we had the Pitt which is a glorified dungeon and now they're bringing a very over simplified version of Nuka World from Fallout 4 into 76. And they'll keep doing that, put up the minimum amount of work into features as long as the subscriptions keep rolling in.Here comes the pros now:1) You can shoot super mutants with a MG-42 machine gun while you're chugging down Nuka-cola Quantums and flying in your power armor like you're Aluminium Man. Basically you can go do whatever the hell you want as long as it puts a smile on your face.Conclusion:Take it with a grain of salt. This is Fallout 4 multiplayer with pretty colors. And a ton of bugs. What Todd Howard said in an interview a while back sums it up pretty good: "We sold 12 million copies of Fallout 4 and now we can't reach those players anymore". And by that he meant reaching their wallets. They've tried with Creation Club, but anyone in their right mind would get free mods instead. 76 is the answer, it's where they can put up a shop and slap a subscription fee to a beloved franchise. Everything is done so you'll spend more time in-game and buy buy buy and then buy some more. That's why there is no mod support, even if they promised it a long time ago. That's why there are artificial problems created in-game, like the limits on stash size and the durability of items, so they can sell you the solutions. Of course you're not forced to buy them, but every year they tease you with the benefits of having a subscription and give you little doses of quality of life for free in the shop. Just like a dealer they try to hook you up and then milk you dry. So be careful, buy it on discount and use it at your own risk. Go through the story, because now there is one, have some fun, but don't make the mistake of getting too attached to it and have great expectations. You'll only be hurt in the long run.

_childDocuments_.review: Fallout 76 had a horrible and laughable start with it's early access and launch. The clown fiesta continued for a very good while and honestly it was much worse than what Elder Scrolls Online ever could be on launch.Usually I'd bat my eye away thinking the developers would just leave it as abandonware, not updating the game and essentially have another Anthem to scoff and laugh at and ridicule the high up executives who think the "release it now, patch it up later" business model is remotely any good.Many bugs were patched, the optimisation was.. improved to a tiny extent but the gameplay still feels marginally far better than what Fallout 4 is and certainly feels like it has more progression and certainly looks and feels better than what Fallout 4 plays like if it weren't for the awkward optimisation.As an MMO, it has an end-game, from a fully functional raid with mechanics and additional difficulties, as well as end-game worthy upgrades that can be acquired from the Scorchbeast Queen - albeit not much of an engaging fight. And I am more curious if other raid-like activities will be introduced into the game.Some builds arguably are busted and should be looked at, but there is a large variety of weapons, perks, armours and enemies that add variety to the game. Most enjoyable enemies are the cryptids, who are visually freaky and can be terrifying at times.Exploration is absolutely perfect, many different areas to visit and many quests and events there are to do to level your character and get into intriguing lore/backstory narratives. And I do think the lack of a major plotline does work for the game, being able to find tid-bits of information by searching for it is more fun (though this is more of an opinion based point.)I emplore those who believe the game doesn't have any redeeming qualities to check out this post made by an ex-Obsidian employee and read it thoroughly, those that do own it should try it out.

_childDocuments_.review: As a disclaimer: I've been playing on and off on console since launch, so this Steam account isn't representative in terms of hours played etc.TLDR: Game is still kind of empty, kind of laggy and kind of meh.I was among the people who were actually hyped to have a multiplayer Fallout game, while everybody else was vocal about only ever wanting deep singleplayer Fallout experiences. I bought at launch and refused to refund even when I saw just how lacking essentially everything about the game was. I thought it had potential. I still think it has potential. The problem is - Bethesda clearly don't.The one actually good update this game ever got was Wastelanders. That's the update that fixed this game's reviews to mostly positive. That's the update that makes people say "you should give the game a try again, it's actually much better than it used to be, don't trust the old negative reviews!". That update? Released 3 years ago. You know what released in the 3 years since then? Nothing of interest. Now... Of course the few hardcore fans who still manage to start this game every day just to rebuild their CAMP for the millionth time in a row will tell you otherwise... They'll tell you that it's perfectly fine and well that a live service game with a pricey "optional" subscription and cash shop receives a single minuscule update per year that lasts you three hours at most. It's not. Fallout 76 wasn't a big game when it released... It still wasn't a big game once Wastelanders released... And it hasn't gotten any bigger since then. You can easily "beat" Fallout 76 unlike most other live service games. And once you do, there won't be anything new for years to come. The new Atlantic City update? Shamefully tiny. Expeditions are just mini dungeons you're meant to grind over and over again for the same rewards. There is nothing here to get excited about. Nothing here to want to come back for. Nothing to sink your teeth into. Small, boring, life support vibe updates. You know what gets regular updates though? Ding ding ding. the CASH SHOP! Buy crap for your CAMP, buy more crap for you CAMP! Buy all the crap for your CAMP because you know this game has nothing to do but decorate your useless ♥♥♥♥♥♥ CAMP with more useless ♥♥♥♥♥♥ cash shop decorations!If you're into comatose, wasted potential, live service games that big companies clearly use as cash cows and nothing more... Hell yeah, this is the game for you! If you wanted a proper Fallout experience with story? Look elsewhere, this game's story is still barebones and lacks RPG elements badly. If you wanted a proper multiplayer live service experience, look elsewhere, because you'll be running the same damned 3 events and 2 expeditions for Fallout 76's remaining lifetime. If Bethesda still had a single brain somewhere in that company, maybe they could finally understand that live service games are meant to get updated. But I guess their entire business strategy is reselling Skyrim a million times and attempting the same with Starfield (sadge that didn't work out so well for you, Todd "it just works" Howard).

_childDocuments_.review: The game was rough at the beginning. But even there i kinda liked it. It had a lot of issues and bugs, but a lot has changed since then.No. It isn't a "perfect" multiplayer Fallout game, but at least a good one by now. Does it deserve all the hate? No. Especially since already since the beginning, many "reviewers" just jumped up on that hate-train back then to smudge Bethesda as some evil company. They didn't care if they review of the game would be anything you could call constructive criticism. Hell many reviews i watched had barely any time played in the game. And even if they did, they often brought up points, that were completely beyond me how they complain about it, but happily crawl up other companies rear entrances who do far worse with their games.The whole Fallout 1st thing. Is it a good service? Not directly. Is it worth it? Not if you aren't take full advantage of everything you get. And even then it is "questionable", but i rather pay 15 bucks a month to be by myself and play with friends without having to worry, that some random idiot runs up to my camp and kills my Deathclaw again.Why do i defend the service then somewhat? Because there are still a lot of subscription games out there, that demand nearly the same amount and WON'T let you play at all, should you not pay them in time. (Looking at you Blizzard.)But people happily defend those companies. Why? I don't know? Probably because they are used to it that they have to pay to get access there. Though there i don't understand why they complain about Fallout 76. No one forces you to get the subscription service. You can still play the game just fine.Some of the worst complaints people had back then are mostly ironed out. There are still bugs and some really annoying ones at that. And they still have a lot to fix and bring to the table. But for the current amount i would say it is a decent game to be bought. It isn't the best "pick" you can make if you want to play with friends, but if you are a fan of the Fallout universe and wanted to play the game with your friends, it is a recommendation worth making.The community itself reminds me a lot of the Warframe community itself. Very open and warm for newer players. Ready to help with a lot without even wanting anything in return most of the time.In my opinion, the game is on the same way as No Mans Sky is now. Everyone had high expectations. Everyone got disappointed. Everyone got angry at the game and devs. The devs took their time to build it up and tried to deliver what people missed out and people started to warm up for the game again.Maybe in a year i even will see some of the "bigger" reviewers give the game another chance and start recommending it the same way i do now already. _childDocuments_.review: Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception and Mask of Truth are two halves of the same story and can't really be broken up. Thus, I will be reviewing them as a whole.This is my favorite VN of all time. The story, characters, sound, art, world, and gameplay all come together to make something magical and I think a lot of other people- even those new to the genre- will be able to enjoy it as well so I’m just going to gush about it and hope that convinces you to try it.Overall, the story will take you about 80 hours to get through on your first go. It seems like a lot, but that time is used very effectively. The characters are organically built up and the way I got attached to them over time is something I’ve only really felt the likes of in the original Mass Effect trilogy. The world gets very fleshed out with both ancient secrets and more mundane details that make it a very rich, interesting place to be. The story takes its time setting up big scenes so they hit like a truck and then paces itself with more lighthearted moments like wannabe Robin Hood pitching gold bars through people’s windows or giving a catgirl a suggestive backrub or getting drunk and stupid with your bros. Then it’s back to political maneuvering, destiny, war-crimes, mecha Godzilla battles, and suffering.The 2D artwork is absolutely gorgeous. The style is distinctive, the artists actually know anatomy, the sprawling landscapes make the world come alive, and the coloring is superb. The 3D sections were designed to run on the Vita so they’re chunky, but they don’t really distract. The screenshots can tell you more about this than words can, so I’ll move on.I still listen to the soundtrack on Spotify on a regular basis. Not every track is fully orchestrated, but even the parts where they didn’t splurge on the production values have excellent compositions that pull you further into the mood. When Utawarerumono pulls out all the stops, it won’t lose to any other video game OST and the way those songs are placed elevate the already good scenes into another world. It almost feels mean at some places. Like, I’m already an emotional basket case, why do you have to rob me of any semblance of dignity I have left by putting that on? On top of that, you have great voice acting for every line in the game. My only complaint about the audio is that one track, Sadame, is underused for how good it is.Utawarerumono has tactics gameplay sections but they’re by no means the main attraction since they only make up 10-20% of the playtime. They’re not going to dethrone tactics giants like Disgaea, but that’s not their job. Their job is to compliment the story, bring you into the action, and break up long sections of reading. For that purpose, they do quite well. If you’re a tactics veteran, there’s enough depth and polish to keep you entertained to the end. If you’re a tactics noob, there’s a turn rewind feature that will make sure you get through just fine. For major encounters, the gameplay is integrated surprisingly well with the story, and the final bosses of each part are made with a lot of care and extra touches so they don’t lag behind how bonkers the story is going.(Truth) This part is the non-stop emotional roller coaster. I can’t keep track of how many times a scene floored me. Prepare for a treat. Oh, and as a tip, when you get to the super obvious final boss, make sure you have the next 6 hours free because once you start nothing is going to be able to pry you away from the screen until you’re done.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth

_childDocuments_.review: Mask of Truth aims to provide a satisfying conclusion to the many plot threads set up in Deception, and it does it masterfully while also being a perfect tribute to everything that came before. The gameplay is mostly the same aside from new characters and some additional moves and skills for returning characters. One neat feature is that the game allows you to carry over some items from the previous game which makes the experience easier. As my friend put it, The soundtrack for Deception is already a treat for the ears, but the additional tracks in this game pushed it to one of my favorite video game soundtracks. And if you’re a fan of insert songs in key moments, get ready cause this game has a feast waiting for you.There isn’t much for me to say on the story because my words cannot do it justice. This entire trilogy is an experience, one that will have a special place in my heart for a long time. “Catharsis” being one of the features listed in the Steam page is no joke.The entire final battle made me have what I could only describe as an ethereal experience. And despite being one of the happiest endings I’ve read, this game made me cry more than I could remember in the last year. You will not regret a single moment of investing your time into the world and characters.Utawarerumono is my favorite series of Visual Novels ever. The entirety of Truth is one roller-coaster of emotions and by the end, it wrung out every last tear it could from my soul. All in all, I can wholeheartedly recommend this game and the trilogy as a whole to new fans and veterans of the Visual Novel genre alike, as well as anyone else that is curious on how “Catharsis” can be an actual game feature.

_childDocuments_.review: Sequel to Mask Of Deception. It is undoubtedly necessary to play the previous game for the best gaming experience. This game can be said to have reached the peak in the game plot, presenting a shocking epic story. The main storyline of the game, as always, is very long, but despite this, there are still many plots and characters that are handled too hastily, while some other parts take too much time to describe. Frankly, I personally think it might be better to split this game into two more games. The game's music also brings players a great gaming experience as always.Nonetheless, this time the game's gameplay is arguably terrible. As a visual novel game with RPG strategy as its selling point, this RPG battle made me feel inferior to the previous one in terms of experience, and even the unreasonable design of several later battles was embarrassing. In the course of the game, the number of vicious bugs encountered is much more than that of the previous game.All in all, I would recommend this game to fans of the series, it won't disappoint you in terms of plot. But in terms of gaming experience, this game can be said to be quite unsatisfactory.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Best gameplay of the trilogy, shakiest story of the trilogy, longest game in the trilogy, and a must-play if you enjoyed either of the first two.Each Utawarerumono game has its strengths and weaknesses, but it should be safe to say that if you enjoy one, you may as well play them all. However, they shouldn't be played in any order. Mask of Truth practically REQUIRES that you've played both previous games; very little of the plot will make any sense if you have not at least played Mask of Deception. Also, Mask of Truth allows you to transfer over a save file from Mask of Deception, a la Arc the Lad 2 or Fire Emblem Radiant Dawn. Mask of Truth is the longest of the trilogy, by a wide margin. While Prelude to the Fallen took me around 21 hours to complete, Mask of Truth's took me 43 (33 hours on the main campaign + 10 hours on the postgame). It's certainly one of the longest games I've played recently. At times, the length was a problem. I felt that there were many scenes which could've been drastically cut down, and they would've been better. In particular, the Nakoku arc took too long, and the entire ending sequence lasted longer than it probably should've. The main villain's motives were questionable; the game doesn't provide a compelling reason why he waited until the final act to play his hand. There's also a part in the final act where the characters talk about why they should NOT bring any soldiers to the final area... Five minutes later, you see that they brought soldiers to the final area. Some stuff in the game doesn't make much sense.Many battle/war scenes are predictable anime fare: you have the enemy on the ropes, but then the enemy activates some super secret power, but then an ally arrives at just the right moment to thwart the enemy. We've all seen it a hundred times before. I get the sense that the writers of Utawarerumono were more adept at writing comedy/slice-of-life than they were at writing wartime SRPG stuff. This is another reason why I feel that Mask of Truth is the weakest of the trilogy, storywise. While Mask of Deception was mostly a whimsical comedy, Mask of Deception is mostly a wartime drama. The former allowed the writers to play to their strengths more. As another point against the game: Fumirul's entire character was entirely pointless and added nothing substantial to the story. On the other hand, Mask of Truth features the best gameplay of the trilogy, and it's not even close. BP allocation is more complex now. Battles have multiple phases now. Enemies actually scale well. AI is improved. The postgame Dream Arena battles absolutely trounce anything that the first two games offered. Dream Arenas #12, #14, and #15 were especially enjoyable and actually made me think. I appreciate SRPG battles that make me think. Completing the trilogy was a fun experience. I'll have to keep an eye out for other hybrid Visual Novel/SRPGs in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, if you’re not familiar with the Utawarerumono series, you should start by playing through  first as it otherwise will spoiler the whole experience. .After playing Mask of Deception, I knew that Mask of Truth will very likely not let me down, especially since many people assured me that this entry focuses even more on its story. Besides, the prequel just left too many mysteries unsolved, so that I couldn’t wait to get to know the whole story. And of course, the cast is too adorable so I was delighted to read more about them and even if the story ends up being disappointing, I could still have fun with the events that revolve around the characters. Luckily for me, the story, as well as character development, is splendid here as well.Usually, I do give a summary of the story so the reader knows what they’re getting in, but in this special case, I’ll refrain from that as only those that finished Mask of Deception will probably read through this review. And those who didn’t won’t get spoiled. That being said, Mask of Truth directly follows the events after its prequel and a bit lengthier although that only means that there is more room to develop a proper storyline. Other than being the last half of the game, it becomes obvious that both games are meant to be played together and could as well be seen as a huge visual novel overall.Although there is a brief explanation of the storyline in the previous game in Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth, it only has the purpose of refreshing the reader's memories in case it was a while ago they last played Mask of Deception. Of course, just the summary isn’t a replacement for the previous game since the whole character development is missing here and hours of gameplay cannot be replaced with a brief summary. Plus, I can say that the experience definitely wouldn’t be the same when I didn’t get familiar with the characters first, even if that meant I had to go through a lot of hours just to read slice-of-life scenes. After all, the player wouldn’t understand the relationship of the cast otherwise.That being said, Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth does seem to only contain minor differences compared to its prequel. I heard that this entry is supposed to more story-heavy and whilst I certainly do agree on that statement, there are still a lot of slice-of-life moments implemented in this game, especially in the beginning. While I couldn’t wait for the story to unfold, I enjoyed that I still got my precious comedic moments with the whole cast although our dream team isn’t together the whole time. There is a similar pattern available here as Mask of Deception started light-hearted as well, only to catch its reader off guard with the story-heavy elements.Talking about the story, whilst I already found the prequel very emotional, this game even managed to surpass it. It hurts the most when I notice how close the cast is when something bad happens to them, yet it was inevitable. That’s the reason I really do appreciate the fluffy moments in the beginning since it only makes its reader getting more attached to the characters – once again. The good thing here is that I found out new aspects about the cast even though I thought I already knew everything about them after having played through Mask of Deception which made me fall in love with each of them a second time.After the end of Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception, I was hoping that Mask of Truth was going into a slightly different way. By that, I mean that the relationships of the characters would become.. well more romantic. Sadly, romance wasn’t one of the main genres at all although it does indeed get more romantic in this entry. It’s very minor though, so a change is barely noticeable although that could mean that the character development is so well executed that explanations regarding the character’s relationship weren’t necessary at all. After all, there were way bigger issues to deal with than romance ones although it was heartwarming when they started to notice how they do feel about each other.The main focus in Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth would be the story, especially in the latter part of the game. I found that this entry even felt gorier than its prequel. Although there isn’t an explicit and detailed presentation, there seems to be more blood spilling here. The reason is probably that the whole game takes place during the war, yet I still found that the events were displayed, well.. redder than I expected. Even when unknown characters died, it made me feel quite uncomfortable, but that’s actually a good thing as the whole theme is supposed to make its reader feel rather gloomy since war isn’t exactly a pleasant thing.Graphic-wise, Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth looks exactly like its prequel: Pretty, beautiful and gorgeous. The only change that I noticed was that the game is divided into sections and when completing one, a menu pops up that lets its reader use their BP points, do different kinds of battles, equip their party members with items or simply save their progress and much more. I liked this menu because I could conveniently spend my BP very often, which I admittedly forgot way too often in Mask of Deception since it does pop up right before a battle as well. You see, the issue with the prequel was that the menu didn’t pop up often during the playthrough. When the player progresses with the story the icon next to this option also hints whether there are different events to go through, a battle or just a longer part of just reading.Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth is a satisfying conclusion that answers a lot of mysteries that were still left unknown in Mask of Deception. Both games should be played together, and those who played the prequel will know what to expect of this game. In the beginning, there are still a lot of fluffy moments although the story will get serious and emotional soon enough. Like the previous game, the battles are engaging and greatly helped with the immersion since it fired me up even more and made me feel like I actively helped the characters out. All in all, Utawarerumono is a series that should be played by everyone who enjoys a good story-heavy game fueled with plenty of slice-of-life elements, plus an adorable cast.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR don't sleep on this title.  Despite being someone who avoids visual novels as a rule, I cannot recommend this game highly enough.As a player I tend to avoid the visual novel genre.  This game (and its predecessor) are most certainly visual novels first.  The vast majority of your time will be spent reading text and letting you choose which sections of the text you will read next.  For my part I typically gravitate towards games that are more focused on delivering their story through solid game play.  I remember going into mask of deception with more than a little disappointment when I realized what I'd just gotten myself into, and I wasn't expecting the experience to leave much of an impression when I was done.  That being said, this series absolutely blew me away.  Since I'm a game play guy I'll start with that.  Combat in this game is highly nuanced and provides the player with a wealth of strategies that can be employed while keeping the superficial mechanics fairly simple on the surface.  Characters interact with their targets through the use of "Action Chains" which can require the player to time a button press or hold a button and time the release (or a combination of these 2 inputs) each with their own visual cues.  As your characters level up they can perform longer chains with more inputs that are, in most cases more effective.  Surface level strategy requires the player to select the appropriate action chains to use while positioning their characters advantageously.  But as most veterans of the series will tell you there is MUCH more to it than that.  Additional mechanics that can (and in certain encounters MUST) be exploited are: hidden inputs for action chains, action chain cancelling, elemental type advantages, Overzeal (kind of a burst mode for each character) management, passive abilities that significantly impact combat, equipment management that drastically alters your tactics, facing and positioning, counters, stat allocation, and status manipulation.  These mechanics give this combat system a truly impressive amount of depth, and while the game does a solid job of introducing each of these systems to you, it's up to you to master them.  Each character in your roster plays VERY differently, but each character also has enough variety in their tool kit to work well with whoever else you bring to a fight.  Team tactics are a must for the endgame, and the sheer volume of strategies the player has at their disposal does more to recommend this combat system than anything I've seen elsewhere.  Do not be fooled by the fact that this game is a visual novel.  The combat system is one of the best I've seen in a long time.  As far as the story goes, I'll simply say: get ready to feel things.  For the most part the narrative is fairly lighthearted until all of a sudden it very much is not.  The ending of mask of deception hits like a truck, and mask of truth somehow manages to improve on even that.  The plot is well crafted, loose ends are tied up appropriately, and characters are well defined and act according to their nature.  While the story has its silly moments (and no small amount of fan service), it never feels arbitrary, and it serves to shift the tone away from what is actually a deadly serious narrative.  This series is amazing, and I hope to see more work from this developer on Steam in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: Don't be alarmed by the playtime, I've finished both games on the PS Vita and bought them on PC because I just love the series so much.This is sort of a sequel to my Mask of Deception review as much as the game itself is a direct sequel, you should read both to get the full picture.Man, where to even start with Mask of Truth..... Mask of Deception ends on a brilliant sequel hook holding amazing promise, and Mask of Truth delivers IN SPADES on that promise. Like I said in my other review, by the end of it all, it almost feels like Mask of Deception was just a massive prologue for what's to come. And Mask of Truth is simply amazing.... The story here is a lot more action-packed (though there are still the classic "slice-of-life" moments the series is known for) and there are a lot more battles. The gameplay has some adjustments that make it feel better to play overall, and some neat new mechanics, it's very solid overall.There's not enough that can be said about Mask of Truth, but at the same time, I can't really say too much without spoiling it all. The very beginning of this game is already a DIRECT sequel to Mask of Deception's ending, which is a huge spoiler in and of itself. All I can say is that this game takes all the qualities of Mask of Deception, and turns them all up to 11. Mask of Deception laid the groundwork that made Mask of Truth possible, and this game absolutely does not disappoint. I already loved it since the first game, but It's here that the series TRULY shines the brightest.Haku is my absolute favorite protagonist out of any game, the development he goes through here is absolutely INSANE. And Kuon is also my favorite heroine, she's such a complex character with a wealth of emotions.It is my absolute favorite game of all time, and the best one in the series by far, that ended the trilogy in the most satisfying way possible. It's really THAT good.I really don't have enough words to put on this review at this point that wouldn't be repeating myself, and there's not much more I can say without actually spoiling stuff, so I'll just finish it by saying...I love Utawarerumono so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ much.

_childDocuments_.review: I do not really review games, but I cannot skip this one. Finished this, and Mask of Deception on consoles, bought on Steam to replay it and be able to review/recommend it. If you are not a fan of text heavy games/VNs but want to try at least one in your life - please choose Utawarerumono series. Fantastic story packed with feels, phenomenal music I still listen to every day, lovable characters, beautiful art, has actual gameplay too, so it's not just reading. It will make you smile, laugh, and cry. It was also made before the whole political correctness fad kicked in, so expect some saucy jokes! I cannot recommend it enough; one of the best things I have experienced in my life. Play in order: Utawarerumono (2002 version or its remake Prelude to the Fallen) -> Mask of Deception -> Mask of Truth. Do NOT start with this one. I promise you will not regret it.Rest in peace, Keiji Fujiwara.
