_childDocuments_.review: WARNING:Mask of Truth (MoT) is is the second half of the second Utawarerumono game. DO NOT play this if you haven't played the 1st half, . It's not required to play the first game ( or the remake  that's soon to be released in english/steam), but playing it will enhance the experience. If you're lazy, watching the 2006 Uta1 anime, or to a less extent the "False Faces" adaptation of MoT if you don't mind some inconsistencies, should be ok. No one can blame you for not wanting to suffer through the long and slow slog that MoD is.Disclaimer:I've already finished the game on both vita and PC. It took me about 80 hours of slow reading to finish main story for the first time, but i've skipped nearly all text on PC and just got all achievs. Hence the "short" 35 hours time.---Review:Follow the epic sci-fan tale of  Hakuoshtor and his mindless followers to reclaim  Yamato . Shed liters of tears with Jesus as he struggles to deceive not only his people, but himself as well, of not being a lazy asѕ drunkard in one of the most recent Visual Novels to join the top ranks of big names like Steins;Gate, Clannad, Fate What/ever, Muv-Luv and Fata Morgana.Honestly, there's a lot more to the story but spoilers are plenty. The short description above only illustrates the setup that Mask of Deception left us with, which is not the biggest part of the game (but Haku's sacrifices for his dead brothers makes it the most beautiful). The story potential and all the mysteries that MoD gave us with its ending events weren't left to waste, and MoT only gets better. Hurray for not spending dozens of hours with pointless slice of life!The translation is one of the better ones i've read in JRPGs, you can cleary notice that it was done by people who knew and cared for the Utaverse. Voice acting is good, but Hakuoshtor's forced voice sounds a bit silly, especially during emotional scenes, but it's bearable.The PC port is quite good as well and i didn't run into any problem during the whole game. Actually, the port is so faithful to the console original that we're stuck playing at 30fps with upscaled assets from 720p up to 1080p. Being a VN, that shouldn't be a huge issue... but the strategy RPG parts of the game require proper timing, with visual/audio cues, for landing critical hits and the 30 fps doesn't help much there. There aren't many SRPG parts compared to the text walls, but they were given proper care for fun, and with a good balance and a bunch of mechanics that you'll actually have to use to see any success... unless you exploit Haku and Fumirul's Overzeal loop. Oh and uh, there's mouse/kb support.Pros:+ Amazing story. No wonder it is so highly praised.+ Translation is pretty good as well, but some terms/names could've gotten a better work.+ Combat is well thought mechanically, and you can fast-forward the animations.Neutral:* Cliche anime characters.* Soundtracks can range from really good original songs to some generic sounding ones, but it's fine overall..* Port is fine, but locked @ 30fps with 720p assets. Shouldn't matter much though.Cons & nitpicks:- The third part of MoT is a powercreep-fest and isn't as interesting as the others.- All the supernatural crap, like the thing about masks turning you into Ultraman/Kaijuu, are so silly. Sometimes it feels like an edgy version of The Mask.- Cringy shounen battles.- Magic or a magical being will solve/screw anything that can't be explained with pseudo-science.- Too many OP chars in the story. Uta1 chars are op just for the sake of them looking cool for the fans, but it's stupid lol.- Protagonist has a terrible time trying to do some sort of "batman voice".- Some of the party members sole reason to exist is to be convenient for the story.- There's always that scene where everyone will encourage the MC, or the other way around, before anything remotely important happens.- The main villain.- Maroro.-  is a dicк.- Anyways, as you can see above, my issues with the story are mostly typical anime things, and Uta2 is still one of my favorite VNs/SRPGs.May the Lord  be with you.

_childDocuments_.review: Not everyday you come across something that is truly special enough to change certain aspects of your life. Even more so, when it's a video game. It would be a disservice to consider this trilogy as anything but that. I was fortunate enough to go through the entirety of the trilogy without getting spoiled and I can confidently say that this is one of my most favourite experiences with any form of media. The final third of Mask of Truth is the stuff dreams are made of.Haku has straight up become my most favourite protagonist. The main cast of Prelude to the Fallen will always have a special place in my heart, but the main cast of both the Mask games will be the new standard against which I will judge a main cast of characters hereon. They truly are special and I deeply mourn the fact that I won't be able to spend my time with them again in the near future. I was beyond satisfied with the ending of the game that managed to provide an excellent conclusion to the protagonists titanic character arc. I couldn't have hoped for a better ending. The final stage/battle is one of the greatest final stages I have played. It's up there with the likes of 13 Sentinels Aegis Rim final stage. Towa Ni is such a precious song, that perfectly complements the overwhelming emotions running throughout the final stage. Many a tears were shed.If White Album 2 didn't manage to convince me about Suara, this trilogy certainly does and there's no Japanese vocalist out there whose songs flood my spotify playlist as much as hers does. I can never hear Kimi ga tame and Koi Yume without tearing up a bit. Nuedori is my most favourite opening song of any game and within a month, I have listened to Rakujitsu no Toki on repeat for over a thousand times. The VA for everyone was top notch, but Haku's is the best voice acting I have seen in a game. The gorgeous artwork of the CGs in this game are second to none, and most of them are going straight into my desktop wallpaper list.As it is always with such memorable stories, I wish I could forget it all and start again from scratch but I am truly grateful for this game which has given me so many wonderful memories, stories, songs and characters to cherish forever. I will never forget this, this joy of having gone through such an epic. Words fail me, in trying to justify the long lasting impact this game is bound to have on me, and I will eagerly look forward to the Aquaplus 30th anniversary next month...hoping, praying that we get even more Utawarerumono content than that was promised. I wish for that, with all my heart.

_childDocuments_.review: Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth is the second chapter of mask Saga. began right after the conclusion of Mask of Deception, the plot kicked into high gear as the MC became fully involved in an all out war while uncovering the secrets of yamato. all the foundation built in mask of deception finally pay off. tons of character development and parts of the world that was mentioned in mask of deception finally revealed. imo it is a great conclusion to the series. if you like deception, there is no question you will love mask of truth. my only complaint with the story is some part of the end feel kinda off because it is the high climax of the series and it assume you to have played the first uta game (mask of deception is the second game and mask of truth is the 3rd) the first UTA game will come out on steam later this year, and to be honest after spoiling myself of the first game plot, the conclusion become really satisfying and tied up the 2 sagas in a neat knot while also leaving some room for speculation or even a potential sequel.now let's talk about combat. the combat is mostly the same, with new characters with new movesets. the problem is mask of truth encounter can be a bit . . . overwhelming in a bad way. it is still relatively easy and simple but sometimes there are just too much and the enemy HP are too high (especially towards the last _childDocuments_.review: The first 35 hours of this game are fantastic. Some of the best storytelling and writing I've ever seen in a VN, or even in a video game of any genre. The gameplay is great, the maps are well designed, the pacing is good and the antagonist is compelling and a good foil for Haku.However, the final 10 hours are terrible...It feels like they try to fit an entire games worth of story, exposition and events into the final 10 hours of the game, and so coming off the first half of the game which was paced well and was interesting throughout, you get a conclusion that feels incredibly rushed and confusing, that leaves a ton of plot holes in what is supposed to be a "definitive ending". A lot of people don't mind the rushed ending since the final boss and epilogue is so good, but at the end I never felt the advertised 'catharsis'. The final arc just left so many questions, so many plot holes and unexplained contrivances, LOTS of asspulls (such as characters being able to run across an entire continent in only a few hours, knowing EXACTLY where the main characters are, setting up an ambush in a heavily fortified secret area, and running across the continent again in a few hours while being gravely wounded) and the whole thing centered around an antagonist that was so boring and poorly written compared to the one that came before. In the end I didn't cry (that much), I was mostly just baffled by what I had just witnessed and annoyed by the fact that the conclusion to the series I had been playing for the past 100 hours was so half assed and convoluted.

_childDocuments_.review: The most grandiose way to end a series. Over a hundred and fifty hours spent alongside some of the most well-written characters, each one more charming than the other. With the stakes at an all-time high, there is nothing they won't sacrifice for the greater good. A story about sacrifice, and one done well.Taking the risk of making an entire 50hr game just the stepping stool of this one was well worth it; Mask of Truth pays off with the greatest of endings. From the vast wallpaper-worthy CGs, the heavenly score, phenomenal voice acting and casting, and writing, Utawarerumono is, from start to finish, an unforgettable ride.Not a single moment is wasted, and for the first time in my life, I wish there was. I could go on another 300 hours of nothing but seeing them interact and bounce off each other like in the slice-of-life parts of the story. I hate not being able to express how good of a series Utawarerumono is, but perhaps I don't even need to, because it speaks for itself in so many ways.I will deeply miss all the characters and the unique, colorful world of Utawarerumono, but I will never forget it and everything it has to offer.

I give the game a 12 out of 10 it was amazing to the very end prepare yourself for zombification.

_childDocuments_.review: Utawarerumono. It is one of the famous Japanese franchise series developed by Aquaplus(Leaf). This series features the outstanding visual novel and SRPG experience with the focus on interesting story, nice anime artworks, and impressive soundtracks. Utawarerumono originated on PC back in 2002. Since then, it has led to a variety of projects, including animation series. According to the official announcement, the series has sold hundreds of thousands of copies in Japan. This time DMM GAMES and ShiraVN played a great role in bringing Utawarerumono series to Steam globally.The second episode(Mask of Deception) is close to the prologue and depicting daily life in general, this third episode(Mask of Truth) focus on the main story parts. This game summarizes both episodes 1(Prelude to the Fallen) and 2(Mask of Deception). So it's good to enjoy everything of Utawarerumono series as much as possible, but if you can't afford it, it might be a good idea to choose Mask of Truth first. The story unfold is quite similar to the first episode. Each one has a different reason, but the protagonists face inevitable wars, struggling to protect their loved ones, and building up the nation. Play time is over 50 hours and provides intense and deep game experience.Gameplay is pretty good. There is quite a lot to enjoy. More game systems have been added than the second volume. For example, there're splendid new co-op final finisher moves. And in the exercise mode, you can randomly divide your units and enjoy mock battle with each other. Scenario battles are quite exciting, not too difficult or too easy. In other words, the game balance is fine. The fan-service contents we expect are well prepared. Such events are quite hot, sometimes funny and heartwarming. Animation and character voices have the highest quality. And you'll fall into the soundtrack of this game. It's quite impressive. As well as, there are extra contents that you can enjoy the whole Utawarerumono series. This shows that the developers put a lot of effort into the game itself.Translation and localization are particularly important in the story-driven games. In that sense, the global Steam version of this Utawarerumono series is fine. The gameplay time for the two episodes of the trilogy will be at least 80 hours. The translation may be somewhat straightforward, but it has given the impression that the most context is smoothly presented. Fortunately, translation doesn't ruin the quality of this great game. The time you spend in this game will be well worth it.Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth. This is a pretty good anime game. Of course, it's a game that anyone can enjoy, but it's probably not for everyone. The preference for the anime game such as this text adventure can vary from user to user, even if it has some RPG elements. As you may know, Utawarerumono Mask series released as the PlayStation version first. This PC Edition is a port from the PlayStation version. So the exposure level for the hot events may be soft. Nevertheless, the game is exciting from the start to the end. Therefore, if you've been interested in this kind of game, don't hesitate. This will definitely be a game for you. Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: DISCLAIMER: If you haven't played Prelude to the Fallen and especially Mask of Deception, I would advise you not read anything about this game yet. AT ALL. Except for this review, it's spoiler free :)The final game of the Utawarerumono trilogy, there is a lot of payoff here to the setup of the second game and the first game's plot. The story is magnificent and very emotional, the characters shine and have surprising depth, and an amazing conclusion for the well crafted world's story awaits. If you haven't played the first and second games, Prelude to the Fallen and Mask of Deception, you really should play those before this one for its plot to be understood.(I'll try and write a review for Prelude to the Fallen once I get it on Steam, too...)The gameplay is a lot stronger than in Mask of Deception, and is pretty good with a lot of nuance and fun mechanics to it, as well as generally good map design. The units are all pretty fun to use, and the balancing is solid as well.The tropes and fanservice of the story are also cut down as the plot heads toward its conclusion, and the flaws of the story are rather minimal, though I won't pretend some don't exist at all. Regardless, it's one of the greatest stories I have ever read, is very thought provoking, and consistently is amazing throughout its length with a conclusion that lives rent free in my head. The story balances calmer scenes and more intense ones very well, and is incredibly engaging, entertaining, and emotionally charged. Play the trilogy, especially for this. It's so incredibly good.---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------If you have questions, consider joining the Discord through the subreddit :)

_childDocuments_.review: Among fans of VNs in the West, the Utawarerumono series has taken on almost a mythical status over the year. As a result, I was very excited when the games got ported to PC. However, after playing what is essentially an $80 game, I'm left feeling very conflicted. I enjoyed the game at certain points, but it also frustrates me greatly. I just felt like maybe I'm getting too old for these anime storylines. What bothers me the most is the game’s overuse of what I’d like to describe as masochistic writing. After every battle that you won, it’s always either “Haha you fall into my trap” or “Haha I didn’t even use half my strength” or “Haha I’ll just walk right out of here like nothing happens even though you just finish me off with that awesome 1k Co-Op final”. Seriously, the gameplay eventually becomes nothing more than side distractions and has no bearing on the story. The game is obsessed with putting the MCs in these scenarios in which they are utterly helpless and overwhelmed. Scenes in which a friendly character is mentally and/or physically tortured would go on and on and on even after the point is made. About half of the game’s scenes consists of some random dude or dudette talking down on the MCs. The MCs never had any decent riposte to these verbal assaults. Usually, the MCs would start crying or are stunned into submission.The gameplay does improve compared to Mask of Deception. Damage is scaled much better now so strategic options actually matter. There are also more variety of maps and objectives. Some battles last a little too long though, but overall I had good experience with the gameplay.If you like SRPG and VN, I still think you should give this series a shot. I just think the series are too expensive and are too long for the amount of enjoyment I got from them.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a great time with this game despite it being the first one in the series I've played. I had knowledge of the previous games through their respective anime and I'm still floored by how much I loved this game without playing the first two. If you're interested in this game, you'll only need to play Mask of Deception to understand the majority of this one as MoD and MoT are one story, while the original is a bit disconnected.GAMEPLAYIf you're interested in playing Utawarerumono: MoT for its combat rather than its story, I suggest you look for another game. However, MoT's gameplay is competent and makes for a break between long reading sessions, although there might be a few too many battles at the end stacked back to back.The game is not difficult by any means as the story is the main focus but from what I've played of Hard Mode, there is a noticeable difficulty jump.I would like to go more in depth on the gameplay but my knowledge on srpgs is lacking but I will say that it was enjoyable, moreso at the end when everyone felt much more powerful. SOUNDTRACKWowzas. I loved the soundtrack for this game. I have the last song from the epilogue playing as I write this review. Many of the songs in this game have a very distinct flute sound and are quite memorable. Unlike other games this long, I didn’t get tired of the soundtrack at all.The music beautifully compliments the scenes with the voiced songs usually emphasizing important moments in the story. The music also switches between comedic and light to serious and emotional perfectly.I’m super glad that there’s a music viewer in the main menu or I’d have a hard time finding these songs. STORY & CHARACTERSThe story is a direct continuation from MoD and tied to the original Utawarerumono. The following will contain spoilers for the first 1-2 hours of the game, though there’s nothing to fear if you’ve already played MoD as the first 2 hours are essentially recap.Following Oshtor’s death in MoD Haku has taken up his friend’s name and is now leading the effort to restore Anju to the throne. Haku and Nekone, Oshtor’s younger sister and the only one who knows Haku’s identity, must now try and keep the image of Oshtor alive as his name is the only one that commands enough respect to see the war through.What follows is some of the most gripping storytelling and characterization I’ve seen in any game. Everyone realizes just how much Haku meant to them and the weight on Haku and Nekone’s shoulders as they continue to lie despite their friends’ sorrows in order to honor Oshtor and bring peace back to Yamato is absolutely heart rending. I’ve lost so much sleep binging this game and can’t help but relentlessly search for more news on possible new games.The pacing is great, though I think the lead up to the ending is a bit weaker than other parts, and the balance between light and heavy scenes is near perfect. If I could erase my memory and play the game for another 50+ hours I would. I didn’t dare think that any scenes would match the early Haku and Nekone scenes but Haku and Kuon scenes come around to prove me wrong.OVERALLIt is only after I finish this game that I realize how much of a fool I am for thinking the anime was "good enough" and I just had to go and buy the prequel. I don't know how my experience would have been if I had played MoD first but hopefully it can help me move past the void this game left in my life.10/10It’s obviously not perfect as the battles dragged sometimes and there was no autosave feature, which would have been wonderful as I screwed up and loaded a save instead of overwriting a save meaning I had to replay an hour of the game. However, there are few stories that manage to draw me in as deep as this one did and my enjoyment of this experience is worthy of a 10.Here's to hoping for more utawarerumono games in the future (Not mobile ones though >:( ).

_childDocuments_.review: A satisfying conclusion to the trilogy, tying up all plot points and conflicts presented in the previous two games. There is just something distinctly emotional about seeing all these characters, this world, this story that I've spent the over a hundred hours becoming invested in all come to a head. Maybe this will truly be the end of the series, or maybe it will not be. I really hope it isn't. I've truly grown attached to this universe, and it wouldn't be so bad to see more of it in the future. If you are interested in epic fantasy storylines with lots of characters and worldbuilding that you can become invested in, then by all means, pick up the utawarerumono series. Now that i've praised the game, I need to point out its flaws. Would I consider Mask of Truth to be the Muv-Luv Alternative of Utawarerumono? Not really. Muv-Luv Alternative went all the way with its story, pulling absolutely no punches and subverting your expectations at every turn. Mask of Truth, however, sometimes fell back on predictable tropes and tedious narrative padding. I was baffled as to why the story kept continuing at certain points. There were definitely much quicker ways to resolve some conflicts presented in the game than what the game actually did. The story didn't HAVE to end the way it did and it felt like the writers weren't organically guiding the story to its conclusion. Rather, they were forcing the story down a certain ending that they wanted, and as a result, some plot developments felt torturously prolonged to reach this ending. From a narrative standpoint, was it a satisfying ending? Kinda. Was it really predictable though? Yes. In addition, I fully suspect that some of this narrative padding was done to fit more gameplay into the plot somehow. The last few fights of the game felt like a token "insert final boss fight here" moment for gameplay purposes. Ideally, gameplay and story should compliment each other, like two sides of the same coin. The gameplay should help immerse players in the story, and bring an interactive storytelling element to the experience. At the beginning of Mask of Truth, the gameplay was succeeding in that regard. I felt more and more involved in the story with each gameplay segment. However, towards the end, the gameplay dragged me away from the story. I just wanted to get it over with. It had overstayed its welcome; it had padded out the story to accommodate itself. It's not that it wasn't fun anymore; it just wasn't needed anymore. But even despite these faults, this game is still one of those games that makes me glad I read visual novels in the first place. It will always have a special place in my heart. Buy it and read it.

_childDocuments_.review: Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth is the deeply satisfying conclusion to an epic trilogy. It nicely ties up major plot points set up at the end of the previous game, Mask of Deception, while delivering no shortage of emotional high moments. The game's combat (i.e. the actual gameplay part), which takes up between a fifth to a quarter of the overall play time, is satisfactory. Combat mechanics are relatively simple like in the previous two games and there isn't a whole lot of strategic depth for fans of tactical RPGs to sink their teeth into. Nonetheless, there were enough meaningful decisions to keep me engaged during fights.As has always been the case with the series, the characters are its strongest point - while Mask of Deception spent most of its run introducing the cast and building up the dynamic between them, we now witness their growth as they persevere through loss and adversity. Mask of Truth is the definitive payoff in a trilogy that I strongly recommend to visual novel fans and newcomers alike.

_childDocuments_.review: Mask of Truth has a hell of a job to do. Not only has it got to find a way to wrap up the previous title, Mask of Deception, but also tie up all the once resolved threads of the original Utawarerumono that have been significantly loosened. It’s the kind of ambition we’ve seen crash and burn numerous times across all media; trying to find a satisfying conclusion to hours and hours of patient build. Mask of Deception wasn’t shy about how it was more or less one big lesson in world building done right in order for Truth to drive things home. It does that. It does that in spades.I’m talking around the point a little because the big twist ending of Deception shakes all the monkeys out of the tree, then asks Truth to put them back. Except now the tree has gone. And all the monkeys are on fire. I know I should absolutely discuss that, except I can’t without wading full stride into deep spoiler territory. So I’m going to pick at this carefully and point out that interested players should categorically play at least the previous game before attempting this one.Yamato, then, is having its share of problems. Once a ridiculously prosperous country that knew few hardships, it’s now been thrust into the slow rumblings of a civil war. There’s no one big reason for all this; for the most part, the people on both sides are just trying to do what they think is right. But you’re probably the rightest! Forced outside the capital into a remote corner of the country, the plot mostly follows Imperial Guardsman, Oshtor, as he and the remainder of the cast from the previous game lick their wounds and start planning a way to take their country back. Only sometimes, it’s more about dethroned princess, Anju, who needs to come to very quick terms with the loss of her entire family and the absolution of her rule. There’s an impostor on her throne, but she needs to accept that if she wages war to reclaim her birthright, a lot of innocent people are going to suffer. A lot of people are going to die. It’s a lot to take on; she might have been bred specifically to rule, but she’s still just an uncertain, mourning child underneath it all.Sometimes it’s not about either of them. Sometimes, it’s not even about Yamato, but harkens back to the location of the original game, Tuskar. Kuon took a leading role in Deception, but its heavy-hitting conclusion perhaps hit her the hardest and she’s returned to the country of her birth. Here, she needs to reassess the things that really matter to her; the loyalty she feels towards her friends and the plight visited upon the country she came to love. But she also has obligations to Tuskar; family she’s neglected in her travels. Whatever she does and wherever she goes, she’s letting someone she cares about down, forcing further hurt upon people already suffering.Everyone in Mask of Truth is suffering. Everyone has lost something once thought irreplaceable, that I’m really trying very hard not to address directly. It features a cast lifted from a previous game that you rarely saw in low spirits, and that so many of them are now a little bit broken in their own unique ways hurts. Truth starts with a cast trying to pick up the pieces, with people trying desperately to lift the more fragile of their friends with vacant smiles and empty platitudes. They poke at the embers of their world, unable to avoid the occasional wallow in self-pity or grief or guilt. And then they pick each other up. And then they chose not to accept the hand they’ve been dealt. And then they fight back.

_childDocuments_.review: Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth is the sequel of Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception, together they have a total of 90-100 hours of gameplay. The difference between the first and the second is that the first was more slice of life like, Mask of Truth is a rollercoaster of emotions between a group of friends, having to keep a painful secret for the greater good, not being able to tell the one you love and admire about it, fighting against overpowered evil all the time and making huge sacrifices. Utawarerumono beat my score for the most played visual novel 3 times, became my favorite VN, one of my favorite animes (if i can include the VN as an anime, the anime adaptation surely skipped a LOT of things for the lack of time in just 26 episodes) and it shall stay between my favorites, especially Mask of Truth!I have been playing for hours in a row with small and few breaks, and with that i mean 8-12 hours. The voice acting is very good and my favorite part in both games is that if the like after a voiced line is a thought or a break and has no voice, the last one keeps playing until another one starts, it brings that atmosphere! It is indeed a very small thing, but it brings me a lot of joy.This one also has some extra menus between chapters where you can train your characters, do challenges, replay old fights and allocate BP, which is a nice addition, i would feel the lack of it if i play the first one again. MoT also has a lot more gameplay, fights are quite expected for the part with wars against rebels, monsters, brainwashed people and even gods, stuff that happened in Mask of Deception too, but A LOT less. It is the reason to try New Game+, you can ignore the story if you want and keep on playing the game, everyone will be so much weaker the second time as you keep everything on your characters, but if you decide to train between them it will be a everlasting battle. The quality of this game is memorable, the soundtrack (over 90 tracks!!!), the artwork of the characters, even the animations look pretty good for their budget, but most importantly the writing, the writing is amazing. It is that big heavy book or set of books that you don't expect finishing but somehow you start the first one and read nonstop until you finish them, can't wait to know more while reading and sad when finishing it, the sadness coming from not having more to consume.The protagonist never thought highly of himself, never thought he valued anything and that people cared enough about him until he had to cover someone else's death and kill his old self. Being dead, playing someone else's role and seeing his friends leave heartbroken of his death without him being able to shout their name and bring them back. We all have someone, someone has us, we are never truly alone, us leaving forever would only cause pain, for this we must live and smile. 10/10, a moonlight flower <3If you want more detailed reviews on awesome games consider following , our curator page.

_childDocuments_.review: There's not a whole lot to say. If you're about to play this game, you have most likely played the previous half, Mask of Deception, and the first game, Prelude to the Fallen (if you haven't, go play them and don't look at anything from this one if you don't want to get spoiled). So you know what to expect.This is where all the setup from Mask of Deception (and partly from Prelude to the Fallen) leads to. For me personally, this is one of the most epic, pure hype stories I've ever experienced to this day. You know how some of your favorite stories have that one or two grand moments where everything about the story just clicks together for you, usually while an insert song or anime opening is playing in the background. These are the moments that you'll remember for a long time, if not for the rest of your life, and which cement a story as one of your favorites. On a rare occasion, these might even be moments that make you sob.Well for me personally, Mask of Truth doesn't have one or two of these, but at the moment I'm counting 9 of them in total. And even though I'm not one to often cry even once while watching/reading stories, this game made me shed tears 3 times in the span of one week. After finishing, I'm completely emotionally exhausted from this ordeal.But to actually provide some information other than my personal, overwhelmingly positive impressions: The combat is pretty much the same as the previous entry, but this time the improved mechanics actually matter a lot more. The main story is capable of throwing some actually pretty difficult boss fights at you every once in a while in order to force you to better utilize some of the now more varied character kits.The story is on another level. If I were to mention at least something negative, it would be that most of what I said applies to only the first 75 %  and the last 5-10 % of the plot. At a certain point, one of the main conflicts and antagonists gets resolved. After which a new, shorter arc begins. This arc is necessary, sure, as it concerns some of the global/large scale loose ends and conflics that had to be left for the end of the story. But this along with the way it is executed just felt to me like such a vibe-killer compared to the emotional rollercoaster that is the main chunk of the game, especially with how meh and frustrating the "new" antagonist felt. Thankfully after you rush through it, the game ends on a high note as the ending puts you back on the hype train and delivers some of the most cathartic moments of the entire series (and for me personally, some of the most cathartic moments of storytelling I've seen in my life so far).

_childDocuments_.review: A good conclusion to the Utawarerumono trilogy (yes, including prelude to the fallen). While Mask of Deception was mostly lighthearted, Mask of Truth has a serious tone where there is a nearly constant threat to our MC's, but it doesn't lose the banter and slice of life moments you like (or dislike idunno) completely. This franchise pulls it off to have some lighthearted slice of life while still having an actual deep plot at the same time.Mask of Deception's overall plot seems to truly advance in the latter half, while Mask of Truth's plot advances steadily throughout the whole game. Utawarerumono's cast has some of the usual trope characters, but plenty of them are likeable and well built. The worldbuilding is great, the storytelling is great and the music + high quality 2D visuals do a great job to pull you into this fantasy world. Overall i would say Utawarerumono has one of the better stories in its genre. It additionally gets some personal bonuspoints for providing some really good emotional/impactful moments .The battle system is the same as its predecessor: fairly standard tactical RPG combat. I didn't really feel joy in challenging myself with it TBH. Also had a few occassions where the rapid forward button in combat made my game crash... losing 30+ minutes of battle time in the progress...I WILL give kudos to the final boss battleThe end itself is.. satisfying, but bittersweet. It also is an end that once again confirms that you should not skip the prequel (prelude to the fallen) to Haku's and Kuon's story. . Once again i recommend the whole Utawarerumono trilogy to anyone who wants to try out/likes:The final score will remain a 8.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: At first, I have to remind you that this game is a continuation of Utawarerumono Mask of Deception and the last part of Utawarerumono Trilogy.The game has a great story with many twists. The soundtrack is awesome especially because of Suara, who is singing opening, endings and some in-game songs. Backgrounds are beautiful and have a lot of details. The srpg part is nice but is really easy so if you are looking for a challenge then you can forget it. But the biggest advantage of Utawarerumono is world-building and character development. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR: If you liked the first game, you'll almost certainly love this one and if you enjoyed the second game, this brings the overall story to a close in a very satisfying way. While the game establishes the plot enough that you can play this as a standalone, I highly recommend you play the previous two games first.Long Version: Thrust into the roll you accepted during the finale of the second game, Haku must now lead his friends and the allies found in a small border nation, to somehow reclaim the enormous kingdom they once knew from the powers that usurped it. While the answers as to who and why of the previous game's betrayal are not fully unearthed until late game, there is plenty to keep the group occupied in the meantime. The balance between story and combat elements is much better in Mask of Truth than it was in Mask of Deception (the second game), and the complexity of the combat is back to Prelude to the Fallen (the first game) levels. (Though as a tiny side note, breaking objects never matters in this game). In a lot of ways, it does the good trilogy thing of incorporating the best bits from all the previous games and implementing them properly.The anime-ness of the story continues, again, for good or for bad. The plot is actually really interesting though. The ending is largely satisfying despite going against a few of my personal preferences. (You will have to watch through the credits, broken up into... I wanna say three sections? Just wait until you actually get to the FIN screen.) Saying much else about the game treads into spoiler territory. Really though, if you've played the first two games, you'll want to play this one. If you haven't, stop now and go play them instead. If you enjoy game one you'll like this one almost guaranteed.

_childDocuments_.review: Really great game in terms of everything (story, world, characters, music, artwork are brilliant) except for one flaw: fights. They are very hard and tedious in Mask of Truth comparing to previous two games even on normal, right after stage 8. Stage 9 keeps you seriously underleveled where you can deal 20-25 damage max per turn to boss, but this boss heals by 100+ almost every turn and damages your tanks with high def with around 80+ dmg, drying out your healers. I had no issues with previous two games on PS Vita, but to complete this game I had to use cheats for x8 experience for my units: I don't want to waste my time on exp grind. There are at least 6-8 stages with very high challenge which catches you completely off guard: you don't expect such brutailty in visual novel with some tactic combat as side-dish.

I hated him in MoD. What a 180 turn, or almost, to the character. He's so much more likable in this one that . While that didn't happen, what I got, pleased me well enough.+The series has this great feeling of "hope". Games like Danganronpa spam about "hope", but feel artificial, while Utawarerumono games have, what I would call, "hope that will likely carry into reality". This "hope" is so well displayed in MoT.+The topic of "hope" also applies to "philosophy and humanity" displayed and discussed in the game. This game could be a bit of an eye-opener for some.+I waited till this moment to mention this about the whole series: Death is often misused in fiction, especially in RPGs. In this series, death is used so well. Makes you cry, you know...+I love how (almost) every character, good or evil, developed throughout the story. I still need more Kuon and Atuy in my life. Atuy probably had the funniest lines here, and I freaking love how honest she was about . The twins are still horny as hell and introducing  to the cast was...very boobyful. Suara's singing makes me emotional in the right way.+This series made me cry again many times.  was so well done I couldn't help but feel deep sadness for him. _childDocuments_.review: This is the first game of a trilogy of visual novel strategy RPG hybrids. They tell a continuous, cumulative story.They play order is:Prelude to the fallenMask of deceptionMask of truthYou can skip free to prelude to the fallen to start with mask of deception, because that game changes the cast and takes place many years later, giving it some distance from the original that allows newcomers to enjoy it while still leaving room for callbacks for people that played the first one. All of the necessary story information presented within the first game is explained in the second and third game. However, you couldn’t skip mask of deception and go straight to mask of truth, because the two games take place one right after the other as a part one and part two scenario to the same story.

_childDocuments_.review: A minor not recomend. For a few specific types that really just like long slow stories, want one game to play for weeks or months depending on how much time they have to commit to them, and are ok with some jank and problems in a story and setting, then it's decent. But it's just... really slow, and so often I'm wanting it to be over or move along faster, and the plot itself has more holes than a colander. They can get away with some of that jank and BS, but they push a LOT at the player as parts of the main story and key elements and problems the player/story is dealing with. So many cases of why is the character so bloody incompetent? Especially when the repeat the same obvious mistake four or five or six times in a row in the story... like... really? It was an obvious mistake before you even did it, but you can't learn at all?Oh well, just lots of issues that pulled me out from getting to invested in the story. The gameplay is ok... not great, kinda slow, but itself often clashes with the story itself in how they present things, even more than the first or second game.  Overall, It's an ok story and I do kind of like some of the characters, but it's just not up there with the first game, so I can't feel like saying yes, buy this, spend tons of time on this one story, it's worth it... when there are plenty of other stories that are faster, better, or even both of those and just free. A few people and types will still enjoy it though, and it's not terrible or that bad, just mediocre... and not quite worth the time investment in my opinion, or the cost once that also gets factored in for most people.I liked the first one, if you are ok with slower paced games with good character development, I'll recommend it. If you just like it, probably stick with only it, if you absolutely love it, then I guess get 2 and 3.2 was frankly just bad on the gameplay and very meh with some bad on the story, though good on some characters, 3 (this one) noticabely improved the gameplay by moving back towards the first games style for stuff, with a few tweaks of it's own to help here or there, but still nothing to write home about. The story is for the first half overall much better than the second, and compares to the first one in some parts, though doesn't have the nice feel I liked from that first one, second half though... gets more mixed, both more interesting and posotive in some points, but also more frusterating as they start seeing how many holes they can punch into the story in order to try and wrap up some ideas they had. I mean.. an enemy unit, that has no access to teleportation or any special logistics, that frankly would probably have trouble even getting out of their starting location... are supposed to somehow know exactly where the players are whey they shouldn't, move half way across the entire country, do a questionable attack, and then return... all in just a few hours. That trip should take days if not more even in the best of conditions, but no, just let it happen in a few hours. Let them know where they are because plot demands they show up to do X thing to the players group... Ya, logic just goes out the window at several points here, but that was one of the worst ones....So in the end, all are slow games, but the first one I enjoyed and felt mostly satisfied by... the second one was mostly just annoying and problematic with the key upside of some characters, and the third one here is too long and drawn out at first, and then rushes to finish up and wow you with a bunch of major story turns and events at the end... but doesn't know how to make them actually all work together so... it's all really forced and kind of pulls you out of it if you tried to get invested in the story and characters actions and stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: "None of your decisions actually matter, now slug it out against these BBEGs for the sake of vague notions."Wow. So original. The journey was fun but the last 18 hours of play were just railroaded padding to mandatory extend (finish?) the game out, and I hate that. If Mask of Deception felt like it ended too soon, then Mask of Truth felt like it just dragged on for eternity towards a foregone conclusion. I get the impression that the director wanted to have a 4th game covering the last 1/4th of this game, but he knew that kind of episodic format wouldn't be acceptable. The journey was fun, it's more Utawarerumono good stuff and chances are you've played 1 and 2 (if not the game assumes you haven't with hours of review of 2's content in the opening), but the ending was Mass Effect 3-tier bitter. If you're reading this planning to purchase the three as a set, just play the first game and consider it ogre for your own sake and time.So without spoiling the plot (since the ending involves spoiling about the last 1/4th of gameplay), the last segment of the game was basically slugfest after slugfest after slugfest in traditional attritional JRPG style. Utawarerumono is known for having villains that act "real" but the last like four fights are just BBEGs as part of what feels like was supposed to be its own game or bonus post-game content, but got tacked on to the end of Mask of Truth because the budget ran out, so you're sitting there going "is THIS the final battle? Is THIS ONE the final battle?" instead of being invested in each fight. The third game features the tragic loss component of the first game, except instead of losing anything you actually care for you are just shown mass suffering of, well, masses, because the BBEGs have to be established as the BBEGs. Going into a little more detail...The last 18 hours of gameplay could easily have been condensed into 3-4. The director opted to have every single character have a quip for every single scene instead of one or two characters commenting on a situation for effect which lead 30 second scenes to be 5 minute scenes instead. If there was something of substance being added that would be fine, but each character's interaction with the scene was equivalent to a reaction video (not adding anything to the conversation) which gets old when there's 10+ characters. You can predict the series of events that will follow pretty much word-for-word from the 12 hour to ending mark onwards. The game gives you a sense of finality on four different occasions and then just proceeds to keep lurching along like "oh yeah nah that wasn't the ending that was just closure" despite major events taking place. That wouldn't be a big deal if the 2nd game and majority of the third game hadn't been slow-going from one event to the next making the sudden acceleration of plot incredibly jarring.The last two boss fights are completely scripted based on your level so that they will drag on and on and on some more, but you can see where the battles are going from a mile away; they're just long for the sake of being long attritional battles (in the second to last boss fight for instance, you're fighting a completely pointless battle against unkillable enemies while only the MC is allowed to fight the BBEG in a way that is 90% scripted and 10% soft lock probability that could force you to have to restart the entire nearly 1 hour fight). Then the game just straight-up copies the first game's ending which is a spit in the face of the first game which had proper pacing and none of this padding for the sake of padding. Then during the epilogue (the only redeemable part of that last portion of the game) goes on and on and on covering what happened to each minor character in the second game, yet despite spending the last 4 hours nostalgiablasting you into oblivion, they can't even wrap up the loose ends from the first game that would have been seen in the third game.The journey was fun, but the ending left an incredibly bitter taste in my mouth. Not bittersweet, just bitter. It was one of those "everything you did for two games doesn't matter" style deus ex Shakespearian endings and I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hate those. The plot holes, contrivances, and arsepulls at the end were just too much.

_childDocuments_.review: I very rarely write reviews. This has to take the cake as my favorite story of all time, and I love it so much that I had to write about it lol. I love every bit of the aesthetic that the game gives, and playing Prelude and Deception before it, this game is the perfect finish to a beautiful trilogy. If you're a fan of anything of deep lore, this game is for you. There is many pieces to a puzzle to put together throughout. Some will dislike the filler that the story provides in between the progression of the story, and that is understandable. At the least, this gives you a chance to understand the characters and their motivations more there.The character design is one of my favorite things in this game, iconic designs that you really see anywhere else, and that flair is only one of the things that this amazing series offers. Genuinely funny moments, cute characters, a story with stakes, and easily pulls you in from Prelude all the way to here, your final point. Beautiful music that resonates the emotion that the game wants you to feel, and unreal art.The game play is great as well throughout the series, testing your brain on harder difficulty. Leveling up the characters feel fulfilling, and it's hard to get tired of it at any point. Every battle and map feels fresh, and the hype around almost every fight is there.I mean it when I say that I recommend this to everyone who likes a good story. I think this series deserves much more recognition in the West, and it's a gem in the sand that if you uncover and face for yourself, you'll like a lot more than you think in most cases.

_childDocuments_.review: Nearly three years after it was first released in the west on PS4 and Vita, us PC players finally get the chance to play Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception and Mask of Truth, the second and third games in the Utawarerumono series. It's about time honestly, as these are some games I have been wanting to play since I first watched the anime adaptation years ago.So for those unfamiliar with it, Utawarerumono is a series of visual novels with tactical RPG elements. The gameplay consists of the player going from reading various story events and dialogue to tactical, turn-based battles on a grid. As with most VNs that have gameplay elements, the focus is not on the gameplay, but rather on the story. However, with Mask of Deception and Mask of Truth, the gameplay is actually pretty good and doesn't feel like it was just tacked onto the experience. It may be no Disgaea, but it has a decent amount of depth to it at least, much more so than I often see with such VN hybrids. The game also provides a couple difficulty options to accommodate for both those that just want to experience the story and those that want more challenging gameplay. On normal difficulty, the battles are pretty much a breeze, but on hard difficulty, not so much.As for the actual story, well, that's something that Mask of Deception and Mask of Truth do really well. Although Mask of Deception is technically the second game in the series, it is set up in such a way as to make it easy for newcomers to enjoy. I personally have never played the first game (which is simply titled "Utawarerumono" and does not have an official English release yet) and had no problems getting into Mask of Deception. The same cannot be said for Mask of Truth though, which absolutely requires that you play Mask of Deception first, lest you be really confused as to what's going on. For those that still want to experience the first game in some form, the 2006 anime is generally considered a good adaptation. I watched it years ago and, while I may not remember much of it, I liked it enough to want to get into the games.Once you actually get into the story, you'll be met with some well-written characters, a vibrant fantasy setting that's big on world-building, and some pretty good overall pacing. The games provide a good mix of serious storytelling and more character-oriented slice of life scenes as well. In fact, I like to think of the two games as brothers. Mask of Deception is the younger brother, who is rather innocent and just wants to have fun in this fantasy world with all of its neat characters. Mask of Truth, on the other hand, is the older brother who has lost his innocence and has experienced the hardships of life. While Mask of Deception does have its serious moments, Mask of Truth is when the real story story kicks in, when everything starts coming together. It's quite the ride and there's a good reason why Mask of Truth is sitting at the #12 spot on VNDB's list of highest-rated visual novels.The art and music, as with the story, are also pretty good in both games. I ran the game at 1440p and, while that is an upscale from 720p, the art looked fine and I didn't notice any blatantly blurry assets or backgrounds. It was definitely some good news, as I'm a big fan of the fantasy aesthetic that the games go for. The music also perfectly matches this aesthetic, with a great blend of energetic battle themes and more laid-back, traditional tracks for the game's dialogue scenes. As someone that has already been listening to these soundtracks for years, it was cool to finally hear this music in-game.And of course, seeing as how these two games have never been released on PC, I should mention the quality of their port. To sum it up, it's pretty good as far as VN ports go. There's all the standard settings one would expect in a VN release, including text speed, auto-mode speed, skip options, and a voice cutoff toggle. However, both games go one step further with fullscreen, borderless, and window options, multiple resolution support, completely rebindable keyboard controls, protagonist voice toggling, and even customizable button prompts dependent on what type of controller you're using. Some of these may sound pretty standard, but with visual novels, sometimes they are hard to come by, so it's nice to see them included here.And before I wrap up this review, I should bring up the censorship question. Both games were released as 15+ titles in Japan, so there's no H-scenes like in the original 2002 PC game. This version of Mask of Truth is the exact same as the Japanese version, but this version of Mask of Deception has one CG that has been changed from the Japanese release. I'll go ahead and throw that CG up on-screen so you can see what was changed. It's a very minor change, but I know that a lot of VN fans are passionate about the subject, so it needs to be noted regardless.Overall though, both Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception and Mask of Truth are solid games all things considered. Great art, great music, gameplay that actually doesn't feel like a distraction from the main story, and a story that's both unique and well-written. The two games have a lot going for them and the fact that they're actually decent PC ports is also a nice bonus. It's about time we got them on PC and now it's just a wait to complete the trilogy with the release of Prelude to the Fallen, a remaster of the first game that is also slated to release on PC.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: WARNING: This is game 3 of a series. Play "Prelude to the Fallen" then "Mask of Deception" first.Disclaimer:My 55 hours of playtime represents one complete play through on Normal difficulty, Played entirely on Steam deck.Short Review:This game is the perfect finish to the series, they really went all out.The only reason you should be here is if you completed the other two games in the series.If you did then buy this one as soon as you are able.Taken as a whole: the entire series is a incomparable masterpiece. Go in as blind as you can, I wont spoil anything but don't even read any more of this review.More details, no spoilers:Once again the pacing is just relentless, playing for just an hour or two a night I was always left with some new development or twist or revelation. There's so many plot points that get woven in and resolved properly that the game goes on for like another 10+ hours after any other game would have wrapped up. There's even a whole load of post credits scenes with some major developments.It never felt rushed despite this. Everything is given its proper amount of time.I will say this game on Normal difficulty is the hardest yet. I never had to grind once but there were some crazy difficulty spikes. Sometimes certain characters were only doing like 1-3 damage and I don't fully understand why.All I'm going to say is save before every fight so you can change your roster if needed, use your brain and look at the win/defeat conditions as well as the type advantages.Welp, Gonna be honest here I enjoyed this series immensely. Probably the best JRPG series I have played in 30+ years of gaming.If this was made with Final Fantasy production values it would likely never be surpassed.I am so glad I got to play it and also really sad that its over. I doubt I will find a game that is anywhere as fun and well written as this for a while but, I haven't played Monochrome Mobius yet so lets see...

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the conclusion of the Utawarerumono series, and what a conclusion it was! I had high hopes for it after the dramatic ending of Mask of Deception and it did not disappoint one bit.This is a heroic tale of a man carrying on the will of his late friend, no matter what sacrifice he must do in order to protect those that were important to both his friend and to himself. The character development is one of the strongest point of this game. Watching the characters grow together through the many hardships that they face is very heartwarming. The pacing is generally very good. It does slow down a little near the end, but it picks up the pace again right in time for the grand finale. Giving a good ending to a long series is always tough, but in my opinion I would say that this game nails it. It's an epic story from beginning to end, and I'm happy to have read it all the way through.The gameplay is for sure at it's peak in this game. For the most part the mechanics are identical to Mask of Deception, so the transition from that game to this one is pretty smooth (whereas there is a bit of a learning curve when you move on from Prelude to the Fallen to MoD as there are substantial differences). However, it brings back the display for battle preparations that was used in PttF and adds some improvements, which is great because that one felt better than the battle preparations menu from MoD. Also, co-op attacks are back together with co-op Final Strikes.Difficulty is at its highest in this game as well. While a good number of the story maps aren't too hard, there are at least a couple that are actually rather challenging. The Dream Arena post-game maps though is definitely where the difficulty goes off the charts. The early ones aren't too bad, but most of them are a good challenge and the toughest ones I can only describe as being brutally hard. These maps will test your game knowledge to their limits. While they can all be beaten without grinding, you might have to repeat some stages to farm BP and items if you ever get stuck. I thoroughly enjoyed this game, both as a VN and as an SRPG. I think this game is one that everyone should play, and even though I only recently finished playing it I can say that it's for sure one of my favorite games of all time.

They're not.Oh yeah!To think Moznu at the end... Whooops, no spoiler in my review. It's nothing big at all, I mean they are big, it really caught me off-guard. _childDocuments_.review: What a fantastic end to the trilogy.Utawarerumono is what happens when you cross cat girls, Fire Emblem-like tactical gameplay with a visual novel that follows a Nakige formula reminiscent of Key (slice-of-life build up, followed up by the emotional and climatic payoff), only that the setting is not the contemporary city setting, but an Oriental one in the "ancient past". It shouldn't work on paper, but the writers clearly had a lot of heart and conviction put in to the story, enough for me to suspend my disbelief and fall hook, line and sinker and love th characters. Prelude was a nice prequel set-up to the world and the seeds of conflict that would rear its head in the subsequent duology. Deception was that nonsensical and utterly hilarious slice-of-life common route (admittedly, did get a bit wee too long with the Haku masochist hijinks) that got us enamored with the cast and cleverly foreshadowed all those hand-to-mouth moments in Truth. Truth laid it all bare; the world, the story, and raw feelings of Haku and co. And it hit it right off the park. I have to say, as much as I am not a fan of Harems, Haku is fantastic Harem protagonist and even just an all-around good guy in general. Like all parodoxical humans, he is flawed and genuine, lazy and reliable, dense and intuitive at the same time.We could with more of him in stories, and our world.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth

_childDocuments_.review: The moment I booted up Mask of Truth, I knew I was in for something special. It gave off a certain air or feeling that was very similar to when I first booted up Muv Luv Alternative for the first time as well, and boy howdy those feelings were not betrayed. What a beautiful, wildly fun, and heartbreaking journey this was. Many reviews I noticed echoed very similar sentiments to what I was wanting to toss into this review as well, so I'll just say that I 2nd a lot of the highlights of Truth  that other's point out. What I will toss into the thunderdome here is, while Mask of Truth continued that high bar already set for it's top tier VA work, amazing soundtrack (which they went above and beyond for the finale here), and stellar writing and world building, what surprised me the most was the creative liberties they took with the combat encounters. I won't spoil the goodies of course, but with the reintroduction of certain mechanics and setups for said combat encounters, the battles definitely  became just as much of a high point as the story itself for me. The ending as well, was just the perfect bow that tied together what was  a 150 hour journey from the start of Prelude, to the end of Truth here.The entire package of Mask of Truth reminded me a lot of Xenoblade Chornicles 3. It truly felt like this was the developers swan song, like this was the last game they were ever going to make. What an unforgettable journey this was. Thank you Aquaplus, for gifting to our big blue planet here this beautifully crafted epic that you'd be hard pressed to find elsewhere.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth

_childDocuments_.review: This game ended up being the perfect ending to a 140 hour trilogy. I was worried that its rating's wouldn't live up to the experience, but count me wrong! Mask of Truth combines all the knowledge you have from the first Utawarerumono game and Mask of Deception into a compelling, high stakes story with characters you love, who only get better as the game progresses. It has all the SoL from Mask of Deception and more; it has all the touching, endgame moments from the first game but better and further explained. I was a little confused at the end of the first game, and Mask of Truth sure did explain it well. Not to mention that this series has some of my favorite characters I've seen in fiction, and its protagonist easily ranks at the top of my list. With more amazing music from Aquaplus's sound team, and beautiful art that hits at all the right moments by Amazuyu Tatsuki and Misato Mitsumi and all the talented, hardworking graphicers at Aquaplus. While the bosses and events have never been a strong part of the series, the gameplay has improved and gotten more complex (in a good way) from Deception. Now that was have Uta 1 remake, the series has a slow incline in improving gameplay, which is exactly what you want from this trilogy. In any case, I could talk forever about it since there is so much to unpack, but I will say that this series surprised me in the best of ways, and shook my to my core, easily one of the most compelling games I have had the pleasure of playing. I hope that more of Leaf/Aquaplus games get released on steam, like an official White Album 2 (never happening) but we are getting Utawarerumono Zan and ToHeart Remake!!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Very satisfying end to the trilogy. It's not without issues but it really is a great game. The first half of the game with the party coming to terms with what happened during the ending of Mask of Deception had some really great writing and strong character moments. The characters really are where this series excels, with Haku and Kuon (can't forget Maroro too) becoming some of my favourite characters ever, their voice acting being especially great too. Unfortunately the second half kinda forgets most of the party exists and a few of them barely get any screen time.There are a few weak arcs throughout though which really did bring down the enjoyment and the pacing. And there were quite a few moments that seemed like they'd be a big deal but nothing really came of them. Like when I also found the main villain to be pretty weak, with his stupid ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ followers. Pieces of ♥♥♥♥. But the final boss after his ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ was so hype that I stopped caring. Easily one of my favourite final boss fights ever, it was so damn good. And the ending itself was really satisfying, though I wish they expanded on it more by seeing more people's reactions to things.Can't forget the great music too, consistently good through the entire trilogy. There's a lot of tracks that are just okay but a lot of standouts too.It's got its fair share of issues but this trilogy is really worth investing your time into. The writing is really great (most of the time) albeit very slow, especially in the second game, but the payoff at the end is one I haven't gotten very often from games. There were ups and downs, but this trilogy really has had a large lasting effect for me after beating it. Haku, the GOAT.

_childDocuments_.review: The tactical JRPG part of this series was never the its strong suit, lacks depth gravely and creativity specially in Prelude to the Fallen, although they improved this part a lot in Mask of Truth yet it's never a good "game" but as a Visual Novel, it might surpass Muv-Luv Alternative in some parts for me.The story in Utawarerumono is nowhere near prefect, some might say it's a bit jarring with loopholes yet its story and world-building, music, character development combined throughout the series despite its fatal flaws in gameplay is what make Utawarerumono great.I dropped the first game after slogging through Prelude to the Fallen's awful gameplay after 10-ish hours, it's really not that engaging and sometimes boring but I am glad that I finally decided to pick up Utawarerumono again and finish it, get used to that sluggish gameplay of the first game and eventually it grows a little on you, once the characters get developed enough, it becomes easier to engage with, then before you know it, you can't stop playing more and more just to know what happens next, how the story goes.Utawarerumono on the surface may be just your typical dating sim but in its very core, it weaves a captivating narrative that brings together a diverse group of characters bound by fate or pure luck, beyond the surface allure of romance, the game delves into the profound journeys of these characters as they navigate personal growth, confront challenges, and ultimately strive to fulfill their individual resolutions. It is a narrative-rich experience that goes beyond the conventional boundaries of its genre, in the later arcs you can really understand why all of these girls fallen to the main character.Just like Muv-Luv, Utawarerumono if not as same is just as great as a emotional catalyst though the feelings it evoke might not be enough to surpass the Muv-Luv trilogy yet the journeys throughout the series can still strengthen the bonds between the characters and the reader.Tragedy is not just a plot device, it's also a catalyst that propels a story into the realms of depth and emotional resonance, a good story necessitates struggles and the Utawarerumono series definitely achieve this narrative successfully.If you like me who enjoys a strong storytelling, well developed characters, engaging plots, not to mention the huge amount of OSTs and CGs/fanservice it can offers, you have it to give the Utawarerumono trilogy a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: To start, this game is the last of its series, and is the second-part to a two-game story. At the minimum, before playing this game, you should play Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception first. If you're interested in what this story and its gameplay might be about, you can find my spoiler-free review and recommendations on the Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception page on Steam. It's been a long time coming, and honestly, I have no idea why I never wrote a review for this game on this platform, but to put it plainly, . I'm going to briefly talk about myself, but feel free to scroll down for my actual review. You see, back in 2019, I bought both Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception and Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth at a local game trading store for under $20 total. I didn't buy them for any particular reason other than because I was buying them on a whim. I figured since they were sequels, I might enjoy them one day, but I honestly didn't have any expectations for them at all. In fact, I completely forgot about them and didn't touch the games until a whole year later when the COVID pandemic started. Jobless, I saw these two games on my shelf and decided that I might as well play them since I had already bought them. At the time (I was 25 years old), and for most of my life, I was unmotivated and depressed, truthfully an empty and pathetic shell of a person who spoke with hypocrisy and let the world mold him. Who I am now is unlike anything I was before, and the only time I look back at my old self is when I look at this game or think about it and its music. This two-game story is the only game(s) that has ever brought me to tears. This story and its characters moved and inspired me to become a better version of myself with each passing day, so I am not exaggerating when I say that this game changed my life.. I still remember everything that I felt from every scene, from every soundtrack, from every voice and the cadence in which these characters spoke. When I finally finished this game, I felt so empty, it was as if there was a massive void inside of me, continuously eating away at me. I couldn't enjoy anything anymore; there was no food, no alcohol, no song, no game, nor story that appealed to me. Yet as empty as I was, the game had also brought me.. life. I applied for a job at a local warehouse, got it, and worked there for months. I hated working there, but every time I felt like quitting, my thoughts would race back to this game, its story, and its characters, and I'd continue pushing on. Fast forward to now (29 years old), I work in a control center, enjoy my work, and I am also studying other material so that I can continue to work towards my goals and better myself. I will forever cherish this story for as long as I live and that is why I bought the games all over again on Steam and replayed them all once each. Story: 9/10The game begins with many heavy feelings as the plot transitions from the end of Mask of Deception. If Mask of Deception is like enjoying a cup of sake in the company of your boon companions under the night of a full moon, then Mask of Truth is nothing less than a fist that slugs you right in the face with the weight of a roller coaster of emotions. Like the characters themselves, you as the audience may find yourself confused, uncertain, and possibly even broken with each development. At the center of political intrigue, you'll experience an unforgettable story about war and death, loyalty and love, hopes and dreams, duty and desires, and.. memories. Oh, gone are the days of enjoying a nice bowl of rulu or lazily resting at the Hakurokaku Inn.. All-in-all, although there are some developments that feel oddly inconsistent when you compare them to the overall fantastic and consistent world-building of this world, they are simply outliers that do not take away from the greatness that is this story. Music: 10/10The OSTs are amazing. Some soundtracks were designed with the intention of playing around motifs which beautifully tugs at nostalgia when you hear them. The music in this series brings many scenes to life, especially the heavy ones.Gameplay: 9/10This game builds on the previous battle system found in Mask of Deception. Several changes include rebalanced abilities and skills, but the best change made is that characters who do not actively participate in battles (due to deployment restrictions) will still gain some experience at the end of a chapter battle so that they do not fall too far behind like in Mask of Deception. Additionally, there are plenty of extra battle-focused content the player can indulge in, unrelated to the story. Difficulty: 7/10Although relatively easy, the game is more difficult than Mask of Deception. Thank you for the memories, Aquaplus, and thank you, _.

_childDocuments_.review: Mask of truth is the 3rd game in the Utawarerumono trilogy and being the climax and payoff directly following mask of deception it is the best entry. There's very little to actually talk about I guess without spoiling a lot of things (Don't read the steam description for the game also lmao as it also contains slight spoilers). But in general the game is a really slow burn starting out with Prelude to the Fallen's introducing the world that all 3 games take place, with most of the important plot points of that game happening near the end. It is also noticeably a lot more disjointed with its scenes and also very noticeably older with its tropes. Starting from Mask of Deception however you can see the improvements in writing almost instantly (at least imo) and from about the 4th quarter onwards through Mask of Truth it stays pretty high on the plot diagram.Mask of Deception is  before starting Mask of Truth while Prelude I guess you could skip but its highly highly recommended for worldbuilding and certain plot points. (Take Muv Luv's Extra as Prelude and Unlimited as Deception as a comparison if you've played those)For my playthrough in total for all 3 games it took just over 90 hours to complete on the hard difficulty. The battles themself are difficult but not overly unfair which makes the combat actually pretty fun (but prelude's combat is also noticeably worse than the latter 2 games). It is a pretty big time investment so that's something to keep in mind.

_childDocuments_.review: After completing all 3 games (Prelude to the Fallen, Mask of Deception, Mask of Truth), this was an absolutely stellar experience. I looked forward to every day I was to get back to the game and progress the story. I wish there was more but am very happy nonetheless to have had the chance to play this series. Although I’ve now completed the story, I still get to play Monochrome Mobius, so there is yet a bit more of this world to enjoy.If the “visual novel” tag tends to turn you off, then please understand this series is a “kinetic” novel. There are no choices, no routes and no self-insert character. It is primarily a narrative experience that you can simply set the dialogue to auto and enjoy watching as though reading a book or listening to an audio-book. There are tactical RPG gameplay sequences when story battles come up, but they are not difficult and largely you will simply be watching the story.I highly recommend the entire series.

_childDocuments_.review: A very pleasing conclusion to the series of tactics games.It wraps up the story threads left open by "Prelude to the Fallen", and is pretty much the second, better half to "Mask of Deception".Tactics battles with timed button prompts and hidden inputs, pleasing tactical combat, and a forgiving "rewind" mechanic that lets you turn back time to practice your button timings and to change tactical decisions instead of reloading an earlier save.The story actually got a few tears out of me, which is a somewhat rare thing for a game nowadays.And then there's the music... Rarely have I come across something that sounds so thoroughly "bittersweet".I dearly hope that there will be more of this series on PC at some point in the future.
