_childDocuments_.review: The finale of the Utawarerumono series which began with Prelude to the Fallen, the story picks up where Mask of Deception left off and gives a satisfying amount of screen time for some of the original crew from Prelude to the Fallen, if there are any fans that played the first title and are considering to play through the sequels. You don't need to play Mask of Deception to enjoy the game or be able to follow the story, but I would recommend picking up Mask of Deception, which allows you to get the full character development and world building that happens before the events in Mask of Truth. There is about 1.5 hours of story review to fill you in at the start of the game and tutorials that help you learn the battle system for people new to the entire game series (or get reacquainted with it). Overall the gameplay has improved compared to Mask of Deception and the game is balanced with reduced difficulty so it doesn't feel like you're on the verge of losing a battle after making a few bad moves and needing to rewind as much. There is actually a built in tutorial that's optional but recommended as combat gets more complex and tips on how to use each character's skills best against certain circumstances.The game is also better organized compared to Mask of Deception in its navigation menu and it's quite visible where to access the replay battle function to pick up any accessories/equipment you may have missed and get some EXP plus BP points. Pacing of the story keeps things exciting and battles are spread out more evenly compared to the lighter tone Mask of Deception that focused a lot on daily life interactions vs. the ongoing strife that encompasses the entirety of Mask of Truth. It's not completely free of bugs but I haven't had any issues that would break the game for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth

_childDocuments_.review: A great ending to the Utawarerumono trilogy.The combat continues to improve slightly over the previous entries, with more depth of action choices and techniques that reward positioning and timing. The training mode also gives more detail on the more advanced tactics and situations that occur, making the optional battles more engaging than in the previous titles.The story and characters continue to be the strong points though, with great writing and a commendable translation. The emotionally versatile voice acting brings a lot of life and colour to the characters, solidifying this as a must play if you are even remotely interested in visual novel style games (I mean, this is that third in the trilogy, so if you made it this far you know what you're getting in for).P.S. I'm not crying! You're crying!

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic entry that completes the story that started all the way from Prelude of the Fallen.Mask of Truth, however, is far more fitting to be called the second part of Mask of Deception rather than its sequel due to the stories of both titles being closely related; you can't have the full experience without having previously experienced Mask of Deception.As a Visual Novel, Mask of Truth has:- Deep and intriguing lore and main storyline- Serious as well as hilarious sub-events that expands character development (some are straight up memes)- An incredibly likable main cast and some of the side characters- Surprisingly consistent use of characters- Stunning artwork (a lot of it are considerably NSFW so be warned)- Top tier musicAs a Tactical RPG, Mask of Truth offers: - An unique take of TRPG combat using a timing-based combo system- Newcomer-friendly due to the rewind system and tutorials- Plenty of curious stages that will test your wits in the post-game In summary, it's highly recommended to purchase Mask of Truth alongside Mask of Deception (the DLC characters carry over, don't worry!) Also, it's best to treat Mask of Truth (as well as Mask of Deception to some extent) as a Visual Novel with an extra TRPG attached to it, but trust me, if you're a fan of Visual Novels the story alone makes it worth the money, just beware that some events might have NSFW CGs attached to it.

_childDocuments_.review: A really great game. As this game is a direct sequel to Mask of Deception(Itsuwari no Kamen), you have to play it first or else you will be spoiled with most of it story as soon as you start a new game. But, I will try to review it based on this game alone as much as possible.First thing first, as I said in my Mask of Deception review, anyone looking to play a great Turn-Based Strategy game may be dissapointed. It's not because this is a bad Turn-Based Strategy game, it's because the game itself more focused on story aspect so play this with a Visual Novel in mind. BUT, the system got improved in this game. Co-op chain system is a good addition to Overzeal system so there are more benefit to staying in Overzeal state. Some character got new moves and of course there are some new playable characters. Also,the new Co-op Finish system is just cool. Other than that, since I have some experience in this kind of genre so I play on Hard difficulty. Even on Hard difficulty the game is not that hard and you don't need to do any grind to beat the game.Now the story. The story overall is really good if you consider all of the game or at least just Mask of Deception and Mask of Truth. I, myself will consider it a masterpiece. But if you only look at this one game, first, as the situation is not very good at the beginning for the main character, so there will be high amount of emotional conflict between characters as the MC need to take the burden from Mask of Deception Ending. After the situation around them stabilize there will be a bit of leisure time where everything seems peaceful even though it shouldn't be. Unlike Mask of Deception though, this will not last too long and the story will progress excitingly soon. After that there will be great story writing until the end of the game. You will also feel character bonds from the peaceful time from the first-half of previous game affecting them so much here.And now for the pros and cons.Pros:-Great character and in game event arts. I really love the art personally.-Good 3D battle graphics. Not that cool, but good. The animation and special effect is good.-Good Turn-Based Strategy gameplay. This got improved from previous game. There are new moves and Co-op system. Co-op Finish is just so cool.-Great story with a really good pacing. With all game combined, I personally consider it as masterpiece.-Each character have their own personality that build up as the story goes.-There is level system but you don't need to grind any of your character. Your usual party setup is enough to beat the game without you going out of the way to grind you characters even if you play on Hard difficulty. And now your unused party member also got first time stage clear exp bonus(but not BP) so they won't be useless later even if you don't bring them to battle often.-Many famous Japanese Voice Actress/Actor so those who enjoy it will love it very much. Overall all VAs doing great jobs on this game.-Great English translation. If you understand Japanese you may feel "Wait, that he isn't exactly say that!", but looking on the context it is not a really wrong translation and is still in line with those characters.Cons:-Battle system gameplay may pale in comparison with many other Turn-Based Strategy games.-Free Battle mode(play previous cleared stage) only useful to get missed achievement and grind for small exp. So, most people may not even need to play it.(I don't even play them until I beat the game)-This is a direct sequel game, not a standalone one, so it is much better to play Mask of Deception first.Conclusion:A really great Visual Novel with Turn-Based Strategy battle system as bonus. The story is really great. As it is a direct sequel to Mask of Deception it is highly recommended to play that first. It is even better if you play the first one(Prelude to the Fallen) too either prior to starting this two games or after finishing them. The story got really good pacing and have so many exciting part.If you want a great story game and don't hate Turn-Based Strategy battle system, I really sure that this game series is a really good one.Really, personally a Masterpiece story for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Utawarerumono Mask of Truth, the final game of the Uta Trilogy, fantastically wraps up the entire storyline, the entire trilogy is top tier in almost every single regard, besides acouple small misteps. If you like VNs, SRPGs or serious fantasy storytelling, you owe it to yourself to play Prelude to the Fallen, Mask of Deception and finally this game, Mask of Truth. You won't be disappointed. _childDocuments_.review: Finally, it had come to the end. It took me extra 50 hours to finish the brutal dream arena after completing the main story but it was worth it. Only one word can describe the ending of Utawarerumono trilogy which is…AMAZING.The story about war and loss, about honor and betrayal, about guilt and deception and most importantly it was the story about love and truth. Utawarerumono was one of the best work of art in term of world building and character development. I love how every important characters including antagonists had the own arc making them closer to the readers. Haku was an extremely well-written protagonist, the last time I’ve seen any protagonist with this much characteristics and development was Takeru from Muv-luv trilogy and it was ages ago, Haku will forever be the only good harem protagonist. The game mechanics have improved a lot compared to its prequel, many characters had better buff and some overpower one was nerf making the gameplay more balance, the tactical side became more relevant than the prequel thank to the variety of status aliments, terrains and overpowered enemies which can make most JRPG fan satisfied. The ending was a bit controversial since it neither conclusive nor opened but in my opinion it worked really well with Utawarerumono universe, it made me not only feel like wanting to know more but also think that it was enough, truly a unique experience. Words cannot describe how much I love this story, it really is a modern classic of Visual Novel medium.Whenever I remember Haku I will remember  this idiom : “For he the man who wear the mask of deception   For he the man who walked through the path of carnage  For he the man who brought hope and salvation for others   For he the one whom legends are sung  For he is the truth Utawarerumono.”

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this story. Is it groundbreaking? No. I was confused at times as to what was going on but there was a gallery that helped answer the questions I had. _childDocuments_.review: It's one story told through two games in case someone who doesn't know. You also can't play just Mask of Truth without Mask of Deception and expect to understand everything, there's no point.Mask of Truth is a lot different from Mask of Deception. It picks up right where Mask of Deception ended, but the tone of the game quickly shifts from lighthearted, to outright depressing and sad. It also keeps the battle system from the first game, but adds some content, like Munechika's trials and the Training battleground which are a nice way to earn some items, learn more about mechanics and just grind some levels. Not to say there aren't any funny moments (which are needed to be honest), but it almost completely turns 180 and has a lot more serious tone. This is where the characters get even more depth and start shining, especially Nekone and Haku. I absolutely loved how their relationship slowly developed and in my eyes it's one of the big highlights. Speaking of which, it has too many to count. The story can be predictable at times, but it has a lot of genuine surprises, huge reveals and it's one of the best stories I've seen so far, if not the best. It deals with a lot of topics like going through loss, forcing yourself to accept lies for the greater good, losing your own persona, value of life, etc. The ending is bittersweet, but I feel like it's a bit more sweet than bitter.The following can be said about both Mask of Decelption and Mask of Truth, there were some music I really disliked, but there are a lot more that I absolutely loved, they were outright beautiful and filled with emotion, so overall I was more than pleased. But what I wasn't pleased with was how it's a 720p/30 fps port. The game came out in 2020 and this is absolutely unacceptable. While it doesn't hinder the experience, this kind of lazy port is a big no-no.It's a huge emotional rollercoaster with a lenghty and fantastic overall story through both games with a fun and deep cast of characters you'll most likely end up loving. This is a must buy, especially if you like VNs and don't mind some turn-based strategy battle system.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth

_childDocuments_.review: This is truly a great story. Bought this game immediately after completing the prequel mask of deception due to that outrageous cliffhanger, then proceed to eat this second part of the story like a madman. This game has much better distribution of battles sections in-between story sections, unlike the previous game which had 3 to 4 hours of uninterrupted text reading.Multiple times ninja cut onions; significant amount of tears shed.Very satisfying ending, with perhaps one the greatest end boss experience I've ever had.Game's tactical rpg side might seem like a sideshow, but has surprising depth that is fun to explore. The added trials missions makes it a lot easier to understand the finer points of the battle system, and post-story battle dedicated section allows you to have fun with the battle system. Combat can be hilariously fun once you know how some characters can become absolutely broken (oshtoru = raid boss, Kuon = nuke, Kiwru = ICBM, Fumirul = Speedwagon).Anyway, strongly recommend, but only after playing Mask of Deception first of course.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm mainly writing this review to be spoiler-free and to show my appreciation for this game, which feels very underrated for a great game. It is a strategy based VN where the main selling point is the lore and world-building of the game, which I personally really liked. This game is the 3rd part of the Utawarerumono Trilogy:1st:  Prelude of the Fallen2nd: Mask of Deception3rd: Mask of TruthAs the stories take place chronologically, I would recommend playing through all 3 of these games or watching the anime before you jump into the 3rd game. However, the anime doesn't capture that charm in my opinion, so I would just recommend playing the game instead. Playtime is approximately 20~30hours per game if you do not grind for experience points and concentrate on the story solely. Pick up this game/trilogy during a sale and enjoy the emotional roller-coaster as you play through the game.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, this is part two of the the Utawarerumono Duology, so if you haven't read part one yet GO READ IT FIRST  AND THE ANIME IS NOT A SUBSTITUTE. It leaves out many important key plot points and thus if you only rely on the anime as your experience of part 1, part 2 will be very confusing. also DONT SEARCH UP ANY MUSIC INVOLVING THIS GAME UNTIL AFTER YOUR DONE READING IT. many of the videos on youtube use cg from the game as a background, with many of them being big spoilers for certain things (i got spoiled this way T^T).Now that i got that warning out of the way, on to gushing about the series.The Utawarerumono series has now officially taken the spot of my Favorite series of all times. everything about this series was just fantastic heck its more then fantastic and i cannot even begin to express how much i love this series. Part 1 end off on a suspense filled cliffhanger that gave us many burning questions and part 2 fully lived up to the hype built up around part 1 while answering everything. This was a fantastic second half of the series and brought about a plethora of memorable moments in the world of Utawarerumono. If you read and enjoyed part one, this is one you definitely want to pick up trust me you'll regret nothing from grabbing this game. The story is fantastic with suspense filled plot that will keep you at the edge of your seat, tearjerker moments that will just make you want to bawl your eyes out, and comedic scenes that will remind you of part one that will feel all the more meaningful among everything else that is going on at the time. The already super loveable characters in part 1 also go through alot of character development that is just amazing to watch and become even more lovable. Overall a fantastic series and i cannot even begin to express how much i love this series its so good that i wish there was more. T^T If there is one issue i have with the game though is the strategy game sections of the game. This has been improved upon greatly compared to mask of deception with many of the battles requiring more strategy while nonetheless still being relatively easy, especially with the 50 turn rewind function the game has. The strategy section also adds to the atmosphere of the game really immersing us with what is going on, however i personally did not like the strategy sections too much due to not being the biggest fan of turn-based strategy gameplay. However, this is only a small component of the game and it only felt like a issue in some of the longer battles which are few and far between.Overall, fantastic game 10000000000000/10 i love this game to pieces and will probably play again sometime in the future. _childDocuments_.review: First off, this review might be biased because I just finished the game and its final scenes are still fresh in my mind. With or without recency bias though, I can confidentally say that Utawarerumono: Mask of Truth was an amazing experience and thus I cannot recommend this game enough.As the third and final installment of the Utawarerumono games you most likely shouldn't pick up this game before you got to experience the previous two. Fortunately there is an anime adaption of both the dated first  as well as the 2nd game for those who do not want to dedicate too much of their time to the trilogy since every game can take well over 60h to complete, although playing the 2nd game "Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception" will give you a deeper understanding of both the world and characters of the Utaverse than the anime will.Now then... First off, while Mask of Truth most definitely isn't without its flaws, the one thing that I thought would bother me the most actually turned out way better than I was expecting. Of course I'm talking about the combat system. While it's not the best turn-based strategy RPG out there (at least gameplay-wise) it does have some very intriguing aspects about the combat that prevents combat from being too repetitive. Mixing in QTEs with the for the genre usually rather slow gameplay combined with some other mechanics give the combat system a surprising amount of depth which makes it quite enjoyable in my opinion.The best part about the Utawarerumono series is without a doubt its worldbuilding, memorable characters and hard-hitting storytelling.  If you've played games like FF or one of the Tales of - games then I am 100% sure you will love this piece of art. This was one of the very few games I would give a lot for the chance to replay them completely blind again. The world and story was just that immersive and gripping.Anyways if you've come this far, I'm sure you're at least interested in the Utaverse to some degree and so I highly recommend you check out the anime of the 1st or 2nd game (or play the 2nd game) first and then decide and hopefully see for yourself just how amazing the conclusion to this absolutely incredible story really is.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, what a journey these two games have been. If you haven't played Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception, turn around and play that first! To not give away any spoilers I will just speak about my feelings while playing the game. You really feel immersed in a grand, mysterious fantastical world. This game really spoke to me. Seeing the characters all struggle to overcome sadness, guilt, betrayal, loss, and love was very touching. There were moments in this game that broke my heart and moments that made you feel on top of the world. The combat isn't especially fancy, but it is deep enough to keep you invested, and it requires enough strategy to keep you on your toes. Overall I would absolutely recommend this game, and this series, for anyone who loves visual novels or is interested in visual novels. This is a good entry visual novel because it breaks up the large amount of reading and text of the novel with gameplay and combat, which keeps you from getting too burned out from reading.

_childDocuments_.review: The final game in probably the best strategy rpg kinetic novel trilogy made yet. In my opinion it is also probably the best game of the three. It acts on and wraps up every story thread from Mask of Deception, as well as spinning it's own story from the world building done in MoD. It has a place for every character from MoD and the majority of characters from the original Utawarerumono. My only criticism is that the last act is very long, the opposite problem which Mask of Deception had, without spoilers to put it in words; there are several times I thought the game was over, then it built up for another climax. By the time the credits rolled I was emotionally exhausted, but a smile was on my face so I suppose it's fine.If you play this game and like it but haven't played the original Utawarerumono from 2002 I would tell you to go play it now. It's still good, though obviously dated. Unfortunately you have spoiled a fair bit of the story for yourself by playing this first, but you are still missing the complete picture, so I think it's still worth it.

detailed_description: Wake up, Hakuowlo. It's time to face the world again. You come to in bed, gravely injured, attended by a girl with twitching furry ears and a lush, bushy tail. In time you come to lead the villagers, to whom you owe your name and your life. When the local nobles threaten them, you threaten the nobility right back... Are you a farmer? A scholar? A traitor? A beast? You've forgotten your past, but has it forgotten you? Command your comrades and fight to defend your family, and discover the secrets of this world—and your own lost history! The first game in the hit Japanese tactics-RPG visual novel series Utawarerumono joins its sequels back on PC! Features 30+ hours of story and gameplay Thoughtful, slick, and active tactics-RPG combat Dynamic Chain Attacks and flashy Co-op Chains All-new Auto-Save functionality Customizable keyboard and mouse controls An unforgettable, evocative soundtrack A touching narrative with a moving ending

_childDocuments_.review: Reading about them in the Glossary is fine, just don't touch them in character select. The game thinks it's clever by enforcing continuity, except in the continuity play order, new players like me play this first. If not for the Complete Bundle, I would refund all the DLC for spoiling later games :/Really I just wanted to save others from my own fate, but if you want an actual review: it's an alright game; plot and events follow a lot of anime tropes but is still pretty cute and charming.The gameplay presents no challenge. I went through the first third on normal without increasing a single stat on any of my characters. Even after changing difficulty to hard there wasn't much difference. The game mechanics are a lot like Fire Emblem (or so I've been told; I've only played a bit of the GBA FE's). However, there is a very convenient built-in rewind function, and optional QTE for critical strike which rewards interaction with the combat animations.As a whole, this game should be taken as an introduction and prologue to the world of Utawarerumono, setting the stage for the latter games. Like stated previously, this game's cast are a bit generic but lovable nonetheless. Still any emotional investment in these characters will be well rewarded in the sequels. Of all the copious amount of media (games, books, movies, etc) I have consumed, Utawarerumono is one of the best if not the best franchise that handles its returning cast in its sequels, showing growth and charming interactions with latter casts.Bit of clarification on series as a whole to those who are completely new to the series as I was:

_childDocuments_.review: The complete Utawarerumono series is finally available on Steam and I want to recommend it, so here goes my review even though I still need to finish two of the three games. It's one of my favourite series due to its great story and storytelling (with both comedy and dramatic scenes done right), impressive world-building, and actual (and good) gameplay. So if you like VNs or RPGs and don't mind slow burners, here's an awesome VN/TRPG hybrid.The first game is Prelude to the Fallen (or Lullaby to the Dying) and works as a standalone game, Mask of Deception is an indirect sequel that's more enjoyable with knowledge from the first game, and Mask of Truth is the finale and requires having played both. I'd recommend playing through them in order now that they're all available, especially with Prelude being self-contained. DLC characters are completely optional, and in Prelude's case I'd even advise against buying them since they're related to MoD and MoT and might spoil things. By the way, don't look anything up about MoT lest you get spoiled.Also, you might have heard about a 18+ version. It's because Utawarerumono was first released as an eroge on PC in 2002 at a time where sex scenes were mostly added to sell more copies; an improved version without H-scenes was released on PlayStation 2 in 2006 and served as the basis for all subsequent re-releases of the game, including this one which is a remake in line with the sequels' style. So basically all versions tell the same story (with extra characters in the "console" re-release), and such scenes were not the main focus in the original release. And worry not, actually relevant ones are still referred to. The sequels however were made without 18+ content in mind due to being made for consoles and Aquaplus moving away from adult-only games.While I'm at it, if you're considering watching the anime instead of playing the game, it's a good enough alternative for the most part. Lemme explain: the adaptation of the first game is overall good and gets most important plot points, but doesn't include elements added in the enhanced version and omits some others that ended up being relevant in the sequels. OVAs however *do* contain characters that were added in the 2006 re-release. Then you have The False Faces, which roughly follows the story of Mask of Deception and is enjoyable if you've played it but is in no way an acceptable substitute due to the sheer amount of changes. Ah, and don't worry about not finding a HD version of the original anime, many shots and 3DCG elements actually held up better in SD; the rest looks great in HD though.Finally, a word about the port. It is unfortunately 720p and 30fps, just like the original console version, however it does not impact the game's quality. I feel like 3D segments in particular would benefit from being rendered at higher resolutions, though other elements might scale poorly and there's a chance the UI was drawn at that resolution. I won't complain about the framerate lock though, since I've seen way too many games end up broken when trying to reach higher framerates. And more importantly, the port has PC-specific features bringing almost everything you might expect from a VN/RPG on PC (yes, that includes proper mouse and keyboard support), as well as customisable button prompts (say, to use DualShock 4 icons). They even added an auto-save feature during battles to all three games and polished the translation, fixing typos as well as awkward sentences (like the infamous "Who the ♥♥♥♥ are they?").I'll massively update this review once I've finished this game. In the meantime, I hope it helps introducing people to the series and clearing things up!
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen

_childDocuments_.review: The pioneering work of the Utawarerumono series shows players another wonderful and magnificent story. As always, it cleverly combines SLG and visual novels, and compared with the other two works in the series, Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen has its unique characteristics.The soul-stirring music and exquisite original paintings allow players to enjoy a retro Japanese traditional visual novel experience, and this SLG battle design is more humane than the other two works, players will hardly encounter excessive difficulties during the game. At the same time, the shaping of some characters in the plot and the description of the daily plot are also very vivid.Still, the game's flaws are pretty glaring. As a visual novel, the plot of this game is obviously weak in the middle stage, which is mainly reflected in the too-fast development of the plot and the insufficient shaping of some characters. And many of the foreshadowings buried in the plot are just passing through or simplification. Even considering that the script of this work was written in 2002, it still has many unqualified places.Overall, this game is worth playing for players interested in the genre, as well as fans of Utawarerumono and Visual Novel games - especially those who played Mask of Deception and Mask of Truth first. But please note that if you haven't played the above two games, then please play Prelude to the Fallen first, you will get the best gaming experience.

_childDocuments_.review: "A journey that is only yours"Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen is a game I have hard time writing about. I want to talk about the game, but I don't know how to put my experience into words. I'll try my best here.Gamers in their 30's, like myself, rarely change their opinions about what or which games they consider to be "the best ever". I've never had a clear number one myself. I enjoy almost all types of games. However, I'm a story guy. I love good stories in the media I consume. I've seen thousands of films and series, played thousands of games since the days of the NES... but I've never cried this much during anything ever.I had to stop multiple times during my journey to cry and think. There are many sad, touching and deep scenes in the game. At one point, I spent an hour just sitting silently on my balcony at night. I wasn't sad. I was touched by the story, storytelling and everything I saw and heard, from the pictures to the music. This particular scene was constructed in such a way I'd never seen in any form of media; the most multilayered scene where everything was perfectly executed. After the scene, I was fairly certain I'd found my all-time favorite game... maybe even my all-time favorite piece of media.These characters, especially Hakuowlo and Eruru, are so well-written good people. I hate watching modern media where there are no good characters, only ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. To experience this god-tier story with these characters, has helped me to feel better about myself and life in general. Younger players might not understand the deeper scenes correctly, only because they lack life experience. I know I wouldn't have if I'd played this 10-15 years ago. There are subtle scenes that are not explained to the player. This reliance on the fact that the player understands what's happening is a rare treat.I had some idea where the story would go, but I was so, so wrong... and many times. I was shocked and jaw wide open time after time. I didn't expect this journey to be so real, brutal and even disgusting at times. I though I was going to play something happy and cheerful. How wrong was I. I did get those moments too. Some comedy in the mix too. But to me, this game is probably the most adult I can think of.The gameplay itself is completely secondary when compared to the story, but it's mighty fine too. Battles on normal are fairly easy for people who have played plenty of turn-based strategy games before. I did fail couple of times thou. Overall, the battle system is good and it has a nice flow to it.After finishing the game, I had to install the next one. I need to complete this journey and see if the other games, and the anime I ordered, are even close to being this great. Can't wait to move onto the Mask of Deception.This is my all-time favorite game. My review can't express how I feel about the game. Many tears of sadness and joy were shed... and will be when I get to playing this one again. I loved every second of this. I hope some of you experience the game like I did.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll get straight to the point: I've been gaming, reading, and watching TV/movies for 30 years, and the Utawarerumono trilogy is, as a whole, the most impactful work of fiction I've ever read.  I cannot recommend it highly enough.  I've been a fan of the series for 15 years now, and every time I come back to it, I'm reminded why I fell in love with it in the first place.This is a modern remake of the first game in the series, and as such, it's the best entry point.  I will say that I consider the first game to be the weakest one in the series -- but saying that is misleading, because it's still a great visual novel that I would recommend to anybody who likes serious fantasy stories.  It's a story about war, personality identity, found family, and the hubris of humanity.  On its surface, it can sometimes seem lighthearted and colorful -- and there are a lot of genuinely heartwarming moments of bonding and familial affection -- but it's also not afraid to have serious drama with meaningful consequences.What makes this game stand apart from the crowd?  One is its cast of characters: the protagonist is an adult man who is level-headed, reliable, and intelligent.  He's not a schoolchild or an idiot; he genuinely earns the trust and affection of the people around him.  The rest of the cast is also a wide range of characters who all may seem tropey on the surface, but all of them have a surprising amount of depth and characterization.The artwork and music are also great; they stood out in the original 2002 version of the game and have been polished up and remastered here, and they're still some of the best in the business.  I would also be remiss to not mention the game's combat system; adding a turn-based, tactical combat system into a visual novel was unheard of in 2002 and is still rare now, and Utawarerumono's battles both help to break up long stretches of reading and also get the reader more immersed in the seriousness of the conflicts.  If I had one complaint to make about the first game, it would just be that the combat system is pretty simple; it's enjoyable, but it won't challenge SRPG veterans.  Like every other aspect of the game, it keeps getting better in the sequels, and Mask of Truth, the final game, is also the best SRPG I've ever played.I will say that the PC ports of these games have one technical issue I'm not a fan of: they're locked at 720p/30Hz.  It's not a huge problem; you're going to spend 80% of the game just looking at still images and reading text, after all.  It would be really nice for the 3D battle sequences to at least be rendered in a higher resolution, but sadly, that's not an option.Despite that, I'm still confident in saying that this is one of the best hidden gems of fantasy storytelling to ever come out of Japan.  Please play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen

_childDocuments_.review: The wait is finally over. 19 years after its original release, us in the West can finally play Utawarerumono in English and on PC. It comes a year after we got the two sequels Utawarerumono: Mask of Deception and Mask of Truth, completing the trilogy on the platform. Now, before I begin, I should give a brief explanation on what exactly this game is, because I know a lot of people just look at the title and are scared off by how long it is. In short, it’s a visual novel with tactical RPG gameplay segments and the first in the larger Utawarerumono series. It’s a bit confusing as we actually got the second and third game in that series (Mask of Deception and Mask of Truth respectively) released on PC last year, so it may have been released out of order, but at least the trilogy is complete now and those that have been holding off on the two sequels can get started with this one.Having watched the 2006 anime adaptation of the game, I went in already knowing how the story would go, but somehow found myself sucked into it yet again. Before I knew it, five hours had passed, a rare occurrence for me when playing visual novels. It starts off relatively slow and mostly lighthearted, but eventually builds up into this bigger, more ambitious fantasy story – one full of likeable characters, interesting plot developments, and a nice overall sense of pacing.In fact, the pacing was largely the reason why I was able to keep reading without noticing the time passing. That and I’m personally a huge fan of fantasy stories with a good grasp on worldbuilding, which is exactly what the beginning of this game offered. However, even when it does get a bit more serious, it never quite loses that lighthearted charm that it starts with – similar to how the plot develops in Mask of Deception. It’s quite unique for the medium and a welcome change of pace as someone that plays a ton of these games.And for those that have seen the anime, the game provides some really good context and insight into the events from it. I watched it many years ago and had a good time returning to that story while also further immersing myself into it – I was actually surprised with how close an adaptation that anime was now that I’ve been playing the game. It is a long one though. The anime may have been 26 episodes, but this is a 30-hour game, so there’s a lot of ground to cover – even if it is the shortest of the trilogy.There’s also a sizeable tactical RPG side to it that comes in the form of turn-based battles on a grid, similar to the Disgaea games. The gameplay during these segments is pretty straightforward and not too in-depth, but an otherwise nice distraction from the story. There are character-specific skills, equipment bonuses, usable items, a leveling system, and even boss fights. It’s not too bad on normal difficulty, but can be ramped up to hard for those that want a challenge. I personally found the normal difficulty to be a nice balance between being able to enjoy the story and having the occasional challenging fight.Right off the bat, what I immediately noticed was the difference in art style between this game and the two sequels. I mean, there was a 13-year gap between them in Japan, but I had thought the art would have been updated to look more in-line with the sequels given that this is a remaster. And honestly, I’m glad they didn’t. The art has been brushed up since its original release for sure, but it still maintains that distinct early 2000’s anime aesthetic. It’s hard to explain exactly what constitutes that, but it was actually quite nostalgic as someone that has seen a lot from that era.Then there’s the music, which is just as good as it is in the sequels and even expanded a bit here. You’re able to choose from the original music and the new “special extended” music when starting up a new game. I tried and enjoyed both of them, each providing the story with its range of laidback, slice of life fantasy tracks and more energetic action tracks for the gameplay parts.I should also talk about the port, as this game is based on the PS4 version released last year by NIS America. Just like the two sequels, it runs at 720p and is locked to 30 fps. However, it does offer in-game options for higher resolutions, it just scales the game to display at them rather than do so natively – the opposite of most VNs that simply change the monitor to match the in-game resolution. These specs are the standard for most visual novels on PC, but I won’t deny that it would have been nice to see higher-res art offered, especially because there are gameplay segments and you can easily tell they are being upscaled.Otherwise, the port is alright. It’s got the usual VN settings, but also offers remappable keyboard controls on top of that along with controller support. This release is actually the definitive edition of the game because it also adds auto-saves and improves the translation a bit compared to its release last year.For those wondering if there are any H-scenes, the short answer is no. The original 2002 release had them, but all subsequent re-releases and remasters had them removed – and it’s honestly for the better given that many compare them to Fate/stay night’s case in that they are completely unnecessary and even detract from the overall story.With all of that said, Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen easily earns my recommendation. It’s an excellently told fantasy story that pretty much gets everything right, with likeable characters, good worldbuilding, and some really nice pacing – enough so that I hardly noticed the time passing while playing. Then there’s the solid art and music backing it up, cementing the game (and by extension, the series) as one of the best fantasy VNs on the market. Honestly, I could see myself using this as a recommendation for those looking to get into visual novels, especially for fantasy fans.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: Is Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen a good game? Yes. That's the shortest, and probably best answer I can give you. If you want to hear more, the following will be some of my ramblings on the game, but be warned they may not be well organized.There are dozens, hundreds of things I could say about this game, how it's a quality remake of a huge piece of my childhood, how the world it presents pulls you in with character-driven world building, a convincing main character, while still keeping a lighthearted tone that stops you from getting tired of worn out. How when things get serious, you feel it, deep in your heart, how even now 12 years after I first played this game, the story still cuts through me, makes me smile, makes me laugh, makes me cry - it's such a ride, and it's such a joy.The biggest changes from the original version I remember playing are the ttrpg segments and the soundtrack - even with the original ost option turned on (which is a very nice touch by the way) the songs are all remasted in higher quality, often with new vocals. The additional songs from the rest of the trilogy added by the extended soundtrack blend in rather seamlessly and the having played through the game with both (a new game plus run was rather mandatory for me) I can comfortably say I like the extended one better, despite my nostalgia.The ttrpg gameplay has been improved a considerable amount. Issues the original had were hammered out by things like equipment, consumable items (you can give healing items to other character so Eruruu isn't your only source of health anymore!) but ultimately it isn't super involved - this is more of a story than a game and while there's enough depth to lose yourself in, nor anything groundbreaking, it's entertaining and a good diversion from the extended story sections - kind of a way to take breaks from all the reading the game has you doing. The new training mode is a perfect example of this; play meaningless, non-story related battles over and over for items, gear, exp - but more just to take a break when you feel like it.As for the story itself, there's far too much to even say. We start, as I'm sure you read by now on the store page, as a man with a mask waking up with no memories. The story is told entirely through his eyes, narrated by his inner thoughts and dictated by his choices - there are no "routes" in this vn, the story is linear. However the large cast of characters, each filled with quirks and unique appeal has a way of drawing you in, while the medieval fantasy setting helps to keep things quite grounded. When our protagonist tries to explain how to grow crops using fertilizer, the villagers simply call it a magic charm and put their faith in him, despite his attempts to explain.Visually, the game is very similar to how it first appeared in 2002 - the resolution has been improved and there has been some cleaning up done to the art, but the style has been preserved and it is stunningly beautiful. Paired with the wonderful soundtrack, I almost find myself crying just looking at the cg gallery and remembering the bittersweet happenings of the story.I'll admit, I'm not very good at this kind of thing - especially when I'm trying not to spoil things, so I think I'll just stop now. Ultimately it's your call, but I honestly cannot recommend this game enough. If you've played either of the other two games, this one is a must try. If you haven't, this is the best place to start the series. If you have any interest in fantasy stories, in visual novels, hell even just in ttrpgs, please, please PLEASE give this a try. You won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: "Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen" is a remake of the game "Utawarerumono (2002)". As the author of this review, I'm very fortunate to be able to experience such a masterpiece. I also took this opportunity to watch『Utawarerumono』, a TV animation adapted from the game of the same name was broadcast as early as 2006. At this moment, in order to preserve the touching and joy of this group of works in my heart, I hereby use this article to express my emotions, as well as my views and understanding of the work.Let's start with the battle link. The battle of this game is a typical SLG war chess game. Its exquisite battle scenes and combat operations with a sense of impact require players to experience it themselves, I’ll not go into too much detail. In contrast, the battle scenes of the anime "Utawarerumono" appear stiff and rough, which does slightly affect the viewing experience. But one thing needs to be explained: in the game, when the gorgeous and cool pictures attract ur attention, u’ll feel restless in a long section of ordinary daily story, and u’re eager to have a battle can bring pleasure and not pay attention to the dialogue of the characters, even if the plot isn’t bad or even lively and interesting. In addition to the battle, I prefer to put the highlight of this review on the core plot, so I’ll talk about the particularly exciting parts of the plot separately.Some villains portrayed in the story have a way of thinking and actions confuse that some people: Nuwangi who bullies the weak, Niwe who’s a fighting maniac, and the emperor Olikakan who vents hatred, etc. Although these villains are in high positions, they have no mercy on the civilians of other countries or even their own country, and are 'proficient in everything' in burning, killing, and looting. This can be called 'individualism' that acts for one's own selfishness and according to one's own wishes. Dii, as the leader behind this series of events, is also「The Great Liberator」who can bring happiness and disaster to people in the setting. He’s a special existence and cannot be simply classified as one of these villains. In addition, Kuuya of Kunnekamun, who is against the White God Hakuowlo in the story, is also the only character who survived the struggle with the protagonist. As for whether it also belongs to the 'villain' I mentioned, it depends on everyone's understanding of the work.Hakuowlo (ハクオロ) is the protagonist, also known as the White God. Hakuowlo is a different emperor in my opinion. He is 'weak', although he’s the ruler of a country, he doesn’t have the domineering and tyranny of the villains, and the decisions are always made by subordinates. Especially the helplessness he showed when he was tied up along with his bed by his 'servant' Karulau and taken to another country to participate in the war was really comical and laughable. In addition, he’s also 'capable', I believe everyone has no doubt about this. After all, he was originally「The Great Liberator」who created the sub-human world, whether it’s politics, military, science and technology. It's just the combination of 'capable' and 'weak' makes the character image of Hakuowlo stand out. Is Hakuowlo a gentle and kind person, or is he not suitable to be an emperor? This’s also left for everyone to think about, I’m just talking about it in general.Love bound by a pact refers to the feelings that the heroine Eruruu(エルルゥ) developed towards Hakuowlo after signing the pact with him, her soul bounded by restrictions of the pact. I think this part can be regarded as one of the places where the artistic effect brought to the audience is 'explosive'. It's just the depict is not in place enough, but it's enough to move the audience.Eruruu is one of the highlights of this work. In the story, her feelings for Hakuowlo seem reasonable to others, but painful to herself. From the beginning, she accompanied Hakuowlo and treated his injuries, to the death of her grandma Tuskur, she and her sister Aruruu were entrusted to Hakuowlo to take care of them. The three of them were like family, this process all explained the rationality of Eruruu's feelings for Hakuowlo. Although the true face of Hakuowlo is「The Great Liberator」, he treats all his companions kindly, especially Eruruu. However, after knowing the pact with Hakuowlo,she hesitated and even denied her feelings. She believed in the so-called "complete dedication from soul to flesh and blood, even a hair" pact, abandoned feelings which had buried deep in her heart. The funny thing is the pact Eruruu has always abided by was neatly abolished by Hakuowlo who knew the truth.This duel is the finale of the story and also the highlight. It’s not only the key to unlocking the mystery of Hakuowlo's life experience, but also the output of different values of this fictional world. The focus is on the dialogue between「Empty Shell of Mine(空蝉)」and「Doppelganger of Mine(分身)」. Note here I deliberately do not use "Hakuowlo" and "Dii" coz I wanna separate the will of God as a「The Great Liberator」from the human. This's a fight between god&god, and a fierce collision of two ideas, not grievances between people.The essential reason for the duel between「Empty Shell」and「Doppelganger」is that the two have different views on ruling the world. 「Empty Shell」believes the world should implement the policy of helping the poor and the needy weak, and harmonious coexistence between races; 「Doppelganger」believes the world is the law of the jungle, and the survival law of the strong survives and the weak perishes. It’s worth reminding although the whole story is narrated from the perspective of the protagonist, but the non-protagonist isn’t necessarily evil. Ofc, there’s no need to refute the individualistic villain mentioned above, and it’s recognized by anyone as bad.Think about the above problem from another angle. Can't both ways of thinking be adopted together? Although the two seem contradictory, there’s still a solution. Recalling the ancient Chinese thoughts on governing the country, there are three famous ones: Confucianism, Taoism, and Legalism. When the society is turbulent, the country is governed by ‘Taoism’, and when the society is stable, the country is governed by ‘Confucianism’. As for ‘Legalism’, both are taken.  It can be seen from this the confrontation between「Empty Shell」and「Doppelganger」isnot unsolvable. Videlicet, the two can take turns to govern the world. Therefore, tracing back the cause of the whole story, we have to blame early awakening of「Empty Shell」. In the end, after discovering he was the embodiment of Uitsualnemetia's good half, Hakuowlo challenged「Dark Witsuarunmitea」Dii, the embodiment of the darker half, and emerged victorious by fusing with it, unifying the「Uitsualnemetia」. Afterward, Hakuowlo asked to be sealed away for a while to prevent any more damage to the world but promised Eruruu that he would see her again. Eruruu and others will uphold the will of「Empty Shell」and continue to develop the world in the direction of their ideal.._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._._.In general, this’s a masterpiece that combines rich emotional descriptions, the collision of different political ideas, and the inheritance of spiritual culture. Its unprecedented worldview setting also shocked me a lot. In the final analysis, when it comes to the explanation of the game title, 'Utawarerumono' means the person or thing (spirit) that is praised. I think the game praises the spirit of「The Great Liberator」of Hakuowlo who sacrifices himself for others, loves the country and the people, and values friendship and righteousness. Even if the god will be destroyed, his spirit will be praised on forever.

_childDocuments_.review: Utawarerumono is a widely praised and beloved trilogy of RPG-Visual Novels, with Prelude being the first game in the series, followed by  and .Within the first few hours of gameplay, this story is sure to suck you in with its lovable cast of characters, comfy atmosphere, and thriving world. I'm not really a fan of RPG gameplay in visual novels, but Utawarerumono seamlessly integrates the RPG gameplay into the main story while not breaking my immersion. The combat while simple, is pretty fun and offers a challenge when it needs to. It takes a while for the story to pick up, but once it gets the ball rolling, you'll be thrust into an epic story filled with conflicts, friendships, love, family, sacrifice, world-changing twists and an ending that will stick to you for days. Definitely an experience I will cherish for years to come and I couldn't be more excited to play the sequels.

_childDocuments_.review: This game starts out super good.  The combat is fun, the writing is good, the voice acting is good.  The story begins with a very dramatic core, (minor spoilers for the very first part of the game) the tale of a people rising up against their unjust rulers.Sadly, it quickly abandons that tone and becomes a waifu-collecting harem hijinks game.  That's not to say it's awful necessarily, if you like anime about a harried male protagonist being pulled in all directions by an ever-growing collection of fawning women, then this might be a good game for you.  For me, I don't really care for those types of stories and more importantly the constant tone switching was too much to bear.  One moment we're in a meeting room discussing the possibility and ramifications of being dragged into a war, the next moment we're being kidnapped by our gang of waifus and dragged into a plan that is definitely going to cause all those awful things we just had a meeting about.  The writers weirdly seem aware of of the political complexities inherent in their story, they just can't resist doing silly anime hijinks anyways.

_childDocuments_.review: Read the full review here: Utawarerumono may be nearly 20 years old, but this port represents the first time the game has received an official English translation release on PC.If all you want to know is whether this is a good port, I can say that I had no issues with the game.  This port is an adaptation of the Vita remaster, so this game can run on a potato.  I should note, however, that some AMD graphics card users reported some screen tearing, although I do not know how bad or widespread this is.The textures are detailed, but the polygon count of character models definitely shows its PlayStation 2 era roots.  Graphically, the game runs at 720p, and is upscaled to fit larger resolutions, resulting in some minor blurriness. The game is also locked at 30 FPS, like most games of the era, although being mostly a visual novel and tactical game, you will notice this less than you would in an action game.The game comes with a multitude of options, with full controller support and an option to change what button prompts are given to you on-screen (from PS or XBox or Switch controller to keyboard icons), and you can rebind keyboard keys, but not controller keys, at least without a 3rd party controller rebinding software.  The game can almost entirely be played with the mouse, however, and you only need a few buttons on the keyboard even during combat sections, since this game is fairly menu-driven.If however, all you are here for is the "plot", keep in mind that no version past the original 2002 release had sex scenes, the game's story was rewritten and expanded since then, and there is zero chance those scenes are being patched in.  If you're adamant about only buying the version with sex scenes, this probably isn't the game for you, anyway, since there's only about six to start with in a 60 hour game.  There was a fan translation patch released years ago, if you can LEGALLY find a copy of the original game.  Keep in mind that the effects of the sex scenes, I.E. the main character having children that are plot-relevant to the sequel games, are still in the game.Gameplay-wise, Utawarerumono is a split between "Tactics" JRPG and a traditional visual novel.  This split skews  towards Visual Novel for the first half of the game, with hour-long novel sections punctuated by 5-minute battle sections.  Utawarerumono takes its time setting up plot threads and raising tension in them before paying them off with a conflict, and the fact that they can be keeping several plot threads baking in the oven at a time can lead to very long stretches between climaxes to individual plot threads.The protagonist of the story, Hakuowlo, is treated as a strategic and political genius by the text itself, but I find it hard to keep up with, as Hakuowlo doesn't just have the typical harem anime protagonist obliviousness to the fact that all the girls are in love with him, he seems to lack any awareness of human emotion whatsoever, needing people to tell him that the guy screaming how he hates him and will kill him is actually angry at him for him to understand.  It seriously undermines the way that the story tries to present the main character as hyper-competent in every way to have him bumble on something so basic.This isn't as serious as the way that the absolute baby-eating cartoon villains of this story undermine the tone, however.  This game wants to be Game of Thrones, with serious intrigues and games of political one-upsmanship, but the villains make Bowser look competent.  The emperor that starts the rebellion that starts this whole mess originally drove the villagers to the point of rebelling against their taxes being so high they faced starvation because he was literally bankrupting the empire paying for hair product to give himself an afro.  I'm not kidding.  The super-serious general guy who the story is trying to play as being torn between loyalty and duty then tries to suggest that maybe burning the empire down for hair product is slightly short-sighted only gets beaten over the head for his troubles... and yet, they still want to play his loyalty to the emperor as serious and tragic, not absolutely moronic.  Sure, Joffrey was manifestly unfit for the throne, but he at least didn't spread the rebellion by burning the villages that  rebelling against him so that every remaining village felt the need to join the rebellion against him just to survive.  Did I mention that, because they didn't have enough screentime for some villains to make you have good reasons to hate them, nearly all the named villains that you're supposed to root for getting killed look like pigs vaguely contorted into human shape that also have weird accents and verbal ticks so they laugh like "NYEHYEHYEH"?With that said, this story is still being re-released for a reason, and it has a full-length 2006 anime available on Funimation for you to watch, so it does eventually get past some of the absurd elements... although some of the later twists can also be considered absurd. (The anime can be a better viewing experience than the visual novel, as there are a lot of fights that are just narrated in the visual novel section that are just text descriptions and sound effects.  Having actual animation and not relying upon a small pool of still images of characters makes the non-interactive story parts much more interesting.)The actual tactical battles feature characters with limited abilities, most similar to games like Fire Emblem.  For example, the healer characters can only heal, never attack.  Mages only use magic, and fighters only physical attack.  You get three main stats besides HP, which are attack or healing power, physical defense, and magic defense.  Each character gets their own turn in the queue, but there is no apparent speed stat, and ending a turn without attacking or moving does not make your next turn come faster, so staying out of range to make an enemy waste a turn is often a good move.  In fact, playing defensively in general and giving your healers as much time as possible to restore your allies is a much better strategy than trying to act aggressively to take down enemy units, even when they are capable of healing, themselves.  Attrition favors the player.The only action elements to the game are a pseudo-quick-time-event where you hit the "confirm" button (left mouse) when a ring lines up during attacks.  This does not actually increase damage or make attacks hit, however, it just adds percentage to a Zeal bar that gives you a special attack when it is full.  In fact, the game is very deterministic in its random elements, even to the point of telling you in advance that you'll do 0 damage when attacking a character with a "chance to deflect arrows" ability when that ability will activate.  A "rewind" function lets you go back up to 50 actions in the move order to allow you to turn battles around, and the dice rolls will be the same every time. A unique way to cut down on save-scumming, for sure.One sour note is the day-one DLC.  These are all characters from the sequel games that are just plugged in as extra party members during battles, and they have no plot relevance.  It might be a version of pay-to-win, but since you have unit deployment caps equal to the number of plot characters you would have anyway, you'd have to take the plot-relevant characters out to field the DLC characters.  It's a transparent no-effort money-grab but at least it's one that's easy to pass up with no negative consequence? I'm not sure if that makes it better or worse.All told, if you're the kind of gamer that hears "visual novel tactics RPG", and thinks this might be your sort of game, you probably won't be too disappointed, some of the narrative elements aside.  If you like the series, and want a "future proof" version that won't die with your PS4, this is the one to get.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: I really liked this game/VN, although it's probably one of those cases where my rational brain tells me it's not as good as I feel it is. It's probably not worth $60, but if you can get it on sale, it's a good recommendation.The characters are likable, although almost none of them really have any time to develop. They remain mostly static throughout the entire story; for instance, one girl starts out as an innocent child who likes honey, and ends the story as an innocent child who likes honey. Character development is certainly not a strength of Utawarerumono, even if, again, characters are likable enough. It more-or-less plays out like a slice-of-life anime, but that's still no excuse to not develop your characters. Look at what Cowboy Bebop did, for instance. Given the "harem" nature of the story at times, I'd say it was a wasted opportunity for the game to not include more in the way of player decisions. Several women in the story throw themselves at the main protagonist. But you can never alter the trajectory of their arcs in any way. It would've been nicer if we could've chosen to foster these relationships organically, a la Sakura Wars. Instead, the story is entirely linear, with 0 decisions that the player ever has to face. One area where Utawarerumono shines is in its worldbuilding. I found myself far more engaged with learning about the different nations and the world's backstory, than I was with some of the characters' relationships. Utawarerumono's setting feels like everything that God Wars should've been, but wasn't. That being said, I won't claim that the game's setting is anything exceptional or revolutionary, as pleasant as it may be. If you boil it down, it's mostly a predictable romp through a Japan-esque world with light sci-fi stylings. And weird, convoluted names. Lots of them: Uitsulnemetia, Amrulineulka, Hakuowlo, and Omkamiyamukai to name a few. (Then there's Dii, as a nice change of pace.)As a strategy RPG, it's mediocre at best. Battles are all extremely easy, to the point that my characters were one-shotting almost every enemy throughout the entire game. AI is mind-numbingly moronic. Even the final boss did not pose a threat to my team, and I didn't grind AT ALL. Oboro in particular is absolutely busted: he has the best mobility in the game, a very high "speed" stat (which functions like in Shining Force; he takes his turns more often than other units), and one of the best attack growths in the game. In Utawarerumono's defense: the SRPG stuff is at least not a detriment to it. This is more than I can say of some other games. It's somewhat disappointing that the game was not more strategically engaging than it is. But meh, it could've been worse, so I'm fine with it. One thing that's particularly odd about the game is how many of the CG backdrops are straight-up recycled from earlier parts. You'll find yourself revisiting the same cliffside road many times, despite the story taking you through the entire continent. Was it really not possible to do better than this? Especially in 2020? For a $60 game?It took me around 20 hours to finish the entire thing, so yeah, probably not worth $60. Yet, all this comes to say: I really did enjoy it, even if my rational brain can pick up on all these areas for improvement. It's possible that Utawarerumono is a worse game than I think it is, and that's fine. I'm looking forward to experiencing the other two Utawarerumono VNs that are also on Steam. I'd be interested in seeing other Visual Novel/Strategy RPG fusions, since it's a rather unexplored concept.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen

_childDocuments_.review: I waited for so long to begin my Utawarerumono journey that when I saw the then upcoming PC release I couldn't believe my luck. An instant day one purchase and 40 or so hours later, however, I can't help but feel I might've been building myself up for disappointment right from the get go. In terms of narrative, gameplay, & production, there's so much to I enjoyed but also so much I truly disliked - I'll do my best to cover all of it.The visual novel elements are beautifully illustrated with each character having a fair collection of sprites & emotional portrayal, which really helps to develop the world early on in the read. The backgrounds are also vivid & detailed, making this near 20 year old VN an absolute pleasure on the eyes... Until you get to the SRPG sections. I'm a realist, and I understand there's not going to be much potential for a major graphical overhaul in a title as niche as this, however I don't think that excuses the art quality of the SRPG sections when a game is priced as high as this one currently is. Despite being shorter than both of its sequels, it's currently 50% more expensive than either of them in the UK, which is a bit of a bitter pill to swallow. At near-AAA prices I'd hope for a little more than what's perhaps best described as upscaled PS2 visuals, but hey, it's not that the game is ugly during these periods - it just isn't anywhere near the quality of the VN segments which have aged incredibly well.Gameplay is also a bit of a hit & miss, with the combat starting off relatively tactical & interesting before devolving into one shotting nearly everything until the final chapter even without any sort of out-of-story combat training. Perhaps this is something that's addressed with the higher difficulties (I played on normal), but again, it's hard to excuse a difficulty curve that looks like an incredibly wide valley (\____________/). Perhaps that's a benefit to those who are just seeking to enjoy the story, but for me, the combat quickly went from engaging to disinteresting, & every time it popped up it seemed like more of a chore than something I was actually enjoying.The story is perhaps the most disjointed & bizarrely paced I've read in a while, with there simply being too much crammed into some (gameplay & non-gameplay) periods & absolutely nothing packed into others (although I've always been a fan of good slice of life, so that's alright with me personally). The ending especially feels incredibly rushed in its pacing which did leave me feeling a little bit empty afterwards, but it's a problem that's fairly consistent throughout the read. There's other issues I took with the story that others might think tread into spoiler territory, so while they're mild at best, I'll mark them as a spoiler (you've been warned!): That said, the world & the lore itself is fascinating. You might find it all to be pretty dense early on, and you'll almost certainly find yourself referring to the in-game glossary to make sense of certain names & their associations, but it's something that pays off in the end, & hopefully over the following installments as well. On another positive note, the cast itself is great & plenty entertaining throughout, which helped turn what would otherwise be an overall negative experience into a pretty positive one, which gives me some hope for when I finally dip my toes into MoD/MoT. The OST, while rarely mindblowing, is enjoyable throughout & compliments the story nicely, though there's little to nothing there I'll be going out of my way to listen to in isolation.On the technical side of things, I experienced zero issues with the PC port. Everything is really well presented, & it controls very well with both KB/M & the good ol' trusty Xbox controller.Overall, it's a recommendation, but a very tentative one (especially at the current price). It's value to me will very much depend on just how much better it's sequels actually are, because while Utawarerumono really does lay the seeds with its strong cast & lore, it really doesn't give them the light they need to properly grow into something beautiful.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen

_childDocuments_.review: The combat is pretty terrible, honestly.  Especially when compared to similar games like Fire Emblem, Langrisser, Tactics Ogre, Symphony of War, just name a grid-based combat game and Utawarerumono will seem rather unintuitive.So why am I recommending it?  Because it's a Visual Novel pretending to be an SRPG.  While games like Trails in the Sky do the "I'm actually a VN even though I pretend to be another genre" better, Utawarerumono manages to have its own charm, with realistic (so far at least, I'm about 3 hours in and some of that time was a bit idle admittedly) characters and a compelling plot.  A VN lives and dies based on its writing and characters, and this game seems to be compelling enough to be worth a read.If you're looking for combat or gameplay, sure, I'll bet other JRPGs like Trails in the Sky and Persona 5 would better fit your needs.  The aforementioned Fire Emblem or Langrisser definitely fit the SRPG itch, including the more recent Symphony of War.  But this game seems to be more of a narrative and story experience than having great gameplay.  If you're cheap or want a free experience, you can try Exit Fate as well.If you're read this whole thing, you're the kind of demographic who might enjoy this game!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing this after finishing the third game.This game is super flawed:* The combat is pretty bad* The start is extremely slow* It's fairly obvious from the way the female characters act, that the original was a H game.However, it's probably my favourite of the series. Hakuowlo is a fantastic main character. All the side characters have their own unique charm and stand out, yet the main heroine has her place.This sets up such good world building for the rest of the series.If you're new to the series, you may have noticed that this game is considered optional and was released after the other two. Make sure you play it, it makes the third game (considered by most to be the best) hit extremely hard.Overall I'd rate this my favourite of the three games for it's characters and story, but most certainly would recommend playing the others if you enjoy this.

_childDocuments_.review: Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen is the recent rerelease of the 2006 PS2 Japan-exclusive game Utawarerumono: Chiriyukusha e no Komoriuta, which, itself, was a rerelease of the 2002 Japan-exclusive PC eroge Utawarerumono. The game has had both significant and minor alterations made to it during its near 20-year (official) Western release, the most obvious being the removal of the eroge scenes available in the original and the massive improvements made to the turn based combat. These scenes being removed does make sense, considering they were always going to fail the Sony check when making the move to console, but it would be unfair to suggest their exclusion is completely painless. Never a hard eroge at heart, Utawarerumono used these parts sparingly, usually to highlight each character’s vulnerability before then being harem’d by the protagonist. This all now happens off screen before the game moves on, hoping you didn’t notice the small hole where the content used to be.If this bothers you, you can do what many of us did back in the day; lean on the excellent fan translation of the original and play it as 2002 intended. But you’d be missing out on a lot. Though the Utawarerumono series is basically a visual novel with turn based combat included, the scope and the competence of said combat has been massively upscaled. Advancements like offering equipment you can win from conquered battles, or discover by destroying hidden objects placed in inconvenient locations around skirmish maps. Depending on their relationship, adjacent allies now have access to blistering co-op attacks that can decimate large swaths of the enemy force if used correctly. There’s extra chapters focusing on the characters most neglected by the original and Easter eggs hidden away for those willing to put in the time to search them out. All the game’s battles are repeatable should you want to delve back into mêlées already beaten to grind levels, or hunt down evasive items you couldn’t claim on the first sweep. There’s exclusive training missions you can trigger any time you like after a certain point of the game. I used them to try and break up the mountains and mountains and mountains of words.There’s a bazillion words no matter which version you partake in (though the original doesn’t have the stellar Japanese voice acting the other titles do), so without a decent story, all the improved combat would be particularly meaningless. Utawarerumono, then, is the tale of an amnesiac man, who is rescued by a rural village and nursed back to health. Not the most auspicious start, but the tale gains strength in how hard it invests in the cast. Given the name Hakuowlo until the time he’s able to remember his own, he spends his initial days carefully recuperating and learning about the world around him. It all seems a little out of place to him; for example, everyone else seems to have little fluffy tails and floppy ears he seems bereft of. It doesn’t seem normal, but what does he know? He’s an amnesia trope, after all. Maybe he’s the weird one.Utawarerumono never, ever hurries. Instead, it patiently builds. Hakuowlo’s saviour turns out to be a timid young healer-in-training named Eruru, who is his main source of companionship while bed-bound, nagging him gently every time he overexerts himself. Slowly, he regains some strength and integrates himself with the village. He discovers how to get past Eruru’s younger sister’s severe stranger anxiety and carefully establishes perhaps his strongest bond throughout his tale. He helps cultivate the village’s farmland with knowledge he didn’t know he had, and is able to bypass problems with a sense of wisdom that even he is surprised by. He grows by helping the people around him and, as he grows, they grow. It could have been a simple, idyllic existence. But that was never meant to be.Slight things escalate. Diminutive enough that they barely register as an issue until they’ve become near insurmountable. The game’s first inkling of antagonists flirt at being stereotypes; the greedy lord who’s found his position in life due to nepotism rather than any particular skillset. His obnoxious son, who thinks his station in life gives him credence to do or take anything he pleases. Except, they’re rarely so two dimensional. The son, Nuwangi, used to live in the village, but his ascension into the noble ranks has rotted away his humble groundings. He wants to catch the eye of the girl he likes, but his mimicry of the corrupt ruling class sees his meaningless power trips take him further and further away from the person he used to be, and estranges him little by little from the affection he seeks. Confused, infuriated and heartbroken, he lashes out. There’s consequences. He can’t deal with them, and he makes things worse. People are forced to take action. Hakuowlo is forced to lead.
