_childDocuments_.review: Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen is the first game in a series of 3 visual novels which depicts a generation of heroes prior to the ones from Mask of Deception and Mask of Truth. It is a combination between a visual novel and a strategy turn based combat game and it lasts from 30 to 35 hours without any idling. Personally, this series is quite a rare find, since I am not usually a fan of visual novels, yet I spent 120 hours reading the whole thing without any real breaks except unavoidable stuff like sleep or chores. I guarantee that a lot of people that enjoy anime, yet don't like reading manga or visual novels will enjoy Utawarerumono regardless of their preferences. I forced a friend that I family share to play them and he loved the series just as much as I did. starts with Hakuowlo, an injured masked man that lost his memories, waking up in a village of friendly people treating his wounds. Those people shortly became his family and Hakuowlo did his part to keep the village on its feet over the threats that kept escalating. It is written in such a way that those challenges they have to face don't feel looped or repetitive unlike big animes such as Naruto or Fairy Tail, there is no "power of friendship" that magically change the flow of fights and, even if it involves some bits of unrealistic illogical evil, the point of view of some antagonists does make sense most of the time. It is a beautiful story that left me a bit sad and jealous over the protagonist's luck to meet such wonderful people.  is a remaster from the original pieces drawn in 2002, when anime was sharper and the shading was rougher, but this does not mean it is bad looking, just look at this:It does have the vibes of old anime, but it is more like a different artstyle rather than inferior quality. I have screenshot every single artwork from the utawarerumono series because I like them so much.Outside the VN interface, in the RPG side of the game, the graphics are not very modern. It involves chibi low-poly characters covered in small sized textures ps2 or ps vita like. I did not personally mind that and don't think it would be a good reason to miss on this game, but it could've been better.   is a mix between the classic Utawarerumono from 2002 and the other 2 ones, but it can be set to classic-only as well. It is calming and emotional, the notes mixed with the voice acting creating a great auditory experience. Moonlit Flower is my favorite one and it luckily appears in all of the 3 visual novels.The gameplay, except for pressing the advance button a million times, involves turn based strategy as stated at the beginning of the review. There are 2 difficulty modes and the normal one is easy enough not to frustrate anyone nor bore you to death. It involves controlling Hakuowlo and the characters that become allies along the story. The remastered version does not include the adult content that existed in the official release from 2002 since the developers decided to widen their target audience. There are no patches, this game is family friendly.Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen (and its 2 sequels), despite being quite pricy, are worthy visual novels that can be enjoyed by everyone, even people that are not into visual novels. Piece of art involving marvelous writing, visuals and sound.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game because I liked Mask of Deception (the 2nd game out of 3) a lot, but, on its own, as a starting point, this game isn't very good. It's  faithful of a recreation of older versions of this 2002 game (it's based on the 2006 ps2 remake). That includes the problems with the pacing and the combat system. Watch the anime adaptation instead; it's much shorter, in terms of the number of hours you're investing, and it actually does some scenes  than this VN. On top of that, all the parts involving fights are handled better in the show.The SRPG combat mechanics are much simpler, and less interesting, than in the sequels. The timed critical hit system is less rewarding so there's less reason to care about it, and the interplay between the skills the characters learn is far lower. Almost all the abilities are boring passive effects that don't do much (including on the paid DLC guest characters from the other games!). There are zero ways (well, almost zero; the DLC character Atuy is an exception) to get extra turns (eg. Zeal filling up or certain skills in Mask of Deception), and even worse, the basic attack chains have almost no interesting effects. In the sequels, basic attack chains can apply certain debuffs or even hit in various AoE patterns. Here, there are no inherent debuffs on attacks in a chain, and most non-team attacks just hit one tile. There's a lot less strategic depth here.My review is still positive just because this is the beginning of a really cool story. The whole series has really cool underlying secrets. They can't even be called plot twists—it's more like a deep rabbit hole.The presentation is great, too. The drawn backgrounds are vibrant, and the character designs are memorable and endearing. The voice acting across all three games is top notch, but this is more true in the sequels. Still, in Prelude to the Fallen, the characters are pretty unique and fun, and they mostly don't fall into boring archetypes.The music is excellent, but a lot of it comes from the sequels.I don't recommend buying the DLC characters. A couple of them are exceptionally good because of strong abilities, good movement range, good stat growths, and (for some) great attack range, but they aren't at all necessary (the exceptionally good DLC characters are Nosuri, Atuy, Sasara, Anju, and Mikazuchi). Even on hard mode, this game isn't challenging, except in the optional, hard-to-unlock postgame extra fight that requires you to unlock all items. Plus, a very notable weakness of the DLC characters is that they can't engage in "Co-op attacks" with other units. Only units from this game's story can do that, and co-op attacks are really powerful, with good status effects, the ability to hit multiple enemies, and great range.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't play this first. There are two other games in this series that were released before this for good reason. This game is technically a remake of the "earliest", but not a good game by today's standards. They didn't make it before the other 2 games for good reasons. Wouldn't really call it a remake either, as it's essentially the same as the actual remake the original got on ps2. Yes, ps2. 2006. So it wasn't exactly much work. But whatsoever.-The writing is very questionable. Flat characters, every villain is mad and throwaway, funny scenes in the middle of bloodshed interchanging with overly serious stuff that's hard to to care about.  On top of that, at the end the game basically throws everything away for reasons, which makes you wonder why it was there to begin with.-The gameplay isn't offensive for the most part, but also not very fun. Status Ailments like to annoy, and this game had the single worst srpg map I've ever seen. A map where (on highest speed) you had to choose "wait" for all your 11 characters for 10 minutes or so, nothing else. Don't know how that actually makes it into a commercial game.-The music is okay, but some of the voices aren't. Notably the protagonist's gets annoying. You CAN mute the protagonist exclusively, but that's a weird thing in itself as well.-The game doesn't like you to actually read fast, which, given the quality, can be quite annoying. Sound effects full stopping text advancing until they are over (and you will hear them A LOT, like slurping, tea pouring..), or several seconds long transitions everywhere. Reading the story can get quickly frustrating.If you enjoyed the other 2 games, this could be interesting for science. Honestly though? Expect nothing. Because there's nothing to be found here. The original was made with a low budget during times where people got very experimental with this medium in Japan. And yes, this is incredibly experimental, if you would've played the original version in 2002. But like many of its brethren from that time, the popularity came from them being fresh, doing new things, and not being actually well done and polished. (they didn't even have the budget to buy a reference book for stuff they were doing, and had to borrow stuff from the library repeatedly... tells you something). To reach that part of the game, you need to beat roughly 70-80% of it. Is it worth it today? For most people I don't think so.

This is a visual novel mixed in with some sequences that are like Final Fantasy Tactics/Ogre Battle, but not quite. _childDocuments_.review: A great story with excellent characters, only held back by some average gameplay and some potential pacing issues.+Story is great, really goes places, very good ending+Well-written and likeable characters the vast majority of the time+Flashy combat finishers look cool+Some absolutely top-tier voice acting, some lines or scenes have extremely memorable delivery+Great artwork+/-Some potential pacing issues, depending on personal taste. This story is heavy on slow-paced character interactions and world-building early on, then transitions to having longer unbroken serious story sequences with occasional breaks of more relaxed scenes, before finally just becoming heavy story sequence after sequence with no breaks or chance to access the base menu.-I thought some of the story moments suffered from the presentation, some scenes rather than just being written and voiced use the 3D battle models and attack animations as part of the story and at times this looked goofy to me, I think just text and voice acting might have been better for certain scenes.-The battles are WAAAAY too easy. I played on normal mode and I think there is a hard mode so some of this is on me but I didn't realise how easy it'd be. No risk of losing, almost no tactical thought required, for the entire game. I think this additionally hurts some of the storytelling; it takes me out of it if a fierce boss goes down in a couple attacks, or a cool enemy powers up and enters a second phase.... only to then die in a SINGLE hit (this happened to me)It took me a long time to get through this game due to both the pacing and the lack of difficulty making the combat not engage me. However, overall the story/characters are the focus and those are mostly excellent, I look forward to playing the sequels.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen

_childDocuments_.review: Remake of the original Utawarerumono, which is a considerably famous game among visual novel fans   A hybrid visual novel/strategy RPG, it is clearly a story-first game, and has a decent plot and an entertaining and likable cast of characters who are really the stars of the show here. While you will spend a decent amount of time battling, at least on Normal difficulty, there's never a reason to grind (though you can do so if you wish for some reason), and getting through the story stages is very easy    I'd say it's mostly not a particularly strong game by itself, but instead adds valuable background to the story of the next two games that will help you enjoy the story of those games to the maximum. While this may seem odd since this was originally a standalone game with no sequels, I feel that is how this game works best today in the presence of the "Mask of" games. So buy it if you plan to play the entire trilogy (or have already played the other two). Either this or Mask of Deception will work as a decent starting point to the series, but definitely do not touch Mask of Truth first. Personally recommend starting with Prelude over Deception     And as another very helpful reviewer has said, do not touch the DLC characters if you care about story and  have not played the other two games

_childDocuments_.review: Game is fantastic. Easily a 7/10 experience. There's a few things that drag it down though. Also, before I get too far, don't even bother looking at or touching the DLC characters. They are spoilers for the later games. They are very much there for people who have previously played the games before this remake came out.First of all, the game is very much a VN first and tactical RPG second. The battles very much feel like an after thought to make it more interesting. The battles are still really fun and interesting but just don't expect a ton of depth. This could be a plus or a negative to some. The game also requires a bit of grinding at times, which can feel like a drag, but the system they have for it is decent enough if you're used to grinding in tactical RPGs. Secondly, the story is fantastic. Is it kind of generic at times? Yeah a little bit but that's part of the fun. Just know that the story only continuously gets more and more interesting as it goes on. There are *a lot* of filler scenes though and some of the filler scenes just felt totally unnecessary at time or just very out of place. The out of place ones are edits from when the game was originally an eroge and for some reason, despite adding nothing to the story, they're still there and just feel completely random. However, as long as you're willing to power through them I promise you the story pays off. Third and finally, the art and sound are fantastic(sometimes). The original art is a bit dated, sure. But it still holds up and I think it's quite beautiful plus the newer re-designs are top tier. The music is on point and the sound design is uhh...interesting. Like many other VNs the sound effects used in game are super repetitive. As a fan of VNs, and someone not usually triggered by sounds, at times the over usage of certain sound effects drove me insane. It was so bad that I had to rush through scenes because I could not stand another moment of hearing said sound. Thankfully they were only in filler scenes so there really was not much lost.The game definitely has it's upsides and downsides but overall i'd say it was a good, maybe even great, game!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Worth going through despite my mixed feelings, just for the sake of setting up the world and some of the recurring characters for the next 2 games, Mask of Deception and Mask of Truth.When I started the Utawarerumono series with this entry and finished the game, I wasn't exactly impressed a whole lot. And now, after playing all 3 games, I'd say that this one is by far the weakest both in terms of story and in terms of gameplay as in both aspects it shows its age.At first I genuinely loved the story and getting introduced to the world throughout the first ~20 % of the game. But at a certain point, the pacing kinda takes a hit as the plot very quickly settles into a loop of quite formulaic mini-arcs varying in quality separated by tons and tons of pretty average, never ending SoL scenes. This continues until the final arc. What actually made me invested again a bit was the ending which I think was handled very well compared to the slog of the middle part of the plot. It even surprised me a little how it managed to make me care about some of the characters at the very end despite feeling exhausted from the pacing and despite the fact that many of the characters felt rather one-note.The gameplay is fine if you don't expect much considering this is primarily a VN. It has some interesting ideas but some of the mechanics (like damage based on positioning) and level design/layout made me feel like I was encouraged to use the same tactic and formation over and over. Which essentially meant creating chokepoints with tanks supported by a healer behind them while obliterating anything that got close with archers in the rear. Nothing in the game really challenged me to the point where I had to change this strategy considerably.While all of this may sound kinda negative and I even felt a bit "meh" after finishing this first entry of the series, I can confidently say that it is still very much worth it to go through this one just for the setup alone. And to be honest, finishing the next 2 games even made me retroactively appreciate this one a bit more, as they provide some relatively satisfying conclusions to some of the characters from this first game.

_childDocuments_.review: This strange word, Utawarerumono, translates roughly to English as "Those of whom legends are sung".The Utawarerumono trilogy provides powerful evidence to support the claim that creative fictional works published as computer software can attain the emotional and psychological complexity and depth associated with literature, the theater, or cinema. These are characters whom you come to know well, who stay with you long after completing the story. In short, they are genuinely memorable. Importantly, this is not because of reliance on cheap jabs designed to provoke a reflexive emotional response, but because of the depth of characterization the authors have achieved through time-honored methods, through patient, careful development and compelling narrative and dialog. Unusually, the series also uses the technique of internally-voiced thoughts, in effect, verbal thought balloons, spoken by the voice actors amidst live interaction occurring in the story. The emotional intensity and depth are also the result of the sheer length of the arcs the authors have developed across three titles, each of substantial length individually. We've all seen what's possible in an hour or two of screenplay. Imagine what's possible in a narrative work involving a couple of hundred hours of reader involvement!Appearing to be set in something resembling the Middle Ages in rural Japan, they plot explodes out of this presumptive setting, revealing itself to be a work of an entirely different genre. This is powerful stuff. Characters evolve over time. They develop. Some die. We are never spared from the impact of events, and nor, by the time they occur, would we wish to be. We come to care about these characters. As in life, things are not monochromatic. There's delightful humor, genuine warmth, real outrage, understandable anger, and sometimes, terrible shame over appalling secrets, all in aid of advancing a deep narrative tale, a legend, worthy of the name. Highly recommended! Well worth your time! Deeply engaging, never a chore to work through, always interesting, sometimes profound, consistently surprising. Utawarerumono is a unique, standard-setting demonstration of what can be achieved with this new story-telling medium by excellent writers, artists, voice actors, and musicians.

_childDocuments_.review: This one...really hurts.  Okay.  So, U:PTTF is not a bad game.  The story is more or less very similar to the original anime version, and it's a good story.  I would recommend it fine on that level.  I really, really wanted to see them redo the original arc in the modern art style, but...the polishing-up of the old art looked better than I'd hoped.  It's not bad.Where I run into difficulties here in recommending the story more widely is that...that's basically all this game did for me.  I was hoping that the game would expand on some of the things that were missing in the transition between this and U:MoD/MoT, like Fumirul, or giving an explanation for Kuon.  Both of these things, it sort of touched on, but then skimmed over very quickly, and did not actually complete the story connections.  Those plot threads felt half-baked and poorly connected, and I was really disappointed to see that the ending was more or less 100% the same as the anime, with nothing (or very little) expanded or added.  It's still a good story, but I wanted a little more to make the whole series cohesive.And then we reach combat.  It fundamentally shifts a few things from MoD/MoT, adding elements like facing and changing the 'quicktime' system, for lack of a better term, from being a critical hit system to adding zeal.  It's *fine.*  I like the facing element, actually, and I find the lack of it noticeable as I go back to replay MoD.  I think I prefer the critical hit system, though.The part that I really didn't like is that a lot of the combat felt...asinine.  It felt like they worked on the story elements, then realized at the last minute they needed to have combat levels too, and jammed stuff in so that they could say it was done.  Several missions were entirely "hit this one thing/these ten identical things for half an hour until they eventually die".  One mission literally had you just running over to a corner and waiting for fifteen minutes.  It felt like filler, and I never felt that way with the later games.  I also...maybe I was doing something horribly, horribly wrong xD but the spellcasters in this game never became useful in the slightest, and maxed out at piddling damage compared to the rest of everyone.TLDR: I love the Utawarerumono series, I love the story.  If you're more of a visual novel type than an anime type, then I think you can play through this absolutely fine and have a rewarding experience.  You'll just have to be patient through some lackluster tactical levels.  But, if you don't have a particular attachment to the visual novel experience, then I think...at this point, if I was advising a friend who was trying to get started in the series, I would recommend they watch the anime and skip this game.  And that's kind of where I'm at with this game as a whole.  It's not *bad*, but to me, it doesn't bring anything extra to the table, and it can be a bit of a bear to get through sometimes.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen

Change the difficulty to normal would save a lot of time.I also recommend the following similar Jrpg genres.1. Trails series. Also great story line and strategic combat.  It is highly recommended to start with Trails in the sky. The sky trilogy  resembles  this Utawarerumono in many aspects. _childDocuments_.review: Great Visual Novel - 8/10Pros:- Very immersive, easy to connect to the characters- Not hard to read in Japanese- Some of the battles are pretty goodCons:- Some filler content that can get annoying, but now that is over, I kinda miss those "days" where everything was calm and happy.- Late stage boss fights with different mechanics are pretty boring.- I didn't like the background story.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen

_childDocuments_.review: Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen is a pretty good game if you're into the visual novel genre and perhaps a good way to get into it if you haven't tried out the genre. There's a good mix of drama, humor, action, cuteness, and you probably will spend a small majority of the game going through the visual novel part. The story is linear so nothing to worry about in terms of saving and reloading to get the ending you want.It has a mix of turn-based tile/tactics/rpg battles thrown into the general text/music storytelling. Battles can be a little challenging but I think the average gamer can figure how to win the battles without thinking too hard. Replaying battles and playing training stages to get EXP, stat points, and items can be a tedious grind but not too bad in the first playthrough (there is a new game + if you want to replay the game after you beat it).First learned about the story watching the anime quite a few years ago, and enjoyed the way it was told and the world it presented alongside the characters. Discovered it was based on a visual novel and that got me to try it out. Compared to the anime adaptation, the original visual novel spends more time developing the characters so you get to know them better and the story. It doesn't just force you along and skip the small day to day interactions that make characters come to life like 23 minute episodes of anime do to try and wrap up story within however many episodes.As someone fluent in Japanese I would say the translations are alright but not the best. But the shortcomings with the translation isn't anything that would present a fatal problem to the story and being able to enjoy the game. Haven't had any crashes while playing the game but did experience some when browsing the bonus material (music, cg, etc.) after clearing the game. If you want to play the game in any of the supported languages, be sure you choose wisely, because the game files are basically re-downloaded again for that language. I have not tested whether or not the save files are compatible but switching the language setting had to be performed in the library (right click and go to properties and choose language), and is not done in-game.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen

_childDocuments_.review: I did not expect this story to be so emotionally stirring. The moment you gain something, something else is shortly taken away. The artstyle and setting of a feudal japan-esque world is profoundly charming and lovely. Both music and voice acting are top notch. The characters are all truly vibrant in their own way, which may be why getting invested in those characters can end up becoming a double-edged sword for the reader.I almost wish this story would have followed a more traditional VN "route" design. The characters are all lovely, so much so that you almost want to dedicate yourself to each of them individually. The gameplay was honestly nothing special, and could have been left out without really harming the final product, but it was certainly not bad either, and did not detract from the experience at all.Personal bias aside, this was a wonderful first installment to a fascinating world.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10Having been introduced to the Utawarerumono series through the anime, I finally get to experience the more detailed story through this game.story 7/10:The prelude is an interesting story, which started great with a mysterious masked person who has amnesia who tries to adapt to a world where strength is right and rises to power as a leader of a country for the people through resourcefulness, strategical brilliance, and camaraderie. This part of the story is like reading a well-paced book.Also all the people other than the protagonist have partial animal parts on them like animal ears and tails, but honestly, that part is pretty much flavor text and fan service.Then came the second part of the story ... which is some sort of sci-fi introduced at breakneck speed ...The pacing went haywire when the story  moved towards its conclusion, but since it's very spoiler-ish to talk about what happens, I'll just complain about things going too fast and crazy and made the finale not nearly as impactful as the chronological successors: mask of deception and truth.The game still presents a good story, but just not on the level of mask of deception and truth.gameplay 7/10:The meat of gameplay is in the tactical rpg element, where you prepare and field your group of companions on a tiled battlefield, as you deal with enemies in turn-based combat.The system is almost the same as the predecessors, but with characters of the prelude story, so it's still a good tactical turn based system that isn't too in-depth.The combat is engaging as you can watch your character perform ridiculously showy string of whoop-ass moveset on the enemies while trying to click on quick-timed mouse event in order to maximize the amount of zeal (Energy or adrenaline) gained through combat, which allows you to perform even more special attacks later.However, in this game, combat is too easy,  This is because the enemies do not become that much stronger as the game progresses, but your characters do become godly. In terms of escalation, your enemies progress in a boring way: they just have better stats. They rarely pull out any interesting new tricks on you ... as a matter of fact, end game enemies are just glorified meat-shields. At a certain point, you come across long and intimating boss introductions after which Oboro (one of your companion) pulls off his ridiculous special combo on the boss and ends up swiftly dispatching the said boss in a single action despite having disadvantageous elemental affinity ...Thus, we have an interesting tactical turn based system that lacks challenge ...Anyway, it's a good enough visual novel with ok gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game's main story but it has a pacing issue. The game starts off way too slow and there are parts of the story which don't really contribute to the main narrative but when the story picks up steam, it takes off like a rocket. The SRPG part of the game is ok, not bad but nothing groundbreaking. If you enjoy a long story and you don't mind a mediocre gameplay and a slow (but mostly good) build up to the apotheosis of the story, then I would recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite visual novels of all time. I was a bit hesitant at first since I wasn't really into the whole ancient Japan type setting, but I grew to love the cast and the worldbuilding was a lot more interesting than I first thought. The combat is sparse enough where I didn't get too annoyed with it and if you play on normal, the combat is fairly easy. The music, atmosphere, cast interactions, and plot felt amazing and overall this is a heavy recommend especially if you can pick it up on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen

_childDocuments_.review: Originally I was attracted to this game, or more specifically series on a whim.  I saw the game in the store and the characters felt very familiar to me, so I watched the series.  I loved it so much that I desired more so here I am, nearly reaching completion of the first of the trilogy of games, and it hasn't disappointed.  The games a little bit on the easier side but I still love it, the characters are all loveable and the story is great expanding on what I already know from the Anime, would very much recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen

_childDocuments_.review: Given the all age version was first released in 2006, I found the game is still enjoyable. Coming from the anime, I would say if you enjoy the anime, you would probably like the game. The plot is 90% similar to that of the anime with a little more details not given in the anime. You would recognize many of the same dialogues from the anime.I got it for around $20 USD when it was on sale and feel $20-30 would be a reasonable price range to get the game.Pros:- Excellent voice acting- Nice 2D graphics- Quite an amount of play time (took me 47 hrs to complete everything)- Battles are quite fun- Great soundtracks (in fact I went from soundtracks -> anime -> game)- Content rich (feels like the developers put in an effort to make it good)Cons:- 3D graphics is showing its age (still playable tho)- Gives you too many items when you can only equip 1 item + 2 consumables, should have made it 2+2- Kind of slow if you are not used to visual novel (which I am not)Overall, I would give the game a 7/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen

_childDocuments_.review: Though not the best, it's my favorite VN. While the route is linear and you can't make any choice, the story is still great and emotional. The gameplay is not very hard but you can increase the difficulty after clearing the game. For your 1st play, get through the "RPG" part as quick as you can and enjoy the story slowly
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen

_childDocuments_.review: So far i'm really enjoying this game, it definitely shows its age a bit but the story is really quite gripping. Only negative I would say is that it doesn't look great on my 4K screen and I have to play it in a window to make it look alright. It's not a deal breaker and definitely understandable given how old the game is, but so far really overjoyed to have picked up this title and can't want to work my way through the trilogy. Truly a gem of a game.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen

_childDocuments_.review: More of a visual novel with a strategy game for intermissions, this is a very enjoyable game and lead me to grab the other two games in the trilogy (which were strangely released before this). The strategy game is turn-based with RPG elements so characters gain levels and you have control over how to build characters. This has the advantage that if you are poor at strategy games then you can repeat levels you have already finished to build up your characters but do not need to do so. As the story segments are very long, I found myself grinding between battles when I started getting tired of the story segment.The story is interesting and does a good job of building up the characters though the story segments make up the bulk of the playing time and tend to be a bit too long for me (though, you can do what I did and replay levels).  Most of the characters do make guest appearances in the sequels, but are mostly contained to this story. Playing this game before the other two games will prevent spoilers and will make the sequels a bit more enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen

_childDocuments_.review: I've played the original one which is sadly not running on modern PCs and it would be nice to have the original available but this is definitely the superior version. I'm still looking for another VN like this (or it's two sequels) and I'm hoping we'll get another installment in this epic series. For lovers or great world-building 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the trilogy and, oh boy, what a ride. But about this game in particular:Story is great, world buiding is very unique and detailed, characters are really lovable and it combines a lot of diferent elements from various genres.The port has some issues, yes, but nothing unforgivable. You will find some outdates CGs here and there but Amazuyu Tatsuki's older and newer art is both great imo, Music is super folk-y and epic, but after 3 VNs, it might get somewhat repetitive if you don't love it like I do.You don't need to play this one to enjoy MoD and MoT but I highly recommend it. You might miss out on character backstories and subtle references in the future.I played a lot of visual novels up to this this point, but the Utawarerumono trilogy has earned a place in my heart. I really felt immersed in this universe and I really loved every character. Give it a go!
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen

_childDocuments_.review: I actually played the PC version of this game. I miss the R18+ contents but this games also shines on its own regardless. I already forgot what took place in the game since it has been more than a decade since I last played it, but I do not remember seeing  it this polished with 3D art and mechanics. I think the old one was a bit more difficult compared to this. I played in hard mode from the very start and I didn't  had that much difficulty, In any case, I  would honestly say this is a good buy, especially when the trilogy is on sale. I haven't had this much fun playing a VN for ages until now.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen

_childDocuments_.review: Largely just good until the last act, despite obvious vestiges of having originally been an eroge. Ended with a fantastic conclusion that re-contextualized the entire plot. Great OST/VA. Fun SRPG, but not much depth. Worldbuilding is good, but hampered by the episodic structure that makes it feel like places are being created piecemeal, rather than having existed all along. 9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen

_childDocuments_.review: Prelude to the fallen is the first entry in the Utawarerumono Visual Novel Trilogy, and follows a protagonist named Hakuowlo who was found unconcious in the woods with no recollections of his memories. This is one of the best visual novel around because of the music, characters, and story. As the story goes Hakuowlo's memories slowly comes back and made significant to the story. The characters are all very enjoyable and unique there is no way anyone could hate on any of them. Although this Visual Novel is listed as 30+ hours long, i can safely say that its atleast 40+ hours long so keep that in mind. All the time spent on this VN is a time well spent Very Reccomended and the sequels in this trilogy only gets better and better
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen

_childDocuments_.review: I didnt played the old version of the game but i did watch the anime years ago, i remembered 2/3 of the game except the very last part of the story which is the most important. It took me 55 hours to have all the achievementsPositives :-A lot of different and enjoyable characters, mostly females, with differents personalities and backstory-Good story, univers and atmosphere : its a mix of drama, slice of life, war and fantasy in a sort of medieval japan. The last quarter of the game is very good storywise.-The OST variety : 100 musics in total from the trilogy games. It was not repetitive at all and some of the tracks are very good.-They keep the artworks of the old game but with better resolution/colors. They're pretty good, sad there isnt more of them.Negatives :-Difficulty is not existent even on hard mode, so the last third of the game was borring during the gameplay, im glad that the story and the characters are very good enough to keep me playing this game. The only map with a bit of difficulty is the bonus one. -Pacing between gameplay and VN is a bit off. Most of the time it's like this : hours of VN non stop, 4-5 battles then VN again etc...-The game is locked at 30fps, its kinda fine since the game is motly a VN with a bit of basic SRPG but come on its 2021...
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 amazing story the game play is kinda meh but the game is mostly light novel anyway which as the first time playing a light novel i came into it very skeptical but i found myself being told a very human down to earth story and i started looking forwards to the evening i could wind down sit down and just listen to a good narrative and take everything in at my own pace.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen

_childDocuments_.review: Utawarerumono is a visual novel with a gripping plot, charming characters, and a world that I've found myself really immersed in. The tactical rpg battles while a bit basic compared to some contemporary tactical rpgs, is still fun and mixes it up a bit with unique battle win conditions, rather than simply route the enemy. I have probably played less than half the game so far, but I highly recommend the game to any anime/VN/tacticalrpg fans
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen

_childDocuments_.review: Utawarerumono is a VN/SRPG hybrid game, that is really well crafted in almost every regard, I have yet to play the sequels but if they hold up to this quality, and hell i've heard they're even better. Then i'm gonna be in for a massive treat. This game made me happy, it made me sad, it made me angry, it made me happy again, then tore my heart out and told me to DEAL WITH IT. It made me cry and I rarely cry at games. The SRPG combat is surprisingly great despite the VN focus, and fights don't take 5 hours to get to like say oldschool Sakura Wars. The characters are wonderful, I was pulled into this damn world and it won't let go. I'm stuck for life.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen

_childDocuments_.review: Figured I'd leave a first-impression review because it's on sale. I'm not actually 4 hours in, more like 2.5 hours and 1.5 hours idling in the background.I got all three titles in the bundle even though I usually don't pay this much for games because I figured that if I was going to be disappointed, I was going to be disappointed on an epic scale, damn it.So far it's a really nice visual novel! Artwork is nice. Sound is nice. Translation is really polished. I'm enjoying learning more about the world. This feels similar to Senren Banka, so far, but that's probably just because it's a common story with common archetypes. Nevertheless, I like this sort of thing, so it's up my alley.One thing that I don't like so far is the lack of choice in the VN portions. You can choose which location to go to next, but you're going to all of them anyway, so it's really not much of a choice.I've only been in one battle so far so I can't say whether this is like the Holy Grail of FFT. I'm guessing not and that the SRPG parts are more tacked-on, but it might increase in depth as I go on.Anywhoozle, I'm going to keep playing/reading, which is nice because there was every possibility that this could have completely tanked for me in the first hour or two. So, if you're on the fence, you've got this positive first-impression review plus a ton of other reviews from people who have played a bit more. Happy gaming!Edit: After playing this for about 20 hours, it has pretty much lost its charm for me. I'm not saying that it's a bad story, it's just too slow-paced to keep me interested and the characters are decent but not memorable like, say, the characters of Disco Elysium, or Planescape: Torment, or Final Fantasy 7. I guess what I'm trying to say that it's average, perfectly serviceable writing, but there's so much average, perfectly serviceable writing. And the combat isn't like FFT or even as much fun as some of the indie tactics games here like Fell Seal: Arbeiter's Mark. So there's a lot of average combat.And, most disheartening of all, there are no choices in the VN. It's kinetic. Completely on rails.So I'm going to cut my playthrough short for now, but keep my positive recommendation, because it's not a bad game. I can see its appeal. For me though, it's just not a great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game.Maybe a bit too easy, even on the HARD difficulty, but totally worth playing for the plot.It's beautiful, nostalgic, complex, sad, romantic and a million other things. It's a really well-crafted plot.The only downside of the plot is that it is a bit slow to take flight, being filled with events with no real meaning. But do not be discouraged, play it until the end and you will certainly feel rewarded.
_childDocuments_.name: Utawarerumono: Prelude to the Fallen

_childDocuments_.review: Prelude to the Fallen follows the story of a young man with no memories who awakens in a strange world, and is taken in by a tribe of kindhearted villagers. He is raised as one of their own, eventually receiving the name "Hakuowlo." When neighboring nations begin to encroach on his village, Hakuoro rises up against the tyrannical invaders, setting off on an unforgettable journey that lives on in the songs of legend.

name: Chorus
detailed_description: Take control of Nara, once the Circle’s deadliest warrior, now their most wanted fugitive, on a quest to destroy the dark cult that created her. Unlock devastating weapons and mind-bending abilities in a true evolution of the space-combat shooter. Along with Forsaken, her sentient starfighter, explore ancient temples, engage in exhilarating zero-g combat, and venture beyond our waking reality. A JOURNEY OF REDEMPTION Lead Nara, an ace pilot facing her haunted past, and Forsaken, her sentient ship. Their quest for redemption will take them across the galaxy and beyond the boundaries of reality, as they fight to unite resistance forces against the Circle and their leader, the Great Prophet, at all costs. VENTURE BEYOND THE VOID Enter a dark new universe, teeming with mystery and rife with conflict. Explore epic locations such as sprawling space stations and strange planes of existence beyond our own. Engage in exhilarating zero-g dogfights from epic cosmic vistas to tight crystalline corridors. Chorus balances the scale and spectacle of space exploration with frenetic, fast-paced action. ONE PILOT, ONE SHIP, ONE LIVING WEAPON Attain powerful and distinct weapons and combat upgrades. Master your ship’s unique drift mechanic and deadly mind-bending abilities, including extra-sensory perception, teleportation and telekinesis, to overcome massive hordes of enemies and take down titanic battleships. Chain your powers together to become the ultimate living weapon. FEATURES A compelling single-player experience Play as dual protagonists Nara and her sentient AI companion and starfighter, Forsaken, on a personal journey of redemption Experience fast-paced, frenetic action that evolves the spirit of classic space shooters Fight to unite resistance forces against the Circle and their ominous leader, the Great Prophet Face down hordes of enemy starfighters, titanic battleships and unknown Void entities Reclaim, upgrade and wield devastating weapons and abilities in zero-g dogfights Explore a dark new sci-fi universe, teeming with mystery and conflict Enjoy gorgeous next gen sci-fi visuals in 4K, from cosmic vistas to sprawling space stations

_childDocuments_.review: 🔵Space based 3rd person combat game with excellent story + background mechanics.🔵Soundtrack is magnificent (Hollywood standard).🔵Progressive story led gameplay.🔵I could not get past the controls; needs HOTAS & an advanced flight model.✔️Looks fantastic✔️Audio is fantastic✔️Soundtrack is Really fantastic.✔️Voice acting fluctuates but is Mostly decent or better.✔️Environments are spectacular.✔️Upgrades, loadouts and ship variety are decent.✔️Emotionally fuelled story keeps you pushing forwards.❌No HOTAS Support.❌Flight Model is clunky and restrictive (No Yaw and no Reverse).❌Tracking enemies and objectives can become confusing.❌No Multiplayer Co-Op❌No first person cockpit view.❌1660ti @4K stutters in combat.⭐Soundtrack + Game Audio + Graphics💡HOTAS SUpport💡Advanced Flight Model for more advanced players looking for more realism.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm eight hours in and I absolutely LOVE this game. It's original, the soundtrack is epic, it has great narrative and character dynamic (especially with the two main characters), and it has solid gameplay which has the best space fighter combat that I've ever experience yet (though you'll have to be patient until you unlock all three weapon types and find Nara's friend, Forsaken). What ever price you pick this up on, it's worth it. My thanks goes out to the developers!
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: At first i was like - when i skip all these cloned side-missions and close my eyes around "memories" then i still have fun... But then i realised that i just skipping like 80% of the game. Why play the game like this? And then i dropped it.*whispers* Played it with a mouse/keyboard without any major problems and i am pretty clumsy in this type of games.*whispers* *softly* Farewell, my friend...
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: I just played through the entire game, and let me tell you I still have no idea what the plot was about, but it doesn't really matter. The insanely fun star ship battles and talking spaceship made it worth every second. I hope the development studio never stops making similar genre games. I'd like to see another game in a completely different universe tell a different story but with similar mechanics. 8/10 best space game yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Quite a challenging game, adventurous story that defines science fiction futuristic game play.  Fantastic graphics and responsive to the players moves with a quickly adaptive graphics AI system and much more to discover.  Reminds me of Skyrim with the 3-d graphics adaptivity and the sound quality.  Feels very real and again, responsive to the players controls.   So far, I am impressed and feel that the dollar per hour is well spent.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: This is terrible. There is no story, no reason for what you are doing. There is no gradual ramp up to gameplay. You just fly around and get your ass kicked until you figure how the systems work and even then it just isn't any fun.  I'm an hour into the game and I still have no idea why I am here, what this "cult" is, what they believe, why they want to kill the other people, etc. This should have been on early access, not a finished product. I am returning it right now.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: While the game play is nicely bug free, and the graphics solid i can not recommend this game.  The AI ships have a habit so zipping out of view and then suddenly vanish, and reappear behind you shooting you from behind.  The AI ships also reacts instantly to your mouse movement, instead of a slight delay after you fire.  The lack of an assisted aim tool made fights more tedious then fun.  Even when you used the hunt ability to get behind ships they would instantly shield in behind.  The first boss fight after entering the void turn out to be uncompleteable even on easy difficulty.  Although there are no timed missions in the game some of the chalanges require good timing which some people just don't have.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: A solid, straightforward space shooter with an uplifting, if imperfectly delivered message. It's mostly story oriented, with some RPG-style progression, but it didn't feel like the build variety was terribly dramatic. Before the end of the story I had my ship maxed out as far as I could determine the game would allow me to, just from doing most of the side activities available to me.You are effectively playing as Darth Vader if they had chosen to join the rebels after a moral crisis.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: - 3rd person only space shooter (you're in a ship 100% of the time)- You stay in the same ship for 90% of the game, no changing ships as you like, and no cosmetics to the ship.- Heavy story emphasis: I was surprised at how engaging it was actually- Abilities, basically magic make the combat very fast and fun when you get used to it. - 100% achievements require a bit of extra effort, but I 100% it at 20 hours.Don't sleep on this one, it's an unexpected treat.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: I overall enjoyed Chorus, but just barely. I am a sucker for space shooters - grew up with X-Wing: Alliance and its ilk - and the combat gets my thumb up. It's exciting, tough without being impossible, and spiced up by the unusual addition of your pilot having essentially magic powers that she can use to even the odds even when vastly outnumbered. The game also must have taken a cue from Star Wars (and Return of the Jedi in particular) because it's chock full of high speed runs in narrow twisty tunnels and capital ships that you need to take down by flying inside and destroying their power reactor. I love that stuff, to those are the pros.The cons are that this game could have been perfect if it had added some kind of rogue-like endless battle mode with increasingly hard hordes of enemies, and instead all it has is a story mode, which wouldn't even be such a big deal if the story wasn't so... ugh. Every voice actor sounds like they're constantly on the verge of an emotional breakdown as they deliver this ponderous tale of a woman who committed a pretty big war crime and has since defected from the cult she used to fight for to help those resisting it. And the tale is delivered via "memories", which are essentially in-game unskippable interactive cutscenes, which you have to go through again, and again, and again, for the whole damn campaign as well as most side quests. The story to me was just uninteresting, and its extremely dour tone also made it dull.The game looks and sounds really cool; the various systems are all very distinct and provide a variety of unusual space environments. Really, the forced narrative was the only negative for me. Still, this is definitely worth a sale price if you like space fighting games (and feel confident about tackling one that has a bit more teeth to it).

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty cool short-and-sweet spaceship game about essentially a sith lord turning to the light and saving the world through having loads of grandiose dogfights made all the more epic and unique due to the inclusion of force powers! While I felt like the game was a little unfocused with some unnecessary open-world elements that drag the pacing down, I'd still consider it a big recommendation for people that are tired of the usual space dogfights and want some more spice added to them!PROS*Very dramatic and compelling story about redemption that's short and sweet, being able to get a complete experience in about 12-15 hours: fun to watch the main characters grow*Great combat design that's much more interesting than your typical endless circling and firing missiles you see in other space dogfighting games: a very diverse cast of enemies forces you to use everything in your toolset from your weapons to your force powers like drifting, teleporting, lightning, dodging and more to win*Incredibly epic scenarios and setpieces like crippling capital chips from the outside before flying into them to blow out their cores, trench runs, tunnel chases, as well as crazy boss battles against gigantic eldritch colossiCONS*Certain aspects of the story feel underdeveloped: some characters become your allies with very little resistance, some plot points that you think would come up later are dropped, culminates in your typical 'balance' and 'believe in yourself' philosophy 101 cliches*While the game has some incredible highs for its combat scenarios, these can be few and far-between the many easy-peasy scenarios that come up alongside just tedious flying around to get to the next objective: my patience grew thin at some points*Underdeveloped systems like ship customization, upgrades, side-quests and collectibles feel very token, like the game was originally going to be a big open-world but then they scrapped it half-way but still left it in: would much prefer a more straight-forward well-paced adventure than this game which lets a lot of superfluous fluff get in the way

_childDocuments_.review: Full of fun space dog-fights set in the beautiful backdrop of a terribly tedious universe. Recommended, if on sale.The good:Flying around looks and feels great. While very simple in its control scheme, everything about traversal and combat feels exciting and weighty. The (very small) collection of ship weapons and powers, while limited in variation or originality, are fun to use. The game performs wonderfully, and has plenty of individually beautiful moments. The BadBY ALL THAT IS HOLY THE STORY-LINE IS TEDIOUS. The (beautiful) setting is very limited in scope. There are only a few maps which you will need to trudge back and forth to over, and over, and over, and over again. You will revisit the same handful of locations and characters for the same few quest types. It feels a bit like the entire game is just one long tutorial sequence for flying your ship that an edgy teen stapled a story to at the last minute. The story and quests are not fun. They aren't motivating. They should not be the reason you buy this game. You should buy this game to have a few fun hours of pulling awesome space acrobatics and blasting pirates to dust with magic space-wizard powers.

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly, i can't reccomend Chorus.The Base is all there. Its somewhat solidly built and the gameplay loop is okay - But everything about it screams "B-GAME".The game is "OK" but you will repeatedly get reminded that it, like nearly every game nowadays, is unfinished or at least badly playtested. Granted, its not as bad as most other titles on the market.Major complaints:- The AOE, oh, the AOE damage effect. I refuse to believe that the developers played their game and thought. "yes, this is fine." It not only distorts your screen so intensely that you can barely see what you are doing, it also makes your vision nearly black and white - when all damage telegraphs, your charge beam visual que and enemy hit zones are colour coded. I CAN'T understand how this gets trough playtesting. This single screen effect got me killed collectively about 25 times on the same 2 occasions where you Can. Not. See. what you are supposed to to.-The objective markers are very small, fade out (??) and appear only 5-10 seconds after a conversation has ended you so just idle in space not knowing where you have to fly next until it appears.- Difficulty spikes MASSIVELY with me having to switch difficulty to medium on the first big boss due to there seemingly not being enough time to burst him down until his global DOT kills you. Feels like it was not playtested.- Same can be said against normal enemies where some that are clearly introduced as hard enemies can be killed within 1-2 seconds flat with your powers, while the normal, base enemy fighter, remains dangerous into lategame. Others feel like crazy bullet sponges.- Capital ships are so laughably easy to kill that a fight gets considerably easier if one spawns in.- The charge attack is what kills you 80% of the time, since the timing window for dodge is small and the visual que is very, very bad. If you fly up the camera blocks most of the visual que as well. Great design.- Starting with midgame, nearly 50% of enemy ships have said broken charge beam attack. There is also another enemy that has an attack that uses the same visual effect for its attack minus the visual que, making you spend your dodge sometimes just to be killed by the real charge beam.- A lot of the fights that randomly spike in difficulty that you fail over and over again, you suddenly win even though you did not change your tactics whatsoever, leaving you with the feeling that its just RNG if you get charge beam attacked in a bad moment and die due to that. Some even being over in 2 minutes when before you spent double that and half the enemies where still alive when you died.- It's normal that your allies do nothing in games, but in this game the trope is pushed to the max with your enemies ignoring them 100% of the time except on certain "protect" missions and you killing 100% of enemy ships. There is also almost no radio chatter so you even "feel" alone even in big fights.- Ship upgrade system is there just so the game can say it has one. - 90% of side missions feel like heavy runtime padding. All this can be patched out. And with some basic issues fixed, i feel like this game is definitely fun. Right now you get your fun tainted again and again by the issues mentioned above.

_childDocuments_.review: Chorus is an arcade space shooter with a focus on its narrative. It has an open world you can explore and traverse, but it's no Freelancer. Trading is nonexistent. The game gives you one ship, three weapon types with several variants as well as up to four "rites" - spells, basically - to play with. Being a space shooter, pressing and holding a button allows you to maintain your momentum as you spin around to shoot enemies behind you. The focus clearly is on flying, shooting and using this game's flavor of space magic, and the game does those things really quite well in my opinion. It is adept at making you feel good about the maneuvers you pull off.The narrative's presentation focuses heavily on the main character to the point of her being practically the only animated human being. It is evident that a significant proportion of the game's budget was put into her, similar to how the portrayal of Senua in Hellblade was a major focus of that game. Both games share a distinctly double-AA feeling. Chorus' characterization of Nara does not reach the same level of quality, unfortunately, but it does offer the main character a sidekick she can bounce off of.I liked my time with the game. Combat was highly enjoyable, exploration and traversal of the open maps was fun. The narrative is a bit esoteric for my taste, but that does not detract from this being a good game. My, as of the time of me writing this, 17 hours in the game amount to me finishing the story and doing practically all side content. I have no desire to replay it anytime soon, but I don't regret paying full price for the time I got out of it. It certainly is refreshing to finish an open world game without having to spend several dozens of hours. Discounted, I'd consider it a hidden gem. If you're on the fence about the game, try the demo.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all -- I do not agree with the hatred this game gathers. Now to the story and actual review.When I was on my early teens I picked a game from sale basket among few others. The game casket read as "Freelancer". Yeap you might already know where I am going here. Freelancer is the game which was groundbreaking in every layer when it came out and even when it's been two decades people still remember and refer it in almost every single time when some new action-spaceflight sim has been released.So did I got the successor for the legendary game? No, but I got Chorus!! The game is just incredible cinematic piece, with great protagonist Nara who evolves throughout the story as a pilot but also as a character. You also meet numerous side characters among companion Forsa who fights with you throughout the game. After tiny linear tutorial the current system is freely to be explored and there is numerous side quests, which are not achieved on space stations but by exploring the environment. Making money as merchant or miner is not an option in this, but several quality side quests compensate that in my opinion. Chorus is strictly battle based, but dogfights are always great fun! There is also many random encounters with different factions to make money, which you use to upgrade your shield defenses and weaponry. There is 3 types of weaponry and while there might not be so much variation the Chorus has another feature in its arsenal.Nara gets access into the Rites, magical abilities to deal with enemies and further you proceed the more of them you get. Nara also collects experience with rites and weapons and this should courage you to try different tactics to deal with enemies for all bonuses are significant and by adapting and learning you are able to do much cool stuff especially in the second half of the game.Speaking of the end game the ending was a true example how to conclude the story! The final minutes the game turned to be a bullet hell in a good way, but what did take the cake was the few last cutscenes - my skin legit went goosebumps and emotions kicked in! I had my expectations low for some games fail to give that final blow, but Chorus scored and for the good!After 18 long hours of flying and shootings I grant that Chorus can be a little bit repetitive and there is few aspects that are left simple. The playing with magics might not be everyone's cup of tea either, especially if one waits more factual setting. However I liked it and fell in love with it!Meet me... in Chorus.

_childDocuments_.review: Space shooters have become quite rare these days and when you see one that is able to catch your attention and guide you through its mysterious and fascinating narrative, you can only try to do your best to highlight its positive aspects. In Chorus you won’t find a space simulator, but a fantastic story-driven space opera.The protagonist, Nara, is an elder space pilot who was once part of a cult known as the Circle, which dominates the galaxy with its supreme power. Tormented by her past, she is now fighting the Great Prophet of the cult in search for redemption. This journey will lead her on a mission to free Forsaken, a sentient and powerful ship that she abandoned soon after leaving the Circle.As you explore many beautiful open environments, you will fight hordes of space pirates, cultist ships and alien forms that are threatening the galaxy. The quality of the lore is exceptional and you really feel like being part of a dangerous, yet believable, universe. Unfortunately, there isn’t a codex explaining everything in detail, but you can get a lot of info from residual memories and (long) dialogues with numerous NPCs.Visually, the game reminded me of  for often showing red twisted geometries and surreal moments. Just like Jesse Faden before (or Senua from ), Nara constantly speaks to herself and you can always hear her thoughts being whispered during dialogues, which greatly enhances her fears, doubts and motivations. Nara and Forsa are obviously the main stars of the game and their relationship is what keeps the narrative always interesting. There are also many other secondary characters, but they don’t have enough screen time to stand out on their own. Except for a few, the supporting NPCs are easily forgettable.That said, the game does an impressive job at keeping the focus on the plot. Even when you are doing one of the many side missions, you are always reminded of the ongoing main events. Initially, you can even find some optional missions that allow you to take a few interesting moral choices; sadly they are soon replaced with more linear ones filled with generic tasks such as escorting allies, rescuing civilians, retrieving cargos, freeing outposts etc. which are still kept acceptable thanks to the great focus on storytelling. You can’t win battles alone and Forsaken will not only be your friend, but your deadly spaceship. You will encounter many types of enemies and each one needs to be dealt by using a different tactic. The combat in Chorus is always quick and spectacular thanks to smooth manoeuvrability and the implementation of Rites. Through them, Nara can learn new abilities like drifting, teleporting behind enemies or boosting at the speed of light; abilities that are extremely important not only during combat, but also for completing a few puzzles and trials. Progressing through the story will give you access to more rites and upgrades, expanding the range of combat possibilities and making you feel in complete control of your spaceship. While there are only three type of weapons you can use (laser, gatling gun and missiles), you can find or buy different types of ammo and mods that affect their stats and aesthetic. Combining weapons and rites is fun and always encouraged as it is the only way to increase your level of mastery.Graphically the game looks quite good with some pretty weapons effects and explosions. The map is open and you can move freely where you want, with new different areas unlocking as you progress with the story. Looking back at it now though, I can’t recall any particular location. There are definitely some breathtaking visuals, but I feel like this galaxy was too static and missing iconic locations while some (like the Resistance HQ) could have been done better. Maybe there were also some budget limitations during the development, because you can see that Nara is the only character appearing during the well animated cutscenes when she is often confronting herself or other faceless models.Sound design and voice acting are brilliant, while the main soundtrack by Pedro Macedo Camacho (featuring Úyanga Bold) is one of the best I ever heard in a videogame and it perfectly fits the sci-fi theme while being tribal and evocative.Chorus brings attention back to epic narrative in space shooters and it does that without forgetting about the importance of gameplay, which is always fun and spectacular. It took me around 20 hours to complete the main story and all secondary missions at standard mode, but you can expect more if you increase the difficulty, although the game doesn’t offer any special reward for that (like better loot or a rare achievement). The challenge in standard mode is still guaranteed, with a few spikes during some more intense moments and boss fights. For some reason you can’t save during main story missions, which means that, before quitting the game thinking it auto-saved, it’s best to check the time of the last save or you might lose some progress.

_childDocuments_.review: A great game!  Takes a bit of time to warm up to, but the powers you get for your ship soon turn the combat into a dream.  Most fights tended towards being slightly too easy, but nothing ever felt tedious.  The final boss battle is a banger and well balanced - I felt like I was on the edge of failure right at the end.  The levels are simply gorgeous as well, which helped to immerse me in the world.  It seems there was a clear effort to make the game similar in style to open-world games like Witcher III, but then replacing people with space ships (for example, entire space ships are direct stand-ins for individual people in most instances).  Mechanically, this means the game has been designed for a lot of wandering, talks, and exploration to find quests.  I think they almost pulled it off, but it possibly would have been better as a linear campaign to keep the energy level up.The story does require you to make some inferences and fill in the blanks.  It's not the best, but it's fine.  The whole idea of an space cult is fantastic, and they strive for the golden mantra of "show, don't tell."  That being said, it could have been improved by more context in certain scenes.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Remember playing Star Fox 64 when it came out and having an absolute blast? Pick this game up and experience that joy all over again, 24 years later. You can even do the aileron roll (what the game incorrectly called a "barrel roll"). Remember watching Knight Rider? Or, seen the movie Stealth? Pick this game up so you can pilot a ship with an attitude. Want to drift a spaceship by transforming it into a "Drift Machine"? Pick this game up so you can do just that.Combat is engaging, graphics are beyond stunning, the little details are well done, the controls are fluid and tight as a drum, the story is fun and engaging, and the open world is so much fun to explore and find hidden items and quests.HOWEVER, where there is good, there is also bad. Several things that come to mind that you'll possibly find annoying would be the constant whispering inner dialogue that goes on. For the first hour or two, you won't think it's that bad, but give it time and it'll start to get on your nerves. It also doesn't come across as natural at times and feels disjointed versus plausible. (Supposedly, the developer actually responded to this complaint in a discussion thread and their response resembled that of a teenager texting; didn't bother capitalizing where they should've and failed to use punctuation correctly. This may not seem like a big deal to some, but to others how they respond can give you one impression or another. Personally, if I was a developer of a pretty good game and wanted to be perceived as someone who takes it seriously and professionally, I wouldn't use the writing skills of a middle-schooler. I mean, c'mon, it doesn't require a lot of effort to write a coherent sentence.)Another issue with the game would be how some missions might not make it so easy to see where you're supposed to go next or what to do. This is rare but one glaring example would be the mission where you have to escape The Guilt: you have to escape it and around the second or third time running away from it you're forced to a red barrier but there is no real hint as what to do. I got stuck/killed every time for the first 6 times I replayed it, only finally getting past the red barrier. Problem is that I had no idea what I did to do so; I was just randomly mashing buttons and trying to go in all sorts of directions while The Guilt was slowly killing me.And, the last thing I can think of is that the traveling long distances (even with "hyper-drive" engaged) can get tedious and boring, especially if you have to do it back and forth with no real form of fast-travel. There IS fast-travel but it's to whatever Space Jump portal you've come in on.All in all, even though it has some issues, which every game has, it's still a fun game to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Considering this is a somewhat Woke game, cobbling some odd things together and with some obvious creative deficiencies it has potential. As hostile as Woke is to people such as myself I'm not so objectionable to it when it's their own games and in this case I'm not certain to what degree it's intended. It's obviously for a female audience in one shape or form and is melding two disparity styles.What it's trying to do, well it's either not entirely possible or usually quite niche. Feminist theory just isn't based on reality which means that it tends to mischaracterise things that don't work as things that should work. If you're conversely doing something such as making a product for females who like something like fast cars that's always going to be a narrow primary audience. This game almost does fairly well in spite of that in that it had the potential to still appeal somewhat to a more general audience. You can get away with a lot so long as the gameplay is there and a few other of the basics are intact. You can put up with a few things not being to your liking but then there is sometimes just too much.This is where the game falls short, on the other areas. I could still enjoy the game just not taking the story line, bad acting, cliche, cheesiness and cringe too seriously nor heeding it much attention. Perhaps gaining some entertainment from laughing at it. There are various UX/QoL issues and bugs (it's hard to tell) to the point that it fails to pass muster. It always irritates me when I see this in gaming. It just takes one person to do one play through to pick up on most of this stuff.There are quite a few issues with bad timing. The decision to use a ground based plane mechanic for a space game is frustrating. Then there is picking up rites remnants and either due to a bug (perhaps opening the menu at the same time) or due to a lack of it telling you everything you've got there's no obvious bonus from it. Having no separate markers for scan and things like loot is extremely irritating. Then you have things such as you save a civilian, you finish and there is chatter which would indicate the conclusion of the encounter but as you leave it fails the mission. At least some of these things are quite easy to fix. It gives the impression of rushing it to wrap things up in the end. I have noticed another toxic tendency to over simplify in product design these days. Perhaps this contributes to some of the issues. I'm not sure.Either way this lack of proper polish is really too much for me. It's compounded by an apparent lack of information where it's needed. I would suggest releasing some basic documentation in future at least, perhaps putting up information on a standard wiki or something, there are a few out there.

_childDocuments_.review: Although I really liked the story and the character it borrows heavily from hellblade in its presentation (which i'm not a fan of)  I liked the story of the main character but the whispering narrative seems one dimensional, however the lead voice female voice actor is excellent. Presentation is big budget for a AA game it has impressive art and character design as well. The open world aspect is half baked and it lacks the  economic depth of a traditional sandbox space game which was in the developers roots with games like galaxy on fire. The loot feels randomized and the constant pop up of random quests is annoying and not interesting enough for you to want to go out of your way to explore. The lack of an fov option in game is critically missing as the game can get u nauseatingly dizzy. The fov can not be changed easily like in an ini file,  and  it requires and unreal cheat code engine instead (not recommended). The developer puts ability gimics like teleport and drift to try to help alleviate but it only makes the movement less fluid and more jarring. The constant ghost flashbacks where she visualizes what happened is pretty low budget and kind of generic feels like filler. Although the main story and cutscenes were great this game fails to have satisfying combat as fluid as like a star fox. The developers bit off more than it could chew in choosing to be open world. It doesn't succeed as a star fox rip off, and can't really compete with the depth of a game like x4 foundations. I'm all for a hybrid of the those 2 games, but the choices in its rpg lite mechanics were too limited and one dimensional gameplay style.  Gameplay was jarring and nauseating, upgrade paths were boring. Lack of freedom in different ship selections and abilities made me get bored after about 5 hours despite the great female lead of the main campaign's dark protagonist. Overall I would have like a more sandbox open style game with different ways to play and progress like space pirate, miner, trader, etc. I would like a sequel with a dark anti-hero in a way and thought it was a really cool idea.  I played with mouse and keyboard which controlled suprisingly ok but the lack of not being able to rebind your keybindings was a huge negative. Not bad, but too shallow to keep me interested. Overall 5/10
