_childDocuments_.review: It may not be Freelancer when it comes to charisma or charm, but it's certainly a good enough space shooter. Following an ex-cultist by the name of Nara, who has a lot of PTSD to deal with since she did something utterly terrible, had a subsequent change of heart and now feels that she has to redeem herself afterwards by going after the powers that be, namely the Circle and their vanished leader, the Prophet. Through this, the game wants to be more grandiose but the campaign is in tens of hours, not hundreds of hours. I always like to take a game slow, especially if there are plenty of places to look into, and so the side missions got a little bit repetitive and there wasn't as much of a connection to other characters. There's no cutscenes of physical interaction with other (human) characters so that detracted from the impact of the story arc. The RPG elements are very light, with the ability to upgrade your ship (which gets switched out early on to something that talks to you, a version of KITT but in space fighter form) in several different ways - gatling gun, laser, missile system and then three mods you can trial. Depending on how you set up your ship, you can get different buffs for different sets of mods and weapons. The battles are either multiple ships on you affairs in space, multiple ships on you in close quarters or multiple ships and mini/full-bosses in space and close quarters. The close quarters ones are where you have to be the most careful and after you develop more powers or 'rites' then it can be damn fun in grabbing a spaceship in the sky and throwing it against a building, with a rather satisfying explosion afterwards and a nasty little laugh from yourself.This is a very much an AA title, but I didn't really come into any bugs except for an annoying one with the mouse pointer in the menu system, so I just switched to arrow keys and 'enter' instead there. A lot of the money seemed to have gone into the final mission, where the music rises, there's a brilliant cutscene and the game suddenly feels that's it's all come together and you're just kicking everybody's backside. After twenty hours into it (the game is probably only around about the 15 hour mark but as I said, I'm sightseeing, leave me alone), it was totally worth the last 15 minutes of fighting off hordes of enemies. And after this it ends and you're left to your own imagination of what's in store for Nara and her friends. Games have a habit of ending a story too abruptly and this also nearly crossed the line, but it saved itself at the end there.Oh, the irony.

_childDocuments_.review: +++ Novel mechanics and abilities.+++ Compelling world build and lore.+++ Varied environments, with both outdoor and indoor spaces.+++ Good pacing between action and exposition scenes.--- Combat can get repetitive at times.--- Not yet developed to its full potential.Chorus signs its name in large letters and it isn't afraid of doing it.  It lays down the foundation for an interesting world, and handily escapes the trap of carousel dogfights common to games of the genre, making combat a delightful affair to engage in.  There's enough to fill 20 hours of play, and all that remains is a drive to know more and do more.  It's a bold offering in absolute terms, yet retains a conservative aspect regarding its own potential - a full-fledged sequel could well be a blockbuster.

_childDocuments_.review: I think the best way to describe Chorus is Star Fox if it came off the rails. Instead of one direction there’s many and not much but generic encounter quests in between. The story is original and has a lot of potential but gets used like a SyFy channel special. It does keep the player just invested enough to get from beginning to end. VA’s are convincing enough. The space-scapes are gorgeous. Locations are interesting and have obstacles that require various abilities the protags pick up. Basically like a metroid-vania.Early on combat is interesting, I would not compare it to something like Ace Combat, or Freelancer (like a lot of other reviews do) again more like Star Fox 64 in ‘All Range Mode’. End game combat is repetitious with powers becoming the primary focus with a few gimmick enemies that add a distinctive arcade (again Star Fox) shoot the blinky flashy bits to blow up the ship.In the end, it’s an okay game that has a lot of unused potential. Hopefully the Dev’s follow up. Price point is okay… but, I’d wait for it to go on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10Chorus is a great spectacle. The game looks gorgeous on max details, and the space battles look amazing when you get a few of your rites back. The story is intriguing without many plot twists and somewhat predictable towards the end, which is fine – it leads you from one epic space battle to another and gives you some context to do battle. Controls (played on Xbox Controller) feel great; switching weapons, using rites, drifting, and boosting all blend into a beautiful space dance of explosions and tight evades. The side missions are also fun and well-written and there are plenty of them to break up from the general events that spawn around you. Overall, it would be a contender for 10/10, but there are two major things that bring it down to 9/10. First, I love achievements, and when the game has so much grinding as this one and does not give you free after the main story is done, it loses a point. Second is the last boss fight, specifically the tunnel chase… whoever designed this one, please just don’t make fast-paced space shooters. The combat in this game feels great, destroying massive battleships is satisfying, and you are telling me that for the final big bad boss, you have me navigating a narrow tunnel with so much **** spawning and blocking your way that you barely are shooting anyone? The snake phase was much better, should have just kept it there.

_childDocuments_.review: Chorus can be likened to games like Freelancer and Everspace 2. At least that's what you get from the core gameplay - third-person, action-oriented space combat. The twist is a fantasy element which adds special powers into the mix. This makes combat stand out from similar games and adds a certain chaotic power fantasy element to it.The story embraces the fantasy element and tackles metaphysical connections between realities and humanity's place and purpose within them. The overall story is interesting and gives you enough threads so the more observant may pick the final revelations earlier than some. A sign of good writing, which unfortunately isn't shared with the dialogue.The characters, including the protagonist - Nara, are mostly uninteresting. Support character dialogue is largely meaningless and has little connection other than to direct you to the next task. The conversations between Nara and her ship's intelligence are a little better, excepting her inner monologue, which is mostly unnecessary and delivered in the most annoying cadence. If you've played Control and didn't like Jesse's thoughts interrupting the dialogue, you won't like Nara's soulless loud whisper.Combat has a hectic flow and you can customise it to your play style with a bevy of ship upgrades. You might choose to favour weapon or ship strength, or enhance your powers. Take note of this for boss fights. Since you can swap out upgrades on the fly, this can be helpful in what are sometimes difficult encounters.This game has enough polish for a budget title to make it worth a play for fans of the genre. It's a decent way to spend up to 20 hours while waiting for a full release of Everspace 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Game has a lot of promise. Too bad it's so on-rails there are hours-long segments where you can't save. I guess nobody responsible for making this game ever had someplace to be.Addendum:Oh. Would I like to revise my review? Yes, Steam, I would!I keep giving this game chances. It waited until after 2 hours to become an incomprehensible mess, so I'm stuck with it now, so I might as well get my money worth, right?Wrong. ♥♥♥♥ this garbage.I thought it was bad enough when it just railroaded you through 6-8 story missions at a time without giving you a logical break point to go about your life. Then I got to the first "boss" fight.The people who made this game have absolutely no idea how to communicate expectations through game play. In all of gaming history, the only lesson they ever seem to have gleaned is "shoot the glowing weak point."Then they added a bunch of garbage mechanics on top of that, but they do zero explanation. So, once you stumble your way into "Oh, you have to shoot all of the different weak points in quick succession to get to the next phase", then they spring this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ on you.Literally the ONLY instruction you get from the game is "Oh, the end of the arm has opened."And the flight area is being consumed by a DOT field. So you make the natural conclusion that you should fly into the end of the arm to get away from the DOT, right?Wrong. ♥♥♥♥ you. Fly into a wall and die.How do you get past the wall?You use the rite aspect that the rest of the boss fight explicitly tried to communicate to you was useless.Congrats, you figured that part out. Now enjoy trying to race through a narrow, rotating corridor full of obstacles. All those walls you learned to knock down? The particle effects they give off are going to make seeing five feet in front of you ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ impossible. Good luck!There is. NO. CONSISTENCY. AT. ALL.You're in a mission dog fight. You've killed approximately twenty seven thousand enemies. The ship you're supposed to be protecting finally runs out of HP and you game over. Then you restart, and you kill only four enemies and the game gives you a cut scene and hums along like nothing is wrong.Did I somehow manage to ignore the only four enemies on the field that made a difference the first time? Is the game changing the rules as I go? _childDocuments_.review: 3 Hours in so far and I can say this was money well spent.*The controls are tight with adequate customization options.*The graphics are good, sometimes great. The facial expressions and rendering are top notch.*The story in this is good! A few interesting surprises in the story telling that will catch you off guard if you can keep from watching other playthroughs. Surprising depth for a game this heavy in shooter mechanics.Chorus stands out from many modern games in that they have carefully crafted the experience for the user. Rather than relying on clunky multi-player mechanics to create unpredictability and make their game periodically interesting from the chaotic nature of multiplayer combat, the developers are comfortable enough telling their story to let the player campaign experience speak for itself.Far too many developers struggle with actually creating content for their games. Chorus is a pleasant shift away from the decades-old trend toward leaning on multiplayer unpredictability and allowing that chaos to supplant a curated experience. Chorus is successful as a standalone game. It tells its story confidently without coddling the player with lengthy cut-scenes and superfluous eye-candy.Chorus shows visual restraint, and in doing so, allows modern gamers to experience an action-driven narrative that will have them exploring and asking questions about the universe they are experiencing, rather than simply grinding through to get to their next shiny trinket (next stage, bigger guns, better shields, etc). Those trinkets are there, but they are not the game, they are a tool used to further the story.Chorus for me is difficult to categorize. Shooter, yes. Bullet hell, at times. Sci-Fi/Space Opera arcadey flight sim? Yes. That's probably the best way to describe it; Sci-Fi/Space Opera, arcadey bullet-hell shooter. Oh and with interesting choices while upgrading and kitting out your ship. You can't take everything that you want and it makes for some interesting trade-offs.

_childDocuments_.review: So I've never been big on flight games but the plot had me curious enough to pull the trigger.Having finished my first playthrough I'm not having buyers remorse. Took me 17 hours to complete the game, including side quests. Might manage to squeeze a few more hours out if you want to spend the time maxing out all of the mastery stuff. The story was great, so much so that I won't be skipping a single cutscene on the second playthrough. The story flowed well and the characters all fit within the world. The ending even triggered that part of my brain that makes everything all tingly.The gameplay mechanics took a bit to adjust to but by the time I finished the "tutorial" map I was good to go. The ability to drift in space made all the difference. Combat was fun and engaging and it was a lot of fun trying out all the different gear sets. Add in the offensive powers you get and you really end up feeling like the badass, unstoppable force.There are a few things that could have been a bit different. A lot of the lore comes from conversations you have when flying around so if you want to hear it all I suggest when one triggers you come to a complete stop as if you're moving and trigger one of the random open world quests it will end any conversation you're having. On the note of the open world quests, it would have been nice to see a bit more variety, by the third zone I had done them all.The side quests are a nice touch but they're a bit... wonky in the way you may not be able to start them and the game won't tell you that till you've flown all the way over there and tried. From a story side, most of them give you a solid conclusion but there are a few that felt like there should have been a part 2. The open world was pretty well done. You can track down little loot boxes that contain credits or a boost to your armor/shields. There are also memories you can trigger for some added context or additional lore however these can be a bit hard to spot in some maps. There are stores you can access via landing pads at bases but I found some of them were a bit of a pain to locate as the marker for the landing pad didn't show up till after I had docked.It would have been nice to see a ng+ or the ability to replay story missions with all of your gear and rites, but I understand it would sort of break the story flow.Bug wise I didn't run into much. Some items spawning inside the floor (On the final map), npcs getting hung up which required a checkpoint restart, and several achievements are bugged.All in all, while it would have been nice if it were a bit longer... it was a good buy.

_childDocuments_.review: All in all I loved playing this game and there are many neat things it does, but there is also quite a bit of jank ...I recon you can sink 15 to 20 hours in it, depending of how many side-quests you do. While the story is flawed and not groundbreaking, it's original and I have never quite seen something exactly like that before.I will be complaining quite a lot, because I feel like this game was this close to greatness, it's sad where it ended. I genuinely do love the game, which is why I am seeing all these flaws in something that I think could have been excellent.I think it's worth playing but there are a bunch of issues that can probably make people quit quite early on.The good things first:+ The combat is pretty good, it's quite satisfying and you often get new abilities that keep things fresh+ Music, sounds and ambiance are great+ The game looks amazing+ The game runs very well, and the loading is very fastAnd then the jank ... - The game looks great, the cut-scenes don't. They  show extreme closeups of Nara's face, and the tracking is just not great: It's uncanny, and the emotions are not really readable ... It's kinda like the VHS in the resident evil 7 remake. It's just realistic enough to look bad.- The side-quests lack polish, and sometimes even main story missions do. You'll get voice-lines referencing things you have not done yet, or saying you still need to do something you have already done, because the game did not expect you to do the quest when you did.- The game starts quests while it's still explaining them. If I got a penny for each time I had to  kill an attacker, but the attacker was dead before I knew it, I'd have two pennies. Which is not a lot but it's weird that it happened at all.- The game gives you powers as you progress ... But you start with a pretty bad ship without any powers and bad weapons, so the first fights are insanely hard, I nearly gave up while in the first zone because even in easy mode a fight against a few pirates was frustratingly difficult.- The equipment system does not have a lot of very interesting items, I had three equipped items that I kept during most of the game, for weapons it's only a case of "do you want it to shoot faster and do less damage, or shoot slower and hit harder?", but at least there are more upgrades- The game loves to play voice-lines depending of where you are, but there is no safety to keep your current dialogue going, so you can very easily cancel a conversation about the story by flying too close to a side-quest.- In a chase missions, the game punishes you for being too close, as obstacles will spawn just behind the chased ship. The problem is that there is no way to know where the obstacles will be, they just spawn in your face ... so the game really just wants you to follow at a very specific optimal distance where you can shoot/hack/etc. but still dodge the spawning obstacles.The story is all over the place. Maybe it's translation, but sometimes it's like there is a carbon monoxide leak in the ship. The game starts with  which drown you in names, to try and give you some context.It's pretty easy to understand the main story arc, but the finer details are ... blurry ...Often the game will drop you little morsels of lore in conversations, but there is a bunch of contradictions, or very surface-level stuff. It sometimes feel like they were completely improvising the details.Even with all the conversations you will have, sometimes you go somewhere without really knowing what you'll do when you get there. Then the game either surprises you with a word salad to justify the puzzle or deflects you to do something else with new story elements that come from a greater lore that you don't know about. At one point, circle pilots will see your ship and tell you that they "are honored of your presence, venerated elder", and then supposedly you can be sneaky in circle territory mere minutes later ? It's a whole plot point that you are in a circle ship and that your allies will be wary about you, but after a while it's dropped and not mentioned ever again.Characters die of easily avoidable deaths, the game says you can't attack X ships for story reasons while the random side-quest you just did had you kill 20 of those guys, Nara will be surprised to learn about something you were explicitly told  before, the circle inner politics and practices are utterly incomprehensible (), tho that may be on purpose.... And

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to start by saying that I have barely any experience with this type of ship flying game, but I got hooked pretty quickly on this.  The graphics overall are excellent, I love the universe they created with tons of detail and flying around just feels great.  Once you start getting some abilities like drifting the game really clicked for me and was so fun, I just explore and keep finding things to do.  The sound design was also excellent, really enjoy the voice acting and just overall sound.  I am only 7 hours in at the time of this review but already consider the game worth its price.  the mastery system where whatever weapons you are using etc will get stronger just by using them is excellent and prods me to vary my arsenal while fighting to level everything up.  The story is pretty interesting as well and I look forward to seeing where it goes.  I will update this review once I finish the game with more.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Great arcade space shooter! One of the best I have ever played. It reminded me of old Freespace games which is a big praise in itself.Graphically its amazing and runs smoothly on GTX1070 in 1440p. Its not easy to make interesting locations in this kind of game, but I found all the maps in this game interesting and distinct. Especially locations that are Cult themed or encased in ice - just gorgeous. Light effects are especially great, even without using ray tracing. Special effects during combat add a lot of flare to dogfighting and visuals of your special powers are fantastic.Not much to say about music, its good but not great, its just kinda there. Voice acting on the other hand is pretty strong especially from our protagonist - Nara. She is a real badass and brings so much emotion to this game. I loved how ruthless she sounded at times, but at other times she was very compassionate and fragile. Other characters like Great Prophet and Rasar are also great. Voice acting really helps to flesh out the story of this game.I found the story to be enjoyable and interesting. Its not amazing, but strong protagonist, her relationship with sentient ship Forsaken and her mysterious past with The Cult kept me interested throughout. It could use some lighter moments, because its all super serious all the time.Gameplay is one of the greatest strengths of Chorus. I am playing using keyboard+mouse and find it to be very enjoyable way to play. Default button layout is great, giving you quick access to all your powers, weapons and moves. Game starts you with some crappy old ship, but you quickly recover Nara's old ship - The Forsaken. Your ship will gradually become stronger thanks to Mastery system that improves your weapons and attributes by completing combat challenges. You also have Nara's Rites which are special "magical" powers, allowing you to teleport behind enemies, shoot lightning, ram everything in your path and more. Your ship can also roll to dodge attacks and drift. Yes, drift. Not something you expect to see outside of racing game, but its such a great mechanic in Chorus. It allows you to fly in one direction while turning your ship to shoot at the targets behind you without losing momentum. You can pull many advanced maneuvers using drift and it never stops being satisfying.My only real gripe with this game is that it sometimes requires you to do puzzles or combat in very confined spaces. It doesn't feel good and your ship's movement doesn't seem designed for this kind of close encounters.I highly recommend Chorus to any space combat fan that enjoyed Everspace or fondly remembers Freespace games. We are long past the golden days of this genre, but Chorus feels fresh and brings many original ideas and mechanics to the table. It does scratch that Freespace itch pretty good.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Freakin' space cultists.  Would perforate again.Controls feel awful at first but start to feel natural once you get a few skills (drift, mainly).  And the finale is top notch, hearkens back to Freespace/Freespace 2 where you're blowing off parts of battleships and then flying inside to strafe the core and then escape.  You can tell it's not a AAA game but the voice acting was surprisingly good for the main character and the graphics were servicable.  And it happily didn't overstay it's welcome - took about 20 hours to beat.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: lots of like, lots to hate.the good stuff is the combat, zipping around and navigating behind enemies and blasting them feels fantastic. the game is gorgeous in the right momentsthe bad. the constant whispering voiceovers from the main character absolutely did my head in, the objectives are often obscured, next stages of missions are often confusing and disorienting especially if you've just been in a fight.Also the checkpoint system will sometimes throw you into a situation where you're 1 milisecond away from death, and unless you've got another save you're ♥♥♥♥ outta luck.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: A definite blast of a title. Hits as many highs as it does mids to lows. Just seems to be missing a lil something extra.Pros-Great ControlsGraphicsSoundStoryCons-Traversing the areas becomes tiresome after your third or fourth trip through the same spotNot enough meaningful engagementsTraveling and queuing the memories for story elementsHalf baked RPG elementsBout 20 hrs to complete on normal. I would maybe wait for a sale, as it is an arcade shooter somewhat fetch quest.If you are looking for just blasting fun this is your game, don't expect really deep mechanics or grinding levels, just a single play through and you'll get everything it has to offer.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: I'm basically in the early stages of the game, enjoying side quests and tier2 of the storyline.  The game plays like StarFox + WoW in a way.  You upgrade your gear, improve your "mastery" (achievements that lead to in-game benefit like dps increases), fetch / murder / escort / explore as quests, and learn to use your special powers --> rites.  It's a fast paced game for sure, probably not great for watching as an observer as it'd be disorienting, but it's quite fun and open world.  One thing I appreciate is how much control you have over your ship's movement speed.  It's a seamless and potent feeling game
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a surprise that it was this good. I picked it up on the sale for $15, and it was worth every bit of that. It's a fast pace space shooter with very good mechanics which make it a stand-out. It took a bit for me to get into for the combat, but once you get a hang of it, you feel really into it. The sound hits it, the music hits it, the combat hits it. I wish there was more opportunity late game to just destroy more and more with everything unlocked. The only complaint I would have is if you miss the threading the needle opportunity in tight spaces, you feel like a dummy in potential chain crashes that follow. If you don't crash, though, there's I felt a genuine sense of euphoria in fitting into the tightest of spots going at a stupidly fast speed. Solid game, do recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Cool space arcade game with lots of magical abilities and happenings.Best maybe compared to Everspace 2, but both have sides where they shine.Enjoyed the ride, took ~15 hours through the main quest with nearly all side quests done. The maps are beautiful and filled with lots of things to do, the combat is fun, especially when you get more and more fancy powers. Gearing and equiment could offer more distinct options, but it mixed well with the powers.There is little incentice to replay it but it was fun while it lasted.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Cool game and great main character but unfortunately its a repetitive, i kinda expected somewhere between ace combat and everspace and its not far off but the game its designed on a more story focus, so that its going to determine if you would actually finish the gameI recommend on a light sale or more.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine if you combined Star Fox, Battlestar Galactica, and Control together. What you would get is Chorus. I played the game on Hard. It was definitely a struggle and there were times where I felt like lowering the difficulty however the enemy design is fair. I wish the game had a higher budget though. You can tell the budget of the game is low given that you never see humans walking around. It's a world where everyone feels like they are just a spaceship. You never really believer that humans are living inside the ships or space stations.

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly, not worth your time. Despite its superior story-telling, Chorus doesn't hold a candle to Everspace2 when it comes to upgradability, tasks, enemies, etc. There are so many aggravating issues with Chorus, like how its triggers are buggy, or when it expects you to do something but doesn't tell you what, the tedious last boss fight, etc. that I only finished it because I wanted to know the end of the story (which, truthfully, I'm not angry with). So go play Everspace2. Even though its story (and spells/Rites/specials) is inferior, the gameplay is far and away better.

_childDocuments_.review: Tried this game a few years ago after playing the demo. When I bought the full game it carried over my progress but was broken. I spent a few hours and couldn't progress from the first area. Pissed. Returned it.Bought it more recently for like $5. And it's definitely worth that sale price. Nothing amazing here, but just enough to be interesting in all areas. Decent combat, decent enemy variety, decent loot system, decent graphics, fine story. The character model looks awful though, wish they just left that out and made all the comms in radio/thumbnail style.If you want a real amazing space combat game, then Everspace 2 is the one. But this will scratch that itch til the next great one.

_childDocuments_.review: Everything Jedi starfighter wanted to beChorus was a fun game with great ideas. It took some time to get used to the ship's mobility, but it was amazing once you got a handle on it. The abilities were great and added a dynamic I have not seen in other space fighter games. The story and designs were well put together.  Enemies were distinct and required varied weapons/abilities options to take them out which led to fun ways to fight battles. While I thoroughly enjoyed the game, I felt there was an issue with content quantity. The game overall was 15 hours with a chunk being me actively looking for side quests. Based on the achievement list it looks like I may have missed some side areas but that just means they were really hidden or it was bugged. Either way, it is not that long. This is a shame because it did not allow enough time to utilize all the powers. While there were occasional larger enemies to face, it felt like there could be more content with fighting them. Just when you get used to fighting one you will not see another until you already forget how to take it down.My biggest peeve with the game is while you are traveling long distances between points dialogue could trigger but gets turned off right as you get somewhere or into a fight and never comes back where it cut off or restarts. My second peeve was there was very little to spend money on, There was so much money by the end of the game but nothing to spend because there was better stuff in the side quests and I could only upgrade the ship so many times. I also could not sell things I did not want which cluttered up the inventory. Lastly, adding one or 2 more fast travel spots per area would have drastically improved moving around maps. I hope this developer gets a chance to work on a similar title with a larger budget.

_childDocuments_.review: The best space shooter EVER! I feel like such a bad ass piloting Forsa. I really hope that they expand on this game. The theme is mature. Game play Bar none. VERY well optimized. Graphics could use some work on the models but your are moving so fast that its irrelevant. I would love to learn more about the universe via different content like an anime. Something leaving feeling the way I felt after watching Yasuke. Its on Netfllix treat your self and watch it if you have not seen it yet.  Story is also great.  After you learn the fight mechanics (Drift) you and Forsa become Death incarnate. Please Play with controller not M&K. You will thank me its a different experience.My review is negative because I lost all of my progress in an initial launch issue that kept you from progressing after a certain point. It only occurred if you played the Demo. Was not to invest another 30hrs. Too bad cause I was enjoying the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I just can't get into the game. If I could have just switched the story off, I probably would have kept the game and ploughed through the missions. But the story, dialogue and dynamic was so grating and immersion-breaking that I could not carry on.TL;DR: Play Everspace 2 instead. More polished gameplay. Better story. Less stiff voice acting. Immersive.Gameplay - mouse and keyboard are somewhat off, wide/tight/fast turns are nearly impossible in any smooth mannerSaving is the usual autosaving nonsense that robs you of the liberty to save as and when you need to. If you need to close the game halfway through a mission, tough.Story - meh. You can see it a mile away and the character redemption arch is rather obvious. You wonder why bother. I appreciate the character is set up as being a badass, but somehow it just amounts to arrogant, cocky and hard to connect with.On the plus side, I love the idea of a night mode to play. The graphics are good and the UI is nice enough. Had it not been for the characters and the premise, I would have quite enjoyed the gameplay on its own.For anyone moaning about my short playtime - live with it. You *are* allowed to form an opinion in the first half hour. A game should give its best sales pitch in the first part to hook the player in and convince the player to give up their time in return for a satisfying and compelling experience. This game did not manage that.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game.  It's a nice, simple space-fighter that doesn't rely  heavily on twitch mechanics...  That is, until it does.  The combat is fun and, once you get used to the drift mechanic, it's quite entertaining.   The rites make things interesting as well, giving you more ways to blow stuff up.Navigating through tight spaces is an absolute , none more frustrating than the fight against , where I found the chase utterly impossible to complete.  I have seen youtube videos of people completing that part, so I know it  possible, however, I was unable to, so, as yet, have not been able to complete my first run through to its entirety.  The writing is a bit hit and miss, but overall, I found the story interesting.  Capital ships are a joke.  They are there simply for you to blow up and, other than certain of their turrets, absolutely no threat, whatsoever.One thing that I would love to see them do is proper joystick integration (having accessibility issues means that I struggle with anything that requires a lot of keys to be pressed at the same time.  I tried to use my Thrustmaster to play this, but had to revert back to mouse and keyboard, as it just didn't work, especially for spirit class ships, where the ship control and aiming are separate.Overall:  A solid 6/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was great. I only learned about it when it released, but after I saw some gameplay I wanted to play this myself.It's a great arcadey space-shooter. Controls feel good. I played with mouse & keyboard and that worked flawlessly. Story was kinda 'meh', voice acting sometimes good, sometimes a bit cringey. Technically this game was perfect. No bugs, no crashes, very good performance. I wished more AAA games would work like this.The biggest draw for this game is absolutely the space combat. You feel like an overpowered badass how quickly you can take down ships once you get a few powers and some nice upgrades. At the end you take down big ships without a problem.Absolute recommendation if you like space-shooters.

_childDocuments_.review: Completed the main and all side quests more on principle than fun exploration -- $5 was about right for quality of the experience.  Otherwise not recommended.  I don't see any replay ability.The story unfolds with hard to hear and fuzzy "memory" recall points that didn't pull me in.  The rebellion aspect was good, but "jedi powers" you develop over time to teleport, streak and jump through and toward enemies felt like unbalanced compensation for poor flight control system.  Combat gets marginally better mid game as you unlock drift / slide ability and you turn into superman.While too few, the level design has some nice visuals, but your destinations and targets are really only revealed via your X-Ray vision senses, not hinted by design.  Not enough places to explore and only 1-2 random encounter experiences with many repeat side quests. Credits become meaningless.I died what felt like hundreds of times on some of the boss fights, restarting at last check point.  Just seemed too grindy.  Everspace and Descent fans will be underwhelmed.

_childDocuments_.review: Positives: Smooth flying, intuitive combat, and Cool environments that are fun to explore. It's also genuinely fun and addicting.Negatives (which very nearly ruin the experience): First and foremost the main character is completely insufferable and emotionally incontinent. You can also feel Larry Fink's Blackrock influence whenever the game makes a cringe attempt to address politics. Finally, there are several critical game mechanics which you are supposed to discover through the trial and error of dying several times. Some aspects of this game will gleefully try your patience. Bottom line is the talented devs designed the gameplay and the DE&I devs "wrote" the "story" - If you get this game, recommend muting the voice acting and it will drastically improve your experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Story 10/10:Ex-Jedi..uhm, -Circle... Master... uhm, Elder - Nara, who wanted to bring peace to the galaxy and thus destroyed Alderaa.. uhm, Nimika Prime, is on her way to redemption. Using her trusty ally space-KITT and the force...uhm, rites, she is on the hunt for psycheledic-turned-evil space-jesus. Genius. It's a feast that you should not miss!One little thing: there seem to be really minor blips in the story, stuff that is not explained well enough. Like why Nara first introduces herself as "scavenger nara", sometimes just "nara", and towards the end as "seeker Nara". Especially as she uses the "seeker" title before you even pass the test to become a seeker.But as I stated before, this is really complaining on a very high niveau.Controls 9/10:The controls are good on pc (keyboard/mouse) and although you have to get used to various things like drifting and re-adjusting the camera. Otherwise quite intuitive and agreeable.Graphics 9/10:Sometimes a bit too psychedelic, and Nara's face animation doesnt feel too natural. Apart from that: really nice graphics, and a continuously conherent style.Gameplay 9/10:Really nice gameplay, cant put it otherwise. Only thing that is wonky sometimes is the targeting box. Sometimes its hard to see when you can hit enemies and when you're off target. Laser seems to randomly miss sometimes, cluster rockets too. That doesnt impact gameplay too much though as you're quite OP anyways with all the rites you get to use.Conclusion: Wanna have a good 60 hours gameplay time, enjoy a good story and cause a lot of things go boom? Buy this game!I'm not playing too much space shooters because often they are overcomplicated. This one isnt, I can only recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: I wish the main story was longer/wish there were more engaging sidequests.  I've played through this game twice now; once on normal and once on hard.  I love the feel and the mechanics and the combat so much.  I would shell out some cash in a heartbeat for a game with this same combat system, but a few more weapon types, ship customization, and maybe PvP.There were a couple of quests that got kinda buggy on the Steam deck but aside from that ran great.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best space combat simulators I have ever played. The story is truly perfect. You play as someone who discovered her world altering powers through evil means. After discovering just what a weapon she could be in the wrong hands, she cast off this mantle of superiority for the sake of all. Now, as a normal human you must relearn what it was to be that killer when the cult you escaped from comes knocking at your door.The extremely steep learning curve is the major detractor to an otherwise flawless game. Do not be discouraged though, as settings help quite a bit.Conclusion: Amazing story combined with the right amount of real world interactions/consequences makes this a must have for anyone who can navigate the flying controls.Try the demo. What do you have to lose?
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: This game catapulted me back to a time when there were still awesome space shooters. Get ready for some breathtaking action! The story is extraordinary and will take you to the end of the game at the speed of light. So don't forget to take a break in between and enjoy the view. The game also reminded me of the good old days in another aspect: on my first run-through, I didn't have a crash or a bug. Respect!
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Very impressed with Chorus. From the very start the game presents very nicely. Good menus and options to configure the game optimally  (DLSS support for example).Starting the game you are eased into using the ship which is not complicated and then story begins.We have a female protagonist who is well voice acted and whom the story revolves around. Without giving any spoilers the story seems solid and provides a decent enough purpose to fly around and blow stuff up.The game world looks quite beautiful in 4k to be honest - some of the best in space maps I have seen.DLSS support helps keep that sweet 120 fps so we have a game that looks amazing, plays very well and has a decent story.Audio is good too with support for 5.1.Combat is cruisy - this is not a hardcore space sim but an arcadey type of design which I like. There is very little downtime going from one waypoint to the next.Once the initial intro missions are completed you are free to fly around a local map and explore and take on side quests as you see fit which is good.There are ship upgrades but again, nothing too full on so no need to be thinking min maxxing etc.This is a nice game to chill and admire the scenery and explore.Overall Chorus is an easy recommend from me and I look forward to completing the campaign fully.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: The game's trailer confused me. I thought this was like Mass Effect. Instead, it's more like Everspace 2 and Rebel Space. Most of the gameplay happens in a third-person spaceship with sizable open-world style maps consisting of the main story and side quests. The story unfolds between a mix of third-person ship perspective and protagonist cinematics. The graphics are outstanding. Voice acting is terrific (although the protagonist's inner-thoughts are a tad strange). Music is cinematic. It's a solid-produced game worth a buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: So many good things hampered by so many bad. The good:Despite the lack of roll control, once you get a hang of the controls, they aren't bad in Forsaken. You can do some decent maneuvers, especially with the rites factored in. Is it great, no. The first ship you pilot and Forsaken look pretty cool.It does manage to make you feel powerful.There is a decent variety of enemies with the standard ships and their variations, capital ships, and faceless.The voice acting is surprisingly not bad. The bad:Environments are very samey. You have 2 regions in one solar system which are near identical asteroid fields, then you have another solar system which is a less dense and darker asteroid field that has a wormhole to a tiny asteroid field, then an ice asteroid field. These asteroid fields are bookended by the interior of a really large space ship and a region with a large space station. Sprinkled throughout are temples. Because the story is linear and side quests bring almost nothing to the table, instead of huge open areas with nothing to do, they should have done smaller areas and tried for more variety.The story is a terrible mess. It wants to be religious, but at the end settles for the matrix. It tries to be emotional, but you don't spend enough time with any side characters to care. It even has something that seems like a time related paradox.Dialogue is poorly written and Nara and Forsaken talk too much in combat. Almost every kill, Nara starts a sentence and Forsaken finishes it.Memories are annoying, you can't continue flying, you have to sit there and wait most of the time.Almost all the ships look terrible.Upgrades are basically useless.By halfway through the game, I had maxed out the missiles and the gatling gun. The best laser is given to you. That left me with loads of currency and nothing to buy.The last rite is a telekinesis that lets you fling ships. I never used it outside of its annoying tutorial, because you get it at the very end of the game.Still, I'm a sucker for flying games. Buy on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game. Not that long, it took about 16 hours, but there was so,e afk time and I cleared all the quests on every map. But don't get bored either. Feels just right.Solid gameplay, nice voice acting, nice story with some cliche, but very... nice in general. Didn't encounter even single bug. Atmosphere is there and I liked it. Some negative review disliked "sad protagonist", but it is good classic story about protagonist put away her powers because of guilt! Star Wars Kyle Katarn for example.There are some, I won't say cons... but strange game design. Market for example. I really don't know why it is there. Except some of last tier guns everything you get from missions is better. And credits also.. strange. If you complete side missions you'll get better hardware then in market, if you'll ignore side missions, you won't get credits to buy something either. But all in all guns are good, enemies are in numbers and variety =)It is what single player game should be: a really good time for right amount of money!
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, if flawed.The game excels in the space combat, particularly as you level up and access more abilities- being able to blink behind a enemy and take them out, or shoulder charge through swarms of enemies to destroy them. The more you play around with them, and your drift ability the more fun it gets. That said, the HUD could do with a lot of refinement - particularly enemies on your radar - its far too easy to lose track of them, especially when your concentrating on dodging incoming fire. I had most fun when taking on the occasional capital ship the story throws at you (though again, knowing what to destroy on the warships could be signposted better).It also has a really good soundtrack that's very middle eastern sounding (almost like Homeworld)- not surprising given the whole title and theme of "Chorus". The voice acting is also good - I really liked the voice they had for the Prophet - reminded me a bit of Bill ♥♥♥♥♥, in a way. The way Nara whispers her thoughts did get a little grating, given shes alone for 90% of the game, and is usually doing it to undercut something she has just said out loud, usually to Forsa.Where it falters a bit is as others have pointed out. Its not that the story is bad - far from it, its a good space opera, but as we are stuck in our ship all the time, it can feel a bit disconnected. There are cutscenes, but most of the plot is passed to us by static talking heads in a comm panel, so it can be a bit hard to follow in places. At one point, you meet up with both your old mentor and your old student, and I found it hard to understand why they join your rebellion. The student in particular- you see his memory of fighting for the Prophet, then later he shows up as a renegade himself with little explanation. Part of this problem I think is that you can encounter memory bubbles as the game progress', giving you insight into things that are happening, but again this can feel a bit disconnected. I did wonder at one point if this was all setting us up for an unreliable narrator moment - like everything we were learning was just peoples perceptions of it, not the truth (Spoiler: I was wrong). The maps can feel a little empty, at least until you get to Nimika, I felt. I suppose that's not uncommon to any space combat game, but still, its a point.Others have also pointed out the difficulty spike in several mini bosses (one in one of the temples in particular). What doesn't help is that these tend to be inside structures, limiting your manoeuvrability, as well as the constant weapons fire laying into you, not giving you much room to work out what your doing. What would have improved things, I think, was to have several hub areas where you leave your ship and walk around. You could talk to the other characters and learn things that way, maybe through a dialogue tree, and pick up missions from them if story related, or have a bulletin board for non story missions. Perhaps even a bit of minor RPG elements? Instead of having a slot for equipment to improve your rites effectiveness, you could spend points on upgrading the bits you want to?A bit more customisation would also have helped- the in game shop for buying upgrades was really underwhelming, to the point I really just used the stuff I scavenged or got given as mission rewards. I finished the game with around 70K credits, but there was little if anything to bother buying. Heck, maybe the option of buying additional inventory slots to load more equipment? You cant even buy custom paint jobs for Forsa (although there is dlc to get one skin).I also said earlier about adding RPG elements - its interesting that Nara is so broken by what she did at Nimika that she doesnt want to lead anyone ever again. That slowly changes over the game as she becomes the rallying cry of the galaxy, and it would have been interesting to see it play out on a dark side/ light side way.So would I recommend this game on balance? - yes absolutly. This game is a lot of fun and well worth getting - how many space flight games come out these days after all?  We don't get enough games in this genre anymore, and that's a sad deficit. Id love a sequel but with a little more tweaking to improve it in areas.

_childDocuments_.review: Chorus is a fantastic game that plays like Everspace from a third-person perspective and keyboard and mouse controls, but instead of just upgrading the ship and the guns, you also upgrade the player, which makes the middle to late game very interesting. The use of rites makes it plausible that Nara can turn the tide of any lopsided battle like she’s Anakin Skywalker in the Clone Wars.  There’s a good variety of enemies and counters, from simple skirmishes to outright fleet battles. The late game adds some extra-dimensional entities that are not even spaceships in the conventional sense which shake things up. There are some set pieces and a nice “assemble” moment at the end where almost every faction that appeared in the game before shows up for the big finale. The production values are very good, the game is polished, looks great, has tight controls and a good soundtrack. Not much to talk about here, it’s a solid game.The story is mostly excellent, with fascinating lore. It takes itself seriously, almost too seriously. While some complain about the dramatic inner monologue like in 1984’s Dune, it’s well-suited because the Jungian theme is perhaps more about internal than external conflict. That's likely why it mostly focuses on the inner struggles of Nara and the ship Forsaken, which is a complex character himself and more than a sidekick to give expository mission dialogue. Chorus has a nice length and while I usually don’t care to get 100%, it was a pleasure to do so because the game is so good. If enjoy this genre, and especially if you remember Wing Commander, this is a hidden gem that you should check out.

_childDocuments_.review: It's so good. It's also kind of refreshing, at least when it comes down to the gameplay.I recommend it even at full price, there is not much replayability for those who loved everspace but I think it's far better than the second opus of the said series.I loved many things and also hated others but overall it's a really great game.It's not too long, 20h or so, not like every stupid RPG which need more than 50h of almost nothing to complete the story.First, the good points. - .It's pretty good. From the general plot to Nara's evolution through the game. It's feel pretty great that just a little tweak to the usual they are bad so you fight them can make such a good story.I saw review saying "It's creepy how the main character talk to herself in her head" well I want to say if you never do that I think you are a machine. - .It's the best point as well as the worst since some people might not enjoy the game because of it.It's not the usual space command with zqsd (wasd) to move on the 2D plan you are on, ae (qe) to roll and space/ctrl to manage height yet it feels pretty natural after 1 or 2 hours at most.Still be aware that at first you might die because you're still thinking with typical control and do a dodge instead of going left or right. - .They're are really good and fit well in the game and in every situation.Weapons sounds are also good shoumdn't give you a headache after 30 minutes.Some sounds feels strange though since I sometimes encountered a rock and it made a metal colliding sound. - .I don't have many to say here apart from they are pretty great and fit well in the game.Now, the "meh" points. - .You will experience in the game some frustrating moment especially in temple or in some fight (boss fight in general) which comes from the poor level design of the places or the ennemies, ennemies in question are big enough and what's asked from you make it a level design problem.In this game, you always go at full speed since the game clearly says to you "do it and you shall not die".But in tight space it's often the very reason you die because you are way too quick and your breaks are those of a train.You need time to slow down and even the drift might not help you since drifting is just freely moving your orientation while you are taken away by your initial speed and direction to make tight turn but it's not that easy to use in tight corridor. - .It might be lacking for some people. - .You have 3 types of weapons: Gatling, does hull damage. Laser, does shield damage. Missile, does armor damage.There is some interesting features inside those categories like some gatling do massive damage at short range or fire heavy ammunition resulting in low fire rate etc.But you'll mainly use the gatling and missile since shield are not that resistant especially in late game and even armor can be taken out with the gatling.I didn't feel the use of the laser since, as I said, gatling do decent damage to shield and since shield can regenerate after some times without taking damage.And changing weapons during fight is sometimes tedious because if I roll too hard on my middle mouse button, I might skip the one I wanted to use. - .It's a passive effect on equipment and need you to have 2 to 4 of those perks to apply an effect. Most are interesting but since you can't upgrade or level up your gears you might have to abandon a gameplay you like because they are not good enough, especially since some of those perk are attached to your weapons which might also forces you to play with a weapon you don't like. - .Money feels useless. It's not the case in early game but once you do some secondary mission or take a bit of time looting you become way too loaded.I think I finished the game with 50k with everything bought in the shop.Looting also feels pretty boring and useless since most of the time you get money, some time you get hull or shield upgrade but since you can buy them in a shop  you are quickly loaded with money  the game stop you from getting them too fast it's also pretty much useless. - .While some are quite easy to take down, most of them are a pain. Their not dangerous but most of the time they are timed objectives to take down and if you fail you gotta do it again. It's better than a massive count of HP but it's still pretty bothersome at times.Finally, the bad points. - .The true first boss to me is the first one you fight in the void.And it's tedious and frustrating.  - .I know. It's a bit too much since every map are not that big but still. To go to a place you need to go to the jump gate or teleport to it if you already visited it once (and it's never said anywhere I discovered it by chance) then you take the jump gate of the system you want to go to and you have to travel all the way to the point you wanted to go to. It's not that long but it's kinda frustrating when you objective is at the very end of the map and you need 2 minutes to go there (especially for FedEx quest, there is some not that much and not too long so it's ok).That's it.Overall, the game is really good and deserve more attention.

_childDocuments_.review: "I meant to do that." -Great Prophet, probablyChorus is great. Medium on story/script, but long in starfighter arcade style gameplay. I thought it was a slog to get from place to place until I noticed you can warp to any jump gate at any time. Exploring the areas and finding the pickups and upgrades was fun and flying anywhere around the environment always feels cool. The space dodge and space drifting never felt old. _childDocuments_.review: I don't mind difficult games. I mind the artificially difficult games that make no sense for their escalating difficulty. Because each step you add to your progress gets overridden instantly by more difficulty, basically forcing you to learn new ways of doing the same ♥♥♥♥ you did before just by adding insanely more difficult enemies. And it's not worth it.Not worth it because there's no good story to back things up. The story, the acting is horrible. The quest system is limited, and although there's obviously a lot more this game could've been, the authors obviously were not able to make it. Because the mechanics are nice, you can have some really fun moments with this game, but the game rushes to spoil your fun as soon as it can.The story itself is weak, like 6-grader level of bad story. Not only the central character has a weak development, her partner is equally badly developed, and the side characters are simply boring. The voice acting is weird. The side-quests are simple fetch quests at best, and quite hard to discover. Sometimes a full-map scan will show these side quests, sometimes it wont. But I could deal with a bad story for the sake of the setting and ship mechanics. However, the masochistic difficulty increase made the game frustratingly unplayable. And it's not like you can get more missions to develop your skill in playing the game - no, there's only the same mission, the same steps, that you can repeat over and over again (from a checkpoint or, if you ALT-F4 out of frustration, the whole thing done again from the start). There are lines of dialogue that just get in the way of the fun.There's a good combat-oriented ship simulator in here, but it's ruined after a few minutes of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great fun. The first hour is a little slow to ease you into it, but when you get the new ship and your first ability, it gets really good.This is a case where the negative reviews seem to just not "get it". Maybe they wanted mindless aiming and shooting. Pay attention, because the game actually does a good job of teaching you how to fight. You have to use the right weapons and abilities at the right time. You have to drift. You have to keep moving and be aggressive. Everything has a counter. When you realize that, you feel nearly unstoppable. It's great!Also check our House of the Dying Sun (especially in VR) if you dig Chorus' vibes and gameplay!

_childDocuments_.review: Flying through space, through asteroid fields, evading stuff and shooting enemies, that is quite fun in this game. I guess that is the main part of the game and thereby I recommend it, although there is a lot bad stuff to say about this game. I played it using mouse and keyboard which works better than expected for a flying game.These are the main negative aspects I found so far:- The story is strange and badly told. Everybody acts overdramatic. The main character keeps talking to herself, which kinda gives you an insight into what she is thinking really, but that gets annoying really fast and a lot of the stuff she just could have said out loud. All the major characters feel shallow. Also she keeps discussing everything with her ship's AI which is really weird. - The character animations at least sometimes do not reflect the voice intonation - for example, Nara sounds like overthinking some stuff but has an angry face at the same time.- The checkpoint/save system is rediculous and needs to be fixed. You can only save BETWEEN missions, and missions have checkpoints. Since sometimes missions autmatically lead into each other (at the end of mission A, mission B starts automatically), this can lead to quite long sections where you can not save the game. For example I just was at a quite difficult section of the game which seemed to be 5 missions or something each leading into each other, creating one very long segment where you can not save inbetween. In the 5th mission, I encountered a totally new enemy type and found out that it would have been wise to buy a different upgrade in mission 3 of this mission streak. But since I have no save file there, my only option would be to restart all 5 missions from the beginning, which of course I don't want to do since the missions took me more than an hour to complete.Also some of the missions do not have enough checkpoints. I encountered something comparable to a boss battle a few days ago, which took quite some time to complete but I did it on the first try. After that, some things happen on accompanying ships which makes one of those ships shoot me all of a sudden, and kill me. Since there was no checkpoint in between, I had to redo the boss battle several times before getting the final part, which feels wrong.- The photo mode is also fun and has a surprising amount of features, however the images are saved to your MyPictures folder instead of the steam library. Getting them over to the steam library is possible but a bit complicated.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like taking unavoidable damage in the face? Do you like one long cut scene cut into many 10 second ones where you have to fly around for 5 seconds in between? _childDocuments_.review: Mixed feelings about this game. Played it at release but wasn't tempted to pay full price for myself. At half price, well meh.I think it's quite a pretty game. It's a weird mix of fairly enjoyable combat (it's not at all trying for 'realism' so I can understand people hoping for that being peeved) with what's effectively an 'open world' to shuttle about in doing secondary missions and shuttling between story missions. The combat is a mix of rock/paper/scissors weapons and space magic and does it perfectly adequately with maybe one or two missions excepted. The story is space hokum but it's fine for what it is. Unlike many others, I wasn't bothered by the constant internal monologue of the protagonist but rather by the fact that the poor voice actor has managed to land on sounding like Foster 'my face is tired' Addison from Mass Effect:Andromeda. Which isn't the happiest of associations to have a player make.Chorus is generally fine but I do keep finding really niggly things which detract from the game, mainly revolving around mission markers and missions triggering or not triggering. Sort of things which you'd hope might have been picked up in the patching done since release, and the sort of thing which will quickly grind if you're not willing to look past them. For me, it's a solid 7/10 game if you fancy flying a space ship while doing alien space magic.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really something, but only in its gameplay experience I feel stood out. At first, it's different from how you usually fly space ships because you cannot manually roll in this game. Instead, you have to click a button that will auto correct your orientation which is somewhat annoying, but manageable. There's no setting to change the ship to manual whatsoever which is unfortunate, but it's not bad once you play this game more and get hang of it. Just remember this is more of a arcade style flight control than your usual one.The only downside that I wish to express is mainly the protagonist itself: I don't like the constant chatter involve with her inner thoughts. I understand that it has to do with the main storyline of who she is, but I wish I didn't have to hear it so often. It can ruin the game experience over time for players who would get irritate of this (no offense).This game is great for its space combat experience, but the scripts on the inner thoughts needs to tone down.Edited: I managed to beat the game, but I want to add something here that I would think / hope that the devs would add this feature in this game:The game lack challenges. There's only one which is the permanent death option, but it's not something I prefer. Instead I want challenges like certain areas you explore would give you that option to test your skill in space and you can replay the challenge missions as much as you want. It can be a race through obstacles or destroy wave after wave of ships. I'm sure someone else can suggest something better, but this is pretty much what comes to mind.I believe this would be great for players who really enjoy this game to where we want to find another reason to jump back in, but not do the story all over again. If the devs can update this game to have this freature, I would be happy to come back and play again.

_childDocuments_.review: I played for about 9 hours and then uninstalled the game. I don't normally do this, especially with games that have so much incredible stuff going on. Ultimately: constant, major problems with the quest system did me in.1. Quests start automatically, and continue through tens of minutes and many multiple battles and map locations.2. Quests cannot be abandoned/postponed. Once the player is in a quest, the only way to end it is to finish successfully.3. The game can not be saved during a quest. Combined with #1 & #2, this means that the player has infrequent, relatively small timing windows for saving progress; enormous swathes of the game spent wondering when the next window will be.4. Frequently, the entirety of quest information given to the player is one oblique sentence with no map information or markers to accompany it.*5. Often the current (unexplained) objective is to just move a few kilometers from wherever you are, or to move to a particular area that isn't marked in any way, to trigger the next piece of quest dialogue.**6. Checkpoints are often placed before long cutscenes with multiple sections (e.g. a cutscene, a dialogue, then a screen introducing a new enemy), which are skippable only after a pregnant pause, and then immediately followed by very challenging combats. Die in combat, load back into cutscenes, repeat ad nauseum; sometimes more time spent skipping cutscenes than playing the game.* I spent inordinate amounts of time looking at walkthroughs and forums just to get single nuggets of information about where to go for a given quest; something that could be handled with simple waypoints. For an open world game that takes place across multiple locations that are hundreds of square kilometers large, this is very frustrating.The one that finally did me in was "Approach Clan Cobra territory." Is "Clan Cobra territory" a place on the map? No. Is there a marker for it? No. You're left wandering around aimlessly, hoping to trigger the next part of a quest. I even found a forum post about that exact quest, someone gave an answer, and it still wasn't enough for me to get the quest back on the rails. After visiting every waypoint on the map and traversing the entire perimeter, I uninstalled the game. (For those familiar with this quest, I *was* through the gate, in the correct zone, and I'm just exhausted enough that I'm not gonna watch a YouTube liveplay just to get there--I am done with this.)** I can't count the number of times the quest stalled out, leaving me absolutely confused about what to do. Then I fly a kilometer in a random direction and suddenly the quest continues on its own. It isn't fun to wonder, repeatedly, if the quest has glitched out, or if the game has broken somehow.* * * * * * *This is such a huge disappointment for me. The game is otherwise fantastic; looks amazing, gameplay is high-octane with a very satisfyingly challenging skill curve. The world/universe are interesting, the maps are well designed. Story is kind of inscrutable, but that's okay. To boot: it runs fantastically well on the Steam Deck.I am simply sick and tired of being constantly ♥♥♥♥♥♥ around by the abusive quest system, and it is on those grounds that I cannot recommend this game to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: The controls in this game are a bit unconventional. They are neither exactly like flight simulator controls nor exactly like 6DoF games. They are more like flight simulator controls, but the stick has yaw control side to side rather than roll control, and by default back is down and forward is up (you can change that). The throttle is on the other stick, along with barrel roll / evade controls.Once you can get used to the controls, this becomes a pretty decent space combat simulation game with a twist: drifting. That is why the controls are the way they are, so they could implement drifting as a play mechanic. Once you get the ability to drift you can use it to continue traveling in one direction while aiming in another, or to change direction very quickly by switching back to your boosters. It's an interesting mechanic to master.The story may not be everyone's cup of tea, but it's not so strange as computer gaming stories go. Yes, you hear Nara's thoughts as whispers, which some may find a bit hard to take. It wasn't a big deal for me.You get three kinds of missions: those that contribute to the main storyline, side missions, and random missions. I highly recommend at least doing most side missions to make yourself more powerful. Some missions are pointed out, but any structure you see on your map could include one or more side missions, so some exploring is warranted.The bottom line for me was: this was a fun mission based space combat game.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Great dogfighting and a good story but it has some pacing and character issues, some weak side content, some rough spots where its budget held it back, and a couple of weird choices wrt the controls.  8/10.  Worth full price imo.This is far from a perfect game but that doesn't stop it from being absolutely magnificent.   There are three main points where I think the game excels.The dogfighting is a tight and responsive power fantasy that has you nimbly sliding sidways through incoming fire while you shred everything that gets thrown at you, I've truly never played another dogfighter that feels quite  good to execute.  The design leans into the player's ability to 'drift' as well, with capital ships giving you conveniently-aligned strips of weak spots to tear through as you pass, or having tunnels you need to fly inside to hit weak spots.  It's a flashy blast, and one that has just enough progression integrated that it feels like there's growth and forward motion without turning things into a slog.The story takes a while to get going.  Nara takes a while to become likeable as a protagonist.   She spends the early hours seeming whiny and fragile in a way that seems to almost break character given her history as a hardened combat pilot, and I never warmed to the creative decision where she whispers everything she thinks.  Her relationship with Forsaken, her sentient fighter, is another sticking point for me - it's understandably adversarial at first, but it spends long enough rehashing the same beats that it becomes fatiguing and I found myself hoping it would move on to the bonding stuff sooner.  God am I glad I stuck with it, though.  The narrative in Chorus has the sort of tight thematic structure that you very rarely see in action games, with its central message influencing everything from the story's structure to the characters and their histories to the metaphysical nature of the setting itself.  I won't spoil how it plays out but there's a magnificent twist right at the end where all the pieces finally fall into place, and it's wonderful.  I almost wish the game was about 25-30% shorter so its pacing could have been tightened up.That setting is the final place where I think Chorus excels.  It's a sort of science-fantasy that we don't see often in games that are explicitly set in space, blending the conventions of other dogfighters with a supernatural or eldritch angle that not only feeds back into the game's story, but serves to give the world a great sense of personality as well.  The Faceless are a truly intimidating and interesting enemy to fight, and the Circle who worship them were characterised very well, growing from what I assumed to be nothing more than faceless zealots to a fascinating and nuanced force with their own theology, structure, internal politics, and hidden divisions.The game does have a few major shortcomings though, things that I think people should be warned about going in.First: The controls feel amazing in open space, but whenever something goes wrong during some of the more star fox trench run sections, you will  feel the lack of dedicated strafe and reverse controls.  I honestly don't understand why the game doesn't have them, possibly to incentivise you to use the drift ability?  I'm not sure.  You don't spend enough time pursued down tunnels full of obstacles for it to seriously impact my enjoyment but it did make some bits annoying.Second: The game's character writing is... fine, not as good as its plotting but still passable, but when you get into the side content it really breaks down sometimes.  I'm not sure if it's just that they only had a handful of voice actors, presumably for budget reasons, but the side missions are seriously a mixed bag.  The stuff toward the end is probably a highlight because it involves interacting with the cult more and getting a better sense of what they actually believe, but the rest of it varies wildly in quality, and it's frustrating because all the game's best gear is locked behind these sidequests, or I'd suggest just skipping most of them entirely.Thirdly and subjectively: The game might be too easy.  The powers are extremely strong and particularly if you do side content, they get upgraded to be even stronger, and you get access to weapons and gear with powerful set bonuses, so on the 'normal' difficulty I was chewing through almost everything except the final boss in moments.  I didn't mind because I enjoyed the power fantasy, but it's worth keeping in mind.Finally, and this one's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ weird: particularly in the side content, this game feels like Pixar's Cars in space.  Nobody ever gets off their ship, everyone has their own ship, and they are so inseparable from that ship that they may as well  the ship.  Things that would normally be done by removing a person from their ship, like imprisonment or torture, are always done by shooting a torture laser into the ship, or impounding the entire ship behind force fields with the prisoner inside.  It's really strange, like the studio's budget for art and animation couldn't handle designing and rigging more than one human character so they just smoothed over all the places where the writing asked for someone to be removed from their ship by doing the thing to the entire ship instead of just the character aboard.That said, for the quality on offer here, this game is , so if the sidequests making me wonder if everyone is a disembodied voice in a space ship is how this game costs half as much as an eighty-dollar AAA release, I'll happily take it.  Heartily recommended to anyone who wants a really fast-paced dogfighter.
