_childDocuments_.review: Story and main characters are pretty interesting, and that's it.  Game can't decide if it wants to be an FPS or a dog fighting flight game, not that it matters.  If all you're after are the open-world fetch quests, boring side quest characters who don't even react to your "change",  and drift mechanic that's only purpose is for these shooting puzzles whose purpose is only to annoy you and stop the main campaign progression, then this is for you.That's right, there is a puzzle drift shooting mechanic that if you don't time right, you will not be able to continue the game.  They're not hard, they're just pointless.  For all the open area you can fly in, get too far away from the invisible wall and you'll be told you're outside quest area.  So, need to take out a few ships and maybe want to have them chase you for a sweet drift turn around kill?  Too bad, that would put you outside the quest area where your only objective is to kill the baddies.The opening is a pretty wild ride, the powers are gimmicks and the asteroid area is uninspired.  Batman detective/witcher vision is getting old as well, time to change that up for a few years.  The cutscenes are also extremely choppy, as if they weren't originally running at 60 fps.  The npcs have no faces, and the devs couldn't even be bothered to change a drone character into another pointless face and just gave them the default npc helmet as well.  Game would have been better off not showing faces on the side of your screen during conversations.Flight between areas is boring and pointless.  Upgrades to the ship are just "making the numbers go up", no real interesting choice of ship mods or gear.I was exciting about this one for a while, love my Freelancer, Independence War 2, but this just made me want to rush to the next story beat to avoid any additional gameplay
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:Graphically, this game is gorgeous, from the meteors, to the backdrop of the vastness of space - very well done. The protagonist was very well designed and has great voice acting to go along with it. Combat is really fun; it takes a bit to get used to, but once you figure out the gist of it, it's only up from there (though I definitely get a little disoriented, considering you can move about the X and Y axes in frikkin space). The upgrades for your ship are cool, and the rites that you pick up through the story make for some interesting combat options also.Cons:I feel like this story could have been SO much more fleshed out. Overall, it's pretty easy to follow and you can pick up on what's going on pretty easily, but it seems to be very surface level. The side-characters aren't very likable at all, and it's kinda obvious that the devs spent a majority of the time fleshing out Nara (rightfully so). The game presents itself as an open-world (err, open-space?) RPG, but it definitely is not that - there aren't many side-missions to partake in and if there are, they're all fairly similar to one another. Map markers on your HUD may as well not even be there - I find myself hitting the scan button every time I'm looking for something hanging around the area - the only one there is your main objective marker.All in all, it's not a bad game. The graphics are beautiful, and the combat is really fun, albeit disorienting at times. The story could be way more fleshed out from the beginning, but there's enough there to give you a general idea of what's going on. I feel like if there was more on-the-ground (or in-the-ship?) gameplay, allowing the player to actually come in contact with the protagonist and supporting characters, it would make it much more worth becoming invested in not only the story, but the characters. The dogfighting in space is definitely what drew me to this game, and I can say it definitely doesn't disappoint in that aspect (you can drift in a spaceship!?) I would say if you were really into dogfights in Star Wars Battlefront this would be up your alley.Solid game - bought it on sale - 3/5

_childDocuments_.review: I started playing from the demo, and continued my save file from there. Huge mistake, both because I missed out on act 1 of the story and because...That said, the game itself is pretty damn fun, balancing difficulty and thrill quite nicely! There are a FEW twitchy missions but it's nothing you shouldn't be able to trial-and-eror your way through on the very rare ocasion it happens.

_childDocuments_.review: Can't say I was a big fan of the story elements (some cool ideas but seriously overwrought), but the graphics are gorgeous and the gameplay is excellent.  There are no over-complicated controls or subsystems to figure out before you can start playing, and as for the actual dogfighting?  The designers deserve a medal for creating a game that a) feels like it has all the speed and exciting 3d maneuvering as classic space dogfight gamesb) is approachable and easy to control.The maps are full of large structures and asteroids, and you can orient yourself to the default angle with the push of a button.  You're in third person, making it easier to keep track of your surroundings.  Projectiles move fast and ships relatively slow, so you don't need to worry very much about leading your target.  One of the first powers you unlock teleports you directly behind the target ship, getting you (back) into position to open fire without complicated maneuvers.  Once you get past the tutorial ship, Forsaken has almost excessively generous maneuverability--you can turn on a dime, brake and accelerate really fast, slow to a crawl to navigate through tight areas... it's just easy and usable in a way that very few dogfighting games are.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Chorus: Great game with issues.In summary, a fun arcade shooter. A few bosses, lots of fancy flying. Nice environments.You’ll want to advance the story until the player obtains the main ship. It is significantly better and can drift.  Most of the “fun” comes with spamming powers. The game really starts shining when you start electrocuting people, drifting, and ramming capital ships to death. Unfortunately most of the cool stuff comes near the end of the game. The issues for me come with the movement. Flight games should  have 6 degrees of freedom. Roll, Pitch, Yaw, Vertical, and Horizontal movement. This game lacks a few of those, you can “roll” to dodge similar to starfox but are unable to naturally roll in any direction. What makes things stranger is in certain parts of the game you can take over ships that have vertical movement. This developer worked on mobile games like galaxy on fire and when they were making a higher budget game, did it not occur to them on PC and console we have more options?In addition to this. At the time of this review the player can’t customize the control layouts.Lack of customization. You have 3 weapon types with upgrades. Can’t change the color of your ship or exhaust. The ship you get near the beginning is the ship you are stuck with.Trigger story elements by flying too close to them. This is annoying when completing side quests.Also, on the topic of side missions, there is no reason to do some of them except for fun and testing powers. _childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a "maybe" rating for this game. Controls and combat feels very good and it is enjoyable, but its burdened by strange story that makes no real sense if you think about it for 2 minutes. Story is trying to be deep philosophical and feels like its written by a teenage girl. What is worse,  developer loves it and is realy trying to sell it to you. And that is my main issue with the game. If this game was mainly about combat I would be fine with that, but most of the gameplay is flying around looking for boring memories with some combat sprinkled here and there. Main character cant shut up and keeps rattling some "deep" bs. And its getting worse with every new location you visit. For a space combat game there is just too much dialogue. Im the kind of guy that likes to finish all side quests, but in last location I just could not force myself to do the side quests, I just wanted it to end.Now back to the gameplay, combat feels good I liked the inclusion of powers. Game is not very challenging even at harder difficulties and with more powers unlocked its realy easy.  There is not many weapons, only few possible upgrades and only one ship you can use. There is main storyline with quite a lot of side quests on most of the maps. There are few not very large maps that are filled with side quests that are OK I guess. Main missions and side quest are nothing special: escort this, kill that, collect that or my "favorite" go look at some memories or some combinations of these. Later in game you get more of those memories quests. Also when you are moving between locations you often get some kind of random encounter quest, there are 3 or 4 variations of these and after you complete few of them they get annoying realy fast.Graphics is looking ok, nothing groundbraking im fine with that.I was expecting some everspace experience by looking at trailers, but in my opinion gameplay was not the focus of the game and its realy a shame, because foundation is there and its good. _childDocuments_.review: Trailer: Chorus is a game with a female protagonist who was a major commander for a civilization called The Circle bent on crushing everyone with an iron fist into peace and harmony under the unification of a single banner ideal named Chorus. Upon seeing the absolute corruption of her superiors through their weilding of power, which lead to her committing an unspeakable act, Nara turns her back on Chorus and her awakened ancestoral powers and flees into the cosmos where she joins a rebel faction called The Enclave and seeks forgiveness and repentance in repairing the lives of the people within this civilization. The game plays very much like a Star Wars spaceship game and reminds me of a blend between Star Fox 64 and Star Fox Adventures. There's a main storyline path to follow and actually interesting side missions that are scripted and completely voiced storylines that build onto the main branch. Rescue a ship and maybe they'll join you later or maybe they'll go crazy and take out one of the ships in your battalion. Are the space pirates all evil? Are your friends actually spies going to betray you? The side missions will nearly all impact your story and add to the lore of the game. Overall, I think this is a great chapter in the spaceship fps genre. I was given this game for free through keymailer.Trailer:

_childDocuments_.review: - Combat gameplay : do NOT rely on the demo, nothing is explained there. The controls take a bit to get used to (left stick is not for controlling the direction for eg) but when you're getting used to it and unlock a few powers, it's really good !- Immersion. The story isn't mindblowing but it's ALL DUBBED (only in English though) and without interruption (very few skippable cinematics, and few "memories", but otherwise it's during the action, you don't have static characters with walls of text). And the pace is good.- Side missions : they didn't bore me. No real FedEx type, no "killing X enemies" or "collecting X loots". And it's still dubbed.- Dynamic missions : a bit repetitive but optional random events are a nice addition.- Graphics : quite good  ! (except cinematics with the main character, I think she has a big head and weird animations sometimes)- Nara, the main character : some people hate the fact she's not "attractive" (very subjective : I find her very ok and don't care about this when 90% of what you see is the ship...). The thing I like is the fact she's not a super hero, not a white paladin cheering every single lost child, not the cocky cliché we often see with short hair women. No, she's just someone struggling with her past and trying to use her powers in a better way.- Interesting bosses, but not enough of them- I didn't experience any crash (the only one was because of Discord, I think), to me it was stable, and perfectly smooth. The few bugs I had on the press version were fixed in a early patch.- The difficulty is not well balanced. To me the game is 80% too easy (even after rising the difficulty settings), the real meat are the bosses. Some have very interesting mechanics. But they are so few !!- No NG+. Usually I don't care about NG+ but in this game you have "masteries" (bonus depending on how ou defeat ennemies, mainly, it's like achievements) you can't do efficiently after you beat the game because there is no area with a lot of enemies and you can't rely on dynamic events to finish it. You can't really use the last mission either : all you do in there is lost because you can't save during a mission and when you defeat the last boss, you go back to your last save.- Some Steam achievements are broken atm.- It's a bit linear. There are a few choices but without any impact on the story. But... that's not a RPG after all.- Customization is nice but a bit poor, it allows different ways to play but no template system to save your build and no real appearance customization.- Music : except the title screen, it's forgettable and not very present.

_childDocuments_.review: While Chorus doesn't perfectly execute everything it sets out to achieve, it hits more often than it misses, and the more I play the more I come to appreciate what Fishlabs are trying to do with Chorus. This is a great space shooter which can best be described as tight, nostalgic, and tactile. Chorus is a straight up video game, it's smaller in scope, finely balanced, not trying hard to milk you for cash, not trying to be a sprawling open epic. It just wants to put you in a bad-ass ship, give you some cool sounding and feeling guns, and go shooting some bad guys in some cool looking locations.It's somewhat reserved scope is one of it's best defining features., there's no sprawling open world to explore, no min-maxing of loot and stats, no collectables and no filler. The game world is a series of inter-connected open areas with a selection of main and side quests to explore and complete. You're never lingering in one area too long before completing it and moving on to the next one. And each optional quest you complete is often worthwhile opening up more optional lore and backstory. In those ways Chorus feels somewhat nostalgic, harking back to the days of the PS3 where games were much simpler and smaller in scope. Chorus feels more akin to something like Rachet and Clank, it's measured and balanced and always focusing on keeping things moving along.Quest rewards and the upgrade system is a mixed bag, on the one hand unlocking new weapons is often exciting, new weapon types function somewhat like alternate firing modes for your three core weapons - Gatling gun, laser, and rockets. Giving you new play styles to experiment with. However most of the time you'll be earning modules which offer pointless % stat increases to things which ultimately do nothing to make your ship feel or play differently. These can largely be forgotten about and that's a shame. It feels like a missed opportunity for these upgrade systems to not mimic the weapons upgrades, giving you new movement styles and the like. The combat in this game is wicked good. Responsive controls that feel good to use, great sound effects and animations which make mowing down enemies satisfying, and the addition of the rites give you powers - such as drift trance - which take out a lot of often encountered frustrations of chasing enemies around in space. The addition of larger ships you fight by flying inside them and shooting their guts is an absolute highlight. Plus some boss battles, and the ability to control the larger battleship at times all add variety to the combat which would otherwise wear thin.Story and character wise this game surprised me. At first, Naras whispering and her voice acting was NOT working for me. At least initially her whispering was happening far too much and the weird ASMR-like quality of the recordings made me cringe. In addition I found Naras voice to be extremely monotone and her delivery overly stiff. However, the more I played the more I understood what Fishlabs were trying to do with Nara as a character. In particular when you meet Forsaken and Nara has someone else to talk to, her whispering is greatly reduced and the dialog between Forsaken and Nora is often genuinely great and thought-provoking. At that point you start to realise that Nara is a broken freak of a person - she's souless. Naras monotone nature is trying to convey that, and while the VA doesn't do the best job, I can at least appreciate the attempt.While the story is extremely simple and the voice acting of Nara and the side characters often doesn't always hold up, the premise of the characters - a baddie turned goodie paired with a sentient ship who has a slightly different agenda - is genuinely interesting to me and extremely unique. Forsaken is the star of the show here, he's got a wicked voice and some genuinely interesting interactions with Nara, and the relationship they have develops in a satisfying way as the game progresses. I don't think everything Fishlabs has tried sticks the landing (like the aforementioned whispering) but I DO appreciate that they've taken a gamble and tried new things. It's these things which form up Chorus into a unique experience in it's own right, one which I will remember for some time, and recommend to everyone with an interest in space games and/or shooters.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great space action game with a few caveats. Because of this I think it's probably most informative to do some pros and cons.Pros+ Excellent arcade action gameplay+ Great sound design and voice acting (for the most part)+ Excellent graphics, particularly partical effects and lighting+ Interesting mechanics in how to manage dogfights+ Different enemy types requiring different approaches, weapons and powers to defeat+ Lots of side missions and a decently-paced story campaignCons- The story starts out quite intriguing, but eventually goes off the rails- Probably linked to the above, the story is poorly designed and paced. - Technically you fly 3 ships, but really there's only 1 that you'll use for 90% of the game- Although there's different enemy types, they're common between cult and pirate factions, and enemy variety is lacking- Fights against capital ships sound fun in theory, but end up getting boring with huge gaping holes and weakpoints- Random in-field events have the ability to interrupt story dialogue, and if they do you will not hear that story dialogue again- While Nara has a character model and mo-cap is used to good effect for her, all other characters have generic still head portraits. That's only for a handful of the main characters too. The rest get generic portraits of pilots helmets.- The final power (known as Rites in the game) is not introduced until just before the last mission and it ends up being completely useless and underwhelming.- No Endgame content. Once you've completed the story and side-missions there is absolutely nothing else to do in the game.So with the above you get an idea of what to expect with the game. I still recommend it because if you can get over the horrible story and some obvious cost-saving design decisions the gameplay . If you want to experience it yourself then feel free to stop here and go get it, but if you want to stick around I will elaborate on the problems I have with the game and , so you've been warned.My first big issue with the game is its lore. For the first act of the game you will be hammered with various lore-building concepts that establish the basics of Chorus's story, none of which will really be explicitly spelled out for you other than Nara is in hiding after being responsible for the destruction of a planet while being an Elder of an organisation known as The Circle. This is when the story is at its most interesting as you are given just enough to speculate on what is actually happening, but not enough to just write it our in front of you and tell you what's going on. In the second, and largest act of the game, you spend most of your time with Forsa (short for Forsaken) who through various story missions and conversations you learn isn't just an AI, but someones soul intentionally pulled from another dimension and jammed in to a containment device aboard the ship. The problem is you find this out in the most confusing and ham-fisted way possible: You're tasked with a mission to visit the station where Forsa was built, but it's been destroyed - yet there's no explanation as to why. The most confusing part is that it's still in use and operational by Nara's mentor who built Forsaken. Later on in the story it's mentioned that the station never belonged to the Circle and was destroyed by them as part of their war with the Najarans. So this all of a sudden becomes a Najaran station that was destroyed by the Circle - but The Circle then used it to build Forsaken and the other Elder ships? What?From this point in the story more contradictions start piling up like the game is actively attempting to retcon the story it was playing out only a few hours earlier: When you reach the final act you enter Nimika, which is entirely under the control of The Circle. The first problem here is Nimika is supposed to be the planet that Nara destroyed which prompted her whole change of heart and fuels her guilt that makes up the 80% of her personality. Except here, with no rhyme, reason or explanation it's still there with just a small chunk missing from it, with what ends up being the most powerful space hub in the galaxy floating outside it. The second problem is, with the entire story up until this point (and Nara herself) trying their darndest to convince you that the entirity of The Circle are religious zealots who brainwash or kill anyone who refuses to join them, all of a sudden 90% of The Circle are peace-loving pilgrims who are embroiled in a civil war against a single militant sect of The Circle who have been the ones causing the problems all along. Are you sh*tting me? The worst part as well, and major spoiler for the ending here so if you really don't want to know how the game ends then don't read further: The soul that was forced in to Forsakens core to make the bloodthirsty 'We must kill the Prophet' AI ends up being , and that's the reason Forsaken is so hell bent on killing his corrupted shell that was left behind when he went through to the faceless dimension and failed his trials. You couldn't make this sh*t up, there are no shortage of scenes and memories Nara goes through showing her with the profit, inside Forsaken before he decides to take up this trial, so how the hell is his soul inside Forsaken when it hasn't even been split from his body when Forsaken is built?Now all of this could be down to me just completely misunderstanding the story, but I'll tell you what would have helped: not having important story conversations between characters interrupted for the 20th f*cking time by a civilian who's ran out of fuel, or a salvageable wreck appearing near me, or Circle ships appearing. Every time this happened, it stopped whatever conversation Nara was having with Forsa or other main characters, and it wasn't picked up again afterwards, so I missed out on so much story content that it's possible I just couldn't have possibly expected to know what was going on at times. Was it ever mentioned that not all of The Circle was evil? Was it ever explained how a soul of a person was made in to an AI while it was still in their body? I'll never know, because once these conversations have been had in the game, they don't happen again unless you start a new save.I realise I've rambled on about the story and how much I disliked it, but the reason for this is the story is the turd that was dropped on a perfectly good bowl of Spaghetti Bolognese. The rest of the game is great, and I can recommend it on the sheer fun of the gameplay alone. That unfortunately just made the fact that the story is so disappointing by the end so much more jarring. Give the demo a go and see if you like the gameplay. If you do, blast through 20ish hours of fun and ignore the story completely.

_childDocuments_.review: Here we are going to a space journey at the war starship, participating in epic battles and completing missions. But if you expect this to be another “Elite”-type game in the “explorer”/”privateer” genre, you probably will be disappointed. The game is actually an “action”/”shooter” with some “open-world” features.If you ever played good old “Freelancer”, you will feel like home in “Chorus”.The space is filled with stations, asteroids and mining outposts. We are flying a small fighter ship, which has limited fire-power but provides high maneuverability. It provides “thruster” speed, which can be used in battle and “cruise” speed for long travels. There are some kind of space high speed highways, which usually connect main points of interest through the particular system. In order to travel to another system we use the jump gates and jump holes.The game is a 3rd person “shooter”: it provides a view of the ship from outside. In battle we are chasing the enemies, dodging attacks, “watching our tail”, using repair nanobots if taken damage and so on. It is everything you usually expect from flying a space fighter.The game is filled with battles and action and provides a nice feeling of free flight, making the entire process quite enjoyable.We have 3 types of weapons: a machine-gun, a laser and a rocket launcher. In order to be effective in combat we should switch between them depending on the enemy we face. The laser is most effective against shields, rockets - against armor and machine-gun - against hulls.In addition we have supernatural powers (called “rites”), which allows us to teleport a short distance, use telekinesis to grab mines and other objects and so on. It reminds me of playing a game like “Control”, but on a larger scale. Having these powers make battles appear more realistic, since we usually have an advantage over our enemies. Thus it does not look absurd when we destroy the entire squadron on our own.Mostly the battles are well balanced, providing enough challenge without too much pressure. However, some will drive you mad. The game has a habit of putting us in close quarters with overpowered enemies, when there is no place to hide from attack, no room to speed up or maneuver, turning the fight into a real pain. So balance can be better.It can be said that the game provides an “open world”. Indeed, you can fly circles around the system picking up random missions, but, overall, the game is linear. There is a main quest, during which Nara will collect all her “rites” and gain access to the other world locations. It provides the most challenging skirmishes, the epic battles of two large space fleets and so on. There are some side quests, at which friends we met during the main quest ask us for help. These are relatively interesting, providing more information about the world and making it appear more lively. Also there are random missions, like kill all pirates in the area, collect cargo from a destroyed ship and so on. These are absolutely unremarkable.Fulfilling extra quests provides a reward in money or equipment, which can be used to enhance our ship. Also some quests are necessary to upgrade Nara’s “rites”.Exploring the world has other benefits as valuables are scattered around different areas. At some stations we can buy equipment, but can not sell it. Up to the end of the game the inventory is filled with outdated weapons and ship upgrades, which can not be converted into money.We can not trade any goods or resources. So there is no room for entrepreneurship here.We can’t buy another ship. Although the game allows us to experience another ship class: the heavy fighter using turrets, during some missions.For the “space simulator” the world is quite small. It has 5 systems in total for us to visit. Although each system does appear quite different: one is a large asteroid field, used by miners, the other is a large space city and so on. The “system” is not a *star system* though. The entire map covers a singular solar system, while a particular location is tied to the orbit of the particular planet. It is not very epic, but suits the game nicely, as the smaller world scale matches the scale and velocity of our ship.The main story is unremarkable: as always we are going to fight some great evil from beyond. They are called “faceless” and can appear out of nowhere driven into our world but human emotions. Once again this reminds me of “Control”.There is a philosophical theme about accepting your inner self with all your flaws, reaching harmony with the Universe and so on, but it is nothing special.The story events presented via radio messages. Nara never meets anyone in person and leaves the cockpit only on rare occasions. The game is relatively short: it takes a few evenings to go through even with all side quests.Graphics is good enough: space, asteroids, ships - everything appears as it should.Optimisation is also good: quick loading, no lags even at the top graphic settings.Sound is unremarkable. Music, effects and voices appear as they should, but there is nothing special.Overall the game is good and enjoyable. Just remember that it is more “action”/”shooter” then “explorer”/”privateer”, although these genres are mixed here.Total rating 7/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Completed the game after 16.9hrs, completing all side quests and the main story. Overall opinion? It's a damn fun space flying game. Feels super satisfying to master the flying in this game and dog-fighting in space with other fighters, which all have a pretty good variety to keep most engagements interesting. The larger enemies you fight are unfortunately a bit mediocre with them all largely just being the same as one another. Story is fine, I have no major praise to give apart from I liked the overall message and theme of the game. Like I said, I really enjoyed the flying and dog-fighting and it's really what carried me from engagement to engagement. And the final boss was super damn fun to fight, unfortunately though you can beat the boss only using 1 of your powers and standard weapons, with another one being next to useless unfortunately. But in the end, I still very much recommend this game. Its not terribly long and I think its length is perfect as it doesn't completely wear itself out.

_childDocuments_.review: Story is boring. The continuos whispering of the main protagonist is nervewracking. But the worst thing, the absolute nightmare is the save system... you can't save the game if not in very small windows between missions, and those windows are very arbitrary and difficult to understand because you are on a mission most of the times. _childDocuments_.review: Game was fun and worth the money on sale.People who say it has a good story are ... confused.Story is like a 12yo kid trying to sound deep. It's like 80% gibberish.The faceless or umm the circle. No idea what the difference is. They are the bad guys.I literally have no idea who they are. _childDocuments_.review: 6 out of 10. I rarely quit a game without finishing it, but this game just seemed like a punishment. _childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: I played this on controller my entire initial playthrough of 17hrs at the time I write this. I believe I finished all the side quests, and I beat the main story on normal difficulty. Overall good, well designed with fun controls and combat. Quest design and mission structure is redundant through out but engaging and well-paced enough that the combat loop made sure that I didn’t mind “having to eat my vegetables” before getting into another fight. Outside of major cutscenes, story presentation consists of having Nara experience “visions” which are often static ghost images of ships while an audio log plays. Characters interact over the radio with static portraits, it’s all kinda budget stuff. That said the main cast’s voice work is really good, the whole thing is quality throughout and I was at times finding myself invested. But the overall presentation of story elements (outside of the rendered cutscenes) feel limited by the scope of the game.The combat loop is pretty great, feels wonderful on controller. A major ability that combat revolves around is drifting, which in this game was very intuitive to me. The other “Rite” abilities further add to what is a great power fantasy. The game also incorporates puzzles that have to be solved with “Rite” abilities sometimes multiple abilities at once.Check out the demo, it’s got a good mixture of encounters that will give you an idea if Chorus is for you.I overall like this game, I think that the story elements padded out a short game. That said the story isn’t bad. I stayed for the game feel and the combat loop and wasn’t disappointed.I wish there were more encounters to play through especially against the larger ships that come up regularly in the later missions. I will likely play through again at a higher difficulty sometime later as I still want more.I hope we see another release like this because the mechanics here make for a fantastic power fantasy.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Some of the most fun I've had in a space flight sim. A great story, paired with smooth, responsive controls, an epic soundtrack, and amazing visuals is packed into a very rewarding package. It's frustratingly difficult at times, but just enough to make you want to power through rather than rage quit.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. I looked at the negative reviews and want to address them first. They seem to come from them not getting far enough in the story. There are some that say that the ship doesn't maneuver well. This is a narrative feature. As the story goes along you will be able to maneuver increasingly well. This game is not an arcade shooter, as it may initially appear. It is actually an open world space game with full 3D exploration. Some people say that the main character weirdly whispers to herself. Again, this is a narrative feature, an important one actually. I don't want to spoil anything, but this changes over time as well. These were the biggest critics I saw so I'm going to go on to my review.Chorus is a a great game. I really hope they create a Chorus 2. The gameplay takes aspects from many different other games to create its own style. The best I can do is describe the feel of the gameplay, which reminds me of the Combat career path in Elite: Dangerous. Your hands will be doing a million things at once to the point that you get deep into the zone while fighting. This kind of game can be hard to play for some people, but it is extremely rewarding to experience once you learn to play instinctively. The story is amazing. The obviously low budget of the game doesn't do it justice. Graphically, it looks like a game from the Xbox 360. Story-wise I would put it up there with some great anime. The game is highly metaphorical. On the surface, the story is very much like Star Wars, with rebels fighting against an Empire. However, the struggle is more about the main character and her struggle to overcome a traumatic past. This could have been overdone, but I believe that the game found just the right balance to pull it off. In conclusion, definitely get this game. It may be hard, but I encourage you to push through the unforgiving tutorials in the game. Feel free to change the button layout if you need to, which I did. The game has a good message, and I hope more people hear it.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: I usually don’t write reviews before I finished a game, but this one is the exception since it’s so damn good, I thought I spread the word a bit since I’m not seeing it get the attention it deserves…sadly. In short: this is worth EVERY PENNY, absolutely brilliant double A game and great value for the price.Long version: So, the game is an arcade space combat shooter. If you’ve played Freelancer, Darks star one, Everspace etc…. then you know exactly what I mean. It’s not a full price game so expect some double A jank, but few and far between. The game also had no bugs whatsoever while playing, which is a breath of fresh air in today’s industry.CombatIt’s just phenomenal. It’s literally everything you can hope for in a game like this. It’s super-fast and visceral, explosions/weapons feel and look great. The game not only has the basics: 3 weapons for 3 different roles…as in 1 weapon against shields, 1 for hull, 1 for hull and booster + an evasive maneuver (barrel-roll obviously) …. but it also has abilities that you can use in combat…and these are really cool, things like chain lightning, teleporting, scanning for weaknesses etc. The enemy variety is also great and especially when the game throws everything at you, usually in main story missions it’s just a blast and you’ll be bobbing and weaving in the game and in your RL chair, smiling all the way. Different weapons also play differently even tho they do the same basic 3 things I said above, so you can have 2 rapid fire guns or 2 “grenade” launchers that fire slowly against hulls for example, things like that. Ship upgrades are basic but do play a role on gameplay, adding less cooldowns, more speed, more dmg etc etc, but only with 3 slots to play with so it’s not very deep.StoryIf you, like me, love to see a good story no matter the type of game, then BOI are you in for a TREAT. The story in this is FANTASTIC…it builds very slowly and is really well paced, best of all, the side quests really remind me of the Witcher 3 quests, as in they tie all the looses ends of the main story together and add a lot to it in the process, making you feel more involved the more you know and do. Your character is basically a pilot/space psychic-witch and her switch from the bad guys to the good guys leads to some great moments between her and the second main character which I wont spoil because he’s quite a cool reveal. Voice-acting is also really good, especially for the main 2 characters.VisualsIt looks just like any good-looking unreal engine game. Explosions and special weapon/ability effects are also cool, while not impairing you’re view by being too excessive. A standout is the ship designs…man I wish there were more of them because especially your ship looks phenomenal; very original ship designs, some of the best in any space game I’ve seen. The systems you visit also look great and they tried to make them feel more alive by adding a few ships (perhaps adding more radio chatter would have helped)Sound Is good on all fronts, but nothing really stands out.Anything bad about it?Well, if you’ve played any of the games mentioned above, then you know that these games can get repetitive, so if you’re one of those people who think a bit of repetitiveness is somehow a bad thing (even tho it’s the basis of any GAME, video or not) then be prepared, because in this game you either explore or you dog-fight. The other bad thing is that you can’t customize much. You are stuck with just one ship and it’s 3 weapons types the entire game, so I can see how some people would not be satisfied.Also, one thing I started to see more and more is that the game, while at the start, on hard difficulty, was quite challenging, the more powers I unlock the easier it gets, a bit too easy.That’s about it. I Highly recommend it and hope to see more from these devs, maybe even make this into a series because it’s just fantastic and reminds me of the good days of freelancer, but even better.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolute underappreciated gem of a game which I enjoyed from beginning to end.Don't let the comments complaining about the checkpoint functionality dissuade you from giving this a go - it's definitely an unnecessary design choice, but the absolute worst I ever had to deal with was repeating about 2 minutes of gameplay - and I suspect it helps a lot with narrative and gameplay flow.Aside from telling a refreshingly intense and (in a good way) simple and engaging story, with a likeable protagonist(s) in an ever-so-slightly unusual setting, the game is just damn fun. The devs developed a very good gameplay loop with what feels like perfect, responsive controls. The abilities are obscenely satisfying to use, and expand as you progress without ever feeling overwhelming - You're not forced to use every tool you're given, but every tool you're given is useful.As someone who is disinterested in completionism, I actively chose to pursue pretty much every sidequest that cropped up just because it was actually fun to fly around in space and zap, dakka, or blast enemies. For me, its only real issues were: By the end of the game I was absolutely LOADED, with little to no items to spend cash on that I had interest in - I feel like it would have been cute to have ship paintjobs as an option, even if only a handful.Basically the same issue, but you do kinda feel the relatively shallow pool of sensible equipment options as you go along - but what you do get is varied and fun, so it didn't bother me so much as just stand out as a relative shortcoming.There are one or two ship designs that it reuses just a TINY bit too much.Some of the sidequests stand out as being distinctly less interesting than the rest - but these also tend to be completable in under a minute or two, so, eh.But... the gameplay, the setting, the music, the art direction, the writing, the ending! *Chef's kiss*There's a small handful of games that make me choose to sit and watch the credits in their entirety, this was one of them.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: An awesome game with a nice story.The story is rich and there is a lot to explore. Only thing I would say is that it would benefit if it was a bit longer since I speed through it in 20 hours.Mechanics are intuitive and easy to learn as well.Got the game to review it but ended up making a full playthrough series!

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10 decent enough space dog fight game, with some pacing problems and is oddly at times, too much and not enough.The way the fighter controls is quite good, but by the end you will have far too many abilities and it'll feel too crowded.The story is well told and whilst the vagueness of the back story adds to the ambience, I really wanted more as without it, getting an emotional investment in story & characters was tricky.Graphics and sounds are good, if a little bland but it runs well and changing game play areas is very quick n seamless.It's not going to outshine the Everspace games, but it's worth getting on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Chorus is a solid title that tries and, for the most part, succeeds at taking the space sim genre in an exciting new direction. The game doesn’t pull any punches when it comes to combat and offers an intriguing story that, while difficult to follow at times, does a great job at immersing you into this dark and sometimes bizarre universe.You can check out my full review right here
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: This game actually seems pretty fun. But I couldn't play it. I hate that it has an "auto-level" button that will roll my ship back to the default orientation. I'd rather have the option to map roll left/right inputs to my controller. I have two paddle buttons on my controller that aren't being used which would be perfect for that.The keyboard options don't even provide the ability to map roll inputs. Which boggles me because there are so many freaking keys available on a keyboard. You can justify not providing mappings on a controller since there are limited inputs. But there is no excuse for not doing so on a keyboard.And on top of all that, they do provide a roll axis mapping for joysticks. So the game engine already supports the roll input functions. Just not for those of us using keyboard/mouse or controllers.I get that this is more of an arcade game, not a space simulator. But not providing a roll mapping in a space game is analogous to not provide a rudder input in a flight game. And yes, I know there are arcade style flight games that don't provide a rudder. Or else they provide a collective yaw/roll input. But you know what? Those games are terrible and annoying to play. Just as is a space shooter that doesn't provide a roll input is terrible and annoying.If they fixed this and provided a roll input for keyboard and/or controller, I'd probably re-buy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Flawed, but great experience.IF YOU PLAYED DEMO: START A NEW GAME. Demo save is incompatible with full game and won't progress any further. You'll be locked to the second map, one of the smallest in the game. Game never tells you that.Writing is a bit simplistic but not too cringey.Controls are fine and ship is responsive (you need to keep your head  though)Combat is flashy and at times you can suck and crash into stuff, but if you pull off some stunts, you'll feel really badass. I loved it and never skipped a fight.Random events are occasionally rewarding (you can get good upgrades instead of money, so dont skip them)Some quests design was questionable (like you're told to follow a ship very closely, but then it suddenly stops and you crash into it).UI is weird, you use E for various actions, like talk to someone, scan environment and DECLINE QUESTS. Accepting is Q. There is no way to change that, and it sucks. I've declined 3 quests (you can restart and accept them) and 1 random event (can't re-accept these ones) due to this bs.Otherwise it feels like a good double-A game.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: To keep it simple: Bad storytelling with a couple of decent moments, but very fun arcadey gameplay.Is it worth it? I left wanting to play it more for the combat, but the story side left a lot to be desired. I think at $40 is a tough sell, but with a decent discount there is a very fun arcadey shooter here.----Plot wise, this is obviously a lower budget game. You get a couple of cutscenes involving the main character for some key moments, but most of the story is told via voice over while looking at the ships. Voice acting varies from “good enough” to “really bad”, but all of that was expected. Where the game fails is in delivering a cohesive story. It starts somewhat interesting with a sci-fi setting but heavily mixing in more fantastical elements. But then it completely loses itself in the middle. It tries to introduce way too much stuff for the time/budget, and the editing and dialog writing leaves a lot to be desired. The main story is very “over-dramatic” and it takes itself way too seriously. I also found some continuity issues depending on the order of some  the end I gave up trying to follow the plot. The final sequence/mission gets a lot better though.But then there is the gameplay, or more specifically, the combat. It’s very arcadey. And actually very fun. You switch between three main weapons (gatling gun, missiles and lasers) and after getting the main ship you start to get a few powers to use. It isn’t super in-depth or anything, but I enjoyed it very much for the length of the game. The non-combat sections drag it down somewhat because of an over reliance on using your “senses” (witcher-sense in space) to follow trails, find objects, etc, but nothing terrible.Structure wise you fly around 4-5 large maps going after main or side objectives. There are also some random events but they are very limited. Upgrades are more or less straightforward if somewhat uninspiring. But you can combine some special ones to get more boosts.Finally, the game leaves on a high note. The final sequence/mission is actually very fun to play and even the story gets a little together. Tip #1: Get your main ship as soon as possible.Tip #2: Use drift way more than I did.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're comparing this to Everspace 1 or 2, or other similar types of games, DON'T(before you read more, i'll admit I didnt get to the newer ship that Nara eventually gets, but im assuming its similar, i spent 4 hours trying to figure out what this game was suppose to be.)the graphics are greatthe combat sucks-turn aim radius bs-can't strafe yet you have thrusters for it-no rotational movement (hello? space game, who thought this up)-no reverse thrusters either-reticles, or lack of have you guessing where to aim properly, yeah hit the ship, but at range that should have a little dot that tells you to aim there to account for distance and velocityif you're going for an arcade like game with a story, i'd give this a meh.Nara: stop whispering, i understand it's a thought to convey to the player, but saying it in a lighter tone is better than whispering like a creeper. You've killed billions just in the intro alone, that should make you have some sort of emotion. OH god the voice acting, the lack of emotion, CHRIST STATION IS BEING ATTACKED! have some sense of humanity. I can't feel for these characters, and for a 40$(CAD) game I was hoping maybe a galaxy on fire level or voice acting at least, and even that sucked (but GOF was meant that way, cheesey)DifficultyExtremeSo I started with extreme thinking it'll be hard, but when im dying because my ship wont move, or npc's are bumping their ships against the station and taking no damage, thats just tilting. Sure hp is limited in healing, but when your enemies only need to take 5-8 shots to kill you and you need to hit them (the most basic MF rookie ship out there) 30 times with the same weapon, that's tilting. Thats not all, you hit one and its like hitting a hornet's nest. I'm not the only target? HardI downgraded thinking must be me, I cant control my ship and enemies are just good, fine. Now the enemies are a bunch of uninterested storm troopers. their aim severely dropped and their aggression dropped to a "slightly miffed".OH and the cutscenes of objectives, why must i stop the game only to have the objective sit there, unskippable, and take over my screen while enemies are moving as well. At extreme mode you would assume the player is competent enough to find it. Also, similar to that press X memory bs. Play it on the background, let me fly around to see the memory like a ghost or something, let me immerse myself rather than stopping me for every little detail. If i've scanned something like an objective, let it sit there until i finish picking it up instead of spamming E like Im a bat. make it disappear if i leave 15km out. i'd give this a >50/100, get it on sale, I cant recommend this to space gamers, this is a game similar to starwars squadron. If "extreme" was THAT difficult and "hard" was like stealing candy from babies, why the massive jump? Bah, its your choice.

_childDocuments_.review: Lot's of arcade fun. This is a perfect translation of the old shooters like Axelay, R-Type, Gradius, etc. into a 3D experience. Definitely don't even try to view this game through any sim or physics lens, just enjoy the experience. The dialogue gets a bit intrusive, and the whole whispered inner-monologue really should have been scrapped. The universe is pretty cool, though the cut-scenes are a bit too emo-art-film to really explain much. Even with the weak aspects, drifting around and strafing enemies like you're Starbuck make this a ton of fun to play.

_childDocuments_.review: This game blew my expectations away. Great game, but keep in mind that it's more of an arcade action style space shooter than a space flight sim....and that suits an oldster like myself. Pretty good graphics, plot is not lame for a change. Scratches an itch. Cuts out a lot of the superfluous crap and gets right into the fun. AFTER a pretty bland welcome/training area. That part almost had me hitting the eject button...but once I got out into the open, I couldn't help but say it- woww..   *blink*This game is easy to play for a casual gamer and a lot of fun. It's third person. Lots of great visuals. To me, it feels like Rogue Squadron from Game Cube, but modern effects and stuff like that. Very happy and I'll tell you  that you should buy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Ace Combat, you'll like this. The story is bland as all hell, even though conceptually the main character should have a really interesting dynamic with both her ship and the rest of the in-game factions.NEVER, EVER SET THE PERMADEATH SETTING TO 'ON'.I'm getting to about the halfway point, by my estimation, and the game has started throwing dozens of insta-kill scenarios at me while the actual dogfighting remains a fun non-threat. Strafing the big ships is awesome, and from a design standpoint I really like the "boss fight" I just got through in the third "area" of the game. I just hate that I died to it like 7+ times on the last section (not that you lose any progress, mind) because it's got both an expanding insta-kill field *and* walls that require powers to shut down *and* lots of spinning brackets that don't allow an easy/fast path through *and* the game expects you to boost through the whole thing *and* a thing you have to shoot at the end so you *also* need to line up a shot while doing all the previous stuff. It *is* a momentary challenge, and I think if the game wasn't auto-killing me while I did all of it I'd have a better time. Also, the final section of that fight literally takes place *inside* a health-drain field, so you're completely at the mercy of the game actually having the boss teleport in and *stay* corporeal long enough for you to kill it. Theoretically, you can do that final "finishing off the boss" segment completely standing still and just occasionally using the dodge maneuver, but a few times in a row the boss spawned a damage pillar right on top of me, constituting an instant-kill when combined with the damage field and presumably doing so to prevent players just turreting the boss there.Imagine playing the game for (at the time of writing) 9+ hours, then getting to this boss, and then after doing the whole boss flawlessly you fly into a pillar at the wrong time and die to crash damage because you go bouncing around inside the tunnel. Imagine you do *that* part flawlessly, and instead you get into that final showdown and the boss just tries to spawn where you are, and it goes "oh, can't do that", so he goes incorporeal again, and doesn't spawn for a second interval. Now you die to chip-damage from the damage field you can't get out of, and your whole save gets deleted.Hell, my first death wasn't even an hour into the game. I was using the Speed Gates like the game TELLS YOU TO, and one of the NPC ships came outta left field and slammed their ship into me. Dead, to a passing Garbage Truck. Game Over, save deleted.Thankfully, I didn't have that feature turned on, but you'll never die to enemies in this game. Only ridiculous insta-kills and game-overs from a buggy/unclear mission. The dogfighting is fun, the enemies make you chase them around and you're constantly outnumbered, but they don't really pose *too* much of a threat because you get super cool OP teleporting powers and sick 360-no-scope drift powers to style on them with.I absolutely recommend this game; It's *lots* of fun and I keep finding myself coming back to shoot just a few more fighters down. Or maybe to get attacked by a big ship I get to fly through, shooting weak points and dodging turrets. Or to see what the last couple of powers are, since even the most basic ones like drifting or teleporting are extremely fun to use and make you feel like a *really good* pilot. Just... don't bother with that Permadeath, I don't know why it's even in there since it doesn't seem to affect anything else and doesn't have any kind of significant narrative weight that I can discern.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a bad game, but not very good either. Graphics are serviceable but not impressive even with all the settings maxed.The powers are the best thing about the game - they do mix things up a bit. The story is also a high point within the game, but it remains only so-so in the grander scheme.My biggest issues are with the controls though. Despite significant tweaking, I just cannot get the KB+M ship controls to feel comfortable. As a space shooter, 6 degrees of freedom makes sense (3 axes of rotation, 3 of movement) but instead we get 2.5 degrees (2 axes of rotation, 0.5 of movement). Not long into the game you unlock an inertial glide to shoot in a different direction than moving, but ship rotation remains sluggish, and apparently the Chorus world has high friction space that slows you down as you glide. The lack of roll and constantly being reoriented "upwards" is annoying too, but is overshadowed by the other problems - particularly the lack of any maneuvering thrusters.Overall the game is perfectly playable and I didn't have any technical issues, but I'll probably just reinstall Everspace (which was great) when I need to scratch my itch for space shooters.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Chorus has engaging (if easy) combat that is a lot of fun. The story is kind of meh and there are a few weird things (a lot of the side quests treat NPC ships as if they were people, for example rescue NPC that's being tortured, the ship of the NPC is inside a torture  field, or that you have to fly up to NPCs to talk to them... I wish there was an arcade mode where you can just shoot things. All in all, if you like  arcadey space shooters it's  quite a great game, but don't expect too much on the story side.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Cool story-focused space dogfighter with interesting environments, many fully-voiced side quests, and fun moment-to-moment gameplay. Don't expect super-realistic combat where you have an unlimited top speed and it takes ages to turn around, but instead expect a game that lets you drift and dash around the battlespace, with powerups and environments that change how you fight. My only complaint is that the game has a shop system that is rather superfluous, since the best items come from missions.Overall, lots of fun and worth purchasing at full price for fans of sci-fi, arcade flying, and story-driven games.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game, the graphics on it are just amazing. It has a real easy flow to the game but it isn't so simple that it becomes boring. There are some challenges with getting used to the physics of some of the game play itself but that's just typical learning curve type scenarios that you find with all new games. Once you get a feel for the game it's one that draws you in and keeps you going. Though the story is a redemption story and one that isn't overly unique or original it is executed well and doesn't take away from the game play itself. Simply put it's hours of just fun and beautiful scenery.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: To this game's credit, the concept and gameplay are generally pretty cool. There's few games that make dogfights fun to me, especially space-based ones, but this is a mild exception to that. Even then, it's still not perfect.Target lock-on is practically non-existent, making fights that should otherwise be relatively quick take far longer than it feels like they should be taking.The story is, honestly, boring. I don't care about the story enough to go through the entirety of the campaign while the gameplay is mildly suboptimal, even if it is occasionally fun to glide through space.Overall, a 5/10 experience. Not memorable enough to warrant finishing it in my opinion, but it's a neat concept and especially good if you like space games where you control an extremely agile craft.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: I am not exactly an expert on shooting games. I play some here and there, but for the most part I prefer to play hack and slash type games. However, there are a few shooters that I really enjoyed playing (Bioshock, Doom, BPM: Bullets Per Minute), so I've started giving shooters more of a chance. While I wouldn't say Chorus is one of my new favorite shooting games, I'd say it's a solid 7/10.One of the main reasons I don't like shooters is that they're mostly cover shooters. What I mean by this is that the bullets are "realistic", so you can't dodge them. Instead, you're supposed to get behind cover and pick off enemies when it's safe to do so. I personally don't really enjoy this. This is why I enjoy Chorus a lot more, because you never have to "hide". This is because as long as you're "boosting" (going at a really fast speed by holding the L2 button), you'll automatically dodge most enemy attacks.That's not to say that the game is easy. While normally being able to automatically dodge attacks would be broken in most games, it's not in a space shooter like Chorus. This is because there's a lot of gameplay elements that you have to master since the game becomes more and more challenging over time:	• There are 3 different weapons you need to switch between, because different weapons are effective against different types of enemies (lasers for shield damage, gatling for hull damage, and missiles for armor damage)	• There's a button you can press to "drift", which allows you to turn very quickly and go from enemy to enemy a lot faster (especially important if an enemy is chasing you from behind)	• There are certain attacks that can't be automatically dodged, so you need to do a barrel roll at the right time to dodge the attack	• Giant ship enemies get introduced, some of which you literally have to go inside them in order to take out various weak points so that the ship goes down in a giant explosion	• You have various special abilities at your disposal, including being able to instantly jump behind enemies, shocking enemies to disable them, becoming a shooting star to destroy any enemies in your way, and telekinetically controlling enemies to throw them against the wall/other enemies.Simply put, the game has a great difficulty/progression curve. Any time I was close to getting bored with the game and feeling it was getting repetitive, the game would introduce a new mechanic for me to enjoy playing around with. Generally speaking, pretty much everything that your ship can do is enjoyable to experience. It was fun using the different weapons. It was fun learning to switch between boosting and drifting seamlessly. It was fun using all of the abilities. Etc…A negative I'll say for this game, at least for me, is that while everything your ship can do was enjoyable to experience for the first few times, eventually it just became "ok" to do. I suspect it's because I like being up close and personal with my enemies a lot more than seeing them explode at a distance. Like, comparing to Doom, from the very beginning of the game until the end, I really enjoyed glory killing. I can't say it ever got old. I can't say the same for multiple things in Chorus. However, if you enjoy space ships and the sci-fi setting, you might enjoy the gameplay a lot more.This game is technically an open world game, but that's being very generous. Fundamentally, you're just going from location to location completing main quests, but you have the option to do side-quests. So it's basically like an RPG game, since there's very few side activities you can do in the "open world". I will say that the side quests are pretty rewarding to do, since some of the best items in the game are obtained from completing side quests.There's a progression system, but it's fairly lacklustre. You can upgrade your hull, shield, weapons, and can equip 3 different modifications. The hull and shield improvements are completely automatic since you just go to a shop and buy upgrades whenever you have the money to spare. The weapon improvements are also fairly automatic since there are 4 different tiers of weapons, and you always want to buy the higher tier of weapons since they have a higher DPS. While the modifications are a lot better (which is not saying much), there's really not a lot to sink your teeth into. The best thing I can say is that certain modifications are parts of "sets", and if you equip 2 or 4 items of the same set, you'll get a set bonus. These set bonuses can be pretty significant, but it's not like you're creating a "build" like in Diablo or Path of Exile or something. 3 choices is not a lot, and you'll very quickly determine the best modifications to suit your playstyle.There's a story, and pretty much every reviewer said it sucked. I agree. There are two big problems with the story:	• There's very little lore/world building: It feels like I am thrust into the middle of the story instead of at the end. This is because there's almost no explanation for things that really should have an explanation. Like, you're in a world where there's a cult who have basically magic powers, they're killing billions of people, there are basically monsters called "Faceless", etc… How do human beings have magic powers? What does this cult believe in so vehemently that they're willing to kill billions of people over it? What the hell are these "Faceless" monsters? Why the ♥♥♥♥ do the cult members keep saying "In Chorus"??? I could go on and on. 	• Everything is too easy for the main character: You're playing as a character (Nara) who has destroyed a planet, killing BILLIONS of people. She's also done a bunch of other horrible things. Like, she's a real piece of ♥♥♥♥ and one of the worst characters you'll ever play as. That's fine. I am all for a redemption arc. But I HATE when everything is so easy for her. For example, Nara left a sentient AI ship (Forsa) alone for SEVEN YEARS, and she was planning on leaving him alone FOREVER. Forsa calls her out for it and is angry. Nara simply says "Please forgive me", and Forsa goes "Ok, but we're equals now"……… that's WAY too easy. Things like this happen very often. At the end of the game, you're supposed to accept that Nara is this beacon of harmony because she's accepted her faults…….screw that ♥♥♥♥. Like, if Hitler did a few nice things here and there and had "accepted his faults", that doesn't suddenly make him a beacon of harmony. Simply put, the writers are trying to do WAY too much. It's one thing to do a redemption arc. It's another thing to try to make you accept that a character who has killed billions is a beacon of harmony by the end of the story. Overall, I enjoyed playing this game. While I didn't enjoy the story, I definitely enjoyed the gameplay since the game did a great job of constantly and steadily introducing new mechanics so that I remained engaged throughout my time with the game. If you can look past a mediocre story and enjoy the gameplay, Chorus is definitely an enjoyable time.

_childDocuments_.review: (Note: This review contains spoilers)In the past 10 years, we've seen an explosion of space games, even as the games who lit the fuse failed to meet expectations (*cough* starcitizenandelite *cough). What sets apart Chorus?It's an open-world (five systems with a few special areas) space shooter with fantasy elements. You play a remorseful former member of a massive cult that is trying to take down what she helped create. About a quarter way through the game, you reunite with your sentient starship, which allows you to preform supernatural abilities and perform maneuvers that would normally have lethal G-forces. These abilities allow you to perform incredibly satisfying kill sequences and pre-empts the usual "circular dance of death" dogfights a lot of space games game.Most missions are fun, although there are some repetitive "emerging threat" missions that I ended up ignoring. There are some corridor missions which I just wanted to get over with. There aren't a ton of massive battles, but what the game does have, including the climax, are awesome.Now, addressing the biggest complaint people have: the main character. Her whispering inner monologue is...annoying. It's fine to have an internal voice, but do you have to whisper everything?The plot itself is fairly bog standard, with some interesting twists on how the cult makes intelligent spaceships. The final sequence (again spoilers) I found stupid and a let down. After you kill the big bad, said big bad does a voiceover that boils down to "I failed so she could succeed" before the credits roll. Yeah... okay buddy. Sure. It was unnecessary addition that should have left out, and puts a bit of a damper on what is otherwise a very solid and engaging shooter.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful locations, good graphics, fun space/aerial combat.  It has an interesting story, although somewhat convoluted and laden with obscure lore and religious influences.  The voice acting of the main two characters is good, but the supporting characters’ voices are hit and miss.  Game itself is very polished, with zero bugs encountered.It took me about 25 hours to finish everything (main campaign and side-missions).Overall, a solid 7.  Recommended, especially at its low price point.

_childDocuments_.review: Female Space Jesus Saves the Universe. Again. - A Feminist Space OperaThis game annoyed me starting at the title screen, where a female chorus (see what I did there) scream loudly at you. Female, emotional music instead of space opera, and you already know what to expect. It's another feminism simulator, this time in space!I'm not talking about the "good" feminism we know from the past, which was all about equality, but the modern one, where women are elevated into almost perfect beings, at the cost of all men. Bumbling buffons, failures, weaklings and cowards is the usual way they are represented. They're basically the same like the people who write these stories.The game has the modern storytelling trope where the main character doesn't shine through her actions, but we're just constantly told by side characters how "perfect" she is. *yawn*Nara is very boring and uninteresting, mumbling (and often whispering) along about her sad past, her guilt for what she did and how she wants to redeem herself. She keeps repeating this over, and over, and over in all sorts of ways, until you don't even listen anymore while she's mumbling or whispering along. Overall I'm extremely uninterested in the story, I don't care what happens to her, any side characters, or any other factions.Gameplay wise it's an open world space shooter, with missions and side missions, stuff to explore, and obviously also the main mission. You can upgrade and exchange your ships weapons, and add two upgrades to it. The guns level up themselves by using, apparently.The shooting is pretty solid, but nothing that hasn't been done before (and better). Overall if you must have a space shooter game and don't care about story or characters, you can find some enjoyment in this. If you love Woke Garbage, go ahead and buy it right away.I personally regret not buying it directly on Steam, because now I can't refund it.UPDATE: I played this game twice after I made the video. First time I ALT-F4'd out of it after about 10 minutes. Second try, a few days later, I ALT-F4'd out of it after 30 minutes. It's flashback after flashback after flashback, which are presented as screenshots of what happened (a bunch of spaceships, for instance), that she uncovers with her magic. Of course she whispers along the images and I can't remember having seen any more boring way to present a story in a game. Then a short fight, and we're back to her magically scanning the universe for more screenshots of what happened, so she can whisper some more... uhh. No thank you!

_childDocuments_.review: WowOkay, so this game is completely awesome. I remember back in the day playing games like Colony Wars and such and this... this really gives me that feeling, the kind of space fighter sim where you're not running a million different things like a battlemech, focusing more on the story and fighting aspects of the game. The controls on the gamepad are really good, responsive, well done. The story is lengthy and fulfilling so far.It does have some minor flaws though. For example you can be in the middle of a conversation and if you're flying around it can get interrupted. Also it has a glitch where the upload bar disappears when doing a sidequest... it's not strictly necessary to be there, but it's annoying. The most major gripe I have is the game has the cookie crumbs leading to other places and I'm not always sure when i should be pursuing them. Also, if you load the game it seems to throw you straight into a mission sometimes, which is annoying.Understand, these gripes don't wreck the game at all. For a fresh game it's nice that the bugs are so minor and not many and it didn't require a bunch of patching right off.For $40 I feel this was fully worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm pretty disappointed, because this game had so much potential, but ultimately fell flat in nearly every area, except aesthetic.Here are my problems with the gameplay:1. For being a space combat game, the level designs and especially the flight system is somehow more vertical than any of the other aerial combat games I've played, which take place within the atmosphere of Earth or an Earth-like planet.2. While there are some unique enemy types, and the game does a pretty decent job with timing enemy introductions, the differences aren't really drastic enough in most cases to make the combat any more interesting, save for one, which is essentially a mini-environment. This is pretty much the only enemy type I've had fun fighting, and also my only source of excitement in this game.3. Save for one exception, nearly all of the combat in this game is just some combination of drift, shoot, drift, shoot, drift, shoot, over and over until you kill everything that's shooting at you. The only nuance to this is that some enemies have shields, which are weak to a different weapon type, so you switch weapons to deal with them.4. Every area you can visit is just an asteroid field with a slightly different layout, which just makes going to a system you've already been to for a side mission exhausting.The premise, theme, characters, etc. were all set up to be insanely cool and unique, but everything just kinda fell flat. It feels like someone was feeling especially creative and came up with a whole universe, made up of a bunch of cool concepts that they came up with, without considering how they would fit together, complete with a broad, overarching narrative. Aside from these things, it feels like everything else in this game was improvised as they went along.Also, the music/atmosphere gets a solid "meh"/10.In summary, the ship designs are cool, but the story is boring, the characters feel 2-dimensional, the scenery is pretty much copy-paste, and the combat feels like it's actively making me worse at playing games.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: The game's mechanics leaves a lot to be desired.Poor mission design and lack of 6-axis controls in a game that goes from open space to confined interior is nothing short of amazingly dumb development choices.. The flight model is somewhere between Freespace and Everspace and somehow fails to be anywhere near as good as either. The sense of speed in open combat is quite good, but in confined interiors it is just way too sluggish, and the bouncy collision physics is just awful.Story is quite good so far, but the last (?) part was infuriating due to the flight model they went with. If a sequel is in the works, please do better.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a positive experience - a lot of good, but some bad.  If you like the fighter combat of something like X4 but in a framework of sporadic superpower fights like Control (also, all the rectangles of Control), you'll have fun here.The combat really is the star of the show here.  It's varied and extremely satisfying, and maintains a challenge via attention - you have a small ship and can be killed very quickly if you're idle, but can defeat vastly greater forces more easily the more engaged with the systems you get.  I loved this.The downside of the combat is that it can be hard to come by, especially later in the game.  Once I unlocked my last power, I barely had anyone to enjoy fighting with it - a shame, since it was fun.  There are no enemy systems or areas you can go to just fight - best you can do is fly in a circle hoping a wave of enemies spawn, and it's usually just a small number of easy ones.The story is engaging.  Not the best I've played recently, but the writing was good enough that I really wanted to see everything through.  I particularly liked the transformation of the player character, which was the true focus.The real side quests are mostly fun, even if some of the writing on them isn't very believable, it works out gameplay wise.The random encounter 'quests'...oof.  I mentioned the combat ones, fun but usually very easy, even in late game areas.  The non combat ones are much worse, most of them are just "fly to this ship, press X, wait for progress bar, here's 1000 credits."The art style is very good, graphics on the larger ships and structures aren't fantastic but they express the desired mood, and the small ships look great.  The skyboxes are nice as well, and, well, it's in space, you'll see a lot of them.The pacing is not great.  Sometimes you're barraged by conversations that overlap and cut each other off - and often happening after some big event when a bit of travel or downtime to think would be best.  Other times you're completely idle.  Room for improvement here.The mission/save system is terrible.  You'll find yourself frustratingly replaying things you already succeeded at, because 'missions' are like a local instanced area.  Plus, not being able to save for long periods - not for difficulty, just due to the design - is frustrating and inconvenient.The minimal HOTAS support is very disappointing, ended up switching to a mouse and keyboard, but it has the X4-style ship mouse controls so it was doable.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't really know what to expect with this game. Added it to my wishlist when it was announced. Story is pretty interesting so far. The main character has this internal monologue that reminds me a bit of Hellblade. Also has a power that lets her sense things. HMMMMM. Anyway the shooting feels good once you get used to the controls. Sorta like Descent and Forsaken. There is a map that shows various locations you can visit. Some have to be found with the sense power or exploring. You can find NPC's with various quest for you to accomplish. They are optional but worth doing because they give good rewards that can power you up for the main quest. You can find credits or power ups while exploring.
