_childDocuments_.review: This is like the exact that ProZD sketch about games that think more gameplay mechanics equals more fun? Yeah this feels exactly like that. This game 100% should have been a linear game, there is no reason it needed to be open world all it does is add unnecessary padding and some really boring side quests. One of which I got right before the final mission was to sit by an NPC ship to give them gas.The story was meh. I honestly started to tune out about midway through which didn't really hamper anything as I could guess at most of the plot; another thing that would have been helped if this game was more linear and there was between mission cut scenes.The one saving grace of this game is that the combat is amazing! Flying past an enemy, drifting to line up a shot, blasting them apart before streaking towards the next enemy. It was all really well done and I didn't even end up using all the abilities (though personally I found the pick up and throw one kind of worthless, it took to long to use and was impossible to aim). If the game was just linear arena fighting I would 10/10 recommend it. The problem is there is just a lot of sitting around listening to NPC's, or slaloming around slow NPC ships as they go from one place to another. Things that shouldn't be a problem because they shouldn't need to be in this game! There was also no skip dialog button I could find during these scenes so all replay value is gone. Also why do I have to hold down on A to purchase something in the shop? This isn't a criticism directed solely at this game lots of games do it and it annoys me so much. Makes bulk purchasing things a complete pain in the ass.Near the end I was all set to not recommend this game. It was so close to just being so boring I couldn't even recommend the good parts. But damn it it got me with the final mission. I'm a sucker for just an all out fleet battle and that's what this pulled out at the last mission and then had a really good "Ultimate Boon" moment where you just rip through the enemy ships and finish the final boss off. And you know what? Yeah, I'll give you that game. You pulled out of the doldrums at the last minute and nailed the finish line. Shame that you over stretched yourself all the way throughout
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Chorus is an impressively substantial game for the $40 price point. A full Normal difficulty run took me almost 17 hours to complete doing most of the available sidequests -- although I apparently missed a bunch according to the achievements. Much longer and more story-focused than I was expecting.I'll start with some of the things that annoyed me: There are a lot of segments especially toward the second half where you'll just instafail a section due to being in the wrong place. There are some fights that should feel epic but are instead frustrating because whoops you didn't get out of the big red beam in the .1 seconds it took to spawn. Fortunately the checkpointing is VERY generous and you'll never have to repeat a boss phase. There's also not a whole lot of weapon variety for a space shooter where you only get one ship and I wanted more options in general. Doesn't seem to be an NG+ yet, which is a little disappointing as you get some of the rites very late into the story and I'd like to replay the game with all my powers intact. Those minor complaints aside, Chorus was a pleasant surprise and I'm already thinking about doing a second run on the hardest difficulty. The combat is fun and flashy with just enough variety to keep things interesting, the inclusion of telekinetic powers is just a genius addition, the sound design is superb, and there are some really impressive visuals throughout. The developers did not let the smaller budget affect the quality of the presentation or controls. When you're flying through some crazy red lighting storm assaulting a huge capitol ship, skewering the bad guys with your psychic fighter jet, that's just good game feels right there. But I think what surprised me most about Chorus was the story. Fundamentally it's a super basic "unite the factions against the Evil Space Empire" kind of deal, but I was into all the little twists and turns along the way. I loved the threeway dynamic between Nara, her sassy backtalking ship, and her cynical inner monologue ASMR. I like games that, for want of a better phrase, "just go for it" and Chorus 100% goes there with its narrative beats.I think if you're a fan of solidly B-tier single-player action adventure games that attempt to tell a focused narrative without looking like some horrible piece of crap, you will thoroughly enjoy Chorus. I'd place it alongside Hellblade, A Plague Tale, and Control as one of my favorites from the last few years.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Played entirely on the Steam Deck with no issues.Chorus is an open space arcade space shooter. There's a main story which will take you about 10-15 hours depending on how many side quests you take on. The game focuses on Nara, the pilot and her spacecraft. The fun thing about Chorus, and what sets it apart from other games like it, is the rite abilities. Chorus takes the typical space dogfight formula and allows you to use mystical space magic to teleport, boost forward, or instantly disable other ships for a few seconds. It was super fun drifting around in space and using the powers to eliminate your enemies like an overpowered god. The story revolves around Nara, your pilot. Eventually you learn about her escape from a Space Cult and the eventual fight against them. There wasn't anything groundbreaking here, but I did enjoy it. My only gripe with the game were the boss fights. They were tough and maybe a little too long. But if you use your powers effectively, you can overcome them. I would recommend this game for a fun take on dogfighting.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: A great space combat game, with very good mechanics – the idea of combining dogfighting with “magical” abilities is very clever, and something I wish other games would try.Chorus has its flaws: the game is somewhat rough around the edges (I kept expecting some kind of game breaking bug, but it actually never came), the story loses its focus on the last third, and bosses are a massive difficulty spike. But the game has amazing combat, featuring “rites” that are basically supernatural abilities allowing the player character to perform incredible stunts. Production value is very high, graphics are good, voice acting is nice (play with headphones!), and the storyline and worldbuilding are interesting, especially when focusing on the bond between the main character and her ship.I strongly recommend this game to fans of Wing Commander and other space combat games.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game with a very interesting story. It was a tad slow to start, but once you get some abilities and upgrades things open up. You get nice open world maps to explore with lots of side content and items to discover. Beautiful graphics and level design, some of the rift worlds and temples left me in awe. The story is very interesting and seems to draw inspiration from Senua's Sacrifice and has lots of internal monologue and hits on subjects of dealing with emotions and mental struggle. Gameplay is phenomenal, Similar to like an advanced Starfox, but not on the rails and far more fast paced. Fans of Arcade space combat games should feel right at home here, as the Dev's say easy to pick up and hard to master. Coming from games like Elite Dangerous, I wish there was some HOTAS support, but the controller does it justice. My two biggest gripes would be Lack of HOTAS support and no First person perspective, other than that give this title a shot. There is a demo and the game speaks for itself. Don't miss out on this one.

_childDocuments_.review: With my 3 hours of hands on Early Access to the game with a big thanks to  here is my review for . is a action packed space shooter with incredibly satisfying combat, a great feel for story talent and a beautiful graphical experience.From the moment I dropped into the game to my trusty buddy  I was constantly put into the front seat. I quickly learned that doing side missions could greatly pay for getting me ship into shape and change the outcome of fights I may otherwise would be unprepared for.For new players I definitely recommend investing into evolving your ship, upgrading it as much as possible and picking up side missions that can give you anything from weapons and credits up to Rifts that give you exciting new abilities.Usually the areas of side missions as well as your main story line have small boxes scattered that provide you with credits and upgrades.  also does a excellent job on making searching around for new items, using your guns or taking on enemies a enjoyable experience thanks to their mastery system that upgrades your guns, senses(these increase your reward gained from small boxes.) and other items through out for example killing enemies, taking down shields or searching for these boxes that are scattered around the galaxies.In terms of performance I noticed a few small lag spikes and keeping in mind I did run the game while streaming in with maximized graphics on a Laptop with a RTX 2080 Super and Intelcore i7 10th Gen definitely tells me game is optimized in a great way but does have its performance hits especially in heavily crowded areas or areas where a lot of fighting is going on.Overall a lot of laptop gamers will be happy to know that on a rig that runs for example a GTX 1050ti or a GTX1060 3GB you be able to run this game in medium to high graphics without any noticable performance hits.For Desktop gamers a rig with either a GTX or RTX card will give you a wonderful experience. I would have to say that the controls are easy to learn with support for both Xbox and  controllers with possibly support for 3rd party controllers like for example  Gaming controllers. I played with a mouse and keyboard and learning the keys was quick although just as a personal preferred option I did like to be able to set ship speeds changing keys to scroll wheel up and down.The game its difficulty is greatly balanced but there are a few hickups. I started my live playthrough on the hard difficulty and in my first boss encounter had to scale back to Medium due to not being familiar enough with the drifting mechanics(on mouse and keyboard you can drift by holding the right mouse button while boosting with shift and using your mouse movement to drift into certain directions) but once I entered the first mission in which "Sav" his wfe "Ree" was under attack of enemies from the circle and I had to deal with 3 ships with a big shields, a good amount of smaller enemies and a time to beat before my allied ships got destroyed I noticed that I had almost no chance winning the ships and been able to only take down 1 ship out of the 3 I had to take out. is a extremely enjoyable game with incredibly satisfying combat that connects well with its combat, although I noticed some small performance hits in crowded areas and the fact that I stood no chance against 3 ships and a big handful of smaller ships I would rate . 10 10 7 8 10 7I hope this review helped everyone here on Steam in considering on purchasing the game or not!Again thanks to  for providing both my Twitch channel  and YouTube channel vidDojo  access to this incredible piece of art and I have a special video still coming out regarding this written review!

_childDocuments_.review: This was a game I bought with middling expectations.  Within the first hour it far exceeded them.  The combat is fun and reactive.  The Rites you gain make you feel powerful.   The story was engaging though not ground breaking.  It gave the game a consistent narrative that made you want to see what was coming next.All in all,  a damn fine game.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a great game. I don't play many flying games so the mechanics had a learning curve but once I figured it out, it was smooth sailing. It has a good story, graphics and controls. My only complaint would be that there isn't a whole in the way of upgrading weapons--upgrades are more focused on utility/power mods. _childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is story driven with some randomized (?) content on the side. There are only 7 areas to explore (not counting the number of story relevant instances), and while the content provides between 10-20 hours of entertainment, I cannot escape the feeling of wanting more. This said, it is a self-contained and internally consistent story. I love what they did with the characters, their flaws and their sacrifices. The final battle invoked the feeling of what Mass Effect 3's end should have been.The gameplay is solid, the mechanics are fair, it is a start for something greater, the story is small but enjoyable. This is The One.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: It feels like: If mass effect started with the full invasion of the reapers, Shepard was alone and no alien species ( so far). _childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Chorus has really good space fighter mechanics, and a cool setting. Flying around and having to pause for weird memories and going into these stupid Temple puzzles... Was tedious and took me away from my time as a space fighter pilot. I will probably finish the game eventually, but I get stuck in every single one of those Temple puzzles and just stop playing for a few weeks.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying it.  In the latter half feels a bit like a superhero game with you warping and charging and zapping all manner of hapless enemy spaceships. Fights are fun and intense in a way that I could never find by slowly rotating until I was behind an enemy ship. It's arcadey both in combat feel and in that they've pared down stuff like fuel management (there is none!), inventory space (if it's ship gear carry whatever! if it's not ship gear it doesn't exist!), ammo (unlimited!), repairs (repair automatically between fights!) and anything else until you're either spending time exploring or fighting.It Starts Slow but after about an hour and a half you'll really see where it's going.The story isn't great but it's okay. They're trying, and I appreciate it. But man, the combat once you've unlocked a few powers is really fun.One of the first things you unlock is "drifting", which is to say rotating your ship quickly while you maintain your vector. That makes for some useful combat applications, but it REALLY picks up maneuvering as you can now boost, drift, boost (boost is unlimited) to make really sharp turns.It's also just, like, not a slog at any point? Like even travelling the longest distances the game has doesn't feel like something you'd want to maybe make some coffee for. I never feel like I need to brace myself to manage cargo slots and market prices while keeping some money for some repairs because I didn't get through the last fight gracefully.There are some design bits that are a touch half-baked, specifically a couple boss fights where suddenly you're taking DOT no matter where you are, you need to get to a certain place and do a thing, but there's a very good chance you'll be on 1/4 health and thus won't have anywhere near the means to accomplish said thing, or like, some minor missions where it's kind of a cake walk due to balance, but nothing really ruins anything, and the checkpointing on boss fights is generous enough that I never felt like "ugh now I gotta do all that other stuff again".And then a very minor UI complaint, which is that you find/buy parts to upgrade shields and hull strength, and that's fine, but when you get a new part it doesn't show you your progress towards the next tier, and doesn't even tell you when you've achieved it.Overall, it's great.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: I know there are some negative reviews, but look. I have many many games in my library and I dont complete a lotbecause I get bored half way through, but this little game stays nice and chrisp till the end.It has a good story and plays like a arcade shooter. The graphics are good as well.If you want some clean fun while flying a space craft this is a game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: I'm about 80% through so I feel pretty confident in saying that this game is def a hidden gem and should be checked out (there's a demo even)!Pros:* Real fun combat* Gorgeous environments & sound* Movement is crazy good and makes for some fun puzzle missionsCons:* Story is a little all over the place* Some side missions are boringHonestly, if you like classic air combat games like star fox, ace combat & rogue squadron this is going to be right up your alley.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: I'll open with saying that I enjoyed this game a lot.Control scheme is simple and a tad odd from the usual WASD and QE for roll. Story is so and so but keeps consistency very well throughout the game that I didn't even notice or cared, didn't challenge my suspension of disbelief as most games nowadays do.Game drip feeds you new weapons and skills at a comfortable pace, letting you accomodate to each one without overwhelming you.People complain that the  writers over exaggerated with explanations, but I personally feels they went for a bit of that Hellblade:Senua's sacrifice madness with the whispers. I liked it.The combat is simple, but fun, it's just fun. It's so much fun.My only complaint is that there's no area to go at and just have mindless endless combat, especially if you're looking to finish some achievements. There are a couple of places where enemies will respawn until objectives are met, but usually you're too lost in the objective /having fun  to remember that you should grind.Overal a nice, well rounded game.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: I was pulled in by visuals and the story it advertised, however was not able to make it past the first few missions due to a glitch where settings would not apply to the game itself. This effecting sensitivity settings, auto aim, and turning settings made it basically unplayable. After a miserable 2 hours of fighting oversensitive controls, I had to give up.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Chorus is a very well-designed futuristic space-combat game. At many levels, it beats the Ace Combat series at delivering a better 'flight-kick'. You don't start off with special abilities; they are gradually earned to seemingly make combat more progressively fluid or 'In Chorus'. I started the game in medium difficulty settings using keyboard and mouse controls. Because much of the combat, at least initially, involves non-locking weapons like the gatling gun and laser, using a mouse tends to be less fun. The controller system provides grounding for the Right Joystick, whereas with the mouse there's no grounding. This is very apparent in a space flight combat game. You even develop a mature astronaut wear after a few hours of gameplay. The story isn't that immersive, but the gameplay and music is. I was forced to switch from Medium difficulty to Easy during an 'escort' mission where I had to face 3 or 4 Vultures and a host of other enemies; it was a little too annoying and I factored 'fun' as my prime as I switched to easy mode. I beat Doom Eternal on Nightmare and at no point did it ever stop being fun. The game's fun now: the flight experience hasn't changed, but combat is a lot less 'dragged-out' and 'navigable'.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't really a review so much as it is me excited as kid on Christmas, that I finally got this game. Played the demo the first day it was available on Xbox and knew immediately I wanted the full game. I avoided cutscenes and story stuff, saving it for when I could experience it how the devs intended. I somehow missed any and every sale it might have been a part of for over a year now but caught it on sale this morning. At this point I could end up piloting a flat tire and firing corn ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ outta my butthole and I wouldn't care. Been in massive need of a slick space shooter with a cool @$$ story. [in a whisper] "You've found the one you've been searching for..."
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: If you like arcady space shooters I can recommend!I played the demo first and then bough the main game - Its a great game overall! Random thoughts:The Demo doesn't do it justice though, the controls are explained through text rather than beeing executed one by one in a tutorial, which makes it a little fiddly to get into. Especially when you try playing with a controller it feels overwhelming. This is fixed in the main-game though!Personally, I reverted back to mouse and keyboard in the end, which is my primary setup anyway, but I wanted to give the gamepad a chance, but couldn't get comfortable with.This game is really polished and feels like the team knew its achievable scope well.Once you master the drifting controls and the rituals in combination with your weapons, its a lot of fun to crush through enemies.VFX is really good in this game and I jumped into photomode once in a while just to take a peek :DIf you're going to tackle the side missions, be prepared for quite a few long travels with the ship. The travels are interrupted/bridged by repetitive "we are in danger..." calls (you don't have todo them, but you kinda want to because money), I would have whished for a bit more variety or at least different dialog lines. You'll receive unique equipment in side-missions so it pays of todo them.The game features a variety of enemies and I really liked taking down the big battleships. The first boss battle felt refreshing after I've spent quite some time shooting down enemies with the same tactics over and over.Throughout the game you will visit different systems, each featuring areas of interest. Exploring them was okay. Even though ships are flying around once in a while, the locations feel empty and lifeless.Note: After playing the demo and then buying the game, you will see the demo-savegame in the main-game, don't continue from that, but start over. It took me a moment to realize there's nothing todo if you continue from it. Weirdly enough that it is displayed and not wiped after buying the game.

_childDocuments_.review: After turning the dialogue volume to 0 and subtitles off, this game is enjoyable, more than enjoyable actually - it's great when being able to focus on the gameplay rather than the cringe dialogue and monologue.It's similar to games like Star Fox, Everspace and Galaxy on Fire which was developed by Fishlabs as well.

_childDocuments_.review: I did not get this when it came out as was a backer for everspace 2 and was playing the beta of that for my space fix. Now ive finished everspace 2 i decided to pick this up. _childDocuments_.review: Probably one of the best space action games you've never played.It's not perfect - the story is good, and while the main characters are well-written, the supporting cast is mixed and some of the storylines seem unfinished. The level of polish on a technical level is impressive, minus some strange pop-ins that happened once or twice. The game is challenging but fair - it may seem really hard at first, but it gets significantly easier as you improve your skills and equipment.I almost bounced off this game because the beginning was very lackluster. I recommend rushing to unlock Forsa ASAP as it changes the way the game plays significantly.

_childDocuments_.review: Complete garbage. the utter embodiment of modern developers having no clue. Between an awful introduction, which is just a re-skinned Star Wars story with absolutely 0 originality, an annoying as hell protagonist who can't stop whispering utter bull in your ear constantly, poor controls and a focus on exploration over action early game, I had 0 desire to continue with this after a very short period of time. _childDocuments_.review: What an absolute labor or love this game was! One of the best space flying/dog fight games I have played with a great story to tell. It is totally worth its price tag if not more. I highly recommend getting this game.Pros:> Atmosphere, really captures space, flight, and fighting.> Graphics in the word really shown while flying around> Story: philosophical, immersive, and all the side missions were great as well you got more enriched into the lore the more you explored and interacted with, > Voice acting was amazing and a huge cast, although some parts were a little cheesy, overall well done> Ship upgrades are limited to 3 slots, you're always sacrificing something for something else but that apart of the challengeCons:> Difficult, in general, & especially at the boss. It's highly recommended you do all the side missions as that's the only way to get a bunch of power ups and money to buy better parts.> Flying is still some of the best I've ever played, but at the same time there's always tight curved corners constantly and you just end up crashing unless you slow down (see net bullet)> The Ship flies to fast for your own good, to steer evasively, but then moves too slow to keep up with time sensitive objectives. Sacrificing all your speed for maneuverability around those corners/environment
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: I finished this game on hard.Played it with a gamepad.The only time i found this game to be hard, was when i was battling a boss. Without spoilering to much, the 2 main bosses are rediculous, but doable, whether you get a hang of it or not.Controls take a little bit getting used to, but once you realise that your main manouverability comes from your abilities its great. This also means that early game you might get frustrated with the turn rate of your ship for example. But once you get your first real ability, its a whole different game.So take all the hate about bad controls with a grain of salt. Yes its more ability focussed, but its not bad. Once you get a hang of it, and learn how to chain your abilities you are literally a flying god and can beat anything the game throws at you.However i would really recommend playing with a gamepad.If anything i found that the normal opponents could be more aggresive to make them more of a challenge.Gameplay wise its very much a RPG on rails. Which means there are fair bits of exploration and the main story line is linear. But there are plenty of sidequests to spend your time on and random encounters to fill in some of the breaks between the main action.Overal i found Chorus to be an enjoyable experience. And if i would have to critique it, it would be that i feel like the main boss gameplay design could be better. But that should not stop anyone from trying out this game.Also i haven't played the demo. Many people struggle with it apparently in terms of difficulty. But i don't think this translates to the actual game.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Chorus will honestly go down as one of the best games I played in 2021, period. It combined storytelling and the feeling of being a complete badass from Ace Combat/ Bioshock, with the space combat experience of Everspace/ Strike Suit Zero. It's also one of the prettiest games I've played, and well optimized at that too; with even single use assets being of a really high quality. The game is a technical and storytelling masterpiece. I never felt as though my time was wasted, and new mechanics were paced REALLY well, constantly adding what I can do/ had to look out for instead of dumping everything from the get-go. Hell, even going into the final act, new mechanics were being thrown at me.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a blast.  The abilities and weapons are fun to use and the mobility of flight and drift are smooth as butter.  Spearing enemy groups makes you feel like a force to be recommended with.  I like how the game doesn't make you feel like a "normal" pilot like in every other flight sim / 4x / etc.  The skills work great with the fast paced combat and the RPG aspects come in the form of finding items to upgrade your systems, improve them, or use skills a number of times to increase their perks.

_childDocuments_.review: What a pleasant surprise. Great graphics, fun gameplay loop, and pretty interesting and different take on the space shoot genre. Drifting is awesome and now I can't play other space games without it lol. Game does a great job making you feel awesome as you move through upgrading - by the end, you feel like a total bada--!Highly recommend picking this one up and I hope there is a sequel and/or other devs use concepts Chorus presented. In Chorus!
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Cool game. It starts off quiet and relatively slow but it does nothing but grow and grow. Once you get your actual ship (not the one you start the game with), the game really picks up speed. Your ship is sentient, so there's a lot of dialog between your character and the ship (which builds on the story really well) so you are not just flying around quietly. Combat is very fast paced, little dogfights. You mostly fly around in an asteroid field that's full of stations and junk and mines and temples and all kinds of intractable things. You can drift around other ships to get behind them to find their weak spot.The maps are pretty big with lots of collectibles to find and places to see. Quests galore, some are only activated when you fly to a (?) on your map. And there's multiple maps (systems) to fly to via warp gates. The graphics are amazing. It is a very polished game.It has controller support, and all keyboard controls are fully customizable in the settings. The missions can be quite long and you can only manually save when you are not on a mission. During missions, the game auto saves your progress at certain points/waypoints.Your ship has multiple weapons and multiple "gear" slots which are all up-gradable via the base store or as quest rewards or in loot boxes strewn about. You also have special "powers" that gradually unlock as you play so you aren't overwhelmed with having everything all at once.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: A surprisingly good, and lengthier than expected, game. The combat is extremely fulfilling and makes you feel like a badass. The story can get dragged down by exposition at times, but it is intriguing. A great game if you're a fan of arcade-y space dogfighting, don't expect any realistic physics here.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: I'm torn on this one. Chorus has a compelling gameplay, but it quite often gets too chaotic for me. It's even hard to track your targets when everything has similar colours. Lore is pretty interesting, but narrative and VO are as bland as it gets. It's also pretty, except that every location feels like a previous one: basically, it's always some asteroid mess.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: One of the big plus of this space shooter is the combat mechanics, the "rites" are able to break the conventional dogfight and the big ship take downs are well done. You will have some "♥♥♥♥ I'm a dogfight god" moments while blazing through enemies, very satisfying.Graphics and story are ok, overall a good game but you can feel with more money and/or time this could have been a masterpiece in its category. Can't wait to see what they will do if ever a second opus is released.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Honest game, knows what it is, doesn't oversell. Map management is kinda finicky, which detracts from the exploration experience. There's some focus on movement and intriguing dark fantasy touches. Battling big ships is enjoyable, but they could use a bit more detail. Battle feeling improves with stronger enemies. Skip side missions until you have your real ship. Solid 7.OKOK. The seven stands, maybe with a + or a small star. The story has a few subtle nuances I didn't immediately expect (or see from miles away. It is still a "not bad for a game" standard, it's still not a masterpiece). I managed to bring it to 100%, and it did get grindy towards the end, but it didn't lose me. It's a recommendation, wish there was a New Game Plus.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: I feel the game has a lot of potential. I really like the artwork, the graphics and the premise of the game, i.e. that of a "system" made of the pilot's (Nara's) abilities and the ship's equipment. Also, the open-ish world is, to me, an indication of a greater plan for the future of the game. There are already quite a lot of activities, including fights, races and mining. It's not an RPG, it's not a space combat game. It does both to a basic degree so far and this way it offers quite a bit of variety of gameplay.As it's just the 1.0 version of the game, I can forgive the following, but I do have to mention as downsides:- the voice acting is bad and that's a shame. The characters feel scripted, no engagement or feeling, just voice lines delivered blandly. I like the plot and the premise of the game, but the voice acting just feels cheap. - also at the audio department, I would like to hear more and louder music. The sound design so far is quite good, but I would appreciate more music and a louder volume, for better immersion;- some bugs for triggers of checkpoints/mission points. Sometimes, the next objective doesn't activate when it should or if you were supposed to find a package which should be somewhere around, sometimes it's missing until you do something like exit and re-enter the mission area or just pause and resume the game.So far, I really like the game and if you ask me, the perfect development would improve replayability and thus include:- more and more diverse abilities for Nara, to make it more or less of an RPG;- some missions on foot maybe, i.e. outside of the ship. Even simple, puzzle-games or basic combat or exploration would be nice. I do get the idea of the "unity" between the pilot and the ship, but it could be a good idea to have them separate for some tasks;- of course, more content, abilities, weapons, quests etc, as the map is promisingly large.I also appreciate the game being single player and I hope that even if it will ever include multiplayer, the single player content will be the focus.To sum up, I'm playing the game with an Xbox controller and I'm not good at it, I died quite a lot and lost tens of dogfights. But I'm having quite a lot of fun, so I do recommend it! Solid performance, beautiful graphics, very fun and quite diverse gameplay!
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: I gave Chorus a chance, since it's been years that i got to play this type of game. And what can i say...The combat is absolute ♥♥♥♥; garbage movement, garbage shooting, combine this with frustrating enemies and their movements. Every fight ist exactly the same:1. fly a curve all the time2. try to land a shot3. always use your medium thrustersIf you stop doing 1 and 3 it's instant death! I did'nt expect anything from Chorus and  was still disappointed. A game that only lives from it's combat and the devs deliver this.Can not recommend buying it.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: This game plays so well, you need to get a bit further into the story to get the more challenging encounters that force you to fully realise the the potential of the ship combat in this game. Its not that you cant do the cool tricks relatively early on, its that no encounter forces you to utilise all your tools until the second "act" of the game. The graphics are really nice. And very good performance too. Some ray traced games run like poop. But this is so smooth on an rtx 3070. I noticed 40% of the steam players haven even finished the intro yet. So I am guessing people bought it and haven't played it. If you are one of the lucky ones to already own the game, but haven't tried it yet cuz of other games. Give them a break and try this. The story is good, but I find it easier to vibe with the script writing if I tell my self it is directly translated from German to English at times. So yes forgive some of the awkward lines, they are rare but they are still there. Some people say you can't save for hours in this game. This is an illusion caused by how some of the main quests chain together. Just pay attention to the main name of the quest. You can abort it and not lose progress if the main name of the quest has just changed. This means you are on the next quest. Aborting lets you go off and save/do other side stuff etc. Take your time to do side quests, they will help you feel more attached to the cause/characters. Which makes the main quests feel deeper as you are more invested in the characters. So yes, the story is good, but perhaps put together in a rookie way.The menu music might be one of the best menu musics out there, along with Halo. Especially if you like really cool choirs. Through out the rest of the game its generally ambient music but for set pieces the choirs come back.. though maybe not as full on as I would like them to be. The main characters inner thoughts are portrayed as whispers to her self.. so yeah. Its cool but also a bit much at times. If you can survive Navi in Ocarina of Time then you're good, cuz this is no where near that level of intrusive. Its more like Hellblade. The game does not hold your hand as far as upgrading your ship goes, and I could not imagine facing the boss of the second act with out all the good loot I had on me by that point (I did all the side stuff up until then). At the same time I am doing my first play through on hard. Hard is punishing, but not dark souls. Difficulty is actually pretty linear if you do side quests too. Still I didn't know how much I loved this game until I beat the boss of the second act. The game does not stuff you full of political messaging like some games do today. The game plays really well out of the box. It's so refreshing actually. In the world of Live Service games and janky ass games like Bethesda and EA titles, this one is a good throw back to a time when games where made to just be a solid experience with out needing mods or waiting for updates etc etc yada yada. And on top of that its a "modern game" still at 2023. I don't think it will grow old any time soon either. Its honestly really underrated.This is not an accurate space sim game. Its not an RPG.. but has a strong narrative none the less. Choices don't always matter, but they sometimes do. I had made some alliances with certain people, spared certain people etc, and in act 2 this came together.If you like arcadey and visceral space combat games, or perhaps female protagonist games like Hellblade and you want to play something different give this a go. Its honestly a steal even at full price. If you like esoteric sci fi stories like.. Final Fantasy 0 or 7, Avatar, Nier.. stuff like that.. you will appreciate what this story is going for. The main plot is simple but there is like a sub plot which is somewhat introspective and deep. I honestly was worried I would regret buying this game, but wow.. no I am so happy I own a copy of this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Good gameplay and art style with a compelling setting to explore. The story is interesting but the limited 'radio conversations' style of dialogue gets a bit boring. Why is the main character whispering internal dialogue??? I really do not know and understand why. It's a good game to dip in and out of for intense 30 mins bursts of play. I think, longer sessions could be repetitive for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a bad game, it just feels 10 years out of date in a bad way. Nothing about it feels especially memorable or innovative. If you like spaceflight (and there is ONLY spaceflight, you never set foot outside your ship except in cutscenes) then it might be worthwhile on deep (DEEP) sale. This is not an RPG, this is an okay arcade space combat sim with some pretty visuals and a stock but passable story. Pretty typical lazy console port. Buy at $5.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: The story takes place in a big region of space where a cult took over and your character a previous cultist gone rogue taking the fight to them in a way.The controls arent frustrating, i mention this because my experience with Sci fi controls are the same as underwater (frustrating and anger inducing)The exploration well idk tbh, cause in a story focused game you wont get a lot of exploration, so i cant compare it with sci fi, but it gives you systems that you can explore while you do the main quests.Fun thing for me was most of the time i didnt have to go and search em out cause 1 - the map has points of interest each with a mission2 - you will mostly stumble into every side quest on your way to a main quest which i think made the game more fun for me.Plot can be confusing but i think i got a good gist of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Plays like game. Thumbs up. Buy on sale.I honestly enjoyed this game. Overall it's a decent play coming in under 20 hours. It's got all the pieces, just lacked polish in game flow and design w/ some of the fights and quest mapping (the last 1/4 of the game is a slog with the back and forth). Good god the last boss 'mission' is painfully dragged out with the chaotic stages and so many particle effects it's hard to even see. I will say, by the end of the game, I felt like a badass flipping and teleporting around just ripping people to shreds. The game does a good job fulfilling the power fantasy as your ship improves. The wolf set with the splinter rockets was absolutely busted but so much fun. The story seemed a little inconsistent, but overall I had a fun time. Glad I played it. My pinky hurts from all the shift boosting for the end of the game. Pros:-DLSS support, runs decent w/ consistent frames.-Decent music and graphics.-Fully voice acted.-Side quests and exploring (scanning) can be rewarding and worthwhile.Cons:-Controller support is very hit and miss (controller wouldn't work in main menu)-A lot of people complained about kb&m but I have NO IDEA how they played w/ controller as the mappingis insane. That said, I did get used to the controls but it shouldn't be a chore to learn them.-Random difficulty spikes, the first and last boss battles are BUSTED compared to most of the game. Down right OBNOXIOUS amounts of crap on the screen and flipping around just to get your target on your screen.-Search / scan indicators are hard to see sometimes.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: This game deserves some praise. It's brave, very well made, and beautiful. It's fairly clear that a lot more effort went on designing the world and the gameplay than the writing, for sure, but the voice acting and the story are functional, if not exactly inspiring. It may lack the polish and development of a AAA studio title with their huge budgets, but it's extremely fun to play, the space combat flows wonderfully, and it doesn't pad itself unnecessarily. Expect about 15-20 hours of playtime for one run through, and just enjoy the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Ah hard one to call. Recommend this game. For one, I'm happy there's another interesting space game. You get multiple systems to visit, upgrade your gear, find credits and items spread all over the place if you care to look for them. BUT; there's a couple of things in here that rub me the wrong way that this might as well have been a negative review.The flight system is just... I don't know what they were even going for. It's very arcade, but yet punishing. What ends up happening is that you boost, fire a bunch drift turn and do it again. But not in a good way to be honest. You don't really get to upgrade your ship, since you have a fixed ship and load-out, but instead you get special powers. Which is great, if it weren't for the fact that you will then have to use them to defeat new enemies all the time. You don't actually get stronger, but you get to deal with yet another mechanism.There's a story here, while straight forward so far, there's a bunch of meat to it. Sadly the delivery is just not very good. You get a lot of inner dialogue, which is for some reason whispered, but... it's not very good? Too much rapid fire cliche lines.You are stuck in 3rd person. There's no radar, just on screen blips to point out objectives and enemies. And frankly, with all the drift turning, I've never been so disoriented in a dog fighting game ever. The default FoV is clearly made for console, aka viewing a large screen over some distance while on a couch or something. It feels too close on a monitor behind a desk with HOTAS and even more-so with KB+M.I've tried the keyboard and mouse (passable), Steam controller as gamepad of choice (not for me), and HOTAS. The last one is the most fun if you ask me. And it allows you to roll! Why isn't this a thing by default!?RTX has been added to this game. I have a capable card, slapped it on and set DLSS to Quality and frankly, I don't notice it at all. I'm not even sure it is on. The menu says so. I get decent looking reflections, but you don't really get a lot out of it in this title? It's right there with COD:MW 2019 in terms of how much it adds. (next to nothing)The game has "bosses" and frankly, I find the mechanics of these rather annoying. Fighting capital ships or bases is good enough, but small though enemies that instantly get fresh shields if you get within 400m of them is just annoying. These take quite some time and have you dodge attacks like your are playing Dark Souls.I really wish movement was a bit more balanced for all parties and that flight had a bit more inertia. There's a bit too much rock-paper-scissors gameplay and too many obligatory "best way" powers going on. The environments and fun the weapons bring to table make up for it. And there are just not many games with story in this genre at the moment.Score breakdown time:Graphics: 8/10. Modern graphics, bit too low textures at timesControls: KB+M: 7, gamepad: 6, HOTAS: 8Sound: 7, music and sound effects are fine, voice acting very mixed.Story: I really don't care too much for it, but it drives things onwards 6? (Might update)Gameplay: 7, would have liked a bit more classic approach moreRPG elements (customisation / exploration): 8. There's some, it's fine, hope it gets better towards the end.Do you like dogfighting in Star Citizen or SW: Squadrons? This is nothing like that.Do you want to have more casual fun, fly around and have story drive you onwards a bit?Get this while on discount. It's a nice never before done game with some personality to it.

_childDocuments_.review: Smooth game, easy to learn flying, not unlike maybe Mass Effect flying but without ME's depth. Fluid fights, and interesting storyline. It's a little limited in that you're always in your ship -- never getting out to go on foot to explore caves or enemy ships -- but it's a lot of fun to barnstorm large battleships, chipping away at your foes, and eventually grinning as you know you upgraded your weapons to enemies to smithereens. But it also comes with important human lessons that apply to just about everyone-- some are basic some are more profound. I don't know that I would have paid retail, but the discounted rate and on easy mode was well worth it and a great way to cap the day.

_childDocuments_.review: In a remote future, humanity has traveled the stars far and wide, only to find its freedom threatened by the Circle, a cult-like organization that seeks to subjugate all under its dominion and wipe the rest out. Once one of their best fighters, protagonist Nara lost faith in the cult's creed, and sought a quiet life at a remote scavenging outpost, its inhabitants none the wiser to her true identity. Begrudgingly, but with determination, she is forced once again to take up arms and seek her almost-forgotten past, when the Circle threatens the Enclave and those that, willing or not, became important parts of her life.The story of Chorus walks a thin, haphazardly drawn line between science and magic, with the Circle harnessing extra-dimensional powers and the confines between thoughts, actions blurring on many occasions. Despite a solid premise, in most cases its lore is scattered like fragments of a space wreckage, never feels cohesive, and ends up with many plot-holes, unanswered questions. The characters, including Nara herself, don't feel interesting enough; while there's an attempt to highlight their development as the story progresses, they feel too one-sided most of the time nonetheless.Defeating a galaxy-spanning cult is no small feat. Nara will need the help of many factions and people, other than regaining her lost powers, called Rites, from remote corners of space. The world is divided in sectors, each closed-off from the next until a specific point in the main quest is reached; it's recommended to clear all the plentiful side-activities in each area before continuing, especially on higher difficulties. While none of them influences the larger plot, they have good variety, as they range from from escort missions, point defense, assassination and a couple more "unique" ones, alas few. Random encounters with enemy patrols or citizen in distress, other than hidden loot crates, will grant small but helpful credit bonuses upon completion, useful to buy new weapons, accessories and upgrades at the nearest station. Some more variety in objective types and more difficulty in their execution would have been welcome, as most side-quests don't exactly pose a great challenge at any point.Highly fast-paced, fluid and with generally low time-to-kill for both yourself and most enemies, the combat system of Chorus is a real gem, as far as space shooters go. Nara will have unparalleled tactical flexibility at her disposal rather soon, thanks to the combination of high-tech weaponry that can be changed on the fly (between Laser, Gatling and Missiles, once unlocked) and supernatural powers called Rites, enabling feats like teleportation, ship disabling or powerful AoE attacks, to name some. As new sectors and missions become available, you'll amass a veritable arsenal of guns and Rite Aspects, that modify each spell with new functions in a permanent way. Weapons and accessories also have "sets", which unlock passive bonuses if equipped together - however, only a few of these are actually worth using, and going for a "mixed" build is just better in most cases.  Using weapons, Rites and doing certain maneuvers improves Nara's Mastery with them, increasing stats like passive damage, resistance, lower energy consumption and more bonuses.On higher difficulties, and especially a bit later with the presence of more difficult enemies, it's not hard to be instantly killed by a volley from a spaceship or a bunch of extra-dimensional horrors. It's not hard to dodge all fire by dodge-spamming, but it's also true that a single false step, bad dodge, wrong teleport can result into instant death, as well as high-speed collision can do in many occasions. Bosses are mostly disappointing, especially later when the set bonuses and advanced weapons simply demolish most of them quickly, even when they're supposed to be legendary figures of the same caliber of Nara, on paper. Larger battles with capital ships, allies and stations look epic, but actually you'll have to do most of the work anyway, so it never feels like having any "real" allies with you at any point, which is, well, disappointing to see. Even after playing all side-missions and finding most if not all memories and lore elements, the story as a whole still feels like an acid trip that went only half right. Some points are obscure, while others don't make much sense at all. Some of the factions you encounter, especially later on, seem to contradict the story's premise or the general lore, while no real explanation for their existence or involvement is ever provided. Chorus tries to play it big on character growth and emotions, yet its insipid protagonist, forgettable side-characters and one-sided main story prove detrimental to this intent.  If there was any attempt at indirect narration or "choose-your-own-interpretation" kind of lore, then something went seriously wrong, because I haven't seen anything to suggest this approach to begin with.

_childDocuments_.review: I've tried a bunch of star-fighter games, but this one honestly has the best combat and handling of any of them. I loved the drifting mechanic and all of the magic spells (rites) you get are super satisfying to use. Its a really fun game.The weakest part of the game is definitely the story. Its a pretty straightforward redemption story, with a interesting twist at the end that I appreciated. The execution of the story was bad though. Basically, you end up staring at a bunch of ships while people talk over video call. Very few cutscenes. The focus of the game is really not the story, but more the combat and mechanics. This game will make you feel like an extremely powerful supernatural being. I really liked how you as the main character (Nara) have an evolving relationship with your ship, which is actually sentient. His name is Forsaken but goes by Forsa. They even talk to each other and make comments about what you're doing during combat. It definitely added to the feeling of tension.Overall, it is a good game and worth picking up.

_childDocuments_.review: It's one of these games that starts rather strong, and then gets progressively worse - not by that much, but at times it really stings. This game's final act feels unfinished, and might cause you some grief - I've played on hard, which probably wasn't the best idea for a first playthrough, but I don't think I'll be playing it again any time soon. It's hard to recommend the game, but I will cautiously do it, just for the gameplay, which is satisfying and unique - after all, the core gameplay is the most important thing about a game, and here, it's solid.I was concerned about the story and acting, as it was mentioned in some of the negative reviews in particular, but then I've looked back at how poorly written those reviews were, which put me at ease. The main story itself isn't bad, but it's balancing on the edge of being cringeworthy, as there are plenty of awkward moments, not just lines, entire scenes (the whispering is something you have to get used to, and I completely understand if some people just disregard it as corny - it's not a good idea, as far as I am concerned, but the actress does a decent job, so it never really bothered me). If a studio like Remedy could take this story and properly rework it, I think it could be amazing, but alas, you get there is, and sometimes, I think it's for the better to suspend your disbelief. It does a decent job and even though the ending is lackluster, the journey was satisfying enough.Initially not convinced, I've eventually really grown to like the combat - when you unlock the first few basic maneuvers, it really becomes second nature, not too overwheming, but complex enough - this is what games like Falconeer would wish they could be. However, at times, you will be facing brief difficulty spikes, with plenty of smaller things that frustrated me, and I've begrudginly pushed through them.There are lots of smaller things I could criticize, like your ship looking like a tiny model inside the hangar, where the devs just didn't manage to capture any scope, but those don't take away from the game being enjoyable and reasonably immersive. I've accepted the game's world, for what it was worth, and had fun with it. The world and music are beautiful, it's not "the top" that would blow your mind, but it certainly felt good existing in this world. Maps are unique, different and stand out from each other.What made my blood boil were the boss fights and few encounters with harder enemies - this game is mainly about combat, so it makes sense that the frustration will come from this. Especially the final boss, which will make you howl "In Chorus!", when you finally lose your mind and curse the developers, to put the game down for few weeks, only to come back and beat the boss rather easily... what gives? The bosses aren't necessarily difficult, but despite some basic instructions, you will be puzzled what exactly you are supposed to do to stay alive, given the game's rather overwhelming nature - you are flying around, very fast, dodging all sorts of crap on your screen, and during these fights, it's very easy to get overwhelmed, as it almost turns into a bullet hell, except in full 3D space. When you get a grip and realize what exactly you're supposed to do, it's quite fair, and there are reasonable checkpoints, but I just wish the game didn't feel so overwhelming at times.This is a prime candidate to be remade by studio like Remedy, who insist on continuously making games, where you run around with a human, so why not a spaceship? The gameplay is great and begs to be adopted by a larger studio with more time and budget to make it into something really special. But for now, if you want something different, and aren't deterred by some jank, give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Really didn't expect the game to be as good or as long as it is. Not done yet, but already worth the money for me. If you like high speed aerial combat, or ever wanted to drift in a spaceship, this is about your only truly good option.Story is decent enough to contain the gameplay, but nothing to cry from the rooftops about.Play it with a controller. If possible, a controller with back buttons you can bind to your drift key. Really allows for a ton more skill expression when you can drift while executing all other abilities.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: This is a GOOD game. Actually, it might be a GREAT game.The space combat is the most fluid and responsive and satisfying I've ever played - mostly for one simple reason: somebody FINALLY figured out a way to get around the 3D combat tracking problem, and it's glorious. The story is fairly compelling, and while I don't personally care for the main character's VO, I can't help but LOVE her whispers, so it evens out. I haven't finished yet, but I'd give this an 8.5/10 so far. There are a few minor gripes - the equipment and ships feel a little limited and I wanted a little more out of the docking experience, but I happily shrug those off for everything else it's delivering. It's very polished, very well done. I'd never heard of this game and took a wild chance on it - so glad I did. Love it. If you want a single player space fighter game to get lost in for a while, this is it.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Way too difficult to be enjoyable, even on easy mode. I'm a casual gamer who likes to relax and have fun and a game like this is more stress and frustration than a pleasurable pursuit. I've maxed out on weapons and defence by doing side missions but the game won't let me upgrade my ship any further even though I have thousands of credits to spend. The story gets to the point where you are overwhelmed by enemy ships and have the equivalent of a timer on many missions so you either die or run out of time. To make matters worse you can't save at check points so end up running out of gaming time and have to play the whole irritating mission from scratch.The only good thing about this game is the beautiful graphics. Other than that you have a cheesy story which after 20 hours I still don't understand. No cockpit view, no walking around space stations. Only one ship and the same 3 enemies over and over again in endless numbers.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Initially had an odd impression from the demo, fun but flawed. Then I saw a video on youtube that there had actually been a patch to add in joystick support which made this an instant buy for me. Started new game then played 7 hours straight, now I reformatted this entire review and now I do recommend this game.I am having an absolutely great time playing. Combat is smooth, the visuals overall are pretty, but the "alien" looking ships are visually oddly uninteresting / low poly?  Some more variety in weapon types would have been great but this game understands balance, not too much of anything. It's not a space sim, more like an arcade version of one. No features are overwhelming so I don't get annoyed or bored. No micro management. no forced fetch quests. The audio options are either TV or Home Cinema, where I just expected "headphones" or something, but it doesn't really matter. Sound design is not exceptional, it's just there. Personally once I really started loving the arcade combat I just put on some energetic synthwave mix and forgot about in-game audio entirely. Audio doesn't have a big role in the game.Looking around with the joystick is both super smooth and super accurate, another thing done right. Aiming is much easier and configurable than in a sim like DCS or Warthunder on their realism mode. Good stuff. One thing that makes me feel uncomfortable is that I can't get out of the plane but in cutscenes, it would have been great to actually explore the stations and connect with the story characters in person in some way without making it a forced walking sim. placing my ship 10 meters next to another to initiate a dialog over radio doesn't do it for me, but it's not a major annoyance. Well worth the money if you are into space / flight / arcade games and want both quick dogfights and free exploration.Pros:- Combat is fun, similar to what I liked about the old SW battlefront 2 space battles but better. - Freedom to explore.- Fetch quests and such side quests are side quests. They are not fillers for the main quests.Cons:- Demo lacks features including joystick support.- Demo dumps you hours into the game lacking context, spoiling weapons / powers.- Using the save from the demo lets you skip said content and I read it leads to a story soft lock.- Keybindings are a pain as they can not be fully customized and unbinding is not possible. I can't unbind the "Z" axis on throttle which my joystick simply doesn't have. Any time I pitch /  yaw / roll I speed up like crazy. Any time I hit a keyboard button this conflicts with my joystick axis randomly overriding my stick. Sometimes a stick button is unresponsive (drifting power) and I suspect this happens when the same button is affecting UI or dialog or something.- Main character and the ship keep talking about everything they hit , see and kill as if driving a car and you are telling the person next to you about every road sign you are seeing. This is not a mayor annoyance but it's there. If you survived the repeating voice lines of Divinity OS then you will barely notice this.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: I expected a thrilling space combat game with Chorus, but instead got bogged down by Nara’s psychological journey. The game often shifts from exciting space battles to tedious sequences of running away from guilt manifestations in cramped corridors. These interruptions break the flow and detract from the core space combat experience. If you want non-stop space action, this game might disappoint.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: Review after 4.8 hours of gameplay - before using the first jump gate: It's basically Space GTA meets the coolest re-creation of Descent you could come up with. Nice edgy story that entertains while not getting in the way. Great graphics and great audio. Easy to play in bite-sized chunks or in long sessions. Def a 9/10 from me. Add 1 if the devs add VR.I really, really, really wish this game had VR. Third person VR is fine. Just let us view this in stereoscopic 3D, and move our head around independent of what's going on with the ship. Don't slow the view down, don't do any of that anti-nausea stuff, people doing VR know what they're doing. Just do basic VR like that. It'll be great. It'll sell a shedload of copies to VR enthusiasts for little work on your behalf. You'll probably have to fix some shaders or the way you display some of the models so they don't look flat, but it'll be worth it. To anyone suggesting it: VorpX doesn't help this game. Some of the geometry ends up looking flat. That's not so great.The game is kind of built up like GTA IV or an open world RPG. You don't steal other cars/ships/whatever, although some missions put you in other ships. The fighting is cool. The audio visual aspect of the game is 11/10, eh, maybe except the human models which aren't so... perfect, but they're fiiiine. The gameplay loop is fun and rewarding, even the repetitive stuff. Pick the game up, shoot some bastards, leave it when you're done.The bad:It's really not so bad so far. I'll point out some stuff that's not really even that annoying, just, eh, kind of "growing pains" I guess.There are some bugs with the game: when you scan, you get markers for stuff you've already done, which seems like a bug. There are "memories" or whatever they are called that are there and give you markers but you can't interact with them. I don't know what they're for. It's weird. Some missions feel slightly buggy or like they could use a little polish, but nothing game breaking or frustrating. For example, I had to restart a mission where I'm chasing a ship that stole some plutonium, and it wasn't clear I was supposed to get in their vicinity, so I chased them for a while and then they "got away". So I had to restart from check point. But it's not so bad because the checkpoints in the game are good and I lost like, eh, 30 seconds of easy flying. So next time I hauled ass and I basically rammed into the ship and it stopped right away ... it was funny in a janky kind of way, but I don't mind. It kind of feels like this project is a little bigger than the team could handle, but they did a great job none the less. Sometimes, you get those intermittent conversations with random people for world building, but if you approach a mission marker, that gets cut off - and you don't hear the rest of the conversation. This one kinda sucks, but eh, the world building isn't ... really that important. Like, those conversations, they add flavour, but they feel like they could be deeper or a little better written. I'm talking about conversations with the station chief in the first part of the game, he kind of feels naiive or something. On the other hand the stuff that Nara says to herself feels cool. The barks from the ship during dogfighting feel a little... juvenile, but I guess they haven't annoyed me yet enough to mind. The whole "metaphysical" part of the world is great and it gives it a nice mysterious atmosphere. Speaking of conversations, it would be nice if other people were actually people, not just helmets, eh, that kind of makes them all sameish. I get it, that's extra budget. Maybe in a patch once the game has earned some money. That is one world building aspect that would make the game more engaging. Also: nara's mouth and teeth cast those weird shadows. Human skin and teeth are actually translucent, so it makes it weird. Maybe the devs could work on that a bit.This game could easily be a new, edgier GTA-like franchise, it's really fleshed out well, the world building is really good, the structure of the open world is similar to GTA IV, you could easily go miles further with it.If you make this one do VR, every single VR headset owner will buy it, guaranteed.

_childDocuments_.review: 6/10 There are some things I really like:It runs well on my desktop and deck, cross saves seamless. Don't know if I had a single graphical hiccup,The combat CAN be very fun. Especially the standard enemies and the bigger ships you can go into and blow up.It introduces a drift and blink mechanic to dog fights. I often find that genre struggles to not devolve into endless banking/flipping/barrel rolling. Another way the combat CAN be fun and creative.I did not like:The story. I don't mind a subpar story by any means. I openly admit that I will skip ahead to get back to combat, which is usually what I look for in games. But I think this game had about 6 hours of story to tell and then it pads it out another 6 hours with redundant retreading on story points. Which, given the story isn't very good to begin with, was redundant. Just not very fun.Speaking of not fun, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ are some of the end game enemies annoying. Not challenging. Not interesting. Annoying. The game started out strong, but like the story, I don't think the developer had a lot of depth. They started running out of ideas and came up with some subpar enemy types later in the game.So it does some things I really like. But it also does things I really dislike. YMMV. But very mid 4 to 6 out of 10 depending on what part of the game I am playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally review games, but I think this time I will.  In an age of rushed, buggy, incomplete, and perpetual early access game releases, this game stands apart.  The gameplay is crisp and solid, the weapons and abilities are fun, and the game is pretty and I need not brook any compromise with graphics to achieve a solid gameplay experience.  If you're looking for a new game that will run on old hardware during this PC parts crisis, Chorus will do the trick.  My PC from 2016 has had no issues whatsoever running it with a GTX 1070 at max settings.  I did have one crash fairly early on, but that was only due to my overly aggressive overclock, which only took one adjustment to correct.The story can get in the way a little, there are a few extended cinematics during story missions which can prove to be a bit of an interruption, and a couple of the time limits are quite unforgiving but I suppose the game does play on go fast or die.  That said I actually do enjoy the story.  It also has great potential for some open world qualities, but what you have is ~40 hours maybe of game world content.  It's enough, and I suspect someone will eventually post a vid of the 100% Completion+Hard+Permadeath run.Also I may just be biased because the whole concept of space fighter pilot ace on a quest for redemption with her AI space fighter partner against totally-not-a-Chaos-cult with warp frakery appeals to me on many levels.
_childDocuments_.name: Chorus

_childDocuments_.review: This is a magic induced space shooter with a little twist to it's controls: you can't really strafe! A and D just gives you a little evade manuver to left and right (that you actually need for some enemies to not getting hit). So you can't "circle" enemies while firing at them. This game is all about gameplay and how you manuver your ship with boost and drift. Holding right mouse button lets the ship keep "drifing" in its current direction while you can turn it around towards enemies. It needs some getting used to and can be frustrating at first, but is soo much more rewarding if you get the hang of it. You need to be aware of sourrounding objects and walls to not crash into them. The ship can withstand 1 heavy impact (looses the shields), but explodes if you boost full speed directly into an obstacele.You need to switch weapons a lot depending on weaknesses of the enemy. And taking apart capital ships bit by bit till flying into them and destroying their core is a blast. There are also magic spells called "rites" like spark shooting to disable shields of ships.Sometimes it feels like a mixture of Doom and Horizon: Zero Dawn with magic - as a space shooter.I really liked it, it felt kinda new to play like a new mixture of things that were there before but no one ever dared to combine them into one game plus something that could be a new control scheme for fast pased space shooters. And if you do everything there is with sidemissions and searching all the hidden reward boxes, you get at least 20 h out of it.

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is pretty much the best space combat I've seen - at least when talking about fast-paced, arcade-y games. Here's some of the parts that make it different and might not be obvious from viewing trailers or videos:- The drift button. While holding rightclick or L1, your ship will continue moving to the same direction, and allows you to eg. turn around and shoot backwards. Eg. when killing stationary turrets or slow enemies, you'll set up your movement so that you'll boost past the turret, enable drift mode, and basically do a drive-by while drifting.- "But why can't you just strafe?" - good question. The drift button is a bit weird to get used to, but once you figure it out, it just makes you think about your movement in a different way - which I personally find fun.- Dodge mechanic - there's a few enemies which require you to press dodge button just before they hit you. I haven't seen this mechanic used in a spacesim before, but it feels nice.- You have 3 weapons, switchable with a keypress at any time. Use laser beam to destroy shields, gatling gun to finish off small enemies, and use rockets to kill slow armored enemies. Standard rock-paper-scissors, but it still works well with the fast combat.- Along with weapons, you also have 3 different abilities which cost slowly recharging energy. One teleports behind the target, one zaps the target destroying their shields, and one is a charge forward which also hurts anything you hit with it. Noteworthy: 2 of your abilities also gives you additional options for mobility. Movement is a huge thing in the whole game, and plays a big part in making the combat feel fast and fun.- Then one thing which I can't fully explain: the highest difficulty (Extreme) makes enemies hit so hard that you die in a couple of seconds if you fly in wrong direction or even slow down too much. But even with the big damage intake, the combat is manageable - I rarely die, but if I die it's always because of a clear mistake which I can learn from (eg. "next time I won't fly directly towards that enemy"). In most space flight games, it usually feels a bit random when trying to dodge hits - I'm really not sure why Chorus is so great at this, but it just works.- Basically if you set the difficulty up to maximum, the game will require spatial awareness, good shooting and timing your dodges properly - it's difficult but in a fair way.The graphics are great both technically and aesthetically. There's really not much to say about it, . It also runs at unlimited fps, which is always nice to see.Music and audio design are also great through the whole game.I also haven't faced any notable technical issues - no weird fps dips, no crashing, the game loads quickly, etc. It's a well made game.Just to comment about the story: I feel like the story by its self is fine and I find it somewhat interesting (history/lore, character arcs, etc), but the storytelling is mid-tier at best. Every now and then the characters and dialogue just gets so edgy or overly dramatic that it makes me cringe.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: If the really really bad storytelling does not give you several strokes, this is an enjoyable game. If badly written stories and voice-acting that feels forced do induce bodily harm on you, this one should be a hard pass.If you want to buy this, wait for at least 50% discount. Do not repeat my mistakes.+ decent graphics+ smooth combat experience+ refreshing special abilites (rites)+ sound design+ no in-game loading screens- really awful story (maybe it's good if you're a member of generation snowflake)- cringy voice-acting and awful subtitling- the TUTORIALS on some rites can get really frustrating (no joke)- cutscene character animations are awful (luckily you can skip)- UI could be better (enemies, friends and neutrals are just white squares unless you have them in direct view)-------------------------------------------------First things first:Valve, when asking me if I would recommend this game, a "Meh" rating would be really nice.This game would earn that rating in particular.It actually is a pretty decent space-shooter. If you can accept that this space has an up and a down.However, the quality of this game is severely diminished by really bad storywriting and voice-acting. The fact that for some reason quotes are quite overused in the subtitles doesn't help either.Let me give you an example:You take on a mission in which you have to kill a couple enemies. You do that. and then your ship AI says: 'We "killed" them!'Well yes, you psychopathic moron. We DID kill them, no need to put that in quotes. And it goes on and on and on like that. All the time.The constant whisper-thinking of your character doesn't help either. Please let me have my own thoughts.I also can't get over the fact that your character killed billions and now is on a guilt-trip. Here's a small toke of insight for you. If you butchered billions you already were a proper psychopath to start with. And if you are a psychopath the murder of billions of people would not weigh down on your conscience, as you would basically have no conscience to speak of.That being said, the game itself (story and voice aside) is pretty good. The flight mechanics are enjoyable and a refreshing touch (I played with an XBOX 360 controller). The missions are mostly fun and -although they technically are- do not feel like a repetetive slog of a grind. The graphics are somewhere between decent and good (epic preset) and i really do like that you have no loading screens between systems.So, is this game for you?Well, if you can endure the torture of going through the story and enjoy mildly challenging combat mechanics, then yes.If however, you like games with at least decent story-telling and character development, then please gain as much distance to this game as you can.

_childDocuments_.review: A solid AA experience, which never quite hits the heights you might hope for, but makes for a fun space shooter. At first it seems hard, but once you stop treating it like a standard space sim and drift instead of turn you shouldn't have any problems with the standard fights. The art and music come together to make every fight feel epic.It does suffer from a couple of nasty difficulty spikes around some bosses, but has a very generous checkpoint system which means you're rarely starting boss fights from scratch.My only disappointment with combat is how allies exist only to look like they're doing something with capital ships only shooting FX. Every fight is you versus the enemy, and that takes something away from the bigger encounters.Story clearly wants to be more epic than it is, with the AA element really showing its hand. It ends up being a bit of a light weight, slightly confusing, and never commits to really following through on any one character.Overall though if you treat this as a fun, arcade spaceship combat game then you're in for a good time.
