_childDocuments_.review: played 5 hours with a buddy just the demo which is 2 characters 2 weapons and 1 map only. the game is really fun and combat is pretty satisfying once you figure out its nuances and quirks. we are planning to play just the demo even more.baught the game just to leave the review really.the catch is it's the 1v1 fighter and it's only fun to play against other people. you will not get into it playing against ai. trust me, there is more than meets the eye once you play a few hours against a human on the same couch or in voice chat.the game is really fun but only if you have actual friends to play with.online 1v1 is p2p yet pretty reliable, me and my buddy are separated by 3 timezones and we had no issues.this game's online lobby will most likely be pretty barren if not outright dead from the get go, that's the problem. zero people in online matchmaking lobby is one of the most frequent complaints in steam reviews.consider it to be a party game more than anything else. the mechanics are very easy to grasp, easy to learn hard to master, you can get a hang of everything in 15 minutes of messing around, there are no intricate combos to memorize and learn. the combat is mostly about mind games, reading and reacting to opponent's moves, positioning baiting whiffs to punish. it kind of reminds of soulslike combat but in pvp 1v1 multiplayer format with everyone on the same build. which is not a bad offering and there aren't that many games like this around. For honor comes to mind t0o of course with a similar 3 positions stance system.the game is competently made and runs perfectly fine on a laptop with 3060 6gig vram card.I will admit $20 as a base asking price might be a little steep for what this game practically is, $15 would've been much better. but the good news is publisher follows Valve suggested regional discounted prices almost to a T.if you don't have actual friends to play it with - just don't buy it. as simple as that.the direct competitor Hellish Quart goes for $17 base, is in early access for 2.5 years and has no online multiplayer whatsoever, you can only play pvp locally or via steam remote play, which is in no way guaranteed to be good enough to enjoy a fighting game or to work at all. for me and my buddy it just didn't load up at all.

_childDocuments_.review: Played all day yesterday, really enjoyed it, but honestly I think it would have been best to put it in the EA oven before an official release as there are several problems that are noticeable just within the first hour of play.What I liked:-Game runs super smoothly overall both from a performance and network* perspective. *(I'll touch on the network side of things again below)-Different maps you fight in are gorgeous-Feels really good to hit a finisher-Camera really gives you the bushido duel to the death vibeWhat I disliked:-Couple of elements missing from the UI, notably: 1-Your ping to the opponent 2-Your stats (especially rating)-Couple of QoL missing: 1- Having to reselect your character, your skin and your weapon every time you enter a match. 2- Unable to rematch/requeue after a match. 3- Going back to Offline -> Versus and having to select Online -> Ranked Match after every match-Sound effects and Music could be improved upon, especially sound effects, not that the current ones are bad, but adding some to certain animations or certain segments, and giving more variety to the current ones would feel better imo (different ones for different characters/weapons maybe?)-Bug: You're not awarded coins and exp if you leave the score screen too fast after a match-Inputs are inverted both horizontally and vertically if you're on p2 side: so this one's a little weird, it's a fighting game convention that a horizontal directional input+strike input move/combo becomes inverted on the p2 side, but in this game, it's also the case for vertical directional input, so a move that requires a up input will need to be inverted to a down input on p2 side to work, that's just weird to me.What will make me quit this game:-I mentioned that the game runs very smoothly above, but unfortunately that's only the case if your opponent isn't in freakin Singapore (shoutout to my homie , our matches may have been laggy but at least I made a friend :D) There isn't any region lock, ping lock, there's nothing, I get that you dont want to split the player base, but if you want the rest of your player base to stay, there needs to have a ping limit 100%.-Expanding on the point above, there is no rollback netcode, meaning that if you play against an opponent with a high enough ping (which the game doesn't tell you in advance), you may have the parry input literally showing on your side, but the opponent's move will still go through, this is super frustrating.I still recommend it, it's good fun!!

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a lot of work that still needs done. I feel that the combo inputs are EXTREMELY cumbersome on the Steam Deck and other controllers. I would not even attempt this game with KB and M. I looked at the commands and such and it just seems weird the way you work the combos with any device. I don't know if there is a lag to the input or what but when I try to flow a combo it just seems sluggish. Learning the combos is key to great duels otherwise you will just end up with a dodge/roll and slice battle which is not quite what Bushido Blade (one of the big influences for this game) had going. I know comparing two games that are literally nearly 30 years apart is not fair. In BB the fight system felt better. You could strike spots on an enemy and slowly disable their ability. example. I could strike low on their leg and make them hobble and move at half or so speed. You could strike their arm and disable their arm. you could disable both arm and leg. It made for a more interesting experience not to mention if you were the one that got those disabling shots and still won the duel it was awesome. Also the maps in BB were larger arenas with multiple tiers you could work with like high and low ground and obstacles you could use.Needless to say it does not QUITE live up to the standard I hoped but I still recommend the game because the devs seem to be listening and I feel they will make improvements. I think if it manages to take off with tournaments it could be a blast but I do agree with some others that maybe an Early Access release would have benefit the game if for no other purpose then to get some of these early bugs squashed before the game took a full released hit of negativity.Other positive items in the game is the customization. There are some fun combinations of clothing and accessories on characters and on weapons which is really the only thing you get with in game currency. They do not change effectiveness of anything, they are purely cosmetic. The negatives currently deal with the somewhat janky controls with mushy movement for combos if that makes sense. There is not a ton of replay in this title either. Once everything is unlocked ranking is all there is and that needs to be implemented differently. The Discord has some good ideas here with ranking tiers and stuff.TL;DR:For $19.99 it is not a bad game. It has good graphics and audio. The battle system is easy to pick up but very difficult to learn. It still needs some fine tuning. Still recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Die by the Blade left an exceptionally positive impression on me. An unusual fighting system sets this game apart from other standard fighting games. You literally have to strike a single but accurate hit to your opponent to win the round, which adds incredible tension and realism to the game. The game does not let you relax because you have to predict your opponent's next move. Mistakes in this game are not forgiven. Very dynamic and fast fights do not let you get bored. 100 percent recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game! It can be quite punishing, but that's what a one-hit-kill fighting game is. If you miss your timing for an attack or parry, block the wrong direction, or fall for a feint, you are dead. Thankfully matches are five lives, so you aren't thrown to the lobby after a single mistake.Practice is essential for mastery, and you should definitely practice sequences from both sides of the screen if you struggle in fights.The tournaments are also extremely fun. It's great to watch others play and see how they approach their favored weapons.Hop in the discord if you want to spar or join hosted tournaments!

_childDocuments_.review: While the game looks visually impressive, it's not worth the money. The lack of penalties for spamming long weapon attacks makes this class incredibly overpowered. When using a katana against opponents wielding a naginata or odachi, you're at a significant disadvantage. Parrying pushes both you and your opponent back, preventing you from reaching them with your weapon.This often results in frustrating scenarios where you block an opponent's attack, counterattack, but miss due to the distance, only to be instantly killed because your move brought you within their range. You can't block during your own attack, and every block pushes you back, making it impossible to close the distance. Dodging isn't effective either, as the opponent's attacks track you. Even if you dodge the first strike in a combo, the second one will still hit you.If you try to block after dodging, you're back to square one, unable to get close. An experienced opponent can exploit this by keeping you at a distance, retreating, or feinting before striking you down after you block. They face no real risk because even if their attack misses or you block, you're still pushed back.This fundamental flaw severely undermines the game's balance and makes it a frustrating experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I can confidently say that Die by the Blade has provided one of the most fun experiences streaming a game (Alienware Twitch Channel) I've had in a long time. The combat is exhilarating, focusing on short bursts of intensity that make it perfect for smack-talking sessions with friends. It's a game that knows exactly what it's about—sword duels that demand timing and patience, where a single strike can be your end. While speaking with the devs, they made it clear that the intention is to make it all about the blade. This reminded me so much of my college days playing Bushido Blade; it hits all the right nostalgic notes.No Microtransactions: A big win in today's gaming landscape. You get the full experience without any pay-to-win elements. Future updates will also include a single player campaign with unique boss fights!Future Content: The promise of a single-player story mode is exciting and something to look forward to.Multiplayer Fun: This game truly shines when played with friends, offering a mix of casual and competitive gameplay that keeps you coming back for more.Best with Friends: While it can be enjoyed solo, the multiplayer aspect is where it really excels.Recommendation:Would I recommend Die by the Blade to other players? Absolutely. Whether you're looking for a casual game night with friends or a competitive showdown, this game delivers on all fronts. If you're a fan of intense, skill-based combat and enjoy games that offer a fair, microtransaction-free experience, Die by the Blade is a must-play. Grab your sword and jump into the fray—you won't be disappointed!

_childDocuments_.review: Die by the Blade is a fun game with a cool concept, but it feels like it's missing some key gameplay elements. If you re into fighting games and looking for a fun time, this one might fall a bit flat. The idea of dying with a single hit is awesome and keeps you on your toes, but it needs more variety to keep things interesting.The learning curve is a bit steep, and it took me about half an hour to get the hang of the controls. The build-up is slow, and the game doesn't always deliver the excitement when you need it. As someone with experience in game design, I think it would be great if they added different game modes, like a story mode or tournaments, to mix things up.Also, the price feels a bit high. I think it should be under $10 to make it more appealing. Overall, it's a game for die-hard fans of traditional Japanese one-hit combat, but it could really shine if the devs expanded the scope a bit and tweaked the design.Despite its flaws, I'd recommend this game to anyone who loves intense 1v1 samurai battles. With some updates, it could be a standout game. Cheers to dev!!!

Unfortunately, I have to say, not much, and I cannot at all condemn those who, upon entering the menu, ask for a refund of the previously paid amount rather than try. If we get some content updates later and expand the already very limited selection of game modes, then it might be worth taking up a weapon and attacking the opponent, but until then, everyone should enter this samuripunk world with caution, because no matter how inviting it seems at first, it will run out of steam in seconds.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be keeping an eye on this game to see if it improves down the road, but in my opinion all it has going for it right now is the arena designs and being able to create custom swords. The fighting is hit or miss, especially when it seems like parrying doesn't register most of the time. The progression system is awful, you could rank up faster by playing offline with the AI set to easy on one round rather than playing an online match, and if you're into offline there's no point raising the round limit or AI difficulty since it all dishes out the same amount of XP and money. Finally, the character stats make no sense (Guy who's said to have cybernetic augments in his bio has the most basic, if not the worst stats out of everyone?) and, while I know it's only a $20 indie game and I told myself I'd ignore it at first, the characters themselves look like they managed to crawl out of a PS3 game. I'm still hopeful that this game will get the updates it needs to become great!

Die by the Blade is a 1v1 weapons-focused fighter where the difference between victory and death can amount to a single strike of the blade.

name: XIII
detailed_description: WHO ARE YOU, REALLY? XIII is the remake of the iconic action game played in first person view initially released in 2003. You play as “XIII”, a man with no identity, in a single player campaign full of twists and turns. Inspired by the eponymous comic book, the game features a unique cel-shading design entirely reinvented. XIII will also offer the possibility to confront your opponents through brutal multiplayer battles. The country is still in shock after the assassination of President Sheridan . You wake up wounded, without any memory, on a deserted beach of the west coast. The only clues to your identity are the number XIII tattooed near your collarbone and a locker key. Despite your amnesia, you discover that you have the reflexes of a fully trained professional fighter. You take the road seeking for pieces of your past, finding out that you played a role in the murder of the President of the United States and uncovering the most horrific conspiracy in the entire history of the country. Features: The remake of the 2003 cult FPS initially released on PC, PlayStation 2, Xbox and Nintendo Gamecube. A new artistic direction that respects the original work and its iconic cel-shading design. Numerous references to the eponymous graphic novel, with onomatopoeia, speech bubbles, panels and more. Music and voices from the original version. A conspiracy-based plot with numerous twists and turns. Varied gameplay with action, infiltration and exploration phases. A breathtaking solo campaign with 34 levels. A brutal arsenal of 15 weapons to get your memory back. Fierce multi-player fights.

_childDocuments_.review: Because of the character limit, instead of a classic review, I'm just going to run through all the positives and negatives:PROS+ Despite the system requirements, the game DO run on Win7, you don't have to patch/mod anything, just install it and you can go to play right away+ Boss fights are tweaked with introducing "divided health bars": if you chunk down a portion of the bosses' health, they go into a dizzy state, where you can do extra damage+ Some very small details added (you can hear a ring when Winslow smashes down the phone, when Colonal MacCall asks you to join back to the conspiracists, in animation XIII shakes his head, etc.)+ Music and voice actors mostly remained the same+ Wildlife added to the Rocky Mountain stage+ Balanced fall damageCONS- Ugly Fortnite-like graphics, and for some reason cutscene animations are even worse, like the animation before the SPADS camp stage are almost as ugly as in a PS1 game, not joking- Removed comic-looking effects- The menu has a really weird, ugly and annoying shaking effect: whatever you do, everything starts to tremble- If you run the game in windowed mode, and you ALT+TAB out, the game still register every single command- Horrendous audio mixing: some voice-lines are so low you can't hear them properly; sometimes it's so loud it'll burst your eardrums out- Removed content: multiple interactions, singings and voice lines were removed, or changed to worse (they somehow made the "Sir Yes Sir' joke unfunny at the asylum stage)- Audio glitches: there are entire fights where you'll never gonna hear a single shot; half of the enemies don't make any noise, same for the weapons- Dumb AI: the enemies either won't notice you when you are in front of them killing others, or they will go directly to you raising an alarm, without you even moving, also, some enemies are highly possible that can see through walls because enemies will detect hidden bodies multiple rooms away if they clip through anything (and they will because this game is garbage), also some enemies hear silenced weapons also from rooms away, making stealth completely obsolete and useless: - The game CONSTATNLY dropping frames, everything stutters, there's not a single fluid moment whatsoever in the game- For the above reason you can experience input lag and input drop as well, such as choosing something in the menu won't register, you can't choses something in the menu (especially noticeable when you start a new game and you want to select the difficulty), also the weapon wheel does the same: despite switching a weapon you just don't change it- Really bad physics: you can't knock enemies out when you fall on their heads from above, etc.- When you kill an enemy, the death animation is delayed, therefore for about 1-2 sec they still stand around without any problems and THEN they collapse. Because enemies are spongier, now you can only know if you really killed someone if you see the "death text" above them- For absolutely no reason the devs changed the environmental objects, so there's no more "only KO run" at the Bristol Hotel- God knows why, but the devs introduced weapon wheel, and with that, introducing that from every weapon type, now you can only carry ONE weapon. You can't have a 9mm AND a .44 Special at the same time, which is pretty bad, but what's even worse is that the Harpoon Gun, the Sniper Rifle, the Rocket Launcher, the Crossbow and MiniGun are on the same "Heavy Weapon" slot, you can only carry one of those- If you change a weapon, for instance the Kalash for the AR, there's a big chance that the dropped weapon will get lost forever, and you can't revert it, you can't change your mind after changing weapons- They introduced wildlife at the Rocky Mountain stage: there's a deer, a couple of foxes and bunnies, but every single animal after they spot you will follow a determined route and the AI of the animals will lead them into one single spot of the stage where you can act like a Disney princess: - During the escape with Carrington, you can soft-lock the game if you kill the last RPG guy before saying the voice-line, but if you push Carrington to the trigger point, you can continue the game: - If an NPC has a determined route, like they open a door or when Jones set up the bomb, they will push you around or even goes underneath you, making you fly: - During the SPADS stage there's raining sounds but no actual rain falling down from the sky above you- During the Bristol Hotel stage if you fail the mission while the shotgun mic equipped, you'll hear white noise for the rest of the stage and you'll experience other audio issues during the rest of the game unless you restart it- There's no animation scene before the sanctuary stage- Helmet equipped soldiers are WAY MORE OVERPOWERED, they almost have as much as health as the bosses in the game- You can't shoot the box bag out at the FBI stage- On some rare occasions if you zoom in with the sniper rifle you can soft lock the game- You can't go down on ladders anymore- With regular fire you can almost never hit anything, even really close targets, but with the alternative zoom method, you have almost 0 recoil and spread- Enemy models are glitching through objects, walls, they constantly shaking, make really weird broken positions, and sometimes even T-poses, not even mentioning the faces- If you grab a body and you put it down, and you start doing this fast, you can glitch inside to their bodies for a brief moment- Enemies instantly pop up out of nowhere- Reduced blow effect: if you throw a grenade into a room or you shoot with the rocket launcher, 9 out of 10 cases you'll only deal damage to one single enemy, while the rest remains harmless- They changed the animation when escaping out of the asylum stage: now the nurse crashes the ambulance because enemies ran into it, making the voice line 'I'll never forget you" obsolete and out of context- Every tree in the game has this really weird, rather creepy moving, where only the upper half of the trees moving from left to ride (like the wind-blows), but it's way faster than the original and more rubbery feel like, it's like a limp ♥♥♥♥, seriously, and every tree does that at the same time, it's really-really ugly- Probably the ugliest water effects in the history of video games- There's no "horror music" sound during the snowman scene- Even when you kill enemies they still finish their conversation- During some flashbacks your in game character (still on the stage) goes into idle animation, so while during flashbacks you can still hear XIII switching magazines and messing around with his weapons- Due to poor hitboxes around 30% of headshots will registered as a body shot- Throwing knives know instantly kill enemies- When you get escorted out of your cell to the shower room, it's almost impossible to make, because of poor hit boxes and detection, the guards will randomly start to punch you despite you are between them and following them as you intended to- The batons of the guards are sometimes floating around their bodies, meters away from them- The hook has a similar physics as in Worms 2's Ninja Rope, so now you can even swing around ledges and bridges at your will, because the closer you are to the end of the hook, the faster your character swings- During cable slide now you always switch to throwing knives or pistol, also, removed the iconic cracking noises- Some interiors, rooms, routes changed, also the secret documents are now at completely different places now- In some cutscenes mouth are not animated at all- All the sailors in the submarine _childDocuments_.review: Well usually, I fully complete the game, and then I write a detailed review for it, but this time I don’t even feel like doing it. This remake is the laziest and the most disrespectful product I have ever seen in my life, a true spit in the face of every XIII fan. I was really waiting for this game and I even played the original game a few months ago just to refresh it in my memory and to be able to compare it after all those years. The original game looks so much better than this rip off - that’s all you have to know about this remake. - If you are familiar with the original game, you should probably remember that the game starts with a comic strips-alike cutscene showing us a short story of what we are dealing with and what is the main story of the game. Well, the developers didn’t even bother too much to recreate it, so they just created a short starting cutscene, where we see the FBI agent, who comes into the room and watches this original comic strip scene on the big screen, absolutely the same as it was back in 2003, no remake at all. That was disgusting, seriously.- The audio in the game appears and disappears all the time for no reason. First, you don’t hear a thing and then you suddenly start hearing background sounds that appear out of nowhere, and then they disappear again. Constant music stuttering and voice acting is so cheap.- Everytime you kill someone, the body drops on the ground with very weird and unworked animation, the whole body turns into some kind of a puppet that dangles on the floor. - Overall graphics and the overall feeling of the game is very odd and unpleasant - it doesn’t feel like it was remade with love and passion. It’s just lazy work with no great visual enhancements at all.I can not and I would not recommend the game in its current state, I don’t know either this game has been abandoned in the middle of the process or is it just day one issues. But if it’s the way the developers wanted their remake to look like - well, this is really awful.

_childDocuments_.review: You have to give credit where credit is due. Following the bitter disappointment of the original remake handled by PlayMagic, publisher Microids tasked developer Tower Five to remake the remake.The results are… mixed. Much of the comic book inspired art is now an improvement over the original. Character models, weapons, and interiors are all better, but some of the exteriors look worse. The atmosphere is sometimes lost. For example, you no longer feel the biting chill from the freezing fog in the wintery levels and you don’t feel the blazing dry heat of the canon levels. Speaking of those canyon levels; sometimes you experience sensory overload due to the over designed artwork.Sound design is better though, as is gameplay. Controller support with aim assist for television players is thankfully included and you now receive an on screen visual  indicator informing you of the direction enemy fire is coming from and objectives. However the beautiful camera shake is not featured in this version that follows large explosions and weirdly the scuba divers are now missing from one small section of the game making the harpoon gun completely unnecessary. But the worst thing, the most egregious change made to the game is to the cutscenes. The stunning comic panel transitions have been replaced with ugly animated 3D scenes that don’t mesh well with the rest of the game and the comic book recap panels are now missing from mission select as well. In the original the player could carry weapons and ammunition throughout the game. In this version weapon loadout is now reset at the start of levels.So would I recommend this game? Yes, yes I would. It’s not perfect, but it’s still a great game and a lot of fun to play. I bought the game for £3.74 in a Steam sale and it was worth every penny. Get it on sale, go in with tempered expectations, and I’m sure you’ll have a blast.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: + Enemies not being bullet sponges, this is something i am glad about as XIII OG was quite prone on making the characters quite health based. Killing now it's very satisfying and it does count on what weapon you use a lot, the guns have quite the oomph and killing people is very satisfying, I LOVED the shotgun SO much in this game.+ More enemies making it more intense, this for some can be a mixed bag but it makes more action packed and also very cool to act upon a situation with multiple enemies taking you by surprise at multiple sides, i loved playing through the chapters and not noticing an enemy was behind a door and else. This makes you more aware of your ammo and how precise you are, as you can hit almost instantly on the head. Guns are all viable and it's quite fun juggling around things whilst fighting.+ I have noticed some extra additions which make the game more interesting, for example on the roof scene with Major Jones, she quickly snaps around and shoots an enemy in the head which was on a roof behind you, it's quite the charm honestly. There are some of these small improvements and pretty appreciated ones too here and there which make it a bit more engaging, some extra animations were added for the arrival of enemies and else from the original game that do not insult the game nor make it more corny.+ Gunplay is extremely fun, i have had a lot of gun fights with a lot of variety of weaponry, the enemies themselves roll on the floor and also dodge bullets, sometimes i ended up missing and not even noticing, they shoot everywhere and try to hit you all the time making it very chaotic and random.+ From the point above i can add that the AI is quite engaging and honestly it's not bad at all, i have definitely saw way worse games with way worse reaction times and also just horrible gameplay, this AI instead actually makes the fighting more intense.+ The new overhaul has increased a LOT the graphics quality of this game and made it almost incredibly good looking, the maps are amazing and incredibly well done resembling well the old game, the characters look so much better since the last update and all look very sharp, cartoonish and on point. Facial animations and other animations of the character are all on point and pretty good! The cartoonish effects which the old game had followed through to this remake, and still are pretty solid!+ From above, for being an actual pretty good looking game, the fact that the FPS in this game is incredibly fluid impresses me, they really have outdone themselves with the performance, playing at a very high graphic fidelity the game looks amazing and plays well (RTX 2060).~ Interaction with cams in the game which helped with positioning of other enemies lacking~ Clipping of sound (slight lag of shots being processed) and lag of reloading animations, floating magazines while running and else, which for some reason happen, it can be quite funky.~ No death animation for XIII, just a death screen in comparison with XIII slowly falling while his heart beats.~ some missing textures and errors here and there, i've noticed one when going down from the EMERALD BASE with the grapple and the electricity was meant to zap you, the top was completely violet for some reason~ Some sounds just don't play, for example: for some reason the zapping sound at the emerald base was not playing, and the animations were pretty meh and weren't giving away where the electricity was coming from.~ non interactable things (Closets, computers, breaking boxes, glass, shooting a sandbag and seeing the sand falling and other things you could have done just by pressing on items which were completely irrelevant to the story in OG game) are not interactable with which imo removes a bit of that "messing around" feel to XIII which was super fun.~ Nostalgia segments are more clear and just have a black and white filter over. This makes it more simplified as before you were almost unable to see people's faces which added a bit to the mistery, the blur imo was much better.~ Removal of dossiers and documents you can find to unlock skills and else (Extras are now discovered through some golden statues, i don't dislike it but i found it a bit meh), which is a bit of a yes and no situation as it was quite a pain in XIII OG too but yknow, kinda miss finding them hiding somewhere to unlock double pistols and etc.~ Removal of initial comic intro where you can see still shots of what the character is seeing with the heartbeat before moving.~ Removal of text based mission end, where a pop up text telling you that the mission was accomplished before the game started a cutscene and else, now it's just a quick fade out.~ Health of main character even at highest difficulties is difficult to go down, it seems that some difficulties need some rebalancing.~ Ally AI still has some strokes here and there, it seems to struggle to do basic things, just like OG XIII, but it just feels plain out dumb sometimes, it isn't horrible though and the game progresses smoothly.~ There's some animations which look quite funky and abnormal, with the 9mm the character literally has a broken thumb and slams the magazine inside the gun for no reason.- Cutscenes, judging by the quality of those cutscenes i believe the overhaul didn't work on the cutscenes again, it seems they are playing directly from some MP4 file inside the game folder because they are not in-game rendered as they are way more simplified and still having weird glitches in the background, making them extremely bland and whatever facial expression wise and else. This of course is  in comparison to the LEGENDARY CARTOON cutscenes of the ORIGINAL. If this was fixed, honestly this game would look gorgeous.- Enemies are super aware in hard difficulty, i was not able to stealth properly because if you kill someone with a silent weapon there is a high chance someone is going to notice, it is borderline annoying, even if OG XIII didn't have a great stealth system i did want to expect the enemies to be a bit dumber to give me more time to react and to avoid whipping a revolver and wake up the entire place.- multiplayer lacking modes, so far there is just ONE mode, only DM. Nothing special which is somewhat disappointing, it would have better if there was nothing at this point, though i cannot complain about this as it's a good side addition. - Some characters still look awful, like the beach girl which you meet at the start, i am honestly wondering what they were thinking with making them look like this.- Too much ammo, too much possibility to kill through practically every boss in seconds. Which makes it less enjoyable as a fight, and makes the player less afraid of them, the health pool should be increased and the difficulty raised when it comes to the enemies you fight.Overall, this game is worth the try, it is worth imo the full price and also the efforts the developers went through is, legit insane. They could have called it a day but ♥♥♥♥ no, they woke up, worked and made it possible for us to try the game and make it playable, it's NOT even that it sold well- Like, i am quite happy this was worked on very well, and i thank the developers a lot for this, but PLEASE IF YOU CAN, FIX THESE LAST THINGS!!! Tower Five you have BALLS of steel and deserve the love coming, please do your best!The XIII community would FALL in love with this game again, and perhaps a lot of other people could be aware of this game one day. It would raise up quite the storm because XIII it's not a 2 bit game, it's legit something interesting with a very beautiful concept which many of us loved.Thank you again! Please do not give up on this game just yet!

_childDocuments_.review: Y'know how System Shock (2023) is a faithful, beautiful remake of a beloved game that improves and builds upon the already legendary original? Yeah, this game (despite the devs attempts to save face) is the exact opposite of that. It is physically painful for me to not just put insults in this text box because of my limitless frustration and contempt for whoever is responsible for this. They should not have released this. They should not have kept it up after the backlash. They should not have tried to fix it. They should not be charging money for this. They should be paying everyone who even looked at the Steam page for this game $100, let alone the unfortunate souls who bought it.Heres a brief list of my actual issues with this game:-It is a one-for-one copy of the original, the only addition (not improvement) is a waypoint.-The textures (even at full resolution) look low-res and pixelated. They don't mesh well with the inconsistent thin/thick black outlines.-There are only a handful of unique character models and they all look like mobile game assets with a crappy thin outline, they do not match the comicbook aesthetic whatsoever.-The animations  and transitions between them look like something I would make. They're very choppy and quick, it makes the game look very amateurish.-The art on the main menu splash screen have inconsistent proportions, their heads are huge and limbs are tiny.

_childDocuments_.review: The original was campy and loose but the charm made it a memorable part of my childhood - I tried to like this remake, I really did - but actually playing the game felt like a chore. At the most basic level, it didn't even support my monitors resolution, which is unforgivable for any game released in 2020. Technical issues aside, a game like XIII has to be , and I kept thinking "If I slog through this next bit, it might get better". It didn't.I keep coming back to the steam store page to see if it's been overhauled and is exciting again. I can forgive a game for being bad, if you can still have fun with it. I still go back to Deus Ex 2 to mess around with it and that was a bad game eighteen years ago. I've picked up second hand no-name budget games for a buck at an op shop that I've had more fun and spent more time with. The XIII remake is worse than bad - it's disappointing; it's charmless, uninteresting and I've yet to find a reason to revisit it. The potential that is wasted here is the greatest tragedy of all.When people point to Cyberpunk 2077 as the gaming disappointment of 2020, I show them this. The damp squib of the year of COVID.

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics aside, what the remake was INTENDED to be was the original game's campaign and levels more or less faithfully recreated (with the original cel-shading replaced by more of a Fortnite-like cartoony art-style), but with new, more "modern" Call of Duty-inspired gameplay, including aim-down-sights, a limited inventory, a simplified health/armor system, and partial regenerating health. Rather similar to what happened with F.E.A.R. 2/F,E,A,R, 3, Bioshock Infinite, Aliens Colonial Marines, etc.If that was all, it'd be divisive but I'd personally find it to be 6-8 hours of decent mindless shoot-bang fun. The problem is what the game was intended to be is currently buried under a massive pile of bugs and glaringly unfinished work the likes of which are frankly shocking. The game feels like it was pushed out the door only 70% complete with placeholder A.I. and character animations.If they'd fix the bugs, completely replace the braindead A.I., and fix the missing animations, and actually polish everything, I'd actually give the game a thumbs up, with the caveat that I recognize it wouldn't be to everyone's taste given the major changes from the original. However, in its current state I'd have to say it's not worth it.Honestly, the original XIII's core identity was mostly its art style and presentation. The actual game mechanics weren't particularly iconic (unlike something like F.E.A.R. or Doom 3 or Halo) and I can more or less understand modernizing it to be more like modern shooters (whereas if they tried to do the same thing to something like F.E.A.R. or Bioshock I'd totally join in on the "look how they massacred my boy" bandwagon). Also, as an aside, I have no problems with the new art style but totally understand people that do. If this art style was used for "Timesplitters 4", for example, I don't think most people would be complaining about the graphics style, but for XIII specifically the issue is the cel shading look was part of the game's core identity. I'm not sure how you'd even do real cel shading in 2020 (Slasher's Keep looks good, but actually uses 2D sprites like the original Doom did). I actually find the art style a refreshing change from the modern, unsustainably expensive push for more and more photorealism, i.e. games like Anthem where they spent 50 million dollars to make photorealistic character models and then use random schlubs from the grocery store as the models for the main characters.

_childDocuments_.review: This "review" is about the reworked version of PlayMagic's flop of XIII remake, that was significantly improved by Tower Five, not the original release of 2020 remake!Full on remake of XIII was always going to be quite controversial due to XIII's impact on cell-shaded graphics and cult status. As a matter of fact, THIS originally was suppose to be just a remaster, but due to Ubisoft being run by amateurs, it quickly turned out no source files for the original XIII were to be found and thus, instead of cancelling the project, the decision was made to remake XIII from scratch. This - after much crunch (due to the PlayMagic's terrible management) and multiple delays - eventually turned out to a total disaster, known as XIII (2020) or XIII remake. Microids clearly being dissatisfied with a quality of the product delivered by PlayMagic, eventually decided to just take the project away from them and give it to Tower Five in an attempt to salvage this disaster.So how is the product now after Tower Five has done their rework? Good. It's not a groundbreaker, but massive amount of issues seemed to have been fixed. From anti-aliasing that was straight up not working (due to PlayMagic hiring many interns and junior developers and over-crunching them to a point, where nobody apparently read notes about deferred rendering being incompatible with MSAA), terrible poor performance, boring gunplay, ridiculous art-style and post-processing that made the game look as bad as Fortnite, to numerous bugs related to ragdolls, clipping through geometry, soflocks - an amount of improvements and fixes that Tower Five had to do, to salvage PlayMagic's mess is truly insane. I have played through the game twice - first time on the highest difficulty, and the other time on lowest gathering collectibles and both times - despite me expecting to have terrible experience - I had a lot of fun. And new post-processing - even if it makes some scenes look a bit flat - is levels above original 2020 version and brings is significantly closer to the style of the 2004 game, while no longer being limited by 2004's graphical limitations.Shooting is fun - a bit random and a bit basic, reminding me a bit of Far Cry 4, but nevertheless it is satisfying. Platforming sections work without any problem. Cutscenes play as intended and I have not encountered any massive graphics issues in any of my playthroughs either (I did encounter minor ones like transparent surfaces being rendered in wrong order - but that happens to everyone). When 3 of my biggest issues are that FOV slider is at the moment broken and clamped to 90 horizontal degrees (instead of 120 that is shows), that at occasion I managed to clip through the ground and that you can still leftovers of original 2020's awful art-style in pre-rendered cutscenes, I think I can fairly confidently say - this is a good game now.As for the price at which to pick up the game? I would probably still say - wait for sale, as I don't think - even after all the fantastic work that Tower Five has put - that this is worth 29,99€. But sub 20€ is a fair deal at which I can easily recommend it.Good job, Tower Five! And props to Microids for not abandoning the game in an awful state.

_childDocuments_.review: ★★☆☆☆ Okay!How does the gameplay fare? You know, I didn't think they could make it worse, but they did. The original XIII isn't known for its gameplay. It's a classic case of style over substance. Now that they've ripped that style to shreds, all they have left to impress with is the gameplay.Environmental detail has seen a major improvement, also. The UI looks way better than it did in the original. The biggest thing this remake does right, though, is its saving system. The original XIII, for all it does right, had a terrible saving system. Checkpoints were few and far between and while the game gave you the illusion of manual saves, loading those saves would take you back to the checkpoint.

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of this writing, I've played through XIII 2 times, once on the hardest difficulty and once on easy. I grabbed every collectible, got every single achievement (minus beating the game on medium difficulty) all in about 16 hours. XIII is riddled with bugs ranging from mildly annoying/funny (heads of enemies glitching out, certain audio cues being off sync) to game breaking (being stuck in an animation that never ends without a full restart of the game, gun sounds not going off at all).There are numerous levels that simply don't have a cutscene to bridge the gaps in time. On one mission, you'll escape by a car/helicopter/plane and then just *pop* into existence in an entirely new map with new weapons and a brand new objective with no real explanation on how you got there and why you're there.The checkpoint system in this game is laughable, especially near the end of the game where you'll have to possibly re-play some of the hardest parts of the game all over again just because the checkpoints are so poorly placed. Add in the horrible boss fights that are just bullet sponges with no reaction to being shot, stabbed or blown up with grenades, and you've got a messy combo.The only benefits to this game are the excellent voice acting jobs by some of the cast, especially that of Major Jones (Eve) and General Carrington (Adam West), an incredibly easy achievement list and some of the weapon animations being pretty well done.Even though I got this at a huge discount (thanks Humble Bundle!), I cannot ever recommend this to anyone. Getting this game at any cost -- hell, even for free -- is too much. The amount of bugs, glitches, missing features and general lack are all painfully obvious, and you'd be better off picking up the classic edition of XIII if you're really wanting to play through the story. Otherwise, skip this and save your time and money.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: The game has been patched twice now with more on the way. In the state the game is now, you're bound to have a better experience! I can now safely recommend the game although it still has several flaws that need fixing.I am a huge fan of the XIII series. I've played the original games back on playstation 2 and gamecube back in the day. When I saw a remake was on its way, of course I would be one of the first people to try it out! But, in the current state of this game, it is not very immersive or enjoyable. Here are a list of issues I've encountered in the first half hour I played through this game:Constant Audio issues:- The audio would cut off, or not even play at all- Music would stutter, sound static especially (and maybe caused?) whenever someone or something makes a sound or says something. I guess the audio just doesn't play nice when more than one sound plays at once.Graphical Issues:- The ragdoll physics are bad. You kill someone and they pretty much just fall over all in the same way, regardless of whatever animation they were just doing. Their bodies also become jello instantly.- After the flashback on the beach, when it took me back to the beach from the boat I was greeted to the lifeguard having no pupils for half a second before her eyes rolled back onto their spot. - Some of the pickups would disappear whenever I get close enough before I could pick them up making it impossible for me to. Then reappear when I get further away from it.General Issues and complaints:- I plugged in my Xbox One controller to play through the game more comfortably, and it detected it just fine in the main menu, and even had the proper bindings in settings. So I navigated the menu using the controller just fine but as soon as I get in-game, it wouldn't let me use it. It just wouldn't respond at all, but when I paused on my keyboard, I could navigate the pause menu just fine with a controller.- The Multiplayer has no bots, is entirely local, and does not have most of the original maps and modes.- The in-game cutscene at the end of the Helicopter Bossfight doesn't show Amos or Carrington (They're invisible?)- The Cutscene after the scene I was talking about was missing audio.- Some of the Cutscenes are missing. I don't get if they are just not in the game or if it just automatically skips. Regardless it makes the transition between levels feel abrupt.The game is missing the more obscure features from the original game:- In Brighton Beach, when the hitman enters and says "Get over here", if you dont open the door and stay at spawn, he enters the building and says some extra dialogue. In the remake he just stops after his second line and doesn't enter.- In Brighton Beach, if you unload the AK47/Kalash onto the Helicopter before it gets away the first time, you can actually make it explode. This makes the rest of the level easier because less enemies spawn since the helicopter is now destroyed. In the remake, this feature is entirely absent.- In the original XIII, there would be security cameras you could check to get an idea of what to expect, and Carrington even makes a point about using it. This feature was entirely absent in the remake, yet Carrington still tells you to check the camera.- In Plain Rock, once you get the master key from one of the guards at the beginning, you are able to backtrack and unlock the cells of other prisoners, allowing you to interact with them directly, get medkits hidden in the cell, and extra dialogue from the SPADS prisoner. You are also able to kill all the inmates if you wish to. ALL of this is absent from the Remake, you cant even unlock the doors or anything.- You can not dual wield with the silenced pistol. In the original game, you were able to hold the silenced pistol on one hand and the unsilenced one on the other hand. Its a completely useless feature but its absent in this game, you can't dual wield pistols unless they're both unsilenced, or else you will drop the one you're holding to pick up the other one.- The weapon wheel is a great addition but it severely restricts your inventory, and some weapons share slots that you don't think should. The Uzi takes the spot of your pistol, and the Rocket Launcher takes the spot of your Sniper rifle which is honestly really restricting. The idea isn't an issue but it should at least allow for you to carry both a sniper and the M60 or RPG. It doesn't make sense that you cant carry two completely different weapons but an Uzi and M16 is fine.I will add more as I continue playing the game. Do I love this game? Yes! Would I recommend it in its current state? No. I hope the criticism is heard and they work towards fixing and polishing this timeless classic!

_childDocuments_.review: Even as a gamer who hasn't played the original XIII, it is obvious that the remake fails to live up to the standard and heights of the original because it fails so heavily as a contemporary title. Despite already receiving a total of around nine gigabytes of patches within its first month, the remake of XIII is a dismal failure which is still substantially broken. The flaws to this title are so rife that it cannot be redeemed or repaired with updates. Instead, the remake needs to be totally rethought and remade from the ground up as a whole new title. The sound design is the worst I have ever heard in gaming where the sound effects of the guns lack any punch and instead sound muffled or softened. Sound effects, in general, are drowned out by the game's score which, for an unexplained reason, causes the sound levels of the dialogue and sound effects to fluctuate from audible to fairly muted. Thanks to the stylistic speech bubbles within the game, I was able to discern character dialogue and key plot events. Meanwhile, the game's animation is utterly atrocious. All of the in game animations and cinematics are stilted and awkward looking in that any of the character's movements completely lack agility. More laughably, the character death animations are strange where, upon the death of a hostile NPC, the enemy shouts "noooo"only to very slowly sink to the floor in a sleep-like state. Furthermore, textures such as water may as well not be there due to the lifeless look and feel of them. The gameplay itself (gunplay, exploration, interactivity with the environment) feels shallow in that the world is barely interactive and there is little to explore. Meanwhile, any of the game's attempts at incorporating stealth into the formula fall flat where it is strictly at the game's behest where the only time there is stealth investment is when the plot calls for such an approach. Otherwise, the player is nearly always limited to the guns blazing approach. But, this is the least of the concerns as the game features substantial game breaking bugs where if a player is not standing at a precise spot at the precise time, event moments will not trigger and the game will not progress. For now, the only fix for this is to reload the mission that features the bug. Finally, boss fights are a farce where they consist of nothing but lazily paced and executed shooting matches which can be resolved with no cover, subterfuge, specialised tactics, gadgets or any effort. Boss fights, including the very finale, are limited to running around the map and shooting at the slow walking NPC until he is dead. That's it. So, does XIII do anything right?Yes. While there are serious flaws with the sound design, the soundtrack itself is good. Musically, the soundtrack consists of fun, jazzy 60s style spy music to give the game an upbeat and slightly retro feel. The art design, when it is free of visual corruptions or glitches, is terrific with its stylistic cell shading and visual tribute to the titular French comic of the 1980s. Finally, the plot is terrific in its content and overall pacing. That's the greatest disappointment with the XIII remake; the elements to make this game a classic are present. It has a great story, terrific soundtrack with a great artistic design while the potential for a diverse gaming experience consisting of action, espionage, stealth and adventure style of gaming is present. All of these elements can and SHOULD work together. But, the game is ineptly assembled to such a point where it feels like a very expensive BETA that should have been withheld from the public. There is no price which could justify purchasing this game with all its flaws. Once again, it is unclear how patches and updates could fix it as too many of the flaws are attributable to the core design. By far, the worst game of 2020 and utterly heartbreaking. 1 out of 5

_childDocuments_.review: Update: Huge improvement!!!This is playable now.  It still has a glitch here and there to include a few places where you can fall through the map to your death, but the problems are now only occasional and not enough to stop someone from finishing the game.  Perhaps it's not the most polished game, but it's passable now.In terms of previous problems:- The sound seems fixed- The enemy behavior scripting is better- The horrific graphic glitches have been absent- An enemy-caused explosion of a barrel definitely damaged enemies - maybe an RPG would too?Original review (for historical context)This is not a user experience to be proud of, yet, but it is definitely a cautionary tale about rushing a release.This could be a great game, but it's just not ready for release, even after two fixes.  .  Strike that, I just had to crank the mouse sensitivity WAY down, which makes it almost playable.Other problems:- The sound cuts out.  - The enemy AI is shockingly bad.  - There are embarrassing graphic glitches.  - Perhaps it's just an opinion, but I don't feel good with the decision that an enemy can shoot RPGs at another enemy without hurting them (but if that was the only flaw, I'd shrug and give it a thumbs up).Nice points:- The soundtrack is AMAZING (as it always was, but now it sounds better when it's not glitching out).  - The concept was there.  - I dig the new art style (although I empathize with those stating that they wish more comic-book aesthetic had survived even if I thought the balance was good).Shame to anyone involved with the decision to rush this release before it was ready.  Props to everyone else who just did their part as best they could.  Here's to hoping the teams are given the chance to polish this up into something people like.I'm really on the fence as to whether or not I should request a refund or just hope things get fixed. _childDocuments_.review: Was really looking forward to this, huge fan of the original and was looking forward to playing a modern take.  Firstly the graphics are completely different, this was probably the most notable thing about the original so it seems like a strange choice.  I actually think its looks quite good but still would of preferred the original design.  However there are some major issues with this.  The glitches...second level I fell through a solid floor to my death.  Dead enemies floating upside down with their legs in the air.  I've currently got to a point where for some reason the next part of the level just won't trigger, this has happened a couple of times in different level.  Some of the animations are very funny, every downed enemy seems to die the same way in this slightly delayed staggered way, doesn't matter how they've been killed, whacked in the head with a chair, headshot, body shot, the same strange animation.  The AI is brilliant for all the wrong reasons.  Sniping people from distance stood with their mate looking directly at them...they go down, their mate either does nothing or moves directly to where they are and looks down and does nothing allowing you to then make further shots! Sometimes whole groups of enemies will do this and it ends up becoming really quite funny.The sound is all over the place especially with voices, you'll keep hearing the same bit of dialogue over and over(usually from the previous cutscene) and its loud like the character is right next to you.  But then you'll be in a room where a character is talking right next to you and you can't hear it all.  It does have the original voice cast though, including David Duchovny's lethargic delivery plus all the enemies shouting "Alert" every 2 minutes so thats nice for those looking for some nostalgia.Then theres the multiplayer which just seems pointless, no bots so from what I can tell all you have is local splitscreen which seems a weird choice in this day and age for a PC game.  Plus there appears to be deathmatch and team deathmatch which is less than what was in the original.  Really disappointing all in all.  I'm sure the developers could turn it around with post release patches but it leaves a slightly sour taste in your mouth the way it currently it is and it is very hard to recommend in the state its currently in.  Whats even weirder is that I think this game got delayed a year, I'd have loved to have seen the state of it when it was originally planned to come out.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played the original a lot, to the point where i can remember about 80% of the dialogue word for word, and other game play mechanics like spawns of enemies / items. So when i saw that there was a remake of my childhood game i was so happy that i couldn't shut up about it, and wanted to play it badly. Now that i have, i wished i didn't, so many things wrong with this game that a bug fix wouldn't help it.    >Core Mechanics:- ADS: It breaks the AI and how the game works, being able to snipe enemies from afar removes the challenge of trying to work around certain weapon arch-types. You can sit back with any ranged weapon like a pistol (.44 mainly) and head shot everyone- Sprint: The AI's aim was bad enough already, so having the player move faster in a game in which the arenas where meant to be played at a slower pace (slower movement speed to allow enemies to hit their shots) breaks the flow of the combat. You can run around everyone in game and get an easy headshot and take barley any damage, also there is a delay when activating sprint and being able to shoot / reload, so that's fun.                                                                                                                                - Weapon Wheel: Being able to hold only one weapon per weapon arch-type kills the fun of having variety with your engagements, having to decide whether not to switch out one weapon for another takes away player freedom.- Cut Scenes are drawn out for no reason but to add that little 'detail' before playing again, it's nice, but having a 15 second ingame cutscene be a 30 second scene because of details gets old fast.                                         >Other Things I Noticed (A short TL:DR One the small things that was off)- Animations looks scuffed; from enemies dying, to use of items, melee items, picking up bodies, etc. It tries either to be too realistic or too fancy with it's animations, which doesn't work well with the arcadey game play.- Sound effects for weapons, reloads, and items are completely gone and replaced with generic audio files found online. The heavy impacts from weapons is gone, reloading is boring, and sometimes it just outright won't work                                                 - The looks of it is completely different from the original, it went from Cel-shaded artstyle with comic strips thrown in there to a dull rounded look. Characters looks like something you would find on Fortnite, and weapons was replaced with a more 'modern' look that makes it looks smaller.- Certain weapons feels weaker in comparison to the original game, probably due to the fact that ADS exists and balancing it would take too long- Ingame events breaking / starting without me being near the trigger causing the AI to stand around doing nothing until i'm directly in their face- Music just doesn't work when it's suppose to or plays after it's intended trigger- XIII and Hard difficulty is a joke, both the AI's terrible aim and aiming from a distance makes every engagement a cake walk. Only died once in the beginning of the game because of learning the controls fully, other than that, flawless playthroughs  - And many more bugs and glitches that it's laughable I love XIII from the first time i played it with my father till now, I even got my friends to play the original and they are enjoying the game. But this newer edition makes me both tilted and confused by it's changes and bugs that I can't even anymore. I would not recommend this version of this game, play the original, and have some fun.    - Also just found out that after downloading this game, my other copies of the 2003 version is breaking or just not working correctly so thanks for that too

_childDocuments_.review: It's rare to see such backlash towards a game- but in this case, it's absolutely warranted.I didn't expect much because I obtained it in a bundle and wanted to play it out of nostalgia. I do remember the classic game fondly, I played it in an area when paper magazines were still thriving, and some were offering complete PC games- that's how I got XIII.I was so taken in that I later read the source material- the ending was such a cliffhanger...We're sill in a period where you can see many remakes and remasters, XII certainly deserver one- but not this... Product. I wouldn't be as critical as others regarding the graphics, but the gameplay, oh my. Normal difficulty is much easier than in the original and the upper difficulty doesn't make the AI smarter, which the big problem. Ennemies like to reload out in the open, fire at non-destructible pieces of the environment or line up in your scope like lemmings. Even playing without too much effort or focus, I mowed them down easily.Bosses are the most pitiful specimens of the bunch : each of them is a non-challenge, charging you mindlessly, getting stuck in nothing, getting dazed too easily. The game itself is quite playable but the few additions - like the waypoints - are plainly not needed.I didn't double check by replaying the original, but I'm almost positive they've also skipped several sections, in the levels or narratively-wise, some transitions between levels are more than abrupt.The barebone multiplayer mode is, of course, completely dead. Even with the lowered price, wether you are a veteran or new to XII, don't bother. Play the original instead.

_childDocuments_.review: First things first, Unity 3D.Who thought this was going to on the Unity 3D engine? Anyone? Nope. Why is it on the Unity 3D engine? Who knows. Whoever made that decision is the reason why this game has such horrific reviews. The animations, Frame Rates and over all clunky feeling the ENTIRE game has is most likely due to the engine being Unity 3D. Watch as you get a solid maybe 70 frames, then your sensitivity will skyrocket as your FPS dips to like 20 and it picks it back up. I ran this game in 1440p, on the lowest settings with a 2080TI and the entire time the game is open your GPU will be hard stuck at 99% usage the entire time this game is open.  Thats the Unity 3D engine for ya.Second stop on this ride is the Animations. A disaster in itself. NONE of the animations I saw ran smoothly/correctly. Many times your gun (Especially the magnum) will clip back to the last frame of the shooting animation, so it just jitters back and forth sometimes. The enemy movement is choppy, and whenever you kill anyone they all to the SAME EXACT death animation every single time. Think of a T pose, but with them holding a finger pistol and then just toppling over. On every single enemy. Completely ruins the immersion every time you kill someone. In a nutshell this is how animations are -  : 3 minutes of just WTF. Basically in the entire gameGraphical wise - I didn't see many issues. It looked good when standing still, hence why the screenshots make the game look amazing on the store page. AI in this game is also just a mess. I played on the second to last hardest difficulty. So basically hard, and in-between trying to aim correctly with the  and messed up animation you can basically just click once on their head and their dead. I barely ever even checked my health unless I was getting sniped, without the snipers and bazookas the damage input to you is next to nothing.I played up until the mission where you go into the tent to bug the guys office. No matter what I did, I always failed the mission as soon as I planted the bug. I hid bodies, did everything but as soon as the guy spawns in it was game over. After 2 tries at that, I gave up and started writing the review. In a nutshell, I do not see many of these issues getting fixed with the current engine and I do not ever see this game going above "Mixed" reviews on steam. Why they thought this was ready to roll out as a completed game is beyond me and is now on my list for THE worst remake I have ever played. For a full playthrough of what I painstakingly went through, you can watch the stream and click anywhere in the video to see this game in its full, depressing glory. By about minute 10 I realized I was in for a treat, and now cannot refund due to steams 2 hours rule. My playthrough - Some dumb lookin deer that just stood there and did nothing, but I remember it being in the original with animations. Just a derp deer -

_childDocuments_.review: Man... where do i start...Just a premise : The game itself currently is not even half bad. The shooting feeling has been improved a lot and there are a couple mechanics that make the game feel more like a compact title that is flowing constantly.But.... yes, BUT... This game is a good 6/10The gameplay itself is almost identical to the original, the maps look really similar to the original, with some obvious reworks of the big ones (Canyon is one of them, it's more compact and there are less empty pointless spaces). Overall the game flows flawlessly, too flawlessly.... There are a lot of mechanics that have been introduced pretty much from the beginning of the game; and this makes it WAY easier than the original.Speaking of difficulty.... Well, there is none.... The original forced you to think twice before acting, you had to sneak more and rethink some strategies.... and this, well... it feels like a linear run and gun. The AI is utterly useless and easily cheesable, especially the bosses. From all the bosses i fought, only the one in the submarine was somehow responsive to reason. The Doctor and Soldier were absolutely clueless. They just stood aimlessly and glitched out giving the opportunity for the player to just fill them with bullets. Speaking of filling with bullets, you can pretty much get trought an entire mission and not die. Most of the time the enemy can be one shot, maybe three shot with the M16, there is no difficult situation, just gun everyone down. The new mechanic of aiming down sights is a great improvement to the shooting, but it makes the game absolutely easy to rush trought. You can shoot enemies down from miles away and they will be absolutely clueless of what's going on. A clear example of this the massive empty space just before getting into the submarine; you can pretty much gun down the entire area from up above. Other than that, the game has been gotten rid of the annoying bits, that gave it a bit of puzzle like approach, probably this decision has been made for the new gen of players that are not famous for patience and thinking.The recreation itself is pretty accurate, there are some bits and bobs that are missing that are minor, but some of them are absolutely immersion breaking. An example of this is the cameras in the mission to free your prisoner. There is a bit where in the original you can see an enemy on camera, prompting one of the main characters to joke about it; they left the text but there is no camera to give more immersion. This goes also for the first bit of that mission, where you cannot look into the monitor to see approaching guards.Overral it's a meh remaster and definetly not worth the OG price.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll recommend this, however, there are some caveats. I have played the classic version before too. I will say that the graphics here are an obvious upgrade. The low polygon counts in the original make the older version of the game look incredibly dated. This, in comparison, looks much more modern. However, as others have noted, the "comic book" art-style and aspects are quite toned down in the remake. I honestly wouldn't have known that it was trying to even have a comic book aesthetic in the remake if it weren't for the borders appearing sometimes and the speech bubbles. The game is cell shaded, yes, but not in a way that screams comic book to me, per se. The original definitely had a comic book vibe woven throughout the game, whereas here, it feels more like an afterthought. Secondly, I can't put my finger on it, but this game gave me the worst eye fatigue with its color palettes. Environments often feel really bright, busy, and washed out. I don't really get eye strain from playing games, however, looking at these environments started taking a toll one hour into playing. This is something that the original classic version didn't do to me, so, I think that a better balance of highlights / shadows / midtones should have been used here. That being said, it was a good game. I only encountered a few glitches, which is apparently a far cry from how glitchy it was upon release. Once, I completely clipped through the floor I was standing on, and fell through it. Secondly, I got stuck in the walls of the submarine. Thirdly, my game did crash randomly twice. And lastly, I did see one NPC stuck between the floor boards, Jumanji style, on the yacht. I'm recommending the game because it does quite a lot better than the original, however, it still trades blows with the original. This will definitely feel more modern on newer PCs. I didn't play the original back when it first released. I was a bit late to discovering XIII, so, I didn't see the classic through the same nostalgia glasses that many others did. If the slight bit of residual glitchiness got patched, and if they perhaps adjusted the color scheme to be better, this would be an easy recommend. However, as it stands, this is a lukewarm recommend from me. I feel as though the art style is Borderlands-esque, yet misses the mark. It's still a slightly glitchy and janky game, however, it is undeniable that they modernized the remake and made it far more palatable for players who are allergic to outdated graphics. For those who don't mind low polygon potato graphics, I recommend the original because it's vastly cheaper (especially when on sale) and has far more of a comic book vibe going for it.

_childDocuments_.review: XIII is a remake of the eponymous 2003 shooter by Ubisoft, developed by PlayMagic and published by Microids in 2020. It is a remake no one asked for, and a few played. Those who did play the game reported numerous bugs and extremely poor performance on launch day. Note that I purchased the game some two years after release when many bugs had been patched. I was someone who really enjoyed the original game, having played through the entire thing in 2022 and then immediately bought and downloaded the remake. At first, I liked the remake, but with the first NPC death animation, I started realizing how mediocre the entire thing is. Where the original oozes with style, charisma, and fun, the remake manages to do the same worse. The cutscenes look bland, the characters are uninteresting, and the music and ambient sounds tend to either disappear or warp like a broken tape recorder. I didn't experience any game-breaking bugs on my playthrough, but I saw a bunch of characters T-posing or making incredible John Carpenter The Thing-like poses, which is both horrifying and funny. I won't get into the game's story or characters, as that is better experienced in the original game, but I will say that 2020's XIII may not be as bad as the reviews make it seem. In its present state, the game is playable from start to finish and performs much better and more steadily. I think the best way to play XIII is the original, but if you ever wish to beat the game or revisit some of the old levels, try the remake, as it can be fun when it works. There is no excuse to release games in a state like XIII was on launch day, but giving credit where it's due, PlayMagic fixed the game as they promised to, and for that, the remake deserves to exist, even though it will never replace the original.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10Let's get this out of the way first, I wasn't there to experience this remake when it was first released. I don't condone developers releasing broken and unfinished games, but it is what it is. With that being said, in this game's current state, it's a significant improvement over the original from 2003. I'm not kidding when I say the addition of aiming down sights and a revamped checkpoint system alone, are enough for me to recommend this remake over the original from 2003, even if it's your first time playing XIII. The original from 2003 may have better comic-book and cutscene presentation, but that's not enough for me to recommend playing that over this, if it means putting up with shoddy shooting mechanics and scarce checkpoints.+ Great soundtrack.+ Good replay value.+ Good weapon variety.+ Bosses have less health.+ Weapons have good impact.+ Good aesthetics and graphics.+ Vastly improved checkpoint system.+ New sprint mechanic improves mobility.+ Switching weapons is much faster. Which is needed for this kind of game.+ New aiming down sights mechanic vastly improves the shooting accuracy.+ Escort objectives are no longer an issue as the escort NPCs are now invincible.- Every level transition removes most of your inventory items.- Cutscenes are unchanged from the 2020 version. The one before the sanctuary level is outright missing.- Stealth sections with instant failure. To be fair, this game wouldn't be a remake if these sections were removed outright.
