name: Scathe
detailed_description: Discord Channel About the Game Blast Your Way Through Bullet Hell! Scathe is an intense, classic FPS with big guns and bloodthirsty demons. You are Scathe, Enforcer of the Legions of Hell, forged from the earth by the Divine Creator himself. And you, like your fallen kin before you, must prove your worth by navigating a deviously crafted maze, entangled with demonic evil at every twist and turn. Grab your Hell Hammer and get ready to unleash your almighty fury! Use Scathe’s brute strength and extreme speed to purge your way through Hell’s most grotesque abominations, as you search for the Hellstones and defeat the all-powerful Guardians that protect them. Drop In/drop Out Online Multiplayer Scathe supports full online crossplay multiplayer where players can drop in and drop out at any time. Already lost deep within the labyrinth? Call upon up to three friends to join the fight. But choose your kin wisely: everyone shares the same pool of lives. Escape the Maze Your task is simple; collect the Hellstones and escape the maze. Choose your own path by navigating expertly handcrafted zones - each filled with danger around every corner. Collect runes, uncover secrets, and smite all that stand in your way. Bullet Hell Scathe is no ordinary FPS… Take on relentless bullet Hell fuelled combat, with deadly projectiles and countless demons at every turn. Utilise Scathe’s incredible speed to smash through your enemies and incoming fire. Lock ‘n Unload Rip through your enemies with Scathe’s insanely powerful arsenal of weapons, each equipped with a devastating secondary fire. Spew hellfire with the Hot Hatch or slice through endless evil with the Bow Blade. As you explore the labyrinth, you’ll encounter ancient relics guarded by the Fallen Mages. Charge up your arcane energy by crushing your enemies and channel it into potent spells. Heal yourself, summon aid, and wreak havoc on the legions of Hell! Honour and Glory New to Scathe: Enforcer Edition includes two new modes and a host of custom modifiers to fine-tune your journey through the underworld. Run and gun through Guardian gauntlets in Speedrun Mode, or let the red mist descend in arena-based Arcade Mode – nothing but you, your weapons, and a room full of demons. Prefer a power fantasy? Tear through Scathe with new starting modifiers like invincibility and infinite Demon Mode, or turn up the heat with Demon Overload! Please note that an Epic Games account is required in order to play Scathe.

Charge up your arcane energy by crushing your enemies and channel it into potent spells. Heal yourself, summon aid, and wreak havoc on the legions of Hell! Honour and Glory New to Scathe: Enforcer Edition includes two new modes and a host of custom modifiers to fine-tune your journey through the underworld. Run and gun through Guardian gauntlets in Speedrun Mode, or let the red mist descend in arena-based Arcade Mode – nothing but you, your weapons, and a room full of demons. Prefer a power fantasy? Tear through Scathe with new starting modifiers like invincibility and infinite Demon Mode, or turn up the heat with Demon Overload! Please note that an Epic Games account is required in order to play Scathe.
short_description: Scathe is an intense, blood-soaked FPS where quick reflexes are the key to surviving bullet Hell. Rip through the labyrinth that stands between you and your ascension. Blast your way through the underworld’s deadliest demons solo or with up to three comrades in drop-in/drop-out online co-op.

_childDocuments_.review: Scathe is a weird game. Maybe I just don't get it.You mow down legions of demons in corridors, scoring points in hopes to get to the green door at the end. And then you repeat. You start off with a machine gun that has infinite bullets, so you keep the left click button pressed until the end of the level. You have numerous lives, which helps considering how rare health pickups are. Weirdly enough, you'll see a lot of pick-ups that you can't use because you don't have unlocked the weapon yet. Why not replace these with pickups you can actually use?The other weapons you unlock look gorgeous (except the crossbow, it looks weak as hell and its weapon switching animation is bugged as of now) but ammo is so scarce that you might as well keep using that infinite ammo starting gun. The shotgun should have been the game's main weapon, to be honest, not that weak assault rifle. I quickly realised that killing demons is pointless, so I just rushed past most of them to reach the end quicker. Some rooms require that you kill the demons to progress, though. Yeah, and turrets seems to be indestructible, so don't waste your time on them even if your cursor turns red.Edit : turns out, turrets can be destroyed but it seems inconsistent. Or the starting gun just sucks, maybe. Yeah, probably that.I guess there's a scoring system of some sort, but I didn't see what purpose it serves. I'm not sure I'll keep playing. Probably for a bit until I move on to the next thing. Or as I said earlier on, maybe I just don't get Scathe. I'll edit this review if I ever get this game.

_childDocuments_.review: In a realm beyond, an eternal battle rages between the Divine Creator and his brother Sacrilegious. Scathe, the Divine’s chosen, is sent to a hellish labyrinth with the final aim of stealing a powerful staff that would break the balance between the two gods.The Labyrinth is divided into zones belonging to three major biomes: Nature, Industrial and Temple. Each is well-diversified, and every stage is unique in layout with a few surprises here and there, visually-appealing. Even so, the levels don’t really have distinctive landmarks in the majority of cases, many will feel like ‘already-seen’.Aside from a demon encyclopedia, there isn’t any additional writing or lore to mention, except some sparse information coming from the two announcers (the Divine and his brother) that will frequently speak in Scathe’s head - and become quite annoying too, given their limited roster of lines and rarely-interesting topics.In each level there will be one thing above all to look for: Runes. These collectibles will be fundamental to unlock the six Guardian Doors around the map, each housing an Hellstone that acts as a key to open the exit of the Labyrinth. Most levels have six runes, some in plain sight, others hidden behind secret areas reachable with jumping puzzles or by activating hidden switches. Other than that, there will be some sparse ammo caches for your weapons, health pickups, and sometimes Dark Relics that grant Scathe spell rings to keep and use.The world map is divided in zones linked to each other by exits, and here comes the worst problem with Scathe: backtracking. To move between levels you’ll need to remember where each exit is located (for 49 levels!), then navigate the premises fighting or dodging enemies that respawn every time (even in 100% cleared levels) and mandatory arenas that won’t let you through until everyone inside is dead. This becomes a huge issue when you encounter a place or boss too hard (or inaccessible) for you, reach other parts of the map to gain weapons and spells, only to then have to go through a dozen already-cleared stages again to go back. If you run out of lives, you’ll respawn in the last visited special room, and that may mean re-doing multiple levels again. Ever heard of fast travel?Fast-paced and high-stakes, the foundation of Scathe’s combat brings everything you would want from a FPS / Bullet Hell hybrid; just a few hits on Hard are all it takes for you to die, thankfully you have ten lives, each allowing you to respawn on the spot - and trust me, that may seem a lot but it’s not (except in boss fights, where it’s actually excessive); death is fast, brutal and common. You’ll bring around the base machine gun with infinite ammo, generally an all-purpose solution, other than other specialized guns. Shotguns, crossbows and laser rifles that each feature powerful primary and secondary fire modes, but also have finite ammo that is generally in scarce quantities due to less-than-ideal economy.You’d think these weapons would be very powerful to have such limited ammo drops and reserves going on, but that’s usually not the case: they’re better than the base one but not a whole other level. The ammo economy is so bad I dealt with most bosses and enemies using only the basic gun, make what you will of it. The fact enemy archetypes are low in number, and that each biome mostly features recolors that are mechanically identical, makes the combat become stale rather fast, especially with all the forced backtracking involved.Your abilities will be fundamental, above all the Dash that allows Scathe to plow through enemies, killing all but the strongest ones instantly, briefly deny bullet damage or make longer jumps while mid-air. Spell rings will allow the casting of magic such as healing, AoE damage and more; each of them is fueled by mana gained from killing enemies and gathering the shards they drop after defeat. The issue with all this is balance yet again, with more than half the rings being gimmicks and a few of them being instead really overpowered.The first special level you’ll come across will be Arenas, requiring you to kill a certain number of mobs for all the exits to unlock, and stay unlocked forever after that. Not to be confused with mini-arenas present in normal levels, which work in the same way, just smaller in scale and respawning each time a transition happens. Weapon rooms are devoid of enemies and grant you a new murder tool, while Boss rooms can only be accessed with a certain total number of Runes and are self-explanatory. The three major and three minor boss fights are of inconsistent quality and difficulty. Some are boring circle-strafe fests, other ones legitimately good, and some feel like a bullet sponge fest. Not to make spoilers, but there actually won’t be a proper final boss beyond the final gate… something different instead, that for most players will prove a letdown.

_childDocuments_.review: An Epic Games Store account is mandatory for playing the game. If you don't have one, you can't play it. Like me. At the moment there is no mention about that on the store page.So when you launch the game, the main screen says "Press Any Key For Start." If you do that your web browser opens and you find yourself at the login page of Epic Games Store. If you press ESC, another Epic Games Store page opens. If you press Alt+F4, two more Epic Games Store pages opens (one for Alt, and one for F4). And if you press CTRL+Alt+Del, three (3) more Epic Games Store pages opens (one for CTRL, one for Alt, and one for Del).A great web browser opener. Solid work of art. 10/10. Would refund again.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun retro horde shooter that forces you to dodge a lot. It certainly has lots of obvious areas for improvement, but most of the negative reviews are from people getting stomped or have no clue how the game works. So, if you can't progress through the game instead of ragequitting I advice you to reduce the difficulty, it's not a shame.After playing for a few hours (on normal & hard) and reaching up to the first boss of the west wing I noticed the game is pretty challenging and you can't just face rush everything, you gotta dodge/hide and in some occasions aim decently well to survive against enemies that abuse verticallity. The game runs excellent for me with no issues and I haven't encountered any bugs as of yet (I didn't try coop at all though where people seem to encounter issues).As for the gameplay itself the gunplay and shooting is kinda bare-bones and basic, it works. But it gets pretty tiring when your starting gun (although being good) is pretty much all you are using. There needs to be some short of balance patch regarding weapons and ammo management - there are literally ammo boxes everywhere that you can't use because you don't even have any new weapons and even if you manage to find a new one their ammo is so limited compared to the infinite ammo of the starting rifle.The base movement of the character is pretty high and it has a small element of air control when you are jumping, not exactly that good as in Doom Eternal or Quake games, which makes it not that usable. But having fast base walking speed at least makes up for it. Also, there is the usual dash-dodge that can also be used to wreck enemies. Generally the resource system of the game is kinda bad, the shards that drop from enemies I have no idea what they are used for (scoring sytem?), also your character has multiple lives which I also don't get it, why not just have 1 life and make it count with more HP. In addition to the above, you are seriously dependant on finding health pick ups that are scattered around the map and you have no clue where they could be, but with practice you learn to find them somehow and survive the levels and ofc as I mentioned before the ammo boxes that are 90% of the time useless for you.Another thing that bothered me was the map navigation system. Since, most of the levels in each wing look familiar you don't really have a clue where you are supposed to go and you can get lost especially if you are a new player. That thing they call a map is too abstract along with the symbols. But you learn to adjust as I did and navigation will be improved the more you play.Some other annoying elements, are the environmental damage that 1 shots you, the fodder that just do nothing and the reskined enemies, the face screen clean (at least you can disable it), some bosses locked behind tons of runes (but I guess that's how the game is meant to be played, to gather runes) and the kinda annoying bloom which can tire your eyes. Gun sounds and animations could use some work as well.As a conclusion don't expect this being Doom Eternal but with coop. It's a super basic maze style retro shooter but with a solid base to enjoy yourself for some hours.I wouldn't have recommended this game if it was made from a bigger studio, but since it's a small indie one you could give this a try. The game is quite affordable with decent fundamentals and devs that seem to be hearing the early feedback.Edit: Finished the game, here is a vid containing all boss fights:

I can't keep playing if i have to continue playing slow for little reward.

_childDocuments_.review: 90 minutes gameplay: I was really excited for this game, another shooter with demon and hell theme, but after almost 2 hours gameplay it wasn't really what I was hoping for. Not saying that this style or genre is bad or anything, it wasn't just for me. I didn't find it fun to play same thing over and over again, same enemies almost same areas. Maybe I didn't understand the concept clearly but the game didn't do a good job of telling me what to do? Gather runes? OK, but to do what exactly? Can I upgrade my character/weapons? Where can I use the runes? Is it for unlocking next area? Why some areas have enemy counters and some don't? What were those blood points, are they useful later? and so on...There are the things that I wish had better and more clear guides or answers.As I said I am not a person to play same game over and over again, have a very limited time to play games and want that 2-3 hours to enjoy, this didn't deliver that to me. Maybe this is fun for you but wasn't for me.Also I F***ing hate those flying things!Visuals are great and game runs very smoothly on my machine, there were no bugs or whatsoever in my gameplay so good job on that aspect. There is very little story and lore but nothing to get excited about, maybe there are more later in the game.Also I played solo so it might be more fun playing co-op.

_childDocuments_.review: Scathe is a troubled game.At first glance it looks like a rather pretty-looking entry in the boomer-shooter genre.At second glance, it has a bit of the stink of a visually nice but poorly put-together asset flip.After having played through the main ending (but not bothering with what appears to be the true ending), the game is stranger than I initially gave it credit for. There is a lot that's missing from this game, but there's also hints of something genuinely interesting here as well.So what is Scathe, anyways? It's not just a boomer shooter or doom ripoff, the store page would have you believe that it takes inspiration from bullet-hell games as well. While it certainly does take inspiration, this appears to be a bit of a game-design dead-end for the game, as it fails to competently mesh the two genres, and can't decide which of the two it should fall back on. The enemies fire slow projectiles with the intent that you dodge them, but fails to arrange those enemies into interesting formations. The patterns you have to dodge are either trivially easy as a single stream of bullets, or literally impossible as a cloud of projectiles surrounds you and hits you from outside your field of vision. The level design consists largely of open rooms and corridors that invite you to charge into the fray, but the bullet patterns encourage you to treat it more conservatively, hiding at long range to treat it as a shooting gallery where you can see the bullets coming your way. The nicely-rendered designs and effects are all there to add the oomph a good shooter needs, but then those same effects obscure the bullets you are supposed to be dodging.And perhaps the greatest sin of this failed meshing: the bosses demand that you aim carefully at their weak points, but also that you stare at the ground and space around them to dodge their bullet patterns. This is literally impossible, and none of the bosses offer any phase transitions or resting phases to allow you time to damage them without worrying about the cloud of death surrounding you. This problem extends to every part of the game, although it is most pronounced on the bosses: the game cannot decide if you should look at the enemies, to kill them, or at their bullets, to dodge them. You are not given enough time to do both. I, personally, played through largely ignoring the bullet-hell mechanics, opting instead to clear enemies fast in order to reduce the amount of bullets they would create.So, well, it's not a bullet-hell game. But what actually is it? What can you expect if you play this game?The most interesting difference Scathe has to other, better entries in the genre is its labyrinth. Although it looks initially like it might be procedually-generated, what with all of its copy-paste corridors and spawning-in enemy waves, all the levels actually appear to be bespoke. They are arranged in a connected grid in a way that may remind you of roguelikes, particularly given the presence of weapon unlock rooms, challenge rooms, and boss rooms, but in fact the game is surprisingly conventional in how its structured. There is no permadeath, there is no metaprogression- you simply move through the map, backtracking when necessary, to collect all the macguffins scattered throughout the dungeon. The closest you will get to a game over is if you run out of lives, which... sends you back to the last weapon room you found, which seem to serve as permanent checkpoints of sorts.This is an interesting and unique setup! It reminds me of old-school dungeon crawlers a bit, exploring a large and maze-like structure to find loot, see the whole map, and finally use that treasure to beat the big bad. It's an old but good formula, and it would be fascinating to see it in the form-factor of an old-school FPS!Alas, although this is the rough shape the game seems to take, it is indeed very rough and is just all-around a difficult experience to enjoy.Despite the stunning visuals, the sound design seems to have taken a backseat and feels soft and unimpactful. The controls, while quite standard for the genre, fail to compensate for many of the rough edges in level design- no mantling and instant-death environmental hazards combine to form unfair-feeling deaths that the judicious application of coyote time would have fixed. The game only begins to see some semblance of balance after you've collected most of the unlocks, as your starting weapon (which is both the least interesting and least powerful of your arsenal) is all you have to work with until you can push through enough rooms to find new weapons. Even then, the ammo economy is so restrictive that you will still be using your starting weapon for the majority of the game, even after unlocking everything, as it's the only weapon with unlimited ammunition....I will go counter to some of the other criticism this game has received, though, and say that I actually like the face-wiping mechanic. It adds a dash of flavor to a gameplay loop that otherwise has almost nothing to distinguish it from other, more polished games. I just wish it was tied to some kind of meaningful gameplay mechanic instead of solely existing as an annoyance.If you do decide to play this game: One of the "dark magics" (rings) is actually a gun. Find that and then you can ignore the ammo economy entirely - it uses blood as ammo, the only resource you get from killing enemies. This frees you up from a lot of the tedium of combat and lets you focus more on enjoying the exploration and secret-hunting part of the game.Overall, this game has too many nice facets and curious vestigial features (the score system seems to do... nothing) for me to fully condemn the concept. What this does smell like to me is the butchered and resurrected cadaver of a more ambitious game, one which perhaps didn't have the time or budget to reach fruition. The game even has a remarkable quantity of fully-voiced dialogue, a clear indication that this was once a game with a script! But now, we only hear those dispensed more or less at random in the middle of firefights.This is not an exhaustive list of problems and complaints about the game, but I don't feel it's necessary to dogpile further on a game which clearly had a troubled development.Overall, I can't recommend this game at any price. I'm sure that there's an interesting story behind its creation, though. Maybe someday we'll get to hear it.

_childDocuments_.review: I am really enjoying this game, but I saw a lot of things in the reviews that I feel should be clarified to help users decide on this game with more information!- People get stuck on the first boss and can't find the exit.  The exit is the way you came in, there is not a new door, you just go back to the previous area or fast travel elsewhere.- You can fast travel to locations you have been to, which lets you move around without having to fight through levels again.- The lives system doesn't reset your progress, unless you lose all your lives before completing a section, then you have to do it over again.  But whatever you complete stays, and if you happen to start in a previous area, you can just fast travel to the other location you were at.- Ammo for the weapons you find is plentiful, the base weapon will cause ammo to drop for the bow, but every other weapon will have ammo drop for that specific weapon.  Which you get by killing enemies, I have yet to run out of ammo in this game.- Dashing through enemies gives you health- Those skull objects you see on walls are switches, which opens stuff to help you locate runes!- You have an overworld map that shows you your progress on each level, along with where you can get new weapons.  The relics you will find visiting a new area that has one, they are not automatically displayed.- The arcade mode does start out dark, just increase the gamma.  It is supposed to have bright red enemies, its 'the zen mode' according to the press release.  Your game is not broken.- You can increase the gibs and gore in the game, just go to your settings to have tons of limbs and stuff flying everywhere!- There is a notice on the page now saying you need Epic Games in order to play, they had to enable it in order to do crossplay between the platforms.  If you have the launcher installed, and you are logged in, it will not ask you to sign in.  Its pretty slick.Overall the game is fun, especially for the current sale price.  It does have some jank here or there, but overall its a fast paced FPS with satisfying weapons and enemies.  I have not been able to try co-op, but I could see that being rad.

_childDocuments_.review: Slaying demons is your thing? You love the fast, brutal fps gameplay from the 90s, that has seen a resurgence with the so called boomer shooters (Amid Evil, Dusk, Iron Fury, Wrath: Aoen of Ruin and many more) during the last years? You prefer better, more detailled visuals than most boomer shooters have to offer? Then play Doom Eternal. In the case of Scathe, I am not sure if I can recommend the game. Probably yes, but it certainly is no masterpiece.Scathe tries to be like the old Doom (or its many clones), just in modern clothing. You can play it with mouse and keyboard (in this case probably the better choice) or play it with your gamepad, play it in Full HD , or even in 4K if you invested in a powerful GPU. Playing on your ultradwide-screen is not possible in native 21:9 resolution, though, which I find completely unacceptable for a professional game released today. Circle-strafe and kill demons, on the ground or flying around. Use different weapons, avoid getting hit by their bullets (you can see them coming) or getting torn-apart in close combat. Enemies seem to spawn everywhere around you, even behind you, and explode in a bloody mess when you hit them. Most of the time you need to wipe off all the blood from your face to see anything. The visuals are not so bad, the sounds from the demons and your weapons are ok. There are ammo packs lying around, but you need to hold the correct weapon to collect them... which makes most of them useless. Health packs are rare. You start with 10 lifes, when you die you can just continue where you died... until all your lifes are gone. Changing the language is not possible, not even outside the game in the Steam properties. Absolutely unacceptable for a new game. Speech is english only. At least you can turn off head bobbing. Gameplay is fluid, and there is a certain charm in running/jumping around like crazy and shooting hordes of demons to a bloody pulp.Slay hordes of demons in this fast and brutal boomer shooter on your 21:9 ultrawidescreen monitor using a stretched 16:9 resolution in the language of your operating system (and only in this language) after you watched the unskippable intro.
_childDocuments_.name: Scathe

_childDocuments_.review: Scathe is a game that wants to do roguelike at a boomer shooter pace. While this is interesting on paper, promising visuals and all it fails to make up for the holes in mashing up those two formulas all while having harsh and unreasonable expectations of a player just shaking hands with it's system. Allow me to explain:Roguelikes usually have you seeing an entire screen where you can plan and react accordingly to certain unites and obstacles- Scathe is an FPS thus your vision is limited even with a higher FOV. The enemies do not have distinct sound queues that allow you to react in a way that is intuitive or even fair honestly. Blood on the floor is just a death hazard and some rooms are so dark I can't even plan for them and just trip up. Other than screaming meatballs- the game does nothing to parse it's hazards outside of a 'is it i nfront of me RIGHT NOW' scale.The music sounds badass, visuals are cool except for the beginning cutscene. Scathe and the deific figure he serves are ugly and generic- poorly constructed designs that fail to set them apart or even cement them in a fond and familiar way. This screams as too derivative of it's inspirations and leans on it's gameplay premise for identity.So you have a game with limited view perspective and cheap shots all around with poorly communicated hazards- so youd think maybe they have a way to make up for health losses with rewarding gameplay? Nope. Just play until you die or find a pickup. This wouldnt be an issue if the arena and all it's actively spawning participants were communicated better on an audio scale- but take cheap/free shots and being wittled down feels bad. On top of this a lot of the puzzles ask you to slow down your pace to do boring and monotonous puzzle platforming which would be cool if they set up the jumps in a way that feels good with the pace of the movement. It simply doesn't. On top of that the game glitched and trapped me in a room before I could close out my first run which feels awful and a bad first impression overall.There are going to be a plethora of mechanics down the line that I'll likely miss but the game feels too much like it was made to taunt it's player instead of warm us up to it's various challenges. I don't find dying fun when it's to obstacles and causes that aren't really made clear in a fair way. Notice I said fair- I don't mind punishing games. Hopefully the game gives the player more ways to combat the poor audio design in terms of survivability or just overall improves the clearly lacking parts. I REALLY want to like this game, but it's not for me until it can give me what other boomer shooter is providing in spades.On top of that- the game is a little too basic. High pace jumping and weaving is okay and all but where's the melee, the sliding, the kicking or other wild tools to bring this some clearer definition? While I understand the game has it's inspirations it doesn't need to ONLY be move fast and shoot good. Is this all locked behind some kind of earnings system later on? I hope not, the run and shoot thing got boring. The gun feedback and music were all that really kept me up until the game glitched.I hope this game improves so I can come back to it and play it. It could really be a welcome entry next to titles like DUSK, CULTIC and other neat high mobility shooters.
_childDocuments_.name: Scathe

_childDocuments_.review: My impressions video: Scathe is unlike any shooter I've ever played, for better or worse. Though it shares some attributes with boomer shooters and roguelites, it's very much its own entity as well.Honestly, I see why this game has such a mixed reception. It's trying to do something different and on that, it definitely succeeds, but this won't be for everyone. I'm giving it a thumbs up because I do enjoy the core gameplay and a lot of the issues I have can be tweaked with updates. You're not getting a more linear DOOM 2016 style experience here, but you're also not getting a first-person roguelite either. You're getting something in between. Not everyone will like it, but I applaud the developer's efforts to make something all its own.
_childDocuments_.name: Scathe

_childDocuments_.review: Scathe is a game that launched with some questionable design decisions, weird audio glitches and some frankly infuriating balance issues. And yet the devs have plugged away to make it as fun and as fine-tuned as possible. That doesn't change the fact that it's a bit odd. The pacing, the labyrinthine level design, the backtracking. This does not play like a typical shooter and it's a game that some people just won't grasp.And yet, I have a soft spot for its weird decisions, its odd pacing, its small yet confusing levels. If you pick up what the game is putting down, it's fun to blast through a few levels. It can be as bite-sized as you want as you head for the level exit and plough through a few short levels. Or you can really commit, and find the hidden relics, weapons and spells. It's punishing, but it's also kind of free form. Like I say. It's a weird game. Weapons and movement are satisfying. The game looks good. If you want a challenge, it delivers in spades. But if you want a straightforward experience, it might be a little alienating, if not aggravating. Personally, I applaud what the developers were attempting, and applaud them even further for how well they've responded to player feedback. If you've an appetite for something curious and can tolerate some frustrations (those screaming ball enemies can burn in the darkest corners of the worst imaginable version of Hell), it's worth picking up.It's hard to flat out recommend Scathe. But it's harder, for me at least, not to appreciate it.
_childDocuments_.name: Scathe

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most poorly balanced games I have ever played, and it's genuinely impressive how the devs managed to make the wrong choice in almost every single scenario. I hate being negative, especially for a game I was actually hyped for, but it seems like it's intentionally bad. Why is there no way to invite players through the game itself? Why is there so few ammo and health pickups with such a limited ammo pool? Why are all the enemies reskins of one another? Why do most deaths feel like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥? Why are there respawning enemies? Why is the machine gun the worst, but still the only usable weapon? This is poor combat and game design shouldn't be a thing anymore, if you've played any FPS game in the past 30 years, you'd have almost none of these issues. But no, it's like it wants to be Serious Sam with the amount of enemies it throws at you, but doesn't have any of the depth that Serious Sam has. If you choose to have such a strict ammo pool, at least give me a way to earn ammo, through aggressive play or doing certain challenges. Or please, for the love of god, let me have some option to get health back. There's so few health drops, and if played with a friend (which still wasn't enough to save this game from becoming boring, which says something), there's literally not enough pickups for the both of you. They don't regenerate over time either, it's such a bizarre choice. I don't get how all of this got past playtesting, it feels wrong. The maps as well, they're very poorly paced and too maze-y. All of them consist of just holding down the left mouse button and hoping to wipe out enough enemies and not fall into a lava pit and get instakilled. The only good thing I can say about it, is that it looks nice. But that is literally it. I wish I could refund this game, since it's really overpriced in my region on Steam, I had to resort to Humble Bundle to get it for the same price as the other regions. Wish I paid that extra in order to be able to refund it. Stay away from this game till it gets rebalanced completely and fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect Retro-Shooter on Unreal 4:Perfect Optimization, Full Rebind of all Keys, plus a more modern Look than most Retro Boomers.The Map is awesome, you have to find your way through a Labyrinth and have to plan your way accordingly. Every Run is different and you will revisit some locations, coming from a totally different angle into the TileSet, just to find all the weapons and magic items. _childDocuments_.review: Scathe is an odd beast. On the surface it looks like Doom Eternal, but in truth that seems to just be the flayed skin draped over its shoulders. It is far closer to classic arcade shooters from the late 80s or early 90s but just in first person. As such it does stand out quite well once you get into the game and fall into its rhythm. To get there though you need to fathom out the obtuse systems as well as have to cope with a number of really weird design choices. Also bugs, the game has lots of weird bugs making for something that people should wait half a year or so before they drop money on it.It must be stated over and over: Scathe is not like Doom, any Doom, at all. Sure it has a very similar “Hell and Brimstone” with the over-the-top heavy metal aesthetics that the modern Doom tiles have, and it is an FPS, but beyond that they play so completely different that it would be like comparing Street Fighter to Streets of Rage because both are 2D fighting games. Where Doom Eternal is far more focused on very precise “Action Chess” style combat where threats are assessed and combated in a very specific way with limited resources, Scathe is a far more liberal affair when it comes to the combat; being given a basic machine gun with infinite ammo (which I may add is good enough for the whole game) setting you up against utterly braindead hordes of foes who all make a beeline for you, firing and doing very little in their power to stay alive. What is interesting about Scathe is how it both almost fills the screen with an almost endless hail of bullets from the enemies, yet the bullets themselves are very slow moving. It was somewhat marketed as a “bullet hell” game, and in ways it reminds more of an early 90s arcade title like Contra or Smash TV than any other FPS game out there. You dodge the mass of enemy incoming fire while you just hold down the fire button and send an almost endless volley of fire in response.In a way the comparison to Doom has really hurt the game. People, making the presumption that this should play like Doom keep commenting on how “bad” the game feels or how annoying the smaller enemies, like the bouncing balls or the bugs are. For Doom, yeah, they would be awful, but when you look back to the enemy styles of those old arcade games, these enemies fit right in. The sooner one can ditch the comparison to ID’s most successful child, the quicker you can come to enjoy Scathe for what it is.On the area of how it feels to play, a good chunk of the game is quite fun. Once you accept the basic rifle is the workhorse and note that the majority of the basic mobs go down quite fast, the basic gameplay loop works as intended and you find yourself in the rhythm of dodging and weaving the incoming fire, prioritising the largest threats and using the side powers (smart bombs, heals, freezes etc.) to get you out of tight spots. While I did not anticipate enjoying it too much I noticed that I had ended up playing over 10 hours of the game and, well, to get me to play more than 2 hours of a lot of things these days is a miracle!So, Scathe is good then?No, at least not yet.For all its originality and decent combat loop, Scathe feels half baked. There are some design elements that range from slightly irksome to outrightly infuriating. The primary issues come in sense of direction and visual design.The game’s levels are effectively small areas consisting of tight corridors and small arenas to fight in. The spaces themselves are fine, and once you get used to the combat they all can be delt with easily enough. The navigation between levels is where things get messy. For starters the levels themselves are interconnected zones that can be accessed at any time and you can leave via any number of exits in an area. Because of this you can wander between areas willy-nilly and, just by chance, you may end up running past wherever you are supposed to be going due to blind luck. This is made worse by the majority of directions you are given are barked at you by a disembodied voice, either of the Creator or the Deceiver, either berating you or praising you. This is so frequent and, quite often, so cryptic that you end up ignoring what they are saying as it becomes background noise. The end result is a confusing navigation system where the map screen shows where you have been but fills in very little else. Because of this lack of direction and with the poor tutorials given I ended up running about with the just the first weapon for the first two hours of play and by that point I was constantly swearing at my screen demanding “Where the f**k do you want me to go?” This whole situation is made considerably worse as there is no fast travel system and, if you need to go back through the whole game to get an item you missed, you have to trek back through EVERYTHING, and for each zone you need to cross everything will have respawned. I rage quit the game twice due to this.Second up is the fact the visual design results in the game being hard to read. To say it has been overdesigned is a bit of an understatement. Sure, it is technically a very nice game to look at, but the readability of the game is kind of horrible in places due to the lighting and the way everything blends into one. Sometimes enemies blend into the background, items such as exploding barrels can be missed as they can look like any other ornament in the arena (vomiting vision obscuring post processing laced flames too) and it can be hard to decipher what parts of the environment are instant death pits.Oh! There are instant death pits. Everywhere. Sometimes they just look like pools of blood and have ramps leading down into them and you only know they are lethal when you step into them and suddenly keel over. This is made worse by there being some areas that look like they have liquid on the ground and, in some cases, said liquid is not lethal. WHAT IS DANGEROUS AND WHAT IS NOT GAME?A visual delight on one hand, but like a lot of those old 90s games, an utter pain to try and read at times.The nail in the coffin for the game (at launch that is) is how many bugs and rough patches that are in the game. Nothing game killing, but annoying. For instance, the music cuts out at times when you pick up some power ups. Creating a new game can transport you into the first boss battle arena that you can’t escape from. Some actions last much longer than the animation frames indicate making the inputs seem to lag. Jumping has got some forms of input lag which makes air dashing break at times and, at others, makes jumps just not register. Lots and lots of problems that can no doubt be fixed, but right now make the game extremely annoying.I want to love Scathe. It has such a cool premise, and its core gameplay is spot on, but it has so many odd design flaws and rough spots that I cannot advise it for the time. Keep an eye on it and see if it gets any love from patches, but for the time, avoid like the hell it depicts!

_childDocuments_.review: And to be fair to myself, the thing Scathe does better than most is make a good first impression and pitch.  The amalgamation of desirable features seem almost too good to be true: drop in/drop out co-op, rogue-like progression with light itemization, and higher-than-average visuals for an indie title.  As a casual bullet-hell fan that nod of inspiration made this harder to ignore.  Oh, and of course the comparisons to Doom helped considerably.That last part is key, because it set the stage for my personal disappointment.  (The excellent first impression begins to fade immediately when you're given your first weapon in the game in the opening minutes - a fully automatic "AR-like" gun with unlimited ammo and an alt fire rocket grenade launcher.  That could feel powerful if tuned correctly - even broken.  But it isn't. The gun is a weak damage hose with a long cool-down burst attack that still feels incredibly weak.  In my opinion it takes more direct fire to kill base mobs than it should, and it felt really bad to me.Fine - it's the first gun you get, it shouldn't feel strong, right?  You'll get something to replace/upgrade it quickly!   You'll notice that my playtime for this is right around an hour, and I figured in that amount of time I'd see something else to shoot with that would feel better and give a nice little power bump.    It was nothing but the weak hose the whole time, even through the first boss fight.  (We'll talk about that boss in a second.)  That's not Doom - not at all.  It's not even most FPS games out there.  Doom gives you a shotgun on the first level - a crude but hugely effective tool that becomes a mainstay in your arsenal for the rest of the game.  Some sort of carrot to keep you going; a meager powerspike and another option just as you're starting to get the hang of things to widen your scope just a bit.Scathe does nothing different in that first hour.  You have a dash that takes too long to recharge to really be useful, and you traverse flat, horizontal corridors without much variety.  That means you strafe with your AR hose and dash occasionally on repeat.  After an hour with that gun, I never, ever want to shoot a gun like it in any game again, ever.The bullet-hell angle is overblown and again, superficial.  I enjoy games like Ikaruga, Robotron, Crimson Clover, etc. on a somewhat casual level, and can at least appreciate what those sorts of titles try to do on a surface level.  Never once dide I make the connection this game is trying to make to an experience anything like those.  You just see a bunch of slow attacks on the screen and you move out of the way, and it honestly doesn't work or feel as good as you want it to.  It feels like the bad guys are attacking you under water, and it might look somewhat like a shmup but the mechanics aren't the same.  Example: enemies spawn haphazardly, so pattern memorization and stuff that's intrinsic to bullet-hell/shmup's is wholly absent.This makes the gameplay feel like a slow, limited box.  You stop wondering about your options or what's in store for you and focus on the fact that your movement is flat, your single gun does 2 things poorly, and your creativity in how you engage with the next room is ultimately limited.  The method for playing well isn't dynamic; avoid bullets behind cover or with strafing, return fire against mobs that respawn endlessly and take too long to kill, and take solace in the fact that these tactics aren't really affected by much that makes the more or less effective.   It makes the gameplay feel sludgy, slow, and uninteresting.  The only way I can describe it is it made me feel "trapped" and powerless.I'll give the dev the benefit of the doubt - maybe I just don't get it.  Maybe I gave up just as it was getting good.  That's possible.  But they didn't give me much early on to make me want to keep trying.  In my opinion, if they fix anything else with this game, figuring that out might be the most important thing.The first boss I encountered sealed Scathe's fate for me (I admittedly HATE bosses in FPS games, so my expectations were low to begin with).  It was some weird octopus/spider looking thing that was only vulnerable on it's small head.  It had a single web attack that it shot at you that was pretty easily dodged.  It followed me around and did nothing else but shoot that at me during the entire encounter.  Early in the fight, it spawns a second  clone of itself.This fight was absolutely  to play through.  To say it was anything less than boring would be both kindly modest and far too subtle - I'm sorry, it sucked.  You spend the whole fight kiting these things and shooting your weak AR-clone at it's head for next to no damage.... and that's it.  There's nothing else to it, that's all you do.  The boss doesn't change attacks, nothing.  After about 5-10 minutes of this, it's over, and if you're like me, you just feel mad that there was nothing else to it than that - and that there was probably no other way to make it more interesting.  Nothing to climb on, no traps to increase damage, no consumables to lob at it, no weakpoints or other ways to exploit the encounter to your advantage.  Just painstakingly apply your pea-hose.I refunded the game after this.   I'm sorry, I don't usually just give up that easily, but I was actually angry after playing that fight.  It was a consistent culmination of my first hour with the game.  I approached Scathe cautiously excited, and this completely blunted that.I think Scathe has a lot of great ideas bastioned by extremely limited - I'll just say it, poor -  core gameplay.  There's huge demand for good co-op shooters.  I admittedly didn't try that aspect, so maybe I jumped ship too early and that may have informed my take on this game differently. However, I'll just have to leave room for that without feeling the need to explore it.I do feel like SP is simply a mess.  Weaponization, movement, shooting, enemies and level design - none of these worked for me.  They didn't seem to offer much to power to me,  the player, and they don't seem to offer a skill path that really made me want to keep playing.  I felt like I was playing about as well after an hour as I did when I started, and I didn't feel like there was much to learn or that anything was going to change.I'll keep an eye on this project going forward, because if they  overhaul some stuff it could be something cool and fun.  But as it is now, in my opinion there are games that are 30 years old with more compelling gameplay than Scathe.  I'm not asking for something that's already been done - quite the contrary - and I think Scathe should totally try to be it's own thing.  But because of the way the bones for this project have been laid, it seems like it's not really sure what it is or what it wants to do, and that's a dealbreaker for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Scathe might look like a nice game from all the videos and screenshots, but in reality, it is one of the/if not the worst game in its own genre I have ever played, so avoid it at all costs.1) LEVEL DESIGN: The levels themselves are as generic as you can imagine and there is nothing that really stands out in a positive way. However, that's not all. The whole game is divided into "zones", with each one representing one level. Now these zones have an entrance and an exit and they are interconnected into one big labyrinth, where you have to find a set amount of runes, which will then allow you to access one of the game's 6 bosses. So basically, the game progression is non linear. There's two HUGE problems though. The first one being, that there is no fast travel, which means that you won't avoid going through some of the levels more than once, meaning you will have to remember their structure in order to be able to find the exits to the next zones. You can imagine how hard that may be given how generic they are. The bigger problem is that whenever you exit a zone, everything inside it immediately respawns. So you might be like: "Oh, but surely there is at least some kind of an upgrade system, that will incentivize killing all the enemies again?". Nope, nothin'. It's just there to make your playthrough last longer. And what makes it even worse, in some of the zones, there are enclosed arenas, which force you to kill all the enemies inside it, before they let you progress through. So you can't really speedrun through the zones you've already explored once, nope, you have to stay in the arena for good five minutes killing everything that spawns, before the game decides that you can go onwards. Terrible decision if you ask me, and the level design is just atrocious. Oh, and don't even get me started on optimization, some of the zones with too much lava are like a slideshow.2) WEAPONS: So I've only found two of the total six weapons in the game, the first one being the basic starting weapon, the second being a shotgun, which upon trying it out, put the final nail in the coffin of this game for me. This is by far the worst shotgun I have ever got my hands onto in any retro FPS shooter. When you shoot it, the gun barely moves or produces any sound, no feeling of shooting a big powerful weapon, nope. But when the bullet you shoot connects with the enemy, instead of slowly shredding it to pieces for long time as is the case with your starting weapon, the enemy just dies. In one shot. Disregarding the distance you are shooting from. They just die. This is completely atrocious weapon balance, which the developers try to make up for, by limiting your ammo for the weapon as much as possible. Now let's talk about how you actually get to the new weapons. Upon finding your starter weapon at the beginning of the game, Scathe immediately throws you into its labyrinth of zones. You keep finding ammo for various weapons and so after like ten zones, where you keep seeing how ineffective your starting weapon is, you start to question yourself, when will you finally get a new weapon? Well dear player, you will have to be lucky, because the weapon is located in one of the zones, without having no indication of which one it is. So what happened to me, was that I went through the whole first biome, including the first two bosses, where fight with one of them took me around 15 minutes, because I was only left with my starting weapon. And then, the very last zone in the biome I did not explore, to which I had to sluggishly backtrack through many arenas, contained the shotgun. And I've already talked about how bad that one feels. So yeah, if you by some luck miss one of the zones containing the new weapon, be prepared for hell.3) ENEMIES: Same as the levels themselves, the enemies are pretty generic too. Sure, some of them may look interesting at first glance, and there was one enemy type that I genuinely appreicated for its idea, the lava jumpers, but there's also a couple of them, that are genuinely frustrating, mainly the physics denying small jumping balls. The biggest problem however, is their low variety. Once you jump into the game, you take a look at the bestiary and you see a lot of entries, at least thirty of them, so you're gonna be like "wow, that's a lot of enemies!". Well... nope. At least half of them are just plain reskins, with the lava jumpers being the best example. Depending on the biome, you have lava jumper, blood jumper or swamp jumper. Now each one of them does completely the same thing, the only difference being their color. Then you have the bosses. I was able to fight two out of six total, and the game divides these into mini-bosses and actual bosses. The mini-bosses are just a regular enemies with a health bar and they rely mostly on their adds in the arena. Why I am saying regular enemies with health bar? Because you can meet each of these three mini-bosses in the normal zones, only with a slight color change and lower health pool. The actual boss was the worm they were showing off in all the game trailers. Now this boss was... fine. Honestly it was the best part of the game for me, but even then it wasn't something that would go above the average. The boss only had two types of attacks and because I was forced to fight it with the basic weapon only, I got pretty fed up with it by the end of the tedious 15 minutes long fight. And as you may have guessed, these bosses take up the entries in the bestiary, so out of 30 entries, you only now have 24. Counting the mini-boss reskins you only have 21, and some other reskins take this up to half. So like 10 original enemies in a game with 40+ levels? Very bad.4) HONORABLE MENTION: Before I get to the conclusion, there is one honorable mention, that I forgot to include in the three of my previous topics. And that is the game's environmental hazards, speaking mainly about the dangerous liquids. Anytime even your pinky touches one of these hazards, be it a lava, acid or for some reason... blood, you instantly die. No pardons, just instakill. And this not only happens with huge pools of those liquids, but also with cracks in the ground. Brilliant right? So you almost feel like a small kid again, trying to avoid cracks in the walkway for fun. Well here, if you don't do that, you die.5) CONCLUSION: If you value your money, avoid this game at all costs. It has bad weapons, bad level design, bad enemy variety, everything is just atrocious. If I had to think, this is the worst game of the year for me right now, when it comes to my expectations compared to what I actually got. There's plenty of other indie retro FPSes craving for your attention, which might not have the same advanced graphics as Scathe has, but they have much more interesting gameplay loops and won't even cost you the same amount of money.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't get it...Is it a roguelike? Is it supposed to be a retro shooter? Is it trying immitate Doom? Is it supposed to be a movement shooter? Is it demonic serious sam?I just don't get it.This game looks cool, but that's all it's got going for it. Visually it's busy with particles, gibs and effects in your face from the get go. It seems the developers may have understood this and added a "wipe face" mechanic, but you can turn that off, so that begs the question "why was this implemented?". The levels look beautiful, but everywhere looks the same, it's almost like they were procedurally generated, which begs the question "is this a roguelike?" They are RIDDLED with ammo pickups for weapons you don't have and in my 40 minutes of gameplay I did not find a single new weapon.Speaking of which, combat is entirely uninspired. The game starts you off with a machine gun with a (very slow to reload) grenade/missile launcher alt attack. The primary fire is so weak you'll spend countless seconds just holding mouse1 at hoards of rank and file enemies. There's absolutely endless hordes of enemies which just run straight at you; some of them hurt on collision, some explode and have a massive AOE with misleading visual explosion size, some hurt on collision and explosion, some only hurt on collision with what feels like no i-frames - it's all so unclear. There's no cohesion to the combat. One level plays entirely like the next and the one after, it's all just corridors and mazes. It took a few encounters to realize that there's no arena lock-in - you're free to go about and ignore ALL combat with little to no penalty. Enemies do not adjust to your trajectory and only fire at where you are currently, making it possible to just run straight to the exit without engaging in combat and taking no damage.The game wants itself to be a bullethell, but gives you the finesse of a supercar as any small input sends you flying in that direction, making you collide with the projectiles you're trying to avoid. Don't even try platforming - it's like there's negative air friction and trying to adjust your trajectory sends you flying.There's barely any explanation to mechanics. I found a ring, but had to go to the options to realize I can use it to heal myself. Mana seems to drop from enemies, but that was unexplained. I haven't found any weapons in 5-6 levels, but sure found a lot of runes, the purpose of which is clear as mud. Apart from the ring in the first level there's no loot! Nothing to justify the exploration and gameplay, just the endless drone of the machine gun and repeating enemy sound effects, some of which are REALLY annoying! Maybe I didn't play long enough, but I draw the line at 40 minutes with no change in gameplay loop.There's an ingame god-like narrator which comments on your escapades, but seems entirely out of place. I don't blame the voice actor but he seems to try too hard and just comes off theatrical. Sometimes I kill a single low-tier enemy and he exclaims how great and ruthless I am, other times I just killed a horde and he's silent. Returning to the weird maze-like level design, it seems like there's no secrets! Just haphazardly thrown around items. At one point the narrator said something along the lines of "There's something hidden in those pools" when I was in a room with flowing sludge; so I jumped in and immediately died to out of bounds - what's with that? For a second I thought there's was something clever about this game, but I was wrong.I had to check if the game was in early access, because it feels so undercooked, apart from the visuals.It's so weird, there's no cohesion, no melding of the systems, just mindless shooting with unsatisfying combat. Looks pretty, but that's it.

_childDocuments_.review: Since I got the game 100% (except a few achievements) with a total play time of 21.3 hours I will write a review about what I love and what bothers me. Scathe is a game that instantly caught me when I first saw it (i think at E3) in 2019. Since then I was hyped for the game. A game that reminded me of some kind of modern Quake 1 made by an Indie studio.When I first started the game I had no expectations for it to be like a Quake or different game. And I was not disappointed. In fact, I loved the game from the first minute of playing!But the longer I played the more things started to bother me while playing.Pros:- I love the dark setting that kind of reminds me of Quake 1's setting.- Simple and short level design but many different levels / zones.- Gameplay feels like a classic shooter modernized- The graphics are beautiful and the artstyle totally fits the game! Everything looks very crisp and clean, no muddy textures. Also I'm happy to see that the game uses modern features like Raytracing, DLSS, DLAA, etc.- There are many different enemies with very unique designs which ususally fit the environment of the current zone.- The rings / spells are a very nice addition to the gameplay since they mostly set buffs / debuffsCons:- Other than the spells, the weapons beside the beginning weapon feel useless. At first, I tried using them. But most of the time it doesnt make a difference what you use and there is no real improvement to the starting weapon. Except that the other weapons run out of ammo as soon as you use them for more than 30 seconds. I would take a look at DOOM Eternal at this point because the developers saw the same problem in their prequel. In Eternal, every weapon has its reason because some weapons are way more effective or even required for certain enemies than others. - The Enemy Spawning sometimes feels on spot, sometimes completely random. This includes some spots where the little yellow spiders spawned on the same spot for like a minute. I just stood there, looking at the same spot farming those spiders. Also sometimes enemies spawn behind you from locations I've just cleared all enemies before.- There is no map for the individual zones and no indicator where to find the gates to the other zones. Additionally to that there is no option to fast travel between zones which basically means that I ended up running trying to dodge enemies and trying to find the gates for hours just to certain zones. And additionally to that if you run out of extra lives you respawn at the last boss level. which was the reason why it took me over an hour just to a zone on the other side of the map. In general I have to say I had lots of fun playing the game. I just feel it needs a "quality of life" update to enhance the user experience. The game still does have quite some bugs but at the time I am writing this, the current game version is the day one version. _childDocuments_.review: Scathe is REALLY fun in the beginning but the longer you play, the more flaws really start to show. Many of the other reviews sum it up pretty well but here are my issues: Keep in mind I've spent the few hours I've played it only in hard mode. (from speaking with friends, a lot of what I complain about here isn't much of an issue on Normal mode. It's just hard mode that makes the artificial difficulty with a terrible lives/checkpoint system. Rather than making the enemies tougher and smarter, the game is just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ to make it harder...Im willing to change my review as time goes on and updates occur) It's fun in the beginning but the longer you play the more you die and have to restart ENTIRE level sections over and over and over and over gets really old really quickly.The ONLY THING that would make this SO MUCH BETTER is if you could gain back a tiny bit of health when you dash into enemies and have a way to somehow gain lives back. It's really weird that these mechanics aren't already baked into the game Scathe is trying to be. Because there is NO push-forward health and lives incentive your best chance of survival is sitting back, peaking corners, and shooting from a distance, and it's really slow and boring that way. It's MUCH more fun slamming your way through causing as much damage as quickly as possible but the game actively discourages you from doing that and it sucks.I really want to try this co-op, but as it stands my first impressions are kind of mixed. I am genuinely enjoying the game but it's just lacking a few common sense features that would make this a truly great game.I haven't played on lower difficulties yet but If they feel more balanced then adding a way to earn lives through your points and refilling health upon dashing would be a decent feature at least for hard mode. The way it is now, it's too easy to cheese the normal sections, then it pushes you into overwhelming combat encounters where damage is unavoidable and there's no real way to recover. These two changes I feel would make casual players like myself enjoy it more, but also make speedrunning super fun. I just feel that having small health drops when you dash an enemy would be a fantastic way to push combat forward and reward the player for using a mechanic that already exists. If you don't engage in combat and sit back to shoot from cover, you never need to dash. May as well make it worthwhile. Even if it is just 2% or 5% health regained per enemy killed, that would make the whole experience 10x better.OR if they don't want to add that mechanic and they're happy with players taking their time, then why not make health regen back to 10% when there's no damage taken for a short period of time? Once the room is clear and you can stop for a bit before moving to the next arena, your health is at least 10% instead of 1%. The number of times I lost lives because I was down to 1hp and a random flying enemy spawned behind me and instakilled me was infuriating because there's also no way of earning that life back.ORRRRR Make health pickups respawn over time at least once or twice over. There just needs to be SOMETHING to get the player back in the fight so it doesn't feel like a slog. BUT I'm still giving it a thumbs up because it's early days and changes can occur. I have faith the devs will listen to the feedback and try to make changes for the better and make this a truly great game. So buy this game if you like fast paced action retro inspired shooters.

_childDocuments_.review: You do not need to have played Doom to understand what a "Doom like" game might be like. This is one of them. Scathe puts a little bit of a twist however, but certainly with a few missed opportunities.Steam Curator Page:Affiliate link:+ Fun Gameplay+ Secondary weapons+ Mostly creative levels+ Drop in multiplayer- Generic at best music- Unintuitive boss fights- No fast travel- No power ups when entering levels- No explanation on weapon unlocks- Enemy variety lacklustre- PlatformingScathe is a bullet hell shooter focused on fast paced movement, accurate firing, dodging enemy fire and platforming.The music is nothing compared to the competition. There are plenty of other games like this out there that do music significantly better. The movements are not precise enough for some of the platforming that this game requires to collect all of the runes and other pickups such as extra lives and power ups during the levels. It does serve it well, however, when you are fighting multiple enemies at once, dodging and swerving around trying to survive.My biggest takeaway in missed opportunities is that this game does not offer some kind of power up when you progress through the next level. This is built similarly to Hades, where once you beat the level you can choose an exit, in a lot of cases more than one. The game is set up as a maze of sorts where you navigate with the goal of finding your way out. It would have been great to see the ability to pick up power ups such as Hades and other games similar to it, but sadly this is not the case here.I would have also liked to see some type of fast travel between levels since there is a lot of backtracking you have to do. Furthermore, the game never really explains what the method is of unlocking new weapons. I have unlocked a weapon by doing nothing, yet when I do things like clearing out one section of the maze or beating a big boss that gives a special drop, I do not unlock anything. I would like to get some more clarity on this.Despite its shortcomings, Scathe was still pretty fun to play for the hours needed to write this overview. It has made me rethink my stance on bullet hell games. I will be adding more to this or making another video entirely if the game releases and brings major changes.

_childDocuments_.review: (2-hours review, this is my second acc for eng reviews)I must say right away that for personal "taste" reasons I do not like the new parts of Doom, and I thought at least "Scathe" would satisfy my genre "gap". But alas, it turned out to be an incredibly bad game, it's not average, or mediocre, it's just bad - it's not even an "old school" shooter, not an "arena shooter", it's a corridor shooter, who the f*** came up with these cooperative races along the corridors? What a brilliant game designer? There is nowhere to turn around, there is nothing to hide behind.. As a result, all pro players will simply stand 3 meters from the next room, aiming at opponents in advance, without entering into a direct dynamic battle, if you consider Serius Sam, for example, as a bad game, then here you you won’t be able to play at all, at least in ss are open large locations, but here you are locked in a rectangular box and there is practically no space for maneuver, I just don’t understand what the gameplay of the game is then? They would have made a rail shooting range then.. You might think that it looks like Quake - well, yes, but there was platforming, there were "multi-storey" levels, but here it`s practically absent, the locations are very narrow and mostly horizontal. And yes, once out of ten I met a really ordinary arena where you could run in circles, and up and down, but that's it, it was 1 room out of 10! This can be considered a statistical error and not taken into account.What else? Yes, the graphics here are good, since this is Unreal, but the locations look empty and poor, no work was done with the environment here, the monster designs are unremarkable, the difficulty is unbearable hardcore, you can’t play alone, It’s generally very unusually done here, you have 3 save slots, and this is something like sorties, you start the game and you have 3 ways to start your journey in a huge labyrinth, like an open world consisting of rooms (which are called different symbols that you don’t remember exactly), you need to find runes to open new rooms, you can return to the previous ones, since in many rooms it’s not even necessary to kill everyone, and if you join someone’s game, then your progress will be overwritten with the general progress from a stranger’s save, but again, you have 3 slots for "sorties", but you can't fail them, if your team spends all their lives, then the last room you reached just restarts.The shooting impact is weak, the sound is even worse, basically you will walk with 1 standard machine gun, because the rest of the weapons like the shotgun and crossbow, at least in the current version of the game, I would call premium, since the ammo for them is unbearably small.Any pluses? Well, a digestible "bloody", albeit in quality as if from Unity, and good designs of a machine gun and a shotgun, and sometimes there will be arenas. If you want to grind local monsters worse than in some Assassin`s game, then please, apparently, I will never get a worthy successor to Doom 1993.

_childDocuments_.review: Scathe is a hectic FPS Boomer Shooter with Bullet Hell elements where you are sent to hell by the Divine Creator to put down his brother’s Sacrilegious ever growing ambition at being the one who rules them all and destroy him.After being sent to hell to stop to quell any potential taking over of the Divine Creator’s kingdom, the path awaits you leading to the final goal is a maze-like labyrinth where you have to figure out and forge which path to take. Some paths will have a benefit to you in your journey, whereas others will only lead to hordes of demons that only seek your death.To assist your journey and ensure the road is paved with the demon's blood, you have an arsenal of weapons that don’t come readily available and require you to scour through levels to find it. Upon finding it, it will be available for you from then on. Mere weapons won’t be enough in your journey, seek out Rings/Relics of Dark Magic from Mages of the past in order to obtain its power. Those Relic’s powers include the ability to freeze, heal, eliminate enemies with a single clench of your fist, demon mode where you are invincible and will deal extra damage and have higher speed, all of which costs demon souls in order to be used.Gameplay-wise it goes without saying that this is a boomer shooter with bullet hell thrown on top to it. Your movements are quick and are only hampered by how fast your reflexes are. The bullet-hell nature of the game is reminiscent of another old-school genre and favorite that pushes up the difficulty scale.Graphically and aesthetically Scathe looks inspired by Doom, in this case it does it well. Everything looks as crisp and something you wouldn’t expect from a 3-man team to master. Being as shiny as it is, the slight downside it may be would be the “chunkiness” and weight of things in the game. For instance when shooting an enemy you expect some hefty meaty noises but it feels and sounds lighter than what you may expect.Another minor thing to note is in the earlier sections of the game, enemies seem more predictable and tend to behave in a weird way. They would use the same pathfinding as each other and walk down the same line, they would run past you as though they are closing down on someone invisible behind you. Weirdly enough the enemy pathfinding and AI seem to fix itself as the game progresses. Initial challenges one to expect is the lack of explanation to navigate to the next levels when looking at the map, it doesn’t tell much and took a while to figure out. The constant dying initially is amplified as one comes to terms to the labyrinth of each level. The variety of demons you encounter though some feel repeated and in a different skin is still quite noteworthy (except those ball-like ones, nobody likes them) and unique. Levels are crafted in a way that makes it truly maze-like to a certain degree. With important pickups being hidden or placed in a way that is harder to reach.For what it bills itself to be, Scathe does it bloody well. It’s intense, gory, challenging and satisfying when being cornered by endless demons and finding your way through them by running and gunning, while you’re using your dark magic until the last drop of blood lands on the floor and everyone’s in pieces as the music similar to Heilung draws to the last groans.
