_childDocuments_.review: I think this game might have potential but it feels like playing an open source arena shooter where the combat loop was designed by a teenager. The biggest problem is the combat is largely devoid of anything resembling depth or any kind of decision making and resource management in real time coupled with an AI that does not pressure you makes the game feel like a joke. the difficulty is laughable and unfun, I would rather play DOOM Eternal on baby mode (ultra-violence) than this. I think I will just go back to Konvaz's Slaughter maps for DOOM Eternal cause this just lacks anything that feels like active engagement and the starting level doesn't feel like it's teaching you abstract skills, it's teaching you hold M1 and move the mouse keys, even less braindead than dark souls' pitiful easy gameplay.if the dev(s) want to make the game good you need real AI diversity, the AI has to have a job and way it interacts with you that is unique, you need to apply pressure to the player to force them to pay attention and make smart decisions and handle pressure with offence well. these are the hallmarks of even highly simplistic games like Dark Souls combat and that was too much... I suspect this game is DOA even after the update.
_childDocuments_.name: Scathe

_childDocuments_.review: Scathe's a fast paced, high intensity first-person shooter... At a glance. Beyond the impressive visuals and hordes of demon's reminiscent of fan favourites, you'll find a more methodical shooter. Where you might be tempted to charge in head-first, you could find taking a moment to assess the situation, reading where the hundreds of bullet's are coming from and approaching the situation accordingly is far more effective.Throw magic into the mix ('Crush', a spell that makes all demons on screen go boom, is a personal favourite) and online co-op, you'll find an experience worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Scathe

_childDocuments_.review: I bought the game for a co-op play with a friend, and got what I wanted (so the review does not reflect any impression of the single player), with modern graphics, just what I like. It turned out to be a simple but working shooter in the old school  style - with a bunch of enemies that shoot huge slow glowing bullets or rush at the hero. The hero, on the contrary, is fast and shoots without reloading weapons, default machine gun is generally infinite. There are even "ten lives" that are given per team, and losing them all erases some of the progress (so this seems like a risky decision in public multiplayer, where a weak player can quickly spend lives or, worse, do it intentionally to mischief).In addition to shooting, there are 6 runes hidden in the levels, the collection of which is also of some interest in order to explore the map in search of secret places. Alas, we collected 99% and spent more than an hour on one map just poking around in all corners. In vain. I have no idea where this rune is hidden, but it made me feel uncomfortable just at the end! Annoys. Even if the collection of secrets practically does not affect anything.I would also criticize the lack of in-game explanation of "how to play". There is a maze with hints of what is hidden in which rooms, and this is important. Like, at start go straight first, not left or right! For us, there was healing magic there, which made the game much easier. And I really miss the ability to teleport to already cleared levels. Walking through completely cleared maps isn't that hard, but it could be skipped.Don't even count on the plot. There is an "ending" here, but it is unlikely to be some kind of moral reward or final challenge. The gameplay is the main thing here, and it suited me.Oh, and the sound of most weapons being fired is very... "gentle". Perhaps this is done so that it does not become deafening from constant fire. But for game where everything explodes with blood and flashes, I would like to feel more powerful even with sfx.
_childDocuments_.name: Scathe

_childDocuments_.review: Well what can I say about Scathe?Let us get the obvious out of the wayIs Scathe an amazing game and does it reimagine the shooter genre? No and yes, Is Scathe Doom?in most cases you will see people trying to compare Scathe to Doom and too some degree I get it and then there are times where I am just WTF are they on about?Now down to the lenghty bit!First off in Doom I have never ever started going backwards while shooting, I have never really had to plan how I move forward or what to take out first, this game makes you think about how you progress how you deal with enemies, since this game is a FPS Bullethell so clearly NOT a Doom clone like so many people are on about.And like I said Scathe is not an amazing game, it is however a great game, and tbh I would never compare it to Doom, I would say Scathe is more of a retro shooter with modern graphics and then, well yeah let us call it metroidish elements thrown into the mix. As you walk back and forth in a maze and various rooms have runes or new weapons or even magic spells.There is nothing ground breaking about Scathe it just plays like a retro shooter with some cool elements thrown into the mix.The only thing I do have to say, some of the weapons just kinda lack that impact I mean the sound stage needs some reworking to give the weapons a bit more omph, but other than that I am having a blast with this game and if you ask me, people are missing out if they read some of the negative reviews.I have to give it to the devs this is a great game and I do hope we will see patches and improvements along the way, especially with the weapons they do need more impact :)But other than that, good job guys :)---- Update -----A little update to my reivew, man this game has been getting updates and just gotten better and better, the recent update 2.0 Enforcer Edition just keeps adding good stuff to the game and making it better, I am so pleased with this game and that I got it on release.And I do NOT get the mixed reviews, but I am guessing some people just left a review played the game to never return, sadly that is a common thing on steam and why I think the review system is flawed.But still keep up the good work great game you have here :)
_childDocuments_.name: Scathe

_childDocuments_.review: It just doesn't quite scratch that itch, don't get me wrong the game is OK, but I really wouldn't go out of my way to play it. I like the look of it and personally enjoy the tribal soundtrack, and I especially like that I can play it with friends, but there are just so many small things that annoy me that kinda kill my enjoyment.It feels like way too many flying enemies spawn which often winds up causing me to get whacked by some ground enemies and spend half the game staring at the ceiling. I don't mind one or two flying units being around to catch me off guard but when they are constantly spawning whilst also zipping around in the air it just starts feeling like a chore to deal with.Certain enemies are just SUPER annoying, basically you better find these bouncing ball enemies really quick or prepare to have someone screaming in your ears for a while til you do, and I get it, they do that so you can ID them but ffs tone it back a few notches, I have the high ground these things are no threat to my character just to my ears. I didn't play long enough to find all the weapons but the one I did find excited me.... and then disappointed me, so the shotgun was neat in that it had a cool alt fire (even though it literally doesn't activate on turret enemies) and it does good damage with it's primary fire, but it is so LAME to actually FIRE the gun it's model barely responds to you pulling the trigger and that just kinda makes it feel real wimpy, when I pull the trigger of a shotgun expect to think "man this things got some kick" not "oh is that all?"  Not to mention you aren't going to get to use the guns you do acquire very much bc ammo pickups are so scarce, to be specific they don't drop, they are just placed around the map sometimes and you have to find them, so don't get too attached to that new toy.A personally issue I had was that the game is all Gore no Glory, enemies just kind of all generically burst into blood mists/globs. I know I'm probably just too spoiled by Doom butt the lack of any finishers or unique kills takes the game down a notch. Lastly, and I am sure you'll see this a lot the core game play loop/exploration just feels bad, the system is as such so that you are generally better off just running past most foes, you'll have to do quite a bit of back tracking to get most collectibles though which isn't optional to some degree as you have to have enough relics to get through certain doors. A lot of time gets spent looking around for one little skull in the wall that you have to shoot in order to open up the doors to relics.
_childDocuments_.name: Scathe

_childDocuments_.review: It grows on you, until you figure out the mechanics and adjust to the game-play. I did initially feel that the game was a little frustrating until I came to understand how to work best and enjoy its quirks. I think it's unfair to compare it to other shooters because Scathe offers a peculiar challenge. If you want something different, give it some time and be patient. Scathe hooked me into an addictive experience of onslaught and mayhem. I do realize, it's a freaking awesome game.
_childDocuments_.name: Scathe

_childDocuments_.review: Remember how those 90's FPS games were so gory and gruesome and had that "one more level" feeling?  Scathe delivers on those points, and more!This game is at a very fast pace, so be prepared taking your time or playing cautiously may punish you, especially with the amount of enemies and projectiles coming right at ya!  You will be swamped with various of enemies, but that is the point.Scathe does not use the traditional methods level progression, it encourages you to use the map the find and use particular exit gates to move on to the next level, which I find quite refreshing and makes you think about where to go next.  Whether you are planning to find all the runes on each level or magic / weapons, you will want to come back to find them all.The guns are glorious, taking from inspiration of the old school Doom, Quake and Hex games.  Them nostalgic feelings are gonna hit you hard.  And the sound art and engineering really do set the scene that you are in the depths of hell trying to get out.The neat feature of playing this game solo, or co-op is great also.  The private co-op or drop in co-op choice is also a really nice feature to have been added to this game.I applaud the Kwalee team for delivering such a great game, and yes while there are some bugs that can ruin the ambience of the game, these are being addressed in the next few patches.Overall, very highly recommend.  Well done all! 👏👏
_childDocuments_.name: Scathe

_childDocuments_.review: Played a few hours roaming a labyrinth, learning the systems, dying over and over (often with little warning) before restarting with more direction. Second save had a completely different layout and biomes, and I navigated directly to the first dark magic without losing all lives. That's the thing about this game-- it's got heavy roguey elements, while being a sort of dungeon crawl fps bullet hell where movement and position matter, without mandating a run and gun sort of playstyle. There are exploration aspects, minor puzzles, and plenty of gibs to litter the floor. It's weird and different with some of the design, like limited ammo for any but the starting gun and enemies spawning out of nowhere ( reminds me of EYE Divine Cybermancy in some ways(. At this point I'm content to sort of live in the dungeon, explore and collect everything I can while looking for bosses. Drop in/out co op too.
_childDocuments_.name: Scathe

_childDocuments_.review: Initial thoughts-- Preview access --I played at least 2 maps of this and honestly it isn't that bad. Waiting on launch to play more so I don't ruin it even more for myself.You start off the game from the **preview** with an unlimited bullet gun which is weird when your first mindset is to compare it to Doom or even Quake. So it's like oh... I don't have to reload and kept pushing it despite that, and there's random things across the map that I tried to pick up and were like Yooo you don't have this item so it's like... I guess those aren't weapons or those items are character specific?I got to the second map, one slight flaw of it, as fun as it is and knowing hey I only have to kill x amount of demons, they will literally spawn out of no where. Yes, random demons will spawn and say hi there, and you sit back and just shoot. It gave me no real reason to push up and attempt to kill the other demons. After killing them all I just got the relics and left.TLDR; Game go pew pew is fun me like it can't wait to play more of it at some point :3... Had to turn sensitivity down because Mercy aim kicks in LOL.**Tech mumbo jumbo**So you kind of start off with the game all set to high settings, and unlimited FPS. When I looked in task manager I was like wtf game is taking 90% of the GPU so I turned the settings down to low... that didn't really help, it was still eating it. Later I thought to myself what if I limit my fps to 60... game actually ran a lot smoother and was taking 30% of my GPU.
_childDocuments_.name: Scathe

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy it, its fast paced, fun, easy to get into and the music is great. First reaction when seeing a game like this is to play it as if you are playing Doom, but the "bullet hell" style makes you focus on dodging and being more tactical which I think is pretty cool I think its got lots of potential and looking forward to playing more
_childDocuments_.name: Scathe

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a bad game. It feels a lot like Immortal Redneck, but only about half as good.Pros:Game is somewhat addicting if you're a completionist.Looks pretty good once you turn the post processing to low.Framerate is really good.Guns are satisfying to use.There are some good encounters that will put you on your feet.Cons:Sound design is awful. The machine gun sounds like a wet fart and a lot of the monster sounds make no sense. And holy piss the low health sound is the worst I've ever heard. If you can't find a health pickup, it never stops.Ammo capacity and pickups for secondary weapons are too stingy.No unlocks. Can't increase ammo capacity or learn spells or unlock weapons. I think this would have been a better approach to what this game has.Traveling between stages can be tedious.If you try to get all the runes for every level, it can be a pain in the ass. Certain exits and certain runes can be very hard to find, usually involving a single obscure wall switch.Most enemies just spew projectiles your direction with no pattern or strategy. The usual solution is to stutter step in one direction then jump over the projectiles and then repeat, which isn't really the spirit of a "bullet hell".Most encounters last way too long. You don't clear a room. You clear a room 10 times in a row, because the enemies keep replenishing for some reason. That doesn't make it harder, it just makes it more tedious.The names of the levels are symbols. Good luck having people write level guides for your game.OH YEAH BY THE WAY:FLOORS THAT KILL YOU. I HAVE DIED TO MONSTERS 0 TIMES. BOSSES 3 TIMES. THE FLOOR 15 TIMES. I AM NOT KIDDING. THE MOVEMENT IS TOO FLOATY FOR HALF THE FLOORS IN THE GAME TO INSTAGIB YOU. MY TOE BRUSHED A LAVA WATERFALL THAT LOOKED LIKE DECORATION AND MY BODY EXPLODED IN FLAMES.
_childDocuments_.name: Scathe

_childDocuments_.review: Scathe is pretty fun. Decent level variety, weapons with limited ammo could be a bit more impactful but overall a solid title with quite a few levels. Gameplay is fluid and the dark magic is an interesting system.It's fairly easy to ignore most of the negative reviews, it's pretty clear the higher overall difficulty of this game is stamping out noobs at a rapid pace. Which generally leads to rage-reviews blaming mechanics. The game works just fine, people are bad. Highly suggest if the game is curb stomping you to change the difficulty to casual. No shame.My only real complaint is that the game conveys information horribly. You basically have no idea what anything is. Could really do with a better tutorial, even just a brief one. Relying on the in-game wiki is terrible.
_childDocuments_.name: Scathe

_childDocuments_.review: Not too far in as have to head to bed, but really enjoyed what I have played of Scathe thusfar! Will give some of my favourite features from my perspective below:Aesthetic & Atmosphere - The settings feel demonically appropriate, lots of blood and guts, tight hallways to navigate with demons trying to sandwich you. It definitely keeps the adrenaline pumping but you can see the Devs also spent time on the gory details to keep you enthralled (well, as enthralled as one can be when trying to escape a Demon sandwich). On managed to see the Industrial and one other zone before I had to stop but am very eager to get back to it! The Demon designs are unnerving and super cool, particularly the few bigger Demons I encountered which had me constantly on the move to avoid their bullets, as they hurt - badly. Overall, the atmosphere felt tense and fiery - just what I'd expect! And the few demons I saw looked great!Gameplay - Whilst I wouldn't call myself a expert at FPS games, I do love them - particularly ones with horror themes and I don't tend to shy away from harder difficulties. Scathe felt like enough of a challenge for me on the normal setting, things are constantly happening - demon sandwiches, the cursed demon bowling balls that squeal and hit hard, making sure to dash attack just at the right time. It all provides a great state of adrenaline, to the point I actually lost track of time and wanted to keep going when I had to stop for the night. It is definitely the kind of game that is easy to get sucked into, and good for a challenge (the game is great at humbling you when you think you're on a roll but always feels fun, as opposed to being overpowered). Bullet hell definitely feels appropriate.Music - One of my favourite things was the music in the game. The music suits the environments perfectly, fast paced, heavy and it provides the momentum to keep moving forward. Pretty sure Metal fans will be right at home here! The BGM lulls and flares at the right time, the sfx of the demons (the demon balls will haunt me forever ;w;) all feels appropriate - and by appropriate I mean gross and horrifying - in the best way. Soundtrack is stellar, definitely a highlight of the game for me.Overall, I can't wait to get back into the game tomorrow. If you're into horror, bullet hells, hell in general, demons, fps, killer soundtracks or maybe all of these things - I can highly recommend it :DKitsuneDemon
_childDocuments_.name: Scathe

_childDocuments_.review: I've enjoyed what I've played of Scathe a lot, it's got the fast paced "boomer shooter" movement and projectile-firing enemies that I enjoy in games like this. The level design that I've seen is also enjoyable to explore/jump around on in firefights, and I think the general "vibe" of the music and atmosphere is very cool.I'm really looking forward to seeing what new weapons I unlock, and playing in co-op mode with my friends, as that's a feature I've been hoping to see more of in this type of game, so I'm very excited for that!I'm also happy to say that it runs flawlessly on Linux using proton, and also plays very nicely on steam deck too. (I'd recommend using gyro controls for the steam deck due to the fast paced nature of the game).Looking forward to playing some more, and I'll be keeping my eyes peeled for future projects from the devs :)
_childDocuments_.name: Scathe

_childDocuments_.review: I will say that the demo for this game was completely misguiding to the complete product.Pros:- Goodish graphics to the level of DOOM 2016- Good shooting mechanics- Good music, when it's playing.Cons:- The demo made it seem it was a linear Doom like experience, but it turn out to be a multiple door system between levels like a rogue-like, but is not a rogue like.- The starting weapon feels good, but when you have to cross to the 4th room with only the starting weapon it feels very afwul very soon.- The level progression is awful since there are no clear objectives to follow in the UI- Level design is a little poor since you have to look for the correct door to get into- It's extremely frustrating when you see ammo all around for the weapons you don't have at the moment.- Navigation between the rooms in order to collect runes, weapons and demon stones are really confusing and annoying.- The narrator voice becomes really annoying really soon.- I wish there was a introduction level that guide you how to start navigating between rooms.Generally the game is more dissapointing than bad, but is still a mixed for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Scathe

_childDocuments_.review: Played the game for 30 minutes then requested a refund. The starting gun is meh and the gameplay is frustrating (not challenging). There is also a constant voice speaking throughout the action and I personally found it very annoying. Big fan of all doom releases and fast paced FPS, but this really got on my nerve very quickly due to the way the enemies are so overpowered and the gun is so weak. Also that voice in the background was a vibe killer. Should have just plugged in good music and let the fun go on.
_childDocuments_.name: Scathe

_childDocuments_.review: I have been following this game since when it was announced and was waiting to buy it on launch. Scathe is a challenging game, it's not for the fainthearted, get ready to be pummelled, riddled with a billion bullets and die a hell of a lot. The other thing is, it is not a linear game, you are navigating a maze and you WILL get lost and you will have to keep playing through some of the same areas to progress. You learn with each run and you'll get through the area quicker. It is fast, frenetic and really takes you back to that retro era of shooters like Serious Sam, Quake and of course Doom. The twist is there's also dark magic and that adds a whole different element to it compared to your average FPS.Where it really shines through is the Co-op, it makes it challenging, and encourages greater teamwork as you have to be aware of your shared life pool and adjust your play accordingly. Really makes for a fun experience with friends. Worth it just for the Co-op experience!For a 3 man dev team, I think this is absolutely fantastic. You guys have done a great job. Looking forward to seeing what you come out with next.
_childDocuments_.name: Scathe

_childDocuments_.review: Scathe is one difficult adrenaline rush of an experience. I had a blast playing it at launch with a party of friends. We had to better our run every time we ran into a hurdle. We got turns laughing and blaming each other, especially at the end of the run when we get to see our scores.This game reminded me for my retro gaming days with Serious Sam and Quake. Had a ton of entertainment and looking forward to future runs with more of my buddies.Happy to see that at launch there are very few bugs and glitches that have to be ironed out. Looking to see more exciting games from the developer.Have fun and keep running like mad, welcome to hell.

_childDocuments_.review:
Scathe is an intense, classic FPS with big guns and even bigger demons. You are Scathe, Enforcer of the Legions of Hell, forged from the earth by the Divine Creator himself. And you, like your fallen kin before you, must prove your worth by navigating a deviously crafted maze, entangled with demonic evil at every twist and turn. So, grab your Hell Hammer and get ready to unleash your almighty fury!

Use Scathe's brute strength and extreme speed to purge your way through Hell's most grotesque abominations, as you search for the Hellstones and defeat the all-powerful Guardians that protect them.

It's time to blast your way out of bullet Hell.

name: Showgunners
detailed_description: In a dystopian future where corporations rule, a brutal reality show is the hottest entertainment property in town! You play as Scarlett Martillo, a contestant out for revenge. To win, you must navigate dangerous urban arenas packed with lethal traps and face off against hordes of heavily-armed psychopaths. Each stage in Showgunners has been hand-crafted to create a curated, turn-based tactical gameplay experience, heightened with the inclusion of a diabolical show director that can hinder Scarlett or help her opponents depending on your performance. This dynamic level design ensures that no two levels play the same way and keep players thinking tactically. Showgunners has been built to challenge and delight players, whether they’re a turn-based tactical game initiate or a long-time fan of the genre! Scarlett won’t be fighting alone. As the story progresses, players will recruit new partners that can turn the tide of battle in all kinds of exciting ways. Upgrade your characters by spending talent points in their unique skill trees and outfitting them with weapons bought at a shop or earned during battle. Hidden challenges within each chapter can unlock more allies, legendary weapons, and helpful items, so be sure to keep an eye out! Players will need to navigate an obstacle course of deadly traps and lethal puzzles in real-time, but be prepared for an ambush at any corner. Psychopathic enemies like the Ogre and the Ronin aren’t the only deadly elements you’ll need to overcome. Combat scenarios are peppered with unique environmental hazards, from ticking time bombs to runaway trains. There is never a dull moment in Showgunners! Gain fame by avoiding death, surviving rounds, and eliminating your enemies with gruesome panache. The more you succeed, the more fans you earn; your growing fame will yield increasingly beneficial sponsorship deals. Streamers, rejoice! Use the native Twitch integration to keep audiences engaged by letting them control the direction of each level. They can add more enemies, change the terrain, add or remove obstacles, or send useful items, all from chat.

name: The Academy: The First Riddle
detailed_description: Hello, Students, and Welcome to the Academy! As the school’s headmistress, it’s my honor to show you some of the features that await you as soon as you enroll. The Academy has always attracted the most curious of minds, so it comes as no surprise that you’re here now. Feel free to come in and take a look around! Explore every corner of the marvelous Academy. Quite magnificent, isn’t it? Don’t worry, you’ll be able to walk these halls and soak in the school in all its splendor. Although the Academy is famous for its more colorful sights, there are darker corners to be found as well. Solve over 200 puzzles and riddles. Only the best and the brightest attend the Academy, and our puzzles will prove if you’re among them. Easy to play, but challenging to master, they are the ultimate test for our students. Unravel the mystery looming over the school and uncover its secrets. A place with such a rich history is also rich with stories. The ones told about this semester, however, will be far greater than all those before. You will soon find that the school also has its fair share of secrets. But, remember, the light will reveal all that lurks in the shadows. Meet memorable characters and make friends (as well as a few foes here and there). The Academy is undoubtedly a special place. But what makes it unique are its students and staff. Only those capable of extraordinary things spend their time on school grounds, so you will always be in the best of company. Take a breather from all the puzzles by exploring the school’s rich lore. They are right when they say that a puzzle waits around every corner of the Academy. However, you will also find that there are plenty of fun activities for students to engage in when they’re not tackling puzzles! That would be all for our tour! Before we end, let me just leave you with this... The Academy’s doors are open to all players looking for a real challenge with a captivating story at its core. I truly believe that’s you, and I look forward to seeing you very soon in the school’s hallways.

_childDocuments_.review: I initially wrote a tentatively positive review - there were just enough OK puzzles in the early game to balance out the clunkers... but having played a little further I'm switching this to a solid negative.  The OK puzzles have dried up, and now it's all:- Way-too-easy filler puzzles- Groaners with arbitrary/dumb solutions- Puzzles with unclear rules/objectives- Just plain broken puzzles: incorrect translations, mismatched names, and wrong answersBefore quitting just now, I hit a travel puzzle where the names didn't match between the image and text, the rules were unclear (was a "mixed route" optional or required?  Did you have to use all 3 forms of transit?) and the final answer was wrong (unless I screwed up super-simple math, or there was some shadow rule I missed).  A game like this needs good puzzles, and they failed way too often.  Sure a game like "Professor Layton" had the occasional groaner puzzle... here that's the vast majority.Now the minor complaints:- Many of the puzzles would be better if they had an actual "interface".  The game let's you draw on the screen... but it does a really crappy job of it (right click should delete, rather than having to swap out tools.. was this originally a mobile game or something?), and often the puzzle picture often obscures whatever notes you might want to make.  If you want me to place pieces on a chessboard, let me drag some pieces around the screen.  But no, they didn't want to do any "per-puzzle" programming, so all you get is a multiple choice or "drop the pin".  Lazy.- The story is incredibly lame, the characters are completely non-memorable, the conversation is dull, the setting is bland.  The game quizzes you on the game's background lore, which is not nearly enough motivation for me to read it.  The school has no character; I can't imagine someone being interested enough to read the tedious lore on every statue/painting.  Thankfully there's always a "next thing" marker, so you don't have to navigate or pay attention to where different rooms are.-Some of the puzzles feel like their answers were updated without updating the image; like, there's details that ended up meaningless, but point towards a mediocre puzzle rather than the dumb one they went with.  -They get two "puzzles" out of every image.  This maybe sounds OK in theory - but in practice it usually means there's just two mostly unrelated puzzles, or there's one "side" of the puzzle that doesn't really work.  So, like the "easy" puzzle is a straightforward, filler question about the picture, and the "hard" is the actual puzzle.  Or the "easy" is the actual puzzle, and the "hard" wants you to pick out a random, arbitrary detail.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a Professor Layton style game with Harry Potter style aesthetics. Its a good starting point for the developer with a lot of possibility for growth.There are a two main areas of concern I have with the game so far and if addressed they could take the game from good to great.The first are the controller controls.  The game has controller support but quite frankly its one of the more awkward control systems ive ever used.  The camera left/right scrolling is controlled by hitting up/down on the right control stick. The camera up/down scrolling is controlled by hitting left/right on the opposite (left) control stick. Ideally this should be remapped so that up is up, down is down, left is left, right is right and all on the same control stick.The second issue, (and more important issue as it pertains to gameplay) is that of translation.  I researched the developer and found they are Croatia based.  Within the first hour or so of the game you will realise that the translations are a little rough and the dialogue is sort of clunky.  This is particularly an issue when solving the already difficult to solve puzzles.  More once I've spent a good while trying to figure out the solution and when I finally did it turned out that if the description for the puzzle had been worded differently, it would have made a lot more sense.  The developer should certainly consider getting a better translator.Aside from that I did experience a glitch that really hampered my progress. Along the way you collect chocolate bars which you can consume to gain clues that help you solve puzzles.  At one point my chocolate bars jumped from 8 to -7... so not only could i no longer use them but as I collected more I wasn't gaining any more chocolate bars but reducing the negative number (for examples it went to -6, then -5, then -4.... i'm gonna have to get to 0 before i can even start using them again)It's in pre-release so I'm guessing there is still time to make some changes here!  This could be a great game and I encourage the developers to go that extra mile! Good work so far. Even in it's current state its fun! Totally recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: The Academy is in a pretty rough state. The story, the characters, and the soundtrack are pretty milquetoast, so the gameplay would have to be the saving grace. There were some genuinely tough puzzles that were still logical that I enjoyed, but at some point the realization set in that the puzzle set is extremely limited. Vast majority of the time you're simply given a picture and an accompanying text giving some description, rules, or limits, and you'll have to either:And that's it. There are so many puzzles that in other games would have variety of mechanisms with moving things around and trying out different solutions in an experimental way, giving you some insight with each attempt at solving. The Academy is basically just a slide show of riddles and forces you to solve puzzles with either your imagination, or you'll run the extreme poverty version of a puzzle with the provided pen tool. And out of all of the puzzles where the pen tool would be the most useful, the optional sudoku-ish puzzles in the newspapers are the one that are missing that.There were certain puzzles where the logic was so obscure I simply brute forced them. Most of them explained the reasoning that was extremely far-fetched with multiple leaps in logic, but then there were a couple where I didn't understand the logic even after the explanation. This just gets worse towards the end, and combined with the clinically inoffensive presentation and realization about the puzzle types makes the experience like chewing through cardboard.And on top of all of this, the game seems to have a lot of bugs (as of June 2020) with achievements being blocked, optional collectibles not unlocking properly, and (at least what I hope is a bug) if you do the sudoku-ish puzzles in the newspapers on the last day, it'll repeat the same puzzle each time.The only moments of true joy were the beginning puzzles as I was blissfully unaware of the nature of things to come, and the sudden realization and inexplicable fit of laughter around the mid-point of the game as it dawned on me that there's exactly one black person in the entire game. And I don't mean just one model that is repeated over and over - there's literally just  black person in this entire upper-class, filthy rich university. I'm still not entirely sure why I found this hilarious, but it has more to do with imagining developers having a panicked, superficial discussion about the racial makeup of the cast and then just hastily adding a single, textbook token black character and calling it a day.If you're absolutely desperate for just  puzzle game, maybe this can do the trick. Other than that, there's no reason for recommending this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The Academy has been referred to as Professor Layton meets Harry Potter. While it does share puzzle structure like Professor Layton and the magical board school aspect of Harry Potter, that is where the similarities end. I have high hopes that this game would fill a riddle puzzle void that was left by the end of the Professor Layton series, but the ending of The Academy has left a lot to be desired. It’s not a bad game, but it’s not a good game either.PROS:-	Good graphics-	Overall story was good, but the middle chapter dragged on. It was a “Fix-Today’s-Problem” story beat by “finding” the McGuffin -	Majority of the puzzles were fun and interest-	Interest setting design-	Likeable characters, if a bit one dimensionalCONS:-	Some puzzles were either too easy (filler puzzles) or to abstract to figure out.-	The side content is too well hiding ever when searching unlocked areas repeatedly.-	The bonus puzzles were the same two puzzle (newspaper logic and the anatomy riddle) for finding their bonus         newspaper or solving the side content.-	There is no way to restart a chapter without deleting the save file.MEH:-	Puzzle points are pointless, unlike Professor Layton.-	Hint system only gives one hint per puzzle. If still stuck look up a guide.-	The controls are a mixed bag. I found using a controller for movement and the mouse to solve puzzles was best.-	Short game.BOTTOM LINE: If you are looking for another Professor Layton game, The Academy is an ok game to play but don’t expect it to be the next Professor Layton series. Buy it if it goes on sale but other than that save your money. A sequel is planned but because of the mixed reception it received, it might be canned.

_childDocuments_.review: At the center of the Academy is a mystery. It’s one that presents itself early on in chapter one (of three total), when strange things begin to spontaneously happen around the students. You play as Sam, an unremarkable brunette boy who opens his front door to find a school uniform sitting outside. From there, the narrative jumps, and you find yourself at the titular Academy. Baron Alistair Holloway founded the place nearly 500 years ago, as a location for people to learn after the unfortunate loss of his wife. The entire story takes place here, and there are more than a few rooms and hallways to explore. The more time you spend at the Academy, the more you realize things aren’t quite right. There’s someone sneaking around after dark, and understanding precisely what they’re after is the core plot of the game. The Baron was a man of more than a few mysteries, and it seems he’s hidden a number of them among the school’s walls.Visually, The Academy is adequate. The lightning in particular has a tendency to make everything sort of shiny, which is good against some models and questionable against others. The characters themselves look fine enough, though most look similar. There were a few graphic errors during the talking head parts, like a hand clipping through a character’s head when they went to cover their mouth or gesture somehow. Outside of that, there’s little variation in face models or clothing, but the environments look well enough to give most of that a pass.The colour palette for the game is bright, giving the environment a cheery air even when eerie things are happening. Personally, I enjoyed the bright colours. It wasn’t uninteresting to look at or walk around in the world, and while character models often look the same, each person has a small detail about them that’s different from everyone else, making it easy enough to tell them apart. One girl has a scar through her eyebrow, another boy is heavier than the others, one girl has a coloured streak in her hair, and so on.The primary method of interacting with the world is through puzzles. Honestly, sometimes the story feels as though it’s there only to lead you into more puzzles. Not all of them are logic based, or math based, or focused on your ability to look at and calculate patterns. Many puzzles throw you for a loop, intentionally trying to confuse you and obfuscate the true answer for something that seems more obvious.When you receive a puzzle from an exam, or to untangle your luggage, or from a ditsy librarian who drops books, they aren’t timed. You get to solve them at your leisure, and once you complete the base puzzle, you’re able to move on to an extra bonus puzzle that claims to be a lot harder. If you’re ever stumped, there is a mechanic to retrieve hints. Scattered throughout the world are chocolate bars, and during the puzzle you can munch one to get one hint about the puzzle to try to guide you in the right direction.Quests are marked on your screen with question marks, golden books, or blue diamonds. Question marks show optional quests, golden books are classes that aren’t required but seem to be important to look into, and the blue diamond is your main quest. The icons always hover in your peripherals, and as you turn to look to them, show what doors to go through to make your way to your goal. As someone who struggles at times with navigation and directions, this helped me try to accomplish everything every single day. Movement is done throughout The Academy in a third person view, and you guide Sam along from room to room. I did this with a mouse and keyboard, only because I couldn’t get my controller to function with the game. Whenever it was plugged in, the mouse would lock in place, or glitch about the screen until I unplugged and restarted it. Wasd+mouse controls were fine, and there’s also an option in menu to play like a point-and-click game if you prefer to steer Sam with your mouse alone.There are also other dailies to accomplish outside of classes and talking to your friends. Each day, the librarian hides a book somewhere in the Academy. Find it, and you can solve two more puzzles inside before it gets put back in her collection. There are also daily puzzles to do in the newspaper, and chocolate bar locations change from day to day. Upon a few attempts to reload the game, puzzles didn’t vary when I went through the day again, but there are enough puzzles in the game to still sate almost anyone.As an avid puzzle fan, I would recommend The Academy: The First Riddle to anyone else who enjoys them as much as I do. The game offers over 200 riddles, puzzles, and one big mystery to solve. While the plot was personally a touch lacking for me, the puzzles themselves stumped me more than once to a point of guessing, and then laughing at myself once I realized the way to solve to get the correct answer. When it comes to any puzzle game, I love when they can confuse me enough to laugh at myself, and The Academy did that to me more than once, making the experience enjoyable despite a few other unpolished aspects.

_childDocuments_.review: The Academy is basically Professor Layton set at a boarding school. So you have the mystery, friendship, adventures, mean teachers, etc. of boarding school fiction (like HP or other similar cultural touchstones) but the main mechanic is completing Layton style logic puzzles. The game looks great, it's got nice music, the characters are nice, the writing is fine (there are parts where it feels a bit "English as a Second Language", but it's fine). The story is pretty meaty and it took me 10 hours to finish the entire game.But the puzzles are quite bad. And that's a real problem when the game is a puzzle game. A numerical majority of the puzzles involve, more or less, figuring out what the "trick" in the puzzle writing is. This is not fun. An example, paraphrased is "At 11PM there are 4 fireflies. Every hour, a new firefly shows up. After 12 hours, how many fireflies are shining their lights?" and the answer is "0, because it's daylight now". Here's another one "Scientists need to mark four frogs for observation. How many different colours would it take to mark the frogs?" Answer: "1, because you could place marks on different locations to tell the frogs apart". It's extremely juvenile. These kinds of joke puzzles are a part of Layton and Puzzle Agent and others in the genre, but they're a very small part and here they're a huge part.Sometimes the puzzles involve relying on contrivances; say, you have a series of circuit boards connected to each other with wires, and you need to fill in the serial number of a circuit board... and the trick is that you can see something resembling a number in the pile of wires. This is not a hard puzzle, that's clearly the answer, but it makes no real sense: why would the arrangement of the wires be the same as the serial number?  Other puzzles are trivially easy ("1159, ____, 1201, 1202. Fill in the blank"). There are 200 puzzles -- well, actually, 100 puzzles that each have two mini puzzles -- and of those 200, I'd say maybe 20-30 are what I'd consider to be actually interesting puzzles. That's an atrociously low hit rate. You could maybe argue the simple puzzles are designed for a kid's audience, but because so many rely on deceptive text or plays on words I would think kids will like it even less.Besides the puzzles there are classroom segments where you are asked pop quizzes about material to be found in books. This has the opportunity to be interesting, but 100% of the material quizzed about is about the founder of the in-game school. I think it makes sense for boarding school fiction to have an internal mythology, but not at the expense of also being a school that makes sense.It feels really crappy to say so much bad about a game that has an awful lot going for it. I'd still vote thumbs up because it looks good and it's sort of got a soothing rhythm in how you go through day after day in the school and make friends and get into adventures. But it's a very mild thumbs up, because they had one important job and they didn't get it right. The developers later made the simple but fun Cats in Time and the great Escape Simulator, both of which I'd recommend over this.

_childDocuments_.review: So I'm really torn apart whether I want to write a negative or positive review...At the time of writing this review I finished the game.I wanted the game to be like Professor Layton. It partially met my hopes but also disappointed.The Story Arc is alright even it's not extraordinary by any means.It just falls a little flat in my opinion. Still there were moments when I felt some tension and I really enjoyed it.Overall I'm a little sad that it's not a detective story that one could solve without the lore of the game. But I guess the Sci-Fi/Fantasy aspect makes it appealing to some.Oh boy!Some of the riddles are a lot of fun. But many aren't. There are many trick questions that are just way too easy.- There are Questions were the answer you enter isn't what is later shown in the solution and makes no sense.- There are sometimes just WRONG answers wanted! (there's a riddle where you have to figure out the cheapest way to travel and I found a way that works better than the solution wanted)- The Bonus-Questions that are supposed to be harder are often just super easy- After finishing a riddle the solution isn't explained. Sometimes there is a text literally telling you "After carefully looking at all possible solutions, this is the only one that fits" so if you didn't understand the riddle and just guessed you still don't understand it!- I miss a diagram displaying the solution if it's something graphic- The clues are ♥♥♥♥♥♥. I miss the Professor Layton clues where there are different stages of clues. Here sometimes you just get a "well you need to look at the numbers" when its already obviously about the numbers.- Since there is a Bonus Riddle for each Riddle that uses the same Graphic you get really confused which parts of the graphic are actually relevant for the riddle you're doing.- I would love to have the option to draw with different colors in the riddle screens- the graphics within the school are sometimes slightly buggy- I played the game in German and the translation definetly isn't perfect! i recommended this game initially to my mother but I'm not sure if I still do because some aspects only make sense when you translate it back to englisch and use a different meaning (harmlass example: there is a water pipe and its literally translated as water flute, which doesnt make any sense)I will revisit the game once walkthroughs come out just to find the last riddles that I didnt find on my own and I'll probably buy the second part once it comes out with the hopes of better riddles and an interesting continuing story arc.I'm not mad, I'm just disappointed. I hoped for really nice riddles and most of them weren't that good, so nope, I don't think  I reccomend the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm currently midgame and I have a few things so far that I would like to share. I have discovered this game, because the developers posted about it on the Professor Layton subreddit. As a huge Professor Layton fan myself, I wanted to play this game, knowing that the team behind The Academy: The First Riddle has played PL games too. I was sure this game would be amazing. However, the game does not even compare to the PL games. Of course, it does not have to to be a succesful game. Yet, it still lacks on various aspects.The story is okay. It is not something refreshing, but it does not necessarily have to be that. However, the story itself is pretty flat. We do not know the main characters motivations and they do not develop themselves. Some side characters seem unnecessary and do not contribute to the story. The story itself does not seem coherent due to these lack of motivations and character developments. Therefore, I was not really invested in the story.The riddles are okay. They are not as hard as the PL games, but we have to keep in mind that this game is not a PL game, but it was inspired by it. I really liked the format of the puzzles. If you've answered the main riddle correctly, you can solve a bonus riddle that is connected to the main riddle. Moreover, you can unlock a main hint by "eating a chocolate bar "that actually help you solve the riddle. Most riddles are multiple choice, meaning you can solve the riddle by clicking on one of the six possible answers. This way, you won't struggle too much when solving a riddle. You can always guess the answer. Even though this might be seen as lazy, I do like this feature, because sometimes I am not that invested in a certain riddle. However, I have noticed that some riddles are straight from the PL games, but are adjusted a bit. Yet, I do believe it is legal for the makers to adjust and present these riddles as their own. It's just that I reckonized some of them. Thus, I already knew the answer.The game mechanics are decent. If you have played many adventure game, the controls will be familiar. The graphics are okay. A bit dull in my opinion, but it is okay.Overall, I don't really like the game as much as I hoped I would. I am just not that invested in the story and its characters. I only play the game for the riddles to be honest. I would recommend the game if you like to solve some riddles, but I would not recommend it for its story.

name: Roadwarden
detailed_description: YOU ARE THE ROADWARDEN A brave stranger putting your life on the line to make a difference in this grim fantasy world . While most people would never risk a solitary journey through the wilder parts of the land, you willingly accept the struggle. You guard travellers, connect isolated villages, support merchants, and repel attacking creatures, bandits, or even undead. TAKE THE PLUNGE A powerful merchant guild has called on your services, sending you on a journey into the unknown planes of a mysterious peninsula in the hopes to expand the guild’s influence even further. _childDocuments_.review: What an awesome game!  Sure, it's text based and you've got to do stuff like... read, but the writing is superb and the stories of the tribes and people you meet are compelling.  The music is relaxing and I find the game a great way to wind down for a couple hours after work.  It's simple in its make-up but managing your money, food, and appearance can be difficult... especially if you go around buying stuff just to see what it can get you in different situations.  And of course, on first play through you don't realize that some items from some people can be bought at pretty big discounts after you reach a certain friendship threshold with them.   I played on normal difficulty which gives you 40 days to complete your mission to open trade up to the peninsula where the story takes place.  Simple, right?Of course, pretty much everyone hates people like you with the stink of the city and an air of sophistication above the average dirt farmer.  So you've got to get the people to trust you and believe that you're a force for good in a world which seems to have abandoned them to their fate.  They're hard, self reliant people who don't think they need anyone's help and in several cases, are dying out because of it.  But that's just the base story line.  There is so much else going on if you really dig around.  Lots of little mysteries to solve and relationships to groom.  I got a bit scatterbrained around the middle and probably wasted a bunch of time being inefficient.  Though I "finished" the game, I'm pretty sure I didn't complete it.  There were several stories I did not finish, hints I didn't understand or couldn't figure out how to follow up on, and a couple settlements with no trade agreement.The game is also short enough that I have no problem playing through it again.  Sure most of the content will be the same, but I have this burning need to figure out a couple of the mysteries I left behind.  I can honestly say the game has been one of the most enjoyable I've played in a while.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Absurdly stellar game. Please partake immediately. I highly recommend this game for its polish, its fun factor, its story, its balance, and its atmosphere.Roadwarden plays a lot like what you'd expect a classic "choose your own adventure" game might play like, but with some very modern appreciable qualities. There's mechanical crunch and resource balancing beyond just "picked the wrong option? you're DEAD, bucko." The balance for a player like me, who is not forward-thinking and is fairly impulsive and is rather meticulous in wanting to DO EVERYTHING and comb the land clean, is impeccable. I finished off my entire quest log down to the very last day of the game's normal-difficulty time budget. Resources aren't scarce, but they're not in abundance either, and grinding is (rather graciously) not an option.Rudimentary planning of your day and routes are fun and necessary to maximize productivity and balance your resources. Even in make-or-break things like combat encounters, the game is dutifully forgiving and allows you to restart immediately from the encounter should you fail, and there are a plethora of options for varying situations. Throughout the game you can collect an abundance of adventurer's tools to make various encounters easier and less taxing on resources, and make you feel clever for planning ahead. Further, the game mixes things up a little in various places, where you don't just get a dialogue box of spoken lines or actions to click, and where you instead in fact need to apply critical thinking and enter in keywords to a "type in the action/question/name/location you wish to know more about" box. The game as a whole rewards forward- and critical-thinking, is deliciously moody with its music and background noises, is very fun and solid in its writing, and really good at making you appreciate (or despise) the people in it. There's a plethora of fluffy actions and choices, and so much interwoven connectivity where completing an action or learning about a thing on one side of the map will offer up a question to ask elsewhere. There are even some simple conversations which allow you to shape the past of the world by recounting your part in it, which is phenomenal for world building.Given a greater time budget, I would have definitely done some things differently and made different choices and preparations, but I still felt very satisfied with my conclusion and the story I wove with my actions. I had to leave some stones unturned for the sake of time, but even that felt good for the sake of having to make tough decisions.For a while in the beginning of my run, I overextended myself very hard. I was coasting on nothing - little health, no money, no resources. I spent the majority of a single day from my delicate 40-day time budget working for a single coin, scarcely enough to fill half a belly, and not enough to even sleep a night on a bed where I was. I traveled with that coin to a distant inn, spent it there for some generous hot meals, and regained just enough strength to continue exploring until I tackled a giant spider and collected its web. The web would be very useful - I could use it at a tailor to upgrade my armor, OR sell it for a healthy chunk of coin to get my legs under me again. Tempted toward the adventurer's need and greed for the former, I instead chose the coin for the sake of practicality - and promptly spent the majority of it to get myself back on track, after which I finally hit a solid stride.I cannot stress enough how good this game is and how worth my time it was.

_childDocuments_.review: Although I can not claim to be an expert when it comes to games that are text-based, with my only experience of it here on Steam with Zombie Exodus and a couple of Flash-based titles from back in the day, the type of game that primarily focuses on text lends itself well to storytelling and those who are less focused on the visuals than they are immersing themselves into a world that is as deep as it is wide.That is to say Roadwarden has a lot to offer where the typical Roleplaying Game experience typically shines in, as you take the role of either a Fighter, Mage or Scholar acting as a 'free-roaming lawman' tasked with investigating the disappearance of a fellow roadwarden that previously visited the northern area some months prior, in which one has to explore the roads connecting the various villages and hamlets together alongside other places of interest.How you go about this is a specialty of the RPG genre, seeing as just simply surviving can be quite a challenge depending on the difficulty chosen as I would personally recommend the Standard difficulty for starting off with to see how far you can go and if it's either too easy or perhaps too tough for you on your first go. (With the 40 days being the standard time limit for how long you are allowed to explore the region, as the Casual difficulty removes this time limit altogether and starts you off with increased resources whilst Restrictive reduces the time limit down to 30 days and makes roaming around in night time more dangerous and even possibly life-endangering!)Though it should be noted that this is far from a hardcore RPG that punishes you whenever it can get the opportunity to, as any failed combat encounters resulting in your death will allow you to step back and try it again which, when combined with the ability to make upwards of several dozen save files, should allow a prepared player to not softlock themselves out of some better outcomes for particular quests or factions.Touching briefly upon the three classes, each one has their own unique advantages that should come expected for anyone who knows their RPG games well, with Fighters having a better melee weapon and specific combat options that guarantee a good or advantageous result over the other two, Mages allow the usage of spells via 'Pneuma' which slowly restores itself each day alongside the use of Spirit Rocks to refill it that can aid you in certain situations where a Fighter would struggle whilst Scholars take a more passive role, choosing not to excel in anything combat-related in favour of using their vast knowledge of the lands and it's mysteries to have a much easier time communicating with the local tribes and solving most puzzles and riddles easier than the other two classes.As far as the survival aspect of this game goes, seeing as I did hint at earlier, the four core stats you have to pay attention to are Vitality, essentially your health that acts as how well you are currently doing that plays into a few physical and endurance-based encounters, Hunger, which primarily acts as what allows you to overcome physical struggles, Gambeson, which acts as your armour and protection from various strikes against both monsters and human enemies alike, and Appearance, which is a surprisingly important factor that many end up neglecting as this impacts not only the prices offered by various vendors (both goods you sell to them and their own goods bought by you) but also how must they trust you, which affects what services they offer to you as well as the quests they give to you. (A fifth does technically exist, but it's class-based and varies from one player to the next)Now for a point of contention here, seeing as one may glance upon the game's description here on Steam and read that it is a 'Text RPG', giving them the vibes that this is some archaic and truly outdated artifact from the early 70's, and feel justified in dismissing this game outright.I can happily confirm that Roadwarden is not THAT old as far as inspirations goes thankfully! Seeing as it offers various charming illustrations of each of the game's many areas that you are likely to be visiting on multiple occasions, which helps to contextualize where you are and give some nice 'flavour' of sorts to the well-written dialogue that you'll be reading throughout your adventures in the north, giving some much-needed background variety that such titles as Zork and Night House (does anyone remember these games truly?) lacked due to the technology being so limited at the time.If there was any criticisms that I did have to raise, personally I would have liked more of an emphasis on the dangers of the north that you are tasked with exploring, seeing as you will rarely die on even the standard difficulty outside of certain battles where choosing the wrong action will guarantee death, (even with the upgraded gambeson and at full vitality + hunger!) since it would have made for a nice addition to throw into the Restrictive difficulty to make it even less forgiving for veterans who may know mostly how the game is played and desire some 'RNG' to a variety of possible encounters, most of whom are more dangerous and present some serious challenge to them!Other than lacking a little of that juicy 'roguelite' spice that I feel would have complimented this otherwise excellent story-focused game and a problematic bug with a specific NPC  that made progression a tad more frustrating than necessary, I feel like this is an overall satisfying experience for those who are after this type of RPG here, given the sheer amount of endings one can experience depending on how much (or little!) they did during their time in the region!In conclusion, for anyone who is after a medieval-themed RPG that takes homage from the likes of the Witcher series or Darkwood and puts the narrative in the limelight whilst gameplay takes second-stage and supports the wonderful storyline crafted by Moral Anxiety Studio, I would highly recommend giving Roadwarden a shot as it's the closest you will get to a modern text RPG that welcomes casual gamers who are willing to give this niche genre a shot which, given all of the effort put into this indie, is a journey that'll stand out from the crowd!Arriving at the post-review section for those who made it this far, here's some tips that I'll put under as spoilers for those who would rather explore and work out the game's mechanics for themselves, however for those who need a helping hand here:

_childDocuments_.review: Roadwarden : By Triple F"Roadwarden," developed by Moral Anxiety Studio, is a text-based RPG that offers a unique blend of interactive storytelling, exploration, and choice-driven gameplay. Released in 2022, the game combines elements of classic RPGs with a visual novel style, placing players in the role of a Roadwarden, an itinerant protector, messenger, and occasional mercenary tasked with patrolling a desolate, isolated peninsula. Unlike many modern RPGs, "Roadwarden" relies primarily on its narrative depth and atmospheric writing rather than flashy graphics or action-heavy combat. The result is an experience that feels both personal and expansive, where every decision, encounter, and discovery impacts the player’s journey through a world filled with intrigue, danger, and lore.At its core, "Roadwarden" is a deeply immersive narrative experience, emphasizing storytelling and player choice as players explore the peninsula and its varied inhabitants. The game’s text-based nature allows for rich, detailed descriptions of the environments, people, and creatures encountered along the way, encouraging players to imagine the world in their own way. The player’s role as a Roadwarden allows them to interact with diverse communities, settle disputes, and uncover the secrets of the peninsula. The branching story paths give the player agency over how they want to approach their role, whether it’s as a compassionate protector, a calculating mercenary, or something in between. This sense of autonomy makes each playthrough feel unique, with choices that influence relationships, alliances, and the very fate of settlements across the peninsula.One of the most striking elements of "Roadwarden" is its focus on survival and resource management, which is carefully woven into the game’s narrative and mechanics. As players venture through the peninsula, they must contend with the harsh realities of being a Roadwarden, such as keeping track of food, money, and supplies while navigating dangerous territories. Decisions are often impacted by these limitations, creating a realistic tension where players must balance helping others with their own survival. The peninsula is unforgiving, with dangers like hostile creatures, unpredictable weather, and treacherous roads. This resource-based challenge adds a level of realism to the player’s journey, reinforcing the idea that being a Roadwarden is a physically and mentally taxing role that requires strategic planning and forethought.The dialogue and choice system in "Roadwarden" is exceptionally nuanced, with conversations that adapt based on the player’s previous choices, skills, and reputation. Interactions are more than just dialogue trees; they’re gateways to the player’s own interpretation of what it means to be a Roadwarden. NPCs have their own agendas and moral complexities, and players can approach situations with a range of tones and choices, from empathy to intimidation. Additionally, skills and character traits chosen at the start of the game, such as knowledge of herbalism or combat experience, unlock unique dialogue options, further influencing how the story unfolds. These choices don’t just impact the current conversation; they often have long-term consequences that can ripple through the rest of the journey, lending weight to every decision.Exploration is another core aspect of "Roadwarden," as players traverse through forests, mountains, and villages, each with its own lore, secrets, and quests. The peninsula is a diverse landscape filled with points of interest, from abandoned ruins and haunted woods to bustling villages and hidden shrines. Unlike many RPGs, "Roadwarden" doesn't rely on a map filled with waypoints; instead, players must learn to navigate based on their knowledge and intuition. Discovering new locations and uncovering the mysteries of the land feels rewarding, as each area holds history, hidden resources, or a chance to impact the lives of the inhabitants. The game encourages slow, deliberate exploration, where players absorb the world’s atmosphere and gather information that can shape future decisions.Visual and sound design are minimalist yet effective, using pixel art and atmospheric soundscapes that complement the game’s text-heavy style. While the visuals are simple, they’re crafted with care, using detailed illustrations to represent various scenes and encounters. The pixel art conveys the desolate beauty of the peninsula, reinforcing the sense of isolation and danger. The sound design is equally understated but impactful, with ambient sounds of rustling trees, distant wildlife, and eerie silences that enhance the immersive quality of the game. This minimalist approach allows players to focus on the narrative while providing just enough visual and auditory cues to create a vivid mental picture of the world they’re exploring."Roadwarden" also shines in its approach to world-building and lore, drawing players into a well-thought-out fantasy world that feels both mysterious and grounded. The peninsula is a land filled with ancient ruins, remnants of lost civilizations, and a complex political landscape. As players progress, they uncover details about the different factions, religions, and communities, each with its own beliefs, customs, and conflicts. The game doesn’t force-feed exposition; instead, players learn about the world naturally through conversations, environmental cues, and the choices they make. This organic approach to storytelling allows players to feel like true explorers, piecing together the history and culture of the peninsula at their own pace.In conclusion, "Roadwarden" is a masterfully crafted narrative RPG that succeeds through its immersive storytelling, complex choice mechanics, and richly detailed world. While it may not appeal to those looking for fast-paced action or cutting-edge graphics, the game offers a profound and atmospheric journey that rewards patience and curiosity. By combining a strong narrative with realistic survival elements and nuanced character interactions, "Roadwarden" creates an experience that feels both intimate and expansive, drawing players into the life of a Roadwarden navigating a land rife with mystery and peril. It’s a unique addition to the RPG genre, and for fans of interactive storytelling and exploration, it’s a journey worth taking.

Just keep in mind, not everyone feels the same about Roadwardens...Roadwarden features:-Quests, lots of them-Loads of endings which change based on every little thing you do-Different religions to pick from, or none at all-Zombies-Lots and lots of text-Ethical and moral dilemmas a plenty -3 classes to pick fromPros:-Top notch worldbuilding, making you really care about every character, settlement, and story you come across-An amazing soundtrack that makes you feel fully immersed in travelling the roads -A pretty carved out economy and money system-Easy to pick up, no quick time events at all and infinite saves in case you want to undo a choice. -You can learn about the beasts of the game and fight them more effectively with the knowledge you haveCons:-The game is essentially a text adventure with pictures, so if you don't like reading a LOT then this might not be for you-Pretty basic class system with few mechanics-Somewhat unengaging combat, though not frequent

_childDocuments_.review: This is a role playing game in the truest sense of the term. You also have a lot of freedom and there's just enough time and resource management involved to make this feel like an actual game (rather than just a visual novel). _childDocuments_.review: If you're even remotely considering buying this and wondering if its the game for you, it is.  It's exactly what you think it is.  Buy it right now.People have blown millions trying to make RPGs that are a tenth as engaging as this.  The music, the systems, the world... it's all fantastic.  The game is almost entirely text driven, but at the same time it's sparing and evokes a world rather than drowning the player in exposition.  The world and the characters in it just come alive in ways that again, far more expensive games utterly fail to pull off.I haven't been as interested in exploring since I played Subnautica, and I haven't been as intrigued by the mysteries in a game since I played Obra Dinn.  This is that good.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Beautifully written, with complex characters and true moral ambiguity. Too many RPG's rely on grimdark, sensationalist violence to convey a sense of high stakes. Roadwarden genuinely creates emotional investment through fully fleshed-out, flawed characters whose arcs are influenced by your choices. And it's not afraid to showcase the full spectrum of human emotion, bringing moments of joy and connection along with wrenching choices and tragic backstories. It's right up there with Spiritfarer in how deeply the game imprints itself on your psyche. Based on other reviews, I initially played with the 40-day time limit, but the deadline really stressed me out. I get why some people like the time constraint, but I love that it can be disabled. Removing it allowed me to fully enjoy both the story and the mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: You can honestly skim a lot of the dialogue and be fine. Combat could be improved dramatically. The game grows on you over time, the last half was dramatically better than the first half. The character writing is phenomenal but I wish the game told you that it is often better to not choose every dialogue option as the game will heavily punish you for saying some things. The final mission is really where the game shines when all the preparation comes together. All in all worth the time and a solid 6/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Everything about this experience is top-notch. The muted color palette gives the world a sense of scarcity and deprivation, only amplified by the somber soundtrack. _childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Masterfully written. The world is full of characters and the setting is so rich and the music makes the experience truly immersive. _childDocuments_.review: This game expertly cuts away a lot of the cruft of the RPG genre, while still keeping a lot of its mechanics. Instead of overly-complex or abstracted combat and traveling, the moment-to-moment play resembles more of a visual novel, with you keeping tabs on your reputation, managing your time, maintaining your needs, and thinking critically about the words you're reading. Every part of the game is delicately interwoven - the narrative, themes, UI, and mechanics - and it all comes together to create a melancholic whole, every piece reinforcing the desperation, not only to remain alive, but to remain whole, a struggle that every other character in the game also faces. The art is occasionally a bit crude, and I don't feel like it's particularly well-served by pixel art, but such choices are cost-effective, and the art is primarily used to accentuate the writing anyway. Also, as is often the case for games with this many words, there are several spelling and grammatical errors, but rarely did they take me out of the experience. The writing allows for a lot of player agency, and it's high-quality enough to make more reading feel like a reward as opposed to a slog. Overall, I'd say the structure of the game alone is enough to make it one of my favorites, fitting itself snugly between two good genres to make a great experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Roadwarden is a wonderful call back to an almost forgotten genre of gaming - text adventures! There's a lot to love here - an engaging world awaits you, brought to life through terse writing, pixel art drawn in dirty sepia tones and a solid soundtrack to accompany your journey. This game really does ooze character - it's you and your horse, in a new world that you don't understand yet - but you will, if you're brave enough to search every nook and cranny!Keep an open mind while you're playing and you may surprise yourself with how much you can get wrapped up in this title. I hope you have a great time with Roadwarden - good luck out there on the road!

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this game, I had a wonderful time playing it. I came into it having never heard of it, I just stumbled on it during the steam sale, the art style caught my eye, and after trying the demo I very quickly realized I would enjoy it and bought the full game.The world and story really immersed me, I found myself thinking about the game when I wasn't playing it, what I needed to do next, what decisions I should make. The writing is good, the cast of characters is varied and interesting, I enjoyed getting to learn more about each character I met, there was often a lot more depth to them than I expected.I played through it twice, the first time my Roadwarden did achieve their goal, but I failed to accomplish a lot of the other things I hoped to, so I almost immediately started a second playthrough! Which was much more successful, although I'm still tempted to play it again sometime soon and see how differently things can turn out.The choices around your Roadwarden are nice, I really like the dialogue choices and the moments where you decide who your character is, as well as building up skills and collecting items to be able to get through different encounters. I struggled a lot more with money in my first playthrough, the second time I got to the point where it largely wasn't an issue for me,The lore around the world felt like it was introduced at a good pace, and I enjoyed the general concepts around it too, like the different views on the wilderness and the creatures, it made me want to know more. The length is good, I'm a pretty quick reader so I probably got through it faster than others might, I was definitely disappointed in a way when it ended but that just speaks to the quality of it, it didn't overstay it's welcome by any means, it didn't feel padded out unnecessarily, it's a nicely contained story.There's more eloquent reviews, (I think this is actually the first ever review I've left) but I wanted to sing the praises of this game because it hit in exactly the right spot for me, and if you enjoy text-based RPGs I would say absolutely pick this one up, heck, even if you don't, just try the demo! See if it draws you in like it did to me. Excited to see if the dev makes more games like this, because I'll certainly play them :) (and coincidentally noticed I own their older game, Tales From Windy Meadow, through a bundle, so I'll be trying that!)
