_childDocuments_.review: Could not recommend this game enough. I fell in love with the story and got very invested into the beauty this game has to offer in its art style and soundtrack. When it comes to gameplay: you can expect a lot of text based combat that's dependent upon your starting class and equipment you packed along the way with you. A well written conversation mechanic that not only makes you learn as much as you can before speaking to characters, but also makes you consider what you say and even if you should reveal some of the things you learn on your journey to people who have a vested interest in them for their own benefit (and sometimes even to another person's detriment). And the occasional quick random encounter that keeps you on your feet coupled with longer, more in-depth encounters that you can prepare for as in-depth or as balls-to-the-wall as you so wish :DIf text based adventures are your cup of tea, play the demo and see what I'm talking about. If you despise reading and wish for God to blind you for the curse of being able to string words together, hit that green button to play the demo and give it a try, it's something new and might still catch your interest with it's medieval fantasy world!Just finished my first ever playthrough and I can say for certain this is one of my all time favorite games now. I'll probably return back to this game in the future to give this game a second run as another class and maybe do it as a roguelike run where I won't savescum as often just to see what happens :PThank you for reading this word salad, give the demo a chance for an hour or so to see how you like it, and may the Wright guide your journey in peace and prosperity traveler!

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of fun playing Roadwarden!Good writing, great worldbuilding. It's a "simple" style of writing, wholly in the good sense. The focus is on content and clear descriptions instead of a fancy wordy style, making it very easy to immerse yourself in the world. The illustrations also do a great job supporting the writing, by always providing the player with a quick impression of their surroundings before reading the details in the text.The challenge level struck a perfect balance for me. Not so difficult that every decision and journey becomes a stressful endeavor, not so easy that it feels like there are no stakes and you're just cruising through. And since you can save and load at any time, every player can fine tune their own difficulty level depending on how often they save.There is a very good balance of choices and consequences. The choices you make allow a good degree of freedom and agency in how to explore the world and how to approach things, without becoming unpredictable, disjointed or overwhelming. I also love that character skills are neatly integrated into gameplay, rather than increasing a bunch of your character numbers.The combat worked really well for me, placing relatively little emphasis on character stats, and a lot on the preparedness and knowledge of both the character and the player. You don't fight a beast with your Axe+2, you fight it with the specific gadget or, even better, piece of knowledge that you encountered along the way.I rate it awesome/10
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Can't remember the last time I played a text-adventure, but this is a good one. _childDocuments_.review: I never got into old school RPGs in this style - Darklands was just a little too impenetrable and I was more into Wizardry than Ultima. But Roadwarden is fantastic. The music is gorgeous and suits the excellent writing that does wonders to set the scene. The art adds to these descriptions in a way that just layers beautifully. Surviving is about making calculated risks and preparing for what could be ahead. Loving my time with this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I haven’t encountered writing anywhere near as good as this since Disco Elysium, yet that isn’t to say one is better than the other. Roadwarden is sort of dark fantasy, while Disco Elysium is an irreverent inspection of human psychology, society, and the Apocalypse. At about thirty hours, I cannot complain about my time with Roadwarden. A part of me is terribly sad to say goodbye to this world and its people, but it certainly didn’t overstay its welcome; that’s important. While I experienced amazing successes, I also made horrible mistakes and oversights that the game punished tastefully and forcefully. I don’t need or want a perfect adventure where everything ends with a neat little bow on top, and Roadwarden delivers just that. Some mysteries were left unsolved, while others were solved a little too well. Succeeding is sometimes a form of failure. So much to chew on, and I am thankful for the adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; It's a lot like playing a good book you can't put down.If you don't like to read you're really not going to like this game, but if you do like dark low/medium fantasy fiction and if you've ever enjoyed a text-based adventure, this is an easy recommendation.The time limit can be a little stressful, but I walked away with an ending I was pretty happy with (but only JUST made it). I would have liked to have explored a few other threads and tied a bow on things, but that also adds a replayable angle to the story, giving you an opportunity to explore other paths or optimize how you approach things on another run.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't love all the dialogue, nor what appeared to be obligatory homosexual references that have no actual relevance to the story... (I mean, I do find myself wondering so often a person's hole of preference, but just not for this title I guess)But all that said, this game is really good. Possibly my favorite one of this genre. The musical score creates an atmosphere immediately and I found myself at times "hearing" the escalation and then with some literal dread pouring over the words that were slowly scrolling the screen. My eyes scrambling, yearning for the "thing" that happened hoping all the while I still have reliable options to progress forward.I love the depth of the NPCs, but the females seem to get a little more love than the males regarding their visual descriptions (just imo). I love the inquiries that require you the player to type what you want to ask about, akin to Sierra games I played in the distant past. There's a level of "secret" information I yearn to unlock every time I'm presented with such a prompt. I've established favorite places in game to sleep, favorite NPCs, and NPCs with which I would prefer not to talk.I think this game is at a great price point and frankly a real gem.

_childDocuments_.review: It's very very good, might be the best low-fantasy media I ever engaged with. You do fight unleaded and kill monsters but 70% of the time the best course of action is running away and the absolutely most important thing you do in this game is gossip. No joke, you can finish the game with flying colors without killing almost anything but if you don't gossip like your life depend on it you're going to die I ♥♥♥♥ you not. The comparison to Disco Elysium is apt. One word of warning though - the open-ended-enter-words puzzles don't really work in wild or the ruins, just try some things until you are pretty sure you got the gist of it and google the solution. Absolutely do not do it with the open-ended-enter-words GOSSIP puzzles though, because it's the best part of the game. Finding some sweet sweet leverage on the bandits or the location of some secret place by asking the right person just feels like magic.

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this game to anyone who has an interest in fantasy or role playing games. It is heavily text based so prepare for a lot of reading, but I was so absorbed that I finished it in 3 days after downloading it. Also, the developer is very nice! I found some grammatical errors while I was going through the game and made a note of them, and messaged the dev on twitter about it and he responded to say thanks and that he would fix them in the next update! For someone who has almost no experience in games like DnD but has always wanted to get into them, this was an amazing introduction! It was thoughtful and engaging and I was very immersed in the story, I felt real urgency when things were happening. I think I got lucky, because my first play through was almost a complete success (I never ran out of money, I never got close to dying, I think I got a good ending for most characters except for 2 of them), but I'm excited to replay and try a new path. Overall, be prepared for a lot of reading, utilize the quick save function, and have a fun time! Also, I played the first time on the setting with no time limit, I recommend this for anyone who has never played this type of game before because it reduced a lot of my anxiety about finding things in time. However if you regularly play these types of games, I think the time limit would be fun and challenging!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun and unique experience.Edit: It's more than that, it turns out the game has far more depth than I initially thought, in terms of both gameplay and world building. The world is rich and detailed, and it feels as if you're just scratching the surface of all of this. It can be hard, sometimes unforgiving, but it all serves to add meaning and substance to the experience. Excellent writing and design, the makers can (and should) feel proud of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I picked up this game on Humble Bundle Choice, I thought, "well I have not played a game like this in years, like since Windows XP, lets give it a shot"..............Then I realized I'd missed Breakfast and Lunch and it was 3 in the afternoon!  Turn off your second monitor, don't have a podcast on, just get invested, you will have an immersive, exciting experience where you feel like you're the true master of your own destiny and the decider on what will happen to this magical peninsula.  REMEMBER the Journal is your best friend when you can't remember who someone is, and sometimes events happen as you leave settlements, so it's worth walking in and out of places!  Also, stopping at locations along the path to somewhere adds no extra travel time, so harvest them berries!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I think this of one of the few games that has the best written material out there, it is very atmospheric and it has an immense lore that you can absolutely fell into comfortably and get lost. It remind me of my youth and all the time spent playing "choose your own adventure" books that I grew up with.THE GOODGraphic: It is super super nice, I wished that there was as well visual pixel art for the unique monster of this place.Music: Perfect match for the game, very enjoyable.Game: - I loved the intro part, it put you right in the tension mood of danger of the world. It really inspired me for a couple of quest that I will run in d&d. - I adored the idea of getting your journal expand as you learn more and more about the world. It makes you want spend all the time of the world to get all the information in the world. - There are so many good characters with their quirks that makes you love or hate them (in a good way)- Surprised with extreme pleasure that depending on your choices people would not talk with you about certain things, there are actually stakes in this game on your talking choices!- Having the chance of inputting free content it is a great addition, for example "licking the tree" it is a great chance of being creative on what we can do with this interactive digital medium respect to books.THE BADGame: - The time-sensitive adventure, I abhor any game that give you a time limit to do something, and unfortunately I couldn't checkout on this feature without making the whole game easier than intended. For me, and I guess for me alone, anything that make me rush instead of wanting to spend more time with your game, it is an absolutely negative idea. I am not gonna have time to replay your game, and neither I have gonna have time to just finish it because I am gonna get distracted by the next hot game that is gonna pop out and distract me from yours (I am saying this with all honesty and love for this game because it is the hard true).- Because I have played a lot of "choose your own adventure" games, I felt that the game was more about talking with the characters than actually doing any real adventuring, and I felt that was lacking in adventuring. So I am obliged to compare to the rhythms of those games and I felt that sometimes the investigation of cities was a bit overwhelming with a lot of unnecessary fluff content just to get some titbits of information (which I have still wanted, but was boring to do so continuously). It made me want to skip it all, and I am a person that I am used to read a lot of books in a year. I wish that the game just cut to the core of things, and keep the interesting part ups than just aimless talking to have your journal expand with info. I want to spend time actually using that info, than instead acquiring it.- Sleeping even in the ground should anyway give you energy, not removing it even if feel a bit uncomfortable. If these people are medieval people and at least hunters they would be used to be on the road, they are not rich nobleman on the first trip (this for me it is the biggest incongruence of all).- Having to write the exact spelling of a names going through the journal, instead of clicking directly on a selective of choices that I have already unlocked.VERDICT:Buy it, but play it with moderation a little bit at time, all the reading on screen is more tiring than usually on books. If this game was voice acted it could absolutely be a masterpiece at the level of Disco Elysium. I hope in future games the developer will find the budget to pull this off.NOTE: I give up on the game, because unfortunatly all the investigating was quite boring for me (and reading text on Twitch Stream it is not very engaging), but the game absolutely deserve praise and attention for introducing a different way to "Choose your own adventure" games, have various twists and turns and evolve the genre. The best out there like "Choice of Robots" or "Sorcery!" they feel old in comparison.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: A part of this game reminds me a little bit of Darklands (an early 1990s text based RPG) which is a great thing. What I like about this game is that while the setting feels grim and hopeless at the beginning, the story does bring a bit of hope if you make the right choices. It has a good story-line and will keep you entertained for several hours.If you like the visual novel / choices matter genre then this a great game to play. If you're also a cheapskate like me, buy it when it is on special for <$10.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Roadwarden was a game that I could not stop thinking about days after having completed it for the first time. Yet, even now, I struggle to gather my thoughts about the game in anyway that might prove helpful to would-be players without simply saying "It's great" or "I love the vibe".I am someone who struggles to read for long periods of time, preferring audiobooks over the written word (it's easier to listen than it is to actively read, at least for me), I found myself utterly absorbed in Roadwarden. I hadn't truly played a proper text-based RPG up until this point and was unsure how I would fair, but I was nonetheless intrigued by Roadwarden's visual style and music; it was strong enough for me to take a leap of faith and give the game a try.I am very glad I did for I found Roadwarden to be an immersive and engrossing adventure, the likes of which I wish I could find more often in video games. The game is full of struggle and hardship. It focuses on the problems of the commonfolk in place of any Dark Lord or Ancient Evil, something I found to be entirely refreshing, with many villages wondering how they are to survive the coming Winter and what they may have to do or sacrifice in order to see Spring.The music in the game is wonderful, both relaxing in town and mysterious on the road, yet remains solemn and lonely. It never quite lets you fully let-go of your concerns and paranoia, even in the relative safety of a village or in the walls of a house, thanks to the ever-present danger from both the wildlife and those who do not trust you or seek to use you for their own ends.Suffice to say, I heartily recommend the game to anyone who has an interest in roleplaying and stories involving exploration.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: This game has some of the best writing of any media I've ever consumed, and a remarkably well characterized world. The gameplay mechanics are interesting and there is plenty of questing to do, but if the idea of exploring around helping various people and staying alive doesn't pique your interest, I'd still recommend it but a second thought may be warranted.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Yep, I can definitely see why the reviews are overwhelmingly positive. The graphics are actually very pleasing; the text-based adventuring will take you on a wild ride; the wide array of characters is amazing, if a bit difficult to remember all the nuance interactions that can trigger; and the missions are surprisingly well crafted; oh, and the bandit? The bandit is a CHAD. I TOOK HIM TO [the place] with three others, and that absolute unit of a man saved the party from an attack AND lived to tell the tale.  But yeah, it is a great game, bolstering a simple yet nice soundtrack, confrontations of endurance, lots of double-crossing, and it's all packed together in a story-driven narrative. Strong recommendation
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I love the sheer amount of worldbuilding that's been put into this. I love the pixel graphics, and I love that pretty much all you have to worry about is the text.Some things like using the text box to search an area is a bit clunky, sometimes requiring keywords that weren't mentioned at the site or may not be intuitive. Also, just doing the bare minimum to survive is very difficult if you run out of dragon bones and have no idea where to get things. At this point I'm just foraging and selling my labor for food and bed rather than actually doing what I'm supposed to in quests.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: If I could give this a side thumb I would, but being forced between Up or Down it's a mild Up.I came to this after having a blast playing  The Life and Suffering of Sir Brante and Suzerain. I was itching for another great visual novel/RPG and this came up.My biggest problem with this game is how much text there is. I thought the aforementioned games had much, much better pacing.I wont get into it too much, but if you're in the mood to read *a lot*, there's some impressive stuff in this game and I'd recommend it. If not, probably a pass.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: This was a phenomenal experience.Roadwarden is a very melancholic, low-fantasy, and text-heavy game that's hard to get into, but once you do, it is probably one of the best narrative experiences out there. Forget "deep plots" they out into the tags of every other AAA title, this is the stuff you want.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Very good so far. If you like this style of choice-based narrative games you will love this. If you don't know what I mean by that think choose your own adventure books or the older text adventure games like zork. That sort of idea on mega steroids. You are a roadwarden, basically someone who has been assigned to this region to patrol the lands, make connections with the local people, and explore the place. There is a lot of story and lore as well as some strategy and moral choices. If you are the kind of person to skip through cutscenes and story to get the "real" gameplay, you might not like this. On the other hand if strategy, story, and lots of role-playing sounds fun roadwarden is for you.For more modern examples of similar games than Zork, on the off-chance you have played the Sorcery! series, this is very comparable to that level of high quality gameplay and writing. Similar to the banner saga as well, besides the turn based tactics gameplay. Suzerain is another example. King of Dragon Pass too.3 hours in and 9/10 so far, I see myself playing this quite a bit.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: It drops you into an strange and confusing world and your journey is all about unraveling that world layer by layer. It's some of the most compelling fantasy story telling I've experienced, to call it immersive is an understatement. If you're willing to spend some time, and buy into this world you will start to feel that you are part of it. You will know these roads and it's people... and they will know you as their warden.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: One of my new favorite indie games. has a great atmosphere and story if you are willing to read the text. I never skipped the dialogue or description boxes and I think it added a lot to my playthrough. Really well done dark fantasy. And its a masterpiece for your wallet. Took me 16 hours to complete the game on one class. A bit less than that on my second character, but the game has high replay-ability since you learn so much more on the second run after you know what you are doing.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually like text-based rpgs, but this game had me coming back again and again! I was charmed by the realism in the world; people aren't always happy to meet you. In fact, more often than not, they're guarded or even hostile. It was a joy getting to build up the roads and make them safer and more profitable. I went from 2 rations and 3 coins to approaching 30 coins and buying new equipment just because I could! Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Good text adventure. The grammar are typos are bad to the point of sometime I have to guess at what the author meant, but you get used to them eventually. That said I would definitely pay for some cleaned up text DLC. A lot of the "right" decisions are possible to figure out by talking to people which is great, and more than a lot of adventure game I play, though there are still a few "you had to think like the developer" ones that feel cheap. Still worth a play though if you like adventure/rpgs and don't mind typing!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Narrative is heavily saturated with feminist ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ at every corner. Grammar sucks. Punctuation sucks. Game loads way too slowly, and even the mouse itself lags. On this pixelated game where everything follows a script, the mouse itself ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ lags. The mouse also disappears from the game menu frequently, returning to the regular appearance, and existing outside of the game (so you can't click anything). Game's narrative is HEAVILY saturated with the author's political leanings. The dialogue is inconsistent in dialect. For example, sometimes within the same interaction, a character will be speaking with a unique, medieval accent that sounds a bit Scottish or Irish, but then say something like, "Nah, I'm good." As if they were a teenager from present times. WTF? Incredibly lazy and amateurish, as if a high schooler made it. Author tries to sound like such a smarty pants, but ends up routinely tripping over themselves with bad grammar, redundant word choice, and clunky sentences.Characters who have provided you information are not listed in the Journal. Only super specific, landed characters on the map are listed. I've had entire conversations with people who had names, but had no Journal entry of their own. Very hard to remember who they were, if at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: One time I got a fantasy book from the library and it got recalled and I never read the ending. After 13 hours, this was my experience with Roadwarden. By my story end I solved no mysteries and failed the main quest because the arbitrary time limit ended the game before the story was done. A game about exploration punishes you for exploring. The writing is not good. A few compelling set pieces are buried in an avalanche of boring exposition with forgettable characters that explain their backstories rather than show any agency or character. Maybe there's an interesting story here but in a the time it took to watch a full season of Game of Thrones plus one of the Lord of the Rings films, I couldn't find it. Play Disco Elysium or Planescape Torment or Choice of Robots. This is not worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Only played for a few hours, but I'm definitely hooked. This is one of those games where the entire appeal is the mystery of discovery. You know nothing. You start from scratch and build in true RPG fashion of what kind of person you want your character to be. I highly recommend it. You can tell they took a great deal of time writing out a ton of dialogue options and fully fleshing out the world.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of the best text adventures I've played, definitely up there with the Sabres series if you are familiar. Pondering change, legacy, ambition, your time spent in this life and does any of it matter. Do you want to be a hero, are you out to make money? Looking for a new home? Your characters class, story and goals are chosen through prompts and really draws you in to who your warden is as a person and how they might act, if you're big into roleplaying. If not, these are still important to ponder for your characters end goal in their journey, aside from the duties of a roadwarden.Personally I think the 40 day time limit adds a lot to the game, but they added custom difficulty so you can turn that off if it's not your jam. Plus there's a console you can cheat with to your hearts content if you get stuck or otherwise need help to push through an obstacle.If it's not clear, absolute 10/10 from me. Pick it up if you enjoy text based adventures.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked those "Choose you own Adventure" books as a kid, then this will probably be right up your alley. And you don't have to keep a notebook (unless you really want to) since all the info is tracked in game. Took 8 hours for my first playthrough and I didn't even get close to 100% completion, so good replayability along with character build and NPC interactions.The writing is very good and the characters don't feel flat or forced. Standard difficulty is not too easy nor too difficult, although it does require you to actually manage resources. If you don't like being constrained to a time limit, Easy mode doesn't have one.Definitely giving this another playthrough or 2.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game with so much to discover. So many possible plot lines and enough to do that (I think) it can't all be done in one standard length run. I've replayed several times trying to do it all and it hasn't got old yet. Even though the puzzles stay the same, each has multiple solutions. The player character can really be a completely different person each time, with different goals, personalities, and of course actions/alliances to the different groups of the world. Nice variety in puzzles too, with some more open-ended exploration, some finding a niche item to use, and some just plain old battle tactic strategies, among others. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Roadwarden is a very well written game with a lot of complex and intertwined plot lines (although you don't realize it until later in the story) It has a nice soundtrack and a lot of memorable characters. I would personally recommend playing on the casual difficulty because the time limit make it nearly impossible to finish all of the quests. It's a very memorable experience and one I'll probably revisit a few times.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: It's a solid game, there's not much bad to say about it, except the fact that it's kind of boring and dull. If you enjoy reading an inordinate amount of dry descriptions, this game may be for you. It's filled with basic characters, the usual light fantasy monsters, and tidbits of worldbuilding we've seen a hundred times.The game promises a gritty adventure in a realistic world, and delivers it, but in a way that is simply not that entertaining. There is a striking lack of sound effects, visual effects, or any kind of support to make it more palatable.Perhaps text-based RPGs aren't for me, again it's not a bad game, and kept me engaged for a while, but at some point I realised I didn't really care about 90% of the text that was presented to me, and I don't really care about any of the characters or what's happening in this little piece of the world. It's as if in pursuit of realism, the game sacrificed entertainment value. All of these scenarios that happen are very real, feel very immersive, and that's something I value greatly. But that's not enough to make something fun. And if it's not fun, why bother?
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: This is an exceptional game that I liked very much. The descriptions combined with the art style are evocative and thematic and fit very will with the atmosphere of the game. This is one of the best "make your own adventure" games I have ever played, and I have played a ton of them. Decisions matter in this game and you will find yourself stressing about them. For a more casual experience, I would suggest playing the "Easy" mode which would allow you enough time to do most of what you want to accomplish and make a lot of money by gambling etc. However, the absence of a time limit of the easy mode does detract a bit from the atmosphere of the game, so for those willing to play and replay this game (and it is good enough to justify at least two playthroughs) I would suggest the normal difficulty.Eudocia for the win.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Roadwarden is not a game that I expected to enjoy too much, as I hadn't played many games like it before. I only bought it because it was on sale and I was running out of other things to play, but man am I glad I did. Roadwarden has so many elements built into it that I didn't expect to find when first playing. I think this game is best to go into mostly blind, as much of its charm comes from learning and adapting to this world that feels familiar to our own, yet noticeably different and more  dangerous. The people you meet and locations you travel to are all changed based on your choices, and I loved seeing my actions slowly shape and even tame all of the different places I once knew nothing about. This game constantly surprised me with just how in depth I could get with different locations and characters, and I truly think its worth a try especially if you haven't played anything like it before.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy reading-heavy RPGs you'll likely be thrilled with this game.  The game is essentially a sophisticated gamebook with a lot of content and lots of opportunities to 'role play.'  The visuals are minimal but the writing is extraordinary and the gritty setting is exciting and mysterious.In another review I saw somebody suggest that this game deserved space on the same shelf as Planescape: Torment or Disco Elysium.  In gameplay it's closer to Elysium, in writing it's closer to Torment.  I love them all, and I would happily recommend this game to anyone who enjoyed either experience.It's good, and it's cheap, and you should play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: what an incredible game this is! the story is complex and layered, and it feels like there are always new twists to learn about different characters. the steep house storyline is heartbreaking, and i'm really fascinated with the religious tensions between the followers of the wright and the pagans. i'm so excited to play again with different choices to see where that takes me! this is the perfect game for anyone who loves adventure, quests, mysteries, and complex fantasy politics :)
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Solid choice based RPG with fun mechanics surrounding interactions. Normal mode had a good balance of preparing and putting effort into preparation of both quests and hazardous travels, as well as a good few choices for almost every scenario, with some leaning more heavily on flavor. One of the best RPG's i've played in a bit that had a timed factor, and it could have loads more replay ability when I next pick it up again.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't played much at this point, but after grinding rogue-lites and winding RPG's this game feels like a breath of fresh air.The dialogue, story, and characters feel natural.  I greatly enjoy the way your choices can influence the narrative, and how every action or dialogue choice leads to what feels like a unique outcome.  The sound design is , chef kiss good.  If you enjoy text-based games, or are looking for a story to immerse yourself in, this game is certainly it.And if you read this, .
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Just an outstanding piece of work. A narrative/text-driven adventure that's fascinating, imaginative, and mysterious, with a beautiful soundtrack to boot. I love the title screen theme and find myself using the OST as background music for writing. The world-building is pretty stellar too. Looking forward to diving into the rest of the game and seeing what it has to offer.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I normally don't leave reviews, but after completing the game (and maybe doing it again for another ending), I feel that the game deserves praise.While this RPG is certainly for not everyone (it's mostly text-based, old school RPG with lots of reading), for those who would love to experience a lore heavy, low magic dark fantasy setting, there is nothing better. You arrive in a harsh, dangerous land with monsters and people who can also be monsters. You can build alliances in the different settlements and the options to do within the 40 days limit on normal is simply staggering. Your choices truly matter in the game, everything has consequences in the end.A fantastic game and a true hidden gem of that.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: What a great hidden gem! I love a good story, and I'm super engaged and invested in the subtle lore and world building Roadwarden offers. Gameplay is literally just making choices and managing your stats and items, but super fulfilling. The NPCs are so well fleshed out and have so much more to offer. I played 7hrs straight and Absolutely love this game. FYI: It has a built in  console if you ever need to tweak things, by pressing shift+o (the letter o). A few helpful commands are:- pc_hp = x (for example 4) for health- mana = x (magic)- coins = x- cleanliness = x- armor = x- pc_food = x (nourishment)items are all in the form of item_nameoftheitem = xso for example item_rations = x
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game that is not for everyone. You play as a roadwarden entrusted with exploring the region, forming relationships, building alliances, solving problems, and occasionally fighting foes. It's a text-based RPG that shone brightest for me when certain relationships with people or villages blossomed after putting in the work with various quests and mundane jobs. However, it is a slow game that often lacks clear direction, even in the end game.I completed the game once and was fairly satisfied with my ending, but I probably won't play it again anytime soon. The combination of your character's gradual progression, the amount of back-and-forth traveling it takes to complete most quests, and the hard limit (unless you're on easy mode) on the number of in-game days means that the game generally follows this path: an early game that is a slog of rarely ever having enough health, armor, money, or time; a mid game that is the most satisfying part of the game where starvation and poverty are no longer concerns and you can finally make progress with all the different quests you've accumulated; and an end game where you eventually run out of having enough in-game days left to complete most of the quests remaining, so you kinda just move around doing mundane work until the end approaches.This game has its great moments, but it does feel like a chore at times and the pace can unexpectedly grind to a crawl. Few things are more demoralizing than talking to a minor character and being faced with a wall of text to read that is more filler than meaningful to your journey. I also had to regularly stop and check my quests, check the map, check my inventory, and read through the glossary of characters I had met to figure out what to do next. I think that could have been addressed by having more prompts about what quests certain items or characters were related to - too often I had collected a bunch of items and had forgotten who they were supposed to be for.As for the good stuff, the characters and relationships you run across throughout the game are great and it's very satisfying to see your character go from a relatively blank slate to someone with alliances, a reputation, and maybe even a few enemies. Unfortunately, due to the time constraints this game imposes, I don't think it's possible to end up on good terms with everyone or even complete every quest unless you're on easy mode or really figure out how to min-max the game, so choose wisely when deciding who to please and piss off.I like the game and would still recommend it, but I wanted to like it more.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, never have i thought about my decisions in game like this before. ive completed the game and it was worth it even when i feel like i missed a lot of stuff and feel like i could have made a more desirable outcome at the end. it kinda like a book with its writing which is ether good or bad depending on who you are but if your looking for a game that is rich in story telling, role play, critical thinking, make your choice or just plain old fun this is a spectacular game to try out.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent game that is easy to get into, while being an excellent challenge. If you are at all a fan of games that pull you in for their story more than anything, then this will be something you will enjoy. The mechanics ranging from your class to your hunger are all made in a way to actively advance the storytelling in this game. Additionally, the freedom this game sometimes provides is astonishing for a text adventure game.I have never played a text adventure game before this but I have not played a better game this year than this one. Hands down. And due to the low price, I would recommend it to anyone who is not afraid of a little reading and has the time to fully immerse themselves into this game
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: This game despite being "text based" can be enjoyed by those both patient enough to read every piece of description yet also those who only skim through the detailed text this game provides. It is deeply satisfying to see how your actions change the world around you in this game, and how various choices and events do make you weigh their benefits or costs. My only criticism of the game is the ability to quick save and load during events or dialogues as that allows someone to always leave with the perfect outcome, yet if one does not wish to use that feature then they do not have to, so it is only a slight complaint. A great purchase, a great story, and the world is written in a outstanding way, it reminds my of the fantasy books I used to read when I had the time to long ago.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I loved it! The world is interesting and the game teaches you how it works at a nice pace. At first, I thought I wouldn't be able to remember so many names and factions, but once I stopped playing, I couldn't stop thinking about what I'd seen and what I had to do for X or Y person. They were alive for me. This was easily one of the best games I've played in terms of story.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Writing this over a year after I played it, it is the deepest and most engaging choose your own adventure novel that I ever played. The game is filled with lore that is relevant and felt throughout the experience, and manifests in a lot of narrative and strategic choices. Among the best stories I have had the pleasure of experiencing in a video game. It is very heavy on reading, so I wouldn't recommend it if that deters you, but otherwise as someone who doesn't have much experience with text heavy rpg games, I highly recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I can honestly say this is one of the greatest games I have ever played. Like I pulled an all-nighter trying to figure out the game's mysteries, the only all-nighter I have ever pulled. I have been thinking about this game's story constantly. It is so incredible. I almost couldn't bring myself to end my second playthrough because I didn't want the story to be over. I'll be starting a third soon.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I'm *really* enjoying this game. It's the first text-based game I've played, and I'm more of an RPG player. It feels significantly more grounded in reality than most other RPGs I have played, which (speaking as a reenactor of the medieval and renaissance periods) is a huge breath of fresh air.Pros:+Rich lore: The game takes place in an area with well-connected NPCs, quests have branching storylines, and the Roadwarden's deeds have consequences which impact others. I would classify it as "low fantasy." Humans are the only "race," but there are fantastical beasts and magic present.+RPG elements: The Roadwarden may choose from one of 3 classes to start with, which drastically alter the way the character interacts with the world. In addition, your character's skills improve as they progress the story, and they acquire equipment which aids them in their journey.+Gender-neutral terminology for both the main character and their horse: The Roadwarden and their trusty mount can be whatever gender and color the player wishes.+Great music: sets the atmosphere of where your character is and the situation in which they are involved.+Replayability: With 3 different classes to choose from, 3 different difficulties, several different dialogue trees to follow, and multiple endings, players can find themselves returning to a different experience with each playthrough.+NPC diversity: I personally appreciate the deliberate inclusion of NPCs of many different skin colors, body types, and hair types, as well as people of different life partner preferences.+Generous save system: Learning to use the F5/F8 quick save/quick load combo is essential to ensure your playthrough goes (mostly) the way you want it to.Cons:-A lot of reading: It is a text-based game, after all. It is an interactive story. This requires the player to pay special attention to the details of the dialogue and text describing the scenarios.-Low visual effects: Again, it is a text-based game. It does include visuals with each scene, and those scenes change slightly as the character accomplishes goals, however the color scheme is less-than-vivid ("OK, apply the medieval filter") which may not appeal to some players.-Can be vague: Some puzzles may drive the player to frustration, simply because they don't know the exact word to type to solve a particular puzzle. I had to rely on the internet to solve more puzzles than I would like.-NPC dialogue learning curve: I appreciate the level of detail that the creators went through to give NPCs from different areas different accents and dialects, it added flavor to the lore. However, some of them require quite a bit of re-reading to ensure you know exactly "hwat" they're saying."Ne ye worry t'much though, 'tis doable."-Some minor grammar issues: Normally not a big deal, but in a text-based game, correct spelling and grammar are critical. It's not rife with errors, but some further editing wouldn't go amiss.-Limited replayability: Once a player knows exactly what each scenario presents, it becomes somewhat trivial to read it through each time. I found that much of my time spent replaying NPC dialogue trees and areas that I knew well was simply tedious. The fun comes from doing things you haven't done before, or finding something new because of a different style of play.I highly recommend this game if you're looking for a low-stress, dark, historical fantasy story where choices matter. If stunning graphics and slaying hordes of demons with your greatsword "Doombringer" are more your thing, perhaps save this game for later.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: The amount of world-building done here is incredible. I spent over an hour reading through the glossary and bestiary of the world before even starting the adventure. Few peoples' experiences with this game are going to be the same with all the many paths and people that will be constantly pulling you in different directions.Be prepared for 16+ hours of reading.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely write reviews, but some games are just that good I had to.Amazing Game, a must buy for anyone interested in a great story game/RPG/text-based adventure game/ or maybe a more relaxing game to wind down in the evenings.I ended up loving this game so much I binged the entire thing in two days. I got immersed in the world like I never have before in an RPG, i cared about these people and the world and stuck to my roadwarden's morals and I didn't do the usual RPG game thing of rapidly changing my personality to get the best out of a situation. My Roadwarden dreamed of being a hero, and a hero they would become. I made them act heroically and protect the roads, and they never told lies or betrayed the trust of others and it felt great. I was even rewarded by this near the end of my playthrough where after enough Heroic acts I felt as if I could be called a Hero and got a permanent health increase.The music and sound design is extremely well done, it has catchy light tunes that aren't too in your face but make for a very nice passive listening. Sometimes in certain areas more enviromental sounds will play like animals far off in the woods and it really plays into how untamed this area is compared to the others and that you should be more careful around here.I really appreciated that you build the world in the game. Throughout the game people will ask your Roadwarden of where they come from and you will get various options to choose from, I remember there is a person that asks you of an old Inn in the city down south and you can say it's still there, or has been gentrified or it has taken a dive in quality and reputation and is one of the roughest parts in the city. This is great as you can choose the world you live in, is it cruel and the poor are downtrodden or things not so bad in the south. And Honestly, I can't even think of anything to nitpick about, there was a fly sound effect for like 5 minutes that was a bit annoying but it really is a perfect game and for that price you really can't beat it. I've gotten nearly double it's worth in playtime and I'm already debating going back in for a 2nd time.Couldn't recommend more, PICK THIS GAME UP!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: A text based CYOA game with survival mechanics such as an inventory and food/health/sleep/cleanliness used as modifiers for your decisions. Great worldbuilding and fully realized characters. Good writing and setting get you interested in the villages and people you meet. A sense of mystery pervades many locations and can be solved through the right questions and travels.Your decisions and actions have will have effects on both the final outcome and how people around the game-world will treat you. There is a time-limit of 40 days on regular difficulty (with options for 30 days or no time-limit) which will force you to prioritize what you want to do by the end. I had not completed all the quests or solved all the mysteries by the end but it felt natural with the coming fall. This combined with 3 different classes (I chose fighter but there is also mage and scholar) leaves me wanting to do a second playthrough to focus on some of the issues left unsolved in my first playthrough.Would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I need a cup of coffee to focus my wits and eyesight before diving into a session of this game, and it is a lot of fun, much like playing a game of D&D by myself. The characters are interesting, and the ever-present danger makes me feel simultaneously very weak and also like a badass whenever I overcome some crazy monster through patience, magic, or steel.I love it. I would definitely purchase another adventure as the Roadwarden, along whatever roads my character travels after securing the wild peninsula for Hovlavan.NB: this game is not for the impatient, or anyone craving action or a dopamine hit, or anyone opposed to reading for hours on end. The gameplay is exclusively three things: reading, thinking, and making choices.Knowing that, if you think you might like this game, you'll probably love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I am a sucker for RPG text games; and this game just kept drawing me back in for more.The story line was great and it was intriguing to learn more about the land and each person. I loved the use of being able to speak with people and inquire about others. The story did have a bit of a lull and slow start, but understandable when it's trying to teach you the gamestyle and how to play. (I encountered a couple error screens after loading a save, but was easily fixed with a restart of the game.)I highly encourage you to play the first playthrough very openly and come up with a character. It's really interesting to see how things play out when select certain responses.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Roadwarden is, by far, the best game I've played this year. Estrangement is a difficult feeling to create in fantasy nowadays. And yet, this game managed to create a universe so rich, so special and so unique that I felt it in the first twenty minutes of playing it. Never had choices felt so important. You're always doubting your place ; you are important and you don't matter, your actions may bear grave consequences, but you're bound by the choices of others.The ambience in this game is mind-blowingly good. The music, the writting, the visuals ; it's a perfect mix. You should play it. You will not and cannot regret it. It will follow you all day long, and after playing it you'll hardly forget any minute of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: The narrative is compelling yet the choices you can make are strictly determined by roster plus some RNG thus lending to a 'map by scum saving' Not a show stopper but coupled with the three 'modes of play' it seems to be pointless to try it on anything other than casual.PROSWhat I liked was the overall ambience in the story-telling. It encouraged me to be nosey yet polite as I was compelled to garner trust. I admire these principles and enjoyed pursuing the individuals stories which hinted at a wider world.CONS:Some basic explanation of the temporal rules afore playing as time is everything yet I have no idea what time it actually is, occasionally told how long an action will take, yet double clicking a previously explored region does not and so reinforces scum saving techniques as a faux kind of tutorial to learn these essential rules.For casual play, this is a fascinating game and well worth the AUD$11 or so, I feel.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite games of all time. If you've ever loved a fantasy novel, you may well find a similar sentiment - there's a lot of reading here, and if you cannot slow you brain enough to consider what you are reading, then you will likely miss a lot of the importance and subtleties which the game presents. Which is not to say that you cannot finish or enjoy the game without reflecting on those subtleties - just that there is much more to be gleaned if you are willing to.Roadwarden is one of those few examples of a game which raises the form to a level of traditional "art." It has it's problems and limitations as any piece will, but what I really appreciate about it is that it does not distill "morality and ethics" into some offensively simplistic "ya wanna be good or bad" option. There are realistically complex nuances - different peoples with sufficiently diverse ideologies and histories and challenges. There often is no "obviously right and good" solution to a problem, because what is right and just for one people is not right and just for all; you must make compromises to achieve your desired outcomes - and even then you still must weigh what will benefit you and your ideology against the benefit to peoples you are mediating on behalf of.I arrived on the peninsula with a stated goal to become a power player in the imperial hierarchy which sent me there in the first place. But by the time I left, after all the effort I invested in understanding and improving the livelihoods and relations of the peoples who inhabited that geography, I wanted to live in the peninsula and do what would be best for those peoples and their livelihoods and their economies without bowing to imperial pressures...With it's profound art style and accomplished narrative, Roadwarden may well be the most meaningful and impact game I have played in a few years. It is hard to believe that Ren'Py has provided it's bones.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game. A simple text based RPG with some images in the background, except it's not as simple as it seems. I love especially that throughout your story, you can develop your background and character very deeply. However, don't expect all of it to come before you load into the game. The more you talk to other characters, the more you can set the world up and give it background. Only thing I wish is that there was more.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: So... I haven't "finished" this game--insofar as one can finish a game with so many possible endings. I did complete one run, and got quite a bad ending! This was because I simply ran out of time (I played on normal difficulty), which I sort of expected, because there's quite a lot of content and you do have to plan out your travels a bit for a 100% run. That is what I was attempting on my second playthrough, before life got in the way. By the time I had time to return to it, it was long enough that I felt I really ought to start from the beginning. I still plan to, but this is really the kind of game you want to dedicate some good time to digging into, which I just haven't had yet.I did enjoy every hour I played it though, which is why I look forward to returning to it eventually.You won't like this game if you don't like reading, or if you're impatient. You need to take your time exploring the options available to you and unraveling the story, which is quite compelling!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: edit2: Okay, the world building is phenomenal. The locations and characters are really unique and the writing really triggered my imagination in a great way. Huge props to the developer. What a labor of love.---The game is pretty good so far, but cloud saving doesn't work*, which is limiting my experience with it. I'm impressed with the amount of content I'll be getting for the price I paid.edit: * cloud saving works except on Steam Deck you need to make sure you override to the latest non-Experimental Proton version
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: 7 hours in but I already know I will have multiple play throughs of this game. The characters are just as dynamic as the world itself and the game lends itself to replayability, I have so much left to explore but as one other review below mentions, this game has made reading cool again - and I couldn’t be more excited to read everything I can. Highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually play text based games like this, however, something about this one seems great.I'm just getting started but really like everything about it.- Great writing- Nice pixel art which really adds to the story and immersion.- You Can save the game anytime you want.- Fantastic UI showing all important info.- Lots of nice choices as you progress.- The story so far is just right for an adventure/RPG- Three character classes to choose from.- Inventory management is simple and meaningful.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: A melancholy and engaging visual novel with RPG elements, Roadwarden presents a masterclass in world building coupled with an engaging plot and interesting mechanics. The game does feel a bit impersonal at times as the player characters is a total cipher and some of the interactions feel a bit mechanical rather than emotional or personal. Overall it is a wonderfully moody and interesting game.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: At first I was curious how a text-based rpg would work in this day and age but Roadwarden really shines. There is plenty to do on the peninsula, from exploring new locations, discovering secrets, and interacting with unique NPCs. I enjoyed the story and need to go back to play it again with a different class and approach. Both the story and the soundtrack are great and the pixel art is well done. While the game may look simple from the outside, there is a lot more going on. Recommended if you want a low stress story game with a great soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: There's something incredibly charming about this game. It's got simple yet pretty pixel graphics, and while very much a visual novel it has a lot of interesting choices and interactions that come up. Unlike most VNs I've encountered it's still very much an RPG, you get to make a lot of choices about who your character is, what they want, and where they came from. Also, there's a lot of work that went into actually studying the daily life of folks in the middle ages. Despite how fantastical the world is the people in it feel very grounded and real because of this. (Bonus points: has queer people existing in a way that doesn't make you feel like there's a dev giving themselves a "world's biggest ally" medal for doing the bare minimum. There's just, queer people that exist in the world and it feels natural and nice.)
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: As a child, my mother would take me to the library and by pure chance I discovered the Lone Wolf gamebook series. As a future gaming enthusiast, I played all 28 of them, with the last one still in reprint. Unfortunately, the series never ended due to the author's death.Roadwarden is the heir to those adventures and to the early text-based video games, infused with the same fantasy setting. In this case, it takes place on a forgotten peninsula, which forests are teeming with monsters ready to punish those who disrespect them.Our role is that of the new roadwarden, the one who keeps the roads safe. This quickly leads us into a whirlwind of people, places, and missions described through isometric maps, a handful of simple yet impactful music, and, of course, a lot of text.It's a strange sensation for a visual zoomer like me. Certainly, the imagination is freer to roam, but it also becomes harder to associate names and concepts. Immediately, Disco Elysium comes to mind, where the protagonist was also exploring a city in search of someone (in his case, himself). I can't say that the level of writing is comparable, nor the added visuals and voice acting, but Roadwarden certainly doesn't disappoint in terms of the depth of its environments, of the situations that arise, and of the subsequent choices to be made, further constrained by a 40-day time limit before winter arrives.4/5
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: One of those game worlds that feels so rich and alive that your presence is just a tiny blip in its grand history. I enjoyed everything about this game and would recommend it to anyone looking to lose themselves in a good RPG who doesn't mind a bit of reading - it reminds me of Disco Elysium in that way. 10/10 I wish I could remove my memories of Roadwarden to experience it fresh once more.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun narrative adventure with multiple ways to approach the challenges. Make sure to take notes, LOTS of notes. The bulk of the game is text, but there are images and some simple animations to keep it interesting. As Roadwarden, you travel around the wilds, help people, chase off or kill monsters, and try to stay alive. Each action takes time, so you have to plan your routes and where to lay your head at the end of the day. The story is engaging and worth taking the time to tease out the secrets of the wilds. It has a good length and doesn't wear out its welcome. I would love to see more adventures in this series or other stories with similar gameplay. If you're looking for a visual novel that doesn't devolve into a romance simulator, give this one a chance!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Went into this game expecting nothing and was pleasantly surprised. The peninsula is dark, oppressive and full of danger. It's hard to tell what is more dangerous, the savage beasts, or the shady locals. Your job is tough, your resources few, and nobody can be trusted, not at first.Without spoiling too much, I liked the writing, the characters and the choices I could make were varied and difficult. I can say it was worth the time and money.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Short version: It's a drag.After a while, you'll have amassed a dozen quests which all rely on the same pattern: go somewhere, do some chores until you're deemed trustworthy, get some hints for one of the quests. Rinse and repeat until someone pays you. The stories are an accumulation of small chunks and none of those I've seen contained an interesting twist or had an epic feel about them. Character interaction feels awkwardly artificial and comes with very little options and combat is frustratingly obscure, as there is no indication of how much the outcome was influenced by the dice. All you can do is quicksave and guess which of the choices might work.My conclusion? If you enjoy reading stories, stick to a good book, as the interactive elements of Roadwarden don't compensate for the lack of a good plot and interesting characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Roadwarden is an  title for anyone who craves a superbly-crafted, meaty, and mature role playing experience.For fans of Disco Elysium, The Witcher, Citizen Sleeper, Planescape Torment — Roadwarden is its own beast yet sits with the greats in terms of ambition and execution.From the moment you reach the title screen and are greeted by random tidbits of lore, to the introduction of the conversation system, and to the unveiling of the player inventory and journal with their wonderfully-written (and evolving!) descriptions — a lot of love and care went into Roadwarden's creation, and boy did it pay off in spades.Support this game. You'll get so much more than your money's worth.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: A masterfully crafted text-based adventure that immerses you in a beautifully detailed world brimming with lore, intrigue, and adventure. This game stands out for its narrative depth and the choices that shape your journey. Roadwarden is a gem for fans of interactive fiction. Its rich storytelling, atmospheric world, and meaningful choices make for a deeply engaging experience. While it may not appeal to those seeking fast-paced action or dynamic visuals, it excels in delivering a captivating narrative journey.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: This game is EXCELLENT. BUT ITS VERY SHORT.It's detailed, fun, has a decent story and choice are meaningful but I've gotten as much or more gametime from Choice of Games/Hosted Game stories and the graphics on this and the map mechanic arent worth the extra money when compared to some of the high end CYOA titles that are half this games cost.Graphics are murky/blurry pixels nothing to praise but better than what you'd find in traditional games like this.The soundtrack is  amazing, I'd listen to this as a background track to life.No leveling, no relationship tracking, everything is measured in achievements and progress. You're characters morality is kind of questioned, and you're given opportunities to lie or be greedy vs honest and kind but sometimes when you'd expect an option there isnt one which is kind of shocking and makes the game less appealing. Oh and you can battle hordes of monsters but a couple humans with sticks are stronger than  45 magic apes...When you finish the game you'll have reached the point in which you think, cool I'm ready for the next chapter, but itll be the end and you'll be torn between this was pretty good and it mightve been too short for my money's worth.In short: buy the game while its on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, so let me start out by saying something.This is one of the most well crafted, diverse and beautiful games i have played in years. About half a year ago, i had a sudden bug to play a text based adventure game that was in the style of old school DOS adventures (Think "black mirror Bandersnatch") but was having EXTREME trouble finding any of them that were worth their salt. I searched high, low, looked on the google play store, picked up a few games that were designed for flash, but none of them had "good enough" quality that seemed like they were worth the hours i put into them... until i found this.Roadwarden is a game that will reward you for staying true to your principles, however you wish to play it. Be it a positive influence, or a negative one. The possibility and diverse interactions of each of the characters, and how they inter-mesh together is incredibly vast, and all of the choices you make ripple effect across the land.This game is not for the light reader however. Extremely important information can get omitted from the mind in a large wall of text. Read carefully, and snuggle up with a cup of hot cocoa as you take on the role of a witcher-like constable keeping the roads of the peninsuila safe.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: An intresting take on the genre. After a while you really start to take intrest in the characters, wanting to know more about them. The script is well written. A well thought game that leaves you with something to think about after finishing the story. Personally I would prefer a couple more options (in certain situations I felt a bit restricted by the choises), but overall a solid 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: i really, really love this game.like a lot of people i'm sure, i was nearly put off this game because of the large walls of text and the game looking like a slow crawl. but after playing it, i had fallen in love with it. i've recommended this game to a handful of my friends already, even though i hadn't even "beaten it."i think this game is probably better if you know a little bit going into it (i had gone in entirely blind), but i don't think that's necessarily a bad thing. this game can be a challenge, but it's meant to be - the life of a roadwarden, in its own description, is not easy. as with everyone else's suggestions, i would definitely recommend starting without a time limit. i just would also take it with a small grain of salt, because i've been having a lot of fun playing with the limit on even if i don't necessarily know what i'm doing still.this game envelopes and swallows me, i can get lost between the words so easily and it's beautiful to me. i love the writing style and i really enjoy the exploration and uncovering of things (including things i already knew). the setting is entirely wonderful, i love opening this game and being greeted with the soft music and whatever ambiance i had left on my save. it immediately draws me in when i click continue or new game.it wasn't my first text adventure, but it was the first one i fell in love with.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic.  Like the choose your own adventure books from the 80's and 90's with a little more RPG.  Time limit is a double edged sword.  Without that pressure the game would be too easy, but it adds some stress to the journey.  Managed to complete everything I could by day 40 though.Don't know if I'll run through it again but multiple options are clear with a few classes to choose from so there is good  replayability.  Was NEVER bored and there is no grind.  Was always excited to come back and play.  A true gem and well worth the time to complete for those interested..
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Playing this game almost makes you feel like you're reading a good book but you can also control the main character in it. It offers so much and the art style is also very nice.It's bummer that it doesn't have more language options. I know so many people who would enjoy this game but they are missing out cause of language barrier.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Please make more of these, I haven't enjoyed an RPG like this in years! This is an unyielding, deep, dark fantasy text-based RPG, bursting with flavour and adventure. This to me is what life really feels like in a small rural community - the world zooms in to a level where people can directly see the fruits of their labour: clear a road and you open up trade for a village, make a friend who then passes the word of your good deeds on to someone in the next village, and so on. The two greatest strengths of this game are its writing and its choice - there is an absurd amount of branching depending on what choices you make and how you talk to the locals, which really gives you a feeling of true choice. The writing isn't florid, but has a very clear style and tone which sets up the tense, distrustful mood of the peninsula as you slowly battle through the wilderness - the world feels alive with its own culture (and villages have their own individual accents), groups have realistic ambitions and foibles, and you very much feel like an outsider. Speaking of which, your exploration of the world carries genuine and thrilling risk - while there is a map, it starts entirely coated in fog of war; you rely on verbal directions and uncover a rough path one careful step at a time. Your patience, local knowledge and foresight are rewarded more than any other game I have ever played.With this type of game, there is usually a very real risk of boredom - you have to chew through thousands of words and the pace is decidedly slow - but I found the game's pacing impeccable. You transition from tense path-finding and diplomacy early on to finally emerging into the late game as a political player on the peninsula, all while keeping an eye on the clock as your allotted 40 days on the job bleed away.Buy this, curl up with a mug of tea and a blanket, and wile away an evening in the vivid Hovlavan wilds.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Everything about this game just hits right on the mark, from the amazing world building to the intense and strategic combat with rich and vivid descriptions and the compelling politics and relations between the characters and factions deeply woven. It feels so satisfying to spend hours going through the peninsula, unravelling the secrets that the northerners are hiding, as your relationship with them constantly evolves, and seeing the tangible payoff of all the work you've done in the relationships or as the icons in the sidebars pile up stretching across the screen. This is especially impactful with the amount and variety of choices the game presents, working towards the chosen starting goal, favouring a faction and choosing weather to put morals/ reputation over greatly needed resources. Which leads me into the great balancing of the game: there is a near constant struggle of balancing hard to replenish vitality, costly food and amour, deceptively important appearance and being rewarded lots of money only to splurge it all on equipment for increasingly difficult battles; moreover, the amount of days given to explore was the perfect amount for me, enough to complete all the major quest lines and deeds while not enough time to fully complete all side quests and extra pieces, stopping the endgame from feeling empty and without much to do (what happened on my second play-through when I knew most of the secrets and obviously completed it sooner).As someone who regularly plays D&D and consumes D&D content, this game is one of my favourites of all time, I love the freedom you can get in some sections as you have to input your own prompt of what to do or who/ what to ask about and the very unique interactions outside of the dialogue box that contribute to the story, leading to many great puzzle solving moments that drove me to interact with the world much further than choosing new dialogue option 6 after npc 17 told me to complete x, y and z. I would best describe road warden as fantasy disco elysium (another one of my favourite titles) with a broader and more open world, and would really recommend to anyone else who enjoyed that game or literally anything else I mentioned above.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing game, that's why is so hard writing this after asking for a refund. I really wanted to play this game and have it be an enjoyable experieence, but truth be told you actually have to like reading a lot, and I just don't have it in me for the amount of reading this game has. The writing is great, the music and ambient sounds are very enjoyable, but can get a little repetitive if you take your time reading, and the pixelart is pretty. If you get this game, you need to know you'll have to take your time reading through a lot of (greatly written) text.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Roadwarden is a game that plays exactly like reading an engaging choose-your-own-adventure low fantasy novel, down to the color palette reminiscent of a well-worn old book. In playing it, I felt immersed in the sense of being an adventurer in a strange land, slowly learning about its people, helping them, and being rewarded for it as they slowly open up to me. The untamed and violent land holds many secrets, and I wasn't able to uncover them all in my first playthrough nor in my second, which I started as soon as the first ended. I highly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys reading, story-rich games, and RPGs, and I recommend that you play through it with the time limit at least once to get a feeling for how the game was meant to be played.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent text-based RPG, with only a few negatives and a bunch of positives.The Good:* Excellent storytelling, characters generally felt believable and motivations make sense for the setting.* Deep lore without being too difficult to navigate** Rewards careful reading of notes/journal information without being too painful if you overlook something* Forgiving save system that gives you enough save slots to reduce tedium and trial-and-error, and allows you to save (almost?) everywhere and at any time.* Items and skills are interesting and varied. Most items have at least one obvious use and a handful of secret/less obvious uses.* Descriptions and tooltips are interesting and often entertaining (particularly those relating to minimal/maximal traits and statuses)The Neutral:* Some interactions with characters and the environment are non-obvious, primarily those relating to acquiring trust.** On the one hand this makes sense since several characters are hostile towards you from the start, and don't give you a step-by-step for earning their trust.** On the other, many areas offer rather straightforward descriptions of what is missing/required to proceed, which usually includes a description of exactly 'how' the missing thing may be obtained.* Some items are prohibitively expensive (even on casual) when exploring the areas they would be most useful in.** This makes sense since it encourages prioritizing goals instead of wandering around aimlessly, however the actions/quests needed to obtain discounts are often those that would have benefited directly from having the item in the first place.The Annoying:* * Some missions require a sizable amount of backtracking and running around, which can feel annoying when the destination is the place you were just at.Overall 9.5/10: An excellent game that makes me wish this were just part 1 of a series.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: What a wonderful tale to play! With excellent writing, good humor and beautiful pixelized illustrations, Roadwarden offers an immersive fantasy world to explore filled with intriguing creatures and fleshed-out characters.Explore the land, meet new people and choose to help them or not, take sides, hunt the wildlife or choose to spare it. Every choice will have consequences and affect the kind of ending you will get.I played the casual mode which, I admit, was fairly easy. With no time limit, I could discover every aspects of the story, fully explore all locations in the game world and complete every possible quests I encountered. I quite enjoyed my playthrough.It was a really beautiful and well written game to play. I can only recommend it to anyone who like fantasy settings and good story-telling.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: At first I was sceptical about how a text adventure would suit me, but Roadwarden was one of my favorit games i played in the past few years.The story is interesting and has a good myth for you to discover peace by peace. The quest design is incredible, where you are given a vague goal at the start of the game and have to make the most out of it.
