_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that I know I will never find again, and I hate that. Everything is done with the maximum attention to detail, creativity, story, atmosphere, the list goes on. Think of whatever you want in a game, story, and journey and be ready to be impressed. I'm so glad that there are people out there willing and able to put their all into what will be labeled a niche experience because I can't imagine whats being missed by everyone who hasn't taken their first step as a Roadwarden!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible game. Every choice has sprawling consequences that forces the player to genuinely think about what they're doing. Where do your loyalties lie? Do the ends justify the means? Should grievous and abhorrent sins be forgiven in the name of progress? These are things you will have to decide, and more in Roadwarde. Highly, highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: It's a Choose Your Own Adventure game bordering on visual novel with well integrated, but small RPG elements and very good writing.✔ addictive atmosphere - I  the roadwarden and I feel like I lost something precious after finishing my adventure✔ writing - both worldbuilding and the multifaceted characters living in it✔ economy - it never feels like you are so rich that currency becomes worthless✔ story/writing itself is often the reward for overcoming challenges, it's realistic and worth it❔ most of you time is spent reading descriptions and dialogues, occasionally making decisions and travelling to new/known locations. That's the "game" and I personally loved it, but your mileage may vary❔ there is not much real rpg-like progression, it's mostly about what equipment and knowledge you carry❔ the pictures add a lot to the writing, but it's a shame they are generally top-down maps or landscapes and never show the characters you encounter❔ I feel like there is some political influence that the writing is pushing in the created world when it comes to gender roles. A lot of it could be explained by , which exists and permeates everything in this world, but definitely not everything. And the game doesn't try to justify any of it, you just have to accept that despite all differences between the villages and their inhabitants they are on the same page regarding this and it's not even worth mentioning. It's not handed badly, definitely not ham-fisted, but could have been better. Exploring possible societies from other worlds is great, but there should be reasons for  could have made them so different✘ the world is smaller than I expected. You can split the game into two halves - first is mostly about discovery, when your map is blank and second about solving as many of the issues/quests you obtained. It's a very rough split, but the first part definitely had more  in it. That's not to say that the second part was bad mind you✘ the game mostly avoids it, but there were some cases where I wanted to use something I had in an encounter, but it was not accounted for by the creatorsIt's the best game of this type I have ever had the pleasure to experience. Play it if you feel like reading something with choice/management gameplay on top. If you don't want to read then stay away - screenshots are very honest.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty, soulful survival adventure game where you play as a Roadwarden, a professional ranger sent to tame the wilds of a fantasy realm. You navigate the land via stylistic pixel art, multiple choice options, and lots and lots of text.If you don't like reading in games, or prefer there to be a voiced narrator, this is not the game for you. You spend around 92% of the game reading conversations, quests, lore and contextual events. The rest of the time you will be managing your survival stats (health, hunger etc) and making decisions on how you want to make your mark on the untamed frontiers you explore.I really like the presentation of this game - the colour palette is very minimalist and crisp. The background music is gorgeous - a reverby twinkling of acoustic guitars, pianos and light percussion. Occasionally I find myself so distracted by the whimsical melodies that I realise I haven't even paid attention to the last three paragraphs of text my eyes have mindlessly scanned.The worldbuilding and lore in this game is very comprehensive, yet restrained and sober for all its dialogue and descriptive quality. This is not high fantasy, nor low fantasy, it's medium fantasy, and it treads this line pretty well.Throughout the game you will be peppered with various quests and tasks, and sometimes it can get a bit headache-inducing. More than once have I travelled straight past a town for which I had completed a quest because I was too fixated on a different one I was trying to complete.Overall though I have very much enjoyed myself so far, and after 7 hours I am nowhere near the end, so there's value for money to be had here. But, again, you need to enjoy reading to get the most out of this title.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: It reminds me of a more in depth version of the old Fighting Fantasy books, its very well written and the choices you have matter.There is an element of the game keeping track of things for you, but its quite refreshing to have to make some notes yourself to use later rather than be spoon fed everything, but anyway its a great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Great text based rpg and adventure game. The writing is captivating and worldbuilding and story is superb. Though by the end of the game i found myself skipping some of the large text descriptions, so maybe text might`ve been sometimes less abundant. But overall i played it almost without rests in 3 lenghty sessions.This game is one of the rare cases when time restrictions work well. The difficulty of encounters is well balanced and quests are varied with non linear based structure with different endings to each one. Because of of all that replay value is substantial. Though i guess there isn`t much difference in endings themselves, because they work mostly like slide-endings from fallout. But your journey may and will be different with different decisions on each playthrough (but it isn`t rogue like, just non linear).
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Very old school text-based adventure, challenging but with intriguing world-building and a sense of reward from unpicking the many tangled mysteries in the story. The pixel graphics really suit the format, and have the feel of tattered, yellowed old treasure maps. I liked the soundtrack a lot too. It felt really fitting for the atmosphere the game is building, and each bit of the map had its own motifs that really conveyed the personalities of the locations.I felt frustrated at times when I couldn't think of the right input or wasn't sure what to do next, but there's not actually much in the game that you can fail so badly that you can't progress at all. I think I got lucky and managed to achieve most things in my quest list and got an ending that didn't feel bad, though I was playing with no time limit, and for how long it all took me, I am certain I would have struggled on a higher difficulty. If you need a lot of guidance in a game, this might not be suitable. But if you like that old school style of having to really work at figuring things out for yourself, this could be a really satisfying game for you.I felt like the vibe is kind of like a cross between Disco Elysium and the Witcher books, both of which I like a lot, so I'm saying that in a complimentary way.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game.  A well-written text-based RPG, and maybe one of the best I've ever played.  Beautiful pixel graphics and a subtle but engaging soundtrack add depth to the nuanced story line.  You definitely want to go into this game blind the first time, as the initial experience is part of the beauty and joy of a good story-telling.  Like any good story, you'll still want to re-visit it and re-tell it from time to time, and the latest updates included with the 1-year anniversary have made the story even better for the next re-telling.  Bravo!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: A very nice game. Slow however still exciting. Simple yet rich. I'm a fairly seasoned reader and the writing is not at all unbecoming, but rather impressive although its modesty. Lately I've leaned towards less intensive games, making the gaming experince a more restful one, and this game suits that need really well.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like you will either be enraptured by this game or drop it as soon as you realize what exactly it is. Its reading, a whole ton of reading, weighing options, more reading, time management, reading, item gathering, managing relationships, and its all wrapped in even more reading.I love this game, and how its story allows you to go about your day as you see fit with so much freedom for a text adventure game. The start of the game is rather unfriendly as you don't have many resources and many people do not enjoy outsiders, but give it some time and you will be able to make your own way in the treacherous lands laid before you.I struggle to have anything truly negative to say about the game outside of a few instances where I felt there were not enough varied dialogue, and I feel like sometimes there are just too many questions to ask, and quite a few scenarios where not asking a question can block you of from something almost completely unrelated, so ask as many questions as you can, for the most part.Apparently the game has quite a few grammatical errors, but I didn't notice them till my friend pointed them out, and it didn't detract from my experience at all, and the weirdly written speech of the accents improved it.This game is definitely a Niche, but I'm so glad I stumbled upon it. Highly recommended to people who can stand the massive walls of text.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: This game is sad, funny, and achingly beautiful at times. It doesn't hold your hand, and it expects you to closely consider how you see and understand what you're reading. I love it. I understand that it may not be for everyone; the premise of a text based game in this day and age places it very much in a niche, but it has good music and excellent writing.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like Roadwarden is the perfect introduction to the text-based genre of RPGs for people who haven't played them before. It's simple enough and has *some* visuals to the keep the casual user engaged, while also delivering a compelling narrative and immersive atmosphere. My one and only criticism is that there is a lack of meaningful choice when it comes to dialogue, so talking to characters can sometimes feel like an exposition dump. Ofcourse, there are moments where how you choose to conduct yourself actually matters, but it's less roleplaying a personality and more like "what do I say to this guy so I don't have to earn his trust by doing chores instead". Overall, an easy 8/10 if you're into narrative-driven experiences and don't mind reading.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: This is my favorite game of 2022.  It's really special and I cannot recommend it enough.  An incredible care put into the scope and stakes of a low fantasy setting such that you always feel like one small traveler, while still conveying the larger scale motions of the world as a whole and making the things you participate in mean something to that whole.Also i really like when people in the game are astonished by seeing a horse for the first time.  Constantly delightful.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: A very good text adventure with pleasantly tight resource management to prop it up: mistakes are not unforgiving but not free of consequences as well.Character creation choices affect your playthrough in a meaningful way, the way you interact with other npcs matter and time limit that restricts your entire adventure helps with pacing a lot.If you're not afraid of reading text and like a good adventure, you are unlikely to be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good text-heavy adventure game. Not really an RPG in the traditional sense, as the progression is more about inventory management than stats. Really nice UI/UX, relaxing music, good writing. Took about 7 hours for my first playthrough. Three starting "classes" and a large number of "ambitions" are available at the start, as well as several ways of resolving the major quests, so there is some replay value.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: What a perfect game. The type that gives you the tools to chart your own path. Essentially a story book game with great music and good art. Amazing script and dialogue that allows you to visualise events clearly. Likeable characters that you feel attached to and want to help. Awesome conflicts and encounters with an amazing main story line and side quests that make you feel proud after completing them. I didn't expect to find interest in such a game but Roadwarden really drew me in. Loved it. Asterion you bastard, you were a hard one to find.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting misteries. Great roleplay without relying on cheap "hats" for your PC. First playthrough will be relatively short if you're playing one of the timed dificulties, but it incentivices replayablility.Overall a great take on text-based adventures that understand how to be more than white text on a black background.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: A text based, great immersive indie RPG. Cheap and great play over a weekend.    4/5+Music and Sound are great at carrying the tone and environment it wants. Whilst there's maybe less variety than i might want whats there will keep you in the spirit of things.+ Lots of good world building and lore if you look for it.+Seemed to be a great deal of freedom in how you go about things. you can play a psycho brawler and be treated as such, but its completely up to you and there is rarely a perfect solution to any problem-/+ Old School RPG. (This is a + for me, a - for others) Its entirely Text based with very few visuals. It wants you to be reading and paying attention. take notes (only a few are taken for you) and use your head, you will not have an objective marker or guide beyond its very quick tutorial. -Some might find it a bit shortIf you want a RPG that lets you experience being A Ranger in a fantasy setting, this is a pretty decent choice.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy a good roleplaying experience with rich and fascinating worldbuilding, you will love Roadwarden! With a relatively simple premise and simple pixel graphics, Roadwarden manages to weave a deeply evocative world full of real people and real danger. I've never had a text based rpg capture my interest so entirely!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a charming style and beginning that can enchant you, but very quickly the numerous cracks start to show and there really isn't all that much under the hood. Skim through the other negative reviews to get a good idea of the problems it has, others have pointed them out well. Plus, some aspects of the world, quests and their presentation are unreasonable to the degree of easily dispelling the suspension of disbelief crucial to enjoying any work of fiction.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: This game has incredible depth to it... I am blown away by the sheer amount of writing that must've went into it.  It's full of interesting secrets and requires a bit of planning and strategy to be successful.  At the start of the game, you're given a 40 day time-limit to try and accomplish your goals of exploring the peninsula (with hopes of establishing it as a colony for your home city). The difficulty lies in making good choices, choosing who you ally yourself with, managing your time on foot as you travel, and taking calculated risks.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic. There is no grinding, and it avoids the issue of so many text based games where you just click all dialogue options with no consequences. There is no "Perfect" ending, and so each adventure can end differently and have interesting paths and outcomes. Saving is easy and so is loading, making it easy to get into and step away from.  I highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Scratched a retro itch I didn't know I had.It's a very pleasant adventure game-♥♥♥-visual novel with a lot of replayability if you go into it blind, due to a number of different decisions (which do, in fact, matter) to make and people to please (or displease).This isn't a crapsack world, but it's not a happy high fantasy one, either. The woods are dangerous and  growing more so by the day. Tightly knit villages are doing everything they can to survive, and the Roadwarden can aid them, or try and steer them from a questionable path.The casual attitude toward queerness and gender was really refreshing for a world that comes off as pre-medieval, with a pseudo-Christian church slowly absorbing Pagan communities.I love the pixel art but it almost makes me wish the soundtrack were equally retro. The relaxing acoustic guitar occasionally got repetitive but was atmospheric and pleasant enough that I wouldn't call it an issue.Highly recommend for visual novel readers and fans of very retro PC gaming.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very good game. although it is not always intuitive or satisfying. I enjoyed the level of effort put into the narrative, as well as the detail. However, it probably could have used some more thought put into the convenience/intuitiveness of the gameplay. It's not easy to describe, but some situations could've use at least a little "hand-holding" ease of access.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Text-based games live or die on the quality of thier writing, and Roadwarden is just... so full of life. The worldbuilding is delightful and strange. Characters are interesting and varied. Choices have consequences, both in gameplay and narrative that affect your game long after quests are completed. There is so much reactivity to your choices, your relationships, your chosen backstory and class, and your inevitable failures that the outcomes you end up with feel cathartic. Actions have consequences. This story gets dark, characters betray and manipulate and struggle to get by, and the roads are never forgiving of mistakes. The growing pressure of the shortening days forcing the player to cut corners, take risks, and make the most of their time in a world that punishes you for every mistake is a mechanic that makes every action matter. This world is harsh--but what good you choose to do isn't insignificant, and even your failures feel fleshed out and earned.Nobody has what it takes to be Roadwarden.Doesn't mean you shouldn't try.SPOILERS BELOWThe last few days of this game were perfect: uncovering the fate of Steep House was one of the most gratifying moments I've had in an RPG, slowly piecing together a decade-old tragedy that shaped the peninsula and continues to haunt its people. Being dragged out of bed and beaten in Howler's Dell after betraying Thais was shocking, and losing Howler's as a safe haven so late into the game almost butchered my run. And then, finally, on my 39th day, assembling a crew to find Asterion... only to learn that the last thing he ever did was break his own legs with a rock so his shell wouldn't wander. Oof. Ough.Wright, I love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: In stark contrast to other text based generated content the crafted nature of how the game evolves, and integrates the RPG elements into your experience along with world (peninsula) development is very well executed. While  a fan of RPG games I usually commit to one character and make it my iteration of canon, however for this story I am very keen to explore it via different RPG elements.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: No reservations recommending this. Highly recommend if you're tired of the constant nonsense we're being sold as video games these days.Restarted once, completed on my second play-through and will be starting my next play through tomorrow, undoubtedly there will be more play-throughs required to find out all the secrets. If you want a musical representation of this game, watch David Bowie's 'Blackstar', it feels like it was made for the game world. Just buy it. You won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Received as a gift from a friend.Good game. Well written and designed. Pays dividends to be attentive to details.Very text heavy, so be prepared to be fully immersed and devote time solely to it. However, I found myself getting over the volume of text once I really got into it. I was also surprised by how slowly invested I was getting into the world of Roadwarden too! By the end of the game, I was kind of left feeling wanting for just a bit more, but I think the length of the game is very satisfying.The beginning was a bit difficult but once you start clearing some quests, you'll get a lot of money that will smooth the experience and make it less stressful.Only criticism I have is that while it's great that the game rewards you for listening and being attentive to dialogue and other bits of information, it is also frustrating that you're relying on remembering that bit of info. A lot of the information can be synthesised which is great, but after you've had a long day and are jumping back into the game after a day or 2 away from it, having to remember something isn't what I want to do to unwind.Definitely recommend if you're into RPGs and are okay with those that are text-heavy.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely phenomenal game. Each character is incredibly well written, with unique interactions at every turn. The story is so rich and immersive, it's easy to get lost for hours in the lines of text that paint a beautiful and wild world in your mind. The game does not hold your hand, and will throw you into scenarios that you will be unprepared for, but always allowing you to escape with your life if you manage your skills and equipment carefully. As you answer prying questions from characters in the game, you write the back-story of your own character as you go. A unique features that allows you to really feel in control of the story, while still learning about it. All in all, the game is incredible. I HIGHLY recommend it to anyone that enjoys reading or text based games, or RPGs in general.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: One of the only games that epitomizes the Perfect vibe of a lonely traveler attempting to carve out a safe existence in the unforgiving wilderness. The wilds will reclaim whatever you take, and it's your job to convince everyone that that isn't the case. Lovely writing & pacing--unlike some other text heavy games, I don't get bored or fatigued reading it (and I say that as someone who /likes/ reading). It somehow has the perfect amount of lore, questions, and conversations without ever trapping you in a hellish infodump. (For example, both Disco Elysium & Pillars of Eternity eventually made my eyes glaze over, as much as I wanted to/do actually like them. Roadwarden doesn't overwhelm, EVEN IF you're the kind of player to Try Every Question and wring out as much lore as you can before an NPC tells you to f off.) The pixel art is delightfully sepia, aged and simple but not /actually/ simple work. It's beautiful. This is a definitely a fantasy world that is long past its prime, and humanity struggles on despite not even really wanting to (except, they must, because they continue to survive). It's a good mix of challenging and forgiving; I'm not a very daring player nor a strategist and occasionally screw up, but I only died once or twice during combat encounters (and you get to try again). Eating and sleeping is very important in Roadwarden, and it can quickly turn into a vicious cycle of "not enough money to sleep somewhere nice or eat --> too tired to work for money." However, you CAN recover, and maybe even prosper. My warden is perpetually stinky and not particularly well-armed, but she's always fed and occasionally well rested, which is pretty good for a game where everything wants to kill you for existing. I love love love it and I'll take 10 more (except I'm glad there's only one).
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Very engaging text-based fantasy adventure with some immersive pixel art. Played it all the way through and got to a satisfying ending. It'd be great if there was an ironman mode where you aren't able to "save scum" (for those without discipline like me). Story is maybe a bit heavy on the exposition due to subtle differences of normal creatures in this fantasy world that need to be explained (horses are massive, people are shorter and more hairy, wolves and cats are more monstrous, etc.)
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most original, innovative games I've played in years. It has its frustrating mechanics, like the throwback "guess which word the dev was thinking of" text interface. But the story is compelling, the gameplay memorable, and the choices you make have significant, lasting effects. Well worth the $15 or whatever.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic and in-depth text based rpg with compelling characters and excellent story building. RPG elements are simplified but are well integrated. I could not put it down once I started and I'm already on my second play through. Would really recommend this to anyone who enjoys AAA RPGs like Skyrim and the Witcher series but in interactive novel form. One of the best stories I've experienced in a while!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, but it suffers from forced diversity that sticks out like a sore thumb. (I LOVED reading that one the characters uses "they" pronoun...LOVED it.) But honestly, not enough of a problem to give a negative review. The negative review is for the deletion of any criticism of said diversity, even if quite a bit of effort was made to be constructive and positive, rather than insulting, like it often can.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: It's like playing a game from the inside of a book. This game is a new step in the evolution of both reading and gaming, and I love it.Simple but wonderful artwork and music compliment a well-fleshed out world, with lots of mystery and interesting characters.I can't wait for the sequels to come from within this fantasy universe!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute masterpiece!- immersive story- dark gritty atmosphere- thrilling exploration- hauntingly beautiful music- relatable characters- choices matter- heavy decisions- believable world- simple but effective visuals- incredible replay-abilityThere are so many endings and outcomes, just finished 4th run and going again to discover more secrets!Would love a sequel/similar text-based adventure.A DLC with voice acting would sell like hotcakes.Memories of these nostalgic adventures is the new benchmark for future games. Thank you to the team for an unforgettable experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: The atmosphere, characters, decision making, music, story- all are so good that it is hard to put it into words! It has got everything you'd want from a text-adventure RPG including perfect art to establish the locations, great reactivity in the dialogue, and plenty of intense moments with tough choices. It's awesome.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: You've heard of walking simulators, now get ready for a reading simulator!If this game was a book, I would have finished it in one sitting, or as close to one sitting as possible. As it was, I finished it in like 15 hours spread across three sessions, one of which stretched well into the wee hours of the morning. At some point I would love to replay it and focus more on a different part of the North than I was inclined to on my first playthrough.The world is beautiful, imaginative, the characters are extremely real, and the writing is very good. It has a realistic/gritty fantasy feeling without being too depressing (well... I'm sure it's possible to make decisions that lead the world to an extremely depressing state... but it's not consistently depressing). The portrayals are thoughtful and sometimes endearing, sometimes exciting, sometimes philosophically provocative.Really awesome tabletop RPG + novel + choose-your-own-adventure book type feeling. I don't read novels super well these days, but I used to love reading fantasy novels as a kid, and it was easy for me to focus on the narration.Would love love love to see more content from these creators.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't finished my first play through but I would highly recommend. This is my kind of RPG which is more Roleplay then game. The story of this game is good but what I will say is that it has fantasic atmosphere mainly due to a great soundtrack. The actual gameplay is simple but because of your 40 day time limit you are really forced to optimize what you are doing. In addition the amount of story lines I have been able to do is crazy. I have like 10 quests! I would highly recommend!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: A treat scratching my itch for something between a really good book and a game. More freedom to explore a story than a book, but without sacrificing the narrative due to gameplay limitation. The game is quite simple, and is more or less an interactive novel, sprinkled in tidbits of resource management and decision-making, at time it can be vague, but with some effort taking notes and immerse yourself in the game world ( which is incredibly easy and fun, considering how well the worldbuilding is presented ) it can be easy to work through. The people in the world felt real, with their own struggles and drives, creating a magical story through the player's own imagination and the writer's masterful choices of words.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Been playing the first few hours of the game, I think this is an excellent deal for roughly $10 for anyone who's into CYOA games. Each class has their own advantages (Which can be used to essentially eliminate poor choices or avoid having to roll a dice), I do highly recommend people new to these kinds of games play the Fighter first because he will have the easier time with the combat encounters at first and those are the most immediate things that can ruin your run. However my brief time with a Mage play-through has been interesting just to see how differently you can play the character with his additional resource of Pneuma (Mana in this universe).The world seems well fleshed out, though be ready to read as the journal is full of information which fills out as you play and engage in dialogue to get more information on subjects, history, individuals, groups, and wildlife. But I love the "frontier-fantasy" setting that they created for this.While not absolutely needed, it might be helpful for you to keep some of your own notes alongside this just for quicker reference, but this is mostly just to save a few button clicks. This is because some conversations will ask you for prompts to type in exactly what you're looking for, and particularly for character names they may not always be in your journal.Dialogue choices do matter, as how you talk to a person can determine how readily they are to share information with you alongside your actions, your religion (if you have any) can also play a role, and there are various options to approach people (and certain subjects will make certain people more icy).The pixel art is well made and gives good imagery to scenes with how much detail they put into it.Overall, I love the frontier-fantasy setting they created here, and barring a the occasional spelling error in descriptions the writing is very well done. Definitely recommend for any classic RPG fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally leave reviews, but this game I felt was truly outstanding. Its a nice sweet text-based adventure where you are a roadwarden, a person hired to travel around an area because the roads are often too dangerous for people to do it on their own. It did an excellent job of describing the world, in both its unfamiliarity and harshness. Your actions have consequences, and it is so satisfying to see that your work as a roadwarden actually is making a difference.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Hands down my favourite text-based RPG. I'm amazed at how much this game managed to do with so little elements. The expansive, non linear narrative and the sense of danger and hardship made this game one I won't forget. I found it had a good rhythm and pace, despite being a relatively slow game.Well worth full price, it'd be a steal at a discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent text adventure incorporating RPG elements. Worldbuilding, characters, scenesetting, resource management, all combining to craft an immersive experience of being the new ranger-mailman trying to fix everyone's issues, make this peninsula slightly less of a hellscape, pet your horse, find where the hell your predecessor Asterion got to, become the land's axe-throwing champion and hopefully not die in the process.Also, the soundtrack is an absolute banger set of serene but distantly ominous fantasy tunes.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: An experience halfway between reading a novel and playing a computer RPG. I have little experience with such games, but really enjoyed it. Most importantly, the characters are memorable, your choices consequential.But many key tradeoffs are handled well, too. A good balance is struck between concise descriptions and providing enough of a sense of immersion in the world. The default time limit is also well chosen, giving you enough leeway that you don't feel rushed for most of the game, but closing the story before you can explore all the narrative threads fully (which would endanger immersion).One little nugget I particularly appreciated were the sleep sequences, in which your decisions are not about what to do, but what and how you recall about your past life.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a ton of fun. The writing is fantastic. The choices and encounters you can have are pretty interesting, intense or just exciting. As others pointed out, don't get this game if you don't like reading non stop. It's really nice to sit back and relax at night while playing this. The music is pretty grim but in a good way and you can always turn it off to crank silent hill ost's while you play if you like. Great purchase, can't wait to dig further in.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game. Great writing, music, atmosphere, world building....Just a thoroughly unique and memorable adventure. My only complaint (besides some typos that are easily forgivable) is that the author seems to really want to include homosexuality, polyamory, and trans characters. This is fine on its own, but there's complete acceptance of all of these by all characters even though the characters in the game are often cruel, xenophobic, tribalistic, religiously zealous, etc. It just felt kind of forced and immersion breaking to me.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Highly satisfying text-heavy adventure story with RPG-lite elements.Excellent characterisation and world-building, although at times the text could be quite dense. With some minor glitches, the story felt satisfying and coherent. Thoroughly enjoyed my playthrough. Would suit someone happy to do a lot of reading; perhaps less so players looking for quick payoffs.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say that hasn't been said- this game is simply the best choose your own adventure game I've ever seen. The setpieces are simplistic yet beautiful, the worldbuilding unique and dynamic, and the freedom to explore the world in your own way is astounding. The world comes alive with the brilliant descriptions found while exploring the Peninsula, and the character's dialogue feels real and engaging. I love this game, and I hope more content like this comes out from this studio.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: This game..there is "something" very immersive about just digesting through the text, having an occasional glace at the visuals which only shows general layout of the scene and the audio which plays in the background; that "something" is your imagination which pulling you into the game.One of the best solo D&D experience ever, packed in a little adventure bookish game, or both.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game that got me hyperfocused from the start. I fully finished one playthrough in only a couple of days but had the utmost fun with it! It also has insane replayability if you give it some time. The soundtrack is stunning and sets the ambiance well. I honestly haven't been able to find any game with the same mechanics yet that has me feeling the same way Roadwarden made me feel while playing. I cannot recommend it enough!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant, complex, demanding  writing. World highly responsive  to  choices you make. Very immersive.  A game  which you  start pretty  much as a  nobody, and end as...  many, many possible things. Most likely, a very morally  ambiguous and more or less efficient ranger of sorts. Best narrative  game  I've  played so far (apart  from Witcher 3 and maybe Mass Effect 2), and an excellent rpg. Oh and yeah, persuasion/haggling  are NOT skills in which  you  can simply pour XP, you have to use your own real life brain.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Fell in love with the game when the initial demo got released ~4 years ago. It is in some ways a streamlined modern RPG combined with RPG's or 80s - Its fully text driven, it has places where you have to actually *write* inputs, but at the same time every location has their own artworks, user interface feels responsive and for the most part - intuitive. The writing itself is rather wonderful as well, with various branching outcomes to the primary linear quest.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: This is just a magnificent piece of writing, and captures a sense of adventure and discovery I haven't felt since I was a young child reading every fantasy book I could get my grubby little hands on at the library, while carrying an unforgiving melancholy that resonates deeply with me as an adult. The picture Roadwarden paints is a harsh one, full of danger and catastrophic mistakes with steep consequences. The people of it's world are a wary, hardscrabble lot with well-deserved suspicion of some foreign agent coming in asking questions and doing a duty no-one really asked for, and the lands you find yourself exploring will gladly kill you and anyone else foolish enough to venture in unprepared, but if you stick it out and learn to survive it's dangers, and give people reasons to trust you, you will find an incredibly vibrant and believable world. The characters are complex and feel very human, and each settlement has a distinct culture, with it's own history, values, dialect, and goals. There are countless different leads on countless different problems to pursue, and most quests can be resolved in multiple ways, with multiple results, and while some people might find the 40 day time limit on standard difficulty polarizing, I think it really enhanced the experience. There simply isn't enough time to figure everything out and resolve every problem, and while this can lead to some very harsh outcomes, it makes the things you *did* take the time to dig into feel that much more significant and real. (Just like real-world roadwork, the final boss is ultimately the deadline.)Across the board, this game is very tightly woven. Nothing feels like an afterthought, and progressing in one area of the story frequently and organically leads to new options and revelations about other parts of the story. Each settlement's history and goals are tied up in everyone else's, and even seemingly minor characters often wind up being tied into a whole bunch of other story threads. The worldbuilding is also very deliberate, and very well-researched, taking heavy inspiration from medieval Europe in a way that manages to feel fresh and grounded rather than cliche, with a really wonderful amount of attention paid to everyday life in the middle ages, whilst putting a fresh spin on classic fantasy monsters and carefully considering how their existence would realistically impact daily life. It also provides the opportunity for you to define the history and culture of the region your character comes from in a very organic way when characters in the game ask what your home is like, which I think is a brilliant choice for a game where the player character comes from a set location and exists in a fixed profession/role.10/10, would improve the lives of those I touch in small ways and acquire a found family to the detriment of the world because I am a mere mortal with finite time and non-negotiable obligations that prevent me from saving the world from massive, complicated, systemic problems again.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Deeply engrossing, well-written and richly atmospheric text-based RPG. Immense feeling of choice and customization plus the depth of the small, but intricately detailed world play remarkably well together here.  Immersive experience, slick pixel art, solid music.  Very glad to have purchased this title. Woulda been a steal at twice the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Great story and atmosphere with interesting characters and excellent writing. I thought I'd dislike the (able to be disabled) time limit, but in the end I'm glad that I left it on, as the increased tension gave more weight to my choices and reinforced the limitations of a single character's influence. The soundtrack is also great and was often stuck in my head. I played nothing but this game until I completed a runthrough. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: A great text-based RPG that rewards you for exploring thoroughly, thinking critically, and writing down notes. Playing it feels like reading a Forgotten Realms fantasy novel, except you are the one deciding how the story will unfold, because you control the protagonist.In terms of gameplay it's similar to text-based RPGs and point-and-click adventure games from the 1980s and 1990s, but with better visuals. In terms of content it kinda reminds me of Planescape Torment crossed with Fallout 1 -- there's more conversation than combat, the game has a time limit, and when the game is over you get to see what happens to each of the settlements you discovered based on your actions throughout the game. I left the game running a few times so my hours on record are inflated but there's easily 30+ hours of content in this game if you take the time to resolve every quest and explore every location. I loved the game so much I binged it over 4 days, and would definitely recommend it to others.However one consideration I will call out is that less than 13% of players have the achievement for finishing the game -- presumably because many don't have the patience to play/read through so many hours of text -- however if you enjoy reading and you've made it this far in my review I'm confident you'll love Roadwarden. For only $11, why not?
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome. You're met with an interesting, dangerous land to explore and peculiar characters to meet from enigmatic druids to down-and-out former soldiers. I'm not a much of a "roleplayer" but while playing I found myself wondering how my character might react in certain situations. It's challenging and even tense at times, with a backing soundtrack and ambience that fits the world nicely.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I wish that there were inexhaustible amount of games like roadwarden. You could tune in to one and then get lost in its new world. I am amazed how expressive it gets while implementing the most superficial UIs and static pictures. Makes me pumped up about making video games. Unique and rewarding. So if you- the reader- could make a game like this. Go ahead, I would play it.Indie games gets higher and higher standing among other video games. There is a lot of independant talented people makes delightful games. This is one of them. I recommend this to anyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't sure if I would enjoy this sort of game. While I sadly don't, this was certainly the right game to try for this. The writing is excellent, the mechanics simple enough to interact well with whatever scenario the writer comes up with and the limited visuals reminds me greatly of reading fantasy books. Many things are never shown, like the omnipresent "beasts" but you can imagine them all to well from the vivid descriptions. The entire game is very stylish and feels wellmade. The introduction is pretty good as well, I didn't feel lost most of the time. Even the replay value seems rather good with three very distinct classes that so far had quite alot of unique interactions and stuff. The only faults I could point to, is that some interactions/ places can flow confusingly and timed quests being really really obnoxious. "Hey, we go hunting in like 9 days, be sure to be here then." Like what? I guess it's fine, you can traverse the entire map in like a day, but still, this is annoying.For me this really doesn't work as a video game as i often feel powerless, unable to plan ahead or "play better" in the moment, while simultaneously giving me far too much freedom and control to be engaging as a story, but I suppose that is simply a personal incompatibility with the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best  tekst-based RPG I ever played. Immerse players in grim story of Roadwarden (kind of Witcher but without powers and super equipment). Game is linear, but you can do things different ways, depends of your profession and character you want to be. Graphic is very basic but together with music , makes game very climatic. If you like novel type of fantasy games , this one can be a good choice.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those "I'm recommending it for fans of text adventures...but..." reviews. Fortunately so far, the worldbuilding and charcters are all interesting and I like the mechanics- they remind me of the Lone Wolf books I read as a kid. My one complaint is the Steam deck support is lacking in the controls section. And if youre reading it, wouldnt it be better to be able to read it on the Steam deck like youre holding a book?Review-I'm old enough to remember the days of Infocom and Magnetic Scrolls and all the other graphical and non graphical text adventures out there. Its really is a lost art - text based adventures are impossible to find nowadays as most people just dont seem interested in reading. And, I'm one of those people who doesnt own a TV or watch movies - I only read and play video games. I love reading, and I read the way people watch media -if I'm relaxing and not gaming I'm reading. I love Roadwarden so far. The only thing I wish is that the Steam Deck support was better - it works, sort of, as the controls are very finicky using the touch screen and controller mouse. It would work better if the pointer wasnt so slim and the "hitbox" for the text options were better. I dont want to sit at my gaming PC and read. I want to curl up with my Steam deck like its a book. And I cant. Which is the only thing thats prevented me from playing this game as much as I want to. I either get annoyed sitting in my gaming chair reading on my giant monitor, or I get annoyed at the finicky Steam deck controls and wander off to read an actual book or play different games. So Devs - this is my one complaint. I love text adventures but can you tweak the controls so its easier to use on Steam Deck?
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. I think I must've got one of the better endings. It's pretty short but for a ~20 hour text-based RPG, Roadwarden's narrative, characters, role-playing, music, and general atmosphere punch pretty far above it's weight. It loves to wear it's influences on it's sleeve and that's awesome. I think if this game was the new standard for text-based games a lot more people would play them.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best story driven games I have played in a while.The story is not forced upon you, the player must venture forward and discover it for themselves. The player is provided no map, locations are only revealed when you see them with your own eyes for the first time. Some locations and settlements can be missed entirely during a playthrough. Some places will be often referenced but shrouded in mystery. Until you see a settlement yourself sometimes you only have rumor and speculation.The characters in this world are unique and have their own motivations or bitter memories. Information is not given freely as an entire group can live and die in isolation.This is not a game that can be completed in a single playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: If you want to feel like you're huddled alone by a campfire, surrounded by beauty and danger on all sides, play Roadwarden. If you want to feel the ache of those long miles on the road, the brief comfort of stopping in a place where no one quite knows you but they're willing to open their doors just long enough to give you respite from the cold, play Roadwarden. If you want to spend blood and sweat clearing paths through the brush, building bridges (some literal, some otherwise) between communities, where no trust is freely given but it can be earned by the hard-working and open-hearted, play Roadwarden. Basically, play Roadwarden.It is one of the most unique RPGs I've ever played. Highly recommend "easy" mode to remove the time limit so you can explore the peninsula at your leisure. I finished one playthrough and immediately ran into another to try to discover secrets I'd missed, earn the trust of characters I had only just met the first time around, and just to get back on that wild, lonely road. Beautiful soundtrack. Beautiful writing. A place you'll carry with you long after the epilogue rolls.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutley fantastic! This game would just not leave my head even after playing it through twice already. I love the writing style, beautifully brought to live with the simple graphics and sound design. Every character you encounter has a believable motivation for their action. They have reasons to trust or distrust you and I found navigating the politics of this world incredibly satisfying. Many games promise that "your actions will have consequences" but I rarely found it as true as in Roadwarden, that will show you them all play out down the line. I am amazed how well Roadwarden manages to offer this complexity without overwhelming the player or ending up holding my hand through all decision. I can´t recommend this game highly enough!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I've just finished the game, and now I sit empty and sad, and don't know what to do.This speaks to the strength of the art, no doubt. But you know how you feel sad that a great story ended, and want to go back, and immediately start a new playthrough? It's not like this for me with Roadwarden. I'm sort of glad it ended... but also would want to have a chance spend just a little more time in the game to uncover all of its mysteries.There is a timer in the game. A final countdown for the entire game. It's a default mode. You could also choose to turn it off when you start. I should have done it. In the end, I didn't have time to finish a couple of main quests.But it was okay. I reached the ending. And I've done a lot. Actually, you could finish the game right after the start. Roadwarden gives the player a lot of freedom. Everything in the game is optional. I think, I had wrong expectations. Maybe, overhyped a bit. The game was compared to Citizen Sleeper and Dysco Elysium, two of my favourite games. Roadwarden does have many things in common with them - it's a narrative emotional RPG with no combat. Just choices.It was good, but just a bit unaligned with my tastes. Just a bit too much exploration at the start (yeah, I'm one of those rare gamers who love RPGs but do not like exploration). Just a bit too hard for me to read text (English is my second language, but I'm quite proficient with it. But not enough for Roadwarden, it seems). A bit too distant of a view. A bit too few ways to develop relationships with some of the characters I would like to do so. Roadwarden is human. It does no shy from portraing generational trauma, religious intolerance, alienation and mistrust. Also, kindness and warmth, friendship and loyalty. It's mysteries are vast, and well-presented. Places feel dictinct, and their denizems are varied.It has some interesting game design elements: you have to manage stats, such as being clean and well-fed, which reflect both in narrative and the way you can overcome encounters. You can choose a way you talk, from threatening to pitiful which affects how others percieve you. You can have many currencies besides actual money - it's not like many of those you meet will have any use of coins in the wilderness.The main progression is tied to gaining trust. You gain trust of a character, they agree to give you more information or to provide some service.Where the game stands out for me is in two different areas.One, small human moments. At one time a tough character asks you of a permission to ride your horse — something they have never done before. Another time, when you have gained the trust of another character, and they let you stay at their home at night, when you wake up, you can choose where to sit. I know it doesn't sound like much, but such small touches let you express yourself in the game, and have people react to that expression. These are quiet and very well written moments.Two, big mysteries. Something happened 10 years ago. What was it? You see ripples affecting the entire game map, and you feel very good when the dots start connecting.Overall, I'm glad I played Roadwarden. I'm a bit sad that it's not 100% for me, and I'm a bit more sad that I didn't answer all the questions I wanted, and I don't feel like I'll play the game again, at least soon.Still, an adventure worthy of your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Wow is there a lot of reading in this game. It's practically a choose your own adventure book. But exploring this strange peninsula and getting to meet it's inhabitants was incredible. And my heart breaking and bleak ending was something special.This game is all text and none of the things that most videogames have. Brilliant words though.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: What to say about this game? The world, the lore, the choices you face and their consequences, the freedom to tackle problems in a variety of ways and express your personality through your character, all of it is so well done and so incredibly captivating. My first playthrough took 15 hours, although I plan to play again with a different class. The class you pick, and the choices you make about your character do have an impact on your experience. FWIW, I thought that playing as a mage was a good choice for a first time character. The magic is helpful (especially healing) and although you don't start with great weapons, it's not difficult to purchase better gear once the game starts.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR in case you don't want to watch the video:1. If you hate reading text or would prefer a fully voiced game, then this is definitely not for you2. Aside from the heavy text reading, the pixel art, world, storytelling, and emergent mechanics are actually really great!3. Fans of classic text based RPG games would definitely love this - its basically the same experience but enhanced with better QoL features and much smoother RPG stats and emergent mechanics like weather, time of day, your current status, and even your appearance and personal hygiene, all affect your interactions around the world.4. Be warned this game can get tough and unforgiving sometimes; but such is life on the unforgiving roads of the north.I would only recommend this to players who enjoy a story rich / story branching experience, and don't mind lots of reading!
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: AAA games have their own problems these days, and I foolishly seek refuge in indie games...only to have discovered time and again they have just as many flaws - albeit different ones.It really is an equal and opposite issues situation, although I do pay much less for indie games, so...What I find is that indie games inject artificial difficulties...I guess to keep up with AAA games?To show we're too cool, and don't make no easy games, man!?I do not know.I only know that like Darkest Dungeon, I was supremely frustrated with what would otherwise be a perfectly fine - if not a great - game, ruined into tediousness by some artificial standards.In this dumb indie game's case it is:AppearanceYes, dear reader, if I do not wash or mend my clothes regularly, then people will not have anything to do with me, and I am in a soft fail loop not knowing how to fix it.I was low on life and rest, and suddenly NO inns would rent a room to me.AND it cost me a LOT OF RESOURCES to clean 1 or 2 points.Up until this point - I was actually enjoying these games as they resembled the excellent Lone Wolf series of books from childhood.Indie Game Developers: THERE IS NO REASON FOR ARTIFICIAL, CRUDELY INJECTED DIFFICULTIES!THIS DOES NOT MAKE YOUR GAME "COOL"!A well-balanced game is good - not something like "appearance" as a stat which affects EVERYTHING!Also, the main character stupidly gives away the REAL reason for his mission - essentially to pave the way for his merchant city to conquer the free-region.So, secret, secret, cannot tell anyone, only hinted at even to the player THEN:"Yes, my city sent me to provide information and contacts to directly control this area not claimed by other great powers."I felt like I was watching The Phantom Menace with characters simply announcing to enemies, passerby and the audience key and secret motivations.Ultimately, this game could have been great, but an amateurish obsession endemic to indie games set in and ruined it.Not worth the time.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Roadwarden is incredible. Last night, after having my eyes glued to my screen for almost nine hours, I checked the time. It was 5 AM. I felt tired going to bed. The thoughts of all my long hauls in Roadwarden swirled. I slept peacefully. I woke up realizing how odd it was - the effect this game has on you. It's something you have to experience for yourself. Roadwarden deserves to be remembered for the ages.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. It should be known and played by more people.The world is very fleshed out and alive, works with or without you. After all in the normal settings you are only to stay there fro 40 days.The atmosphere is grim, the dangers abundant. Everyone will ask for something in return for anything. Caring only for yourself is a strategy, but good people are everywhere and helping others can help you in return.Just hop on the saddle and explore.The only drawback I can think of (for some people, it wasn't a drawback for me) is the amount of text you have to read. Some clues are not marked anywhere else and you need to carefully remember (or take notes, this functionality exists in the game) what people told you in case it won't be marked in your journal or map.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: An intimate (and sometimes oppressive) storytelling experience that delights in building a compelling narrative at the cost of traditional gameplay elements. True text-based adventures such as Zork are a relic of the past, but Roadwarden attempts to lightly modernize the experience for those nostalgic for it. The game features useful user features where it counts, with helpful icons on the overworld map and a well-populated, yet not over-saturated journal. The writing is good, playing to its strengths by focusing on the setting and atmosphere, with characters feeling like they're a natural feature within the peninsula's sordid landscape rather than larger-than-life personalities.The game has delightful pixel art, but chooses not to depict any of its characters. The game lets you decide for yourself to embrace its forceful difficulty on its terms, or set your own through an extremely generous save system. You'll no doubt become familiar with the handful of tracks that play throughout your adventure, but much like the game itself, it does not overstay its welcome. The topics addressed by the writing did an excellent job of addressing darker themes and difficult choices, without souring the experience by trotting out unnecessary gore or sexual violence. For those weighing the value of the game, I would encourage you to buy it if you would similarly find value in a dark fantasy novella. Roadwarden achieves its clear objective in that it focuses primarily (both through pixel art and through its textual descriptions) on the places you go and the path you take to get there. I encourage all interested to try out the demo, as the opening hour of the game presented there is an experience that sets the tone, but flourishes further throughout the full game.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: The game is incredibly fun, and extremely addicting. It's mostly story based, but it does have a sweet and simple gameplay loop that keeps you moving through it. That being a moving around between settlements and ruins to heal, repair, eat, and sleep. My only real complaint is that I wish there was more content. A sequel or DLC could do this game nicely.The story and setting is also extremely solid, along with being unique from most fantasy settings. You can very easily take this whole setting and turn it into a unique DND campaign. (Any DMs, take note)
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: The game offers a really well written story based CYOA (with restrictions).It's surprisingly very polished and well thought out, I especially love the sierra "Type out" what you want to do, for certain puzzles, instead of being multiple choice, etc. It reminds me of my childhood, sitting in my room, reading books and turning the pages, and immediately turning them back because I didn't like the outcome. I'm definitely really enjoying this, and will continue to.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing text based adventure game, extremely relaxing and intriguing. I've just finished my first playthrough after near enough 14 hours, but I still know there is a lot in the game undiscovered. The choices you make and the paths you choose shape the attitude of the people within the world. I would highly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys investigation, planning and exploration games.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: I was a little hesitant about this game because of the minimal 2D graphics and large amount of reading, but I'm very glad I gave it a chance! In fact, I played the game twice so that I could complete more of the quests and get a better outcome for the land. The characters are well-written and the world is pleasant to explore and discover.What I feel is especially unique is the game's balanced sense of urgency. One has to manage completing quests, exploring the peninsula, solving puzzles, staying well fed, keeping enough money in your pocket, and staying safe, all within the 40 day time limit. It is difficult to achieve all of your goals, but at the same time it is not overwhelming.There is a lot of reading when you get started, and it takes a while to get a handle on all the names and places, but unlike others I did not feel that I had to keep notes: the in-game journal was sufficient to keep my head straight. Once I had gotten familiar with the basic mechanics, I had a hard time keeping myself from the game, and the reading and minimal graphics felt like no hindrance for enjoying it.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Very interesting story based game. Fun text adventure with replayablility.  You pick your class and go adventuring along the roads. What you do often effects the world you inhabit.  There are things you can only do as certain class too, which encourages multiple playthroughs of the game. The graphics completely fit the style of story telling and gameplay.  This is tied with Sunday Gold as the best new game I've played this year.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: An enjoyable game, did one playthrough so far, with the time limit of 40 days and as the warrior. It's well written and an interesting setting. Not a lot of points where you have no idea what to do next, except a few, but those make sense to be more difficult as well. One negative is that some names don't get saved in your notebook, and some do, and some don't but then do later. So when I had learnt the name of a person earlier, I couldn't find it back when I met them at a later point. The archive was already too far along to be able to read it back as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Roadwarden is a realistic, hirstorical game with matured characters and marvelous sparks. I'm still impressed by this game. It feels more like a world, a story you participate in. I can't expres my enthousiasm enough with words written here. What I can say is that it became one of my favorites beside Gothic (2), Fallout (NV), Hades & Slay the Spire. I'm under impression of the authors erodution, imagination and yet a narrative approach where he lets poignant darkness exist beside grounded fantasy.Check his world out in google, it's named Viaticum (from Aureus). I'm awating new series and hoping for a new tabletop rpg to overthrow the prevailing modern stuff. Stay authentical and keep the good work up.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Chill experience but the writing is very rough. I didn't feel that there was coherence to the characters and world. The fantasy aspect is very front-loaded without any thought. There are so many monsters they describe in one scene with no consideration of the environment that breaks me out of the setting. Dialogue feels stiff and the descriptive writing is overdone, less is more. Tolkien can get away with 3 paragraphs of describing a forest because he actually sets up a good scene.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Without a doubt, it's an insanely immersive adventure, and all the little graphical elements almost make you forget that this is a text game - with events vividly appearing in your mind. I can still see my character standing there, shirtless, boots half immersed in the swamp waters, axe in hand, facing some kind of mountain lion; bleeding, dirty, but determined. And yet, Roadwarden suffers from a pretty major issue which holds it back greatly: there's a time limit, and it's rather tight. I hold this somewhat unpopular opinion that time limits aren't bad per se - they can add a lot of tension and additional strategic layer in which you need to consider your options very carefully; but they need to be well communicated and reasonable. Here, the limit is well communicated, but I don't think it's reasonable at all.To keep it short: I played the game with the foreknowledge that the time limit is tight, tried my best to minimise pointless travel, always acted with intent, was mindful of my resources and chose my goals carefully. And even with all that the ending I got wasn't one I'd call good; I simply didn't have the time, or even visible means, to complete a pretty crucial quest.Now, you could say, what's the problem? Just replay the game, go straight for the important goals, choose your options better, etc. And to that I say: no. And that's for a very simple reason. (the game allows you to replay it, that's not what I meant)Think about it. For all the clamouring about replayability, whenever people talk about their most potent experiences with a game, they usually say "when I first saw X..." or "it blew my mind when I realised that Y". It's simply not the same when you're doing it again, it can even feel like you're being dishonest, since you - the player - have knowledge that the player character doesn't. This argument might feel nonsensical in the age of wikis, roguelikes and social media, but there still are many, many games that are straightforward stories - and Roadwarden is one of them.And what a story it is. It really manages to suck you in; your dialogue choices matter, your decisions affect the world around you. Your resources are limited, and so is your power. You need to maintain your health and hunger, but also the state of your armour and even your hygiene. Wash yourself in the river, maybe brush your teeth if you bought a teeth cleaning set, or perhaps pay for a bath in the village? But it's so expensive. Anyway, you need to wash off the blood on your face, and your clothes are torn from getting through the thicket, better visit the tailor.The worldbuilding manages to avoid being your generic fantasy with some cool twists, such as the fact that human bodies just kind of rise on their own after death, as if everybody had a dormant zombie virus from birth. Horses are a rarity, and your equine companion is often seen as a curiosity by almost everybody; the previous roadwarden used a big lizard as a mount instead. Also, you often get asked about otherwise unseen parts of the world, and whatever you answer will be treated as true for the rest of the playthrough, that's pretty cool.But what's really golden about this whole game is that it really feels like an adventure through an unknown territory. The closest thing I'd compare it to is a pen-and-paper RPG session, where you truly feel like anything can happen, and everything is so viscerally real. The quality of the writing is excellent, too; it has this rare quality that comes from being written by a non-native English speaker who managed to attain the mastery of the language the hard way (the writer is Polish).There's a lot more to say about Roadwarden, but I think I've said enough. The time limit is a grievous wound on an otherwise impeccable experience; luckily, you can select easy mode which disables it - and I suggest you do just that, pride be damned. Or simply be prepared to play more than once. Either way; if you don't mind reading in games, I can easily say that Roadwarden is very much worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Basically a young adult-level CYOA book with tons of illustration, dice rolls that don't get over-used, and sensibly succinct prose.You are a roadwarden, a job that spends as much time in the saddle as it does in danger. Although keeping roads clear is part of your work description, you're really little more than a lawfully-sponsored adventurer: You're to explore the paths of a wild peninsula and build a rapport with its isolated villages to make them malleable to the suggestion of foreign commerce. You have 40 days to gather a report and make vital connections for the investments of the merchant guild that hired you. How you spend your time is your own discretion, but it should always be advancing your goals in some way. There's always things that need doing, and it's up to you to adequately prioritize them.There are choices both banal and important, with equally polarized consequences. Items and equipment to collect, some of which offer utilities to make your travels less weary and others that have no readily apparent usage, and encounters to face with varying degrees of assurance. Do you use your meager savings to invest in a paper lantern for help with dark and dangerous places, or treat yourself to a teeth-cleaning kit that will help you make better impressions of trustworthiness on people? Do you sell an old bronze axe head you found for some quick and pivotal wealth, or keep it while looking for a handle so you can turn it into a new weapon? Engaged with a saurian beast, do you prefer to keep an eye on its tail in case it whips at you, or do you pay attention to its maw to be sure it won't bite you? Decisions aplenty across all kinds of interactions. Some correct, some incorrect, some pointless either way, and some based on chance.Ultimately however, a playthrough won't be difficult. It's very easily save-scummed and meta-gamed, especially going through it subsequently. But if you go blindly with the flow, through good and bad, the narrative will immerse you in ways that haven't existed since the MUDs of yore. The characters you share drinks with, the questions you ask each other, and the struggles your journey drags you through will feel like more than just text on a screen.It takes all the engrossment of a good book and applies it to an interactive medium. And for practically  the price of a decent paperback book? It's hard not to recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best RPG I played in 2024 so far, and I'd say it should be on any top list of RPGs for people to play (as long as they are willing to read).Let me tell you what brought me over in totality:You are a Roadwarden sent to an untamed land where your duty is to help out distant villages and to keep the roads safe while you are also You can choose if you're a warrior, scholar or mage (and maybe something else I forget)You have to explore the whole place with basically zero knowledge, and you have to get the local scoop from the people you meetYou can infer a lot of extra information by just paying attentionBut one of the best features is that sometimes you don't get a text choice you instead get a text prompt option, like in old DOS games. Like "What are you looking for?" and then you type what you want to see. It's not always there, only in specific scenes.The thing that made me recommend it, is that in one of the settlements you get a chance to use this text prompt it asks you "Who do you wish to look for?" and I basically exhausted all the usual options, like leader, smith, merchant, church etc.So I'm thinking, what else can I even ask and i look at my Appearance stat (your cleanliness + clothes):I'm dirty as ♥♥♥♥, so i need some cleaning to be presentable to the people of the land. So I type in"maid" (because I forgot how you call a bathmaid)This ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game put me on a sidequest to become a matchmaker for villagers because of that promptas two villagers (one of them a *maid*) are looking for a spouse.
_childDocuments_.name: Roadwarden

_childDocuments_.review: Roadwarden is amazing game. It's very slow, but in a good way. Deeply atmospheric and well written.After completing it today in 19 hours. I got few suggestions for the Developer and (heavy spoilers) Why I didnt like it.So first suggestion: Since there is many places and characters, it's sometimes a bit hard to follow who everyone is. Pillars of eternity 2 had a system where highlighted names could be hovered over and had a little information box to remind you. I wish you could add something similar.Second suggestion: The "find a correct word" puzzles were fun, but sometimes extremely hard if you don't find certain right word. I would often understand what the Developer was trying to hint at, but just could not find the right command. You could maybe give a bit more hints, or make the right command a bit broader. It's not fun if you have to google what your supposed to write, after it takes too long to figure it out.Alright spoilers time:I would really hope to see a sequel in the future. There is couple of rough things that could be still polished with the story and couple of mechanics, but that should be fairly easy to fix. I could swap my review to recommended when the endgame is a bit better addressed.TLDR; Great game, but story and mechanics could still use a bit polish.

Playing as a Roadwarden in a medieval world, I was captivated by its rich narrative and strategic elements. With its high replayability and immersive storytelling, "Roadwarden" is a must-play for fans of narrative-driven games.
