No money mean no need extra map size.4. Music kinda bad for me.Play again next update.
_childDocuments_.name: Nebuchadnezzar

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing experience close to nostalgia when playing Nebuchadnezzar because it is very similar to Zeus or Pharaoh with a few new features that makes it even more interesting such as being able to move stock around, have a view of production chain and its efficiencies index, ... Great work by the developing team!
_childDocuments_.name: Nebuchadnezzar

_childDocuments_.review: I'm enjoying the game. I'm through 6 of the campaign missions so far. Pay attention to the tool tips and understand how the range of workers, buildings, and distribution works together and you'll be booming. I'm not a super big city builder genre fan but this one looked cool due to the setting so i gave it a shot. I recommended it a friend and she will start it up soon as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Nebuchadnezzar

_childDocuments_.review: Cool Game, will continue to get better as the developer keeps adding more things to the game.  I bought it maybe 6 months ago and continue to check in when new things are created.  A bit different than the sierra city builder games you just have to be cognizant of how you set up your city.  Hopefully looking forward to military and other things being built in future.  Can't get people to move into my villas at this time
_childDocuments_.name: Nebuchadnezzar

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent city builder. Reminds me a lot of Caesar 2. It's challenging and rewarding, has good music, and I love the art style. I do wish I could just zoom out enough to see the whole edge of the maps, I would rather see black space around the board instead of having the view locked to the playable map edges.
_childDocuments_.name: Nebuchadnezzar

_childDocuments_.review: i was watching someone play the game and got hooked by the soundtrack, let me tell you something, its amazing! its clear that the developers were highly impacted by caesar3 , its basically the same game but better, because they already had the tamplet for the game they invested more in the facts, story telling, history and really managed to capture the that ancient era and make it really interesting to read and learn about human history, i never write comment on game but i could not ignore the amazing soundtrack and very informative history lessons which corrilates to the upcoming mission, its great, and very refreshing even to veteran ceaser gamers. i really recommend the experience and looking forward to see what will come next.
_childDocuments_.name: Nebuchadnezzar

_childDocuments_.review: The Historical info in the game is great. Very much like TiltedMill Children of the Nile ; ) A few things i dislike which makes the game challenging, Warehouses take up 9 squares, and barely hold any stock, ugh 36. fml and space is very limited. I shake my fist at whoever makes the maps, you ♥♥♥♥. Definitely makes each map a real puzzler on how I'll make this work. Trade is very important. Also Warehouses and Market placement, zoning , again you ♥♥♥♥♥, it makes for a good challenge. Over all good strategy builder game. Try it.
_childDocuments_.name: Nebuchadnezzar

_childDocuments_.review: I was feeling nostalgic and wanted to find a game that "played like Caesar III". I can confidently say, Nebuchadnezzar vastly surpassed my expectations. Caesar III was a lot about fitting lots of buildings clustered around housing. Nebuchadnezzar improves upon that formula by making the challenge less about what is right next to your housing, and much more about how you can set up effective logistics networks while fitting it within limited space for building. I had to restart a couple of maps, but did not mind at all - it felt like a rewarding learning experience.One thing to note: do not ignore early requests for firefighters, healers, or guards. If you do, you can get caught in a loop where they are literally putting out fires instead of preventing them, causing more fires and making it difficult to recover. Mind your civil services!
_childDocuments_.name: Nebuchadnezzar

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best city-building game I have ever played.  And I've been playing them since the mid 90s.  First, it has zero bugs and doesn't lag when cities get too big; a common problem in city building games.  Second, it focuses almost realistically on the economy.  You have to balance resources, labor and capital, or like in real life, the civilization can collapse.  Trade is also very important in this game.  Unlike other games where trade is just for extra income or "prestige", in this game you cannot grow without trade, just like real life.  I saw other comments complaining about "why can't i produce certain goods and can only obtain it through trade?"   Like dude, that's the whole point of trade.
_childDocuments_.name: Nebuchadnezzar

_childDocuments_.review: Walking into this game, expect to be hand held A LOT. Now having played dozens of city builders in the past, I thought that I could "wing-it" and wack the tutorials hand away. Unfortunately, my attempts building a city resulted in a mass fire, and with the King asking for my beheading to be effective immediately. I took five steps back and went through the hand-holding, although I hate it I was able to fully grasp the vital functions of the game, and the most important in knowing how to prevent fires from turning everything into ash and cinder. Although the game does require some more polish on game-play. The music, art and sound effects are fantastic, but those alone cannot hold the game together if the complex planning mechanics aren't smoothed out.
_childDocuments_.name: Nebuchadnezzar

_childDocuments_.review: City Buildings simulation in the early stages of mankind.Similar to Caesar and the like.The UI is not bad (might need some tweaking here and there, but is already quite fleshed out). Updates are coming in rather regularly. Devs seem responsive.Overall quite enjoyable game. And for this price tag (especially during a promotion) there is not much you can do wrong (unless you dont like this genre of games ;)).Works fine with Linux (Manjaro)
_childDocuments_.name: Nebuchadnezzar

_childDocuments_.review: I've only been playing for a little bit into the campaign but I'm loving it so far. It's doesn't have as much personality or polish as Zeus or Pharaoh, but it definitely scratches the itch of the classic isometric city builder. It has some nice QoL improvements over the other titles though, especially in terms of available economic statistics and walker logistics. It's gotten great support from the devs post release too. Though I'm glad I waited to buy because it seems it wasn't quite finished when it was first released, but it seems to be in a stable, well-balanced, and fun to play state with the current release. I would definitely recommend at least giving it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Nebuchadnezzar

_childDocuments_.review: You can build your own temples = 10/10.I wish there were more buildings that you can build this way and more customization to them as well. Like world wonders.I haven't played enough of the game to tell if these temples give any additional bonuses to your city, I seen it has been mentioned like prestige but I am talking more about crops yield, less fires, etc.An idea: during construction you would choose certain parts which if combined give bonuses, for example, if you need some education bonus then build chambers for teachers and scientists in the temple.
_childDocuments_.name: Nebuchadnezzar

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great. A good 2D isometric management game like pharao and caesar series. And also a good educative campaign who teach you the history of the fertile crescent. It's really pleasant to play. I'm eager to see what Nepos Games will release in further years. Buy this game if you like Pharao and Caesar, you will not be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Nebuchadnezzar

_childDocuments_.review: Classic city builder in which the known problems of classic city builders are all solved with micro management. It does not dethrone Zeus as the top dog but is a solid game, especially in the later campaign levels or free play.Remarks:1. The biggest problem is that war and walls are not in the game (which is quite tragic since the walls of Uruk deserved special mention in the Gilgamesh epos), which made my cities always sprawling monstrosities with multiple separate centers. (there is no incentive to make it fit in a wall)2. The start of the campaign is also more of a puzzle game than a city builder, since the levels are tiny and the problem is how to fit everything. 3. Once you first balanced your budget a given level is also essentially solved. So don't expect hard challenges. 4. There are three different social classes that work different jobs. Especially the fact that the social classes in the higher tiers depend on each other makes it more interesting than older classic city builders.
_childDocuments_.name: Nebuchadnezzar

_childDocuments_.review: Very good little city builder, which is based on a classic gameplay for this type of game.It's stands out by its period choice (mesopotamian) and its possibility of custumizing the templesbulding.The old graphic style gives a little retro side to the game and i like it even if it's not to everyone's taste.However some contents are missing out but the devs team is very active and they are even patching the gameby adding some features, that's pushing me to put a positive remark to encourage them.To conclued for me it's a good relaxing city builder with a great future to come.
_childDocuments_.name: Nebuchadnezzar

_childDocuments_.review: If you ever loved Zeus or Pharaoh in your youth and want to go back to a good old isometric city builder and enjoy that kind of nostalgia love, that game is right up your alley, and will give you everything you need. It even comes with new ideas and quality of life elements that will make the experience great. The extra elements come with a bit of difficulty however, so just chilling while playing it isn't going to work. You'll have to use your brain !
_childDocuments_.name: Nebuchadnezzar

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a absoulute recomendation! It is not really as easy to progress in campain as earlier games in same gengre but after a reconsider I realize that it acctually is totally fine by me. First levels is close to "puzzles" where you acctually dont have a million ways to progress in campain. The best with this slim way forward is that you will have to learn a certain machanic before going forward. Example: If you dont have food to supply every household for a advancing voctory you could always stop delivering, make them leave, fill up wherehouses and advance by a city developement boom later on? =) Later maps seem more free and every map gives more content and things to consider in building the perfect city. Trade pollution (I guess noice?) and appealing is added quite early (its where Im now!) but one of the most challenging stuff is distribution from industries/farms to warehouse to markets. Also a complete new thing for me is a feel of a moore slim budget. The whoole "overproduction stuff" does not always forgive you in this game. Every guy working has a salary and my absolute best advice is not trying to hold down unemployment. Popoulation will come and go over the years and its not economically holdable to give everyone a job just because they move in to the city. If you overproduce bread and milk it will only cost you extra salaries and from Ive experienced, very unalike earlier games, you have to sack ppl and give up industries (or just deeactivate) in order to make a balance of economy. Here its not about making everyone working =) Who knows - criminality and riots might show up in later content but 40% unemployment will decrease when people leave the city? =) But as for every Pharao lover Id say this is a very much recomendation! Pharao, wich is close to unplayable today (the jumpy move map thing makes you eyes tired) has been given a newer version. Ofcourse this is more of a hanging gardens and ofcourse its a updatet version ready to attract both older and new fans of the gengre? Its good looking, has nice music and has a content and complexity that thrills me to get further into the game. Its also a smooth progress with a good tutorial dercribing every new content in a good way before starting every new map.My best thumps up on this one!
_childDocuments_.name: Nebuchadnezzar

_childDocuments_.review: I Am Loving it Brings Back the Sierra Games Feel with Enhanced everything. Still adding features, a coupleof things missing to make it even more enjoyable but defently once you get the game mechanics you can really grow your city. No Pressures its a relaxing city builder. Brings back childhood memories.
_childDocuments_.name: Nebuchadnezzar

_childDocuments_.review: Old time with Faraon, Kleopatra and Cezar come back !First rule of scenario maps --> do everything to get trade as soon its possible - without it.... you are done ;)I do hope for mutch bigger maps for endless mode (scenario) in future, because If you wish have all buildings on map - you soon out of place ;D Devs work hard on game and are helping as well if you get problem! Nice to have this game - and if you remember old Cezar times its nice memory bringer :)
_childDocuments_.name: Nebuchadnezzar

_childDocuments_.review: What exists in the game is pretty good. However this is not a finished game. It is pretty clear there are a ton of features they are still slowly developing for the game and adding. At launch it didn't include a sandbox, for instance, meaning the campaign was the only way to play the game. It is a bit fishy they came out of early access in this state.That said, what is here, is pretty fun. It's an old Zeus/Cleopatra/Rome type game and scratches the itch nicely. I just am not going to play it for a year and see where it ends up.
_childDocuments_.name: Nebuchadnezzar

_childDocuments_.review: Unique and fun economy sim game I could sink a lot of time into. City builder with a heavy focus on managing resources, logistics and trade. Amazing to see the free-play and bigger maps in the latest patch, campaigns are challenging and this opens up the game a whole lot more. Looking forward to what they bring out next, would love to see a tech tree and more maps.
_childDocuments_.name: Nebuchadnezzar

_childDocuments_.review: Very clearly a game by Pharaoh fans, for Pharaoh fans. While it can feel quite bare, they've managed to simplify and transform the formula a bit. With control over your walkers' routes (no more "forced walkers" for me!) and no fire, collapse, entertainment or religion, the campaign levels end up as quite streamlined and chill logistics puzzles to get to the monument building and objectives. The production and trading views make setting up a steady system surprisingly easy (well, when things go wrong you know it was your own fault), and the custom monuments are fun. So I'm happy to see this game, happy to have bought it, and am looking forward to more content, scenarios and mods!The later levels need more types of industry, so the challenge becomes setting them all up, in sufficient quantities, without running out of money. Often you'll need to rush a monument to get prestige and unlock a trading partner in order to generate a steady income. But the lack of disasters and the ease of keeping your city in a steady state (such that you can always speed it up as you wait for something to accumulate) keeps it pretty chill.
_childDocuments_.name: Nebuchadnezzar

_childDocuments_.review: 8.5 out of 10.0! I can without any doubt in my mind advise to grab this game if you enjoy these sort of games. It plays so much like Pharaoh back in the day but offers a few changes here and there to give it its own feel. It’s based on a totally different area so don’t expect those we’ll know pyramids. The game is actually pretty challenging I’m about three missions from the end and it gets harder and harder to more you go in but when you beat it feels so good! No sandbox here that won’t be until the next patch. All in all grab this game it’s a total steal for the price it’s at now. I have encountered ZERO bugs all user based error. Step learning curve for new folks.
_childDocuments_.name: Nebuchadnezzar

_childDocuments_.review: Not for linux users. First time I ran it around launch, I experienced multiple display issues (artifacting, if you can call it that on 2d...).Now I revisited it and it got fixed, but quitting the game crashes my entire x server, forcing me to reboot.This is a botched launch for linux. Maybe in a couple of months it'll be game worthy. Don't buy it now unless you've got free time to QA their product.
_childDocuments_.name: Nebuchadnezzar

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. Its easy to get into and playing on the harder levels can be challenging: dealing with irrigation, logistics and having a positive income.  The historical setting, artwork and music are nice too and make for a chilled experience.I found the game pretty addictive and entertaining to the point where I got all the achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: Nebuchadnezzar

_childDocuments_.review: Really good. Vibes are reminiscent of Pharaoh/Emperor:RotMK Sierra Studios nostalgia but with unique features and definite improvements to the supply chain mechanics that were sorely needed in those old classics. It looks good, but I will say this is a case of "gameplay outshines the graphics". Personally, I am a fan of the isometric 2D format for city-builders and while this game does give me a little to complain about (sure, I'd love higher resolution textures and more animations, and I miss the old SS games's walker verbal blurbs) the gameplay is what I am here for and it does not disappoint. The campaign is all there is at the moment, but it is solid. I like the historical background that previews each mission, and the tutorial was both short and sufficient to get you rolling instead of needlessly holding your hand the whole way through.The biggest surprise is the soundtrack. It just... fits. After 24 hours in game, I can feel it starting to get repetitious, but that is because I've essentially listened to the OST 24 times in the last few days. The ambient sounds of middle eastern bazaars and the lute and vocals are all excellent and help build the immersion.I can't speak to challenge level (I'm a scrub casual gamer who usually plays on "easy") but although I've restarted a few missions after realizing my massive city was critically malfunctional (I find it easier to start fresh than to try fixing messes), I have kept the game on its higher difficulty level (easy-normal are the choices). The difficulty is determined by import/export prices and the labor demands of your industries.TL,DR If you liked Pharaoh, Emperor or even the old Caesar series years ago, you definitely should consider picking this up. It's right up your alley.Edit: as of 3/8/2021, the devs have announced they are adding several features, including sandbox and something I missed from the old Sierra Studios games: walker voiceovers!
_childDocuments_.name: Nebuchadnezzar

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: I'm very pleased with how the games is getting updated! Would really love to get a new campaing to experience all the new stuff in a progression mode :) +  classical city-building experience, just like Caesar III and Pharaoh +  beautiful 2D graphics*+  relaxing experience, no rush+  Tetris city builder style gameplay +  game runs (nowadays worth mentioning) -  lacking military management and complexity -  no sandbox mode (promised soon) -  *the sprite resolution is all over the place + no upscaling support resulting in blurry images when zooming in or out of the default position (tested on 1920x1080 and 2560x1440)For me, this is a quiet and relaxing game where I honestly just build pretty cities. Don't expect much more from it. The mechanics are simple and easy to understand, and most mistakes are easily rectifiable.  The lack of any threats (apart from running out of space on the map) makes this a game for more casual play where you just don't have to worry much, or plan. This is not inherently bad as some of the "hardcore" gamers would lead you to believe, but if you are looking for a challenging city building with multiple layers of management, try something else. Overall, I'm enjoying the experience, especially after studies or UN Doom Eternal challenge runs ;) In the future, I would love to see the developers expanding their vision for the game and I'm looking forward to any new updates.
_childDocuments_.name: Nebuchadnezzar

_childDocuments_.review: Loved Pharoah / Cleopatra. This is more of a Sim City than a Kingdom Simulator. I miss the groups and tiers of building types. Aka Water supplies, multitude of house tiers, proximity effects, military, walls, guard posts. Festival squares, all of these add character and influence design in these games. While there may be some of what made the past games great. There could and should be quite a bit more depth in all systems. All in all having a great time playing, worth the $20 to see where they take it.
_childDocuments_.name: Nebuchadnezzar

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game only to people who like History and the beginning of civilization in Mesopotamia. The developers took good care to include nice info about that period from well reputed data sources, so this is a great way to learn history. Since the game is simple, I´m eager to see future DLCs of other contemporaneous civilizations, such as the Indus Valley, or Egypt. May be even farther civilization beginnings, such as China or Norte Chico. On the other hand, as a City building game, this game is way subpar to others with similar price and more content, it is 2D-only, not-pretty, simplistic in the bad way, not-charming, with unnecessarily complicated mechanics, and it doesn’t give a good sense of achievement.
_childDocuments_.name: Nebuchadnezzar

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed the old Cesear and Pharoah games this is for you.Revised, game does have some quirks, I would still recommend it if your a fan of the style. My biggest complaint would be the range of the warehouses, it's far too short and then you need to take up more tiles to have good transported around the city. I think it would be far better if the shops and workshops would just go to a warehouse that has what they need instead of having to have a close warehouse and having goods transported all around the city.
_childDocuments_.name: Nebuchadnezzar

_childDocuments_.review: If you remember fondly Cesar 3, Cleopatra and Zeus, the Nebuchadnezzar is the game for you! Similar look and gameplay, but improved in just the right places (like workers paths and monuments). If that is what those guys can do on a just released game, I'm more than confident that in the years to come we'll have a true gen in our hands. In the meantime, I'm just going to sink hundreds of happy hours in Nebuchanezzar!
_childDocuments_.name: Nebuchadnezzar

_childDocuments_.review: Yes i would recommend this game, but i have concerns tho.i worried its going to end up like banished, no updates, no DLC's, it will all be about MODS.ATM i find the game unfinished, for a finished game where we had no early access.There are no scenerio's what so ever, the is no SANDBOX MODE ( free play ), just a tutorial.Unable to rotate the map, maps are to small.But even with all that i love it, back to basic city building, i just was expecting to much from this, got my hopes up to high.Good job Dev team, all i ask is that you accualy keep on top of things.
_childDocuments_.name: Nebuchadnezzar

_childDocuments_.review: Game is rather good. Similar concept to Pharaoh and Caesar 3, has some new stuff, and reduced stress level. Economy is at beginner level, monument building difficulty reduced comparing to Pharaoh, tough house building and evolution is a little harder to achieve and maintain. Lacks of sandbox and scenarios. Id say this game is worth its 20$ price. Looking forward to updates.
_childDocuments_.name: Nebuchadnezzar

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up playing the caesar/pharaoh/zues series and i was excited to see someone taking up the mantle. However Nebuchadnezzar is not able to measure up.it missing many things from it like firewatch or this you buildings don't break , also all the relics things like temple and co missing , the music and theathre are missing . so i was looking forward to it, but yes hmmm unsure now about the gameIt lacks character and feels very basic. Granted i am not fully into the campaign but the story missions are slowly paced and have goals that take quite a long time to accomplish. That coupled with a very bare bones economy mean that you can leave the game running and walk away with no risk
_childDocuments_.name: Nebuchadnezzar

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really loving this game so far. It has the feel of a late 90's and early 00's city builder, it actually contains historical information and it is incredibly satisfying and relaxing just creating a city set in one of history's fascinating time eras. I do have to add, because I have seen some negative reviews about this issue, this game's focus is not on conquest, you can not make armies and invade other cities, this game's focus is on city building.  I personally love it so far and everyone interested in building and maintaining an economy rather than just fighting will certainly be charmed by this game as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Nebuchadnezzar

_childDocuments_.review: There are a few weird things, like water being required for T2 houses when milk is required for T1 houses (I believe it should be inverted).There are also a troublesome features like the logistic and job priority which require too many clics and can be annoying.But overall it's cool game, and a great base for future improvement.
_childDocuments_.name: Nebuchadnezzar

_childDocuments_.review: After 4 hours saying u recommend a game is maybe soon but I like it as a whole.Of course it reminds of the old impression games.There were complaints by people it was way too easy but for me it is really not that easy.I have fun with it and hope to have many hours of playing this game in front of me, modders are already busy with this game and more content will be added soon.
_childDocuments_.name: Nebuchadnezzar

_childDocuments_.review: The game is still missing a lot of content, feels more like an early access gameThere are too few poduction chains and they have at most 1 manufactoring process in betweenDecorations are very basic only The campaign maps are very small and the game is way to easy even on normal. For me it was as if the port is just a money printing machine. Never struggled with laborers or productivity, and people move in just about everywhere instantly so you can just spam houses if you need more people.And most of all i dont get why you need to build a market just to then deliver the good directly to the people. But as it seems Amazon is everywhere now ... even in the past.All in al i see the potential of the game but it is just not there jet. I dont know how many of you know Emperor: Rise of the Middle Kingdom but Nebuchadnezzar fells like a stripped down remake of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Nebuchadnezzar

_childDocuments_.review: Nebuchadnezzar is a classic isometric city builder game inviting players to experience the mysterious history and culture of ancient Mesopotamia. In the campaign, players get to rule over influential historical cities filled with magnificent monuments.

name: King Arthur: Knight's Tale
detailed_description: Our brand new King Arthur game is OUT NOW About the Game You are Sir Mordred, the nemesis of King Arthur, the former black knight of the grim tales. You killed King Arthur, but with his dying breath, he struck you down. You both died – and yet, you both live. The Lady of the Lake, the ruler of the mystical island of Avalon brought you back to end a true nightmare. She wants you to go on a knightly quest. She wants you to finish what you have begun. Kill King Arthur – or whatever he has become after she took his dying vessel to Avalon.. A Role-playing Tactical Game Experience a unique hybrid between turn-based tactical games and traditional, character-centric RPGs! This dark fantasy version of the Arthurian mythology invites you to manage a team of heroes on the dangerous battlefield, while also engaging in moral choices, hero management, and the rebuilding of Camelot. The dark fate of the kingdom Explore a land of nightmares where vile monsters and magical creatures lurk within castles and forests. The battle between Arthur and Mordred brought death, both of them falling at the hands of each other, and now the consequences unfold. Arthur, resurrected in Avalon, is now an undying mad king, his pain slowly turning this magical place into a nightmare version of Britannia. You are Mordred, brought back to life to find Arthur, and ultimately, kill him to end this accursed condition. The Round Table reborn Gather your knights and send them on quests involving deep, tactical battles! Assemble a team of heroes, selecting from six classes (Defender, Champion, Marksman, Vanguard, Arcanist, Sage). Level them up, gain unique skill points, equip the best items looted from missions. But beware! Heroes can die, and the treatment of their injuries, curses, diseases take time. Between missions, make sure that Camelot has the right facilities for recovery, and prepare different heroes for different quests. A question of loyalty Heroes are your main resources – but no mere numbers! They have their own distinct personalities, goals, rivalries (even unique traits, skills and bond benefits). They will observe your decisions closely! Settle disputes, grant favours, select heroes who can work together, send them on missions they are comfortable with. Tread carefully, because their loyalty depends on many factors. They can even leave and turn against you! The making of a monarch You, as a king, have a personality as well, shaped by your actions and moral choices. The Morality Chart will represent your status between Christianity and Old Faith, between Tyranny and Righteousness. Your choices affect values on this chart, influencing both gameplay and narrative. The weight of decisions Knight's Tale offers four different difficulty modes, from laid-back storytelling to the most grueling battles Avalon has ever seen. Those looking for even more challenge can also try Roguelite Mode. Here, every small decision matters – not only the moral choices, but actions taken in the turn-based combat as well. The campaign unfolds with a roguelite twist: no reloads, only regrets! The thrill of dealing with the consequences is half the fun, but your decisions also affect the story. Each playthrough can unfold differently, branching in unexpected ways. The end is only the beginning Play through the campaign (once or see multiple paths), and after that, you unlock the endgame, reserved only for the bravest. Tough new challenges appear on the map with mythic bossfights, random quests, more loot and character progression ultimately leading to the banishing of Balor, the monstrous god-king of the Fomorians. At release, King Arthur: Knight's Tale will be available with English voice acting, with English, German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Russian, Chinese, Hungarian text localization. We may add other languages later.

_childDocuments_.review: I am ahuge X-com 2 fan and this game has certainly scratched that itch whilst we await (HOPEFULLY) Xcom 3.It is great how it gives you choices and thus allows further play-throughs. I plan on playing this multiple times choosing different religions and behaviour and obviously upping the difficutly level each time.I find it exciting that it uses actual knights and i love the sound of the armour as they are walking. At present my only downfall is i wish we could keep more knights even if it was just a backup squad hate having to drop some and when they are gone they are gone.
_childDocuments_.name: King Arthur: Knight's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Great turn-based tactics. Despite its simple graphics, the game is captivating with its design, and it seems stunningly beautiful. The gameplay leaves only pleasant impressions, and hints of a further plot and game possibilities give me hope that a masterpiece awaits us.Unfortunately, there is very little content in the game at the moment (in fact, three story missions), and a strange message about what further we will see after the release. I hope that the developers will release periodic updates, and I will be able to complete the entire game in Early Access.I can't recommend it to everyone and everyone, because it's not a game yet, it's just a demo of the game, but heck, I just can't give a negative rating for this.It's worth noting that the game has problems, which is not surprising. One of them is the FPS drawdown in a village attacked by bandits. I hope there will be no more of them for release.In the meantime, I put this game on a par with Druidstone and hope to also have a lot of fun from it in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: King Arthur: Knight's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: I never review games but am an avid gamer.  I really enjoyed this one.  The story was great and the mechanics were well executed.  Highly recommended if you enjoy turn-based tactical combat with a new take an an archetypal story that remains true to the heritage of Albion, yet refreshingly devoid of the unnecessary and all-too-common social injections that increasingly tend to taint the gaming experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good tactical rpg. At first i thought game size was crazy high, then i heard it came down to that level from 100+ gb. Now its on a quite fine spot. There are a few loopholes in the game design, like you might be forced to not have any quest to go if you cnat manage your roster well - which means basically you will get stuck. But overall, combat is very well implement. This is what matters in such gamesthe most.Animations, visuals are decent. Quests arent boring. Characters have their own differences to feel unique enough. Even same classes have some differences here and there.No brainer. Very good game for its price.
_childDocuments_.name: King Arthur: Knight's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Would definitely recommend this game to anyone who really likes turn base games like X-Com, Rome Expeditions,Mutant Year Zero:Road to Eden, etc. Companions are unique, Story is Above average, Combat and features are also above average, Cool concept with the Castle building features and choices are what i really like about this game. If the Devs are reading this, please fix some of the maps having low fps specially the mission with Sir Yvain. I found a workaround by Turning off Anti Aliasing. Would also love to have a dedicated or keybind of "End Turn" for QoL purposes.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game, but it could've been better. The good part of KAKT is the deep gameplay. It's an absolute blast to manage your troops' injuries, make decisions that affect morality, distribute equipment, issue decrees, and build your kingdom. KAKT has all the makings of classic turn-based strategy gameplay; battles themselves are like XCOM but with far less luck (which is a good thing), while the base-building here is a bit less obtuse than in XCOM. Furthermore, KAKT has several difficulty selectors and dozens of playable characters, ensuring a fresh experience with each playthrough. As far as core gameplay goes, I have practically no complaints. ...The bad? Everything else. The graphics are dull and depressing. The music is dull and unmemorable, to the point that I muted the game and listened to Iron Maiden or Tesla instead. The story is a "subversion" of Arthurian mythos, but it's predictable, generic, and all the dialogue takes itself too seriously. Like virtually every other western RPG I've played, KAKT fails to craft a compelling or remotely interesting narrative. Take away the Arthurian names like Mordred or Guinevere, and these characters could've been from any number of 100+ dark fantasy RPGs. The setting and tropes have been done to death -- maybe some people like them, but these tropes do nothing for me. What I would've liked was a way to more easily skip all of the dialogue. I started zoning out towards the end of Act 2 (about halfway through the game) and just pressing the ESC key to skip dialogue. Even so, many lines can't be skipped for some reason. This game was made 20 years after Final Fantasy 10: have we STILL not learned that it's a bad idea to NOT have a cutscene skip button?Not only this, but battles themselves take too long because you need to hold the spacebar to speed up animations. Why is there no setting to AUTOMATICALLY speed up all animations? I loved the battles, so why not let me skip the fluff and get right to the meat and potatoes? Games like Warriors of the Nile or GBA Fire Emblem were excellent in this respect. If your greatest asset is strategic, snappy gameplay, then you should lean more on that crutch. During every mission, you also have exploration segments. These are entirely pointless, and take up way more time than they should. Characters move sluggishly, so it takes forever to get from point A to point B. You will often find yourself backtracking from point B to point A and then point B again. The exploration segments have almost no secrets to discover aside from a few stray loot pieces, which begs the question: why not simply GIVE the player this loot after every battle? What are you accomplishing by putting a chest at the end of the mission which the player can actually miss? Too many resources were wasted on these pointless exploration filler segments. KAKT would've been entirely better if the developers had eschewed these completely....Nonetheless, KAKT is a competently-designed and exceptionally deep strategy game. Again, the core gameplay mechanics are basically immaculate. There's a lot here for any fans of turn-based strategy. It's just too bad that KAKT put in so many obstacles to prevent us from enjoying its greatest asset.
_childDocuments_.name: King Arthur: Knight's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Great tactical-strategy game with character development (gear, skill tree) and city development (upgrading Camelot). Art direction is great along with music - really captures the tone and doesn't come off as a bright colored cartoon. Normal difficulty is probably too easy for people experienced with the genre (XCOM-like games). Later missions (beyond act 2) need some balance and some aspects need tweaking (AP and damage percentage gain). _childDocuments_.review: I changed my initial review because it turned out i am just bad and haven gotten gud. This is a good game that could be great if they changed a few flaws. - combat gets very repetitive. to little enemy variance and to little hero variance combined with a long game and lots of "grinding" gets on you after a while. If this game was only 40 hours long i would have liked it a lot more probably.- hero/knight variance is non existant and it's what turns the game really sour in my mouth. You get lots of different knights but they all share one of like 6 or 7 builds with the same skills sometimes a bit mixed up. Nothing is more disappointing than unlocking a mission to get Sir Galahad or Sir Lancelot and then realizing they do the exact same ♥♥♥♥ your random knight from the start of the game does. But hey they don't get leveled up either to your current average hero level meaning they are completely useless. At the point where you can unlock them your highest hero level will be like 12-14 and you get them at 8...- There are to many knights to get, to little space for them at your court and you can't replace old ones with new ones usually because new ones are always under leveled as ♥♥♥♥. Usually in games like this you can sacrifice knights to complete a mission and then a new one takes its place like in darkest dungeon. This doesn't really work here because if a mission is so hard that you lose a knight you will probably not even be able to complete the mission. And a new one can't take it's place because it will be to underleveled. This  could work if you could start a mission, let 4 knights do some damage, die and then mission saves the progress. But that's not the case. And since you only get missions appropriate to your level you can't really level up low level knights. You will have a core of 6, maaaybe 8 knights that are high level enough to use. But honestly thats already stretched the xp to thin. Better to just power level 6 and ignore anyone else. Considering there is like 20+ knights to get, that is a joke. If you at any point want to try out a new knight to see if you like him you are already wasting xp and the game will punish your for it 20 hours later when your main squad is to weak. But this can all be fixed preeetty easily. Add more variety to knight skills, maybe some enemy variety. Reduce difficulty in mid to end game and change xp gaining and start level for new knights so you can actually use different ones. Maybe add progress saving of some sort to missions so there is a point in having knights die. If they would fix these things i would give the game a 9/10At the moment it's more like a 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: alright I am writing this review as of 9/17/2021 during it's early access period so keep that in mindthings I Love about this game!1: the morality system is really cool, I think it could fleshed out more with more bonuses and other things added but if you decided to just leave it as is. It would still be pretty cool, I am also including the choices you make in this game here. I like how after every mission Mordred is forced to make a decision whether it be something as simple as building a couple shrines on the road to help Christian pilgrims, to one of your knights got pretty drunk and burned down a tavern. and these decisions affect your followers loyalty and your morality, be a rightful ruler who believes in the old gods of Avalon, or be a tyrannical christian king who burns heretics at the stake or vise versa. Each action has an overbearing consequence and I love it, the written dialogue in these is also really good and props on whoever wrote them.2: the story! I love the story in this game, the could have easily made it one of those cookie cutter lets slap ye old king Arthur in here and have him hunt down Mordred/Lancelot/the black knight as they reap carnage through Britannia/Avalon like is usually the case in most games about King Arthur but the didn't, the wrote a story about Mordred and made him the hero/anti-hero and the, at least as far as I am in this game, did a fantastic job he's a bit edgy and cynical but that's to honestly be expected. I like how a lot of the knights also have their own motivations and you guys stayed true to a lot of the original tales of king Arthur when writing them.3:the city building! I love the city building and how your morality meter above affects to a certain degree what you can do with it, for example if you go heavy into the christian faith you can unlock an upgrade that adds healing friars to the cathedral speeding up critical injury healing by 20 percent (at least I think it does something like that can't quite remember) I wish you could do a little more but it is just fine as it is if not.things that I wish I could see!1: some more customization would be nice, it would be nice to see the actual land, Camelot, heck even Mordreds armor being changed based on his morality meter. make him an old faith rightful ruler (which I decided to do) he has white armor adorned with symbols of the old faith, Camelot has great trees growing in it and banners adorned with old faith symbols. I would love to see something like that but wouldn't be too hurt if I miss it2: movments a bit janky, not a deal breaker for me in the slightest as its weird at some points but not annoying a little fix here and there could probably fix it 3: long as hell loading screen, like en garde why! but it's not deal breakingthings I wish would be changed1: Mordreds a defender class... ok but that doesn't really tell me anything, a tutorial on how a class works/what the do would be awesome but either its not easy to find that info or its not there, if you could do a short "hey this character is a defender class, they do this, this is how to best utilize them" when you first acquire them, that would be awesome2: ser Yvaine's dialogue isn't...great, his side quest is also a bit annoying as there isn't any explanation on how the big bads in it work so its a lot of insta killing trial and error, having him do a little spiel in the beginning of each fight would help for future runs, also his side quest is the only one that consistently crashed my pc, I have no clue why but it did it not one, not twice, but thrice and I had just about given up on it when it worked the forth timefinal thoughtsits a great game that needs some polish, and for an early access game it's pretty bloody fleshed out and glorious, I love a lot of the combat, love a lot of the mechanics and world building and can't wait to get my hands on the finished product!

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't quite expect to go on such a ramble when I set out to write my review, I'm outlining how game mechanics makes for a somewhat frustrating experience and that is difficult to do without context for how the systems work. There is a handy conclusion at the bottom if you can't be bothered to read it, i would recommend you read it though to understand why I recommend playing on normal.I find the game, okay.The gameplay is decent, it doesn't shatter any ceilings but doesn't bore me either. The balance is odd and doesn't feel good I find. It's the usual shtick where your characters and their health is incredibly valuable and the enemy act like their guys are expendable, they also play to hurt you.I'll elaborate: The enemies are coming at you to kill your guys, they don't care about their own lives. So hurt enemies doesn't play defensively, they don't run or surrender, they will do whatever they can to take you down with them. That isn't to bad on its own, no fun chasing down fleeing enemies. But it forces you to play very defensively, let the enemies come to you while you save up action points, remember that whoever spends action points on movement gets the fewest attacks. So you'll be setting up in a choke point and waiting whenever possible, your knights are powerful, but not much more powerful than the stronger enemies and there are ALOT of enemies.Which is an issue as well, the sheer amount of enemies makes cleave and AoE abilities invaluable, if your character doesn't have AoE you might as well not bring it.Now for my biggest gripe in terms of gameplay: Recovery. I understand that health is supposed to be valuable and any time you take a hit, it's supposed to be a minor defeat, but King Arthur: Knight's Tale doesn't handle this part well, in my opinion.Your knights have 3 types is health:Vitality, this only regenerates outside of missions and it takes time, lose all your vitality and you lose the knight.HP, this is a health buffer that you can recover during the missions and it will fully recover between missions.Armour, this is your damage reduction, it will be worn down as you take hits. A character with alot of armour will take no damage to his HP until the armour is well worn down, as it gets low, some damage will bleed over into HP or Vitality if no HP is available. Armour can also be recovered during missions.It is a solid system, but it is frustrating like you wouldn't believe to deal with because of the way you recover lost HP/Armour. The way you recover is by resting at campfires, these are one-time uses and you have a varying amount of them in each mission, usually 3. When you use a campfire, you can either recover 50% of lost HP or 50% of lost armour, whichever you chose is applied to ALL your characters, their individual needs be damned.This means that if you have a guy in heavy armour who has lost 4 of his 8 armour, you'd want to recover armour since no damage has bleed through to his HP yet.At the same time you have a rogue type character who has lost 3 of his 3 armour and 80% of his HP, he's almost down to Vitality and you don't want to take Vitality damage. Vitality damage causes semi-permanent wounds and eventually death.So what do you recover? the rogue guy really needs the HP, but it's going to disappear again very quickly since he's still out of armour. Or do you recover Armour since your whole team benefit from it, but your rogue will be in deep trouble as he has no HP buffer and his 2 armour is negligible, damage will bleed over into HP/Vitality immediately.It's a tough choice and while there are other ways to recover HP/Armour, they are rarely substantial. Healing Potions are good, but you can carry a maximum of 2 on each character and they are kinda expensive, come in limited quantities and you can't share them around during a mission, so when one guy is out of armour and starts taking HP damage, he'll be needing potions that you have available on other characters, but can't share.Right, so that was a ramble and a half, health recovery is limited, there are a lot of enemies and they will do as much damage to you as they can.Now for the kicker, the enemies will absolutely tunnel the weakest target that they can reach.So that rogue is going to draw attention like crazy, if you hide him and let one of your beefy guys hold the front, his armour will wear out and he will be just as squishy as the rogue and a prime target for every enemy around. I'm sure you can see the issue, now that your beefy guy has lost most of his armour, you have to hide him as well, or spend a campfire to recover his armour, but recovering just one guys armour is a waste. So you go into the next battle where you then hide the beefy guy and the rogue (not hide entirely of cause, but they hang back and only act where it's safe)."But if damage is such a drag, why don't you bring a tank or two then?" because of the kicker i just explained, the enemies will ignore him if they get the chance. Which is of cause smart, but it doesn't make for fun gameplay, i brought a character that does significantly less damage than a two-hander or dualwielder in the hopes that he could mitigate incoming damage, and he does not because the enemy prefer every other target but him.You can force them to attack him if you send him ahead alone so he's the only available target, but then he'll be surrounded and overwhelmed. Remember that there are A LOT of enemies and they all chip away at his armour and when that is gone, he's as squishy as the rogue. A little moreso even as his heavy armour is still limiting his action points despite having lost all defensive properties.I played the game on hard or the roguelike difficulty, I forgot what exactly they call it. Combat and recovery might be much better on normal difficulty, I wouldn't know. I disliked the story, world and characters so there wasn't much point in trying it on normal.I might just be dumb, but the story was a hot mess and the characters could really use some work. Everybody is undead, but everybody hates the undead, but there are also a faction of undead that are all evil and mindless and there are also classic undead i think which are like necromancer minions but mindless and not part of the undead faction.Mordred was evil, but now that he is undead and Arthur is undead, Arthur has turned evil and Mordred is still evil, but fighting Arthus is a good thing. Mordred does good things, but he constantly acts evil, like he does good against his will.And the character banter is some of the funniest ♥♥♥♥, well i say banter, it's more like spontaneous short monologues. Mordred, your main character, isn't required on missions and since he's one of those tanks that get ignored, why would you bring him. Since the main character isn't always there and there are a lot of characters, they can't feasibly make dialogue between group members. So it's just short monologues where characters will elaborate on their history, their dreams and desires and it is really strange and out of place most of the time.One of the characters sounds like a 90s TV-commercial in his delivery and suddenly blurts out "I used to get into all sorts of trouble chasing romance. But even after swearing off romance, i still get into a lot of trouble". Funny as it is, it really breaks any immersion you might have. He's one of the worse ones but they are all like that, suddenly, unprompted, completely out of nowhere, a character will just tell you about that time their dad was mean to them.In conclusion, the game overall is okay. Don't expect much from the story and the gameplay has some serious jank when it comes to health and recovery. I won't recommend the game, but if you are interested and the issues I've outlined isn't deal-breaking, then i won't try to talk you out of it. I would recommend playing on normal though and hope it alleviate some of the issues.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good turn-based RPG, and surprisingly high production value for the budget. (with actual cinematics for the intro as well as at the end of each act). Combat is quite interesting and the devs have managed to make each mission feel fresh in its own way, even if you've already faced that enemy several times. Actually mostly manages to avoid the "reverse difficulty curve" that plagues many turn-based games (not fully though, act 4 is arguably easier than either act 2 or 3 but that's still quite good)There are 6 classes but most knights have one or two unique skills which can make two knights of the same class play quite differently from each other. A few of the knights even have more pronounced differences (one Sage is much more offensive and less support-based than the class usually is, for instance) and thus a unique playstyle. On the other hand, there are admittedly a couple of identical knights, especially for the Champion class (3 of them have the exact same skillset, though it's not a bad one)One word about the "morality system": it's not one. It should be seen more as part of your character build than as an actual "morality system" that tracks your choices in a traditional RPG. Since there are heroes and various bonuses unlocked by pushing deeper into the "morality tree", the devs very clearly expect you to choose one side and (mostly) stick to it. I don't think it's a bad thing personally, but you'll be disappointed if you're expecting a more traditional alignment or karma system. On the other hand, your morality still has some impact on the game because there are a couple of side quests in the lategame that change pretty drastically based on your previous choices. A good reason to replay the game with different choices, especially since two different moralities will get access to a number of unique heroes which might change your playstyle.

_childDocuments_.review: **Update:I did my [below] initial review at about 30 hours in. Now I'm at 112 hours playtime (which is true playtime!) and finished with the main campaign. It likely won't take you 'as' long, since I took my time and did every side quest, etc. Simply put: this is likely one of my favorite games of all-time. It's also one with some of the most hours in my entire library. For me I can now say, confidently, that it was far more enjoyable than even the stellar XCOM games were. That's not too shabby a thing to be able to say! Filled with atmosphere & grit, story & lore, and stellar production values -- it never got stale for me. Attesting to that...I typically never, (really) NEVER go into endgame content -- I'm usually there for the campaign & story and then split...and yet here, I can't get enough and am in the middle of my first endgame mission.Definitely get this. For me, it has been wonderful. //ORIGINAL REVIEW: I am absolutely hooked on this game in a way that only XCOM 1 & 2 were ever able to do. I'm actually enjoy this MORE, however, as here it doesn't "rush" you to complete missions in a set amount of turns. I also was never a fan of having to build 'defenses' for my bases in XCOM...I mainly just wanted to focus on missions & outfitting my characters. I'm glad they haven't implemented either 'feature' here (there is some base-building, but it's not exhaustive), and thus they keep the experience more focused. The setting, atmosphere, story, and presentation are all stellar -- they absolutely nailed what it appears they set out to do here. I've seen some people mention the side-missions getting repetitive and boring, though I myself haven't found that to be the case. I've been on every one offered, and thus far the story elements differentiate them enough for me to feel intrigued. Even if they hadn't though, the combat mechanics are so fun that to a certain extent it doesn't matter. I'm 30 hours in right now, and am only 1 mission into Act 2. Each time I sit down to play this I can't wait to dive in...and I'm continually having a great time. Definitely grab this one!

_childDocuments_.review: (X-posted to my Wordpress blog, Gunlord500)Fantastic little game from an otherwise obscure Hungarian studio. It's a "grimdark" riff on Arthurian mythology and plays almost like a combo of Fire Emblem and X-COM. You play as Mordred, Arthur's bastard son who killed him in the original myths. In this game, it seems like Arthur has returned from the dead, but not as the glorious returning savior, but a demon corrupting the island of Avalon. So the Lady of the Lake revives Mordred and tells him to rebuild Camelot and recruit all the knights of the Round Table, who she also brought back from the dead after they all fell during the last battle of Arthurian myth (the Battle of Camlann). You do this by taking a party of up to four knights, who die permanently if their vitality reaches zero (though their HP stat restores after every mission) and whom you recruit over the course of the missions, into various stages/adventures. In those stages you can explore with the mouse cursor and click on things a la typical CRPG, opening chests or hidden objects for gold and loot, or interacting with people you can hurt or help, but when you meet enemies you engage in turn-based, panel-based battle where you spend AP to move and attack. It's simple but very engaging since your knights, as they level up, can get a very wide range of abilities ranging from whirlwind strikes to magic attacks to shields and so on.Aside from that, you then have the strategic layer, where you spend the money (and building resources) from missions on rebuilding Camelot to either get more equipment, better healing for persistent injuries your knights may suffer, or other bennies. You can also make decisions that make you good or evil (helping peasants is Righteous, killing them for their gold is Tyrant), and Christian or "old faith" (building churches makes you Christian, building temples to the old Celtic myth gods makes you Old Faith), and your decisions on both those axes can make your knights more or less loyal to you (influencing their performance in battle) and which of them you can recruit.The plot isn't fantastic, but it's more engaging than you might expect at first and you won't understand why Arthur became "evil" until you really know your English/Irish/Welsh mythology. It's also quite satisfying to both watch your knights level up and become more powerful, lead them in the turn-based battles, and make Camelot nice and shiny. The voice acting is pretty good, the graphics above average, and the music is okay, not great, not bad. Put a hundred hours into this and I'm very happy with it.Some critiques:The postgame/endgame, I am very sorry to say, is absolute garbage. I beat the entire game on Hard but set the endgame down to story because it was so boring and annoying. Just endless spam of the same enemies you've fought before, but with massively bloated, beyond all reason, HP pools. Incredibly tedious, though at least the new bosses are nice.In general, it can be very hard/annoying to click on the right unit if there are a bunch of them grouped together--you often need to wiggle the camera around and even then it's iffy to get the right one.Finally, the strategy portions of the game seem a *little* undercooked. It's fun rebuilding Camelot from ruins to a grand castle, but there aren't really any relationships you can build between characters or lore you can unlock, as in Fire Emblem. Some characters have special missions attached to them, which is cool, but after those missions there's no further development at all for your knights. Also, in keeping with the historical Round Table, you can only have up to 12 knights in your roster, but you can recruit so many it seems like a waste, especially since you can never bring more than 4 with you on a mission. It would have been nice for an upgrade, a la XCOM, for larger squad sizes, and also there should have been some stuff for your other recruited knights to do beyond fighting so you wouldn't have a whole roster full of "aspirant knights" if you don't lose many of your own.Still, these critiques aren't enough to take away from a very solid strategy game. Like I said, got a hundred hours out of this, so I heartily recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game about 10 consecutive hours a day, every day, for 8 days. And I would keep playing, if there was anything relevant left to do. So... yeah, it's .Its biggest downside is that it requires Windows 10 (I installed it just to play this and it literally destroyed my computer. Had to buy an entire new one, and it still dies on me  in the morning, forcing me to open the case and keep swapping GPUs in and out for an hour or more until I can finally get into Windows. F**k Bill Gates and his minions, I hope they all die in agony. I didn't have a  problem in some 10 years using Windows 7.)In King Arthur: Knight's Tale, you are Mordred -- king Arthur's nemesis. Despite being a natural born A-hole, you can still choose to be "good" or "evil."You'll take a party of 4 heroes into missions, and a fifth one sometimes joins you during them. You are free to select those 4 heroes from the ones you have available. There are many different ones to unlock, via missions and Alignment (you can be Old Faith or Christian, Righteous or Tyrant, with each path unlocking some specific heroes, bonuses, decrees and whatnot.)Missions are fairly straightforward. You walk around with your party in a fairly sized map, picking up some loot and killing everything in your way, until there's nothing left to kill and you win.Combat is turn-based, and it's pretty good. You have an Action Points pool that can be largely extended, as well as some movement-exclusive points to spend. The game does not trap you into the hateful "one move, one action" scheme.Heroes can be Defenders, Champions, Vanguards, Sages or Arcanists. Each class has its own skill tree, and there's always some difference in these skills between different heroes of the same class.The skill trees are good enough to make you think about how you want to build each character, and every skill is useful -- there are no useless fillers in it. Every skill point helps.There is usually a bunch of different missions to do -- a main one, and several side ones. Once you run out of side quests, you gotta do the main one to unlock more. Events will pop up every now and then, requiring you to make a decision that will affect your Alignment or send one of your knights away for the duration of one mission (these will come back with extra xp, loyalty, gold/building materials and/or items).Each of your knights has their own Alignment, and yours affects their loyalty. Their personal traits, events and items can also have an effect. If one of you guys has a negative loyalty, they suffer debuffs. With a positive one, they get +10% damage, then an extra +10%, and finally +1 AP. So, it matters a lot.Each of your knights also has 4 item slots (armor, weapon, artifact and trinket) and 2 potion ones. Items can be common, rare or epic, and they have interesting enough stats to make a  difference, sometimes even defining a build.In between missions, you can manage Camelot. You can buy/sell items there (for gold, or exclusively epic items for another currency whose name I forgot), heal your knights, fix their injuries, give them Court Titles to gain loyalty, respec them for a price, or upgrade Camelot's structures for bonuses.King Arthur: Knight's Tale is actually replayable, since you unlock different knights depending on your Alignment and some different missions as well.The game crashed on me . In the End Game, one of my skills kept bugging and not doing damage properly every now and then, and skills/items that were supposed to restore some of one of my knight's AP were not proc'ing. It worked fine during most of the game, though. All in all, the game is pretty stable.I have no idea why it takes 121gb of your HD, though, and the fog effect is extraordinarily heavy on the GPU. The graphics are nothing outstanding, and most places are too monochromatic. It's kind of boring, visually. But nothing that actually bothers you. It's not .Oh, there a few cutscenes in the game too and, despite most of them being fairly simple (the scene, as a whole) they are very well done.If you are a turn-based combat fan who also likes to build and equip your characters, this is a great game for you.I love that stuff and, as I said in the beginning, this game kept me hooked from start to finish, for a total of 81 hours (and I might replay it, to take a different moral path). Totally recommended. Worth full price.P.S.: play on "Very Hard." Also, go Righteous/Old Faith -- you'll get much more interesting knights. Galahad and The Red Knight (last unlocks from Christian and Tyrant paths, respectively) are both Defenders, and Defenders . The only advantage in going Tyrant is having a loyal Sir Balin, which is actually a pretty big advantage once you realize how OP [the good] Vanguards are. You could go Tyrant/Old Faith, but that would cost you Sir Tegyr, which is the other good Vanguard that can become loyal, since Lady Boudicea never will, and he's Rightful/Christian. Well, actually, the only way to get two good top-loyalty Vanguards is to go Tyrant/Christian (Balin + Tegyr) but, otherwise, such path totally sucks. Just... go Rightful/Old Faith -- it's cooler and a -1 AP Boudicea is still fine as a Vanguard (though she joins up considerably later than Balin and Tegyr).At a certain point, you also get to choose between, let's say, a chick and a dude to join you (trying not to spoil anything). The dude is Old Faith only, the chick is Old Faith/Tyrant, and they are two of the best heroes in the game. The one you choose is definitely going to be in your main party. If you go Rightful/Christian, you'll make both of them useless.

_childDocuments_.review: After a long time was looking for a RPG and man, this is a good one.I always wanted to play as a Black Knight..... the tyrant path is quite good XD. The morality system is a great idea to  get a different roster depending on where you behave like a knight or tyrant or even based on your alliegance with old and new gods. I don't  really care about being good or bad I just played to get Black and  Red Knight and they have some awesome skills.Play style is somewhate a cross between  traditional party RPG and Witcher (inventory/potions), i.e., dont expect to dive into a fight after finding some potions or loot they cannot be equipped/swapped unless you are back to your castle. Injured party members with injury status need to be sent to hospice (hospital) to heal over mission turns i.e., for type of injury and method of healing selected they wont be available for that many missions. Yes, you have to be careful with who or how you play per mission. The knights/sages/marksmen who dont participate in missions will not gain xp to level up. You need to build a training ground to send them to training to earn XP which if you do they wont be available for few missions depending on what training you chose. So there is an active party and an idle party both can gain XP depending on how you play. DEATH is imminent it sucks to have an untrained idle party member swapping your active mission roster just to find out they suck in middle stages of game. And lets say your main DPS disher Champion is getting treated for injury not available for 2 missions and your other champion is on training.. LOL.. you are in a pinch youll need to bring the injured guy with injured status or cancel the training and bring the other guy to fight.... both way you get pwned. This is a good game concept.This is what sets this game apart from other RPG, you cant just dive into combat, heal, grab loot equip/swap stuff right away and flee a battle .. Nope not possible. If you are looking at Divinity Sin, Diablo series and this one NOPE. Youll die.Combat system is great. Showing your back to enemies, how you position who and where is relatively important else its game over. There are certain loot that give your invulnerable armor, blocking, piercing/bleed attacks etc that helps. So preparation is key and not all rune loot is  equippable by all party members - makes sense you cant have a a sage wearing Black Knights heavy armor and vice versa, so depending on Vanguard, Champion, Sage, Mage, Marksmen runes for equipment is different, so youll have to be happy with rare loots coming right off the bat.Overall played a couple of acts and Ive enjoyed it so far, its not an open map or do anything anyway type of missions, so its quite linear. Youll get objectives pointing here and there around the map thats about it, and youll trigger scripted enemies and fights who appear in the same position no matter how many times you trigger the same combat (something like XCOM). And you have the flexibility to place your party positions on defined areas in map if you had checked them out earlier. Checking the enemy positions will help opening various places as starting point to a fight rather than clubbing your party members in default mission fight which may end up your party getting killed. Difficulty -> Ive played on hard right off the bat and man its tuff. On main act missions (progressing story) I get either by champion/vanguard with injury status and have to swap them out with idle party roster. Sucks but thats how it goes. Ended up getting Champions (main DPS disher) injured and the party sucked in mid acts as the enemy AIs dish heavy damage and they  gangup on the less armored members. LVL up your idle roster or dont stick to on party only in HARD mode. AI is not that smart but it can gang up on a less armored member and every pesky archer and brute will beeline towards them  depending who can get killed easily, having a defender nearby helps. Not going to talk about the story and stuff read it online so what does not go for me are as below:- Chest/GoldDunno who came up with the concept of scrounge for gold/chests getting 16 gold, 24 gold etc that you get depending on the chest size and area. The main characters here are  like Lancelot, Black Knight, Red Knight do you think these knights give a damn  about some mangy chest   or  random dead body with pocket change as gold?   This concept is rubbish.   I can understand loot rune rarity but gold ..MEH.. For me it shouldve been atleast treasures that can be sold to merchant for a large sum starting from 5000 gold pieces and above. Scrounging for gold doesnt seem to fit considering the characters we play with. If the "Finish Mission" was hit its better to get all loot and gold summed up into a screen. I dont see a point of getting told .. Oh not some treasure chests are still there.. yeah right for 16 and 20 gold you want my party to haul ass all over the map to get these puny sum, year right. just trashy concept.Defender/Vanguard- The DPS of Defender/Vanguard is too low or not balanced with runes. Sometimes it kills the game if   not with the correct setup. e.g., heavy armor reduces 1-2 movement AP and  gives good stats (armor invulerability or extra APs or passive traits)  but without movement your guys cant do ♥♥♥♥, just get picked off by those pesky IGNORE ARMOR and reduce HP archers.Injury Status- Let the champions/defenders/vanguards who have injury and come back healed have a chance of developing some passive trait. There is no point to veterans who come back fully healed.AI Dead Archers- Some maps have pesky dead archers that will directly start tearing off your health desipte your armor or armor stats, not sure how this seems to work or I havent seen the dead archer stats saying Ignore Armor and do piercing damage directly, even  with a well equiped Defender facing the dead archer they take off the HP directly fairly easily.Graphics for Runes- Rune graphic SUCKs, need to hover to the rune items to get a decent read of what it is and what it does, what stats it gives,   I can't make out what the rune is or does off the large screen. We are in 2022 bad item display? Really?......... Please change the rune images.Audio for Combat- Sounds bad, not sure if its due to those Wav files inside the banks but the sword swing audio sounds really bad. :'(  My Defender swings and sounds like some link chain hitting a wall. My vanguard swings two handed sword and sounds like iron pieces falling into mud. Its metal clashing against metal aint it, thats not how poleaxes, long swords sounds.. there is a major difference between one/double hand swords, poleaxes, polearms, long swords clashing with enemy armor :'(

_childDocuments_.review: Review based on first playthrough as Old Faith / Tyrant on Hard difficulty (Very Hard on the the last few missions in End Game). I love this game! It’s a game that wasn’t initially on my list to play but when I heard about the undead twist to the King Arthurian lore I was intrigued. The character progression wasn’t as complicated as some other games, but I enjoyed this aspect. It let me just play the game. I didn’t have to research online to min/max my Heroes, I just played the game. I picked skills that sounded good and went on with my life. Tristan was my go to Vanguard dps despite ppl saying he was subpar to Boudicea. He fit my story and how I wanted to play and he was great. No regrets. There was some subpar voice acting but most of the heroes were spot on. Mordred’s voice was awesome and I tried to always bring him to missions even when he had 2 permanent injuries. He’s tough, he didn’t mind. The battles were turn-based on a grid, but what was different (for me) was that you get to use all your action points first (unless it’s an ambush) and then the enemy used all theirs, rinse and repeat. There were no initiative rolls to deal with.One thing I would’ve preferred was to keep all my heroes. When I wanted to use a new hero, but my active roster was full I had to dismiss someone permanently. I like collecting so it would’ve been nice if once dismissed they hung out in the Aspirant’s Hero lounge, but oh well. In terms of replayability, there’s a morality chart with 4 quadrants and some heroes only available if you play a particular alignment. Plus, you can replay an alignment with totally different heroes (well except Mordred has to come on main story quests).TLDR - I bought the game at full price and have no regrets. It’s a fun game. If you like turn-based rpgs set in a dark fantasy world, I say give it try.  Get it. Play it. Profit.

_childDocuments_.review: So let me be fair here.I love this game, and I'm immensely biased towards Mordred especially since he's my favorite of King Arthur's Knights.However I do have to be honest here as well, this is a very fun game and anyone who's fond of the XCOM formula, or anything similar will find a lot to love here.That rings true as well if you enjoy the King Arthur mythos, this game literally oozes nothing but flavor from it's core, and it's a joy to play.Then there's the times I can't play it...Now this could be just the fact that my computer isn't state of the art, it's a gaming PC from roughly 4-5 years ago, but runs most current games just fine.  Exceptions being newer Triple A titles like Call of Duty and so on.Sometimes this game will run like a dream, and the experience is nothing short of fantastic, other times it will chug and not even be playable since I can't move without needing to wait roughly 3 full seconds for the game to catch up.In fairness this really only ever happens in levels that the undead are present in, so I'm not sure if that's my PC's fault, or something they still need to iron out in game.  It's important enough that I need to note it.Now a few people have complained here and there about the voice work and I don't personally see the issue.  It's got Mordred hamming it up as the dark edgy knight he's written out as, and you have Sir Kay with the over-boistrorous lines that make me giggle like an idiot.  I think the voice work is fine.Music is ok, I like the main menu theme, it's quite catchy, but otherwise I can't say the music stands out terribly much.The core gameplay of exploring around as a small squad of knights, and then engaging in battles is immensely fun.  There isn't the ever persistence issue from XCOM where you are bound to miss some really awkward attacks, and the attacks look rather nice, though it's not immensely flashy for the most part.I do wish we could replay levels we've already gone through, even if not to grind for XP and gold, then otherwise just to play them again.  Though I can understand this is still in Early Access.However something that is rather shattering are the prices for healing heroes if they end up wounded in this game.  You could be spending more then what you make on 3 expeditions to heal one hero if you accidentally flubbed up a bit.  It's not cheap, and money is a hard commodity to come by along with building supplies.Overall though, with what the game is, I do highly recommend it, even if it's more based on personal bias.  There's a good start to something amazing here, and it really shouldn't be overlooked.PROSOozes atmosphere and tension for King Arthur lovers.Playing as Mordred is a treat in and of itself.Gameplay in general is hard to put down and is heavily fun.CONSIf not running on some seriously nice hardware, chugging is gonna be noticeable and can ruin the experience.Some prices in game are ludicrous and can leave you banked out trying to help one individual out.Replayability in it's current state isn't gonna be very high.Honestly despite my problems, I'd definitely give this an 8/10.  It's a good start to what I'm confidant can be an amazing game.
