_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun game but it's way too long for the type of combat it has, let me explain.Being a turned based combat your team takes it's turn then the enemy team does. The problem appears when you get 5+ encounters per mission with 10-15 enemies it will burn you down and get sick of the combat just like me. There are barely any good upgrades. Most of the skills are bad and don't help you that much. The armors and weapons are a joke and the trinkets are worthless aside from 3-4 relics that give you extra powers (teleport, life steal, heal).I really hate the companion mechanic where you have a maximum amount of characters permitted and in order to get more active ones you have to dismiss the ones you already have.The story expects you to know every damned character in the arthurian mythology and what battles happened. I know just what was presented on the Merlin tv show from 2008I resisted this tiresome combat up until midway through act 3 and it's enough for me considering i'm getting at least 10+ enemies per encounter with 4-5 encounters per map.It's an ok game but not at the current price tag of 45 euros. Maybe when it's around 20 it might be a good time to pick it up. I rate it at around a 6/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I backed this when it was a Kickstarter because it looked cool and showed great promise. Fast forward through early access and full release and it still looks cool, but that’s about it. It is very ambitious but tries to do way too much and doesn’t deliver.Let’s talk about story, battle mechanics, and game mechanics.The story is promising. It takes place after the canonical legends end and something has gone horribly wrong and it's up to us to fix. The trouble is, it's a poorly told story and quickly falls apart. Luckily it’s linear, but the end result is that you feel shoehorned through the devs’ ramblings rather than invited on a quest. Most of your plot development takes place during missions where the dialogue goes from ok to incomprehensible. (I'm honestly shocked at the poor grammatical quality of the English script, poor narrative quality aside.) Dialogue choices don’t really add much and the only impactful choices you get are either required “let’s go!” type responses that are needed to move you through a dungeon or “do I side with Character A or Character B” and add one to my court instead of the other.Worse, characters are more caricatures. Because this story takes places after the end of the Arthurian saga, once more or less everyone is dead, literally every player in Arthuriana is available and the devs bring them all along for the ride. The problem is that they also play a lot of inside baseball and swamp the player in characters who get little development. This is a high bar for players and bad storytelling, but also means the folks we interact with have the depth of a daytime soap opera cast, veering towards tyrannical Christian’s and virtuous pagans in a way that becomes predictable and off putting. None of my characters have died yet, but if they did I wouldn’t mourn them, I’d just replace them with another jaunty knight with more or less the same skill set and a similarly poorly communicated backstory and significance. Then, we'd just happily bumble through the next missions as they make non sequitur comments that don't really add anything to the experience. The mind-numbingly linear nature of the story, the poor plot development, and the flat characters give me little reason to finish this game, let alone replay it.On to the battle system! Ah, the battles. There is a delightful array of skills and the classes are fairly well developed to fit traditional RPG roles with a unique flair.  There’s also something satisfying about hacking down wave after wave…after wave after wave…after….wave…of the same types of enemies map after map after similar map. As you might guess from the description, it becomes boring and unsatisfying quickly. Each mission is effectively a skirmish and feels like a one-off since the narrative development of the game is lacking. I’m not totally sure why I’m in a (bog / crypt / wasteland) again, but if I run around enough I’ll meet some (bandits / skeletons / barbarians) sooner or later and if I kill enough of them then the mission will end. The maps themselves are beautiful, as is the character art, but it doesn’t make up for the fact that every battle after you encounter a new type of enemy feels like a repeat of the last one. There’s an attempt on some missions to add in named characters as mini-bosses or dungeon bosses but, again, when the world building is lacking at the macro level, I struggle as a player to get hyped up to take on Sir Named-Skeleton IV, who was prideful in life, alongside all his mates when it’s just another skeleton fight. It’s gotten to the point where I dread the battles, not because they’re difficult, but because they are so repetitious, boring, and shallow. It's just a grind.Ok, let’s talk broader game mechanics, specifically: base building, item acquisition, and companion management.The base building mechanics are fine, though often a bit clunky and neither revolutionary nor particularly impressive. The bonuses some companions can give to different buildings is a nice plus, but it’s a minor bonus. Resource acquisition is totally based on mission outcomes save for the occasional world event, so you may be rolling in gold that you can trade for building points at unfavorable rates, or you can wait it out to build that addition to the Round Table until you finally get a mission that rewards you in build points. There's no real rhyme or reason, the game just trundles on and you make the best worst choice you can without ever having sufficient resources. This is fine because the bonuses offered by different buildings are nice, but they don’t feel particularly significant - there's nothing I felt I had to have beyond the basics.Item acquisition is random, as is the way that things show up in the shops. This means that you just work with what you get and if you don’t get anything better for a particular companion over the next 5 to 10 missions, well, that’s the luck of it. While uninspiring and making things feel stagnant, I didn’t find this hampered my progress much since damage and defense progression feels pretty flat. It might benefit from a tier of unique weapons that have to be reassembled like “the Excalibur” so that there’s something predictable for folks to work towards. Instead, I feel swamped in bland junk with low resale value.Finally, the knights of the round table. I've commented a bit on them already in relation to their character development, but let's talk about party management. You find these folks all over - some from story quests, some from optional quests, some from unlockable quests based on your moral decision making. With few exceptions, this all feels arbitrary and comes down to the poor world building. The devs decided who be available when and it just feels capricious and annoying, or it would if they had character and weren't just a series of interchangeable class archetypes.Once you acquire a character for your court, there is little to no relationship development. There may be a little dialogue during missions or they can do a little quest of there own, but you don’t have dialogue with them in a meaningful way, you don’t get to know them. Once they join your court, they’re just sort of there. To suck more of the joy out of things, you’re also limited on space, so after a while you’ve got to start kicking knights out or letting them die if there are particular knights you want to have. There's no real reason for this I can see beyond the devs wanting to force a choice on players.This brings us to the loyalty system. Loyalty, and the bonuses you get from it, is more or less determined by the moral choices you make. These hit at a macro level rather than an individual level, meaning in the late game you’re shoehorned into what characters you can use most effectively based on the alignment you choose. If you’re a pagan, all your Christians will hate you. If you’re a tyrant, all your just folks will hate you. If you get someone who’s a tyrannical Christian, well, it’s a wash, which is fine as mechanics go but makes no sense from a narrative point of view. This also means neutral heroes just sort of persist, never getting penalties but also never getting bonuses. Luckily, the bonuses and penalties you get aren't very significant so your characters liking or not liking you feels more of a cosmetic choice than a game changer.In sum, the battle mechanics and graphics are stellar, but that is worth little when the cost is paid in lackluster world-building, poor narrative, and shallow characters. Make me emotionally invest in the characters, make the loyalty system worthwhile and sensible, clean up the script, give things proper context and then I'd be more than happy to give this beautiful game more time. Til then, it's just a flat, boring grind.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good. It has it's issues, but it's early access. Grammar, a few collision issues, had a few save issues. But the only one that really bothers me is what I'm encountering lately - framerate issues. I'm on a very capable setup (no, I'm not flex my "specs" bro) and I'm having issues about 9 hours in. We'll see if that improves.Otherwise, it really is like XCOM medieval version. There are no misses or dodges and I really like that. Shielded units can block, of course. Inventory management and base upgrades is simplistic. I'm playing on Hard difficulty and that's a decent challenge. I tried starting on the ironman-type setting and it was brutal. I wouldn't recommend that on a first try as some enemies literally explode and it's game over. The game doesn't tell you that either lol, you just get blown up and you learn. I've been enjoying the game, but it's definitely clunky and it's possible Devs will have that all resolved upon release. I appreciate they are not rushing the release, either. I'd say it's currently 7/10 with FAR more potential if they can polish it up a bit.

_childDocuments_.review: I do like this game a lot  Others have described it so i just comment some of the issues raised by others. The game is quite difficult  ( I think it is but I'm an average player I think/hope) . However there are many difficulty levels from a walk in the park to ridiculously difficult for a pensioner like me.  There are also some   difficulty spikes but they can be overcome by resetting the difficulty level for any scenario whilst in Camelot . Cheesy perhaps but no one else need know.1. I completely agree with the poster who complained that party members can't share potions. Each character can only have 2, Apparently there is an upgrade that can allow a char. to have a 3rd but I've never  been able to get that. This means that I  have to use hit point recovery points only and a very occasional armour repair potion but I rely on camp fires to mend armour.  Shame as there are many types of potion and single-use are in practice unavailable. There ar some potions/scrolls that can be used pre-mission and last for the mission and there are useful - and rare2 Some quests require/forbid a particular char. from participating. That's OK but it can be a pain because you rarely have more than 4 or 5 decent knights for the scenario. There is training for other knights in your rota, but in reality that does  not enable them  keep up3. Side quests don't always require sending out a knight, but the result seems to be   a bit hit and miss. Success seems to be dependant on the lavel/abilties of the knight sent out, but  I have no way of knowing. Success can sometimes bring in useful benefits but often they only benefit the knight who was sent  because he/she wasn't useful for main quests.4. My sanity has been saved  by  checking out you-tube gudes for all aspects . I've found Maxallos betst though there were nade in 2022 so may be slightly out of date in some respects,5. I do like the high-camp absurd armour etc and the voice acting is excellent - rather than the  uninspired  quality heard in many other games6. The worst part for me is 1 of the missions (level 4 I think) in which saves are disabled. It is difficult for me to be able to play  the whole mission in 1 session. The lack of saves is an unnecessary and disrespectful of my time especially as I get quite a few CTDs  when playing: though that may just be on my PC as  I haven't read other complaints about crashing.All in all though an excellent game which  is very goood value for money and could and should easily be made even better with a few tweaks.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: satisfying, dark, medieval X-ComMessage for devs: Take good care of the story. Focus on atmosphere (see Darkest Dungeon 1) and heavy-duty story, take some inspiration from Dark Souls 1 if needed. Great work, looking forward for more.Pros: - Surprisingly addicting x-com like with a great twist on the legend. - The dark setting adds to the experience, with very nice music that reflects the Pagan and Old Druidic Ways- Good customization for heroes for both skills and items- Good customization for the kingdom (i.e. build orders, construction, etc)- Nice RPG options for Pagan Vs Christianity, and Benevolent Ruler Vs Tyrant which adds depthPros:- Could get "grindly" later on, and unless you have a good story to support this grind as a foundation it might become stale- Dialogue seems uninspired - especially YOUR own options to interact with characters, often times seems.... silly and childish, you might ask yourself internally: "oh wow, this...doesnt seem like smth Mordred would say at all..."- I would appreciate some recognition for higher level difficulties, maybe even a stupid achievement or something, or perhaps even one single dialogue line, anything really, ANY recognition for playing in harder diffs plus roguelite, anything at all- Takes time until you get to unlock the "good stuff" in the talent tree, plus you cant diverge from ONE single path, otherwise you fight your own progress in the talent tree.Overall yes quite good, would buy a decent DLC and follow-up.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a top notch Turn Based Strategy game with elements of Darkest Dungeon, Xcom, and believe it or not, RPG like exploration. If Xcom, Divine Divinity 2 or Darkest Dungeon are your thing, buy this game; don't wait for a sale, because I hope the Developers make enough profit to make a bigger sequel. This game reminds me very much of the original Xcom remake, in that it has great core systems, but is lacking in scope and budget; a sequel could be something along the lines of Xcom2. The combat system is very similar to Xcom, but with a greater emphasis on attacking, planning mid battle ( Xcom lets you setup encounters, with positioning and attacks, this game does not, which takes a bit getting used to) , staying on the offense is key here in most battles. Maximizing your damage and setting up your damage dealers with buffs is a priority. There is a base building aspect and an over world map, but it resembles Darkest Dungeon more than Xcom. Lastly, I think the system in the game that seemed to have the least time and effort put in, could easily be the most interesting, if it was expanded upon in a sequel, the exploration and real time control while in a map. You can navigate the maps with a WASD control scheme, and although the environments do not stand out ( the environmental graphics are passable but nothing great) there are glimpses of good map design, that have secrets, lighting torches to open doors etc., and many hidden areas with extra rewards and side quests, like a traditional RPG. Overall, I still consider XCom2 the mark to meet in this genre of game, that being said, if XCom2 =-100, I give King Arthur: Knight's Tale an 85. It is worth anyone's time that is interested in this genre of game: it adds and borrows a few things from adjacent genres to great effect. The game ran great for me with only one crash in 50 hours; also, the lack of Mod support and cosmetic changes or visual upgrades for your characters are glaring omissions.Positives: A great Xcom like game- good voice acting- music- sound effects- animations- I had one crash to desktop in a 50 hour campaign- the game runs great with HIgh FPS ( due to simple environments and lack of destructibility)Some Negatives: The environments are lacking in detail and can be a bit Janky (hit boxes) in areas- lacking enemy variety- no cosmetic upgrades or changes for your characters. This is a huge thing for me, especially in regards to replayability. None of the items or armor you equip effect your appearance, so your characters look the same from the beginning to the end of the game.- No Mod support

_childDocuments_.review: Rock solid game for those who like this genre.  Pros:  - Resource management is straightforward, makes sense, doesn't get cluttered and stays balanced.  Your money decisions are not going to be easy.-  ambiance and music are on the button.  Dialogue is interesting and quests are loaded with winks to those who know their Arthurian lore.  - Combat mechanics are clean and AI knows what's up.- Alignment system rewards you without being intrusive- Graphics hold up, portraits also very good, UI is clean.- Progression system has some building options and some of the classes actually require a learning curve to use.Cons:- Kinda wish there was a little more granularity in the difficulty modes. _childDocuments_.review: A fantasy xcom, what's not to like?You start with a couple of knights and you unlock more as you progress trough the story. The knights you unlock and some missions depend on the choices you make, although most of the missions and the mains ones are allways the same.As your progress, your knights level up and unlock new skills and you get better gear. The missions are real time until combat starts. Then it's turn based and you and the enemies have action points to move, attack and use skills. Depending of the knights there are several different strategies and it's very rewarding to discover tactics that allow your knights to kill a lot of enemies without giving them chance to strike back. It's not super deep, but the combats are tactical enough and fun. Although you unlock several knight, you can only take 4 for each mission. I played the campaign twice, to unlock the 2 morality and religion knights, and in both cases I ended up using mostly 4 to 6 knights on each, that were my favorites. The others were just there.The graphics are nice but not mind blowing. The sounds and music are also nice.Regarding the achievements, they are simple and not very hard to get them all. If you do a roguelite and evil morality campaign you can unlock them all in one go plus and online game (don't have to win). I did 2 campaigns and  it was fun. Doing all side missions took me about 50 hours for each campaign.Now lets wait for a DLC with more missions perhaps.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a very well-designed strategy based RPG. This category definitely needs more resources. Recommended for all S-RPG lovers. The game itself is a combination of exploring, simulation, and turn-based strategy moves. Well-told stories. The difficulty levels are quite different from one another. Yet, even the hardest level is not too bad. So take some time, think about your moves, and plan your resources well.Now the negatives:The map exploration kinda just got thrown out of the window post ACT II. Little to No surprise at all. Four-member squad seems too small. There are only few types of enemies, which makes the game a little redundant post ACT II. Same with the classes, only a few different classes available. Even if you want to use different characters, usually you cannot do that since many of them are not even close to the level that the quests are requesting.

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it.  The story really worked here. Familiar characters seen through a new angle.At first glance there are only 6 characters, but most characters have a unique feature about them and a few are very different than their base class. For example, there are 3 or 4 flavors of Arcanist; this keeps variety high.  I found all builds were at least somewhat viable and even more interesting there were characters I loved in act 1 and 2 and stopped using in act 3 and vice versa; that kept it fresh.  Their contribution to the strategy layer made for some tough decision making and that is one pillar of making a game with RPG elements.The AI was competent most of the time; they would attempt to flank and generally avoid walking into overwatch.  The only glaring mistake I saw as when the AI swarmed an invulnerable character.  The varieties of enemies were ok.  You’ll definitely see them again and again; part of that is there are a lot of missions.  Challenge could use some tweaking, at least in one instance.  I had one character mission that party wiped me multiple times before I made adjustments and got through with multiple injuries but the other missions before and after that I breezed through; they were rated the same level.  Other than that, and 1 other non-plot mission, the balance was consistent. If you like turn based tactical that isn’t in the cover shooter style pick this up.  Note, Marksman can also do cover shoot but that isn’t the entire game principal like some others in this genre.

_childDocuments_.review: To put it simply: this is a sort of XCOM with swords and magic, and (at least for me) with a more engaging story. If you like this kind of tactical games, this game won't disappoint you.The pros:- great gameplay, combat and story- 6 different classes (and enough options/abilities to make different builds of each class)- amazing design (dark medieval fantasy)- good voice acting- interesting morality/faith system, encouraging replayabilityThe cons:- the limit of only 12 heroes with no ability to swap them between reserve and active, you either keep them active, or dismiss them for good (*)- the endgame (after campaign) ramps the difficulty up several levels (!), might not be for everyone(*) Although the fact that you cannot try all the heroes in one gameplay encourages to play the game again, especially for the ones locked at certain moral/faith level, it is frustrating to not being able to swap them at least for a trial mission. An option to swap active heroes for other in the reserve (with some kind of cool-down mechanic, damaging their loyalty or something else to limit its use) would improve this game.(!) For the main campaign you can choose the difficulty, but after the campaign, when you start the endgame and its many missions (which is 100% cool that they added it), although it would seem that you're still playing on the same difficulty, you encounter enemies with much more health and/or higher number of them at once, for the balefire mission, it gets ridiculous. That may be great for those seeking tougher challenges (but hey, you already have the difficulty setting...), but for more "casual" players, it turns each mission into a long bothersome and cumbersome task, IMO.

_childDocuments_.review: To whom I would recommend this game:- if you love turn-based tactical combat. Then this game will absorb you- if you like or don't mind a very dark and cruel fantasy storyTo whom I would NOT recommend this game:- if you expect an immersive RPG - if you dont like cruel storiesPros:- lots of recruitable heroes that allow you to create different fighting teams for every mission - a lot of side missions and a seperately playable endgame mode- well designed and adjustable difficutlty levels (though if you have experience with tactical combat and you'd like to think a bit more about your combats I recommend you to play on "hard" difficutlty. I played on "normal" and did not lose a single hero and only had to reload once in the entire campaign.)- my absolute highlights of this game are two: 1. Heroes can get minor and major injuries, which might seriously affect their fighting power. And they need to be treated for that to cure them. I also very much like the split of your health bar into HP and Vitality-Points.  2. You have a base (Camelot) which you can improve over time in the matter that seems the most helpful to you. Cons:- if you play all the side missions you will see the same kind of adversaries over and over again. :/- the very fact that you CANNOT OPEN YOUR HEROES' EQUIPMENT PROFIL DURING MISSIONS is super frustrating, absolutely annoying and simply not understandable !!! Do the devs expect me to memorize all the buffs and debuffs of my equipment? - comparing items is a nightmare !! A lot of items look the same, the description window jumps around and heros do have individual item bags but all share one. What is more, the item headline sums up situational damage output and presents it as overal damage output: e.g. "this sword does +7 more damage than the one you have equipped" but the +7 might come from damage bonuses against only certain type of foes or be otherwise situational and so the help is basically misleading !- the mission design is very flat. You cant walk two meters without coming across YET ANOTHER pile of human carcasses or heaps of human skulls or bones, or walls of human skulls. This very quickly has the reverse effect of the intended: before the first mission is over you are already numb to it. It then only serves as a reminder that you walk through a very cruel world and everyone aim (including yours) seems to be to eradicate the world from evey living being.- last but not least, and I know I could say that about almost all fanatasy stories in video games: the story is kinda garbage imao ;)

_childDocuments_.review: Mission difficulty is wildly random; some missions give enemies map wide buffs and spawn every encounter as an ambush with 15+ enemies behind your party and others a boringly easy with 5-8 enemies per fight in front of you visible before you engage.The alignment system seems very interesting but is terribly skewed in character distribution, almost all of 2 of the classes (sage and arcanist) are one alignment, and one alignment had 7 heroes while another boasts 11.There are still also several bugs and balance issues present in the game. Some character skills and passives do not stack or work in brokenly powerful ways. Your projected damage is not modified by the weakness debuff, but is modified but positive buffs, so you have to be very careful and count every modifier in some fights or you might leave a corpse at 1 hp (despite your minimum damage promising to destroy it) letting it return to full life and armor and take its turn.Edit: The new checks put in place for the vanguard class are a very good step forward but the lack of mission rebalancing shows very little foresight on the developers behalf. Once they adjust the missions now that theyve removed most players crutch, I'll come back and give it another try.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I'm giving this a negative review. I don't think you should buy it right now. TLDR; 7/10 it's a buggy unbalanced game, but if you can deal with that it's fun. It feels like it's still in early access, which is very disappointing for a full release. Not as bad as Cyberpunk's release, but they could have done a lot better since it was in early access for quite a while.That said, I do believe it will be worth your money in a month or two because it was released in a rather buggy state. I have crashed 4 times in 33 hours, soft locked twice, lost a save twice (in fact my first campaign was lost because it seemed to have never made a save file in the first place), and encountered many graphical bugs including glitches, frame rate drops, and texture problems.Audio is a solid 8/10, one note footstep balancing is awful, very loud or squelchy all the time when moving about.Voice acting is hit or miss, some actors were clearly very enthusiastic, others kind of just phoned it in. The Black Knight is as hilarious as it is bad, strongly recommend recruiting him for the amusement, but I can't take him seriously which I thought was the tone of the game.Gameplay 9/10, the concept is solid, the gameplay is there and it is full of replayability. Characters have different skills at different points, even unique skills that others can't obtain or not until extremely late game. You will have opportunities to collect many knights to hone your roster, however currently you cannot dismiss a prospective knight that you're not interested in accepting to your table without first accepting him onto your table then banishing him. 'There's a lot of equipment, and resource management feels fair, if quite tight, if you like buying gear from the merchant, you will be short on cash when events come up because this game is quite frugal. I expected it to open up later and be a bit more generous, but it doesn't, you can mitigate it however by using certain knights in certain positions to increase your gains and rewards.Combat is fun, challenging some of the time, occasionally frustrating, and it is clear some missions are in dire need of a balance pass. It seems some of the Knight or Lady recruitment missions can be exceptionally punishing, though often your party of four is somewhat aided by the presence of a temporary fifth member on those missions, even so they are among the most difficult missions. Combat is turn based, with you almost always having the initiative, I can count on one hand the times I was ambushed in 33 hours of gameplay. You execute your entire teams actions then wait through the enemy's entire turn, you can speed this up in game. Actions, spells, attacks, and movement all cost AP, very similar to Divinity Original Sin, though this game seems to be more generous with AP regeneration. At one point one of my champions had an axe that teleported him to another nearby enemy after he killed one, with enough AP regeneration on kills he was able to telegank entire rooms, very satisfying if not very fair. There are classes, defender (tank), champion (melee 2hand dps), vanguard (dual wield rogue type with sneak attack bonuses and traps), marksman (bow class with poison and fire), sage (Buffer-blaster mage), and arcanist (Blaster-buffer mage). I found class balance to be a little strange, there is an achievement for using 4 marksmen in a single party, but it feels really really bad as a composition, MMs don't feel like they do enough damage unless you have a pile of max damage overwatch bows and let them walk into your fire. I found my best successes were tank, and three big melee beatsticks, though the vanguards damage output is not to be underestimated. When you start getting mages later they can hyper your dps classes and often do more damage through their buffs than their spells.I should note I have not tried the multiplayer aspect, though it is there, I won't make any conjecture on it except I have a feeling it may resemble XCOM multiplayer which is a wild cluster at the best of times.Graphically 5/10, this game is doing nothing to push envelopes, which should mean they have all their graphical stuff worked out. However as mentioned before it drops frame rates constantly, the graphic options are quite limited currently with very little indication of what is being changed. As for color palettes, I hope you like grey and green, because 75% of this game is that color, its a dark palette for a dark tone to match the developer's vision of the game. One other graphical issue is there is something uncannily off about the Lady of the Lake in the cut scenes, something is wrong with her proportions and the way she talks, at points I thought she was going full mouth of Sauron, very creepy.Story 7/10 It's fun, lots to read, and most of it is voice acted, quests follow a formula of go into an area, meet someone, resolve their problems occasionally in non violent ways, but often violently, you can definitely play a villain or a hero and experience two sides of a coin with some repercussions for it and a morality gauge with unlocks for playing into those roles. There are a handful of times when it gets hamfisted and the evil is almost cartoonish, but by the same measure the good can be as well. Christianity and Paganism play large parts in this game as well, but they don't try to do it offensively, but there is a constant presence and many of your knights fall on one side or the other and will show their loyalty for siding with them.Overall 7/10 game, it has bugs, it has problems, but at the time of writing this review devs had released a hotfix patch, which funny enough had typos and duplicate entries in the patch notes. It's still a fun game, but feels like it was rushed out of early access and therefore still feels like an early access game, that's not really acceptable and you should wait until the game is ready before purchasing.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR 5/10. Not a bad game by any means, just "meh".-----------------------------So, lets' starts with the basics.GRAPHICS & ARTSTYLE: 3/10One word: boring. The developers went for the "paint everything bleak grey" artstyle, I'm assuming to give a grim-dark-depressing vibe of the world. Unfortunately, it failts completely. You wander from one grey zone into another grey zone with grey houses, grey graveyards, grey people, grey castles that are impossible to distinguish from one another. As for the quality of the graphics - they are right in the middle of the road. Not bad, but hardly enough to warrant a single "this looks good!" from you.STORY & LORE: 5/10.I do like the setting, but again it is not very well implemented. You are playing as sir Mordred, one of the more evil knights of the Round Table, and encounter various knights on your journeys. Well first of all, while the knight quests (getting the companions) are interesting, there is zero interaction afterwards. They stay in your party and there is not much more to it. What's even more weird is running through the world, when one of the knights in your party says something like "Sir Mordred, I wonder if you have really changed?". You would expect a snarky remark from Mordred or at least something - but no, nothing happens.I also have to add that SIr Mordred is meant to be quite an evil character, from his appearance to his dialogue and voicelines. But the game allows you to roleplay him in a few ways. This breaks the immersion quite a bit, because some decisions - especially the RIGHTFUL ones (more on that in the alighnment section) completely contradict Sir Mordred's nature and are something he would never say or do.The quests are also pretty meh. Most of them are either "kill everyone" or "find 5 of something" and give you a simple reward at the end. In other words, pretty unremarkable.MORALITY & AlIGHNMENT: 5/10It was supposed to be a fun system where you can make different choices that affect your morality (rightful vs tyrant) and religion (old faith vs christian). The problem is that the best bonuses and characters are locked behind going deep into either direction, and staying neutral is the worst outcome. So instead it becomes a "I need good old faith buffs, so I will have to make all the old faith choices" situation.COMBAT: 6/10If you've played something like Divinity Original Sin you will be very familiar with this type of combat. This game does it pretty well. There are however a few things I didn't like:1) The difficulty usually comes not from the enemies but froms swarming you with 20 or even 30 enemies at a time, which I didn't find very fun.2) In the beginning, the characters have too few skills to be fun. Most of them have a basic attack and one other skill, which doesn't give too much variety to combat3) The battles get repetitive very fast. It's usually using the same tactics again and again while trying not to get swarmedVOICE ACTING: 8/10Really well done, I enjoyed most of the characters, and Sir Mordred sounded really goodMUSIC: 3/10There was something playing. I have no memory of it.ICING ON THE CAKEThe Game is still 120GB(!!!) in size. Yup, you heard it right, it's of the same size as Dragon Age 1, Dragon Age 2, Dragon Age Inquisition and Divinity Original Sin combined.Overall, I found it to be a pretty average game. It's definitely not a bad game. But when compared to Pathfinder, Dragon Age, Divinity: Original Sin or even XCOM, it pales in comparison.

It's just my thing.The premise: Once and Future King has perished and now you, his mortal enemy, the traitor, must bring order back to Avalon.Pros:1.  I cannot stress enough just how pretty this game is. Everything from loading screens to the environments to the main characters looks polished and detailed. The armour you and your heroes are wearing is just so. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. beautiful. Some of the enemy models (that you can talk to before stabbing them with your sword) look the same but it honestly didn't bother me that much. All plot-important characters look unique anyway.2.  This is a weird one but in this game your companions are mortal (unless you're playing on easy) and that's a good thing. It's your job to make sure they survive otherwise they go straight to Camelot's crypt. I'm pretty sure you can go there and pay your respects or weep or whatever Avalon's king is supposed to do there when he isn't busy trying to earn money to reconstruct another wing of the fortress or make sure his people won't die of a plague. You can be a tyrant ruling over your charges with an iron fist or you can become a righteous king taking care of his people in the time of need. The whole thing is made all the more interesting by the fact that you are the Traitor. People hate you and distrust you by default. You being kind of an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ while talking to them does nothing to endear you to them either.Cons:1.  Overall, the voice acting is great, but I did encounter some unvoiced lines. 2. Sometimes when you try to pick up loot Sir Mordred will just start walking in a random direction without you pressing anything to make him move. _childDocuments_.review: I bought this game for two reasons:1) I like to fund Indies as, they are often as good or better than, the big titles at twice the price.  2) I know of Neocore Games from the similar VanHelsing game which, I thought they did a good job-with.- I agree with one of the community who commented on the lack of content (2 main story quests, 7 side quests) leading to a refund.  NeoCore walks a fine line in asking the community for full support contribution vs. expectation for reasonable content.- I'm not refunding as, I found the story and content to be compelling enough to finish the game as it stands and look forward to the developer bulking up quickly on existing content.I liked: - The story, music (a little repetitive), assignment of tokens representing armor, weapons, rings and artifacts.- Upgrade-able castle buildings, nothing new but, a definite must-have for this type of game.- No crashes at 21 hours of play time, decent graphics (at least I had no issues with an MSI G73).I didn't like:- The full (Indie) price of the game vs. minimal content (more of a demo than a full in-development game).  I'm inclined to let this slide as, I'm familiar with NeocoreGames and believe they will earn the trust placed in them.- No mapped keys for essential buttons used all the time during combat (Overwatch, Reserve, End Turn) making combat way too "clicky."  Probably simple oversight but, hope NC addresses it.- Very simple-looking mini-map (and main map) stands out as underwhelming, relative decently-present graphics in the battle area.  More importantly, it lacks independent orientation relative to the group's current facing (i.e. mini-map should rotate with the group for better bearing on group's position relative to the terrain).Summary:Good start to a game by a known good developer but, manage your investment expectations, definitely a demo at this point.  The game is currently one evening's worth of gameplay at best.  If you need 40 hours or better of game play, maybe wait a few weeks.

_childDocuments_.review: I find the game challenging and filled with interesting story content throughout. I bought the game at a discount (on sale) and have easily got my money's worth already after 34 hours played. Each knight has different skills to build up, and finding the right equipment for them is fun and interesting each step of the way. Your knights can get pretty beat up from fights, but there is means of healing them up, and getting them back in the fight without to much difficulty. I have thoroughly enjoyed playing this game for both its value, dark setting, building, and its combat structure.  I look forward to see where the story goes and will play the game through to the end.

_childDocuments_.review: I do recommend this game for anyone who's a fan of tactical/turn based grid gameplay or into King Arthur/Camelot lorePros:+Combat is fun and fair. I'm playing on "Moderate" difficulty (between Normal and Hard), and the game sits at a very nice sweet spot difficulty wise+Some people won't care for it, but I like the unique characters and their stories+EVERYTHING is voice acted, and voice acted well+Game runs smoothly, no crashes+There's a "just one more mission" sort of vibe the game gives off because of the aboveNeutral:-A lot of people are bothered by the 12 hero limit. Hasn't bugged me at all to this point-The Camelot/base building idea is cool, but needs to be more fleshed out to shine. Think a very basic version of base building in Darkest Dungeon-The world map looks cool and thematic, but all you're doing is choosing missions from it. There's room for some more neat stuff here.-Classes tend to be same-y with a couple skill variations here and there. This could have been better, but isn't horrible (meaning one Vanguard class feels very similar to another Vanguard class unit)Negatives:-A lot of QOL things need to be added i.e. range indicators for ranged units when they haven't moved.-The level design is very same-y. Grimdark color palettes, no verticality-Level objectives are always the same: kill everything you see. Some variety would have been nice.-I'm maybe 15-20 hours in thus far (AFK time and all), and I'm seeing a lot of the same enemies. So far, there have been 2 enemy "factions" introduced (Lost and Pict)-No aesthetic changes when putting on new armor/weapons (this is a bummer)All in all, I'm enjoying this and will continue playing it. However, you should know the primary draw for me has been the combat simply because of the nice level of difficulty and good mix of strategy and tactics. This may not be for everyone because of some of the stuff above.

_childDocuments_.review: It´s good to be bad.. or the tale from other side of the round table..After the final battle between King Arthur and his arch nemesis Mordred the story ends.. normally - with Arthurs death. "King Arthur: Knights Tale" just begins and with it a quite different view on especially Mordred and the Knights of the round table. Since he has to save Avalon from destruction, by killing Arthur again!To do this you follow the story of what exactly happened with the Lady of the Lake, Arthur and forbidden rituals. All this while building up a new and improved Round table, made up of dark versions of the original Lords and Ladies. To do this, you can choose from five classes (Defender - Champion - Vanguard - Archer and Magicians). All of these have their own character (which gives some nice rpg elements from time to time) and also a bit different skill trees, which offers diversion in the strategy department.You will need a good setup in the over 50 chapters (including side quests), while hunting Arthur and fighting all kind of enemies of the realm. While your group of four characters runs in kind of Diablo-like levels, which range from castle cellar to Fey lands but always keep their dark/grim atmosphere, you fight in turn based combats. While a good Defender as tank is nearly a must in my opinion, you can build your party as you like and as fits your style. Due the wide variety in skill sets/weapon and items as well as special perks, the possibilites are nearly without limit. During the missions you also should repair your camelot, so you can heal your fighters, send them on training and get better equipment.The battles themself mostly throw you against an superior number of enemies, which are also working adequatly in the AI department (e.g. the archers use cover, front warriors like to attack the flank and especially your weaker characters). So you always need a good and fitting group, to prevail. Also keeping an eye on the strenghts and weaknesses is key to victory.Last but not least there are also quite some dilemmas for you as ruler to solve. Most of these will change your alignment, which goes from Old Faith versus Christian and Lawful versus Evil. Depending on these scales you can recruit some extra fighters and get bonus to your rule. While this makes it even more interesting to try at least a second playthrough, it makes you ignore the actual content of the decisions  most of the time and just further your alignment.Despite this and some levels, where it is not really easy to keep an overview of where to go (despite a quite useful map), are these already the main drawbacks of an otherwise very well done strategic game, with much charme. Maybe the fixed number of twelve Knights (and that you cannot just set one on the bench - if you fire a guy he´s gone for good) is also a bit annoying, but it also makes you think harder, whom you actually take on.Conclusio: I like the bad guys most of the time, so this games story was ideal for me. Besides that i very much liked that they gave most of the people some character, with even a bit of interaction from time to time. So i can fully recommend this Jagged Alliance in the Arthurian Universe for every strategy fan.Point Score: 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: I HIGHLY RECOMMEND THIS GAME!!! I LOVE KING ARTHUR: KNIGHTS TALE!!! From start to finish, this game exceeded my expectations. This is my new favorite Tactical RPG. Well done, NeocoreGames! You nailed it!!! I have not been this hooked on a tactical RPG game and it's story in this genre since Xcom 2. I honestly prefer and enjoy this setting (dark fantasy/medieval) to the science fiction. I have over 50+ hours in King Arthur: Knight's Tale and I have passed all the acts on Normal. (I tried hard mode until around level 7 or 8 when I got stuck and couldn't progress, so i reloaded back a quest and changed the difficulty to Normal which still was a tough game for me through the end, but not overly punishing. It was honestly just right in my opinion).  I am currently exploring the NEW Endgame quests and mini-game battles. AND I'm still enjoying the hell out of this game! ++ The good +++ The quests offered a lot of variety which caused me to change up my strategy depending on what kind of foe I was facing. There were some very unique twists and surprises that kept me on my toes. + The story is well written and compelling. It's a grand tale with a twist on a tiresome story you've heard many times before. This is NOT that story... it's a tale that you would not expect from the traditional King Arthur. At first I was a little apprehensive about it, but after a few quests I was sold on uncovering the whole story of Mordred and I enjoyed every minute making him into the new person he was becoming and became. + The characters/knights you uncover are captivating and each had their own unique abilities besides their class that made them special. I enjoyed trying out different parties, but ultimately i focused on about 8 different knights over the course of the game. These became my main "go to" knights for missions. My favorites besides Mordred were: Sir Kay, Sir Bors, Lady Dadraine, Sir Tygre, Sir Lancelot, Sir Percival, the White Knight and Merlin of course!         ----- TIP: The first couple acts I recommend using Mordred every quest if you can, a second tank or heavy hitter, an archer, and a mage. OR you can do really well once your Merlin and/or Archer level up past 10 by just taking one of them and then Mordred, another defender, and a champion. So basically you will have 3 tanks with complementing abilities and one range class to pick off the mages and archers. But I wouldn't do this until Act 3 or 4. + The Quest variety was very good in my opinion. The game certainly exceeded my expectations in this area. A few could get slightly repetitive on occasion, but no more repetitive than Xcom 2's missions. The story made me pretty much overlook any similar fights I would encounter. + The music, score, and sounds are absolute perfect and fitting for this grand story. + The events were great! I enjoyed reading them, (very well written and entertaining) and making the decisions on my characters morality as a leader was something I looked forward to doing. + Camelot/castle management was enjoyable. It was fairly simple, but a very nice and welcomed addition to the game, that kept things very interesting in between each quest. I found myself spending a lot of time deciding how to upgrade my knights, from selling outdated gear to buying new gear, to applying skill points. Along with the strategy of managing my gold and what upgrades to invest in Camelot. Not to mention how to handle injuries of my knights, should I send this guy to hospice or take him on a mission with half vitality, to sending knights to the cathedral to heal deep wounds to sending my knights to the training yard for free for a few turns or should I just speed up the training and send them on a joust for a few gold coins. It was fun to manage! + The Battles were the HIGHLIGHT of this game, great strategy, lots of enemies to slaughter, while always being outnumbered.. and i mean VERY outnumbered. It was always very rewarding for me to find ways to get out of a sticky situation, whereby by the initial looks of the fight I appeared like I was going to get absolutely raped. Then to turn it around and win the fight with less wounds that I ever expected. This was sooo rewarding and a hell of a lot of fun! + The mini map was a little confusing for me at first, but i after I went into the settings and changed it so it wouldn't rotate with me and stayed with North on the top, this helped me out tremendously. I liked how they did the map and how you explore around to find shrines, chests, added side quests, etc. -- What could they have done better -- - Added elevation to the maps. - Added destructible objects in the environment- Made the benefits of cover more clear. - Maybe a text box with statistics of each battle (e.g. how much damage did I do or didn't do and why) or an option to turn it on for the nerd in us all. ;-) OVERALL:This game had a lot of layers that I did not initially expect. I think this is what really made this game for me:The layers are:1. Event decisions2. Quests variety3. Camelot management4. Skill upgrades, equipment, and loot (in-between quests) 5. Real time Map exploration6. Awesome Turn-based battles with your party/knights7. Incredible grand storyI HIGHLY RECOMMEND THIS GAME. I hope they add some DLC's to continue the story even more and maybe consider a Knights Tale 2 someday down the road! I'm a fan! I give it a 9.5 out of 10. "If you love Tactical RPG's like Xcom and dark fantasy/medieval setting then this game is a MUST play!!"

_childDocuments_.review: For some reason I gave this game a positive review two years ago. Trying to replay it in 2024, I have no idea why. The core of King Arthur: Knight's Tale is a fun (if mindless) strategy game, but the designers have conspired to ruin the experience at every possible opportunity. The levels are unbearable slogs of pointless combat encounters with meaningless rewards. They are all horrifically protracted and drawn out with far more enemies than are necessary for no reason. The boss fights are agonizing. Every level is the same. The roguelike XCOM structure makes no sense given the narrative focus with Mordred as a protagonist, and being restricted to four heroes at a time is baffling. The classes have no variety and the gear and base management systems are unbelievably tedious. Every fight is exactly the same. At the point where I finally gave up on this second playthrough, I made it to a major boss fight, fought through countless pointless miserable battles that went on for way too long and were obviously padding, defeated the boss, only to find out that he had another phase, where he recovered 100% of his HP, summoned six ads, and then teleported my entire party into a single spot--they had been spread out--in what felt like a glitch. He then killed us all with a single round of AoE attacks.lol. lmao. ♥♥♥♥ this game. Avoid.

_childDocuments_.review: I can not recommend this game.Limiting your team to prebuilt knights at first seemed okay, but it gets pretty stale when there are no more.   The level of customization is an issue, I get that the lead character (to keep the narrative thread) needs to be, for the most part, the same in all the play-throughs, but the lack of custom builds, with not only their skills but lack of control of attributes, is lackluster. Another issue is the very closed design forces your team through a path where you must meet the boss at the end.   It may seem reasonable, but it limits the world when there is no discernible variation in what you must do--and limits the replayability of the map, like trying a different path next time.The maps are good but solidly two-dimensional.  They employ some good visual tricks to make a path appear raised, but this is much different from what you expect today.   One map promised something unusual; it was defending a cemetery, but it was not so much defending but the same as the other maps.   I admit the idea of protecting a location after the other maps had me psyched--until, again, I saw it. It had good voice narration and some exciting dialog,  but the character dynamics needed to be there.   And even the outcome of the dialogue was not very impressive, and I really wanted some shocking consequences.  The game started with a fascinating, almost dark mirror of the Arthur legend, which had a uniqueness that compelled me to buy it.  Great idea,  but the development path or time considerations took it down a much more static road that needed to be more worthy of the story.

_childDocuments_.review: This could've been a "mixed" review if Steam would've allowed it.TL:DR: interesting but flawed, grab it on sale if you have tolerance for bugs, potentially including a broken save file.A solid turn-based tactical combat/RPG hybrid with lots of similarities to xcom and the like, set in a dark fantasy world inspired by Arthurian legends, marred by a buggy engine, balance issues and game design without a clear direction.Tactical battles are the strongest part of the game. At the core it is a very good evolution of modern standards for tactical combat. A return to the proper AP mechanics is certainly helps make combat much more nuanced and complex. Some ideas are still to gimmicky for my liking but this does not hinder the gameplay.Home base management is a bit bare bones, with nothing particularly interesting, unique or impactfull. Just the run of the mill services(recruitment, healing, passive resource generation, minor incremental buffs etc). Plot in intriguing but very thin. This might've been ok for a regular tactics game for for a RPG/tactics hybrid it does feel like there's not much to it. It also seems that for the character who is supposed to be the protagonist, devs were lacking direction in terms of choosing between him being a character with his own personality or a pair of shoes for the player to fill.Voice acting is a bit of a mixed bag as well. Actors are clearly skilled but delivery is all over the place, which is usually due to dialogue lines being recorded without knowing much about the dialogue context or it's other participants.Visually, the game is good but nothing to write home about. I like the gritty and realistic art style, it's much more appealing compared to more cartoony style of the aforementioned fraxis xcom games. There are some visual glitches but nothing that will on its own, ruin your experience.Unfortunately, this cannot be said about other bugs. While the game is not completely plagued by them, there are certain issues that may significantly hinder the play(some players reported noticeable performance issues) or outright wipe your progress. As of the time of this review, there are a couple of known issues that either break the tactical gameplay or wipe all saves altogether. It does seem like only some players experience these(personally, I haven't been subjected to either) but there are enough reports out there for this to be a significant concern. In addition to that, there are balance issues which, while not particularly significant, are also adding more negativity to the overall experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Although there is a potentially good game here, in its present state it's not worth buying.First off, there is no excuse for this game to be 120gb install.  NONE.  I have games in my library with much better graphics, FMV, etc and they are not even close to 120gb in size.   Game stutters a lot, probably due to having to read through 120gb worth of files.  This shows poor optimization on the devs part.  You would expect stutters in games like Dying Light, DMC, etc not in a turn-based tactical game.The premise of the game, however, is a sign of hope for the future.  If you loved the X-Com games this would be right at home next to them.  It is, in many ways, X-Com set in Arthurian times.  There is research, moral choices and permadeath.  I did get the game refunded.  I will keep an eye on this game and if they can compress some files and get the size down A LOT, then I'll probably give it another try.  Until then, I strongly suggest waiting til the devs finish optimizing the game as it surely isn't right now.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Great graphics. They really did a good job with the voice acting as well. If you love games like Divinity Original Sin, you will also love this game. The potential for replayability is there too. My only complaint is that classes are non-changeable! But that's just part of the game design and it forces the player to make a balanced team rather than one absolute beast of a favorite character. This game calls for you to complete missions each separated in Acts (Act 1, Act 2, etc) fighting mobs of monsters and exploring to find loot. The turn-based combat makes you manage action points and spend them on skills, attacks, or movement. Characters have individual classes such as Defender, Champion, Vanguard, Arcanist, Sage, Marksmen that are set and non-changeable. The graphics are great on my GE75 Raider laptop. The story so far is interesting and the morality system is a neat addition that unlocks unique missions or buffs depending on what alignment you go for (Christian vs. Old Faith or Tyrant vs. Rightful). The gameplay is smooth for me. The difficulty level is pretty high. I chose to start off my first playthrough on Very Hard and Roguelite. This was a punishing experience. I recommend Classic over Roguelite for your first playthrough (trust me). Classic allows you to save intermittently and restart missions whereas Roguelite does not allow any mission restarting and autosaves for you after each encounter/fight. The missions are variable in difficulty as well. Sometimes you'll be mowing down everything in your path, and other times you quite literally crawl to the finish line.  The dialogue options do not offer any versatility but rather feel that all options lead to the same result or even the same reply from NPC's. Saying something respectful vs. choosing an option that's disrespectful often goads the same NPC reply. The RPG aspect of the game is missing. There's no costume customization, so the characters will look the same from beginning to end despite changes in gear. Overall, the game offers many different characters to experiment with and gives a story that is unique in the King Arthur dimension. The story was interesting, and I was impressed at the voice acting as well. Play it!
_childDocuments_.name: King Arthur: Knight's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun turn-based RPG game with a bit of strategy involved. While the game mechanics are simple, there is a layer of complexity involved that reminds me of playing Chess. The AI can be decent as well, at times choosing to ignore your tank to go for your lower-health party members. I really enjoy the medieval Britain lore and the visual effects can be captivating, however the written/audio dialogue can be a bit jarring at times- as if it was passed through Google translate (which I can give the company a pass on, as the gameplay loop is very enjoyable).
_childDocuments_.name: King Arthur: Knight's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Great TBS game with a weird twist on Arthurian Legend. The story is quite good with KA:KT starting after the ending of said legend while imagining all of the characters you know from the knights of the roundtable in a sort of afterlife. The easiest description of the mechanics of the game would be a fantasy xcom-like. The gameplay is fun and very tactical with things like unit facing being critical. Each class is distinct and you gain unique characters throughout that add to the variety. It does have some difficulty spikes but these are easily manageable with the multiple difficulty levels changeable pretty much on the fly. Lastly, I'm pretty impressed with the developers of KA:KT. They maintain a presence on the forums and respond to issues almost daily. They are also responsive to bugs and balance issues without making kneejerk changes to their game. If you are a fan of TBS games and fantasy settings you will probably like this game.
_childDocuments_.name: King Arthur: Knight's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: I normally wait to write a review. I rarely write a review unless a game is amazing or it is terrible.This game is amazing. It has all the elements that I love. If you read the description you already know there is deep authurian lore and tactical combat with a strategy/rpg element. That in and of itself is "Good enough" for me to automatically like it.But, I *LOVE* this game for one main reason: You are Mordred, a dread knight with a past that you cannot change. However, you can change your future.Yes, there are some linear or binary decisions in this game, but how it feels when you play the "tyrant"  - feels right.A lot of games give you the option of what I call "mustache evil" - the Snidely whiplash villain who is evil for evil's sake. That's dumb. mordred's dialogue is so much better when he chooses tyrant options. He has no regard for serfs and expects them to work. He doesn't just do destructive things. He expects them to toil. if he chooses the 'rightful' options, you get the sense that he is struggling with morality and seeking to atone for a past.The same of old way and christian. At first, I thought it may be mutually exclusive to be a Christian tyrant, but the way that plays out is that he is more like a Crusader who believes in killing heretics and crusades. It's also rather meaningful. even though the story continues based on your choices - there are consequences to decisions, including who you can recruit. The game feels well balanced, and honestly - the only thing I do not like is that there is no announced DLC or Part II announced yet - this is a game that is going to stand the test of the time. It's just good game design.

_childDocuments_.review: Over 25 hours into this, and I cannot recommend it. It's grindy, repetitive, and crashes from time to time. I never legitimately fought the big monsters you see in the videos and images on the Store page. Either they don't exist, or they're very deep in the game. I did every side quest and handled every event that popped up along the way, and felt like I was just spinning my wheels getting no where. The different battlefields look different, but feel the same. The story/lore of the game has nothing to do with Arthurian legend other than the names of the characters and places. If it didn't crash after I was an hour into a quest more than once, I would have played it through despite all that, but it did. I love Arthurian legend, and really wanted to love this game; sadly that isn't where things ended up. Find something else to play.

_childDocuments_.review: KA KT has good turn-based combat, lots of characters to develop with four classes and lots of unique variants of the classes. The "knights" are all representations of the knights and leaders of Arthurian legend. The voice overs, cut scenes, and graphics overall are very good. My only criticism of the game is that is does become a bit "grindy" / "samey" at times and that some knights are really good and others are not, which can require that you select certain knights and avoid others to be successful at higher difficulty. The game has multiple mutually exclusive "take this knight or that knight" decisions throughout the game. There are also different morality and religion choices that give you access to some knights and not others or apply a large loyatly penalty (which affects combat performance) to knights whose morality or religion are in conflict with yours. For example, if you are a Rightful leader, Tyrant knights will suffer loyalty penalties and some Tyrant knights may not offer their services to you at all. Between the morality and religion choices that in part decide which knights you can use at all or without penalty and the different difficulty levels, this game does offer some replay ability. Recommend:  8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Performance: Zero issues with the game crashing/freezing/stuttering on my 3440x1440 resolution at 200 FPS.  I have saved and reloaded a few times without any issues, and left the game running for about five hours on pause then came back without any issues. Gameplay: The game is enjoyable overall with easy to learn mechanics and the ability to put together a diverse team. Even similar classes will all eventually have similar abilities but at different points throughout the game. My only current issue is that so far the game has been very EASY - I chose to start on normal difficulty (I know I can raise it) since I wanted to see how it was planned out and I have just destroyed everything without losing any armor. I have 11 heroes unlocked all of whom are level six and I can put together really any combination and steamroll the missions. I will be raising the difficulty to compensate for this. Price: Honestly I am enjoying this game immensely, but I am unsure it should be a $45 price tag. It feels and plays like an indie game and should be priced along that route. It has a lot of bloated gameplay with exploring the map looking for gold/items ensuring that you push bag all the hidden fog before moving on to the next mission.

_childDocuments_.review: So, to start with the postives, I am playing this game on normal mode and I felt challenged, while never feeling like anything was unfair. I had to reload a few times to not lose some characters, but I hate losing characters. The story is strong and engaging enough to keep my attention through all the murdery bits. The graphics are pretty damn good and I rarely saw any glitches. It is a great "dark" setting without being too overly hard (though if You like that kind of thing they have modes for you). Cons: I have been having to play streaming from my laptop because this game makes my 3090 stop sending a signal to my monitor, not sure what the cause is, but it only happens with early access/indie games (had the same thing happen with Satisfactory and the new stuff in Raft).There isn't really a lot of explanation of systems (like the laws, decrees, and how getting multiple points of Christianity vs old god affects things (so I just went pure old god and righteous just in case).The last complaint is recent, and it is because of the new expansion. It is NOT optimized for a four person party, hell even when they give you a fifth NPC during a mission it is still ridiculous. It might not be as bad if they didn't close you into areas, but when you are surrounded by 15 fomorians and their minions and you have two squares behind you life gets ♥♥♥♥♥♥ real fast. Overall a great game, but the expansion definitely need some work or some free souls to start to get some gear (I had mostly relics on my characters and they were still getting owned come expansion.)I backed this project on Kickstarter.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of tactical RPGs, I was eager to try out King Arthur: Knight's Tale. However, despite its promising premise, the game ultimately fails to deliver. The pacing is slow and tedious, making it difficult to stay engaged. Furthermore, the characters lack depth, and the storylines are uninteresting, failing to capture my attention.To make matters worse, the repetitive gameplay only serves to exacerbate the game's issues. While the combat mechanics are decent, the overall experience is simply not worth the investment of time and effort.Overall, King Arthur: Knight's Tale is a bad game on almost every front. I cannot recommend King Arthur: Knight's Tale to fans of tactical RPGs.

_childDocuments_.review: Since this is still quite early into development there isn't much content. You can play a handful of missions and if you want to replay anything you have to continuously start a new game to do so. The price tag is objectively too high when the devs are using consumers at their primary testers; very obvious bugs are present in game. If you want to pay to be essentially be a qa  tester then this is for you. Early access is always quite ambiguous as some early access games are near complete products whilst others are just starting to come together; this certainly falls under the latter. This isn't worth the price tag unless you really like this studio or have a strong desire to submit feedback in its development. Devs tentative estimate is completion this year and given it's current state i would say it's a lot of copy paste assets and functions (that's why very basic things are bugged like armor values). From what i've gather that seems to be the trend for them. It could still be fun when it's finished but i expect to see lots of cutting corners. When things are released in a state of 'did you play your own game?' it does not inspire confidence.

_childDocuments_.review: Mostly fun and varied. This is exactly the kind of game type/setting I really enjoy so will admit I'm a bit biased to ignore some flaws, but overall really enjoyed it and binged my way through it. By the end it was a slog and a bit grindy and I was glad to end it though. I have approx 1.5 playthroughs so probably ~150 hours were on a single play-through on hardest difficulty which for some is just too much of a commitment. But if for you this is what you're after it might be a plus. For me it mostly was a positive thing to sink my teeth into.Positives:1. The theme/setting works well2. There's reasonable replay value with different alignment and a different "endgame" option3. Base upgrade system is decent4. Variety of items5. Variety of characters and synergies6. Variety of levels/enemies & a few bossesNegatives:1. The "walking around the map" to find fights, gold etc, can be a bit tedious after a while.2. The scenario difficulty varies hugely, some scenarios are over very easily and others can take hours of re-tries.3.The game is a bit too long/grindy. You could probably cut ~30% of the game out and it be just as fun.This is especially true if you play on easier difficulties - you'll bring the same squad every time and do the same actions most fights (I played Ironman hardest difficulty which forced me to vary my squad due to injuries but once I had a super squad that never got injured I brought this same squad for the rest of the game because I couldn't risk a "weak" squad getting stuck on an impossible scenario)

_childDocuments_.review: Even though King Arthur: Knight's Tale is a very decent game it's simply not recommendable as the graphics, the overall performance as well as the games stability are blatantly still stuck in alpha.Obviously there are other issues with the game as well as many positive things to say about it but everything is just overshadowed by the questionable performance paired with old graphics and mediocre game stability. So this is what this review will be focus on:.) The world map needs more GPU power than witcher 3 on ultra with simple hairworks enabled.World Map all settings maxed out: Default view:  Zoomed out:  World Map all lowest settings & everything disabled:Default view:  Zoomed out:  VSync is obviously always off & there is no frame cap, resolution = 1920x1080, full screen - no borderless or windowed mode. Tested with Nvidia Driver v516.40 release 15.06.2022 & v516.59 release 28.06.22.The white fog you see on the lowest settings screenshots is not a bug, this is what the low visibility setting looks like and what's required to be dialled in for okay-ish FPS on the worldmap. It will also whiten the screen like this with all other settings maxed out.Naturally there are no separate graphic options for the world map and the rest of the game.Btw. The recommended GPU is a nVidia 1060. I run a 1660 ti (manually oc’d to its stable limits) which has about twice the “power” of a 1060. So I leave you to imagine how utterly poor the world map would run on the recommended 1060 or its, likely even more struggling, AMD counterpart..) The general graphics are outdated but require, comparatively, oftentimes an insane amount of GPU power. In the right circumstances the game can look good but these circumstances are very, very rare and more often than not it just looks, at best, okay-ish or more like a mobile game for your phone.Maxed: All low/disabled:  Maxed in combat:  (keep in mind that this is still very early in the game so it likely only goes downhill from here)Honestly, Diablo 3 from 2012 looks almost as good as King Arthur does. (a part of the textures ofc.)Diablo 3 maxed screenshots:   King Arthur maxed:  <- seriously, look at this one.  And now we add in the fact that Diablo 3 barely even needs 25% of the GPU power which King Arthur does and are just left to wonder how that works. Games like Grim Dawn, XCom 2 (maybe even 1), Divinity: Original Sin or even the individual units from Total War: Warhammer 1, all look massively better than King Arthur does and yet require noticeable lower GPU power to do so. It's just mind blowing..) CPU usage spikes.I’m still running a quad core with HT, so 4c/8t on 4.3GHZ. Plenty enough for this game one would assume and it is, well technically. Yet I can measure CPU usage spikes up to pretty much 90% even when capped at 66 FPS. Why I do not know and I can't imagine what would possibly require that high CPU usage in this game (no, it's not the loading screen) but I might as well put it out there. .) GPU usage spikes.Similar to the broken world map there are areas in the game which will, instantly and w/o any reason, tank your FPS massively by maxing the GPU usage..) Loading is fast but it basically maxes out the read speed of my 860 EVO SSD. Never seen a game do that before... or even come close. So R.I.P. HDD users. (This issue is probably thanks to the recent installation size compression “patch”).) The text isn't even aligned. This is just one of quite a few examples.  (look in the middle).) Tutorial videos stutter the game. When the game shows you its PiP-videos (=Picture in Picture) your frame times will go unstable and you will likely feel the stutter going until you close them..) There's a button to highlight “interactive objects” but it does not work. Not even if you rebind it..) The UI for the graphic settings is pure s**t..) The minimap inside missions is drawn so half arsed that you oftentimes can't tell whether that's a passage, the end of the map or just a poor job. .) Achievements don't work properly. .) I had a “game crashed” pop-up but could continue playing normally and just alt-tab the popup away. After pressing “ok” on the popup, the game finally "crashed". Happened twice in 30h playtime.Also the crash window will automatically, w/o asking you for permission, submit the crash data to the devs. Not exactly certain here but I have a strong feeling that this is not GDPR compliant..) The game sort of “locks up” but continues to run normally just that you can't issue any inputs anymore, nor can you open the menu or do anything really so you have to kill it via the windows task manager.This also happened twice during my 30h playtime. With the two crashes from the point above and this two "lock ups" we are basically at one forced restart every 7,5 hours of playtime, noice. I dont know if all of this is sheer incompetence, malice or “just” lazyness but whatever it is, it nowhere near justifies the asking price of 45€.So dear steam reviewers:Stop accepting barely passable as being ok. It's not, even if it's “just” the graphics/performance and/or “just” the occasional crash.Incompetence should not be rewarded. Otherwise we will never get anything made properly anymore, ever. And dear Developers:Fix Your Game. When? Yesterday would have been appropriate. Or you know, better yet, before YOU decided to leave early access.However, I really do have to give props for making the missions run extremely smoothly. If FPS capped via RTSS the game sticks to my set 66FPS / 15.15ms framtimes inside actual missions. No hitches, no spikes, no frametime hiccups, not even by just a few MS, no nothing - an extremely smooth experience worthy of contesting ESports titles in this aspect. (Until any of the aforementioned issues strike that is…).

_childDocuments_.review: It's okay. There's a lot of wasted opportunity to make this a good or even great game. The story itself is good, but suffers from very lousy dialogues or, more often, monologues. Lady of the Lake: "Oh no, they mustn't go there."Mordred: "I'm gonna go there."The voice acting is terrible and kills any immersion. It's like the male roles were narrated by Cpt. Raimond Holt from Brooklyn 99: The female voices are not any better. So far, 10 hours in, the game crashed on me a single time, but the autosave literally saved the situation. What makes me recommend this game is the combat system which, so far, seems to be done very well. There's no strategic layer and the economical system is completely pointless. But the game does a good job at scratching that "give me some shiny new things to put in my character's equipment slots"-itch we roleplayers are so dependend on. So all in all, on a scale from 1 to  5 I'd give this game 3.6 points. Not great, not terrible.
