_childDocuments_.review: Totally subjective, but I think that the turn-based strategy loop is excellent - good diversity of character classes, great upgrade system with real impact, a basic RTS system with building upgrades, etc... the core of this game is excellent, as is the overall 'look' - the animations are excellent, as is the overall feel of the battles.The complication comes with some tech issues I encountered, that seem to stem from a Vega-class GPU issue that causes persistent crashing around mission level 4. I tried everything to solve it, but nothing worked until I tried playing it on my non-Vega laptop, and had no issues at all. Obviously if you have a Vega card, Google the issue first, but I'd avoid it - there are dozens of Vega owners reporting the same thing. Even if you don't, I might recommend this game closer to the $20 range rather than the current $40 range - I'm 20 hours in, and although I enjoy the gameplay loop, I have to admit that one battle does feel alot like the next, and the next, and so on - you can change out characters, you can mix up classes and upgrades, but it only changes so much... there aren't bonuses for higher ground, there are obstacles, but not really a 'cover' system like X-com and the like... again, I really like the feel of the battles, but its hard to avoid the fact that there's alot of repetition.For my money, Solasta was worth closer to the $40-$60 range, whereas I think Arthur is a safer bet closer to $20, where I got it on sale. Even if I quit now, which I have no plans to, I think its more than delivered $1 per hour's worth of entertainment, no question.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been out a few years and I took a fast look at Neo-core Games effort into the world of Camelot. Let's get to what I liked and what needs to be better.What I enjoyed:Aesthetics: Old school, Gothic medieval presentations that made the original Disciples, Heroes of Might and Magic, and terrific art-style that struck the heart of sword wielders fans. So far so good.Class Warfare: The game is described beautifully as classes rule. Tanks, DPs, Range, Vanguards, Monkeys! Magic, all great stuff. Lore: It will honor those classic tales of Camelot for sure. Gear: Gimme that gear. Have at Thee! Potions! Three tier character skill builds. Buildings: Yep, like Darkest Dungeon or Heroes of Might and Magic, you get building bonuses.New Ideas: Morality, Vitality and Essence systems give you a nice twist to normal character building, but...Sounds: Voice, Light blood, Sounds, turn base tactics, and role fantasy are developed well. What I feel they need to improveIsometric; Again no one is learning from Mordheim's great inclusion of third person environmental development. This falls to good old isometric, nothing wrong with that, but its been done to death. Developers need to get it through their heads, players have out grown this overhead view. Put them into the action. TRPG: This plays like a combat objective game than a old fashion role playing game. Broken Builds: Yep, you will build super tanks and crushing dps builds that can cut into the challenge of the game. stay off the internet, or they are playing for you. Morality: I would have liked to have seen new created characters that you don't face later if you don't select that route. This truly hurts replay-ability. Graphic miss match: The portrait should match the animation. Details matterRepetitive Tactics: After a while you will grow weary of the same battles.VS system: Done to death in base chess implementation in turn base games. This again offers nothing new as 4, 5, 6 vs endless chess board enemies have been done forever. Bring something new to your army collecting. Be creative in this old dull format. Final Take:Look, despite nothing new here in the massive library of turn base games made in the past forty years. King Arthur does a lot right than wrong. It will give you plenty of hours of fun and if you love turn based, then this one may be for you. You may get 30 heroes and plenty of combinations and despite its developing notations and size of this game, which was way too much. You are limited due to the parameters they set upon themselves. RPG's need to push the envelope of not just mutation and upgrading systems, but go beyond the chess board. King Arthur is a fun game and its base has the potential to be built on, but will be constricted by its template mechanics. See the video game-play up top in discussion to see if the game play is for you. Wait for a nice sale and you may have another addition to old school turn base games. Sir Mordred and his knights are old school fun.  My Score 3.4 out of 5.

_childDocuments_.review: nice game, main focus is on the turn based combat. Kind of similar to Expeditions Rome combat, but instead of a bunch of legionaires you field just 4 but supernatural knights.Edit:I have finished the game now and the combat went from worrying about a single enemy, shield bashing him to knock him down etc...to laying lightning storms and snow fields on the battlefield to shock and chill whole entire enemy squadrons so they cant act at all. So at least in my playthrough the combat was not samey like other people claim. There was a nice progression in power and fantasy from lvl 1-20Outside of combat its pretty light, a few events, equipping your knights, building some things in your castle...kind of like Darkest Dungeon but the stakes are lower.What i really like about the game is that the atmosphere and some of the art reminds me of Disciples 2, but i guess that info is useless to 99.99% of people on steam, but still.

_childDocuments_.review: King Arthur: Knight's Tale takes the classic story around King Arthur and his Knights of the Round Table and adds more fantasy and grittyness to it.In short the gameplay can be described as Fantasy XCOM. The combat and management outside of combat are very strategical but if you just want to play through the story you can just adjust the difficulty (at any point in the game).Gameplay 8.5/10 - Very enjoyable, strategical combat and kingdom managementSoundtrack 6/10 - The tracks that are in the game are pretty darn good, but after hours of playing it can get repetitive. The game needs more tracks that differ from mission to mission and depending on how far the player has progressed in the gamePlot 8/10 - If you only know the surface of the story surrounding King Arthur, then in this game you will learn much more about it and all the characters that are involved in the tale. Thus far I have really enjoyed slipping into the role of the treacherous Sir Mordred and as a player that usually dislikes playing "the bad guy" I really like that the game allows the player to morph Mordred into a morally gray or even good protagonist.Visuals 8/10 - Level design, ui design, character design certainly are good but still far from perfectVoice Acting 8/10 - About 80% of the game is voice acted (Thank god!) and the quality of it is really good which in result really helps to get the player involved in this games universe.

_childDocuments_.review: A surprisingly solid game. Well designed and good atmosphere, a lot of replay value. It's a hard tell from its marketing materials exactly what's special about it, and I must say there isn't a lot, but it's just very well rounded and designed to fit its theme, also polished enough to not feel any absurdities that's so common plagued even high production games nowadays. Though I'm never into all the king arthur stuff and have no idea who is who, it still got very decent gameplay value. Only wish there is a quick start mode that gives you an initial set of knights, without going through the tutorial stuff again for each new start.
_childDocuments_.name: King Arthur: Knight's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: The content is there and the combat system is done right, but when a game is so boring and repetitive it can't be a thumbs up review.Every map and every encounter is scripted, and this should mean a lot variety in map design and combat situations, but indeed it is the opposite. Every map is the same and every encounter is the same.Enemy variety is really bad, undead already feel old on the second encounter and they have the armored knight and the archer type. It's 20 missions I'm hoping that the next one will have something peculiar but nope, same map, undead knights and undead archers.There are 30+ charactrers to unlock and use, but there are only 6 classes so all these characters are just reskins with the same pool of abilities. BTW there's a morality an loialty system that forces you to dismiss forever the vast majority of characters you unlock. Maybe it's for balancing sake, but for sure it never felt fun to kick away characters forever from your team.The story is superlinear and nothing appeals for a second run, but i highly doubt the vast majority of players will ever see the end of their first run anyway.Nowaday there are many turn based games made right to waste money and time with this one.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of both Arthurian legend and tactical RPGs, I can't say I see the appeal. From a story perspective, it spits on the core Arthurian narrative in favor of kind of a mid-90s antihero vibe, if you can even call it a story. Familiar names are brought up but the character of the knights involved is captured only in little text biographies you can read if you choose to do so. (By the way, knights ride horses. it's kind of an important detail that the devs somehow missed). From a gameplay perspective, at a tactical level, it makes you think, but every action you take looks and sounds bland and uninspired. Missions drag on, and I often would save and exit halfway through one just to give my boredom a little time to wear off. There are enough good games out for me to set this one down even though people say it gets better.

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't an absolute yes. But overall, I enjoy the game. The Morality System is an interesting mechanic that lends the game depth and replayability. The classes are fascinating. The base building is sufficiently in-depth for TTRPGs. There could be a bit more roleplay between characters. And the choice and consequence is gradual, nothing Earth-shattering like Virmire in Mass Effect. But it's not done poorly for what it is. The game is reasonably well-balanced. The difficulty spikes at the beginning of each act are logical. And the variety of classes (and characters within each class) makes for quality replayability.My one complaint with the game is the story is so determined to be grimdark that the "heroes" are all gray goo. Joe Abercrombie couldn't be this morally ambiguous for 50hrs of story. And that didn't convince me before grimdark became as overused a genre as traditional fantasy it claims to rebel against. Tone matters. And the lack of tonal variety definitely impacts the enjoyment of the game. And that negatively impacts the replayability I mentioned above. Also, like every Tactical RPG, there's a slog. Missions feel repetitive, grinding heroes through side content is definitely a thing. You can train heroes. But that still takes considerable time to bring them up to speed. If you've played XCom-style games, you know what the mid-game is going to consist of. You either accept this as part of the nature of such games. Or you don't. All in all, a good game. Worth playing for TRPG fans. Definitely worth playing if you love Grimdark. But if you want to feel like you're changing the world, for better or ill, then it becomes a harder sell. And if you're not interested in TRPGs, it's not for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed the game at first. Love the narrative and the game type. However after 17h (second-half of act 2), the game slowly becomes boring and annoying to me. You are simply forced to aimlessly wonder in big and confusing maps facing endless waves of attack and ambush. and for what? At this point of the game, there isn't much interesting development in narrative or character. There isn't much freedom in choosing your playing styles. All RPG elements has worn off, leaving the game sort of like a fancier version of angry birds. The game has also come harder towards the end even after the player has completed all side requests and has carefully managed 'the castle'. This gave the player no sense of development or compliment.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game.I only have one complain about it, and it's that there is no randomness on the map and mission generation. I wish there would be even the slightest variance on where mobs spawn, or exact enemy group configurations, to increase the replayability a bit, but sadly it's all scripted, so it hinders the game a bit (as opposed to XCOM for example, where most missions can be randomized in certain maps, tilesets, enemies, etc, whilst the key ones are always the same).That said, still did two complete playthroughs to experience different facets of the game, and was frequently impressed with the aesthetics, the cinematics, the story, the enemies, it's just a fantastic effort. The end game missions are also a cool opportunity to min-max your comp with added challenges, whereas most games just end, and you never get to play at full strength.The fact that there is a new season coming soon, and an expansion further ahead, makes me extremely excited for new playthroughs in the future, and the fact that there are ~some~ gameplay altering mods is also a plus.Love it, high recommendation for turn-based games fans. Will replay often.(I'm a sucker for turn-based strategy games. Stuff like XCom & 2 & Long War, Divinity Original Sin & 2, Phoenix Point, and all that jazz)

_childDocuments_.review: First things first, 88 hours and fully completed on normal Rightful Christian morality picks.  Huge thumbs up from a fan of the XCOM/Pheonix Point game lover.  This game scratches a number of itches for turn based RPG'ish strategy.  The story is a plus that I would classify as "good Medieval fantasy with a few nice twists".The game is a tale of post death Arthur and Mordred.  There are some good plot twists, and choices to make regarding the story (mostly flavor but some game impacting).Game difficulty can be switched on the fly.  Game choices can be rough, and permadeath (with a caveat) is possible.  The depth of the game mechanically cannot be understated for something without a AAA pedigree, there are so many layers to your choices for gear, skills, and morality, and class that it was close to overwhelming.  Combat is immersive and at higher difficulties very, very punishing (I boosted the difficulty a number of times through the playthrough for certain areas to get a sense of it).Gear matters and there are some added abilities to items that create some great combo's.  Do your homework (plan choices ahead of time) for the skill tree and morality tree.  Each can be tricky and you while you can respec at cost for skills, morality choices are permanent.If you want to max out characters you have to be a completionist.  I really wish someone would have told me to explore every nook and cranny at the start.  Training multiple characters can get both expensive and be time consuming (which matters).  Filling up a round table also requires doing pretty much everything and not having a lot of bad luck with injuries (which take your characters our of action for a bit).I highly reccommend spreading out bonus skill/exp to your top four choices for party members.  When in doubt, give it to Mordred.  If you min/max, DO NOT use immunity essence potions until you are sure your build/top end gear wont double up and feel like a waste.  On the other hand, holding onto essence pots the whole game means you didnt get much use out of it until the end, my suggestion...save em till Act 2 and figure things out there when you have an idea of your main party makeup and are further along the morality trees.There is alot more to love about the game but this thing is long enough for now.  Have fun!

_childDocuments_.review: This is definitely recommended. Fans of turn-based games will enjoy this immensely. The story is not anything to write home about, but it is not totally garbage either. The game is brilliant, very, very addictive.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay: 4/10Story: 7/10Graphics: 5/10I am a die hard fan of top down turn-based RPG's with over 300-400 hours between X-Com, Divinity, and co.The first 10-15 hours of the game is quite enjoyable, being introduced to all the new systems, and the world. I don't know too much about the lore of King Arthur, but I was originally quite intrigued. Giving you a varied amount of choices through dialogue and "side-quests." The game-play itself is your standard turn based combat, but with no RNG which is good or bad depending who you are. So the fights pretty much play itself out without too much thought involved. The AI itself is very bad.Now for the bad, after 15 hours you will notice the game play gets quite repetitive. The battles are all the same, the missions are all the same, and I would say I had only one slightly 'close' encounter during the first 20 hours that made me have to use my brain slightly. The fight mechanics are quite shallow to say the least with no variations at all. The RPG elements begin to fall off because your "equipment" doesn't really change how your characters look or feel. They're just simple stats with the occasional "grant ability: heal." You also cannot organize your inventory at all?Building Camelot feels quite... underwhelming. The world feels dead, even exploration of the maps is lackluster. I can see the potential that this game has, and I tried my best to really like the game, but it needs a lot more work and content. This is a perfect game for an intro to top down turn-based RPG, but it doesn't hold a candle to X-Com or Divinity.

The gameplay, while not particularly challenging for a turn based (like Divinity or Pathfinder) is fun and enjoyable to repeat. I'm 32 hours in and have still not finished Act 3, and I know there's endgame content as well. Potentially interested in another playthrough to go about the morality tree a different way (choice tree mentioned earlier). Would definitely recommend this game to anyone who likes turn based, choice games!

_childDocuments_.review: I really would like to recommend this game. But I won't. Actually, I like the genre, I liked how it is made, the idea is pretty good. But taking everything at once it didn't work out at all. You may compare the game with Divinity Original Sin, and Larian Games wins without a fight.The main problem with King Arthur is that this game is very monotonous, repetitive and as a result very boring. It takes about 45 hours to complete, at during these 45 hours you will see the same surroundings (except some locations in part 4) and will hear to the same pathetic dialogs. The storyline is another issue. Actually, the idea was initially great - it is visible that the plot author really likes arthurian tales. So it would be really great to use all the characters and their relationship to build the story and secondary quests. But know - for example, . So all these nice tales are simply lost in vain. However, each knight has a very detailed story. So why you cared so much and never used that?The world is actually dead, there's no sign of life in the conversation which you are hearing again and again and again: - Save me! - Thank you knights. As a conclusion, I may say that the game may be so much better. It looks raw, like it was planned to do much more, but only 10% were budgeted. There were some bright spots in this sad story - an homage to Monty Python and the Holy Grail (the rabbit, favourite colour and others). These things were lovely and made me continue when I was about to give up. But apart from that the experience was upsetting.

Much of what I could write about has already been said better by other reviewers so I´ll just add something I´ve really noticed after having restarted the campaign on hard 3 times. _childDocuments_.review: Whoa!  When they said "Early" they weren't kidding - what you have here is a fully functioning tech demo of a very (very!) short section of the game.  And a very pretty turn based fantasy brawler it is; leaning in heavily on a Darkest Dungeon vibe/party structure - quest/campfire rests/quest/return; with something like a Banner Saga combat that, like Banner Saga, sometimes feels a little basic.  Since hits are automatic (no RNG or skill checks) it plays more like Gloomhaven or a tactical board game than a "roll playing" RPG.  Move character here.  Hit thing.  Move character there.  Hit things.  Hopefully it blossoms later.The plot is Grimdark as grim; a Diablo like corrupted Avalon where the absence of Arthur has resulted in the Lady of the Lake resurrecting you, his mortal enemy, from your mortal wounds to help rid the land of the scourge besetting it. You set about rebuilding the Round Table and purging the land of evil, well, the guys slightly more evil than you.I hope they also make combat a bit crunchier and weightier; right now you are pretty much rewarded with numbers when you thump your foes - hit locations/effects, more individuated powers/weapons, killcam zooms and meatier/gorier feedback would be good.  Its a little clean, and it needs the crunch of dirt under its fingernails. And the balance... sheesh. One early side mission has you catching 5 crossbowmen over a distance, with spawning undead mobs under your feet, and a boss that does DoT and ranged attacks... simultaneously, with the party unable to heal in-combat. Right now, its like walking in on your Mom starting to make a cake and getting the first lick of the bowl, and hoping it turns out well.  And yeah, its pretty tasty.  Pretty as heck. If they lean in on the story and city building (you rebuild Camelot), assert more character through the individual knights as champions, and differentiate the powers/classes/option a little more, could be great!

_childDocuments_.review: Fixed all of the issues I noted below. The music is notably great.  OLD REVIEW:Why I gave it a chance: turn based historical rpg with decent graphics and a storyline. I was really looking forward to this one. What it has going for it:- armor system is actually pretty good, the mechanic works and adds a layer of tactical strategy in fights- the storyline is pretty good, although the characters are canned stereotypes- the turn based combat has a good ui and actually hits the spot between fun and difficult Why I gave it a negative review: - $40 price tag for a game that in its current state gives about 5-6 hours of gameplay- frame rate, this just isn't optimized to warrant a full price release- ironman mode doesn't save mid mission, so if you mess up just quit out of the game normally and the game will load before you started the mission. Also, since you can't manual save that means if you exit at any point during a mission you have to start over - stealth option seems like it could be powerful on some units but zero opportunities to actually use it  - Empty maps that seem procedurally generated, and that's not a good thing when so many side paths go nowhere and do nothing- movement inputs are clunky, and buffered keyboard inputs sometimes continue even after choosing a different move direction (only way to clear the buffer is right click move, this only happens when using WASD)- progression early is stunted at best, you don't have enough resources to build both the cure wounds and heal vitality buildings when you need them, let alone if your party gets cursed by the first banshee you see- poor optimization overallOverall, this isn't worth the price tag as is. This would need another 1-2 years of polish and added content.

_childDocuments_.review: It would be unfair not to recommend this game.... and then comes the "but". It just feels like a blend of some of the most amazing games I've ever played and not a very good one. The game is divided in to two maps. The campaign map which is where you launch your missions from and manage your knights and town, and a mission map on which you do the tactical fighting and exploring until you find every piece of loot.The campaign map resembles the darkest dungeon the most where you train your knights, choose their skills, build your town and research upgrades, send your knights to rehab, select your party and launch the next mission etc. Simply said the darkest dungeon copy with an exception of some nice touches like knights' loyalty and morality chart.The mission map is just an annoying square map which you have to fully explore like a good loot addict. You move in real time until you encounter enemies at which point that small portion of the map becomes a turn based tactical battle arena. The whole thing resembles divinity original sin 2 but in a very simplified way. it also has some xcom elements like a square grid and half cover and full cover which feels so pointless considering that most of the knights and enemies are melee. However unlike in xcom and divinity, in this game elevation advantage does not exist which i felt like was a big miss. The tactical combat complexity when compared to similar games made me feel like I was playing chess where every playing field is virtually the same meaningless grid with a couple of  meaningless pillars and walls here and there.In conclusion i cannot say that the game is bad. Like i said at the start this is a blend of some of the most amazing games I've played but if you played those games like me you will find this one underwhelming. PS the size of 120 GB for this game is just ..... no comment.

_childDocuments_.review: No single killer flaw, but it's death by a thousand cuts. Critically, the game is very unstable, I'm getting a CTD every hour or two of place; it's also poorly optimised going by the noise of my fans. And this might just be me, but there's something about the tiny fonts and undifferentiable sprites on a low contrast, drab background that makes my eyes water profusely if I try to play the game for more than an hour at a time.In terms of gameplay the main problem is that the battles aren't really tactical; they just involve getting swamped by the same 3 enemies every battle (shield dude, archer dude, two-handed dude). The options to fight back are limited, uncreative, and barely change from one battle to the next. The "mission" maps (a layer between the campaign over world and the turn based battles) involve clumsily walking around drab terrain filled with invisible walls in order to stumble into battles or click on loot as you see it. The base-building at Camelot is an uninspiring exercise in clicking through skill trees for the sake of it, and the same holds for party management generally. Because you have more heroes than good equipment, the game encourages you to redistribute it between every mission to have the 4 you'll embark with outfitted well. When the most effective way to play the game is also the dullest, that's bad design.It's not just the mechanics that are disappointing. The dialogue and world-building give the impression of a 13 year old trying to be as embarrassingly emo as possible, while the voice acting is painfully over-exaggerated. I burst out laughing when some zombie knight, with a voice so gravelly it would put Batman to shame, said "we will drench the earth with your blood". Even in a caricature of grimdark fantasy that would be too much, in a game trying to play it straight it's ridiculous. And it's constantly like that, with characters reminding you of how they're massive edge lords at every opportunity. Only to then go "ouch, that really hurt" when hit in combat.It's not all bad however. The 2-axis morality system seems like it might help replayability some what, and interacts with the base-building events reasonably well. The ability to have the heroes who are "off-duty" go on missions or train on there own is an interesting idea. The two-tier HP system where some recovers after every mission but damage beyond that carries over to the world map is a nice balancing act.The game doesn't do anything terribly (beyond being critically unstable), but it doesn't do much right either. None of the 3 tiers of the game (battles, missions, world) work particularly well. It's just about good enough for me to keep going when I'm very bored, but that's a much lower bar than me actually recommending the game to someone. If you want a low-fantasy turn-based tactical RPG, I'd say check out "Fell Seal: Arbiter's Mark" first.

_childDocuments_.review: Arthurian turn based strategy. Control Mordred after his death and the fall of Camelot. The Lady has chosen Mordred as the defender of Avalon after Arthur resurrection brought him back as a bloodthirsty monster. Gather the resurrected, or in one case undead, knights to form your own round table, rebuild Camelot, and rule as either a righteous or tyrannical king and as one that either sides with the Christian or Old faith.There are 33 recruitable characters (up to 11 you can keep in service) that have their own passive positive and negative traits, morality that influences their loyalty, many having different or solely unique skills either replacing attacks or adding to skill trees, and they tend to have their own look or type of weapon for a different visual flair. Most can be gained on one playthrough but eight are unique to your morality and religious path meaning you can only get four of those eight and four of them are unique to your combined morality and religious path meaning you only can get one of those four. Each of those characters also has their own unique mission where you recruit them. All eight classes are well made with good synergy, different ways to build them from their skill choices and the gear you acquire, and some of the gear may work for a class but may be much more useful on a particular character with the unique abilities to compliment it. Some characters end up changing up their class quite a bit with the Faerie Knight being the Arcanist made class but having defensive abilities, a teleport, and longer ranged melee attacks that turn him into a strong and tanky melee combatant, Mordred is a defender and while he is very survivable he trades the support abilities and taunts important for the others in the class for more damage and a few lightning and debuffing spells, Lancelot trades a lot of the defensive skills of the other Champion classes to focus on the damage side and being a bit more maneuverable while gaining a powerful support skill. The Marksmen class was very useful in the beginning but was the only one that started to fall off a bit over time for me on the hard difficulty while the Defender class (apart from Mordred) could be very situational depending on how maps were set up (very useful on some maps to taunt enemies, run away, and have the enemy units charge into awaiting overwatch attacks by your other characters). Merlin was the only character that felt completely broken (ignoring that I didn't get any of the tyrant or Christian locked heroes) being able to wipe out entire battlefield alone with fire attacks with the right equipment and being able to set up decoys to tie up enemies.In between battles you will be upgrading Camelot with gold and building supplies to improve the merchant store, magic store, training facilities for characters you aren't using, and healing locations that are meant for removing permeant injuries or healing vitality health that starts to take damage after characters lose their armor and HP. Events show up that might either have you just making a decision to gain or lose supplies, loyalty, alignment or faith reputation or there can be missions to send a knight on where that can come back having succeeded or failed (typically based on sending one of the correct class/alignment/faith) with more experience, loyalty, with items, or with injuries.Good production value. Decent voice acting. The few cutscenes the game has look good. It is a long game with a lot of side missions, where ever character even has has their own recruitment mission. After you finish the main story in act four there are new missions in what is basically a kind of fifth act with less story elements. The length can make the game drag a bit but with the frequency of new characters, leveling up characters bringing new useful abilities, and each act introducing a new faction of enemies it never got boring. Act 4's side missions even see you with unique quests depending on what morality and faith you followed, running into some of the characters you would have missed. New free content seems to be planned with the first free update having you play through a few story missions controlling what was an enemy faction in the main game.It should have allowed you to customize your movement formation that decides how your characters stand when a battle starts more, you can only take four knights with you at a time but many missions will see one or two other characters joining you and the set formations are only made for parties of four. Ridiculously high space requirement of over 100GB (edit: they have now significantly reduced the size), PC runs a bit hot for this type of game though not to the point that it is causing problems. There were some bugs that have been recently fixed and there are still a few issues with some items and certain character traits and skills but nothing game breaking, anything that I noticed seems to be something they have plans to fix.Screenshots:

_childDocuments_.review: The game is much more Darkest Dungeon than XCOM. Overall quite polished and the production value here is surprising. But now with 30 hours in, playing on hard, I just can't find the motivation to continue the story, which I think I'm not even close to 50% yet.And this is the issue: the game is super slow and grindy across all fronts: story is obtuse and confusing; characters are uninteresting, don't banter with each other and have no interaction among themselves; castle meta progression is uninspired and unsatisfying; combat and missions, while having a decent enough system underneath, end up being samey and repetitive.When you think on some other similar tactics games: Battle Brothers, XCOM, Darkest Dungeon, etc they at least offer some strong points outside the core tactics combat itself to keep us motivated: either a strong story, good theme, customizable characters, meaningful meta progression, unique encounters and challenges, etc. But this is not the case here. While the arthurian legend is familiar, it is done in a unique but honestly uninteresting way, and since your characters are all pre-set, you lose the power that other games have in making your own unique units and creating characterization for them in your mind, your own head-canon.So why the positive recommend? Welll as I said, I was pleasantly surprised by the polished production quality that the game has overall. Oh and the music is excellent, albeit there is only a few tracks, all of the are top tier. From an aesthetic perspective, if you told me this was some lost cRPG from the classic era I would have believed you. And the combat is decent enough as well and held up for about 15 hours of gameplay.It's just not enough for 30h of gameplay (and counting! like I said it seems that I'm not even close to the halfway point of the game which is just ludicrous for a story based game to be this slow and grindy) so I've about had my fill and I'm done with the game. Give it a try for yourself but for me, even as a hardcore fan of tactical games, as I described above I find the other elements of the game to be lacking.

TLDR: I've reversed my recommendation and I am totally stoked about it! Tons more content, released later with a lot of improvements. And it wasn't abandonware! This game is solid all around from the story choices, party choices, turn based tactics combat, animations, etcIf you like xcom style gameplay with solid story and tons of replayability, this is for youOld: Tons of potential, want to reverse my recommendation as fans of the devs and prior games, do not believe will follow EA timeframe, too much missing content, prime candidate for proof of concept and abandonware

_childDocuments_.review: Quite a bit to enjoy in the game but a number of related design flaws lead, ultimately, to a frustrating experience.So what are the shortcomings?* The heroes/classes are seriously imbalanced and it is all too easy to make poor choices which, when you eventually realise you made bad selections, can't be reversed.* Due to the injury system heroes are sometimes unavailable whilst they heal up which, in turn, means that you need to maintain strong A and B Teams but a couple of bad hero choices and your B Team won't be viable.* B Team heroes can train (level up) whilst the A Team is away on missions but seats in the training centre are limited. It is impossible to keep all 12 heroes properly levelled up so, once again, if you make a couple of bad choices it isn't possible for the under levelled heroes to recover.* Game balance is generally quite good but there are still a few missions that present huge spikes in difficulty. If you have unwittingly hobbled yourself by choosing the 'wrong' heroes you are toast (a problem greatly exacerbated by the issues referred to above).* RNG - Getting a strong party of heroes is not only dependant on making informed choices but also upon gear but gear drops are RNG. Get lucky on drops, figure out a decent build and you are golden but if the RNG gods are displeased with you then your team of limping heroes will really struggle.I got to Act 4 before finally giving up the struggle. If I could be bothered with a second play-through I now have the knowledge to avoid most of the pitfalls but, for now at least I have had enough!

_childDocuments_.review: Sad to say, but not great. Questionable balance and design, lack of variety, and mostly terrible voice acting and visuals. I think most of the other reviews have covered those issues sufficiently.But the real thing that soured this for me was the health and injury system. I'm writing from the perspective who chose to play on the highest difficulty, so that might've exacerbated the issues with the underlying system. Allow me to elaborate.Your heroes essentially have 3 health bars - armor (reduces damage), health (basically temporary HP), and vitality (permanent HP). Damage to vitality is persistent, and can only mostly be healed between missions only, which either takes a lot of time, or costs some resources to do quickly. In-mission, when you start taking permanent health damage, no matter how big or small, you start suffering permanent injuries. These also can be healed, but they are done separately (!) from health. These can vary from absolutely meaningless, to utterly crippling (no attack of opportunity, losing AP on hit, etc). This whole system could in theory be really cool to encourage you to be very strategic about keeping your guys super safe from permanent damage, but that's simply not numerically possible if you're trying to clear the maps fully. You ARE going to take vitality damage. You ARE going to suffer injuries. After 10 hours of playtime, I basically have a roster of half-dead cripples, and even after pumping all my resources into healing upgrades, I -cannot-  bring a fully healthy team into missions. Which would be fine, but then I am faced with fights where it is numerically impossible for me to win without losing characters, because the encounters were likely built with healthy characters in mind. And the fights are pretty damn tough, the game does not pull punches. I like that every fights is essentially a giant puzzle to kill everything before suffering major damage, which is sometimes doable, but oftentimes you WILL have to tank some big hits, which can be game-losing if your characters already came in injured.So yeah, plenty of interesting ideas in this game, but I question their execution. The full asking price for this game is kind of ludicrous for the quality it provides.

_childDocuments_.review: Maps are a little repetitious, class mechanics could be improved, and the gearing system is quite basic. However, it still manages to pull off great turn-based combat that remains fun and engaging. The story is decent enough to keep you interested, and it features an end-game for those who really enjoy the combat and wish to keep on grinding. There is also some replay-ability as each religion/morality yields unique characters and you will need more than one play through to experience them all. There is also resource management to consider to unlock/upgrade buildings, gain extra character slots, heal your party and purchase new gear which adds a unique element. Overall a great game for anyone who enjoys turn-based combat. The difficulty options scale well and is welcoming enough for those who are new to turn-based combat on the easier difficulties while still providing a challenge for veterans on the harder difficulties.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun in the early game. It all goes out the window in the late game. Suddenly you get swarmed with enemies, but have few (if any) AEO/defensive options to fend them off with. Unit types that are OP in the early game are suddenly useless, and you realize you've invested all your gold/time/expereince leveling up units that are now liabilites. The devs actually programed in a cover system, which they make decent use of in the early game. Yet in the late game there's no cover available in any of the encounters. Your guys are just... out there. Trying to guess the enemies range and hoping they aren't in it.  It's like they never bothered to playtest anything past the first half of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked previous King Arthur games for it´s dark theme and RTS/RPG combination.New Arthur game is more squad focused tactical RPG with base (Camelot) management.Now you live the story of dreaded Mordred, nemesis of King Arthur in dark and ruthless world of Britannia/Avalon. _childDocuments_.review: This game is really great. The graphics are awesome, the setting is cool, the main mechanics are really nice, it is just great.And yet, there is one mechanic that makes it unbearable: Everything you do on the strategic level is timed in played missions. So if you need something to get finished for your next mission, and it takes one mission to finish, then you are out of luck. e.g. I had Sir Mordred badly wounded after a side mission. Tough luck, no big deal, had enough gold for the Cathedral, so all good. Sent him in, one mission until he is healed again. The problem: I only had one mission left to play at this point, and that mission required Mordred to be there. So... Catch 22... Game broken, Game lost, throw everything away and start from the very beginning again.Or choose to cheat... This is such a stupid design decision, I can't even find words for it...

_childDocuments_.review: So i'll start by saying there's still some changes that the game needs to make, like some skill passives do literally nothing currently. _childDocuments_.review: It's a very fun and solid turn based RPG game. The graphics are good with a few small visual bugs here and there. The combat system has a good amount of depth and character building. The main issue with the variety of builds involves the status effects, primarily bleed and poison. There are many enemies, and an entire enemy faction type, that are just immune to these effects and this obviously upsets people because they feel it limits their build options. This is mostly an early game problem however. In the end game where the enemy variety is much larger and having more gear and characters etc to pick from you can really design your team to better suit what you're going to fight as the missions tell you ahead of time what enemy type you will be fighting. Beyond that, there is a bit of a balance problem between the class types. Defenders, champions and arcanists are definitely stronger than marksman, sages and vanguards with the exception of like one sage being good but that's because she plays as more of an arcanist.TLDR: Fun game, fun combat, good depth with some balancing issues

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: I requested a refund for this game as it is in it's current state.-Graphics:Usually the visuals of a game are not a big issue for me but outside of cinematics this game looks ten years old. Given the sparse content in this early build and bland assets, I can't guess where the size of this game comes from.-Gameplay:From combat to preparations, this game feels like a watered-down XCOM clone. All the systems are reskins of XCOM but medieval themed and hollow feeling.-Sound:The music is decent quality and fitting for the setting. The sound effects, while being of decent quality, get repetitive quickly although I would be willing to chalk that up to the game still being very early access.-Story:For me, this aspect of a game can make it worth playing even if every other part of it falls short. However, the story from the first couple of main quest missions available seems canned. It's just trying too hard to be gritty and dark and not trying hard enough to be compelling. Again, I know this game is far from complete but you'd think the story would be written enough to get that hook into players and make them want to know more about the world they're in or the people they control. I can't even tell you what the main character's motivations are outside of simply being told by an NPC what the main objective is. You're not given a reason to be invested and neither are the characters, it's just "Well, she said to do the thing again so I guess we're doing it again." -Conclusion:I'm usually far more forgiving when it comes to Early Access titles but this time I'm simply not impressed and see troubling signs of what this game is meant to be versus what I would prefer to play. If this game were just a DLC for XCOM that converted it from Sci-Fi to Dark Fantasy and cost only $20, I'd buy that. If this game did something new or innovative, almost anything at all, I'd at least be willing to stick around for updates. If this game was more than a counterfeit of better games and managed to get a few things down that made it stand out whatsoever, I would not be so harsh. While this game is far from complete, it already seems like the team behind it is already out of ideas and that's a shame. I love turn-based tactics games as well as Dark Fantasy but this game misses on both.

_childDocuments_.review: The game starts out ok but it wears thin very quickly. The developers just do not have the writers to bring out the best in this lore. I expected a story like Expeditions: Rome that kept me guessing and wondering until the end, eager to find out what was going to happen next. None of that was the case here.There is a morality system but it does not seem to make much difference to the game, it just means that you will receive different knights during your playthrough depending on the choices you make. These knights are only different in name though, knights do not have meaningful unique abilities to them so it really does not matter which knights you get. By the third act you would expect your knights to have some OP abilities that changes up how the game plays, they don't. The tactics at the end of the game is the same as the start, send in the tank (Mordred) let him absorb damage as you slowly whittle down the HP of the enemies with your other knights. Each mission is made up of 3-5 fights, each with 10 or so enemies, there is little variation in how these fights play out, there is little variation in the enemies you face, they may look different but they mostly attack the same, you do this over and over and over again.A melee focused game such as this should have the environment interaction aspect like Divinity Original Sin but it doesn't. It means that every fight plays out exactly the same

_childDocuments_.review: The game is OK, it's a well done game if you like the genre. There is nothing really great about it, whether we talk about the graphisms, the gameplay, the story, the RPG part or the soundtrack. But there is also nothing bad neither.It lacks of flavour and epicness, but still an interesting all around ok experience.I have to mention though that I hesitated to give a negative review because there is actually something really badly done: the balance of the game is terrible and made me quit the game - I didn't want to do a negative review because I still enjoyed overall my +50 hours + I felt that the developers, all considered, wanted to deliver a solid experience + because I believe it's a fixable issue.Indeed I was really disappointed about the balance: I played in hard difficulty to have some challenge, being experienced in the genre. What the game gives is a super easy act 1 and act 2 with barely no challenge. Ok it's the first 2 acts, I guess it's acceptable, I could have played in "super hard" mode etc. etc.But what was really unaccaptable is the spike of difficulty that starts around act 3.1) It's just very sudden, you don't know why and how but you get punished really hard for anything. I really dislike the idea of the difficulty changing from day to night in just 1-3 quests, but ok I guess I asked for challenge, so be it.2) But what was really infuriating is that the difficulty can actually litterally prevent you from advancing in the game, at least without some heavy backtracking thanks to some hopefully well timed saved that you "should have done". Indeed the way it works is that you manage your "roster", so if you happened to not have your top soldiers at the wrong moment (spike of difficulty mentionned), you might end up stuck in the next quest. The flaw here is that there is no way to exp or loot anywhere - and yes I did all the secondary quests. You can maybe manage to go through but generally with so much sacrifice that it will inevitably snowballs into a dead end at some point (without you realizing at the moment - so except if you enjoy going back to an old old save, you'll end up at a worse point, which makes it even more infuriating on the waste of time). Overall since there is no way to catchup, you can be stuck at any time, and that could steem from a small mistake you did 4-5 quests ago, which, you guessed it, couldn't imagine at the moment.3) Finally the difficulty is very punishing, which I guess is OK if you play it hard, but there are some frustrating mecanics on which you really can't do anything about, except, again, backtrack, reload the mission with a new roster and waste an hour for nothing (because it's not allowed to end a mission with too much casualties (cf. point n°2). For instance, "surprise" fight where you can't position your army, and the ennemy starts first, damaging instantly your backline. Other example, your tank being perma CC'ed which prevents him from protecting your squishies (yes you technically can spec into "anti-cc", but here we come again on point 2 : if you didn't spec you are rekt execpt if you want to restart the game from the middle - also it's really not fun to spec in anti-cc since it's just passives). So overall some gameplay flaws with anti-fun mecanics which could be fine if the game wasn't that punishing (and by punishing, I mean again the point 2 : small casualty = lead to a dead end after few quests)

_childDocuments_.review: Bug-free 0/10 - has critical game-breaking bug, the one that made me drop the game is following: enemies can't finish the turn, must be something to do with double Raven and speeding-up the animation. And it's double nasty since you can't save mid-battle and these were super-hard battles that can't be circumvented by lowering the difficulty. Feeling bad to load early and put the region aside since I cleared the rest of location. In other words you lose almost an hour of play with that bug. This is the only reason "King Arthur: Knight's Tale" gets no recommendation, even though the game is very polished and optimized.One more battle syndrome 8/10 - strong enough to skip a bedtime. Metagame 4/10 - global map is there only for graph-like campaign, where your decisions are very limited, could be easily 7/10 with a bit more buildings, extra easy quests for levelling and basically a bit more decision-making on a global map.Tactics 7/10 - I've seen better tactical variety and difficulty adjustments. Extra points for some super rare but satisfying combos. Some battles feel way too puzzle-like and AI deliberately puts you in bad battle positions. It seems that the game is pushing you to specializing to combat some races differently, which is not my thing, I love having more or less universal types. Items 6/10 - Very boring, not a lot of variety, some seem way too random and beg for a building that lets you change one of the parameters for gold. Most of various items and scrolls are useless to take a slot. So you end up getting a lot of similar looking things that do not make you excited. Min-maxing 8/10 - very satisfying, you want to level-up your characters and keep them alive. Some skills and their progression seem useless. Some characters have way too many underwhelming skills and passives. Got my best fighter dead after healing, it seems this mechanic is not explained and you don't even get a screen on the fact someone has died and why.Production value 9/10 - close to "XCom", better than "Expeditions: Rome" and "Wartales". Cool cinematics and animations. Writing and story 7/10 - not bad, but anticlimactic. Nice writing, a lot of texts but not too bloated. Good voiceovers.Region layer 5/10 - the region levels looks awesome in terms of graphics assets and variety, but doesn't offer many options for decision if the intention was a rogue-like layout. The map option is useless, doesn't show unpassable and passable way. You spend too much time going back while not having any way to speed-up the animation or pathfinding over the map or fast travel. I'm not sure about WASD controls as well. The engine and rendering for the region level is good though. Region-level design is also bad because you are constantly stuck in something that looks passable but it's not.

_childDocuments_.review: King Arthur: Knight's Tale is a top tier party-based tactical RPG with turn-based combat. You get more than two dozen characters to choose from for your party, pulled from a variety of source material on the Arthurian mythos, but largely inspired by the 1981 movie "Excalibur", a timeless masterpiece. The lore and writing may seem a bit convoluted to the hardcore history and mythology buffs like me, but it remains an interesting and entertaining take on the subject. You play as Mordred, Arthur's son and nemesis. His alignment is determined by you. There are morality checks in the game that steer you towards tyranny or righteousness, christianity or paganism. For my first play through I had a lot of fun playing the pagan tyrant and recruiting The Black Knight, The Red Knight, Morgana et. al. ("The Black Knight always wins!" At one point he actually says "it's just a flesh wound.") But I honestly think that the righteous path has better battle perks so I'm looking forward to a second playthrough to unlock The White Knight, Lancelot and the others. With very high production values, the game is beautiful and interesting to look at once you remove the screen film typical of this game engine.* The character and NPC models are highly detailed, like meticulously painted miniatures. I love the attention they put into each one, it really brings them to life and makes them easy to discern in the field. Voice acting is also top tier, very high quality and complete, no half-read lines here. Enemies are fairly diverse and just as detailed as your party. Animations are smooth and realistic. Soundtrack is epic. Combat is closer to Gears Tactics or D:OS2 than XCOM2 or Phoenix Point, but they pull the best of them together here so it has more predictable ballistics than its predecessors. Overwatch is more precise and more effective. The focus here is on melee and magic, archery to a lesser degree. There are a lot of skills to unlock. The skill trees are individuated for each character, so it stays fresh and interesting. My only complaint is with skill progression and dps; for the majority of the game, all your skills do about the same damage as your default basic attack, so there isn't any incentive to use them other than mixing it up. Later in the game, you will start to unlock some really cool AOE magic attacks though. Poison and DOT affects are relatively weak, with the exception of bleeding. But none of the DOT stacks afaik. All in all, this is the best turn-based rpg to come out this year so far. There are others, but this one tops the list. I abandoned them to play this one a second time, and I rarely play a game more than once. It's that good. This is a must play for any turn based tactics fan. *I made a ReShade preset that removes the screen film and clarifies the image, deepens colors, darkens shadows and illuminates globally. Made for 4k UHD OLED, 2k mmv.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is rock solid at 1.0.  Well worth the wait, but it's not without it's problems.Great storytelling, excellent combat (AP is shared between movement and combat), and good difficulty (it's no cake walk and you will almost certainly replay a map or start over).  There are different ways to play and engage in combat.  You can freely roam maps, unlock which skills to acquire, choose who to take in combat, who to go on missions, and more.  There's equipment drops (in the form of sigils, jewelry, and accessories) like weapons, armor, and most of these are class specific.  But, it does add some theorycrafting.  Also, choices really do matter because of the morality system.  You can be an evil tyrant or a holy knight.  Want a tank or dps?  Your decisions will determine who you can recruit and who can't.  The alignment also affects damage bonuses per loyalty.  The more loyalty, the more damage and AP you can have per character.  There's also your keep, where you can heal your units from injuries (think Darkest Dungeon) and a market to sell and buy gear.   There's also a few other base features that give bonuses to loyalty (which increases unit damage) and training that you can send units on to level while you leave them.  Adding a character to maintain one of the areas can add more specific bonuses to all your characters as well.What I like:32:9 SupportFree roam, rotating map (though it can be confusing , but I think that adds a little to the mood)MusicVoice acting - sometimes very excellentDark Arthurian atmosphere - Think The Green Knight Good amount of character craftingWhat I don't like:Cannot disengage in combat without getting hit (unless you have movement skills or the enemy is taunted)Sometimes terrible VA.  Yvain and the Hermit (aka the Cadbury cream egg guy) come to mind.  Even Mordred's voice has changed (it can be jarring).  Also, it seems like the Lorax made an appearance...End game has very little VA - when it does, it's incorrect (merchant woman has a male voice)Not enough high end relicsTraits and morality leave very little experimentationSome keep upgrades paths do not feel worthwhileSome characters seem to be 'best in class' leaving others as also ransVery little ways to tailor the gameplay - you only get difficulty - rogue-like is locked at hard and you cannot save in your keep.  After early access, this has shaped into an excellent SRPG.  Performance seems a lot better.  There still is a lot of QoL that needs to take place, but well worth the wait and recommended.

Then, you will be thrown into the middle of a tough fight at the end of a mission, which may have some challenge.  It's as if the rest of the game was just tacked on to make it soooo much longer than needed.  I'm thinking devs completed a good game, testers beat it quickly, and marketing said make it longer.Also can't switch between controller and keyboard/mouse without changing settings every time.  I like using a controller, but keyboard is a huge advantage and why I play computer games, not console.Has some good concepts, decent combat when they actually try.  It's just layered in what is basically forced grinding.  Does have a way to speed up enemy animations though, which is so nice.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is pretty cool and all but can we talk about design choices?1) Skills are hidden in skill tree. The dumbest idea I've ever seen considering character leveling process. It forces you to blindly put skill points into things that will be made absolete later.2) Main character is a tank and he is bad at it. Unlike most of the tanks you don't get the taunt but instead you get useless lightning strike that at later levels does exactly 0 damage. (and "stun" that it has still allows enemies to make full attack against you)3) Speaking about characters... Most of the knights that you unlock for morality chart are terrible. They got terrible skills, terrible proficiencies.4) Unbalanced missions. Every mission is a total rng. Some crappy side mission with no apparent threat can absolutly demolish your party just because game designers desided to throw at you 4 knights with 15 armor and 6 crossbows. For no reason, without a warning. Just fk you. You can't level team B on side missions.  They will die.5) Worst of all - Rng relic loot. All relic loot in the game is rng. Doesn't matter, right? Wrong. Many early encounters DEMAND that you have a relic loot equiped in order to beat them and tbh most of the relic loot is absolute garbage that could also debuff you. Playing roguelike mode and rolling bad relics? Doomed, fk you.6) Invulnerable enemies. WHY?! At some point game starts swarming you with enemies that can become invulnerable to all damage for 1 turn (and can still attack you ofc). It's boring in best cases and makes you want to abandon melee in a game about KNIGHTS in worst cases...7) Another enemy point. (because it deserves another point) 50/50 evasion enemies. Yes, you can stun them BUT they swarm you in such numbers that it's not a reliable option and they can murder your knights in 1-2 turns.8) Point seven brings us to the last point - non-viable melee gameplay. If you have to be in melee in this game then it's better be one turn (and you kill your enemy in this one turn). All knights that got no shield are made of paper and die in two turns in melee.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent strategy gameSome minor rpg elements, pick some skills and equipment. Choose if your going tyrant/rightful or christian/old faith. I wouldn't call this a proper rpg at all though, choices are few and you have to stick to the path your on or you lose out so its more of a few choices rather than proper choice and consequence. Story so far seems interesting, Im extremely familiar with the Arthurian Cycle and this is a fun take on it especially for those familiar. However if your totally new to the myths then its a basic serviceable take on Avalon.Building your group and synergizing skill choices and tactics is where this games bread and butter is at and it does it excellently. I can see replaying this on a harder setting in the future as I come to grips with it more. Currently going through on Moderate and its a bit easy but not too easy.I have already gotten my money's worth and I suggest this game for any fan of tactical rpgs, xcom style games etc. If you enjoy the mythos on top of that then this is a no-brainer purchase.Hope they make another game like this whether its a sequel or another in the same genre but different story. Dev's know what makes a fun Trpg!

_childDocuments_.review: very good. almost feels rouge like. its a mission then base mission then base kind of game. upgrade base, manage resources, go on mission, go back to base, upgrade things, manage resources, go on mission. very good turn based combat. whole team takes a turn and you pick what order they do things then enemy goes. i like this a lot more than 1 character than another. for instance you can hit an enemy with one character to bring target down to 50% hp then select another character to bolt them to finish them off then change back to fisrt character and move and attack again if you have the AP points for it. bringing a high lvl of dynamic fluid combat to turn based combat. its challenging as you can not see stats or characteristics of buffs from gear in a mission/combat. so you have to look at things in depth at the castle before you go out to battle and have a good understanding of how your characters and builds will synergize. for instance if you have a guy that does 10 more damage to bleeding targets.....you will have no way of knowing this during combat. you just have to know it by memorizing it from his character sheet before a mission. Very fun once you get into it.
_childDocuments_.name: King Arthur: Knight's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: This is early access so there are still a couple of kinks to be worked out which is to be expected. When EA first dropped it was almost unplayable. Now, however, it runs pretty smoothly. As it currently exists, the game is a lot of fun tactically. The missions are challenging and require thought to win. I've restarted several times and think I am just about through with the EA content. There's a lot of promise with things to come. There are many nods to Excalibur and even the old Pendragon RPG that I appreciated. My hope is that the game will transcend from its dark, gloomy, gray  beginnings to something more colorful and vibrant depending on your morality choices and decisions. The existing content hints at this (at least to me) and that would certainly be consistent with its "Excalibur" feel. The characters are interesting and the skill tree decisions, etc. are meaningfully different. This game should have a lot of replayability. My only serious criticism at this point is that you cannot save during missions. Some developers pride themselves on making games just that bit of extra difficult. Some players like this. I personally do not. I have no problem making "no saves" a difficulty setting option if that's your pleasure but you ought to be able to save during missions by default. Some of these missions are long. Not being able to stop and come back is problematic.

_childDocuments_.review: Gets repetitive and I got burnt out during Act 4. Events are very annoying, indirectly forcing you to send someone from your main party away for 1 mission to increase loyalty and because of this, you need to replace with someone from the backup knight which I do not care. Juggling morality and faith all in all gets tiring and basically in the end my party of Tyrant Old Faith - Modred, Black Knight, Boudecea, Morgana. Somewhere during late game, I have to dismiss almost every knight whos Christian due to Morgana's negative Pagan trait and I just realised Morgana already has -3 loyalty due to this which I am not aware of. So the main question is, why is the potion that removes negative trait came so late in the game? Treasures and loots gets predictable and most of them are just junks. Sometimes the loots has something useful. Generally, it is difficult to equip your favourite knights with things you'd like due to the randomness of the Enchanted tower and Merchant. The restocking cooldown doesn't help with this at all as sometimes only 1 or 2 items get refreshed. The side missions sometimes felt simply like fillers to level up your knights. This game is enjoyable for the first 2 Acts but after that it slowly degrades in interests. There are others small to medium things I do not like in this game but can't recall them after my first 80 hours playthrough. I am just happy able to finish up to the final mission and I guess I got my money worth. Will I go for a second playthrough? Absolutely not. Time to move on.

_childDocuments_.name: King Arthur: Knight's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Hard to give this a positive or a negative. I finished the campaign and played some of the endgame. The cinematics are pretty good, and the knight armours are nice. Some interesting skills and tactical decisions. Each mission is samey but different enough to keep you playing. But I can see why some people will get bored of it quickly. Some builds are very overpowered.. Sir Lancelot with some questionable items and skills... I played on hard and the end game builds were so overpowered it was basically almost god mode. King Arthur is like a concert that teases you throughout the whole experience, but ultimately never hit any high climax. It was just fun enough to keep you going. By the end of it I enjoyed my experience, learnt a few turn-based builds I have never seen, but never felt blown away by anything. The end game content (including the mini-campaign) were linear and boring I could not finish it.If you are not a big fan of turn-based tactics or knights in cool armour, might want to wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: So, the feeling I get from this game is that once you finish Act 1, which takes about 10 hours, including all side missions, you've seen the entire game. The combat is.....fine. Its probably the most enjoyable part of the game tbh. It gets the job done but its very simple and the enemy variety is lacking. Some enemies serve only to annoy you, and they do a very good job.The story is.....idk. I went into this game excited by the premise and setting and was looking forward to the story. But I can't say anything really ever grabbed my attention. After 5 or so hours I just tuned all the dialogue out because it all felt so inconsequential. The graphics are ..... okay. I really dislike the design of the main character, he feels like an antagonist out of an indie rpg that came out in 2010. Maybe thats the point idk. The world is very grimdark, so if grey is your favorite color, youre in luck, youll never see another color. Personally, its just not for me. In general, the graphics look a little dated, but its fine. Nothing really stands out.The "base" system is sort of cool. Im not huge fan of the injury system which 2 of the main buildings work for. The training system was good. A lot of the upgrades I looked at for the various buildings seemed not that great or interesting, but maybe i didnt look hard enough or maybe i dont remember properly.All being said, I picked this game up on a big discount and while I really looked forward to this game, after Act 1, I dont think I could manage to suck it up through another 3 acts of what I imagine are basically the same thing.

_childDocuments_.review: I very rarely write reviews for games, but this was such an unexpected gem I wanted to flag it for other turn based strategy game lovers. If you ever wanted X-com but with a medieval setting and magic, you'll really enjoy this. Pick from a squad of legendary heroes, each with unique classes, skills, traits etc. Build up your home city for improvments, gather valuable loot and equipment for your soliders. There is also a morality system that gives it a slight choice based flavour, although this doesn't seem like a huge part of the game.Story is okay, similar to other strategy games, the real meat is in the gameplay and upgrades. But you can tell alot of love went into this game.It is also absolutely beautiful, I actually wish you could zoom in slightly more to see the awesome landscapes and character models.

_childDocuments_.review: Boys cannot be girls.Changed to a Not Recommend. i got so bored, that I never launched the game again, and have zero desire to do so.ONLY ON SALEThis is an 'In Between' recommendation. Its not bad, but its also not great. On 50% sale, go ahead and grab it. Its simply not worth $45. But dont bother with the DLCs, which launch separately from the Main Menu.Its no longer 120 gigs install.. I believe its now about 38 gigs, as it always should have beenIm only a few hours in, and I can already see that its not very deep. Its very repetitive, but may have some replay value, if different [party setups are enough to make you want to play again. Perhaps some alignment choices.Its just SO SLOW! These little maps, shouldnt take more than 15 minutes or so.. But because this is turn based, each map drags on for over an hour. You cant play short session, and long sessions doesnt see much progress made. I am now 24 hrs in, and am only lvl 7. Ive not failed, or lost a hero yet, playing on the 3rd difficulty. Progression is quite linear, as missions are chosen from an overworld map, and are very small maps. Think Expeditions: Vikings, minus any dialog and role play. You will have main missions, some side missions, and an occasional event option. It is a tactics combat game, with kingdom management.THIS is whats really killing it for me:Overwatch is pointless, as the enemies will literally waste turns in order to not step into the overwatch zone. Ive even sat and tested it, and watched as they refuse to move, or even walk an entire circle around a melee character, to avoid the attack. The ai is far too binary. It sticks to a very strict script. Target the lowest armor, lowest hp, and avoid all overwatch zones and traps. This sucks! Different builds is the ONLY thing in this game that retains excitement, but much of it is void due to the ai completely nullifying some of the abilities. (traps, overwatch, creating firing lanes, ambush zones, etc) This means your only course of action is brute force forward momentum, and just eating the damage, as enemies will completely turtle!Heroes have their own talent tree, which have 3 tiers that unlock. But it doesnt do enough to change up the monotony. The combat is the same, over and over again, with the same enemies, over and over again.You can equip some items to your heroes, but nothing changes their appearance, and weapons are predefined. Anything you equip is just a numerical boost, or slight affect. Passive increases only. Later on, there does seem to be some items which grant some legendary affects, as well as powers gained from upgrades to your castle. Both of which are nice, and much needed!Movement, and traversing the maps is really bad. Partly because the maps are poorly made, and difficult to read (another Neocore staple), and the mechanics themselves are very janky. I cannot explain how bad this feels, without actually having you feel it for yourself. The character will just randomly slow down to a crawl, like hes waste deep in mud. The camera angle is a little restrictive, and the view distance is atrocious.The soundtrack is pretty awful. Its very rare to have music, and what music does play, is the type that puts you to sleep. Soundtrack is always a Neocore weak point.That said, some of this is not very informative, and is the reason I stopped to review it. Im still not understanding what armor points do exactly, or what causes some of them to be stripped. I just did a side mission, where it said not to get close to a particular enemy, but I dont know why, or how to tell what the buff is in the future, without being told specifically. Then, he obviously got close, and it didnt do anything. My archer killed him, and he exploded... Very sillyAll in all, its just very slow, and a little TOO relaxing, with the ambient music only... Im struggling to continue playing, after only 1 dayTrue to Neocore form, the graphics look a certain way that all their titles do. They also have some oddness in the way the controls work, and some mechanics of them game. They desperately need a new art designer. Every single game theyve made, has the same exact washed out color pallet, where environment is difficult to read.Al the characters are left handed, and its very jarring! It REALLY bothers me.The performance seems to be a biut much. I have an Ryzen 5 5600x, and rtx 3060, with 12gigs of RAM, and was a little surprised that i needed to lower a couple settings to high, from ultra. There wasnt much of a visual difference, but the frames seemed to be slightly smoother.Ill update as I goTLDR*Its little more than a turn based combat game. Theres not alot here. Sale ONLY!*Camelot upgrades simply serve as stat boosts*Music is non existent*Its highly repetitive, and becomes boring quickly*Map and art design are not good*Linear progression*Difficulty is just lots of enemies at once*It gets boring very quickly*Equipment and Talent trees help fuel feeling of progression, but its not enough to change up the repetitive combat.

_childDocuments_.review: Good but flawed. Nice twist on the Arthurian legend, and lots of opportunities for upgrading heroes. But defects include: you can't use loot in mission, you don't know what the loot is until the mission is over, you can't share healing potions/weapons/armour in mission, and unlike XCOM2, you can't save in combat. The 'moral' index is clever, i.e. be goody or a baddy and rewards/new heroes will vary. But when you choose options giving moral points, you don't know how many points you're getting, so no way of carefully choosing to maximise choices. Loot/purchasable items are pretty pathetic. The game's OK, but I soon went back to XCOM2.

_childDocuments_.review: To start off this is an awesome game, the combat system is really polished and complimented by the management in between missions. If you are looking for a one sentence review, I am a huge fan of turn-based tactical RPG's and King Arthur Knight's Tale is a great addition to the genre with a beautiful battle system however it can begin to feel repetitive at times with lengthy mission times. The overall gist of the game is that you will go on a mission that includes a short storyline through several battles that will earn you XP, loot, gold, and building materials. In between missions you will be using those currencies to select upgrades for Camelot to provide different benefits, making kingly decisions on different events that affect what kind of leader you are, and deciding what to do with heroes that are not on your missions roster such as training or healing. Certain decisions you make will affect your morale compass between Righteous and Tyrant as well as Christian and Old Faith. Progressing in any one direction will unlock new characters and other benefits. I really enjoyed the management piece in between missions. Finding a really useful upgrade and then setting out on another mission to get the currency to afford the upgrade all played into each other nicely, making it hard to find a good stopping point at times. However, after hours and hours of game play I did begin to tire of the side missions and began to only want to progress the main story. The missions are lengthy and turn-based combat is not necessarily quick. While this may sound negative, I think that is still a nod to the developers that put out a full length game and not just half a game blocked by paid dlc at a later date. Overall: 8/10 - Would recommend to a friend
