_childDocuments_.review: A dang fine game! Albeit a bit unbalanced. Sir Balin be ballin'King Arthur: Knight's Tale is a very fun squad-based, tactics-y, strategy RPG. Set in ye olden days of King Arthur and Ser Mordred the Dread Knight, you wake up after the two clashed and murderated each other in a rather bloody battle. You are tasked with rebuilding Camelot, and saving Avalon (think of England, but in another world. D&D players can think of England, but the Feywild). There's a few twists in the story, but they're fairly minor, and don't change the story much. Your heroes level up, usually one level every mission, or at least every other, you take them on. You get a full cadre of 12 heroes active, but you get a few more, so you have to decide which hero you want to remove from court and which one you want to run with. You will also not be able to have ALL of them at max levle by the end of the story. But most of them, if you switch out regularly. Which you don't need. I'll spoiler you that much of the story. You DO NOT need to train two (or more) squads. You cna run with one squad from start to finish. Whether tha is good or bad is your decision to make.The heroes follow a general archetype, Ranger, Caster (melee caster and the stereotypical mass-incinerator), 2h-Warrior, Tank, Rogue, but they all have a slightly different set of actives and passives. The exception being Vanguards (Rogues). They all have the same actives and passives, from what I remember. But that's not necessarily bad, since they're also brokenly OP. Seriously.Speaking of broken, the balance is a bit off. Vanguards start out squishy and stupid stronk, and they get even more stupidly strong and they get less squishy. Archers start out nice, but they fall off for the most part their attacks don't improve that well, and their ultility becomes less important. The tanks start off doing mediocre damage and taking very little, and they basically become nearly-impenetrable walls of steel, that deal little damage, but have nice utility. Your arcanists/wizards start out squishy, and stay squishy, but they get more devastating against multiple enemies, and get more crowd control.Your melee wizards are there for support, and their damage is, and stays, laughable. Their supportiness gets better, though.I wish I could say much about the 2h-warriors, but I ditched them in favour of Vanguards very early and never looked back.The gearing of your heroes is quite diverse, you have weapons, armour, trinkets, and support items (potions/scrolls), in four levels of quality and five stages of level requirements. For the most part the items are randomly generated, but the highest tier of quality has set stats, since every one of those items has a name.And some of those are silly strong, too. The interface is serviceable, but nothing special, it IS in the way of things, sometimes. Especially when you try to move your heroes from one space to another, and when drawing the area of effect for line-based spells and abilities. Overall, there's room for improvement, but it's not ruining the game.Performance so far also seems fine. Nothing spectacular, the effects aren't anything super-outstanding, but also don't pull you out of it. A solid performance, overall.The only gripe I really have with the game is the length of some of the missions. ESPECIALLY some of the sidequests definitely take longer than they should. But they are still overall short enough. On Normal difficulty, every mission took me around 20-30 minutes. To clear the enemies and sweep for all treasures. With maybe a handful of exceptions.Overall, I recommend this, but if you want something with a REALLY deep story, this isn't gonna be it for you. It's fairly standard, but the fights are fun, the balance is broken on the fun side of the scale, and some items are good modifiers to your playstyle. I'm good with having bought it at full price. It's worth the money in my eyes.

_childDocuments_.review: King Arthur is a great turn-based tactical strategy game.  It has some RPG-elements without being a full RPG.  There's no real heal spells or holy trinity synergy in the game so your tactical decisions feel impactful.  It's reminiscent of XCOM but without that crazy RNG.  The graphics were great and the music always felt very moody and fitting for the game's setting.  I'd give this game a solid 8 - maybe even an 8.5.  The story wasn't my favorite and I never felt fully invested in it but it certainly wasn't bad.  Playing the "bad guy" was actually a lot of fun and Mordred has an awesome personality in his dialog options.If you enjoy games in this genre I give it a big thumbs-up and my full recommendation.  If you're more of an XCOM player or a full RPG guy then I'd wait for a sale but still recommend you pick it up.  I finished the main campaign on Normal difficulty in about 74 hours.  I'm not a great tactical mind and usually play the game on Normal or Hard but definitely not ULTRA HARD or NIGHTMARE.  If you're the kind of player who is really looking for a tactical challenge I would bump this up to HARD at the bare minimum.  The depth of your roster doesn't really get tested unless your heroes are injured and start spending turns in the cathedral or hospice.  The city-management portion of the game felt a little shallow but occasionally interesting.  It's definitely not as involved as XCOM but what it does - it does well.

_childDocuments_.review: Before i say anything about this game there is one thing we all can agree on. The game has a really high potential and it reminds me of my all time favorite game Disciplace and yes i know its super early access but still there are number of things that need to be fixed really fast First of all the optimization need work, i played threw the game and 80% of the time i had no problems with but there are times when the game drops to 30 and even to 8! FPS despite the graphics options especially on areas with a lot of fog or in fights with more the 10 enemies on the screen Second thing that bugged me was the de-synchronization between sound and the animations of attacks even in 60+FPS there where some problems with units making the animation and the sound just didnt catch up with it or the other way around The last thing that was bugging me is the flow of the game. Its slow. Dont get me wrong i dont want this game to be lightening fast or something but.... the animations even in more then 120 FPS feel like that are slowed down to 30 FPS and it feels clunky and strange like all of that was forcefully made to look like a movie but it failed. The attacks, the unit movements, the skill animations they need to be a little more dynamic in my opinion with more energy to give the characters ( or enemies ) more life to them Personally i would like the game to have better equipment animations. For example when im equipping new set of armor i want my character to change a little or with a new weapon rune to give the weapon that he or she is holding a different look Despite all of that plus some smaller problems i do like this game really its enjoyable it has the right dark fantasy setting, the story is ok and the building system looks solid ( but it needs more options like really ) so for now i can give it 6.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: To be frank, this game would deserve a neutral rating, but sadly there is nothing like that available. Also, it is not a bad game per se, rather than the core gameplay loop is severely broken for me. Which means that some people may perfectly enjoy it (assuming that they are content with excess grinding). On the surface it does everything right; X-Com-esque combat, dark fantasy King Arthur lore (similar to Neocore's previous King Arthur RTSes) and some of the mechanics are heavily Darkest Dungeon (1) influenced. You have an HQ you can keep upgrading and go to missions from that place with a roster of Arthurian heroes. Looks nice, plays nice, sounds nice (minus the voice talents, it really feels like not humans are behind those, but text to speech synthesizer reads the script).So what is the problem? For me, the game is super grindy and extremely convoluted. Let's start with the latter one. You can build plenty of buildings (like DD) and you can upgrade them to give more slots for treatment/training/etc. However, upgrading is not freeform, there is a dependency chart between upgrades, which you have to follow. Ok, no biggie (although it took me a while to figure out how can I open a second slot to treat vitality), I can live with that. Nevertheless, everything is expensive, so one must enter the constant loop of grinding by going through copycat missions. Fighting the same enemies, in the same scenery (which doesn't help you to visually guide where can you go and where is an invisible wall), looking for lootable places just to get 20 or 30 gold coins. Then you get the same (visually represented) artifacts, which you can equip, just one of them gives you +2 damage in overwatch, instead of giving +1 to burning arrow. After a few hours I just dumped all the ♥♥♥♥ at the merchant, because I get a headache after every mission, looking at the visually same 6 clover, same 7 tusk amulet figuring out which one suits my playstyle better.Let's be honest, Darkest Dungeon was grindy too, but fun, as the gameplay loop was interesting, engaging. You could experiment with different builds, different classes, approaches and such. Here, in Knight's Tale it's just... lackluster. First, I only encountered five classes (some of them plays fairly similar), actually four, because the wizard I received was so annoying, that I dismissed. Sadly, I didn't know that (as of level 6) I won't get any wizards, sooo I'm stuck without a spellcaster. Somebody wrote in his (her?) review -and I found it spot on- that regardless of how many heroes you have, you will stuck with a few. Because either you can't keep the ones you dig (because it conflicts with your choices/faith), or simply they are just uninteresting or outright irritating (as the heroes talk and behave slightly differently). I really would like to get rid of the womanizer crossbowmen guy from my team (as he is cheesy as ♥♥♥♥), but can't, since I only have melee heroes apart of him and another archer.Speaking of missions, usually those end up with running around on maps of a few rotated artstyles which wear out their welcome super fast. Although there are "optional" side missions, those don't really feel optional, as main story missions have a level requirement, which you better adhere to. Leveling your heroes is done through missions (or in the training field, but time there passes based on number of missions you perform, so catch of 22), which pit you against the same enemies. I encountered three types so far, with only a handful of classes. Alternative may be to focus on the mission objective and stop exploring, but that also isn't a viable approach, as you will trigger fights (only a small amount of them are optional) automatically.Again, is it a bad game? No. But it's definitely super grindy with a limited variety of enemies and sceneries, which you must perform, shall you want to build your buildings, level up your heroes, etc. And this comes from someone, who actually enjoyed Darkest Dungeon, but this type of soulless grind is just way too much for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Unoptimised garbage. _childDocuments_.review: It's basically Darkest Dungeon (the first one), but with with isometric exploration and combat. Although the DD influences are ubiquitous, they've managed to change it up enough to make it feel like a new game. It's not perfect, there are issues with the interface, among other things, but it's mostly nothing you can't live with or won't get used to. The story has been decent so far, the sound acting ranges from good to some characters making me want to stick forks in my ears when they're in party (looking at you Sir Tristran!) and the soundtrack still kicks butt after almost 30 hours of play.This game is so heavily DD influenced it's hard for me to compare it to anything else or describe it otherwise. It's not the same game, but there are a LOT of similarities throughout. If you enjoyed Darkest Dungeon, you might want to give this one a go (and vice versa). If you didn't, you should probably steer clear.

_childDocuments_.review: I would rate this neutral, not thumbs down. It actually probably deserves a thumbs up, but I'm putting thumbs down to balance out the reviews since I think the game's current rating is higher than it actually deserves.I've played the game on all difficulties. Normal is far too easy, Moderate is whatever, Hard is OK (other than end game HP sponges which serve no purpose other than making the fights very long), Very Hard has some issues I will go into later.The game gets a 6.5/10 (it was 7, then I came to realize a few things) here's why:-- The Good1. Interesting combat the first (and maybe second, I'm on my second time and we'll see if I can actually make it through, but I doubt it) time around, decent puzzles to solve mixed throughout the game2. Fun building of the city3. Character builds are great! 4. Some of the gear is interesting, and I do like the thrill of the RNG.5. The game looks and feels good to me, with decent UI (wish I could change equipment mid-mission though)-- The Neutral1. The story is OK. Nothing special, but it isn't bad. Not a pro nor a con.-- The Bad1. Music is repetitive/boring. Listen to something else.2. Repetitive voice lines. 3. Low replayability - long missions for no reason with static encounters    - You have to do these missions or you will have not enough resources or XP. "Side Mission" is a lie.    - You pretty much have to do these missions the "right way" and boringly slog through them, as you are almost always outnumbered and mobs become super HP sponges later.4. Characters seem very limiting. You can only bring 4, and you can only have 12 in your roster. This is OK, but what isn't ok:     a. Many chars are locked by alignment, which in itself is okay, but PLAYSTYLES are locked behind the alignment       - Want good champs and the best defender? Be a tyrant christian       - Want good arcanists? Be tyrant old faith       - Want good sages and a few really good arcanists? Be rightful old faith       - Want a mix of decent to very good hero picks? Be rightful christian. In a way, this makes it have some replayability... but it doesn't, unfortunately, because the game becomes a slog when you replay it and have seen the missions before. See point 3.5. Game Balance (There's a decent mod that SOMEWHAT addresses point A, enhanced edition, but I have my own qualms with it and feel like it just shifts the tier list) a.  All difficulties -  Marksman are flat useless (you can use them on normal because that difficulty is so easy, but even on that difficulty they are really bad and you might struggle some). There is one (arguably two in late game) good vanguard(s), and traps are just bad. Defenders are limited in usefulness (sometimes very needed). Champions and Arcanists are the best classes in this game, pretty much by a large margin. b. Very Hard - I have mixed feelings. The AI is better, but it is also worse. At least they pick targets better and actually try to kill you. Problem is, they will *always* go for backstabs, at the cost of proccing opportunity attacks. In some ways, VH is easier than Hard, because you can just trick the stupid AI into proccing opportunity attacks and it isn't smart enough to not do that and commit suicide. At the same time - this is a good move, a lot of times, with how much of HP sponges they are. But I wish they were smart enough to not commit suicide (like if they were low hp).6. Gear is all RNG (it's a pro and con)Overall, I would recommend this game on sale for a one hitter. And it's ALMOST good enough that I would wholly recommend it, but the game has some issues that prevent that from being reality.  I would definitely try out a #2 though... I would just watch some gameplay videos, carefully, first.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of things that are incredible good, expect no comfort features though.For example, the map is very hard to read in most missions and you can't click on the map to go somewhere, gotta walk there all by yourself, which is a little annoying if you wanna walk back and look if you missed something, like hidden treasures which the game doesn't tell you how to find in the first place, which I don't mind cause you'll just stumble upon it.The combat is very good in my opinion, even though it is simple in the beginning it has some some depth which increases later in the game. It makes think which of my 4 abilities I should use to do max damage here. The class system supports the combat in a good way and one class can differ for different characters which adds to the characters in the game and the character of the game. Also the characters have some personality in Knight's Tale, unlike in most games, which you can underline with your equipment if you're down for some rollplaying in your game.Now to a apparant problem Knight's Tale has that all games of this genre have. The combat is slow and the fights are many. Enemy variety is ok but to entertain the majority of people it is lacking. Need I say anything else? I don't think so. Oh and also no autocombat here, which would kill the immersion anyways. Me: "Spits on might and magic"Did I write about the amazing graphics this game has yet? Guess what, they are amazing and the best I've seen so far in this genre. I didn't know you can design so many knights in so many different ways. Sir Mordred is by far the best in my opinion though. There are a few bugs, most are just funny and I'd let them pass as features except for one I've run across so far. You can use wasd to move, but if you move into a invisible wall, which are placed sometimes on the border of the map, you can't move at all. So you gotta restart the mission. Don't worry these invisible walls are marked, so just be careful or just move with your mouse like most people do. And no they don't kill the immersion, at least that's what I think.I already wrote about the characters in Knight's Tale and guess what, you can't have all of them, you gotta straight up delete some characters from your game. For now it hasn't been a problem for me, cause so far I could just throw out characters that I despise, those little ♥♥♥♥♥. But I'm afraid there will be to many characters that I like so I'll have to make a choice I don't want to make.Equipment scaling with level has been done rather poorly I think, Every 5 levels the equipment gets significantly stronger and can only be worn by a character who is the same or higher level. I would suggest that equipment can have any level and any character can wear any equipment, for the simply reason that a low level character becomes to much of a burden, which can be solved in a way but not to my satisfaction. Also when you reach for example level 10, the gear you get is just way over the top, making every previous equipment mostly useless. This howevery does not ruin the game, just an issue I'd rather not have.Anything else? Maybe I'll update this review later who knows.

_childDocuments_.review: NO SPOILERS =]King Arthur: Knight's Tale is a tactical RPG set in Avalon, of classic Arthurian history.  The game has an immediate plot twist, in that you are playing Mordred - originally a major antagonist, who died and has since risen from the dead, to restore order to Camelot, and lay to rest the tormented spirit of King Arthur himself.  You get all this information from the introductory cutscene.The Good----------The game is a reasonably slow-paced affair, but this isn't a *bad* thing as it gives you plenty of time to get to grips with the mechanics, the characters, and so on.One of the things I particularly enjoyed about it is that you get to hold court, as in you have to make a number of decisions along the way which drive you either in the direction or law or chaos, and Christianity or the Old Ways.  You also get to rebuild, renovate and improve Camelot and its buildings, which is a welcome strategic component to the game that makes it more than just a simple tactical RPG.I also like how you only have so many slots for heroes, meaning when you acquire *more* people in your roster, you *will* need to retire some of your legacy Knights, so it pays to start sorting them into ones you really want to keep and develop, and ones you really aren't bothered about, from an early stage.One quick tip if I may - wand your enemies to see what their movement is on the next turn.  This can help you stay outside their movement area, thereby ensuring you don't get hit too soon =]The Bad---------The decision to include some British and some American voice-actors is a puzzling one to me, as the tale of King Arthur is typically thought of as a British one, so when you have (for example "the Hermit") voiced in an American accent, whereas a number of the Knights of the Round Table have strong British accents, it can be a slightly jarring experience.Additionally, some of the text features typos which is a really *minor* thing, but ... yeah.There is one other slightly frustrating element to the game, which is that when you need to heal characters (and you will), you will need to remove them from your active roster by sending them to one of two healing structures, and they will be out of action for a number of game turns, meaning you'll have to do other quests without them.  If you aren't careful, this can mean you're missing a pivotal character (e.g. Mordred) for a mission, so you'll have to go with (potentially) a character you haven't levelled-up as much, and this can be an issue.All told the game feels solid, decent, and enjoyable.  The range of spells and special abilities makes it an enjoyable experience, and when you have a strong feel for your tactical style, you can make some serious progress with it.  Just remember to pay attention to all the options as you play, and you'll be fine ! =DI'd give it a solid 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This review comes from a Hardcore play through on Hard. About halfway through Act 3 of 4. Reviewer loves Battle Brothers, Darkest Dungeon, and Iratus. Was lukewarm on Expeditions: Rome. May be overly long, but if you want a detailed explanation - this is the review for you.This game is surprisingly good and exceeded my expectations in many areas. There are some areas of "ok" quality, but it leans into what it does well and allows the player to really enjoy the game as a result. The game doesn't make the mistake of leaning into low quality gameplay loops that distract from the experience and what you get is a very satisfying tactical RPG with satisfying character and party management elements.On a scale of 1-10 and then explained:Story - 9Party and Kingdom Management - 8Classes and Customization - 6Tactical Combat - 8Pacing - 8Stay fairly brief here, but the world is a really interesting twist on Arthurian legend. The way characters are introduced is great and I enjoyed the way the game explored the individual knights and the overarching plot. My only complaint here is that there are so many knights that it misses an opportunity to add more depth to your knights.Many of these knights could, and should, have significant relationships and stories to explore between each other and the game only does a superficial job of exploring these. Understandable, but an opportunity to go from "good" to "incredible." The management of Camelot is fairly similar to what you might experience in Darkest Dungeon. This works quite well and was enjoyable. Not too complex, but not too lean either. A nice side dish on the side of the experience. Your party members may, or may not, contribute helpfully to your operation in Camelot and this makes your overall knight selection a bit more varied.The one drawback for many people is that your core party is limited to 12 active knights. In a game that offers you many more, it "feels bad" to have to make choices to exclude certain knights. I found myself wanting everyone, but I had to make some very difficult decisions about who to include and who to dismiss, or not add, to my team. The game has a morality system that encourages you to only accept knights from your alignment decisions, but it still felt like you were "missing out" when you have to dismiss a knight or not accept a knight. I learned to accept this and it is ok, but as a player, this did not "feel good." In spite of the negative feeling with it - the system just works. I have to commend it because the game is balanced quite well around it, no matter how little the player may like it. If the player was permitted to manage more than 12 knights, the infrastructure would not adequately support it as keeping them all leveled and equipped would become tedious and problematic. I believe that the system that is introduced here is fine, but it is "less good" than other systems that exist in RPGs. Your knights are limited to a specific armor weight class and weapon set. You customize their performance through skill point allocation (which is unique to them based on one of 6 classes and some unique nuances of the knight).Items in the game are really just "sigils" that modify the performance of the character. Think Darkest Dungeon, but with slots dedicated to Weapons, Armor, and Trinkets. There are no cosmetic adjustments or truly functional changes that happen here.Once again - I favor more complexity here - but the game just makes it work. The simplicity in this domain allows you to focus more on what the game does quite well, and as a result it bothers me less in this title than it may in other titles. There is just enough player agency in the way you build your characters to move them slightly into different sub-archetypes that it works out - but you are not going to get a vast array of alternatives that you might be looking for in other RPGs. In this game, you are fine-tuning your knight slightly, but nothing is going to make him anything other than the Tank, DPS, or Support that he is intended to be.The tactical combat system here is surprisingly good. Especially since it lacks so many modern innovations. A few things that, on the surface, are not great:- Very linear environments with simple battlefields that have light cover and obstruction scattered across it.- No elevation changes.- Very low RNG (could be favorable depending on the kind of gamer you are). The result? You get more of a tactical puzzle to solve where you are trying to figure out how to mitigate damage in the best way possible while maximizing your damage output. With almost no RNG, you can very accurately predict how your turn is going to go. The AI is very predictable and easy to manipulate, which is kind of needed here because you would not be able to manage the conflicts against a more sophisticated AI.In some of the fights later on your knights are arrayed against some pretty heavy odds and if the AI did not just charge into your battle plan it would be significantly more difficult. I thought I would not like this system, but at least at the difficulty level I am playing, the battles are difficult but achievable. Your knights are healthy enough that you can make a mistake or two and not lose them, and it is easy to see where you made the mistake to begin with. Repeated mistakes will kill a knight, but RNG and a couple of missteps will not. This makes the hardcore experience very engaging and very satisfying and I have been enjoying it significantly. Pacing in the game is above average. They do not waste a lot of time on crafting elements, mini-games, or other garbage that distracts from the gameplay loop. Result? You move from combat to combat, go to camelot to deal with your loot, manage your kingdom, rinse, and repeat. The only "time waster" is you kind of move around the map looking for hidden chests and loot. It is not egregious here because loot is frequently found behind battles, but there is more of it than I would like.Overall, I felt like the game is respectful of my time and I find myself doing stuff I enjoy constantly while I play it.

_childDocuments_.review: after having spend a lot more time with Arthur i sadly have to change my recommendation.yes, it's kinda XCOM, yes it looks neat, and yes both the scenario and the characters are fresh and interesting.but that's about where my positives end.the strategic layer is laughable underdeveloped. you rebuild the basic structures of Camelot (merchant, magic tower, healing ward, etc.), each having their own handfull of upgrades, and you can assign Knights to positions. it's okay, but very very basic.from time to time a "side"-event pops up, which is a text-bubble, and you making a choice. that's it. again very basic. and then you get to chose a mission, sometimes this means there are 2-3 side missions on the map and a main mission; but since side-missions are not bound to some sort of times, there ain't much difficult choices here.then there's one of the selling points of the game: the large roster of potential characters. and yes...there are a metric ton of potential Knights for you to recruit.each divided into classes, but still even then each having one or two unqiue features.the issues here pop up especialy later on when you realize that the very basic skill-tree just makes the whole size of the roster collapse. yes, two Sages might have 1-2 different skills (passive or active), but the skill pool is so tiny, that they still kinda all feel the same. this mixed with the encounter design and combat mechanics, just doesn't work well. nearly every encounter plays exactly the same, feels the same and it get's dreary..realy boring tbh. where games like XCOM, Phoenix or Grey Knights got enviromental destrucion, different mission targets, differences in hight, real cover which feels like a real game element (in Arthur it's kinda pointless tbh.), Arthur got: walk in a room, enemies pop up, you 4 man team clobbers em...done. sometimes you get 1 to 2 more chars (very rarely), but all the very basic combat mechanics mixed with your tiny team size, just...again plays very boring in the long run.and i kid you not: it's all the content in the game. every tiny side mission, every main mission...the hight of enjoyment is when an enemy is protected by totems, or totems respawn corpses.which also leads in the overall design. the size of the game was just to much for a studio like Neocore. the amount of Knights, while giving em personality would've broken bigger studios. the result is you getting a mission, where you will recruit said Knight, some dialogue during said mission..and that's that. very few knights get their own "special" side-mission, which works exactly the same. from this point foreward they only spout some random lines, like your main char does, during all other missions. unlike modern XCOM-ish games there's no personal interaction on the strategic layer, no talking to your advisors, no mini-cutscenes, nothing. they remain a silent, head-shot-portraits until you take em into a mission to spout their random lines again. which also goes for the unique on spin of all those small stories from the Arthur times. most end with the recruit mission, don't play any role, don't lead to nothing. there are some exceptions like characters linked to the Grail or Excalibur, but most others die the moment you finish the recruit mission. it's not a bad game, it's just exceedingly boring. the tiny skill pool, the tiny active skill pool, the tiny active unit roster, the boring skill tree, the minimal strategic layer, the text-box-events...even the good grafics never change much: it's darkish, gothic and that's that. which goes also for your characters loadout; there are 0 model changes. you don't loot weapons or armor, their budget-shortcut was you looting "runes", which in reality are weapons and armor, but they could skip the 3D-modeling work...but this also means your roster never changes their appearance (unless you get "skins" from outside of the game).as much as i like Neocore, this ain't it. there are just way to many better options around. the moment to moment gameplay just ain't there. if you never played a XCOM-like and you dabble into a light version that doesn't overwhelm you with options and possibilities Arthur might be for you, but i don't see veterans of the genre making it to the ending...i couldn't.
_childDocuments_.name: King Arthur: Knight's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: I had fun with this tactical RPG. I like medieval setting in games, so I loved all the lore I found here.  The story was interesting, battles were entertaining and characters were great. Sadly, this system of "Christian"/"old faith" and tyrant/rightful was dumb and made me force myself to pick some answers and quests to get new characters and upgrades to buildings. I also think that balance is a mess in King Arthur. As far as Act II goes, everything is super-easy. Then we have Act III that is a large spike in difficulty, and then we go back to ultra-easy mode with a final fight that is a joke. Burning/poison and some relic made last fight... Well, you can guess… I didn't like that.  Overall, this is a great game for the price of $30, and it gave me 50~ hours of fun. I definitely recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: King Arthur: Knight's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Slow and Repetitive! but It's still a good game!If they could add a version of the game where the Knight rotation didn't exist, the whole healing and gaining experience, it's just all too bothersome. Rather would have fewer knights with diverging talent trees or something that aren't under leveled.Then you got the world map where quests appear and clicking one loads you into a smaller area where you can run around looking for fights, interactions, loot etc. Time spent in that area is too long, too many repetitive fights, they should halve it. Furthermore they should remove the roaming part all together. It should automatically start at the fight and give some options whats routes to go and hint what perils or rewards could be had! Because god forbid you missed a marker and have to zigzag your slow ass group back to that place.Game has too much going on I would say, less would be more in this case.

_childDocuments_.name: King Arthur: Knight's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Pros- A fleshed out look at Arthurian Legend mixed with some of its own unique touches.- Solid amount of flexibility in regards to builds for different knights, e.g. Focusing on AOE skills early for your Champions or tanking abilities with defenders.- A bit of extra replayability thanks to the morality system.- Most of the characters I found quite charming, if you like good guys or evil tyrants their should be someone for every playstyle.Cons- Early game (particularly Act 1-2) are very dry when it comes to combat, simply put there wasn't enough enemy variety making the fights drag on.- Some small bugs/crashes while playing, such as tooltips bugging out and audio cutting out in some sections for no reason. - The music, while fitting the kind of game, became quite repetitive to the point I had to switch to my own playlist- The Endgame balance (specific to postgame) is dry and boring, didn't endure it more than a few hours before leaving it alone as I didn't find it interesting or enjoyable to fight waves of high HP enemies just for some loot. - A small criticism is the party size. Only 4 characters with the occasional guest just felt bad when you have around 30 Knights I would recommend picking this game up on sale as I did, pretty fun overall despite some of my criticisms.
_childDocuments_.name: King Arthur: Knight's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: The best way to describe this is probably a kind of fantasy X-Com with Darkest Dungeon influences. It's pretty good stuff. It has a linear rpg frame, but it forgoes the habitual heavy emphasis on narrative in favour of the tactical gameplay. Not that there isn't any narrative, and what is there is good, it anchors the action and is well-written. The presentation is "grim dark", as they say, with fairly extreme stuff (like mentions of rape), but there is a kind of levity and black humour in the dialog. The narrative is really there to serve the gameplay and not the other way around. I for once prefer this. The gameplay is fine-tuned, it feels like nothing is superfluous ; the difficulty is good, the levelling and customization has plenty of impact, the items are meaningful and have qualitative effects (and not just quantitative ones), the alignment system is quite interesting and gives the game replayability. The fights are not that hard if you pay attention - I think the game could be a bit more difficult - but as it's designed for ironman ("roguelike") play, it does require careful planning and knowledge of the different situations (which are composed of your team's abilities and the enemies'). The only real problem I have with the release (it has no bugs) is the file size, which is very excessive and quite unwarranted. Other than that, definitively a great game for tactical players, hopefully we see some interesting dlcs as a follow-up.EDIT : the devs are fixing the game's size to reasonable proportions. Very good of them, now this game has no faults, at least according to my review.
_childDocuments_.name: King Arthur: Knight's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: I kickstarted the game and enjoyed it.  I did run into a battle with the red knight that basically ended my play through because I just could not get through it with the compliment of companions I took.  Other than that the story is fun and it is an interesting twist on the Arthurian story.  I love turn based tactical games and this one did not disappoint.
_childDocuments_.name: King Arthur: Knight's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: The good:This is a fun dark fantasy XCOM-alike.The bad: The plot's nothing to write home about and the voice acting is flatter than a desk.The ugly:The graphics aren't anything to write home about, either.Verdict: wait for a sale, and then get it because it's worth the 70ish Shekels you'll be paying (but not its full asking price).
_childDocuments_.name: King Arthur: Knight's Tale

_childDocuments_.review: A unique hybrid between turn-based tactical games and traditional, character-centric RPGs. Knight's Tale is a modern retelling of a classic Arthurian mythology story filtered through the dark fantasy tropes, a twist on the traditional tales of chivalry.

name: Coral Island
detailed_description: Meet The Dateables About the Game It’s time to leave big-city life in Pokyo behind and start a new chapter of your life on Coral Island! Be who you want and create the idyllic farm of your dreams, where you’ll tend crops, nurture animals, and build a bond with the natural world around you. Help revitalize the nearby town and its surrounding coral reefs, and forge relationships with a vibrant community of more than 70 fellow people who call Coral Island home. Farm. Decorate. Craft. Explore. Relax. Your future—and the future of Coral Island—is what you make of it. Build Your Dream Farm Transform your overrun land on Coral Island into a lush and lively dreamscape—you decide what to build, what crops to grow, and which animals you’d like to tend. Write your own story : The story changes with each season, but life goes with the flow. Spend your days exploring, or build a life with someone special. Save the seas, brave the caves, or focus on your farm. It’s up to you! Be yourself : Choose from a wide variety of outfits, accessories, and physiques—you’ll find plenty of options to express yourself, find your style, and be whoever you want to be. Befriend a diverse cast of islanders : Get to know the 70+ characters from all walks of life who live on Coral Island. Converse with them, find out more about their interests, and try to impress them with just the right gift. Find that special someone : Meet 25 singles who are ready to mingle! Build relationships, sweep them off their feet, and find the one—and when you’re ready, embark on a new chapter of your story together at the farm. Restore an island once paradise : Make Coral Island a better place for everyone! Take part in community projects to liven up the town, expand the local museum, and discover how to restore heritage sites. Increase the town's rank and your community will thrive! Catch of the day : Island living has a lot of perks, including being just a stone's throw away from fun activities like hunting for insects and catching fish. Dive the ocean & mine the caverns : Go diving to restore the coral reef, or mine precious gemstones in the cavern. Whatever you decide to do, you’ll find loot to hone your tools and upgrade the quality of your livestock and crops.

short_description: Coral Island is a vibrant and laid-back reimagining of farm sim games. Be who you want and experience enchanting island living at your own pace—live off the land, nurture animals, build relationships with a diverse cast of townsfolk, and make the world around you a more vital and harmonious place.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm so glad I kickstartered this game. I Love how unique the animations and the character expressions are. The characters are vibrant and fit so well in this world. I just got to fall and the array off plants and crops is wild! Definitely check this out if you are a fan of Harvest Moon, Stardew Valley and any cozy game!

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoying this game a lot. It's got a great blend of farming sim mechanics, super similar to SDV with a few extra things to like diving and collecting for the museum.What really makes it stand out is the attention to detail in both the characters and the settings. The devs have poured a lot of love into this game and it shines through in a relaxing, kind and excellent game.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: I normally don't write reviews however I felt Coral Island deserves the hype, I had kept my eye on the game since before it even released and bought it the second it was available for early access on PC and for PS5 as well (I'd love to buy it on switch as well but unfortunately it's not available on switch). Anyways onto the actual review. I know most people are like "ugh another farming sim" but honestly this game is definitely worth the purchase. The design of the characters alone should make anyone buy it. The amount of diversity in the cast is amazing ! It's unfortunately one of the things some other games have lacked :( But the characters overall personality and design wise are so so beautiful and unique they all feel different from each other ! The farming aspect of the game is quite different as well from other games ! They have a bunch of new tools and items to use to help your farming life more easy and fun ! The game itself not only has your typical dateable characters and farming aspect but also introduces diving and not only do you get to know the characters in more depth but also uncover all different secrets in the world including the existence of mermaids ! I also really love the use of recycling and helping clean up after an oil spill disaster ! Also getting to fill up a museum with creatures,gems, artifacts, etc that i spent so much time farming feels so so rewarding! I truly truly recommend this game to everyone ! It's family friendly and also has some options for those who may need certain features such as colorblind options and dyslexic font options ! There is also an option to slow down the time and also has an option where you freely move in the mines without being attacked by monsters ! There's so so many other helpful features and tools and overall this game is a blessing !
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: I've been looking for a good farming/ life sim after many hours of SDV and Coral Island scratches that itch. The music is catchy and relaxing, the graphics are very aesthetically pleasing, and the game play is a lot of fun. There's a lot that can be done and focused on like farming, mining, or relationship building, or you can easily mix them up with it being too stressful. I love how large the island is, there's so much to explore, and I still haven't unlocked a lot of content. There are a few "buggy" items I've noticed, like when trying to enter a building getting the dialog to pop up can be tricky (the museum is a good example) and catching bugs can feel wonky trying to align the net and swing where I am actually aiming. Small things that are expected in Early Access. I look forward to what the Devs will bring to the game! 10/10 recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: It has a lot of potential. A 3d Stardew valley with a bigger map, bigger farm more people and more activities to fill your day. I like the diving and all the furniture you can add to your farm and house. The expansion of the cooking with all the cooking items is neat also.Lots of stuff still missing at the moment. Lets hope it doesn't get abandoned in early access.

_childDocuments_.review: Game mechanism wise there is almost no difference from Stardew Valley. The main plot is also similar. Player is still collecting stuff for the museum; fighting against big evil corp; taking over the family farm. Even the mining cave is exactly the same (finding holes to descend, elevator every 5 levels etc.). For a farming sim in general it's still pretty solid. But for people like me who's looking for something new after hundreds of hours in Stardew (AND modded stardew valley!), the first few hours of this game feels very underwhelming, and kinda boring. I do like the character design, but I wish the main story is more captivating.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Not great, not terrible. Has a bunch of issues and feels incomplete, but you can still have a lot of fun tooThe good:- Very relaxing overall atmosphere, with no time limits other than for errands- Option to make ingame days progress slower (down to 50%) - great for further reducing how stressful it feels- Very diverse characters: lots of different ethnicities, ages etc. One character has visible stretch marks as another example. Really well done!- Awesome character customization options: There is a nonbinary body option (never seen that in a game before), and besides the "Mr", "Ms" and "Mx" default adresses you can also define custom ones \- fantastic! You can also always change your name, how you want to be adressed, and the look of your character during the game.- Setting: It's not revolutionary, you take over the family farm as usual in this genre. But it still offers some cool environments and history- Automation features, like auto fertilizer or auto chests (haven't unlocked a lot of them yet so can't talk about how well they work, but offering automation features at all is good)- Items show if you've already donated them either to the museum or for bundles. Other information is severely lacking, but this particular aspect is great- Fast travel feels good to unlock over time and useThe bad:One of the main issues is that there is only extremely limited information available ingame, to the point where it gets difficult to play without using an external wiki. A lot of other games in the genre fall into the same trap, but that's no excuse to follow that trend. Gifts are particularly annoying because they come up all the time: Why can't you ask what a character likes? Are you really supposed to trial and error all possible gifts for every character? Sometimes characters tell you what they (dis)like in a dialogue - but then the game doesn't actually update the information in the known character (dis)likes so you have to memorize it, or write a list yourself. You were this close to having at least one mechanic to help with this, that wouldn't really have been enough but at least something, and then you fumbled even that.But gifts are far from the only info that is missing. Other examples: You only see sell price of items when in a shop or accessing the shipping chest, you can't see what seasons plants grow in, the list goes on. There is even a section with info on crops etc in the codex - but it just doesn't give you any of the relevant info, like price or season etc. This is the perfect opportunity to include info directly ingame with a system already in place, and then it just has basically no useful information. You also can't look at open bundles and what you need unless you are physically there, for some bundles you only need to donate some of the items which leaves some items as permanently showing "not offered" even though you've completed the bundle. The list goes on. It's just a mess trying to get to the information you want, and you'll just end up using the wiki a lot instead.There are lots of shallow characters, and meaningless / forgettable cutscenes. You'll go "...neat, i guess?" and then move on as if nothing has happened in most cases. It doesn't really develop characters or does much of anything else. Haven't finished the game yet so maybe this will change, but so far it's been disappointing.Inconsistent UI: For regular crops, if you hover over an unwatered crop with your watering can your cursor turns into a watering can to show you can / should water it. With saplings, the cursor does not change and i had to learn through the external wiki that you do in fact have to water them.Inconsistent controls: Sometimes you have to click right click to progress dialogue. Sometimes you have to press right click. Good luck always remembering which to use.Bad combat controls in particular: With a sword, your character also dashes forward when you attack. This actually makes you dash *through* enemies a lot of the time, which leaves you flailing around back and forth trying to hit enemies. Yikes! How did this get through playtesting, it's just awful. Hammers don't suffer the same issue at least which automatically makes them preferrable as weapons.Repeating gameplay: Underwater exploration and caverns are painfully similar. For both you destroy piles of items in hopes of finding the way forward, based on RNG. The aesthetics of the underwater exploration are cool, but that's still lazy and boring game design to use the same mechanics.Lack of quality of life features. Example: To fill up a recycler to craft scrap from trash, you have to click 20 times. There is no button that i'm aware of that just fills it up. That's not great accessibility wise, although it can be solved with an autohotkey script at least. You also always have to equip the item to put them into a crafting building. Which is further frustrating because of:Painful inventory management. One thing that constantly infuriates me is that if you are accessing a chest, then you cannot move items from one slot to another in your own inventory. In other words, you cannot sort your inventory while accessing storage, which means you have to frequently open a chest, transfer items, close the screen, reopen inventory screen, sort etc. And if you want to transfer something else, guess what, time to open and close screens again. Fun! And there's no reason for it to be this way, hold-dragging items would not conflict with anything so why can't you just do that?Overall, the game has a lot going for it, but it's also missing a lot of polish, ingame information, quality of life features, and character developments. It's not bad, but prepare to be frustrated in places. Stardew Valley is a much more polished experience in just about every way in comparison, and if you haven't played that yet then would recommend you give that a go first. But if you've played games in the genre already and are looking for something new, then Coral Island is definitely worth checking out.

_childDocuments_.review: Coral Island is a farming simulator with many different ideas and unusual, but interesting designs. When I say this the art style is absolutely gorgeous and detailed. The story is fleshed out somewhat (I still haven't finished yet) as of this review. The road map is a thing and I am excited to see some of the future updates for the game. So where do we begin:Short Summary: It is true to the genre close to a harvest moon like experience but better in sense of gameplay and okay with character development (It feels bland to me, but I have not finished everything). It's harvest moon on garbage island, turn garbage island into nice island. Has the genre's normal downsides (lull periods, tycoon peaking, etc.)What makes this game different from other farming sims?-You grow seeds, raise animals and sell them for profit to save your dying town.-You clean the ocean by tediously/hypnotically using a sickle to gather every, single bit of trash in the entire water map (You don't have to get it all, but I'm a degenerate).-This game's message is very clear, it's about recycling and taken care of our island home.-There are several story lines that can be interesting but personally I am more into the merfolk's part. What's the farming like?-You can farm above the water or in it (Farming underwater takes a while to get to)-You can make the farm almost fully automated without a factory like idea. What else does this game feature?-Lots to collect (Progression is dictated by this, so would say there is alot of collecting)-Simple crafting system/progression  (Gather x build y, gather x research z)-Ranking system: hit ranks to gain more things and progress the plot. -Plenty of things to aim for, however I still feel it's missing a sort of spark to motivate me to want to learn more about the island (This may also be because I've played alot of games like this). Why recommend it?-Devs are active, not always the most communicative but active. -The game is very fleshed out, lots of things to do and discover, you are encouraged to explore.-Very much so worth the price, however you can get a good deal different sales during the year. -There is quite alot to this game compared to other games, it has seen itself to full release and is very stable. Any cons? (Not really deal breakers, just minor annoyances and things I feel like people would wanna know) -I dislike the combat for caves, it's just annoying. Serves no purpose besides collecting things and mining. Plus being a nuisance. -Can become tedious, and point of time where it feels like there's nothing much else to do after about two or three years in the game. (This is just a common problem in this genre sometimes). -It's very player driven story, and collecting progresses the story. So if you miss something early in the year you will have to wait the entire year to get what you missed the first time.  - It loses steam after sometime in certain parts of the game, where it just kinda lulls until you get to the good parts. -This is probably just me but I dont feel a bond with anyone. Some of the characters just seem bland, not all characters need to pop but I just don't really like anyone. The game is fine, but the story for me is just boring. -Animal farming is boring and the normal feed animal or let them out. At least you can reskin them but I don't care for this part of the game either.-Having a horse makes no difference if i can just teleport, plus the animation just makes it feel weird.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: 3.5/5 Overall, I actually really love this game. It has a lot of the classic hallmarks of a farming simulation RPG, but with enough new content to not be redundant. The main issue with it is that it is unfinished. I still think it's worth playing in it's unfinished state, but I wish that they Stairway Games hadn't marketed is as a "full release" with several parts of the main storylines still unfinished. Pros: - Characters customization: You have the opportunity to be a plus-sized character and use they/they pronouns which I love. There are nots of cute hairstyles and it's pretty easy to customize your look. - Flexible time: You have the option of making time move slower or quicker, which I think is a great addition as it allows you to play the game more casually or more intensely based on your preference. - LGBTQ+ Representation: There are multiple canonically queer and non-binary characters. - Farming: The team has chosen a great selection of crops and I really like the additions they've made to the sprinklers. I also like that they clearly took inspiration from some of the most popular Stardew Mods, like Automation. - Diving and Ocean-Adjacent Mechanics: Honestly, diving and ocean exploration might be the best addition to the farming sim RPG format. All of the interconnected mechanics feel extremely well thought out: the shells, the collectible critters, the different kinds of kelp, the dehydrator, the coffers, the research objectives and prizes, etc. My only criticism would be that I wish garbage accumulated more quickly. - Critters and Museum: I love the inclusion of an Animal Crossing-style net and bug/critter collection system. And I love that the museum combines the best features of both the Animal Crossing museum and the Stardew museum. - The Island and General Aesthetic: I really like map layout and the rate at which new areas are opened. I also really like the general aesthetic, very bright and friendly and tropical. - Character Design: All of the NPCs are super cute and very diverse. And they all have different outfits for each season, and even change into a bathing suit when at the beach!! They also have A LOT of dialogue. - Holidays/Events: I actually think that Coral Island has some of the best holidays out of any farming sim RPG. They all have a ton of little mini games that are super fun, there is character dialogue in the days before and after the event which makes it feel very organic, attending events has an impact on your relationships with the villagers, and some events even change slightly from year to year. Cons:- Combat: The combat is pretty lacklustre. To be honest, I'm not a big combat fan to begin with, so I don't really mind how easy combat is. However, I can see how a lot of people would find it boring. There are very few different mobs and they're all extremely easily to defeat. - Lacklustre Romances: In general, the romances lack, well... romance. You basically get one romance-based heart event with your love interest (the 10-heart event). And there isn't a ton of dialogue specific to dating. However, Stairway Games have stated that they plan on expanding the romance in the future. (Specifically, I know they've said they're going to add a playdate option, which I imagine will function similar to My Time At Portia). There also just isn't a lot of gameplay included in the marriage + children mechanics. But again, these are also supposed to be updated. But at the time being, there just doesn't seem to be a lot of point in romancing characters. - Typos and Glitches: Honestly, there are a lot of issues with dialogues and glitches. This is to be expected considering it's an unfinished game, but I don't think Stairway should have labeled the game as a full release while there are still so many issues. I will say, the team is extremely responsive to bug reports and dialogue errors on Discord. - Weather RNG: This mainly applies to the collection of critters. But there are many instances where a lack of stability in the RNG messes up a play through. For example: The red king arowana fish is only available for six days of the year and only appears during Rainy/Stormy/Windy weather. I have played three years of the game and have never managed to have the correct weather during these six days, meaning I've never been able to complete the museum. Things like this could easily be configured to make sure that certain days of the year are guaranteed to have certain weather. - Clicking Through Dialogue: Okay, this is probably more of a personal preference. But characters will often have 4-6 dialogues per day. And sometimes it can feel a little tedious have to keep clicking to talk to the NPC over and over again. I wish that some of the dialogue was grouped together into a slightly longer dialogue so I didn't have to click to re-talk to them so many times.

_childDocuments_.review: Been watching the progress of this game for a few years now, eagerly waiting to to inherit a new farm. I was not disappointed in the least! _childDocuments_.review: The "Not Reccommended" is ONLY because the game isn't finished. If/when it is finished, I will change this.If you are a more story-oriented player and the RPG and story progression elements of a game as opposed to grinding resources and doing more repetitive actions? - do NOT buy this game in its current state. I will explain more below.However, if you prefer the more "chill", repetitive gameplay over the story & RPG elements of a game - Go for it, but maybe wait for a sale. I say wait for a sale, because honestly it doesn't feel fair paying full price for an unfinished game.I'll outline the bad / meh parts first:- The game is unfinished. There is yet to be developed plot / map areas / object & npc interactions. - After the first in-game year the game gets kind of grind-y.- While you're given the chance to romance townies, there are barely any cutscenes/interactions that distinguish a romanced character from just someone you're friends with. That is cutscenes with character X play out as you earn hearts in the same way regardless if you're romancing them or not. - There are some bugs with characters getting stuck, resources disappearing from machines. It's nothing game-breaking, but it gets annoying after a while.-The weather mechanics they have in place are kind of questionable. More rainy seasons (fall/spring) and winter barely get any weather (rain/snow) at all. Yet you have game objectives tied to weather. You can't "summon" weather to appear (as of the current game version) like in Stardew Valley with the rain totem for example. So you're stuck with 98% sunny days.Now to the good stuff:- The game looks gorgeous. The animation and the style of animation and art available in the game is stunning.- There is a focus on ecology, heritage, and a strong sense of community which is beautiful.- The underwater stuff is fascinating but it currently suffers from lacking any content beyond the main story mission & cleaning up the sea. Hopefully the next update will fix that.- The gameplay flows smoothly.-Even though the game is unfinished and missing both plot, character progression, and map areas, between the collectibles & quests to improve the land and sea you have plenty to do. I'm 47 hours in and I still haven't finished the offerings or museum collections.But currently, the 2 biggest things this game has going for it is it's pretty and it's kind of chill as unlike other similar games you don't really have a deadline of complete objective X by time Y (yet). Hope this is helpful.

_childDocuments_.review: As a kickstarter backer, I am severely disappointed and ashamed at the state of the game, especially after it showed so much promise.Despite getting out of Early Access and being version 1.0, Coral Island is NOT finished in the slightest.Worst part about it is that the early game is good until you're a couple of seasons in, which is why I assume it's been reviewed positively recently. I suspect most recent reviews just haven't gotten to the unfinished parts.I'm talking bugs aplenty, missing or incomplete features and even whole segments of the game that lead to nowhere and don't leave an impact. Missing assets such costumes characters mention they are wearing and map portraits, placeholder texts such as "TBD" and <PlayerName>, underwater critters using the wrong models and just looking like a bunch of buggy textures floating around, poor performance in certain areas, pets not moving and so much more.Progression is really weird as well.For example, getting a stable and a horse to move faster takes a fair bit of investment, yet you unlock free fast traveling to pretty much all major and important areas really quickly making the horse more of a nuisance to use rather than an upgrade. Especially since getting off the horse not only has a weird default keybind that is on the other side of the keyboard (K), but also because the animation is slow and you can't forage on a horse. You're better off staying on foot and using space bar to dash (Which the game never tells you you can do).The game also fails to tell you what to do to achieve certain things. There are these withered trees that you obviously have to restore, but despite having restored some of them, I have no idea as to how and when it happened. I just randomly noticed they changed while walking by. None of the NPCs mention it and there doesn't seem to be any reward either.There are also these weird "magic" cutscenes that sometimes happen during the night indicating some kind of change or happening that I have no idea what causes them or what they do. Nothing seemed to have changed when going to the area they happened in. There was only a single time where I found a new path that was unlocked, but there didn't seem to be anything there except more blocked off areas and a "shortcut" to a place I can fast travel to.Rewards for progressing are a joke as well. Altar bundle rewards (Think of community building rooms in Stardew) are basically useless. I haven't fully completed any of the 4 altars, and only a handful of bundles inside of them, but what I've gotten so far has not been worth it whatsoever. Oooh, wow, 8 seeds I can use next season. Thanks game, I'll subtract them from the +500 I need to buy. Sure, Stardew has the same rewards, but there you at least know you're working towards a bigger, unique reward that isn't just "this is pretty now" which seems to be a theme in CI.Mining is yet another issue. Coral Island splits up their mines into 4 different caverns with different 'themes'. But in actuality, they all pretty much look and feel the same. Each mine houses one of the 4 different ore. But here's where the issue comes in. Because you can only find a single type of ore in each mine, you often have to go back to earlier mines to grind for copper which is tedious. And ore nodes spawn way too infrequent and reward way too little ore. I'm talking whole floors without a single node and each node can give as little as 1 ore. And you need 5 to smelt into a bar. And the reward chests you get every 10 or so floors are not exciting either. You get like a couple of craftable (and in most cases useless) tools in the first few, but outside of that it's just the same food item over and over and over. You get 2 weapons across all the chests in the game. A hammer, which is inferior to the starting sword in every single way and an upgraded sword, which is decent, but you can buy an equally strong or even better weapon for just a little bit of money. The only real useful thing you get out of these chests are the explosives, but even those aren't too expensive to craft.And the combat in the mines is a joke. It's floaty, unsatisfying and unengaging. You just take the sword and spam left click until the enemy dies. No enemies are a real threat to you, they all die pretty quickly and are fought the same way. This also makes the tools I mentioned earlier pretty useless and a waste of time and resources. Even when an enemy gets to attack, their attacks are just as floaty and buggy. For example, some enemies still hurt you long after their attack animation appears to be over and others can still attack you in their death animation.But what about the other activities?-Farming is alright.-I barely touched ranching, it didn't seem to be worth the effort.-Fishing is slow and boring. I always seem to find the same fish no matter whether I fish in the ocean, lake or rivers.-Bug catching is unrewarding at best and frustrating at worst with some bugs fleeing as soon as you're in catch range.-Diving. Oh geez I mentioned diving. Not only is diving linked to one of the unfinished segments of the game, but said unfinished segment is your reward for enduring the slowest, most repetitive chore of the entire game. Your movement speed underwater is so slow and there is trash  that you need to remove. While it does do a good job at getting the game's message across, it doesn't work well in the concept of this game. Everything is just so slow, from walking, to removing to having and having to hit some trash piles multiple times. And your reward? A confusing area with no purpose and unfinished characters. Oh and kelp which is the only reason to put up with this crap as it's used for crafting and upgrades, but you find that littered all over the place.Super confusingly, there are also 4 different underwater caverns which have to be unlocked by clearing out the zones they're in. But they house nothing but rooms to farm infinite trash! Even more insulting, considering the one character that mentions these caves tells you that they might be of value to you. And the caves once again show that this game is unfinished, since they're NES Zelda-like square rooms with doors on each wall. Said doors only open once you clear enough trash. But there is no feedback when they open. No sound, no animation, the stones blocking the path just get deleted in plain sight. And the other rooms also just contain more trash.Completing the underwater quest seems to unlock another quest that seems to allow you to turn into a “merfolk” and hopefully fixes the movement speed issue and maybe fleshes out the place more, but that is only AFTER you explored and cleared the ENTIRE MAP already. At this point I was fed up with this section and never went back to diving except in the rare instances where I needed kelp. Maybe it fleshes out the underwater kingdom more, who knows, but the path leading up to it is so slow, repetitive and unenticing that I simply couldn’t be bothered to do that now as well, just for the  that there might be something more to that area. After all, everything leading up to this quest pointed towards a big, fat NO.I really wanted to like or at least "finish" the game, despite its state. But I only managed to get a few days into my first winter before finally waving my white flag.I gave up once I ran into a bug that created duplicates of all my tools in my inventory that you can't delete, drop or sell. All I did was try to enchant the tools, and once I opened the menu they just appeared.I also read that there is a major issue during the winter festival that will straight up permanently delete your tools if you don't watch out. of these issues would be actual issues if the game was still in early access and marked as unfinished. But this is unacceptable.TL;DR: Check the title.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fun! I had this game from early access but only tried it after full release and it was worth the wait! As per now, most of the bugs are getting fixed. So far, I haven't encountered any game-breaking bugs like what other people mentioned. There are still minor, inconveniencing bugs but they won't affect much of the gameplay imo. Main quest is still in development. You'll progress quite far (enough to get you hooked), hit the ceiling, and make do with weekly errands for the time being as you wait for the next update. Based on their 2024 roadmap, though, this game seems very promising but you just gotta have the patience to wait some more.  Still, honestly this game is quite addictive so waiting feels like torture (is it good or bad lol). There are some things I'm not quite fond of though, but maybe it's just me:1. Heart events for some dateables don't really have anything to do with us. It's okay if it's for other NPCs, but for bachelors/bachelorettes, it's a bit awkward how our chara will just stand there🧍‍♂️ without interacting. It feels kinda disengaging in a way. Good thing there's an option to skip😅2. As a nosey person, it's a bit disheartening that there's a chat limit (gift limit is understandable, but talking? come on). Characters, even those with 8 hearts or more, will just straight up ignore you after like 3-4 bubble chats (ngl this is hilarious in a way). I don't mind repeated text lines, I just wanna see them talk more😣3. We can't save other than after going to bed. So it's all or nothing for the whole day. We can't even have multiple save files. One chara, one save file, and it automatically saves once a day. That's it, take it or leave it. (pssst if you tinker with your local save files you can still get the backups)Overall, this game worth your every cents. I wouldn't say it's a blatant copy of Stardew, cause let's be real even that is also inspired by harvest moon, no? This game may be inspired from Stardew (idk), but this game adds a lot of cultural points native to Asia (esp. Indonesia) also design and style are ike apples and oranges. Scientifically speaking, this game spots the gap and room for improvements and they Delivered, so I see no issues. Other mechanics, of course they'd be similar. What are you expecting from a farming sims game? You wanna solve math each time you harvest a crop or what? LmaooCan't wait for more updates (literally I'm on my edge I'm keeping tabs on their socials). Keep up the good work, dev team! Semangat Mas Mbak bakoh♡

Definitely a triple A game being sold for an indie price in my opinion. I highly recommend this game to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: Obviously I'm still pretty early on for this type of game (day like 14 out of probably hundreds?), but so far am really enjoying it. There's a lot of different directions to go, always something to change up what you're doing so far. There are some nice QoL options that weren't in Stardew when I last played it, like you can customize how fast time moves (down to 50% I believe) and make combat more or less optional in the caves. There are, approximately, 1 million named NPCs to talk to and mingle with. Cute animals galore with great names. The librarian is even wearing a cardigan which is the attention to detail you don't always get. I think it perhaps introduces you into the game a bit more gently than Stardew does, for people who got overwhelmed with that. There is still a LOT going on once you get going.

_childDocuments_.review: Review is subject to change.The game is... AWESOME! It gives me so many throwback Stardew Valley feelings, and it feels like such a refreshment in the genre. It not only reproduces the cozy farm game feeling well, but it also introduces much more mechanics. In other words - it brings something fresh without steering away too much from the vibe. However...As of me writing this (v0.5-205) the game is littered with bugs, a lot of which make it pretty hard, if not unable to progress. I've been posting some of my encountered bugs on developer's Discord as well as browsing the reported bugs and well... the list keeps growing, while the community manager only assures players of a fix coming "in a future update", without giving any context as to when to expect a fix. From crashes to inventory wipes to even forcing player to ALT + F4 due to broken interface, I cannot say I would recommend you getting this game at this very moment. Instead, wait for it to release with the fixes, so that your experience isn't as scuffed as mine is.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game a lot, but a game about conservation and environmental preservation on an island (aka a unique ecosystem with many endemics) shouldn't have outdoor cats just wandering around (which cause upwards of 3 billion bird deaths per year in the usa alone, and have been the cause of multiple mass extinctions on many island ecosystems). In addition, the world is a bit big for the speed the character moves, and it's hard to reach things in a timely fashion when the map is complex like this.

_childDocuments_.review: This game still has a long way to go, but it is exceptional, even as is. While I question some of the writing and dev priorities, the world presented is rich, and vibrant, including unique gameplay that you don't often see in farming sims like this. The premise that you need to clean up the island is refreshing and fun. The artwork is exceptional. I disagree very much with the reviews that say the diversity is "forced" or "pandering". You're on an island in the south pacific -- it feels very natural that such an island would have many types of people. I also like that the romance options don't trend too young or seem like they're barely adults. They've lived lives, run their own businesses. They might even be single parents, and that is refreshing. Only nitpick is that the museum feels very tacked on, and is very difficult to fill up. The game is still very much in the early stages so if you don't want an incomplete game (not many festivals are finished, some dialogue options have placeholder text) but you can see where it is going, and that's very encouraging. I recommend it, especially on sale or buying when it's finished.EDIT: The gameplay of this game is really awesome and unique. The underwater portion is some of the most fun and completely atypical of what you typically see in a life/farming sim. The variety of romances continues to be great.🚨🚨 EDIT 2: 🚨🚨I cannot in good conscience recommend this game to anyone in its current state. It has so much potential, great mechanics, interesting gameplay, and a diverse cast. Unfortunately potential is all it has. Since the 1.0 release I was hopeful that many of the incomplete aspects of the games would be completely fleshed out, as is typical of games. In just about every other Early Access game, incomplete parts of the story are completed for 1.0. There may be bugs (even game breaking ones) but the storyline is whole, the character arcs are whole, and it is by itself a complete standalone product that can be improved upon down the line. You expect bugs but you expect the main story to be complete.That's not the case with coral island. This is an incomplete game. The main storyline is incomplete. Some of the romances are incomplete. Major portions of the game that are touted as unlockable as a main function of the gameplay are incomplete and thus *not* unlockable. It seems like huge portions of this game are simply not finished. This is not a v1.0 quality game. This game is still in early access, despite the label and the price bump. Do not buy this game. There is so much to complete you should not play this game unless you are prepared for your save to be wiped whenever they eventually get to finishing the main quest line.It is completely beyond me why this was rushed to release.There are many more complete farming/life sims out there. You should play one of those instead.

All cooked items will display the effect it has and produces two (which you can easily gift to townsfolk)! Recent additions of the auto chest have made some interesting automation to the farm.
