_childDocuments_.review: One of the few post-Stardew games that ACTUALLY changes and refines the genre instead of being a cash grab cozy farming game with little development or support. Below might have spoilers depending on your definition of spoiler.Here's how it's better than Stardew:1. Theme. Stardew is farming. Coral Island is farming AND healing the land, whether it be through diving and clearing out the ocean or helping restore the island's heritage sites. There's greater purpose imo because of this.2. Quality of Life. Imagine your Stardew game with your QoL mods. Coral Island has it innate already -- within reason. You can craft things in the cave using resources in your chests back home. Mousing over an item tells you if it's a museum or shrine item and if you'd already donated or offered it. The tarash cans even visibly change to look empty after you've dumpster dived so you know what cans you've hit and not.3. Diversity. The NPCs come from a variety of cultures, have personalities and interests beyond stereotypical jock/sketer/gamer/etc, and come in different shapes even. It's wholesome and warms my heart. The nod toward culture and heritage comes through in the game's storytelling, design, and crops also.4. Large map. There is SO much to the town, the lake, the beach, etc. There's always some place to check for forage-ables and something to do.5. Progression. I always feel like I'm progressing beyond the museum or altar donations because, for example, I foraged enough to gain a bonus to my stamina and even my speed. The level up options are great and the skill paths aren't locked as in Stardew. I love feeling the slow increase in my stamina rather than bursts of increases from stardrops.6. DIVING. Such a cool mechanic with an ecofriendly theme. I heard there are mermaids later..? I haven't reached that part.7. BUG-CATCHING. Also cool.8. Cooler pets. You can have a bunny or lizard, not just cat or dog! The pets are SO cute.9. Fishing. I like the fishing mechanics more but this is purely subjective.Things Stardew does better:1. Multiplayer. That's it. But this will come out later in Coral Island.

The different festivals and seasons also give a nice breath of fresh air every now and then.8/10 ~ Ya can adopt pets!

_childDocuments_.review: If you like animal crossing, little wood, or stardew valley this is a great choice for you. Pros:Artwork & Character design - you can see they put extra thought into including people of all kinds (my only gripe is I wish there were more options for dark mysterious types to romance)Combat - Combat is fun and simple swinging your weapon is satisfying with the movementLots to do - At first it seemed a little overwhelming but you can really pick and choose what you want to accomplishLevel System - The more you do the more you level that particular treeMusic - Nice and relaxingStory - Main story seems pretty basic but with so much to explore and so many characters to meet it doesn't need to be too complicatedCons:(This game is in Alpha so im sure many of these will change)- Minor bugs that can sometimes break immersion- A bit confusing at first, no clear tutorial on where to find things such as crafting menus ect.- The days feel a little too quick, (Time flows a bit too quickly)- Storage systems work nicely for inserting items into chest but taking out into your inventory can be a bit awkward- The main antagonist of the story is literally named Karen, like I get it but does it have to be so literal? You can see this trope throughout the story most of the time its funny but for some reason this just kinda made me roll my eyes a bit.Overall really great relaxing game! You can definitely get lost in this one for hours at a time.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who grew up spending most of my time playing Harvest Moon games... Coral Island is AMAZING. I played a little bit of Stardew Valley when it first came out, and although it is a lovely game, it never quite hooked me in the way Harvest Moon games did. Coral Island is so special and charming. The lore is interesting and the designs are truly beautiful. Some of the more fleshed-out characters have so much personality to them that it doesn't feel like a chore to sit through cutscenes and read dialogue lol. I'm in a weird and transitory period in my life right now and this game has inspired me to start sewing my own clothes and take more risks with the sculptures I create. There is something really comforting about the atmosphere. Honestly, more than anything, it's comforting that the developers even imagined up a world like this and decided to share it with us.

_childDocuments_.review: for the people complaining about it being like stardew:news flash:people love stardew because it is so many of them and the best parts combined. with modding abilities.others are complaining about well.. early access hiccups. wait until full release then. no ones forcing you to play right now. This game constantly shows you how much love the devs put into it. you see the characters do so many various animations, they hang out together, have conversations, the families can be seen playing at various areas of the games maps such as the volleyball court.everyone has personal backstories and are unique. A fan favorite seems to be suki, who has stretch marks and is dealing with leaving kids father and self improvement.theres someone for everyone.this game has the best of the farm sim game genre in it, with extras such as animal crossing activities liek bug catching and diving.NO MATTER how you want to play, it is viable. wanna farm? farmwanna catch bugs nonstop? catch bugs.wanna only fish? fish.wanna gather and mine only? do that.you can easily make money off all the side activities. you can make your farm into a huge bee sanctuary and flower garden if you want. it can literally be anything you want. things also place well beside each other no annoying gaps like in animal crossing decorating.the hair styles freaking suck but they are adding more and sculpting them right now for players. if you look at the discord and see the daily lists the devs post on there of things they actively work on its absolutely amazing and exhaustive. they are putting so much effort into this, and if you crash a lot and ask things the discord devs from the game will personally reply a lot or ask you for your crash reports/save files to fix whatever issue with very quick times!!! its the middle of the night for them and one of them is currently looking over my broken file after the patch this morning that seemed to break a lot of ppls save files.the festivals are fun and have mini games that are new to play with the villagers. and you can see a lot of signs and notes in game about how the devs plan on putting something there.this game when it is done is going to be amazing. it will have high replayability due to the MASSIVE amount of characters in it to choose from, and how you can really just do anything and have it be a viable main activity for your farm.if early access is going to bug you, and the chance of needing to be wiped and starting over will end it for you, then please just wait for full release.if you dont mind it though and still just want to test the waters i encourage you to really take your time to talk to people multiple times, and take your time looking around and watching the animations and things cause its so so so lovely.i have played so much, i played alpha and tested as well and i never rlly see any conversation repeats.  theres also the universally liked gifts that are easy to craft.there are problems sure but they are being fixed. controller was so lovely to play with in alpha but a patch broke it and its still currently being repaired. if you just take some time to look over the dev diaries on the discord and really appreciate the potential this game is truly amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game has the potential to be one of the best, new farming games. Personally I'm having a blast with it, and it works perfectly on the Steam Deck!Here is what I like:-The colorful world and diverse characters-28 romancable characters - The focus on environmentalism and cleaning up the island around you-There are quite a few festivals, that have a variety of new themes I haven't seen in other games in this genre  (although I personally find the mini games frustrating)-Theres a lot to do: farming (theres plenty of farming animals to chose from), fishing, mining, bug catching, cooking. And a museum to fill up with all your collected items -A lot of character customization options (including pronouns and body types) and clothing -You can change the exterior style of your house and farm buildingsIssues I have with the game:-The full story is not released, there are items marked as TBD-The character lack distinct personality, they have about 3 lines a day that repeat pretty often. If you date or marry these characters, their lines barely change-You can adopts pets. But only one pet and they don't currently do anything other than stand in their bed, and move around every so often-There are mermaids, but their story isn't finished yet either-I have had lag issues, freezing issues and occasional crashing issues. I assume these will be fixed in an update soonHere are some notable features coming in 2024 (unclear on if it will be free or paid. I assume they will be free but you never know these days):-Tourist system-Hangout/Dating mechanic-A big Merfolk update-Ocean farming and ranching-More story-Children update (you can have children in the game currently, but I assume this will add more to them)-Savannah access-Island visit-Multiplayer

_childDocuments_.review: I've spent nearly 80 hours in Coral Island, and I’m loving the journey! 🌴 It’s got everything I wanted in a farming sim. While it doesn't feel completely "finished" (but what is these days?), the game has a solid foundation and plenty of content to explore. There’s definitely a grind that could be made more enjoyable with managing your own shop and/or some optional daily mini-games (like Urbz: Sims in the City-style mini-games with level progression as you improve) to take a break from button-mashing through trash and rocks, but it’s still been pretty engaging overall.That said, a few things could make this game even better. If you like the social aspects of these games, be aware that relationships with townsfolk currently feel a bit underdeveloped. Friendships and marriage don't seem to offer any in-game benefits right now, so it can feel pointless to engage with others. It’d be great if friendships offered store discounts or other perks, and if marriage partners, children, and pets could help on the farm.The only technical issues I've noticed were some minor lag during movement and the “Disguise Wanted” cutscene replaying. Otherwise, it’s been running great on default settings on the Steam Deck. Overall, Coral Island is a fun, relaxing game, and I’m excited to see how it grows!

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing game.  Well worth the Early Access.  It has a clear update schedule with many additions to come and is still quite a large game as is with much to do.  Its diversity and cultural awareness is very thoughtful and enlightening.  There is a little bit for everyone in this game with so much more planned to be added and expounded upon.  The game plays well and the Devs seem really open to constructive criticism and suggestions for future implementations.  Its similar to the genre that we are used to, but has a refreshing take on it that makes it feel like a whole new game.  Especially the diving.  You can go fishing just like in other games, farming, collecting for temple bundles, mining, light combat, etc. but the diving.....An amazing new addition and extremely put together with a story of its own.  Speaking of the story line without any spoilers, it gives this game a step above others in this genre and really makes everything feel like it has a purpose and is tied together.  I would definitely recommend this game and in its current Early Access form as it is so well put together, so much yet to come, and I am 30 solid hours of game play in and I have just started to really scratch the surface.  Enjoy this one!

_childDocuments_.review: Caveat Emptor!tldr: Don't grab this unless you're ok with an unfinished game.I hope to change this review as what there is of this game so far I have enjoyed. I generally avoid Early Access games, I like to enjoy finished products and don't get as much enjoyment as some out of seeing works in progress. Coral Island's development and the generally positive attention it has been getting left me optimistic so I purchased when it exited early access, but the 1.0 release feels like an attempt to get enough money to finish a kickstarter that ran out of cash (or worse, cash in on what's been finished and never touch it again. Fingers crossed that isn't the case).This game should not have received a "full release." While there is a lot of game to enjoy, much of it is still incomplete, including main aspects of the story framework the farming simulator hangs itself on. Much of that content is well beyond the two hours of play Steam allows refunds at though, so don't pick it up unless you're ok with that ahead of time.

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly struggled for some time on deciding if I should recommend the game. However, in the end I cannot overlook that the devs are trying to sell a game that is de facto still in early access as a "full release". The game is fun and the art is beautiful. I can even live with the bugs. However, at every turn of the game I have to wonder if what I am building towards will even be in the game. Looking through the recent reviews, you will quickly discover a long, long list of missing features and content. What feels worst to me is how dead the underwater portion of the game feels. That is, after all, a core element of the game and one of the parts that elevates it above a mere Stardew Valley clone. But as the devs themselves say in a recent update: These are parts of the game planned for 2024. Which seems odd given that the store page itself already promises buyers that you can romance some of the merfolk. Except that this is not yet included in the current "full release".My recommendation is honestly to buy My Time at Sandrock instead. Fully fleshed out, a ridiculous amout of content, and a wonderful cast of quirky, fully voiced characters. If you want the mystical and magical elements, you might also consider the charming Wylde Flowers. Coral Island, meanwhile, will be worth a purchase once it actually comes out of early access in a year or two.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game I wanted to love. It's in one of my favorite genres, it hits all the notes, but I just can't say I enjoy it, for a few reasons.One, it's horrifically derivative; as other reviewers put it, it's "we have Stardew Valley at home." This game does absolutely nothing that Stardew Valley doesn't already do better (and that goes fivefold if you have any of the major Stardew quality-of-life mods like UI Info Suite.) It's the _same game_ but nowhere near as well done. Stardew's characters are more memorable, the heart events and plotlines better written (and again, speaking of mods, Stardew Valley Expanded and Ridgeside Village are practically free DLC. You know any expansions this game gets won't be free.)So if there's another game that does everything this game does, at half the price (or less, if you get Stardew on sale), then why choose this game over that one when you could be playing that one?Two, it's laughably unfinished. This is not a 1.0 release as of November of 2023. It's still very much in Early Access, they just don't want to say that anymore because they apparently needed the money and released it on consoles as a 1.0 and changed the version number on Steam to go with it. Even their roadmap all but says this out loud; it'll be Q4 of 2024, or maybe even 2025, before this game is even realistically a 1.0 release.Three, it's buggy in ways that break the game. Machines don't work right, events don't fire, quests don't advance...they couldn't even copy Stardew right.And just a personal gripe, but there's a musical motif in Spring in this game that is so blatantly a Wild Horseradish Jam copy that it's all but winking at how it got one over on you.Seriously. If you haven't played Stardew Valley, buy that instead. And if you have played Stardew Valley, just go play it again and save yourself 30 bucks.

_childDocuments_.review: I've Been playing a fair bit of Coral Island recently, almost done with the first year and starting to accumulate the Tier 4 tools.  It's solid, but I haven't been able to figure out what really sets it apart from the rest of the genre.  It just seems like a straight-up Stardew Valley knockoff with more supernatural elements, and I've never really enjoyed the supernatural angle in these games.  Even Stardew built on Harvest Moon/Story of Seasons' foundation, it wasn't just a straight clone.The "cleaning up the island" thing would be a very cool hook if it felt like they did more with it, but as it stands, Portia/Sandrock did more with that in terms of you actually doing something.  Instead, you just leave offerings (the Community Center from SV crossed with the Harvest Goddess from HM), dive into the mine with something good happening at floor 40 of each area, donate to the museum, and clear trash in the ocean to activate relics that clean the ocean for you, and the improvements just sort of happen on their own once you do get a certain amount of "town points" for doing those.  The diving is pretty weak too, it's not appreciably different from the mines except you use the sickle instead of a pick.  Using kelp for permanent passive upgrades to seeds and crop quality is cool, though.Character-wise, the LGBTQ representation is obviously great (the character artist clearly favored the G part more than I'd personally prefer, but that's not a flaw, just not my personal orientation, and even that may say more about what I generally expect male/female character designs to look like), but none of the characters feel like they have much personality to me, and several of the designs kind of blend together.  It doesn't help that despite the 1.0 release, it's clearly not "finished" finished.Overall, like I said, it's solid, and I haven't stopped playing yet, but I can't tell if I actually like it or if I'm just addicted to the gameplay loop.  Another recent Steam review said "I wish there was a Neutral option," and that's kind of where I'm at too.  It's worth a look if you've already played the hell out of Stardew and Portia/Sandrock, especially if you get it on sale, but generally speaking, I can't say I'd recommend it over others in the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: A graphically-superior, yet shallow-er clone of Stardew Valley. Over the past two months, I have played four different farming sims. It all started with Disney's Dreamlight Valley, which then revived my interest in Stardew Valley (which I haven't played since 2019) and I played that game for a while. Then, Wylde Flowers came out and I absolutely fell in love with that game! Lastly, I played Coral Island — it is the weakest of the four by far.The main issue with Coral Island is its reluctance to be its own thing. All of the other games I mentioned do heavily borrow ideas from Stardew Valley, but manage to add something original to the formula, giving it a unique spin. Coral Island, on the other hand, is just a graphically-updated version of Stardew Valley and feels more like a themed mod of it (like, hey, here's Stardew Valley but in Southeast Asia!). It copypastes many of the same things that I find annoying about SV (like the fact that you can only save the game by sleeping, for instance). Instead of trying to improve on the formula Stardew Valley has established, Coral Island just copies its homework without trying to fix any of its problems or use any creativity beyond the different geographical setting.Also, the most recent update to the game wiped out my save file (and I'm not the only one who encountered that issue). I've never had this happen to me before despite playing many different early access titles, so this, to me, showcases that the developers bit off more than the can chew and released their game to the public way too early, especially considering how limited the game is at its current state.

_childDocuments_.review: Played for 250 hours and completed pretty much everything in the 1.1 update. I'll go over some topics I think it’s important and worth talking about (and that i don't see many people talking) + Not mentioning the word ''stardew valley'' for an ENTIRE review challenge.This is a very nice game, with innovative and fresh features in the genre, the world feels alive, the nature and tropical atmosphere + charismatic and lovely NPCs. You can tell it was made with passion, creativity and by people who actually cared. However, nothing is perfect and there are quite a few things and problems you need to consider, the worst of it all (at least for me) was the massive grind and boring gameplay loop, and even tho in the short term you feel like you are progressing in everything you do, the game fails in awarding you for all the trouble and massive hours of grind. Activities just like any other farming sim games, but here we got Ocean Diving, where you help to restore and clear trash from the ocean and exploring an underwater world with ocean creatures and some very nicely put mermaid and ocean folklore. It’s very nice, but it ends up being quite repetitive at a late point. , making it very grindy and repetitive as these are essential tasks for the main story progression and takes very, very long to ''complete''.Progression also feels very slow, completing the bundles, story, and maxing out skills takes a very long time, [/b]wouldn’t be a problem if the rewards weren’t so poor, unsatisfying, and even ‘’outdated’’ at the point of the game you’ll finally complete them[/b]. Getting gold is a bit hard and at the endgame when you are finally swimming in it, there won’t be much to spend on.Not to mention the amount of bundles you gotta complete that takes forever and when you finally do, you’ll unlock even more bundles to complete. 😭The objectives in general feel somewhat very ‘linear’, I truly wished things were more ‘laid back’, unpredictable and chill.Characters are one high point of this game, a very diverse cast and it makes the game feel truly alive, every single one has a distinct personality and if you are a person who likes to hear what they have to say, you’ll like it a lot!, some storylines are very good and well written, very easy and accessible to relate in many states of life.The bad thing is: there are TOO MANY of them and it takes a long time to progress in the friendship. If you decide to speak to everyone around the town, you'll lose more than half of a day doing it for sure. And of course, you won’t be interested in every single NPC, but it takes SO LONG for any kind of progression, it adds a lot of the feeling of ‘’massive’’ into the game.The romance/dating is also a bit dull, with cute cutscenes and dating events, but they won’t say anything different to you in everyday life or anything, it’s like it’s not happening at all. Feels incomplete.  ✿ Character customization is VERY CUTE and there's a huge variety of cosmetics and clothing items.  ✿ Farm customization and house decoration can be a little bit clunky in the square grid (the house has a terrible design) but you can turn out to make very nice inspired decor with tons of different sets, needs some minor improvements and polishing tho! ✿ Festivals are very unique and original, and it has actual fun minigames and cutscenes, just wished the rewards were a little better. ✿ Huge shoutout to the numerous easter eggs, from a BMO and Sponge Bob inspo decorations, to programs in the in game TV referring real shows  and movies like Game of Thrones, Masterchef and even Kpop survival reality shows (Produce 101, we love you!) ✿ The main story was very predictable and a bit disappointing, the game is very original and ambitious and I ended up expecting something new and original for the closing of the story too. Looking forward to new updates, hopefully, it’ll redeem itself in the future.✿ Few acid humor and double meaning dialogues here, had moments asking myself howtf was it even possible, they really got me. ''Groo got stoned and slept'' but he actually got stoned, became a stone for real lol  This review sounds a little too negative and harsh, but I just wanted to highlight some points I don’t see people talking about and in my opinion, are somewhat important. I loved playing this game, felt massive most of the time, but ended up appreciating a lot of the little details of it. Truly wished it were more of a 'laid back' chill and cozy game, even tho there shouldn't be pressure to complete or anything, I felt a bit of it. More updates will arrive in the future,  and hopefully, they will fix and improve some quality-of-life aspects needed for a better-polished game in general.

_childDocuments_.review: This is like Stardew Valley and Animal Crossing, there is just so much more to do. In the beginning this might feel like a lot is coming at you and you might get overwhelmed, but at the same time, there is no timer or certain limit to get it all done, Lots of stuff being completed also kinda depends on luck and with the latest quality of life updates it's even better, however, the latest update also caused some minor bugs, like trying to harvest crops on the ground when you bag is full makes the veggies and fruits become stuck for the entire playthrough, until you restart your game, also a text bar of a fish got stuck above my head for days on. There is plenty to romance in this game, 28 total characters, there are different species of characters, a very big world and ocean world to explore, loads of lore and story, the festivals feel alive, and there is more minigames and winning those minigames is worth your while, you get paid, and get points, it is profitable to befriend the townsfolk, it is also recommended you save everything, do not throw anything away or ship it because you think it is worthless, nearly everything in this game has a use or purpose. ship veggies, fish and stuff you have in abundance instead. Also Multiplayer is on it's way. All in all I give this game a 9/10A very enjoyable farming simulator with the best of all previous games before it. If you're a fan of the old harvest moon, rune factory games but also love the more recent stardew valley, animal crossing new horizons, story of seasons, etc than this game is for you. Don't let the first few in-game days overwhelm you, take everything as it is and just do whatever you feel like. Also I recommend looking online for some good deals. I myself got this on MMOGA for 6.69

_childDocuments_.review: I generally can recommend this game, however I often feel like it's missing the spark to be one of my favorite games. Maybe in a few months there will be updates to change that. However, there are a bunch of things that need fixing, so I made a list below: *I don't like*: - the bugs (obviously)- no explaination of festival minigames (still unsure how the swimming race works)- at the beginning very overwhelming, should add a guide to walk to certain places, or find places on the map- people I can submit quests to should be in a different color on the map, to more easily find them (yes I know there is a searching tool)- you can have only one pet (why am I able to buy more pet beds tho?)- nature looks too planed (it should feel natural/wild)- monster fights are way too easy (first mine)- I hate the sound the letter box makes*bugs I encountered*:- having the same scarecrows-aren't-allowed-in-town event/discussion twice (end spring and beginning summer)- getting the same letter two days in a row- getting a letter to meet somewhere and then the event/meeting not starting when I arrive- sounds not being played, when an activity is done- monster being half stuck in the ground so my attacks don't reach/hit- empty textbox after earthquake at night (right after starting the game)- not sure if that's a bug, but I should be able to submit a quest even tho the person is "busy", I had to wait hours for that one guy to finish his chess-game to give him his item- mermaid hair flowing in front of their body instead of behind when swimming (cutscene with king)- visual glitches, at the very edge of the field some artisian device are partly disappearing- I think I once in spring didn't get my money at the end of the day- after 27h playing with my mouse, the game suddenly wants to force me using a controler (???)Why am I still playing tho? The farming and crafting aspect is very well done. I also like mindlessly cleaning the ocean and catching sea animals and bugs. So far I am in autumn and I intend to continue playing for now.Please give out updates as soon as possible!

_childDocuments_.review: Look, I really like this game, and it's clear a lot of thought went into its creation. The characters are fun, diverse, and there's an element of authentic/genuine cultural identity that's been well represented and upheld in the game. There is a lot of potential, a lot of fun to be had in this game. Honestly, the modding scene is going to be amazing. THAT BEING SAID - the above is what makes a good visual novel. This, unfortunately, is a video game that has been presented as a complete, finished package. It is not. The amount of little glitches and bugs in almost all the mechanics of the game is lowkey embarrassing. The more hours I play, the more I question the quality control process. The characters, storylines, and features start to feel more like an empty marketing gimmick, valuing quantity over quality - which feels a lot more upsetting in this game than it has for me playing other similar games in the past. I think it's because I'm subconsciously upset at seeing how much love, research and respect for culture went into the character and environmental design, and then constantly noticing how the poorly tested mechanics of the game let that love and care down. I'll continue to play it, if only because I have paid access to WeMod, and I like doing little tasks that give my ADHD ass that tasty, tasty dopamine, but I also see myself getting bored of it pretty quickly if an update doesn't come out before the end of the year. Do with it what you will, but as someone who paid full price the week it came out (no early access) I'd hold off for now. It says v1.0. It really should be more like v.0.75

_childDocuments_.review: i have hundreds and hundreds of hours in all kinds of life sims and especially farming sims. this is one of my favorite genres of games, and this is a game i've had my eye on since pre-release.so far here are my thoughts, concerns and feedback; interesting points and some pros:- very inclusive, there is no girl and boy gender, different body type with sliders!- selling bin similar to stardew- theres fishing and bug catching and a museum for them like animal crossing- a general store that has a scheduled day closed similar to stardew- mining and a villain character that wants to make the small town a corporate place like stardew- i love the character art- i love interacting with the strays and animals on the island, and them having cute personalities that show through their actions- i love the diversity of the characters, their identities and their character design- many ethnicities and backgrounds, theres one girl in the inn with stretchmarks and i rlly love that attention to detail and realism ngl- the ambience of the town is SO GOOD!! i love the details in the foliage, the interiors, the layout of the town, how big it is, and generally just a VERY pretty game :)- dating system similar to stardew but havent explored it yet we will see how far that content goes, i.e. can we get married and live together like stardew?feedback/cons, etc: (this game is in early access im not rlly that upset about these just commenting on them so devs can fix for full release)- sometimes characters have red eyes kinda scary haha- the movement is very robotic - the audio settings dont really allow for some sounds to be very low, i have some settings to the lowest possible and they are still very loud- if i lower master volume those sounds just disappear instead of being lowered further- some of the audios in the game feel not very satisfying; i.e. footsteps have no diversity, its like the same one footstep but played over and over (but they do change on the terrain youre on, like sand/wood/stone/dirt)- the town is so so big which i LOVE!! but running is so slow to get around on; granted there are horses and i havent gotten this yet so might change this bit but they seem more of a grind to get and in the mean time it can take like an in-game hour to get from point a to point b sometimes- especially since the general store is so far away x)- some of the hairstyle models are clunky with the textures being a little messed up- the hairstyles bounce a LOT when your character is turning/moving, they look like jello hahaALL IN ALL! right now im in love, and very happy with it, ill come back if anything changes with my opinion and i look forward to the updates, bug fixes, and new content :) ive played stardew into the ground at this point so im so excited for this game and have been for as long as i have known about it. fingers crossed my love stays the same.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a lot of potential here. It does clearly take a lot of inspiration from the other games of it's genre, uncannily so, but so do the rest of the games, everyone inspires the next - that's fine.The farming is standard but enjoyable. The museum and collecting is great! The mines are fun (though I feel there needs to be tweaks to how and how often the next level stairs appear). And the quest lines and stories are nice :)What isn't fine is the fact that the game seems to lack a significant amount of polish. Crashes, lag, weird dialogue triggering (Somebodies wife/husband congratulating us on our engagement ... to them ... days after our own weddings?). Entire quest lines are unfinished, ending in simple WIP tags and to be continued - after the 1.0 release.I really feel like some of the costs and values need significant tweaking. Moving a farm building costs money, destroying it costs over 3 times that? Clothes, and appliance seem prohibitively expensive. After upgrading the house to have a kitchen, you can't even cook unless you drop another 3k on an oven.I know the games in the genre have slow progression, but it does feel like a -crawl- at the start - as you progress this does ease, perhaps the curve just needs shallowing just a tad?Give it a few large patches and I'm sure this game will shine ... but it isn't there yet.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a huge farming sim fan, and have to say, Coral Island has the potential to give Stardew Valley and Harvest Moon a run for their money in terms of leaders in the genre once it is complete. In comparison to many farming sims, Coral Island has a solid story-line, and added a lot of new elements that feel innovative and fresh in the genre. ( Diving is incredibly addictive! ) You can tell the devs have a real vision with this game, and it makes a genre that can feel generic incredibly unique and memorable. This game is by no means finished, but for the first 20-30 hours, you really don't notice it. It isn't until you start to get mid-tier gear and build deeper connections with some of the villagers that has you feeling the content is less than whole. I hope that as development of this game continues they can work on better writing in regards to the townsfolks relationships with your farmer. A lot of the cut scenes feel lifeless, and often times you only have one choice for responding during these interactions. I think most people come to this genre for the dating-sim like elements and intimate feel of living in a small town. I just asked Raj to be my date mate, and every cutscene before that was related to their business with no indication of interest in my farmer. One of the best aspects of games like Harvest Moon is the subtle change in interactions with your farmer as their heart events progress. As the game currently stands, the elements I find most enjoyable are mining, diving, and crafting. I appreciate the innovation in crafting by having universal chests so you can craft items without having to have it in your inventory, and I can tell by many of those small things that as Coral Island develops, it will be an incredibly solid and great game. ( For the first 20 hours... it already is! )

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has played since early access, and has logged around 80 hours in game, let's go through it!Now, I've played pretty much every cozy & farming game known; I feel because of that, I have a great mindset of what this game is doing well, as well as lacking.This game is pretty much 3-D Stardew, except it has more of an island theme, and is mainly focused on things like pollution, culture, & caring for the planet we were given. It teaches the audience to be more mindful, and also to have more care for the oceans with the diving mechanic! So far, it is a great game that the devs clearly care about, as they always are great at catching glitches & bugs as soon as we tell them. This is clearly a project made with love, and the devs show it.Now, this game just released out of early access; have some patience with it! There are so many things to do, and I'm still working on quests & upgrading tools! I love every update, and get so excited when they're announced and I dedicate a few days to catch up to the update, and learn it as best as I can. For a game that is relatively newly released, I think it's fun to play and I would recommend it. However, keep in mind that it is not finished yet, and there's still lots of content to be released! The devs don't need to be rushed either, they're doing a great job communicating with their audience and ensuring that the game they have & the content they release is quality over quantity. Dreamlight Valley can take notes!

_childDocuments_.review: After the number of hours I've sunk into this game it was difficult for me to decide whether to leave a positive or negative review. In the end though, and in spite of the fact that I'll continue to play it for now, I cannot give it a positive review. There's just too many tiny things that spoil the comfy/cozy feeling games like this usually provide. From the mines feeling unrewarding, to the ocean cleanup being a drag. The character frequently feel borderline unlikable. Then there's the bugs that have gone half a year without being fixed. The ones that stand out annoy me the most are with the artisan machines. Pause the game too long an certain artisan machines bug out and will never complete until you close the game. That's annoying enough but then the tappers are ALSO bugged that they lose progress when the game is closed. Overall the game DOES have potential that it fails to fully deliver on.Edit: As of 5/30/24 the bugs have grown too unbearable to to continue trying to like this game. Have requested a refund and awaiting a response.

_childDocuments_.review: Not your typical farming simulator, from 75+ hours played it pulls various activities from games like Stardew Valley, Harvest Moon as well as games like Animal Crossing and puts it all into one. I've found great satisfaction in the diving mechanics, enjoyed the variety of festivals and the overarching story I've experienced so far.The large variety in both the museum and collections is great and I have honestly never found a point where I've been stuck for what to do next. I couldn't recommend this game highly enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: They are calling this version 1.0 but the game itself is very much an early access game at this point. I still recommend this game because they are still doing updates. They tend to do one major update for each season, and then do bug fixes and smaller updates in-between.  There are a few big things they have yet to complete yet such as marriage, and having kids, and the story plots. There is still lots of things to do while waiting for those updates to come. I have played Coral Island since the alpha version, I paid for it through kickstarter. It's a relaxing farm sim type game that gives a unique twist of being on an island. The main story plot is all about cleaning up the island, defeating the company that wants to oil drill, all the while making friends, farming, and romances. It is early access at this point, but has a lot of potencial. Many things are finished, but the story is still being completed along with several quests. They do have a roadmap that they have been following really well for what gets completed. They continiously update the game, more info can be found on their discord. For those who want a complete game I would wait until after early access is over.

_childDocuments_.review: Coral Island at a glance has almost everything I wanted from a farming sim - great looking and diverse characters, a mixture of real and fantastic elements, a rare tropical setting, etc. The game also tackles real ecosystem problems. However, the game felt very mismanaged during early access, leading to it being released 1.0 while missing major content. The devs almost doubled the price to catch the holiday sale number, with an unfinished game. That alone can tell you more about the project than anything else I'm going to say.But besides being unfinished, the game feels lacking in many crucial aspects that are not easily fixed. The writing for instance is subpar. Many key characters I was excited about don't really have any character arc. Take Kenny and Rafael, for example. (Some early spoilers, be warned.) From the moment you meet them, you know they are nice guys. But after several personal events about them, and more than halfway through their heart progression, what more have you learned about them? Nothing. They are still nice guys without any nuances. Their stories are focused entirely on something besides their personalities. I still don't know why Rafael wants to forge this magic hammer, or why Kenny wants to decipher this scroll. It feels completely random. Compare this to Stardew Valley, you learn so much about each character's motivations and dreams, and you see their growth with your own eyes.The game also fails to capture the gravity of ecosystem problems. Basically all you need to do in the game is to find some kind of magic altar, donate random plants to the goddess, and the ecosystem is fixed? It sends a wrong kind of message. Oh the goddess will revitalize the island, and the mermaids will fix the oil spillage. No? Lessening damage done to the ecosystem requires knowledge and a lot of work. It's not easy and not "magical". I almost wish they haven't put the focus of the game on this topic, when they aren't capable of getting it right.One last thing, the game classified tomatoes as fruit. Tomatoes are the fruit part of the plant, just like cucumbers, pumpkins, chili peppers. But if you try to classify it in a culinary sense (fruits vs. vegetables vs. grains), it's a vegetable. This "tomatoes are actually fruits" thing needs to die. It's a misunderstanding of the double meanings of the word "fruit". Literally unplayable.

_childDocuments_.review: Unbalanced, unfinished, full of bugs (and dialogue typos) beta that is still being developed, yet was forceably released out of early acess as a finished game and was asked by devs to promote it for free. Wait until at LEAST 2025 or 2026 before getting it because there's still tons content that needs to be added (there's a HUGE chunk of the story that is missing & the unuseable empty buildings, animals, and scenery just sit there), the duilogues are shallow (and buggy, and if you romance someone, they don't feel like your partner at all), and I suspect that every time they release a BIG big update, you'll need to restart the game again to experience it the way you're supposed to. Cleaning the ocean for the third time? I am NOT doing that by hand again (and for what? For not getting the promised content? Yikes.)Finishing the altar offerings and the museum donations right now feels impossible because the needed scavengeables, gems, resources, fish just don't spawn, and that was my last straw to write this review. I dislike when a game should be fun, but instead feels like a chore despite its great potential.It's a Can't Recommend until it's fixed and finished.P.S.: Oh, and the game has no manual save which is a HUGE no.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't have much time to play games anymore due to the amount of time I have free waning more and more each day, however, this is an expenditure of the rare resource I feel is quite well worth it.1. (Just to state what every other review has said) This game is as much of a Stardew clone as Stardew is Rune Factory clone as Rune Factory is a Harvest Moon clone. Long story short, genres are not exclusive to singular games.2. NPC's feel like people I have genuinely met before.Barring 1-2 NPCs who I genuinely have no care for, almost every NPC I have met I feel I have met throughout my life. It could make my review biased as I feel a more emotional connection due to the similarities to past friends and family members, but its my review so sue me over it.3. Balance of stylization and reality.This game clearly has an artistic style, the title of which I know not, and yet some of its mechanics feel as though its what has been missing from other titles. One of the negative reviews found that swinging and missing with tools consuming stamina was a bad mechanic, yet I found it the exact opposite. Having cut down a few trees myself (and missing occasionally missing, specifically as I was removing stumps), you do get exhausted just from the action of swinging the tool and not even necessarily hitting. And its not even as though its a severe punishment, it is a single energy point and you have a good 400 to start out each day.4. Sheer mass of content.Occasionally I will encounter some games that simply have too much going on and get lost within the labyrinths of their activities. Yet, everything seems to be well connected and every activity worth while. You may dive, fish, farm, bug hunt, to acquire your funds and do whatever you wish with them without feeling you're missing out upon another option altogether. It truly has something for near everyone.5. Level of Detail.Each character has a different outfit for each season, leaves have glistening drops in the rain, puddles temporarily appear, (I haven't seen snow yet, but please do share if there are footprints left after each step), and various other details that escape me at the moment because, well, they're small details, not monumentous achievements.6. Graphics.This is quite a simple game from a graphical perspective, but it is still quite beautiful. Water looks as actual water, sand appears as sand, and while it is stylized, the world still seems as though it is of this world. People don't strange cartoonish features similar to caricatures, they have the appearances of people drawn with artistic flare. This all without mentioning the amount of hand drawn art there is from the TV programs to the character portraits. And anything hand drawn will always bear my appreciation and amazement.Nothing is without negatives however.1. Camera.It feels extremely distant. I know some people wish you could rotate the camera, however, all storefronts and signs are from the set angle, so you would mostly see blank walls. Yet, the distance of the camera makes it very difficult to appreciate all the finer details, such as the glisten of leaves in the rain or the finer details on character 3D models.2. Music.This is very much a personal preference and bias as a musician, but a negative I feel all the same. Much of the sound track follows the same tropical theme as the games style does as well. However, constantly hearing tropical music is... sickening to me... Bright floral notes and pieces can be pleasant in short intervals, however, deeper and more resounding bass notes are much more pleasant over time as even should they grow old, it simply devolves into pleasant background noise, and not an annoying tick in the back of the mind.3. Animations.It is clear the animations are being worked on what with them not being entirely synced up per model, and the amount of animations used is quite amazing. However, the tool swing animation with the leg lifted feels awkward and strange to see. The fact snails will move at mach 10 when alerted is hilarious, however, not quite true to life. And general walking animations can feel slippery, like within a hazy dream, chasing after an ambiguous figure in a fog ridden land.4. Customization.Same as animations, its clear its being worked on, especially hair styles because... well... they're severely limited a little lack luster at the moment of review. However, I truly enjoy fashion and creating various outfits to suite different themes. Whilst there are various customizable clothing pieces with shirts, hoodies, shoes, and shorts/skirts/pants, there's a lack of some pieces such as socks, dresses, scarves(?don't see scarves in many games, could be an interesting addition?), coats, etc.However, this game has so much potential, and the approach the devs have to its creation gives me a very hopeful and bright outlook for the future of the game. Not to mention the clear roadmap of what will be available upon full release.Should you enjoy farming sims or casual games in general, you will almost certainly adore this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, If I had to describe this game in one word, I would use "hollow". During my entire time playing that was the word constantly playing in my headDo note, that I played only slightly under two hours, so I may have not seen most of the content, but most of my problems have a lot to do with the game itself and its general mechanics. So this review is more of my impressions of this game just in time for this game to be refundableSure, you may argue that you cannot criticise a farming sim until you play X amount of hours, but I will say that Stardew Valley had me hooked from the first few minutes and I played for three days straight after that. Besides, if you dont't enjoy the game in the first few hours, it's still a failure of a designerAnd I know that a lot of people get very defensive when you criticise an early access game, but I feel like those problems need to be addressed, because I do actually hope that those negatives will be fixed. Will they? God I hope. Still, criticisms should always be welcomed, because that's how games get betterSo let me get into my review, but first, let's start with few that I actually liked* Positives- The artstyle is very pretty. Though, something is just off with the character art. Still, the art is really charming and colourful. The colour pallete is fairly mild, yet the game is still not afraid of using colour when needed. All of this results in a very pleasant to look at game.However, I have to say, isometric perspective REALLY doesn't work for this game. Usually isometric games are fairly simplistic, but everything in this game is detailed enough to be noisy to the eyes. This game should've have been a full 3D or something like Animal Crossing where the camera is much closer but still fixed. Because as it is, this game makes me feel kind of ill when I move fastThe enviromental design is also fantastic. You can see that a lot of love and care went into designing enviroment. The houses got the most love. Interiors really sparkle with personality and it has been a joy exploring everyone's homes. Frankly, every human made place in this game is a joy of a designer. Procreative areas outside don't fall in quality eitherBut also don't forget natural enviroments. Going outside immediately paints a picture of a tropical island, with monkeys everywhere, bright lush greenery and exotic plants. Fantastic work on worldbuilding in general- Music is pleasant and fits the tropical feeling of the game, though not much to say about it apart from that- Sound design is pleasant and not annoying to the ears, but I'm no sound engineer, so nothing else I can say about that.- The game also has plenty of small QOL features that many farming games lack. For example: you can see your entire farm at once with the press of a button, you can see how much each item sells for, you can see exact whereabouts of villagers on the map, and etc.- You actually have rivals in this game. It's really weird that in many other farming games you are the only provider in the entire city, so this was very refreshing to see.* Negatives- This game is WAY too big. It will take you two full ingame days to explore everything on the map (and I mean all buildings and introduce yourself to all the NPCs. I'm not talking about any content beyond that). This game also has over 72 NPCs (rough estimate, because I did not count animals and I don't know which of those have social links) and 28 of them are romanceable. Holy hell, this seems a bit excessive.I'm sure that when you are into 100 hours and an ingame year into the game, this additional content is nice because you always have something to do, but at the start this much is just insane. All this content being dumped on you is really confusing and makes it hard to care to do anything at all.I remember some people complaining about Stardew Valley, and how the game is too stressfull because of so much to do and how the time is always ticking, so I really want to see those people's reaction to this game.You can't even run in this game and the default walking speed is SLOW as hell. You do have a dash, which you will spam a lot, until you get a fast travel (which I heard is in the game),  but it looks really silly so not idealThat's one of the side effects of a big world. It takes forever to travel through it, so you'll have less time to engage with most of game's content. It's also a massive pain in the ass to try to find a specific place on the map because of just how much there is on it. I'm sure you get used to it after a while, but early in the game it's rather painful.- Another massive issue is that you are not given any reason to care about anything happening in the game at all.The game starts with a character creation, and the only thing after that is literally words on the screen "You leave Pokyo to start a life on new island", after which you see yourself traveling on a ship to the island. Then you speak to a mayor who simply welcomes you and implies that you've been to that island before, and then him and a carpenter show you your new house. Done. That's the entire intro. After that the game starts.Did you know that one of the main story elements is the fact that there was an oil spill in the water near the island? Wanna know how you learn this information? From a random NPCs. No, not a specific NPCs, oh no. Some villagers will mention an oil spill if you talk to them. That's right, the MAIN conflict of the game is first time mentioned in a random throwaway dialogue. You can also learn it when you meet the main villain on the 4-5 day, but you'll likely to learn it from a random NPC first.I'm not asking them to shove me all the information in my face, but it would be nice if the essential story elements were actually explainedYou are given no reason to care. Why should I care about this place and all those people?In comparison to Stardew Valley, you are presented with the fact that your character is sick of city life and wants to live a simpler life in a friendly community. I'm sure everyone who lives in a city has that thought at least once. It's a simple premise, but it establishes underlying reason to want to be in that world. They even have the same subplot as stardew valley. There is a vllian who wants to destroy nature for profit, except in stardew valey there was atleast some nuance, there was atleast some reason to care for that character (he was quite charming. ngl). Here they just made her outright evil (They also called her Karen, ffs)Speaking of people, villagers in this game seem incredibly shallow (at least at first). They will give you two dialogue lines when you first meet them per day and nothing else. Which is fine itself, I guess, but the problem is that they don't give you anything to work with. How am I supposed to see who I want to pursue a relationship with, if the characters give me the most bland and generic lines (some of them do seem to react to weather dynamically, so I hope that's an actual feature and not just a one time thing, because that's neat).For example, when you first meet Alice, the blonde female character, or whatever her name was, she tells you that she recognises you. Except, there's nothing you can do to ask her how she knows you. She just tells you that, and dialogue ends. I don't know her, so why am I not allowed to question who the hell is that woman is and why she knows me?- Another issue is that the game feels too rough on the gameplay side. You only have movement animations in 8 directions so every time you want to go diagonally it makes a really awkward snapping movement. The game is also tiled, as in, it's divided by blocks, like most farming sims, however because of the way movement works, it's awkward to line up the tiles which makes for a really awkward farming and combat- Speaking of combat and mining. Somehow the combat is even worse than in Stardew. I know, I was shocked myself.

_childDocuments_.review: It's probably a fine game but there are some small irritations that pushed me away from the game. > I can understand why there's a confirmation window when you apply changes in the settings, but I guess I'm just used to these small things like applying changes immediately, so idk if that's a negative point> Probably another half-negative comment is related to the character-creating tab, there are just small amount of triggers and tumblers you can adjust. Probably it's just the art-style of the game itself, so idk. I personally didn't like poor variety of things the game offers in order to create a character> Not to be a perfectionist especially when the game is not released fully (or is?) but some animations are just bad like during conversations (they are exaggerated imo). Also the conversation windows as well could've contain more lines in-one-go so that characters talking wouldn't take so long to end, you'll get tired of talking to NPCs 'cause it takes so much time. Maybe it's just me being impatient> Now's the biggest reason I feel like affected me more to abandon playing this game after only 7 hours: the buttons are just random. For example, while having a conversation with NPC to proceed to next line of dialogue - you click mouse2 (right click) which is kind of odd imo, but it's fine you can get used to it. However, when you approach some surroundings stuff (a fountain for example) it shows you the text and to continue playing (after you've relieved your curiousity) you have to use mouse1 (left click) for some reason. I don't understand this decision: you ought to be awared of this every time you try to inspect anything. And finally what's ridiculous: you know when the game gives you pop-ups with guidelines or something, like 'to plant a tree - just come to a place where the square becomes green and click on it' - well, in order to continue and close this pop-up you must use the button R. Now explain that to me, it's just something I can't process in my mind.> Inventory and chests interaction also leaves me questions. In order to automatically put the whole stack of a material (wood, for example) you click on it in your inventory with M1 whereas M2 sends it one by one. Again, you can get used to it, nothing difficult, but when you want the same operation reversed (material from chest to inventory) - you click M1 on it and... it sticks to your cursor and you have to manually put it in the inventory. Now that's just stupid. Overall I feel like the game itself might become good product like another farm-like games with plot and stuff, but in a current state of TECHNICAL issues that I've faced - I don't feel like playing it. It's just uncomfortable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: A Relaxing Paradise of Fun and Discovery!As an avid fan of simulation games, Coral Island has completely captivated my gaming experience with its charm and depth. From the moment I set foot on its pristine shores, I was immersed in a world of endless possibilities and serene beauty.One of the standout features of Coral Island is its stunning visuals. The vibrant colors of the coral reefs, the lush greenery of the tropical forests, and the crystal-clear waters of the ocean create a breathtaking backdrop for exploration. Every detail is meticulously crafted, making each location a joy to discover.Game play wise, Coral Island offers a perfect blend of farming, fishing, and social interactions. Whether I'm tending to my crops, casting my line into the sea to catch exotic fish, or chatting with friendly villagers, every activity feels meaningful and rewarding. The progression system is well-balanced, allowing me to grow my farm and expand my influence on the island at my own pace.What truly sets Coral Island apart is its dedication to environmental conservation and sustainability. As I work towards restoring the island's ecosystem and supporting local wildlife, I feel a sense of accomplishment knowing that my actions have a positive impact on the virtual world around me.Furthermore, the characters in Coral Island are diverse and memorable, each with their own unique personalities and stories to uncover. Building relationships with them through meaningful interactions and fulfilling quests adds another layer of depth to the game, making the island feel alive with possibilities.Overall, Coral Island is a gem of a game that combines relaxing game play with meaningful simulation elements. Whether you're a fan of farming sims or simply looking for a virtual paradise to escape to, Coral Island is sure to delight with its beautiful world, engaging activities, and heartfelt message of conservation. I wholeheartedly recommend it to anyone looking for a positive and enriching gaming experience!

_childDocuments_.review: I really didn't want to give this game a negative. I forced myself to play on, waited patiently for updates (took >8 months btw) but since I tell my friends not to buy it (yet) irl, I guess that counts as a non-recommendation. CI is a huge waste of potential and could've been the next stardew. The art and world setting is incredibly beautiful, and as someone from SEA I really enjoy seeing the mesh of indo culture in the game, but the praise ends here. The biggest problem with this game is BUGS. Bugs, bugs, a crash here and there, more bugs. Was their programmer hired from wish or did they come from an entomology degree? Who knows?I bought this game before the 1.0 release back in Nov 2023 but seeing as that they'll wipe your files I decided to wait for 1.0. To my surprise the mermaid content (which is literally in the screenshots on the store page btw?) was totally non-existent in the "full" release. Ppl defended the devs saying it was never part of 1.0 and was "always" part of a later update/roadmap. That's where all the "incomplete" reviews came from. But well never mind I am only interested in mermaid stuff, so I waited. 8 months passed and I'm way past refund deadline. 1.1 is finally here in July 2024. Super excited; dove right in.Gameplay wise it's your typical farming sim. Crops to sell, cows to feed, villagers to romance. A lot of things follow SV's format to the T. The harvest fest where you have to bring a crop to put into the huge crock pot, the inane mining format that unfortunately got popular thanks to SV where you have to mine rocks until you find a rope(stairs in sv) down, and every 5 levels you get an elevator. But there's a lot of unique SE-asian mini games in other seasons for you to enjoy. Oh, they give you sprinklers early, which I love, but no one tells you using sprinklers do NOT give you farming points apparently, so you'd be in year 3 with your farming level still at 5/10, but I digress.The characters are ok. The writing is pretty mid ngl and half the time I have to fight the intense urge not to hit the Skip button. I am the type of person who usually romances (if possible) or max out all relationships with every character just to read their story, regardless of gender and this is the first farming game I legit wasn't sure if I could put myself through this. Quantity > Quality is a great way to describe the writing. Here are some early heart events: You help carry a sofa because someone is moving. You watch 3 people get into an argument that has nothing to do with you. Dude broke the library pc. Dude has daddy problems. Another dude has rich daddy problems. A girl complains. Some of these are completely unnecessary to split into 2 heart then 3 heart events and could've just been squeezed into a 5 heart, then 8 heart event because the early heart ones are a serious waste of time. I got to get up for work irl tmr and I really don't care that your shoe has a hole in it bro. Btw, there's NO divorce in this game so be careful who you give that heart knot to.Anyway, you can put crops into machines (mayo maker, aging barrel, bee hives for honey, etc), but the machines break EVERY OTHER DAY. They literally just stop working. The crafting bar is full but you cannot pick up your produce or remove it. If you look this up in the discussions there's hundreds of threads dating back 1+ years about this. It gets worse the longer you play it so it's definitely some kind of memory leak but everyone refuses to acknowledge the possibility their game was programmed by a blind man and his puppy stepping on his keyboard. If you ask/beg/pray for a fix, CI's keyboard warriors will run to reply, "Just restart your game." or my personal fav "The devs can't reproduce the bug." As if that's an answer...? So if you're going to buy this game, be prepared to restart it after every other day. If you're totally ok with the devs not respecting your time, you'll enjoy this game. Here's more: The chest you put in your barn to store the milk pail/sheers & hay has disappeared completely. You post asking for help. The reply you will get (from the same few people) is, "Well you shouldn't have put a chest in the barn." Then why tf did the game allow me to and why did the chest work for 3 days?? Oh and if you put fences touching the barn your fences will also disappear. The answer to that was, "Leave a space." lol.Another one: "Bug: Quests or altar (bundles in SV) don't accept different/mixed quality of the item." The reply: "Well don't donate mixed qualities." While you might think hey this isn't a bug it's a feature, why are you complaining about this? Picture this: You are now in year 2 and most of your items are gold~osmium quality. You finally get the other 4 pieces out of 5 to donate, but it won't go in because previously you put in ONE bronze quality in yr 1 so now you are STUCK with all bronzes. How in the world are you going to find bronze quality now? But apparently this is OK and a "feature" and we should all just stop bullying the devs.....You get the idea of the kind of stellar replies from the community. But what about the devs? Well they reply maybe once every 2-3 weeks, if at all, and they'll copypasta reply "Send us your save file and a video of the bug and what you were doing before it happened." as if everyone just sits around recording their 200 hour intense crop watering sessions. If you don't, well, oopsie, we can't reproduce the bug. The game was working perfectly fine BEFORE a patch but is suddenly stuttering and lagging after it? Well the answer was, "Lower your graphics quality" or "What card are you on? You need a good GPU to play this game." (as if it wasn't working fine before the update..) "4080" No more replies. Tree planting event was working fine before a hotfix (which they had to upload 2 more hotfixes to fix their hotfix, and they broke automatic chests along the way, just sayin') but now you will faint and lose all your tools. "We are aware. Just get your tools back from the blacksmith." Ok great, what about my sword? "Just buy one." This is one of the first few events in Spring btw, and the bug affects mostly new files/new players, who have NO MONEY. The problem is all these people replying and shielding the devs have like 400 hours in the game and are way past all of these issues when they affect you the most. If you have high stamina and 5 mil gold then yeah, you won't faint and lose all your tools so this isn't a problem at all. These are the same people who are active on discord too so the devs basically live in an echo chamber.I personally experienced 2 crashes in Spring year 1 alone, then later had some weird bug where I could NOT interact with anything, so I literally couldn't sleep in my bed and I fainted. I restarted the game/day and it went fine so I just continued, but a in-game week later the same thing happened at a different location/time. Reported it, and got the "Send us a video" from the dev and a "What other apps did you have running while you're playing the game?"Everything wrong with the game is some how your fault. You shouldn't have done the thing. You shouldn't have listened to youtube while you play. You shouldn't put chests in the barn. Express your unhappiness in the discussions? Get clown badges and whiteknight replies about how the devs are poor widdle babies, never to be blamed. (And yes pls do give me more on this review to prove my point.) "Hey my bug from the last patch wasn't fixed." "I bet you didn't reply to the devs." ..I literally got a reply like this. LOL bruh.I tried my best to like this game. I really did. It would've been so good. The thought about how they royally blew their 1mil dollar kickstarter (convert this to Rupiah & you'd have AAA game level of funding btw...) and this is what they came up with is just painful. Maybe hire more staff including one who can actually program, 6 testers, and a CS. See you in 4 years. Hopefully that's enough time to fix this mess.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game back in early Access and I kind of regret it. There was so much promise but theres a few things that fall flat and the biggest issue: they brought it out of Early access too early, the game isn't finished and in its current state has game breaking bugs. Personally I just spent 7 hours playing this weekend just for me to try and load into today to a crashed save file. Even the backup crashes... The cutscenes are painful to watch and Ive never in my experience of playing farm sims skipped so many scenes out of boredom. _childDocuments_.review: Its the little things that keep me playing.While there is very little content, as of when I'm writing this review, I must say there is more work placed into this game than I had initially anticipated for an early access. Let me start by saying that this game is by no means complete, its very bare bones. HOWEVER, it's when I find myself very put off from lack of content that I see the most amazing work that was put in. Example 1: RainI was sitting for a good few minutes while it was raining in game completely mesmerised by the texturing of the rain movement against hard surfaces, be it leaves on a palm tree or the damn roof! The attention to detail to rain surface physics were mind blowing with how life-like it looked when it hit anything solid.Example 2: Placed FlooringNo, seriously, I mean it. The flooring you can place in your farm house. I'm not talkign about how nice it looks aesthetically. (TBH I couldn't care less half the time) That being said, ANGLED IMAGING! Literally the visualisation of these tiles is from an angle and will change based on how deep into your house you walk, allowing for a truly beautiful three-dimensional effect that I absolutely adore.Example 3: Character PersonalitiesI play ALOT of farming sims, to the point where its harder to name what I haven't played. Many of the characters within those can feel very washed up, phoned in, fake, or generally generic. I'm unbelievably shocked and ecstatic about how diverse the personalities of the islanders are. The first villager I actually spoke to was Leah and immediately put off by her attitude, then came Bree who I couldn't really tell if she was being nice or just channelling some sassy southern charm. Yet meeting Yuri and Zarah I was floored by HOW different everyone was and how it spanned all the villagers. All in all this game feels like the perfect marriage of Stardew Valley and Story of Seasons (Real Harvest Moon) and a smidge of AC. You can completely see all the love, support and effort that when into it while playing even with limited content. I definitely look forward to more updates and its official release! Thank you guys for all the hard work and keep going!!Also the signs switch from open to close, like i said, Its the little things.

I started two farms in Early Access, and thus had to start for the third time in 1.0, but I think I'm going to finally go through the story in this play through. It's a fun farming sim, calling back to the mechanics that made Harvest Moon so great. There is so much to do and many customization options that make the game even more relaxing, something I've come to really appreciate. It strikes a balance between frantically managing all my resources (which I low-key enjoy) and a genuine cozy and laid-back experience (which I really enjoy). Is it a revolutionary farming sim? Probably not. But that's not what I wanted out of Coral Island--I enjoy it for its solid gaming loop of farming and interacting with the town, standout beautiful tropical setting, and diverse marriageable candidates.
