_childDocuments_.review: I recently stumbled across Coral Island, and having grown up on Harvest Moons, and having played Stardew Valley on basically every platform available to man, I really wanted to try something else. The art style seemed really nice, and I got it on a discount.After having finished the first year (which took about 50-ish hours), and having made a decent chunk of progress in the main plots of the game, I can confidently recommend this game to virtually every aficionado of the genre. - The art style. The game looks  good. Every NPC has a hand drawn sprite which changes throughout the seasons, all of them even have beach sprites and of course, multiple expressions. The actual 3D game looks good as well, everything pops really well and the town really looks good with all the different decorations that are around all year round, especially around the Winter time. Same goes for every item: the sprites are beautiful, especially for all the produce that's available. As a European, I have never seen a good chunk of the vegetables and fruits the game offers, so seeing them so well drawn feels really nice.- The festivals. I feel like the festivals are, simply put, really nice. All of them have one or more minigame to play which adds to the immersion, each of them have a nice, hand drawn, animated title card and it's just really fun to play around the festivals. The winter week-long festival was especially nice because it really reminded me of those Christmas markets you find around towns.- The quantity of content. Most of these farming sim games tend to have the same gameplay loop: wake up, tend to the farm/animals, spend your stamina/time doing something around the map, sell your produce, go to sleep, repeat; and maybe do some quest, chat with someone in the meantime to build your relationships. And that's good: that's the loop you expect playing such a game, and Coral Island isn't substantially different; however it adds a couple of activities you normally don't find in most other farming sims: bug catching and ocean diving, and to an extent, the Museum. Bug catching work very similar to Animal Crossing: you swing a net and get a bug, but here you have to be careful they don't run away. The Museum is identical to Animal Crossing's one: you give new fish, bugs, gems, artifacts, and critters to the Museum and get some stuff back. This simply adds a nice chunk of playtime and activities to the game in order to finish up the museum, although this may feel grindy at times. And finally:- Ocean diving. This is Coral Island's biggest and most unique mechanic. It works similarly to a traditional "mine" in this game: you break tons of trash in the ocean, find a special item (similarly to how you find stairs in the mines) to eventually go deeper, and you can even find special forageables, critters, and a ton of treasure chest while down there. You also find kelp, which are essential to enhancing your net and fishing rod, bust most importantly: everything on your farm. This is essential to getting better produce and should be prioritized over most other activities, at least in my opinion. You also use kelp to craft a ton of items, many of which are fundamental such as sprinklers, or you refine trash into scraps which are used in the creation of most machines and then some. It's also essential to one of the game's biggest plot lines, and helps with raising the town rating. The sound and the visual design is really good, and it's really pleasing seeing all the coral heal up as you work. Diving looks good and feels relaxing, whereas the mines feel a little more invested due to the mobs.- The bugs. The game has a bunch of relatively small and yet mildly annoying bugs. My character's sidecut seldom disappears into a bald spot and I have to change my clothes. Sometimes the tile indicator simply disappears, and it's infuriating, especially in the mines. There was a bug recently that caused tools to degrade permanently but it got quickly fixed. Sometimes there are graver bugs, but so far nothing truly disruptive to my experience but a mild eyeroll. Anyways: they are there and it would feel disingenuous to not mention it.- The music. This is more of a pet peeve than anything else, but I feel like the music is... whatever. Not the music score itself, but rather how it just doesn't play a lot of the time. The game feels silent a lot of the time, and it very, very jarringly starts and stops music when you change zones in the island. I just wish it was betterly executed, but again, worth a mention.- Some minigames. Ok, some minigames are... poorly made. The ring toss in the Spooky Festival is kind of impossible to understand and I had to look up how it worked because the controls were really not helping. This also expands to most other other minigames: some can be practiced, other can't, none of them have a tutorial to them which would greatly help, even a one page scheme would greatly help this instead of just inferring what you're supposed to do. - The Spooky Festival is clearly unfinished. This isn't something "bad", but it was a little jarring: every character mentions they have some cool costume on during the festival when it's just not true. It takes a little out of the immersion, and while they mentioned 1.2 will be the "Spooky Season Update", so far it's a functional festival but the iconic Halloween thing, costumes, is so far missing. Which kind of sucks, especially when you get a lot of goofy costumes for yourself.- I really like the vast asian inspirations and influence in the game, from character design to ambience design, everything oozes this and it's lovely, especially since most of these farming sims tend to have vaguely similar ambience.- I also really like the variety in body types in NPCs and bachelors/bachelorettes. From Mark to Wakuu, from Pablo to Rafael, then from Aaliah to Eva, from Chaem to Lily, the game has one for all tastes. The recent 1.1 update even added two merpeople to the marriage pool. I also like the hangouts you can do, they're nice and short but help add something onto the very old, very established formula of run-up-to-Person-gift-favourite-item-leave to grind hearts these games tend to have. That's it then! This was a little longer than I expected, but I really enjoy the game, and I really want other people to try it out and support these talented and passionate devs. Bye!

_childDocuments_.review: With early access since October 11, 2022, Coral Island, the newest farm simulator game, was officially released on November 14, 2023.Highlights:1. Narrative and Freedom:Coral Island offers a compelling narrative for farm simulation enthusiasts, reminiscent of the beloved Stardew Valley. The game provides a relaxing and enjoyable experience as players embark on a new farming adventure on the paradise island of Coral Island. The freedom to pursue personal objectives without the pressure of meeting predefined goals enhances the immersive gameplay.2. Rich Character Interactions:The game impresses with its well-developed characters, each possessing unique traits, preferences, and even favorite items. The attention to detail in character design and the inclusion of NPCs with distinct personalities contribute to a vibrant and lifelike in-game world. The ability to build relationships through gift-giving adds depth to the gaming experience.3. Aesthetically Pleasing Design:Coral Island stands out for its well-crafted design, blending 2D and 3D elements seamlessly. The soft and delicate designs, coupled with beautiful, colorful, and unsaturated visuals, create a visually appealing and cozy atmosphere. The game's soundtrack and ambient sounds enhance the overall immersive experience.4. Diverse Gameplay Elements:The game offers a variety of gameplay elements, including character customization, exploration, missions, and farm management. The inclusion of a journal tracking achievements and statistics, along with a reward system tied to skill improvement, adds depth and engagement to the overall farming simulator experience.Bugs:1. Technical Issues:Despite its visual appeal, Coral Island suffers from notable technical issues, particularly in terms of system requirements and gameplay performance. The game's recommended specifications may not be sufficient, leading to freezes, crashes, and a less-than-fluid experience during transitions.2. Progress Loss and Transition Delays:Players may encounter frustrating setbacks, such as progress loss due to unexpected game closures. Additionally, the game's transitions between locations, despite being part of an open-world concept, suffer from delays, affecting the overall fluidity of the gaming experience.3. Lack of Language Support:While Coral Island supports multiple languages, the absence of an interface and subtitles in Portuguese may be a drawback for Portuguese-speaking players. Expanding language support could enhance accessibility and cater to a broader audience.In conclusion, Coral Island impresses with its engaging narrative, rich character interactions, and aesthetically pleasing design. However, the game falls short in addressing technical issues and could benefit from additional language support, improving the overall player experience. However, everything mentioned here may change.

_childDocuments_.review: I have 4 hours now in the game, and from what I can see, I like it. Full disclosure, I kickstarted it on the art and premise, but have largely stayed away until the 1.0 release.I recommend the game with some caveats. First, it's not done, which is unfortunate given the 1.0 release on paper. There are some things which are still being worked on, (and some of those just came out in the recent patch). Things like Marriage, the Merfolk, side bits of story and quests. The game doesn't feel unfinished, but there are components that will def add value that are known and being developed still. Second, it is not perfectly optimized. The game hitches here and there, there are minor rendering slowdowns and slightly laggy bits. You can play through these, but it is a minor nuisance.The good: This is truly a modern farm sim in a lot of ways. A huge cast of interesting characters, a very progressive, ecological storyline, a big world to explore, it seems like a lot of items, complexity, and crafting at hand. Everything is gorgeous. The music is a delight, the slow unfurl of the story that engages you in this very immediate islander take on climate change is especially welcome. I want to know more about all these characters, and what representation at hand. Truly a gift from the developers to so intricately weave together what feels like a very alive community.The animations of SO MANY little things are spectacular. People's houses feel lived in, they feel personal, and unique. Everyone has a kind of voice in the world, and it shows.If you liked Stardew for how it massively advanced the genre, I firmly believe Coral Island will be the next major step forward. It's just on the way there, not quite at it yet.

While it's not a complete game, it has come a long way this year and I look forward to seeing it continue! Recommend if you are looking for a calm laid back sim that isn't like the others out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not done, I had a wonderful time playing this game, and thought that the time I was spending completing things would be rewarded as promised, but instead was met with a WIP at questlines, characters advertised as "Romanceable" having absolutely no dialogue, along with a not insignificant portion of characters. Quite a few significant bugs, and lacking a lot of what makes these games rewarding.In many ways, this game felt like a improved Stardew Valley, but they advertised a 1.0 launch for an unfinished game. I plan on playing more of this game in a year or two when the game is actually done, but in the meantime, please don't support creators increasing the price and dropping a "1.0 Launch" far before the game is actually done.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: After being an avid Stardew Valley lover for years, and having played the Animal Crossing games for many hours, I was looking for a fresh new game to satiate my need for games like these. Well, this one hits all the boxes. It has magical creatures, love interests, town events, and of course farming and collecting. If you're looking for something to scratch the farming sim itch but with a little extra magic, this is the game for you! Also, the devs are doing an absolutely amazing job at putting out new content for a new game like this, so props to the team!
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: The next stardew valley and harvest moon.  Many automation options as you progress and lots of interesting romantic options.  But honestly it's not fleshed out enough.  The romance feels flat, barely any scenes and the end game is incomplete.  I'd still recommend it but I'd like to see it as game that feels finished.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: Although only clocking two hours at the time of this review, I do want to say this has been an enjoyable journey so far. There's a lot of things the game does right and a few things it does poorly. For a game that is in Early Access I want to say it runs really well and looks very polished (both graphically and it's UI). The game is much like Stardew Valley, so if you've played this you will more or less feel at home with how this game works. My only few gripes is that I couldn't find a way to remap keys for the game, pressing I / J to open inventory or M for Map is so frustrating, I think keys should be swapped to TAB for ease of access. Another gripe I have is the story is quite bland and not as "interesting". Another thing the game could improve on are animations and interactivity. Other than this the games solid and I look forward to the updates in the games Roadmap.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: Coral Island is FUN! I originally saw complaints about it being too much like Stardew Valley, and to be fair, when the game first starts it really does feel unoriginal. However, the longer I played the more unique it seemed and I got totally swept in! The one thing I must ask though is: how can you release a game that's not finished? I literally can't place furniture in my expanded house or watch the 10 heart cutscene with one of the bachelors because of bugs.I'm hoping they fix this soon, as I don't see why I should keep playing until major content like that works... Once they do, though, I'll be all for picking it up again!
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: This has been a great game so far. I've felt like it is balanced to play. I have enjoyed the journey from early-game to end-game, and can't wait to see what other surprises are in-store for me! Character customization is great. I would love more options for clothing and furniture, and interactions with furniture, but there's quite an extensive catalogue of clothing and furniture already!Ways of automating are easy to understand, and feel good once you get there, never too easy!NPCs, even the non-dateables, feel like real people, and it's easy to get swept up in their stories and really care about them.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very great game with lots to do! I've go around 300hrs clocked and haven't completed the game or have anything to show for it because the game keeps crashing and wont load my save. I bought a steam deck and i still cant play it. i have to make a new game every time it crashes because the old save wont open without crashing and now the game wont even launch.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: Kind of hard to review a game that isn't even finished yet. Buuuut... there's a lot here so far, and what they have is excellent. Love how diverse the cast is, and all the little details. The events are so fun! There's actual mini games! And the romanceable cast is pretty great, too. Really looking forward to them adding marriage and other features because right now those are missing and I think everyone should know that before picking it up. I have no doubt this is going to be excellent upon full release.Edit now that the game is out of EA:I'm really disappointed. There are many, many things that should have been fixed before release (bugs that have been lingering since the beginning, for one thing)... but the thing that bothers me the most is that the main story is not done. It's "WIP." At the very least upon a game's release, I want the main story to be done! I'm fine waiting for extra features, but this is sad to me. I want the game to succeed because it's so cute and has a lot of personality. When you adopt pets from the adoption center, they become lifeless dolls in your house and just sit in the beds. They had more personality at the adoption center. You can't befriend or romance the merfolk, still. There are quests that say "TBD." It doesn't feel like anything has changed between EA and release, sadly.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: It's definitely the alpha version of the game, and there are a few rough patches here and there (which isnt surprising! its early on in its release), but the game is incredibly charming and the characters are so awesome! the dialogue and unique animations really make them feel alive. im already hooked!!
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: Great game that's not finished.  Many core systems are not complete (dating, children, town S teir, main quest abruptly ends with "WIP" in text boxes, heart events, underwater / mermaid area).  Along with that there are many things that don't work.  Automation is busted, machines frequently just stop working and no longer produce, heart events don't trigger, underwater caves spawn in over world and soft lock your day.Even with those complaints aside, i had a blast with my time with this game and will defiantly come back once the devs have the chance to finish the game.  Id highly recommend putting this game on your wish-list / follow and wait until everything is fixed.  The developers recently released a 2024 roadmap that appears to aim to fix all of my complaints.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best Harvest Moon/Stardew Valley-like farming life sims I have ever played. The pacing is perfect. As you do and collect things throughout the game, you gradually unlock new plants, animals, and features. And as things unlock, efficiency improves so that more things can be done in a day. It is that constant slow drip of satisfaction.And the characters that populate the world are some of the best. The character portraits are pretty and emotive, and the dialogue is vast enough that it never felt repetitive. Plus, they actually change clothes with the season!The only real flaw is the several obvious placeholders that exist for features that were either cut or are planned for the future (e.g. relationships with some magical NPCs, library book donations, an entire hidden jungle section, etc.). I'm sure they will be filled out in the future, but as of now they just feel weird.As of the current version, I have experienced no game-breaking bugs. I see the occasional spelling error or weird graphical glitch, but it otherwise runs perfectly fine.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: It's like the marriage of Harvest Moon and Stardew Valley and they have a 3D beautiful child with a unique personality.If you're familiar with Harvest Moon and Stardew Valley, then you'll find Coral Island's gameplay very familiar. What makes this game unique from the latter is Coral Island is designed in 3D with beautiful graphics. If you've played a dating sim before, the people in Coral Island look like a dating sim, which is attractive. Coral Island also has a strong conservation agenda for the ocean, which is brilliant. Coral Island also has a variety of races and cultures, especially the culture of Indonesia. Overall, Coral Island is the best farming simulation game that exists today.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, this is a fantastic farming sim and probably one of my favourites of all time. The characters are incredible, the storyline gives you plenty of things to do, the museum alone is a work of art, the chickens have exactly 0 braincells and I can adopt a lizard as a pet. The only thing that gives me trouble is the fishing minigame, I wish there were an option to turn it off since it involves a lot of holding and releasing which can get to your wrists.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: Not recommended as of right now. Wait until the bugs are fixed.Repeating cutscenes, audio playing when it shouldn't be, sound effects not working, late game machines not working correctly, persisting speech bubbles, enemies and loot falling through floors. I backed this on KS over 3 years ago, and it's been out for almost 2 (albeit in early access for some of that) - this is now classed as fully released game, and I really would expect better than this. I would recommend fixing the bugs in the existing content before adding more filler content.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: Very good farming sim, not unlike Stardew Valley, but with tropical flair, more characters, more options to play and lots of fun! Still in development, but what is there so far is absolutely amazing, the festivals are detailed, varied and feel new and exciting. Graphics are great. Really love the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: I do truly love this game, I've had it sitting in my library and didn't play at all until the 1.0 release. I can't compare this game to Stardew Valley because Coral island is it's own game. The colours, the soundtracks, a lot of different bachelors(bachelorettes) as well as the dev team still promising future content and updates while being fully transparent. This game started off on the right foot and I can't wait to keep playing more.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a good work. However, at present, the localization of Chinese is very poor. Looking forward to the follow-up update. By the way, there are too few choices of hair and clothes for people to pinch. All hair is short hair, no long hair. I hope to add mini-map and identify the task guide map logo in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: Can't say I can fully recommend this game 100% yet, perhaps 75% but it's got amazing potential (and the only reason I gave it a thumbs up). A lot of what we currently have is lovely and ambitious. However the game sorely needs to be updated and given lot's of love as soon as possible. Many glitches and unfinished parts of the game reared itself 20 hours into my play through. Which absolutely was noticeable immediately with the combat against the monsters in the mine. I'm hoping the team can really manage to gives us as many updates and quality of life changes as needed in the same way that the team for My time at Sandrock does with it's game. While I do love big maps, this one is big and yet feels empty. Sadly a large map does not equal lived in even when the characters are doing their own thing, which btw confused me because events would go off when I was on complete opposite sides of the map to where the character with high friendship was... Another downside of the large map is even when I have the ability to change the speed of how fast the day goes or how fast my character is able to dash, it feels like there's too little time to do all the things we're told we can do. Not to mention not enough substance at the moment to keep the days from feeling less...lacking.I do wish this team the best, because we all need to remember that Stardew is amazing but it took awhile to get to where it needed to be and still receives many updates to this day. I believe this game will become greater than it is now but it will depend wholly on the team.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: Coral Island is an amazing game, especially if you love farming games like Stardew Valley. The switch to 3D graphics is a game-changer. Rverything looks so colorful and beautiful.The farming part is even better. You can grow crops, take care of animals, and the whole process feels more realistic. The 3D style makes it all more fun and interesting. The characters in the game are cool and you feel a connection with them. The music in the game is nice and fits well with the feel of the game as well.If you like farming games, you should definitely try this.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: So, I wanted to play Stardew Valley today, but thought I would look for an alternative. Boy, I am glad I did. This is excellent. Yes it is basically a 3D Stardew Valley, but I struggle to see what is wrong with that!Very relaxing, lovely art style, good audio. I do wonder if the Dev consulted ConcernedApe because it is 100% a rip off of Stardew.I have encountered one or two placeholders where the full dev work isn't complete yet, but the mechanics of the whole game work very well. Absolutely recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing game. I really enjoy the interactions with all the NPCs! If you like farming sims, cultures, and a bit of fantasy, you'll love this game! I'm so excited for the mermaid updates to be released so we can interact with them more! Overall I highly recommend the game and would encourage anyone to try it. Especially if they are a fan of Stardew + want to support this company! (also screw Bobby LOL iykyk)
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: I've been having a great time playing this game, but I've decided to shelve it for now and check it out again next year to see how it's coming along. Despite being labeled version 1.0, it still feels like it's in early access. So, as much as I want to, I can't really recommend Coral Island in its current state. I noticed that it tends to stutter quite a bit, which can be frustrating. The dialogue is good, but it can get a bit repetitive after a while. The biggest bummer was that the romantic conversations with NPCs don't feel much different from regular ones. I wish they'd acknowledge the player more or flirt a bit. Some of the animations, like waving and horse riding, for example, look a little stiff and could use some polish. The festivals are fun for the most part, but some of the mini-games, like the pet race and pumpkin smashing, could be better. There's also a handful of bugs that I've come across that others have also mentioned. Overall, it's a fun and relaxing game. I put in a generous amount of time and can honestly keep going, but I'd feel like I'd be doing the game a disservice by not playing it when it's fully fleshed out. Sadly, it just isn't there right now. I'm hoping that Stairway continues to take note of community feedback and work on making the game even better.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: Delving into the realm of yet another farming simulation might prompt the question of whether Coral Island distinguishes itself or merely assimilates into the crowded genre. Sure, in Coral Island you can build the farm of your dreams but there is so much more than that in this game.Of course you do have all of the pieces youd expect in a game like this. Foraging, growing crops, having farm animals, fishing, bug catching, as well as mining. As you get past all the normal farming mechanics in the game you will quickly learn that there is so much more to this game than a lot of the other farming sims that have graced us in the last few months including a story with giants and goddesses as well as a diving mechanic where you clean up the ocean. The dating mechanic and NPCs are really fleshed out as well which is great.Listen cozy gamers, I hear you when you say that you are so sick of every single farming sim being compared to stardew valley but genuinely, this is the absolute closest thing to a 3D stardew valley that you are going to find.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: I have been waiting for it since kickstarter and it did not disappoint at all. They have given what they promised and more. I would recommend it to people who likes playing Stardew Valley and Animal Crossing.Besides the typical farming/ranching, they have diving, cleaning up the ocean, they have fish and bug catching, they have fossil collecting, and more (I have yet to unlock many things including marriage,  and ); but what I really love about the game though is the small details they've added. I love how every day before a holiday, everyone talks about it. Their dialogues change according to recent events that happened or will happen, even talk about the current weather. Their dialogues are not always repetitive. I also love how everyone wear different clothing every season. They have so many events/cutscenes and heart events and I feel so engaged with all of it. My favorite added feature would be the hangout events you can invite them to, where you get to choose where you'll go and what you'll do both. I especially love how there's a lot of everything: romanceable candidates, crops, trees, land and sea animals, products, furniture, clothing, holidays, adoptable pets, etc., it feels overwhelming so it's better not to rush everything. The only issue I have with this game are some bugs, but I appreciate that the developers are always on it and has not affected a lot of my game time.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: As much time as I've put into this game, I cannot suggest purchasing and supporting it. First of all, as many others have said, it's nowhere near a 1.0 game. It's not done. There are actually points that say Work in Progress. But, to me, the most damning issue is that so much of this game was straight copy/pasted from Stardew Valley that it's a bit sickening. It's one thing to create a game similar or based on something else, but we are talking straight copying of mechanics and systems. There are additions in various areas and some changes, but on the whole it's as if someone made an art mod for Stardew Valley and is selling it as a different game.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: What I love most is the dedication to providing a good user experience.  They roadmap updates effectively which gives them time to smooth out any bugs that get user side and get new features/updates out, so despite being so fresh it runs really well and I rarely encounter any issues.I actually have to say I have no cons to this game.  The things it doesn't currently have are coming our way, and sure I get antsy and want some of these things sooner, but can't rush quality.The inclusiveness of the characters, the diversity, the beautiful artwork and soundtrack, believable and compelling storylines/interactions, and a community that cares.  Really hard not to love this game and the people who made it happen!
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a shot-for-shot Stardew valley clone, down to the shy blacksmith, shipping bin in front of the house, and museum donations (in fairness, also an Animal Crossing feature.)Though I do appriceate the racial diversity of the cast, I feel like there isn't enough to set this game apart from Stardew.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: It's a lovely chilled farming sim game and I would highly recommend the game but......Currently in the state it's in, its a big DO NOT BUY, today alone I've sank 4 odd hours and a good hour or so progress gone, due to constant crashing and you can't save until the end of the day, so when you get to save the game and the game starts to save but crashes instead, it's beyond annoying.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: Even with the Early Release, this game has enough content to make you feel satisfied. The dialogue has not repeated itself (from what I've noticed) and all the NPC are lovely and fleshed out in a satisfying way. Of course, there isn't a lot of character or story development since it is, after all an Early Release but everything that I've seen so far makes me so excited for the full release of the game.Also: YOU CAN HOP FENCES ON YOUR FARM how useful is that!!
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: For the moment, this is a no.I've got over 300 hours in this game and DO enjoy it, but the performance is getting worse and worse.  I've always had stuttering issues, even though my computer meets or exceeds the recommended specs and YES my drivers are up to date but it was, mostly, functional.Lately, it's become an unplayable mess.In the last two real life weeks I've had:An entire species of fruit tress vanish when the seasons changed instead of starting to blossom as they should for that season.Crashed TWICE in the later game cavern after being there for most of the in-game day.Many items get 'stuck' when my inventory was full and then cannot be retrieved when inventory cleared.  (The ones in the greenhouse I get the next day but have lost pick ups in previously  mentioned cavern.Being repeatedly told my inventory is full when it is not.Getting merit points every day for having completed the tree planting all three previous years.  (Latest hotfix was said to have fixed this, it did not.)Recently, the devs added a guide for heart events, where and when to trigger them.  This is a good thing.  I've had a 'go to X at Y time' not activate for a character for a few in-game weeks now.Every time I fish getting 'lucky angler' which should instantly catch me the fish yet it does not.  (Or it's the double fish, can't remember, either way, it doesn't happen.)The exclamation point pop-up saying a shop has 'new items' when they do not and haven't for awhile.The auto-collector in one of my barns showing it has items, when it does not, and not clearing until I click its auto-sort button.  (Yes, its on the land farm, not the sea farm.)Almost all of my 70+ learned recipes suddenly saying I've never cooked them.And then today, receiving an achievement for cooking all recipes when I don't even HAVE them all.  (And unsure if that will prevent me from getting the rest of the recipes in the future.)I adore this game and, despite smaller hiccups and a few things being unclear (like the underwater barn needing the temperature device even though there's no indication of season changes on the underwater farm, like with the crops, I was having a rather nice time.  Now?  I'm afraid to keep playing for fear I'll encounter a bug that will completely break my game.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game to those who love the story of season sequels...what I love about this game are :- good graphic, e.q: I love the detail that developers added to the crops moving and shaking while we were walking or watering them- good music of course- lots of sexy NPC Characters ..for the story of season kinda game I mean like damn.., NOT GONNA LIE abt that!- the detail of NPC's routine, I found that they were doing yoga, volleyball, fishing, etc- and also I love the rain graphic when the rain hits the wooden board near the beach or hits the roof, so real, the board and the roof look so wet like it's something real...and people... WHAT I LOVE MOST... is that INDONESIAN made the game.. and as an Indonesian as well, I AM SO PROUD FOR THIS GAME. PROUD OF THEIR WORK... All we need is the complete version, hope they will release it soon enough... I CAN'T WAIT
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: This game really is a great addition to the genre, even unfinished. I'm a die-hard Stardew fan and I've found it hard to find any farming/life sims that can give me the same level of satisfaction. I think Coral Island can be that. Visually it's a delight. There's enough new stuff to do that it doesn't feel like a rehash of other farming/life sims. I'm very excited to see the game at full release when the kinks have been ironed out, I think this has all-time great potential.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: When Coral Island was in early access, I played ~ 30 hours, and have since stacked up another ~40 hours after the 1.0 release.  The game really feels like a solid Stardew Valley in a 3D isometric representation; however, has several key things that make it unique.  Ocean exploration is fun, and adds a new dynamic to upgrading bug nets and fishing rods, the mines are diverse (4 tiers x 40 levels each, for 120 total levels), and there seem to be great crops to grow in each season.I'm just approaching the portion of the game where you can start automation -- auto feeders, collectors, petting, and there's some farm / crop automation I'm yet to work with such as auto seeding, moving chests and so forth.Despite all the great happenings with the game (and having a 1.0 release), there's still a bit to be done for the game to be fully complete.  Some items (like bones) are still flagged with TBD as the purpose, and some of the Main Story Quest is still incomplete.  I'm 75+ hours in though, and haven't run out of things to do; so, is it worth it?  Yes.  Would it be better if everything was done and polished?  Well, yes, but it isn't stopping the fun.In all, I'd say Coral Island is a great game, and well worth a play through.  On sale - a definite purchase.  Full price, still worth it, but I'd leave it to your discretion.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: The amount of serotonin this game gives me is immense. Literally had me looking up if tree planting volunteer programs were a thing in my area. Not only is this game an incredible fresh take on the traditional farming sim a la Harvest Moon or Stardew Valley, it inspires optimism and hope around climate activism on a small scale. Yes, a lot of the environmental healing involves . But a lack of realism doesn't change that this game really does feel like a refreshing burst of sunshine in the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: For being in early access still frankly this is spectacular. It's got all the markers of a classic farming sim, shades of what people loved from the OG Harvest Moon titles and, of course, plenty that's reminiscent of the beloved Stardew Valley. What's more original is the diverse setting and cast of npcs and a strong focus on environmentalism. I have stumbled upon some minor bugs and glitches here and there but I've seen far worse in triple A titles tbh.I'm extremely excited to see how much more fleshed out the game will become as it gets closer to being completed.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: Game released as 1.0 when it's clearly still in early access (too many bugs and unfinished parts). There's obviously a lot of love and attention put into the game but the fact that the devs have not addressed the topic at all is incredibly offensive. I would've been fine with it if they gave even the smallest inkling of an apology or explanation for it but it just seems like they turn blind and deaf any time the issue is brought up.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: The only reason I'm not willing to recommend the game is because of how incomplete and buggy it is despite being a fully released game. I wish they kept it in early access, I've been so excited to play this game for months and I was unfortunately very disappointed throughout my gameplay. Yes, I had a lot of fun and I do like the content that it has so far, but it is NOT a finished game; which is my main point. I wanted to explore the romance options of the merfolk only to learn that dialogue is very limited and there is nothing to do in their kingdom but rest. So even though they claim you can romance the princess and so on, I can't see any possibility of doing so as I played it. I'd like to suggest you wait to purchase the game till it's more complete and less buggy. I know it has things in store but the information of the game they give doesn't match the content it has.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Gamebreaking bugs after 100 hours? Maybe one day this game will be finished and working, who knows.With the 1.1 update the game is (finally) complete. Story complete, and with only some minor bugs on my end. Gameplay wise its a little shallow; Mostly copy-pasted from the farm-sim template and combat is beyond dreadful, but its a super charming game with a unique visual identify regardless. And while shallow in places, it does do some unique things as well. Enough to make it its own thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only mostly through year one, but here goes.I try to avoid comparisons to Stardew Valley, especially in the farming sim/RPG genre. Usually those comparisons end up being the basic staples of the genre and they don't allow room for the game to stand on its own.That said, comparisons to Stardew Valley are unavoidable when it comes to this game. At its heart, from a gameplay perspective, it feels like someone took one part Animal Crossing New Horizons and four parts Stardew Valley and stuck it in a blender. That's not necessarily a bad thing, but the spectre of its predecessor looms large.THAT SAID. This game is still unique enough to stand on its own. Not to spoil anything, but the mysticism and fantastical elements are MUCH more explicit and involved than in SDV. There are more characters, but because there's no friendship decay it doesn't feel overwhelming. There's more to explore, more mechanics, more characters, and honestly out of all the farming sims I've seen and played this one is pretty solid and unique.I've only played since 1.1, since I usually avoid EA games and I'm not involved in the fandom or community surrounding this game. So this perspective is from someone who came in blind to the finished (?) product. I'd love to see more- romanceable giants, maybe, or being allowed to romance Antonio. But I like what I've seen so far. Will update this if that changes lol
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I really love this gamelike any typical farming sims with a lot of elements being copied from other games in the genre, but with a modern twist it made it feel very fresh to me. I love the art style, i love the little secrets and.... EARLY GAME TELEPORTATION?!?!?!? SOLDI think the EA period hurt the game overall with a lot of people playing EA and then having to restart with full release. Lost a good chunk of player base right off the bat because people didnt want to return.If you like farming sims, try it out!
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: This is the most gorgeous farming sim game I have ever played! Everything is so cute and detailed. The characters' houses show what they like through environmental storytelling, and the map is already huge!With the quests, collectables, amount of NPCs and big world, I think there is plenty of content to already enjoy, so the price of the game is more than fair.Since it is still very early on in early access, there are some bugs and issues popping up once in a while, but the devoper team is constantly working hard on rooting them out and rolling out hotfixes.I play on the Steam Deck, which works great despite it not being officially supported. The only caveat with this being that controller support for the game will be added later, so you have to use Steam's conroller binding functions (which, honestly also work amazing). For anyone else planning to play on the Deck, my advice would be: absolutely. Go for it. But do lower the graphics settings preset to medium and turn of anti-aliasing, it'll help prevent big FPS drops.
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: I am obsessed with this game. It is everything I have wanted and more in a farming sim. It is early access, so please set your expectations accordingly BUT just know that even as an early access version, this game is FORSURE worth every penny. Also, I cannot wait to see what is added to the game with all the planned future updates!
_childDocuments_.name: Coral Island

_childDocuments_.review: In short I would recommend this game for those who like cozy games and don't mind one that can be a little more difficult. Longer explanation: Obviously this kind of game lends itself to "inclusion" of people that can be otherwise excluded from life and things in general. It does a good job of including all kinds of people and age ranges. The game is a cross between Animal Crossing and The Sims games. More detailed and difficult than than Animal Crossing; but in some ways not as detailed as the Sims. Not quite a fair comparison to The Sims since the The Sims is not a farming game. That being said there is a lot of detail in this game and I found the "Halloween" activity to be very enjoyable and you can tell the makers put a lot of love into the details at the activity. The game still has some bugs. For example: I did have an odd thing happened where I was locked in the craft menu and I could do anything so I had to restart the game which meant I lost all that I had done within that day. Which brings me to my biggest complaint is that you can't save the game whenever you want. The game is saved when your character goes to sleep. So I have gone to sleep at times to make sure I don't loose my progress if something significant happened that day which meant I also lost a full day of stuff I could have done. Have played for over 30 hours so far and I have really enjoyed the game; particularly the romance mechanic since it is fun to see if you can get a character to become your significant other. There is a good portion of the map that is "fogged" out. If the fogged out area represents the full map that gets revealed as you play than the full map is huge. Also besides the bugs there is room for improvement for example the NPC only reveal a few things that that like and just keep repeating what they like rather than revealing other things they like as you talk to them. You have to do a lot of talking with them before you even scratch the surface of what they like so it becomes a guessing game and there is no way to ask them what they like either. But besides any negatives I have mentioned I would buy the game again (if I had too); because I have enjoyed it that much. oh one more thing the game does not hold your hand and tell you how things work; but thankfully there is info on the internet.

_childDocuments_.review: Alrighty so here's my "first impression." Overall, I love the game and I'm excited to see where it goes. Pros:-The game itself is really beautiful in terms of graphics, and each character has gorgeous original art. -The NPCs are lovely. I'm convinced anyone who says they're not hasn't spent enough time speaking to them. Sure, the dialogue isn't state of the art, but overall they're well defined and lovable. Everyone has a personality.-Love love LOVE the fact that this is essentially Stardew with more realistic graphics. Don't get me wrong, Stardew is undefeated and the pixel art is iconic, but I was missing a game that felt more "real" and 3D. -If you love Animal Crossing and Stardew, this is 100% the game for you. It combines some of the best aspects of both.-Same-day house upgrades!!! Oh yeah. No more 3 day wait for Robin, they get on it. Tools still have a day waiting period though but that's fine. -No dark scenes when traveling around town/the farm, so you can go from each outdoor location to the next without a pause. -Okay. You have to note the diversity in this game because wow. We have black and brown characters, tattoos, prosthetics, and WLW vibes to go around. No mods required (looking at you, Stardew). -Themes involving conservation and pollution are always fantastic. Cons: -Stardew. Yep, Stardew. The game borrows a little too much from it, which generally isn't an issue, but c'mon, we have characters named Leah and Emily. There are a billion traditional feminine names out there. And the city itself is called Star— so like...it needs a little more originality. It didn't kill it, but it's definitely a little odd for a seasoned Stardew player. SPOILERS!!!!!!! the plot is essentially identical to SDV with less dimension(ish). -Although it was recently updated to include controller support, it was obvious designed specifically for a mouse and keyboard. It's very difficult to maneuver with a controller, and the keybinds are very glitchy. -Slow dialogue...to be fair, Stardew and many other games have this issue. Long cut scenes and pauses. I don't want to skip the conversation but I'm seriously bored by the end of it. -No tutorial, which is mostly okay, but fishing is hard without one. I had to Google a few things, especially since the keybinds are wonky, but not impossible. -Why do we have a single 2D view of a 3D game???-There are bugs and glitches, but this is early access. It's actually pretty well developed for EA.-KEYBINDS are pretty much impossible to change, or at least they are for me. They're all mixed up so it takes some fiddling and getting used to. Overall, please do not let the cons deter you. I have enjoyed every second of this game so far, and I can't wait to see what comes in the future. Even if you're not a fan of early access games, I still highly recommend it. There's plenty to do. And even with all the negative aspects, I can tell it's gonna be great. 9.999/10

_childDocuments_.review: When I read reviews saying that Coral Island is basically just 3D Stardew Valley, my thought was "well yeah, it was definitely inspired by SDV, just like SDV was inspired by other games". But upon playing it goes beyond simply inspiration, it is quite literally Stardew Valley, but tropical flavor. Not really a deal breaker for me, since I love these kinds of games. If I have a good time playing it, then for me it's good.It is your typical "save the small community from big bad corporation through the powers of farming and magic". While not a bad premise, the likenesses with SDV is a bit off-putting. Your goal so far is to submit certain collections of items to a place of local importance and doing so grants you boons, all the while balancing making money off your farm. Sound familiar? Again, it's not a bad premise, but I was hoping for something a little more original. At least it's not a Community Center, I guess.The game is visually fantastic, and the sound design is great. The UI is smooth and pleasant to move through, and I have no complaints about the controls. The playable area itself is huge and admittedly a little confusing to navigate, I found myself having to look at the map numerous times to find my way around.Now some minor complaints. Upon visiting the Ranch I was absolutely delighted to see quail and llamas (or alpacas? I could not tell) roaming around in pens. It excited me because finally, some unique and original farm animals! But alas, when I went into the Ranch store to verify this, all I saw were chickens and cows for sale. Extremely disappointing. They even looked as basic as you could get. The chickens were white and boring, and the cows were your typical "round, white with black spots" appearance every other game uses for cows. They couldn't have made them look more unique, given the setting? Even the horse looked boring. Fishing in this game gets a resounding "meh, it's alright". I love fishing in every game I play, and while it's not bad, it's not exactly fun either. Bait is not implemented yet, so it takes an eternity to get a fish on the line, and there's no way to upgrade your fishing rod (yet?). Bug catching, frankly, sucks. Even with the two upgrades I have that make me harder to detect sneaking up on them. I don't know if their models are just laid over the environment weird or what but sometimes they aren't really where they appear to be and it's hard to find their hitbox. Not to mention, they walk faster than you are in sneak mode so you can't catch up to them half the time before they spook and flee.Another problem I have is with the NPC Pablo, but it's more of a personal issue. The first two things out of his mouth upon first meeting you is "I had no idea you would look like THAT!" and "You're surprisingly cute!" And this creep is portrayed as a morally good, upstanding member of the town? If someone said that to me when they just met me, I would be beyond uncomfortable, I don't care how good looking they are. Honestly a surprising interaction in a game like this.Anyway, I am giving this game a very tentative positive review because despite the SDV likeness, and disappointment about the Ranch animals, and the Pablo thing, I am having a good time playing and nothing so far is a hard deal breaker. I just really hope the developers don't pull a My Time At Portia and eventually say "well, story's finished, game over :)" and move on.

_childDocuments_.review: Coral Island (EA) ReviewCoral Island is getting a lot of positive reviews and some folks are wondering if it will displace Stardew Valley in the farming sim genre.Well ...There's a lot to like about Coral Island. You land on a tropical island, own a farm, meet (and romance) a lot of nice - and some not so nice -"townies" and soon discover there is something mysterious going on. That soon gets your attention, and the game succeeds in keeping a well-paced story moving toward unraveling the mysteries of the island. But it's still in Early Access, so 1) it has bugs and 2) much will likely change by the time it gets to its final version.The thing to know about this game is that it's built on the foundations of its predecessors, namely Harvest Moon, Stardew Valley, My Time at Portia, No Place Like Home, and probably a few others. That's probably true of every new sandbox game that walks in these footsteps. The result is a mishmash of all of the above, with some adjustments in the margins. For example, if you are familiar with the mine in Harvest Moon, then that's what you're getting in Coral Island, with a dash of monsters. And if you've played Stardew Valley, then you are familiar with the main quest. In Coral Island, the main quest is pretty much the same, with a few minor adjustments. So if you're a fan of the games mentioned above, you'll feel at home with Coral Island.That Coral Island doesn't veer very far from its predecessors' concepts makes it more of an update to the genre than a replacement of previous games, and I suspect that's what the game intends. But it also preserves the purity of the genre, which is praiseworthy, and I hope that doesn't change once the game leaves Early Access. The exception to this formula is that the game adds diving - and it's a winning feature. Expect to spend a lot of time diving. There is room for improvement, though. The controls are okay but could use some TLC. Key-mapping currently is not available. And some of the social features and events are kind of static - more like placeholders for planned events, but that's likely to change.  I would definitely recommend Coral Island, but probably wait until some of the bugs are patched. Bear in mind that the price could go up once the game leaves Early Access.

_childDocuments_.review: Good casual game BUT comes with a couple of flaws still that hopefully will be fixed eventually.As someone that played a lot of farming games from the original Harvest Moon to Rune Factory, the game had a few nice fresh elements at first. The positive:- All in all I enjoyed the first 40-50 hours/first year of the game, which is why I am giving a thumbs up. - There is a lot of available animals and plants to grow and decorating your farm or house can be a lot of fun if you enjoy such things. - There is a lot of different types of bachelors and bachelorettes, so everyone is sure to find someone fitting their taste.- The landscape is super beautiful and really highlights the tropical island aspect of the game. Cleaning up the ocean also makes it a very beautiful place to roam around.- Every character has a unique storyline/event. Even non-dateable characters each have their own events.The negative:- Once you reach the 1 year mark, discovered most of the mines and ocean (which is easy to manage within the first 2-3 seasons of the game), it starts to become very repetitive and is mostly about completing achievements. - Even though the mermaids/-men are advertised as singles (hence supposed to be dateable), as soon as you finish the ocean and expect to be able to finally befriend them, they suddenly have no dialogue anymore. You can't even talk to them.- Some of the character events are rather random or end in a way that SHOULD have consequences for the game but once the cutscene is over, it's as if the event never happened.- There is no actual fighting system. The mines have monsters but fighting them is pretty much just button smashing and that's it. It makes the monsters seem like an afterthought and random addition to the game as they pose absolutely no threat at all when going through the mines.- I had to restart the game multiple times because I couldn't pick up artisan products from my machines, which double-sucks because you can only safe when ending the current day.- In multiple cutscenes, the NPCs just didn't show up. It was a bit awkward watching a dinner scene with only 1 of 3 characters present.If the game was early access or still in a sort of testing phase, I wouldn't mind at all, but releasing a full game and still having that sort of issues is kinda iffy.Final Thoughts:Coral Island is a great cozy game and is a lot of fun for about 40-50 hours before becoming repetitive and turning into an achievement-hunt. I wish there was a bit more world-story to discover new areas or actually make use of the battle system. Still: All in all I can recommend it. Once the bugs are fixed and you can actually befriend the merfolk, it is absolutely worth getting!

_childDocuments_.review: "Coral Island" on Steam is a gem among farm simulation games, offering a delightful escape into a vibrant, laid-back island life. This game allows you to break free from the hustle of big-city life and create your own pastoral paradise. With the freedom to customize your farm, players can grow crops, nurture animals, and engage in a variety of crafting and decoration activities. The game's world changes with the seasons, offering a dynamic and evolving gameplay experience.One of the most appealing aspects of "Coral Island" is its emphasis on community and relationships. The game features over 70 unique characters, each with their own stories and personalities. Players can build relationships with these islanders, finding out about their interests and gifting them appropriately. For those looking for romance, there are 25 eligible singles ready to mingle, allowing players to find a partner and start a new chapter together on the farm.The game also has an ecological aspect, as players can partake in restoring the island to its former glory. This includes revitalizing the town, expanding the local museum, and even diving to restore coral reefs. These activities not only improve the island but also provide resources to enhance your farming capabilities.The overwhelmingly positive reviews on Steam, with 90% of over 9,661 reviews being positive, attest to the game's appeal and quality. Players praise its relaxing nature, the depth of its content, and its engaging community features​​.Overall, "Coral Island" is a beautifully crafted game that offers a rich and rewarding experience, perfect for those who enjoy farm simulations with a strong sense of community and ecological awareness.

_childDocuments_.review: It's just Stardew Valley.Coral Island's a farm simulation game that's still in development as I write this. Your character moves to a tropical island where they start running a farm, and get involved in the lives of the depressed locals as a soulless corporation tries to buy up the island.Just like in Stardew Valley.You go into caves in the woods near your house to fight monsters, and dig up metal to upgrade your tools, or geodes that you take to the local blacksmith to break open and reveal treasures.Just like in Stardew Valley.There's an empty museum it's up to you to refill by finding jewels and ancient artifacts.Just like in Stardew Valley.There's a supernatural helper who'll open new areas or unlock extra features after you give them all the things in certain groups of items they ask you to find.Just like in Stardew Valley.There's a festival where you can get free friendship points with everybody in town if you add something really tasty to the potluck soup.Just like in Stardew Valley.The highest upgrade for your tools is made with a magic purple metal.Just like in Stardew Valley.Swinging farm tools uses up energy, but swinging swords mysteriously doesn't.Just like in Stardew Valley.The general store's closed on Wednesday.Just like in Stardew Valley.Basically, it's Stardew Valley with better art, and a few areas where they go one step farther. Like besides fishing, there's also a bug-catching feature. Or like how SV talked about mermaids living near the beach, this game lets you go scuba diving and actually meet them.But me, I've already played the hell out of Stardew Valley. I'm not super excited by a game that obviously took all its cues from a game I've already played the hell out of.If you liked Stardew Valley, but wished there was a bit more content, or a few more romance options, this is the perfect game for you! It does what I'm sure it set out to do, and it does do it pretty well. This is a good farm/life sim game with a lot of things to check out.But if you were satisfied with the game this is based on and already sunk hundreds of hours into that, like I was, Coral Island's just more of the same.

_childDocuments_.review: It's generally a good game, modeled closely on Stardew Valley. However, as of mid-December 2023, despite bearing the 1.0 version number, it feels neither content-complete, feature-complete, nor sufficiently polished. Overall, I'd say wait a year before buying this, and it'll probably be excellent at that point.For example, although the character has an armor slot and an NPC mentions wearing armor as "common sense", to my knowledge and from checking online there is no armor actually available in the game. More generally, the combat system is IMO very far from done. The monsters do laughably little damage, and at the end of the first mine you're given a (war)hammer, the most powerful weapon in the game. I think the intent was to give a mildly-powerful hammer, but presently all hammers have exactly the same abilities and stats except for price. However, you don't initially realize that because the place that sells weapons  or any other indication of what they can do.Additionally, I've noticed several places where text is missing (an item with "TBD" as its description, meaning "to be done"), incorrect (text for revealing fossils is actually a duplicate of the text for opening geodes/coffers), or oddly worded (in a way that feels like it was translated). I'm playing in English, and other languages may vary.Finally, I'm most of the way through the ocean and it's outright boring. You hit garbage with a scythe, over and over. When you finish one area, you advance to another area where you do the same thing. When you gain access to the city, it's pretty lifeless. Then more garbage, and then access to the sea caves, where all I've seen so far is more hitting garbage with a scythe. Various bits of NPC dialog make it sound like there's more to be found, but I've struck something like 10k pieces of garbage with a scythe so far and would like a little more variety by this point.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game. as a stardew enjoyer, it is so enjoyable and fun and expands on a lot of the things I would look for in a game like this like no other does! one of my favorite additions is from the newest update, where you can ask NPCs to hang out and do different activities around the town (which is so so cute with the romanceable NPCS of course!) the feature has a lot more detail than I expected-- you can pick from a dozen different locations that offer a interesting array of things, from spa days at the salon to picnics, yoga, fishing at the lake, visiting the museum or volunteering, playing volleyball, shell hunting at the beach, getting tacos at the food truck, and so much more. it's seriously one of the best features, trust me. another one of my favorite features is the artstyle, and how everyone wears different outfits for each season that you can see in their portraits and in their profiles in the relationships tab (where you can cycle through each outfit and expressions!) everyone has different expressions, and their own dialogues, interests, and hang out spots around town. god, it's so cute. everything I ever wanted from SDV and more.there's a lot to do, from mining, fishing, ranching, farming, and my favorite-- diving and cleaning up the ocean. it's borderline addicting. I'm excited about the  section, as someone who loves  it's sooo cute and fun.some of the only downsides to the game sofar have been: special shoutout for wakuu, alice, and eva, my favorite npcs. astronomer who dyes his hair a different color for every season, and has a chicken graphic that sticks out from his shirt pocket? a sweet girl that wears cozy outfits and loves the summer, with a twin sister? and I buy bread from Sam's everyday, just for Eva (it's the thought that counts!)glad I backed this game all those years ago and am delighted with every new update that comes out. worth the buy at this point, new and old purchases, for sure! if you've been on the fence about this game because of early access and updates, definitely grab it. or, on sale if you're really doubtful. you won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: Coral Island is a fantastic game! It has a brilliant and cute art style that is impossible not to love, the characters are well drawn and thought out thoroughly, I love how Alice is a mother and she proudly displays her stretch marks on her stomach. The game has a lot of similarities with games like Animal crossings and Stardew valley especially the latter but that doesn't make it less fun to play. I really love how many characters you can choose from to get to know etc. The scuba diving part is super unique and fun to explore. _childDocuments_.review: Alright, where to start?   Firstly, I backed this on kickstarter a long time ago and I've been poking around a bit on EA and Beta.   Thrilled, the game is good fun if you're in to the farming sim genre; it takes a lot of inspiration from Stardew and Harvest Moon, but adds a Paradise Island twist to it.   The graphics are lovely and there are all kinds of things I love, from being able to change the styling of my house on the exterior, to the diving mechanic, to the variety of dating candidates.   There's lots of pets, outfits and things to do to earn money.   When my chicken lays an egg I can sell it, cook it, make it into mayo or even put it in a mason jar and make it into something else.   It's the same with crops too.   This game will be great.Wait.   "will"?Yep, here's the elephant in the room.  As of 23rd November 2023 I would call this game unfinished, and it should not have been released in its current state.  I love this game, but it breaks my heart a little to sit here and say the negative.  But I have to, because it's not fair on anyone for me to proclaim it's the best ever and leave it at that.I actually bought the game on console because I have issues sitting at my desk for long periods.   On the console there are a variety of quite serious bugs; multiple crashes, stuttering, lack of sound and music.   Am I chopping a tree?  Mining rocks?  Couldn't tell you, it doesn't make a sound.    Some mini games will actually delete everything in your inventory, so here's a tip:  Remove all your stuff before going to an event.Oh and console players can't move furniture in their homes either.  I'm dying here, I have all these nice things and can't do much with them.But every game releases with bugs, we know that.  For PC and console the content of the game is not finished.   Several major things end with TBD or WIP.   My husband talks to me like it's our first time meeting, there's no commentary about being married and there was none about dating either.  I know some things were slated to be added after 1.0 like the stretch goals, but at least wrap the quests up with a temporary ending and a hint for the future rather than just WIP.  I'm persevering, I'm in year 2 now, but it still kills me when npcs go "oh hi you're the new farmer?" like I haven't been chatting with them every day for a year.I'm upset not just because of these, but because of two things.  Whilst this is going on, there's little communication I've seen from the devs outside of discord.  They need to be yelling about what they're fixing from the rooftops.  Their twitter feed for the first week was votes on hottest npc.    Secondly, I feel sad for people going into this blind and the 1.0 release being their first experience.  All they will see is most of the bad, and not the good that most of us have seen during beta and EA.  First impressions count and right now Coral Island is not hitting the mark.tl;dr Game is fab, I love it, but the bugs and unfinished content are really hurting it right now.

_childDocuments_.review: As of now I cannot recommended this game, because I find it to be quite deceitful to advertise this game as full release as it is clearly still in early access. Here are a few examples. The first two points might be a design choice but I don't understand why you go into full release when these "teething troubles" still exist.- Inventory controls have not been thought through yet. you click on an item and it goes directly into the open chest. you click on an item in the chest and you're able to place it where you want in your inventory. But you cannot swap it with an item already in your inventory. you have to put it on an empty slot. Also you cannot split stacks. If you want to grab half of the trash from your 999 trash stack, you have to press a button 500 times or pres and hold it for a minute or two.- hitting an enemy three consecutive times makes you stagger them which means they get pushed a few meters away from you and stops them from attacking for a moment. Weirdly, the pushing back also lets them glitch through obstacles which you then have to circumvent to use the staggering to attack them- flickering textures on the edge of your screen as well as flickering shadows in general- filling a machine with resources does not work with click and hold. you always have to click 20 times to fill up the recycling machine for example.- when your energy gets low, the colors in the game desaturate and your character starts to move more slowly. There's a button in the game menu to turn that off. Sadly that button has no effect.- highly variable loading times. I have installed on an SSD and entering the same building can sometimes take 2 seconds to load, sometimes 15- you can own a pet but as of now my pet has never left the house and does exactly nothing but sitting in its bed from dawn till dusk.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to love this but it's hard to recommend a game that came out of early access nearly a year ago and isn't complete despite being on version 1.1 and asking for $30. There were some things I enjoyed, hence the 70 hours, but they were mostly mindless, repetitive activities like mining or cleaning the ocean that were easy to mentally check out from and spend hours doing. At some point, I realized  I was just playing it to scratch the farm sim itch. The characters feel hollow. Many heart events don't even involve the player and a lot of them are straight out of other media, like bits from Friends. It goes beyond homage and inspiration, and instead just directly copies these well-known scenes. It reads like the writers didn't have ideas (were there professional writers involved with this game?). Honestly, almost everything feels kind of hollow. So many things feel like they're in the game because that's what farm sims are supposed to have, not because it was meaningful for this game.I should note that there ARE some good points here. The game is gorgeous and I love the tropical setting. The character appearances are cute. It's great to see aspects of cultures that you don't often see incorporated into games! When the developers split away from their "inspirations" and make unique choices, that's when the game shines. But that doesn't happen often, and it almost makes me more disappointed with the whole thing. Someone involved at some point clearly had a creative vision and I wish that was harnessed more. But considering this game received over $1.5 million in backing in 2021, multiple promised rewards still aren't or will never be available, and the game still isn't complete, I really can't recommend this game.

The good far outweighs the bad. -I love how it resembles Stardew and SoS so much in the best ways possible. _childDocuments_.review: Though there may be good things about this game it is missing certain basic quality of life features combined with a stamina system that is overbearing, and a main line quest that so far appears to be a collect-a-thon that overall hurts this game to the point I cannot recommend it at this time.  The only reason why I am still playing it, is because I am a diehard Harvest Moon, Story of Seasons, Stardew Valley, and Sun Haven fan so I can handle games that are not quite as good (My profile avatar is from HM: ANB).So a few of the quality of life features that are missing: - No stamina use when tools do nothing.  If you accidentally water the same crop twice well count that extra stamina gone, or if you miss aim your pickaxe in the mine... well sorry you just wasted stamina. - Smart tool aiming.  Do not let tools target squares they cannot interact with.  In the mines my pickaxe loves to aim at the tiles next to the rocks I am trying to smash, which results in missing that pairs poorly with the previous missing quality of life feature.  To see a good example of smart tool aiming Sun Haven has this mastered. - Queued actions.  When I am hoeing or watering and click on the next tile before the previous action is finished, be smart enough to know to actually perform that action. - Hold to perform continuous actions.  Clicking on 100+ crops to harvest or water them is bad.  In other farming games they are smart enough to know that with the basic tools since they cannot be charged if the player holds down the action key let them do a continuous action so they don't kill their finger clicking on every single crop or tile.Stamina system: - It takes a base of 20 stamina to catch a fish and it takes 20 stamina to catch bugs.  Why is bug catching so stamina intensive?  Fishing makes sense but bug catching does not considering a miss swipe only costs 1 stamina. - You start out with 450 stamina which translates out to 150 actions (this does get better, but in early game first impressions matter).  Might sound like a lot, but every watering counts as an action.  So if you have a nice 10x10 field with 4 scarecrows that is 96 actions every day to water your crops in early game leaving only 162 stamina.  Might sound like a lot, but a trip into the mines will deplete that very fast. - Other activities outside the farm drain stamina fast resulting in you being left with the only thing you can do is foraging.  This in turn causes a huge chunk of the game to become gated in early game.  For example lets say I want to start raising some chickens, I need bronze ingots to make the coop.  Which means I need to do mining, but I have no stamina to do mining (and the ore spawn rate on the first floors is terrible, on one run I found no ore on floors 5, 6, and 7).Main plot line:So early game I am presented with two main goals: 1) Fetch a bunch of items for this quest, and 2) Fetch a bunch of different items for this quest.  I did not mind Stardew Valley bundles, but this game cranked it up to a level that it is off putting to me considering how a number of said items involve activities which drain stamina extremely fast and thus make them tedious to collect.  I am low on stamina and see a bug I might need, do I really want to waste 20 stamina on a bug I might not end up needing?  Meanwhile the town folk so far have not really shown any effort on their part for contributing to save their town that they supposedly treasure.  I am the new guy, why am I doing all the hard work to save their town/island?
