_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of the original Aragami 1 and was expecting/wanting something similar (or anything like the original), ABSOLUTELY DO NOT BUY! NOT FOR YOU! Aragami 2 plays more like an arcade quick-kill speedrun then a stealth game (classic mode sucks). It's an okay game in it's own right, but nothing like the original. Should not have marketed this as a sequel, will no longer be buying any future games or DLC.This is one of those games where I wish steam had a middle-ground option. Honestly, buy it when there's a large sale.  -❌ Frustrating at worse, tolerable at best. (Why are we shoving combat in a supposed stealth series??)-🆗  It's okay. Kinda boring. Lacks variety and laughably easy. -✅ Fun. Nothing like the original. -🆗 Looks better, not great. I prefer Aragami 1's cell-shaded style.-❌ It seems like there was barely any thought put into it. -❌ An unborn child could play this with their eyes closed. -❌  What story? It's just plot-holes??-👍 Encountered no bugs when I came back to give it a second chance.-👍  Functional, with new changes.             -Could not test bugs for co-op. -❌  You will find yourself replaying the same few maps over, and over, and over again for the next 20-40 hours :)  BLOATING AND PADDED PLAY TIME The game is severely bloated, with only 9 maps and over 20+ missions- you will be forced to replay the same map over, and over, and over again. During replays some changes are made, but none of them are substantial enough to make it worthwhile. The most you'll find is the addition of more guards, or another section of the map (that you've already played) opens up. I'm not particularly against more content, my problem with the bloat is the repetitiveness of it. Level design is very lackluster which  further bogs down the game. Guards are seemingly placed at random barley watching each other, patrol routes that  don't cover anything substantial, and very uninspired map designs that do not take into account the player's incredibly flexible movement system. The ability to run in, kill everyone in "stealth" with no detection is easier then ever. You can clearly tell that quantity over quality was the main design philosophy here.  Played a little bit, didn't like. Feels like a half-assed attempt at replicating the original game's clever use of light/shadow mechanics. The most classic mode does is nerf you slightly (the game is so easy that it basically doesn't matter), and give you an extra teleport as if you needed another one on top of your 5 million OTHER movement techniques. It really feels like the dev's don't understand what made the original game as loved as it was. Tacking on a poorly replicated movement system from the first game won't work. One, the replicated system is half-assed in Aragmi 2, and two Aragami 2 was not made to handle Aragami 1 mechanics. In Aragami 1, the core mechanics of shadow/light were baked into the level/map design. Aragami 2 maps, were not made with those core mechanics in mind. All it does is make 'classic mode' look like some half-assed attempt at appeasing fans of the original Aragami 1. Honestly, Classic mode was unnecessary, and a waste of resources. Tacking on stuff from Aragami 1 won't work unless you commit to it fully. Just pick one thing and stick with it. Don't try to pander to both because in the end you'll just end up disappointing everyone. ❌I only have this to say: It's clunky, awkward, and frustrating. Just, no. Stop. 🆗Again, not much to say here. It's okay. Due to the repetitiveness, and lackluster level design it gets really boring. ❌I like the village and the music that plays in it. However I think it's a bit large, it poses the same problem as MHW Astera: too big, and annoying to traverse.Outside of the home base, the maps are fairly boring. Nothing super special going on here, pretty standard ninja, fuedal-Japan inspired setting. The lack of variety really hurts, since the main campaign will have you replaying the same few maps for the rest of the game. I played the entire game only doing ghost runs (100% kill, 0 detection), and it was still easy. Raising guard detection rates and fields of view will help with difficult but only for a little bit. I don't think tweaking some numbers is going to help with difficulty all that much.The biggest problem is guard AI is stupidly stupid, and unbelievable easy to abuse. The most you have to do here is find an enemy, make sure no one is watching him (which is basically 90% of the time), kill them, coin-flip if you should hide the body, and then move on. Not to mention guard placement is absolutely awful. They barely watch each other's backs at all. ❌Skip it, save yourself the headache. Plot-holes, and plot-contrivances out the wazoo. Terrible voice-acting. Animations/Cut scenes still leave much to be desired. Very boring dialogue, uncompelling one-dimensional characters I hesitate to even call characters, and the single most generic morally-grey three act story I've seen in a long time.  🆗I suspect this game's graphics won't age very well if you're buying this later down the line. -✅Hiding bodies is no longer a skill -✅Sound plays a little bit of a larger role in stealth runs -✅One new enemy type. -✅Co-op mode is now 3 player -✅ Playstyle choice, Stealth kill + no kill -❌There are only four enemy types in the game (technically 5, but not really). Not a huge demerit in a stealth game, but with a game as bloated & repetitive as this- it really brings the game down. -❌Would like to reiterate, why is there a half-assed combat system in a stealth game?-❌Too easy on any stealth run (ghost, spirit, demon). -❌SPOILER FOR LAST MISSION:  -❌When playing co-op, difficulty and guard-count is not increased to account for multiplayer.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great game that I would say is a challenge and gets me looking to where I should be going for taking a stealth route, but I am thankful that there is a combat system where you can fight back instead of running and hiding, but i could still do the run and hide tactic to get the hostiles to search for me till they give up. _childDocuments_.review: Aragami 2 is a different game from its predecessor.Evaluated on its own merits, it feels unpolished and repetitive at times. After coming to peace with the fact that the combat is not a general-purpose tool, and instead an ability which helps you silence a single enemy that has spotted you, I began to even enjoy it like the minigame it is. The movement is immensely satisfying and yet to get old. I dislike the hub world, as it really doesn't add any value to the game as a whole, and serves as little more than a place to keep all the dialogue, customization and consumable menus.While my review may sound negative, Aragami 2 has so perfectly nailed down the core gameplay that I can overlook those flaws, and have a good time doing it.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me just begin by saying the game is good and even though i recommend it, it is not like a very highly recommended game, that goes for the FIRST game, this however is different and does not have the same charm as the first game IMO. Aragami 2 is a lot less narrative driven and so your story and character does not hold a certain "attention" through out the game and this can make the game a little dull and boring at times.The changes made to Aragami 2 might put off some fans of the first game, even though they introduced the "classic mode" it is still not the same as the first game as that game was built around that mechanic while Aragami 2 is more of a add on feature after many fan feedbacks. It's still interesting don't get me wrong, and I use classic mode more often than I do with the new mode. XD but it's just not the same thing. If anything it kinda makes the game a little easier under this new game direction of Aragami 2 as you're more agile and action oriented, then add a way to move in shadows? yup pretty deadly, sometimes too deadly. But you have the option now to switch to your preferred mode which is awesome. As mentioned, the sequel has a focus on agility and action based combat, this works pretty well especially when you are not trying to compare the game to death with the previous title. As a stealth-action game it is a good game, very fun at that but I do find that the mission types that we are given can get a little repetitive and boring, Also with it's one-off do it right the first try approach (you have 2 chances to redo a level if you fail, but the optimal way is to not get caught/seen for the bonus rewards) it can get a little tedious and this puts me off a little and not replaying the mission again as I felt a little burnt out from a failed run. Perhaps this is my own fault as I do have some stealth-game-mood-swings, if i'm not in the head space for it, I can't play a stealth game properly and I become impatient lol. Overall it's a pretty neat stealth game that does things differently from the first game, perhaps it was unfairly reviewed by many just on the basis of that, which I find to be unfortunate, yet understandable.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr Buy the first game instead.With the story contradicting everything we knew about the Aragami from the first game, the vast amounts of bugs, the repetitive missions that only happen in 6 or so locations as well as the questionable changes to how the powers of the Aragami work, I recommend you just buy the first game.The first game was unique and the shadows weren't just your ally, they were your only lifeline and being caught was death. _childDocuments_.review: Its not Tenchu... but I'll take it. And I like it!I wasn't a fan of the original Aragami. I like this sort of 'ninja simulator'. Im really disappointing that many who look at this game seem to believe that this is just another stealth game. I fail to identify another single game that resembles this is so much as people seem to suggest. All the parts combined make it IMO only truly resemble Tenchu Z. From the way you can go over mission maps again with different goals, to the feudal era inspired setting. I can name as many contrasts to the myriad games that others are comparing this to. The stealth genre is wide and varied. If we judge, say, 1st person shooters by the same standard literally all those wildly hailed games appear to be clones of one and other, but we dont judge them so harshly. Why do we do so here?Its not without flaws. Controls can get a little wonky, sure sometimes; but gameplay is overall tight. One of my complaints is that i think its overall too bright, even with brightness set low. At some point we begin to nitpick. Overall this is filling a very specific gaming style which, honest to goodness, has been missing for decades. Its an enjoyable experience to boot.

_childDocuments_.review: Aragami 2 nails all of the things that matter to me and suffers from a lack of polish in areas that don't matter to me.  I think it's a great game that any fan of this dying (dead?) genre should experience, just unfortunately not at $35.  It's been on sale for 50% off every seasonal Steam sale so pick it up when the next one rolls around. -Precise and fluid movement mechanics-Visually impressive animations-Strong balance between stealth and combat mechanics-Demanding but balanced enemy perception-Diverse items, tools, and skills -Resource management-Thoughtful and interesting level design that incentivizes situational awareness and exploration-Encourages a variety of playstyles-Increased rewards for better player performance-Good/great soundtrack-Decent story, interesting characters-Character customization-Multiplayer-Unpolished story execution or pacing issues-Lack of facial animations for dialogue-Some grind-Occasional bugs that appear when pushing your playstyle to its limitsAragami 2 nails all of the things I find really important, provides most of the things I like, and does suffer from a lack of polish in areas that I can absolutely tolerate.  If you agree with the above answers and questions then you should absolutely go ahead and buy it.  If you're not sure, wait for a sale, and if you disagree then it's probably not for you.In regards to some other reviews I wanted to clear some things up and provide my own opinions. -The story is not bad.  It is creative, it's certainly interesting enough, and if you don't skip through dialogue and cutscenes it does make sense.  There are some issues with pacing, but missions are 10-20 minutes maximum depending on your playstyle and it's probably best played over a few weeks.  I personally really enjoyed the themes, ideas, and emotions conveyed by the characters, even if was simply presented.-There was a big update a while ago that added multiple difficulty settings and fixed many bugs.  The game starts out very easy and progressively gets harder.  Playing on hard difficulty increases XP and gold rewards compared to normal so you'll actually find yourself acquiring new items and skills faster and building a diverse toolkit.  I don't think I would've enjoyed the game as much on normal.-I never had a single crash, gamebreaking bug, or outrageously annoying bug.  It takes some time to learn what kinds of windows you have with enemy detection rate and perception, but playing conservatively you will never feel cheated.-I didn't find the maps repetitive.  Yes, there are 7 or 8 maps that get re-used for 50 missions, but at the beginning you are confined to small areas, and as you play later missions you are taken to new areas,  By the end the scale of the maps is fairly gigantic.  I personally liked this approach because gaining some familiarity with the environment is important for stealth games and there is much less backtracking than an entirely open world game.  It combines a sandbox feeling with a linear level design approach which I think is really cool.  I think it's better to think of the maps in terms of biomes rather than copy-pasted assets, because the latter is absolutely not the case.One final note: LinceWorks is no more, so there will likely never be a sequel.  The multiplayer still works perfectly fine, but you won't be finding public lobbies to play with randos.

_childDocuments_.review: Ayoo i think it's about time for Aragami 3. But Bring back the targeted shadow teleport from the first game, i miss it a lot here. _childDocuments_.review: A really great stealth game. Nothing more satisfying than observing your enemies movements, sticking to the shadows and striking at the most opportune moment to knock out all your foes in an area without being seen or heard. You can choose complete stealth, complete fighting, or a mix. Similarly, the way you approach missions can be done from multiple angles. The maps sort of have a relatively open feel to them, with each location being able to be approached from different directions. So there is a good feeling of control over the way you do each mission. Did feel a little bit long, but the gameplay was so enjoyable that I didn't mind too much. This story was simple, which actually worked in this game's favour and I enjoyed it. The game only had a couple of issues. First of all, you can't manually save, so if you mess up during a mission and get spotted (and you're going for complete stealth runs) you have to start the whole mission over again. More complex missions can take anywhere from 30-50 minutes, so messing up at the late stage of a mission was very frustrating. Second, in rare cases, the button prompts for performing actions on enemies wouldn't appear. Aside from that, there were only some very minor animation bugs. Overall, this was a fantastic stealth game. It's a shame to see the dev team has disbanded, but I wish them all the best in their future endeavours.

_childDocuments_.review: For this game coming out literally yesterday, It is a very clean and polished experience. My buddy and I are about 5 hours in. This includes, playing the levels and also searching for collectibles and blueprints hidden away in tough to find areas and achieving Ghost (never being detected) and Demon (killing every hostile on the map). So far we haven't gotten too much of the story as the missions are not exactly tied into the whole big plot right now. They feel a bit more like filler missions to increase your xp and level. Hopefully we get into a bit more of the story between the difference of awakend and normal Aragami.The gameplay is vastly different from the first game, no longer having to manage and use shadows to get around. Its' about a stamina bar now. In the first game you get caught you HAVE to get back into stealth in order to kill an enemy, but in this game it has more of a souls-esque combat system with attacks, parries, and dodges. You no longer have to stay in a shadow to be able to teleport, the stamina bar shows whether or not you can shadow leap to ledges. _childDocuments_.review: I almost have no words for this review, as I think everything shown has already been said.But anyhow..Aragami 2 does not feel like a sequel. I have to get that out of the way. It's a total different approach. Almost like a reboot really. While Aragami 1 was mostly stealth focused, and got you in absolute great trouble if spotted (hell, my adrenaline was rising when I heard that horn go over..), Aragami 2 basically is the definition of stabbing someone infront of an enemy, saying "nothing to see here" and dumping the body in some tall grass or off a cliff. The stealth isn't a big focus anymore. Sure, it's recommended, and the combat is only really there so you have a way of defending yourself if you manage to screw up the stealth (Unpopular opinion: I...Actually kinda liked the combat. It's so janky making it funny but the camera movements and the quick decision to kill or knock out on the end is actually quite epic.), but stealth is really nerfed compared to the first game.I did have fun with the game though. Running around the levels, killing enemies while blood spurts everywhere and dropping bodies or throwing them off cliffs feels nice and great. But..Well..The best I can put it as is that it does not feel like an Aragami game. So if you are a fan of the first game and see this game called Aragami 2, and you probably going "Oh more Aragami?! HELL YEAH!", then don't expect much. The reaction you SHOULD be giving to enjoy this game is "Oh another game from the same devs? Seems quite nice!" because really..There's just so much different here compared to the first game but it CAN actually be quite fun (DESPITE THE REPEATING MISSIONS, I ALMOST FORGOT ABOUT THAT. THE MISSIONS ARE QUITE REPETITIVE BUT THEY DON'T GET TOO MUCH IN THE WAY IF YOU ARE A CASUAL PLAYER LIKE ME. I JUST PLAY FOR THE FUN ANYWAYS TO ENJOY THE REST). I just can only recommend it if you don't mind everything I just said..It's still a pretty fun game for me, despite feeling like an entirely different game. I suggest playing the tutorial and the first mission first (and maybe the second one too if you have the time for it), because that's kinda what you will be expecting for the rest of the game. Sort of. Just with different levels. If you don't like it then refund it. Don't waste more time. That's the best advice I can give.-------------------------EDIT: Ok so there's a new update, introducing Classic mode, which is much more closer to Aragami 1. I suppose it's a good decision but it's really a "too little, too late" situation. I mean I guess it's okay, I played it for a bit. I just want them to add the shadow paths as well and the rest.

_childDocuments_.review: TL/DR Version: This game is an absolutely soulless trash sequel - only bearable if you play it in co-op and can laugh about it being so sh*tLong textwall version:This game is poor on all fronts.For example it has some of the most garbage and uninspired level design I've seen in a long time.Literally every "faction" and location is using the EXACT same building styles etc. - it's like everything is cloned and nothing makes sense.Ironically even a watermill runs opposite of the stream in a small river of some level - very obviously the level designer just didn't give a ♥♥♥♥ how things look and if they make sense.Also the level decoration is just wow, a skeleton on a torture table and a random skull next to it on the table, just that this skull is tiny. Couldn't even bother to scale the damn object.Even simple stuff like the grass is just hovering above the ground in some areas, really showing you nobody even bothered to ever look at what they made.The world isn't instinctive to interact with either. Many simple walls can't be stood on or walked on for example. You can smash in wood/pergament doors but not wood frame windows (not even with a skill and with audible noise, because yeah...).Heck... some buildings are built in a way that there are no stairs or doors to reach certain rooms. Everyone just freaking wallclimbs into their flat, right?Even just trees in random places, inculding inside granite rocks... nobody ever looked at these levels before release.Completely lifeless trash - castles are literally only filled by solders which come in mostly the same type and all look exactly like clones. Apparently they replicate by just drinking from the same cup or something, women not required.Even prisoner cells are empty. No life anywhere...You found a backpack in the game? Don't even dream of being able to loot that.Story telling is super weak and animations are extremely poor. "She fainted" - what you see is the person not fainted and just looking at someone else.Some lines are... dubbed? I'm not sure if it's even a japanese speaker or an AI voice, sounds really poor and only a fraction of the lines are kinda dubbed?Full of bugs, sometimes skills don't trigger. Or you collect "secrets" and they just don't count.AI is dumb as bread. They literally have line of sight of you killing someone and don't respond. Or see a pool of blood and their friend missing, why care? Whoever programmed this never saw a lifeform respond.They don't see you if you're sitting on a tent in front of them, in 3m height.Heck, a corpse hanging out (because we don't know what ragdolling is...) over a ledge? No biggie, they don't care.dMission markers don't work correctly.Objectives are displayed for a few seconds and then you can't find them nowhere.More random crap? Well, if you hang on a ledge and kill the enemy, it gets stabbed and then lifted over it as if it was weightless, on one arm mind you... If you just knock him out the enemy will just stay there, because why not.The mission status shows you how many collectibles or hostiles you have from a mission - it doesn't show you how much gold you found though.Even the UI design is crap. Why is there a moving texture behind life and stamina but not behind skills?Want even worse? Well, of course you can't assign skills to hotkeys yourself. Meaning if you learn a new one or get a new item the game randomly sorts it as it wants for you.Speaking of UI, not even the item descriptions where made by someone that played the game. Kurotsuba leggings for example say "engraved kneecaps" - too bad that item has only ONE kneecap. Well, ♥♥♥♥ happens if devs don't play their own effing game or if the designer of the item doesn't write the description and instead just asks ChatGPT.Heck, even the graphics are insanely bad. Standard features like ambient oclusion are not used.Even the shadows are implemented extremely bad - why care right, in a STEALTH game.It's... just so bad I doubt the programmers EVER played it themselves.It's literally a great example of why indie games are not always made with love and passion.I'd suggest to grab this on a big sale if at all and can only recommend to ever play this in co-op, that way you can at least laugh off some of that incompetent development.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Dishonored or Mark of the Ninja or maybe Assassins Creed you will like this game, it can't quite keep up but if you've been thirsting for something since SC: Blacklist, this is it.It's a third person, ninja stealth game with the usual mechanics, but less "powers" than you're used to from either of the above but better movement, with optional secrets hidden in the levels to unlock consumable tools and visuals amor and dyes, very similar in aethetics to Dauntless.You have a rating system at the end of missions that shows you time, hostiles killed, alive and knocked out, if you've been spotted or killed, you can only die twice and the mission is over, unfortunately these "medals" have 0 practical use or impact and the ratings in general are VERY generous, you do get more EXP based on rating tho.The only cons are a couple indie bugs to be expected, but the re-use of levels. The game maybe has 6 or so relatively big levels and missions take place in differently sized parts of them. As much as I like the game, that gets kinda boring quick, same with the same 3 enemies, only many hours in do you see 1 new kind.There has been serious budgeting in the story department but it gets the message across. I feel like the game has been hamstrung by a lack of budget, because of whats there is good, but there should just be more. And when my biggest complaint is that there should be more, then that must be a compliment.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really looking forward to this game after I finished the first part. Now that I'm done, I'm almost sad that it's over.Of course, I've heard about the problems and bugs and read about them in the reviews. Either I was very lucky with my gaming experience or some people exaggerate a bit because the second part is different from the first.While I played alone, I didn't have any problems at all. I was able to complete all levels and tasks. That's why I have a suspicion that some problems are related to the multiplayer. However, not many problems occurred there either. The biggest problem would be that you go into a level and you can't use your abilities, so you can't take out the enemies. However, this problem could be fixed by restarting the level/game. Of course, this isn't ideal, but it doesn't make the game unplayable or unenjoyable.In general, I would recommend Aragami 2 in multiplayer. It's significantly more fun and the levels are easier. The story was good and interesting. The differences from the first part are clearly noticeable, but I don't think they are bad changes. The games aren't directly connected, so I think the change is pretty cool. I was happy to experience something new. Of course, you have to get used to it, but personally I like the gameplay in this part more. The gameplay feels free and flexible and I just enjoy it.I can only recommend the game and when the bugs in the multiplayer are gone, I would also recommend the game at full price. If you are unsure, you can buy it in the sale.

I'm so glad they went in this direction, it's a huge improvement.There are a few bugs here and there... I eradicated most people in a map through brutal combat and stealth kills... but it gave me the "spirit" rank and said no one was killed, made me laugh. This game and it's developers deserve a gaming award... Best Stealth/Action Game 2021.

_childDocuments_.review: I am really enjoying Aragemi 2. I regularly team up with a friend, the game play is fluid and the story line excellent. I would say there are some minor bugs that can annoy the worst being sliding through walls with a knock out only to find yourself on the side with a guard who is active. That's a bit of a downer especially when you are near the end of the map and have stealthed it thus far.  Still it's not a big enough of a bug for me to not play the game and it has happened a few times. It's seen as we need to go through it again anyway to achieve the kill all or no hostiles killed so no biggy.  The other downside is the mission locations, "Reach the Area" is very non-specific and a map would help. Again not something that makes me not want to play the game.  A save function in the town would also be handy as I normally finish a mission, regear and talk to anyone I need to. If you quit then it forgets everyone you spoke to and all the gear you bought goes. Anyway those minor issues are nothing for how good this game is. If you liked the first you will like this one. All in all a good game with minor bugs that they will probably fix....

_childDocuments_.review: Just like the first game this is not worth the price. I paid like 3 euros and still think i over payed. Stealth mechanics are simple, lack depth and missions lack life. This whole game lacks life. There are 51 missions when the game could be 20 missions easily, so you just spend most of your playtime doing the same fetch quests on the same maps. It lacks the prequels charm with all its abilities being nerfed or just boring. You end up doing the same painful and long missions that seem to lead nowhere, with no incentive or anything since the story is lacklustre and not even remotely interesting. On top off all this the game is still a buggy mess just like the first and still badly optimised just like the first. This game developer literally somehow got a chance to fix what was wrong with the first game with this sequel and decided to just make the same game, but way worse. Hope the game studio goes under for wasting 11 hours i will never get back.

UI is no longer integrated with the game, the addition of combat as a focus makes for glitchy assassinations from time to time, shadows are no longer a key feature of the game, nor is light a debuffthe game now wastes time having you go back and forth to a hub world, skills recharge instead of needing "charges" currency and shop consumables are now a feature which whatever but i find it annoying, the game will have you jump through the same like 10 maps 5/6 times.What we have now is, ironically, a soulless stealth game. That said i have and will continue to play this game to completion. I'd maybe recommend it for people who DO want just a generic stealth game but for fans of the original its just a shell of its predecessor. That said i probably will slog through it eventually to 100% completion

Sometimes this makes the body invisible.Long range Fireball guys try to swat flies in an visual attack loopTens to upwards of 100+ people floating in the sky.  A few are T-posing.  Some are walking.  Some are dead.T-Posing guards slide at you while only moving their head, tracking you perfectlyT-Posing guards try to roleplay as an owl and snap their necks 180 degreesT-Posing guards attack you without drawing their sword through their sheer psychic willpower and mightAll unarmed civilians do a draw weapon animation with an invisible sword when they discover you that should be exclusive to guards before running away (this one is not multiplayer exclusive)People have stinky green auras around them (maybe a future mechanic I shouldn't know about yet in chapter one)Clipping through walls into buildings that aren't meant to have an inside, and getting stuck inside of them for 20 minutes until you manage to clip back outClipping through the floor and falling for 10 seconds before being warped 2 minutes into the pastClipping through the floor in the main lobby and seeing the underworldWhen secondary players load into a level they will see all enemy health bars for a brief momentSeeing copies of other players after a restart in the position they were as the game restarted (this one can stack so you can see multiple clones of a player)Cloning guards until there are so many in a lobby it becomes physically impossible to complete, but they're only real to some playersSometimes when a sniper shoots a fireball just as they die, the fireball's VFX staysThrowing corpses through walls. _childDocuments_.review: Hello my stealthy friend! Have you played Aragami? If not, what are you doing?? Play the first Aragami!Aragami 2 changes many things from its first game, such as the stealth component. Sadly, while in Aragami stealth was never an option, you can play Aragami 2 without being so cautious. I understand the choice in order to reach more gamers, but I am sad. However, with this game you can play with your friends thorugh the whole story (being it optional, and with no achievement related to play it with friends), something also added later on in Aragami, and I thank that the game offers this option.The visual design changes also drastically. While Aragami uses the graphic design as a conduit for the story, Aragami 2 would have benefit from that design style. Again, I understand the choice in order to reah more people. While the story is catchy, the problem from my point of view is that being divided in so many quests makes does not help in getting you involved in the story, as it feels like a side effect from your missions.Aragami 2 is not as good as Aragami, but it is not a bad game. Probably, and at risk of being contradictory, if you have not played Aragami before this one, you might enjoy much more than I did. But, hey, play Aragami!
_childDocuments_.name: Aragami 2

_childDocuments_.review: Aragami is an excellent game to this day, but its sequel feels like the team over at Lince Works wanted to give us the world by implementing more modern experience and money systems, more free-flowing movement, a whole new combat system, massively improved and personalized customization, consumables and build-making, tons of collectibles... wildly ambitious for a small team. And on all of these fronts, Lince Works actually pulled it off and delivered these features.My issue with Aragami 2 is that so many games have these features already, but the Aragami series had its own unique things going for it that I loved so much, which are now just husks of their former selves. Shadows are now meaningless compared to the almighty power of being two feet above your enemy, money grinding for items you have to buy isn't nearly as satisfying to get as it used to be when you obtained a no-kill medal in every single level and earned your new outfit, and most egregious of all?I say this with all the love in my heart I can summon: this game is not finished. Bugs occur constantly, the polish is not present, time and budget was poorly allocated. I could've lived without grinding for gold, wandering around looking for collectibles, or having weird and ineffective methods to completing the missions like consumables and combat if it meant we didn't constantly have to restart because all the enemies turned immortal and started T-posing at us again, or if gameplay wasn't balanced in such a way that you could get free undetected aerial kills on literally any enemy just by jumping.TL;DRThis is a good stealth game for the price. It's just not Aragami.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is great,The complaint about it being not Aragami is understandable.The problem with Aragami 2 is that, it used "Aragami" franchise,It's like expecting Tenchu (Aragami 1), but getting Shinobido (Aragami 2).Where Tenchu is more of a stealth with puzzle solving approach, Shinobido stealth approach is by giving the player more freedom (Especially in movement, controls, and utilities) at the cost of puzzle-like stealth gameplay.Perhaps if it comes under different title, the complain would not be there.Anyway, combat is smooth, the Map is less linear (Compared to Aragami 1), Movement and control are fluid, stealth is great, and hard mode could be a bit even more harder.Overall a great stealth game.I have some nitpick with the camera being too shaky at indoors or tight corners situation, and how the color is reduced when stamina is low.But is minor issue.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, I'll admit to you all that this game has a lot of bugs at this current state however if you push the right buttons, time the right attacks and keep your powers lined up for trouble you can get yourself out of a lot of the things that happen. This game is 9 chapters of honest fun if you like story and assassin's creed feel combat and stealth. I wish there were more games like it but with less glitches. I'm going to give you all a heads up about what glitches to be aware of and please do inform the devs of this if you encounter them aswell. (not including falling through the map, they tried to fix that with the teleporting): out of enemy sight line detection (getting detected anyways) : collision issues: Server frame rates (not a glitch just want to check): Teleporting Guards (not the ninjas) : Lack of objective: Duplicating Objectives: Guards float when picked up and can no longer be picked up: Objective not registering pick up and can no longer be picked up : Stuck to ledges that aren't there: Floating Ledges: non climbable ledges : no collision guards: floating Guards: lack of connection lines. Or any other you guys may think up. I'm genuinely curious about your thoughts on the game personally. Do cut this game some slack because it is just the beginning of its release.

_childDocuments_.review: First I want to say that I absolutely love the first game and sadly this game throws out everything that made the first game special. I still really enjoy this game and it is a very fun experience but don't expect it to be anything like the original. Honestly my biggest complaint is that Aragami 2 ignores much of the lore established in the first game. Shadows no longer matter, you being an aragami is not even special since there is an entire community of them, and you now have your raven abilities without having your bird. With that being said it sucks that the devs ignored so much from the original.So why did I end up giving this game a recommendation? It's honestly because the game is still solid and enjoyable. It has a much larger storyline and it is still just as satisfying finding creative ways to slice every enemy apart without being seen. I do hope to see this series continue but hopefully they go back to hiding in the Shadows and discourage being detected.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic! I enjoyed the first Aragami and the second game definitely improves on structure and combat. _childDocuments_.review: Sigh, I've waited for so long just to get disappointed-Let's start with some positive points:1. I like the new combat mechanism, it's actually fun and more interactive!2. The graphics are not quite better, but the resolution is definitely higher.3. The first cut scene mentions one event of the main story in Agarami 1 --> so saying that there are no relations to the first part is not exactly correct.Now the negative ones:1. The health and stamina bar literally look like they were copied and pasted out of an online RPG game which is set in the 18th century (same goes for the enemies).2. And even though the first cut scene slightly mentions the first story, it still is something completely new and could be sold as a different game... 3. In comparison to Aragami 1 this game has become an open World RPG with quests which follow a basic storyline. So basically a game like Horizon Zero Dawn, The Witcher, etc. 4. In addition to the completely new storyline, there has also been an entire switch with the characters who play an important role.5. A lot of designs in the game look copied and pasted and not like the original Aragami style... )):=> Conclusion: It just makes me so damn sad, that I've spent 20 Euros for well not really what I wanted... and it makes me sad that this game could've been so much better. But out of whatever reason, the developers didn't care about Aragami 1 at all and didn't feel the need to continue that story in the "second part". It just doesn't feel like you're playing Aragami. It feels like a bad rip off that you're playing because your mom or dad didn't want to pay for the real game.So yeah, I'm really sorry, but I simply can't recommend this- it pains me to write this....

_childDocuments_.review: The first game was a challenging, fun, and unique stealth game that I thoroughly enjoyed playing and replaying. This is everything that the first game was not. I played through the prologue and the first mission and I kept thinking to myself, "This feels nothing like Aragami." There's no hook to the story that made me invested--in fact, it just left me confused and irritated. The stealth mechanics are severely dumbed down, the levels felt linear, and the ability to engage in open combat was not a welcome one. Probably the one good thing was the ability to do non-lethal takedowns, though I kinda feel like that made getting a Spirit walkthrough too easy. This is nowhere near the challenge, nor the fun, nor the heart of the first game. In fact, I'd say that this is a sequel in-name-only, because not only does it not feel at all like the first game, it doesn't feel related to it, either. Don't bother.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game quite a bit, but I cannot recommend it based on its price, even on sale. Everything it does right can be found better in other games.I really enjoyed the first game for its gameplay and aesthetic, but had issues with a lackluster story. Here's how the sequel compares.The gameplay is still very fun, although it feels like they've put less focus on the character blending into shadow, which was practically the identity of the original game. They've also shoehorned in a combat system, which I largely avoided. I praised the original game for dense environments that fit the stealth mechanics, however this game ramps up in difficulty by making levels longer/larger. This is far less fun, as a single attempt of a level can be over an hour long.A notable appeal of the original Aragami was the cell-shaded stylisation, which suited the player character's ability to disappear into shadows. The sequel has abandoned that unique artstyle, losing a big part of what made the franchise stand out.I didn't care for the story in the original game, and couldn't get into the new story either. Aragami 2 introduced a hub world to fit the new multiplayer gameplay. Along with it brought plenty of running around to NPCs, just to be talked at until the next level becomes accessible.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a wonderful game by itself, but not as a follow up to Aragami.Don't get me wrong, the game looks amazing compared to the first. And the gameplay (when it works) is rather smooth and satisfying. I know the game just released so take everything I'm going to say with a grain of salt. But I do believe there are three things that could fix this as a sequel to Aragami, not just being a standalone title.The online stability is shaky but given it's week one. I don't expect much quite yet. That's one issue that can be easily resolved and knowing the devs, will probably get fixed rather quickly.The combat feels like I'm playing For Honor or Dark Souls. I don't feel the same rush I did with Aragami where I could truly use being a ninja to my advantage. I feel more like a Samurai than a Ninja. In the previous installment, you had a rather generous amount of base game options to assassinate someone. In this, if I'm not on top of the enemy, I'm coin-flipping if I'm going to kill them or get thrown into detection and combat. It's nowhere near rewarding as planning out your kill and timing it against the surrounding enemies.While I heavily enjoy the new movement mechanics. They are insanely good and I love the momentum you can use to just traverse the map with ease (assuming you don't just break your ankles because that's new). But the stamina is insanely low from the start. The comparison I use for this is the shadow meter in Aragami. With the first installment, you were able to teleport from spot to spot based on how well you actually used the shadows and how much you kept yourself from being seen. In this, when you teleport, you've now lost 50% of your stamina. And that's just base game. Base game Aragami 1 allowed atleast four consecutive teleports assuming you stayed in shadow.Overall, this game makes me wanna play Aragami 1 more than play Aragami 2. I have high hopes that either one, the devs make changes to reflect the masterpiece that was Aragami 1 or two, the community mods this game in ways that will look to improve upon the experience. But I couldn't get past 75 minutes before these took a mental toll on my playthrough. I will more than likely redo / edit my review and outlook on this game, assuming the game gets the love and attention that the community gave Aragami 1.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is quite a bit of a change from the first one, at first I didn't enjoy the change and was as annoyed as some of the others who wanted just more of the first game. Warping to shadows was removed and replaced to warping to ledges, waiting in shadows to recover your ability is gone and replaced with constant stamina recovery, combat is now a thing instead of being 1 hit, the list goes on. However after playing several levels I got use to the new mechanics and found it somewhat refreshing. Sure it wouldn't force me to restart the level after being discovered and getting hit by the enemy, but I could still restart the mission myself if I wanted a more of a challenging pure stealth run. You're not exactly forced to use the direct combat that they introduced (except for some specific mission objectives). There are bugs at launch but the developer is very actively addressing them as they are brought up and discovered. If you enjoyed the first game and you are open to learn new mechanics instead of having a carbon copy, it is a fun game especially with a friend. The bugs at release can be frustrating at times but they can also provide some hilarious moments, like when an enemy asserts his dominance over you with a T-Pose launching fireballs from his crotch (The Dev has already addressed this bug).

_childDocuments_.review: First of all I need to say, that I love stealth games. So much so that I play all these games with maximum stealthiness - no kills, no detections, no knocking enemies out.I think this is a decent game but except for the last few missions which felt interesting and meaningful everything before that were just lazy filler missions. So let me summarize my gameplay critics quickly: (Behind the hyphen is an explanation)1. The abilities are far too overpowered.2. The missions are as said mostly lazy and extremely short - I think the average playtime for most missions was about 8 minutes.3. The enemy detect invisibility. - Sometimes they detect you while being invisible and not by running into you but just randomly.4. Enemy sight is inconsistent - Sometimes they can see you above them sometimes you are completely invisible just by being an a small houses roof5. The enemy AI too often gets stuck - This is especially noticeable in "An simple mission". Not a single try without at least 1 enemy getting stuck and watching a rock for eternity. 6. Stealth kill mechanics are inconsistent - Sometimes when the indicator is visible your character still performs a normal attack instead of the stealth kill.7. Enemies/Players clip through terrain - To me as a player this happend only a few times but enemies fall through the floor or clip into rocks all the time8. Hard landings are inconsistent - Fall from 20m - no Problem soft landing <> drop one floor - hard landingOther than gameplay issues the voice acting is mediocre at best and seems to be always a single word in japanese or the start of a sentence. I did not care at the beginning but it really annoyed me later on.And last but not least the characters are honestly unlikeable and have very little depth. The story on the whole is slightly engaging and at least the last few chapters were enjoyable.So as a complete rating:Graphics: 5/10Gameplay 3/10Story 6/10Audio 4/10If you like the stealth genre maybe - otherwise I would strongly discourage buying this game.

_childDocuments_.review: For the people who say Aragami 2 is different from the first one. They have a classic mode which makes the gameplay more similar to the first game.I always wanted something similar to Tenchu Z and this is the closes I've seen to it so far. The first Aragami was pretty boring for me, so Aragami 2 was a fun experience alone and with some friends. To keep the review somewhat short; the complaints are similar to everyone elses'.- The maps are repetitive. You'll be seeing the same locations very often, but some times there's open sections or closed sections. - The online can be laggy and can be frustrating.- The game mechanics are very simple, letting you dispatch your enemies with the same strategy. This can be subjective, whether you like simplistic or complicated game mechanics.- The objectives are mundane. Go in, objective, escape. _childDocuments_.review: TL:DR - Game has its faults but very fun and challenging depending how you wish to play, lovely hub world and characters however it is a little buggy (these are quickly being solved by active dev team however) but still playable to completion.+ New enemy types+ Collectables+ Bigger environments + Beautiful OST- Sword fighting- A.I is stupid most times- Some bugsI jumped on this as soon as I saw it seeing as I loved the first Aragami and was excited to see what improvements they would do, where the story will go and so forth.I love you can unlock different looks and colours to customise more and feel more like your own shadow and the music/hub world is beautiful, I cannot get enough of it, wish there was some sit options lurking about to enjoy the view.Sadly it doesn't feel fully like an Aragami game as you cannot shadow teleport but you are a bit faster in this one and able to multi bounce to places if you have enough stealth bar which is so satisfying when you combo it and get some speed away.But more I played the more I got used to this new play-style specially when going for all the medals per level again which I feel the more difficulty comes in trying to do two at once.I will say, I HATE the combat system. It feels forced and doesn't make the game feel like stealth, I miss the 1 hit and your dead bit due to it made you focus on stealth and being careful, who do I take out first? can I even take them out yet, maybe I need another skill to help me here.If you are caught you can either sword-fight them which feels clunky and I refuse to use, anytime I am seen and this is forced, I put my sword away and just run which is often quicker because the enemy A.I easily loses you and you can just turn around and slice them in half right after.Certain parts of the maps, mostly stairs or corners of the floor you can easily see through and see the bottomless void which takes me out of the game knowing it is there and feels unfinished and in some maps you can clip through objects too easily.Does this break the game? no as you are teleported back to your location if you do this but shame it happens  to begin with.

_childDocuments_.review: It's... Different from the first game, which in and of itself isn't a negative. But it's not what I was looking for. I'm unsure whether or not I can call any of my gripes "critiques" since they aren't necessarily bad from an objective viewpoint. I dunno, I just couldn't bring myself to play more of it. The game just feels  in a way I can't explain. In other words, this isn't a review, just a rambling text justifying to nobody in particular why I don't like the game.-Shadow dash is now context sensitive, i.e it only works when teleporting to ledges and overhangs. A design decision, since the player has added mobility in other ways. Still a bit weird, since the whole shadow teleportation juju is the bread and butter of the last game. It's kinda like a fourth installment of the dishonored franchise not having a blink/far reach move. You could say that there's a forward dash move, but the control you have over it it quite limited.-Shadows aren't nearly as impactful to gameplay. I'm not saying that it's a bad thing that a sequel does things differently, but once again, it is a core mechanic being altered. It didn't feel much like shadows were vital to my survival as it should be. Especially now that your energy isn't tied to it anymore, being instead influenced by your stamina bar.- I didn't play this game too much, but it was a weird choice to make the game so bright. So much for the quiet, somber mood of the predecessor.-Double jumping and sprinting feels nice, but you need to start every sprint by dashing, which takes half of your entire stamina bar.-Combat is a simple dodge/parry affair. Not terrible, though quite dull. I don't care for it since it further deemphasizes stealth. Aragami was a pure stealth game, since the odds were heavily stacked against you when spotted. This could have worked, if I found it fun enough to bother engaging in the combat.- I can't speak for the missions since I didn't play the game for too long, That being said, there's now a limited amount of times you are allowed to fail a mission, and there is no "reload from checkpoint" thing. In other words, if you're a stealth-purist such as myself, I reckon you'll have fun with the "restart mission" button. Either that, or they cranked down the difficulty far enough that it wouldn't matter. -It is VERY worrying that the mission that I did play felt like a procedurally generated level in a live-service game. Something more akin to what you'd find in Warframe. The tutorial and first mission felt quite dull, not being nearly as gripping as any of the missions in the first game, including the tutorial. -Skills are level based. Interesting, but the "Fastest Way to Farm XP" guide I saw before starting the game set off some alarm bells. Whether or not this is an issue remains to be seen. The game seems more geared towards the multiplayer side of things with how the mission selection and rewards are displayed, and I'm not sure how to feel about that. I'd bet good money that you'll have to replay missions for meager rewards, or maybe even play rehashed maps with new objectives. The fact that the first mission only used HALF of the map hints at this.-Games tend to get harder, but damn this felt like taking candy from a baby that has suffered rapid onset crib death. Giving enemies a wide berth is easy peasy since several spinal discs have been removed from their necks, preventing them from looking up. A severe vitamin a deficiency would also explain their apparent blindness. I only got spotted when I decided to shank the main bloke in a camp to see how they would react. Otherwise, circumventing the enemies is a cakewalk.-The levels and mission structure feels... Wrong, somehow. Like they were made for several different purposes so that a randomly generated objective could be applied after the fact. Akin to the tilesets in Warframe, albeit nowhere as memorable. I can't explain it. It's like a sixth sense has developed after years of playing games. Like I am CONVINCED that they'll rehash maps with new objectives later. And ho-boy. If the absence of the "Restart Checkpoint" button along with the resource rewards is any indication, this game probably goes for shorter, less interesting missions than the first game.-Honestly it may just have been that the mission select screen coupled with the simplistic mission screamed "Anthem", "Godfall" and "The Division".-Additionally, there's just some form of accursed ethereal jank that I wasn't present in the first Aragami.Am I being too harsh?Maybe.I just can't bring myself to like Aragami 2 nor recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's worth noting that while Aragami 2 improves on the visual style, music and feel of the original, it is not entirely the same style of game. Aragami 1 was very much built around the teleporting through shadows mechanic. Whereas Aragami 2 is more like, what if the early Tenchu games without the clunky controls and mobility. That's the feel I get while playing the game, zipping through the levels like a shadow of death ready to perform my mission.I understand some people have concerns. The reused levels on the one hand, might seem repetitive to some, for me I like the way you come back to the same location, with different guard layouts and different areas of the map to infiltrate.Some say the fluid movement makes the game too easy. I think that may be true if your goal is simply to finish a given level. I still find it challenging going for some of the triple playstyle elements, especially the unseen aspects.Some have complained about the unattackable civilians who exist solely to raise the alarm. Whilst they did confuse me the first time I met one, this is not an unknown concept in the genre and is an interesting obstacle that can't be dealt with in the usual, stabby manner.I haven't tried the co-op yet but I know the slower pace of Aragami 1 was sometimes frustrating in co-op, especially simply waiting to recharge or waiting patiently for guard patterns so you could breach an area on  a no-kills run. The improved mobility feels like it would really benefit the co-op experience and I'm eager to try it.There are some minor bugs. Nothing too drastic for me. Fell through the world once and there's a vaulting bug that's been addressed and marked for patching but these kind of things are expected for an indie project.Ultimately, I sat down to play this at 6pm last night "for an hour or two" and finished up around 1am. So, yeah, beyond all those concerns I still had an absolute blast. I still think there's some room for improvement for an Aragami 3 to really encapsulate the full modern Tenchu experience but this is yet another giant leap forward. In a market still oddly devoid of such games, Aragami will continue to be king.

_childDocuments_.review: Plays worse than a typical day 1 release. Every single mission is riddled with bugs that break immersion and cause frustration. Enemies just walk into you while you are invisible or in shadow or foliage, they don't need to even indicate they have seen you... they just walk up and kill you. When you try and stealth kill enemies, its a 50/50 chance the game will actually let you subdue/ kill them or let you use your abilities. Map design looks great, with really nice textures but the sudden walls that appear to block off the inaccessible regions can be very jarring at times, and with no way to map your journey, direction or locate objectives (which only appear in shadow vision at very close range) make it easy to get lost, repeating the same steps over and over again, especially if attempting a full stealth run. Due especially to the last point, it feels like the game encourages you to fail in order to memorise the map and objective locations. This is fine for the first few missions but when every mission relies on this tactic, it isnt great. Being unable to tell the exact location of party members when playing in co-op also makes it extremely challenging to coordinate, even if in voice chat or the same room. Overpriced for the sheer number of bugs and frustration.Update 2022Still game-breaking bugs. Still terrible. Classic mode also has a bug that disables WASD sometimes too. Dont buy.

_childDocuments_.review: As a stealth game fan I will go a bit in depth with this soTL;DR This is a very beefy and quite enjoyable 3rd person sneaking game, that improves upon the original in almost every aspect and I highly recommend to fans of the genre (especially Tenchu and Shinobido bros)That being said its a bit of a rocky game. The Unity assets are nice but result to the game not having much visual identity. Especially after ditching the previous more Okami themed aesthetic. If you pierce through this facade and some rough animations(hello there air assassinations) a fun sneaker lies within.Level design is fun and kurai's new mobility is fitting to this aspect. When you get on with the flow of the stage and the powers it turns in a breakneck speed stealth puzzle that is challenging enough and never overstays its welcome. The tempo is great and it reminds me of Tenchu and Shinobido where situations are diffused quickly and have an arcady feel to them. Sound is great and Emi Evans singing is always a welcome feature in any game lets be honest. The death cries are repetitive and in a beefy game like this it can be a bit of a mind numbing affair. That being said, if you grew up with (guess what) Tenchu you are propably immune to this aspect.Story like the first one is non existent and an excuse to slit throats and sneak, nothing more there. Overall this is easy to recommend, to any fan of the genre. Immersion is a thumbs down, especially with the new art style. So if you are looking for a deep immersive dive to feudal Japan this aint it chief. But if youre up for some sweet feeling stealthing and chaos this a big yes.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. Definitely a huge improvement over the first game. Unlike the first one, the special abilities you unlock are available to use without going to a specific area on the map in the first game. It felt like there were a lot better missions too because it wasn't too strict on the stealth(at least for me). The special abilities allow for unique and different builds for your character. Replay Value: I could see myself playing this again in the future, but as if now, seeing no option for a new game plus, it gets a little boring after collecting everything I needed. There are 48 levels with 48 perks. The game starts to get easier as you achieve more useful perks but I also noticed that you can change the difficulty for missions, so I kinda lost my motivation to continue playing the game. There are collectibles as well but I don't see myself collecting all of them. Maybe back in the day when I had more time to kill.  The sword combat is okay. It's not too hard to understand but it becomes boring after you could only do so much with left click and right click to parry. It will take a while before I can enjoy this game again.The missions do seem repetitive because some missions are on the same map but you start off in a different area. Some of the missions made me feel like I was playing Assassin's Creed. I love the stealth, though. I'm also glad they added cool combat mechanics in to this with the sword fighting.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the sloppiest most unpolished messes I have ever played. The game is full of bugs, actually hindering you from trying to do the stealth route. Enemies tend to just.. not be exectuable/knockdown-able forcing you into a route you don't want to play. I played in coop the entire time and the amount of resets we had to do because of bugs or inconsistencies (like ranged enemies being onehit-able with Shurikens but then in another attempt surviving two Shurikens before getting into a downed state on the ground (but still alive)) is incredible. If you enjoyed Aragami 1, do not be fooled. This is anything but a Sequel. The entire essence of a full stealth game is pulled out due to the addition of a new combat system. That's right, health bars are a thing now, combined with stamina bars for you and enemies so you can parry hits to get an opening for an insta-kill hit. Don't get me wrong, the combat system is fun (if it works), but after having thoroughly enjoyed the first game, a sequel seemed very promising to me. Also, seeing the Ninja, Stealth and Assassin tags kind of made me think I would get a game primarily designed with these ideas in mind yet it feels like the actual blade to blade combat was what they intended to be the key aspect/selling point of the game.When I complained about the bugs online, the community told me to "Just live with it, they have been there since launch" which shows an inability to fix these bugs or maybe it's indifference. Either way, this unpolished and sloppy mess is something I would advice against buying, especially if you are looking for a stealth game like the first one.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a far cry different from the first, that is for certain. The branching perk selections are a nice step up from the original, especially because the abilities are unlocked through combat proficiency (whereas in the original you had to find hidden scrolls to unlock skill points that could be spent on abilities and upgrades). It's also nice that there are multiple profiles now; that way I can experiment with different perk trees and progress through the game at my own pace while maintaining a co-op profile geared more toward shared utilities that help us as a group, and have a single-player profile with abilities that only help myself. It could be from playing Aragami on the hardest difficulty prior to my play-through of this, but it seems that the difficulty for Aragami 2 is significantly lower. The controls for this are much more intuitive (you can jump around finally - yay!), and the combat mechanics are a breath of fresh-air from the first. In the original you physically couldn't duel any of the enemies because you're basically a shadow demon and all the enemy NPCs wield light magic; in this one, you can get a second chance to redeem yourself if an enemy discovers you: one good-ol'-fashioned sword fight where you can block their attacks, parry their blows with well-timed counters, and mash M1 until their health goes down. At first I was honestly a little bit disappointed with the combat because it is so different from the first (and all-too familiar from other games...), but overall it's not too far off from the first. I took the original as more of a strategic elimination puzzle; like chess meets Assassin's Creed. You had to be careful and plan out your eliminations in the original: wait for the patrolling guards to get into position for you to spring your ambush; there's a lot of that in this one, but it's mostly a matter of waiting in a patch of tall grass, or behind a fence; in the original I loved being able to watch from around a corner, teleport to a shadow behind the guard to take him out, and then teleport to another shadow. Biggest drawback right now I would say is the co-op; there are legitimately game-breaking bugs for online play that make the game not only un-fun but an exercise in futility: if you restart a mission, there's a high chance that player 2 will not be able to see stealth indicators on enemies and see which ones are spotting them or if they are about to be spotted; same with using shadow abilities that normally leave a status effect on NPCs as well as an indicator of how long that status will last. Additionally, the actions for assassination kills don't always appear on enemies after restarting the game; co-op players could walk right up to an enemy and count coup with them, but there is no prompt for assassinating them, so clicking the M1 button will just slash at them, which will always lead to the player being discovered. The only way around that is to stun the enemies with a one-time-use utility or a shadow power with a long cooldown - even though player 1 has no such issues.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game on classic mode with my wife. Extraordinarily fun which is what counts.A very nice break from Sekiro. Similar combat but nowhere near as difficult. The game is challenging enough but not Sekiro hard. If you really enjoy being challenged (frustrated) and playing the same level on Mario 1000 times, this isn't the game for you. Story is pretty lack luster but you can skip all cut scenes and click through most conversations. You don't need to know what's going on in the story to enjoy the combat and stealth aspects of the game.The combat animations and npc deaths are very satisfying.Other reviews complain about glitches. They weren't a big deal. The game fixes most shadow leap glitches on its own.Other reviews also complain about the lack of new maps. It would have been nice if there were more maps, however returning to the same maps with different objectives and at different locations gives enough variety when playing with a friend. Also returning to the map gives you a chance to look around for collectables that you might not have found the first time. Overall really enjoyed the content in this game and would recommend to friends / couples.Also, we didn't like how they added Sekiro / Arkham style combat to this game. When you play in classic mode, if you get discovered it's basically sudden death. We found this a lot more challenging and more interesting way to play so we stuck with the classic mode for the entire game.Hope this helped you with your decision.Cheers,

_childDocuments_.review: This game is extremely buggy even a few months after release, and not in a goofy funny way that you can continue with, but in a game breaking "cannot continue" way.Tried to play this with my friends several times, whoever wrote the MP code/syncing needs to be replaced - multiplayer is a buggy mess. A good game breaking example that happened often was simply trying to move a body, it resulted consistently in the player being stuck in a carrying pose, unable to do anything but walk around and thus unable to complete the mission.Another is the combat, which is not the point of the game - but a friend can be slashing the enemy in the back and not register any hits ever. Not in a latency way, but as in if one person is engaged in combat with an enemy, an ally cannot connect with a sword strike.I overlooked the graphics from the Xbox 360 era, because I simply don't care about graphics. But to release a sequel, that shows 3 characters on the front cover (hence advertising itself as a multiplayer game) and being this broken in MP? That isn't really forgivable.If you want to play it alone, buy it - if you want to play with your friends, buy something else.

_childDocuments_.review: I got bored in an hour.I read my review on the first Aragami game written 4 years ago, not a particularly exciting game but I enjoyed it. This sequel feels like breaking the original game into 100 levels, and ruining the fun.Game encourages players to explore, you can do dash, double jump, short distance teleport, basically you free roam the town. It feels good to overlook a place full of enemies without their acknowledgement, except... you enter the same map again in later levels, it is extended but most parts remain the same. The more you play, the less you will see. After beating 15 levels, I find this game asks you to 1) Eavesdropping 2)Steal 3)Kill 4)abduct or rescue. Missions are highly repeated, if you finish chapter 1 you've seen everything and better stop there. The way you play is not limited, kill or being a ghost, but a lot of time I spent was on locating. You can see through walls and know nearby enemies and loot, this could be further. I have to be everywhere to locate targets, and there is really not much to see.Everything you do consumes the physical bar, the sword fight is challenging since you cannot attack constantly. An abduct or rescue mission can be difficult, when carrying a guy on the shoulder you cannot double jump or shadow leap, just run past angry enemies. You can buy clothes but they mostly just vary in color. You gain exp after each level to unlock skill tree, plain and basic.  That's pretty much about everything you do in the game. I can't even play for 2 hours to get the card drops.

_childDocuments_.review: The game tells you plainly through its trailers and tags what its about, before delivering upon these promises beautifully.During this years autumn sales I bought this game for myself and a friend, we both started it up and got to it and had great fun and a few laughs at our own early game blunders.five missions deep into our co-op experience and we start having a few operator moments,Y'know synchronized take downs and all that.The games quite fun and has wonderful design in both its visual presentation and its music.In my nearly eight hours as of making this review I ran into very few issues and most of those rather minor;The first I encountered was a bug with corpses making it so you pick them up but also don't levitating them in the air where you picked them up at.The second was a gold purse spawn in a region with a mine, this one is altogether minor but denies you 100% gold if the purse spawns in one of the shrines in the hills.The third and currently final one is more funny than anything another friend of mine bought the game, joined us and we began to catch him up in the story, on one of the theft missions when he interacted with one of the bags he generated an entirely new(?)(Maybe not he mighta just teleported one) unconscious guard.8.5/10 Love it!
