_childDocuments_.review: Based on the review comments that I've read so far there are two camps.1. People wanted a direct gameplay sequel to Aragami 1or2. People who played Aragami 1 really wanted a spiritual successor to the Tenchu seriesThose who are in camp 1 will certainly disappointed.I'm not disappointed. To be clear...that means I'm in camp 2.Aragami 2 still has many bugs and the levels may not be as open as my favorite ninja game of all time, Tenchu 1, but Aragami 2 certainly does scratch that *Tenchu itch. I'm the type of person who would play the soundtrack to Tenchu 1 while playing Sekiro and now I'm that same person, but playing the soundtrack to Tenchu 1 while playing Aragami 2.While the combat is certainly more QTE (quick-time-event) than I would like, it is less brutally difficult as Sekiro...and for someone who just wants to come home from work and pretend to be a ninja for a few hours, that's good with me.My hope is that the developers continue to sculpt this game into what it could be for those who are in Camp 2. The movement flow feels pretty svelte and I love moving from a double jump to a dash to a teleport. However, The teleport system is still a little buggy and there are some roofs that you can't teleport on while there are others you can. While I wait for the next update, I'm very happy with what is on offer here.Cheers and thanks Devs!P.S.Please Devs, create a Steam Workshop where we can create our own levels. I really want to play the ninth level from Tenchu 1 using this game's mechanics and engine.*If you find yourself to have a Tenchu itch please consult a doctor as soon as possible.

_childDocuments_.review: Although I have complaints about the game, I did enjoy playing it to 100% completion. The game isn't a sequel or even a prequel to the first game, its more of an adjacent storyline from the same universe that is linear but a bit less fleshed out than you will expect from a game sharing the title of the first Aragami, that was almost all story.Overall, if you can get over the odd genre switch up mid game, which only really affects one level being annoying to complete, after that, it mostly returns to normal. The game plays a bit like a faux MMO, with a hub and a way to visit levels as you want after you have completed the original story run for that level.It feels like playing with others is the better way to play, I played it solo, so its doable solo and enjoyable, but definitely feels like it was partially designed for co-op play as the better route. Once you've done all the achievements, the game has basically no replayability, cause by then you've done everything. So you really have to pick if you want to play solo or co-op, as doing both is going to be a mirror run, and probably not as enjoyable the second time round.

_childDocuments_.review: Aragami 2 is a-lot different compared to Aragami 1. The Graphics style has changed from a beautiful unique Cell-shading to a (In my opinion, still nice) standard indie style. Hiding in the shadows still looks very cool. They removed the "shadow blot" from the first game which allowed you to teleport freely anywhere to make your own path, they also removed the "Yurei/Pacifict" and "Kami/Lethal" reward skins for whatever reason and replaced them with a standard "You did this!" at the end results screen. Your shadow abilities no longer need to regenerate in the shadows because that system has been removed by a standard stamina bar that works in Light and darkness. Powers are also on a cool down and can be used an infinite amount of time. The difficulty has decreased with the amount of movement you have now, enemies are somewhat blind unless you stand in-front of them or just generally be careless. Which you will later on in the game when you unlock more of the stronger abilities. The A.I is very easily exploitable as-well, you can be seen killing someone and if you are fast enough hide yourself and the body and the A.I will forget about you without any penalty to your overall results.The new combat system is similar but overall a dollar store copy of Dark Souls. In short It's not good. Parrying enemies attacks feels really good and rewarding and enemies can also parry players who spam attack buttons. You can also parry projectiles.Heavy attacks are very useless as they made the animation very flashy but very slow, It's mostly designed to take on enemies who group up on you but with how long the animation takes they'll either hit you before the animation finishes or kill you. But other than that you basically just wail on these dudes until their own stamina/guard breaks and you can either kill or knock them out.Customisation is greatly appreciated compared to Aragami 1. However alot of the customisation is found closer to the end of the game which is a real shame since you'll be stuck with the same outfits and dyes for a very long time. Also the outfits and dyes are very expensive so look around for all the gold in each mission.There's no penalty for killing everyone except one optional side mission that tasks you to NOT kill everyone you see and remain unseen

_childDocuments_.review: It pains me to have to rate an Aragami sequel negatively. For starters this isn't an Aragami game. It's called Aragami, you play as an Aragami, but this isn't Aragami. They basically gutted what made Aragami unique. I'm a big fan of the first one and could look past some of it's quirks as it was Lince's first game. I was hoping to see some major improvements in terms of game play, animation, and the addition of cut content from the previous game such as multiple endings depending on play style. In that 5 year gap however it seems like things never really progressed such as animations and the core game play got worse.     The whole concept of light vs shadow is completely obliterated from both a story and game play perspective. You no longer have the cape which served as a unique display similar to denote your power. It lessened the need for a UI and made the game more immersive. It refilled in the shadows and depleted in the light or when using powers. Instead it is replaced by generic stamina bar that refills regardless of the situation. Light has no effect on it at all anymore just making light something to avoid because it makes you easier to see just like literally every other stealth game on the market.    This concept has been so completely butchered that even the shadow village is just filled to the brim with lanterns and they aren't even some special kind of laterns with a blue flame or something to make it more shadowy or something. Just a whole bunch of normal lanterns that would have drained Aragami's power completely in the previous game. This also extends to missions as well where the sun is literally still in the sky in some levels something well established in the previous game would completely  wipe out Aragami. It's actually astonishing how it isn't intentional when they go this far to entirely go against every established concept of the previous game.     Next is the graphics. I'll keep this one relatively short. They certainly look nice, but I wouldn't call them an improvement. For a game so centered around shadows, cel-shading was a a perfect style to go with. The last game's graphics fit a lot better. The one thing the new game did improve upon was the character faces. If they kept the cell shading and just went with higher poly-counts and more detailed character models/environments that would've been perfect.     The animations were a true travesty. After 5 years I was hoping for some improvements, but it really is hard to tell the difference between the 2 games. The cutscenes have terrible model clipping, the sword fights are clunky when knocking out from above, there is no special animation, your character just lands and performs the normal knockout animation.     The movement system changes are easily the worst things to be changed alongside the light vs shadow elements. You no longer have the same freedom of movement you had in the first game which is incredibly odd when they seem to be encouraging more freedom in terms of the story, approach to enemies, and level design. You no longer have the freedom of the shadow leap. It is exclusively relegated to ledge climbing now. Instead you have a short dash which you cannot see or control the distance. This has lead to a bunch of times where there are 2 patches of tall grass far apart and I will dash from one to the other and fall short right in front of an enemy. In the previous game this wasn't an issue as you knew the exact range of your dash and even if it wasn't close enough, you knew that and could work with that information.     The grass patches were an interesting concept lost with the core game play of Aragami. In the previous game bushes served a similar purpose and refilled your shadow essence, but were more sparse. If they kept the core gameplay, then the grass could act similar to bushes, but wouldn't refill your essence giving you temporary cover, but limiting you on your ways out if you were low on essence going in.     The knock-out system is again a mixed bag. In the previous game pacifist runs were more challenging and the ending even prodded you to play a pacifist run. It wasn't really a necessity in the first game, but with how limited you are in terms of movement in 2 it is a requirement as you are no longer able to slink by many enemies.     The combat system was completely not needed. I play stealth games to be stealthy. Not play a "stealth is optional for this mission" type of game. Whenever I was spotted in Aragami 2 I would just find myself restarting anyways because the game actively punishes you for engaging in any kind of combat by lowering your rank at the end of levels. The few times I did get spotted and just decided to try and fight, it never resulted in a duel as other enemies in the area would get alerted to and immediately run over making it 2,3, or 4 on 1 fights. It's a completely and utterly pointless system. In Aragami getting spotted was usually an immediate death sentence, but with enough skill you could warp behind the enemy and kill  the enemy before  he could raise an alarm. That skill reward system is just gone now.I really wish this game was just a buggy mess because that would mean that it would be patched down the line, but Aragami 2 is so fundamentally flawed to the core that no amount of patches can turn this into a proper Aragami sequel. If you are new to Aragami and are thinking about getting into the series, just buy Aragami 1.For being 5 years older it has:-better and more stylized graphics-much more unique and enjoyable game play to set it apart from other games of this genre-it's biggest flaw is the cutscene animations, but Aragami 2 did nothing much to improve on this anyways.All that and you save $10.

_childDocuments_.review: Sequel to the (what I would call) indie marvel Aragami of 2016, this game is more of its predecessor in all the wrong areas.Child of 5 hellish development years, Aragami 2 presents itself with a more complex combat system, streamlined levels and a new realistic aesthetic.When in the first instalment of the series you could be insta killed when discovered, now you have to painfully play what is in reality a minigame of timings, to get out of the situation, because gone is your ability to kill enemies instantly that would have otherwise allowed you to cover the mistake.The levels even if larger they are only used for one half during a mission, leaving the other part empty and lifeless, breaking the immersion.And even if the graphic someone could tell has improved, it is now harder to discern enemies from scenery and when they tried their best to reintroduce a "classic" mode, it is clear the old main-mechanic concerning shadows does not work anymore due to the less-sylized look.Yeah, because now you no longer have a shadow-fueled meter to use your abilities, they have been downgraded to simple cooldowns that are slower if you are near a light-source.Overall it is clear from my review that I didn't like the game, it is way less fun, and it is obviously the result of a troubled development brought to the team by an overly-ambitious scope. Nevertheless, I am sad that this game ultimately killed the studio.Have a nice day
_childDocuments_.name: Aragami 2

_childDocuments_.review: I am a very big fan of the original Aragami and completed it multiple times. I even speedran it in under 10 minutes. Consequently I (and the friend I played with in Aragami 1 COOP) were pretty hyped when we saw there should be a Sequel. Both of us immidiately preordered the game as we were hoping for a more refined Aragami, with a immersive story, cool stealth and nice new abilities. When the game finally feleased we immidiately started playing and were shocked. The game has next to nothing in common with its predecessor. The Shadow teleport which defined the first game is gone, replaced by a boring sprint and ledgegrap. The 1 vs 1 fighting is very lacking and feels kind of clunky. Moreover it has no real purpose as you are basically dead when you come to fight in a 1vs1. The COmbat could have been very good in boss fights which could have brought the aragami franchise to a new level, but guess what there are nearly no bossfight. The Abilities in this game feel boring as they are your standard stealth game abilities. The next really bad point is the story. There is no story or atleast not a story that you are really a part of. After each mission some characters tell you some information, but that is just boring as you see nothing of that exact story in the game itself. In Addition to that the level structure of the game is very lacking. Remember the unique levels in Aragami 1. They are gone, in this game you are constantly revisiting the same maps with some new tasks (like destroy 5 barrels). This makes the game feel very repetitive, boring and uninspired. I am honestly very dissapointed. The game is not completely bad, but lacks the identity of an aragami game.If you like Aragami I would not recommend buying it.
_childDocuments_.name: Aragami 2

_childDocuments_.review: I was of mixed opinion about Aragami 2.There were a significant number of changes from the original game, such as the addition of jumping and a lot more verticality.There were also a number of bugs that never got fixed, such as using the 'whisper' ability on an enemy (to call them towards you) and having them walk THROUGH the cover that you were sheltering behind, thus detecting you without the ability to assassinate or knock them out like normal. As a result, you have combat, you have a player detection, and you get a lower score. Annoying.I also encountered a glitch in one level where all of the enemy were moving in circles almost on the spot, making it near impossible to take them out without cheesing abilities, and waiting a minute for the cooldown to expire, then doing it again. It made that level frustrating too.Aragami 2 also has a MUCH lengthier campaign, consisting of about 8 maps that are reused about 5 times each with very slight differences (ie. opening up a previously blocked segment, and closing off a previously open one). And it was here that I found the most frustration. Given there are about 52 missions in the game, by the end of it I just wanted it to be over cause I knew the levels back to front.  I also had no desire to replay the game or any of the missions to collect all of the collectibles - simply because I had seen the levels so much that I was sick of them. It'd probably be more fun playing coop with people, but playing Solo it just became repetitive, with the only difference between levels really being the placement of enemy, and the enemy types.That said, the story was pretty cool. I'm actually disappointed the Devs have closed, and we won't see a sequel to this. Because while there was little linking Aragami 1 and 2, the ending to 2 definitely opened up future game options, and left me wanting more.Overall, I would definitely recommend it, especially when it's on sale. Despite all of the issues I've listed above, it's still a really good entry into this genre of game even against titles from "AAA" developers.

_childDocuments_.review: Aragami 1 was amazing, one of the funnest stealth games I've ever played. Recently I bought Aragami 2 thinking that it'd top it considering it was made 5 years after... little did I know I was in for one of the most repetitive play-through ever. Nothing about this game is good. The multiplayer is all messed up as well the controls. In Aragami 1 the key binds are really good, in Aragami 2 the key binds are crappy and all over the place and guess what.. you can't even change them, the key bind mapping doesn't save. So on top of the multiplayer not working if you wanted to play by yourself than you better buckle up because these key binds and mechanics are horrible. Don't buy this buy Aragami 1 instead

_childDocuments_.review: Aragami 2 is not like its predecessor at all. The gameplay is changed in almost every possible way, which also explains most of the negative reviews.However, in my opinion it was a change for the better. Aragami 1 is amazing, but it is very limited in terms of movement (no jumping, slow paced) and customisation. These two aspects alone make Aragami 2 a much deeper experience (also adding to the replayability) where you can switch between different playstyles all while personalising your Aragami. Aragami 2 also has a lot more missions, while Aragami 1 could be completed in under 10 hours. However, the sequel is reusing a lot of the same maps, you are just playing different parts of the same map each time. Overall I don't think that's a problem either, you'll always get maps or parts of maps that you haven't seen before and the maps that you played before are great to experiment with your new skills.

_childDocuments_.review: So I played for like 90 minutes when writing this. And I have a reson that will be separated much lower. Also I will probably heavily edit this as my experience with this game will proceed.Firstly I have to say it feels a bit different, I kinda miss that whole shadow play from the first game, it was cool feeling and mechanic. Movement system in this one is fluid and fast paced, no need to sit in the shadows to recharge but also no jumping from shadow to shadow with ability. Difficulty seems to go more casual and friendly, as they added clumsy combat system. I love how stupid the combat system is, because it is telling me that this is not inteded as way to play, but more like failsafe, when one enemy sees me. Also non lethal takedown is now an option. I love vanity and there is now a piece to piece to piece customization of the character unlocked through the game.Skills... yeah I liked the unlock system in frist game more as I could spent my points in a short skill tree made for that ability. Now I want something advanced, I dont need only to save for a while but I need to chew my way through skills I dont want/see the fun in them that much. Whistle for luring is now a single target whisper, so easier to use to lure only the one guy you want and not his whole gang and neighbourhood.But there is a good reason why I am sitting here and writing this. Yes I like the game so far, but one thing was harrasing my stealth tries. The game has no solid walls, everyone and everything is a ghost! I could pick up collectibles through walls, I once threw uncouncious body through wallm got detected and then that alerted enemy has killed me through the wall in the corner of the house. For me it ruins the game a bit.At least it annoyed me to the point of shutting the game down and rant about it here.

_childDocuments_.review: In Aragami 1 you had an intimate relationship with the darkness. It hid you, it recharged your essence. You were eagerly looking out for the next patch of shadow to teleport to, or a safe spot to create a shadow in. Aragami 1 is a pure stealth game, failure is quick, death is swift, running away requires reflexes and an escape plan.This game is very different from the first one - no longer a pure stealth title, and should be much more bearable to dip into for non-purists. It feels like Tenchu, but with dumbed down Sekiro combat.Couple of points from my thoughts if you want to consider:Every stealth fan will enjoy this game, but stealth purists will probably not enjoy it to the maximum. The biggest difference compared to the first game is pace. Aragami 1 is slow and unforgiving, while Aragami 2 is directly opposite.

_childDocuments_.review: In short:A sequel only in name, if you are coming into this game expecting more gameplay like the first you'll be left extremely disappointed, even the iconic freeform teleporting and creating of shadows is not in this sequel.What is there instead is a much faster and more open feeling sandbox that is an absolute blast to burst through due to the sheer amount of options available to you at any time. If I had to choose between the two I'd most definitely prefer the sequelGood:- Looks, sounds and feels great- The movement system is extremely open, especially compared to the first game, allowing you to (sometimes literally) soar throughout the entire map- Customization allows you to really adjust depending on how you want to play, almost all skills provide new options in one way or anotherMeh:- A ton of missions involve going to already explored maps but with a different objective, minor tweaks to enemy placement and new small pieces of the map opened up, expect to see the same maps a lot.- On the easy side of stealth games, especially when reaching the higher levels and opening up more abilities- AI can be questionable at times, especially in their yellow "aware but not quite alerted" state- Minor bugs such as the FPS limiter not properly working when set to 60FPS and mouse sensitivity glitching out after conversations (note: opening the ability wheel fixes this)Bad:- Performance on certain maps can tank, nothing unplayable but there are certainly dips on some of the bigger maps- No key rebinding (apparently being worked on but, atleast at the time of writing, not ingame)- The story is (atleast imo) meh and most missions more feel like side missions in any other game- Currently on launch face to face combat is near-unplayable when playing as a client in someone else's game due to extreme desync, stealth has no issues with this though and feels great-

_childDocuments_.review: When i first started playing this game i had a bug that stopped me from knocking out or killing enemies after i fixed the issue (cap your frame rate to 60), I have to say i really like this game. _childDocuments_.review: I loved Aragami. It was one of my first games and still one of my favourites to this day. The art was great, the skills were interesting to explore and try out, the way combat worked with everyone being one-hit was brilliant. While it was meant to be stealth, it was fun just to run trough and see how many people you could get with the given mobility. And I think the mobility was awesome. Just being able to teleport to shadows made interesting level design possible. I was hyped for Aragami 2. So I avoided all spoilers, I did not want to know anything. And recently it was on sale and I bought it. I expected Aragami but with new features, new abilities, maybe some new enemy types. What did I get? A game which looked worse and felt worse. It implemented aragami features like the shadow dash. But only to certain places or as a dash with a set distance. Not a tool to carefully maneuver the level and trick enemies. As soon as I saw the health bar, I was disappointed. I wanted aragami. Not another combat game. And I got to the first real fight. At that point, I realized they just made a cheap version of Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice. Dont get me wrong, love that game too. But it just felt way more sluggish and generally worse. Lince works, I love Aragami. So please, give us more Aragami. Other people can make Souls-likes

_childDocuments_.review: Fans of the first Aragami be warned: this is a VERY different kind of game. Still fun, but different. Whereas the first was relatively restrained and had much slower-paced gameplay, Aragami 2 goes absolutely tennis balls to the walls in terms of giving you the ultimate ninja power fantasy: teleport all over the place, assault enemies from any angle, summon shadows to distract or kill your enemies, *become completely invisible* (which I always feel is cheating in a stealth game) - you're a ninja in the Naruto sense of the term, AKA 'YER A WIZARD HARRY'.Despite being nominally a 'stealth' game, there are very few sections where you're forced to be stealthy: your basic movement abilities are so ridiculous (jump, double jump, dash, mid-air dash, teleport to ledge) and the levels so open that you can usually bypass enemies completely - or else get the drop on them with no chance for them to retaliate. You can limit your power usage and play oldschool cover-to-cover stealth if you really want to, but it seems to me like the devs wanted Aragami 2 to feel more like a sandbox than a stealth game - and you certainly do get a lot of freedom with all your unlockable powers and ninja tools.Aragami 2 takes a very different approach to level design than its predecessor. Rather than a linear sequence of different levels, 2 has a dozen or so more open levels that you keep revisiting in different missions - which is fine because the levels have different start points, objective areas, enemy positions and routes depending on the mission, such that playing different missions in the same level still feels fresh - although after a while you will start to notice the same kinds of mission cropping up again and again. Still, the level design is good: each level has its own distinct theme that affects the challenges you'll face there, there are lots of little hidden nooks for you to explore (usually with some kind of reward for finding them) and you are often rewarded for creative pathfinding (hint: always consider the vertical option). If you push your movement abilities to their limit you can cover some insane distances, so play around and see what you can do. If you find yourself thinking 'Can I reach that ledge from here?', the answer is usually yes.The game has multiplayer and customisable avatars if you're into that kind of thing, and I can certainly see how this might be fun to mess around in with a couple of friends, executing perfectly planned simultaneous strikes or (far more likely) running around in a blind panic causing chaos wherever you go. But I haven't done any of that, so I can't comment on it - same goes for the somewhat Sekiro-ish combat. Call me a stick in the mud if you like, but Aragami is a stealth game and that's how I'mma play it.Like the first Aragami it has a slightly janky charm to it: it's fun and achieves what it sets out to do, despite not being the most polished product. I've encountered a few small bugs, like vaulting over a wall while carrying someone puts you in a drifting repeated vaulting animation until you press the drop button, which is probably not intended behaviour but certainly gave me a good laugh. Then of course there's the weird decision to use a Simlish equivalent of Japanese as the language spoken by the characters in the game, despite many of the names being Japanese and, well, it being a ninja game set in a faux Sengoku era fantasy world. If you're gonna go weeb, why not go FULL weeb in true Ghost of Tsushima fashion? I guess the devs didn't have enough money to hire a full time Japanese translator, or just wanted to focus on the gameplay? Not that it really matters, since the writing isn't the strong point of the game anyway. The devs gave me a full set of magical teleporting wizard ninja powers to abuse and that's exactly what I'm going to do. I hope you will too.

_childDocuments_.review: Game removed all of the fun parts from the first game and added a bunch of bugs and a weak fight system. Will admit the aesthetics are reasonably pleasing but lacks the darkness of the original which is kinda core to the gameedit: Having played some more from when I wrote the review and having gotten used to the movement a bit, there are a few mechanics that I prefer in the new one such as, aerial kills are now a lot more satisfying as you must jump before the option to kill comes up. however, I don't really understand the direction of the game, the idea as far as I am aware is we are a shadow creation, and yet we are working to make a living, what kind of shadow creature needs grain? and unlike the first game shadows seem to have very little to do with the game apart from making it harder to see you, ie. no shadow teleportation etc.I am also not a particularly big fan of the two lives business - either make it you only have one life to beat the mission or you have checkpoints like the original, but that is a minor detail.Also NEVER jump while carrying an enemy as you may float off into the distance and have to reset the whole level by quitting or having a coop teammate lose on purpose to restart.I would say this could be considered a good game in its own right if it had not been labelled as a successor to the first game as it makes little sense to do so given the difference is like night and day.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great but i dont like the direction they took some stuff in. For example they removed the iconic teleport/blink from the last game and now its just a leap that only works on ledges and a dash which is cool i guess. They added more ui to this game which wasnt as unique as in the original, in aragami 1 you would have a cape that would show you how much shadow essence you got and how many times you can use your powers. Also they removed the shadow mechanic where you need stay in shadow to recharge your essence the only reason the shadow exists is to make you invisible which i wasnt a huge fan of. The story was downgraded from the first game like dont get me wrong the first game didnt have a blockbuster story either but it was more enjoyable and actually made sense, however in aragami 2 story is all over the place. Although some parts of the story can be interesting at times for example where the game teaches you about the aragami race and where they came from. Besides that the only other negative thing i can think of is some of the missions get a bit repetitive. But wait after all of that why do i recommend this game? Simple, its fun the movement is fluid the combat is only used as a last resort stealth system is lowkey better than the entire assassins creed franchise (take the profitsoft) if you enjoyed the first game you will enjoy this one try it you will hate it at first but this game grows on you after some time.

_childDocuments_.review: As it's own game, I can recommend it (after a few hotfixes for several bugs regarding ledges, stamina and combat), but it is definitely a far cry from the original. It introduces a slight talent tree that adds to the game, but that's about it. The stealth system is too buggy, and when you go to kill an enemy in stealth it's a toss up if you'll kill them or get attacked while you're in mid animation. All in all, it's a fine ninja game when you get past the bugs, but it's not a game I'd compare to the original.
_childDocuments_.name: Aragami 2

_childDocuments_.review: Aragami 2, a sequel of the first game Aragami. My overall experience is great with this game but somehow I think it lacks in content. But we'll get to those later, for now let's talk about stories and stuffs.The story sets in hundreds of years after the first game, with only a little bit of connection between them. The general characteristics of an Aragami has been rewritten, losing some characteristics from the first game. But that's no issue, since everything can change after time passes. The overall story is nice, with a little twist here and there and there are also some wrenching moments as well. So yeah, for me I felt like the main story is pretty good.The game truly allow us to build our own character, whether it's appearance or ability we are able to customise them to our hearts content. Whether is head-on attacks or stealth based the game got you covered. This make the game much easier than the first, but much more fun too so I guess it's worth the trade-off. I liked this game more than the first as it provides more freedom than the first (aerial movement, dashes, chain-kill and etc).Now onto the lacks in content part, I felt like they could've release more story contents, like how they did it for the first game. In case if you don't know, the first game has a DLC campaign which brings out new story prior to the events. I mean why don't they do it here? Why not release a DLC with a story prior or after the events? I always liked DLCs like these which introduce new maps, new characters, new storylines and let the players know what happens after the main story. Since we received other updates on difficulty and several stuff like classic mode, I felt like my comments before sounds a bit greedy. But you know what? I don't care, I want more and if they release stuff like those I will happily buy it. Overall, the game is good. Like real good, but I wish we have more content.
_childDocuments_.name: Aragami 2

_childDocuments_.review: Even though i did have a fun time with this game during Co-op sessions, i can't recommend this to anybody.The Combat feels like it's in early alpha stages at best and is easily broken if you play co-op.Missions just consist of listening in on guards talking, rescuing someone, grabbing intel or taking out a target. This gets boring real fast as the game has you play several areas many times over, all of which are kinda just okay levels.This leads me to one of the biggest disappointments, the skill tree. The skills are lackluster at best and just feel like a ploy to get you level up as much as possible. Also, Stamina is lost while wondering around the Hub area of the game which is really annoying, especially considering how far apart everything is.
_childDocuments_.name: Aragami 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game -- but definitely more fun for co-op. And it's no sequel to Aragami 1.There's less strategy, less "puzzles", less thinking in general -- it's sekiro combat, metal gear solid style stealth ("!"), and a lot of fetch-questing. The story is worse (Aragami 1 had a weird, quirky story line that I actually enjoyed -- this was a little boring in comparison), and parrying as a non-host is impossible in co-op.However, the maps are larger, speed runs are more fun (trying to find the best path to do everything, and to get the "no-kill/never-seen" or "kill everyone" without triggering too much combat), collectibles are enjoyable to find, and there's enough (though repetitive) content to grind through to sink over 20 hours in.I think it deserves the mixed review, but I enjoyed it and recommend it. 3 player co-op is also pretty cool though I never tried it.

_childDocuments_.review: Games direction is confusing.The combat is janky and is just annoying to deal with.The new changes to mobility from the first game to this game add the expectation of more freedom and higher pace of gameplay, funny enough the game punishes you for using the new mobility changes and you no longer have shadow step which was a focal point of the first game but you can now only teleport to ledges. _childDocuments_.review: I will not say this game has an amazing story or anything over the top but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is it one of the most wonderful multiplayer experiences ever. One of my best friends and I played through every workshop map, story mission, and dlc we could get for the first game and its sequel completely nails the aesthetic in the same way. What is that aesthetic you may ask? _childDocuments_.review: I played the game for 8 hours, but haven't beaten it. I thumbed it down because of one big drawback. The game seems to have stagnated for a long time. The core gameplay as such is actually AMAZING! The movement, the abilities - they're all very cool. The first 3 hours of the game I absolutely LOVED. Then it all got samey. By this, I mean the environments are a mix of 2-3 areas, with just the placement of buildings rearranged. This is the only reason I found myself not wanting to play the game anymore. And I recently 100% AC: Origins, so take that for what you will. AC: Origins, not only had a prettier world, but it had the "Wow" factor going for itself in regular intervals with a story that actually gripped me. Aragami 2 has better gameplay than it for sure, but it just doesn't pull me in enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Very different from the first game, which I really enjoyed. But does it's own thing well enough that I don't mind. There aren't enough out there imo.Runs like native on Linux with proton GE too, which is always a big plus to me :)

_childDocuments_.review: For all the problems of the buggy launch, looking forward to this game for a long time turned out to be 100% worth it. Linceworks is scratching a 'stealth-action' itch I can't find anywhere, and I've gotten a lot of my friends to buy and enjoy the game despite the bugs. I'm currently playing through the campaign solely with friends and though the story is a bit much to keep up with, we know who we're allied with, we know who the stabbable bastards are, and that ever the two shall meet.Will update this review once I finish the game.Update after finishing the game:For the fantastic second-by-second gameplay, the boss was unfortunately a walk in the park marred by unskippable cutscenes of a shady enemy being quite literally Pain from Naruto Shippuden but slightly edgier. The overall escalation of the game from start to finish offers a very nice scaling in difficulty and I absolutely enjoyed the game through and through. _childDocuments_.review: Aragami 2 is a pretty good stealth game, that's about all I can say about it. Be warned it is a significant deviation from the first. It much more closely relates to the likes of Shadow of Mordor or Assassins Creed. In fact, I would consider Aragami 2 not a sequel but rather another game entirely, set in the same world. Lore wise, they are likely a significantly apart in time.I'd recommend picking this up on a sale.It does have nice additions from the first, such as more robust character customization and more options for how to build your character skill and stat-wise. The game is roughly twice as  long as the first, ignoring collectibles/replaying missions. The new movement system and combat is rather fun to master.However, there are a fair amount of downsides, like bugs and lack of music (What is there is beautiful though). My greatest complaint, other then deviating from the first so much, is that missions repeat the same level and enemy layouts (But with different mission starting points), which is a huge downgrade from the first which had better and more carefully crafted levels. This causes the story to take a hit as well, as lore is mostly covered in-between levels rather then in the moment.Overall, the game is a fine stealth game. You will be disappointed if you go in expecting an experience more like the first Aragami.

_childDocuments_.review: Aragami is back, and this time, you spend some time in the haven, where you accept missions, use portal to get to the mission, do it, and then you use a portal to get back to the haven. I know what you are thinking, this is the exact same gameplay as Doom Eternal! So, to help avoid confusion, I will tell you a simple way how to distinguish between these two games. In one of them you are a total hardcore badass that rips and tears through the enemies, and in the other you play as the Doom Guy.I bet some of you already read some of the negative reviews for this game. If you didn't, let me sum them up for you:And it is true. This game feels a bit less like the pureblooded sequel of the original. More like a love child of Aragami, Tenchu, and Mark of the Ninja. So, if you love these games, you will definitely find a place in your heart for Aragami 2.This time around you can make the Aragami your own. You will have access to various masks, armors, weapons and colors, making him more unique and personal.At the end of each level you are rated based on your performance. There are bonus points for avoiding detection, and then a bonus for not killing anyone or killing all the enemies. Thanks to that there is no option to knock out your enemy without killing him.Weirdly enough, Aragami 2 is probably the only game where finishing the mission without a single kill is way easier than killing everyone, because you don't have to traverse the whole map, looking for every poor soul in all the weird places.I have noticed some of the reviews call this game "linear", a vulgar word for any game except Call of Duty, right? Problem is that Aragami 2 isn't really that linear. You have to do missions in certain order, but often you will get more than one mission and then the sequence is up to you. And during the mission there is no predetermined path to take, it's up to you how you will handle the task, what path you will take, how much you will roam around, etc.A skill "tree" is available, tree being a bit funny word to use here, it works more like a building. You have one floor of the building with skills unlocked and more points you will put to those skills, more floors with more skills you will unlock. Each skill is unique, but yet useful. You won't find yourself wasting points on needless skills just because you need to unlock more skills, every skill has use and you will love using each one you unlock.As for the variety of the skills, there is your common stuff: Invisibility, shadow killing, creating shadow dopplegangers, etc. And also some more tactical skills like seeing the path the enemy took or the path the enemy is about to take.One of the most useful skills is probably the Whisper, skill that allows you to attract enemies towards your position, separating them from the herd and dealing with them privately. I definitely recommend not only unlocking this skill, but also upgrading it early on, as it will allow you to target Whisper on individual enemies and not all enemies nearby.Yup, there is equipment now. Shurikens, sleeping/stun darts, poison darts, smoke bombs, health potions, etc. Using these is the key to success, especially considering the combat system.You remember that time in the original Aragami that you got discovered and then had about 1 second of life left? Not anymore. Now you can take multiple hits and enemies usually attack from close, they don't possess the one projectile hit instakill anymore. Combat system itself is similar to the games like Sekiro and it takes some skill to take the enemy down in direct combat. But beware, if there are multiple enemies, it is super easy to die, either from enemies or from taking the fall damage after you try to escape with an ounce of life left. Thankfully you have now 2 lives for each mission. You die once, and you recover at the closest checkpoint with all the mission progress saved. Die second time and you have to restart the mission.Thankfully even multiple enemies at once are not a problem once you learn the mechanics and once you start using your skills and equipment to their fullest.

_childDocuments_.review: Big BIG downgrade from Aragami 1. I was very dissapointed!!!You are better off buying the 1st one.It seems it wasn't made by the same people. The best aspect of the game which was to move in stealth in shadows, and find a way to traverse the level and go behind enemies in clever ways, was made into a mode and very poorly implemented.The game is way brighter with no much contrast between shadows and light, which makes sense, since It doesn't matter if you are a shadow warrior now, you just parkour. What was your target audience...5 year-olds on consoles?The maps look VERY staged, poorly designed and fake.Not even gonna discuss the enemies who do very obvious routes so you kill them in a specific way. And also are totally blind, can't see more than 20 meters or so.Parkour is worse. Controls say "climb UP" on the window when you are hanging, but you cant stand on the window ledge, it forces you on the other side and drops you down. There is no interesting story-line like before, you just do missions, and you go to a boring old guy to give you skills.Graphics are worse, only the character model is better, but all other enemies and characters are identical twins and boring.There's mountains clipping on each other if you see at the end of the map.Try running and fighting enemies while jumping, physics on the game will make you float over enemies head, and also you get hit even if you are in the air jumping away.Take away the stupid combat, bring back the devs who made the first one.There also is this weird map borders that make you feel like you are in an arena, couldn't settle for natural environment borders? Get the Aragami 1 you'll love it. This one is bad.Stay away, complete waste of money!!!I think the devs just wanted to push something out with focus on multiplayer. Whose ever decision that was from the company, just know you failed, and everyone can see that.Thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not the first one. NOT EVEN CLOSE!In the first Aragami, if you were seen, you generally died. You had all kinds of ways to keep from being seen, but if you were, that was often it. Game over but the shouting. It was  a very hard core stealth experience with a massive learning curve and for those of us who enjoy skulking in the shadows, it was epic!This game is different. This sequel's art style is similar, but not quite the same. Lore wise, it has very little to do with the first game. (No spoilers here) You can stealth through levels and leave nothing but the occasional unconscious guard in your wake. Or you can draw your sword and cut a bloody swath through the horde. I TRULY do not recommend trying that at low levels, fair warning!!!This game is different, but from what I have seen, it is fun. I play as a true stealth aficionado. If I am seen or have to kill anyone but my target, I consider that a failed mission. I have yet to be able to play through without even knocking any enemies out, but I think it can be done.I am not done with the campaign yet and I will probably update this review after I finish, but for now, the ONLY problem I have with this game is technical. There are screen tearing issues, guards who teleport, pathing issues both enemy and character, and a few other interesting things here and there.  That said? If you truly want to play as a shadow essence ninja, this game will give it to you. Not perfect, but darned good for any of us who dream of being ninjas.Haven't tried co-op yet. Sort of looking forward to that, sort of not. In my experience, the Internet hates us all equally.(VERY frustrated edit after several more hours of playing) Okay, this game is not hard even for pure stealth runs WHEN IT WORKS. When it doesn't work, it is impossible. Stealth is sort of working, sort of not. Enemies all the way across the map hear you when you kill an enemy, but enemies right beside you do not. Corner attacks where you grab an enemy just as they pass a corner, work about 1/2 the time. Sometimes they see you (and chase you down and kill you!) when you are invisible, sometimes not. Sometimes Whisper acts as if it isn't upgraded and pulls everyone in the area, sometimes it works fine. If it wasn't so blasted random, it wouldn't be NEARLY as frustrating. It can be fun, but ONLY when it works.

_childDocuments_.review: Man, I'm so happy with this game lolTook 40h to finish everything (story, collectibles, etc)TLDR: - Extremely charming art and world and a nice simple story.  - Stealth gameplay on "Hard" is challenging enough thanks to the stamina bar and enemy AI (decent!!) - Online Co Op works well even across the planet (friends from Hong Kong and LA) and provides a really cool experience that opens up more aggressive and creative routes through levels that are not as viable in solo play.  - If you want an Assassin's Creed stealth experience, with Sekiro's ninja fun, and without the Ubisoft bloat of AC games, this is the PERFECT game for that.- The price is extremely fair :D

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a major departure from the original that might have upset a large number of fans of the original but definitely felt amazing to play for me. It's faster, snappier, it features a combat system that allows you to recover against a single enemy while struggling against many, making it somewhat of a perfect feature to implement to a stealth action game. In fact, some of the most fun I've had in this game wasn't just planning and perfectly executing a plan, it's the times that I mess up and end up getting chased by a small horde of enemies. I end up having to use all my abilities and tools to my advantage which is simply great game design.My gripes are mainly that the original had level structures that allow for traversal itself to become a puzzle which added to the challenge of stealth. Finding out where to go and how to get there was part of the fun of the original. It's something that doesn't appear nearly as much in this game which takes more of a far cry style of planning then attacking a settlement approach.As for other things, I'm really not a fan of hearing fake japanese in a very japanese inspired game. Whenever you hear someone speak, it just sounds like a japanese version of simlish. Some words sound right and then it's followed up with jibberish.I'm not too fond of the way the game handles ledge teleporting sometimes. It's great most of the time cause it works most of the time. It's very fun running and jumping then saving yourself by teleporting to a ledge, but the game never properly conveys when you can't teleport to a ledge so sometimes you take that risk and end up falling for it.As for minor gripes, the customisation sucks. Dyes have four colours and one of them, you can't choose cause it's the default colour. Much prefer a colour wheel. And the amount of customisation that I've gotten so far isn't that numerable.Overall: I love this game. It's a pure encapsulation of the phrase "Diamond in the rough". And I was sad to hear that the studio isn't gonna be able to make anymore games. I hope this gets the cult classic status it deserves. Aragami 1 and 2 both deserve it.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought my friend and I a copy of this game as we both loved the first game and this sequel is a massive improvement. I do have some negative feedback and hope that the devs may see it and fix the issues. Aragami 2 has three player co-op unlike the first which was only two player and has an immense amount of detail and upgrades/gear. The stealth is really fun, although I loved the "Shadow System" in the first, I do really enjoy the knockout and kill with the shadow dashing and shadow leaping. I feel as though this game was heavily inspired by the decent and original Tenchu games which is one of the key reasons I got into and love stealth games. The combat system although it may not be, it feels like it tried to be like Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice. That's not a bad thing though as it has been pulled off well and enjoyable when I want to mess around instead of playing seriously and being a sneaky boy. I highly recommend this to stealth fans and fans of games like Sekiro, Tenchu, Splinter Cell and Metal Gear. It has a lot of replay value thus far as just under four hours I am only on mission 8 (Collectable hunting, getting all three awards and S rank) and seems to be many more missions ahead. Okay. So I hope this gets read or passed on and maybe these are known issues, bugs or connection errors. Also, a few ideas are noted.- Mission boundaries break in CO-OP mode for the client so they can reach out of bound areas and collect statues for areas further on in the game. - The De-sync issues with CO-OP can make the game very hard. Client can't attack, use items, gets detected across the map or through walls even though crouched or standing still and the combat is near-on impossible as a client. - Game lobby in CO-OP breaks and soft-locks if you jump in the water behind the quest board in the village as a mission is about to start and you infinitely get stuck teleporting back from land to air and can't move nor does the mission start. - Some enemies don't spawn on screen at a certain range or camera angle (if it's tilted to the right etc) or until you get closer to them. Encountered this as the host of a two player CO-OP game on numerous occasions (i.e: Mission 2, 3, 5 and 7 specifically for me). - Add a description whether or not the armour and gear pieces such as headgear, torso, legs and sword have an effect on armour rating, stealth, damage and noise. - Add a keybinding for the cover system. Not everyone likes sticky cover (if that's what people still call it).- Add a keybinding for individual powers. Personally and my friend thinks the same, it isn't the best for some people to have a "next" and "previous". I would love to be able to tap "1" and equip my Kunai's then press "3" to equip the Amnesia needles etc. - Add additional knockout take-down animations. I personally love and prefer to do non-lethal runs but it is tiring seeing the same animation every time. Maybe a variation, an aerial knockout looks different to a sneak from behind. Thank you anyhow. Great job thus far and I am enjoying the game. Appreciate the love put into this and hope we see some future DLC. Edit: Playing on Beta version which is more stable than the live version. Patch 1.0.27899.0 Beta.

_childDocuments_.review: Aragami 2 is nothing like Aragami 1. Other than a similar main character design and some teleporting mechanics, just about everything else is different.The original Aragami was tough. Every kill you made had to be methodical, and you only had small windows to do so. Guards actually paid attention to their surroundings. It was stealth only, or die. The shadow mechanic also made it enjoyable; stick to the shadows and avoid bright lights, lest you lose your teleporting powers. And the better you got at the game, the quicker and more precise you could teleport around the map, making you feel like a real ninja.And abilities while powerful, were limited to 3 uses each time. You could not simply abuse them because they wouldn't recharge automatically.On top of that, the world in Aragami felt vibrant, and the story actually at least made some sense.In Aragami 2 however, everything that made the original great is now gone. You can no longer perform long range teleports (unless it's to a rooftop or cliff). Shadow is now automatically recharged via a generic stamina bar. Abilities also simply refresh on a timer. No longer do you need to care whether you're standing in the light or dark. As a matter of fact, you can simply crouch and walk around because the guards are all short sighted. You can have guards literally staring in your direction and you can kill a guard in full view and not alert them, so long as there's some distance between you and them. You can also abuse teleporting to rooftops without ever having to worry about finding ways to recharge your stamina, since the shadow gauge is no longer a thing.Oh and if you get caught by a guard? Who cares? Just button mash him to death with your sword since they die in 3 hits (you don't even need to parry because they attack so slow and are straight up just weaker than you), or teleport up to a nearby rooftop since your stamina recharges so quickly. The best part? You can engage in direct combat with a guard, and you won't even attract the attention of other nearby guards unless they have a direct line of sight on you; they're all hard of hearing.And say you choose to teleport away, the guard chasing you won't even alert other guards to your presence. Instead, they just mindlessly run about trying to look for you, before giving up and returning to their original posts as if nothing ever happened. No heightened alert, nothing. Oh we had an assassin in our midst? Oh well nevermind, out of sight out of mind. And if that didn't make things easy enough, you can now carry bodies and hide them in bushes that just so happen to be everywhere! You no longer have to worry about where you kill any of your targets at all! But oh wait, there's more to make the game even easier! You can now very conveniently look through walls to see guards whenever you like, at absolutely no cost whatsoever!Also, goodbye air and teleport assassinations. It's hilarious that the tutorial describes air assassinations as being a thing, when it's really just you jumping, landing, and then performing a regular kill on land. Seriously, aren't stealth games supposed to be at least somewhat challenging? Aragami 2 even hilariously gives you potions to heal yourself, and I never once found any need to use them in the 4 missions that I played. What is this watered down crap?And while I do like that you can jump and even double jump and consider it an improvement to the original game, it doesn't really add any real variation to missions, albeit making it more convenient to get over short ledges.I played 4 missions and despite them having "different" objectives, they're pretty much the same at its core. There are no differences between assassinating a target, marking barrels, or collecting items since you employ the exact same approach for all of them. It's just a matter of killing guards with dumb AI, and roaming around a map that feels lifeless. And yes, Aragami 1 was also about assassinating many targets. But you know what made that experience exciting? The level design! There were many scenarios in the original in which multiple guards were stationed in a way where they had clear view of one another, which meant that you had to find ways to pick them off one by one, or use cool abilities to kill multiples of them in one go.In Aragami 2 however? The guards appear to be stationed pretty much randomly with little to no thought behind their placement. Some guards just stand still and stare into places where you wouldn't even need to traverse. Virtually no finesse or planning is required to pick off enemies at all.No, Aragami 2 does not have improved graphics; it just uses very typical 3D looking models as opposed to the old cel-shading graphics, which while isn't horrible, isn't at all to my liking. Something about it just feels off and cheap, like as if this were a parody rendered game seen on Family Guy.- To pick up items, close tooltips, or upgrade abilities, you gotta tediously hold down the interact button. Most games learned their lesson and got rid of this crap; eg Assassins Creed.- Cosmetics aren't earned via achievements like in Aragami 1, but are bought using otherwise mostly pointless currency that are randomly scattered around maps.If you've never played the original Aragami, I suppose Aragami 2 isn't a bad game. If you're a fan of the original however, this game is a massive disappointment. Perhaps Lince Works felt the original's difficulty prevented other players from enjoying it, but to make Aragami 2 this pathetically dull and watered down is a total crying shame.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun, brutal, and hilarious. Hilarious with friends, anyway. Highly recommended, especially if you have a friend or two tag along with you. Just beware: the swordfighting is not as easy as the gameplay trailers make it look! You have to get really good at parrying, or else you'll get slaughtered. Best to stick to stealth kills/knockouts for your first few hours of the game, if not your entire time playing.Edit: Finished the game co-op. In conclusion: Story meh, gameplay great with some bugs here and there. When I say some, I mean some that are frequent, while there are many that are rare. The game does reuse a lot of environments for later missions, but they mix up the objectives, enemy placements, and enemy types to where it's not shameless at all. There are tons of powers, with my favorite being Shadow Kill. It made me say SHADOW KILL out loud to my friends whenever I used it. Is it worth the price? Co-op, absolutely. Single player....mmmmmmmmaybe. You might want to wait for a price drop if you won't be playing with anyone else, and trust me you'll want to play with friends not randoms. Stealth games with randoms sounds like hell.With lots of character customization, powers, mobility, and co-op potential, this game is an easy 8/10 or higher for me. One thing I would improve aside from getting rid of certain bugs and glitches is the swordfighting. It's a little clunky especially in co-op. For some reason I always had issues with hit detection during sword fighting during co-op, to where my strikes would just pass thru enemies, dealing little to no damage, while they deal full damage to me. Another thing I'd change is how detection works in co-op. For some reason, if one of your pals gets seen, you are also seen, in the sense that you can't stealth kill someone from behind while they're fighting/chasing one of your friends. Why not? We're ninjas. We use distractions, even those such as a person leading enemies into a trap to be backstabbed. You could do this in Splinter Cell Conviction but not in this game unfortunately. Co-op: Full price. Single player: Maybe wait for a discount.

The rank s follow the same line, but I found it a little strange to kill some enemies in an area, be seen and get this rank in the end, as well as the difficulty that the most difficult method seemed to me sometimes continue to be the easy (seemed to me kind of unbalanced). _childDocuments_.review: Ill give some pros/cons and comparisons bewteen the gamesPros: -New combat system where when youre caught its more of a battle you have to fight instead of getting knocked back and killed instantly.-Versatility in kills can range between knock outs and killing out right, but can now be done from a jump teleport and depending on height is how loud the kill/ko is, quite fun to play with-New AI is pretty cool, theyre now able to jump over and off fences to chase you down and check out noises. do note the can jump up and down back and forth so tricking the AI is barely a thing anymore,Cons:-Brand new movement is strange, no more teleporting shadow to shadow to avoid detection, its now a shadow roll like 2 feet then your visible and sprinting after the roll. hard to get used to after playing the first game-Teleportation itself is a hassle now, it seems like the only thing you get to teleport too is ledges that your usually seen doing-Detection is incredibly fast for a stealth game, they will spot you and start attacking you within 1.5 seconds and without an instant teleport into safety its just about impossible to avoid detection when youre first caught out-Combat AI/Targeting Combat is really not fun or intresting, you kinda just take on one at a time while fliping back and forth between enemys to see which one is winding up the longest attack known to man.-Graphics look like theyre pulled straight out of unity engine. They abandoned the first games semi-ink style to replace it with what looks kinda like rough plastic action figures-Stamina is one of the worst things they added, just about everything takes stamina, Teleporting, running, rolling, combat in entirety and if you get caught up in a fight and lose all your stamina get ready for the biggest whirlwind of your life because the enemies will straight up combo 2/3 of your hp while your character sits there like he has Carl Wheezers asthma -THERES FALL DAMAGE-Stealth kills/KO Animations are almost the exact same no matter what, where, or who youre doing them toComparatively: This game shares almost 0% of what the first game was, where as the first game you would want to find out a way to get rid of everyone in a very fast strategic method as in this game you kinda just throw youself into combact and murder everyone by parrying. Stamina has taken place of shadow usage and will regain no matter if your in the light or hidden in shadow but runs out faster than you would ever expect of a combat systemGame is still fun with friends, but thats usually the case with any multiplayer gameTL;DR: Its a fun game so far, but you shouldnt play this because you loved the first one, you are sadly mistaken if you think this will be anything like it. It kinda feels like your just a Warrior with teleportation

_childDocuments_.review: AI is incredibly busted sometimes, and some of the games mechanics don't always work they way they are supposed to. This game needs a lot of bug fixes and updates before it is fully playable.The game also takes wayyyyy too long to actually level up your character. After 10 hours of gameplay, I have a total of 2 abilites. Just 2. And this game doesn't even let you fully upgrade your character. It tries to be something it isn't by making you have a limited number of skill points and having to make "builds". Despite the game only having a handful of skills to choose from to begin with. Also, it doesn't even have a matchmaking system. So, if you didn't bring your own friends, it is a strictly single player game. This game also seems to have a hard time deciding what ledges you can actually grab. A large portion of the game is being able to quickly ascend large buildings to get away and plan your next attack. But sometimes a roof is too slanted and your character can't grab onto the ledge, or in some cases, you CAN grab the ledge. But in those cases, you often get stuck and can't pull yourself up.Overall, the gameplay can be pretty fun sometimes. Slicing through enemies and disappearing around corners, or knocking out gaurds and hiding their bodies in a safe spot so they aren't spotted. But all too often the game falls apart and doesn't let you do what you want to.

_childDocuments_.review: A solid indie game in my book! It's probably a hot take, but I actually enjoyed the changes made for Aragami 2. Ranging from gameplay to (some) lore, it was nice to see the devs play around with this world & if there's ever an Aragami 3 - I do hope some elements carry over & maybe even mix in with the first!Going into the mechanics, as I stated it was a fun approach. Mixing up my skills & runes based on how I felt like completing a mission really helped break up some of the repetitiveness of levels, especially since I would often go back to grab any collectibles I missed, secure an S rank, or fill out one of the 3 (or, i suppose now with Classic mode, 4) badges. I do think the demon/combat "class" could have been worked on some more, as this is a game that penalizes you for being discovered & you can't really get to that corner unless you're seen from the start of the mission. For how the stealth factor was handled, I feel as if it wasn't as harsh a change as some make it out to be; I found it more fun to experiment how I'd get around a certain area as compared to one, though I will admit - I missed being able to just jump into nearby shadows. However, it wasn't such an issue that it ruined my playthrough.NPC wise, I thought the little community the MC ended up in was really enjoyable! I found myself talking to them after every mission to see if there was anything new, and while there wasn't most times, it still felt nice to go around and say hi when I could. If there is any DLC for this game, I would love to see more dialogue! Especially for Danjuro. Honestly just give me a DLC focusing on him. Also a pink dye, please. <3Aragami 2 isn't perfect; the bugs (while being worked on!) did make story & current 100% completion progress a bit tedious, as I said earlier - the levels can get a little repetitive, and there were just some parts of the story that didn't land as well as the initial conflict you're faced with at the start of the game. But in the end, I still found it enjoyable to play through & these issues never got in the way of that. If you're looking for a quick game to casually play or just want to add something different to your library, I'd personally recommend this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I got gifted this game for PS5 shortly after buying it but couldn't refund it. Nonetheless I played it to completion, so disregard to tiny playtime lolAs a kid I was an avid fan of the Sly Cooper games. If you're not familiar, they're a quadrilogy of stealth-action 3D platformers themed as a comic noir type story. They're incredibly fun games and I sincerely recommend them, especially if you liked this game.Anyhow that leads me to my main point. I've long been on a crusade of sorts to find a game that would invoke that same action-stealth-platforming hybrid that seemingly no other game besides Sly has ever pulled off. Playing this game was like the moment in Ratatouille where the food critic gets a flashback to eating his mother's cooking as a child. It's like a smartly crafted hybrid of both Sly Cooper and a little bit of Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice, with just the tiniest sprinkle of Hitman thrown in for good measure.My only strong critiques are that the controls overall are a tad bit clunky (especially the combat, but from certain perspectives that could be argued as actually quite good game design), the environments are slightly samey, and there's no New Game Plus to encourage a full playthrough with all the cool abilities you unlock during the course of the game.Conclusion: Aragami 2 is one of my favorite games I've ever played. I'm in the middle of my second playthrough and having a blast just like I did the first time. Worth every penny you pay, worth every second you spend with it.Rest easy, Lince Works. I hope the extraordinary talent you once had has found steady employment elsewhere, they deserve the world after this masterpiece

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of the first game, I was very excited to run through the campaign with my friend as we did before.This game was such a disappointment. It lost every single ounce of the charm that the first game had. The first game was simple, unique, engaging, and, while lacking in the depth of its narrative, it shone through because it strove to be a clean, fun game about bouncing between shadows and executing stealth kills.This game was none of that. It was ENTIRELY too long--it overstayed its welcome at least twofold. The worst part about its length is that it was so artificial. You run through the same levels over and over until you're sick of playing the game. The combat system was entirely unnecessary, and such a tragic mistake on the part of the developers--in multiplayer, only the host as any chance of actually successfully parrying attacks, or, even more disappointing, even knowing what the hell is going on in the first place. The person joining the host can just swing at an engaged enemy over and over again to no avail, and then suddenly get killed by a swing that you never had a chance to block (not that you even could with how poor the desync/net code was). The narrative felt so forced and it was impossible to find any way to feel attached to any of the characters because they were so bland. The first game's lack of a real narrative didn't act as a detraction from the games value, but some how everything they included in the second game only drew away from what was supposed to have been a fun, engaging experience.This is a classic example of developers biting off more than they can chew. It tried to do everything except build upon the foundation that made the first game great, and none of the other things it tried to do came together in any cohesive way that left a good taste in my mouth. It pains me to ♥♥♥♥ on this game, because I really really enjoyed the first one, but the developers made far too many mistakes with the sequel. I really hate how much I didn't enjoy this unfortunately.

_childDocuments_.review: (Review Mid Game (Chap 4), spoilerless)TL:DR ***All*** the polish went into the gameplay. Freedom of movement lets you yeet yourself around the map while knocking people out. Why is parrying so unforgiving? If you're looking for a planed, high-difficulty, sneaky backstabs only where you skulk around in the dark like the Original Aragami, you might be a little disappointed, but if your open to new ideas, this game takes the Aragami foruma and lets you fly with it.The game doesn't show its best cards immediately, the story is unclear and confusing and the combat tutorial just highlights how clunky it is (and you can’t change controls anywhere?). However, it's obvious the time and effort went into polishing the movement and stealth gameplay to high hell rather than giving the story the attention, and the sword fighting is clearly a “In case of emergencies.”', and you're not meant to run into a 1v20 sword fight. Gameplay this thing is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ goldmine for 1 main reason: Freedom of movement. The only ability downgrade we got from OG Aragami is that we can now only teleport to ledges rather than everywhere we want. However, we now have a double jump and a dash, and the importance of shadows has been reduced. Why is this a good thing? Insane movement techs combined with the fact you can knock someone out at any time, in any direction, as long as they're not on full alert, is very very fun. Dash into a jump to soar through the sky and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ BODY some poor dude across the courtyard, teleport to a ledge and smash a dudes skull on the fence, and double jump then dash to get vertical height with your distance to get back to the roof unseen. The game is as fast and flows as quickly as you want it to and it excells at making you feel powerful without being unbalanced. The final note is the note of the “♥♥♥♥♥♥ cascade” where being caught by 1 guard causes all of Japan to know your exact position and tuned it a little too far to the other side of the scale. Guards are blind, dumb and basically never call reinforcements further than 20 meters away. In exchange if you do get caught, they can chase you down basically as fast as you can run unless you're good with teleporting. Treat them more as the game's puzzle pieces than actual guards. Good game. Bring up to 2 friends. Extra tidbits:• Don't look out of bounds too hard. Especially in the capital. • Don't throw important people into black end-of-map voids, they are unrecoverable. • Do throw people off cliffs because it's funny.

_childDocuments_.review: Different sense of pace to the original.  The introduction of a more general purpose stamina bar that covers shadow moves and ledge grabs and the change from 'painting' shadows to create handholds in the original to a narrower ledge grab system take time to get used to, but once you adapt to them they create interesting flexibility as you work your way through areas.  You can also hang from ledges now as a means to avoid detection or get a kill.Aragami 1 has a slower pace with tight AI patterns and not a lot of way to divert enemies while remaining undetected- challenging but rewarding in one way.  Aragami 2 has adjusted this in a few interesting ways with a more open skill tree and then thrown more enemies into more openly designed levels so you can slowly peel armies apart into dark areas and take them out quietly.A combat system that I'm not so fond of has given you an opportunity to fight back if detected, but what's nice is even after you're seen you get a brief moment to either take individual enemies out or use a move that incapacitates them long enough to do so, like throwing an amnesia needle at them or Mesmerize them.  You have to react quickly to pull this off, the game doesn't afford you a slowdown to react aside from bringing up the skill wheel, and even then it's over pretty quick.I'm a little over 20 hours into the game, in Chapter 3, have been playing through each level for pacifist/no detect medals and then immediately playing them over with a kill/no detect mindset instead.  One thing worth noting if you're playing is that the level rank system seems a lot more concerned with detection than with consistency, so if you're going for stealth S rank you don't have to knock out every enemy, completing the objective sight unseen is enough.  That's why when you pause the game you'll see an indicator of how many enemies you've killed, for the Oni medal (kill everyone), but no such indicator for how many enemies you've knocked out.Generally- highly recommended.  I have yet to try co op play yet but I hope to do so in the future, because the levels seem friendly to carving out areas for multiple players without stepping on toes.  In singleplayer this gets a solid endorsement, which if I had stopped at the prologue level I might not have felt as solid about.  If you like the first Aragami, give it some time and adjust to its sense of pacing.  It's different in a way that, having played this far in, I'm a lot more confident is a benefit to the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really torn on this game. On the one hand, hit detection is spotty, I fell through the map numerous times, enemies are inconsistent on if they will or won't see you, maps are reused to an excessive degree, and everything just has a general feel of being rushed and unpolished. On the other, once you get past the initial jankiness of it all, the movement feels really good, late game abilities are satisfying to use, exploration gets easier and more rewarding, and everything starts being really fun. This unfortunately took 20 hours to get to that point, but it's worth it. There is a ton of wasted potential, and it feels nothing like the first game. It really needed more time in development to iron out some annoying hit detection errors and polish up animations and whatnot. Despite all that, there are great ideas you can see working, and fun mechanics that are cool to use. Overall had more fun than not, there's just a lot of frustration to be had before you can get to the fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Aragami 1 and I want to say off the bat that this game should've been called "Aragami: ___" instead of being marketed as a sequel—because it isn't. That aside, I truly think this game is phenomenal and once you get the hang of it definitely an easier stealth game, but what truly makes this game shine is the movement—there is so much fun and fluidity in being able to shadow leap to ledges and in air and the combinations you can pull off with that move set. Regarding Aragami 1's essential mechanic of staying in the shadows/teleporting between them being somewhat absent, the Classic Mode definitely scratches the itch (although you can't place shadows like in the first game, so you're limited to the dark places already on the map (there are a lot, and it honestly works great), and does change up gameplay  to make it different from how Aragami 2 was designed. I wish Lince Works didn't go under after this project because it's apparent that they really liked the concepts they were going for and with more and more refinement could've reached a near-perfect product. I really enjoyed this game despite the few design choices which aren't the best, and also have to commend the devs for doing things like Classic Mode and increasing the level cap post-launch due to player feedback. Highly recommend playing this game, it's a fun take on the stealth genre with a lot of enjoyable gameplay mechanics and abilities, but it's not Aragami 1, or a sequel to it.
