_childDocuments_.name: White Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Overall the game was pretty alright. (I'll do my best not to put spoilers in)Is it worth buying at full price? Depends on what you look for in a game. If you are looking for harder puzzles, this is probably not it. However, if you are looking for a well thought out dystopian story then you're in for a treat. (It has much darker themes than I originally thought it would have so proceed with caution.) Disturbing in the best way :DThe graphics of the game were fitting though sometimes its hard to see your character with everything that's going on. I played with Ultra graphics on a 1920x1080 resolution. It made everything much clearer compared to the default starting settings. I play on a laptop and there were no frame issues with the settings being on "Ultra".The game has no "how to play" prompts during the start; If you've played platformers before, its pretty standard and easy to figure out - there is also a way to check on the Settings tab if you'd prefer. Most of the game is shown through actions, with very little dialogue. The dialogue that is provided comes in the form of advertisements and videos.The game itself is pretty short- at a casual pace including snack breaks it took a little over 3hours. Easy to finish in once sitting. While i was playing i didn't encounter any bugs and the game ran very smoothly, the only issue i did have was in the middle of Chapter 3 where i had to redo it. I made a blunder and died on a jump to a chained hook, when I was respawned i couldn't run at full speed because of the chicks swarming. I tried to get rid of them in different ways but i gave up and just restarted the chapter. (If you end up buying the game you'll see what what part i'm talking about.)-----Final thoughts,  In MY PERSONAL OPINION this game is enjoyable but "meh". I usually buy platformers for the puzzles and the ones White Shadow created were mostly straightforward (which is not a bad thing) with little difficulty.OBJECTIVELY, its well produced. It certainly goes above and beyond what it promises in terms of atmosphere and story.
_childDocuments_.name: White Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: I would have recommended this for fans of Limbo/Inside/Little Nightmares but there was a bug that stopped me from advancing. _childDocuments_.name: White Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: For such a short game, I don't regret any of the money I spent on it. $20 is a bit steep for 2 hours, but the game really does make up for it. It tells so much without a single line of dialog. When it does directly outline things, it does so in a very gut punching way.The story is strange and almost dream like as we move through a setting of a strict ethno-class based society. It does fall a little short in that it mainly shows the consequences of racism and xenophobia where as the people perpetuating it really do more so feel like part of the background with a few rare exceptions. There are a few moments (mainly when a phone is used) that leaves the lack of voice acting particularly noticeable.However, as it stands, as divorced from our own reality as this world might be, the imagery and sound design are spot on enough that I really wish they actually showed more of the world and the consequences of the Wolves' leadership. It feels like we got such a thin slice of this world and the ending leaves the probability of a sequel to be very slim.Expect to spend about 2.5 hours on this. More if you want to try and get 100% completion and, to be honest, this is the kind of game that's worth showing off to friends over a voice call.

_childDocuments_.review: While I'm a fan of puzzle platformers, I'm not someone who feels that one should necessarily emulate other popular examples of the genre. Any complaints I make aren't about whether the game deviates from expectations but on things that affect the game's enjoyment.This game had all the ingredients to be something special. It had an interesting setting and aesthetic.  I was wiling to overlook that parts went beyond mere nods to Animal Farm. In the end, though, it's potential exceeded its results.  First, the game ran slowly. In areas where timing was essential I bottomed out the graphical settings to have a workable if muddied game. This is a real shame as the designs were certainly one of the highlights for me. It was occasionally buggy, including one checkpoint where I kept restoring midfall. I felt too much of the game (especially after chapter 3) was more an extended guided tour than a game with actions.  The exposition dump in the latter half needed more show less tell. Finally the plot itself -- and this may be something that I'm blindly missing -- seemed to have the trappings of deeper meaning without presenting anything beyond that which was already obvious in Animal Farm. I don't mind if a story is open-ended with multiple interpretations, but I'm struggling with one that makes sense from start to finish.I wish the makers of this game the best of luck, and if they make another game I will look it over; though I may decide whether to buy it based on others who play it before me.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm usually not much of a puzzle plattformer player, but I really enjoyed White Shadows. It's a short(ish) game, even though it took me 4+ hours to finish it. The scenery/world is beautifully dystophian, dark and detailed. The classical music fits the gameplay perfectly. I was also really impressed by the few changes of perspective during the game. The game deals with/reflects on real-life issues. So playing White Shadows was sometimes emotional and made me uncomfortable, worried, excited and sad at times. I look forward to more releases from Monokel.
_childDocuments_.name: White Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: White Shadows isn't a perfect game but the developers deserve credit for the thoughtful work they put into this. I guess if you were to make a musical analogy, you might say that "Black and Blue" and "Tattoo You" by the Rolling Stones aren't classic masterpieces like "Beggar's Banquet" or "Exile on Main Street" but they still qualify as being quite good overall. The puzzles in White Shadows aren't too innovative--I can't think of anything here in terms of puzzles that I haven't already seen before in one game or another--but where it really excels is in the world building. This is simply a darkly fascinating, deeply layered world that looks almost like stop motion animation. There's a definite, exquisite sense of cinematography in this game. The old fashioned, classical soundtrack perfectly compliments the action and the story here. Speaking of the story, it's well done throughout--George Orwell's "Animal Farm" is an obvious influence--but I feel that it falters in the final chapter...the ending feels too abrupt and vague. It's feels almost as if they ran out of time and money and didn't provide the game with a well fleshed out ending to the story. Like I said initially, the game isn't perfect but it is a truly interesting piece of art and it's still well worth your time. The developers tried hard with this and deserve credit. Hopefully they do another project that's even better than this! 8 out of 10 stars. One of the ten best games I've played this year,

_childDocuments_.review: Step out of the cuckoo clock and into this monochromatic nightmare of twisting cables and bright signs of propaganda illuminating the world below. ALL ANIMALS ARE EQUAL.This game is an absolute treat. It is visually stunning with dynamic camera movements making the game feel more like a cinematic experience. I don't want to say a lot because one needs to simply experience this game and I highly recommend you do. Stop often. Look at everything and most of all, just enjoy this game. It isn't long, spanning only a couple of hours, but I am grateful I got even that long.Monokel came out with an absolute masterpiece for their first game, great job to all involved.

_childDocuments_.name: White Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: The visuals totally sucked me into wanting to play this game. The theme of the game is for sure something we have seen before and Monokels take was beautifully done. The choice to make the game monochrome really helped bring out the stunning visual backdrops the game has and the parts of the game that had background music were such a perfect fit.Gameplay is pretty straightforward and very similar to games like Limbo, Little Nightmares and Inside to name a few. Things do open up as the game progresses with Ravengirl evolving along with the story.I very much look forward to what Monokel come up with next.
_childDocuments_.name: White Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: (SPOILERS) White shadows is great at conveying references to animal farm and the many abuses under a communist/fascist regime. Having a similar social hierarchy with the wolves being in charge like the corrupt pigs, the rats being like the guard dogs, the pigs as the common ignorant people, and with the birds being an analogy to the persecuted Jews under Hitler's leadership. Game-play wise, it was lacking, with the ending being anti-climatic. It felt more like a movie than an actual interactive puzzle game.  A show and tell approach may have been what the developers wanted, but I just wanted another Limbo experience!
_childDocuments_.name: White Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I thought this game was very good. A little rough around the edges, but i also understand that this was probably a very ambitious first game for this company.This game is very visually pleasing and interesting, although for what it holds visually, it lacks in gameplay. The movement is a bit clunky at times and the character feels a little bit floaty. There was no bugs to be found other than occasional stutters and objects clipping through each other during cutscenes. The game is a puzzle game, but also not really. Puzzles were not hard and could be solved with little effort, and dramatic scenes didn't feel tense. They were more leisurely which is why I am glad this game is short. The story was good and interesting, but also felt a little out of place or not cohesive. As a game is visual and atmospheric, it is supposed to be immersive. One thing that very much ruined that was the audio. Either repetitive, not really existing, or taking away or not adding much. The classical music is a good touch but did not fit in a lot of the scenes.Overall good game, I recommend it to anyone interested in these kind of games. Although the price is a little bit expensive for how short the game is, but i do not regret buying it.
_childDocuments_.name: White Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked the setting and the dark creativity. The way the soundtrack goes along with the game is nice.Criticism: A lot of waiting. _childDocuments_.name: White Shadows

name: Paradise Killer
detailed_description: Buzz About the Game An island outside of reality. A rogue human civilization hoping to resurrect dead alien gods. A murder behind locked doors. Paradise is an island that regenerates every few millennia. The psychic power that the alien worshipers within release into the universe is meant to feed and eventually resurrect their fallen deities. But this force also attracts undesired interest from demons, who eventually corrupt each island — until a new alternate reality is birthed by the Council. The system isn’t perfect, but it will be one day — on Perfect 25, the next island-to-be. But on the eve of rebirth, the Council is murdered and Paradise is killed. In the aftermath, the “investigation freak” Lady Love Dies is summoned from exile to find the culprit. This is the crime to end all crimes. What are the facts? What are the truths? Are they the same? Return to Paradise Island in this updated and enhanced version of Paradise Killer, featuring new music and new mysterious beings, additional quests and rewards, extra Starlight skins, and more collectibles to find, plus performance improvements, a HUDless mode and Steam achievements. A free update for all players, available now. Featuring DX12 support, ray tracing* (DX12 only), advanced upscaling (NVidia DLSS and AMD SR), and a host of other visual and performance updates, Paradise Island looks more stunning than ever! You are tasked with finding the killer and building an airtight case against them. Take your case to trial and argue your interpretation of the evidence. Only when someone is successfully convicted can the crime be considered solved and Paradise be saved. The “truth” is that there are many possible killers, and many ways to build a case. Even if you make a convincing case for prosecution and get someone convicted, is the mystery really solved? Paradise is an island set in an alternate future history filled with cryptic lore and even more mysteries. Examine bizarre relics to learn more about this world’s surreal history. You choose who to accuse, and build a case to support conviction. Everyone on Paradise has a secret to hide and something to gain. Old friends become new suspects, forcing you to choose between the evidence, the greater good and your own beliefs. There are many possible murderers, but who you pick will define your own personal truth. Let your personal computer and electronic assistant Starlight be your guide through another dance of an investigation. Collect evidence, record testimony and interpret the facts to form your own truth. Solve hieroglyph puzzles on ancient nightmare computers to discover new areas of the island, find concealed evidence and reveal terrifying secrets. Paradise Killer has a suite of accessibility options that allow you to tailor the game to suit your needs. *Raytracing requires a compatible NVidia RTX GPU, DirectX 12 and Windows 10 Build 1809. To play with Raytracing, please launch the game in DirectX 12 mode.

short_description: Paradise Island, a world outside reality. There’s been a murder that only 'investigation freak' Lady Love Dies can solve. Gather evidence and interrogate suspects in this open world adventure. You can accuse anyone, but you’ll have to prove your case in trial. It’s up to you to decide who’s guilty.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually do games that have the vaporwave aesthetic, since they tend to be too chaotic to have a coherent story or plot, but to my surprise the vaporwave definitely fits in with the amazing narrative and history the game weaves. Paradise Killer was definitely a worthy purchase. I had so much fun exploring the game world, I could parkour everywhere and anywhere I could think to go, and the world felt open to me like no other game could even though the game world is pretty small. The graphics were *amazing*. Reflective surfaces reflected without any lag and the game world was overall breathtakingly beautiful. Exploring and going back and forth between characters never felt like a chore.With the plot the game made me feel very smart following up on leads. I overall love the ambiguity the game has with its narrative and the mystery that unfolds with it. I have been yearning for a game that weaves the truth as it goes, a game that doesn't have a 'canon' so to speak. I know I have heard people complaining about the ambiguity of it, but I absolutely love the game for it and its ingenuity.A big plus is that all the characters are either hot or aesthetically pleasing. Yes, even Shinji.So my thoughts in a summary: 10/10, wouldn't play again since I don't think this game has a lot of replayability (which honestly isn't a bad thing), but definitely would lose my memory and experience it again.

_childDocuments_.review: Danganronpa in a Lovecraft-inspired open world. The characters are incredibly wacky and fun, the soundtrack and visual style are excellent (again, similar to Danganronpa), the mystery has quite a few great twists and the ability to go to trial at any point is interesting.The low points are, unfortunately, the trials at the end of the game. So don't go into them with expectations of some satisfying climax - your character will basically just rattle off evidence until the defendants fold and confess. Thankfully, they are a tiny part of the game (<1 hour), so it's forgivable.Would recommend, *especially* if you like Danganronpa.

_childDocuments_.review: I completed this game on gamepass, but I loved it so damn much that I rebought it on steam just to review it. I don't think the story is particularly amazing. It's good, and has plenty of twists and turns, but it's not a game changer. However, the aesthetic, the music, the world, the lore... Those things are ALL game changers. This game is CRIMINALLY underrated. My favorite aspect by far is the world and the lore. It's so rich, like every inch of this game is teeming with such creativity, love, and artistic flourish. The game's characters are fine, they are deep enough to not hold the world design and lore back. It's still enjoyable to learn about the characters inner workings, their secrets, and interpersonal relations. I think Love Dies is one of the more compelling characters and I wish there was more about her. But the STAR of the show is the world. Cthulu-vaporwave, with just absolutely incredible lore. The island sequences, the syndicate, the "real world", the citizen's place in it all, it's hard not to spoil with how many cool things there are. I do wish they explored it more, because much of it is told through knick-knacks you find around the world. I love the item descriptions, they evoke such strong emotion... but I wish more of that was through mechanics of the game itself. Don't get this game for the story, or the characters. Get this game to VIBE. It just has such a strong aesthetic, while I want to spend more time there. I want to vacation there. But I don't ever want to live in Paradise. And that, in-and-of itself makes the world so very compelling.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing this review after finishing the Story. It took me about 14 hours to finish this game, although I must admit, that I was exploring the whole island and collecting collectibles that crossed me. I would say you can finish the main story of this game in about 7-10 hours, depending of how thorough you are searching for evidence. When first starting this game I was a bit confused about the whole idea of a syndicate trying to create the perfect island and how each island ended in mass slaughtering of citizens. Well there's a whole religious theme in this game, but nonetheless the further one plays the more you are curious about why the next sequence "Perfect 25" was overshadowed by murdering the whole syndicate council. Whosdunnit? You are called as the investigator from exile to find out who did it, interrogate the remaining people on the island (a few have already been moved to the next island), crack computer puzzles (which are fairly easy tbh) and find evidence for the murder of the council. At any point of the game you can go to the judge who called upon you to start the trial where you need to provide evidence. I must say I have not tried starting the trial right away (wouldnt make alot of sense for an investigator right?) but I was collecting every bit of information that I could find. There's a grand scheme in the murder of the council, it actually was surprisingly twisted, and I enjoyed playing this game alot. I actually enjoyed the vaporwave style of the game, the soundtrack is awesome and there's a little demon (Shinji) who I actually appreciated to much, I tried to get any conversation I could with him (he's roaming the free world in a few locations).I should mention there are about 3 or 4 side quests in this game from ghosts and a dog, but they were "nice to have" to me. They didn't add anything to the main plot nor did they feel like they rewarded you enough to finish them. They are probably added so the island does not feel too empty in some areas, which is fine by me. Can you bring justice to the murdered council? Can you help bring perfection to the next island "Perfect 25"? It is for you to find out.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic title, couldn't stop playing it once I started. Albeit it being a rather short title, with my playtime clocking around 9 hours, i feel the price paid for the title is very much worth it, but I'd also recommend picking it up on sale too.The game play is rather simple, being a game where you spend time exploring the open world looking for clues, which are either found as an item, or by talking with npcs, with the end goal of the game being solving the murder case your character has been recruited to solve. Exploring the island is the real highlight of the title, with the island itself not only full of charm, but its chock full of collectibles that help paint a picture of what's actually going on in the game, independent of the murder. And boy, its really crazy, and it helps paint the ultimate act of the game in a different light.  The characters in this game are great, with some of them having great backstories and overall character designs. Some however, look like an amateur Tumblr artist drew them, in a Miku Binder Thomas Jefferson kind of way, but overall still really postive. The atmosphere and ambiance for this game is impeccable, with an amazing soundtrack, matched by a retro lofi graphics that work surprisingly well together. Lady Blue is my personal favorite from the OST, but the entire OST is straight fire, and helps nail the mood for the short time you play this game.The story for the game, well, the main plot of the murder mystery is very passable, as the finale of the game doesn't have any true canonical endings, with you ultimately playing judge, jury, and executioner with the rest of cast as you like, depending on what evidence you find and what you CHOOSE to present or hide. But personally enjoyed all the twists you find leading up the ending of the game, some of them I didn't see coming from a mile away, Overall, 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: The vaporwave whodunit - that's the perfect way to describe this game. Amazing music, fun style and interesting story. What else could you want? Maybe multiple ways to solve a mystery? Or a way to  anyone you want? Maybe some cute dog or a funny demon? Cause this game has it all.I had fun time playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: An actual investigation game that lets you actually go around, gather clues and draw your own conclusions, eventually presenting them to form the truth you want to show. The plot is quite interesting and it has plenty of twists to make it all full of proper discovery. The music is damn fine and provides a great backdrop.The fast travel system actually using your limited blood crystals is very much unappreciated. If there was some renewable currency to use at this.... one might feel better. Also, NOTHING tells you that the foot baths are worth the cost. Some things are downright unintiuitive and you will need to throw yourself at them to get somewhere. Sometimes you might feel like you hit a brick wall when there is in fact more to see. The lore is downright bizarre at first, making one feel like they have been lost in a world that makes very little sense.Also, as a native Romanian, Akiko REALLY bothers me. I tend to kill my sound whenever she is talking simply because her randomly chosen swears shoved in dialogue feel like an insult. Also, her repertoire is so limited it gets jarring after a bit, especially since most of the time it does not make sense. But I can't afford to stop ALL the blurbs of speech from the others.Overall, flawed.... but GOOD.

_childDocuments_.review: No danger or death, just investigation on an aesthetically beautiful and relaxing environment. It's a very relaxing game where exploration and willingness to explore and is important. Much of the island is empty but there's a reason for that and left behind are the keepsakes, mementos, and clues to the residence. You discover all that as you try to uncover a who committed a mass murder. I like really like this game's style and music, although there is little direction and having character get miffed you asked them about something on a whim can be annoying. Still I recommend it as a "before bed" game to unwind and relax.

_childDocuments_.review: The Good:- Nani the hell?- All, and I mean all, of the characters are unique feeling and have a different chemistry with Lady LD as well as clear motives and even family trees and backgrounds that they are tied too. Very well written cast considering there is a lot of them- The actual case is unique and even though its more of a VN when it comes to investigation the investigating is pretty fun. Finding the clues and using them all in a big flashy trial at the end is a great format.- Oh God the OST is amazing, literally just wall to wall bangers.- The island has this weird vapourwave inspired look about it and I know that's gonna make some people roll their eyes but I honestly think this is one of the best applications I've ever seen this "aesthetic" used.- The dialogue is pretty funny at times especially when interacting with Doom Jazz and the vending machines.- I know its minor but I love the names in this game. Dr. Doom Jazz, Crimson Acid, Sam Daybreak. Idk I think they all sound cool.- Thank Christ there's a fast travel because the island is big and kind of daunting when you're released into it to explore and solve the case.- Did I mention the amazing OST?The Bad:- As mentioned before its not really an investigation game. More like a spot the evidence and have it explained to you game. I don't think this is a negative per se but don't come in expecting Ace Attorney or something.- The Nightmare Computer stuff is basically a waste of time. The same puzzle about 20 times.- One of the main pieces of evidence is literally in a hole in a mountain. Which is weirdly placed and the only case of bad game design.- This is a game which should have voice acting because the 4 lines every character has get repetitive very quickly (NERONICITO!)... except for Nani the hell of course.Massive thumbs up recommendation ignore the losers who say its not hard enough. Focus on the story and the pleasantly floaty platforming.

_childDocuments_.review: Just a unique and incredibly stylish game with the sort of game world you'll remember forever. Great story, amazing soundtrack, tonnes to explore, find, investigate. I guess the only thing to say against it is that investigation side of things is pretty much done for you - it's not really a pen and paper puzzler like that, more watching an episode of a really weird cop show.

_childDocuments_.review: Just like many others, I went into this game thinking it would be similar to Phoenix Wright or Danganronpa. However, these games are not similar at all. That's not a negative for the game itself I just thought I would bring it up since a lot of the other reviews are wrong when they compare those games with this one.For the game itself, it does have a lot of good things going for it. The art is beautiful, the music is fantastic, and the writing is stellar. The characters are very interesting but I wish I could talk to them more. I guess that just means I liked them but wanted to know more about them.The negatives are far more glaring. The game advertises itself on its open world which at first is really cool to see and you want to explore it all. However, when you actually start exploring you realize just how overwhelming the size of the island is. This is probably in part to the terrible map you're given that makes it super hard to navigate especially in the housing area. The game also hamfists this awful traversal gameplay into it. The geometry of the island is really bad and it's hard to know if you can climb a rock or not. This is a problem since the characters you need to talk to are so far spread out around the island that you have to constantly traverse the environment in order to talk to them. There's a lot of running back and forth between characters whether it's waiting to hang out with them again or to get one piece of evidence from one character and then running across the map to talk to another on what you just learned just to have to run back to that first character. It all felt more like a checklist rather than wanting to go talk to a character at a specific moment when I got a specific piece of evidence. I also got really sick of the blood gem popup every time I picked one up. Yeah it's a cool aesthetic for the splash screen and audio but after the 50th time seeing it I'm sick of it.Another issue is the detective gameplay. I mentioned not being like Phoenix Wright isn't a negative for this game but there is quite literally no detective working going on in this game. You're given a checklist of questions to ask characters depending on the other clues you have obtained and sometimes you can choose 1 of 2 responses to characters which I'm pretty sure don't actually make a difference other than what they reply with. This all leads into the trial which is really cool to see everything come together into one big event, but it takes literally no brain effort to do it. You're just given the choice on which character you want to prosecute for each crime and then just go through all the evidence one by one that you already obtained. There is no deductive reasoning in the trial. There's also no post-trial dialogue that changes depending on your actions in the trial. I understand the point of the trial is supposed to make up your own truth on what you believed happened so it's open to interpretation, but I was upset when the characters alive after the trial didn't have anything special to say about what had happened, especially if you end up deciding to kill one of their friends.I would recommend this game to people who just want a VN with a cool aesthetic, world building, and characters. If you're here for gameplay in an open world or big brain detective work and trial you've come to the wrong place.

_childDocuments_.review: Paradise Killer: Take the legendary game Myst. Give it a bubblegum pink miami vice murder mystery gods and godlike acid trip. Bam, you've got this game.You are an exiled detective on a world created by godlike beings in an effort to create the perfect paradise. Due to corruption and flaws, many attempts have been made. The game takes place on the 24th island sequence and once again, things have gone terribly wrong resulting in mass murder of the council, leadership of the paradise. Lead Paradise Investigator 'Lady Love Dies' (all the characters have wild names. Dr. Doom Jazz is another example) has been exiled for 30 million days since the 13th island due to a mistake involving god corruption that nearly killed everyone. She's been brought back as the only person that can possibly figure out what happened with the murder of the council. You must scour the island for clues and testimony to figure who was behind the murders so that the guilty can be executed before everyone else can advance to the 25th perfect island.The game oozes vibe and style. It is a very unique experience. I enjoyed unraveling the mystery and solving the case. Rarely felt frustrated at what to do next or anything like that. Solid 8.5-9/10

_childDocuments_.review: I'm very on the fence with the game, but the mechanics ultimately tip the balance away from recommending it. Working out the mystery is fun to do on paper, or in your head, but the conclusion of all that work is a simple checklist from a judge to determine whether you've picked up enough collectables. There's no understanding check and no need for you to have been paying attention. If you walked everywhere and clicked everything, you will crack the case, even if you didn't read a shred of dialogue.And that's not really a murder investigation game. It's a collectable hunting game.A few red herrings (there aren't any) and a better ending sequence that tested the player's understanding of the case and allowed you to prosecute the trials would have totally made this experience. Instead, I just look back on it as a something I'll soon forget about, and wouldn't have gotten into had I known it for what it was.

_childDocuments_.review: I whole heartedly recommend playing this game. I instantly fell in love with the world of Paradise Killer. It's a wonderfully bizarre reality that is full of character, and full of wonderful characters. You play as the wonderfully named, Lady Love Dies, an investigator whose been exiled for roughly 3 million days. You're called back to investigate the murder of the ruling council. On the way you come across multiple crimes which may or may not be connected, and you have to investigate, interrogate, and explore an island which is located outside reality for clues.All of the members of the ruling party that are on the island are suspects, and you go around questioning them to try to get them to contradict themselves, and to get testimonies about the doings of the other suspects.Scouring crime scenes, and getting access to the primary crime scene, rewards exploration, and attention to detail.In the end, you don't have to find every single piece of information, but in order to do things right, you have to decide by yourself who is to blame, and you have to prove your case using evidence.The game isn't without its flaws. You can always see which suspects have outstanding questions unanswered, but you're able to ask them irrelevant questions, so you can easily waste time going to ask them about things that they can't possibly answer.There is a secret character which you're supposed to meet early in the game. If you don't, as it was in my case, you trigger a cutscene between the two of you, mentioning things that never happened.I had tons of fun exploring this bizarre world, and everything it had to offer, and it's very unfortunate that only about 6% of the players, have played enough to get the first upgrade.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This was a genuine gem that I just so happened to randomly get in a Humble Bundle. I have never heard of it prior to playing, which is a surprise because its very much a masterpiece of the modern adventure genre. At first glance, it may seem like a vaporwave meme, but it's got so much more depth than just that superb artistic style. It's the most realistic exploration of criminal investigation that I have ever seen; eschewing the normalized detecting through physical clues and crime scenes for a more nuanced approach of investigating through witness testimony. There is a web of deceit and conspiracy that one must wade through to find facts of the case, and the game does it so well.There is a delicate line that this game balances on, but it makes it through to the end without ever falling over. It's so small but so densely packed with both a unique environment that begs to be explored and diverse characters to be dissected. Everything this game presents is great: the artistic style, the music, and movement and platforming, the interview based evidence gathering gameplay, and the writing--they all coalesce into a personal masterpiece. I enjoyed this game thoroughly. It is a true gem.5/5
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: A nice change of pace coming from Danganronpa. Being able to freely pursue what you want without having to be spoon-fed the answers actually makes you appreciate what you find. You can end the game at any time and go to the final trial with what you have, or exhaust all the evidence the island has before finishing up. There are plenty of angles to look at, but ultimately, each crime does have a right answer. It is a bit short at only 10 hours, but it is well worth it for the price.

_childDocuments_.review: The Mystery as a whole is extremely compelling. A supernatural murder where events could not possibly happen if they were confined to our own world had me interested from the start. Usually something of this caliber would be difficult to pull off since you can pull anything out of thin air and make it feel cheap. They avoided this by setting up all the players prior and ensured that you understood the capabilities of every being involved. I was engrossed for the first couple of hours. However...As a Mystery GAME, it's nothing more than moving through a large Hub getting from one NPC to the next and occasionally finding points of interest on the way. You are hardly piecing clues together, as the player character is doing this for you. Evidence does not need to be presented, just collected and the game will inform you of where you need to go next. Normally this would be okay if they left things up for interpretation and let things escalate during the Trial sequence where you put everything together and reveal a big conspiracy. "But that's exactly what happens!" you may say if you have played the game before, but all i did was click on the text prompts and let the character i was controlling do all the deducing for me. You merely have to accuse the right person and the game will take care of the rest for you. You cannot be wrong at any point other than the initial accusations during the trial, which are usually spelled out for you by the game if you found any amount of clues while investigating.Navigating around the map is tedious, it's exciting when you find clues initially but given the size of the map it becomes cumbersome rather quickly. Whilst fast travel exists, it's difficult to tell where you're actually going unless you really study the map and even so it still requires you to go through several time consuming menus. Platforming around the hub is awful even with all of the upgrades you can get as there's no way to alter your trajectory once you leave the ground. There are collectables scattered throughout the hub, but it is more tedious to collect these objects than it is enjoyable for the previously stated reasons. I appreciate how open the map is and how you can tackle the game in any order you wish, but I ultimately did not like its execution and would have preferred something more condensed.It actually pains me to not recommend this. It's oozing with style and I thoroughly enjoyed the setting and the characters. Although I enjoyed my time with it initially, that Paradise was killed rather quickly and that feeling was replaced with a general apathy (haha i put the title of the game in my review). If you enjoy walking simulators and want just a story I could see myself recommending this, but as a game about "Gathering Evidence and Interrogating suspects" I would give it a pass.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really interesting open world investigation game. Cruise around a vaporwave paradise, interview suspects, collect evidence, build a case. The music is delightful and the world is really well realized, with lots of ~Deepest Lore~ to find. The collectables are interesting and well-written even if many of them don't do anything. I've barely questioned anyone over 6 hours and am just enjoying exploring the island and finding all the secrets and nooks and crannies. The investigation that I have uncovered is really interesting and I'm pretty hooked.I know the artstyle is a little weird but you get used to it and it even starts to syngerize with the strange world. I think this will become a cult classic.  EDIT: Finished the game at ~12 hours and found it really satisfying. The court mechanic is handled well and I was actually a little surprised by how everything went down. I found the conclusion to be really interesting and the mystery crafted by the game is extremely well executed. I have two minor gripes: I played the trial twice, once completely straight with the truth, and once choosing to hide an NPC's involvement because I liked them. The game makes no acknowledgement that anything is different. However, I'm sure that's by design because that would be like a real investigation.My other gripe is the lack of a fully pilotable jet ski, hang glider, speed boat, or helicopter. I really like cruising around the island and being able to do a pleasure cruise around it would have owned.All in all, PARADISE KILLER sticks the landing and leaves me hungry for more.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Uncovering lore and worldbuilding in this game is just as fascinating as finding clues, and the world has enough depth that I constantly wanted to learn more about it, even after scouring the island from end to end. If you're looking for something that scratches the itch for both mystery and exploration at the same time, this is definitely the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't been able to stop thinking about it since I played it. If you're like me and you're sick of similar games coming out, I guarantee you will not have played anything like this. It's beautiful, rewarding and the atmosphere (in no small part thanks to the music) is unlike anything else on the steam store. GET IT NOW!
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic. Go in blind, the more you know the less impressive the game becomes. It's in a similar vein to the Outer Wilds in a lot of ways. Explore, you can find answers out of order, or sleuth and follow each clue to their conclusion.The joy of this game is solving the murder, the trial at the end is a bit of a let down, don't expect it to be on the same tier as Phoenix Wright at the end or the adrenaline rush of the Outer Wilds.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty cool game. I enjoyed mainly exploring the initial world and at the end piecing it all together. I wish there were more interactions with characters together while exploring, because sometimes they feel isolated across the island until the end. Still a really fun one to go through and an interesting world to learn about
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10 - This game is a super engaging and wacky mystery thriller. Good music, cool characters, and secrets to find EVERYWHERE. This game encourages you to think about the mystery and explore every inch of the map. The ending and some gross looking textures leave a little bit more to be desired, but overall a super fun game that I beat in less than 24 hours after buying because I was so engaged.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: A short-ish (I pretty much completed all the important content in my 11 hours of playtime) but very satisfying investigation game. The best way I can describe it is: Vaporwave Danganronpa in a Lovecraftian setting. If that confuses and intrigues you, read on.Setting aside, it's a classic whodunnit kind of story. You play as Lady Love Dies, an investigator called back from exile to find out who killed the Councile of Paradise Island, a weird metaphysical reality bubble created by a group of immortals called the Syndicate in a bid to resurrect ancient dead Gods from outer space. There's a previously convicted murderer who escaped his jail and was found at the scene of the crime with the blood of the victims on him, so it seems an open and shut case... but of course, it's not that easy. Talk with the residents, snoop around, solve a few puzzles, find clues, and eventually, start a Trial and make your case. The gameplay itself is pretty simple, and it's basically a Visual Novel with an open world setting, but the setting, character writing and dialogue are fantastic and are worth alone playing. Great atmosphere and a really good mystery too - I enjoyed a lot piecing together all the various hints and information as the many mysteries and conspiracies in the island unfolded. Definitely recommended, especially if you enjoy detective stories!
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy games like the Ace Attorney or the Danganronpa trilogies, then I highly recommend giving Paradise Killer a shot. From the beginning, you are thrown into a giant crime scene and left on your own to investigate and uncover the culprit. I enjoy how the game doesn't hold your hand and give you an easy trail to follow, and the way your collected evidence is organized makes it that much easier to keep track of everything. The game also has custom pacing in which you can end the investigating phase at any point and move on towards the end game. This allows for players to take in as much or as little as they want. I really appreciate not having time pass/being rushed towards a conclusion because you certainly need the time to reason through your evidence and notes.As for how the game looks and sounds? It's incredible. The aesthetic of the map really helps build the world around it and makes for just a really cool looking game. The soundtrack is just top-notch.  I'd say at least 2 of my in-game hours are from me just running around and jammin' out to those sweet, sweet tunes.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Paradise Killer is an open world detective adventure game with the most insane cast of characters you can imagine. The closest comparison I can make is the Phoenix Wright series, but even then it's only a close approximation as I don't think I've ever played anything like it.The 80s Japan vaporware aesthetic combined with some superb music and a well thought out mystery has definitely made it a memorable experience that I don't think I'll soon forget and the soundtrack will be a part of my playlist for a very long time. Would totally recommend to anyone who likes a good mystery and I hope to see more games from the studio.There are only two "negatives" I can think about:- The voice acting, it's bad, like really really bad. You get voice quips from characters during dialogue that sound like they were recorded in a bathroom and don't match the dialogue at all.An example would be the text saying "I don't think so" and the VO being "WHAT THE HELL?!".Not a word for word example but you'll know what I am talking about.Thankfully there is an option to disable the voice quips, so not a problem really.- Some of the character art is quite sloppy, some frames can look good, but others are just deformed. Crimson is a prime example of this, her upper body just looks horrific in some frames, hopefully this will get cleaned up in the next game.Overall the game has been solid and I think is a must have for any fans of the genre, whatever genre that was.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great murder mystery I had enough fun that I did everything including all the collectibles. There is a slight drag near the end as evidence becomes less frequent and more spread out but it is still very fun. The story is really good and the way this game approaches the final truth is very interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like nothing I've ever played before. There are some elements of other games in here, but nothing quite describes this game well without expressing it is a Vaporwave Detective game. Every minute of my time playing the game I was just in awe of the world's unique design elements and the world building given by the artifacts and characters relaying information. The music is exactly what you'd expect with Vaporwave themes. A lot of comfortable jazzy 80's sounding music and you have the ability to create your own playlist of the music in game, which more games should allow that.The characters are mostly text based speaking, but do have some audio lines, though they aren't anything really to talk about. They sound unique and frankly I wish there were more of them, so I didn't hear the same 5/6 lines repeated over my playthrough. It doesn't necessarily detract from the experience, but I feel like they could've had at least more responses especially considering how dynamic the conversations can become based on what evidence you are speaking to them about. The characters are also vibrant and they each stand out against each other, so you never feel confused as to who you are talking about or to, even though they have some interesting names to say the least. They are 2D images in a 3D environment but somehow the aesthetic works really well for me. There are only so many characters to interact with and in game they mention the names of other ones who are not on the island anymore. I really wish this game had a random selection of the list of 18 characters, and offered multiple stories based on which characters were available in your story thereby giving it an immense amount of replay-ability. 90% of the collectibles you will find in this game are the currency used in the game Blood Crystals. There are littered everywhere, and I mean EVERYWHERE. You can unlock new movement abilities and a useful skill to help see where all collectibles are for a few seconds, but it has infinite uses. If you collect every single Blood Crystal you can use all of them needed for the entire game and have a surplus of 55. So do not feel afraid to use the fast travel system even though I rarely did. The other collectibles are Artifacts which give some interesting lore and information about the world you are in, but for the most part they did absolutely nothing. I would love it if there were more NPC's like the citizens looking for more of the items or asking questions regarding the in game lore to make it worthwhile having collected them all. There is no minimap and to be honest the in game map is not very useful minus the times you need to fast travel, since the names are fairly informative of where you want to go. At times I wished for some further mapping, but realistically there are so many unique landscapes and design elements that the more you walk around and explore, the better you'll feel about knowing your surroundings. Plus early on in the game, they give you the ability to hold a button to see the location of all major characters to talk to, which will come in handy. I should also mention that there is a respawn function in the game in case you get stuck or lost, it'll move you to a recent save station nearby. However, there are locations, since you can freely explore every inch of the island, where you can get stuck and the respawn function may not work. I only had this issue once, but it really reminded me that this game DOES NOT AUTOSAVE. Due to you having the ability to go anywhere and speak to anyone, the game asks you to save manually. Thankfully there are tons, and I mean tons, of save stations which also work as the fast travel locations. Overall, I loved this game from start to finish. I was streaming this game to a few friends of mine over the course of my playthrough and the details and exactly what happened on that day were so intriguing. The game makes a point early on, I believe before you even start the game if I recall correctly, that you are not given definitive answers. You are given pieces of a puzzle that fits together by deducing logically reasoning. You can prove the truth by your answers, you just need to be firm in your decision. At any time you can choose to end the game by going to Trial, but I urge everyone playing this to fully explore the island and learn every last detail you can. There are some things left to be desired, mainly the game offers nothing more than a single experience especially if you get the story correct, but that doesn't mean this game is bad. If you are a fan of detective games/novels and want to immerse yourself in one of the most bizarre worlds I've ever been put into, I highly recommend this game. You are doing yourself a disservice if you don't allow these developers to show you what a wild story they have in play for you.  8/10 Worth every penny I spent.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This game is easily one of the best games I've played in years. The dialogue is interesting and punchy, the visuals are beautiful, and even the act of completing your collection has a great explorative quality too it. Part of me wishes I could have kept playing this game forever, but the short length was just the right length for the story it wanted to tell. A masterpiece of game design.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This was one of the best first person platformers I've ever played, the movement mechanics made it so that i almost never bothered with fast travel. The genre mashing was also done very well; Lovecraftian gods, alternate history, platforming/open world, detective work and relationship builder are all things i wouldn't expect to work together, but they do, very well.I will say that I expected something out of the relics other than just lore, and that the trial feels like it could have had more work after the amount of time I spent collecting everything (it felt very much like a footnote to the rest of the game when it should've been the climax, and there's basically no revelations in said trial that you cant come to during investigation).All in all though for a game that can be completed in 10 minutes to the 13 hours i took, it was a very solid start, and I'm looking forward to a possible sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I liked this game. Not a lot, but enough. I have a few grievances here and there that would 100% need to be addressed before I would play some sort of theoretical sequel, but the gripes aren't enough to make me dislike it the first time. I'll list them as a "buyer beware" but ultimately it'd only be an issue if I had to slog through it AGAIN.So the entire game revolves around a currency that the game doesn't even really revolve around, except when it does. If you played it, you'll understand. This currency, blood crystals, is everywhere. Collectables are everywhere. Clues are somewhere. I guess the theory was that you were supposed to leave no stone unturned, and the reward was this currency. But that's basically indistinguishable from filler. It was a nice change of pace flying around everywhere, but ultimately wasn't super rewarding. You need this currency for fast travel (which is super weird) and for a few story-critical things. My advice: pick them up as you find them. Foot baths and vending machines are 100% necessary. They might not seem like it. Never pass them up.The game's theme is that facts aren't necessarily the truth, and they nail it. Except that by "nail that" I mean "you can get the killers by doing a fraction of the game but you don't know the whole story and it'll be super obvious that you don't". There's really not a point in the game until the VERY END after you've done everything that you can reasonably say "ok this person did this, this person did not do this." What that means, is that ultimately you'll just feel encouraged to do everything and get all the facts and get this one truth. They do a good job trying, but maybe not the best theme to have in a murder mystery?The game sits comfortably in a place where I'm happy I played it, I'll never replay it and I'll need to be talked into playing a sequel. If this ♥♥♥♥ isn't your jam, hard pass. If you're looking for a murder mystery game, you can do worse. If you can do better, and you probably can, I strongly recommend those games. But you can definitely do worse.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: interesting character/story, unfortunately you spend 99% of the time running around in circles for hours. The exploration is not interesting because it is not challenging. You don't observe a situation and make deductions based on the actual environmental detail. Rather, you click on and collect neatly packaged "clues" that show up as glowing squares. The game becomes more an exercise of patience to walk along every square inch to find all of the clues. Further, the collected clues simply open up additional dialogue options. There is not much thought needed to complete the game, up until the very last scene where you finally can put the pieces together.To provide a counter example: In The Outer Wilds every clue gives you knowledge about how the world works. The player then has to use this understanding to figure out what to do next. The freedom of 3D exploration benefits this game as it is impossible to simply brute force your way. The player must actively engage with the clues and knowledge in order to progress. whereas in Paradise Killers, you can more or less ignore everything, and simply treat the game as one big fetch quest for the first few hours to collect all the clues and run back and forth between characters, before getting to the actually interesting part of piecing together the story.Unfortunately environments in Paradise Killers are not interesting to explore, and don't contribute to the investigation. There are few details in the actual 3D environment that area relevant. Many clues within single screen snapshots anyway, like in the Pheonix Wright games. In that series, clue collection can also be more or less brute forced collected by simply clicking on everything. However, you are limited to just a few screens, and it is fairly streamlined process to collect all the information you need. Paradise Killer feels like playing Phoenix Wright if every scene change required half an hour of walking to the next location, and another half an hour looking in every nook to make sure you didn't miss anything. Even moving between characters takes a very long time. Overall, I felt like there was potentially an interesting story to tell, but it just got bogged down by wasting the players time with hours and hours of tedious busy work slowing the actual story progression to a snails pace.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Got this as a gift, and didn't think much of it at first. When i did give it the time it engrossed me, and finding out the killers identity was a fun mystery. The animations were well done, and the island was well built. I had as much fun exploring as I did unraveling the knot of mystery.10/10 would Anime Sherlock Holmes again.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: While this investigation adventure reminds me of Ace Attorney, in a good way, just with a retro/-synthwave spin,  it gave me severe motion sickness less than an hour into playing it. Something about the field of vision seems off. Anyone found a fix for this?What helped me alleviate some of the motion sickness (allowing me to play longer):1. turn off all screen shake, blurring effects, rendering options, moving backgrounds2. playing the game on the lowest pixel on lowest resolution settings in windowed modeAfter doing all the things above I managed to make it to the end of the game without nausea. I have lukewarm feelings about the ending, while I liked the open-endedness and available ending choices, they didn't feel as impactful as I would have liked. It would have been nice to see the consequences of the choices you make, even if just in text form.Why I still recommend it: It's worth a play purely for the worldbuilding, storytelling, humour and aesthetics.Adorable Shinji and his quirky, thoughtful and at times deranged commentary is the best part of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing detective games for a good chunk of my life now, starting with Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney on the DS (and all of the entries of it that are available to play in English one way or another). There have been a huge number of takes on the detective genre, and Paradise Killer is probably the one that has actually made me feel the most like a detective when playing it.STORY:The story is, um, unique, to say the least. It's about as "out there" as you can really get with a story - basically, it's set on an island full of alien worshippers (they call these aliens "Gods" and "Demons", though really it seems like they're basically interchangeable and whether something is a god or a demon depends on how much they like them), and all members of the governing Council of the island are murdered. You have to investigate the members of the Syndicate in the role of Lady Love Dies, someone who has been exiled due to (minor spoiler, it's mentioned fairly early on) .The story is actually quite entertaining though, and it can become very addictive to learn more about what's going on on the island. Without going too much into spoiler territory, I'd say the story is fairly satisfying. You're not going to predict how it all works out quickly, to say the least, although when you're near the end of the game it can be fairly obvious what happened and it just ends up getting to the point where you're going round for evidence to prove it. This actually does feel like what a real detective would be doing anyway, though, so that's not a negative.CHARACTERS:The characters are absolutely insane. I mean that in a good way though - they're very interesting and lively. From the mysterious Crimson Acid, to the Scottish playboy Doctor Doom Jazz, to the religious zealot Witness to the End, you're going to find many characters that you want to interact with repeatedly. Sadly, you only get a few "hangout" sessions with each of them but you learn more about what motivates them and how they relate to the island and other characters. GAMEPLAY:As you're exploring an entire open-world island, it's easy to feel overwhelmed when playing it due to the lack of initial direction, as well as just the seemingly endless scope of the various different parts of the story (at first). It took me a while to realise that the "Relics" you obtain are not actually part of evidence - they're actually fairly irrelevant in the grand scheme of things beyond wanting to be a completionist and understand more about the lore of the story. And considering this game lacks Steam achievements, the motivation for that is fairly low. When you do end up figuring out how everything actually pieces together, and you get in the swing of "following the notes" (the main page in Starlight, the in-game computer system that you can access at any time), it's actually a lot more clear how to progress. It's made even easier by making sure that you use the ability to scan the locations of people so you know where to find people you haven't talked to yet.The problem with the notes system however is sometimes the clues are *extremely* vague. You should, in theory, be able to complete the game just by exploring everything and pressing E to investigate everything you come up against, but there are a few "notes" in Starlight that are really obtuse in how you solve them. Don't feel bad if you have to do a bit of Googling for hints to figure it out; I had to twice. The other issue I came across is that quite often it can be frustrating following a lead, then talking to characters who just flat-out dismiss evidence that you present to them which gets you nowhere. I guess this is because really the only place the evidence matters is the trial, but it would be nice if more of an emphasis on evidence gathering was placed upon a sequence of evidence presenting.The trial is kind of disappointing. The following spoiler just explains the gameplay of the trial without revealing any story information: Despite these issues I've raised with the gameplay, they are not deal-breakers at all - the vast majority of the game is very fun to play simply due to having an open world to explore and the story of the game fragmented in a way that makes it feel extremely satisfying to piece together. GRAPHICS:The art style in this game is really nice. The basic world is not anything graphically spectacular - don't go in expecting Cyberpunk 2077 level graphical detail - but it still feels like a vibrant and colourful game. The 2D characters existing in the 3D environment feels very much like Danganronpa, although obviously the gameplay is very different. I really enjoyed the look and feel of the game throughout.MUSIC:The music is definitely , but after a while I ended up zoning out of the music and focusing on what I was doing. I think the problem is there isn't a specific "soundtrack" for each area of the game, or for specific things happening, although there are certain soundscapes in the background for areas like the beach and the "desolation cell" (play the game to figure out what that one means!). The music is just whatever in-game music you've selected to play, over the top of that. All of the music did feel like it "fit" in the game, just felt like there wasn't much direction in how the music related to the game however.Overall I'd still recommend this game to anyone who likes games of the detective/mystery genre, despite the few flaws I've mentioned above. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Great detective game where a complicated murder that gets even more confusing the more you learn. Great soundtrack and protagonist that gave me Bayonetta vibes. All of the characters were interesting with unique designs and personalities. The most unique thing about this game though is the world. Taking place in a world where space gods came to humanity, bestowing them with technology and knowledge (also kind of enslaving them). humanity rebelled and went to war with the gods and their worshipers. Many gods were killed or lost but with the dying breath of "Silent Goat" he bestowed his worshipers (the Syndicate) with the knowledge to build islands in a separate pocket dimension to channel the psychic energy from worship and death into reincarnating the fallen gods. Unfortunately for the syndicate, all islands have failed and fallen to demonic entities, island 1 to 24. And on the final day of 24 the entire council gets murdered and you have to figure out how. (hope I got all that info right lol)It can be a lot thrown at you at once but after a little bit of time you'll figure out the lore and deep and intertwined it is with the world. Having an interesting open world with lots of little puzzles and clues really worked in this games favor. and your character being in exile for 3 million days and just dropped back into meeting the characters again after so long (who are all immortal btw) gives the player a good sense of learning who these people are now thats its been so long since you've seen them. It's hard to talk about this game without spoiling it but all I can say is play it. Get completely immersed in the interesting world that's been made here.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most unique games I've ever played. Probably the first game where you actually make deductions based on evidence like an actual detective and can use evidence to come to your own conclusions way before your character does. The visual style is such a mishmash but somehow it just works. The music is a fantastic blend of synthwave and smooth jazz. The worldbuilding is beyond anything I've seen in games and is the most original setting for a game I've ever had the pleasure of playing. The pixel hunting aspect can get a bit tiresome but, for the most part, actual clues and evidence is usually in obvious places and extras aren't all that necessary but you'd be advised to at least have enough to get certain collectibles and gather testimonies from a particular character though it's enough if you keep a buffer of 15 gems all the time. The weakest aspect is probably the ending which requires some degree of stretching even with the crazy wild setting but it's wrapped up fairly neatlyHighly recommended for how unique of an experience it is
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a very uniquely beautiful and weird aesthetic and an awesome soundtrack. The game itself is not really difficult, most of the difficulty of the game comes from exploring all the locations and looking for (very obviously presented) clues. The murder mystery did not interest me all that much actually, I was pulled in much more by the worldbuilding, lore and the weird landscape you get to explore. The characters are quite interesting and the general worldbuilding is something I would like to see explored further in a future release.If you are looking for a complex murder mystery detective game this is probably not it, but the game is something very unique that still warrants exploring its world in my opinion. The game took me about 10 hours to 100% with all collectibles (though a decent amount of them are unnecessary for completion or the story). All in all I did really enjoy the game though not in the way I originally expected to.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: The best visual novel I experienced. I played it immediately after Obra Dinn and the contrast in the aesthetics was super refreshing. The setting is completely surreal but despite this the world building is extremely well-done, so this crazy universe quickly starts to make sense for us.The good:+ The JoJo-esque colorful aesthetics+ The jazzy tracks+ Exploring the island freely+ Gradually piecing together your case file like a real inspector and understanding what happened feels very satisfying+ The freedom to accuse who you wantThe bad:- While everything plot-relevant is consistent with the universe, the optional collectibles, on the other hand, bring pieces of lore that feel completely random. I get that they're more about setting up an atmosphere than actual world building, but I feel like it harms all the aforementioned work that has been done to have a consistent universe.- The constant ringing of the phones used to save the game gets annoying fast.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: A combination of vaporwave inspired walking sim and detective themed visual novel, Paradise Killer spends the entirety of its 10-15 hour run in the slow lane, letting you soak in its ambiance and get to know its characters. It took me a while to warm to the way it presents itself, but after giving it a chance I found myself invested in learning about Paradise and rooting out the corruption within it.The soundtrack, by the way, is the best thing about this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I started it up and wanted to refund it after 10 minutes, then I remembered all the Overwhelmingly Positive reviews and played on. To my surprise the game started to grow on me. When the investigation part kicked in, the fantastic musical score began to blend in so nicely with the surroundings and the crazy story setting started to make sense. The people who wrote this sure have a great imagination. The madness works because it is presented with such believability and flair. Great stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable one time experience. The investigation itself is linear though the game allows you to start the trial and press charges at any point, there's even an achievement for performing the trial immediately and then rushing back to the car for end credits. The atmosphere is great if you like the vapor-wave aesthetic. The setting is positively bizarre, I read through all the collectibles and enjoyed it. Platforming can be tricky at times, but there are upgrades scattered across the island, best to get them first.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: --The game looks beautiful. The setting is a virtual simulation which looks like a tropical, upscale Tokyo. --The dialogue is fun, especially for the demon characters. The mysteries are not bad.--The tone is wildly dark. The government ruling over the island openly and regularly kidnaps and murders thousands of slaves to collect blood sacrifices to bring back ancient alien gods. There is no way to fight the mass-murder or slavery in any way or bring its perpetrators to justice. The only crimes you DO get to solve are crimes against the leaders running the mass murder system. You're not an actual investigator, you're a Peter Strezok fixer. --Gameplay design is stunningly unfriendly. No auto-save is savage. Money is critically limited, and *finite*, there's only so many crystals to pick up around the map, but costs are NOT finite, every time you want to use the fast-travel system costs money. So expect to slog your way up like 10 super-tall-ass apartments collecting $1 at a time because there is no other way to pay for stuff. Being broke all the time absolutely sucked. Peter Strezok doesn't pick up $1 at a time. --The map system is complete garbage. It's like walking from New York to New Jersey and you somehow end up in California with no idea how you got there, how to reach your intended destination, or how the hell they screwed up a map that badly. The same guy who took out the autosave, no doubt. --The upgrade system is super-non-intuitive. All of the mobility upgrades are trapped behind $5 footbaths in a game where $5 is a lot and there's no indication the footbath matters. Each footbath gives you a superpower like a double-jump or dash jump that make moving around MUCH more livable. If you don't blindly spend $5 on the footbaths you are in for a whirlwind of hurt.--The execution on the trial is lacking. In a classic mystery game like Ace Attorney, the first part of the game will be you collecting evidence and then in the trial the game challenges you to piece together the evidence to show you understand the case and can see through the culprit's lies. In this game, if you have all the evidence, your character will just read it out and then the person will be found guilty, with no choices or deductions or mental work on the part of the player. This felt very rushed.

_childDocuments_.review: I will start off by saying I do not normally write review, but this game has compelled me to do so.I would wholeheartedly recommend Paradise Killers. _childDocuments_.review: [NO SPOILERS] (And YES, I do compare this heavily to Danganronpa in my review)Coming from someone who loved the Danganronpa franchine, I gotta admit I am a bit dissapointed with Paradise Killer.The game is obviously attributed to the works of the Danganronpa franchise as the two share a uncanny amount of similarities. Yet, I can't help but feel like they somehow placed a strong focus on the most boring elements from Danganronpa - and at the same time but a lack of focus on the elements that made Danganronpa a good franchise. To elaborate on this, I feel like the investigation parts of the Danganronpa games are what holds the games back the most. Walking in the halls is clunky, and all you do is click "INTERACT" with anything that lights up when you approach it. While it is interesting to slowly start building your take on the crime based on this, I feel like Paradise Killer just streches this to 11. The island is way to big, and you spend the majority of your time just walking from A to B. Yes, there is a fast travel feature but it costs money and honestly takes forever to finish because they show this fancy taxi animation whenever you use it. Additionally, all the amount of crazy ♥♥♥♥ that happens is just a tad bit too excessive (and that's coming from the Danganronpa fan). When the game decides to introduce new plot-points and laws of the universe we are in at the ending segment of the game, it feels kind of annoying to have all your pre-thought notions out the window. As for where I felt the game under-delivered compared to Danganronpa is within the conclusion of the story. For the sake of keeping this spoiler-free I won't mention any specifics. But I kinda got the feeling this system was left half-finished. At the point where you are accusing suspects for crime X, there is no option to select multiple suspects and it feels like the game just instantly "knows" you meant to select the ones you did. Which feels kinda underwhelming because it sort of puts things in a "it'll be alright no matter what you pick". All of these accusations were also (mostly) only consisting of you (the player), the judge and the accused, which I found really lacking in terms of writing. Surely it would've been more natural for all the testimonies to speak for themselves instead of a prompt shown on screen that "character Y testified to this earlier". This also brings me into the manner of which this accusation was done. All you do is click through all your gathered intel, which is sorted out for you. There is almost zero choices to make here, zero ways you present your evidence, zero ways in which you argue your claims and zero ways the defendant tries to disprove your claims. Which completely breaks the entire "gotcha!" moment the game builds up to with the whole trial imitating a TV show! :((TL;DRIdk, maybe I'm just being harsh on Paradise Killer because I expected more out of a game with such stellar reviews. But in my opinion, you should definitively play Danganronpa > Paradise Killer. Unless the anime aesthetic of the game is a absolute no-go for you and you're more into LGBT characters, then that's fair - this is a good game; I just had higher hopes.
