_childDocuments_.review: What?! You never heard about most bizzare first person adventure game? You never heard about murder mystery involving gods, demonology and immortal people on artificial tropical paradise? Don't worry me neither until a week ago on this roller coaster.Now, now let's chill. This is cleverly written open world detective VN game that gives you WHOLE CONTROL over the course of story and charms you with it's beauty. It's your choice how will you start and end investigations. You have all influence on the story and it's hell of a twisted story so take care. Presented with artistic locations and insanity spiced with perfect music jams. Hours fly by when you spend time with different characters also antagonists and you just see more and more of this island. Part of the fun is exploring even if it all is confusing. Even though you run like headless chicken for most time talking to people observing days and nights in paradise, it is a good time once you know how to appreciate it.Once you get a grisp on this island madness it's P-E-R-F-E-C-T. And it's sort of a charm that you will remember for a long while. Go back for more until there is nothing left. Do I dare to say that Paradise Killer is designed as 10/10? Yes, because I still want to see other islands give me my perfect 25 th and let me "Stay Forever".
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely stunning, aesthetically gorgeous exploration walking sim with light investigation elements and very minor platforming mechanics. Unique setting and worldbuilding, vibrant environments, colorful characters, great music and a tiny bit of murder mystery.This is THE Vaporwave game. Atmosphere hits you like a truck. It's very pink. It has hearts, crystals and butterflies everywhere. It's soaked with blood and cosmic dread.The world is the biggest mystery here, albeit of a self-revealing kind. It's very honest in what it is. There is no subversion, because the setting itself is a subversion. Right at the beginning of the game you get a wall-of-text style blunt exposition of a controversially appealing, painfully desirable un-reality. It's quite literally a cultish eldritch paradise, an ultimate Lovecraftian Utopia.The island is mostly empty for... reasons; there is a small cast of characters you interact with, but the rest of the game is so midnight. A place where you shouldn't be. I can't help but feel I am not supposed to see any of this. Level design is very organic and very deliberate - dense and overwhelming, suspended in fragile balance, like a box of colorful blocks knocked over by a capricious, monstrous child. This place is so incredibly chill, so bittersweet, so liminal; unmistakably artificial, but oh so believable and full of life, from the heartbeat of its power plant, down to ominous ambience of the Dead Zone, peppered with ghosts and memories of past and future lives and loves.Item descriptions give glimpses of even more sinister world. Don't go into the shallows. Don't trust the clouds. Something is pushing against membrane in the sky, watching through the scanlines. A weirdcore level of wrongness.The characters' cheerful attitude and flashy design clashes with their nightmarish existence; they are not oblivious or cartoonishly evil, they are aware, just don't really care that much. Maybe they are just totally stoned all the time; I mean, who wouldn't be?Either way, they  what they are. And they  what they are doing.Including our protagonist, yes.And I absolutely love that. Unironically, zero hypocrisy in that mindset, just the very nature of these beings and the state of affairs. A refreshing take on an ordinary routine, so to say.These are all more of minor nitpicks or neutral things, which could be better.This is NOT a detective game. You play as an investigator, but there is next to none actual investigation work. Everything is built on exploration. Go everywhere, collect everything, talk to everyone. Yes, it all ties together nicely at the end, in a very satisfying way at that, and you can more or less influence the outcome and weave your own truth - assuming you have found enough evidence to make your own decisions on who to  accuse. But still, most of the mystery is being spelled out for you as you go. Yes, the plot/story is mildly engaging, has a number of unexpected twists and turns and red herrings, but it's completely outshined by  in the game. The story itself is strictly secondary to the brilliant worldbuilding. It's not necessarily a flaw though, but likely an artistic choice, a narrative decision - and I fully respect and accept that.Graphics are a bit sloppy. Everything is very low-poly, textures are simple and visibly tiled, and water looks more like a strange jelly. Perhaps this was a trade-off - the island is choke-full of little details and lush greenery, animated, glistening, reflecting; the map is fairly big, elaborate and seamless, and you can see most of it from a vantage point; and with all of that the game runs very smooth on max settings, with only minor pop-in noticeable from time to time. Besides, the visuals do their job in conveying the style and creating atmosphere, the game looks pretty and all needed visual cues are very distinct.The characters are flat in every sense of the word. Partial voice acting is confusing, visual novel style catch phrases are mostly cringe, but you get used to that and they become a natural part of the garish presentation.The open structure of the game is both a blessing and a curse. I just picked a direction and went wherever, getting lost in absolutely massive residential area for hours; the game allows you to do that, I can appreciate that, but so many lines and plot points will be out of order. And with a huge amount of collectibles in this game, you rarely find anything worthwhile; mostly it's all kinds of fluff and currency - collecting for the sake of the process itself, dopamine dings and bits of lore.Paradise Killer is definitely not a game for everyone. It's very niche both in overall feel and gameplay, its themes are based on a specific worldview and aesthetics, which may not be your cup of tea or even cause strong rejection. But if you feel it calling to you, if you are vibing with it, then go for it without doubts. It's one of a kind, unforgettable experience.Your visit into this infinitely intriguing world is unforgivably brief. Perhaps it's meant to be this way - a fleeting reality, subtle like butterfly wings. You've seen all there is to see, done all you could, and now the birds are dead, the skies are red, the seas are raging and the music is failing. As credits roll, as Island 24 inevitably slips into oblivion, under a spell of a nostalgic song we can only dream about our own Perfect 25.  Preferably with less (or ) carnage.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: After years playing Ace Attorney and Danganronpa games, the desire for a trial where it's up to me to decide the culprit and make sure to gather all the evidence is real. Finally, a game has let me be the investigator and follow the leads rather than the storyline. Paradise Killer is brilliant, one of those games that move an entire genre forward on their own, and one of those games I wish I could forget so I can enjoy it again.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I always love a good mystery/whodunnit, so I was intrigued by this game. It combines a really vibey aesthetic and soundtrack, incredibly unique worldbuilding and eccentric characters to build an experience I still think about. It's really fun going around and unravelling the story, so if you like detective games it's definitely worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: So, up front, recommending this with a catch. I really enjoyed what it brought to the table, but it isn't quite what it advertises.It WILL give you a great setting, a clash of styles that I've taken to calling "Cthulhu vaporwave." Miami beach condos within view of walled-off sites of demonic destruction and temples of marble and gold where immortals make blood sacrifices to alien gods. The main draw of the game is to wander the island, bob your head to the future funk soundtrack, and enjoy the strange characters and stranger locations.It WON'T give you a deep investigative experience. Paradise Killer is much closer to a walking simulator than a game where you would actually need to solve mysteries. You can dig up information for your investigation for at least a dozen hours, but the reward is mostly the journey itself. You can end the search and begin the trial as soon as you have enough evidence to point a finger at anyone. The end result is of little consequence, and the trial itself is probably the least interesting part of the game even though it puts some finishing touches on what you found before then, but the journey is, in my opinion, enthralling.The other aspects of the game that you are better off knowing beforehand are regarding the collectibles. Blood crystals are the currency used for any exchanges:Secrets, purchased from a particular character, which can aid in your investigation.Drinks from vending machines, which are purely for lore if you want to know more.Foot baths, which, for whatever reason, give you powerups which make navigation significantly easier: one gives you the ability to see hidden objects, the other lets you double-jump. Neither of which you need, but are helpful.Drinks, purchased from another character, to allow you to have chats with them.And the fast travel system, both unlocking nodes as well as using them to travel between them. This is the part of the game that I think just flat-out sucks, since it encourages you to not use the conveniences you've earned, but since I finished the game with 40 crystals in my pocket and I'm sure I missed a few, I think you can be fairly liberal in your use of them to go to areas that you know will have new developments.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Probably not as politically meaningful (and definitely not as open-ended) as Disco Elysium, and not as cleverly contrapted as Return of the Obra Dinn - but still, those are personal favorites of mine and arguably among Paradise Killer's closest peers in these regards. This one's politics are definitely a lot less silly than they appear to be at first - on the contrary, the allegories seem to me to hold up pretty well, with the general population being used as cannon fodder by elites that care only about their own well-being, ideological disputes and power plays (with the military having to pick their side), their indifference to everything else playfully disguised as sun-bathed cosmic horror (and it actually works, somewhat surprisingly so). Also, the complete freedom given in how to proceed with the investigation (who do you talk to, what do you discuss, what do you look for, how thoroughly you do so, who do you accuse in the end, for what and based on which evidence etc.), while a little overwhelming at first, becomes tremendously engaging as things go and leads to a surprisingly complex endgame: piecing everything together right before the final series of trials was both intellectually challenging and very rewarding, while the ending felt right in its ambivalence.Oh, and of course, the game's presentation (visuals, music) and sense of style are both top-notch.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: At the very start I didn’t get the game at all, it was weird and surreal, but slowly, as I started to collect stuff and walk around the island, I started to like it more, it’s really cool and really surreal, I enjoyed it so much that I got EVERYTHING I COULD. It’s not a game for everyone, but all the lore and the cult like stuff is really cool to learn.You gotta give it a shot, the lore is weird but very interesting, and as you slowly explore and learn more about the case, you start to understand the world more. It has great characters and REALLY good music.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10The mystery keeps you on your toes until the end. really solid game for such a small studio. Now there are some minor points that knock a few points off this game for me:I personally find the Island to be WAY TOO BIG. Can't say I'm a fan of running around so much.Also most of the collectibles are absolutely useless, unless you're into meaningless lore. The blood stones on the other hand you pretty much NEED to collect if you stumble across them cause they fuel fast travel and you will fast travel, A LOT, unless you enjoy wasting your own time. While playing, you keep darting around between these characters, learning new information. You don't wanna walk the same, sometimes very convoluted path to reach the character you need 20 times or more. Also the distorted sound the collectibles make when you're near them is so annoying I felt like I wanted to pick them up just to get rid of the noise. Even though these might sound like a lot of negative criticisms, I thoroughly enjoyed my time with this game. I'm looking forward to their future projects
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: "I'll grab a drink 'cos it's gonna take a while, To get a taste for the lie behind the smile"Straight-forward "detective", item collection game. But where this game really shines is the story & atmosphere! The characters and lore of this world are so deep and rich, you can't help but get absorbed. And the vaporwave synth soundtrack is amazing. It ties together the pop-like graphics of this beautiful, superficial environment with the hidden darkness of a brutal dystopia.It really is a shame that this game isn't more popular and widely known. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hard review to write. There is a lot to love here and I'm all onboard to play a followup game in the same style if this dev wants to make one. Then game would have greatly benefited from a better introduction. It dose a decent job of teaching you how to play but the game throws you immediately into investigating a murder mystery with no time to bond with with the suspects and the world is also such a unique fantasy setting it's hard to get into the world at first because there is nothing grounding you to the setting. When this game get's going it's incredibly fun tracking down leads and unwinding this complex and strange murder mystery in an unique version of the afterlife. While many twists are predictable, figuring out why and how the different inhabitants on the island committed various crimes is genuinely thrilling. The problem arises towards the end when you spend the majority of your time tracking down leads that end up re-enforcing what you already knew.The game's conclusion isn't as explosive or as exciting as similar games so it ends on kind of a low note. All the revelations are stuff you have already figured out but that's the nature of this game. It's more about the investigation and less about the trial which is a interesting take but it means the high point of the story is hours before the end and it ends when you either track down every lead or get tired of looking.The bulk of this game is fantastic and must be experienced but it would have benefited greatly from a more exciting introduction and conclusion. If you are looking for something to play after painscreek killings is very similar in structure but dose not have the production values of this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: 2/5Pros:Edgy narrative with plenty of flashy elements.Unique and distinctive art style.Cons:Too many details introduced before giving players a general understanding of the world settings.Excessive conversations before the actual gameplay begins.Causes me 3D motion sickness, making it hard to play for more than 30 minutes.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: AA - Absolutely Astonished. Wonderful Visuals, Sounds, OST, Story.... Dont expect too much from the gameplay (Its more of a novel and walk aroundie finding things). But gosh i wasnt even mad about that.... The game is soo beautiful, its just great to be there.I do recommend getting to the Trials after finishing all the notes.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: 3.5 / 5.0Paradise killer is a first-person open world investigation game that revolves around solving a murder mystery. The game has a lot of character and style and it's undoubtedly influenced by the works of Suda 51/Grasshoper Manufacture in several aspects such as character designs, visual art direction, quirky stories/dialogues, and even audio effects. The world/island is very fun to explore and features collectibles and different places to explore and gather clues for your investigation. Interestingly enough, you can go to the final trial as soon/late as you want. The idea is to gather as many clues as possible to hone down on what characters are suspects and finally guilty but ultimately there is no right or wrong ending in terms on who's at fault; it all depends on your personal judgment and interpretation of how the case went based on the testimonials and clues you gathered. Overall, I highly recommend this game if you are a fan of Suda 51 works and are looking for a unique investigation/detective game thanks to its setting and characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Played this mostly on Switch, but man this game is oozing with style and charm. Memorable characters, and an interesting story. I'm not quite finished with it, but I am intrigued by how so many people seem to have different motives, and it's up to you to decide which leads you want to pursue, and what you believe is the truth.Quite mysterious. I'm being somewhat vague, because it really is something worth experiencing without too much before knowledge.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: There's really nothing else like this. A detective game that essentially engages in no hand-holding. Beyond markers reminding you that you have new questions for the other characters, the game is perfectly willing to let you miss evidence that is absolutely material to the investigation. The structure of the trial at the end supports the open-ended nature of the investigation mechanics - you're free to accuse anyone of any of the committed crimes. The final sequence of the game is a bit less reactive than one might like, but the number of permutations that the trial can potentially take probably precluded characters reacting to some of the more informed choices the player can make about who to accuse. More games like this, please.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: A crazy, open world, detective game in a style that's best described as "a threesome between Danganronpa, Jojo and Phoenix Wright" Outstanding aesthetics and art direction. Great, inspired soundtrack. An open world mistery free for you to unravel at the pacing you want, disclosing itself as you chill out, free roam in the smartly crafted Paradise Island or talk to the interesting and quirky suspects and witnesses you'll meet. There's Lovecraftian horror to be found here, too (as you are investigating the murder of the heads of a cult - which you are a part of - whose goal is to bring back to life ancient dead gods from outer space), but beware: it's Lovecraftian horror completely revamped by the modern Vaporwave sensitivity affirmed today. Summarizing, last, but no least: this game is great and, more important thing, has reshaped the rules of detective games adapting them to an open world map, devoid of the usually hand driven narrative of this type of games.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This game is good, setting is interesting (alien gods who require a paradise planet for normal human gods? Something to that degree.) Very vaporwave and good music to boot. Overall an interesting game if you enjoy talking to characters and gathering evidence to come to a conclusion you are happy with and learning about a strange and unique world that combines a 90s retro feel with a strange spiritual presence to it.You can skip this part of the review as it is more of my personal opinion:My only complaint is that you only meet one alien god and the explanation for things in the world don't answer much. I really enjoyed learning about the world but it only had me asking more questions than anything. Also some of the aesthetics make things look more satanic/evil than divine. It truly doesn't seem like much care was put into the religious aspect of the game and the characters except for one are even deeply religious or religious at all. With a game built around gods especially polytheism it seems more that the aesthetics were really focused on rather than the material itself. It's just really confusing because it seems more like nobody even cares about the gods at all yet they spend all these resources to appease them. I won't drone on but if that aspect of the story was nailed or at least had some better direction then I think the games story and setting would have really flourished. Other than that, it was fun playing and exploring.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: In Paradise Killer, you are an immortal investigator, recently released from eternal exile to solve a heinous locked-room murder mystery. The main attraction here is in the details of the setting: the style, sound design, character design, music, lore, writing, everything about the aesthetic is fantastic. The story itself is sufficiently twisty and takes a lot of exploring and investigating to discover the whole picture. The characters are all great, even the ones I hated. You can really feel all the love and attention that the small dev team put into making it, especially in all the small QoL touches throughout.My main gripes while I was playing through it were that the actual platforming controls were pretty nasty (though did improve by the end) and that the copyediting could have used a little work. I would also say that, by the end, the world started to feel a little empty and small as I had explored every nook, cranny, and dialog option. And the actual trial itself (and ending) weren't nearly as satisfying as uncovering all the evidence in the first place. I imagine that if I hadn't been so thorough in my explorations the trial might have been more interesting, as there were no surprises in it for me.Nevertheless, none of those gripes are enough to ruin anything about the experience for me. I'm still hung up on how I feel about the Day Breaks.Overall, this was a unique world that was a ton of fun to explore, especially earlier on as I was still getting the hang of it, and I very much enjoyed the time I spent in it. I don't think it holds much in the way of replay value, but the 17 hours I spent here left a pretty big impression the first time through, and I would happily recommend this at full price ($20). I even went so far as to immediately go and buy the soundtrack and art book DLC after finishing, just to support them.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty good.First hour was learning the premise of the game, it's mechanics and controls, and then you're thrown into investigating a mass murder. After that, I spent another 8 hours interrogating each suspect, and every character is really cool, except for Yuri and Akiko. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.The city was cool. Getting around with Blood shards and stuff was quite annoying however, and it could've shaved down an hour or two of game play if you just had to unlock fast travel points instead of unlocking them and then paying to fast travel. The movement in this game is also kind of eh. Trying to jump over stuff was a pain sometimes, even with the double jump upgrade. The dark zone and Second Seal room were also very atmospheric and gave me a bit of anxiety going through them.The trial was satisfying. It didn't feel like I wasted my time majority of the evidence I presented. Although, it felt very simple to get the right verdicts if you spent the same amount of time as I did. The most interesting part of the trial was choosing which suspect is responsible for each case file, which I enjoyed even though there were at most three people to choose from.This game has mad potential, and if it got a DLC or expansion that involves the 25th Island, I would play it in a heartbeat.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beautiful. I love the high tech future atmosphere. Wandering around the desolate island looking for clues and money is fun and interesting. I particularly like that they have audio clues for things you're supposed to find. I looooove the synth music that plays sporadically throughout the game, and that one of the rewards for exploring everything is more music tracks. The dialogue is a little over the top wacky and metaphysical, but you kind of adjust to it, and I got to the point where finding Shinji, the blue demon who follows you around, was really something I looked forward to. Some of the character illustrations were honestly gorgeous, others could have used a little refining. And ALL of the voice acting is bad. Really. Bad. Overall, this is not going to be a game for everyone. It's a little hard to figure out what's going on and how to actually play the game, but after an adjustment phase it's almost relaxing. I really have enjoyed my time in paradise island #24.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Fascinating game lay, you actually get to feel like a detective as youre mainly left to make your own conclusions. The world is huge and beautiful which also also includescollectibles to hunt down throughout the game. Most riddles are fun to solve, besides the nightmare computers which I found very boring. Luckily they dont take long to get past. The one thing that really disappointed me though is the implementation of the final trials which felt mostly like dialogue to click through. I wasnt really doing anything any more and there was no way to fail. So, for me, Paradise Killer was 22.5 hours of mystery solving with a somewhat anticlimactic ending. Still, the characters (esp. Shingi) and the ingenious conspiracy story make up for that.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: A lot people complain, that the trial at the end is not interactive enough.I think it was perfect to end this game this way. after all the collecting and exploring it was nice to get an elaborate ending with all the information you might've missed.The cool thing about this game is, that you can play it as long as you're motivated. And when you reach the point where you think it's enough, you can finish it, be it 15 mins, or 15 hours. Fantastic.And of course i have to mention the killer soundtrack!!
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I came into paradise killers with somewhat low expectations after picking it up in the humble bundle and giving it a go on whim, as visual novel type games aren't usually my thing. To say I was blown away would be a criminal understatement.It was a totally unique and refreshing experience that had me enthralled all the way through. It's been years since since I have played a game so captivated by the story and setting. Not only is the utterly bizarre world of paradise killer fascinating to explore and learn about, but the intertwined story of murder and conspiracy is gripping all the way through. The ending was great and it truly felt as if I had solved the case through exploration and detective work rather than being led there.The Visual style and soundtrack also leave nothing to be desired, both being exceptional in their own right. Add that on and I'm struggling to find faults with this masterpiece< and it makes me seriously excited to see what is next from Kaizen Game Works.I cannot recommend this incredible game enough, pick it up and give it a chance and I promise you will not be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic open world detective game! Wonderfully complex world and characters and lots of secrets and history to uncover. Music is fantastic! The aesthetic is a cool blend of vapor-wave and ancient Egypt which gives the island you explore are really lived-in feel. Writing is excellent and gives life to several wild characters such as Lady Love Dies, Doctor Doom Jazz, and Crimson Acid to name a few.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings on this game but I think that overall I would lean to recommending it. First of all, I think if you're looking for a crime solving investigation game, this might be a bit disappointing. I think the main gameplay is more of a collect-a-thon around a large map with occasionally frustrating platforming. The characters are fun, and for the first 6 hours of my playthrough I was invested in learning about them all and how the crime played out. At a certain point, about halfway through my playtime, I got tired of having to run back and forth to talk to characters about one small thing only for them to reveal another detail that meant having to run across the island to talk to the same character I had just spoken to. To not be too negative, I think that the soundtrack is stellar and the main theme, especially the version with lyrics that plays over the end credits, is such a great song that I've had it on loop on Spotify for days after completing the game. I think that for someone on the fence with this game, you should know that there is certainly an emphasis on exploration and that it can be overwhelming to see just how many collectibles there are scattered around the island. If you're looking for a really tight story with a clear, correct solution, this might not be for you. To the developers, I really do hope you make a sequel or at least another game in the same style. I feel like so many elements were so close to being great but a few too many frustrating design choices left me feeling a little lukewarm by the end. That being said, I still felt compelled to 100% the game so take from that what you will. My critiques come from a place of wanting to see this game fully realized and for it to reach its full potential and I hope that one day I can play another game from Kaizen Game Works!
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: the vaporwave aesthetic is p good there's a lot of good music to collect the world is very pretty the puzzles aren't very hard as u can brute force all of them as they are simple switch puzzles and the starlight puzzles are almost all the same so you'll probably try a few times on your first attempt and remember the patterns for the rest of the locksthe trial tho is a little too brutal, some characters had no real reason to be judged that harshly due to their contribution being so minuscule 2 characters are written in such a way that you know they are guilty and i think it's a bit sad mostly for the most involved of the 2 as their reasoning in partaking was completely understandable and their finale judgment too harsh, which i think kinda ruins the mystery. i was hoping for a big plot twist for that chara but it never really came overhaul its a good game with an amazing world with great vibes that you're free to explore, most characters are interesting and i'd recommend giving it a go if you like the vaporwave aesthetic and or like murder mysteries
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Paradise Killer is a weird looking game that isn't actually that weird once you get dug into it. Oh the character designs are a bit odd and there is that blue rectangle headed naked fox demon following you around but honestly at its core PK is just a kind of exploration/collectathon/detective game. You spend most your time going from place to place, hunting down leads, talking to people for testimonies, and occasionally finding new things off the beaten path. While not an overly long game if your just concerned with the trial aspect, there are enough collectables to keep you occupied for much much longer.   The game is not without its flaws, unfortunately explaining those flaws would require spoilers. Still even with them I would recommend the game to anyone looking to do some mystery solving without having the game hold your hand, because this game does not hold your hand very much at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: this is what indie games are all about. its experimental, it prioritises art direction over blind realism, and it isn't interested in wasting your time (yeah there's some backtracking to get all the testimonies, but that's what fast travels for). its not without problems, the platforming is a little stiff (but not strictly necessary) and some of the evidence is a little too well hidden (that's what meditation's for) but its heavily outweighed by all the positives. do yourself a favour and pick this game up if it looks or sounds even remotely interesting, you wont regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Very interesting setting and the best detective game I ever played, with the player free to explore the entire island at your own pace. Interesting point is that you can start the final trial whenever you want, and the game just gives you a result depending on the evidence you have and who you choose to accuse, without grading you on your outcome being "right". It's up to you whether you are satisfied with what you get.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This one's a little weird. It's a detective game about talking to suspects and uncovering secrets, sure, but it's also a 3D platformer collectathon with an unlockable double-jump and air-dash. It also takes place in a slightly bonkers setting that will take a while to fully understand, but I ultimately found very compelling. On top of all that, I think the sexy goat lady wants to sleep with me? I thought I was a respectable lady, but now I'm not so sure... What I'm trying to say is, you've got to meet the game on its level. I got a lot out of it and by the end was fully hooked by the mystery, characters, and aesthetics. But, know what you're getting yourself in for, I can imagine a lot of people bouncing off of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: A cool combination of a murder mystery visual novel and an explorey, first-person platformer, set in a psychedelic, glamorous, otherworldly paradise gone wrong. Feels like an avant-garde itch.io game on TONS of steroids, in the best possible way.My only criticism is that the game is badly in need of a map; there's one in-game but it looks like a joke that was drawn in MS Paint (which doesn't match the rest of the game at all), and I was perpetually lost and trying to find places I'd already been multiple times. This is alleviated somewhat by a feature that shows you the direction and distance of the characters, but doesn't help when trying to solve puzzles or navigate to a specific area or building.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this expecting a short, little indie game that I might open once or twice and then forget about it. I was wrong. There is clearly a ton of passion behind the game, and so much more content than I expected, especially for the price, and I'm probably not even halfway through. The game doesn't have AAA visuals, but has a surprisingly complex and compelling story that I cannot get enough of. The gameplay is hard to describe, but feels almost like a mixture of just about everything, and it works. I've been trapped at home with flickering power due to the recent storms in Texas, and honestly, all I've thought about was this game. It's easily one of my favorites now, and certainly enough for me to write my first game review, ever.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: this game is so bisexual it makes me so happy. apart from that the music is generally good vibes mixed with absolute banger and the character desing is just on point. the only grudge i have for this game is that the movement is pretty stiff when moving around and that the backstories of the previous islands should have been more mentioned. This is a solid 9/10 when it comes to a good single player game, but it's also an incredibly good game when it comes to asthethics.P.s: i can't wait for a game set in this universe (if it's a sequel or not) because i loved every single minute :D
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: fantastic game, kept a notepad with me and by the end it became a journal that looked like ramblings of some cultist fanatic. overwhelming at first but everything slowly falls into place.At times it can feel repetitive and I walked away to do something else but the mystery slowly seeped in, distracting me from whatever I was doing; I couldn't stop thinking about the case! These times where I wasn't playing the game were arguably the most immersive and it was at these times where I came to some groundbreaking theories that would bring me running back to the computer to follow the leads.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. The story was enjoyable and unique. I liked the exploration aspect of the game as well. If you like text based story games with exploration and unique story, this is for you. My only two cons would be the map itself was almost useless so getting around sometimes was a bit confusing and the ending seemed a little predetermined/let down. I was still satisfied with the game, but thought perhaps there should have been a bit better ending. Overall though this is a fantastic, fun game.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: if you're like me, you've probably asked yourself "what if eldritch cosmic horror gods were real, and what if rich tech bros leached their power to live forever and warp reality around them, creating a hopelessly stratified society in which they extract labor and literal blood from an underclass in order to feed their gods and themselves, and--for the sake of appearances--wrapped everything in a veneer of pastel vaporwave liberal democracy so that nobody feels too sad about it?"this game answers that very normal and common question. and also allows you to solve solve some murders.it's pretty good, and it only takes about 15 hours. the store page kind of sells it short, but it's definitely one of the most enjoyable things I've played this year.however... if you've ever unironically used the word "woke," I would be remiss if I did not offer some ⚠️Content Advisories⚠️ in order to help you decide on your purchase:❌game features Political genders and ethnicities❌protagonist is Political❌Political social commentary❌ladders and crates are Political (pink)✅woke feminists did NOT censor "vagina bones," even on male characters!

_childDocuments_.review: Idk. It's not bad and maybe I just had too hight expectations baased on other reviews, but there is simply not a single aspect above just ok.Idk, I've just played it for about 3 days, finished it to 100%, wasn't bored, had some basic satisfaction, but it just doesn't left anything inside me and probably will be completely forgoten in a couple of days
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game with an interesting plot and use of such, people find similarities to danganronpa (specially 2, which yeah it was cleary an influence) but i'd rather compare it to the kill the past games by suda51, a Flower, sun and rain with a bit of silver case mixed in so highly recommend if you like KTP and viceversa.While it wasn't the hardest mystery to solve (once you have most of the evidence the picture is pretty clear) it did have a few reveals that shocked me. The characters are very well utilized and it's great how you can choose which evidence to ignore or use circumstantial shenanigans to incriminate whoever you want, basically deciding if you wanna spare or doom anyone. This does come with a drawback, there's not really an ending? you just present evidence and those found guilty are executed, sure there's different dialogues but you don't really get anything out of choosing any route besides self satisfaction. Even so, it was a fun game and i enjoyed looking for evidence and interacting with the great cast.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: It's like someone made a non-linear Danganronpa game and threw in some collectathon elements + vaporwave and cosmic space-gods. Enjoyed the game most of the time and would gladly recommend it to anyone interested in playing a detective. Also a really good value for money since I invested about 20 hours in it. Definitely worth the time.That being said, there are some issues. The world is big and it takes a lot of time to navigate from one place to another, especially in the almost maze-like city. There is a fast-travel system, but it costs in-game money and I found it inconvenient altogether cause you can only travel to specific points on the map. This wouldn't be a problem, but there is a lot of back-and-forth running in the game, because every time you get a new clue, you get new dialogue options with one or multiple suspects. This is especially irritating when you discover a major alibi-breaking evidence and want to corner someone with it, travel across the map, and then all they have to say is something like "So what?". And that's it.Another weird and somewhat annoying design choice has to do with doors. There are a few special rooms in the game that you can access by opening a pink door in the game world. For some reason though, some of these doors are placed in locations that make absolutely no sense. For example, a random office door on the side of a building above a thousand mile abyss, accessible only by hugging the wall on a narrow ledge. I stumbled upon a lot of these by mere accident, not because I actually noticed them and decided to investigate.The final thing that bugged me a little was that I was kinda confused about how the endgame trial would actually play out once I reached that point in the game. Because of this, I wanted to exhaust every dialogue option and gather everything from the world just be sure I had everything I needed, cause I had no idea what I was expected to do in the trial. This kind of uncertainty felt a bit counterproductive to the "free-form" investigation the game wanted me to conduct.+ Interesting concept+ Soundtrack+ World building+ A E S T H E T I C S- Constant back and forth running- Poor fast travel system- Weird placement of some doors and evidence which you might or might not stumble upon by accident.- Unclear endgame requirements.

_childDocuments_.review: Unique artstyle, gorgeous soundtrack, interesting premise, and solid writing. While some of the text could have used editing (mostly with misplaced or omitted punctuation), the overall narrative flow is barely affected. The characters feel distinct from one another, and the story is engaging. The actual gameplay is somewhat sparse, only having a few puzzles and platforming sections, but it's easy to forget when you get absorbed into the story.This is one of the most unique experiences I've ever had with a video game. I struggled to describe it to my friends, as I struggle to do so here, but I can easily find the words to recommend this game.It's a beautifully illustrated investigation with an amazing soundtrack to accompany you on your interrogations of the interesting and unique citizens of Island 24. The story is riveting (though a bit confusing at first), and nothing is as it seems. Your investigations will show you how little of what you see can be trusted.I found the philosophical undertones engaging as the game grappled with deep universal questions such as "What purpose do we serve? How do we find meaning? Do you need to go to the bathroom in an eternal paradise?"Yes, this game even has a sense of humor.I highly recommend this game. It's relatively short (~15 hours for me, and I completed essentially everything) and incredibly engaging.

_childDocuments_.review: Paradise Killer is a wonderful, wacky detective game of the likes I've never played. The game is two games in one. The bigger part of the game is a first-person walking sim where you wander around a VR dayglo vaporwave island picking up random collectables that add to the lore and occasionally provide evidence in the cases you are investigating. The smaller part of the game is an Ace Attorney-style visual novel that triggers when you enter into dialog with the characters or start the final trial.The walking sim section is the better game. The vaporwave aesthetic is perfect, and it's a delight to wander the buildings and the beaches listening to the relaxing synthpop soundtrack. There are no jumping puzzles, no timed puzzles, no enemies, so you can investigate at your own pace. You feel like a real detective, checking out different locations, hacking locks and scouring the scene for clues. The world is aggressively weird at first, but as you persevere with the lore you start to get a feel for this strange island and its culture.The VN section is a bit less successful. The dialog itself is well-written, and although the characters exist in a bizarre, alien world, they feel believable in that context. Uncovering their motives is a lot of fun, as is flirting and engaging in casual banter... But by the end it feels like there is little emotional weight behind any of the relationships, because the light-hearted tone of the dialog doesn't change even when you uncover clear evidence of guilt. Then at the trial you can choose to accuse and convict anyone you like, which results in summary executions that none of the surviving characters react to either. I understand the technical reason - if the developers had set up a more linear storyline with scripted emotional beats, then it would undermine the open world/free roam investigative concept - but it's still a bit of a let-down.All that said, if you like walking sims or detective games, Paradise Killer is worth buying. It has a strong aesthetic, the world is deep, the characters feel believable (at least during the early/mid-game) and it is a ton of fun investigating the crimes.

_childDocuments_.review: In Paradise Killer, you play as a detective who has just come out of exile (prison) and is tasked with solving a large crime. Explore the weird and wonderful world of Paradise Killer to see if you can KILL JUSTICE.DLC?There is no playable DLC, the rest of the DLC is just OST, B-Sides and Artwork.Game's Story - 9/10The game's story is wonderful. It's very unique and has a lot of interesting premises. I enjoyed solving the mystery but felt there were still several things that just weren't commented on, which felt important to the case.Visuals - 4/5The visuals are also very unique and serve the game well, my favourite part about the visuals were the crime scenes which I felt gave a nice and shocking contrast to the rather cartoony feel of the game.Audio - 6/10SFX - 3/5I got nothing to say here, nothing to complain about. Nothing stands out but nothing exactly shocking. They tried to put some voice acting in the game, however it felt unnecessary since each character could only say about 10 things.Music - 3/5The music is fine, it isn't bad but I just don't feel anything from it.Gameplay - 6/10A lot of people call this a walking simulator, but they fail to acknowledge that the detective side of things is a part of the gameplay. Yes, there is a lot of walking and a few uninteresting puzzles and collectibles. However, the investigation makes the game intriguing and interesting and that is a part of the gameplay, if it wasn't though the gameplay score would be much lower.Value For Money - 7/10If you can you might as well try to pick it up on a sale but it isn't too bad at full price either.Other - 4/5Performance - 2/2The game runs extremely well.Bugs - 2/2I found a bug, which softlocked me when I was going for the Speedrun Achievement. However, it was very obscure and I probably only activated it via my auto-clicker. Other than that, I didn't find any game bugs at all. Little tip: You can hold "R" to respawn.Community - 0/1There is basically no community for this game, at all. Which is expected for singleplayer story games.Overall - 74/100This is a great and unusual murder mystery game, that you will definitely enjoy if you can get into a story. There is a lot of accessibility options which is nice. Also, remember to turn on Adult Content because all it does is censor swear words and you might as well have them uncensored.

_childDocuments_.review: Frankly, this is one of the best murder mystery games out there. The general aesthetic is.... special, as you can see from the screenshots, and I was a little doubtful going in, but it's grown on me a lot. Every single person had distinctive and complex character development, the world building is immense and very original, and the case itself is really complicated but holds really well together once you've found all the evidence. I always felt very engaged in solving the mystery, even if the infodump at the beginning could be a little overwhelming at first.A few minor pitfalls: Something about the movement made me slightly seasick at times. Also, some of the most crucial pieces of evidence can only be found by randomly stumbling around the island, and I don't recommend starting the trial until all leads have been cleared and all evidence is collected, as every single piece counts.Finally, going back and forth between different people can get tiring near the end once you've explored everything else, I recommend using fast travel liberally. Still, strong recommend from me, this was a very creative and memorable experience

_childDocuments_.review: Paradise Killer has forced me to think about a world where everyone is superbly attractive and shop at an H&M catering to fashion designers. When the palm trees sway in the ocean breeze on island 24, the wood groans a detached sigh about the malaise of paradise. The farms are flanked by perfect pyramids beckoning the farmer to dream of life off of the land they were abducted to. Island 24 is a beautiful thing. Vast apartment blocks tower over intimate parks with gilding generously applied to everything. It's a space made to worship, and when walking through the comically long hallways, it's hard not to feel blessed by a sweet curse.It's residents, or what remains of them, feel perfect too in a sad way. They long for things outside their station, promises unspoken, denied by birth, by love, by circumstance. Love Dies, the detective freak, was conned a long time ago and forced to exile. The crime to end all crimes has happened, and without the intervention of Love Dies, the involved may find the things they seek. But to call their pursuit justice, that is not the truth, and a detective has to find truth. You will be treated to a lush soundtrack, spaces contort in uncomfortable ways, but I found a lot of comfort in navigating the weird vistas of 24. I can only dream of what "Perfect 25" might look like. In this game too, I wonder what might happen if more people were involved. At the core is a game about walking, talking, and collecting. Objects are placed with a steady deliberation, but the logic can be unreadable much to the games credit. Would more time and effort make Paradise Killer better? Would inventory systems, multiplayer, high scores, rich animated figures really benefit this composition?Paradise Killer kept accidentally directing my attention to what this thing could be, and it was distracting from the thing that it is. If not for the demonic invasion, could people be happy on 24, paradise that it might be. I found myself in their longing, but for what comes next. I do not know if there is such a thing as a better Paradise Killer, but I do know that Paradise Killer is inspiring enough a product to bring interested eyes to the future of this team. Characters swirl in layers upon each other, the efforts of Love Dies often bring discomfort as more truth becomes known. Worth putting the time in, and worth sinking the dollar in for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: A brilliant adventure/detective game where you are an investigator for a Doomsday Cult. An age-proof cult called The Syndicate attempts to create paradise on earth by establishing man-made Islands to which they abduct people to worship the elder gods. The worship is supposed to usher paradise but can also invite demonic corruption. Time after time, demons show up, an island is "killed", 'citizens', that is the abducted labor and prayer force are "purged" and a new island is made. In-between the tranistion to what was to be the best Island yet, the heads of the cult are killed. So they turn to you, an Invetigator exiled many Islands ago for demonic corruption. Interrogate suspects, find evidence and then make your case in court for whom should be held liable and what should the penalty be. The game can "end" at any time, as you can start the end trial whenever you want, but you know, you should have a solid idea of what went on first. Or just wing it. Up to you. Depending on your investigation and how persuasive you are, who gets punished, and for what can change every playthrough. Heck, you might find yourself not giving the court the full picture depending on how you view the situation. The premise and setting are fantastic, and the detectiving is more than solid. The game has a very particular aesthethic but it will grow on you. Dont miss this one.

I couldn't stop exploring, trying to figure out the puzzles, finding people to talk to and finding as many items as possible, The story is wild, the blue demon is hilarious and I found myself completely engrossed in the world.I don't know what I was expecting, but this wasn't it. _childDocuments_.review: Had a wonderful time with this indie gem, it's definitely a little rough around the edges but it's absolutely worth your time and money if you're even remotely a fan of murder mystery games.Paradise Killer exists at the cross-section of Danganronpa and something more open ended like Disco Elysium, with a simple collectathon tagged on for good measure. What makes it unique in the genre is that the game actually expects you to do the investigating, figure out what happened and come up with conclusions yourself - no part of this process is particularly complex in this game but doing all of it on your own time and thinking things through with your own human brain is actually super satisfying. Coming into the trial knowing exactly what happened, who did what and the whole sequence of events is a great feeling.Finally, it's what I always wanted, a game that lets you feel like Poirot calling in all the suspects at the end of the story and telling them exactly how it is! All of this doesn't even touch on the crazy, intriguing setting, surprisingly in-depth and compelling world-building or great sound track. Great little game, I'm looking forward to checking out whatever the developer comes up with next.

_childDocuments_.review: I had no idea what I was getting myself into with this game, as the only other mystery game I've played like this was Disco Elysium, which is incredible in its own right, but this game blew my f**king socks off. It took a little while to pick up some steam, and I'll admit that I definitely spent the first several hours at least kinda bored and just wandering around, waiting for the story to pick up, but when it does,  This game legitimately had me thinking about it when I wasn't playing, and trying to work out the details of the plot as it was  engaging once it started to open up a bit. If you're feeling a bit apprehensive, I get you, as I was a bit apprehensive as well staring at this game in my library, not knowing at all what any of this is going to be like, but after completing it, I can safely say this is a game legitimately so good I wish I could empty my brain of knowledge about it and replay it again fresh.

_childDocuments_.review: Paradise Killer is what you get if you crossed the tone and stylings of Suda 51’s games, Ace Attorney, a bit of a collectathon platformer, and a whole bunch of dead mall style vaporwave. I first played the demo back during Ludo Narra Con months back and it intrigued me and I’m happy to see that it ended up being one of the best detective games I’ve played alongside the likes of Sherlock Holmes: Crimes and Punishments, Her Story, and Obra Dinn. Paradise Killer does its own unique style of detective game, with a strong focus on exploration as you travel around the 24th Paradise to find clues that helps you solve the case. The game guides you a bit on potential leads to follow so you have an idea how much you still need to do but it does not hold your hand at all when it comes to interpreting all your collected evidence to figure out whodunnit. You also interrogate suspects, but it’s less like say, Ace Attorney and Contradiction, where you have to trap them in their lies, but more of showing them evidence or asking them about their or other characters’ alibis and motives to glean more information. You also interact them to build rapport so they can eventually open up to you with more clues. You will have to do some exploring if you want to get currency to help solve the case but I honestly felt it entertaining to do, though you don’t need to go too crazy, I had a large surplus of blood crystals for most of the game. You also can get two upgrades that aid you with this, a double jump and a secret radar that makes this easier. There’s also sidequests to do and just random minutiae to collect that adds to the game’s world-building of the setting. Said setting is a real interesting one too, a world of decadent zealot blood cultists sacrificing the downtrodden underclass like livestock to try and make a “perfect paradise” for their insane cosmic horror gods; the anti-capitalist allegory isn’t hard to get. The vaporwave aesthetic really genuinely helps to build the satire and allegory of the game too, as it utilizes the satirical edge of the genre that mocks consumer culture exemplified in the 80’s mall; exploring Paradise 24 even feels like exploring a dead mall because most of its denizens have packed up to leave to the 25th instance of Paradise, “Perfect 25.” The character writing is solid too as you have to deal with a bunch of oddball suspects in your quest for the truth. The soundtrack, mainly compromised of vaporwave, is also great, being peak chill.You can actually go right to the trial at any time and can do so immediately once you’re let loose, though obviously you aren’t gonna get the full picture at all. But when you do really put the work into it it’s a really great climax that feels rewarding when you successfully pieced everything together and you can pretty much do that where there is barely any loose ends. One problem though is that because the game goes with the mentality that there is no “right solution” even though there clearly is a correct path to your investigation that ties everything together it makes the denouement of the game super weak. The characters have nothing to really comment about the results of the trial and the game doesn’t really take what you did into account much in said denouement. The protag, Lady Love Dies, especially feels completely removed from the ramifications of the trial that can happen and you’re just straight up railroaded into having her just move to Perfect 25 even though you can play as her someone that despises the Paradise Elite for her unjust exile and their corrupt society and is only solving the case out of obligation/love of investigating. She also has nothing to say about you potentially executing people she considers old friends which is pretty glaring. This railroading also rather ruins the themes of the story a bit too because it feels like the writers kind of just threw their hands in the air and said “Hey maybe the 25th instance of this dystopia designed by insane capitalist blood priests won’t be completely awful too?!” The weirdest thing is in this post-trial section is that you can just randomly gun down or exile people which just feels tacked on and undermines the importance of the trial and all the work you put into it.  Despite all this it doesn’t truly ruin the game, it’s just a disappointment how much the game peters out in its denouement because of everything before it being so strong.Ultimately though Paradise Killer is a fantastic and stylish detective game that belongs aside the greats and is one of my favorite games of this year.

_childDocuments_.review: Very unusual and interesting, but not without flaws. It's indie, so don't expect high production value in all areas. If I had to define its main genre, it would be "3D platformer" (in 1st person), but you may like this even if, like me, you don't care much about this kind of game. Here are my comments divided in topics: by far the best the game has to offer. The lore, the characters (and their names), the worldbuilding, it's all very good, weird and unique. The plot itself is not brilliant, but this universe is fantastic and I hope we get to revisit it (in Perfect 25 or in a previous or future island sequence), even if it's in a totally different gaming genre.  Initially I was really bothered (since "Deadly Premonition" I wasn't so put off by a game's graphics), but they grew on me after a while. It gets better when you disable the night/day cycle, because the game looks worse at night _ also, it makes more sense, because the action happens on a single day after the crime. Reminded me a bit of the original "Myst"; it has a retro feel and it's more quirky than beautiful.  Not the most optimized game. I had to turn off reflections to make it run smoothly. Played the DX12 version.  Good overall. Voice acting is very sparse, but not bad. The lauded soundtrack is OK, especially when the  (which only happens during the ).  Not really great as a detective or courtroom game ("L.A. Noire", "Sherlock Holmes: Crimes & Punishments" and "Aviary Attorney" are better in those regards). You just collect evidence and make interviews (and for the most part dialogue choices don't matter). When you are ready to wrap up, there are trials and , even if they . Besides, afterwards you can , even without . Most of the game consists of exploration of the small, but intricate open world _ this is , though, since it's highly interactive and demands 3D platforming abilities if you're going to be thorough.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a surreal murder mystery about the death of god-like beings in a not so perfect paradise. It has an incredibly interesting world and engaging characters that I can't help but think about regularly. The game is never what you think, it always finds new ways to surprise and intrigue you. I had low expectations at the start, as this kind of game isn't normally my thing, but this quickly shot up as one of my favorite games of all time. I simply can't recommend it enough.

This game reminds me of The Blackwell Chronicals mixed with Danganronpa (except in this game, Joey from BWC's is a laptop ahahahaha!!!). It's a WILD combination that I could never even dreamed of encountering. Amazingly well done. Some of the conversation is a bit... interesting? The most fun I had was in collecting the currency spread across the whole island and then buying some powerups to get even more money. The protagonist, as for a fat girl, can really jump. _childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: A collectathon game with detective elements, not the other way around.I expected it to be more like Ace Attorney or Danganronpa in terms of the general process, but in the end your choices don't really matter much outside of pointing out suspects at the very end, which are heavily telegraphed in most cases. It's basically a visual novel that's even less interactive than the games mentioned.Controls are pretty damn bad, honestly. Not only does your character barely have air control when jumping, the dashing move you unlock doesn't change your character's flight trajectory after using it, leading to a good amount of frustration when trying to get those pesky relics and clues somewhere high up.The premise of the game and the case itself are pretty good, but it had  much "fictional" stuff thrown in, for my taste at least: . At some point I just stopped trying to unravel the story myself and basically thought "Whatever, we'll see what devs came up with this time, no need to think about reasons/causes much since new stuff gets made up so fast.". Obviously this wasn't the case with Ace Attorney/Danganronpa games, they were pretty grounded in reality while still having mythical stuff there and there, it was fun to figure stuff out.7/10, had fun clearing the entire map even with annoying controls.

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyable vaporwave, (small) open world, murder investigation with KILLER music.  The demo turned me off initially with the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥-y writing (mostly from Shinji) and character designs that felt like they were trying too hard BUT once i settled into the groove of the game, all that was in the rear-view.  There's some minor aesthetic, UI and sundry annoyances (tip: turn off voices after a couple of hours) but I actually sat down to beat the game and thought about playing it during the day, which is a lot more than I can say for nearly every other game I've played for the past couple of years.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: For people who adore the Zero Escape / Nonary Game series, AI: Somnium Files, Pheonix Wright, and Danganronpa series and looking for something like them this is NOT for you.The world is interesting and the characters are OK, but I felt no attachment to either. The world is littered with collectibles which are supposed to serve as tidbits of interesting lore but instead just waste your time. The game is littered with animations all of which serve little purpose but to waste your time. Every single collectible you pick up - including the game's generic currency - displays a full-screen flash-card + audio queue that needs to be manually closed out of. Every single time you 'fast' travel, you have to go to a telephone, wait for a loading screen to get into the vehicle, THEN choose a location to teleport to. Finally the 'detective' piece - what I believed should be the most important part of the game is simply a collectathon as well with the most anticlimactic payoff I've seen. Throughout the game you literally go into your menu and go through a checklist of items to figure out until the list is no longer there, running back and forth and back and forth and back and forth between the suspects as you go. As you collect the evidence you piece together a 'truth'.The trial, which after ~7 hours of running around in circles for clues consists of no cross-examination, accusation, back and forth. No catching people in a lie, contradiction, or detective work needed. Just another checklist with a bunch of dialogue. Now I'm not saying every game needs to be Danganronpa, but I mean there is no payoff at all. I was holding out and genuinely excited for the trial, and it was entirely flaccid. Endings are critical for me in games and this one left a bad taste in my mouth. It's open ended, which is fine, and you design your own truth - but there's only 1-2 real answers, and the game basically tells you who to choose as well. The immortal demi-gods of the world practically roll over once you provide your checklist that you ran around collecting. The entire end felt lackluster, unimpactful, tacky and most of all unsatisfying - and in my opinion is the most important part of these types of games.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, enthralling story, hours aren't accurate because I spend a lot of time thinking about what might have happened even when not playing. It has a great art direction and soundtrack that I wish was in more games. Overall there really isn't any flaws if looking for a great story driven mystery game but if you are looking for gameplay there isn't a lot more than some simple puzzles and walking to talk to people. _childDocuments_.review: Disregard my playtime, I had a friend play it and I also did all the achievement.I never played danganrompa or all other games that people compare this game to, so all I can say is that while at start it's hard to grasp what is going on (maybe I'm just slow idk) by the nature of mine (and hopefully yours) curious mind I started to put pieces together, not only to solve the various mysteries but also the nature of the universe this game takes part.the crime(s) is very complicated by nature and even when you think you have a lead new branches splits in your way but overall the story is well constructed.my only dislike is the collect-a-ton that this game offers, there are like 100 items and you'll only need like 6-7 to complete the game yet the world is scatterd with those. nice flavor text but gets boring when it becomes too much (in my opinion) also the value in the game, blood crystals, don't worry too much about it, you'll find plenty enough to buy all the things they are used for. so if you ever see a prompt to spend them, do it, better sooner than later you'll end up needing anythithing that can be bought with crystals anyway.non spoiler but if you collect them all and you are worried about the fast travel costs, I had used fast travels only 10 times and I had like around 40 crystals left after buying up EVERYTHING that could be bought, so just use your crystals without problems and you'll be less tressed than I was lol

_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Such an odd world. I love it for all its quirks and color. I’m just not convinced that I love the game. It’s a whodunnit, set on an island paradise where man has transcended his limitations, and is now constructing a series of island resorts in search of a perfect paradise. It’s a pure adventure game, with character and dialogue and conflicting motivations. But it’s also staged in a rather big world, where you traverse where you want, when you want -- horizontally and vertically. It’s a weird combination. And not necessarily one where the one genre complements the other. But it is what it is, I guess. It’s one of the few games I’ve played that has tasked me with both parkouring around, gathering relevant and irrelevant collectibles like a platformer -- whilst also unralveing a murder plot in a tighly scripted narrative by interviewing inhabitants and witnesses.There’s a lot to process at the outset, but it does reside a bit into the background as soon as you encounter the colorful cast of characters and start to converse. The story is actually very fun, with loads of twists and turns -- and some unexpected genre bending to go with it. It’s unique, to say the least.Carefully recommended, if you think you like this sort of thing. Whatever it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: An open-world murder mystery game with killer vaporwave visual appeals and city-pop soundtracks. The game has creative and interesting level design along with fun traversal system, somewhat akin to 3D platformer games, which encourages you to explore the whole places (and the plotline) freely with maximum degree of player's agency. The game's writing along  with its unique level design contribute to the superb world and character building along with their expansive, lush, and luxurious lore. Confusing at first glance, the lore, characters, and the plot have lots of depth and coherence as well; while they're absurd and ridiculous, they still make more sense than Danganronpa's. Gameplay-wise, while Paradise Killer might not be as mentally challenging as Return of the Obra Dinn (as it's just exploring and talking to ppl), I feel like it manages to make you feel like an actual detective more, similar to Her story, because you need to form hypotheses and stories from evidences and testimonies by yourself and the truth is what you made from facts you discovered.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and interesting Detective game that exceeded my expectations. So far I do not have any gripes, except that the fast travel system is hard to initially understand the specific locations after choosing a general area, since it is through text and not specific points on the map.(Edit): I initially wanted to mention that it was kind of difficult to find things, and that I was afraid of running out of a limited currency. This is actually not much of an issue. All I will say is that I recommend treating your character well, pamper them, it'll pay off. Some characters are really charming, and it will cause variables beyond facts and truth to interplay with how you carry out justice.

_childDocuments_.review: What I thought I was getting was a Phoenix Wright game that was just one big case, and it's up to you to know when the mystery is solved and you're ready to move on from the investigation phase to the trial phase.  What I actually got was a game with no incorrect dialogue options, and summaries of everything you learn.  That makes it so as long as you follow the leads in your notebook and look for the two(?) pieces of evidence in the world, you can't possibly fail to put the mystery together.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: There isn't anything quite like early japanese mystery visual novels. It's not the high detail pixelated streets of japan, but the feel is just as cool. A fairly short game, a combination of collectathon and a 3D visual novel mystery, Paradise Killer is a great excuse for listening to too much city pop again. You can spend the time to solve the mystery completely or just botch the entire thing in ten minutes. My only criticism is that I wish it were longer. It is not nearly as detailed a mystery as I would like, especially the ending, which plays itself a bit too much. Ultimately for the length of the game I can't complain. I hope there will be more like this to come. There is nothing quite like solving a galactic murder scheme while city pop is blasting on the city speaker system, and the only god we summoned is laughing at how incompetent we are.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: I beat the game, got all the acheivements and my review still stands. The only things I would (and wish I could) change about Paradise Killer are its many typos and grammatical mistakes.***Original Review:I am really liking this game and wish I could call it perfect, since it's very close, at least as far as indie games go. While it doesn't have amazing AAA graphics or high-action gameplay, it does what it aims to do extremely well. I'm near the end at this point and have found most of the collectibles, so I'd be surprised if I encounter anything new that drastically changes my mind about the game's quality. If I do, I'll update my review.As for what I like, I would say almost everything about this game is enjoyable. The story and lore are extremely wild and intriguing, like an 80s detective movie with alien gods/demons and corrupt immortal politicians. The bizarre, hypersexualized aesthetic also makes for a unique experience. An like many other reviewer's have said, this game really does make you feel like a detective. There is a lot to take in and it can be a bit overwhelming at first, especially since you can go pretty much anywhere right at the start. However, as you piece together the evidence and get to know the characters, things start to fall into place. The thing that has been bothering me most is the spelling and grammar mistakes. While most of them are not too obstructive, others make it difficult to understand (and sometimes even contradict) the character's intentions. For instance, at one point, Lydia says "now" when she meant to say "no," which reverses the meaning of her sentence. In another instance, Crimson says "it" instead of "is" but for some reasons adds a different "is" in the wrong place. The most common mistake by far is the lack of commas before characters' names and question phrases. For example, a character might say, "Are you an idiot freak?" when they meant to say, "Are you an idiot, freak?" Or, they might say, "It is great isn't it?" instead of, "It is great, isn't it?" Most of the time, it's easy enough to understand what the character is trying to say, but sometimes it's confusing. The amount mistakes like this (there are a lot of them) makes it seem like the developers didn't really care enough to address read through the script before publishing the game, which is a bit disheartening, since this game is basically a visual novel. Part of me wishes I was capable of making a mod to fix these textual mistakes, or that I could persuade the developers to hire me as an editor. While minor in the grand scheme of things, this game does involve a lot of reading. Encountering so many textual mistakes makes the writing seem amateurish, which may turn some people off to what is otherwise an incredibly engrossing and detailed story. In sum, I would say you should definitely play this game if a detective game with a bizarre, supernatural story and deep lore sounds interesting to you, as this game does all these things well. However, I hope the developers will consider releasing an update that fixes the many spelling/grammar mistakes, so their story (which they obvious put a lot of effort into crafting) can really shine.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a Phoenix Wright or a Danganronpa fan, this is probably not for you. The debate gameplay in those games is meat and potatoes, this game doesn't have it. Some of the aesthetics can be horribly jarring though, as it does use a fair bit of background which are just normal real life pictures but in really low res. The OST is pretty good.
