_childDocuments_.review: Easily one of my favourite games. If something gets me to go after every single collectible despite not even having an achievement for it (sad), I must have really liked it.It's very unique in its style and identity unlike other vapor wave-inspired things that often rely on the aesthetic so much that it all becomes generic. This is definitely not the case here: the vapor wave is the icing on the cake; the writing and design has you quite immersed in the universe, and actually paying attention to little tidbits of lore that you can find. Its sense of humour is lovely as well. Characters are varied and might cause intense dislike and hatred in the player, to sympathy and adoration.I'm not generally a big fan of investigation games a la Ace Attorney et all, but this game is different in that your role of investigating is a lot more direct and within your control, not least of which because it happens in a 3D world rather than classic 2D and point-and-click games. The quirks of the art design throughout are quite nice, and the sound design does great to enhance it (there is a part of the world I hated going into because the sound design was so great it made me shudder when I had to go there).I might be on the minority when it comes to this last one, but I also felt that the game (and especially the ending) brought up interesting questions to me about what justice (and a judiciary and criminal justice system) actually even is and represents; but the game is not concerned with answering any of those questions, rather it gives the player a lovely lore to munch into and take it however or as far as they want to take it.I'd love if there was more variance to the potential endings - after spending so much time with all the characters, and considering the different options you can take at the end, more detailed differences when you do those would be great, but ultimately the journey was so good for me that that lack of variance at the end couldn't sully it.

_childDocuments_.review: Heeeesitant recommend. If you go for it, do so on sale.Psychedelic vaporwave walking simulator with good tunes, vibing and collectibles first, investigation second. I completed almost everything, didn't bother getting every collectible. Reason why I got most of them, is explained in negatives.+ Pretty uniquely themed+ Looks good+ Rather good music (saves the game)+ Funny, at times+ Lore building, while in a nonsensical setting, is consistent* The only minigame is passable, nothing crazy bad/good* Investigation struck me as amateurish/nonsensical, which partly makes sense considering the theming, but in the end it did not deliver for me personally- More or less entire game is combo of fetch quest or walking around collecting items, with occasional dialogue- Movement upgrades exist, but are hidden in the world and there's no tell where, I missed one of them untill I looked it up after beating the game. _childDocuments_.review: There are a few things to like about Paradise Killer: the open yet compact world, the unexpectedly interesting movement, and the unique and well realized setting.Other than those specifics, I don't think the game delivers. The central mystery is inelegant, crowded with perpendicular motives. The writing swerves between twee and overbearingly philosophical, and is undermined by constant mistakes in grammar and punctuation. The voice acting is mediocre and repetitive to the point of breaking immersion. The aesthetic has that classic vaporwave problem: it's ugly — but with a wink! — which doesn't stop it from still just being ugly. Nothing wrong with the character designs, though the portraits themselves lag behind those of many freeware VNs. The puzzles are either trial-and-error affairs or fetch quests in disguise.Ultimately, the trial sequence is a summary of previous information that asks little of you in the way of deduction. The game wraps up abruptly, without acknowledging the player's choices almost at all. I can appreciate what was attempted here, but unless you suspect you're squarely in the target demo, I wouldn't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Lying beneath the somewhat rough-looking environmental visuals of this game is a truly superb mystery narrative with a strange and fascinating setting built up to support it and a solid cast of characters. The open-ended nature of the investigation feels liberating and provides for surprising twists and revelations as you uncover the secrets of the island.No bit of exploration felt unrewarding, as I traversed places I felt sure were nothing but set dressing, but to my surprise they held rewards for the diligent investigator (even if sometimes it was just some currency). Many of the items you can uncover on the island are not immediately relevant to the case, but they give little windows into the weird setting and provide enough information to contextualize the characters and the mystery while leaving out enough to keep my sense of wonder provoked. That feels like a rare art in games, especially today.This game shows that less can be more. The mechanics and most of the visuals are simple, but it is approachable enough that even someone without a lot of experience with video games could get a grasp on how to play, and anyone with an interest in exploration, excellent murder mysteries, or delving into a strange setting has the opportunity to enjoy themselves.This game has gotten some great critical reception, but it deserves more community buzz too. If you are on the fence about this, I highly encourage you to try the game out. I highly doubt that you will be disappointed.P.S. The soundtrack is also a banger.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR- A very pretty game with a good soundtrack that will hook you for about 6 hours, then you realize you're bored and the story is a few red herrings, a few misdirects, and a bunch of deus ex machina.   If you want a walking sim through a repetitive and bland world, this game has you covered. The general way to play this game is:  start game, have no idea what you're doing, run around the island to unlock all the fast travel points you can, writing down which ones are closest to the main NPCs, get the few ghost side quests as you pick up enough blood crystals to buy drinks, the 3 “footbath” upgrades, and get the 3 new types of symbols to open the doors (worship, cosmos, and pyramids).  Once you have done enough collectible collecting to get those upgrades (or for the lazy use cheat engine and cut off hours of wasted time hunting for blood crystals), then for all intents and purposes, this game is just walking between NPCs asking the same questions and getting the same variants of the answer “Did you ask the other NPC?” or “Here's a half truth, a lie, and the other guy is lying to you” (or for crimson paying a few blood crystals to get evidence for the final case). This will go on as you finish getting all the fast travel points, use the investigative mode to pick up phones, jump off mountains (no fall damage), and going through the doors using the computers and the picture matching mini-game. Depending on the speed you find a few key items (or look at a achievement guide to find out what main puzzles and actions correlate with the items that lead to plot twists), the mystery behind the murder and the 4 “gates” that lead to the scene of the murder are rather lackluster. I will say that this game at least had me consider whether or not I should “prosecute” certain characters at the end, after all attempted murder or setting up a murder isn't the same as actually being the person holding the knife to kill someone or being the one ordering someone to hold the knife, so the game has that going for it. It doesn't make anything more interesting in the long term, but it did give me a few minutes of considering before I started the final trial. Finally, I'd point out that this game has little to no replay-ability. Once you've gotten a rough idea of what actually occurred, all the little details you go hunting for are to flesh out how to prove things, and unless your looking for achievements, there is little enjoyment to reading bland flavor text about how “Genmaicha tea is the best and everyone who thinks otherwise is lying or hasn't tried it”. Trying to make the double jump or air dash physics work is an exercise in frustration, and the thought of starting from even my pretrial safety save doesn't motivate me to finish hunting down all the collectibles. I'm sure this game had some highlights for me over the 9 or 10 hours I sank into it beyond the “I kind of want to know what the heck happened”, it's just a shame I can't remember them.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine if Agatha Christie wrote a crossover of Warhammer 40k and Stargate, used the characters from Danganronpa, and set the whole thing in the Miami of Miami Vice. Because that's basically what Paradise Killer is. It's also an incredibly ambitious who-done-it where there's few clear answers and the truth is left up for you to shape based on the facts that you find. And it's set in an absolutely vivid world.The island itself, both in design and story, is the game's strongest aspect. It's an absolutely insane mish-mash of vaporwave visuals and music and colors over a "paradise" fueled by slave labor for corporate entities and bloody mass slaughter in Sumerian temples to satiate the appetites of horrors from beyond the stars. It's massive Brutalist buildings lording over cramped Japanese shantytowns, with colorful corporate mascots and posters advertising idol contests next to blood soaked altars and the ever present fear of demonic corruption. You're given no backstory or understanding of the mythology before you're dropped into the world and left to piece it together through conversation and finding relics and doodads. As every worldbuilding brick dropped into place and I saw just how horrendous and colorful the world I was in, the more engrossed I was in the island and its history and people. Gameplay wise, it doesn't deviate too much from detective visual novel standards, but with a heavier emphasis on exploration and hunting for secrets. You talk to people, find info or hear something that contradicts their statements, talk again, etc etc. There's a bit of a relationship system to the game, akin to visual novels, but it's light and doesn't consist of much more than clicking the special dialog option when it's available. It doesn't seem to lead to any special routes or anything. You can max out your relationship with every character, learn a little about them, and get a special flavor item that tells you more about them or the island. The mystery plot and trial aspect will draw a lot of comparisons to Danganronpa (such as the one that I did) and while it definitely does take some inspiration from there, the truth is much more malleable in this game. As characters remind you constantly, "facts" and "truth" are not the same thing and it is up to the investigator to stitch together a narrative out of the facts presented and I think this is the game's second strongest aspect: by developing your relationships to characters, you are actually allowed to (attempt) to present your case in a way that lets a guilty party you're fond of go free or pin one or more crimes on a character you don't like that much. Instead of a strict linear story, much of the evidence discovered in the game points to more than one suspect and you can choose to ignore (or build a case on) weaker, tenuous, or circumstantial pieces of evidence to push the story in the way that you want. That absolutely fascinated me and felt like my character was an active participant in the politicking, the conspiracies, and the backstabbing that was prevalent in the rest of the cast. (That said, as a caveat, if you're the sort that needs a concrete, developer-created "good" or "right" or "true" ending, this game might disappoint you as there isn't one. There seems to be a series of immutable facts about the events that led to the crimes, but the exact perpetrators and their level of involvement is up to your discretion and if you feel that might leave you unsatisfied in the story, this might not be the game for you. I personally find player-shaped narratives and stories told through the player-character's biases to be a huge reason why I become so engrossed in games like this and is part of the reason I recommend this game so highly, so this is definitely a Your Mileage May Vary sort of game.)The game's two strengths are a bit weighed down by a few weaknesses: the island is huge and largely very colorful with lots to explore, but the map is not useful at all except as a general guide to where major landmarks are. A fast travel system exists, but it costs some of the game's (admittedly plentiful) currency to use, and some areas of the world feel underdeveloped and under utilized compared to others. The ambitious goal of letting you shape your own narrative of events leaves a few characters underdeveloped compared to others and one or two pieces of evidence that don't seem to fit into any of the possible explanations for the crimes. The trials themselves lack the excitement of Danganronpa's mini-games and in one occasion, I presented a piece of evidence that led to the conviction of a character I wanted to spare because the option to pick it was vaguely described. There were also a few minor issues here and there, like UI elements not disappearing when they should or misspelled words, but none of these issues - major or minor - detract from the overall depth and enjoyment to be had with this game. It's easily one of my favorite game worlds already and totally worth a play if you're at all interested in mystery games, colorful and strange worlds, and ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up narratives.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been on a bit of an investigation/ detective game binge and I picked up Paradise Killer because I found the aesthetic interesting, but I came away with much more than I hoped for. From the incredible City Pop soundtrack, fascinating worldbuilding, clever and fun dialogue and writing, and a cast of suspects that are both both strange and sympathetic with plenty of mysteries to uncover, I recommend this game to someone looking to get their investigation freak on!As a general game, it's a good 8/10. As an investigation game, it lacks thought provoking puzzles or mysteries to chew on. It's more of an exploration game rather than an actual deduction game. But it's still an absolutely worthwhile experience if you can get past that lack of investigative depth, and appreciate Island Sequence 24 for what it has rather than what it doesn't.Enjoy paradise!
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Whodunit meets city pop in a Japanese urban aesthetic? Sign me up. I was a little iffy at first and found the realities of the setting extremely confusing, but I'm glad I stuck with it, because it turned out to be a great ride. The mystery and the plot are well-crafted and keep you guessing, though it all becomes increasingly clear as you collect more clues. There's a lot of backtracking involved, which can get a little tiresome, and the way the island is structured can get really confusing, but as you unlock more and more fast travel points, it gets a little easier to navigate. However, the game could have used a couple of proofreading passes because I found a lot of punctuation and spelling errors.If you're a fan of the Ace Attorney and Danganronpa games, this is an absolute must.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: If you're the type of person to enjoy a walking simulator or a casual mystery game, I cannot recommend Paradise killer enough. It is far from perfect, and there are certainly some repetition issues with the puzzles. You will be rewarded for tracking down every lead you can sniff out, so take your time. You may be forced to make some difficult choices in the name of justice.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: when a game swings hard for the fences of originality that can end up in tragedy, this is not the case for paradise killer. Everything about this game has a flavor you've never tasted. What at first seems to be an impossible to digest lore becomes common knowledge to the player. Everything in this game, from the character's names and looks to the surreal world in which it takes place, is breathtakingly fresh. at times it did get a little repetitive walking around the same settings snooping for clues but then i'd stumble on something i didn't see previously and then i was back to being the super detective this island needs. Give this game a shot
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Getting thrown into this strange world of Gods, crystals, and great music was intimidating at first - but exploring the island blind, making relationships with the memorable characters, and actively putting the pieces of the mystery together myself was deeply rewarding. Fun and surreal, the game doesn't try to explain itself to you - so it is best to surrender yourself to the world, and dive in.Only one small issue. A needed upgrade for my computer was provided in a specific vending machine. I forgot which one and couldn't recall the dialog instruction I was given (Could be user error, I didn't see it in the log.) Either way, would recommend the community discussion tab on steam if you run into a problem, as searching online for guides was difficult.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very unique and full of depth. It's not like LA noire or something like that where there are individual cases that you can quickly run through. It's more like disco elysium where even though the world is small it has a million things going on and a web of conspiracies. There is technically only one case to solve but there is so many moving parts that it's gonna be awhile before you think you've figured it out. Very weird world and characters too. Haven't really seen this type of environment in a game before. Lovin' the game so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of fun exploring the island and uncovering all the evidence. Only wish the island had been a little easier to get around on. Even the fast-travel mechanic was a bit cumbersome.The story you're investigating is remarkably intricate and there's quite a lot of evidence and testimony to discover. And during the trial, as nobody seems truly innocent, there are some tough choices to make. Truth be told, I wanted to ensure that this horrible civilisation would not continue.The weakest part of the game in my opinion was after the trial and speaking to those who remained. A more extensive epilogue for those characters would have been nice.On the whole, I'd say this is unlike any other game I've ever played and that alone would be enough to recommend it. But more than that, I had fun and was intrigued.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: phoenix wright investigation kind of game with great story and characters, the soundtrack is spot on with the aesthetic being one on the things i enjoyed most.a little rough on the edges game. some tasks are a bit tedious and searching for clues on the island isn't that intuitive. anyways, i think it had huge potential, but overall i like it. hope one day we can see a higher budget sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Killer aesthetic and worldbuilding elevates this game from what's otherwise a pretty standard detective game into something special. I have two critiques:Gating fast travel and some progression behind collecting blood gems is a  annoying, but it wasn't really a big deal. The system just felt kind of out of place, and with how much running back and forth was necessary I'd have liked fast travel to be a bit less restrictive. Still, I can kind of understand their reasoning - they wanted you to see the world they crafted instead of teleporting from person to person.The characters' personalities fall just a bit short of being as colorful as their design - the one exception here is Shinji, who has a very small role in the overall tale. It's not that the characterization is poor, just that I was expecting a little more from how eye catching their designs were.Would I recommend it still? Absolutely. My gripes are small and don't ruin the rest of it.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought it just for the soundtrack but after playing a bit, I was hooked. I wanted to play more and more. Soundtrack is amazing. Every music is an eargasm. Art style is really good. Game is unique and story is well written. There are many twist and turns that will confuse you. Characters are very likable. _childDocuments_.review: Better considered a piece of interactive fiction than a game, from my perspective.  But I enjoyed it.  I think I might have enjoyed it more as a graphic novel? It has a bunch of wonderfully absurd and weird elements.  The seemingly low quality of the graphics adds the experience rather than detracts from it.  The final sequence was a little bit of a let down, but there is a sense of not really knowing what the "truth" was, which is cool
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Sure, this is an investigation game. Take all the time you need, talk to everyone, find all the secrets... but where is game is truly off-the-wall is the setting and flavor. A society of immortals, living in eternal youth for millennia, pledged to worship vast unknowable god/alien/demons, while enslaving regular people to do their mundane work before slaughtering them all to harvest their blood and psychic energies? I'm amazed that a rebellion against the "protagonists" of this game was never the story of the game. After about 5 hours I was equally fascinated and nauseated by the story of this game. The murder mystery just seemed like sideshow. I fully recommend playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: In my reviewe I will focus on the aspects that stood out the most, namely the art, soundtrack, and characters, as well as less than pleasant experience with the platforming and exploration elements.Paradise Killer presents a fascinating visual experience with its stunning art style. The vibrant colors and unique character designs create an immersive world that is both captivating and intriguing. The game's aesthetic is undoubtedly one of its strongest points, as it sets the tone for the unconventional narrative that unfolds throughout the gameplay.The soundtrack is equally impressive, featuring a diverse collection of vaporware tracks that perfectly complement the game's atmosphere. From upbeat tunes that evoke a sense of exploration and adventure to more somber melodies that capture the darker themes of the story, the soundtrack enhances the overall experience immensely.The story is complex and engaging, with many twists and turns that kept me enthralled until the very end. The characters are well-written and fleshed out, with their own motivations and secrets that are slowly revealed as you progress.However, as someone who did not enjoy the platforming and exploration aspects of the game, I found these elements to be very tedious. The open-world exploration can feel overwhelming at times, and the platforming sections are frustrating. That said, the captivating art, immersive soundtrack, and memorable characters make it worth pushing through these less enjoyable aspects to fully appreciate the game's unique charm.In conclusion, Paradise Killer is a uniquely captivating experience that excels in its art style, soundtrack, and character development. While the platforming and exploration aspects almost made me quit, the game's strengths pulled me in, and I appreciated a rich narrative experience and a unique, immersive world.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: The amount of creativity and artistry in this game should move the bar.  You should play this game if you're into story and style.  And every game developer should play this game, to remind themselves of what's possible.Maybe it's true that only a small studio is capable of going as hard as this.  Maybe if you have a big budget, you have more managers looking over your shoulder and getting spooked about how many pink marble statues of old gods you're putting between the beach umbrellas, how straight-out weird you're getting in your quest for the sublime.  But you gotta go for it, boys.  Strive, strive, for that perfect 25.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of detective-style games and so I was really happy to discover that Paradise Killer existed a few weeks ago.  It's not a perfect game but if you like murder mysteries set in a non-traditional environment then by all means, please try it. The scenery and layout is beautiful, as are the character "sprites" The music fits the game well - there's also a variety of tracks.The sleuthing makes sense - everything is logical and you can deduce stuff before you find certain pieces of evidence. I didn't mind the voice acting, but during the conversations they seemed a bit too repetitive and arbitrary. Thankfully you can turn it off in the settings.Whilst I liked the characters it was hard to feel invested... everything seemed a little too disjointed. Maybe a bit more history at the start could rectify this but it may just be the setting, whilst beautiful, didn't gel with the investigation.It's not exactly a con but I think achievements would have made it a little more enjoyable for me, especially since I spent a lot of time bouncing around picking up random little objects. So in short, fun game, I'd give it a 6.5/10. Thanks for coming to my TED talk.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Surreal murder mystery game. Style feels very Danganronpa-ish with flat sprite NPCs. You chase down clues on an island in this awkward walking simulator, sometimes borderline platformer. Pastel colors and smooth music everywhere. I've seen some people complaining that the endgame is a bit un-interactive but I had not problems with it.Only complaint I have is that fast travel costs ingame currency, which is finite. So I ended up almost never using it and walked everywhere. Might annoy some.Would you like a weird who-dunnit game? Get this!
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: It's a bit jank, in a charming way. Like all the characters are flat sprites in a 3d world. It reaks of amateurish, but isn't really buggy at all. Someone clearly didn't bite off more then they could chew making it, which I respect. The game play is like... an open world 3d phoenix wright in a wild scifi/magic setting. There's only one trial at the end, and you get to present the evidence you've gathered. The plot is twisted enough to keep it interesting. Recommended
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Look. Paradise Killer is not a good game. Paradise Killer is, however, a fantastic world with an interesting story to tell, and I'm not convinced that there's a better way to tell it. Mechanically speaking, the investigation isn't as thorough or as interesting as that of Ace Attorney or even Professor Layton, but the meta-narrative of the difference between facts and truth and between judgment and justice make it all worthwhile. I've found myself thinking about this game long after I'd finished playing, and that's a testament to its strength. For a first-time game developer, I'm blown away by Kaizen's  product as writing is typically a secondary concern (and also the hardest thing to get spot-on!). I'm definitely going to buy whatever they make next, and I'd recommend you do the same.TL;DR Paradise Killer is, more than anything else, something different. It may not be for you, but I heartily recommend giving it a try if only to see how weird things can get.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game for 9 hours in a row, and personally it was rather grating.The story feels a bit flat- Predictable, and the outcome is based purely on the player's investigative choices and skill. It feels as though, even though there is an outcome, it has no real standing on the plot or outcome- This game could certainly could have used a set of endings for each decision you made.The music does not fit the general 'vibe' of an Investigative game, making the game feel more like a grating sandbox, and while there is an 'in-world' reason for this, it would be much more preferred if the music gave off a vibe fitting the situation or game aesthetic.- Felt weird walking into a bloody room with really peppy pop/punk music playing.I understand the game is a sandbox game, and 'walking' and 'enjoying the environment' is a part of that, but for those who are purely invested in the story, punishing them by making the Fast Travel system cost currency is rather irritating at best.Which reminds me of the map system, which was vague- I would have preferred a detailed map I could have read directions on to a general location map.It feels like most of the content in this game is back and forth walking (teleporting if you explore enough), and your character being unable to ask someone about evidence relating to them unless you have a direct lead connecting them to that said evidence; also collecting random collectables. So, in all.Pros:- Good worldbuilding (The lore pickups and the backstory is great, the story itself is not.)- Good art style and voice acting.- Will give them props for some of their accessibility options.Cons:- Nondynamic storytelling that makes your choices feel rather moot, could have been more mixed.- Music does not fit genre, and can be repetitive and grating.- Fast travel shouldn't cost money, even if your game is about sandbox and exploration.- Bad UI, Map certainly could have been more intuitive.- Minigame quickly became repetitive, as did dialogue, talking, and walking.All in all, I can see WHY people would like this game- Don't get me wrong, it's a decent game, but it's not my cup of tea; but I also don't think it deserves all the hype it has and has been getting.If you decide to get this, do so with a grain of salt, or at least take into consideration that this game is an EXPLORATION SANDBOX game first, and everything else is mostly sidelined to that.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like Danganronpa, but consistently good instead of occasionally good (I have played all the mainline DR games). There is only one case, but it's a real doozy, and there is more than one "right" answer. You can massage things a bit based on your own morality.The ending leaves things open for future games in this setting, and I very much hope that comes to pass.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Love it so much! The worldbuilding, art direction, characters, soundtrack, and story were all excellent! The world they build into just a 12-15 hour game was amazing. I loved going around exploring the island slowly uncovering the mysteries within. The characters were all very interesting with their own unique set of motivations and interests. The game gives you a fair bit of freedom in approaching the case, you can accuse anyone you want in the trial and back up it with whatever evidence you have leaving it fairly open ended. Of course there are right answers but how you get there is up to you. I definitely recommend! Also an amazing soundtrack was mostly done by Barry "Epoch" Topping who also made the soundtrack for "Thatcher's Tech Base" mod for Doom 2. I just thought that was a fun fact cause it's a fun mod.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly strange and one-of-a-kind experience. On the one hand, the vaporwave aesthetic has been done before, and usually in some sort of retro or nostalgic context. Here though, it's combined with cuneiform tablets, upbeat music, and unique character art. The reason to play this though, is for the story and atmosphere. The more you learn about this strange place with it's odd customs and social hierarchy, the more you want to find out more. The final trial where you get to combine your evidence into arguments to convict the guilty is the real cherry on top. I would've liked the world to be a little more alive though. The 3D exploration is the weakest part, and I could see this done as a sort of visual novel with point and click sections and it being just as good. Hopefully if we get a sequel they'll develop that a bit more.But man, what a trip. I highly recommend it if you're willing to explore and read to absorb yourself into this odd world.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Paradise Killer is a strange experience- one that has me stuck dead in the middle. The game brings confusion in that it is a blend of Visual Novel and Collectathon/Exploration. Which understandably makes this game VERY polarizing for people and made me nervous when buying the game. Personally I'm not a massive fan of Visual Novels however I did enjoy what Paradise Killer had to offer- and ultimately I think the 'Collect/Explore' part of the game was what weighed down so heavily on my thoughts aside from spoilers.So one issue is that the game is like a playground except I keep winding up on the bottom of the slide and needing to worm my way back up to other elements. The Island feels off because of this factor since on the Farm/Harbor side of the map there's no quick way to jump yourself back up to the higher portions of the Island or to the other side (without paying or unlocking a 'shortcut' which is less of a shortcut than it should be). For the most part because of my wariness towards the game I couldn't bring myself to actively taxi around the island knowing it costs money which is limited in the scope of the game. So to be clear a vast VAST majority of collectables don't matter at all and are simply lore dumps. What the game consists of is going to one characters and exhausting their dialogues of importance (since you can ask really REALLY stupid questions and get a stupid response) and then travelling to the next character and so on and so forth. While you do this there's an option to raise your relationship level which is important to getting more clues for the mystery. What happened for me was that I got every collectable and had finished nearly every investigation case but was STILL short 1-3 more hangouts with each character which required me to (at this point filthy rich) taxi myself around the island yapping to people to raise my relationships to max level. This part of the 'game' felt exhausting and started having me question what the point of the game part was supposed to even mean. Sure there are one or two areas you have to literally explore to find, but outside of that there's no real meaning to not just have this as a straight Visual Novel instead. I think the game would MASSIVELY benefit if there had been GAMEPLAY like jump puzzles or something to do to traverse the island. Having said all this you still don't HAVE to collect everything or max every relationship as you can bring any amount of evidence to the trial.I do think the initial exploration of the Island was fun, I think there were some cool areas (Deadzone, Opulent Temple) and I think there were some... bland kinda whatever areas (Agriculture/Harbor, Citizen Apartments/Houses, etc). I'll also say that the lore was fantastic and went together smoothly. I've seen too many OTHER fiction stories that go for a similar approach of strange gods in a strange land and fail spectacularly, which was NOT the case here. The mystery of the main plot was also written well especially in terms as how you experience and slowly figure out each step in the case (although it'd be different for each player). I like too that the game responds to the player finding out a mystery before a character reveals it in dialogue, responding instantly. There were VERY few instances of the dialogue not matching with what I knew from exploring/talking. The one limiting factor was the tame responses from EVERY character when mine accuses them point blank of having done a crime with completely damning evidence. I get the game is trying to make it seem like anyone could have done anything, but it's to the point of having a gun with fingerprints and showing the murderer you have the gun and they just go "It's not mine" - "That's not my DNA". Like ???. Not a SINGLE character flipped when I had that amount of evidence and was talking to them, which is such a shame for character writing. My big BIG issue comes from, well spoilers.

_childDocuments_.review: This might be the best detective game I've ever played. It has a delightfully unhinged plot and aesthetic but at its core it is a true exercise in fact gathering and deduction.As a big fan of the genre, there's relatively few games that actually pull off a satisfying conclusion once you've gathered your facts (what Jon Ingold called the "sudoku problem"). Paradise Killer on the other hand has a wonderfully dramatic and interesting finale, complete with new surprises and entertaining options in the epilogue. Even when I had all the facts, I still had to think hard about my decisions during the trials and put in a bit of planning to get everything laid out successfully. It really made all the work put in gathering evidence and exploring every nook and cranny of the island feel worth it, even though that process itself was plenty fun, with lots of interesting lore to find, characters to interview, and mysteries to solve. Great soundtrack too.As with all the best detective stories, the facts are there for you to find if you can, but in the end you decide the truth. For better or worse. Fantastic experience, 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game. Ambiance is on point, characters are all amazing and the investigation is really interesting. Gets a bit repetitive sometimes with traveling around and the platforming but the game gives you all the tools to make it fun. Many plot twists and crazy world building. A definite recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Good game. The crime-solving aspect is I guess technically open-ended in that the game will allow you to screw it up and see the end credits and technically never confirms who is or is not a culprit, but if you chase down every lead and pick up every collectible you will arrive at a pretty clear understanding of the case in a fairly straightforward manner.The environment is I think helped more by the worldbuilding than the "open world" format. It's kinda vaporwave Bloodborne and maybe strays occasionally into "lore for lore's sake" but serves to keep things unsettling.As for the map, it's a cool tropical island that's fun to explore but I'd say it's more like a very large puzzle room than an "open world". There's nothing dynamic, and the only thing to unlock is fast travel waypoints. In terms of scale it just starts to rub up against that annoying sensation that everything is slightly too small to be believable. It's not Death Stranding's "walk across the US in an hour" levels of cramped, but they tell you there's 3,000 civilians living in like a handful of apartment buildings and only like a third of the Syndicate have an identifiable "home". I do appreciate the attention to detail of putting farms, a power plant with poles and lines running around the island, a convenience store, etc.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Feels good to explore and uncover parts of the story. Really liked the themes that were presented by each character, each one also had believable personalities even with their quirks.The mechanics and the story flowed well into each other very smoothly nothing really ruined the experience of anything else
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: A unique and really fun investigation game. It forces you to use your brain to solve puzzles but is also casual enough to play in a relaxing fashion. Really liked the original world and how insane everything really is. Its a fantastic backdrop for a mystery. Well done. I played through it all and got the investigation solved in 22 hours. I like how the game allows you to explore in whatever fashion and order you choose to, in a manner most games don't. I will remember this one for awhile and will definitely play a sequel when it happens.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Well, that was  The setting was very creative and interesting, the character art was really cool, and the music was jazzy and neat, but the investigation was just a dozen hours worth of running around doing parkour to pick up worthless trinkets, the writing felt a little noticeably amateurish (sometimes through pointless pretentiousness) to me at times, the trial was basically just clicking through a checklist to get dialog where you reveal all the things you learned during parkour, and the ending was just "And then the protagonist  because it was her job. Life goes on. End of game" which felt pretty unsatisfying to me. The best part was the weird little anarchy-loving demon you keep finding throughout the game. He and the protagonist have some great Phoenix-Wright-and-Maya-Fey-type banter, and I kinda wish the game had been less nonlinear in large part because it would have given the devs an opportunity to better integrate him into the plot rather than just having you do parkour to pick up random interactions with him like they're trinkets (also because when I play a game about solving mysteries I normally don't want the longest most engaging part of the gameplay to consist of doing parkour to pick up trinkets)
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Even though Paradise Killer is pitched as a detective game, it is actually, at its core, a collectathon. You're dropped in this open world full of oddly delightful characters and must talk to each of them and look for evidence to solve some crimes. So, nothing extraordinary here. However, if the "what" doesn't stand out, the "how" is absolutely brilliant. These are the main points that made me fall in love with this game:1. It's simply a joy to control the character and just traverse the island, leaping and dashing. The exploration and platforming feels sooo good. It feels like looking for Korok seeds in an urban environment with forgiving physics and no fall damage. The controls might seem weird at first, but they're easy to get used to.2. The World building is fantastic. It gives off this "Tolkien" vibe of there being a huge world, full of history and life, and you're just experiencing a thin slice of all that (here's hoping for a sequel!).3. Character design is unique. Really flamboyant and over-the-top. It perfectly matches the character's personalities, the story and the overall feel of the island. Everybody is interesting and it's fun to talk to them all, even the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.4. The writing is really good too. The plot is well-crafted and intriguing. The dialogue and the object descriptions are witty and fun to read.Now, about the actual detective aspect of it, the game is a little lackluster. Even though the story is great, it doesn't really require you to piece the clues together yourself or anything: as long as you're thorough enough in your exploration, the solution to the mysteries are basically spoon-fed to you. In the trial that marks the end of the game, very little is asked of the player (as opposed to, say, an Ace Attorney or Danganronpa game).All things considered, I loved the time I spent playing Paradise Killer. It's a very successful blend of exploration and visual novel. Highly recommended for anyone who likes either or both these types of game. Especially so if you liked Outer Wilds, Subnautica, Zero Escape and Danganronpa.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Not a huge fan tbh. The world is extremely interesting (especially the unusual artifacts hinting at the existence of some horrific elder god on the far side of the moon, and the existence of some kind of extra-solar alien threat), and the music is really good, and the character art is really cool. I didn't really play it enough to determine if it's a "good" game, so I'm not going to say that it's a "bad" game (a nearly meaningless label, anyway). Everything in this game is *weird*, and not in what I would consider an inherently good way. Everything that I encountered in my limited playtime just felt like nonsense. The character interactions, the techno/psychobabble, the item descriptions. I dunno. Not my jam, but it might be yours.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: An astonishing game.Has the exploration of Elder Scrolls or modern Fallout, combined with one of the most imaginative and best-written worlds I have experienced in 30 years of gaming.It's like your favourite sci-fi book was spliced with an anime and an Elder Scrolls game, set to an amazing electronic soundtrack.Highly, highly recommend for people who enjoy the language of games (exploration, rewards for platforming skills and exploring hidden places, collectibles) but also the language of storytelling and imagination. I will buy a sequel on Day One.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. Extremely satisfying story. I loved piecing together all the stories in my head without necessarily being told everything. Pacing is tight, I could always think of something to do next. I've never seen an aesthetic even remotely like this anywhere else and it's fascinating to see every time.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Paradise Killer is a well written visual novel that breathes fresh life into Danganronpa-sytled games.I loved the open-world aspect and the choice to start the endgame trials anytime during my playthrough. The story was enjoyable, soundtrack is phenomenal, and the characters and motivations all made sense.The endgame trial is my low point of the game. It became a process of spamming the advance button to move along text for ~20 minutes, as the game reads along the evidence I have collected against my accused.  I was expecting an experience similar to Phoenix Wright, where the player uses clues at the right moments to build a case. Because of this, my experience felt more akin to a collectibles game rather than a deductive-reasoning game. I would recommend this if you like visual novels or wanted a game with exploration and tons of collectibles, well worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Paradise Killer is not at all what I thought it would be, aside from a detective mystery game.It's a fun, part occult, part supernatural mystery game with a dash of platformer and collect-a-thon with a sprinkle of love. I don't generally care for the collecting aspects of games but I felt compelled in this instance as worked to solve the case of the Paradise Killer.The world is well crafted, the story is interesting and feels unique, and the characters are well written. The game isn't without flaws, but for such a relatively small dev team, I think they have made something special.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun and engaging. The replay value isnt huge, and I have some things I disagree about with how the story ends, but I loved it all the same! Its got dangonrampa and ace attorney energy, and has a very nice, robust journal system that helps you not stress about remembering details about what people said. It also has oodles of accessability options to help make the game play exactly how you need it too. All in all, get this game if youre looking for a fun murder mystery story set in a unique,  a e s t h e t i c  world that really has the players experience in mind.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't recommend this game more to help with the metrics of the site. I know it's a rotten tomatoes style, percentage of positive review type thing, but "Overwhelmingly Positive" has certain connotations that can lead people to be very disappointed with this game. One of those people was myself. In truth, I find this a more middling game that has some impressive strengths along with some unfortunately large flaws.Paradise Killer is a hyper stylized murder mystery game that takes place in an original alternate universe dominated by cosmic gods and demons. To start off with some positives, the island on which the game takes place is very visually interesting and populated by a killer... by a wonderful soundtrack. Really, the soundtrack alone is so good that it helped get over a LOT of this game's shortcomings. That said, the island is far too big for the amount of exploration that is encouraged. This is further compounded by how limited your traversal is in the beginning of the game. Additionally, the island has some confusing geometry in the name of admittedly interesting design. Trying to navigate to specific locations can lead to frequently becoming lost or falling to areas where you have to restart.These transportation annoyances should be lessened by the fact that the game has a fast travel system, right? Wrong. In an over indulgence of flavor and attempted detail, the system can feel to be more of a slog than just travelling. If you want to access fast travel, you will first have to activate a telephone to act as a fast travel spot. Sure, this is a proven way to keep people limited to places they've been before. I would argue that it is pointless in this game, as there are only two or three telephones in areas that would require unlocking a path first. Allowing the player to simply travel to a number of beacons with a few requiring activation would have cut down on the needless busywork the game uses to stretch out the play time.  Furthermore, the fast travel system is one of the slowest I have encountered. Once you have paid the fee and selected fast travel, you don't get to just zip over to the other location. Instead, you get a crash scene as the transition loads, and then you are riding in a car with another character. She asks you where you want to go, another (quick)  load screen, and then you're there. I'll be lenient and say this whole process takes about 15 seconds. Now, this may not seem like a lot, however it causes the prospect of simply walking to where you need to go to be much more appealing unless the location is on the opposite side of the island. The fact that you have to pay to use it as well makes it even worse, which leads me to another point.Blood gems, the currency of the island, are both too plentiful and largely useless. How can there be too much money, you ask? When there is a several second "item get!" screen each time you find one, and you'll be finding them all over the place. Usually only ever single blood gems on their own, unless you are able to finish one of the scant side quests to earn, *gasp* TWO blood gems. Despite their abundance, to the point of finding them getting the same disappointed energy as unwrapping underwear for Christmas, there is a hard limit on the number in the game, which makes them paradoxically feel too valuable to use on non-limited transactions, i.e. fast travel. While they are largely useless, there are a few instances where you NEED them in unknown quantities in order to find information about the game. Starlight (your laptop) generally require some amount of blood gems to unlock, there is a character who requires blood gems for testimony, and there are shrines that require blood gems to activate. While, in the end, you probably only need about 20 in order to unlock every bit of game affecting content, you don't know that until the very end so you will constantly have the RPG problem of "I can't use this now, I might need it later!"Now, if somehow you have read to this point, you might be thinking that I'm spending a lot of time complaining about what are, at best, tertiary systems. Surely these are just nitpicks if that is what you're complaining about. However, that is the experience of Paradise Killer, constant painful thorns in your sides. You're right, though, I could overlook these if the rest of the game slammed it out of the park like Mark McGuire on a day with some extra potent 'juice." Sadly, the most egregious of Paradise Killer's faults is its writing.Any game that says 'Nani the Hell' deserves scorn.The main crux of Paradise Killer's game play is investigating a mass murder. This is primarily done by means of dialog with the various characters of the island. The problem is that 90% of these characters are absolutely  vile, and, . In a game where the whole point is unraveling the mystery and trying to piece together a crime, I found myself dreading talking to people, especially if I knew that they'd have a lot to say. Everyone is very one note and easy to grasp within the first few lines of talking to them. There are no surprises that will make you second guess your first impression; that's just how they are. There is no subtlety, no depth to any motives, and no complexity to any of their ♥♥♥♥♥♥, ♥♥♥♥♥♥ personalities. That said, some can be nice to talk to and there are a few instances where you interact with people you are supposed to be friends with and you actually feel like the characters are friends.This game has far, far too many "I'm fourteen and this is deep" moments. The main character's catchphrase is "facts and truth are not the same" and the game wants to make this a theme. However, it does nothing to establish what it means by this, just waving it around like "if you don't understand, that just means you're not smart enough to." At the very end, it started to feel like it was meaning that by 'truth' it meant a forced perception of reality a la 1984's 2+2=5. However, our investigative main character has made no indication at all of wanting to do anything but to find the pure reality of what happened. If, say, the character had either a goal of framing the story in a particular way or had a history of distorting facts to create outcomes she desired, then that could have been worked in as a character moment, but that is not the case. There is no character arc in the game at all, in fact. The only difference in the characters by the end of the game is that several of them are dead. I guess you are also free to participate in you murderous cult as well rather than watch from the sidelines, so hurray?Finally, there's the mystery itself. Now, I'd be lying if I said that it was a total flop. There is some intrigue to be had here and the revelation moments did feel nice. That said, said revelation moments where a bit -too- packed compared to other parts of the game where it could feel like you were just spinning your wheels. My main complaint here is the resolution. Not necessarily the answer to the mystery, which was fine, but in the game treated itself as if it was not as decisively solved as it had been in the trial. My guess is that, since you can start the trial at any time, they wrote with the assumption that you didn't scour everything before starting? Possible, but it still made the game feel like it thought it was much deeper than it was. Which, to be fair, the writing regularly does. Now I have rambled a lot, so I will end here. Sure, I could go into how the EXECUTION OF JUSTICE was a bit bungled, how the puzzles were worthless, or how ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ pretty the game could look at times, but I'm out of space. In the end, the game is one of glaring flaws that is held together by some very intense style work. To fix it, I'd give Paradise Killer a C.

_childDocuments_.review: Paradise Killer is a decent deductive game that has arguably too many collectibles (even with the in-game searching upgrade) that ultimately detract from the game for me. Instead of investigating, my completionist tendencies took over, leading all of my interest away from the mystery. Upon gathering all evidence and having all the conversations, the actual presentation of your deductions is lackluster and ultimately has no impact in some ways.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This game reignited my passion for video games and got me excited for what we'll be able to do with the medium with enough time, creativity, and talent.Immediately you are thrown into the world of Paradise KIller, and it seems like everything has been crafted in-world and has been there all along, from the branding on song packaging, to each and every character and their connections in the world.Characters are well-crafted both writing and design-wise, with a nice blend of Jodorowsky extravagance and Jojo's bizzare Adventure-ness permeating through their designs, while maintaining a feeling of uniqueness.The music is phenomenal; it is a drive through the city outskirts under a digital hot pink sunset orchestrated, and matches the tone of Paradise Killer perfectly, from the low-key synth's accompanied by cruising, distorted electric guitar ballads, to electronic organ solo's, creating a modern interpretation of 80's synth and euro pop with it's own unique personality.Minor gameplay element spoilers below:All in all, the game is a solid 9/10 for me, in that it provides something new, fresh, and exciting, and implements it's ideas, themes, and story in a well-crafted game with a few minor hiccups. It's current reviews and relative success is a testament to the clear time, effort, and love the developers poured into this game, and I can't wait to see more from them.But why are you reading this? Who am I to tell you what the truth is? Do you want facts or truth?It's time to breathe life back into paradise.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This a great mystery game, but it's emphasis is mostly on the Exploration and Investigation side. It's very fun and very satisfying to piece the story together. But where this game REALLY stands out is the worldbuilding and setting. Not only is the world uniquely done, but all of the unique aspects are important to the story and not just there for flavor. Great soundtrack, great aesthetics, great story. If you're looking for a fun mystery game with a fresh take, I highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: -Music is really nice on its own and also fits the game’s vibe perfectly-The story is intriguing, keeps you want to move forward all the way till the end-A seemingly well-thought-out world was built to encase the game and similarly various and interesting characters inhabit it-Massive amounts of accessibility settings-While the base controls feel off, you can rebind almost everything, or just get used to it being slightly flawed-I find the visual representation of the protagonist doesn’t fit with either their character nor their voice actress-while not ugly per say, graphics certainly could be way better-failure to commit (ie. giving a character a personality of swearing a lot, but not actually having “♥♥♥♥” in the sentence, but rather f**k – why not just decide one way or another and commit? Or the case of the phallos demon actually not showing their wood or the case of voice overs below)-partial voice acting takes away both the pleasure of listening to a nice dub and at the same time the immersion of reading conversation and imagining whatever voice you’d like for each participant-around the 10th or so hour, running back and forth between characters for just 1 line updates becomes a bit jarring-surprisingly no steam achievements, if you’re into thoseWhile the Paradise Killer experience starts out rough on the back of weird sounding sentences and a rough control scheme, I’d say it takes an hour tops to get used to both of these. _childDocuments_.review: Paradise killer is one of the best murder mysteries i played, every angle of the island is filled with clues and various side missions, not dispersive thanks to the mission tab granting hints on where to find stuff and the backstory of both the characters and the island is rich. the final act gets very intense where you battle with your proves and knowledge. Remember when Love Dies only the truth remains.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed playing Paradise killer. It's an open world mystery game where you explore and collect evidence and talk to people. As you do this, you piece together a truth of what went down. The game is in some ways a bit like a 3d platformer too since you move around the island collecting clues while exploring. Due to it’s open ended nature, you have freedom to explore the island at your own pace in whatever order you want. I didn’t actually end up going to where the crime took place for quite a while as I was happy to just be roaming around, exploring the world, and collected alibis/evidence.The world building is also very distinct. The world is run by the syndicate, whose end goal is to revive the dead alien gods they worship. When world inevitably falls to demonic corruption, they simply create a new paradise that’s closer to perfection and move everyone to it. In the game Paradise Killer, a brutal mass murder occurs just as one of these transitions is being finalized and you are called out of exile to uncover what happened. There aren’t many people left who haven’t moved onto the next paradise yet and so you have to piece together a truth from their words and evidence you find to determine which of them is responsible.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: This game was absolutely amazing. While I did have a few gripes with the game it didn't take away from the over-all experience that it lends itself to.Positives: The game is absolutely gorgeous. I'm not sure if it is inspired by Danganronpa but if it is it shows brilliantly in the artwork, from the 3d landscapes that are absolutely stunning in their colors as well as how they are over-all designed mixed with the 2d artwork of the complex and creative characters. The story was also quite creative. It left me guessing in quite a few places, and ultimately it was a fine game of being absolutely certain on the guilt of one half, and everything falling into place by time the trial happened. It was fantastic. I also found the world building amazing, from the characters themselves making me fall in love with them to the general lore of the world such as the various gods that existed to the entire system that the paradises function in, and by the end of the game I was still hungry to learn more about the world and revisit this setting again, even if it wasn't necessarily with the characters I grew to like.Mixed: Theres only one thing that I truly dislike about the game, and only one thing I feel mixed about. Their minor nitpicks, but it would be unfair not to list them. I loved the world building, the way the world was introduced to you, and the implications the lore had in the grand scheme of things, but at the same time it made me feel like I was drowning in information. As it stands, I wouldn't have it any other way and I wouldn't want the sequel to change in its world building, but as I have seen somewhere else it feels like your playing a sequel or reading the second novel of a series. Your given a lot of information your expected to know, and never really explained this information bluntly. Your left to pick up pieces and interpret the lore as you go. Its not terrible, and I quite enjoyed it, but at the same time I almost would be hard pressed to say I don't know much about this world in general. I want to know more about it.Negatives: The one negative I have is about one of the final parts of the game. At one part of the game I had pretty much talked to everyone, 'befriended' everyone, and thought I had gathered all the evidence. I'm fairly certain I hadn't, as I did find that I was missing one piece of evidence at the end of the game, but at that point I was convinced I had figured everything out. I would have started the trial without a key piece of evidence that completely exposes the main killer. I found it by complete accident. It didn't ruin the game, but I was starting to have problems by that point and wish the location of this last critical piece of evidence was better hinted at, or in a better location.Over-all: It was fantastic. It had problems, but they were so minor that it didn't subtract from the game itself in the slightest. I hope they continue this world in some fashion. Thank you for the fantastic experience, and I couldn't recommend more even if I tried!
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot understand the amount of positive reviews this game is getting. The story is bland, Paradise Killer just dumps fanfiction level exposition about demons, gods and whatnot on you. It's full of nonsensical character names and absurd lore to a point where the whole thing doesn't really make any sense and comes off as uninteresting. It simply lacks substance, charm and execution to pull this kind of thing off.Another big problem is that the world is just empty, artificially inflated with copy pasted assets and models to a point where  it's simply boring and looks uglier than it would otherwise. There's hardly anything to find in the dull streets and paths around the island - no npcs, no interesting places, nothing - just bits of lore and in-game currency pick ups. The currency that you apparently need for unlocking some clues/tools and fast traveling, which again just feels like another trick to artificially inflate the play time. Whoever decided that fast traveling in a game like this should cost currency should probably consider a career path other than game design.Honestly the first 40 minutes were so bland that I can't be bothered to see if theres anything more under the crust.The only good things I find about it are the artwork and music. They're stylish and catchy, too bad they cant carry the game on their own.Paradise Killer tries so hard to immitate Danganronpa but falls flat on its face in every aspect. Spare yourself the disappointment and play something else.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I was enthralled into this game for several days. My poor partner had to deal with me every few hours coming to him with a million theories only to show up a couple hours later completely disproving myself! Even up until the VERY end that is the only time when I figured out what REALLY happened. Thats how you know this game is good. You can't find the solution easily, plus all of the characters are so dynamic! Except for one guy, who's sole purpose in life is to be a jerk to you, but I digress.I recommend this game to anyone that enjoys open world game play, mystery solving, and those that enjoy story rich games. I am sad that I have finished this game and can't wait to see what Kaizen comes up with next!
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an interesting mix of Danganronpa/Visual Novel/Open-world exploration with a heavy dose of vaporwave aesthetic sprinkled all over it.The gameplay is all about building up evidence/statement/alibis/alibi-breakers surrounding several aspects of the Big Murder Case the protagonist gets called out of exile to solve, all for a final trial showdown after you feel you collected enough evidence on your Starlight laptop and have a good idea of who did what.   If I had to give it a numerical score it would be around  so I do end up recommending it.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I disliked the massive amount of walking back-and-forth between the characters to interrogate them, but I loved the adventurous aspect of this game. The game world is strange, beautiful and a joy to explore. Even after 10 hours I came across a part of the map that I'd completely missed somehow. Great soundtrack, it was a really relaxing time and just what I needed.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: The environment and music is so good in this game I feel like I'm literally taking a holiday on a beach resort every time I play it. Great vibe. The murder mystery is well crafted too and it is satisfying gradually piecing together what took place and why. The story is very interesting and explores esoteric and philosophical themes.  The game uses a lot of environmental storytelling, and there are cool things to find out about how the island operates and what it's about around every corner. The dialogue and characters are very well written and there's a lot of great humor throughout the game.Also, it has some of the best movement mechanics around, with a double jump and dash being available, and this makes traversing the island a breeze.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome quest in the style of the 80s with a great musical environment. Acidic bright colors at the same time like Danganronpa series and like Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney - really good combination.Lore of this game at the beginning are...difficult. BUT! It's worth understanding, believe me.I rarely write reviews but in this case, I really want to thank the guys from Kaizen Game Works. Game is perfect. We NEED more chapter of it. Keep up the good work!
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing investigative experience. You'll need a few hours in order to completely understand the story that unfolded and is unfolding before you but after that, is a boundary-free, completely surreal experience.The investigation is entertaining and rewarding, and the vaporwave atmosphere simply amazing (the OST does a wonderful job). I just wished for a more nuanced final trial - if you gather enough clues, there's no real failure chance. I wished there were more games like this! I fell in love with every part of the story and the island.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent, low stress, exploration murder mystery game full of great lore and creepy surreal cosmic cults.  If you enjoy poking at corners and finding ways up and over obstacles for the hell of it, you will love this game.  The music is amazing and so is the whole aesthetic.I spent most of my early play just exploring places rather than talking to NPCs and it added to the slow buildup of "What is wrong with this place?!? WHAT IS EVEN GOING ON?" a bit more entertaining, but by no means is it the only way to play it.If there is anything I'm sad about, it's that I wanted more lore/secrets/easter eggs to find.  I give this game 5 out of 5, totally fun and worth checking out.

_childDocuments_.review: An entertaining open-world visual novel that has the player running around solving a conspiracy, speaking to suspects and collecting evidence in any order that they choose.I hesitate to call this a great detective game however, as the player's computer companion automates most of the brain work. The endgame trial is a pretty big letdown as well, as the player will "achieve victory" regardless of who they accuse and the evidence they present.Still, I had a great time with Paradise Killer. Catchy tunes and memorable characters. I would recommend it to others who are looking for a fun mystery that doesn't take itself too seriously.

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly this one didn't do it for me. Being a huge Fan of Ace Attorney and Danganronpa i was very excited when I saw that one at the PC Gamer Show in 2020. So be warned I am gonna draw some comparisons to those games in this review. If you don't think that's fair you should probably read a different review.Anyway the first impression of the game was very nice for me. It had an interesting cast, the worldbuilding is interesting and something completely unique and the overall aesthetic is completely unmatched. However what kills it for me is the lack of a red threat throughout the story. It really does feel like an Ace Attorney or Danganronpa game but you are playing all 4-6 cases single game would have at the same time! You see, those games get often critisiced for being too linear, but that means you unravel the mysteries the way they were meant to be unraveled, one after the other. Paradise Killer gives you complete freedom in how to solve the case but that ends up with overwhelming you with details and new loose ends that I straight up kept forgetting what I am even investigating in the first place. Pair that with the fact that every single topic in the game is a dialouge option for each and every character on the Island. As you can imagine many times all a character can say about a very specific topic is "Sorry I don't know anything about that, you should ask XYZ about that!". This wouldn't be a problem if the games map wouldn't mark these as new dialouge everytime they unlock. So you might end up traveling across half the map and walk down paths you have already walked through five times to reach a character with "new dialouge options" just for them to tell you to get lost because why would they know what the Islands barkeeper had for breakfast at the morning of the murder (Exaggaration, i  don't think that was a plotpoint in the game). In ace attorney and Dangarnonpa you get like 3-5 Dialouge dialouge options for a character and those actually make sense asking. Sure not all of those are revealing critical plot points but at least they offer more than just "IDK LOL".At the end of it all, maybe it actually is me and not the game. Maybe some people will enjoy it for the exact reasons why I hated it. But after i realized that I just didn't care anymore because it felt like I spent 8 hours getting nowhere, I just kinda stopped. This was sadly not the cool "whodunit" I expected.

_childDocuments_.review: Short version: Set voice frequency to never, otherwise an excellent mystery game that might kickstart a whole new genre. Don't just watch a playthrough, you can investigate and learn things in a different order from another player, making the journey one of a kind. Don't expect a Phoenix Wright style trial though, investigating is the main part of the game.Long:The limited time 1 hour demo for this game during the online PAX event was the first time I had seen or heard of it, yet it grabbed me immediately. I'm generally not a fan of walking sims, but combining danger free exploration with a mystery to solve changes that completely for me. Finding information about the background of the setting and characters is as rewarding as finding actual evidence for the case, and the soundtrack to it all is excellent. I wishlisted it and bought it day one.My one complaint for the full game is that the demo didn't have voice acting yet, and was better for it. The voice actors themselves do a fine job, but the lines they can say rarely match well to what's on screen, and the main characters "Nani the hell?" shouldn't be in there at all. I turned voices off entirely after she kept ruining genuinely surprising revelations by making me groan at an already old meme. This is my only real complaint about the whole game though.Like any mystery game there is a fixed amount of evidence to find and definite answers to every question. Unlike every other mystery game, your first playthrough won't be exactly the same as anyone else; you can find evidence in a completely different order from another player. As an example, I was sure I had the whole thing figured out until I found another piece of evidence near the very end that complicated things. The actual trials are quite short and to the point, but the journey to them is the main appeal with this game.I'm not sure if I found out everything, but I'm happy with the ending I got and enjoyed every minute of it. Definitely got my money's worth.

_childDocuments_.review: Half of the game I played offline, so the hours shown don't match what I actually played (about 15~16hrs).Seriously, it's been such a great experience. Bought it during the Steam Sales just before it was given to me on July 2021's Humble Bundle and have no regrets about not returning it.The exploration is pretty well done, although you have to move back and forth between characters every time you discover anything and fast travel has a limited currency paywall, so you decide you don't need to fast travel as everything is relatively close (may take 2-3 minutes in the endgame when you know everything, which is when you really have to move that much) and it can be bothersome at the end.You have trails about where to go and what to do at all times, so you'll never feel stuck. Some clues can only be obtained through increasing your relationship levels with others, so I would really encourage it.The trials can be accessed at any point you feel you have enough clues to pinpoint the crime to somebody, which is great. You can do whatever you want at any point, and have many places to explore so feel free to move around the island to uncover another piece of truth.I've been thinking about the game nonstop these days that I've been playing it, what really happened and who was involved in the crime. It really has been a great experience, and I would recommend it to anyone that has an interest in detective-like games. It is really fun too if what you are looking for is a collectathon. And the mixture of both is just glorious.Have fun in Paradise!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm honestly not sure how I feel about this game. On the one hand, it is a pretty good mystery game with a very unique flavor and world to it that makes me want to always be learning more about it. On the other though, the gameplay mechanics themselves are tedious and the ending felt like I was intentionally fed two solutions on purpose for the sole purpose of making me unsure as to which was the right one. I spent some time painstakingly trying to figure out which was the correct answer and it turned out to not matter as much as I thought, which I found to be a bit of a let down. It could have been though that I was super tired from staying up late because I couldn't stop playing and my brain didn't fully understand. The gameplay was also quite tedious as it was a lot of running around somewhat aimlessly over a space that was simply too large.There were also quite a few core mechanics that were never explained and I wish I had known right out of the gate. Like hey you should go get a foot bath because that allows you to see any pickup items around you. Or hey you should go to all of the Syndicate symbols because those are the computer terminals to progress the main plot. Or hey, don't worry about fast travel costs, just get the foot bath so you can see pickup items and then you will never run out of blood crystals. I would have done like 50% less wandering aimlessly around if I had known this stuff to be honest.Overall though, I would play a Paradise Killer 2 with a cleaner ending and less tedious gameplay mechanics and would recommend this game for detective fans who want something genuinely unique and interesting.Also, the final version of the main song that plays throughout the game absolutely slaps.
