_childDocuments_.review: The aesthetics speak for themselves: pop-vaporwave, bureaucratic pagan mysticism, and a lot of blood. The vaporwave deployment of archaeological visual motifs (cuneiform, pyramids, etc.) runs the risk of being corny and Orientalist at times, but the setting of  relates to "the real world" in such a way to be cohesive and interesting. and  are absolutely touchstones, among others, both for the character design as well as the core gameplay elements. That being said, there are some bold choices that make  unique:Overall,  wants you to engage with its geography and narrative atmosphere, and it expects you to be responsible for that. That means getting lost, picking up Blood Crystals (the currency), and collecting countless "meaningless" items, each containing a couple sentences of flavor text. Sure it may feel offensive to have to pay tokens for fast travel and other things, but the game gives you audio clues to find them, so just explore, and don't be scared of running out.The game doesn't strive for a singular climactic moment during the trial -- you accuse someone and exhaust the dialogue the game calculates from your evidence and choices. This is a breath of fresh air coming from the linearity of other investigation games whose endings are bogged down by riddles and monologues.  lets me make discoveries and deductions on my own, and doesn't make me perform them in the game. All that is expedited so  can do what other investigation games don't, which is to provide a world worth investigating alongside the crime.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautifully bizarre game that is a nice take on the investigatory murder-mystery game genre. The art direction and theming is beautifully on-point throughout the experience, but the alien nature of the setting doesn't get in the way of understanding the case - any relevant aspects are neatly worked into your experience, and the major twists of the case are set up nicely with the dialogues that you experience on the way.The mystery presented is a compelling one, and the characters are well-developed and have motivations that tie into their backgrounds appropriately and are convincing as to how they influence their actions. The designs of some of them, and their attitudes, are both hilarious and endearing. The setting, while hugely alien to reality, is internally consistent enough to support everything that goes on, and remains just relatable enough that the ways in which it differs from how reality really works stand out when they come up.In terms of negatives, the game could have done a little bit more to push you towards using the foot baths - they provide quality-of-life upgrades that I would have missed if a friend hadn't urged me to use them. The game might have worked better with a time limit of some sort - as it is, the fact that you can go to the final trial early, without having all of the information, is less impactful. Having more pressure to work directly on unraveling the most important threads you have, and to budget your time wisely, might have made that more significant. But the lack of a restriction really made it easier to enjoy the weird intricacies of the island, and to figure out some of the stranger and more out-of-the-way twists.All-in-all, a game I'm very happy to recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I like to wait a little time after playing a game to give it a proper review. It allows me to have some perspective on it and not go with my initial impulsive thoughts. The sound design, story and aesthetics in this game are killer. It's a special game indeed where I remember the audio so sharply and fondly in my mind. It is not without its flaws. The endless walking (noted by most reviewers as an annoying feature), the slightly dodgy map and the frustrating fast travel system could all be improved. It says something that I began to see this quirks as being charming as I continued to play the game. I accepted them as I accepted some of the buggier aspects of games I loved in childhood. I reflected on the virtues of the imperfect game, a game where its charm shines so particularly despite and because of its quirks.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good and memorable game. Not a great or legendary one. But definitely good and definitely memorable and a great experience. The gameplay wasn't perfect but that doesn't make a game as a whole. The sum of it parts add up to something better.What I  about the game:- The core gameplay involved an investigation. However the menus and dialogues can get quite unwieldy and tedious after reading through a lot and I didn't find the main investigation notes to be coherent with my own thought/discovery process on the island.- Light spoiler about the entire game, not the plot:  Non-spoiler summary: The game can feel a bit like a visual novel instead of an investigation if you carefully explore all your options.- The Blood Crystal system could use some work. I was hoarding them like crazy, not using them for fast travel (traveling across the island is quite boring if you've explored all that before) and ended up wasting a lot of time relatively to just walk from one place to another while in hindsight I've could have used those crystals.These were my main points that this wasn't a great game yet. But what made it a great experience?What I :- The atmosphere. My god, is it a beautiful mind♥♥♥♥y vaporwave style atmosphere and executed very right under the limitations of being a small studio. - The music. Incredible. Paradise (stay forever) is still living in my head rent-free since I completed it a few days ago.- Worldbuilding. The places you visit truly feel like a mystery with a story about it. While the places were abandoned, it didn't feel like I was headed anywhere that was devoid of all life. That only happened when I finished it and went back.- It was ruthless in its convictions. They had an idea in mind and nearly minimalistically added everything that supported that idea which was totally an oddball considering the current AAA atmosphere and I respect them for strongly following that vision.- The movement was really good, could have used some spit and shine on some places, but the act of walking itself was effortless,  and I never really felt it was in the way. - I really liked the idea of being able to open-world explore a lot of leads and clues and come to your own conclusions.All in all, with its beauties and flaws, I'd recommend this game if you're interested in well-written murder mysteries, banging city pop music, strange worlds and/or vaporwave aesthetic. If you like all of them, this game is probably for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Paradise Killer is an open world visual novel, the visual novel aspect of this game is good, but the open world aspect, not so much. A game with a good story that is unfortunately undone by it's  monotonous open world traversal and gameplay loop. The environments look fun and are vibey, but really lack detail and storytelling. The world design and environment sorts of break down in to a monotonous maze in which you are constantly battling against it's verticality and winding passageways to get to a character or a piece of evidence. The game world is filled with meaningless collectibles that don't really incentivize exploration. However, Paradise Killer's lore is exceptional. One of the most unique settings that I've ever seen in the video game medium. A trans-dimensional religious cult called the Syndicate utilizes humans from alternate realities to assist in the re-summoning of dead gods. Syndicate members are high society and live forever, toiling at their endless attempts to summon the gods. Demon's endlessly assault the syndicate corrupting their efforts which requires them to recreate their reality (island) to start the process anew. Each iteration of the island is an attempt at creating a perfect incorruptible environment. It's really cool stuff. The game also has a really great city pop soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely write reviews, but in the case of Paradise Killer I'll make an exception because it's one of the most unique and interesting games I've ever played. The world is completely insane and yet feels cohesive and lived in, with characters as believable as they are memorable. The murder mystery gameplay manages to be simple without being boring, and there's a massive amount of collectable artefacts and currency to encourage you to explore the map. It helps if you're as much of a sucker for some top tier vaporwave aesthetic as I am...This has quickly risen to being one of my favourite games of all time, and I really hope we see a Paradise Killer 2 at some point!

_childDocuments_.review: Some games are just made for you.So, when I first read about Kaizen Game Works’  – a murder mystery on a weird tropical island – I figured it would be exactly my kind of paradise. Glitzy and cool and dangerous, with plenty neon. It was, and maybe that would’ve been enough. But to my immense pleasure it turned out to be oh so much more.Describing the game isn’t easy; it’s such a singular experience. Playing it, I kept thinking of an episode of Michael Mann’s 1980s cop show, , where one of the characters, Trudy, encountered a UFO. That episode is not much liked, and for good reason. It’s a bit of a far cry from the drug cartels and corrupt yuppies Crockett and Tubbs spent their time fighting. Sometimes genre-blending just doesn’t work. Yet in a weird way,  inadvertently asks where that UFO came from and what it wanted with Trudy - answering it in the wildest way possible.If she  been whisked away, Trudy would have found herself on a metaphysical island with a population of human slaves governed by immortal aliens who are trying to bring their ancient gods back to life. Trudy wouldn’t have liked that and eventually would have been sacrificed in a blood ritual as the next island came into being. Because these islands keep failing, right. Failing miserably to achieve their eschatological ends. So, they get rebooted. Perfectionism’s a ♥♥♥♥♥.The world of  is bizarre. Overwhelmingly so. It’s loaded with lore – a dreaded word and, in the wrong hands, easily the real paradise killer. But in a masterstroke of storytelling,  makes that absurdity the point. Even though you’re reading a ton of text and reaching for esoteric details, it’s conveyed as part of the  of the place.That place, the island, is deserted, save the depraved Syndicate who govern it, and the cruelty of its existence is as bright as its false sun. Its overloaded history has produced a cadre of mad, evil, scheming immortals, whose conspiracies warrant the arrival of Lady Love Dies – the “investigation freak”. Someone has murdered the island’s council, and no one’s moving on until she learns whodunit.The open-world island is massive and gorgeous. With its aesthetic beauty and eccentric characters, it’s something totally unique. I couldn’t get enough of being there, even though there’s a relative parsity of stuff to  do. Mostly you’ll be looking for clues, finding collectables, and speaking with suspects. It’s in the latter that  comes brilliantly to life.Whether it’s the flirty playfulness of Doctor Doom Jazz or the cool condescension of Carmelina Silence,  suspects are perfect whodunit material. Lady Love Dies has been out of action for a while – an unfortunate exile involving a demon – so some of these people are new, but others are old friends. What they all are is guilty of , and diagnosing that guilt is your job. Every conversation sharpens your understanding of the crime, leading to fresh clues and surprising confessions.The web of intrigue is complex, and unravelling it is properly electrifying. When you feel like you’ve put all the pieces in place, it’s up to you who to accuse. For my part, I felt I’d achieved a real sense of catharsis, and yet I was sure I’d missed some minute clue that allowed one of the lesser culprits to wriggle free. Sure because as much as that island was something of a dream, it was an evil dream, and absolutely everyone in it a monster. In that context, guilt is a strange and heightened phenomenon......but I guess some things never die.* I went the whole review without mentioning the ECSTATICALLY GOOD soundtrack. For shame.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: It's "fine".The game is basically a walking simulator collectathon for 8 hours while you go talk to people and collect evidence. I'm sure there's an audience for that type of game, but I'm not it.The trial felt underwhelming. I was expecting a Danganronpa/Phoenix Wright style trial where you need to select proper evidence/rebuttals, but you basically just pick a person and show the evidence to convict them. No real deduction is needed.Following the evidence and piecing together the story was pretty fun, but there's at least a 2-3 hour time investment of mundane searching before you get to that point.There's a good game in here, but I don't think the time investment is worth the payoff.But you can abuse physics to wavedash to move stupidly fast once you get a certain upgrade, which made grinding a bit more bearable. The "fast travel" ironically takes too long and is a waste of time imo.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game, it's kind of like one huge open world chapter of an Ace Attorney game but in an alternate reality. The art of all the characters is really striking, the music is good, the alternate world babylon is really fun. I was actually pretty surprised with how big the island was and how much there was to explore. I liked to come back and chat with most of the characters over and over and see all their reactions. The trial at the end was a lot of fun--I thought it was going to be more serious, like an Ace Attorney trial (you know, no mistakes) but it was really refreshing to see that there was some flexibility to have different outcomes. The achievements for this game were really fun to get as well. With some games its such a drag to collect 100% of the game objects or whatever, but I really didn't want this game to end. Maybe there will be more crimes to investigate on Perfect 25?
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Paradise Killer is a wonderful detective game in an interesting world. This game does an amazing job of making you feel like there are secrets around every corner, and makes you want to scour the map for every last one to make sure that you have your story straight through the twists and turns it takes you on.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: A compelling murder mystery with a unique and creative setting.The premise this game runs with is that you spend the game gathering evidence preparing for the final trial where you can seek any charges you think you can prove. It's a cool alternative to the Ace Attorney style you usually see of being on-railed to a complete and canonical answer that you figure out during the trial. Makes the player feel more responsible for sleuthing and solving the case.Another surprisingly large aspect of the game is collectibles littered throughout the game world in well hidden places. I was often climbing around on the geometry in any way I could in search of them. For the most part they are purely optional collectibles, but there's a few instances of meaningful evidence being found tucked away in a spot like this (though as I said before, any and all evidence is ALSO optional in this game).
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Fair warning: your enjoyment of this game will likely hinge on how much you like the open world setting. It's a world with a few puzzles, lots of collectables, and no combat, and you are encouraged to look through every single nook and cranny first before using fast travel (you need blood crystals to unlock and use fast travel, and they're scattered throughout the map). There's also no compass to tell you your exact position on the map and where you're going; you're left to try to figure out for yourself where you need to go/what you need to do next. I personally love the open world setting but if what I described might be a problem you might have more fun just sticking with the Ace Attorney games.  With all that said, I cannot recommend Paradise Killer enough. The mystery is intriguing, the investigation is full of twists and turns, the ensemble cast is fantastic, and the whole aesthetic of the game is just absolutely gorgeous. Without spoiling too much, while the game does imply that there is a 'correct' route, you ultimately decide how the game ends and what defines 'justice', especially as you gather more evidence and build your relationships with the suspects. It's a game that will make you question your choices, and if you're into games that make you think and stay under your skin for awhile, you've come to the right place. Go play Paradise Killer now!
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: It is a walking simulator where you have to find and pick up stuff. That's the 95% of the game. The rest is some kind of investigation. The "investigation" is you find stuff and exhaust every speech option. In the end, there is a trial, where you tell everything you find. THE END.I only maxed out because I'm a sucker for exploration and I have a little OCD. I didn't enjoy it

_childDocuments_.review: my first ever steam review goes to a game that deserves it. the atmosphere of the game feels somewhat niche, which was perfect for me, but wasn't too gaudy otherwise. the storyline wasn't predictable, and i did have a few plot twists that really caught me off guard! i wouldn't recommend the game if you were 100% just in it for the storyline, however, as it might be a little.. tedious? to collect all the evidence. anyways 8.5/10!
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Paradise Killer is a fantastic game.The gameplay is lightweight but you have a whole Vaporwave island to explore at your own leisure and the story is the perfect mix of absurdity and mystery to keep you going. While talking to all the characters at your own pace you start connecting the dots and you can never be sure what you will find out next. Every time you wander off on the island you get rewarded for your adventurous nature and the vibe of the island and environment is immaculate. The soundtrack is so good there probably are meme reviews made in the template of "Amazing Album, came with a free game".The one thing that didn't sit right with me though was the trials at the end of the game: You spent the whole game thinking about the murder case and at the end, they made it a bit too easy for you by accumulating all the evidence against the suspects automatically. I wish that during the trials we would have to individually select the evidence we want to present from our little helper computer Starlight and decide for ourselves what's important and what's not or rather weave our own truth as any  good lawyer would. The other issue is the executions that happen so nonchalantly because you spent the whole game talking, maybe even bonding with the characters and then they perish without another word or conclusion, that was kinda unsatisfying.However, if you are into Vaporwave, exploration, or stories with strong mysteries, please check this one out.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game, it looks beautiful and the story is really compelling - the voice acting took some getting used to but I think it works as a stylistic choice. I did feel at the end like I wasn't sure if I had done everything I could have or if there was more left to discover; I think for completionist players like me it would really benefit from having achievements (e.g. exploration achievements like "collect all blood crystals" or story achievements like "").
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic. Interesting world, stellar music, crazy characters (both in design and in the general sense) and a compelling mystery. You play a fallen immortal detective that is recalled to active duty after the ruling elite of your demi-god caste is murdered right before the end of the world (don't worry, a new one has been built). The game gives you freedom to approach the investigation how you see fit, with a wonderfully designed world full of secrets and shortcuts to uncover.It has a few minor issues like some grammar mistakes and a couple obtuse puzzles, but well worth a trip to this bizarre little world.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Such a novel and intriguing concept for a game!Paradise Killer executes the open world mystery game idea perfectly, with a unique cast of quirky characters and an artstyle that reinforces the one of a kind setting and atmosphere flawlessly.And, I have to add this, the soundtrack is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing. Epoch did a really great job, and it genuinely elevates Paradise Killer to an entirely new level altogether.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a fun experience that's not really like any other game I've played before. The characters, setting and lore are all interesting and contain a depth that makes them exciting to learn about over the course of the game. The premise of the murder you work to solve is compelling, and the way the game approaches constructing the truth and enacting justice at the end is innovative and allows a shocking amount of room for player input. Paradise Killer is one of the best experiences I've had with a game in a while, and my only complaint is that I wish there was more. [EDIT: They just released a huge free update with more!!] The pacing is up to you, as the world is wide open for the entirety of the game, but the mystery moves along at a pace as you learn more that, even if you take your sweet time, doesn't make any of it feel slow. I highly recommend this game to anyone who's interested in the concept, even if this genre isn't usually what they go for. Paradise Killer is a fantastic experience, and I'm really looking forward to seeing what Kaizen Game Works does next after playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: tldr; Detective Conan on LSD feat. David Lynch - The Walking SimulatorThis is a rather unique game, with its combination of deep world building, weird and quirky characters, the neon-bright tropical island setting and its zealous themes and architecture. In it's core it's a detective game where you, "the investigation freak", explore an island and all its nooks and crannies, as well as talking to the various inhabitants, to find clues that help you solve various crimes linked to the mass-murder of the island's council.First of all, there's a lot to explore, from hidden rooms to artefacts, vending machines and even secret characters. Oddly enough, the devs did not enable achievements it seems, even though this game is something of a collectathon, with a ton of hidden objects scattered throughout the world. Most of them serve as currency, which after a bit of exploring you should have enough of to buy anything you can, so don't feel like you have to save up, while the rest is used for world building (although some are gameplay-relevant as well).Speaking of which, this game does a great job of creating a really unique and seemingly deep world, that has a rich past, it's own rules and traditions and confidently radiates a certain vibe. More games should be this brave and venture away from the boringly over-used themes of Greek mythology, Middle Ages, angsty teen dramas etc. and just build their own world. Kaizen surely succeeded in that and it makes the game feel fresh and interesting.It might be important to also note that there is no combat in this game, it really is just a walking simulator with parkour elements and dialogue. There are sometimes choice options in the dialogue but they seem to be more flavour than actually affecting anything. Technically, there are also puzzles thrown into the mix, but they feel more like an alibi and are easily the weakest part of the game. They are neither difficult nor engaging. Some are crucial to entering closed off areas and finding the most important clues. Others only have currency rewards, which I found a little disappointing. The strength definitely lies in the plot and the odd characters and in the satisfying process of unveiling the truth behind all the secrets. Although, in reality, it's just about finding the clues and then everything is just kind of presented to you. It's not a game where you have to use logic to find loopholes in someone's alibi or come up with a story yourself. Whenever a clue has not been concluded yet, it means you haven't found an item, a location or spoken to a person enough. Despite that, it is still a lot of fun to roam the island, simply because it's so quirky and otherworldly and invites you to have a look around, jump on rooftops and parkour your way around. And the characters have their own personalities, accents and stories to tell. Some even give you further clues after you speak to them enough in private.The most fulfilling part of the game is however the trial at the end. Serving justice is exactly what you will want after the roughly 10-14 hour island marathon.If you like somewhat weird games with a slow pace, an inventive and intriguing plot, fresh ideas and themes, funky music and the certain pizzazz that other games often lack, then you will enjoy this one. It may not be a masterpiece but it should really be praised for how brave and unique it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: A game absolutely oozing personality. Beautiful art style, fantastic sound track, and a bewitching island to run riot in. The characters you encounter are fun and interesting in their own ways. A wonderful, spunky and utterly charming protagonist. It's an eighties-retro-lovercraftian-detective game, what else is there to say? It's really good!

_childDocuments_.review: The Sherlock Holmes games (especially the later ones like Crimes & Punishments and Devil's Daughter) focus more on forming deductions based on evidence obtained through puzzle-solving. Something like L.A. Noire focuses on correct answers obtained through gaming the interrogation system. Now, I'm not a detective but I think Paradise Killer, in its simplicity, is a truer detective experience.By letting you explore this very large island, gather evidence, question suspects about the evidence you've found, and establishing the timeline of events until you're satisfied with it (rather than explicitly tracking completion, not unlike Her Story), it does end up feeling closer to what an actual detective would do to solve a murder mystery. In that way this game is most similar to a Sherlock Holmes: Consulting Detective, and the structure is largely the same -- once you feel you have enough to make your case, you begin the process of answering questions about the crime(s), accuse people, and then present your evidence.It's worth saying that this game is weird as ♥♥♥♥. The lore and mythology in this game are as wild, unique, and intriguing as the trailer would lead you to believe. It took me some time to familiarize myself with the terms and traditions of this world, but over time I developed a fluency and began to uncover the conspiracies and understand the motives in the context of how that world operates.Also that soundtrack. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.

_childDocuments_.review: Weird and wonderful game.A very visually and conceptually striking world. Constantly rewards you for exploration: clues, currency, and world-building/color. Great, layered mystery. Unlocking movement upgrades seems well-timed with your mastery of navigating environments. The bright pink colors signifying interaction objects is super helpful. Characters are memorable and unique. If you like Danganronpa, Phoenix Wright, etc., the logic, clues, and case file system will pull you in. If you like exploration, you'll be rewarded for that.Also, there's a cute dog!Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this because I like mystery-solving games and the way it was advertised (you can accuse anyone at any point in the game) intrigued me. I wasn't initially very impressed, though. The characters and world seemed overly weird and quirky, and first-person viewpoint made me queasy, and gameplay mostly seemed to involve running around and picking up random items that didn't seem to be very useful. I frequently got lost and wasn't really sure what I was doing.After some fiddling with the display settings to reduce the queasiness, I started to enjoy exploring the island and figuring out its secrets. Checking the Discussion forums also helped - some of the game's most helpful features are only accessible if you do things that you might be unwilling to do because they cost Blood Crystals, a finite resource you collect as you explore the island. Yes, there are only so many Blood Crystals, and you could paint yourself into a corner if you use "fast travel" too often (it costs one Blood Crystal to activate a fast travel point and one Blood Crystal to fast travel), but seemingly useless things like  are very much worth spending Blood Crystals on. I bought every item on the island that I could find, paid for every available service and scrap of information, used fast travel a handful of times, and still ended the game with about 50 Blood Crystals (with a few probably still on balconies, because I eventually decided those were too much of a pain to get).A few hours of exploration later, and the world and mystery itself hooked me. Every time I thought I'd been everywhere, I discovered new hidden areas that provided me with more evidence and potential areas of investigation (and more Blood Crystals). I had to laugh, because this was a murder mystery and it took me somewhere between 13-16 hours to finally reach the crime scene. I'd previously found two other places I'd thought were the crime scene, due to all the blood, but it turns out that these characters live in a world that is really fond of bloodshed. (Speaking of bloodshed: although certain areas of the map have a very sinister feel to them, there's no way for you to die in this game. Falling into deep blue water will send you to a nearby Save spot, but that's it. Jump off buildings all you want - sometimes that's the easiest way to get from one place to another.)The trial aspect didn't work at all the way I would have expected, based on what I'd initially heard about the game. True, you can accuse anyone at any time, but you have to have the necessary evidence in order for your accusation to stick, and it's not like the evidence, crimes, and suspects change every time you play. The main thing is that, the longer you play and the more you explore, the more likely you are to uncover all layers of what occurred on the island.I'm pretty sure I've collected all the evidence it's possible to collect, so I conducted my first trial. Although I didn't think the results were necessarily false, I wasn't satisfied with how things turned out (the only punishment is execution - I'd have preferred a couple people to have been exiled instead, if they really had to be punished), so I'll probably replay the trial another time or two to see if I can get a more satisfying and less upsetting ending. Overall, I highly recommend this, but be aware that it takes a while to really become good, and I imagine the first areas you're drawn to explore will affect your initial impressions a lot. (Personally, I first ended up at K. HX's place, where I debated whether it was safe to jump off a cliff, did so, and was then worried that I'd never figure out how to get off the beach and back to somewhere more interesting again.}
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: In considering what to write for this review, fresh off the back of completing the game to what I would consider to be "best ending", I find it difficult to nail down my exact feelings about the game. Not to say that I don't like it; quite the opposite, I found that I really really loved this game finishing the trials of the game and finding the truth was bitter sweet.I'll gloss over the plot a bit. You are an investigator, a crime has occurred, it is up to you to find the truth. Things pretty quickly start to unravel as you discover that not everything is as it would seem. A detective drama at heart, but what Paradise Killer does best is world building. The basic premise revolves around the main characters all being part of a syndicate to revive their dead gods. And from there, the lore of the world that is born forth sucked me in almost instantly. Learning about the gods, the little "Paradise" that the Syndicate has been building for several millennia, it gave the world an unexpected depth. I found myself gladly reading every scrap of lore I could find to glean new insights into the world of Paradise Killer.Graphically, the game isn't going to be taxing on most low-mid range PCs, so anyone with even basic on-board graphics and no graphics card can jump in and enjoy it. The story of Paradise Killer takes place on a massive island that is "Paradise" and is a fully free-roaming 3D world. I found myself spending hours just running around the island finding many of the various collectibles in the world or searching for new leads in the investigation.I wanted to separate this line to make a point. While exploring, you will be treated to an incredibly good soundtrack. And you will find more songs as you explore, adding to the excellent tunes that you can listen to while seeking out clues or trying to track down lore about the world itself.The game is not incredibly long but can be padded out depending on how quickly you want to close the case or are able to find evidence. Lady Love Dies' personal computer will track the evidence and leads you have found, organized into "Notes" for leads and "Cases" for evidence and clues that are sorted. The notes section was helpful to me when trying to find some of the crucial evidence I was missing, but I did end up having to look up a couple of clue locations because the notes were either too vague or I was looking in the wrong place. As an example, one of the notes will tell you to search a particular building "from top to bottom" for clues. And when they say that, they mean literally, including evidence at the very bottom and the very top of the building. If you want to find the "true" ending and gather all the evidence, careful examination and exploration are key, otherwise you will find that you still have some loose ends to tie up at the very end.All-in-all, Paradise Killer is probably going to be one of the top 5 games I played this year. With a tight 8-10 hours of play (if you just want to solve the case and not 100% the collectibles), the story and world do not become stale before the case has been solved and kept me riveted, even once I was fairly sure I knew the truth of the crimes. And honestly, my friends can't get me to shut up about it so that's a 10/10 in my book!

_childDocuments_.review: Original, weird and enthralling. At first I was completely lost in a mad world, with a very confusing history, and a crime to be solved that I knew nothing about. And little by little, by exploring Paradise Island, talking to its few remaining inhabitants, and collecting bits of information here and there, it all started to make sense. Well, the NPCs, the crimes, the motives and so on all made sense. Paradise is still a mystery to me.I really liked this game. Sure it has dated graphics, and the controls are a bit clunky, but the story and the scenario are really worth it.

_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: A truly wonderful hidden gem of a game. The setting, characters, and murder mystery are all extremely unique. I have never experienced a fictional universe like the one presented by Paradise Killer. Although extremely bizarre and psychedelic, it has its own internally consistent rules and lore that makes the setting work, no matter how outlandish everything might seem. Everything that is presented to you is so absurd yet so genuine and unironic, that slowly the absurd becomes the plausible. Then the plausible becomes the mundane. Yes, this is a game that managed to make a vaporwave-inspired metaphysical universe with immortal beings with names like "Kiwami Eyes" or "Crimson Acid" existing in a pocket dimension kidnapping and enslaving humans like cattle to farm their psychic energy to resurrect a bunch of genocidal gods seem reasonable and mundane. Trust me, that's not even a tenth of the picture. But this game sells itself as a murder mystery. How's the mystery then? The mystery is wonderfully complex, and the investigative gameplay is one of the most organic that I've ever had the pleasure of experiencing. The key difference between this game and most other detective games is the fact that it has a free-roaming 3D sandbox, like Danganronpa or LA Noire but with much more verticality and higher density of ♥♥♥♥ to find. Exploration really is the name of the game here, as the things you find in the environment are usually 10x more revealing than whatever these shady ass characters are feeding you. Facts and evidence are presented to you in completely random order, or more specifically, in the order than you stumble upon them in the sandbox. And believe me, every single second, you will stumble into some sort of clue merely by exploring this jam-packed sandbox that the developers have so lovingly crafted. They really put in the effort to fill this place with secrets and answers, and I have had multiple instances where I've wandered off into an obscure corner of the map just to see if the devs have put an easter egg in there or something, only to discover that there is a massive clue to solving the mystery hidden right there in the corner. Along with Danganronpa, Phoenix Wright, or the Zero Escape games, this game is the patron saint of those "OH ♥♥♥♥" moments where you realize something you thought was true was actually wrong all along. TLDR: The world is surreal and unique, the characters are colorful and fun, the mystery is complex with intertwining plot threads, character motivations, and political intrigue, and the investigative gameplay is extremely immersive and rewarding. Get this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Great vapourwave murder mystery game whose characters and setting sucked me in, and didn't let me out until I had literally 100%'d it. Then it refused to leave my head for days. It trusts the player to come up with their own conclusions, and execute justice accordingly. All the while runs an insightful commentary on politics, classism, scapegoating and justice. Each character is beautifully-designed, extremely memorable and has their own fleshed-out motives and beliefs. Great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game.One of the best investigation games I've seen, the freedom it gives really made me feel like I was investigating, trying to piece together what was happening etc.One interesting thing (trying hard not to spoil) is that while I  there is a definite truth as to what happened and I think I figured it out, the game never tells you whether you did a good job or not. It just lets you find all the clues and make your own truth. Do you think you figured it out? Are there parts you're not sure about?Moreover you are free to do what you want with the clues. Maybe you find out that a character you really liked committed a crime. Maybe you can forgot to mention it, or find a way to pin it on someone else. Someone else you dislike but you're pretty sure is innocent. Maybe you commit to pure justice and kill your friends and spare your enemies. No matter what you choose the game won't tell you anything, you're the only one judging whether you did good or not.And finally there is the vibe. The game could have worked in a more boring setting, but there is something about that island, with the unique art style, with that music, that will make you really feel like you've been there. It will stay with you for a while.Really, really strong recommend, and thanks to the team for a genuinely amazing experience
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Paradise Killer's brilliance is in its understanding of the aspects of murder mystery that are most fun. The bombastic characters, uncovering clues, making suspects trip over their own stories revealing they know more than they're letting on. Capped by a satisfying trial, which allows you to prove your story true if you're clever enough in use of facts.All packed into a beautiful Y2K meets psychedelic vaporwave, sexy esotericism aesthetic, scored by a city pop soundtrack that'll make you want to stay forever.Paradise Killer turns truth and facts into two separate gameplay elements, separate narrative elements. And I think that's beautiful.

_childDocuments_.review: This game gets a "sorta" recommend from me.I have 100% this game (all evidence and collectibles) in about 9.8 hours.: Great mystery with some tedious gameplayStory:+Great mystery and fun to unravel-Very little world-building and character developmentIn terms of the story, the mystery itself was very fun. There is a lot of good intrigue and the game is good at throwing you off and making you doubt who did it until you assemble most of the evidence. There were fun twists and was a pretty satisfying in that way.The world they've built for this story is interesting, but very little about it is revealed. There is some flavor text that gives slightly more detail, but if its not important to the mystery, it is not expanded on. Similarly, the characters have distinct personalities and unique histories, but their characters remain very static throughout the story making them unengaging clue-dispensers after a while.Gameplay:+Assembling clues is fun and interesting-Map is not fun to navigate-Collectibles are bad and pad the game outThe actual act of gathering clues and talking to witnesses is pretty fun. The clues are distributed carefully, letting the intrigue draw you in. There are also very few sequence breaks despite being able to get clues in almost any order. The trial sequence at the end where you present your evidence and accuse the killer was very hype and very satisfying. Unfortunately everything else kinda sucks.Some clues are hidden way out of sight and can be very annoying to find. Most clue locations are signaled in some way, but a few are not. There is at least one clue hidden in a corner of a high area and a corner of a low area. I would've never found them if I wasn't searching for some of the optional collectibles.The optional collectibles are atrocious and serve only to pad out the game time. The first collectible is money, which is limited and scattered everywhere. They are used for 2 characters' dialogue, payment to fast travel, and for unlocking more collectibles. Although there are an excess amount, having a limited currency used for fast traveling makes me not want to fast travel, especially since I will have to hunt for the money to pay for them. The money as a whole feels pretty unnecessary.There are whiskey bottles that allow you to listen to a conversation elsewhere in the world. These conversations have very little connection to the mystery, very little world-building, and feel kinda unnecessary.Relics are optional collectibles with some flavor text. Unfortunately, half of them have duplicate flavor text that can be found in the environment. There are also a set of collectibles with basically no flavor text like a pepper that says: "Somebody was growing peppers here." Because of that, they are not worth picking up except for...The collectible marker you can unlock will mark all collectibles in front of you. Some of the clues also count as collectibles and will be marked. Unfortunately, there is no way to tell what kind of collectible they are until you're close enough to pick them up and there are so many collectibles that your entire screen is filled with markers. Also some clues (despite picking them up like some other clues) are not marked.The whole civilian areas are completely devoid of anything but collectibles. They are difficult to navigate as there are a lot of turns, and is disproportionately large compared to their importance, this combined with the fast travel system needing payment makes going from suspect to suspect annoying. Also the mountains suck.Slightly spoilerish complaints:Conclusion:While I have been very harsh on the gameplay, I still enjoyed Paradise Killer. The story was engaging and I was very invested in solving the mystery. I still feel like I can recommend this game despite tedious gameplay elements. Give it a try if you enjoy interesting mysteries.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the Ace Attorney games, Paradise Killer scratched that same mystery + courtroom justice itch for me, and then some. I loved the setting, the worldbuilding, the characters. Despite getting into some dastardly deeds, I couldn't help but get attached to everyone! I appreciated how the game organized all the data and evidence into a straightforward, easy to navigate interface with Starlight. It's easy to get overwhelmed by a lot of information with mystery games like this, but as the game progressed things just kinda started to click for me, which was nice.  I also found it kinda relaxing to just...leave the story a bit and just wander around the island, parkour up buildings and cliffs just to see what I could find.A lot of love was put into this game, and I am absolutely hoping for a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: The best detective game I think I've ever played. The choice and freedom to accuse whoever based on evidence, rather than having your hand held by the narrative, is astounding. Not long ago I watched a very interesting video about the difficulty of creating a detective game where you truly feel like a detective. This tops games like LA Noire, Sherlock Holmes games, and many other games I've played where you're role-playing an investigator - at least in terms of making me feel like a real detective. Seriously, please play this game.I watched a few review videos which complained about things like the voice actors not acting all the dialogue and instead saying phrases or words on repeat, and how the exploration felt 'too limitless'. I think these kinds of criticisms for a game that exceeds every expectation are so ridiculous. I think the voices, even when not acting out full dialogue, really make the characters stand out. And I absolutely LOVE the exploration. I played all in all for around 20hrs and a good bit of that was spent jumping around the landscape to see the island from a different perspective (and find blood diamonds and "trash"). I could go on forever I think. But it's almost 3am. I beg you to PLAY THIS GAME. The world is so interesting and surprisingly deeper than a lot of games with a playtime of 40hrs.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing soundtrack and a fun mystery to solve. The worldbuilding is truly unique and it was a joy to learn more about Paradise and the characters living here. However, one main gripe I have is that there is no real reward for truly solving the mystery. You can completely fumble the mystery and accuse the wrong person every case and still receive the same ending you get from discovering the actual truth of the case. The main trial is also lackluster as suspects aren't really smart and don't do anything except say the worst lies/excuses you've ever heard or just completely cave at the first evidence presented. There's no debates over the evidence; it's just Lady Love Dies little circus.Would still recommend this game. A colorful cast with great designs and a colorful world with lots to explore. Slowly discovering the truth of the mystery was great fun even if the finale left me feeling a bit disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: I love having a 3D world to explore, but without real-time combat or need for controller skills, so this game helped scratch that itch. I found the story very engaging (though with occasional typos and I turned off the annoying sporadic voice acting). The story was revealed at a good pace through exploring the island. I always discovered more when I needed to, and never felt bored or stuck. I enjoyed that going off-piste in Paradise Killer often turned out to be the right choice, revealing evidence, or sometimes another blood crystal or relic, but either way rewarding my exploration. Some reviewers found travelling around the island to be quite tedious. I have a low tolerance of repetition, but I didn’t personally find this to be the case with Paradise Killer. I rarely needed to revisit spaces. I made exploration of the environment the focus, chatting with characters as I passed them, which I think helped. It was only towards the end the focus switched to just travelling back and forth between characters to tie up loose ends – but the fast travel points helped and leaping from high places was a fun way to get around faster.I felt I had a high level of agency in the development of the story (through choosing where to go and who to speak to next), which I really value, and I liked that I needed to review the evidence and decide who to accuse. The answers ultimately were quite apparent, but I enjoyed that I had to spend a little time reading the evidence for the different layers to come into focus. The only aspect of the gameplay I found disappointing was the mechanic for breaking into computers – this was a missed opportunity for some proper puzzles. The length of the game was just right (ignore my Steam play time – I often leave my games paused while I do other things, which annoyingly gets counted). It took enough effort to feel satisfying and concluded just before boredom set in.

I think many people will be unsatisfied with the available endings, but I thought it fit with the overarching themes of the world.

_childDocuments_.review: Give this game a chance. I'll admit, my first experience trying to play Paradise Killer was not a good one. I'm not typically a player of open world games, so in my initial attempt to get my bearings, I found myself wandering aimlessly around the many similar-looking apartment buildings, unable to find the people I was supposed to talk to or the scenes I was supposed to investigate. The story was strange, the scenes were trippy, and I got frustrated.But when I finally came back to this game to try again, in earnest, I loved what I found.Paradise Killer is a visual novel that breaks the mold and allows you, as immortal Investigator Lady Love Dies, to hunt for clues on a surreal manufactured island on the brink of collapse in order to solve the crime to end all crimes: a locked-room murder of Paradise's council members. If that didn't make any sense to you, don't worry about it. In fact, don't worry about much! Here are a few lessons to help you navigate this odd yet rewarding game.Once you've played for a while, you're sure to fall in love with the vaporwave aesthetic, the fascinating characters, the absolutely bonkers world-building, and the intrigue of the mystery. My best advice is to stick with it, even if you're not sure. This game's strength is that it really makes you feel like you're the investigator: you snoop, you sleuth, you interrogate--and then you take people to trial. When you finally reach that ending, it's up to you to make sure you have the facts straight so you can deliver the truth.Truly, the only downside for me was how difficult it was to find my way around--and how much stuff there is to collect with no real purpose for some of it. I literally got lost again with only minutes left of the game. That kind of tedious gameplay can take the wind out of your sails a bit, but the rest of the story is so worth it. Wholeheartedly recommend this unique and addicting game!

_childDocuments_.review: This is an *absolute* GEM! I got completely lost in the world of Paradise 24. It's the perfect blend of acid visuals, incredible narrative, interesting sleuthing, idyllic exploration, quirky characters, insanely good music, and a mountain of collectables (yey!). Watching the story unfold hour to hour with its twists and turns was an absolute joy and I cannot recommend this game enough :) Keeping my eye on these Devs!10/10! Highly recommend! :)

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of very few games (and probably not only games) that manages to create a convincing atmosphere of total madness. Or being high. If you've ever read Philip K.♥♥♥♥ and felt the terror creeping out of the pages and mixing with your own reality, you'll know what I mean. Except that madness in Paradise Killer is not grim and punishing. It's bright and colorful, and the game universe is very consistent with almost zero inner contradictions. You started playing and don't understand a thing? Nevermind, just play along! In an hour you'll know enough about gods, demons, vending machines and reality folding drives. Technically, this game is a wild mix of metroidvania, 3D platformer, and visual novel. It rewards you for exploring the world, though you're not obliged to do so. What's nice, there's always more than one way to get what you want, be that an item on a rooftop or a piece of evidence. You can always find your way around, if you don't feel like following the "default" path. Under its somewhat silly appearance, this game hides a solid captivating plot, a detective story with alibis and evidence, lies and truths. Everyone has their agency. Everyone can be found guilty. They can, however, be framed. They can both be guilty AND be framed at the same time. It's up to you to decide who's to blame in the end.And the music will keep playing out in your head long long long after you close the game. Even if you normally don't listen to the music like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: I would have preferred the game concentrated on the narrative, investigation, and character interaction parts rather than having open world collect-athon. collect Blood Crystals, gems, find all the Jackal guys, random items, collect evidence. unlock fast travel. collect soda cans. collect relationships with everyone. do side quests. Its too much. Even with the provided cheat/hint system (which is slow to activate) revealing locations of every single collectible, It's just too much to bother with. I also found it difficult to follow the trail of the case. There is big info dumps and long conversations I couldn't really follow. It's helpful all information gathered has summarized notes in-game, but there's so much information I still found it confusing and not an enjoyable way of interacting with information or characters.As an exploration game, this is a decent. There's plenty of things to find and places to explore. The surreal 80's/90's retro-wave aesthetic is quirky and fun. There is some fun banter and bizarre sense of humor if you can bother to get through the conversations. As a detective game, I don't find it very satisfying. The comparison between Ace Attorney and Paradise Killer is unreasonable. There is no character development, emotional moments, or satisfying "ah ha" conclusions. It did scratch the klepto-itch till i got bored. DNF

_childDocuments_.review: Sigh... I wish Steam had a notation based ranking system, because I would not just "Recommend" it. Indeed, Paradise Killer got me very surprised... and disappointed. And I don't really want to recommend it... Listen, I don't have any history of investigation games, like Danganronpa or Ace Attorney, but I played some similar games, some very old like Mortevielle Manor and some recent like Obra Dinn. So I went into this game a bit blind, that's for sure. Yet, I am a gamer, so my analysis still stands, surely.I was VERY hyped for that game! When it came out, I so wanted it, it called me! Picture it: a mystery/crime investigation, in a seemingly fantastic world of urban fantasy, a mix of synthwave, vaporwave, japanizing cyberpunk... visual novel mechanisms with First Person platformer gameplay... huge island to explore, lots of things to collect, NPCs to talk to, amazing music... everything looked SO promising! But after 20~ish hours, I can tell you: it is all just average. Let us go back to the list, one item at a time:1) Very hyped I was for sure, but was it my fault? was it the devs fault? the marketing? the reviews? With all that overall hype, I am not really sure. Probably mainly me: I personally believed Paradise Killer was a game that it was eventually not, so my bad I guess. Let me explain in further details below.2) A mystery/investigation, yes it is, but is it good? Not really. The story ends up being just interesting, not fascinating, and the more you play, the more you get the big picture... in an obvious, boring way. No big secrets really. The conspiracy gets obvious the more you dig. It sounds logical written like that, but the rendering of it is just... unsatisfying in terms of depth/plot twists. The worst of all? the BIG plot twist, THE piece of evidence that makes you solve EVERYTHING, is... hidden in the middle of nowhere, in a totally random, empty place, and I noticed it eventually after roaming through the island for 15 hours. In other words, you could totally miss it. Worse: you could start a new game, get to that place, find the thing and get the solution... this... is totally wrong in terms of game design, or just mystery writing... anyway. Don't even rush to the ending to know how it ends: you can actually end it whatever way you want, because, as they proclaim: YOUR facts, YOUR truth... yeah... I should have guessed.3) A world of urban fantasy, mix of synthwave, vaporwave, japanizing cyberpunk... Seriously, this was mostly rubbish to me. I was so let down on that one. The island is just devoid of life. It feels like a gamejam project, or a prototype. The art is so tacky/kitsch/clumsy, and very Japan-wannabe... I lived so many years in Japan and this art did nothing to me, actually worse. Maybe when I was 15 and fantasizing Japan? All the art, the pictures, the buildings, felt so... trivial, lots of very poor choices made by people idealizing Japan. All the urban fantasy lore and background also felt heavily insipid, somehow pretentious in all their obscure naming and weird mix of satanic + cocktail + dancefloor + cocaine style - seriously though, how is that a thing? I don't care for religion but this was so heavily satanic I laughed, all these goats, blood, sexy costumes, flashy poses wink wink... like what the F?! Do people enjoy that? It felt so out of touch, unlinked to the damn mystery that I wanted to enjoy...4) visual novel mechanisms with First Person platformer gameplay: what a let down here too... The visual novel mechanisms are okay-ish, though very repetitive and clumsy - talk 2 or 3 times to a NPC, this will activate a level of friendliness that makes him say "Hey there is actually a secret I need to share with you..." and you feel like you found something! But when you realize the whole dozen of NPCs in the game have the same threshold, the wallpaper fell off, the immersion was broken, what a heavy, sad choice of a mechanism! The First Person part was interesting, the platforming gimmick can get funny here and there (with upgrades to your jumping gameplay), but nothing more than a Refunct, and much less than a Mirror's Edge.5) Huge island to explore, lots of things to collect, NPCs to talk to: that is true, and yet it gets boring very quickly. The level design is totally unbalanced, like sometimes very interesting, sometimes so bad... A typical Japanese mansion building with 12 floors and an outside staircase? Yep, climb that, one at a time... with nothing in between. You want a fast travel to the other side of the island? Sure: pay a crystal. Don't have a crystal? There is like a 100 of them, scattered everywhere on the island, in the most stupid, random places. By the way, save yourself the rage: I gathered them all, all the crystals. Also ALL the relics, ALL the offerings, ALL the dialogues, ALL the drinks... It gave me nothing. NO--THING. That felt so unrewarding, so ungrateful from the devs... Not even a Steam achievement, not even a hidden something... Why, then? Why?6) Amazing music: YES! The only thing I was not disappointed with. Very good, groovy, inspired sound track. At least that was very well made, if you are into funky, a bit tacky music. I loved it.The conclusion? Paradise Killer is not a bad game, not even mediocre. It is a nice, little indie game, a bit weird, not great. An interesting, indie take on detective games. I just regret having spent that price, AND built so much expectation on it. Somehow it gave me the same feeling as for Cloudpunk if you know. I still recommend it IF you have the time and money to give it a try.Easter egg for the maniacs: if some of you remember the old WalkingInCircles flash game, I wanted to believe it would be similar... but WiC gave me more contemplative bliss than this game... how about that?!

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let superficial looks and cheap graphic turn you off before you are invested in the game. This is about the best detective and narrative game out there in a while and it shines in so many ways, and a lot of things that just as similarly want to make you jump off from a high place (looking at you developers!).The Good.1. Lovable cast of characters that always keep you wanting to find out more about them, and finding if they are guilty of the crime at hand. There are some stereotypes villains sure you already smell a mile away as going to be at the barrel of your gun, and also some lacklustre characters (hey doc, you need a personality), but a religious zealot, a goat headed idol who you can get the jiggy with it, a skeleton bar tender and super irritating military head of security are among the characters you can interact with, oh and don't forget the demons and gods.2. The world building is nothing like I have found and it shows when the first thing they have you do is ask you to jump off and hit the ground way way up without dying its going to be a fun trip. A mix of god worshippers, world creating immortals, awaken gods, demon possessed civilians and you know you are in for a heck of a trip. 3. The environment and landscape, it looks like you stepped into a low grade 90s game budget and tech but the look itself is deceptive, dig deeper and you would find the world is quite deep with many layers and nooks to explore, and hide secrets. While not Elden Ring gorgeous or graphic card killing beauty, it has its own charms that grows on you after a while. And there is beauty if you look hard enough.4. The final trial is a masterpiece, allowing you the freedom to craft a whodunnit using the clues you gathered and framing it to a narrative, less Sherlock Holmes, more Cluedo inspired. It's brilliant and you really made me tug my conscience not lay the blame on some good friends which you ended up getting buddy buddy with, or maybe i just went and killed everyone in the end, just because you allowed it. heck that can happen, yes.5. The treasure hunt which isn't obligatory but for an achievement perfectionist is irresistible, you turn what can be a short end game to spending hours doing side quests and exploring the world and forgot about the main story on many occasions as you stumble into a new secret or area by accident.The Bad1. I hate hate hate platformers and trick jumps, but dang did you make me suckered into it just to find all those secrets and you devs are really really sadistic in some of the placement of these areas. Fortunately, or by design the mystery reveal power given in the end was a blessing. Jumping off a building and making you go up 10 floors only to slip up again and repeating it wilfully, you got me good,2. Your achievement for the speed run, now you really made me sweat blood to get this final one, you terrible terrible person, to make it so delightfully triumphant when you get that last shinji, or last piece of mystery or win a 10 m killer speed run, dang maybe its the other way round and I'm just a masochist. 3. Putting fast travel with a paywall, evil evil but you also gave enough currency to solve everything and with change, but still, evil, I walked like enough for my daily cardio in this world.4. Your placement of some of the items in the world, you devil!!!! You really made me work for it.5. I want more demons! and cute doggos!Final say, get the game, you will not regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a game that caught my eye at Summer Games Fest, and I decided to give it a try as a it seemed like just the kind of low-energy game I could manage to play after my work day (as I'm often just too tired for anything that requires too much precision button pressing)And, boy, was it a good decision.Paradise Killer is a great game. Its not something I'd ever really played before, but theres a lot to enjoy here. The murder mystery is well crafted, truly gripping and is immensely satisfying when it all finally starts clicking into place. I don't want to admit how long I spent going over this case while I was trying to fall asleep. My total playtime clocked in at 14 hours, so you could easily get through it in a single  dedicated day, but I was playing in smaller sessions of 2-3 hours. So... lots of time to think the facts over before I finally went to Trial. The world of Paradise Killer is... bonkers. Utterly bonkers. But I adore it. The game (and the murder mystery) is made so much stronger for its worldbuilding, lore and history. I was not really expecting space gods and demons, but i am 100% down for every bit of it. Its integral to the core of the murder plot, and found there wasn't much in the way of worldbuilding that wasn't, in some way, relevant to the main plot. I also appreciated how much there was to explore and find in the open world. I've become very fed up of games whose maps are "open world" only to increase the amount of time it takes to go from a to b, instead of actually giving you something to . Paradise Killer, as a detective game, actively wants you to go everywhere and look at everything.I don't want to potentially spoil too much here, but justGame goodGive it a chance

_childDocuments_.review: It's a collectathon, not much detective reasoning going on. You explore the island, talk to the suspects, and everything gets slowly laid out in front of you. This is not necessarily a bad thing, but it's not a high brow detective reasoning game.However, the atmosphere is amazing, I love the art style, the dialogue is snappy, and the backstory/lore is absolutely, fantastically, ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up. Without spoilers, there's not a lot that is expanded on - which I would have loved - but if you enjoy lovecraft, or SCP, or just a messed up timeline, you'll love it.I don't see much replay value, but it's 10 hours I'm extremely happy with.
_childDocuments_.name: Paradise Killer

_childDocuments_.review: Its a dope mystery game, that's bogged down a bit by the tediousness of the large world.The game oozes style. All the characters look cool, the music is great, and the general setting of the world you're placed feels unique. The game-play itself is sort of your typical detective/investigation style (though on the lighter side), where you talk to people, find clues, explore the island, and eventually piece it all together to try to solve the mystery. What's kinda cool and different about this game is it gives you this world and characters, and then says let me know when you're ready to solve. So you have the freedom to end the game whenever you think you have what you need to solve the case. If you really wanted to you could just shoot for it the second you're dropped in, though I wouldn't recommend that lol.The only real issue with the game is the size of the world. Unfortunately, for how enjoyable the game and mystery is, it gets a little tedious at times due to just how big the world itself is. You'll find yourself running back and forth between a lot of the same locations as you talk to characters and and uncover new information, and by the halfway point it can get kinda annoying. There is fast travel (and there are actually a lot of fast travel points), but it costs a limited in-game currency. There is a decent bit of the currency to find in the world, but it is also used for other things as well. Unless you're constantly going out of your way to find it all, you will have to be mindful of your use as it costs currency to both unlock a fast travel point and for each use of a fast travel point. It also doesn't help that the world is for the most part empty (), so there isn't a ton to see on your way from point A to B out side of collectibles (and currency of course!), that in my opinion didn't really add a ton to the game or story. That being said there are puzzles and secrets to uncover across the world, but just not enough to really warrant the size or the constant running back and forth. I think this is really the only thing holding the game back.All that being said, I still had a blast with this game and thinks its worth the time and money, despite the gripes I had with some parts of it
